bugs.impact: Version 11.3.0 and earlier, tmm can crash. Version 11.4.0 and later, disabled connections may be reused.
bugs.workaround: Version 11.3.0 and earlier: If HTTP::disable is being called in a client-side event, OneConnect must be disabled in a server-side event. This can be done by including 'ONECONNECT::reuse disable' in the client-side event (so a new connection is created), setting a variable, and then invoking ONECONNECT::reuse disable in SERVER_CONNECTED Example: set oc_reuse_ss_disable 1 ONECONNECT::reuse disable CACHE::disable COMPRESS::disable HTTP::disable Add this (or merge with an existing SERVER_CONNECTED event in the iRule): when SERVER_CONNECTED { if { [info exists oc_reuse_ss_disable] } { ONECONNECT::reuse disable ONECONNECT::detach disable } } 11.4.0 and later: Replace "ONECONNECT::reuse disable" with "set oc_reuse_ss_disable 1" in the iRule client-side event. Add this (or merge with an existing SERVER_CONNECTED event in the iRule): when SERVER_CONNECTED { if { [info exists oc_reuse_ss_disable] } { ONECONNECT::reuse disable } }
bugs.fix: TMM no longer restarts when a OneConnect profile is applied to a virtual server and OneConnect reuse is disabled on the server side by an iRule.

bugs.title: Trust upgrade fails when upgrading from version 10.x to version 11.x.
bugs.symptoms: Trust upgrade fails when upgrading from version 10.x to version 11.x. The upgrade fails without apparent error, but there will be one of the two following error messages in /var/log/ltm log: -- com.f5.devmgmt.certmgmt.TrustConfigUpdateForHAPairTask.run(TrustConfigUpdateForHAPairTask.java:425): Trust configuration update for HA Pair has failed: [STACK TRACE: {java.lang.Exception: Config sync password is invalid.}{ at com.f5.devmgmt.certmgmt.TrustConfigUpdateForHAPairTask.run(TrustConfigUpdateForHAPairTask.java:200)}. -- devmgmtd[7983]: 015a0000:3: Trust Config Update: [TrustConfigUpdateForHAPair.cpp:521 ] Skipping already-completed trust.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading high availability version 10.x configurations that use the factory default admin password.
bugs.impact: Trust upgrade for version 10.x high availability configuration fails.
bugs.workaround: Change the default admin password in the 10.x configuration before upgrading to 11.0.0.
bugs.fix: Upgrades of high availability configurations from version 10.x to version 11.x or later now succeed, even if the 10.x system was still using the factory default admin password. It is recommended that you change the default admin password before deployment.

bugs.title: FTP mirroring fails when landing on tmm0
bugs.symptoms: There is an issue that is rarely encountered in FTP mirroring.
bugs.conditions: FTP mirroring occasionally fails when connections come from tmm0.
bugs.impact: When it does fail, the idle timer on the standby is not updated and the connection is reaped in the 30-50 second range.

bugs.title: ACL support for VPN tunnels
bugs.symptoms: ACL is not supported for connections between VPN tunnel clients.
bugs.conditions: Using APM network access.
bugs.impact: Cannot use ACL for connections between VPN tunnel clients.
bugs.fix: ACLs are now supported for connections between VPN tunnel clients. The following steps describe how to run ACLs for VPN/APM Network access tunnel clients: 1. Create an iRule : root@(bigip3923mgmt)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Eval:Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list ltm rule na_acl_leasepool ltm rule na_acl_leasepool { when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { if { [ACL::eval -l7 ] == 0 } { log local0. "no l7 acl" } } } 2. Attach it to related rules (not as iRule for virtual server) for network access virtual. To do so, use following tmsh command (there is no GUI to attach the iRule as related rules for a virtual server): modify ltm virtual vs_https related-rules { na_acl_leasepool }

bugs.title: Very Long URIs May Cause Delays
bugs.symptoms: Very long URI strings may cause delays in processing.
bugs.conditions: When a URI exceeds an average size, the system may slow down as it attempts to handle an excessively long string.
bugs.impact: Some processing delays.
bugs.workaround: This can be mitigated in application design, but there is no solution for existing applications that use excessively long URIs.

bugs.title: response_log_size_limit does not limit the log size.
bugs.symptoms: The internal parameter response_log_size_limit does not limit the log size.
bugs.conditions: The internal parameter response_log_size_limit is configured.
bugs.impact: Response log size limit is not applied.
bugs.fix: response_log_size_limit now correctly limits the log size.The internal parameter name was changed from response_logging_size_limit to response_log_size_limit .

bugs.title: Remove managers create/modify/delete ability from TMSH on GTM datacenters, links, servers, prober-pools, and topology errors incorrectly, and receive a database error when performed
bugs.symptoms: A "Manager" role has the ability to create/modify/delete GTM data centers, links, servers, prober pools, and topology objects from TMSH, but they do not have this permission in the database, so they get an error.
bugs.conditions: Someone of "Manager" roll attempts to create/modify/delete a GTM datacenter, link, server, prober-pools, or topology objects.
bugs.impact: Error message thrown
bugs.workaround: Error thrown is correct, but user's shouldn't be able to even get this far in tmsh.
bugs.fix: Removed Manager's ability to create/modify/delete GTM data centers, links, servers, prober-pools, and topology objects. This was already prevented through validation code, but now TMSH users only have access to view these objects.

bugs.title: Outgoing RIP advertisements may have incorrect source port
bugs.symptoms: TMM may change the source port of RIP packets send by ripd to something other than 520. Neighbor routers will not accept these packets and RIP routing will not work. If the TMM instance handling the outgoing packet would not be selected to handle return traffic by the hashing algorithm in use, the source port of the traffic will be modified so the hashing algorithm returns the same TMM instance.
bugs.conditions: Multiple TMM instances, RIP routing configured.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing using RIP will not work if the traffic hash of the packets does not match the TMM handling the outgoing traffic.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer modifies the source port of RIP traffic.

bugs.title: APM allows only limited resources to be added to webtop
bugs.symptoms: When trying to add more resources to a webtop that already contains a large number of resources, the command may fail.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the webtop already has a large number (hundreds or thousands, depending on configuration) of resources configured, and new webtop resources are added.
bugs.impact: APM policy execution will have a problem.
bugs.workaround: Limit the number of resources that can be added to the webtop.
bugs.fix: Increased the limit of resources that can be configured for the webtop.

bugs.title: TCP sends RST when regular close might succeed
bugs.symptoms: A TCP connection closing due to a TCP::close iRule suddenly ABORTS with a "No Server Selected" RST cause.
bugs.conditions: iRules close the connection on an early TCL event, before a load balancing decision is made. There is no pool member available.
bugs.impact: The connection closes ungracefully.

bugs.title: Disabling iRule events that are executing or pending execution will work correctly
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule event is executing or about to execute, disabling that event will not work correctly. The TMM will fail to complete the execution of the iRule, perhaps causing connection stalls. You may see the following signature in the LTM log: tmm info tmm[30823]: 01220009:6: Pending rule event CLIENT_ACCEPTED aborted on flow 10.10.0.1:59609->10.10.0.51:80 (listener: /Common/vs1)
bugs.conditions: An iRule event is disabled while it is executing (parked), or pending execution. Disabling an event from within its own rule will only work if no parking command executes afterwards.
bugs.impact: Connection stalls
bugs.workaround: If an iRule wants to disable itself, move that disabling to the end of the rule. This may make this issue less likely to occur.
bugs.fix: iRule events can be disabled at any time. If an iRule is disabled while it is executing, or pending execution, it will still run to completion. The next invocation of the iRule event will be disabled.

bugs.title: There is no indication that a failed standby cannot go active.
bugs.symptoms: There is no indication that a failed standby cannot go active. One example is if pool-min-up-members fails. In this case the device will go standby and since this condition may persist, it will not be able to go active.
bugs.conditions: When a standby fails, there is no indication that it cannot go active.
bugs.impact: It is not apparent that the standby cannot go active.
bugs.fix: -- The chassis display state of 'failed' is shown when a chassis is in the Standby state and one or more global fail-safe(s) is active on the chassis. -- The traffic group state of 'failsafe-fault' is displayed when a traffic group is in the Standby state and one or more global fail-safe(s) is active on the chassis. -- The commands 'show cm traffic-group' and 'show cm device' display the Standby state. -- Updated GUI to show failover status, as well updates to the overview and device screens under device management.
bugs.behavior: The system now provides indication that a failed standby cannot go active. -- The chassis display state of 'failed' is shown when a chassis is in the Standby state and one or more global fail-safe(s) is active on the chassis. -- The traffic group state of 'failed' is displayed when a traffic group is in the Standby state and one or more global fail-safe(s) is active on the chassis. -- The commands 'show cm traffic-group' and 'show cm device. display the Standby state. -- Updated GUI to show failover status, as well updates to the overview and device screens under device management.

bugs.title: No verification prompt when executing 'load sys config default' for resource administrator role
bugs.symptoms: When logged in as a resource administrator "load sys config default", which restores the configuration to factory defaults, doesn't prompt for verification as it should. If you execute the command from a normal administrator role you do get a prompt.
bugs.conditions: Login as a resource administrator run "load sys config default" restore begins without a verification prompt.
bugs.impact: System restore initiated without prompt when run as a resource administrator.

bugs.title: Access policy objects are created inconsistently depending on whether created using wizard or manually.
bugs.symptoms: Network Access (NA) wizard policy incorrectly labels 'Advanced Resource Assign' as 'Resource Assign' in VPE.
bugs.conditions: This is evident when viewing the label following completion of the NA wizard.
bugs.impact: The label in the VPE is 'Resource Assign', where it should be 'Advanced Resource Assign'.
bugs.fix: The label of Resource Assign agent created by the Network Access wizard is changed to Advanced Resource Assign, which is correct. Also the Wizard's user(admin) is presented with the choice of full/special webtop.

bugs.title: show ltm pool doesn't show the most updated info
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh show ltm pool' command doesn't show the latest updates for connection and rate limits. The connection and rate limits do not get published to the UI until a monitor instantiates a state change on the pool member or node.
bugs.conditions: Configure a pool member or node to have connection or rate limits.
bugs.impact: Statistics displayed using tmsh may not be current.
bugs.workaround: First run "tmsh show ltm pool members' to trigger update. Note: This does not impact the data path, it is only a UI issue.

bugs.title: iRules might return incorrect data when multiple partitions and/or folders contain objects with the same name
bugs.symptoms: iRules might return incorrect data when the BIG-IP configuration has folders or multiple administrative partitions that contain objects with the same name. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- Client connections receive incorrect data. -- The BIG-IP system incorrectly load balances client connections.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The configuration includes objects of the same name in different folders or administrative partitions -- An iRule references the object without using the fully-qualified path, e.g. "pool example_pool" instead of "pool /Common/folder1/example_pool"
bugs.impact: Client connections receive incorrect data, or are load balanced incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, always specify full paths to objects referenced in iRules, e.g. instead of: pool example_pool use: pool /Common/example_pool

bugs.title: The space character in a path prefix is not evaluated correctly.
bugs.symptoms: The space character in a path prefix is not evaluated correctly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a space character in a path prefix.
bugs.impact: The system does not evaluate the path prefix correctly.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, use the regular expression in a path segment match.

bugs.title: Loading UCS with low GTM Autoconf Delay drops pool Members from config
bugs.symptoms: Pool members loaded from the UCS are not in the configuration. If there are objects dependent on them, this may prevent the GTM config from loading completely.
bugs.conditions: GTM and LTM are enabled, Autoconf Delay is very low, there are GTM autoconfigured pool members from LTM virtual servers, and subsequently a UCS is loaded.
bugs.impact: GTM config loaded from the UCS might be overwritten and Pool Members might be lost from it.
bugs.workaround: bigstart stop gtmd during UCS load, or set the autoconf delay to be much higher than the time required to load the UCS.
bugs.fix: Loading UCS with low GTM Autoconf Delay now completes correctly.

bugs.title: iRule STREAM command internal error causes connection drop
bugs.symptoms: The connection might drop when STREAM::expression command is used.
bugs.conditions: The regular expression in STREAM::expression command has look-ahead pattern.
bugs.impact: The connection gets dropped.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using the look-ahead pattern.
bugs.fix: iRule STREAM command internal error no longer causes connection drop.

bugs.title: BIG-IP sends ND probes for all masquerading MAC addresses on all VLANs, so MAC might associated with multiple VLANs.
bugs.symptoms: Since traffic groups are not bound to any specific VLAN, so Neighbor Discovery (ND) for link-local addresses go out on all VLANs. This occurs because traffic groups are not bound to any particular VLAN or interface. Since MAC is bound to the traffic group, it is not bounded to particular VLAN either.
bugs.conditions: Using MAC masquerade addresses on VLANs. TMM creates new link-local address for each masquerading MAC. Thus, the same link-local address might be used on all interfaces, which means that the system might use the same MAC on different VLANs. For example, in the following configuration, you might expect that traffic-group-1 and MAC 02:23:e9:74:e2:c4 are bound only to VLAN Internal. However, you can create another self IP address, assign it to different VLANs or route domains, and have them be part of the same traffic group. A traffic group is about availability and not about routing or partitioning. Configuration =========== net self 10.10.10.10%1 { address 10.10.10.10%1/23 allow-service { default } floating enabled traffic-group traffic-group-1 unit 1 vlan Internal }.
bugs.impact: Although this is intended functionality, some users might not expect the behavior. BIG-IP sends ND probes for all masquerading addresses on all VLANs. Although switches typically build up forwarding tables per VLAN, there are some switches that might not correctly, which results in failure to forward packets as expected. That might impact other traffic, including IPv4.
bugs.workaround: Set the db variable tm.macmasqaddr_per_vlan to True. This ensures that a single source MAC is associated with a single VLAN ID, and is guaranteed to be unique per VLAN.

bugs.title: import_all_from_archive_file and import_all_from_archive_stream does not create file objects.
bugs.symptoms: An attempt to transition certs/keys/etc. from a 10.2.x configuration to version 11.5.4, 11.6.0, 11.6.1, or 12.0.0 configuration using import_all_from_archive_stream results in the files being copied to the directories under /config/ssl/, but no file-objects are created on the target system.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you attempt to transition certs/keys/etc. from a 10.2.x configuration to version 11.5.4, 11.6.0, 11.6.1, or 12.0.0 configuration using import_all_from_archive_stream.
bugs.impact: Files being copied to the directories under /config/ssl/, but no file-objects are created on the target system.
bugs.fix: Attempting to transition certs/keys/etc from a 10.2.x configuration to version 11.5.4, 11.6.0, 11.6.1, or 12.0.0 configuration using import_all_from_archive_stream now creates the file-objects on the target system in addition to the files being copied to the directories under /config/ssl/.

bugs.title: Manage Sessions are not showing correct current sessions on VIPRION chassis.
bugs.symptoms: Manage Sessions are not showing correct current sessions on VIPRION chassis.
bugs.conditions: This occurs using APM on VIPRION chassis.
bugs.impact: On the Admin Page, Access Policy, Manage Sessions, Current sessions is missing, which makes it difficult to find all the sessions to delete those sessions.

bugs.title: Unnecessary buffering of client-side egress in some circumstances.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP can perform unnecessary buffering of client-side egress in some circumstances. This can cause a tmm crash on out of memory. Analysis of the core by support indicates that the system has run out of memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this event to occur but it has been observed when modules like APM and ASM are enabled.

bugs.title: mcp error 0x1020003 may be logged to /var/log/tmm when TMM crashes
bugs.symptoms: A message beginning with 'mcp error: 0x1020003' may be logged to /var/log/tmm when TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: TMM crashes.
bugs.impact: This is an MCP error that is logged erroneously upon TMM shutdown, and does not indicate an issue with MCP.
bugs.fix: The message is no longer logged when TMM crashes.

bugs.title: Unable to create and update data-group in a single transaction
bugs.symptoms: Transaction fails with data-group not found error. This can occur if an iApp creates and modifies a data-group in the same transaction.
bugs.conditions: Creating and updating data-group in a single transaction.
bugs.impact: Unable to create and update data-group in a single transaction which, if split, could leave stray data-group objects if the update fails.
bugs.workaround: Split the data-group create and update into seperate transactions and handle cleanup if update transaction fails.

bugs.title: Network failover without a management address causes active-active after unit1 reboot
bugs.symptoms: A device in a Device Service Cluster may erroneously claim Active status when it is rebooted. This results in an Active/Active situation, which may resolve itself by causing a failover.
bugs.conditions: If a Device Service Cluster is configured with only self-IPs for unicast network failover communication, or if the management network between the peers is unavailable, the device may not detect that the peer is active when it is starting up. When using only self-IPs, communication with the peers is disrupted while the TMM is starting up.
bugs.impact: Unexpected failover may cause traffic interruption.
bugs.workaround: Configuring multiple redundant network failover paths, including the management network will reduce the possibility of this problem.

bugs.title: Using CLIENT_ACCEPTED iRule to set SNAT pool on OneConnect virtual server interferes with keepalive connections
bugs.symptoms: Using the 'snatpool' command in the CLIENT_ACCEPTED iRule event causes keepalive requests to originate from the self-IP of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: An iRule using the 'snatpool' command in CLIENT_ACCEPTED.
bugs.impact: Keepalive connections occasionally source from the BIG-IP system's self-IP address.
bugs.workaround: Use the HTTP_REQUEST event to set the SNAT pool.
bugs.fix: A virtual server no longer intermittently causes HTTP Keep-Alive connections to use a self IP address as the secure network address translation (SNAT) address.
bugs.behavior: The persistence record attached to a connection is no longer reset upon pool member detachment when using OneConnect. When using OneConnect, the pool member detaches on the completion of every response. This causes subsequent requests to be load balanced to the original pool member.

bugs.title: HTTP::respond/redirect might crash TMM under low-memory conditions
bugs.symptoms: HTTP::respond/redirect might crash TMM under low-memory conditions.
bugs.conditions: Under low-memory conditions, if a new HTTP connection triggers an HTTP::respond/redirect event.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Reduce memory usage
bugs.fix: HTTP::respond/redirect no longer crashes TMM under low-memory conditions.

bugs.title: IPv6.port format in iRule pool command is not errored out
bugs.symptoms: iRule pool command does not allow IPv6.port format, but it is taken and there is no error message.
bugs.conditions: The IPv6 address and port are in one argument in the format of Ipv6.port.
bugs.impact: The connection gets reset.
bugs.workaround: Use twp argument, e.g.: Ipv6 port
bugs.fix: In this release, the iRule pool command supports the IPv6.port format.

bugs.title: Clarification of pool member session enabling versus pool member monitor enabling
bugs.symptoms: In previous documentation of LocalLB::Pool::set_member_monitor_state and set_member_session_enabled_state lead to some confusion for those using the API.
bugs.conditions: Reading the documentation.
bugs.impact: Confusion in the expected behavior for both functions.
bugs.workaround: Experimentation with the SOAP api and observation of BIG-IP behavior.
bugs.fix: When set_member_session_enabled_state sets a pool member to disabled, then current connections will be maintained, but no more connections will be allowed. When set_member_monitor_state sets a pool member to disabled, then all connections will be killed immediately and no more connections will be allowed.

bugs.title: HSB lockup might occur when TMM tries unsuccessfully to reset HSB.
bugs.symptoms: An HSB lockup might occur when the TMM driver tries to reset HSB and the effort is not successful. After several failed attempts, a bad DMA packet causes tmm to crash. This failure can also result in a "DMA lockup on transmitter failure" reported in the TMM log files.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on HSB platforms that have AMD processors, which include the BIG-IP 6900, 8900, 8950, 11000, and 11050N platforms, and the VIPRION B4200 and B4200N blades.
bugs.impact: The HSB is non-functional and requires reinitialization. This occurs after the BIG-IP is rebooted, which is automatically triggered when this condition occurs.

bugs.title: Four new settings 'IBR-to', 'IBR-within', 'MC-to', and 'MC-within' are added to replace 'IBR' and 'MC' settings at WAM policy assembly page.
bugs.symptoms: Beginning with version 11.2.0, WAM parses and IBR/MC links inside a CSS file. Four new settings 'IBR-to', 'IBR-within', 'MC-to', and 'MC-within' are added to replace 'IBR' and 'MC' settings at WAM policy assembly page.
bugs.conditions: Beginning with version 11.2.0.
bugs.impact: For custom policies that have 'IBR' and 'MC' enabled, 'IBR-to', 'IBR-within', 'MC-to', and 'MC-within' will be enabled too after migration to this release. In other words, WAM will IBR/MC CSS files for these policies.
bugs.workaround: If you prefer not to use this feature, you must disable the settings on corresponding policy nodes.

bugs.title: Cluster member disable or reboot can leak a few cross blade trunk packets
bugs.symptoms: Using the cluster member 'disable' command with a trunk that spans blades might cause a brief period where received broadcast and multicast packets egress out the enabled trunk members of the cluster.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on a trunk that spans blades.
bugs.impact: To an external device running spanning tree protocol or variant, this can look like a loop.
bugs.fix: Cluster member disable or reboot no longer leaks a few cross-blade trunk packets.

bugs.title: mysqld incorrectly classifies the lost+found directory as a database location resulting in benign errors in the mysql log.
bugs.symptoms: mysqld incorrectly classifies the lost+found directory as a database location resulting in benign errors in the mysql log. [ERROR] Invalid (old?) table or database name 'lost+found' 120104 7:12:52 [ERROR] /usr/sbin/mysqld: Can't find file: './lost+found/AVR_STAT_CLIENT_IP_T.frm' (errno: 13)
bugs.conditions: This occurs in all versions of BIG-IP running MySQL including all of 11.x and 12.x.
bugs.impact: None. The error is benign.

bugs.title: tmrouted restart after reconfiguration of previously deleted route domain
bugs.symptoms: When a non-default route domain is configured for dynamic routing, then subsequently deleted and re-added, tmrouted might restart.
bugs.conditions: Non-default route domains in use.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing for all route domains is interrupted.
bugs.fix: tmrouted no longer restarts when reconfiguring a previously deleted route domain.

bugs.title: Logon failure when Access Policy contains On-Demand Cert Agent for legacy logon method
bugs.symptoms: Username and password are not sent when the On-Demand Cert Auth agent is used in an access policy.
bugs.conditions: - On-Demand Cert Auth agent is used in an access policy. - Clients: iOS, Android, Windows Mobile, and Linux CLI.
bugs.impact: Logon fails. This is a known limitation for clients that utilize legacy logon method (this includes clients running iOS, Android, Windows Mobile clients, Linux CLI, etc). The limitation occurs because the On-Demand Cert Agent triggers a few client redirects (HTTP 302) for renegotiation, and that causes the post data to my.activation to be lost.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, put the Logon page agent before the On-Demand Cert Agent in the access policy.

bugs.title: Support for SPDY over TLS
bugs.symptoms: There is no support for SPDY over TLS.
bugs.conditions: Trying to use SPDY over TLS.
bugs.impact: Cannot use SPDY over TLS.
bugs.fix: This release adds SPDY classification support.

bugs.title: Users are not synchronized if created in a partition
bugs.symptoms: Users in partitions attached to sync-only device groups do not sync to other devices in that device group.
bugs.conditions: There are users whose active partitions are attached to a sync-only device group.
bugs.impact: This affects sync-only device groups only, not the failover device group.

bugs.title: TMM crashes if there is an error in a SERVER_CLOSED iRule on a FastL4 virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes if there is an error in a SERVER_CLOSED iRule on a FastL4 virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is an error in a SERVER_CLOSED iRule on a FastL4 virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, ensure there are never any errors in SERVER_CLOSED iRules on FastL4 virtual servers.

bugs.title: Front-end Kerberos Authentication fails when Request Based Authentication is enabled and non-standard port is in use
bugs.symptoms: Front-end Kerberos Authentication fails.
bugs.conditions: -- Kerberos front-end authentication is configured. -- Request based authentication (RBA) is enabled. -- Virtual server is configured with non-standard HTTP/HTTPS port.
bugs.impact: End user clients cannot log in.
bugs.workaround: Configure the virtual server to use the standard port.

bugs.title: Internal Datagroup Entries are added one at a time in TMM
bugs.symptoms: You may see entries coming in one at a time while an iRule is running.
bugs.conditions: Using internal datagroup in an iRule.
bugs.impact: iRule operates incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: Use an external datagroup instead of an internal datagroup.

bugs.title: Provisioning a module may fail to reload page.
bugs.symptoms: Provisioning a module may fail to reload page.
bugs.conditions: Provisioning a module and automatically reloading.
bugs.impact: An error may be displayed although the reprovisioning may be successful.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Provisioning a module no longer fails to reload page.

bugs.title: 'with' statement in web applications works wrong in some cases
bugs.symptoms: Web-application misbehavior (exception, wrong rendering, and so on).
bugs.conditions: If the JavasScript operator 'with' is used in web-application code and, if after rewriting, 'F5_ScopeChain' is found within the 'with' statement in these contexts: ...F5_Inflate_xxxxx(F5_ScopeChain,... ...F5_Deflate_xxxxx(F5_ScopeChain,... ...F5_Invoke_xxxxx(F5_ScopeChain,... then there is probability of this issue.
bugs.impact: Web-application functionality.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, an iRule can be used for changing an 'interesting' variable name within the function's body. No general iRule exists. For each case, a custom iRule must be created as workaround.

bugs.title: Deleting and recreating pool members with named nodes can cause config sync to fail.
bugs.symptoms: Config sync fails after changing an IP address of a pool member with a node name. IP addr change achieved by deleting the pool member and node then recreating the pool member/node.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following steps are followed. 1. Delete an existing pool member that has a node name set. 2. Recreate the pool member with a different IP address using the same node name before syncing the config. 3. Sync the configuration. ltm pool ip_mod_pl { members { ip_mod2_nd:http { address 10.168.1.4 } ip_mod_nd:http { address 10.168.1.1 } } } ltm node ip_mod2_nd { address 10.168.1.4 } tmsh modify ltm pool ip_mod_pl members delete { ip_mod2_nd:http} tmsh delete ltm node ip_mod2_nd tmsh modify ltm pool ip_mod_pl members add { ip_mod2_nd:http { address 10.168.1.5 }} tmsh run cm config-sync to-group S48-S49 On versions 11.4.0 and later, the issue happens only if a full is performed. Note that full loads may still complete successfully on occasion, even if full-load-on-sync is false for the device group.
bugs.impact: Config sync fails.
bugs.workaround: Delete the pool member and node on the peer then sync the configuration. The issue does not affect pool members/nodes with no name associated with the node.

bugs.title: No message when removing PSU from chassis.
bugs.symptoms: When a power supply is removed from a chassis, there is no warning or alert message on the console.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when removing a PSU from a chassis, and there is insufficient power from the plugged in PSUs.
bugs.impact: NOTICE-level log messages are posted in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.workaround: PSU changes can be detected using the command 'tmsh show sys hardware'.

bugs.title: Stats presented by the MIB sysVlanStatTable does not match sflow vlan stats
bugs.symptoms: Stats presented by the MIB sysVlanStatTable does not match sflow vlan stats.
bugs.conditions: Running the following command returns data inconsistent with sflow statistics: snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysVlanStatTable.
bugs.impact: Incorrect interpretation of vlan stats. As a result of fixing this issue, F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysVlanStatTable is obsoleted, IF-MIB::ifXTable should be used instead.
bugs.fix: The IF-MIB::ifXTable was implemented to use the same stats as sflow. The F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysVlanStatTable is obsolete.
bugs.behavior: F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysVlanStatTable is obsoleted, IF-MIB::ifXTable should be used instead.

bugs.title: min-up-members and using gateway-failsafe-device on the same pool.
bugs.symptoms: The system does not require setting a pool's min-up-members greater than 0 (zero) when also using gateway-failsafe-device on the same pool.
bugs.conditions: A pool's min-up-members is 0 when gateway-failsafe-device is set.
bugs.impact: Failure to set min-up-members greater than 0 when using gateway-failsafe-device might cause errors. The tmm might crash.
bugs.workaround: Set min-up-members greater than 0 when using gateway-failsafe-device.

bugs.title: imish 'terminal monitor' command does not have any effect in TMOS
bugs.symptoms: When you run the imish 'terminal monitor' command, you do not receive the expected results. The imish command has no effect in TMOS.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running imish command.
bugs.impact: There is no display of debug logs in the imish session.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to configure the log file (under /var/log) and use the tail command to monitor it in real-time. Note: For this workaround, users must have access to bash.

bugs.title: Erroneously enabling image optimization on policy nodes matching HTML or CSS content causes that content to become uncacheable, and the system posts S10206 codes.
bugs.symptoms: Erroneously enabling image optimization on policy nodes matching HTML or CSS content causes that content to become uncacheable, and the system posts S10206 codes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when enabling image optimization on nodes that match content that can be parsed (for example, HTML or CSS content).
bugs.impact: Content is not cached and responses return S10206 codes.

bugs.title: Cannot use ssldump to decrypt SSL traffic protected by netHSM key
bugs.symptoms: If the captured traffic is protected by netHSM, it cannot be decrypted, even with the access to the netHSM key.
bugs.conditions: SSL traffic protected by netHSM keys.
bugs.impact: Cannot decrypt the netHSM key-protected SSL traffic using ssldump.

bugs.title: Remote Auth user names containing blank space cannot login through TMSH.
bugs.symptoms: Remote Auth user names containing blank space cannot login through TMSH.
bugs.conditions: Remote authentication configuration needs to be setup, and the BIG-IP system should be configured to use remote authentication rather than local auth.
bugs.impact: Users cannot log into the box using TMSH.
bugs.fix: Remote user authentication now allows blank space in user names.

bugs.title: Authorization requests not being cached when allowed.
bugs.symptoms: Requests containing authorization headers are not cached under any circumstance, not complying with RFC 2626 14.8.
bugs.conditions: -- Requests containing Authorization headers. -- OWS returning responses with either cache-control:public, must-revalidate or s-maxage.
bugs.impact: The cache benefit is not seen in objects that should be cached that are requested using authentication headers.
bugs.fix: Now the authentication header handling complies with RFC 2616 14.8, based on the OWS response headers.

bugs.title: Crond does not apply timezone changes
bugs.symptoms: When the timezone a BIG-IP is updated crond does not apply the new timezone
bugs.conditions: Device timezone updated
bugs.impact: Cron scheduled tasks do not execute at the expected time
bugs.workaround: Restart the affected device after applying timezone changes

bugs.title: web-acceleration profile not working with access profile
bugs.symptoms: With Access Policy Manager Portal Access, if you add a web-acceleration profile to the Local Traffic virtual server, it does not take effect until the you go to the command line and type "bigstart restart tmm". The web-acceleration profile is important to Portal Access performance, so this step is necessary to ensure caching occurs for Portal Access content.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server configured with Access profile, and a web-accelerator profile is added to it
bugs.impact: Web acceleration is not enabled on the virtual server, which negatively impacts performance of APM on that virtual.
bugs.workaround: At the command line, type bigstart restart tmm.

bugs.title: Duplicated cert/keys/chain might cause SIGABRTs and low-memory conditions
bugs.symptoms: SSL per-virtual stats might cause SSL profile cert/keys/chain to be instantiated per-virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using cert/keys/chain in SSL profile virtual servers.
bugs.impact: In this case, cert/keys/chain are duplicated and those duplicates might cause excessive memory use and disk activity which might lead to SIGABRTs and low-memory conditions.
bugs.fix: Improved memory management when there are duplicated keys or certs.

bugs.title: A FastL4 virtual server does not always return from suspending commands.
bugs.symptoms: A FastL4 virtual server does not always return from suspending commands.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using a suspending iRule command in CLIENT_DATA in FastL4.
bugs.impact: If an 'after' command is executed, it does not return until the connection times out. This is most noticeable in a DNS configuration.
bugs.workaround: Do not include parking commands in CLIENT_DATA in FastL4.

bugs.title: Management IP changes are not synced to the device group.
bugs.symptoms: A device group shows a device as offline when it was previously working, and the device's management IP address has recently changed.
bugs.conditions: When the management IP is changed on a device in a trust domain, it is not updated in the device group even though its config sync IP is a SelfIP and config sync continues to work. Other devices show it offline under Device Management :: Devices.
bugs.impact: Incorrect device status displayed when looking at the device group.
bugs.workaround: To resolve this, the device that changed must be discovered from a device that is not changed. Note: If you attempt to discover a device that is not changed from the device that is changed, the operation loses the hostname and other configuration objects.

bugs.title: Certain user roles do not trigger config sync for the 'modify auth password' command
bugs.symptoms: If users with the certain roles change their password, the BIG-IP system does not detect that it is out-of-sync with its peer and does not trigger an automatic sync:
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple BIG-IP devices in a Device Service Cluster that sync configurations with each other. -- A user with one of the following roles logs in and changes their password: + guest + operator + application-editor + manager + certificate-manager + irule-manager + resource-admin + auditor + administrator
bugs.impact: The system does not detect that it is out of sync with its peer, and does not report this condition. If automatic sync is enabled, a sync does not automatically occur.
bugs.workaround: Force a full config sync to the peer systems.

bugs.title: Portal Access Resource does not support session variables in custom HTTP Headers
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access Resource does not support session variables in custom HTTP Headers.
bugs.conditions: Here is example of Portal Access Resource, where session variable %{session.last.logon.username} substitution is expected: apm resource portal-access minmal_patching { acl-order 2 customization-group minmal_patchinb_resource_web_app_customization host-replace-string 192.168.20.41 host-search-strings 192.168.20.41 items { item { compression-type none host * order 1 paths * port any scheme any subnet 0.0.0.0/0 headers { { name X-G2-User value "%{session.last.logon.username}" } { name X-G2-Groupe value testheader } } } } patching-type min-patch path-match-case false scheme-patching true }
bugs.impact: No substitution for session variables in custom HTTP headers.
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used.

bugs.title: HSL::open iRule causes Virtual Server to go green
bugs.symptoms: An iRule configured with HSL::open will cause the virtual server to which it's attached to be marked as green (up), even if there are no available pool members.
bugs.conditions: iRule attached to a virtual server that contains HSL::open as the first command.
bugs.impact: Connections are reset if the pool contains no members.
bugs.workaround: In your iRule, instead of configuring HSL::open like the following: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { set hsl [HSL::open -proto UDP -pool My_HSL_Pool] } Set a variable before calling HSL::open when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { set mypool My_HSL_Pool set hsl [HSL::open -proto UDP -pool $mypool] } The pool's status will then be properly propagated to the virtual server status.

bugs.title: iRule TCP::close on vip with Ramcache can cause TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: iRule TCP::close on vip with Ramcache can cause TMM restart
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using TCP::close in an iRule inside HTTP_REQUEST while RAM cache is configured.
bugs.impact: Unknown
bugs.workaround: Disable RAM cache.

bugs.title: Multidomain SSO requires a default pool be configured
bugs.symptoms: When configuring multidomain SSO, a pool must be assigned to the virtual, even if one is not being used. A typical symptom of not assigning the pool is that after logon, the user will be redirected back to another logon page.
bugs.conditions: Any use case of multidomain SSO where there is no pool configured on the virtual servers, and there is not a webtop assigned.
bugs.impact: There are two known use cases where this is commonly encountered. 1) LTM + Secure Connectivity virtuals do not usually have a default pool configured. 2) The pool is being configured through an iRule
bugs.workaround: When configuring multidomain SSO, always assign a default pool to the virtual server.
bugs.fix: Some of the logic in ACCESS was updated to add consideration of dynamic pool assignments (eg. iRules) in addition to the default pool. Default pool is no longer needed for multidomain SSO.

bugs.title: Client detection does not work for new browsers and always Download client prompt is shown
bugs.symptoms: When APM end-users connect to APM, they are prompted to down the Citrix client even if their browser does not support it.
bugs.conditions: Webtop is used with the latest browsers (who have disabled NPAPI support) to access the Citrix published resources.
bugs.impact: Users are prompted to Download the client every time they access the webtop.
bugs.fix: Automatic client detection functionality for Receiver Clients has been disabled from the APM webtop and is now a manual setting. See the note for ID427028 for more information.

bugs.title: Multidomain SSO shows login page when switching to webtop virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Issue # 1 When you click on the webtop (which accesses the root URL of the application) that shares a multi-domain SSO with the virtual server (with a webtop resource assigned), the existing session is deleted and you must re-authenticate. Issue # 2 When you access the virtual server (with an access policy attached) and the webtop UI opens, if you then opens a new tab and access the same virtual server, the existing session is deleted and you must re-authenticate.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is configured. -- A configured virtual server that assigns a webtop. -- A webtop link that shares an access profile with that virtual server. -- You click this webtop link.
bugs.impact: Existing APM session is deleted and you are required to re-authenticate.
bugs.fix: The existing session now continues, and you are not required to re-authenticate under these conditions.

bugs.title: Geolocation information cannot be modified in New Session log entry
bugs.symptoms: The user is attempting to overwrite the output of geo-location database before the new session log entry is created.
bugs.conditions: This is an enhancement, where a user is attempting to change values of geo-location information in the log entry. The overwriting of the values is being attempted so as to further assist in reporting.
bugs.impact: The geo-location information values in the log entry cannot be changed.
bugs.workaround: The geo-location information (ST/CC/C) are available through session variables. In access policy these session variables can be overwritten using 'variable assignment agent' and a new log entry can be created using 'log agent'. The reporting tool can make use of this 'new' log entry and parse/use the overwritten geo-location information.

bugs.title: Cannot use TMSH to change virtual server type
bugs.symptoms: You cannot use TMSH to change the virtual server type, for example, take an IP forwarding virtual server and reconfigure it into a vanilla FastL4 or standard virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Want to change a non-standard virtual server to a standard virtual.
bugs.impact: There is no provision to change the virtual server type through TMSH.
bugs.workaround: Use GUI to make the change.

bugs.title: LTM pool member link in a route domain is wrong in Network Map.
bugs.symptoms: Pool member link in a route domain in Network Map is broken.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for pool members that exist in a route domain.
bugs.impact: System cannot correctly read the % used with route domains.
bugs.fix: LTM pool member link in a route domain is now in the correct Network Map.

bugs.title: RSA SecurID node secret is not synced to the standby node
bugs.symptoms: When RSA SecurID node secret files are created on the active node, the files are not synced to the standby node. As a result, user will not be able to log on after switchover.
bugs.conditions: RSA node secret files are created on the active node after the first successful authentication.
bugs.impact: Service will be inaccessible after switchover.
bugs.workaround: 1. Copy node secret files /config/aaa/ace/Common/<rsa_securid_aaa_server>/sdstatus.12 and /config/aaa/ace/Common/<rsa_securid_aaa_server>/securid from the active node to the same directory on the standby node. 2. Wait for at least 30 seconds 3. Execute the command "tmsh save sys config" to commit the changes to disk.
bugs.fix: The SecurID node secret file monitoring algorithm was updated so that a new node secret file can be detected. Also, aced now authenticates with mcpd so that any node secret file object changes will be accepted by the mcpd.

bugs.title: OAM reporting Access Server down with JDK version 1.6.0_27 or later
bugs.symptoms: Cannot connect to Access Server. When running eamtest tool to check the functionality between OAM and the access server are working correctly, the following error is seen: Preparing to connect to Access Server. Please wait. Access Server you specified is currently down. Please check your Access Server.oamconfig[2368]: Could not configure OAM
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs only when OAM server is installed with JDK version 1.6.0_27 or later.
bugs.impact: Cannot connect to backend OAM server using BIG-IP AccessGate.
bugs.workaround: Install older version of JDK than v1.6.0_27.
bugs.fix: Applied OAM ASDK patch given by Oracle, so OAM no longer reports Access Server down with JDK version 1.6.0_27 or later.

bugs.title: Flash items on webpage do not load correctly through APM portal
bugs.symptoms: The Portal Access feature in APM does not support Flex Runtime Shared Libraries using ActionScript3.
bugs.conditions: Access Portal enabled Applications contain flash content that were created with Flex.
bugs.impact: Flex applet does not work through Portal.
bugs.fix: Portal Access is not able to rewrite signed .swz Flex framework library files.

bugs.title: Support Route Domains for VDI deployments (Citrix, VMware View, RDP)
bugs.symptoms: VDI deployments (Citrix, VMware Horizon View, and Microsoft Remote Desktop (RDP)) do not support non-default route domains for backend addresses.
bugs.conditions: APM deployment used for some remote desktop access (Citrix, VMware Horizon View, or RDP).
bugs.impact: Cannot use non-default route domains for VDI deployments.
bugs.fix: For VDI deployments, the route domain to be used is either taken from session.assigned.route_domain variable or (if sessvar is not available) the route domain of the virtual server is used. Note: This doesn't work for the environments that make use of other APM configuration objects that currently don't support non-default route domains, such as WebSSO.
bugs.behavior: Previously, VDI deployments (Citrix, VMware Horizon View, and RDP) did not support non-default route domains for backend addresses. Now, the route domain to be used is either taken from session.assigned.route_domain variable or (if sessvar is not available) the route domain of the virtual server is used. Note: This doesn't work for the environments that make use of other APM configuration objects that currently don't support non-default route domains, such as WebSSO.

bugs.title: Allow the HTTP::payload command to be used in the HTTP_REJECT iRule event
bugs.symptoms: It is difficult to obtain the contents of an HTTP request or response that the BIG-IP system rejects. (This requires using a complex iRule involving TCP::collect, with some performance cost.)
bugs.conditions: An HTTP request or response fails a test at the parsing stage. It may be too large, have too many headers, have invalid structure, or some other issue.
bugs.impact: Difficult to obtain the contents of an HTTP request or response that the BIG-IP system rejects.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule with TCP::collect to obtain this information. Note: This might result in a performance cost.
bugs.fix: The contents of a rejected HTTP request or response is now available in the HTTP_REJECT iRule event from the HTTP::payload command. This allows rejected requests and responses to be logged via an iRule script, and later inspected.

bugs.title: SNMP_DCA_BASE monitor does not recognize Threshold and Coefficient
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP_DCA_BASE monitor does not return the correct weight.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the SNMP_DCA_BASE monitor. On version 10.x the threshold and coefficient values existed so this may be discovered after upgrading. For more information on configuring SNMP DCA see SOL14110: Creating a custom SNMP DCA or SNMP DCA Base monitor at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/100/sol14110.html
bugs.impact: Dynamic load balancing does not work properly with the SNMP_DCA_BASE monitor.

bugs.title: TMSH Command to retrieve the memory consumption of the bd process
bugs.symptoms: There is no tmsh commands to retrieve the memory consumption of the bd process.
bugs.conditions: tmsh commands don't show bd process memory usage.
bugs.impact: Difficult to diagnose memory consumption issues.
bugs.workaround: Review messages individually in /var/log/ts/bd.log. ### For ASM bd current memory consumption use the following grep command cat /ts/log/bd.log | grep "UMU: total" UMU: total 106 ( 0M) VM (1639M) RSS (164M) SWAP ( 0M) trans 0 UMU: total 106 ( 0M) VM (1639M) RSS (163M) SWAP ( 0M) trans 0 UMU: total 5 ( 0M) VM (1612M) RSS (163M) SWAP ( 0M) trans 0 ### For XML memory consumption in bd process do the following on a big-ip. *WARNING*: The following steps enable debug prints to the bd.log it may cause to an excessive io, handle with care on production boxes. 1. add the following 3 lines the /etc/ts/bd/logger.cfg MODULE=BD_XML; LOG_LEVEL=TS_INFO | TS_DEBUG; FILE = 2; 2. Run a CLI tool. /usr/share/ts/bin/set_active.pl --update_logger_cfg To stop the debug prints, remove the 3 mentioned lines from the logger.cfg file and run the CLI tool again.
bugs.fix: The following command now reports memory consumption of the bd process: tmctl asm_memory_util_stats For specific fields -s option can be used, for example: tmctl asm_memory_util_stats -s total_xml_mem_used,total_xml_max_mem

bugs.title: GTM Device IP translation address not available from iControl
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to set the IP translation address from iControl.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a GTM Server that requires an IP translation address.
bugs.impact: A different interface must be used to configure the address.
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI or tmsh commands to configure the address.
bugs.fix: The GTM Device IP translation address is now configurable by iControl.

bugs.title: Configuration utility may become non-responsive or fail to load.
bugs.symptoms: While doing normal operations via the configuration utility, the status indicators may become non-responsive or fail to load, the GUI could become very sluggish, and you could be unable to load the GUI, or you could be taken to the license activation screen.
bugs.conditions: This has been reported most frequently when deleting local users (Access Policy :: Local User DB : Manage Users), but has been encountered in other ways. The issue might require deleting a user and then remaining on the Manage Users page until an internal timeout of approximately 10 minutes passes.
bugs.impact: Unable to log into the GUI or GUI shows blank page
bugs.workaround: Run the command 'bigstart restart tomcat' or reboot the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Configuration utility now responds as expected when deleting local users (Access Policy :: Local User DB : Manage Users), or under other conditions in which an internal timeout results in GUI non-responsiveness because of an incomplete transaction close.

bugs.title: Objects configured with a connection rate-limit and yellow status
bugs.symptoms: The availability status for objects configured with a connection rate-limit can remain yellow even if the object is available to handle traffic.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using objects configured with a connection rate-limit.
bugs.impact: Once the connection rate falls below the configured value, the object's status continues to show unavailable until the object receives additional traffic.
bugs.fix: Objects configured with a connection rate-limit will now show status available whenever the connection rate falls below the configured value.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as IdP with SAML resources assigned to access policy requires webtop
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP configured as an IdP with SAML resources assigned to the access policy requires a webtop to be assigned to the access policy.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP configured as an IdP. -- SAML resources assigned to the access policy.
bugs.impact: You cannot successfully execute the access policy without assigning a webtop to the access policy.
bugs.fix: When BIG-IP is configured as an IdP and SAML resources are assigned in the access policy, the access policy no longer requires that a webtop be assigned.

bugs.title: MCP unexpectedly exits, "failure has occurred, There is no active database transaction, status: 0 -
bugs.symptoms: MCP exits unexpectedly and you see a trace in the ltm log file similar to: Feb 9 12:54:41 localhost err mcpd[9995]: 01070596:3: An unexpected failure has occurred, There is no active database transaction, status: 0 - EdbDbConnection.cpp, line 133, exiting...
bugs.conditions: Unexpected MCP exit.
bugs.impact: MCP is already exiting, so there is no impact.
bugs.fix: Changed ordering of shutdown operations to avoid MCP error message for benign condition.

bugs.title: Added the transparent option for DNS monitor
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to create transparent DNS monitor in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Trying to configure a DNS monitor as transparent.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the GUI to create a transparent DNS monitor.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to configure the transparent option for DNS monitors.
bugs.fix: The DNS monitor now has the transparent option available from the GUI.

bugs.title: Upgrade process does not update Tcl scripts
bugs.symptoms: The upgrade process does not update Tcl scripts (such as iRules) in the configuration.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading Tcl scripts (such as iRules).
bugs.impact: This might cause issues when iRule syntax changes between releases. After upgrading, you might need to modify iRules to reflect any changes in iRule syntax.
bugs.workaround: None. ★ This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Networks Technical Support web site: http://www.f5.com/support/ The AskF5 web site: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/home The F5 DevCentral web site: http://devcentral.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Tue Aug 21 10:28:09 2018 PDT Copyright F5 Networks (2018) - All Rights Reserved Contact Support

bugs.title: GETs for an unsatisfiable range on a compressed document results in full bypass on expiration.
bugs.symptoms: If you cache a compressed document normally, and then switch to asking for a range beyond the end of the document, you get a 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable response from WAM, but only while the cached content has a positive lifetime. As soon as the document expires and needs re-validation with the OWS, the response from WAM is a complete bypass, with no WAM related headers at all, resulting in partial content reflecting the full uncompressed content-range.
bugs.conditions: Cache a compressed document normally, and then switch to requesting a range beyond the end of the document.
bugs.impact: 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable response.

bugs.title: Error message in dmesg and kern.log: vpd r/w failed
bugs.symptoms: When running dmesg, you might see errors similar to the following: 0000:17:00.0: vpd r/w failed. This is typically considered a firmware issue on the device, and you can contact the card vendor for a firmware update. This error can be seen in /var/log/kern.log as well.
bugs.conditions: This can occur whenever 'lspci -vv' (or 'lspci -vvv', e.g., during qkview generation) is executed.
bugs.impact: This is a benign firmware message, and you can safely ignore it.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, but this is not a functional issue.

bugs.title: Improved security for Apache.
bugs.symptoms: Improved security for Apache.
bugs.conditions: Improved security for Apache.
bugs.impact: Improved security for Apache.

bugs.title: Volume threshold and time threshold support in Gx reporting
bugs.symptoms: In this release, volume threshold is supported. However, time threshold does not qualify for Gx reporting, even though it is present in GUI and TMSH
bugs.conditions: Configuring volume threshold and time threshold in Gx reporting.
bugs.impact: Configuring volume threshold does not work as expected. Configuring time threshold has no effect because it is not supported.
bugs.fix: Volume threshold and time threshold have been removed from the GUI and TMSH for Gx reporting.

bugs.title: Active Session Count graph underflow
bugs.symptoms: On all platforms, the active session count might be significantly large at times likely due to a counter underflow.
bugs.impact: Wrong active session graphs are presented at certain times.
bugs.fix: The active session count graphs no longer becomes significantly large at times due to a counter underflow.

bugs.title: Use of a # in a TACACS secret causes remote auth to fail
bugs.symptoms: TACACS remote auth fails when the TACACS secret contains the '#' character.
bugs.conditions: TACACS secret contains the '#' character.
bugs.impact: TACACS remote auth fails.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the '#' character in the TACACS secret.

bugs.title: mcpd and datastor volumes on blades
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd validation will fail and cause daemons to restart if the datastor volume sizes on a cluster are not the same on all blades and the sum of the used web-acceleration profile cache sizes is higher than the datastor volume size on a secondary blade.
bugs.conditions: All of the following conditions must be met to cause this problem: 1) chassis with blades having different size hard drives (mixed blade types on a chassis) 2) AAM provisioned 3) having web-acceleration profiles configured with applications attached and large cache size values 4) virtual servers with web-acceleration profiles from above 5) sum of the different web-acceleration profiles' cache size values from above is greater than the datastor (AAM) volume on any secondary blade
bugs.impact: Mcpd and daemons go into a restart loop on secondary blades and managing the chassis becomes hard.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the sum of the web-acceleration profile cache size values is smaller than the smallest datastor volume. Ideally, don't configure the profiles for the maximum cache size possible.

bugs.title: "WEBSSO::select" cannot use SSOv2 configuration objects
bugs.symptoms: Selecting an SSO configuration with WEBSSO::select does not work for form-based client-initiated and SAML SSO configurations.
bugs.conditions: iRule utilizing WEBSSO::select
bugs.impact: iRule validation error that might look like the following: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/test_sso] error: Unable to find sso_config (test) referenced at line 4: [WEBSSO::select test]
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, use a variable to assign the configuration object name: set sso_config /Common/SAML-config WEBSSO::select $sso_config unset sso_config

bugs.title: SAML Error: Invalid request received from remote client is too big
bugs.symptoms: Some SAML deployments will produce SAML Assertions or SAML Authentication Requests in POST data that are larger than 64KB. When this occurs, an error message will be produced in the APM log: "Invalid request received from remote client is too big."
bugs.conditions: When a BIG-IP systems acts as a SAML service provider, it supports only assertions of size 64K or less. Also, when a BIG-IP system acts as a SAML IdP, it supports only authentication requests of size 64K or less.
bugs.impact: SAML cannot be used in BIG-IP as IdP or BIG-IP as SP with deployments that cause large POST data from clients.
bugs.workaround: No workaround possible.

bugs.title: Access Policy Export / Import fails when folders are used
bugs.symptoms: APM has an Import / Export function to import and expor Access Policies to import on a separate BIG-IP system. This fails when Access Policies are contained inside of subfolders. Since most iApps (Microsoft Exchange, Citrix, or VMware View) produce Access Policies that contain subfolders, the effective result is that iApp-generated Access Policies cannot be imported or exported to another BIG-IP system. On export you may see this error: Export Error: Profile partition Common/OWA_F5.app is not admin's partition Common or Common. On import you may see this error: Import Error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: The object (Customization Group /Common/<resource>) is owned by a non-existent application (/Common/<iApp folder>/<resource>). Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: iApp generated configuration (Microsoft Exchange, Citrix, or VMware View). Import / export of profile/policy.
bugs.impact: Cannot import / export iApp-generated Access Policies to / from another BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: No workaround, although Policy Sync might help with configuration migration / synchronization.
bugs.fix: iApp-generated Access Policies can now be imported from or exported to another BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: HTTP monitors with long send or receive strings may not save or update
bugs.symptoms: HTTP monitors with long send or receive strings may not save or update. When you attempt to save or update an affected monitor configuration, a warning message similar to the following example appears on the Configuration utility screen: Some Fields below contain errors. Correct them before continuing. Value may not contain literal newline characters.
bugs.conditions: You use a Google Chrome or Safari web browser. You attempt to configure a long send or receive string that contains word wraps within the text box of the Configuration utility.
bugs.impact: You are unable to create or update affected HTTP monitors using the Configuration utility.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can use the Internet Explorer or Firefox browser. Alternatively, you may use the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) to create the HTTP monitor.

bugs.title: LCD listener error during shutdown
bugs.symptoms: During shutdown you see this error message: 012a0004:4: LCD listener write to LCDd exception: Psuedo Terminal: File I/O Error [Bad file descriptor] at PseudoTermDev.cpp:93
bugs.conditions: This can occur when shutting down a blade on a VIPRION 4400 platform.
bugs.impact: This occurs on shutdown and is cosmetic, and can be ignored.
bugs.fix: The system now detects and handles the interruption during shutdown, to exit cleanly without error messages.

bugs.title: No support for multi-valued attributes inside SAML assertion.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system acts as a SAML IdP, you cannot create the assertion with multi-valued attributes. When the BIG-IP system acts as a SAML SP and there is a multi-valued attribute inside the assertion, then the BIG-IP system processes only the first value of that multi-valued attribute.
bugs.conditions: Administrator attempts to configure SAML multi-valued attribute.
bugs.impact: End user might not be able to access the SP service Or he might end up getting partial service depending on how the SP is configured.
bugs.fix: APM now supports multi-valued SAML attributes inside a SAML assertion.

bugs.title: Message: err chmand[5011]: 012a0003:3: Physical disk CF1/HD1 not found for logical disk delete
bugs.symptoms: On a VIPRION system during failover in which the blade transitioning from secondary to primary, log messages make it appear that chmand is looking to delete logical disks on CF1 and HD1.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on VIPRION systems.
bugs.impact: The ltm log displays messages: -- err chmand[6909]: 012a0003:3: Physical disk CF1 not found for logical disk delete'. -- err chmand[6909]: 012a0003:3: Physical disk HD1 not found for logical disk delete'.
bugs.workaround: None. These messages are benign and you can safely ignore them.

bugs.title: qpdf cores when processing a document with no pages
bugs.symptoms: When linearizing a PDF, qpdf cores when processing a document with no pages.
bugs.conditions: This likely occurs when the PDF contains no content, or invalid content.
bugs.impact: The qpdf process attempts to refer to the first page without checking whether it exists, and produces a Segfault and core file when the file has no first page.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no formal workaround, the core is small and happens infrequently, in most cases, so you can safely ignore it, unless it is happening so frequently and impacts performance. As long as the PDF contains valid content, linearization works as expected. If the content is invalid and qpdf cores, the system serves the original PDF.
bugs.fix: When linearizing a PDF, qpdf no longer cores when processing a document with no pages.

bugs.title: Parameter Value Substitution in Assembly cannot handle '&' in a link within an HTML doc.
bugs.symptoms: Assembly parameter substitution option Query Parameter target does not recognize escaped XML entities. If the URL to be substituted has multiple query parameters, the parameters that follow the '&' may not work as expected. For example, if the URL to be substituted has a pattern of field1=x&field2=y, substitution works for both fields. However, if the URL is field1=x&field2=y, substitution works for the 'field1' parameter, but does not work for the 'field2' parameter.
bugs.conditions: Using '&' in a link within an HTML doc.
bugs.impact: Parameter Value Substitution does not work.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, include the escape sequence as part of the Query Parameter Name. In the example, a Query Parameter of 'field1=x&&field2' yields the expected substitution.

bugs.title: VADC: Virtual Servers are not accessible through VLAN without any interface.
bugs.symptoms: On Virtual Edition (VE), if a VLAN was created without any assigned interface, then it will get 00:98:76:54:32:10 MAC address. This address is not functional for accessing any virtual server via such VLAN.
bugs.conditions: The issue is VE-specific due to vmw-compat VLAN MAC assignment policy.
bugs.impact: This behavior is different from BIG-IP v11.0.0 (and earlier) where VLANs without any interface had MAC address 00:00:00:00:00:00. The 00:98:76:54:32:10 MAC address is not functional for accessing any virtual server via such VLAN.
bugs.workaround: Possible workarounds: 1. Attach/detach an interface. 2. Manually assign 00:00:00:00:00:00 to VLAN (e.g., by using the ip command).

bugs.title: IP ToS not passing through with SIP LB
bugs.symptoms: Egress flow doesn't show the ToS bit even though ingress flow has ToS bit set.
bugs.conditions: Non zero ToS value in the ingress flow
bugs.impact: Ingress flow ToS value is not propagated to egress flow
bugs.workaround: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { set client_tos [IP::tos] } when SERVER_CONNECTED { IP::tos $client_tos }
bugs.fix: Propagate the ToS bit from ingress flow to the egress flow.

bugs.title: Allowing tilde in HTTP Profile fields Response Headers Allowed and Encrypt Cookies
bugs.symptoms: You will be unable to use the tilde (~) character in the fields Response Headers Allowed and Encrypt Cookies when using the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use the tilde character in HTTP Profile fields Response Headers Allowed and Encrypt Cookies in HTTP Profiles.
bugs.impact: The GUI errors out with an error: Bad Characters. Only the following special characters are allowed: period, dash and underscore (.-_). Multiple arguments should be separated by spaces."
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create/update HTTP Profile fields Response Headers Allowed and Encrypt Cookies that need a tilde character.
bugs.fix: The tilde character can now be used in HTTP Profile fields Response Headers Allowed and Encrypt Cookies.

bugs.title: System does not report tmm memory with consideration of threading
bugs.symptoms: Using the command 'tmsh show sys memory' may display zero usage for some entries.
bugs.conditions: This applies when using a platform that provides memory management per-process; this is all current hardware platforms, but does not apply to VCMP or VE.
bugs.impact: The division of memory usage may not be clear.
bugs.workaround: None. However, the information shows the most important value, which is the memory utilization of each process.

bugs.title: FastL4 tcp handshake timeout is not honored, connection lives for idle timeout.
bugs.symptoms: When FastL4 performs hardware acceleration at TCP handshake, FastL4 handshake timeout is not honored.
bugs.conditions: When FastL4 performs hardware acceleration at SYN time, once a flow is offloaded to hardware, the flow switches to using idle timeout instead of standard established timeout.
bugs.impact: FastL4 tcp handshake timeout is not honored, connection lives for idle timeout.
bugs.fix: FastL4 no longer switches to idle timeout before data is received, so the 5-second TCP handshake timeout holds until the first data arrives, at which time it switches to idle timeout.

bugs.title: Configured flow control not applied to Copper SFPs
bugs.symptoms: On affected platforms, flow control configured for an external interface is not applied if the interface is populated with a Copper SFP. The 'tmsh list net interface' command may show the 'Flow Control' setting for the interface as the configured value (such as 'tx-rx'). However, the 'tmsh show net interface' command may show the 'Flow Control' setting for the interface as 'none', and the remote node connected to the interface in question may show no flow control on the connection.
bugs.conditions: This may occur with interfaces populated with Copper SFPs on the following BIG-IP and VIPRION platforms: -- BIG-IP 10000-/12000-series appliances -- VIPRION B4300-series blades -- VIPRION B2250 blades
bugs.impact: No flow control as configured on affected interfaces.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Set flow control to none for the affected interfaces. 2. Set flow control to the desired value for the affected interfaces.

bugs.title: The fields displayed in the 'tmsh show net ipsec' should be visible through SNMP
bugs.symptoms: The status information about traffic selectors in IPsec can be displayed with the TMSH command 'show net ipsec', but there is no way to manage the BIG-IP system and gather data using SNMP.
bugs.conditions: Using SNMP to query the BIG-IP system for IPsec traffic selector status.
bugs.impact: Use TMSH or customized SNMP solutions.
bugs.workaround: None. ★ This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Networks Technical Support web site: http://www.f5.com/support/ The AskF5 web site: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/home The F5 DevCentral web site: http://devcentral.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Wed Jul 25 14:20:34 2018 EDT Copyright F5 Networks (2018) - All Rights Reserved Contact Support
bugs.fix: The IPsec SPD stat table has been added to the F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM MIB.

bugs.title: APM Network Accces tunnel slows down and loses data in secure renegotiation on Linux and Mac clients
bugs.symptoms: VPN connection on Linux and Mac clients can slow down and may loose some packets while performing secure re-negotiation on TLS or DTLS Network Access tunnel.
bugs.conditions: Secure re-negotiation configured on APM virtual server.
bugs.impact: Users can experience disconnects or traffic loss on APM Network Access connection.
bugs.fix: APM clients for Linux and Mac modified to perform better during secure re-negotiation.

bugs.title: Application icons (Finder, Spotlight, Launchpad, Notification Center, Dock, Menu Bar) have been updated for retina displays.
Web UI: Error when accessing PEM->Policy page by a non-admin(operator/firewall manager) user.
bugs.symptoms: A non-admin user(operator/firewall manager) can not access PEM GUI pages. Even the error which is shown is not meaningful to the user.
bugs.conditions: A non-admin user(operator/firewall manager) trying to access PEM GUI pages.
bugs.impact: A non-admin user(operator/firewall manager) can not access/configure PEM options from GUI.
bugs.workaround: None. Operators and firewall managers do not have a meaningful role in PEM.

bugs.title: PEM Data plane listeners when created with cmp-hash not equal to src-ip may break PEM functionality
bugs.symptoms: Subscriber lookup failures.
bugs.conditions: PEM Data plane listeners configured with cmp-hash not set to src-ip.
bugs.impact: Potential breakage in PEM functionality.
bugs.workaround: Change the VLAN cmp-hash to src-ip.
bugs.fix: At the PEM data plane listener page, only VLANs with src-ip or dst-ip hash can be chosen.

bugs.title: Proxy.pac file larger than 32 KB is not supported
bugs.symptoms: Proxy.pac file larger than 32 KB is not downloaded and edge client may fail to provide network access.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM, MAC Edge Client, network access, proxy.pac URL pointing to the file greater than 32 KB.
bugs.impact: User might not be able to access internal resources and Edge Client might go into connect/disconnect loop.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac now supports Proxy.pac file size of up to 1 MB; previously, the limit was 32KB.

bugs.title: Standby system offers option to Apply Access Policy even though it has been synced
bugs.symptoms: After syncing an access policy from the active system to the standby, the standby system will still prompt you to apply the access policy, even though it is in sync with the primary
bugs.conditions: Device group configured and an access policy is synced from the active device to the standby device(s).
bugs.impact: The message is erroneous on the standby, as the policy was already synced.
bugs.workaround: The standby device will no longer prompt to sync the access policy if it has already been synced from the active device.

bugs.title: State mirroring within eight-blade VIPRION 4800 chassis
bugs.symptoms: State mirroring within the eight-blade VIPRION 4800 chassis is not supported for this release. To workaround this, mirror between two separate chassis.
bugs.conditions: State mirroring within eight-blade VIPRION 4800 chassis
bugs.impact: Although this is not supported, you might see intermittent successful mirroring attempts when configured.
bugs.workaround: Mirror between two separate chassis.

bugs.title: Rule modifications reset active counters.
bugs.symptoms: When an existing rule is modified or when it transitions from active to inactive due to scheduling, the associated hit counters are reset.
bugs.conditions: An exiting rule is modified or changes state from active to inactive (or vice versa) due to scheduling.
bugs.impact: Rule hit counters are reset and accurate hit counts across scheduling intervals/modifications are not possible.

bugs.title: Java app-tunnel freezes in the Initializing state after clicking Allow Once using IE
bugs.symptoms: This is a rare issue that happens for Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) when pop-up screens are set to be blocked by browser. When you launch a Java app-tunnel for the first time in Internet Explorer, the message 'Allow pop-ups for this site?' is displayed. In rare cases, when you click Allow once, the Java app-tunnel freezes in the Initializing state and cannot be used.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the IE browser. -- Launch a Java app-tunnel. -- In response to the 'Allow pop-ups for this site?' message, click Allow Once.
bugs.impact: Java app-tunnel freezes in the Initializing state and cannot be used.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, add a virtual server to the allowed sites for pop-ups from Tools :: Internet options in Internet Explorer.

bugs.title: The imish utility cores while checking help strings for OSPF6 vertex-threshold
bugs.symptoms: The imish (vtysh) utility dumps core while checking help strings for the OSPF6 vertex-threshold command from OSPF mode.
bugs.conditions: -- Routing enabled. -- Configuring OSPF vertex-threshold for either IPv4 or IPv6. -- Requesting help for the OSPF6 vertex-threshold command.
bugs.impact: There is an imish (vtysh) crash.
bugs.fix: Updated with the proper help strings for the OSPF6 vertex-threshold command.

bugs.title: NTLM Auth does not work if FQDN to domain controller is set to a invalid domain controller
bugs.symptoms: If you enter a bad FQDN for domain controller in an NTLM Auth configuration and a DNS server responds with DNS SERVFAIL, the NTLM Auth configuration does not work even after you fix the incorrect FQDN.
bugs.conditions: NTLM auth configured in APM Invalid domain controller specified, or the domain controller goes down.
bugs.impact: NTLM auth will stop working.
bugs.workaround: To work around this problem, after you correct the FQDN in the NTLM Auth configuration, restart the ECA plugin and NLAD daemon using this command: bigstart restart nlad. Note: To avoid future problems due to misconfigurations, you can configure your DNS server to return a negative response.

bugs.title: OpenSSL certificate directories excluded in qkview/ihealth.
bugs.symptoms: When examining qkview captured files, all the certificates are excluded.
bugs.conditions: A normal qkview uploaded to iHealth does not show any certificates.
bugs.impact: Cannot view the certificates to determine whether there are related issues. If the qkview contains an OpenSSL key file in a directory that gets captured, the key file might be exposed in the iHealth (qkview) output.
