bugs.workaround: Certificates must be transferred manually or examined on the BIG-IP system directly.
bugs.fix: Certificates are now included. All OpenSSL key files are excluded, regardless of location. Also, the certificate files are searched for included private keys.
bugs.behavior: OpenSSL Certificate directories are now included in qkview. OpenSSL Keys are excluded, no matter where they are placed.

bugs.title: Using the restart cm trust-domain command to recreate certificates required by device trust.
bugs.symptoms: The device trust manages the certificates and keys SSL connections require between devices used for configuration synchronization. You should always have the necessary certificates and keys. If they are not present, device trust fails.
bugs.conditions: This might occur after manually removing the 'cm' stanzas from the config file, and reloading the configuration.
bugs.impact: No certificates and keys exist. If there are no certificates and keys, device trust cannot be set up, and the system cannot complete the SSL connections necessary for config synchronization.
bugs.workaround: To recreate the certs and keys, run the command: restart cm trust-domain.
bugs.fix: This release contains a new tmsh command 'restart cm trust-domain' to restart device trust in this circumstances.

bugs.title: TCP Half Open monitors sourced from specific source ports can fail
bugs.symptoms: TCP Half Open monitors; when sourced from ports 1097 (except on some platforms), 1098, 1099, and 3306; will fail. Upon receipt of SYN-ACK from the monitored device, TMOS will filter the packet and respond with ICMP port unreachable.
bugs.conditions: Use one or more TCP Half Open monitors. Port 1097 will not be affected on the BIG-IP 800, 1600, 3600, 3900, 6900, 8900 (and derivative), 11000, or 11050 platforms.
bugs.impact: May result in false monitor failures.
bugs.workaround: 1. Use a monitor type other than TCP Half Open. 2. Modify iptables by removing the relevant iptable rules. For all platforms: -- /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 3306 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable. -- /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 3306 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset. -- /sbin/iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 3306 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset. Then, for platforms where port 1097 is affected: -- /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 1097:1099 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable -- /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 1097:1099 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset -- /sbin/iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 1097:1099 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset Or for platforms where port 1097 is not affected: -- /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 1098:1099 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable -- /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 1098:1099 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset -- /sbin/iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 1098:1099 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset
bugs.fix: TCP Half Open monitors sourced from certain ports now handle traffic as expected.

bugs.title: APM Logout page is not protected against CSRF attack.
bugs.symptoms: Users with active APM session could be tricked into logging out from the BIG-IP system by visiting attacker's website and clicking on a link which would perform CSRF against APM logout page.
bugs.conditions: An attacker can create a link to BIG-IP system's logout page on an external malicious web-site. Alternatively, such links could be sent to user via email. If a user is tricked into clicking this link, the user's BIG-IP APM session will be terminated.
bugs.impact: APM session could be terminated by an attacker.
bugs.fix: A new configuration db variable, Tmm.Access.LogoutUrlRefererHeaderCheck was added to perform a Referer header check on all requests to APM logout page. The new db variable is disabled by default. Enabling this variable will cause a Referer header check to be performed for all requests that attempt to terminate an APM session. Use caution when enabling this db variable because it may affect logout functionality in some cases. Specifically, any custom iRules used to redirect users to logout URLs may not function properly. In addition, SAML single logout (although terminating a user's session) may reset the browser connection under certain conditions when the db variable is enabled.

bugs.title: If the OSPF derived MTU is different from the path MTU, OSPF may not function as expected
bugs.symptoms: If the maximum transmission unit (MTU) for a network running OSPF is different from ZebOS, or if its neighbor router has configured for its interface MTU, OSPF adjacencies may not form, or some datagrams may be rejected.
bugs.conditions: TMM has cached a reduced path MTU for a network that is smaller than the configured MTU of the interface. OSPF running on that interface.
bugs.impact: OSPF adjacencies never fully form and routes are not exchanged.
bugs.workaround: Restarting TMM clears the cached maximum transmission unit (MTU), and allowing all interface MTUs to function with default values should prevent a mismatch.
bugs.fix: OSPF traffic is no longer subject to cached route MTUs and will not be obstructed by route metrics with MTUs smaller than the interface MTU.

bugs.title: Host-originated traffic cannot use a nexthop in a different route domain
bugs.symptoms: If a route uses a nexthop in a different route domain, traffic originating from the host will not be forwarded to that nexthop.
bugs.conditions: Multiple route domains, gateway route that matches traffic using a nexthop in a different route domain.
bugs.impact: Nodes reached by the route cannot be monitored.
bugs.fix: Host-originated traffic can now use a nexthop in a different route domain.

bugs.title: Installing a hotfix may cause APD to continuously restart
bugs.symptoms: If you install a hotfix ISO over an existing installation that has APM provisioned, APD continuously restarts.
bugs.conditions: Install a hotfix ISO over an existing installation that has APM provisioned.
bugs.impact: APD continuously restarts.
bugs.workaround: To install this hotfix, type these commands: # tmsh delete sys software volume <target volume> # tmsh install sys software hotfix Hotfix-BIGIP-<your hotfix version>.iso volume <target volume> create-volume

bugs.title: Office on Mac cannot open SharePoint files through web applications
bugs.symptoms: Office for Mac 2011 gets login page html instead of document when "open in Office" used SharePoint.
bugs.conditions: Cannot open Office document using SharePoint.
bugs.impact: Not able to view the document from Portal Access.

bugs.title: Client side checks on Windows Phone 8
bugs.symptoms: Client side checks, such as antivirus, firewall, file, process, and so on, should be skipped for Microsoft Windows Phone 8, but are not skipped.
bugs.conditions: Access Profiled configured to use client side checks. Windows Phone 8 clients attempt to establish connection
bugs.impact: Windows Phone 8 users are prompted to install client components, but they cannot.
bugs.fix: Client side checks, such as antivirus, firewall, file, process, and so on, will be skipped for Microsoft Windows Phone 8.

bugs.title: New APIs for iControl SOAP Trust management
bugs.symptoms: iControl SOAP APIs do not include interfaces for getting the members of the trust, so you cannot retrieve the authority and non-authority devices that belong to the trust.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl APIs.
bugs.impact: Cannot retrieve authority and non-authority devices that belong to the trust.
bugs.fix: This release adds two interfaces to Management/Trust iControl SOAP to retrieve the authority and non-authority devices that are part of the trust. The methods are called get_non_authority_device and get_authority_device.
bugs.behavior: This release adds two interfaces to Management/Trust iControl SOAP to retrieve the authority and non-authority devices that are part of the trust. The methods are called get_non_authority_device and get_authority_device.

bugs.title: PSM - SMTP 500 error when HELO message is fragmented
bugs.symptoms: False positive SMTP blocking
bugs.conditions: The SMTP HELO message arrives in more than one TCP packet
bugs.impact: A false positive blocking, 500 error message.

bugs.title: After deleting a partition object, "01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid mcpd context, folder not found ([folder name])" error is generated on ltm log file.
bugs.symptoms: After GUI session timeout (i.e., exceeded "auth-pam-idle-timeout" value) and user is automatically logged out, while clicking "Log in" button to re-login to GUI, the following error message may be shown with "Continue" button. ---------- This BIG-IP system has encountered a configuration problem that may prevent the Configuration utility from functioning properly. To prevent adverse effects on the system, F5 recommends that you restrict your use of the Configuration utility to critical tasks only until the problem is resolved. Beware that attempting to modify your configuration in this state with the Configuration utility may cause your configuration to be overwritten. ---------- When this problem happens, error messages will be recorded on log files, too. /// ltm log /// 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid mcpd context, folder not found ([folder name]). /// tomcat/catalina.out, webui.log /// login.index_jsp:error - java.sql.SQLException: General error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid mcpd context, folder not found ([folder name]) in statement [SELECT SINGLE * FROM ltcfg_instance_field WHERE container = '' AND instance_name = '/Common/system' AND class_name = 'system' AND field_name = 'hostname'] User can re-login to GUI by pressing "Continue" button although GUI error and logs indicates something critical happened.
bugs.conditions: - A GUI session expired while you were logged in and referencing to specific partition object (i.e., changed partition at upper right corner on GUI). - The partition object, which was referred before GUI session expired, has been deleted.
bugs.impact: A GUI warning message is generated while trying to re-login to GUI. Configuration error messages were also recorded on log files.
bugs.workaround: Press "Continue" button and retry logging in to GUI, and after then try switching partition between "Common" and "All [Read Only]" at upper right corner on GUI. Alternatively, restart tomcat service by "tmsh restart /sys service tomcat" and refresh GUI session.

bugs.title: Cache::Header content-length Returns Zero when Response Status is 304
bugs.symptoms: The Cache::Header content-length returns zero.
bugs.conditions: A 304 response.
bugs.impact: Inside an iRule, CACHE::header content-length is null on 304 responses, and CACHE::header exists content-length will be False.
bugs.workaround: The Content-Length header may not be present at all in the response, and it is inappropriate to add a content-length header to a 304 response that is not zero. Optionally, the X-Cntnt-Length header value can be used, if you want to get the length of the cached document from a 304 response. In short, the CACHE::header commands give access to the response headers, not the cached headers.

bugs.title: The iRule node command does not function as expected when invoked from the LB_SELECTED event.
bugs.symptoms: The iRule node command does not function properly when invoked from the LB_SELECTED event.
bugs.conditions: Using an iRule in which the 'node' command in the LB_SELECTED event modifies the node or port.
bugs.impact: Although logs from the iRule may indicate the node and/or port was modified, the changes are not applied, as a subsequent tcpdump confirms.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to use node under LB_SELECTED if it is paired with LB::reselect. If port is changed in the node command, the configuration with port-translation is required. A load balancing decision can also be changed under other events, for example CLIENT_ACCEPTED.

bugs.title: Some Java applications do not work through BIG-IP server
bugs.symptoms: Some Java applications do not work through the BIG-IP server.
bugs.impact: Users are unable to use some web applications that use Java applets.
bugs.fix: Fixed bug that resulted in incorrect loading of Java applets (Java applications).

bugs.title: CGNAT hairpinning is not supported for NAT64
bugs.symptoms: Hairpin connections are not supported for NAT64.
bugs.conditions: -- lsnpool with NAT64. -- Hairpinning enabled.
bugs.impact: Hairpinned connections do not work
bugs.workaround: Hairpin via upstream router.
bugs.fix: Hairpin connections are now supported for NAT64.
bugs.behavior: Hairpin connections are now supported for NAT64.

bugs.title: ArcSight HSL is not supported for most system daemons
bugs.symptoms: If a HSL configuration is defined that tries to publish logs from core system daemons (chmand, TMM, fpdd, merged, etc.) to an ArcSight destination, this will not work properly, and instead, all log messages at debug level and higher (from that daemon) will be captured in the local system log files. For instance, configuring a wide-open filter that captures all traffic, such as the following, will result in many core daemons logging debug logs to /var/log/ltm on the BIG-IP system: sys log-config filter remote-log-filter { publisher publisher } sys log-config publisher publisher { destinations { arcsight { } } } sys log-config destination remote-high-speed-log hsl { pool-name pool_arcsight } sys log-config destination arcsight arcsight { forward-to hsl }
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a high-speed logger is configured with the ArcSight remote log servers as the destination.
bugs.impact: As a result of this, the system will log excessively to the local log files.
bugs.workaround: Only configure log filters that publish logs to ArcSight for supported (AFM, ASM, and SWG) components.

bugs.title: OnDemand cert auth redirect omits port information
bugs.symptoms: On-Demand Cert Auth redirect does not honor a port other than 443 in virtual server.
bugs.conditions: On-Demand Cert Auth is used in an access policy that's assigned to a virtual server with non-standard port.
bugs.impact: The redirect URL is missing the port information, hence subsequent client connections aren't successful.
bugs.fix: On Demand Cert Auth support for non standard port has been added to include the port information from VS as part of redirect URL.

bugs.title: https/ssl monitor closes immediately (rather than awaiting remote close-notify)
bugs.symptoms: SSL-based monitors (such as https) continue to maintain an open connection for up to ~15 seconds after the monitor probe is completed, when connecting to an SSL enabled web server that fails to send close-notify before FIN.
bugs.conditions: Configuration uses SSL-based monitors (such as https), where your SSL enabled web server fails to send close-notify before FIN.
bugs.impact: SSL-enabled monitors wait ~15 seconds before closing the connection and reclaiming resources. Although this behavior is correct according to the SSL protocol, it has the potential to introduce a limited amount of connection stacking on the monitored host.
bugs.workaround: Your SSL enabled web server should send close-notify before FIN for SSL-based monitors to close immediately.
bugs.fix: Previous behavior for an SSL-based monitor (such as https) sent a shutdown notification to the remote-server, and awaited a close-reply (shutdown acknowledgement) response for up to 15 seconds. When an SSL-enabled web server fails to send close-notify, the SSL-based monitor hangs in CLOSE_WAIT for ~15 seconds before sending FIN and closing the connection. This waiting consumes resources that are unavailable for other monitoring, which is observed to be significant on certain configurations with high https monitor loads. New behavior is to close the connection immediately after sending shutdown notification to the remote server, and not await a shutdown acknowledgement.

bugs.title: Linux client hangs after receiving the application data
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receiver for Linux hangs when connecting to APM configured as Citrix WI replacement.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix WI replacement mode and Citrix Receiver for Linux is used.
bugs.impact: Unable to use Citrix Receiver for Linux.
bugs.fix: Now APM correctly handles connections from Citrix Receiver for Linux.

bugs.title: HSBe2 falls off the PCI bus
bugs.symptoms: While restarting the host tmm on a VCMP capable platform, an HSB on one of the blades stops responding and cannot be found, causing all tmms on the blade to fail to pass traffic. A large packet burst may be observed when this happens. Restarting the blade will clear the condition.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this condition. It was observed on BIG-IP 10000 and 12000 platforms, as well as B4300 blades. This is an intermittent issue that was seen rarely, restarting the host tmm seemed to trigger it more frequently.
bugs.impact: Traffic is interrupted, tmms non responsive on the blade or VCMP instance with the affected HSBe2
bugs.fix: Fixed a lockup issue with HSBe2

bugs.title: sys db tmrouted.rhifailoverdelay does not seem to work
bugs.symptoms: The problem is that the sys db tmrouted.rhifailoverdelay value <value> does not seem to take any effect, and the route is being withdrawn, sometimes before the newly active device is able to advertise the virtual address, leaving a blackhole route.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during a failover.
bugs.impact: Temporary black hole for a route.
bugs.fix: Fixed tmrouted to not bypass rhifailoverdelay during op-state change.

bugs.title: Changing the provision.tmmcount db variable value results in continuous tmm restarts
bugs.symptoms: Changing the 'provision.tmmcount' db variable value results in continuous tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: Changing 'provision.tmmcount' db variable value.
bugs.impact: Continuous tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: After making a change to the number of TMMs (provision.tmmcount), save the configuration and reboot the system.

bugs.title: WAM/AAM does not inline content that is not already cached or served from OWS with status 200 OK.
bugs.symptoms: When configured to inline content, WAM/AAM does not inline content that is not already cached or served from OWS with status 200 OK.
bugs.conditions: When configured to inline content.
bugs.impact: WAM/AAM does not inline content.

bugs.title: New pool members take all requests until lb_value catches up.
bugs.symptoms: When a new pool member is added, the system assigns it a lb_value of 0, which causes new pool members to take all requests until the lb_values for all pool members are reset to accommodate the new member.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in a pool that uses predictive or observed load balancing modes, typically with a slow ramp time that is small or zero.
bugs.impact: When the pool member goes out of slow ramp before handling a connection, that pool member becomes the preferred pick for every request until its lb_value is reset in order with the other members.
bugs.workaround: Add the pool member disabled, and then enable it. If a member is added disabled and then enabled, the lb_values are correctly set, and the problem does not occur.
bugs.fix: The system now initializes lb_value to the minimum current lb_value for unused pool members. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: DHCP broadcast traffic will create a session if was processed on a PEM enabled UDP virtual
bugs.symptoms: If a PEM enabled UDP virtual (i.e., a virtual that has SPM profile) was hit by DHCP broadcasting traffic, then SPM will create a subscriber session for address 0.0.0.0
bugs.conditions: PEM enabled UDP virtual DHCP broadcast traffic on the network the virtual is listening on No virtual servers configured to handle the DHCP traffic
bugs.impact: Extra subscriber session(s) created that shouldn't be created.
bugs.workaround: Create a DHCP virtual that has subscriber discovery turned on. The subscriber discovery can be turned on via the DHCPv4 profile that is attached to the virtual. This way any DHCP broadcasting traffic should be handled by this virtual.

bugs.title: vCMP provisioning may cause continual tmm crash.
bugs.symptoms: vCMP provisioning may cause continual tmm crash. In rare cases, tmm cores when VCMP is provisioned/deprovisioned. The tmm log file presents messages similar to the following: panic: ../dev/cn1120/n3_compress.c:555: Assertion 'enough n3_comp_dev structs' failed.
bugs.conditions: 1) LTM is provisioned. 2) Provision vCMP. 3) View the tmm log file/system process table/etc.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: 1) Save the system configuration. 2) Reboot 3) After reboot, ensure that the device stays active and has only twoNitrox 3 Compression Devices listed in /var/log/tmm: -- notice n3-compress0 PASS 0.1: Nitrox 3 Compression Device -- notice n3-compress1 PASS 0.1: Nitrox 3 Compression Device
bugs.fix: The system now prevents the tmm from starting up in the case where vCMP is provisioned/deprovisioned. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system unreachable for IPv6 traffic via PCI pass-through interfaces as current ixgbevf drivers do not support multicast receive.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system is unreachable for IPv6 traffic via PCI pass-through interfaces, because current ixgbevf drivers do not support multicast receive.
bugs.conditions: When configured to see IPv6 traffic on a PCI pass-through interface, the BIG-IP guest is not able to see this traffic.
bugs.impact: PCI pass-through interfaces are unable to see IPv6 traffic.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP system is now reachable for IPv6 traffic via PCI pass-through interfaces as current ixgbevf drivers do not support multicast receive.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system may use an ephemeral source port when sending SNMP IPv6 UDP response.
bugs.symptoms: When SNMP IPv6 UDP queries are directed from client to self-ip, response from the BIG-IP system does not preserve source port. An ephemeral source port will be used, instead of the source port 161.
bugs.conditions: SNMP IPv6 UDP query only.
bugs.impact: SNMP query fails.
bugs.fix: A problem of SNMP IPv6 UDP response from the BIG-IP system with an ephemeral source port has been solved.

bugs.title: Pre-v11.x and 11.x GTM devices should not share the same sync group
bugs.symptoms: If the sync group is intact and you are doing a rolling upgrade of your sync group from pre-v11.x to v11.x, you will experience flapping of the monitored objects due to the two versions not fully understanding iQuery messages.
bugs.conditions: This occurs while upgrading systems in a device group, and one or more of the devices are running a version prior to 11.0.0
bugs.impact: Could cause flapping of object status.
bugs.workaround: Use live install on volumes to complete upgrades on each system and then switch over all systems to the new v11.x systems at the same time, essentially, eliminating a window where the sync group contains both v11.x and pre-v11.x systems.

bugs.title: Hosted Content connected object import issues
bugs.symptoms: If object of policy is linked with hosted content, import will fail unless similarly named object is not created on target box. The import error looks similar to the following: "Configuration error: Cannot find sandbox file (Common/hosted-content:loginNew.html_1361913754973) referred in resource webtop (/Common/Import-ChangeProperty) Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed."
bugs.conditions: This can occur if you are using Hosted Content and you are using Export/Import to copy an access policy from one APM to a new APM that does not have the Hosted Content files already on it.
bugs.impact: The import will fail on the new device.
bugs.workaround: Unlink objects from hosted content or replicate similar objects under similar names in hosted content first

bugs.title: Remote login shell hardening
bugs.symptoms: The expected behavior is for privilege roles such as admin, resource-admin, etc. to have capability for root access when required.
bugs.impact: Potential for local privilege escalation.
bugs.workaround: Restrict any users in the affected roles to GUI access, i.e. remoteconsoleaccess none.
bugs.fix: Console login now consistent with ssh.

bugs.title: ICMP messages can be throttled without log message
bugs.symptoms: When TM.MaxICMPRate is reached, TMM will drop ICMP requests. There is no visibility in logs when that happens.
bugs.conditions: Excessive ICMP traffic.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact but it is harder to troubleshoot such condition.
bugs.workaround: use TMM counters

bugs.title: qkview may generate error messages for very long file names
bugs.symptoms: File names that contain more than 100 characters in the full pathname cannot be added to qkview files. If such filenames are encountered by qkview, they will be discarded. This will be indicated in both the meta.xml file and the qkview_run.data file.
bugs.conditions: Filenames under paths collected by qkview exceed 100 characters in length.
bugs.impact: possible file containing useful diagnostic information is omitted.
bugs.workaround: Run qkview manually, and observe errors output to stderr. Copy these files manually to examine their contents.

bugs.title: Edge client continues to use old IP address even when server IP address changed
bugs.symptoms: Edge client goes in reconnect loop if the server it connected to went down and DNS assigned a new IP Address to server host name.
bugs.conditions: 1) Edge clients connected successfully to a server. 2) Server goes down and DNS resolves the server host name to a different IP address
bugs.impact: - Client goes in a reconnect loop and needs to be restarted to successfully connect to new IP address.
bugs.workaround: Restart Edge Client
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP Edge Client resolves the host name during reconnection and initiates full reconnection after an IP address change is detected.

bugs.title: MCPD can core as a result of another component shutting down prematurely
bugs.symptoms: During a small window of opportunity, mcpd can core if it is told to restart. This often occurs when another component has failed.
bugs.conditions: This issue generally occurs when another component has a problem which then initiates an mcpd restart.
bugs.impact: An mcpd core file is generated during shutdown, and it may initially appear as if mcpd coring was the cause of the restart.
bugs.fix: Ensured that the active device sync connection is destroyed when mcpd is shutting down.

bugs.title: vCMPD will not reattach to guest
bugs.symptoms: If a vcmp guest is deleted while vcmpd is not running (aka vcmpd has crashed and is coming back up), vcmpd will not reattach to that guest because mcpd never said it exists and as a result will never shut it down.
bugs.conditions: vCMPD deleted while vCMPD is not running
bugs.impact: Vcmpd should be changed to scan that directory at startup to check for any "lost" guests and kill them if necessary.
bugs.fix: On vcmpd startup, handle any guest deletions that happened while vcmpd wasn't running

bugs.title: Network Access session closed without warning
bugs.symptoms: A Network Access webtop does not show warning windows about session expiration. A full webtop does not show warnings intermittently.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on all clients logged in via Network Access
bugs.impact: When sessions expire, they are closed without prompting or warning.

bugs.title: Thales HSM support on Chassis cluster-mode.
bugs.symptoms: Unable to correctly install and use Thales network-HSM in cluster-mode on BIG-IP chassis such as VIPRION.
bugs.conditions: Use Thales Network-HSM with BIG-IP chassis systems such as VIPRION in cluster mode.
bugs.impact: Unable to use Thales HSM with BIG-IP chassis system cluster-mode.
bugs.workaround: Follow manual install procedures for Thales install on each slot.
bugs.fix: Thales HSM install now needs to be done only on the primary slot on the BIG-IP cluster-mode chassis systems such as VIPRION. A single install on primary slot will take care of installing Thales on all active slots. On any already-open sessions to the BIG-IP slot(s), the PATH environment variable will need to be reloaded by executing 'source ~/.bash_profile' in order to be able to use Thales utilities. If at a later stage, a new blade is added or a disabled or powered-off blade is made active or is powered-on, the user will have to run 'thales-sync.sh -v' *only* on the new secondary slot. If the new slot is made primary before running thales-sync.sh on it, then the regular install procedure using nethsm-thales-install.sh will be required on the new primary slot.

bugs.title: Error: 'err chmand[8873]: Error sending MCP system_information (err:1020003)
bugs.symptoms: Upon shutdown, the system posts the message 'err chmand[8873]: Error sending MCP system_information (err:1020003)’ to the ltm log.
bugs.conditions: This might occur intermittently when shutting down the system.
bugs.impact: This message is benign, and the system should power up correctly.

bugs.title: Key install or deletion failure on FIPS key names longer than 32 chars on some platforms
bugs.symptoms: Key operations might not succeed as expected when the key names are longer than 32 characters.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with keynames longer than 32 characters on the 6900 (D104), 8900 (D106), 8950 (D107), 11999 (E101), 11050 (E102), 10000/10050/10200/10250 (D113) platforms.
bugs.impact: FIPS key install and key deletion might fail. Deletion of the FIPS key with a keyname longer than 32 characters deletes the key from the BIG-IP configuration but does not delete the key from the FIPS card. Similarly, importing a key with keyname longer than 32 characters into the FIPS card fails.
bugs.workaround: Use keynames of a maximum of 32-characters for FIPS keys.
bugs.fix: FIPS key labels longer than 32 characters now get truncated to 32 characters. Those keys with the same first 32 characters are truncated, and the system attaches an underscore and number to a total of 32 characters; for example fipssamplekeylabelof32characte_1, fipssamplekeylabelof32characte_2, and so on. BIG-IP uses the FIPS handles when querying the FIPS cards for keys, so the fact that the FIPS key labels are different from the BIG-IP key names does not matter and does not affect traffic.

bugs.title: APM does not restore NLAD connections when the configuration is restored from an UCS file
bugs.symptoms: After the upgrade, if the previous configuration used NTLM front end authentication, the functionality is not restored.
bugs.conditions: NTLM configured and UCS file is saved prior to restoring a dive to factory defaults. tmsh load sys config default is run to restore the system to the default state
bugs.impact: NTLM auth will not work, and this error will appear in /var/log/apm: err nlad[6921]: 01620000:3: <0x55b5db90> nlclnt[3c80a0a0a] init: Error [0xc000006d,NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE] connecting to DC
bugs.workaround: After the upgrade, manually delete the existing NTLM machine account configurations and then recreate them.

bugs.title: BIG-IP LTM Log Indicates Chassis Power Turned Off During Fan Speed Failures
bugs.symptoms: If a power supply fan unit becomes jammed or experiences a failure that prohibits the minimum RPM threshold to be met, the LTM log will erroneously indicate that the power supply has been turned off. For example: localhost crit chmand[8482]: 012a0013:2: Blade 0 hardware sensor critical alarm: Power Supply 2 GPIO status(73-610-125): Bad localhost crit chmand[8482]: 012a0013:2: Blade 0 hardware sensor critical alarm: Power supply #2 fan-1: Bad localhost warning chmand[8482]: 012a0018:4: Chassis power module 2 turned off.
bugs.conditions: Any kind of power supply fan failure that prevents the unit from achieving the minimum spec. for RPMs.
bugs.impact: Misleading log message.

bugs.title: APM - when Edge Clients, some JS contents are different causing warning
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent JS Error in sesstimeout.js during access to full webtop by Edge Clients.
bugs.conditions: -- At least two different Edge Clients with User Agent strings based on Internet Explorer version 11 (IE11). -- A version of IE earlier that IE11 is used to access full webtop resource.
bugs.impact: If 'Display notification about all script errors' is enabled in IE (Internet Options :: Advanced tab) IE displays JS error messages. One client might encounter a JS Syntax error, depending on TMM count and APM RAMCACHE content. Note: There is no impact on product functionality, because Edge Clients do not call JS code from sesstimeout.js. The error is cosmetic only and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: Special APM resource assignment branch for standalone Edge Clients can be configured in VPE to access 'webtop-type network', (NA_only_webtop resource does not include /vdesk/sesstimeout.js and /vdesk/hometab.js).
bugs.fix: A javascript error no longer is intermittently displayed during a Network Access VPN session from the APM Full Webtop.

bugs.title: Hardware data display inaccuracies
bugs.symptoms: Sensor location fields show truncated. The Part Number and the PCA titles appear to be not right for some platforms because of the specific nature of the titles.
bugs.conditions: When displaying the hardware details you could see the problems in the sensor data and in the Hardware Version Information. This appears when running the command tmsh show sys hardware
bugs.impact: Missing sensor location data, and inaccuracy when naming the titles of the hardware characteristics.
bugs.fix: Fixed the truncation problem for the sensor location increasing the size of the data used for retrieving it; and used Part Number and PCA to have generic titles that apply to all platforms.

bugs.title: iControl SOAP returns get_ff_present error
bugs.symptoms: In /var/log/ltm, you notice the following error: err iControlPortal.cgi[3811]: 01180009:3: get_ff_present feature flag 313 out of range.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on certain hotfixes, such as 11.3.0 HF1 through HF4, and 12.1.1 HF2 for certain feature flags. It is triggered when running the iControl command SystemInfo.get_product_info
bugs.impact: Error is returned by iControl when it is unable to recognize a feature flag.

bugs.title: Update/overwrite of FIPS keys error
bugs.symptoms: After deleting and re-creating a FIPS key, sync to other devices fails and /var/log/ltm gives the following error: crit tmm[10817]: 01260010:2: FIPS acceleration device failure: fips_poll_completed_reqs: req: 78 status: 0x40000116 : ERR_HSM_ERROR Note that this error is logged on any FIPS-related error, it might be this issue if you were attempting to replace FIPS keys with an identical name on devices in a device group.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on FIPS-enabled devices in a device group when a FIPS key is deleted and an identically-named FIPS key is added.
bugs.impact: Sync of the FIPS key fails.
bugs.workaround: If you are encountering this, you can do the following workaround. Impact of workaround: this should have no negative impact to the system since your objective is to replace the FIPS keys. - Detach all keys/certs from all SSL Profiles and delete all keys via script on the standby System - Run “tmsh show sys crypto fips” and verify all keys have been deleted - Run a configsync with override and verify the sync has been carried out successfully.

bugs.title: Stream filter cannot match literal (
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to match a literal ( (open parenthesis) in the stream filter.
bugs.conditions: Stream filter enabled. Stream expression includes a ( not intended as the opening of a regex group.
bugs.impact: Unable to directly match expression that contains a literal (.
bugs.workaround: Use octal character encoding to resolve stream filter conflicts, as shown in this example: ( = \050 ) = \051 so instead of the expression: function\(param1\), use the expression: function\050param1\051.

bugs.title: vCMP guest unit_key empty
bugs.symptoms: A vCMP guest fails to load, and mcpd crashes on start-up. Running 'tmsh list vcmp guest' on the host reveals that sym-unit-key is empty or does not exist.
bugs.conditions: There are a number of ways that this can be encountered. The most common is an RMA replacement of a VCMP-capable blade, or when moving a ucs from one device to another device of the same type, if the device unit key becomes corrupted, or if the master key file (/config/bigip/kstore/master) becomes corrupted.
bugs.impact: Configuration of vCMP guest fails to load, mcpd crashes.
bugs.workaround: Remove the encrypted attributes from the config and reenter them in plaintext.

bugs.title: Deploying large firewall policy configuration changes can exhaust available memory on the BIG-IP device.
bugs.symptoms: Processing large configuration changes on an under-provisioned or overly-utilized BIG-IP device could result in memory and resource exhaustion. Errors will be reported on the BIG-IP device logs if this condition occurs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs while BIG-IP is deploying large firewall policy configuration changes.
bugs.impact: If resources are exhausted on the BIG-IP devices, users could experience traffic interruption on the BIG-IP device.
bugs.workaround: Check the memory and the performance of the BIG-IP system prior to deploying any large configuration change sets. This will help alleviate any performance or resource exhaustion issues that could occur when processing large configuration changes on a heavily-loaded BIG-IP device.

bugs.title: Do not restrict AD to be the last auth agent for View Client
bugs.symptoms: Previously we required that AD Auth agent to be the last authentication agent in the policy to make it work correctly with native VMware View client.
bugs.conditions: User's password got expired and user is requested to change it.
bugs.impact: User got error message even for successful password change.
bugs.fix: If used, the AD Auth agent no longer needs to be the last authentication agent in an access policy for VMware View. Now username, password, and domain from AD Auth are preserved and passed to the backend.

bugs.title: OpenSSL bug can prevent RSA keys from rolling forward
bugs.symptoms: When trying to upgrade from version 10.x to version 11.x, SSL keys can fail to roll forward. The roll-forward process does not handle what appears to be an OpenSSL bug (tested through OpenSSL 1.0.1c).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when rolling forward RSA keys from version 10.x to 11.x.
bugs.impact: Rather than receiving the expected decrypt failure unable to load Private Key with a bad decrypt, approximately 0.3% respond differently, where the return is non-zero and does not contain 'bad decrypt'. In this case, the system considers the key bad even though it is fine.
bugs.fix: All SSL keys from version 10.x can be loaded correctly using the UCS file.

bugs.title: Too many iso images in /shared/images causes swap
bugs.symptoms: Secondary blades in a cluster go into swap when there are too many iso images in /shared/images.
bugs.conditions: Too many iso images in /shared/images.
bugs.impact: Secondary blades are slow.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh or the GUI to delete as many iso images from /shared/images as feasible.

bugs.title: LTM policy fails to decompress compressed http requests
bugs.symptoms: Administrator configures LTM policy to decompress http request (so, for example, that ASM can check it). However compressed requests are not decompressed.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs always when there is a decompress action on an LTM policy.
bugs.impact: Requests and/or responses are not decompressed as desired.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be added to the virtual server to override policy setting. (DECOMPRESS::enable, DECOMPRESS::disable).
bugs.fix: A coding change has been made to cause LTM decompress action to work as expected.

bugs.title: Changing Master Key on the standby might cause secondaries to restart processes
bugs.symptoms: Changing Master Key on the standby of an HA configuration on a chassis might cause secondaries to restart processes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you modify the master key on standby chassis.
bugs.impact: Users might not be able to access the cluster. The secondary blades of that chassis might experience continuous restarts of mcpd and other daemons, accompanied by 'decrypt failure' messages in the ltm log.
bugs.workaround: Run the command bigstart restart on secondaries to return system functionality. In general, you should change master keys on the primary in the cluster.

bugs.title: HTTP is more efficient in buffering data
bugs.symptoms: Expiration of HTTP connections.
bugs.conditions: If many small packets are received, then the HTTP filter may buffer those packets inefficiently.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory usage for buffering data.
bugs.fix: HTTP is more efficient in buffering data so that HTTP connections do not get expired early.

bugs.title: Rare crash with vip-targeting-vip and stale connections on VIPRION platforms
bugs.symptoms: Rare TMM crash bug with vip-targeting-vip. Core analysis is typically necessary to determine whether this bug is the cause.
bugs.conditions: Triggering this bug is difficult and seems to require vip-targeting-vip (e.g., use of the 'virtual' command in an iRule) and more than one blade.
bugs.impact: In rare situations, the TMM crashes.
bugs.workaround: None. This occurs rarely, and the system recovers automatically. Although this workaround has not be verified, in situations where virtual A targets virtual B via the 'virtual' command, it should be sufficient for virtual A to have shorter timeouts than virtual B.

bugs.title: When switch edit files in advanced customization without saving, the changes will be lost
bugs.symptoms: When you switch from editing one file to editing another file in advanced customization without saving the first file, changes to the first file are lost.
bugs.impact: This is not user friendly as a user may spend a lot of time on editing the file. When clicking another file, the user does not know that changes will be lost and are not recoverable.
bugs.workaround: A user can only modify the file again after the change is lost.

bugs.title: TMM could crash when modifying HTML profile configuration
bugs.symptoms: Modification of configuration for a virtual with HTML profile attached may cause a tmm crash if there are open connections with html content.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable virtual server (or make sure that it does not have open connections in any other way) before modifying configuration.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue in HTML profile which could cause a tmm crash during configuration change on a virtual with open connections.

bugs.title: On UDP virtual under CLIENT_DATA event load balance does not work
bugs.symptoms: On a UDP virtual server, iRule commands (e.g., pool) to change the load-balancing decision have no effect when they are in the CLIENT_DATA event.
bugs.conditions: UDP virtual server and CLIENT_DATA event.
bugs.impact: Load balance does not work. Depending on the command and the configuration, there might be other impacts. For example, for the pool command, since there is no default pool, packets might be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Use CLIENT_ACCEPTED instead.

bugs.title: FIPS key deletion by-handle does not post an error if corresponding key object exists but the keyname is more than 32 characters long
bugs.symptoms: Starting 11.4.0, 'tmsh delete sys crypto fips by-handle handle#' command is expected to throw an error if the key object corresponding to this FIPS key handle exists in BIG-IP config. However, this does not work if the key name is longer than 32 characters because the operation relies on key name being the same as the FIPS key label, which is not the case for keynames of greater than 32 chars.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP contains a FIPS key object with a name that is longer than 32 characters. User attempts 'tmsh delete sys crypto fips by-handle handle#' for this FIPS key handle. The expected error does not occur, and the operation deletes the FIPS key from the FIPS card, which makes the BIG-IP key object invalid.
bugs.impact: The corresponding BIG-IP key object is now invalid with no corresponding FIPS key in FIPS card. Traffic using this key object will fail.
bugs.workaround: Use keynames shorter than 32 characters for FIPS keys.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now posts an error if the user tries to manually delete a particular FIPS key by-handle while its corresponding key object exists in BIG-IP configuration, regardless of the length of the key name. IMPORTANT: FIPS key deletion by-handle should still be executed with caution because the FIPS handle might belong to keys in different boot locations of the BIG-IP configuration. Deleting those FIPS keys does not throw an error, but will make FIPS keys in the other boot locations invalid and unusable.

bugs.title: Connection Rate Limit Mode when limit is exceeded by one client also throttles others
bugs.symptoms: Connection Rate Limit Mode is set to Per Virtual Server and Source Address, you might encounter unexpected results. Once a particular client is above the limit, other clients (other source IP addresses) are also throttled by the system.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following manner: There is a configured connection rate limit per virtual server per client; one client exceeds the configured rate limit; and the virtual server also throttles other, unrelated clients.
bugs.impact: The virtual server throttles clients that are not exceeding the connection rate limit.
bugs.fix: Connection Rate Limit Mode when limit is exceeded by one client no longer throttles others.

bugs.title: Default routes from standby system when HA is configured in NSSA
bugs.symptoms: In an NSSA configuration with a DR, BDR, and HA-configured BIG-IP systems, there are three default routes, one each from DR, BDR, and the standby BIG-IP system. The standby BIG-IP system should not send out any default routes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using OSPF in an NSSA configuration with a DR, BDR and HA pair BIG-IP systems.
bugs.impact: Traffic is incorrectly directed to the standby and dropped.
bugs.fix: There are now no default routes from the standby BIG-IP system in an HA pair. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Multi-line TXT records truncated by ZoneRunner file import
bugs.symptoms: Checking your TXT record in the web interface causes the system to give an error. Querying for the data against a listener for the record reveals that the TXT rdata is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: GTM enabled and a zone file with a TXT record that has multi-line rdata has been imported via the GUI into ZoneRunner.
bugs.impact: Your DNS TXT records will be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Enter your multi-line TXT records via the web interface as single line, quote separated lines.
bugs.fix: Multi-line TXT records are no longer truncated.

bugs.title: All Messages report does not display any data when the Log Levels are selected to filter data based on Log levels
bugs.symptoms: When an admin runs All Messages report and selects some Log Level checkboxes in the Report Parameters popup to filter out messages by log level, the report does not show any data.
bugs.impact: Cannot filter the All Messages report by Log Level.
bugs.fix: The All Messages Report now displays data correctly when the log level filter is used.
bugs.conditions: Select some log levels on the All Messages report.

bugs.title: External Datagroup records not listed
bugs.symptoms: Using the list command does not display the records of an external datagroup.
bugs.conditions: Using an external datagroup.
bugs.impact: Can't see external datagroup entries.
bugs.fix: Can now see entries using the following tmsh command: show ltm data-group external XYZ external-records.

bugs.title: Firewall software check cannot detect state of ipfw on MAC OS X
bugs.symptoms: The Firewall software check cannot detect the state of ipfw software on MAC OS X. Also, because of some underlying issue, the HD encryption software check cannot detect encrypted locations by FileVault software on MAC OS X.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM, Firewall software check, HD encryption software check.
bugs.impact: Firewall software check cannot detect state of ipfw on MAC OS X.

bugs.title: invalidation may be delayed when compressed and uncompressed requests are present
bugs.symptoms: invalidation may be delayed when compressed and uncompressed requests are present.
bugs.conditions: If content is cached only uncompressed before it is invalidated and after invalidation is requested only compressed, the invalidation may be delayed by several requests.
bugs.impact: Old content may be served several extra times.
bugs.workaround: Repeatedly request the contents until the invalidation happens.

bugs.title: Content cached compressed and uncompressed may invalidate separately
bugs.symptoms: When static content is cached both compressed and uncompressed, they may not invalidate simultaneously.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a mix of compressed and uncompressed requests for static content, combined with triggered or ESI invalidations of that content.
bugs.impact: This may result in their cache ages being different. This might result in extra revalidations after invalidations and unexpected cache lifetimes.

bugs.title: scriptd incorrectly reports that it is running on a secondary blade
bugs.symptoms: scriptd might indicate that it is running on a secondary blade, even when the process is running on a primary blade or an appliance. The error condition generates this log message: 014f000f:7: Becoming secondary cluster member
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are not well understood, but it is a rare occurrence.
bugs.impact: Perpetual iCall handlers do not run, so scripts running under the control of a daemon do not run.
bugs.workaround: Issue the command 'bigstart restart scriptd' on an affected blade or device.
bugs.fix: scriptd no longer incorrectly reports that it is running on a secondary blade when it is not.

bugs.title: Out of Memory Error
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes due to a segmentation violation early in a WAM interface. Most likely, before the crash occurs the logs should show messages indicating that the sweeper was activated one or more times.
bugs.conditions: Only happens when free memory is very low to non-existent.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes.
bugs.workaround: Reduce load on box if possible.
bugs.fix: Guards were placed on the module interfaces to bypass the module when the necessary memory could not be allocated for a connection.

bugs.title: ePVA continues to accelerate IP Forwarding VS traffic even in Standby
bugs.symptoms: When the active BIG-IP unit in a redundant configuration becomes the standby unit after a failover event, the traffic sent to the virtual servers with hardware acceleration enabled will continue to be accelerated by the ePVA hardware on the original active unit (current standby unit). These offloaded flows will eventually be evicted after the failover switch period (16 second by default) though, and it does not affect the new active unit (original standby unit) to offload the flows to hardware for acceleration. As a result, accelerated traffic can still be observed on the standby unit.
bugs.conditions: When a failover event happens in a redundant configuration with virtual servers that have hardware acceleration enabled.
bugs.impact: No performance impact or traffic interruption. You might observe unexpected traffic on standby unit.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.fix: The standby unit now evicts the accelerated flows from the ePVA hardware after the failover event. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Config load does not skip leading whitespaces if iRule starts with #
bugs.symptoms: When iRules are saved into bigip.conf, the first line is automatically indented with four whitespaces. Usually these whitespaces are removed when the config is loaded, but when an iRule starts with commented lines, the whitespace is not removed. Every subsequent save/load operation adds another four whitespaces. When users adds checksum to the iRule, loading fails at checksum verification error
bugs.conditions: This occurs when both conditions are true: 1. Line 1 begins with a # character and white spaces. 2. The checksum operation is performed on the iRule.
bugs.impact: Load failure.
bugs.workaround: Remove the whitespace at the beginning of the iRule

bugs.title: The 'Restore down' button can be hidden for full-screen RDP resources.
bugs.symptoms: The issue occurs when a user clicks the 'Restore down' button. After that RDP is inside a window but the maximize button is grayed out so user is not able to restore window to full screen.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for VPN users using RDP resources.
bugs.impact: End users report that they are unable to restore the window to full screen.
bugs.fix: You can specify showrestorebutton:i:0 in Custom Parameters for a remote desktop of the RDP type. The Restore down button will no longer display.

bugs.title: Unable to determine what topology record was selected from pool and pool member decision logging
bugs.symptoms: Gtm pool and pool member selection and traversal logs do not indicate what topology records were used when using topology load balancing.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when topology is used for load balancing either by selecting the topology load balancing method on a gtm pool or wideip, or by selecting Quality of Service (QoS) with a non-zero topology weight.
bugs.impact: It may be more difficult to diagnose problems with a topology configuration.
bugs.workaround: None. This information cannot be easily gleaned from elsewhere.
bugs.fix: If pool or pool member traversal logging is enabled on a wideip and a listener has an attached dns profile that has logging enabled and a logging profile, then topology selections will be logged when topology is used for load balancing, including when a topology QoS score is generated.

bugs.title: Renewing certificates with SAN input in the GUI leads to error.
bugs.symptoms: Renewing an existing certificate fails using the GUI if a user provides Subject Alternative Name (SAN) as input.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI, provide SAN while renewing certificate.
bugs.impact: Cannot renew certificate using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Do not provide SAN information while renewing certificates. As an alternative, you can create a new certificate with a SAN. Impact of workaround: Performing the suggested workaround should not have a negative impact on your system.
bugs.fix: Renewing an existing certificate now succeeds if a user provides Subject Alternative Name (SAN) as input in the GUI.

bugs.title: Low memory condition caused by Ram Cache may result in TMM core
bugs.symptoms: As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptoms: - The TMM process crashes with a SIGABRT - The BIG-IP system fails over to the peer system in a high-availability configuration. - The BIG-IP system generates a TMM core file in the /var/core directory.
bugs.conditions: - Associating a Web Acceleration profile with a virtual server - TMM has become deficient in memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: Tmm no longer crashes in certain low memory conditions with Ram Cache enabled.

bugs.title: Responses from DNS transparent cache will no longer contain RRSIG for queries without DO bit set
bugs.symptoms: DNS transparent cache may have RRSIG in the responses for queries without DO bit set.
bugs.conditions: DNS transparent cache receives a DNS query without DO bit set. If the query is answered by a DNSSEC zone of a pool member. The response returned to the client will contain RRSIG.
bugs.impact: Responses contain unnecessary RR sets. Not RFC compliant.
bugs.fix: Queries answered by DNS transparent cache will no longer add RRSIG to the response if DO bit is not set in the query.

bugs.title: Delayed response by very busy MCPD disrupts communication with TMM
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts without any core file on startup or when mcpd is loading the configuration if the size of configuration is considered large (e.g., more than 1000 passive monitors). TMM restarts without any core file while running "tmsh show sys connection" or "tmsh show sys connection" with a large connection table (e.g., 500 KB and 600 KM, respectively).
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The mcpd process loads a large configuration with thousands of objects. -- The platform is running 12 or more TMM instances (BIG-IP 11000/11050 platforms, or VIPRION B4300 blades). Or: -- You run "tmsh show sys connection" or "tmsh show sys connection all-properties". -- The platform is running 12 or more TMM instances (BIG-IP 11000/11050 platforms, or VIPRION B4300/B4450 blades).
bugs.impact: Traffic processed by the affected TMM instance is interrupted while TMM restarts. TMM might enter a restart loop and restart multiple times, without producing a core file. You might see errors similar to the following in log/tmm or log/daemon: -- LTM01 crit tmm11[28599]: 01010020:2: MCP Connection aborted, exiting. -- LTM01 emerg logger: Re-starting tmm. This might cause serious traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: This workaround is a mitigation and may not work in all cases; the zero-window timeout may need to be adjusted to a higher value for some configurations. To work around this issue, increase the timeout used for the MCP connection. 1. Open the tmm_base.tcl file for modification. 2. Locate the tcp _mcptcp stanza. 3. Add the following line: zero_window_timeout 300000 This lengthens the timeout, which avoids the restart. For more information, see K14498: The mcpd connection to TMM may time out on either startup or configuration load and cause TMM to restart, available here: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14498.
bugs.fix: For most configurations, TMM no longer restarts on startup/config-load if it has too many objects to publish back during config load. The mitigation fix increases an internal buffer. This provides sufficient time for most configurations. Some configurations might require still more time. If the issue still occurs, you can increase the zero-window timeout until the configuration loads without problems. To completely address the issue

bugs.title: APM SharePoint integration might not work using Internet Explorer 10 on Microsoft Windows 8.
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft Windows 8 does not share persistent cookies between the browser and Office components. This prevents session management tools like APM from connecting Windows 8 clients with SharePoint services. The Microsoft case number is 112090575901186.
bugs.conditions: APM SharePoint integration in IE 10 on Windows 8
bugs.impact: System produces an error when trying to open documents from SharePoint through APM.
bugs.workaround: Word/Excel integration (i.e., Document library features) support is fixed by KB2846960.

bugs.title: Notification for required reboot when Credential Management Service is changed.
bugs.symptoms: The credential manager doesn't work without a reboot so the user is required to enter credentials again while logging in on APM.
bugs.conditions: Credential manager is updated.
bugs.impact: End users need to re-enter credentials

bugs.title: Portal Acccess resources with proxy require hostnames to be resolvable to BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access resources with proxy host configured and no DNS record available to BIG-IP will be blocked by APM ACL. All requests to these resources will result in APM DNS error page.
bugs.impact: Some resources accessible only via proxy cannot be configured to work through APM Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Use intranet DNS server for BIG-IP, or add resources behind proxy server to a DNS server configuration.
bugs.fix: Portal Access resources with proxy host configured and no DNS record available to BIG-IP are no longer blocked by APM ACL.

bugs.title: APM requires external IP address to be specified for PCoIP client to connect to via NAT
bugs.symptoms: APM requires that you specify an externally visible IP address for PCoIP client to connect to when it differs from virtual server IP address. (You set the IP address using the 'view.proxy_addr' session variable.)
bugs.conditions: VMware Horizon PCoIP client connects via a NAT (i.e., APM's externally visible IP address differs from the virtual server IP address).
bugs.impact: This configuration is non-obvious and can lead to confusion.
bugs.workaround: Set the IP address using the 'view.proxy_addr' session variable.
bugs.fix: Now, for PCoIP clients, which support name resolution, APM does not require explicit configuration of an externally visible IP address via the 'view.proxy_addr' session variable. Note: VMware Horizon clients for most platforms (Windows, Mac, Android, and iOS) except Linux, support name resolution.

bugs.title: Error logged by SSOv2 plugin when unholding request done event
bugs.symptoms: Errors are logged by SSOv2 plugin while processing traffic: err tmm2[29966]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_extract_uri, Line: 12335 err tmm2[29966]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_block_irule_events_for_uri, Line: 15888 err tmm2: 014d0002:3: SSOv2 plugin error(-1) in sso/sso.c:1018
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered during normal operation while SSO is configured.
bugs.impact: Errors are logged erroneously, this does not impact request processing.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround

bugs.title: Creating an SNMP v3 user using the Configuration utility or tmsh adds passwords in plain text to the snmpd.conf file
bugs.symptoms: Creating or modifying SNMP v3 users using the GUI or tmsh adds passwords in plain text to the /config/net-snmp/snmpd.conf file.
bugs.conditions: You have created or modified an SNMP v3 user using the GUI or with the command 'tmsh modify sys snmp users ...'
bugs.impact: SNMP v3 user passwords are visible to those with root read access on the BIG-IP system until you run bigstart restart to restart the snmp process.
bugs.workaround: Run the command 'bigstart restart snmp' to restart snmp after creating or modifying SNMP v3 users. This results in encrypted passwords in the file.

bugs.title: Network Access related log messages logged after VPN tunnel is closed
bugs.symptoms:
When a Network Access session and an APM session are closed simultaneously, one of these logs is written at the NOTICE level: apm logs: "VPN Cleanup: failed to release IPv4 ERR_ARG" tmm logs: "address

in leasepool is unassigned - can't release"
bugs.conditions: This happens when a Network Access resource and a Network Access webtop are assigned using the Advanced Resource Assign action, and the Network Access session is closed.
bugs.impact: These are logged at the notice level, and can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: BIG-IP JavaScript includes can be improperly injected in case of conditional commment presence
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript does not work if a page contains conditional comments inside its head tag.
bugs.conditions: Presence of conditional comments contain very first script tag. Example: <html> <!--[if lt IE 9]> <script src="foo.js"></script> <![endif]--> <script> document.write("foo"); </script> </html>
bugs.impact: JavaScript does not work.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, use an iRule. The exact commands to use depend on the situation.
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed by adding necessary JavaScript includes into every conditional branch.

bugs.title: Sync issues with certain objects' parameters.
bugs.symptoms: Synchronized configuration objects may contain invalid parameters after you delete an object and create a different object type with the same name.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The BIG-IP systems are configured as part of a Device Group. -- You delete a configuration object of one type and then create a different type of object that uses the same name. -- The new object's configuration is synchronized to the other systems of the Device Group.
bugs.impact: An invalid configuration on the box that is synced to, and no obvious warning signs.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following methods: -- Synchronize the configuration after you delete the original object and before you create the new object. -- Use a different name for the new configuration object.

bugs.title: tcl_platform is no longer in the static:: namespace
bugs.symptoms: In previous versions of iRules, the variable tcl_platform was readable as: 'set myvar static::tcl_platform'. However with recent changes, the variable is in the global, not static namespace and should be accessed as '::tcl_platform'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on pre-11.4.0 iRules that use the variable 'static::tcl_platform'.
bugs.impact: iRules that worked properly under earlier versions can result in runtime Tcl exceptions (disrupting traffic) after an upgrade to v11.4.0 or later, if those iRules reference static::tcl_platform.
bugs.workaround: To map tcl_platform into the static namespace in an iRule, use the following: when RULE_INIT { upvar #0 tcl_platform static::tcl_platform }. Or you can use ::tcl_platform instead of static::tcl_platform. Note: The latter workaround might demote a virtual server from CMP. For more information, see K14544: The tcl_platform iRules variable is not in the static:: namespace, available here: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K14544.

bugs.title: Removing the gateway failsafe pool in web interface does not set the pool::gateway failsafe device property to none
bugs.symptoms: Removing the gateway failsafe pool in the web interface does not set the pool::gateway failsafe device property to none.
bugs.conditions: When the gateway failsafe pool is removed from web user interface, the pool maintains the prior gateway failsafe device. This is seen on listing the pool in tmsh.
bugs.impact: Creates confusion about the current pool::gateway failsafe device configuration.
bugs.workaround: The pool::gateway failsafe device property can be set to none using tmsh.

bugs.title: Bypass disabling the redirection controls configuration of APM RDP Resource.
bugs.symptoms: User can bypass RDP resource redirection restrictions between RDP remote machine and local machine.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create RDP resource. Disable redirection parameter. 2. Launch the resource. 3. Launch RDP Client, enable redirection parameter.
bugs.impact: User can bypass RDP resource restrictions.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: User is not allowed to perform any redirection controls of the RDP resource.

bugs.title: bigd cores when route-domain tagged to a pool with monitor as gateway_ICMP is deleted
bugs.symptoms: bigd restarts once, and afterwards, subsequent pings from the monitor fails.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when assigning an ICMP monitor to a pool member, specifying a route domain that does not exist.
bugs.impact: For bigd, a single restart is actually harmless. The invalid config will cause monitor failures, since the route domain no longer exists, the pool member will be marked down.
bugs.fix: bigd no longer cores when route-domain tagged to a pool with monitor as gateway_ICMP is deleted.

bugs.title: syslog messages over 8 KB in length cause logstatd to exit
bugs.symptoms: Creating a syslog longer than 8 KB in length might cause logstatd to issue an exception and exit.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system processes a syslog message that is longer than 8 KB.
bugs.impact: logstatd exits and posts a message similar to the following: localhost emerg logger: Re-starting logstatd.
bugs.workaround: Configure syslog smaller than (or equal to) 8 KB using a command similar to the following in bigip_base.conf: sys syslog { include "options { ... log_msg_size(8192); };" }.
bugs.fix: syslog messages over 8 KB can now be processed, and the system does not exit. Note that the system does not process any log entry that is three times the buffer length or greater than 12 KB.

bugs.title: GTM might mark down LTM virtual servers in non-zero RDs named with special characters
bugs.symptoms: LTM virtual servers that are in a non-zero route domain (RD) named using special characters, might be incorrectly marked down by GTM.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM virtual servers with a '.' (dot) or ';' (semi-colon) in the name. -- Configured in a non-zero RD.
bugs.impact: GTM marks those LTM virtual servers down.
bugs.workaround: This workaround involves changing the GTM config. To make the config work properly, the GTM must be configured with 1 (one) server stanza for each RD on the LTM system that has virtual servers. The following example configuration creates 3 virtual servers, 1 for each RD. Each server then discovers and probes only the virtual servers in the RD. (NOTE: Remove the 'expose-route-domains yes' option from the server stanza. If that remains 'on', then each server lists all of the virtual servers on the LTM, creating duplicates. Furthermore, virtual servers in an RD that does not match the server's RD, are marked down. For the following example: -- on server 10.5.76.239 in route domain 0, all virtual servers in RD1 and RD2 will be red (marked down). -- on server 10.10.10.39 in route domain 1, all virtual servers in RD0 and RD2 will be red. -- on server 10.10.11.39 in route domain 2, all virtual servers in RD0 and RD1 will be red.) For example: 1. If the LTM system is configured with the following self IP addresses (that is, 3 self IP addresses in default RD, RD1, and RD2): net self 10.5.76.239 { address 10.5.76.239/24 allow-service all traffic-group traffic-group-local-only vlan vlan-576 } net self 10.10.11.39%2 { address 10.10.11.39%2/24 allow-service { default } traffic-group traffic-group-local-only vlan vlan-3273 } net self 10.10.10.39%1 { address 10.10.10.39%1/24 allow-service { default } traffic-group traffic-group-local-only vlan vlan-3270 } 2. There are the following virtual servers in each RD: ltm virtual vs.rd0.dottest { destination 10.5.76.39:http ip-protocol tcp mask 255.255.255.255 pool p1 profiles { tcp { } } vlans-disabled } ltm virtual vs.rd1.dottest { destination 10.10.10.39%1:http ip-protocol tcp mask 255.255.255.255 pool p1 profiles { tcp { } } vlans-disabled } ltm virtual vs.rd2.dottest { destination 10.10.11.39%2:http ip-protocol tcp mask 255.255.255.255 pool p2 profiles { tcp { } } vlans-disabled } 3. The GTM must be configured as follows: gtm server /Common/B3600-R18-S39-RD0.lab.ss.example.com { addresses { 10.5.76.239 { device-name B3600-R18-S39.lab.ss.example.com } } datacenter /Common/DC1 monitor /Common/bigip virtual-server-discovery enabled } gtm server /Common/B3600-R18-S39-RD1.lab.ss.example.com { addresses { 10.10.10.39 { device-name B3600-R18-S39.lab.ss.example.com } } datacenter /Common/DC1 monitor /Common/bigip virtual-server-discovery enabled } gtm server /Common/B3600-R18-S39-RD2.lab.ss.example.com { addresses { 10.10.11.39 { device-name B3600-R18-S39.lab.ss.example.com } } datacenter /Common/DC1 monitor /Common/bigip virtual-server-discovery enabled }

bugs.title: Parking iRules in CLIENT_DATA on virtual without assigned pool may not return
bugs.symptoms: If a virtual server is created without an assigned pool (i.e. the pool is assigned in the iRule) and the iRule parks, the iRule may not return from suspension and the packet will be dropped.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is created and an iRule is assigned that parks, and the virtual server has no assigned default pool.
bugs.impact: Packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Either use the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event for UDP data or assign a default pool.

bugs.title: parent.document.write(some_html_with_script) hangs up parent frame for IE browsers
bugs.symptoms: A statement such as: parent.document.write(some_html_with_script) hangs the parent frame for Internet Explorer browsers
bugs.conditions: Internet Explorer 10 through Internet Explorer 11
bugs.impact: Some web-applications are affected by this bug.
bugs.fix: Parent HTML page dynamic re-writing is supported in case of Internet Explorer 10-11: JavaScript statements like parent.document.write(some_html_with_script) are handled correctly.

bugs.title: tmsh modify net interface with invalid interface name or attributes will create an interface in cluster or VE environments
bugs.symptoms: tmsh modify net interface commands with either invalid interface names, or invalid attribute names will appear to create new interfaces. An invalid interface will show up in "show net interfaces"
bugs.conditions: Only happens on clustered or virtual environments, not on appliances.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic only - extraneous interfaces show up in tmsh show net interface.
bugs.workaround: guishell -c "delete from interface where name='12345/is_this_correct'"

bugs.title: iRule command [DOSL7::profile] returns empty value
bugs.symptoms: iRule command [DOSL7::profile] returns an empty value.
bugs.conditions: iRule with the [DOSL7::profile] command attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The iRule returns an empty value.
bugs.fix: The [DOSL7::profile] command now returns the DoS profile name attached to virtual server, as expected.

bugs.title: Request logging not logging pool name with APM
bugs.symptoms: Pool name is not being logged when access profile is attached to the virtual.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a pool for syslog server called "syslog-pool" 2. Create a request logging profile like the following: ltm profile request-log reqlog-pool { app-service none defaults-from request-log response-log-pool syslog-pool response-log-template "Path is $HTTP_PATH, Pool is $VIRTUAL_POOL_NAME" response-logging enabled } 3. Attach it to an HTTP virtual server with a valid default pool. 4. Send some requests and observe the path and pool are logged. 5. Create an access profile. Edit access policy to be "Start -> Allow". 6. Attach it to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Pool name is not being logged most of the time.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Rename 'IP Address Intelligence' to 'IP Intelligence'
bugs.symptoms: Some fields in sub-menus, tooltips, etc., of the application still 'IP Address Intelligence' instead og 'IP Intelligence'.
bugs.conditions: 'IP Address Intelligence' occurs in some places, such as in Event Logs, Requests, Charts, etc. For example, the older phrase occurs in Security :: Application Security : Policy : Audit : Log , Security :: Reporting : Scheduled Reports :: New Reporting Schedule, and other locations.
bugs.impact: This has no functional impact. Simply, the phrase 'IP Address Intelligence' was replaced with 'IP Intelligence', but not all visible occurrences have been changed.
bugs.workaround: No workaround needed, this is a cosmetic issue only.
bugs.fix: All visible occurrences have now been changed from 'IP Address Intelligence' to 'IP Intelligence'.

bugs.title: State Mirroring does not work for an HA pair that uses only hardwired (serial) failover, without network failover
bugs.symptoms: Failovers between devices in a HA pair might result in an unexpected disruption of traffic (for instance, if virtual servers are configured for mirroring). Persistence / session table information would similarly be missing on the newly-active system.
bugs.conditions: Platform that supports hardwired failover, configured for hardwired failover. (Note: this excludes chassis-based platforms, as well as VCMP guests and VEs) Network failover disabled.
bugs.impact: - Failovers may result in unexpected disruption of traffic that failed to be mirrored. - Session database (SessionDB things, iRule session table, persistence table, etc) will not be mirrored, as expected, which may result in unknown unexpected traffic failures.
bugs.workaround: Enable network failover, then restart all TMMs. Note: workaround will temporarily disrupt traffic.
bugs.fix: State Mirroring now works for HA configurations that use only hardwired (serial) failover, without network failover.

bugs.title: apm_mobile_ppc.css has duplicate 1st line
bugs.symptoms: An extra line (that consists of "<?") appears at the top of the apm_mobile_ppc.css file and causes an error like this one: Jul 9 08:37:10 roeislfl4gm err httpd_sam[13917]: [error] [client 127.1.1.4] PHP Parse error: syntax error, unexpected '&lt;' in /var/sam/www/php_include/webtop/renderer/customization/general_ui/Common/tmsproext-apm_general_ui/en/apm_mobile_ppc.css on line 2
bugs.impact: Generate an error message in /var/log/http_errors log file.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, remove the extra line ("<?") from var/sam/www/php_include/webtop/renderer/customization/general_ui/Common/tmsproext-apm_general_ui/en/apm_mobile_ppc.css.
bugs.conditions: Generate error log messages

bugs.title: Loading a SCF after modifying self IP may cause route in Linux kernel to be dropped
bugs.symptoms: Loading a SCF after modifying self IP may cause route in Linux kernel to be dropped. Linux host applications may not be able to connect when they are expected to.
bugs.conditions: Create a config with a self IP on a VLAN and a default gateway route on that VLAN, save a SCF file, then modify the self IP in that SCF file and then load the SCF.
bugs.impact: Linux kernel default gateway route is dropped and host applications looking for the route may not be able to connect.
bugs.workaround: Reset the config to default before loading modified SCF: 1. tmsh load sys default. 2. tmsh load sys scf SCF_flename. For more information, see SOL14572: Routes configured in a single configuration file may be missing from the Linux kernel route table after loading the single configuration file, available here: http://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/500/sol14572.

bugs.title: Tab completion in the tmsh might not list all transparent monitors
bugs.symptoms: If you create or modify a GTM link in tmsh to include a monitor, and attempt to list the available monitors using tab completion, only monitors of type bigip-link or gateway-icmp are listed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Custom transparent monitor. -- Monitor type is not Gateway ICMP. -- Use tab completion in tmsh to display all available custom transparent.
bugs.impact: If the user attempts to apply a transparent http, https, tcp, tcp-half-open, or udp monitor, to a link, it will not be listed by tab completion.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue when associating the monitor with a GTM link using the tmsh utility. To do so, you can manually type the name of a custom transparent monitor.

bugs.title: On VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID OID reports Chassis ID not Blade ID
bugs.symptoms: On VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID OID reports the ID of the Chassis. This differs from the behavior on VIPRION 4xxx-series platforms, where the SNMP sysObjectID OID reports the ID of the Blade.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms: - C2xxx-series chassis - B2xxx-series blades
bugs.impact: SNMP queries to identify the System ID of VIPRION platforms will identify different classes of hardware component on VIPRION 2xxx-series vs. 4xxx-series platforms.
