bugs.fix: On VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID OID now reports the ID of the Blade, to match the behavior on VIPRION 4xxx-series platforms. Previously, SNMP sysObjectID reported the ID of the Chassis on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms.
bugs.behavior: On VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID OID now reports the ID of the Blade, to match the behavior on VIPRION 4xxx-series platforms. Previously, SNMP sysObjectID reported the ID of the Chassis on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms.

bugs.title: GUI shows incorrect number of members of pool in HA group after pool config is sync'ed from peer unit.
bugs.symptoms: GUI shows incorrect number of members of pool in high availability (HA) group after pool config is sync'ed from peer unit.
bugs.conditions: This is triggered when automatic sync is configured with incremental synchronization on a sync-failover device group. It will be visible on the HA Groups page in the Pools section after a configuration sync is performed from a device where the pool members were modified.
bugs.impact: The number of pool members listed in the HA Groups page is incorrect (e.g., shows 2 when it should show 1, 3 when it should show 2). Although this issue is cosmetic, it makes it difficult to configure the HA Group on the affected device.
bugs.workaround: The incorrect pool member display can be fixed on the affected device, by running the following tmsh command: Impact of procedure: This command loads the saved configuration, so any in-memory changes (i.e., changes that have not been saved to disk) will be lost. Since the affected device is a sync target, and no other changes should have been made, it should be safe to run this command. tmsh load sys config
bugs.fix: High availability (HA) Groups page now displays the expected pool members on the sync target device after an automatic incremental sync is performed.

bugs.title: mcpd debug logging hardening
bugs.symptoms: mcpd should obfuscate sensitive information even in debug logging mode
bugs.conditions: mcpd log level set to Debug
bugs.impact: Certain commands can log too much information
bugs.workaround: MCP logging is at the Notice level by default. You should only use the Debug log level for certain troubleshooting efforts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with mcpd debug logging.

bugs.title: Windows EdgeClient's configuration file could be corrupted on system reboot/sleep
bugs.symptoms: User is prompted for message box prompt about corrupted config file on system start up.
bugs.conditions: Undefined. Somehow related to improper shutdown/hibernate/poweroff.
bugs.impact: Profile is reset to default values. User is annoyed.
bugs.workaround: http://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/10000/900/sol10935
bugs.fix: Configuration file handling for the BIG-IP Edge Client was improved to prevent configuration corruption.

bugs.title: Blade number not displayed in CPU status alerts
bugs.symptoms: Messages displayed on the VIPRION chassis LCD display always reference the blade number of the Primary blade in the chassis at the time that the message was issued. The slot number where the blade-specific condition is not included in message in the LCD display. In the case of CPU status alerts, where the CPU temperature is too high or the CPU fan speed is too low, the identification of the blade is not included in the console output or log messages produced by the system_check utility.
bugs.conditions: Affects: VIPRION B4100 (PB100), B4200 (PB200) and B4300-series blades in VIPRION C4400, C4480 and C4800 chassis. VIPRION B2100, B2150 and B2250 blades in VIPRION C2400 and C2200 chassis with external LCD displays attached.
bugs.impact: It may not be possible to accurately determine which blade has actually experienced a blade-specific condition reported on the chassis LCD display.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following commands to examine the CPU measurements to determine which CPU on which blade is experiencing excessive temperature and/or slow fan speed: 1. tmsh show sys hardware 2. tmctl cpu_status_stat
bugs.fix: The system_check utility now logs the blade number as part of CPU status alerts to the system console and log messages. Such detail is not made available on the LCD display.

bugs.title: exporting to a CSV file may fail and the Admin UI is inaccessible
bugs.symptoms: If there are a large number of APM report records, exporting them to a CSV file might fail and the Admin GUI can then become inaccessible.
bugs.conditions: When the amount of report data is large.
bugs.impact: The Admin UI is inaccessible.
bugs.workaround: Avoid exporting large amounts of report data.

bugs.title: Firewall ACL Schedules may not work when configured with a daily schedule that starts before the specified start date and time
bugs.symptoms: If the daily schedule for a rule starts before the start date and time specified in the schedule. For example, assume the current time is 2013-07-26 16:20:00. If you specify the following schedule and associate it with a rule, the rule will not get scheduled at all. tmsh modify security firewall schedule sched1 {date-valid-start 2013-07-26:16:24:00 date-valid-end 2013-07-26:16:29:00 daily-hour-start 16:23 daily-hour-end 16:27 }
bugs.conditions: The daily-hour-start needs to be configured to occur before the date-valid-start.
bugs.impact: The scheduled rule will not become active when configured in this manner.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, make sure that date-valid-start is not before daily-hour-start. A working example, assuming the current time is 2013-07-26 16:20:00. Configure the date-valid-start to be the previous day: tmsh modify security firewall schedule sched1 {date-valid-start 2013-07-25:16:24:00 date-valid-end 2013-07-26:16:29:00 daily-hour-start 16:23 daily-hour-end 16:27 }

bugs.title: Updating iRule procs while in use can cause a core
bugs.symptoms: When updating an iRule that is in process or parked and has existing connections and uses a proc, a core can occur due to incorrect internal reference counting.
bugs.conditions: High traffic iRule that both parks and uses a proc.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system might temporarily fail to process traffic, and fail over if configured as part of a high availability (HA) pair.
bugs.workaround: Disable listener before updating iRule. For more information, see SOL14654: Updating an iRule that uses sideband connections may cause TMM to core, available here: http://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/600/sol14654.
bugs.fix: Updating an iRule that uses sideband connections no longer causes TMM to core.

bugs.title: In Admin UI, import of CSV file with users very slow to process complete CSV.
bugs.symptoms: Importing users from a file into a local user database takes a long time. The admin must wait until all users get created. The wait time depends of number of users.
bugs.conditions: This happens when importing a long list of users from a CSV file to a local user database.
bugs.impact: Because loading users takes a long time, an administrator user might not know what to do and retry multiple times.
bugs.workaround: An administrator must wait until the users load to the database without making additional attempts.
bugs.fix: The performance of a bulk user import operation from a CSV file into APM local user database via the Admin GUI is improved dramatically.

bugs.title: APM Polices does not work in VIPRION 4800 chassis if there is no slot1
bugs.symptoms: Access policies does not get executed according to the configuration in a VIPRION 4800 chassis. User will not be able to use those policies.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens only on VIPRION 4800 and only if there is no active slot1 as primary or standby
bugs.impact: User will not be able to use the access polices that are configured in BIG-IP
bugs.workaround: Always use slot1 in the VIPRION 4800
bugs.fix: Access policies now work properly in VIPRION 4800 with no slot1.

bugs.title: Delay in SWG forwarding with an Expect: 100-continue
bugs.symptoms: When the client sends an HTTP POST with an "Expect: 100-continue", APM will fail to forward it to the backend server. The client will wait about 3 seconds to timeout before sending the actual data of the POST request.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the APM is deployed in SWG explicit mode.
bugs.impact: The client will not receive a 100-continue. Usually, it waits for about 3 seconds and then forwards the data anyway.
bugs.workaround: The following iRule appears to resolve the issue. when HTTP_REQUEST { if {([HTTP::method] eq "POST") && [HTTP::header exists "Expect"] } { HTTP::header remove "Expect" SSL::respond "HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n" } }
bugs.fix: SWG explicit prompts with 100-continue to process the POST data immediately.

bugs.title: Support Citrix or VMware view resources launch client selection prompt
bugs.symptoms: Automatic client detection does not work for Citrix receiver or VMware Horizon View client if it is already installed.
bugs.conditions: Citrix or View resource is launched from APM webtop and automatic client does not work.
bugs.impact: End user is shown a Citrix prompt even though Citrix receiver is already installed.
bugs.fix: Citrix or VMware Horizon View resources published on APM Webtop can be launched either using their native clients or HTML5 client. Automatic client detection does not work in recent browsers. Due to that, whenever a resource could be launched using either of the two (Native client or HTML5), a prompt is shown to the APM end user to select the appropriate client for resource launch. The preference is saved, so the system uses it for subsequent resource launch. If the APM end user wants to see the current settings and to change their preference, they can use 'VDI Settings' menu item shown in the webtop toolbar. There is admin preferred settings can be used from access policy of VPE agent. Possible values are "native", "html5" or "". Default value of this variable is empty string (""). It is shown as 'Prompt User' in VMware View Policy VPE agent. New Behavior for Citrix: Name of Admin preferred VPE session variable is 'session.citrix.preferred_client'. If admin-preferred value is not provided or given value of empty string, APM end user is shown the prompt to select the client type for launching first time they click on the application/desktop. After that, their chosen value is saved in the browser. The HTML5 option is shown only when the html5 package is installed on Citrix client bundle. If the html5 package is not available, the native client URL is shown for native client download for the first time. If admin preferred value is "native", the native client URL is shown to download either the Citrix receiver client. New Behavior for View: Name of admin-preferred VPE session variable is 'session.vmware_view.preferred_client'. There is already the 'VMware View Policy' VPE agent to select this variable value. For View, only RDS desktop is supported for HTML5 launch. If the admin-preferred value is 'Prompt User', the APM end user is prompted for the client type selection. And the native client download link is shown for VMware Horizon client download. For apps, native client is directly launched.

bugs.title: Accept-language is not respected if there is no session context for page requested.
bugs.symptoms: Localization settings are determined when the session is created. As a result, when the user logs out, there is user context left for APM to determine what language to present to the user. So, when user is using the localized logon page, after the refresh it turns to the default language.
bugs.conditions: After configuring the preferred language, When refreshing login page twice, language is changed to default Eng.
bugs.impact: APM page doesn't load the preferred language after refreshing twice.

bugs.title: VIPRION C4800-series chassis Annunciator card numbering appears backwards
bugs.symptoms: VIPRION C4800-series chassis contain two Annunciator cards which perform chassis-level hardware-management functionality. Each card is located in a numbered slot accessible via the chassis front panel after removing the LCD display. BIG-IP utilities (such as the 'bladectl' utility or the 'tmsh show sys hardware' command) label the annunciator cards numerically opposite from the chassis front-panel slot labels. - The annunciator card located in physical slot 2 is identified as 'Annunciator'. - The annunciator card located in physical slot 1 is identified as 'Annunciator 2'.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION C4800-series chassis running affected versions of BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Inconsistency between logical and physical numbering of the chassis annunciator cards can cause confusion when one of the annunciator cards requires replacement or other service.
bugs.workaround: Remember that numerical identification of chassis annunciator cards in the TMOS UI is reversed from the physical annunciator slot numbering.

bugs.title: asm_config_server_rpc might crash during ASM policy sync
bugs.symptoms: asm_config_server_rpc might crash during ASM policy sync. asm_config_server restarts after the core, and resumes synchronization. There is no effect on configuration or on traffic.
bugs.conditions: ASM sync enabled.
bugs.impact: asm_config_server restarts after the core, and resumes synchronization. There is no effect on configuration or on traffic.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a scenario in which asm_config_server_rpc might crash during ASM policy sync.

bugs.title: ipport hash type is not programmed in new blade
bugs.symptoms: When inserting a new blade in a VIPRION C2400 chassis, with UDP or TCP hash set to 'ipport', the new blade uses the 'port' hash instead. Rebooting the blade or restarting bcm56xxd and tmm causes the correct DAG (Disaggregator) hash to be used.
bugs.conditions: UDP or TCP hash algorithm changed from default (e.g. changed from 'port' to 'ipport'). -- UDP or TCP virtual servers configured. -- New blade inserted into chassis. New blade includes external interface to which traffic will arrive.
bugs.impact: Prevents adequate distribution of traffic within a chassis, which may disrupt traffic flows or reduce the traffic throughput of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the new blade after it has been configured. Issue the 'bigstart restart' command (to restart the bcm56xxd and tmm modules and program the DAG with the correct hash type).

bugs.title: Insufficiently detailed causes for session deletion.
bugs.symptoms: When a session is deleted for a reason unrelated to explicit admin action, a generic log message appears: 'Session deleted due to user inactivity or errors.' The message does not distinguish user inactivity from 'error', so the log message indicates a possible error when perhaps none had occurred.
bugs.conditions: Normal user inactivity is indistinguishable from numerous other causes related to policy actions.
bugs.impact: Cannot troubleshoot a session termination cause because there is no ability to determine whether the session was deleted because of normal user inactivity or due to some other cause.
bugs.fix: The session deletion cause has been added as an enhancement to the session deletion log functionality.

bugs.title: Removing a DNS cache from configuration can cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Removing a DNS cache from the configuration with outstanding packets on the server side can cause a TMM crash if those responses time out after the resolver removed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with DNS traffic in progress when removing a configured DNS cache from the configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This occurs with DNS traffic in progress. Disabling the listener using that cache and waiting 60 seconds before removing the cache prevents this from occurring.
bugs.fix: Deleting a cache resolver no longer results in outstanding packet issues.

bugs.title: SAML SSO could fail if SAML configuration contains special XML characters (&,<,>,",')
bugs.symptoms: SAML AuthRequest and Assertion generation could fail if the configuration (IdpEntityID, ACS, SAML Attributes, and so on) contain special XML characters, such as [&,<,>,",'].
bugs.conditions: - Assertion signing is enabled on BIG-IP as IdP. - SAML Configuration (IdpEntityID, ACS, not-encrypted SAML Attributes, ACS URL, SP Entity ID, SLO URL) contains special characters, e.g. [&,<,>,",']
bugs.impact: SAML AuthRequest and Assertion generation could fail.
bugs.workaround: You can replace special XML character with XML-escape codes in the configuration: " " ' ' < < > > & & For example, replace "http://f5.com/acs_url?user=5&password=pass" with "http://f5.com/acs_url?user=5&password=pass"
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system, when configured as an Identity Provider (IdP), can now successfully create SAML assertions even when the BIG-IP configuration contains special XML characters.

bugs.title: TCP stalls in tagged vlan-group with unic
bugs.symptoms: 1. Error in tmm log - ifoutput(992): Invalid TSO type error 2. Performance degradation or traffic may not pass.
bugs.conditions: 1. Guest vlan tagging is in use. 2. For fastL4 profile, tm.tcplargereceiveoffload DB variable set to enable.
bugs.impact: Performance degradation or traffic stall.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following: 1. Use host vlan tagging instead of guest vlan tagging. 2. Set tm.tcplargereceiveoffload DB to disable. For some synthetic NICs #2 may not work and #1 is preferable.

bugs.title: Lowering virtual server connection limit does not work when traffic is being processed
bugs.symptoms: Lowering the virtual server connection limit does not work when traffic is already being processed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when: -- The virtual server has a connection limit set. -- The virtual server is processing traffic. -- The virtual server connection limit is reset to a lower value.
bugs.impact: New virtual server configuration does not use the new, lower value to limit the number of connections. It will remain this way until the connection count goes below the new threshold.
bugs.workaround: Change virtual server connection limit configuration when there is no traffic.

bugs.title: dtca-bundle.crt file version can be out of sync with config
bugs.symptoms: The version of the dtca-bundle.crt file saved in config filestore can get out of sync with the version noted in the BIG-IP configuration file. When this happens BIG-IP attempts to restore the version from the trash can. If the trash can has been purged then the version can not be restored and configuration does not load, and emits the following error: _identify_jobs_todo:(/Common/dtca-bundle.crt) :Failed: name (/Common/dtca-bundle.crt) No copy in trash-bin to restore from. - sys/validation/FileObject.cpp, line 3064
bugs.conditions: This appears to be a timing problem related to saving the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.impact: This error prevents configuration from loading.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to edit the configuration file so that the version number matches the version in file store.
bugs.fix: This bug fix reduces the occurrence of this bug but does not eliminate it.

bugs.title: Policy with auto-detect encoding is not configured on target of device group sync
bugs.symptoms: Device management: A security policy is not configured on the target device if the Auto detect option is selected for this security policy on the source device.
bugs.conditions: A security policy is created with auto-detect encoding with device group sync configured.
bugs.impact: On the target device of device group sync, the security policy appears as unconfigured.
bugs.workaround: After policy encoding has been detected, manually push sync to peer devices.
bugs.fix: Auto-detect encoding for security policy is preserved in device group sync.

bugs.title: No support for external link down time on network failover
bugs.symptoms: For switch based platforms, the bcm56xxd daemon monitors the active/standby state using the failover.bigipunitmask DB variable and if this indicates a transition from Active to Standby, it downs external links and starts a timer for re-enabling the links after a customer-specified delay as per the failover.standby.linkdowntime DB variable.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP 2000 series and 4000 series platforms.
bugs.impact: No support for external link down time on network failover.
bugs.fix: External link down time on network failover is now supported on BIG-IP 2000 series and 4000 series platforms. You can find the Link Down Time on Failover option in the GUI under Device Management :: Device Groups :: [device_group_name] :: Failover.

bugs.title: Log file permissions lock down
bugs.symptoms: Log file permissions for one specific log file were incorrectly set. This has been fixed to address an issue with CCE-26812-8, CCE-26821-9 and CCE-27190-8 syslog-ng configuration/permissions.
bugs.conditions: Since only Administrators can have advanced shell access, they are on the only ones who could be able to see the log files. This just sets the file permissions the same as the rest.
bugs.impact: Very little impact.
bugs.fix: /var/log/catalina.out permissions changed to be more secure.

bugs.title: tmipsecd cores when deleting a non-existing traffic selector
bugs.symptoms: tmipsecd cores when a to-be-removed traffic selector is not found in the internal database on tmipsecd.
bugs.conditions: This is a rare race condition.
bugs.impact: IPsec tunnel flapping and core dump.
bugs.fix: TMIPSECD logs a critical message instead of coring, and IPsec tunnel flapping and core dump no longer occurs when deleting a non-existing traffic selector.

bugs.title: ePVA does not work with lasthop pools with only one member
bugs.symptoms: ePVA does not work with lasthop pools with only one member.
bugs.conditions: ePVA does not work with lasthop pools with only one member.
bugs.impact: ePVA does not work with lasthop pools with only one member.

bugs.title: Some monitor types assigned to the same node IP:port in different Route Domains may collide and mark the object down.
bugs.symptoms: A race condition may occur in which a monitor instance is killed abruptly if another copy of the same monitor attempts to check health of the same node IP:port in a different route domain. The killed monitor will then contribute to a monitoring timeout and potentially mark the node as down. This issue occurs because the PID file created to prevent duplicate monitoring of the same pool member is not sufficiently unique to distinguish between route domains. For example, SIP monitor named "sip_london" applied to pool members 1.2.3.4%100 and 1.2.3.4%200 would share the same PID file: /var/run/SIP__Common_sip_london.::ffff:1.2.3.40..5060.pid
bugs.conditions: For health monitor types which execute outside of the bigd process (see list below), a health monitor profile is assigned to monitor 2 different nodes which have the same IP:port in different route domains. The affected monitor types include: Diameter IMAP LDAP NNTP POP3 Radius Radius Accounting RPC Scripted SIP SMB SMTP WAP
bugs.impact: Pool members may flap down/up.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, perform the following steps: 1. Create a duplicate copy of the monitor profile, and add the route domain to the name of the monitor profile. For example: ltm monitor radius /Common/radius_seattle_rd43 { default-from /Common/radius_seattle } 2. For nodes or pool members in that route domain, replace the old monitor profile with the new duplicate monitor profile.

bugs.title: 2000/4000 platforms can end up in indeterminate ARL/FDB state
bugs.symptoms: 2000/4000 platforms can end up in indeterminate ARL/FDB state under certain conditions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when one of these platforms is subjected to a stream of frames arriving from one MAC address on two different ports on a VLAN simultaneously.
bugs.impact: The result is an indeterminate ARL/FDB state.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Traffic that does not match any virtual or Self IP is dropped silently (without any logs or statistics)
bugs.symptoms: When AFM is operating in Default Deny mode, traffic that does not match a Virtual or Self IP is dropped/rejected silently without any counter increment or logging (if global default drop logging is enabled).
bugs.conditions: VIP/SelfIP Default Action is set to Drop/Reject. Global Default Action is set to Drop and global rule logging is enabled. Traffic does not match any virtual or selfip.
bugs.impact: While there is no impact on the traffic that does not match virtual or Self IP (and is correctly being dropped), the issue is not updating any counters or logging (if enabled).
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When operating in firewall (AFM) mode i.e. default deny, the BIG-IP system will now count and log (if enabled) any traffic that does not match a Virtual or Self IP and is being dropped/rejected.

bugs.title: VXLAN daemon may restart when 8000 VXLAN tunnels are configured
bugs.symptoms: VXLAN daemon may restart when 8000 VXLAN tunnels are configured.
bugs.conditions: 8000 VXLAN tunnels are configured.
bugs.impact: VXLAN daemon restart.
bugs.fix: VXLAN daemon does not restart when 8000 VXLAN tunnels are configured.

bugs.title: Utility to parse LOP error entries
bugs.symptoms: When LOP (Lights Out Processor) communication errors occur and are logged in the LTM log, the log entries reference LOP Object IDs, result codes, etc. that are indecipherable (without source code access).
bugs.conditions: When the LOP is down or not responding for some reason.
bugs.impact: Lack of a means to decode the log entries prevents support engineers, BIG-IP administrators, etc. from performing initial triage of these errors to determine whether they can be safely ignored (e.g., relate to other errors logged or known conditions such as removal of a power supply), or require further investigation.
bugs.workaround: Currently, such questions can only be answered by opening a SR for analysis.
bugs.fix: Using the lopd_debug utility, one can easily decipher the error messages. # lopd_debug -h lopd_debug: [ -h ] Help : Display this message [ -f filename ] Parse File : Parse <filename> for LOP errors [ -S status# (hex) ] Status : Display the Status of LOP communication [ -a action# (hex) ] Action : Display the Action performed by LOP [ -o objectId# (hex) ] Object : Display the Object Id [ -s slotId# (hex) ] Slot : Display the Slot [ -r returnCode# (hex) ] Return Code : Display the Return Status of LOP communication

bugs.title: HTML rewriting on client side might be slow on large buffers for some operations
bugs.symptoms: The browser window appears to freeze for several seconds. Some Portal Access wrappers for client-side JavaScript code might use a slow version of HTML rewriting code. In earlier versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE), it can take more than a minute to process assignment of 2.5 MB of HTML code in JavaScript.
bugs.conditions: -- Using IE in compatibility mode. -- 1 MB of dynamic HTML generated by JavaScript on the client side.
bugs.impact: Pages accessed through Portal Access might not be responsive for several seconds.

bugs.title: APM config snapshot disappears and users see "Access Policy configuration has changed on gateway"
bugs.symptoms: In scenarios where there are multiple slots on a chassis in an HA pair (in both vCMP and chassis only mode), the error "Access Policy configuration has changed on gateway" might be displayed when a user connects to a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: It can occur in conditions when : - right after when the whole chassis is rebooted - secondary/slave slot's tmm cores. - disabling a slot on chassis
bugs.impact: Customer would see following message when they connect to virtual server "Access Policy configuration has changed on gateway"
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, type the command "bigstart restart apd" on the primary slot.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed by having the primary blade of the chassis/vCMP to recreate config snapshots if a secondary blade transitions from online to offline and vice versa.

bugs.title: iRule binary scan may core TMM when the offset is large
bugs.symptoms: Binary command does not check if the offset argument is beyond the internal buffer boundary, this may core TMM. Here is an example: binary scan [TCP::payload] @${offset_num}c var1 if "offset_num" is larger than payload buffer length, TMM may core.
bugs.conditions: Here is an example: binary scan [TCP::payload] @${offset_num}c var1 if "offset_num" is larger than payload buffer length, TMM may core.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Check payload length and compare with the offset argument before using the command.
bugs.fix: Check the offset value before moving the cursor.

bugs.title: Mac OS X support for nslookup and dig utilities to use VPN DNS
bugs.symptoms: Network access from browser or Edge Client on Mac does not change system DNS configuration the way that the nslookup and dig utilities expect. Once network access is established, the nslookup and dig utilities do not utilize DNS servers and DNS search suffixes set by SSL VPN.
bugs.conditions: NA access with DNS servers and DNS search suffixes, Network Access from browser or Edge Client on Mac OS X.
bugs.impact: The system should behave as expected except for the nslookup, dig, and host utilites.
bugs.fix: The nslookup, host and dig utilities are now able to use DNS server and DNS search suffixes set by SSL-VPN.

bugs.title: Under rare conditions, the TMM process may produce a core file and restart upon failover, with the Assertion 'laddr is not NULL' error message
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, you might encounter a situation in which tmm dumps a core, and the system writes to the logs a message similar to the following: notice panic: ../base/listener.c:1116: Assertion 'laddr is not NULL' failed.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that result in this error are unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time, but the system recovers without any user action.

bugs.title: TMSH crashes in rare initial tunnel configurations
bugs.symptoms: In rare BIG-IP configuration scenarios, TMM may crash during its startup process when the tunnel configurations are loaded.
bugs.conditions: During TMM startup, a tunnel is created, then immediately removed during the configuration load period, when TMM neighbor messages may be in flight via the tunnel. When the race condition fits, the neighbor message may land on an invalid tunnel.
bugs.impact: TMM crash in rare race conditions.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes on neighbor messages during the initial tunnel config load process.

bugs.title: tmsh: modify gtm server 'xxx' virtual-servers replace-all-with 'yyy' fails
bugs.symptoms: If you have a gtm server object for which you wish to modify its virtual servers, the following tmsh command fails: modify gtm server <gtm-server-name> virtual-servers replace-all-with <vs-name> with this error: "The requested Virtual Server (/Common/<gtm-server-name> ) was not found."
bugs.conditions: You have a gtm server object whose virtual servers you are attempting to modify via the replace-all-with method.
bugs.impact: You cannot set the virtual server(s) on a gtm server object via the replace-all-with method in tmsh.
bugs.workaround: You still can still add and delete virtual servers to the gtm server object via tmsh, you just cannot use the replace-all-with method to accomplish this.
bugs.fix: Fixed replace-all-with command in relation to GTM Virtual Servers.

bugs.title: Full webtop title is not localized
bugs.symptoms: Full webtop title is not localized, it is only showing F5 Dynamic Webtop.
bugs.conditions: This issue is always occuring.
bugs.impact: This issue is cosmetic and does not prevent work.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The full webtop title is now localized with APM.

bugs.title: APMD process core due to missing exception handling in execute agents
bugs.symptoms: APMD cores due to a missing exception handling in APMD while executing access policy agent.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using APM.
bugs.impact: APMD might core due to a missing exception handling in APMD while executing access policy agent.
bugs.fix: Processing is now provided for exceptions that could occur when using a Kerberos Auth agent in a multi-domain SSO configuration.

bugs.title: Cannot add vlans to whitelist if they contain a hyphen
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to add a vlan to the DoS protection whitelist and the vlan contains a hyphen, the following validation error is returned: 01071792:3: Vlan should be numeric form as vlan number / mask
bugs.conditions: Adding a vlan containing a hyphen to the whitelist
bugs.impact: Unable to add vlans that contain a hyphen
bugs.workaround: Instead of using the vlan by name, just specify the vlan tag #. Ignore the drop down menu offering the vlan names.

bugs.title: SWG Reports: Overview and Reports do not show correct data.
bugs.symptoms: When traffic is very sparse, the report may be incorrect and omit information due to skipped aggregation process of collected data. The original fix caused heavy spikes to the CPU every 5 minutes.
bugs.conditions: Very sparse traffic with significant gaps.
bugs.impact: AVR reports may be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Aggregation of data when traffic is very sparse with significant gaps is now done correctly, and also occurs when data is queried, instead of every 5 minutes in order to avoid a 5 minute CPU spiking issue.

bugs.title: HTML reserved characters not supported as part of SAML RelayState
bugs.symptoms: If the RelayState parameter includes HTML and XHTML special characters, then BIG-IP as IdP or BIG-IP as SP does not process them correctly, and does not send complete RelayState value to the Peer.
bugs.conditions: Using special characters
bugs.impact: SAML integration may not work properly with other products when configured RelayState parameter includes special characters.
bugs.workaround: To use reserved characters in HTML (",',&,<,>) as part of SAML RelaySate, convert them to their HTML entities (", ', &, <, >).
bugs.fix: When the BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP) or Service Provider (SP), it now URL encodes (or decodes, as applicable) the RelayState parameter.

bugs.title: Need proactive alerts for APM license usage
bugs.symptoms: Customer would like APM to generate proactive alerts when license usage reaches a certain threshold
bugs.impact: Without proactive alert, customer will not know that license consumption is near the maximum allowed and, hence, will not be prepared for the event of license being exhausted.
bugs.fix: Support for generating a license usage alert when a threshold is crossed has been added.

bugs.title: APM configurations can fail to load on newly-installed systems
bugs.symptoms: APM upgrades fail if the /shared/apm directory is not present before you load the configuration. APM writes a configuration loading error to the /var/log/ltm file with content similar to this: Oct 25 08:42:11 localhost notice mcpd[6311]: 0107165d:5: copy_file: EPSEC::In copy_file - src (/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/epsec_package_d/:Common:EPSEC:Images:epsec-1.0.0-160.0.iso_14866_1) dst (/shared/apm/images/epsec-1.0.0-160.0.iso) Oct 25 08:42:11 localhost notice mcpd[6311]: 0107165d:5: copy_file: Failed in file copy errno=(No such file or directory) .... 01071558:3: EPSEC - File Copy to /shared location failed Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: If the system is fresh from manufacturing or has had a recent formatting installation, it is vulnerable to this upgrade defect. The failure is only observed if the configuration being applied contains elements of APM.
bugs.impact: After booting into an upgraded system, the configuration will fail to load. A load failure can also be observed when manually loading a UCS file.
bugs.workaround: Create the directory /shared/apm and try to load the configuration again.
bugs.fix: Releases with this fix will load the configuration properly. There is no need for users to first create the /shared/apm directory.

bugs.title: BFD GTSM IMI shell commands don't work
bugs.symptoms: BFD GTSM IMI shell commands 'bfd gtsm enable' and 'bfd gtsm disable' commands are disabled and have no effect.
bugs.conditions: This problem shows up when BFD is configured, and attempt to configure GTSM feature of BFD.
bugs.impact: GTSM feature is not usable.

bugs.title: SAML SLO does not work if one of SLO Request URL, SLO Response URL not configured
bugs.symptoms: SAML Single Logout (SLO) does not work when all of the following are true: The BIG-IP system is acting as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP) or SAML Service Provier (SP); The other party configuration has SLO configured; The SP connector or IdP connector on the BIG-IP system is missing a SAML SLO Request URL or SAML SLO Response URL.
bugs.conditions: If SAML SLO is configured with SAML other party and other party does not have both SLO Request URL and SLO Response URL.
bugs.impact: SAML SLO does not work.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, configure both SAML SLO Request URL and SAML SLO Response URL for SP and IdP connectors.

bugs.title: SAML SSO might fail due to clock skew
bugs.symptoms: Other SAML Service Provider (SP) implementations might reject a SAML assertion generated by the BIG-IP system if the clock on the other system is running behind the clock on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured as SAML IdP. SAML SP is implemented by another vendor. Other vendor's implementation does not have clock skew tolerance. SP's clock is behind IdP's clock.
bugs.impact: SAML SSO might fail.
bugs.workaround: Adjust the clock on SP system to the time that is set on the BIG-IP system that acts as the SAML Identity Provider (IdP).

bugs.title: Ramcache handling of Cache-Control: no-cache directive in Response
bugs.symptoms: Previously, when a Cache-Control header from the OWS contained a no-cache directive, RAM Cache mistakenly interpreted that the same as a no-store directive.
bugs.conditions: Configure a virtual server with HTTP caching.
bugs.impact: Failure to cache a cachable document.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: RAM Cache will now cache the document, and then do a conditional get on each request (treating the document according to RFC 7234 semantics).

bugs.title: Management NIC speed reported as 'none'
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes,after mcpd get restarted, mcpd does not get management port NIC speed information from chmand; 'tmsh show net interface' might shows the speed of mgmt interface as 'none'.
bugs.conditions: Management interface is up, and then restart mcpd.
bugs.impact: The 'tmsh show net interface' commands cannot show correct management speed.
bugs.workaround: You can resolve this issue by restarting the chmand process. On appliances (BIG-IP platforms), run the following command: bigstart restart chmand. On VIPRION systems, run the following command: clsh "bigstart restart chmand".
bugs.fix: The tmsh utility now reliably displays the current media of the BIG-IP system's management port even if the mcpd daemon has restarted.

bugs.title: qkview files may contain truncated configuration files
bugs.symptoms: When running qkview, copies of the configuration files contained within the /config directory may be truncated if they are larger than 5 MB.
bugs.conditions: -- /config/bigip.conf is greater than 5 MB. -- Running qkview.
bugs.impact: Some configuration data may be missing when uploaded to iHealth.
bugs.workaround: Copy /config/bigip*.conf from the BIG-IP device and provide these files to the Support Engineer.

bugs.title: Disabling bundled interfaces affects first member of associated unbundled interfaces
bugs.symptoms: When the bundled interface (e.g., 2.1) is disabled, it might result in link issues observed with the first member of the associated unbundled interfaces (e.g., 1.1).
bugs.conditions: Disabling bundled interfaces affects first member of associated unbundled interfaces.
bugs.impact: Traffic unable to pass due to ports 'Down' status.
bugs.workaround: Do not disable the associated bundled interface (e.g., 2.1) when intending to use the first member of the associated unbundled interfaces (e.g., 1.1). Same for the interface bundle/unbundle relationships for 2.2/1.5, 2.3/1.9, vice-versa, etc.
bugs.fix: Disabling bundled interfaces no longer affects the first member of associated unbundled interfaces.

bugs.title: DTLS does not work with rfcdtls cipher on the B2250 blade
bugs.symptoms: DTLS does not work with rfcdtls cipher on the B2250 blade.
bugs.conditions: This occurs as a result of hardware acceleration offload on the B2250 blade when using dtls on vCMP.
bugs.impact: DTLS does not work with rfcdtls cipher on the B2250 blade

bugs.title: A monitor removed from GTM link cannot be deleted: 'monitor is in use'
bugs.symptoms: A monitor removed from GTM link cannot be deleted. Attempting to delete the monitor results in an error message similar to the following: 01070083:3: Monitor /Common/custom_gtm_mon is in use.
bugs.conditions: Deleting a custom monitor that was formerly used by a GTM link. 1. Create a custom GTM monitor that can be used on a link. 2. Create a GTM link, and add the custom monitor to it. 3. Remove the monitor from the link. 4. Attempt to delete the monitor.
bugs.impact: Unable to delete monitor.
bugs.workaround: Reload the GTM config and delete the monitor.
bugs.fix: This release enables deletion of a monitor removed from GTM link, and no monitor-in-use error message is returned.

bugs.title: Web applications might rewrite their event handlers
bugs.symptoms: Web applications might rewrite their event handlers.
bugs.conditions: If a web application edits event handlers dynamically.
bugs.impact: Event handlers might become corrupted.

bugs.title: APD crashes with a segmentation fault.
bugs.symptoms: Uninitialized CRLDP or OCSP field might cause a crash because of possible memory corruption.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is an uninitialized field in the Crldp or OCSP module.
bugs.impact: APD crashes with a segmentation fault. Uninitialized field might cause a crash trying to free the client connection.
bugs.fix: Crashes because of an uninitialized field in the CRLDP or OCSP module no longer occur.

bugs.title: New Event dialog widget is shifted to the left and Description field does not have action widget
bugs.symptoms: When you access Microsoft SharePoint 2013 through APM and use a rewrite profile, the rewritten New Event dialog box is shifted to the left and action widgets are not displayed above the Description field.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs in Internet Explorer 11 with meta http-equiv='X-UA-Compatible' content='IE=10'.
bugs.impact: SharePoint 2013 malfunctions.
bugs.workaround: You could potentially use an iRule to mitigate the problem.
bugs.fix: Portal Access now correctly displays a New Event window for Microsoft SharePoint 2013 from Internet Explorer 11.

bugs.title: TACACS log forwarder truncates logs to 1 KB
bugs.symptoms: TACACS log forwarder truncates logs to 1 KB.
bugs.conditions: When the log size is bigger than 1 KB.
bugs.impact: Log text will be truncated.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now allows up to an 8 KB log message size.

bugs.title: HTTP::retry doesn't work in an early server response
bugs.symptoms: If a HTTP_RESPONSE event fires due to the server sending an early response (i.e. a response before the entire request has been sent), then HTTP::retry does not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: Client begins sending a request. The server responds before that request is completely sent. A HTTP::retry is called in the HTTP_RESPONSE event.
bugs.impact: Typically, early server responses are error conditions.
bugs.workaround: HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect may be used at the cost of an extra client-side request.

bugs.title: Tmsh 'show sys hardware' displays Platform ID instead of platform name
bugs.symptoms: While running a version of BIG-IP older than the most recent release on a new hardware platform (recently purchased or recently acquired through RMA exchange), the 'tmsh show sys hardware' command may display the Platform ID code in place of the official F5 platform name. For example, the 'tmsh show sys hardware' command may display a Platform ID like the following: Platform Name D113 instead of the official platform marketing name, such as: Platform Name BIG-IP 10000F
bugs.conditions: This may occur if the version of BIG-IP software installed is not the most recent release, and the hardware platform is a newer variant (due to added hardware features or other manufacturing change) than was originally supported by the older BIG-IP software release. Note: The source of the platform information comes in a file: /etc/hal/MARKETING-NAMES. With each release, this file is updated to reflect the platforms available at time of release. The marketing-names package version serves as an identifier of the age of the marketing-names package.
bugs.impact: Custom automation scripts which depend on correctly matching F5 platform marketing names may fail to match the platform ID.
bugs.workaround: Update platform-identification scripts to include the relevant platform IDs among the recognized match values. Note: To get the newest marketing-names package, you must upgrade to a newer BIG-IP release, or specifically request an individual engineering hotfix to address the issue.
bugs.fix: The system now shows marketing names of platforms that were relatively current at the time of each release, but this issue might occur on any release. It is not possible to predict whether this issue will be present on a specific platform for a specific software version. This is true because the system relies on a specific file to provide all marketing names for BIG-IP platforms. That file might not be updated for every release, and additional hardware might be released after a software version is shipped. Therefore, you might have to use the platform designation rather than the marketing name in your custom automation scripts. Note: You can find marketing names of platforms here: K9476: The F5 hardware/software compatibility matrix :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K9476.

bugs.title: Oracle Access Manager 'Clear local Config Cache' button deletes incorrect config.cache file
bugs.symptoms: Pressing the 'Clear Local Config Cache' button on the Access :: Oracle Access Manager properties page, will delete the /config/aaa/oam/config.cache file.
bugs.conditions: When Oracle Access Manger is configured along with one or more AccessGates, the system generates a config.cache file under a file path that includes Partition and AccessGate name. For example, for an AccessGate named AccessGate1 configured in the /Common partition, the system generates a local cache file at the following path: /config/aaa/oam/Common/oampd/AccessGate1/config.cache. By default the system has a template cache file found at: /config/aaa/oam/config.cache.
bugs.impact: Pressing the 'Clear Local Config Cache' button will incorrectly delete the template file, but not the actual local config.cache generated for the configured AccessGate. Deletion of the template file has no impact to the admin or the system. However, since the system does not delete the correct file for a specific AccessGate, the system will not force Access Policy Manager to bootstrap the AccessGate, nor will it be reinitialized against the OAM access server.
bugs.fix: The 'Clear Local Config Cache' button has been removed from the Oracle Access Manager properties page, and has moved to the AccessGate Properties page. Additional handling was added to process the request and delete the appropriate local config.cache file for the specific AccessGate.

bugs.title: Remote logging of staged signatures and staged sets
bugs.symptoms: There is no option to see matched staged signature in the remote logging
bugs.conditions: A user has remote logger configured. There is no configuration option to see the stage signatures.
bugs.impact: A user without local logger can't make good decisions about the staged signatures
bugs.workaround: Add a local logger
bugs.fix: Added staged signatures ids, names and sets to the remote logger .

bugs.title: Erroneous 'FIPS open failed' error on platforms without FIPS hardware
bugs.symptoms: The following error may be logged on BIG-IP platforms which do not contain a FIPS hardware device: date_and_time hostname err iControlPortal.cgi[30667]: Checking for FIPS card.. FIPS open failed.
bugs.conditions: This error occurs when the iControl get_certificate_bundle function is invoked on BIG-IP platforms that do not contain a FIPS hardware device. The F5 Enterprise Manager product makes frequent use the iControl get_certificate_bundle function.
bugs.impact: This error message does not indicate a functional problem and should be ignored.
bugs.fix: The following error is no longer logged erroneously on BIG-IP platforms which do not contain a FIPS hardware device: date_and_time hostname err iControlPortal.cgi[30667]: Checking for FIPS card.. FIPS open failed.

bugs.title: ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers with hybrid certificate (RSA signed EC cert)
bugs.symptoms: ECDHE-ECDSA cipher does not work with hybrid certificate (RSA signed EC cert). Log files may indicate SSL handshake error or a 'no shared ciphers' error.
bugs.conditions: Using a hybrid certificate (RSA signed EC cert).
bugs.impact: ECDHE-ECDSA cipher does not work with hybrid certificate (RSA signed EC cert).
bugs.fix: The system now supports ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers with hybrid certificate (RSA signed EC cert).

bugs.title: Support RFC7919 Negotiated Finite Field Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral parameters
bugs.symptoms: RFC7919 Negotiated Finite Field Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral (FFDHE) parameters are not supported.
bugs.conditions: This affects ciphersuites that use Diffie–Hellman key exchange.
bugs.impact: Support for larger FFDHE groups will be chosen if offered by the client. There is an impact to performance versus previously chosen Diffie–Hellman 1024.
bugs.fix: RFC7919 Negotiated Finite Field Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral (FFDHE) parameters are now supported.
bugs.behavior: RFC7919 Negotiated FFDHE parameters are now supported. The FFDHE2048, FFDHE3072, FFDHE4096 keys are supported in this release. The default is DHE 2048 bits. In previous versions, the default DHE key size was 1024 bits. If you want to continue to use DHE 1024 you can enable db var tmm.ssl.dh1024, by default it is disabled. For more information, and for steps to use this feature, see K79342815: BIG-IP support for RFC7919 Negotiated Finite Field Diffie-Hellman Ephemeral (FFDHE) :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K79342815.

bugs.title: SSL proxy session ID cache does not respect limit set by tmm.proxyssl.cachesize
bugs.symptoms: After setting tmm.proxyssl.cachesize to a non-default value and restarting TMM, the new maximum size is not respected, either causing too many or too few entries to be retained. This can lead to memory exhaustion over time.
bugs.conditions: Proxy SSL feature enabled with non-default tmm.proxyssl.cachesize value set.
bugs.impact: The setting has no effect, so if it is being used to avoid low-memory conditions, the low-memory conditions persist.
bugs.fix: The tmm.proxyssl.cachesize and tmm.proxyssl.bucketcount settings are now respected when set and TMM has been restarted after the new values have been set.

bugs.title: Install of partial EPSEC file causes mcpd to crash, followed by multiple cores.
bugs.symptoms: Install of partial EPSEC file causes mcpd to crash, followed by multiple cores.
bugs.conditions: -- Attempt to upload a current EPSEC file. -- Upload stalls and appears hung. -- Close the web browser used for uploading epsec. -- Attempt to install the partially uploaded file.
bugs.impact: mcpd crashes, followed by multiple cores.
bugs.workaround: Upload the EPSEC file completely, and try the installation again.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now correctly handles incomplete or failed uploads of EPSEC software updates via the web admin GUI.

bugs.title: The HTTP Explicit Proxy and the SOCKS Proxy do not support AAAA address lookups
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP Explicit Proxy and the SOCKS Proxy do not support IPv6 AAAA DNS lookups. They ar limited to IPv4 DNS records. This will prevent IPv6-only addresses from being resolved.
bugs.conditions: The destination URI resolves to an IPv6-only address.
bugs.impact: The destination will be unreachable.
bugs.fix: The HTTP Explicit Proxy and the SOCKS proxy are now IPv6 address aware. The default is to attempt to resolve the IPv4 A record first, before trying the AAAA record.
bugs.behavior: The HTTP Explicit Proxy and the SOCKS proxy are now IPv6 address aware. The default is to attempt to resolve the IPv4 A record first, before trying the AAAA record.

bugs.title: Cannot load UCS from different BIG-IP system using Secure Vault
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP system uses in Secure Vault to encrypt secure fields, you cannot load that UCS to another BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a UCS originates on a BIG-IP system whose secure fields are encrypted using Secure Vault. The reason is that the Master Key to the Secure Vault has been encrypted with the Unit key of the originating BIG-IP system. The Unit key is unique to each system.
bugs.impact: UCS load fails.

bugs.title: Error when creating for reconfiguration iApp Application Services: Error parsing template:MCP call 'mcpmsg_set_string_item(msg, CID2TAG(m_cid), val.c_str())'
bugs.symptoms: Error when creating iApp Application Services for reconfiguration: Error parsing template:MCP call 'mcpmsg_set_string_item(msg, CID2TAG(m_cid), val.c_str())'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the configuration contains a very large number of items that the iApp Template might be querying for (for example, a large number of pools).
bugs.impact: Cannot create or modify application services. The system posts the error message: Error parsing template:MCP call 'mcpmsg_set_string_item(msg, CID2TAG(m_cid), val.c_str())' failed with error: 16908375, 01020057:3: The string with more than 65535 characters cannot be stored in a message.

bugs.title: CGNAT: iRules invoking LSN::pool for an lsn_pool that is not connected to a virtual server will not be able to use inbound connections
bugs.symptoms: lsn-pool inbound setting does not work when not associated with a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: lsn-pool with inbound or hairpinning enabled That lsn-pool is not associated with a virtual server but is assigned by an iRule.
bugs.impact: inbound and hairpinning is not enabled for subscribers using that lsn-pool when assigned via an iRule.
bugs.workaround: Create a virtual server for each lsn-pool.

bugs.title: The tcpdump utility may fail to capture packets
bugs.symptoms: Although packets are flowing correctly through the BIG-IP system, the tcpdump utility may capture no packets when certain command options are used.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - You configure tcpdump to listen for packets on a physical interface (e.g., -i 1.1). - You configure tcpdump to save the packets to a file in binary format (e.g., -w /var/tmp/example.pcap). - You configure tcpdump to produce verbose output while capturing packets (e.g., -v, -vv or -vvv).
bugs.impact: The tcpdump utility does not capture any packets, which may create confusion for a BIG-IP Administrator performing troubleshooting on the system. This issue does not affect the traffic-passing abilities of the system, however.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by starting the tcpdump utility without the -v, -vv or -vvv verbose output options.

bugs.title: JavaScript can misbehave in case of the 'X-UA-Compatible' META tag when a client uses IE11
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript can misbehave when encountering the 'X-UA-Compatible' META tag from clients using Microsoft Internet Explorer 11.
bugs.conditions: Internet Explorer 11 and meta http-equiv='X-UA-Compatible' content='IE=10'.
bugs.impact: Web application malfunction.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule.
bugs.fix: JavaScript now correctly handles the X-UA-Compatible meta tag from clients using Microsoft Internet Explorer 11.

bugs.title: DNS cache resolver TCP current connection stats not always decremented properly
bugs.symptoms: DNS cache resolver TCP current connection stats are not always decremented properly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when gathering statistics.
bugs.impact: Indirectly causes max connections to be wrong.
bugs.fix: DNS cache resolver TCP current connection stats are now decremented properly.

bugs.title: Session variables defined within the "Relay State" parameter of an SP initiated SSO session may fail.
bugs.symptoms: Session variables, such as, %{session.server.landinguri}, are not processes as part of Relay State parameter in BIG-IP SP service configuration.
bugs.conditions: Session variable configured as part of Relay State parameter in BIG-IP SP service configuration and SP initiated SAML SSO is used.
bugs.impact: Session variables are not processed
bugs.workaround: Do not use session variables inside Relay State configuration for BIG-IP SP service.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system SAML Service Provider (SP) service now supports and processes session variables as part of the RelayState parameter.

bugs.title: The msgAuthoritativeEngineBoots and msgAuthoritativeEngineTime values contained in SNMPv3 trap message may be incorrect after the SNMP agent reboot.
bugs.symptoms: After the reboot of the SNMP agent (snmpd), the SNMPv3 trap messages generated from the BIG-IP may contain the incorrect msgAuthoritativeEngineBoots and msgAuthoritativeEngineTime values. After that, msgAuthoritativeEngineBoots value will also be out of sync with the engineBoots value in /config/net-snmp/snmpd.conf.
bugs.conditions: Configure SNMPv3 trap destination on the BIG-IP system and observe the msgAuthoritativeEngineBoots and msgAuthoritativeEngineTime values in the generated trap messages. Reboot the SNMP agent (e.g., 'tmsh restart sys service snmpd') and observe these values again in the subsequent SNMPv3 trap messages.
bugs.impact: Some SNMP monitoring servers (e.g., SpectroSERVER) can lose the ability to poll the BIG-IP system. When the BIG-IP system sends out the incorrect values, the monitoring server thinks the information has been spoofed and it loses the ability to poll the BIG-IP until manual intervention.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Optical SFP modules shows a higher optical power output for disabled switch ports
bugs.symptoms: Some optical SFP/SFP+ modules may continue to provide optical power output higher than the specified detection threshold when the port has been disabled. As a result, the remote connected device may indicate a false positive link state.
bugs.conditions: The SFP or SFP+ module switch port has been disabled on the BIG-IP system. The problem occurs due to the optical transmitter in the SFP/SFP+ module not being disabled when the switch port itself is in a disabled state. The problem may occur with certain optical SFP/SFP+ modules, including all or a subset of individual modules with the following part numbers: OPT-0010-00 (1G-SR) OPT-0011-00 (1G-LR) OPT-0016-00 (10G-SR) OPT-0017-00 (10G-LR) For a list of F5 supported Fiber Gigabit Ethernet SFP, XFP, SFP+ and QSFP+ modules, see SOL6097: Specifications of the Fiber Gigabit Ethernet SFP, XFP, SFP+ and QSFP+ module ports on BIG-IP system platforms, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/6000/000/sol6097.html.
bugs.impact: Link status may be incorrectly reported as up on remote connected device.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, when disabling an affected switch port on the BIG-IP system, you can also disable the connected port on the remote device.
bugs.fix: Optical SFP/SFP+ modules now show the correct optical power output for disabled switch ports, which no longer attributes to false link states.

bugs.title: big3d might exit during loading of large configs or when a connection to mcpd is dropped.
bugs.symptoms: If big3d loses its connection to MCPD and cannot reconnect immediately, big3d retries too often and re-uses timer IDs incorrectly. This might result in a core dump with either SIGABRT or SIGSEV. One way this can happen is that while processing very large configs, the mcpd process does not respond to queries from the big3d process.
bugs.conditions: A large configuration file (for example, larger than 10 MB) or a very busy MCPD/control plane.
bugs.impact: big3d core errors.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Very large configuration files (for example, larger than 10 MB) or a very busy MCPD/control plane no longer causes big3d core errors.

bugs.title: clientssl profile has no key/cert pair
bugs.symptoms: After starting tmm, you notice the following critical error in /var/log/tmm, but the system otherwise boots and performs normally: crit tmm[11621]: 01260000:2: Profile profile-name: clientssl profile has no key/cert pair.
bugs.conditions: This can occur during start-up of tmm (usually during system boot-up).
bugs.impact: If the system otherwise performs normally (i.e., you do have the correct clientssl certificate installed), this error is benign; during initial start-up it is possible that the clientssl profile data has not yet been loaded at the right time. In this case the critical log message is misleading.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now logs a critical error 'clientssl profile has no key/cert pair' only if the clientssl profile truly does not have a certificate configured.

bugs.title: Data groups can be deleted even when in use by FIX profile
bugs.symptoms: A data group can be deleted even while it is referenced by an applied FIX profile.
bugs.conditions: A data group is referenced by a FIX profile and the data group is deleted.
bugs.impact: The FIX message receiver will not process messages.
bugs.workaround: Do not delete a data group that is referenced by a SIP profile. First change the configuration of all FIX profiles, removing any references to the data group, then delete the data group.

bugs.title: ERR_NOT_FOUND. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access_license.c, Function: access_read_license_settings, Line: 204
bugs.symptoms: The system posts this error: ERR_NOT_FOUND. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access_license.c, Function: access_read_license_settings, Line: 204.
bugs.conditions: This benign error occurs with an LTM Base license or APM standalone license in the following circumstances: -- APM is provisioned. -- License is upgraded. -- System is booted up or restarted.
bugs.impact: This error does not indicate any error condition, and you can safely ignore it.
bugs.fix: An error referencing the access_license.c file is no longer logged during provisioning, system startup, reboot, or license upgrade.

bugs.title: TMM may crash if fastl4 vs has fragmeneted pkt
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash if a fast L4 profile has a fragmented packet
bugs.conditions: fastl4 configure incoming fragmented packets
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: In fast L4 profile, enable option "Reassemble IP Fragments"
bugs.fix: Improved handling of a fragmented packet that could cause a crash if using a fastL4 profile.

bugs.title: Sensor critical alarm: Main board +0.9V_CN35XX
bugs.symptoms: TMOS may log a critical alarm for the 0.9 volt sensor even though the voltage is in the nominal range. Bug 447349 is a duplicate of this bug. The log message reads "Blade 0 hardware sensor critical alarm: Main board +0.9V_CN35XX voltage: 888 mV"
bugs.conditions: When the host is powered off using the AOM menu, the LBH will detect an under voltage condition for all non-standby voltage rails. This puts the sensors in the critical state. When the host powers the voltage rails turn on and the sensors transition back to the nominal state as the voltage rises. The 0.9 volt rail on some systems does not get high enough to clear the alert even though the voltage makes it into the nominal range.
bugs.impact: There will be a single ltm log message indicating this critical alarm, however the voltage reported in the log message will be in the nominal range.
bugs.workaround: Do not power cycle the host with the AOM menu. This error does not occur with an AC power cycle.
bugs.fix: The 7000 Series platform no longer reports a false positive sensor out-of-range error when the Host is powered off using the AOM.

bugs.title: Race condition in APM windows client on modifying DNS search suffix
bugs.symptoms: Race condition in APM client have a potential to leave "SearchList" registry key (DNS search suffix) in corrupted state.
bugs.conditions: Windows user connecting and disconnecting network access connection to BIG-IP APM.
bugs.impact: Windows can get incorrect DNS search suffix after using using network access connection to BIG-IP APM server. This issue is a race condition and may happen at random.
bugs.fix: Addressed race condition in APM client on modifying DNS search suffix on Windows-based systems.

bugs.title: LTM policies do not accept special characters in HTTP header names
bugs.symptoms: LTM policies do not accept special characters in HTTP header names.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when trying to use a '$' character in a header name.
bugs.impact: The system posts a validation error. For example, for the value $WSRA, the system posts the following message: 01071748:3: Policy '/Common/ft1_pool_select', rule 'notvar2'; invalid name, value '$WSRA'.

bugs.title: Import of Access Profile config that contains ssl-cert is failing
bugs.symptoms: An access profile configuration that uses an SSL Certificate fails to import. This happens because of a change in the method to import SSL certificates.
bugs.conditions: Access Profile configuration contains (SSL) Certificate File object, that is configurations that include OCSP responder, Certificate Authority Profile or ServerSSL Profile.
bugs.impact: Serious. It's not possible to import configs that contain above mentioned objects to another box, which might prevent users from distributing profiles manually or properly importing a backup/
bugs.workaround: You can either exclude above-\ mentioned objects prior to export and then recreate them after the import or (not recommended) edit the config manually and import the SSL certificate prior to import.
bugs.fix: You can import an access profile that includes an SSL certificate object in its configuration objects.

bugs.title: SAML SP service metadata exported from APM may fail to import.
bugs.symptoms: SAML SP service metadata exported from APM contains elements in incorrect order which might cause it to fail to be imported by other implementations.
bugs.conditions: When SAML metadata is exported from BIG-IP when it is acting as SAML Service Provider, the order of 'SingleLogoutService' and 'AssertionConsumerService' are not right.
bugs.impact: Import of SAML metadata with SAML IdP from BIG-IP as SP might fail.
bugs.workaround: Edit exported metadata: change the order of elements in the SPSSODescriptor so that SingleLogoutService element goes first in the sequence.
bugs.fix: SAML metadata elements are exported in correct order.

bugs.title: Issues using bigip1 as a device name, 'Can't save/checkpoint DB object' message
bugs.symptoms: Using 'bigip1' as a device name results in various unexpected behaviors. For example, when configuring high availability (HA), you might see the following error message: -- 01070710:3: Can't save/checkpoint DB object, class:devicegroup_device status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuring HA. -- Using 'bigip1' as the device name.
bugs.impact: Various unexpected behaviors, including that the system posts an error similar to the following: 01070710:3: Can't save/checkpoint DB object, class:devicegroup_device status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: Before configuring high availability, set the device name to something other than 'bigip1'. Otherwise, the configuration will not work as expected. The BIG-IP system reserves 'bigip1' as the factory default device name. Do not use 'bigip1' for device names in your configuration.

bugs.title: Web Services signature verification failed.
bugs.symptoms: Uploading an SSL certificate to the Web Services Security configuration may generate an error message. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- The Web Services signature verification fails. -- Uploading the client certificate to the BIG-IP system causes validation to fail, and the system generates an error message similar to the following example: Validation failed. Please upload valid .PEM file
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You are configuring the Web Service Security settings in an XML profile. -- You attempt to import client or server certificates into the BIG-IP ASM certificate pool.
bugs.impact: Web Services signature verification failed.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: PEM: CCR-U triggered by RAR during Gy session will have not have Requested Service Unit(RSU)
bugs.symptoms: When RAR message is triggered by OCS to reauthorize rating groups associated in the Gy session then corresponding CCR-U will not have any requested service unit (RSU)
bugs.conditions: RAR triggered by OCS and CCR-U will not have any RSU in the message for the rating group.
bugs.impact: if no RSU in the CCR-U then OCS may not grant correct quota for the rating groups.
bugs.workaround: here is no workaround at this time'
bugs.fix: Requested Service Unit (RSU) is present in the CCR-U triggered by OCS

bugs.title: APM does not support multimon and monitors custom properties for RDP resources
bugs.symptoms: Remote desktop (RDP) resources does not support the custom parameters "use multimon" and "span monitors".
bugs.conditions: Accessing RDP resources through APM.
bugs.impact: Cannot use multiple monitors when accessing RDP resources through APM.
bugs.fix: APM now supports custom parameters "use multimon" and "span monitors" for RDP resources when the resources are accessed through APM webtop. Note that this is supported only for native RDP clients.

bugs.title: Please avoid name "none" for branch rules
bugs.symptoms: Access policy visual policy editor item created with a branch caption of "none" cannot be opened or edited properly after being exported and re-imported.
bugs.conditions: A branch caption of "none" for an access policy visual policy editor item.
bugs.impact: Any access policy action.
bugs.workaround: In visual policy editor: Before you export an access policy, check for elements with caption "none" in branch rules and change the caption. To avoid this issue, refrain from using the name "none" for branch rules.

bugs.title: Support Email-Based Account Discovery through BIG-IP APM
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Email-Based Account discovery does not work when BIG-IP APM is used to proxy Citrix VDI.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM is configured in StoreFront integration mode.
bugs.impact: Email-Based Account discovery does not work
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now APM supports Email discovery for Citrix Receiver when configured as StoreFront proxy.

bugs.title: Web UI: iSession Profile properties page displays incorrect parent profile name.
bugs.symptoms: Local Traffic :: Profiles :: iSession Profile properties page displays incorrect parent profile name.
bugs.conditions: -- Viewing parent profile for an iSession profile. -- 'iSession' is set as parent profile . -- Another profile exists with name beginning from 'a' to 'h'.
bugs.impact: Incorrect information is displayed on the GUI even though the database has the correct information.
bugs.workaround: View the properties of iSession profile from tmsh.
bugs.fix: In the iSession properties page, GUI now sets the 'iSession' profile in Parent Profile dropdown list when 'iSession' is the parent profile. This matches the behavior of profiles other than 'iSession'.

bugs.title: PEM: CCR-U triggered during Gy session may not have Request Service Unit (RSU)
bugs.symptoms: CCR-U triggered by PEM when managing Gy session may not have Requested-service-unit (RSU) in the message.
bugs.conditions: When rating group is idle for a while and periodically quota request is sent after the timeout then this request will not Requested-Service-Unit (RSU) in the CCR-U message.
bugs.impact: If no RSU being encoded then OCS may not allocate right quota the the session.
bugs.workaround: there is no workaround at this time
bugs.fix: RSU is now being encoded in all rating groups in CCR-U except the one which are marked as Final reporting.

bugs.title: When log filters include tamd, tamd process may leak descriptors
bugs.symptoms: The log filter functionality in TMOS allows users to publish logs from a specific set of processes to various log destinations.
bugs.conditions: Configure log filter that includes tamd.
bugs.impact: Client authentication might fail. When a log filter includes tamd, the tamd process might start to leak descriptors.
bugs.workaround: Do not define log filters that include tamd (tamd is included in 'all').
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer sends tamd log messages to the configured remote log destinations.

bugs.title: Access Profile Type of SSO requires SSO configuration at create time
bugs.symptoms: If you start to create an Access Profile and you set the Profile Type to SSO, you cannot complete the configuration from the New Profile screen unless an SSO configuration already exists.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to create a new Access Profile of Type SSO without having an existing SSO to select.
bugs.impact: Cannot create a new Access Profile of Type SSO until an SSO Configuration has been created and then selected for use within Access Profile.
bugs.workaround: To work around this problem, you can create an SSO Configuration prior to creating the new Access Profile of Type SSO.

bugs.title: DNS Filtering driver causes crash/BSOD
bugs.symptoms: DNS Relay proxy service causing Client App tunnel crash or BSOD (DRIVER_FAULT).
bugs.conditions: Using DNS relay filtering driver in Windows XP SP3.
bugs.impact: Client App tunnel crash/BSOD. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.fix: Fixed BSOD caused by DNS relay filtering driver in very specific condition on Microsoft Windows XP SP3.

bugs.title: Network Firewall event logs page pops up date/time picker automatically during drag-and-drop
bugs.symptoms: Network Firewall event logs page pops up date/time picker automatically during drag-and-drop of the time field in the table to the custom search area.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in AFM when dragging and dropping a time from the log event list table
bugs.impact: Datetime picker pops up automatically
bugs.fix: Datetime picker no longer pops up date/time picker during drag and drop.

bugs.title: Node flapping may, in rare cases, lead to inconsistent persistence behavior
bugs.symptoms: If persistence is used, and a node is marked down and then up in quick succession (less than about 7 seconds), then persistence may act inconsistently (meaning, not all connections expected to persist to a server will do so). Further requests in certain circumstances may hang (the client will be left waiting for a response).
bugs.conditions: Persistence, rapid node flapping, new connection (via a TMM with an existing connection) after node has been re-marked as up.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent persistence behaviors. If persistence records are examined, you might find multiple, conflicting entries. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.workaround: Add an iRule command to the PERSIST_DOWN event that deletes the persistence entry for this connection. One example might be: when PERSIST_DOWN { persist delete source_addr [IP::client_addr] } For more information, see SOL14918: Node flapping may cause inconsistent persistence records, available here: http://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/900/sol14918.html.
bugs.fix: The system now deletes a persist entry from all peer TMMs when it is deleted in any TMM, so no conflicts occur.

bugs.title: Brute Force Login
bugs.symptoms: In this release, you can configure the Brute Force Login protection with more granular detection rates.
bugs.conditions: Low traffic environment that typically sees less than 1 login failure per second but still wishes to trigger Brute Force prevention.
bugs.impact: Unable to appropriately configure Brute Force prevention.
bugs.fix: To improve brute force mitigation, we made the following changes: -We added a new internal parameter: bf_num_sec_per_value. This defines how many seconds is a single measure unit for a failed login. For example, if you want to configure 7 failed logins per 5 seconds, in the Configuration utility configure "7" as the threshold value (the "Failed Login Attempts Rate reached" setting in the Detection Criteria area of the Brute Force Protection Configuration screen), and from the command line configure "5" as the value of this internal parameter. If this value is configured, the system will detect an attack only by the threshold (and not by the increase). If this value is configured, all traffic from suspicious IP addresses are blocked. The default value for the internal parameter is 1 second. -In the Configuration utility, we removed the validation for all the threshold and minimal values. You can put now very low values such as 1 or 2 in the detection and suspicious criteria.

bugs.title: HTML5 VMware View Client does not work with APM when Virtual Server is on non-default route domain
bugs.symptoms: HTML5 VMware View Client does not work with APM when Virtual Server is on non-default route domain.
bugs.conditions: HTML5 VMware View client is used on APM Webtop to access VMware View desktops through a Virtual Server that is on non-default route domain.
bugs.impact: HTML5 VMware View Client does not work.
bugs.fix: HTML5 VMware View Client now works with APM when the virtual server is on a non-default route domain.

bugs.title: IPv6 link-local vlan tag handling incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Validation is not allowing IPv6 link-local address with vlan tag
bugs.conditions: Trying to create IPv6 link-local with vlan tag notation, or bits in the second group of the IPv6 address.
bugs.impact: When trying to use the same IPv6 address on multiple vlans
bugs.workaround: Put the desired IPv6 link-local address with the vlan tag notation in bigip_base.conf, and run "tmsh load sys config"
bugs.fix: Validation now allows IPv6 link-local address with %vlan notation.
bugs.behavior: It's no longer possible to use %vlan notation with non-link-local IPv6 address as object name.

bugs.title: PEM:Initial quota request in the rating group request is not as configured.
bugs.symptoms: When quota request is being sent for the rating group for the first time the initial quota request in the request is not as configured.
bugs.conditions: Quota request for a rating group is sent for the first time for the session and initial quota request for the rating group not as configured.
bugs.impact: If not initial quota request then OCS may not allocate right quota for the the session.
bugs.workaround: here is no workaround at this time
