bugs.fix: Initial quota request is sent the request for quota as configured.

bugs.title: iApp creation fails with non-admin users
bugs.symptoms: This error message may occur when Application Editor or Manager users try to create an iApp instance: Error parsing template:Tcl_Init failed: (invalid command name "file" while executing "file join $i init.tcl" (procedure "tclInit" line 21) invoked from within "tclInit" line:46)
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when an iApp instance is being created by a non-admin user. Application Editor and Manager users have been specifically tested.
bugs.impact: The iApp creation fails.
bugs.workaround: iApp creation will succeed if performed by an admin user.
bugs.fix: iApp creation by non-admin users previously could fail with this error: Error parsing template:Tcl_Init failed: (invalid command name "file" while executing "file join $i init.tcl" (procedure "tclInit" line 21) invoked from within "tclInit" line:46) This no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Javascript: getAttribute() returns mangled event handlers
bugs.symptoms: All event handlers in HTML page are rewritten by APM. If some script uses getAttribute() call to obtain event handler code, it gets rewritten code. This may lead to incorrect results.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with event handlers defined.
bugs.impact: If a script uses event handler source code, it might work incorrectly.

bugs.title: Client certificate SSL authentication unable to bind to LDAP server
bugs.symptoms: When LDAP Client Certificate SSL Authentication is configured to bind to the LDAP server with a password, the bind fails due to an incorrect password.
bugs.conditions: LDAP client certificate SSL authentication enabled LDAP server requires password to bind
bugs.impact: Client certificates cannot be authenticated
bugs.fix: LDAP client certificate SSL authentication sends correct bind password to LDAP server

bugs.title: Discrepancy between Throughput and Detailed Througput data
bugs.symptoms: Discrepancy between Throughput and Detailed Throughput graphs.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include vCMP guest with ePVA virtual servers in guest.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is a discrepancy between Throughput and Detailed Througput graphs.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: ePVA statistics is included with the Throughput data to accurately match Detailed Throughput data.

bugs.title: Citrix Receiver for Linux is unable to receive full applications list.
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receiver for Linux shows only a part of applications list when connecting to APM.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix Replacement and Citrix Receiver for Linux is used.
bugs.impact: Citrix Receiver for Linux shows only a part of applications list.

bugs.title: System does not reconnect to SafeNet HSM if connection is interrupted
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not reconnect to SafeNet HSM if the connection is interrupted. That means that SSL connections that utilize a key stored on the network HSM fail.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the BIG-IP system is configured to use a SafeNet network HSM and the connection between the BIG-IP system and the network HSM is interrupted.
bugs.impact: When this occurs, the system experiences traffic interruptions for SSL connections that utilize a key stored on the network HSM until manual corrective action is taken.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, restart the pkcs11d process using the command 'tmsh restart sys service pkcs11d'.

bugs.title: Different time-stamps are translated to the same time (due to DST clock change) and causes database errors
bugs.symptoms: Due to DST (Daylight Savings Time) - Different timestamps can be translated to the same (local) time
bugs.conditions: DST clock change has occurred
bugs.impact: Analytics database cannot create new partition after DST clock change
bugs.fix: Appending the time-stamp to the partition name, so that if time is the same, the time-stamp will make the partition name different.

bugs.title: Portal access resource item modifications are not synced
bugs.symptoms: This issue is seen with policies that use Portal Access with any resource item. If the policy is synced for the first time, all the corresponding resources are seen to be synced correctly to the target. However, if the resource item is modified and we try to sync again, the resource item modifications are not synced over to the target devices.
bugs.conditions: The following conditions are necessary to trigger this issue. The policy should have portal access resource and the resource item should have been modified before syncing the same policy again.
bugs.impact: Resource item modifications are not synced over to the target devices.
bugs.fix: A user can now sync the changes to all location-specific objects, such as, optimized-app in network-access, or pool item in pool, after setting the Use Source Configuration on Target option to YES in the policy sync dialog box.

bugs.title: Connection to a Self IP to network HSM may not be established after the BIG-IP system reboots.
bugs.symptoms: SSL connections or DNSSEC operations that utilize a key stored on the network HSM may fail.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured to use a network HSM. The BIG-IP system connects to the network HSM using a Self IP address. The BIG-IP system is rebooted or all of the BIG-IP services are restarted.
bugs.impact: Traffic interruptions for SSL connections or DNSSEC operations that utilize a key stored on the network HSM until manual corrective action is taken.
bugs.workaround: Restart the pkcs11d process. The command is "tmsh restart sys service pkcs11d".

bugs.title: APM policy sync resulting in failover device group sync may make the failover sync fail
bugs.symptoms: If an APM policy sync puts the new policy on a member of a sync-failover device group then the sync of the sync-failover group may fail.
bugs.conditions: * At least three devices in trust. * Two devices in a sync-failover device group. * Two devices in a sync-only device group suitable for APM policy sync. * The policy is synchronized from a device that is not in the sync-failover device group.
bugs.impact: Sync will fail, but full load sync will then succeed.
bugs.workaround: Using a full load sync (the force option on the GUI sync page) will work.
bugs.fix: If an APM policy sync puts the new policy on a member of a sync-failover device group then the sync of the sync-failover group used to fail. This now succeeds.

bugs.title: Order of members in AAA server pools now show in reverse order of Priority Group
bugs.symptoms: Members of AAA server pools are listed in increasing order of priority group. This shows the node most likely to be serving current requests at the bottom of the list.
bugs.conditions: Viewing pool members in the list.
bugs.impact: Potential confusion when viewing of pool members, potentially counter-intuitive.
bugs.fix: Now, the nodes of a AAA pool are shown in decreasing order of priority group, which places the node currently serving requests at the top of the list.
bugs.behavior: Order of members in AAA server pools now show in reverse order of Priority Group.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as SP fails to report unsupported key transport algorithms when processing encrypted assertions
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP system configured as a Service Provider (SP) supports only rsa-oaep for key transport (http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#rsa-oaep-mgf1p). When the BIG-IP system configured as SP receives a SAML assertion with an unsupported encryption algorithm (for example, rsa-1_5 for key transport instead of rsa-oaep), the BIG-IP system fails to report that algorithms are unsupported, and proceeds to the decryption phase, which fails. The only issue here is the error reported does not directly point to the cause of failure which makes troubleshooting more difficult.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system configured as an SP receives a SAML assertion that is encrypted or contains encrypted attributes.
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting could take longer.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Missing SNMP alerts for Virtual Server enabled/disabled.
bugs.symptoms: When user enables or disables a virtual server, the SNMP traps do not exist. However, when virtual server changes up/down state due to pool member monitoring, the traps exist.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system configured for sending SNMP traps.
bugs.impact: SNMP traps when a user manually enables/disables virtual servers are not sent.

bugs.title: NTLM authentication does not work due to incorrect NetBIOS name
bugs.symptoms: Internally, the BIG-IP system assumes that the NetBIOS name always matches the prefix of the DNS name. For example, if the domain name is sales.company.com, then the NetBIOS name must be SALES. If the NetBIOS name does not meet this assumption, NTLM and/or Kerberos front-end authentication never work even when configured correctly. Under a Disjoint Namespace Scenario deployment, the NetBIOS name and prefix of the DNS name do not match, and the BIG-IP system cannot establish an SCHANNEL with the Active Directory server.
bugs.conditions: NetBIOS name does not match with the suffix of the DNS name.
bugs.impact: NTLM front-end authentication does not work as there is no SCHANNEL to Active Directory which can be used to verify the user's credentials.
bugs.workaround: Change the ActiveDirectory deployment to match its NetBIOS and DNS name.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP 11.6.0 HF6 introduced the Apm.NetBIOS.DomainName db variable as a global NetBIOS domain name. When the variable is defined with a non-default value, that value will be used as NetBIOS domain name during configuration. When the variable is defined with the default value (which is "<null>"), then APM reverts to extracting NetBIOS domain name from FQDN. This means when this db variable is set with a non-default value, only one NetBIOS domain is usable. Note: Support for the Apm.NetBIOS.DomainName db variable is discontinued in version 12.0.0 and later. For BIG-IP 12.0.0, when you create a Machine Account in APM, APM performs a domain join, retrieves the NetBIOS domain name from the Active Directory server, stores it in the configuration, and uses it for NTLM authentication. To use the new behavior, delete the existing machine account and recreate it. Otherwise, the machine account continues to obtain the NetBIOS name the way it did before version 12.0.0.

bugs.title: When IKEv2 is in use, user can only associate one Traffic Selector object with the IKE Peer object
bugs.symptoms: Only one Traffic Selector can be associate with one IKE Peer when IKEv2 is in use.
bugs.conditions: When IKEv2 is selected to negotiate IPsec Tunnel
bugs.impact: User can only associate one Traffic Selector per IKE Peer
bugs.fix: User can associate multiple Traffic Selector MCP objects with one IKE Peer object

bugs.title: Monitors removed from a pool after sync operation
bugs.symptoms: Monitors might be removed from a pool after sync operation.
bugs.conditions: If devices are in a failover device group, and this group contains a pool with multiple health monitors enabled, then using the 'Overwrite Configuration' option.
bugs.impact: Monitors might be removed from a pool on the devices that received a sync.
bugs.fix: Monitors are no longer removed from a pool on the devices that received a sync.

bugs.title: Response Logging generates a blank $HTTP_STATUS response when used with certain iRule commands.
bugs.symptoms: Response Logging generates a blank $HTTP_STATUS response when used with certain iRule commands.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: A virtual server with Response Logging configured has an iRule assigned that uses either the HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect command. The Request Logging profile gives you the ability to specify the data and format for HTTP requests and responses that you want to include within the log file. Parameters, such as $HTTP_STATUS, are used to specify information that is included within the log file. The HTTP::respond and HTTP::redirect iRule commands allow you to customize the response sent to the client and are intended to run immediately when triggered. Therefore, no further processing of response data should occur. As a result, the system logs blank status information when using the $HTTP_STATUS parameter within the Request Logging profile for Response Logging.
bugs.impact: The system logs invalid information. As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom: -- BIG-IP iHealth lists Heuristic H465653 on the Diagnostics :: Identified :: Medium screen. If $HTTP_STATUS is used within the Response Logging template, the output will be blank.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can use the iRule to generate the required logs, rather than the Request Logging profile. If an iRule is calling HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect, you can log directly from that iRule using the log iRule command, and record parts of the old response, or the new one, depending on what is required.

bugs.title: Default port should be removed from Location header value in http redirect
bugs.symptoms: Browser recognizes page loaded with URL without default port and page loaded after receiving Location header that contains rewritten URL with default port included in it as different pages and loads page twice.
bugs.conditions: Resource is loaded through Portal Access; page is loaded after receiving Location header with default port included in rewritten part; navigation occurs to this page without default port in domain part (for example, to anchor in this page).
bugs.impact: Resource is loaded twice and this can possibly change behavior of backend.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: TMM cores dumps due to an iSession "valid event" assertion failure
bugs.symptoms: An APM network access tunnel abort causes TMM to core dump due to an iSession 'valid event' assertion failure.
bugs.conditions: An APM network access tunnel is aborted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Empty X-WA-Surrogate header in WAM symmetric deployment
bugs.symptoms: In WAM symmetric deployment, the X-WA-Surrogate header is used to communicate OWS lifetime values from the central device to the remote. In some cases, an empty X-WA-Surrogate header may be sent.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when central originates a 304 response when the original response from OWS does not contain cache-control headers.
bugs.impact: This occurs only when OWS sends no cache-control headers, so the remote still computes the correct lifetime, making the impact minimal.

bugs.title: Added DB Variable to configure 'difok' variable in password policy
bugs.symptoms: The difok variable enforces the number of characters that must differ between a user's old password and new password. Prior to this release, the number of characters that must differ was not configurable, and just stayed at the default value.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure a required number of characters a new password must differ from the old.
bugs.impact: The number of characters that were required to differ between an old and new password were set by default and could not be configured.
bugs.fix: This release adds a db variable that allows for configuration of the difok variable from TMSH using the command: modify /sys db password.difok value <value>

bugs.title: Unknown BigDB variable type 'port_list'
bugs.symptoms: You see the following in /var/log/ltm: notice dag.roundrobin.udp.portlist: Unknown BigDB variable type 'port_list' This can also be observed by running tmsh modify sys db dag.roundrobin.udp.portlist value A tmm crash could also occur if it is doing round robin load balancing of udp and attempts to load balance a fragmented udp payload.
bugs.conditions: The error will occur when tmm starts.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP will now recognize dag.roundrobin.udp.portlist

bugs.title: New connections may be reset when a client reuses the same port as it used for a recently closed connection
bugs.symptoms: If a client reuses the same port that it used for a recently closed connection, the new connection may receive a RST in response to the client's SYN.
bugs.conditions: A client reuses the same port that it used for a recently closed connection. The 4-tuple of local address, local port, remote address, and remote port must be the same to trigger this issue.
bugs.impact: New connections reusing a 4-tuple may be reset for a brief period following a connection close.
bugs.workaround: Lowering the "Close Wait" and "Fin Wait 1" timeouts in the TCP profile will shorten the amount of time that a particular 4-tuple remains unusable.
bugs.fix: Improved abort handling to better clean up hanging connections.

bugs.title: TMSH incorrectly shows the 'Expires' date for ramcache profile on server content with an expiry date greater than or equal to year 2038.
bugs.symptoms: The command "tmsh show ltm profile ramcache" shows an incorrect 'Expires' date for content whose correct expiry date is after the year 2038.
bugs.conditions: A Virtual Server is configured with the ramcache profile and request content from the server contains an expiry date >= year 2038
bugs.impact: When you run 'tmsh ltm profile ramcache', the Expires date is incorrect. There is no operational impact.

bugs.title: qkview might loop writing output file if MCPD fails during execution
bugs.symptoms: If qkview is executed, and while it is executing, a problem arises with MCPD, it is possible that qkview may enter a loop where it continually writes the following lines to the file ./mcp_module.xml: end_transaction.
bugs.conditions: 1. qkview is run while mcpd is executing properly. 2. mcpd enters unstable state while qkview is running.
bugs.impact: Disk can fill up, causing a system failure.
bugs.workaround: Do not run qkview if mcpd has been acting unpredictably.
bugs.fix: Qkview MCP module has been corrected to prevent qkview from looping infinitely when failing to connect to MCPD.

bugs.title: Sweeper incorrectly reaps a flow that had matched global (or rtdom) rule with action 'Accept Decisive' after the latest firewall configuration change
bugs.symptoms: Sweeper incorrectly reaps a flow that matches a rule in either global or corresponding route-domain classifier with action = Accept Decisive in the scenario when this particular classifier did not change (and there are no matching rules in the corresponding VIP/SelfIP classifier and VIP/SelfIP default action is set to Drop or Reject).
bugs.conditions: AFM is enabled and configured in Default Deny mode. A flow matches a global (or route domain) rule with action set to Accept Decisively at time of flow creation. However, this flow also does not match any VIP/SelfIP rule Later, a firewall policy change triggers Kill-on-the-Fly sweeper to re-evaluate all the existing connections against new firewall configuration that results in this undesired behavior.
bugs.impact: This incorrect behavior would result in legitimate existing connections being dropped after a firewall policy configuration change (that are supposed to be accepted in firewall configuration).
bugs.workaround: AFM Kill-on-the-fly feature (in sweeper) can be disabled using the db variable - tm.sweeper.flow.acl

bugs.title: sso and apm split tunnelling log message is at notice level
bugs.symptoms: This split tunnelling log message is written at the notice level: "Username used for SSO contains domain information. Please enable 'Split domain from full Username' option in the Logon Page if domain info should be separated from username for SSO to work properly".
bugs.conditions: Username used for SSO contains domain information
bugs.impact: logged at notice level for each request in /var/log/apm
bugs.fix: This split tunnelling log message is no longer written at the notice level: "Username used for SSO contains domain information. Please enable 'Split domain from full Username' option in the Logon Page if domain info should be separated from username for SSO to work properly" The log is now written at the informational level.

bugs.title: Apply Policy Fails After Policy Diff and Merge
bugs.symptoms: Merging global extractions with references to URLs or File Types from one security policy to another introduces a data inconsistency that prevents Apply Policy actions on the target policy.
bugs.conditions: A security policy with global extractions that has references to URLs or File Types is merged to another security policy.
bugs.impact: A data inconsistency is introduced that prevents Apply Policy actions on the target policy.
bugs.workaround: Remove the extractions from the list of found changes before using auto-merge, and add the extraction manually if desired.
bugs.fix: Global extractions now merge correctly using Policy Diff.

bugs.title: Upgrade from some versions to 11.6.0 can fail with APM rewrite profile
bugs.symptoms: Configuration will not load. BIG-IP system is nonfunctional after upgrade to 11.6.0. Log message: Configuration error: cannot attach profile (/Common/rewriteplugin) to virtual server (/Common/apm_virtual_server)
bugs.conditions: This happens on upgrade from 11.4.1 to 11.6.0.
bugs.impact: As a result, the site is down after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, manually edit bigip.conf to remove: /Common/rewriteplugin { } from the Virtual Server configuration stanza.

bugs.title: TMM can crash when a large number of SSL objects are created
bugs.symptoms: Administrative operations which trigger a full reload of SSL cert, key, or CRL files can cause TMM to abort. TMM will miss its heartbeat, at which time it will be killed by sod daemon via SIGABRT.
bugs.conditions: Configuration contains a large number of SSL certs, keys and/or CRLs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove any unused SSL objects from configuration.
bugs.fix: The system now loads the virtual IP addresses and associated SSL Certs/Keys in batches, so that TMM config load no longer exceeds its allowed CPU time.

bugs.title: Newly added or updated signatures are erroneously added to Manual user-defined signature sets.
bugs.symptoms: You encounter unexpected violation when you assign a user defined signature to an unblocking signature set.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the signature is added to another blocking signature set simultaneously.
bugs.impact: 'Unexpected' violation occurs
bugs.fix: Newly added or updated signatures are no longer erroneously added to Manual user-defined signature sets that were created by policy import.

bugs.title: BIG-IP 2000/4000: Source port on NAT connections are modified when they should be preserved
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system is modifying the source port on NAT connections.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when NAT is configured on the BIG-IP system. This occurs on BIG-IP 2000/4000 hardware platforms.
bugs.impact: This impacts any applications where the source port is expected to be preserved.
bugs.fix: The source port is always preserved for NAT connections.
bugs.behavior: The source port is always preserved for NAT connections.

bugs.title: Partition behavior of iApps corrected
bugs.symptoms: Since v11.4.0, iApps have looked for the non-existence of '/Common/cookie' as the indicator of Edge licensing, since cookie persistence is not provided with Edge Gateways. This test reads incorrectly if the iApp is run from a partition other than /Common, and has been replaced with a direct test for the appropriate license features.
bugs.impact: This test reads incorrectly. The iApp reports an error and fails to configure.
bugs.workaround: To workaround, make a copy of the iApp template and change two instances of the 'set is_edge' statement to 'set is_edge 0'.
bugs.fix: Certain iApps now operate normally when executed from an administrative partition other than /Common.
bugs.conditions: Using partition other than /common on BIG-IP systems in association with the following iApps: -- f5.http -- f5.bea_weblogic -- f5.sap_erp -- f5.peoplesoft_9 -- f5.sharepoint_2010 -- f5.dns -- f5.diameter -- f5.radius -- f5.ldap -- f5.oracle_ebs -- f5.microsoft_iis.

bugs.title: UCS archive restore causes file duplication in filestore
bugs.symptoms: UCS archive restoration process duplicates files if there is already an existing file with same version. This causes UCS archives to increase in size during subsequent archive / restoration process.
bugs.conditions: Here is an example of how this might occur: 1.) On two APM-configured devices (unit A, unit B), with the same software version and same EPSEC version. 2.) Create a UCS on unit A, and restore that UCS to unit B. 3.) The system duplicates the EPSEC version from unit B.
bugs.impact: UCS created is larger by the size of the duplicated file (in the example, the UCS is approximately 30 MB larger because it contains two copies of EPSEC).
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: monpd core dumps in case of MySQL crash
bugs.symptoms: When MySQL crashes, the monpd process creates a core dump.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when MySQL crashes or does not start correctly.
bugs.impact: Reports not available for the duration of MySQL going down.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue where monpd would intermittently do a core dump due to a MySQL crash, and reports would not be available during the crash.

bugs.title: Event Correlation is not enabled on vCMP guests if the disk is SSD.
bugs.symptoms: The event correlation page says "event correlation not supported on this platform"
bugs.conditions: This can occur when looking at event correlation on VCMP guests.
bugs.impact: Event correlation does not work on VCMP guests.
bugs.fix: Event Correlation is now enabled on vCMP guests if the disk is SSD, but only if the host is running BIG-IP version 11.6.0 HF4 or later.

bugs.title: Trunk remains down and interface's status is 'uninit' after mcpd restart
bugs.symptoms: Trunk down and interface's status is 'uninit' and log files indicate mcpd restarted.
bugs.conditions: This occurs upon mcpd restart on 2000/4000 series platform.
bugs.impact: Failover as a result of mcpd restart. Trunks are unable to pass traffic. The interface that report the status 'uninit' are able to pass traffic after mcpd and related services restart; the message is cosmetic only.
bugs.workaround: Run the command: tmsh restart sys service pfmand. The restart of pfmand helps update the interface status, which in turn helps update the trunk status.
bugs.fix: Trunk now comes up without error messages after mcpd restarts on 2000/4000 series platforms.

bugs.title: Enable change password within vmview client when password doesn't meet the AD policy requirements
bugs.symptoms: Previously VMWare View client hung/disconnected if the attempt to change an expired password had failed due to the AD policy requirements.
bugs.conditions: User's password is expired but the new password provided doesn't meet the policy requirements.
bugs.impact: VMWare View client freezes/hangs, user gets confused.
bugs.fix: Improved VMware View native client error reporting and prompting for the new password.

bugs.title: SWG is seen on platforms with less than 8 GB of memory
bugs.symptoms: Although there is a tmsh provision command shown for Secure Web Gateway (SWG) on platforms with less than 8 GB of memory, running the command fails because there is no support for SWG on those platforms.
bugs.conditions: This applies to certain BIG-IP appliances that have less than 8 GB of memory, and to vCMP and VE guests with less than 8 GB of memory allocated. (For memory information, see the Platform Guide for your platform.)
bugs.impact: Provisioning fails with a message similar to the following: Provisioning failed with error 1 - 'Memory limit exceeded. 5656 MB are required to provision these modules, but only 3964 MB are available.'
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to provision SWG on platforms with less than 8 GB of memory.

bugs.title: ConfigSync failing with sFlow error
bugs.symptoms: An sFlow error may occur during sync of a device.
bugs.conditions: Exact conditions are unknown and difficult to reproduce, but some possible conditions include sync operations following delete/create of a virtual server or profiles (either directly or by deleting/creating an iApp), sync following failover
bugs.impact: Sync might fail, which can impact connection mirroring, and other system operations. The system posts an sflow message similar to the following: 'Can't save/checkpoint DB object, class:sflow_http_virtual_data_source status:13'.
bugs.workaround: Force the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration. For more information, see SOL13030, Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration, available here: Link: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/000/sol13030.html.
bugs.fix: Sync now completes successfully, without sflow error.

bugs.title: Support RDP connections to arbitrary servers from APM Webtop
bugs.symptoms: VDI RDP resources must be statically defined by the administrator; end users connecting to the APM Webtop are unable to define their own RDP connections.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when accessing RDP resources from the Webtop.
bugs.impact: End users wanting to connect to an RDP resource not explicitly listed on the webtop are unable to configure a connection.
bugs.fix: An RDP resource of type "User defined" has been added to APM. If you add this as a resource, end users will be able to specify their own RDP resources to connect to.

bugs.title: Lifetime heuristic behavior changes between 10.x and 11.x
bugs.symptoms: In version 10.x, lifetime heuristic runs on auto-pilot, that is, PVAC calculates the heuristic cache lifetime when 1) there is no OWS Cache-Control values or, 2) all honored OWS Cache-Control directives are absent. In v11.x, WebAccelerator (WA)/Application Acceleration Manager (AAM) use heuristic cache lifetime in these two cases, and there is no WebAccelerator Cache Settings Maximum Age configured.
bugs.conditions: This is observable when using WA/AAM and comparing lifetime heuristic behavior in versions 10.x and 11.x.
bugs.impact: The behavior differs.

bugs.title: APM form-based SSOv1 values allows url encoding of some special characters like '-'
bugs.symptoms: In APM form-based SSO, some special characters are incorrectly URL-encoded for certain fields, such as hidden parameters. (This does not apply to form-based client-initiated SSO.)
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using form-based SSO with a hidden parameter that contains a special character, such as dash ( - ), underscore ( _ ), period ( . ), exclamation mark ( ! ), tilde ( ~ ), asterisk ( * ), left round bracket ( ( ), right round bracket ( ) ), and backslash ( \ ).
bugs.impact: Form might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, use form-based client-initiated SSO if possible. Form-based client-initiated SSO has the correct URL encoding implementation. Alternatively, use an iRule to change the special ASCII characters back to the correct character.

bugs.title: CACHE::header insert fails with 'Out of bounds' error for 301 Cache response
bugs.symptoms: Notice the following log message in /var/log/ltm, err tmm3[12122]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/set_xcache_header <CACHE_RESPONSE> - Out of bounds (line 1) invoked from within "CACHE::header insert Via F5-CACHE" Also, notice the missing header in the HTTP response.
bugs.conditions: 1. Enabled Web Acceleration profile 2. Handling CACHE_RESPONSE iRule event 3. 301 response is cached
bugs.impact: Missing header in the HTTP response
bugs.workaround: Remove the header insert command from the iRule
bugs.fix: Keep the cache information in sync with packet data

bugs.title: /etc/monitors/monitors_logrotate.conf contains an error
bugs.symptoms: The primary symptom will be unrotated monitor log files. Other symptoms include: - Error messages: -- error: /etc/monitors/monitors_logrotate.conf:6 unknown unit 'B' -- error: found error in /var/log/monitors/*.log , skipping - No disk space
bugs.conditions: This occurs in /etc/monitors/monitors_logrotate.conf.
bugs.impact: Monitor logs will not consider file size for rotation criteria. An email notification is generated periodically, which references an error in /etc/monitors/monitors_logrotate.conf.
bugs.workaround: edit /etc/monitors/monitors_logrotate.conf to be "size=5M" instead of "size=5MB" the file should look like this once edited: /var/log/monitors/*.log { compress missingok notifempty rotate 7 size=5M olddir=/var/log/monitors }
bugs.fix: Monitor log rotation functionality has been restored, so that emails with error statements sent to the postmaster every 30 minutes have been stopped.

bugs.title: Logd core formed, while executing provisioning run script(mod_combo_7000_12721.py) on 5000 and 7000 series platforms
bugs.symptoms: Logd core formed while executing provisioning run script(mod_combo_7000_12721.py) on 5000 and 7000 series platforms.
bugs.conditions: While executing provisioning run script(mod_combo_7000_12721.py) on 5000 and 7000 series platforms.
bugs.impact: logd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Run the tmsh command: logd restart.
bugs.fix: Fixed a threading pitfall that could cause deadlock between DB rotation and loading threads.

bugs.title: LTM Policy allows user-specified status code for redirect action
bugs.symptoms: Previously an HTTP redirect always specified a status code of 302. Now you can specify a return code in the range of 300-399, with a default value of 302. Of particular interest is the ability to return 301 to indicate 'Permanent redirect'.
bugs.conditions: LTM Policy with an action of 'forward-redirect'.
bugs.impact: Previously, the only value available was 301. You can now specify any status code in the Redirect range.
bugs.workaround: This is new functionality, and there is nothing to mitigate or work around.
bugs.fix: You may now specify any status code in the range 300-399 for LTM Policy redirect action. The default value is 302.
bugs.behavior: The system now provides additional capability for user-specified status codes for redirect actions. Previously an HTTP redirect always specified a status code of 302. Now, you can specify a return code in the range of 300-399, with the default value of 302.

bugs.title: Empty Webtop when large number of resources assigned to access policy.
bugs.symptoms: When a large number of resources (more than 25) is assigned to an access policy with full a webtop, the system displays an empty webtop when accessed the second time.
bugs.conditions: Large number of resources assigned to access policy.
bugs.impact: Failed to display large number of resources on webtop when accessed second time.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, you can only use fewer resources.

bugs.title: Incorrect assignment of ASM policy to virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect assignment of ASM policy to LTM virtual server occurs when it is managed from the Local Traffic > Virtual Servers > Virtual Server List > <vs_name> > Security > Policies screen when the same ASM policy is assigned to multiple LTM virtual servers by the means of a single LTM policy (L7 policy).
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned, and an ASM policy is assigned to multiple LTM virtual servers by the means of a single LTM policy (L7 policy).
bugs.impact: Changes are applied to all LTM virtual servers that are assigned with the relevant LTM policy (L7 policy) instead of changing only the currently managed LTM virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Assignment of ASM policies to LTM policies and to LTM virtual can be handled from the following screens: 1) LTM policies: Local Traffic > Policies > Policy List > <L7_policy_name> > Properties 1) LTM virtuals: Local Traffic > Virtual Servers > Virtual Server List > <vs_name> > Resources
bugs.fix: The assignment of an ASM policy to an LTM virtual server at from Local Traffic > Virtual Servers > Virtual Server List > <vs_name> > Security > Policies is now NOT available when there is a one-to-many relationship between the underlying LTM policy to LTM virtual servers/ASM policies. In addition, the message 'Manual Configuration (Advanced)' is displayed in the 'Application Security Policy' field on that screen.

bugs.title: HA group must be set up before running ccmode
bugs.symptoms: HA peer discovery process fails when running ccmode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if the ccmode utility (for installations requiring Common Criteria compliance) is run prior to set-up of an HA group.
bugs.impact: Unable to set up HA group. In the GUI, upon attempting the Peer Discovery step, the system returns an iControl connection failure error.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Create all HA groups before running the ccmode utility. -- Complete the following process on both systems prior to initial HA setup or before adding a new device: 1. Run the fommand: tmsh modify sys httpd ssl-protocol "all -SSLv2". 2. Run the command: tmsh save sys config. 3. Perform HA-setup/device-addition. 4. Return the httpd ssl-protocol option to the value that conforms to Common Criteria requirements. To do so, run the following two commands: a. tmsh modify sys httpd ssl-protocol "all -SSLv2 -SSLv3". b. tmsh save sys config.

bugs.title: Link Controller fails to auto-create a self-server
bugs.symptoms: Link Controller will create a data center, but fails to create a GTM server for itself. Any LTM virtual servers configured will not show up as members in the Wide IP configuration.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Users must manually create and maintain the GTM server
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create a GTM server: Standalone: create gtm server <self host name> datacenter Default_DC addresses add { 10.20.0.1 { device-name <self host name> } } virtual-server-discovery enabled product single-bigip Redundant: create gtm server <self host name> datacenter Default_DC addresses add { 10.20.0.1 { device-name <self host name> } 10.20.0.2 { device-name <peer host name>} } virtual-server-discovery enabled product redundant-bigip
bugs.fix: Not fixed

bugs.title: Pendsect log entries have an unexpected severity
bugs.symptoms: Pendsect logs non-errors with a 'warning' severity.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when pendsect is executed.
bugs.impact: Unexpected log entries. When pendsect is executed and does not find any disk errors, it logs the following at the warning level: warning pendsect[21788]: pendsect: /dev/sdb no Pending Sectors detected. This is not an error. The message is posted at the incorrect severity level and does not indicate a problem with the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Adjusted severity level of various logs generated by pendsect script, so that informational messages are not logged as warnings.

bugs.title: Content length header leading whitespaces should not be counted as digits
bugs.symptoms: A customer has reported that they are seeing a non-trivial number of requests blocked with "HTTP Protocol compliance failed - Unparsable content length".
bugs.conditions: The customer has a proxy before ASM that adds whitespaces before the content-length.
bugs.impact: False positive of blocked requests upon content length headers with leading whitespaces.
bugs.fix: The system no longer blocks content length headers with leading whitespaces, because it is legal. The system used to issue the "HTTP protocol compliance failed" sub-violation: "Unparsable request content".

bugs.title: vCMP guest names in statistics limited to 32 characters
bugs.symptoms: Having vCMP guest names that exceed 32 characters might impact the display of statistics for the guests.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with vCMP guest names that exceed 32 characters.
bugs.impact: The tmstat table entries can collapse and omit stats for guests with names longer than 32 characters.
bugs.workaround: Change configuration to use shorter names. Note: Changing names requires stopping traffic processing on the guests.
bugs.fix: vCMP guest names in statistics are no longer limited to 32 characters. The maximum limit of vCMP guest names has been increased to 255 characters.

bugs.title: Hardware Security Module (HSM) CSR and certificate fields constraints: 15 characters and no spaces.
bugs.symptoms: While using the tmsh command or fipskey.nethsm utility to create HSM keys/csr/cert, Locality, Province, Organization names cannot be longer than 15 characters. While using the tmsh command to create HSM keys/csr/cert, Locality, Province, Organization names, common name cannot process multiple words. The system accepts only the content up to the first space character.
bugs.conditions: HSM keys/csr/cert, Locality, Province, Organization names, common name are longer than 15 characters or consists of strings separated by space characters.
bugs.impact: The system truncates field content to 15 characters or to the string up to the first space character.
bugs.workaround: Use strings shorter than or equal to 15 characters. Use strings without spaces. To use strings containing spaces, quote the entire string and delimit spaces with a backslash character (\). For example, for the string F5 Networks Inc, use this: "F5\ Networks\ Inc". Note that the delimiting slash still counts as a character.
bugs.fix: You can now create HSM CSR and certificate fields containing space characters and use strings longer than 15 characters for keys/csr/cert, Locality, Province, Organization names, common name fields.

bugs.title: Licensed SSL and compression limits totals are not shown
bugs.symptoms: Licensed SSL and compression limits totals are not shown.
bugs.conditions: Any multi-core system with SSL and/or compression licensed.
bugs.impact: Might result in confusion or assumption of different limits than actually exist. This is a cosmetic issue and does not affect system functionality.

bugs.title: Demangle filter crash
bugs.symptoms: Demangle filter crashes with a SIGBUF.
bugs.conditions: Very long URLs must be used and the demangle filter must be in the chain.
bugs.impact: HTTP requests with very long URL cannot be processed.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, add this code to the iRule: when HTTP_REQUEST { log local0. "Refer length is [string length [HTTP::header Referer] ]" if { [string length [HTTP::header Referer] ] > 4000 } { HTTP::header remove Referer } }
bugs.fix: Long URLs (up to 16K long) are handled correctly.

bugs.title: Log shows 'socket error: resource temporarily unavailable'
bugs.symptoms: Response cannot be sent to remote clients. This happens rarely with extremely large access policy configurations. While writing response to tmm, APD gets /socket error: Resource temporarily unavailable'.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue are not yet known. The issue cannot be reproduced.
bugs.impact: The system still works. Reconnect restores working function.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Time zone changes do not apply to log timestamps without tmm restart
bugs.symptoms: When the timezone of the BIG-IP system changes, logging timestamps are not updated to the new timezone.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the timezone of the BIG-IP system changes.
bugs.impact: /var/log/ltm logs will have the correct time from the other processes that log, but tmm logs will have the incorrect time. The time remains incorrect until tmm or the system is restarted. There are potential issues with processes that depend on correct localtime in tmm.
bugs.workaround: In tmsh, run one or both of the following commands: 'restart tmm'. -- bigstart restart tmm.
bugs.fix: tmsh modify sys ntp timezone <timezone> will now send a message to TMM so it will reload the timezone.

bugs.title: OneConnect security improvements.
bugs.symptoms: OneConnect security improvements.
bugs.conditions: OneConnect security improvements.
bugs.impact: OneConnect security improvements.
bugs.fix: OneConnect security improvements.

bugs.title: MPTCP Timeout value configuration error checking is not working
bugs.symptoms: MPTCP Timeout valid range for version 11.5.x is [60..36000], but the error message is incorrect. It says value must be between [1..10].
bugs.conditions: -- Using MPTCP Timeout. -- Configured for 11.5.x. No other software versions are affected. -- Entering a value outside the range of [60..36000].
bugs.impact: Error message displays the wrong range [1..10] for MPTCP Timeout in error message. Correct range should be [60..36000].

bugs.title: IP::stats iRule command reports incorrect information past 2**31 bits
bugs.symptoms: Due to a mistaken internal object-size conversion, the statistical data used by the IP::stats iRule command reports a negative number when the data exceeds 2**31.
bugs.conditions: Transferring more than 2 gigabytes or 2 billion packets on a connection that then uses IP::stats commands in an iRule will show a negative number.
bugs.impact: iRules cannot rely on the validity of the IP::stats counters when more than 2 gigabytes have been transferred.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to a fixed version.
bugs.fix: iRules now uses a 64-bit object

bugs.title: DNSX Transfers Occur on DNSX authoritative server change
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express authoritative servers do not update zone information when you change the authoritative server for that zone until the next successful zone transfer from the new server.
bugs.conditions: Create a DNS Express zone and provide an authoritative DNS Express server for that zone, wait for zone transfer to occur, and then change the authoritative server.
bugs.impact: Data from the original server is still served until the next successful zone transfer from the new server or the zone expires.
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the DNSX zone with the new server information.
bugs.fix: Changing a DNSX authoritative server for a zone will cause the BIG-IP to stop serving data from the original server and trigger a transfer request to the new server to obtain new data.

bugs.title: APD Active Directory module memory leak in exception
bugs.symptoms: The APD Active Directory module might leak memory if an exception happens.
bugs.conditions: exception happens when request is being processed
bugs.impact: session request failed, apd leaks a memory
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: APD is now more robust and handles exceptions in AD module properly.

bugs.title: GUI inaccessible on chassis when var/log/audit log is full
bugs.symptoms: When MCP logging on a chassis is set to Enabled, Verbose, or Debug for Audit Logging, the system sends numerous messages to the var/log/audit log. This causes the log to fill, which might render the GUI inaccessible.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on chassis only when the Audit Logging option MCP is set to Enabled, Verbose, or Debug.
bugs.impact: When the var/log/audit log is full, the GUI might become inaccessible.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to specify Disabled for the MCP option in Audit Logging (available under the System :: Logs).
bugs.fix: The primary blade formerly sent a message to all secondaries every second telling them to change the primary selection time. (The actual timestamp is correct and is the same every second.) Over time, this might fill up the audit log. This no longer occurs, and the message is now sent only when the primary actually changes.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE instances created using OpenStack interfaces may fail to detect the KVM hypervisor
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) instances created using OpenStack interfaces may fail to detect the Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) hypervisor.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You are deploying a BIG-IP VE instance on a KVM hypervisor. -- You are using the OpenStack interface tool set to perform the deployment.
bugs.impact: As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- The BIG-IP VE instance fails to start. -- When starting the BIG-IP VE instance, diagnostic messages may indicate that the hypervisor is not recognized.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can modify your OpenStack compute nodes to run all instances as KVM. To do so, perform the following procedure: Note: The workaround assumes that your compute nodes use KVM as the default hypervisor. Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system. 1. Log in to the OpenStack compute node as the root user. 2. Using an editor, create a file in the /etc/nova directory named release. 3. Add the following content to the new file: [Nova] vendor = Red Hat product = Bochs package = RHEL 6.3.0 PC 4. Restart all services or reboot the compute note. 5. Redeploy a new BIG-IP VE instance using the OpenStack interface tool set.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP VE instances created using OpenStack interfaces now detect the KVM hypervisor. Important: If you performed the steps to work around this issue (as described in the known issue for this bug), removing the workaround might require a license change.

bugs.title: TMM assert 'spdy pcb initialized' in spdy_process()
bugs.symptoms: TMM assert 'spdy pcb initialized' in spdy_process() caused by a HUDEVT_ABORTED on a zero'd SPDY ctx from iSession.
bugs.conditions: -- APM, iSession, and SPDY filter configured. -- iClient unexpectedly closes the connection (by sending FIN) before handshaking complete.
bugs.impact: TMM Asserts.
bugs.workaround: 1. Fix iClient configuration. 2. Remove SPDY profile from the chain.
bugs.fix: This release fixes iSession so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: In low memory situations initializing the HTTP parser will cause the TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: When the TMM is low in memory and HTTP is configured, the configuration process may initialize a new HTTP parser. If that initialization fails, then the TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: A virtual containing HTTP is configured or re-configured when the TMM is under extreme memory pressure.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Configuring a HTTP filter during extreme memory pressure will no longer cause the TMM to crash.

bugs.title: zxfrd might crash when the zone file (zxfrd.bin) is deleted from the directory /var/db
bugs.symptoms: zxfrd might crash when the zone file zxfrd.bin is deleted and zxfrd is restarted.
bugs.conditions: Manually delete zxfrd.bin and restart zxfrd.
bugs.impact: The zxfrd daemon might crash.
bugs.workaround: Never manually delete zxfrd.bin.
bugs.fix: Manually deleting zxfrd.bin should no longer crash the zxfrd daemon.

bugs.title: FW Release: Incorporate VIPRION 2250 LOP firmware v1.20
bugs.symptoms: This is a standard bug used for tracking the incorporation of Firmware changes.
bugs.conditions: The purpose of this change is to integrate a firmware package into the BIG-IP build.
bugs.impact: None expected.
bugs.fix: FW Release: Incorporated VIPRION 2250 LOP firmware v1.20 into BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Out-of-order TCP packets may be dropped
bugs.symptoms: Out-of-order TCP packet will be dropped if it occurs during 3-way handshake.
bugs.conditions: Client initiates TCP connection to BIG-IP with ACK segment arriving after (i.e., out-of-order) a second packet. Resultant sequence: 1. Client - BIG-IP : SYN 2. BIG-IP - Client : SYN-ACK 3. Client - BIG-IP : PSH, ACK (w/Segment #2) =-- Out-of-order ; Must be retransmitted. 4. Client - BIG-IP : ACK (w/Segment #1)
bugs.impact: Packet must be retransmitted by client.
bugs.fix: Out-of-order segments received before 3WHS is completed are no longer dropped.

bugs.title: Issues with Outlook Web App through APM Portal Access only on InternetExplorer11
bugs.symptoms: Access to Office365 Outlook Web Access services using Portal Access is broken for HTML5-supported browsers. The user is redirected to the APM Logout page after successfully logging in to Office365.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when user accesses Office365 Outlook Web Access application through APM Portal Access using Internet Explorer 11.
bugs.impact: User cannot get access to Mailbox in Office365 Outlook Web Access through Portal Access using HTML5-supported browsers.
bugs.workaround: This example iRule disables OWA offline-caching support: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [string tolower [HTTP::uri]] contains "/owa/manifests/appcachemanifesthandler.ashx" } { HTTP::respond 404 } }
bugs.fix: Portal Access now removes references to a HTML5 offline cache manifests when rewriting HTML pages. This change prevents web applications from loading such manifests.

bugs.title: DNS cache resolver connections can be slow to terminate
bugs.symptoms: An excessive number of DNS cache resolver connections can build up if local configuration errors (routing, interfaces, VLANs) exist.
bugs.conditions: Local networking configuration errors exist.
bugs.impact: An excessive number of outbound DNS cache connections are present.
bugs.workaround: Ensure default routes for IPv4 and IPv6 are properly configured and operational.
bugs.fix: Local connection errors now cause immediate connection termination.

bugs.title: DNS Express zone creation, deletion or updates can slow down or stop other DNS services.
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express zone creation, deletion or updates can slow down or stop other DNS services.
bugs.conditions: Any action that causes a the DNS Express zone database to be updated, including zone creation, deletion or zone transfer.
bugs.impact: Other DNS Services may stop working.
bugs.workaround: Restarting tmm will resolve the issue temporarily, until the next update. If DNS Express is not being used, removing any DNS Express config will prevent this issue from triggering.
bugs.fix: An improperly handled file descriptor caused the issue. This file description is now properly closed preventing the problem.

bugs.title: SSO does not work with Password with '+' character for Citrix Storefront integration mode
bugs.symptoms: A password containing a '+' (plus) character is not accepted, and authentication error is shown to the end-user.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server is configured in Citrix integration mode. Storefront is configured in Passthrough gateway authentication mode.
bugs.impact: Password with special character '+' can not be used.
bugs.workaround: Use password with no '+' character.
bugs.fix: Accept password with '+' character correctly.

bugs.title: Only one delegation account supported for Kerberos SSO for a same domain
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to configure more than one delegation account to be used in Kerberos SSO for the same realm. Single sign-on fails in case there is more than one delegation account for a same realm.
bugs.conditions: There is a need to configure two or more delegation accounts for Kerberos SSO to provide single-sign-on to resources in the same domain
bugs.impact: Impossible to separate SSO objects to different resources by defining separate delegation accounts.
bugs.workaround: Use the same delegation account for all the resources across one particular domain.
bugs.fix: It is now possible to use multiple kerberos S4U constrained delegation accounts for the same realm by configuring separate kerberos SSO objects and switching between them using iRules, Portal Access ACLs, multidomain mode SSO, or a Per-Request Access Policy switch.

bugs.title: Config sync of SecurID config file fails on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: If APM is provisioned, after uploading a new SecurID config file via the GUI, mcpd restarts and fails to sync on device group peers.
bugs.conditions: This happens on a device group peer with APM provisioned, only after using the GUI to update the SecurID configuration. This can also happen on chassis secondary blades.
bugs.impact: The peer receiving the sync restarts mcpd, which in turn restarts several other daemons. The peer never receives the config file properly.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh: tmsh modify apm aaa securid <name> config-files modify { sdconf.rec { local-path /path/to/sdconf.rec } }.
bugs.fix: The fix changes the behavior of transactions. Previously, if a single transaction contained a delete operation and a modify of the object just deleted, the outcome was that the object was deleted and the modify was silently ignored. This was different behavior from a delete followed by a create, which ignored the delete and internally modified the object. Since that modify is sent to the peer as a modify, the object must have the same behavior as a delete-plus-create operation. So the new behavior is that, when a single transaction contains a delete followed by a modify of the same object, then the delete is ignored and the modify is applied.
bugs.behavior: With this release, there is a change to the behavior of transactions. Previously, if a single transaction contained a delete operation and a modify of the object just deleted, the outcome was that the object was deleted and the modify was silently ignored. This was different behavior from a delete followed by a create, which ignored the delete and internally modified the object. Since that modify is sent to the peer as a modify, the object must have the same behavior as a delete-plus-create operation. So the new behavior is that, when a single transaction contains a delete followed by a modify of the same object, then the delete is ignored and the modify is applied.

bugs.title: Autosync occurring in Sync-Failover ASM
bugs.symptoms: On Primary/ACTIVE, Secondary/STBY configurations, when the ASM device group is selected from the GUI on a secondary/STBY system, config sync automatically occurs and pushes the config from STBY to ACTIVE systems, overwriting existing policies on ACTIVE.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure high availability for Sync-Failover. -- Enable ASM sync on the Sync-Failover device group.
bugs.impact: The system automatically performs a config sync operation, and pushes the config from STBY to ACTIVE systems, overwriting existing policies on ACTIVE.
bugs.fix: When enabling ASM sync on a Sync-Failover device group, automatic sync no longer occurs if the Sync-Failover device group is 'In Sync' before enabling ASM sync on it.

bugs.title: TMM fast forwarded flows are offloaded to ePVA
bugs.symptoms: TMM fast forwarded flows are offloaded to ePVA, which is incorrect behavior. The symptom various depending on the FastL4 profile's PVA acceleration setting. If PVA acceleration is set to full, then the connection is established and handled by software (TMM). It is not offloaded to the ePVA. If PVA acceleration is set to guaranteed, then the connection will be reset.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a virtual is configured with a FastL4 profile using HW acceleration (ePVA).
bugs.impact: TMM fast forwarded flows are offloaded to ePVA, which is incorrect behavior.
bugs.workaround: For versions 11.3.x and 11.4.0, there is no workaround. On version 11.4.1 or later, you can use the following command to turn off tmm fast forward when using the guaranteed hardware acceleration mode: 'tmsh modify sys db tmm.ffwd.enable value false'.
bugs.fix: TMM fast forwarded flows are no longer offloaded to ePVA, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Wrong overlapping status is shown if there are firewall rules with source or destination port range that begins with "1"
bugs.symptoms: Wrong overlapping status is shown if there are rules with source or destination port range that begins with "1" configured in the system.
bugs.conditions: Firewall rules with source or destination port range that begins with "1" configured in the system.
bugs.impact: Rules that are not overlapped or conflicting will be shown as overlapped or conflicting.
bugs.fix: Fix the overlapping detection function to properly handle the port ranges.

bugs.title: Manual start of a BIG-IP APM service may trigger 100 percent CPU utilization.
bugs.symptoms: As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptoms: -- BIG-IP iHealth lists Heuristic H465125 on the Diagnostics :: Identified :: High screen. -- The BIG-IP APM service that you started causes system CPU utilization to increases over time, and eventually to consume all available CPU. -- Users may be unable to access the BIG-IP APM access profiles. -- When you view the Configuration utility, dashboard CPU consumption continually increases. -- In the /var/log/ltm log file, you may observe log messages similar to the following examples. notice chmand[6792]: 012a0005:5: Cpu utilization over 300 seconds is 100%, exceeded log level 80% notice chmand[6792]: 012a0005:5: Cpu utilization over 300 seconds is 100%, exceeded log level 80%
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The BIG-IP service is already running. -- You manually start the BIG-IP service from the command line either directly or by using bigstart. -- The BIG-IP service is running one of the following services: aced, acctd, apd, eam, rba, or websso
bugs.impact: The user may be unable to access the system, and the BIG-IP APM system may stop responding.
bugs.workaround: Never start any daemon manually. The proper way to start, stop, and restart daemons on the BIG-IP system is to use the bigstart utility: bigstart start daemonname bigstart stop daemonname bigstart restart daemonname

bugs.title: foreign key index error on local traffic-only group
bugs.symptoms: When running the load verify command (tmsh load sys config verify) on a scf file, an error is thrown: 01070712:3: Values (/Common/traffic-group-local-only) specified for self IP (/Common/10.7.7.3_24): foreign key index (traffic_group_fk) do not point at an item that exists in the database. Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed. However, the config will still successfully load when the verify parameter is not specified.
bugs.conditions: Running tmsh load sys config file verify on a scf file with a local traffic group in it. traffic-group-local-only groups are not loaded during config verify which triggers the error.
bugs.impact: Config verify fails.
bugs.workaround: If there are otherwise no other errors in the configuration, it should be able to load successfully using tmsh load sys config file filename.
bugs.fix: Running tmsh load sys config file verify no longer throws a foreign key error on traffic-only group.

bugs.title: TCP virtual server/UDP virtual server without datagram-LB mode enabled running DNS cache and suspending iRules might cause TMM crash.
bugs.symptoms: When a TCP virtual server, or a UDP virtual server without datagram-LB mode enabled, runs an iRule which suspends itself, and the traffic that virtual server is handling is destined for the DNS cache, subsequent responses attempting to execute an iRule crash TMM because the first response is suspended. Those subsequent responses should be queued before attempting to execute the iRule.
bugs.conditions: Configuration contains TCP virtual server, or a UDP virtual server without datagram-LB mode enabled running DNS cache and suspending iRules or there is iRule execution error.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Enable datagram-LB mode on the UDP profile. There is no workaround in the case of TCP.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer restarts when configuration contains TCP virtual server, or a UDP virtual server without datagram-LB mode enabled running DNS cache and suspending iRules.

bugs.title: APM does not support Vmware View 'Log in as current user' feature
bugs.symptoms: Even though 'Log in as current user' feature is enabled on Vmware View Connection server, when a Windows user accesses a View resource through APM, user is asked to authenticate.
bugs.conditions: 1. 'Log in as current user' feature is enabled on Vmware View Connection server. 2. Vmware View Connection Server is behind APM. 3. Windows user is in same Active Directory domain as View Connection Server and is already logged into Windows desktop. 4. User attempts to access a View resource through APM.
bugs.impact: User is required to authenticate to APM.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: APM now supports "Logon as current user" feature for Horizon client on Windows.Once logged into Windows desktop, user can access View resources without being prompted to login.

bugs.title: FTP data flows do not count toward LSN pool client connection limit
bugs.symptoms: When FTP is used with LSN pools, the data connections do not count towards the LSN client connection limit count.
bugs.conditions: FTP is configured with LSN pool whose client connection limit value is greater than zero.
bugs.impact: Data connections (active/passive mode) are not counted. This might result in a subscriber being able to create more connections than specified by LSN pool client connection limit

bugs.title: Initial boot from non-Primary blades causes daemon restarts and error messages on VIPRION B4300/B4300N blades and on the VIPRION C2200 chassis.
bugs.symptoms: Initial boot from non-Primary blades causes daemon restarts and error messages on VIPRION B4300/B4300N blades and on the VIPRION C2200 chassis. Messages posted might appear similar to the following: -- snmpd[7175]: custom mib initialization completed. total 0 custom mib entry registered. -- snmpd[7175]: Turning on AgentX master support. -- restorecond: Reset file context /etc/mtab: system_u:object_r:etc_t:s0-system_u:object_r:etc_runtime_t:s0 -- sflow_agent[8639]: sflow_mcp.cpp::556: sflow_agent[8639]: Processed max messages (201) in a loop.
bugs.conditions: This happens on each blade except blade1 (which is the Primary).
bugs.impact: When this occurs, the system posts various error messages and the daemon restarts.
bugs.workaround: Reboot. Subsequent reboots do not cause the daemon restarts.

bugs.title: Connections with ramcache and clientssl profile allowing non-SSL traffic may stall
bugs.symptoms: Connections with both ramcache and clientssl profile allowing non-SSL traffic connection may stall under certain unusual conditions.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with ramcache and clientssl profile allowing non-SSL traffic.
bugs.impact: The connection stalls until reset by the client or expired by the sweeper. The client may see a response from the server.
bugs.workaround: No practical workaround.
bugs.fix: Connections no longer stall on virtual servers with ramcache and clientssl profile allowing non-SSL traffic.

bugs.title: Current Sessions stat does not increment/decrement correctly.
bugs.symptoms: Current Sessions stat does not increment/decrement correctly.
bugs.conditions: On a virtual server with an HTTP filter, if either side closes the connection after the HTTP request has been forwarded to the server but before the server has sent its response, the pool member's cur_sessions stat is incremented but not decremented.
bugs.impact: Difficult to determine an accurate number of Current Sessions. Current Sessions stat appears unexpectedly large, for example, Current Sessions : 18446744073709551615, rather than as expected, Current Sessions : 0.
bugs.fix: On a virtual server with an HTTP filter, Current Sessions stat now increments/decrements correctly if either side closes the connection after the HTTP request has been forwarded to the server but before the server has sent its response.

bugs.title: APM Exchange Proxy does not honor tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize DB variable and is subject to ID 405348
bugs.symptoms: APM Exchange Proxy does not honor tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize DB variable and is subject to ID 405348 (ActiveSync client fails to login to APM with large POST body)
bugs.conditions: ActiveSync client large POST body tries to log into APM.
bugs.impact: ActiveSync client with large POST body cannot log in even when tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize DB variable is configured
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now APM Exchange Proxy honors the tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize DB variable. Modify the tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize DB variable with a value larger than the maximum email body size you would like to support. The maximum supported value is 25000000 (25MB).

bugs.title: The Citrix Client Detection process may incorrectly prompt for the installation of client software.
bugs.symptoms: The Citrix Client Detection process may incorrectly prompt for the installation of client software. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: During subsequent access sessions, when accessing the Citrix resource, the webtop session displays the following message: -- Citrix client not detected -- Clicking the Skip button of the Citrix client download allows the Citrix session to initiate. -- Enabling the Add APM virtual server to the Internet Explorer Compatibility view setting eliminates the "Citrix client not detected" prompt.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP APM system is configured for Citrix replacement mode. -- You are using Internet Explorer 11. -- Citrix client software is installed on your device. -- You establish a new access session and attempt to access the Citrix resource.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP APM webtop prompts you to install the Citrix client software.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can add the BIG-IP APM virtual server to the Internet Explorer Compatibility view setting on the client device. Impact of workaround: Performing the suggested workaround should not have a negative impact on your system
bugs.fix: The Citrix Client Detection process now correctly prompts for the installation of client software.

bugs.title: Cannot have 2 distinct 'contains' conditions on the same LTM policy operand
bugs.symptoms: Cannot express conditions such as 'user-agent contains 'Android' AND 'Mobile'. LTM policies have operands that can be matched against a set of values, causing a match when the operand matches one of these values. There is no way to use current functionality to match all of the values. One specific situation in which this is needed is to configure 'contains'.
bugs.conditions: Specify an ltm rule with 2 conditions with the same operand and match type, for example: conditions { 0 { http-header name User-Agent contains values { Android } } 1 { http-header name User-Agent contains values { Mobile } }
bugs.impact: The policy does not work. The system posts an error message similar to the following: Failed to compile the combined policies.
bugs.fix: LTM policies now allow for rules to have multiple conditions on the same operand and same match type so that 'user-agent contains 'Android' AND 'Mobile' can now be expressed by specifying: conditions { 0 { http-header name User-Agent contains values { Android } } 1 { http-header name User-Agent contains values { Mobile } }

bugs.title: CuSFP module plugged in during links-down state will cause remote link-up
bugs.symptoms: If a CuSFP module is plugged into a port that is in a links-down state while connected via a cable to a remote switch or other network connection, the remote switch will report a links-up state. A port on the BIG-IP or VIPRION device may be in a links-down state while BIG-IP is not in a running state, or if the network interface has been administratively disabled.
bugs.conditions: Issue has been primarily observed with VIPRION B2100 or B2150 blades. However, the problem could potentially occur on other VIPRION blades or BIG-IP appliances which employ a Broadcom hardware switch (i.e., most F5 hardware products). BIG-IP appliances which do NOT employ a Broadcom hardware switch include: BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series appliances.
bugs.impact: The remote switch may erroneously attempt to direct traffic to what is seen as an active link, which the BIG-IP or VIPRION device will not be able to process.
bugs.workaround: You may work around this problem by any of the following methods: 1. Unplug the cable connecting the CuSFP (Copper SFP) module to the remote network connection before plugging the CuSFP into the port on the BIG-IP or VIPRION device. 2. Wait until the port on the BIG-IP or VIPRION device is in an enabled/links-up state before plugging in the CuSFP. 3. Enable the port on the BIG-IP or VIPRION device after plugging in the CuSFP.
bugs.fix: A remote network connection no longer shows as Up/Link when a CuSFP module is plugged into a port on a BIG-IP or VIPRION device that is in a links-down state, while connected via a cable to the remote switch/other network connection.

bugs.title: Core in parked transaction due to evicted stand-in document
bugs.symptoms: TMM core error in a previously parked transaction
bugs.conditions: * Stand-in is enabled on the policy. * Request queueing is turned on in the policy * Document may have been removed from entity due to not matching policy on node.
bugs.impact: Loss of service.
bugs.workaround: * Disable stand-in and/or Request queueing
bugs.fix: TMM will no longer crash. If the stand-in document is NULL, the transaction will be bypassed and treated as if not found in cache.

bugs.title: Chassis with MCPD audit logging enabled will sync updates to device group state
bugs.symptoms: If mcpd audit logging is enabled on a chassis, updates to device group state will be recorded on every configuration change, even if CMI is not configured or no synchronizable object was modified.
bugs.conditions: This only applies on chassis systems with at least one secondary blade, and the log messages only appear if mcpd audit logging is enabled.
bugs.impact: Updates to device group state will be recorded on every configuration change.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: If mcpd audit logging is enabled on a chassis, updates to device group state were in past versions recorded on every configuration change, even if CMI was not configured or no synchronizable object was modified. This no longer happens, and these log messages are now only generated if the state actually changes.

bugs.title: APM incorrectly supports 'redirect' ending in an access policy for web browser clients when deployed for Citrix Web Interface in proxy mode.
bugs.symptoms: When your access policy uses 'redirect' as the ending (policy result is 'redirect'), Citrix ICA Patcher fails with error: Jan 29 04:17:15 bigip3 err tmm[29825]: 01490000:3: ICA Patcher: Invalid session a5cced0f8a360d58829a8551b6bed4e8
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered if your access policy ends with Redirect instead of Allow.
bugs.impact: Clients will be unable to connect.
bugs.workaround: Use 'allow' policy ending and do redirect in ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED event.
bugs.fix: APM correctly supports 'redirect' ending in an access policy for web browser clients when deployed for Citrix Web Interface in proxy mode.

bugs.title: Requests Export: Japanese characters (SHIFT-JIS) unreadable in PDF
bugs.symptoms: Japanese characters (SHIFT-JIS) unreadable in PDF.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you try to export requests containing Japanese characters. This also occurs with some other Asian languages
bugs.impact: PDF not readable when exporting requests
bugs.fix: Because the BIG-IP system's PDF-generating mechanism does not support all character encodings, you now have the option of exporting Requests and Event Correlation as an HTML file, or as a PDF file.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may report getLopSensorData warnings at boot time or when changing a PSU
bugs.symptoms: When booting a BIG-IP device, or performing a hot swap operation of one of its power supplies, the following kind of log messages may be displayed for a brief time: localhost warning chmand[7059]: 012a0004:4: getLopSensorData: LopDev: sendLopCmd: Lopd status: 1 packet: action=1 obj_id=115 sub_obj=0 slot_id=ff result=24 len=0 crc=6576 payload= (error code:0x24) localhost warning chmand[7059]: 012a0004:4: getLopSensorData: LopDev: sendLopCmd: Lopd status: 1 packet: action=1 obj_id=16f sub_obj=1 slot_id=ff result=1 len=0 crc=acaf payload= (error code:0x1) These messages should not persist, and when a real error occurs it should be accompanied by additional warnings and alerts from the system.
bugs.conditions: The condition occurs when the sensor monitoring process tries to obtain information from power supply model types that are supported but not actually installed. It does this until it discovers the actual model type installed, or that no power supply is installed. The specific conditions under which this is likely to happen are when the BIG-IP software is re-started or a power supply is changed while the system is running.
bugs.impact: A few additional log messages that indicate a warning when there is no legitimate failure.
bugs.workaround: None. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP no longer logs getLopSensorData warnings with error code 0x24 for newly-inserted power supplies (PSUs).

bugs.title: GUI Node Address List does not display by hostname.
bugs.symptoms: The GUI does not display hostname in node list despite having a host entry in /etc/hosts and the 'Display Host Names When Possible' setting enabled in system
bugs.conditions: Having a host entry in /etc/hosts, and the 'Display Host Names When Possible' setting enabled in system.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to find a node by name.
bugs.workaround: Use the Pool member list to find a note by hostname.

bugs.title: GUI: SNMPV3 Incorrectly requires "OID" when creating an SNMP user.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP GUI incorrectly requires an OID to be specified when creating an SNMPv3 user.
bugs.conditions: Creating an SNMPv3 user via the BIG-IP GUI.
bugs.impact: An OID can be used to restrict the view that the user has to a particular branch of the tree, but should not be a required attribute.
bugs.workaround: - Enter a value of ".1" (with a leading dot) to allow access to all OIDs (or) - Create the user using tmsh instead of the GUI, where the oid-subset attribute is not mandatory.

bugs.title: TMM crashes at startup when reprovisioning.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes at startup when reprovisioning.
bugs.conditions: Although there are several potential causes for this issue, they are difficult to quantify. For example, when provisioning stops the tmm, subsequent processing that finishes the provisioning activity might restart some daemons.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes on startup because it cannot obtain the memory allocated. In the specific case of provisioning failure, and depending on the modules being provisioned the system might post messages similar to the following: -- err mcpd[7608]: 01070066:3: Publication not found in mcpd for publisher Id WAMD_McpInvalidation_Publisher. -- err mprov:1265:: 'Reserving huge memory failed (desired amount: 6295 pages [12590 MiB], allocated: 4248 pages [ 8496 MiB].' -- err mprov:1265:: 'Resource reallocation could not be completed - A reboot is necessary for provisioning to complete.'
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.

bugs.title: Renewing machine-account password does not update the serviceId for associated ntlm-auth.
bugs.symptoms: Renewing machine-account password does not update the serviceId for associated ntlm-auth. Because of this issue, you might see the following symptoms: -- End users report that they cannot access email. -- NTLM logons stop working for all users. -- Log file shows errors similar to the following: err nlad[12384]: 01620000:3: <0x566d4b90> nlclnt[71601c70a] init: Error [0xc000006d,NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE] connecting to DC.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system has an NTLM machine account configured, but it is not known exactly what triggers the error. It can be triggered if the machine account credentials change, but the symptom might not show up for days since the connection can be reused.
