bugs.impact: End users will be unable to connect.
bugs.workaround: Correct the problem by running the following command: bigstart restart eca.

bugs.title: tmm sigsegv
bugs.symptoms: A tmm crash was encountered during normal operation.
bugs.conditions: It is not known all of the conditions that trigger this, but it is related to use of the internal string cache in certain deployments such as PEM and LTM's DNS resolver.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Version disclosure
bugs.symptoms: Portal rewritten pages contain unencoded version information.
bugs.conditions: APM portal configured
bugs.impact: Software version disclosure
bugs.workaround: # # Substitute plain text BIGIP version in 01000-rules.js cache-fm.js, cache-fm-debug.js # by md5sum of this plain text. # # INSTUCTIONS: # # a) as root on BIG-IP system, change directory to /var/sam/www/webtop/private/fm and place this script there; # b) backup files modified by this script: # 01000-rules.js # cache-fm.js # cache-fm-debug.js # c) execute this script; # d) restart services: # tmsh restart sys service tmm # tmsh restart sys service rewrite # # Note: This should be done for all systems in the failover configuration. # STAMP=`grep BIGIP 01000-rules.js | sed "/F5_version/s/.*special_object[^']*'\([^']*\)'\".*/\1/"` if [ -z "$STAMP" ] ; then echo "Nothing is done. F5_version is already obfuscated" exit; else STAMPMD5=`echo -n $STAMP | md5sum | awk '{print $1}'` for i in 01000-rules.js cache-fm.js cache-fm-debug.js do sed "/F5_version/s/\(.*special_object[^']*'\)[^']*\('\".*\)/\1$STAMPMD5\2/" $i > $i.obfusc cp $i.obfusc $i rm $i.obfusc done echo "F5_version $STAMP is converted into md5sum $STAMPMD5" fi
bugs.fix: [Portal Access] BIG-IP version is obfuscated.

bugs.title: TCP zero window suspends data transfer
bugs.symptoms: HTTP pipeline request might cause TCP window stay at 0 and not recover.
bugs.conditions: This intermittent issue occurs when HTTP pipeline requests are sent, and those requests use the GET method.
bugs.impact: When this occurs, the resulting TCP zero window suspends data transfer. It is possible that the TCP window will be reduced to 0 (zero) and never recover.
bugs.fix: HTTP pipeline request no longer causes TCP window stay at 0 when HTTP pipeline requests are sent, and those requests use the GET method.

bugs.title: 'load sys config verify' commands cause loss of sync configuration and initiates a provisioning cycle
bugs.symptoms: The commands 'load sys config from-terminal verify' and 'load sys config file <filename> verify' causes loss of sync configuration and initiates a provisioning cycle. The 'verify' option on the 'load sys config' command is designed to ensure that a configuration (either from a file or pasted to the terminal) is valid, but not have it take effect.
bugs.conditions: This affects the ConfigSync communication channel if configured.
bugs.impact: The ConfigSync connection, including the connections to other devices, might be lost. In addition, provisioning might be impacted.
bugs.workaround: You can avoid this issue by using the 'load sys config from-terminal verify' and 'load sys config file <filename> verify' commands 'merge' option, which keeps the current configuration during the validation step. Once affected by this issue, the workaround is to re-load the full configuration using the following command: tmsh load sys config partitions all.
bugs.fix: Previously, the commands 'load sys config from-terminal verify' and 'load sys config file <filename> verify' did some operations related to sync and provisioning, though they are supposed to check only the validity of the configuration (without changing it). This has been resolved.

bugs.title: devmgmtd may crash during provisioning
bugs.symptoms: devmgmtd (also known as devmgmtd++ on older versions) may crash during some provisioning operations.
bugs.conditions: This happens during some provisioning operations.
bugs.impact: A core dump will be left on the device, but no further ill effects.

bugs.title: SIP response from the server to the client get dropped
bugs.symptoms: SIP responses are not forwarded to the client. Instead, the system drops those SIP responses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using SIP OneConnect with an iRule that uses the node/snat command in SIP_RESPONSE event in the iRule to direct the SIP response from the server.
bugs.impact: Some SIP flows do not complete, which affects the SIP clients.
bugs.workaround: Remove the node/snat command from SIP_RESPONSE event processing in the iRule.
bugs.fix: iRules node/snat command in the iRule SIP_RESPONSE event now works correctly.

bugs.title: Using an iRule nexthop to "vlan:mac address" does not forward the packet
bugs.symptoms: iRule: nexthop to 'vlan:mac address' does not forward the packet.
bugs.conditions: HTTP request to a port 80 virtual server with a default pool and an iRule that specifies nexthop to a MAC address on the internal VLAN.
bugs.impact: Packet forwarding does not occur.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Updating multiple items in a list only make one change
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to add several items to a list (ex. urlContentProfiles for urls), the one of the new values is added to the list.
bugs.conditions: ASM REST is used to PATCH a resource to add/update multiple items in an array field.
bugs.impact: The resource is not updated as expected and Policy enforcement may not be as expected.
bugs.workaround: Send the same request multiple times, or make only one modification at a time.
bugs.fix: List values are now correctly updated via ASM REST.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as IdP does not support Attribute Name Format Identifiers
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP as identity provider (IdP) does not support "Attribute Name Format Identifiers". It always uses "Unspecified" format for each attribute as part of the created SAML assertion.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as IdP
bugs.impact: Attribute Name Format Identifiers is reported as "Unspecified" format for each attribute as part of the created SAML assertion.
bugs.fix: APM as IdP SAML support has been improved to allow GUI changes to configure Name Format for assertion attributes on SAML IdP page: - Allow enum selection of name format with default value 'unspecified' - Allow editing of name format for all attributes.

bugs.title: Loading the default configuration may cause the mcpd process to restart and produce a core file.
bugs.symptoms: Loading the default configuration may cause the mcpd process to restart and produce a core file.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: After you successfully load a UCS file that was created on a different system, you attempt to restore the system to factory defaults by loading the default configuration. When you load the default configuration, if the mcpd process is unable to decrypt the master-key, or attributes exist that were encrypted with a key other than the current master-key, the mcpd process restarts and produces a core file. These situations may occur if an RMA has occurred and you install a UCS from one device to another device of the same type, if the device unit key becomes corrupted, or if the master key file (/config/bigip/kstore/master) becomes corrupted.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic and fail over if configured as part of a high-availability system.
bugs.fix: Fixed crashes in mcpd and other daemons when the master-key cannot be decrypted, or when attributes exist that were encrypted with a key other than the current master-key. These situations may occur when a RMA occurs, when moving a UCS from one device to another device of the same type, if the device unit key becomes corrupted, or if the master key file (/config/bigip/kstore/master) becomes corrupted.

bugs.title: apd and apmd constantly restarting
bugs.symptoms: If mcpd fails to start for some reason, apd and apmd will continuously crash. Symptoms in /var/log/ltm: err tmsh[892]: 01420006:3: "apm" unexpected argument and there will be an apmd and apd core.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if mcpd fails to start or crashes on the standby.
bugs.impact: Multiple core files, system will not pass traffic
bugs.fix: Fixed a condition where apd and apmd would try to start if mcpd was not running.

bugs.title: Error message 'Gx uninit failed!' and 'Gy unint failed!' received during boot of the system
bugs.symptoms: During booting of the system, error message "Gx uninit failed!' and 'Gy unint failed!' is received repeatedly.
bugs.conditions: -- Gx or Gy is not licensed for PEM to use. -- Rebooting the system.
bugs.impact: Undesired error message is received.
bugs.fix: In debug mode only, the system posts 'Gx not initialized' or 'Gy not initialized' for the purpose of alerting users to unlicensed Gx and Gy.

bugs.title: Diameter Monitor not waiting for all fragments
bugs.symptoms: When the server returns response in two fragments, the Diameter monitor sends an ACK for the first fragment followed by a FIN and then a reset.
bugs.conditions: Server returns response in two fragments.
bugs.impact: Pool member is marked down.
bugs.fix: Diameter Monitor now handles fragments as expected.

bugs.title: Fallback source persistence entry is not used when primary SSL persistence fails
bugs.symptoms: The existing source persistence record is not used as fallback for a second SSL request from the same source. The second request may be load balanced to a different pool member than the first one. Sometimes multiple source persistence records may be created pointing to different pool members.
bugs.conditions: SSL persistence configured as primary persistence method on a SSL VIP. Source persistence configured as fallback persistence method. The same client sends a second SSL request, but sends a different session ID so that SSL persistence look up fails.
bugs.impact: Requests are load balanced to different pool members instead of the same one. In other words, source fallback persistence does not work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: Fallback source persistence entry is now used when primary SSL persistence fails.

bugs.title: Sometimes VMware View client 2.3 for Windows can't launch desktops via APM
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes VMware View client 2.3 for Windows cannot launch desktops using APM.
bugs.conditions: APM configured as PCoIP Proxy.
bugs.impact: VMware View client 2.3 for Windows cannot launch desktops.
bugs.workaround: Apply the following iRule: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::path] == "/broker/xml" && [HTTP::header Expect] == "100-continue" } { SSL::respond "HTTP/1.0 100 Continue\r\n\r\n" } }
bugs.fix: VMware View client 2.3 for Windows can consistently launch desktops using APM.

bugs.title: Occasionally customers see chunk boundaries as part of HTTP response
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, users see chunk boundaries as part of HTTP response if the virtual server is configured with rewrite profile variant and some other profiles.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with rewrite profile variant and some other profiles like OneConnect and NTLM could cause HTTP response to be double-chunked.
bugs.impact: End users may see random characters displayed on their web pages, or the page may fail to render because it contains invalid HTML markup.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this problem, use an iRule to rechunk the HTTP response always.
bugs.fix: Simple iRule is added inside code to rechunk the response in HTTP_RESPONSE event when the content is already chunked by backend/application servers.

bugs.title: iControl error when discover ASM from EM
bugs.symptoms: iControl request for iControl:ASM/Policy::get_list() fail EM connections fail to ASM devices
bugs.conditions: iControl fails to call to the ASM portion of iControl, and produces an error message. <faultstring xsi:type="xsd:string">Exception caught in ASM::urn:iControl:ASM/Policy::get_list() Exception: Common::OperationFailed primary_error_code : 0 (0x00000000) secondary_error_code : 0 error_string : Unset policy</faultstring>
bugs.impact: Discovery and refreshing devices fails, and EM cannot manage devices with ASM.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: EM can now discover ASM devices.

bugs.title: Portal Access / JavaScript code which uses reserved keywords for object field names may not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript code with object field names equal to reserved keywords is not handled correctly by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript code with objects containing fields with reserved keywords as a name, for example: a.default = 1;
bugs.impact: JavaScript code is not rewritten and may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to use iRule to rename field names in original code.
bugs.fix: Now JavaScript with reserved keywords as field names is handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: BIG-IP UDP virtual server may not send ICMP Destination Unreachable message Code 3 (port unreachable).
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP UDP virtual server may not send an ICMP Destination Unreachable message Code 3 (port unreachable). As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptoms: -- Client applications may not respond or appear to hang. -- When attempting to troubleshoot the connectivity issue from remote devices, no ICMP diagnostic data is available from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: All pool members for the UDP virtual server are unavailable.
bugs.impact: In versions 11.3.0 through 11.4.1, the system silently drops the request. In versions 11.5.0 and later, the system sends back the ICMP message with type 13 ('administratively filtered').

bugs.title: tmm segfault: hud_mptcp_handler HUDCTL_PERFORM_METHOD
bugs.symptoms: TMM segmentation fault in hud_mptcp_handler when servicing HUDCTL_PERFORM_METHOD.
bugs.conditions: This happens when "tmsh show sys conn" command issued with connections in "forwarding" state.
bugs.impact: The tmm will crash and restart.
bugs.workaround: Do not issue "tmsh show sys conn" command.
bugs.fix: This problem is fixed by proper connection queue usage.

bugs.title: PEM source or destination flow filter attempts match against both source and destination IPs of a flow
bugs.symptoms: In the event that the source and destination IPs fall in the same range, it is possible that a source-IP (or destination-IP) based flow-filter may match against the destination-IP (or source-IP) of the packet resulting in potentially wrong flows receiving a policy.
bugs.conditions: Source and Destination networks must have overlapping prefix(es)
bugs.impact: A wrong flow may have inappropriate policies applied to it.
bugs.fix: The bug is fixed and given to the customer as 11.5.0-18 HF.

bugs.title: Early HTTP response might cause rare 'server drained' assertion
bugs.symptoms: Early HTTP response from the server might cause 'server drained' assertion and traffic disruption.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the server sends an early response, which might occur if the server responded before the system completed processing the entire incoming HTTP request data from the client. A filter other than HTTP is also required on the chain.
bugs.impact: The system posts a 'server drained' assertion and traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: None, however, this issue occurs very rarely.
bugs.fix: HTTP will not cause a "server drained" assertion if a server ends a connection in an early server response.

bugs.title: SSL server does not check and validate Change Cipher Spec payload.
bugs.symptoms: SSL server does not check and validate Change Cipher Spec payload.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a clientssl profile is used.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to this issue.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: clientssl profile (SSL server) now checks the Change Cipher Spec payload received from the SSL client, and ensures that the Change Cipher Spec payload is a single byte of value '1'.

bugs.title: Citrix Wyse clients when working with StoreFront in integration mode
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support Citrix Wyse clients when working with StoreFront in integration mode.
bugs.conditions: Using APM with Citrix Wyse clients when working with StoreFront in integration mode.
bugs.impact: Citrix Wyse clients are unable to connect to APM.
bugs.workaround: Use the following iRule: priority 1 when HTTP_REQUEST { set string [HTTP::header value Cookie] if {$string contains "NSC_AAAC=xyz"}{ regsub {NSC_AAAC=xyz;?} $string {} tmp regsub {NSC_DLGE=xyz;?} $tmp {} result HTTP::header replace Cookie $result } }

bugs.title: ASM REST: Incorrect/Duplicate REST id for policy after a copy is made
bugs.symptoms: When comparing two policies using Policy Diff, the system might make a copy of the policies being compared. When this happens, the copy will carry the same REST ID as the original policy. This will confuse REST clients and block BIG-IQ discovery.
bugs.conditions: -- Compare two policies using Policy Diff. -- The system creates a copy.
bugs.impact: The copy will carry the same REST ID as the original policy. This will confuse REST clients and block BIG-IQ discovery.
bugs.workaround: Export the copied policy, delete the duplicate copy, and import the policy again.
bugs.fix: Copied policies now are correctly assigned a new REST ID.

bugs.title: Fixed mistakes in French localization
bugs.symptoms: French localization contains mistakes
bugs.conditions: French locale configured on user machine
bugs.impact: User observes incorrect translation
bugs.fix: Mistakes in French localization were fixed.

bugs.title: Error using GUI when setting debug option on GTM SIP monitor.
bugs.symptoms: Error using GUI to set the debug option on GTM SIP monitor.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when no headers are configured for GTM SIP monitors.
bugs.impact: Cannot set debug using the GUI. System posts the following error: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to set the debug option for GTM SIP monitors.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an error that occurred when no headers were configured for GTM SIP monitors.

bugs.title: IP packets that are fragmented by TMM, the fragments will have their DF bit
bugs.symptoms: IP packets that are fragmented by TMM, the fragments will have their DF bit set if tm.pathmtudiscovery is set to enable (this is the default setting for this dbvar). This is perfectly compliant with RFC standards, and it is the correct thing to do.
bugs.conditions: IP packet that needs to be fragmented by TMM due to MTU restriction on the egress VLAN/interface. Non RFC compliant downstream switches that do not want to see the DF bit set in IP fragments.
bugs.impact: Non-RFC compliant switches by other vendors may reject a fragment with DF bit leading to packet being dropped or treated as a bad packet by them.
bugs.workaround: Setting tm.pathmtudiscovery to disable results in DF bit not being set on the fragments.
bugs.fix: tm.pathmtudontfragoverride dbvar introduced. If the value is changed from 'disable' (this is the default) to 'enable', then DF bit will not be set in IP fragments generated by TMM.

bugs.title: HTTP iRules break Citrix HTML5 functionality
bugs.symptoms: HTTP iRules break Citrix HTML5 functionality.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when HTTP iRule is used on the Citrix HTML5 virtual server.
bugs.impact: Citrix HTML5 functionality breaks
bugs.workaround: Use "priority 1" for HTTP iRules.
bugs.fix: Now HTTP iRules do not affect Citrix HTML5 functionality.

bugs.title: ASM OWA Exchange 2010 Application-Ready Security Policy should change URL content profile.
bugs.symptoms: ASM OWA Exchange 2010 Application-Ready Security Policy should change URL content profile.
bugs.conditions: 1. Apply OWA Exchange 2010 Application-Ready Security Policy template. 2. Template that contains 'apply_value_signature' on /Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync URL.
bugs.impact: Crashing ASM Enforcer daemon.
bugs.workaround: Change the OWA Exchange 2010 Application-Ready Security Policy template to remove 'apply_value_signature' on /Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync URL.
bugs.fix: Changed the OWA Exchange 2010 Application-Ready Security Policy template to remove 'apply_value_signature' on /Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync URL in avoid bd core.

bugs.title: HA group combined with other failover (e.g., VLAN Failsafe or Gateway Failsafe)
bugs.symptoms: Combining HA group with other types of failover mechanism such as VLAN Failsafe or Gateway Failsafe results in traffic going to failed device.
bugs.conditions: HA-group should not be combined with other types of failover mechanism such as VLAN Failsafe or Gateway Failsafe. If these mechanisms are combined, the failsafe causes all traffic groups to go to standby on the failed device.
bugs.impact: Because the HA Group score might favor the failed device, there could be no active traffic group on any device.
bugs.workaround: Replace the failover VLAN or Gateway with an HA group. Note: HA group should not be combined with other types of failover mechanism such as VLAN Failsafe or Gateway Failsafe. If these mechanisms are combined, the failsafe causes all traffic groups to go to standby on the failed device.
bugs.fix: If a device goes to standby due to a failsafe operation, the HA Group Scores on that device are forced to zero, so that the traffic groups can become active on an active device. This is the correct behavior.
bugs.behavior: In the previous code, if a user configured both HA Group Score and an HA Failsafe, when the failsafe triggered, all traffic groups on the failed device would transition to Standby. However, the group score for that device would remain at the prior value so that the traffic group would not become active on another device. The result was a traffic group that was not active on any device. With this change, the traffic group score on the failed device is forced to 0, since the failsafe condition indicates that the device is not acceptable to host any traffic group. The HA Group scoring algorithm then activates the traffic group on the best remaining non-failed device.

bugs.title: The leasepool stat query should only return primary blade data.
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP and "leasepool show" command are not working.
bugs.conditions: Both single and HA Chassis configuration with lease pool.
bugs.impact: SNMP and "leasepool show" command does not return good leasepool stats.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround to this issue.

bugs.title: APM User Identity daemon doesn't generate core
bugs.symptoms: OMAPD is a daemon that stores all the IP->User mappings. It doesn't seem to generate cores. It will be hard to debug issues when it crashes.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Cores will not be generated.
bugs.fix: OMAPD now generates core files making debugging easy.

bugs.title: ConfigSync over IPv6 fails due to wrong rsync formatting
bugs.symptoms: ConfigSync over IPv6 fails due to wrong rsync formatting.
bugs.conditions: Config sync is enabled on IPv6.
bugs.impact: Config sync over ipv6 can not be used. /var/log/ltm logs show following error logs: -- err mcpd[5269]: 01071392:3: Background command '/usr/bin/rsync --rsync-path=/usr/bin/rsync -at --blocking-io /var/named/config/ rsync://fd88:8888:1:f5::1/var_name' failed. The command exited with status 10. -- err mcpd[5269]: 01071392:3: Background command '/usr/bin/rsync --rsync-path=/usr/bin/rsync -at --blocking-io /config/big3d/ rsync://fd88:8888:1:f5::1/big3d' failed. The command exited with status 10.
bugs.workaround: Use config sync over IPv4.

bugs.title: SSL Key/Certificate in different partition with Subject Alternative Name (SAN)
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to create an SSL key/certificate in partition other than Common, with Subject Alternative Name (SAN)
bugs.conditions: In a partition other than Common, create a new SSL key/certificate with SAN.
bugs.impact: SSL key/certificate is not created.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create an SSL key/certificate with SAN in a partition other than Common.
bugs.fix: You can now create an SSL Key/Certificate in partition other than Common, with Subject Alternative Name (SAN).

bugs.title: DPD packet drops with keyed VLAN connections
bugs.symptoms: The DPD (Dead Peer Detection) packets are dropped after the IPsec tunnel is up. This occurs because the BIG-IP system drops DPD packets because keyed VLAN connections are enabled. The system tries to match the VLAN ID along with other parameters for DPD packets.
bugs.conditions: Enable keyed VLAN connections and bring up IPsec tunnel.
bugs.impact: The tunnel does not stay up because of the DPD failure. The match should be done for the host interface instead of the actual VLAN interface.
bugs.fix: Changed the interface match to look up host interface instead of VLAN interface.

bugs.title: If key associated with monitor is stored in external hsm, monitor fails.
bugs.symptoms: Monitor does not work with netHSM keys.
bugs.conditions: Configure netHSM keys and monitor.
bugs.impact: Monitor does not work.

bugs.title: Illegal metachar override can be added to policy which prevents Apply Policy
bugs.symptoms: Illegal metacharacter override can be added to the security policy. This subsequently prevents the security policy from being applied. This can be see in /var/log/asm.1_transformed: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Feb 25 11:35:25 bigip2 info perl[10112]: 01310053:6: ASMConfig change: Parameter P3 [update]: Overridden Value Meta-characters were set to 0x3f - allowed. Feb 25 11:35:31 bigip2 info perl[10112]: 01310053:6: ASMConfig change: Parameter P9 [update]: Overridden Value Meta-characters were set to 0x3a - allowed, 0x7fffffff - allowed. ----------------------------------------------------------------------
bugs.conditions: When upgrading from 11.3 to 11.5, and when importing your exported policy, it produces an error and failed to roll forward.
bugs.impact: This subsequently prevents the policy from being applied. It could not apply configuration; set active failed.

bugs.title: HTTPS monitors do not work with FIPS keys
bugs.symptoms: If HTTPS monitor is configured with FIPS key, the monitor connection to the backend server is unsuccessful and consequently, the corresponding pool is marked down.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP FIPS platforms (except 6900F, 8900F) using FIPS keys with HTTPS monitor(s).
bugs.impact: Pool is incorrectly marked down.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: Monitors configured with FIPS keys now work and the pool status is marked correctly.

bugs.title: RADIUS Authentication fails when username or password contain non-ASCII characters
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS Authentication fails when the logon name contains non-ASCII characters. The problem is caused due to failure in conversion from UTF-8 to Windows-1252.
bugs.conditions: RADIUS authentication is configured and username/password contain non-ASCII characters.
bugs.impact: Users are not able to log in.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: Now it is possible to configure charset decoding behavior. You can decode usernames and passwords into CP-1252 (original behavior) or use UTF-8 charset (in this case, RADIUS Auth sends the username and password unmodified).

bugs.title: Cross-domain functionality is broken in AD Query
bugs.symptoms: Cross-domain functionality is broken in AD Query agent due to DNS resolving library upgrade.
bugs.conditions: AD Query is configured with cross-domain option enabled.
bugs.impact: Users from trusted domains cannot pass access policy because AD Query agent failure.
bugs.fix: AD Query parses DNS response properly and cross-domain functionality works as expected.

bugs.title: The correct cipher may not be chosen on session resumption.
bugs.symptoms: During session resumption, the same cipher must be used as was during the original session. If the original session negotiates cipher A, and the resumed clienthello contains cipher A and B, the BIG-IP system might choose cipher B, which is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: The original ClientHello contains a different cipher list from the resuming one, and the resuming one contains a stronger cipher than was originally chosen.
bugs.impact: Not strictly RFC compliant.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: When the original ClientHello and resuming ClientHello contain different ciphers, if the original cipher is in the resuming ClientHello it will be chosen and the session resumed, otherwise a full handshake will be used.

bugs.title: An MPTCP connection that receives an MP_FASTCLOSE might not clean up its flows
bugs.symptoms: An MPTCP connection that never expires can be seen using the command "tmsh show sys conn". Its idle time periodically resets to 0.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is configured with a TCP profile with "Multipath TCP" enabled. BIG-IP receives an MP_FASTCLOSE while the BIG-IP is advertising a zero window.
bugs.impact: A connection remains that never expires; its idle time periodically resets to 0.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed MP_FASTCLOSE handling.

bugs.title: Tunneled Health Monitor traffic fails on Standby device
bugs.symptoms: Monitor traffic fails on the Standby devices when using a floating local endpoint address for the tunnels.
bugs.conditions: Tunnels are configured with a floating local endpoint address.
bugs.impact: Failover takes longer because the status of the pool server on the Standby device needs to be rediscovered upon failover.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Monitors now work on the Standby devices in an HA configuration.

bugs.title: APM does not support more than one traffic group with different HA order
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support more than one traffic group with different HA order. Here is an example configuration: cm traffic-group /Common/traffic-group-1 { ha-order { /Common/RM-F5-SKY.IT-01.sky.local } unit-id 1 } cm traffic-group /Common/traffic-group-2 { ha-order { /Common/RM-F5-SKY.IT-02.sky.local } unit-id 2 } This configuration causes the creation of an Active/Active HA pair and APM does not support this configuration. APM supports Active/Standby HA pair only.
bugs.conditions: Configure two or more traffic groups with different HA order.
bugs.impact: APM does not support this configuration.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP no longer allows an invalid configuration where APM services exist in more than one traffic group simultaneously

bugs.title: tmctl leasepool_stat and snmp apmLeasepoolStatTable return incorrect values
bugs.symptoms: On a multi-blade chassis, tmctl leasepool_stat for some slots may not be in sync. In addition, query of snmp apmLeasepoolStatTable returns values that do not match the tmctl leasepool_stat output for the current primary slot.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs after a blade or tmm of a blade restarts.
bugs.impact: Incorrect stats only. No impact to fuctionality.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the correct system object to track current primary slot, which ensures that counters in leasepool_stat that have global context (that is, cur_member, cur_assigned, cur_free, max_assigned) are synced to all blades.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when enabling DOS sweep/flood if a TMM process has multiple threads
bugs.symptoms: There is a bug caused by race condition in the library used by the AFM Sweep/flood feature. When the Sweep/flood feature is enabled, if one TMM process has multiple threads, one thread may attempt to access the memory released by another thread at some time. In this situation, TMM may crash due to access an invalid memory segment.
bugs.conditions: (1) AFM sweep/flood enabled (2) A single TMM process has multiple threads. (3) race condition occurs
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable thread or disable sweep/flood
bugs.fix: TMM will not crash when enabling DOS sweep/flood detection feature regardless of threading.

bugs.title: DNS cache resolver cannot send egress traffic on a VLAN with src-ip or dst-ip cmp hash configured
bugs.symptoms: DNS cache resolver or validating resolver does not function properly and fails to resolve DNS requests.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system is using non-default cmp hashes configured on its egress VLANs.
bugs.impact: It is difficult to both use non-default cmp hashes on system VLANs and use a DNS cache resolver on the same BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Configure a separate VLAN for the cache resolver's use that uses the default cmp hash. Set the system's default route to direct resolver traffic to this VLAN. This VLAN can be placed in a new route domain, if other features require route domain zero's default route pointing elsewhere.
bugs.fix: DNS cache resolver or validating resolver now functions properly, successfully resolving DNS requests when using non-default cmp hashes configured on its egress VLANs.

bugs.title: iClient does not handle multiple messages in one payload.
bugs.symptoms: iClient does not handle multiple messages in one payload leading to possible memory leak symptoms.
bugs.conditions: If by chance multiple messages arrive as one from the BIG-IP Edge Client.
bugs.impact: Possible memory leak symptoms.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: If multiple messages arrive from BIG-IP Edge Client in one payload, the system processes them correctly.

bugs.title: HTTP virtual servers with cookie persistence might reset incoming connections
bugs.symptoms: Incoming TCP connection to HTTP virtual server receives RST during 3-way handshake
bugs.conditions: Incoming connection matches existing cookie persistence record and would be persisted to a pool member whose connection limit has been reached.
bugs.impact: TCP connection fails.
bugs.fix: Cookie persistence records are ignored when the connection limit of the persisted pool member has been reached. This results in incoming connections to be offloaded to another pool member (if available).

bugs.title: Incremental sync causes incorrect accounting of member count of pools
bugs.symptoms: If a sync-compatible pool is created and given pool members, pushing that sync operation will cause the member count to be incorrect on all other devices.
bugs.conditions: This only affects device groups where incremental sync is in use.
bugs.impact: The number of pool members will be displayed incorrectly at various points (GTM statistics, the ltmPoolMemberCnt SNMP variable, and the GUI).
bugs.workaround: Perform a sync between the creation of the pool and the pool members.
bugs.fix: The pool member count is now always calculated accurately, even across configuration synchronizations.

bugs.title: Machine Certificate Checker Agent always works in "Match Subject CN to FQDN" mode
bugs.symptoms: Limited/normal user cannot pass Machine Cert Auth through 'Successful' branch if Agent is configured to match certificate by any condition except Match FQDN.
bugs.conditions: Machine Cert Auth agent configured to match certificate by any condition except Match FQDN. Current user has no rights to access private key directly (that means elevation or service is required).
bugs.impact: User cannot pass Machine Cert Authorization.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue that caused Machine Cert Checker service to always work in "Match Subject CN to FQDN" mode.

bugs.title: NVGRE tunnel traffic might stall if the sys db variable tm.tcplargereceiveoffload is set to 'enable'
bugs.symptoms: NVGRE tunnel traffic might stall if the sys db variable tm.tcplargereceiveoffload is set to 'enable'.
bugs.conditions: The sys db variable tm.tcplargereceiveoffload is set to 'enable'.
bugs.impact: NVGRE tunnel traffic might stall.
bugs.workaround: Set the sys db variable tm.tcplargereceiveoffload to 'disable'. The default value of this variable is 'disable', so it is very unlikely that you will encounter this error condition in normal operating conditions.
bugs.fix: NVGRE tunnel traffic no longer stalls when the sys db variable tm.tcplargereceiveoffload is set to 'enable'.

bugs.title: DNS Express zone creation, deletion or updates can slow down or stop other DNS services.
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express zone creation, deletion or updates can slow down or stop other DNS services.
bugs.conditions: Any action that causes a the DNS Express zone database to be updated, including zone creation, deletion or zone transfer.
bugs.impact: Other DNS Services may stop working.
bugs.workaround: Restarting tmm will resolve the issue temporarily, until the next update. If DNS Express is not being used, removing any DNS Express config will prevent this issue from triggering.
bugs.fix: An issue with ann unclosed file descriptor that was impacting DNS Express zone modification has been fixed.

bugs.title: SNMP trap engineID should not be configsynced between HA-pairs
bugs.symptoms: When configuring an engine_id for a SNMPv3 trap destination, the engine_id was synchronized to all HA peers.
bugs.conditions: All
bugs.impact: Received SNMPv3 traps would appear as if they originated from the same Big-IP system after failover to a backup Big-IP.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to disbale configsync (change 'yes' to 'no') on engine_id in /defaults/config_base.conf. However, you must first remount the /usr partition to modify the file and then run tmsh load. For more information on remounting the /usr partition, see SOL11302: The /usr file system is mounted in read-only mode at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/11000/300/sol11302.html

bugs.title: IP iRules may cause TMM to segfault in low memory scenarios
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core during low memory conditions when executing iRules containing the following commands: IP::local_addr IP::remote_addr IP::client_addr IP::server_addr
bugs.conditions: No memory available to allocate IP iRule objects.
bugs.impact: TMM will be restarted.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: Memory allocations are verified when using the following iRules: IP::local_addr IP::remote_addr IP::client_addr IP::server_addr

bugs.title: Added support of SAML Single Logout to Edgeclient.
bugs.symptoms: SAML single logout does not work on BIG-IP Edge Client. The BIG-IP (as IdP) system shows the session as active.
bugs.conditions: Edge client, BIG-IP as SAML.
bugs.impact: Edge client logout doesn't function correctly.
bugs.fix: SAML single logout is now supported on BIG-IP Edge Client.

bugs.title: userauth_hostbased mismatch: warnings from VIPRION for localhost or slotN
bugs.symptoms: Error messages indicating userauth_hostbased mismatch are posted.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION-based system or VIPRION-hosted vCMP guest. This also occurs on a single slot.
bugs.impact: The sshd userauth_hostbased mismatch messages are innocuous only if they appear for the client sending one of the following: localhost, localhost.localdomain, slot1, slot2, slot3, slot4, slot5, slot6, slot7, or slot8. The system might post warning messages from sshd similar to the following: userauth_hostbased mismatch: client sends slot1, but the system resolves 127.3.0.1 to 127.3.0.1.
bugs.fix: The system no longer posts extraneous warning messages caused by SSH connections from peers on the 127.0.0.0/8 subnet.

bugs.title: Java core formed when modifying global-settings.
bugs.symptoms: Unknown
bugs.conditions: This is a general problem related to low stack size, but was observed during internal testing of /sys global-settings.
bugs.impact: Unknown
bugs.fix: JVM's default stack size per thread has been increased to 384KB

bugs.title: clientssl profile validation fails to detect config with no cert/key name and no cert/key
bugs.symptoms: The system does not prevent creation of a clientssl profile with no cert-key-chain name and no cert/key (or a cert/key of 'default'), and does not post an error alerting the user to the condition. The system creates the profile without error. This can cause issues when upgrading.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when attempting to create a clientssl profile without a cert-key-chain name or cert/key, or a cert/key of 'default'. Note: The system should prevent this, but does not do so in versions 11.5.1, 11.5.2, or 11.5.3.
bugs.impact: The system incorrectly allows a blank cert-key-chain name and an empty cert/key in clientssl profiles. When upgrading such a profile to versions 11.5.4, 11.6.0, 12.0.0, or later, the configuration fails to load with a message similar to the following: -- 01070315:3: profile /Common/my_client_ssl requires a key Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. -- 01071ac9:3: Unable to load the certificate file () - error:2006D080:BIO routines:BIO_new_file:no such file.
bugs.workaround: Use the following steps to work around this issue: -- To correct the configuration, run the following command: sed -ie '/"" { }/d' /config/bigip.conf. -- To load the modified configuration, run the following command: tmsh load sys config. Note: To determine whether profiles are affected, run the following command: grep '"" { }' /config/bigip.conf -A2 -B1. On affected profiles, the system returns the following output: cert-key-chain { "" { }.
bugs.fix: The system now presents an error message when attempting to create a clientssl profile without a cert-key-chain name and a cert/key (or a cert/key of 'default'), and prevents the creation of the profile, so potential upgrade failures no longer occur.

bugs.title: small memory leak observed in audit_forwarder
bugs.symptoms: some small memory leak observed in audit_fowarer
bugs.conditions: Audit_forwarder is used, especially in some error conditions.
bugs.impact: memory usage of audit_forwarder increases at a very slow pace.
bugs.fix: No more memory leak observed after fix.

bugs.title: UDP profile improvement for flexible TTL handling
bugs.symptoms: The UDP virtual used by PEM treats TTL differently than the standard UDP forwarding virtual. The standard UDP forwarding virtual decrements TTL whereas the PEM UDP virtual reinitializes TTL to 255. In the event that there is a routing loop in the network which traverses a BIG-IP running PEM, this behavior would prevent TTL from expiring and thus exacerbate the effects of the loop.
bugs.conditions: This inconsistency of TTL handling between standard LTM virtual and PEM virtual (with PEM enabled).
bugs.impact: A PEM virtual doesn't have the flexibility to decrement the TTL value on PEM UDP listener because it is always reset to 255.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this.
bugs.fix: With this improvement, you will have the flexibility to define the TTL handling behavior (decrease by 1 vs. resetting to 255). This can be archived by change db variable(tmm.udp.ttl.mode) on 11.6.0 hotfix: tmsh modify sys db tmm.udp.ttl.mode value "decrement"

bugs.title: Nexthop to tmm0 ref-count leakage could cause TMM core
bugs.symptoms: Each use of the interface tmm0 for inter-TMM communication is supposed to increment its count of nexthop references. When the use of the interface is expired, the reference count is supposed to decrement, but in this case, the reference count is not decremented.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when TMM runs over an extended period of time, and internal communication between TMMs over tmm0 is heavy during the period.
bugs.impact: Reference count leaks, which causes the count to monotonically increase, which eventually might cause TMM to crash and restart.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: The nexthop reference count of the interface tmm0 is thoroughly examined and corrected, so it no longer leaks ref counts.

bugs.title: 'Show all' button has no effect or becomes hidden for short period of time
bugs.symptoms: If you update the time scale with your mouse when looking at AVR statistics, a 'Show all' button will momentarily appear, then disappear after a few seconds. Clicking it does nothing. The button is not supposed to appear at all.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when viewing any statistics in Statistics :: Analytics and changing the time scale.
bugs.impact: Show All button appears but does not persist, and clicking Show All does nothing
bugs.workaround: Manually extend the time range to the full scope of time you wish to see
bugs.fix: The Show All button has been removed from the analytics pages.

bugs.title: Portal Access issues with Firefox version 26.0.0 or later
bugs.symptoms: Using Firefox version 26.0.0 or later with some web-applications can fail. The page may stop loading and/or rendering page.
bugs.conditions: Firefox version 26.0.0 or later, asynchronously loaded script which works with cookies and DOM in same time. A good example is google analytics script in the page.
bugs.impact: Web-application stops loading/rendering.
bugs.workaround: No general workaround.
bugs.fix: When using portal access on Firefox with some applications, the browser would go into deadlock. This no longer occurs.

bugs.title: TMM crash on UDP DNS virtual without datagram-load-balancing enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash on UDP DNS virtual without datagram-load-balancing enabled.
bugs.conditions: DNS virtual server without datagram lb mode.
bugs.impact: TMM crash with a backtrace including dns_dev_pool coring at line 360. Failover and potential traffic interruption.
bugs.workaround: Enable datagram-lb-mode in the UDP profile used by the DNS virtual server, or turn off DNS queuing via the db variable dns.queuing.

bugs.title: Added support for BIG-IP 10350N NEBS platform.
bugs.fix: This release adds support for the BIG-IP 10350N NEBS platform.

bugs.title: Improved handling of signature_algorithms extension to avoid using SHA1 in TLS handshake signatures
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP uses SHA1 in handshake signature, even though the client indicates support for stronger hash algorithms.
bugs.conditions: When BIG-IP acts as TLS server (applies to clientssl SSL Profile): - SSL Profile "SSL Sign Hash" set to ANY. The use of other choices is not recommended. - Client sends signature_algorithms extension that includes SHA256. - ECDSA X.509 certificate has additional logic. If the TLS client doesn't send signature_algorithms, BIG-IP will choose SHA256.
bugs.impact: The updated code respects client signature_algorithms extension. If possible, BIG-IP now prefers SHA256 in the handshake signature based on the content of the signature_algorithms extension. BIG-IP further upgrades the hash algorithm to SHA384 from SHA256 when P-384 is used, e.g. when P-384 ECDSA X.509 certificate is used in the handshake. This additional enhancement only applies to the code base starting from 12.0; it was not ported to the 11.x code base. The signature_algorithms extension is defined in TLS 1.2. It's not not present in prior versions of the protocol. This logic attempts to avoid the use of SHA1 in TLS handshake, whenever possible. This change does not affect signatures used in X.509 certificates as these signatures are created by the X.509 CAs and not by BIG-IP. The only time SHA1 will be used in the handshake signature is when either of the following is true: - RSA key is used and the signature_algorithms extension is missing or - signature_algorithms is present and only lists SHA1. These conditions are expected to not hold for modern TLS clients, resulting in the upgrade to the SHA256 or better.
bugs.behavior: Respect client signature_algorithms extension. If possible, prefer SHA256 in handshake signature.

bugs.title: VMWare View applications are not available on BIG-IP APM webtops
bugs.symptoms: VMWare View applications are not available on BIG-IP APM webtops.
bugs.conditions: Beginning in BIG-IP APM 11.6.0 HF4, VMware Horizon 6 View applications can be made available on BIG-IP APM webtops. When you integrate the BIG-IP APM system with VMware View Connection Servers, BIG-IP APM webtops can now present View applications as well as remote desktops.
bugs.impact: In versions prior to BIG-IP APM 11.6.0 HF4, the BIG-IP APM system can only present VMware Horizon 6 View remote desktops. VMware Horizon 6 View applications are only available from View desktop resources.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is expanded functionality.
bugs.fix: VMware View applications are available on APM webtop now.

bugs.title: SPDY may cause the TMM to crash if it aborts while there are stalled streams.
bugs.symptoms: If SPDY has a stalled stream and it is being aborted, it may cause the TMM to crash due to referencing cleared state. 100 Continue messages appeared in response bodies. 100 Continue responses sent in the same packet as the response could stall the stream.
bugs.conditions: SPDY aborts due to a miss-ordered event. SPDY then sees egress, and marks the stream as stalled. SPDY aborts the connection to the client, and marks the stream as unknown. Finally, the stream aborts again and dereferences the NULL pointer to the client when it tries to unstall itself. A 100 Continue message in a response, either by itself, or in the same packet as the response body.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: SPDY will no longer cause a TMM crash when it aborts, followed by egress, followed by a second abort. SPDY will handle 100 Continue messages correctly by ignoring them.

bugs.title: mcpd instances on secondary blades might restart on boot
bugs.symptoms: Secondary blades' mcpd instances might restart on boot.
bugs.conditions: This might occur intermittently on VIPRION bladed systems or VCMP guests. This might be the result of a race condition that occurs when /config is synced between the blades and when the mcpd process starts.
bugs.impact: The mcpd process restarts on secondary blades. The process eventually returns to normal, and the system finishes booting. The system posts messages similar to the following: 01071038:5: Secondaries couldn't load master key from the database. 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01071029:5: Master Key not present.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: SIP media flows do not count toward LSN pool client connection limit
bugs.symptoms: When SIP is used with LSN pools, the media connections do not count towards the LSN client connection limit count.
bugs.conditions: SIP ALG is configured with an LSN pool whose client connection limit value is greater than zero.
bugs.impact: Media connections are not counted. This might result in a subscriber being able to create more connections than specified by LSN pool client connection limit

bugs.title: Assigning 'after' object to a variable causes memory leaks
bugs.symptoms: Assigning 'after' object to a variable prevents the release of the 'after' object and its related connflow object, resulting in a memory leak for 'connflow', 'tcl (variable)', 'tclrule_pcb', and 'filter (variable)'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the 'after' iRule command and assigning it to a variable.
bugs.impact: TMM crash or TMM memory usage increases.
bugs.workaround: Unset the variable containing the 'after' object, for example: when HTTP_REQUEST priority 800 { set SCRIPT_ID [\ after $static::one_second { log local0. "$LOG_MSG" } \ ] } when CLIENT_CLOSED { unset SCRIPT_ID }
bugs.fix: Assigning 'after' object to a variable no longer causes memory leaks.

bugs.title: in VPE %xx symbols such as the variable assign agent might be invalidly decoded.
bugs.symptoms: in VPE %xx symbols might invalidly decode If user assignment string contains percent encoded symbols like: "%60", "%7E", "%21", "%40", "%23" etc Saved string is written properly but re-readed and displayed as character "`", "~", "!", "@", "#" Therefore new saving might cause uneeded re-encoding of such symbols
bugs.conditions: Variable assign agent. Assigned string contains %xx symbol
bugs.impact: Medium. Customer is confused and might not be able to modify saved and then loaded string
bugs.workaround: 1. Direct bigip.conf editing 2. Saving proper string in other location and copy paste before modification so %xx encoded symbols would stay preserved
bugs.fix: Issue fixed, encoding doesn't reencode/redecode symbols anymore.

bugs.title: IPsec IKEv1 configuration change resets all existing IPsec IKEv1 tunnels.
bugs.symptoms: IPsec IKEv1 configuration change resets all existing IPsec IKEv1 tunnels.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the IPsec IKEv1 configuration is modified.
bugs.impact: All existing IPsec IKEv1 tunnels are reset.
bugs.workaround: None available.

bugs.title: AFM Optimizations to improve run-time and memory usage.
bugs.symptoms: AFM Optimizations to improve run-time and memory usage.
bugs.impact: Potential run-time and memory-usage issues.
bugs.conditions: Running AFM.

bugs.title: Removal of AFM inline rules
bugs.symptoms: All inline rules have been removed from AFM as of this release. All new rules must be created in policies. An update script is available to move current inline rules to policies.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on upgrade to 11.6.0 or later.
bugs.impact: Inline rules are no longer supported.
bugs.workaround: Management port rules are excluded, and are still configured inline. In place of inline rules, users should create firewall policies which are attached by reference to firewall contexts as necessary. During an upgrade, existing inline rules associated with these contexts are moved into new auto-generated policies. These auto-generated policies are prepended with VersionUpgradeAutoGenPolicy- to simplify identification. Auto-generated policies are automatically enforced on the respective context to which the previous inline rules apply. If you have HA pairs, auto-generated policies that are applied to non-floating self IPs are usable only for that self IP, and are not synced among HA peers. This behavior replicates the previous behavior for inline rules applied to non-floating self IPs. Other auto-generated policies are not affected. However, if a policy generated for another context is later applied to a non-floating self IP, the sync for that policy will be permanently disabled.

bugs.title: Invalid data is merged with next valid SIP message causing SIP connection failures
bugs.symptoms: SIP phone connections fail.
bugs.conditions: SIP over UDP.
bugs.impact: SIP phone connections fail.
bugs.workaround: Create a packet filter to discard the invalid UDP datagrams.
bugs.fix: Invalid UDP datagrams that interfered with SIP processing are now dropped.

bugs.title: RTSP profile idle timeout is not applied if it is longer than the TCP profile timeout
bugs.symptoms: The minimum of the Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) and TCP profile timeouts is applied to the RTP and RTCP connflows associated with an RTSP connection.
bugs.conditions: This problem can leave UDP connflows for RTP and RTCP open for a shorter time period than desired.
bugs.impact: The shorter timeout (either RTSP profile or TCP profile) is used for the idle timeout on RTP and RTCP flows associated with an RTSP connection.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue configure both the TCP and the RTSP profile so that the idle timeout periods are the same.
bugs.fix: With the fix, the RTP and RTCP timeouts use the value configured in the RTSP profile.

bugs.title: Read-only account can save system config
bugs.symptoms: A read-only user can run the tmsh save sys config command, which saves the configuration including changes made by other read/write users.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when logged in as a read-only user and running save sys config in tmsh.
bugs.impact: Read-only users are able to run save sys config in tmsh.

bugs.title: Error messages are not clear when adding member to device trust fails
bugs.symptoms: If you cannot reach the IP address of a device that you are adding to a device trust then the error message does not properly display in the GUI. For some errors the message is empty and for some errors the message contains unformatted xml data.
bugs.conditions: This problem occurs when adding a peer or subordinate to the device trust where the IP address cannot be reached.
bugs.impact: User cannot be sure what the problem with adding the device really is.
bugs.workaround: Verify that the address is correct and that you are able to route to the device you are trying to add to the device trust.
bugs.fix: During trust initiation when the peer is unreachable, the system now posts the error message is "This device is not found."

bugs.title: Monitor traffic rejected with ICMP message, causing node down
bugs.symptoms: Firewall rules intended to restrict access to an APM daemon running on the BIG-IP system might incorrectly interfere with TCP monitor traffic generated by the BIG-IP system on port 54321.
bugs.conditions: This can occur even if a BIG-IP system is not provisioned for APM or SWG.
bugs.impact: This may result in monitors incorrectly failing, and pool members incorrectly marked down. A packet capture of the monitor traffic will show the BIG-IP system receive a SYN/ACK from a pool member, and respond with an ICMP port unreachable error.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, add these iptables commands to the '/config/startup' script, and reboot the BIG-IP system (or manually run these commands once). These commands modify the firewall rule to prevent interference with monitoring: /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 54321 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable /sbin/iptables -D INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 54321 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset /sbin/iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 54321 --tcp-flags ACK,SYN SYN -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset
bugs.fix: Firewall rules no longer incorrectly interfere with TCP monitor traffic generated by the BIG-IP system on port 54321.

bugs.title: BIG-IP might send both session ID and server certificate during renegotiation
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP initiates renegotiation, it might send both the session ID and the server certificate. This will cause the client to alert() with `unexpected message'
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP initiates renegotiation.
bugs.impact: The SSL connection will fail.
bugs.fix: If BIG-IP intends to do a complete handshake it will not send a session ID. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Multiple content type headers detection
bugs.symptoms: ASM bypass techniques were found during Pentest.
bugs.conditions: Send traffic with multiple content type headers.
bugs.impact: Causes ASM to misbehave within the headers request parser, and fails to detect the relevant requests' content type.

bugs.title: When creating users, their role and partition information are normally expected.
bugs.symptoms: If for some special reasons, the role and partition information are not present, there are two cases where this might occur: When the user's role and partition information is not provided, by default, the no-access role and all partitions are assumed. If the user's role and partition are explicitly deleted, this is also allowed with no further error message. This is potentially useful in cases where you want to preserve the user data such as password for later re-activation the user. In both cases, the user cannot login successfully due to the lack of the necessary role-partition information.
bugs.conditions: User's role and partition information is missing or removed.
bugs.impact: The user with missing role and partition information is prohibited from login.

bugs.title: ICMP PMTU handling causes multiple retransmissions
bugs.symptoms: When an improperly large TCP Maximum Segment Size (MSS) triggers ICMP PMTU messages, TCP responds by resending the entire send queue with the new MSS.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you configure a path with an MTU less than 1500 Bytes and attempt a file transfer with initcwnd greater than 1.
bugs.impact: Large amounts of duplicate retransmission.
bugs.fix: No multiple retransmission of the entire send queue when the MSS size is improperly large.

bugs.title: HTTP filter waits until part of the body is received before sending small headers
bugs.symptoms: If the HTTP filter expects a body attached to a response, the filter waits for part of that body to arrive before sending headers smaller than 16 KB.This is done for performance reasons, to minimize the number of packets sent. (Since the headers are usually smaller than a single packet.) If a misconfigured server waits to send a body, or fails to send one at all, the BIG-IP system waits until the connection ends before sending the response. This has been seen to affect redirect responses with no content length header.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- A response indicating a body. -- The headers are smaller than 16 KB. -- The body takes time to arrive, or never arrives at all.
bugs.impact: The connection might appear to stall until the server-side sends a body or disconnects.
bugs.workaround: The headers can be padded to be larger than 16 KB by an iRule. (This causes the BIG-IP system not to wait.) HTTP::respond might also be useful to emulate a redirect response manually.

bugs.title: Improper regex/glob validation in web-acceleration and http-compression profiles
bugs.symptoms: The use of regex or glob patterns in certain MCP configuration objects leads to inconsistent parsing across MCP and TMM. For glob patterns, for example, the TMM produces an error indicating that the regex is invalid, while entries such as *.js are correctly treated as globs.
bugs.conditions: MCP configuration objects supporting regex and glob inclusion/exclusion patterns lead to inconsistent parsing across MCP/TMM.
bugs.impact: Cacheable objects are improperly cached or are not cached, or objects are deflated or are not deflated in opposition to the customer's intent.
bugs.fix: The parsing of regex and glob patterns has been improved for consistent behavior across MCP and TMM.

bugs.title: DNS cache statistics incorrect
bugs.symptoms: DNS Cache statistics might skew high due to shared information between TMMs incrementing the same statistic multiple times.
bugs.conditions: Any DNS Cache might see this issue.
bugs.impact: DNS Cache Statistics are listed as higher than they should have been.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround.
bugs.fix: DNS Cache Statistics are no longer being incremented multiple times for the same action.

bugs.title: EM analytic does not build SSL connection with discovered BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: EM analytic does not build SSL connection with discovered BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: When using management SSL client profile.
bugs.impact: EM analytic cannot connect to discovered BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Enterprise Manager analytics now works with BIG-IP systems running version 11.5.0 or later.

bugs.title: Separate MIBS needed for tracking Access Sessions and Connectivity Sessions
bugs.symptoms: Using MIB F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmGlobalConnectivityStatCurConns displays incorrect information and description.
bugs.conditions: Using SNMP MIB F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmGlobalConnectivityStatCurConns.
bugs.impact: Using MIB F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmGlobalConnectivityStatCurConns displays incorrect information and description.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Access Sessions and Connectivity Sessions are now exposed correctly in SNMP MIBS.

bugs.title: Home directory is purged when the admin changes user password.
bugs.symptoms: When an admin changes a user's password, the contents of the home directory are purged, that is, the system deletes some or all of the files in that user's home directory.
bugs.conditions: This happens whenever a user's password is modified. Can also be triggered by an upgrade from 10.x.
bugs.impact: Some or all of the files in that user's home directory are deleted.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround for the basic case at this time. However, when this is caused by a 10.x-to-11.x upgrade, the original files can be recovered by booting back into the 10.x boot location and copying them off the system (or by extracting them from a UCS, or by mounting the root lvm volume from the previous boot location).
bugs.fix: On password change by an admin user for a user, the home directory of the user is left intact.

bugs.title: Explicit links lost after adding server IP addresses using GUI
bugs.symptoms: When using the web user interface to add server IP addresses to an existing Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB) server, any existing server IP addresses that have an explicit link configured are lost.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after adding a new IP address to the server. This can be examined by using tmsh to list the server and its associated explicit link.
bugs.impact: If a link goes down, everything on the link goes down, so it is possible that unexpected resources will go down, if the GTM servers or virtual servers lose their explicitly defined links. Preliminary testing suggests that when these explicit links are lost, GTM might auto-match the server IP addresses (or virtual servers) to a different link, and this link might be different from the one the user explicitly configured.
bugs.workaround: When configuring servers that are using explicit links, using tmsh (not the web UI) to edit the server properties, prevents explicit links from being erased.

bugs.title: Policy History Files are missing after device group sync
bugs.symptoms: Policy history revision files in the /var/ts/dms/policy/policy_versions/* directories are erased after a device group sync.
bugs.conditions: 1. Set up a sync-failover device group with ASM sync enabled. 2. Create a policy and synchronize the devices
bugs.impact: Old policy version files disappear every other sync.
bugs.workaround: Manually sync again after a spurious ASM change.

bugs.title: Memory issues possible with really long interface names
bugs.symptoms: When an interface has a very long name, it is possible for various functions to overrun the memory allocated and cause other problems. The other problems will vary, depending on what is running at the time of the memory overrun.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if the interface is associated with a non-default route domain.
bugs.impact: Possible loss of client connectivity or random errors possibly resulting in cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Long interface names no longer cause issues.

bugs.title: Platform marketing name for B4300 is incorrectly shown as A108
bugs.symptoms: When viewing the hardware information, the name will display as A108 instead of BIG-IP VPR-B4300
bugs.conditions: Running Viprion B4300 and reviewing the hardware information via one of the management consoles.
bugs.impact: Incorrect name displayed.
bugs.fix: Platform marketing name for BIG-IP VPR-B4300 is now correct when viewed from management console.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not support IPv4-mapped-IPv6 notation in the configuration with prefix length greater than 32
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not allow IPv4-mapped-IPv6 notation (with prefix length greater than 32) in tmsh or GUI. When trying to add '::ffff:0.0.0.0/96' to an address list or directly to a rule the system posts an error: Error parsing IP address: ::ffff:0.0.0.0/96.
bugs.conditions: -- IPv4-mapped-IPv6 notation in the configuration. -- Adding prefix length greater than 32.
bugs.impact: Cannot successfully specify an IPv4-mapped-IPv6 block to be configured in AFM firewall rule (and possibly other AFM configurations as well).
bugs.workaround: To drop the IPv4-mapped-IPv6 block, enable the following DoS db variable: dos.dropv4mapped.
bugs.fix: You can now use tmsh for IPv4-mapped-IPv6 notation with prefix length greater than 32.

bugs.title: On a virtual server with the ipother profile assigned, iRule firing on CLIENT_ACCEPTED with discard or reject action may cause TMM to core
bugs.symptoms: When using ipother profile, if there is an iRule that fires on CLIENT_ACCEPTED that contains a discard or reject action, TMM is going to failover.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with ipother profile and an iRule firing on CLIENT_ACCEPTED with discard or reject action.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use CLIENT_DATA as the firing event for the iRule. Will have the same expected result when discarding the connection.

bugs.title: Citrix Storefront native protocol
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support native Citrix StoreFront protocol when APM is configured in proxy mode with Citrix StoreFront. It does support the legacy protocol, but this means that clients can connect to only one application.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in deployments using Citrix StoreFront.
bugs.impact: Clients can only connect to one application.
bugs.fix: Now APM supports native Citrix StoreFront protocol when APM is configured in proxy mode with Citrix StoreFront. To enable this protocol with existing configurations, please recreate accounts in Citrix Receiver clients.

bugs.title: Persistence record marked expired though related connection is still active
bugs.symptoms: A persistence record might be marked expired even though its corresponding connection is still active and passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using persistence.
bugs.impact: Persist records disappear in spite of flow activity that is more recent than the persist timeout.
bugs.workaround: Set the timeout of persist to at least 33 seconds longer than the related flow timeout.
bugs.fix: Persistence records are maintained when connection and persistence timeouts are with 33 seconds of each other.

bugs.title: Sensor read faults with DC power supply
bugs.symptoms: While running BIG-IP v11.5.0 or later on a BIG-IP 2000-/4000-/5000-/7000-/10000-series appliances using DC power supplies, error messages containing the following strings may appear in /var/log/ltm: err chmand[####]: 012a0003:3: Sensor read fault for Power supply #1 fan-1 err chmand[[####]: 012a0003:3: Sensor read fault for Power supply #1 meas. inlet temp err chmand[####]: 012a0003:3: Sensor read fault for Power supply #2 fan-1 err chmand[####]: 012a0003:3: Sensor read fault for Power supply #2 meas. inlet temp
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP 2000-/4000-/5000-/7000-/10000-series appliances - DC power supplies (FND850 for 10000-series, FND300 for 2000-/4000-/5000-/7000-series) - Running BIG-IP v11.5.0 or later.
bugs.impact: These errors result from a mismatch in the list of power supply sensors queried by BIG-IP, and the sensors actually present in a DC power supply. These errors do not indicate a problem with the power supply in question.
bugs.workaround: These errors, when occurring under the conditions described, can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: Power supply sensor values are successfully read without errors on BIG-IP 2000-/4000-/5000-/7000-/10000-series appliances with DC power supplies.

bugs.title: Direct links for frame content, with 'Frame.src = url'
bugs.symptoms: Direct links in web-application with Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: Direct links for frame content, when using 'Frame.src = url'.
bugs.impact: Web-Application misfunction.
bugs.fix: Correct rewriting for obj.src = some_url was added to support Web Applications.

bugs.title: L4 forwarding and TSO can cause rare TMM outages
bugs.symptoms: In certain rare circumstances using L4 forwarding and TSO, the MSS sizes on client and server sides in combination with internal processing can cause an internal mismatch resulting in a TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: This applies only when using L4 forwarding virtuals with TSO; additional exact external conditions are still under investigation.
bugs.impact: This issue causes a failover or TMM outage.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM will properly handle cases when the MSS sizes would have led to underflow.

bugs.title: SSL Session resumption with hybrid handshake might fail
bugs.symptoms: When using SSL session resumption during a hybrid handshake (sslv2 with tls1.0), the resumption might fail.
bugs.conditions: SSL session resumption is allowed, and is using a hybrid handshake.
bugs.impact: Session resumption would fail, necessitating a complete handshake to reconnect.
bugs.workaround: Disable SSL Session Cache
bugs.fix: SSL Session resumption now works in all expected cases.

bugs.title: DTLS cannot handle client certificate when client does not send CertVerify message.
bugs.symptoms: For DTLS, CCS record will be held until all other handshake messages besides Finish are handled. When pcm is set to request, client may not send CertVfy message. BIG-IP system waits for CertVfy until the timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- Reordered DTLS handshake. -- Client does not send CertVerify message
bugs.impact: BIG-IP waits for CertVfy until timeout.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Add BIG-IP hostname to system's static DNS host entries
bugs.symptoms: In a GTM deployed configuration BIG-IP resolves to different IP addresses. If the IP address used when establishing a network access connection is different while accessing (after the network access is established) a corporate resource, then this corporate URL access will be denied.
bugs.conditions: GTM deployment. BIG-IP network access configuration and corporate resource resolves to different BIG-IP than the one to which network access is established.
bugs.impact: Access to corporate resources might be denied.
bugs.workaround: Configure BIG-IP system with static host DNS entry.
bugs.fix: A certain scenario in GTM deployment was fixed where access to certain corporate resource might be denied despite network access connection.

bugs.title: iOS Edge Client is not able to establish per-app VPN connections with APM when it has VPE with On-Demand certificate authentication without assigned webtop resource.
bugs.symptoms: iOS Edge Client is not able to establish per-app VPN connections with APM when it has VPE with On-Demand certificate authentication agent without assigned webtop resource.
bugs.conditions: VPE with On-Demand certificate authentication without assigned webtop resource.
bugs.impact: Cannot use iOS Edge Client to establish per-app VPN connections.
bugs.workaround: Add resource assignment agent with webtop resource.

bugs.title: Web scraping/brute force may break application on IE6/IE7
bugs.symptoms: A blank page is shown on IE6/IE7 browsers when Web Scraping is enabled with Bot Detection set to Blocking mode, or Client Side Integrity Defense is enabled in Blocking mode in either Web Scraping or Brute Force.
bugs.conditions: 1. Clients using IE6 or IE7 browser. 2. Web Scraping is enabled with Bot Detection set to blocking mode, OR Client Side Integrity Defense is enabled in blocking mode in either Web Scraping or Brute Force.
bugs.impact: 1. Blank page is shown and user does not reach the page

bugs.title: Multipath TCP (MPTCP): TMM crash in stockpile management
bugs.symptoms: The tmm may core when using MPTCP.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under conditions of MPTCP heavy usage.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Traffic misclassified and matching wrong rule in CPM policy.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic matches the wrong rule in Centralized Policy Management (CPM) policy. User traffic is matching either uri or host headers to rules that should not match the header.
bugs.conditions: This issue is caused by long list of hosts in certain rules resulting in wrong execution of statemachine due to wraparound in shifting.
bugs.impact: Misclassification and forwarding of traffic.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A range check has now been added to correctly classify and forward traffic in the case of incorrect rules in CPM policies.

bugs.title: Remotely authenticated users may still obey local password policy
bugs.symptoms: If a local password policy with password expiry is set, even remotely authenticated users are subject to the password policy. This may disallow users whose password has been remotely authenticated but who have an expired password.
bugs.conditions: Local password policy is set, but remote authentication used.
bugs.impact: some users may be locked out after the password policy expires their password.
bugs.workaround: Do not use a local password policy with remote authentication.
bugs.fix: User created when remote auth is configured will not have password expiry applied.

bugs.title: tmm crash when using sip_info persistence without a sip profile
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes. You see the following in /var/log/ltm: notice hudfilter_init: filter 'SIPP' init failed.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a virtual server with sip_info persistence but a sip profile is not assigned.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Make sure you configure a sip profile on any virtual that has sip_info persistence configured.
bugs.fix: If you try to configure sip_info persistence on a virtual without a sip profile, you will get a validation error: 01070651:3: SIP persistence on virtual server /Common/test requires a TCP/UDP/SCTP profile, SIP profile, and cannot be used with an FTP/HTTP profile.

bugs.title: Configuration utility allows for mismatch in IP protocol and transport profile
bugs.symptoms: tmsh allows configuration of a virtual server with mismatched ip-protocol and transport-layer profile. For example, ip-protocol tcp with a UDP profile or ip-protocol udp with a TCP profile.
bugs.conditions: Configure a virtual server with mismatched ip-protocol and transport-layer profiles (e.g. ip-protocol udp, profiles { tcp }).
bugs.impact: Traffic reaching a misconfigured virtual server can crash tmm, resulting in an outage.
bugs.workaround: Configure virtual server with matching ip-protocol and transport-layer profile.

bugs.title: FTP active mode does not work with NAT64 and inherit enabled
bugs.symptoms: An FTP connection in active mode and with inherit-parent-profile enabled in FTP profile using LSN source address translation does not work.
bugs.conditions: Config includes a virtual with nat64 enabled with an attached ftp with inherit-parent-profile enabled. Also using LSN source-address translation. Then initiate an FTP connection then switch ftp mode to active. This problem is only seen when the "Inherit Parent Profile" box is checked within the FTP profile.
bugs.impact: You are unable to use FTP in active mode with this configuration.

bugs.title: When DNS resolution for AppTunnel resource fails, the resource is removed
bugs.symptoms: App tunnel gets removed from webtop if one of items is not DNS resolvable.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when at least one of items in app tunnel resource is not DNS resolvable.
bugs.impact: If one of the items in app tunnel resource is not DNS resolvable, the app tunnel resource gets removed.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: APM removes an app tunnel resource from a webtop only if all resource items are not DNS resolvable; otherwise, the app tunnel continues to work with resource items that are DNS resolvable.

bugs.title: Loading of configuration fails intermittently due to WOC Plug-in-related issues.
bugs.symptoms: Loading of configuration fails intermittently due to WOC Plug-in-related issues.
bugs.conditions: This rarely encountered issue occurs when the BIG-IP system is configured with AAM (formerly WOM/WOC/WAM) objects when there is an attempt to change/load the configuration.
bugs.impact: Configuration load fails. Cannot change the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Manually change the configuration and restart/reboot the system.
bugs.fix: Loading of configuration no longer fails due to WOC Plug-in-related issues.

bugs.title: Cookies handling issue with Safari on iOS6, iOS7
