bugs.symptoms: Wrong cookies set send to backend with some requests. The issue is very intermittent.
bugs.conditions: Web-Application with Portal Access when Safari on iOS6, iOS7 is used.
bugs.impact: Web-Application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Web applications with portal access using Safari on iOS now work correctly when an 'onbeforeunload' event occurs.

bugs.title: EAM not redirecting stdout/stderr from standard libraries to /var/log/apm
bugs.symptoms: Logs from standard libraries were not redirected to /var/log/apm in EAM plugin.
bugs.conditions: Stdout/stderr from standard libraries are affected.
bugs.impact: stderr/ stdout from standard libraries were not logged and that impacted troubleshooting effort.
bugs.workaround: No workaround to log stderr/stdout
bugs.fix: [OAM] Redirecting stdout/stderr from standard libraries to /var/log/apm. This is now fixed.

bugs.title: No EAM- log stacktrace in /var/log/apm on EAM crash event.
bugs.symptoms: On EAM crash event, stack trace or fault address were not logged in /var/log/apm.
bugs.conditions: EAM crash and the signal handler did not log much details on /var/log/apm
bugs.impact: Core debugging is made easier with improved signal handler to log stack trace, fault address etc.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: [OAM] Improve signal handler to log stack trace, fault address etc. to /var/log/apm - this is now fixed.

bugs.title: SSL Persistence Profile Causing High CPU Usage
bugs.symptoms: Some connections through a virtual server using SSL persistence hang and cause a high CPU condition in tmm.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when SSL persistence is configured as the default persistence profile, and there is a fallback profile of either source_addr or dest_addr.
bugs.impact: Large increase in CPU usage on the box and a percentage of SSL connections through the virtual server are delayed and eventually reset
bugs.fix: SSL Persistence Profile now operates correctly, and does not cause high CPU usage.

bugs.title: openldap/ldap.conf file is not part of ucs backup archive.
bugs.symptoms: /etc/openldap/ldap.conf is not saved as part of a UCS backup.
bugs.conditions: /usr/libdata/configsync/cs.dat file on the BIG-IP sysesm does not have the entry for /etc/openldap/ldap.conf.
bugs.impact: Any changes in /etc/openldap/ldap.conf will not get backed up.
bugs.fix: Added /etc/openldap/ldap.conf file to cs.dat.

bugs.title: LTM UCS load merge trunk config issue
bugs.symptoms: Performing the ucs sys load command does not overwrite trunk interface configuration, it merges with the existent setting. When loading UCS with RMA flag, you may not get expected results. The expected outcome is that the trunk is overwritten, not merged.
bugs.conditions: Current configuration has a trunk with several interface members. The UCS to be loaded contains the same trunk name but with other interfaces.
bugs.impact: The trunk incorrectly appears as merged, having both sets of interfaces. The config on disk bigip_base.conf shows the correct config. Reboot does not resolve the issue.
bugs.workaround: 1. Restore the BIG-IP configuration to factory default settings using the command sequence: -- load sys config default. -- load sys ucs example.ucs no-license. -- save sys config. 2. Force the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration with the command sequence: touch /service/mcpd/forceload. -- load sys ucs example.ucs no-license. -- save sys config.
bugs.fix: Trunk config member interfaces are no longer merged during load. Only the trunk member interfaces defined in the config are present after a load.

bugs.title: RESOLV:: iRule commands and sFlow don't function correctly when using non-default CMP hashing.
bugs.symptoms: Packets originating from the RESOLV:: iRule commands and sFlow are not routed correctly when using non-default CMP hashing on external and internal VLANs.
bugs.conditions: External and internal VLANs have, respectively, src-ip and dst-ip cmp hashing configured.
bugs.impact: Packets are dropped.
bugs.fix: RESOLV:: iRule commands and sFlow now function correctly when using non-default CMP hashing.

bugs.title: The ECA process may produce a core file when processing HTTP headers
bugs.symptoms: The ECA process may produce a core file when processing HTTP headers. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: In the /var/log/apm file, you may observe log messages similar to the following example: notice eca[20847]: 01620010:5: ** SIGSEGV ** notice eca[20847]: 01620010:5: fault time: < date > The ECA process generates a core file in the /var/core directory.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The BIG-IP APM system is configured with the ECA log level of debug. -- The ECA process receives and attempts to process an HTTP cookie header, where the cookie value is greater than 1023 characters.
bugs.impact: The ECA process temporarily stops processing traffic and then restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable the debugging log. To work around this issue, you can revert the log level setting for the ECA (log.eca.level) process back to the default of Notice. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Debug logging is disabled for the ECA process. Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: tmsh Type the following command: modify /sys db log.eca.level value Notice Save the configuration change by typing the following command: save /sys config To exit the tmsh utility, type the following command: quit
bugs.fix: ECA can properly handle HTTP cookie header longer than 1023 characters when log level is set to debug.

bugs.title: A 'status down' message is logged when enabling a pool member that was previously disabled
bugs.symptoms: When a pool member is disabled and subsequently re-enabled, it logs a message saying that the monitor status is down for a very short time (just prior to coming back up). This is because the system is in the state 'forced down' when the pool member is disabled, and when it is re-enabled, it transitions to the state 'down', and then immediately to the state 'up', and each of these transitions is logged.
bugs.conditions: A pool member is disabled, then re-enabled.
bugs.impact: A potentially confusing log message. No other functional impact.
bugs.fix: The system no longer logs the transition from 'forced down' to 'down.

bugs.title: non-printable characters are escaped before hexencoding
bugs.symptoms: In non-printable values of AD/LDAP attributes, BIG-IP processing escapes the "|" (pipe) character.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is an AD/LDAP query in use and the query returns binary attributes with the "|" (pipe) character.
bugs.impact: This creates a problem when the value is processed back to its previous value, a process that includes removing the escape characters. In this case, the resulting data does not match the original binary data.
bugs.workaround: Unescape binary attribute values after hexdecode manipulation to match the original value.
bugs.fix: When an AD or LDAP query is in use and the query returns binary attributes with the "|" (pipe) character, APM now checks whether the value contains non-printable characters, and if so, hex encodes the value. If the value is printable, APM escapes the "\" and "|" characters (because "|" is used as a separator for multivalue attributes).

bugs.title: [Mac][Edge] Edge client doesn't handle ending redirects to the same box if second access policy assumes interaction
bugs.symptoms: Mac Edge Client doesn't work properly with ending redirects if the redirect is to the same box (another VS) and second access policy contains agents that assume interaction (Logon page, Message box, Mac Process check).
bugs.conditions: Redirect not working when subsequent agent assumes interaction.
bugs.impact: Redirect not working.
bugs.fix: Redirect works when the subsequent agent assumes interaction.

bugs.title: Time field may not display correctly in log search function
bugs.symptoms: On the event log page, searching by time and clicking on another field will cause the time field to not display.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Display temporarily omits the time field.
bugs.workaround: Clicking a second time causes the time field to display.
bugs.fix: The time field in the event log search function now displays correctly.

bugs.title: Cluster status may be incorrect on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: Cluster status may be out of date on secondary blades.
bugs.conditions: There is a race condition that becomes apparent when the cluster status is changed on the primary. This change may not be affected on the secondary.
bugs.impact: The cluster status when viewed on a secondary blade may not be up to date. clusterd's status will be correct, but mcpd's copy of the message may be out of date.
bugs.workaround: This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.fix: Changes are now immediately reflected on secondary blades when the cluster status is changed on the primary blade.

bugs.title: TMM Crash can lead to crash of other processes
bugs.symptoms: When TMM is crashing abnormally, the restart procedure can lead to following crashes of other processes in the system.
bugs.conditions: Relates to cases in which TMM crashes abnormally as a result of other issues.
bugs.impact: The crash of the other processes has no impact on the system, as the fact that TMM already crashed is the main impact. There is evidence of the other processes crash, since there are core dump files, so it is raising concerns about why several processes crashed and leads to customer escalations.
bugs.fix: The non-TMM processes are shut down more gracefully and are not crashing with core dumps during the system restart.

bugs.title: Check SACK report before treating as dupack
bugs.symptoms: TCP uses duplicate acks as a sign that data has left the network. When SACK is enabled, the SACK contains better information about this. When SACK indicates no data has left, do not execute duplicate ACK processing.
bugs.conditions: SACK is enabled and duplicate ACKs arrive.
bugs.impact: TCP sends data in excess of what is authorized by the congestion window.
bugs.workaround: It's a mild performance impact, so no workaround is necessary.
bugs.fix: Consider SACK information before dupack processing.

bugs.title: APMD cores in Kerberos authentication, when the agent tries to derefence a null authparam session variable.
bugs.symptoms: APMD cores in Kerberos authentication, when the agent tries to derefence a null authparam session variable.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using client based Kerberos authentication without an authparam.
bugs.impact: APMD process cores and restarts.
bugs.fix: If an authparam is not found in the local cache, an empty string will be returned to the caller. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Error L4 packets encounter configured whitelist entries that do not match the protocol
bugs.symptoms: For error vectors, the system matches only VLAN keys and not the associated protocols.
bugs.conditions: If an error packet is sent that should be dropped.
bugs.impact: An error packet's protocol is not compared with configured whitelist protocol entries, so they are not getting dropped.
bugs.fix: Error packet's protocol will now be matched with the specified protocol in the whitelist entries, so appropriate action will be taken.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when offloading one-way UDP FastL4 flow
bugs.symptoms: When handling UDP traffic on a FastL4 VIP, sometimes the TMM tries to offload both client and server flow when there is only one way traffic (either client-side or server-side). That would result TMM crashed on invalid pointer access.
bugs.conditions: HSBe2 platform, FastL4 VIP for UDP traffic, and one-way traffic during run time.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM now handles one way UDP traffic offloading correctly.

bugs.title: Ramcache causes failed transactions.
bugs.symptoms: In a keep alive transaction, the second or later request is not responded to, and the TCP connection is aborted.
bugs.conditions: When an OWS closes a keep alive connection when it should not. This implies a possible a web server defect.
bugs.impact: Keep alive connections will not work consistently.
bugs.workaround: An iRule set that rewrites the Connection header on 1.1 version transactions may mitigate this, but at the cost of requiring a separate connection per requested object. If the web server error is intermittent, it may be more efficient to allow for the occasional retry.

bugs.title: TMM crashes if request URI is empty or longer than 4096 bytes.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and restarts.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using URL redirection on APM. If the request uri is empty or greater than 4096 bytes it can trigger this.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Insure the request URI is not empty or longer than 4096 bytes.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes if request URI is empty or longer than 4096 bytes.

bugs.title: iRules source different procs from different partitions and executes the incorrect proc.
bugs.symptoms: iRules source different procs from different partitions and executes the incorrect proc.
bugs.conditions: Multiple iRule procs defined in multiple admin partitions.
bugs.impact: iRules "proc" lookup algorithm is not deterministic, or Virtual Servers are improperly caching and sharing the lookup results.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, ensure all iRule proc names defined in the BIG-IP configuration are unique.

bugs.title: Large POST requests are not handled well by APM.
bugs.symptoms: Large (4 MB or more) POST requests cause APM to crash if the request is retried. (The default limit is 64 KB, but can be increased in the configuration.)
bugs.conditions: An unusually large POST limit in APM. A big POST that needs to be retried.
bugs.impact: The TMM may core. The TMM lacks the required contiguous block of memory due to fragmentation.
bugs.workaround: Make sure POST limit is 4 MB or lower.
bugs.fix: APM no longer cores when configured to accept large POST requests, and the POST cannot be buffered.

bugs.title: tmm may crash if default gateway pool contains members that it cannot route to
bugs.symptoms: tmm may crash in an invalid routing setup
bugs.conditions: create gw pool member that is unreachable and not local on any subnet
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: do not create invalid routing setup

bugs.title: General Database Error when accessing Clusters or Templates page
bugs.symptoms: On multi-blade chassis systems, the Templates and Clusters pages conflict. If you navigate to the Clusters page and then navigate to Templates, the Templates page will be blank and post a General Database Error, and vice versa.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only in a multi-blade chassis system (i.e., where there is a Clusters page).
bugs.impact: Ability to configure via the UI is degraded. System posts an error in catalina.out: ERROR [TP-Processor3] application_005ftemplate.list_jsp:_jspService - Column not found: SLOT_ID in statement [SELECT LIMIT 0 10 OPTIMIZED * FROM app_template ORDER BY slot_id ASC].
bugs.workaround: Restart tomcat each time you want to use these pages.
bugs.fix: Accessing Template and Cluster pages now load correctly.

bugs.title: Hardwired failover asserts active even when standalone
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP software versions 11.2.1, 11.3.0, 11.4.0, 11.4.1, 11.5.0, 11.5.1, 11.5.2, 11.5.3, 11.5.4, 11.6.0, and 12.0.0, the serial failover 'Active' signal is asserted even if the unit is not configured to be in a high availability (HA) pair. A unit can become Standalone if the configuration is reset, or if a return merchandise authorization (RMA) is performed. If the serial cable is still connected to its peer, then the HA peer may defer the Active status to the Standalone system, which does not actually take over and process traffic.
bugs.conditions: Serial cable failover in-use between two members of an HA pair.
bugs.impact: Traffic is interrupted when the Active unit transitions to Standby.
bugs.workaround: During an RMA, the serial cable failover can be temporarily disabled on the Active unit by issuing the following command: tmsh modify sys db failover.usetty01 value disable
bugs.fix: A Standalone unit does not spuriously assert that it is Active if the unit is not configured to be in a high availability (HA) pair when the serial cable is connected during failover. (This is the version 10.x behavior.)

bugs.title: FW RELEASE: Incorporate B2250 BIOS 1.26.012.0
bugs.symptoms: The purpose of this bug is to incorporate firmware into the BIG-IP Release.
bugs.conditions: The purpose of this bug is to incorporate firmware into the BIG-IP Release when there is a change to the maintenance firmware.
bugs.impact: There is no impact with this change.
bugs.fix: FW RELEASE: Incorporated B2250 BIOS 1.26.012.0 into BIG-IP release.

bugs.title: VIPRION B2100-series BIOS version 1.06.043.0 update
bugs.symptoms: 1. The Disk Erase operation takes longer than expected, and may time out before completion. The Disk Erase progress bar may show 100% with 1 minute still remaining. 2. Pressing the ESC key at Disk Erase confirmation dialogs results in continuation. Pressing the ESC key in the Disk Erase intermittently causes the highlighted action to be performed. (ID458683-1)
bugs.conditions: Affects VIPRION B2100 and B2150 blades.
bugs.impact: 1. The Disk Erase operation may time out before completion. The Disk Erase progress bar may show 100% completion prematurely. 2. Disk Erase operations may be initiated unintentionally. (ID458683-1)

bugs.title: BIOS 4.01.006.0 for BIG-IP 10000, 10250, 10350 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: BIOS 4.01.006.0 for BIG-IP 10000, 10250, 10350 platforms.
bugs.conditions: Firmware earlier than BIOS 4.01.006.0 on the BIG-IP 10000, 10250, 10350 platforms.
bugs.impact: Updated BIOS needed.
bugs.fix: BIOS 4.01.006.0 has been incorporated into the BIG-IP 10000, 10250, 10350 platforms.

bugs.title: Address collision reported when the Primary blade goes down or its TMM crashes in an Chassis IntraCluster environment.
bugs.symptoms: In Chassis IntraCluster environment; when the Primary blade or its TMM goes down for any reason, (e.g., crash, restart, or shut down) the system posts 'IPv4 Addr collision' messages in APM logs.
bugs.conditions: This happens when a Chassis platform is used in IntraCluster mode with APM's Network Access.
bugs.impact: Address collision is reported in the logs, and affected clients (that have duplicate IP addresses - both the original ones and the new ones) might intermittently lose connectivity.
bugs.fix: Now the TMM leasepool IP information for the primary blade is mirrored on the oldest secondary blade, so the system no longer posts 'IPv4 Addr collision' messages.

bugs.title: BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series BIOS version 2.02.171.0 update
bugs.symptoms: 1. The Disk Erase operation takes longer than expected, and may time out before completion. The Disk Erase progress bar may show 100% with 1 minute still remaining. 2. Pressing the ESC key at Disk Erase confirmation dialogs results in continuation. Pressing the ESC key in the Disk Erase intermittently causes the highlighted action to be performed. (ID458683-4)
bugs.conditions: Affects BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series appliances.
bugs.impact: 1. The Disk Erase operation may time out before completion. The Disk Erase progress bar may show 100% completion prematurely. 2. Disk Erase operations may be initiated unintentionally. (ID458683-4)

bugs.title: VIPRION B4300 BIOS version 2.03.052.0 update
bugs.symptoms: 1. The Disk Erase operation takes longer than expected, and may time out before completion. The Disk Erase progress bar may show 100% with 1 minute still remaining. 2. Pressing the ESC key at Disk Erase confirmation dialogs results in continuation. Pressing the ESC key in the Disk Erase intermittently causes the highlighted action to be performed. (ID458683-2)
bugs.conditions: Affects VIPRION B4300 series blades.
bugs.impact: 1. The Disk Erase operation may time out before completion. The Disk Erase progress bar may show 100% completion prematurely. 2. Disk Erase operations may be initiated unintentionally. (ID458683-2)

bugs.title: FW RELEASE: Incorporate 5000, 5050, 5250 BIOS 2.06.214.0
bugs.symptoms: This is a standard bug used for tracking the incorporation of Firmware changes.
bugs.conditions: The purpose of this change is to integrate a firmware package into the BIG-IP build.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to this fix.
bugs.fix: Incorporated 5000, 5050, 5250 BIOS 2.06.214.0 into BIG-IP firmware.

bugs.title: SASP monitor starts a new connection to the Group Workload Manager (GWM) server when a connection to it already exists
bugs.symptoms: When the SASP monitor starts up, it can attempt to open a new TCP connection to the GWM server when another connection exists to it.
bugs.conditions: This happens when a GWM server sends the SendWeight messages to SASP monitor immediately after the registration of the pool member is complete, but the registration of all the pool members is not complete.
bugs.impact: The SASP monitor fins an existing TCP connection to the GWM server.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The Send Weight messages are processed only after the registration of all the pool members is complete. Monitor logging has been vastly improved. In addition, there was a crashing bug that caused the SASPD_monitor process to be restarted. That bug has been fixed.

bugs.title: Changes in captive portal probe URL
bugs.symptoms: The system uses a Microsoft-specific captive portal detection URL (http://www.msftncsi.com/ncsi.txt).
bugs.conditions: Using APM.
bugs.impact: With this bug we are trying trying to change it to F5 captive portal detection URL (http://www.f5.com/apps/all/avail.txt), and at the same time provide an ability for the customers to change behavior through modifying client settings in the registry.
bugs.fix: The system now uses an F5 Networks-specific captive portal probe URL in BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows instead of the default Microsoft-specific captive portal detection URL. An administrator for a Windows-based system can override use of the F5 captive portal URL by changing the following registry keys: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess.[ActiveWebProbeHost| ActiveWebProbePath | ActiveWebProbeContent].

bugs.title: On systems with multiple blades, large queries can cause TMM to restart
bugs.symptoms: When executing a chunked query (such as "show sys connection") that returns a lot of data, the primary MCP can get overwhelmed by the amount of data it is receiving from both its blade's TMMs and the secondary MCPs. It gives the data from its own TMMs priority, which eventually causes the secondary MCPs to run out of memory. At this point the MCP memory safeguards kick in and the secondary MCPs stop receiving data from their TMMs. The TMMs wait 20 seconds under these conditions, and if they have been unable to send data to MCP during that time, they exit and restart.
bugs.conditions: System must have multiple blades and execute a chunked query (for connection data or persistence records, for example) that returns a lot of data.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts and the system is unusable during that time.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Increased MCP's throughput by limiting the amount of data sent in a given chunk.

bugs.title: MCPD sync errors and restart after multiple modifications to file object in chassis
bugs.symptoms: Upon modifying file objects on a VIPRION chassis and synchronizing those changes to another VIPRION chassis in a device sync group, the following symptoms may occur: 1. Errors are logged to /var/log/ltm similar to the following: err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync: link_stat "/config/filestore/.snapshots_d/<_additional_path_to/_affected_file_object_>" (in csync) failed: No such file or directory (2) ) errno(0) errstr(). err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync error: some files could not be transferred (code 23) at main.c(1298) [receiver=2.6.8] syncer /usr/bin/rsync failed! (5888) () Couldn't rsync files for mcpd. ) errno(0) errstr(). err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync process failed.) errno(255) errstr(). err mcpd[<#>]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files.. 2. MCPD may restart on a secondary blade in a VIPRION chassis that is receiving the configuration sync from the chassis where the file object changes were made.
bugs.conditions: This symptom may occur under the following conditions: 1. Two or more VIPRION chassis are configured in a device sync group. 2. File objects (such as SSL certificates) are added/modified/deleted on one chassis in the group. 3. These changes are synchronized to other members of the device sync group. 4. While the previous changes are still being synchronized to all blades in all chassis in the device sync group, an overlapping set of file objects are added/modified/deleted on a chassis in the group (typically the same chassis as in step 2). 5. While the previous sync operation is still in progress, these subsequent changes are synchronized to other members of the device sync group.
bugs.impact: Temporary loss of functionality, including interruption in traffic, on one or more secondary blades in one or more VIPRION chassis that are receiving the configuration sync.
bugs.workaround: After performing one set of file-object modifications and synchronizing those changes to the HA group members, wait for one or more minutes to allow all changes to be synchronized to all blades in all member chassis before making and synchronizing additional file-object changes.
bugs.fix: After performing one set of file-object modifications and synchronizing those changes to the HA group members, wait for one or more minutes to allow all changes to be synchronized to all blades in all member chassis before making and synchronizing additional file-object changes.

bugs.title: NetHSM key is displayed as normal in GUI
bugs.symptoms: A NetHSM' key type is displayed as 'normal' in the GUI when it should be displayed as 'nethsm'.
bugs.conditions: When a key is created using NetHSM.
bugs.impact: The 'Security Type' field of the key's property appears to be 'Normal,' when it should be NetHSM.
bugs.fix: NetHSM key is displayed as normal in GUI as NetHSM, as expected.

bugs.title: Kerberos Auth might fail if client request contains Authorization header
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured with Kerberos Auth agent and the client sends a request with an Authorization header prior to the "HTTP 401" challenge, authentication fails.
bugs.conditions: An auth request to the BIG-IP systems contains Authorization header; Kerberos Auth is configured.
bugs.impact: Authentication can fail and the client might see a login prompt again when the IP address changes.
bugs.fix: Client's Kerberos auth will succeed now.

bugs.title: Generated assertion contains HEX-encoded attributes
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system serving as SAML identity provider (IdP), generates an assertion, the message might contain HEX-encoded values.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when user authenticates against LDAP/AD/RADIUS, and retrieved from AAA server attributes contain non-ASCII values. These non-ASCII values are then used by BIG-IP as Identity Provider in generated Assertion.
bugs.impact: SAML SSO might fail if Service Provider is not be able to process HEX-encoded attributes.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for IdentityProvider. On Service Provider side, assertion attribute values that begin with '0x' could be treated as HEX encoded. Such values can be HEX decoded after SP processed assertion.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP as Identity Provider now base64-encodes non-UTF8 attributes, as expected.

bugs.title: Cannot rename some files using CIFS optimization of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot rename some files using CIFS optimization of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Happens with BIG-IP systems with WOM configuration and CIFS optimization enabled and the files names are very long.
bugs.impact: Unable to rename files with long filenames using CIFS optimization of the BIG-IP system. wocplugin core.
bugs.fix: You can now rename files with long filenames using CIFS optimization of the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Content of 'Tower' column in 'Policy Enforcement/Subscribers/Active Sessions' table is displayed incorrectly.
bugs.symptoms: The tower column in the Active Sessions table (Policy Enforcement : Subscribers) is displayed incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: Viewing 'Tower' column in 'Policy Enforcement/Subscribers/Active Sessions' table.
bugs.impact: There is no impact. This is a cosmetic issue only.
bugs.workaround: None needed.

bugs.title: Edge client CTU report does not contain interface MTU value
bugs.symptoms: Client troubleshooting utility reports do not log the value of MTU on network interfaces.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the APM client CTU report.
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting MTU related issues become difficult.
bugs.workaround: Use third party tools to capture MTU values.

bugs.title: TCP connection can become stuck if client closes early
bugs.symptoms: Connection remains half-open and appears in connflow table after receiving FIN/ACK from serverside. the BIG-IP system never sends FIN/ACK to serverside to indicate connection has been closed.
bugs.conditions: Clientside connection is closed before serverside completes 3-way handshake. Serverside never completes 3-way handshake and LB::reselect command is issue via iRule.
bugs.impact: Connection remains half-open and stuck in connflow table
bugs.fix: Serverside connections established due to LB::reselect will now correctly get closed after the 3-way handshake completes if the corresponding clientside connection has already been closed.

bugs.title: MAC edge client doesn't follow HTTP 302 redirect if new site has untrusted self-signed certificate
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac does not follow HTTP 302 redirect if new site has an untrusted self-signed certificate.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Gateway and Mac Edge Client and HTTP 302 redirect to new site with untrusted certificate
bugs.impact: User might not be able to log in if HTTP 302 redirect is configured for a site with an untrusted certificate.
bugs.workaround: Configure APM with trusted certificate or configure client machine to trust APM's certificate
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac now follows HTTP 302 redirect if the new site has an untrusted self-signed certificate and the user will be able to log in successfully.

bugs.title: AVR: Collecting geolocation IDs
bugs.symptoms: Long computation in geolocation handling might cause Keep-Alive timer to stop the bd process.
bugs.conditions: This bug occurred during stress run when bd is running.
bugs.impact: The bd process halts and restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: This release improves the way AVR collects geolocation information, so the long computation does not take place, and the Keep-Alive timer does not stop the bd process.

bugs.title: Occasional extreme large value reported for tmm-info five-min-avg-usage-ratio
bugs.symptoms: The command tmsh -m show sys tmm-info field-fmt occasionally shows an invalid value such as: five-min-avg-usage-ratio 184467440737093465
bugs.conditions: This occurs under normal operation.
bugs.impact: Faulty displayed value with zero functional impact.

bugs.title: Virtual server with Portal Access and DOS profile resets connection
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server resets connection.
bugs.conditions: Requests are dropped on a virtual server that meets all of the following criteria: -- APM Access Policy. -- DOS Profile with Application Enabled. -- SSL profile on serverside.
bugs.impact: The system posts an error similar to the following: err apd[4646]: 01490000:3: AccessPolicyD.cpp func: 'process_request()' line: 736 Msg: EXCEPTION AccessPolicyD.cpp line:653 function: process_request - error 4 reading/parsing response from socket.
bugs.workaround: Either disable the DOS profile on the virtual server, or disable the SSL profile on the serverside.
bugs.fix: Virtual server with Portal Access, DOS profile, and SSL profile configuration no longer resets connections.

bugs.title: Change ip-address to ip-address-list in iControl REST because muliple IPs are supported in 11.6
bugs.symptoms: Starting with the 11.6.0 release, multiple IP addresses are supported for pem subscribers. The previous iControl REST functionality used ip-address to expose the address, this has changed to ip-address-list. As a result, tm.pem.Subscriber ipAddress property support has been removed from TMSH. This causes issues with iControl-REST compatibility.
bugs.conditions: Using ip-address in iControl REST commands for pem subscribers.
bugs.impact: Scripts that configure pem subscriber ip-address will not work in 11.6.0 and later.
bugs.workaround: Change ip-address to ip-address-list.

bugs.title: DB variable 'qinq.cos' does not work in all cases on 5000 and C2400 platforms
bugs.symptoms: On the 5000 and C2400 platforms, when the DB variable 'qinq.cos' is set to 'inner'; a packets inner priority bits do not determine the CoS mapping when the incoming packet is customer-tagged and the outgoing interface is service-tagged.
bugs.conditions: On 5000 and C2400 platforms.
bugs.impact: Incorrect egress CoS queue mapping. In this case, all packets are mapped to CoS queue 0.
bugs.fix: On the 5000 and C2400 platforms, when the DB variable 'qinq.cos' is set to 'inner', the packets are now handled as expected.

bugs.title: 'tmsh list net tunnels' and GUI tunnel access fail for non-admin users
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh list net tunnels' and GUI tunnel access fail for non-admin users. Non-admin users have access to all partitions via tmsh.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for non-admin users on the tunnel list page when selecting a predefined tunnel or one that has been configured.
bugs.impact: The command or operation fails. The system displays the following error: Unexpected Error: Can't display all items, can't get object count from mcpd.
bugs.fix: Non-admin users can now use the GUI to access the tunnel list page or properties for a configured tunnel without error.

bugs.title: AD/LDAP server connection failures might cause apd to stop processing requests when service is restored
bugs.symptoms: AD/LDAP server connection failures might cause APM apd to stop processing requests when service is restored. These symptoms accompany the problem: - Too many file descriptors open by apd. - 'Too many open files' error messages in the log file. - Running qkview to gather diagnostic data reveals the information similar to the following in 'netstat -pano' from qkview: tcp 270 0 127.0.0.1:10001 10.10.225.85:53212 ESTABLISHED 12191/apd off (0.00/0/0) tcp 269 0 127.0.0.1:10001 10.10.225.4:56305 ESTABLISHED 12191/apd off (0.00/0/0) tcp 272 0 127.0.0.1:10001 10.10.57.10:57508 CLOSE_WAIT 12191/apd off (0.00/0/0) tcp 0 0 127.1.1.1:56230 127.7.0.1:389 ESTABLISHED 12191/apd keepalive (1909.72/0/0) The last line with timer 'keepalive (1909.72/0/0)' indicates that apd has been waiting for a response for too long. Other lines with Recv-Q '272' indicate that apd is not reading incoming requests as expected (specifically, that the internal worker queue is overloaded because all threads are waiting for the one hanging thread to be processed).
bugs.conditions: This occurs between the connect and search phases of the AD/LDAP server connection operation, most likely when a AAA Server is configured to use pool as a backend. In this case, apd can always connect locally to layered virtual server, but the pool monitor has a server availability check interval, so a lag in the request to an unavailable server might cause apd to hang.
bugs.impact: Potential connection failures to backend server.
bugs.fix: Active Directory and LDAP server connection operations time out in 3 minutes, so a thread does not block any other, and service can recover as soon as the connection to the backend is restored.

bugs.title: long session var processing in variable assignment agent
bugs.symptoms: before the fix, there was no way to operate session variables > 4096 bytes in variable assignment agent
bugs.conditions: variable assignment agent uses session variable that is longer than 4Kb (value)
bugs.impact: cannot process some well known attributes of from active directory server like memberOf if user is a member of thousands groups OR member if group has thousands of members
bugs.fix: There is no limit on session variable value length in the variable assign agent.

bugs.title: CGNAT PBA mode when setting block lifetime timeouts, may not be able to terminate SIP-ALG media flows
bugs.symptoms: If CGNAT Port block allocation (PBA) is configured for block lifetimes, when the lifetime expires, the system terminates any flows still associated with that port block. However, SIP media flows cannot be terminated, so the block cannot be released until the media flows terminate.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Using CGNAT PBA mode. -- block lifetime set. -- Using SIP-ALG. -- Media flows outlive block lifetime.
bugs.impact: Blocks cannot be released as expected until media flows terminate.

bugs.title: Support for XMLHttpRequest is extended
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript exceptions occur.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs with web-application JavaScript code using XMLHttpRequest.
bugs.impact: Web-application logic and behavior can be broken.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: XMLHttpRequest rewriting is improved, so that patched objects behave the same way (or close enough) as original ones on a given browser.

bugs.title: HTTP compression browser workarounds incorrectly match modern browsers.
bugs.symptoms: When a User-Agent identifies a browser which has known compression limitations, the 'browser workarounds' disable compression. Browsers requiring these workarounds include: - Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 - Netscape Navigator 4.1 - Netscape Navigator 5.0 Unfortunately, the functionality will falsely identify many modern browsers as needing compression workarounds, disabling compression.
bugs.conditions: Enable HTTP compression browser workarounds.
bugs.impact: HTTP compression will not compress responses for modern browsers.
bugs.workaround: Disable browser workarounds. If legacy clients require compression workarounds, use an iRule that selectively disables compression depending on the User-Agent.
bugs.behavior: Starting Evergreen release we will be deprecating the browser-workarounds option in HTTP compression profile. All related code handling the option in the deflate filter is being removed. The option will no longer be seen in GUI, and will show up as deprecated in tmsh and SNMP.

bugs.title: AFM DoS UDP PortList configuration is not migrated automatically
bugs.symptoms: When a DoS UDP port list is configured via sys db variables dos.udplimiter, the configuration is not automatically migrated during upgrades.
bugs.conditions: AFM DoS with UDP PortList configuration and customer upgrade from pre 11.6.0.
bugs.impact: AFM DoS UDP PortList configuration is not migrated automatically
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, migrate the configuration manually using the tmsh command: security dos udp-portlist { } .

bugs.title: Failover triggered due to a TMM crash resulting from unavailable APM renderer pool members.
bugs.symptoms: When the APM Access renderer or renderer pool (used for serving internal pages) goes down for an unknown reason, tmm goes into retry loop and sod kills the tmm.
bugs.conditions: For the problem to occur, at the very least, APM must be in use. The problem showed up in the past with a mangled iRule in place.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This has only been observed with an incorrectly formed iRule. So it is likely that fixing an associated iRule to operate as intended will resolve the problem. If this occurs without an associated iRule, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Now when an APM renderer or renderer pool (used for serving internal pages) goes down, APM detects the unavailability and sends a TCP Reset to the client.

bugs.title: FQDN Nodes: mcp validation check error msg verb tense: "Modify of ephemeral nodes not permitted"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to Enable, Disable, Force Offline, or Delete an ephemeral node, the UI returns an error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Modify of ephemeral nodes is not permitted.
bugs.conditions: Enabling, disabling, forcing offline, or deleting an ephemeral node.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact on the system. This is a cosmetic issue. The wording of the returned error message is more accurately reflected as 'Modification of ephemeral nodes...' or 'Modifying ephemeral nodes...'

bugs.title: DF flag is not set on the egress fragmented packets
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, fragmented ICMP packets are forwarded without their don't-fragment (DF) bit set.
bugs.conditions: AAM (WOM) is licensed.
bugs.impact: Unexpected behavior might occur. Specific behavior depends on the configuration.

bugs.title: Source address persistence record times out even while traffic is flowing on FastL4 profile virtual server
bugs.symptoms: A source address persistence record created on a virtual server with a FastL4 profile times out and is aged out even while traffic is flowing through that flow. The traffic that results in this issue is UDP with checksum of 0.
bugs.conditions: The profile has to be FastL4. Traffic that is either UDP with checksum of 0, or SCTP, or ESP, are definitely affected.
bugs.impact: Source address persistence is not usable as the entry ages out when it should not.
bugs.fix: Source address persistence record no longer times out unexpectedly on FastL4 profile virtual server.

bugs.title: TMM crash when processing ACCESS::session iRule without an attached Access Policy
bugs.symptoms: When using the ACCESS::session create iRule without an Access Policy in place, TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1. No Access Policy is attached to virtual server and 2. The ACCESS::session create iRule is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This version allows the iRule, ACCESS::session create, to work even when an access policy is not attached to the virtual server.

bugs.title: SSL connection may not survive multiple failovers or delay response
bugs.symptoms: The system does not support SSL mirroring with L7 mirroring. When an SSL connection is mirrored, after a few failovers, the connection is reset or the response is delayed for up to several minutes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when SSL connections are mirrored.
bugs.impact: The connection is reset or the response is delayed for up to several minutes. The BIG-IP system does not forward the request to the server. In addition, you cannot use L7 features like iRules on mirrored SSL virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Do not use SSL mirroring with L7 mirroring. SSL mirroring is not supported with L7 mirroring.

bugs.title: Headers starting with X-F5 may cause problems if not X-F5-REST-Coordination-Id
bugs.symptoms: Some URIs passed to the BIG-IP system with X-F5 that are not X-F5-REST-Coordination-Id may improperly parse the HTTP request headers. These include iControl-REST URIs /mgmt/tm/analytics/... /mgmt/tm/vcmp/... /mgmt/tm/actions/... /mgmt/tm/gtm/... /mgmt/tm/ltm/... /mgmt/tm/net/... /mgmt/tm/pem/... /mgmt/tm/util/... /mgmt/tm/sys/... /mgmt/tm/cli/... /mgmt/tm/secuirty/... /mgmt/tm/ilx/... /mgmt/tm/apm/... /mgmt/tm/transaction/... /mgmt/tm/auth/... /mgmt/tm/wom/... /mgmt/tm/cm/... /mgmt/tm/wam/...
bugs.conditions: Headers prefixed with X-F5 that are not X-F5-REST-Coordination-Id.
bugs.impact: Headers are not parsed properly.
bugs.fix: The system now checks for the full header name to properly parse instead requiring X-F5 to determine whether or not it is the X-F5-REST-Coordination-Id header.

bugs.title: Configuration utility allows for mismatch in IP protocol and transport profile
bugs.symptoms: tmsh allows configuration of a virtual server with mismatched ip-protocol and transport-layer profile. For example, ip-protocol tcp with a UDP profile or ip-protocol udp with a TCP profile, or ip-protocol any with a TCP profile.
bugs.conditions: Configure a virtual server with mismatched ip-protocol and transport-layer profiles (e.g., ip-protocol udp, profiles { tcp }).
bugs.impact: Traffic reaching a misconfigured virtual server can crash tmm, resulting in an outage.
bugs.workaround: Configure virtual server with matching ip-protocol and transport-layer profile.
bugs.fix: Validation for both TCP and UDP profiles has been updated to correctly require the profile type and protocol type to match.

bugs.title: Clock advanced messages with large amount of data maintained in DNS Express zones
bugs.symptoms: Clock advanced messages with a large amount of data maintained in DNS Express (DNSX) zones, the TMM can suffer from clock advances when performing the DB reload.
bugs.conditions: Large enough zones into DNSX (several hundred thousand to several million records depending on hardware).
bugs.impact: Clock advance messages in log. No traffic can be passed for this duration. When DNS Express zones are updated, you may see messages similar to the following in the /var/log/ltm log: notice tmm[25454]: 01010029:5: Clock advanced by 121 ticks.
bugs.workaround: Prevent all updates to DNSX zones.
bugs.fix: AXFR and IXFR to DNS Express (DNSX) with large zones has been significantly improved. DNSX DB now reside in /shared to resolve DB size issues.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system drops non-zero version EDNS requests
bugs.symptoms: If a query from a client contains a non-zero EDNS version, the query is dropped instead of sending an appropriate response.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with DNS profile/processing when a client sends a query with non-zero EDNS version.
bugs.impact: Dropped queries, retries, and then time-outs occur.
bugs.fix: If the EDNS version is not zero, the query passes through the filter and is not dropped.

bugs.title: The COMPAT SSL stack does not support connection mirroring
bugs.symptoms: SSL mirrored connections using compat ciphers may fail after failover. COMPAT cipher support was removed entirely in 14.0.0.
bugs.conditions: SSL connection mirroring and COMPAT cipher use.
bugs.impact: Possible connection failure.
bugs.workaround: Disable COMPAT ciphers.

bugs.title: 'tmsh load sys config gtm-only' resets link assignments
bugs.symptoms: Loading configuration clears the link assignments displayed in the UI.
bugs.conditions: GTM is provisioned and a GTM server, virtual server, and link are configured. If the config is loaded then any link assignments will no longer be displayed in the UI.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic bug. The control plane loses that information on a load and it never gets updated.
bugs.workaround: Making a non-functional change to the server or link (e.g. the description) should cause GTM to update the links in the control plane (mcpd).

bugs.title: Aced service does not recover if child process dies.
bugs.symptoms: If a child process is killed, cored, or dies, the parent process does not restart it and the service stops serving SecurID authentication.
bugs.conditions: In some exceptional cases, the child process exits.
bugs.impact: SecurID authentication failed, but service recovered by runsv.
bugs.fix: Now, aced can restart a child process only. There is no need to exit the main process and restart all the children.

bugs.title: Enabling ASM AJAX blocking response page feature causing cross domain AJAX requests to fail
bugs.symptoms: When AJAX blocking response page feature is enabled, ASM's pre-injected javascript code adds a custom header to each outgoing ajax request. Adding the header to a cross domain ajax request forces browsers to send an OPTIONS preflight request, if a back-end server doesn't not treat the pre-flight request properly, the request will fail resulting in broken functionality of a web application.
bugs.conditions: Provision asm, attach asm policy to a virtual server and configure Enable AJAX blocking response page feature.
bugs.impact: Broken cross domain ajax requests
bugs.workaround: Disable AJAX blocking response page feature in ASM policy.
bugs.fix: Avoid adding custom headers to cross domain ajax request.

bugs.title: URIs with space characters may not work properly in ODATA query
bugs.symptoms: ODATA query strings such as: $filter=partition eq 'Common' may not work correctly unless the spaces are encoded with +.
bugs.conditions: ODATA query strings with spaces.
bugs.impact: The query will fail with a 400 error.
bugs.workaround: Encode the query string space characters with + as replacement.
bugs.fix: URIs with space characters now work properly in ODATA query.

bugs.title: failed tmsh command generate double logs
bugs.symptoms: A single failed tmsh command generates two identical audit logs, and audit_forwarder sends two logs to audit server (TACACS+ in this example).
bugs.conditions: tmsh audit is on and tmsh command is failed from mcpd validation. This does not occur with successful commands.
bugs.impact: Here is an example of the failure: tmsh create ltm pool pool20 01020066:3: The requested pool (/Common/pool20) already exists in partition Common Tue May 20 16:27:17 2014 10.10.10.201 root unknown unknown update service=system protocol=ip task_id=130start_time=1400627369 event=cmd_acct reason=May 20 16:09:29 aftest notice tmsh[20175]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=20175 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[01020066:3: The requested pool (/Common/pool20) already exists in partition Common.] cmd_data=create ltm pool pool20 Tue May 20 16:27:17 2014 10.10.10.201 root unknown unknown update service=system protocol=ip task_id=132start_time=1400627369 event=cmd_acct reason=May 20 16:09:29 aftest notice tmsh[20175]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=20175 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[01020066:3: The requested pool (/Common/pool20) already exists in partition Common.] cmd_data=create ltm pool pool20
bugs.fix: Failed tmsh command no longer generates double logs.

bugs.title: FIPS keys might not be recoverable from UCS
bugs.symptoms: FIPS exported keys get created only on the unit on which the FIPS key is created or imported. This FIPS exported key does not get created on the HA peer.
bugs.conditions: HA setup with multiple FIPS devices.
bugs.impact: The UCS created on such a HA peer does not contain the FIPS .exp key files. Restoring such a UCS does not recover the FIPS keys. If a FIPS unit is returned to F5 Networks for a replacement unit, the recovery of FIPS keys is not straightforward on the new unit, or might not be possible.
bugs.workaround: Manually copy the .exp file from the peer or generate the UCS on the peer and load it manually. You can use the command line to scp copy all FIPS exported keys from /config/ssl/ssl.cavfips/ from one HA peer to the other and also vice versa, so that each of them have all the FIPS exported key files.
bugs.fix: FIPS exported keys now get created on the HA peer as well as on the unit on which the FIPS key is created or imported.

bugs.title: syscalld logs erroneous and benign timeout messages
bugs.symptoms: The syscalld timeout mechanism might cause premature logging of OPERATION_TIMEOUT messages.
bugs.conditions: No specific configuration is required.
bugs.impact: The system posts the message: syscalld[21190]: 0127000a:3: OPERATION_TIMEOUT 'command' may be hung or taking a long time. This may cause some operations, such as establishing CMI trust, to fail and need to be launched again.
bugs.fix: syscalld's timeout mechanism no longer emits an OPERATION_TIMEOUT message, unless the message appropriately reflects the condition of the system.

bugs.title: VMware View client freezes when APM PCoIP is used and user authentication fails against VCS 5.3
bugs.symptoms: VMware View client freezes
bugs.conditions: APM PC-over-IP (PCoIP) is used and user authentication fails against View Connection Server (VCS) 5.3.
bugs.impact: VMware View client freezes, user unable to log in
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: VMware View client does not freeze when APM PC-over-IP (PCoIP) is used and user authentication fails against View Connection Server 5.3.

bugs.title: Hardware Compression in CaveCreek may cause excessive memory consumption.
bugs.symptoms: Closely related to BZ456859. Symptoms appear as slow, but unbounded, growth in xfrag allocation.
bugs.conditions: Highly-varying compression payload sizes, plus time.
bugs.impact: Tmm may segfault and leave a core that indicates a high xfrag memory usage.
bugs.workaround: Do not use hardware compression.
bugs.fix: Flat-buffer allocator for hardware compression tuned to be less greedy.

bugs.title: Behavior Change: HA Score calculation when minimum-threshold attribute is in use
bugs.symptoms: HA Groups periodically compute an HA health score to determine which BIG-IP device is the 'best' device to host a Traffic Group. If another device has a better score than the current device then the Traffic Group fails over to the other device. The HA Group provides a set of thresholds that, if not met, will evoke failover regardless of HA scores. Some problems with this are the following: The HA score measured by two devices may vary slightly over time. The device with the 'best' score may vary thus triggering unnecessary failovers even though the difference in the scores is negligible. The current method is not flexible. HA groups cannot be easily incorporate other 'boolean' values (i.e VLAN failsafe) or other methods that pick the next active device, (i.e load-aware algorithm). For these reasons, the HA Group has been refactored into two separate objects, HA Monitor and HA Score, to decouple failure detection from failure remediation. An HA Monitor determines when a traffic group can no longer run on the current device. The HA Score failover method picks the highest scoring device as the next device to host the traffic group. An HA monitor may be combined with other Failover Methods to, for example, failover to the next device in round robin order. If any component (trunk, pool, cluster member) of a high availability (HA) group violates its 'minimum' requirement (defined by the 'minimum-threshold'), the total HA group score is not forced to 0 (zero) if there is an active bonus set.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration contains an HA group with associated components (trunks, pools, cluster members). -- 'Minimum-threshold' setting of any of those members is non-zero. -- Non-zero number of members.
bugs.impact: Because of how HA group score is calculated, the system might incorrectly report a viable traffic group or may fail over unnecessarily.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to configure the 'minimum-threshold' parameter for each of the HA group components (trunks, pools, and cluster members) to a value that specifies the minimum number of monitored objects required to consider this contributor valid.

bugs.title: stpd attempts to connect to slots in a chassis that are empty
bugs.symptoms: In a chassis environment stpd attempts to connect to slots that are empty. These connection attempts are unsuccessful and will result in repeated stpd errors in the ltm log: err stpd[7707]: 01290003:3: Attempt to send 15 bytes to inettcp://127.3.0.4:4401 timed out after 8 seconds
bugs.conditions: This issue exists when there is one or more empty slots in a chassis.
bugs.impact: Repeated stpd errors in the ltm log. This is a cosmetic error that can be ignored safely.
bugs.fix: The stpd process now checks to ensure that a slot is populated before attempting to connect to that slot.

bugs.title: NA Admin UI requires options that are not needed
bugs.symptoms: You must provide 'Client proxy address' or 'Client Proxy Autoconfig Script' values even if "Use Client Proxy" is selected in the Network Access configuration UI.
bugs.conditions: "Use Client Proxy" option is selected in Network Access configuration UI.
bugs.impact: Administrator is required to enter configuration values that won't be used.
bugs.workaround: Method #1: Enter dummy values for the required fields. Method #2: Add a variable assign to the VPE (before the resource assign) with the following expression : { expression "return {<client_proxy>1</client_proxy><client_proxy_use_local_proxy>1</client_proxy_use_local_proxy>}" varname config.connectivity_resource_network_access./Common/<network_access_resource>.client_proxy_settings }
bugs.fix: Not Fixed

bugs.title: File descriptor leak when running some TMSH commands through scriptd
bugs.symptoms: File descriptors for pipes are leaking when executing some TMSH commands through scriptd.
bugs.conditions: TMSH commands must execute via scriptd (for example, running tmsh::modify in an iCall, but there may be other conditions that lead to the leak).
bugs.impact: iCall scripts cease to function, and scriptd must be restarted. Eventually the system logs error messages similar to the following: err scriptd[11946]: 014f0013:3: Script (/Common) generated this Tcl error: script did not successfully complete: the pipe system call failed, Too many open files.
bugs.fix: All pipes are closed when a TMSH command is completed, so file descriptors no longer leak when running some TMSH commands through scriptd.

bugs.title: Integration of Firmware for the 2000 Series Blades
bugs.symptoms: Integration of Firmware for the 2000 Series Blades.
bugs.conditions: When firmware has changes that benefit platforms, it is internally released and updated in the latest version of software.
bugs.impact: This will improve functioning of the hardware.
bugs.workaround: None. This is an action item.
bugs.fix: Integration of Firmware for the 2000 Series Blades.

bugs.title: Google Docs does not work through Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: User is unable to use Google Docs through Portal Access due to multiple errors both shown by web application itself and in JS console.
bugs.conditions: Google Docs is accessed through Portal Access.
bugs.impact: It is impossible to use Google Docs through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: HTTP responses are not cached when response-adapt is applied
bugs.symptoms: When a response-adapt profile is applied on a virtual with ramcache, HTTP responses are not cached.
bugs.conditions: Both ramcache and response-adapt on a virtual.
bugs.impact: HTTP responses are not cached.
bugs.fix: HTTP responses modified by response-adapt are cached.

bugs.title: Serverside SSL cannot be disabled if Rewrite profile is attached
bugs.symptoms: Cannot disable serverside SSL via iRule command or CPM policy.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on a virtual server that meets the following conditions: - Rewrite profile - Serverssl profile - iRule using the 'SSL::Disable serverside' command in an HTTP_REQUEST event or a CPM policy with a 'server-ssl disable' action and an http-uri condition.
bugs.impact: Cannot disable serverside SSL.
bugs.workaround: Utilize iRule with 'SSL::Disable serverside command in the SERVER_CONNECTED event.
bugs.fix: Allows serverside SSL to be disabled by iRule or CPM policy.

bugs.title: Customized cert-key-chain of a client ssl profile might be reverted to its parent's.
bugs.symptoms: In some circumstance, when loading the configuration a client ssl profile with a custom cert-key-chain might be overwritten.
bugs.conditions: Customized cert-key-chain of a client ssl profile.
bugs.impact: The cert-key-chain of a profile is not what is expected.
bugs.fix: Customized cert-key-chain of the child client-ssl profile is reverted to parent's profile cert-key-chain during config load.

bugs.title: Policy Rule Missing from TMSH Overlapping Status Output
bugs.symptoms: Policy rule column which shows a referencing rule in policies which have rule-lists may be missing from the advanced rule status or a.k.a. overlapping-status mode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using rules that reference rule-lists
bugs.impact: You may not be able to see the real rules that reference the rule-lists. The impact is minimal.
bugs.workaround: In regular firewall rule modes, such as "show security firewall policy" or "show ltm virtual fw-enforced-policy", etc, you can still see Referencing Rule column.
bugs.fix: Missing Referencing Rule column is added to overlapping status mode.

bugs.title: 'tmsh list ltm message-routing' and 'tmsh show ltm message-routing' fail for non-admin users
bugs.symptoms: Running the commands 'tmsh list ltm message-routing' and 'tmsh show ltm message-routing' fail for non-admin users, even though non-admin users have tmsh access to all partitions.
bugs.conditions: A non-admin user is logged in via tmsh.
bugs.impact: The non-admin user cannot run the command 'list ltm message-routing' or 'show ltm message-routing' via tmsh. The system posts an error message similar to the following: Unexpected Error: Can't display all items, can't get object count from mcpd.
bugs.fix: Non-admin users can now successfully run the commands 'tmsh list ltm message-routing' and 'tmsh show ltm message-routing'.

bugs.title: Possible tmm crash when modifying html pages with HTML profile.
bugs.symptoms: With certain combinations of append_to_tag/prepend_to_tag rules and input fragments, HTML profile could get stuck in an infinite loop.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove HTML profile from virtual server. Or, modify profile rules in a way that would not cause loop.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue in HTML profile which could cause an infinite loop while processing HTML page with certain rules.

bugs.title: PEM: CCR-I for the Gx session has only one subscriber ID type even if session created has more than one type
bugs.symptoms: When a PEM session is created by radius/irule and there are more that one subscriber ID types associated to the session then only one of them is sent.
bugs.conditions: Subscriber session has more that one subscriber ID types but just one type sent.
bugs.impact: If PCRF is expecting all the subscriber IDs associated to the session then only one of them being sent.
bugs.workaround: here is no workaround at this time'
bugs.fix: All the associated subscriber ID types (imsi, e164, private) are sent of the CCR-I message for the session if they are present during session creation.

bugs.title: Quickly repeated external datagroup loads might cause TMM crash.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes while loading an external datagroup that has already been loaded.
bugs.conditions: External datagroup is already loaded, and is then re-loaded.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To avoid this issue, wait a few seconds between load and reload the same external data group.

bugs.title: Show proper error message when VMware View client sends invalid credentials to APM
bugs.symptoms: The View client shows no information or error page if the user types the wrong password or username
bugs.conditions: Bad credentials supplied to Vmware View client connecting using APM.
bugs.impact: End user would not know if the failed login was caused by bad credentials or for another reason.
bugs.fix: VMware View client displays a proper message when a user enters invalid credentials.

bugs.title: Validation of IP/mask for SNMP allowed-addresses list.
bugs.symptoms: The GUI option Client Allow List and the TMSH allowed-address property require IP address values. However, the system does not prevent entering a non-IP address value.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs on both BIG-IQ and BIG-IP system, and is always applicable when configuring SNMP allowed-addresses.
bugs.impact: The CLI and GUI do not validate IP/mask for SNMP configurations within the allowed-addresses list.
bugs.workaround: Double check IP/mask entries for the GUI option Client Allow List and the TMSH allowed-address property.
bugs.fix: Address, network address and hostname validation is now performed.

bugs.title: Failure of mcpd with invalid authentication context.
bugs.symptoms: MCPd cores.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this core.
bugs.impact: Mcpd restarts
bugs.fix: Failure of mcpd with invalid authentication context no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Multiple root certificates with same 'subject' and 'issuer' may cause the tmm to core.
bugs.symptoms: Two or more root certificates with the same 'subject' and 'issuer' but different serial numbers may cause the tmm to core. The core was due to an assert failure in size caused by a loop in certificate chain construction.
bugs.conditions: When multiple certificates with the same 'subject' and 'issuer' are in a CA file, and the CA file is configured in SSL profile as trusted CAs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Keep only one certificate for a given 'subject' and 'issuer' in CA file. Do not leave two certificates with the same 'subject' and 'issuer' in a CA file.
bugs.fix: Resolved a failure when the customer installs another self-signed certificate with same subject/issuer before a self-signed certificate expires.

bugs.title: Copying Access Profile with Machine Cert Agent check fails
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to copy an Access Profile with Machine Cert Check Agent, it fails with no error message on the web interface nor in the a log file.
bugs.conditions: Copying of Profile Access with Access Policy that has Machine Cert Check Agent with cert assigned
bugs.impact: The copy fails, and no error message is displayed.
bugs.workaround: Edit access policy, remove machine certificate assignment Copy Edit access policy, set machine certificate back
bugs.fix: Now it is possible to copy an access profile that contains a Machine Cert access policy item.

bugs.title: DNS logging does not support Splunk format log
bugs.symptoms: DNS logging does not support Splunk format logging. It fails to log the events, instead logging err messages: hostname="XXXXXXXXXXXXX.XX",errdefs_msgno="01230140:3:
bugs.conditions: DNS logging configured for Splunk format.
bugs.impact: DNS logging does not log Splunk format to HSL.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to send Splunk-formatted messages to the Splunk server. For example: ltm rule dns_logging_to_splunk { when DNS_REQUEST { set ldns [IP::client_addr] set vs_name [virtual name] set q_name [DNS::question name] set q_type [DNS::question type] set hsl [HSL::open -proto UDP -pool splunk-servers] HSL::send $hsl "<190>,f5-dns-event=DNS_REQUEST,ldns=$ldns,virtual=$vs_name,query_name=$q_name,query_type=$q_type" } when DNS_RESPONSE { set ldns [IP::client_addr] set vs_name [virtual name] set q_name [DNS::question name] set q_type [DNS::question type] set answer [DNS::answer] set hsl [HSL::open -proto UDP -pool splunk-servers] HSL::send $hsl "<190>,f5-dns-event=DNS_RESPONSE,ldns=$ldns,virtual=$vs_name,query_name=$q_name,query_type=$q_type,answer=＼"$answer＼"" } }

bugs.title: Errors and unavailable virtual server upon deactivation of ASM policy that is assigned to a non-default rule of L7 policy
bugs.symptoms: When trying to deactivate a policy used in a non-default L7 policy, you get the following error, and the policy is deactivated: "MCP Validation error - 01071726:3: Cannot deactivate policy action '/Common/vs126'. It is in use by ltm policy '/Common/l7_policy'." In addition, the virtual server becomes unavailable after the deactivation.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned. ASM policy is assigned to a non-default L7 policy.
bugs.impact: Virtual server is unavailable. ASM policy assigned to the LTM virtual server is broken.
bugs.workaround: Prior to the deactivation of such an ASM policy, remove it from all L7 policies from the following screen: Local Traffic > Policies > Policy List > <L7_policy_name> > Properties.
bugs.fix: The deactivation of an ASM policy that is assigned to a non-default rule in an LTM policy produces a verbose and meaningful error message, and the virtual server is now available after the deactivation.

bugs.title: Rule lists may not display schedules for rules that have them
bugs.symptoms: Rule lists may not display schedules for rules that have them.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at Active Rules or policies if they have schedules assigned to them.
bugs.impact: The rule list will display that each rule with a schedule is scheduled, but will not show which schedule is associated with the rule.
bugs.fix: Rule lists now correctly display schedules for rules.

bugs.title: Intermittent tmm core
bugs.symptoms: tmm intermittently cores. Stack trace signature indicates "packet is locked by a driver"
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an intermittent tmm core

bugs.title: Datastor cores and restarts.
bugs.symptoms: Datastor cores and restarts. This occurs potentially because of generational issues, object replacement from archive, and the possibility that an object was deleted in the interim.
bugs.conditions: Traffic patterns that shift from low to moderate velocity with strong tiling to decoherent, high velocity traffic can cause this to occur when request queuing is turned on.
bugs.impact: Temporary cache outage. The cache must then be completely reseeded. A datastor core file is written, and datastor is restarted.
bugs.fix: Fixed potential crash and removed some extraneous time stamps from logged messages.

bugs.title: Client may legitimately send a range request for the cached JS/CSS content which is no longer valid.
bugs.symptoms: When JS/CSS minification feature is turned on, some client may legitimately send a range request for the cached JS/CSS content which is no longer valid due to content size reduction by the feature. In that case, TMM may spin out of control, and eventually be killed by SOD.
bugs.conditions: Client retrieves the JS/CSS content from WAM and get the unminified content. Turn on JS/CSS minification. Client issues range request for the JS/CSS content using the content size it knows about, which is prior to minification. WAM will try to serve to content with the range request, which technically is no longer valid due to content size shrinkage.
bugs.impact: TMM becomes unresponsive and SOD will kill it.
bugs.workaround: Turn off JS/CSS minification

bugs.title: Insufficient error information when netHSM is used without proper licensing
bugs.symptoms: Trying to use a netHSM key without the HSM license causes the SSL handshake to fail with the general error in sign server key exchange.
bugs.conditions: This issue might occur when using netHSM without HSM licensing.
bugs.impact: The system posts potentially confusing errors similar to the following (with ssl debug logs turned on): -- debug tmm3[28399]: 01260009:7: Connection error: ssl_hs_vfy_sign_srvkeyxchg:8309: sign_srvkeyxchg (80) -- info tmm3[28399]: 01260013:6: SSL Handshake failed for TCP 10.10.10.13:47804 -> 10.10.10.23:443
bugs.workaround: License HSM. To determine whether this is the issue related to these messages, you can turn on tmm.verbose. Then, if netHSM is not licensed, you can find the following message at /var/log/tmm: notice No license for external HSM.
bugs.fix: Now, if netHSM is not licensed, the system provides a clear error indicating that a license is needed.

bugs.title: Tcpdump enhancement for better SSL/TLS data analysis
bugs.symptoms: tcpdump does not have the functionality to help analysis of encrypted data issues such as issues during encrypted TLS 1.3 handshakes, encrypted SSL/TLS payload for TLS 1.3, TLS 1.2 and earlier.
bugs.conditions: When there is a need to look at the encrypted traffic in an SSL/TLS connection or when there is a need to debug the encrypted handshake of TLS 1.3.
bugs.impact: No ability to debug and analyze encrypted handshake and encrypted data of SSL/TLS connections.
bugs.workaround: You can use the OpenSSL keylogfile option to gather the same information needed to decrypt. This has to be done separately from the tcpdump capture.
bugs.fix: In this release, there is a '--f5 ssl' option provided, which along with setting the dbvar 'tcpdump.sslprovider' to 'enable' supports capture of information needed to decrypt encrypted handshake and data.
bugs.behavior: tcpdump has a new option: '--f5 ssl. When the db variable 'tcpdump.sslprovider' is set to 'enable', the tcpdump operation captures information needed to decrypt encrypted handshake and data.

bugs.title: Active Rule page may display incorrectly if showing multiple rules and at least one rule list
bugs.symptoms: The Active Rule page will truncate the display of active rules if there is more than one page worth of rules to display plus one or more rule lists.
bugs.conditions: More rules than will display on a single page and at least one rule list.
bugs.impact: Difficulty in reviewing and editing firewall rules.
bugs.workaround: It may be possible to review the assigned rules through the individual Policy pages.
bugs.fix: The Active Rule page now displays large numbers of rules correctly along with rule lists.

bugs.title: Wrong parsing of Country Code (Geo) from address region list if Country name contains parentheses.
bugs.symptoms: Wrong parsing of Country Code (Geo) from address region list if Country name contains parentheses.
bugs.conditions: If Country name contains parentheses, then an error is thrown and it cannot be added to the address list
bugs.impact: Address List creation Page
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to add the country Name with parentheses
bugs.fix: If the country Name contains parentheses, it can now be added to the address list page.

bugs.title: Mac Edge fails to pass machine certificate inspection if domain component is included in search criteria
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac fails to recognize DC component in certificate common name field. Edge Client fails to pass machine certificate inspection if domain component is included in search regular expression.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac, machine certificate agent, DC component in common name search regex
bugs.impact: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac might fail to log in.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac now passes Machine Certificate inspection when domain component is included in search criteria.

bugs.title: VIPRION B2100-series LOP firmware version 2.10 update
bugs.symptoms: Booting the blade via PXE results in garbled PXE menu. (ID464614)
bugs.conditions: VIPRION B2100 and B2150 blades with LOP firmware version 2.09.
bugs.impact: PXE menu display is garbled, although responds correctly to correct inputs.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin may crash if webtrace or debug log level is enabled for Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite plugin may crash on large javascript files and tags when webtrace or debug log for Portal Access is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Portal Access log level is set to "Debug", or Web Application Trace feature of Portal Access is active.
bugs.impact: Portal Access is temporarily unavailable. Core file for 'rewrite' process is generated.
bugs.workaround: Disable webtrace Change Portal Access log level to Notice
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where Rewrite plugin could crash when collecting webtrace or debug logs for Portal Access.

bugs.title: Some HTTP::cookie iRule commands can cause TMM to core if required arguments are missing
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores when executing an HTTP::cookie command in an iRule. If the command does not have the minimum required number of arguments, the code is not checking for this condition; it assumes they are there.
bugs.conditions: An iRule command must execute an HTTP::cookie command (such as "HTTP::cookie sanitize") with missing required arguments.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure all HTTP::cookie commands in iRules have the correct number of arguments. A work around is to add a line "log local0. some text" before the line "HTTP::cookie sanitize". Then, there will be no tmm crash.
bugs.fix: Check to make sure all required arguments are present in an HTTP::cookie command prior to attempting to use them.

bugs.title: Message about missing database variable found in ltm log.
bugs.symptoms: You see this message in the install log: liveinstall.log.0:01020036:3: The requested database variable (config.encryption) was not found.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after using 'tmsh sys software' commands
bugs.impact: none, the error is benign.

bugs.title: iControl LocalLB::ProfileClientSSL::create and create_v2 methods result in crash when not in /Common
bugs.symptoms: The iControlPortal process crashes if the LocalLB::ProfileClientSSL::create or create_v2 methods are called outside of the /Common partition.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using iControl to create Client SSL profiles in partitions other than /Common.
bugs.impact: The iControl portal crashes with a 500 Internal Server Error. The Client SSL profile is not created.
bugs.workaround: Create Client SSL profile in the /Common partition.
bugs.fix: LocalLB::ProfileClientSSL::create and create_v2 methods now work correctly when used in partitions other than /Common.

bugs.title: Unhandled connection error in iprepd causes memory leak in iprepd or merged
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system fails to connect to the IP reputation database server (either using a proxy or not), it causes a memory leak in one of the internal daemons (iprepd and/or merged).
bugs.conditions: IP-reputation is enabled and it fails to connect to the database server (usually to the proxy of the database server or there is a bad/non-existent connection outside).
bugs.impact: This issue causes a slow memory leak in the iprepd or merged daemon.
bugs.workaround: Fix the proxy to the ipreputation or the connection to the IP reputation or turn off IP reputation.
bugs.fix: Even if the BIG-IP system fails to connect to the IP reputation database server (either using a proxy or not), it no longer causes a memory leak in one of the internal daemons.

bugs.title: Fix for Policy Rule Names Displaying Distorted in Rare Conditions
bugs.symptoms: Policy rule names are same as firewall rules, except when a rule list is used, they also show the name for referencing rule to rulelist. In rare conditions, these names may show distorted data.
bugs.conditions: You have a firewall policy with a rule list in it.
bugs.impact: Referencing rule names may look distorted. No impact on performance or process.
bugs.fix: Upon investigation, a basic memory problem is diagnosed and fixed.

bugs.title: wamd process keeps restarting during provisioning on the BIG-IP 4000 series platforms.
bugs.symptoms: wamd process keeps restarting. The /var/log/kern.log contains messages similar to the following: info kernel: wamd[29081]: segfault at 78 ip 000000005793c3e0 sp 00000000ff887d30 error 4 in libumem_mt.so[57928000+2c000]
bugs.conditions: This occurs intermittently during provisioning on the BIG-IP 4000 series platforms, and might indicate a race condition in between provisioning and wamd.
bugs.impact: System cannot provision modules and start up properly.

bugs.title: Failure notice from '/usr/bin/set-rsync-mgmt-fw close' seen on each boot.
bugs.symptoms: The ltm log file will have a line per cluster member at boot that contains a message similar to this: Background command '/usr/bin/set-rsync-mgmt-fw close' failed. The command exited with status 1.
