bugs.conditions: Observable in a log file after boot. Only applies to VIPRION chassis.
bugs.impact: The message is innocuous and can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: An error like this formerly appeared on chassis boot: Background command '/usr/bin/set-rsync-mgmt-fw close' failed. The command exited with status 1. This message was always harmless but now no longer appears.
bugs.workaround: None needed.

bugs.title: GUI unable to open and configure iApp Application.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use the GUI to open an existing iApp Application. The GUI throws a database error.
bugs.conditions: Open an existing iApp Application from the GUI or create a new iApp Application and try to configure it.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure the iApp Application from the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to configure the iApp Application.
bugs.fix: Can now use the GUI to retrieve and configure existing iApp Applications.

bugs.title: Mirrored persistence information is not retained while flows are active
bugs.symptoms: Mirrored persistence information is not retained. This is most visible on long-running flows, where the mirrored entry is removed while the flow is still active.
bugs.conditions: Mirrored flows with persistence profiles assigned to the VIP, or when persistence profiles are marked to mirror persistence entries.
bugs.impact: If a failover occurs, a new load balancing pick is made for new flows.
bugs.fix: Mirrored persistence records are now correctly retained.

bugs.title: TMM cores with TMM log error 'Assertion "flow in use" failed.' when isuing FastHTTP.
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores with the TMM log showing the error 'Assertion "flow in use" failed.' This is an infrequent race condition.
bugs.conditions: This is an infrequent race condition. The actual set of events that leads to this core is unknown. However, this requires FastHTTP to be configured, and it is known that this happens when the FastHTTP connection is closing.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use FastHTTP.
bugs.fix: The system now provides checks to mitigate the race condition on close of FastHTTP to avoid the core.

bugs.title: Invalid MAX-ACCESS clause for deprecated variables: ltmNodeAddrNewSessionEnable and ltmPoolMemberNewSessionEnable.
bugs.symptoms: Invalid MAX-ACCESS clause for deprecated variables: ltmNodeAddrNewSessionEnable and ltmPoolMemberNewSessionEnable.
bugs.conditions: Using deprecated variables: ltmNodeAddrNewSessionEnable and ltmPoolMemberNewSessionEnable.
bugs.impact: User is unable compile MIB (using smidump) if deprecated objects are not ignored.
bugs.workaround: Modify MAX-ACCESS to read-only.
bugs.fix: MAX-ACCESS clause is now correct for deprecated variables: ltmNodeAddrNewSessionEnable and ltmPoolMemberNewSessionEnable.

bugs.title: Page rendering is incorrect when both CSS inline and JavaScript reordering are enabled
bugs.symptoms: When both CSS inline and JavaScript reordering are enabled, page rendering might be incorrect due to missing 'src' attribute in a script tag.
bugs.conditions: Have AAM provisioned and a policy with both CSS inline and JavaScript reordering enabled and attached to a virtual server. Have a page with both CSS and JavaScript resources associated requested via the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Web pages do render correctly.
bugs.workaround: Disable either of the optimizations.

bugs.title: Large number inlining URLs may cause a connection reset
bugs.symptoms: Using AAM to inline a large number of JavaScripts in HTML code might result in resetting a connection and not serving the requested page to the client.
bugs.conditions: Provision AAM and have a policy with inlining enabled for a large number of configured JavaScripts used in a single HTML page. Send a request to this page.
bugs.impact: When conditions are met there is a chance that the connection will be reset and the content won't be served to the client.
bugs.workaround: Reducing the number of inlining-enabled JavaScripts might result in properly serving the page.

bugs.title: Response is halted or reset when the request has an ignore profile
bugs.symptoms: Response is halted for some seconds or doesn't arrive at all (fin or rst)
bugs.conditions: The request has a "do nothing" profile. Request is a POST. This happens more frequently if the response size is large.
bugs.impact: Response to that request is halted for some seconds or doesn't arrive at all (fin or rst)
bugs.workaround: Change the content profile of that URL. Note that this workaround may cause false positive attack signatures and/or other false positive.

bugs.title: If net self description size =65K, gtmd restarts continuously
bugs.symptoms: The gtmd process restarts continuously.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the net self <IP> description >= <65K string> 'Description', 'Location', 'Contact', or 'Comment' field for the device (Device Management>Devices>Properties) > = <65K string>
bugs.impact: When this happens, gtmd is unable to perform its duties.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: An issue that caused gtmd to restart because of long descriptions has been fixed.

bugs.title: Compression from BIG-IP APM to client is still present even if it is disabled in connectivity profile.
bugs.symptoms: Connectivity profile compression setting specifies compression level for BIG-IP-to-client direction. Compression from BIG-IP-APM-to-client is still present even if it is disabled in connectivity profile.
bugs.conditions: GZIP compression is enabled in network access resource. GZIP compression level is set to 0 (No compression) in the Network Access section of the connectivity profile. Expected behavior: there is compression in client-to-BIG-IP direction, there is no compression in BIG-IP-to-client direction. Observed behavior: there is compression in both directions.
bugs.impact: Compression from BIG-IP-to-client direction can not be turned off by connectivity profile setting.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, modify the value of the compression.strategy db variable to "speed": tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy value speed

bugs.title: DNS Express daemon, zxfrd, can not start if its binary cache has filled /var
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express daemon, zxfrd, cannot start if its binary cache has filled the /var directory.
bugs.conditions: Using DNS Express and the /var directory is filled.
bugs.impact: Zxfrd will continually restart.
bugs.workaround: No workaround, but if in zxfrd restart loop due to this issue you can mitigate the issue by deleting /var/db/tmmdns.bin and then running the following command: bigstart restart zxfrd.
bugs.fix: DNS Express daemon, zxfrd, will now check to see if /var is full or if the tmmdns.bin database file is corrupted. If either of these conditions is true, zxfrd will not continually restart.

bugs.title: Graceful Restart does not function when primary blade is rebooted
bugs.symptoms: When primary blade in rebooted, the system halts all daemons, including those that maintain the routing table. This might flush routing table before the secondary blade becomes active, and that might cause traffic outages. Because of this issue, you might see the following symptom: Dynamic routes advertised by the BIG-IP system and by the neighbors, are deleted due to the shutdown. OSPF withdraws the routes advertised to the neighbor.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the primary blade in rebooted.
bugs.impact: Traffic flow may be impacted. Note: The graceful restart process is initiated on the new primary blade at this point, which recovers the routes.
bugs.workaround: Force blade failover first before rebooting blade. To force an active blade or cluster into a standby state: 1. Navigate to System :: High Availability :: Failover :: Redundancy. 2. Click Force to Standby. With failover, the new blade becomes primary and picks up routing functions before the reboot halts the routing daemons.
bugs.fix: The shutdown process now forces blade failover first before rebooting the blade, which enables the secondary to pick up the routing table before becoming primary.

bugs.title: Tab-completion does not work for TCP/HTTP profiles with ltm virtual profiles
bugs.symptoms: Tab-completion does not work for TCP/HTTP profiles with the command: ltm virtual profiles.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with TCP and HTTP profiles when using Tab-completion in tmsh.
bugs.impact: Cannot use Tab-complete with TCP or HTTP profiles.
bugs.workaround: Type the profile name out completely, instead of using tab-completion to complete the name of the profile.

bugs.title: Allow setting of the AAA Radius server timeout value larger than 60 seconds
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes 60 sec timeout for AAA Radius server is not enough especially when users need to provide input. Following error message will be displayed when user tries to set timeout value greater than 60 : "01090676:3: The requested timeout value (120) out of range for aaa radius server (/Common/test-radius-server). (1-60)"
bugs.conditions: This only occurs whenever following conditions are met: - APM is licensed and provisioned - AAA Radius server is configured - Radius Auth agent is included in the access policy
bugs.impact: Users can not set timeout value to more than 60 sec for AAA Radius server. If response time is more than 60 sec from AAA Radius server, users may not login and access resources if two factor auth is configured.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Increased the AAA Radius Server timeout range from 0-60 to 0-180.

bugs.title: Intermittent 'AgentX' warning messages in syslog/ZebOS log files
bugs.symptoms: When routing protocols ospfv2, ospfv3, bgp, rip, ripng are configured to exchange routing information, the system posts agentx-related warning messages in the syslog/zebos log files similar to the following: <date+time> warnings: <protocol> : AgentX: process_packet (<state name> state), ... <date+time> warnings: <protocol> : AgentX: requested pdu : 1
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a BIG-IP system is configured for SNMP traps on the ZebOS routing protocols.
bugs.impact: These warning messages are cosmetic and may be logged intermittently, possibly resulting in a large number of messages.
bugs.fix: Benign agentx warning messages are no longer logged for the routing protocols ospfv2, ospfv3, bgp, rip, ripng.

bugs.title: In rare cases, an upgrade (or a restart) can result in an Active/Active state
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading or restarting, the system starts up in an active state even if the peer system is already active.
bugs.conditions: An upgrade or system restart for an active/standby pair. The issue occurs intermittently and is timing-dependent. There is code executed during sod's initialization that attempts to detect when communication between mcpd and sod has gone bad; this code does this by checking for "end transaction" messages. If 30 or more messages from mcpd are received without an "end transaction" message, sod will reset its connection with mcpd. While the connection is being reset, it is possible for sod to miss messages from mcpd. Depending on which messages it misses, sod may end up in a bad state and exhibit the symptoms of this bug. If this occurs after an upgrade, it does not matter which version one is upgrading from.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that both systems take traffic.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the 'sod' daemon on the system after an upgrade or reboot clears the condition. This causes the system to go offline and will disrupt traffic. Standard BIG-IP appliance: bigstart restart sod VIPRION system: clsh bigstart restart sod
bugs.fix: In this release, the system ensures that an upgrade or a restart can never result in an Active/Active state.

bugs.title: In Chrome browser, displayed user role switches to Unknown for few seconds after switching partitions.
bugs.symptoms: When certain users switch partitions, their displayed role shows Unknown. After a few seconds, the appropriate role displays for the active partition.
bugs.conditions: A user with access only to specific partitions and switches partitions. This occurs only with the Chrome browser.
bugs.impact: Unknown is shown as their role in the top bar in the GUI. This issue is only cosmetic, the user's actual role changes immediately. Any activity in the intervening time period is performed as the user's true role in that partition.
bugs.workaround: Use Firefox or Internet Explorer browsers.

bugs.title: Continuous policy checks on windows might fail incorrectly in some cases
bugs.symptoms: If continuous software check (for antivirus, firewall and so on) is configured to ignore certain configurations (state, last scan time, and so on.) and any of these configurations changes on the client system, then continuous check kills the session. For example, if a continuous antivirus software check on server is configured to ignore the last scan time, for example, and if antivirus last scan time changes in the middle of the policy (or if a scan completes in the middle while in connection), then continuous software check kills the session. This happens because recurrent software check compares the entire result string of the antivirus check with the result string returned by the first check.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following are true: 1. Software checks (Antivirus, Firewall, and so on), Windows File, or Windows Process are included in the access policy. 2. Continuous software check is enabled. 3. The client is a Windows-based system.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that continuous checks could kill the session.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Continuous policy checks now do not kill the session if a property that was configured to be ignored changes on the client side.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Partial PATCH to User-Defined Signature-Set Filter Resets Other Fields to Defaults
bugs.symptoms: Update any "filter" field for signature-set changes other unchanged "filter" fields to default.
bugs.conditions: REST Client is used to configure ASM and partial objects (only changed fields) are sent in a PATCH
bugs.impact: A User-Defined Filter Based Signature Set may not contain the expected signatures
bugs.workaround: When updating the object via a PATCH, send the fully populated object.
bugs.fix: Filter fields that are not explicitly specified in the PATCH call are correctly left unchanged.

bugs.title: Missing sys DeviceModel OID for VIPRION C2200 chassis
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP sysObjectID OID returns a value of Unknown for VIPRION C2200 chassis.
bugs.conditions: Affected versions of BIG-IP running on VIPRION B2xxx-series blades in a VIPRION C2200 chassis.
bugs.impact: The VIPRION C2200 chassis is not identified as such by the SNMP sysObjectID OID.
bugs.fix: The sys DeviceModel OID for VIPRION C2200 (Viprion2200) chassis is now present in the F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB.

bugs.title: Cannot set the value of a session variable with a leading hyphen.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot set the value of an ACCESS::session variable with a leading hyphen.
bugs.conditions: Using a leading hyphen for the value of the session variable, for example: ACCESS::session set data var_name -value.
bugs.impact: Cannot use hyphen in session variable value. The system posts and error message similar to the following: err tmm3[12741]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/pass <ACCESS_POLICY_AGENT_EVENT> - bad option name (line 1)setting variable var_name for sid (null) failed (line 1)Illegal argument (line 1) (line 1) invoked from within "ACCESS::session data set var_name "-foo""
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: In this release, an extra parameter, made up of two dashes (--), was added. When -- is inserted before a value, the value can start with a hyphen; for example, "ACCESS::session set data var_name -- -value".

bugs.title: Heartbeat, UDP packet with only double CRLF, on existing SIP flow results in connection loss.
bugs.symptoms: Heartbeat, UDP packet with only double CRLF, on existing SIP flow might result in connection loss.
bugs.conditions: SIP heartbeat message, a UDP packet with double CRLF, sent by the client to the server.
bugs.impact: Connection might be terminated.
bugs.fix: The heartbeat SIP message, which is a UDP packet with CRLF, is ignored and connection is maintained.

bugs.title: Added warning message when maximum session timeout is reached
bugs.symptoms: Perviously when EdgeClient reaches maximum session timoeut it simply disconnects with no indication of reason.
bugs.conditions: Session reaches maximum timeout
bugs.impact: User may be confused
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP Edge Client shows warning about session expiration when maximum session timeout is reached.

bugs.title: SNAT automap may select source address that is not attached to egress VLAN/interface
bugs.symptoms: Egress packets have a source address that is not associated with the VLAN or interface.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the following conditions are met: - Virtual utilizes SNAT automap. - There exists a route matching a self-ip on interface A to a VLAN on interface B.
bugs.impact: Packets may not be routed properly.
bugs.workaround: Use SNAT pool instead of automap.
bugs.fix: SNAT Automap now matches self-ip against selected SNAT pool member instead of the pool member route.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is used as SAML SP, signatures created by IBM Tivoli Federated Identity Manager may fail validation
bugs.symptoms: Signature validation fails when received signed assertion is generated by IBM Tivoli Federated Identity Manager.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the BIG-IP system is configured as SP and received assertion is signed.
bugs.impact: Issue impacts SSO, users cannot login with SAML.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Issue with signature validation is fixed.

bugs.title: On HSB platforms which don't have HW DoS, bad cksum pkts could cause perf drop
bugs.symptoms: If you have a HSB platform that does not have HW DoS features then bad TCP/UDP/IP checksum pkts could cause a performance drop.
bugs.conditions: -- Platform which does not have HW DoS. -- A very high number of bad checksum packets are received
bugs.impact: Performance will not be optimum.
bugs.workaround: Create a file with name 'tmm_init.tcl' in '/config' containing the following lines: HSB::netc_ipcsum_drop yes HSB::netc_l4csum_drop yes And then reboot.

bugs.title: modify sshd config gererates error messages while sshd not running
bugs.symptoms: Modifying banner and banner-text while sshd service is disabled, result in error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when modifying banner and banner-text while sshd service is disabled.
bugs.impact: The system posts an error.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to change config order to enable login before banner change, or perform the operations in separate commands. -- tmsh modify sys sshd login enabled banner disabled banner-text none. -- tmsh modify sys sshd login enabled. -- tmsh modify sys sshd banner disabled banner-text none.

bugs.title: Customization GUI not showing proper error message when modify customization group file created from iApps
bugs.symptoms: Objects that are created through iApps cannot be modified unless the user explicitly specifies to allow modification. An incorrect error message appears When the user tries to modify the object.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the user tries to modify a customization group file created through iApps.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that an incorrect error message appears, which might confuse the administrator.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Loading ucs file after install 11.6.0 on top of 11.5.0 failed when Gx reporting is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: After installing BIG-IP 11.6.0 on top of BIG-IP 11.5.0, a saved ucs file might need to be loaded. If the Gx reporting is enabled, the ucs file loading will fail.
bugs.conditions: 1. upgrade from BIG-IP 11.5.0 to BIG-IP 11.6.0 2. load saved ucs file
bugs.impact: Old ucs file cannot be used after upgrading from BIG-IP 11.5.0 to BIG-IP 11.6.0
bugs.workaround: disable Gx reporting
bugs.fix: After the fix, an upgrade to BIG-IP 11.6.0 from BIG-IP 11.5.0 followed by a UCS load completes successfully.

bugs.title: Allow special characters importing SSL Key and Certificate except backslash.
bugs.symptoms: GUI validation does not allow for special characters in the SSL Key and Certificate names. Whereas tmsh allows for special characters.
bugs.conditions: Import an SSL Key or Certificate with a name that contains a question mark, colon, at sign, exclamation mark, ampersand, or pound sign (hashtag): ?:@!&#.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the GUI to manage Key or Certificate created in tmsh with special characters in their name.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to manage the Key or Certificate.
bugs.fix: The GUI now allows special characters when importing SSL Key and Certificate. Note that backslash, \ is not supported as a character in the name.

bugs.title: Log files limited to 24 hours
bugs.symptoms: In this release, the max log size setting is 1024. This causes large systems (multiple blades, high-availability) to truncate log files, and often prevent log files from storing messages for more than 24 hours.
bugs.conditions: Multiple blades in a high-availability configuration.
bugs.impact: Cannot have log files spanning more than 24 hours. This makes it very difficult to use the log when diagnosing problems, because the system overwrites the files before the customer can report the issue.
bugs.workaround: Change the max-file-size for logrotate from '1024' (the default) to '0' to prevent logrotate from truncating log files. This workaround is also documented in SOL16015: The BIG-IP system may truncate log files, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/000/sol16015.html. This can be done from tmsh by running a command such as: tmsh modify /sys log-rotate max-file-size 0
bugs.fix: The max log size setting is now greater than 1024, which allows large systems (multiple blades, high-availability) to store messages for more than 24 hours.

bugs.title: Deleting OPSWAT/Epsec packages from GUI does not delete files from disk causing UCS packages to bloat
bugs.symptoms: If there were multiple EPSEC packages installed on a BIG-IP system and if a UCS backup is taken subsequently, that UCS backup will contain all the files causing the UCS to become huge. Installing this UCS may fail due to disk space limitations.
bugs.conditions: For this issue, multiple EPSEC packages have to be installed in the system and the UCS of this system is created.
bugs.impact: UCS fails to install due to its large size.
bugs.workaround: One can do the following: 1. Delete the EPSEC package from the GUI. 2. Then go the /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/epsec_package_d/ Find the extra files for which there is no corresponding entry in /config/bigip.conf. 3. Delete those extraneous files manually using rm.
bugs.fix: When you delete EPSEC packages using the GUI, APM now correctly deletes the corresponding EPSEC ISO file from the filestore (/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/epsec_package_d/). Before creating archives, administrators are now required to delete non-active EPSEC packages using the GUI to make sure that non-active EPSEC ISO files are not included in the archives. Although this issue has been resolved for newly downloaded EPSEC ISO files, you might still need to perform some cleanup: 1. You must remove previous leftover EPSEC ISO files as follows: a. Delete the EPSEC package from the GUI: Select System > Software Management > Antivirus Check Updates; select an existing EPSEC package from the list and click Delete. b. Go to /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/epsec_package_d/ and find files for which there is no corresponding entry in /config/bigip.conf. c. Delete those extraneous files manually using the rm command. 2. You cannot import huge previously created UCS archives. Instead, you should delete non-active EPSEC packages prior to creating a UCS. 3. If you want to include only one (active) EPSEC ISO in a UCS archive, you must first delete non-active EPSEC packages using the GUI.

bugs.title: Running Response Analytics for SSL Bypass traffic allows connection and does not have URL Request Log information
bugs.symptoms: SWG report (Access Policy ›› Event Logs : URL Request Logs ) doesn't show the logs for HTTPS site when in SSL bypass mode when Response Analytics Agent is present in per-request policy.
bugs.conditions: SWG Explicit Per-request policy: Start -> Protocol Lookup (HTTPS) -> Category Lookup (SNI) -> SSL Bypass Set -> Response Analytics -> Allow
bugs.impact: Admin is not aware of the SSL Bypass traffic being processed as no log information is available in URL Request Logs

bugs.title: TMM core in AAM assembly code during high memory utilization
bugs.symptoms: TMM core is seen in AAM assembly code during high memory utilization.
bugs.conditions: AAM is provisioned. High memory utilization scenario resulting in sweeper aggressive mode being triggered. This results in connections getting reset. Inlining or smart client cache is enabled in AAM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: TCP syncookie and Selective NACK (profile option) causes traffic to be dropped
bugs.symptoms: TCP syncookie and Selective NACK (profile option) causes traffic to be dropped.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Selective NACK enabled in TCP profile. -- TCP syncookie mode. -- No Selective NACK option in TCP options from client SYN.
bugs.impact: Traffic might be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Disable Selective NACK option in TCP profile.
bugs.fix: TCP syncookie and Selective NACK (profile option) now works correctly.

bugs.title: Default cron script /usr/share/mysql/purge_mysql_logs.pl throws error.
bugs.symptoms: The /usr/share/mysql/purge_mysql_logs.pl script that ships with the new install (and is run hourly via cron) throws an error. The script is meant to be exited if AAM, ASM and PSM are not provisioned, but the check is not done appropriately and it continues execution, failing later.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system with no AAM, ASM, and PSM provisioned, when running the script /etc/cron.hourly/purge_mysql_logs.pl (linked to /usr/share/mysql/purge_mysql_logs.pl)
bugs.impact: The script gives false output and attempts to execute invalid actions. The system posts the following error: Usage: $class->connect([$dsn [,$user [,$passwd [,\%attr]]]]) at /etc/cron.hourly/purge_mysql_logs.pl line 27.
bugs.workaround: Provision AAM, ASM, or PSM. Or modify the script using the following procedure: Remount /usr partition as RW: # mount -o remount -rw /usr Edit /usr/share/mysql/purge_mysql_logs.pl and change the original check: unless( $provisioned_am || $provisioned_asm || $provisioned_psm ) { exit 0; } to: unless( $provisioned_am == 1 || $provisioned_asm == 1 || $provisioned_psm == 1 ) { exit 0; }

bugs.title: WAM CSS minification can add spaces to the output, potentially coring TMM (in rare cases)
bugs.symptoms: TMM coring, or exhibiting strange behavior. Checking the WAM stats reveals an underflow for bytes_minified in wam_css_stat, for example: active parses bytes_parsed bytes_queued partial_parses partial_parse_bytes ------ ------ ------------ ------------ -------------- ------------------- 0 4 612 0 4 586 annotations resets parser_errors bytes_minified images_inlined ----------- ------ ------------- -------------------- -------------- 5 0 0 18446744073709551564 0 images_bytes_inlined images_uninlined images_uninlined_expiry -------------------- ---------------- ----------------------- 0 0 0
bugs.conditions: The CSS data that is being minified must already be minified and contain no extraneous whitespace.
bugs.impact: TMM may core or behave unexpectedly. The wam_css_stat stat's bytes_minified will be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Disable CSS minification.
bugs.fix: Extra spaces are no longer added to the minified CSS.

bugs.title: IDE DMA timeouts can result in stuck processes
bugs.symptoms: If the device experiences an IDE DMA timeout, some processes become unresponsive and the kernel logs messages containing 'DMA timeout error' in kern.log. An unfulfilled request from the kernel of the IDE device might result in uninterruptible, stuck processes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on VIPRION B4100/B4100N (A100), B4200/B4200N (A107) blades and on Virtual Edition (VE) configurations deployed with IDE storage drivers (Xen, Hyper-V).
bugs.impact: This condition can cause the i/o request to never complete and result in unresponsive and uninterruptible processes. Various symptoms result depending on the affected process. Some conditions might require a power cycle to correct.
bugs.fix: IDE DMA timeouts no longer result in become unresponsive on VIPRION B4100/B4100N (A100), B4200/B4200N (A107) blades and on Virtual Edition (VE) configurations deployed with IDE storage drivers (Xen, Hyper-V).

bugs.title: sysObjectID SNMP OID returns 'linux' instead of BIG-IP platform.
bugs.symptoms: sysObjectID SNMP OID returns 'linux' instead of BIG-IP platform.
bugs.conditions: Poll for sysObjectID OID.
bugs.impact: sysObjectID OID value does not uniquely identify the BIG-IP product. Polling for sysObjectID OID always returns value 'linux': snmpget -v2c -c 'community' localhost sysObjectID.0 RFC1213-MIB::sysObjectID.0 = OID: NET-SNMP-TC::linux
bugs.fix: sysObjectID OID now correctly returns the appropriate BIG-IP platform.

bugs.title: Management interface sending erroneous IPv6 MLD or IPv4 IGMP packets
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP management interface may erroneously send IPv6 Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) Listener Query or IPv4 Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) Membership Query packets.
bugs.conditions: Any platform that uses Linux interface 'mgmt' as opposed to 'eth0'. This is applicable for all platforms except the following: 1600, 3600, 3900, 6900, 8900, 8950, 11000, 11050, VE (Virtual Edition guests), and vCMP (vCMP guests hosted by BIG-IP platforms).
bugs.impact: No production traffic impact, but extra management traffic. Some switches may report an IGMP or MLD error when connected to the mgmt port.
bugs.workaround: Disable the unwanted MLD and IGMP packets by doing the following: echo 0 > /sys/class/net/mgmt/bridge/multicast_snooping. This is applicable for all platforms except the following: 1600, 3600, 3900, 6900, 8900, 8950, 11000, 11050, VE (Virtual Edition guests), and VCMP (vCMP guests hosted by BIG-IP platforms).

bugs.title: FQDN nodes or pool members show Green (Available) when DNS responds with NXDOMAIN
bugs.symptoms: FQDN nodes and pool members show a status of Green (Available) when the DNS server responds to the FQDN name resolution query with an NXDOMAIN response.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the DNS server returns an NXDOMAIN response for the configured FQDN name.
bugs.impact: FQDN nodes and pool members may appear to be Available when no ephemeral nodes/pool members have been created.
bugs.fix: FQDN nodes and pool members show a status of Yellow (Unavailable) when the DNS server responds to the FQDN name resolution query with an NXDOMAIN response. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.
bugs.behavior: FQDN ephemeral nodes are now deleted when the DNS server responds to the FQDN name resolution query with an NXDOMAIN response. This change in behavior was introduced by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: Fix in the Guardium to ASM protocol
bugs.symptoms: Guardium doesn't find a message from ASM. The username doesn't appear in the Guardium logs.
bugs.conditions: A big response arrives.
bugs.impact: The username doesn't appear in the guardium logs
bugs.fix: We moved the Guardium message notification from the RESPONSE event to the RESPONSE_DONE event. Username now appears in the Guardium logs.

bugs.title: passphrase visible in audit log
bugs.symptoms: With audit logging enabled, you notice that after updating a password for an account it is visible in /var/log/audit
bugs.conditions: This occurs when audit logging is enabled.
bugs.impact: Password is visible in the audit log.
bugs.workaround: Disable audit logging.
bugs.fix: The password is no longer logged in the audit log.

bugs.title: In some cases user cannot go to external sites through proxy when vpn is connected
bugs.symptoms: In some cases user cannot go to external sites through proxy when vpn is connected
bugs.conditions: -Edge client from APM is used to establish VPN to a FirePass server. - User's machine cannot resolve DNS name of the site that user is attempting to connect to. - Proxy server is used.
bugs.impact: User cannot browse external sites.
bugs.fix: Added new configuration option "Do not enforce IP scopes in Proxy-Auto-Configuration". Administrators who want support for such scenario can enable this option in their NA configuration.

bugs.title: Leak due to monitor status reporting
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd memory steadily increases until it runs out. Running "strings" on the resulting core file reveals many instances of a monitor error message.
bugs.conditions: Must have a monitor configured that generates an error message.
bugs.impact: Slow system performance, unexpected crash and failover.
bugs.workaround: Disable the monitor.
bugs.fix: Previously, mcpd might leak memory when returning an error message that contained the reason for a monitor failure. The message now reports the reason without leaking memory.

bugs.title: Searching ASM Request Log for requests with specific violations
bugs.symptoms: Filtering the ASM Request Log for requests that match some violations did not return expected results.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the Request Log Filter is used for specific violations such as "Web Scraping detected."
bugs.impact: Request Log search does not return expected matches.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The Request log filter for violations now functions as expected. Previously, filtering the ASM Request Log for requests that match some violations did not return expected results.

bugs.title: Error messages in AVR monpd log
bugs.symptoms: The following errors (similar) appear in the monpd log: monpd|INFO|Jun 18 13:40:08.947|12463| [stat_bridge_thread::load_file, ] Some rows of load_stat_asm_http_ip_1403124000.1 not loaded (18194 rows affected)
bugs.conditions: In rare cases that include stress traffic and other rare conditions.
bugs.impact: There can be very small percentage of lost statistics (approximately 0.002%).
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue in which the system had duplicated data, leading to display of the following warning message in the AVR monpd log: 'Some rows of load_stat_asm_http_ip_xxxxxxxxxx.x not loaded (xxxxx rows affected)'.

bugs.title: UCS file from earlier version may not load into 11.5.0 or later image
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to upgrade to 11.5.0 or later, from an earlier release, some .ucs files may cause the system to run out of memory, and the kernel to kill the process. You may also see an error: "UCS application failed; unknown cause."
bugs.conditions: In the .ucs file, in bigip.conf, is a section like this: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/my-clientssl { ... defaults-from /Common/wom-default-clientssl ... } The problem happens because /Common/wom-default-clientssl and /Common/clientssl-insecure-compatible was not defined in a couple of our fixup scripts, resulting in infinite recursion in another fixup script.
bugs.impact: It can be impossible to upgrade the software image to 11.5.0 or later because the config fixup exits in error.
bugs.workaround: A workaround is to change instances of "wom-default-clientssl" and "clientssl-insecure-compatible" to "clientssl" in the configuration files in the UCS archive.
bugs.fix: "wom-default-clientssl" and "clientssl-insecure-compatible" were added to two fixup scripts, and code to prevent infinite recursion was added to another script.

bugs.title: An LB_FAILED iRule that references an undefined value can cause Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) failover.
bugs.symptoms: If an LB_FAILED iRule calls HTTP::respond and references an undefined value, then Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) can crash or failover. The following is in the ltm logfile showing the undefined value reference: Jun 19 11:10:04 bigip1 err tmm[9515]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/rule_lbpickfailed <LB_FAILED> - can't read "value": no such variable while executing "log local0. "$value doesn't exist""
bugs.conditions: The following have to be configured in order for this to reproduce: 1. An http profile with web acceleration and http compression enabled: profiles { /Common/http { } /Common/optimized-acceleration { } /Common/tcp { } /Common/wan-optimized-compression { } } 2. An LB_FAILED iRule that calls HTTP::respond and references an undefined value: when LB_FAILED { HTTP::respond 200 content "content" log local0. "$value doesn't exist" }
bugs.impact: The TMM crashes.
bugs.workaround: Fix iRule by not referencing an undefined value within LB_FAILED.

bugs.title: When Kerberos authentication is used with RBA enabled, the first POST request sent to the BIG-IP system could be lost under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: When Kerberos authentication is used with request-based authentication (RBA) enabled, the first POST request sent to the BIG-IP system could be replaced by a dummy POST and authentication then fails. This can occur when the BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP) and the http-post SSO binding is used.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: 1. RBA is enabled. 2. Kerberos Auth is used. 3. The first request to the BIG-IP system before session has been established is a POST request.
bugs.impact: Some functionality may not behave properly; for example, when the BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML IdP and an http-post SSO binding is used, AuthnRequest can get lost and authentication will fail.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, edit the access policy and, in the properties for the Kerberos Auth item, set Request Based Auth to Disabled.

bugs.title: Network Access logs missing session ID
bugs.symptoms: Without session ID in client logs, it's hard to correlate client and server-side logs.
bugs.impact: Hard to troubleshoot client logs
bugs.fix: Now Network Access components print session ID in four messages: Starting pending session ID: %sessionid, Session %sessionid established, Session %sessionid closed: Status, and Failed to open session %sessionid.

bugs.title: IPsec interop with Cisco systems intermittent outages
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, traffic going through an IPsec tunnel from BIG-IP systems to Cisco systems stops after a certain period of time and recovers after an hour.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when there is more than one pair of IPsec SAs negotiated and triggers redundant SA removal on the Cisco router.
bugs.impact: IPsec tunnel stops passing traffic until the trouble IPsec SA expires and the new set of IPsec SAs are negotiated.
bugs.workaround: Delete the trouble IPsec SAs
bugs.fix: The system now works correctly, without stopping traffic going through an IPsec tunnel from BIG-IP systems to Cisco systems.

bugs.title: TMM can crash with SIGFPE assertion 'valid ctx crule_cnt' when a firewall iRule and OneConnect are used together.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with SIGFPE assertion 'valid ctx crule_cnt'.
bugs.conditions: -- Firewall iRule configured. -- OneConnect configured. Note: A firewall policy (eventually referencing a firewall iRule) can be applied to places other than a virtual server. For instance, a firewall policy can be applied to a route-domain. This might still cause interaction with a virtual server equipped with OneConnect, and lead to the issue.
bugs.impact: TMM dumps core and restarts. This can disrupt traffic or lead to a failover on redundant units.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not simultaneously configuring firewall iRules and OneConnect.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with SIGFPE assertion 'valid ctx crule_cnt'.

bugs.title: The worldwide City database (City2) does not contain all of the appropriate Proxy strings.
bugs.symptoms: Digital Element's proxy information is not available in the City2 database.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the City2 database available from an F5 partner.
bugs.impact: In the case of a customer obtaining and installing the city database, Digital Element's proxy information is not included.
bugs.fix: The worldwide City database (City2) now includes Digital Element's proxy information.

bugs.title: Connection reset with client value of "/" in rewrite profile
bugs.symptoms: When virtual server has rewrite-uri-translation rewrite profile with Client value of / and an Access Policy is also on that virtual server then the connection will reset, reset cause will be "Access encountered an error (Out of memory..."
bugs.conditions: Connection reset with out of memory. - Virtual Server - Access Policy - rewrite-uri-translation rewrite profile - URI Rules -> Client value is /
bugs.impact: - Clients fail to connect to virtual server solution - FSE's customer POC is failing
bugs.workaround: Do not use / as a Client value within a URI Rule within a rewrite-uri-translation rewrite profile Do not specify an Access Policy and a rewrite-uri-translation rewrite profile that has a / as Client value within a URI Rule

bugs.title: Filters may not work correctly with websockets or CONNECT
bugs.symptoms: If filters that buffer messages exist on the chain, then when HTTP switches to pass-through mode, those filters may spuriously fail to see the headers of the response that cased that switch. The problem is due to HTTP immediately switching into pass-through mode, and then sending the headers as raw data through the chain.
bugs.conditions: A filter on the chain that buffers a RESPONSE_DONE message, and HTTP switches to pass-through, combined with looking at the headers in a filter other than HTTP. This is more likely to happen if the server sends data immediately after a successful CONNECT or transition to websockets. (Without waiting for a response from the client.)
bugs.impact: The TMM may core, or wrong information may be obtained from filters looking at the HTTP headers of a response that causes a switch to pass-through mode.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: HTTP now waits until all filters have seen a 101 Switching Protocols or CONNECT 200 Connected response before switching into pass-through mode.

bugs.title: TMM crash when MPTCP JOIN arrives in the middle of a flow
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when MPTCP JOIN arrives in the middle of a flow.
bugs.conditions: No workaround
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A MPTCP JOIN arriving in the middle of a flow is now handled correctly.

bugs.title: Enforcer core related to specific error condition in the session db
bugs.symptoms: A bd restart, and failover if redundant configuration exists, may occur. The core file will show tm_untimeout () as the coring frame.
bugs.conditions: -- Load on the system. -- Heavy usage of the sessiondb infrastructure.
bugs.impact: Traffic will reset while the bd restart or while the failover is happening.
bugs.workaround: Disable session tracking from the ASM policy.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an Enforcer crash related to a specific error condition in the session db.

bugs.title: IPv4 Allocation failure ... is out of addresses
bugs.symptoms: Existing Network Access clients have problems reconnecting.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the lease pool IP addresses are allocated to Network Access clients.
bugs.impact: Existing clients cannot reconnect. The system posts messages to the APM logs: IPv4 Allocation failure ... is out of addresses.
bugs.workaround: Assign more IP addresses in the lease pool.
bugs.fix: Network Access clients can reconnect now and the lease pool does not run out of IP addresses.

bugs.title: OWA2013 may work incorrectly via Portal Access in IE10/11
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript error appears if user tries to view or change settings in OWA2013 via Portal Access in Internet Explorer 10/11.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: Internet Explorer 10 or 11 and OWA2013.
bugs.impact: User cannot change settings in OWA2013.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now it is possible to view and/or change settings in OWA2013 via Portal Access using Internet Explorer 10/11.

bugs.title: OWA2013 may work incorrectly via Portal Access in IE10/11
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript error appears if user tries to view/change settings in OWA2013 via Portal Access in Internet Explorer 10/11.
bugs.conditions: Internet Explorer 10 or 11 OWA2013
bugs.impact: User cannot change settings in OWA2013.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is known.
bugs.fix: Now it is possible to view and/or change settings in OWA2013 via Portal Access using Internet Explorer 10/11.

bugs.title: The output of DNS::edns0 subnet address command is not stored properly in a variable
bugs.symptoms: When the iRule command "DNS::ends0 subnet address" is an IPv4 address and is stored in a variable, it might not be interpreted properly by other iRule commands that expect an IP address (for example, the "whereis" command).
bugs.conditions: The output of "DNS::ends0 subnet address" command returns an IPv4 address and it is stored in a variable.
bugs.impact: Other iRule commands that utilize the variable may not work as expected (for example, the "whereis" command).
bugs.workaround: When utilizing the variable, force a string interpretation of the value. For example, rather than: set srcip [DNS::ends0 subnet address] set srccountry [whereis $srcip country] Use set srcip [DNS::ends0 subnet address] set srccountry [whereis [string tolower $srcip] country]

bugs.title: Unexpected ordering of internal events can lead to TMM core.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core and failover with the following tcp4 assert: ../modules/hudfilter/tcp4/tcp4.c:937: %svalid pcb%s.
bugs.conditions: If the TCP profile receives a spurious event it can cause TMM to crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Unexpected ordering of internal events no longer leads to TMM core.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Monitors with domain username do not save/load correctly
bugs.symptoms: Using the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) to create or modify an object with a string parameter may fail with an error.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: • You use the tmsh utility to create or modify an object with a string that uses a backslash (\) to escape a double quotation mark (") character.
bugs.impact: Users may not be able to modify strings by using the tmsh utility.
bugs.workaround: The username field must be adjusted in the /config/bigip.conf file to specify the username field with a domain using a \\ syntax. For example: domain\user would need to be configured as: domain\\user.
bugs.fix: tmsh utility does not process backslashes and embedded double quotation marks as expected.

bugs.title: APM Portal Access becomes unresponsive.
bugs.symptoms: APM Portal Access becomes unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: Using APM Portal Access with application cookies that require more than 32 KB of storage.
bugs.impact: APM Portal Access becomes unresponsive and rewrite plugins consume 100% of the CPU.
bugs.fix: Now, when the 32 KB cookie storage limit is reached, the oldest application cookie is discarded, allowing the application to continue processing new data.

bugs.title: The Update Check operation reports a different version of IP geolocation database than what is installed.
bugs.symptoms: The Update Check operation reports a different version of the IP geolocation database than what is installed.
bugs.conditions: When Update Check runs, either automatically or manually, by pressing Update Now.
bugs.impact: Update Check reports the wrong version of the IP geolocation database, which results in the Update Check operation continually reporting IP geolocation database available as an update.
bugs.fix: The Update Check operation now reports the correct (installed) version of the IP geolocation database.

bugs.title: TMSH crypto commands do not work with the TMSH batch mode
bugs.symptoms: tmsh crypto commands will fail when executed in tmsh batch mode.
bugs.conditions: tmsh batch mode and 'sys crypto' commands.
bugs.impact: tmsh crypto commands will fail when executed in tmsh batch mode.
bugs.workaround: Run the tmsh 'sys crypto' commands outside of a 'cli transaction' i.e. not in batch mode.

bugs.title: Receiving several ConfigSync requests in a short period of time may cause the mcpd process to restart and produce a core file
bugs.symptoms: Receiving several configuration synchronization (ConfigSync) requests, in a short period of time, may cause the mcpd process to exhaust memory resources, restart, and produce a core file. Note: The Automatic Sync feature can exacerbate this issue. The Automatic Sync feature is disabled by default. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: Performing a ConfigSync operation causes the BIG-IP system to experience a brief service interruption while the mcpd process restarts. If configured as part of a high availability (HA) group, the BIG-IP system fails over. The BIG-IP system generates an mcpd core file.
bugs.conditions: Receiving several configuration synchronization (ConfigSync) requests with a short interval.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may experience a brief service interruption while the mcpd process restarts.
bugs.fix: Sync of a folder delete or create now will send an incremental sync if possible. Sync of a folder modify that changes the device group still will trigger a full load; this is necessary and does not indicate an issue.

bugs.title: Multi-blade systems can experience active/standby flapping after both units rebooted
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting multi-bladed BIG-IP systems configured for failover, one or more of the systems has some of its blades flap from active to standby.
bugs.conditions: Rebooting systems fairly close in time from one another (about a minute apart). Traffic group must reference an HA group.
bugs.impact: Invalid redundant status.
bugs.workaround: Modify the traffic group to no longer reference an HA group: tmsh modify cm traffic-group traffic-group-1 ha-group none.
bugs.fix: Multi-blade systems no longer experience active/standby flapping after both units are rebooted, so the following MCPD error message no longer occur at the secondary blades: err mcpd[6528]: 010717b5:3: HA group (HA) cannot be removed. It is used by traffic group (/Common/traffic-group-1 ).

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS configuration load failure from invalid bigip_gtm.conf file.
bugs.symptoms: Config reload fails when renewing the license or performing a new install based on the current config. This appears to be the result of a invalid bigip_gtm.conf which is used to load the config rather than the mcpdb.bin.
bugs.conditions: If any virtual servers are configured with a dependency list that includes other virtual servers from the same BIG-IP system, BIG-IP DNS creates an invalid bigip_gtm.conf file.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP DNS config will fail to load when triggered to load from config file
bugs.fix: Depends-on block is populated correctly with the virtual server info and no error was thrown when reloading BIG-IP DNS config.

bugs.title: Config fails to load after upgrade to 11.5.1 when iApp requires PSM module.
bugs.symptoms: Protocol Security Module (PSM) provisioning was removed in 11.5.0. Upgrading a config fails to load after upgrade to 11.5.1 when an iApp requires PSM module.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to 11.5.1 when an iApp requires PSM module.
bugs.impact: The upgrade fails as the configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Remove PSM from the list of enabled modules from affected iApp templates before upgrading.

bugs.title: Initial sync fails for upgraded pair (11.5.x to 11.6)
bugs.symptoms: Config sync fails immediately after upgrade from 11.5.x to 11.6.
bugs.conditions: Config sync fails immediately after upgrade from 11.5.x to 11.6.
bugs.impact: Configurations may not sync if the devices were upgraded from 11.5 to 11.6.
bugs.workaround: No consistent workaround.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue where config sync failed on 11.5.x devices after upgrading to 11.6.

bugs.title: Using non-standard lettercasing for header name results in misleading error during commit of transaction
bugs.symptoms: As part of adding commands to a transaction for iControl REST call, the header name to be used is "X-F5-REST-Coordination-Id." However, if you mix the letter casing to something else, such as: "x-f5-rest-coordination-id" then when you commit this transaction you will get this misleading error: "there is no command to commit in the transaction." Your command and transaction will succeed, but the error implies it did not.
bugs.conditions: Using the non-standard letter casing for that header name during the iControl REST call to add commands to a transaction.
bugs.impact: It looks like the transaction failed, when in fact, it may have succeeded.
bugs.workaround: Use the proper letter casing for that header name as shown above.
bugs.fix: Use the proper letter casing for that header name as shown above.

bugs.title: Inconsistent SafeNet key deletion in BIG-IP and Safenet HSM
bugs.symptoms: Under some conditions, when deleting a SafeNet key, the key is deleted from HSM but not from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens when the BIG-IP system satisfies the following conditions: 1. A SafeNet-generated key is in use by a clientSSL profile. 2. Safenet HSM is installed.
bugs.impact: If this clientSSL profile is currently used by a virtual server, then SSL connection to this virtual server fails since the key is not in HSM.
bugs.workaround: 1. Remove the key/cert from the clientSSL profile, so that they become 'not in use'. 2. Delete the not-in-use key/cert from the BIG-IP system. 2. Configure another key/cert in the clientSSL profile.
bugs.fix: In this release, when deleting a SafeNet key, the key is deleted from HSM as well as from the BIG-IP system

bugs.title: Crash when using FIX tag maps and a FIX message arrives without a SenderCompID.
bugs.symptoms: Crash when using FIX tag maps and a FIX message arrives without a SenderCompID.
bugs.conditions: LTM virtuals using the fix-map tcp profile.
bugs.impact: tmm can crash
bugs.fix: Fix crash when no SenderCompID is supplied

bugs.title: MPTCP Flows may hang whan an MTU mismatch occurs on the network.
bugs.symptoms: System did not correctly handle the ICMP message reporting an MTU mismatch for MPTCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP traffic MTU mismatch.
bugs.impact: Degraded operation, some flows might hang.
bugs.fix: System correctly handles ICMP notification for MPTCP traffic.

bugs.title: SNAT translation traffic group inheritance does not sync across devices
bugs.symptoms: When a snat-translation object is created, and its inherited-traffic-group property is set, this property does not sync to other devices.
bugs.conditions: This is relevant for any setup with multiple devices in a CMI failover device group.
bugs.impact: The inherited-traffic-group property must be manually maintained on all devices.
bugs.workaround: Enable the 'full sync' option instead of using incremental sync.
bugs.fix: SNAT translation traffic group inheritance now syncs across devices using incremental sync.

bugs.title: Monpd errors appear when AVR loads data to MySQL
bugs.symptoms: An error of the form "Too many partitions (4) defined for DB table..." will appear in both /var/log/ltm and /var/log/avr/monpd.log
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when traffic is running and AVR is being used by any of the following provisioned modules: AVR, ASM, PEM, AFM, or SWG.
bugs.impact: No actual impact on data accuracy or performance - only errors in /var/log/ltm and /var/log/avr/monpd.log
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Error messages such as "Too many partitions (4) defined for DB table..." no longer appear in the log files.

bugs.title: Portal access: external links in SVG tags are not rewitten
bugs.symptoms: If HTML page contains SVG tag with external reference inside, this reference is not rewritten.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with SVG tag and external reference inside this tag, for example: <html><body><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <image x="20" y="20" width="300" height="80" xlink:href="http://example.com/logo.gif" /> </svg></body></html>
bugs.impact: SVG external references may not be loaded correctly
bugs.workaround: It is possible to prepare iRule to replace URL in SVG external references.

bugs.title: audit_forwarded started error message
bugs.symptoms: During system start you see the following error message in /var/log/ltm: bigip01 err audit_forwarder: audit_forwarder started"
bugs.conditions: This message can be displayed during either system start or system restart.
bugs.impact: None. This notice should be logged at the info log level, not error level.
bugs.fix: The audit forwarder starting message is now displayed at the info level.

bugs.title: Large big3d memory footprint.
bugs.symptoms: The big3d process might take up a large amount of memory.
bugs.conditions: Using GTM in various configurations.
bugs.impact: Large big3d memory footprint. This is a configuration- and usage-dependent issue.
bugs.fix: Reduced big3d memory footprint.

bugs.title: A SecureVault rekey operation may fail if configuration contains a blank password protected by SecureVault
bugs.symptoms: If the configuration includes encrypted items (for example, an LDAP bind password) that are empty strings, a SecureVault rekey operation fails.
bugs.conditions: Empty string as encrypted configuration item. This might occur when using the tmsh command 'modify /sys crypto master-key, or during the introduction of a device into a Trust Domain.
bugs.impact: The rekey operation fails, and the system posts an error similar to the following: with this error: 01071029:5: master_decrypt failed during rekey. This might result in a ConfigSync failure.
bugs.workaround: Do not use empty strings as passwords. Alternately, remove the problematic configuration object (which may require changing system authentication to a different source), perform the rekey operation, and then recreate the configuration.

bugs.title: TMM segfault in mpctp_switch_conns
bugs.symptoms: TMM segfault in mpctp_switch_conns
bugs.conditions: This can occur is mptcp is configured and there is an invalid tcp session.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts
bugs.workaround: Do not configure mptcp in the tcp profile.

bugs.title: JavaScript index expressions with a comma are not properly rewritten
bugs.symptoms: If there are expressions like a[b,c] within JavaScript code, these expressions will return a[b] instead of a[c] after rewriting with Portal Access. This could lead to JavaScript exceptions, or silent flaws in logic of application.
bugs.impact: This issue leads to exceptions or broken logic of customer's backend application.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: JavaScript index expressions with list of values are now correctly rewritten by Portal Access.

bugs.title: Management client-ssl profile does not support multiple key/cert pair.
bugs.symptoms: Management SSL client-ssl profile does not support multiple key/cert pair.
bugs.conditions: Management client-ssl profile.
bugs.impact: It supports only one key/cert pair which is stored in profile key/cert/chain/passphrase. cert-key-chain in client-ssl profile is not a valid selection. Selecting cert/key pair from cert-key-chain could cause problem.
bugs.fix: Management SSL client-ssl profile should ignore cet-key-chain structures and get the unique cert/key pair from profile key/cert/chain/passphrase.

bugs.title: Address list summary page does not display the description for individual address list entries.
bugs.symptoms: Description for an address list entry is not displayed in the address list summary page
bugs.conditions: 'Description' for address list entry (created from tmsh) is not displayed in the address list summary page (in the GUI).
bugs.impact: The value for 'description' is not seen in the GUI
bugs.workaround: View the description in tmsh.
bugs.fix: Address list summary page displays the description for individual address list entries.

bugs.title: ConfigSync might fail with modified system-supplied profiles
bugs.symptoms: A config sync operation might fail with a parent-profile-not-found error message, despite the fact that the parent profile is present in the running configuration of both systems.
bugs.conditions: On the sync target (the system receiving the configuration, and the one that reports a sync failure), a system-supplied profile (e.g. /Common/serverssl) has been modified, and is present in /config/bigip.conf.
bugs.impact: An administrator is unable to synchronize system configurations. The system might post messages similar to the following example: '01020036:3: The requested parent profile (/Common/serverssl) was not found.'
bugs.workaround: One of the following: 1. Manually replicate the changes on the base profile to the system that is sourcing the config sync. 2. Undo the changes to the base profile on the system that is receiving the config sync (to do so, save the configuration, manually remove the base profile from /config/bigip.conf, and then re-load the configuration), and then perform a force sync operation. 3. Perform a sync in the other direction. Important: Performing a sync in this direction overrides any unsync'd changes on the other system.

bugs.title: TMM aborted by SOD due to heartbeat failure when trying to load huge firewall policies.
bugs.symptoms: TMM gets terminated by SOD daemon due to heartbeat failure.
bugs.conditions: This might occur intermittently when trying to load huge firewall policies.
bugs.impact: This might (intermittently) trigger TMM abort by DOS due to heartbeat failure.
bugs.workaround: Disable TMM heartbeat.
bugs.fix: TMM is no longer terminated by SOD due to heartbeat failure (when trying to load huge firewall policies).

bugs.title: User Modification Denied error on initial bootup
bugs.symptoms: Upon reviewing the log file in /var/log/ltm, you might see the following error: err mcpd[8105]: 01070820:3: User Modification Denied: User (root) may not change the role of system account (admin)
bugs.conditions: This happens only during the first reboot after a software install. If the error is seen again, the audit log should be checked. This may also happen when creating or deleting a user with the Administrator role.
bugs.impact: There is no known impact at this time.

bugs.title: HTTP OneConnect on wildcard non-translating virtual server does not reuse connections
bugs.symptoms: Server-side flows are not reused. In this version of the software, the system disables reuse of server-side flows if the server-side flow is established without use of a pool.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using HTTP OneConnect on wildcard non-translating virtual servers.
bugs.impact: This causes virtual servers that do not use pools to create a new server-side connection for every HTTP request, which results in excessive back-end connection traffic.
bugs.workaround: For all virtual servers except for APM virtual servers, you can use the following iRule to reuse connections: when HTTP_REQUEST_RELEASE { if {[HTTP::request_num] == 0} { ONECONNECT::reuse enable } }

bugs.title: When persistence is overriden from cookie to some other persistence method, the cookie should not be sent.
bugs.symptoms: If cookie persistence is configured, then persistence cookies will be sent to the client. However, if the persistence profile is overridden by an iRule "persist" command, that cookie should not be sent.
bugs.conditions: 1) A cookie persistence profile is used, and it is overridden to some other persistence method via an iRule. 2) Passive cookie persistence is used, the "always send" option is off, and cookie encryption is enabled.
bugs.impact: 1) Extra persistence cookies may be included in a response even if they are not required by the current persistence method. 2) Passive cookies may not be encrypted in some situations.
bugs.workaround: 1) The extra cookie can be removed by an iRule. 2) Turn the "always send" option on if using passive persistence cookies.
bugs.fix: 1) Persistence cookies will not be inserted if the persistence method is changed from cookie persistence to some other persistence method. 2) Passive persistence cookies will be encrypted even if the "always send" option is off.

bugs.title: TMM might panic when processing SIP messages due to invalid route domain
bugs.symptoms: TMM might panic when processing SIP messages due to invalid route domain.
bugs.conditions: SIP Requests are being processed with a via header that does not contain an 'rport' attribute. SIP profile attached to the virtual server has 'dialog aware' enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM panics with following string: 'domain != RT_DOMAIN_NONE'.
bugs.workaround: Disable the 'dialog aware' option on the SIP profile, or configure SIP OneConnect.
bugs.fix: TMM sets a known route domain when processing SIP Requests to prevent panics caused by an invalid route domain.

bugs.title: When evaluation/demonstration features expire, features enabled by both evaluation and perpetual licenses also expire
bugs.symptoms: Evaluation features cause perpetual features to expire when the evaluation license expires.
bugs.conditions: -- Perpetual license with an evaluation/demonstration add-on feature. -- The add-on license expires or is expired.
bugs.impact: When an evaluation/demonstration add-on license expires, features included in both the evaluation add-on as well as the regular, perpetual license stop working. This behavior is covered in F5 article K4679: BIG-IP evaluation and demonstration licenses do expire :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K4679.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, activate the license from the command line: When reactivating an existing license, and deactivating an expired evaluation license key, specify the base registration key and add-on (if any), and use the -i option for the expired evaluation license key in the get_dossier command. For example, if the expired evaluation license key is ABCDEFG-ZZZZZZZ, use the following command: get_dossier -b ABCDE-ABCDE-ABCDE-ABCDE-ABCDEFG -a ABCDEFG-ABCDEFG -i ABCDEFG-ZZZZZZZ You can find these steps detailed in K2595: Activating and installing a license file from the command line :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K2595. This part in particular is required to work around this issue

bugs.title: ConfigSync may fail if HA pair has dissimilar cert-key-chain sub-object names within an SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: MCPD may generate one of the following validation errors as a result of a ConfigSync, or a config load, or attaching an SSL profile to a virtual server, or modifying a virtual server: 0107149e:3: Virtual server /Common/name-of-virtual-server has more than one clientssl/serverssl profile with same server name. 010717e1:3: Client SSL profile cannot contain more than one set of same certificate/key type.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when HA pairs have dissimilar cert-key-chain names within an SSL profile, and the changes were synchronized to the peer device. Either the ConfigSync will fail (if the SSL profile was attached to a virtual server), or the ConfigSync will succeed, but on the receiving device, the SSL profile will have two cert-key-chain objects. This happens given the following conditions: - Systems are performing a full (not incremental) sync - SSL profile is attached to a virtual server - cert-key-chain sub-object has differing names on the two devices
bugs.impact: Depending on the manifestation of this issue one of the following can happen: - administrator may be prevented from performing further configuration operations - administrator may be prevented from synchronizing the configuration - the configuration may not load
bugs.workaround: Find the client-ssl profile name for the virtual server that fails to load. List and compare the cert-key-chain names of the client-ssl profile on the devices in the HA configuration. Choose the correct cert-key-chain name and ensure the cert-key-chain name is the same on all devices. Synchronize the configuration.
bugs.fix: The ConfigSync operation completes successfully if HA pair has dissimilar cert-key-chain sub-object names within an SSL profile.

bugs.title: System outage can occur with MPTCP traffic.
bugs.symptoms: System outage can occur when a pool member is unreachable for MPTCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP traffic. Serverside unreachable.
bugs.impact: System outage can occur.
bugs.fix: System correctly handles ICMP unreachable for MPTCP traffic.

bugs.title: Web Scraping Mitigation: Display of request status when configuration includes an ASM iRule
bugs.symptoms: A wrong display of the request status (as a blocked request) for requests that were only alarmed.
bugs.conditions: Web scraping in alarm mode, ASM iRules in place.
bugs.impact: A wrong display of the request status as if it is a blocked request when it was alarmed request.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When web scraping mitigation configuration mode is set to Alarm (log) and there is an ASM iRule, the iRule no longer displays requests as being blocked when they are actually logged and not blocked.

bugs.title: Mac Edge client on Mac mini receives settings for iOS Edge Client
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac on Mac mini receives settings for iOS Edge Client. Edge Client behavior might be different than expected if Mac Edge Client settings are different from iOS Edge Client settings.
bugs.conditions: Mac mini, iOS Edge and Mac Edge Client setting in connectivity profile on BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Different than expected behavior of Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.fix: Edge Client for Mac on Mac mini now uses the settings for the Mac Edge Client in the connectivity profile on BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Managing apd connection from tmm
bugs.symptoms: apd and logd consumes a large percentageof CPU.
bugs.conditions: APM Session receives TCPRST or no response when under heavy connection request load from tmm for authentication, which leaves unprocessed requests in the queue.
bugs.impact: APD (authentication server) become unresponsive, which causes all new user sessions to fail.
bugs.fix: The system now handles a large number of connection requests for authentication using a throttling mechanism to manage the requests.

bugs.title: APM New Session performance graph displays incorrect timed out/error value
bugs.symptoms: The timed out/error value shown in the APM New Session performance graph is supposed to show only the count for sessions that were terminated due to inactivity or error while in the access policy evaluation state. However, it also includes sessions that were timed out after they passed access policy evaluation. As a result, the timed out/error value is larger than the actual value.
bugs.conditions: If sessions are timed out in established state, the stats will show up in the New Session graph.

bugs.title: The upgrade process can discard valid HTTP Class URLs
bugs.symptoms: A customer trying to upgrade from a version 11.x (where x < 4) to a 11.5.x may get this error: ERROR: The httpclass profile(s) for policy <HTTP Class profile name> did not roll forward: policy rule(s) created from <HTTP Class profile name> do not contain a proper URL. See Solution SOL14409. This occurs even though the HTTP Class object is compliant with the syntax described in SOL14409 and SOL15206.
bugs.conditions: - Version is < 11.4.0 and >= 11.0.0 - There are httpclass profiles in the customer's bigip.conf - url-rewrite value is different than none, but valid - The customer tries to upgrade to 11.5.x
bugs.impact: Potential issues when upgrading from 11.x (where x < 4) to 11.5.x that aren't described in SOL14409 and SOL15206.
bugs.workaround: - Re-package the original UCS modifying bigip.conf file so that url-rewrite value goes in quotes (url-rewrite "/my/new/uri/") - Avoid the validations described in SOL15206: load the original UCS into a 11.4.x box, then create a new UCS from there and load it into the desired 11.5.x.

bugs.title: In Configuration Utility, unable to view or edit objects in Local Traffic :: iRules :: Data Group List
bugs.symptoms: Navigate to Local Traffic :: iRules :: Data Group List and click on any existing objects. User will see a No Access error, instead of the Data Group object.
bugs.conditions: Data Group objects exist.
bugs.impact: User will be unable to view or edit Data Group objects in the Configuration Utility.
bugs.workaround: View and edit objects in tmsh.

bugs.title: Virtual with FastL4 with loose initiation and close enabled might result in TMM core
bugs.symptoms: Virtual with FastL4, loose initiation and loose close enabled might result in TMM core.
bugs.conditions: The problem can occur when the following conditions are met: - Virtual server with FastL4 profile. - FastL4 profile has loose initiation and loose close enabled. - TCP FIN is received that is not associated with an existing connection.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable loose initiation and loose close on FastL4 profile
bugs.fix: FastL4 component now validates existence of connection peer upon reception of TCP FIN.

bugs.title: Setting a remote syslog destination to a localhost address results in recursive log messages.
bugs.symptoms: Setting a remote syslog destination to a localhost address results in recursive log messages.
bugs.conditions: Using 127.0.0.1 or a hostname resolving to it as a host for syslog's remote-server.
bugs.impact: Using a localhost address as a remote syslog destination results in continual log entries until the BIG-IP system runs out of disk space.
bugs.workaround: Use a non-local remote host for syslog's remote-server.

bugs.title: /config/.../policy_sync_d Directory Is 100% Full
bugs.symptoms: After a policy sync operation, the Policy Sync history file objects remain within the /config/.../policy_sync_d directory.
bugs.conditions: This issue is further exacerbated when customization an/or sandbox (hosted content) files are associated with the profiles being synced.
bugs.impact: Over time the saved number and size of the Policy Sync history files can grow to fill all available space.
bugs.workaround: The psync-history objects and related data files can be manually deleted by running the following commands from within tmsh context: `cd /Common/PolicySyncHistory` `delete apm policy psync-history all` `save sys config partitions all` Please note that the above steps will remove all psync-history and related file objects from your local device. Which means, you will no longer have entries within the history tab of your Policy Sync page of the Admin GUI.
bugs.fix: After a policy sync operation, the Policy Sync history file objects no longer remain within the /config/.../policy_sync_d directory as expected.

bugs.title: Machine Certificate checker now correctly works in Internet Explorer 11
bugs.symptoms: Machine Certificate checker hangs in Internet Explorer 11.x if you are not using compatibility mode.
bugs.conditions: Machine certificate used in Internet Explorer version 11.x with compatibility mode turned off.
bugs.impact: Cannot pass APM policy
bugs.workaround: Add APM hostname to compatibility view list.
bugs.fix: Machine Certificate checker now works correctly in Internet Explorer 11.

bugs.title: HTML5 WebSocket API is not supported in Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: WebSocket API is currently not supported in Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Applications won't be able to establish WebSocket connection through Portal Access
bugs.workaround: It's possible to provide an iRule workaround for specific application and deployment on request.

bugs.title: The HTTP explicit proxy may leak memory in some cases
bugs.symptoms: When the HTTP explicit proxy generates error pages it may leak memory in some cases.
bugs.conditions: The HTTP explicit proxy is used, and an error occurs that triggers an error page to be generated.
bugs.impact: The TMM's available memory will slowly decrease over time.
bugs.workaround: Using a smaller error page may make the memory leak less likely.
bugs.fix: The HTTP Explicit proxy feature will no longer leak memory when error pages are generated.

bugs.title: tmm restart issue when number of cores in license differs from number of system CPUs.
bugs.symptoms: tmm continuous restart issue when number of cores specified in the in license differs from the number of CPUs on the system.
bugs.conditions: The value of perf_VE_cores in /config/bigip.license is different from the number of CPUs on virtual machine.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Manually set the value of DB variable provision.tmmcount to the value of perf_VE_cores specified in the license. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db provision.tmmcount _value_.

bugs.title: Tcpdump captures nothing when filtered by VLAN tag
bugs.symptoms: There is no output generated for tcpdump when filtered by the VLAN tag. Without the filter, output can be seen.
bugs.conditions: -- Use guest VLAN tagging. -- Tcpdump with the VLAN tag filter.
bugs.impact: No output for tcpdump, which makes troubleshooting difficult.
bugs.workaround: Use tcpdump without the VLAN tag filter and then filter using standard Linux tools (e.g., grep).

bugs.title: Some IPv6 client connections get RST when connecting to APM virtual
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 clients connecting to APM virtual server that renders some page, e.g., logon page, webtop, or message box, might get connection resets.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 client has the last 4 bytes of the IP address set to some special-purpose address, e.g., multicast address.
bugs.impact: Client connection is reset.
bugs.workaround: Change the last 4 bytes of the client IPv6 address to avoid the IPv4 special-address range.
bugs.fix: All IPv6 clients can now connect through APM virtual server, regardless of the values of the last 4 bytes of the address.

bugs.title: Priority groups may result in traffic being load balanced to a single pool member.
bugs.symptoms: Priority groups may result in traffic being load balanced to a single pool member.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Multiple priority groups. -- Slow ramp feature enabled (TCP profile). -- Active priority group goes offline. -- Member in the newly active group goes offline then online (triggering slow ramp feature).
bugs.impact: Traffic is improperly load balanced.
bugs.workaround: Disable slow ramp feature in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system calculates the correct number of members in the active priority group when the slow ramp feature is triggered.

bugs.title: Portal Access rewrite daemon may crash while processing some Flash files
bugs.symptoms: high load of the box, rewrite core files.
