bugs.conditions: This happens in a very rare situation when flash files were produced with specification violations. Specifically, list of objects within tag DefineSprite is not terminated with tag End while it always should be terminated this way.
bugs.impact: Portal Access is temporarily unavailable. Core file for 'rewrite' process is generated.
bugs.fix: Portal Access no longer crashes when rewriting some incorrect Adobe Flash files.

bugs.title: TMM crash after traffic stress with rapid changes to Traffic capturing profiles
bugs.symptoms: Rare condition of TMM crash due to traffic stress with rapid changes made to Traffic capturing profiles.
bugs.conditions: 1. Traffic capturing feature is on, under heavy traffic. 2. Modifications are being made to traffic capturing configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Turn off traffic capturing feature, or minimize making changes to the Traffic capturing profile while under heavy load.
bugs.fix: A rare condition was fixed where TMM crashed due to traffic stress with rapid changes made to Traffic capturing profiles.

bugs.title: ACCESS logs non-fatal snapshot errors
bugs.symptoms: Logs like this will appear in /var/log/apm: Jun 25 11:45:24 JASSL302 err tmm[9517]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_ARG. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access_snapshot.c, Function: access_config_snapshot_list_delete, Line: 552 Jun 25 11:45:24 JASSL302 err tmm[9517]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_ARG. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access_snapshot.c, Function: access_config_snapshot_final_callback, Line: 233 Jun 25 11:45:24 JASSL302 err tmm[9517]: 01490537:3: tmm.session.51e51c88bb7a9_13oooooooooooooooo: Access failed to delete configuration snapshot. Err: Illegal argument.
bugs.conditions: These errors can occur during normal operating conditions due to configuration changes, HA failovers, or APD restarts. The error should be treated as non-fatal.
bugs.impact: Logging non-fatal error messages is confusing to administrators
bugs.fix: These errors are now logged at NOTICE level.

bugs.title: Incorrect and benign log message of bandwidth utilization exceeded when licensed with rate limit in VE
bugs.symptoms: When Virtual Edition (VE) is licensed with limited throughput, tmm checks and enforces rate limits. However, due to the nature of clustering in data plane, individual tmm processes performs the check independently (that is, divided by the number of tmms on the system). Thus, the check result is not accurate from global rate perspective. In this case, the system log messages that indicates data rate exceeds licensed rate.
bugs.conditions: Multiple tmm in VE and licensed with limited date rate, when only some of the tmms are processing traffic.
bugs.impact: Message indicating data rate exceeds licensed rate.
bugs.fix: Incorrect and benign log message of bandwidth utilization exceeded when licensed with rate limit in Virtual Edition no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Excessive IP fragmentation on tmm_bp vlan causes ftp data loss with vlan name >= 16 characters long
bugs.symptoms: When a vlan name is >= 16 characters including the /Common/ folder name prefix, the internal packet size will exceed the configured MTU size of 1582 on the MPI channel. This causes excessive IP fragmentation on tmm_bp vlan and high cpu usage. In some cases it can also cause packet loss.
bugs.conditions: Vlan names (16 characters or longer) are being used. This length also counts the name of the partition.
bugs.impact: This can cause excessive IP fragmentation on tmm_bp vlan and high cpu usage. In some cases it would also cause packet loss.
bugs.workaround: Use shorter vlan names.
bugs.fix: A new db variable vlan.backplane.mtu has been added to configure tmm_bp vlan mtu size, and the new default backplane MTU is set to to 1640.
bugs.behavior: A new db variable vlan.backplane.mtu has been added to configure tmm_bp vlan mtu size, and the new default backplane MTU is set to to 1640.

bugs.title: snmpd cores or crashes with no logging when restarted by sod
bugs.symptoms: Prior to sod restarting snmpd following a heartbeat timeout, there are often no snmpd warning/error logs leading up to the restart condition that might indicate root-cause.
bugs.conditions: snmpd can be blocked waiting for mcpd responses to its database queries. This is typically experienced when CPU utilization is very high.
bugs.impact: sod continues restarting snmpd (and generating a core dump) as long as the blocking conditions continue for longer than the configured snmpd heartbeat interval. During this time, external MIB queries might timeout/fail.
bugs.workaround: Address CPU utilization issues.
bugs.fix: The snmpd daemon now periodically logs warning messages regarding slow query responses from mcpd. snmpd also attempts to maintain heart-beat communication with sod under these conditions.

bugs.title: The Enforcer should exclude session awareness violations when counting illegal requests.
bugs.symptoms: Getting False positive by blocking requests.
bugs.conditions: Session Awareness is enabled.
bugs.impact: Release session status from being blocked/logged can be renewed if illegal traffic runs at the same time even with 'Disallowed access...' violation only
bugs.fix: The Enforcer now excludes session awareness violations when counting illegal requests for session awareness actions. Previously, these violations were counted and therefore prematurely caused the session status to be "Blocked".

bugs.title: Creating static ARP entry with unreachable IP address causes BIG-IP to be unreachable after reboot
bugs.symptoms: Saved configuration may not load if static ARP entries are configured that do not match a self IP subnet.
bugs.conditions: Saved config with static ARP whose IP falls outside of any self IP subnet.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the config fails to load.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue remove the static ARP entry from saved config by manually editing config file.
bugs.fix: Static ARP entries that fall outside of configured self IP addresses can now be loaded. However, this invalid configuration is now avoided by requiring static ARP entries in a self IP subnet to be removed before a self IP can be removed.

bugs.title: iRule data-groups are not checked for existence
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule specifies a data-group that is not in Common, or that does not have an explicit path to it, it does not result in an error when the iRule is saved, or during runtime.
bugs.conditions: User saves an iRule with a data-group not in Common or with an explicit path to it.
bugs.impact: When such an iRule is saved, it can cause all traffic to fail.

bugs.title: Memory corruption in f5::rest::CRestServer::g_portToServerMap
bugs.symptoms: Abort during guestagentd static deinitialization
bugs.conditions: Daemon and threads are shutdown
bugs.impact: Crash in guestagentd and CRestServer
bugs.fix: Fix crash on shutdown in guestagentd and CRestServer

bugs.title: Policy Sync cause target vCMP guest secondary slots to reboot when guest(s) is deployed on multiple slots.
bugs.symptoms: The guests (target) from the device group restarts after policy sync successfully completed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs only when the target guests are created across the slots by sharing CPU, disk etc in vCMP.
bugs.impact: The guests are usable during restart.
bugs.workaround: The guests should be created in a single slot and not across slots.

bugs.title: Using native View clients, cannot launch desktops and applications from multiple VMware back-ends
bugs.symptoms: If APM is configured to protect multiple VMware resources (VCS servers), you can launch desktops and applications only from the first resource. Attempts to launch desktop or applications from other resources result in error.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is configured to protect multiple VMware resources (VCS servers). -- You attempt to launch a desktop or application using the native VMware client.
bugs.impact: Cannot access desktops and applications from multiple VMware back-ends.
bugs.workaround: Use HTML5 client instead.
bugs.fix: APM now supports launching of desktops and applications from multiple View resources using native View clients. Note: Linux and Mac are not supported, as VMware has yet to add support for mid-parameter on Linux and Mac native clients.

bugs.title: Memory leak in Export Policy operation
bugs.symptoms: Performing the Export Policy operation creates a memory leak.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned. A long-lived process exports many security policies without being restarted.
bugs.impact: If a long-lived process exports many security policies, the device can run out of memory.
bugs.workaround: Restart the long-lived process that exports many security policies with the following command: # pkill -f asm_config_server_rpc_handler.pl
bugs.fix: A standard Perl package 'YAML::LibYAML' was upgraded to a newer version in order to prevent a memory leak that sometimes occurred after exporting a security policy.

bugs.title: Standby responds to traceroute on mirror enabled forwarding virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Standby responds with ICMP time exceeded message on mirror enabled forwarding virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: HA configuration, IP forwarding virtual server, mirroring enabled, non-floating self IP address, simultaneous flood of ICMP packet to both active and standby systems.
bugs.impact: Standby responds with ICMP time-exceeded message.
bugs.workaround: Disable mirroring in forwarding virtual server, or remove non-floating self IP address on standby system.

bugs.title: If the configuration contains a filename with the $ character, then saving the UCS fails.
bugs.symptoms: If the configuration contains a filename or username with the $ character, then saving the UCS fails. Examples of filenames include cm cert cache-path and cm key cache-path. tmsh save sys ucs <ucs-id> fails for such configuration. The error displayed appears similar to the following.: Fatal: executing: md5sum /var/tmp/filestore_temp/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/:Common:?><.crt_53783_1 Operation aborted. /var/tmp/configsync.spec: Error creating package.
bugs.conditions: Filenames or username in configuration contain $ character. For example, cm cert cache-path or cm key cache-path.
bugs.impact: Saving UCS fails.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the $ character as part of the filenames or usernames in the configuration.

bugs.title: Datastor High Velocity Traffic Pattern Changes
bugs.symptoms: During periods of high velocity in the traffic pattern, datastor will seem to stop caching new objects.
bugs.conditions: A traffic pattern that requires that a given percentage of the working set be displaced in order to move the cache content towards the new working set.
bugs.impact: For web sites that have a fairly static working set, this will reduce the efficacy of their caching by a percentage relative to the write reserve.
bugs.fix: Datastor will now reserve a given percentage of the obj table for the writing of new objects, forcing out objects to maintain this percentage. By default, if a new object cannot be created after a given period of time, datastor will log a message, then restart. Controlling how many contiguous failures before restart, the percentage of the obj table to reserve for writing, and how to restart datastor has been exposed as a new command line parameter. A change has been made to datastor to more readily allow for analyzing its core files.
bugs.behavior: Datastor will now reserve a given percentage of the obj table for the writing of new objects. By default, if a new object cannot be created after a given period of time, datastor will log a message, then restart. Controlling how many contiguous failures, the percentage of the obj table to reserve for writing, and how to restart datastor has been exposed as a new command line parameter.

bugs.title: Malformed cookies can break persistence
bugs.symptoms: Clients sending a malformed cookie (that is, a space character that precedes the persistence cookie) might prevent the parsing of a valid persistence cookie.
bugs.conditions: HTTP request contains malformed cookie value that occurs before the BIG-IP system persistence cookie, For example: Cookie:foo=bar =bar; BIGipServerhttp=60361226.20480.0001
bugs.impact: Persistence is ignored.
bugs.fix: Cookie values containing space character are parsed properly.

bugs.title: Ignoring null values for parameters with different content types
bugs.symptoms: You cannot configure the system to ignore a null value for parameters defined as file upload regardless of the content-type of the parameter in the request. Following the multipart null flow, the system first looks into the content type defined for the parameter in the request itself. If the parameter is defined as textual, the system does not allow a null to appear there, regardless of the policy configuration for that parameter.
bugs.conditions: Parameter is defined in the multipart request as textual and has a null in it.
bugs.impact: A null-in-request violation occurs.
bugs.fix: There is a new internal parameter: 'ignore_null_in_multipart_text'. When the internal parameter is set, the system does not issue a null-in-request violation when a null appears in the request. -- If the parameter is defined as file upload in the security policy, no violation is issued. -- If the parameter is defined as something else, the system issues the violation 'null-in-multipart request'. -- If the parameter is not defined in the security policy, the system issues the violation 'null-in request'. To use the new parameter, run the following commands, in sequence: -- /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ignore_null_in_multipart_text 1 -- bigstart restart asm
bugs.behavior: This release introduces a parameter ignore_null_in_multipart_text. To use it, run the following commands in sequence: -- /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ignore_null_in_multipart_text 1 -- bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: iframe with JavaScript in 'src' attribute not handled correctly in IE11
bugs.symptoms: If an HTML page contains an iframe with JavaScript code in the src attribute, some web applications might not work correctly through portal access in Internet Explorer 11.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include Internet Explorer 11 and iframe with JavaScript in the src attribute: <iframe src="javascript: some code...">
bugs.impact: Some Web applications may work incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: If an HTML page contains an iframe with JavaScript code in the src attribute, it is handled correctly in Internet Explorer 11 through Portal Access.

bugs.title: Fixed issue causing EdgeClient to work improperly behind environment with CaptivePortal.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-Ip Edge Client may display a window that will not close with the content of F5 probe file, however Network Access (NA) works.
bugs.conditions: Special environment with captive portal and proxy.
bugs.impact: User can be confused by window shown.
bugs.fix: Resolved rare condition that caused BIG-IP Edge Client to work improperly when a client uses proxy to connect to the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE instances do not work with an encrypted disk in AWS.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP VE instances cannot use encrypted disks in AWS as encryption-decryption introduces some data corruption in the disk that causes failure in some of the TMOS daemons at run-time.
bugs.conditions: Deploy a BIG-IP VE guests in AWS with an encrypted disk.
bugs.impact: TMM cores at startup, and does not start.
bugs.workaround: Do not use encrypted disks in AWS for BIG-IP VE instances.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP VE instances can now work with an encrypted disk in AWS.

bugs.title: TMM might crash with session-related commands in iRules.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash with session-related commands in iRules.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1) session/table command. 2) client_closed/server_closed iRule.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using client_closed and sever_closed iRules at same time, in a virtual server using session/table command in iRule.

bugs.title: AD/LDAP group name matching should be case-insensitive
bugs.symptoms: AD/LDAP Group Name mapping fails due to the case sensitive matching. It should be case insensitive.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using AD/LDAP Group name mapping.
bugs.impact: Cannot find the intended group.
bugs.fix: AD/LDAP Group Name mapping now is using case-insensitive comparison. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: APM::RBA reset due to a leaked HUDEVT_REQUEST_DONE
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes the APM RBA plugin resets and writes an error to the log that includes this phrase: [0x19fd874:459] Internal error (APM::RBA requested abort (trans end error)). The problem can happen intermittently and usually occurs when multiple tabs are used.
bugs.conditions: Most reproductions involve multiple tabs. End user starts access policy in one tab, and is delivered a login page. Then the end user opens a new tab, and attempts to evaluate the access policy in that tab. The reset comes from the RBA plugin, but this can be reproduced without Kerberos being configured.
bugs.impact: There are intermittent connection resets. Depending on the URL of the second tab, it should have terminated the existing session and started a new one, or it should have rendered a 404 page explaining that the access policy is already running in a different tab.
bugs.fix: Fixed intermittent resets when access policy execution in progress simultaneously from multiple browser tabs.

bugs.title: Ram cache evictions spikes with change of access policy leading to slow webtop rendering
bugs.symptoms: When there is a high load on the system and a user changes an access policy, it can lead to slow rendering of the webtop or the access page.
bugs.conditions: High load with change of access policy around that time.
bugs.impact: Slow webtop/access page rendering.
bugs.fix: Access policy changes are now handled gracefully.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
Access policy in progress with multiple tabs, landing URL set to the tab in which policy is completed.
bugs.symptoms: When URLs from multiple browser tabs start an access policy, the session is created with the landing URL from the first tab that started the session, not with URL that continued and finished creating the access session.
bugs.conditions: Accessing the access policy VIP with different landing URLs before access policy session created. This causes the access policy to run from two different landing URLs.
bugs.impact: This may cause BIG-IP as SAML SP unable to establish a session with IdP. In the case of LTM and APM, the user is always redirected to the URL from first tab after policy execution finishes.
bugs.fix: When URLs from multiple browser tabs start an access policy, the landing URL is set to the URL from the browser that finished the access policy execution.

bugs.title: gtmparse segfaults when loading wideip.conf because of duplicate virtual server names
bugs.symptoms: gtmparse segfaults when loading wideip.conf with duplicate virtual server names, or whose names differ only by spaces.
bugs.conditions: wideip.conf contains duplicate virtual server name definitions, or the virtual server names are unique only because of leading or trailing spaces.
bugs.impact: gtmparse segfaults during a wideip.conf load, causing GTM configuration load to fail.
bugs.workaround: Change virtual server definitions so that there are no duplicate named virtual servers. Note that adding only leading or trailing spaces does not result in a unique virtual server name.
bugs.fix: gtmparse will now throw descriptive errors when encountering duplicate vs names in wideip.conf, for example: ./gtm/wideip.conf:61: "opt_vs_long_def: vs set name vs_1 on vs 10.221.43.28:1545 failed, duplicate name exists" at character '1545' in line: name "vs_1" address 10.221.43.28:1545

bugs.title: Standby node sends a summary LSA for the default route into a stub area with the same metric value as that of Active node.
bugs.symptoms: Active and standby nodes are sending summary LSAs for a default route into a stub area with a metric value of 1. sh ip route displays default route with active and standby nodes as gateways.
bugs.conditions: HA pair is configured to be in an ospf session for a stub area with DR and BDR ospf routers. Area 0 is configured on the HA pair.
bugs.impact: The traffic from DR or BDR nodes in the stub area might be sent to the standby node.
bugs.fix: Standby node sends LSA summary for the default route with a value of 16777215. The OSPF routers in the stub area pick an active node as the gateway for the default route.

bugs.title: TMM cores via assert during EPSV command
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores via assert during EPSV command from clients when The FTP filter rewrites the commands.
bugs.conditions: This rarely encountered issue occurs with the use of line feed (NL) characters in rewritten commands.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use a TCP collect iRule to detect and insert the missing CR.
bugs.fix: FTP filter now accepts NL-only line-ending when rewriting EPSV command.

bugs.title: After deleting external data-group, importing a new or editing existing external data-group does not propagate to TMM
bugs.symptoms: After deleting external data-group, importing a new or existing external data-group does not propagate to TMM. Although the import/modify individually seem to work as expected with no errors displayed in the web interface, the ltm log shows 'update queued', but does not show 'update finished' for the imported/modified datagroup. tmctl ext_class_stat command shows that the deleted data-groups are still in the TMM and existing data-groups stay the same and do not reflect the modification that are made to them via GUI.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when working in an administrative partition other than Common.
bugs.impact: iRules associated with the data-groups do not behave as expected if data-group is deleted and afterwards when data-group modifications are made.
bugs.workaround: There are two options for workarounds: 1. Use short names for the data-group files. It is the long names that are problematic. This is the recommended workaround. 2. Reboot. This causes the mcpd to re-load the data-groups and corrects the situation.
bugs.fix: After deleting external data-group, importing a new or editing existing external data-group now works as expected.

bugs.title: Certain SMTP servers (Windows) do not receive complete email due to missing CRLF header terminator in Emails generated by APM Email agent.
bugs.symptoms: Emails sent by the APM Email Agent when received by certain SMTP servers do not contain subject and body. This is caused by an incomplete header terminating character (LF) used in the Email Agent. CRLF needs to be used at the end of header and as a separator between the header and email body as per RFC 5322.
bugs.conditions: Certain SMTP servers does not accept the LF terminator used in the Emails generated by APM Email agent.
bugs.impact: Email message with Empty body received by certain SMTP server.
bugs.fix: The APM Email agent now generates emails using CRLF at the end of the header and as a separator between the header and the email body, conforming to RFC 5322.

bugs.title: Number of decoding passes configuration
bugs.symptoms: The decoding passes number selected in the "Evasion technique detected" sub-violation setting affects URI and parameter input. However, this setting does not affect the number of decoding passes that the system performs on headers, which is always two.
bugs.conditions: Headers legally may have more than two or more levels of percent decoding
bugs.impact: A false positive violation is issued.
bugs.fix: The number of decoding passes for headers is now taken from the "Evasion technique detected" sub-violation setting.

bugs.title: Infrastructural changes for VMware View 6 support.
APM does not support VMware View application remoting.
bugs.symptoms: VMware View 6 has introduced support for application remoting. This is currently not functional in APM.
bugs.conditions: Deployments where VMWare View 6 has been deployed
bugs.impact: Unable to use View's application remoting features through APM.
bugs.fix: APM now supports VMware View application remoting.

bugs.title: The big3d agent restarts periodically when upgrading the agent on a v11.4.0 or prior system and Common Criteria mode is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: The big3d agent restarts periodically if a v11.4.0 or earlier system with Common Criteria mode enabled is updated with a newer version of the big3d agent.
bugs.conditions: A v11.4.0 or earlier system is updated to run a newer version of the big3d agent and Common Criteria mode is enabled.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is periodic restarting of the big3d agent.
bugs.workaround: Disable Common Criteria mode. Alternatively, restore the prior version of the big3d agent.
bugs.fix: The big3d agent has been modified to run in a mode that eliminates inconsistencies with version 11.4.0 and earlier.

bugs.title: Compression.strategy "SIZE" is not working
bugs.symptoms: The Compression strategy Size is not working as expected. Instead of performing compression in the software, the system use the hardware compression provider to compress HTTP server responses.
bugs.conditions: 1. Compression.strategy "SIZE" 2. Create a http vs with http compress profile
bugs.impact: Compression data is done in hardware rather than software.
bugs.workaround: Set compression.providerbusy to 0
bugs.fix: Compression.strategy "SIZE" would cause software to do the compression.

bugs.title: Add 'Date:' header in email message generated by APM Email agent to comply with RFC 5322.
bugs.symptoms: Emails sent by Email agent, when received by certain SMTP servers, contain an empty body. Email needs to comply with RFC 5322 and should include the Date: header.
bugs.conditions: Certain SMTP servers (new Microsoft hosted email service) send an empty email body when the Date: header is missing from the email message
bugs.impact: Empty email body received.
bugs.fix: Emails sent by the Email agent now include the Date: header in compliance with RFC 5322.

bugs.title: Firstboot early syslog-ng log: /var/run/httpd.pipe does not exist
bugs.symptoms: Early syslog-ng starts up with a config file that references /var/run/httpd.pipe, but it does not exist and syslog-ng logs the following: <date> <host> notice syslog-ng: Error opening file for reading; filename=\'/var/run/httpd.pipe\', error=\'No such file or directory (2)\'
bugs.conditions: First boot of a newly installed system uses a different syslog-ng.conf file, but only on the first boot of a newly installed system. After first boot, the real syslog-ng config file is used. The following log appears in /var/log/boot.log [only in 11.x releases]: Sep 4 10:17:35 localhost notice syslog-ng: Error opening file for reading; filename=\'/var/run/httpd.pipe\', error=\'No such file or directory (2)\'
bugs.impact: There is no actual impact due to this behavior because: (1) syslog-ng is restarted with the correct syslog-ng configuration later in the boot. (2) httpd is not started until later which means there is no actual usage of /var/run/httpd.pipe.
bugs.fix: Prior to starting the early syslog-ng, create the missing file /var/run/httpd.pipe. This also happens later when etc/init.d/syslog-ng is run, but does nothing because the early syslog-ng startup script creates the missing file.

bugs.title: Invalid port blocks are incorrectly counted as active zombie blocks.
bugs.symptoms: After changing the LSN pool configuration while port blocks are active, the port blocks may become invalid because they are no longer be in the pool. An active port block may also become invalid if a translation request occurs during the short period of time between when a block expires and when we process the expiration. These invalid blocks are incorrectly counted in the 'Active zombie port block' count. Since the invalid blocks are not zombie blocks, the count is not decremented when the invalid block expiration is processed.
bugs.conditions: More than one lsn-pool with overlapping address spaces, and virtual servers using these lsn-pools. Zombie timeout must be enabled on the pool and there must be active zombie port blocks.
bugs.impact: The PBA zombie statistics for the lsn-pool may be invalid.
bugs.fix: The system can now invalidate an active port block if a translation request occurs during the short period of time between when a block expires and when we process the expiration, so PBA zombie statistics for the lsn-pool are now measured correctly.

bugs.title: Disabling interface keeps DISABLED state even after enabling
bugs.symptoms: When you disable an interface, the state shows DISABLED. When you enable that interface, the indication for the interface still shows DISABLED.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using both tmsh and the GUI.
bugs.impact: The state of the interface remains DISABLED. However, the interface passes traffic after enabling.
bugs.workaround: You can reboot correct the indicator.
bugs.fix: When you disable an interface, the state shows DISABLED. When you enable that interface, the indication for the interface now shows ENABLED.

bugs.title: VDI plugin crashes when trying to respond to client after client has disconnected
bugs.symptoms: VDI plugin crashes when trying to respond to client after client has disconnected.
bugs.conditions: Client has disconnected, VDI plugin tries to send response to the client.
bugs.impact: VDI plugin crash.
bugs.fix: The VDI plugin does not crash when trying to respond to a client after the client has disconnected.

bugs.title: Static subscriber sessions lost after bigstart restart
bugs.symptoms: Sessions are not created on standby device
bugs.conditions: Bigstart restart active device. Standby will become active and sessions should be created on new active. Before the old active comes online, Bigstart restart the new active.
bugs.impact: Sessions are not created on new active device
bugs.fix: Corrected intermittent HA issues in static subscriber provisioning

bugs.title: Manually adding username/password in ZebOS can cause imi to core
bugs.symptoms: Manually adding a username and encrypted password into ZebOS, either by using imish command line, or by modifying zebos.conf directly, might cause imi to core.
bugs.conditions: Manually modifying the zebos.conf configuration file or adding a non-existing user using imish.
bugs.impact: The user interface to ZebOS, imi, might core. Other functionality should not be affected.
bugs.workaround: Do not add the configuration manually in ZebOS. Use the BIG-IP system facilities for adding/modifying ZebOS users.
bugs.fix: imi no longer cores when attempting to add a user via the imish command line.

bugs.title: Unmangled requests when form.submit with arguments is called in the page
bugs.symptoms: Expressions such as form.submit(something) are not being rewritten by Portal Access. This may cause direct URL or unmangled paths in a request. Such requests fail, and the application could stop working.
bugs.impact: Web applications might send unmangled requests and stop working.
bugs.workaround: An iRule workaround is possible, but it will be unique for each web application.
bugs.fix: Calls of form.submit with arguments are now correctly handled by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: The form.submit() expressions not properly rewritten.

bugs.title: ICAP loses payload at start of request in response to long execution time of iRule
bugs.symptoms: A long-running iRule in ICAP_REQUEST can cause the loss of payload while the iRule is running, resulting in the beginning of the payload being omitted in the request to the ICAP server. (Note that headers are unaffected.)
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- request-adapt or response-adapt is used. -- IVS with ICAP. -- iRule on ICAP_REQUEST event that takes a long time to execute.
bugs.impact: ICAP request to ICAP server can lose the beginning of the payload.
bugs.workaround: When possible, keep iRule duration short by minimizing processing in ICAP_REQUEST and avoiding unnecessary processing, or move the processing elsewhere.
bugs.fix: The complete request payload is now sent to the ICAP server, even in the presence of a long-running iRule in ICAP_REQUEST.

bugs.title: DisableCaptivePortalDetection registry key doesn't work as expected. This is now fixed.
TMM crash in a rare case of flow optimization
bugs.symptoms: During a special case of optimization the peer connflow is released. Subsequent references to connflow result in crash.
bugs.conditions: When PEM hudfilter is optimized & server sends a reset, the code checks a non-existent peer connection.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The code path checks for NULL connflow before attempting to access the data structure.

bugs.title: Analytics scheduled report: "predefinedReportName" and "multiLeveledReport" are mutually exclusive
bugs.symptoms: Analytics scheduled report: You create a non-loadable configuration by changing "predefinedReportName" to "multiLeveledReport", or the reverse for an "analytics application-security scheduled-report".
bugs.conditions: Trying to modify an existing scheduled-report type from predefined to multi-leveled or vice versa caused error message. This was true for both tmsh and REST-API.
bugs.impact: The entire system configuration is not loaded.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit /config/bigip.conf so that "predefinedReportName" and "multiLeveledReport" do not appear together in the same Analytics scheduled report.
bugs.fix: REST API: You can now modify a scheduled-report type, and it will automatically reset the other type's attribute ("predefinedReportName" or "multiLeveledReport").

bugs.title: DHCPv4: When configured in forwarding mode, BIG-IP will support client messages that use either UDP 67 or 68 as the source port.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured in forwarding mode and is connected to a DHCP relay agent, if the relay agent sends DHCP packets to the DHCP server using UDP 68, which is not RFC 2131 compliant, instead of 67, as the source port, the BIG-IP system drops DHCP reply packets from the DHCP server.
bugs.conditions: 1) The BIG-IP system configured in forwarding mode, and sits between a DHCP relay agent and the DHCP server. 2) DHCP relay agent does not comply to RFC by using UDP 68 as the source port.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system drops DHCP server reply packets, which uses UDP 67 as destination port, to the DHCP relay agent.
bugs.fix: Properly handles port translation when non-compliant UDP port 68 is received in packets from the DHCP relay agent.

bugs.title: IP Intelligence report data is not roll-forwarded between installations as it should
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade process does not apply on AVR-DWBL tables, and thus will show no data after the upgrade.
bugs.impact: AVR statistics for DWBL will lose their data.
bugs.fix: DWBL statistics tables are now backed-up to be used in the new version after the upgrade.

bugs.title: Highly fragmented SSL records can result in bad record errors on Nitrox based systems
bugs.symptoms: If a highly fragmented SSL record is decrypted by a system with a Cavium Nitrox card, the system will incorrectly respond with a bad SSL record error.
bugs.conditions: Highly fragmented SSL records and a system with a Cavium Nitrox card.
bugs.impact: Lost SSL connections.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The Nitrox driver was updated to properly handle highly fragmented SSL records.

bugs.title: Potential false positive report of DMA RX lockup failure
bugs.symptoms: Due to mixed traffic in the same ring, heartbeat message might not be received in time and therefore system report DMA RX lockup after a period of time.
bugs.conditions: Mixed traffic stressing into DMA ring 0 and have impacts to heartbeat healthy messages.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and report HSB DMA RX lockup
bugs.fix: The false positive report of RX HSB DMA lockup had been eliminated as long as the ring is moving.

bugs.title: Duration counter for customized Edge Client
bugs.symptoms: The session duration counter does not display properly if Edge Client customization includes logo with size which differs from the size of the default logo.
bugs.conditions: This is visible on the Edge Client if you are displaying a custom logo.
bugs.impact: The impact is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Fixed alignment of connection duration counter for customized BIG-IP Edge Client.

bugs.title: tmsh and tmctl report unusually high counter values
bugs.symptoms: When running the command 'tmctl profile_access_stat', the values displayed for sessions_eval_cur, sessions_active_cur, and/or sessions_estab_cur mignt be unusually high.
bugs.conditions: The issue might appear if the following events happen, in sequence: 1. Some sessions have been established. 2. On a chassis system, a blade restarts. On an appliance system, tmm restarts on the active system, which triggers failover. 3. Some of the existing sessions log out after the chassis or appliance is back online.
bugs.impact: The profile access stat might report inaccurate readings. The system returns results similar to the following: -- sessions_active_cur 18446744073709551615. -- sessions_eval_cur 18446744073709551615.
bugs.fix: tmsh and tmctl now report the expected correct counter values.

bugs.title: Management IP address change interaction with HA heartbeat / failover traffic
bugs.symptoms: When the management IP address changes (either as a result of enabling mgmt-dhcp, or the leased address changing), the system does not synchronize this updated address to other devices in the failover device group / trust domain. (That is, the system does not trigger an update to the device_trust_group.)
bugs.conditions: This occurs on HA configurations.
bugs.impact: This can cause disruption in an HA environment. The sod process discards any HA heartbeat traffic it receives (e.g., traffic over the self IP addresses) that does not contain a 'known' cluster_mgmt_ip.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may report getLopSensorData warnings at boot time or when changing a PSU
bugs.symptoms: When booting a BIG-IP device, or performing a hot swap operation of one of its power supplies, the following kind of log messages may be displayed for a brief time: localhost warning chmand[7059]: 012a0004:4: getLopSensorData: LopDev: sendLopCmd: Lopd status: 1 packet: action=1 obj_id=115 sub_obj=0 slot_id=ff result=24 len=0 crc=6576 payload= (error code:0x24) localhost warning chmand[7059]: 012a0004:4: getLopSensorData: LopDev: sendLopCmd: Lopd status: 1 packet: action=1 obj_id=16f sub_obj=1 slot_id=ff result=1 len=0 crc=acaf payload= (error code:0x1) These messages should not persist, and when a real error occurs it should be accompanied by additional warnings and alerts from the system.
bugs.conditions: The condition occurs when the sensor monitoring process tries to obtain information from power supply model types that are supported but not actually installed. It does this until it discovers the actual model type installed, or that no power supply is installed. The specific conditions under which this is likely to happen are when the BIG-IP software is re-started or a power supply is changed while the system is running.
bugs.impact: A few additional log messages that indicate a warning when there is no legitimate failure.
bugs.workaround: None. This is cosmetic.

bugs.title: The vCMP worker-lite system occasionally stops due to timeouts
bugs.symptoms: The VCMP host side of the worker-lite system has a shorter timeout that the VCMP guest side. This can cause a worker-lite VCMP host to silently stop processing worker-lite requests for a VCMP guest.
bugs.conditions: This issue affects worker-lite based VCMP hosts running any version of VCMP guests that are processing SSL and compression traffic.
bugs.impact: SSL and compression traffic does not pass through VCMP guests running on an affected VCMP host. The system posts error messages in /var/log/ltm, similar to the following: Device error: crypto codec 'device-name' queue is stuck.
bugs.workaround: To resume processing of SSL and compression traffic in a VCMP guest, restart the guest tmm by issuing a 'bigstart restart tmm' from within the guest. Restarting a VCMP guest by setting its state from 'deployed' to 'provisioned' and then back to 'deployed' also resumes processing of SSL and compression traffic.
bugs.fix: Corrected a VCMP timeout issue that might have prevented a VCMP guests from processing SSL and compression traffic.

bugs.title: A SIP virtual server may crash while trying to send a message if the connection is in the process of shutting down
bugs.symptoms: A SIP virtual server may try to access a freed data structure while sending a message if the connection is in the process of shutting down.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: SIP virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM will crash, which will disrupt traffic and can cause a system to go offline / failover while processes restart.
bugs.fix: The crash that can occur if a SIP virtual server is trying to send a message while a connection is shutting down will no longer occur.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: When you force-offline a node, the associated pool member State shows Disabled, but behaves like it is Forced Offline.
bugs.symptoms: When you force-offline a node, the associated pool member State shows 'Disabled (Only persistent or active connections allowed)', not 'Forced Offline (Only active connections allowed)' in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Force-offline a node, and then view the associated pool member State.
bugs.impact: Existing persistence records disappear, and the connection get load balanced to the available pool member, which is forced offline behavior. The state of the pool member is gray and 'disabled', not 'forced offline'.

bugs.title: Customization group template file might cause mcpd to restart
bugs.symptoms: A config sync or tmsh transaction might fail and make mcpd restart if the config sync or tmsh transaction includes a misconfigured object and simultaneously includes a customization group template file. If strict updates are enabled on iApp and Adv Customization is performed that MCPd could crash tpp.
bugs.conditions: The config sync or tmsh transaction includes a misconfigured object and includes a customization group template file.
bugs.impact: The config sync or tmsh transaction fails, and mcpd exits. Note: Avoid configurations that put customization group template file objects through a config sync or tmsh transaction, when that transaction might contain an object configured with an invalid value. This results in a configuration error. Here is one example of the types of messages that may be displayed when this occurs: -- info mcpd[12395]: 01071528:6: Device group '/Common/f5omb' sync inconsistent, Incremental config sync may not be complete on one or more devices in this devicegroup, Sync status may not be consistent until incremental config sync is complete. -- err mcpd[12395]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Cannot apply template as cache path for (customization template file logon.inc customization group /Common/ap_deptSharePt_act_logon_page_ag) cannot be empty. -- err mcpd[12395]: 01070596:3: An unexpected failure has occurred, - apm/validation/APMCustomizationFileObject.cpp, line 1825, exiting... -- info sod[5467]: 010c0009:6: Lost connection to mcpd - reestablishing. -- err zxfrd[12033]: 0153e0f7:3: Lost connection to mcpd.
bugs.fix: This release corrects the configuration error that occurred in the config sync or tmsh transaction whose configuration included a misconfigured object and a customization group template file.

bugs.title: Cipher dhe-rsa-aes256-sha256 is missing from the SSL cipher list
bugs.symptoms: Cipher dhe-rsa-aes256-sha256 is missing from the ssl cipher list.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under all conditions.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the user will be unable to connect with the specified cipher.
bugs.fix: Cipher id 0x006b (dhe-rsa-aes256-sha256) has been added.

bugs.title: eventd sweep timer scheduling on deleted consumer can cause CPU and memory consumption to grow
bugs.symptoms: eventd spins at 100% and memory consumption grows over time.
bugs.conditions: If an eventd consumer is deleted while there are events pending, eventd can spin at 100% and its memory consumption will grow.
bugs.impact: System may be impacted due to eventd cycle usage, and eventually experience increasing memory consumption.

bugs.title: Memory leak with multiple client SSL profiles.
bugs.symptoms: If multiple client SSL profiles are attached to a virtual server, memory will leak each time any profile is changed.
bugs.conditions: Multiple client SSL profiles are attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Memory will leak a small amount of memory.
bugs.fix: Multiple client SSL profiles attached to a virtual server no longer causes memory to be leaked.

bugs.title: Cannot use 'default' as the FIPS security officer password.
bugs.symptoms: Trying to use 'default' as the FIPS security officer password results in an invalid encryption error from the fips-util.
bugs.conditions: Trying to use 'default' as the FIPS security officer password.
bugs.impact: You cannot use the word 'default' as the security officer password. Although this is expected behavior, the error message posted does not provide a relevant explanation. The system posts errors similar to the following: -- Invalid encrypted password. -- Failed to set security officer's password: 1073742342. -- Failed to create security domain. -- INITIALIZATION FAILED! -- The FIPS device is NOT operational. In version 11.1.0 and earlier, the error was similar to the following: -- Creating crypto user and crypto officer identities. -- password should not be default. -- Failed to set security officer's password.
bugs.workaround: Use a password other than the word 'default'.
bugs.fix: Disallow 'default' to be used as the Security Officer password.

bugs.title: tmrouted crashes after a series configuration changes
bugs.symptoms: When multiple route domains with multiple routing protocols with heartbeat enabled are repeatedly created and deleted, the tmrouted daemon may restart.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Heartbeat is enabled. -- Multiple route domains and routing protocols are created and deleted in a short time interval.
bugs.impact: The tmrouted crashes and it might lead to packet loss with regard to forwarding.
bugs.fix: The tmrouted functions normally when multiple route domains with multiple routing protocols, with heartbeat enabled, are created and deleted repeatedly.

bugs.title: VCMP: Warning messages in AVR log
bugs.symptoms: You see the following in the avr log: "AVRDATA_QUERY|WARNING|Jul 21 17:21:44.775|3101|lib/avrdata/query/http_main_query.c:0488| HTTP Main, got an entity with invalid key: 3, 3, 0"
bugs.conditions: It is not known what causes this to happen.
bugs.impact: Beyond the log messages, it is not known if there is any other impact. It is possible that AVR statistics could be incorrect, or could fail to report any statistics.
bugs.fix: VCMP: We fixed an issue where the system incorrectly displayed the following warning message in the AVR log: "HTTP Main, got an entity with invalid key".

bugs.title: Memory issues when there is a lot of data in /var/annotate (annotations for dashboard)
bugs.symptoms: When there is a large number annotations in /var/annotate, tomcat might run out of memory when the dashboard requests the annotations. The tomcat process logs an out-of-memory error, and the dashboard reports an error: -- SEVERE: Servlet.service() for servlet org.apache.jsp.dashboard.annotations_jsp threw exception java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space. -- Unrecoverable Communications Error. Please close this window and log in via the BIG-IP Configuration Utility.
bugs.conditions: -- Large number of configuration events, i.e., too many annotations in /var/annotate. -- Click anything other than the default '5 minutes' tab.
bugs.impact: The the dashboard attempts to load all annotations into memory, but cannot. Dashboard must be restarted and can only be used at the 5-minute zoom level.
bugs.workaround: -- Delete the files in /var/annotate. -- Increase the tomcat memory: provision.tomcat.extramb = 320

bugs.title: IE8: "An error has occurred while trying to process your request" while viewing active sessions
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, in IE8, while searching for particular active session by session IP an error message appears. The error message says that the system is trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: PEM enabled, with subscriber sessions active. IE8 Viewing active sessions via Policy Enforcement :: Subscribers
bugs.impact: IE8 will not display the page
bugs.workaround: Try refreshing the page, or try other browsers such as Chrome or Firefox.

bugs.title: SNAT pool stats are reflected in global SNAT stats
bugs.symptoms: There is a virtual server with SNAT pool configured. And a global default SNAT also configured similar to SNAT pool configuration. Traffic that hits virtual and uses the virtual SNAT pool to translate the source address. The same traffic stats will be reflected in default global SNAT though the default SNAT is not being used.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server has a SNAT configured. There is a global default SNAT configured similar to the configured SNAT pool.
bugs.impact: SNAT pool stats are reflected in global SNAT stats.
bugs.workaround: Configure the default SNAT in a different VLAN.
bugs.fix: The system now releases the default SNAT from the virtual server if there is a SNAT configuration directly associated with the virtual server.

bugs.title: Adding slots to running guests with host-iso can become stuck
bugs.symptoms: An added guest slot continually waits for a product image
bugs.conditions: the guest is running a version provided by a block-device-image or block-device-hotfix the guest is not running the deployed version of software there are no local copies of the iso in /shared/images on the guests
bugs.impact: additional guest slots will remain down until the installation image source is corrected
bugs.workaround: copy each guest's running version's iso into /shared/images of each guest cluster and wait for the iso to sync to all members before inserting a new blade when running 11.6.0
bugs.fix: Adding slots to running guests with host-iso no longer becomes stuck.

bugs.title: The Dashboard charts may dip when a blade is rebooted.
bugs.symptoms: The dashboard charts for active sessions and established session counts drop suddenly.
bugs.conditions: This happens when both of the following conditions are met 1. A blade is coming up online to join other already running blades. 2. Session event, i.e., user login or logout, occurs while the blade is coming up.
bugs.impact: The charts will remain inaccurate until next session event occurs.
bugs.workaround: The charts will be updated to correct value if new session is created.
bugs.fix: Dashboard no longer displays a dip in active session count when primary blade comes back from a reboot.

bugs.title: RADIUS session statistics for the subscribers created with an iRule running on the RADIUS virtual server are not incremented.
bugs.symptoms: The RADIUS session statistics for the subscribers created with an iRule running on the RADIUS virtual server are not incremented.
bugs.conditions: Session created via iRule running on the RADIUS virtual server.
bugs.impact: RADIUS session statistics are not incremented.
bugs.fix: The session statistics for sessions created by RADIUS is now incremented whenever the user runs an iRule on the RADIUS virtual server, that creates a new session.

bugs.title: tmm crash while changing acceleration policy
bugs.symptoms: If the JPEG-XR quality value in the acceleration policy is changed while traffic is running, TMM can crash.
bugs.conditions: Change JPEG-XR quality quality with request queuing enabled. TMM will crash if a request hits the TMM that owned the cached JPEG
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Don't use the Optimize to Client setting.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when the JPEG-XR quality value in the acceleration policy is changed while traffic is running.

bugs.title: SMTPS race condition after STARTTLS may cause incorrect SMTP responses
bugs.symptoms: After STARTTLS handshake, SMTP communication fails due to one of the following reasons: - BIG-IP system responses to SMTP client are not synchronized (that is, the responses do not match the requested commands). - SMTPS profile activation mode is 'require' and the BIG-IP system responds with '530 Must issue a STARTTLS command first.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- A virtual server configured with an SMTPS profile. -- After the STARTTLS handshake on the client side and the BIG-IP system has sent an RSET command to SMTP server, the BIG-IP system receives a command (such as HELO or EHLO) from an SMTP client before the BIG-IP system receives the RSET response from SMTP server.
bugs.impact: SMTP communication using the SMTPS profile might not succeed. intermittently or consistently.
bugs.fix: SMTP commands received after STARTTLS are now correctly buffered by SMTPS profile until the SMTP server is ready to receive them.

bugs.title: If you try to create more than 264 AVR profiles, avrd might crash.
bugs.symptoms: The maximum number of AVR profiles in the system is 264. If you try to create more than 264 AVR profiles, avrd might crash.
bugs.conditions: Creating more than 264 AVR profiles
bugs.impact: avrd crashes.
bugs.fix: The maximum number of AVR profiles in the system is 264. If you try to create more than 264 AVR profiles, MCP now generates the following message: "Can't generate more than 264 AVR profiles", and the system will not create the profiles.

bugs.title: Datastor Now Uses Syslog-ng
bugs.symptoms: Datastor did not use the normal syslog facility, causing some very rare disk full errors in /var/log.
bugs.conditions: When datastor is heavily overloaded or experiencing a traffic pattern that it was not designed for, it can generate copious notice messages to its log. Because datastor writes directly to its log, log rotation may seem to work, but inadvertently leave a large, hidden file in /var/log.
bugs.impact: In very rare cases, this hidden large file may cause out of disc errors, preventing logging from occurring.
bugs.workaround: Log rotate can be configured to restart datastor if this becomes an issue.
bugs.fix: Datastor now uses syslog-ng.

bugs.title: BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms do not support RSS with L4 data on SCTP
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms do not support RSS with L4 data on SCTP. If multiple connections are attempted, the same port is computed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms with SCTP configured.
bugs.impact: This causes 'Inet port collision' log errors, and the connection is terminated.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms now support RSS with L4 data on SCTP.

bugs.title: Virtual server with RequestAdapt/ResponseAdapt profiles along with a OneConnect profile
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not allow you to configure a virtual server with RequestAdapt/ResponseAdapt profiles along with a OneConnect profile. If you attach a ClientSSL profile, however, the configuration is allowed, which is incorrect behavior.
bugs.conditions: Create a virtual server, add tcp, request-adapt, and one-connect profiles along with ClientSSL.
bugs.impact: This unsupported configuration might have many unknown side effects in TMM.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure a virtual server with one-connect and requestadapt or responseadapt profiles.
bugs.fix: Configurations of request-/response-adapt combined with one-connect along with ClientSSL profiles are now handled correctly.

bugs.title: Transparent Proxy + On-Demand Cert Auth will reset
bugs.symptoms: After evaluating the access policy with an on-demand cert auth agent, there will be a connection reset.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under these conditions: SWG Transparent Proxy with a On-Demand Cert Auth agent.
bugs.impact: The user is not redirected back to their original landing URI. However, in known reproductions the access policy has already completed, and been set to allow. Future requests from the user will be correctly proxied to the backend.
bugs.workaround: If on-demand cert auth is needed, there is no workaround.

bugs.title: FastL4 connections reset with pva-acceleration set to guaranteed
bugs.symptoms: With 'pva-acceleration' set to 'guaranteed', the BIG-IP system can take up to five seconds to detect that one of either the client-side or server-side connections has not been offloaded to the ePVA hardware.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with 'pva-acceleration' set to 'guaranteed' and only one of client or server connections is offloaded to hardware.
bugs.impact: This results in the connection that has not been offloaded being reset five seconds after being established.
bugs.fix: FastL4 connections are now handles correctly with pva-acceleration set to guaranteed, and are no longer reset.

bugs.title: httpd_apm access_log remains empty after log rotation
bugs.symptoms: The /var/log/httpd/access_log file remains empty after log rotation.
bugs.conditions: At least one log rotation which happens at 4:00am every day of the box time
bugs.impact: access_log are missing
bugs.workaround: "bigstart restart httpd_apm" must be part of the cronjob every day [around 4:30am] after log rotation.
bugs.fix: Logging to access_log continues after log rotation.

bugs.title: RAID disk failure and alert.conf log message mismatch results in no trap
bugs.symptoms: Due to a mismatch between the definition of an alert for RAID disk failure in alert.conf, and the actual log message syntax, the appropriate SNMP traps are not issued when a disk is failing.
bugs.conditions: This happens when there is a RAID disk failure and the definition RAID disk failure in alert.conf is similar to the following: alert BIGIP_RAID_DISK_FAILURE "raid[0-9]: Disk failure .*?" { snmptrap OID=".1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.96"; lcdwarn description="RAID disk failure." priority="3" }
bugs.impact: Actual log message syntax matches the following: 'alert kernel: md/raid1:md12: Disk failure on dm-29, disabling device.' As a result, there is no SNMP trap for a failing disk, so no SNMP trap is issued, and the LCD message is not displayed.
bugs.workaround: For information about configuring custom traps, see SOL3727: Configuring custom SNMP traps, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/3000/700/sol3727.html.
bugs.fix: RAID disk failure and alert.conf log message now match, so appropriate SNMP traps are now issued when a disk is failing.

bugs.title: Renaming a virtual server causes unexpected configuration load failure
bugs.symptoms: Manually renaming a virtual server causes unexpected configuration load failure.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all the following conditions are met: -- The BIG-IP system configuration containing a virtual server that was renamed by editing bigip.conf manually -- The virtual server has an empty pool, or has a pool with pool members and a monitor.
bugs.impact: Cannot reload configuration. The system posts the following error: 01020056:3: Error computing object status for virtual_server broken (old_virtual_server_name). Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: Note: Traffic may be temporarily disrupted while the updated configuration loads. Perform any one of the following: -- Remove the pool assignment from the virtual before renaming. -- Ensure the pool contains members before renaming. If the pool has a monitor, temporarily remove the monitor and add it back after renaming. To load the updated configuration, after renaming, issue 'bigstart restart'.
bugs.fix: Manually editing the system configuration and renaming a virtual server with an empty pool no longer causes an unexpected error when reloading the configuration.

bugs.title: Chassis Temperature Status not showing Nitrox3x3 temperatures
bugs.symptoms: On a system with Nitrox3x3 addon cards, the system hardware sensors don't include temperature readings for the Nitrox 3x3 sensors.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP 12050/12250 platforms
bugs.impact: No information about the sensors on the Nitrox3x3 card is reported to the user.
bugs.fix: F5 support for new hardware platforms.

bugs.title: Systems which do not use RAID show confusing RAID status on the LCD
bugs.symptoms: The front panel LCD displays confusing RAID information on some systems which do not use RAID. On the front panel LCD, a RAID Status menu indicates that the single drive installed is Undefined. For systems configured in this way, you can safely ignore this display because the system is not using the RAID interface.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on some early 6900 and 8900 platforms, and 7000, 10000, and 12000 series platforms that shipped with a single SSD.
bugs.impact: This issue is cosmetic, and does not indicate a functional issue.

bugs.title: Emergency alert treated as critical on the 10000s, 10200v, 10250v, and 10350vN platforms.
bugs.symptoms: Failed system fan emergency alert is exhibited as critical alert at LED and LCD screen.
bugs.conditions: A failure of a system fan on the 10000s, 10200v, 10250v, and 10350vN platforms causes this issue to appear.
bugs.impact: This is a relatively minor event. Although the alarm is reported as critical, it should be treated at an emergency level and not critical.

bugs.title: Javascript sibmit() method could be rewritten incorrectly inside of 'with' statement.
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access could incorrectly rewrite Javascript submit() method if it's called in scope of 'with' statement and without object.
bugs.impact: Form cannot be submitted from script on page.
bugs.workaround: Create an iRule which adds explicit object reference to submit() call.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where Portal Access could incorrectly rewrite a form submit initiated from Javascript.

bugs.title: Kerberos Request-Based Auth (RBA) failure when session is initially created on a different VIP.
bugs.symptoms: Kerberos Request-Based Auth (RBA) failure when session is initially created on a different VIP.
bugs.conditions: APM access policy is configured with Kerberos authentication and the attempted authentication session was was initially created on a different VIP.
bugs.impact: Error occurs with no error message. The system should post an error message similar to the following: (Failure VIP Name): Kerberos Request-Based Auth failed because session was initially created on a different VIP (Original VIP Name). Please either disable RBA on the originating access profile, or remove the domain cookie.
bugs.workaround: Either disable RBA on the originating access profile, or remove the domain cookie.
bugs.fix: With the fix, APMD correctly handles the request for Kerberos Request-Based Auth, and posts the proper error message.

bugs.title: SNMP hbInterval value not set to 300 sec after upgrade from 11.2.x to 11.3.0 or later
bugs.symptoms: The hbInterval determines the amount of time the snmpd daemon can wait for a response. Software versions 11.2.x use an hbInterval of 60 sec. Software versions 11.3.0 and later use an hbInterval of 300 sec.
bugs.conditions: When upgrading from version 11.2.x to version 11.3.0 or later.
bugs.impact: After upgrade, the hbInterval is still set to 60 sec and not set to 300 sec. An snmpd core is created.
bugs.workaround: Edit bigipTrafficMgmt.conf and set hbInterval value to 300 using the following procedure: 1. Run the command: bigstart stop snmpd. 2. Change the value of hbInterval in /config/snmp/bigipTrafficMgmt.conf and save the file. 3. Run the command: bigstart start snmpd.
bugs.fix: When upgrading from a release that did not have the hbInterval set to 300, the new release now has hbInterval set to 300.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as IdP may rejects AuthnRequest with specific NameID format
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP as IdP rejects authentication request stating InvalidNameID Policy when received Authentication request contains NameID format "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:unspecified"
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured as an IdP. Received authentication request contains NameID format "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:unspecified" (Note SAML2.0).
bugs.impact: SAML Authentication request is rejected.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure SAML SP to create AuthnRequest with either 1. The following NameID format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:unspecified 2. Empty NameID format
bugs.fix: Fixed to accept NameID format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:unspecified

bugs.title: Improved Machine Certificate Checker matching criteria for FQDN case
bugs.symptoms: Machine cert check agent might fail if the certificate was issued with extended fields or to a domain machine.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the machine is outside of domain and the certificate is issued to a domain machine.
bugs.impact: Machine cert check agent might fail on MAC OS X/Windows for the machines currently outside of domain.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Machine cert check agent matching criteria for FQDN has been improved.

bugs.title: Route domain stats can not be reset by using F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmRouteDomainStatResetStats
bugs.symptoms: The operation does not reset the statistics.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: Stats are not reset.
bugs.fix: Added backend support, so this stat reset now works.

bugs.title: Policy Diff on merging missing URLs
bugs.symptoms: Policy Merge fails when trying to propagate a missing URL from one Security Policy to another.
bugs.conditions: Policy Diff is performed on two Security Policies and one has URLs defined that the other does not.
bugs.impact: Policy Merge Fails
bugs.fix: Policy Diff no longer fails when trying to merge a missing URL to another security policy.

bugs.title: ASM Standalone license has to include URL and HTML Rewrite
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade to 11.6.0, the system now reports 'URI Translation (Not Licensed)', yet the license package has not changed. There was no issue when running 11.4.1 with an ASM Standalone license and using the URL Rewrite functionality with URI Translation (under Local Traffic :: Profiles :: Services :: Rewrite).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Running 11.6.0. -- ASM Standalone license. -- URL Rewrite functionality with URI Translation.
bugs.impact: An ASM Standalone license generated for 11.6.0 does not include ltm_rewrite_uri. Therefore, regardless of what is configured in a rewrite profile, the profile is inoperative when assigned to a virtual server.
bugs.workaround: None available.
bugs.fix: In this release, ltm_rewrite_html and ltm_rewrite_url are enabled when mod_asm is enabled, so the system functions as expected for URL Rewrite functionality with URI Translation operations.

bugs.title: Fixed a few issues in HTTP Auth module
bugs.symptoms: 1. possible buffer overflow when session var CookieClientData is >8K 2. inappropriate use of mc_get_session_var in agent that may cause apd crash 3. per-request memory leak of cookies struct
bugs.conditions: 1. session variable CookieClientData is > 8K 2. apd may crash unexpectedly when HTTP Auth agent cannot get session variable 3. When HTTP Auth agent is configured for an Access Policy apd might leak memory per-request
bugs.impact: apd might crash apd might leak memory per-request

bugs.title: In AD Query agent, resolving of nested groups may cause apd to spin
bugs.symptoms: Access policy daemon (apd) consumes approximately 100% CPU and puts a heavy load on the network sometimes when resolving nested groups in AD Query. The AD Group Cache updates in a loop.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the user belongs to a parent domain, and is a member of a group that belongs to a sub-domain. For example, user belongs to parent.com, group belongs to child.parent.com; the user is a member of the group. The "fetch nested groups" option is enabled for AD Query.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the user will be unable to resolve nested groups and unable to finish AD Query.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
'OID not increasing error' during snmpwalk
bugs.symptoms: The following message when querying SNMP ipCidrRouteTable: 'Error: OID not increasing: IP-FORWARD-MIB::ipCidrRouteDest.172.27.96.0.255.255.255.0.0.0.0.0.0 >= IP-FORWARD-MIB::ipCidrRouteDest.172.27.96.0.255.255.255.0.0.0.0.0.0'. Also, querying specifically for ipCidrRouteAge OID under ipCidrRouteTable, can cause snmpd to core.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are dual management routes in the default routing table, main. For example: # ip route show table main / ip route show ... 172.27.96.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 172.27.96.18 172.27.96.0/24 dev eth0 scope link src 172.27.96.18 metric 9 ...
bugs.impact: snmpwalk error and/or snmpd core.
bugs.workaround: Delete the duplicate route with metric 9: ip route del 172.27.96.0/24 dev eth0 scope link src 172.27.96.18 metric 9
bugs.fix: snmpwalk now finishes successfully without 'OID not increasing' error, so snmpd no longer core.

bugs.title: IPsec interop problem when using AES-GCM.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP AES-GCM negotiation through IKEv2 does not accept the case of no integrity algorithm. This can happen with the tunnel configured to use AES-GCM.
bugs.conditions: When configuring IPsec tunnel to use AES-GCM to inter-operate between two BIG-IPs of version 11.6 and 12.0, or configuring IPsec tunnel on a BIG-IP of 11.6 to inter-operate with another vendor using AES-GCM.
bugs.impact: The IPsec tunnel will not be established.
bugs.workaround: For BIG-IP only, ensure both sides of the tunnel are the same release level.
bugs.fix: Do not include integrity algorithm for AES-GCM.

bugs.title: Error at attempt to add GeoIP with parentheses.
bugs.symptoms: You will get an error if you attempt to add GeoIP with parentheses to a rule. For example one GeoIP code is Cocos (Keeling) Islands (CC), where you will see this error: Error: 0107179c:3: The specified Geo Location Country Code(Keeling) on (TCP) is invalid
bugs.conditions: Attempting to add a GeoIP string that contains a parenthesis
bugs.impact: Unable to ad the GeoIP
bugs.fix: You can now add GeoIP regions containing parenthesis.

bugs.title: Missing a tunnel FDB endpoint configuration in VXLAN tunnels could result in memory leak
bugs.symptoms: For VXLAN tunnels with flooding type "multipoint" and "none", if a tunnel FDB endpoint is missing in the configuration and that endpoint sends traffic to the BIG-IP, memory leak could occur when the BIG-IP receives the traffic.
bugs.conditions: Missing a tunnel FDB endpoint in the configuration.
bugs.impact: Memory leak could occur.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that a tunnel FDB endpoint is configured if that endpoint is expected to send traffic to the BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: No memory leak occurs even if a tunnel FDB endpoint is missing in the configuration and that endpoint sends traffic to the BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Multiple DHCP solicit packets may not succeed.
bugs.symptoms: Some DHCP solicit packets might be dropped.
bugs.impact: The assignment of an address to an end node may be delayed as some DHCP Solicit packets might be discarded.
bugs.fix: In this release, multiple requests succeed using a single server flow, and the system sends the request back to the client using original connflow.
bugs.conditions: If the same server flow is used for multiple requests only one of them will succeed, the other request may never succeed. The request is dropped by the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Websso truncates cookie domain value
bugs.symptoms: Cookies assigned during back end authentication may not be returned to back end servers. The failures require the set-cookie header contain a domain assignment and the domain value must begin with a dot.
bugs.conditions: 401 response from a back end has Set-Cookie headers containing domain assignments that begin with a dot.
bugs.impact: Applications protected by the above authorization may not work.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be used to catch the 401 response. If it contains one or more Set-Cookie headers, check each for a domain attribute. Remove the initial dot in the domain value, if present.
bugs.fix: WebSSO processes domain fields in Set-Cookie headers correctly.

bugs.title: HD Encryption check should provide an option to choose drive
bugs.symptoms: HD Encryption check only allows the administrator to check for all HD encryption status of all drives on the system, including temporary drives like USB. There is no way for the administrator to check the encryption status of only the system drive.
bugs.conditions: APM, HD encryption check, and Edge client
bugs.impact: Cannot check encryption status of only the system drive.
bugs.fix: HD Encryption check now provides a way to check encryption status of all drives or system drive only.

bugs.title: Incorrect HTML form handling.
bugs.symptoms: If one of the HTML forms on a page is added dynamically, it is possible that other forms cannot be submitted via portal access.
bugs.conditions: - HTML form added dynamically. - absolute action path for one of another forms on this page.
bugs.impact: Action path may be rewritten incorrectly and the form cannot be submitted.
bugs.fix: Now absolute action path for any form in HTML page is rewritten correctly at submit time.

bugs.title: If encryption is disabled, an alert is sent with the correct username.
F5 support for new hardware platforms.
It's possible to exhaust monpd's Thrift server connections by simply not closing the connection on the client side
bugs.symptoms: It's possible to open a connection to monpd's Thrift server and if the client does not actively close it, the connection will persist indefinitely (even if it's idle). As a result of this issue, you might experience the following symptoms: -- Cannot access event logs or reports. -- Cannot run tmsh analytics commands.
bugs.conditions: Client system opens a connection to monpd's Thrift server (port 9090 or 9091), and does not close it.
bugs.impact: If the number of allowed connections to monpd's Thrift server is reached, monpd will not receive new connections. Since the idle connections can persist indefinitely this will deny service from monpd.
bugs.workaround: No workaround (except for manually killing open idle connections).
bugs.fix: Idle connections are closed after one minute.

bugs.title: Unrecognized DNS records can cause mcpd to core during a DNS cache query
bugs.symptoms: mcpd cores during a DNS cache record query if a DNS record with an unknown type is in the cache. mcpd attempts to translate the record's type into a text string, but ends up with a NULL pointer instead.
bugs.conditions: A DNS record with a type unknown by mcpd must exist in the DNS cache during the query.
bugs.impact: mcpd cores, causing either a failover (if there is a standby unit) or an outage while mcpd restarts (if there is no standby unit).
bugs.fix: Unrecognized DNS records no longer cause mcpd to core during a DNS cache query.

bugs.title: No URL path in the Browser Automation alert
bugs.symptoms: Vtoken alerts are sent without the protected URL path in alert payload. This impacts alerts analysis, since it is impossible to determine the origin URL of the alert.
bugs.conditions: 1. Automatic transactions enabled on a URL. 2. Automatic transaction alert is generated.
bugs.impact: No URL path in the Browser Automation alert. This makes vtoken alerts analysis difficult and more time consuming.
bugs.fix: Fixed the client_request_uri so there is now a URL path in the Browser Automation alert.

bugs.title: SNMP reports the incorrect product name for the BIG-IP 10350 NEBS platform.
bugs.symptoms: SNMP reports the incorrect product name for the BIG-IP 10350 NEBS platform.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using SNMP to report the BIG-IP 10350 NEBS platform name when running 11.6.0 HF2.
bugs.impact: SNMP reports the incorrect platform name: BIG-IP 10050N, instead of the correct platform name: BIG-IP 10350N.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to view the correct platform name.
bugs.fix: SNMP now reports the correct product name for the BIG-IP 10350 NEBS platform.

bugs.title: System might fail to unchunk server response when compression is enabled
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP virtual server is configured with a compression profile and either: - an NTLM profile - or an APM access policy When a pool member sends a chunked (and uncompressed) HTTP response to the BIG-IP system (Transfer-Encoding: chunked), if the BIG-IP system compresses the payload, it does so without unchunking it. This results in the BIG-IP system sending the client a malformed response that contains chunked encoding markers in the compressed content.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- The NTLM and OneConnect profiles are applied to a virtual server. This can also be triggered when replacing the NTLM profile with an APM access policy configuration on the virtual server. -- HTTP compression is enabled on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: HTTP responses to the client are malformed. When decompressed, the HTTP response payload incorrectly contains HTTP chunked encoding markers.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can either modify the type of response chunking or disable compression. For information on how to do so, see K14030: The BIG-IP system may fail to unchunk server responses when compression is enabled, available here: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14030.
bugs.fix: This release properly manages chunking and unchunking when compression is configured, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Server SSL profile unable to complete SSL handshake when server selects DHE-based key exchange, and is configured with 2048-bit or larger DH keys
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP virtual server is configured with a Server SSL profile, and a pool member or server selects a DHE-based ciphersuite (e.g. DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA), the BIG-IP system might not successfully complete an SSL handshake with the server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions exist: - HTTPS Pool member or server. - Virtual server with Server SSL profile. - Server is configured with 2048-bit or larger Diffie-Hellman keys.
bugs.impact: Traffic to affected pool members fails, although the pool members are marked up by HTTPS monitors.
bugs.workaround: Either disable the use of ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (DHE) key exchange on the backend servers, select a smaller set of DH parameters on the backend servers, or disable DHE ciphersuites in affected virtual servers' Server SSL profiles.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP system now successfully completes an SSL handshake with a server that is using Diffie-Hellman parameters that are 2048-bits or larger, up to 4096-bits.
