bugs.title: When the BIG-IP system is configured as Service Provider, APD may restart under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured as Service Provider, APD may restart under certain conditions.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML Service Provider and BIG-IP receives a signed assertion that contains empty "Reference URI" in Signature element.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that APD restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed issues that caused APD to restart when the BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML Service Provider and BIG-IP receives a signed assertion that contains an empty Reference URI in the Signature element.

bugs.title: SOD posts error message: Config digest module error: Traffic group device not found
bugs.symptoms: SOD posts error message: Config digest module error: Traffic group device not found.
bugs.conditions: In a failover device group, if a peer device (non self device) has gone through a management IP address change, SOD fails to clean up the old IP address from its internal storage, so the system subsequently and incorrectly behaves as if there is a 'configuration data inconsistent' error.
bugs.impact: This issue may cause the HA failover next-active device selection to fall back to the static (IP-based) selection algorithm. As a result, your DSC group with more than 2 devices, selects a device other than the intended device to take over services.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue, you can perform configSync to propagate the new management IP peer, and then restart the sod process. To restart sod, at the command line run the following command: bigstart restart sod

bugs.title: ConfigSync operation failing with rarely occurring sFlow error
bugs.symptoms: An sFlow error may occur during config sync or load of a BIG-IP device.
bugs.conditions: Exact conditions are unknown and difficult to reproduce, but some possible conditions include config sync or load operations following delete/create of a virtual server or profiles (either directly or by deleting/creating an iApp), sync following failover
bugs.impact: Config sync or load operation might fail. This occurs rarely. When this occurs, the system posts a message similar to the following: 'Can't save/checkpoint DB object, class:sflow_http_virtual_data_source status:13'
bugs.workaround: Force the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration. For more information, see K13030, Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration, available here: Link: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030.
bugs.fix: The ConfigSync operation completes successfully, and the sFlow error no longer occurs.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ at times cannot discover BIG-IP running TMOS 11.6.0 - 11.6.0 HF3, failure reason: Failed getting time zone.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IQ attempt to obtain BIG-IP provisioning state using REST API (GET request using HTTP/HTTPS) fails as the forwarder to service the requests is not available.
bugs.conditions: Any BIG-IQ GET request e.g., to obtain provisioning state of the BIG-IP. This occurs with version 11.6.0 - 11.6.0 HF3 only.
bugs.impact: Any script using REST API to manage the BIG-IP or BIG-IQ attempting to manage BIG-IP will fail.
bugs.workaround: Run the following two commands sequentially: bigstart restart restjavad bigstart restart icrd
bugs.fix: Improved TMOS 11.6.0 - 11.6.0 HF3 handling of GET commands from BIG-IQ to BIG-IP systems.

bugs.title: iControl GlobalLB::PoolMember get_all_statistics and get_monitor_association cause memory leaks
bugs.symptoms: iControl methods GlobalLB::PoolMember::get_all_statistics and get_monitor_association can cause memory leaks, which can quickly become problematic when querying large GTM configurations often.
bugs.impact: Memory leak can become very large with big configurations.
bugs.workaround: Restart the iControlPortal (bigstart restart httpd).
bugs.fix: GlobalLB::PoolMember get_all_statistics and get_monitor_association methods no longer cause memory leak.

bugs.title: Period characters in GTM virtual server naming
bugs.symptoms: The period and colon characters in GTM virtual server names are converted to underscores ( _ ) after upgrading to version 11.x.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from version 10.x to version 11.x.
bugs.impact: Production monitoring when your production GTM systems are upgraded.

bugs.title: LB_FAILED may not be triggered if persistence member is down
bugs.symptoms: LB_FAILED may not be triggered if persistence member is down.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions exist: - Incoming connection has cookie matching persistence entry. - Persisted pool member has been marked down. - No other pool members are available.
bugs.impact: Cannot utilize LB::reselect command.
bugs.fix: LB_FAILED event is correctly triggered when persistence pool member is not available or offline.

bugs.title: RAM cache evictions spikes with change of access policy which may lead to slow webtop rendering
bugs.symptoms: When there is a high load on the system and a user changes an access policy, it can lead to slow rendering of the webtop or the access page.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when there is a high load with change of access policy around that time.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is slow webtop/access page rendering.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Access policy changes are handled gracefully.

bugs.title: IP addresses are not properly cleaned from lookup tables, so there might be no room for new IP addresses to be collected.
bugs.symptoms: IP addresses are not properly cleaned from lookup tables, so there might be no room for new IP addresses to be collected. System might post many messages in the avrd log, including ones similar to the following: -- AVRDATA_QUERY|WARNING|... lib/avrdata/query/http_main_query.c:0547| HTTP Main, got an entity with invalid key: 2, 3, 0 -- AVRDATA_QUERY|WARNING|... lib/avrdata/query/http_main_query.c:0841| Skip the entity with invalid key
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using AVR when the system is idle after traffic IP lookups.
bugs.impact: New IP addresses might not be collected. It is possible that AVR statistics could be incorrect, or could fail to report any statistics.
bugs.fix: IP addresses are now properly cleaned from lookup tables, making room so new IP addresses can be collected.

bugs.title: Applying ASM security policy repeatedly fills disk partition on a chassis
bugs.symptoms: Applying ASM security policy repeatedly on a chassis will cause /var disk partition to fill.
bugs.conditions: ASM security policy is applied repeatedly on a chassis.
bugs.impact: /var disk partition is filled.
bugs.workaround: Delete the contents of /var/ts/var/cluster/send.
bugs.fix: An ASM security policy can be repeatedly applied on a chassis without filling the disk partition.

bugs.title: ePVA IPv6 feature is not available
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 full hardware acceleration with ePVA feature is disabled. An issue was uncovered in the 2.3.x bitstream that results in Flow Status Updates (FSUs) due to a collision eviction being corrupted in certain cases. This occurs when the flow cache entry being evicted and the incoming snoop are different sizes. In the 2.3.x bitstream design, the IPv4 and SYN VIP flow cache entries and snoops are the same size, and the IPv6 flow cache entries and snoops are larger than IPv4/SYN VIP. There are no FSU-related issues when a cache entry is evicted due to a collision by a same size snoop, and there are no issues when an eviction is explicitly requested by software via the evict opcode.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION B2250 blade with ePVA acceleration, IPv6.
bugs.impact: Cannot enable full acceleration for an IPv6 VIP.
bugs.fix: ePVA IPv6 feature is now available in this release.

bugs.title: No 'base-installable' images (release plus hotfix) for VM
bugs.symptoms: F5 virtual machine (VM) images are not released for hotfixes. The process of applying hotfixes for VMs is to install the released version of the software, and then apply the required hotfix on top of it.
bugs.conditions: Hotfix releases for VM installations.
bugs.impact: Two installation steps, where one might be expected.
bugs.workaround: Install the released version of the software, and then apply the required hotfix.
bugs.fix: This release contains base installation virtual machine (VM) images in addition to the hotfix updates. The VM images now consist of base release software, with hotfixes already applied. That means the system is immediately ready for deployment after hotfix installation, and no longer requires two steps (install the base installation image, and then install the hotfix).

bugs.title: Client SSL on partition other than /Common does not load if no key/cert/inherit-certkeychain
bugs.symptoms: Client SSL configurations on a partition other than /Common do not load if there is no key/cert or inherit-certkeychain.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1. There is a configuration in a folder/partition other than /Common. 2. crypto-server-default-clientssl, or another clientssl profile, has no key/cert or inherit-certkeychain configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot load configuration or UCS.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, complete the following steps: 1. modify /defaults/profile_base.conf and /config/profile_base.conf -- config # vim /defaults/profile_base.conf -- config # vim /config/profile_base.conf -- Locate crypto-server-default-clientssl and add the key/cert-related configuration to it. Specifically, change the profile information to match the following: ltm profile client-ssl crypto-server-default-clientssl { defaults-from /Common/clientssl cert-key-chain { default { cert /Common/default.crt chain none key /Common/default.key passphrase none } } cert /Common/default.crt chain none key /Common/default.key passphrase none inherit-certkeychain true ciphers DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 renegotiate-period 21600 cache-size 0 } 2. For clientssl other than crypto-server-default-clientssl, make sure key/cert and/or inherit-certkeychain is set. 3. Load the configuration by running the command: tmsh load sys conf
bugs.fix: Client SSL configurations on a partition other than /Common do not now have a default key/cert and inherit-certkeychain, so the configuration loads correctly.

bugs.title: TMM restart, SIGSEGV messages, and core
bugs.symptoms: Certain conditions might produce error messages similar to the following, in the core file/tmm.log: -- RVAvpBigIP01 notice RIP=0x8cc872 -- RVAvpBigIP01 notice session_process_pending_event_callback ERROR: could not send callback to 192.168.96.27:50441 - 192.168.96.28:443 ERR_NOT_FOUND.
bugs.conditions: This occurs because of a race condition, for example, one between the HTTP and APM-related profiles during which an APM-profile-related action completes after the HTTP-profile closes the connection.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The race condition that occurred has been fixed, so no APM-profile-related actions complete after the HTTP-profile closes the connection.

bugs.title: OS X 10.10 Yosemite support
bugs.symptoms: OS X 10.10 Yosemite support doesn't exist. Components are not signed with version 2 signatures
bugs.conditions: OS X Yosemite, mac edge client components with version 1
bugs.impact: gatekeeper might throw warnings.
bugs.fix: Code signing of executables (app, plugin and installer) have been updated to Apple's latest (v2) signature requirement.

bugs.title: Rare issue: client session might not be restored by fingerprint in the Web Scraping mitigation.
bugs.symptoms: It is possible for a user to restart the ASM session in a rare case.
bugs.conditions: There are Java-Script obfuscation changes.
bugs.impact: Clients can bypass web scraping violations.
bugs.fix: We fixed a rare problem in the Web Scraping mitigation, where a client session would not be restored by fingerprint.

bugs.title: TMM crash when processing unexpected HTTP response in WAM
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when processing unexpected HTTP response in WAM
bugs.conditions: Three conditions: WAM enabled virtual server WAM disabled during request phase WAM enabled during response phase
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not disable WAM during request processing unless it will also be disabled during response processing. If WAM is disabled, close the connection after the response with HTTP::Close to ensure it cannot be used for future requests.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when processing unexpected HTTP response in WAM.

bugs.title: Analysis processes appear to use high CPU though not affecting data plane
bugs.symptoms: The average system CPU usage and the busiest CPU in the dashboard can appear to be exceptionally high when a module with dedicated analysis processes like AVR is being used. These processes have dedicated resources so they do not impact the resources used by the critical data plane, so the high CPU usage is misleading.
bugs.conditions: A module such as AVR that has dedicated analysis processes must be provisioned.
bugs.impact: The system CPU usage and busiest CPU appear to be higher than expected.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to examine the detailed per CPU graphs and note that the high CPU is limited to the analysis processor which is the CPU with the highest number on a BIG-IP appliance.
bugs.fix: Average system CPU and busiest CPU calculation is now based on the critical data plane processing.
bugs.behavior: Average system CPU and busiest CPU calculation is now based on the critical data plane processing.

bugs.title: Identical source integrity alerts are present.
bugs.symptoms: Unnecessary alerts are sent, when the same protected page is requested by an end-user.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when source integrity URLs are configured and the user refreshes the page.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary alerts are sent, cluttering the alert dashboard.
bugs.fix: Repeating identical alerts are now prevented.

bugs.title: TMM may restart when SLO response is received on SLO request URL (.../post/sls)
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system expects to receive SLO responses on a particular URL: (.../post/slr). TMM may restart when SLO response is received on an SLO request URL (.../post/sls).
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured as SAML SP or IdP. SLO response is received on SLO request URL.
bugs.impact: TMM reboots and is temporarily unavailable.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: 1. Reconfigure another SAML party to send SLO messages to a proper URL. 2. Disable SLO
bugs.fix: Proper validation was added to check correct messages were received on proper URL. Logging was added for failing cases.

bugs.title: Add timestamps to logstatd logs for Policy Sync
bugs.symptoms: Log messages in /var/tmp/logstatd.log used for Policy Sync do not have timestamps which makes troubleshooting very difficult.
bugs.conditions: Run Policy Sync.
bugs.impact: Serviceability. logstatd.log used for Policy Sync do not have timestamps.
bugs.fix: A timestamp is now prepended to each log message line in logstatd.log for Policy Sync.

bugs.title: igbvf driver leaks xfrags when partial jumbo frame received
bugs.symptoms: On platforms utilizing the igbvf driver, xfrags can be leaked if a partial jumbo frame is received.
bugs.conditions: On platforms utilizing the igbvf driver, xfrags can be leaked if a partial jumbo frame is received.
bugs.impact: TMM memory usage increases over time and eventually TMM crashes due to lack of memory.
bugs.fix: The igbvf driver no longer leaks xfrags when a partial jumbo frame is received.

bugs.title: FTP connections are being offloaded to ePVA
bugs.symptoms: FTP connections are offloaded to acceleration hardware embedded Packet Velocity Acceleration (ePVA) chip.
bugs.conditions: SNAT listener
bugs.impact: FTP data connections fail due to lack of translation in PORT commands.
bugs.workaround: Use FTP virtual instead of SNAT listener.
bugs.fix: FTP connections will no longer be offload to ePVA hardware when traversing through a SNAT listener.

bugs.title: [Flash AS3] ApplicationDomain matching fails for relative URLs
bugs.symptoms: URL matching fails for child SWFs loaded from URL without hostname. SWFs from the same backend host are loaded into an isolated ApplicationDomain, and can't see objects from parent SWF. Application doesn't work or throws exceptions.
bugs.conditions: Child SWFs cannot access parent SWF.
bugs.impact: Application doesn't work or throw exceptions.
bugs.workaround: Disable the flash patching
bugs.fix: [Flash AS3] URL matching succeeds for child SWFs loaded from URL without hostname.

bugs.title: Upgrading from previous versions
bugs.symptoms: Configuration upgrade from versions 11.2, 11.1, or 11.0 fails when two analytics profiles on different partitions are configured with the same remote login server IP address.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from versions 11.2, 11.1, or 11.0 when two analytics profiles on different partitions are configured with the same remote login server IP address.
bugs.impact: Upgrade process fails.
bugs.workaround: Remove the external logging configuration on the source partition, upgrade, and then restore the configuration as needed.
bugs.fix: Configuration upgrade from versions 11.2, 11.1, or 11.0 now succeeds and works correctly even when two analytics profiles on different partitions are configured with the same remote login server IP address.

bugs.title: PEM: Session policy list may be lost if there is an radius update of custom attributes
bugs.symptoms: If for a session, if radius update is received and an IRULE is triggered to create/update custom attributes, then session may loose its provisioned policies.
bugs.conditions: PEM irule for radius profile updating custom attributes.
bugs.impact: No proper policing of session.
bugs.fix: Custom attribute for create or update no longer harms the policy list.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as IdP can send incorrect 'Issuer' element for some SLO requests under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: When client initiates Single Logout (SLO) on the BIG-IP system as IdP which is associated with multiple SP connectors, IdP will send SLO request message to each SP to which user has connected within this session. If user has connected to multiple SP (bound to different IdP) within the same session, the SLO messages f is sent with 'Issuer'element referencing the name of the last IdP service user has accessed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when: 1.BIG-IP is configured as IdP. 2.BIG-IP has more then one IdP configuration object. 3.IdP objects are assigned as resources to the same Access Policy. 4.Each IdP configuration is bound to at least one SP-connector. 5.Client initiated SLO on IdP.
bugs.impact: Impact is based on recipient of the message. Recipient (SP) may reject the SLO request, or process it successfully based on implementation.
bugs.workaround: Disable SLO on BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of form if it contains a tag with id=action
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, a form with absolute path in the action is handled incorrectly in Internet Explorer 7, 8, and 9. The resulting action path is wrong and the form cannot be submitted.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under these conditions: HTML Form with absolute action path; a tag with id=action inside this form; IE7-9
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the web application can not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now forms with absolute action path and tag with id=action inside are handled correctly.

bugs.title: IKEv1 daemon crashes when flushing SAs
bugs.symptoms: IKEv1 daemon (racoon) may occasionally crash because of freeing null pointer when the IKEv1 negotiation data is flushed.
bugs.conditions: The IKEv1 security associations are flushed by user issued commands.
bugs.impact: IKEv1 daemon (racoon) crashes and restarts, losing unrelated but useful state information. IKEv1 daemon (racoon) can re-establish security associations on demand by user traffic.
bugs.fix: A safety check during memory management function can prevent such erroneous memory freeing event. Crash is no longer seen.

bugs.title: OpenSSL Security Advisory 8/6/14 (1.0.1i Update).
EAM process fails to register channel threads (MPI channel) with TMM, and subsequent system call fails.
bugs.symptoms: On EAM process initialization, the plugin is unable to register a thread (MPI channel) with TMM on rare occasions. A subsequent system call to end the process fails.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: EAM plugin is up but the access gates are not initialized correctly.
bugs.workaround: Establish connection to OAM server. bigstart stop eam Clear config.cache from each accessgates by deleting /config/aaa/oam/<partition_name>/<aaa_oam_obj_name>/<accessgate_name>/config.cache using commandline. bigstart restart eam
bugs.fix: EAM plugin initialization is fixed, now the plugin register with TMM process will not fail.

bugs.title: Infrastructural changes for VMware View 6 support.
Nitrox crypto hardware may attempt soft reset while currently resetting
bugs.symptoms: Nitrox crypto hardware may attempt soft reset to clear a stuck condition while already engaged in a soft reset attempt.
bugs.conditions: Soft reset is needed to clear a stuck condition occurring in the timeframe during which another soft reset is occurring.
bugs.impact: The initial soft reset attempt does not complete as the process is restarted by the new attempt.
bugs.workaround: Correct the condition resulting in the need for the soft reset to clear the stuck condition or disable hardware-based crypto acceleration by setting db variable 'tmm.ssl.cn.shunt' to disable. To disable hardware-based crypto acceleration issue the following command: tmsh modify sys db tmm.ssl.cn.shunt value disable Note: Disabling hardware-based crypto acceleration results in all crypto actions being processed in software, which might result in higher CPU and memory usage based on traffic patterns.
bugs.fix: A crypto soft reset attempt is now allowed to complete before another soft reset attempt can occur.

bugs.title: Internal build improvement.
Remote logs without attack ID and mitigation fields
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes customers are getting empty values within dos_attack_id and dos_mitigation_action fields in the remote logger.
bugs.conditions: When proactive is turned on attack logs are issued without attack.
bugs.impact: Sometimes customers are getting empty values within dos_attack_id and dos_mitigation_action fields in the remote logger.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: DoS for Application Security now reports suspicious entities only if the application is under attack, or as part of proactive mitigation. DoS for Application Security no longer reports suspicious entities if an attack has not occurred, because this led to logs with empty attack IDs and blank mitigation methods.

bugs.title: Profiles with a large number of regexps can cause excessive memory usage.
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes on out of memory.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if you are using a lot of profiles that rely on regular expressions, such as compression or deflate.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Fix ssl_profile nref counter problem.
bugs.symptoms: ssl_profile memory leak.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after several iterations of the following steps: (1) Create ssl_profiles (2) Use ssl_profiles to complete a number of handshake operations. (3) Delete ssl_profiles.
bugs.impact: ssl_profile memory leak.
bugs.fix: ssl_profile no longer leaks memory when creating and deleting a number of profiles that have completed handshake operations.

bugs.title: Missing validation of disallowing empty DC configuration list
bugs.symptoms: NTLM authentication feature requires at least one Domain Controller to be specified in the NTLM Auth Configuration Domain Controller FQDN list. This is as designed to prevent unwanted load on the server because NTLM authentication is performed on a per connection basis. There is no DC autodiscovery mechanism implemented for NTLM authentication, by design. To effect the feature, we need the administrator to specify particular servers. Having this list empty caused an unexpected behavior, in which authentication is not performed and yet is considered a success. The configuration of the Domain Controller for an NTLM authentication configuration is different from the configuration of the Domain Controller for an NTLM machine account. For the NTLM machine account, the BIG-IP system can automatically discover one of the available DCs using DNS method or the administrator can specify a DC. We are asking administrators to specify at least one Domain Controller for NTLM Auth configurations in the Domain Controller FQDN list.
bugs.conditions: Domain Controller configuration is allowed to be empty which is both incorrect and unsupported.
bugs.impact: misbehave with incorrect and unsupported configuration, and causes no authentication is being performed.
bugs.fix: In this release, the Domain Controller (DC) fully qualified domain name (FQDN) list for an NTLM Auth Configuration is mandatory. Before you upgrade, ensure that the DC FQDN list for each NTLM Auth Configuration contains at least one domain controller FQDN. You can perform this verification from the GUI or by using tmsh. In tmsh, you can add the following line (dc-fqdn-list { <fqdn> } ) for each ntlm auth configuration as shown in this example. apm ntlm ntlm-auth ntlm_test { app-service none dc-fqdn-list { dc01.example.com } machine-account-name mdc1 partition Common service-id 2 }

bugs.title: Core caused by incorrect accounting of I/O flows
bugs.symptoms: I/O flows for the Cavium Nitrox are not always added to the count- but are always subtracted correctly, causing an imbalance.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only on platforms using the Cavium Nitrox chip.
bugs.impact: Incorrect accounting allowed the number of flows to drop below zero, triggering an assert and a core.
bugs.fix: Resolved core caused by accounting miscalculation of Nitrox I/O flows

bugs.title: Viewing DNS::Zones:Zones:Zones List:Statistics in the GUI generates error.
bugs.symptoms: DNS::Zones:Zones:Zones List:Statistics shows the error 'An error has occurred while trying to process your request'.
bugs.conditions: View DNSX Zone Status through the GUI.
bugs.impact: Cannot view statistics for DNSX Zones.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh instead.
bugs.fix: No error occurs while navigating to DNS::Zones:Zones:Zones List:Statistics.

bugs.title: Use of HTTP::retry may cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Use of HTTP::retry may cause TMM to crash in certain scenarios.
bugs.conditions: Use of HTTP::retry may cause TMM to crash in certain scenarios.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: HTTP::retry no longer causes TMM to crash.

bugs.title: BIG-IP goes offline after time change
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP goes offline after time changes backward
bugs.conditions: Time changed. ASM or FPS was just provisioned.
bugs.impact: Box is offline.
bugs.workaround: restart datasyncd daemon
bugs.fix: We fixed a problem where the system would become OFFLINE when moving the system time backwards soon after provisioning ASM or FPS.

bugs.title: CATEGORY::filetype command may cause tmm to crash and restart
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule command is created using the CATEGORY::filetype command, the tmm may eventually suffer a failure, and restart.
bugs.conditions: A bug in the implementation of CATEGORY::filetype iRule command triggers undefined behavior, leading to tmm crash and restart.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The errant code was corrected to remove the undefined behavior.

bugs.title: Microsoft RDP Client for Mac OS X ver. 8.0.9 does not work correctly with BIG-IP APM.
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft RDP Client for Mac OS X ver. 8.0.9 does not work correctly with BIG-IP APM.
bugs.conditions: Using Microsoft RDP Client for Mac OS X ver. 8.0.9.
bugs.impact: Does not work correctly with BIG-IP APM.
bugs.fix: Microsoft RDP Client for Mac OS X ver. 8.0.9 now correctly works with BIG-IP APM.

bugs.title: Submitting an HTML form that does not have an action attribute is a 404 error and 'null' in the request URL.
bugs.symptoms: The result of submitting an HTML form that does not have an action attribute is a 404 error and 'null' in the request URL.
bugs.conditions: Form tag does not have action attribute.
bugs.impact: Form cannot be submitted.
bugs.workaround: Add attribute "action=''" into the HTML form tag, either by modifying the source or by using an iRule.
bugs.fix: Now HTML forms without action attribute are handled correctly.

bugs.title: TCP::close in CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may result in tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: TCP::close in CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may cause tmm to crash.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when TCP::close is called within a CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use TCP::close in CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event
bugs.fix: Connection remains open after dispatching CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event, which prevents accessing invalid memory.

bugs.title: In some cases Edge Client for Windows does not re-resolve server hostname while reconnecting
bugs.symptoms: If BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows connects to APM server using FQDN, it does not re-resolve the server hostname while reconnecting. In failover scenarios where one APM server goes down, Edge Client will continually try to connect to the non-existent IP of the APM server that went down and will not switch over to the next APM server.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions. 1. Edge Client is connected to APM server using FQDN and 2. More than one APM servers are configured and a GTM, or another DNS server, is used for failing over.
bugs.impact: The client does not re-resolve the server hostname while reconnecting and needs to be restarted to successfully connect again.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, restart Edge Client and connect again.
bugs.fix: Resolved this issue: when APM is configured with URL (https://....), BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows does not resolve the APM hostname while reconnecting.

bugs.title: All alerts are sent only to the customer's BIGIP. From there, the customer can decide where they are sent.
Category Lookup by SNI doesn't work for SWG transparent + Mobile AppTunnel in case of using SWG SSL bypass
bugs.symptoms: Category lookup by SNI doesn't work for Mobile Application Tunnels (i.e. iOS perAppVPN). An error "SWG Scheme not assigned to main access policy" appears.
bugs.conditions: SWG transparent + Mobile AppTunnel in use. Issue is reproducible only with "SSL Forward Proxy Bypass" option in SSL profile for layered virtual server.
bugs.impact: Per-request policy will fail when it hits the category lookup agent with conditions specified.
bugs.workaround: "Remove SSL Forward Proxy Bypass" option in SSL profile for layered virtual server.

bugs.title: cur_conns number different in tmstat and snmp output.
bugs.symptoms: The current connections (cur_conns) number different in tmstat and snmp output.
bugs.conditions: This problem occurs when MPTCP is used.
bugs.impact: Incorrect cur_conns counting when using MPTCP.
bugs.fix: The discrepancies in current connections (cur_conns) between tmstat and snmp has been corrected.

bugs.title: Edge client remembers specific virtual server URI after it is redirected
bugs.symptoms: When client is redirected with HTTP 302, either from Access policy or from iRule, it remembers the URL of the server it was redirected to, even after a hard disconnect.
bugs.impact: Certain configurations in which APM server is selected based on location (or other attributes) of the client will not work as intended and user will continue to use the same APM that it used the first time.
bugs.workaround: Restart edge client and connect again.
bugs.fix: Resolved issue when BIG-IP Edge Client remembers a specific virtual server URI after it is redirected.

bugs.title: Empty or invalid configuration, or during exception in NTLM, handling might not work as expected.
bugs.symptoms: When the system encounters an empty or invalid configuration, or during exception in NTLM, handling might not work as expected.
bugs.conditions: Empty DC list configured in the NTLM configuration.
bugs.impact: NTLM authentication won't work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Fix the configuration - make sure that DC list is not empty.
bugs.fix: ECA data plane has been updated to include additional security change against empty configuration.

bugs.title: Tunnel reconnect with v2.02 does not occur
bugs.symptoms: Tunnel reconnect does not happen when DTLS is enabled
bugs.conditions: Configure SSL profile Enable DTLS in NA resource Establish NA connection from the device
bugs.impact: Reconnect does not happen
bugs.fix: A HelloRequest is re-transmitted if not responded by a ClientHello

bugs.title: SSL persistence profile does not find the server certificate.
bugs.symptoms: When an SSL record is constructed in a certain way, the SSL persistence code might not detect the server certificate.
bugs.conditions: SSL persistence profile is configured.
bugs.impact: Loss of functionality
bugs.fix: SSL now correctly parses the handshake records.

bugs.title: Data integrity data is no longer sent when it is not required.
Synchronization problem in AVR lookups sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash
bugs.symptoms: There is a synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.
bugs.conditions: AVR is provisioned or report statistic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: We fixed a synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes caused TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.

bugs.title: tmm can crash if a client-ssl profile is in use without a CRL
bugs.symptoms: TMM can crash if a client-ssl profile is in use without a certificate revocation list (CRL) configured.
bugs.conditions: A client-ssl profile is in use without a configured CRL, and the customer has an Engineering Hotfix installed that includes the fix for ID384451.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes if a client-ssl profile is in use without a certificate revocation list (CRL) configured.

bugs.title: Stats for legacy PVA connection flows are not relevant on ePVA platforms.
bugs.symptoms: The pva.tot_conns and pva.cur_conns in the virtual_server_stat tmstat table are used for stats for legacy PVA platforms with hardware only accelerated connection flows. In the current ePVA based platforms, all accelerated connection flows are counted as 'PVA assisted' flows, and the ePVA related stats are in the tot_pva_assist_conns and the curr_pva_assist_conns columns.
bugs.conditions: This applies when viewing pva.tot_conns and pva.cur_conns in the virtual_server_stat tmstat table on current ePVA based platforms.
bugs.impact: Stats for legacy PVA connection flows are not relevant on ePVA platforms, which might result in a bit of confusion when viewing virtual_server_stat table. However, the tmstat tables are not generally relevant for end users.
bugs.workaround: View tot_pva_assist_conns and curr_pva_assist_conns columns to view ePVA related stats.

bugs.title: Windows Phone 8.1 built-in browser is not properly detected by BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: Windows Phone 8.1 built-in browser is not properly detected by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Windows Phone 8.1 built-in browser.
bugs.impact: Built-in browser is not properly detected.
bugs.fix: Microsoft Windows Phone 8.1 built-in browser is now properly detected by the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Input handling error in GTM GUI
bugs.symptoms: Certain input sequences are not processed correctly in the GTM WebUI
bugs.conditions: GTM provisioned
bugs.impact: Incorrect output from GTM UI web pages
bugs.fix: Correctly process input in the GTM WebUI

bugs.title: Flaw in CSRF protection mechanism
bugs.symptoms: Flaw in Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection mechanism.
bugs.conditions: CSRF protection is configured.
bugs.impact: Flaw in Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection mechanism.
bugs.fix: Internal testing found and resolved a flaw in the CSRF mechanism

bugs.title: Custom X-forwarded-for headers should take prioriy over xff headers
bugs.symptoms: If a HTTP flow has both an X-Forwarded-For (XFF) header and a custom header containing the true client IP, the IP in the XFF header will take priority.
bugs.conditions: Both X-forwarded-for and custom headers are marked and used. A Request arrives with both X-forwarded-for and a custom header.
bugs.impact: wrong source IP is listed. May apply wrong irules, wrong ip intelligence etc.

bugs.title: Per-core and system CPU usage graphs do not match
bugs.symptoms: There are discrepancies between the per-core CPU usage graphs and the system CPU usage graph.
bugs.conditions: Normal running conditions.
bugs.impact: The system does not report the actual CPU usage. In some places the per-core usage is high while the system usage does not reflect that, and in other places the system usage is high, while the per-core usage is flat.
bugs.fix: System now reports matching CPU usage in the per-core CPU usage graphs and the system CPU usage graph.

bugs.title: full "/shared" filesystem prevents tmsh from running
bugs.symptoms: Example: [root@localhost:/S1-green-P:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh show sys hardware Unexpected Error: Can't create temp directory, /var/tmp/tmsh/DfRf5Z, errno 28] No space left on device
bugs.conditions: Typical activity that will fill up the "/shared" filesystem is storage of too many software images in "/shared/images", or leaving too many configuration archives in "/var/tmp". (/var/tmp is a symlink to /shared/tmp)
bugs.impact: The system cannot be managed.
bugs.workaround: Remove some files
bugs.fix: 'tmsh' remains functional even if the "/shared" filesystem is full.

bugs.title: VIPRION Host PIC firmware version 7.02 update
bugs.symptoms: Correctly report part numbers of current-manufacture VIPRION B4300 series blades (part numbers 400-0076-00 and 400-0077-00).
bugs.conditions: Affects VIPRION B4300 series blades.
bugs.impact: Features of current-manufacture VIPRION B4300 series blades (part numbers 400-0076-00 and 400-0077-00) may not be properly supported by the BIG-IP software.
bugs.fix: VIPRION Host PIC firmware version 7.02 update now supports all expected BIG-IP software features on VIPRION B4300 blades.

bugs.title: HTTP::respond in explicit proxy scenarios may cause TMM crash due to assert
bugs.symptoms: Use of HTTP::respond in HTTP_REQUEST iRule event in explicit proxy scenarios may cause TMM to assert and crash due to improper handling of HTTP::respond. HTTP:collect doesn't work properly in explicit proxy scenarios.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs with use of HTTP::respond or HTTP::collect in explicit proxy scenarios.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: HTTP::respond no longer asserts and HTTP::collect now works as expected when used from HTTP_REQUEST in explicit proxy scenarios.

bugs.title: The TMM may restart when processing single logout (SLO) messages.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP is configured as IdP and is processing SLO message from SP. Due to internal error, SAML metadata can get corrupted, and cause the TMM to restart.
bugs.conditions: Internal processing error.
bugs.impact: The TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, disable SLO on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Issue is fixed that caused TMM to occasionally restart when processing SLO messages.

bugs.title: Connections may hang until timeout if a LTM policy action failed
bugs.symptoms: When an LTM policy action that takes place during an HTTP request or response fails (which is very rare), the affected connection hangs until a timeout occurs.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when you attach an LTM policy to a virtual with a rule that has an action that fails. Now send a request that matches that rule. The command 'tmsh show ltm policy' will show the action failed, but the connection 'hangs' until timeout.
bugs.impact: When an LTM policy action fails, affected connections hang until they time out.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When an LTM policy action fails, the affected connection no longer hangs until timeout, but rather gets reset immediately.

bugs.title: Changing virtual server type from Standard to Performance (HTTP) can make it impossible to connect to VIP
bugs.symptoms: After changing TCP virtual server type from Standard to Performance (HTTP), it might no longer be possible to connect to previously working VIP. The connection to VIP will be silently dropped.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when changing a Standard TCP virtual server type to Performance (HTTP).
bugs.impact: Might not connect to the VIP, and results in the message: 'Connection timed out.'
bugs.workaround: Change virtual server type from Standard to Performance (Layer 4), then change type from Performance (Layer 4) to Performance (HTTP).
bugs.fix: Changing virtual server type from Standard to Performance (HTTP) now works as expected to connect to VIP.

bugs.title: APM OAM should be sending a single Cookie header with the cookies delimited by semi-colon.
bugs.symptoms: Authentication with OAM ObSSOCookie failed after the mutiple cookies added by APM EAM module was sent with a comma delimiter to separate them. EAM should be making a single Cookie header with the cookies delimited by semi-colon.
bugs.conditions: Authentication with OAM ObSSOCookie fails after multiple cookies added by APM EAM module are sent with comma delimiter to separate them.
bugs.impact: Authentication with OAM ObSSOCookie fails and user is required to authenticate again with credentials.
bugs.workaround: no workaround
bugs.fix: EAM used to send multiple cookies headers in HTTP message. Multiple HTTP headers like this are treated as comma-separated by some receivers. Now EAM adds a single Cookie header with the cookies delimited by semi-colon.

bugs.title: FastL4 with FIX late-bind enabled may not honor client-timeout
bugs.symptoms: When insufficient initial data is received, the FastL4 fix late-bind timeout recovery action is not taken (no RST sent with disconnection and no default pool use with fallback).
bugs.conditions: FastL4 profile with FIX late-bind enabled and insufficient data is received.
bugs.impact: The client-timeout feature does not work. Client connections seem to hang, and RST is not sent (when timeout-recovery disconnect) or the connection does not continue with standard FastL4 behavior (when timeout-recovery fallback) if enough initial data does not arrive within the client-timeout.
bugs.workaround: Setting tcp-handshake-timeout to a value that is greater than client-timeout might allow this to work.
bugs.fix: FastL4 with FIX late-bind enabled now honors client-timeout.

bugs.title: Plugin based endpoint checking clients do not work with Chrome and Firefox
bugs.symptoms: Because of browser restrictions, F5 Networks' VPN and endpoint checking client do not work on Chrome and Firefox browsers.
bugs.conditions: Chrome or Firefox is used to connect to APM -Access policy contains client side end point checks -User attempts to launch VPN from these browsers
bugs.impact: In first case, access policy will fail. In second case, VPN cannot be launched from browser.
bugs.workaround: Use Internet Explorer.
bugs.fix: This release of APM contains web clients based on newer architecture which does not use plugins. These clients are launched using URL scheme, so they now work with Chrome and Firefox as well as Internet Explorer.

bugs.title: BCM56xxd might restart due to parity errors
bugs.symptoms: The TMOS daemon bcm56xxd may restart due to parity errors.
bugs.conditions: Under rare conditions, the bcm56xxd process may restart due to parity errors. This issue only affects the following hardware platforms: BIG-IP 6900 (D104) BIG-IP 8900 (D106) BIG-IP 8950 (D107) BIG-IP 11000 (E101) BIG-IP 11050 (E102) BIG-IP 5000 series (C109) BIG-IP 7000 series (D110) BIG-IP 10000s/10050s/10200v/10250v (D113) VIPRION blade B2100 (A109) VIPRION blade B2150 (A113) VIPRION blade B2250 (A112) VIPRION blade B4100 (A100) VIPRION blade B4200 (A107) VIPRION blade B4300 (A108) VIPRION blade B4340N (A110) Note: The bcm56xxd process is the switch driver daemon for the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: bcm56xxd re-initializes the internal switch, which might briefly affect data traffic. The system might report memory parity errors in different tables within bcm56xxd by posting log messages similar to the following: info bcm56xxd[8127]: 012c0016:6: unit 0 L2_ENTRY_ONLY entry 120673 parity error. -- info bcm56xxd[8127]: 012c0012:6: Exiting on parity errors. -- notice mcpd[7108]: 01070406:5: Removed publication with publisher id BCM56xxPublisher. -- info bcm56xxd: 012c0013:6: BCM56xxd starting. debug=0, foreground=1, packet=1, bcm_debug=0x7, soc_debug=0x0 The following types of messages may be logged if a parity error is detected by the broadcom chip in an area that is not used by user data. These type of errors will not trigger a driver restart, and are not user impacting, however they can generate a large number of log entries. F5 recommend rebooting the device to clear this state 012c0016:6: unit 0 FP_TCAM entry 1127 TCAM parity error 012c0016:6: unit 0 SER parity failure without valid count soc_xgs3_mem_dma: EGR_SERVICE_COUNTER_TABLE_X.epipe0 failed(NAK)

bugs.title: Failed to load config after removing peer from sync-only group
bugs.symptoms: Load sys config fails.
bugs.conditions: Loading config after removing peer from sync-only device group.
bugs.impact: Failed to load config.
bugs.workaround: Remove peer device from the sync-only device group on which policy sync has been performed previously.
bugs.fix: A user can now load sys config even after removing the peer from the sync-only group.

bugs.title: Fixed routing table management for cases when 2 or more interfaces are used
bugs.symptoms: Some routes are not restored correctly if the system has 2 or more network interfaces.
bugs.conditions: Interface is only affected if: 1) Not used for Network Access connection. 2) Physically UP at the start of test. 3) Physically brought DOWN before connecting to Network Access. 4) Physically brought UP again after Network Access is disconnected.
bugs.impact: Some routes are not restored correctly.
bugs.fix: Improved routing table management for two or more network interfaces.

bugs.title: HTTP caching configured in a Web Acceleration profile may dispatch internal messages out-of-order, leading to assert
bugs.symptoms: HTTP caching configured in a Web Acceleration profile may dispatch internal messages out-of-order, leading to assert
bugs.conditions: Assert may occur when the following conditions are met: - Virtual server has HTTP caching configured in a Web Acceleration profile. - Virtual server has mirroring enabled. - Device is in standby mode. - Active unit is unable to fulfill incoming HTTP request (ramcache entry is invalid / no pool members). - Standby unit is able to fulfill mirrored request (ramcache entry is valid).
bugs.impact: Due to this rarely occurring race condition, a tmm_panic occurs ('valid pcb') when a connection is being closed and the ramcache feature is able fulfill an incoming request. Standby unit becomes temporarily unavailable.
bugs.workaround: Do not use connection mirroring when HTTP caching is configured in a Web Acceleration.
bugs.fix: HTTP caching configured in a Web Acceleration profile no longer dispatches internal messages out-of-order, leading to assert.

bugs.title: BD crash when trying to report attack signatures
bugs.symptoms: The Enforcer rarely crashes when logging attack signatures.
bugs.conditions: A rare issue that happens suddenly when reporting attack signatures to the logs.
bugs.impact: Traffic resets, failover.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue that rarely caused the Enforcer to crash when logging attack signatures.

bugs.title: AWS - VE is locked out after live install on 2nd slot.
bugs.symptoms: SSH access might be blocked on VE (launched in AWS) after live install on 2nd slot is performed and VE is booted to 2nd slot.
bugs.conditions: VE running in AWS Live install performed on 2nd slot and VE is booted to it.
bugs.impact: SSH access to the box might be lost. It's effectively locked out since there is no console access to this VM.
bugs.fix: The public key for ssh access is obtained from AWS metadata service on 1st boot.

bugs.title: Now tag end is determined correctly in case of dynamically created content.
BD may crash when enabling Base64 Decoding on Wildcard cookie
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.conditions: Enabling Base64 Decoding on Wildcard cookie.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.fix: The Enforcer no longer crashes when Base64 Decoding is enabled on a wildcard cookie.

bugs.title: Session Awareness: Requests are reset
bugs.symptoms: Long Requests (greater than 10 MB) are being reset.
bugs.conditions: 1. Send traffic of long requests (greater than 10 MB) 2. enable Session Awareness with log all requests is enabled for a session.
bugs.impact: Long Requests (greater than 10 MB) are being reset.
bugs.fix: Requests are no longer reset when session awareness is enabled, log all requests is enabled for a session, and a large POST request (greater than 10 MB) is sent when the "buffer exceed max length" violation is disabled.

bugs.title: 'tmsh load /sys config from-terminal' (or from file) with a reference to an external file fails
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh load /sys config from-terminal" or "tmsh load /sys config file' for objects that have references to external files (such as external monitors, ifiles, SSL certs, data groups) will fail.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running the command 'tmsh load /sys config from-terminal' or 'tmsh load /sys config from-terminal' on an object that references a file external to the configuration (using source-path or cache-path).
bugs.impact: The system posts an error similar to: Failed: name (/Common/external_monitor_name) cache path expected to be non empty. This error prevents using cut and paste to configure certain configuration objects.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can add the appropriate stanzas to the bigip.conf file manually and do a full load of the configuration, upload the external files individually through the GUI, or use the 'tmsh create sys file' command.

bugs.title: Improved Hot Fix installation.
SSL stream throughput slows down when hardware SSL offloading is in use
bugs.symptoms: When performing LAN-speed transfers of large files (hundreds of MB) over SSL, or transfers of small ssl records, the throughput speed of the transfer significantly drops if the hardware SSL offloading is performed. The performance drop is from ~30% - ~50% depending on the cipher suite used.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when hardware SSL offloading is turned on.
bugs.impact: The performance degrades from ~30% - ~50% depending on the cipher suite used.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can modify the High-Speed Bridge (HSB) scheduler. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system. Modifying the scheduler.hsbpollmode.ltm db key Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: tmsh To set the db key value to always, type the following command: modify /sys db scheduler.hsbpollmode.ltm value always Save the changes by typing the following command: save /sys config

bugs.title: Inband monitor does not mark pool member offline as expected
bugs.symptoms: The inband monitor might not cause pool members/pools to be marked offline after the expected number of failures.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server with an inband monitor.
bugs.impact: Traffic might be disrupted for a longer-than-expected period of time after a pool member goes offline. The issue might be more readily apparent when there is only one pool member.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Edge Client may hang for sometime when disconnecting from Firepass server
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client hangs in "Disconnecting" state for some time if the backend server is FirePass.
bugs.conditions: FirePass server as backend
bugs.impact: User has to wait
bugs.fix: Issue fixed. Now BIG-IP Edge Client disconnects from FirePass smoothly without delays.

bugs.title: APM does not support Microsoft Remote Desktop 8.0.8 client for iOS to work using APM as RD Gateway.
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support Microsoft Remote Desktop 8.0.8 client for iOS to work using APM as RD Gateway.
bugs.conditions: Using Microsoft Remote Desktop 8.0.8 client.
bugs.impact: iOS client does not work when using APM as RD Gateway.
bugs.workaround: priority 1 when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::header rdg-client-generation] == "iOS=1" } { HTTP::respond 404 TCP::close event disable all } }
bugs.fix: Support Microsoft Remote Desktop 8.0.8 client for iOS to work using APM as RD Gateway.

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client crashes on OS X 10.7 if a user adds new server using its IP address rather than DNS name
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac crashes on OS X 10.7 if a user adds a new server using its IP address rather than its DNS name.
bugs.conditions: Create an APM virtual server IP address using the Edge Client for Mac
bugs.impact: Edge Client crashes
bugs.workaround: Use DNS name rather than IP address when adding a new server.
bugs.fix: On BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac on OS X 10.7, a user can successfully add a new server using IP address.

bugs.title: TCP Server MSS option is ignored in verified accept mode
bugs.symptoms: After enabling 'verified-accept' in the TCP profile, window scaling is not working on server side connection. More specifically, the BIG-IP system ignores window scaling from the back-end server.
bugs.conditions: Enabling 'verified-accept' in TCP profile.
bugs.impact: the BIG-IP system ignores window scaling from the back-end server.
bugs.workaround: Disable 'verified-accept' in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: Window scaling with back-end server now works when 'verified-accept' is enabled in the TCP profile.

bugs.title: Adding SR-IOV and VLAN tagging in the F5 VE with Emulex NIC
bugs.symptoms: SR-IOV and VLAN tagging were not supported for Emulex NICs prior version 11.5.1. The underlying NIC driver from Emulex lacked such support.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when VE running on host with Emulex NICs.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is no SR-IOV and VLAN tagging support.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The latest Emulex NIC driver was included in 11.5.1-HF5. It supports SR-IOV and VLAN tagging when Emulex NICs are used.

bugs.title: In APM OAM authentication, ObSSOCookie _lastUseTime was not updated.
bugs.symptoms: _lastUseTime in APM OAM ObSSOCookie is not updated after the user is authenticated using ObSSOCookie. This results in ObSSOCookie expiring prematurely.
bugs.conditions: User is already authenticated and provided with an ObSSOCookie.
bugs.impact: With ObSSOCookie gets expired prematurely and authentication with ObSSOCookie fails, User is asked to submit credentials for authentication.
bugs.workaround: No known workaround
bugs.fix: Issue Fixed. _lastUseTime in OAM ObSSOCookie is updated on successful authentication and authorization process.

bugs.title: notice HA: ha_enabled_put(daemon_heartbeat, tmm, FALSE/TRUE)
bugs.symptoms: On VIPRION B2250 and B4300/B4340N blades, you might encounter log entries of this type: notice HA: ha_enabled_put(daemon_heartbeat, tmm, FALSE): error 01140012 or notice HA: ha_enabled_put(daemon_heartbeat, tmm, TRUE): error 01140012.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only on VIPRION B2250, B4300, B4340N blades.
bugs.impact: The system posts the error messages. These messages are benign and can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: TMM generates a core file when dynamically loading a shared library.
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to dynamically link a shared library, TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: Dynamically loading more than a certain number of shared libraries will result in a tmm core.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Invalid attempt to free TMM memory is ignored.

bugs.title: Brute Force end attack operation mode reported as blocking while it was actually in transparent mode
bugs.symptoms: When the Brute-Force attack_status ended log message appear - the operation mode changed to Blocking even though he has set it as Alarm on the configuration.
bugs.conditions: When brute force configured to work in Transparent mode
bugs.impact: False reporting during Transparent Brute Force attack.
bugs.fix: Brute force reporting: The brute force reported operation mode (Transparent or Blocking) is now the same when the attack starts and ends. Previously, sometimes the system would change the operation mode logged when the attack ended.

bugs.title: Bypass unicode validation on XML and JSON profiles by internal parameter
bugs.symptoms: Some UTF-8 characters in JSON data can result in the "Malformed JSON data" violation.
bugs.conditions: JSON and UTF-8 handling -- There are applications that use unicode characters that are not mapped as allowed by the ASM XML/JSON parser.
bugs.impact: The ASM identified properly formatted JSON data as malformed.
bugs.fix: So that you can bypass unicode validation on XML and JSON profiles, we added two internal parameters: - relax_unicode_in_xml: The default is 0 which is the current behavior. When the value is changed to 1, a bad unicode character does not produce an XML malformed violation. A bad unicode character might be a legal unicode character that does not appear in the mapping of the system's XML parser. - relax_unicode_in_json: The default is 0 which is the current behavior. When the value is changed to 1, a bad unicode character does not produce a JSON malformed violation. A bad unicode character might be a legal unicode character that does not appear in the mapping of the system's JSON parser.

bugs.title: False positive malformed json on legitimate unicode character
bugs.symptoms: A malformed json violation is reported on legitimate json payload.
bugs.conditions: A unicode character that is not mapped in the json parser arrives with the payload.
bugs.impact: False positive violation, which might block a legitimate transaction.

bugs.title: tmm crash on uninitialized variable
bugs.symptoms: tmm occasionally crashes when server_key and client_key variables are not initialized before being used.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using an FTP virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes when server_key and client_key variables are uninitialized.

bugs.title: Tmrouted restarted after a series of creating/deleting route domains and adding/deleting protocols due to seg fault
bugs.symptoms: When multiple route domains and multiple routing protocols per route domain are repeatedly created and deleted, the tmrouted crashes and restarts.
bugs.conditions: multiple route domains with multiple routing protocols per each route domain are created and deleted repeatedly in a short time intervals.
bugs.impact: The routing information is lost and the tables need to be built again. This might cause packet loss.
bugs.fix: Repeated creation and deletion of route domains and routing protocols led to a race condition between the start timer of the routing protocols and inconsistent memory state of the deleted routing protocols. This fix resolves the race condition.

bugs.title: TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, crash
bugs.symptoms: Synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.
bugs.conditions: Using AVR.
bugs.impact: TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Resolved an issue leading to tmm core when multiple modules, including ASM, APM, AFM, ADM and AVR, are provisioned.

bugs.title: DHE-RSA-AES256-SHA256 and DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 should only be supported for tls1.2
bugs.symptoms: DHE-RSA-AES256-SHA256 and DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 are visible for other protocols, but are only supported for TLS1.2.
bugs.conditions: These should only show up under TLS1.2 but they are visible for other protocols.
bugs.impact: Selecting these might have unexpected results.
bugs.fix: Resolved issue to ensure that DHE-RSA-AES256-SHA256 and DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 is supported only for TLS1.2.

bugs.title: BFD IPv6 session display command in IMI shell display the wrong remote port number.
bugs.symptoms: 'show bfd session detail' command displays the wrong BFD port number of 13784 or 14784 for IPv6 BFD sessions. This is a cosmetic issue. TMM uses the correct port numbers of 3784 or 4784 for single/multihop sessions respectively.
bugs.conditions: BFD configured using IPv6 addresses. Display session state via IMI shell command 'show bfd session detail'
bugs.impact: Wrong port number is displayed. No functional impact as the right port numbers are used.

bugs.title: WAM Range HTTP header limited to 8 ranges
bugs.symptoms: When doing a request with multiple ranges, depending on the current state of the document in the cache (due to previous requests), WAM responds with 'HTTP 416 Requested range not satisfiable'.
bugs.conditions: Client requesting more than 8 ranges in a single HTTP Range request for a document that has an active cache record.
bugs.impact: Document is not possible retrieve, even with valid range values.
bugs.workaround: Force the document to not be cached in the Policy and to be always proxied to the OWS.
bugs.fix: Use db variable Wam.Cache.Range.MaxRanges to increase the number of max allowed sub-ranges in a HTTP range request. It defaults to a maximum of 8 sub-ranges, however it can be increased up to 32.

bugs.title: SSL accelerator card does not function on the BIG-IP 12250 platform.
bugs.symptoms: SSL accelerator card does not function on the BIG-IP 12250 platform.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP 12250 platforms running 11.6.0 hf1.
bugs.impact: SSL acceleration does not work.
bugs.fix: SSL acceleration support is now present for the BIG-IP 12250 platform.

bugs.title: Occasional inability to cache optimized PDFs and images
bugs.symptoms: Restarting the datastor service can result in some optimized PDFs or optimized images becoming un-cacheable
bugs.conditions: If WAM has a handle to cached content in datastor which no longer exists because datastor restarted or evicted it, and if this content is an image or PDF which WAM optimized, and if two requests for such content arrive on the same TCP connection, the second can get incorrectly cached such that it can not be served or replaced until tmm is restarted.
bugs.impact: Certain URLs become uncacheable, thus reducing effectiveness of WAM.
bugs.workaround: Disable client keep-alive in the HTTP profile (change Maximum Requests in the HTTP profile from 0 to 1) or disable PDF linearization and image optimization. A partial workaround is to use wa_clear_cache instead of restarting datastor to clear the cache. Content which datastor evicts might still suffer (but this is unlikely).
bugs.fix: Restarting datastor no longer results in the possibility of some optimized PDFs or optimized images becoming uncacheable.

bugs.title: Use true timeout instead of retries limit in when to give up initializing FIPS device, and subsequently power cycle the unit to recover FIPS device.
SSL handshake delay when SSL mirroring enabled or mirrored connection fails to recover after failover.
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake delay when SSL mirroring enabled, or mirrored connection fails to recover after failover.
bugs.conditions: Mirroring enabled on TCP virtual server.
bugs.impact: - SSL handshake delayed for 80% of SSL handshake timeout. - Mirrored connection fails to recover after failover. - In rare situations the SSL handshake might be delayed after the ClientHello is transmitted or a mirrored connection may fail to recover after failover.
bugs.workaround: Set connection.syncookies.threshold (or, in the GUI, SYN Check Activation Threshold) to 0 and enable hardware syncookies in the TCP profile.

bugs.title: mcpd core during sync
bugs.symptoms: mcpd can run out of memory and core when a device in a sync group is sending an extremely high volume of sync messages.
bugs.conditions: The exact cause of this is unknown, and it has been seen very rarely with a large sync in a sync group. Large incremental syncs could be a symptom of other things happening between the devices which could trigger the core.
bugs.impact: mcpd cores and restarts if it runs out or memory. Only through inspection of the core file can this condition be detected.

bugs.title: ePVA FIX: no RST for an unaccelerated flow targeting a network virtual
bugs.symptoms: A network virtual server configured with guaranteed acceleration fails to receive a RST for a flow that is not accelerated. They see a RST when targeting a host virtual. This results in the client sending packet retransmissions continuously, since the client has no indication that the connection was closed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with guaranteed latency.
bugs.impact: The system drops flows.
bugs.fix: The system now sends RST in guaranteed mode for an ePVA flow when the packet is received in software.

bugs.title: fastL4: acceleration state is incorrectly reported on show sys conn
bugs.symptoms: The results of the command show sys conn shows both-sides of two connections are accelerated, which means there should be four accelerated flows. But the ePVA accelerated flow count only shows three accelerated flows, which is what is expected with this combination of IP/port addresses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using FastL4 and acceleration.
bugs.impact: The system reports incorrect status.
bugs.fix: The system now updates accelerated status after the flow has been successfully inserted into the ePVA, so the correct state is reported.

bugs.title: TMM may panic when resuming DNS_REQUEST iRule event
bugs.symptoms: TMM panic when executing DNS_REQUEST event.
bugs.conditions: The TMM panics when the following events have occurred: - DNS_RESPONSE event has been suspended. - DNS_REQUEST event is executed.
bugs.impact: TMM restart.
bugs.fix: In this release, the system clears suspended iRules that have failed before executing new events.

bugs.title: Set active fails after accept learning suggestion for illegal metachar Policy with encoding iso-8859-1
bugs.symptoms: The GUI reports the following error: Could not apply configuration; Set active failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Policy is configured for an application language like iso-8859-1 or iso-8859-15. -- Learning suggestions that stem from multi byte UTF-8 parameter values (Illegal Meta Character in Value) are accepted.
bugs.impact: Set active fails. Policy changes cannot be applied.
bugs.workaround: Go to Parameters list and for each parameter with override 'Allow' for the metachar 'ÿ' remove the override completely: choose the override, click on '>>' and click on update.

bugs.title: User logged in as Auditor can't view SAML IdP configuration data; Edit button greyed out.
bugs.symptoms: A user that is logged in as Auditor cannot view SAML Identity Provider (IdP) configuration data; the Edit button is not available.
bugs.conditions: This happens to users that are not authorized and to any user in the partition "All [Read Only]".
bugs.impact: User cannot view object details in read-only mode only.
bugs.workaround: The user can view read-only object details using tmsh commands.
bugs.fix: Show Edit button' label as 'View', on login of user with out write permission.

bugs.title: Suspended DNS_RESPONSE events are not resumed
bugs.symptoms: iRules that cause the DNS_RESPONSE event to suspend will not be resumed.
bugs.conditions: DNS_RESPONSE event with command that causes it to be suspended.
bugs.impact: DNS_RESPONSE event does not complete execution.
bugs.workaround: Do not use iRule commands in DNS_RESPONSE event that result in suspension.
bugs.fix: DNS_RESPONSE events are now resumed after suspension.

bugs.title: TMM can crash if receiving radius start or stop messages with multiple IP but no subscriber ID.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes if the radius start/stop messages received have multiple IP addresses but have no subscriber ID.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: Receiving radius start or stop messages; the radius message has multiple IP addresses listed; and the radius message dose not have subscriber ID.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After the fix, TMM does not crash if receiving the radius message specified in the above condition

bugs.title: ZebOS using BGP ECMP may not correctly update the ECMP paths when one of the paths goes down and comes back up
bugs.symptoms: ZebOS using BGP equal-cost multi-path routing (ECMP) might not correctly update the ECMP paths when one of the paths goes down and comes back up.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a downstream ECMP link is disabled such that one of the two equal-cost paths becomes unavailable, and is then enable.
bugs.impact: ECMP does not function as desired because both available paths are not utilized. This can only be recovered by clearing the BGP connection on the affected ECMP path.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
APM IPv6 Network Access connection may fail in some cases
bugs.symptoms: When the client provided link local address contains zeros for first 4+ bytes, the IPv6 Network Access connection will fail due to listener bind failure.
bugs.conditions: When the first 4+ bytes of IPv6 Link Local address are zeros this bug will show up.
bugs.impact: IPv6 Network Access Tunnels may not succeed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this.
bugs.fix: For a certain set of IPv6 link local addresses, the IPv6 Network Access tunnel may not succeed due to listener lookup failure. This code change fixes this issue.

bugs.title: Restored the proper behavior, which is the correct error messages being returned.
Shun-global category initially created for global shun enforcement, is no longer present.
Resolved issue found by internal F5 testing in shun processing to make system more reliable for customers.
When ICAP cuts off request payload, OneConnect does not drop the connection
bugs.symptoms: After sending an ICAP preview, the BIG-IP system waits for a response from the ICAP server. If the BIG-IP system receives the complete ICAP response before it has completed sending the ICAP request (for example, when the response contains an encapsulated 302 redirect), it stops sending the request payload and closes the TCP connection. However when a OneConnect profile (CONNPOOL filter) is on the IVS, the TCP connection to the ICAP server is not terminated.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Using ICAP and OneConnect profiles on an IVS. -- The BIG-IP ICAP client has resumed sending the request body on receiving a 200-OK response after the preview. -- ICAP server response completes before it has received the entire request body (for example, encapsulated redirect).
bugs.impact: The ICAP server cannot detect the end of the ICAP request so might get confused.
bugs.workaround: Do not use OneConnect. As an alternative, if the ICAP server completes its response, it could ignore any further input from the client until it detects another RESPMOD or REQMOD indicating the beginning of a new transaction. ICAP servers are not required to do this, but it would allow connection reuse in the case where the server completes its response before the request is complete.
bugs.fix: In this release, if the BIG-IP system receives the complete ICAP response from the ICAP server before it has completed sending the ICAP request, and a OneConnect profile is on the IVS, the TCP connection to the ICAP server is terminated and that connection is not reused.

bugs.title: App type 0 session Update Failed on PEMDB: ERR_INPROGRESS
bugs.symptoms: The log "App type 0 session Update Failed on PEMDB: ERR_INPROGRESS" shows up even the log level is set to Critical, it should be logged at debug log level.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under normal PEM operation, and is part of PEM debug logging.
bugs.impact: This log is for debugging, it can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: Adjusted Logging levels to remove potentialy confusing messages.

bugs.title: Deleting multiple VXLAN tunnels with flooding type multipoint can cause TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: Deleting multiple VXLAN tunnels with flooding type multipoint can cause TMM restart.
bugs.conditions: Deleting multiple VXLAN tunnels with flooding type multipoint.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and a TMM core is generated.
bugs.fix: No TMM restart when deleting multiple VXLAN tunnels with flooding type multipoint.

bugs.title: TMM may crash in SSL
bugs.symptoms: When SSL is configured in TMM, a crash might occur if events happen in a specific (unknown) order.
bugs.conditions: ClientSSL is configured on a virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The TMM exit and restart that occurred in certain circumstances when processing SSL traffic has been fixed.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
Dual management routes in the main routing table
bugs.symptoms: Dual management routes might exist in the default routing table, main. On version 11.6.0, the the system also produces an error message when querying SNMP ipCidrRouteTable.
bugs.conditions: In versions earlier that 11.6.0, conditions are unknown other than observing the dual management routes in the main routing table. On version 11.6.0, the condition is snmpwalking ipCidrRouteTable.
bugs.impact: On affected versions earlier than 11.6.0, there are dual management routes in the main routing table. On version 11.6.0, you might also receive an error upon querying SNMP ipCidrRouteTable and/or snmpd core.
bugs.workaround: To recover from this issue, delete the duplicate route.
bugs.fix: The main routing table now has a single entry for the management network.

bugs.title: Only one of several VMware View Desktop/Application pools with the same display name can be launched from APM Webtop
bugs.symptoms: Only one of several VMware View Desktop/Application pools with the same display name can be launched from APM Webtop.
bugs.conditions: Configuration with VMware View Desktop/Application pools with the same display name.
bugs.impact: Only one of several VMware View Desktop/Application pools with the same display name can be launched.
bugs.workaround: Use unique display names for VMware View Desktop/Application pools.
bugs.fix: All of VMware View Desktop/Application pools with the same display name can now be launched from APM Webtop.

bugs.title: Occasional crash when SSL session mirroring is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, when SSL session mirroring is enabled, TMM will crash.
bugs.conditions: unknown
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: OSPFv3 session gets stuck in loading state
bugs.symptoms: When running tmsh ipv6 ospf neighbor, you see one or more neighbors stuck at Loading. Other adjacent network equipment might report the neighbor at Full.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using OSPFv3
bugs.impact: Neighbor discovery fails to complete
bugs.fix: OSPFv3 sessions no longer get stuck in loading state.

bugs.title: Simultaneous stats query and pool configuration change results in process exit on secondary.
bugs.symptoms: Simultaneous stats query and pool configuration change results in process exit on secondary.
bugs.conditions: Running parallel operations in tmsh/GUI or multiple tmsh operations on pool objects. For example, running 'tmsh show' command while simultaneously updating the monitor on the pool in the GUI.
bugs.impact: The primary restarts, and the slot goes down, resulting in potential traffic impact. The ltm logs display error messages similar to the following: -- err mcpd[29041]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020036:3: The requested pool (/Common/CYBS-P-UBC-43) was not found. -- notice mcpd[8487]: 0107092a:5: Secondary slot 1 disconnected.
bugs.workaround: Use the absolute name of the pool in the tmsh command: /partition_name/pool_name.
bugs.fix: TMSH command now automatically issues the absolute path by using the context for the current connection to MCPd, so there are no MCPd restarts in this case.

bugs.title: iQuery connection resets every 24 hours
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP GTM iQuery connections may reset during Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) key renegotiation. -- Virtual servers are temporarily marked down once every 24 hours. -- In the /var/log/gtm file, you observe messages that appear similar to the following example: - iqmgmt_receive: SSL error:140940E5:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:ssl handshake failure - err gtmd[10767]: 011ae0fa:3: iqmgmt_receive: SSL error: error:140940E5:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:ssl handshake failure (336150757) - alert gtmd[10767]: 011a500c:1: SNMP_TRAP: Box 10.20.30.1 state change green --> red (Box 10.20.30.1 on Unavailable)
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: -- SSL renegotiation occurs during an iQuery connection. The big3d process will attempt to renegotiate SSL keys every 24 hours. However, when the BIG-IP GTM system receives the SSL Client Hello message during renegotiation, the big3d process responds with a TCP FIN and closes the connection rather than renegotiating the session.
bugs.impact: Resources monitored by the BIG-IP GTM system are temporarily marked down until the iQuery connection is reestablished. Note: This is a subtly different issue from the one (with a very similar error, 140940F5 vs 140940E5) described in Bug ID 679316: iQuery connections reset during SSL renegotiation :: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID679316.html. A BIG-IP system affected by this bug ID477240 might also be affected by ID679316, for which there is no fix.
bugs.fix: SSL properly renegotiates rather than terminates connections when the session expires.

bugs.title: Fixed crash in mcpq with bad user input
Improved XML Parsing
bugs.symptoms: With certain requests, XML parsing improperly returns the incorrect document.
bugs.conditions: A certain set of parameters are sent to pages which utilize DocumentBuilderFactory to process and return XML documents.
bugs.impact: The document that was requested is not returned. Another document is returned instead.
bugs.fix: XML Parser configuration was changed to ensure only correct documents are returned to all requests.

bugs.title: Fixes possible segfault
