bugs.symptoms: When generic message is configured with the message parser disabled and messages are pushed to the outgoing connection faster than it is able to receive them, a segfault may occur.
bugs.conditions: When generic message is configured with the message parser disabled and messages are pushed to the outgoing connection faster than it is able to receive them.
bugs.impact: Segfault occurs.
bugs.workaround: None known
bugs.fix: Fixed the segfault that occurred in generic message when a HUDEVT_SENT is received and the parser is disabled.

bugs.title: SASP Monitor may core
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, the SASP monitor cores.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the SASP monitor is configured in push mode.
bugs.impact: When the monitor cores, a pool member gets marked down, which might lead to an outage. This occurs rarely.
bugs.fix: SASP monitor no longer cores when configured in push mode.

bugs.title: LTM might reset and cause out-of-ports
bugs.symptoms: Passive FTP using FTP range iRule might intermittently cause out-of-ports reset.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using passive FTP with an range of FTP ports in an iRule.
bugs.impact: LTM resets.
bugs.fix: Passive FTP using FTP range iRule no longer causes out-of-ports reset.

bugs.title: Phishing referrer checks are now performed in requests to all URLs, including those ones that are not configured as protected URLs.
Malware alerts are no longer sent from phishing sites when the domain does not match the expected domain of the virtual server.
Roll forward from 11.3.0 with iApp configured fails to load correctly and causes bd to core
bugs.symptoms: ts_debug.log: ----------- asm|INFO|Aug 14 19:10:41.710|12226|,,MCP Validation error - 010715bd:3: The parent folder is owned by application service (/Common/SharePoint.app/SharePoint), the object ownership cannot be changed to (). -----------
bugs.conditions: This occurs after committing the Database changes, but the system then rolls back the UCS files under /ts/var/account. This can occur on a config roll forward from 11.3.0 and earlier to a later version.
bugs.impact: this causes an inconsistency for the files BD will expect when starting, and lead to BD coring. The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic as it recovers from BD restarting.
bugs.workaround: Disable ASM for iApps before upgrade, and then re-enable.
bugs.fix: We fixed an error that caused the Enforcer to crash if you tried to roll forward a system configuration containing an iApp (application service) from version 11.3.0 or earlier.

bugs.title: APM client improved to support 2 interface connected to the same network segment
bugs.symptoms: APM client was not able to re-connect automatically on a system with 2 or more interfaces connected to the same network segment. This happens when physical interface get disconnected. User had to wait for a few minutes (or manually press disconnect and then connect button) to restore VPN connection.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a system has two or more interfaces connected to the same network segment.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the client is unable to reconnect automatically.
bugs.workaround: Manually press disconnect and then connect button to restore VPN connection.
bugs.fix: Client modified to restore routing table state and select active interface (on a system connected to the same network segment through multiple interfaces).

bugs.title: Wrong HTML rewriting at client side for very special case
bugs.symptoms: HTML attributes may be handled incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: Attributes with names that include a hyphen (-) are concatenated with legal event names. For example: <some_tag aaa-onclick=zzzz> <some_tag1 onclick-bbb=yyyy>
bugs.impact: This issue affects web application functionality.
bugs.fix: HTML Attributes with names that include a hyphen (-) are now handled correctly in Portal Access.

bugs.title: Enable ssh for admin account and disable ssh for root account for Amazon deployments
bugs.symptoms: Amazon's recent requirement was to disable ssh access for root account. All the management on the AWS instance should be done through different account using ssh.
bugs.conditions: Amazon AWS environment.
bugs.impact: There will be no root access for VMs from next Amazon Market release. The replacement is admin account. All management functionality will be available by ssh-in using admin account.
bugs.fix: F5 disabled ssh for root account for VMs in Amazon cloud (after Amazon mandated it). F5 enabled ssh permissions for built-in admin account. The default shell for admin account is tmsh (instead of bash). On all new Amazon deployments all management tasks should be done through admin account.
bugs.behavior: There will be no root access for VMs from next Amazon Market release. The replacement is admin account. All management functionality will be available by ssh-in using admin account.

bugs.title: 'ACCESS::policy evaluate' iRule command causes crash of apmd daemon
bugs.symptoms: Call of the ACCESS::policy evaluate iRule command in affected builds causes crash of APDM daemon.
bugs.impact: As a result, access policy evaluation cannot be initiated from iRules.
bugs.fix: APMD no longer crashes with null Tcl interpreter object when used with the ACCESS::policy evaluate iRule command.

bugs.title: Resource Assign Agent shows javascript error
bugs.symptoms: When opening full resource assign, users encounter the following error while trying to edit the Visual Policy Editor (VPE): "Error While creating agent class (pCustomRAMapping_class is not defined)"
bugs.conditions: Attempt to edit resource assign.
bugs.impact: Unable to edit resource assign.
bugs.workaround: Edit bigip.conf directly.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 support.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP's http/2 support is not compatible with draft-14
bugs.conditions: The IETF released draft-14, BIG-IP is compatible with draft-13.
bugs.impact: None known.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 supports IETF HTTP-WG http2-draft-14.

bugs.title: Valid iRule command FLOWTABLE::limit gets rejected when virtual server or route domain name is not specified
bugs.symptoms: An iRule cannot be saved with the following valid iRule commands: FLOWTABLE::limit virtual FLOWTABLE::limit route_domain
bugs.conditions: Saving an iRule
bugs.impact: iRule cannot be saved.
bugs.workaround: Use the following commands instead: FLOWTABLE::limit virtual [virtual name] FLOWTABLE::limit route_domain [ROUTE::domain]
bugs.fix: An iRule using the following commands can now be saved: FLOWTABLE::limit virtual FLOWTABLE::limit route_domain

bugs.title: ICMP monitor does not work on DAG Round Robin enabled VLANs
bugs.symptoms: ICMP monitor does not work on the VLANs with DAG Round Robin set to enabled.
bugs.conditions: For a VLAN, the DAG Round Robin option is enabled.
bugs.impact: ICMP monitor will be down.
bugs.workaround: Utilize another monitor or disable the DAG Round Robin option.
bugs.fix: Apply DAG Round Robin to icmp echo only.

bugs.title: Portal Access rewriting leads to page reload in Firefox
bugs.symptoms: Endless page reload after Portal Access rewriting in Firefox.
bugs.conditions: Browser is Firefox; there is an expression similar to "location.hash = ''" in the Javascript code.
bugs.impact: Customer cannot access page with Firefox.
bugs.workaround: An iRule, which changes javascript code from {location.hash = ''} to {location.hash = '#'}. Note that such iRule should be written for specific application, that's why there's no generic solution in this section.
bugs.fix: In Portal Access assignment of empty string to location.hash property no longer causes page reload loop in Firefox.

bugs.title: HSB v2.3.12.1 bitstream integrated to fix HSB firmware issues
bugs.symptoms: There exist some HSB firmware issues in BIG-IP software versions running HSB bitstream versions earlier than v2.3.12.1.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION C2400 chassis, the 2000-series platforms, and B2250 blades using HSB bitstream versions earlier than v2.3.12.1.
bugs.impact: Firmware issues.
bugs.fix: An updated HSB bitstream is included in BIG-IP software version 11.6.0 HF2 and later.

bugs.title: Detail missing from power supply 'Bad' status log messages
bugs.symptoms: When an internal hardware sensor alert is received indicating a 'Bad' power supply status, no detail is included which indicates which characteristic of the power supply's state is resulting in a 'Bad' overall status for the power supply. In this scenario, the message logged at default logging level contains information similar to the following: ... crit chmand[...]: 012a0013:2: Blade 0 hardware sensor critical alarm: Power Supply 2 GPIO status(SPAFFIV03G): Bad
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP 2000-/4000-/5000-/7000-/10000-series appliances or VIPRION B2100-/B2200-series blades, in which one or more installed power supplies triggers an internal hardware sensor alert indicating a 'Bad' power supply status.
bugs.impact: Unable to diagnose cause of 'Bad' power supply status at default logging level to determine whether the probable cause is due to a power supply hardware fault or a possible external power source issue.
bugs.workaround: If power supply errors continue to be logged: 1. Set the libhal logging level to 'Debug': tmsh mod sys db log.libhal.level { value "Debug" } 2. Let the system run in this configuration for at least a few minutes to collect a number of chmand error logs, such as: ... debug chmand[...]: 012a0007:7: Power Supply 1 alert objid:0x16f local:1 status:0x3 pin:0x2 action:0xd ... debug chmand[...]: 012a0007:7: Received Sensor Alert: sensor id 0x16f slot 0xff ... debug chmand[...]: 012a0007:7: Power Supply 1 alert objid:0x16f local:1 status:0x1 pin:0x2 action:0x3. 3. Set the libhal logging level back to 'Notice': tmsh mod sys db log.libhal.level { value "Notice" } 4. Take a qkview or an archive of /var/log/ltm, and engage F5 Professional Services for further analysis.
bugs.fix: When an internal hardware sensor alert is received indicating a 'Bad' power supply status, additional detail is now logged to help identify the cause of the 'Bad' overall status for the power supply.

bugs.title: TMM crash (panic) in AFM pktclass code (Assertion 'classifier ref non-zero' failed.) when virtual server has SPDY or HTTP Prefetching enabled along with AFM Rules.
bugs.symptoms: TMM will crash (panic) in AFM pktclass code with following signature: Assertion 'classifier ref non-zero' failed.
bugs.conditions: For this to happen, following conditions must be met: - AFM is enabled. - Virtual Server has AFM Rules (policy). - Either SPDY profile OR HTTP prefetching enabled. - Then the AFM Rule (policy) on this Virtual Server is modified.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM crash (panic) is fixed now and TMM no longer panics in scenarios with SPDY or HTTP Prefetching enabled.

bugs.title: GUI LTM Profile ClientSSL Passphrase does not accept semicolons
bugs.symptoms: When entering a passphrase for a ClientSSL Profile, an error may be thrown. The error appears similar to the following: 01020066:3: The requested ClientSSL CertKeyChain Entry (/Common/semicolon) already exists in partition Common.
bugs.conditions: -- Create or edit a Client SSL Profile via the GUI. -- Use a semicolon in the passphrase.
bugs.impact: The GUI is not allowing the use of a valid character in the passphrase.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to enter a passphrase with a semicolon.
bugs.fix: Enabled GUI to accept a passphrase with a semicolon.

bugs.title: Inconsistent behavior sending RST on self IP with Port Lockdown None
bugs.symptoms: Depending on the release, sending a SYN packet to a self IP address with Port Lockdown set to Allow None might respond to the SYN with a RST packet, or might silently drop the SYN.
bugs.conditions: With Port Lockdown configured to Allow None, the LTM behaves differently upon receiving a SYN packet. In 11.2.1 HF16, 11.3.0 and 11.4.1, when receiving a SYN packet the LTM replies with RST. In 11.4.0, and in all other versions of the BIG-IP software, when receiving a SYN packet the LTM does not reply (sends a REJECT).
bugs.impact: Inconsistent behavior based on version; sometimes RST in response to SYN on closed port, and sometimes nothing (REJECT). Because the traffic is not allowed in either case, there is no fundamental impact. This is primarily a behavioral difference between releases.

bugs.title: SSL Certificate can accommodate & (ampersand) in the Common Name, Organization Name, Division and SAN.
bugs.symptoms: When an & (ampersand) character is entered for Common Name, Organization Name, Division or SAN in an SSL Certificate, the ampersand is escaped and replaced with an & string.
bugs.conditions: Create or renew an existing certificate with an ampersand in the Common Name, Organization Name, Division, or SAN.
bugs.impact: The system escapes the ampersand with an & string. Names such as AT&T that generate certificates that escape the ampersand character do not work as expected.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly converts the '&' (ampersand) character in the Certificate and ensures that the Peer Device process is still operating.

bugs.title: SSL profile passphrase may be displayed in clear text on the Dashboard
bugs.symptoms: Whenever there is a configuration change, it is indicated by a red dot in the dashboard. When the user clicks on it they can see the SSL passphrase, passwords, etc.
bugs.conditions: This happens whenever there is a config change event.
bugs.impact: Visible to any user who may not have the permission to see it
bugs.fix: Now, passphrases, secrets, passwords, and so on, do not display in clear text and appear as "*****".

bugs.title: Safari 8 does not use Network Access proxy.
bugs.symptoms: Network Access (NA) proxy settings are applied to the system, but Safari 8 doesn't use them.
bugs.conditions: Using Safari 8.
bugs.impact: End users trying to use the Network Access feature of APM will be unable to if they are connecting using Safari 8. Safari 8 was available on OSX Yosemite.
bugs.workaround: Network Access can be launched using other browsers like Firefox and Chrome.
bugs.fix: Safari 8 will now properly use the admin-defined proxy settings if available.

bugs.title: Deleting a URL, that is part of a parameter extraction, from the security policy when the Automatic Policy Builder is enabled and performing a URL extraction update no longer causes the Policy Builder daemon to crash.
ZebOS config load may fail if password begins with numeric character
bugs.symptoms: ZebOS config load might fail if a password begins with a number.
bugs.conditions: In config file, set a password that begins with a number. e.g., neighbor 1.2.3.4 password 0abcdefghijkl
bugs.impact: ZebOS config load fails.
bugs.workaround: Use a password beginning with an alpha character.
bugs.fix: ZebOS config now loads correctly when the password begins with a number.

bugs.title: ESP ICSA support is non-functional on versions 11.4.0 and up
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to turn on ICSA logging for ESP packets will lead to the following logs. Aug 21 10:47:17 2000a info tmm1[10347]: 01070417:6: ICSA: source: %A, destination: %A, spi: 0x%x, seqno: 0x%x ESP packet discarded: "inbound"
bugs.conditions: ICSA logging for ESP packets is enabled. ESP connections are sent through the BIG-IP. Logs similar to the following are found in /var/log/ICSA Aug 21 10:47:17 2000a info tmm1[10347]: 01070417:6: ICSA: source: %A, destination: %A, spi: 0x%x, seqno: 0x%x ESP packet discarded: "inbound"
bugs.impact: ICSA logging misses information that is required for certification.
bugs.fix: ICSA logging no longer misses information that is required for certification.

bugs.title: An automatic transaction alert is now also sent when a Transaction data cookie is missing in a request.
After modifying the protocol profile on an SCTP virtual, the logs may contain error messages
bugs.symptoms: Error messages are logged in the tmm and ltm logs: /var/log/tmm: <13> Sep 4 10:07:29 localhost notice hudfilter_init: 'proxy' is not a bottom-level filter. /var/log/ltm Sep 4 10:07:29 localhost err tmm1[14942]: 01010008:3: Proxy initialization failed for /Common/sctp_echo Sep 4 10:07:29 localhost err tmm[14942]: 01010008:3: Proxy initialization failed for /Common/sctp_echo
bugs.conditions: Modify an SCTP virtual by changing the protocol profiles so that the client-side and server-side profiles are are both the same profile.
bugs.impact: The only impact is that an ominous error message is logged.

bugs.title: Some strings on BIG-IP APM EDGE Client User Interface were not localized
bugs.symptoms: Some text in internationalized Edge Client was still shown in English.
bugs.conditions: Use of internationalized edge client
bugs.impact: Some strings were displayed in English instead of localized language.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP APM Edge Client User Interface Translation has been updated. UI messages and labels have now been translated into several languages.

bugs.title: System can crash referencing compression provider where selection of provider has been deferred
bugs.symptoms: System can crash referencing compression provider where selection of provider has been deferred.
bugs.conditions: Network flow that is likely to require compression is detected. Unusual condition occurs where provider is never selected, but system reference selected provider anyway.
bugs.impact: Tmm cores, Unit fails over. This occurs intermittently.
bugs.workaround: Run the command: tmsh modify sys db compression.allowproviderselectiondeferral value disable
bugs.fix: Select provider in previously unknown case, prior to reference. New feature defers selection of provider to improve provider selection behavior.

bugs.title: Displayed SSL profile statistics might be incorrect
bugs.symptoms: When issuing `tmsh show ltm profile client-ssl', the hardware acceleration statistics might be incorrect in some instances.
bugs.conditions: Negotiated ciphers are partially accelerated (the handshake is done in software, the encryption in hardware).
bugs.impact: None. This is a display only issue.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The displayed SSL profile statistics are now correct.

bugs.title: Internal structure improvements, no customer facing functionality changes have been made.
Shun bug fix. Shun documentation updated for this build release.
Instance-specific monitor logging fails for pool members created in iApps
bugs.symptoms: Errors when enabling Debug Monitoring for an iApp-created pool member and disabling strict updates for the iApp.
bugs.conditions: Create pool members via an iApp, and attempt to enable logging on the pool member.
bugs.impact: Instance-specific monitor logging fails for pool members created in iApps. The log is never created. The system posts error messages in /var/log/ltm stating the log file cannot be opened.
bugs.workaround: If logging is required, bigdlog is available. To enable logging, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db bigd.debug value enabled.

bugs.title: The action attribute value of a form HTML tag is not properly rewritten in the Minimal Content Rewriting mode when it starts with "/"
bugs.symptoms: If the action URL of a form HTML tag begins with "/" and the Minimal Content Rewriting list contains the current host name, this URL is erroneously rewritten with adding of "/f5-w-" prefix.
bugs.conditions: The current host name is in Minimal Content Rewriting list.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is a possible web application malfunction.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, create a particular iRule for each case.
bugs.fix: The action attribute value of a form HTML tag is now properly rewritten in the Minimal Content Rewriting mode when it starts with a forward slash (/).

bugs.title: Fixed alerts in IE9
Installation of FIPS .exp key files sets incorrect public exponent.
bugs.symptoms: Newer FIPS platforms use NGFIPS devices, which seem to be returning the public exponent in little-endian format, when the FIPS exported keys (.exp key files) are imported into FIPS cards. Since F5's code was expecting this in big-endian format, this leads to incorrect public exponent value being written in the key file.
bugs.conditions: Using FIPS platforms (except the older 8900/6900 FIPS platforms): 1. Put two FIPS platforms in the same FIPS security domain without configuring them in a device group. 2. Create or install a key into FIPS card on box1. 3. Copy the key's FIPS exported key (from /config/ssl/ssl.cavfips/) to box2. 4. Install this FIPS .exp key file on box2 using: 'tmsh install sys crypto key <keyname> from-local-file <.exp file path> security-type fips'
bugs.impact: If the corresponding certificate was copied from box1 to box2 and then installed on box2, configuring this key/cert on a SSL profile will lead to the error 'key and certificate do not match'. If the corresponding certificate is newly created on box2 after the key install, then SSL traffic using this key/cert will fail.
bugs.fix: FIPS exported keys can now be correctly installed on other FIPS platforms that belong to the same FIPS security domain.

bugs.title: APM Native RDP Proxy does not allow users to authenticate without specifying a domain name.
bugs.symptoms: APM Native RDP Proxy does not allow users to authenticate without specifying a domain name.
bugs.conditions: 1. APM is configured as Remote Desktop Gateway (RDG) 2. User attempts to login without specifying domain name
bugs.impact: Connection fails and the user is not able to login.
bugs.workaround: Specify domain name along with user id.
bugs.fix: APM Native RDP Proxy now allows users to authenticate without specifying a domain name. Previously, domain name was required.

bugs.title: The command 'show ltm pool detail' returns duplicate members in some cases
bugs.symptoms: The command "show ltm pool <poolname> detail" may show duplicate pool members in some conditions.
bugs.conditions: The conditions required are that the same IP address must be used for multiple members and one member must have :0 port.
bugs.impact: Redundant pool members listed when running the command.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: 'show ltm pool detail' no longer returns duplicate entries for members where their IP matches that of another member whose port is 'any'.

bugs.title: Unnecessary re-transmission of packets on ICMP notifications even when MTU is not changed
bugs.symptoms: Re-transmission of fragment needed packets.
bugs.conditions: Multiple ICMP Destination Unreachable with Fragmentation needed code messages.
bugs.impact: Burst traffic generated.
bugs.workaround: Disable Path MTU Discovery by doing the following, "tmsh modify sys db tm.enforcepathmtu value disable"
bugs.fix: BIG-IP no longer re-transmits packets if the MTU is not changed.

bugs.title: WinInet handle leak in Edge Client on Windows
bugs.symptoms: WinInet handle leak in Edge Client on Windows
bugs.conditions: EdgeClient on Windows, general use
bugs.impact: This leak has slight/minor impact on consuming resources
bugs.fix: WinInet handle leak was eliminated.

bugs.title: [MAC][NA] Routing table is not restored correctly in multi-homed environment if server settings disallow local subnet access
bugs.symptoms: Routing table is not restored correctly after edge client disconnects in multi-homed environment if server settings disallow local subnet access
bugs.conditions: multi-homed environment, server settings disallow local subnet access, MAC edge client
bugs.impact: Routing table might be corrupted
bugs.fix: An issue with routing table not being restored correctly in multi-homed environment when server settings disallow local subnet access is now fixed.

bugs.title: The JS engine update is included in the hotfix.
Edge-Client client shows an error about corrupted config file, when User's profile and temp folders located on different partitions
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows client shows an error about corrupted config file, when User's profile and temp folders are located on different partitions
bugs.conditions: Edge Client for Windows. User's profile and temp folders are located on different partitions.
bugs.impact: Configuration will not be saved.
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows correctly handles a profile located on a different partition.

bugs.title: Some AVR statistics not collected properly
bugs.symptoms: AVR fails to report HTTP statistics.
bugs.conditions: Analytics or dos profile attached to the virtual IP.
bugs.impact: HTTP statistics are not shown.
bugs.fix: Fixed an HTTP statistics reporting problem with AVR.

bugs.title: Changing management IP can lead to bd crash
bugs.symptoms: A bd crashe after a management IP change.
bugs.conditions: Remote logger is configured, high traffic volume and a configuration changed for the management IP.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is a system outage as the bd restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a crash that could happen when management IP configuration was changed.

bugs.title: Memory leak in BIG-IP APM Edge Client Windows API.
bugs.symptoms: There is a possible memory leak in the BIG-IP APM Edge Client Windows API.
bugs.conditions: Memory can leak in the Edge Client when it fails to connect.
bugs.impact: It is not known what the impact is.
bugs.fix: A memory leak in the Windows Edge Client has been fixed.

bugs.title: PEM subscriber sessions are created without PEM licensed, if "radiusLB-subscriber-awre" profile is configured.
bugs.symptoms: If LTM virtual server has the RADIUS profile 'radiusLB-subscriber-awre' configured, the PEM subscriber session will be created, even if the BIG-IP system is not licensed for PEM, which can cause 100% TMM usage due to the overhead of processing RADIUS messages.
bugs.conditions: The RADIUS profile 'radiusLB-subscriber-awre' is configured on the LTM virtual server for non-PEM configurations.
bugs.impact: 100% TMM usage due to PEM subscriber session being created, even when the BIG-IP system is not licensed for the PEM module.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to avoid the misconfiguration by not associating the RADIUS profile 'radiusLB-subscriber-awre' to LTM virtual servers for non-PEM configurations, such as when there is no PEM license for the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: A validation has been added to prevent the RADIUS profile 'radiusLB-subscriber-awre' from being mistakenly associated with the LTM virtual server, when the BIG-IP system is not licensed for PEM.

bugs.title: Unnecessary re-transmission of packets on higher ICMP PMTU.
bugs.symptoms: LTM re-transmits TCP segments even when ICMP Path maximum transmission unit (PMTU) is higher than existing MTU.
bugs.conditions: ICMP PMTU is higher than existing MTU.
bugs.impact: Burst traffic generated.
bugs.workaround: Disable Path MTU Discovery by entering the command: tmsh modify sys db tm.enforcepathmtu value disable.
bugs.fix: Fixed unnecessary re-transmission of packets on higher ICMP Path maximum transmission unit (PMTU).

bugs.title: Core in sip filter due to sending of HUDEVT message while processing of HUDCTL message
bugs.symptoms: There is a tmm core caused by the looping of the SIP message.
bugs.conditions: The looping back of the message might occur because of a timing error, for example, in response to iRule logic that sends a HUDEVT message while processing a HUDCTL message.
bugs.impact: The system cores. This might result in SIP traffic not being forwarded to the server.
bugs.fix: Core in sip filter no longer occurs when sending HUDEVT message while processing of HUDCTL message.

bugs.title: Improve log details when "Detection invalid host header ()" is logged
bugs.symptoms: There is no way for the APM admin to determine the source of the sessions for the log message "Detected invalid host header ()", even at debug level logging.
bugs.conditions: 1- Create APM virtual with any access policy 2- On another BIG-IP, create a pool with an HTTPS monitor to that APM virtual server. 3- Notice the logging in APM.
bugs.impact: It is difficult for admin to determine the source of the error.
bugs.fix: New addition to the log message: "Detected invalid host header () originating from IP <IP address>"

bugs.title: Whitelist count could increment incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: The whitelist count for UDP flood may increment incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: when ICMP traffic is coming in, the UDP flood whitelist count will increament
bugs.impact: The counts for whitelist will be seen increamenting

bugs.title: AFM Online Help updated: DoS Detection Threshold Percentage
bugs.symptoms: AFM Online Help was not updated after 11.4.0 to reflect a change in behavior. Prior to 11.4.0 the DoS Detection Threshold Percentage function would drop packets if an attack was detected. This was regarded as unintuitive when there was a separate rate-limit configuration element that customers could use to drop traffic when an attack was detected.
bugs.conditions: Anyone referring to OLH for a DoS vector Threshold Percentage Increase.
bugs.impact: Inaccurate description of feature behavior.
bugs.workaround: Disregard erroneous information in OLH.
bugs.fix: AFM Online Help has been updated to reflect a change in behavior in the DoS Detection Threshold Percentage. After 11.4.0 the DoS Detection Threshold Percentage function no longer drops packets if an attack was detected. OLH now reflects this.

bugs.title: Microsoft RDP client for iOS doesn't work against F5 APM for versions >= 8.1.0
bugs.symptoms: RDP client for iOS fails to connect to APM configured as RemoteDesktop Gateway.
bugs.conditions: F5 APM configured as RemoteDesktop Gateway iOS RDP client configured to use APM as RD Gateway in order to connect to the intranet terminal server.
bugs.impact: iOS users can't access their backends.
bugs.fix: Fix has improved iOS client recognition so that it works fine for the latest released version.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of HTML entities in attribute values
bugs.symptoms: If an HTML tag attribute contains HTML entities inside its value, this value may not be processed correctly by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: For example, if a form action begins with '/' instead of '/', it will be rewritten although absolute action path should be left untouched. This leads to incorrect behavior of this web application.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now HTML tag attributes with HTML entities inside their values are processed correctly.

bugs.title: 'tmsh show info' command now shows correct value for action from IP Intelligence lookup.
Irrelevant alerts are stopped if phishing is detected.
When using the SSL forward proxy feature, clients might be presented with expired certificates.
bugs.symptoms: When SSL forward proxy feature is enabled, the certificates cached might not expire at the right time resulting in expired certificates being presented to the clients.
bugs.conditions: When using the SSL forward proxy feature.
bugs.impact: Incorrect certificates are presented to the clients.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the cached certs in: show ltm clientssl-proxy cached-certs.
bugs.fix: Cached certificates are now handled correctly.

bugs.title: Don't include maximum TCP options length in calculating MSS on ICMP PMTU.
bugs.symptoms: TCP segment size is 40 bytes less.
bugs.conditions: ICMP implementation using Path MTU (PMTU)
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is less data per TCP segment.
bugs.workaround: Disable Path MTU Discovery by doing the following, "tmsh modify sys db tm.enforcepathmtu value disable"
bugs.fix: BIG-IP no longer includes maximum TCP options length in calculating MSS on ICMP PMTU.

bugs.title: No validation for Shun TTL lengths
bugs.symptoms: TTL lengths can get truncated due to being too large.
bugs.conditions: A large TTL value, above 2^31.
bugs.impact: Bits get truncated, so the value is wrong.
bugs.workaround: Don't enter 10+ year long TTL values.
bugs.fix: IP Intelligence now rejects ip-ttl values that are above 2^31. This value determines how long an IP address will be shunned.

bugs.title: dwbld race with mcpd causes core.
bugs.symptoms: dwbld depends on MCP for configuration. If mcpd has not completely initialized when dwbld queries it (for tags), this can result in a core.
bugs.conditions: dwbld queries mcpd for tags.
bugs.impact: dwbld core.
bugs.fix: dwbld now waits for mcpd to completely initialize, preventing a core.

bugs.title: HTTP URLs with embedded credentials are not working in Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: If a web application uses HTTP URLs with embedded credentials, then they do not work with Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: Application with embedded credentials in the URL
bugs.impact: Web-application logic might not work as expected.
bugs.fix: Now URLs with embedded credentials are handled correctly in Portal Access. These credentials are not passed to back-end server, however.

bugs.title: Window.postMessage() does not send objects
bugs.symptoms: Websites are broken if they use postMessage to send objects. There could or could not be an error in the JavaScript console based on web application.
bugs.conditions: Web-Application that uses Window.postMessage() with Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Web-Application can't use Window.postMessage() to send non-string data with Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Window.postMessage supports sending objects.

bugs.title: Shun-Category infrastructure code fix.
Enforcer memory leak
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.conditions: Traffic with parameters.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.fix: We fixed an issue that sometimes caused ASM to run out of memory.

bugs.title: ASM internal parameters for high availability timeout was not handled correctly
bugs.symptoms: The internal parameters bd_hb_interval and bd_hb_interval_low_platforms are not handled correctly and a different value is registered against the high availability (HA) system. This causes the system to have faster than expected failovers. Also, when bypass asm is turned on and a bigstart restart asm was applied, a failover happens.
bugs.conditions: Two possible conditions: 1. An internal parameter is configured for the timeout to the HA system. When ASM does not send a lifesign to the HA system for 10 seconds (instead of the configured time) 2. bypass asm is internal parameter is applied and a bigstart restart asm happens.
bugs.impact: A failover happens.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release fixes internal parameter processing for the high availability lifesign timeout.

bugs.title: Incorrect 'FIPS import for failed for key' failure when operation actually succeeds
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect debug failure log.
bugs.conditions: Found internally by test, conditions for this issue are unknown.
bugs.impact: False failure logged.
bugs.fix: Fix debug failure log found by internal F5 testing.

bugs.title: OAM10g form based AuthN is not working for a single/multiple domain.
bugs.symptoms: OAM10g form based AuthN is not working for a single/multiple domain.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include double encoding of parameters and race condition on parsing form body.
bugs.impact: Form based OAM authentication might not work.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed all the issues found during the testing of OAM Form-based AuthN scheme, for both single domain and multiple domain.

bugs.title: load sys config default does not work with iCR
bugs.symptoms: load sys config default does not work with iControl REST (iCR). Running the command 'load sys config default' through the iCR interface fails and returns an similar to the following: { "code": 500, "errorStack": [], "message": "Failed to append to temp tar file \"/var/tmp/tmsh/9X0zkv/data\" cache path \"/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/trust_certificate_d/:Common:dtca.crt_37022_1\"exit code (2).\n" }.
bugs.impact: iCR cannot be used for loading default system config.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to load the default configuration.
bugs.fix: The load sys config default command functions correctly through iControl REST (iCR) using the following syntax: curl -sk -u admin:muadib https://ip-address/mgmt/tm/sys/config -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST -d '{"command":"load","name":"default"}'.
bugs.conditions: Running the command 'load sys config default' through the iCR interface.

bugs.title: Hardware compression test fails on 5000 series, 7000 series, 10000 series platforms
bugs.symptoms: Internally executed hardware acceleration tests fail while running a platform-check utility command.
bugs.conditions: Running hardware acceleration tests with the platform-check utility command on the following platforms: 5000 series, 7000 series, 10000 series.
bugs.impact: Tests fail.
bugs.fix: Internally executed hardware acceleration tests no longer fail while running a platform-check utility command.

bugs.title: DNSX Zone Transfer functionality preserved after power loss
bugs.symptoms: Zone transfer daemon, zxfrd, will restart endlessly until it is stopped. On the console there will be emergency system alerts every few seconds saying that zxfrd is restarting. Because of the frequency of these alerts, it will be impossible to use the console for anything. In addition, zone transfers initiated by the BIG-IP will not succeed.
bugs.conditions: If BIG-IP loses power in the middle of a DNS zone transfer, zone data may be corrupted upon booting up. This results in a nonfunctional zxfrd.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP will not be able to transfer zone data from other servers and the TMOS console will be unusable until zxfrd is stopped.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands in the console of your affected BIG-IP: bigstart stop zxfrd cd /var/db && rm -f tmmdns.bin zxfrd.bin bigstart start zxfrd
bugs.fix: With this fix, zone data is no longer susceptible to corruption from power loss.

bugs.title: Fastl4 TCP connection trasitions are not logged
bugs.symptoms: For fastl4 Virtual Server TCP connection transitions are not logged
bugs.conditions: When TCP connections are established and closed for fastl4 virtual Server , the events are not logged
bugs.impact: No logging information for the TCP state transitions for fastl4
bugs.fix: An enhancement that allows logging the TCP events and errors on fastL4 virtual.

bugs.title: Cannot delete keys in subfolders using the BIG-IP GUI
bugs.symptoms: Cannot delete keys in subfolders using the BIG-IP GUI.
bugs.conditions: Deletion of keys in subfolders using web GUI.
bugs.impact: Keys are not deleted.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, delete keys in subfolders using tmsh.
bugs.fix: Keys in subfolders can now be successfully deleted using web GUI.

bugs.title: Username displayed with trailing "&" sign
bugs.symptoms: In Phishing alerts, the username may be displayed in the alert dashboard with an "&" sign appended.
bugs.conditions: Phishing user alerts.
bugs.impact: Incorrect username shown in alert dashboard.
bugs.fix: Removed the extra "&" sign.

bugs.title: A validation was added that disallows configuring a parameter with both “Encrypt” and “Identify as Username” settings enabled together.
BIG-IP with many active ASM accounts after a restart
bugs.symptoms: After a restart, a BIG-IP with ASM provisioned having many active accounts will restart in cycles.
bugs.conditions: Restart a BIG-IP with ASM provisioned having many active accounts.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP flips between the Active and INOPERATIVE states forever.
bugs.fix: After you restart a BIG-IP system with ASM provisioned that has many active accounts, you no longer experience frequent restarts.

bugs.title: Hourly Billing AMIs for 11.6.0 contain internal instead of production license
bugs.symptoms: In previous F5 Amazon Marketplace releases Hourly Billing AMIs were generated with internal/dev license.
bugs.conditions: Amazon Marketplace Hourly Billing AMIs.
bugs.impact: The internal/dev license for Hourly Billing AMIs has been replaced with proper production license.
bugs.fix: The internal/dev license for Hourly Billing AMIs has been replaced with proper production license.

bugs.title: SIP::discard is not invoked for all request messages
bugs.symptoms: SIP::discard is invoked only for the first two request messages, and the other request messages are allowed to pass through.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when an iRule that uses SIP::discard, for example: when SIP_REQUEST { SIP::discard }.
bugs.impact: Any iRule that uses SIP::discard might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can use MR::message drop in MR event to drop the message instead
bugs.fix: The ingress queue for the messages is cleared properly when SIP::discard iRule is present. Now all request messages are correctly dropped if the SIP::discard iRule is present in SIP_REQUEST event.

bugs.title: ICSA logging issues on versions 11.4.0 and later
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to turn on ICSA logging for non-ESP packets lead to the following log messages. Aug 21 10:47:17 2000a info tmm1[10347]: 01070417:6: ICSA: source: %A, destination: %A, spi: 0x%x, seqno: 0x%x ESP packet discarded: 'inbound'.
bugs.conditions: ICSA logging is enabled. Connections are sent through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: ICSA logging misses information that is required for certification. Logs similar to the following are found in /var/log/ICSA Aug 21 10:47:17 2000a info tmm1[10347]: 01070417:6: ICSA: source: %A, destination: %A, spi: 0x%x, seqno: 0x%x ESP packet discarded: 'inbound'.
bugs.fix: Resolved issue that ICSA logging did not contain information that is required for certification.

bugs.title: LTM Policy supports fallback pool
bugs.symptoms: The new 'fallback-pool' is an extension to the 'pool' forwarding action. If for some reason the primary pool within that action is not available, traffic will be forwarded to the fallback pool. Previously if the pool was not available, the connection would get reset. This new parameter makes LTM Policy forwarding to a pool more resilient to failures of the primary pool.
bugs.conditions: -- Selects a forwarding action of 'pool', specifying pool name. -- For that forward-to-pool action, specify a fallback pool. Note: The fallback pool must be different from the primary pool name.
bugs.impact: This is new functionality.
bugs.fix: LTM Policy now supports fallback pool.
bugs.behavior: - With this change, you can select 'fallback-pool' along with primary 'pool' using LTM policy. - If the primary pool present in the forward action is unavailable, the LTM policy will forward traffic to the fallback pool. - Sample Usage ltm policy Drafts/mypolicy { controls { forwarding } last-modified 2018-05-21:11:31:27 requires { http } rules { 1 { actions { 1 { forward select fallback-pool fallback_pool pool http_pool } } } } status draft } - 'fallback-pool' is an extension of the 'pool' param present in the same action, and LTM policy will forward traffic only if primary 'pool' within that action is not available. - Also, you must specify 'pool' along with 'fallback-pool', and both cannot have same pool name.

bugs.title: DC PSU reported as AC
bugs.symptoms: When powering up a DC chassis, if one DC PSU is plugged in before the other DC PSU, the system may report the second PSU to be plugged in as an AC PSU.
bugs.conditions: The following platforms with 2 DC PSUs installed: 10000, 10050, 10055, 10200, 10350, 12050
bugs.impact: TMOS reports the wrong PSU type to the user.
bugs.workaround: Removing the DC PSU which is being reported incorrectly and reinstalling will work around this problem: - Remove PSU for > 30 seconds or until TMOS reports PSU is not present. - Insert PSU
bugs.fix: On BIG-IP 10000/12000 Series platforms, the system no longer reports a secondary DC power supply that is installed, but not powered on, as an AC power supply, when power is applied to the secondary DC power supply.

bugs.title: The issue has been fixed so that DHCP profile with Radius AAA authentication will always function as expected.
TMM core during certificate verification against CRL
bugs.symptoms: TMM core during certificate verification against CRL.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include a Client/Server SSL profile with CRL enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable CRL on the Client/Server SSL profile
bugs.fix: Prevent TMM core during certificate verification against CRL

bugs.title: Powered down DC PSU is treated as not-present
bugs.symptoms: When power is removed from the PSU but the PSU remains in the system, 'tmsh show sys hardware' reports the PSU as 'not-present'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when an installed DC powered PSU loses power, and the user runs the command 'tmsh show sys hardware'.
bugs.impact: Only the message is incorrect. Although the PSU is present, the system cannot read its data without power, so the system marks the PSU 'not present'. Once power is restored, all information is available.
bugs.workaround: Plug the power cable into the PSU. The system can now detect the power supply status and read the PSU info.

bugs.title: ZoneRunner can fail to respond to commands after a VE resume.
bugs.symptoms: The ZoneRunner GUI can become unresponsive after a VE resume.
bugs.conditions: This is due to the "lo:" interface not being recreated during the resume processing. ZoneRunner relies on this interface to communicate with the on box BIND server.
bugs.impact: ZoneRunner cannot create/modify/delete/query records from the on box BIND server
bugs.workaround: Restart ZoneRunner after a VE resume with the command: bigstart restart zonerunner.
bugs.fix: ZoneRunner now uses the tmm0 interface to communicate with BIND.

bugs.title: stpd tries to use bcm56xxd before it has started which results in error messages in ltm log
bugs.symptoms: There is a race condition when the daemons startup where stpd is coming up before bcm56xxd. The stpd daemon tries to use bcm56xxd before it has started. You see the following in /var/log/ltm: err stpd[8241]: 01290003:3: HalmsgTerminalImpl_::sendMessage() Unable to send to any BCM56XXD address
bugs.conditions: Affects switch based platforms that use bcm56xxd.
bugs.impact: Several error messages appear in the ltm log: Feb 9 15:06:23 localhost err stpd[9390]: 01290003:3: HalmsgTerminalImpl_::sendMessage() Unable to send to any BCM56XXD address Feb 9 15:06:23 localhost err stpd[9390]: 01280012:3: HAL packet request sendMessage failed (slot 0)

bugs.title: Deleting a virtual server does not delete the resource record (RR) in ZoneRunner Daemon (ZRD)
bugs.symptoms: The resource record (RR) in ZoneRunner Daemon (ZRD) is not deleted when the associated Virtual Server is deleted from the Global Traffic Manager (GTM) server object.
bugs.conditions: Conditions that lead to this issue include a GTM server object with a Virtual Server; a pool with the above virtual server; a wideip using the above pool as resources; and deleting the virtual server from the GTM server object.
bugs.impact: BIND will contain and return RRs that were intended to be deleted. The RR is orphaned and could only be deleted manually from ZRD.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue you can delete the GTM server associated with the virtual server to be deleted, but this would delete other associated virtual servers too. Alternatively, you can manually delete the RR in ZRD.
bugs.fix: Deleting a virtual server now correctly deletes the resource record (RR) in ZoneRunner Daemon (ZRD).

bugs.title: Cannot create VXLAN tunnels with the same local-address and different multicast addresses.
bugs.symptoms: MCP throws an validation error when attempting to create VXLAN tunnels with the same local-address and different multicast addresses.
bugs.conditions: Create VXLAN tunnels with the same local-address and different multicast addresses.
bugs.impact: Cannot create VXLAN tunnels with the same local-address and different multicast addresses.
bugs.workaround: Use a different local-address for each multicast group when creating multicast VXLAN tunnels.
bugs.fix: Can create VXLAN tunnels with the same local-address and different multicast addresses.
bugs.behavior: You can now create multicast VXLAN tunnels with the same local-address and different multicast addresses.

bugs.title: Hardware parity error mitigation on 10000s/10200v/10250v platforms and B4300/B4340N and B2250 blades
bugs.symptoms: In rare occurrences, BIG-IP hardware is susceptible to parity errors due to unknown source.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only on the BIG-IP 10000s/10200v/10250v platforms, and on the VIPRION B4300/B4340N and B2250 blades. The exact trigger of the parity error is unknown at this time.
bugs.impact: This impacts several series of BIG-IP products with hardware parity error mitigation capabilities.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting BIG-IP hardware should clear issues caused by hardware parity errors.
bugs.fix: This release includes functionality to leverage hardware parity error mitigation capabilities, which reduces the number of fatal errors.

bugs.title: TMM might crash when DSACK is enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash when DSACK is enabled
bugs.conditions: This occurs rarely on a virtual server configured with a TCP profile that has DSACK (Duplicate Selective Acknowledgement) enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use TCP profile with the DSACK feature enabled.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer attempts to transmit DSACKs after reassembly queue has been purged, so no TMM crash occurs.

bugs.title: TMM hangs and receives SIGABRT due to race condition during DNS db load
bugs.symptoms: The TMM attempts a DNS db load while starting.
bugs.conditions: This is a potential race condition that might occur intermittently after the restart.
bugs.impact: One thread hangs indefinitely and tmm receives a SIGABRT after a period of time.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a potential race condition that occurred during DNS db load.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
Unexpected iSession tunnel state transition causes TMM to restart.
bugs.symptoms: A TMM process cores due to a 'valid event' assertion failure in isession_handle_evt().
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur when a virtual server's iSession profile is modified while idle iSession connections are awaiting reuse. The iSession profile must have connection reuse enabled for this problem to occur.
bugs.impact: An assertion failure causes tmm to create a core file and restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable reuse-connection in iSession profile.
bugs.fix: Unexpected iSession tunnel state transitions are handled without causing TMM to restart or create a core file.

bugs.title: FTP active mode does not work with LSN pool modes PBA and Deterministic when FTP profile port=any
bugs.symptoms: FTP active mode does not work
bugs.conditions: When PBA or Deterministic mode is configured on the LSN pool and FTP profile port=any
bugs.impact: FTP active mode does not work
bugs.workaround: Use FTP passive mode

bugs.title: 'readPowerSupplyRegister error' in LTM log
bugs.symptoms: The 'readPowerSupplyRegister error' is logged in LTM log when DC PSU loses its power.
bugs.conditions: When a DC powered PSU loses its power, the system logs 'readPowerSupplyRegister error' messages in the LTM log. This occurs because PSU data is not available without power.
bugs.impact: The 'readPowerSupplyRegister error' messages occur because PSU data is not available without power. When the system is in this state, you can safely ignore these messages.
bugs.workaround: None. You can safely ignore this error message in this case.

bugs.title: Error message in ltm log: bcm56xxd: reading L2 entry Operation failed bs_arl.cpp.
bugs.symptoms: Error message in ltm log: bcm56xxd: reading L2 entry Operation failed bs_arl.cpp.
bugs.conditions: bcm56xxd periodically reads the switch's internal L2 table to save certain L2 information for internal debug use. Reads to unused entries of this table might fail and produce an error.
bugs.impact: Error messages in /var/log/ltm. Messages appear similar to the following: err bcm56xxd[7453]: 012c0011:3: Error: reading L2 entry 68416: Operation failed bs_arl.cpp(1579)
bugs.fix: In this release, the seldom-used internal debug table has been removed, which eliminates the periodic accesses.

bugs.title: monpd/ltm log errors after Hotfix is applied
bugs.symptoms: When you apply a hotfix on an already configured and working volume, many errors are logged in the monpd/ltm logs. Note: The system uses the monpd process in conjunction with the avrd process (Analytics) for reporting application performance data. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: In the /var/log/ltm file, you observe error messages similar to the following example: err DB[10860]: monpd|ERR|Jan 01 09:00:00.123|12345| [DB::mysql_query_safe, query failed] Error (error number 1243) executing SQL string : EXECUTE stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions USING @table_name,@table_name Because : Unknown prepared statement handler (stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions) given to EXECUTE err DB[10860]: monpd|ERR|Sep 02 09:00:00.123|12345| [DB::run_sql_query, mysql_query_safe] Error executing SQL query: EXECUTE stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions USING @table_name,@table_name Because : Unknown prepared statement handler (stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions) given to EXECUTE In the /var/log/avr/monpd.log file, you observe error messages similar to the following example: monpd|ERR|Jan 1 09:00:00.123|12345| [DB::mysql_query_safe, query failed] Error (error number 1243) executing SQL string : EXECUTE stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions USING @table_name,@table_name Because : Unknown prepared statement handler (stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions) given to EXECUTE monpd|ERR|Jan 1 09:00:00.123|12345| [DB::run_sql_query, mysql_query_safe] Error executing SQL query: EXECUTE stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions USING @table_name,@table_name Because : Unknown prepared statement handler (stmt_select_table_with_too_many_partitions) given to EXECUTE
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have provisioned the Application Visibility and Reporting module. -- You have recently installed a software hotfix. -- You have rebooted the BIG-IP system into the newly hotfixed boot location. -- You have provisioned one of the following modules: AFM, APM, ASM, AVR, CGN, DNS, FPS, PEM, PSM, SWG, or vCMP.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system consumes a small amount of additional disk space. These are cosmetic, benign errors.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue. However, you can stop the system from logging the monpd errors by rebuilding the Application Visibility and Reporting database. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: The following procedure does not disable monpd logging. Normal monpd log entries will continue to be written to the /var/log/avr/monpd.log file. Log in to the BIG-IP command line. Type the following command: mysql -p`perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw` AVR < /var/avr/avr_srv_code.sql To restart the monpd process, type the following command: bigstart restart monpd

bugs.title: Loading a UCS file with no-platform-check stalls at platform check
bugs.symptoms: Loading a UCS file with the no-platform-check option does not bypass the platform check (which it should).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the no-platform-check option to load a UCS file from a different platform. This issue occurs only in version 11.6.0 (the base software), 11.6.0 HF1, 11.6.0 HF2, and 11.6.0 HF3.
bugs.impact: The user cannot load UCS files from other platforms. The system posts the following error message: ERROR: The platform on the system is different from the platform in the UCS. Can't install the UCS. To bypass platform check, use no-platform-check option.
bugs.workaround: On the system where you are installing the UCS, use tmsh to run the following commands: -- modify sys db ucs.platformcheck value false. -- load sys ucs my_ucs_filename.
bugs.fix: The no-platform-check option now bypasses the platform check, which allows the user to load UCS files from other platforms.

bugs.title: Setting appropriate TX driver settings for 40 GB interfaces.
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, the VIPRION C4800 chassis might experience an inability to establish some connections due to losing packets in one direction while in transit between blades.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION C4800 chassis.
bugs.impact: When the problem is due to this issue, one or more 5.x or 6.x interfaces show status as 'up' but the corresponding media as 'none'. Inability to establish some connections. The problem is consistent, depending on source and destination IP and port.
bugs.fix: VIPRION C4800 backplane interfaces are now given proper settings to prevent unidirectional traffic issues.

bugs.title: SSL traffic is not forwarded to destination
bugs.symptoms: SSL traffic is not forwarded to the backend server.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when SSL session reused is enabled (which is standard behavior).
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that SSL traffic is interrupted (flows are dropped).
bugs.workaround: Remove the _sys_CEC_SSL_client_policy policy from the SSL VS.
bugs.fix: Bug fix in classification library that caused SSL traffic not to be forwarded to the destination.

bugs.title: Different Outlook users with same password and client IP are tied to a single APM session when using Basic auth
bugs.symptoms: Different Outlook users are tied to a single APM session.
bugs.conditions: Users have identical passwords and come from the same client IP address.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is APM does not validate Outlook credentials.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: APM correctly validates Outlook credentials and creates new APM session for users that come from the same IP and have identical passwords.

bugs.title: SessionDb may be trapped in wrong HA state during initialization
bugs.symptoms: An error case may happen on BIG-IP if the following conditions are met: 1. There are two BIG-IPs configured as inter-cluster HA. 2. These two BIG-IPs are multi-blade chasis system. 3. Master record with independent subkeys is added to SessionDB. The observed symptom this that you can explicitly deleted such a master record, but auto expiration mechanisms (timeout & lifetime) will not work on it, and this record will live forever until it is explicitly deleted.
bugs.conditions: Inter-chassis mirroring Chassis w/ multiple blades
bugs.impact: an inconsistent state between systems can cause persistence entries to never timeout. This will impact CGNAT records stored in SessionDB such as persistence records and PBA blocks.

bugs.title: CPU statistics reported by the tmstat command may spike or go negative
bugs.symptoms: On bladed systems, the results from the 'tmstat' and 'tmstat cpu' commands may spike high or go negative due to a issue with how per-blade statistics are collected.
bugs.conditions: Error in the timing of statistics collection such that display is incorrect.
bugs.impact: Incorrect display of CPU statistics.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The CPU statistics display has been fixed.

bugs.title: If a "refresh" response header should not be rewritten, it can crash the rewrite plugin or be improperly rewritten
bugs.symptoms: If a "Refresh" response header should not be rewritten, it can crash the rewrite plugin or be improperly rewritten.
bugs.conditions: If URL in a "Refresh" header matches the bypass list, plugin crashes; if it is related to the current path, it is rewritten as an empty string.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is a possible web application malfunction.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Portal Access no longer crashes if a URL in a Refresh header matches a Portal Access bypass list entry.

bugs.title: Force to Standby does not work with HA Groups configured.
bugs.symptoms: Using Force to Standby does not work if HA Groups are configured. In older releases, the operation is allowed, but has no effect, or is unreliable. In newer releases, the operation is disallowed.
bugs.conditions: Configure HA Group scoring for a traffic-group.
bugs.impact: Administrator must make configuration changes (disable HA Groups) in order to force a particular device to become Active.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to disable the HA Group on the Active device, perform the failover, and then re-enable the HA Group. For more information, see K14515: The Force to Standby feature should not be used when the HA group feature is enabled, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14515.
bugs.fix: Force to Standby is allowed for traffic-groups configured with HA Group scoring.
bugs.behavior: Previously, traffic-group Force to Standby was disallowed if HA Groups are configured, it is now allowed.

bugs.title: Transaction will fail when deleting pool member and related node
bugs.symptoms: Removing a pool and the related nodes in the same transaction will fail. It will output an error message similar to the following: 01070110:3: Node address '/Common/12.33.22.2' is referenced by a member of pool '/Common/mypool'.
bugs.conditions: Create a pool, add a single pool member (which creates the associated node). If you then delete the pool and node in the same transaction, the transaction will fail.
bugs.impact: A pool and related nodes cannot be deleted within the same transaction.
bugs.workaround: If you delete the pool and nodes in 2 separate transactions, the process will succeed.
bugs.fix: The pool-member reference check for the node was moved to a later stage of validation, allowing the pool and pool members to be updated/deleted. This ensures that when the delete code for the node checks for references from a pool, there will be none.

bugs.title: Sync may fail after deleting a persistence profile
bugs.symptoms: After syncing configuration, the following error occurs: 'One or more persistence attributes are incompatible with the persistence mode for profile'.
bugs.conditions: This happens if automatic sync is disabled on a device group and a user both creates and deletes a persistence profile before manually syncing the configuration.
bugs.impact: Peer boxes fail to load the configuration.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: 1. Perform a full sync instead of an incremental sync. 2. Create the profile, then perform a sync, and then delete the profile, and perform a separate sync.
bugs.fix: This was an invalid error case being handled internally and was removed.

bugs.title: TMM core
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashed
bugs.conditions: Debug level was enabled for FPS module and load traffic was sent to machine
bugs.impact: Machine in offline state
bugs.workaround: Do not enable debug level during load traffic
bugs.fix: TMM should no longer crash after enabling debug level of FPS module.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
F5 support for new hardware platforms.
F5 support for new hardware platforms.
F5 support for new hardware platforms.
tmm crash in ipsec when ipsec-policy and ike-peer do not match.
bugs.symptoms: While making changes to ipsec, tmm can crash.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when ipsec-policy and ike-peer IP addresses do not match.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the ike-peer "tunnel-remote-address" and ipsec-policy "remote-address" are the same.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes in ipsec when ipsec-policy and ike-peer do not match.

bugs.title: Status incorrect for vCMP host and guest with different blades as primary
bugs.symptoms: If a licensing operation happens when the vCMP host and a guest have different blades as primary, then the status might show an incorrect number of downed links.
bugs.conditions: vCMP host and guest have different blades specified as the primary.
bugs.impact: Although the system might report an incorrect number of downed links, this is a cosmetic issue. The system functions correctly.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the host and guest have the same blades specified as the primary.

bugs.title: bigd crash on improper monitor configuration (timeout less than the interval) for Tcl monitors.
bugs.symptoms: bigd crash on improper monitor configuration (timeout less than the interval) for Tcl monitors.
bugs.conditions: Tcl Monitors: FTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, when the timeout is less than the interval. Might also occur if the Tcl worker is in a stuck state, due to pool member not responding within the configured timeout.
bugs.impact: bigd crashes and posts an error message similar to the following: Received invalid magic value in the stream'.
bugs.workaround: Correct the monitor timeout to be higher than interval. Generally, the timeout should be ((3 * interval) + 1) seconds. Note: This workaround might not work in cases where the failure is due to Tcl worker being in a stuck state due to the pool member not responding within the configured timeout.
bugs.fix: The system no longer crashes when Tcl monitors are improperly configured, that is, when the timeout specified is less than the interval.

bugs.title: TMM generates hundreds of ICMP packets in response to a single packet
bugs.symptoms: TMM generates hundreds of ICMP packets in response to a single packet.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on a VIP2VIP configuration when the server on the second virtual server becomes unreachable.
bugs.impact: tmm sends hundreds of ICMP packets to the client upon receiving single packet from client.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer generates hundreds of ICMP packets when the server on the second virtual server in a VIP2VIP configuration becomes unreachable.

bugs.title: Multi-tab protection problems with multi-domain SSO
bugs.symptoms: When APM is configured with multi-domain SSO, and an unauthenticated user opens multiple tabs simultaneously to different protected domains, then one of the tabs will be issued an error page indicating authentication is in progress. That page offers a link to reset the session and begin a fresh authentication sequence. Clicking on the link will result in the same error page being presented.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured with multi-domain SSO, and an unauthenticated user opens multiple tabs simultaneously to different protected domains, and then follows the link to reset the session.
bugs.impact: The user will be unable to establish a session until the session itself has expired or the browser is restarted.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The errant behavior is caused by an improper URL being presented by the error page. When APM checks the improper URL, it causes it to issue the same error page. This has now been corrected.

bugs.title: We fixed a memory leak in the FPS plugin when alerts are sent by the BIG-IP.
SR C1800930 - GUI crashs - and SQL errors
bugs.symptoms: The WebUI is unusable as it can take 30 seconds to a minute to load different pages. Other times the user will get the "service restarting" message. They have tried multiple browsers and changed the maximum connections to the config utility from 20 to 50 and back to 20 when that didn't help.
bugs.conditions: The customer says that he can get it to occur by having 3 users log into the config utility and then click around randomly until it crashes.
bugs.impact: GUI inaccessible
bugs.workaround: Work around is available by removing the following from the httpd.conf: -------------- # If DCOEP is defined then enable the related configuration. <IfDefine DCOEP> ... </IfDefine> -------------- This can be done by modifying the template /defaults/config/templates/httpd.tmpl.

bugs.title: Corresponding protocol profiles must exist on both clientside/serverside
bugs.symptoms: Virtual servers configured without protocol profiles on both the clientside and serverside do not pass traffic.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on virtual servers configured without protocol profiles on both the clientside and serverside.
bugs.impact: Attempts to connect to the virtual server might result in RSTs ('no local listener'), or the virtual address might not respond to ARP if there are no other functional virtual servers on the same virtual address. Virtual servers affected by this issue do not pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: If a protocol profile with a context (clientside or serverside) is specified when defining a virtual server, ensure that a protocol profile is specified for the peer context.

bugs.title: BCM debug logging cannot be turned off once enabled
bugs.symptoms: Log messages continue to appear after being disabled.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the BCM daemon loglevel is increased to debug and a non-zero mask is set.
bugs.impact: Unexpected log messages. The volume of logs from bcm56xxd debug can be overwhelming, and being unable to stop them risks filling the filesystem where they are logged.
bugs.workaround: Restart bcm56xxd daemon. Note: Restarting this daemon affects traffic.

bugs.title: Memory leaks when iSession and iControl are configured
bugs.symptoms: Memory leaks might occur when iSession and iControl are configured.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using iSession on APM.
bugs.impact: Memory leaks.
bugs.fix: This release resolves memory leaks that occurred when iSession and iControl were configured.

bugs.title: TMM crashes if new IP address is added to a session through radius interim update message.
bugs.symptoms: TMM goes to crash if new IP address is added to an existing session via radius interim update message.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when: 1. There is an existing session established. 2. Update the existing session with a new IP address using radius interim update.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After a fix, the new IP address can be added to an existing session through radius interim update message without causing a crash.

bugs.title: OSPFv2 Redistributed routes are deleted after blade failover with Graceful Restart
bugs.symptoms: OSPFv2 Redistributed routes are getting deleted after blade failover
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure OSPFv2 and enable Graceful restart 2. Add static routes on Chassis and redistribute static through ospfv2 blade failover
bugs.impact: Routes are deleted after failover.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows does not enable you to generate a client troubleshooting report from the user interface.
bugs.symptoms: If end users of the Edge Client are encountering difficulty connecting, it is not easy for them to provide you with a troubleshooting report so you can diagnose the problem.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with Edge Client users.
bugs.impact: This makes it difficult to diagnose the problem with end users trying to connect with the Edge Client.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows now enables you to generate a client troubleshooting report from the user interface.

bugs.title: TMM restarts during iSession tunnel reuse.
bugs.symptoms: An "Isession data not drained" assertion failure causes a TMM process to create a core file and restart.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server has an iSession profile with Reuse Connection enabled along with deduplication and/or compression enabled.
bugs.impact: The TMM process creates a core file and restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Backslashes in policy rule added/duplicated when modified in GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Policy no longer matches rule after modification via the GUI.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the policy rule contains literal backslash.
bugs.impact: The policy does not match the expected condition.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to make policy changes.
bugs.fix: Backslashes in policy rule are now correctly escapsed when modified in GUI.

bugs.title: Adding a new chassis and syncing the configuration cause mcpd to restart.
bugs.symptoms: In a sync-failover device group, upon adding a chassis for the first time and pushing the configuration to it, its secondary blades will have an mcpd restart. This error message will be logged: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group [name to commit id [...] failed with error 010718e7:3: The requested primary admin user (admin) must have a password set..
bugs.conditions: This applies only to trust domains containing VIPRION chassis or VCMP guests, not standalone appliances.
bugs.impact: Most other services will also be impacted.
bugs.fix: Adding a new chassis and syncing the configuration no longer causes mcpd to restart.

bugs.title: Install of FIPS exported key files (.exp) causes device-group sync failure
bugs.symptoms: Install of FIPS exported key files (.exp) on one BIG-IP causes device group sync to fail.
bugs.conditions: With two or more FIPS BIG-IPs configured in a device group, install a correct FIPS exported key file (.exp key) on bigip1. This exp file must be from a FIPS box belonging to the same FIPS security domain.
bugs.impact: Device group sync failed.
bugs.workaround: Copy the FIPS .exp file to the peer. Install this .exp key file on the peer also, similar to how it was installed on the first BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: FIPS exported keys can now be successfully installed in FIPS cards without causing config-sync failure.

bugs.title: Vague error - Error ERR_BOUNDS connflow ... processing pullup of control message.
bugs.symptoms: PPTP filter emits a vague error message in the ltm log, for example: 'Error ERR_BOUNDS connflow 74.14.223.32:1723 -- 121.54.54.11:34976 processing pullup of control message,' or 'Error ERR_BOUNDS connflow 65.93.152.110:1723 -- 121.54.54.11:2004 processing egress message.'
bugs.conditions: PPTP ALG is configured. CGNAT is configured. Non-PPTP traffic is being directed to port 1723.
bugs.impact: These messages are cosmetic only, and can be ignored safely, but may indicate that another protocol is using port 1723.
bugs.fix: Error ERR_BOUNDS loglevel has changed from ERR to DEBUG, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Perform VS DWBL lookup after accept-decisive firewall rule match at global level
Packets not counted in tmctl ip_intelligence_stat on accept-decisively ACL match
bugs.symptoms: We missed counting packets in the IPI tmctl table when a matching rule resulted in accept-decisively match.
bugs.conditions: An ACL rule with accept-decisively as action along with IPI configuration.
bugs.impact: This caused a change of behavior compared to a prior version.
bugs.fix: We now count packets in the IPI tmctl table when a matching rule results in accept-decisively match.

bugs.title: IKE peer (ike-peer) configuration objects in non-Common partition are visible to all in GUI
bugs.symptoms: IKE peer configuration objects ('ike-peer') in non-Common partition are visible to all users via the web UI.
bugs.conditions: - Partitions are in use. - IPsec is configured in a partition other than /Common. - An IKE peer object is configured in partition that is not /Common.
bugs.impact: All users can see the IKE peer object using the web UI even though the object does not belong to the /Common partition. Users in one partition can see list of IKE peer objects belonging to other partitions. There is inconsistent partition behavior for IKE peer objects on the BIG-IP system and these objects will not be stored in their respective partition configuration files.
bugs.fix: IKE peer configuration objects are now stored in their respective partition configuration files on the BIG-IP system. The web UI will not display the partitioned IKE peer configuration objects to unauthorized users.

bugs.title: Stats and Logging for ADAPT dynamic contexts, and IVS Transaction Logging
bugs.symptoms: The stats for request-adapt and response-adapt profile aggregate all dynamic contexts into a single row, which can hinder debug or analysis of the use of dynamic adaptation contexts. The interface between the parent virtual server with those profiles, and the internal virtual server, cannot be packet-captured, which can increase the difficulty with debugging.
bugs.conditions: Adaption profile request-adapt or response-adapt, and an internal virtual server.
bugs.impact: Difficult to debug and analyze dynamic context behavior. Difficult to diagnose IVS related issues due to lack of visibility of the internal non-TCP interface.
bugs.fix: Statistics for request-adapt and response-adapt profiles now use separate rows for dynamic contexts, allowing greater visibility into usage of each dynamic context by name. Log messages for request-adapt and response-adapt provide key flow information. Additional messages provide information regarding dynamic contexts. Log messages for an internal virtual server provide transaction information to increase visibility on the software interface between the ADAPT filter and an internal virtual server.
bugs.behavior: Statistics for request-adapt and response-adapt profiles use separate rows for dynamic contexts by name (previously they were all aggregated into the single stats row for the profile). Log messages for request-adapt and response-adapt provide key flow information, and additional messages provide more information regarding dynamic contexts. The log level is set by the existing DB variable log.adapt.level. More log messages for an internal virtual server provide transaction information to increase visibility on the internal IVS interface between the ADAPT filter and an IVS. The log level is set by the existing DB variable log.ivs.level.

bugs.title: APD, APMD, MCPD communication error failure now reported with error code
bugs.symptoms: When an unexpected error is received during communication between apd, apmd, and mcpd, it throws an exception.
bugs.conditions: Rarely reproducible, failed communication between apd, apmd, and mcpd.
bugs.impact: The system cores without an error code indicating the reason. This hampers finding the actual cause for the error.
bugs.fix: Now, when an error occurs, the system prints an error code in HEX, which facilitates finding the reason for the error.

bugs.title: Message: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request
bugs.symptoms: The system posts messages in ltm log similar to the following: err mcpd[7172]: 0107167d:3: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request (unknown request), tag (20594).
bugs.conditions: This occurs on a bladed system from an snmp query against blade_voltage_stat.
bugs.impact: For bladed systems, the system does not report the blade voltage. For systems that are not bladed system, there is no publisher for this query. This message is cosmetic for non-bladed systems, and you can safely ignore it.
bugs.fix: The main query processing file was not included during build-time. The file has been added and the stats should now show as expected.

bugs.title: Modifying edge client application folder causes gatekeeper to throw warning
bugs.symptoms: Configuration file exist in edge client application folder and this keeps getting modified by edge client (e.g. when user adds new server), gatekeeper throws warning if this file is modified by edge client.
bugs.conditions: MAC Edge client, OS X Yosemite, configuration.
bugs.impact: Gatekeeper throws warning, edge client might keep working correctly.
