bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client does not update its application directory anymore; instead it uses /Libarary/Application\ Support/ directory.

bugs.title: F5 support for new hardware platforms.
During OAM SDK initialization, ObConfig initialization returns wrong accessgate ID
bugs.symptoms: OAM ObConfig Initialization returns wrong accessgate ID, and that resulted in EAM setting wrong domain for the ObSSOCookie.
bugs.conditions: After network connection failure with backend OAM server, ObConfig initilization returned past Accessgate ID.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that ObConfig initialization returns the wrong accessgate ID.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: AccessGate init should now fail initialization and retry in case of an AccessGate ID mismatch. If all retries fail, then the AccessGate remains uninitialized. The administrator should clear the config cache for all the AccessGates and restart the EAM process.

bugs.title: Delayed update of Virtual Address might not always happen.
bugs.symptoms: When a Virtual IP status changes such that a Virtual Address should transition from down to up, the update does not always get to all subscribers.
bugs.conditions: Route Health Injection (RHI)-enabled Virtual Address and routing protocol on the Virtual IP.
bugs.impact: RHI might never be re-announced. The delayed update might not propagate the status change, because of the assumption that the previous update reached all subscribers, and might skip the delayed update.
bugs.fix: Virtual Address delayed update mechanism now sends delayed updates approximately three seconds after change, regardless of previous status, guaranteeing that Virtual Address status reaches all subscribers.

bugs.title: tmm log flood: isession_handle_evt: bad transition:7
bugs.symptoms: tmm log flood with the event: 01470000:3: iSession: Connection error: isession_handle_evt:6680: isession_handle_evt: bad transition:7
bugs.conditions: This may happen when using APM.
bugs.impact: The tmm log is filled with unnecessary events.
bugs.fix: Fixed iControl / iSession memory leak issue; set proper log level to prevent log flooding.

bugs.title: ADAPT should be able to work with OneConnect
bugs.symptoms: The request-adapt and response-adapt profiles are unable to work with the OneConnect profile, and so those combinations are not allowed in the same virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to combine request-adapt or response-adapt profile with OneConnect profile on the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: When adaptation is being used, the connection cannot be kept open and reused for multiple HTTP transactions.
bugs.fix: The OneConnect profile can be combined with either or both of request-adapt and response-adapt profiles on a virtual server. Both client and server HTTP connections are reused.

bugs.title: AVR and APM: TMM crashes
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent TMM crash when APM and AVR are provisioned together.
bugs.conditions: AVR enabled with APM.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. This is an intermittent issue. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable AVR.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue that intermittently caused TMM to crash when APM and AVR were provisioned together.

bugs.title: Fixed user inspection in Internet Explorer 9
Edge Client for Mac blocks textexpander application's functionality
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac blocks textexpander application's functionality. Edge Client does npt release secure input and from there on textexpander application does not expand keywords.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP access policy must have logon page configured with password field. Edge Client for Mac connects to such a BIG-IP
bugs.impact: textexpander fails to expand recognized keywords
bugs.workaround: Click on submit button with mouse or press tab to move focus on submit button and then hit return.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac was fixed so that it does not block textexpander's functionality.

bugs.title: Connections to virtual servers with port-preserve property will cause connections to leak in TMM
bugs.symptoms: Connections leak, exhausting the memory over time and causing TMM to re-start.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with port-preserve setting. Tunneled APM connections in a CMP environment (many TMM processes).
bugs.impact: TMM process re-starts causing traffic disruption. Low performance is also seen due to the high number of leaked connections.
bugs.fix: The internal listeners that are created to forward the connections between TMM processes are now deleted when no longer needed, so new connections are not created, which prevents a memory leak.

bugs.title: Internal misbehavior of the SPDY filter
bugs.symptoms: The SPDY filter may send events to a child flow, after that child flow has been deleted. When a filter for the delete child flow processes this event, it may crash.
bugs.conditions: The conditions that trigger this are unclear. The fix eliminates the behavior that caused a crash. The crash only occurs with a complex virtual server configuration and even then very rarely.
bugs.impact: The tmm crashes.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The SPDY filter no longer sends events up on deleted child flows, thus preventing a possible crash.

bugs.title: Secondary IP flows are not forwarded in multiple IP session
bugs.symptoms: If a session is created with 2 IP address then flows associated to secondary IP (2nd IP of the session) are not forwarded properly and consequently policies are not applied.
bugs.conditions: A multiple IP session with 2 IP address in the session.
bugs.impact: Policies are not applied accordingly for all the flows associated to secondary IP of the session.
bugs.fix: Have to upgrade to hotifix or new version with this fix.

bugs.title: Support SIP/DNS DOS only for UDP packets and SIP DOS does not drop packets but count drops
bugs.symptoms: SIP DOS does not drop the packets after attack is detected but counts the stats for drop packets.
bugs.conditions: SIP DOS attack is detected.
bugs.impact: SIP DOS Attack packets will not be dropped.
bugs.fix: This fix causes the system to drop SIP DoS attack packets. This change also restricts SIP/DNS DoS detection only to UDP packets. SIP/DNS DoS attacks over TCP and SCTP are not detected.
bugs.behavior: Prior to this release, SIP/DNS DOS detection and mitigation was supported on TCP,UDP and SCTP protocol packets. With this release SIP/DNS DOS detection and mitigation is only for UDP protocol packets. SIP/DNS DOS attacks will not be detected for TCP and SCTP protocol packets.

bugs.title: Category defaulted to whitelist when a valid category was not specified
bugs.symptoms: When a category not present was specified, a default of zero was being used which defaulted to Whitelist.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a nonexistent shun category.
bugs.impact: The category is set to the default, which is Whitelist.
bugs.fix: Category defaulted to whitelist when a valid category was not specified.

bugs.title: The big3d daemon does not receive config updates from mcpd
bugs.symptoms: Any Enterprise Manager device connected to a BIG-IP v11.6.0 will not receive configuration change notifications (including status) for nodes, pool members, or pools and will require manual refresh of configuration for those types. Stats and other configuration items remain unaffected.
bugs.conditions: This only affects EM devices and potentially MangementPack connections to a BIG-IP. The BIG-IP must be version 11.6.0 only, but the EM may be any version.
bugs.impact: The impact of this bug is that Enterprise Manager devices will not receive configuration update notifications for nodes, pool members, or pools. This includes status changes. Stats and other configuration items remain unaffected.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The mapping for subscription groups has been fixed so that the SUBSCRIPTION_NODE_ADDRESS and other similar subscription groups will not be overwritten by the SUBSCRIPTION_MONITOR group.

bugs.title: Packet loop in VLAN Group
bugs.symptoms: On an active VIPRION or vCMP guest with a VLAN Group configuration, the CPU usage unexpectedly rises, and traffic flowing through the device may experience high latency and packet drops. A packet capture shows packets looping internally between VLAN members of the VLAN Group.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using a VLAN Group (in Translucent or Transparent mode) on VIPRION hardware (including vCMP guest of a VIPRION), and an IP address conflict exists between the BIG-IP and another device on the VLAN Group. Note: The device causing the IP conflict may be unrelated to packets that are found looping in a packet capture.
bugs.impact: This results in high CPU usage and potentially unresponsive GUI. Traffic flowing through the VLAN Group may experience high latency and packet drops. The Self IP on the affected VLAN becomes almost impossible to reach.
bugs.workaround: Disable vlangroup.flow.allocate db variable to prevent flow creation for vlangroup forwarded packets.
bugs.fix: Internal vlangroup loop no longer occurs when the Translucent/Transparent vlangroup setting exists with a duplicate IP address.

bugs.title: HA mirroring can overflow buffer limits on larger platforms
bugs.symptoms: When using mirroring, some connections between HA peers may overflow buffers and enter a state in which the buffer is repeatedly reset due to overflow.
bugs.conditions: LTM logs show resets, usually within one minute of each other. Viewing tmctl ha_stat shows the 'overflows' count incrementing by one approximately every minute or less. The 'buffered' count then increases, until at the maximum the 'overflows' count increments again. This does not apply to cases in which client and server bandwidth are far in excess of mirroring bandwidth, nor to cases in which there are occasional but not frequent overflows.
bugs.impact: In this state, failover can lose more than the expected number of L4 connections, and no L7 connections are mirrored. Note that any failure invalidates L7 mirroring; L4 mirroring recovers from occasional HA connection failures including those related to overflow (provided the HA connection remains up for at least one minute after reconnecting).
bugs.workaround: Try increasing the statemirror.queuelen to 256 MB (the current maximum) until repeated buffer overflows stop. If overflows continue after the maximum is set, there is no further workaround.
bugs.fix: Increased the maximum statemirror.queuelen db variable limits. If necessary, the statemirror.queuelen can now be increased beyond 256 MB up to 1 GB. Note that increasing the statemirror.queuelen increases memory requirements to approximately twice the queuelen multiplied by the number of TMMs, and also increases the time required to detect an error in the mirroring connection. The statemirror.queuelen should be kept as low as possible to prevent repeated failure.

bugs.title: Fixed issue causing TunnelServer to crash during reconnect
bugs.symptoms: TunnelServer may crash in rare conditions during reconnect.
bugs.conditions: Crash may happens when PC wakes up after hibernate
bugs.impact: User sees confusing message about crashed TunnelServer.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue that caused TunnelServer to crash during reconnect.

bugs.title: [GTM] Move address from one HA redundant LTM to another could cause BIG-IP monitor fail
bugs.symptoms: [GTM] Move address from one HA redundant LTM to another could cause BIG-IP monitor failure.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP redundant LTM server configuration with one address at 'Address List' and another at 'Peer Address List', one of the addresses is moved from another.
bugs.impact: Only one of the redundant LTM systems get probed. If the probed LTM is standby, it ignores the probe request. Available BIG-IP redundant LTM server is marked down; the monitor does not work, and all hosted virtual servers are marked down.
bugs.workaround: In the GUI, delete the address from either the "Address List" or "Peer Address List" and click "Update". Then add the address to the other field and click "Update".

bugs.title: qkview will not collect lib directories.
bugs.symptoms: qkview collects subdirectories in /var/run. In 11.6.0, this directory contains symbolic links to /lib64 and /usr/lib64. These directories contain a lot of files that are static and not required for problem diagnosis.
bugs.impact: qkviews can take a long time to transmit and to interpret due to the large file size.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The lib directories /usr/lib64 and /lib64 will no longer be collected in qkview.
bugs.behavior: qkview now explicitly excludes file collection from the lib and lib64 directories (as well as /usr/lib and /usr/lib64).

bugs.title: Added options to troubleshoot client by disabling specific features
bugs.symptoms: It is impossible to turn off specific features on specific clients for troubleshooting purposes.
bugs.conditions: Always using Edge client
bugs.impact: Lack of these options made client troubleshooting difficult as the options could only be set on the server.
bugs.fix: Added following features: DWORD key Default value HKLM only ------------------------------------------------------------------ UseLocalProxy false yes EnableEdgeClientUpdate true yes EnableWebComponentsUpdate true yes EnableDTLSTransport (Bug484847) true no EnableNACompression true no EnableOptimizedTunnelCompression true no SessionChecksInterval 10000 no ------------------------------------------------------------------ ("false" == 0, "true" - any value except 0); Key: HKLM( or HKCU)\Software\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess Zero value for SessionChecksInterval disables this features completely. "HLKM only" means that that feature can be only be disabled/enabled by value located at HKLM sub-tree, features with "no" can be disabled using both HKLM (Local Machine) and HKCU (current User). CLIENT control channel is not yet implemented

bugs.title: IPs can be added for infinite duration
bugs.symptoms: Keyword 'infinite' is not seen as valid by tmsh. This fix allows the user to use 'infinite' as a valid input to tmsh.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure an infinite TTL via TMSH for shun list entries.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to add a shunned IP to a shun list with infinite TTL.
bugs.fix: This fix allows the user to use 'infinite' as a valid input to tmsh.

bugs.title: Logging might show unnecessary messages when Citrix Receiver connects to Storefront: err tmm[20105]: 01490563:3: 00000000: Access stats encountered error: Failed to add/delete session entry (ERR_NOT_FOUND).
bugs.symptoms: Logging might show unnecessary messages when Citrix Receiver connects to Storefront: err tmm[20105]: 01490563:3: 00000000: Access stats encountered error: Failed to add/delete session entry (ERR_NOT_FOUND).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when VDI log level is set to Debug.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP logs an error message: err tmm[20105]: 01490563:3: 00000000: Access stats encountered error: Failed to add/delete session entry (ERR_NOT_FOUND). This message is cosmetic and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: Set VDI log level to a level above Debug.
bugs.fix: Improved error logging to not show unnecessary messages on default level.

bugs.title: Tcl parks during HTTP::collect, and serverssl is present, data can be truncated
bugs.symptoms: If Tcl parks during HTTP::collect, and serverssl is present, data can be truncated. serverssl can send an 'early' EOF when notified by the server.
bugs.conditions: serverssl with a server that notifies SSL of connection termination. If Tcl is parked during a HTTP::collect call, then it is possible for the EOF to be placed before the data collected. If that occurs, then the data is dropped. Use of HTTP::collect in an iRule on the server-side. If HTTP::collect is called within the HTTP_RESPONSE_DATA event, the occurrence is much more likely.
bugs.impact: The server response is truncated.
bugs.fix: A response from the server is no longer truncated in some situations when the serverssl profile is combined with the use of the HTTP::collect iRule command.

bugs.title: AFM DoS ICMP sweep mitigation performance impact
bugs.symptoms: In AFM DoS, the performance of ICMP Sweep Vector Mitigation brings down the performance of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: ICMP Traffic levels at 4 million pps from ~100 Src IP addresses, with the AFM DoS Sweep vector enabled to mitigate ICMP traffic.
bugs.impact: Slower performance of the BIG-IP system. A lot of CPU is used to mitigate the AFM DoS Sweep vector.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable the AFM DoS Sweep vector for ICMP Traffic when the attack rate is over 4 Million pps.
bugs.fix: AFM DoS ICMP sweep mitigation performance issues have been alleviated.

bugs.title: A TCP profile with 'Rate Pace" or 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled fails to successfully establish a connection.
bugs.symptoms: TCP connection establishment fails on some virtuals.
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile with advanced options like 'Rate Pace' or 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled, needs to be in use.
bugs.impact: All TCP connections using a tcp profile which has advanced options like 'Rate Pace' or 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled will fail to establish a connection.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using the tcp profile options like 'Rate Pace' or 'Tail Loss Probe'. If these options are a must requirement then there is no other workaround, other than to upgrade to a build with fix.
bugs.fix: A TCP profile with 'Rate Pace" or 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled now successfully establishes a connection.

bugs.title: pkcs11d with a high thread count can result in high CPU utilization
bugs.symptoms: When pkcs11d is set to use a very high thread count, CPU utilization can increase dramatically.
bugs.conditions: The thread count for pkcs11d is set higher than the default.
bugs.impact: Less CPU available for other processes.
bugs.workaround: Do not set the db variable for pkcs11d thread count (/sys crypto fips external-hsm num-threads) higher than the default.

bugs.title: tmrouted daemon may core due to daemon_heartbeat
bugs.symptoms: In rare instances, tmrouted for dynamic routing may core with a message similar to the following: warning sod[8953]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat tmrouted fails action is restart.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely occurring issue that occurs due to timing-related interactions in dynamic routing operations.
bugs.impact: tmrouted cores and restarts.
bugs.fix: tmrouted now operates normally under these conditions.

bugs.title: APM client components are not using extended logging by default.
bugs.symptoms: If end users of APM are encountering issues, extended client logs are disabled by default. This makes troubleshooting more difficult, and you would need to work with the end user to enable extended logging and try to reproduce the symptom they are seeing.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for end users connecting to APM
bugs.impact: Extended logs are not present by default, which makes troubleshooting client-side issues more difficult
bugs.fix: APM client components are now using extended logging by default.

bugs.title: Software auto update schedule settings are not synced
bugs.symptoms: Software auto update settings are not synced between two devices in a sync group.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include performing a full sync with systems that have different auto-update settings.
bugs.impact: This can lead to software auto update settings not being consistent across two devices.
bugs.workaround: Adjust the software-update configuration on each device in a configuration synchronization group.
bugs.fix: Changed auto update settings to sync.

bugs.title: 'General database error' trying to view Local Traffic :: Pools :: Pool List.
bugs.symptoms: 'General database error' trying to view Local Traffic :: Pools :: Pool List.
bugs.conditions: Be in the Nodes List section with columns ordered by Address, and then navigate to Local Traffic :: Pools :: Pool List.
bugs.impact: Cannot view pool list. System posts 'General database error'.
bugs.workaround: Order the Nodes List by a column other than Address.
bugs.fix: 'General database error' no longer occurs when trying to view Local Traffic :: Pools :: Pool List from Nodes List when the nodes are sorted by address.

bugs.title: Traffic does not flow through VPN tunnel in environements where proxy server is load balanced
bugs.symptoms: VPN will appear to be established but no traffic will flow through the VPN tunnel.
bugs.conditions: VPN is established through proxy server. DNS returns different IP address for subsequent name resolution query for proxy server.
bugs.impact: No traffic flows through VPN tunnel.
bugs.workaround: Use IP address for proxy server instead of name.
bugs.fix: Resolved intermittent routing table issue that caused Traffic not to flow through tunnel if proxy server is load balanced.

bugs.title: F5_Inflate_text(o, incr, v) wrapper need to be fixed for case when o is script tag
bugs.symptoms: A web application can get an unrewritten dynamically-generated script when not using Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs when scriptTag.text='source script' and the browser is not Internet Explorer.
bugs.impact: As a result, the web application misfunctions.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The wrapper for scriptTag.text='source script' now rewrites 'source script' for all browsers.

bugs.title: Add needed attributes to AMI name during generation.
Software auto update schedule settings can be reset during a full sync
bugs.symptoms: After performing a full sync, the auto update settings of the target machine are reset to defaults.
bugs.conditions: Perform a full sync to a system that has non-default auto update settings.
bugs.impact: Auto update settings can get out of sync, and be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: After a full sync, ensure that the auto update settings on both systems are set as desired.
bugs.fix: The auto update settings no longer reset during a sync operation.

bugs.title: Request group incorrectly deleted prior to being processed
bugs.symptoms: After performing a full sync, sometimes the BIG-IP systems remain out of sync.
bugs.conditions: A full sync must be performed. There must be more than one active connection to mcpd, and one of them must get disconnected before the sync completes.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP systems remain out of sync even after a sync operation.
bugs.workaround: There are 2 possible workaround: 1) Reset device trust and then re-associate peer devices. 2) Set sync-leader using the following tmsh command. (You might need to run the command more than once until the cid.id of the lagging device is equal or greater than the peer unit.) 'tmsh modify cm device-group fail_over_group_name devices modify { name_of_standby_device { set-sync-leader } }'. Note: You can run the following command from the active device to view any cid.id mismatch, and if further set-sync-leader commands are necessary: 'tmsh run cm watch-devicegroup-device'.
bugs.fix: After performing a full sync, BIG-IP systems remain in sync as expected, even when active mcpd connections are deleted before the sync completes.

bugs.title: The pool members of a wide IP in Link Controller can not be modified once created
bugs.symptoms: After wide IP is created in the Linked Controller, a user cannot modify them from the GUI member page.
bugs.conditions: When trying to update the pool members of a wide IP in Link Controller, an error occurs.
bugs.impact: After wide IP is created in the Linked Controller, a user must use to use tmsh to modify members or use the GUI to delete the wide IP and recreate it with different virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to change pool members: tmsh modify gtm pool <pool name> members add { <server>:<vs> }.
bugs.fix: The pool members of a wide IP in Link Controller can now be modified from the GUI pool member page.

bugs.title: vs-index is set differently on each blade in a chassis
bugs.symptoms: The vs-index field on virtual servers differs on each blade in a chassis.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on chassis systems when creating a virtual server on a multi-blade VIPRION and on multi-blade vCMP guests.
bugs.impact: The recently created virtual server holds different vs_index across blades (typically, the virtual servers differ by one, when compared with the active blade). From that point on, every newly created virtual server carries that inconsistency, so that vs-index is set differently on each blade in a chassis.
bugs.workaround: Follow the procedure in SOL13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/000/sol13030.html) to clear the configuration cache and reload configuration after reboot.
bugs.fix: The vs-index is now the same on each blade in a chassis on a multi-blade VIPRION and on multi-blade vCMP guests.

bugs.title: Change the default value of pccd.hash.load.factor to 25
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes the firewall rule BLOB is very big even though the configurations do not seems to be very big.
bugs.conditions: The BLOB size depends on many factors such as Src/Dst IP addresses in a rule. There is no straightforward rule to estimate the size of the BLOB from static inspection of the rules. Two set of configurations that look very similar can generate BLOB of very different sizes sometimes.
bugs.impact: One factor that contribute to the BLOB size is the load factor (percentage of fullness) of the internal hash tables. The load factor specifies the minimum percentage of fullness that need to be reached before the table is expanded to a larger size.
bugs.workaround: You can manually set the hash load factor from 0 (don't check) to 75.
bugs.fix: The load factor controls the minimum percentage of fullness that need to be reached before the table is expanded to a larger size. Setting it to 25 by default prevent the firewall rule compiler from growing the table size too aggressively and results in big firewall BLOB.

bugs.title: User name case sensitivity issue
bugs.symptoms: Create a local user (for dynamic user too) starting with upper case. When responding to logon page, user can enter all lower case or upper case or any combination of the same. User gets authenticated, however, for all different combinations of user names, it creates an entry in memcache. Actually there should be only one. So when the user gets deleted, all other entries remains in memcache.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs While entering user name during logon page response.
bugs.impact: This issue causes dangling memcache entries which does not have accountability.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: While creating memcache entry, we now normalize the username into utf8 lowerecase. This makes sure, there is only one entry for all combination of usernames.

bugs.title: Active Directory Query doesn't populate all values of multi-value attributes
bugs.symptoms: If some attribute requested by Active Directory (AD) Query contains multiple values (for example, memberOf), then the last value is omitted in the corresponding session variable.
bugs.conditions: Active Directory attribute has multiple values.
bugs.impact: Access policy may make wrong decision based on session variables registered by AD Query.
bugs.fix: All values are now populated as session variables as expected.

bugs.title: Fallback may be attempted incorrectly in an abort after an Early Server Response
bugs.symptoms: After an Early Server Response, the BIG-IP system might attempt to generate a fallback response if an error occurs. However, the response has already partially egressed, so this does not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: Fallback configured or enabled by an iRule. An early server response triggers an error that leads to an Abort being raised. The Abort triggers a fallback response inappropriately.
bugs.impact: The server-side might read HTTP data structures after they have already been freed. A fallback can be generated on the server-side, leading to a use-after-free if the client side has already aborted.
bugs.fix: A fallback response is no longer inappropriately generated after an error after an Early Server Response.

bugs.title: Rare Watchdog Restart of TMM and Datastor
bugs.symptoms: The TMM and Datastor get killed and restarted by the watchdog process.
bugs.conditions: If the server pool is inadequate, or responses are too slow, datastor can experience a resource starvation problem.
bugs.impact: TMM and Datastor will be killed by the watchdog process.
bugs.workaround: None. This usually occurs when your server pool is experiencing problems, delays, or simply has too few servers to handle the load.

bugs.title: Information on "OPSWAT Integration Libraries V3" is missing from CTU report
bugs.symptoms: Information on "OPSWAT Integration Libraries V3" is missing from CTU report
bugs.conditions: "OPSWAT Integration Libraries V3" are installed on the PC.
bugs.impact: Information on "OPSWAT Integration Libraries V3" is not available in CTU report
bugs.fix: CTU report now includes information on "OPSWAT Integration Libraries V3".

bugs.title: Many 'tmsh save sys config gtm-only partitions all' stack memory issue.
bugs.symptoms: Suitably large GTM configurations can take longer to save to the bigip_gtm.conf file than the configured timeout.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when GSLB automatic configuration save is enabled, many changes are made that require configuration save, and the gtm.global-settings.general.automatic-configuration-save-timeout is less than the length of time it takes to save the configuration to file.
bugs.impact: Making numerous changes might lead to multiple instances of the save operation running simultaneously. Large memory consumption, potentially leading to a crash.
bugs.workaround: Set gtm.global-settings.general.automatic-configuration-save-timeout to a larger value or disable automatic configuration saving for GTM / GSLB.
bugs.fix: Simultaneous GTM configuration saves no longer occur, so memory is not consumed for them.

bugs.title: TMM might core when deleting an entry for a user in a Radius AAA cache
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash resulting in temporary loss of service
bugs.conditions: Radius AAA in use with user entries present.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when deleting a user in the Radius AAA cache.

bugs.title: Automated Phone Home update check time is randomized to prevent intermittent problem when all machines would access the service at once.
AAM concatenation set memory leak on configuration change
bugs.symptoms: When AAM configuration is reloaded, it can leak some data structures associated with concatenation sets
bugs.conditions: AAM provisioned and concatenation sets defined
bugs.impact: tmm memory consumption will slowly grow
bugs.workaround: restart tmm to free memory
bugs.fix: Reloading AAM configuration no longer leaks memory associated with concatenation sets.

bugs.title: The user inspection logic has been fixed.
MySQL performance
bugs.symptoms: MySQL usage would spike to 100% for extended periods of time.
bugs.conditions: Occurs after several thousand policy configuration changes have been made to the system.
bugs.impact: Slow ASM GUI pages.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A MySQL performance issue was fixed.

bugs.title: APM on a multi blade chassis: On an idle machine 'rewrite' processes can takes up to half CPU cycles.
bugs.symptoms: On an idle machine 'rewrite' processes can takes up to half CPU cycles.
bugs.conditions: APM on a multi blade chassis (this is debatable. Two attached SRs are for 5250V systems)
bugs.impact: APM box performance degaraded.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: An internal APM issue related to this Bug is fixed.

bugs.title: Signature reporting details for sensitive data violation
bugs.symptoms: ASM blocks some requests that match signatures of the 'XPath Injection' attack type, but specific details regarding the violations are not visible for the affected requests as the signatures match sensitive parameters.
bugs.conditions: Request with sensitive data, a signature match inside the sensitive data.
bugs.impact: You cannot view or learn about violations in the GUI for signatures that match on sensitive parameters.
bugs.workaround: Suggestions of how to acquire the sig id: 1. Attach a custom remote logger that includes the violation details field and the support id. Note: You can configure only these two. 2. Turn on the ATTACK_SIG logger module for the bd.log and grep for 'Matched SIGID:' messages. 3. Remove the sensitive configuration. Note: This might not work for your environment.
bugs.fix: Signature names that are matched inside sensitive data are now shown in the violation details in the Configuration utility.

bugs.title: Memory leak in monpd when LTM and AVR or ASM are provisioned
bugs.symptoms: When processing 'empty' reports (that is, reports containing no data), monpd has a memory leak.
bugs.conditions: This might happen when no traffic or data runs for more than 5 minutes through a module that reports to AVR, and therefore no data should be presented by AVR.
bugs.impact: Memory is gradually exhausted.
bugs.workaround: To prevent this issue, monitor memory usage and restart monpd prior to the system running out of memory.
bugs.fix: Previously, a memory leak in the monpd daemon occurred in some situations. It no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Navigation parameter from POST data is not reported
bugs.symptoms: A navigation parameter in the POST data is not reported.
bugs.conditions: -- Navigation parameter(s) are configured. -- A navigation parameter appears in the post data. -- The URL and the navigation parameter sums up to a specific size.
bugs.impact: The navigation parameter is not reported.

bugs.title: OSPF daemon asserts and generates core
bugs.symptoms: The OSPF daemon might assert if receiving a Link Status (LS) Update header with a length greater than 255 bytes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the LSA header length is greater than 255 bytes in length.
bugs.impact: OSPF daemon asserts and generates a core, which might cause a service outage.
bugs.fix: OSPF daemon no longer asserts when receiving a Link Status (LS) Update Packet with an LSA header whose length is greater than 255 bytes.

bugs.title: mib-2 ipAddrTable interface index does not correlate to ifTable
bugs.symptoms: The ipaddrTable's ipAdEntIfIndex value does not match the ifTable's ifIndex value for the same interface.
bugs.conditions: Using SNMP to monitor F5 and other network devices.
bugs.impact: Data in the mib-2 ifTable does not correlate to the data in the ipAddrTable.
bugs.workaround: Use the F5 MIB to monitor F5 devices.
bugs.fix: The ipaddrTable's ipAdEntIfIndex value now matches the ifTable's ifIndex value for the same interface.

bugs.title: Disable isession control channel on demand.
bugs.symptoms: Customers running into isession related issues.
bugs.conditions: This happens when APM has been running.
bugs.impact: TMM could run out of memory because of these issues.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: If customer does not need optimized tunnels, app tunnels, remote desktop then he can safely disable the db variable "isession.ctrl.apm" which disables isession. Then do "bigstart restart tmm apd" so that the db variable takes effect.

bugs.title: A possible TMM crash in some circumstances.
bugs.symptoms: If TCP::Close is called during the SSL handshake, the TMM might crash.
bugs.conditions: TCP::close is called during an SSL handshake
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: When closing the connection before or during an SSL/TLS handshake, use the "drop" or "reject" command instead of the TCP::close command.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer produces a core file when the TCP::close iRule command is executed during an SSL handshake.

bugs.title: Failover error message 'sod out of shmem' in /var/log/ltm
bugs.symptoms: You might see a failover error message 'sod out of shmem' in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs vary based on the configured shared memory usage.
bugs.impact: Failover might not function fully. System posts the message 'err sod[6300]: 01140003:3: Out of shmem, increment amount' in /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf.
bugs.workaround: Manually modify /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf as follows: Change this line: 'ha segment path: /sod table pages: 2' to this: 'ha segment path: /sod table pages: 4'. Save the file and reboot the system.
bugs.fix: Amount of shmem for sod has been increased.

bugs.title: AFM DoS Sweep Vector could log attack detected msgs from a non-attacking src IP
bugs.symptoms: When a AFM DoS Sweep/Flood attack is ongoing there is a chance that we could log a non-attacking src IP (which is sending packets which are below the detect threshold) as an attacker in the "attack_sampled" AFM DoS log message.
bugs.conditions: When the AFM DoS Sweep or Flood attack is ongoing, and we have multiple src IPs (attackers and non-attackers) sending packets which match the AFM DoS Sweep or Flood vector, we could see the "attack sampled" log from a IP which is not actually sending packets above the configured attack rate.
bugs.impact: The log message could list an innocent src IP as an attacker. In AVR also you could see this IP as an attacker.
bugs.workaround: None, since the log message is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Improved security logging to reduce incorrect messages.

bugs.title: Source Address Add field is not shown if some Source FQDN is set
bugs.symptoms: rGUI does allow FQDNs as an input for firewall rules.
bugs.conditions: Using pre-v12.0.0.
bugs.impact: Source Address Add field is not shown.
bugs.workaround: None. 11.6.1 and earlier does not support FQDNs as an input for firewall rules.

bugs.title: BD may crash within HTTP payload parser.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.conditions: Fix JSON parser issue with errors in escaped character - will not copy an error character.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: We fixed an issue of specific requests that sometimes caused the Enforcer to crash.

bugs.title: Internal misbehavior of the SPDY filter
bugs.symptoms: The SPDY filter incorrectly handles the error case in which a child flow is aborted.
bugs.conditions: A child flow that is aborted for any reason would trigger an superfluous ABORT event to be sent by SPDY.
bugs.impact: Potential disruption of valid client traffic, in theory.
bugs.fix: SPDY no longer sends superfluous aborts to an already aborting child flow.

bugs.title: tmm can crash and/or use the wrong CRL in certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: tmm can crash and/or use the wrong certificate revocation list (CRL) in certain conditions.
bugs.conditions: Several client-ssl profiles are configured with different CRLs. Then, either the CRLs are configured or the client-ssl profiles are deleted.
bugs.impact: tmm might crash and/or use the wrong CRL. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: When adding and deleting multiple client-ssl profiles configured with differing certificate revocation lists (CRLs), tmm no longer crashes and/or uses the wrong CRL.

bugs.title: Certain blade failure events may result in a 10+ second delay in failover occurring
bugs.symptoms: For certain blade failures scenarios the HA score on the remaining blades does not update, and thus a failover does not occur, for at least ten seconds. This is because the remaining blades wait for a ten second timeout period before marking the powered-off blade as down.
bugs.conditions: A blade is powered off via the serial console or the 'bladectl' command, or the blade is physically removed from the chassis, and the chassis is configured in an HA pair where the loss of a blade should result in a failover.
bugs.impact: The expected failover will not occur for at least ten seconds
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue.

bugs.title: SASPD monitor cores
bugs.symptoms: SASP monitor process core dumping during a state change.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the SASP monitor is configured in push mode.
bugs.impact: Pool member is marked down, which leads to monitor outage.
bugs.fix: SASP monitor no longer core dumps during a state change in push mode.

bugs.title: LSN_DELETE messages may not be logged in PBA mode
bugs.symptoms: LSN_DELETE messages are missing when in PBA mode, even if configured in the log profile.
bugs.conditions: An lsn-pool in PBA mode, a log profile that enables LSN_DELETE messages, and a connection that is torn down.
bugs.impact: Individual connection logs may be missing.
bugs.workaround: Use the PBA logging to determine which subscriber was using a translation endpoint.
bugs.fix: LSN_DELETE messages are now present when in PBA mode, if configured in the log profile.

bugs.title: DHCP: Need an upgrade script for DHCPRELAY virtuals for BIG-IP version 11.5 and 11.4
bugs.symptoms: When you upgrade from 11.4 or 11.5 to 11.6 configuration while you have a virtual of type DHCPRELAY, the configuration loading will fail.
bugs.conditions: The user must have DHCPRELAY virtual for this to happen.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that configuration load will fail until you fix the issue.
bugs.workaround: Manually go in bigip.conf and remove the udp{} profile and instead add dhcpv4 or dhcpv6 profile under this virtual. Also, you need to set the mode of operation (relay or forwarding) in that profile you are attaching. Forwarding mode work with unicast DHCP traffic, while Relay mode works with Broadcast or multicast traffic.

bugs.title: Using an SCF to modify a self IP address might cause problems
bugs.symptoms: The system encounters issues when you save a self IP in one SCF, then delete the self IP and recreate it using the same name but specifying a different IP address.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you load the SCF and try the delete/recreate a second time.
bugs.impact: The system posts an error similar to the following: 01070712:3: Cannot create IP address 10.10.10.5/27 in vlan 'internal' in rd0 - netlink error: 17 (File exists) - net/validation/routing.cpp, line 701
bugs.workaround: To work around this, you can run the command bigstart restart mcpd. As an alternative, you can issue the following commands prior to loading the scf file: 'tmsh delete net self <self_name>' 'ip addr delete <IpAddress>/<netmask> dev <vlan_name>.
bugs.fix: Fixed a problem where the user loads an SCF that has a different self IP than the current configuration the IP does not change.

bugs.title: Allow NTLM feature to be enabled with APM Limited license
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system has an APM Limited license, NTLM is silently disabled and the connection goes through. This breaks many (all) use-cases for Exchange + APM.
bugs.conditions: APM and Exchange are deployed together with APM Limited / Lite license.
bugs.impact: Exchange cannot be used with APM Limited license when NTLM frontend authentication is selected, which is used in essentially all APM + Exchange deployments.
bugs.fix: The NTLM frontend authentication (ECA) feature can now be used with an APM Limited license. Typically, this is for Exchange deployments.

bugs.title: Browser displays error in console in Firefox 3.6.22
bugs.symptoms: When using Websafe on some very old versions of Firefox, inspecting the browser's console shows a JavaScript error message.
bugs.conditions: End user browses a WebSafe protected page using Firefox 3.6.22.
bugs.impact: Browser's console shows a JavaScript error message.
bugs.workaround: Use a new version of Firefox.
bugs.fix: No errors are triggered when using Firefox 3.6.22.

bugs.title: Old password is not verified during password change from View client.
bugs.symptoms: Old password is not verified during password change from View client. When user's AD password is expired, the system requires the user to change it on logon. Typically for changing the password both old a new passwords are provided.
bugs.conditions: When user's AD password is expired.
bugs.impact: Old password is not verified during password change from View client.
bugs.fix: Now APM verifies the user's old password before submitting the new one to AD when native VMware View client is used.

bugs.title: The false positive has been fixed.
Possible response truncation when using an asynchronous iRule command in ICAP_RESPONSE event
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP client may receive only a partial response from the ICAP server after a long-running iRule in the ICAP_RESPONSE event on the internal virtual server.
bugs.conditions: A long-running iRule command executes asynchronously in the ICAP_RESPONSE event.
bugs.impact: HTTP client receives a partial response but the tail is truncated.

bugs.title: APD and APMD cores during shutdown.
bugs.symptoms: When apd and apmd shutdown while they are still processing, the system cores while accessing policy configuration data.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with a second apd or apmd process while an apd or apmd process is already running. The second apd or apmd process goes down (because one process is already up).
bugs.impact: During this shutdown process, the system cores.
bugs.fix: APD and APMD no longer core during shutdown of a second occurrence of APD or APMD.

bugs.title: Adding TCP iRules to PEM space
bugs.symptoms: TCP iRules are missing in the PEM space.
bugs.conditions: When writing iRules scripts in PEM space, TCP iRules is not working.
bugs.impact: TCP iRules are not functioning if trying to run in PEM space
bugs.fix: TCP iRules have been added to PEM space and thus functioning properly

bugs.title: Text in buttons not centered correctly for higher DPI settings
bugs.symptoms: When high DPI setting are used in Windows, text in buttons is not centered correctly and may run outside the boundaries of buttons.
bugs.conditions: User interface is displayed and user has set a higher DPI setting for Windows.
bugs.impact: Button text does not look correct.
bugs.workaround: Set DPI settings back to default.
bugs.fix: Buttons are now correctly scaled for Windows DPI setting.

bugs.title: Accessing Sharepoint web application portal interferes with IdP initiated SAML SSO
bugs.symptoms: Accessing SharePoint web application portal with SSO configured for path /* (as part of portal access resource item) first will break IdP intiated Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) single sign-on (SSO).
bugs.conditions: Having SharePoint Portal Access resource as well as SAML resource on full webtop. Access SharePoint application by clicking first on SharePoint icon on full webtop and then SAML resource causes SAML SSO to break.
bugs.impact: End user will see 404 NotFound page.

bugs.title: Very long FTP command may be ignored.
bugs.symptoms: FTP commands are delimited with carriage returns. If the BIG-IP system receives a large buffer with no carriage returns, then it passes the data through without inspecting for or acting on commands. Since the only commands the system acts on should be delimited within a reasonable size, this does not affect FTP behavior and protects the BIG-IP system against large amounts of data that is not FTP command data is passed across FTP.
bugs.conditions: If the FTP profile encounters command buffers that contain many carriage returns without valid command data.
bugs.impact: Then the buffers are passed on without inspection. Under normal conditions there is no impact. If there is invalid data followed by valid data, however, then the valid data may be ignored.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the FTP profile for traffic other than FTP.
bugs.fix: The FTP profile does not process invalid command data

bugs.title: Can not delete and re-create a new virtual server that uses the same virtual address in the same transaction

bugs.impact: Transaction may fail
bugs.workaround: Use create and delete in separate transactions
bugs.fix: Transactions where virtual servers are deleted and re-created with the same virtual IP address will now complete successfully.

bugs.title: Possible performance degradation in AWS cloud

To do so, use the following commands to: 1. set the appropriate DB variable to 0 (zero), and 2. restart tmm: 1. setdb Scheduler.UnicAsleepRxLimit.LTM 0. 2. bigstart restart tmm.
bugs.fix: Throughput and new connections per/sec are now comparable in AWS for SR-IOV enabled instances and in other instances.

bugs.symptoms: Cannot delete keys without extension .key (and certificates without extension .crt) using iControl SOAP.
bugs.conditions: You attempt to delete SSL certificates or keys without the .crt or .key extensions. Such objects may have been previously created using the tmsh utility.

bugs.fix: It is now possible to delete keys without extension .key (and certificates without extension .crt) using iControl SOAP.

bugs.title: APM MySQL database full as log_session_details table keeps growing
bugs.symptoms: APM stores session reporting data in "apm" MySQL database, under log_session_details table, but never does any cleanup. This causes the table to continuously grow. Eventually this consumes all disk, potentially corrupting the SQL data, and stopping services on the BIG-IP system that rely on MySQL.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: APM is provisioned; and 350M APM sessions are created over any period of time (each row in log_session_details consumes ~20 bytes).
bugs.impact: MySql volume (12G) will fill with data, potentially stopping or degrading services in the box that rely on MySQL. Including: ASM, AVR, APM Reporting, Web UI, and QkView.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to manually clean up the log_session_details table in MySQL database. First, retrieve the randomly generated MySQL password per box, using the following shell command as the root user. For example, # perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw PjL7mq+fFJ where PjL7mq+fFJ is the random password at MySQL installation in this example. Use this password in the following command for clean-up. # /usr/bin/mysql -uroot -pPjL7mq+fFJ --database=apm -e "delete from log_session_details where active = 'N';" This will delete all those rows that are referred to by an inactive session.

bugs.title: Client SSL profiles might fail to complete handshake, system logs critical-level error '01260000:2: Profile name-of-profile: could not load key/certificate'
bugs.symptoms: - SSL (e.g., HTTPS) virtual servers fail to negotiate SSL handshake. Operations on the device stall (not immediately fail). - At a packet capture level, the BIG-IP system acknowledges the Client Hello, but does not send a Server Hello. - System logs critical-level messages similar to the following whenever a user or the system modifies a virtual server: crit tmm[14270]: 01260000:2: Profile name-of-profile: could not load key/certificate.
bugs.conditions: This issue might occur after an upgrade at the time of the initial ConfigSync; the device that receives the initial ConfigSync is likely to be affected. This issue might also occur if an administrator makes changes to certificates and keys referenced by an SSL profile (for example, deletes and recreates a certificate or key with the same name), and then performs a ConfigSync to the peer device; the peer device may be affected.
bugs.impact: All traffic to affected SSL virtual servers is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: After a device has been affected, restarting the affected TMMs resolves the issue. Note that restarting TMM temporarily disrupts traffic (or causes a failover). You can restart the TMMs by running 'bigstart restart tmm' on the affected appliance, or 'clsh bigstart restart tmm' on an affected VIPRION system.
bugs.fix: SSL virtual servers now successfully negotiate SSL handshake, so the device no longer logs the following message: crit tmm[14270]: 01260000:2: Profile name-of-profile: could not load key/certificate.

bugs.title: HTTP compression might cause TMM crash in low-memory conditions
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash in HTTP compression in low-memory conditions when unable to initialize the compression provider.
bugs.conditions: HTTP compression is configured and TMM is low on memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove HTTP compression from the virtual to avoid the issue.
bugs.fix: HTTP compression now gracefully handles failed compression provider initialization.

bugs.title: Incorrect bash prompt for created admin role users
bugs.symptoms: Users created with admin or resource-admin roles with access to bash shell might show an incorrect prompt on the bash command line.
bugs.conditions: Created user with: - admin or resource-admin roles. - Bash command line access.
bugs.impact: Users might see the command line prompt referring to 'root' instead of the created user.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now shows the correct bash prompt for admin and resource admin roles for created users on the bash command line.

bugs.title: High CPU consumption and unresponsive interface of the menubar icon after 20-30 minutes
bugs.symptoms: MAC edge client has high CPU consumption and unresponsive interface of the menubar icon after 20-30 minutes
bugs.conditions: MAC Edge client usage for 20-30 minutes
bugs.impact: Hig CPU consumption and unresponsive menubar resource
bugs.fix: An issue with BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac consuming high CPU and having an unresponsive menu icon on OS X 10.10 Yosemite is now fixed.

bugs.title: No support in license files for 'hourly billing'.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use internal-only, non-production licenses for hourly billing purpose. License files contain 'internal development'-only designation.
bugs.conditions: -- Cloud installations of BIG-IP software. -- Attempting to use hourly billing.
bugs.impact: The 'internal development'-only licenses contain no support for hourly billing functionality.
bugs.fix: Production AWS License files have been updated to support hourly billing.

bugs.title: Access policy v2 memory leak during object deletion in tmm.
bugs.symptoms: A small memory leak everytime a per request access policy is deleted.
bugs.conditions: If the access policy delete was done before execute_access_policy' released the ref count, the access policy was getting deleted even though its still being used for one session. If the access policy delete was done when the access policy was not being used by any session, the access policy was not getting deleted.
bugs.impact: A small memory leak everytime a per request access policy is deleted.
bugs.fix: 1) In 'access_policy_add', increment the access policy reference count before adding the access policy to the global access policy hash table. 2) In 'release_access_policy' dont return 'access_policy->ref_count' at the end of the function. The 'access_policy' could have potentially been deleted and freed by this point. The return value is not really used so just dont return any value.

bugs.title: Large values may display as negative numbers for 32-bit integer variables in the MIB
bugs.symptoms: Some gauges in the MIB are incorrectly typed as 32-bit integers. This might cause large values to display as negative numbers.
bugs.conditions: Values that are incorrectly typed may display incorrectly.
bugs.impact: Display of values is incorrect.
bugs.fix: MIB variables have been correctly typed as Gauge32, which is unsigned, and will not display as a negative number when it grows large.
bugs.behavior: before fix [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] images # tmsh modify ltm pool bob queue-depth-limit 4000000000 [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] images # snmpwalk -v 2c -c public localhost F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolQueueDepthLimit F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolQueueDepthLimit."/Common/bob" = INTEGER: -294967296 [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] images # after fix [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh create ltm pool test [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh modify ltm pool test queue-depth-limit 4000000000 [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # snmpwalk -v 2c -c public localhost F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolQueueDepthLimit F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolQueueDepthLimit."/Common/test" = Gauge32: 4000000000 [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config #

bugs.title: Increased the timeout after starting VM.
Rarely seen Edge Client for Mac crash on session disconnect
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client crashed a couple of times in persistent testing on session disconnect.
bugs.conditions: Long persistent connection to APM.
bugs.impact: Edge Client crashes on session disconnect, but restarting Edge Client works fine.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, restart Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac now gracefully handles session disconnect on long-lived persistent connections.

bugs.title: With fastL4, incorrect MSS value might be used if SYN has options without MSS specified
bugs.symptoms: Due to the incorrect MSS value, TMM might core because based on the MSS value the outgoing packet attempts to use TSO, which is not correct. This can result in a crash.
bugs.conditions: A virtual using fastL4 where a SYN packet with options is received, but the SYN packet does not contain an MSS option.
bugs.impact: If this issue occurs, then TMM will core resulting in a failover/reboot of the system.
bugs.fix: The correct MSS value is now used when SYN has options without MSS specified, so TMM no longer cores.

bugs.title: TMM/APMD fail to communicate when handling a large amount of data under high load conditions.
bugs.symptoms: VPN users begin to report that they are unable to connect to a normally functioning (but busy) APM virtual. The virtual server is using an iRule configured with ACCESS::POLICY evaluate.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using the 'ACCESS::POLICY evaluate' iRule with a large number of new users per second when handling a large amount of data.
bugs.impact: Multiple failures. The system posts messages similar to the following in debug tmm logs with failing policy execution: notice acs_mpi_send/912: ACS: IPC send channel stuck!
bugs.fix: TMM/APMD now properly communicates when handling a large amount of data under high load conditions.

bugs.title: APM sends a logout Bookmarked Access whitelist URL when session is expired.
bugs.symptoms: You will see a logout page for bookmarked APM whitelist URL after session is expired.
bugs.conditions: This condition will occur if the user has bookmarked a APM whitelist entry and tries to access this bookmarked URL after some time (Access session is expired).
bugs.impact: User sees a logout page instead of a logon to revalidate themselves.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: If a session is expired and a query is made with an Access whitelist and query parameters, APM code did not handle the case properly and sent a logout page. APM now enables the user to revalidate by starting the Access policy again.

bugs.title: In some traffic situations, virtuals using SSL can excessively buffer client data instead of closing the TCP window
bugs.symptoms: In some traffic situations, TMM can excessively buffer client data instead of closing the TCP window. This buffering occurs based on internal race conditions that are not directly controllable. This occurs only when the BIG-IP is providing SSL termination or origination. In extreme circumstances with a slow connection, this could ultimately lead to out of memory situations.
bugs.conditions: The virtual must be providing SSL termination and/or origination.
bugs.impact: Increased memory usage, possibly leading to tmm crashing.
bugs.fix: Flow control through SSL is consistent and no longer leaves the chain misordered on flow control.

bugs.title: Restrict the permissions for private keys
bugs.symptoms: Use security best practices for keys on BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Protected keys to industry best practices.
bugs.fix: The permissions for SSL keys are more restricted.

bugs.title: MCP continues running after "Unexpected exception caught in MCPProcessor::rm_DBLowHighWide" error
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd configuration errors on secondary blades of a VIPRION platform may disrupt data plane functionality. As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom: The system logs messages in the /var/log/ltm file that appear similar to the following example: -- err mcpd[7624]: 01070935:3: Unexpected exception caught in MCPProcessor::rm_DBLowHighWide(). -- err bcm56xxd[5081]: 012c0010:3: Error trunk <trunk_name> on unit 0 does not exist bsx.c(2429).
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The mcpd process is restarted on a secondary blade of a VIPRION platform. -- The mcpd process receives an error when attempting to load the configuration. For example: err mcpd[7624]: 010717b5:3: HA group (HA) cannot be removed. It is used by traffic group (/Common/traffic-group-1 ).
bugs.impact: VLAN and trunk members are not programmed correctly, resulting in disrupted traffic flow. If a trunk has members spanning multiple blades, and if the trunk hashing algorithm selects a member port on a secondary blade for a given traffic flow, that traffic flow will be disrupted.
bugs.fix: The system now handles these conditions so that the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: No Access error when trying to access iFile object in Local Traffic :: iRules : iFile list
bugs.symptoms: After uploading a file to the system and creating the iFile object, the user is unable to access the object.
bugs.conditions: Uploading a file to the system and creating the iFile object.
bugs.impact: The system posts a No Access error, and the user is unable to access the iFile object
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Accessing iFile object in Local Traffic :: iRules : iFile list now works correctly and no longer produces No Access error.

bugs.title: vlan-groups configured with a single member VLAN result in memory leak
bugs.symptoms: If a vlan-group contains only a single member VLAN, tmm begins to leak memory as observed in 'tmctl memory_usage_stat'.
bugs.conditions: Configure a vlan-group with a single member VLAN.
bugs.impact: Continuous memory leaks might eventuallyresult in traffic disruptions.
bugs.workaround: Remove vlan-groups containing a single member VLAN or configure at least two member VLANs per vlan-group
bugs.fix: Single-member vlan-groups no longer leak memory.

bugs.title: Internal objects can have load failures on restarted blades
bugs.symptoms: If the primary blade of a chassis is reset, once it rejoins the cluster as a secondary its configuration may fail to load with errors that look like this: 01070088:3: The requested object name (/Common/default-eviction-policy) is invalid. 01070935:3: Unexpected exception caught in MCPProcessor::rm_DBLowHighWide(). 01070734:3: Configuration error: MCPProcessor::check_initialization: 01070734:3: Configuration error: URL category (/Common/Abortion) cannot be deleted. It is being used by a URL filter.
bugs.conditions: This only affects chassis.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that mcpd will not finish startup unless the workaround steps are performed.
bugs.workaround: Log in to the affected blade, remove the binary database (/bin/rm -v /var/db/mcp*), and restart all services on the blade (bigstart restart).
bugs.fix: Formerly, the primary blade of a chassis is reset, once it rejoins the cluster as a secondary its configuration may fail to load with errors that look like this: 01070088:3: The requested object name (/Common/default-eviction-policy) is invalid. 01070935:3: Unexpected exception caught in MCPProcessor::rm_DBLowHighWide(). 01070734:3: Configuration error: MCPProcessor::check_initialization: 01070734:3: Configuration error: URL category (/Common/Abortion) cannot be deleted. It is being used by a URL filter. The system will now load successfully and not hit this error.

bugs.title: Overlapping vCMP guest MAC addresses
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent traffic disruptions such as unexpected resets and drops may occur as the result of MAC address conflicts between vCMP guests on an affected hypervisor and/or conflict with other F5 devices with adjacent MAC address ranges.
bugs.conditions: MCPD has restarted on a vCMP hypervisor, and vCMP guest instances with more than 2 VLANs are deployed after the MCPD restart.
bugs.impact: Intermittent traffic disruptions such as unexpected resets and drops.
bugs.workaround: 1. Restart vCMPD on the hypervisor. 2. Re-deploy the vCMP Guest by setting it to "Configured", then "Deployed" again. Note, you need to set to "Configured", not "Provisioned".
bugs.fix: MAC address conflicts no longer occur between vCMP guests when the vCMP hypervisor is running a fixed version. If a vCMP guest running a fixed version detects that the hypervisor has provided an invalid set of MAC addresses, the guest will log an error similar to err chmand[28121]: 012a0003:3: unexpected init failure : VcmpPlatform: MAC pool size from hypervisor is zero crit chmand[28121]: 012a0002:2: critical platform initialize failure. exiting... and not start.

bugs.title: when iSession control channel is disabled, don't assign app tunnel, MSRDP, opt tunnel resources
bugs.symptoms: Customers running into iSession related issues.
bugs.conditions: This happens when APM has been running.
bugs.impact: Some of the Network Access resources may not run properly when iSession control channel is disabled.
bugs.fix: When the iSession control channel is disabled through db variable, then some of the Network Access resources, including App tunnel, Microsoft RDP, and optimized tunnel resources, will not be assigned to the session.

bugs.title: TMM crashes if iRule PSC::ip_address is used after RADIUS Authentication of DHCP discovery.
bugs.symptoms: Using iRule PSC::ip_address can cause TMM crash after RADIUS authentication of DHCP discovery is conducted.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure DHCPv4-based subscriber discovery in Relay mode. 2. Configure RADIUS Authentication for DHCPv4 profile. 3. Using PSC::pa_address command in an iRule for RADIUS Authentication virtual 4. Initiate RADIUS authentication process.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The fix fixes the crash problem in using the PSC::ip_address with the RADIUS authentication process

bugs.title: Serial number of a blade is not cleared in show command after it is moved
bugs.symptoms: In a partially populated chassis, if a blade is moved from one slot to another, the serial number is still shown in the previous slot from this command: guishell -c "select slot_id, serial_number from chassis_slot" The stale serial number is also visible in the user interface.
bugs.conditions: In a partially populated chassis, a blade is moved from one slot to another.
bugs.impact: This issue is not harmful, but displays incorrect information.
bugs.workaround: The brute-force workaround is to reboot chassis.

bugs.title: Cached route MTUs may be set to the value of TM.MinPathMTU even if the path MTU is lower than that value.
bugs.symptoms: ICMP type 3 code 4 (needsfrag) messages are elicited when TMM transmits packets at the TM.MinPathMTU size if the path MTU is lower than that value.
bugs.conditions: Path MTU discovery results are cached by default. If a client responds to an IP datagram with an ICMP needsfrag message with a very small MTU (smaller than the value of the TM.MinPathMTU database variable), the cached path MTU value will be set to the TM.MinPathMTU value even though this still isn't able to traverse the path. This can affect multiple endpoints when a low MTU is advertised by an endpoint (misconfigured or malicious) behind a shared NAT address.
bugs.impact: TMM may use and enforce a low path MTU for clients capable of handling a higher path MTU, but may use an MTU too high to reach clients whose path MTU is lower than TM.MinPathMTU. This metric will live for 10 minutes by default.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time. The route metric lifetime can be lowered using route.metrics.timeout db key.
bugs.fix: Path MTUs lower than the value of TM.MinPathMTU will no longer be cached by TMM.

bugs.title: Configure the client of choice to be launched from APM webtop
bugs.symptoms: Currently, for VMware View resources a modal dialog prompting the user to choose the preferred client is shown whenever they launch an application. For Citrix, the client used is determined by heuristics checking the presence of Citrix Receiver on the user system or HTML5 client bundle on APM. Now, for both types of resources the preferred client can be set by the administrator. For VMware View, this client will be launched immediately (if available) without a modal dialog. For Citrix, this will also apply as long as the chosen client is available.
bugs.conditions: VMware View or Citrix resource configured and assigned to the webtop.
bugs.impact: Provide better control over the client to be used for launching applications to the administrator.
bugs.fix: Administrators can now enforce which VDI client is used on APM Webtop: native or HTML5. For VMware View, the preferred client can be set in the VMware View Policy agent in VPE. For Citrix, the session variable session.citrix.preferred_client needs to be set to either "html5" or "native".

bugs.title: Unrecognized EDNS0 option may be considered malformed.
bugs.symptoms: Unrecognized edns0 option may be considered malformed and dropped by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Client sending queries with non-standard edns0 option code. The BIG-IP system is configured with a DNS profile.
bugs.impact: All queries containing unrecognized option code are dropped. RFC says unrecognized options MUST be ignored.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, write an iRule to parse binary UDP payload; remove option from edns0 record.
bugs.fix: Unrecognized DNS EDNS0 options are now ignored.

bugs.title: tmm might crash under load when logging profile is used with packet classification
bugs.symptoms: When tmm is under heavy load it may run out of memory and crash under certain conditions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1. Packet classification is enabled 2. Security logging profile is used with 'log translation fields' option enabled. 3. Fast flow forwarding is enabled on forwarding virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, do one of the following: -- Disable 'log translation fields' in the security logging profile. -- Disable fast flow forwarding.
bugs.fix: This fixes a memory leak when TMM is overloaded and forwards flows to the peer, and packet classification is enabled with 'log translation fields' in the logging profile.

bugs.title: If Identify as Username is enabled for a parameter, the Encrypt checkbox is not grayed out.
bugs.symptoms: If "Identify as Username" is enabled for a parameter in URL Properties under FPS Profile, the "Encrypt" checkbox is not grayed out.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS.
bugs.impact: Application Encryption may not work properly when selecting the Encrypt checkbox.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: If Identify as Username is enabled for a parameter, the Encrypt checkbox becomes grayed out. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: When creating or modifying URL properties in an anti-fraud profile, under the Parameters tab, there is the following limitation: If Identify as Username is enabled, Encrypt is permanently disabled. And if Encrypt is enabled, Identify as Username is permanently disabled.
Failed to add/delete session entry (ERR_NOT_FOUND)
bugs.symptoms: You see the following log entries in /var/log/ltm: err tmm[10575]: 01490558:3: 00000000: Access stats encountered error: Failed to add/delete session entry (ERR_NOT_FOUND) Clients may report a “session already in progress” warning when they try to go to one protected resource, and then another, without logging in first.
bugs.conditions: -- APM configured, access policy in use -- Client reaches the logon page but does not log in
bugs.impact: Log message is logged to /var/log/ltm. It can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: Change to signature list of manual Signature Sets does not take effect.
bugs.symptoms: When the signature list of a manual Attack Signature Set is modified, the change does not affect enforcement or remote logging.
bugs.conditions: The signature list of a manual Attack Signature Set is modified (with no other change to the Signature Set).
bugs.impact: The change does not take effect in signature enforcement or remote logging.
bugs.workaround: Any spurious change to the signature set (such as unchecking/checking 'Assign to Policy by Default'), or unassigning and reassigning the signature set to the affected policy.
bugs.fix: When the signature list of a manual Attack Signature Set is modified, enforcement and remote logging are now updated correctly.

bugs.title: RADIUS accounting message with multiple IPv6 prefix causes TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: When RADIUS Accounting message contains multiple Framed-IPv6-Prefix AVPs all these AVPs except the first one are parsed incorrectly, and in some cases may lead to tmm crash with core.
bugs.conditions: RADIUS Subscriber discovery is enabled in PEM. RADIUS Accounting message contains multiple Framed-IPv6-Prefix AVPs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: For adding multiple IPv6 prefixes into a single PEM session use multiple RADIUS Accounting messages containing a single Framed-IPv6-Prefix AVP for each. The tmm.pem.session.provisioning.continuous sys db variable should be set to true.
bugs.fix: Fixes the TMM crash problem, and radius accounting message with multiple IPv6-prefix is now parsed correctly.

bugs.title: Nitrox got stuck when processed certain SSL records
bugs.symptoms: During decryption, Nitrox queue got stuck when processed certain SSL records.
bugs.conditions: Nitrox device is used to decrypt SSL records.
bugs.impact: The Nitrox device queue got stuck.
bugs.fix: Ensure SSL record is not malformed before sending it to Nitrox for decryption.

bugs.title: Delete firewall rule in GUI changes port settings in other rules to 'any'
bugs.symptoms: Using the GUI to delete a network firewall rule causes a change to other rules that specify ports.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the GUI to delete a firewall rule, and there are other rules that are limited to specific ports.
bugs.impact: The port changes to 'any' in all network firewall rules that specify ports. For example, any firewall rules that match traffic on port '80' change to match on port 'any' when this issue occurs.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh, iControl, and BIG-IQ to manage firewall rules. Use port lists instead of specifying ports. These could include lists with a single port.
bugs.fix: Using the GUI to delete a rule no longer changes ports specified in other rules to 'any.'

bugs.title: BIG-IP crash when processing packet and running iRule at the same time
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system sometimes crashes if it is processing packets and iRules at the same time.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include having iRule scripts and processing iRule tasks, and processing incoming traffic along with the iRule tasks.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the BIG-IP system goes to crash intermittently.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed the iRule processing problem that is causing the BIG-IP to crash while processing incoming packets.

bugs.title: The aced process may restart in a loop
bugs.symptoms: The aced process may restart in an infinite loop if a parent process cannot start. This can result in a user not being able to log in using their valid SecurID credentials. You may notice repeated "re-starting aced" messages in the log file.
bugs.conditions: If a parent process dies, the child process may hold server port 60000. If this occurs, then new parent process cannot start.
bugs.impact: RSA SecurID authentication fails
bugs.fix: Now, the aced process behaves as expected. A child process never listens at server port.

bugs.title: Clientside or serverside command with parking command crashes TMM
bugs.symptoms: Any parking iRule command used inside clientside or serverside crashes TMM.
bugs.conditions: Parking command used inside clientside or serverside.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: See if you really need to run the parking command inside clientside/serverside, if not, move the command outside.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when an iRule executes a parking command inside a 'clientside' or 'serverside' context-switching command.

bugs.title: Alerts have been reordered.
Virtual Edition second installation slot and VMWare
bugs.symptoms: You cannot install TMOS on 2nd slot on BIG-IP VE 11.5.1 LTM-only image for VMWare.
bugs.conditions: The LTM-only BIG-IP VE deployed on VMWare.
bugs.impact: Inconvenience. As a workaround , you must manually delete 2nd slot and then do the installation.
bugs.workaround: [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # tmsh install sys software image BIGIP-11.6.0.0.0.401.iso volume HD1.2 [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # tmsh show sys software ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Sys::Software Status Volume Product Version Build Active Status ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 yes complete HD1.2 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 no failed (Disk full (volume group). See SOL#10636) [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # tmsh delete sys software volume HD1.2 [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # tmsh show sys software --------------------------------------------------------------------- Sys::Software Status Volume Product Version Build Active Status --------------------------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 yes complete HD1.2 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 no failed to delete volumeset [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # reboot # Login again: [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] config # tmsh show sys software --------------------------------------------------- Sys::Software Status Volume Product Version Build Active Status --------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 yes complete [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] config # cd /shared/images [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # tmsh install sys software image BIGIP-11.6.0.0.0.401.iso volume HD1.2 create-volume [root@cblee_11:LICENSE EXPIRED:Standalone] images # tmsh show sys software --------------------------------------------------- Sys::Software Status Volume Product Version Build Active Status --------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 yes complete HD1.2 BIG-IP 11.6.0 0.0.401 no complete
bugs.fix: OVA will only create 1 slot and leave the remaining disk space free.

bugs.title: After updating a key/certificate in place and synchronizing the configuration, TMM may log critical-level messages that it could not load a key, certificate, or chain.
bugs.symptoms: After updating a key/certificate in place and synchronizing the configuration, TMM may log critical-level messages about loading a key, certificate, or chain.
