bugs.conditions: A certificate and/or key referenced by an SSL profile are deleted and then recreated, and then that is synchronized (via a full sync, not an incremental sync) to peer devices.
bugs.impact: In 11.5.0 and later, this message indicates an issue that impacts traffic to affected virtual servers: 01260000:2: Profile /Common/otters: could not load key/certificate. In versions earlier than 11.5.0, these messages can safely be ignored: -- 01260000:2: Profile /Common/otters-ssl: could not load key file. -- 01260000:2: Profile /Common/otters-ssl: could load neither certificate nor chain file
bugs.fix: TMM still log critical-level messages, but the system function properly and traffic is not affected.

bugs.title: Messages logged when registering with LOP daemon (lopd) or CAN daemon (cand)
bugs.symptoms: When the log filter is configured to filter at the 'Informational' log level, the logs can get filled with 'client /var/run/lopd.chmand.lopuns already registered' messages when registering with either the Lights Out Processor daemon (lopd) or the CAN daemon (cand). These messages appear in the log every two seconds on systems with lopd, or every 20 seconds on systems with cand.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using a remote syslog logging filter with the 'Severity' field set to 'Informational'.
bugs.impact: Logs fill with messages. These messages are related to communication with the Lights Out Processor daemon (lopd) or with the CAN daemon (cand), and are completely benign, so you can safely ignore them.
bugs.workaround: Change the remote syslog logging level to 'Notice'.
bugs.fix: Reduced the log level for registering with the LOP (lights out processor) and CAN daemon (cand) to the debug level.

bugs.title: Users not able to log on after failover
bugs.symptoms: Users fail the access policy check after failover happens. The command 'configdump -allkeys' does not display any entry for the access profile.
bugs.conditions: The issue will show up after the following events: 1. The TMM on the active node restarts or crashes, the node become standby. 2. TMM and APD restart. APD re-creates config snapshots in the SessionDB. 3. The snapshots just created get deleted. 4. Failover happens again and the node becomes active. 5. Users fail to log on
bugs.impact: Users cannot log on
bugs.workaround: Run 'bigstart restart apd' to re-create config snapshots.
bugs.fix: APM checks config snapshots periodically and recreates them if any are missing.

bugs.title: TCP and UDP was classified as Unknown by classification library
bugs.symptoms: When traffic didn't map to any of the supported Application Layer protocol/service it was classified as Unknown which is misleading and doesn't provide enough granularity.
bugs.conditions: Traffic didn't map to any of the supported Application Layer protocol.
bugs.impact: Misleading classification results
bugs.fix: Instead of classifying traffic as Unknown we will now tag flows as TCP or UDP depending what type of traffic is seen by the classification library

bugs.title: interface STP state stays in blocked when added to STP as disabled
bugs.symptoms: When two interfaces are disabled and added to Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) in the VLAN configuration, the second interface stays in 'blocked' STP state.
bugs.conditions: At least two interfaces exist in disabled state, added to STP.
bugs.impact: The blocked port does not send out data.
bugs.workaround: If the STP flag is disabled and re-enabled on the blocked interface, after the port is enabled, the port STP status is re-evaluated to the correct state.
bugs.fix: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) now checks for the disabled state of the port before adding it as an STP member.

bugs.title: QinQ tag-mode can be set on unsupported platforms
bugs.symptoms: tmsh does not validate QinQ tag-mode and allows invalid values to be set.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when trying to set QinQ tag-mode to values other than 'none' on unsupported platforms. Only platforms with ePVA support QinQ tagging.
bugs.impact: Although you can set !in! tag-mode, the configuration has no effect. There is no negative impact on system functionality.
bugs.workaround: Only configure QinQ tag-mode on the following platforms: BIG-IP 5050s/5250v/7050s/7250v/10050s/10250v and VIPRION B2150 SSD-based models.
bugs.fix: QinQ tag-mode is now properly validated when configuring a VLAN via tmsh.

bugs.title: APM Portal Access is inaccessible.
bugs.symptoms: APM Portal Access is inaccessible.
bugs.conditions: One of sessions reaches 64 KB of Portal Access application cookie storage.
bugs.impact: Rewrite plugin crashes; APM Portal Access becomes inaccessible. Shortly after this plugin crashes with *** glibc detected *** memory-corruption-message. The rewrite daemon log contains following lines: - notice rewrite - cookie.cpp:543 : updateCookieSessionStore : expiring cookie ...
bugs.fix: Rewrite plugin no longer crashes when Portal Access application cookies require more than 32 KB of storage.

bugs.title: Certificate_summary is not created at peer when the chain certificate is synced to HA peer.
bugs.symptoms: The other Peer of a high-availability (HA) pair cannot show the summary of cert-chain by 'tmsh run sys crypto check-cert verbose enabled' after config-sync.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: 1. On the command line or in the GUI, setup an HA Pair 2. Import Certificate chain to one BIG-IP system. 3. 'run config-sync' to sync the Certificate chain to the peer BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: After a ConfigSync operation, the certificate chain summary is not created on other HA peers.
bugs.workaround: Copy the cert-chain file to a place (such as /shared/tmp/), and update the cert-chain using a command similar to the following: modify sys file ssl-cert Cert-Chain_Browser_Serv.crt source-path file:/shared/tmp/Cert-Chain_Browser_Serv.crt_58761_1

bugs.title: Incremental sync of iApp changes may fail
bugs.symptoms: Incremental sync of the deletion of an iApp instance may fail, with the error message indicating that certain objects owned by the application are still in use. Alternatively, child objects that should have been deleted when reconfiguring an iApp instance may remain on peer devices after incremental sync has completed.
bugs.conditions: Incremental sync of the deletion of an iApp instance. Incremental sync of deleting a child object, if the iApp implementation script creates the parent object without child objects, and then separately adds the replacement child objects.
bugs.impact: An attempt to delete an iApp may cause a sync failure. An attempt to reconfigure an iApp without a previously existing child object (pool member, etc.) may cause the object to continue to exist on peer devices.
bugs.workaround: Full load sync (either the 'Overwrite Configuration' option on the Device Management Overview page, or temporarily setting the device group to full load only), and then performing the sync operation completes successfully.
bugs.fix: Incremental sync of the deletion of an iApp instance now completes successfully. Incremental sync of iApp changes, where the iApp template creates a parent object separately from child objects now syncs correctly.

bugs.title: aws-failover-tgactive.sh doesn't skip network forwarding virtuals
bugs.symptoms: When there are forwarding virtual servers with SNATs defined in the configuration, the reassignment of IP addresses for virtual servers does not happen correctly in Amazon Web Services (AWS).
bugs.conditions: Forwarding virtual servers with SNATs defined.
bugs.impact: HA failover is impacted.
bugs.fix: The reassignment of IP addresses for forwarding virtual servers with SNATs defined in the configuration now occurs as expected in Amazon Web Services (AWS).

bugs.title: DTLS cannot be disabled on Edge Client for troubleshooting purposes
bugs.symptoms: There is no client side option to disable DTLS. This option can be very useful in troubleshooting client connectivity issues.
bugs.conditions: It is required to debug DTLS versus TLS connections.
bugs.impact: Troubleshooting connectivity issues becomes difficult.
bugs.workaround: Disable DTLS on server side.
bugs.fix: Now you can add new registry keys and use them to disable DTLS on both BIG-IP Edge Client and browsers. Using these keys, you can disable DTLS on a particular client without changing the BIG-IP system configuration. To disable DTLS on a client machine: Create registry DWORD value (keys are both valid for both x64 and x86 systems): HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess\EnableDTLSTransport or HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess\EnableDTLSTransport and set to 0

bugs.title: Citrix remote desktop visible even if the user cannot access it
bugs.symptoms: When a remote desktop has auto logon enabled and has no resources assigned for the user, its folder icon is still visible from APM webtop.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with APM with Citrix XML Broker Integration with Dynamic Web top, and you have users configured to not use the desktop
bugs.impact: These users can see the remote desktop.
bugs.fix: Now when a remote desktop has auto logon enabled and has no resources assigned for the user, its folder icon is hidden from APM webtop.

bugs.title: A standby-standby state can be created when auto failback acts in a CRC disagreement scenario
bugs.symptoms: A standby-standby state can occur after a failback if there is a CRC disagreement between peers.
bugs.conditions: HA pair using auto failback. There must be a CRC disagreement between peers. The failback preferred system must have a lower traffic group score than its peers. NOTE: CRC disagreements may lead to other issues and the customer is strongly advised to sync the devices to remove the disagreement.
bugs.impact: It's a site down situation as all the objects in the traffic group will become unreachable.
bugs.workaround: Sync devices to remove the CRC disagreement.
bugs.fix: Ensure that the preferred system goes active after auto failback, even if its traffic group score is lower than that of its peers.

bugs.title: UDP connflow may aborted from parked iRule in server_closed.
bugs.symptoms: Some UDP idle flows will abort a parked iRule after the UDP idle timeout.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: 1) UDP virtual, drop connection on response. 2) client_closed and server_close iRule, and parked in irule for a long time 3) make the the virtual expired when iRule is parking.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is the iRule aborts and impacts performance. The user cannot keep accurate connection count per client using iRules.
bugs.workaround: Set the idle timeout to a different value in client and sever will make it happen much less frequently.
bugs.fix: Resolve problem of double calling functions that caused iRule to abort.

bugs.title: MCPD cores when the Check Service Date in the license is not current.
bugs.symptoms: MCPD cores when the license has not been reactivated, causing the Check Service Date to be before the release date, and there are modified default profiles in the config.
bugs.conditions: A license with a check Service Date before the release of the current version and a config with modified default profiles.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not function.
bugs.workaround: Reactivate the license prior to upgrade.
bugs.fix: MCPD no longer cores when the license has not been reactivated, the Check Service Date is before the release date, and there are profiles in the config.

bugs.title: RADIUS::avp replace command cores TMM when only two arguments are passed to it
bugs.symptoms: The RADIUS::avp replace iRule command will core when only two arguments are passed to it.
bugs.conditions: Must be running an iRule that executes a RADIUS::avp replace command with only two arguments.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when only two arguments are passed to the RADIUS::avp replace command.

bugs.title: wom_verify_config does not recognize iSession profile in /Common sub-partition
bugs.symptoms: The wom_verify_config does not recognize iSession profile in /Common sub-partition.
bugs.conditions: iApps creates some objects (virtual, profiles) under /Common/DMZPrimary.vysbank.com.app/. These objects are invisible to wom_verify_config.
bugs.impact: wom_verify_config cannot verify the system configuration.
bugs.fix: The wom_verify_config now recognizes objects in sub-partitions.

bugs.title: Support for TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV
bugs.symptoms: Virtual servers configured with a Client SSL profile do not support the Transport Layer Security (TLS) Fallback Signaling Cipher Suite Value (SCSV) in Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) ClientHello transactions.
bugs.fix: When the SSL ClientHello contains the SCSV marker, if the client protocol offered is not the latest that the virtual server supports, a fatal alert will be sent. For more information, see SOL16935: Support for the TLS Fallback SCSV https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/900/sol16935.html

bugs.title: TMM might crash if unable to find persistence cookie
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash and generate a core if unable to find persistence cookie.
bugs.conditions: Although specific conditions for this issue are unknown, it is possibly due to having a virtual with cookie persistence enabled and iRules that disable persistence.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM now verifies that a persistence cookie was successfully found before extracting it from HTTP responses.

bugs.title: LDAP agent does not escape '=' character in LDAP DN
bugs.symptoms: Starting from BIG-IP 11.6.0, session variables may have modifiers when used in configuration, such as: %{session.logon.last.ldap.dn:ldapdn} With session variable modifier "ldapdn", the resultant value should be escaped by LDAP DN rules. The rules include an equals (=) character which should be escaped, but it is not.
bugs.conditions: LDAP session variable that contains LDAP DN is used in configuration with "ldapdn" session variable modifier.
bugs.impact: Depends on the purpose of usage session variable with "ldapdn" modifier in a configuration.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to escape '=' character using the Variable Assign agent before using that session variable with the modifier in other configurations.
bugs.fix: Now the session variable modifier "ldapdn" escapes the equal sign (=) character as well as other characters that require escaping.

bugs.title: AVR core witch include tmstat backtrace
bugs.symptoms: due to a synchronization problem in AVR, some tmstat data (relevant to AVR only) got corrupted. This corruption can cause AVR core.
bugs.conditions: Provision AVR.
bugs.impact: This bug cause AVR core.
bugs.fix: The synchronization problem fixed.

bugs.title: Enable directory protection
bugs.symptoms: PATH_INFO feature does not support any directory protection.
bugs.conditions: Configuring directory without dot '.' in its name as protected URL with turned on PATH_INFO feature.
bugs.impact: The configured directory contents are not protected.
bugs.workaround: Only directories with dot '.' in their name can be configured as protected by turning on PATH_INFO feature.
bugs.fix: Enabled protection on a complete directory of protected URLs.

bugs.title: Fixed root cause of crash - improper memory managment.
TMM dumps core file when loading configuration or starting up
bugs.symptoms: TMM dumps core file when configuration file is being loaded or when TMM is starting up.
bugs.conditions: This error happens when there is no APM license installed.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly handles configuration load when there is no APM license.

bugs.title: Click-to-Run version of Office 2013 does not work inside PWS (Protected WorkSpace)
bugs.symptoms: Click-to-Run Office 2013 applications fail to start inside Microsoft Windows Protected Workspace without any error message.
bugs.conditions: Click-to-Run version of Office 2013 is used under PWS
bugs.impact: Click-to-Run version of Office 2013 does not work inside PWS
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, use the full installation of Office 2013.
bugs.fix: Click-to-Run Office 2013 applications can start inside Microsoft Windows Protected Workspace (PWS) now.

bugs.title: EncryptedAssertion may not be processed by BIG-IP as SP when EncryptedKey element is specified by RetrievalMethod Element by external IdP.
bugs.symptoms: An encrypted assertion from an external SAML Identity Provider (IdP) can contain the RetrievalMethod element to specify a link to the EncryptedKey element. The EncryptedKey element contains the key for decrypting the CipherData associated with an EncryptedData element. BIG-IP configured as a Service Provider (SP) does not support the RetrievalMethod element while processing an encrypted assertion. As a result, the assertion is not processed properly, and error messages are printed to the log files: "Cannot decrypt SAML Assertion" and "failed to process encrypted assertion, error: Cipher value from EncryptedKey element not found".
bugs.conditions: External IdP uses RetrievalMethod to specify EncryptedKey element. BIG-IP is configured as SP. BIG-IP requires received assertions to be encrypted.
bugs.impact: Authentication will fail due to inability to process assertion.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, reconfigure IdP to use embedded EncryptedKey instead of using RetrievalMethod.

bugs.title: Online help about persistent cookies does not specify supported use
bugs.symptoms: Online help for creating an access profile and for creating SSO/Auth Domains does not specify that persistent cookies are supported only in an LTM-APM configuration.
bugs.conditions: Online Help
bugs.impact: Help page is unclear.
bugs.fix: Online help has been updated to clarify the use of persistent cookies for SSO Across Authentication Domains. Persistent cookies are supported only when a session is started using an LTM-APM access profile type.

bugs.title: TMM might restart under certain conditions when executing SLO.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart when Single Logout (SLO) request/response contains an invalid 'Issuer' attribute.
bugs.conditions: SLO is configured on BIG-IP as SP or IdP. SLO request or response is received from SP/IdP for which there is no current session.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable SLO.
bugs.fix: The system now handles Single Logout (SLO) response/request so that TMM no longer restarts.

bugs.title: iRule virtual command allows for protocol mismatch, resulting in crash
bugs.symptoms: iRule 'virtual' command allows for protocol mismatch.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server with an iRule which leverages the 'virtual' command targeting a virtual server that differs in protocol. For example, a UDP virtual server targeting a TCP virtual server.
bugs.impact: tmm might crash with assert: 'Must be syncookie'. Traffic is interrupted.
bugs.workaround: This is the result of a misconfiguration. Modify iRules to ensure L4 protocols match between virtual servers.
bugs.fix: Resolved issue where TMM might crash with assert: 'Must be syncookie' when the iRule 'virtual' command leads to a protocol mismatch.

bugs.title: Default SNMP community 'public' is re-added after the upgrade
bugs.symptoms: If the SNMP default community (public) has been removed from the configuration, and a new version of the software is installed, the default community will be added to the new configuration.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the SNMP default community will be added to the new configuration.
bugs.workaround: After upgrading to versions after 11.4.0, delete the default 'public' community again.
bugs.fix: The default community string 'public' is not add to the SNMP configuration on upgrade if it has been deleted in the previous software configuration
bugs.conditions: A software upgrade after the default community string has been removed.

bugs.title: Tag <NameIDFormat> in SAML metadata may contain wrong attributes
bugs.symptoms: When Big-IP is used as SAML IdP, SAML metadata could contain invalid NameIDFormat, e.g.: <NameIDFormat Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:SOAP" index="0" isDefault="true">urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress</NameIDFormat>
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as IdP. SAML Artifact Resolution Service is not configured.
bugs.impact: Metadata could fail to be imported to external Service Providers.
bugs.workaround: Manually correct metadata. E.g. replace this: "<NameIDFormat Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:SOAP" index="0" isDefault="true">urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress</NameIDFormat>" with this: "<NameIDFormat>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress</NameIDFormat>"
bugs.fix: Issue where SAML metadata Tag NameIDFormat would contain invalid information under certain conditions is now fixed.

bugs.title: TMM crashes while executing multiple FLOW_INIT events and one of the event triggers an abort.
bugs.symptoms: Critical system failure due to TMM process restarting.
bugs.conditions: Following conditions may suffice to trigger the TMM crash: AFM rule match triggers an iRule execution with multiple FLOW_INIT events and one of the events will cause the connection to be aborted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: A crash bug when executing multiple FLOW_INIT events has been fixed.

bugs.title: Firewall ACL counters for staged policy attached to a Virtual/SelfIP are not incremented when a policy with a similar rule to drop/reject packets is enforced by the Global or Route Domain context
bugs.symptoms: Staged ACL Rule attached to VS or Self IP will never be hit if similar Rule with drop/reject action attached to an upper context as Enforced.
bugs.conditions: Policy should be staged at the Virtual or SelfIP context and enforced at the Global or Route Domain level. The action should be drop/reject.
bugs.impact: Staged policy counters are not incremented correctly. Example: We have 2 FW Policies (Policy1 and Policy2) with the same Rules: security firewall policy Policy1 { rules { Rule1 { action reject destination { addresses { 10.10.10.11 { } } } } } } Policy1 attached to Global context as enforced: security firewall global-rules { enforced-policy Policy1 } Policy2 attached to VS as staged: ltm virtual VS4_TCP { destination 10.10.10.11:any fw-staged-policy Policy2 ip-protocol tcp ...... } If we send traffic to hit this rule: Policy1:Rule1 will be hit but Policy2:Rule1 will not be hit. tmctl -w120 fw_rule_stat context_type context_name rule_name micro_rules counter last_hit_time ------------ ------------ --------- ----------- ------- ------------- global Rule1 1 10 1413898646 tmctl -w120 fw_staged_rule_stat context_type context_name rule_name micro_rules counter last_hit_time ------------ --------------- --------- ----------- ------- ------------- virtual /Common/VS4_TCP Rule1 1 0 0
bugs.fix: Counters for staged ACL rules now increment even when a match at a broader context is enforced. For example, a staged ACL rule in a policy assigned to a Virtual Server will now have policy counters increment even if an enforced policy assigned at the Global or Route Domain context matches.

bugs.title: The mcpd process may leak memory when using tmsh to modify user attributes
bugs.symptoms: The Master Control Program Daemon (mcpd) may leak memory when you use the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) to modify user attributes. Note: The mcpd process is the messenger process that allows userland processes to communicate with the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM), and the other way around. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- You are unable to configure the BIG-IP system. -- You are unable to obtain statistics, or statistics may not be accurate. -- In the /var/log/ltm file, you may observe an error message similar to the following example: 02001018:system library:fopen:Too many open files
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: -- You are using the tmsh modify auth <user> command options to modify local user accounts. Some of the options include the following: description User description. partition-access The administrative partition which user has access. password Set or modify the user password. role Specifies the user role for the user account. shell Specifies the shell to which the user has access.
bugs.impact: -- You cannot obtain or update the system status. -- You cannot configure the BIG-IP system. -- Userland processes may not be functional.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue. To restore mcpd functionality, you can restart mcpd from the command line. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of procedure: Restarting the mcpd process interrupts all traffic processing on the BIG-IP system. You should perform this procedure during a maintenance window. Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: tmsh To restart the mcpd process, type the following command: restart sys service mcpd
bugs.fix: Ensure all user directory file descriptors are closed.

bugs.title: Unable to apply ASM policy with forwarding CPM policy via GUI, generic error
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to apply an ASM policy to a virtual server that is using LTM forwarding, the user interface spits back an error: "an error has occurred while trying to process your request."
bugs.conditions: Happens only in rare situations.
bugs.impact: Local Traffic Virtual Servers : Virtual Server List <http_vip> >> Security >> Policies... Receive ERROR: "An error has occurred while trying to process your request"
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: TMM may core when an APM virtual server has a OneConnect profile attached to the virtual server
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core if an APM virtual server detaches from its current resource and attaches to a different resource while handling requests.
bugs.conditions: This crash is most likely to occur when an APM virtual server is configured with a OneConnect profile. However, as long as there is the possibility that the resource APM should connect to is decided after the client connection is established (e.g., based on the HTTP Host header), this issue is possible. This would include iRules that change the backend resource, the load balancer makes a decision to switch the resource, or APM is configured to possibly interface with a number of different resources.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: If OneConnect is present, removing its profiles from APM virtual servers greatly reduces the likelihood of this issue occurring. If the issue occurs without OneConnect, the other mitigation is to place APM in its own virtual, configured to interface with a layered virtual which remains constant. The layered virtual may then use iRules or load balance as normal. The APM virtual server cannot detach from one resource and re-attach to a different resource.
bugs.fix: APM virtual servers that can cause the resource to switch during request handling (as is most noticed with OneConnect profiles attached to them) will no longer cause TMM to crash and restart.

bugs.title: OSPF redistributing connected subnets that are configured in the network element with infinity metric in a HA pair.
bugs.symptoms: In a HA pair setup, the active node is sending an As_External Link-State Advertisement (LSA) with infinity metric value for the redistributed connected subnets that are configured in the network element of the OSPF.
bugs.conditions: HA pair with redistributed connected subnets and subnets configured in the network element in the OSPF.
bugs.impact: The active node in the HA pair sends an LSA with infinity metric that gets exchanged in the other networks affecting the routing process.
bugs.workaround: Clear ip ospf process fixes the issue. However, it is not an effective solution in a production environment.
bugs.fix: OSPF sessions in an HA pair doesn't send an As_External LSA for the subnets that are configured as network element and redistributed as connected subnets.

bugs.title: Machine Info Agent should have a fallback branch
bugs.symptoms: Machine Info agent is not supported for legacy logon clients (for example, mobile clients and Linux CLI); it is only supported for web logon clients (browsers and BIG-IP Edge Clients). However, the Machine Info agent does not throw any error if a legacy logon client connects to APM with the Machine Info agent in it.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with a Machine Info agent in the access policy and legacy logon clients.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the Machine Info agent does not create any machine information-related session variables for legacy logon clients, neither does it indicate that it is not supported.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, use the Client Type agent to distinguish between legacy logon or web logon clients. And then only add the Machine Info agent in web logon clients branch.
bugs.fix: The Machine Info agent now differentiates between legacy logon clients and web logon clients by creating an error session variable. The error session variable is set to 1 when legacy logon clients connect to APM and 0 otherwise.

bugs.title: Application Layer encryption not working on password field in certain situations
bugs.symptoms: URL matching did not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: Other HTTP header like Referrer also contains '?'.
bugs.impact: Plugin side of vCrypt and other configured features is not working.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed the application layer encryption for certain situations.

bugs.title: License activation may not proceed if MCPD is not fully operational
bugs.symptoms: When the MCPD is not fully started, the activation process may fail.
bugs.conditions: When the MCPD service is not fully operational, and an attempt is made to perform activation, the activation may fail, due to incomplete data in the message to the activation service.
bugs.impact: Activation of license may not succeed.
bugs.workaround: Wait until MCPD is fully operational before performing license activation.
bugs.fix: Activation function has been modified to eliminate dependency on the MCPD.

bugs.title: APM logon page missing title
bugs.symptoms: On the BIG-IP APM logon page, a title may not appear.
bugs.conditions: RSA error message contains newline symbols. (For example RSA 8.1 uses such message)
bugs.impact: May cause usability issues.
bugs.fix: Now the title displays correctly on the logon page; RSA error messages are now sanitized.

bugs.title: Fixed synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes caused TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.
Enabled protection is queried before requests are sent.
The datasyncd process may keep restarting during the first 30 minutes following a hotfix installation
bugs.symptoms: After an installation of an 11.6.0 hotfix, the datasyncd process may keep restarting during 30 minutes. This is rare, but if it does happen, the system will remain offline during this time, until the state is automatically recovered.
bugs.conditions: An 11.6.0 hotfix is being installed on a system that is already running 11.6.0, and has either ASM or FPS provisioned.
bugs.impact: During 30 minutes following the hotfix installation, the system remains offline and does not handle traffic.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: We corrected a rare scenario that caused a machine to remain offline for 30 minutes after an 11.6.0 hotfix installation.

bugs.title: French translation does not properly fit buttons in BIG-IP Edge client on Windows
bugs.symptoms: French translation does not properly fit buttons in BIG-IP Edge Client on Windows-based systems.
bugs.conditions: French translation in BIG-IP Edge Client on Windows.
bugs.impact: Text does not fit buttons.
bugs.fix: Translated French text has been corrected to properly fit buttons in BIG-IP Edge Client on Windows-based systems.

bugs.title: Prevent wamd shutdown cores
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances, wamd cores while trying to exit.
bugs.conditions: wamd during shutdown.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary core files generated consuming some resources.
bugs.fix: wamd no longer cores and now exits gracefully when shutting down.

bugs.title: Unable to configure a virtual server with Stats profile and SIP profile in 11.6.0
bugs.symptoms: Profile validation unintentionally prevents using a Stats profile with a SIP profile in the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: Unable to add a Stats profile to a virtual server containing a SIP profile.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: You can now configure both a Stats profile and a SIP profile in the same virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure a Stats profile with a SIP profile in the same virtual server.

bugs.title: iApp re-deployment causes mcpd on secondaries to restart
bugs.symptoms: iApp redeployment causes mcpd on secondaries to restart.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when redeploying iApps with the locally cached files in place.
bugs.impact: mcpd restarts on secondaries.
bugs.fix: iApp redeployment now works correctly, and no longer causes mcpd on secondaries to restart.

bugs.title: TCP MSS is incorrect after ICMP PMTU message.
bugs.symptoms: After ICMP PMTU message, new TCP packets are well below the maximum size.
bugs.conditions: After receiving ICMP PMTU messages, which leads to use of undersized TCP packets.
bugs.impact: Reduced throughput of TCP connections.
bugs.workaround: Configure TCP MSS to the true value.

bugs.title: audit_forwarder sending invalid NAS IP Address attributes
bugs.symptoms: Forwarded auditing messages contain the incorrect nas-ip-address attribute. It should be the local IP of the box. Instead nas-ip-address is another, random IP address.
bugs.conditions: This seems to work fine when the BIG-IP is a virtual machine.The issue reproduces only on the actual hardware.
bugs.impact: Cannot pass certification because config auditing is not working as expected (invalid NAS IP Address).
bugs.fix: Forwarded auditing messages now contain the correct nas-ip-address attribute, so config auditing is now working as expected.

bugs.title: Fixed Network Access renegotiation procedure
bugs.symptoms: Network Access reconnects on every SSL renegotiation attempt on Windows 7 for TLS1.2 and TLS1.1 if client cert is requested.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: Windows 7. -- TLS 1.1/TLS1.2. -- Client cert set to 'required' at Virtual Server's Client Cert profile.
bugs.impact: Reconnect on every SSL renegotiation attempt.
bugs.fix: Fixed Network Access renegotiation procedure on TLS1.1 and TLS1.2 for Microsoft Windows 7.

bugs.title: Interrnal build improvement for AMI generation
Network Access should provide client IP address on reconnect log records
bugs.symptoms: Network Access should provide client IP address on reconnect log records
bugs.conditions: - Connect a client via network access - observe log of Client IP - Disconnect and reconnect from a different client IP (or the same one)
bugs.impact: note that the log messages generated for the session do not include the client IP address.

bugs.title: GUI PVA connection maximum statistic is always zero
bugs.symptoms: The GUI PVA connection maximum statistic is always zero, regardless of the number of PVA connections established.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when fastL4 connections are used.
bugs.impact: The customer cannot determine the maximum number of PVA connections because the stat is always zero.
bugs.fix: Improved the statistics for updating the number of PVA connections when using fastL4.

bugs.title: After upgrading from v10 to v11 in a FIPS HA setup, config-sync fails
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from TMOS v10 to TMOS v11 in a FIPS HA setup, config-sync will fail.
bugs.conditions: In a FIPS HA setup, upgrade from v10 to v11. After upgrade, trigger config-sync.
bugs.impact: HA devices will be in sync failed state
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Config-sync will now be successful after upgrading from v10

bugs.title: GUI creating key files with .key extensions in the name causing errors
bugs.symptoms: When using the GUI, if a user adds a '.key' extension to the name, the file will be created with an extra .key extension to the file.
bugs.conditions: When a key file name is 'test.key' entered from the GUI it is created with 'test.key.key'.
bugs.impact: The extra '.key' extension causes problems with deletion/Archive etc. GUI posts the following error: Not Found.
bugs.workaround: Delete the key and recreate without the .key in the name.
bugs.fix: The GUI will prevent names with reserved extensions such as '.key'.

bugs.title: Maximum connections is not accurate when TMM load is uneven
bugs.symptoms: Maximum connections is not accurate when TMM load is unevenly distributed. Maximum connection statistics report the sum of maximum connections per TMM, not the maximum connections virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the load disaggregated to available TMMs is uneven.
bugs.impact: This causes the various TMMs to measure their individual maximum connections at significantly different times, resulting in higher-than-expected maximum connections.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the configuration matches traffic patterns, so the load of connections is evenly distributed across all TMMs.

bugs.title: Management port unreachable after install
bugs.symptoms: Management port IP address does not respond to pings after upgrade/reboot.
bugs.conditions: Install upgrade to 11.2.1-hf-tmos build 1454 (a pre-release build of 11.2.1 HF14).
bugs.impact: Problems in build 1454 prevent the correct initialization of the management interface. This build should not be installed.
bugs.workaround: Install 11.2.1 HF14 or later.
bugs.fix: Resolved installation error in a pre-release build of 11.2.1 HF14 that caused the system to fail to initialize the management port. The officially released 11.2.1 HF14 does not have this problem.

bugs.title: lsn-pool connection limits may be invalid when mirroring is enabled
bugs.symptoms: A client may not be able to create as many connections as allowed because mirroring may cause a connection to be counted more than once against the connection limit.
bugs.conditions: An lsn-pool with connection limits enabled, assigned to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Clients may not be able to open as many connections as they should be able to open. The connections will fail.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: With the fix in place, clients may open the full number of allowable connections.

bugs.title: WebSafe signatures were updated.
There is no syslog destination for dosl7 logging
bugs.symptoms: It's not possible to configure the syslog destination for dosl7 logging.
bugs.conditions: A customer wants to configure a syslog destination for dosl7
bugs.impact: There is an error message when attempting to attach to the virtual server a publisher that has a destination with a non splunk/arcsight destination.
bugs.workaround: A possible workaround should be to send the splunk logging to another machine that has syslog-ng configured as logger and alertd to make traps from it. (not nice)

bugs.title: HTTP Protocol Compliance options should not be modified during import/upgrade
bugs.symptoms: HTTP Protocol Compliance options are enabled upon version upgrade or security policy import from a prior version.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when configuration was upgraded to 11.6.0, or security policy was imported from prior version to 11.6.0.
bugs.impact: HTTP Protocol Compliance options are enabled.
bugs.workaround: Set HTTP Protocol Compliance options to desired values after import/upgrade.
bugs.fix: HTTP Protocol Compliance options are correctly preserved after a security policy import or a version upgrade.

bugs.title: The vCMP guest lost watchdog heartbeat, and the host restarted it.
bugs.symptoms: The guest on one slot stops activating its watchdog for 30 seconds, and the host vcmpd restarts the guest. The host logs messages: -- 01510014:1: vCMP guest <guestname> heartbeat timeout at the halfway mark. -- 01510013:1: vCMP guest <guestname> lost heartbeat. In a multi-slot guest, the other, unaffected guest slots /var/log/ltm can report 'clusterd FAILED' and show evidence of the faulty slot going down.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown. This is a rarely encountered issue.
bugs.impact: Guest restart on one slot.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time. To assist in capturing potential missed messages from the guest serial console, beginning in version 12.0.0, you can enable the db variables vcmp.guest.console and vcmp.guest.console.logging to log the output to a host-side file. To activate the logging, the guest must be re-deployed.

bugs.title: GUI iFile delete confirmation page lists incorrect items to be deleted
bugs.symptoms: When deleting iFile objects from the GUI, all items listed on the confirm delete page display the name of the first iFile object. The correct items are still deleted, so this issue is cosmetic only.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when deleting any iFile object that is not the first one when ordered alphabetically. For example, in a configuration with three iFiles named 'Aardvark,' 'Anteater,' and 'Avalanche,' electing to delete Anteater and Avalanche in a single operation results in a delete confirmation page that displays two delete-confirmation entries, each of which shows the name 'Aardvark.' Similarly, when attempting to delete Anteater alone, the screen shows the name 'Aardvark.'
bugs.impact: The iFile confirm-delete page shows the wrong items. The correct items are deleted. This bug is cosmetic only and does not impact functionality
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh for deleting iFile objects
bugs.fix: When deleting iFile objects from the GUI, the delete-confirmation page now lists the correct items to be deleted.

bugs.title: tmm intermittently reports that it cannot find FIPS key
bugs.symptoms: You may see the following critical error message in /var/log/ltm: "FIPS acceleration device failure: cannot locate key"
bugs.conditions: There is FIPS card in the BIG-IP and the key is retrieved. It is not known the exact conditions that cause this, but it seems to be related to GTM being enabled.
bugs.impact: SSL can not locate the key from the FIPS card, and SSL will not function properly.
bugs.workaround: None known, but restarting tmm or rebooting might correct the condition.
bugs.fix: SSL can now correctly locate the key from the FIPS card, and SSL will function properly.

bugs.title: Enahnced support for proxy servers that resolve to multiple IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: VPN might fail to connect in environments where DNS returns multiple IP address for the proxy server host name. This includes both Edge client and web client.
bugs.conditions: Proxy server name is resolved to multiple IP address, or the proxy server IP address changes on a subsequent call to the DNS resolver.
bugs.impact: VPN connection might fail.
bugs.workaround: Configure DNS to persist an IP addresses for the proxy host name.
bugs.fix: Added support for scenarios where proxy host name resolves to multiple addresses.

bugs.title: Cannot remove a profile from a virtual server and delete it inside a transaction
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to remove a profile from a virtual server and delete that same profile within a transaction, the system returns an error indicating that the profile is not found.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server configured with a profile.
bugs.impact: Delete operation does not complete.
bugs.workaround: Remove the profile and then delete it in separate transactions.

bugs.title: vCMP guests are unable to access NTP or RSYNC via their management network.
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to access an external NTP server or RSYNC server from within a vCMP guest over the management network fails to pass traffic.
bugs.conditions: This issue affects vCMP guests running any BIG-IP software version when running on a vCMP hypervisor running software version 11.6.0.
bugs.impact: vCMP guests are unable to configure an external NTP server reachable over the management network.
bugs.workaround: An NTP server may be configured using a self-ip and the data plane network without issue. If access is required via the management port, execute the following steps: 1) Add the commands iptables -t nat -D PREROUTING -m physdev --physdev-in mgmt_vm_tap_+ -j ACCEPT iptables -t nat -I PREROUTING 1 -m physdev --physdev-in mgmt_vm_tap_+ -j ACCEPT to /config/startup on the vCMP hypervisor. This will ensure the workaround persists across reboots. 2) Run the following command at the vCMP hypervisor bash prompt: clsh iptables -t nat -I PREROUTING 1 -m physdev --physdev-in mgmt_vm_tap_+ -j ACCEPT Rebooting the hypervisor or affected guests is not required.
bugs.fix: An issue has been corrected which affected NTP and RSYNC access via the management network in vCMP guests.

bugs.title: VDI plugin crashes when View client disconnects prematurely
bugs.symptoms: VDI plugin crashes when View client disconnects prematurely
bugs.conditions: View client disconnects prematurely
bugs.impact: VDI plugin crash
bugs.fix: VDI plugin does not crash when View client disconnects prematurely

bugs.title: BD crash upon stress on session tracking
bugs.symptoms: An ASM bd process crash occurs in a specific scenario that involves system stress and session tracking, or the crash can be reached rarely from slow responses/servers with session tracking.
bugs.conditions: ASM under heavy load, session tracking is running.
bugs.impact: A bd process crash, failover, and/or traffic resets.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a system crash scenario that occurred with session tracking.

bugs.title: Enable Bittorrent classification in Qosmos by default
bugs.symptoms: Due to poor accuracy of bittorrent classification field is asking to have qosmos enabled by default. This was tested as part of the SR investigation and confirmed working at a customer site.
bugs.conditions: Running BitTorrent for a long period of time.
bugs.impact: Poor accuracy of classification of BitTorrent traffic.
bugs.workaround: tmsh modify sys db tmm.gpa.cec.behavioral_protocols value 183,271,553,580,597,1040,1041,842
bugs.fix: Bittorrent classification is now enabled in Qosmos by default.

bugs.title: triplets-not-allowed threshold too high because LTM minimum requirements for 6G guests are coming from 8G table
bugs.symptoms: The system might post the following error when the provisioned modules should be supported: 01071008:3: Provisioning failed with error 255 - 'Physical memory (6144MiB) insufficient for 3 or more modules.'
bugs.conditions: VCMP guests and VE guests with memory between 5632 MiB and 6250 MiB.
bugs.impact: Not allowed to provision more than 3 modules.
bugs.workaround: Create VCMP guests with 4 or more CPUs. Configure the VE guests with more than 6250 MiB of memory available.
bugs.fix: Three or more modules can be provisioned on VCMP guests and VE guests having 5632 MiB or more memory.
bugs.behavior: You are now allowed to provision any number of combinations of modules on platforms with 5.5 GiB of memory or more so long as there are resources available. Previously, 3 or more modules were not allowed to be provisioned on platforms with 6 GiB or less. Note that Application Acceleration Manager (AAM) cannot be provisioned with any other module; AAM can only be provisioned standalone.

bugs.title: FPS alerts
bugs.symptoms: Fraud Protection Service (FPS) alerts are not being sent.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using FPS.
bugs.impact: Alerts for the user credentials are not being sent.
bugs.fix: Improved alerting for Fraud Protection Service (FPS).

bugs.title: System might reuse TCP source ports too quickly on the server side.
bugs.symptoms: System might reuse TCP source ports too quickly on server side when dag hash is ip-only and sourceport mode is set to change.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the dag-cmp hash is ip-only, and the virtual server or PEM-forwarding endpoints sourceport mode is set to change. The BIG-IP system might reuse some TCP source ports on the server side.
bugs.impact: Conflicting flows result in connections being reset.
bugs.fix: In this release, reuse of TCP source ports is sequential, which eliminates the issue of TCP source ports being used too quickly on the server side.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Addition of a DoS Profile Along with a Required Profile May Fail
bugs.symptoms: Certain DoS Profiles require a preliminary profile to be attached as well. For example DNS enabled DoS profile may require DNS profile to be attached first. However in cases where both profiles are being attached at the same time, an error may be thrown telling the user that the required profile is not attached.
bugs.conditions: A DoS profile needs to be attached at the same time with its required profile. For example, Application DoS Profile requires HTTP profile to be attached as well.
bugs.impact: If you have such DoS profiles in use and attach such profiles in single transaction you may be affected (GUI operations or iControl REST api).
bugs.fix: It is now possible to attach a DoS Profile and a required supporting profile in a single transaction.

bugs.title: The allowed range of 'status-age' in OCSP Stapling Parameters (for clientSSL OCSP Stapling) might not be wide enough for some of the scenarios
bugs.symptoms: The allowed range of 'status-age' in OCSP Stapling Parameters was 0 - 86400 (0 to 1 day in seconds). This range might not be enough to support some of the scenarios wherein the acceptable value could be as high as a 7-10 days.
bugs.impact: OCSP response is discarded even when it is acceptable as valid.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The allowed range of 'status-age' has been changed to 0 - MAX_INT, with 0 indicating that the status-age check is not performed. That is, it is not checked if the 'thisUpdate' value in the OCSP response is lagging in time by a specified value. Also, the default value of the status-age has been changed to 86400 (one day in seconds).

bugs.title: Change in the caching duration of OCSP response when there is an error
bugs.symptoms: Some of the OCSP responses that indicate an error (such as 'unauthorized' response from the responder) are cached indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: Some of the OCSP responses that indicate an error (such as 'unauthorized' response from the responder).
bugs.impact: Responses are cached indefinitely.
bugs.workaround: The response can be deleted from the cache so as to obtain a new response. The new response will be cached based on whether it is valid, and whether the responder indicates an error.
bugs.fix: Except when the responder sends a certificate-status 'revoked', or a response status 'signature required', the response is cached for the duration given by the 'cache-error-timeout' field.

bugs.title: Qkview might hang
bugs.symptoms: A corrupted filestore causes qkview to hang.
bugs.conditions: This occurs due to filestore mapping issues. This might also occur when there are files listed in the filestore are missing.
bugs.impact: Qkview hangs and sync attempts silently fail due to filestore mapping issue. The system might post error messages similar to the following: err mcpd[4596]: 0107134e:3: Failed while making snapshot: (Failed to link files existing(/config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt) new(/config/.snapshots_d/certificate_d/1389867940_:Common:ca-bundle.crt_1) errno(2)(No such file or directory).) errno(2) errstr(No such file or directory).
bugs.fix: A corrupted filestore no longer causes qkview to hang.

bugs.title: LSN translation failures when persistence is enabled, cmp-hash is set to src-ip on ingress VLAN and to dst-ip on egress VLAN and using a small port range
bugs.symptoms: LSN Translation failures in persistence mode when cmp-hash is set to src-ip on ingress VLAN and to dst-ip on egress VLAN.
bugs.conditions: Persistence is enabled on the LSN pool, and cmp-hash is set to src-ip on ingress VLAN and to dst-ip on egress VLAN, when the lsn-pool port range is relatively small (under 1000), or a blade is added or removed. Translation mode is NAPT or PBA.
bugs.impact: Translation failures. The system posts an error similar to the following: debug tmm9[25268]: 01670012:7: [0.9] Translation failed client 200.200.200.101,10096.
bugs.workaround: Adequately provision the LSN pool.
bugs.fix: This release resolves CGNAT translation failures in persistence mode when cmp-hash is set to src-ip on ingress VLAN and to dst-ip on egress VLAN.

bugs.title: Software upgrade in vCMP guest may stay get stuck with "waiting for product image" status despite image being present
bugs.symptoms: In the rare case that a particular ISO image exists both on the vCMP host and vCMP guest and is then deleted from either the host or the guest, starting an install inside the guest using that image will result in the install becoming stuck with the "waiting for product image" status. Note that when deleting the image from the host, the guest should then still be able to install the image that exists on its local file system, and when deleting the image from the guest, the guest should still be able to install the image from the host (E.g. using the "tmsh install sys block-device-image image_name command). However, in either case, having deleted the image from either the host or the guest leaves the guest system thinking that neither image exists, and thus the install process is unable to find the image that was not deleted.
bugs.conditions: This issue will only occur on vCMP guests and only when the same ISO image has been copied to both the host and guest, one of the images is deleted, and install of the remaining image is attempted.
bugs.impact: The install process will remain stuck inside the guest until the workaround is performed.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, delete the remaining image from either the host or the guest and then re-copy the image to the host and/or the guest. The install process should then proceed.

bugs.title: Number of CPU allocated for ASM guests
bugs.symptoms: The TMM plugin manager does not expect/support an ASM guest configuration of 10 cores, thus its calculations as to the number of devices required and numbering does not match the existing number of threads/devices.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are 10 CPUs allocated for ASM guests.
bugs.impact: System does not start up or has intermittent failures if running.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of cores to 8 or increase the number to 12.
bugs.fix: This release disables channel splitting/division when number of TMMs is not a supported number, so ASM guests work correctly.

bugs.title: Hybrid higig/front panel port packet discard (Ingress back-pressure v.s. Egress queue discard) counts can be expected during bursty or severe MMU traffic congestion on B4300/B2200/10000/12000-family platforms.
bugs.symptoms: Different discard configurations as set on B4300/B2200/10000/12000-family platform interfaces, may result in different packet discard type counts, when the switch encounters bursty or severe MMU congestion.
bugs.conditions: Dissimilar congestion discard counts observed for switch ports supporting normal v.s. extended unicast queues.
bugs.impact: When switch ports encounters congestion, ports supporting extended unicast queue ports may show ingress back-pressure discard counts, as opposed to egress queue discard counts for ports supporting regular unicast queue ports.
bugs.fix: Enabled egress CoS queue discard settings also for switch ports supporting extended unicast queues, as currently set for ports supporting normal unicast queues.

bugs.title: Front panel Ethernet TX pause flow-control non-functional
bugs.symptoms: Front panel port Ethernet TX pause is currently disabled for the following platforms: B4200, B4300, B2100, B2150, B2250, 5000-series, 7000-series, 10000-series, 11000-series, and 12250.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the B4200, B4300, B2100, B2150, B2250, 5000-series, 7000-series, 10000-series, 11000-series, and 12250 platforms.
bugs.impact: Front panel Ethernet TX pause flow-control non-functional.

bugs.title: End of Life announcement for inbound and outbound cost-based link load balancing and inbound link path-based load balancing.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP Link Controller and BIG-IP GTM link cost-based and inbound link path-based load balancing features have reached End of Life (EoL).
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Link Controller and BIG-IP GTM link cost-based and inbound link path-based load balancing features.
bugs.impact: Cannot use these features.
bugs.fix: Link cost and inbound link path load balancing software support has reached EOL. For more information, see SOL15834: End of Life announcement for inbound and outbound cost-based link load balancing and inbound link path-based load balancing, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/800/sol15834.html.

bugs.title: Importing local db users from a CSV file that has no UID set, displays incorrect information in the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Importing local db users from a CSV file that has no UID set, displays incorrect information in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: When importing the local DB user from the CSV file, with no UID value provided.
bugs.impact: All users imported without UIDs will be mapped to one user's detail entry (that is, fname, lname, email, and so on). So all such users show the same first name, last name, email, and other user details.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Importing local db users with no UID set now generates a Unique ID and stores each user's details in the database.

bugs.title: SSL::collect, SSL::release iRule events might not work as expected in a mirroring configuration.
bugs.symptoms: SSL::collect, SSL::release iRule events might not work as expected in a mirroring configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL::collect, SSL::release iRule events. -- High availability (HA) configuration that includes mirroring.
bugs.impact: iRules do not operate as expected on mirrored connections.

bugs.title: TMM "unexpected message" assert in diameter_tcl_handler()
bugs.symptoms: When a flow is marked CONNFLOW_FLAG_NOEXPIRE, eviction algorithms are still run. No eviction algorithms should be run on flows marked CONNFLOW_FLAG_NOEXPIRE.
bugs.conditions: Analysis of TMM core file with flow leak.
bugs.impact: Elevated memory usage, may result eventual TMM failover due to out-of-memory.
bugs.fix: Fixed in versions later than 11.6.1

bugs.title: TMM may generate core during certain config change.
bugs.symptoms: While the sandbox file is being used by data-plane, if the admin changes configuration to delete this sandbox file, the TMM may generate core due to accessing freed up memory.
bugs.conditions: While data-plane is handling requests for the sandbox files, if admin deletes it from the control plane.
bugs.impact: TMM may core, which may cause APM service to become unavailable for some time.
bugs.fix: Access whitelist entries are refcount-ed to prevent freeing of the memory while it is still being used.

bugs.title: Provide an option to delete the session if IP class address Limit reached when new IP being added and create a new one instead.
bugs.symptoms: When Multiple IP feature is supported, If a new IP needs to be add to session will fail if IP address limit is reached for particular class of IP addresses. So, if old IPs are not removed from the session even though subscriber may not be using it, we disallow new IP assignment and hence subscriber traffic might be blocked/not polcied as IP address was not added to session.
bugs.conditions: IP class address limit for the session and new IP address add for the same same subscriber session arrives.
bugs.impact: Session does not get created by radius, but by traffic and there is no subscriber ID assigned to it. PCRF may decline to give policy and hence Subscriber traffic may not be policed as expected.
bugs.fix: Now added a db variable Tmm.pem.session.delete.if.max.ipaddr.per.class.exceeded which is by default set to TRUE. Now. when a new IP address add request comes via Radius and Session IP limit has reached, then we delete the current session and create a new one altogether. So that new Subscriber session is not affected.

bugs.title: Mcpd may restart continuously when a new blade is inserted into a chassis running vCMP
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd restarts continuously when a new blade is inserted into a chassis running vCMP.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur when a vCMP guest is deployed to a blade which is then replaced as in an RMA situation or if the blade has its BIG-IP image reinstalled.
bugs.impact: The newly inserted blade is unable to join the BIG-IP cluster.
bugs.workaround: If the new blade is rebooted manually, it is able to properly cluster with the rest of the chassis after restart.
bugs.fix: An issue has been resolved which could cause mcpd to continuously restart after a chassis blade replacement.

bugs.title: When qkview is killed, it might leave temporary files on disk
bugs.symptoms: qkview removes its temporary files on exit. However, if qkview is killed externally, for example by CTRL-C, temporary files remain on the disk.
bugs.conditions: qkview is running, and is killed with a signal, such as CTRL-C.
bugs.impact: Unneeded files remain in /var/tmp, and possibly in other locations. This might contribute to a disk filling up with garbage data.
bugs.workaround: Delete files in /var/tmp.

bugs.title: openssl v1.0.1j.
bugs.symptoms: openssl has been updated to version 1.0.1j
bugs.fix: openssl has been updated to version 1.0.1j.

bugs.title: moving VLAN from route-domain being deleted in the same transaction can cause errors
bugs.symptoms: Error can occur when removing VLAN(s) from route-domain, and deleting the said route-domain in the same transaction can cause errors.
bugs.conditions: In a transaction, removing the VLAN membership from route-domain, and deleting the same route-domain.
bugs.impact: Transactional deletion of route-domain and route-domain VLAN membership changes in the same transaction.
bugs.workaround: Perform route-domain VLAN changes, and route-domain deletion in different transaction.

bugs.title: Requests not logged locally on the device
bugs.symptoms: After deactivating or deleting security policies and then activating other policies, sometimes requests would not be logged on the local device.
bugs.conditions: Deactivating/deleting security policies and then activating other policies.
bugs.impact: Requests would not be logged on the local device
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM
bugs.fix: ASM now properly tracks security policy changes, and correctly logs requests.

bugs.title: SSL connections reset after failover.
bugs.symptoms: Connection stalls and/or connection is reset due to handshake timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- Mirroring enabled on SSL virtual server. -- Failover occurs during SSL handshake (i.e., negotiation/renegotiation).
bugs.impact: SSL connections might stall or be reset on failover.

bugs.title: Chassis fan status alert not observed on BIG-IP 2000/4000/5000/7000/10000/12000/VPR-B4300/VPR-B2100/VPR-B4450N
bugs.symptoms: Chassis fan status alert not observed in system_check logs or as SNMP trap. One can only observe sensor alerts about the fan sensor values being outside the threshold limits on the console, logs and LCD.
bugs.conditions: When there is a hardware issue with the chassis fans.
bugs.impact: Malfunctioning chassis fans can affect the cooling of the system. If the temperature within the system goes beyond the threshold, the system will self shutdown to prevent any hardware damage.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: We can now see explicit alerts about the chassis fan being bad/defective on the console, logs and LCD.

bugs.title: SWG database download via proxy
bugs.symptoms: You are required to setup an additional separate shared public Internet access to deal just with the downloads only for the SWG module. This is also against internal security policies, it is not allowed for a device initiated connections to the Internet without being handled by a proxy infrastructure.
bugs.conditions: SWG Database Download.
bugs.impact: Without this feature, your security policy cannot be satisfied for database downloads without which SWG functionality cannot work.
bugs.fix: Device specific proxy configuration fields (proxy ip, proxy port, username and password) has been added to configure the proxy to be used. To enable SWG database download through proxy, new option "Use Proxy" has been added in SWG Database Settings to use the configured proxy for SWG database download.

bugs.title: Mismatched IPsec policy configuration causes racoon to core after failed IPsec tunnel negotiation
bugs.symptoms: Mismatched IPsec policy configuration causes racoon to core intermittently after failed IPsec tunnel negotiation.
bugs.conditions: During IPsec Tunnel negotiation, IKE Phase 1 negotiation succeeds and ISAKMP security association is created, but phase 2 (Quick mode) for IPsec security associations fails due to mismatched IPsec policy configuration. This intermittent error occurs because of a memory issue that causes heap corruption.
bugs.impact: Intermittently, the racoon daemon cores and crashes when there are earlier failed phase 2 negotiations.
bugs.workaround: Make sure IPsec policies such as encryption/authentication algorithms for the data going through IPsec tunnel on the remote device match the IPsec policy configured on the BIG-IP system for the same IPsec Tunnel.
bugs.fix: The racoon daemon no longer crashes due to mismatched IPsec policy configuration.

bugs.title: Config load failure with 'Input error: can't create user' after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Unable to load config after upgrade or reboot if the admin account is disabled and replaced with a custom user. The system posts the message: 01070829:5: Input error: can't create user, role partition mapping, user does not exist, username, Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. On single-NIC virtual deployments, if the admin account is disabled and replaced with a custom user, the system will experience this issue any time the system is rebooted. Logs similar to the following may appear in /var/log/ltm: notice sod[6214]: 010c005e:5: Waiting for mcpd to reach phase base, current phase is platform. notice mcpd[4672]: 01070829:5: Input error: can't create user, role partition mapping, user does not exist, security err tmsh[7444]: 01420006:3: Loading configuration process failed. emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all base" - failed. -- 01070829:5: Input error: can't create user, role partition mapping, user does not exist, security Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. err mcpd[4672]: 01070422:3: Base configuration load failed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when upgrading or rebooting a system on which the root admin account is disabled and replaced with a custom admin user account. This occurs on single-NIC virtual deployments in version 12.0.0, when a system on which the root admin account is disabled and replaced with a custom admin user account is rebooted. To verify single-NIC is enabled: tmsh list sys db provision.1nic. To verify a custom administrator has been defined: tmsh list sys db systemauth.primaryadminuser.
bugs.impact: You cannot upgrade if the root admin account is disabled. On single-NIC virtual deployment configurations in version 12.0.0, the system fails to load the configuration after a reboot.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue. To resolve this issue, you can reboot the BIG-IP system back to the previous working boot location that has the admin user disabled. For single-NIC virtual deployments, you can re-enable the default admin user account. To do so, perform one of the following procedures: Impact of workaround: Since the BIG-IP System is already in the inoperative state, performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system. Rebooting the BIG-IP system back to the previous working boot location: Log in to the Traffic Management shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: tmsh To reboot the BIG-IP system to the desired boot location, type the following command syntax: reboot volume <boot_location> Re-enabling the default admin user account on BIG-IP system (for single-NIC virtual deployments): Azure BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE): Log in to tmshby typing the following command: tmsh Re-enable the default admin user account by typing the following command: modify /sys db systemauth.primaryadminuser value admin Re-load BIG-IP configuration by typing the following command: load /sys config Amazon Web Services BIG-IP VE: Log in to tmshby typing the following command: tmsh Re-enable the default admin user account by typing the following command: modify /sys db systemauth.primaryadminuser value admin Update the password for the default admin user by typing the following command syntax: modify /auth user admin password <password> Re-load BIG-IP configuration by typing the following command: load /sys config
bugs.fix: Can now successfully load the configuration after upgrade if the admin account is disabled and replaced with a custom user, and no 'Input error: can't create user' error occurs.

bugs.title: Suspend/save/migrate LTM VE functionality is not supported for Community XEN.
bugs.symptoms: LTM Virtual Edition (VE) does not support the cloud features suspend/save/migration for Community Xen Hypervisor.
bugs.conditions: Community Xen Hypervisor.
bugs.impact: Reduces migration functionality on Community Xen Hypervisor platform.
bugs.workaround: Save the standard configuration in a UCS file and migrate the UCS file to different instances as needed.

bugs.title: Duplicate 'Source Address Translation' field on Virtual Server properties page
bugs.symptoms: On the Virtual Server page, with the type equal to 'Performance (HTTP)', the 'Source Address Translation' field will appear twice. The first field is correct. The second field should be ignored.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server type equal to 'Performance (HTTP)'
bugs.impact: Filling in the second won't have any affect, but it is confusing.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the second field.

bugs.title: The TMM process may restart and produce a core file when using the SSL::disable clientside iRule command within a HTTP_REQUEST event
bugs.symptoms: The Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) process may restart and produce a core file when using the SSL::disable client-side iRule command within an HTTP_REQUEST event. Symptoms As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: The BIG-IP system fails over to another host in the device group. The BIG-IP system generates a TMM core file to the /shared/core directory. The BIG-IP system temporarily fails to process traffic.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: You have configured a virtual server that uses an iRule. The iRule contains the SSL::disable client-side iRule command within an HTTP_REQUEST event. The virtual server processes traffic that triggers the HTTP_REQUEST event while processing encrypted traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not put 'SSL::disable clientside' inside HTTP_REQUEST.
bugs.fix: The Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) process no longer restarts and produces a core file when using the SSL::disable client-side iRule command within an HTTP_REQUEST event.

bugs.title: SMTP monitor on non-default route domain fails to create socket
bugs.symptoms: SMTP monitor on non-default route domain fails to create socket
bugs.conditions: SMTP monitors on a non-default route domain.
bugs.impact: SMTP monitor pool members are DOWN. If debug logging is enabled for the monitor, the system posts messages in the monitors debug log: Notice 'ERROR: failed to connect 10.50.1.100%20:25 error: couldn't open socket: host is unreachable'.
bugs.workaround: Create an External monitor using SMTP_monitor.
bugs.fix: SMTP monitor no longer fails when using a non-default route domain.

bugs.title: iRule compilation fails on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: While upgrading, the configuration load fails and you see an error similar to the following: localhost emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all" - failed. -- Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 40) "{" unknown property
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to 11.6.x versions may cause iRule compilation failures if the iRule contains whitespace instead of an opening brace after the event. For example: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED {
bugs.impact: Configuration will fail to load on upgrade.
bugs.workaround: You can edit bigip.conf and manually correct the line in the iRule by putting the opening brace on tbe same line as the event, then reload the configuration with tmsh load sys config. Example: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED {
bugs.fix: Fix tcl parsing if there is a whitespace before the new line.

bugs.title: Navigating to iApps :: Templates :: MyTemplate :: Properties in the GUI presents a blank page
bugs.symptoms: Navigating to iApps :: Templates :: MyTemplate :: Properties in the GUI presents a blank page.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are more than 150 applications using the same template.
bugs.impact: Cannot edit the iApp template.
bugs.workaround: Recommendation is to copy the iApp template to a different name and assign half of the application services to that new template.

bugs.title: Large file transfer hangs when HTTP is in passthrough mode
bugs.symptoms: Large file transfer hangs when HTTP is in passthrough mode. The HTTP profile may switch into passthrough mode for a number of reasons, including enforcement (the http-transparent profile options), the CONNECT HTTP method, iRule, unknown method detection, or switching protocols.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with HTTP profile configured. -- HTTP profile goes into passthrough mode. -- Large file transfer occurs.
bugs.impact: File transfer hangs.
bugs.fix: Flow control implemented in HTTP profile when in passthrough mode.

bugs.title: Corrupt memory
bugs.symptoms: The Thrift server raises an unhandled exception.
bugs.conditions: Using Thrift server when encountering an unhandled exception.
bugs.impact: AVRD crashes.
bugs.fix: AVRD now handles an unhandled exception when using the Thrift server.

bugs.title: Fixed problem with iNotes 9 Instant Messaging
bugs.symptoms: iNotes 9 IM (Sametime) is not working. There are errors in JS Console.
bugs.conditions: User is connected to iNotes 9 through Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Sametime in iNotes 9 is not accessible.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: iNotes 9 Sametime (instant messaging) is working now.

bugs.title: F5-prelogon user profile folder are not fully cleaned-up
bugs.symptoms: When a user logs on using Network Logon in Windows, it triggers access policy execution, and the policy creates a temporary user, f5 Pre-Logon User. This causes the operating system to create a profile folder on the computer. After several executions, these folders start to accumulate because they are not removed properly after policy execution is complete. Each time the access policy runs, it creates a user folder of the form f5 Pre-Logon User.<HOSTNAME>.xyz in the C:\Users folder.
bugs.conditions: A user logs on to the computer using Network Logon in Windows. (Windows Logon Integration)
bugs.impact: Disk runs out of space and user is confused.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, delete folders manually.

bugs.title: SSL persistence uses noticeably more memory
bugs.symptoms: In releases prior to 11.4.0, SSL persistence used very little memory. Beginning in version 11.4.0 and continuing, the amount of memory has increased.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when SSL persistence is enabled.
bugs.impact: This results in less memory being available for other flows, and might eventually result in TMM being out of memory.
bugs.fix: SSL persistence memory handling has been improved, so that sufficient memory is available for other flows.

bugs.title: JavaRDP client disconnects
bugs.symptoms: JavaRDP client disconnects user's session when user interacts before the handshake is complete.
bugs.conditions: The might occur when the network connection is slow but the user is fast enough to click the mouse within the client area or press a key on the keyboard. In this case the RDP client attempts to send this input event to the server.
bugs.impact: Because the RDP handshake is not completed at this point, the server aborts the connection.
bugs.workaround: Do not interact within the client area before the window fills with an image from the server. When that occurs, the connection is clearly established and all handshakes are completed.
bugs.fix: JavaRDP client session starts correctly now, and the system does not process extraneous input that occurs before the handshake completes.

bugs.title: In client-ssl profile which serves as server side, BIG-IP SSL does not initialize in initialization function.
bugs.symptoms: In client-ssl profile that serves as the server side. BIG-IP SSL does not initialize some parameters.
bugs.conditions: In client-ssl profile which serves as the server side and retransmitting fragmented datagrams.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake fails. Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) crash while retransmitting fragmented datagrams.
bugs.fix: In client-ssl profile which serves as server side, BIG-IP SSL now initializes parameters in initialization function as expected.

bugs.title: If you configure the remote user authentication server such as LDAP, make sure it is available.
bugs.symptoms: If the authentication server is not available such as failure to respond to ping, and when creating/modifying a user in TMSH and setting a password, the TMSH appears to hang for more than 60 seconds. Any of outstanding GUI sessions might also time out. Note: If you are adding/modifying a user and not setting a password there is no problem.
bugs.conditions: -- The authentication server is not available (such as failure to respond to ping). -- Creating/modifying a user in TMSH and setting a password.
bugs.impact: TMSH appears to hang for more than 60 seconds. Any of outstanding GUI sessions might also time out.

bugs.title: CIDR can now be used for SNAT Origin Address List
bugs.symptoms: A validation error occurred when address in IP/CIDR format is entered into the address list field, although it still accepts an address in IP/IP format.
bugs.conditions: When address in IP/CIDR format is entered into the address list field.
bugs.impact: Validation error occurs, although the field still accepts an address in IP/IP format.
bugs.fix: Validation error is no longer thrown and address in IP/CIDR format is now handled correctly.

bugs.title: Potentially confusing wamd shutdown error messages
bugs.symptoms: When shutting down, wamd might log debug messages that appear serious.
bugs.conditions: wamd shutdown.
