bugs.impact: Unnecessary log messages generated, similar to the following: -- WA Debug (17637): * WARNING: The server encountered an unexpected condition. -- WA Debug (17637): * Contact F5 support if you are experiencing problems and include -- WA Debug (17637): * the following diagnostic information. These messages are cosmetic and do not indicate a problem with the system.
bugs.fix: The wamd process no longer generates potentially alarming debug log messages when shutting down.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system sends unnecessary gratuitous ARPs
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system sends unnecessary gratuitous ARPs for its virtual IP addresses and self IP addresses.
bugs.conditions: When the virtual server status transitions from online to offline status or vice versa.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends out a large number of unwanted gratuitous ARPs if the virtual server changes its status rapidly. If devices connected to the BIG-IP system have rate limits configured, the devices might start ignoring the ARPs sent by the BIG-IP system, which might cause the devices to miss the critical gratuitous ARPs sent on HA failover. This might affect HA functionality.
bugs.fix: The system no longer sends unnecessary gratuitous ARPs when pool member state changes cause virtual server status changes.

bugs.title: TMM may restart when MPTCP traffic is being handled.
bugs.symptoms: There are some conditions where when multi-path TCP (MPTCP) traffic is being handled by an MPTCP-enabled virtual server might cause TMM to restart.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP traffic is being handled by a L7 virtual server.
bugs.impact: The TMM might restart when this condition occurs.
bugs.fix: TMM may restart when multi-path TCP (MPTCP) traffic is being handled.

bugs.title: Access policy cannot enter Windows Protected Workspace on Internet Explorer versions 10 and 11, and edge client.
bugs.symptoms: An access policy cannot enter Windows Protected Workspace on Internet Explorer versions 10 and 11, and Windows Edge client.
bugs.conditions: Internet Explorer versions 10 and 11.
bugs.impact: Access policy cannot enter Windows Protected Workspace.
bugs.workaround: Use a browser other than Internet Explorer versions 10 and 11.
bugs.fix: An access policy can now enter Windows Protected Workspace on Internet Explorer versions 10 and 11.

bugs.title: AVRD does not print out an error message when the external logging fails
bugs.symptoms: External logging of AVR statistics is done by HSL framework, if a message is failed to be sent to the syslog server, then AVR does not log this error.
bugs.conditions: If network is under stress, there is a possibility that the external logging will not be 100% transmitted
bugs.impact: The logging application will not receive all log entries.
bugs.fix: AVR is logging about HSL sending error. It is important to notice that it is still not 100% sure that the message will arrive to the destination, since an application level ack does not exist in syslog, but this by definition.

bugs.title: Validation error in MCPD for FQDN nodes
bugs.symptoms: Validation does not enforce unique FQDN nodes across folders.
bugs.conditions: Create two nodes with the same FQDN in two different folders.
bugs.impact: This issue can cause undefined behavior
bugs.workaround: Ensure FQDN nodes, like regular IP nodes, to be unique across folders.
bugs.fix: Ensure FQDN nodes, like regular IP nodes, to be unique across folders.

bugs.title: PVA status, statistics not shown correctly in UI
bugs.symptoms: When affected versions of BIG-IP are running on VIPRION B2250 blades, the PVA status and statistics are not displayed correctly (missing entirely) from the user interface.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION B2250 blades running affected versions of BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: PVA appears to be disabled/unavailable. PVA statistics are not available. PVA functionality is actually enabled and operating in the data plane.
bugs.workaround: Example of incorrect display: # guishell -c 'select name,has_pva,pva_version from platform' -------------------------------- | NAME | HAS_PVA | PVA_VERSION | -------------------------------- | A112 | false | | <<< incorrect -------------------------------- # tmsh show ltm virtual ------------------------------------------------------------------ Ltm::Virtual Server: vs1 ------------------------------------------------------------------ Status Availability : unknown State : enabled Reason : The children pool member(s) either don't have service checking enabled, or service check results are not available yet CMP : enabled CMP Mode : all-cpus Destination : 30.30.30.1:80 <<< missing 'PVA Acceleration' item
bugs.fix: PVA status and statistics are displayed correctly for VIPRION B2250 blades.

bugs.title: "cipher" memory can leak
bugs.symptoms: When performing SSL handshakes, memory usage can increase. Examining "cipher" memory in the "memory_usage_stat" may show large amounts of "cipher"memory allocated.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP performing SSL handshakes.
bugs.impact: Memory usage increases until no more memory is available.
bugs.fix: "cipher" memory no longer leaks.

bugs.title: [AFM] packets from good ip's are being dropped by DoS Sweep & Flood logic
bugs.symptoms: Rate tracker library is not accurate.
bugs.conditions: When traffic is at very low rate.
bugs.impact: Traffic from good IP addresses could end up being dropped.
bugs.fix: AFM no longer drops packets from good IP addresses during sweep and flood.

bugs.title: IPsec IKEv2 tmm crash hud_ike_ingress_pkt()
bugs.symptoms: Using IPsec IKEv2 the tmm may crash in hud_ike_ingress_pkt() because of an uninitialized variable.
bugs.conditions: Using IPsec IKEv2.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Code hardening
When BIG-IP virtual accessed with multiple tabs with long initial URLs before session creation can cause TMM crash.
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP virtual server is accessed from multiple tabs with long initial URLs before session creation, this might cause TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: Rare condition: a user opens the browser and different tabs in the browser pointing to BIG-IP APM virtual server and they cause the access policy to run from both tabs. If the length of the encoded URL falls into 4K boundary then TMM might crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Proper checks were added before processing the URL so that, if there is a long initial URL, the BIG-IP system does not process it, and a user might see a reset. After establishing the session in other tabs, the user can access the long URL again.

bugs.title: Memory corruption can occur with SPDY/HTTP2 profile(s)
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server using either the SPDY or HTTP2 profiles can experience random memory corruption due to a double free of memory.
bugs.conditions: SPDY/HTTP2 filter is configured on the virtual.
bugs.impact: This results in a TMM crash in random components due to memory corruption.
bugs.workaround: Do not use SPDY2/HTTP2 profiles.
bugs.fix: A memory corruption in the SPDY/HTTP2 profiles has been fixed.

bugs.title: Now web VPN client correctly minimizes IE window to tray
bugs.symptoms: An Internet Explorer window remains on taskbar on Network Access connect even if 'minimize to tray' option is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Internet Explorer is used and 'minimize to tray' option is enabled
bugs.impact: IE window stays on desktop
bugs.fix: Now an Internet Explorer window is correctly minimized to tray.

bugs.title: Bot signature is not matched
bugs.symptoms: Bot signature is not matched although its content appears in request.
bugs.conditions: Configure several bot signatures and send request that contain the signature. Some signature may not be matched.
bugs.impact: Signature that should be matched and blocked may reach the application.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: All configured signature are now matched.

bugs.title: Machine Cert allows mismatched SubjectCN and FQDN for browsers in case of valid cert
bugs.symptoms: Browser clients allow Machine Cert Auth agent to pass even if the match SubjectCN and FQDN criteria is not satisfied. It only happens if the selected certificate is recognized by the BIG-IP system but does not fit the Machine Cert Auth selection criteria.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs with a Mac and the browser client, with the Machine Cert Auth agent in the access policy, and a valid certificate.
bugs.impact: Browser allows network access to be established even though it should not
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, add more search criteria in the Machine Cert Auth agent.
bugs.fix: Browser client now selects the appropriate certificate when the match SubjectCN and FQDN criteria is specified in the Machine Cert Auth agent.

bugs.title: TMM might panic due to OpenSSL failure during handshake generation
bugs.symptoms: TMM might panic due to OpenSSL failure during handshake generation.
bugs.conditions: Low memory. Software-based SSL handshake generation.
bugs.impact: TMM outage.
bugs.fix: The system now checks for OpenSSL failures during SSL handshake generation, so TMM no longer panics.

bugs.title: chmand needs to check for LopUnsSensClientExists status after registering for unsolicited alerts with lopd
bugs.symptoms: chmand fails to register for unsolicited LOP events, meaning that asynchronous alerts from lopd will not seen or reported by chmand. A message is seen in /var/log/ltm that contains the phrase, "failed to register for LOP at <address>"
bugs.conditions: Occurs when chmand has been re-started after it has already synchronized once with lopd.
bugs.impact: Asynchronous events from lopd will not be reported or handled, such as fan tray removal/insertion and PSU removal/insertion. Alerts that are driven by system_check through polling sensor values and comparing them to specified limits, however, will still be operational.
bugs.workaround: Re-start lopd: # bigstart restart lopd
bugs.fix: Modified chmand to recognize the case where unsolicited alert registration with lopd has already occurred so that it no longer treats it as an error.

bugs.title: HTTP with NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE message and with payload more than 4KB cause the NTLM front end authentication to stall
bugs.symptoms: NTLM authentication cannot be completed in the following circumstances. It is observed that some non-Microsoft HTTP clients might start NTLM authentication by sending a NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE message together with a payload. As part of NTLM protocol, the response to this request should be a 401 status with an NTLMSSP_CHALLENGE message which renders the payload from the initial request unnecessary. However, the issue is that currently the BIG-IP system has a limit of 4KB for initial buffer, and does not drop it. This causes a deadlock between the BIG-IP server and HTTP client, as the BIG-IP notifies the client that it cannot receive the payload any more by closing the TCP receive window, and the client tries to complete sending all of the requests to be able to send the final NTLMSSP_AUTHENTICATE message.
bugs.conditions: The client sends NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE message with payload of more than 4KB and the BIG-IP system performs NTLM authentication for this request.
bugs.impact: NTLM authentication cannot be completed.

bugs.title: Sync fails if file object is created and deleted before sync to peer BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Sync fails if you create/import a file object and delete it before triggering manual sync; ltm logs contain messages similar to the following: Standby: -- err mcpd[7339]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files.. -- err mcpd[7339]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/test to commit id 42 6079477704784246664 /Common/test failed with error 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files... Active: -- err mcpd[6319]: 0107134a:3: File object by name (/Common/filename) is missing.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- BIG-IP systems configured for high availability (HA) are not configured to sync automatically, and incremental synchronization is enabled (these are the default settings). -- One or more file objects are created and deleted before performing a sync from Active to Standby.
bugs.impact: Sync fails.
bugs.workaround: When you create/add a file object, make sure to sync before deleting it. If a system is already in this state, perform a full sync and overwrite the configuration, as described in K13887: Forcing a BIG-IP device group member to initiate a ConfigSync operation :: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K13887.

bugs.title: Empty violation details for attack signatures
bugs.symptoms: Attack signatures detected on a transaction. The reporting does not show the details of all attack signatures.
bugs.conditions: Different signature sets are applied to different policies, and then a transaction with attack signatures appears on a request.
bugs.impact: Not all the detected attack signature details are shown. In some cases, there are empty violation details for certain attack signatures.
bugs.fix: All attack signature details are now shown.

bugs.title: Configuration upgrade failure due to change in an ASM predefined report name
bugs.symptoms: A configuration load failure occurs after creating an ASM predefined report in a previous version and upgrading.
bugs.conditions: Define scheduled report on top of "Top alerted URLs" on 11.3.0 and upgrade the version.
bugs.impact: Version upgrade fails (the BIG-IP becomes unusable).
bugs.workaround: Change the "/Common/Top Alerted URLs" reference in the bigip.conf file of the UCS to "/Common/Top Alarmed URLs", and then load the modified UCS.
bugs.fix: If an ASM predefined report was created in a previous version and the system was updated, it could have caused the configuration upgrade to fail. This failure no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Running out of memory while parsing large XML SOAP requests
bugs.symptoms: Running out of memory while parsing large XML SOAP requests.
bugs.conditions: System parses as XML a large multipart file upload.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary memory allocations which could cause the Enforcer to run out of memory. The system posts an error similar to the following: 'ASM out of memory error: event code X239 Exceeded maximum memory assigned for XML/JSON processing'.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue where the system parsed as XML a large multipart file upload. Doing that caused unnecessary memory allocations which could cause the Enforcer to run out of memory. The following error message was displayed "ASM out of memory error: event code X239 Exceeded maximum memory assigned for XML/JSON processing".

bugs.title: Deletion of FIPS keys by-handle may delete key in FIPS-card even if key exists in BIG-IP config
bugs.symptoms: 11.4.0 onwards, deletion of FIPS keys by-handle is expected to throw error if the BIG-IP config contains that key object. However, if the key name is different from the FIPS-label of the key, such deletion by-handle will delete key from FIPS card without checking BIG-IP config. It will not delete that key from BIG-IP config.
bugs.conditions: Delete FIPS key by-handle using tmsh when the key name is different from the FIPS-label of the key.
bugs.impact: FIPS key deletion by-handle may not throw expected error when the FIPS handle corresponds to a key in the BIG-IP config and will delete the key from FIPS card without deleting the key in the BIG-IP config.
bugs.workaround: First, FIPS key deletion by-handle should be used only for FIPS key handles that don't have corresponding key objects in the BIG-IP config. If the FIPS key deletion was desired and by-handle deletion is already performed which did not delete the key from BIG-IP config, then follow the below workaround: After executing: 'tmsh delete sys crypto fips by-handle <handle-number>' check if the corresponding key still exists in BIG-IP config by executing: 'tmsh list sys crypto key' If the concerned key did not get deleted, execute: 'tmsh delete sys crypto key <keyname>'
bugs.fix: The system now handles the case in which deleting FIPS key by-handle using tmsh when the key name is different from the FIPS-label of the key.

bugs.title: Flow based reporting attribute mismatch between TMUI and TCL
bugs.symptoms: Several fields are missed in PEM format script reporting. Several fields in format script use usec, which should be milli-seconds.
bugs.conditions: In PEM session and flow format script reporting.
bugs.impact: Some new fields are added. For session, here are the new fields: last-sent-msec report-id report-version timestamp-msec For flow, here are the new fields: flow-start-milli-seconds flow-end-milli-seconds report-id route-domain report-version timestamp-msec vlan-id
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: To keep the backward compatibility, the following fields are still kept. But the values of those *-usec below are 0 now, representing that they are not meaningful; we just do not want to break the users' existing scripts. For session: last-sent-usec timestamp-usec module-id For flow: flow-start-time-usec flow-end-time-usec timestamp-usec

bugs.title: Webroot cloud lookup support
bugs.symptoms: PEM does not have the ability to query the Webroot cloud database for URLs that are only available in the Webroot server in the cloud. There is one global Webroot database on the BIG-IP system, which contains millions of URLs it can categorize. However, the Webroot URL categorization database is hosted on their cloud, and can categorize billions of URLs. In certain countries, some of the popular URLs can only be categorized by the Webroot cloud database.
bugs.conditions: This only occurs when Webroot cloud lookup enabled. The Webroot cloud lookup features is disabled by default.
bugs.impact: Certain URLs are categorized as unknown by the local Webroot database that is managed on the BIG-IP system, even though they could be categorized by the Webroot cloud service.
bugs.fix: The support is added, so that PEM can perform the Webroot cloud lookup asynchronously and cache the categorization result. When feature requests with the same URL arrives, PEM will be able to categorize the URL based on the cached Webroot cloud lookup result.

bugs.title: TMM cores when Woodside congestion control is used.
bugs.symptoms: In Woodside congestion control, the congestion window is used to calculate the minimum delay. During this calculation, if congestion window is 0, division by congestion window (0) causes a core during the calculation.
bugs.conditions: The congestion window becomes 0.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use another congestion control rather than Woodside.
bugs.fix: A TMM crash bug when using Woodside congestion control has been fixed. The issue was a division by 0 bug.

bugs.title: F5 Enterprise MIB attribute sysTmmStatMemoryTotal returning zero
bugs.symptoms: An SNMP query for F5 Enterprise MIB attribue sysTmmStatMemoryTotal and several others were returning zero values after upgrading to v11.6.0 HF6 or higher.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: These values are incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Similar queries can be made to equivalent MIB attributes provided in units of kilobytes using SNMP type Gauge. In the case of sysTmmStatMemoryTotal, sysTmmStatMemoryTotalKb can be queried.
bugs.fix: For the affected MIB attributes in 11.6.0 HF6 and higher, zero values are no longer returned. Units of measurements continue to be in bytes using SNMP attribute type Counter64.

bugs.title: Sometimes auto-blacklisting will not function after the provisioning of AFM and APM modules
bugs.symptoms: occasionally dwbl will crash after the provisioning of AFM and APM modules
bugs.conditions: provisioning of AFM and APM modules in BIG-IP at same time
bugs.impact: sometimes auto-blacklisting will not function because of the crash
bugs.fix: Fixed rare crash bug that could occur when provisioning AFM and APM modules at the same time.

bugs.title: Configuring VDI profile when APM is not provisioned, but does not.
bugs.symptoms: LTM GUI allows you to configure a VDI profile when APM is not provisioned, but since APM is not provisioned the profile will not work.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered if APM was previously provisioned and one or more VDI profiles were configured. Upon de-provisioning APM, the profiles are still visible in the GUI.
bugs.impact: There should be no impact other than the GUI allowing you to configure something that cannot be used unless APM is provisioned.
bugs.fix: The GUI no longer allows you to configure VDI profile when APM is not provisioned.

bugs.title: Added HTML information to external source alerts.
Generic malware false positives
bugs.symptoms: False positive js_vhtml alert is sent when browsing to protected page with malware detection enabled.
bugs.conditions: Malware detection enabled.
bugs.impact: False positive js_vhtml alert will be sent.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a false positive alert and does not indicate an actual alert condition.
bugs.fix: Signatures updated to handle false positive js_vhtml alert that was sent when browsing to protected page with malware detection enabled.

bugs.title: RADIUS::avp command fails when AVP contains multiple attribute (VSA).
bugs.symptoms: The RADIUS::avp command fails when AVP contains multiple attributes (VSA) within an AVP.
bugs.conditions: One AVP contains multiple attributes (VSA).
bugs.impact: RADIUS::avp command fails.
bugs.fix: RADIUS::avp command now completes successfully when AVP contains multiple attribute (VSA).

bugs.title: Memory type stats is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: When tmm allocates memory, it adds up stats per memory type allocated. AAM is not properly marking memory type for strings objects, affecting other types of memory stats depending on configuration and release.
bugs.conditions: AAM is provisioned and there are virtuals in BIG-IP configuration which have web acceleration profiles associated with one or more AAM policies.
bugs.impact: Stats for some types of memory can be skewed causing troubleshooting issues.

bugs.title: Incorrect reporting of PVA current and maximum connection with SERVER_CONNECTED event
bugs.symptoms: PVA current and maximum stats are incorrectly reported when using a FastL4 profile with a SERVER_CONNECTED iRule event. For each connection that is established, the current connection count is incremented twice and decremented only once when the connection is terminated. This leads to a lingering connection, which skews the stats.
bugs.conditions: A fastL4 virtual with a SERVER_CONNECTED iRule event.
bugs.impact: The current and maximum PVA stats are incorrectly reported.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: SMTP monitor could not create socket on IPv6 node address
bugs.symptoms: SMTP Tcl monitor cannot create socket on IPv6 node address.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include SMTP monitors with IPv6 pool members.
bugs.impact: SMTP monitor IPv6 pool members are DOWN.
bugs.workaround: Create a External monitor using SMTP_monitor
bugs.fix: SMTP monitor successfully monitors IPv6 pool members

bugs.title: Kerberos Auth might fail in case BIG-IP is configured with multiple AAA Kerberos Servers
bugs.symptoms: In case BIG-IP is configured with multiple AAA Kerberos Server objects and those Kerberos Server uses different keytabs for different service account but for the same realm, authentication may fail intermittently
bugs.conditions: - multiple AAA Kerberos Servers created - AAA Kerberos servers are configured with different keytabs - the keytabs are for different service accounts but for the same realm
bugs.impact: Kerberos authentication fails, user cannot log in
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, it is suggested to merge keytab files and use cumulative keytab file for all AAA Kerberos Servers Administrator can merge keytab files with "ktutil" kerberos utility that is installed at BIG-IP. 1. run ktutil 2. load all the keytab files to merge using: rkt <file> 3. you cal list currently loaded entries with "l" 4. after you load all required keytabs, save new keytab with wkt <newfile>

bugs.title: Loading iRules from file deletes the last few comment lines
bugs.symptoms: Loading iRules from the iRules file deletes the last few comment lines immediately preceding the closing bracket.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when loading an iRule file containing a comment after the last closing brace and then upgrading to a known affected version
bugs.impact: Although the comments are removed, this does not affect iRule functionality.
bugs.workaround: Add comments in places other than immediately above the closing bracket.

bugs.title: Cannot add FQDN node if management route is not configured
bugs.symptoms: Upon trying to create a FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name) node without the management route configured, an error is displayed: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Please configure a default gateway.
bugs.conditions: A basic LTM configuration with DNS lookup server setup
bugs.impact: User must configure a management route - even if they otherwise do not need one or have one configured.
bugs.workaround: Create a temporary management-route default gateway in order to add nodes using their FQDN: 1) tmsh create sys management-route default gateway 172.28.22.254 == create default management-route. 2) tmsh create ltm node mydomain.com fqdn { name mydomain.com } == create FQDN node. 3) tmsh delete sys management-route default == remove default management-route.
bugs.fix: It is no longer required that a default management route is setup in order to add nodes via their FQDN.

bugs.title: Improved TLS protocol negotiation with clients supporting TLS1.3
bugs.symptoms: When a TLS client connects to a BIG-IP TLS server requesting TLS1.3, the handshake will fail. A message will be logged in the Local Traffic Manager (LTM) log about a handshake failure. The estimated deployment of clients supporting TLS1.3 is 2016.
bugs.conditions: A TLS client handshake with the protocol version set to TLS1.3 in the ClientHello.
bugs.impact: Lower performance is the most likely outcome. The hanshake requesting TLS1.3 will fail, after which a client will reconnect with a TLS 1.2 hanhdshake and succeed. The worst case scenario is inability to establish a connection for clients that only implement standard TLS version negotiation mechanism. The estimated deployment of clients supporting TLS1.3 is 2016.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TLS server code can now handle ClientHello.protocol_version that is higher than TLS1.2, according to the TLS1.2 specification.

bugs.title: Duplicate DNSSEC keys can cause failed upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: When DNSSEC keys are stored in HSM and the system is upgraded, config load can fail because of duplicate keys in HSM.
bugs.conditions: DNSSEC keys in HSM. Upgrade or UCS load of configuration that contains the same keys.
bugs.impact: Failed upgrade or config load.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP DNS/mcpd now checks for an existing key and does not import keys that already exist.

bugs.title: ASM user interface extremely slow to respond (e.g., longer that 2 minutes to render policy list)
bugs.symptoms: ASM screens take a long time to load. MySQL spikes in usage.
bugs.conditions: Occurs after several thousand policy configuration changes have been made to the system.
bugs.impact: Slow ASM user interface pages.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now takes less time for ASM screens to load.

bugs.title: /shared/vmisolinks present on systems running versions where block-devices are not present
bugs.symptoms: /shared/vmisolinks is not removed from vCMP hosts when booting into builds that do not support block-device-image and block-device-hotfix vcmp installations.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in 11.6.0 or later with vCMP provisioned. In pre-11.6.0 versions, vCMP does not have to be provisioned.
bugs.impact: /shared/vmisolinks is present and takes up space. /shared can artificially fill up and cause warnings.
bugs.workaround: /shared/vmisolinks can be safely removed from older versions with the following command sequence: -- 'clsh rm -rf /shared/vmisolinks'. -- 'clsh ls -al /shared/vmisolinks'. After removing the /shared/vmisolinks directory from each cluster member or the appliance as a vCMP host, the space warnings related to /shared/vmisolinks will cease.
bugs.fix: /shared/vmisolinks is now properly cleaned up upon system startup.

bugs.title: The dynamic routes for the default route might be flushed during operations on non-default route domains.
bugs.symptoms: The dynamic routes for the default route might be flushed during operations on non-default route domains. For example when non-default route domain is deleted TMM, the operation also removes routes in the default route domain.
bugs.conditions: This happens on configuration changes and failover.
bugs.impact: Routing in default route domain might be impacted until tmrouted is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Avoid deleting non-default route domains. Issuing a bigstart restart tmrouted returns the system to a consistent state.
bugs.fix: The dynamic routes for the default route are no longer flushed during operations on non-default route domains.

bugs.title: LSN translation may occur after an iRule error.
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule throws an error, the default is to abort the connection. When the error occurs in the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event and the Virtual Server is using source-address-translation type LSN, the source address translation may be executed before the connection is aborted. The address translation may succeed even though the connection fails.
bugs.conditions: A Virtual Server is using source-address-translation type LSN and has an iRule that does not handle errors.
bugs.impact: There are a number of possible side effects depending on configuration: - Any LSN commands in the failing iRule may be ignored. - LSN Pool translation statistics may be incremented. - A log message indicating a successful translation may be output. - Multiple RSTs may be sent for the aborted connection. - PBA port blocks may be allocated. - Persistence mapping entries may be created. - Inbound mapping entries may be created.
bugs.workaround: Use the Tcl catch command to handle Tcl errors. When an error occurs, use the LSN::disable command to prevent the translation.

bugs.title: UCS load may fail if the UCS contains FIPS keys with names containing dot
bugs.symptoms: UCS load may fail if the UCS file contains FIPS keys with names containing dot ( . ).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the configuration includes at least one FIPS key with name containing a dot ( . ).
bugs.impact: UCS loading fails.
bugs.fix: UCS load now completes successfully if the saved configuration includes FIPS keys with names containing dot ( . ).

bugs.title: Applying Access Policy with an unused macro crashes TMM.
bugs.symptoms: When an Access Policy has a macro attached but does not use the macro anywhere, applying the Access Policy crashes TMM.
bugs.conditions: Access Policy that has a macro attached but is not using the macro at any point in the policy.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Delete all unused macros.
bugs.fix: Access Policy can now successfully contain a macro attached but does not use the macro anywhere.

bugs.title: Persistence Records display in GUI might cause system crash with large number of records
bugs.symptoms: Using the GUI to view Persistence Records statistics in GUI when there are a large number of records might crash the system. (Persistence Records are available for LTM and GTM by navigating to Statistics :: Module Statistics, clicking on Local Traffic, DNS Delivery, or DNS GSLB and then selecting 'Persistence Records' for Statistics Type.)
bugs.conditions: This occurs when viewing statistics in the GUI for a large number of Persistence Records (approximately 100,000, but the number might depend on system configuration and capacity).
bugs.impact: The system runs out of memory and fails over.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to see Persistence Records and associated statistics. For LTM and GTM Delivery: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records. For GTM GSLB: tmsh show gtm persist destination | level | target-name | key | max-results | target-type.
bugs.fix: The fix for this issue allows management of the visibility of Persistence Records using three db variables: ui.statistics.modulestatistics.<localtraffic | dnsdelivery | dnsgslb>.persistencerecords. A db variable setting of "false" prevents the potential system crashes with a large number of persistence records. Beginning in version 12.0.0, the three db variables default to 'false', preventing use of the config utility to display the persistence records. For fixed versions of 11.5 and 11.6, the db variables default to 'true' to avoid a change in behavior within these versions. It is necessary to modify those variables to 'false' to prevent use of the config utility to display persistence records. To set the db variable: -- for LTM Persistence Records, run the command: modify sys db ui.statistics.modulestatistics.localtraffic.persistencerecords value true -- for DNS Delivery Persistence Records, run the command: modify sys db ui.statistics.modulestatistics.dnsdelivery.persistencerecords value true -- for DNSGSLB, run the command: modify sys db ui.statistics.modulestatistics.dnsgslb.persistencerecords value true Important: When you enable the db variable, the GUI-specific out-of-memory condition might occur if you have a large number of records. In that case, you should use tmsh to see Persistence Records and associated statistics. For LTM and GTM Delivery: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records. For GTM GSLB: tmsh show gtm persist destination | level | target-name | key | max-results | target-type.
bugs.behavior: Beginning in version 12.0.0, the db variable ui.statistics.modulestatistics.<localtraffic | dnsdelivery | dnsgslb>.persistencerecords defaults to 'false'. In previous versions, the default was 'true.' That means that Persistence Records are no longer visible by default in the GUI. This prevents potential system crashes with a large number of persistence records. You can manage visibility of Persistence Records using the db variable. Important: When you enable the db variable, the GUI-specific out-of-memory condition might occur if you have a large number of records. In that case, you should use TMSH to see Persistence Records and associated statistics. For example, for LTM, you can use the following command: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records. To set the db variable: -- for LTM Persistence Records, run the command: modify sys db ui.statistics.modulestatistics.localtraffic.persistencerecords value true -- for DNS Delivery Persistence Records, run the command: modify sys db ui.statistics.modulestatistics.dnsdelivery.persistencerecords value true -- for DNSGSLB, run the command: modify sys db ui.statistics.modulestatistics.dnsgslb.persistencerecords value true

bugs.title: iControl REST API is unable to retrieve any sys service attributes via GET request
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST API is unable to retrieve all sys service attributes or any individual sys service attribute via GET request
bugs.conditions: -- Use iControl REST API to retrieve any sys service via GET request
bugs.impact: The iControl REST API response doesn't have these elements. iControl REST does not provide visibility for sys service attributes
bugs.fix: iControl REST API is now able to return sys service attribute information via GET request

bugs.title: User name with leading or trailing spaces creates problems.
bugs.symptoms: User name containing leading or trailing spaces (e.g., ' user1 ') results in processing errors. When the user entry gets created in MySQL it treats the user name ' user1 ' as if it were 'user1', stripping out the spaces at the beginning and the end of the name. The memcache entry does not do the same.
bugs.conditions: -- There is a user name containing leading or trailing spaces (e.g., ' user1 '). -- There is the same user name without leading or trailing spaces (e.g., 'user1').
bugs.impact: Unnecessary memcache entries. There will be multiple entries for the same user (one with and one without spaces). When the dynamic user gets deleted, the regular user name is deleted from memcache and from MySQL; the other user entry remains in memcache.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now trims leading and trailing spaces from any user name before using it. So the user name is uniform everywhere.

bugs.title: Memcache entry for dynamic user leaks
bugs.symptoms: A race condition causes a memcache entry to remain in memcache forever.
bugs.conditions: Due to a race condition between identifying dynamic users in MySQL and removing them from memcache (based on timestamp), some memcache entries remain. Although the entry is removed from MySQL, it remains in memcache.
bugs.impact: The user state information for the user remains unchanged. If the user is locked out in memcache, the user state remains locked out.
bugs.workaround: The only way to recover is to remove the user using telnet to access memcache (which is not a typical operation and is difficult to perform).
bugs.fix: Now a self expiry is set for each memcache object (which is configurable). With this change, each user remains in the cache only for the configured duration.

bugs.title: FTP port might occasionally be reused faster than expected
bugs.symptoms: FTP port is randomly selected and occasionally might be reused quickly.
bugs.conditions: FTP active mode. Source Port is set to change.
bugs.impact: FTP port might occasionally be reused faster than expected.
bugs.fix: FTP port selection uses a round robin method to avoid quick-reuse as much as possible.

bugs.title: TMM may assert if HTTP is disabled by another filter while it is parked
bugs.symptoms: If HTTP is parked in an iRule, if it is disabled by another filter on the client-side it will assert with the message: TCL passthrough switch state only valid server-side.
bugs.conditions: A HTTP iRule on the client side parks. Another filter tells HTTP to disable itself.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the TMM will crash.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using HTTP::disable in iRules that can run simultaneously with with iRules triggered by the HTTP filter. Instead, disable
bugs.fix: HTTP will no longer crash if HTTP is disabled while it is parked on the client side.

bugs.title: There is no configurable TCP timewait timer for Fast L4 virtual servers.
bugs.symptoms: Fast L4 does not have configurable TCP timewait support.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered on Fast L4 profiles, the TCP timewait is not configurable.
bugs.impact: Fast L4 TCP connflow will be torn down immediately after close. In some cases, a timewait period is needed before the connflow is torn down.
bugs.fix: There is a new configurable TCP timewait option: tmsh modify ltm profile tcp <profile_name> time-wait-timeout <value>.

bugs.title: mod_ssl: missing support for TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2
bugs.symptoms: This is due to using older versions of httpd (which includes mod_ssl ...). Newer versions of httpd as of 2.2.15-39 include the necessary support for TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2.
bugs.conditions: Any older versions of httpd which are not upgraded to 2.2.15-39 or selectively patched for the mod_ssl component will not be able to provide support for TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2. Note that in older releases, there is a dependency on openssl 1.0.1 for a backport of the mod_ssl changes to actually support TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2.
bugs.impact: No support is provided for TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to one of the following: 12.0.0-hf1 - includes changes to mod_ssl 12.1.0 - includes update to httpd 2.2.15-39
bugs.fix: Upgrade to httpd 2.2.15-39 (from el6.6) provides the needed changes to mod_ssl to support TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2.

bugs.title: Proxy configuration might not to be restored correctly in some rare cases
bugs.symptoms: Local proxy configuration on Mac OS X might not to be restored correctly in some rare cases.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac is connected, tunnel drops for some reason, race condition happens during proxy configuration restoration which causes it to not be restored properly.
bugs.impact: Proxy configuration might not to be restored correctly in some rare case.
bugs.fix: A rare case where proxy configuration might not be restored correctly has been fixed.

bugs.title: SSL filter might report codec alerts repeatedly
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores due to Out of Memory (OOM), and xdata is the majority of the memory consumption.
bugs.conditions: The SSL enters a failure mode where it appears to transmit alert messages repeatedly until TMM is OOM, which causes the transmissions to stop due to lack of memory. TMM then cores due to lack of memory.
bugs.impact: The system might crash. (Massive xfrag usage, degraded performance, eventual TMM OOM.)
bugs.fix: Clear codec alert after propagation so SSL filter no longer reports alerts indefinitely.

bugs.title: Protected Workspace is not supported on Windows 10
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support Protected Workspace on Windows 10
bugs.conditions: Protected Workspace action configured on BIG-IP APM server. Users connecting to BIG-IP APM using Windows 10 client.
bugs.impact: Users cannot use Protected Workspace feature on Windows 10.
bugs.fix: Protected Workspace disabled on Windows 10 client.

bugs.title: A false negative mandatory words alert in Internet Explorer 8 has been fixed.
Some controls on a web page might stop working.
bugs.symptoms: Some controls on a web page might stop working.
bugs.conditions: Some events with that execute in web applications.
bugs.impact: Unexpected web application malfunctions.
bugs.workaround: Create an iRule specific to each case.
bugs.fix: Problems with EventTarget.addEventListener() new feature support were fixed.

bugs.title: Determinstic NAT State information incomplete for HSL log format
bugs.symptoms: Deterministic NAT state information incomplete for HSL log format, could possibly result in incorrect reverse and forward map for dnatutil when using with HSL logged state information.
bugs.conditions: Found to affect VIPRION B2250 blades with HTSPLIT enabled, when using dnatutil with HSL logged deterministic NAT state for reverse map.
bugs.impact: Reverse and forward map could be incorrect when use with HSL logged deterministic NAT state information.
bugs.workaround: Use LTM logged deterministic NAT state information for reverse or forward map.
bugs.fix: HSL logged deterministic NAT state information can be use to correctly forward and reverse map.

bugs.title: SSLv2 based handshake causing handshake failures
bugs.symptoms: You are experiencing SSL handshake failures. There are error messages in /var/log/ltm similar to the following: tmm[16895]: 01260009:7: Connection error:9044: invalid pre-master secret (40)
bugs.conditions: -- Client SSL profiles configured. -- Client sends a CLIENTHELLO containing a SSLv2 or TLSv1 version in the handshake message.
bugs.impact: SSL connection unable to establish; error generated. Note: This occurs only for clients that send SSLv2 or TLSv1 in the CLIENTHELLO.
bugs.fix: ClientHello SSLv2 issue is now fixed.
bugs.behavior: During the SSL Handshake, the BIG-IP system strictly checks the protocol version in the pre-master secret to verify it matches with the protocol version used in the Client Hello.

bugs.title: Subscriber-level AVR statistics display the subscriber-type as "Unknown" for subscribers created using Radius Acct-Start
bugs.symptoms: Subscriber-level AVR statistics display subscriber-type as "Unknown" instead of "Dynamic" for subscribers created using a RADIUS Accounting-Start message.
bugs.conditions: Subscriber should be created using a Radius Acct-Start message.
bugs.impact: Incorrect subscriber-type in subscriber-level AVR statistics.
bugs.fix: Populate the correct subscriber-type in subscriber-level AVR statistics.

bugs.title: Nitrox crypto accelerator can sometimes hang when encrypting SSL records
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes when encrypting certain SSL records, the Cavium Nitrox crypto accelerator can hang with the LTM log message 'request queue stuck'.
bugs.conditions: Certain SSL records on a system with a Cavium Nitrox card.
bugs.impact: Nitrox crypto accelerator can hang.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the unit often frees up the Cavium Nitrox crypto accelerator chip, but should be considered a temporary solution and not a permanent fix, as the issue may return.
bugs.fix: The Nitrox crypto accelerator no longer hangs with certain SSL records.

bugs.title: Memory leak in access framework
bugs.symptoms: When multiple concurrent attempts are made to access a resource protected by APM, one of these attempts proceeds to policy execution and the rest get a message stating that session evaluation is in progress. The page that delivers this message has a unique identifier in the URL that causes the caching of this page to be ineffective. Multiple cache entries are created and these entries present themselves as a leak.
bugs.conditions: Use of APM. Multiple concurrent accesses to a resource protected by a virtual server with an APM profile attached. Note that no prior established sessions must exist for that client for this to happen.
bugs.impact: A memory leak occurs.
bugs.fix: The APM page caching now omits the unique identifier in the key. As a result, a single page, or a small fixed number of pages, can serve a multitude of clients without an increase in memory usage.

bugs.title: Added fail-over mechanism for phishing alerts.
Legal IP addresses sometimes logged in Attack Started/Stopped message.
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes legal IP addresses are logged as attack started/stopped messages.
bugs.conditions: AFM licensed and provisioned and Sweep & Flood Vector enabled.
bugs.impact: Logging.
bugs.fix: IP addresses are not logged any more for START/STOP messages. Only sampled messages will have packet details.

bugs.title: Encrypt checkbox should be greyed out for a new parameter when Application Layer Encryption is disabled under URL Configuration.
bugs.symptoms: Encrypt checkbox is not greyed out for a new parameter when Application Layer Encryption is disabled under URL Configuration.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS
bugs.impact: Configuration may not be saved.
bugs.workaround: Manually disable Encrypt parameter or use tmsh disable Application Layer Encryption.
bugs.fix: Now Encrypt checkbox is grayed out for a new parameter when Application Layer Encryption is disabled under URL Configuration.

bugs.title: URL Latencies page: pagination limited to 180 pages
bugs.symptoms: When there is a lot of information in URL Latencies with paging being available for more than 180 pages, no data is being displayed when switching to any of the pages above 180
bugs.conditions: URLs count exceeds 1800
bugs.impact: Not all URLs will be visible
bugs.workaround: Filtering can be used to limit the number of results below 1800.
bugs.fix: Number of reported URLs is now limited to 1000 (100 pages), consistent with other reporting pages.

bugs.title: Rare deadlock in CustomDialer component
bugs.symptoms: Windows 7 systems hang at a black screen after a reboot. This requires a hard boot to resolve.
bugs.conditions: CustomDialer component.
bugs.impact: Cannot log in. Requires hard boot to resolve.
bugs.fix: The CustomDialer component has been updated to prevent a rarely occurring deadlock.

bugs.title: Cipher string text box does not resize itself
bugs.symptoms: The cipher string text box is a fixed width, making it difficult to see long cipher strings.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when viewing the cipher string text box in the GUI for clientssl and serverssl profiles.
bugs.impact: If the cipher string is long, it can be hard to read.
bugs.fix: The cipher string HTML element now dynamically resizes itself with the cipher string.

bugs.title: Added ASM internal parameter to add more XML memory
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to add more than 1.2 GB of memory to the XML parser.
bugs.conditions: More than 1.2 GB of XML memory is needed for the XML parser.
bugs.impact: XML out-of-memory messages; traffic dropped.
bugs.fix: This release adds the internal parameter 'additional_xml_memory_in_mb' that enables specifying an additional amount of XML memory (as specified in MB).

bugs.title: A false positive mandatory words alert in old Firefox versions has been fixed.
CMI: Manual sync does not allow overwrite of 'newer' ASM config
bugs.symptoms: ASM Sync was designed to only request the ASM portion of the configuration if it recognizes that a peer has a newer configuration. This precludes the ability to 'roll back' changes on a device by pushing from the peer that still has the older configuration.
bugs.conditions: Devices are set up in a Manual Sync ASM-enabled group.
bugs.impact: User is unable to 'roll back' changes on a device by pushing from the peer that has an older configuration.
bugs.workaround: Make a spurious change on the device that has an older config and then push the changes to the peer.
bugs.fix: An older ASM configuration can now be manually pushed to a peer in a device group.

bugs.title: Phishing referrer checks are now correctly ignored for the configured URLs.
TMM SIGSEGV in sctp_output due to NULL snd_dst
bugs.symptoms: Crash in tmm sctp_output routine.
bugs.conditions: SCTP incorrectly processes a duplicate or unexpected COOKIE_ECHO following association shutdown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash.

bugs.title: SSL negotiation may fail when SPDY profile is enabled
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake fails when SPDY profile is attached.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Client (i.e., Chrome for Android) attempts to use SPDY protocol using Next Protocol Negotiation (NPN) during SSL handshake. -- BIG-IP system has a Cavium Nitrox card.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake or other connection failure.
bugs.workaround: Remove SPDY profile.
bugs.fix: SSL handshake now completes successfully when a SPDY profile is attached when Next Protocol Negotiation (NPN) is detected on a BIG-IP system with a Cavium Nitrox accelerator.

bugs.title: EAM is a CMP plugin and spins up one thread per TMM.
bugs.symptoms: When OAM is enabled on a virtual, an 'eam' v1 plugin profile is added to the virtual. Due to ht-split performance changes (specifically addition of "plugin_threads" field in BZ439449the eam plugin profile claims to be a CMP-enabled plugin but forces the thread count to 1. This causes the number of MPI devices to be 0, thus no channel is spun up - all connections through the virtual result in "No plugin configuration found" error in /var/log/ltm and the connection is reset. SYMPTOM: Virtuals with OAM enabled do not pass traffic - "No plugin configuration found" errors in /var/log/ltm
bugs.conditions: HTTP virtual with OAM enabled
bugs.impact: Traffic outage on OAM-enabled virtuals
bugs.workaround: hand-edit of /defaults/config_base.conf plugin_threads { class-name profile_eam container none instance-name eam value "1" <-- change this to "tmms" }
bugs.fix: EAM is a CMP plugin and spins up one thread per TMM.

bugs.title: SSL persistence can prematurely terminate TCP connection
bugs.symptoms: SSL [session id] persistence might prematurely close (FIN) a TCP connection before forwarding all data.
bugs.conditions: SSL persistence must be in use. A slow client side (WAN) exacerbates the issue.
bugs.impact: Premature close of TCP connection and potential data loss.
bugs.workaround: Disable SSL persistence.
bugs.fix: SSL [session id] persistence no longer prematurely terminate TCP connection.

bugs.title: [big3d] Possible memory leakage for auto-discovery error events.
bugs.symptoms: The big3d process may leak memory. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: You notice a progressive increase in the amount of memory that the big3d process uses. The big3d process produces a core file in the /shared/core directory. The BIG-IP system unexpectedly fails over to another system in the device group. The monitoring system marks the monitored device as unavailable.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: Your system is actively monitored by a BIG-IP GTM or Enterprise Manager system. The monitoring system is configured with discovery enabled. The big3d process returns error messages to monitor requests.
bugs.impact: Memory usage for the big3d process increases, and may eventually affect other services and overall system performance.
bugs.fix: big3d no longer leaks memory during auto-discovery failure events.

bugs.title: tmsh show sys connection output is corrected
bugs.symptoms: tmsh show sys connection output is corrupted for certain user roles.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for users with user roles that do not have access to all partitions.
bugs.impact: The output from tmsh show sys connection is corrupted. After issuing this command, the output of subsequent tmsh commands might not be correct or complete.
bugs.workaround: Quit out of tmsh. Restart the shell. Do not use the show sys connection command for users that do not have access to all partitions. Use the GUI instead to get this information.
bugs.fix: tmsh show sys connection output is correct for users that do not have access to all partitions.

bugs.title: Using proxy for IP intelligence updates
bugs.symptoms: When connecting to the proxy server, the iprepd daemon doesn't send in CONNECT request the value of DB variable iprep.server but its locally resolved IP address.
bugs.conditions: The following DB variables are configured to use proxy: proxy.host proxy.port This presents a problem when the proxy server is configured to allow only IPs that have a reverse lookup.
bugs.impact: When the proxy sees the traffic it denies it, because the reverse lookup for that server IP is not present.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the workarounds: -- Do not use proxy. -- Check the server IP address regularly and maintain proxy white list manually.
bugs.fix: Now the iprepd daemon sends CONNECT request with the value of DB variable iprep.server and lets the proxy server do the DNS lookup.

bugs.title: SNMP attribute type incorrect for certain OIDs
bugs.symptoms: The following OIDs have an incorrect setting of Gauge when they should be Integer: sysIntfMediaIndex sysIfIndex sysPacketFilterAddrIndex sysPacketFilterVlanIndex sysPacketFilterMacIndex sysStpBridgeTreeStatIndex sysStpInterfaceTreeStatIndex sysHostCpuIndex sysIntfMediaSfpIndex
bugs.conditions: SNMP queries to some F5 enterprise OIDs.
bugs.impact: The attribute type mismatch may cause some MIB browsers to report errors because of a failure to strictly adhere to the SNMP standard.
bugs.fix: All F5 enterprise MIB attribute which include a limited value range have been changed to type Integer.

bugs.title: No eud.log found on /var/tmp for 7000 series and 10000 series
bugs.symptoms: Running the command 'eud_log' on a BIG-IP 7000 series and 10000 series platform produces the following output: -- info: No EUD log found in /var/tmp. Searching boot volume -- info: No eud.log found on sda.dat.boot.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the 7000 series and 10000 series.
bugs.impact: This message indicates that eud.log file cannot be detected in the incorrect directory /var/tmp. However, the file does exist in the /var/log directory, which is the correct directory.

bugs.title: Upgrade can fail to load config due to tcp profile no longer allowing time-wait-timeout of 4294967295 (indefinite).
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade to v11.6.0 can fail with the following error message: 01070712:3: The value (-1) is outside the acceptable value set [value equal to or less than 600000] for time_wait_timeout in type TCP Profile for item <tcp_profile_name> Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: A tcp profile exists with tcp_long_timeout equal to 4294967295 (indefinite).
bugs.impact: Upgrade to v11.6.0 fails and leaves device in INOPERATIVE state.
bugs.workaround: Change tcp_long_timeout prior to upgrade to a value in the range from 0 to 600000 inclusive OR, if already upgraded, edit bigip.conf to set tcp_long_timeout to a value in the range from 0 to 600000 inclusive and run "tmsh load sys config".
bugs.fix: BIG-IP configurations now load successfully after an upgrade if the TCP profile's Time Wait value is set to 4294967295

bugs.title: Parking command called from inside catch statement
bugs.symptoms: If inside a proc or control statement (if, for, while) and a parking command (like table, session, open, send, RESOLVE::lookup) which is called from catch statement followed by a command which results in TCL error (caught), TMM will core with SIGFPE panic and this message: panic: TclExecuteByteCode execution failure: end stack top < start stack top Example (THIS CODE MAY CAUSE TMM TO CRASH if this procedure is called): proc id491771 { # WILL CAUSE TMM TO CRASH catch { [table lookup "key"] } } The correct usage of "catch" is without the brackets: proc id491771 { catch { table lookup "key" } }
bugs.conditions: 1) A parking command like "table" 2) The very next operation generates an error 3) Both commands are inside a "catch" block 4) And this catch block exists within a proc or control statement (e.g., if, for, while)
bugs.impact: TMM cores with a SIGFPE and this panic string: panic: TclExecuteByteCode execution failure: end stack top < start stack top
bugs.workaround: Any command which completes without parking after the parking command but before the error will prevent the issue. For instance set A "a" Another solution is to move "catch" statement outside of proc or control statement into body of script. Alternately remove the square brackets that indicate that the result of the command should be evaluated in this specific case. The use of brackets in this way is likely a mistake in coding of the iRule.

bugs.title: Better retransmit recovery in a lossy network.
bugs.symptoms: When a network is inherently lossy, the system might unnecessarily lose a TCP connection if a tail drop of all in-flight data happens. This problem can also happen with a configured a rate-shaper/BWC policy with a very low bandwidth limit.
bugs.conditions: During a TCP data transfer if all the data sent out is being dropped in the network, delayed ACKs will not be available for a fast re-transmit/recovery. The problem is exaggerated if the system is already in a re-transmit back-off.
bugs.impact: Connection slow down, even TCP-connection reset in the worst cases. Depending on how lossy or throttled a network is, the impact varies from slowing down or losing a connection once in a while to losing most connections.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Upon receiving partial acks we reset the re-transmit back-off.

bugs.title: GET on non-existent pool members does not show error
bugs.symptoms: Performing a GET on nonexistent pool members does not show an error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using iControl REST with nonexistent pool members.
bugs.impact: The returned response typically indicates an almost-empty resource instead of a not-found error.
bugs.workaround: Use members GET for all members and iterate through the items returned to determine if a pool member exists.
bugs.fix: Performing a GET on nonexistent pool members now shows an error when using iControl REST with nonexistent pool members.

bugs.title: GTM iRule command [LB::status up] gives error
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to create this GTM iRule when DNS_REQUEST { LB::status up } you'll get this error in the logs: "01070151:3: Rule [/Common/irule_test] error: /Common/irule_test:2: error: [invalid option "up" must be: vs pool mbr][up]"
bugs.conditions: Creating GTM iRules
bugs.impact: Can't use this specific iRule command syntax.

bugs.title: Changing the ending of a macro in Access Policy crashes TMM.
bugs.symptoms: The default ending for a macro is out. Changing this to anything else crashes the TMM and causes it to core.
bugs.conditions: Create a macro, change the ending.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed to allow for name changes to the macro endings, so that macros are no longer required to end in out.

bugs.title: Now Windows Logon Integration does not recreate temporary user for logon execution each time
bugs.symptoms: Temporary user 'f5 Pre-Logon User' is created and deleted each time it is used which prevents the performance of domain operations like adding that user to specific domain group or setting properties because the SSID changes every time.
bugs.conditions: This happens when both of these conditions exist: 1. Windows Logon Integration is used. 2. Enforce access policy execution option is selected.
bugs.impact: As a result, it is impossible to manage the temporary user 'f5 Pre-Logon User'.
bugs.fix: Now the 'f5 Pre-Logon User' is created only once, which allows a Domain or System Administrator to manage it, because the SSID does not change. When the user is no longer required (that is, when the logon process is complete), 'f5 Pre-Logon User' is disabled and remains disabled until the next usage.

bugs.title: Inline JavaScript with HTML entities may be handled incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: If JavaScript code is included into an HTML page and contains HTML entities inside, it may be processed incorrectly by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: HTML page which contains inline JavaScript code with HTML entities inside.
bugs.impact: Web application does not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule for each individual case to correct this behavior.
bugs.fix: Now JavaScript code with HTML entities inside is processed correctly.

bugs.title: Edge clients shuts down the DTLS channel if the state of IP address on the adapter that was used to build the tunnel, changes to deprecated.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client shuts down the DTLS channel if the state of IP address on the adapter that was used to build the tunnel changes to deprecated.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Client monitors the state of IP address for the DTLS tunnel, so the system can react quickly to any network connectivity issues. The monitor correctly disconnects the tunnel if the adapter loses the IP address. However, there is an issue that causes the tunnel to shut down when the state of IP address is changed to deprecated.
bugs.impact: Tunnel processing halts.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client now keeps the DTLS connection until the IP address becomes invalid, as expected.

bugs.title: Applying a monitor to pool and pool member may cause an issue.
bugs.symptoms: Typically, when applying a monitor to pool and a monitor to pool member, there are no issues. In a scenario where the pool monitor is incompatible with the pool member, it can cause validation issue.
bugs.conditions: A scenario where the pool monitor is incompatible with the pool member, it can cause validation issue. For example, a pool with an http monitor and a wildcard pool member (even if pool member had its own monitor).
bugs.impact: Failed transaction or configuration load.
bugs.workaround: Remove the pool monitor, load, then add pool monitor back.
bugs.fix: Instances in which the pool monitor is incompatible with the pool member are now validated correctly.

bugs.title: When logging out of Office 365 TMM may restart
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart when a user initiates single logout (SLO) from Microsoft Office 365 configured as a SAML Service Provider (SP).
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: 1. The BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP) with Office 365 configured as a SAML Service Provider (SP). 2. Single logout (SLO) is configured on the BIG-IP system. 3. As a part of a SLO request, the SP sends unsupported query parameters.
bugs.impact: Under certain conditions TMM may restart.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, disable SLO on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer restarts when a user initiates single logout (SLO) from Microsoft Office 365 configured as a SAML Service Provider (SP).

bugs.title: Support Android RDP client 8.1.3 with APM remote desktop gateway
bugs.symptoms: Support Android RDP client 8.1.3 with APM remote desktop gateway
bugs.impact: User's cannot run up-to-date official Android RDP client against APM as RDG.
bugs.fix: Support Android RDP client 8.1.3 with APM remote desktop gateway

bugs.title: Recurring file checker doesn't interrupt session if client machine has missing file
bugs.symptoms: If file required for recurring file checker agent is deleted on client machine when session already established - session would not be interrupted.
bugs.conditions: File checker agent is used. Recurring check is enabled for it.
bugs.impact: Session is not interrupted when it should be.
bugs.fix: Now session is interrupted when file required for recurring file check is missing.

bugs.title: SSL profiles using password protected SSL keys cause config utility error
bugs.symptoms: A config utility error occurs when attempting to modify client SSL profile.
bugs.conditions: A client SSL profile with a password protected SSL key.
bugs.impact: Modification of SSL profile fails.
bugs.workaround: use tmsh to modify profile.
bugs.fix: Make ckcName same for both GUI and TMSH

bugs.title: vCMP guests fail the image verification check
bugs.symptoms: IF BIG-IP image verification is enabled, vCMP guests may report that image verification has failed when you attempt to upgrade, even if you place the .sig file and .iso image on the vCMP guest.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP image verification is enabled (sys db liveinstall.checksig value "enable") vCMP guests exist New BIG-IP .iso image and .sig file is uploaded to the host and to the guests, and an upgrade is triggered.
bugs.impact: The software install will fail on the vCMP guests, the software install status will be reported as "failed (Repository must be a file for signature validation ; /tmp/lind_util.CIcASU.)"
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can disable automatic image verification and do image verification manually before installing. Impact of workaround: this will have no impact to the system. To disable automatic image verification, run the following tmsh command: tmsh modify sys db liveinstall.checksig value "disable" To manually verify the image, please see K24341140: Verifying BIG-IP software images using .sig and .pem files, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K24341140

bugs.title: HTTP request logging reports incorrect response code
bugs.symptoms: HTTP request logging reports 200/OK response code before any response has been received.
bugs.conditions: HTTP request logging enabled.
bugs.impact: Misleading messages in the logs. These messages are benign and can safely be ignored.
bugs.fix: Response code now reported only in HTTP response logs.

bugs.title: BIOS initial release
bugs.symptoms: This is a report of the initial release of BIOS 1.05.033.0.
bugs.conditions: New BIOS release.
bugs.impact: BIOS is updated to BIOS 1.05.033.0.
bugs.fix: Initial BIOS 1.05.033.0 release. No issues.

bugs.title: Virtual deletion failure possible when using sFlow
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to delete virtual server objects may fail when sFlow polling is in progress. This error message might occur intermittently when trying to delete a virtual server: 01070265:3: The Virtual Server (vs_name) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a sflow http data source (ds_name).
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP configuration contains one or more sFlow receivers that are actively polled. -- Your BIG-IP system contains a virtual server that references an HTTP profile. -- You attempt to delete the virtual server object.
bugs.impact: Users cannot delete virtual server objects when sFlow polling is in progress.
bugs.fix: This error message no longer occurs when trying to delete a virtual and using sFlow: 01070265:3: The Virtual Server (vs_name) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a sflow http data source (ds_name).
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to remove attached HTTP profile that has sflow enabled before attempting to delete virtual server.

bugs.title: FPS injection only into success responses
bugs.symptoms: FPS JavaScript was injected into HTTP responses regardless their status code.
bugs.conditions: Error response (status code 404).
bugs.impact: WebSafe components are easily identified.
bugs.fix: FPS JavaScript is now injected only into responses with 2xx status codes.

bugs.title: JavaScript error during CSRF protection
bugs.symptoms: Since Javascript is executed on client side. When it comes to page render, javascript errors might break your page.
bugs.conditions: Using Internet Explorer 8 with CSRF ASM enabled.
bugs.impact: Since Javascript is executed on client side. When it comes to page render, javascript errors might break your page.
bugs.fix: After upgrading to BIG-IP version 11.6.0, using Internet Explorer 8, there is no longer the JavaScript error "Object doesn't support this action" when using the CSRF protection feature. Note that despite the error message, there was CSRF protection.

bugs.title: Resolved LSOs are overwritten by source device in new Policy Sync with new LSO
bugs.symptoms: Previously resolved Location-Specific Object (LSO) on target devices are overwritten by values on source device in a new Policy Sync operation with new LSO to resolve.
bugs.conditions: Perform a Policy Sync on a profile with LSO, make changes to the LSO on resolution. Perform another Policy Sync on the same profile with new LSO that requires resolution
bugs.impact: Previously customized values for LSO on target device are lost.
bugs.workaround: Config the value back on target device after the new sync.
bugs.fix: Customized LSO values on target device from previous Policy Sync will be retained after a new Policy Sync with new LSO.

bugs.title: Elliptic Curves Extension in ServerHello might cause failed SSL connection.
bugs.symptoms: Supported Elliptic Curves Extension is present in ServerHello, but some clients cannot process it.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when Supported Elliptic Curves Extension is present in ServerHello when presented to a client that cannot process it.
bugs.impact: Failed SSL connection.
bugs.fix: Elliptic Curves Extension has been removed to support more types of clients.

bugs.title: Small but continuous mcpd memory leak associated with statistics.
bugs.symptoms: A small amount of memory is allocated and not released each time the statsd process gathers the global access statistic information. Symptoms include a small but constant rise in memory usage associated with statistics. Note: Although the memory leak occurs in association with APM statistics specifically, APM does not need to be provisioned for the leak to occur.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during normal operation.
bugs.impact: Over a long period of time, mcpd runs out of memory. The system periodically posts messages similar to the following in /shared/tmp/mcpd.out: mcpd: BUG: tmstat_dealloc invoked on a handle with rows outstanding; release all rows before calling tmstat_dealloc.
bugs.fix: An issue has been fixed that resulted in a small, periodic mcpd memory leak associated with statistics.

bugs.title: Office365 generated SAML SLO message causes browser connection to be reset.
bugs.symptoms: When a user initiates SAML single logout (SLO) from Microsoft Office 365 (as a Service Provider), the request is terminated by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under all of the following conditions: 1. The BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML Identity Provider (IdP). 2. Microsoft Office 365 is configured as a SAML Service Provider (SP). 3. SP-initiated SLO is attempted and the SLO message contains a detached signature.
bugs.impact: As a result, SLO is not executed and sessions on the BIG-IP system and the SP are left alive.
bugs.fix: Microsoft Office 365 generated SAML SLO message no longer causes browser connection to reset.

bugs.title: A false positive mandatory words alert in Internet Explorer has been fixed.
All blades in a cluster remain offline after provisioning ASM or FPS
bugs.symptoms: After provisioning either ASM or FPS on a cluster, the system may reach a state in which the datasyncd process will keep all of the blades offline. The system will repeatedly switch the primary blade, but never successfully transition to online.
bugs.conditions: This is a rare scenario that may happen when provisioning either ASM or FPS on a cluster.
bugs.impact: If this state is reached, all of the blades will remain offline and not handle incoming traffic until the entire chassis is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: If this scenario happens, the workaround is to reboot the entire chassis, or individually reboot all of the blades roughly at the same time.
bugs.fix: Fixed a rare scenario in which all the blades in a cluster remain offline after provisioning either ASM or FPS.

bugs.title: Export of huge policies might endup with 'too many pipes opened' error
bugs.symptoms: Export of huge policies might endup with 'too many pipes opened' error. Policy must be >321 element
bugs.conditions: Huge policy (300+ elements i.e. ~100 items)
bugs.impact: It's not possible to export access policy
bugs.fix: Extra huge policies are exportable

bugs.title: MRF SIP iRules events not raised if previous message's event is still running
bugs.symptoms: The SIP_REQUEST, SIP_RESPONSE, SIP_REQUEST_SEND or SIP_RESPONSE_SEND iRule event may not be raised for a message if the previous message on that connection has an iRule script still executing.
bugs.conditions: The previous message's SIP event performs an asynchronous operation (such as the commands after or table).
bugs.impact: The iRule scripts for SIP messages may not execute on all messages received or sent.
bugs.fix: SIP events now execute as expected on all messages received or sent.

bugs.title: Export of huge policies might ends up with 'too many pipes opened' error
bugs.symptoms: Export of huge policies might ends up with 'too many pipes opened' error. Policy must be >321 elements
bugs.conditions: Huge policy (300+ elements i.e. ~100 items)
bugs.impact: It's not possible to export access policy
bugs.fix: Extra huge policies are exportable

bugs.title: Route domains' firewall policies may be removed after sync
bugs.symptoms: If you modify the firewall policy of a route domain, and then sync, then it may be removed rather than changed on devices receiving the sync.
bugs.conditions: This affects full load sync (full load checkbox is enabled, or the 'Overwrite Configuration' option was selected), but not incremental sync.
bugs.impact: Firewall rules may be removed.
bugs.workaround: Set the policy to none, sync, then set it to the desired value and sync again.
bugs.fix: If you modify the firewall policy of a route domain, and then sync, then it could be removed rather than changed on devices receiving the sync. This no longer happens.

bugs.title: Priority order of Diameter Router Profile static routes determined by order in bigip.conf
bugs.symptoms: Priority order of Diameter Router Profile static routes is determined by order in bigip.conf. In the GUI, it appears that the user can assign priority order to static routes for a Diameter Router Profile.
bugs.conditions: If there are multiple static routes attached to a Diameter Router Profile, the first route that appears in the list of routes in bigip.conf is the one the system uses.
bugs.impact: This can cause BIG-IP to choose a route that is not what you expected.
bugs.workaround: To change the priority order of static routes for a Diameter Router Profile, the user must manually edit the bigip.conf configuration file, or use tmsh to manually order the static routes in the Router Profile.

bugs.title: Updated SWG Implementation Guide to specify need to disable Address Translation on virtual server for SSL.
HTTP Basic authentication module logs clear text password in /var/log/apm at debug level
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP parser logs a clear text password in the /var/log/apm log file from a debug log message. This occurs only when the accesscontrol log level is debug and HTTP authentication of type Basic is used in the access policy.
bugs.conditions: The accesscontrol log level is debug and HTTP authentication of type Basic is used in the access policy.
bugs.impact: A clear text password is logged in /var/log/apm.
bugs.workaround: Change the accesscontrol log level to informational or higher.
bugs.fix: HTTP parser is fixed and to log obfuscated password in /var/log/apm.

bugs.title: Changing the netmask on an advertised virtual address causes it to stop being advertised until tmrouted is restarted
bugs.symptoms: After changing the netmask of an advertised virtual address, the address is no longer advertised.
bugs.conditions: Must have an advertised virtual address, and change its netmask.
bugs.impact: tmrouted must be restarted whenever the netmask of an advertised virtual address is changed.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmrouted whenever the netmask of an advertised virtual address is changed.
bugs.fix: Now, an advertised route remains advertised after its netmask is changed.

bugs.title: Incorrect persistence entries are created when invoking cookie hash persistence within an iRule using offset and length parameters.
bugs.symptoms: When using a cookie hash persistence profile and an iRule to provide finer granularity using offset and length parameters to calculate the hash, the system creates incorrect persistence entries.
bugs.conditions: Cookie hash persistence profile and iRule on top of that specifies offset and length of the cookie to be used for hashing is needed.
bugs.impact: Incorrect persistence entries are created.
bugs.fix: Using cookie hash persistence and invoking cookie hash persistence from within an iRule now works as expected.

bugs.title: flash.net.NetConnection::connect() has an erroneous security check
bugs.symptoms: Accessing some content in a different domain does not work as expected because of an erroneous security check.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when getting a URI property immediately after calling the connect() method.
bugs.impact: Possible Flash web application malfunction, but symptoms vary.
bugs.fix: The erroneous security check has been fixed, so accessing some content in a different domain now works as expected.

bugs.title: Diameter traffic not restricted to virtual server assigned to static route
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server that is assigned to a static route is not honored. Specifically, traffic is not filtered to be only on that virtual server.
bugs.conditions: A static route is configured with a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The traffic continues to be routed to the static route without matching the virtual server.
bugs.fix: Diameter traffic is now restricted to the virtual server assigned to a static route, as expected.

bugs.title: RBA eam and websso daemons segfaulting while provisioning
bugs.symptoms: Crash while provisioning
bugs.conditions: This sometimes seem to happen with only APM being provisioned and not being tested for APM functionality.
bugs.impact: RBA eam and websso daemons are segfaulting

bugs.title: syscalld core dumps now keep more debugging information
