bugs.symptoms: syscalld has a fixed-size queue of jobs. If this fills up, then it will intentionally dump core, but this core dump has little visibility into what commands were being run at the time.
bugs.conditions: syscalld is mostly invoked by the GUI or CMI sync to trigger the configuration being saved.
bugs.impact: syscalld core dumps will occur and generate customer cases, but it is difficult for a developer to obtain any useful information.
bugs.fix: syscalld has a fixed-size queue of jobs. If this fills up, then it will intentionally dump core, but this core dump used to have little visibility into what commands were being run at the time. It now maintains a list of the most recently run commands that will be written into the core file.

bugs.title: Device version in AFM log message could be empty
bugs.symptoms: Device version in AFM log message could be empty
bugs.conditions: When a log message is generated for AFM events
bugs.impact: Log message will not have device version
bugs.fix: AFM log messages not correctly show device version.

bugs.title: SNMP error: Unknown Object Identifier (Index out of range:0 ) for sysCpuSensorSlot
bugs.symptoms: An SNMP query for sysCpuSensorSlot 0 returns 'Unknown Object Identifier (Index out of range:0 ) for sysCpuSensorSlot'.
bugs.conditions: SNMP query for sysCpuSensorSlot 0.
bugs.impact: SNMP MIB variable sysCpuSensorSlot 0 is not available.
bugs.workaround: Use the command 'tmctl cpu_info_stat' on the BIG-IP system to retrieve the sysCpuSensorSlot value.
bugs.fix: The software that generates the F5 BIG-IP MIBs has been updated to allow a slot 0 return value.

bugs.title: BGP disabling graceful-restart in ZebOS does not persist and is automatically enabled
bugs.symptoms: The ZebOS command to 'disable' BGP graceful-restart works temporarily, but is reset to 'enable' after system restart.
bugs.conditions: Setting BGP graceful-restart to enable and restarting the system.
bugs.impact: Cannot disable graceful-restart past a restart operation.
bugs.behavior: Graceful restart can now be disabled at the command line and the setting persists through reboots.
bugs.fix: Now, disabling graceful-restart and persists through system reboot.

bugs.title: Restoring UCS file breaks auto-sync requiring forced sync.
bugs.symptoms: Automatic sync will temporarily not work after loading a UCS.
bugs.conditions: Load of a UCS on an affected hotfix.
bugs.impact: Until a manual sync is done, auto-sync will not occur.
bugs.workaround: Perform a forced manual sync and then the system will return to operation.
bugs.fix: Restoring UCS file now retains auto-sync functionality.

bugs.title: Fixed possible issue causing Edge Client to crash during reconnect
bugs.symptoms: Edge Client may rarely crash during reconnect.
bugs.conditions: Session reconnection using Edge Client. When APM session closes on BIG-IP (by a timeout, or by other options, for example, 'Restrict to Single Client IP') the Edge Client starts new session. Occasionally when reestablishing connection to the BIG-IP system, the Edge Client crashes.
bugs.impact: Rarely encountered crash.
bugs.fix: Fixed possible issue that could cause BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows to crash during reconnect.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Edge Client uses generic icon set even if F5 icon set is configured
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge client uses generic icon set even if F5 icon set is configured.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP MAC Edge client customized for a specific language.
bugs.impact: The UI might show the generic icon set for MAC edge client in the system menu.
bugs.workaround: Remove customization for that language.
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP Edge Client uses the set of icons that the configuration specifies. Also, F5 icons no longer display for a split second during application launch when the configuration specifies the generic set of icons.

bugs.title: Concurrent REST calls on a single endpoint may fail
bugs.symptoms: Concurrent REST PATCH calls on a particular endpoint, or configuration by BIG-IQ, may fail due to database deadlocks.
bugs.conditions: Concurrent REST PATCH calls were made on a particular endpoint, or device was configured by BIG-IQ.
bugs.impact: Configuration changes fail due to database deadlock.
bugs.workaround: Return values from REST calls should be checked before proceeding to next call.
bugs.fix: Fixed a MySQL deadlock that occurred when using REST API to send several patch requests to parameters of a security policy.

bugs.title: Function::call() and Function::apply() wrapping does not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: Function::call() and Function::apply() wrapping does not work as expected.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using an indirect method call.
bugs.impact: Possible Adobe Flash web application malfunction, but the symptoms can vary.
bugs.fix: Indirect method call using Function::call() or Function::apply() works properly now.

bugs.title: License checks for fictive URLs and injected tags
bugs.symptoms: FPS plugin doesn't check the required license for fictive requests from JavaScript and for injected tags, like phishing CSS and image.
bugs.conditions: Feature is unlicensed.
bugs.impact: Injected tags may cause false positive alerts.
bugs.fix: Phishing tags are no longer injected into HTML when phishing is not licensed. And responses to virtual URLs are sent only if the required feature is licensed.
bugs.behavior: Phishing tags are no longer injected into HTML when phishing protection is not licensed. And responses to virtual URLs are sent only if the required feature is licensed.

bugs.title: ASM attack appear ongoing forever if restarting dosl7d during an attack
bugs.symptoms: If dosl7d is restarted during an attack it doesn't write the "end attack" event to logdb.
bugs.conditions: Restarting dosl7d in the middle of an ASM attack (including actions that implicitly cause dosl7d restart like tmm restart or reboot).
bugs.impact: Attack appears ongoing in Dos Overview page (even though it should be marked "ended").
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: TMM core due to SACK hole value mismatch
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores with 'sack scoreboard population counts valid' assert. The TMM core occurs due to lost-packet retransmitted packet value mismatch.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when processing retransmitted packets configured for selective acknowledgement (SACK), when multipath TCP (MPTCP) and selective negative acknowledgement (SNACK) are enabled with a SNACK-supporting client.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Disable MPTCP. -- Disable the SNACK option in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: TMM handles the case, and no longer cores due to lost-packet retransmitted packet value mismatch.

bugs.title: A TMM core that was found during performance testing was fixed.
DNS record data may have domain names compressed when using iRules
bugs.symptoms: Some DNS record types forbid dns name compression in their record data, e.g., the NAPTR Replacement field. For certain parts of the DNS feature set, some of these record datum may have compressed names, e.g., DNS iRules, DNSSEC, GTM.
bugs.conditions: Using iRules.
bugs.impact: Some clients may expect uncompressed names and may not be able to follow compression pointers. This may cause the client to fail to use the RR.
bugs.fix: Fields are properly not compressed, e.g., the NAPTR Replacement field.

bugs.title: tmsh allows cipher group creation with non-existent "require" or "exclude" cipher rule.
bugs.symptoms: Using tmsh it is possible to create a cipher group referencing a non-existent cipher rule with tmsh even if this configuration is invalid.
bugs.conditions: Use tmsh to create a cipher group referencing a non-existent cipher rule using a command like this, where the 'require' or the 'exclude' directive comes after the 'allow' directive. The non-existent cipher rule is "no-exist" in these examples: tmsh create ltm cipher group test-group { allow add { f5-default } require add { no-exist } } tmsh create ltm cipher group test-group { allow add { f5-default } exclude add { no-exist } }
bugs.impact: The result is an invalid configuration that can break configuration synchronisation between BIG-IP peers in some cases (after upgrades, or full configuration reload, for example). Also, when navigating to the cipher group the GUI does not show it. The GUI may also show this error: "An error has occurred while trying to process your request. "
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI to create a new cipher groups. When using tmsh, don't create a cipher group referencing a non-existent cipher rule.

bugs.title: iApps do not support FQDN nodes
bugs.symptoms: All iApps fail when FQDN nodes are included as pool members in an iApp-generated pool.
bugs.conditions: - In an iApp, create a pool with nodes defined by FQDN. - In an iApp, attempt to reconfigure, or even open, make no change, and click update.
bugs.impact: GUI shows the following error: 'script did not successfully complete: (field not present: 'address'...'.
bugs.workaround: Create the pool outside of the iApp and attach it with the 'use existing pool' option, which is a feature of all recent F5 Networks iApps.

bugs.title: TMM might crash when using PPTP with profile logging enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash when using PPTP with profile logging enabled.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- PPTP-ALG with log profile enabled. -- CGNAT configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable logging from the PPTP profile.
bugs.fix: Using PPTP with profile logging now works correctly and no longer causes TMM to crash.

bugs.title: Upgrade failure from version 11.4.0 due to incorrect configuration being saved
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade failure, after saving a custom filter based on a client IP address in the Requests logs, loading the configuration, or upgrading from it, might fail.
bugs.conditions: After saving a custom filter based on a client IP address in the Requests logs.
bugs.impact: Configuration is not loaded.
bugs.workaround: Edit /config/bigip.conf, search for the following line, and delete it: values { \? }.
bugs.fix: After saving a custom filter based on a client IP address in the Requests logs, loading the configuration, or upgrading from it, now completes successfully.

bugs.title: Virtual Server with misconfigured profiles may block upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Server with unmatched context settings in a profile might block upgrade.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a virtual server configured with a TCP, UDP, or SCTP profile set with either (context clientside) or (context serverside), but without a corresponding profile with the other proxy side (serverside or clientside, respectively).
bugs.impact: Cannot upgrade and roll-forward a configuration, and the system might post the following error message: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Less than the required minimum number of profiles found on /Common/test-vip5: At least 1 Of but Not more than 1 Of (UDP Profile, TCP Profile, SCTP Profile)
bugs.workaround: There are 2 workarounds: 1: Before upgrade, modify the existing configuration, by either removing the (context) line or by adding the corresponding context, and then saving the UCS file. 2: After a failed attempt to load the UCS file, manually modify the UCS file as described in workaround 1., and then load the file again.

bugs.title: TMM crashes on the standby when starting up in HA config and Active processing traffic in APM module
bugs.symptoms: On a standby unit, TMM dumps core files when it is starting up and continues to do so when the active unit is handling traffic in the APM module.
bugs.conditions: The issue happens on APM systems when high availability is configured and the following conditions are met: 1. The active device is busy processing traffic. 2. Some sessions on the active device are terminated. 3. The TMM in standby device is starting up.
bugs.impact: TMM on the standby device crashes with SEGV, which causes existing sessions not stored on the standby device and users have to re-login should failover occur.
bugs.fix: In APM HA environments, the system now prevents global status from being updated before the initialization is completed on a standby device. TMM on the standby no longer dumps core files on startup.

bugs.title: tmm crash while initializing the URL filter context for SWG.
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash while initializing the URL filter context for SWG.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this crash. It may be connected to BIG-IP being unable to update the SWG database.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes while initializing the URL filter context for SWG.

bugs.title: System matches messages to previous Diameter Route Application ID after modifying ID value
bugs.symptoms: System matches to previous Diameter Route Application ID after modifying the application ID value.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after modifying the application ID value for a Diameter Route object.
bugs.impact: The Diameter Route might continue to match Diameter messages against the old application ID until TMM is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Always restart TMM after changing the value of application ID in a Diameter Route.
bugs.fix: System now matches to the correct Diameter Route Application ID after modifying the application ID value.

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS cannot use a loopback address with fallback IP load balancing
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP DNS cannot use a loopback address with fallback IP load balancing.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP DNS pool using fallback IP load balancing.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure a loopback address using fallback IP load balancing.
bugs.fix: Now, a BIG-IP DNS Pool fallback IP address can be localhost.

bugs.title: The fix strengthens certificate validation, including hostname verification.
Certain rapidly-terminating UDP virtuals may core on standby
bugs.symptoms: Based on an internal race condition, it is possible for certain flows to cause cores on standby BIG-IPs when using connection mirroring on layer 7 VIPs. This does not apply to use of mirroring on Performance or Performance (HTTP) virtuals.
bugs.conditions: Standard UDP virtual using connection mirroring.
bugs.impact: Restart of the standby tmm. No connections are affected, though if packets are set to require acknowledgements from the standby there may be a brief delay in processing for some or all connections.

bugs.title: APD or APMD should not assert when it can do more by logging error message before exiting.
bugs.symptoms: APD or APMD asserts and exits without logging error messages to aid in debugging the error.
bugs.conditions: In some rare situation apmd (for example, access 'profile not found', failure in 'loading policy object'), APD, APMD assert. This results in dumping core.
bugs.impact: Restarting of APD, APMD and core file.
bugs.fix: Now, in some rare situations where previously APD or APMD would assert, the system logs proper error messages before exiting. This results in restarting APD or APMD.

bugs.title: PAC file download mechanism race condition
bugs.symptoms: PAC file download mechanism might encounter a race condition if /etc/hosts is patched with the static entry of the host that contains PAC file.
bugs.conditions: The /etc/hosts is patched with the static entry of the host that contains PAC file.
bugs.impact: Proxy PAC file fails to download.
bugs.workaround: Add delay in proxy PAC file download to avoid race condition.
bugs.fix: PAC file download mechanism now avoids a race condition if /etc/hosts is patched with the static entry of the host that contains PAC file.

bugs.title: Deterministic NAT state information from HSL is not usable on VIPRION B4300 blades
bugs.symptoms: Deterministic NAT HSL state information is not useable by dnatutil, resulting in "Unparseable line" error.
bugs.conditions: Deterministic NAT and HSL logging for LSN pool on a VIPRION B4300 blade.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the HSL logged state information for dnatutil.
bugs.workaround: Use LTM logged deterministic NAT state information.
bugs.fix: Deterministic NAT state information from HSL is now usable on VIPRION B4300 blades.

bugs.title: HTML Event handlers may not work if 'eval' is redefined
bugs.symptoms: If 'eval' JavaScript call is redefined in HTML page, event handlers may not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: There may be many ways to re-define 'eval'. For example: <form> <button name=eval onclick="someFunction();">Button</button> </form> In this case 'onclick' event handler will not work through Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly. In the worst case scenario, the browser (Internet Explorer 9 or later) may crash.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Network access to FP does not work on Yosemite using APM Mac Edge Client.
bugs.symptoms: If APM BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac on OS X Yosemite attempts to connect to FirePass, network access cannot be established.
bugs.conditions: APM Edge Client for Mac on OS X Yosemite connecting to FirePass.
bugs.impact: Network access cannot be established with FirePass.
bugs.fix: Network access can now be established with FirePass using APM BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac on OS X Yosemite.

bugs.title: Poor performance in clipboard channel when copying
bugs.symptoms: JavaRDP client hangs when user tries to copy very large text fragment into clipboard.
bugs.conditions: User tries to copy very large text fragment.
bugs.impact: JavaRDP client lags or hangs on copying. In the worst case, user should close and reconnect JavaRDP client.
bugs.fix: Clipboard channel has significantly better performance now.

bugs.title: TMSH setting certain values for 'ip-protocol' has incorrect behavior
bugs.symptoms: Using TMSH to set certain values for 'ip-protocol' does not set the expected value. For example, setting 'ip-protocol' value to 'any', 'ip', 'hopopt', the value for 'ip-protocol' may be set incorrectly. This occurs because TMSH cannot determine the exact mapping because of the one-to-many relationship (for example: 0 maps to 'any', to 'ip', and to 'hopopt').
bugs.conditions: TMSH commands for setting 'ip-protocol'.
bugs.impact: The system does not set the expected value. For example, if you specify 'ipv6-auth', tmsh lists it as 'ah'. Specifying 'ipv6-crypt' results in 'esp'. Specifying 'esp' results in 'ipv6-crypt'. Specifying 'ah' results in 'ipv6-auth'. Specifying 'hopopt' results in 'any'. Specifying 'ip' results in 'any'.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when PPTP finds a redirected flow when checking for an existing tunnel
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when PPTP finds a redirected flow when checking for an existing tunnel.
bugs.conditions: PPTP-ALG and CGNAT on a chassis system when a blade has been added with a stale PPTP tunnel.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now drops the new flow/tunnel and allow it to clean up, so TMM no longer crashes when PPTP finds a redirected flow when checking for an existing tunnel.

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client, with primary language of German shows unneeded text shown under disconnected status.
bugs.symptoms: With BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac, when primary language is set to German on the Mac, the text shown under the disconnected status contains extra, unneeded text wording.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client for Mac, when primary language is set to German on the Mac.
bugs.impact: Shows the following message: 'Um eine Verbindung herzustellen, wählen Sie aus dem Menü oben einen Server aus, und klicken Sie dann auf die Schaltfläche 'Auto-Verbindung' oder 'Verbinden' sichern und Werner der Seite standen aufs Auge drücken als Schadenersatz einer Woche kein Telefonat erneute.'
bugs.fix: For BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac with primary language of German, the content that displays under disconnected status is now correct, without any unneeded text.

bugs.title: [GUI] [GTM] Cannot remove the first listed dependent virtual server from dependency list.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use the GUI to remove the first virtual server listed in alphabetical order from the dependent list of virtual server if there are multiple virtual servers in the dependency list.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with several dependency virtual servers configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot manage virtual server dependency list using GUI as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use the corresponding tmsh commands to manage the virtual server dependency list.
bugs.fix: You can now use the GUI to remove the alphabetically first virtual server from the dependent list of virtual servers.

bugs.title: Proxy SSL caused tmm to core by dereferencing a null pointer
bugs.symptoms: When server side SSL decides to 'passthrough' the traffic, it requests that the client side convert itself to 'passthrough' mode, but the client side SSL was already in a closing state (due to timeout).
bugs.conditions: When both Proxy SSL and Proxy SSL Passthrough are enabled. Proxy SSL changes to passthrough mode, but the client side is closed or has timed out.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now checks that the state is not in closing state before updating the statistics.

bugs.title: 'tmsh install sys software block-device-image' installs the local image instead of the block-device image.
bugs.symptoms: Both the 'tmsh install sys software image' and 'tmsh install sys software block-device-image' commands set the software_desired row corresponding with the target volume, to the product/version/build of the image specified for installation. The lind process, which manages software installation/volume creation tasks, then uses that product/version/build to search for a matching image. If both a local image and a block-device-image exist with the same product/version/build, the lind picks one based on its own preference. Because of the lind preference for local images, this might result in a local image being installed, even though the command issued is 'tmsh install sys software block-device-image'.
bugs.conditions: -- There exists both a local image and a block-device-image with the same product/version/build. -- You run the following command: tmsh install sys software block-device-image
bugs.impact: The system installs the local image instead of the block-device image. In most cases, this is not an issue: the requested software is still installed, so the goal is achieved. In some cases, however, the image chosen by lind is not actually accessible. In this case, installation fails.
bugs.workaround: Delete any local images mirroring the block device being installed.
bugs.fix: The lind now conducts a 'read test' when searching for available images. If an image is readable and has the proper checksum, it will be used, so the installation request will not fail if it is at all possible.

bugs.title: The HTTP_REQUEST iRule event may cause the TMM to crash if the explicit proxy is used
bugs.symptoms: If the flow inside a HTTP_REQUEST event raised by the explicit proxy is expired, the TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: The explicit proxy is configured for HTTP, and the HTTP_REQUEST iRule event is used.
bugs.impact: If state-changing commands are used within the HTTP_REQUEST event raised by the explicit proxy, they may not work correctly, and TMM might crash.
bugs.workaround: Avoid the HTTP_REQUEST event if possible.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes when under load when the HTTP_REQUEST iRule handler is used with the explicit proxy. HTTP state-changing commands used within HTTP_REQUEST on the explicit proxy works correctly.

bugs.title: In specific cases, persist cookie insert fails to insert a session cookie when using an iRule
bugs.symptoms: The 'persist cookie insert' and 'persist cookie rewrite' iRule commands fail to set session cookies.
bugs.conditions: A persistence cookie profile with a timeout of zero must be applied. If either command is used without an explicit timeout, LTM will fail to set a session cookie.
bugs.impact: TMM sets a cookie that expires using timeout of 180 instead of a session cookie.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly specify a 0 for the cookie timeout in the iRule.
bugs.fix: Cookie persistence now works as expected.

bugs.title: HSB lockup after HiGig MAC reset
bugs.symptoms: HSB lockups can occur after a HiGig MAC reset on BIG-IP 5000/7000-series and 10250 platforms.
bugs.conditions: -- HiGig MAC reset. -- BIG-IP 5000/7000-series and 10250 platforms.
bugs.impact: An HSB lockup results in a NIC failsafe and reboot of the unit. The system posts messages similar to the following in the LTM log: -- bcm56xxd[8161]: 012c0015:6: Link: 4.1 is DOWN. -- bcm56xxd[8161]: 012c0012:6: Reset HSBe2 (bus 1) HGM0 MAC completed on higig2 link 4.1 down event. -- bcm56xxd[8161]: 012c0015:6: Link: 4.1 is UP. ... -- tmm2[13842]: 01230111:2: Interface 0.3: HSB DMA lockup on transmitter failure.
bugs.fix: HSB lockups no longer occur after a HiGig MAC reset on BIG-IP 5000/7000-series and 10250 platforms.

bugs.title: Failed to sync connectivity or rewrite profile created from non-default profile
bugs.symptoms: Policy sync fails with error status "Created failed on target" on target devices.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a connectivity or rewrite profile from the default one. 2. Create another child profile using the one created above as parent. 3. Create a virtual server, with the child connectivity and/or rewrite profile, and an access policy. 4. Initiate a policy sync for the access profile.
bugs.impact: Policy sync function fails.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, create connectivity or rewrite profile, only use the default profile as parent; or, have the non-default parent profile sync first to target devices.

bugs.title: iControl REST for ASM Character Sets returns invalid characters (greater than 127 (0x7f) ) for Multi-Byte Encodings
bugs.symptoms: The REST endpoint for Character Sets returns items that are invalid to send back to the endpoint as a PATCH. This can cause an API client to get unexpected errors
bugs.conditions: A Security Policy exists with a Single-Byte Encoding configured, and REST API is being used.
bugs.impact: Objects returned by the endpoint will fail validation when sent back to the endpoint. Additionally this will not match output from the same endpoint (if enabled) on 11.5.2-HF1+, and could confuse API clients that attempt to compare Security Policies.

bugs.title: CSS patcher crashes when a quoted value consists of spaces only
bugs.symptoms: CSS content that contains some spaces between quotes leads to rewrite crash. Example: ... background: url(' ') // some spaces between quotes ...
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this problem include any case when CSS content contains a quoted value which consists of spaces only.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue causes a rewrite crash which leads to a possible web application malfunction.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, create a particular iRule that removes mentioned spaces between quotes.

bugs.title: localdbmgr process in constant restart/core loop
bugs.symptoms: The localdbmgr process keeps crashing repeatedly.
bugs.conditions: The issue is caused by corruption in the contents stored in the memcache. Although the conditions under which the memory corruption occurs are not reproducible, this is a rarely occurring issue.
bugs.impact: The localdbmgr process crashes repeatedly.
bugs.fix: The localdbmgr process has been updated in order to gracefully handle corruption in the memcache contents.

bugs.title: Port exhaustion errors on VIPRION 4800 when using CGNAT
bugs.symptoms: You may see the following on a VIPRION 4800 platform configured to use LSN deterministic NAT: crit tmm3[12240]: 01010201:2: Inet port exhaustion on ...
bugs.conditions: VIPRION 4800 platform with multiple blades with LSN deterministic NAT
bugs.impact: DNAT port exhaustion alert
bugs.workaround: Change LSN Pool members for LSN deterministic NAT pools, which will trigger a deterministic NAT data rebuild.
bugs.fix: TMM translations after blade failure or startup can be properly reverse-mapped by dnatutil, which fixes the port exhaustion alerts.

bugs.title: Unable to create GTM Listener with non-default protocol profile.
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to create a GTM Listener with anything besides a default protocol profile causes a duplicate profile error.
bugs.conditions: Create a GTM Listener with a protocol profile other than udp_gtm_dns or tcp.
bugs.impact: GTM listener creation does not complete.
bugs.workaround: Create a GTM Listener using a default protocol profile, and then modify the protocol profile settings.
bugs.fix: You can now create GTM Listener with non-default protocol profile.

bugs.title: Rare outages possible when using config sync and node-based load balancing
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances it is possible for tmm to experience an outage when processing traffic and using config sync. This is rare and appears to be related to a combination of config sync and processing traffic shortly after the tmm is brought online.
bugs.conditions: Using config sync and node-based load balancing. This has only been observed early in traffic processing during a config sync; it does not appear to be related to how long the tmm has been online (e.g., online and not processing traffic or online in standby does not seem to make any difference; however, issuing a config sync and failing over at the same time might cause this to occur.)
bugs.impact: Interruption in service or HA failover.
bugs.fix: Fixed a error that rarely occurred using config sync and node-based load balancing early in traffic processing.

bugs.title: The hostagentd daemon should not be running in non-vcmp mode.
bugs.symptoms: The hostagentd daemon is running when vCMP is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on all platforms that support vCMP.
bugs.impact: In non-vCMP mode, hostagentd is an unnecessary system process. It may use a small amount of memory and cpu but does not otherwise impact system performance or traffic passing.
bugs.workaround: Hostagentd may be disabled by issuing 'bigstart disable hostagentd' on all blades of a chassis or on an appliance system.
bugs.fix: The hostagentd daemon is no longer started when the BIG-IP system is not provisioned for vCMP.

bugs.title: Segfault originating from flow_lookup_nexthop.
bugs.symptoms: Segfault originating from flow_lookup_nexthop when neighbor_resolve is not able to determine the next hop.
bugs.conditions: Memory pressure or error condition.
bugs.impact: tmm core and tmms restart.
bugs.fix: Segfault originating from flow_lookup_nexthop problem has been corrected.

bugs.title: Safari 8 continues using proxy for network access resource in some cases when it shouldn't
bugs.symptoms: If a client machine uses proxy and Network Access does not specify any proxy, then Safari should not use proxy for some Network Access resource after the Network Access tunnel is created. However, Safari does so. This problem occurs with Safari 8. Other versions of Safari and other browsers work as expected in our testing. Apple has been notified: rdar://problem/18651124
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs when all of these conditions exist: 1. OS = Mac OS X Yosemite. 2. Configuration = Client machine has local proxy configured and Network Access on BIG-IP system access policy does not specify any proxy. 3. Action = Accessing Network Access resource after tunnel is created.
bugs.impact: As a result, some Network Access resource might be unavailable.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: tmsh displays wrong cert expiration date on 'show gtm iquery' (later than Jan 18 2038).
bugs.symptoms: When displaying iQuery stats in tmsh, the expiration date of the certificate appears to be in the past.
bugs.conditions: Certificate expiration date is beyond Jan 18, 2038 (Max epoch represented by signed 32 bit int).
bugs.impact: The certificate remains valid. This is a cosmetic issue only.

bugs.title: mcpd log messages: Failed to unpublish LOIPC object
bugs.symptoms: The system posts the following error: err mcpd[7143]: 010716d6:3: Failed to unpublish LOIPC object for (loipc_name.1417443578.297505208). Call to (shm_unlink) failed with errno (2) errstr (No such file or directory).
bugs.conditions: This is an intermittent issue that occurs on standby systems in High Availability (HA) configurations. In this case, the system is attempting to remove a file/directory that does not exist. Either the file has already been removed or it was not created.
bugs.impact: This is a benign error that can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: The system now suppresses logging when attempting to delete non-existent file.

bugs.title: TMM may core in low memory situations during SSL egress handling
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core in low memory situations during SSL egress handling.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Low memory. -- SSL connections
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores in low-memory situations during SSL egress handling.

bugs.title: SAML IdP and SP configured in same access profile not supported
bugs.symptoms: SLO might not work properly under certain conditions. When a user attempts to start SLO, the connection gets reset. The system logs messages such as the following: RST sent from x.x.x.x:433 to x.x.x.x:xxxx, [0xxxxxx:xxx] Internal error ((APM::SSO) Error in reading sp info from session db failed)
bugs.conditions: All conditions must be met: 1. Both BIG-IP as SP and BIG-IP as IdP are configured on the same access profile. 2. SLO is configured for both BIG-IP as IdP and BIG-IP as SP. 3. SLO is executed in multiple TCP sessions between the user's browser and the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: SLO is not properly executed; users's session might not be terminated.
bugs.fix: A problem with SAML single-logout has been fixed.

bugs.title: LDAP extended error info only available at debug log level which could affect Branch rules
bugs.symptoms: LDAP session variable contains only simple error message at INFO log level and requires DEBUG log level to display the full error message. This variable is displayed in the logon page after logon failure.
bugs.conditions: LDAP Auth/Query is configured and there is need for extended error details at NON debug log level.
bugs.impact: Branch rules in visual policy editor based on extended error message will not work correctly in 11.6.
bugs.fix: A new session variable is introduced: session.ldap.last.errmsgext which contains extended error information at any log level. The existing session.ldap.last.errmsg variable contains only simple error message (decoded error code).
bugs.behavior: A new session variable is introduced, session.ldap.last.errmsgext, which contains extended error information at any log level. The existing session.ldap.last.errmsg variable now contains only a simple error message (decoded error code). Branch rules in visual policy editor based on extended error message will not work correctly.

bugs.title: Resolved build issues to install updated library and include files.
Connecting to FP with APM edge client is causing corporate network to be inaccessible
bugs.symptoms: Connecting to FirePass with a BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac that was downloaded from APM might not provide complete network access.
bugs.conditions: APM Edge Client, Firepass server, network access connection.
bugs.impact: Incomplete network access.
bugs.fix: All configured networks are now reachable when connecting to FirePass using a BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac downloaded from APM.

bugs.title: BWC related tmm core
bugs.symptoms: tmm coredumps while BWC is processing packets.
bugs.conditions: BWC is being enabled on a virtual server that does not have any BWC iRules enabled. Reasons for this are being investigated.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Avoid a divide by zero while computing average packet size.

bugs.title: Logon page is not displayed correctly when 'force password change' is on for local users.
bugs.symptoms: Logon page is not displayed correctly when 'force password change' is on for local users.
bugs.conditions: When more than one logon page is configured in the Access policy, and the administrator sets 'Force Password Change' in the local user account database.
bugs.impact: Although it is correct behavior to require an initial password change and to require a logon after changing the password, the expected first page is a one-time password-change request, instead of the same change-password change page displayed twice.
bugs.workaround: The current workaround is to add 'Variable Assign' agent in the LocalDB Auth Successful branch with a custom variable, for example: session.logon.page.challenge = expr { 0 }.
bugs.fix: The system now shows the correct logon page after the successful password change.

bugs.title: An error occurs on Active Rules page after attempting to reorder Rules in a Policy
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs on Active Rules page after attempting to reorder Rules in a Policy: "An error has occurred while trying to process your request."
bugs.conditions: Attempting to reorder rules if they span more than one page
bugs.impact: You cannot reorder the rules, and an error message is displayed, "An error has occurred while trying to process your request."
bugs.fix: Reordering of rules is now working.

bugs.title: Flash AS3 with ExternalInterface call may not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: Flash web applications might not work as expected with ActionScript 3 (AS3) using statements such as the following: flash.external.ExternalInterface("eval", "document.location.href")
bugs.conditions: Using statements such as the following in AS3 scripts: flash.external.ExternalInterface("eval", "document.location.href")
bugs.impact: Possible web application malfunction; rewrites not occurring as expected.

bugs.title: Add new log messages for AFM rule blob load/activation in datapath.
bugs.symptoms: Prior to fix, as AFM rule blob is compiled/serialized by pktclass-daemon and TMM is notified to activate it in datapath, there is no visibility to identify if the activation failed or succeeded.
bugs.conditions: AFM rule serialization message is processed by TMM
bugs.impact: End user lacks any visibility if the AFM rule serialized blob is successfully being used in the data path.
bugs.fix: With the fix, now we log message (in /var/log/ltm) as AFM rule serialized blob is activated in data path.

bugs.title: ECDH negotiation failures logged as critical errors.
bugs.symptoms: When a failure occurs in an SSL negotiation involving Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) key agreement, a critical error may be logged. However, an SSL negotiation failure is not a critical issue.
bugs.conditions: An SSL negotiation failure involving ECDH key agreement.
bugs.impact: Spurious critical error logs.
bugs.workaround: Treat SSL ECDH negotiation failures as non-critical errors.
bugs.fix: These ECDH failures are now logged as non-critical errors.

bugs.title: Use different application ID after user application is deleted
bugs.symptoms: When user creates a custom application and then deletes it, they cannot create another application with the previously used ID even though the old application no longer exists
bugs.conditions: Delete user application, create a new one with the same ID
bugs.impact: Error in tmm log. Cannot create the application.
bugs.workaround: Use different ID when creating new applications.

bugs.title: iApps fail when using FQDN nodes in pools
bugs.symptoms: Use of FQDN nodes causes errors in almost all f5-supported iapps.
bugs.conditions: 1. create an FQDN node named "foo" that refers to the fqdn "www.foo.com" 2. create an iapp instance using the attached ephemeral_example template 3. enter "foo" when prompted by the iapp for a node name 4. click "finished" and observe the pool in the component view 5. click "reconfigure" 6. click "finished".
bugs.impact: iApp will throw an error: "0107189b:3: Cannot delete ephemeral object: /Common/foo-173.194.33.144."
bugs.fix: The iApp mark-and-sweep framework should be modified to ignore ephemeral pool members when modifying iApp-managed pools.

bugs.title: IPsec tunnel interface causes TMM core at times
bugs.symptoms: If users choose to modify the tunnel interface attributes, such as MTU value, TMM cores. This can occur regardless if traffic has flowed through the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: When IPsec tunnel interface has its configuration modified.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid modifying IPsec tunnel interface. Configure IPsec tunnel interface in one shot, using either create or delete.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores if users choose to modify the tunnel interface attributes, such as MTU value.

bugs.title: Ephemeral node health status may report as 'unknown' rather than the expected 'offline'
bugs.symptoms: Ephemeral node health status may report as 'unknown' rather than the expected 'offline'.
bugs.conditions: Change the monitor rule on the node several times.
bugs.impact: Node may be in unknown status when it should be offline.
bugs.workaround: Reset bigd.
bugs.fix: Ephemeral node health status now reports 'offline' rather than 'unknown' in cases in which the monitor is offline.

bugs.title: DB monitor functionality might cause memory issues
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts continuously.
bugs.conditions: DB monitors configured
bugs.impact: System stops responding. System posts message: notice panic: FATAL: mmap of: /dev/mprov/tmm/tmm.4 length 1480589312 offset 4441767936 failed 12 (Cannot allocate memory).
bugs.workaround: Either kill the DB monitor java process or issue a bigstart restart.
bugs.fix: DB monitor functionality might cause memory issues.

bugs.title: Configuration fails with Syntax Error after upgrading from pre-11.5.0 releases
bugs.symptoms: Configuration fails with Syntax Error after upgrading to 11.5.0 from pre-11.5.0 releases.
bugs.conditions: When upgrading from a pre-11.5.0 release to version 11.5.0, the key/cert have an extra period in the name (for example mykey..key and mycert..crt). Beginning with version 11.5.0, multiple key/cert pairs are associated with one clientssl, so each key/cert pair has a name. During upgrade, the system provides a name for each key/cert, which can cause problems if the existing key/cert name contains a period character.
bugs.impact: Configuration load fails, and the system posts the alert: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 12) one or more configuration identifiers must be provided.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the bigip.conf to add a title for the cert-key-chain, and then run the command: tmsh load sys config.
bugs.fix: Before v11.5.0, Clientssl profile only supports one key/cert pair, no name associated with the key/cert pair. In v11.5.0, multiple key/cert pairs are associated with one clientssl, so each key/cert pair has a name.

bugs.title: iRule can be deleted even though it exists in a rule-list
bugs.symptoms: The rule-list will reference a non existent iRule.
bugs.conditions: Have a rule-list that contains an iRule, and then delete that iRule.
bugs.impact: iRule will no longer have an effect, even though it still appears to be contained in the rule-list.
bugs.workaround: Do not delete an iRule if it is referenced by a rule-list.
bugs.fix: Introduced validation to ensure that a referenced iRule cannot be deleted.

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client cannot be downloaded sometimes from management UI
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac cannot be downloaded from the management GUI.
bugs.conditions: Mac Edge Client, BIG-IP management UI.
bugs.impact: Mac Edge Client cannot be downloaded.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac can now be downloaded from the connectivity profile screen of the APM GUI.

bugs.title: Some user defined ASM reports are not loading correctly after upgrade from 11.4 upwards
bugs.symptoms: Some fields of user defined filters from older versions cannot be loaded in the new version, after an upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Custom user filter is defined. Most common when Source Client IP field is set.
bugs.impact: Filters cannot be applied correctly due to values not being recognized.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrade, the filters should be manually saved, and later on re-created on the new version.
bugs.fix: A better value upgrade has been implemented, and a warning message is displayed to the user about the situation.

bugs.title: UI Breadcrumb text does not always match the menu or tab selected
bugs.symptoms: When an Admin visits the UI and clicks on an item within the left-hand menu the corresponding tab will also be selected at the top of the right content pane, and above that there will be corresponding breadcrumb text. In some cases the breadcrumb text does not change as expected.
bugs.conditions: This usually occurs when the admin visits screens using different GUI implementations. In this case if the admin clicked into "Local Traffic >> Profiles : Services : HTTP" from the menu on the left hand side, and then selected Rewrite from within the Services tab, the breadcrumb text would still read "Local Traffic >> Profiles : Services : HTTP" rather than the expected "Local Traffic >> Profiles : Services : Rewrite".
bugs.impact: The breadcrumb text does not change as expected.
bugs.fix: The breadcrumb text now changes as expected, depending upon the menu or tab item the admin selects.

bugs.title: SSL verification error occurs when using server side certificate.
bugs.symptoms: SSL is stuck at signature check for server side certificates and hence can't complete the SSL handshake.
bugs.conditions: The issue can be seen when it meets the following conditions: 1. The backend server is Microsoft IIS or Netty. 2. serverSSL profile requires server side certificate authentication.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake fails. The handshake hangs until the timeout.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can configure the back-end Netty based SSL servers to use a Certificate Authority (CA) signed certificate. Otherwise, do not use use 'peer-cert-mode require'.
bugs.fix: SSL verification error no longer occurs when using server side certificate.

bugs.title: Virtual status becomes yellow and gets connection limit alert when all pool members forced down
bugs.symptoms: Invalid display of virtual status.
bugs.conditions: When all pool members forced down and the pool member's connection limit has been reached.
bugs.impact: Virtual monitor status becomes yellow and receives the following connection limit alert: The pool member's connection limit has been reached.
bugs.fix: Virtual status now stays red if all the pool members are down.

bugs.title: iApps/tmsh cannot reconfigure pools that have monitors associated with them.
bugs.symptoms: iApps are unable to reconfigure pools that have monitors associated with them.
bugs.conditions: Using tmsh or iApps in the GUI to re-configure the pool monitor (for example, changing the monitor from 'http' to 'none').
bugs.impact: Monitor change does not occur. GUI or tmsh might post an error similar to the following: Monitor rule not found.
bugs.fix: Users can now remove a monitor from a pool / set it to 'none' through tmsh or a GUI iApp transaction.

bugs.title: Connection limit on nodes causes TMM infinite loop and heartbeat failure with heavy traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM might experience an infinite loop when selecting an available node for load balancing under heavy traffic conditions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the connection limit is specified for nodes, and there is heavy traffic.
bugs.impact: This causes a 10-second TMM heartbeat failure and a SIGABRT in TMM. The device goes offline and traffic processing is disrupted.
bugs.fix: Connection limit on nodes now works correctly, and no longer causes tmm to loop indefinitely with heavy traffic.

bugs.title: Tunnel Server crash if probed on loopback listener.
bugs.symptoms: VPN client might disconnect and reconnect.
bugs.conditions: Unexpected request is sent on tunnel server loopback listener.
bugs.impact: Tunnel server crashes resulting in VPN disconnection and reconnection.
bugs.fix: Additional check implemented in tunnel server before accepting incoming connection.

bugs.title: TMM core with CCA-I policy received with uninstall
bugs.symptoms: If a CCA-I is received with Charging-Rule-Remove AVP for the session then TMM will core.
bugs.conditions: CCA-I message received with charging-rule-remove AVP
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed the tmm crash when CCA-I with policy uninstall is received.

bugs.title: APM RDP connection gets dropped on AFM firewall policy change
bugs.symptoms: An active RDP connection over APM VPN tunnel gets dropped when administrator makes a change to the AFM firewall policy.
bugs.conditions: APM tunnel and its application connections are subject to AFM firewall policy.
bugs.impact: RDP session disconnects and automatically reconnects.
bugs.workaround: Add an Allow rule to the firewall policy for destination TCP port 3389.
bugs.fix: RDP connections no longer get dropped during AFM firewall policy changes.

bugs.title: Resets when session awareness enabled
bugs.symptoms: A connection reset may occur when a transaction takes a long time (more than 10 seconds together from the request start till the response end).
bugs.conditions: The session tracking feature is turned on and long transaction occurs.
bugs.impact: A connection reset.
bugs.workaround: Turn off session tracking.
bugs.fix: Connection resets no longer occur when session awareness is enabled and the server response takes a long time.

bugs.title: Deleting a rewrite profile fails to delete the dependent objects.
bugs.symptoms: Deleting a rewrite profile fails to delete the dependent objects.
bugs.conditions: Deleting a rewrite profile.
bugs.impact: ConfigSync fails with a message similar to the following: err mcpd[6817]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Values (/Common/rewrite_profile) specified for rewrite rules URI (/Common/rewrite_profile rewrite_uri_rule): foreign key index (rewrite_rules_uri_fk) do not point at an item that exists in the database.
bugs.workaround: On an affected system (for example, the system sourcing a ConfigSync), save and then re-load the configuration. This causes mcpd to remove the vestigial object. To do so, run the following commands, in sequence: -- tmsh save sys config partitions all. -- tmsh load sys config partitions all. Ensuring that is enabled on device groups also mitigates this issue.

bugs.title: GUI throws an error in some situations when an ASM policy is assigned to virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to apply an ASM policy to a virtual server that is using LTM forwarding, the GUI no longer returns an error: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when navigating to Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers : Virtual Server List :: 'http_vip' :: Security :: Policies...
bugs.impact: The system posts an error: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.fix: When attempting to apply an ASM policy to a virtual server that is using LTM forwarding, the GUI no longer returns an error: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.

bugs.title: system_check shows stale chassis fan tray data after the chassis is removed
bugs.symptoms: After a chassis fan tray is removed, the system_check utility still shows the stale data from time before the removal.
bugs.conditions: Remove chassis fan tray
bugs.impact: There is a warning in the ltm log when the chassis fan tray is removed. So, the impact of the system_check inconsistency is small.

bugs.title: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records sometimes shows an incorrect number of entries on VIPRION chassis
bugs.symptoms: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records or tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records client-addr <client ip> sometimes shows an incorrect number of entries on VIPRION chassis.
bugs.conditions: When there are multiple slots on a VIPRION chassis, and the command is executed on a secondary from the primary.
bugs.impact: Results are not reported correctly in tmsh. Results display a fluctuating number of src ip persistence entries.
bugs.workaround: Specify the virtual server name in the tmsh command directly, instead of running the command for all virtual servers.

bugs.title: Creating new Active Rule to assign policy to a VIP forces user to create rule
bugs.symptoms: Creating new Active Rule to assign policy to a VIP forces you to create rule because the "Type" list does not appear. The Type List would allow you to select a policy instead of creating an unwanted rule to make the rule properties dialogue go away.
bugs.conditions: Create a new rule on Active Rules page
bugs.impact: User inconvenience.
bugs.workaround: Assign the Policy to the virtual server on the Virtual server page via the Security tab.

bugs.title: SOAP Methods Were Not Being Validated For WSDL Based XML Profiles
bugs.symptoms: After configuring an XML Content Profile from a WSDL file, the system was not validating the SOAP Methods.
bugs.conditions: WSDL Based XML Content Profiles with SOAP Methods are used on the system.
bugs.impact: SOAP Traffic was not properly validated.
bugs.fix: WSDL based XML Content Profiles are now enforced correctly.

bugs.title: Disabling/enabling Rule within Rule List causes disabling/enabling of other Rule with the same name
bugs.symptoms: Disabling/enabling Rule within Rule List causes disabling/enabling of a different but same-named Rule in a single Policy on the Active Rule Page in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Only happens it the Rule names are the same with a single policy.
bugs.impact: Potentially, the incorrect Rule is disabled.
bugs.workaround: Make sure Rules have different names.
bugs.fix: The system now enables/disables only the selected Rule, regardless of the existence of other, same-name Rules in the policy.

bugs.title: TMM crash when moving to standby
bugs.symptoms: During the active to standby to transition while passing traffic, tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when the following conditions are met: -- The transition from active to standby occurs. -- There exists an active SCTP association which has already been torn down on the clientside. -- The serverside is still attempting to establish an association to a nonresponsive pool member at the moment that the transition occurs.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes on the standby, then restarts. If other traffic groups are active on the newly-standby unit, they will be disrupted.

bugs.title: APM does not apply route domain configured in visual policy editor to Java RDP connections.
bugs.symptoms: APM does not apply route domain configured in visual policy editor to Java RDP connections.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered if your Java RDP connections are configured to use route domains.
bugs.impact: You will be unable to configure a route domain for the resource.
bugs.fix: You can now configure a route domain in the visual policy editor for Java RDP connections.

bugs.title: APM does not apply route domain configured in visual policy editor to Java AppTunnel connections.
bugs.symptoms: APM does not apply route domain configured in visual policy editor to Java AppTunnel connections.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered if your Java AppTunnel connections are using route domains.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure or use the route domain.
bugs.fix: In this release you can configure a route domain in the visual policy editor to Java AppTunnel connections.

bugs.title: APM does not apply route domain configured in visual policy editor to Citrix/VMware View connections when their backends are specified as hostname/IP address.
bugs.symptoms: APM does not apply the route domain that is configured in visual policy editor to Citrix or VMware View connections when the Citrix or the VMware View backend is specified in the resource using a hostname or an IP address.
bugs.conditions: Citrix or VMWare View resources configured, and they use route domains
bugs.impact: Traffic is not sent to the resource's route domain.
bugs.fix: APM applies the route domain that is configured in visual policy editor to Citrix or VMware View connections when the Citrix or the VMware View backend is specified in the resource using a hostname or an IP address. Note that if the Virtual Server and the resource are in different route domains and route domains have strict isolation mode, you may see an error in the Ltm log: err tmm[18245]: 01230140:3: RST sent from 172.29.74.80:443 to 172.29.68.233:54767, [0x1f2920c:1989] Route domain not reachable (strict mode) To correct this, ensure you set the virtual server route domain to be the parent of the Resource route domain.

bugs.title: APM does not support using session variables for the destination address in Citrix and VMware View remote desktop resources.
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support using session variables for the destination address in Citrix and VMware View remote desktop resources.
bugs.conditions: N/A, this release note describes an enhancement.
bugs.fix: APM supports using session variables for the destination address in Citrix and VMware View remote desktop resources by configuring %{session.logon.last.domain} in the remote-desktop resource.

bugs.title: Firewall rule compilation will fail in certain scenario when there are multiple scheduled AFM rules and one of the non scheduled AFM rule is modified.
bugs.symptoms: Firewall rule compilation will fail and following message will appear in /var/log/ltm: Serialization failed: No Blobs available. pktclass-daemon will transit in the failed state and any further firewall rule modifications will be rejected till the corrective action is taken.
bugs.conditions: For this issue to manifest, following conditions may suffice: i) Presence of multiple scheduled firewall rules (expiring at different intervals). ii) Presence of non scheduled firewall rules. iii) Modify any non scheduled firewall rules in between the time interval of expiry to any 2 scheduled rules.
bugs.impact: Firewall rule compilation will fail and pktclass-daemon will go into failed state causing any further firewall rule update to be ignored till user-initiated corrective action is taken.
bugs.fix: The aforementioned incorrect behavior has been fixed.

bugs.title: AVR and APM: TMM crashes (additional fixes for ID 480350)
bugs.symptoms: tmm can crash with AVR configured.
bugs.conditions: AVR and APM are used together.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: We fixed an issue that intermittently caused TMM to crash when APM and AVR are provisioned together. This fix is additional to the one provided in ID 480350.

bugs.title: Secondary Blades Request a Sync
bugs.symptoms: Secondary blades requesting ASM sync "ASM is now entering sync recovery state. Requesting complete configuration from" noise in the logs, and needless sync work done. This issue does not affect enforcement or the actual sync state of the devices, it is just requesting extra synchronizations when they may not be needed.
bugs.conditions: Secondary blade restarts in unsynchronized mode.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary sync events are created
bugs.workaround: Restarting the asm_config_server process on the secondary blade should alleviate the issue, but it may recur.
bugs.fix: To optimize the system, DSC synchronization is no longer requested from secondary blades. This issue did not affect enforcement or the actual synchronization state of the devices.

bugs.title: HTTP header that is larger than 64K can be analyzed incorrectly, leading to TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Fixed a problem that occurred when extracting request headers. This problem could sometimes cause TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: Turn on "page load time" in analytic profile. AVR need to get request with HTTP header that bigger than 64K.

bugs.title: Portal Access incorectly rewrites expressions with JavaScript typeof operator
bugs.symptoms: The Portal Access module transforms intranet web application code to make it accessible via an APM virtual server. One of these transformations might incorrectly rewrite expressions with 'typeof' operator, though you might not see any immediate visible effect.
bugs.conditions: The issue affects expressions like 'typeof something' where 'something' is expected to be transformed by Portal Access. For example, with the original code similar to 'var l = window.location; if (typeof l.href) {...}' unrewritten typeof argument causes condition to fail.
bugs.impact: When Portal Access accesses the intranet application containing such code, expressions with typeof operator may have wrong value, leading application to incorrect code paths. As a result, the application might fail with a very obscure and difficult to diagnose errors.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule for each specific case. There is no global workaround.

bugs.title: Supports ID496560 for better handling of ingress events.
iRule object in non-Common partition referenced from another partition breaks upgrade/config load
bugs.symptoms: iRule object in non-Common partition referenced from another partition results in upgrade/configuration load failure in 11.x/12.x.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when upgrading/loading a configuration containing an iRule in one non-Common partition that references an object in another non-Common partition. A configuration of this type can be saved only using pre-11.x versions of the software.
bugs.impact: The config upgrade fails, and the UCS/configuration files cannot be loaded. The system posts an error message similar to the following: 'myucs.ucs' failed with the following error message: 'Rule [/UNCOMMONPARTITION/RULEABC] error: Unable to find rule_object (...) referenced at line xyz: [element]'.

bugs.title: Configuration loads may fail because the 'default-device' on a traffic-group object does not contain a valid value.
bugs.symptoms: After renaming a CM device object, or performing an upgrade from a version prior to 11.4.0, configuration loads may fail because the 'default-device' on a traffic-group object does not contain a valid value.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when one of the following conditions is met: -- You load the BIG-IP configuration. -- You upgrade the BIG-IP system software. -- You perform a configuration synchronization (ConfigSync) operation for the device group. The 'default-device' attribute has been deprecated beginning in 11.4.0 in favor of new functionality. Prior to 11.4.0, default-device was used to specify the device-group member that failback tries to make active. From 11.4.0 and later, when auto-failback is enabled, the system uses the first member of the 'Failover Order' ('ha-order' in tmsh). In 11.4.0 and later, this field is not used, but will fail validation if it contains a value that does not reference the name of an existing device-group member, or the value 'none'.
bugs.impact: Although the configuration can be saved, it fails when being loaded (for example, in response to a ConfigSync operation, during software upgrade, or when running the command: 'tmsh load sys config').
bugs.workaround: Modify any traffic-group default-device attributes that refer to the now-deprecated, default-device name. Note: The system does not use this value, regardless of how you set it. To work around this issue, you can modify the traffic-group default-device attribute to refer to default-device none. To do so, perform the following procedure: 1. Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: tmsh 2. To list the configured default device for a traffic group, use the following command syntax: list /cm traffic-group <traffic group name> For example, to list the configured default device for traffic-group-1, type the following command: list /cm traffic-group traffic-group-1 3. Use none as the default device for your traffic group using the following command syntax: modify cm traffic-group <traffic group name> default-device <default device name>. For example, to modify your default device to none for traffic-group-1, type the following command: modify cm traffic-group traffic-group-1 default-device none 4. Save the configuration changes by typing the following command: save /sys config
bugs.fix: Renaming a device also renames the associated traffic-group's default device, so configuration load now completes successfully.

bugs.title: Monitor Parameters saved to config in a certain order may not construct parameters correctly
bugs.symptoms: When configuring both a monitor and a child monitor, if the two monitors are saved in reverse order, the default monitor parameters will not be created. For example: ltm monitor tcp /Common/child { defaults-from /Common/parent destination *.990 interval 5 ip-dscp 0 time-until-up 0 timeout 16 } ltm monitor tcp /Common/parent { defaults-from /Common/tcp destination *:* interval 5 ip-dscp 0 time-until-up 0 timeout 16 } Some of the default parameters for the above configuration will not be created upon loading config.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are at least two monitors, and the child custom monitor appears before the parent monitor. Must have a parent that derives from a root monitor, and a child that derives from the parent monitor.
bugs.impact: Possible undefined behavior in bigd, and failing iControl calls. On performing a 'tmsh load sys config verify' the system posts an error message similar to the following: 01070740:3: Performance monitor /Common/http-a may not have the manual resume feature. Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: A possible workaround involves switching the order of the monitors in the config file. This can either be accomplished manually, or by naming things in alphabetical order, such that the parent precedes the child: ltm monitor tcp /Common/aaa_parent { defaults-from /Common/tcp destination *:* interval 5 ip-dscp 0 time-until-up 0 timeout 16 } ltm monitor tcp /Common/bbb_child { defaults-from /Common/aaa_parent destination *.990 interval 5 ip-dscp 0 time-until-up 0 timeout 16 }
bugs.fix: The system now handles a configuration in which a child custom monitor precedes the parent's, so that monitor parameters are constructed properly.

bugs.title: [GTM] [big3d] Unable to receive mark LTM virtual server up if there is another VS with same ltm_name for the bigip monitor
bugs.symptoms: [GTM] [big3d] Unable to mark LTM virtual server up if there is another virtual server with same ltm_name for the bigip monitor.
bugs.conditions: LTM (running BIG-IP software older than v11.2.0) with a virtual server: /Common/http_vip with destination /Common/192.168.10.34:80. GTM (running BIG-IP software newer than v11.5.0) with this LTM as a BIG-IP Server. Two virtual servers on LTM: One with the original LTM virtual server address, and the other with the translated address: 1. name ltm_http_vip :: destination 192.168.10.34:80 :: monitor /Common/bigip. 2. name ltm_http_trans_vip :: destination 10.10.10.34:80 :: translation-address 192.168.10.34:80 :: monitor /Common/bigip.
bugs.impact: Both virtual servers are marked up for a brief interval. After a few minutes, one of them is marked down.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use a monitor other than bigip. -- Replace /shared/bin/big3d on the LTM system with a copy of a version v11.2.1 or later big3d.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP health monitor no longer incorrectly marks down virtual servers with a duplicate ltm-name when there are BIG-IP GTM systems with differing software versions monitoring BIG-IP LTM virtual servers using the bigip monitor.

bugs.title: Big-IP Edge client for Windows fails to connect to Firepass server if tunnel is established through a proxy
bugs.symptoms: In a reconnect scenario, Big-IP Edge Client cannot connect to a FirePass server if the tunnel was established through a proxy server.
bugs.conditions: Proxy is used to create VPN tunnel. The server is FirePass.
bugs.impact: The client fails to restore the VPN connection to the FirePass server.
bugs.workaround: Restart client.
bugs.fix: Added backward compatibility changes to BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows to work properly with FirePass.

bugs.title: TMM may restart when accessing SAML resource under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: When a user performs SAML Identity Provider (IdP)-initiated web single sign-on (Web SSO) using Artifact binding and the Artifact Resolution Service is not configured on IdP, TMM may restart.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under all of the following conditions: 1. The BIG-IP system is configured as a SAML IdP. 2. The IdP service does not have Artifact Resolution Service configured. 3. The corresponding Service Provider (SP) connector object, which is bound to the IdP, has Artifact binding configured. 4. The SAML Resource from this IdP is published on a webtop.
bugs.impact: As a result, TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, configure an Artifact Resolution Service and assign it to the IdP object.
bugs.fix: An issue where TMM would restart under certain conditions is now fixed.

bugs.title: Flows may not be mirrored successfully when static routes and gateways are defined.
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances, some L4 flows may not be successfully remirrored when a standby BIG-IP comes online. This involves a race condition when there are multiple routes and/or gateways defined; if the new standby device does not yet have the lasthop information when it gets the mirrored flow.
bugs.conditions: Using mirroring with layer 4 virtuals, with gateways and/or static routes defined.
bugs.impact: Not all flows will have been successfully remirrored to the standby device.
bugs.workaround: Usually "bigstart restart tmm" will recover most or all of the L4 flows. This does not work perfectly all of the time, but is far less likely to encounter the error condition than a "bigstart restart" or "shutdown -r".
bugs.fix: The standby device ignores the route to the client when accepting mirrored connections. If failover occurs without a route back to the client, the connection will still fail on failover.

bugs.title: Crash when receiving RADIUS message to update PEM static subscriber.
bugs.symptoms: Crash when receiving RADIUS message to update PEM static subscriber.
bugs.conditions: 1) A large number of PEM static subscribers in the system, for example, 100K. 2) Sends RADIUS messages for these 100K subscribers to update info.
bugs.impact: System crash.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP system no longer crashes when updating the static subscribers with RADIUS messages.

bugs.title: Update offenders more aggressively. Increase batch size for Dwbld processing.
bugs.symptoms: Offenders are not blacklisted fast enough.
bugs.conditions: DoS configured with auto-blacklisting
bugs.impact: When DoS doesn't track offenders aggressively, it doesn't report them. Once reported, Dwbld processes the offenders in smaller batches. This impacts how soon an offender is blacklisted.
bugs.fix: DoS code reports offenders more aggressively. Dwbld processes offenders with bigger batches.

bugs.title: Policy field is not marked as containing errors when creating a Rule without a Policy
bugs.symptoms: Policy field is not marked as containing errors when creating a Rule without a Policy. The system posts the following error message without explicitly calling out the policy field omission: 01070712:3: Invalid primary key on fw_policy_rule object - path is empty.
bugs.conditions: Create a rule without a policy.
bugs.impact: Posted error message does not indicate the error. Unclear feedback from UI validation.
bugs.workaround: Always fill out policy field when creating rules.

bugs.title: PEM configured with BWC doing PEM policy changes could trigger leak
bugs.symptoms: When PEM is configured to use bwc policy and cause re-evaluations due to pem policy change in configuration and/or PCRX could cause leak in bwc memory for active flows.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: PEM is configured to use BWC. -- System is processing active flows. -- PEM is applying a policy change event for live flows.
bugs.impact: PEM configured with BWC doing PEM policy changes might trigger leak. Eventual low memory conditions, possibly followed by TMM core and traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, complete the following steps: -- Restart tmm. -- Upgrade the image. -- Avoid PEM policy change events for live traffic flows. -- Attach BWC to the PEM policy after PEM policy change events.
bugs.fix: The case in which the PEM policy is modified while the system is processing live traffic, PEM now initiates policy re-evaluation and BWC is attached correctly to the policy, so no memory leak occurs.

bugs.title: Modifying an existing ipsec policy configuration object might cause tmm to crash
bugs.symptoms: Modifying an existing ipsec policy configuration object might cause tmm to crash
bugs.conditions: Modifying an existing ipsec policy configuration object that's not associated with any traffic selector that's assigned to an ikev2 ike peer configuration object.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Delete and re-create the ipsec policy mcp object
bugs.fix: tmm will not crash when user modify an existing ipsec policy configuration object

bugs.title: APM Migrates to Google reCAPTCHA API Version 2.0
bugs.symptoms: Google introduced reCAPTCHA API v2 in December 2014. The v2 API will not work with API key pair generated for v1 API. With APM migrating to reCAPTCHA v2, the key pair that works with previous releases of the APM will stop functioning after upgrade. Google recommends sites that are using v1 API to register new keys and upgrade to v2. (See https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/faq)
bugs.conditions: When key pair generated for v1 API is used in the reCAPTCHA configuration.
bugs.impact: Users will not be able to log in.
bugs.behavior: Before upgrade, admin is required to register a new key pair with Google. After upgrade, the "secret" and "site key" fields on the reCAPTCHA admin UI are populated with the old keys. Replace the old keys with the new keys obtained from Google. Furthermore, the "Verification URL", "Challenge URL", and "Noscript URL" fields are populated with the URLs for Google reCAPTCHA v2 service, not those that were specified before the upgrade. If a virtual server has been configured for v1 verification using HTTPS, the virtual server needs to add client side SSL profile and the "Verification URL" field should point to the virtual server. Moreover, the "CAPTCHA Theme" is obsolete and is replaced by v2 CAPTCHA render configuration parameters with the following default values: Data Theme = Light Data Type = Image Data Size = Normal

bugs.title: Log filled with 'hash grow: malloc failed' log messages.
bugs.symptoms: Excessive 'hash grow: malloc failed' messages in the ltm log: err tmm10[31888]: hash grow: malloc failed. The message indicates that the cache has reached a point where it needs to be resized because memory allocation failed.
bugs.conditions: The messages are visible when viewing the ltm log during low memory conditions, perhaps due to memory leaks or high memory usage.
bugs.impact: Log filled with 'hash grow: malloc failed' log messages. Although the failure of the allocation can occur during normal operation, the number of messages is excessive, as it does not provide any useful information after the first failure.
bugs.workaround: To filter out hash grow: malloc failed errors from the log, set dnscacheresolver.loglevel to critical or emerg. For example, to set log level to critical, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db dnscacheresolver.loglevel value critical. This records only critical errors to the log.

bugs.title: Tmm crash (SIGABRT) when any Tcl method executed in an iRule's FLOW_INIT event returns error.
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crash (SIGABRT) when any Tcl method executed in an iRule's FLOW_INIT event returns error.
bugs.conditions: A Tcl method executed in an iRule's FLOW_INIT event returns an error.
bugs.impact: Tmm crash (SIGABRT). Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Tmm may restart when SAML SLO is triggered
bugs.symptoms: Tmm restarts when SLO is executed.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as SAML SP or IdP, single logout is configured on appropriate objects.
bugs.impact: tmm may restart
bugs.workaround: Disable SAML SLO
bugs.fix: TMM will no longer restart when SAML SLO is triggered.

bugs.title: Clear schedue name when setting firewall rule state from Scheduled to Enabled/Disabled.
bugs.symptoms: Schedule name was not getting cleared when firewall rule state was changed from Scheduled to Enabled/Disabled.
bugs.conditions: Happens when firewall rule state was changed from Scheduled to Enabled/Disabled.
bugs.impact: AFM Policy Editor

bugs.title: ISO images 2 GiB or larger will not sync to secondary blades on a chassis
Global whitelist count exhausted prematurely
bugs.symptoms: You receive an error message with this signature: error 0107181d:3: Cannot create white list entry, maximum limit 8 entries reached.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when configuring entries on both BIG-IP's in a sync group and syncing them. The whitelist count may be less than 8 but the error is still generated.
bugs.impact: You may receive an error message while creating a whitelist telling them they've exceeded the global whitelist count limit.
bugs.fix: An internal inconsistency with the system that oversees the whitelist count has been fixed.

bugs.title: Thales install fails if the BIG-IP system is also configured as the RFS
bugs.symptoms: Thales install fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the BIG-IP system is also configured as the RFS.
bugs.impact: Cannot use Thales HSM with the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: In the following procedure, when running nethsm-thales-rfs-install.sh, the script returns the IP address used by the RFS server. Use that IP address when running the 'rfs-setup' command. When prompted with: Did you successfully run the above 'rfs-setup' command on the RFS server? (Yes/No), perform the following steps: 1. Open a new SSH connection to the BIG-IP system. 2. Run the following command: /opt/nfast/bin/rfs-setup --force -g --write-noauth x.x.x.x. 3. Return to nethsm-thales-install.sh SSH screen and answer 'Yes'. The script should now exit with a success message.
bugs.fix: Thales install script now runs successfully when the BIG-IP system is also configured as the RFS.

bugs.title: Unable to delete reconfigured HTTP iApp when auto-sync is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When deleting an HTTP iApp, the system posts errors similar to this in the LTM log, along with similar sync errors in the GUI: -- err mcpd[6629]: 01070265:3: The HTTP Profile (/Common/http-test-farm1.app/http-test-farm1_http) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a sflow http data source (16). -- err mcpd[6629]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/HA_Group to commit id 895 6070871290648001573 /Common/cr-ltm-bb2.ns.uwaterloo.ca 0 failed with error 01070265:3: The HTTP Profile (/Common/http-test-farm1.app/http-test-farm1_http) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a sflow http data source (16).
bugs.conditions: Auto-sync must be enabled. HTTP iApp must have been reconfigured prior to deleting the iApp.
bugs.impact: Sync failure. Cannot delete the iApp manually after the error occurs.
