bugs.workaround: Do not use auto-sync. If the sync failure has already occurred, refer to SOL13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/000/sol13030.html) for information on how to restore configuration sync.
bugs.fix: Ensure the sFlow data source is removed from an HTTP profile when it is deleted.

bugs.title: Can't add a ICMPv6 type and code to a FW rule.
bugs.symptoms: Can't add a ICMPv6 type and code to a FW rule
bugs.conditions: choose the protocol as ICMPv6 and try to add a type and code.
bugs.impact: Firewall Rule Creation Page gets affected.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to add ICMPv6 type and code to a FW rule.
bugs.fix: GUI now accepts firewall rules specifying ICMPv6 with type and code.

bugs.title: New users cannot log in to Windows-based systems after installing BIG-IP EDGE client in certain deployment
bugs.symptoms: New users cannot log in to Windows-based systems after installing BIG-IP Edge client in certain deployments.
bugs.conditions: This is a rare, environment-based issue.
bugs.impact: New users cannot log in to Windows-based systems
bugs.workaround: Remove \F5 Networks\VPN\client.f5c file.
bugs.fix: A rare, environment-based issue that prevented new users from logging in to Windows-based systems has been fixed.

bugs.title: TMM crash while executing FLOW_INIT event (with multiple commands that abort the connection) in an iRule attached to an AFM firewall rule.
bugs.symptoms: Critical system failure due to TMM process restarting.
bugs.conditions: Following conditions will trigger the TMM crash: i) AFM rule match triggers an iRule execution. ii) iRule has one (or more) FLOW_INIT event with 2 (or more) commands that result in aborting the connection (e.g. 'drop' followed by 'reject')
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The aforementioned TMM crash has been fixed.

bugs.title: Blank popups in APM Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Blank popups or empty frames in APM Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: -- APM Portal Access. -- Patching locally defined function named Open.
bugs.impact: Blank popups or empty frames in APM Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule workaround specific to missing element.

bugs.title: Wrong use of custom XFF headers when there are multiple matches
bugs.symptoms: A specific case of multiple matching XFF headers and special settings, that lead to treating one of the supplied XFF headers, but not the desired one.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configuring at least one custom XFF header in the HTTP profile. 2. The incoming request has at least 2 headers that match the custom headers. 3. The DB variable avr.alwaysuselastxff is set to 0.
bugs.impact: The incoming request is treated as coming from an IP address that is not the desired address, this affects the reports and the identification of this request by the DoS system.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to set an iRule that will do the logic of the comparing the XFF headers, remove the unnecessary ones, and keep only the desired one.
bugs.fix: The desired XFF header is taken as the one that represents the HTTP request IP address.

bugs.title: Extraneous dedup_admin core
bugs.symptoms: There have been some extraneous dedup_admin cores generated during system shutdown.
bugs.conditions: Race condition during shutdown of vcmp with 2 blades.
bugs.impact: Extraneous dedup_admin core generated.
bugs.fix: Missing virtual destructor was added.

bugs.title: Correctly assign severity to check component alerts
bugs.symptoms: Check component alerts can be caused by legitimate browser settings. There is no way to distinguish this from malware alerts.
bugs.conditions: Check component alerts are sent.
bugs.impact: Difficult to identify users that are infected with malware.
bugs.fix: Differentiate between low severity and high severity component check alerts.
bugs.behavior: A new DB variable "AntiFraud.ComponentsValidation.Method" has been added that controls the type of request that the component check is performed on (all, get, post, or none)

bugs.title: Policy name field appears on Rule creation page even if Policy is selected
bugs.symptoms: The Policy name field appears on the Rule creation page even if the Policy is selected, requiring the user to reselect the policy.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when creating a rule for a policy and applying it to a context.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue and has no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: Reselect the desired policy.

bugs.title: SSL Forward Proxy server side now supports all key exchange methods.
bugs.symptoms: SSL Forward Proxy implementation requires the clientssl and serverssl profiles to configure at least one RSA ciphersuite. If the backend server uses ciphersuites other than RSA key exchange such as (ECDHE-ECDSA, ECDH-ECDSA, DHE-DSS), the connection fails.
bugs.conditions: Must use RSA key exchange on the server side, meaning that it is not possible to have server side SSL uses key exchange methods--such as ECDHE-ECDSA, ECDH-ECDSA, DHE-DSS--while the client side still uses RSA key exchange.
bugs.impact: SSL Forward Proxy on the server side cannot be configured to use all key exchange methods the SSL module supports, and is limited to RSA.
bugs.fix: SSL Forward Proxy server side supports all key exchange methods. Previously, SSL Forward Proxy on the server side only supported RSA, ECDHE-RSA, and EDH-RSA key exchange methods.
bugs.behavior: SSL Forward Proxy server side supports all key exchange methods. Previously, SSL Forward Proxy on the server side only supported RSA, ECDHE-RSA, and EDH-RSA key exchange methods.

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client behaves erratically while establishing network access connection
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac does not establish a network access connection, or if it can establish a connection, then it drops the connection. A user might see a cycle of connect/re-connect again.
bugs.conditions: OS X Yosemite, network access, BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.impact: User cannot establish network access connection.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac can now establish a connection correctly. An issue with routing table patch coding deleting an essential route has been resolved.

bugs.title: MAC Edge client crashed during routine Network Access.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac crashes during routine Network Access operations.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client for Mac and BIG-IP v11.6.0. This is a rarely occurring issue. Specific conditions are unknown.
bugs.impact: MAC Edge client crashes.
bugs.workaround: Restart Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.fix: A rarely occurring issue where BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac would crash randomly during regular Network Access connection has been fixed.

bugs.title: track L7DOS entities in irules in transparent mode only when attack occurs
bugs.symptoms: L7DOS entities in transparent mode was shown always regardless if there was attack or not
bugs.conditions: You have configured an irule to log entities that attack in DOS attack, and DOS is in transparent mode.
bugs.impact: A large number of entities are being logged even if an attack is not occurring.

bugs.title: Chrome developer console shows error with iRules LX Workspace Editor
bugs.symptoms: While using the iRules LX Workspace editor, it's possible to see an error if the developer console or other JavaScript console is being used. The error takes the form of: Refused to load the image 'data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==' because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "default-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'". Note that 'img-src' was not explicitly set, so 'default-src' is used as a fallback.
bugs.conditions: Opening files in the iRules LX Workspace editor
bugs.impact: There is no impact. The image trying to be loaded isn't necessary.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to upgrade to TMOS v13 or later or upgrade the Chrome version being used.
bugs.fix: Prevent browser console error when using iRules LX Workspace Editor

bugs.title: Improve High Speed Bridge diagnostic logging on transmit/receive failures
bugs.symptoms: When an HSB transmitter or receive failure occurs, no information is provided on the state of the HSB transmit/receive rings prior to the failure.
bugs.conditions: The HSB experiences a transmitter or receive failure.
bugs.impact: The unit is rebooted.
bugs.fix: Improved High Speed Bridge diagnostic logging on transmit/receive failures.

bugs.title: The vCMP worker-lite system is unable to reattach to the host after errors occur.
bugs.symptoms: The vCMP worker-lite system is unable to reattach to the host after errors or timeouts occur between the vCMP guest and host.
bugs.conditions: This issue affects worker-lite based systems running vCMP guests at 11.4.1 HF6 or 11.5.1 HF6 with any version of BIG-IP running in the hypervisor. Affected systems are PB200, B2100, B2150, and B4300 Viprion blades.
bugs.impact: SSL and compression traffic does not pass through an affected vCMP guest.
bugs.workaround: To resume SSL and compression traffic processing, the guest tmm process must be restarted, either by issuing 'bigstart restart tmm' within the vCMP guest, or by taking the guest to a provisioned state then back to deployed from the hypervisor.

bugs.title: The RA bit on DNS response may not be set
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances, the recursion available (RA) bit may be unset in responses from DNS cache.
bugs.conditions: If the system caches a message from the authoritative server without the rd bit, and subsequent queries with rd set find that message, the first message will not be used because the rd bit is not set. In this case, the operation falls back to the rrset cache and composes a message, but leaves the RA bit unset. This is appropriate for the transparent cache, but not the non-transparent cache.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that recursion available is not signaled to clients so they may not treat the DNS cache as an available resolver.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, write an iRule to set the RA bit when the cache is a resolver. Must also check origin for CACHE.
bugs.fix: The RA bit is set for the response when the cache resolver answers the query from the fast path.

bugs.title: TMM performance may be impacted when server node is flapping and persist is used
bugs.symptoms: TMM consumes a higher percentage of the CPU resources when handling traffic.
bugs.conditions: This intermittent issue occurs when a pool members goes up and down when using source_addr persistence.
bugs.impact: System performance is impacted.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The intermittent performance impact no longer occurs when a pool members goes up and down when using source_addr persistence.

bugs.title: Tmm cores while using APM network access and no leasepool is created on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores in Network Access scenario when no leasepool is created on the BIG-IP system and IP address assignment is done through the Variable Assign agent (mcget {session.ldap.last.attr.vpnClientIp}).
bugs.conditions: APM network access and no leasepool is created on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, create a leasepool on the BIG-IP system; it does not need to be attached to an access policy.
bugs.fix: TMM does not core now when using APM network access and no leasepool is created on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: BIG-IP DoS via buffer overflow in rrdstats
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP DoS via buffer overflow in rrdstats
bugs.conditions: rrdstats given malformatted input
bugs.impact: Crash in rrdstats - some services unavailable while rrdstats down
bugs.workaround: No workaround. rrdstats will be restarted by BIG-IP
bugs.fix: Improved request parsing to make it more robust against invalid formats.

bugs.title: Configuring of ICMPv4/ICMPv6 ip-protocol in mgmt port ACL Rules generated error
bugs.symptoms: PCCD gives error exhausted; causes inability to activate new mgmt port rules.
bugs.conditions: The mgmt port is configured as an IPV4 interface and an ICMPv6 protocol rule is applied with the action set to reject or vice-versa.
bugs.impact: error: resources exhausted; causes inability to activate new mgmt port rules
bugs.fix: Validation added to block invalid application of management firewall rule specifying ICMPv6 when management interface is configured with only IPv4 address. Validation also detects the reverse condition (IPv6 management address, ICMPv4 firewall rule). A descriptive error message is added.

bugs.title: iApp GUI: Unable to add FW Policy/Rule to context via iApp
bugs.symptoms: Unable to add FW Policy/Rule to context via iApp. Error message appears: "General database error retrieving information."
bugs.impact: Unable to create FW rules via iApp.
bugs.workaround: The issue is fixed. But could configure via tmsh.
bugs.fix: Fixed

bugs.title: Tuning of Application DoS URL qualification criteria
bugs.symptoms: Application DoS can not be tuned in order to tell which transactions are qualified for client side mitigation.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in response to the following scenario: 1. Create new L7-DoS profile, enable CS injection prevention. 2. Send more than 10 requests to a qualified URL. Make sure that URL is detected as qualified. 3. Send 1 request with HEAD or TRACE methods.
bugs.impact: URL will be detected as non-qualified. AVR does not qualify URLs according to the system's qualification criteria.
bugs.fix: This release provides tuning for the Application DoS URL qualification criteria.

bugs.title: Qkview does not include the incremental ConfigSync cache
bugs.symptoms: Qkview does not include the incremental ConfigSync cache.
bugs.conditions: Running Qkview on a system on which incremental ConfigSync caches exist.
bugs.impact: Diagnostic data useful (or sometimes necessary) for troubleshooting ConfigSync issues is not captured as part of a Qkview.
bugs.workaround: Collect output of "tmsh show /cm device-group name-of-device-group-or-'all'-keyword incremental-config-sync-cache".
bugs.fix: Qkview now includes the incremental ConfigSync cache when running the following command: /usr/bin/tmsh -a show cm device-group all incremental-config-sync-cache.

bugs.title: Enabling specific logging may trigger other unrelated events to be logged.
bugs.symptoms: When logging is enabled for TCP events some internal traffic like UDP could be logged.
bugs.conditions: When logging is enabled in AFM for TCP events.
bugs.impact: Some unwanted log messages with show up
bugs.workaround: There is no work around.
bugs.fix: Fixed a bug where undesired traffic was logged when TCP events logs were enabled.

bugs.title: Some TCP re-transmits on translucent vlangroup skip bit-flip on source MAC address
bugs.symptoms: Some packets re-transmitted as part of a full-proxy, non-SNAT'd TCP virtual server on a translucent-mode vlangroup do not correctly have the translucent-mode bit-flip applied.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with a translucent vlangroup and full virtual server with no SNAT.
bugs.impact: Egressing traffic with the source-MAC of another host can potentially lead to traffic loops.
bugs.workaround: Enable SNAT on the virtual server.
bugs.fix: All TCP re-transmits have the proper source MAC address.

bugs.title: Policy Export: BIG-IP does not export redirect URL for 'Login Response Page'
bugs.symptoms: ASM does not export redirect URLs in 'Login Response Page' for XML policies.
bugs.conditions: Redirect URL in 'Login Response Page' is used in ASM security policy.
bugs.impact: Redirect response page is missing from the security policy.
bugs.workaround: Use binary policy export for exporting redirection response pages for login URL.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue with XML policy export where the redirect response page was missing from the security policy.

bugs.title: PEM configured with BWC doing pem policy changes could trigger leak
bugs.symptoms: When PEM is configured to use bwc policy and cause re-evaluations due to pem policy change in configuration and/or PCRX could cause leak in bwc memory for active flows.
bugs.conditions: - PEM need to be configured to use bwc. - Active flows. - PEM policy change event for live flows.
bugs.impact: - memory leak.
bugs.workaround: - restart tmm. - upgrade image. - avoid PEM policy change event for live traffic flows. - attach bwc to pem policy after PEM policy change event.
bugs.fix: The case when PEM policy is modified on live traffic, PEM initiates policy re-evaluation. In process internally bwc is detached and attached. During this, the flow active flag is not cleared thus during flow release memory is not released.

bugs.title: The HTTP:payload command could cause the TMM to crash if invoked in a non-HTTP event
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP::payload command could cause the TMM to crash if invoked when HTTP had already started egressing data to other filters. This could only happen if HTTP::payload was used in a non-HTTP event.
bugs.conditions: HTTP::payload is used in a non-HTTP iRule.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use i.e. ASM::payload if you want the payload within an ASM event.
bugs.fix: HTTP::payload will no longer cause a TMM crash if invoked in a non-HTTP event. Instead, an error will be returned to the iRule.

bugs.title: APM End user interface pages customized using session data will render using defaults when session data is not available.
bugs.symptoms: Any APM end user interface pages that use data from the user's session will require that session to be active in order to display content as expected. When actions such as a "refresh" of the logout page are executed, the page that is rendered no longer has access to session data used for rendering it originally. As a result, such actions will result in the display of content derived from defaults.
bugs.conditions: The following conditions have to exist for this issue to occur: - Use of APM. - Customization of end user interface pages. - Use of data from the user's session for customization (e.g. results from evaluation of data to determine client type).
bugs.impact: Customized pages will render using default data due to unavailability of session data.
bugs.workaround: Use advanced customization in a manner that it only relies on available data for each type of customized content (e.g. for logout page, do not rely on session data).

bugs.title: "General database error retrieving information" appears on Self Ip Security page after removing a rule and refreshing the page
bugs.symptoms: The error "General database error retrieving information" appears on the Self IP Security page after removing a rule and refreshing the page.
bugs.conditions: Error occurs after deleting a rule from the Self IP Security page
bugs.impact: The user must refresh the page to continue configuring that feature.
bugs.workaround: You can navigate again to Network :: Self IPs : self_ip_name : Security when this issues occurs. The issue does not stop the user from deleting the rule itself.

bugs.title: ASM Request log does not show log messages.
bugs.symptoms: The request log does not show log messages related to ASM.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when first assigning the application logging profile, and then assigning the DOS logging profile on the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: There will not be log messages related to ASM.
bugs.workaround: Remove the ASM logging profile, apply and re-add the application logging profile.
bugs.fix: ASM request log now shows log messages related to ASM, even if the application logging profile was assigned to the virtual server before the DOS logging profile was assigned to it.

bugs.title: Incorrect AFM firewall rule counter update after pktclass-daemon restarts.
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect firewall rule counters are updated upon classifying traffic when rules are re-ordered AND pktclass-daemon is also restarted.
bugs.conditions: pktclass-daemon restarts and there are active firewall rules present (at any context).
bugs.impact: While there is no incorrect behavior in matching/classifying traffic, updating incorrect rule counter may lead to impression that traffic is being classified incorrectly.
bugs.fix: The issue regarding update of incorrect rule counter (after pktclass-daemon restarts) has been fixed.

bugs.title: 5200 does not forward STP BPDUs across VLAN groups when in PASSTHRU mode
bugs.symptoms: When configured for bridging all traffic, 5200 platform does not bridge STP BPDUs when in PASSTHRU mode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions: -- Configure a VLAN group and configure to bridge all traffic. -- Configure STP in PASSTHRU mode.
bugs.impact: The 5200 platform does not forward STP BPDUs across VLAN groups when in PASSTHRU mode, so STP PASSTHRU mode does not work correctly between VLAN groups.
bugs.fix: The 5200 platform now forwards STP BPDUs across VLAN groups when in PASSTHRU mode.

bugs.title: DNS express doesn't send zone notify response
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server on the BIG-IP system receives a zone notify message, it does not send a response message back. Instead, it sends the original notify message back to the remote name server.
bugs.conditions: A zone notify message is sent to a virtual server with a DNS profile. The zone is configured to allow notify from the sender and the notify action is set to be consumed.
bugs.impact: The remote name server sends the notify message to the BIG-IP system several times since the remote name server does not receive a response message.
bugs.fix: TMM will correctly send a response message back when processing a zone notify message from a remote name server.

bugs.title: Manage ASM security policies from BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: Certain aspects of ASM Security Policies on BIG-IP 11.5.2 cannot be managed by BIG-IQ Security.
bugs.conditions: Using BIG-IQ Security to manage ASM on BIG-IP 11.5.2.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ Security cannot effectively manage ASM on BIG-IP 11.5.2.
bugs.fix: New ASM security policies can now be created by BIG-IQ version 4.5. Currently, discovery of 11.5.2 HF1 by a 4.5 BIG-IQ is disabled by default on the BIG-IP system, and can be turned on by changing the rest_api_extensions option to '1' on the Advanced Configuration/System Variables screen in the ASM user interface (navigate to Security: Options: Application Security: Advanced Configuration: System Variables) on the BIG-IP system. After saving the change, the user is instructed to do a 'tmsh restart sys service asm'. Additionally, the user should restart the httpd service via: 'bigstart restart httpd'.

bugs.title: Upgrading with ASM iRule and virtual server with no websecurity profile
bugs.symptoms: If you have an iRule that uses "ASM::*" assigned to a virtual server with no websecurity profile, when trying to upgrade from BIG-IP version 11.4.0 to any newer version, the upgrade fails, and you receive the following error message: ----------------- ASM::disable in rule (iRule_name) requires an associated WEBSECURITY profile on the virtual server (virtual_server_name). -----------------
bugs.conditions: On version 11.4: 1) Have an iRule that uses ASM::*, e.g. when HTTP_REQUEST { ASM::disable } 2) Create a virtual server and associate an ASM policy with it via CPM (L7) policy 3) Assign the iRule to the VS 4) Remove the CPM policy from the VS Now upgrade to any newer version OR Save the ucs and try to manually install it on any newer version
bugs.impact: Fails to upgrade. Fails to install ucs.
bugs.workaround: Prior to upgrading and/or saving the ucs, for all virtual servers that have no websecurity profile assigned to them, remove all iRules that contain 'ASM::*' actions.
bugs.fix: You can now successfully upgrade from version 11.4.0 to any newer version even if you have an iRule that uses "ASM::*" and a virtual server with no websecurity profile assigned because the upgrade/ucs_install mechanism now detaches the ASM iRule from the virtual server.

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client fails intermittently with machine certificate inspection
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac fails intermittently with machine certificate inspection when "Match CN with FQDN" setting is configured.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs with BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac and machine certificate agent when in the access policy "Match CN with FQDN" is set.
bugs.impact: Edge ClienT fails to pass machine certificate inspection.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac does not fail intermittently with machine certificate inspection agent.

bugs.title: Incorrect overlapping status shown when a rule in a rule list has the same name as a rule not in that list
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect overlapping status (redundant or conflicting) is shown when a rule in a rule list has the same name as a rule not in that list.
bugs.conditions: Identical rule names in both in the Rule List and outside the rule list.
bugs.impact: Potentially misleading presentation.
bugs.workaround: use different rule names

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Server-side URL parser interprets &# in URL as HTML entity in any case
bugs.symptoms: URL may contain a character sequence, &# (ampersand, pound) that is not a part of HTML entity, for instance: http://example.com/some/path?query&#fragment In this example, &# is not a beginning of a valid HTML entity and should be left untouched at rewriting.
bugs.conditions: URL containing a &# character sequence that is not a part of HTML entity.
bugs.impact: URL with &# inside may not be rewritten.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule with two steps: - Modifies the original URL to let it be rewritten. - Modifies the rewritten URL to revert changes made by 1st step, as shown in the following example: a) Original URL: http://example.com/path?aa=bb&#fragment. b) URL after 1st step of iRule: http://example.com/path?aa=bb&@F5_@#fragment. c) Rewritten URL before 2nd step of iRule: https://bigip.system.name.com/f5-w-687474703a2f2f6578616d706c652e636f6d$$/path?aa=bb&F5CH=I@F5_@#fragment. d) URI corrected by 2nd step of iRule: https://bigip.system.name.com/f5-w-687474703a2f2f6578616d706c652e636f6d$$/path?aa=bb&F5CH=I#fragment. In other words, the second step removes insertions made by the first step.
bugs.fix: Now, a URL containing &# character sequences are rewritten correctly, even if the &# fragment does not belong to a valid HTML entity.

bugs.title: SSL profile fails to initialize and might cause SSL operation issues
bugs.symptoms: When the SSL profile fails to initialize, it causes the SSL enter pass-through mode instead of rejecting traffic.
bugs.conditions: SSL profile fails to initialize, for example, due to failure to load cert/key files.
bugs.impact: SSL enters pass-through mode instead of rejecting traffic. As a side effect, ConfigSync might fail, as the communication channel does not establish because of a hung SSL connection.
bugs.workaround: Make sure cert/key is available and has the proper grant access mode.
bugs.fix: When the SSL profile fails to initialize, it now causes the SSL to reject traffic correctly.

bugs.title: Module provisioning doesn't properly account for disk space
bugs.symptoms: You are able to provision modules, but module daemons fail to start.
bugs.conditions: Low free disk space on HD1 as reported by tmsh list sys disk logical-disk
bugs.impact: The module(s) provisioned may not function.

bugs.title: Errors logged in bd.log coming from the ACY module
bugs.symptoms: Cosmetic errors logged in bd.log from the ACY module: 'acy_prepare_RWdas failed to init rwkm-report_kw_data report'.
bugs.conditions: Configuration changes between signature sets on a security policy.
bugs.impact: False errors appear constantly. These errors are cosmetic, and do not indicate a problem with the system.
bugs.fix: We fixed false error logs that were coming from the ACY module.

bugs.title: Config snapshots are deleted when failover happens
bugs.symptoms: When failover occurs, the config snapshots on the new active node might be deleted during the HA state transition. As a result, a user might encounter one of the errors below: 1. Login failure/denied. 2. Some webtop resources are missing after successful login.
bugs.conditions: When the standby node switches to active.
bugs.impact: User cannot login or access some resources after login.
bugs.workaround: Restart APD by running the command: bigstart restart apd.
bugs.fix: Now APD uses a short time interval for periodic checking of config snapshots right after failover happens. If config snapshots are found to be missing, APD recreates them. After a few such cycles, APD reverts to using a long time interval for the check.

bugs.title: Black List Classes/Black List Categories terminology inconsistency
bugs.symptoms: There is a terminology inconsistency in how the GUI in AFM 11.5.0 IP Intelligence, which refers to 'Black List Classes', and AFM 11.6.0 IP Intelligence, which refers to 'Black List Categories'. In addition, viewing 11.6.0 labels on Reporting or Event Logs for IP Intelligence reads 'Class', where they should read 'Category'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when comparing AFM screens in 11.5.0 and 11.6.0.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent terminology might result in customer confusion.
bugs.fix: Black List Classes is now correctly referred to as Black List Categories in AFM 11.6.0 IP Intelligence, which makes the term consistent across the GUI versions.

bugs.title: Client can fail to start a new session in multi-domain SSO.
bugs.symptoms: A client cannot start a new session from the session expired page if the session expires on the primary auth domain before the policy completes.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure multi-domain SSO. -- Client attempts to access an application (www.site.com) and is then redirected to the auth domain (www.primaryauth.com). -- The auth policy is allowed to expire without completing.
bugs.impact: The 'start a new session' prompt cannot send the client back to the application to restart the policy, since that information was lost when the session expired. The client must use the back button to return to the application to start a new session.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, in Customization, modify the HREF for the Session Expired Message so that it redirects to www.site.com. In the customization text for the Session Expired Message, replace [SESSION_RESTART_URL] with the session variable %{session.server.network.name}.

bugs.title: Troubleshooting enhancement: improve logging details for AWS failover failure.
bugs.symptoms: Logging information on BIG-IP VE for Failover on AWS was inadequate and did not provide the reason for failures in Failover.
bugs.conditions: Traffic-group failover sometimes failed without providing specific reason for the failure.
bugs.impact: The lack of logging messages that could pin-point the mis-configuration or connectivity issues on AWS makes it difficult to determine what is causing the Failover to fail.
bugs.fix: Added more logging details for AWS failover failure to assist in detecting problems in failover.
bugs.behavior: Previously, the following AWS permissions were required when running failover: ec2:AssignPrivateIpAddresses and ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces. Failover could fail because of region or key issues, and so an additional AWS permission, ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus, is now also required for running failover.
bugs.workaround: Adding more logging information in failover script resolves this issue and provides enough information to the customer to detect problems in failover.

bugs.title: it is possible to get infinite loop in LDAP Query while resolving nested groups
bugs.symptoms: Processing nested groups might cause an infinite loop.
bugs.conditions: LDAP query is configured to get group membership using 'member' attribute. On the LDAP server, group1 has group2 as a member and group2 has group1 as a membermember (membership loop), then the LDAP Query falls into an infinite loop trying to resolve nested groups.
bugs.impact: User cannot pass access policy that contains the affected agent. The apd process must be restarted to re-initialize LDAP agent.
bugs.fix: The LDAP Query resolves group membership including nested groups as expected.

bugs.title: Rare cases of errors when loading data into mysql
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, some AVR data was formed with duplicated rows, causing errors when inserting saving the data in mysql. You will see the following in monpd.log: "Some rows of load_stat_ip_1420015200.1 not loaded (22670 rows affected).".
bugs.conditions: This can occur when avr loads.
bugs.impact: Loss of some statistical data.
bugs.fix: We fixed an issue where in some cases, some AVR data was formed with duplicated rows, and triggered errors when saving the data in mysql.

bugs.title: wom_verify_config produces unneccesarily elevated messages in ltm log
bugs.symptoms: The wom_verify_config utility sometimes produces error-level messages in ltm log, that should be informational or warning.
bugs.conditions: When WOM is not fully configured.
bugs.impact: Error-level messages in the ltm log can result in unexpected action being taken, where an information or warning level message may not.
bugs.fix: The messages created by wom_verify_config have been cleaned up.

bugs.title: OneConnect does not reuse existing connections in VIP targeting VIP configuration
bugs.symptoms: Significant increase in Active Connections and Connections per Second for virtual servers that receive connections from another virtual server with the Policy action 'virtual' or iRule command 'virtual' and the client virtual server has a OneConnect profile. The connections per second will match the rate of HTTP requests sent to the server virtual server. A packet capture would reveal that OneConnect is not reusing previously opened connections, and previously opened connections remain idle until timeout.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when either of the following conditions are met: -- Virtual-to-virtual configuration with OneConnect profile. -- iRule contains the following command: node <ip> <port>.
bugs.impact: An increase in CPU and memory resources occurs due to the increase in connections established and connections that remain in memory.
bugs.workaround: If not required, remove the OneConnect profile from the client virtual server.
bugs.fix: Connections are correctly reused even with VIP on VIP configuration.

bugs.title: Deleting trust-domain fails when standby IP is in ha-order
bugs.symptoms: Deleting trust-domain fails when the ha-order traffic group contains a standby unit's IP address.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a non-local device that is used by the HA order in one of the traffic groups.
bugs.impact: Unable to delete trust domain. The tmsh command 'delete cm trust-domain all' intermittently hangs. Pressing Ctrl + C shows: Unexpected Error: Could not reset trust-domain (error from devmgmtd): Error reading from server...' In the /var/log/ltm the system posts the message: 'err devmgmtd[7887]: 015a0000:3: -unknown- failed on -unknown-.devicegroup: 01071761:3: Cannot delete device (BIG-IPsystem.example.com) from device group (/Common/sync-failover-1) because it is used by HA order on traffic group (/Common/traffic-group-2)'.
bugs.workaround: Retrying sometimes succeeds. Removing the ha-order traffic group also allows the operation to succeed.
bugs.fix: Deletion of a device trust domain now completes successfully when the BIG-IP system is a member of a device trust domain configured with a traffic group high-availability order that references a device other than the local system.

bugs.title: Client side or server side SSL handshake may fail if it involves SHA512-signed certificates in TLS1.2
bugs.symptoms: A handshake with either client-ssl or server-ssl when presented with a certificate signed/hashed with sha512 may fail.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen when it meets the following 3 conditions. 1. The SSL connection is using TLS1.2 2. The backend server's certificate is signed/hashed with sha512. 3. The backend server is Microsoft IIS server. More precisely, a server that strictly enforces the RFC policy for TLS1.2: 'If the client provided a 'signature_algorithms' extension, then all certificates provided by the server MUST be signed by a hash/signature algorithm pair that appears in that extension.' This kind of server rejects the SSL connection if the BIG-IP system does not advertise sha512 when sending the clienthello message. Microsoft IIS server does strictly enforce this rejection behavior, although Apache and OpenSSL servers do not. On the client side: 1. Client is trying to establish SSL connection using TLS1.2. 2. Client-ssl is configured with client-cert authentication. 3. Client is configured with sha512-signed certificate only. When the BIG-IP system sends a CertificateRequest that does not include sha512, the client might send back a null certificate.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system cannot establish SSL connection with the backend server. Client fails to establish an SSL connection with the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this: -- Use TLS1/TLS1.1/SSL3 instead of TLS1.2. -- Configure the backend server to use certificates signed/hashed with something other than sha512. -- Use a backend server other than Microsoft IIS.
bugs.fix: For the serverside, the system now contains sha512 in the signature_algorithms extension when sending the clienthello with TLS1.2 (when you configures 'ANY' in the SSL sign hash option in the serverssl profile), so that the server does not reject the SSL connection because the BIG-IP system does not contain sha512 in the clienthello. sha512 is also included on the clientside, so that if the client uses sha512 to hash/sign the certvfy message, the BIG-IP system (acting as a server) does not reject to verify it (when you configures 'ANY' in the SSL sign hash option in the clientssl profile).

bugs.title: Synchronization problem in AVR lookups sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash
bugs.symptoms: There is a synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.
bugs.conditions: AVR is provisioned or report statistic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: We fixed a synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes caused TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.
bugs.fix: This is a duplicate of ID 475439.

bugs.title: Added "Collect full URL" functionality.
bugs.symptoms: Added functionality to collect the full URL (with host name) to AVR statistics.
bugs.conditions: In tmsh, run the command: modify sys db avr.includeserverinuri value disable Run traffic with the URL http://172.29.33.87/debug The URL that will be written to the lookup table is: "/debug" In tmsh, run the command: modify sys db avr.includeserverinuri value enable Run traffic with the URL http://172.29.33.87/debug The URL that will be written to the lookup table is: "172.29.33.87/debug"
bugs.impact: Now possible to collect full URLs
bugs.fix: Added functionality to collect the full URL (with host name) to AVR statistics.

bugs.title: JSON UTF16 content could be blocked by ASM as Malformed JSON
bugs.symptoms: When JSON UTF16 content is handled by ASM and the content includes one of the characters below, the request could be blocked by ASM policy. XML_CHAR_BACKSLASH XML_CHAR_LEFT_CURLY_BRACKET XML_CHAR_RIGHT_CURLY_BRACKET
bugs.conditions: ASM policy assigned to a virtual server and the policy configured to enforce JSON content.
bugs.impact: False positive request blocking.
bugs.fix: JSON unicode_charmap table has been fixed, thus UTF16 characters are interpreted correctly.

bugs.title: System statistics may fail to update, or report negative deltas due to delayed stats merging.
bugs.symptoms: Under some conditions, the BIG-IP system might fail to report statistics over time. This can manifest as statistics reporting unchanging statistics (e.g., all zeroes (0)), or as sudden spikes in traffic, or as negative deltas in some counters. The system performance graphs will also appear to have gaps / be missing data at the times that this occurs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are frequent changes occurring to the underlying statistics data structures. This might occur under the following conditions: -- The system is spawning/reaping processes on a frequent basis (e.g., when there is a large number of external monitors). -- iRules are frequently using 'SSL::profile' to select different SSL profiles on a virtual server (this can cause per-virtual server, per-profile statistics to be created and deleted on a regular basis).
bugs.impact: Statistics fail to merge, which results in incorrect view of system behavior and operation.
bugs.workaround: This issue has two workarounds: 1. Reduce the frequency of changes in the statistics data structures. The specific action to take depends on what is triggering them. To do so, use any or all of the following: -- Reduce the frequency of configuration changes. -- Reduce the use of 'SSL::profile' in iRules. -- Reduce the number/frequency of processes being spawned by the system. 2. The second workaround has two parts: a) Switch statistics roll-ups to the 'slow_merge' method, which causes the system to spend more CPU merging statistics. To do so, set the 'merged.method' DB key to 'slow_merge' using the following command: tmsh modify sys db merged.method value slow_merge b) Change the merge-interval value to 2 to reduce CPU usage when merge-method is slow-merge. tmsh modify /sys db merged.merge.interval {value "2"} Note: Performing the second workaround has the side-effect of disabling tmstat snapshots on the device. The tmstat snapshots are intended for F5-internal use only: the lack of snapshots will have no bearing on the functionality of your system; however, F5 Support might be impacted in their ability to troubleshoot issues on your system. 3. tmsh modify sys db tmm.ssl.defaultlistenerstatrow value enable Trade-off of enabling by default: rolling iRule-selected-profile stats into _listener means per-VS granularity for those connections is lost

bugs.title: FastL4 does not honor the MSS override value in the FastL4 profile with syncookies
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 does not honor the MSS override value in the FastL4 profile when syncookies are in use. This can lead to cases where the advertised MSS value in the SYN/ACK is larger than the MSS override value.
bugs.conditions: The FastL4 profile specifies a non-zero MSS override value and syncookies mode is active.
bugs.impact: The wrong MSS value is advertised during 3WHS.
bugs.fix: FastL4 now honors the MSS override value in the FastL4 profile with syncookies.
bugs.behavior: The BIG-IP system advertises MSS in the SYN/ACK is based on the MSS override value in the FastL4 profile. Previously, this was only based on the VLAN's MTU.

bugs.title: An optimistic ACK sent by a server in response to a BIG-IP FIN/ACK packet result in a FIN/ACK storm.
bugs.symptoms: An optimistic ACK sent by a server in response to a BIG-IP FIN/ACK packet results in a FIN/ACK storm.
bugs.conditions: When an ACK with an 'invalid' sequence number is received, the resulting calculations involving the incoming seqno and rcv_nxt causes an outgoing ACK to be generated which will repeat if the server behavior repeats.
bugs.impact: Many connections delayed and CPU usage is very high. Peak usage is around 90%. Traffic suffers severe deterioration.
bugs.fix: This problem is now corrected by ensuring that when outgoing ACK is being generated that the FIN is stripped if it is not a retransmission of the FIN.

bugs.title: Windows File Check does not work if the filename starts with an ampersand
bugs.symptoms: Windows File Check does not work if the filename starts with an ampersand.
bugs.conditions: Run Windows file check and add a file name that starts with an ampersand.
bugs.impact: Depends upon access policy, but in the worst case a user might be allowed to log in.
bugs.fix: Access policy Windows File check now works with a file name that starts with an ampersand (&).

bugs.title: Standby unit might bridge network ingress packets when bridge_in_standby is disabled
bugs.symptoms: On a standby unit with a vlangroup configured with multiple VLAN members and bridge_in_standby attribute set to false, the unit might still bridge network ingress packets across the vlangroup, if those packet happen to match the host monitor traffic flows.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: Configure a vlangroup with multiple VLAN members in HA configuration and set vlangroup's bridge_in_standby attribute to false. Configure monitors to use non-default monitor rules (ICMP, etc.).
bugs.impact: This results in a traffic bridging loop among active and standby unis. Excessive traffic load might take down monitors on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Standby unit no longer bridges network ingress packets when bridge_in_standby is disabled. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Validation does not check that all keys/certificates are removed from the clientSSL profile
bugs.symptoms: Using iControl, a system admin is able to remove all the keys/certificates associated with a clientSSL profile. If this remains in the configuration and the system is upgraded to a version that validates that there are no empty keys or chains, the config will fail to load and will post this error signature in /var/log/ltm: emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all" - failed. -- 01070315:3: profile <Client SSL profile> requires a key Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl to remove keys and certificates from a clientSSL profile. Note: This issue may not be seen initially if the clientSSL profile is not in use. Upgrading to a version that performs validation against empty keys and chains, such as an upgrade from 11.5.1 to 11.6.0, will reveal the issue.
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: SSL profiles with no keys or certificates are invalid profiles. Make sure you fully delete all profiles if this is your intention. Also be careful not to leave the profile and delete only the key and certificate using iControl.

bugs.title: Bug 464651 introduced change-in-behavior for SSL server cert chains by not including the root certificate
bugs.symptoms: Bug 464651 fixed a loop issue that occurred when building a certificate chain caused by an invalid configuration in certificates. That fix unintentionally excluded the root certificate in the chain. While it is still a valid certificate chain, it does result in a change-in-behavior issue that is unacceptable in certain cases.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in versions containing the fix for Bug 464651 (11.4.1, 11.5.4).
bugs.impact: In some instances, the root certificate must be included in the certificate chain. In other cases, the certificate validation fails.
bugs.fix: This fix restores the previous behavior by including the root certificate in the chain.

bugs.title: Qkview may store information in the wrong format
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new monitor, some information may be stored in the wrong format.
bugs.conditions: Create a new monitor. Run qkview.
bugs.impact: Occasionally, some information stored for the new monitor will be in the incorrect format.
bugs.fix: Monitor information is now stored in the correct format.

bugs.title: RAM cache serves zero length documents.
bugs.symptoms: RAM cache serves zero length documents.
bugs.conditions: Forcing caching in an iRule.
bugs.impact: RAM Cache will cache a HEAD response, if an iRule is configured to force it to do so. This causes RAM cache to serve zero length documents.
bugs.workaround: If the HTTP operation is a HEAD request, do not cache the response.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Edge Client for MAC shows wrong SSL protocol version; does not display the protocol version that was negotiated.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac shows the wrong SSL protocol version in Details; it does not display the protocol version that was negotiated.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac displays the incorrect SSL protocol version now in Details.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac displays the correct SSL protocol version now in Details.

bugs.title: LTM v10.2.x to v11.x upgrade misses partition name on node specific monitor
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from v10.2.x to v11.x, the node monitor name does not acquire full path or partition information. Similarly, creating a node with a monitor via TMSH, the node monitor name does not show partition information; however, configuring a node via GUI does add partition information. If a node with a specific none monitor is later forced down and then re-enabled, the node will remain in a marked down by monitor state.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from v10.2.x to v11.x.
bugs.impact: For nodes that have a specific monitor of "none", if the node is forced down and then re-enabled via tmsh or the node list in the GUI, the node will be marked down by the monitor. If the node is re-enabled from the node properties page in the GUI, this issue does not occur. For other monitor types or pool and pool member monitors, the issue is cosmetic.
bugs.workaround: Load sys config base, then load sys config. Then in both the GUI and TMSH add partition info to the node monitor.

bugs.title: SIP Filter drops UDP flow when ingressq len limit is reached.
bugs.symptoms: UDP stats shows increase in the number of flows and valid SIP messages are dropped.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when an iRule processing delay occurs (session db operations) combined with increase in the SIP incoming flow.
bugs.impact: SIP UDP flows are dropped.
bugs.fix: The SIP UDP flow now remains when the ingress len limit is reached.

bugs.title: Order Zones statistics would cause database error
bugs.symptoms: 'General database error retrieving information' error in GUI.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the GUI to view Statistics for DNS zones.
bugs.impact: Not able to view Statistics from GUI for DNS zones.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to view Statistics for DNS zones.
bugs.fix: 'General database error retrieving information' error no longer occurs when viewing DNS zone statistics from the GUI.

bugs.title: A static subscriber's session is not deleted if master-IP is deleted from the subscriber's list of IPs
bugs.symptoms: A stale session is left behind.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a session by sending radius start messages to static subscriber that learns IP addresses dynamically. 2. remove master IP from static subscriber list. 3. delete static subscriber. 4. Use pem_sessiondump --list to see that the session is not deleted.
bugs.impact: No functional issue.
bugs.fix: Reprovison session if IP removed/added in SSP case too. This will fix session delete if Master IP being removed

bugs.title: "persist add" in server-side iRule event can result in "Client Addr" being pool member address
bugs.symptoms: When using Universal Persistence, depending on how an iRule is implemented, the Client Addr field in persist records may be the selected pool member's address, instead of the client address.
bugs.conditions: Universal Persistence
bugs.impact: The "Client Address" field in persistence records may be wrong. Note that this field is not used for anything in the data path, so this issue is purely cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Persist record now has correct "Client Addr" even when the owner for the persist record is in different TMM.

bugs.title: Customized logout page is not displayed after logon failure
bugs.symptoms: Default logout page is displayed instead of customized logout page after maximum logon attempts allowed is reached.
bugs.conditions: 1. Access profile has customized logout page. 2. The number of failed logon attempts reaches what is allowed by the policy.
bugs.impact: User will not see the customized logout page.
bugs.fix: Customized logout page is now displayed after logon failure.

bugs.title: boot menu titles might not contain volume suffix
bugs.symptoms: The title of a boot entry normally contains a suffix which is the name of the volume in which it resides, in angle brackets. Ex: BIG-IP 11.6.0 Build 3.0.364 <MD1.2> When BIG-IP 11.6.0 hf3 is installed, the resulting boot entry is missing the suffix: BIG-IP 11.6.0 Build 3.0.412
bugs.conditions: occurs when hotfix 11.6.0 hf3 is installed
bugs.workaround: none necessary
bugs.fix: Improved installer for HFR.

bugs.title: Nitrox might report bad records on highly fragmented SSL records
bugs.symptoms: When using an AES-GCM cipher on highly fragmented SSL records, platforms with Cavium Nitrox cards might report Bad records.
bugs.conditions: The negotiated cipher is one of the AES-GCM ciphers, and the MTU is such that the SSL records are highly fragmented.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system disconnects Client SSL connections prematurely. The SSL profile shows a number of Bad records.
bugs.fix: The processing buffers reserve the proper number of subsequent parameters.

bugs.title: Improved performance loading thousands of Virtual Servers
bugs.symptoms: In v11.5.1 and newer, when loading thousands of Virtual Servers, mcpd might become overloaded, causing loads to take a long time, or fail entirely when mcpd times out and is restarted. This might be more severe if GTM was enabled.
bugs.conditions: Thousands of Virtual Servers, GTM enabled. The problem is caused when tracking the state of Virtual Address changes and broadcasting those state changes under certain circumstances.
bugs.impact: Might cause long load times or configuration load failure because of mcpd timeout and restart.
bugs.workaround: Disable GTM. Reduce the number of Virtual Addresses.
bugs.fix: The Virtual Address state change code was improved in multiple areas: 1. GTM is checked for provisioning. 2. Each individual Virtual Address is checked for GTM association before assuming it needs to be broadcast. 3. Virtual Address changes caused by the Virtual Server, Pool, or Virtual Address changes are processed at a higher priority. 4. Virtual Address changes caused by a GTM state change are processed after the Virtual Server changes in #3. 5. All Virtual Address changes are processed on a queue that limits the number per mcpd event loop, preventing Virtual Address status changes from blocking normal mcpd operations.
bugs.behavior: The Virtual Address state change code was improved in multiple areas: 1. GTM is checked for provisioning. 2. Each individual Virtual Address is checked for GTM association before assuming it needs to be broadcast. 3. Virtual Address changes caused by the Virtual Server, Pool, or Virtual Address changes are processed at a higher priority. 4. Virtual Address changes caused by a GTM state change are processed after the Virtual Server changes in #3. 5. All Virtual Address changes are processed on a queue that limits the number per mcpd event loop, preventing Virtual Address status changes from blocking normal mcpd operations.

bugs.title: In case of intra_cluster ha, node flapping may still lead to inconsistent persistence entries across TMMs
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistent persistence entries across TMMs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions are met: -- intra_cluster HA configuration. -- node flapping.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent persistence behaviors.
bugs.workaround: Add an iRule command to the PERSIST_DOWN event that deletes the persistence entry for this connection. One example might be: when PERSIST_DOWN { persist delete source_addr [IP::client_addr] } For more information, see SOL14918: Node flapping may cause inconsistent persistence records, available here: http://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/900/sol14918.html.
bugs.fix: An issue involving inconsistent behavior of persistence across TMMs is fixed.

bugs.title: Incoming NTP packets from configured NTP server to non-local IP breaks outgoing NTP
bugs.symptoms: When incoming NTP packets from the configured NTP server arrive for a non-local IP on a BIG-IP system that is either a Virtual Edition (VE) guest, an appliance, or a vCMP guest on an appliance host, an iptables rule is triggered that results in further outgoing packets to the NTP server to have their destination IP addresses changed to 127.3.0.0, which is not routable and thus causes NTP time syncs to stop.
bugs.conditions: An NTP server is configured on a BIG-IP system that is either a VE, an appliance, or a vCMP guest on an appliance host, and packets arrive from the configured NTP server destined for an IP address belonging to another machine on the network. This can happen for several reasons: 1) The customer has a device on the same management network doing very low-to-zero volume of traffic over its management port. NTP syncs time less often than the L2 FDB expiration time. 2) The customer is using a L2 topology that uses redundant switches with NIC teaming / bonding, and one of the hosts cuts over to the other switch. This also causes transmits of packets that have no valid L2 FDB entry. 3) An STP topology change occurs in a given network, causing switches to drop L2 FDB entries for relevant hosts and flood unknown unicast destination traffic to all ports of a given VLAN. 4) Any unicast misdirection of NTP traffic to the management port not covered above.
bugs.impact: NTP time syncing stops on affected BIG-IP systems.
bugs.workaround: To remove the iptables rule that is causing the problem: # iptables -t nat -D bpnet-in -p udp --dport 123 -j DNAT --to-destination 127.3.0.0. Comment out the following line in the function setup_virtual_backplane() in the file /etc/init.d/cluster to prevent the rule from coming back upon reboot: iptables -t nat -A bpnet-in -p udp --dport 123 -j DNAT --to-destination $int_mgmtip.
bugs.fix: Incoming NTP packets from configured NTP server to non-local IP now works correctly with outgoing NTP.

bugs.title: [SMTP Configuration] Encrypted password not shown in GUI
bugs.symptoms: Under SMTP configuration, when authentication is enabled (the "use authentication" check box is checked) and a user name and password are configured, the password field is empty in the configuration utility when accessing the newly created SMTP object. TMSH shows the password in hash format.
bugs.conditions: 1. authentication is enabled. 2. username and password are configured.
bugs.impact: SMTP authentication fails.
bugs.workaround: After saving the SMTP configuration for the first time using the configuration utility, use only TMSH, REST API, or iControl to edit it or re-enter the password. Note: This will not fix sending AVR e-mails. The only way to send e-mail before this fix is using a non-authenticated SMTP server.
bugs.fix: Under SMTP configuration, when authentication is enabled (the "use authentication" check box is checked) and a user name and password are configured, the password is correctly decrypted using standard BIG-IP tools.

bugs.title: OpenSSL library updated to version 1.0.1l
TMM core if identical radius starts messages received
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores and restarts with identical radius start messages are received by BIG-IP when PEM provisioned.
bugs.conditions: Identical radius start message received by PEM to create session.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed tmm core issue when duplicate radius start messages are received by handling it properly.

bugs.title: TMM may core during failover due to invalid memory access in IPsec components
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores when transitioning from standby to active.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when the following conditions are met: -- An IPsec tunnel is enabled. -- The BIG-IP system is a member of an HA pair. -- The BIG-IP system transitions from standby to active.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a race condition that might have caused IPsec components to access previously freed memory.

bugs.title: Virtual Address status may not be reliably communicated with route daemon
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, when the Virtual Server status changes, the Virtual Address status may not me communicated to the routing services (that is, the tmrouted service). This can result in incorrect routes.
bugs.conditions: Exact conditions unknown, but it can occur when the Virtual Server status changes.
bugs.impact: Virtual Addresses may have advertised routes when they are down, or vice versa.
bugs.fix: The Virtual Address state change code was improved in multiple areas: 1. GTM is checked for provisioning. 2. Each individual Virtual Address is checked for GTM association before assuming it needs to be broadcast. 3. Virtual Address changes caused by the Virtual Server, Pool, or Virtual Address changes are processed at a higher priority. 4. Virtual Address changes caused by a GTM state change are processed after the Virtual Server changes in #3. 5. All Virtual Address changes are processed on a queue that limits the number per mcpd event loop, preventing Virtual Address status changes from blocking normal mcpd operations.
bugs.behavior: The Virtual Address state change code was improved in multiple areas: 1. GTM is checked for provisioning. 2. Each individual Virtual Address is checked for GTM association before assuming it needs to be broadcast. 3. Virtual Address changes caused by the Virtual Server, Pool, or Virtual Address changes are processed at a higher priority. 4. Virtual Address changes caused by a GTM state change are processed after the Virtual Server changes in #3. 5. All Virtual Address changes are processed on a queue that limits the number per mcpd event loop, preventing Virtual Address status changes from blocking normal mcpd operations.

bugs.title: TMM Core as SIP hudnode leaks
bugs.symptoms: There is a memory leak when using SIP in TCP/ClientSSL configurations.
bugs.conditions: The leak occurs when the clientside flow is torn down in response to the SSL handshake not completing.
bugs.impact: Because the SSL handshake is not complete, the SIP handler cannot complete the operation as expected, which results in an error and a memory leak of the SIP handler. The tmm memory increases, which eventually requires restarting tmm as a workaround.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround to prevents the issue, you can recover from the memory-leak condition by restarting tmm.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a memory leak that occurred when using SIP in TCP/ClientSSL configurations, when the clientside flow was torn down in response to the SSL handshake not completing. The system now frees the SIP handler upon receiving the notification of a failed SSL handshake, so that the connection is rejected, the system performs the proper cleanup of the SIP handler, and no memory leak occurs.

bugs.title: 'Data publisher not found or not implemented' mcpd error message when iRule is loaded from tmsh.
bugs.symptoms: 'Data publisher not found or not implemented' mcpd error message when iRule is loaded from tmsh. The system posts the following mcpd error message in ltm log when an iRule is loaded from tmsh: err mcpd[5834]: 0107167d:3: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request (unknown request), tag (6589).
bugs.conditions: When merging config files, the error message may show up in system log.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact observed.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit and merge config files.

bugs.title: dnatutil exits when reverse mapping one of the snippet results in "No tmms on the blade" error
bugs.symptoms: DNATutil exits with the error "dnatutil: No tmms on the blade."
bugs.conditions: A DNAT state log entry that is interpreted as invalid
bugs.impact: DNATUtil will not be able to parse the whole log file for reverse mappings
bugs.workaround: remove the DNAT state chunk that produces the error.
bugs.fix: DNATUtil will continue on even if it encounters an error. It will report the error but not exit.

bugs.title: "Any IPv4 or IPv6" choice in sweep attack has atypical definition
bugs.symptoms: OLH does not convey the function of Any IPv4 or Any IPv6 choice in single endpoint sweep attack configuration.
bugs.conditions: When one of these options is chosen, the configuration does not behave as expected and detect "any" traffic.
bugs.impact: When selected, the endpoint sweep attack detects only traffic "other than TCP, UDP, ICMP, or IGMP."
bugs.fix: In the DoS Device Protection configuration for a Single Endpoint Sweep attack, the packet types "Any IPv4" and "Any IPv6" do not actually apply to all IPv4 and IPv6 traffic. Rather, these categories apply to any traffic other than TCP, UDP, ICMP, or IGMP. This has been clarified in the system online help.

bugs.title: ASM and APM on same virtual server caused Set-Cookie header modification done by ASM not honored by APM websso.
bugs.symptoms: With APM and ASM configured on the same virtual server, cookie validation on ASM could modify the Set-Cookie header sent by the application server or inject another Set-Cookie header. APM websso module does not honor the Set-Cookie modification, nor the injection. ASM subsequently causes the connection to reset.
bugs.conditions: With APM and ASM configured on the same virtual server, if cookie validation on ASM modifies the Set-Cookie header sent by the application server or injects another Set-Cookie header, then APM websso module does not honor this.
bugs.impact: Connection reset on the above condition.
bugs.workaround: Use layered virtual servers with an iRule virtual command to send traffic from the ASM virtual server to an APM virtual server with ARP disabled instead of having everything on one virtual server.
bugs.fix: The APM websso module is modified to handle an ASM use case. Now the websso reparses the HTTP 401 response header from the server at the client side in addition to the current parsing at server-side processing. With this fix any Set-Cookie modification or addition by ASM is sent to server in the response to 401 header.

bugs.title: PB4300 blade doesn't disaggregate ESP traffic based on IP addresses in hareware
bugs.symptoms: PB4300 blade tries to disaggregate the ESP traffic based on the IPsec ESP Security Parameter Index (SPI) value in hardware. But the blade used doesnâ€™t have that capability, which causes ESP traffic being sent to one HSB and results in throughput degradation.
bugs.conditions: When PB4300 receives ESP traffic.
bugs.impact: Throughput degradation.
bugs.fix: The PB4300 blade now uses IP addresses to disaggregate ESP traffic in hardware, so throughput is no longer impacted.

bugs.title: Synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash
bugs.symptoms: There is a synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes causes TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.
bugs.conditions: AVR is provisioned or report statistic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release corrects a synchronization problem in AVR lookups that sometimes caused TMM and other daemons, such as the Enforcer, to crash.

bugs.title: XML validation files are not correctly imported/upgraded
bugs.symptoms: XML validation files are not assigned to the correct XML profiles after upgrade/policy import.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned XML profiles with XML validation files assigned
bugs.impact: XML validation files are not assigned to the correct XML profiles.
bugs.fix: XML validation files are now assigned to the correct XML profiles.

bugs.title: Setting log level for ZoneRunner has no effect.
bugs.symptoms: Modifying the log level for ZoneRunner does not change the log level. This is a bug in the handling of the log level change message within ZoneRunner
bugs.conditions: If a GTM config sync is also occurring, the GTM can get into a state where all queries go unanswered until the GTM config loads and/or the BIND zones load.
bugs.impact: BIND queries go unanswered until the zone is loaded into BIND.
bugs.workaround: Assuming that the desired log level is "DEBUG", the following steps will force zonerunner to log debug messages to /var/tmp/zrd.out On the BIG-IP system: touch /service/zrd/debug bigstart restart zrd

bugs.title: TMM core might occur if FLOW_INIT iRule attached to Virtual server
bugs.symptoms: TMM core is seen when FLOW_INIT iRule is applied to Virtual server for global rule
bugs.conditions: When logging is enabled and a FLOW_INIT rule is applied and the system gets packets but cannot find virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM core and restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no work around
bugs.fix: Added check for NULL context in connflow to avoid rare crash bug.

bugs.title: Use of cookie hash persist, local cache entry may not removed upon connection close.
bugs.symptoms: Orphaned persistence record.
bugs.conditions: Cookie hash persistence is configured. No persistence record exists. The connection is assigned to a tmm thread that doesn't own the record.
bugs.impact: Possible persistence records discrepancy between tmm threads.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Dereferenced local cache entry is now always removed on connection close.

bugs.title: Heavy memory usage while using FastL4/BIGTCP virtual server with HTTP profile
bugs.symptoms: When a FastL4 virtual server with HTTP profile is used, certain kinds of traffic may cause huge memory growth and result in out-of-memory situation.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 virtual server with HTTP profile. -- Handles HTTP cloaking traffic that starts up as HTTP and then switches over to non-HTTP data
bugs.impact: Memory growth could grow unbounded due to lack of flow control. This may lead to out of memory conditions eventually. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can perform one of the following actions: -- If the HTTP profile is required, use a standard virtual server rather than performance (FastL4) type. -- If the HTTP profile is not required, you can remove the HTTP profile from the virtual server. -- To process connections that change from HTTP to non-HTTP, create an iRule that uses HTTP::disable after the first HTTP_REQUEST or HTTP_RESPONSE boundary can be identified.
bugs.fix: If the FastL4 virtual server with HTTP profile handles HTTP cloaking traffic that starts up as HTTP and then switches over to non-HTTP data then a http-transparent profile can now be added to the FastL4 virtual. Then the following workaround must be implemented so memory growth no longer increases unbounded due to lack of flow control. Workaround -- Use FastL4 and HTTP-Transparent profile combinations instead. -- Set the http-transparent profile attribute enforcement.pipeline to 'pass-through'. This allows the HTTP filter to run in 'passthrough' mode which avoids the excessive memory consumption.

bugs.title: Manager Role inconsistency between GUI and TMSH
bugs.symptoms: Users configured with the 'Manager' role who log into GUI cannot create or the following Secure Web Gateway objects: -- Secure Web Gateway :: Applications. -- Secure Web Gateway :: Application Filters. -- Secure Web Gateway :: URL Categories.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Users configured with the 'Manager' role log into GUI.
bugs.impact: User is unable to use GUI to as 'Manager' to create or delete the objects.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: Permissions have been corrected on the GUI, and the 'Manager' role now operates as expected with Secure Web Gateway objects.

bugs.title: Introduce a new sys db variable to control number of merges per second of Rate Tracker library.
bugs.symptoms: The accuracy of the rate limit for the Sweep and Flood vectors is affected by the number of merges per second in Rate Tracker library.
bugs.conditions: When sweep and flood vector is enabled in AFM module.
bugs.impact: No way to control number of merges per second of Rate Tracker, which could help in Rate Tracker libray accuracy.
bugs.fix: Introduce a new sys db variable to control number of merges per second of Rate Tracker library.

bugs.title: Network Access can be interrupted if second NIC is disconnected
bugs.symptoms: Networks Access connection breaks if second NIC disconnects. Both NICs should be connected to same network. This happens for a specific Network Access configuration.
bugs.conditions: Network Access configuration: * Full tunnel with "Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection" set to true. * Split tunneling with "Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection" set to true, Address space is 0.0.0.0/0. Client with 2 NICs both connected to the same network.
bugs.impact: NA is interrupted.

bugs.title: Unable to modify 'gtm region region-members' via iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: Unable to modify 'gtm region region-members' via iControl REST. The system posts error 400 Invalid region type messages.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to modify gtm region region-members via iControl REST.
bugs.impact: Unable to use iControl REST to configure this portion of the GTM/DNS configuration.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to modify GTM Regions.
bugs.fix: You can once again modify GTM Regions via iControl REST.
bugs.behavior: Escaping use has changed to more closely match tmsh command. v11.x "regionMembers":[{"name": "state\ \"US/New Mexico\""}] v13.x "regionMembers":[{"name": "state\ US/New Mexico"}]

bugs.title: Recompile iControl, zrd and TS when upgrading BIND
In FIPS HA setup, peer may use the FIPS public-handle instead of the FIPS private-handle
bugs.symptoms: In FIPS HA setup when the FIPS private handle of x.key on Device A is a FIPS public handle of x.key on Device B, Device B (the HA peer) gets the configuration from Device A and operates as if the handle is correct because the modulus matches, but it actually is the public-handle and not the private-handle.
bugs.conditions: FIPS HA setup and FIPS private handle of x.key on Device A is a FIPS public handle of x.key on Device B.
bugs.impact: With this configuration, when the device fails over, it can lead to traffic failure. This occurs because TMM tries to use the public-handle when it should be using the private-handle.
bugs.fix: FIPS HA peer verifies the FIPS handle type to confirm that it uses only the private FIPS handles.

bugs.title: mcpd sometimes exits while doing a file sync operation
bugs.symptoms: mcpd exits randomly. If mcpd debug logging is enabled, the system might post an operation similar to the following: Received request message from connection 0x5fe47008 (user %cmi-mcpd-peer-/Common/LNJDCZ-VPN1.example): query_all { sync_file { sync_file_file_to_sync "/var/apm/localdb/mysql_bkup.sql" sync_file_target_dg "/Common/HA_Rhodes_APM" sync_file_postprocess_action "/usr/libexec/localdb_mysql_restore.sh" sync_file_originator "/Common/LNJDCZ-VPN1.example" } }
bugs.conditions: mcpd is performing a file sync.
bugs.impact: Randomly, mcpd exits, triggering a failover.
bugs.fix: Ensured mcpd no longer exits while performing a file sync.

bugs.title: OSPF: Multiple ECMP default routes not distributed to TMM
bugs.symptoms: TMM route table does not use both ECMP routes for the default route.
bugs.conditions: When using ECMP and OSPF.
bugs.impact: Does not use both equal-cost routes to route traffic.

bugs.title: rsync daemon does not stop listening after configsync-ip set to none
bugs.symptoms: If a device is not in a Device Services Clustering configuration, but has configsync-ip set on its self device object, and this configsync-ip is set to none, an rsync daemon continues to listen on the old configsync-ip.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Device is not in a Device Services Clustering configuration. -- Self device has a configsync-ip set.
bugs.impact: The rsync server may continue to listen even after it is expected that it will not listen.
bugs.fix: The rsync daemon is now shut down properly when the configsync-ip is set to none, and no longer listens on configsync-ip.

bugs.title: AFM DoS Single Endpoint Sweep and Flood Vectors crash TMM under heavy traffic.
bugs.symptoms: With AFM DoS Single Endpoint Sweep and Flood Vectors configured, TMM might crash while processing a huge amount of the configured attack traffic.
bugs.conditions: AFM DoS Single Endpoint Sweep and Flood attack vector is enabled in the AFM module.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure the AFM DoS Single Endpoint Sweep and Flood Vector.
bugs.fix: AFM DoS Single Endpoint Sweep and Flood Vectors now correctly handles traffic so that TMM does not crash.

bugs.title: if window.onload is assigned null, then null should be retrieved
bugs.symptoms: After window.onload=null, non null value is returned from window.onload.
bugs.conditions: Web application that assigns null to window.onload and expects to obtain null in window.onload then.
bugs.impact: Web application logic can be broken.
bugs.fix: After window.unload=null, null is returned by getting value of window.onload;

bugs.title: APM CTU doesn't pick up logs for Machine Certificate Service
bugs.symptoms: CTU report does not contain logs from Machine Certificate Service.
bugs.conditions: When the CTU report is run, it does not contain data in the logs.
bugs.impact: Logs are not available to technical staff
bugs.workaround: You can pick up logs manually from C:\Windows\Temp\logterminal.txt.
bugs.fix: CTU correctly pick ups logs for Machine Cert service.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Rewrite helpers do not work with documents created with createHTMLDocument() call
bugs.symptoms: Result of document.implementation.createHTMLDocument("") lacks some properties (parentWindow,defaultView,etc...) rewrite wrappers are throwing exceptions when trying to access them. Examples of broken wrappers: F5_Inflate/Deflate_domain, F5_Invoke_appendChild.
bugs.conditions: Rewrite helpers failed to access documents created by createHTMLDocument()
bugs.impact: Oracle Web App graphs do not load on pages created by Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { # ID475163: F5_Invoke_submit() breaks forms without action # ID501505: [Portal Access] Lots of our helpers don't work for documents created with createHTMLDocument. set is_475163 0 set is_501505 0 if { [HTTP::uri] contains "1411250302/zenwebclient/web.do?cafWebSesInit=true"} { set is_475163 1 REWRITE::post_process 1 } if { [HTTP::uri] contains "/combined_static_includes_2.js"} { set is_501505 1 REWRITE::post_process 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { if { $is_475163 == 1 } { set location [string first \ {<form id="form_client} \ [REWRITE::payload]] if { $location > 0 } { REWRITE::payload replace [expr $location + 5] 0 { action="" } set is_475163 0 } } if { $is_501505 == 1 } { set location [string first \ {createHTMLDocument("");} \ [REWRITE::payload]] if { $location > 0 } { REWRITE::payload replace [expr $location + 23 ] 0 {f.parentWindow=top;} set is_501505 0 } } }
bugs.fix: Rewrite helpers should work with documents created by document.implementation.createHTMLDocument("")

bugs.title: If a very large number of monitors is configured, bigd can run out of file descriptors when it is restarted.
bugs.symptoms: When using a very large number of monitors, bigd may run out of file descriptors when it is restarted.
bugs.conditions: A system with a large number of monitors configured.
bugs.impact: bigd cores and gets into a restart loop; monitors no longer work properly. The ltm log might contain error messages similar to the following: socket error: Too many open files.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of monitors on the system.
