bugs.fix: bigd no longer runs out of file descriptors during restart when using a very large number of monitors.

bugs.title: Very large configuration can cause transaction timeouts on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: Messages with 'end_transaction message timeout on connection 0x5ea9a9c8 (user mcpd-primary)' in them in the ltm log after a secondary blade is inserted or restarted.
bugs.conditions: A multi-bladed system with a very large configuration that takes more than a minute to transfer to secondary blades.
bugs.impact: mcpd's transaction does not complete and the configuration is not loaded properly.
bugs.fix: Increased the transaction timeout to accommodate very large configuration transfers.

bugs.title: Spurious Configuration Synchronizations
bugs.symptoms: Some items (for example, Incidents) were considered to be config elements that require synchronization when their status changes (such as being read), but are not actually synchronized in a device group.
bugs.conditions: Event Correlation Incidents occur and are read by the user while in a manual sync device group for ASM.
bugs.impact: The synchronization state of a device group erroneously changes to "Pending"
bugs.fix: Items that are not synchronized across a device group no longer cause changes to the synchronization state.

bugs.title: Core file appears on vCMP after restarting the primary blade twice
bugs.symptoms: pccd cores on vCMP after restarting the primary blade twice.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: 1) bigstart restart on primary blade. 2) waiting until this blade load (and become secondary). 3) bigstart restart on new primary blade.
bugs.impact: Brief disruption of firewall rule updates.
bugs.workaround: Pccd should recover and functional normally after coring. No extra action is needed.

bugs.title: TMM crash in RESOLV::lookup for multi-RR TXT record
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a specific ASSERT-based backtrace.
bugs.conditions: Requires an LTM listener with an iRule that has a RESOLV::lookup command querying for a TXT record and receiving multiple RRs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes due to the behavior of the LTM listener with an iRule that has a RESOLV::lookup command when parsing its return values.

bugs.title: System does not prevent low quality JPEGs from optimizing to higher quality (becoming larger) does not work when AAM image optimization enabled and JPEG quality in policy is higher than JPEGs on OWS.
bugs.symptoms: The test to prevent JPEGs on OWS with low quality from being 'optimized' to higher quality (if the quality setting in WAM policy is higher than in the file on OWS) is not working.
bugs.conditions: AAM image optimization enabled and the JPEG quality in AAM policy is higher than the JPEGs on OWS.
bugs.impact: image optimization can make the file significantly bigger.
bugs.workaround: Add the line below to /service/wamd/settings (create the file if it does not exist): export WAMD_OPT_IMAGES_NO_BIGGER=all Note this will return the original file if the 'optimized' one comes out bigger: subtly different behavior than making any other requested changes but leaving the quality the same as the file on OWS.
bugs.fix: The test to prevent low quality JPEGs from optimizing to higher quality (becoming larger) is fixed.

bugs.title: Selenium is not detected by headless mechanism when using client version without server
bugs.symptoms: DoSL7 Proactive Bot Defense (Block requests from suspicious browsers) detects selenium when the selenium server is running and a listener has opened on one of specific ports.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when ASM is provisioned with proactive bot defense enabled, when accessing the page for a first time.
bugs.impact: If a bot is running selenium client package only it is not being blocked by DoSL7 Proactive Bot Defense mechanism.
bugs.fix: Selenium detection mechanism has improved and if a bot uses FF or Chrome selenium driver it is detected by PBD's javascript code via checking existence of required chrome plugins and FF webdriver.

bugs.title: Cannot delete keys/certificates whose names start with 0 (zero).
bugs.symptoms: Cannot delete keys/certificates whose names start with 0 (zero).
bugs.conditions: Trying to delete a key/certificate who names start with 0.
bugs.impact: Trying to delete a key/certificate whose name starts with 0, the GUI shows the confirm delete page, but there is no key or certificate listed, and after clicking delete again, the system displays the key/certificate list page, with the key/certificate still there.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh or iControl to delete keys/certificates whose names start with 0 (zero).

bugs.title: BWC rate limit instability on large number of live dynamic flows
bugs.symptoms: max-user-rate configuration changes constantly on large number of live dynamic flows.
bugs.conditions: This issue appears very intermittently.
bugs.impact: This results in a lower-than-expected total rate.
bugs.workaround: Avoid rapid constant configuration changes on live traffic. Restart tmm to recover.

bugs.title: HA failsafe triggering on standby device does not clear next active for that device.
bugs.symptoms: An HA failsafe triggering on a standby device that is marked as next active for a traffic group does not clear the next active setting for that device. This leaves the system in a state in which the device designated as next active cannot take over for the active device in the case of a failure.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) setup with two or more devices in a device trust and device group. -- HA failsafes are configured on one or more devices in the device group. -- The HA failsafes are triggered on a device that is currently in the standby state and designated next active for a traffic group.
bugs.impact: A device marked as next active for a traffic group with a triggered HA failsafe does not take over a traffic group in the case of a failure on the active switch.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to force the device in question offline, so that another device is marked as next active.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly removes the next active setting for a device when it is in standby mode and an HA failsafe triggers. This causes a new device to be picked as next active if one is in standby mode and capable of running the traffic group.

bugs.title: TMM may experience an outage when an iRule fails in LB_SELECTED.
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule fails in LB_SELECTED, it is possible for TMM to crash. The TMM failure is an intermittent, timing-related issue..
bugs.conditions: Using iRules with a rule for when LB_SELECTED is operating on a node/pool member.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Add a sys db tunable to make Sweep and Flood vectors be rate-limited per-TMM process
bugs.symptoms: There is a need for Sweep and Flood vectors to be very accurate (+-5%). To ensure that Sweep and Flood can be very accurate the system needs a mode in which the Sweep and Flood vectors work per-TMM process. In this case the traffic must be very well distributed for it to be effective. BIG-IP systems now has a sys db tunable which is: dos.globalsflimits which is true by default. If the tunable is set to false, then the Sweep and Flood vectors work per-TMM process. The limits that have been configured are divided equally among the various TMM processes, and because the traffic is well-distributed among the TMM processes, the system will get close to the limits specified.
bugs.conditions: When Sweep and Flood vector is enabled in AFM module.
bugs.impact: If the db variable is changed to false, the incoming traffic must be well distributed.
bugs.fix: Add a sys db tunable to make Sweep and Flood vectors be rate-limited per-TMM process.

bugs.title: MAC client components do not log version numbers in log file.
bugs.symptoms: Some client components do not log version numbers in the log file.
bugs.conditions: Mac client components.
bugs.impact: Lack of version numbers in the log file.
bugs.fix: Client components for Mac now log version numbers in log files.

bugs.title: Qkview may store information in the wrong format
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new monitor, some information may be stored in the wrong format.
bugs.conditions: Create a new monitor. Run qkview.
bugs.impact: Occasionally, some information stored for the new monitor will be in the incorrect format.
bugs.fix: Monitor information is now stored in the correct format.

bugs.title: Qkview may store information in the wrong format
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new monitor, some information may be stored in the wrong format.
bugs.conditions: Create a new monitor. Run qkview.
bugs.impact: Occasionally, some information stored for the new monitor will be in the incorrect format.
bugs.fix: Monitor information is now stored in the correct format.

bugs.title: Hash Cookie Persistence interaction with persistence iRules
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server is configured with fallback persistence, which looks up information from a session table (e.g., source address persistence) and the cookie is associated with an iRule that performs cookie insert, periodically TMM uses the default cookie name instead of the cookie name set in the iRule.
bugs.conditions: - Fallback persistence configured. - Using 'persist cookie insert' with custom cookie name in iRule.
bugs.impact: The cookie inserted by TMM will switch between the configured cookie name and the default cookie name (e.g., BIGip<cookie_name><pool_name>Server). Persistence may fail to work correctly when the persist iRule command overrides from cookie to hash-cookie persistence.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Archiving EC cert/key fails with error 'EC keys are incompatible for Webserver/EM/iQuery.'
bugs.symptoms: When archiving cert/key via GUI, the following error message is displayed : 'EC keys are incompatible for Webserver/EM/iQuery.'
bugs.conditions: When archiving cert/key via GUI.
bugs.impact: Intermittently, an error is received when trying to archive key or certificates via GUI.
bugs.fix: iControl stores the mode info and set a default value to it, so no error is reported..

bugs.title: DTLS fragments do not work for ClientHello message.
bugs.symptoms: DTLS fragments do not work for ClientHello message.
bugs.conditions: DTLS ClientHello splits into multiple fragments.
bugs.impact: Both first handshake and renegotiation are affected.
bugs.fix: DTLS ClientHello fragments are now handled.

bugs.title: Connectivity and traffic interruption issues caused by a stuck HSB transmit ring
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP can experience sudden and permanent traffic interruption, impacting all traffic through TMM.
bugs.conditions: With TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) enabled, it is possible to fill up the High-Speed Bridge (HSB) transmit ring, resulting in a stuck transmit ring. The exact conditions under which this occurs is unknown, but it requires sudden transmission of a number of large packets that require TSO in order to result in a full transmit ring.
bugs.impact: The HSB's transmit ring becomes stuck. This requires a TMM restart in order to clear.
bugs.workaround: Disable TSO. This can be done using the following steps: 1. tmsh modify sys db tm.tcpsegmentationoffload value disable 2. bigstart restart tmm. If TSO is not disabled, three related fixes are needed to fully address the issue: -- ID 466260, covered in SOL15953: TMM may produce a core file with the 'Assertion we always have room in tx ring! failed' error message. -- ID 502238, covered in SOL16736: The BIG-IP system may lose connectivity and fail to process all traffic through TMM if the HSB is overloaded. -- ID 509782, covered in SOL16780: The BIG-IP system may drop TSO packets. The Solutions are available here: -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/900/sol15953.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16736.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16780.html
bugs.fix: Three related fixes are needed to fully address the issue: -- ID 466260, covered in SOL15953: TMM may produce a core file with the 'Assertion we always have room in tx ring! failed' error message. -- ID 502238, covered in SOL16736: The BIG-IP system may lose connectivity and fail to process all traffic through TMM if the HSB is overloaded. -- ID 509782, covered in SOL16780: The BIG-IP system may drop TSO packets. The Solutions are available here: -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/900/sol15953.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16736.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16780.html

bugs.title: Large post requests may fail using form based SSO.
bugs.symptoms: SSOV2 modifies the payload for big post requests and since the server does not understand this, so all such transactions fail.
bugs.conditions: Large post requests using form based SSO.
bugs.impact: SSOV2 is a very common use case for APM. Many applications are configured with SSOV2. Any large post in such case will fail.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The fix essentially does not modify the payload so the applications have no problem.

bugs.title: Make the RateTracker tier3 initialization number less variant.
bugs.symptoms: Sweep and Flood vectors may exceed configured rate limit values by 10%-30$.
bugs.conditions: When Sweep and Flood vector is enabled in AFM module.
bugs.impact: Sweep and Flood attack detection at higher than configured levels.
bugs.fix: An optimization was made to Rate Tracker that makes attack detection more accurate.

bugs.title: Network Access connection might reset for large proxy.pac files.
bugs.symptoms: Network Access connection might reset when large proxy.pac files are configured in the access policy.
bugs.conditions: MAC Edge client, browsers, Network Access, large proxy.pac file.
bugs.impact: Network Access connection might reset.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the proxy.pac file size to be less than 10 KB.
bugs.fix: Network Access connection does not reset if a large proxy.pac file is configured.

bugs.title: After enabling a blade/HA member, pool members are marked down because monitoring starts too soon.
bugs.symptoms: The external monitoring daemon (bigd) sends monitoring traffic before tmm is ready to receive those responses. The response traffic is routed to a tmm on another blade/HA member. This tmm responds to the server with an ICMP "Unreachable" message. Meanwhile, the originating tmm on the new blade/HA member marks the pool member "down" because it never received the server's response.
bugs.conditions: Start with at least 1 blade enabled in a chassis or one HA member configured, and pass traffic constantly through a virtual server with a monitor-enabled pool attached. Then, enable a new blade in the cluster or a new HA member.
bugs.impact: Some packets are lost for several seconds. It can be longer depending on the total number of pool members.
bugs.workaround: Before adding a new blade to a chassis or a member to the HA configuration that is actively processing traffic, temporarily remove the monitor(s) from the pool. Once the new blade/HA member is up, manually add the monitor(s) back to the pool.
bugs.fix: When a VIPRION blade or BIG-IP HA member comes on-line, the bigd process on the blade/HA member no longer starts health monitors prematurely, which could have caused some monitored objects to be marked down incorrectly.
bugs.behavior: The external monitoring daemon (bigd) no longer sends monitoring traffic while the blade (cluster member) is offline or disabled, or while the HA member (chassis or appliance) is offline (including forced offline).

bugs.title: Mirrored connections on standby device do not get closed when Verified Accept is enabled
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, the BIG-IP may cause mirrored connections on the standby device to persist.
bugs.conditions: - Mirror enabled on the Virtual server - Verified accept enabled on the TCP profile
bugs.impact: Resource leak on the standby device which could cause an outage
bugs.workaround: Do not enable verified accept on mirrored flows.
bugs.fix: Mirrored connections to the standby device will now be properly closed on the standby.

bugs.title: The tmm may core if the DHCP virtual is reconfigured while the existing virtual has recently (<30s) been used to carry DHCP traffic.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core.
bugs.conditions: Have a functioning DHCP virtual that has been used to process DHCP packets. Reconfigure the virtual within 30s of the last packet.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: The tmm may core if the DHCP virtual is reconfigured while the existing virtual has recently (<30s) been used to carry DHCP traffic.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core.
bugs.conditions: Have a functioning DHCP virtual that has been used to process DHCP packets. Reconfigure the virtual within 30s of the last packet.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Improve reliability of LOP/LBH firmware updates
bugs.symptoms: Certain F5 appliances and blades implement the Always On Management functionality via a LOP (Lights Out Processor) or LBH (Lights Out Processor/Backplane Microcontroller Hybrid) device. Under rare conditions, if a critical kernel event occurs while the LOP/LBH firmware is being updated to a newer version, the LOP/LBH firmware image may become corrupted on the LOP/LBH device.
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur on the following F5 Network appliances and blades: -- BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series, 5000-/7000-series, 10000-/12000-series appliances. -- VIPRION B2100, B2150, B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: If the LOP/LBH firmware becomes corrupted, the LOP/LBH device does not function properly, affecting critical chassis-management functionality such as identification of platform details including a blade's current slot in the chassis, obtaining current license state, and monitoring of chassis health information.
bugs.fix: LOP/LBH firmware updates are protected against rare corruption by critical kernel events.

bugs.title: Traffic intermittently dropped in syncookie mode, especially when hardware syncookie is on
bugs.symptoms: In certain corner cases, BIG-IP software rejects valid SYN-Cookie responses due to incorrect hardware algorithm masking on the software side.
bugs.conditions: This issue appears only on hardware-SYN-Cookie-capable platforms when running the hardware SYN-Cookie algorithm.
bugs.impact: Intermittent connection failures.
bugs.workaround: Run software SYN-Cookie algorithm. Use the DB variable. This makes sure software is running correct generation and validation algorithm.
bugs.fix: Traffic is now handled correctly in certain corner cases involving hardware syncookies.

bugs.title: Deleting files and file object references in a single transaction might cause validation errors
bugs.symptoms: Deleting files and file object references in a single transaction can lead to a validation error. This might occur during device group configuration sync, an iApp, a tmsh cli transaction, or an iControl transaction.
bugs.conditions: A file object is deleted in the same transaction that its references are also deleted.
bugs.impact: This can cause an invalid validation error, including during a config sync.
bugs.workaround: In the case of iControl and tmsh, file object references must first be deleted/removed in a separate transaction. In the case of config sync, perform a full sync.
bugs.fix: File objects properly resolve references within the transaction, so there are no validation errors when deleting files and file object references in a single transaction.

bugs.title: Incoming SYN generates unexpected ACK when connection cannot be recycled
bugs.symptoms: Incoming SYN causes the BIG-IP system to generate ACK instead of SYN-ACK.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when the following conditions are met: - IP addresses and ports of SYN match an existing connection; - Sequence number of the SYN is greater than 2^31+ from previously sent FIN; - Existing connection is in TIME_WAIT state; - Virtual server has time_wait_recycle enabled.
bugs.impact: Client will generate RST and connection must be re-tried.
bugs.workaround: Set time-wait-timeout to 1 millisecond per SOL12673.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system will no longer generate an ACK to incoming SYNs which match an existing connection that cannot be recycled.

bugs.title: clientside and serverside command crashes TMM
bugs.symptoms: When the parking command is used inside clientside or serverside, tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: Parking command, e.g. table command, is used inside clientside or serverside command.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Move the parking command outside clientside or serverside command.
bugs.fix: Parking command can run inside clientside and serverside. The client side connection must exist when clientside command runs; the server side connection must exist when serverside command runs; otherwise the clientside and serverside commands fail.
bugs.behavior: clientside and serverside command error out if client side or server side connection does not exist at the time the command runs. Here is an example of where this might occur: clientside { SSL::disable }. This script fails if the client side connection does not exist. To work correctly, change the script to: SSL::disable clientside.

bugs.title: REST API hangs due to icrd startup issues
bugs.symptoms: The symptoms are that iControl REST requests can go un-responded or come back with bad responses.
bugs.conditions: icrd starts much before restjavad
bugs.impact: Unusable REST API.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to restart the icrd service after ascertaining that restjavad is running - 'bigstart status restjavad' followed by 'bigstart restart icrd'.
bugs.fix: Now the icrd service will wait until the restjavad service is completely up and responding.

bugs.title: Deleting an in-use custom policy template
bugs.symptoms: If a user tries to delete a custom policy template while there are still security policies in the system that were created from that template, the delete will fail. This also leaves the custom template in an unusable state that can neither be used to create further Policies nor can it ever be deleted.
bugs.conditions: A security policy exists on the system that was created from a custom template. The user then tries to delete the template before removing the policy from the system.
bugs.impact: The custom template becomes unusable for creating new policies, and cannot be deleted even after there are no longer any policies created from it left on the system.
bugs.workaround: Contact support for a script that will disassociate all user defined policy templates from existing policies. This will allow any user defined template to be successfully deleted.
bugs.fix: If you fail to delete a custom policy template because an existing security policy refers to it, it no longer leaves the custom policy template in an unusable state.

bugs.title: Unable get response from virtual server after node flapping
bugs.symptoms: If persistence is used, and a node is marked down and then up in quick succession (less than about 7 seconds), then persistence may act inconsistently.
bugs.conditions: Persistence, rapid node flapping, new connection (via a TMM with an existing connection) after node has been re-marked as up.
bugs.impact: Persistence may act inconsistently (meaning, not all connections expected to persist to a server will do so). In certain circumstances, requests may hang (the client is connected, waiting for a response).
bugs.fix: The system now deletes a persist entry from all peer TMMs when it is deleted in any TMM, so no conflicts occur.

bugs.title: Make the RateTracker threshold a constant
bugs.symptoms: Dynamic detection threshold may impact Sweep and Flood detection rate accuracy under high traffic conditions.
bugs.conditions: When Sweep and Flood is enabled in AFM module.
bugs.impact: Some Sweep and Flood functionality might not provide sufficient detection rate accuracy.
bugs.fix: The RateTracker threshold is now a constant, which improves detection rate accuracy.

bugs.title: clientside and serverside command crashes TMM
bugs.symptoms: When parking command is used inside clientside or serverside, tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: Parking command, e.g., the table command, is used inside clientside or serverside command.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Move the parking command outside clientside or serverside command.
bugs.fix: Parking command can run inside clientside and serverside. The client side connection must exist when clientside command runs; the server side connection must exist when serverside command runs; otherwise the clientside and serverside commands fail.

bugs.title: Excessive MPI net traffic can cause tmm panics on chassis systems
bugs.symptoms: Excessive MPI net traffic can cause tmm panics on chassis systems.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on chassis systems with excessive internal traffic resulting from abnormal load distribution or excessive session DB usage. The session DB usage can be the result of modules or of custom iRules that store session data.
bugs.impact: Temporary outage and possible failover when using HA. The source conditions will also continue on the new active device, which can cause repeated failovers. When this occurs, the tmm logs will contain messages similar to: notice MPI stream: connection to node 127.20.3.24 expired for reason: TCP retransmit timeout
bugs.workaround: If affected by this when using iRules to create custom keys and data, this can be partially mitigated by consolidating multiple keys and using smaller key lengths as possible. This is affected by the amount of data stored as well, but large keys can exacerbate the issue.
bugs.fix: Excessive MPI net traffic no longer causes tmm panics on chassis systems.

bugs.title: FPS malicious words doesn't trigger alert when ignore list is defined
bugs.symptoms: When the malicious words ignore list is not empty, all malicious words are ignored, whether or not they are on the ignore list.
bugs.conditions: FPS malicious words feature is enabled and a words is configured to be ignored.
bugs.impact: No malicious words alerts are sent for that page.
bugs.workaround: Empty the malicious words ignore list.
bugs.fix: Ignore list now works correctly.

bugs.title: XML validation files are broken after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: XML validation files are not assigned to the correct XML profiles after upgrade/policy import. The upgrade fails with the following signature in /var/log/asm: crit perl[15504]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::DbUtils::insert_data_to_table): Row 431 of table PLC.PL_CONTENT_PROFILE_VALUE_METACHARS is missing profile_id (277) -- skipping F5::ImportExportPolicy::Binary
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned, XML profiles with XML validation files assigned. This can trigger on upgrade to 11.6.0.
bugs.impact: XML validation files are not assigned to the correct XML profiles.
bugs.fix: XML validation files are now assigned to the correct XML profiles.

bugs.title: Under heavy load, hardware crypto queues may become unavailable.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is under heavy load, it may erroneously determine that the hardware crypto queues are unavailable and trigger an HA failover event.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system under heavy load and using hardware crypto.
bugs.impact: HA failover. You might see messages similar to the following: -- crit tmm2[22560]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec cn-crypto-2 queue is stuck. -- warning sod[6892]: 01140029:4: HA crypto_failsafe_t cn-crypto-2 fails action is failover. -- notice sod[6892]: 010c0052:5: Standby for traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP system now performs an extra check to determine whether the crypto hardware queues are available.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when unable to allocate large amount of provisioned memory
bugs.symptoms: TMM panics and core dumps when unable to allocate the full amount of provisioned memory for each TMM instance.
bugs.conditions: The situation may occur when TMM starts (or restarts) while a process is still holding into large amounts of memory and TMM is unable to allocate the provisioned memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The fix is a change in the TMM startup process

bugs.title: Persistence, connection limits and HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect may result in RST
bugs.symptoms: Client connections to a virtual server with persistence, connection limits, and an iRule that issues an HTTP response may receive a RST with a cause of "pmbr enqueue failed" even though connection queuing is not enabled.
bugs.conditions: This can happen if the connection makes an HTTP request and an iRule directly responds to the first request on the connection. A future request on that TCP connection would be reset if it is persisted to a pool member that is at its connection limit. The iRule would use HTTP::respond (without "connection close") or HTTP::redirect.
bugs.impact: Clients may receive a RST and fail to connect to an available pool member under some traffic patterns.
bugs.workaround: If using HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect in an iRule, change to HTTP::respond with the "Connection close" option in order to force the connection to terminate and the client to start a new connection after the redirect is sent.
bugs.fix: Persistence, connection limits and HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect no longer result in RST.

bugs.title: After network access is established browser sometimes receives truncated proxy.pac file
bugs.symptoms: On MAC OSX platform, After network access is established, poxy.pac received by the browser is truncated.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if proxy.pac file is larger than 65535 bytes (~65 KB).
bugs.impact: Large proxy.pac file might not be downloaded or might be truncated.
bugs.workaround: Reduce proxy.pac file size so that merge file is less than ~65 KB.
bugs.fix: Merged (by F5 tunnel server) proxy.pac is now NOT truncated when sent to the browser even if its size is greater than ~65 KB.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when cloned packet incorrectly marked for TSO
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores
bugs.conditions: 1. Clone pool configured 2. Clone MTU > Client or Server MTU 3. tm.tcpsegmentationoffload db var in "disable" state 4. TSO enabled in client or server side interface 5. TSO disabled in clone interface
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove the configured clone pool
bugs.fix: Prevent TMM crash due to cloned packet incorrectly marked for TSO.

bugs.title: SSL persistence may cause connection resets
bugs.symptoms: If SSL persistence is enabled, and the resulting connection does not use SSL (that is, it is plaintext), the connection may be reset.
bugs.conditions: SSL persistence is enabled on a virtual that does not use SSL.
bugs.impact: The connection is reset.
bugs.fix: SSL persistence no longer cause the connection to be reset with non-SSL traffic.

bugs.title: SMTP monitor fails on multi line greeting banner in SMTP server
bugs.symptoms: SMTP monitor fails
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a multi line greeting banner is configured in SMTP server.
bugs.impact: SMTP monitor fails.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, configure a single line greeting banner in SMTP server.
bugs.fix: SMTP monitor succeeds with multi line greeting banner in SMTP server.

bugs.title: Intermittent JavaScript failure on Safari on Macintosh computer or device.
bugs.symptoms: On first page load, JavaScript encryption occasionally fails due to a bug in Safari's JavaScript interpreter.
bugs.conditions: Open protected page in Safari on a Macintosh computer or device.
bugs.impact: Protection fails.
bugs.workaround: Install 11.6.0 hotfix 4 or later
bugs.fix: FPS client-side operation supports improved handling of protected pages in Safari on iOS and OSX.

bugs.title: Memory leak can occur when there is a compressed response, and abnormal termination of the connection
bugs.symptoms: Memory utilization grows over time.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the BIG-IP system sends a compressed response, and an abnormal termination of the connection occurs.
bugs.impact: Memory leak in TMM that grows over time.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuration of Application DoS with Client-side mitigation.
bugs.fix: A memory leak has been fixed that occurred when there was a compressed response and an abnormal termination of the connection.

bugs.title: BGP cannot redistribute IPv4 routes learned from OSPFv3.
bugs.symptoms: OSPFv3 Route redistribution to BGP does not work.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system with BGP and OSPFv3 configured. -- Route redistribution enabled.
bugs.impact: OSPFv3 is capable of learning IPv4 routes from its neighbors. However, BGP is not redistributing IPv4 routes learned from OSPFv3.
bugs.fix: IPv4 routes learned from OSPFv3 are now correctly redistributed by BGP.

bugs.title: Use 64 bit instead of 10 bit for Rate Tracker library hashing.
bugs.symptoms: Rate Tracker 10 bit hashing may cause inaccurate rate-limits by the Sweep & Flood DoS vectors.
bugs.conditions: When Sweep and Flood vector is enabled in AFM module.
bugs.impact: Impact to Sweep and Flood detection rate accuracy.
bugs.fix: The system now uses 64 bit instead of 10 bit for Rate Tracker hashing, which results in more accuracy in attack detection and mitigation.

bugs.title: Statistics profiles cannot be configured along with HTTP transparent profile on the same virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: Statistics profiles cannot be configured along with HTTP transparent profile on the same virtual server.
bugs.conditions: HTTP transparent profile is attached to a virtual server. Statistics profile now cannot be attached to the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: Only a Statistics profile or an HTTP transparent profile may be assigned to a single virtual server.
bugs.fix: The validation logic is now changed so as to allow a Statistics profiles and an HTTP transparent profile to be attached to the same virtual server simultaneously.

bugs.title: TMM core logging from TMM while attempting to connect to remote logging server
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash and coredump while logging to remote logging server.
bugs.conditions: The problem might occur when a log message is created as the result of errors that can occur during log-connection establishment. The crash specifically occurs when an error occurs while attempting to connect to the remote logging server.
bugs.impact: TMM runs out of stack and dumps core. Stack trace shows recursion in errdefs. The system cannot function under these conditions. This is an issue that might occur anytime logs are generated when managing resources that are also used by the logging system itself.
bugs.workaround: Two possible workarounds are available: 1) Create a log filter specifically for message-id :1010235: that either discards or directs such messages to local syslogs. 2) If the problem occurs on TMM startup, disable and then re-enable the corresponding log source once the TMM starts up.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes and coredumps while logging to remote logging server.

bugs.title: Tmm core when switching from interface tunnel to policy based tunnel
bugs.symptoms: When the configuration is changed from interface tunnel to policy based tunnel, tmm crashes. Most likely this is a timing issue where the pnh is not updated while the policy was updated. So the policy_type (policy_interface vs policy_ipsec) mismatched.
bugs.conditions: Traffic passing in the background and change the configuration from interface tunnel to policy based tunnel.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: When switching from interface tunnel to policy based tunnel, tmm cores.

bugs.title: ECDHE_ECDSA and DHE_DSS ciphers do not work with OpenSSL 1.0.1k and later
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP SSL when using ciphers ECDHE_ECDSA and DHE_DSS does not work consistently with OpenSSL clients using OpenSSL versions 1.0.1k or later.
bugs.conditions: When the ciphers used are ECDHE_ECDSA or DHE_DSS, and the OpenSSL clients have versions later than OpenSSL 1.0.1k.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake failed. The OpenSSL clients might encounter a decryption error while reading the server key exchange.
bugs.workaround: Use OpenSSL versions earlier than OpenSSL 1.0.1k.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP SSL now works well with ciphers ECDHE_ECDSA or DHE_DSS with OpenSSL client version OpenSSL 1.0.1k and later.

bugs.title: Some SIP UDP connections are lost immediately after enabling a blade on the Active HA unit.
bugs.symptoms: When a blade is enabled on a cluster while it is actively processing SIP UDP traffic, some packets might be lost.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in an Active HA cluster containing VIPRION B2100 blades with the udp.hash value set to 'ipport' and client-side round robin TMM disaggregation enabled.
bugs.impact: Some SIP UDP traffic packets might be lost.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable a blade in a cluster while the blade is processing SIP UDP traffic.
bugs.fix: Some SIP UDP connections are now retained after enabling a blade on the Active HA unit.
bugs.behavior: As part of this fix, there are two new DB variables: -- arp.gratuitousrate -- arp.gratuitousburst The functionality of these DB variables is documented in K11985: Overview of the arp.gratuitousrate and arp.gratuitousburst database variables :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K11985.

bugs.title: APM sets MRHSession cookie on /cgi/login request from Citrix Receivers
bugs.symptoms: When Citrix Receiver clients send /cgi/login reqeust APM replies with a response containing MRHSession cookie.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix replacement or proxy and Citrix Receiver clients are used.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary cookie value sent to the client.
bugs.fix: APM no longer sets MRHSession cookie on /cgi/login request from Citrix Receivers.

bugs.title: SIP REFER, INFO, and UPDATE request do not trigger SIP_REQUEST or SIP_REQUEST_SEND iRule events
bugs.symptoms: SIP REFER, INFO, and UPDATE requests do not trigger iRule events.
bugs.conditions: The occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Virtual server has a SIP profile. -- Virtual server has iRule(s) containing SIP_REQUEST or SIP_REQUEST_SEND events. -- SIP REFER, INFO, or UPDATE request is received on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: iRule event is not executed.
bugs.fix: SIP REFER, INFO, and UPDATE requests now trigger the SIP_REQUEST and SIP_REQUEST_SEND iRule events. This is the correct behavior.

bugs.title: Configuration upgrade failure due to change in an ASM predefined report name
bugs.symptoms: A configuration load failure occurs after creating an ASM predefined report in a previous version and upgrading.
bugs.conditions: Define scheduled report on top of 'Top alerted URLs' on previous version and upgrade the version. This can trigger on an upgrade to 11.6.0, but is fixed in 11.6.1 and beyond.
bugs.impact: Version upgrade fails, and the BIG-IP system is not usable.
bugs.workaround: Change the '/Common/Top Alerted URLs' reference in the bigip.conf file of the UCS to '/Common/Top Alarmed URLs', and then load the modified UCS.
bugs.fix: A configuration load failure no longer occurs after creating an ASM predefined report in a previous version and upgrading.

bugs.title: BD enforcer updates may be stuck after BD restart
bugs.symptoms: If BD enforcer restarts during an update, the current configuration update will get stuck and no further updates will be performed.
bugs.conditions: BD enforcer restarts during an update.
bugs.impact: The current configuration update will get stuck and no further updates will be performed.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: BD enforcer updates continue to process correctly even after BD restart.

bugs.title: DTLS session should not be closed when it receives a bad record.
bugs.symptoms: According to RFC6347: 4.1.2.7. Handling Invalid Records: 'Unlike TLS, DTLS is resilient in the face of invalid records (e.g., invalid formatting, length, MAC, etc.). In general, invalid records SHOULD be silently discarded, thus preserving the association; however, an error MAY be logged for diagnostic purposes. Implementations which choose to generate an alert instead, MUST generate fatal level alerts to avoid attacks where the attacker repeatedly probes the implementation to see how it responds to various types of error. Note that if DTLS is run over UDP, then any implementation which does this will be extremely susceptible to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks because UDP forgery is so easy. Thus, this practice is NOT RECOMMENDED for such transports.' In the BIG-IP implementation, DTLS chooses to disconnect the session when it receives invalid record.
bugs.conditions: DTLS receives a bad record packet.
bugs.impact: DTLS disconnects the session.
bugs.fix: The system now silently discards all of the invalid records and preserves the association. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: [LTM] [DNS] [LOG] debug log information is logged even when "dnscacheresolver.loglevel" set to higher than debug
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system logs debug log information when 'dnscacheresolver.loglevel' is set to higher than debug. For example, 'dnscacheresolver.loglevel' is set to notice.
bugs.conditions: 'dnscacheresolver.loglevel' log level is set to higher than 'debug'.
bugs.impact: Although it might be difficult to determine the severity of the logging information, there is no known negative impact on the system.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Slow performance with delete_string_class_member in iControl-SOAP
bugs.symptoms: Starting 11.5.1 HF6, deleting ~9000 strings takes about 60 seconds to complete.
bugs.conditions: Delete a large number of strings with the delete_string_class_member API in iControl-SOAP.
bugs.impact: Poor performance and can cause time out
bugs.fix: With the fix in place, deleting ~9000 strings take about 5 seconds.

bugs.title: MS WebService html component doesn't work after rewriting
bugs.symptoms: MS webservice.htc component provides javascript interface for SOAP services for Internet Explorer. It stops working after rewriting through reverse proxy.
bugs.conditions: It works with F5CH=I, and other html components are working through APM too. That means that the issue is with something we change in this file.
bugs.impact: MS WebService component stops working.
bugs.workaround: --- when HTTP_REQUEST { # Downgrade IE compatibility mode set downgrade_ie_compat 0 if { [HTTP::path] contains "PreviewQualitySheet.aspx" } { set UAString [string tolower [HTTP::header User-Agent]] if { ! ($UAString contains "msie 8.") and ! ($UAString contains "msie 7.")} { set downgrade_ie_compat 8 } } # do not rewrite WebService HTML Component # because IE ignores it after rewriting. # patching a few things manually instead set ms_webservice_fix 0 if { [HTTP::uri] ends_with "webservice.htc"} { set ms_webservice_fix 1 HTTP::uri "[HTTP::uri]?F5CH=I" if { [HTTP::version] eq "1.1" } { if { [HTTP::header is_keepalive] } { HTTP::header replace "Connection" "Keep-Alive" } HTTP::version "1.0" } } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { $downgrade_ie_compat > 0 && ! [HTTP::header exists X-UA-Compatible] } { HTTP::header replace "X-UA-Compatible" "IE=$downgrade_ie_compat" } if { $ms_webservice_fix == 1 } { if { [HTTP::header exists "Content-Length"] and \ [HTTP::header "Content-Length"] > 0 and \ [HTTP::header "Content-Length"] <= 1048576 } { HTTP::collect [HTTP::header Content-Length] } else { HTTP::collect 1048576 } } } when HTTP_RESPONSE_DATA { if { $ms_webservice_fix == 1 } { set location [string first \ {if (co.userName == null)} \ [HTTP::payload]] if { $location > 0 } { HTTP::payload replace $location 0 {loc=F5_WrapURL(loc);} } } HTTP::release }
bugs.fix: Microsoft WebService HTML component no longer stops working after rewriting.

bugs.title: Support Citrix HTML5 client bundle in non-default partition
bugs.symptoms: If the Citrix html5 client bundle is configured in non-default partition, users cannot launch HTML5 Citrix application.
bugs.conditions: Citrix html5 client bundle is configured in non-default partition.
bugs.impact: Users cannot launch HTML5 Citrix application.
bugs.workaround: write an iRule that will replace /public/citrix with /Partition/public/citrix
bugs.fix: Now APM supports Citrix HTML5 client bundle in non-default partition

bugs.title: Configure bwc policy category max rate
bugs.symptoms: When category max rate percentage is configured with a low value, for example, a lower value relative to the policy max user rate, some packets might be dropped.
bugs.conditions: The bwc policy is configured as dynamic, with categories. And the category max rate is configured to low value when the policy is being provisioned and mapped to traffic flows.
bugs.impact: The packets in flows using the bwc policy and category may be dropped, the flows mapped to the category might not be able to pass packets.
bugs.workaround: Configure category rate in absolute value and higher value relative to policy max user rate.
bugs.fix: Category max rate percentage is now configured to ensure valid settings.

bugs.title: Citrix receivers cannot authenticate
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receivers does not successfully authenticate when username or password contain ampersand and Storefront is configured without APM gateway.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with Citrix Receivers for all users that have an ampersand in either their username or password.
bugs.impact: These users cannot authenticate.
bugs.workaround: For affected users that have an ampersand in their password, you can ask them to change to a password that does not contain an ampersand.
bugs.fix: Citrix Receivers successfully authenticate when username or password contain ampersand and Storefront is configured without APM gateway.

bugs.title: AFM policies not synced
bugs.symptoms: During configuration sync you notice that AFM policies are not enforced on one of the devices, and you see errors in /var/log/ltm: crit tmm1[25043]: 015e0001:2: pktclass: pktclass_blobs not initialized.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this, but it is encountered during system initialization.
bugs.impact: Policies do not sync and the sync does not recover.

bugs.title: The requested unknown (1936) was not found.
bugs.symptoms: mcpd restarts leaving the message "The requested unknown (1936) was not found"
bugs.conditions: The conditions for this bug are somewhat unknown. Older versions of Big-IP have a simple lookup for display names. This display name table only has a select few configuration items in it, where everything else returns "unknown". So any configuration error that is generated from using a type that is not defined in the table could potentially lead to this error.
bugs.impact: MCPD restarts, causing system-wide restarting of daemons.

bugs.title: High CPU usage when DNS cache resolver sends a large number of DNS queries to the backend name server.
bugs.symptoms: When DNS cache resolver is resolving a DNS query, it might send queries to the backend name server iteratively. If the name server is responding slowly and the cache resolver is sending queries to name servers at a high rate, the CPU usage of the BIG-IP system might be vary high.
bugs.conditions: (1) Configure the cache resolver to have a large value (, for example, 40 KB) for both max-concurrent-queries and max-concurrent-udp. (2) The cache resolver sends queries to the name servers at a high rate. (3) The backend name server is responding slowly to the cache resolver.
bugs.impact: The CPU usage might be extremely high. Site might be unstable.
bugs.workaround: Configure the cache resolver to have a default value for both max-concurrent-queries and max-concurrent-udp.
bugs.fix: The CPU usage does not increase unexpectedly when the cache resolver sends a large number of DNS queries to slow backend name servers.

bugs.title: lsn-pool member routes not properly propagated to routing table when lsn-pool routing-advertisement is enabled
bugs.symptoms: lsn-pool with route-advertisement enabled does not have routes properly propagated to the routing-table.
bugs.conditions: when route-domain routing protocol is enabled after lsn-pool route-advertisement is enabled and lsn-pool member added.
bugs.impact: route entries for lsn-pool members with route-advertisement enabled.
bugs.workaround: Either 1) restart tmrouted after enable routing-protocol for the desired route-domain. 2) toggle routing-advertisement on lsn-pool after enable routing-protocol for the desired route-domain.
bugs.fix: route-domain with routing-protocol enabled will have routes for lsn-pool members, regardless of ordering in which routing-protocol or route-advertisement is enabled.

bugs.title: Generate CCR-T first and then CCR-I if session being replaced
bugs.symptoms: CCR-I was send first and then CCR-T was sent if same subscriber session is created with different IP. This could cause confusion to PCRF when it sees at period of time 2 active sessions for the same subscriber.
bugs.conditions: A session is created with subscriber ID say S1 and IP1 and new radius start or session create request arrives with S1 and IP2.
bugs.impact: CCR-I generated first and then CCR-T which will cause confusion to PCRF who maintain subscriber ID as their key to subscriber session.
bugs.fix: Upgrade to latest hotfix or version which has the fix for the issue.

bugs.title: document.write()/document.writeln() redefinition does not work
bugs.symptoms: document.write()/document.writeln() redefinition does not work. Initial function is used instead.
bugs.conditions: When web application JavaScript tries to redefine document.write() and/or document.writeln().
bugs.impact: Web application layout an/or logic can be broken.
bugs.fix: Web application JavaScript can successfully redefine document.write and document.writeln.

bugs.title: iOS and Mac receivers cannot create account on Citrix StoreFront in proxy mode
bugs.symptoms: Creating a new account in Citrix Receiver for MacOS or iOS fails.
bugs.conditions: User creates a new account in Citrix Receiver for MacOS or iOS
bugs.impact: User is not able to access Store. An error is displayed and the account is not created.
bugs.fix: Make sure AGEE auth request doesn't contain Connection: close header to keep the connection alive.

bugs.title: RR-DAG enabled UDP ports may be used as source ports for locally originated traffic
bugs.symptoms: RR-DAG enabled UDP ports may be used as the source port on locally originated connections.
bugs.conditions: Disaggregation mode set to RR-DAG
bugs.impact: Connections may be forwarded between tmms resulting in a performance impact
bugs.fix: RRDAG enabled ports can no longer be selected as a source port for locally originated connections.

bugs.title: Enforcer cores after upgrade upon the first request
bugs.symptoms: If an ASM security policy contains entities with an invalid configuration from a previous version, UCS load will fail and leave the device in an inconsistent state, leading to BD crash.
bugs.conditions: -- An ASM security policy contains entities with an invalid configuration from a previous version. -- This can occur on an upgrade from 11.5.x to 11.6.0 prior to HF5.
bugs.impact: UCS load will fail and leave the device in an inconsistent state, leading to BD crash.
bugs.workaround: Correct ASM entity configuration before upgrade.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an upgrade issue where the Enforcer crashed after the upgrade upon the first request.

bugs.title: Virtual creation with the multicast IPv6 address returns error message
bugs.symptoms: When LTM has DHCPv6 profile attached to a virtual server with relay mode configured with multicast IPv6 address, it will return error message, '01020064:3: IPv6 Address ff02::1:2 is invalid, Multicast address not allowed.'
bugs.conditions: Create an IPv6 virtual with multicast IPv6 address with DHCPv6 profile (relay mode) attached.
bugs.impact: Cannot create a IPv6 virtual server with multicast IPv6 address and DHCPv6 relay mode profile attached.
bugs.fix: Can now create an IPv6 virtual with multicast IPv6 address with DHCPv6 profile (relay mode) attached.

bugs.title: Attack signatures are not blocked after signature/set change
bugs.symptoms: System wide signature updates, like Attack Signature Update, can cause some security policies to erroneously change their enforcement of attack signatures to Transparent mode.
bugs.conditions: There are security policies in both Transparent and Blocking mode, and there is an update to the system's attack signatures.
bugs.impact: A security policy will not block attack signatures that are meant to be blocked.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the transparent/enforce flag on a security policy, and apply the security policy.
bugs.fix: We fixed an issue that caused false positives or a lack of enforcement (such as not blocking) when attack signatures were updated or modified.

bugs.title: Secondary blade shows "unknown" sync status while primary shows "in sync"
bugs.symptoms: On a VIPRION Chassis in a sync/failover devicegroup, the secondary blade may show sync status "unknown" although the primary blade shows "in sync".
bugs.conditions: VIPRION Chassis with multiple blades, in a sync/failover devicegroup with at least one other device.
bugs.impact: There should be no impact on function; it just fails to display the correct status.

bugs.title: Double count for PEM action and policy with forwarding endpoint
bugs.symptoms: The policy & action hit count for subscribers is incremented twice.
bugs.conditions: 1. The subscriber is of the origin data traffic. 2. The flow that created the subscriber lives longer than 60 seconds.
bugs.impact: In the above mentioned condition, which is very rare, the action & policy count is incremented twice.

bugs.title: https monitors might fail to re-use SSL sessions.
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshakes for https monitors might fail to correctly re-use SSL session IDs.
bugs.conditions: A configuration that utilizes https monitors to servers that implement an SSL session cache. More servers utilizing the same https monitor make the problem more likely to occur. For the monitor flapping or false negative symptom in 11.5.0 or higher, a monitor must be configured for a combination of TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.2 servers.
bugs.impact: The bigd process might consume more CPU than necessary because it might always be performing complete SSL handshakes with monitored servers. BIG-IP version 11.5.0 or higher in environments with both TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.2 servers that perform SSL session caching may experience monitor flapping or servers that are marked down unexpectedly.
bugs.fix: https monitors now properly perform SSL session re-use.

bugs.title: iRules in event ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT or ADAPT_RESPONSE_RESULT cannot see modified headers
bugs.symptoms: ADAPT iRules cannot inspect adapted headers because the rule sees the original headers before the request is adapted. Similarly for the ADAPT_RESPONSE_RESULT event.
bugs.conditions: Using request-adapt or response-adapt profiles, and an internal virtual server that can modify the HTTP headers. Along with an iRule such as: when ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT { log local0. "Modified host = [HTTP::host]" }
bugs.impact: It is impossible to inspect the modified headers. One consequence is that if a request adaptation modifies the 'Host:' value, it is not possible to use an iRule to apply that to the transport connection, and as a result the modified request goes to the original server.
bugs.fix: Two new ADAPT iRule events have been added (ADAPT_REQUEST_HEADERS and ADAPT_RESPONSE_HEADERS) which trigger after ADAPT has received the modified headers, when the IVS is returning a modified request or response. They do not trigger when the IVS has instructed ADAPT to bypass or a service-down condition has occurred.
bugs.behavior: Two new ADAPT iRule events have been added (ADAPT_REQUEST_HEADERS and ADAPT_RESPONSE_HEADERS) which trigger after ADAPT has received the modified headers, when the IVS is returning a modified request or response. They do not trigger when the IVS has instructed ADAPT to bypass or a service-down condition has occurred.

bugs.title: Cannot search Citrix Applications inside folders
bugs.symptoms: Search in webtop will not consider Citrix applications inside folders while searching.
bugs.conditions: Citrix applications available inside folder
bugs.impact: Unable to search Citrix applications inside folders.

bugs.title: ICMP attack thresholds
bugs.symptoms: ICMP flood protection triggers at an earlier than expected threshold if all of the ICMP attack traffic contains the same ID. This is because all traffic is sent to the same tmm when it contains the same ID but the threshold takes into account the number of tmms.
bugs.conditions: When ICMP traffic is sent with the same ICMP id, and the DoS threshold was configured assuming the ICMP traffic would be spread across all tmms.
bugs.impact: The forwarded ICMP traffic has higher priority that regular traffic causing normal traffic to potentially get dropped sooner as compared to forwarded traffic.
bugs.fix: ICMP attack traffic with same ID being forwarded to a single TMM for processing is now tagged with the correct priority.

bugs.title: When a virtual's ARP or ICMP is disabled, the wrong mac address is used
bugs.symptoms: When using tmsh to modify the icmp_enabled or arp_enabled property of a virtual address object from true to false, tmm does not reset the internal state properly. This results in a tmm using the VLAN's true MAC as the source MAC instead of the traffic group's MAC masquerade address.
bugs.conditions: Using MAC masquerading in a high availability (HA) traffic group.
bugs.impact: Packets may be dropped by switches or routing tables improperly updated.
bugs.fix: When a virtual server's ARP or ICMP is disabled, the correct MAC address is now used.

bugs.title: AVR HTTP External log - missing fields
bugs.symptoms: New fields were added to HTTP statistics in version 11.6 and they are available in the Configuration utility, but they were not exported out to the external log.
bugs.conditions: Use AVR HTTP profile, with the external log option.
bugs.impact: Some information that AVR can provide is missing.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: We added these previously missing fields to the external report: DosL7ProfileName TransactionOutcome DosL7AttackID

bugs.title: Logon Page agent gets empty user input in clientless mode 3 when a Variable Assign agent resides in front of it.
bugs.symptoms: APM is unable to complete the access policy when there is a Variable Assign agent in front of a Logon Page agent.
bugs.conditions: Access policy has a Variable Assign agent in front of a Logon Page agent.
bugs.impact: APM is unable to complete the access policy.
bugs.fix: Now APM can successfully run access policies where a Variable Assign agent resides in front of a Logon Page agent.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system sometimes takes longer on boot up to become Active.
bugs.symptoms: The system takes several minutes longer than normal after boot up to go from Offline to Active.
bugs.conditions: This timing issue occurs rarely on boot up. This might more frequently occur on older platforms running newer versions of the software.
bugs.impact: Because of a timing issue during system load, it takes longer for the system to become ready to pass traffic after being deployed or rebooted.
bugs.fix: A BIG-IP system no longer take longer than normal to become Active on boot up due to this particular underlying issue.

bugs.title: Upgrading to 11.5.0 and later might associate a disabled HA group to traffic groups.
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system has a disabled HA Group and is upgraded to 11.5.x or later, the disabled group might be associated with traffic groups on upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Pre-upgrade there is exists a HA Group that is disabled. Upgrade to 11.5.x or later from 10.2.x or 11.x (pre-11.5.0) to a version earlier than 12.0.0, 11.5.4, or 11.6.1.
bugs.impact: If the BIG-IP system is rebooted after the upgrade, it's possible that the switch will fail over because the HA group score is used even though the HA group is disabled.
bugs.workaround: After the upgrade, check all traffic groups and ensure that none of them are configured to use a disabled HA Group.
bugs.fix: Upgrading to 11.5.0 and later no longer associates a disabled HA group to traffic groups. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: AAA Local User Database may sync across failover groups
bugs.symptoms: APM units that are not in the same BIG-IP Sync-Failover group are sharing local user entries. The system may possibly also experience higher management CPU load as a result of frequently syncing the local user database.
bugs.conditions: There is at least one sync-failover group in the Device Management :: Device Groups list, and there are devices listed in Device Management :: Devices list that are not members of that sync-failover group (either standalone or members of another device group), and those devices are provisioned with APM.
bugs.impact: Unwanted sharing of local user database between sync-failover groups and/or standalone devices. The system may also experience higher management CPU load as a result of frequently syncing the local user database. Under severe conditions where the database is synced multiple times per minute continually for hours or days, the rapid syncing of the database may result in unexpected failover.
bugs.fix: AAA Local User Database now syncs correctly.

bugs.title: IPsec tunnel connection from BIG-IP to some Cisco ASA does not stay up when DPD (Dead Peer Detection) is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When establishing IPsec tunnel from the BIG-IP system to some Cisco devices enabled with an older Dead Peer Detection (DPD) implementation, IPsec tunnel does not stay up because of a mismatched Cookie field in the DPD message.
bugs.conditions: An IPsec tunnel connection from a BIG-IP system to certain Cisco ASA configurations does not stay up when DPD is enabled
bugs.impact: IPsec tunnel goes down, traffic stops.
bugs.workaround: Disable Dead Peer Detection for the Ike Peer configuration to the Cisco devices exhibiting this issue.
bugs.fix: IPsec Tunnel between the BIG-IP system and CISCO devices with older Dead Peer Detection (DPD) are no longer brought down because of mismatched Cookie Field in the DPD messages.

bugs.title: Trailing space present after 'tmsh ltm pool members monitor' attribute value
bugs.symptoms: Values returned from the tmsh command 'ltm pool pool members monitor' have a trailing space, such as returning '/Common/myhttps ' (note the trailing-space). This trailing-space is also observed for the value returned from a REST call.
bugs.conditions: 'tmsh' or a REST call is used to return the 'monitor' for pool members.
bugs.impact: Scripts or custom applications processing this returned output may wish to 'trim' whitespace on the value (as a trailing space is present); or should not assume the trailing space will be present in the future (as this behavior is not guaranteed).
bugs.workaround: Use a script or custom applications to 'trim' trailing whitespace for returned values.
bugs.fix: Values returned from the tmsh command 'ltm pool pool members monitor' no longer have a trailing space.

bugs.title: FQDN: node without service checking reported as 'service checking enabled, no results yet'
bugs.symptoms: When an FQDN Node has no Node Default or Node Specific monitor associated, the ephemeral nodes' status is 'Unknown (enabled)- Node address service checking is enabled but result is not available yet.' A standard node configured without a monitor has the correct status: 'Unknown (enabled) - Node address does not have service checking enabled.'
bugs.conditions: FQDN node created with one or more valid records returned for the FQDN, and no node default or node-specific health monitor configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine actual state of pool member.
bugs.fix: FQDN node without service checking has the correct status: 'Unknown (enabled) - Node address does not have service checking enabled.'

bugs.title: PVA accelerated 3WHS packets are sent in wrong hardware COS queue
bugs.symptoms: Under full ePVA acceleration, 3WHS (3-way handshake) packets from VIP to node will always egress on hardware COS queue 3, regardless of COS queue mapping configured on the system.
bugs.conditions: The packets needs to be fully accelerated by ePVA.
bugs.impact: Potential performance downgrade.
bugs.fix: PVA accelerated 3WHS packets are new egressed on correct hardware COS queue.

bugs.title: Session check interval now has minimum value
bugs.symptoms: Session check interval can be changed or turned off completely for debug purposes.
bugs.conditions: Using the session check interval.
bugs.impact: Session check interval may be set to excessively short value.
bugs.fix: Session check interval now has a minimum (5000 msec), which prevents the value from being too small.

bugs.title: Valid RADIUS sessions deleted on no session inactivity if no subscriber traffic exists during session timeout period.
bugs.symptoms: Valid sessions may be deleted after the session timeout period expires with no subscriber traffic, even if RADIUS accounting updates are being sent within the timeout period.
bugs.conditions: Sessions are created through RADIUS and remain open with no subscriber traffic for 2 minutes or longer.
bugs.impact: Valid sessions fail due to lack of activity and the user must re-authenticate. RADIUS Accounting-Request updates are not sufficient to keep the sessions open.
bugs.fix: Alive or Valid sessions won't be deleted before the timeout any more due to a lack of traffic.

bugs.title: DTLS should not update 'expected next sequence number' when the record is bad.
bugs.symptoms: DTLS updates the 'expected next sequence number' even if the record is bad. This might cause the unexpected sequence number of good records dropping.
bugs.conditions: DTLS receives a bad record with a very large sequence number.
bugs.impact: DTLS might drop the good records that have smaller sequence number packets than the bad records.
bugs.fix: The system now updates the 'expected next sequence number' only when the record is good.

bugs.title: Policy auto-merge of Policy Diff
bugs.symptoms: Running auto-merge on the Diff of two policies fails.
bugs.conditions: Running auto-merge on the Diff results of two policies.
bugs.impact: Policies cannot be auto-merged after viewing Diff.
bugs.fix: The auto-merge functionality of Policy Diff now works as expected.

bugs.title: GUI Local Traffic Pool list does not show certain Pools with name containing 'mam'.
bugs.symptoms: Local Traffic Pool list does not show Pools with names that contain the characters 'mam' starting at the 5th position of the name.
bugs.conditions: This occurs using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Cannot see these pools in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to list pools with mam in the name.
bugs.fix: Pools with a name that end in mam are now showing up in the Pools list in the GUI.

bugs.title: Certificate chain verification is not working correctly on server SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: Handshake failures during certificate chain verification.
bugs.conditions: -- Using Internet Information Services (IIS) for Windows Server. -- The ca-file is set to root CA. -- Configured with DHE, ECDHE ciphersuite, or client auth (anything except the RSA-based key transport suite), such as AES128-SHA.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake failures: BIG-IP system does not respond to server hello done with IIS. This occurs because the 'Server Hello', 'Certificate', 'Server Key Exchange', 'Certificate Request' and 'Server Hello Done' are all in single SSL record, which does not trigger the next state and the operation stalls.
bugs.workaround: Add intermediate certificates.

bugs.title: Use of DHCP relay virtual server might result in tmm crash 'top filter'.
bugs.symptoms: The Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) may produce a core file with the 'Assertion "top filter" failed' error message. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: Your BIG-IP system fails over to the standby system if configured for HA. Messages similar to the following example are logged to the /var/log/tmm* files: notice panic: ../modules/hudfilter/hudnode.c:310: Assertion "top filter" failed. Messages similar to the following example are logged to the /var/log/ltm file: notice sod[8810]: 01140045:5: HA reports tmm NOT ready. Messages similar to the following example are logged to the /var/log/messages file: notice logger: Started writing core file: /var/core/tmm.0.bld2384.0.core.gz for PID 13897 notice logger: Finished writing 236194271 bytes for core file: /var/core/tmm.0.bld2384.0.core.gz for PID 13897 Your BIG-IP system generates TMM core files to the /var/core directory, with a time stamp that correlates to the traffic interruption, similar to the following example: -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 226M Apr 13 15:09 tmm.0.bld2384.0.core.gz
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: A Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) relay virtual server and another BIG-IP virtual server are both configured to use the same IP address and port combination.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic as it recovers from TMM restarting, and systems configured as part of a high availability (HA) group may fail over. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuring virtual servers that share address:port with DHCP relay virtual server. In releases prior to version 11.5.4, use regular IP forwarding virtual servers if the virtual server is not for Relay but just for 'forwarding'. When the virtual server destination is not 255.255.255.255, it is typically for forwarding, not for Relay.
bugs.fix: Verify existing serverside flows are actual relay flows before reusing it.

bugs.title: "translate address" and "translate port" are enabled by default when configure from GUI
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server configured for LSN via GUI CGNAT menu may have "translate address" and "translate port" enabled by default, which would cause LSN translation to fail.
bugs.conditions: Configuring CGNAT virtual server
bugs.impact: Configured CGNAT virtual server with incorrect "translate address" and "translate port" settings
bugs.workaround: Manually modify "translate address" and "translate port" to disabled
bugs.fix: Virtual server configured for LSN via GUI CGNAT menu no longer have "translate address" and "translate port" enabled by default.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when RDP client connects to APM configured as Remote Desktop Gateway
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when RDP client connects to APM configured as Remote Desktop Gateway.
bugs.conditions: APM configured as Remote Desktop Gateway. RDP client connects to APM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM crash is fixed for the scenario where RDP client connects to APM configured as Remote Desktop Gateway.

bugs.title: Duplicated snat-translation addresses are possible (a named and an anonymous (created by snatpool) one)
bugs.symptoms: It is possible to have duplicated snat-translation addresses if one is explicitly created (named one) and the other is implicitly created when adding anonymous addresses to a snatpool.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions required other than to perform the configuration changes.
bugs.impact: As duplicated snat-translation addresses may exist, any change to an address entry that is assigned to an snatpool might not affect the right entry, for example, with the following snat-addresses: snat_address_01 address 1.2.3.1 1.2.3.1(anonymous) address 1.2.3.1 And the following snatpool: snat_pool { 1.2.3.1 1.2.3.2 } If there is a change in snat_address_01 (whose address is part of snat_pool (1.2.3.1)), then the actual snat_pool member (anonymous 1.2.3.1) will not be updated with the new setting, and there will be no effect.
bugs.fix: The system now automatically converts anonymous addresses added to snatpool into named snat-translation objects if they exist.

bugs.title: In ASM Manual Sync Only group, policies do not stay deleted or inactive on secondary after sync is pushed
bugs.symptoms: An inactive ASM policy on a sync target is suddenly re-activated.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when ASM manual sync is configured, and a policy is de-activated or deleted. The time stamp of the policy does not get updated, so the active policy will take precedence and re-activate it.
bugs.impact: If the user deactivates or deletes a policy on one device and then pushes the ASM config to the other device, the policies will end up being reactivated (or recreated as a default policy) on the other device.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to make a change to Policy one of the machines before de-activating it, to update its timestamp to newer than the other machine.
bugs.fix: When loading the ASM side of a UCS, ensure that the MCP data is updated correctly for policies that have become inactive or have been deleted.

bugs.title: Configuring a route domain with 32 bit subnet mask, 128 bit mask saved instead
bugs.symptoms: When creating a policy using a route domain and a full 32 bit subnet mask, the ASM saves it as a 128 bit mask.
bugs.conditions: Provisioned ASM
bugs.impact: Wrong 128 bit subnet mask is saved instead of the configured 32 bit mask.
bugs.fix: When creating a security policy using a route domain and a full 32 bit subnet mask, ASM no longer saves it as a 128 bit mask.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: SSLv3 is disabled by default on the management interface of BIG-IP on AWS Marketplace
bugs.symptoms: SSLv3 has known security issues. To make BIG-IP more secure on AWS, it is disabled by default on the management and data interfaces. This can cause legacy client connections which require SSLv3 to fail.
bugs.conditions: SSLv3 disabled on management interface of BIG-IP on AWS Marketplace.
bugs.impact: Legacy client connections that require SSLv3 might fail.
bugs.workaround: F5 does not recommend changing the default SSL profiles, but they can be configured per K13171: Configuring the cipher strength for SSL profiles (11.x), https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13171, and K17370: Configuring the cipher strength for SSL profiles (12.x - 13.x), https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K17370.

bugs.title: wom_verify_config is slow when there are a large number of virtuals configured
bugs.symptoms: wom_verify_config is slow when a large number of virtuals are defined (1000s). This affects qkview as well.
bugs.conditions: AAM needs to be provisioned with a large number of virtuals defined (1000s).
bugs.impact: wom_verify_config and quikview take a long time to complete.
bugs.fix: Removed wom_verify_config from qkview.

bugs.title: Modifying a monitored pool with a gateway failsafe device can put secondary into restart loop
bugs.symptoms: Modifying a monitored pool with a gateway failsafe device might put secondary into restart loop.
bugs.conditions: Only occurs in clustered environments, when modifying a monitored pool to set the gateway failsafe device while the secondary is down. Symptom occurs when the secondary comes back up and attempts to update the health status of a pool.
bugs.impact: Secondary in a restart loop.
bugs.workaround: Remove the gateway failsafe device. Re-apply when the blade is up.

bugs.title: MAP implementation not working with EA bits length set to 0.
bugs.symptoms: MAP implementation not working with EA bits length set to 0.
bugs.conditions: MAP-E tunnel profile is configured with (ea-bits-length == 0) and (ip4-prefix-length greater than 0). - Case when (ea-bits-length == 0) and (ip4-prefix-length is greater than 0). - Case when (ip6-prefix-length plus ea-bits-length, which is the MAP domain prefix-length) is greater than 48 bits. In this case, the Interface ID in the IPv6 destination address will be overwritten.
bugs.impact: MAP-E tunnel does not work.
bugs.fix: MAP implementation is now working with EA bits length set to 0.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system might send an egress packet with a priority different from that of ingress packet on the same flow.
bugs.symptoms: When the hardware COS queue feature is enabled, in some cases the BIG-IP system sends an egress packet with a priority different from that of ingress packet on the same flow.
bugs.conditions: Hardware COS queue feature is enabled.
bugs.impact: Egress packets are sent with an incorrect packet priority and delivered on the incorrect switch COS queues, resulting in lower performance.
bugs.fix: Packet priority passthrough mode is now sending correct packet priority and delivering on the correct switch COS queue.

bugs.title: Some special characters are not properly handled for username and password fields in TCL monitors
bugs.symptoms: Pool members are taken down
bugs.conditions: special characters like ", \ in the username or password fields in FTP, IMAP, POP3
bugs.impact: Pool members are taken down
bugs.workaround: Remove the special characters from the password and username.
bugs.fix: Handle special characters properly for username and password fields

bugs.title: Webroot cloud lookup granularity
bugs.symptoms: When Webroot cloud lookup is enabled and a URL that can not be categorized using the local Webroot database managed on the BIG-IP system, the Webroot cloud database look up is performed in a way that the entire URL is considered as one query rather than by its subparts.
bugs.conditions: If Webroot cloud lookup is enabled, and if the first request is: example.com/url1 and second request is example.com/url2, the second URL request results in an unnecessary cloud lookup.
bugs.impact: Potential performance impact due to additional, unnecessary Webroot cloud lookup. This only occurs when Webroot cloud lookup enabled. The Webroot cloud lookup features is disabled by default.
bugs.fix: The issue has been addressed with granular Webroot cloud lookup so that the 1st URL Webroot cloud lookup request gets all cloud results, so that additional Webroot cloud lookups could be avoided.

bugs.title: Delete and create of the same object can cause secondary blades' mcpd processes to restart.
bugs.symptoms: A single transaction containing both a delete and a create of the same object can, for certain types of objects, cause the secondary blades' mcpd processes to restart because of validation failure. The validation error appears similar to the following: 01020036:3: The requested object type (object name) was not found.
bugs.conditions: This has been seen to occur when an APM policy agent logon page is modified, and the error reports that its customization group cannot be found. In BIG-IP v11.6.0 HF6 and BIG-IP v11.5.4 and BIG-IP v11.5.4 HF1, this can also occur when an iApp creates a virtual server.
bugs.impact: mcpd restarts on every secondary blade, causing most other system services to restart as well. This might result in a temporary loss of traffic on all secondary blades. After mcpd restarts, the new configuration is accepted and the system returns to normal operation.
bugs.fix: For certain types of objects, an incorrect message was sent to the secondary blades' mcpd processes if an object of that type was deleted and then recreated within a single transaction.
