bugs.title: VXLAN tunnels with floating local addresses generate incorrect gratuitous ARPs on standby device
bugs.symptoms: VXLAN tunnels with floating local addresses generate incorrect gratuitous ARPs on the standby device.
bugs.conditions: A VXLAN tunnel with a floating local address on the standby device.
bugs.impact: Incorrect gratuitous ARPs are generated on the standby device.
bugs.fix: VXLAN tunnels with floating local addresses no longer generate incorrect gratuitous ARPs on the standby device.

bugs.title: Improved reliability of a module interfacing with HSM
bugs.symptoms: Assuming that tmm has crashed and auto-restarted, traffic may stop for profiles with HSM keys.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using HSM keys, and TMM crashes.
bugs.impact: Encrypted traffic will not be processed, even after daemons restart.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM, e.g. with 'bigstart restart tmm pkcs11d'
bugs.fix: Fixed a race condition that may prevent proper initialization of an inter-process communication between TMM and pkcs11d.

bugs.title: Bad outer IPv4 UDP checksum observed on egressing VxLAN traffic on VIPRION chassis and 5000 series appliances
bugs.symptoms: The egress VxLAN traffic on VIPRION chassis and 5000 series appliances has bad UDP checksum in its outer UDP header. The BIG-IP hardware does not support UDP checksum offload for VxLAN traffic if the outer UDP header is IPv4. The BIG-IP hardware uses UDP destination port 4789 to identify VxLAN traffic. This occurs when sending UDP traffic with source port 8472 to a VIPRION platform, regardless of VXLAN.
bugs.conditions: The outer UDP header of egress VxLAN traffic on VIPRION chassis and 5000 series appliances is IPv4 and has destination port equal to 4789 (5000 series) or 8472 (VIPRION).
bugs.impact: The egress VxLAN traffic is dropped due to bad UDP checksum. Incoming UDP traffic with source port 8742 is dropped.
bugs.workaround: Set db variable iptunnel.vxlan.udpport to 0. So the BIG-IP system hardware does not classify UDP destination port equal to 4789 as VxLAN traffic. Disable HW checksum
bugs.fix: VIPRION chassis and 5000 series appliances no longer generate bad bad outer IPv4 UDP checksums on egressing VxLAN traffic.

bugs.title: Intermittent or complete SSL handshake failure with netHSM keys
bugs.symptoms: 1) When the network HSM takes too long to respond, TMM is considered down. For chassis, this causes failover to other blades. Since all blades share the same netHSM, these blades might quickly fail as well. If that happens, all tmm traffic will be down. There might be many reasons causing netHSM delay/failure. For appliance and VE, it may cause intermittent or all SSL handshake failure, depending on the network HSM connection reliability. 2) With high memory consumption due to heavy configuration, if PKCS11d is restarted, the system might also experience PKCS11d service malfunctions, which might be seen as intermittent or complete SSL handshake failures, depending on each TMM's memory usage.
bugs.conditions: This affects all platforms - chassis, appliance, and VE. 1) netHSM has delay or failure. 2) High memory usage due to heavy configuration or provisioning followed by PKCS11d restart.
bugs.impact: 1) All blades in chassis are put into "disabled" mode leading to all SSL handshake failure. 2) PKCS11d service malfunction, which might be seen as intermittent or all SSL handshake failures.
bugs.workaround: 1) Restart the chassis to clear the state. 2) Reboot.
bugs.fix: 1) The timeout trigger is now disabled for failover when netHSM is used. Although there might be many reasons for such failures, with this fix, netHSM-related SSL failures won't cause all blades to be disabled. 2) The system now resets shared memory queues at creation, to avoid potential memory corruption.

bugs.title: vCMP VIPRION: internal flooded unicast packets with multi-slot trunks impact performance
bugs.symptoms: Occasional duplicated ICMP replies to a guest self-IP by multiple TMMs in a multi-slot guest. Also results in guest unicast traffic showing up in the host VLAN tcpdump because by design, a flooded unicast packet visits the host TMM and is then sent to the appropriate guest.
bugs.conditions: When a blade can receive traffic for a vCMP guest that is not deployed on its own blade, L2 learning inconsistencies can result in the FDB entry for the guest VLAN MAC timing out and causing unicast floods (destination-lookup-fail) packets. For example, in a 4-slot trunk and a 3-slot guest topology, the one slot not hosting the guest is subject to FDB entry timeouts due to normal traffic flow.
bugs.impact: Packets and connections continue to flow but more broadcast traffic than expected runs through the vCMP host TMM. This can cause extra CPU utilization and switch drops.
bugs.workaround: This situation is corrected any time the guest sends out a broadcast packet on its VLAN MAC. For example, the normal action of TMM emitting an ARP for an external node (for example a monitor whether reachable or not) can correct the situation because the ARP will update all the blades' internal FDB entries for the guest VLAN MAC and halt the flooded unicast situation until the FDB entry times out again.
bugs.fix: There is no longer duplicate traffic on vCMP guest when a blade can receive traffic for a vCMP guest that is not deployed on its own blade.

bugs.title: Suspended 'after' commands may result in unexpected behaviors
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected iRule behavior, crashes or aborts.
bugs.conditions: Can occur when a virtual server has a OneConnect profile and an iRule using the 'after' command.
bugs.impact: tmm crash.
bugs.fix: Connections are ineligible for re-use while there is still a pending, suspended or in-progress 'after' iRule. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: SPDY profile with activation-mode always may not load on upgrade to 11.6.0 or later
bugs.symptoms: In 11.5.x and earlier versions it was possible to have a SPDY profile with the following combination of settings: activate-mode always, and protocol-versions { spdy3 spdy2 http1.1 }. In 11.6.0 this was changed to allow only a single protocol-version in conjunction with 'activation-mode always'.
bugs.conditions: A SPDY profile with activate-mode always and multiple protocol versions for protocol-versions.
bugs.impact: This might cause a failure when upgrading from prior versions to 11.6.0 or later.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading make sure all SPDY profiles with 'activation-mode always' only have a single 'protocol-versions' value set.
bugs.fix: A SPDY profile with 'activation-mode always' and multiple 'protocol-versions' no longer causes an upgrade to fail. Instead upgrade changes the profile such that the 'protocol-versions' field only contains the highest SPDY protocol version that was listed before the upgrade.

bugs.title: [IE10]: attachEvent does not work
bugs.symptoms: Websites are broken in Internet Explorer if they use postMessage to send objects. There could be errors in the JavaScript console.
bugs.conditions: Web application in Internet Explorer 8, 9 or 10 that uses window.postMessage() and recieves message with handler added through window.attachEvent() working through Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Web-Application cannot use Window.postMessage() to send data with Portal Access in Internet Explorer.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: The 'onmessage' handler added with window.attachEvent() now correctly recieves data sent through window.postMessage().

bugs.title: A TMM memory leak when HTTP protocol security enabled profile and no AFM license
bugs.symptoms: This command : tmctl memory_usage_stat | (head -n 2; grep httpsec) shows increased memory on the httpsec::httpsec_plugin per transaction.
bugs.conditions: HTTP protocol security profile is enabled while AFM is not licensed.
bugs.impact: TMM memory increased on each transaction.
bugs.workaround: License AFM
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak on TMM when AFM is not licensed and HTTP security enabled profile is assigned to a virtual server.

bugs.title: VCMP guests on a specific host may be restarted when that host system experiences large date/time changes
bugs.symptoms: After a large (> 7 months) change in system date/time, either manually or via NTPD, VCMP guests may be killed and restarted.
bugs.impact: Temporary loss of service of data path elements, until killed guests are restarted.
bugs.workaround: Avoid large changes in system time during critical hours of operation. It may be better to bring down guests administratively, make the date/time change, and then bring the guest back up rather than allowing them to be killed/restarted automatically due to heartbeat timer expiration.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP is provisioned. -- There is a large change (longer than 7 months, for example), to the system date/time.

bugs.title: tmsh load sys config merge file 'filename' takes signficant time for firewall rulelist configuration
bugs.symptoms: For certain configurations with deeply nested structures in it ex: some of the firewall rule rule-list configuration, requires excessive time for the tmsh load config file merge operation.
bugs.conditions: Configurations containing deeply nested structures.
bugs.impact: The time for the merge is significantly more than the time needed for load operation.
bugs.workaround: If you are affected of long load times during merging a configuration file into existing one, you can instead append the config file to the respective bigip_base.conf or bigip.conf file manually.
bugs.fix: The tmsh load sys config merge operation performance was optimized. With this optimization the time for merge operation is slightly greater than the load operation.

bugs.title: Excessive time to save/list a firewall rule-list configuration
bugs.symptoms: A configuration containing a large number of firewall rule-list::rules might take an excessively long time to save. Similarly, excessive times are seen for listing the firewall configuration.
bugs.conditions: Large number of AFM rules.
bugs.impact: A long time to save or list the configuration. While this issue was noticed for a firewall rule-list::rules configuration, the same issue might occur for deeply nested configurations.
bugs.fix: The save and list times for the numerous firewall rules/deeply nested configurations [example: firewall rule-list::rules] is significantly reduced.

bugs.title: Start uri is blank when going through portal in ie, but loads fine in firefox
bugs.symptoms: Clicking on Start URI through portal can end up with a blank page when using IE. Firefox browser works just fine.
bugs.conditions: Using IE browser to write to a previously closed document using document.write() can result in a blank page as document.open() returns a null object.
bugs.impact: A blank page.
bugs.fix: Now old document reference is used if document.open returns 'null'. So document.write() for closed document works as expected.

bugs.title: iFrames with 'javascript:' scheme in SRC may not work
bugs.symptoms: Some applications do not work with Portal Access, resulting in an error 'F5_Invoke_write is not defined' on JavaScript Console.
bugs.conditions: Web application that uses IFrames with 'javascript:' scheme in SRC attribute runs through Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Web application does not work through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Global rule association to policy is lost after loading config.
bugs.symptoms: The association of a global rule to a policy appears to be lost after loading a config by directly loading, saving, upgrading, and config syncing. As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom: After re-enabling a global policy and waiting for an unspecified period of time, you observe that the policy is disabled again.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you associate a global rule with a policy, and then initiate an operation that causes config load.
bugs.impact: Policies are removed from enforcement in the global context.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can add back the rules manually, or, if you have not configured a route domain, you can apply route domain rules to Route Domain 0, which is effectively the same as the global rule context when no other route domains are configured. Impact of workaround: If you have other route domains configured, Route Domain 0 is no longer usable as a global context.
bugs.fix: The association of a global rule to a policy is now retained after loading a config by directly loading, saving, upgrading, and config syncing.

bugs.title: Asynchronous Tasks for Long-Running command control
bugs.symptoms: Long-running operations via the iControl/REST interface might lead to timeouts and non-responsiveness to new requests while the operation completes, with no way to return the result. While transactions can mitigate this by permitting polling on the status of the transaction, not all operations are permitted in transactions.
bugs.conditions: Heavily loaded systems might result in some commands, particularly save sys config, or save sys ucs, taking so long to complete that they time out. Until the operation completes, further operations can not be started by the same user.
bugs.impact: This makes automated control problematic, as it removes control over long-running operations.
bugs.workaround: Where possible, run long-running iControl/REST commands in transactions.

bugs.title: Ephemeral pool members may not inherit attributes from FQDN parent
bugs.symptoms: Newly resolved pool members do not have the appropriate attributes (priority, connlimit, etc.).
bugs.conditions: Parent FQDN has non-default attributes and a new ephemeral member is resolved.
bugs.impact: Ephemeral pool members have unexpected attributes.
bugs.fix: Ephemeral pool member now correctly inherits attributes from parent node upon resolution.

bugs.title: Occasional connections reset when using persistence
bugs.symptoms: Occasional connections will be reset when using persistence. If tracking reset causes, the reset cause will be "Persist add entry not found."
bugs.conditions: This occurs only within the first 32 seconds of a tmm receiving traffic after startup. The client request further has to arrive on the exactly correct tmm on a chassis. This does not reproduce on non-chassis devices.
bugs.impact: Occasional reset connections. After 32 seconds of receiving traffic, the issue abates.
bugs.fix: Spurious resets of new persistent connections no longer occur.

bugs.title: ASM restarts periodically with errors in asm_config_server.log: ASM Config server died unexpectedly
bugs.symptoms: ASM restarts periodically with the following error in the asm_config_server.log: ASM Config server died unexpectedly.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Running v11.5.2-hf-asm.
bugs.impact: ASM restarts periodically with the following error in the asm_config_server.log: ASM Config server died unexpectedly.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a syntax error that caused the system to periodically restart.

bugs.title: Edge-client crashes after switching to network with Captive Portal auth
bugs.symptoms: When switching to a network with Captive Portal authentication, the Edge-client becomes unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: - Captive Portal uses https logon page - Network switching done by unplugging network cable from NIC or disconnecting from wireless network (not disabling network interface).
bugs.impact: Edge-client crashes
bugs.fix: Corrected invalid pointer by update pointer name.

bugs.title: BWC traffic blocked
bugs.symptoms: BWC traffic blocked when configured using percentages and the configuration is modified.
bugs.conditions: Modifying configurations of BWC categories using percentages.
bugs.impact: BWC traffic is blocked.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to not configure with percentages but configure with bandwidth.
bugs.fix: The problem with modifying BWC configured percentages has been corrected.

bugs.title: EdgeClient shows incorrect warning message about session expiration
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client shows an incorrect warning message once a network access connection is established.
bugs.conditions: Access Policy has disabled Maximum Session timeout (set to 0) and Network Access webtop is used.
bugs.impact: Versions that have session expiration timeout display all zeroes instead of the timeout value. This is a cosmetic issue that does not indicate incorrect system functionality.
bugs.fix: Now, the BIG-IP Edge Client does not show an incorrect cosmetic warning message.

bugs.title: TSO packets can be dropped with low MTU
bugs.symptoms: If an interface is configured with a low MTU, it is possible for the system to drop TSO packets. This can be observed looking at the tx_drop_tso_bigpkt stat in the tmm/hsb_internal_fsc table.
bugs.conditions: The interface is configured with a low MTU, usually 750 or lower. If TMM then attempts to use TSO for a packet, there is a chance this packet will be dropped.
bugs.impact: Large TSO packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Increase the MTU or disable TSO. If TSO is not disabled, three related fixes are needed to fully address the issue: -- ID 466260, covered in SOL15953: TMM may produce a core file with the 'Assertion we always have room in tx ring! failed' error message. -- ID 502238, covered in SOL16736: The BIG-IP system may lose connectivity and fail to process all traffic through TMM if the HSB is overloaded. -- ID 509782, covered in SOL16780: The BIG-IP system may drop TSO packets. The Solutions are available here: -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/900/sol15953.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16736.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16780.html
bugs.fix: Three related fixes are needed to fully address the issue: -- ID 466260, covered in SOL15953: TMM may produce a core file with the 'Assertion we always have room in tx ring! failed' error message. -- ID 502238, covered in SOL16736: The BIG-IP system may lose connectivity and fail to process all traffic through TMM if the HSB is overloaded. -- ID 509782, covered in SOL16780: The BIG-IP system may drop TSO packets. The Solutions are available here: -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/900/sol15953.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16736.html -- https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/700/sol16780.html

bugs.title: Rare crash and core dump of TMM or bd after rebooting a device or joining a trust domain.
bugs.symptoms: The TMM process or bd daemon may crash and core dump within 24 hours of either rebooting a device, restarting TMM, or joining a trust domain. This may also happen on a standalone device that has been rebooted.
bugs.conditions: Traffic arrives to a virtual server that is configured with: an anti-fraud profile, an ASM Security Policy, or a DOS profile that has 'Application Security' enabled.
bugs.impact: The crash might happen only within 24 hours of either rebooting a device, restarting TMM, or joining a trust domain. The TMM or bd crash causes the device to not handle traffic while the process is being restarted.
bugs.workaround: Performing the following actions prevents the crash from happening. Requires shell access to the device. ( 1. ) Edit the file /etc/bigstart/scripts/datasyncd: Remove the last line, which contains: exec /usr/share/datasync/bin/datasyncd >> /var/log/datasync/datasyncd.log In its place, add this: exec >> /var/log/datasync/datasyncd.log 2>&1 echo "`date`: fix start." set -x tmsh list security datasync local-profile tmsh list security datasync local-profile | grep '^security' | awk '{print $4}' | while read -r table; do tmsh modify security datasync local-profile $table max-gen-rows infinite; done tmsh list security datasync local-profile set +x echo "`date`: fix end." exec /usr/share/datasync/bin/datasyncd ( 2. ) Run 'bigstart restart tmm'. NOTE: This causes the device to be offline and not handle traffic while TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a potential (but rare) crash of either TMM or the Enforcer that may happen within 24 hours of either rebooting a device, or joining a trust domain.

bugs.title: Incorrect counter for SelfIP traffic on cluster
bugs.symptoms: SelfIP traffic is always handled on the primary blade on a cluster and if it's disaggregated to non-primary blade, it gets internally forwarded to the primary blade. Due to this, AFM was double classifying this traffic (only on cluster) causing incorrect AFM ACL/IPI counts.
bugs.conditions: SelfIP traffic is disaggregated to non-primary blade on a cluster and AFM is enabled
bugs.impact: Incorrect AFM ACL/IPI rule counters due to internal forwarding of SelfIP traffic on a cluster from non-primary to primary blade causing AFM to match/classify these packets twice.
bugs.fix: With the fix, self IP traffic on a cluster is counted correctly for AFM ACL/IPI matches.

bugs.title: Blob activation fails due to counter revision
bugs.symptoms: Activation of Blob failed after config from ucs files (saved config has policy with atleast 1 rule) and running config has a policy (with same name) without any rules
bugs.conditions: Running config has a policy (say policy name = X) with no rules and associated to a context. Saved config (UCS) has a different policy (but same name X) with at least 1 rule. When loading UCS (saved config), blob activation fails due to TMM not being able to revise counters for the new container.
bugs.impact: Activation fails
bugs.fix: Correct counter tracking

bugs.title: Improved handling of cookie values inside SWG blocked page.
bugs.symptoms: Certain components of cookies are not escaped and might negatively impact functionality.
bugs.conditions: Use of a reject ending in a per-request access policy.
bugs.impact: Potential disruption of functionality.
bugs.fix: Improved the way that the system processes cookie values in an SWG blocked page.

bugs.title: BD crash when a specific configuration change happens
bugs.symptoms: A reconfiguration or security application attaching to a VIP or a new security policy or other big config change followed by a traffic halting/resetting, a shrinking message in the bd.log followed by A BD crash.
bugs.conditions: Remote logger with "report anomalies" attached to the virtual, a session transaction attack is on-going and a configuration change of the session transaction configuration together with a custom header (for XFF) configuration. This can happen also when adding new web applications to existing virtual server or attaching existing web application to a virtual server while there is a session transaction attack on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic halted, a failover and traffic resets. BD will startup with the updated configuration in place.
bugs.workaround: Don't add security policies or attach security policies to a virtual server or reconfigure security policy or change the session transaction configuration together with the custom header configuration while there is a session transaction attack going on a virtual that has remote logger attached.
bugs.fix: A crash that happens upon a specific configuration change was fixed.

bugs.title: Spurious HA group configuration errors can be displayed during reboot of other DSC cluster members.
bugs.symptoms: When a DSC cluster is configured using HA Groups, spurious HA group configuration errors can be displayed when rebooting another member of the DSC cluster. These messages can appear in the output of the "show cm traffic-group", or on the Device Management -> Traffic Groups page.
bugs.conditions: HA-DSC Cluster with 2 or members. HA-Groups are configured on one or more traffic groups on all Cluster members. A Cluster member is rebooted, and an administrator is viewing the Device Management- > Traffic Groups page, or issuing the "show cm traffic-group" .
bugs.impact: A message displaying that all traffic group(s) should have an HA Group configured may be incorrectly displayed. This has no affect on the operation of the system, and will clear once the cluster member has finished rebooting.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround or mitigation other than upgrading to a release with the required fix.
bugs.fix: HA Daemon has been updated to correctly track the configuration of HA Groups on other devices during device reboots.

bugs.title: Access Policy memory is not cleared between access policy executions
bugs.symptoms: APD has a Tcl interpreter that can process commands provided inside an Access policy, for variable assignment or other purposes. The Tcl environment provided does not reliably clear Tcl variables assigned in prior executions, so care must be taken to initialize the potentially dirty variables if they are used.
bugs.conditions: User uses some Tcl variables that can potentially be not initialized. For example, a variable assign: session.test = regexp {(.+)@example.com} "[mcget {session.logon.last.username}]" foo captured; return $captured Note that here, the regex may match or not match depending on the user input. If it does not match, the variable "captured" *may* contain the results from a different user who logged in previously.
bugs.impact: Unexpected results from Access Policy execution.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, any variable that was used must be checked. For example, instead of the regex statement above, this could be used: if { [regexp {(.+)example.com} "[mcget {session.logon.last.username}]" foo captured] == 1 } { return $captured; } else { return "nomatch"; } This way, if the regex does NOT match, then the result will be "nomatch" instead of potentially containing results from a previous session.

bugs.title: Revised BIG-IP CGNAT Implementations content
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP 11.6.0 CGNAT Implementations manual includes SIP ALG content for security, dialog_aware, insert_record_route_header settings. Also, content refers to the SIP Security check box, instead of the SIP Firewall check box.
bugs.conditions: Content for a SIP profile includes steps for configuring the Dialog Aware check box, the Security check box, and the Insert Record-Route Header check box, which cause an error. Content also refers to the SIP Security check box, instead of the SIP Firewall check box.
bugs.impact: Configuring the Dialog Aware check box, the Security check box, and the Insert Record-Route Header check box, causes an error. Content incorrectly refers to the SIP Security check box, instead of the SIP Firewall check box.
bugs.workaround: Deleted content for configuring the Dialog Aware check box, the Security check box, and the Insert Record-Route Header check box. Changed content referring to the SIP Security check box to the SIP Firewall check box.
bugs.fix: Documentation is revised to omit content for configuring the Dialog Aware check box, the Security check box, and the Insert Record-Route Header check box. Documentation also now refers to the SIP Firewall check box instead of the SIP Security check box.

bugs.title: HSB performance can be suboptimal when transmitting TSO packets.
bugs.symptoms: For heavily fragmented TSO packets, it is possible to populate a high percentage of the HSB's transmit ring.
bugs.conditions: This can happen when transmitting large fragmented TSO packets.
bugs.impact: Suboptimal behavior might be seen when transmitting large fragmented TSO packets. There is a rare chance it can lead to a full or stuck transmit ring.
bugs.workaround: Disable TSO.

bugs.title: Outgoing MAP tunnel statistics not updated
bugs.symptoms: Outgoing statistics for MAP tunnels are not being shown in the 'tmsh show net tunnels command.
bugs.conditions: When sending bidirectional traffic over a MAP tunnel between a client and server across a DUT.
bugs.impact: Only incoming traffic is shown in the 'tmsh show net tunnels' command output. This is a cosmetic error, and does not indicate incorrect functionality.
bugs.fix: Outgoing statistics for MAP tunnels are now included in the 'tmsh show net tunnels command.

bugs.title: potential TMM crash when AFM DoS Sweep & Flood is configured
bugs.symptoms: TMM could crash and restart.
bugs.conditions: If you have AFM DoS Sweep & Flood vector configured and incoming traffic at such a rate that this vector is being triggered then there is a possibility of getting this crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure the AFM Sweep & Flood DoS vector.
bugs.fix: Codefix has been checked in to resolve the crash bug.

bugs.title: DNS Express zone RR statistics are correctly reset after zxfrd restart
bugs.symptoms: After restarting zxfrd, the RR type-count statistics are not correctly reset when doing an incremental zone transfer to the BIG-IP system on DNSX zones with capital letters in their name.
bugs.conditions: Restart zxfrd, or reboot the BIG-IP system. The RR type-count statistics is reset to 0.
bugs.impact: DNS Express zone RR type-count statistics are inaccurate after zxfrd restart for DNSX zones with capital letters in their name.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Remove /var/db/tmmdns.bin and restart zxfrd. -- Recreate the DNSX zone names to use all lowercase.
bugs.fix: DNS Express zone RR type-count statistics are correctly set after restarting zxfrd.

bugs.title: Upon de-provisioning, ASM does not release disk resources.
bugs.symptoms: ASM is deprovisioned but asm logical volume remains.
bugs.conditions: provision and then de-provision asm
bugs.impact: ASM is deprovisioned but asm logical volume remains.
bugs.workaround: after asm is de-provisioned, run this in CLI: - tmsh delete sys disk application-volume asmdata - tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: All descriptions for address-list members are flushed after the address-list was updated
bugs.symptoms: 'Description' for address-list entries created from tmsh gets deleted when the corresponding address-list object is updated from GUI.
bugs.conditions: When a user updates an address-list object with member's description set, it gets deleted.
bugs.impact: User will lose the description value set for its members.
bugs.workaround: Not update the address list entry from GUI when its members have a 'description.'
bugs.fix: Descriptions created for address list members from tmsh no longer get deleted when a user updates the address list object.

bugs.title: All descriptions for ports-list's members are flushed after the port-list was updated
bugs.symptoms: 'Description' for port-list entries created from tmsh gets deleted when the corresponding port-list object is updated from GUI.
bugs.conditions: When a user updates an port-list object with member's description set, it gets deleted.
bugs.impact: User will lose the description value set for its members.
bugs.workaround: Not update the port list entry from GUI when its members have a 'description', or use tmsh to update port list
bugs.fix: Descriptions created for port list members from tmsh no longer get deleted when a user updates the port list object.

bugs.title: TMM core associated with smtps profile.
bugs.symptoms: tmm can core when the smtps profile is enabled.
bugs.conditions: This is an intermittent core seen when the smtps profile is enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm will no longer core from using the smtps profile.

bugs.title: learning_manager crash
bugs.symptoms: learning_manager crashed and restarted.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned, learning_manager running and traffic is flowing through ASM.
bugs.impact: learning_manager restarted

bugs.title: Create ASM security policy by BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: Certain aspects of ASM Security Policies on BIG-IP 11.5.2 could not be managed by BIG-IQ Security.
bugs.conditions: New ASM security policies can now be created by BIG-IQ version 4.5. Currently it's disabled by default, and can be turned on by changing the rest_api_extensions option to "1" on the Advanced Configuration/System Variables page in the ASM GUI, and then restarting httpd.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ Security cannot effectively manage ASM on BIG-IP 11.5.2.
bugs.fix: New ASM security policies can now be created by BIG-IQ version 4.5. Currently it's disabled by default, and can be turned on by changing the rest_api_extensions option to "1" on the Advanced Configuration/System Variables page in the ASM GUI, and then restarting httpd.

bugs.title: bcm56xxd might core when restarting due to bundling config change.
bugs.symptoms: A race condition exists where bcm56xxd might core while restarting due to a bundling configuration change if it is still processing other config messages from MCP. This affects all platforms that support interface bundling.
bugs.conditions: Interface bundling change requiring a restart while still processing configuration messages.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary core file produced since the daemon is restarting anyway.
bugs.fix: Fixed possible race condition which resulted in a bcm56xxd core.

bugs.title: TMM may occasionally restart with a core file when deployed VCMP guests are stopped
bugs.symptoms: VCMP guest shutdown can interfere with execution of the VCMP hypervisor TMM, causing 'Clock advanced' messages and TMM restarts wit corresponding core files.
bugs.conditions: vCMP guests in state 'deployed' are modified to state 'provisioned' or 'configured', or are deleted entirely. The likelihood of a TMM restart increases with the number of guests that are stopping at the same time.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Shut down vCMP guests one at a time to reduce the likelihood of encountering this issue.
bugs.fix: Resolved occasional TMM restarts when stopping vCMP guests on 12050 and 10350N appliances

bugs.title: Disabling some events while in the event, then running some commands can cause tmm to core.
bugs.symptoms: If an event is disabled inside the event itself, and then a Tcl command that executes asynchronously is executed, TMM can core.
bugs.conditions: An event is disabled from inside the event, and then a parking command is issued. Example: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { $a == $b } { event disable HTTP_REQUEST } after 100 log local0. "foo" }
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable events as the last command before exiting the event. For example: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { $a == $b } { event disable HTTP_REQUEST return } }
bugs.fix: TMM can cores if an event is disabled inside the event itself, and then a Tcl command that executes asynchronously is executed.

bugs.title: NAT64 ICMP may fail with SP DAG and a small number of IPv4 addresses.
bugs.symptoms: ICMP requests from IPv6 clients are successfully translated and sent but the replies are dropped.
bugs.conditions: A NAT64 enabled virtual server and SP DAG (cmp-hash set to src-ip or dst-ip) when there is a small number of IPv4 addresses available.
bugs.impact: ICMP fails
bugs.workaround: Increase the number of IPv4 addresses available for NAT64 translation.

bugs.title: DNS Express zone RR type-count statistics are missing in some cases
bugs.symptoms: When displaying DNS zone data with multiple instances, if one has no resource record data, the following instance also displays an empty resource record data even there is something to display.
bugs.conditions: When displaying DNS zone data with multiple instances, and one has no resource record data.
bugs.impact: Missing Resource Record data when the data is not empty.
bugs.workaround: Query the specific DNS Zone data instance instead of the 'query all'.
bugs.fix: DNS Express zone RR type-count statistics now display correctly.

bugs.title: TMM logs carry a generic hostname at startup
bugs.symptoms: During startup, TMM processes the log with the tmm process name for a hostname until the system initializes enough to get the BIG-IP system's configured host name.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during startup when the system writes messages to the log.
bugs.impact: It might not be possible to determine the source of a given TMM startup log for consolidated off-box logs from many BIG-IP systems.

bugs.title: In some cases Access does not redirect client requests
bugs.symptoms: A client may receive the following error message upon request: "The requested file could not be found on the server. Please contact system administrator."
bugs.conditions: Client requests received by Access running on BIG-IP versions 11.4.0 to 11.6.0 may encounter this issue.
bugs.impact: Client request is not fulfilled and error message received.
bugs.fix: Resolved issue in which clients receive a file not found message from Access due to out of date White List entry in OPSWAT.

bugs.title: System Crashes after Sync in an ASM-only Device Group.
bugs.symptoms: System crashes after an ASM Sync in an ASM-only Device Group.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1) Two devices with both a full-sync device group, and a sync-only, ASM-enabled device group. Both manual sync groups. 2) Have a policy active on a virtual server on both devices. 3) Deactivate the policy on one device. 4) Push the ASM config from that device to another device.
bugs.impact: Peer Device is left in an inconsistent state and BD crashes.
bugs.fix: ASM Configuration Sync now will gracefully handle being unable to deactivate when it conflicts with LTM config.

bugs.title: Add logging to indicate that compression engine is stalled.
bugs.symptoms: Hardware compression slowly and progressively fails to handle compression operations. The system posts the following errors in ltm.log: crit tmm3[14130]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Nitrox 3. If the compression engine stalls, there is no logging-trail to indicate there is a problem.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system encounters errors during hardware compression handling and the compression engine stalls.
bugs.impact: Compression completely stalls, or CPU can be driven up by software-based compression. No indication of what the issue is.
bugs.workaround: Disable compression, or select 'software only' compression.
bugs.fix: Previously, if the compression engine stalled, there would be no logging-trail to indicate there was a problem. This release adds logging and stats for detecting a compression engine stall.

bugs.title: Interfaces might be re-enabled unexpectedly when loading a partition
bugs.symptoms: Loading of a set of partitions not including Common might re-enable interfaces that were previously disabled.
bugs.conditions: Loading of a set of partitions not including Common.
bugs.impact: Interfaces might be unexpectedly reenabled. (It is expected that 'load sys config partitions { anotherpartition }' will only affect objects in the /anotherpartition folder.)
bugs.fix: Loading of a set of partitions not including Common no longer re-enables interfaces that were previously disabled.

bugs.title: Broken DNS resolution on Linux client when "DNS Default Domain Suffix" is empty
bugs.symptoms: DNS resolution can break for a Linux client when the "DNS Default Domain Suffix" setting is empty in a Network Access configuration in APM.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Gateway, Linux CLI and empty "DNS Default Domain Suffix" in Network Access configuration
bugs.impact: DNS resolution might not work on Linux
bugs.workaround: Configure "DNS default domain suffix" in network access configuration
bugs.fix: DNS resolution on Linux works now even when the "DNS Default Domain Suffix" setting in the Network Access configuration is empty.

bugs.title: SNAT Origin Address List is now stored correctly when first created
bugs.symptoms: Creating a SNAT under Local Traffic :: Address Translation : SNAT List and specifying an address list under origin, there is no host or network SNAT type to select from.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in this scenario: 1. Create a SNAT and specify an address list with a /24 mask and update. 2. Run the command: tmsh list ltm snat SNAT_created.
bugs.impact: A /32 IP address will show instead. For example, 1.1.1.0/24 will be translated to 1.1.1.0/32.
bugs.fix: SNAT Origin Address List is now stored correctly when first created.

bugs.title: B4450 L4 No ePVA or L7 throughput lower than expected
bugs.symptoms: L4 no ePVA and L7 performance was limited to as little as 146Gbps under some traffic conditions instead of the advertised capability of 160Gbps.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the B4450 blade.
bugs.impact: Performance lower than expected
bugs.fix: Driver enhancements to 12.1.2 and 13.0 enable full 160G performance

bugs.title: [DNS] Config change in dns cache resolver does not take effect until tmm restart
bugs.symptoms: Config change in DNS cache resolver does not take effect until tmm restart.
bugs.conditions: Make changes to LTM DNS cache resolver.
bugs.impact: Changes made to DNS cache resolver are not in effect until tmm restarts. For example, changes to the DNS cache resolver's parameters Max. Concurrent Queries and Allowed Query Time do not load into the system until tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm after making changes, or create a new DNS cache profile.
bugs.fix: Config change in DNS cache resolver now take effect immediately and no longer require tmm restart.

bugs.title: BIG-IP MPTCP Checksum calculation might be incorrect.
bugs.symptoms: RFC 6824 specifies that a data sequence mapping also contains a checksum of the data that this mapping covers, if use of checksums has been negotiated at the MP_CAPABLE exchange. However, the BIG-IP implementation only calculates a checksum for a mapping of a single packet.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP checksum enabled by either client or the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The MPTCP checksum may be computed incorrectly and may cause connection failures if MPTCP checksums have been negotiated.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround available if the client cannot disable checksums and sends a checksum covering a DSS mapping larger than a single packet.

bugs.title: Websso start URI match fails if there are more than 2 start URI's in SSO configuration.
bugs.symptoms: If more than 2 start URIs are configured, start URI parsing does not work correctly. This results in no start URI match and websso failure.
bugs.conditions: SSO error happens only if there are more than 2 start URIs configured in the SSO configuration.
bugs.impact: SSO V1(websso) fails for configured start URI due to start URI mismatch.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Websso config start URI parsing was wrong when there are multiple lines in start URI configuration. Websso start URI parsing is fixed.

bugs.title: iRule table command resumption can clear the header buffer before the HTTP command completes
bugs.symptoms: iRule table command resumption can clear the header buffer before the HTTP command completes.
bugs.conditions: An HTTP request was attempted with an iRule table command that resumed after parking.
bugs.impact: Results in a SIGABRT. The header names might intermittently output incorrectly, and report empty names and/or parts of the request line.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: iRule resumption after halting now works correctly.

bugs.title: PEM::enable / PEM::disable iRule errors out with an error message
bugs.symptoms: When trying to use PEM::enable and PEM::disable irule, error message is shown, indicating the irule procedure is undefined.
bugs.conditions: Using PEM::enable or PEM::disable irule in the irule script
bugs.impact: PEM::enable and PEM::disable irule cannot be used.
bugs.fix: Add correct validation to the PEM::enable and PEM::disable irule. After the fix, the irules can be used, no more error message.

bugs.title: Create and Delete buttons should be disabled for Security :: Protocol Security : Security Profiles : DNS when accessed as Firewall Manager.
bugs.symptoms: Create and Delete buttons should be disabled for Security :: Protocol Security : Security Profiles : DNS when accessed as Firewall Manager.
bugs.conditions: User with role of Firewall Manager and accessing Security :: Protocol Security : Security Profiles : DNS
bugs.impact: Firewall Manager has extra abilities not considered in scope for the role. Therefore a validation error will be thrown similar to the following: "01070822:3: Access Denied: user (username) does not have create access to object (dns_security)"

bugs.title: Using ECA:metadata iRule command might cause MCPD failure.
bugs.symptoms: Using the ECA::metadata iRule command in an iRule might cause configuration errors.
bugs.conditions: Using ECA::metadata command in the iRule.
bugs.impact: Configuration cannot be loaded or saved.
bugs.workaround: Use ECA::select command instead of ECA::metadata command.

bugs.title: PEM::info irule does not take effect if used right after PEM::session config policy irule
bugs.symptoms: Using the PEM::info irule to set the session attribute right after PEM::session config policy irule set the referential policy does not work. The session attribute is not set correctly in this case.
bugs.conditions: Use the PEM::session config policy irule and PEM::info irule one after the other.
bugs.impact: PEM::info irule does not set the session attribute as expected.
bugs.workaround: Putting a delay, "after 10" in between these two irules in the irule script.
bugs.fix: After the fix, the PEM::session info irule is setting the pem session attribute correctly, even using immediately after the PEM::session config policy irule.

bugs.title: Manage ASM security policies from BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: Certain aspects of ASM Security Policies on BIG-IP 11.5.2 could not be managed by BIG-IQ Security.
bugs.conditions: REST shows redirect URL in Response Page in case action type "redirect".
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ Security cannot effectively manage ASM on BIG-IP 11.5.2.
bugs.fix: New ASM security policies can now be created by BIG-IQ version 4.5. Currently it's disabled by default, and can be turned on by changing the rest_api_extensions option to "1" on the Advanced Configuration/System Variables page in the ASM GUI, and then restarting httpd.

bugs.title: Manage ASM security policies from BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: Certain aspects of ASM Security Policies on BIG-IP 11.5.2 could not be managed by BIG-IQ Security.
bugs.conditions: New ASM security policies can now be created by BIG-IQ version 4.5. Currently it's disabled by default, and can be turned on by changing the rest_api_extensions option to "1" on the Advanced Configuration/System Variables page in the ASM GUI, and then restarting httpd.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ Security cannot effectively manage ASM on BIG-IP 11.5.2.
bugs.fix: This is a part of ID 498361.

bugs.title: Server initiated renegotiation fails with dhe_dss/ecdhe_ecdsa and ecdh_ecdsa ciphers. BIG-IP sends bad client key exchange.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP SSL when serves as a SSL client and the ciphers used are ECDHE_ECDSA or DHE_DSS, it will send a bad client key exchange to SSL server in server initiated renegotiation.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP acts as a SSL client and the ciphers used are ECDHE_ECDSA or DHE_DSS in server initiated renegotiation.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake failed. The SSL server may reset the SSL connection with an error: digest check failed, or ssl handshake failed.
bugs.workaround: Do not use ciphers ECDHE_ECDSA or DHE_DSS.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP SSL now works well with ciphers ECDHE_ECDSA or DHE_DSS in server initiated renegotiation where BIG-IP acts as a client.

bugs.title: [LC] snmp_link monitor is not listed as available when creating link objects
bugs.symptoms: GUI: snmp_link is not listed from Available monitor list when creating link objects. TMSH: snmp_link is not shown when using TAB to show monitor options when creating link objects.
bugs.conditions: When creating GTM link objects.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine whether snmp_link monitor can be used. Must manually input snmp_link to associate snmp_link to a link object.
bugs.workaround: Through tmsh, manually type snmp_link as monitor when creating link objects.
bugs.fix: snmp_link monitor is now listed as available when creating link objects.

bugs.title: CRL critical extensions not supported
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to import a Certificate Revocation List (CRL), the import fails and you encounter this error: validate_file_contents:(/Common/my.crl) :Invalidate CRL.-- critical extensions not supported.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when attempting to import a CRL that contains extensions marked as critical. Microsoft CA 2012 sets the X509v3 Issuing Distribution Point to critical by default.
bugs.impact: CRL import fails.

bugs.title: Database monitors do not support IPv6 nodes
bugs.symptoms: Unable to monitor IPv6 nodes.
bugs.conditions: Pool configured with a DB monitor (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle or Postgres) and IPv6 nodes.
bugs.impact: IPv6 nodes are reported down and do not receive traffic.
bugs.fix: Database monitors now support monitoring IPv6 nodes.

bugs.title: TMM crashes on the disabled secondary blade and bigstart restart or reboot is triggered.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on the disabled secondary blade and bigstart restart or reboot is triggered.
bugs.conditions: Disabled the secondary blade.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes after the secondary blade is disabled.

bugs.title: Status of connection limited pool is reported incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: Status of connection limited pool or member is shown as available, even if the nodes have a connection limit and the limit has been met or exceeded.
bugs.conditions: Node connection limit is reached on all nodes.
bugs.impact: Misleading status indicator - virtual server and pool reports UP and nodes report DOWN.

bugs.title: Password-less SSH access after tmsh load of UCS may require password after install.
bugs.symptoms: Should an account such as admin have password-less SSH access, after loading the UCS config or doing a live install and moving the config, SSH access no longer works without a password.
bugs.conditions: User has .ssh/authorized_keys file owned with uid=0.
bugs.impact: tmsh load sys ucs config replaces the uid ownership of /home/user_name/.ssh/authorized_keys incorrectly, which prevents SSH access without passwords.
bugs.workaround: Create a directory in /var/ssh for each user, move .ssh/authorized_keys there, and then link to the moved file in the ~/.ssh directory. In that case, UCS load affects the link, but not the linked file, so password-less SSH access is maintained. Note: A UCS file taken after the workaround will not include the file /var/ssh/<username>/authorized_keys. If you have a plan to load the UCS on a different unit, for example, for the purposes of RMA, please save the file individually.
bugs.fix: Password-less SSH access is now maintained after tmsh load (or install and move config) of UCS.

bugs.title: Virtual address is advertised to ZebOS (as visible via imi shell) while unavailable.
bugs.symptoms: OSPFv2 does not advertise Virtual Addresses upon monitor state changes.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing must be configured. Virtual address is not associated with a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Route availability inappropriately advertised. The virtual address shows is advertised in ZebOS as available when it is not.

bugs.title: "selfLink" for ASM Policy was incorrect for iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: After using iControl REST to assign a policy to a virtual server, the JSON response had an incorrect selfLink for the policy.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl REST to assign a policy to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: API Clients depending on the correct selfLink being returned may experience issue.
bugs.fix: Previously, if you used iControl REST to assign a policy to a virtual server, the JSON response had an incorrect selfLink for the policy. This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: tmsh run sys crypto check-cert to support arbitrary certificate file name.
bugs.symptoms: tmsh run sys crypto check-cert does not support arbitrary certificate file names. This syntax works for running check-cert: [root@localhost:/S1-green-P:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh run sys crypto check-cert default.crt verbose enabled log enabled stdout enabled However, this does not (with the file path specified): [root@localhost:/S1-green-P:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh run sys crypto check-cert /config/ssl/ssl.crt/default.crt verbose enabled log enabled stdout enabled
bugs.fix: Added new function support.
bugs.behavior: tmsh run sys crypto check-cert to support arbitrary certificate file name.

bugs.title: Config sync fails after changing monitor in iApp
bugs.symptoms: Unable to modify a pool monitor and delete it in the same transaction.
bugs.conditions: A pool must have the monitor associated with it before the tmsh transaction, and must be the same as the monitor being deleted in the transaction.
bugs.impact: Unable to submit multiple changes in a single transaction.
bugs.workaround: Modify the pool monitor and delete it in separate transactions.
bugs.fix: Monitor modification and deletion can now happen in the same transaction.

bugs.title: Repeated install/uninstall of policy with usage monitoring stops after second time
bugs.symptoms: Usage monitoring as required by the policy stops working.
bugs.conditions: Policy configured with usage monitoring is installed/uninstalled multiple times within a session.
bugs.impact: Usage reporting stops working.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly handles the case in which a policy with usage monitoring is installed and removed multiple times.

bugs.title: TMM core due to invalid memory access while handling CMP acknowledgement
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, TMM might core due to invalid memory access while handling a CMP acknowledgement.
bugs.conditions: Memory is not validated before handling a CMP acknowledgement.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Memory is now validated before handling a CMP acknowledgement.

bugs.title: IPsec Policy Link not functional.
bugs.symptoms: The IPsec Policy Link on the Network :: IPsec :: Traffic Selectors :: List page is not functional.
bugs.conditions: IPsec Traffic Selectors configured.
bugs.impact: Inability to manage IPsec via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use the main navigation menu on the left of the screen to go to Network :: IPsec :: Traffic Selectors :: List, and select the desired IPsec Policy.
bugs.fix: The IPsec Policy Link on the Network :: IPsec :: Traffic Selectors :: List page now functions as expected.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP ASM bd process may produce a core file when a large BIG-IP ASM configuration is modified on a loaded system
bugs.symptoms: Under rare circumstances, the BIG-IP ASM bd process may produce a core file. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: Your BIG-IP ASM system temporarily fails to pass traffic. Your BIG-IP ASM bd process restarts and creates a core file in the /var/core/ directory.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: You perform an extensive reconfiguration to many BIG-IP ASM policies while your BIG-IP ASM system is under heavy load. Impact
bugs.impact: Traffic processing is interrupted while the bd process restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a bd crash that happens upon configuration change with very large deployments.

bugs.title: UMU memory is not released when remote logger can't reach its detination
bugs.symptoms: UMU memory is printed in the bd.log as being held although there is no traffic in the system.
bugs.conditions: Remote logger has an unreachable detination
bugs.impact: Some memory is wasted and is not released for a long time
bugs.workaround: Fix the remote logger configuration, or the network issue
bugs.fix: We fixed UMU memory slow releases that occurred when the remote logger's destination was unreachable.

bugs.title: HTTP::disable does not work after the first request/response.
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP::disable command does not work correctly after the first request is complete. If called during the second request (or response), then the connection is reset with an error message.
bugs.conditions: HTTP::disable is called in a request after the first. The pass-through data reaches the server-side before the server-side HTTP filter expects it.
bugs.impact: The connection is reset.
bugs.fix: HTTP::disable now works correctly after the first request or response.

bugs.title: SIP SUBSCRIBE message not forwarded by BIG-IP when configured as SIP ALG with translation.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not forward messages when configured as SIP ALG with translation.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured as SIP ALG with translation, and the subscriber sends a SUBSCRIBE message to receive a notification.
bugs.impact: The Subscriber does not receive any notification regarding the subscribed events.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly forwards messages when configured as SIP ALG with translation.

bugs.title: Cannot view Pools list by Address
bugs.symptoms: You cannot view Pools page after attempting to sort Nodes by the Address column.
bugs.conditions: User sorts by the Address column on the Nodes page and then navigates to the Pools page. The system posts the error: General database error retrieving information. This error persists until you either delete the JSESSIONID cookie or navigate back to the Nodes page and sort by Name.
bugs.impact: Receive error navigating to the Pools page in this case.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: (1) Delete the JSESSIONID cookie. (2) Sort by Name on the Node page before navigating to the Pools page.
bugs.fix: Correct the cookie name to avoid naming conflicts between node list page and pool list page.

bugs.title: <SecurID Soft Token Messages> are not translated
bugs.symptoms: <SecurID Soft Token Messages> are not translated
bugs.conditions: Always in case of SecurID soft token error.
bugs.impact: Minimal. They are valid customization entries in English and could be translated by admin.
bugs.workaround: Customization has entries for this, so they are translatable

bugs.title: Pagination issue on firewall policy rules page
bugs.symptoms: Firewall policy rules page shows only the first 100 rules in the policy.
bugs.conditions: This is an issue when there are more than 100 rules configured in a policy.
bugs.impact: User is only able to see the first 100 rules in the policy
bugs.fix: Firewall policy rules page is now able to view more than 100 rules.

bugs.title: Memory leak on request Cookie header longer than 1024 bytes
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak on request Cookie header longer than 1024 bytes.
bugs.conditions: Client is sending 'Cookie' request header with more than 1024 bytes of data to APM Portal Access host.
bugs.impact: Memory used by 'rewrite' process keeps increasing and leads to 'out of memory' logs and possibly failover.
bugs.fix: Portal Access no longer leaks memory on large Cookie request headers from the client.

bugs.title: Manage ASM security policies from BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: Certain aspects of ASM Security Policies on BIG-IP 11.5.2 could not be managed by BIG-IQ Security.
bugs.conditions: New ASM security policies can now be created by BIG-IQ version 4.5. Currently it's disabled by default, and can be turned on by changing the rest_api_extensions option to "1" on the Advanced Configuration/System Variables page in the ASM GUI, and then restarting httpd.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ Security cannot effectively manage ASM on BIG-IP 11.5.2.
bugs.fix: This is a part of ID 498361.

bugs.title: Possible TMM crash when evaluating expression for per-request policy agents.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash when evaluating expressions in per-request policy agents and possible loss of service.
bugs.conditions: APM is licensed and per-request policy is attached to the virtual. Per-request policy have agents which have configured expressions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove expressions from agent in per-request policy.
bugs.fix: Applied a different mechanism to evaluation agent's expression to fix this possible crash.

bugs.title: Correlation restarting on a multi-bladed vCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: The following error will appear in ASM log: Watchdog detected failure for process. Process name: correlation, Failure: Insufficient number of threads
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned on a multi-bladed vCMP guest
bugs.impact: Correlation daemon endlessly restarting
bugs.fix: To prevent endless restarting, correlation is now disabled on a multi-bladed vCMP guest.

bugs.title: Request Logging profile cannot be configured with HTTP transparent profile
bugs.symptoms: Cannot configure both a Request Logging profile and an HTTP transparent profile on the same virtual server.
bugs.conditions: HTTP transparent profile is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Request Logging profile cannot be configured on the same virtual server.
bugs.fix: The system now supports a simultaneously configuring both a Request Logging profile and an HTTP transparent profile on a single virtual server.

bugs.title: snmpd segmentation fault at get_bigip_profile_user_stat()
bugs.symptoms: snmpd can core dump due to segmentation fault with the error snmpd[<pid>]: segfault at 0 ip <ip> sp 00000000ff8bec50 error 4 in bigipTrafficMgmt.so
bugs.conditions: An uncommon race condition.
bugs.impact: None. snmpd is automatically restarted.
bugs.fix: A check was added to gracefully handle the race condition and prevent core dump.

bugs.title: A large number of regular expressions in match rules on path-segments may cause an AAM policy to take too long to load
bugs.symptoms: When loading an AAM policy, the tmm compiles the rules to an internal structure that is efficient for execution. Some conditions however may cause this process to take too long and the tmm gets halted before the system has finished compiling the policy.
bugs.conditions: The compilation time increases dramatically when regular expressions are used on more than one or 2 operands. Since you can have conditions on many different path-segments (e.g. the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc), using regular expression on path-segments are a likely way to trigger this condition.
bugs.impact: The compilation time increases dramatically when regular expressions are used on more than one or two operands. Since conditions might exist on many different path-segments (e.g., the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.), using regular expression on path-segments is a likely way to trigger this condition.
bugs.fix: Now, you can prevent AAM policy compilation from taking too long by turning the regular expression into plain matches using the '\' character to escape those symbols that turn a string into a regular expression. For example, previously, 'favicon.ico' was treated as a regular expression because '.' means 'any character'. Now the user can specify 'favicon\\.ico' (double '\' required by tmsh), which causes the '.' to mean the period character, thus avoiding the (unintended) regular expression.

bugs.title: Virtual Address advertised while unavailable
bugs.symptoms: An unavailable virtual address is advertised in dynamic routing health injection after the BIG-IP system loads the configuration (including after a restart or 'tmsh load sys config' operation).
bugs.conditions: The configuration contains a virtual-address with 'enabled' set to 'yes', 'route-advertisement' set to 'enabled', and the 'server-scope' set to 'any'. The BIG-IP system already has the same virtual-address configured with 'server-scope' as 'any'.
bugs.impact: Routes appear available on the route table when they are not, which might result in traffic being routed to unavailable servers.
bugs.workaround: Modify the virtual-address' 'server-scope' from the current value to another value and then back to the original value.
bugs.fix: Virtual address status is updated after load, so no unavailable virtual address is advertised.

bugs.title: TMUI hardening
bugs.symptoms: The TMUI does not follow best security practices when handling malicious requests.
bugs.conditions: Access to TMUI via the management interface.
bugs.impact: The TMUI does not follow best security practices when handling malicious requests.
bugs.fix: The TMUI does now follows best security practices when handling malicious requests.

bugs.title: DTLS does not support PFS ciphers
bugs.symptoms: DTLS does not support PFS ciphers such as ECDHE-RSA-* ciphers.
bugs.conditions: Use of DTLS.
bugs.impact: Creates a situation where only non-forward secure ciphers are used for DTLS. If a non-forward secure cipher is used and if an encryption key is compromised, then previously-recorded encrypted traffic can be decrypted.
bugs.fix: Added support for two PFS ciphers: * ECDHE-RSA-AES128-CBC-SHA * ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-SHA
bugs.behavior: Added support for two PFS ciphers: * ECDHE-RSA-AES128-CBC-SHA * ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-SHA These will now be negotiated by default depending on cipher set up in the SSL profile.

bugs.title: On standby TMM can core when active system sends leasepool HA commands to standby device
bugs.symptoms: On standby system TMM can core after it comes up when the active system sends leasepool HA commands to the standby device.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on standby systems when the active system sends it leasepool HA commands.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: On a standby system, TMM no longer cores after it comes up when an active system sends leasepool HA commands to the standby device.

bugs.title: Performance improvement in packet processing.
bugs.symptoms: There is a potential memory leak.
bugs.conditions: Undisclosed conditions for fragmented packet processing.
bugs.impact: Memory leak.
bugs.workaround: 1. External Firewall 2. F5 AFM product can be used.

bugs.title: The fipskey.nethsm utility does not support or enforce RFC 3280 with regards to field length Upper/Lower Bounds.
bugs.symptoms: The fipskey.nethsm utility does not support or enforce RFC 3280 with regards to field length Upper Bounds.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when user uses fipskey.nethsm utility to create the X509 certificate with the paramerers country, province, locality, org,orgunit, dnscommon, email whose length exceeds than the RFC specified upper bound limit.
bugs.impact: Noncompliance to the RFC.
bugs.workaround: Limit the various field input length to be less than RFC upper bound

bugs.title: URL Categorization: URL lookup is performed on URL without query string starting v13.0
bugs.symptoms: Prior to v13.0, URL Category was looked up using the entire URL, which included the query string. As of version 13.0.0, BIG-IP no longer uses the query string when looking up category by URL.
bugs.conditions: URL categorization feature is enbaled
bugs.impact: No visible impact
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now ignores the query string when looking up categories by URL.

bugs.title: The HTTP_DISABLED event does not trigger in some cases
bugs.symptoms: HTTP_DISABLED is not triggered by the HTTP::disable iRule command, requests using the CONNECT method, and Web-sockets traffic.
bugs.conditions: If the HTTP filter is switched into pass-through mode by the HTTP::disable command, CONNECT requests, or via Web-sockets traffic.
bugs.impact: The HTTP_DISABLED event does not trigger.
bugs.workaround: This issue has the following workaround: -- For HTTP::disable, add the logging code within HTTP_DISABLED after that iRule command. -- For CONNECT, use an iRule to match the method in HTTP_REQUEST, and check that 200 Connected is returned as the status in HTTP_RESPONSE. If so, invoke the logging code within HTTP_DISABLED. -- For Web-sockets, use an iRule to match the 101 Switching Protocols status code in HTTP_RESPONSE. If this happens invoke the logging code that is also within HTTP_DISABLED.

bugs.title: Support RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm in server SSL certificate
bugs.symptoms: The SSL handshake will fail if the certificate configured in client SSL profile cert-key-chain is signed by RSASSA-PSS.
bugs.conditions: A certificate with signature algorithm RSASSA-PSS is used in client SSL profile.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake between the client and BIG-IP SSL will fail.
bugs.workaround: Don't use certificate with signature algorithm: rsassaPss.
bugs.fix: SSL handshake will succeed when using a certificate signed by RSASSA-PSS in the client SSL profile.
bugs.behavior: Before the change: SSL handshake would fail if the certificate configured in the client SSL profile cert-key-chain was signed by RSASSA-PSS. The system does not support a certificate with RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm. After the change: SSL handshake will succeed when using a certificate signed by RSASSA-PSS in the client SSL profile. This doesn't fix the case when the client auth. has PSS in the X.509 cert chain neither add PSS support to the TLS portion (only to "our" X.509 server cert chain).

bugs.title: Using replace-all-with to modify a rule list doesn't work if you specify an existing rule name
bugs.symptoms: Using replace-all-with to modify a rule list doesn't work if you specify an existing rule name. The system attempts to modify the existing rule.
bugs.conditions: Rule list, attempt to replace-all-with and specify a rule name that exists.
bugs.impact: Difficulty modifying the rule list.
bugs.workaround: When using replace-all-with, use new rule names.

bugs.title: Rewriting URLs at client side does not rewrite multi-line URLs
bugs.symptoms: Exception posted when rewriting multi-line URLs on the client side.
bugs.conditions: Using multi-line URLs in client-side JavaScript code.
bugs.impact: Web-application logic might not work as expected. The system might post a message similar to the following: Unable to get property '2' of undefined or null reference.
bugs.fix: This release fixes client-side URL rewriting for multi-line URLs.

bugs.title: ICRD child processes may survive shutdown
bugs.symptoms: ICRD child processes (icrd_child) may still exist after icrd is stopped and restarted.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP versions 11.5.3 through 11.5.9. The cause of the orphaned processes is unknown.
bugs.impact: Orphaned processes left running on a BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: [GTM] GTM external monitor is not correctly synced in GTM sync group without device group
bugs.symptoms: GTM external monitor is not correctly synced in GTM sync group without device group.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1. GTM systems exist in the same GTM sync group but not in the same device group. The GTM external monitor refers to non-default system file.
bugs.impact: The GTM external monitor is not synced correctly and configuration fails on the peer GTM system. The system posts an error similar to the following: err iqsyncer[20361]: 011ae104:3: Gtm config sync result from local mcpd: result { result_code 17237778 result_message '01070712:3: Values (/Common/bad_external_monitor.sh) specified for external monitor parameter (/Common/external_test 2 RUN_I=): foreign key index (to_file) do not point at an item that exists in the database.' }
bugs.workaround: Configure both GTM systems in the same GTM sync group and the same device group.

bugs.title: Management port loses connectivity during AOM reset
bugs.symptoms: After resetting AOM, you are unable to connect to the BIG-IP management port.
bugs.conditions: This occurs immediately after resetting AOM and during the AOM reboot.
bugs.impact: Unable to connect to the management port

bugs.title: TMM core observed during SSL cert-related tmsh execution.
bugs.symptoms: A crash could be seen when SSL forward proxy is enabled.
bugs.conditions: TMM core observed during SSL cert-related tmsh execution.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a core observed when SSL forward proxy is enabled.

bugs.title: Client connection timeout after clicking Log In to Access Policy Manager on a Chassis
bugs.symptoms: Clients connecting via Edge Client or Network Access to Access Policy Manager running on a chassis will experience a connection timeout after clicking Log In
bugs.conditions: 1. Two or more blades chassis with APM provisioned 2. Create Portal Access/NA. start > logon page > portal resource (portal webtop, resource)> Allow. 3. Create access session using browser.
bugs.impact: Access session never finishes and browser does not render portal.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Access Policy Manager running on a chassis will correctly process the client's Log In command.

bugs.title: 'sessiondump -allkeys' command hangs
bugs.symptoms: 'sessiondump -allkeys' command hangs and does not display all the entries when the number of sessions is very large, for example, 100,000 sessions.
bugs.conditions: With a setup where there are 100,000 sessions, running a 'sessiondump -allkeys' command.
bugs.impact: The operation hangs.
bugs.fix: Sessiondump has been restructured. Now, performing a 'sessiondump -allkeys' command completes as expected, for example, in approximately 2 minutes in the case of 100,000 sessions.

bugs.title: Policy auto-merge of Policy Diff
bugs.symptoms: Running auto-merge on the Diff of two policies fails.
bugs.conditions: Running auto-merge on the Diff results of two policies.
bugs.impact: Policies cannot be auto-merged after viewing Diff.
bugs.fix: The auto-merge functionality of Policy Diff now works as expected.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Edge Client does not display logon page for FirePass
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client cannot display FirePass logon page: "Connecting..." status; instead, Edge Client displays blank pages. As a result, clients cannot use the latest BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac with FirePass.
bugs.conditions: Firepass and APM-supplied build of BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.impact: User cannot log in to Firepass if using BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac.
bugs.workaround: Update to latest client
bugs.fix: Clients using the BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac supplied with this APM release can continue to log in and do not get stuck at a "Connecting..." screen.

bugs.title: Large numbers of ERR_UNKNOWN appearing in the logs
bugs.symptoms: There are times when LTM Policy subsystem attempts to execute particular actions, which fail and result in LTM Policy writing an error to the logs with an error type of ERR_UNKNOWN.
bugs.conditions: While not limited only to the ASM module, this has been observed when ASM is active and experiencing high traffic volumes. The logging of ERR_UNKNOWN occurs when filters and plug-ins experience failures (such as out of memory) and react by initiating a reset of the connection. When these filters and plug-ins return an error to LTM Policy, LTM Policy logs ERR_UNKNOWN, as it should.
bugs.impact: This is a case of unnecessary logging, and there is no adverse effect other than a higher-than-normal amount of logging.
bugs.fix: Before logging ERR_UNKNOWN, LTM Policy now checks to see whether a filter or plug-in has marked the connection to be reset. If the connection is about to be reset, then ERR_UNKNOWN is not logged.

bugs.title: Event Log Filter using Policy Group isn't accurate
bugs.symptoms: Request Log - filter by policy group does not work.
bugs.conditions: At least one policy group created and used.
bugs.impact: Request Log - filter by policy group does not work.
bugs.fix: Request Log - filter by policy group now works correctly.

bugs.title: Using REST API to Update ASM Attack Signatures Fails
bugs.symptoms: The Attack Signature Update task remains in "STARTED" status.
bugs.conditions: ASM REST API is being used with the /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/update-signatures endpoint.
bugs.impact: REST API cannot be used to trigger an immediate download of new Attack Signatures.
bugs.workaround: Use scheduled updates or GUI to update Attack Signatures.
bugs.fix: REST Update Signatures Task now works correctly.

bugs.title: DB variable added to determine DNS UDP truncation behavior.
bugs.symptoms: There is no option to change the DNS UDP truncation value to something other than 512 bytes.
bugs.impact: Certain network topologies that might require the UDP DNS to be passed through or have a higher limit cannot configure for it.
bugs.fix: There is now a DB variable to control DNS UDP truncation behavior: dns.udptruncate. When dns.udptruncate is enabled, UDP DNS responses are truncated if the response is larger than 512 bytes. When dns.udptruncate is disabled, the message is not truncated, and the full message is received. If the client specifies a non-default size via EDNS, the message is truncated if the response is larger than the specified size regardless of the value of dns.udptruncate.
bugs.conditions: Using DNS UDP truncation.
bugs.behavior: There is now a DB variable to control DNS UDP truncation behavior: dns.udptruncate. When dns.udptruncate is enabled, UDP DNS responses are truncated if the response is larger than 512 bytes. When dns.udptruncate is disabled, the message is not truncated, and the full message is received. If the client specifies a non-default size via EDNS, the message is truncated if the response is larger than the specified size regardless of the value of dns.udptruncate.

bugs.title: CGNAT SIP ALG - RTP connection not created after INVITE
bugs.symptoms: The client has no audio when it makes a call.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a client initiates a call with a CSeqID value greater than 64 KB.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails to create a media channel for audio/video traffic.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly creates a media channel for audio/video traffic when the CSeqID value greater than 64 KB.

bugs.title: A db variable to disable verification of SCTP checksum when ingress packet checksum is zero
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP system drops SCTP INIT multi-homing message with checksum 0x00000000.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the SCTP packet's verification tag is 0x00000000 and the checksum also is 0x00000000.
bugs.impact: System drops these SCTP packets.
bugs.fix: Added a db variable to disable verification of SCTP checksum when ingress packet's checksum is zero. The current default behavior is not changed if this db variable is not enabled.

bugs.title: TMM restart while relicensing the BIG-IP using the base license.
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart while relicensing the BIG-IP on base license expiration.
bugs.conditions: - Provisioning the following modules: LTM, AFM, PEM, CGNAT, ASM, FPS, APM, AVR, GTM - Base license should have expired
bugs.impact: Results in a TMM restart
bugs.fix: TMM restart has been resolved. Relicensing is not an issue.

bugs.title: Improved UDP DNS packet truncation
bugs.symptoms: UDP responses from the DNS cache were not truncated properly. This is primarily seen in DNS tools, such as dig or Wireshark that would mark the response as malformed. Regular resolver clients handled the responses correctly noting the tc bit in the response header.
bugs.conditions: UDP DNS responses larger than the size requested by the client, typically 512 bytes.
bugs.impact: Packets may be flagged as malformed by DNS packet analyzers. There are no known issues with regular DNS client resolvers.
bugs.fix: The DNS Cache now properly fills in response data and handles truncation as expected.

bugs.title: Remote role group authentication fails with a space in LDAP attribute group name
bugs.symptoms: Remote role group authentication fails if there is a space in attribute name of remote-role role-info.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the auth remote-role role-info attribute name contains a space character.
bugs.impact: LDAP authentication fails.
bugs.workaround: Remove space characters from LDAP attribute group name. Another option is to use '\20' in place of spaces in the remote-role's role-info member-of attribute, for example: memberOf=CN=Some Big Group,CN=Users,DC=DOMAIN,DC=COM becomes: memberOf=CN=Some\20Big\20Group,CN=Users,DC=DOMAIN,DC=COM
