bugs.fix: Remote role group authentication now succeeds as expected with a space in LDAP attribute group name.

bugs.title: No SNMP traps from APM
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support SNMP traps for its error messages.
bugs.conditions: This is on APM.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to monitor APM stability via SNMP.
bugs.workaround: No workaround possible.
bugs.fix: Now APM supports several types of SNMP traps (licensing issues, HA state transitions).

bugs.title: Self IP address cannot be deleted when its VLAN is associated with static route
bugs.symptoms: A self IP address cannot be deleted when its VLAN is associated with a static route
bugs.conditions: The self IP address' VLAN is associated with a static route.
bugs.impact: Self IP address cannot be deleted.
bugs.workaround: Temporarily remove the static route entries, delete the self IP, and then add the static route entries again.
bugs.fix: A self IP now can be deleted even when its VLAN is associated with a static route, as long as at least one self IP exists on that VLAN. If the static route is IPv4, then an IPv6 self IP does not meet the requirement, and vice versa.

bugs.title: Machine certificate agent on OS X 10.8 and OS X 10.9 uses local host name instead of hostname
bugs.symptoms: Machine certificate agent checker on client might extract wrong certificate based on LocalHostName if it is not same as hostname. Machine certificate agent checker might fail.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM with machine certificate agent.
bugs.impact: Machine certificate check might fail
bugs.fix: Machine Cert Auth agent passes on OS X 10.8 and OS X 10.9.

bugs.title: Install does not complete (stays at 0%) because the UCS save operation hangs while backing up the AVR database.
bugs.symptoms: Install does not complete (stays at 0%) because the UCS save operation hangs while backing up the AVR database.
bugs.conditions: /var/db/mysqlpw file does not exist (was not created due to lack of space, MySQL never ran, or another reason).
bugs.impact: Upgrade process does not complete.
bugs.fix: The UCS save operation no longer hangs while backing up the AVR database. If the file /var/db/mysqlpw doesn't exist, the UCS saving process will fail and the following error message will be displayed: File /var/db/mysqlpw not found.

bugs.title: Dynamic user record removed from memcache but remains in MySQL
bugs.symptoms: When the system fetches a dynamic user record from MySQL and places the record into memcache, the record might remain there in an unmodified state for ten days.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a dynamic user record is removed from memcache but remains in MySQL, due to an intermittent race condition between apmd/memcache and localdbmgr.
bugs.impact: Dynamic user, if locked out, remains in memcache for ten days. During this interval, the dynamic user record is unusable.
bugs.workaround: The Admin can remove the user by deleting the associated memcache record.
bugs.fix: Now APM handles the condition in which a dynamic user record is removed from memcache but remains in MySQL due to an intermittent race condition between apmd/memcache and localdbmgr.

bugs.title: Changing per request policy in the middle of data traffic can cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: Changing per request policy while BIG-IP serving the user requests can cause TMM to restart. This makes the TMM services unavailable until TMM is back.
bugs.conditions: Administrator has to change the per-request policy while TMM serving user requests.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Change per-request policy in planned scheduled maintenance window where there is no user traffic expected.
bugs.fix: TMM does not crash and administrator can change per-request policy any time now.

bugs.title: Hardware flow stats are not consistently cleared during fastl4 flow teardown.
bugs.symptoms: The PVA stat curr_pva_assist_conn is not being updated properly for certain Fast L4 flows.
bugs.conditions: 1) Fast L4 virtual server. 2) PVA-acceleration enabled. This occurs when the connection flow is not created because UDP traffic arrives at an undefined port on the virtual server. The curr_pva_assist_conn value is incremented though there are no active PVA flows. This can also occur when LTM gets ICMP unreachable messages from the serverside.
bugs.impact: Stats counts for Fast L4 virtual server, curr_pva_assist_conn value and 'Current SYN Cache', show invalid counts. If the hardware SYN cookie protection is on, the SYN cookie protection may be activated when it is not supposed to.
bugs.fix: Stats counts for Fast L4 virtual server, curr_pva_assist_conn value and 'Current SYN Cache', now show the correct counts.

bugs.title: Forwarding of flooded VXLAN-encapsulated unicast frames may introduce additional forwarding
bugs.symptoms: In VXLAN overlays, unicast frames are flooded (via multicast or unicast replication) when the destination MAC address is known and the remote endpoint is unknown. Upon receiving a flooded unicast frame, the BIG-IP system might forward the frame again to yet another endpoint. Eventually an additional L2 hop might be introduced between the sender and the receiver. This applies to both the multicast and the multipoint (unicast replication) configurations of VXLAN.
bugs.conditions: This affects deployments with three or more VXLAN endpoints.
bugs.impact: The introduction of an additional hop adds unnecessary latency.
bugs.fix: In this release, the system does no L2 forwarding of encapsulated frames received from one endpoint and destined to another within the same overlay (VXLAN VNI/Tunnel), so no extra hop is added.

bugs.title: Increased latency during connection setup when using FastL4 profile and connection mirroring.
bugs.symptoms: Connection setup when using FastL4 profile and connection mirroring takes longer than previous versions.
bugs.conditions: FastL4 profile with connection mirroring.
bugs.impact: Slight delay during connection setup.
bugs.workaround: Disable tm.fastl4_ack_mirror. Optionally, enable tm.fastl4_mirroring_taciturn for signal to noise ratio improvements. This helps resolve connection setup latency.
bugs.fix: Disable Nagle algorithm on TCP/HA profile to improve performance.

bugs.title: Firewall rules specifying wildcard IPv6 addresses match IPv4 addresses
bugs.symptoms: A Firewall Rule with Src/Dst = ::/0 (or 0::0/0) matches any IPv6 traffic which is correct, but also matches any IPv4 traffic which is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: Network Firewall Rule with wildcard IPv6 source or destination address ::0 or 0::0/0.
bugs.impact: IPv4 traffic will match.
bugs.fix: A Firewall Rule with Src/Dst = ::/0 (or 0::0/0) no longer incorrectly matches any IPv4 traffic.

bugs.title: BD crash during brute force attack on cluster environement
bugs.symptoms: A BD crash happens when there is a brute force attack on a blade environment.
bugs.conditions: Brute force attack, blade environment.
bugs.impact: BD crash, traffic sessions reset, failover.
bugs.fix: The blade system no longer experiences a BD crash when a brute force attack happens.

bugs.title: Continuous "Invalid sadb message" upon issuing "racoonctl -l show-sa esp"
bugs.symptoms: Racoonctl utility is not designed to display large number of SA's and it will display "Invalid sadb message" continuously.
bugs.conditions: If the system has large number of IPsec SA's.
bugs.impact: Continuous "Invalid sadb message" will be displayed upon issuing "racoonctl -l show-sa esp" and racoonctl utility will not work.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH instead. "tmsh show net ipsec ipsec-sa" will provide more accurate IPsec security association information.
bugs.fix: This changes should provide a user to retrieve SA's based on specific addresses using racoonctl utility.

bugs.title: Add logging to indicate the nitrox3 compression engine is stalled.
bugs.symptoms: The compression engine stops functioning, and new compression requests may fail. Examination of tmctl compress table shows no changes for accelerated compression, over time.
bugs.conditions: Invalid request data passed into the compression engine can stall the accelerated compression engine.
bugs.impact: No compression; or possibly compression performed only in software (which drives up the CPU).
bugs.workaround: Disable accelerated compression.

bugs.title: Added urlcatblindquery iRule command
bugs.symptoms: The PEM module lacks the ability to query the customDB that is encrypted using an iRule command. When the urlcatblindquery iRule is used, PEM will not try to parse the input, rather it will allow direct queries against the customDB and categorize the input accordingly.
bugs.conditions: This is a special enhancement that only applies when the new urlcatblindquery iRule is used in one specific PEM use case.
bugs.impact: This has no impact to existing PEM URL Categorization features and it's behavior.
bugs.fix: The new iRule comamnd, urlcatblindquery is added to support existing use cases.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Unable to Configure Clickjacking Protection via REST
bugs.symptoms: The REST API for URLs was missing a field for Clickjacking Protection configuration. When trying to configure that 'Rendering in Frames' should only be allowed from a single URL, there is no field to specify that URL.
bugs.conditions: REST API is being used to configure Clickjacking Protection for URLs.
bugs.impact: A REST API client is unable to correctly configure protection that is meant to be allowed only from a specified URL.
bugs.workaround: Configure via the GUI instead of REST.
bugs.fix: This release adds the missing field for REST to specify the 'only-from' clickjacking URL: 'allowRenderingInFramesOnlyFrom'.

bugs.title: Policy parameter fields minimumValue and maximumValue do not accept decimal values through REST but accept decimal through GUI
bugs.symptoms: Create security policy named "policy1" Send POST to -------------------------- https://<BIG-IP>/mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<asm-policy-uuid>/parameters -------------------------- with body: -------------------------- { "name": "decimal", "dataType": "decimal", "maximumValue": 20.1 } -------------------------- you will get error saying: -------------------------- "Could not parse/validate the Parameter. Field value for maximumValue must be an integer." --------------------------
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Not able to create a decimal parameter with floating "minimumValue" and "maximumValue" properties using REST API.
bugs.fix: It is now possible to create a decimal parameter with floating "minimumValue" and "maximumValue" properties using REST API.

bugs.title: Socket error when Webroot cloud lookup is enabled under stress condition
bugs.symptoms: When Webroot cloud lookup is enabled and the BIG-IP system is under stress load with URLs that cannot be categorized by the local Webroot database managed on the BIG-IP system, the wr_urldbd daemon may return the socket error 'EAI_AGAIN error'. As a result, some of the Webroot cloud lookups are not performed, and relevant URLs are categorized as UNKNOWN. After a large number of cloud lookups, the daemon runs out of sockets. The cloud queries do not go through. URLs get categorized as UNKNOWN.
bugs.conditions: If Webroot cloud lookup is enabled while there is heavy traffic with URLs that cannot be categorized by the local Webroot database managed on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Due to the socket error under stress load for Webroot cloud lookups relevant URLs could be categorized as UNKNOWN. This only occurs when Webroot cloud lookup enabled. The Webroot cloud lookup features is disabled by default.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed by releasing sockets properly, so that the wr_urldbd will recover from temporary socket exhaustion.

bugs.title: ASM REST Error When Trying To Create a Custom Manual Signature Set
bugs.symptoms: If the user attempts to create a Custom Manual Signature Set with an assigned System via REST, an error is thrown and the transaction fails.
bugs.conditions: The user attempts to create a Custom Manual Signature Set with an assigned System via REST.
bugs.impact: An error is thrown and the transaction fails.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: Kerberos SSO fails if KDC is not specified
bugs.symptoms: When you configure single sign-on (SSO) using Kerberos, and you do not fill in the KDC field on the configuration page (Access Policy > SSO Configurations > Kerberos) , you may encounter an error. The error may be similar to: <Date> slot2/BIGIP1 err websso.0[29236]: 014d0005:3: Kerberos: can't get TGT for host/svcf5kerberos.corpdev.apdev.local@CORPDEV.APDEV.LOCAL - Cannot contact any KDC for realm 'CORPDEV.APDEV.LOCAL' (-1765328228)
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you do not specify a value for KDC when configuring SSO with Kerberos.
bugs.impact: SSO fails
bugs.workaround: Has a workaround, administrator should edit /etc/krb5.conf file manually and set option dns_lookup_kdc=true Note that this workaround is: not synced across cluster not backed up not audited not upgrade safe not re-provision safe may revert during other maintenance operations

bugs.title: https monitor fails to work with MD5 with RSA as signature hash algorithm
bugs.symptoms: https monitor fails to work with server that has MD5 with RSA as signature hash algorithm
bugs.conditions: https monitor, server using MD5 with RSA.
bugs.impact: https monitor fails
bugs.workaround: configure the back end server to use another cipher

bugs.title: ospf6d might leak memory distribute-list is used
bugs.symptoms: Memory might be leaked when a distribute-list is used to filter routes between OSPFv3 and the Routing Information Base (RIB). The leak may lead to a crash unrelated to memory exhaustion.
bugs.conditions: OSPFv3 in use with a distribute-list, and LSAs in the database whose prefixes will be filtered by the distribute-list.
bugs.impact: ospf6d crashes interrupt all dynamic routing using OSPFv3.
bugs.workaround: Position the BIG-IP system in the network so there are no LSAs that need to be filtered using a distribute-list, such as in a stub area.
bugs.fix: ospf6d no longer crashes when a distribute-list is configured.

bugs.title: LDAP Query may fail if user belongs to a group from foreign domain
bugs.symptoms: LDAP Query might fail if a user belongs to a group from a foreign domain.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when LDAP Query is configured with the option Fetch groups to which the user or group belong, and the user belongs to a group from a foreign domain.
bugs.impact: Login fails. LDAP Query fails with error: Referral, 0000202B: RefErr: DSID-03100747, data 0, 1 access points ref 1: 'example.domain'.
bugs.fix: Do not try to resolve group membership if the group belongs to a foreign domain.

bugs.title: TMM may crash if Fast L4 virtual server has fragmented packets
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when the following conditions are met: Fast L4 virtual server. -- Incoming fragmented packets.
bugs.impact: tmm might crash.
bugs.workaround: In the Fast L4 profile, enable the option 'Reassemble IP Fragments'.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes if Fast L4 virtual servers have fragmented packets

bugs.title: d10200: tmm core when using ASM-FPS-AVR-APM-DOS on virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: When tmm is running out of memory because of overload or other conditions and if APM is configured, tmm could potentially crash.
bugs.conditions: tmm is already running out of memory
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: localdb_mysql_restore.sh failed with exit code
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios, deleting a dynamic user entry from memory does not clear the entry from the underlying table.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when a dynamic user record is marked for deletion but has not yet been removed when the dynamic user representing that record is re-authenticated.
bugs.impact: Over time, the table grows in size due to stale records.
bugs.fix: Orphaned dynamic user records are now correctly deleted.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes with a default monitor may cause configuration load failure
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to load a configuration containing FQDN nodes, a default-node-monitor and non-Common partitions can fail due to invalid partition reference.
bugs.conditions: Node in a non-Common partition and a default-node-monitor configured.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load. The system posts an error message similar to the following: 01070726:3: Node /Common/name.of.fqdn.node in partition Common cannot reference monitored object /Common/name.of.fqdn.node /Common/partition1 in partition another_partition.
bugs.workaround: If possible, use FQDN nodes only in the Common partition.
bugs.fix: FQDN nodes with a default monitor no longer cause configuration load failure.

bugs.title: VIPRION B2150 blades show up as unknown when SNMP queries the OID sysObjectID.
bugs.symptoms: VIPRION B2150 blades with SSD show up as unknown when SNMP queries the OID sysObjectID.
bugs.conditions: SNMP queries the OID sysObjectID.
bugs.impact: You cannot identify any VIPRION B2150 blades with SDD using SNMP.
bugs.fix: Added new SNMP OID for VIPRION B2150 blades with SSD.

bugs.title: SAML Service Provider generated SLO requests do not contain 'SessionIndex' attribute
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is used as SAML Service Provider, and SP-initiated Single Logout (SLO) is executed, the SLO request message does not contain the 'SessionIndex' attribute'. As a result, the external IdP might not be able to terminate the user's session.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured as SP. SLO is initiated by SP.
bugs.impact: External IdP may not be able to terminate user's session.
bugs.fix: SAML Service Provider generated SLO requests contain needed attributes

bugs.title: Edge client is missing localization of some English text in Japanese locale
bugs.symptoms: Edge Client is missing localization of some English text in Japanese locale.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client in Japanese locale
bugs.impact: Edge Client shows some text in english
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client is correctly localized for Japanese locale.

bugs.title: RPZ may not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: A query may incorrectly not match the RPZ database, getting an answer from the cache instead of triggering the RPZ action.
bugs.conditions: DNS Cache with a Response Policy Zone.
bugs.impact: A DNS client may not be filtered by the RPZ database as expected.
bugs.fix: A DNS client will be properly filtered by the RPZ database.

bugs.title: FastL4 connection may get RSTs in case of hardware syncookie enabled.
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, ACK is sent to server without SYN, connection get RST.
bugs.conditions: 1) FastL4 virtual server. 2) Hardware syncookie enabled. 3) Might more commonly occur with forwarding virtual servers. 4) Often happens when egress router has ARP timeout.
bugs.impact: Some connections will be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Configure a static ARP to all neighbors (routers) to avoid most issues.
bugs.fix: An issue with hardware syncookies and FastL4 connections has been resolved.

bugs.title: Only one of the TMMs load the classification library after an IM package upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Not all traffic is processed by the classification library from the newly installed IM package. Flows that go through TMM that didn't load the new library will continue being classified by the old library.
bugs.impact: Possible misclassification of some of the flows since they will be processed by the old library.
bugs.workaround: run the following command after the upgrade 'bigstart restart tmm'
bugs.fix: The fix addresses the problem by loading the library on all TMMs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when updating the classification library.

bugs.title: Improper processing of crypto error condition might cause memory issues.
bugs.symptoms: Improper processing of a crypto error condition might cause memory issues.
bugs.conditions: Error when processing certain crypto commands.
bugs.impact: The error might cause TMM to crash.
bugs.fix: If certain crypto commands return an error, but memory is allocated successfully, the system now completes the operation as expected.

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client doesnt send client data if access policy expired
bugs.symptoms: If an access policy expires (for example, if a user took too long to enter password ) then BIG-IP Edge Client displays a new page with link "Start a New session". Clicking this link causes Edge Client for Mac to be detected as browser by BIG-IP APM.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client in use, access policy expires.
bugs.impact: Edge Client is detected as browser.
bugs.workaround: Click disconnect button and Connect buttons on Edge Client.
bugs.fix: APM no longer detects BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac as a browser when a user clicks "Start a New session" on access policy expired page.

bugs.title: Management traffic from nodes being health monitored might cause health monitors to fail.
bugs.symptoms: Management traffic from nodes being health monitored might cause health monitors to fail.
bugs.conditions: Health monitor checking node_ip:port where 1024 is less than or equal to port, which is less than 65536. Node periodically connects back to management service on self IP (e.g., iControl, GUI, SSH).
bugs.impact: Traffic is not sent to the node while the monitor is failing.
bugs.fix: Management traffic from nodes being health monitored no longer causes health monitors to fail.

bugs.title: LBH firmware v3.07 update for BIG-IP 5000-/7000-series appliances
bugs.symptoms: The following issues may be observed on BIG-IP 5000-/7000-series appliances: 1. When a system shuts down due to a over temperature condition, the name of the sensor that triggered the shutdown does not display. 2. Unable to configure AOM IP address using the DHCP Menu Option, with the system responding with the message: Error: Failed to configure AOM management port. 3. TMOS may log a critical alarm for the 0.9 volt sensor even though the voltage is in the nominal range.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP 5000-/7000-series appliances with LBH firmware versions prior to v3.07 may experience each of the above issues under the following corresponding conditions: 1. Over temperature, thermal shutdown. 2. When trying to configure an IP address for AOM using the N - Configure AOM network option. 3. When the host is powered off using the AOM menu, the LBH will detect an under voltage condition for all non-standby voltage rails.
bugs.impact: The impacts of these issues are: 1. The user cannot determine which sensor triggered the thermal shutdown. 2. Unable to configure the AOM address using DHCP. 3. There will be a single ltm log message indicating this critical alarm, however the voltage reported in the log message will be in the nominal range.
bugs.workaround: Corresponding workarounds include: 1. None. 2. None. 3. Do not power cycle the host with the AOM menu. This error does not occur with an AC power cycle.
bugs.fix: LBH firmware v3.07 update for BIG-IP 5000-/7000-series appliances now works as expected.

bugs.title: TMM might core when a profile is changed.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might core when a profile is changed.
bugs.conditions: A "standard" type virtual server configured with the TCP or SCTP protocol profile, and a Persistence, Access or Auth profile. This issue might occur in either of the following scenarios: -- Change profile on the active device. -- Change profile on the standby device and perform a config sync to the active ones.
bugs.impact: TMM might core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now reinitializes the TCP proxy filter chain on profile change, so that tmm no longer cores.

bugs.title: Add X25519 support for SSL ECDHE.
bugs.symptoms: There is no X25519 support for SSL ECDHE.
bugs.conditions: Trying to use X25519 for SSL ECDHE.
bugs.impact: SSL client/server will not be able to use X25519 for ECDHE.
bugs.workaround: In a typical configuration, this does not impact SSL connections unless SSL client/server exclusively requires X25519 for ECDHE. For most application, P-256/P-384 will be used instead.
bugs.fix: Added X25519 support for SSL ECDHE.

bugs.title: Incorrect of failing sideband connections from within iRule may leak memory
bugs.symptoms: When using sideband connections within iRules, the internal TMM memory structures might leak if the sideband destination is not reachable (routing, etc.).
bugs.conditions: Unreachable sideband destination that lead to failures of the sideband connection creation, e.g. destination is not reachable via routing.
bugs.impact: Gradual memory usage in TMM, which can lead to aggressive memory sweeper and eventual failover/outage. This might manifest in gradual increment of TMM memory usage in graphs, particularly, the following: -- High number of connfails in tmctl sb_stats. -- High number of allocated memory in tmctl sb_cache.
bugs.workaround: Correct possible reachability issues to the sideband destination.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer leaks memory when the sideband destination is unreachable.

bugs.title: TMM asserts when certain ICMP packets (e.g multicast echo) are classified by AFM and match rules at Global and Route Domain context with logging enabled for these rules and also log-translations is enabled in AFM Logging configuration.
bugs.symptoms: TMM asserts when certain ICMP packets are classified by AFM and match rules at the Global and Route Domain context with logging and log-translations enabled.
bugs.conditions: This might occur in the following configurations: -- AFM Rule Logging is enabled and Log Translations is enabled in Log Profile, -- Server side AVR Statistics collection is enabled under Security :: Reporting. -- Certain ICMP packets (such as multicast ICMP echo) are classified and match AFM rules at Global and Route Domain contexts.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes (assert). Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disabling log-translations in AFM Logging Profile configuration can prevent the TMM crash for these types of ICMP packets.
bugs.fix: TMM crash (assert) for certain ICMP packets when classified by AFM and logging is enabled with log-translations has been fixed.

bugs.title: An snmpwalk with a large configuration can take too long, causing snmpd or mcpd restarts
bugs.symptoms: The snmpwalk will fail and the mcpd daemon could be restarted.
bugs.conditions: The configuration must be large so that the number of configured items related to the snmpwalk are in the tens of thousands.
bugs.impact: Failure to read SNMP data, mcpd restart and temporary loss of service.
bugs.workaround: Spread the configuration among more BIG-IPs or avoid running snmpwalks.
bugs.fix: Cache internal query data to optimize statistical queries.

bugs.title: Some autodiscovered virtuals may be removed from pools.
bugs.symptoms: As part of a larger effort to refine Virtual Server Auto Discovery and monitoring, several changes were made to improve cross version interoperability and Virtual Server matching. As part of these fixes, an error was introduced which caused some virtual servers to be deleted and rediscovered. This removed them from the Pool they were assigned to, which can cause load balancing errors.
bugs.conditions: This can occur with Virtual Servers that were originally specified on a pre-folder aware version of BIG-IP, such as 10.2.x. When they are discovered by a folder aware version, they may be deleted from the GTM config and re-added with "/Common/" prepended to the name.
bugs.impact: Some virtual servers will be removed from Pools. The virtual server will be deleted and recreated, but not added back to the pool. This will result in incorrect load balancing decisions.
bugs.workaround: Changing the GTM config to add the virtual servers back to the pool will resolve the issue.
bugs.fix: The discovery and monitoring of virtual servers has been made more robust to deal with cases of multiple GTM VSes pointing at the same LTM virtual, as well as naming/folderization issues.

bugs.title: ldap query fails when user is assigned to newly created group and that group is set as primary group
bugs.symptoms: In MS Active Directory there is a special attribute primaryGroupID for a user. BIG-IP caches AD groups to resolve primaryGroupID into group DN. when new group is created in the domain and assigned to a user as primaryGroup, BIG-IP cannot find that group by ID in it's cache, and tries to fetch new group from domain using primaryGroupToken attribute. the query fails as primaryGroupToken is constructed attribute and cannot be a part of filter expression
bugs.conditions: new group is created in the domain, the new group is assigned to the user, the group is set as primary group for the user
bugs.impact: user cannot login
bugs.workaround: clear group cache for AAA LDAP Server. during next user's login, the cache will be built from scratch and the new group will be in the cache - no need to retrieve it from server.
bugs.fix: after fix, group is retrieved from server using objectSid attribute.

bugs.title: Connections might be reset when using SSL::disable and enable command
bugs.symptoms: Enable/disable of SSL filter in quick succession might cause connection reset.
bugs.conditions: SSL filter is disabled then quickly re-enabled.
bugs.impact: Connection is unexpectedly reset/lost.
bugs.workaround: Do not re-enable SSL filter immediately after disabling it.
bugs.fix: SSL::disable command no longer incorrectly flags a connection as disabled when enable/disable SSL filter in quick succession.

bugs.title: '-decode' option produce incorrect value when it decodes a single value
bugs.symptoms: When a session variable set by AD/LDAP module is HEX-encoded, it is possible to decode it with the -decode option for the mcget command. The option works correctly when the session variable contains multiple values (such as | 0xABCD | 0xDCBA |), but it does not work properly with a single encoded value (such as0xABCD).
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: the -decode option is specified when retrieving a HEX-encoded variable, and the session variable contains only one value/
bugs.impact: As a result, the access policy does not follow the expected branch rule.
bugs.workaround: While decoding a single value, the mcget command produces a result like EncodedValueDecodedValue. For example, for encoded string 0x616161, the result of the operation will be 616161aaa. It is possible to write a Tcl expression in the Variable Assign agent that truncates the left half of the string and leaves aaa, the decoded value only.
bugs.fix: The -decode option works as expected for single-value and multi-value session variables.

bugs.title: AFM Kill-on-the-fly does not re-evaluate existing flows against any Virtual/SelfIP ACL policies if a Global or Route-Domain rule action is modified from Accept-Decisively to Accept.
bugs.symptoms: Existing flows are not re-evaluated against Virtual Server AFM policies in Kill-on-the-fly if a previous Global or Route Domain AFM rule with action = Accept Decisively is modified to action = Accept.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned and licensed. Have a Global AFM (or route domain) rule with action = Accept Decisive and also have a virtual server AFM rule. Initial flow will be allowed due to global AFM rule action being Accept-decisively and will not be matched against Virtual Server Rule. Now, modify the global AFM rule action to Accept. This should trigger Kill-on-the-fly to re-evaluate all existing flows against AFM policies.
bugs.impact: Existing flows bypass Virtual Server AFM Policy match evaluation in the sweeper under the conditions specified above.
bugs.fix: With this fix, existing flows will be evaluated against virtual server ACL policy if a previous Global or Route Domain AFM rule with action = Accept Decisively is modified to action = Accept.

bugs.title: Occasional TMM crash when HTTP payload is scanned through SWG
bugs.symptoms: TMM core might occur when SWG is provisioned and content scanning is enabled. TMM restarts automatically after the core occurs.
bugs.conditions: When the BIG-IP system is provisioned with SWG and content is scanned through SWG.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable content scanning in SWG as workaround.
bugs.fix: The timer associated with SWG content scanning is now removed properly so TMM no longer crashes.

bugs.title: APM(ACCESS)/SWG filter might process SessionDB replies after flow has been aborted resulting in orphaned timer
bugs.symptoms: APM(ACCESS)/SWG filter might process SessionDB replies after flow has been aborted resulting in orphaned timer.
bugs.conditions: APM(ACCESS)/SWG.
bugs.impact: This results in rare TMM crashes/cores. The backtrace from cores usually point to the timer.
bugs.fix: APM(ACCESS)/SWG filter operation no longer results in orphaned timers.

bugs.title: Transaction validation errors on object references
bugs.symptoms: If certain objects are deleted then created within the same transaction, transaction errors might occur.
bugs.conditions: This is exclusive to transactions either via iControl, tmsh cli transaction, or a device group config sync. An object must be deleted and re-created in the same transaction. The object that was deleted must have configured references to other objects. For example, a virtual server can reference a profile or a VLAN. If it does, and there is a virtual server delete-and-create operation in the same transaction, mcpd fails to clean up the join reference on delete and complains when it tries to recreate it.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary mcpd validation failure. The system posts an error message similar to the following: 01020066:3: The requested virtual server profile (/Common/vs1 /Common/tcp) already exists in partition Common.
bugs.workaround: If a user needs to delete and re-create an object, perform the delete in one transaction and the create in a subsequent transaction.
bugs.fix: Attempts to delete and recreate objects within the same transaction now complete successfully.

bugs.title: AAM Policy not all regex characters can be used via the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Cannot specify certain regex syntax when configuring Client IP for 'Matching' or 'Validation' rules in an AAM Policy.
bugs.conditions: Adding regex characters such as \, [, ], ^, $ to an existing policy. Parentheses appear to be allowed, but do not save the information correctly.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the GUI to configure the policy with certain regex strings. The system posts the following error message: The field Value has invalid characters.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh, and escape special wild-card characters with '\': For example at add 10.[0-9]$: modify wam policy Drafts/test_policy nodes modify { t1 { matching modify { client-ip { values replace-all-with { 10.\[0-9\]$ } } } } }.

bugs.title: Incorrect metric restoration on Network Access on disconnect (Windows)
bugs.symptoms: The metric after Network Access disconnect differs from metric before Network Access for default route.
bugs.conditions: Using Network Access on Windows systems.
bugs.impact: A multi-home environment might experience routing issues after disconnecting Network Access, for example, by default traffic might go through Wi-Fi instead of wired networks.
bugs.workaround: Disable and enable the network adapter.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing incorrect metric restoration on Network Access on disconnect.

bugs.title: Slow response from GUI when listing Event Logs
bugs.symptoms: Slow GUI performance in Request Log for Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.conditions: IE8-IE11 used
bugs.impact: Slow GUI performance in Request Log for Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.workaround: You can remove all columns with IP in configuration or reduce number of entries per page
bugs.fix: GeoIP tooltip library rewritten to improve performance in all browsers.

bugs.title: CSRF doesn't apply web application callback registered as XMLHttpRequest.onload in IE8-10
bugs.symptoms: Since Javascript is executed on client side. When it comes to page render, javascript errors might break your page.
bugs.conditions: Using Internet Explorer 8-10 with CSRF ASM enabled.
bugs.impact: Since Javascript is executed on client side. When it comes to page render, javascript errors might break your page.

bugs.title: HTML5 client is not available on APM Full Webtop when using VMware Horizon 6.1
bugs.symptoms: When Horizon v6.1 is deployed using an APM Full webtop, the option to launch the View HTML5 client is missing.
bugs.conditions: VMware Horizon and VMware View agents have been upgraded to v6.1 (v3.4 for clients) or a new v6.1 deployment.
bugs.impact: Users are not able to use HTML5 View client to launch View remote desktops from an APM full webtop.
bugs.workaround: An alternative access methods are available as a temporary workaround to provide access for Horizon users. Administrators can have users use the native VMware View clients instead of using the APM full webtop with the HTML5 View client.
bugs.fix: Starting with release v6.1 of VMware Horizon, the public API that APM uses for integration with View Connection Server has changed. This caused an issue where the View HTML5 client was no longer available to launch View desktops when deployed on an APM Full Webtop. The option to launch a View HTML5 client is now available again on the APM Full Webtop.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Expected Content Value Is Not Set When Setting The responseActionType For A Response Page
bugs.symptoms: When setting the responseActionType, such as "default" or "soap-fault", to a value that has an expected related unmodifiable responseContent value, the expected responseContent is not set. As a result an empty response page is returned when ASM blocks a request.
bugs.conditions: Via ASM REST a client changes the responseActionType from "custom" to "default" or "soap-fault".
bugs.impact: An empty response page is returned when ASM blocks a request.
bugs.workaround: The alternate response body can be set explicitly via REST
bugs.fix: Expected responseContent is now set when changing responseActionType to a static content type like "default" or "soap-fault" using ASM REST.

bugs.title: Incomplete support for special characters in input field names
bugs.symptoms: When HTML input fields with special character in their names were configured for data integrity, false positive alerts were sent
bugs.conditions: HTML fields with special characters in their names.
bugs.impact: False positive automatic transactions (data integirty) alerts.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure data integrity checks on fields with special characters in the name.
bugs.fix: Encoding was fixed and now special characters are supported.

bugs.title: Tab collisions
bugs.symptoms: Multiple tabs writing to the same cookie with different keys.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using FPS.
bugs.impact: False positive alerts for automatic transactions.
bugs.fix: Fix case of multiple tabs writing to the same cookie with different keys.

bugs.title: The audit logs report that there is an unsuccessful attempt to install a mysql user on the system
bugs.symptoms: There are "/usr/sbin/useradd" and "/usr/sbin/groupmod" related errors in '/var/log/auditd/audit.log'
bugs.conditions: Provisioning AFM and/or APM after ASM is already provisioned.
bugs.impact: "/usr/sbin/useradd" and "/usr/sbin/groupmod" related errors in '/var/log/auditd/audit.log' no other impact

bugs.title: String iStat rollup not consistent with multiple blades
bugs.symptoms: An iStat of type string does not merge consistently in a multi-bladed chassis, so the value read on different blades at the same time may differ.
bugs.conditions: The iStat must be of type string, and the chassis must have multiple blades.
bugs.impact: The value of the iStat after the merge differs on different blades.
bugs.workaround: Use clsh to write the string iStat value to all blades together.
bugs.fix: The rollup of strings is based on a timestamp of the last update, but this value was not preserved through the first level of merge so the second level done on each blade was arbitrary. Now, the value is preserved, so the iStat value for multiple blades is correct.

bugs.title: RADIUS Auth/Acct might fail if server response size is more than 2K
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS authentication or accounting fails when a response from the backend server is bigger than 2048 bytes
bugs.conditions: Response from backend server is bigger than 2048 bytes
bugs.impact: RADIUS Auth/Acct agent failed.
bugs.fix: Now RADIUS Auth and RADIUS Acct agents can successfully parse packets of sizes up to 4K, which is the maximum allowed RADIUS packet size. At the moment the BIG-IP system does not support RADIUS packet fragmentation.

bugs.title: CGNAT hairpin connections using multiple route-domains are not supported
bugs.symptoms: When subscribers are in a different route-domain from the route-domain used for the prefix in the LSN pool, hairpin connections cannot be established.
bugs.conditions: The route-domain used on the Virtual Server is different from the route-domain used on the prefix in the LSN pool.
bugs.impact: Subscribers cannot make connections to each other using public (translated) addresses.
bugs.workaround: The routes can be configured so the hairpinning takes place on an external router.

bugs.title: UAC prompt is shown for machine cert check for non-limited users, even if machine cert check service is running
bugs.symptoms: UAC prompt is shown for machine cert check for non-limited users, even if Machine Cert Check service is running on client Windows machine.
bugs.conditions: Current user is non-limited. Machine Cert Check service is running. User tries to pass Access Policy.
bugs.impact: Non-limited user has to press 'ok' in UAC window.
bugs.fix: Now Machine Certificate Check service is used for certificate verification even for non-limited users.

bugs.title: Transaction validation errors on object references
bugs.symptoms: MCP validation error when adding/removing reference and adding/deleting an object in the same transaction.
bugs.conditions: During device group config sync, iControl transactions, and tmsh operations. For example, delete and create the same virtual server and specify a profile/VLAN, or remove a profile from a virtual server and then delete the profile in the same transaction.
bugs.impact: Validation error. The system posts an error similar to the following: transaction failed: 01020066:3: The requested virtual server profile (/Common/vs1 /Common/http1) already exists in partition Common. When deleting, the message is: 01020036:3: The requested virtual server profile (/Common/vs1 http1) was not found.
bugs.workaround: The removal of the object reference must be done in a separate transaction. For example, if you want to delete a profile that is being used, create one transaction removing it from virtual servers, then a second transaction deleting the profile.
bugs.fix: The system now supports adding/removing a reference and the object in a single transaction.

bugs.title: False positive scenario causes SMTP transactions to hang and eventually reset.
bugs.symptoms: Upon specific SMTP traffic, connection hangs and eventually resets.
bugs.conditions: SMTP profile with 'protocol security' turned on is attached to the virtual server, and the response is processed in bulk.
bugs.impact: Connection hangs and eventually resets.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a scenario in which SMTP transactions were hanging and blocked upon specific traffic.

bugs.title: Allow request logs to be filtered by destination IP
bugs.symptoms: Request Log: Missing useful filter by Destination IP.
bugs.impact: Missing a useful filter.
bugs.fix: Filter by Destination IP was added to the Request log.

bugs.title: TSO packet initialization failure due to out-of-memory condition.
bugs.symptoms: TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) packet initialization failure due to out-of-memory condition with the message: packet is locked by a driver.
bugs.conditions: This is related to tmm running out of memory while configured with TSO, on BIG-IP or VIPRION platforms which implement the HSB (High Speed Bridge) device in hardware. This problem may occur on all currently-supported BIG-IP or VIPRION platforms EXCEPT the following: BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series appliances. BIG-IP 1600, 3600 appliances.
bugs.impact: TMM posts the assert message: packet is locked by a driver, then crashes.
bugs.workaround: Disable TSO (for more information, see SOL15609: Overview of TCP Segmentation Offload, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/600/sol15609.html): To enable or disable TSO functionality, you can use the following command syntax: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcpsegmentationoffload value <enable | disable> Note: After modifying the tm.tcpsegmentationoffload database variable, you must restart the TMM daemon by running the bigstart restart tmm command. Restarting TMM temporarily interrupts traffic processing. F5 recommends running this command only during a maintenance window.
bugs.fix: TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) packet is now cleared correctly with no packet-locked message.

bugs.title: Store source port higher than 32767 in Request Log record
bugs.symptoms: Any Request Log record for request with source port higher than 32767 will have source port equal to 32767.
bugs.conditions: Request Log record get wrong source port when source port value of request higher than 32767.
bugs.impact: Request Log record has wrong source port if source port value higher than 32767.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaroud
bugs.fix: The Request log record now gets the correct source port even when the source port value of the request is higher than 32767.

bugs.title: Internal unit test issue found by F5 testing prior to release.
bugs.symptoms: Internal unit test fails, catching an issue with SPDY.
bugs.impact: Unable to compile tmm.
bugs.fix: Resolve an internal build issue found by F5 testing before release.

bugs.title: New iOS-based VPN client may fail to create IPv6 VPN tunnels
bugs.symptoms: Newer iOS-based VPN client does not provide MAC address during IPCP negotiation. This prevents the IPv6 VPN tunnel from getting established.
bugs.conditions: It affects only iOS-based IPv6 VPN connection requests.
bugs.impact: This impacts only IPv6 VPN tunnel requests from iOS-based devices.
bugs.fix: Newer iOS-based VPN clients can successfully create IPv6 VPN tunnels.

bugs.title: [GUI][GTM] GUI does not prefix partition to device-name for BIG-IP DNS Server IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: IP addresses associated with a BIG-IP DNS server object may not be viewable from the Configuration utility.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You use the Configuration utility to create a BIG-IP DNS server object with one or more IP addresses. -- You then use the Configuration utility to add one or more IP addresses to a BIG-IP DNS server object. -- You use the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) to add one or more additional IP addresses to the BIG-IP GTM server object. -- From the Configuration utility, you navigate to DNS :: GSLB :: Servers :: [BIG-IP DNS Server Name] and then view the BIG-IP DNS server object IP addresses in the Address List box.
bugs.impact: Only the BIG-IP GTM server object IP addresses that are added from the tmsh utility display in the Configuration utility. After tmsh modifies the BIG-IP DNS server by adding another IP address, the GUI fails to show those IP addresses previously added using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create and modify IP addresses on BIG-IP DNS servers. Or use only the Configuration utility or only the tmsh utility to create and modify BIG-IP GTM server object IP addresses.
bugs.fix: GUI now adds the partition prefix to device-name for BIG-IP DNS Server IP addresses, so IP addresses associated with a BIG-IP DNS server object are now viewable from the Configuration utility.

bugs.title: connflow_precise_check_begin does not check for NULL
bugs.symptoms: Currently connflow_precise_check_begin does not check for NULL for its parameters while hudproxy has plenty of places where it calls connflow_precise_check_begin with NULL.
bugs.conditions: Connection Rate Limit is configured
bugs.impact: This leads to NULL pointer dereference and subsequent tmm crash
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fix NULL pointer dereference in connflow_precise_check_begin

bugs.title: Change firewall rules with ip-protocol ICMP and ICMP type 0, code 0 cause pccd crash
bugs.symptoms: Change firewall rules with ip-protocol ICMP and ICMP type 0, code 0 cause pccd crash
bugs.conditions: Firewall rules with ip-protocol ICMP and type 0, code 0 are configured and then modified.
bugs.impact: pccd abort.
bugs.fix: Handled the insertion and deletion of icmp type 0/code 0 entries correctly when compiling the firewall rules.

bugs.title: Provide a way to enable connection bar for Citrix desktops only
bugs.symptoms: When connection bar is enabled via Custom Parameters in a Citrix resource it's applied to both applications and desktops.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix replacement mode and connection bar is enabled via Custom Parameters in a Citrix resource.
bugs.impact: Connection bar is displayed for applications where it may not be needed.
bugs.fix: APM now enables connection bar for Citrx desktops by default. This can be disabled by specifying ConnectionBar=0 in Custom Parameters of the Citrix Remote Desktop resource.

bugs.title: Logging profile configuration is updated unnecessarily
bugs.symptoms: Logging profile configuration is updated in the ASM data plane unnecessarily, due to changes in pool member state.
bugs.conditions: Pool member state changes frequently.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary logging profile configuration updates are sent to ASM data plane.
bugs.fix: Logging profile configuration is updated in the ASM data plane only when it is modified, and not unnecessarily.

bugs.title: TMM core when viewing connection table
bugs.symptoms: In very rare conditions tmm may core on viewing the connection table.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when a configuration meets all of the following conditions: - A NAT. - An AFM reject rule for ICMP. The user views the connection table on the system.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not view the connection table when this configuration combination exists.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when viewing the connection table.

bugs.title: [TMSH][GTM] Add validation for special characters like Ctrl+k for gtm object names
bugs.symptoms: GTM objects display ^K characters, cannot be assigned to other objects When editing bigip_gtm.conf using the CLI, it is possible to use some characters in server, virtual server, and pool names. These characters can be saved to the config as a space or as a special character. Characters include ^K ^B, ^N, ^L.
bugs.conditions: Editing bigip_gtm.conf using CLI.
bugs.impact: 1. Config is not displayed properly. 2. Odd problems happen when object has such names, for example, it fails to add virtual server to a server with such names, in 11.5.1 and 11.4.1 virtual servers cannot be assigned to pools, pools to wideips etc.
bugs.workaround: Do not use such characters (CTRL+) for objects.

bugs.title: VXLAN: Remote MAC address movement does not trigger ARL updates across TMMs.
bugs.symptoms: In a VXLAN tunnel, a remote MAC address movement from one endpoint to another does not trigger ARL updates across all TMMs. As a result, some TMMs may contain stale ARL entries which can impact traffic forwarding. Also, when using 'tmsh show net fdb tunnel', there is a duplicated MAC address associated with different endpoints in the same tunnel.
bugs.conditions: When a remote MAC address is moved from one endpoint to another. For example, when a BIG-IP system in an HA setup configured with a masquerading MAC address changes its state from 'standby' to 'active'.
bugs.impact: This issue could impact traffic forwarding in VXLAN tunnels.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no complete workaround, you can mitigate the situation by making sure that the network is properly configured so that every device uses a unique MAC address. For example, in a network with an HA setup, try not to use masquerading MAC addresses.
bugs.fix: This version of software more consistently handles the condition of a remote MAC address being moved from one endpoint to another.

bugs.title: tmm shows stats for unused TCP4 SYN cache and TCP SYN cache.
bugs.symptoms: On the LTM do command 'tmsh show sys mem |grep -i syn', tmm shows stats for unused TCP4 SYN cache and TCP SYN cache.
bugs.conditions: LTM do command 'tmsh show sys mem |grep -i syn'.
bugs.impact: Shows TCP4 SYN cache and TCP SYN cache. These two stats are not used and do not reflect any actual mem usage in LTM.

bugs.title: Modifying an in-use rate-shaping profile may prevent from being rate shaped
bugs.symptoms: Modifying an in-use rate-shaping profile might prevent existing connections from being rate shaped.
bugs.conditions: Modify a rate-shaping profile attached to a virtual server with active connflows.
bugs.impact: Active connflows might no longer be rate shaped.

bugs.title: Running gtm_add can result in error message about encrypted attributes.
bugs.symptoms: Because of changes in the way master keys are handled, running gtm_add may result in an error message and an unloadable LTM configuration.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running gtm_add to connect GTM devices where the master keys are different.
bugs.impact: Configuration will fail to load, with an error similar to the following: Error trying to rekey: 01071769:3: Decryption of the field (secret) for object (/Common/sctp) failed.
bugs.fix: The gtm_add script now saves the BIG-IP configuration (using tmsh save system config) when the master keys are exchanged. This is necessary for proper functioning of configuration parsing and loading.

bugs.title: Rare TMM Cores with TCP SACK and Early Retransmit
bugs.symptoms: In certain isolated cases, TCP profiles with Early Retransmit and SACK enabled will cause a TMM Crash.
bugs.conditions: The connection is not in fast recovery but a SACK hole has been retransmitted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable Early Retransmit in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: Early retransmit now handles corner cases where the SACK scoreboard is empty.

bugs.title: Special internal handling needed when hotfixing the f5base RPM.
bugs.symptoms: Hotfixing f5base could cause LOP based platforms to fail to come up due to the roundabout way management port network config is stored / regenerated.
bugs.conditions: f5base added to a hotfix rollup or EHF.
bugs.impact: The issue needed to be corrected before a hotfix containing a new f5base RPM could be released. Not seen in the field.
bugs.workaround: A work-around was included in the hotfix; changes to the way the management port is configured were introduced into the upcoming release code to avoid similar problems in the future.

bugs.title: Apply policy operation hangs
bugs.symptoms: Apply policy operation hangs. The system logs the following messages in /ts/log/asm_config_server.log: ---------------- F5::SetActive::Impl::send_update_core,,Still waiting for response from bd_agent (XXX seconds) ---------------- Where 'XXX' is ever growing... High CPU usage, by the 'asm_config_server' process, while the apply policy is stuck.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. Apply policy is executed (manually or automatically, by Policy Builder for an example). bd/bd_agent are restarted (for any reason) during the apply policy operation.
bugs.impact: Apply policy operation hangs.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following commands: -- bigstart restart asm. -- pkill -f asm_config_server.
bugs.fix: Apply policy operation now has a timeout threshold, which prevents the apply policy operation from hanging.

bugs.title: Nexthop object can be freed while still referenced by another structure
bugs.symptoms: Use after free of the Nexthop object may cause memory corruption or tmm core.
bugs.conditions: This can happen if the proxy connection takes some time to complete, creating a large enough time window where the nexthop object might be freed.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system might crash. This is a very timing/memory-usage dependent issue that is rarely encountered.
bugs.fix: Management of nexthop object reference counting is more consistent.

bugs.title: SWG Category Lookup using Subject.CN results in a crash if the certificate presented does not have a Subject.CN.
bugs.symptoms: When accessing HTTPS websites (via SWG) that present a certificate without a CN in the subject, a TMM crash occurs.
bugs.conditions: SWG explicit or transparent proxy using Category Lookup in the per-request access policy with Subject.CN as input. The crash only happens when accessing a site that has no CN in the Certificate's subject - this is not a common condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use Category lookup with SNI as input.
bugs.fix: When Category Lookup is configured to use Subject.CN as input, if the certificate subject does not contain a CN, APM processes the error correctly by logging an error.

bugs.title: db variable to disable rate-tracker
bugs.symptoms: Rate-tracker can't be disabled.
bugs.conditions: Internal F5 testing determined certain use cases had rate-tracker enabled when expecting the ability to disable the functionality.
bugs.impact: If you want to disable rate-tracker you are unable to do so.
bugs.fix: Added db variable (dos.globalsflimit) to disable rate-tracker.

bugs.title: gtm listener cannot be listed across partitions
bugs.symptoms: Unable to reference (perform operations: list, create, modify ...) gtm listeners across partitions.
bugs.conditions: -- In one partition. -- Listener in another partition. -- Attempt to perform operations on the listener in the other partition. For example, the current partition is /Common, and a listener exists in /DifferentPartition, and you try to perform operations on the listener under /DifferentPartition.
bugs.impact: Cannot perform any operations on that listener. The listener will be listed as non-existent.
bugs.workaround: Change to the partition where the listener exists before performing any operations on it.
bugs.fix: The system can now reference GTM listeners across partitions.

bugs.title: crypto-failsafe fail condition not cleared when crypto device restored
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP system may not clear a crypto-failsafe condition after recovering from a cryptographic hardware lockup. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: The output of the tmsh show sys ha-status command appears similar to the following example: ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Sys::HA Status Slot Feature Key Action Fail ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 crypto-failsafe cn-crypto-11 failover yes In the /var/log/ltm file, you observe messages similar to the following examples: -- crit tmm[9184]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec cn-crypto-0 queue is stuck. -- notice sod[8874]: 01140029:5: HA crypto_failsafe_t cn-crypto-0 fails action is failover.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP platform uses internal cryptographic hardware (such as, for vCMP, a Nitrox Lite SSL hardware accelerator card) or external cryptographic hardware (such as SafeNet/Thales hardware security module (HSM)). -- The cryptographic hardware fails and subsequently recovers.
bugs.impact: If the crypto-failsafe action is to fail over, you will be unable to activate the BIG-IP system even after the cryptographic hardware recovers.
bugs.workaround: To restore the crypto-failsafe high availability (HA) fail status, restart tmm by issuing the following command: bigstart restart tmm. Note: On VIPRION platforms, this command must be run on the appropriate blade.
bugs.fix: The system now allows the crypto device to be restored and not keep the crypto-failsafe HA status in the fail state.

bugs.title: Server-side DSR tunnel flow never expires
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores and memory exhaustion using Direct Server Return (DSR). DSR establishes a one-way tunnel between the BIG-IP system and the back-end servers using the clients' IP addresses as the tunnel local-address on the BIG-IP system. These flows never expire.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP virtual servers using DSR tunnels to send client traffic to the server.
bugs.impact: Server-side DSR tunnel flow never expires. Because the DSR tunnels use client's IP address as the tunnel local-address and the server's IP address as the tunnel remote-address, a single DSR setup might introduce as many tunnels as the clients' requests. When these tunnels do not expire, the BIG-IP system memory resource might be used up eventually, causing TMM cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Individual DSR tunnels are removed after the corresponding client's user flows expire.

bugs.title: 10.2.1 system with SSL profile specifying ciphers 'DEFAULT:!HIGH:!MEDIUM' fails to upgrade to 11.5.1, 11.5.2, 11.5.3, or 11.6.0.
bugs.symptoms: SSL ciphers 'DEFAULT:!HIGH:!MEDIUM' are allowed in 10.2.1 but will prevent a config from loading in 11.5.1, 11.5.2, 11.5.3, or 11.6.0. This cipher specification is not relevant for software versions 11.5.1, 11.5.2, 11.5.3, or 11.6.0, because all the DEFAULT ciphers fall within HIGH and MEDIUM ciphers. Turning off HIGH and MEDIUM effectively leaves the system with no ciphers to select from. This is the DEFAULT for 11.5.1. !SSLv2:!SSLv3:!MD5:!EXPORT:RSA+AES:RSA+3DES:RSA+RC4:ECDHE+AES:ECDHE+3DES:ECDHE+RC4
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a 10.2.1 system with an SSL profile specifying ciphers 'DEFAULT:!HIGH:!MEDIUM' is used on a system running version 11.5.1, 11.5.2, 11.5.3, or 11.6.0, either by upgrading, or by manual UCS installation. This is an example of such a profile. profile serverssl serverssl-low_encryption { defaults from serverssl ciphers "DEFAULT:!HIGH:!MEDIUM" }
bugs.impact: Upon reboot into version 11.5.1, 11.5.2, 11.5.3, or 11.6.0, or upon load of a UCS from 10.2.1, the configuration fails to load. The operation fails with an error similar to the following. 01070311:3: Ciphers list <list>' for profile <profile name> denies all clients
bugs.workaround: Search for this cipher 'DEFAULT:!HIGH:!MEDIUM' and modify before upgrading. For information about what value to use, see K13156: SSL ciphers used in the default SSL profiles (11.x - 13.x) :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13156.

bugs.title: GTM Fails to change GTM server with IPv4 'Address Translation enabled
bugs.symptoms: Using the GUI when adding an IPv4 address translation, GTM fails to change GTM server that has IPv4 'Address Translation' enabled.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the GUI to add an IPv4 translated address that alphabetically or numerically precedes an existing IPv4 translated address. For example, there is an Address: 192.168.10.12 and Translation: 10.26.10.12, and you add IP address 11.12.10.12.
bugs.impact: GTM server property cannot be updated. When updating GTM server properties, the system posts errors such as the following: 01020037:3: The requested GTM IP (192.168.10.11 /Common/LTM64) already exists.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to make these types of changes.
bugs.fix: Using the GUI when adding an IPv4 address translation, GTM now successfully changes GTM server that has IPv4 'Address Translation' enabled.

bugs.title: OCSP Responder URL is case sensitive, scheme part is required
bugs.symptoms: OCSP Responder fails to initialize if scheme is not specified ("myhost.org" instead of "http://myhost.org") OR scheme is not lowercase ("myHost.org" instead of "http://myhost.org")
bugs.conditions: URL field doesn't contain scheme part (http/https) or scheme part is not all lowercase
bugs.impact: OCSP responder failed to initialize - OCSP authentication fails
bugs.workaround: configure URL starting with http:// or https://
bugs.fix: apm will lowercase scheme part of the specified URL if it's http or https. apm will throw configuration error if scheme is not specified for the URL or wrong scheme provided (anything other than http/https)

bugs.title: Some BIG-IP objects have no tmsh description field so description text configured in GUI is lost on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Some BIG-IP Access Policy objects have no description field in tmsh, but they do have Description field in the GUI. When defining the Description field in the GUI, the content is lost upon upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- Using tmsh. -- Various Access Policy objects. Here are some examples of the GUI counterparts: + Secure connectivity profile (Access Policy :: Secure Connectivity). + Active Directory trusted domains (Access Policy :: AAA Servers :: Active Directory Trusted Domains). + Microsoft Exchange (Access Policy :: Application Access :: Microsoft Exchange). + AAA Servers :: Endpoint Management Systems + SSO Configurations :: HTTP Basic + SSO Configurations :: NTLMV1 + SSO Configurations :: NTLMV2 + SSO Configurations :: Kerberos + SSO Configurations :: Forms + SAML :: BIG-IP IdP Automation
bugs.impact: Cannot use tmsh to specify the description. If there is a description specified using the GUI, that definition is lost upon upgrade.

bugs.title: TMM crash when processing AAM-optimized video URLs
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash when processing HTTP requests for certain types of AAM-optimized videos.
bugs.conditions: AAM-enabled VIP with video optimization and IBR enabled by AAM policy.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable AAM processing of AAM-optimized video URLs.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when processing HTTP requests for certain types of AAM-optimized videos.

bugs.title: TMM Crash on Relative URL
bugs.symptoms: When a relative path that starts with ../ is presented to WAM, the code that attempts to rewrite the URL into an absolute, regular form potentially causes TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: AAM profile on VIP.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: An iRule that removes or modifies the URL path to be non-relative, or at least to start with a forward slash will protect WAM from this issue.
bugs.fix: Fix for relative paths that do not start with a forward slash, but do include parent directory references.

bugs.title: Fluctuating/inconsistent number of health monitors for pool member
bugs.symptoms: The Local Traffic :: Pools :: pool_name :: Members :: pool_member_name displays an inconsistent and fluctuating number of health monitors for a pool member.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you are using partitions (i.e., folders) and route domains, and use the GUI to display the health monitors for a pool member.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine the correct number health monitors for pool member correctly. For example, given a pool which was assigned two health monitors, sometimes the screen will display two health monitors, one or none at all.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to display the health monitors for a pool member.
bugs.fix: The system now displays the correct number of health monitors for pool members for configurations containing administrative partitions and route domains.

bugs.title: Unnecessary ssh key pair exist for root user in AWS and Azure.
bugs.symptoms: Unnecessary ssh key pair exist for root user in AWS and Azure. - root account is by default disabled in VE cloud platforms like AWS and Azure. However, an ssh public-private keypair is created by BIG-IP startup for root user that lives under /root/.ssh/ directory.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE deployment in cloud platforms like AWS and Azure.
bugs.impact: Mostly cosmetic impact as root ssh keypair is unused and unnecessary on BIG-IP VE cloud platforms as root account is by default disabled and only way to access the deployed instance is through the admin account.
bugs.workaround: You can manually delete /var/ssh/root/identity* files to remove unnecessary ssh keypair for the root account created as part of BIG-IP VE startup.
bugs.fix: Not applicable.

bugs.title: Portal Access scripts had not been inserted into HTML page in some cases
bugs.symptoms: If HTML page contains forms with absolute action paths, Portal Access scripts must be inserted into this page. But if there are no other reasons to include them, these scripts were not included.
bugs.conditions: HTML page which consists of the form with absolute action path, for instance: <form action='/cgi-bin/a.gci"> </form>
bugs.impact: The form can not be submitted because browser fires JavaScript error.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to use iRule to insert Portal Access scripts into rewritten HTML page.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access scripts are inserted into HTML page if it contains forms with absolute action path.

bugs.title: [ZRD] A memory leak in Zrd
bugs.symptoms: Memory leaks for zrd when performing multiple wide IP alias updating.
bugs.conditions: When an add, modification, or deletion of a GTM Wide IP Alias is made through the GUI or tmsh there is a small memory leak in zrd. This memory leak is not significant for any one change, but it might become noticeable after hundreds or thousands of changes when viewing memory consumption through 'top' or other tools.
bugs.impact: Memory leak after multiple wide IP alias updates.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, you can mitigate potential system performance impacts by restarting zrd, which clears out the memory usage. To do so, run the command: bigstart restart zrd.
bugs.fix: Memory no longer leaks in zrd when performing multiple wide IP alias updating.

bugs.title: [ZRD] A memory leak in zrd
bugs.symptoms: Memory leaks for zrd when performing wide IP alias updating.
bugs.conditions: When an add, modification, or deletion of a GTM Wide IP Alias is made through the GUI or tmsh, there is a small memory leak in zrd. Although this memory leak is small for any one change, it could be noticeable after hundreds or thousands of changes when viewing memory consumption through 'top' or other tools.
bugs.impact: Memory leak after multiple wide IP alias create/update operations.
bugs.workaround: If the zrd memory usage is negatively impacting system performance, you can restart zrd and clear out the memory usage by running the command: bigstart restart zrd.
bugs.fix: Memory no longer leaks for zrd when performing wide IP alias updating.

bugs.title: Virtual servers with priority groups reset incoming connections when a non-zero connection limit is increased
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server has priority groups and connection limit configured, if the connection limit is reached and is increased while the member is limited, then subsequent connections will be reset rather than allowed.
bugs.conditions: Using priority groups and a non-zero connection limit, with one of the following load balancing methods: least-connections-member, least-sessions, ratio-member, ratio-least-connections-member, ratio-session. The issue occurs when the connection limit is adjusted higher when the connection limit is reached on the high-priority pool.
bugs.impact: New connections are reset without being able to send traffic.
bugs.workaround: If it is feasible to adjust the priorities, adjust the connection limit to its initial value, and adjust the priority groups so that the traffic currently on the limited pool drains out. When the pool has no connections, increase the limit to restore the correct priorities.
bugs.fix: Make pool member eligible for load balancing if its not connection limited after modifying its connection limit.

bugs.title: Delayed ehash initialization causes crash when memory is fragmented.
bugs.symptoms: When first using a new feature (fpm, firewall) under memory fragmentation conditions, if the feature uses an ehash table, TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: Severe memory fragmentation, where contiguous allocations are not satisfied, combined with initial use of a new feature.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Utilize all features shortly after TMM comes up, so all initial allocations are performed.
bugs.fix: Certain allocations are no longer delayed. Delayed allocations which fail retry with smaller sizes, possibly reducing performance.

bugs.title: Active FTP session with inherit profile and address translation disabled may not decrement pool member current connections statistics
bugs.symptoms: Current connections seen in the poolmember statistics via tmsh might show a non-decremented number over time.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - FTP virtual server with address translate disabled. - FTP profile with inherit parent profile. - Active FTP session. Running the command: tmsh show ltm pool pool_name.
bugs.impact: The current connections statistics value does not decrement upon data connection closure. While this is primarily cosmetic, it might impact connections when used in combination with limit calculations.
bugs.workaround: Disable inherit parent profile in the FTP profile.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly represents the pool current connections in the specific configuration combination.

bugs.title: Matched ASM signatures cannot be accessed easily from iRules.
bugs.symptoms: Matched ASM signatures cannot be accessed easily from iRules.
bugs.conditions: A signature was matched.
bugs.impact: It is very difficult to make rules that have different behavior according to specific signatures.
bugs.workaround: The signatures IDs can be seen through the violation_details, but difficult parsing is required to get these and act upon these.
bugs.fix: The following commands have been added to the ASM_REQUEST_DONE event. ASM::signature ids - Returns the IDs of signatures. ASM::signature names - Returns a list with the names of the signatures found in the transaction. ASM::signature set_names - Returns a list with the set names of the signatures. Also note that further fixes added the staged signatures: ASM::signature staged_ids - Returns a list of staged signatures IDs. ASM::signature staged_names - Returns a list of staged signatures names. ASM::signature staged_set_names - Returns a list of staged signatures set names. Note that the signature names list is limited to 3 signatures and the signature IDs list is limited to 10 signatures.
bugs.behavior: iRules commands have been added to retrieve the matched signature IDs, names and sets. The following commands have been added to the ASM_REQUEST_DONE event. ASM::signature ids - Returns the IDs of signatures. ASM::signature names - Returns a list with the names of the signatures found in the transaction. ASM::signature set_names - Returns a list with the set names of the signatures. Also note that further fixes added the staged signatures: ASM::signature staged_ids - Returns a list of staged signatures IDs. ASM::signature staged_names - Returns a list of staged signatures names. ASM::signature staged_set_names - Returns a list of staged signatures set names. Note that the signature names list is limited to 3 signatures and the signature IDs list is limited to 10 signatures.

bugs.title: Certain ICMP packets are evaluated twice against Global and Route Domain ACL rules.
bugs.symptoms: Certain ICMP packets (such as ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable) match twice against Global and Route-Domain ACL rules.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned and licensed. Create a Global and/or Route Domain ACL policy with a rule matching ICMP traffic. Send ICMP packet such as Destination Unreachable.
bugs.impact: Global and Route-Domain ACL rules are evaluated twice under conditions specified above. This causes the rule counters to be incremented by 2 (instead of 1) and may cause double logging if enabled.
bugs.fix: ICMP traffic is now evaluated only once against Global and Route-Domain ACL rules.

bugs.title: Event Logs -> Brute Force Attacks can't show details after navigating to another page
bugs.symptoms: After using the pagination mechanism on the Brute Force Attacks screen, the user is unable to open the attack details.
bugs.conditions: Navigate to another page on Event Logs -> Brute Force Attacks
bugs.impact: The user is unable to see the brute force attack details.
bugs.fix: The pagination mechanism was fixed on the Brute Force Attacks screen.

bugs.title: Intermittent TMM core when using DNS cache with forward zones
bugs.symptoms: TMM can intermittently crash when using the DNS cache resolver.
bugs.conditions: When a cache configuration is "removed" there are conditions where a refcount is not properly managed that would lead to memory being deleted before the last user is done with it.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM will no longer intermittently core when using the DNS cache resolver.

bugs.title: Update EPSEC package to latest verified in 11.6.0 branch
bugs.symptoms: EPSEC was out of date and we are updating to the latest.
bugs.impact: EPSEC contains old package and some endpoint security checks like machine cert, antivirus, firewall might fail.
bugs.fix: 11.6.0 branch contains most recent verified EPSEC package.

bugs.title: BD crash on specific signature sets configuration.
bugs.symptoms: A BD crash, failover and/or traffic interruption.
bugs.conditions: Two different signature sets with different sizes (i.e, number of signatures in a set) are assigned to two different security policies. The issue relates to a scenario where there is traffic that generates a lot of violations/staging or suggestions.
bugs.impact: A BD crash, a failover, and/or traffic interruption.
bugs.workaround: Assign the same set(s) to all the security policies.
bugs.fix: Crash issue that is related to a specific configuration was fixed.

bugs.title: bd agent listens on all addresses instead of the localhost only
bugs.symptoms: bd agent listens on all addresses instead of the localhost only.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned.
bugs.impact: bd agent might crash in reponse to a simple telnet request from an external connection.
bugs.fix: bd agent now listens on localhost only.

bugs.title: Multiple teardown conditions can cause crash
bugs.symptoms: When iRules direct the teardown of a TCP connection after some delay, another event might tear down the connection during the delay. When the iRule-directed abort finally arrives, the system crashes.
bugs.conditions: (1) An iRule or other cross-layer message can trigger a ABORT after teardown. (2) The TCP profile has settings that invoke the correct TCP implementation: (a) 11.5.x: mptcp is enabled (b) 11.6.x: mptcp, rate-pace, or tail-loss-probe are enabled, OR TCP uses Vegas, Illinois, Woodside, CHD, CDG, Cubic, or Westwood congestion control.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Suspend iRules with this behavior.
bugs.fix: When receiving ABORT commands, TCP catches cases where the connection is already closed.

bugs.title: Sweep and flood may crash if it is enabled when AFM is not licensed or provisioned.
bugs.symptoms: When AFM is not not licensed or provisioned, the user might still be able to enable Sweep and Flood.
bugs.conditions: Enable Sweep and Flood vector when AFM is not not licensed or provisioned.
bugs.impact: TMM might crash.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuring Sweep and Flood vectors when AFM is not licensed or provisioned
bugs.fix: Sweep and flood may crash if it is enabled when AFM is not licensed or provisioned, user should avoid configuring sweep and flood vectors when AFM is not licensed or provisioned.
