bugs.title: Tcl monitor not working with Courier IMAP server
bugs.symptoms: Tcl monitor produces FTP error with Courier IMAP server.
bugs.conditions: Courier IMAP Server when there is no message in the mailbox.
bugs.impact: IMAP monitor fails, potentially resulting in downed pool members. The systems posts an error similar to the following: ERROR: failed to complete the transfer, error code: 8 error message: FTP: weird server reply.
bugs.workaround: Add a message to the monitored mailbox.
bugs.fix: IMAP TCL monitor now works without error with Courier IMAP server when the monitored mailbox is empty.

bugs.title: 5% drop in Webroot cloud lookup performance with mixed upper/lowercase URLs
bugs.symptoms: When Webroot cloud lookup is enabled, and URL inputs cannot be categorized by the local Webroot database managed on the BIG-IP system because the URLs contain a mix of upper/lowercase characters, there may be 5% drop in the Webroot cloud lookup performance.
bugs.conditions: If Webroot cloud lookup is enabled, and all URLs are unknown to the local databasedand consist of a mix of upper/lowercase letters.
bugs.impact: There could be 5% drop for Webroot cloud lookup performance in this case. This only occurs when Webroot cloud lookup enabled. The Webroot cloud lookup features is disabled by default.
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed by improving/optimizing URL normalization prior to Webroot cloud lookup.

bugs.title: TMM core when multiple PPTP calls from the same client
bugs.symptoms: TMM can core when there are multiple PPTP calls arrive from the same client.
bugs.conditions: PPTP ALG virtual server with CGNAT.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when multiple PPTP calls arrives from the same client.

bugs.title: Config load fails after upgrading from v11.6.1 to v12.0.0
bugs.symptoms: Config load fails after upgrading from v11.6.1 to v12.0.0: Error: fatal: (Can't load component definition 'service_policy_global' for command 'service-policy-global') (framework/SchemaCmd.cpp, line 279), exiting.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Application Acceleration Manager (AAM) is provisioned and configured on v11.6.1, then you upgrade to version v12.0.0.
bugs.impact: Config load fails.
bugs.workaround: Since 11.6.1 came after 12.0.0 was released, upgrade from 11.6.1 to 12.1.0 instead.

bugs.title: Unique truncated SNMP OIDs.
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP generates SNMP OID-required truncation in order to stay within the OID max length limit of 128, the truncated OID is not always consistent or unique.
bugs.conditions: An SNMP table has a unique index (key) consisting of one or more table attributes of various types. String type index attributes with values lengths approaching or exceeding 128 characters expose this truncation issue.
bugs.impact: SNMP get, get-next, and set commands might fail or even operate on incorrect data when the target OID is not consistent or unique.
bugs.workaround: The long string values triggering this issue are typically identified as user-supplied names that were introduced as part of BIG-IP configuration. Often these names can be reconfigured to a shorter length.
bugs.fix: Truncated OIDs are now appended with a unique check-sum value that remains unchanged from one query to the next.

bugs.title: Repeated BD cores.
bugs.symptoms: The bd process crashes and produces a core file in the /var/core directory.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what conditions trigger the crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a bd core related to tcl processing

bugs.title: LSN pool with small port range may not use all ports
bugs.symptoms: When LSN pool port range is small, some ports may not be used for translation.
bugs.conditions: LSN pool port range is small.
bugs.impact: Even though free ports are available, they are not used for translation and the connection fails
bugs.workaround: Set the LSN pool port range to default value of 1025 - 65535

bugs.title: Configuration objects with more than four vlans in vlan list may cause memory utilization to increase over time
bugs.symptoms: tmm memory growth over time.
bugs.conditions: Conditions leading to this issue include: one or more virtual servers, NATs, SNATs, or LSNs with more than four VLANS in a vlan allow or vlan deny list.
bugs.impact: tmm memory usage can grow over time eventually causing memory exhaustion.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: Minimize the number of VLANs in the VLAN list for virtual servers, NATs, SNATs and LSNs. Minimize the number of configurations changes to Self-IPs, virtual servers, NATs, SNATs and LSNs.
bugs.fix: Configuration objects with more than four vlans in vlan list no longer causes memory utilization to increase over time.

bugs.title: PVA stats only being reported on virtual-server and system-level basis.
bugs.symptoms: The VLAN/interfaces stats do not include PVA stats. PVA stats are reported on a per-virtual-server including virtual server plus pool and pool members.
bugs.conditions: Viewing PVA stats.
bugs.impact: Interfaces stats only count TMM software traffic stats, and do not include PVA traffic stats. Although this is by design, it makes it difficult to monitor per-VLAN throughput on their devices.
bugs.workaround: Retrieve pool member PVA stats for server-side PVA stats on the associated VLANs. Also look at PVA stats in the virtual server stats for client-side PVA stats. Note: On the client side, the virtual server might be configured to run on multiple VLANs, so the client-side details are not included in the stats.
bugs.behavior: Unknown
bugs.fix: The system now reports per-device PVA traffic stats in VLAN and interface stats.

bugs.title: Using qos_score command in RULE_INIT event causes TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when the iRule with qos_score command in RULE_INIT event is added to a wide IP.
bugs.conditions: Configured iRule with qos_score command in RULE_INIT event that is added to a wide IP.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: Do not use qos_score command in RULE_INIT event.
bugs.fix: qos_score command is disallowed in RULE_INIT event.

bugs.title: TMM may not reset connection when receiving an ICMP error
bugs.symptoms: Connection is not reset after receiving an ICMP error
bugs.conditions: TMM receives an ICMP error after sending a TCP/SYN on a FastL4 virtual
bugs.impact: Delayed shutdown of connection
bugs.fix: TMM will now reset FastL4 connections when receiving an ICMP error in response to TCP/SYN.

bugs.title: Server side timewait close state causes long establishment under port reuse
bugs.symptoms: When the server TCP connection is under timewait closing state, if a new client connection is initiated toward the server under the BIG-IP SYN-Cookie mode, the server respond with ACK instead of SYN+ACK for the SYN received. The BIG-IP system drops this ACK and retransmit the SYN, till timeout occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 is under SYN-Cookie mode. -- The previous server connection is under time wait close state. -- New client connection is reusing the port to get to the same server TCP connection.
bugs.impact: Longer establishment time and retry.
bugs.fix: When ACK is received instead of SYN+ACK in this case, the system resets the server side to quick recovery, ensuring a quick recovery.

bugs.title: "Session variables" report may show empty if session variable value contains non-English characters
bugs.symptoms: "Session variables" report may show empty if session variable value contains non-English characters
bugs.conditions: For active session only.
bugs.impact: User cannot see the Session Variable information for active session.
bugs.workaround: Use English characters for network configuration, such as host name, user name...
bugs.fix: "Session variables" report shows correct information for any language characters.

bugs.title: Assertion 'valid proxy' can occur after a configuration change with active IVS flows.
bugs.symptoms: When a configuration update or sync takes place while there are active connections on an affected internal virtual server (IVS), and a new connection is initiated during the update, the TMM can assert 'valid proxy' and crash. If there were are no preexisting active connections, the assertion does not occur, but connections initiated during the configuration update might be in a bad state and cause unpredictable effects.
bugs.conditions: 1. Active flows exist on an internal virtual server (IVS). Necessary to trigger the assertion. 2. A configuration update or sync affecting that IVS is in progress. 3. A new connection is initiated to that IVS during the update.
bugs.impact: This is intermittent and rarely encountered. When all preexisting connection flows on this IVS tear down, a 'valid proxy' assertion can trigger and cause a TMM crash and restart, resulting in lost connections across the BIG-IP system or blade. New IVS connection flows initiated during the configuration update might be in a bad state and exhibit unpredictable effects, even if there is no crash.
bugs.workaround: Try to avoid configuration changes affecting any IVS while connections are active. This is intermittent so most likely will not manifest, even with active connections.
bugs.fix: When a configuration update or sync takes place while there are active connections on an affected internal virtual server (IVS), new connections fail and log an error message indicating that the IVS is not ready for connections. If the connections are to an ICAP server, the BIG-IP system performs the service-down-action configured in the request-adapt or response-adapt profile of the virtual server that attempted to initiate the connection. There are no assertions or unpredictable effects. Any new connections that failed for this reason may be retried after the configuration update is complete.

bugs.title: Revised AWS Setup Guide
bugs.symptoms: tmsh is now the default shell for AWS VE. Documentation revised to remove "tmsh" from all tmsh command line entries.
bugs.conditions: Log in to an SSH session with the AWS VE. Initiate any tmsh command by starting the entry with "tmsh." The result is a syntax error.
bugs.impact: No tmsh commands can be executed. Without the ability to revise the AWS virtual machine (VM) password using tmsh, the VM can not be used.
bugs.workaround: Omit the word "tmsh" from command entries.
bugs.fix: Documentation revised to clarify tmsh command entries.

bugs.title: Linux command line client fails with on-demand cert
bugs.symptoms: Linux command line client fails with On-Demand Cert Auth.
bugs.conditions: End user needs to be running Linux command line client and the On-Demand Cert Auth agent.
bugs.impact: Depending upon the access policy, the user might fail to log in and establish a Network Access connection.
bugs.fix: Linux command line client works with On-Demand Cert Auth now.

bugs.title: TMSH listing with wildcards prevents the child object from being displayed
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh list command is attempted with an identifier that specifies use of wildcard match character (*) , the results returned may not print the nested objects contained within the parent object. For example, the list ltm pool* command will print all pools that begin with the word pool, but will fail to list the profiles that are within the pool.
bugs.conditions: tmsh list with a wildcard character specified for parent object.
bugs.impact: Missing details of nested objects when tmsh list is invoked with wildcard character (*) specified in the object identifier
bugs.fix: The tmsh list with a wildcard character specified in the object identifier result contains all the nested objects. For the example specified, the results would now be as follows: (tmos)# list ltm pool pool* ltm pool pool-http-1 { members { 10.1.3.1:http { address 10.1.3.1 inherit-profile disabled profiles { nvgre { } } } } } The missing profile objects are now listed correctly, as expected.

bugs.title: Woodside falsely detects congestion
bugs.symptoms: The TCP profile Congestion Control Woodside falsely detects congestion and might reduce its own performance.
bugs.conditions: High-bandwidth, low-delay connections (i.e., a large congestion window).
bugs.impact: Performance impact when using the Woodside congestion control algorithm, and TMM might crash.
bugs.workaround: Use a TCP profile Congestion Control other than Woodside.
bugs.fix: The Woodside congestion control algorithm now correctly detects congestion without false alarms.

bugs.title: IKEv1 for IPsec does not work when VLAN cmp-hash is set to non-default values
bugs.symptoms: When the cmp-hash of the VLAN interface used by IKEv1 is set to non-default values (dst-ip or src-ip) for load-balancing IKEv1 traffic purposes; IKEv1 will fail.
bugs.conditions: The VLAN interface used for IKEv1 traffic sets its cmp-hash value to non-default values.
bugs.impact: IPsec does not work.
bugs.workaround: Set the cmp-hash value of the VLAN interface for IKEv1 traffic to "default".
bugs.fix: IKEv1 can re-establish its IKE SAs after the VLAN with IKEv1 traffic changes its cmp-hash setting (currently available options are "default, src-ip, dst-ip).

bugs.title: HTML5 Receivers for Storefront 2.5 and 2.1 are not working on Google Chrome 40+
bugs.symptoms: Google Chrome version 40+ shows JavaScript errors when using HTML5 Receivers for Storefront 2.5 and 2.1.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix proxy or replacement and HTML5 Receivers for Storefront 2.5 or 2.1 are used.
bugs.impact: HTML5 Receivers for Storefront 2.5 or 2.1 can't be used.
bugs.workaround: Need to edit the HTML5 receiver files as suggested by Citrix. http://discussions.citrix.com/topic/361040-storefront-21-html5-broken-on-chrome-v40/ 1) Edit SessionWindow.html file at "C:\Program Files\Citrix\Receiver StoreFront\HTML5Client\src\SessionWindow.html" 2) Find <meta http-equiv="content-security-policy" content="default-src 'none'; 3) Add child-src directive <meta http-equiv="content-security-policy" content="default-src 'none'; child-src 'self';

bugs.title: User failed to get profile license in VIPRION 4800 chassis if slot 1 is not enabled
bugs.symptoms: Connection is reset when user tries to log on to an APM virtual server. APM log shows ERR_NOT_FOUND while getting profile license.
bugs.conditions: The issue happens if slot 1 in a VIPRION 4800 chassis is not occupied or is occupied but not enabled.
bugs.impact: User logon failure.
bugs.workaround: Detach APM access profile from the virtual server and then reattach it.
bugs.fix: Access policies now work properly in VIPRION 4800 with no slot1.

bugs.title: bigd process uses a large percentage of CPU
bugs.symptoms: With a very large number of monitors, the bigd process can consume more than 80% CPU when a slow HTTP server returns an error.
bugs.conditions: ~8000 HTTP/HTTPS monitors, and a slow HTTP server returns a 500 error.
bugs.impact: bigd process uses a large percentage of CPU.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of repeated headers
bugs.symptoms: If a http/2 request, forwarded to an http/1.1, produces a response that has the same header occurring more than once, the http/2 response would be encoded incorrectly and can't be processed by the http/2 browser.
bugs.conditions: Responses that contain the same header (with possibly different values) more than once.
bugs.impact: Browser fail to process responses.
bugs.workaround: For the set-cookie header there is no work-around because each cookie requires its own header. For other headers, an iRule could potentially be used to concatenate the values of repeated headers.
bugs.fix: The http/2 protocol handling now correctly encodes repeated headers.

bugs.title: Multiple Relay in DHCP relay is not working.
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP is behind another DHCP relay, then the packets are not sent to the server, instead they are dropped.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a DHCP virtual server is configured with a profile based on dhcpv4_fwd.
bugs.impact: This used to work on 11.4.x so if you are running on version 11.4.x and upgrade to 11.6.x, the virtual server may not function correctly.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, do the following: 1. Configure a unicast IP address for the BIG-IP DHCPv4 listener destination address field. 2. Configure the same IP address as the DHCP server IP address on DHCP relay agent. This way the BIG-IP system can load balance DHCP load on to a pool of DHCP servers.
bugs.fix: Multiple Relay in DHCP relay is now working.

bugs.title: TMM may have a CPU spike if match cross persist is used.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may have a CPU spike. A few(very few) connections may fail.
bugs.conditions: 1) Match cross persist is used. 2) Long idle time out makes the symptom worse. 3) Persist HA makes the symptom worse.
bugs.impact: TMM may have a CPU spike. A few(very few) connections may fail.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using match across persist.
bugs.fix: Match across persistence no longer causes CPU spike.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system may erroneously remove an iApp association from the virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may erroneously remove an iApp association from the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when merging configurations in tmsh, in iControl when using Management.ChangeControl.put_config, and during incremental sync when the iApp is modified, but there is no modification to the virtual server. There are two sets of conditions under which this issue might occur: 1. iApp, virtual server, and persistence profile are configured and associated prior to merge. 2. - High availability pair defined over a Device Group with Incremental Sync specified (that is, Full Sync is disabled). - iApp with one or more virtual servers deployed on one or more peers. - iApp is reconfigured on one of the peers with no modification of the Virtual Server configuration. - Config sync to a peer unit.
bugs.impact: This removes iApp association with the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you should add the affected virtual server name to the list of commands during the merge process. For example, you should add ltm virtual server iApp-test_vs { } to the tmsh merge script during the merge process: cli admin-partitions { update-partition Common } ltm persistence source-addr /Common/put-config-test { app-service none defaults-from /Common/source_addr mirror enabled timeout 300 } ltm virtual iApp-test_vs { }
bugs.fix: Modifying a persistence profile while updating a partition during a merge config no longer disassociates the iApp from the virtual server.

bugs.title: SSL reports certificate verification OK even verification returns failure for pcm=request.
bugs.symptoms: When peer certificate mode (PCM) is configured as request, even if the certificate is invalid (certificate verification returns failure), SSL returns OK.
bugs.conditions: Client authenticate is configured with pcm=request.
bugs.impact: SSL returns the incorrect verification result.
bugs.fix: Client authentication is configured with peer certificate mode (PCM) is configured as request, SSL now returns the correct verification result.

bugs.title: DTLS may send corrupted records when the DB variable tmm.ssl.dtlsmaxcrs is not the default value 1.
bugs.symptoms: DTLS may send corrupted records when the DB variable tmm.ssl.dtlsmaxcrs is not the default value 1.
bugs.conditions: When DB variable tmm.ssl.dtlsmaxcrs is not 1.
bugs.impact: DTLS sends corrupted record.
bugs.workaround: Set tmm.ssl.dtlsmaxcrs to 1.
bugs.fix: DTLS no longer sends corrupted records when DB variable tmm.ssl.dtlsmaxcrs is not default value 1.

bugs.title: Gateways for excluded address space routes are not adjusted correctly during roaming between networks on Windows machines
bugs.symptoms: Gateways for excluded address space routes are not adjusted correctly during roaming between networks on Windows machines.
bugs.conditions: Client Windows machine roams between different networks (Wi-Fi or Ethernet) when the BIG-IP system has configured split-tunneling.
bugs.impact: Excluded address space routes are not applied.
bugs.fix: Fixed reason causing this issue; now excluded address routes are applied correctly even if a client machine roams between different networks.

bugs.title: After upgrade from any pre-11.4.x to 11.4.x through 12.0.0, the configured redirect URL location is empty.
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade from any pre-11.4.x to 11.4.x through 12.0.0, the configured redirect URL location is empty.
bugs.conditions: 1) ASM is provisioned and there is a redirect URL configured on any pre-11.4.x. 2) Upgrade to 11.4.x, 11.5.3, or 11.6.0. This does not occur in 11.5.4, 11.6.1, or 12.0.0 and beyond.
bugs.impact: The configured redirect URL location is empty.
bugs.fix: The configured redirect URL location is now preserved after upgrade from any pre-11.4.x to 11.4.x through 12.0.0.

bugs.title: Full ASM Config Sync was happening too often in a Full Sync Auto-Sync Device Group
bugs.symptoms: ASM is only supposed to request a Full Sync if there has been a Manual Full Sync request, or if an incremental / auto sync indicates that the state is inconsistent with that of its peers. The system was mistakenly requesting a Full Sync on every config change in an Auto-Sync, Full Sync group even when it was in a consistent state.
bugs.conditions: A Device Group is configured with Auto-Sync, Full Sync, and ASM enabled.
bugs.impact: Noise on the network, extra CPU usage, Policy Builder restarting on receiving peer.
bugs.workaround: Disable "Full Sync" on the device group
bugs.fix: The system no longer requests a Full ASM Configuration Sync on every full auto sync in a device group.

bugs.title: devmgmtd file object leak
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, devmgmtd might leak file descriptors.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when attempting to add a device to trust by specifying a hostname instead of an IP address, where this hostname is not valid.
bugs.impact: devmgmtd may restart, logging an error that it has 'too many open files'. Although the failed reaction is correct (restarting because there is an existing error condition), the system presents an error message that does not indicate the issue.
bugs.fix: devmgmtd no longer leaks file descriptors in a certain error path (which would sometimes cause it to dump core).

bugs.title: Multiple TCP keepalive timers for same Fast L4 flow
bugs.symptoms: Multiple TCP keepalive timers for same Fast L4 flow.
bugs.conditions: Fast L4 profile with TCP Keepalive option enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM core.
bugs.workaround: Disable TCP Keepalive option from the Fast L4 profile.
bugs.fix: Prevent starting multiple TCP keepalive timer for the same fastL4 flow

bugs.title: Rarely occurring SOD core causes failover.
bugs.symptoms: Spontaneous failover occurs rarely due to a SOD core dump.
bugs.conditions: Cannot reproduce the issue reliably, so conditions for the crash are unknown.
bugs.impact: When SOD cores, all traffic groups fail over to another device. Non-mirrored flows will be interrupted.
bugs.fix: Errors in handling memory have been fixed to prevent allocation failure.

bugs.title: ZoneRunner might fail when loading valid zone files.
bugs.symptoms: ZoneRunner might fail to load valid zone files which contain two or more consecutive lines which are $TTL directives, blank lines, comment-only lines, or some combination of the above.
bugs.conditions: DNS : Zones : Zonerunner : Zone List: Create. Select 'Load from File' in Records Creation Method.
bugs.impact: The user cannot load a zone file via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Workaround 1: Remove consecutive blank lines, and comment-only lines from the zone file before uploading it to the GUI. Specify the domain in the line following any $ directive lines before uploading the zone file to the GUI. Workaround 2: 1. Freeze zones, stop zrd. 2. Copy zone file from donor GTM to new GTM. 3. Check and adjust chown of zone file. 4. Start zrd, thaw zones. 5. Restart named.
bugs.fix: ZoneRunner will no longer crash when parsing zone files containing $TTL directives, blank lines, comment-only lines, or some combination of the above.

bugs.title: ZoneRunner might fail to load valid zone files.
bugs.symptoms: ZoneRunner might fail to load valid zone files which contain two or more consecutive lines which are $TTL directives, blank lines, comment-only lines, or some combination of the above.
bugs.conditions: DNS : Zones : Zonerunner : Zone List: Create. Select 'Load from File' in Records Creation Method.
bugs.impact: The user cannot load a zone file via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Workaround 1: Remove consecutive blank lines, and comment-only lines from the zone file before uploading it to the GUI. Specify the domain in the line following any $ directive lines before uploading the zone file to the GUI. Workaround 2: 1. Freeze zones, stop zrd. 2. Copy zone file from donor GTM to new GTM. 3. Check and adjust chown of zone file. 4. Start zrd, thaw zones. 5. Restart named.
bugs.fix: ZoneRunner now successfully loads zone files that contain $TTL directives, blank lines, comment-only lines, or some combination of the above.

bugs.title: Portal Access: JavaScript in Shift-JIS encoding may be handled incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: Since Shift-JIS character encoding scheme uses yen character in place of backslash, JavaScript code with backslashes may be handled incorrectly by Portal Access. This may lead to incorrect web application behavior.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page or JavaScript file with Shift-JIS encoding scheme. - JavaScript code with backslashes.
bugs.impact: JavaScript code with backslashes cannot be parsed by Portal Access if the code uses Shift-JIS character encoding.
bugs.fix: Now JavaScript code with Shift-JIS character encoding scheme and backslashes inside the code is handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: URLs with backslashes in the path may not be handled correctly in Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Safari, Chrome, Edge and Internet Explorer support backslashes in URL path and treat them as slashes. But Portal Access converts backslashes in URLs to slashes explicitly; this may cause unexpected results in some web applications. Note that FireFox has no such support.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with URL with backslashes in the path, for example: <a href=http://some.com\some\path/file.ext>
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: In some cases it is possible to modify rewritten URLs by iRule.
bugs.fix: Now URLs with backslashes are supported correctly by Portal Access for all browsers except for Internet Explorer 7--9 and FireFox.

bugs.title: tmsh listing of a nonexistent ltm monitor returns incorrect results.
bugs.symptoms: tmsh listing of a nonexistent ltm monitor returns incorrect results. (tmos)# list ltm monitor gateway-icmp http ltm monitor gateway-icmp http { adaptive disabled destination *:* interval 5 time-until-up 0 timeout 16 user-defined IP_TOS 0 user-defined SEND "GET /\r\n" }. Note there is no gateway-icmp monitor named http present. The output corresponds to the HTTP monitor.
bugs.conditions: The issue arises only when querying for a nonexistent monitor whose name matches a valid monitor type, for example, http, https, icmp, and so on.
bugs.impact: tmsh listing of a nonexistent ltm monitor returns incorrect results. For example, the following command returns a gateway-icmp http configuration even though it does not exist: (tmos)# list ltm monitor gateway-icmp http.
bugs.workaround: Use the following command to return the correct results: tmsh list ltm monitor gateway-icmp gateway-icmp. (tmos)# list ltm monitor gateway-icmp does_not_exist 01020036:3: The requested monitor (/Common/does_not_exist) was not found. The listing of non-existing monitor also returns an error as expected.

bugs.title: RSA key with DSA-signed or ECDSA-signed certificate silently fails handshake.
bugs.symptoms: RSA key with DSA-signed or ECDSA-signed certificate silently fails handshake.
bugs.conditions: The key cert pair type matches one of the following combinations: 1. RSA key/DSA-signed cert. 2. RSA key/ECDSA-signed cert.
bugs.impact: When this kind of key/cert pair is configured in a Client SSL profile that is used by a virtual server, the SSL handshake to the virtual server fails.
bugs.workaround: Do not use this kind of 'hybrid' key/cert pair in the Client SSL profile. Instead, use the combination such as RSA key/RSA-signed cert, EC key/ECDSA-signed cert, or DSA key/DSA-signed cert.
bugs.fix: An RSA key with DSA-signed or ECDSA-signed cert no longer fails the SSL handshake. You can now configure those in the Client SSL profile and the SSL handshake completes as expected.

bugs.title: Add client type detection for Microsoft Edge browser
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft Edge browser cannot be detected by Client Type action item agent in access policy.
bugs.conditions: Microsoft Edge browser, Client Type action item agent in access policy on BIG-IP APM.
bugs.impact: Microsoft Edge browser is not detected by Client Type action item and the webtop might not display properly or might display resources that are not supported.
bugs.fix: Improvement: Microsoft Edge browser is now detected properly and only supported resources are shown on the webtop now. All components that require ActiveX are not supported.

bugs.title: Unable to log out of the GUI in IE8
bugs.symptoms: "Log out" button doesn't work in Microsoft Internet Explorer version 8 (IE8).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when clicking the "Log out" button in the GUI while using IE8.
bugs.impact: You cannot log out with the "Log out" button
bugs.workaround: Close and reopen IE8.
bugs.fix: You can now log out with the "Log out" button in Microsoft Internet Explorer version 8 (IE8).

bugs.title: NAT traffic group inheritance does not sync across devices
bugs.symptoms: When a NAT object is created, and its inherited-traffic-group property is set, this property does not sync to other devices.
bugs.conditions: This is relevant for any setup with multiple devices in a CMI failover device group.
bugs.impact: The inherited-traffic-group property must be manually maintained on all devices.
bugs.workaround: Enable the 'full sync' option instead of using incremental sync.
bugs.fix: NAT traffic group inheritance now syncs across devices using incremental sync.

bugs.title: CSS minification can on occasion remove necessary whitespace
bugs.symptoms: CSS minification can on occasion remove necessary whitespace. Example of incorrectly minified content: //Comment1 @import url("http://example.com/test.jpeg"); becomes //Comment1@import url("http://example.com/test.jpeg");
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using minification on CSS.
bugs.impact: CSS minification might remove necessary whitespace.
bugs.workaround: Disable minification on CSS.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue which was causing removal of necessary whitespaces in CSS minification.

bugs.title: AVR-HTTP (and Application DoS): Detection of pool-member is sometimes incorrect
bugs.symptoms: AVR sometimes detects the incorrect BIG-IP module that created a response to an HTTP transaction.
bugs.conditions: Using AVR HTTP profile or Application DoS, and having a transaction that was responded to by a BIG-IP modules, such as DoS, Cache, iRules, and so on.
bugs.impact: 1. AVR report an incorrect module. 2. Application DoS is using this information for its decisions, and thus can choose a mitigation action that is different from the desired one.
bugs.fix: The detection of the internal module is done correctly, so that the correct mitigation action is chosen.

bugs.title: SNMP requests fail and subsnmpd reports that it has been terminated.
bugs.symptoms: After an unspecified period of time, SNMP requests fail and subsnmpd reports that it has been terminated.
bugs.conditions: SNMP polls sent to a system start to fail after a few days, until subsnmpd is restarted. When in the failed state, you can determine the status of subsnmpd by running the following command: tmsh show sys services. Here is an example of the status when the system is in this state: subsnmpd run (pid 4649) 26 days, got TERM.
bugs.impact: Loss of snmp data set to a client. The /var/log/snmpd.log contains numerous messages similar to the following: Received broken packet. Closing session. The /var/log/sflow_agent.log contains numerous messages similar to the following: AgentX session to master agent attempted to be re-opened.
bugs.workaround: Restart subsnmpd using the following command: bigstart restart subsnmpd.
bugs.fix: SNMP requests handling has been improved to ensure that requests no longer fail after a number of days.

bugs.title: bigd detection and logging of load and overload
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is configured with a very large number of monitor instances (multiple thousands) probing at relatively fast intervals, BIG-IP may not be able to keep up with its servicing load. This can be indicated by pool members being marked down/up (flapping) that were not actually having connectivity problems.
bugs.conditions: Heavy monitor instance probe rate (monitor instance probes per second).
bugs.impact: When overloaded, bigd is unable to probe consistently which may result in odd or unpredictable pool member up/down behavior.
bugs.workaround: The main way to mitigate overload issues is either to reduce the number of monitor instances, to increase the probe time to probe less often, and/or to switch monitored pool members/nodes to simpler, lower-overhead monitor (i.e. ICMP instead of HTTP, or HTTP instead of HTTPS).
bugs.fix: This particular fix does not change the problem or mitigation steps. Rather, it helps detect when overloading has occurred. When it has been determined that overloading has occurred, a message will be logged to /var/log/ltm to indicate this. By default, the overload message will be triggered if the main 1/10 second (100 ms) loop takes, on average, more than 150 ms to service. This overload threshold value can be adjusted with the new Bigd.Overload.Latency sys db variable. The variable indicates the number of ms latency at which servicing the 100 ms main loop is considered overload. In addition, main loop latency logging has been added to /var/log/bigdlog. The latency information will be logged every 15 seconds. The main loop latency information will be logged whenever Bigd.Debug is enabled, or if the new sys db variable Bigd.Debug.TimingStats is enabled. The new Bigd.Debug.TimingStats variable allows the main loop latency stats to be emitted even if other debug information, which can be quite verbose, is suppressed. The main loop latency information is such: insts, avg-5m mean-5m stddev5, avg-1m mean-1m stddev1 insts: # of active monitor instances being monitored avg-5m: weighted decaying average loop latency over 5 minutes mean-5m: mean average loop latency over 5 minutes stddev5: standard deviation of loop latency over 5 minutes avg-1m: weighted decaying average loop latency over 1 minute mean-1m: mean average loop latency over 1 minute stddev1: standard deviation of loop latency over 1 minute Once again, these average/mean values are measuring the 100 ms service loop, which under normal circumstances should always complete in close to 100 ms. When the value rises above 100 ms, that means we are not able to service all our monitor instances in a timely fashion.

bugs.title: Some auto-discovered virtual servers may be removed from pools.
bugs.symptoms: As part of a larger effort to refine Virtual Server Auto Discovery and monitoring, several changes were made to improve cross-version interoperablility and virtual server matching. As part of these fixes, an error was introduced which caused some virtual servers to be deleted and rediscovered. This removed them from the pool they were assigned to, which can cause load balancing errors.
bugs.conditions: This can occur with virtual servers that were originally configured on a pre-folder-aware version of the software, such as 10.2.x.
bugs.impact: When the virtual servers are discovered by a folder-aware version, they may be deleted from the GTM config and re-added with /Common/ prepended to its name. Some virtual servers will be removed from pools. The virtual server will be deleted and recreated, but not added back to the pool. This will result in incorrect load balancing decisions.
bugs.workaround: To resolve the issue, change the GTM config to add the virtual servers back to the pool.
bugs.fix: The discovery and monitoring of virtual servers has been made more robust to deal with cases of multiple GTM virtual servers pointing at the same LTM virtual, as well as naming/folderization issues.

bugs.title: HTTP::retry incorrectly converts its input
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP::retry iRule converts its input into UTF8. If the input is a bytearray using some other locale, then bytes with the high-bit set may be corrupted. The resulting corrupted request will then be sent to the server as the retried request.
bugs.conditions: The input to HTTP::retry is a TCL bytearray rather than a TCL string. The output from some commands i.e. HTTP::payload is a bytearray. Strings are in the UTF8 format, Bytearrays are not.
bugs.impact: Non-ascii characters may be corrupted when HTTP::retry is used.
bugs.fix: The HTTP::retry command no longer corrupts input that isn't in the UTF8 format.

bugs.title: Log ID 01490538 may be truncated
bugs.symptoms: Log ID 01490538 may appear truncated in /var/log/apm. It is supposed to say "Configuration snapshot deleted by Access".
bugs.conditions: Access profile snapshots are timing out and being deleted by the system.
bugs.impact: Most likely just corrupted log messages. A very slight chance of a crash, due to the string terminator being written to the wrong location in memory.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Log ID 01450538 prints correctly to /var/log/apm now.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system as SAML Service Provider cannot process some messages from SimpleSAMLphp under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is used as Service Provider with SimpleSAMLphp as Identity Provider, processing of signed artifact response messages from IdP may fail with following error: Digest of SignedInfo mismatch.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP system is configured as SP. - Artifact binding is used for SSO. - Artifact response message from IdP is signed.
bugs.impact: User SSO may not work.
bugs.workaround: Use POST binding instead of Artifact.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system configured as SAML Service Provider can now correctly process messages from SimpleSAMLphp so that user SSL works as expected.

bugs.title: Applications including Internet Explorer using Microsoft's Secure Channel (Schannel) may fail SSL/TLS handshakes
bugs.symptoms: Applications including Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) using the Microsoft Secure Channel ('Schannel') TLS library may experience TLS handshake failures while accessing virtual servers with Client SSL profiles. When the client and server select a TLS ciphersuite that utilizes ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (DHE) key exchange, the server (the BIG-IP system) sends a ServerKeyExchange message with Diffie-Hellman parameters to the client. For a subset of the generated parameters (approximately 1 in 128 for 1024-bit DH parameters), the length of the encoded 'dh_Ys' parameter is less than the length of the encoded 'dh_P' parameter. As a result of that encoding combined with an issue with the Schannel library, the client experiences a fatal error and is unable to complete the TLS handshake. When this issue occurs, only a subset (potentially only one) TMM may experience handshake failures, because each TMM generates unique DH parameters. Handshake failures may last for up to an hour, as each TMM regenerates parameters every hour.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual servers with Client SSL profiles. - Client applications using the Secure Channel (Schannel) TLS library. Relevant clients include IE. - The BIG-IP system selects a ciphersuite that uses DHE key exchange. Note that the ECDHE key exchange is unaffected.
bugs.impact: Schannel-based applications may be unable to complete TLS handshakes with one more TMMs on a system for up to an hour. Other clients are unaffected, and can successfully complete TLS handshakes.
bugs.workaround: Disable DHE cipher suites in client-ssl profiles, as follows: * 'DEFAULT:!EDH' to permanently remove DH-based ciphersuites. * 'DEFAULT:-EDH:DEFAULT+EDH' to move them to the end of the preference list.
bugs.fix: In order to avoid this issue, the BIG-IP ensures that the encoded Diffie-Hellman parameters ('dh_p' and 'dh_Ys') in TLS ServerKeyExchange are always the same length by padding 'dh_Ys' with leading 0x00 bytes.

bugs.title: tmsh save sys config file /var/tmp or /shared/tmp can make some BIG-IP functionality unusable
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh save sys config file /var/tmp or /shared/tmp or a relative path to these directories (for example, /config/../shared/tmp) saves the scf with the specified real path. However, since the /var/tmp directory is used internally by BIG-IP daemons, some functionality may be rendered unusable till the /var/tmp symlink to /shared/tmp is restored.
bugs.conditions: Saving the sys config file /var/tmp or /shared/tmp (or a relative patch to one of these directories).
bugs.impact: Some system functionality may be rendered unusable.
bugs.workaround: Use the following commands to delete the scf and restore the symlink and reset the permissions of the /shared/tmp directory: -- rm -f /var/tmp -- ln -s /shared/tmp /var/ -- chmod 01777 /shared/tmp -- bigstart restart
bugs.fix: The /var/tmp or /shared/tmp are now invalid paths for the tmsh save sys config file command.

bugs.title: A request that should be blocked was forwarded to the server
bugs.symptoms: A request that should be blocked is forwarded to to the server.
bugs.conditions: The following conditions - 1. The "do nothing" header content profile on the request URL OR the request is longer than the max buffer size. while the exceed buffer length violation is turned off. (both cases causes an ignore payload state). 2. An irule or session tracking is assigned on the virual server.
bugs.impact: In case the request should have been blocked, it will arrive to the server.
bugs.fix: We fixed a scenario where a request that should have been blocked still reached the server.

bugs.title: The DNS monitor may delay marking an object down or never mark it down
bugs.symptoms: The DNS monitor may not mark an object down within the monitor timeout period or may never mark the object down.
bugs.conditions: A DNS monitor with no configured recv string and the monitor receives an ICMP error other than port unreachable.
bugs.impact: The DNS monitor may not mark an object down within the monitor timeout period or may never mark the object down.
bugs.workaround: Supply an appropriate recv string to the monitor definition: tmsh modify ltm monitor dns mydns recv 10.1.1.1 Or add another monitor to the object: tmsh modify ltm pool dnspool monitor min 2 of { mydns gateway_icmp }
bugs.fix: DNS monitor should mark server down when getting ICMP admin prohibited error. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: DNS::return iRule can lead to infinite packet processing loop
bugs.symptoms: An improperly coded iRule can lead to an infinite loop. This generally occurs when the DNS::return command is used in the DNS_RESPONSE event. The simplest example is: when DNS_RESPONSE { DNS::return } Every time a request is finished, this event will push the request back into the DNS filter to be processed again, endlessly.
bugs.conditions: DNS::return command in a DNS_RESPONSE event with no path to skip the DNS::return command.
bugs.impact: If enough requests trigger this path, system resources will eventually be fully consumed processing
bugs.workaround: If DNS::request is being used in a DNS_RESPONSE event, be very certain that it is being properly used.
bugs.fix: A TCL error is now thrown if a loop is detected, if this re-process path is triggered 10 times. The error takes the form: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/irule_infinite_loop <DNS_RESPONSE> - DNS::return loop detected. invoked from within "DNS::return"

bugs.title: Parsing the DN (for subject or issuer) in a certificate does not take into account all the possible RDNs.
bugs.symptoms: The system recognizes and displays to the user a few relative distinguished names (RDNs): division name, state name, locality name, organization name, country name, and common name.
bugs.conditions: RDNs other than those in the subject/issuer are not parsed correctly.
bugs.impact: Parsing the DN (for subject or issuer) might combine fields that result in RDN values that are longer than allowed. This causes issues when trying to store these in Enterprise Manager (EM) database.
bugs.fix: All relative distinguished names (RDNs) are now parsed as expected. Previously, the system correctly parsed RDNs for division name, state name, locality name, organization name, country name, and common name. Now, the system correctly parses all RDNs.

bugs.title: Spurious RTO Detection Triggers Early Exit from Fast Recovery.
bugs.symptoms: When Fast Retransmit follows a spurious RTO, detection of the spurious RTO can overwrite Fast Recovery state and trigger premature exit. Spurious RTO detection can trigger crashes. Otherwise, in certain configurations, there can be an very slight decrease in performance.
bugs.conditions: A step change in delay causes a spurious TCP RTO, accompanied by significant packet reordering and additional packet loss.
bugs.impact: Possible crashes. Otherwise, a very small decrease in performance in certain configurations.
bugs.workaround: Disable Early Retransmit.

bugs.title: apd may crash when RADIUS accounting message is greater than 2K
bugs.symptoms: If the RADIUS Acct agent is configured for an access policy, and there are a lot of attributes with total size greater than 2K, apd may crash.
bugs.conditions: RADIUS Acct agent is configured and an AP with numerous attributes in RADIUS Acct request
bugs.impact: service becomes unavailable while restarting apd process
bugs.fix: The maximum size of RADIUS packet is now set to 4K (RFC2865). If the total size of attributes is greater than 4K, the packet will be truncated to 4K.

bugs.title: Resetting virtual server stat increments cur_conns stat in clientssl profile
bugs.symptoms: When there are active connections on the virtual server, resetting its virtual server stat through tmsh reset-stats ltm virtual virtual_name, doubles the client ssl profile cur_conns/cur_native_conns/cur_compat_conns.
bugs.conditions: - SSL virtual server. - Active connections on the virtual server. - Virtual server stat reset which active connections are occurring.
bugs.impact: Invalid statistics values on the client ssl profile stats.
bugs.fix: Resetting virtual server stats no longer increments cur_conns stat in clientssl profile, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: tmm crash with ssl
bugs.symptoms: Under some rare conditions, a problem with SSL might cause TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: An SSL alert is sent during the SSL handshake.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None known
bugs.fix: A tmm crash related to alerts during a SSL handshake failure has been fixed.

bugs.title: HTTP monitor might add extra CR/LF pairs to HTTP body when supplied
bugs.symptoms: When supplying HTTP containing body text to the HTTP monitor, the system might append extra CR/LF pairs to the end.
bugs.conditions: HTTP monitor with text specifying HTTP body text.
bugs.impact: This may cause malformed POST or PUT messages.
bugs.workaround: Limited work-around entails providing an alternative HTTP health check that does not require PUTting or POSTing a body.
bugs.fix: The HTTP monitor has been fixed to avoid adding additional CR/LF pairs, except for the case where only headers are supplied and there are insufficient CR/LF supplied to terminate the headers.

bugs.title: DNSSEC unsigned referral response is improperly formatted
bugs.symptoms: When DNSSEC signs an unsigned referral response, the contained NSEC3 resource record has an empty type bitmap. Type bitmap should contain an NS type.
bugs.conditions: DNSSEC processing an unsigned referral response from DNS server.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC referral response is not RFC compliant.
bugs.fix: NS type added to NSEC3 type bitmap, so that DNSSEC unsigned referral response is properly formatted.

bugs.title: APM cannot get groups from an LDAP server, when LDAP server is configured to use non-default port
bugs.symptoms: Starting from BIG-IP APM 11.6.0, there is a new feature called LDAP Group Resource Assign agent. The agent relies on a group list that is retrieved at AAA > LDAP Server > Groups configuration page. AAA LDAP Server fails to update the group list when the backend LDAP server is configured to use a port other than 389 (the default port).
bugs.conditions: Backend LDAP server is configured to use a non-default port (a port other than 389). LDAP Group Resource Assign agent is added to an Access Policy.
bugs.impact: It is impossible to update group list from LDAP server. LDAP Group Resource Assign agent does not provide a list of LDAP groups for easy configuration.
bugs.fix: LDAP groups can now be retrieved from an LDAP server that uses a non-default port (a port other than 389).

bugs.title: statsd crash when failed to open stats files
bugs.symptoms: When certain errors occur trying to open stats files, the statsd daemon could crash calling tmidx_free.
bugs.conditions: Something like permissions, file descriptor exhaustion, etc. that could lead to an error opening stats files.
bugs.impact: The statsd daemon crashes leaving a core file and a gap in collecting systems stats and historical stats.

bugs.title: OPT-0015 on 10000-series appliance may cause bcm56xxd restarts
bugs.symptoms: Changing configuration (enable/disable/auto-negotiation) on copper SFPs on 10000-series appliance might cause an internal bus to hang. Symptoms are bcm56xxd process restarts, and the interfaces may show as unknown.
bugs.conditions: Only copper SFPs OPT-0015 on 10000-series appliances exhibit this problem.
bugs.impact: The bcm56xxd process restarts, and the interfaces may show as unknown.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, follow these steps: 1) Force the system offline. 2) Reboot the system. 3) Release the system's offline status.
bugs.fix: The bcm56xxd daemon detects a bus problem and resets the bus to recover communications with SFP transceivers.

bugs.title: [GUI] [GTM] Cannot delete Region if attempting to delete another region referenced by a record.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot delete a region even though it is not referenced by any record.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after a failed attempt to delete a region that is referenced by a record.
bugs.impact: Hard to manage topology regions.
bugs.workaround: Restart mcpd.
bugs.fix: Can now delete regions after failed deletion.

bugs.title: 'array' command not functional from within MOS context
bugs.symptoms: The array command does not produce correct results.
bugs.conditions: MOS shell
bugs.impact: array cannot be managed
bugs.workaround: manage the array from TMOS

bugs.title: Pool member not turning 'blue' when monitor removed from pool
bugs.symptoms: Pool member's status does not update when a monitor is removed from the pool.
bugs.conditions: Must have a pool configured with a monitor and pool members
bugs.impact: Traffic may be routed incorrectly
bugs.workaround: One may be able to update the pool member status by toggling the pool member's state down and then up again.
bugs.fix: The pool member's status updates when the pool's monitor is removed.

bugs.title: GTM Monitor Needs Special Escape Character Treatment
bugs.symptoms: When searching received data for bytes that are regex metacharacters such as $ (dollar sign), . (period), ? (question mark), etc., the search string typically requires backslash characters to escape these. Such escaped characters result in non-matching behavior in GTM monitors without warning in the GUI. The GUI also validates Perl (non-POSIX) character classes such as \d rather than [:digit:], but these Perl extensions do not search properly.
bugs.conditions: Any running GTM monitor.
bugs.impact: If a GTM monitor's expression contains regex Perl extension character classes or escaped regex metacharacters, a member's status might be incorrectly labeled.
bugs.workaround: When escaping a regular expression metacharacter, an \x5C can be entered as a substitute for a backslash. If searching for whitespace or digits, use [:space:] and [:digit:] rather than \s and \d. For example, searching for 'HTTP/ 1.1' in a GTM HTTP monitor, you can enter the search expression HTTP/ 1\x5C.1, which the regex compiler interprets as 'HTTP/ 1\.1', to search for the period character rather than interpreting the period ( . ) as the 'any non-null byte' metacharacter.

bugs.title: ClientSSL profile might have the wrong key/certificate/chain when created with a specific set of steps
bugs.symptoms: ClientSSL profile might have the wrong key/certificate/chain when created with a specific set of steps.
bugs.conditions: Create a ClientSSL profile (p1) with user-defined key/certificate/chain. Create another clientSSL profile (p2) with all default fields. Modify p2 to have the defaults from p1.
bugs.impact: GUI shows the right key/certificate/chain in p2, whereas tmsh shows p2 to have default key and certificate.
bugs.fix: ClientSSL profile now has the correct key/certificate/chain when multiple profiles are created with differing key/certificate/chain values.

bugs.title: logd core near end of its life cycle
bugs.symptoms: logd can core on shutdown.
bugs.conditions: Forcing shutdown of logd
bugs.impact: logd does not shut down gracefully.
bugs.fix: This is seen when forcing shutdown of logd only.

bugs.title: Existing connections can choose incorrect route when crossing non-strict route-domains
bugs.symptoms: After modifying the BIG-IP system's routing table, traffic for some existing connections might be interrupted because an incorrect route starts being used.
bugs.conditions: After a routing table modification, routes might be reselected for a portion of connections through the BIG-IP system. When a connection crosses non-strict route-domains, the routing table from a route-domain that is different from the route-domain used during connection start-up may be used.
bugs.impact: This might lead to traffic following a different path to the destination and traffic interruption. New connections will work properly, this only affects existing connections.
bugs.fix: Existing connections now choose the correct route when crossing non-strict route-domains.

bugs.title: When non-HTTP traffic causes the server-side to receive unexpected data, the connection will be dropped
bugs.symptoms: Non-HTTP traffic can have the server-side send data outside the usual request-response pairing. (Either before a request, or extra data after a response is complete.) If so, HTTP will reject the connection as the server state is now unknown. However, if HTTP is acting as a Transparent proxy, switching to pass-through mode and disabling HTTP may be a better course of action.
bugs.conditions: Non-HTTP data sent to the server-side not belonging to a response.
bugs.impact: Banner protocols, where the a server will respond before seeing any data will not pass through the Transparent HTTP proxy. Non-HTTP protocols that start with a pseudo-HTTP response, followed by extra data will reject the connection when the extra data is seen.
bugs.workaround: It may be possible to use HTTP::disable to disable the HTTP filter when some signature of the non-HTTP protocol is seen.
bugs.fix: The transparent HTTP profile's passthrough-pipeline option now allows unexpected server-side ingress to switch the Transparent HTTP proxy into pass-through mode.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system resets client without sending error report when certificate is revoked
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured for OCSP authentication, if the OCSP server reports that a certificate has been revoked, client connections are reset without sending SSL error alerts.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system configured for OCSP authentication.
bugs.impact: Client connections are reset without sending SSL error alerts.
bugs.workaround: Use the following iRule for the OSCP authentication profile instead of the system-supplied iRule: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { set tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid 0 set tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_done 0 } when CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT { if {[SSL::cert count] == 0} { return } set ssl_version [SSL::cipher version] set tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_done 0 if {$tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid == 0} { set tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid [AUTH::start pam default_ssl_ocsp] AUTH::subscribe $tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid } AUTH::cert_credential $tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid [SSL::cert 0] AUTH::cert_issuer_credential $tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid [SSL::cert issuer 0] AUTH::authenticate $tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid SSL::handshake hold } when CLIENTSSL_HANDSHAKE { set tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_done 1 } when AUTH_RESULT { if {[info exists tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid] && ($tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_sid == [AUTH::last_event_session_id])} { set tmm_auth_status [AUTH::status] array set tmm_auth_response_data [AUTH::response_data] if {$tmm_auth_status == 0} { set tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_done 1 SSL::handshake resume } elseif {($tmm_auth_status == 1) && ($tmm_auth_response_data(ocsp:response:status) eq "revoked")} { if { $ssl_version equals "TLSv1.2" } { set hex_version "0303" } elseif { $ssl_version equals "TLSv1.1" } { set hex_version "0302" } elseif { $ssl_version equals "TLSv1.0" } { set hex_version "0301" } else { reject } set hex_response "15${hex_version}0002022C" set bin_response [binary format H* $hex_response] TCP::respond "$bin_response" TCP::close } elseif {($tmm_auth_status != -1) || ($tmm_auth_ssl_ocsp_done == 0)} { reject } } }

bugs.title: View Client cannot change AD password in Cross Domain mode
bugs.symptoms: View Client cannot change Active Directory password in Cross Domain mode.
bugs.conditions: 1. Access policy for View Client uses Cross Domain authentication. 2. View Client user trying to log into APM belongs to a different AD domain than the one configured in AD Auth agent (cross-domain auth). 3. User's password is expired.
bugs.impact: User cannot change expired password, so cannot use VMware View.
bugs.fix: View Client can now change AD password in Cross Domain mode, as expected.

bugs.title: Include proxy hostname in logs in case of name resolution failure
bugs.symptoms: It's hard to troubleshoot cases when proxy name resolution failure happens.
bugs.conditions: Troubleshooting is required in proxy name resolution area.
bugs.impact: Network Engineer has problems with identifying root cause.
bugs.fix: Now proxy hostname is printed to logfile when resolution fails.

bugs.title: TMM may crash if access profile is updated while connections are active
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system has a virtual server with an access profile. There is live traffic using that virtual. If the access profile is updated, enforcement of certain behaviors on the live traffic may end up accessing stale profile data, and result in a crash.
bugs.conditions: If an access profile is attached to a virtual server, and the profile is updated while the virtual has active connections.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: (These are untested...) Without HA, (1) disable virtuals using access profile, (2) delete any active connections on the virtuals, (3) update access profile, and, (4) enable virtuals. With HA, (1) update access profile on standby, (2) failover to the standby, and (3) sync the configuration.
bugs.fix: Upon access profile update, cleanup of the previous profile data is deferred until there are no active connections referencing it.

bugs.title: Improved handling of certain HTTP types.
bugs.symptoms: Improperly formatted HTTP connection through BIG-IP may cause the connection to hang and eventually timeout.
bugs.conditions: If the HTTP version token in the request is improperly crafted, BIG-IP ends up treating the request as HTTP 0.9. Hence any data after the first CRLF is held back by BIG-IP due to pipeline handling, and is not passed to the backend server. If the backend server is Apache or IIS, this improperly crafted HTTP request line causes the request to be treated as 1.1, and both the servers wait for the Host header and CRLFs. Since no data is forthcoming, the connection hangs and the backend servers timeout the connection a few seconds later. F5 Networks would like to acknowledge Eitan Caspi, Security Researcher of Liacom Systems, Israel for bringing this to our attention.
bugs.impact: This has the potential to exhaust the number of connections at the backend.
bugs.workaround: Mitigations: 1) iRule that can drop the connections after a specified amount of idle time. 2) iRule to validate the request line in an iRule and fix it. 3) Tuning of profile timeouts 4) ASM prevents this issue.
bugs.fix: This release has improved handling of certain HTTP types, so that an HTTP request with a version token that is not properly crafted is no longer treated as HTTP 0.9. This has the effect of all of the request data being forwarded to the backend.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ iApp statistics corrected for partition use cases
bugs.symptoms: When the f5.http iApp is deployed in a partition, the icall script fails to get stats because it assumes the application is in /Common.
bugs.conditions: iApps are running in an administrative partition.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ fails to get statistics from iApps running on BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Certain iApps deployed by BIG-IQ now provide statistics.

bugs.title: The HTTP::payload iRules API appends garbage to content when transfer-encoding is chunked
bugs.symptoms: Using the HTTP::payload iRules API within the iRules HTTP_RESPONSE_DATA event yields bogus data in the inspected content, when the server sends a chunked HTTP response (HTTP/1.1 Transfer-Encoding: chunked). The following characters are appended to the actual content: CR-LF-0-CR-LF-CR-LF (H'0d0a300d0a0d0a' ..0....).
bugs.conditions: HTTP::payload iRules API used within the HTTP_RESPONSE_DATA iRules event, when server responds with a chunked HTTP payload (HTTP/1.1 Transfer-Encoding: chunked).
bugs.impact: Invalid content returned by the HTTP::payload iRules API when server sends a chunked HTTP response.
bugs.workaround: The iRule author can work around this issue by changing the request protocol to HTTP 1.0, since that prevents chunked transfer encoding. However, that would be inefficient because it breaks connection reuse. Workaround is just to add: HTTP::version "1.0" in HTTP_REQUEST event.

bugs.title: Safenet HSM Traffic failure after system reboot/switchover
bugs.symptoms: SafeNet hardware security module (HSM) Traffic failure after system reboot/switchover.
bugs.conditions: Restart of services on primary or secondary blade.
bugs.impact: Now traffic will fail. There will be no pkcs11 connection on new primary blade.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to restart pkcs11d on the secondary blade.
bugs.fix: Wait and try SafeNet hardware security module (HSM) communication when MCPD is fully loaded.

bugs.title: Modifying the default antifraud profile causes device group sync failures
bugs.symptoms: A device group sync results in the following error: 01070700:3: The attributes of a root profile (/Common/antifraud) cannot be set to 'default'.
bugs.conditions: The default /Common/antifraud profile is modified from its default values while in a device group.
bugs.impact: Sync fails and can be difficult to recover.
bugs.workaround: Don't modify the base profile; create a new one instead. Recovery could involve running SOL13887 against a peer with an unmodified base profile, but this will delete any changes made. If that is not an acceptable solution, you can tmsh save sys config, remove the /Common/antifraud profile from bigip.conf, then tmsh load sys config.

bugs.title: ASM policy creation fails with after upgrading
bugs.symptoms: You cannot create an ASM security policy after upgrading to version 11.6.x. You will see the following error message: ------------------ # tmsh create asm policy /Common/blabla active encoding utf-8 Unexpected Error: ASMConfig exception: [101] Policy 'Security Policy /Common/blabla' already exists in this policy. ------------------ It does not matter if the security policy was created by the command line or by the Configuration utility.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned Upgrade to 11.6.X
bugs.impact: ASM policies cannot be created.
bugs.workaround: Please apply the following workaround, as root user, from the command line of the affected BIG-IP. Please run these exact commands - copy and paste into the command line: --------------------- # mysql -uroot -p`perl -MF5::DbUtils -e 'print F5::DbUtils::get_mysql_password(user => qw{root})'` -e 'DELETE FROM PLC.PL_SESSION_AWARENESS_VIOLATIONS WHERE policy_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM PLC.PL_POLICIES)' --------------------- Be advised that this operation will permanently affect the mentioned database table. It is strongly advised to first create a backup of the running configuration by running the following command from the command line of the affected BIG-IP: --------------------- # tmsh save sys ucs /shared/tmp/backup.ucs --------------------- Before applying the workaround, first make sure that you indeed need one. You can do that by running this in the command line: --------------------- # mysql -uroot -p`perl -MF5::DbUtils -e 'print F5::DbUtils::get_mysql_password(user => qw{root})'` -e 'SELECT * FROM PLC.PL_SESSION_AWARENESS_VIOLATIONS WHERE policy_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM PLC.PL_POLICIES)' --------------------- In case this query does not return any output - it means that there is no need to apply the mentioned workaround. In case you do need to apply the workaround, you can use the same "SELECT *" query to validate the workaround, after it has been applied. Namely, after the workaround was applied, the "SELECT *" query should return no output.
bugs.fix: We've fixed ASM policy creation so that it does not fail after upgrade

bugs.title: The CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may not be triggered.
bugs.symptoms: Using the SSL persistence profile, the CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT event might not be triggered during renegotiation.
bugs.conditions: The SSL persistence profile is in use, and an iRule depends upon the CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT event.
bugs.impact: The CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may not be triggered. iRule command SSL::cert does not access certs retrieved from on-demand cert auth. This is functioning as designed.

bugs.title: Missing NTLMSSP_TARGET_INFO flag on NTLMSSP_CHALLENGE message
bugs.symptoms: NTLMSSP_TARGET_INFO flag is set on NTLMSSP_CHALLENGE message that is generated by ECA, although Target Info attribute itself is included. Certain NTLM clients may ignore the target info attribute due to this issue, and fall back to use NTLM v1 authentication. With ActiveDirectory default configuration this is not an issue. However, if you had specifically required NTLMv2 in your policy, then the authentication will never succeed due to mismatch of the protocol.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when NTLMv2 is set to required and NTLMv1 is denied in your ActiveDirectory policy.
bugs.impact: Users cannot authenticate.
bugs.fix: NTLM client that depends on NTLMSSP_TARGET_INFO flag can complete NTLM authentication using NTLMv2 protocol.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system may stop the normal processing of SSL traffic and dump a TMM core file
bugs.symptoms: During the handshake, an SSL alert is sent. The same alert is then sent repeatedly leading to resource-related issues such as increased memory usage and TMM cores. With db variable log.ssl.level set to Debug, the log might then fill with the alert message.
bugs.conditions: An SSL alert is sent during the handshake.
bugs.impact: Resource-depletion leading to TMM core and interruption of service.
bugs.fix: During the handshake, an SSL alert is sent. In this release, the same alert is sent only once, so there are no resource-related issues such as increased memory usage and TMM cores.

bugs.title: Cookie rewrite mangles 'Set-Cookie' headers
bugs.symptoms: 'Set-Cookie' headers are syntactically invalid.
bugs.conditions: Rewrite profile and 'Set-Cookie' header has 'Expires' attribute before 'Path' attribute.
bugs.impact: 'Set-Cookie' headers in the client side become syntactically invalid (two 'Path' values that can be contradictory, plus a broken 'Expires' string).
bugs.workaround: Put the 'Path' attribute before 'Expires' attribute.
bugs.fix: The 'Expires' attribute is now properly parsed.

bugs.title: New LSN Stat,Total End Points (IPv4/IPv6), deprecates the stat Total End Points
bugs.symptoms: The stat Total End Points displays an incorrect value when an IPv6 address with a small prefix is configured in LSN Pool.
bugs.conditions: Any IPv6 address with a small prefix is configured as pool member for an LSN pool.
bugs.impact: The statistic shows incorrect values when an IPv6 address with small prefix is configured in LSN pools.
bugs.fix: This release introduces a new stat, Total Endpoints (IPv4/IPv6), which displays the correct statistic values. Refer to the new statistic, Total End Points (IPv4/IPv6) for correct information when IPv6 addresses are added in LSN Pool.

bugs.title: [Mac][Linux][NA] TLS tunnel freezes on Mac and Linux in case of SSL renegotiation
bugs.symptoms: TLS tunnel freezes on Mac and Linux in case of SSL renegotiation.
bugs.conditions: TLS tunnel on Mac and Linux and SSL renegotiation happens
bugs.impact: Tunnel freezes and user cannot pass data traffic.
bugs.workaround: Restart session with BIG-IP
bugs.fix: Tunnel no longer freezes on SSL renegotiation on MAC and Linux.

bugs.title: Incorrect value of form action attribute inside 'onsubmit' event handler in some cases
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect value of 'action' form attribute may be used inside 'onsubmit' event handlers if original 'action' is an absolute path.
bugs.conditions: HTML form with absolute path in 'action' attribute; 'onsubmit' event handler for this form.
bugs.impact: Web application may work incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: There is no general workaround. But if 'action' value can be converted to relative path or to full URL (with host), this can be done using iRule.
bugs.fix: Now value of form 'action' attribute is correct inside event handlers.

bugs.title: The -decode option should be added to expressions in AD and LDAP group mapping.
bugs.symptoms: -decoded option is needed.
bugs.conditions: upgrade to 11.6.0
bugs.impact: in 11.6.0, if you create a rule to match an AD group in an "AD group resource assign" it will create something like this in the bigip.conf: expression "expr { [mcget -decode {session.ad.last.attr.memberOf}] contains \"CN=TEST,\" }" Prior to 11.6.0 the generated config was: expression "expr { [mcget {session.ad.last.attr.memberOf}] contains \"CN=TEST,\" }" The upgrade script does not take care of adding the "-decode" option which result in no groups being displayed in the VPE after an upgrade to 11.6.0
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: issue resolved, the -decode and lower string comparison added to expressions in AD and LDAP Group Mapping during upgrade.

bugs.title: Network Access on disconnect restores redundant default route after looped network roaming for Windows clients
bugs.symptoms: Windows Network Access restores redundant default route if client roaming from networks in loop e.g.: NetworkA -> NetworkB -> NetworkA.
bugs.conditions: * Connect NIC to NetworkA * Connect to VPN * Roam to another wifi network SSID (NetworkB) * Roam back to the original wifi SSID in step #1 (NetworkA)
bugs.impact: Incorrect default route may cause routing issues on client machine if metric of interfaces connected to NetworkB is lower than metric of interfaces connected to NetworkA
bugs.fix: Fixed issue causing redundant default route under described conditions.

bugs.title: Client waits seconds before page finishes load
bugs.symptoms: If page-load-time is enabled in the AVR profile, and the response is small enough to not be chunked, AVR will "promise" to the client a CSPM injection in the response by adding to the Content-length header. If the response contains no <html> tag, AVR will "change its mind" and won't inject the JavaScript, causing the client to wait for the missing bytes until timeout.
bugs.conditions: Page-load-time is enabled in the AVR profile
bugs.impact: Client waits many seconds until timeout.
bugs.fix: If page-load-time is enabled in the AVR profile, and the response is small enough to not be chunked, AVR will "promise" to the client a CSPM injection in the response by adding to the Content-length header. If no <html> tag is found in the response, the system now injects empty spaces to fill in the missing bytes in order to prevent the client from timing out.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ Discovery of an 11.5.2 EHF1-19 BIG-IP fails
bugs.symptoms: If you use a BIG-IQ device to discover a BIG-IP device running version 11.5.2 EHF1-19, the discovery fails with the message "Error querying iControl Rest for ASM Policy - Response Pages in."
bugs.conditions: BIG-IQ deployed, and attempting to discover a BIG-IP running 11.5.4 HF 1-19.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ discovery will fail with error.
bugs.workaround: Delete one of the installation volumes on the BIG-IP system and re-install the BIG-IP hotfix. For example, these are the tmsh commands to remove the volume and install the hotfix: # tmsh delete sys software volume HDx.y # tmsh install sys software hotfix Hotfix-BIG-IP-whatever-hotfix.iso volume HDx.y create-volume reboot where 'HDx.y' is a (any) desired target software volume. After the boot, run the following commands: # /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add rest_api_extensions 1 # tmsh restart sys service asm Wait for the BIG-IP device to become 'Active' again and then restart the discovery process from the BIG-IQ system.

bugs.title: Possible error when parsing for certain URL categorization input.
bugs.symptoms: The system might encounter an error when parsing for certain URL categorization input.
bugs.conditions: Enable PEM URL categorization to categorize the URLs from traffic processed by PEM virtual servers.
bugs.impact: TMM restart, with potential service interruption during the TMM restart.
bugs.fix: The parsing mechanism for the URL input has been fixed to handle multiple corner cases of the URL categorization.

bugs.title: RADIUS accounting STOP message may not include long class attributes
bugs.symptoms: The class attribute should be sent back to RADIUS server unmodified. However, if the RADIUS server is configured to send lots of long class attributes, the BIG-IP system might drop them when sending accounting stop message.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured with an Access Policy that contains RADIUS Acct agent. The RADIUS server is configured to send class attributes with total size of greater than 512bytes.
bugs.impact: RADIUS Accounting server doesn't receive STOP message when user session is over.
bugs.fix: Previously, the BIG-IP system would not send an accounting stop message if class attributes were more than 512 bytes total size. Now, BIG-IP system sends the accounting stop message, but does not include class attributes.

bugs.title: Auditor role: Exporting the Request Log
bugs.symptoms: Users with the Auditor role cannot export from the Request log.
bugs.conditions: Users with Auditor role trying to export from the Request log. Using a software version 11.5.x or 11.6.x.
bugs.impact: Cannot export from the Request log.

bugs.title: Upgrade process fails to convert ASM predefined scheduled-reports.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade from versions prior to 11.5 fail, if the scheduled report is using the predefined settings named: Top alerted and blocked policies.
bugs.conditions: There is a scheduled report that is using the predefined settings named: Top alerted and blocked policies. It can be triggered on upgrade to versions prior to 11.5.4, 11.6.1, and 12.0.0
bugs.impact: Upgrade process fails.
bugs.fix: A scheduled report using the predefined settings named: 'Top alerted and blocked policies' no longer causes upgrades from versions prior to 11.5 to fail. The upgrade process now renames the predefined report-type to the correct one and thus the upgrade process does not fail anymore.

bugs.title: Request is forwarded truncated to the server after answering challenge on a big request
bugs.symptoms: Large requests (over 5K) arrive truncated to the server when web scraping bot detection is enabled, or a brute force/session opening attack is ongoing with client-side mitigation.
bugs.conditions: The request size is between 5k-10k. Web scraping bot detection is turned on, or a brute force/session opening attack is ongoing with client-side mitigation.
bugs.impact: The client side challenge mechanism causes a truncation of the request forwarded to the server. Only the first 5k of the request arrives to the server.
bugs.workaround: Change the internal parameter size max_raw_request_len to 10000.
bugs.fix: The system's client-side challenge mechanism no longer truncates large requests (those over 5K) forwarded to the server.

bugs.title: [PA] - Failing to properly patch webapp link, link not working
bugs.symptoms: Any attribute URL in a HTML content is rewritten as "javascript:location=..." if is <base> tag is situated before the tag with the attribute, a content hint is not set in the HTML rules for the attribute and it's not the cookieless mode.
bugs.conditions: Webapp link is not properly patched.
bugs.impact: Rewritten links are not accessible.
bugs.fix: WebApp links are now properly rewritten.

bugs.title: Maximum connections statistic on node incorrect, shows higher than connection limit
bugs.symptoms: If a node is configured with a connection limit, the display may show a maximum connection count equal to the number of pool members using that node.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when nodes are configured with connection limits, and more than 1 pool member is using that node.
bugs.impact: Maximum connections statistic on node shows higher than the specified connection limit. This is a display issue only. The actual connection limit is enforced.

bugs.title: device trust setup can require restart of devmgmtd
bugs.symptoms: Depending on the order of operations, the device trust might enter a state in which the device trust connections between devices are continuously reset and messaging about self-signed certificates.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when devices are being added to and deleted from the device trust.
bugs.impact: This prevents devices from being able to communicate with each other. The device trust goes to Disconnected and cannot synchronize.
bugs.workaround: A restart of the devmgmtd daemon clears any stale cached information that it has. However, the administrator may still need to reset the device trust (remove devices from the trust and re-add them).
bugs.fix: The system now correctly resets device trust when devices are being added to and deleted from the device trust.

bugs.title: Cannot use tmsh to load valid configuration created using the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use tmsh to load a valid configuration created using the GUI.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with the following configuration: 1) Configure server with :* members. 2) Configure member-specific gateway-icmp monitor for the :* member. 3) Assign any L4/7 monitor at the server level. (http/tcp, etc., with the default '*:*' destination in the monitor).
