bugs.impact: Although the configuration is valid, it fails to load with error: err iqsyncer[16456]: 011ae104:3: Gtm config sync result from local mcpd: result { result_code 17237538 result_message '01070622:3: The monitor /Common/my-tcp-half has a wildcard destination service and cannot be associated with a node that has a zero service.' }
bugs.workaround: Remove the parent TCP monitor.
bugs.fix: The server configuration of :* members now loads without error using tmsh.

bugs.title: Assigning value to window.onerror in empty window lead to exception.
bugs.symptoms: Assigning value to window.onerror in empty window might lead to load failure.
bugs.conditions: Portal access configured, and there are links on pages that stop working after rewrite when assigning value to some empty window's onerror handler.
bugs.impact: Page does not load.

bugs.title: [Policy Sync] UI General Exception Error when sync a policy in non-default partition as non-default admin user
bugs.symptoms: Failed to sync a policy in non-Common partition as a non-default admin user.
bugs.conditions: Log in as different admin user than the default "admin". Sync a policy that was created in a non-Common partition..
bugs.impact: Policy Sync fails
bugs.workaround: Log in as default "admin" user.
bugs.fix: APM allows a user to log in as any admin user to sync policy in any partition.

bugs.title: Abnormally high CPU utilization from external SSL/OpenSSL monitors
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may experience high CPU utilization when SSL/OpenSSL monitors are used to obtain availability status for 30 or more pool members.
bugs.conditions: External SSL monitors using OpenSSL. This includes but is not limited to EAV, ldap, sip, soap, firepass, snmpdca, real-server, wmi, virtual-location. Builtin monitors are not affected, e.g., https, inband.
bugs.impact: High CPU utilization reported with potential performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can use a different type of monitor to obtain pool member availability status. Impact of workaround: Performing the recommended workaround should not have a negative impact on your system.
bugs.fix: The CPU utilization is reduced when SSL/OpenSSL monitors are used to obtain availability status for 30 or more pool members.

bugs.title: tmm crash: valid proxy
bugs.symptoms: tmm might crash in extremely rare circumstances when a virtual server is used during an update. Standard process is for virtual servers to be unavailable until the configuration update is complete; there are extremely rare circumstances when it is possible for a connection to use a virtual server before it is ready.
bugs.conditions: This requires that traffic is running during a configuration update, including a config sync from an HA peer. There must be a virtual server or configuration that uses a second virtual server while traffic is running: these include vip-on-vip using iRules and WAM prefetch, but might include other internal conditions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption, possible failover to another device if HA is configured. If using keepalive or other means to keep the connection alive, then a long amount of time might pass between the creation of the invalid flow and any impact from the error.
bugs.fix: If a virtual server is used during an update (that is, before the virtual server is ready), an error message is now posted to tmm log files, and a small amount of memory is used each time this message is logged.

bugs.title: SIP statistics upgrade
bugs.symptoms: SIP data is lost when upgrading.
bugs.conditions: Collect SIP data, Upgrade to newer version (from 11.5.0 to 12.0.0 or beyond).
bugs.impact: SIP data is lost.
bugs.fix: After upgrading from version 11.5.3 and later, collected SIP statistics are now moved to the new version.

bugs.title: cspm script isn't injected in text/html chuncked response
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP Client Side Performance Monitoring (CSPM) script does not get injected in chunked response causing the "Page load time" feature to not work properly.
bugs.conditions: This happens for chunked (large) web pages.
bugs.impact: The "Page load time" feature does not work properly and page load time stats do not exist for these responses.
bugs.workaround: None known
bugs.fix: Page load time is displayed correctly even for chunked responses.

bugs.title: vCMP guest memory growth due to large number of /var/run/tmstats-rsync.* files.
bugs.symptoms: Extremely large and increasing number of files present, of the form /var/run/tmstats-rsync.*. This is a memory-backed directory, and these files are never automatically moved or deleted, hence the vCMP guest may eventually experience swap and out of memory conditions.
bugs.conditions: vCMP guests upload statistics to the VCMP host periodically. In a small percentage of vCMP guests which have large configurations, these statistics take up an unusually high amount of space. This is not an error, but it exceeds the 6 MB limit that the host accepts. The host's refusal to accept the file triggers behavior in the guest that logs the condition to /var/run/tmstats-rsync.*. If the file size never decreases, this happens repeatedly and indefinitely.
bugs.impact: In swap and low memory conditions, the vCMP guest suffers performance problems and instability.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can disable guest health statistic collection on the vCMP host. To do so, perform one of the following procedures: Disabling statistic collection for the tmsh show vcmp health command. Impact of workaround: This procedure affects values returned by the tmsh show vcmp health stats command. 1. Log in to the command line of the vCMP host. If the device is a VIPRION, ensure you are logged in to the primary blade. 2. To disable statistic collection, type the following command: tmsh modify vcmp guest all capabilities add { stats-isolated-mode }.
bugs.fix: The /var/run/tmstats-rsync.* files are no longer generated. Instead, statistics are kept in the vCMP guest to track failures to send stats to the host. You can see these by running the following command in the guest: tmctl -d blade vcmpd/rsync_stat. If the guest is a multi-slot guest on a VIPRION platform, this command shows separate stats for each slot it's run on.

bugs.title: Sync when licensed for ASM/AFM fails to sync pool with "Load balancing feature not licensed" error
bugs.symptoms: When adding a single pool member to a pool associated to a virtual server, the sync fails with error message 'Load balancing feature not licensed.' from peer.
bugs.conditions: ASM/AFM licensed, a pool assigned to a virtual server, a single pool member is added.
bugs.impact: Sync fails.
bugs.workaround: Perform a sync between the creation of the pool and the pool members.

bugs.title: PEM session lookup by subscriber ID in TMSH fails if same IP is being used to create session with different subscriber ID
bugs.symptoms: IF an existing session is being replaced by new session with same IP address but different subscriber ID then if we try to lookup the session based on new subscriber ID from tmsh, then lookup will fail.
bugs.conditions: Existing session replaced by new session with same IP and different subscriber ID.
bugs.impact: Lookup for new session fails and replacing of new session will fail too.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed and should work as expected.

bugs.title: apm network access tunnel ephemeral listeners ignore irules (related-rules from main virtual )
bugs.symptoms: If you want to change timeout values for server-side initiated flows inside Network Access tunnels, ephemeral listeners ignore irules. There seems to be a workaround for this through tmsh (not ui) by attaching iRules (related-rules) to main virtual that gets run on ephemeral listeners. (These ephemeral listeners are created by Network Access tunnels for lease-pool IPs.) The command for this is (for example): tmsh modify ltm virtual vs_dtls related-rules { idle_time } The problem here was APM Network Access used to ignore the related-rules on main virtual and the rules weren't triggered.
bugs.conditions: APM Network access use case.
bugs.impact: Related rules on main virtual are not applied to ephmeral listeners; (these ephemeral listeners are created by Network Access tunnels for lease-pool IPs).
bugs.fix: iRules get executed on Ephemeral listeners.

bugs.title: Flows dropped with initiate data from sever on virtual servers with HTTP
bugs.symptoms: Accepted Events held when HTTP is present on the hudchain
bugs.conditions: HTTP present on on hudchain
bugs.impact: Data flows dropped
bugs.fix: Enable checking of HTTP state and pass Accepted events

bugs.title: Throughput drop and rxbadsum stat increase in tagged VLAN with LRO/GRO on BIG-IP VE running on ESX platforms with particular network hardware
bugs.symptoms: TCP throughput might be severely impacted for traffic traversing a tagged VLAN and BCM57800/BCM57810 NIC on BIG-IP VEs. The 'rxbadsum' counts increase as received LRO'd traffic is ignored by TMM.
bugs.conditions: 1. Traffic traverses a tagged VLAN. 2. This issue might be related to systems using Broadcom BCM57800 or BCM57810 NICs. However in general, the required condition is reception of packets with VLAN header are received in uNIC driver.
bugs.impact: Potential throughput drop during a high volume of data transfer.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: 1. Avoid using tagged VLANs. 2. Run the following commands on the ESX hypervisor to disable LRO/GRO system-wide, followed by a reboot. -- esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Net/Vmxnet2HwLRO -i 0. -- esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Net/Vmxnet3HwLRO -i 0. -- esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Net/Vmxnet2SwLRO -i 0. -- esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Net/Vmxnet3SwLRO -i 0. -- esxcli system settings advanced set -o /Net/VmxnetSwLROSL -i 0.
bugs.fix: Change in L4 packet header offset, resulting from VLAN header insertion, is being accounted for to verify checksum.

bugs.title: JavaScript challenge fails when coming within iframe with different domain than main page
bugs.symptoms: The JavaScript Challenge fails when coming within an iframe that is on a different domain than the main page.
bugs.conditions: 1. The web application uses an iframe coming from a different domain than the main page, AND 2. Any of the following options are enabled on an ASM Policy or Application DoS Profile attached to the Virtual Server which is handling the iframe: a. DoS Client-Side Integrity Defense Mitigation (affecting only during attack mitigation) b. DoS CAPTCHA Mitigation (affecting only during attack mitigation) c. Device-ID (fingerprint) d. Web Scraping Bot Detection Challenge e. Proactive Bot Defense (with/without "Block Suspicious Browsers")
bugs.impact: On the browser, the iframe will fail to load, leaving a white box, or the following message: "Please enable browser cookies to view the page content." There may be error messages in the browser's console.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to workaround the problem using Proactive Bot Defense (DoS Profile) and iRules. This works even if the problem is in Web Scraping and DoS profile was not previously used. The following steps must be done for the Virtual Server handling the iframe, as well as the one handling the main page. 1. Attach a DoS profile to the Virtual Server (if not already attached). 2. Disable TPS-based detection (unless already enabled, or it is desired). 3. Enable Proactive Bot Defense on the DoS profile (if not already enabled). a. Disable "Block Suspicious Browsers" (unless already enabled, or it is desired). b. Configure Cross-Domain Requests to "Allow configured domains; validate upon request". c. Add the domain of the main page to the Related Site Domains. 4. Attach the following iRule to the virtual server: ltm rule rule_fix_cross_domain_challenges { when HTTP_REQUEST { set refdom "" regexp -nocase {^https?://([^/]*).*$} [HTTP::header referer] -> refdom log local0. "uri [HTTP::uri] host [HTTP::host] referer [HTTP::header referer] refdom $refdom" if { $refdom ne "" && $refdom ne [HTTP::host] } { BOTDEFENSE::cs_allowed false } } } NOTES: 1. The challenges must run on the main page. The following rule block could be used to force the challenges to run on a specified URL or URLs. when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::uri] eq "/" } { BOTDEFENSE::cs_allowed true } } 2. If additional URLs are getting blocked or challenged as a result of Proactive Bot Defense and it is unwanted, it is possible to control them in the iRule by checking for URLs and using the "BOTDEFENSE::action allow" command.
bugs.fix: JavaScript challenges no longer fail when coming within an iframe on a different domain than the main page.

bugs.title: dnatutil utility needs update because DAG changed.
bugs.symptoms: dnatutil utility needs update because DAG changed.
bugs.conditions: CGNAT configured
bugs.impact: STDERR: dnatutil: Newer version of the utility is required to process the data (required daglib id: 5666df06f3570ad26976e607e02f71f7).
bugs.fix: dnatutil utility has been updated because DAG changed.

bugs.title: ICMP errors may reset FastL4 connections unexpectedly
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 connections may be reset when receiving an ICMP packet
bugs.conditions: ICMP packet with an embedded TCP packet is received on an ePVA accelerated flow
bugs.impact: Connection is reset
bugs.fix: TCP sequence numbers embedded in an ICMP packet are no longer validated on ePVA accelerated flows.

bugs.title: Memory leak on L7 Dynamic ACL
bugs.symptoms: There is a memory leak on Dynamic ACL with regard for HTTP related configuration such as HTTP host name, and HTTP URI path in ACL entry. The leaks occurs for every session as these entries are generated per session bases.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using L7 Dynamic Access Control Lists.
bugs.impact: TMM memory usage increases.
bugs.workaround: Use static ACL whenever possible.
bugs.fix: L7 Dynamic ACL is no longer leaking memory.

bugs.title: External pluggable module interfaces not disabled correctly.
bugs.symptoms: External pluggable module interface may show link UP status, when administratively disabled.
bugs.conditions: Disable any external pluggable module interface that is connected to an enabled peer interface.
bugs.impact: Disabled external pluggable module interface may link UP and potentially pass traffic.
bugs.fix: Software fix prevents disabled external pluggable module interface from being re-enabled, as a result of periodic linkscan operations.

bugs.title: APM "Session Variables" report shows user passwords in plain text
bugs.symptoms: APM Session Variables report shows user passwords in plain text.
bugs.conditions: Has password session variable.
bugs.impact: It is not safe to show users' password in plain text.
bugs.fix: APM Session Variables report masks user passwords, displaying ************ instead.

bugs.title: Added/updated signatures are added to certain corrupted Manual user-defined sets.
bugs.symptoms: Signature set may contain signatures which are not supposed to be part of the set.
bugs.conditions: Corrupted manual user-defined signature sets can no longer be created after the fix for Bug 441075. However, pre-existing corrupted manual sets will not be corrected by roll-forward/upgrade from a version prior to the fix.
bugs.impact: Requests may get blocked due to attack signatures which are actually not supposed to be in the policy.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, to prevent signatures from being added to these Signature Sets in the future, use the following SQL: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- DELETE FROM PLC.NEGSIG_SET_FILTERS where set_id in (SELECT set_id FROM PLC.NEGSIG_SETS where flg_is_manual = 1) ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Alternatively, delete the affected Signature Set and re-create as manual.
bugs.fix: Pre-existing, corrupted, user-defined (manual) signature sets are now corrected after upgrading from an older version.

bugs.title: Citrix HTML5 Receiver does not properly display initial tour and icons
bugs.symptoms: When trying to connect with Citrix HTML5 Receiver, the initial tour screen does not display properly.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix replacement mode and Citrix HTML5 Receiver client 1.4-1.6 is used.
bugs.impact: Issues with GUI user experience. User is presented with an improperly formatted page without icons.
bugs.workaround: 1. Open /config/bigip.conf for edit. 2. Replace 'content-type text/plain' with 'content-type text/css' in HTML5Client(.*).css sections. 3. Replace 'content-type text/plain' with 'content-type text/javascript' in HTML5Client(.*).js sections/ 4. Save the file. 5. From the console, type the following command: tmsh load sys config.
bugs.fix: Now APM correctly sets content type of CSS and JavaScript files when configuring Citrix HTML5 client bundle.

bugs.title: Flows are closed as expired rather than closed gracefully.
bugs.symptoms: Flows are closed as expired rather than closed gracefully.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is passing about 400 requests per second, which causes system congestion.
bugs.impact: Response timeouts.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP now closes TCP connection after requests for FPS JavaScript.

bugs.title: Possible segfault during hardware accelerated compression.
bugs.symptoms: Segfault and core-dump of tmm when using gzip, deflate, or zlib hardware accelerated compression compress or decompress operations.
bugs.conditions: Requests for compression on the hardware accelerator might cause a segfault.
bugs.impact: Tmm restarts when the issue is encountered.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware accelerated compression.
bugs.fix: Cancelled flow contexts involving a compression context no longer segfault when the in-flight operation completes.

bugs.title: Duplicate server entries in Server List.
bugs.symptoms: There are multiple entries in the server list, possibly with different connection strings.
bugs.conditions: Client ends up with duplicate entries in the server list if it connects to different virtual servers that have the same aliases in the connectivity profile.
bugs.impact: Duplicate server entries in Server List.
bugs.workaround: Avoid duplicate aliases across connectivity profiles on servers that client connects to.
bugs.fix: Single entry in the server list.

bugs.title: [Policy Sync] OutOfMemoryError exception when syncing big and complex APM policy
bugs.symptoms: Policy sync fails with out-of-memory error on target device with big and complex policy.
bugs.conditions: Profile of big size, for example, excessive use of ACL resource.
bugs.impact: Policy Sync fails.
bugs.fix: APM allows a user to sync a large and complex policy.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin could crash on malformed ActionScript 3 block in Flash file
bugs.symptoms: The rewrite plugin crashes. The following log message is in the log: ../fm_patchers/abc/abcScanner.cpp:70: void abc::abcScanner::has(size_t): Assertion `GetRemaining() >= (ssize_t)l' failed.
bugs.conditions: Input file is truncated or contains invalid bytecode instructions at the end of doabc/doabcdefine tag.
bugs.impact: Portal Access services restart.
bugs.fix: Rewrite plugin no longer crashes on truncated or malformed Adobe Flash files with incorrect ActionScript 3 method body blocks.

bugs.title: Components validation alert
bugs.symptoms: Components validation alert is a special case where field client_request_uri is filled with referrer value (configured as protected URL). In addition referrer value is sent in field http_referrer.
bugs.conditions: FPS plugin sends components validation alert.
bugs.impact: Incorrect info in alerts.
bugs.fix: Now client_request_uri has current URL and http_referrer has referrer value.
bugs.behavior: Now client_request_uri has current URL and http_referrer has referrer value.

bugs.title: Perl Core After Apply Policy Action
bugs.symptoms: Apply policy causes a perl core Further apply policy do not work
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. LTM provisioned. An ASM policy exists that is referenced by an LTM (L7) policy which is not assigned to any LTM virtual server.
bugs.impact: Apply policy causes a perl core and ASM config event dispatcher crash. ASM config event dispatcher then is not restarted and remains down. Further apply policy do not work.
bugs.workaround: Make sure that if an ASM policy exists that is referenced by an LTM (L7) policy then such LTM (L7) policy is assigned to some LTM virtual server. one can create a dummy LTM virtual server for that purpose.
bugs.fix: Perl no longer cores and crashes ASM config event dispatcher in the case of an apply policy to an ASM policy that is referenced by an LTM (L7) policy which is not assigned to any LTM virtual server.

bugs.title: Java applet does not work
bugs.symptoms: Web applications may work incorrectly through Portal Access if they use Java applets.
bugs.conditions: Website uses Java applet that is loaded with deprecated <applet> HTML tag.
bugs.impact: Websites can't use Java applets.
bugs.fix: Java applets now work correctly through Portal Access.

bugs.title: iControl portal restarts
bugs.symptoms: iControl portal can restart during EM discovery.
bugs.conditions: EM discovery/device refresh
bugs.impact: iControl portal restarts causing an outage of using iControl

bugs.title: save-on-auto-sync can spawn multiple invocations of tmsh, starving system of memory
bugs.symptoms: Unit demonstrates behaviors consistent with out-of-memory condition. 'top' and 'ps' may show multiple tmsh processes waiting to run.
bugs.conditions: Enable auto-sync and save-on-auto-sync.
bugs.impact: Low memory condition may result in system instability.
bugs.fix: Enabled auto-sync and save-on-auto-sync no longer causes out-of-memory condition.

bugs.title: Reuse existing option is ignored for smtp servers
bugs.symptoms: If policy is imported with reuse existing objects option and there is appropriate SMTP server, the newly imported policy would create and use a new one instead reusing the existing one.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Minor - easy to fix after import
bugs.workaround: Open assignment and reuse existing SMTP server, then delete old one.
bugs.fix: Reuse existing option works properly for SMTP servers.

bugs.title: tmm restart due to oversubscribed DNS resolver
bugs.symptoms: A max-concurrent-queries configuration setting significantly above default can lead to a situation that causes tmm to restart in certain traffic loads.
bugs.conditions: DNS cache resolver configured with max-concurrent-queries setting significantly above default.
bugs.impact: tmm is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Set the max-concurrent-queries configuration value closer to default.
bugs.fix: A max-concurrent-queries configuration setting significantly above default no longer leads to a situation that causes tmm to restart in certain traffic loads.

bugs.title: TMM ASSERTs due to subkey_record field corruption in the SessionDB.
bugs.symptoms: TMM ASSERTs on 'Subkey is a subkey' in the SessionDB when releasing a record.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely encountered issue that might require SAML traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM ASSERTS, and the system stops passing traffic.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when using woodside congestion control
bugs.symptoms: In certainly configurations using woodside congestion control, TMM may crash
bugs.conditions: Woodside congestion control along with multiple profile options enabled and certain traffic may cause an issue where tmm may crash.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash causing a failover event
bugs.workaround: Switching from woodside to illinois congestion control avoids issue.
bugs.fix: Woodside congestion control along with multiple profile options enabled and certain traffic no longer causes an issue where tmm may core.

bugs.title: Ability to edit iCall scripts is removed from resource administrator role
bugs.symptoms: A user account with resource administrator role assignment is able to modify user accounts using iCall scripts.
bugs.conditions: Resource administrators attempting to modify iCall scripts will be denied access. Such users will still be able to create iCall handlers that reference existing scripts.
bugs.impact: Resource administrators are no longer able to modify iCall script objects.
bugs.workaround: To manage iCall scripts the user account must be assigned the administrator role.
bugs.fix: We have removed access to modify iCall scripts for the Resource Administrator role. iCall handlers can still be created that refer to scripts created by an administrator.

bugs.title: Connection inside Windows VPN tunnel may break if renegotiation is enabled in SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: VPN connection on Microsoft Windows may temporary stop passing traffic while performing secure TLS renegotiation. Although this lasts only for a few seconds, for some applications, it may result in connection stall or loss.
bugs.conditions: - APM clients for Windows. - Secure renegotiation (by time or a size) configured on TLS profile on BIG-IP APM.
bugs.impact: VPN connection on Windows momentarily stops passing traffic.

bugs.title: Specific iRule commands may generate a core file
bugs.symptoms: Accessing the information within a HTTP Authorization header via the HTTP::username, HTTP::password (or other method), may cause the TMM to generate a core file on some requests.
bugs.conditions: iRule that makes use of the HTTP::username, HTTP::password commands, or the sflow feature.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM generates a core file.
bugs.workaround: Modify iRule to manually truncate the size of the HTTP Authorization header.
bugs.fix: HTTP::username, HTTP::password iRule commands, and the sflow feature no longer generate a core file.

bugs.title: Changing Security Policy Application Language Is Not Validated or Propagated Properly
bugs.symptoms: After changing the Application Language for a Security Policy and pushing the changes over a manual sync device group, the device group's status immediately returns to "Changes Pending". Additionally calls through the REST interface erroneously allowed a client to change the language for a policy where it was already set.
bugs.conditions: A Security Policy was set to "Auto-Detect" the Application Language, and then set to a specific encoding. Or an application language is already set and is changed through the REST API. Issue is seen most prominently in a device group when ASM sync is enabled on a Manual Sync Failover Group
bugs.impact: 1) The change to encoding is not seen if looking at the result in tmsh. 2) In a manual sync group, after the change has been pushed to its peers, the change is correctly written to the MCP configuration when it is loaded. This appears as a new pending change from the peer device, and the device group appears out of sync again.
bugs.workaround: Push another sync from the peer to the original device.
bugs.fix: Changes to Language encoding are now validated and propagated correctly.

bugs.title: Route domain creation may fail if simultaneously creating and modifying a route domain
bugs.symptoms: Failure trying to create and modify a route domain in a single operation.
bugs.conditions: Performing create and modify operations in the same transactions, as can be done using tmsh and iControl.
bugs.impact: Transaction fails. Even though an ID is passed in with the create method, the system posts an error similar to the following: 01070734:3: Configuration error: route-domain Name /Common/test_rd_200 is non-numeric, so an ID must be specified.
bugs.workaround: Perform create and modify operations in different transactions.
bugs.fix: Fixed a scenario where route domain creation might fail when using create and modify in the same transaction.

bugs.title: The iControl Management.Zone.get_zone() method can return zone options in a format inconsistent for use with the Management.Zone.set_zone_option() method.
bugs.symptoms: Using the string returned in the options_seq field by the iControl Management.Zone.get_zone method in the Management.Zone.set_zone_option method can result in an 'Invalid zone option syntax...' error.
bugs.conditions: Use of the string returned by the iControl Management.Zone.get_zone method in the Management.Zone.set_zone_option() method.
bugs.impact: Strings returned in the options_seq field by the iControl Management.Zone.get_zone method cannot be used in the Management.Zone.set_zone_option() method unless they are reformatted consistent with the format expected by the Management.Zone.set_zone_option() method.
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI to set the zone options. Alternatively, modify the strings returned in the options_seq field by the iControl Management.Zone.get_zone method to a format consistent with those expected by the Management.Zone.set_zone_option() method. For example, modify options_seq to have each option as a single string (rather than the masters string, which is returned as 3 separate options strings).
bugs.fix: The iControl Management.Zone.get_zone_v2() method returns a value in the options_seq field in a format that is consistent with the format expected by the Management.Zone.set_zone_option() method.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin should check length of Flash files and tags
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access Flash patcher could crash or apply incorrect modifications on some malformed Flash files.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a Flash file is truncated or contains incorrect length value in file or tag headers.
bugs.impact: It may cause a crash and restart of Portal Access services.
bugs.fix: Rewrite plugin now correctly processes Adobe Flash files with invalid length in file or tag header.

bugs.title: In PBA mode subscribers cannot initiate more than 512 connections to the same server IP:port
bugs.symptoms: In PBA mode connections fail and new port blocks are not allocated when subscriber attempts more than 512 connections to the same server IP and port.
bugs.conditions: PBA mode is configured on the LSN pool and inbound connections setting is set to disabled.
bugs.impact: Subscribers can initiate only 512 connections to particular server IP:port.
bugs.workaround: Set 'Inbound connections' setting in the LSN pool to 'Automatic'.

bugs.title: Edge client contains multiple duplicate entries in server list
bugs.symptoms: Edge client contains multiple duplicate entries in the server list.
bugs.conditions: Edge client with duplicate entries in connectivity profile.
bugs.impact: Edge client shows duplicate entries.
bugs.workaround: Do not create duplicate entries in connectivity profile
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac doesn't show duplicate entries in the servers list.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP Edge Client for Mac no longer shows duplicate entries in the servers list.

bugs.title: XML policy import adds default entities if the relevant element list (in policy xml doc) is specified and empty
bugs.symptoms: Default entities (File types, Parameters, URLs, Cookies, Signatures, Redirection Domains and Brute Force Log-In URLs) are added to the policy upon XML policy import.
bugs.conditions: ASM policy with entities of some type (File types, Parameters, URLs, Cookies, Signatures, Redirection Domains and Brute Force Log-In URLs) deleted (all entities of that type). Export it to XML and then import that XML back - the default entities are added.
bugs.impact: XML policy import adds default entities if the relevant element list (in policy XML doc) is specified and empty.
bugs.workaround: The relevant element list (in the policy XML doc), that is specified and empty, should be completely removed (from the policy XML doc).
bugs.fix: ASM no longer adds default entities if the relevant element list (in the policy XML document) is specified and empty.

bugs.title: High ASCII characters availability for policy encoding
bugs.symptoms: High ASCII characters are not available, for any policy encoding, in any of the character sets except 'Headers : Character Set'.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: High ASCII characters are not available, for any policy encoding, in any of the character sets except 'Headers : Character Set'.
bugs.fix: High ASCII characters are now available, for the relevant policy encodings, in all character sets.

bugs.title: Alerts sent by the lcdwarn utility are not shown in tmsh
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in BIG-IP version 12.1.0, the 'tmsh show sys alert lcd' command displays the list of alerts sent to the LCD front panel display. The command-line utility lcdwarn can be used to send alert messages to the LCD front panel display. Alert messages sent to the LCD front panel display by the lcdwarn utility are not included in the list of alerts shown by the 'tmsh show sys alert lcd' command.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the lcdwarn utility to send alert messages to the LCD front panel display. Such messages are typically sent for testing purposes. This problem occurs on affected BIG-IP software versions running on all BIG-IP and VIPRION hardware platforms.
bugs.impact: The 'tmsh show sys alert lcd' command may not include all alert messages sent to the LCD front panel display. Messages sent by the lcdwarn utility are not shown.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic issue.

bugs.title: Dynamic ARP entry may replace a static entry in non-primary TMM instances.
bugs.symptoms: In a very rare occasion, a dynamic ARP entry may replace a static entry in non-primary TMM instances. When the BIG-IP system attempts to send packets to an address, "tmsh show net arp" lists two entries for the address: one static and the other shows up as "incomplete" status.
bugs.conditions: The issue is due to a very rare race condition, and the BIG-IP system is configured with a static ARP entry.
bugs.impact: The issue may impact traffic flow if traffic goes through non-primary TMM instances.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround but the issue is very rare to occur.
bugs.fix: Dynamic ARP entry no longer replaces a static entry in non-primary TMM instances.

bugs.title: Network failover packets on the management interface sometimes have an incorrect source-IP
bugs.symptoms: After reboot, network failover packets might be transmitted with an internal source address, on the 127/8 network.
bugs.conditions: This problem might occur if the members of a device service clustering (DSC)/high availability (HA) device group have management ports on different IP networks, so that a management-route is necessary for them to communicate.
bugs.impact: If there are intervening firewalls or routers that drop packets with improper/unroutable source addresses, then the members of the device group cannot communicate on this channel.
bugs.workaround: Remove the management-route from tmsh, and add a static route to the Linux kernel routing table. For example: # tmsh delete sys management-route 10.208.101.0/24 # tmsh save sys config # echo "10.208.101.0/24 via 10.208.102.254 dev eth0" > /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/route-eth0 # reboot
bugs.fix: Network failover packets on the management interface now have the correct source-IP when device service clustering (DSC)/high availability (HA) device group have management ports on different IP networks, so that a management-route is necessary for them to communicate.

bugs.title: Upgrade from 11.2.x (or earlier) to 11.5.x/11.6.x can fail when an active DoS profile exists with 'Prevention Duration' set to a value less than 5
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade fails with this error: --------------------- The de-escalation period can be either zero or greater than or equal to the escalation period ---------------------
bugs.conditions: -- ASM is provisioned. -- Active DoS profile exists with 'Prevention Duration' set to a value less than 5.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails with this error: --------------------- The de-escalation period can be either zero or greater than or equal to the escalation period ---------------------
bugs.workaround: Set the 'Prevention Duration' to at least 'Maximum 5 seconds' in all active DoS profiles.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the upgrade process to work with active DoS profiles that have the 'Prevention Duration' setting set to a value less than 5.

bugs.title: Include default values in XML Policy Export
bugs.symptoms: XML Policy Export does not include some entities, unless their values are different from the system's default settings
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned export security policy in XML format
bugs.impact: XML Policy Export does not include some entities, unless their values are different from the system's default settings
bugs.fix: We now exclude defaults from XML policy export only when exporting a minimal XML.

bugs.title: Hypervisor might replace vCMP guest SYN-Cookie secrets
bugs.symptoms: Traffic suddenly stops passing on platforms in vCMP mode when SYN-cookie mode is triggered. Occasionally, under HW-SYN-Cookie mode, HW-SYN-Cookie validation can fail, which triggers the software SYN-Cookie procedure, which does succeed. Under vCMP guest, you might notice hwalgo_accept increasing under TMCTL table epva_hwvipstat. If this packet's destination is the local high-layer TCP stack, there is no functional impact. Otherwise, there might be a performance impact. Under vCMP mirroring, however, the packet (failed to validate by FPGA), is sent to the remote TMM, which does not have the correct secret to validate, which causes the connection issue.
bugs.conditions: vCMP provisioning setup.
bugs.impact: Under vCMP guest, you might notice hwalgo_accept increased under TMCTL table epva_hwvipstat, which, if under HW-SYN-Cookie mode, everything will be validated automatically by FPGA instead. You might also notice hwalgo_invalid, if the FPGA used the updated secret for SYN-Cookie generation from the hypervisor, and when guest and hypervisor secret index overlaps. Even though guest and hypervisor secret index might not be the same, the history secret might be updated by hypervisor, which might trigger additional hwalgo_accept. Under vCMP mirroring, however, the packet (failed to validate by FPGA), is sent to the remote TMM, which does not have the correct secret to validate, so the error rate could be higher.
bugs.workaround: On the vCMP hypervisor, run the following commands. 1. echo "EPVA::enable_secret_diag true" > /config/tmm_init.tcl. 2. bigstart restart TMM. On a multiple blade system, you must run these commands on all blades.
bugs.fix: Hypervisor no longer replaces vCMP guest SYN-Cookie secrets.

bugs.title: Fixed memory leak in restjavad's Authentication Token worker
bugs.symptoms: There is a memory leak that causes the Authentication Token worker to run Out of Memory after approximately 27,000 token requests, when running with 96 MB image on a BIG-IP system. Any service might receive the OutOfMemory exception, so the external symptoms might vary (e.g., Socket failure, Bad Gateway, and others). To identify this issue, check for Out Of Memory exceptions in /var/log/restjavad.0.log.
bugs.conditions: This usually occurs when scripting against the rest interface. On a vCMP guest, guestagentd generates an authentication token every 90 seconds so that hostagentd on the vCMP hypervisor can make periodic REST calls to the guest. This info is used to populate the 'tmsh show vcmp health' stats.
bugs.impact: It takes a long time to log in 27,000 times, when logons come in through the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Restart restjavad after 10,000 tokens. To stop auth token generation on vCMP guests, on the hypervisor run the commands: -- tmsh modify vcmp guest all capabilities add { stats isolated-mode }. -- bigstart restart hostagentd
bugs.fix: Fixes a memory leak in Authentication Token mechanism in restjavad.

bugs.title: CGNAT - Rare TMM core with Deterministic NAT
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances TMM may core when using deterministic NAT due to a divide by zero error.
bugs.conditions: CGNAT using deterministic NAT mode and persistence enabled. This error only occurs if a previous connection created an address persistence entry using the second address. This crash is dependent on both the configuration and the traffic. When the number of subscriber addresses that disaggregates to a TMM is not evenly divided by the number of translation addresses that disaggregates to the same TMM, connections from one or more subscribers may be assigned to blocks from two translation addresses. Depending on the exact address ratio, there may be only one port using the second address. Due to an off-by-one error, the number of ports available for the second address may be set to zero when it should be set to one. This causes the divide by zero fault.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: pkcs11d initialization retry might post misleading error messages and eventually result in a pkcs11d core
bugs.symptoms: The retry of pkcs11d initialization might post misleading error messages and eventually result in a pkcs11d core.
bugs.conditions: When pkcs11d retries to wait for other services such as tmm or mcpd.
bugs.impact: After the system reboots, the /var/log/ltm shows initialize errors and the /var/log/daemon.log shows pkcs11_initialize messages: -- err pkcs11d[6247]: 01680002:3: Pkcs11 Initialize error (this is misleading; pkcs11d is actually retrying). -- err pkcs11d[6247]: Nethsm: pkcs11_initialize C_GetSlotList error 0x00000000, number of slots 0.
bugs.workaround: Retry pkcs11d restart when tmm and mcpd are both ready.
bugs.fix: The retry of pkcs11d initialization no longer posts misleading error messages when pkcs11d retries to wait for other services such as tmm or mcpd.

bugs.title: Auto-Detect Language policy has disallowed high ASCII meta-characters even after encoding is set to UTF-8
bugs.symptoms: Auto-Detect Language policy has disallowed high ASCII meta-characters even after encoding is set to UTF-8, which results in suggestions for allowing meta-characters that cannot be accepted.
bugs.conditions: Auto-Detect Language policy is created, and then set to UTF-8 encoding.
bugs.impact: Suggestions for allowing high ASCII meta-characters cannot be accepted.
bugs.fix: Auto-Detect Language policy no longer contains disallowed high ASCII meta-characters.

bugs.title: Incorrect configuration in BigTCP Virtual servers can lead to TMM core
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect configuration on an irule associated to a BigTCP virtual server can lead to TMM to core.
bugs.conditions: The following circumstances are needed: - BigTCP Virtual server - FastL4 profile with syncookies enabled. - Invalid iRule that will fail to execute, on LB_FAILED - Syncookie currently activated in that moment.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Correct or remove the irule event and coring will no longer occur.
bugs.fix: TMM now correctly handles the specific scenario to no longer core.

bugs.title: Images transcoded to WebP format delivered to Edge browser
bugs.symptoms: The Microsoft Edge browser does not support, and cannot render WebP format images. The AAM image optimization framework improperly classifies the Edge browser as being capable of supporting WebP and delivers WebP-transcoded images to such clients.
bugs.conditions: The AAM system's image optimization as well as the "optimize for client" setting must both be enabled, and the associated acceleration policy and application associated with one or more virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Some images will fail to render on the Edge browser.
bugs.workaround: Disable the "optimize for client" attribute in the applicable policies' acceleration assembly settings.
bugs.fix: Transcoded WebP images are no longer served to the Edge browser. By default, transcoded JPEG-XR is also no longer served to the Edge browser, but the db variable ccdb.allow.edge.jpegxr may be used to override this.

bugs.title: Network Access doesn't restore loopback route on multi-homed machine
bugs.symptoms: Network Access on Windows doesn't restore loopback route for one adapter on multi-homed (Ethernet + Wi-Fi) machine.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens if: 1. Network Access was established via Ethernet 2. Ethernet cable was unplugged 3. Network Access reconnects using Wi-Fi 4. Ethernet cable is plugged in back
bugs.impact: Minor routing issues may occur if one special loopback is removed. To restore this route affected adapter should be disabled and enabled.
bugs.fix: Fixed issues causing improper routing table management.

bugs.title: Traceroute through BIG-IP may display destination IP address at BIG-IP hop
bugs.symptoms: When performing traceroute through a BIG-IP device, the traceroute utility may display the destination IP in place of the hop where BIG-IP is located, instead of a Self IP address of the BIG-IP device at that hop.
bugs.conditions: No return route for the client IP address exists on the BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to the performance of traffic through the BIG-IP device. The impact occurs only when reading and interpreting the results of a traceroute utility.
bugs.workaround: If possible and allowed, add route entry for the traceroute client subnet.
bugs.fix: Traceroute through BIG-IP now displays a Self IP address of the BIG-IP device at that hop. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Keep-alive transmissions do not resume after failover of flows on an L4 virtual, when the sequence number is known
bugs.symptoms: After failover of an L4 flow that is using keep-alive, the keep-alive transmissions do not resume after traffic has flowed through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Using HA mirroring of L4 connections, with keep-alive enabled on the profile for TCP. After a failover, there was traffic before the flow timed out, then the traffic becomes idle. If there is no traffic after failover, the correct sequence numbers are unknown, then this is expected behavior: the flow times out due to inactivity. If there is traffic after failover, the correct TCP sequence numbers are known; if there is traffic after failover, and then the flow becomes idle, keep-alive transmissions should resume.
bugs.impact: Flows after failover with TCP keep-alive age out and expire even if traffic is available to set the sequence numbers. Depending on the configuration options, subsequent packets may reset or transparently create a new flow (if TCP loose initiation is enabled).
bugs.fix: Keep-alive transmissions now resume after failover of flows on an L4 virtual, when the sequence number is known

bugs.title: Possible crash in SPDY
bugs.symptoms: In very rare circumstances related to SPDY protocol handling together with a compression profile a crash may occur.
bugs.conditions: This is very rare and the exact circumstances are unclear, It involves SPDY, a compression profile and a congested client connection and a stream being reset by the browser (using a RST_STREAM frame).
bugs.impact: Very rarely a crash may occur.
bugs.workaround: Don't apply the compression profile.
bugs.fix: A sporadic crash when using SPDY together with a compression profile no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Assertion "valid pcb" in TCP4 with ICAP adaptation
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with assertion "valid pcb" in tcp4.c
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with request-adapt or response-adapt profile. Congested client or TCP small window (flow-control is active). Multiple HTTP requests in a single client connection. More likely with iRules that park.
bugs.impact: Intermittent crash under load. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Assertion "valid pcb" does not occur.

bugs.title: Session hangs when trying to switch state to provisioned
bugs.symptoms: iRule sessions may hang when switching state
bugs.conditions: Applying iRule to a client data virtual may cause state to hang
bugs.impact: Session state will hang
bugs.fix: Release the call back ctx connflow after setting session state asynchronously

bugs.title: PEM: Session is not replaced by third and subsequent RADIUS start messages containing specific multiple IPs
bugs.symptoms: PEM session is not replaced with a new one when for the subscriber
bugs.conditions: When the same radius start message is sent 3 times and more.
bugs.impact: Session not being replaced will still be applying old policy for the session.
bugs.workaround: Make sure radius stop is being for the subscriber before a new radius start is sent.
bugs.fix: Issue has been fixed now. Session should be replaced when any number of radius start messages are received associated to the subscriber

bugs.title: HTTP closes connection if client sends non-keepalive request and server responds with 200 OK on One-Connect enabled virtual
bugs.symptoms: If the client sends a non-keepalive CONNECT request (in HTTP 1.0 with no Connection header, in 1.1 with Connection: close) to a OneConnect-enabled virtual server, HTTP forces the connection closed by sending FIN on both client and server flows, even if the server responds with a 200. If the connect is successful, HTTP should leave flows open regardless of the HTTP headers.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP and OneConnect profiles are attached to the virtual server. - Client sends a non-keepalive CONNECT request (either 1.0/no-Connection-Header request or 1.1/'Connection: close' header. - Server responds to the CONNECT request with successful 200 OK.
bugs.impact: HTTP adds a Connection: close header when responding to the client after a successful response is received from the server. In addition, HTTP closes the connection by sending FIN on both client and server flows. If the server responds to the CONNECT request with 200 OK, the connection should remain open.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following iRule to work around this issue: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::method] eq "CONNECT" } { HTTP::disable } }
bugs.fix: HTTP now keeps the connection open if client sends a non-keepalive request and server responds with 200 OK on One-Connect enabled virtual. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Attack stopped and start messages should not have source/dst ip addresses in log messages
bugs.symptoms: DoS attack start and stop messages log the source and destination IP addresses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when AFM logs the DoS attack start / stop messages.
bugs.impact: Attack start and stop log messages in DoS should not have srcip and destip.
bugs.fix: Attack stopped and start messages are logged as NULL

bugs.title: Memory leak in Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Memory consumption of "rewrite.*" processes is growing constantly. On manually taken core file, result of following command is large (more than 100000). zcat <core-file.gz> | strings -n 15 | grep "^/f5-w-" | wc -l
bugs.conditions: Memory leaks in cases when POST request content could be modified by Portal Access (for example, xml).
bugs.impact: Rewrite processes may use all available memory on the box and then cause 'Out of memory' condition and failover.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak of request urls in rewrite plug-in.

bugs.title: Traceroute and ICMP errors may be blocked by AFM policy
bugs.symptoms: ICMP error packets for existing connections can be blocked by AFM policy. Diagnostics that use ICMP error messages, such as traceroute, may fail to display information beyond the AFM device.
bugs.conditions: The AFM policy has a rule to drop or reject that can match the IP header of ICMP messages going from a router IP address back to the client or server IP address that sent the original packet.
bugs.impact: Network diagnostics such as traceroute through an AFM device will not display information from routers between the AFM device and the destination IP address.
bugs.workaround: If possible and allowed, create an AFM rule matching the affected ICMP packets with an action of accept-decisively.

bugs.title: Missing health monitor information for FQDN members
bugs.symptoms: Health monitor information and status are both missing for FQDN nodes and pool members.
bugs.conditions: FQDN nodes or pool members.
bugs.impact: GUI does not show health monitors info/status in node properties page, pool member properties page, or monitor instances page. Difficulty checking health monitor info/status for FQDN members.
bugs.workaround: Check logs for this info.

bugs.title: Cluster is removed from HA group on restart
bugs.symptoms: When the system is rebooted (or "bigstart restart" is executed), any HA groups with clusters in them will have those clusters removed.
bugs.conditions: Chassis-based system with an ha-group and ha-group-cluster configured. All blades have to reboot, since if a single blade is rebooted it pulls the running-config from the primary slot.
bugs.impact: HA cluster configuration is missing every time all the blades are rebooted.
bugs.fix: Reverted changes made for ID481611.

bugs.title: referer header in request is not completely deflated at gateway, f5-w-dobledot paths are not reduced
bugs.symptoms: Referer header received by backend contains in the path component(s) 'f5-w-doubledot'.
bugs.conditions: There were doubledot components in referer URL (for example: '../../test.html').
bugs.impact: Backend can be confused after receiving referer header with different value.
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used to fix referer header value; no general iRule exists.

bugs.title: CMI device credentials (device name or password) containing XML special charactersresults in peer discovery error
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to set up CMI device credentials (device name or password), an error message can result if the device name (of the current device, or the newly specified name for the target device) or the administrator password (for the target device) contains certain characters. The error message has this format: java.io.IOException: Could not read response from server: ParseError at [row,col]:[1,225] Message: Element type 'bigip2' must be followed by either attribute specifications, '>' or '/>'.
bugs.conditions: The list of characters is any XML special character (less than, greater than, or ampersand).
bugs.impact: Failure to set up CMI sync.
bugs.workaround: For the device name, these characters are illegal and a different device name should be chosen. If the current device has any of the specified characters, you can use the command 'mv cm device source-name target-name' to change the name of the device. There is no workaround if the relevant character is in the password field, except to change the password.

bugs.title: [Policy Sync] Connectivity profile with a customized logo fails
bugs.symptoms: Policy sync failed with a customized logo in connectivity profile.
bugs.conditions: Configure a customized logo on the connectivity profile. Associate the profile with the access profile through a virtual server. Start a policy sync.
bugs.impact: Policy Sync fails.
bugs.workaround: Keep the default logo for connectivity profile. After syncing to target, customize directly on the devices.
bugs.fix: A user can include a customized logo in a connectivity profile and sync it.

bugs.title: Config sync of SecurID config file fails on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: After uploading a new SecurID config file using the GUI, mcpd restarts and fails to sync the file to the secondary.
bugs.conditions: If APM is provisioned, and upload a new SecurID config file via the GUI. This can also happen on device group peers.
bugs.impact: The secondary blade restarts mcpd, which in turn restarts several other daemons. The secondary blade never receives the config file, so if it becomes primary, it does not have the correct configuration.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh: tmsh modify apm aaa securid secureid-name config-files modify { sdconf.rec { local-path /path/to/sdconf.rec } }.

bugs.title: Individual attack signature can't be disabled on a specific header
bugs.symptoms: A specific attack signature is matched on a specific header or a specific allowed cookie. You are unable to disable it only on a specific header/cookie and not on the policy
bugs.conditions: a specific signature is matched only on a specific header or cookie.
bugs.impact: Disabling the signature on the policy may miss attacks. Enabling the signature will cause false positives on the occurrence on the header/cookie
bugs.fix: Added the functionality to disable specific attack signature on a specific header or cookie.

bugs.title: ASM triggers geo-based dos mitigation against RFC1918 addresses.
bugs.symptoms: A geo-based IP mitigation dos attacked started against an internal IP address.
bugs.conditions: Traffic from internal addresses is arriving to the system. A geo location mitigation is configured for DosL7.
bugs.impact: All internal addresses getting blocked as a geo location.
bugs.workaround: Whitelist the internal addresses. Note: Doing this prevents all types of mitigation from these IP addresses.
bugs.fix: RFC1918 is not considered as a geolocation and during geolocation mitigation, traffic from these IPs will not get dropped. These IP addresses can still get mitigated during other mitigations. A new internal parameter, DOSL7.geolocation_drop_private_ips, default disable, is introduced. When enabled, the system changes this behavior so internal IP addresses do mitigate in the geolocation mitigation.

bugs.title: Secondary MCPD restarts when SAML IdP or SP Connector is created
bugs.symptoms: Secondary MCPD restarts when the admin creates APM SAML IdP Connector (or SP Connectors) from attached metadata on the primary blade.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP chassis with multiple blades where the configuration includes APM SAML IdP Connector or SP Connector created from attached metadata file.
bugs.impact: Secondary slot's MCPD restarts.

bugs.title: Multiple IP is not added through iRule after setting the state of a session to provision by iRule
bugs.symptoms: Provisioning an iRule may not add multiple IP's when state is set to provisioned
bugs.conditions: iRule with multiple IP's may not get added when provisioned
bugs.impact: IP's not present in the session
bugs.fix: Release the call back ctx connflow after setting session state asynchronously.

bugs.title: Tmm cores while changing properties of PEM policies and rules.
bugs.symptoms: If a policy with session reporting is configured on the BIG-IP system, and the policy is changed to remove this action, then a tmm core might be observed.
bugs.conditions: -- Session reporting is configured. -- Traffic is being processed. -- The policy is modified to remove the session reporting action.
bugs.impact: This core occurs rarely. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Deleting a session reporting action will not cause a tmm core.
bugs.workaround: None, except not removing session reporting while traffic is being processed.

bugs.title: 'tmsh load sys config' fails after key conversion to FIPS using web GUI
bugs.symptoms: Web GUI does not save config after key conversion to FIPS
bugs.conditions: On a Cavium-FIPS BIG-IP, create a normal key and then covert to FIPS using web GUI
bugs.impact: 'tmsh load sys config' fails
bugs.workaround: Two possible workarounds: 1) Run 'tmsh save sys config' after the key conversion to FIPS using web GUI 2) Convert normal key to FIPS using tmsh instead of web GUI
bugs.fix: Web GUI is now fixed to properly save config after key conversion to FIPS

bugs.title: TMM may crash when a client resets a connection
bugs.symptoms: When a client resets a connection while AAM is preparing to serve a response from cache TMM may crash causing failover and restart of AAM. A profile on a virtual from another BIG-IP module (other than AAM and LTM) may contribute to the issue.
bugs.conditions: 1) AAM must be provisioned. 2) A response to the requested URL must be cached and fresh. 3) Client resets a connection immediately after the request is done and the response has not started to serve.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Install the fix.
bugs.fix: Fix removes the condition when AAM starts to serve the response to the already aborting connection.

bugs.title: Using tmsh to display the number of elements in a DNS cache may cause high CPU utilization, and the tmsh command may not complete
bugs.symptoms: After running the tmsh command "show ltm dns cache records <key|msg|nameserver|rrset> cache <name> count-only" you may experience the following symptoms: - One of the TMM instances on the system climbs to 100% CPU utilization for a prolonged amount of time. - The odd-numbered hyperthread (i.e. 1) corresponding to the even-numbered hyperthread (i.e. 0) where the busy TMM instance is running is partially halted by the HT-Split feature (this will be observable in utilities such as "top" and by the presence of "Idle enforce starting" log messages in the /var/log/kern.log file). - After waiting for a very long time, the tmsh command may not actually return and display a record count. - The tmsh command does not respond to CTRL+C and continues running.
bugs.conditions: A DNS cache contains a large number of records and the BIG-IP Administrator runs the following tmsh command to determine the exact record count: "show ltm dns cache records <key|msg|nameserver|rrset> cache <name> count-only"
bugs.impact: Due to the high CPU utilization, traffic handling is impaired. Control-plane processes can also become affected, leading to different issues (this depends on the size and load of the BIG-IP system). For example, the lacpd process can become descheduled causing trunks to flap.
bugs.workaround: Do not run the specified tmsh command. If you have run the specified tmsh command and this has not returned after a very long time and you want restore normal system operation, perform the following steps: 1) Press CTRL+Z to background execution of the command. 2) Enter the "killall -9 tmsh" command (if you have multiple tmsh commands running and only want to kill the affected one, you will have to identify the correct tmsh process using utilities such as ps and top). If your login shell is tmsh and not bash, simply close your SSH session to the BIG-IP system (as you won't be able to perform the aforementioned steps).

bugs.title: hostagentd memory leak on VCMP hosts
bugs.symptoms: hostagentd may leak memory on BIG-IPs with VCMP provisioned.
bugs.conditions: VCMP provisioned with VCMP guests deployed.
bugs.impact: hostagentd will grow to consume all available host memory, which may eventually affect other services and overall system performance.
bugs.fix: This release resolves the memory leak that occurred when publishing VCMP host statistics to guests.

bugs.title: iApp templates are visible with only vCMP provisioned.
bugs.symptoms: iApp templates are visible with only vCMP provisioned. Depending on the iApp template, other modules must also be provisioned, for example, LTM, GTM, and so on, must be provisioned for certain iApp. Although template authors can templates even with only vCMP provisioned, the application does not work without the required modules provisioned.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when vCMP is provisioned as Dedicated and an author makes changes in an iApp with the assumption that the functionality is available because the iApp is visible.
bugs.impact: iApps are visible that are inappropriate for the provisioning. The system posts an error message if the user attempts to create an app from that template.
bugs.workaround: Provision the modules needed for the iApp to work.
bugs.fix: Hide a DNS and iApps menu when VCMP is provisioned

bugs.title: TCP Receive Window error messages are inconsistent on UI
bugs.symptoms: Different invalid inputs for Receive Window resulted in inconsistent error messages in TMUI.
bugs.conditions: Input invalid options (e.g, -1 and 0) for TCP Receive Window in TMUI.
bugs.impact: User is presented with two different input ranges whereas for both invalid options one correct input range should have been present.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMUI for TCP Receive Window is fixed for invalid inputs.

bugs.title: Some password policy changes are not reflected in /etc/shadow when synced in a CMI device group
bugs.symptoms: Some password policy settings (maximum and minimum durations, expiration warning) are reflected in /etc/shadow when a user's password is changed. In a CMI device group, changes to password policy are correctly synced, but the settings reflected in /etc/shadow are not.
bugs.conditions: CMI device group configured; maximum or minimum duration, or expiration warning, settings of password policy are used; user password is changed.
bugs.impact: Password policy may not be enforced consistently across all devices.

bugs.title: ICMP errors cause the associated FastL4/TCP connection to be reset
bugs.symptoms: When there are ICMP unreachable errors, the associated FastL4/TCP connection is reset by the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: There is an end to end connection from a client to server via BIG-IP and there is an ICMP error from the BIG-IP to pool member.
bugs.impact: FastL4/TCP connection from the client to BIG-IP will be reset.
bugs.fix: Provide a DB variable "TM.FastL4_rst_on_icmp" which is enabled by default. When enabled, the connection will be reset on ICMP errors. If the DB variable is disabled, ICMP errors will not result in the connection being torn down by the BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Configuration upgrade of httpclass which has the 'hosts' attribute done incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: A config with the deprecated 'httpclass' which has the 'hosts' attribute, on an upgrade to later version, gets converted to an LTM policy with the attributes 'http-host host values (value)'.
bugs.conditions: Needs a config with the 'httpclass' in it, which has the hosts attribute. F5 has replaced the HTTP Class profile with the introduction of the Local Traffic Policies feature in BIG-IP 11.4.0. During an upgrade to BIG-IP 11.4.0, if your configuration contains an HTTP Class profile, the BIG-IP system attempts to migrate the HTTP Class profile to an equivalent local traffic policy. You can find more information in SOL14409: The HTTP Class profile is no longer available in BIG-IP 11.4.0 and later, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/400/sol14409.html.
bugs.impact: The policy tries to match only the 'host' part of the HTTP Host header. The policy should be trying to match 'all' (that is, 'host' and 'port') instead. Note: F5 has replaced the HTTP Class profile with the introduction of the Local Traffic Policies feature in BIG-IP 11.4.0. During an upgrade to BIG-IP 11.4.0, if your configuration contains an HTTP Class profile, the BIG-IP system attempts to migrate the HTTP Class profile to an equivalent local traffic policy.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the config after upgrade to convert 'http-host host' to 'http-host all', for example: http-host host <====== values { tempbus.ladpc.net.il:3433 } } to http-host all <====== values { tempbus.ladpc.net.il:3433 } }
bugs.fix: Fixed the upgrade script to convert using the attribute 'all' instead of 'host'

bugs.title: sflow_agent may crash during BIG-IP system shutdown
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system is being shutdown or rebooted, or the sflow_agent is exiting for some other reason, the sflow_agent daemon may crash and produce a core.
bugs.conditions: Shutdown or restart of the BIG-IP system, or termination of the sflow_agent for any other reason
bugs.impact: sflow_agent might crash. There is no effective impact, since the BIG-IP system or process is already in the process of shutting down.
bugs.fix: During shutdown, the sflow_agent daemon does not crash.

bugs.title: TMM memory leak when RAR messages received from PCRF to delete for a non-existing sessions in PEM
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory leak. Memory consumption of TMM increases constantly and never reduces.
bugs.conditions: RAR messages with session-release cause received from PCRF for sessions where PEM does not have.
bugs.impact: Memory leak and eventually TMM will have to be restarted.
bugs.workaround: Make sure RAR messages are not sent for sessions which are non-existent in PEM
bugs.fix: This issues has been fixed now. No more memory leaks when RAR messages with session-release AVP set for non-existent sessions in PEM

bugs.title: DNS Relay proxy service doesn't resolve static hosts in certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: DNS Relay proxy service does not resolve static hosts if no DNS server is configured at the Network Access resource.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: DNS Relay proxy service is installed on machine; A DNS server is configured at the Network Access resource; Full Tunnel mode is used.
bugs.impact: Static hosts are not resolvable on client.
bugs.workaround: Specify a bogus DNS server in Network Access resource (for example Virtual Server address).

bugs.title: BIG-IP continues to monitor APM AAA pool with old monitor after monitor changed
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP APM continues to use old monitor (in addition to new monitor configuration) for APM AAA pool after the monitor type is modified.
bugs.conditions: APM AAA pool's monitor configuration is modified via the APM GUI.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP APM continues to use old monitor (in addition to new monitor) to monitor pool members for an AAA pool.
bugs.workaround: Once a system is affected by this issue, the misbehavior can be resolved by doing the following: Save and re-load the configuration to correct the incorrect information in mcpd: tmsh save sys config partitions all && tmsh load sys config partitions all

bugs.title: Qkview generates error-level message
bugs.symptoms: In version 11.6.0, if AVR is not provisioned but a module that uses AVR (for example, APM) is provisioned, the Qkview utility generates the following error-level log message: err tmsh[18617]: 01420006:3: virtual is not a valid entity.
bugs.conditions: AVR not provisioned, but modules that use AVR (e.g. APM, AFM) are provisioned.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. There is no impact on traffic.
bugs.workaround: This is a benign error message that can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: After restart, system remains in the INOPERATIVE state
bugs.symptoms: After restarting, it is normal for the system to remain in some state other than "Green/Active" for a few minutes while the system daemons complete their initialization. During this time the following advanced shell command may produce one or more lines of output: # bigstart status | grep waiting However, if this condition persists for more than five minutes after access to the root shell via the management interface is available, then you may be experiencing this defect.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP versions 11.5.x, 11.6.x or 12.0.x that have received the fix for bug 502443 but *not* 522784, may experience this issue. There are no officially supported BIG-IP releases that have this condition.
bugs.impact: As long as the system remains in the INOPERATIVE state, neither LTM nor ASM will function.
bugs.workaround: In order to work around this problem, de-provision ASM.
bugs.fix: Resolves a deadlock at startup, when LTM and ASM are provisioned, that may occur as a result of the fix for 502443.

bugs.title: HTML rewriting on client might leave 'style' attribute unrewritten.
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, the 'style' attribute of HTML tag containing CSS styles is not rewritten.
bugs.conditions: This happens when HTML is added to a page using document.write or assignment to innerHTML.
bugs.impact: Images added with inline CSS styles are not displayed. Direct requests to the backend are sent from browser.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to rewrite the 'style' attribute before adding HTML to the page.
bugs.fix: The HTML 'style' attribute is correctly rewritten for any tag.

bugs.title: MCPD can core as a result of another component shutting down prematurely
bugs.symptoms: During a small window of opportunity, mcpd can core if it is told to restart. This often occurs when another component has failed.
bugs.conditions: This issue generally occurs when another component has a problem which then initiates an mcpd restart.
bugs.impact: An mcpd core file is generated during shutdown, and it may initially appear as if mcpd coring was the cause of the restart.
bugs.fix: Ensured that connections are not deleted twice when shutting down, so mcpd no longer cores.

bugs.title: [TMSH] nested wildcard deletion will delete all the objects (matched or not matched)
bugs.symptoms: Nested wildcard deletion deletes all of the objects (matched or not matched).
bugs.conditions: Use deletion in a nested TMSH command. For example: tmsh modify gtm server GTM1 virtual-servers delete {f*} This deletes all virtual servers even if none of the servers match. The same issue applies to pool members.
bugs.impact: All objects are deleted, instead of those targeted for delete.
bugs.fix: Nested wildcard deletion now deletes matched objects only.

bugs.title: Hide the cleartext Session ID (MRHSessionCookie) visible as part of URL query param to prevent unauthorized access.
bugs.symptoms: Customer does not want to clearly expose the MRHSession cookie value in the URL because they found that they could bypass the authentication by putting the F5SSO_SID value into the MRHSession cookie from another laptop and gain access to the same virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Set up multidomain SSO, use httpwatch or tcpdump to capture the traffic and look at the F5SSO_SID in the URL. Set this value into the cookie from another location, and gain access to the virtual.
bugs.impact: Unauthorized access allows security breach.
bugs.workaround: iRule Workaround: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { if { [HTTP::is_redirect] } { log local0. "Redirect detected with Location header: [HTTP::header Location]" set loc [HTTP::header Location] if { $loc contains "F5SSO_SID" } { # Using F5SSO_SID hashed value inside Location header set F5_sid [string range $loc [expr {[string last "F5SSO_SID" $loc] + 10}] [string length $loc]] log local0. "F5_sid: $F5_sid" set shasid [URI::encode [b64encode [sha512 $F5_sid]]] # we create one subtable to access the hash from the sessionid table add -subtable "sha" $shasid $F5_sid indefinite indefinite log local0. "adding sessionID $F5_sid to ssha subtable with value $shasid" set newloc [string map [list $F5_sid $shasid] $loc] log local0. "Location after obfuscation: $newloc" HTTP::header replace Location $newloc unset loc unset newloc } } } when HTTP_REQUEST { log local0. "received [HTTP::method] [HTTP::host] [HTTP::uri]" if { [HTTP::uri] contains "F5Networks-SSO-Resp" } { # Switch F5SSO_SID value back from hash to real value log local0. "[HTTP::uri] contains F5Networks-SSO-Resp" set newuri2 [HTTP::uri] set F5_hash_b64 [string range $newuri2 [expr {[string first "F5SSO_SID=" $newuri2] + [string length "F5SSO_SID="]} ] [string length $newuri2] ] log local0. "F5SSO_SID value in base64 is: $F5_hash_b64" set lookup_sid [table lookup -subtable "sha" $F5_hash_b64] log local0. "lookup_sid is: $lookup_sid" set newuri2 [string map [list $F5_hash_b64 $lookup_sid] [HTTP::uri]] HTTP::uri $newuri2 log local0. "URI with SID: $newuri2" unset newuri2 unset lookup_sid unset F5_hash_b64 } # route traffic to internal APM VS accordingly if { [HTTP::host] == "www.primaryauth.com" } { use virtual VS_internal_primaryauth } elseif { [HTTP::host] == "www.site.com" } { use virtual VS_internal_site1 } }
bugs.fix: Following changes were made to avoid vulnerability attack of F5SSO_SID: 1.) While re-directing, Append a 8 byte generated random token in place of F5SSO-ID and store the value of SID in session-DB with the token as key. 2.) When the response comes with the token, lookup in session-DB to identify the SID value and delete the token to prevent future use of token by any illegitimate user attack.

bugs.title: diam_app_process_async_lookup may cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash
bugs.conditions: TMM may crash with diam_app_process_async_lookup when the traffic is triggered to the virtual which has gx profile
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fix double free for serdes message

bugs.title: Provide an option to encode subscription ID in CCR-U/CCR-T messages over Gx/Gy
bugs.symptoms: Some PCRF's require subscription ID in all CCR messages over Gx/Gy for easier session management.
bugs.impact: Some PCRF's will not work properly with PEM if subscription ID is not specified in CCR-u and CCR-T messages.
bugs.workaround: Set the sys db variable to True to see Subscription ID in CCR-u and CCR-T messages as well: Tmm.diameter.application.encode.subscriber.id.in.all.ccr Note: By default it is set to True.
bugs.conditions: PEM with Gx enabled and connected to a PCRF.

bugs.title: tmsh crashes when trying to perform a wildcard delete of iRules
bugs.symptoms: tmsh will crash with a segmentation fault if an administrator attempts to delete iRules using wildcard syntax (e.g., 'tmsh delete ltm rule rules\*'). This occurs if the object name includes either an asterisk (*) or left square bracket ([).
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP administrator runs a command such as the following: tmsh delete ltm rule rules\*
bugs.impact: tmsh crashes with a segmentation fault. The system is otherwise not impacted.
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to use wildcard syntax to delete iRules; instead, delete each iRule individually.

bugs.title: Websso cores when it tries to shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Websso core file is generated when it is in the process of shutting down.
bugs.conditions: Websso can be shutdown and restarted for many reasons. For example, when provisioning happens or when a mcpd or tmm process restarts.
bugs.impact: The impact is minimal because Websso cores during shutdown and will be restarted correctly.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Websso now handles shutdown events gracefully, and no core file is generated.

bugs.title: Merged may crash when file descriptors exhausted
bugs.symptoms: The merged daemon crashes.
bugs.conditions: The limit on file descriptors is exceeded.
bugs.impact: Merged crashes leaving a core file. The collection of system stats and merging of blade stats will not work until merged restarts.
bugs.workaround: Monitor the system file descriptor use and avoid exceeding the limit.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash bug in Merged.

bugs.title: Disabling on-demand-compile/on-demand-deploy on standby, sometimes the setting will revert back to enabled on the active or standby automatically
bugs.symptoms: On a HA pair disabling on-demand-compile/on-demand-deploy on standby gets synced across but finally causes on-demand-deploy to revert back to enabled on the active or standby
bugs.conditions: This only happen when 1. Active device is not in "quiescent" state when the on-demand feature is disabled. 2. The configuration change is done from standby device.
bugs.impact: on-demand-compile and on-demand-deploy may be enabled when not desired.
bugs.workaround: The general guideline of using the on-demand features is that all configuration changes should be done from Active device, not from standby devices.

bugs.title: Disabling/enabling blades in cluster can result in inconsistent failover state
bugs.symptoms: Not all blades in the cluster agree about the high availability (HA) status.
bugs.conditions: Disabling and enabling blades in a chassis that is configured to use HA Groups can sometimes result in a blade staying in standby even though the other blades in the chassis have gone active.
bugs.impact: When the blades disagree about active/standby state, traffic might be disrupted.
bugs.fix: Disabling/enabling blades in cluster no longer results in inconsistent failover state.

bugs.title: Change in route domain in NAT configuration does not take effect until restart
