bugs.symptoms: When the route domain of the originating address of a NAT configuration is changed without the address itself being changed, the change does not take effect. Viewing the configuration through tmsh and the GUI indicates that the change has worked, when it is not yet in use.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when editing an existing NAT configuration and changing the route domain without changing the address.
bugs.impact: The intended NAT change is not in effect.
bugs.workaround: In order to make the change take effect, delete and recreate the NAT or restart tmm.

bugs.title: In vpe if the LDAP server returns "cn=" (lower case) dn/group match fails
bugs.symptoms: In rare case when dn is returned with cn= in lower case VPE is failing to match groupnames
bugs.conditions: Server that returns cn in low case
bugs.impact: Group mapping doesn't work
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Fixed to support CN in both upper & lower cases.

bugs.title: DNS resolver multiplexing might cause unexpected behaviors
bugs.symptoms: DNS resolver multiplexing might cause unexpected behaviors, resulting in multiple error message: notice hud_msg_queue is full.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with a DNS resolver configured.
bugs.impact: TMM cores or connflows not expiring. System posts messages similar to the following: notice hud_msg_queue is full.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores and connflows expire as expected. System posts messages similar to the following: notice hud_msg_queue is full.

bugs.title: Expired files are not cleaned up after receiving an ASM Manual Synchronization
bugs.symptoms: If a device only receives full ASM sync files from its peers, it never performs cleanup of files that are no longer needed.
bugs.conditions: An ASM manual synchronization device group is being used.
bugs.impact: May eventually lead to disk space exhaustion.
bugs.fix: Files are now correctly cleaned up after loading a new configuration.

bugs.title: Citrix HTML5 client fails to start from Storefront in integration mode when Access Policy is configured with Redirect ending.
bugs.symptoms: Citrix HTML5 client fails to start from Storefront in integration mode when Access Policy is configured with Redirect ending. If an access policy has Redirect ending, the Citrix HTML5 client will fail to start with HTTP 400 error.
bugs.conditions: Citrix Storefront configured in integration mode through APM.
bugs.impact: HTML5 client not usable for this sort of integration
bugs.fix: Fixed Citrix HTML5 handling code so that it works fine with the Redirect endings in access policies.

bugs.title: Apply Policy finishes with coapi_query failure displayed
bugs.symptoms: GUI actions to apply policy appear to fail with an error message regarding coapi_query.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: The policy is correctly applied locally, the coapi_query error message occurs after the commit. This error, however, prevents correct behavior for device group synchronization of the change.
bugs.workaround: Use REST API to apply the policy: POST https://<MGMT_IP>/mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/apply-policy { "policy": { "fullPath": "/Common/<POLICY_NAME>" } }
bugs.fix: This release fixes an error that intermittently caused the Apply Policy action to fail.

bugs.title: ASM REST: MCP Persistence is not triggered via REST actions
bugs.symptoms: Some REST calls that affect Security policies should be persistent to BIG-IP config files after their completion (create, delete, association to virtual servers, and changing language encoding), but are not.
bugs.conditions: REST API is being used to manage Security Policies.
bugs.impact: If the device is restarted configuration may be lost.
bugs.workaround: Any other action that will persist configuration (like an ASM config change through the GUI, or any LTM configuration change).
bugs.fix: Configuration is now correctly persisted when required after ASM REST actions.

bugs.title: TMM may core when using iRule custom actions in PEM policies
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores
bugs.conditions: When using custom iRule actions in a PEM policy, triggering a use of the action or modifying the action will cause the TMM to reset.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using custom iRule actions in PEM policies.
bugs.fix: Freeing of memory for storing the custom action was done to a different pool than whence it was allocated; used the correct free routine.

bugs.title: Authentication fails with StoreFront protocol
bugs.symptoms: Wyse fails to authenticate through APM
bugs.conditions: Wyse fails to auth through APM when it configured for SF proxy protocol
bugs.impact: Authentication fails
bugs.fix: Support StoreFront Protocol for Wyse client

bugs.title: aced daemon might crash on exit
bugs.symptoms: When the aced process is going to exit (daemon shutdown/restart), it might generate a core file intermittently.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when aced daemon shuts down.
bugs.impact: This causes a core file to be generated.
bugs.fix: The aced process no longer intermittently generates a core file.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Creating too many iFiles causes tmm crash.
bugs.symptoms: Tmm might crash when too many iFiles are created.
bugs.conditions: The crash has been seen with 1700 iFiles on a BIG-IP with 6 tmm threads.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: - Increase the number of file descriptors (ulimit -n) in /etc/bigstart/scripts/tmm. - bigstart restart tmm.
bugs.fix: The maximum number of open file descriptors now scales with the number of tmm threads, so tmm no longer crashes when a very large number of iFiles (e.g., 1700) are created.

bugs.title: In very rare cases Machine Certificate service may fail to find private key
bugs.symptoms: Non-elevated client component is able to find certificate but not the key, while machine cert service/F5 Elevation Helper fails to find certificate. f5certhelper.txt (helper) or logterminal.txt (in windows\temp folder for service) contains: 1, , 0, , EXCEPTION - CCertInfo::FindCertificateInStore: CertFindCertificateInStore failed with error code: 80092004
bugs.conditions: IE/Edge Client is not running under Admin user. Special certificate is used.
bugs.impact: User fails to pass access policy.
bugs.workaround: Run IE/BIG-IP Edge Client under administrator.
bugs.fix: Now both service and elevation helper can find those specific certificates.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is used as SAML Identity Provider(IdP), TMM may restart under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP is used as IdP. - Client or Service Provider sends a number of specific invalid requests to BIG-IP
bugs.impact: TMM is not available while restarting
bugs.fix: Issue where TMM would restart as a result of invalid user request is now fixed.

bugs.title: Minor memory leak on IdP when SLO is configured on bound SP connectors.
bugs.symptoms: Several bytes of memory are leaked when SAML SSO is executed on BIG-IP system, configured as an Identity Provider (IdP), when the Service Provider (SP) connector has single logout (SLO) configured.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as Identity Provider, and SLO is configured for bound SP Connector.
bugs.impact: Several bytes of memory are leaked.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, disable SLO on SP connectors.
bugs.fix: Fixed memory leaks in SAML Identity Provider (IdP) when when SLO is configured in a Service Provider (SP) connector.

bugs.title: Windows Cache and Session Control cannot support a period in the access profile name
bugs.symptoms: An access profile name containing a period will not work when using Windows Cache and Session Control. For example '/Common/test.profile' will not work. When evaluating the access policy, an end-user will be redirected to an error page.
bugs.conditions: Applies to any APM with Windows Cache and Session Control.
bugs.impact: Access Profile names cannot include a dot. Invalid name: '/Common/profile.name' Valid name: '/Common/profile_name'
bugs.fix: One of the PHP files for cache control has a regex that looks for invalid access profile names. This regex had previously flagged any profile name with a period to be invalid. The regex has been updated to allow periods.

bugs.title: mcpd on secondary blades will restart with an error message about a sflow_http_virtual_data_source object
bugs.symptoms: mcpd on secondary blades may restart and log an error of the following form: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01070734:3: Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (sflow_http_virtual_data_source) object ID (44). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:sflow_http_virtual_data_source status:13)... failed validation with error 17237812.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions under which this occurs are not well understood. The immediately triggering event is a change in the cluster's primary blade.
bugs.impact: All services on an affected blade restart.
bugs.fix: mcpd on secondary blades may restart and log an sflow_http_virtual_data_source error after a change in the cluster's primary blade.

bugs.title: Log an error message when firewall rule serialization fails due to maximum blob limit being hit.
bugs.symptoms: Prior to fix, if AFM rule serialization fails due to OOM condition in pktclass-daemon, it's not identifiable if the failure is due to Out of Memory condition or the Max Blob limit being reached. Both the errors were logged as OOM in /var/log/ltm
bugs.conditions: AFM rule serialization fails due to max blob limit
bugs.impact: Hard to isolate the problem that serialization failed due to max blob limit
bugs.fix: With the fix, AFM rule serialization failure due to max blob limit is logged appropriately in /var/log/ltm making it easier to identify the cause of the failure.

bugs.title: pkcs11d core when connecting to SafeNet HSM
bugs.symptoms: Very occasionally, using the SafeNet hardware security module (HSM) results in a pkcs11d core.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the SafeNet HSM is used. Because of the rare and intermittent nature of the issue, other required conditions are not known.
bugs.impact: pkcs11d cores, and HSM-based SSL traffic fails. This occurs as a result of the SafeNet library. It is not a BIG-IP system-specific issue.
bugs.fix: The SafeNet library has been updated, and pkcs11d no longer cores intermittently.

bugs.title: COMPRESS::enable keeps compression enabled for a subsequent HTTP request.
bugs.symptoms: COMPRESS::enable keeps compression enabled for a subsequent HTTP request. The response for the first HTTP request enables the compression, but it is not used since the payload is empty. For the second HTTP request (whose URI indicates that it is not supposed to be compressed), the system still compresses the response because the first request did not disable compression.
bugs.conditions: Subsequent HTTP requests in the same TCP connection. - First HTTP response contains empty payload and enabling the compression. - Second HTTP response still gets compressed.
bugs.impact: Unintended compression for subsequent HTTP responses.
bugs.workaround: Disable compression in the else case manually in the iRule using COMPRESS::disable.
bugs.fix: Compression is now disabled after an HTTP response with empty payload for iRule-based enabling.

bugs.title: In a device group, installing a UCS (on any one of the peers in group) does not propagate the ASU file (that is bundled with UCS) to other peers
bugs.symptoms: In a device group, after installing a UCS file (on any one of the peers in group), an inconsistent state of Application security update version is achieved between peer machines.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned. Device group with ASM sync enabled. Install UCS file with a bundled ASU version different then the currently installed.
bugs.impact: An inconsistent state of ASU version is achieved between peer machines.
bugs.workaround: Manually trigger ASU update/install from: Security > Security Updates > Application Security

bugs.title: Upgrade from 10.x to 11.2.0 or later does not add existing routing protocols to RD0.
bugs.symptoms: If you are directly upgrading from version 10.x to version 11.2.0 or later with a working dynamic routing protocols configuration may encounter that the routing protocol is disabled on upgrade to 11.2.0 or later.
bugs.conditions: - Upgrade from 10.x to 11.2.0 or later. - Routing protocol enabled in tmrouted dbkeys. - No route domain 0 (zero) (RD0) configuration, that is defaults of all VLANs in RD0, no comment, leading to no existing configuration in bigip_base.conf
bugs.impact: Routing protocol information is missing from RD0, ZebOS is not running (although configured).
bugs.workaround: There are several workarounds to this issue: - Causing the RD0 configuration to exist by adding a comment to the 10.x description field and saving prior to upgrade. - Re-adding the routing protocol to the RD0 configuration after the upgrade. - Perform an intermediate upgrade from 10.x to 11.0.0 or 11.1.0 prior to upgrading to an 11.2.0 or later version.
bugs.fix: Routing protocols are now correctly configured on Route Domain 0 (zero) (RD0) after upgrade to version 11.2.0 or later.

bugs.title: Power Supply status reported incorrectly after LBH reset
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP appliances with the Backplane Micro-Controller Hybrid (LBH) type of Always-On-Management device, Power Supply status reporting and enumeration may function incorrectly if the LBH resets due to a watchdog reboot or other cause.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series, BIG-IP 5000-/7000-series, and BIG-IP 10000-/12000-series platforms.
bugs.impact: Resets of the LBH device occur very rarely. When this issue occurs, the status reporting and enumeration of appliance power supplies may be inaccurate. Errors may be reported when attempting to obtain sensor values from non-present power supplies. Power supply presence, status and identification may be reported incorrectly following power supply removal or reinsertion.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue and restore correct reporting of power supply status, you can restart the chmand process. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Restarting the chmand process also restarts core BIG-IP system daemons such as TMM. Running this procedure interrupts traffic processing. 1.Log in to the BIG-IP command line. 2.To restart the chmand process, type the following command: bigstart restart chmand.
bugs.fix: Power Supply status is now reported correctly after LBH reset.

bugs.title: Upgrade: file path failure for process name attribute in snmp.
bugs.symptoms: The upgrade operation might fail to update the file path name for snmp.process_name, causing a validation error.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 10.x. to 11.5.1 or later.
bugs.impact: The upgrade operation does not remove the parent path name from process-monitors, which might cause a validation error.
bugs.workaround: Edit the process name path in /config/BIG-IP_sys.conf to reflect the location. For more information, see K13540: The BIG-IP system may return inaccurate results for the prTable SNMP object at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13540.

bugs.title: Support two-factor authentication for Citrix Receivers in StoreFront proxy mode
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receivers do not detect 2-factor authentication when connecting to APM.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured as StoreFront proxy and 2-factor authentication is used.
bugs.impact: Citrix Receivers do not detect 2-factor authentication.
bugs.workaround: To enable 2-factor authentication, put a Variable Assign agent in front of the Logon Page in VPE with the following expression: session.citrix.client_auth_type = expr {"1"}.
bugs.fix: Added support for two-factor authentication for Citrix Receivers in StoreFront proxy mode.
bugs.behavior: Two-factor RSA+AD auth for Citrix Receiver clients now requires a new VPE configuration when APM is configured in StoreFront Integration mode. Note: To avoid a potential issue, if Citrix Receiver was already configured against APM, the Receiver accounts must be recreated.

bugs.title: When iRule or Web-Acceleration profile demotes HTTP request from HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/1.0, OneConnect may not pool serverside connections
bugs.symptoms: An HTTP virtual server with OneConnect and RAM Cache will not consistently keep server-side connections alive and idle (for reuse), depending on the HTTP version that the client uses. Clients that use HTTP/1.1 will result in fewer serverside connections being reused.
bugs.conditions: HTTP virtual server with HTTP cache enabled (in RAM cache mode, not AAM mode) and OneConnect profile. Alternately, an iRule that down-steps the HTTP request version to HTTP/1.0
bugs.impact: Increased server utilization and number of ports in use / timewait / finwait as a result of OneConnect and RAM Cache closing serverside connections more frequently than expected. Inconsistent behavior as a result of client HTTP version.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can work around this issue by inserting a Connection: Keep-Alive header.

bugs.title: TCP reset with RTSP Too Big error when streaming interleaved data
bugs.symptoms: RTSP connection containing interleaved streams is aborted mid-stream, causing loss of data. This occurs when there is packet loss and retransmission due to an unreliable connection. A RST is sent by BIG-IP with cause "Too big". There is an RTSP profile parameter Maximum Header Size. When the RTSP filter receives a burst of reassembled stream data that exceeds this size, it aborts with that RST cause. When this parameter is raised above the value of parameter Maximum Queued Data, that parameter is exceeded and the RST cause is "Hudfilter abort". When both parameters are raised much higher, an abort is less likely, but can still occur with cause "Out of memory" (which is a false report as the system is not out of memory).
bugs.conditions: RTSP profile configured. Interleaved stream. Packet retransmissions due to an unreliable connection.
bugs.impact: RTSP traffic is interrupted or dropped TCP session is reset with a cause of "Too Big" or "Hudfilter abort".
bugs.workaround: Set both the Maximum Header Size and Maximum Queued Data values to a value greater than 64 KB. This reduces the likelihood of failure, but is only a partial workaround.
bugs.fix: RTSP interleaved traffic passes reliably, even over an unreliable connection experiencing packet retransmission.

bugs.title: istats help not clear for negative increment
bugs.symptoms: The help for the istats command line tool was not clear on how to specify a negative increment for a gauge iStat.
bugs.conditions: Try to increment a gauge iStat by a negative amount using the istats command line tool.
bugs.impact: Bash shell would print a cryptic error and the help did not clarify how to make it work
bugs.workaround: Research bash shell options for the cryptic error.
bugs.fix: The help for the istats command line was augmented to clearly state that the double-dash option should be specified before the negative number.

bugs.title: 'warning: Failed to find EUDs' message during formatting installation
bugs.symptoms: The following message may appear on the console: warning: Failed to find EUDs warning: Failed to get volume id for EUD
bugs.conditions: This warning occurs during a formatting installation.
bugs.impact: No impact. The message was intended to be logged at the 'info' level.
bugs.fix: The 'warning: Failed to find EUDs' diagnostic message during installation has been changed from a warning to info

bugs.title: Session entries may timeout prematurely on some TMMs
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios, session entries may not be refreshed when the TMM that owns the entry is used to process the connection.
bugs.conditions: When the TMM owning the session entry is a different one to the TMM handling the connection and the entry is retrieved, for example via irule, "session lookup uie"; the timeout will be extended. When the TMM owning the entry and the one handling the connection is the same, then the entry may not have its timeout changed and lead to premature removal.
bugs.impact: Different TMMs may behave differently and cause confusion when using the session table.
bugs.fix: Session table entries now consistently get their timeout values touched in all scenarios.

bugs.title: Deletion of key/cert/csr fails to update bigip.conf.
bugs.symptoms: Deletion of key/cert/csr fails to update bigip.conf.
bugs.conditions: Use the GUI to delete a key/cert/csr or all of them together, and notice that bigip.conf is not changed.
bugs.impact: Because of this, any deletion from GUI brings back the configuration object after a 'tmsh load sys config'.
bugs.fix: Deletion of key/cert/csr fails now updates bigip.conf as expected.

bugs.title: Certificate bundle summary information does not propagate to device group peers
bugs.symptoms: Certificate summary information about individual certificates in a bundle does not propagate to device group peers after a config sync.
bugs.conditions: A certificate file is create in a folder synced to a device group.
bugs.impact: Certificate information about the bundle is not displayed on peers. However, the bundle itself is intact and available.
bugs.workaround: Upload certificates independently on active and standby devices, and then sync. Note: After applying the workaround, you might still see the wrong expiry dates on the GUI. To check the expiration status of the SSL certificates, use the tmsh command: tmsh list sys crypto cert <certificate name>

bugs.title: tmsh error map not included in /etc/alertd
bugs.symptoms: tmsh error map is not included in /etc/alertd.
bugs.conditions: File /etc/alertd/bigip_tmsh_error_maps.h missing.
bugs.impact: The tmsh error maps include certificate expiration warnings (i.e., BIGIP_TMSH_TMSH_CERT_EXPIRED, BIGIP_TMSH_TMSH_CERT_WILL_EXPIRE). This information is used to create alerts. Not having the map makes it difficult to create alerts for tmsh related errors (e.g., certificate expiration warnings).

bugs.title: IPv4 link-local addresses can cause TMM crash when used in conjunction with ECMP routes
bugs.symptoms: TMM can crash and ECMP routes via IPv4 link-local addresses may not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: This happens only for specific IP range with dynamic routing and multiple next hops.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using 169.254 prefix.
bugs.fix: ECMP routes are working correctly and TMM does not crash

bugs.title: Adding multiple signatures concurrently via REST
bugs.symptoms: Adding multiple ASM signatures concurrently in REST actions causes deadlock.
bugs.conditions: Multiple ASM signatures are added concurrently using REST.
bugs.impact: Some signature REST add actions will fail due to deadlock.
bugs.workaround: Wait until signature add action has completed in REST before issuing the next add.
bugs.fix: Multiple signatures can be added concurrently using REST.

bugs.title: Incorrect parsing of abnormal request headers during DOS attacks
bugs.symptoms: When the DOS profile is in use, and a client-side mitigation is active, in some rare cases the request headers were parsed incorrectly, causing valid requests to be reset.
bugs.conditions: DOS profile is used, DOS attack is active and mitigated using Client-Side Integrity. This is only relevant for the requests which are marked for DOS mitigation.
bugs.impact: Some valid requests are blocked during the client-side DOS mitigation.

bugs.title: Control sending alerts during the source integrity learning process
bugs.symptoms: False positive alerts might be sent while source integrity learning process.
bugs.conditions: Learn mode is configured for a tag, and URL's content is dynamic.
bugs.impact: Source integrity low severity alerts will be sent on every mismatch, before a mature valued has learned.
bugs.fix: The sending of low score alerts during the source integrity learning process is now controlled by a DB variable.

bugs.title: iRule ISTATS::remove does not work
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule invokes ISTATS::remove to remove an iStat, the iStat is not removed.
bugs.conditions: Invoking the ISTATS::remove command from an iRule.
bugs.impact: The value of the iStat remains defined.
bugs.workaround: Use istats-triggers and iCall scripts to invoke the iStats command line tool indirectly.

bugs.title: The DB variable provision.tomcat.extramb is cleared on first boot.
bugs.symptoms: The DB variable provision.tomcat.extramb is 0 (zero) after upgrading using a configuration with the variable set to a non-zero value.
bugs.conditions: The DB variable provision.tomcat.extramb set to a value other than 0 before installing.
bugs.impact: The DB value is not rolled forward, so the GUI gets less than expected amount of memory.
bugs.workaround: After the first boot, set the DB variable provision.tomcat.extramb to the desired amount or restore the saved UCS at /var/local/ucs/config.ucs.
bugs.fix: The DB variable provision.tomcat.extramb now retains the specified value when rolling forward a configuration.

bugs.title: Unable to run lvreduce
bugs.symptoms: Unable to run lvreduce command due to missing program 'blockdev'. (The missing program 'blockdev' is part of the util-linux-extras package.)
bugs.conditions: Attempting to reallocate disk resources when upgrading a vCMP system.
bugs.impact: Cannot reallocate the vmdisks app volume.
bugs.workaround: Acquire the /sbin/blockdev executable from a different BIG-IP device running version 11.6.0-HF6 or 12.x, and install it on the BIG-IP device affected by this issue. Note: If the receiving system is a multi-blade VIPRION, you must install the file on each blade. If you do not have a suitable donor device available, you can contact F5 Support, who will be able to supply the executable to you. Note: Using a blockdev executable from another source is not recommended.
bugs.fix: The blockdev utility is now present, so you can run the lvreduce command to reallocate the vmdisks app volume.

bugs.title: Multiple Source addresses are not allowed on a TMSH SNMP community
bugs.symptoms: If multiple source addresses are specified on a TMSH snmp community command (add, modify,delete, replace-all). Only the first address will be saved.
bugs.conditions: Specifying multiple source addresses are specified on a TMSH snmp community command.
bugs.impact: The command is accepted, but only the first address will be allowed snmp access.
bugs.workaround: Add an additional source address to another snmp community object that has the same community string.
bugs.fix: The validation for source address from the snmp community object has been changed so that only one address can be entered at a time. Multiple source address can be entered only one address at a time.

bugs.title: PEM: Invalid HSL log generated when when session with static subscriber deleted.
bugs.symptoms: Invalid HSL logs generated when static subscriber session is deleted
bugs.conditions: HSL logging configured in the subscriber policy and static subscriber session is deleted.
bugs.impact: Invalid HSL log lines will create discrepancy.
bugs.workaround: Manually filter out these lines from HSL logs.
bugs.fix: Issues has been fixed now. NO more extra lines in HSL logs.

bugs.title: Missing power supplies issue warning message that should be just a notice message.
bugs.symptoms: Missing power supplies issue warning message in /var/log/ltm when the message should be just a notice. Absent power supplies should be notice level, not warning level since this is a normal acceptable way of running a system.
bugs.conditions: Running chassis with absent power supplies, or with power not applied, will cause ltm to issue warning messages.
bugs.impact: Extra logging.
bugs.workaround: Ignore missing power supply warning messages.
bugs.fix: Missing power supplies issue warning message in /var/log/ltm when the message should be just a notice. Absent power supplies should be notice level, not warning level since this is a normal acceptable way of running a system.

bugs.title: Error updating daemon ha heartbeat
bugs.symptoms: During shutdown you see the following error in /var/log/ltm: err vcmpd[8590]: 01510004:3: Error updating daemon ha heartbeat: VcmpdHeartbeat.cpp:251 error 0x01140031
bugs.conditions: This issue applies only on shutdown if the shutdown takes a long time.
bugs.impact: Error messages are displayed, but as long as this is occurring only on shutdown this means that vcmpd is unable to communicate with sod, which has already shut down.
bugs.fix: vcmpd will now only log "Error updating daemon ha heartbeat" if the system is not shutting down.

bugs.title: The MOS boot process appears to hang.
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP 2000 series or BIG-IP 4000 series device is booted into MOS (either manually or as a result of a user running the image2disk utility), the MOS boot process appears to hang. In reality, MOS boots successfully, but loses its connection to the BIG-IP system's serial console.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP 2000 series or BIG-IP 4000 series device with a MOS version older than 2.8.9 - 587.0 is booted from MOS.
bugs.impact: If you booted into MOS manually, you cannot carry out the tasks that you had set out to do. You must reset the device (either physically or via the AOM menu) to recover it. If the system booted into MOS automatically (as a result of a user running the image2disk utility to perform a clean installation), the installation completes successfully and the system reboots correctly at the end of the installation. However, you cannot see and follow the re-imaging process because of this issue. In this case, you can watch the (seemingly hung) serial console until the system reboots by itself.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by performing a temporary installation of BIG-IP version 12.0.0 to a new boot slot. No further action is required. This temporary installation of BIG-IP version 12.0.0 can be deleted once completed. This temporary installation of version 12.0.0 has the effect of upgrading MOS to a version which resolves this issue.
bugs.fix: A BIG-IP 2000 series or BIG-IP 4000 series device with a MOS version older than 2.8.9 - 587.0 is booted from MOS now retains its connection to the serial console.

bugs.title: Can delete last ip address on a gtm server but cannot load a config with a gtm server with no ips
bugs.symptoms: Current configuration validation will allow a user to delete the last (only remaining) IP address on a GTM server. However, since a GTM server cannot be created/loaded without at least one IP address, the configuration will fail to load.
bugs.conditions: User has deleted the last IP address on a GTM server.
bugs.impact: Configuration load will fail. If the GTMs are in a sync group, this will also break sync because the config change cannot be loaded by any GTM.
bugs.workaround: User must either delete the server from the config if it has no more valid IPs, or must add at least one IP to the server's IP address list.
bugs.fix: Extended MCPD validation to ensure any deleted GTM link/GTM server addresses do not leave parent objects without addresses.

bugs.title: iControl command pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 may fail if httpd is restarted or session times out.
bugs.symptoms: When pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 is used immediately after httpd is restarted, or when pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 is used after the session-timeout period, an 'Internal error' response is received. This issue is not seen if another iControl call is made and pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 is tried after that.
bugs.conditions: pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 is used immediately after httpd is restarted, or when pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 is used after the session-timeout period.
bugs.impact: iControl command may fail if httpd is restarted or session times out.
bugs.fix: iControl command pkcs12_import_from_file_v2 now completes successfully if httpd is restarted or session times out.

bugs.title: TMM may crash if PEM report format script with iRule are executed on top of existing parked iRule
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash under race condition, that if there is PEM flow reporting with format script that contains iRules accessing info from/to different TMMs gets executed when there is already an iRule executed and access different iRules on top of a connection/flow, and the connection/flow is reset. The fix will not execute the format script if it sees an irule is already parked for that flow. As a result, no log message will be sent in this case. In the versions before the fix, the user may have seen a log with stale info, or might see duplicate logs. After the fix, no log will be sent out in the situation described above.
bugs.conditions: 1. PEM flow reporting is enabled with format script that contains iRules access info from/to different TMMs 2. an iRule script that will access info from/to different TMM (that is, it will be parked on the connection/flow) is being executed and parked on the connection/flow 3. the connect/flow is reset 4. the PEM flow reporting with format script in #1 gets executed.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: A patch will be needed for such tmm crash under race condition, when PEM flow reporting with format script are required along with iRules.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed by making sure that PEM flow reporting with format script will not be executed if it detects another iRule script is already parked on the flow. However, given this is quite rare race condition, the PEM flow reporting with format script will be triggered again when reporting condition (volume or time based) is met and there is no concurrent iRule scripted parked.

bugs.title: Fix TMSH show and reset-stats commands for multi-ip sessions defect.
bugs.symptoms: TMSH show and reset-stats commands doesn't work properly for multi-ip sessions.
bugs.conditions: Sessions are multi-ip sessions with at least on ipv6 addr.
bugs.impact: reset-stats does not clear individual IP stats
bugs.fix: Fix TMSH pem sessiondb show and reset-stats commands with all-properties option. The pem_session_mult_ip_data_stats struct doesn't include the ipv6 prefix length information.

bugs.title: Adding multiple signature sets concurrently via REST
bugs.symptoms: Adding multiple ASM signature sets concurrently in REST actions causes deadlock.
bugs.conditions: Multiple ASM signature sets are added concurrently using REST.
bugs.impact: Some signature set REST add actions will fail due to deadlock.
bugs.workaround: Wait until signature set add action has completed in REST before issuing the next add.
bugs.fix: Multiple signature sets can be added concurrently using REST.

bugs.title: Excessive output for tmsh show running-config
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh show running-config displays many default configuration items. Although the output does display the user-configuration items as expected, it is not expected to include default configuration items in the output.
bugs.conditions: tmsh show sys running-config.
bugs.impact: The presence of excessive default configuration items makes the tmsh show running-config output parsing difficult.
bugs.fix: tmsh show sys running-config shows minimal default configuration.

bugs.title: Generate HF roll-up images for Virtual Edition platforms.
bugs.symptoms: Release HF roll-up images for Virtual Edition.
bugs.conditions: Building images for Virtual Edition.
bugs.impact: Release HF roll-up images for Virtual Edition.

bugs.title: Requests/responses may not be fully delivered to plugin in some circumstances
bugs.symptoms: If a plugin disables itself when encountering a request or response it is not interested in, subsequent requests or responses on the same connection may not be fully delivered to the plugin, causing the plugin and/or user application to function incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: The one known case where this occurs is when the WebSafe module is deployed and user applications being processed on WebSafe connections make use of POST requests.
bugs.impact: WebSafe connections may not function correctly. The problem is intermittent and depends on both the application and browser behaviors.
bugs.fix: Plugins now receive the full request/response when additional requests/responses on the same connection after encountering a request/response it is not interested in.

bugs.title: SElinux violations prevent cpcfg from touching /service/mcpd/forceload
bugs.symptoms: 'cpcfg' fails when copying configurations to an adjacent boot location.
bugs.conditions: 11.5.3 and 11.6.0 installed on two boot locations
bugs.impact: 'cpcfg' cannot be used
bugs.workaround: re-install software to target volume. configuration will be properly rolled forward as final step in software installation
bugs.fix: Corrected parameter count mismatch

bugs.title: Wildcard NAPTR record after deleting the NAPTR records
bugs.symptoms: There is a dns query issue when adding/deleting a NAPTR record through the Zonerunner.
bugs.conditions: After deleting a specific NAPTR record, the previously added wildcard NAPTR record will fail for wildcard dig queries and the system does not show the correct subdomains.
bugs.impact: Wildcard NAPTR record call fails after deleting the NAPTR records.
bugs.fix: Wildcard NAPTR record call now completes successfully after deleting the NAPTR records.

bugs.title: DNS licensed rate limits might be unintentionally activated.
bugs.symptoms: DNS licensed rate limits might be unintentionally activated.
bugs.conditions: This might occur with a license in which DNS services is unlimited, but BIG-IP DNS (formerly GTM) is limited.
bugs.impact: DNS licensed rate limits might be unintentionally activated. Rate counters will activate, even though rates are unlimited, which unnecessarily uses CPU cycles. Also, features that indirectly look at rate flags such as hardware DNS, might deactivate improperly even though rates are unlimited.
bugs.fix: DNS licensed rate limits are now handled as expected.

bugs.title: Use a DB variable to control whether IPsec interface should enforce policy check
bugs.symptoms: IPsec tunnel interface enforces the traffic-selector policy on its internal traffic. That is, the source and destination addresses of the packet going through the tunnel must comply with the traffic selector associated with the tunnel. Otherwise, the packet will be dropped. Sometimes, such policy enforcement is not needed.
bugs.conditions: You want to use the IPsec tunnel interface as a secure transport, and do not want the interface to filter traffic.
bugs.impact: Limit the use of the IPsec interface feature for traffic protection.
bugs.workaround: IPsec tunnel interface can be associated with a traffic selector that can accommodate the desired traffic.

bugs.title: PCCD optimization for IP address range
bugs.symptoms: Pccd blob size grow too big with large scale policy configuration. Which cause slow compilation and serialization.
bugs.conditions: large scale policy configuration.
bugs.impact: Slow compilation/serialization and large pccd blob.
bugs.fix: With PCCD ip address range optimization, PCCD will reduce it's compilation/serialization time and blob size.

bugs.title: IPsec interface is not forwarding TCP flow to the host when the destination is tunnel self-ip
bugs.symptoms: IPsec tunnel interface presents IPsec service via the regular network interface. Inherently, the self-IP address should allow external hosts to connect to the BIG-IP via TCP/UDP to this IP address. However, the connection is hairpinned back to the IPsec tunnel interface.
bugs.conditions: Create IPsec tunnel interface and assigned a self-IP with "allow-service all" so that the self-IP may accept external connections. At the other end of the IPsec tunnel, try TCP connection using "telnet", observe the "telnet" command fail.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP cannot accomplish certain services provided on the BIG-IP host, such as BGP over TCP.
bugs.workaround: A iRule can be created to forward the external connection on the IPsec tunnel self-IP to the host IP 127.0.0.1. Example, ltm virtual http_host { destination 10.99.0.11:80 ip-forward ip-protocol tcp mask 255.255.255.255 profiles { fastl4_stateless { } } rules { local_node } source 0.0.0.0/0 translate-address disabled translate-port disabled } ltm rule local_node { when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { node 127.0.0.1 80 } } 10.99.0.11 is the self-IP of the IPsec tunnel interface.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP can properly handle TCP/UDP connections to the BIG-IP over IPsec interface using its tunnel self-IP.

bugs.title: APM Log is filled with errors about failing to add/delete session entry
bugs.symptoms: APM log is filled with the following error when the issue occurs: May 21 16:34:16 BIG-IP4013mgmt err tmm2[20158]: 01490558:3: 00000000: Access stats encountered error: Failed to add/delete session entry (ERR_NOT_FOUND)
bugs.conditions: If a session times out before it completes policy evaluation, APM will still attempt to delete its marker from the established session namespace and, hence, results in ERR_NOT_FOUND error
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. However, APM log may become useless if the volume of the error is big.
bugs.fix: Access Filter now skips session marker deletion if the timed-out session is not in established state.

bugs.title: TMM crash when quering the session information
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when quering the session information using "tmsh show pem sessiondb subscriber-id "
bugs.conditions: Using tmsh show pem sessiondb subscriber-id to query session information
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Restore the display order of the multiple IP based on the order they are added

bugs.title: non_blocking_send/receive do not correctly handle EINTR situation for poll() == 0
bugs.symptoms: Interrupted poll() function in RemoteMcpConn.cpp functions non_blocking_receive and send is not properly handled.
bugs.conditions: Run a script processing async transactions in parallel with a script running basic REST calls.
bugs.impact: Either icrd_child will lock up or various calls will fail with 'operation canceled' response messages.

bugs.title: Windows info agent could not be passed from Windows 10
bugs.symptoms: APM endpoint check action "Windows Info agent" was not able to detect Windows 10 clients.
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP APM support Windows Info action on Windows 10 clients.

bugs.title: 'forward' command does not work if virtual server has attached pool
bugs.symptoms: The iRule 'forward' command does not result in connections being routed to the proper destination if the virtual server has an attached pool.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with: - Pool. - iRule that issues 'forward' commands.
bugs.impact: Connections are routed to pool member instead of destination determined by network routes.
bugs.workaround: Remove pool assigned to virtual server and select the pool using an iRule with a 'pool' command when 'forward' command is not issued.
bugs.fix: 'forward' command releases previously selected pool member to enabled connection to be routed based on packet destination, as expected.

bugs.title: Restarting TMM or failover offline causes causes bigd 'emerg logger' error message
bugs.symptoms: Stopping and starting the tmm causes bigd to restart with an 'emerg logger' error message. The restart is expected behavior, but the error-level message is not.
bugs.conditions: On active unit run one of the following commands: -- bigstart restart tmm. -- bigstart stop tmm;bigstart start tmm. -- bigstart stop tmm;bigstart start. -- tmsh run sys failover offline.
bugs.impact: bigd restarts and a message is logged to the console similar to the following: emerg logger: Re-starting bigd. Traffic monitoring ceases until TMM restart is complete. For the failover offline, impact is limited as unit is sent offline.

bugs.title: Rebooting active device before syncing a manual sync device group causes both devices to compile and deploy the blob
bugs.symptoms: On a standby in a manual sync device group with pccd in pending compile state, rebooting the active before syncing causes both devices to compile and deploy the blob
bugs.conditions: This only happen when 1. The BIG-IP configuration contains device groups that are configured to "manual sync". 2. Active device is not in "quiescent" state when it is rebooted.
bugs.impact: Some parts of the configuration that are not manually compiled into blob earlier are now compiled and enforced automatically. It is recommended that the user checks the current firewall configuration and make any adjustment if needed.

bugs.title: Fix a crash issue when querying SSP with multi-ip.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when querying SSP with multi-ip configured.
bugs.conditions: TMM crash when querying SSP with multi-ip configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fix TMM crash when querying SSP with multi-ip configured.

bugs.title: Add obfuscator tuning tools
bugs.symptoms: Difficult for F5 consultants to debug Websafe module.
bugs.conditions: When support for Websafe is requested by customers.
bugs.impact: Difficult for F5 consultants to debug Websafe module.
bugs.fix: Tools have been added to help consultants fine-tune the FPS obfuscator for better performance.

bugs.title: Executing tmsh clientssl-proxy cached-certs crashes tmm
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash while executing "tmsh clientssl-proxy cached-certs" command
bugs.conditions: ssl forward proxy virtual with a clientssl profile name longer than 32 characters which includes the partition name as well. (/Common/<profilename> -> has length more than 32 chars).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Keep the profile name lengths less than 32 chars, or do not run the command until fixed.
bugs.fix: The "tmsh clientssl-proxy cached-certs" command will now run successfully with profile name lengths longer than 32 characters.

bugs.title: iRule commands do not validate session scope
bugs.symptoms: Assume that a user establishes a session on one virtual server. If the user learns his session ID, he may attempt to reuse that session ID to gain access to resources guarded by a different virtual server. When this happens, the iRule access session commands like [ACCESS::session sid] and [ACCESS::session exists] do not validate the scope of the session. The iRules consider sessions from other virtual servers to be valid, which can cause unintended results and potentially lead to end-users gaining higher privileges than administrators intended.
bugs.conditions: There may be multiple access profiles assigned to multiple virtual servers, but the iRule session commands will treat all sessions the same.
bugs.impact: If the administrator is not careful with how the iRule session commands are used, it can result in a user bypassing the access policy and receiving higher privileges than the administrator intended.
bugs.workaround: Care must be used to ensure that iRules using the session commands do not result in unintended behavior. An iRule similar to one below can be used to restrict a session to the virtual server on which it was created: when ACCESS_ACL_ALLOWED { set sessionlistener [ACCESS::session data get "session.server.listener.name"] set virtualname [virtual name] if { [HTTP::cookie MRHSession] != "" } { if { not ($sessionlistener equals $virtualname) } { # enter whatever command you wish to use to prevent the connection reject } } }

bugs.title: Networks Access PAC file now can be located on SMB share
bugs.symptoms: Network Access web components or Edge Client fail to download PAC file if it is located on SMB share as file:////pac.file.hoster.local/config.pac.
bugs.conditions: Network Access with Client Proxy Settings Enabled, PAC file path is set to somewhere on SMB share.
bugs.impact: Impossible to configure Network Access with PAC file located on SMB share.
bugs.workaround: Put PAC file to HTTP server, configure Network Access accordingly.
bugs.fix: Now Network Access components can obtain PAC file from SMB share.

bugs.title: List of IPs in "tmsh show pem sessiondb subscriber-id " may be reversed.
bugs.symptoms: IPs show up in an order that is not expected.
bugs.conditions: Occurs always
bugs.impact: Nothing functional.
bugs.fix: Added code to display the IP addresses in the order they were added to the session.

bugs.title: DTLS renegotiation sequence number compatibility
bugs.symptoms: OpenSSL library was modified to keep it compatible with RFC 6347 complaint DTLS server renegotiation sequence number implementation.
bugs.conditions: The old OpenSSL library is not compatible with RFC6347, the new OpenSSL library is modified to be compatible with RFC6347. The current APM client is compatible with old OpenSSL library, not the new OpenSSL library.
bugs.impact: The current APM client is not compatible with new OpenSSL libary.
bugs.fix: The APM client is now compatible with both the old and new OpenSSL library.

bugs.title: Max TPS is always 0
bugs.symptoms: 'Max TPS and Throughput' in analytics profile should show the Max TPS metric in Statistics :: Analytics : HTTP : Transactions, View-by: Virtual Servers, Measurement: Max TPS. The value is always 0.
bugs.conditions: This occurs whenever you view the 'Max TPS and Throughput' value in the analytics profile.
bugs.impact: Max TPS reports 0 instead of the actual value.
bugs.fix: Max TPS now shows the real number

bugs.title: Requests for deflate encoding of gzip documents may crash TMM
bugs.symptoms: When searching for documents in the gzip cache, if a document has been cached with gzip encoding but a non-deflate compression method (i.e., CM != 0x08) and the client has requested deflate compression, TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: -- WAM/AAM enabled on VIP. -- HTTP compression enabled on VIP. -- Document served with gzip encoding and non-deflate compression. -- Document has entered the gzip cache. -- Client HTTP request specifies deflate encoding.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that only the deflate method is used in gzip-compressed documents that will be cached by WAM/AAM. With most web servers this is the default behavior and cannot be changed. Alternatively, remove the 'Accept-Encoding: deflate' header using an iRule so that no clients can request deflate encoding.
bugs.fix: Correctly handles requests for deflate compression of cached gzip documents with non-deflate compression methods.

bugs.title: Redirect loop when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled and deployment has multiple domains
bugs.symptoms: A redirect loop may happen for some users, when the Proactive Bot Defense feature is enabled, and the deployment consists of multiple domains.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense is enabled on a DOS profile that is assigned to a Virtual Server, and the deployment consists of multiple domains.
bugs.impact: Some users may occasionally be blocked from accessing certain URLs of a website due a redirect loop that could happen. In most cases, a page-refresh attempted by the user will load the page properly.
bugs.workaround: Applying the following iRule will workaround the problem: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::cookie exists "TSPD_101_R0"] } { if { [HTTP::cookie exists "TSPD_101"] } { HTTP::cookie remove "TSPD_101" } } }
bugs.fix: Occasional redirect loops caused by the Proactive Bot Defense mechanism no longer occur when multiple domains are deployed.

bugs.title: TMM could miss heart beats when opening IP Reputation database file resulting in SIGABRT by sod
bugs.symptoms: The IP Reputation database file is not loaded during initialization. It is loaded the first time it is needed. Sometimes the 'open' call on the database file and/or the subsequent 'mmap' call could take a very long time resulting in missed heartbeats from the tmm to sod.
bugs.conditions: Multiple open calls for IP Reputation database file.
bugs.impact: Results in sod sending SIGABRT to tmm.

bugs.title: FQDN ephemeral nodes not re-populated after deleted and re-created
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, ephemeral nodes that are force deleted may not repopulate as expected.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when there is a Sync group and multiple FQDNs resolve to the same IP address.
bugs.impact: Ephemeral nodes may not repopulate as expected.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: FQDN ephemeral nodes are now repopulated after force deletion.

bugs.title: Debug TMM Crashes During Initialization
bugs.symptoms: Debug version of TMM (tmm.debug) generates core file and fails to start up.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens when running debug version of TMM on a multi-blade chassis/vCMP.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Revert to use default version of TMM (tmm.default)
bugs.fix: Removed unnecessary debug assert statements from TMM.

bugs.title: tmsh load sys config merge file filename.scf base command does not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: The presence of base option indicates that only the base objects in the configuration should be considered for the save operation. The non-base objects in the configuration should be ignored. However, this is not true for the following command: tmsh load sys config merge file filename.scf base.
bugs.conditions: Running the command: tmsh load sys config merge file filename.scf base.
bugs.impact: This command ignores the base option. When specified with the merge option the base option is ignored. It merges the non-base configuration objects. It does not load only the base config objects as specified in the command.
bugs.fix: tmsh load sys config merge file filename.scf base command now loads only the base config objects as specified in the command.

bugs.title: Memory leak of inbound sockets in restjavad.
bugs.symptoms: restjavad might run out of memory due to inactive sockets piling up in memory. The symptom will be 'Out of memory' messages in the /var/logrestjavad.0.log and any new rest calls will fail. The URL that fails is random.
bugs.conditions: Occurs after a few hours of use.
bugs.impact: Memory leak of inbound sockets in restjavad. restjavad becomes inoperative.
bugs.workaround: Restart restjavad with the following command: bigstart restart restjavad. Note: You can run the command periodically from a cron script.
bugs.fix: Inbound sockets in restjavad no longer causes a memory leak.

bugs.title: Configurable behavior if PCRF returns unknown session ID in middle of session.
bugs.symptoms: If PEM sends CCR-U, and PCRF responds with CCA-U (PCRF lost session), PEM ignores the response and sends CCR-U.
bugs.conditions: PCRF lost session (reboot/failover) and responds to session update requests with unknown session ID.
bugs.impact: Session remains for a long period of time with PCRF not acknowledging.
bugs.workaround: To enable PCRF can get the context back, it is recommended that you delete the session on the PEM end (configurable), and also recreate the same session (configurable). When PCRF indicates that the session ID unknown, set the following Sys db variable to TRUE to have PEM delete the session: tmm.pem.diameter.application.trigger.delete.onPeer.failure. To have PEM recreate the session, set the following Sys db variable to TRUE: tmm.pem.session.ppe.recreate.afterPeerFailure.
bugs.fix: PCRF no longer returns unknown session ID in middle of session.

bugs.title: tmm memory leak with SSL forward proxy virtual server having CLIENTSSL_CLIENTHELLO with SNI lookup.
bugs.symptoms: tmm memory leak with SSL forward proxy virtual server having CLIENTSSL_CLIENTHELLO with SNI lookup.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server (vs1) configured with SSL forward proxy. - vs1 is attached to an iRule which has following events and actions: CLIENT_ACCEPTED does TCP::collect, CLIENT_DATA does TCP::release. CLIENTSSL_CLIENTHELLO does SNI lookup.
bugs.impact: Double SNI lookup happens instead of single lookup. tmm memory leak and eventual out-of-memory.
bugs.fix: SSL with forward proxy no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: SSL with forward proxy can leak memory
bugs.symptoms: Under some conditions, SSL with forward proxy might leak memory.
bugs.conditions: Forward proxy is enabled on a BIG-IP system that is running multiple TMM instances.
bugs.impact: Service degradation leading to an eventual reboot.
bugs.fix: SSL with forward proxy no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: AVR reports of last year are missing the last month data
bugs.symptoms: Reports are missing the latest data collected for them. Each report-type is missing a different portion of the data which is relative to the report-type. This issue becomes very noticeable when creating long-term reports. For example, a 'last-year' report might omit the last month data, 'last-month' report might omit the last week data, and so on.
bugs.conditions: Every report that is done on a long history time range.
bugs.impact: The presented data can be confusing and misleading.
bugs.fix: A new data aggregation mechanism was inserted, so that all reports include activity up to the last hour. There is an option to make it available even for the last 5 minutes, although that might lead to too much CPU and disk load every 5 minutes. There is also an option to turn off this new aggregation mechanism if you are not interested in accurate long-history reports, and the aggregation task that takes place once an hour is too heavy for this machine.

bugs.title: SNMP manager doesn't accept community name in double quotes in packet capture.
bugs.symptoms: When configuring SNMP trap via tmsh sys snmp v2-traps (trap2sink directive) or v1-traps (trapsink directive) commands, the community name contains double quotes in packet capture. This causes a problem as SNMP manager doesn't accept the trap because of the community mismatch. On the other hand, if traps are configured using tmsh sys snmp traps (trapsess directive), community name doesn't contain double quotes, which is an expected behavior.
bugs.conditions: Use tmsh sys snmp v2-traps or tmsh sys snmp v1-traps to configure SNMP traps.
bugs.impact: Community name contains double quotes in packet capture, which causes the SNMP manager to reject the trap because of the community mismatch.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh sys snmp traps.

bugs.title: PEM: Duplicate sessions formed with same IP
bugs.symptoms: For a single IP address we see 2 sessions in the system when we do pem_sessiondump --list.
bugs.conditions: Create a static subscriber configuration without the IP address and send radius start to create session with 2 IP address. Delete the master IP (first one) and send radius start with same IP.
bugs.impact: Duplicate sessions creates confusion as to which session is the active one used for an IP.
bugs.workaround: Make sure radius stop is received for both the IP addresses before sending a new one.
bugs.fix: Issues has been fixed now. No more duplicate sessions for the same IP address.

bugs.title: SSL client certificate verification during SSL handshake might leak a reference to the issuer certificate.
bugs.symptoms: SSL client certificate verification during SSL handshake might leak a reference to the issuer certificate causing TMM memory leakage over time.
bugs.conditions: clientssl in use with the client presenting a certificate for verification.
bugs.impact: TMM memory leak.
bugs.fix: Client certificate verification now releases all references and the memory leak no longer occurs.

bugs.title: VPE fails to display access policy
bugs.symptoms: VPE fails to display access policy Server request for 'vpeDialogue' is failed: Request status=500
bugs.conditions: Always for certain HF
bugs.impact: Error message is displayed and VPE does not work
bugs.workaround: No workaround, software upgrade needed
bugs.fix: Functionality restored

bugs.title: TMM may crash if loadbalancing to node's IP in iRule routed towards an unreachable nexthop.
bugs.symptoms: In a specific combination of events TMM may core.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - Load balancing a flow to an ip_tuple (e.g., the Tcl 'node' command). - That address is not directly connected. - The matched route is a gateway pool that contains a pool member that is not reachable.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure correct routing to all destinations with reachable next hops.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when load balancing to a node's IP address in iRule, routed towards an unreachable nexthop.

bugs.title: A disabled blade is spontaneously re-enabled
bugs.symptoms: If a secondary blade in a 'ready' state becomes primary and then quickly is disabled, it does not send a cluster packet for ten seconds. A new primary, therefore, is not elected for ten seconds (the heartbeat timeout), instead of the expected time (immediately). The other blades, including the new primary, never receive the message that the blade was set to disabled, so the blade is be re-enabled without the user requesting it.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only if the blade disable operations occur very shortly after the primary blade is moved.
bugs.impact: A blade that the user expects to be disabled is spuriously re-enabled. User interfaces to access configuration, such as tmsh and the GUI might hang for the ten-second interval. The system posts an error message similar to the following: load_config_files: '/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all base' - failed. -- Unexpected Error: Saving and loading configuration is only allowed on the primary slot.
bugs.workaround: Wait ten seconds after disabling a blade before disabling another blade.
bugs.fix: A previously disabled blade is no longer spuriously re-enabled if the primary blade is moved around quickly.

bugs.title: OSPFv3 may not completely recover from "clear ipv6 ospf process"
bugs.symptoms: Open Shortest Path First version 3(OSPFv3) Link link-state advertisements (LSAs) may not be re-originated from the BIG-IP system if a neighboring router sends the LSA back to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Blade failover occurs on a chassis, 'clear ipv6 ospf process' is run, or ospf6d crashes.
bugs.impact: Routes from Link LSAs generated by the BIG-IP may be missing in the OSPFv3 network.
bugs.workaround: Disable OSPFv3 on the BIG-IP system until the Link LSA has been purged from the network. To do so, remove OSPFv3 from the route domain for approximately 10 seconds and then add it back.
bugs.fix: Link LSAs are correctly re-originated by the BIG-IP system when the LSAs are sent to the BIG-IP by a neighbor router.

bugs.title: Windows 10 platform detection for BIG-IP EDGE Client
bugs.symptoms: The session.client.platform variable contains "Win8.1" for BIG-IP Edge Client on Windows 10.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP APM was enhanced to report session.client.platform session variable for BIG-IP Edge Client on Windows 10.

bugs.title: Parameter matching inconsistency
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes valid parameters from request are not matched to configured protected parameters. May work correctly in one browser while failing to work in another.
bugs.conditions: Request is bigger than one xfrag and parameter name is divided between two xfrags.
bugs.impact: Configured parameter won't be matched.
bugs.workaround: Remove unimportant cookies or add dummy cookies in order to shift parameter name inside the request. May resolve the issue. Differ between browsers.

bugs.title: TMM crashes with SIGABRT
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with SIGABRT (sod crashes the tmm). This error appears in the LTM logs: HA daemon_heartbeat tmm fails action is go offline down links and restart
bugs.conditions: IP reputation is turned on, and the IP reputation database is reloaded.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a rare scenario where TMM was halted when the IP reputation daemon was loading a new IP reputation database.

bugs.title: Renewing default.crt through openssl command shows previous expiry date while listing in TMUI
bugs.symptoms: TMUI 'System :: File management :: SSL Certificate List default certificate shows previous expiration date until MCP config is force loaded.
bugs.conditions: The default.crt is renewed using the command line (because there is no way to renew the default certificate is not using the GUI).
bugs.impact: GUI will still shows the old expiration date. This is a GUI SSL Certificate list page issue; the certificate details page shows the correct expiration date, and the device works as expected with the newly generated certificate.
bugs.workaround: To reflect the new certificate expiration date, have MCP force load config as described in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030).

bugs.title: VMware View RSA/RADIUS two factor authentication fails
bugs.symptoms: VMware View client fails to authenticate with APM configured for RSA/RADIUS two factor authentication.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for VMWare View proxy with RSA or RADIUS two factor authentication and VMware View client is used.
bugs.impact: User sees a confusing error message.
bugs.workaround: Click "OK" on an error message "The username or password is not correct. Please try again.". Enter valid AD credentials and login again.
bugs.fix: Now APM correctly handles VMware View RSA/RADIUS two factor authentication.

bugs.title: AFM attack may never end on AVR dos overview page in a chassis based BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: In a BIG-IP chassis, it is possible that the AFM "attack started" event and "attack stopped" event happen on two different slots of the chassis. In that case avrd is not able to detect and report "attack stopped" event and the user would continue to see "attack ongoing" in the DoS Overview Page.
bugs.conditions: This will only happen in a BIG-IP chassis based system with multiple slots, and if the AFM DoS "attack started" and "attack stopped" events are given to different slots.
bugs.impact: User will get confused when he see that the AFM DoS Overview Page still shows the attack as ongoing when it has actually stopped.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: With this change the bug has been fixed and now the AFM DoS Overview Page will always know when a attack has stopped.

bugs.title: BIG-IP crashes in debug mode when using PEM iRule to create session with calling-station-id and called-station-id

bugs.title: Monitor delete-and-create within a transaction fails
bugs.symptoms: A transaction fails when it attempts to delete a pool and associated monitor, and within that same transaction then attempts to create that same pool with a different monitor. The transaction fail message is: 'Monitor -old_monitor_name- is in use' This behavior is due to transaction validation, where a delete-and-create of the pool within that same transaction causes validation to fail (and the transaction to be aborted). The monitor cannot be deleted as long as the pool uses that monitor, and the pool will not be deleted at the conclusion of the transaction because later in the same transaction that same pool will be (re-)created.
bugs.conditions: -- A pool exists with an associated monitor. -- A transaction is attempted to delete that pool and monitor, and then recreate that pool with a different monitor.
bugs.impact: The transaction fails. The configuration is not changed, and the BIG-IP system continues to function as if the transaction had not been attempted.
bugs.workaround: Perform the desired steps outside a transaction to replace the monitor, and/or delete and recreate the pool.

bugs.title: Improvements to the Single DH use option in SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: "Single DH use" option in Client SSL or Server SSL profile was ignored in some cases.
bugs.conditions: "Single DH use" is set in Client SSL or Server SSL profile.
bugs.impact: "Single DH use" was always effectively "on" for DHE-based ciphersuites in any Server SSL profile. Single DH use had no effect for ECDHE ciphersuites in any SSL profile or DHE ciphersuites in any ClientSSL profile. The main benefit of the Single DH use is to provide true/ultimate perfect forward secrecy. The aim of such high security posture is to be able to claim that no encryption key resides in memory on BIG-IP beyond a single TLS session. This security posture requires disabling of TLS session reuse, TLS session ticket, and the matching behaviour of any TLS client. The benefit of this fix is to primarily address these high security needs. DHE ciphersuites on BIG-IP use periodically re-generated custom DHE groups in any SSL profile. The use of custom DHE groups implies that the massive pre-computation needed to efficiently solve DH discrete logarithm problem (DH DLP) is only helpful for the lifetime of a given DHE group. Provided that the DH DLP is easy, "Single DH use" doesn't materially slow down the DLP attacks. ECDHE groups provide sufficient security today making ECDHE DLP infeasible. Please refer to 2015 LogJam attack for the background.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: Slot 2 is inactive after reboot
