bugs.title: Support Third-party OTP providers and APM Native OTP authentication for Citrix Receiver clients
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receiver clients could not be authenticated using Third-party OTP providers or APM Native OTP.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured as Citrix Integration or Replacement mode and uses OTP based authentication.
bugs.impact: OTP based second factor authentication could not be used.
bugs.fix: Support Third-party OTP providers and APM Native OTP authentication for Citrix Receiver clients

bugs.title: Upgrade sets client/server SSL profiles Ciphers field to DEFAULT if upgraded cipherstring effectively contains no ciphersuites.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade sets client/server SSL profiles Ciphers field to DEFAULT if the upgraded cipherstring would effectively contain no ciphersuites.
bugs.conditions: This is relevant when the following conditions are met: * Upgrading to version 12.0.0. * Client/server SSL profile is configured with the COMPAT keyword.
bugs.impact: The system changes 'COMPAT' to 'DEFAULT'. Upgrade posts a warning similar to the following: WARNING: ciphers in clientssl profile TheProfile has been reset to DEFAULT from MD5. This occurs because the BIG-IP software version 12.0.0 COMPAT set is empty by default. To prevent security issues and upgrade failures due to an empty ciphersuite, the upgrade operation replaces 'COMPAT' with 'DEFAULT'. This is not considered a software defect, but instead assists users with maintenance of ciphersuites. It is expected that some legacy ciphersuites will be removed from default sets in major releases of BIG-IP system software, which might require user action to account for this change.
bugs.workaround: Because the upgrade script replaces the configured cipherstring, you should determine whether 'DEFAULT' is a suitable set of ciphersuites, and make necessary adjustments. For more information, see SOL13156: SSL ciphers used in the default SSL profiles (11.x - 12.x), available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/100/sol13156.html. Best practice recommends periodic review of the enabled cipherstrings that are considered secure, since these change over time. Such a review should prevent future occurrence of the condition.

bugs.title: "Minimize to tray" option doesn't work in IE with latest updates if APM is not in Trusted Sites list
bugs.symptoms: KB3058515 introduces new security changes in Internet Explorer versions 9, 10, and 11. As a result, it is unable to create a tray icon from a plug-in that running on site that is not in the Trusted Sites list.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: 1. KB3058515 is installed. 2. Client machine has Internet Explorer version 9, 10 or 11. 3. APM virtual server is not in Trusted Sites list.
bugs.impact: Minimize to tray option does not work.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, uninstall KB3058515 or add APM to the Trusted Sites list.

bugs.title: Rare 'No LopCmd reply match found' error in getLopReg
bugs.symptoms: An error message similar to the following might be logged at rare intervals while the BIG-IP system is operating normally: warning chmand[7018]: 012a0004:4: getLopReg exception: No LopCmd reply match found for action=0x1 obj_id=0x67 subobj=0x0 slot=0xff. This message might be followed by a log message similar to one of the following: err chmand[7018]: 012a0003:3: GET_MEDIA failure (status=0xffffffff) page=0x%1 reg=0x0. err chmand[32142]: 012a0003:3: GET_STAT failure (status=0xffffffff) page=0x%20 reg=0x50. This message might be followed by a log message similar to the following: warning chmand[5847]: 012a0004:4: getLopReg: lop data size does not match, u16DataLen=0x5 expected=0x7.
bugs.conditions: This problem might occur rarely on the BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series, 5000-/7000-series, and 10000-/12000-series appliances, and on VIPRION 2100, 2150, and 2250 blades.
bugs.impact: This problem might occur if the response to a request to read the status of the hardware registers for the management interface is delayed beyond the normally-expected timeout value. When this problem occurs, status of the management interface might be reported incorrectly, which might cause the management interface to flap momentarily. In this scenario, subsequent requests typically complete successfully, at which point status of the management interface is again reported normally, and expected functionality restored.

bugs.title: BIG-IP crash caused by PSC::ip_address iRule is fixed
bugs.symptoms: When using PSC::ip_address iRule to get the ip list for DHCP-based subscriber discovery and RADIUS Authentication message, BIG-IP crashed and restarted.
bugs.conditions: Using PSC::ip_address iRule to get ip address list in DHCP-based subscriber discovery and RADIUS Authentication messages
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: The inherit-certkeychain field of a clientSSL profile is not synchronized correctly on a standby BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: When creating a clientSSL profile at the active BIG-IP system, its inherit-certkeychain field is true by default, however, it appears to be false on the standby BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP systems are deployed as high-availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.impact: All units in an HA configuration should have the same configuration and the same behavior. Mismatching units in the HA configuration might lead to unexpected mismatching behavior.
bugs.fix: With the fix, the inherit-certkeychain field of a newly created client SSL profile is set correctly on a standby BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: IP Intelligence update failed: Missing SSL certificate
bugs.symptoms: IP Intelligence is failing the update due to missing certificate. You will see these errors in /var/log/ltm: err iprepd[5600]: 015c0004:3: Certificate verification error: 20 err iprepd[5600]: 015c0004:3: nSendReceiveSsl failed SSL handshake The certificate of vector.brightcloud.com was changed recently.
bugs.conditions: This is seen when attempting to update the IP Intelligence database.
bugs.impact: IP Intelligence database will not update.
bugs.workaround: Add the new brightcloud certificate to the end of the chain.
bugs.fix: This release contains an updated certificate chain.

bugs.title: When Many entities are displayed on the "Illegal Meta Character in Value" manual traffic learning screen, the Configuration utility becomes unresponsive.
bugs.symptoms: When around 500 entities are displayed on the "Illegal Meta Character in Value" manual traffic learning screen, the Configuration utility becomes unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: When around 500 entities are displayed on the "Illegal Meta Character in Value" manual traffic learning screen.
bugs.impact: The Configuration utility becomes unresponsive.
bugs.fix: We limited the number of entities displayed on the "Illegal Meta Character in Value" manual traffic learning screen to a realistic limit in order to prevent the Configuration utility from becoming unresponsive.

bugs.title: DOSL7::enable with profile requires full path but is not validated
bugs.symptoms: When using an iRule with the DOSL7::enable command and supplying a DoS profile as argument, the full path must be used. However, there is no configuration validation to support the requirement. This causes the following log message to appear repeatedly in /var/log/tmm*: notice CONF|NTCE|dosl7_update_application_conf_external:0769|could not find conf for profile crc 2884018011, name dos_profile The log message appears for every relevant request, so depending on the iRule, it might fill the log.
bugs.conditions: -- Use the DOSL7::enable iRule command. -- Supply a DoS profile without the profile's full path.
bugs.impact: -- Traffic does not go through the profile specified in the iRule. -- Flooding of log messages in /var/log/tmm*. -- There is no validation to prevent the incorrect syntax.
bugs.workaround: Supply the profile name with its full path when using the DOSL7::enable iRule command, for example: Use this syntax: -- DOSL7::enable /Common/dos_profile Not this syntax: -- DOSL7::enable dos_profile The syntax that you use to write iRules is based on the Tool Command Language (Tcl) programming standard. Thus, you can use many of the standard Tcl commands, plus a robust set of extensions that Local Traffic Manager provides to help you further increase load balancing efficiency. Important: When referencing an object within an iRule, you must include the full path name of the object. Examples are: HTTP::class select /Common/$asm_class and set file [ ifile get "/Common/ifileURL" ]. For example: 'DOSL7::enable /Common/dos_profile' is valid, while 'DOSL7::enable dos_profile' is invalid.

bugs.title: TCP reject Virtual Servers may not respond with TCP reset
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, reject Virtual servers configured with IP protocol TCP may not respond to TCP SYN packets with a TCP RST; silently dropping them. All-protocols and UDP reject virtual servers are unaffected.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual Server, type Reject - Virtual server ip-protocol only TCP.
bugs.impact: TCP SYN packets are silently dropped.
bugs.workaround: Use all-protocols or use a standard VIP and reject via iRule.

bugs.title: pagemem tmctl table changed to page_stats
bugs.symptoms: TMM has a tmctl statistic table called pagemem which shows two elements: available pages and used pages. These provide the totals across all TMM threads, and while accurate, they do not show fragmentation.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at the pagemen statistics.
bugs.impact: This can lead to situations where TMM might try and allocate a large number of contiguous pages, which will fail, even though the pagemem avail stat shows the total pages being available.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.fix: The pagemem tmctl table has been replaced with a new table called page_stats which provides much more detailed information about physical page clustering. The original 'avail' and 'used' statistics are still there, although they are reported on a per-thread basis. Additional statistic buckets for page diagnostics are introduced.

bugs.title: tmm might crash with 'DHCP:dhcp_server_flow_connect' error when the server flow is already connected to a different client.
bugs.symptoms: When the DHCP server flow is trying to connect to the same client flow that is already connected and not released, there might be a tmm crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using the dhcpv6 profile.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes with 'DHCP:dhcp_server_flow_connect' error when the server flow is already connected to a different client.

bugs.title: Memory leak in ssl
bugs.symptoms: An intermittent memory leak was encountered in SSL
bugs.conditions: This can occur under certain conditions when using Client SSL profiles
bugs.impact: The amount of memory leaked is quite small, but over time enough memory would leak that TMM would have to reboot.
bugs.fix: An intermittent memory leak in SSL was fixed

bugs.title: AVR not reporting the activity of standby systems.
bugs.symptoms: When working in Active/Standby configurations, the standby system is completely ignored when generating an AVR report. The standby system might have been an active system in the past, so its statistics should also be counted.
bugs.conditions: Configuration with Active and Standby systems.
bugs.impact: Some historical activity might not be reported by AVR.
bugs.fix: We added device group support, and the user can now choose the device group to query from.

bugs.title: System remains OFFLINE after running tmsh run cm config-sync recover-sync
bugs.symptoms: When ASM is provisioned, running the command "tmsh run cm config-sync recover-sync" causes the device to remain offline. This command should reset all of the local device configuration, but the device should come back online after several minutes.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned and FPS is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: System remains OFFLINE and not handling incoming traffic.
bugs.workaround: Two workaround options: 1. Re-provision ASM: tmsh modify sys provision level nominal 2. Reboot the device

bugs.title: VCMP: Large vdisk was unable to migrate in 15 minute timeout
bugs.symptoms: A 25G+ vdisk did not complete migration from one blade to another within the timeout and was stopped.
bugs.conditions: When an existing single slot guest is allocated to a different slot the VCMP host moves the vdisk to the new slot. This process is referred to as vdisk migration.
bugs.impact: The vdisk was not moved and results in the following message to /var/log/ltm: <date> <slot>/ltm err vcmpd[13859]: 01510004:3: Guest (<name>): Failure - VDisk migration process from slot [N] failed. Timed out after 900 seconds.
bugs.workaround: Increase the migrating timeout db var: sys db vcmp.timeout.migrating { value "2700" }

bugs.title: GUI does not retain reflect connection type of "No Server" for AAA CRLDP server
bugs.symptoms: When you set a new or existing AAA CRLDP to have a "Server Connection" to "No Server" and save it from GUI, subsequent visits to the CRLDP properties page would show Server Connection being set to Direct.
bugs.conditions: This happened under all conditions from GUI.
bugs.impact: The GUI presents the incorrect state. It is confusing to administrator.
bugs.workaround: TMSH can be used to set the "Server Connection" back to "No Server" by setting the address to be "::" and saving.

bugs.title: ASM periodic updates (cron) write errors to log
bugs.symptoms: ASM periodic updates (run via cron) write errors to log when ASM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: ASM is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: Errors appears in ASM logs.
bugs.fix: Errors no longer appear in ASM logs when ASM is not provisioned.

bugs.title: On shutdown, SOD very infrequently cores due to an internal processing error during the shutdown.
bugs.symptoms: On shutdown, SOD very infrequently cores due to an internal processing error during the shutdown.
bugs.conditions: System shutdown. Unable to reproduce the issue reliably, so conditions for the crash are unknown
bugs.impact: Since the core happens on shutdown, operation on the device is not affected, but a core file may be generated.

bugs.title: Windows 8 client may not be able to renew DHCP lease

bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Edge Client is running on Windows 8. "Allow access to local DHCP servers" is checked in Network Access settings.

bugs.title: Packet filters are by-passed for some fragmented ICMP echo requests to a virtual address
bugs.symptoms: A packet filter is in place to block ICMP traffic to a virtual address, but the virtual address responds to ICMP echo requests.
bugs.conditions: A packet filter is in place to block ICMP echo request traffic to a virtual address, and a fragmented ICMP echo request is received by the BIG-IP system. If the ICMP echo request needs to be forwarded to another tmm, the packet-filter is not honored.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not blocked despite the existence of a packet-filter rule.
bugs.workaround: Use AFM rather than packet-filter. Note: This may require additional licensing.
bugs.fix: When a packet filter is in place to block ICMP echo request traffic to a virtual address, and a fragmented ICMP echo request is received by the BIG-IP system, the packet filter is now honored.

bugs.title: reject in iRule event FLOW_INIT may not respond with a RST

bugs.conditions: iRule on a tcp virtual IP which has reject in FLOW_INIT event.
bugs.impact: RST is not sent

bugs.title: Quota Policy Added multiple times will lead to reset of Subscriber flows

bugs.conditions: If a same policy with quota management action is added multiple times to the session through RAR (or CCA-u) then after 32 installs, any flow for the session is reset.
bugs.impact: Flows getting reset means subscribers having issue with using service.
bugs.workaround: PCRF should make sure that for the session same policy is not being added to multiple times.

bugs.title: PEM: New Requested units empty for when used units matches granted service units
bugs.symptoms: Requested Service Units field in CCR-U message in Gy will be empty for certain rating group requests in MSCC AVP
bugs.conditions: If used Service units matches exactly with granted service units. (Extremely rare)
bugs.impact: RSU being empty might trigger OCS allocating incorrect granted service unit for the rating group
bugs.workaround: Work around is to ignore Requested service Unit AVP if zero by the OCS or just use used service units AVP since RSU is empty.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed now. RSU will be not be empty even if used service units matches Granted service units AVP.

bugs.title: The device management daemon can crash with a malloc error
bugs.symptoms: The device management daemon can core if a timeout condition occurs during an iControl query. The daemon recovers and proceeds with the operation.
bugs.conditions: A timeout can occur during an iControl query and in some instances this can cause a core.
bugs.impact: The daemon crashes and recovers.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The device management daemon no longer causes a crash when a timeout condition occurs during an iControl query.

bugs.title: Virtual ARP ICMP echo settings are flipped on reloading a 10.x configuration on 11.4.x or later.
bugs.symptoms: A 10.x UCS containing LTM virtual servers with ARP set to disable. Loading the 10.x UCS on 11.4.x or later system leads to the ARP and ICMP echo setting value being flipped each time the load occurs.
bugs.conditions: Reloading a 10.x UCS containing virtual servers on 11.4.x or later system.
bugs.impact: ARP and ICMP echo setting value being flipped each time the load occurs. Note that the ICMP echo virtual field will be flipped even if ARP is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Delete the LTM virtual servers on the 11.x/12.x version system prior to re-loading the 10.x UCS.

bugs.title: Upgrade failure when CertKeyChain exists in non-Common partition
bugs.symptoms: Pre-11.6.0 configuration may fail to load on a BIG-IP system running version 11.6.0 (or greater).
bugs.conditions: Configuration contains a SSL profile with an explicit Certificate Key Chain in a non-Common partition.
bugs.impact: This issue leads to a configuration load failure.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Certificate Key Chain will inherit its partition from the parent SSL profile on creation.

bugs.title: Generating new default certificate and key pairs for BIG-IP ssl profiles via CLI will not be reflected in GUI or in tmsh
bugs.symptoms: Using the CLI to generate new default certificate and key pairs for BIG-IP ssl profiles are not reflected in the GUI or tmsh.
bugs.conditions: Using OpenSSL commands to generate a new default certificate and key pair, as described in SOL13579: Generating new default certificate and key pairs for BIG-IP ssl profiles, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/500/sol13579.html.
bugs.impact: After the renewal, tmsh list sys file ssl-cert default.crt command or the general properties in the GUI SSL Cert List shows the old one. This is a cosmetic issue only. The system uses the new default.
bugs.workaround: Perform a force reload of mcpd by running the following commands: -- touch /service/mcpd/forceload. -- tmsh restart sys service mcpd.
bugs.fix: After renewing certificates with OpenSSL, you can now use the simpler command "tmsh install sys crypto cert default.crt from-local-file /config/ssl/ssl.crt/default.crt" and the new certificate is immediately reflected in tmsh list and the GUI. Alternatively, "tmsh load sys config" also now properly recognizes the renewed certificate. No manual mcpd restart is required with either method.

bugs.title: Loading cli preference that does not contain the user attribute will fail
bugs.symptoms: The cli preference config objects under certain circumstances can be saved without a user attribute. The loading of such a cli preference will result in error "Loading a preference requires user name specified".
bugs.impact: Loading scf, ucs configuration will fail
bugs.workaround: Remove the cli preference that does contains the user from the configuration (/config/bigip_user.conf or SCF) and reload.
bugs.fix: tmsh ignores the cli preference that does not contain the user attribute. The loading of configuration containing prior mentioned objects succeeds.

bugs.title: Using an iRule to enable/disable a profile does not enable/disable the profile
bugs.symptoms: When using an iRule to enable/disable a profile, the profile is being enabled/disabled on every other iRule invocation.
bugs.conditions: Reusing a connection between requests and using an iRule to enable/disable a profile.
bugs.impact: The profile will not be enabled/disabled.

bugs.title: Errors in monpd log after upgrade from version 11.5.x regarding deprecated widgets
bugs.symptoms: Errors appear in monpd log after upgrading from version 11.5.x regarding deprecated widgets. For example, "Failed on primary blade: Undefined entity dosl7_ip was used".
bugs.conditions: Defining widgets in 11.5.x with entities that are no longer in use in later versions and upgrading to 11.6.x or 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: Errors in monpd log (no other "serious" impact).
bugs.workaround: After upgrading to new version remove all widgets from the Analytics :: HTTP : Overview page and the Security :: Overview : Summary page and create new ones.

bugs.title: TMM may core with invalid lasthop pool configuration
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances, TMM may core if the unit is configured with an invalid, non-local lasthop pool
bugs.conditions: 1) BIG-IP system with VIP and lasthop pool with non-local pool member. 2) Sys db tm.lhpnomemberaction set to 2.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure lasthop pool to use local members/addresses.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores with an invalid lasthop pool configuration.

bugs.title: IE11 on Windows 10 doesn't show tooltips/toast notifications when Network Access changes state
bugs.symptoms: Tooltips/Toast notification are not displayed when Network Access changes state (Connect, Disconnect, Reconnect, etc). Beginning with Microsoft Windows 8, tooltips are replaced by Toast Notifications; Windows does not convert tooltips to toast notification for F5 WebComponent in Windows 10.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: Internet Explorer 11. Windows 10. Networks Access changes state.
bugs.impact: User is not notified about state change.
bugs.workaround: To enable tooltips, in Group Policy change this setting: "User Configuration \ Administrative Templates \ Start Menu and Taskbar \ Disable showing balloon notifications as toasts" to Enable.

bugs.title: Control plane CPU usage reported too high
bugs.symptoms: The system CPU usage is reported as the higher of the data plane averaqe and the control plane average. In certain cases, the control plane average was being calculated at about double.
bugs.conditions: When the data plane CPU usage was lower than the control plane CPU usage. This can occur when there is little client traffic flowing through the BIG-IP but the control plane is busy, say installing software.
bugs.impact: Typically, since client traffic drives data plane CPU usage, control plane CPU usage is less than data plane CPU usage at normal client loads.
bugs.workaround: This can safely be ignored at low data plane usage and will not be evident when data plane usage increases.
bugs.fix: The calculation of the control plane CPU usage no longer includes other CPUs.

bugs.title: Recently-manufactured hardware may not be identified with the correct model name and SNMP OID
bugs.symptoms: The model names and corresponding SNMP OIDs of BIG-IP and VIPRION hardware may not be identified correctly. 1. Under the 'tmsh show sys hardware' command, the 'Type' field under 'System Information' may show the alphanumeric Platform Identifier (e.g., C113) instead of the BIG-IP/VIPRION model name (e.g., 4200v). 2. The SNMP sysObjectID OID (1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0) may show a value of 'F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB::unknown' instead of the model-specific identifier.
bugs.conditions: This problem may occur when running older BIG-IP software releases on BIG-IP or VIPRION hardware platforms that were manufactured after the BIG-IP software release. Each BIG-IP software release contains a database used to map platform hardware part numbers to BIG-IP or VIPRION model names. If a BIG-IP or VIPRION hardware platform is manufactured after this BIG-IP software release, this new hardware may contain updates that result in a minor revision to its platform hardware part number. If this revised platform hardware part number is not found in the database included in the BIG-IP software release, its corresponding model name cannot be determined. The SNMP sysObjectID OID value is based on the resolved model name. If the model name cannot be determined, the SNMP sysObjectID OID returns 'F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB::unknown'.
bugs.impact: Unable to identify recently-manufactured BIG-IP or VIPRION hardware platforms.
bugs.workaround: 1. Identify the hardware platform by its Platform ID, and correlate this to the Platform Name using SOL9476: The F5 hardware/software compatibility matrix at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/9000/400/sol9476.html. 2. Query the SNMP F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysPlatformInfoName.0 object to obtain the hardware identifier, and correlate this to the Platform Name (e.g., from the 'Platform support' in the appropriate BIG-IP software Release Notes).
bugs.fix: BIG-IP software correctly identifies recently-manufactured BIG-IP or VIPRION hardware platforms with the correct model name and SNMP sysObjectID OID.

bugs.title: AFM address lists are not sorted while trying to create a new rule.
bugs.symptoms: AFM address lists are not sorted while trying to create a new rule.
bugs.conditions: Seen only in the rule creation page.
bugs.impact: AFM address lists are not sorted in the rule creation page.
bugs.fix: AFM address lists are now sorted in the rule creation page.

bugs.title: @import "url" is not recognized by client-side CSS patcher
bugs.symptoms: Not rewriten links from CSS.
bugs.conditions: CSS which contains: @import "url" or @import 'url'
bugs.impact: Unmangled requests resulting in error and customer confusion. Wrong rendering of pages.
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used. No general workaround exists.
bugs.fix: Fixed CSS rewriting for: @import "URL" and @import 'URL'

bugs.title: SharePoint ActiveX wrappers should check object type before rewriting URL
bugs.symptoms: Some our Invoke wrappers don't check if they are called against correct object and function. This may lead to a double rewriting of URLs, or to a corrupted URLs (like in the case of Sharepoint wrappers).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using rewrite with SharePoint applications.
bugs.impact: The rewritten URL will be malformed, and end users may be unable to view certain document types.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround for ID528598: -------- when HTTP_REQUEST { # ID528598: Sharepoint ActiveX wrappers should check object type before rewriting URL # Rename ViewDocument to openDocument in order to avoid special rewriting. if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "/EmployeeFormsAndVideos" } { set bug528598 1 # log local0. "ID528598: modifying page at [HTTP::uri]" if { [HTTP::version] eq "1.1" } { if { [HTTP::header is_keepalive] } { HTTP::header replace "Connection" "Keep-Alive" } HTTP::version "1.0" } } elseif { [info exists bug528598] } { unset bug528598 } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { [info exists bug528598] } { if { [HTTP::header exists "Content-Length"] and \ [HTTP::header "Content-Length"] > 0 and \ [HTTP::header "Content-Length"] <= 1048576 } { HTTP::collect [HTTP::header Content-Length] } else { HTTP::collect 1048576 } } } when HTTP_RESPONSE_DATA { if { [info exists bug528598] } { unset bug528598 set location [string last {.ViewDocument} \ [HTTP::payload]] while { $location > 0 && \ $location < [expr {[HTTP::payload length] - 13}] } { HTTP::payload replace $location 5 {.open} set location [string last {.ViewDocument} \ [HTTP::payload]] } unset location } }
bugs.fix: A check is now performed to ensure the underlying object is really an ActiveX object before rewriting the object.

bugs.title: BIG-IP EDGE Client can indefinitely stay "disconnecting..." state when captive portal session expired
bugs.symptoms: Edge Client can stuck in "disconnecting..." state if connected through with captive portal session and captive portal session expired. This happens when BIG-IP EDGE client keep HTTP connection to captive portal probe URL alive.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP EDGE Client for Windows connecting to BIG-IP APM on network with active captive portal. Captive portal session expired before user terminate active Network Access connection.
bugs.impact: When user run into this condition BIG-IP EDGE client for Windows cannot connect to BIG-IP APM server without restart.
bugs.workaround: User can exit and restart BIG-IP EDGE client.
bugs.fix: Captive portal detection request modified to properly close HTTP connection.

bugs.title: Guest cannot ping any management IP on the local host system when guest-to-host communication is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When guest-to-host communication is enabled by setting the "vcmp.mgmt.allow_host_guest_communication" to "true", a guest VM is unable to ping any management IP residing on the local host BIG-IP system. Note that SSH to such an IP works. On clustered systems, a guest VM is unable to ping the cluster floating management IP of the local host cluster, if the local host blade is the primary blade of the host cluster. However, the guest VM is able to ping the cluster member management IP of non-local host blades and the cluster floating management IP, if a non-local host blade is the primary blade of the host cluster.
bugs.conditions: A guest VM attempts to ping a management IP that resides on the local host BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The user may mistakenly believe that, since they are unable to ping a management IP residing on the local host BIG-IP system, that they are also unable to SSH to that IP.
bugs.workaround: Note that a guest VM is still able to SSH to a management IP residing on the local host BIG-IP system, even if pinging that IP does not work. If pinging of such an IP is desirable from a guest VM whose host BIG-IP system does not include the fix for this issue, then the following commands can be run on the host BIG-IP system as the 'root' user to make pinging the IP work: # iptables -I vcmp_mgmt 2 -p icmp -j ACCEPT # iptables-save > /etc/sysconfig/iptables Note: On clustered host BIG-IP systems, these commands should be run on every blade. Note: These commands will result in pings working across reboots, but an upgrade will reset the saved iptables rules and thus result in pings not working once more, unless the host BIG-IP system is being upgraded to a version that includes the fix for this issue.
bugs.fix: Guest VMs are now able to ping any management IP residing on the local host BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Sessiondump does not accept single dash options
bugs.symptoms: sessiondump switched to double dash options like `sessiondump --list` and was no longer backward compatible with single dash options like `sessiondump -list`
bugs.conditions: This bug is only applicable if BZ 511900 is being integrated to an engineering hotfix for an 11.x version. BZ 511900 was included in 12.0 and improved sessiondump performance but broke backward compatibility. However, the regression was identified during the 12.0 development, and was fixed before 12.0 released.
bugs.impact: Minimal impact. Only applies to customers that request and receive an engineering hotfix that includes BZ 511900 to get a faster sessiondump. Functionality is the same, but utility scripts that were using the old commands will need to be updated to the new ones
bugs.workaround: Use the double dash option. The option names have not changed, and the functionality of sessiondump has not changed.
bugs.fix: It now accepts both double and single dash options.

bugs.title: rare tmm crash when ipother irule parks
bugs.symptoms: TMM System may crash under rare condition for traffic that goes through IPOther virtual with an iRule script that parks the data flow. This occurs rarely, and it will only happen if a data flow that goes through IPOther VIP is aborted when an iRule is parked on the same flow. When the iRUle resumes, the IPOther VIP forward the original packet and tmm may crash when PEM uses the freed data of the flow that is already freed.
bugs.conditions: With PEM licensed/enalbed, associate an iRule script with iRule command that will park (e.g., the table command) against the IPOther virtual. At last, the data traffic that goes through PEM IPOther virtual get aborted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: A possible workaround is not to use iRule command that will park in the iRule script that is attached to IPOther virtual. For example, there are information that could be retrieved by PEM::session command instead of using table command. If iRule command that will cause parking must be used, then this fix along with the fix of bug 484278.
bugs.fix: The crash has been fixed and the should no longer be observed.

bugs.title: AD/LDAP cache size reduced
bugs.symptoms: When AD or LDAP Query module built a group cache, that cache contained an unnecessary attribute that was never used.
bugs.conditions: AD/LDAP Query module is configured with option that requires building of a local group cache.
bugs.impact: apd process size grows significantly after group cache is built. If several different caches are maintained at the same time, the process size can hit the 4 GB limit.
bugs.fix: Removed an unnecessary attribute from cache. As a result, the group cache size and APD process size have been reduced.

bugs.title: In some cases HTML body.onload event handler is not executed via portal access.
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer 7 (and any newer version in compatibility mode) ignores inline body.onload event handler if it is already assigned in previously executed script. This may prevent execution of user-defined body.onload event handler in some cases if the page is accessed using Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs under these conditions: Internet Explorer version 7 or newer in compatibility mode, and HTML page with inline body.onload event handler _and_ <script> or <meta> tags before <body> tag.
bugs.impact: Web application may work incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to change the HTML page in an iRule converting inline body.onload event handler into an explicit JavaScript function assigned to the body.onload event using the attachEvent() call.
bugs.fix: Now HTML inline body.onload event handler is executed correctly in all cases if the page is accessed through Portal Access.

bugs.title: TCP keeps retransmitting when ICMP Destination Unreachable-Fragmentation Required messages are received.
bugs.symptoms: In a Standard virtual server, a data segment will be retransmitted when an ICMP Type 3, Code 4, message with an MTU (greater than or equal to 0) is received. The retransmission occurs until there are no ICMP Type 3, Code 4 messages, a connection times out, or an ACK is received.
bugs.conditions: Router or client sends ICMP frag messages with random MTU values. It can be increasing, decreasing, same, or 0 MTU.
bugs.impact: Packets might fill up the pipe and cause a minor outage.
bugs.fix: TCP drops the second or later ICMP Type 3, Code 4 message. If the second packet is a valid ICMP packet, the downstream router will send another ICMP Type 3, Code 4 message.

bugs.title: When tcp connection is aborting tmm can crash with "hud_oob consumed" message
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with "hud_oob consumed" message in the log.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely occurring edge case. It can be seen when tcp has been aborted and messages exist in an internal queue.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tcp aborts correctly when there are messages in an internal queue.

bugs.title: DNS Cache might use cached data from ADDITIONAL sections in ANSWER responses.
bugs.symptoms: DNS Caching might use cached data from ADDITIONAL sections of previous lookups in the ANSWER section of responses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using DNS Caching.
bugs.impact: The data from the ADDITIONAL section might be used in the ANSWER section of DNS responses. The data might be stale or incorrect.
bugs.fix: The DNS Cache now correctly ignores data from the ADDITIONAL section when constructing the ANSWER section.

bugs.title: Relaxing validation against "_" character for ActiveDirectory server FQDN for NTLM authentication
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system applies standard fully qualified domain name (FQDN) validation for Active Directory server FQDN. Unfortunately, Microsoft allows non-standard FQDN as well. (https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/library/cc959336.aspx) At Non RFC strictness level, Active Directory allows additional "_" characters to be used everywhere in the DNS name. AD server that has "_" in its DNS name cannot be used for domain join operation for creating machine account or for authentication AD server for NTLM authentication. Both Multibyte and Any Character strictness level predictably can cause problem to our internal code; we do not support them.
bugs.conditions: AD server DNS name contains "_".
bugs.impact: Cannot be used for domain join for machine account creation or for target authentication server for NTLM authentication.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, you can rename the Active Directory server.
bugs.fix: Now an Active Directory server DNS name that contains an underscore (_) can be used for a machine account and NTLM authentication.

bugs.title: PEM: RAR after session being deleted from Radius/TMSH when connection down will return RAA with success code.
bugs.symptoms: PEM responds with RAA with DIAMETER_SUCCESS code even though session has been deleted.
bugs.conditions: Diameter virtual is down, then RADIUS sessions are deleted via tmsh, then the Diameter virtual is brought back up
bugs.impact: PCRF might be misled as it thinks session exists.
bugs.workaround: Make sure PCRF sends RAR with at least 1 policy and the PEM will responds with RAA with unable to comply
bugs.fix: PEM will send RAA with UNABLE_TO_COMPLY code if session is marked for deleted.

bugs.title: Source NAT translation doesn't work when APM is disabled using iRule
bugs.symptoms: Source NAT translation does not happen and server-side connection fails.
bugs.conditions: ACCESS::disable iRule is added to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Proxy's server-side connection fails.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the ACCESS::disable iRule command.
bugs.fix: Restore the source address translation correctly even if an iRule has disabled APM.

bugs.title: NAT names with spaces in them do not upgrade properly
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading to an affected version, if a NAT has a name with spaces in it, the upgraded configuration does not load.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system must be configured with NATs that have spaces in their names. When an upgrade is performed to 11.5.0 through 11.5.3 or to 11.6.0 this can be triggered.
bugs.impact: The configuration does not load on the upgraded system.
bugs.workaround: Remove spaces in NAT names before upgrading. Specifically: the initial letter must be a letter, underscore ( _ ), or forward slash ( / ), and subsequent characters may be letters, numbers, periods ( . ), hyphens ( - ), underscores ( _ ), or forward slashes ( / ).
bugs.fix: NAT names with spaces in them now upgrade properly.

bugs.title: Config-Sync after non-Common partition config changes results in extraneous config stanzas in the config files of the non-Common partition
bugs.symptoms: Configuration stanzas that do not belong in the files of a non-Common partition appear there. These stanzas could include, for example, 'net trunk' or 'sys ha-group' objects.
bugs.conditions: -- The system includes partitions other than Common. -- Configuration in a partition other than Common is modified. -- A Config-Sync operation not involving an overwrite takes place (it is also possible to reproduce this issue on a standalone BIG-IP system by doing a save operation like the following: "tmsh save sys config partitions { Common other }").
bugs.impact: /config/partitions/<partition_name>/bigip_base.conf will contain extraneous config stanzas (such as the ones mentioned in Symptoms). /config/bigip_base.conf will no longer contain config stanzas that belong there. Note that the impact is mostly cosmetic. An affected device will still be able to correctly load its configuration even if some config stanzas appear in the wrong flat config file. However, Administrators performing audits of the flat config files will be perplexed as to why some stanzas are moving back and forth between partitions.
bugs.workaround: If you wish to restore your flat config files to their proper state after the issue has already occurred, simply run "tmsh save sys config" on the affected device. Alternatively, to prevent the issue in the first place, you can Config-Sync using the following command "tmsh run cm config-sync force-full-load-push to-group <device-group>". Note that neither workaround is permanent and the issue will reoccur.

bugs.title: TMM may core when using Request Adapt profile
bugs.symptoms: tmm core file
bugs.conditions: Serverside connection is detached after processing HTTP response
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Cleaned up invalid references in Adapt component after serverside connection detachment

bugs.title: Support limited to 1000 BIG-IP system users.
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to load sys config default fails with an error similar to the following error: 010719a2:3: PostgreSQL database error: ERROR: out of shared memory ... PL/pgSQL function rbac_drop_user(name) line 3 at EXECUTE statement Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Configuring more than 1000 BIG-IP system users.
bugs.impact: Cannot log in. In this version of BIG-IP, no more than 1000 BIG-IP system users are supported. This limit is applied to the sum of all local BIG-IP system users and any remote BIG-IP system users who will log in to the system.
bugs.fix: Support is no longer limited to 1000 BIG-IP system users.

bugs.title: Benign warning during formatting installation
bugs.symptoms: The system posts a benign warning during formatting installation: warning: array conf_write could not find data disk.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during formatting installation.
bugs.impact: This is a benign error message that does not indicate an issue with the system. You can safely ignore it.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is a cosmetic message.
bugs.fix: This benign warning during formatting installation has been eliminated: warning: array conf_write could not find data disk.

bugs.title: Upgrade from 10.x fails on valid clientssl profile with BIGpipe parsing error
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade from 10.x fails with the error 'emerg load_config_files: '/usr/libexec/bigpipe load' - failed. -- BIGpipe parsing error (/config/bigpipe/bigip.conf Line 67): 012e0020:3: The requested item (myclientssl {) is invalid (profile_arg ` show ` list ` edit ` delete ` stats reset) for 'profile'."
bugs.conditions: Attempting to upgrade from 10.x to 11.6.1 or specific 11.5.3 and 11.5.4 engineering hotfixes with custom Certificate and Key in the clientssl profile.
bugs.impact: Unable to upgrade successfully and BIG-IP will be inoperative. You will be unable to log into the BIG-IP GUI. The error signature in /var/log/ltm will exist, and /config/bigip.conf will probably not exist.
bugs.workaround: Delete the following line from all ssl profiles in /config/bigpipe/bigip.conf: inherit-certkeychain false. To complete the upgrade, run the following command: /usr/libexec/bigpipe load. After config load is successful, run the following command: tmsh save sys config && tmsh load sys config.
bugs.fix: Upgrade from 10.x now completes successfully with a valid clientssl profile, and produces no BIGpipe parsing error.

bugs.title: Win10 and IE11 is not determined in case of DIRECT rule of proxy autoconfig script
bugs.symptoms: Windows 10 and Internet Explorer 11 is not determined in case of DIRECT rule is used to connect to BIG-IP in proxy autoconfig script configured locally.
bugs.conditions: Local proxy autoconfig scrip, DIRECT rule for BIG-IP virtual server, Internet Explorer 11.
bugs.impact: Internet Explorer 11 is not detected properly.
bugs.fix: Internet Explorer 11 on Microsoft Windows 10 is detected correctly now if local proxy autoconfig script is configured with DIRECT rule for BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Local-only network IP forwarding virtual server not forwarding traffic on standby system
bugs.symptoms: A local-only network IP forwarding virtual server does not forward traffic on standby systems.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP systems in an high-availability (HA) device cluster. An IP forwarding virtual server in traffic-group-local-only.
bugs.impact: Traffic is forwarded only on active BIG-IP systems.

bugs.title: PEM: After Diameter Fatal-Grace time expiry, Some subscriber sessions might be deleted very soon
bugs.symptoms: Some subscriber sessions getting deleted as soon they are created even if there is no trigger to delete these sessions
bugs.conditions: Fatal-grace time too low and PCRF connection going down for a long period of time and then coming up later.
bugs.impact: Subscribers traffic is not policed as the corresponding sessions are deleted as soon as they are created.
bugs.workaround: Make sure Fatal-grace timer is disabled.
bugs.fix: Issue is fixed now. Fatal Grace time expiry will not cause sessions to be deleted as soon as they are created.

bugs.title: Short HTTP monitor responses can incorrectly mark virtual servers down.
bugs.symptoms: Despite successful probe response, BIG-IP DNS marks virtual server down.
bugs.conditions: HTTP server sends HTTP response that is shorter than 64 bytes.
bugs.impact: Virtual servers are incorrectly marked down.
bugs.workaround: Modify server response or use a TCP monitor.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP DNS HTTP/1.x monitor probe now requires 17, rather than 64 bytes of response payload, so HTTP monitor responses HTTP response that is shorter than 64 bytes no longer incorrectly mark virtual servers down.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition Kernel Panic under load
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Edition instances may crash with a kernel panic under heavy traffic load.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Edition instances passing 10 Gbps of traffic on interfaces that support LRO.
bugs.impact: When the issue occurs the Virtual Edition instance will reboot.
bugs.workaround: Disable LRO on the underlying hypervisor, if possible.
bugs.fix: Virtual Edition instances now stays active when instances passing 10 Gbps of traffic on interfaces that support LRO.

bugs.title: Multiple Session ha state changes may cause TMM to core
bugs.symptoms: The cause of the crash is due to multiple session ha state changes in session_ha_peer_status in a very short period of time. On the active unit when the peer comes back up the session ha state changes to SESSION_HA_RESEND_NEEDED. This state change requires a call to session_ha_marker_reset to prevent the session sweeper from queueing the session ha marker when it is already in the session ha marker queue. Queueing the marker when it's already queued results in corruption of the queue which is caught by the QUEUEDEBUG_TAILQ_INSERT_TAIL macro.
bugs.conditions: Multiple session HA state changes
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Remove session ha maker when peer comes back up.

bugs.title: IPsec IKEv1 connectivity issues
bugs.symptoms: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels do not come up and IKE negotiations is not initiated/ or does not complete.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure the BIG-IP system with IPsec IKEv1 tunnel. 2. Send traffic to match the selectors, and it fails. Although it may succeed intermittently. The following chassis scenario might also cause the issue: 1. Configure the VIPRION chassis with IPsec IKEv1 tunnel. 2. Send traffic to match the selectors, and the intended traffic is secured. IPsec IKEv1 tunnels are established. 3. Perform bigstart restart on the secondary blade. 4. Observe Traffic does not pass, and shows IKE negotiation failures.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels do not get established and the intended traffic is not secured. Traffic does not pass, and shows IKE negotiation failures.
bugs.workaround: There is a workaround for the chassis platform: Perform bigstart restart of tmm on all blades. There is no workaround for non-chassis platforms.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP systems and VIPRION platforms now successfully establish IPsec IKEv1 tunnels and secure and pass the intended traffic.

bugs.title: MCP validation error while deactivating a policy that is assigned to a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When deactivating a security policy via REST, and the policy is assigned to a virtual server, then BIG-IP reports the following error: ---------------------------- "MCP Validation error - 01071726:3: Cannot deactivate policy action '/Common/<VS_name>'. It is in use by ltm policy '/Common/<L7_policy_name>'.", ---------------------------- However, the security policy becomes inactive and remains assigned to virtual server. This will cause the virtual server to stop processing network traffic, and there will be the following errors in 'bd.log': ---------------------------- BD_MISC|ERR |Jun 24 12:53:35.698|17566|src/acc_reject_policy.c:0165|Account id 10 has no reject policy configured. Cannot get data ----------------------------
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned, with a security policy assigned to a Virtual Server, then the security policy is deactivated via the REST API
bugs.impact: An inactive security policy remains assigned to a Virtual Server
bugs.workaround: Deactivate the security policy via GUI at: 'Security :: Application Security : Security Policies : Active Policies':
bugs.fix: The deactivation of a security policy using the REST API now removes the association of the deactivated policy from the virtual server, resulting in no errors and consistent configuration state.

bugs.title: CSS attribute name
bugs.symptoms: CSS attribute name was configured in the profile, but not passed to JavaScript where the hard-coded default value was used.
bugs.conditions: Default value of CSS attribute name is changed in the profile.
bugs.impact: False positive CSS alerts.
bugs.workaround: Do not change default value of CSS attribute name.

bugs.title: Errornous JS injections
bugs.symptoms: JS was injected into pages with any "Content-Type" and it broke functionality of some pages.
bugs.conditions: Page "Content-Type" is not "text/html".
bugs.impact: Page functionality may be broken.
bugs.fix: The FPS plugin now injects JavaScript only in responses where the value of the header "Content-Type" starts from "text/html".

bugs.title: On HA setups ASM session tracking page display an empty list when in fact there are asm entries in session db
bugs.symptoms: When session tracking actions are enabled in ASM policy, an HTTP request may be blocked based on HTTP session or username and illegal traffic that has been sent from this session. The blocked request is reported in the security events log, but there is no option to release the username using the Configuration utility.
bugs.conditions: High availability (HA) setup, and ASM with Session tracking actions enabled.
bugs.impact: Usernames and HTTP sessions are blocked by ASM without an option to release them from the Configuration utility.
bugs.workaround: Stop and start tmm on all devices in the HA group by running the following commands: -- bigstart stop tmm -- bigstart start tmm
bugs.fix: Using the Configuration utility, BIG-IP system administrators can now release blocked usernames and sessions. This is done on the Session Tracking Status screen.

bugs.title: LDAP StartTLS may fail on serverside when persistence is configured
bugs.symptoms: In some circumstances LDAP may fail to setup StartTLS on the server-side when instructed by a LDAP client when the LDAP virtual server is in use with a persistence profile.
bugs.conditions: - LDAP virtual server with client and server profiles. - LDAP profiles with STARTTLS Activation Mode set to Allow. - Persistence profile (for example, src addr persistence).
bugs.impact: Serverside does not upgrade to TLS.
bugs.workaround: Do not use LDAP virtual server in conjunction with persistence.

bugs.title: Crash observed with HSL logging
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, we see a crash with HSL logging.
bugs.conditions: Configure a HSL endpoint with session reporting. This crash is observed when multiple sessions are configured with hsl session reporting.
bugs.impact: Tmm cores.
bugs.fix: The crash was due to variables shared across threads. Changed this to a per thread variable.

bugs.title: Improvements in building Cloud images
bugs.symptoms: Improvements in building Cloud images.
bugs.conditions: Building Cloud images.
bugs.impact: Internal
bugs.fix: Improvements in building Cloud images.

bugs.title: DNS Cache can use cached data from ADDITIONAL sections in answers after RRset cache cleared
bugs.symptoms: On deleting the RRset cache, an incorrect answer could be served out of the message cache.
bugs.conditions: The RRset cache is cleared but the message cache is not.
bugs.impact: A deleted or cleared answer may be served
bugs.fix: Now, the RRset cache entries are marked as delete using ID instead of TTL.

bugs.title: Diameter monitor logging displays hex when monitor failing instead of the AVP which the monitor is failing on.
bugs.symptoms: Failed diameter monitor logging displays hex instead of the AVP on which the monitor failed.
bugs.conditions: Logging is enabled on a pool member which is being checked by a diameter monitor, and the monitor is failing.
bugs.impact: Difficult to determine the reason for the diameter monitor failure.

bugs.title: Installation may fail with the error "(Storage modification process conflict.)".
bugs.symptoms: On chassis, installation may fail with the error "(Storage modification process conflict.)".
bugs.conditions: This happens when deleting a boot location and then quickly installing new software to that boot location.
bugs.impact: Minimal; the installation can be restarted.
bugs.workaround: Delete the failed volume and restart the installation.
bugs.fix: On chassis, there was one possible case where the installation would occasionally fail with the error "(Storage modification process conflict.)". This case has been fixed.

bugs.title: AVR missing some configuration changes in multiblade system
bugs.symptoms: Some DB variables affect the behavior of AVR, but if they are modified in a multiblade system, then not all blades will be aware of the change, which later leads to errors in functionality.
bugs.conditions: Multiblade system, having one of the following changes: 1. New primary blade is selected. 2. Change to AVR max number of entities in the DB.
bugs.impact: Data might not be loaded into the DB, or not be queried correctly.
bugs.workaround: Restart of monpd solves the problem.
bugs.fix: Configuration changes in multiblade systems are now treated correctly.

bugs.title: Incorrect reports on multi-bladed systems
bugs.symptoms: Reports on multi-bladed systems might contain incorrect data, if the blades are active at different times, and do not share the same level of history. A report appears on a different time range than expected.
bugs.conditions: Example: A setup with 3 blades, and 2 are down while the active 1 receives traffic for a full day. Later the 2 down blades go up. The resulting report for 'last day' contains data only for the previous hour, even though traffic has been passing through it for the last day.
bugs.impact: Report not as expected.
bugs.fix: Reports on multi-bladed systems are now displayed correctly even when the blades are active at different times, and do not share the same level of history.

bugs.title: Input Names that are configured as "Parameters" in BIG-IP and are getting encoded in special characters via the EncodedURI JavaScript function are ignored after the submission.
bugs.symptoms: Input Names that are configured as "Parameters" in BIG-IP and are getting encoded in special characters via the EncodedURI JavaScript function are ignored after the submission.
bugs.conditions: After configuring the required input in BIG-IP system, login to the page and submitting it.
bugs.impact: There is no decryption action on that input's value. The password/encryption target do not go through the decryption phase, and therefore will not succeed in login into the account.

bugs.title: Connection mirroring with OneConnect on a virtual server can cause TMM crash on standby unit
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on the standby unit.
bugs.conditions: This is a standby-only failure. Connection mirroring on a OneConnect virtual server can lead to a TMM crash during connection establishment.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts, and the standby is not available for failover. When the standby unit comes back up it does not have the mirrored flows from the active unit, so failover results in loss of those connection flows.
bugs.fix: Connection mirroring on a OneConnect virtual server now successfully recovers from a TMM crash during connection establishment, so no mirrored connection flows are lost.

bugs.title: OSPF may not process updates to redistributed routes
bugs.symptoms: When routes redistributed into OSPF are rapidly added and removed, OSPF may not reflect all of the updates in its LSA database.
bugs.conditions: External routes, such as kernel or static, redistributed into OSPF being rapidly added and removed. This my happen when using Route Health Injection and enabling/disabling a virtual address.
bugs.impact: The OSPF may have stale or missing LSAs for redistributed routes.
bugs.workaround: Identify the OSPF process ID for the affected route domain using "ps | grep ospfd" and terminate it using the kill command. This disrupts dynamic routing using OSPF.
bugs.fix: The OSPF LSA database correctly reflects the state of redistributed routes after rapid updates.

bugs.title: FIPS firmware v2.2 update on BIG-IP 5250, 7200F, 10200F, and 11050F platforms running the Cavium Nitrox XL FIPS cards.
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP 5250, 7200F, 10200F, and 11050F platforms running the Cavium Nitrox XL FIPS cards, the FIPS firmware version 2.1 has been moved to the Legacy list by NIST as the RNG function does not meet modern-day FIPS standards. For more information, see the external resource, available here: http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/STM/cmvp/documents/140-1/140val-all.htm.
bugs.conditions: This impacts BIG-IP 5250, 7200F, 10200F, and 11050F FIPS platforms running FIPS firmware 2.1 or earlier. You can tell what firmware you have installed by running the following command at the command line: fipsutil info The firmware version listed should be the following: CN16XX-NFBE-FW-2.2-130013.
bugs.impact: All platforms shipped prior to June 30th, 2016, contain an older firmware version and must be updated to run the NIST-approved version. To comply with current NIST requirements, the new firmware has deprecated support for 1024-bit key creation. Existing 1024-bit keys in the device can still be used normally.
bugs.workaround: F5 Networks has released a downloadable firmware installer that you can download and apply to the platforms containing the FIPS firmware 2.1 or earlier. For more information about FIPS compliance, see SOL7837: Overview of FIPS 140-2 EAL Level 2 and 3 RoHS Certification Status, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/7000/800/sol7837.html.
bugs.fix: FIPS firmware v2.2 update on BIG-IP 5250, 7200F, 10200F, and 11050F platforms running the Cavium Nitrox XL FIPS cards.

bugs.title: The TCP::option iRules command fails following upgrade to BIG-IP 11.x
bugs.symptoms: The iRules command TCP::option fails after you upgrade to BIG-IP 11.x. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- F5 iHealth lists Heuristic H539210 on the Diagnostics :: Identified :: Medium screen. -- You upgrade from BIG-IP 10.2.x to BIG-IP 11.x and see that iRules causes an error and triggers the following event: -- CLIENT_ACCEPTED - Illegal argument. TCP::option get on profile without tcp option setting (line 1) invoked from within 'TCP::option get 8'.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You use an iRule that contains the command TCP::option to gather TCP option information from the TCP header. -- You set the database variable Rules.Tcpoption.settings to specify a TCP option to collect.
bugs.impact: iRules that use TCP::option and depend on Rules.Tcpoption.settings do not work as you expect when you upgrade from BIG-IP 10.2.x to BIG-IP 11.x.
bugs.workaround: Configure TCP profile after upgrade that collects the version-specific TCP::option for iRules, as shown in the following example: create ltm profile tcp profile_name tcp-options "{8 last}" To work around this issue, configure the TCP profile after the upgrade that collects the appropriate TCP option for the iRule. Refer to the following article for information about changes to the TCP::option command in 11.x: TCP on F5 Cloud Docs :: https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/TCP.html

bugs.title: CGNAT: Changing the PBA client-block-limit on a LSN pool while blocks are allocated can lead to incorrect 'Clients Using Max Port Blocks' counts in the stats
bugs.symptoms: Statistic will be incorrect or negative: 'Clients Using Max Port Blocks'.
bugs.conditions: Changing the PBA client-block-limit on a LSN pool while there are active blocks and connections might result in incorrect 'Clients Using Max Port Blocks' counts in the stats.
bugs.impact: 'Clients Using Max Port Blocks' count is used for monitoring the number of clients that have reached the block limit, then this will impact operations and monitoring of lsn-pool status.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the BIG-IP system resets the counter.

bugs.title: Mcpd will crash if load too many SSL certificates
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd/TMM will crash if load too many SSL certificates.
bugs.conditions: Loading too many SSL certificates at a time, for example, 4000 or more SSL certificates.
bugs.impact: Mcpd/TMM might crash.
bugs.workaround: Split the config file into several smaller ones.

bugs.title: AD/LDAP groupmapping is overencoding group names with backslashes
bugs.symptoms: Adding a group value that contains space(s) manually in AD/LDAP Group Resource Assign actions will result in the space(s) being escaped and thus invalidating match attempts. For example, adding group 'Foo Bar' (without the quotes) will result in an expression found in bigip.conf as follows: expression "expr { [mcget -decode {session.ldap.last.attr.memberOf}] contains \"CN=Foo\\\\ Bar\" }" The value '\"CN=Foo\\\\ Bar\"' will not match a memberOf group returned that contains 'CN=Foo Bar,...'.
bugs.conditions: Spaces are encoded with backslashes.
bugs.impact: Matching for memberOf group will not working.

bugs.title: Illegal meta characters on XML tags -
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from 11.4.1 to 11.6.0, 11.6.1 or 12.0.0, you see a lot of "Illegal meta character in value" false positives on your XML content. The flagged character are valid within XML (<, >, /, :, etc.) and the affected URLs are associated with legitimate XML profiles via header-based content profiles. From the security event report, one can see that the invalid characters are for the global UNNAMED wildcard parameter and that the request is a multipart POST.
bugs.conditions: XML profile is assigned to the wildcard URL and having Header-Based Content profile.
bugs.impact: False positive violations could happen on the parameter enforcement (as it's not a parameter content but XML).

bugs.title: OCSP Agent does not honor the AIA setting in the client cert even though 'Ignore AIA' option is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: OCSP Agent does not honor the AIA setting in the client cert even though 'Ignore AIA' option is disabled.
bugs.conditions: -- User certificate has AIA configured. -- Option 'Ignore AIA' is unchecked. -- APM is configured.
bugs.impact: OCSP auth might fail as wrong URL is used.
bugs.workaround: 1. Clean URL field. 2. Uncheck option 'Ignore AIA'.
bugs.fix: If the option 'Ignore AIA' is unchecked, APM uses AIA from certificate even if URL is configured for AAA OCSP responder. This is correct behavior.
bugs.behavior: If the option 'Ignore AIA' is unchecked, APM uses AIA from certificate even if URL is configured for AAA OCSP responder. To use the configured URL, the 'Ignore AIA' setting has to be checked.

bugs.title: Improvements in building hotfix images for hypervisors.
bugs.symptoms: The name of HF/EHF ISOs changed recently and the filter used to locate them needs to change.
bugs.conditions: Building hotfix images for hypervisors.
bugs.impact: There are issues providing bundled images.
bugs.fix: This release provides improvements for building hotfix images for hypervisors.

bugs.title: Support for New Platform: BIG-IP 10350 FIPS
bugs.symptoms: Support for New Platform: BIG-IP 10350 FIPS, effective in 11.5.4 HF1
bugs.conditions: This details the new platform name.
bugs.impact: This is an added platform. There is no impact to the product.
bugs.workaround: None needed.
bugs.fix: This release provides support for New Platform: BIG-IP 10350 FIPS. You can find more information in Platform Guide: 10000 Series, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/products/big-ip_ltm/manuals/product/pg-10200v.html.
bugs.behavior: This release provides support for New Platform: BIG-IP 10350 FIPS. You can find more information in Platform Guide: 10000 Series, available here: https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/products/big-ip_ltm/manuals/product/pg-10200v.html.

bugs.title: Crit tmm error messages due to race condition that occurs during RebootHost on 10000, 10050, 10055, 10200F, 10350N, 12050, and 12250 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: When the IOMMU is enabled, the system may report crit tmm error messages due to a race condition that might occurs during start-up. Error messages appear in /var/log/ltm, similar to the following: crit tmm[14967]: 01010025:2: Device error: hsb interface 0 coalesce timed out. crit tmm[14967]: 01010025:2: Device error: hsb interface pde 0 access failed. crit tmm[14967]: 01230017:2: Unable to attach to PCI device 03:00.01 for Interface 0.1. ... crit tmm[14967]: 01010260:2: Hardware Error(Co-Processor): n3-crypto1 request queue stuck.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on startup as a result of a race condition between chmand and tmm with IOMMU enabled.
bugs.impact: System remains INOPERATIVE and reports crit tmm error messages. Note: Although IOMMU is disabled by default, you can enable it using the BIOS utility, and newer platforms might enable it by default.
bugs.workaround: To recover from the INOPERATIVE state, disable IOMMU with the following command and restart the BIG-IP system: tmsh modify sys db kernel.iommu valued isable

bugs.title: SPDAG on VIPRION B2250 blades might cause traffic imbalance among TMMs
bugs.symptoms: When SPDAG is turned on VIPRION B2250 blades, the traffic imbalance among TMMs might be observed.
bugs.conditions: Enable SPDAG on VIPRION B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: The traffic imbalance can lower the throughput of VIPRION B2250 blades.
bugs.workaround: Adding or removing B2250 blades might mitigate the imbalance. If you are running BIG-IP versions 11.6.1 or 11.6.1 HF1, add the following to /config/tmm_init.tcl file: dag::use_p8_sp_hash yes
bugs.fix: A new DAG hash is added for SPDAG on VIPRION B2250 blades, which can resolve the SPDAG traffic imbalance. The new DAG hash can be turned on by setting tmm tcl variable, dag::use_p8_sp_hash, to yes. Add the following to /config/tmm_init.tcl file: dag::use_p8_sp_hash yes

bugs.title: Rate limit configured on a node can be exceeded
bugs.symptoms: Rate limit configured on a node is not honored and is exceeded. The excess per second can be as much as 10 (100%) when the limit is configured as 10.
bugs.conditions: More than 1 tmm needs to be there. Rate limit needs to be configured on the node.
bugs.impact: Node rate limit feature does not work as intended.
bugs.workaround: Rate limit can be shifted from the node to pool member and it works.

bugs.title: Added SSL certificate expiration date as an OID into F5 MIBs
bugs.symptoms: SSL certificate expiration date is not viewable in viewable as an SNMP OID.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to view an SSL certificate expiration date in SNMP information.
bugs.impact: The impact is that SSL certificate expiration date is not viewable in viewable as an SNMP OID.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: SSL Certificate Expiration Date is now viewable as an SNMP OID. These are viewable under the sysCertificateFileObject as either a text format at sysCertificateFileObjectExpirationString in textual form such as "Aug 13 21:21:29 2031 GMT" or as the internal date format at sysCertificateFileObjectExpirationDate in unix time form such as "1944422489".
bugs.behavior: This release adds an SSL certificate expiration date as an OID into F5 MIBs. SSL Certificate Expiration Date is now viewable as an SNMP OID. These are viewable under the sysCertificateFileObject as either a text format at sysCertificateFileObjectExpirationString in textual form such as "Aug 13 21:21:29 2031 GMT" or as the internal date format at sysCertificateFileObjectExpirationDate in unix time form such as "1944422489".

bugs.title: Some AVR tables that hold ASM statistics are not being backed up in upgrade process.
bugs.symptoms: Some AVR tables that hold ASM statistics are not being backed up in the upgrade process when upgrading to a new version with ASM data present in AVR stat tables.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading to new version.
bugs.impact: Some ASM data is lost after upgrade.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly backs up AVR tables that hold ASM statistics that were previously not backed up when upgrading to a new version.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes: ephemeral nodes not being created for resolved FQDN hosts
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to 11.6.0 HF5 the ephemeral fqdn node lists are no longer auto-populating.
bugs.conditions: Use the fqdn nodes feature. Have correctly configured dns name-servers, and upgrade to 11.6.0 HF5
bugs.impact: The fqdn nodes feature is unusable and possible upgrades must be rolled back.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: FQDN node lists now correctly auto-populate.

bugs.title: MultiConnect is incompatible with CORS policy
bugs.symptoms: The issue happens when MultiConnect is enabled and a resource is reloaded by a user request. If the browsers have CORS policy enforcement applied to the resource, the consequent requests for the resource are forwarded to a subdomain and a CORS header "Origin" is inserted into the request. In response the browser expects "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header with a value allowing the subdomain as a host in the request. AAM doesn't recognize the header and just ignores it or has it passed to OWS which doesn't expect it.
bugs.conditions: An AAM policy with MultiConnect option is configured and attached to a virtual. There are resource(s) in a page are used for which CORS policy is enforced in a client browser, for example, font file for CSS.
bugs.impact: Lack of loading of the resource which may result in incorrect rendering of the page.
bugs.workaround: 1) Disable MultiConnect. 2) Create an iRule to properly process Origin header.

bugs.title: IP fragments can cause TMM to crash when packet filtering is enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM can crash when an IP fragment is received and packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur when packet filtering is enabled and an IP fragment is received on the non-owning TMM. To determine if packet filtering is enabled, then the packetfilter setting can be queried by using the 'tmsh list sys db packetfilter' command.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable packet filtering.
bugs.fix: When packet filtering is enabled and an IP fragment is received on the non-owning TMM, TMM forwards the IP fragment without issue.

bugs.title: tmsh sys log filter is displays in UTC time
bugs.symptoms: When using the time-based log filters hour, minute, and second, tmsh returns results based on UTC time.
bugs.conditions: Use range filter for 'tmsh show sys log' in either of the following ways: Filter logs by hour. Filter logs for less than 8 hours.
bugs.impact: tmsh does not filter the log correctly with 'range' filter.
bugs.workaround: Calculate the difference between the local BIG-IP system time and UTC, or change the system time to UTC.

bugs.title: Some Session Tracking data points are lost on TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: Session Tracking data points, that are added by ASM upon traffic, based on Session Tracking thresholds configuration, are lost when TMM restarts.
bugs.conditions: ASM Provisioned. Session Tracking feature is ON.
bugs.impact: Session Tracking data points may be added by ASM upon traffic. These are data points with action 'Block-All'. These data points are lost when TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the Session Tracking data points persistence, so that the 'Block-All' Session Tracking data points, which are added by ASM upon traffic, are not lost when TMM restarts.

bugs.title: EAM plugin uses high memory when serving very high concurrent user load
bugs.symptoms: EAM plugin cannot sustain high concurrent user load and will be killed by memory monitors. EAM is cored and restarted. Any requests coming during restart will not be served.
bugs.conditions: This issue was found internally during in stress testing and was reported externally when experiencing high concurrent user load.
bugs.impact: As a result, EAM cored and restarted; users cannot authenticate during process restart.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: There was a memory usage issue in the EAM plugin. This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: Windows Phone 10 platform detection
bugs.symptoms: Windows Phone 10 platform is not currently detected
bugs.conditions: Windows Phone 10 platform , BIG-IP APM system
bugs.impact: Windows Phone 10 platform is not detected correctly by BIG-IP
bugs.fix: Windows Phone 10 platform is detected correctly now.

bugs.title: TMM crash in DNS processing on a TCP virtual
bugs.symptoms: TMM can crash while processing DNS requests on a TCP virtual server.
bugs.conditions: A TCP DNS virtual server combined with a DNS iRule that suspends and a client that closes its connection before receiving a response to its DNS request.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: While no true workaround exists, the situation can be avoiding by removing any one of the conditions above.
bugs.fix: TMM now properly handles DNS requests through a TCP virtual where the client closes the connection during iRule processing.

bugs.title: F5 SFP+ module becomes unpopulated after mcpd is restarted in a clustered environment.
bugs.symptoms: When MCPD restarts on one of the B2100 blades, trunk interfaces on the blade are not coming up.
bugs.conditions: MCPD restarts in a clustered environment (chassis).
bugs.impact: TMM will not process traffic on the blade where mcpd restarted.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm (bigstart restart tmm) on the blade that shows the interface down.
bugs.fix: Fixed in corrections for bug 502443-9.

bugs.title: per-request policy logs frequently in apm logs
bugs.symptoms: Many logs from per-request policy execution framework are seen in APM logs
bugs.conditions: SWG is licensed and provisioned and response analytics agent is part of per-request policy.
bugs.impact: Many logs in APM and excessive logging might impact the performance too.
bugs.workaround: Remove /Common/All-Images from Response analytics agent in per-request policy.
bugs.fix: Correctly fixed the issue for excluded contents in response analytics agent, so these logs are not written frequently to APM logs.

bugs.title: Login page may generate unexpected HTML output
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstance the administrative login page may generate unexpected HTML output
bugs.conditions: External authentication enabled
bugs.impact: Unexpected output to client browser
bugs.fix: The login page now generates the expected output.

bugs.title: Add detail to urldbmgr log messages regarding database download failures
bugs.symptoms: Error messages from urldbmgrd do not provide enough detail about the cause when a database cannot be downloaded.
bugs.conditions: Database download failure from urldbmgr.
bugs.impact: If a BIG-IP system is having issues getting the databases there should be enough information to attempt to fix the issue using log data.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: In FastL4 TCP virtual servers, ICMP might send wrong SEQ number/ACK number.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may send ICMP messages that contain an incorrect tcp seq ack number in the embedded msg body.
bugs.conditions: FastL4 TCP virtual servers. Syncookie mode.
bugs.impact: The TCP connflow might be aborted if an ICMP message (such as More fragment) is received.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system sends correct SEQ and ACK number in ICMP messages.

bugs.title: Messages can't be sent from OWA2010 via Portal Access if form-based SSOv2 is in use.
bugs.symptoms: OWA displays error message when trying to send new email. POST request size is more than 300Kb and POST data contains large "SCRIPT id=F5_helperDataStringsId" tag. Due to this issue request data becomes large enough to be affected by Bug502269 in SSOv2. Therefore if SSOv2 is enabled in this Access Policy, request content will be corrupted and OWA server will respond with '400 Bad Request' code instead of sending email.
bugs.impact: Users can't send messages in some versions of OWA.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where extra data was added to some OWA2010 requests making it impossible to send messages in configuration with Form-based SSOv2.

bugs.title: Legacy DAG algorithm reuses high source port numbers frequently
bugs.symptoms: A service on a pool member will receive connections frequently with a source port number above 65400, especially when the incoming connections to the Virtual IP listener are generated by test tools that increment their source port numbers sequentially. This could lead to premature SNAT port exhaustion, if SNAT is also being used.
bugs.conditions: The issue appears to be limited to the legacy DAG algorithm on the VIPRION PB100 and PB200 blades. All supported versions of BIG-IP will exhibit this issue on this hardware when this DAG algorithm is used. The problem is not exhibited when the incoming sessions' source port numbers have a reasonable amount of entropy (as one would normally see with real Internet traffic); however, the use of test tools, or even intentional malicious traffic may cause this issue to be seen.
bugs.impact: The issue could result in resource contention (such as SNAT pool port exhaustion), or problems with the pool member services distinguishing between sessions. A notable exception: Port reuse before TIME_WAIT expires is specifically NOT an impact of this issue.
