bugs.workaround: To work around SNAT pool port exhaustion, increase the pool size, or change to auto-map. An iRule may be used to help pool member services better distinguish incoming sessions.
bugs.fix: The software emulation of the legacy DAG algorithm used on VIPRION PB100 and PB200 has been updated to more evenly distribute the source port numbers of sessions arriving at pool member services.

bugs.title: UDP traffic sent to the host may leak memory under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: Possible memory leak with UDP traffic.
bugs.conditions: When UDP traffic is sent to the host.
bugs.impact: If memory leak becomes large enough over time, there could be a reboot.
bugs.workaround: Block UDP traffic to the host.
bugs.fix: Memory no longer leaks when UDP traffic is sent to the host.

bugs.title: AFM Logging regression for Global/Route Domain Rules incorrectly using virtual server logging profile (if it exists)
bugs.symptoms: Due to a related change in AFM ACL handling, global and route domain rule's were being logged (incorrectly) by the virtual server's AFM log profile (if it exists). This is incorrect since the behavior has always been that Global and Route Domain AFM rule logging is controlled by global-network log profile only.
bugs.conditions: Global or Route Domain AFM ACL rule matches and logging is enabled. Also, the matched virtual server has a logging profile attached to it.
bugs.impact: This causes a regression (and inadvertent change in behavior) for Global and Route Domain AFM rule logging.
bugs.fix: With the fix, global and route domain AFM rule logging is controlled by global-network log profile (as has been the case since inception).

bugs.title: New Dyre Signature added to Generic Malware Detection
bugs.symptoms: Some variants of Dyre were not detected.
bugs.conditions: Some variants of Dyre were not detected.
bugs.impact: Some variants of Dyre were not detected.
bugs.workaround: Receive updated bait signatures from F5 Websafe representative.
bugs.fix: New Dyre Signature added.

bugs.title: TCP profile option Verified Accept might cause iRule processing to run twice in very specific circumstances.
bugs.symptoms: A specific combination of configuration options might cause iRule processing to run the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event twice.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - Standard Virtual Server is configured. - Virtual Server is configured with a TCP profile in which Verified Accept is enabled. - Address translation is enabled on the Virtual Server. - Node selection occurs in the iRule via node command. - Client sends the initial data to be sent on the ACK of the three-way-handshake.
bugs.impact: Depending on the scenario, this might result in the specific connection being reset.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following workarounds: - Disable Verified Accept in the TCP profile. - Modify the iRule to run the commands in the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event once, by setting a variable and checking it on subsequent runs.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly processes initial data on the ACK of a three-way handshake when used with Verified Accept so iRule processing does not run the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event twice.

bugs.title: HA pair in a typical Active/Standby configuration becomes Active/Active after a software upgrade
bugs.symptoms: HA pair should remain in active/standby state after the software upgrade but instead goes into an active/active state.
bugs.conditions: Occurs in an active/standby HA pair which has a medium size configuration of pools and virtual servers (at least 30 objects total). The standby device is upgraded first and then it is rebooted. After reboot, the HA pair goes into an Active/Active state. Upgrades to 11.5.0 through 11.5.3 as well as to 11.6.0 are impacted.
bugs.impact: Active/Standby configuration is lost.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the HA pair back to active/standby.
bugs.fix: HA pair in a typical Active/Standby configuration now remain Active/Standby after a software upgrade.

bugs.title: Adding interfaces to trunk fails if trunk and interfaces are forced to lower speed
bugs.symptoms: If a trunk is created from interfaces that have lower than max speed (e.g., 100full-duplex on 1GbE links) adding a new interface fails. When this occurs, the system posts an error similar to the following: 01070619:3: Interface 1.4 media type is incompatible with other trunk members.
bugs.conditions: Interfaces use a lower speed then their capacity. Trunk is created where the highest speed of any of the members is this reduced speed. Interface, also lowered, is added to the trunk.
bugs.impact: Interface cannot be added to the trunk.
bugs.workaround: Remove all interfaces, readd them all at the same time.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly adds interfaces to a trunk formed from interfaces running at a lowered speed.

bugs.title: MySql query fails with error number 1615 'Prepared statement needs to be re-prepared'
bugs.symptoms: MySql query fails with error number 1615 'Prepared statement needs to be re-prepared'. Errors in monpd.log similar to the following: [DB::mysql_query_safe, query failed] Error (error number 1615) executing SQL string ...
bugs.conditions: This is due to a MySql bug. For information, see 'Prepared-Statement fails when MySQL-Server under load', available here: http://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=42041
bugs.impact: Monpd loses functionality
bugs.workaround: Restart monpd.
bugs.fix: Error number 1615, 'Prepared statement needs to be re-prepared', no longer occurs in the monpd.log.

bugs.title: BIG-IP TLS doesn't correctly verify Finished.verify_data on non-Cavium platforms
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP does not verify every byte in the Finished message of an TLS handshake but does properly validate the MAC of the Finished message.
bugs.conditions: * The BIG-IP platform contains a Cavium SSL accelerator card but the affected TLS connection is not accelerated by the Cavium SSL accelerator card. The following list some examples when a TLS connection is not accelerated by the Cavium card: * The ciphers used by the TLS connection are not fully accelerated in the Cavium card. For more information about ciphers that are fully hardware accelerated, refer to SOL13213: SSL ciphers that are fully hardware accelerated on BIG-IP platforms (11.x) * The BIG-IP platform does not contain a Cavium SSL accelerator card. The following list the BIG-IP platforms that do not contain a Cavium SSL accelerator card: * BIG-IP 2000 platforms * BIG-IP 4000 platforms * BIG-IP Virtual Edition
bugs.impact: F5 believes the reported behavior does not have security implications at this time.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP TLS doesn't correctly verify Finished.verify_data on non-Cavium platforms.

bugs.title: Copy profile might end up with error
bugs.symptoms: Copy profile might end up with error about two items are sharing the same agent
bugs.conditions: Very rare - long policy names, similar name parts
bugs.impact: Minor - you would need to choose different name for new policy
bugs.fix: Issue resolved.

bugs.title: Missing entry in SQL table leads to misleading ASM reports
bugs.symptoms: Some reports of ASM violations were generated with missing activity.
bugs.conditions: When there are many entities to report and some are getting aggregated, then the aggregated activity was not reported.
bugs.impact: Misleading reports of ASM activity.
bugs.fix: Aggregated activity is now reported even when there are many entities to report and some are aggregated.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to manually insert the missing entry to mysql. The exact values that need to be inserted vary from one customer to another and require mysql dump to be created and the PD team to inspect it, in order to decide which values should be inserted. It is better that customers upgrade to a fixed version rather than trying to work around it.

bugs.title: Support for StoreFront proxy
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receivers fail to auth when APM is configured in the integration mode against Citrix StoreFront 3.0 in ICA patching mode
bugs.conditions: APM configured in the integration mode
bugs.impact: Storefront responds with "error-bad-request" error on ExplicitForms request from APM
bugs.fix: Support Citrix StoreFront 3.0 in ICA patching proxy mode

bugs.title: The NTLM login is not recognized as failed login.
bugs.symptoms: The NTLM login is not recognized as failed login.
bugs.conditions: -- A NTLM configured login page. -- The username arrives in UTF-16 (as curl sends it) or in another encoding that cannot be converted. -- The login fails.
bugs.impact: The brute force mitigation will not work in this case.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue regarding login pages with the NTLM authentication type.

bugs.title: Support Citrix Receiver 4.3 for Windows in PNAgent mode
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Receiver for Windows 4.3 fails to authenticate in PNAgent mode in both integration and replacement configurations.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for Citrix integration or replacement and Citrix Receiver for Windows 4.3 is used in PNAgent mode.
bugs.impact: Citrix Receiver for Windows 4.3 fails to authenticate.
bugs.workaround: Use Citrix Receiver for Windows 4.1 or 4.2. Launch applications from Web.
bugs.fix: Now APM supports Citrix Receiver 4.3 for Windows in PNAgent mode.

bugs.title: A partial response arrives to the client when response logging is turned on
bugs.symptoms: When response logging is turned on, the client receives only a partial response.
bugs.conditions: Response logging is turned on. The response is chunked.
bugs.impact: The response arrives as chunked, but not all the chunks arriving, causing the client to wait for the traffic continuation.
bugs.fix: All chunks of a chunked response arrive when response logging is enabled.

bugs.title: tmm memory leak in traffic handling
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios TMM may suffer from a memory leak while handling certain types of TCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: Undisclosed conditions for packet processing.
bugs.impact: TMM will leak memory.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer leaks memory while processing certain types of TCP traffic.

bugs.title: List commands on non-existent iRules incorrectly succeeds.
bugs.symptoms: In certain cases, issuing an iControl REST or tmsh list rule command on a non-existent iRule can return successfully with an empty list. Instead it should return an error that the specified iRule does not exist.
bugs.conditions: If any iRule happens to exist in a different folder than the current folder context.
bugs.impact: The user is unable to rely on receiving an error from tmsh or iControl REST if they query for iRules that do not exist.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Issuing a list command for a non-existent iRule now successfully returns an error.

bugs.title: Web navigation flow may be reset when main page responds with non-HTML content
bugs.symptoms: In some web applications, the navigation flow may break (connection reset) if a main URL (login page, for example) is responding with a content that is not an HTML one, or if the response is dynamic, and occasionally not an HTML one.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense is enabled on a DOS profile that is attached to a Virtual Server, and one of the main URLs of the web application (login page, home page, etc.) occasionally responds with a non-HTML content, blank content, or redirect response with no body.
bugs.impact: Users may experience a connection reset while navigating through the website, usually after several minutes.
bugs.fix: Connection resets are no longer experienced on normal web navigation of a site that is protected by the Proactive Bot Defense mechanism, and one of the main pages of the web application occasionally responds with a non-HTML content.

bugs.title: FTP/SMTP traffic related bd crash
bugs.symptoms: Protocol Security: The Enforcer may crash upon FTP or SMTP traffic using remote logging.
bugs.conditions: FTP/SMTP traffic and remote logging assigned. Crash happens on a rare occasion.
bugs.impact: bd crash, traffic disturbance.
bugs.workaround: Remove the remote logging from FTP/SMTP.
bugs.fix: Protocol Security: The Enforcer no longer crashes upon FTP or SMTP traffic using remote logging.

bugs.title: Call to Apply Policy can be lost and never retried in an autosync device group
bugs.symptoms: ASM Changes in an auto-sync device group are sent over a direct channel to a device's peers. In rare conditions it is possible that messages are lost over this channel. Configuration changes have fallbacks to ensure the missing change will be noticed, but there is no such fallback currently for Apply Policy calls. Therefore, if an Apply Policy call goes missing in an autosync group, it will never retry.
bugs.conditions: ASM sync is configured on an autosync device group.
bugs.impact: Enforcement changes will not take effect on the peer devices until the next Apply Policy action.
bugs.workaround: Make a spurious change to the policy and set it active again.

bugs.title: Windows 10 App Store VPN Client must be detected by BIG-IP APM
bugs.symptoms: Windows 10 App Store VPN Client is not detected by BIG-IP APM out of the box via client type agent
bugs.conditions: Windows 10 App Store VPN Client, BIG-IP APM , client type agent
bugs.impact: Windows 10 App Store VPN Client is not detected by BIG-IP APM out of the box
bugs.fix: Windows 10 App Store VPN Client is now detected by BIG-IP APM out of the box using the Client Type agent.

bugs.title: SNMP support for standard MIBs and Traps is incomplete
bugs.symptoms: Areas of the standard MIB and Traps were incomplete and needed to be addressed for third party management tools to be used to manage the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: Standard MIBs and Traps are required for SNMP based management tools.
bugs.impact: Other tools must be used to query the BIG-IP when SNMP support does not cover an area.

bugs.title: apmd, apd, localmgr random crash
bugs.symptoms: APMD, APD, and localmgr crash upon invalid mcpd request with certain DB variables.
bugs.conditions: This problem rarely happens: mcpd sends null db variables conncrtl.
bugs.impact: APMD, APD, and localmgr will crash.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The problem was fixed by variable protection in related modules.

bugs.title: Support SSL serverside certificate validation using OCSP and CRLDP (CRL distribution point)
bugs.symptoms: The system does only basic checks for the SSL certificate sent from SSL servers without going through valid protocols (for example, OCSP, CRL, SCVP). It at most allows a user to configure a pre-downloaded static CRL file for certificate authentication. However, in SSL forward proxy mode the SSL servers and hence their certificates dynamically change, so certificate authentication against a static CRL file is not an optimal configuration.
bugs.conditions: When the system needs to do SSL handshake with SSL servers.
bugs.impact: If the SSL server (or HTTP server) is using a revoked certificate, there is no way that the system can know which is a vulnerability.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The system can now verify the status of the certificate from the SSL servers, by sending outbound queries to OCSP or CRLDP.

bugs.title: APM ACLs can block ICA file generation on APM Webtop
bugs.symptoms: APM ACLs can block ICA file generation on APM Webtop. As a result, Citrix app on APM Webtop cannot be started.
bugs.conditions: APM ACLs are blocking internal ICA file generation request. Example is a deny-all L4 ACL.
bugs.impact: Citrix app on APM Webtop cannot be started.
bugs.workaround: Add allow ACL to allow ICA file generation request destined for hte virtual server servicing the Citrix. ACL logging from /var/log/pktfilter to determine the rule for such allow ACL.

bugs.title: SSL version in the record layer of ClientHello is not set to be the lowest supported version.
bugs.symptoms: In the ClientHello message, the system is now setting the SSL version in the record layer to be the same as version value of ClientHello message, which is the highest SSL version now supported. Although RFC 5246 appendix E.1 does not give specific advice on how to set the TLS versions, the de facto standard used by all major browsers and TLS stacks is to set the ClientHello as follows: SSL Record: Content Type: Handshake (22) Version: $LOWEST_VERSION Handshake Record: Handshake Type: Client Hello (1) Version: $HIGHEST_VERSION The BIG-IP system implementation tells the SSL peer that the system supports only SSL versions from the $HIGHEST_VERSION through the $HIGHEST_VERSION instead of from the $LOWEST_VERSION through the $HIGHEST_VERSION, which effectively limits the range of SSL versions the system can negotiate with the SSL peer.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the highest SSL version that the BIG-IP system supports does not fall into the range that an SSL peer supports. For example, with SSL peer support configured for TLS1.0 or TLS1.1, if the BIG-IP system sets the highest SSL version to be TLS1.2, then there will be no version that the SSL peer thinks they have in common, and SSL handshake fails.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake fails.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: The SSL version in the record layer of ClientHello is now set to be the lowest supported version, which eliminates that issue that occurred when the highest SSL version that the BIG-IP system supports did not fall into the range that an SSL peer supports.

bugs.title: [MAC][NA] Routing table is not updated correctly in connected state when new adapter is added
bugs.symptoms: Routing table is not updated correctly in connected state when new adapter is added to the system.
bugs.conditions: SSL VPN tunnel is established and new adapter is added to the system. For example, Wi-Fi connected when tunnel is established already over Ethernet adapter.
bugs.impact: Routing table might be corrupted.
bugs.workaround: Restart OS X.
bugs.fix: Routing table now updates correctly when new adapter is added to the system while SSL VPN tunnel is already established over an network adapter.

bugs.title: Hourly AWS VE license breaks after reboot with default tmm route/gateway.
bugs.symptoms: In AWS Hourly instances, if a default gateway is added, the hourly license may fail, causing BIG-IP to fail to come up to a running state. Error messages will resemble the following: Jul 6 19:26:14 ip-10-0-0-104 err mcpd[22186]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: MCPProcessor::check_initialization: Jul 6 19:26:17 ip-10-0-0-104 err mcpd[22186]: 010717ff:3: [Licensing]: Failure in establishing instance identity.
bugs.conditions: Hourly instance in AWS with default tmm route added.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP VE will fail to fully start, rendering the instance unusable.
bugs.workaround: Temporary removal of default tmm route resolves this problem. The tmm route can be added back once MCPD is in the running state.
bugs.fix: The problem with default tmm route breaking Hourly licenses has been resolved. The default tmm route no longer affects the license check on Hourly billing Virtual Edition.

bugs.title: Case-sensitivity on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Case-sensitive setting of the default profile is saved in bigip.conf
bugs.conditions: Save button was pressed in GUI before upgrade.
bugs.impact: Upgrade failure.
bugs.workaround: Remove case-sensitive from bigip.conf manually.
bugs.fix: We fixed in GUI a Save issue that caused upgrade failure of the default profile.

bugs.title: False-Positive Phishing alert in Safari on iPad
bugs.symptoms: Very intermittent issue of false positive phishing alerts seen in alerts dashboard, all coming from ipads.
bugs.conditions: ipad accesses page with Websafe phishing protection.
bugs.impact: False positive phishing alert.
bugs.fix: Obfuscator updated to work around a bug in Apple's Safari javascript engine.

bugs.title: tmm can crash when the reply pkt to a service flow request is a DoS pkt
bugs.symptoms: tmm can crash
bugs.conditions: If a service flow (or any flow which does not have a listener) sends a request out and we get back a packet which needs to be counted towards a network DoS vector, it can cause the tmm to crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Don't configure AFM DoS vectors.
bugs.fix: A crash bug in DoS protection has been fixed.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Custom Signature Set Created via REST is Different Than When Created From GUI
bugs.symptoms: When importing a policy that utilizes a custom signature set, ASM checks whether that signature set is already exists on the system. If it does not exist, then it creates a new set. When a set is created via REST it does not correctly set an internal field that does get set via creation by the GUI or XML import. This causes unexpected behavior and extra signatures being created when a REST client, such as BIG-IQ, attempts to co-ordinate changes across devices utilizing import via XML and REST calls.
bugs.conditions: A Custom filter-based signature set is created by the GUI and then attached to a security policy. The security is exported in XML format. On a different device an identical signature set is created via REST. The security policy is then imported on that device.
bugs.impact: Extraneous signature sets are created, and false differences appear with regards to which signature sets are attached to which policies across multiple devices.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, custom filter-based signature sets should be created only via REST or only via GUI across multiple devices.
bugs.fix: Custom filter-based signature sets created using REST or the Configuration utility now have the same internal settings and match for XML security policy export/import.

bugs.title: Local Traffic Policy Rules Condition List select value to update with existing values.
bugs.symptoms: When viewing/editing Policy Rule, when selecting Conditions in the table, the Condition value is not updated with the existing values in the table.
bugs.conditions: A Policy with Rule(s) with defined Conditions where the Condition value is something other than the first value in the dropdown list, usually 'equals'. When a row in the table is selected, the Condition changes to the existing value in the table.
bugs.impact: This can cause confusion to the user when the values are not synchronized with the values in the table.
bugs.workaround: When the user saves, the original value is preserved. There is no adverse affect on the data other than it can be confusing.
bugs.fix: Local Traffic Policy Rules Condition List select value now updates along with existing values.

bugs.title: Machine Certificate Checker is not backward compatible with 11.4.1 (and below) when MatchFQDN rule is used
bugs.symptoms: Machine Certificate Checker (client side) is not backward compatible with BIG-IP 11.4.1 and earlier when MatchFQDN rule is used
bugs.conditions: Machine Certificate checker agent uses MatchFQDN rule in Access Policy of BIG-IP version 11.4.1 and earlier. New BIG-IP Edge Client (version greater than 11.4.1) is used against old BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Machine Certificate checker agent may fail. Policy goes wrong way.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue causing Machine Certificate checker agent backward incompatibility.

bugs.title: [LTM] [DNS] Maximum RTT value for nameserver cache still exists after nameserver cache is deleted
bugs.symptoms: If RTT value for nameserver cache reached the maximum value as 120000, even after executing 'delete ltm dns cache nameserver', BIG-IP still keeps the past maximum RTT value.
bugs.conditions: The RTT for the nameserver cache reached the maximum value of 120000.
bugs.impact: This can cause dns response failure.
bugs.workaround: Change size for nameserver-cache-count to reset the nameserver cache. # tmsh modify /ltm dns cache resolver my_dns_cache nameserver-cache-count 16536
bugs.fix: Maximum RTT value for nameserver cache is now deleted when the nameserver cache is deleted, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: SNMP passphrases appear to change each time they are displayed in TMSH
bugs.symptoms: When SNMPv3 users are configured with authentication and privacy passwords, the TMSH display of encrypted passwords appears to change at each redisplay.
bugs.conditions: Using TMSH to repeatedly display SNMPv3 user's encrypted authentication and privacy passwords.
bugs.impact: This makes it appear that the passwords are changing when only their encrypted representation has been updated, which might give incorrect information to monitoring systems that automatically detect configuration changes.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMSH display has been changed so that both the shallow encrypted and master key encrypted versions of the password display (the two keywords are auth-password/auth-password-encrypted and privacy-password/privacy-password-encrypted). This eliminates the issue of the SNMP passphrases appearing to change each time they are displayed in TMSH. To avoid triggering a false positive for configuration changes, monitoring systems should watch the auth-password and privacy-password values (not the deprecated -encrypted values). Note: The auth-password-encrypted and privacy-password-encrypted keywords have been deprecated but display for backwards compatibility.
bugs.behavior: TMSH display has been changed so that both the shallow encrypted and master key encrypted versions of the password display (the two keywords are auth-password/auth-password-encrypted and privacy-password/privacy-password-encrypted). The auth-password-encrypted and privacy-password-encrypted keywords have been deprecated but display for backwards compatibility. Note: To avoid triggering a false positive for configuration changes, monitoring systems should watch the auth-password and privacy-password values (not the deprecated -encrypted values).

bugs.title: Use of GTP Profile Requires Extended Protocols License
bugs.symptoms: Until this release, the requirement of acquiring a license for Extended Protocols to use the GTP protocol has not been enforced. After this release, that requirement will be enforced.
bugs.conditions: Usage of GTP Profile without Extended Protocols license
bugs.impact: Users will be unable to use GTP Profile without Extended Protocols License.

bugs.title: When FormBased SSO or SAML SSO are configured, tmm may restart at startup
bugs.symptoms: Under unlikely circumstances, tmm threads may run into synchronization issue at startup initialization, causing BIG-IP Failover
bugs.conditions: - SAML SSO or Form Based SSO are configured. - TMM is in process of starting (during reboot or for any other reason).
bugs.impact: Impact is BIG-IP will failover at start time. If tmm has successfully started - no further impact will be observed.
bugs.workaround: Remove Form Based SSO, and SAML objects from configuration.
bugs.fix: A thread synchronization issue that caused tmm startup issues has been fixed.

bugs.title: lsndb cores with "Assertion `size < bin_key_size' failed"
bugs.symptoms: When there are many entries in the session database and a user attempts to delete them with "lsndb del all", this can cause lsndb to core with "Assertion 'size < bin_key_size' failed". The user may see lots of "Error: Connection to internal DB failed (err: Cannot assign requested address [99])" messages displayed to the console. In addition not all of the session database entries will be deleted.
bugs.conditions: - LSN is configured with persistence, inbound-connections automatic, or PBA enabled. - There are over 100,000+ Session database entries (e.g. persistence, inbound, or PBA entries). - User attempts to manually delete all entries with "lsndb del all"
bugs.impact: - Session database cannot be properly cleared using the lsndb util.
bugs.fix: lsndb no longer cores while deleting large amounts of session database entries.

bugs.title: Client to log value of "SearchList" registry key.
bugs.conditions: Windows user connecting and disconnecting network access connection to BIG-IP APM server.
bugs.fix: To provide better traceability, APM client creates log entry each time F5 software reads or writes "SearchList" or "SearchList_F5_BACKUP_VALUE" registry keys.

bugs.title: IP reputation Spam Sources category is not enforced
bugs.symptoms: An IP address that is a spam source is not blocked or issues an alarm.
bugs.conditions: -- IP reputation is licensed and updated. -- The IP reputation feature is configured in the ASM.
bugs.impact: Traffic coming from an IP address of a spammer might get through ASM. Note that if the IP address has other IP reputation categories, it will be blocked.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can detect this category and issue a custom violation.
bugs.fix: This release adds the spam source category to the IP reputation feature.

bugs.title: Upgrade fails to 11.5.0 and later if 'defaults-from none' is under profile '/Common/clientssl'.
bugs.symptoms: If the client-ssl profile is /Common/clientssl, its parent profile is supposed to be /Common/clientssl. But the configuration could potentially use 'defaults-from none'.
bugs.conditions: This condition could be caused by executing the following command when generating the configuration. 'tmsh modify ltm profile client-ssl clientssl defaults-from none'
bugs.impact: The upgrade fails after booting into the new release, during the config loading phase. This occurs because the script extracts the line 'defaults-from none' and treats 'none' as its parent profile.
bugs.workaround: Edit the configuration prior to upgrading, changing the defaults-from value on the client-ssl profile to the name of that profile.
bugs.fix: Upgrade no longer fails if 'defaults-from none' is under profile '/Common/clientssl'.

bugs.title: PAC file download errors disconnect the tunnel
bugs.symptoms: Any failure to download PAC file is treated as fatal error. If edge client fails to download PAC file VPN connection cannot be established.
bugs.conditions: -PAC file cannot be downloaded by edge client
bugs.impact: Tunnel disconnects in case of PAC file download errors.
bugs.workaround: Fix infrastructure issues that result in PAC file download failure
bugs.fix: PAC file download and merging issues were considered critical before and Edge Client disconnects the tunnel. This behavior is controlled by a new setting called "Ignore PAC download error" on BIG-IP now.
bugs.behavior: PAC file download and merging issues were considered critical before and BIG-IP Edge Client disconnects the tunnel. This behavior is controlled by a new setting called "Ignore PAC download error" on BIG-IP now.

bugs.title: APM fails to handle compressed ICA file in integration mode
bugs.symptoms: Citrix application or desktop cannot be started in integration mode with Citrix StoreFront 3.0
bugs.conditions: APM is configured for StoreFront 3.0 proxy and HTTP compression is enabled on the StoreFront server.
bugs.impact: Citrix application or desktop cannot be started.
bugs.fix: Now APM supports Citrix StoreFront 3.0 in integration mode with HTTP compression enabled on the StoreFront server.

bugs.title: Static Link route to /32 pool member can end using dst broadcast MAC
bugs.symptoms: After assigning a static route to a node on a specific VLAN, ARPs are no longer generated, and all traffic to the node uses a broadcast (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff) MAC.
bugs.conditions: Static VLAN route to a poolmember/node with a /32 mask.
bugs.impact: This can cause the monitors to fail and the poolmember/node to be marked down.
bugs.workaround: Use a non /32 mask or use a gateway route instead.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly uses ARP to determine the destination MAC of a host routed via a /32 vlan route.

bugs.title: Changing from a standard virtual server to a FastHTTP server may stop processing traffic
bugs.symptoms: With a pre-existing Virtual Server, modifications that change from an L7 virtual to a FastHTTP virtual may stop processing traffic.
bugs.conditions: Using a standard virtual, switch to a FastHTTP virtual.
bugs.impact: The virtual stops processing traffic until a bigstart restart.
bugs.workaround: Perform a bigstart restart.

bugs.title: [GTM] ZRD cannot create reverse zones for stub, slave and forward zones
bugs.symptoms: ZRD cannot create reverse zones for zone types stub, slave, and forward (that is, zone types other than Master).
bugs.conditions: Creating zone for ZRD with zone types other than Master.
bugs.impact: Cannot create reverse zones. This is as-designed behavior: reverse zones must include SOA and NS records, which are only available for Master zones.

bugs.title: Some HTTP commands fail validation when it is in a proc and the proc is called from another proc
bugs.symptoms: The following HTTP commands fail validation: HTTP::uri HTTP:version HTTP::header HTTP::method Validation fails with the following error: HTTP::uri command in a proc in rule (<the rule>) under event at virtual-server (<the virtual>) does not satisfy cmd/event/profile requirement.
bugs.conditions: Command is in a proc and the proc is called from another proc.
bugs.impact: Config load fails.
bugs.workaround: Directly call the proc from an iRule, instead of from the proc.
bugs.fix: The HTTP::uri, HTTP:version, HTTP::header, HTTP::method HTTP commands now pass validation when they are in a proc and the proc is called from another proc.

bugs.title: Setting 'Untrusted Certificate Response Control' to ignore in server SSL profile does not ignore self-signed untrusted certificates.
bugs.symptoms: Setting 'Untrusted Certificate Response Control' to ignore in server SSL profile does not ignore self-signed untrusted certificates.
bugs.conditions: In server SSL profiles with 'Untrusted Certificate Response Control' set to ignore. When backend server sends self-signed untrusted certificate.
bugs.impact: The ltm log displays this error: Peer cert verify error: unable to verify the first certificate.
bugs.fix: Ignore X509_V_ERR_UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE certificate validation error message when serverssl profile sets 'Untrusted Certificate Response Control' to ignore.

bugs.title: No validation error attempting to modify a record in an external data-group using iControl SOAP.
bugs.symptoms: As a result of changes to data-groups between versions 10.x and 11.x, external data-groups are not allowed to have modified records. This was fixed in tmsh, but not propagated to iControl SOAP.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to modify a record in an external data-group using iControl SOAP.
bugs.impact: No validation error.

bugs.title: Traffic capture filter not catching all relevant transactions
bugs.symptoms: The traffic capture filter does not catch all relevant transactions.
bugs.conditions: When a traffic capture filter is set.
bugs.impact: Not all relevant transactions are captured.
bugs.fix: The traffic capture filter now catches all relevant transactions.

bugs.title: Several "Standard MIB" OIDs were not supported correctly
bugs.symptoms: Certain OIDs in the IP-MIB, IF-MIB and Etherlike-MIB were either not supported by the Big-IP, or the returned MIB query data related to the interface index (IfIndex) was incorrect or inconsistent with the IfIndex returned by the IF-MIB::ifTable.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions.
bugs.impact: Customer could not relate interface data from one MIB table to another.

bugs.title: TMM may core on resuming iRule if the underlying flow has been deleted.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core on resuming iRule if the underlying flow has been deleted.
bugs.conditions: A flow is deleted (RST from the other end is one way) while an iRule operating on that flow is parked. On resumption, the iRule accesses freed memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use iRules that may cause parking.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores on resuming iRule if the underlying flow has been deleted.

bugs.title: tmsh config file merge may fail when AFM security log profile is present in merged file
bugs.symptoms: A config file merge into an existing config may fail with "unknown-property" message.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when you are doing a config file merge. The error encountered was with a parameter called "built-in enabled".
bugs.impact: All releases and modules are affected.
bugs.workaround: The offending parameter may be deleted from the merge file, however this may result in the value for the deleted parameter not set correctly in the existing config.
bugs.fix: Fixed a problem with tmsh config file merge failing when AFM security log profile is present in merged file.

bugs.title: Increasing memory usage due to continual creation of authentication tokens
bugs.symptoms: The AuthTokenWorker creates new indexed state objects. Some are unable to be deleted because they are shared between instances. Generations of tokens build up, however the generational scavenger only runs when disk space is tight. Restjavad can run out of memory before the scavenger ever gets to run.
bugs.conditions: Tokens shared between instances
bugs.impact: Generations of tokens build up
bugs.fix: Add another trigger to the generational scavenger such that it also triggers when memory is tight as well as when disk space is tight.

bugs.title: Display 'description' for port list members
bugs.symptoms: Descriptions for port list's members are not displayed in GUI
bugs.conditions: Create a port list with 'description' set for its members (using tmsh). When the portlist list page is accessed from GUI, the description set for the members (on tmsh) is not displayed.
bugs.impact: Users will not be able to see the description
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to view the description for portlist members on tmsh
bugs.fix: Descriptions for port list members are now displayed in the GUI.

bugs.title: tmm crash with assert "resume on different script"
bugs.symptoms: In a rare race condition involving stalled server-side TCP connections on which a RST is received and a asynchronously executing client-side iRule for event CLIENT_CLOSED the tmm can crash with assert "resume on different script".
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this assert/crash is triggered are hard to reproduce.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid asynchronously executing CLIENT_CLOSED iRules (e.g. those that use 'after' or 'table' or 'session' commands - this is not an exhaustive list).
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes with assert "resume on different script"

bugs.title: sessiondump is not reusing connections
bugs.symptoms: sessiondump opens a TCP connection to TMM. It really only needs to make one connection, but it was actually making one connection for each request. This is visible in a packet capture or by monitoring the number of sockets left in TIME_WAIT state On a box that had 1000 sessions, a little over 1000 sockets were generated by the sessiondump call: # netstat -a | grep memcache | grep TIME_WAIT | wc 3 18 267 # sessiondump --allkeys 1> /dev/null # netstat -a | grep memcache | grep TIME_WAIT | wc 1054 6324 93806
bugs.conditions: This issue is most relevant when BZ511900 is present. That fix improved sessiondump performance by eliminating the amount of process forking. The connection reuse problem isn't really a visible problem until after that. BZ 511900 was included in 12.0 BZ 533422 (this bug) was included with 12.1 So relevant to all 12.0 customers and to 11.x customers that request a hotfix with BZ 511900
bugs.impact: The extra connections have a minor throughput impact, because of the cost of establishing TCP 3WHS. The more important impact is that on a large system (around 20k sessions or more), this will be creating a lot of sockets in a very short period of time. These sockets go into TIME_WAIT and are not immediately reusable. The box could run out of sockets and sessiondump will exit.
bugs.fix: The sessiondump utility now reuses the TCP connections.

bugs.title: Insufficient data for determining cause of HSB lockup.
bugs.symptoms: When an HSB lockup occurs only the HSB registers are dumped into the TMM log files for diagnosing the failure. There is no core file containing stats and the state of the HSB driver when the failure occurred to help diagnose the failure.
bugs.conditions: When an HSB lockup occurs.
bugs.impact: There is limited data is available for root cause analysis.
bugs.fix: On HSB lockup, the system now generate a core file, which contains stats and the state of the HSB driver when the failure occurred to help diagnose the failure.

bugs.title: Core file may be overwritten.
bugs.symptoms: Core file might be overwritten, removing useful information to determine a RCA for the initial event.
bugs.conditions: -- A tmm, bigd, or mcpd core file exists. -- A process occurs that results in a new core file being generated.
bugs.impact: The previously created core file is overwritten. Unable to provide F5 with a useful core for RCA.
bugs.fix: You can now use new tmsh command under sys core to configure the BIG-IP system to not overwrite existing tmm, bigd, or mcpd core files, and instead create multiple core files, or skip creation of the core file.

bugs.title: qkview crash
bugs.symptoms: Qkview may crash or hang. You might see this error message in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[8003]: 0107134e:3: Failed while making snapshot: (Failed to link files existing(/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/...
bugs.conditions: Changing large configurations while running qkview or missing files from the /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/external_monitor_d directory can cause qkview to crash or hang.
bugs.impact: You will be unable to generate a qkview file for support.
bugs.workaround: Make sure any iControl scripts that are making changes are allowed to complete. If you deleted any external monitor files from /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d, restore the external-monitor file and re-run qkview.
bugs.fix: The system now handles running qkview while creating 20,000 or more pools or removing an external monitor from the /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/external_monitor_d directory, so these conditions no longer cause qkview crash or hang issues.

bugs.title: Data plane Listener summary does not show LSN translation correctly
bugs.symptoms: When configuring a new data plane virtual server group, and CGNAT is licensed, you have the ability to select an address translation value of LSN, and then select an LSN pool. This is accepted and configured correctly, but when viewing the data plane group after this point, the address translation type shows as "{{renderSnatValue(listenerVs}}", and should show as "LSN"
bugs.conditions: Create a CGNAT LSN pool. Create a new PEM data plane listener, set the address translation to LSN, select the pool, save, then view the resulting group summary .
bugs.impact: Data plane Listener summary does not show LSN translation correctly
bugs.fix: Correct the UI so that it handles the LSN address translation type correctly.

bugs.title: Memory leak in CGNAT can result in crash
bugs.symptoms: tmm leaks cmp memory, resulting in crash. 'tmctl memory_usage_stat' reports very high cmp memory utilization.
bugs.conditions: Configure hairpin mode or inbound connection handling set to automatic.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system might run out of memory and crash.
bugs.workaround: Avoid hairpin mode or inbound connection handling set to automatic.
bugs.fix: Fixed CGNAT memory leak that occurred when configured for hairpin mode or when inbound connection handling is set to automatic.

bugs.title: Support for View HTML5 client v3.5 shipped with VCS 6.2
bugs.symptoms: The upcoming release of VMware Horizon View Connection Server 6.2 introduces a few changes to the View HTML5 client. This fix catches up with those changes to provide seamless support at APM side.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM configured as PCoIP proxy and set up against VMware VCS 6.2 with HTML5 client installed.
bugs.impact: Launching View HTML5 client from APM webtop may not work properly.
bugs.fix: Added support for View HTML5 client v3.5 shipped with View Connection Server 6.2.

bugs.title: DNS decision logging can trigger TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Applying load balance decision logging to the DNS profile can cause TMM to crash when a query is load balanced to a last resort pool that is unavailable.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS logging is enabled and log profile set on the DNS profile. -- A Wide IP is configured with a last resort pool. -- The last resort pool is unavailable. -- A query is load balanced to the last resort pool.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable decision logging for the DNS profile, or discontinue use of the last resort pool feature.
bugs.fix: DNS decision logging no longer causse TMM to crash when a last resort pool is configured for a Wide IP, that last resort pool is unavailable, and a query is load balanced to that last resort pool.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Client side HTML rewriter should not rewrite content within "textarea" tag.
bugs.symptoms: The client-side HTML rewriter rewrites content within the "textarea" tag.
bugs.conditions: Web-application dynamically creates HTML content on the client side that contains the textarea tag.
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction is possible.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time
bugs.fix: Content rewriting is suppressed on the client side for the textarea tag.

bugs.title: DHCPv6 packets arriving via tunnel are not forwarded to backend server on VIPRION
bugs.symptoms: Packet traces show DHCPv6 packets arriving via IPv6/IPv4 tunnel, are forwarded to the VIP but the packet is not forwarded to the backend server on VIPRION devices.
bugs.conditions: DHCPv6 packets arriving via IPv6/IPv4 tunnel interface on a multi-bladed VIPRION system.
bugs.impact: The DHCP packet is not forwarded to the backend server.
bugs.workaround: Use a single-bladed system.
bugs.fix: The system now processes DHCP packets on the local blade instead of dropping them, if those packets come from a tunnel interface.

bugs.title: Required syntax for iRule command DIAMETER::avp create has changed
bugs.symptoms: When saving an iRule which uses 'DIAMETER::avp create', if the command does not have a 'type' argument then a validation warning will be issued. In previous versions, this argument was optional.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when calls to 'DIAMETER::avp create' do not provide a 'type' argument.
bugs.impact: Behavior of the command itself has not changed, and iRules using it will continue to function as expected. This is a change only in the validation of the command.
bugs.workaround: Review all iRules and ensure that calls to 'DIAMETER::avp create' provide a 'type' argument.
bugs.behavior: When saving an iRule which uses 'DIAMETER::avp create', if the command does not have a 'type' argument then a validation warning will be issued. In previous versions, this argument was optional. Behavior of the command itself has not changed, and iRules using it will continue to function as expected. This is a change only in the validation of the command. You should review all iRules and ensure that calls to 'DIAMETER::avp create' provide a 'type' argument.

bugs.title: Creating multiple address entries in data-group might result in records being incorrectly deleted
bugs.symptoms: Using the GUI to create multiple address entries in data-group might result in records being incorrectly deleted
bugs.conditions: Creating multiple address entries in data-group
bugs.impact: Cannot add/remove IP addresses from existing data groups without affecting existing IP addresses through GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to add/remove IP addresses from existing data groups.
bugs.fix: You can now use the GUI to add/remove IP addresses from a data-group IP address list without affecting other IP addresses.

bugs.title: Unable to create new rule for virtual server if order is set to "before"/"after"
bugs.symptoms: Not able to create a new rule for virtual server when the order is set to "before"/"after".
bugs.conditions: Happens only when the order is set to "before"/"after"
bugs.impact: Unable to create a new rule from the virtual server page

bugs.title: Internal Virtual Server in partition fails to load from saved config
bugs.symptoms: Loading a successfully configured internal Virtual Server from the config fails with the following message: -- 01070712:3: Values (/part2/0.0.0.0%2) specified for Virtual Server (/part2/ICAP_request): foreign key index (name_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- You are running a BIG-IP system with no configuration. -- You have created an external VLAN with an interface. -- You have created a non-default route domain, and associated it with a newly created VLAN. -- You have created a virtual server, and configured a pool in a partition other than /Common. -- You have saved the configuration. Here is an example of how this might occur. Run the following commands. - tmsh - create net vlan external interfaces add { 1.2 } - create net route-domain 2 vlans add { external } - create auth partition part2 default-route-domain 2 - cd ../part2 - create ltm pool icap_pool members add { 10.10.10.10:8080 } - create ltm virtual ICAP_request destination 0.0.0.0:0 mask 0.0.0.0 internal ip-protocol tcp profiles add { tcp } pool icap_pool - save sys config - load sys config partitions all verify.
bugs.impact: The operation creates a virtual server but cannot load it from saved config.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can use the Common partition to complete the configuration.
bugs.fix: You can now configure an internal virtual server in a partition and load the config successfully.

bugs.title: DNS Cache response missing additional section
bugs.symptoms: Resolver cache lookups are missing authority and additional sections.
bugs.conditions: Resolver cache lookups could be missing the authority and additional sections for A and AAAA queries if the DO bit is also not set.
bugs.impact: If the requesting client needs the information that would normally be included in the authority or additional sections, it would have to make additional queries to acquire that data.
bugs.fix: The resolver cache now correctly includes the information available for the authority and additional sections if the information is available.

bugs.title: SNMP Memory Leak on a VIPRION system.
bugs.symptoms: The snmpd image increases in size on a VIPRION system.
bugs.conditions: Run continuous snmpbulkwalk operations.
bugs.impact: The snmpd image increases, and might eventually result in a crash. The ltm log might contain an error message similar to the following: err mcpd[7061]: 01071087:3: Killed process for snmpd as current count of messages (965505855) keeps building.
bugs.workaround: To reset the memory usage and stop the snmpd daemon from coring, run the following command: bigstart restart snmpd.
bugs.fix: The snmpd image no longer increases in size on a VIPRION system processor.

bugs.title: Extra Proxy on Image Size Change
bugs.symptoms: Using AAM with image optimization, if an image which is large enough to be stored in datastor is replaced with one that is small enough to fit into the small object cache, AAM will proxy to the OWS one additional time before starting to serve the image from cache.
bugs.conditions: AAM, image optimization, and a change in image size on the OWS.
bugs.impact: One additional proxy after the larger image is replaced with the smaller one.

bugs.title: PEM::subscriber info irule command can cause tmm core
bugs.symptoms: Running an irule script that contains the PEM::subscriber info command can result in a tmm core. If the command runs synchronously, the core will not be observed.
bugs.conditions: The core occurs only if the PEM::subscriber info command runs asynchronously.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: PEM::subscriber info commands no longer cause tmm to core.

bugs.title: Portal Access: Space-like characters in EUC character sets may be handled incorrectly.
bugs.symptoms: Extended Unix Code (EUC) character sets include several white space characters which have no ASCII equivalents. These characters are not recognized as white spaces by Portal Access. This may lead to incorrect handling of HTML pages, XML files and/or JavaScript files in these character sets.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page, XML file or JavaScript file in any EUC encoding scheme (EUC-JP, for example).
bugs.impact: Page or file in EUC encoding scheme may not be parsed correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to replace non-ASCII compatible white space characters by ordinal spaces.
bugs.fix: Now text content using EUC character encoding schemes is handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: Double loopback nexthop release might cause TMM core.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might restart after logging an 'Assertion "nexthop ref valid" failed' message.
bugs.conditions: Traffic is sent from one tmm to a tunnel in another tmm, but the tunnel does not exist.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a TMM crash due to an extra loopback nexthop release.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Server-side URL parser does not recognize URLs with HTML entities in scheme part
bugs.symptoms: Not rewritten URLs in HTML.
bugs.conditions: HTML with URLs which contains HTML entities in scheme part
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The APM Portal Access Rewrite URL parser has been improved to handle conditions where HTML entities are present in the scheme part of a URL.

bugs.title: Memory leak while running some of PEM::session and PEM::subscriber commands.
bugs.symptoms: When running an irule that has PEM::session info commands, it was observed that the memory consumption by the PEM module kept going up till and the system eventually ran out of memory.
bugs.conditions: Create an irule that has PEM::session info commands that run asynchronously and attach it to one of the virtuals in use.
bugs.impact: System runs out of memory.
bugs.fix: The memory leak while executing the commands - <PEM::session info /PEM::subscriber info/PEM::session config policy/PEM::subscriber config policy> has been fixed. The leak only occurs when these commands run asynchronously.

bugs.title: HA on AWS uses default AWS endpoint (EC2_URL).
bugs.symptoms: HA doesn't work on Government clouds on AWS.
bugs.conditions: AWS endpoints for government clouds are different compared to their public offerings. Amazon recommendation is to construct the end-point (EC2_URL) dynamically based on: [<service name>.<region>.<services/domain>] construct.
bugs.impact: HA doesn't work on Government clouds on AWS.
bugs.workaround: EC2 endpoint can be constructed dynamically by: - Query EC2 Metadata service for <DOMAIN> name (curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/services/domain) - Read the instance <REGION> from /shared/vadc/aws/iid-document - Declare global variable EC2_URL by using above two values in following format: export EC2_URL="http://ec2.<REGION>.<DOMAIN>"
bugs.fix: BIG-IP HA on AWS dynamically constructs the EC2 service endpoint based on the domain-name and region attached with the running instance.

bugs.title: VLAN failsafe triggering on standby leaks memory
bugs.symptoms: Memory is leaked when VLAN failsafe is active and sending ICMP probes.
bugs.conditions: VLAN failsafe active and sending ICMP probes on standby and configured with failsafe-action failover.
bugs.impact: Memory leak causing aggressive sweeper and eventually TMM crash on standby.
bugs.fix: Memory is no longer leaked when VLAN failsafe is active and sending ICMP probes.

bugs.title: [JavaPatcher] Java Applet class methods not properly implemented
bugs.symptoms: Three F5 Java class methods, getImage(), getAudioClip(), and play(), cannot take more than one parameters.
bugs.conditions: F5 Java class methods not properly implemented.
bugs.impact: Backend video cannot be played.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround specific to the backend web app available upon request.

bugs.title: SNMP configured trap-source might not be used in v1 snmp traps.
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, SNMP v1 traps with configured trap-source might fail to use the configured address, and will use the default management port IP address instead.
bugs.conditions: - SNMP v1 traps and destination configured. - trap-source configured.
bugs.impact: Traps will have the incorrect agent-addr set, and SNMP configured trap-source might not be used.
bugs.fix: SNMP v1 traps now correctly use the configured trap-source.

bugs.title: [SSL] Config sync problems when modifying cert in default client-ssl profile
bugs.symptoms: Config sync problems after modifying cert in default client-ssl profile when the profile is already active and in use on members in a high availability configuration.
bugs.conditions: Modify cert in default client-ssl profile and perform a config sync operation.
bugs.impact: After config sync, units in the sync group have different cert/key settings for client-ssl profiles. You can see this in the inherit-certkeychain setting, which changes from 'true' to 'false' after syncing the configuration with the changed default value.
bugs.workaround: 1. Remove client-ssl definitions from bigip.conf on each unit. 2. Reload the config. 3. Synchronize the config.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly syncs the default client-ssl profile that was modified with a new cert and key, so the active and standby unit configurations now have the correct cert/key settings after config sync.

bugs.title: Passphrase protected signing keys are not supported by SAML IDP/SP
bugs.symptoms: Signing operation may fail if the BIG-IP system is used as a SAML Identity Provider or Service Provider and is configured to use passphrase-protected signing keys.
bugs.conditions: Private key used to perform digital signing operations is passphrase protected.
bugs.impact: SAML protocol will not function properly due to inability to sign messages.
bugs.workaround: To work around the problem, remove the passphrase from the signing key.

bugs.title: rest_uuid should be calculated from the actual values inserted to the entity
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP computes the case-sensitive rest_uuid values for HTTP headers but stores the headers as case-insensitive.
bugs.conditions: This is an example: 1. Go to Security>>Application Security>>Headers>>HTTP Headers. 2. Choose 'Custom...' for the name of the header. 3. Create a custom header as follows use name 'Abc' with Capital letter. 4. Remember the ID generated in the JSON element. 5. Delete the header. 6. Create a new custom header and use the name 'abc'. Actual Results: The ID of 'abc' and the ID of 'Abc' are different.
bugs.impact: Two identical normalized values may have different rest_uuid.
bugs.fix: The REST "id" field is now calculated from the actual values inserted to the entity, and not on the user-input values.

bugs.title: Issue a Body in Get sub violation for GET request with content type header
bugs.symptoms: A GET request without payload but with payload indication doesn't issue the body in get violation.
bugs.conditions: A Get request without payload arrives. The request has a content type header although there is no payload.
bugs.impact: A suspicious request goes by undetected.
bugs.workaround: Add an iRule that removes this request from the ASM and issues a custom violation.
bugs.fix: A GET request without payload but with content type header will issue the body in GET sub violation.

bugs.title: Live update with moving config breaks password-less ssh access
bugs.symptoms: Authorized_keys file changed with link to /var/ssh/admin/authorized_keys but file in /var/ssh/... not created.
bugs.conditions: Use clean tmos-bugs-staging based VM. Do Live install. Do change boot location via GUI with 'Install Configuration' = 'Yes'
bugs.impact: breaks password-less ssh access
bugs.workaround: If save and load sys ucs before live install then file will be created in /var/.. and successfully moved to new volume.

bugs.title: Tab completion for ltm policy-strategy shows extra values
bugs.symptoms: In tmsh, when making changes to ltm policy-strategy, tab completion displays extra suggested completions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when tmsh user is in the ltm policy-strategy area and presses the Tab key.
bugs.impact: Additional parameters which are not pertinent to the ltm policy-strategy operation will be displayed, which might lead to trial-and-error to successfully complete the operation.
bugs.fix: Tab completion for ltm policy-strategy correctly displays valid operands.

bugs.title: Session will be replaced rather than re-created when we update a new IP addr along with the existing IP addr.
bugs.symptoms: Session will be deleted and re-created when we update a new IP addr along with the original IP addr in the session.
bugs.conditions: It happens when we try to update a new IP addr with the existing IP addr for an existing session.
bugs.impact: Session replaced when updating a new IP along with the existing IP address.
bugs.fix: Session will be replaced rather than re-created when we update a new IP addr along with the existing IP addr.

bugs.title: Some Text on French Localized Edge client on windows has grammatical error
bugs.symptoms: Grammatically incorrect text is displayed in Edge Client UI localized for French language.
bugs.conditions: French Localized version of Edge Client is used.
bugs.impact: Branding.
bugs.fix: Fixed grammar.

bugs.title: CRLDP AAA server in non-default partition uses self-ip in default partition with strict isolation
bugs.symptoms: CRLDP AAA server connection is made on the default interface which may not be part of the requesting partition.
bugs.conditions: A CRLDP resource is configured in a non-default partition and strict isolation is enabled.
bugs.impact: The CRLDP request is sent on the default interface for the box. If the AAA server is reachable from that interface there is no adverse impact.

bugs.title: Dynamically discovered routes might fail to remirror connections.
bugs.symptoms: When using dynamic routing, it's possible that L4 connections fail to remirror after a restart on the standby device. Initial mirroring works as expected, but remirroring might not work.
bugs.conditions: Using dynamic routes and mirroring, and either the active or standby restarts. If the active restarts, failover completes correctly, but connections might not remirror to the previously active device after it comes back online.
bugs.impact: Dynamically discovered routes might fail to remirror connections. One-way failover, similar to L7 virtual servers. Initial failover works as expected; subsequent failovers might drop connections.
bugs.workaround: Provide a static route instead of dynamic routes.
bugs.fix: Remirroring L4 connections using dynamic routes works correctly. (Note that when using dynamic routes it is not guaranteed that the active and standby systems will use the same routes; if the same routing is required on both active and standby fails over, there might be some dropped connections.)

bugs.title: SIP monitor marks down member if response has different whitespace in header fields.
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances the SIP monitor may incorrectly mark a SIP pool member down. This is due to the comparison the monitor makes of the standard header fields in the SIP monitor request to the response.
bugs.conditions: SIP monitor and response differ in the use of whitespace in the header fields, for example, 'field:value' and 'field: value'.
bugs.impact: Unable to monitor the SIP pool member accurately using the standard SIP monitor because the pool member will be marked down.
bugs.workaround: Use other types of monitors, e.g., UDP.
bugs.fix: SIP monitor now correctly processes monitor responses when the use of whitespace in header fields differ.

bugs.title: Collecting DoS stats using iControl REST doesn't work when the stat in question has a space in its name.
bugs.symptoms: Collecting DoS stats using iControl REST doesn't work when the stat in question has a space in its name.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl REST to collect DoS stats.
bugs.impact: Failure to obtain desired stats.

bugs.title: Dependency on Adobe Flash removed from the BIG IP Dashboard
bugs.symptoms: Adobe Flash technology has inherent security issues and due to the approaching EOL, it became necessary to remove the dependency of Adobe Flash from the BIG-IP Dashboard.
bugs.conditions: This is an existing feature in BIG-IP which uses Adobe Flash
bugs.impact: Adobe Flash has security issues which, after EOL of the software, may cause issues.
bugs.workaround: Because the Dashboard has a dependency on Flash technology, there is no workaround other than not to use the Dashboard.
bugs.fix: Dashboard is no longer dependent on the Flash technology, and has been replaced with a more modern GUI which does not use Flash technology.

bugs.title: Fixed TMM crash when iRule configuration is modified.
bugs.symptoms: iRule configuration modification may result in TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: When iRule configuration is modified.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed TMM crash when iRule configuration is modified.

bugs.title: qkview may exclude certain log files from /var/log
bugs.symptoms: After generating a qkview, the tmm.start log file is missing.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently while generating a qkview.
bugs.impact: Certain key log files that might be needed for troubleshooting are missing from the qkview.
bugs.fix: After generating a qkview, the tmm.start log file is now present.

bugs.title: HA configuration may fail over when standby has only base configuration loaded.
bugs.symptoms: The active unit may fail over when only the base configuration is loaded on a standby system, and HA communications in the HA configuration is interrupted.
bugs.conditions: Only base configuration loaded on standby and HA communications are disrupted.
bugs.impact: Potential site outage.
bugs.workaround: Configure HA to use multiple network interfaces. Avoid loading only the base configuration on HA configurations.
bugs.fix: HA configuration no longer fails over when a standby system has only the base configuration loaded.

bugs.title: Upgrade BIND to address CVE 2015-5477
bugs.symptoms: See SOL https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/16000/900/sol16909.html for complete information. BIND will issue a REQUIRE assert and exit under certain conditions. It will automatically be restarted by bigstart.
bugs.conditions: A deliberately constructed packet can exploit an error in the handling of queries for TKEY records, permitting denial of service.
bugs.impact: DNS resolutions that are answered by the on box BIND server may be interrupted.
bugs.workaround: Please see F5 Solution SOL16909.
bugs.fix: BIND was upgraded, which addresses this vulnerability. F5 is less vulnerable than the industry rating due to system design.

bugs.title: Disabling a renamed pool member removes member from pool.
bugs.symptoms: Disabling a renamed pool member removes member from pool.
bugs.conditions: Must set db variable mcpd.mvenabled to true.
bugs.impact: Unpredictable behavior; missing configuration.
bugs.workaround: Restart mcpd after rename and save.

bugs.title: Deleting APM virtual server produces ERR_NOT_FOUND error
bugs.symptoms: When a APM virtual server is deleted on the active, the following error message will be seen in the APM log on the standby. "Failed to delete profile stats namespaces"
bugs.conditions: This issue happens when a APM virtual is deleted on the active and the change is subsequently synced to the standby
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact.
bugs.fix: Access Filter now ignores the ERR_NOT_FOUND error when deleting the profile stats namespace.

bugs.title: Swapping VLAN names in config results in switch daemon core and restart.
bugs.symptoms: Changing names of configured VLANs directly in the configuration file and reloading results in a bcm56xxd switch daemon core and restart.
bugs.conditions: Applies to all switch based platforms, when modifying the VLAN names directly in the configuration file and reloading.
bugs.impact: Switch daemon drops core, restarts, and reconfigures the switch.
bugs.workaround: First delete any existing VLANs, and then recreate then with new names.
bugs.fix: Add additional protection and error logging for VLAN-name- and VLAN-ID-lookup failures in the switch daemon.

bugs.title: TMM may core with rate limiting enabled and service-down-action reselect on poolmembers
bugs.symptoms: TMM may produce a core file when calculating the rate limit in certain circumstances.
bugs.conditions: VIP/pool configuration contains: - Pool configured with + Action On Service Down is set to Reselect - Pool members configured with + Connection Rate Limit is set If all pool members go down, this can trigger the core
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove rate limit configuration.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores in certain conditions with rate limiting and service-down-action reselect on poolmembers

bugs.title: Incorrect key/certificate when creating clientSSL profile and modifying key/cert in the same transaction.
bugs.symptoms: Creating clientSSL profile and modifying key and/or certificate in the same transaction causes the profile to be created with incorrect key and/or certificate. This has impact on clientSSL profile creation using iApp.
bugs.conditions: - Start a transaction. - Create a clientSSL profile and mention any desired 'defaults-from'profile. - Modify key and/or cert - End transaction Or Use iApp for creating clientSSL profile with key/cert different from the defaults.
bugs.impact: clientSSL profile is created with the wrong key/cert.
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed so that the right key/cert is associated with the clientSSL profile when transactions or iApps are used.

bugs.title: AFM Security checks were not being done for DNS over TCP
bugs.symptoms: We had disabled DNS Query Filtering and DNS DoS checks for DNS over TCP.
bugs.conditions: DNS over TCP and either DNS DoS configured or DNS Query filtering configured.
bugs.impact: Query Filtering and DNS DoS feature was not present for DNS over TCP.
bugs.workaround: Use DNS over UDP.
bugs.fix: We have now enabled DNS Query filtering and DNS DoS checks regardless of the L4 protocol.

bugs.title: When using session tickets, the session id sent might be incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances, when SSL session is resumed using session tickets, the BIG-IP system might send an incorrect session id.
bugs.conditions: Session tickets are enabled.
bugs.impact: The session id sent might be incorrect
bugs.workaround: Do not enable session tickets.
bugs.fix: When using session tickets, the session id sent is now correct.

bugs.title: VMware View HTML5 client may load/initialize with delays
bugs.symptoms: When HTML5 client is used to access VMware View remote desktops, it may sometimes take about 30 seconds to initialize.
bugs.conditions: APM Webtop with a VMware View remote desktop assigned available for HTML5 client launch.
bugs.impact: Slow HTML5 client initialization.
bugs.workaround: - Go to admin UI -> Local Traffic -> Profiles: Services: HTTP and create new http profile. - Set Unchunk (or Rechunk) for "Response Chunking" option and save it. - Assign this http profile to the Virtual Server.
bugs.fix: Fixed the handling of chunked responses coming during the HTML5 client load.

bugs.title: Allow swapping of vlan names in config for switch based platforms
bugs.symptoms: Reloading of config with prior vlan names swapped, was not allowed by bcm56xxd and resulted in an error message being logged.
bugs.conditions: Reload a config file where the names of existing vlans are being swapped.
bugs.impact: Swapping of preexisting vlan names were not handled correctly on switch based platforms.
bugs.workaround: Modify the tag for one of the pair of configured vlans, whose names are being swapped, to a different tag and save the config. Modify the config with just the names swapped and original vlan tags and reload the config.
bugs.fix: Allow the switch daemon to handle the swapping of vlan names for a pair of configured vlans.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system drops UDP packets while iRule is suspended
bugs.symptoms: Any virtual server with UDP profile executing iRule using parking command such as table set. The BIG-IP system drops all UDP packets received while waiting for iRule execution to be completed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using iRules containing a parking command in virtual server with UDP profiles. For more information on iRules that suspend processing, see SOL12962: Some iRule commands temporarily suspend iRule processing at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/12000/900/sol12962.html
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system drops all UDP packets until iRule execution is completed.
bugs.workaround: Enable datagram-load-balancing in UDP profile associated with the virtual server. It will aggregate flows and process them in parallel based on the timeout setting.

bugs.title: Connections to LSN pools in PBA mode may cause tmm core if used in conjunction with udp_gtm_dns profile.
bugs.symptoms: LSN configured in PBA mode can cause tmm to core if a connection needs to obtain resources from a remote tmm process. This occurs most frequently during heavy load or when there is a small translation space(low number of translation addresses) configured on the PBA lsnpool.
bugs.conditions: - LSN with PBA mode configured. - udp_gtm_dns profile configured on the virtual server handling traffic. - Heavy traffic or small translation space.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove udp_gtm_dns profile from the virtual server, and replace it with fast L4.
bugs.fix: LSN pool configured with PBA mode no longer crashes with heavy load and udp_gtm_dns profile configured.

bugs.title: APM log tables initial rotation in MySQL may be wrong
bugs.symptoms: APM uses local MySQL to store logs and automatically rotate the log tables when the log table size exceeds a limit, which removes the oldest log table and make room for a new current log table. However, the initial timestamps of those log tables may be very close--or the same in 1-second granularity of MySQL timestamps--right after the installation that initially creates those log tables. Due to the timestamp granularity, it may be wrong for APM to choose the oldest log table to remove in the first round of rotation, resulting in removal of log data that are not the oldest. After the first rotation, the log table rotation should work as normal.
bugs.conditions: The first round of log table rotation after installation
bugs.impact: Log data that are not the oldest may be removed at the first round of log table rotation.

bugs.title: [tmsh/iCRD/GUI] Do not automatically add extensions to SSL key/cert/crl/csr file objects
bugs.symptoms: Using iControl REST's process (iCRD) with 'sys crypto' always fails, and the GUI does not work with SSL file objects created without extensions using tmsh (with 'sys file') during the create process.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating SSL certificates/keys/CRL/CSR objects using iControl (with 'sys crypto') or tmsh (with 'sys file'). -- Specifying the file extension associated with the object: .crt/.key/.crl/.csr.
bugs.impact: The system creates a file with two extensions, for example, specifying the filename csrname.crt creates a file named csrname.crt.csr in folder /config/ssl/ssl.csr/. -- Using iCRD with 'sys crypto' fails. -- The BIG-IP GUI exhibits the following behavior: + Inconsistently manages those files improperly. + May return errors (e.g., 'An error has occurred while trying to process your request.' or 'No certificate.'). + May confuse two objects (e.g., 'web-server' and 'web-server.crt'). + GUI cannot create an archive (System :: File Management : SSL Certificate List :: Archive) containing one of these files, and reports an error similar to the following: Key management library returned bad status: -2, Not Found.
bugs.workaround: When creating SSL-related file objects via tmsh 'sys file' or iCRD with 'sys crypto', do include a file extension (.crt/.key/.crl/.csr) in the object name, even if it is the extension associated with the type of object. This is because the system explicitly adds the appropriate file extension during the create operation for ('sys crypto') but does not add extensions for ('sys file').
bugs.fix: tmsh, iCRD, and GUI no longer implicitly add extensions to key/cert/csr/crl file objects to create/query/delete commands. The system will use the exact name/label specified during the create operation.
bugs.behavior: tmsh, iControl REST daemon (iCRD), and the GUI no longer implicitly adds extensions to key/cert/csr/crl file objects when using create/query/delete commands, and the system will use the exact name/label specified. For example, if you specify the name 'test' when using tmsh, iCRD, or the GUI to create a key and a certificate, the system will create the key named 'test' and certificate named 'test' (without an extension). Therefore, you must always specify the correct extension for the type of object you are creating. iControl SOAP has no change in behavior with file objects. A new hidden/non-default header was added for KeyManagement iControl SOAP calls, which when provided, makes iControl keymgmt APIs behave like tmsh 'sys crypto' APIs by not implicitly adding extensions. Note that this header is not enabled by default and is currently used by the GUI.

bugs.title: RelayState passed from IdP to SP is not used as a landing URI for IdP initiated SAML SSO
bugs.symptoms: When performing IdP-initiated SAML SSO, the Identity Provider (IdP) has the option to send a RelayState to a Service Provider (SP). This RelayState can be used as a URI to redirect users to after authentication is completed. When the BIG-IP system is configured as an SP, it does not use the RelayState received from an IdP as a URL to redirect to after SAML SSO is completed.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs when all of these conditions are true: BIG-IP is used as SP IdP-initiated SAML SSO is performed. IdP sends a RelayState to SP.
bugs.impact: User will not be redirected to a resource passed from IdP.
bugs.workaround: SP could be configured with a RelayState to specify a resource to serve to users after completion of SAML SSO.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system, when configured as a SAML Service Provider (SP), will now accept RelayState from an Identity Provider (IdP) to be used as a resource to serve to users after completion of SAML SSO.

bugs.title: Response Pages custom content with \n instead of \r\n on policy import.
bugs.symptoms: After importing policy with custom content on the Default Response Page, new lines are changed from \r\n to \n. They should not change.
bugs.conditions:
1. Create New Policy. 2. Go to Security : Application Security : Policy : Response Pages. 3. On Default Response Page, change Response Type to 'Custom Response'. 4. Add 'Enters' to the 'Response Body' and save it. (for example: Request RejectedThe requested URL was rejected. Please consult with your administrator.

Your support ID is: <%TS.request.ID()%>). 5. View the REST state of the response page and see that the new lines are represented by ' '. 6. Export the policy to XML. 7. Import the policy back (replace the old policy). 8. Now the 'new lines' in the content of the response page presented by ' ' instead of ' '.
bugs.impact: New lines are changed from \r\n to \n.
