bugs.workaround: In the GUI, Go to Security : Application Security : Policy : Response Pages, remove and add the 'Enters' and click 'Save' for the Default Response Page.
bugs.fix: After importing a policy with custom content on the Default Response Page, new lines are no longer changed from \r\n.

bugs.title: Table values are not correctly cleaned and can occupy entire disk space.
bugs.symptoms: AVR data in MySQL might grow to fill all disk space.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when DNS table receives a large number of entries that are not being evicted when they are no longer needed.
bugs.impact: MySQL stops responding. Site might experience down time due to full disk.
bugs.workaround: If monitoring disk space and AVR data takes more than 70% of the space, reset AVR data by running the following commands sequentially: -- touch /var/avr/init_avrdb. -- bigstart restart monpd.
bugs.fix: In this release, the system handles AVR data in MySQL so that database size no longer grows beyond a certain point.

bugs.title: Confusing message in edge client logs
bugs.symptoms: Edge client logs contain several instances of log messages similar to the following: GetCookie, Cookie F5_ST not set.
bugs.conditions: Use of Edge client on Microsoft Windows in typical operations.
bugs.impact: Log cluttering make it difficult to troubleshoot genuine issues.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Readability of Windows Edge Client have been improved by reducing background messages about browser object cookies.

bugs.title: Enhancement: ltm virtual translate-port, translate-address are not listed if they are enabled
bugs.symptoms: Consider the listing of the ltm virtual vsach below. The translate-port, translate-address properties are not listed. This implies that these properties are set to their default value of true. tmsh does not list default values. In case these are set to false, they will be listed. (tmos)# list ltm virtual ltm virtual vsach { destination 1.1.1.1:http mask 255.255.255.255 profiles { fastL4 { } } source 0.0.0.0/0 vs-index 3 }
bugs.conditions: Presence of a ltm virtual in the configuration with its destination port any (ex: x.y.z.w:any) and translate-port enabled. When listing this ltm virtual the translate-port, translate-address are not displayed.
bugs.impact: Cannot know the actual value of virtual::translate-port, translate-address attributes until the workaround is applied.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly list the property (tmos)# list ltm virtual sach translate-port ltm virtual vsach { translate-port enabled }
bugs.fix: Post change the above mentioned properties will always be listed, irrespective if they have default value or not.

bugs.title: Policy creation error after resolving LSO in policy sync for a big policy
bugs.symptoms: An error dialog popup with title "Policy Creation Error" and text " Request timeout Status text communication failure" after resolving LSOs and clicking on "finish" button.
bugs.conditions: - Import or create a big policy, e.g. 2.7MB for the .conf and 1.6MB for the resources in the res directory, 1100 ACLs with 9600 ACL entries in them. - Initiate a policy, resolve LSOs and click "finish"
bugs.impact: GUI won't recover.
bugs.workaround: Running following shell command from console: bigstart restart tomcat

bugs.title: Password history is not enforced when root, Administrator, or User Manager changes another user's password
bugs.symptoms: When logged in as root, or as a user with Administrator or User Manager role, an attempt to change a user's password will succeed, even if the new password is in password history. (An ordinary user changing their own password will be prevented from making this change.)
bugs.conditions: password-memory field of auth password-policy set to nonzero value
bugs.impact: Privileged users might circumvent the password history restriction.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate this, you should only permit management access to BIG-IP systems over a secure network, and limit shell access to trusted users.

bugs.title: SMTP monitor might mark the server down even if the server answers the HELO message.
bugs.symptoms: The SMTP monitor marks a server down even when the server responds with a 250 message to the HELO command. Monitor debug output might show the following error messages: -- ERROR: failed to complete the transfer, error code: 28 error message: Time-out. -- ERROR: failed to complete the transfer, error code: 56 error message: Recv failure: Connection reset by peer.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under any of the following conditions: -- The monitored server does not close the TCP connection (does not send a FIN) after receiving a QUIT command from the client. -- The server does not include the word 'Bye' in the 221 message in response to the 'quit' sent by the BIG-IP system. -- The server issues a RST for any reason after the BIG-IP system has successfully received the 250 response to the HELO message.
bugs.impact: The monitored server is marked down when it is not.
bugs.fix: SMTP monitor now considers the server up if it receives a successful response to the HELO command.

bugs.title: Microsoft Edge browser is not supported
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support the Microsoft Edge browser for various APM use cases, including SSLVPN and end point inspection.
bugs.conditions: Edge browser is used to establish connection to APM.
bugs.impact: Cannot establish connection APM using Edge browser.
bugs.workaround: Use Microsoft Internet Explorer.
bugs.fix: APM now supports Microsoft Edge browser.

bugs.title: Not enough free disk space for live install of BIG-IP 12.0.0 from 11.5.3 VE
bugs.symptoms: Not enough free disk space for live install of 12.0.0.
bugs.conditions: Initial install of BIG-IP VE GOOD 11.5.3. Upgrade to 12.0.0
bugs.impact: Unable to install 12.0.0 on 2nd slot.
bugs.workaround: Grow the virtual disk before installing 12.0.0.
bugs.fix: Increased the size of virtual disk so that there is enough free disk space for live install of BIG-IP 12.0.0 from 11.5.3 VE.

bugs.title: When binary database is not present, during mcp load, unexpected creation of VLAN membership in 'cist' STP singleton
bugs.symptoms: When user removes a VLAN from a Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) instance, it appears in stp instance 0. This is by design.
bugs.conditions: Deleting a VLAN from an STP instance.
bugs.impact: Minor: VLANS deleted from an STP instance do not "disappear", they are instead added to STP instance 0.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: BD crashes when attempting to access a closed connection
bugs.symptoms: The Enforcer Application system generates a BD core file to the /shared/core directory.
bugs.conditions: One or more of these features is turned on - Session tracking, web scraping, ICAP, ASM irules. The client side or the server side pre-maturely closes the connection. Some load happens on this traffic.
bugs.impact: The Enforcer Application system may temporarily fail to process traffic.

bugs.title: Transparent inherited TCP monitors may fail on loading configuration
bugs.symptoms: LTM monitor configuration may fail to reload from disk if the monitor name occurs alphabetically prior to the inherited-from monitor.
bugs.conditions: Monitor A inheriting from Monitor B, where both monitors are of type 'transparent'.
bugs.impact: Configuration from disk fails to load. System posts an error message similar to the following: 1070045:3: Monitor /Common/test1 type cannot have transparent attribute. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: Rename monitors so they occur in the required alphabetical order to support inheritance.
bugs.fix: Transparent inherited TCP monitors no longer fail on loading configuration.

bugs.title: As more virtual addresses are added to the BIG-IP running in AWS, the network failover time increases.
bugs.symptoms: As more virtual addresses are added to the BIG-IP running in AWS, the network failover time increases.
bugs.conditions: Same region failover in AWS.
bugs.impact: Network failover time degrades as the number of virtual addresses increases.
bugs.fix: Failover time for BIG-IPs that have multiple virtual addresses on the same interface has been improved. Failover time mostly depends now on the number of the interfaces with floating objects (and only slightly depends on the number of floating objects). This significantly improves the failover duration for configurations which were previously showing the longest duration.

bugs.title: DHCPv6 - pool member not selected if it returns from DOWN state
bugs.symptoms: A DHCP relay that has more than one poolmember configured, forwards requests to all of them as expected. However, if there is a constant flow of DHCP traffic from the client, and monitors change the state of these poolmembers, a poolmember that was down, does not get traffic when it comes up, and a poolmember that goes down, still receives forwarded DHCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: Pool members states are changed after sessions are created.
bugs.impact: Pool members are not used if they become active after sessions are created, or remain in use when they are inactive.
bugs.workaround: After pool members state are changed, delete all the sessions and re-create them.

bugs.title: Device groups sharing common folders can cause conflicting folder settings
bugs.symptoms: Syncing a device group can overwrite the folder settings of another device group.
bugs.conditions: * There are multiple device groups configured (e.g. DG1, DG2, etc.). * A subfolder is assigned to a different device group than the parent folder (e.g., /PARENT is assigned to DG1 and /PARENT/CHILD is assigned DG2). * A device is a member of the device group assigned to the subfolder, but not the device group of parent folder (e.g., BIG-IP1 is a member of DG2 but not DG1). * There is a second device that is in both device groups (e.g., BIG-IP2 in both DG1 and DG2). * The device syncs configuration in the subfolders device group (e.g., BIG-IP1 makes a change to an object in /PARENT/CHILD and syncs it to peers).
bugs.impact: The parent folder may lose configuration. In particular, it may no longer be associated with the device group (i.e. /PARENT will no longer be associated with DG1 on BIG-IP2).
bugs.workaround: The recommendation is create separate partitions for the different device groups and make sure subfolders always inherit the device group and traffic group settings of the parent/partition folder.

bugs.title: Incoming SYNs that match an existing connection may complete the handshake but will be RST with the cause of 'TCP 3WHS rejected' or 'No flow found for ACK' on subsequent packets.
bugs.symptoms: Incoming SYNs that match an existing connection may complete the handshake but will be RST with the cause of 'TCP 3WHS rejected' on subsequent packets.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the existing connection is closing while waiting on an ACK to the last FIN.
bugs.impact: Unexpected RSTs (Clientside).

bugs.title: Session variable report can be blank in many cases
bugs.symptoms: For an access policy that includes On-Demand Cert Auth, Dynamic ACL, Per-App VPN, and other components, the Session Variable Report output can be blank.
bugs.conditions: On-Demand Cert Auth in an access policy. DACL in access policy. Per-App VPN access policy. probably others.
bugs.impact: The Session Variable report is empty.
bugs.workaround: Check the session variable using command sessiondump.
bugs.fix: For an access policy that includes On-Demand Cert Auth, Dynamic ACL, or Per-App VPN, the Session Variable Report now shows session variables correctly.

bugs.title: tmm crashes on "ACCESS::session data set -secure" in iRule
bugs.symptoms: You encounter a tmm crash when your configuration contains an iRule that uses "ACCESS::session data set -secure"
bugs.conditions: Use of "ACCESS::session data set -secure" in an iRule
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash related to the "ACCESS::session data set -secure" command

bugs.title: Occasional host-tmm connections within a chassis will fail (affects APM processes trying to connect to a tmm)
bugs.symptoms: When using features that require a process on the host to connect to a specific tmm within a chassis, those connections sometimes fail. This can result in improper behavior of the feature, such as failure to create sessions in APM.
bugs.conditions: Using a module and feature that requires host-tmm communication within a chassis.
bugs.impact: Possible service failure, such as disallowing entry to APM.
bugs.fix: Host-to-tmm connections within a chassis no longer fail.

bugs.title: Policy Sync Status stuck at initiated syncing to subgroup after doing to parent group
bugs.symptoms: Policy sync status of source device gets stuck at "Initiated" and never transitions to completed.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create two sync-only device groups so that one contains all the members of the other. 2. Initiate a policy sync to the bigger group. 3. Initiate a policy sync to the smaller group.
bugs.impact: Policy sync cannot complete and status remains "Initiated".

bugs.title: LTM : Virtual Address List page uses LTM : Nodes List search filter.
bugs.symptoms: LTM : Virtual Address List page doesn't have it's own filter but uses other object's filter like Node list or Access policy.
bugs.conditions: Specifying a search filter on the Nodes page and then navigating to the Virtual Address page.
bugs.impact: Displays an empty virtual server list or only the virtual address matching the node addresses.
bugs.workaround: Remove the filter on the LTM : Nodes List before viewing the LTM : Virtual Address List.
bugs.fix: Specifying a search filter on LTM : Nodes List no longer affects the output on LTM : Virtual Address List. Virtual Address List now has its own fixed, general filter, and is not affected by filter settings on any other object.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE may restart tmm if descheduled by hypervisor for extended periods
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) configuration may restart the tmm process if it is descheduled for 10 seconds or more. This generally happens only on oversubscribed systems.
bugs.conditions: -- Overprovision resources on a hypervisor without any CPU reservations for a BIG-IP system. -- Cause enough work to happen where the BIG-IP system cannot be scheduled to run for 10 seconds.
bugs.impact: The tmm potentially restarts due to an ABORT signal. This does not always happen, depending upon what happens to run first (tmm or sod) when the BIG-IP system gets a chance to run. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Reserve ample CPU resources to guarantee that tmm gets an opportunity to touch its watchdog within 10 seconds. -- Do not provision enough jobs on a hypervisor host such that the BIG-IP system is not allotted sufficient CPU cycles.

bugs.title: APM PAM module does not handle local-only users list correctly
bugs.symptoms: The following log messages are shown in /var/log/secure, when remote-auth (APM based) is configured and when trying to authenticate local users: -- notice httpd[8281]: pam_apm: module returning Failure, ClientHandler auth failed!(admin) -- notice httpd[8281]: 01070417:5: AUDIT - user admin - RAW: httpd(mod_auth_pam): user=admin(admin) partition=[All] level=Administrator tty=/sbin/nologin host=X.X.X.X attempts=1 start="Wed Jan 17 14:49:21 2018" This failure log shows that the system first attempts to authenticate local users (like admin, root, etc.) remotely.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when following conditions are met: - APM is provisioned on a BIG-IP system. - APM-based remote-auth is configured. - Local users (like admin, root, etc.) attempt to log into the management interface of that BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Local users credentials are sent to remote authentication servers which will return auth failure. However, in the second attempt, the system attempts to authenticate a user locally, and it will succeed, as expected. Check below logs: -- notice httpd[8281]: pam_apm: module returning Failure, ClientHandler auth failed!(admin) -- notice httpd[8281]: 01070417:5: AUDIT - user admin - RAW: httpd(mod_auth_pam): user=admin(admin) partition=[All] level=Administrator tty=/sbin/nologin host=X.X.X.X attempts=1 start="Wed Jan 17 14:49:21 2018"
bugs.fix: Local users are authenticated locally. The system no longer sends request to remote servers for local users.

bugs.title: Packet Sizing Issues after Receipt of PMTU
bugs.symptoms: TCP sends IP fragments in spite of PMTU message.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has received an ICMP PMTU message.
bugs.impact: IP fragmentation.
bugs.workaround: Set the MSS in the TCP profile sufficiently low to avoid inducing ICMP messages in the future.
bugs.fix: Properly process ICMP packets.

bugs.title: VCMP Host: statistic discrepancy when guests use pva disabled virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: When guests use ePVA disabled virtuals the host double-counts packets and bits in the host side throughput counters.
bugs.conditions: VCMP guest disable pva in a virtual. Observe host throughput statistics (packets, bits).
bugs.impact: Incorrect representation of traffic flowing through the BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Secondary blade may restart services if configuration elements are deleted using a * wildcard.
bugs.symptoms: In certain situations a chassis based system with more than one working blade may encounter service restart on the secondary blade.
bugs.conditions: - Chassis system with 2 or more working blades. - Configuration to be deleted via tmsh using a wildcard. For instance: tmsh delete ltm virtual test*
bugs.impact: Services will restart on the secondary blade.
bugs.workaround: Do not use * wildcards with tmsh when deleting configuration elements on a chassis system.
bugs.fix: Services no longer restart on a secondary blade when deleting configuration elements via tmsh using a * wildcard.

bugs.title: Ensure min_path_mtu is functioning as designed.
bugs.symptoms: A route metrics mtu value lower than min_path mtu could be set
bugs.conditions: A mtu lower than min_path_mtu.
bugs.impact: The expected db variable min_path_mtu was not be correctly followed with unexpected results in certain conditions.
bugs.fix: Resolved error to ensure min_path_mtu is enforced as lowest mtu value as designed.

bugs.title: Installation of Edge Client can cause Windows 10 crash in some cases
bugs.symptoms: connecting to an APM box which has support for Windows 10 can cause the OS to crash. After reboot the next attempt will be successful
bugs.conditions: - Windows 10 - APM box supporting Windows 10 - user installed F5 VPN driver from an APM box, not supporting Windows 10
bugs.impact: User can lose some data
bugs.workaround: Before connecting old VPN driver instances must be manually removed using Device Manager
bugs.fix: Installation of BIG-IP Edge Client on Windows 10 does not cause system crash anymore.

bugs.title: PEM: CPU spike seen when iRule tries to update nonexistent sessions.
bugs.symptoms: CPU spikes and remains high, eventually leading to TMM core.
bugs.conditions: iRule is used to update a session with policies for a session that does not exist.
bugs.impact: CPU spike. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the session exists if you plan to use iRules to update sessions with policies.
bugs.fix: CPU spike are no longer seen, even if iRule tries to update nonexistent sessions.

bugs.title: Fix ssl_session memory corruption when many sessions and heavy traffic.
bugs.symptoms: ssl_session memory corruption might occur when there are many sessions and heavy traffic. The SSL session is freed but not removed from cache. The cache contains the freed SSL session which can cause a crash when the cache entry is removed later.
bugs.conditions: Many SSL session and heavy traffic.
bugs.impact: ssl_session memory corruption.
bugs.fix: This memory corruption issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Component checks wait for page load
bugs.symptoms: FPS component checks to not run until the entire page is ready, causing false-positive check-component alerts if the user navigates before load finishes
bugs.conditions: User navigates quickly between protected pages
bugs.impact: False positive component-check alerts
bugs.workaround: Filter false-positives in FPS dashboard
bugs.fix: Check Components now initializes as soon as FPS code runs and then updates when page is loaded.

bugs.title: Fastl4 profile sends RST packet when idle timeout value set to 'immediate'
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual is configured with a Fastl4 profile and the idle timeout value is set to 'immediate', traffic is handled improperly and a RST is issued.
bugs.conditions: A virtual is processing traffic that contains a Fastl4 profile with idle timeout set to 'immediate'.
bugs.impact: Traffic is Reset on a virtual where it should properly handle the traffic.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using the 'immediate' setting for the idle timeout value on a Fastl4 profile.

bugs.title: Second push is required after deactivating Active Security Policy and Sync flag indicates "In Sync" status
bugs.symptoms: Changes made to security policies are not synced to peer. The sync status says "In sync" but the policy changes have not been made.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when making changes to security policies with policies on each device in a sync-only ASM device group.
bugs.impact: Changes are not propagated to the other devices in the sync-only device group, yet the sync status says it is in sync (the sync-failover group will say changes are pending). If you perform a second sync, the changes are pushed to the other devices.
bugs.workaround: Performing a second sync will push the changes to the other devices.

bugs.title: EdgeClient may crash if special Network Access configuration is used
bugs.symptoms: EdgeClient crashes during connect or disconnect process. Exact time may differ from time to time.
bugs.conditions: EdgeClient may crash if Network Access contains configuration which includes: Full-tunnel Allow DHCP or Allow Local subnets is used There is a proxy between client and APM
bugs.impact: EdgeClient crashes prevent Access Network to work
bugs.workaround: Remove on of conditions causing crash to happen
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Edge Client now correctly processes particular Network Access configurations.

bugs.title: NAT available in DNS section but config load fails with standalone license
bugs.symptoms: config load fails with error: 01070356:3: NAT feature not licensed. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: A NAT object is created for GTM/LC standalone license box.
bugs.impact: config fails to load.
bugs.fix: Configuration loading no longer fails with a NAT in DNS section.

bugs.title: Monpd might core if asking for export report by email while monpd is terminating
bugs.symptoms: Core file is created by monpd if you try to export a report by email while monpd is terminating.
bugs.conditions: Very rare case that can happen if user asks to export report by email in the middle of monpd's graceful termination (due to restart or other reason) will cause core dump (not graceful termination).
bugs.workaround: Fixed to code to avoid this behavior.
bugs.fix: Exporting a report by email in the middle of monpd's graceful termination (due to restart or other reason) will no longer cause a core dump.

bugs.title: tmm might crash after modifying virtual server SSL profiles in SNI configuration under load
bugs.symptoms: Making configuration changes to SSL profiles for the virtual server configured for SSL SNI might crash tmm under load. The BIG-IP system may generate an assertion failure panic string in the /var/log/tmm file that appears similar to the following example: panic: Assertion "valid type" failed.
bugs.conditions: 1. LTM virtual server is configured with multiple SSL profiles, one of which is the default SNI profile. 2. The BIG-IP system is under traffic load. 3. A change is made to any of the SSL profiles configured on the virtual server, or SSL profiles are added or removed from the virtual server profile list.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Making SSL profiles configuration changes now complete successfully.

bugs.title: Machine certificate checker fails to use Machine cert check service if Windows has certain display languages
bugs.symptoms: Machine certificate checker agent fails to use machine certificate checker service for Windows if it has certain display language, for example Polish. In failed case logs contain: 2015-08-04,18:37:59:042, 924,756,, 1, , 330, CCertCheckCtrl::CheckPrivateKey, EXCEPTION caught: CCertCheckCtrl::CheckPrivateKey - EXCEPTION 2015-08-04,18:38:00:618, 924,756,, 1, \RPCConnector.cpp, 85, UCredMgrService::RpcConnect, EXCEPTION - Failed to set binding handle's authentication, authorization and security QOS info (RPC_STATUS: 1332) 2015-08-04,18:38:00:618, 924,756,, 1, \RPCConnector.cpp, 88, RPCConnector::Connect, EXCEPTION caught: UCredMgrService::RpcConnect - EXCEPTION 2015-08-04,18:38:00:618, 924,756,, 1, \MCClient.h, 86, MCClient::Verify, Failed to perform PRC-call:error=1702
bugs.conditions: Windows with non-english display language Machine certificate checker is supposed to use Machine Certificate Checker service
bugs.impact: Machine certificate checker cannot be passed using Machine cert service.
bugs.workaround: Switch display language to English.
bugs.fix: Machine certificate checker service works now with a display language other than English.

bugs.title: Monitor instances may not get deleted during configuration merge load
bugs.symptoms: After performing a configuration merge load (for example, "tmsh load sys config merge ...") that changes an existing pool's monitor, old monitor instances may not get deleted. This can result in a system generating monitor requests that are no longer part of the configuration. It can also result in the system logging messages such as the following: err mcpd[8793]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Can't find monitor rule: 42.
bugs.conditions: Pools with monitors configured must exist. The merge load must replace the pool's monitor.
bugs.impact: Multiple monitor instances may be active on some pool members. This may result in incorrect monitoring status.
bugs.workaround: Once a system is affected by this issue, the misbehavior can be resolved by doing the following: 1. Save and re-load the configuration to correct the incorrect information in mcpd: tmsh save sys config partitions all && tmsh load sys config partitions all 2. Restart bigd: On an appliance: bigstart restart bigd On a chassis: clsh bigstart restart bigd
bugs.fix: Ensure that all relevant monitor instances are deleted when replacing a pool's monitor.

bugs.title: Buffer overflow for large session messages
bugs.symptoms: System with multiple blades may crash when when configured with functionality that utilizes SessionDB.
bugs.conditions: On a multi-blade machine, send an MPI message larger than 64K between blades (typically a session message).
bugs.impact: Core or potential data corruption.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a buffer overflow for large session messages.

bugs.title: EVAL shown in CLI Mode even after purchasing subscription license for SWG.
bugs.symptoms: EVAL shown in CLI Mode even after purchasing subscription license for SWG.
bugs.conditions: Users have a subscription license for SWG.
bugs.impact: The user will see EVAL in the CLI.
bugs.workaround: Ignore EVAL as seen in the CLI. The feature operates as expected.
bugs.fix: EVAL is no longer shown in CLI Mode after purchasing subscription license for SWG.

bugs.title: Configuration containing a virtual server with a named wildcard destination address ('any6') may fail to load
bugs.symptoms: Configuration fails to load with an error similar to the following: A port number or service name is missing for '/Common/any6%2.0'. Please specify a port number or service name using the syntax '/Common/any6%2.0:<port>'.
bugs.conditions: Configuration contains a virtual with destination address in the form of: any6%<route domain>.<port>.
bugs.impact: Configuration load failure.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now uses the correct port delimiter when parsing destination addresses containing a named wildcard service and non-default route domain.

bugs.title: The iControl response to adding a device to a device trust may time out
bugs.symptoms: When using iControl to add a device to a device trust, it may appear that the iControl command has failed due to timeout of the response. However, the device has been added to the trust; it is the response to the iControl command that has timed out.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl to add a device to a device trust.
bugs.impact: The operation returns an error message even though the device was properly added to the trust.

bugs.title: Only one action per sensor is displayed in sensor_limit_table and system_check
bugs.symptoms: A list of sensors is displayed in the sensor_limit_table or by the system_check utility, with the actions taken when the sensor data exceeds its defined limit. On the affected versions, each sensor item is displayed only once, even if multiple limits and actions are defined for the sensor. Additional limits and actions defined for the sensor are not displayed.
bugs.conditions: This problem occurs when the affected version of the BIG-IP software is running on the following hardware platforms: BIG-IP 2000-/4000-/5000-/7000-/10000-/12000-series appliances and VIPRION B2100, B2150, B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: The system does not show the complete set of defined sensor limits and corresponding BIG-IP system actions when there are multiple limits and actions defined. Only one action is displayed for each sensor. The system_check utility will only evaluate sensor measurements against limits that appear in its sensor limit tables. Missing sensor limits will not be evaluated, and corresponding alerts will not be issued.
bugs.fix: The system now shows a list of sensors in the sensor_limit_table or by the system_check utility, with the actions taken when the sensor data exceeds its defined limit.

bugs.title: Incremental Manual sync does not allow overwrite of 'newer' ASM config
bugs.symptoms: ASM Sync was designed to only request the ASM portion of the configuration if it recognizes that a peer has a newer configuration. This precluded the ability to 'roll back' changes on a device by pushing from the peer that still has the older configuration.
bugs.conditions: Devices are set up in an Incremental Manual Sync ASM-enabled group.
bugs.impact: User is unable to 'roll back' changes on a device by pushing from the peer that has an older configuration.
bugs.workaround: Make a spurious change on the device that has an older configuration and then push the changes to the peer.
bugs.fix: Older ASM configurations can now be pushed to a peer in an incremental sync manual device group.

bugs.title: SSL handshakes on 4200/2200 can cause TMM cores.
bugs.symptoms: When processing SSL handshakes in the crypto acceleration hardware, a BIG-IP 2000 or 4000 platform might experience a TMM core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when processing SSL handshakes in the crypto acceleration hardware. The issue is very unlikely to be seen other than on BIG-IP version 11.6.0 HF5 or on version 12.0.0 base install.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The crypto acceleration hardware driver for the 2200/4200 has been fixed to avoid memory corruption.

bugs.title: iControl REST asynchronous tasks may block other tasks from running
bugs.symptoms: If an iControl REST asynchronous task is running, other iControl REST queries (synchronous or asynchronous) will wait until the asynchronous task completes before executing. If the asynchronous task is long-running, subsequent requests will block for a long time.
bugs.conditions: -- Executing an iControl REST task asynchronously. -- Performing further iControl REST tasks (synchronous or asynchronous) while the asynchronous task is still running.
bugs.impact: Potential (and unexpected) long wait times while running a task asynchronously.

bugs.title: TMM core file on pool member down with rate limit configured
bugs.symptoms: TMM may produce a core file when attempting to retry to calculate the rate-limit on a pool member that has gone down.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - service-down-action reselect. - rate limit specified. - traffic load balanced to pool members. - traffic is over the rate for all pool members. - all pool members go down.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove rate-limit configuration.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer produces a core file when attempting to retry to calculate the rate-limit on a pool member that has gone down.

bugs.title: P-256 ECDH performance improvements
bugs.symptoms: Recent changes in the TLS clients to only use perfect forward secrecy (PFS) ciphersuites in default configuration may degrade TLS handshake rate on BIG-IP, may cause higher CPU utilization on the BIG-IP, or both. An example of a recent change is Apple iOS's App Transport Security changes to only enable ECDH ephemeral ciphersuites (the ciphersuites with the ECDHE suffix).
bugs.conditions: Large portion of TLS client only offers *ECDHE* ciphersuites in their TLS CLientHello, the average size of the TLS session is small (e.g. in kilobytes), and the TLS session resumption is not used. In other words, the conditions such that the TLS handshakes likely negotiate ECDHE ciphersuites with short sessions.
bugs.impact: With this improvement, the TLS handshake rate with a ciphersuite ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 is expected to be ~50% higher on hardware platforms without Intel Cave Creek acceleration (released in 2015 and earlier). Internal testing has shown variations in the improvement between 20% and 80% with this enhancement. The comparison is against the current 12.0.x (or 11.6.x) release. The performance of ECDSA with P-256 was also improved. Conversely, previous versions of the BIG-IP will have correspondingly lower performance, or worse for older releases.
bugs.workaround: Order ciphersuite selection so that ECDH ciphersuites are least preferred. One method to accomplish this is to ensure that the clientssl profile's cipherstring contains 'ecdhe:ecdhe_ecdsa' at the end of the list. This will only matter/needed when non-PFS cipherssuites are allowed in the profile and are offered by the client.
bugs.fix: Performance improvements for P-256 ECDH and ECDSA algorithms.

bugs.title: SSO token login does not work due to remote role update failures.
bugs.symptoms: SSO token login does not work due to remote role update failures.
bugs.conditions: SSO between Enterprise Manager (EM) and a BIG-IP system using a third party authentication system, such as LDAP.
bugs.impact: Incorrect role assignment causing SSO login to not work. The system posts messages similar to the following: -- notice mcpd[6165]: 01070829:5: Input error: Remote user message dropped (adm184789 in [All]) because duplicate partition. -- err mcpd[6165]: 01070827:3: User login disallowed: User (adm184789) is not an administrator, does not have a UID of zero, and has not been assigned a role on a partition.
bugs.workaround: Login using remote user credentials on the BIG-IP system. This properly updates the role for the remote user.
bugs.fix: SSO token login now works with the correct role assignments to a remote user.

bugs.title: tmm assert 'valid private'
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes with the following message in /var/log/ltm: Assertion "valid private" failed This is followed by a **SIGFPE** message.
bugs.conditions: This is an internal issue which occurs when processing syn cookies on a non-TCP4 flow.
bugs.impact: The tmm assert 'valid private', core, and restart.
bugs.fix: The system now performs SYN cookie validation only on TCP flows.

bugs.title: TMM may apply SYN cookie validation to packets before generating any SYN cookies
bugs.symptoms: SYN cookie validation is applied when SYN cookies are not active
bugs.conditions: Internal TMM clock has overflowed and is near 0 ACK packet has been received that does not match an existing connection flow
bugs.impact: Validation can be applied to a listener/proxy that does not support SYN cookies which can lead to a tmm core.
bugs.fix: SYN cookie validation will not be applied if SYN cookies have not been activated.

bugs.title: Configurable maximum message size limit for restjavad
bugs.symptoms: if the client issues a request to iControl REST that results in a large amount of data (approx 200 MB), restjavad goes into an out-of-memory condition when attempting to serialize the response prior to returning it to the client.
bugs.conditions: A message is received by restjavad that is larger than the total free heap space. The most common cause is that the system sends a broard query to icrd, which returns a very large response (approx 200 MB).
bugs.impact: restjavad becomes unresponsive until it is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: This fix exposes the maximum message size limit and allows a Network operator to change it by posting to a new configuration worker. An example is included below. The actual value varies by installation - load, average message size etc. Set it too low and the clients will receive 5xx errors even though there is sufficient memory. Set it too high and dangerously-large messages do not get dropped and might cause an out-of-memory exception. 5 MB is a recommended starting value. An example of setting the maximum message body size to 5kB (5000 bytes) on a machine called 'green.' The password needs to be changed appropriately. curl -s -k -u admin:PASSWORD -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H 'Connection: keep-alive' -X PUT "https://green/mgmt/shared/server/messaging/settings/8100" -d '{"maxMessageBodySize": "5000" }'.
bugs.fix: There is now a configurable maximum message size limit for restjavad. Restjavad still reaches an out-of-memory condition if it receives very large messages (approx 200 MB), but there is now an option of setting a 'hard cap' that causes restjavad to discard these large messages, preventing the out-of-memory condition.

bugs.title: scriptd may core when MCP connection is lost
bugs.symptoms: Scriptd loses MCP connection may cause scriptd to core.
bugs.conditions: Unknown, Only known to reproduce in an F5 internal test.
bugs.impact: None known.
bugs.fix: A possible case of scriptd dumping core has been fixed.

bugs.title: Save Password checkbox setting is not remembered on Mac Edge Client.
bugs.symptoms: Save Password checkbox setting is not remembered on Mac Edge Client.
bugs.conditions: Mac Edge Client is used, and the Save Password checkbox is unchecked.
bugs.impact: Checkbox reverts to checked, so users must uncheck the box every time they don't want to save the password.
bugs.fix: Now the Mac Edge Client remembers previous "Save Password" checkbox setting.

bugs.title: ICAP implementation incorrect when HTTP request or response is missing a payload
bugs.symptoms: The ICAP request sent to the ICAP server always contains a payload even if the HTTP request or response to be modified does not contain one.
bugs.conditions: HTTP request or response does not contain a payload.
bugs.impact: If an HTTP request or response to be modified does not contain a payload, the ICAP client sends a zero-byte HTTP payload instead.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly identifies an empty HTTP payload and sends the appropriate ICAP header, identifying that there is no HTTP payload included.

bugs.title: REST: Filtering login pages or parameters by their associated URL does not work
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to filter the collection of configured login pages by their URL, the full list is returned instead of the desired results. The same problem exists for URL level Parameters.
bugs.conditions: The login-pages or parameters collection endpoints are queried with the following $filter: $filter=url/name eq '<URL NAME>'
bugs.impact: Incorrect results are returned to the REST client
bugs.fix: REST $filter for associated URLs on login-pages and parameters endpoints now works correctly.

bugs.title: DNS resolution does not work on a Windows 10 desktop with multiple NICs after VPN connection has been established in some cases
bugs.symptoms: DNS resolution stops working on a Microsoft Windows 10 desktop when the VPN connection is established.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the client system meets all of the following conditions: - Running BIG-IP software version Hotfix-BIGIP-11.5.3.1.47.167-HF1-ENG.iso. - Running Microsoft Windows version 10. - Has multiple NICs and one of them is in the disconnected state, with a statically assigned IPv4 configuration.
bugs.impact: User cannot access resources by DNS name.
bugs.workaround: Disable disconnected NICs that have a statically assigned IPv4 configuration.
bugs.fix: After VPN connection has been established, DNS resolution works, in the case of a Windows 10 desktop with multiple NICs and one of them is in a disconnected state and has a statically assigned IPv4 configuration.

bugs.title: TMM stack trace when killed by monitoring process when stuck in loop always logged in parent TMM thread log file.
bugs.symptoms: TMM stack trace when killed by monitoring process when stuck in loop always logged in parent TMM thread log file instead of looping TMM thread log file.
bugs.conditions: TMM stuck in a loop and aborted by monitor process.
bugs.impact: Unclear which TMM thread was looping and resulted in crash and failover.

bugs.title: Reprovisioning an active system may cause APMD to crash
bugs.symptoms: Provisioning restarts the APM daemons. If the system is currently passing traffic, orderly shutdown is disrupted and APMD can crash.
bugs.conditions: There must be authentication requests in progress while provisioning is attempted. The new requests recreate objects removed during shutdown which leads to a crash.
bugs.impact: APMD creates a core file. As provisioning is run by the administrator, the service interruption is intentional. There is no additional impact on users.
bugs.workaround: None needed.

bugs.title: Stats refinements for reporting Unhandled Query Actions :: Drops
bugs.symptoms: There are five drop down sections for Unhandled Query Actions: Allow Drop Reject Hint No Error but in statistics page, there are only four Unhandled Query Actions: Drops Rejects Hints No Errors Drops refers to the dropped packets for the system, not specifically for Unhandled Query Actions. It would be more clear if there were one dropped packets stats for the system, and another specifically for Unhandled. And also add stats for Allow packets under Unhandled.
bugs.conditions: Statistics pages for Unhandled Query Actions :: Drops.
bugs.impact: May be confusing to determine what the statistics mean.

bugs.title: Client side checks on CentOS 7 don't work.
bugs.symptoms: Client side checks such as antivirus, firewall, process, file, and so on, on CentOS 7 do not work. Server logs show "Access encountered error: ERR_ARG" for these clients.
bugs.conditions: This happens when client-side checks are configured on the BIG-IP system and CentOS 7 and Firefox client connecting to this BIG-IP shows symptoms
bugs.impact: Clients from CentOS 7 are not able to connect to BIG-IP APM.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: VE shows INOPERATIVE status until at least one VLAN is configured and attached to an interface.
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Edition (VE) deployed with 1 CPU only shows INOPERATIVE status until at least one VLAN is both configured and attached to an interface.
bugs.conditions: Install the BIG-IP Virtual Edition software on a VM with 1 CPU (1 CPU/2048 MB RAM option available in OVA) and license, but do not create any VLANs (or create VLANs, but do not attach them to an interface).
bugs.impact: In the CLI, device remains in INOPERATIVE state, but shows ACTIVE in the GUI. This might cause unneeded delay trying to rectify what appears to be a license issue when there is none.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, configure at least one VLAN and attach it to an interface.

bugs.title: SNMP: ifXTable walk should produce the available counter values instead of zero
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP ifXTable is presenting zeros for attributes hc_in_multicast_pkts and hc_out_multicast_pkts. However, this data is available on the Big-IP and should be presented.
bugs.conditions: snmpwalk the ifTable and the ifXTable. The ifTable shows Counter32 values for attributes in_multicast_pkts and out_multicast_pkts, but the ifXTable shows zeros for the Counter64 equivalent attributes hc_in_multicast_pkts and hc_out_multicast_pkts (except for vlans, which are correct).
bugs.impact: Inability to characterize/view counts for the above-referenced multicast packets via SNMP.
bugs.fix: The snmp walk described in the Symptom/Known issues field gives meaningful results after application of this hotfix.

bugs.title: bigd may crash due to a heartbeat timeout
bugs.symptoms: bigd crashes and generates a core file. The system logs entries in /var/log/ltm that are similar to the following: sod[5853]: 01140029:5: HA daemon_heartbeat bigd fails action is restart. This issue is more likely to occur if /var/log/ltm contains entries similar to the following: info bigd[5947]: reap_child: child process PID = 9198 exited with signal = 9.
bugs.conditions: External monitors that run for a long time and are killed by the next iteration of the monitor. For example, the LTM external monitor 'sample_monitor' contains logic to kill a running monitor if it runs too long.
bugs.impact: bigd crashes and generates a core file. Monitoring is interrupted.
bugs.fix: External monitors that run for a long time and are killed by the next iteration of the monitor now recover without bigd crashing and generating a core file.
bugs.behavior: bigd now logs child process exit messages in /var/log/bigdlog (so bigd.debug must be enabled) rather than in /var/log/ltm. This allows the logging to be controllable. Successful command exits are also logged for completeness since this the log messages only appears when debugging is enabled.

bugs.title: HTML filter is truncating the server response when sending it to client
bugs.symptoms: The response to the client is truncated.
bugs.conditions: When a server sends a compressed response to a flow that has an associated HTML profile. Note: Being a compressed response may not be a prerequisite. Instead, a compressed response might just reveal the issue more easily due to the asynchronous nature of inflating. The same issue is observed with rewrite profile also.
bugs.impact: The response is truncated when it reaches the client.
bugs.fix: No truncation of response to client

bugs.title: EAM core while using Oracle Access Manager
bugs.symptoms: Authentication with Oracle Access Manager can result in an exception while checking whether authentication is required. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.conditions: This event can be triggered while using the Oracle Access Manager.
bugs.impact: An unhandled exception will cause EAM to core and possible access outage.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: EAM handles exceptions gracefully during the authentication process when Oracle Access Manager is used.

bugs.title: A specific NTLM client fails to authenticate with BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Specific NTLM client (such as Android Lync 2013) fails to authenticate with BIG-IP as it sends a particular NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE which BIG-IP was not able to parse properly and throws an error. This effectively stops the authentication process, and this particular client never completes the authentication.
bugs.conditions: Specific NTLM client. It is not clear whether this issues affect a particular version of Android Lync 2013 or a particular Android version.
bugs.impact: Cannot complete the authentication, hence, not allowed to access protected resources.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for the affected clients.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now processes NTLM requests for affected Lync clients, and users of the client are able to authenticate.

bugs.title: SPDY child flow aborted while stalled leaves freed SPDY stream in SPDY stalled list
bugs.symptoms: The Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) process may produce a core file and restart when processing SPDY traffic. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: - The BIG-IP system fails over to the standby system if configured as a high-availability pair. - The BIG-IP system generates a TMM core file to the /shared/core directory.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - You associate a virtual server with a SPDY profile. - The virtual server processes a SPDY client connection with more than two concurrent streams. - The SPDY client connection stalls and is subsequently aborted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM process no longer produces a core file and restart when processing SPDY traffic issue that occurred when a virtual server processed a SPDY client connection with more than two concurrent streams, and the SPDY client connection stalled and was subsequently aborted.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Firmware update that includes might take over 15 minutes. Do not turn off device.
bugs.symptoms: On certain platforms, firmware updates might take over 15 minutes to complete. It is very important to wait until update completes. Do not turn on the device until the operation is finished.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the following iSeries platforms: i2000, i4000, i5000, i7000, and i10000.
bugs.impact: Reboot takes a long time. The GUI posts the following message: Reboot in progress Please do not turn off your device. Depending on your configuration, reboot time will vary, taking 5 to 20 minutes. To view reboot progress, connect to the serial port of your device or access the system hypervisor.
bugs.fix: Although reboot takes a long time on the iSeries platforms, the GUI posts a message containing a time range, similar to the following message: Reboot in progress Please do not turn off your device. Depending on your configuration, reboot time will vary, taking 5 to 20 minutes. To view reboot progress, connect to the serial port of your device or access the system hypervisor.

bugs.title: When logging, if the length of argument value is very long, log buffer overflows.
bugs.symptoms: If Access Policy event logs include long string arguments (greater than 8 KB), the log buffer grows while processing each log parameter. The log information can overflow to other files such as user.log and message.log.
bugs.conditions: -- Larger value for log parameters (mainly of string type). -- The parameters are very long (greater than 8 KB), for example, assigning big strings into session variables.
bugs.impact: Log information gets truncated, and some amount spills over to user.log and message.log.

bugs.title: Using the pool command in HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST event occasionally fails
bugs.symptoms: Use of HTTP::proxy disable with a pool command occasionally fails.
bugs.conditions: For each session, the very first request with the Proxy-Authorization header will get a RST, although the authentication is successful. That means that the request is not proxied to the backend proxy. Further requests are processed normally.
bugs.impact: Connection is being RST when pool command is used in HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST iRule. Subsequent requests go through successfully.

bugs.title: Cannot use self-link URI in iControl REST calls with gtm topology
bugs.symptoms: The self-link URI cannot be used in iControl REST calls with gtm topology.
bugs.conditions: User issues iControl REST commands for gtm topology that include the self-link URI.
bugs.impact: The given command is not executed and the system posts the following error message: "Topologies must specify both regions: ldns: server:".
bugs.workaround: Do not use the self-link in iControl REST commands with gtm topology.
bugs.fix: You can now use self-link URI in gtm topology-related iControl REST commands. Be sure to format the gtm topology OID string using the following rules: 1) Use only a single space between each item in the topology string. 2) Use a fully-pathed name for datacenter, isp, region, and pool objects. For example: "ldns: subnet 11.11.11.0/24 server: datacenter /Common/DC"

bugs.title: Disabled db var Watchdog.State prevents vCMP guest activation.
bugs.symptoms: If a vCMP guest user disables the watchdog using the db variable Watchdog.State, then the vCMP guest does not reach a running state as reported by the vCMP host.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the user sets sys db Watchdog.State value disable.
bugs.impact: vCMP guest fails to be operational.
bugs.workaround: Do not change the Watchdog.State db variable. The vCMP host requires the watchdog to monitor the guest health.

bugs.title: The file /etc/wr_urldbd/bcsdk.cfg needs to be included in the .ucs file
bugs.symptoms: /etc/wr_urldbd/bcsdk.cfg is not included in the .ucs file when saving the configuration.
bugs.conditions: using tmsh to save sys ucs <file_name>. The /etc/wr_urldbd/bcsdk.cfg is not saved in the file
bugs.impact: URLcat webroot configuration is not included in the ucs
bugs.workaround: no workaround
bugs.fix: After the fix, now tmsh save ucs command will save the /etc/wr_urldbd/bcsdk.cfg in the .ucs file

bugs.title: No logs for Proactive Bot Defense drops.
bugs.symptoms: A RST happens upon a request. There are no loggings or indication regarding this reset.
bugs.conditions: The VS has application dos attached with the proactive bot defense turned on.
bugs.impact: A connection terminates. The logging absence causes confusion.

bugs.title: Large ASM REST response causes all REST to hang
bugs.symptoms: the REST framework hangs and becomes not responsive when ASM REST sends a big response for a REST call
bugs.conditions: asm provisioned generate a REST call, to asm endpoint, that yields a large REST response. This could be a REST call returning a large XML document, for an example.
bugs.impact: REST framework hangs and becomes not responsive
bugs.fix: We have placed safeguards to protect the REST framework.

bugs.title: HA daemon_heartbeat mcpd fails on load sys config
bugs.symptoms: A particular stage of validation can take longer than the ha-daemon heartbeat interval, and while nothing is actually wrong, the system responds as if there is an unresponsive daemon, so the system restarts it.
bugs.conditions: iRules must be present in the configuration that the system is loading.
bugs.impact: MCPd restarts.
bugs.workaround: On the BIG-IP system, run the command: tmsh mod sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat disabled.
bugs.fix: Added additional heartbeats during validation, so HA daemon_heartbeat mcpd no longer fails on load sys config.

bugs.title: Debug header may show misleading information when Symmetric deployment is configured
bugs.symptoms: X-WA-Info header shows that a response was served from a remote BIG-IP while it was served from the central BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has to be configured as a central device in AAM Symmetric Deployment, a policy node allows caching of a compressed response. After the response is cached, X-WA-Info header shows that the response was served from a remote BIG-IP for the consequent requests.
bugs.impact: Information is misleading and may cause confusion in interpretation of http request/response flow. It requires to match the debug header to BIG-IP configuration to extract correct information. If the traffic capture is separated from the configuration snapshot, it may increase a chance of a mistake during analysis.
bugs.workaround: While this information is misleading, it still contains useful information which can be extracted and confirmed with a configuration snapshot.

bugs.title: tmm may leak connflow and memory on vCMP guest.
bugs.symptoms: tmm may leak connflow and memory on vCMP guests.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on a vCMP guest when only one tmm is provisioned on the blade.
bugs.impact: tmm leaks memory and might eventually crash from an out-of-memory condition.
bugs.workaround: Provision more than one tmm.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer leaks connflows and memory on vCMP guests when only one tmm is provisioned.

bugs.title: Zebos: extended community attributes are exchanged incorrectly in BGP updates.
bugs.symptoms: 1. BGP is not sending extended community attributes in BGP Updates to its neighbors in versions prior to 11.6.0. 2. BGP is unable to accept new BGP UPDATE messages that contain extended communities from its neighbors in version 11.6.0 and later. 3. On the sending neighbor, the route-map is reapplied to the prefix every time the connection is torn down by the neighbor, resulting in an ever increasing extended community list.
bugs.conditions: Configure BGP extended community attribute.
bugs.impact: Loss of/incorrect info related to extended community attribute.
bugs.fix: The BGP extended community attributes now work as expected.

bugs.title: tmm crash when DoS protection and behavior analysis enabled on virtual server
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash when DoS protection and behavior analysis enabled on virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1) Provision AFM and LTM. 2) Enable DoS protection, Behavior Analysis in DoS profiles. 3) DoS profile is associated on a virtual server 4) Bad packets are sent to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: DoS-network behavioral analysis should be never configured since it does not provide any needed functionality. If any security dos profiles contain 'behavioral-analysis enabled', these should be changed to 'behavioral-analysis disabled.

bugs.title: URLs with different path parameters values are seen as different URLs
bugs.symptoms: URLs with different path parameters values are seen as different URLs. The parameters themselves are enforced as part of a URL and not as parameters values.
bugs.conditions: An application uses path parameters (where the URL path is composed from different parameters values)
bugs.impact: This causes the URL with different values to be seen as different URLs, making the automatic policy builder cumbersome or unworkable.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Added a path parameter configuration and enforcement.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing SSL traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing SSL traffic.
bugs.conditions: SSL profile enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes SSL traffic as expected.

bugs.title: mcpd will continually restart on newly inserted secondary blades when certain configuration exists on the primary
bugs.symptoms: When a secondary blade's mcpd starts up, it may continually restart, failing to load, when the primary blade has a certain configuration. The easiest way to reproduce this is to insert a new blade into an existing running cluster. This will happen when a link local IPv4 self IP is in use and the DB variable config.allow.rfc3927 is set to disabled (which is the default). It is not possible to create such self IPs unless the DB variable is first enabled, the object is created, and then the DB variable is disabled. In certain scenarios a secondary blade mcpd may go into a restart loop when receiving the configuration from the primary blade if ipv4 link local SelfIP addresses are in use enabled by DBKey config.allow.rfc3927.
bugs.conditions: This happens only on MCP startup on secondary blades, when a link local IPv4 self IP is configured, and when the DB variable config.allow.rfc3927 is set to disabled (which is the default).
bugs.impact: Secondary blade will not become part of the cluster and will not be able to process traffic. Continual log messages will show up on existing blades announcing that mcpd is continually restarting.
bugs.workaround: Enable the config.allow.rfc3927 DB variable on the primary to suspend this validation.
bugs.fix: When a link local IPv4 self IP is in use and the DB variable config.allow.rfc3927 is set to disabled (which is the default), mcpd would previously fail to start on a newly inserted secondary blade. This no longer occurs.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Attack Signature Update cannot roll back to older attack signatures
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to roll back to an older attack signature update using the REST interface
bugs.conditions: REST is used to manage Attack Signature Updates on a BIG-IP device, and an older version than the currently installed file is desired to be installed.
bugs.impact: REST clients have no way to fully manage Attack Signature Updates for the BIG-IP
bugs.workaround: The GUI can be used to roll back to an earlier version
bugs.fix: The REST API now includes support for the "allowOlderTimestamp" field to the update-signatures task in order to allow rolling back to an older attack signature update using the REST interface. POST https://<host>/mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/update-signatures/ { "allowOlderTimestamp": true, <Rest of body as usual> }

bugs.title: ASM REST: DESC modifier for $orderby option does not affect results
bugs.symptoms: Collections returned from the REST API can be sorted by a field from the $orderby ODATA parameter. The default sort order is ascending, but it is meant to allow a "DESC" modified to sort in descending order. The "DESC" modifier has no effect on the sort order.
bugs.conditions: ASM REST API is used to retrieve a collection with the elements sorted by a field's value in descending order.
bugs.impact: The collection is always returned in ascending sort order even if it descending order was requested.
bugs.fix: The DESC operator is now honored for the $orderby ODATA parameter on ASM REST API requests.

bugs.title: peer/clientside/serverside script with parking command may cause tmm to core.
bugs.symptoms: When the peer/clientside/serverside iRule contains parking commands, or in NTLM profiles (which utilize parking commands), tmm might core upon connection reuse.
bugs.conditions: 1. The iRule used in peer/clientside/serverside contains a parking command. 2. The connection is reused. This might occur in OneConnect configurations, for example. In configurations that do not have parking iRule commands, this issue might also occur when the NTLM profile is in use, as the NTLM profile also utilizes parking. Note: The NTLM profile might be deployed automatically if you are using a SharePoint iApp.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use parking commands in cases where the system might reuse the connection. If the issue occurs with the NTLM profile, do not use the NTLM profile, if possible.
bugs.fix: When the peer/clientside/serverside iRule contains parking commands, or when using NTLM profiles that utilize parking commands, tmm no longer cores upon connection reuse.

bugs.title: "show sys pptp-call-info" command can cause tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Core when "show sys pptp-call-info" is called.
bugs.conditions: On BIG-IP with fastl4 virtual server forwarding PPTP GRE traffic, TMSH "show sys pptp-call-info" command can cause crash in TMM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not issue "show sys pptp-call-info" command on BIG-IP forwarding PPTP GRE traffic.
bugs.fix: Fixed crash from incorrectly matching PPTP ALG traffic in forwarding fastl4 virtual server.

bugs.title: vCMP guest with redirect-http-to-https enabled may see incorrect set of block-device-images and block-device-hotfixes.
bugs.symptoms: The block-device-image and block-device-hotfix components allow a vCMP guest to view and install TMOS images located on the vCMP host, if permitted by the host. When the redirect-http-to-https setting is enabled on a vCMP guest, the set of host-provided images visible to the guest may be inconsistent with what is actually present on the host. If a guest tries to install an image that is present in its block-device-image or block-device-hotfix lists, but not present on the host, the installation will fail. Similarly, if a guest tries to install an image that is not present in its block-device-image or block-device-hotfix lists, but present on the host, the installation will fail.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when the redirect-http-to-https setting is enabled on the vCMP guest. This setting can be viewed with "tmsh list sys httpd redirect-http-to-https". It is disabled by default.
bugs.impact: The vCMP guest may not be able to list or install one or more block-device-images or block-device-hotfixes provided by the vCMP host. The guest will still be able to install images and hotfixes on its own filesystem.
bugs.workaround: The issue can be worked around by disabling the redirect-http-to-https setting with "tmsh modify sys httpd redirect-http-to-https disabled". Shortly after disabling this setting, the set of block-device-images and block-device-hotfixes visible to the guest will synchronize with what is present on the host.

bugs.title: TMM core due to SIGSEGV
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core due to a SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: Occurs rarely. Specific conditions unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an intermittent tmm core related to Bug 540571.

bugs.title: TMM cores when multicast address is set as destination IP via iRules and LSN is configured
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core when an iRule changes the destination address of a connection to use a multicast address such as 224.0.0.1. When the BIG-IP system looks up the route, it returns an internal route with no interface designed for use with multicast traffic. LSN expects to find an interface and crashes when it attempts to use the non-existent interface.
bugs.conditions: - CGNAT enabled and LSN pools configured on active virtual server that accepts traffic. - On the same virtual server, an iRule is configured that changes the destination IP to a multicast address in the 224.0.0.0/24 network.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Remove the offending iRule that is sending traffic to the 224.0.0.0/24 network. -- Prevent traffic from using that destination in the iRule.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when multicast address is set as destination IP via iRules and LSN is configured. Now, the system fails connections when the route's IFC is null, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: big3d may fail to install on systems configured with an SSH banner
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system is configured to display a banner at SSH login, big3d_install may be unable to update the big3d daemon on that device.
bugs.conditions: sshd banner enabled.
bugs.impact: big3d_install fails to install big3d on the target remote BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: 1. Disable the SSH banner on the target device: tmsh modify /sys sshd banner disabled. 2. Add the target: bigip_add target_name. 3. Re-enable the SSH banner: tmsh modify /sys sshd banner enabled.
bugs.fix: big3d now installs correctly on systems configured with an SSH banner.

bugs.title: GUI Device Management Overview to display device_trust_group
bugs.symptoms: The Device Management Overview page is displaying a blank page in the Device Groups panel.
bugs.conditions: No special condition is required.
bugs.impact: The Device Management Overview page does not display any information. This might be especially confusing when devices are not in sync.
bugs.fix: Device Management Overview page now displays the device and device group details in the Device Groups panel.

bugs.title: Multiple SIGSEGV with core and failover with no logged indicator
bugs.symptoms: A multimodule HA pair under high load fails over.
bugs.conditions: This can occur with multiple modules configured (AFM, ASM, APM, GTM, LTM) and high concurrent load.
bugs.impact: Instability in HA.
bugs.fix: Fix to free memory with same length as used for alloc using umem_alloc.

bugs.title: Parsing malformed keys may cause BIND to exit due to a failed assertion in buffer.c
bugs.symptoms: Parsing a malformed DNSSEC key can cause a validating resolver to exit due to a failed assertion in buffer.c
bugs.conditions: BIND Versions affected: 9.9.0->9.9.7-P2, 9.10.0->9.10.2-P3
bugs.impact: It is possible for a remote attacker to deliberately trigger this condition, for example by using a query which requires a response from a zone containing a deliberately malformed key
bugs.fix: Upgrade BIND to latest: 9.9.7-P3

bugs.title: An incorrect boundary check can trigger a REQUIRE assertion failure in openpgpkey_61.c
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect boundary check in openpgpkey_61.c can cause named to terminate due to a REQUIRE assertion failure
bugs.conditions: BIND Versions affected: 9.9.7 -> 9.9.7-P2, 9.10.2 -> 9.10.2-P3
bugs.impact: A server which encounters this error will terminate due to a REQUIRE assertion failure, resulting in denial of service to clients
bugs.fix: Upgrade BIND to latest: 9.9.7-P3

bugs.title: Update/deletion of SNMPv3 user does not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: After creation of an SNMPv3 user via the GUI, SNMP operations for that user do not work if the admin subsequently modifies the user. Deletion of the SNMPv3 user also does not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: Save (even without modification) an SNMPv3 user after creation, or delete an SNMPv3 user.
bugs.impact: SNMP operations for that user do not work if the admin subsequently modifies the user. TMSH reports a deleted user as gone, but net-snmp does not process the deletion.
bugs.fix: Using the GUI to update/delete SNMPv3 users now works as expected.

bugs.title: Config sync fails after creating a partition.
bugs.symptoms: Config sync fails after creating a partition. A config sync error similar to the following occurs: Configuration error: Can't associate (/P1/pool1) with folder (/P1) folder does not exist
bugs.conditions: This error occurs when a folder is created in the same transaction that an object is also created in that folder. This can be done either by explicitly using tmsh or iControl transaction mechanisms or through incremental sync of APM where folders get created.
bugs.impact: A transaction will fail or incremental sync on APM will fail on a peer.
bugs.workaround: In the case of transactions, create partitions and folders in a separate transaction from any object creation. For incremental sync of APM, force a full sync by using the 'Overwrite Configuration' option in the UI.

bugs.title: Unevenly loaded tmms while using syncookies may cause occasional spurious connection resets.
bugs.symptoms: Flows for a syncookie-enabled listener might occasionally receive a RST after responding correctly to a syncookie challenge.
bugs.conditions: -- Fast Flow Forwarding is enabled. -- At least one tmm thread is heavily loaded, with higher memory utilization, but has not reached its syncookie thresholds. -- At least one other tmm thread is less heavily loaded but has met its syncookie threshold. -- Syncookie activation is recorded on only one tmm thread.
bugs.impact: Occasional clients take an incorrect path and have their valid syncookie ACKs rejected with a TCP RST and must retry.
bugs.workaround: Set db variable tmm.ffwd.enable = false. Doing this may modestly reduce peak performance on CPU bound loads.
bugs.fix: Fixed occasional RST in response to valid syncookie ACKs when under uneven load.

bugs.title: TMSH list node filtering no longer filters correctly.
bugs.symptoms: In some circumstances the use of filters in the 'tmsh list ltm node' command no longer works correctly, returning all values instead.
bugs.conditions: Use of filter in the 'tmsh list ltm node' command.
bugs.impact: Filter is not applied, so all results are returned.

bugs.title: Memory leak due to unnecessary logging profile configuration updates.
bugs.symptoms: There is a memory leak in ASM control plane daemons after processing many calls in a long lived process
bugs.conditions: A) Pool member state changes frequently. or B) Manual learning is enabled (versions 12.x)
bugs.impact: Memory consumption by ASM control plane daemons increases.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM - which will cause a failover and a down time OR just kill asm_config_server by: ----------------------- pkill -f asm_config_server ----------------------- which will get restarted back by ASM process watchdog in ~15 seconds and should not cause failover nor downtime.
bugs.fix: An async worker lifecycle was introduced so long lived processes will now dispatch a fixed number of calls to their workers before retiring them.

bugs.title: Monitors with a send attribute set to 'none' are lost on save
bugs.symptoms: Monitors that have a send, recv, or recv-disable attribute set to 'none' are lost on configuration save.
bugs.impact: Monitor may send unexpected string.
bugs.fix: Monitor send, recv, and recv-disable attributes now retains a 'none' value on configuration save.
bugs.conditions: Monitor has a send, recv, or recv-disable attribute set to 'none'.

bugs.title: Safenet connection may fail on restarting pkcs11d or HSM reboot or if the connection to HSM is lost and then resumed
bugs.symptoms: netHSM usage may fail for Safenet users with error message in the ltm log similar to the following: warning tmm1[11930]: 01260009:4: Connection error: ssl_hs_vfy_sign_srvkeyxchg:9678: sign_srvkeyxchg (80). info tmm1[11930]: 01260013:6: SSL Handshake failed for TCP 10.10.0.1:59513 -> 10.10.1.150:20001. warning pkcs11d[12005]: 01680022:4: Crypto operation [2] failed. crit tmm1[11930]: 01260010:2: FIPS acceleration device failure: fips_poll_completed_reqs: req: 56 status: 0x1 : Cancel.
bugs.conditions: This may happen for any of the following conditions: -- Restart pkcs11d without starting tmm immediately after. -- Network connection between the BIG-IP and HSM is interrupted and then restored. -- HSM is rebooted without being followed by a restart to pkcs11d and tmm.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake failure with a message similar to the following: SSL Handshake failed for TCP 10.10.0.1:59513 -> 10.10.1.150:20001.
bugs.workaround: For Safenet, always restart tmm after restarting pkcs11d. To do so, run the following commands: bigstart restart pkcs11d bigstart restart tmm When the networking to HSM is restored or after a HSM reboot, always run the following commands: bigstart restart pkcs11d bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: After restarting pkcs11d, Safenet connections no longer fails with the message 'cannot locate key'.

bugs.title: HTTP/HTTPS monitors transmit unexpected data to monitored node.
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/HTTPS) monitors send unexpected data (crlfcrlf) after completion of TCP and/or SSL handshake.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/HTTPS monitor with a send attribute set to 'none'. HTTP/HTTPS monitors with a 'none' send string should complete the TCP handshake(+SSL handshake) and then close the connection without sending any data.
bugs.impact: A monitor configured with a 'none' send string sends a 4-byte string, \r\n\r\n (crlfcrlf), after completing the handshake. This is ignored by the monitored node, which might cause it to be marked down.
bugs.fix: HTTP/HTTPS monitor no longer transmits any L7 data when send attribute is set to 'none'.

bugs.title: Network Access clients experience delays when resolving a host
bugs.symptoms: The DNS Relay proxy for Network Access clients operating in split-tunnel mode intercepts a client's DNS request for a non-matching host and will forward it to the client's local DNS server. If the client contains multiple NICs, one containing a down or invalid DNS server, this could cause a delay in resolving the host.
bugs.conditions: Network Access with the DNS Relay Proxy configured A client machine has multiple NICs One of the NICs has an invalid or down DNS server configured Client attempts to resolve a host not matching the Network Access policy
bugs.impact: Clients will experience unusual delays (10+ seconds) when resolving hosts.
bugs.workaround: Clients can check their system setup and remove the affected interfaces that contain an invalid DNS server (virtual machine network adapters are becoming increasingly common and can exhibit this), or they can ensure that they are mapped only to valid DNS servers that can resolve the host.
bugs.fix: The DNS Relay proxy will now avoid sending DNS requests to down DNS servers for DNS requests that do not match the Network Access policy while Network Access is connected.

bugs.title: Clientless NA fails when iRule agent is present in access policy
bugs.symptoms: The failure happens when we get the redirect to /vdesk/webtop.eui. This is in the whitelist as a portal protected URI, and when it doesn't have a valid sid, the action is to create a new session. Because this is clientless mode, there aren't any cookies, so it thinks it needs to create a new session. Then the old session is deleted, causing the logs to report a logout due to user request.
bugs.conditions: Windows 8.1 + APM 11.5.3. Logon page -> irule agent -> Advanced resource assign (NA+NA webtop) -> Allow (no auth for logon page, everything should lead to allow) Try to log on with the Windows inbox VPN client.
bugs.impact: VPN connection Failed; stating error invalid credentials. Logs show session deleted due to user logout request.

bugs.title: Unexpected transition from Forced Offline to Standby to Active
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP configuration is reset to default, and then restored from a saved UCS that was taken while the system was Forced Offline, the system will be restored to the Forced Offline state, but the state may not persist across reboots.
bugs.conditions: Restore a saved UCS that was created while the BIG-IP system was Forced Offline.
bugs.impact: System may unexpectedly go Active after a reboot.
bugs.fix: Device forced offline remains forced offline after restoring a UCS and rebooting.

bugs.title: Sync of tunnels might cause restore of deleted tunnels.
bugs.symptoms: After a full load sync, tunnels may be spuriously added to the default route domain for the partition that contains them.
bugs.conditions: Viewing tunnels after a full load sync.
bugs.impact: This might result in a deleted tunnel being restored to the configuration.
bugs.fix: Sync of tunnels no longer causes restore of deleted tunnels.

bugs.title: Component installation appears hung if wrong password is entered
bugs.symptoms: While establishing network access with APM, APM might require admin password to install components responsible establishing network access. Installation appears hung if wrong "sudo" or "root" password is entered on this screen.
bugs.conditions: Network access, Linux OS, firefox browser client.
bugs.impact: Bad user experience.
bugs.workaround: Once the wrong password is entered restart the browser and reestablish connection with BIG-IP and enter correct password.

bugs.title: ASM REST: XML Profile Validation File Associations are Removed on a Partial PATCH Request
bugs.symptoms: Updating an XML Profile via ASM REST with a partial body (ex. just an updated description) removes all attached WSDL validation files as if it had also received: "validationFiles": []
bugs.conditions: XML Profiles that utilize validation files are updated via REST
