bugs.impact: If the full validation files structure is not re-iterated in the body, then the entire list of WSDL validation files will be emptied. This will cause the XML Schema to not be validated properly during enforcement.
bugs.workaround: Run the validation file association task again after updating the XML Profile
bugs.fix: ASM REST now correctly updates only specified fields on a PATCH request.

bugs.title: AWS AMIs for BIG-IP VE will now have volumes set to be deleted upon instance termination.
bugs.symptoms: The default settings of an AMI is not to delete an attached volume of an instance when the instance is terminated. This results in extra effort to delete a volume manually after terminating the instance. If not done always, the orphaned volume causes extra bills.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP VE is launched from an AMI in the marketplace.
bugs.impact: Volumes attached to BIG-IP VE instances will be deleted automatically when the instance is terminated. This option is set to be default now. If you want to keep a volume even after terminating a BIG-IP VE instance, you will have to set it to not be deleted upon termination during instance launch in AWS console.
bugs.fix: A BIG-IP VE AWS image now has the option set such that when an instance is launched out of it, that BIG-IP VE instance will have volumes which are set to be deleted upon termination by default.
bugs.behavior: A BIG-IP VE AWS image now has the option set such that when an instance is launched out of it, that BIG-IP VE instance will have volumes which are set to be deleted upon termination by default.

bugs.title: Defining more than 10 remote-role groups can result in authentication failure
bugs.symptoms: Authentication fails, indicating the affected user is associated with an "unknown" role: notice httpd[2112]: pam_bigip_authz: authenticated user bob with role 12345678 ([unknown]) in partition /bin/false
bugs.conditions: Define more than 10 remote-role groups and authenticate with a user having more than 10 roles.
bugs.impact: User cannot authenticate.

bugs.title: IPsec NAT-T (IKEv1) not working properly
bugs.symptoms: The incorrect source port is chosen for the IPsec/IKE NAT-T UDP encapsulated traffic. When IKE decides to float port when NAT device is detected, it should use port 4500 for both its source port and destination port.
bugs.conditions: NAT traversal is enabled on the IKE Peer configuration object and NAT device is detected during IKE negotiation.
bugs.impact: When NAT-T is enabled, IPsec tunnel cannot be established.
bugs.fix: Now, when NAT-T is enabled, IPsec tunnel can be established as expected.

bugs.title: FQDN ephemeral nodes not repopulated after recreating with swapped IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, ephemeral nodes that are force-deleted may not repopulate as expected.
bugs.conditions: Sync group, multiple FQDNs resolving to different IP addresses. FQDNs deleted and re-created, with IP addresses swapped from deleted nodes to re-created ones.
bugs.impact: Ephemeral nodes may not repopulate as expected.
bugs.fix: FQDN ephemeral nodes are now repopulated after being force-deleted and re-created with different IP addresses.

bugs.title: PEM : Diameter virtual reconfiguration might stop CCR-I/U/T going out for subscriber sessions
bugs.symptoms: Radius Start, Stop does not trigger any diameter traffic except DWR/DWA.
bugs.conditions: Diameter virtual reconfiguration and possibly any virtual configuration change might trigger this behavior.
bugs.impact: Subscriber sessions created by radius are not provisioned by the PCRF. Sessions that are deleted are also not reported to PCRF or Usage reports are also not reported.
bugs.workaround: Restarting TMM is the only work around for now.
bugs.fix: Issue has been fixed now. Even if diameter configuration is changed there should be no impact on CCR-I/U/T being stopped.

bugs.title: APD/APMD Crashes While Verifying CAPTCHA
bugs.symptoms: APD (pre v12.0.0) or APMD (v12.0.0) crashes in libcurl function when verifying CAPTCHA
bugs.conditions: This issue shows up when multiple sessions are being verified for CAPTCHA at SimpleLogonPageAgent.
bugs.impact: Authentication service will be disrupted until APD/APMD is up again.
bugs.fix: Create one cURL session for each user session that requires CAPTCHA verification

bugs.title: Memory leak and potential crash bug in secure channel cookie handling
bugs.symptoms: Under certain rare circumstances, the process handling secure channel cookies may leak memory. It may also result in underflow crashes in Tcl and other processes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under rare conditions.
bugs.impact: Eventual out of memory condition or crash.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a memory leak and potential crash bug in secure channel cookie handling.

bugs.title: Monitor inheriting time-until-up and up-interval from parent incorrectly via GU
bugs.symptoms: Monitors inherit incorrect time-until-up and up-interval from parent.
bugs.conditions: Create a parent monitor with non-default time-until-up and up-interval values. Using the GUI, create a child monitor.
bugs.impact: The child monitor's time-until-up interval value is set to default (0). The up-interval value is incorrectly inherited from the parent.
bugs.workaround: Set the time-until-up value for the child to the desired value.

bugs.title: Sync-only device groups cannot be applied to iApp-generated configs
bugs.symptoms: Sync-only device groups cannot be applied to the /Common folder or any folder containing ties to /Common. iApps make reference to objects in /Common, often including the iApp template itself (e.g., /Common/f5.http). There is no issue with failover device-groups.
bugs.conditions: When sync-only device groups and iApps are used together.
bugs.impact: Sync cannot be set up.
bugs.workaround: Copy and reconfigure the iApp template to load in a folder other than /Common. If the iApp is tied to a CLI script, the script and all references to the script must also be moved to a non-Common folder.

bugs.title: ASM REST: PATCH to XML Profiles with unmodified "validationFiles" fails
bugs.symptoms: The "validationFiles" is not allowed to be modified via a PATCH call and will fail validation. Even if validationFiles is passed back in unmodified, the call still fails.
bugs.conditions: An ASM REST client attempts to PATCH the mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/xml-profiles/<ID> endpoint using "validationFiles"
bugs.impact: The XML Profile cannot be modified
bugs.workaround: The user can PATCH the object without supplying this field. However if there were Validation Files before, then Bug 541406 will affect them, removing the existing Validation Files. The XML validation file association task would then need to be run again.
bugs.fix: ASM REST: The system correctly recognizes that the validationFiles field has not changed in value and does not fail the call.

bugs.title: tmm segfault: hud_process_upper
bugs.symptoms: The tmm fails with a segmentation fault in hud_process_upper.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely occurring issue whose causes are not well understood.
bugs.impact: The tmm fails and restarts.

bugs.title: tmm might loop and get killed by sod when the system tries to process an invalid-message-length MPI message.
bugs.symptoms: tmm might loop and get killed by sod when the system tries to process an invalid-message-length MPI message. You might notice the following in /var/log/ltm prior to the core: notice MPI stream: connection to node nodedadress expired for reason: Internal error (bad magic) (mpi_proxy.c:664)
bugs.conditions: This is an internal condition related to TMMs passing messages between each other. The cause of the invalid internal message is unknown.
bugs.impact: tmm might loop, using 100% of CPU, and eventually get killed by sod.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer loops and gets killed by sod when the system tries to process an invalid MPI message.

bugs.title: Update to RHEL6 kernel
bugs.symptoms: Rare race condition between two (or more) threads operating on the same buffer_head/journal_head may cause a kernel panic
bugs.conditions: Running RHEL6 kernel under heavy disk load, more likely on a vCMP host
bugs.impact: Unexpected machine reboot causing loss of service
bugs.fix: Redhat provided an update to RHEL6.7 F5 backported to RHEL6.4, 6.5: jbd2: Fix oops in jbd2_journal_remove_journal_head() jbd: Fix oops in journal_remove_journal_head()

bugs.title: In rare circumstances, it is possible for the TCP timestamps sent by the BIG-IP system to be inconsistent between blades.
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances, it is possible for the TCP timestamps sent by the BIG-IP system to be inconsistent between blades. TCP monitors may fail because the server fails to respond to the initial TCP SYN. TCP traffic that utilizes a SNAT may fail because the server fails to respond to the initial TCP SYN.
bugs.conditions: A server with tcp_tw_recycle enabled. A multi-blade BIG-IP chassis.
bugs.impact: Monitor failures or traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: After confirming that the time is properly synchronized across the chassis, reboot the chassis. Alternatively, if your servers do not require tcp_tw_recycle to be enabled, it is recommended that you disable this setting on your servers.

bugs.title: TMM continually restarts due to HSB failure
bugs.symptoms: The HSB device returns invalid data to TMM, resulting in a TMM core. This condition persists for each TMM start and can be observed in the TMM logs as a series of SIGSEGV or SIGFPE signals every time TMM attempts to start.
bugs.conditions: -- It is unknown under what conditions this error occurs. -- This occurs only on BIG-IP 6900 (D104), 3900 (C106), and 8900 (D106) platforms.
bugs.impact: TMM continually restarts, requiring manual intervention to reboot the unit. Traffic disrupted.

bugs.title: Snmpd V1 and V2c view based access.
bugs.symptoms: SNMP v3 allows for 'views' to be created. These views can be a union of multiple sub-branch OID access config statements. Users/groups can then be assigned to a view.
bugs.conditions: If more that one snmpd view is specified per community string the second view is not accessible. Note: A view is a portion of a MIB tree defined by an OID.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not support view configuration. If multiple views are created using the lines: rouser USER [noauth|auth|priv [OID]], the system adds only one of them to the snmpd.conf file.
bugs.workaround: Multiple views with the same community string are not supported.

bugs.title: GUI might cause MIB files to be uncompressed when downloading from GUI with Chrome.
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances the BIG-IP GUI might cause MIB files to be served uncompressed, but with tar.gz extension.
bugs.conditions: Use Chrome to download BIG-IP MIB files from the GUI.
bugs.impact: MIB files are uncompressed.
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to uncompress the MIB files further if downloaded with Chrome. Simply untar and use as normal. Renaming the file may help avoid further confusion.

bugs.title: no login name may appear when running ssh commands through management port
bugs.symptoms: ssh root@mgmt_port_ip_address "bash -cl 'tmsh show sys sof'" displays "logname: no login name"
bugs.conditions: ssh root@mgmt_port_ip_address "bash -cl 'tmsh show sys sof'" displays "logname: no login name"
bugs.impact: Display issue
bugs.fix: Properly display login name

bugs.title: Portal rewrite does not properly transform responses generated by BIG-IP as SAML IdP
bugs.symptoms: SAML IdP responses are not properly rewritten through the reverse proxy engine.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP as IdP (SAML and Portal Access) with a service provider that is not a BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Although SAML and Portal Access are not supported in this configuration, SAML IdP responses should not be bypassing the Portal Access rewrite engine.

bugs.title: Denied message in audit log on first time boot
bugs.symptoms: After booting BIG-IP for the first time, you may see a 'denied' message for the lastlog file in /var/log/audit.log: type=AVC msg=audit(1440786377.593:32): avc: denied { read write } for pid=5922 comm="login" name="lastlog" dev=md2 ino=18 scontext=system_u:system_r:local_login_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 tcontext=system_u:object_r:var_log_t:s0 tclass=file.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on first time boot of devices that contain version 11.x software in one of the image slots.
bugs.impact: This error message is benign and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is cosmetic and does not indicate an issue with the system.
bugs.fix: Fixed an erroneous error message in the audit log related to lastlog during manufacturing install.

bugs.title: SSL::disable for alerts does not take effect and first alert fails
bugs.symptoms: Command 'SSL::disable serverside' fails when sending alerts.
bugs.conditions: The alert is received on an already established clientside TCP connection that has a current connection through to the regular virtual server pool member.
bugs.impact: Alert may take a very long time (more than 30 seconds) to receive a response from the alert server.
bugs.workaround: To resolve the issue, add a OneConnect profile to the virtual server, or use an iRule that performs an 'LB::detach' when a request is received for /rstats/.
bugs.fix: Command 'SSL::disable serverside' now completes successfully when sending alerts.

bugs.title: 'Unhandled keyword ()' error message in GUI and/or various ASM logs
bugs.symptoms: 'Unhandled keyword ()' error message may appear in 'Session Awareness Tracking' GUI page and/or various ASM logs, such as: learning manager log, asm config server log, main asm log. In the case of learning manager, it causes a crash of the latter. Learning manager process is then restarted ~15 seconds later.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. Session Awareness Tracking is enabled.
bugs.impact: Uninformative errors in 'Session Awareness Tracking' GUI page and/or various ASM logs, such as: learning manager log, asm config server log, main asm log. Learning manager process restart.
bugs.fix: Learning manager now handles the 'Unhandled keyword ()' exception in a graceful manner and does not crash.

bugs.title: bigd detection and logging of load and overload
bugs.symptoms: The bigd process cannot detect overload, and does not log its load status. This makes it difficult to determine whether bigd is close to its limits.
bugs.conditions: The bigd process might reach limits when there is very high load with high probe rate (monitor instances per second).
bugs.impact: bigd might fail to service monitors in a timely fashion, when under extreme load, which might result in 'flapping' nodes/pool members (where the node/pool member goes down and back up even though the server itself has not gone down).
bugs.workaround: -- Increase the probe interval for monitors so they probe less often. -- Switch from more 'expensive' monitors (e.g., https) to simpler monitors (e.g., http, tcp, tcp half-open, icmp).
bugs.fix: This release provides modifications to peak performance to significantly reduce the chance of node flapping. In addition, the ability to monitor bigd load has been added. Because bigd is not integrated with tmstats, the system logs load stats to the debug log file, /var/log/bigdlog. When debug logging is turned on, stats are mixed with the debug output. Load stats can be emitted independently with the following sys db var: modify sys db bigd.debug.timingstats value enable. With this db variable enabled, the system emits bigd load data to the debug log periodically (every 15 seconds per bigd process). The columns correspond to these stats: - load (0-100%) 1-minute mean. - load (0-100%) 5-minute mean. - number of monitor instances active for this bigd process. - number of active file descriptors, 30-second average, this process. - peak number of active file descriptors past 30 seconds, this process. In addition, the system logs warning messages to /var/log/ltm when bigd reaches 80%, 90%, and 95% load levels. The system logs an overload error to /var/log/ltm when bigd detects it is overloaded. The load level indicating overload is in the bigd.overload.latency sys db variable, which is set to 98% load, by default.

bugs.title: WebSafe alerts with HTML attached cause the page to run slowly
bugs.symptoms: When 'Attach HTML to alerts' is enabled, large webpages might run slowly.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Attach HTML to alerts' is enabled. -- Page source is large. -- WebSafe alert is sent. -- Using Microsoft Internet Explorer version 8 (IE8) or earlier browser version.
bugs.impact: Page may experience a noticeable delay in reacting to user actions.
bugs.workaround: Disable 'Attach HTML to alerts'. Use beforeloadfunction to disable only on IE8: function(c){ function isOldIE(ver) { var ua = navigator.userAgent.toLowerCase(); return (ua.indexOf('msie') > -1) ? parseInt(ua.split('msie')[1]) <= ver : false; } if (isOldIE(8)) { c.A.B.P = false; } }
bugs.fix: HTML encoding for WebSafe alerts is now faster and can be configured to send only a section of the page source.

bugs.title: Fallback alert mechanism can result in page refresh in Internet Explorer 8
bugs.symptoms: If browser sent alerts fail to be received, secondary sending mechanisms may cause page to refresh in browser.
bugs.conditions: Internet explorer 8 or older. HTML page with websafe enabled. HTML page contains a form. Alert sent. Alert receives failed response.
bugs.impact: HTML page refreshes in browser
bugs.fix: Fallback alert mechanism no longer results in page refresh in older browsers.

bugs.title: APM logon page copyright should show the current year
bugs.symptoms: APM logon page shows copyright valid to 1999-2014.
bugs.conditions: -- APM logon page. -- Running v11.5.3.
bugs.impact: Incorrect copyright date.
bugs.workaround: Go to customization, select the profile, and change footer text.

bugs.title: bigd intentionally cores when it should shutdown cleanly
bugs.symptoms: Bigd can core instead of graceful shutdown under certain error conditions where a core is not needed.
bugs.conditions: Anything that caused bigd to shutdown under abnormal conditions.
bugs.impact: Bigd crash, core file created. Note that the shutdown scenario was already under error conditions, so this is not a sign that something has broken or failed outside that condition that caused the shutdown.
bugs.fix: Made bigd more selective about the situations where it self-cores on abnormal shutdown.

bugs.title: bigd may experience a heartbeat failure when tcp-half-open monitors are used
bugs.symptoms: bigd generates a core file and restarts. The system writes a message to /var/log/ltm that is similar to the following: notice sod[6504]: 01140029:5: HA daemon_heartbeat bigd fails action is restart.
bugs.conditions: tcp-half-open monitors are in use.
bugs.impact: bigd restarts and there is an interruption in monitoring.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, but this has been seen extremely rarely.

bugs.title: No default boot volume is set when installing a vCMP guest from a hotfix iso.
bugs.symptoms: When creating a vCMP guest using both an initial-image and initial-hotfix, the default boot volume is not set. This causes any future software installation performed inside that guest to automatically become the default boot volume.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a vCMP guest is created from a hotfix build of BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: The default boot location is not set, which causes subsequent software installations inside the guest to be automatically marked default. Upon a reboot of an affected guest, the system boots into a newly installed volume, which might not be the desired behavior.
bugs.workaround: Once the vCMP guest is running perform the following steps: 1. Login to the guest via ssh or the vconsole utility. 2. Run the switchboot utility. 3. Select the appropriate volume to be the default boot location (there might be only one option in this list). 4. Press enter. If the selected boot location is the current or only volume, it is marked as the default boot volume and the guest does not reboot. If the selected boot location is not the currently booted volume, the guest immediately reboots into the selected volume. Verify the operation was successful by issuing the command: grub_default -l. The output of the command should resemble this: -- config # grub_default -l HD1.1 active yes default yes title BIG-IP 11.6.0 Build 5.0.429 As long as the appropriate volume is marked 'default yes', the operation is complete.

bugs.title: If there is OCSP Stapling enabled on a clientSSL profile, under certain remote conditions, TMM could crash
bugs.symptoms: If there is OCSP Stapling enabled on a clientSSL profile, under certain remote conditions, TMM could crash.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - There is an OCSP request in progress. - There is a configuration change. - The handshake is aborted. - The HTTP response for the OCSP request indicates a status code that is not 200.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes if there is OCSP Stapling enabled on a clientSSL profile, under certain remote conditions.

bugs.title: SNMP reports invalid data from global_stat, avg server-side cur_conns (for 5s, 1m, 5m).
bugs.symptoms: SNMP reports invalid data from global_stat, avg server-side cur_conns (for 5s, 1m, 5m).
bugs.conditions: Querying the OIDs.
bugs.impact: Unable to monitor the moving averages of the current connection counts as they return 0.
bugs.workaround: There is no known workaround.
bugs.fix: SNMP now reports valid data from global_stat, avg server-side cur_conns (for 5s, 1m, 5m).

bugs.title: Tmm crash observed during load testing
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes, stack trace in logs.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server has a 0.0.0.0:3868, port 3868 is not disabled and the vlan list is not disabled for the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Block the port 3868 in this case or disable the virtual's vlan list to prevent creation of client side connection.

bugs.title: Specific numbers that are not credit card numbers are being masked as such
bugs.symptoms: ASM blocks or masks when a specific credit card number range with specific length appears in the response.
bugs.conditions: The Data Guard feature is turned on and set to Block, Alarm or Mask. The responses contains credit card numbers with specific ranges.
bugs.impact: The traffic passes masked or blocked to the end client.
bugs.workaround: a partial workaround is to turn off the Data Guard feature, then none of the credit cards numbers will be masked nor blocked.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly masks and/or blocks only relevant credit cards, specifically not masking credit card numbers starting with specific number that are in a length range.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when IPsec SA are deleted during HA Active to Standby or vice versa event
bugs.symptoms: TMM can crash when IPsec SA's are deleted using TMSH or racoonctl utility during HA Active to Standby or vice versa.
bugs.conditions: During the HA Active to standby or vice versa event, Use of TMSH or racoonctl utility to delete IPsec SA's can cause TMM crash. This is a race condition and can occur rarely.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Running TMSH command or racoonctl utility to delete IPsec SA's during HA Active to Standby or vice versa event does not result in TMM crash and IPsec SA's will be deleted as per the request.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system should support cipher suites ChaCha20 and Poly1305
bugs.symptoms: This release adds support for cipher suites ChaCha20 and Poly1305.
bugs.conditions: Using cipher suites.
bugs.impact: Can now configure ChaCha20 and Poly1305.
bugs.fix: This release provides support for ChaCha20 and Poly1305.
bugs.behavior: This release adds support for cipher suite ChaCha20 and Poly1305 to the crypto library.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition: Disk partition /var shows 100% after live install to 12.0.0
bugs.symptoms: After installing a new Virtual Edition software instance and booting into it, disk partition /var shows 100%
bugs.conditions: Virtual Edition only
bugs.impact: System is generally un-usable; applications cannot operate without space in /var.
bugs.workaround: 1) reboot into the previous software location 2) delete the new software location that is non-functional 3) remove this file: /shared/.tmi_config/global_attributes 4) install the new software again.
bugs.fix: after applying the fix, subsequent operations that install new software will size the /var filesystem appropriately.

bugs.title: Logging profile with trailing whitespace cannot be associated with VS in GUI
bugs.symptoms: A security logging profile with trailing whitespace cannot be associated with a Virtual Server from the "Virtual Server > Security" page in GUI.
bugs.conditions: The user attempts to associate a security logging profile with trailing whitespace with a Virtual Server from the "Virtual Server > Security" page in GUI.
bugs.impact: An error message occurs ("01020036:3: The requested firewall virtual log profile (/Common/profile name) was not found.").
bugs.workaround: The logging profile can be associated with the Virtual Server using tmsh. Also, please note that trailing whitespace on a configuration entity is not recommended and the issue can be easily avoided by adhering to entity naming best practices.

bugs.title: Upgrading v11.6.0 to v12.x in a sync-failover group might cause mcpd to become unresponsive.
bugs.symptoms: Failover event on traffic-group-1 causes mcpd to generate messages like this: 01070711:3: Caught runtime exception, Failed to collect files (Invalid IP Address: ).. 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files.. ... 0107134b:3: (Child rsync being terminated due to timeout. Total size in Kb: 0 timeout in secs: 10 start-time: Mon Aug 24 11:35:42 2015 max-end-time: Mon Aug 24 11:35:42 2015 time now: Mon Aug 24 11:35:42 2015 ) errno(0) errstr(). 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files..
bugs.conditions: -- Some systems in the trust are running a pre-12.x version of TMOS. -- Some systems in a device group have been upgraded to 12.x. -- A failover event occurs on traffic-group-1. -- This appears to be most evident in APM configurations.
bugs.impact: mcpd on the devices running pre-12.x version may become unresponsive. Upgrade fails.
bugs.fix: This release corrects an issue in which a group of devices in a trust domain could potentially cause mcpd to become unresponsive and log failure messages.

bugs.title: Global traffic statistics does not include PVA statistics
bugs.symptoms: Global traffic statistics shown in the GUI and in TMSH are not correct.
bugs.conditions: Hardware acceleration enabled.
bugs.impact: Statistics discrepancy in global traffic statistics.
bugs.fix: Global traffic statistics now includes the correct PVA statistics in the GUI and in TMSH.

bugs.title: apd may crash if an un-encoded session variable contains "0x"
bugs.symptoms: when a session variable value contains "0x" (for example 'value0x not encoded'), apd process treat the value as HEX-encoded and tries to decode it. decoding the not-encoded string causes apd to crash
bugs.conditions: session variable contains substring "0x"
bugs.impact: apd crash
bugs.fix: With this release: 1. Only values starting from 0x are treated as hex-encoded. 2. If hex decoding fails, apd does not crash.

bugs.title: ACCESS iRule commands do not work reliably in HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST event
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system is configured with explicit HTTP proxy, ACCESS iRule does not work reliably in HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST. The issue happens when the current ACCESS iRule searches the associated session ID from the connection itself in these ways: either the session ID is embedded in the request, or the connection has been processed by ACCESS previously. When neither condition is satisfied, then current ACCESS iRule cannot find the associated session ID.
bugs.conditions: ACCESS iRule such as ACCESS::session data get/set, ACCESS::session exists, session ID is not provided by the caller, and caller expects the session ID to be resolved internally.
bugs.impact: Whenever ACCESS iRule commands cannot find the associated session ID, ACCESS iRule commands are processed as if the caller provided an empty session ID in its arguments. As a result, ACCESS::iRule commands return an empty result.
bugs.workaround: If possible, use ACCESS_ACL_ALLOWED as the event for the iRule, when the session ID is known. This would work for a BIG-IP system configured for reverse proxy or forward proxy.
bugs.fix: Fixed to allow ACCESS iRule commands in commands such as HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST where previously there was not enough data for them to execute. Note that this fix is only for IP based sessions where the access policy is NOT evaluated via iRule, but in the usual method (attached to virtual). A separate bug has been created to address the issue for NTLM based sessions and sessions where "ACCESS::policy evaluate" has been used.

bugs.title: Update kernel to latest public RHEL6.4 kernel: 2.6.32-358.61.1.el6
bugs.symptoms: This is a major update from RHEL6.4 2.6.32-358.23.2 used in 11.6.0 releases (including all 11.6.0 hotfixes). This includes many critical bugfixes and security fixes as of the last published kernel Redhat Security Advisory: https://rhn.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2015-1030.html Note that there are some additional security fixes beyond RHSA-2015-1030.html which have been backported from upstream RHEL6 kernels: 6.5, 6.6 and 6.7. This does not include later 6.4 kernel updates from Redhat which are only available for Redhat AUS customers: https://rhn.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2015-1211.html https://rhn.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2015-1643.html https://rhn.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2015-1843.html https://rhn.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2015-2005.html https://rhn.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2016-0004.html
bugs.conditions: This is a kernel-related update.
bugs.impact: Addresses many critical bugfixes and security fixes.
bugs.workaround: None needed.
bugs.fix: Updated kernel to 2.6.32-358.61.1.el6 [RHEL6.4].

bugs.title: Serverside connections may fail to detach when using the HTTP and OneConnect profiles
bugs.symptoms: Serverside connection does not detach when using OneConnect profile
bugs.conditions: An HTTP/1.1 response without Content-Length header is received in response to an HTTP/1.0 HEAD request
bugs.impact: HTTP requests on the same connection are not LB'ed across pool members.
bugs.workaround: Remove OneConnect profile
bugs.fix: Ensure serverside detachment when handling HTTP responses to HEAD requests.

bugs.title: Expose pre_established_connections in tmm.tcp and tmm.tcp4
bugs.symptoms: The pre_established_connections profile setting is used to ensure BIG-IP does not respond to the clients SYN with a SYN-ACK until it receives a SYN-ACK from the server, indicating that the port is open (default value is false). However these statistics are not visible in tmstat.
bugs.conditions: Profiles with pre_established_connections set to true
bugs.impact: Unable to see the statistics, network troubleshooting difficulty.
bugs.fix: pre_established_connections is exposed in tmm.tcp and tmm.tcp4 as pe_connects. This value is the current number of opened but not fully established connections when using either the Verified Accept or Fast Open TCP options.

bugs.title: Verified Accept counter 'verified_accept_connections' might underflow.
bugs.symptoms: Verified Accept counter 'verified_accept_connections' might underflow.
bugs.conditions: When the verified accept setting on a TCP profile is changed for an active virtual server.
bugs.impact: When the counter underflows, new connections on any verified-accept enabled virtual server are dropped. The counter will never recover.
bugs.workaround: Avoid changing the verified accept setting on a TCP profile for an active virtual server.
bugs.fix: This release corrects the issue in which the Verified Accept counter 'verified_accept_connections' might underflow.

bugs.title: Fragmented ICMP Echo to Virtual Address may not receive response
bugs.symptoms: In a very specific scenario, a response to an IPv4 ICMP Echo to a Virtual address may not reach back to the originator.
bugs.conditions: - Client network MTU is lower than the BIG-IP system's ingress VLAN's MTU. - Client ICMP Echo is larger than Client's MTU and fragmented.
bugs.impact: Response is not received at client.
bugs.workaround: In certain version 11.x/12.x environments, it may be acceptable to disable PathMTU discovery. If it is, this can be worked around by disabling the following DB Key: tmsh modify sys db tm.pathmtudiscovery value disable Note this workaround is not possible in BIG-IP software versions 10.x. 10.x does not have a workaround.
bugs.fix: Client now receives correctly ICMP echo response from Virtual Address when echo request has been fragmented.

bugs.title: Bundled state for B2250 40G interfaces may not be displayed or show as "unsupported"
bugs.symptoms: After a clean install, the Bundled attribute for the B2250 interfaces may not be displayed or show as "unsupported". Examples: [root@localhost:/S2-green-P:NO LICENSE:Standalone] config # tmsh list net interface bundle net interface 2/1.1 { bundle not-supported <--this is expected if there is no bundling info for the interface. } ... net interface 2/2.1 { bundle not-supported <------error! } net interface 2/2.2 { bundle not-supported <-----error } net interface 2/2.3 { bundle not-supported <---error } net interface 2/2.4 { bundle not-supported <----error } net interface 2/mgmt { bundle not-supported } [root@localhost:/S2-green-P:NO LICENSE:Standalone] config # tmsh list net interface 2/2.1 2/2.2 2/2.3 2/2.4 net interface 2/2.1 { if-index 706 <--------should say "bundle disabled" mac-address 00:23:e9:82:d4:c7 media-max 40000-FD mtu 9198 } ...
bugs.conditions: Perform a clean install on a B2250 (an install where both the image is replaced and the interface configuration is overwritten with an initial configuration).
bugs.impact: The "bundle" property is not available.
bugs.workaround: Run the following tmsh command to restore bundling properties: "tmsh modify net interface 1/2.1 bundle enabled/disabled"
bugs.fix: Bundled state for B2250 40G interfaces are now displayed with the correct interface designation.

bugs.title: document.parentWindow value should be preserved
bugs.symptoms: Web-application misfunction
bugs.conditions: Non IE web-application make some decision by checking document.parentWindow value.
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used as workaround
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed.

bugs.title: bigd loses connection to mcpd on debug data dump
bugs.symptoms: The 'bigd' connection to 'mcpd' may be lost on large configurations (more than 1 KB pool members) when a debug data dump is triggered through a manual 'kill -USR1 <bigd-pid>', possibly resulting in only a partial diagnostic data dump. When the 'bigd' process is manually killed to trigger a diagnostic data dump, large configurations (with more than a thousand pool members) may cause the 'bigd' process to appear 'stuck' as those instances are logged, causing the process to be killed and restarted by the 'sod' daemon. In this case, it is possible that only a partial diagnostic dump is performed before the 'bigd' process is restarted.
bugs.conditions: -- 'bigd' is running with a large configuration (more than a thousand pool members). -- The 'bigd' process is manually killed to trigger a diagnostic dump (such as through 'kill -USR1 <bigd-pid>'). -- The 'sod' daemon finds the 'bigd' process unresponsive (causing it to terminate and restart 'bigd').
bugs.impact: The 'bigd' diagnostic dump may be incomplete, as the process was terminated before all logging information is written.
bugs.workaround: Turn off the 'bigd' heartbeat monitoring before manually initiating a 'bigd' diagnostic dump; or run a smaller representative configuration before triggering the diagnostic dump. Note: Make sure to turn back on the 'bigd' heartbeat monitoring afterward.
bugs.fix: The 'bigd' connection to 'mcpd' remains intact on large configurations (more than 1 KB pool members) when a debug data dump is triggered through a manual 'kill -USR1 <bigd-pid>', such that the diagnostic data dump is always complete.

bugs.title: BIG-IP UDP virtual server may not send ICMP Destination Unreachable message Code 3 (port unreachable).
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP UDP virtual server may not send an ICMP Destination Unreachable message Code 3 (port unreachable). As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptoms: -- Client applications may not respond or appear to hang. -- When attempting to troubleshoot the connectivity issue from remote devices, no ICMP diagnostic data is available from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: All pool members for the UDP virtual server are unavailable.
bugs.impact: In versions 11.3.0 through 11.4.1, the system silently drops the request. In versions 11.5.0 and later, the system sends back the ICMP message with type 13 ('administratively filtered').
bugs.fix: LTM now sends back an ICMP Destination Unreachable message Code 3 (port unreachable), which is expected behavior.
bugs.behavior: In version 11.2.1 and earlier, the system responded to a request with an ICMP packet containing the type code 'port unreach' when a UDP virtual server pool member was down due to no available pool members. For the same scenario in versions 11.3.0 through 11.4.1, the system sends no ICMP packet. In versions 11.5.0 through this hotfix/release, the system sends an ICMP packet containing the 'administratively filtered' type code for the same scenario. In this hotfix/release, the 11.2.1 behavior is restored. In this case, the system responds with an ICMP packet containing the type code set to 'port unreach'.

bugs.title: Unable to load certificate/key pair
bugs.symptoms: After creating SSL profile, 'could not load key/certificate file' appears in /var/log/ltm with profile name. Unable to connect to virtual with SSL profile.
bugs.conditions: Certificate uses sha1WithRSA or dsaWithSHA1_2 signature algorithm.
bugs.impact: Unable to load certificate.
bugs.fix: Can now load certificates with sha1WithRSA or dsaWithSHA1_2 signature algorithm.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system's management port drops egress Ethernet multicast traffic
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system's management port drops egress Ethernet multicast traffic. You may experience this issue if you employ certain routing techniques in the network segment the management port connects to. For example, you may experience this issue if the BIG-IP system's default gateway on the management network is a pair of Check Point Secure Gateways configured in Load Sharing Multicast Mode. In this case, the IP address of the default gateway resolves to a L2 multicast address and, because of this issue, the BIG-IP system's management port ends up dropping traffic destined the default gateway.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions are required to trigger this issue. However, only customers with unusual routing configurations are likely to actually notice this issue.
bugs.impact: As a result of this issue, certain destinations or certain services will not be reachable via the BIG-IP system's management port.
bugs.workaround: The Linux host configures a single-interface bridge over the management port to make certain tasks simpler. This issue has been shown to go away when multicast snooping is disabled for said bridge. You can disable multicast snooping for the management bridge by running the following command: # echo 0 > /sys/class/net/mgmt/bridge/multicast_snooping On a VIPRION chassis, the aforementioned command would have to be run on each blade. The command is not permanent and the change is lost after a reboot of the system. To make the change permanent, you can add the command to the /config/startup file.

bugs.title: New Hourly Billable VE instances in AWS and Azure register with F5 Licensing Server for Support.
bugs.symptoms: Phone support is not available for hourly billing customers in cloud marketplaces.
bugs.conditions: All hourly billing VE instances in AWS Marketplace.
bugs.impact: Phone support is not available for hourly billing VE instances.
bugs.fix: New Hourly Billable VE instances in AWS and Azure register with F5 Licensing Server for Support.
bugs.behavior: Changed licensing for hourly billing instances from pre-licensed image to template reg key which must be licensed through the license server.

bugs.title: IPSEC Tunnel fails for more than one minute randomly.
bugs.symptoms: IPsec IKEv1: DPD ACK may be dropped when excessive DPD message exchange. This causes the IPsec tunnel to fail.
bugs.conditions: Excessive DPD message exchange.
bugs.impact: Connection resets.
bugs.fix: Excessive DPD message exchange no longer causes the IPsec tunnel to fail.

bugs.title: Flows for a FastL4 profile that are forwarded may now be accelerated.
bugs.symptoms: Forwarded FastL4 profiles are not accelerated.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when any of the following conditions is met: -- Using a preserve-strict setting on a virtual server. -- Using the "snat" command in an iRule. -- Using CGNAT with few available endpoints.
bugs.impact: Forwarded FastL4 flows are not accelerated.

bugs.title: ASM REST: PATCH to custom signature set's attackTypeReference are ignored
bugs.symptoms: When trying to update filter/attackTypeReference for a User-Defined Filter-Based Signature Set (/mgmt/tm/asm/signature-set/<ID>), the PATCH call completes successfully, but the change never occurred.
bugs.conditions: Using the REST API, a user tries to update filter/attackTypeReference for a User-Defined Filter-Based Signature Set (/mgmt/tm/asm/signature-set/<ID>)
bugs.impact: The PATCH call completes successfully, but the change never occurred. This may result in the Signature Set not containing the expected signatures.
bugs.workaround: The bug only exists via the REST API, the GUI can be used to change this value.
bugs.fix: The attackTypeReference field is now correctly updated using a REST PATCH.

bugs.title: Idle timeout changes to five seconds when using PVA full or Assisted acceleration.
bugs.symptoms: When FastL4 performs hardware acceleration during the TCP handshake, the FastL4 handshake timeout is not updated to match the profile timeout value after the connection is established.
bugs.conditions: Accelerated, established TCP flows with no traffic for more than five seconds.
bugs.impact: TCP flows in the established state are dropped if they have more than five seconds of inactivity.
bugs.workaround: Disable embedded Packet Velocity Acceleration (ePVA) acceleration.
bugs.fix: Once the TCP connection reaches established state, the idle timeout is now set to the value found in the associated profile. By default the profile timeout value is 300 seconds.

bugs.title: Issues when using remote authentication when users have different partition access on different devices
bugs.symptoms: User validation failing when adding a partition when the [All] partition already exists, or when adding [All] partition if a specific (non-All) partition is already configured for that user. For example, on config sync, the system might post an error similar to the following: error 01070821:3: User Restriction Error: Once configured for specific partition(s), user cannot have [all].
bugs.conditions: Devices configured for remote authentication. User A on device 1 with role on all-partitions. User A on device 2 with role restricted to a single partition. Perform operation that involves accessing partitions on each device. For example, a config sync operation. The config sync issue occurs because one device is trying to sync an [All] partition to a peer that has a non-All partition already configured for a user.
bugs.impact: The system posts User Restriction Errors and operations (such as config sync) fail.
bugs.workaround: Switch to local authentication on device 1 to perform operations on multiple devices on which a single user has different partition access configured. After completing the operations, switch back to remote authentication on device 1.
bugs.fix: User authentication completes successfully for operations on multiple devices on which a single user has different partition access configured.

bugs.title: tmm core while logging from TMM during failover
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash and coredump while logging to remote logging server when an HA failover occurs.
bugs.conditions: The problem might occur when: 1. A log message is created as the result of errors that can occur during log-connection establishment. 2. An error occurs while attempting to connect to the remote logging server. 3. The Primary HA member fails over. The crash occurs on the HA member which was the Primary member prior to the failover.
bugs.impact: TMM runs out of stack and dumps core. Stack trace shows recursion in errdefs. The system cannot function under these conditions. This is an issue that might occur anytime logs are generated when managing resources that are also used by the logging system itself.
bugs.workaround: Two possible workarounds are available: 1) Create a log filter specifically for message-id :1010235: that either discards or directs such messages to local syslogs. 2) If the problem occurs on TMM startup, disable and then re-enable the corresponding log source once the TMM starts up.
bugs.fix: Logging recursion no longer occurs in TMM during failover while the system is attempting to connect to the remote logging server.

bugs.title: Monitors packets are sent even when pool member is 'Forced Offline'.
bugs.symptoms: If you have a pool member associated with more than one virtual server and the pool member is marked Forced-Offline, the pool monitor will continue to function if the monitor is assigned to both pools.
bugs.conditions: -- Pools containing identical members. -- Pool monitoring configured. -- Pool members are Forced Offline.
bugs.impact: Monitors packets are sent even when pool member is 'Forced Offline'.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Virtual Edition may have minimal disk space for the /var software partition when deploying from the OVA file for the Better or Best license bundle.
bugs.symptoms: The size of /var volume is 500 MB instead of 3 GB for BETTER and BEST license bundles.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE BETTER and BEST vm_bundle images.
bugs.impact: Not enough space in /var.
bugs.workaround: In the current volume: 1. Modify global_attributes file. * The global_attributes file is located at /shared/.tmi_config, so modify global_attributes file by using vi command. From: {"TMI_VOLUME_FIX_VAR_MIB":"500","TMI_VOLUME_FIX_CONFIG_MIB":"500"} To: {"TMI_VOLUME_FIX_VAR_MIB":"3000","TMI_VOLUME_FIX_CONFIG_MIB":"500"} 2. Install version. 3. Modify global_attributes file to back original value. 4. Switchboot to newly installed volume. 5. To change /var to 3 GB and from tmsh, run the following command: modify /sys disk directory /var new-size 3145728 6. Reboot.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Virtual Edition now has 3GB of disk space for the /var software partition when deploying from OVA for the Better or Best license bundle

bugs.title: distance cli command without access name in OSPF posts a memory allocation error.
bugs.symptoms: OSPF distance command gives error and is not effective in changing Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) behavior.
bugs.conditions: throwing a memory allocation error when the distance command is used without an access list name. The access list name is optional parameter in the following command (WORD represents the optional access list name): distance <1-255> A.B.C.D/M (WORD|).
bugs.impact: The distance command does not function correctly and posts a memory allocation error.

bugs.title: Virtual server profile changes are ignored if it has /Common/remotedesktop and /Common/vdi assigned (Citrix/Vmware View iApp)
bugs.symptoms: Changes to the profiles that are assigned to a virtual server are ignored if the /Common/remotedesktop and /Common/vdi profiles are already assigned to it. Some iApps that F5 provides to create Citrix or VMware View configurations assign those profiles to a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: /Common/remotedesktop and /Common/vdi profiles are assigned to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Changes to the profiles assigned to a virtual server (adding a new new profile, deleting a profile, changing existing profiles) have no effect until either of these occurs: The /Common/vdi profile is removed from the virtual server or tmm is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to remove /Common/vdi from the profiles for the virtual server. (There is no option in the GUI that allows you to do this.)
bugs.fix: The /Common/remotedesktop and /Common/vdi profiles can be assigned to a virtual server without affecting other profiles.

bugs.title: MRF SIP: Add support for NEGOTIATE method
bugs.symptoms: The SIP parser drops NEGOTIATE messages.
bugs.conditions: -- SIP parser. -- NEGOTIATE messages received.
bugs.impact: If a SIP NEGOTIATE message was received, it would be dropped as an invalid SIP method.

bugs.title: "tmsh install sys crypto cert" command fails to overwrite existing certificate
bugs.symptoms: When using "tmsh install sys crypto cert cert_name from-local-file /cert_path/cert_file.crt" command, if a cert with the same name has already exists, it should still allow the cert import and overwrite the existing cert if "no-overwrite" is not specified in this tmsh command. However, it fails to overwrite the cert in this case, and still complains that "The requested cert(cert_name.crt) already exists in this scope."
bugs.conditions: -- Using "tmsh install sys crypto cert" to import a cert -- The "no-overwrite" option is not specified in the tmsh command. -- The specified cert name already exists.
bugs.impact: Unable to simultaneously update and overwrite a certificate using tmsh.
bugs.workaround: Although you cannot simultaneously update and overwrite the cert using tmsh, you can achieve the same result using these separate steps: 1. To remove the cert, which prevents the existing cert-overwrite situation, run the following command: tmsh install sys crypto cert cert_name. 2. Run the following command to update the cert: tmsh cert import command.

bugs.title: OSPF distance command does not persist across restarts.
bugs.symptoms: When ospfd is restarted, the value configured for the OSPF distance command is lost.
bugs.conditions: The distance command is configured in OSPF and the ospfd process is restarted.
bugs.impact: The distance command does not function as configured, which affects OSPF behavior.

bugs.title: Add SSL maximum aggregate active handshakes per profile and per global
bugs.symptoms: There is no limit to the number of active SSL handshakes on one BIG-IP system. With many calls, memory can be exhausted and cause system problems.
bugs.conditions: When the BIG-IP system has too many active SSL handshakes.
bugs.impact: The memory and/or CPU can be exhausted.
bugs.fix: Added limitation for active SSL handshakes to prevent CPU and memory exhaustion. There is a new db variable 'tmm.ssl.maxactivehandshakes' that limits the total number of active SSL handshakes. By default this variable is set to '0', which means no limit.
bugs.behavior: There is a new db variable 'tmm.ssl.maxactivehandshakes', which limits the total number of active SSL handshakes. By default this variable is set to '0', which means no limit.

bugs.title: Log activation/deactivation of TM.TCPMemoryPressure
bugs.symptoms: The TCP memory pressure feature allows packets to be randomly dropped when the TMM is running low on available memory. The issue is that these packets are dropped silently.
bugs.conditions: TM.TCPMemoryPressure set to "enable".
bugs.impact: Packets are dropped, where the cause of the drop cannot be easily determined.
bugs.fix: Logging added in /var/log/ltm for activation and deactivation of TCP memory pressure. The deactivation message also includes the number of packets and bytes dropped.

bugs.title: Send RAA when RAR is sent by PCRF and session is deleted immediately after its created.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP does not send RAA for certain sessions.
bugs.conditions: If session is created , CCR-I is send, CCA-I received and session is deleted immediately then RAA for RAR update from the PCRF for the session is not sent.
bugs.impact: PCRF has no way of knowing why RAA was not received for the session.
bugs.workaround: No workaround and this is extremely remote scenario where radius start and stop are received almost at the same time.

bugs.title: TMM might core when using HTTP::header in a serverside event
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances TMM might core when using an HTTP iRule command in a HTTP_REQUEST_SEND serverside event.
bugs.conditions: - iRule with an HTTP command in a serverside event prior to the serverside being completely established, such as HTTP_REQUEST_SEND. - OneConnect configured on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: The command might either return invalid value or lead to a condition where TMM might core.
bugs.workaround: Use the {clientside} Tcl command to execute on the client side. Alternatively, you might use the HTTP_REQUEST_RELEASE event for HTTP inspection/modification on the server-side.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when using HTTP iRule commands on the server-side of the HTTP_REQUEST_SEND event.

bugs.title: Incoming INVITE SIP message to Subscriber is dropped when working with Asterix Proxy
bugs.symptoms: Incoming SIP call from Asterix SIP Server to registered subscriber fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on incoming SIP Call to subscriber registered with Asterix server. The call request goes to Asterix which sends an INVITE to the subscriber through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Calls to Asterix SIP subscribers fail when they are behind BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Enabling tmm.verbose mode produces messages that can be mistaken for errors.
bugs.symptoms: When tmm first starts, the system logs multiple messages containing the words "error:" and "best_error:" in the tmm log files when tmm.verbose is enabled, and hardware accelerators are present.
bugs.conditions: Must have an accelerator device, and enable tmm.verbose logging.
bugs.impact: The system posts messages that could be mistaken for errors. For example: en: 1, clkf: 13, pll_MHz: 650, ddr_hertz: 650000000, error: 17000000, best_error: 667000000. These are not errors, and may be safely ignored.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the lines with format similar to the following: en: 1, clkf: 13, pll_MHz: 650, ddr_hertz: 650000000, error: 17000000, best_error: 667000000
bugs.fix: The cosmetic messages containing 'err' and 'best err' are no longer posted on initial tmm startup when tmm.verbose logging on hardware accelerated devices.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when forwarding an inbound connection on Large Scale NAT (LSN) pool
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when forwarding an inbound connection and the flow sweeper tries to update the flow before the forwarding operation completes.
bugs.conditions: A small or over utilized LSN pool that creates inbound entries that require forwarding.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Add more IP addresses to the LSN pool.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when forwarding inbound connections configured with an LSN pool

bugs.title: [iRule] [Stats] iRule is not generating any stats for executed iRules.
bugs.symptoms: iRule is not generating any stats for executed iRules when the rule is removed/edited and then re-added to the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following steps are taken: 1. Move/edit an iRule that is attached to a virtual server. 2. Pass traffic to the virtual server. 3. Add the iRule back to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: No iRule usage stats available.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm.
bugs.fix: iRule now generates stats for executed iRules when the rule is removed/edited and then re-added to the virtual server.

bugs.title: Dashboard fails to export derived throughput history
bugs.symptoms: Dashboard fails to export derived throughput history.
bugs.conditions: Exporting derived throughput history in the Dashboard.
bugs.impact: The derived stats are not included in the export file.
bugs.workaround: The derived stats can be calculated from the exported raw stats.
bugs.fix: Dashboard now includes derived throughput history in export.

bugs.title: ASSERT in CSP in packet_reuse
bugs.symptoms: Causes TMM to crash
bugs.conditions: This crash will happen on LTM virtuals that meet the following two configuration criteria: - the virtual is configured with fasthttp profile. - the virtual's enabled VLAN is mapped to the _loopback interface.
bugs.impact: Crash and restart of TMM
bugs.fix: Fixed the logic in determining if we are an L7 loopback connection. This way CSP receives only packets that it owns and can be re-used

bugs.title: Idle timeout changes to five seconds when using PVA full or Assisted acceleration.
bugs.symptoms: When FastL4 performs hardware acceleration during the TCP handshake, the FastL4 handshake timeout is not updated to match the profile timeout value after the connection is established.
bugs.conditions: Accelerated, established TCP flows with no traffic for more than five seconds.
bugs.impact: TCP flows in the established state are dropped if they have more than five seconds of inactivity.
bugs.workaround: Disable embedded Packet Velocity Acceleration (ePVA) acceleration.
bugs.fix: Once the TCP connection reaches established state, the idle timeout is set to the value found in the associated profile. By default the profile timeout value is 300 seconds.

bugs.title: Java VM crash while monitoring DB
bugs.symptoms: The Java VM crashed while attempting to monitor the proper functioning of a DB
bugs.conditions: Unknown
bugs.impact: One known occurrence. Failure affects a single attempt at monitoring the DB.
bugs.workaround: Based on the information available, this failure is not persistent. A single attempt at monitoring the DB failed and proper functioning resumed without intervention.

bugs.title: Vlangroup may have its MAC address set to 02:00:00:00:00 on first configuration load
bugs.symptoms: Transparent/translucent Vlangroup may have its MAC address set to 02:00:00:00:00 on either the first configuration load after an upgrade or on a manual mcpd db clear/reload.
bugs.conditions: Transparent/Translucent vlangroup configured. Upgrade to later version (11.3.0 through 12.1.0) or manually delete mcpd DB binary.
bugs.impact: Vlangroup MAC address is incorrect and can adversely affect traffic transversing the vlangroup.
bugs.workaround: Reload configuration or alter vlangroup configuration: e.g: set back and forth between transparency modes.
bugs.fix: Vlangroups now correctly establish MAC addresses on first configuration load.

bugs.title: ICAP 2xx response (except 200, 204) is treated as error
bugs.symptoms: An ICAP status code from the ICAP server of any 2xx response other than 200 or 204, is treated as an error, causing a reset of the ICAP connection and the service-down-action to be performed on the parent virtual server (as configured in the requestadapt or responseadapt profile). The RFC 3507 requires the ICAP client (the BIG-IP server) to handle the response normally (i.e., like it handles 200).
bugs.conditions: The ICAP server returns a 2xx status code that is not defined explicitly for ICAP.
bugs.impact: Transactions involving an ICAP server that returns a non-ICAP 2xx response do not work, and the service-down action is performed.
bugs.workaround: If possible, have the ICAP server return status code 200.
bugs.fix: An ICAP status code from the ICAP server of any 2xx response other than 200 or 204, is treated as a normal 200 status code; thus the encapsulated HTTP request or response is returned to the HTTP client or server.

bugs.title: dnatutil aborts when encountering parse errors
bugs.symptoms: dnatutil abort further processing of logs when it encounters a recoverable parse error.
bugs.conditions: Using dnatutil on log entries that resemble parseable logs, but failed to be processed by dnatutil
bugs.impact: Usage of dnatutil
bugs.workaround: Filter out questionable log entries as reported by dnatutil

bugs.title: Edge client connection fails: keeps reconnecting when captive portal probe URL is not available at www.f5.com
bugs.symptoms: Using Edge client on Microsoft Windows to establish a VPN repeatedly connects and disconnects.
bugs.conditions: Edge client on Windows is used to establish VPN.
bugs.impact: Cannot establish VPN. This occurs because The F5 probe URL page used by earlier versions of the Edge client has been decommissioned.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to upgrade to a more recent Edge client for Windows.

bugs.title: Special characters might change input.
bugs.symptoms: Special characters by users might change the intended data.
bugs.conditions: Use of special characters.
bugs.impact: Incorrect or unwanted response.
bugs.fix: Updated data handling to properly account for special characters.

bugs.title: On shutdown, SOD and other daemons very infrequently cores due to an internal processing error during the shutdown.
bugs.symptoms: On shutdown, SOD very infrequently cores due to an internal processing error during the shutdown.
bugs.conditions: System shutdown. Unable to reproduce the issue reliably, so conditions for the crash are unknown
bugs.impact: Since the core happens on shutdown, operation on the device is not affected, but a core file may be generated.

bugs.title: Creating local user for previously remote user results in incomplete user definition.
bugs.symptoms: Creating a local user for a user who previously authenticated using a remote mechanism (e.g. LDAP, RADIUS) results in a user who has no partition-access. Additionally, the user cannot be modified via web UI.
bugs.conditions: Configure remote system authentication. Create a local user for remotely authenticated user.
bugs.impact: User cannot authenticate. User name does not appear in User List.
bugs.workaround: After initial creation, modify local user via tmsh to include appropriate partition-access.

bugs.title: Performance degradation when mapping a custom TACDB with large number of entries
bugs.symptoms: When mapping a custom TACDB with a large number of entries (this was seen on a database containing more than 300K entries), a small performance degradation of throughput is seen for about 10 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Mapping a large custom TACDB.
bugs.impact: Throughput performance is impacted.

bugs.title: Aced crashed occasionally while shutting down
bugs.symptoms: An aced core file might be generated when it tries to terminate.
bugs.conditions: Any time aced process tries to exit due to, among others: 1. Receive SIGTERM signal; 2. MCP query or process notification error;
bugs.impact: There is no impact to normal aced service. This crash only happens when aced is trying to shutdown.
bugs.workaround: No workaround available

bugs.title: TMM can crash if using the v6rd profile
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash intermittently when traffic is sent through v6rd profile-configured tunnels.
bugs.conditions: Specific conditions required for encountering this issue are not well understood.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed root cause of TMM core related to the v6rd profile, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Configuration may fail to load when upgrading from version 10.x.
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade from 10.x to 11.5.3 HF2, configuration fails to load with the following error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid primary key on monitor_param object () - not a full path 2.
bugs.conditions: Configuration contains a user-created monitor (A) that inherits from user-created monitor (B). Monitor A appears first within the configuration files and monitor B does not have a 'destination' attribute.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Re-order monitors such that Monitor B appears first, or add a 'destination' attribute (i.e., 'destination *:*') to monitor B.
bugs.fix: 10.x upgrade now completes successfully, even when parent monitors appear later in the monitor list, or when there is no destination attribute in the child monitor.

bugs.title: VMware View USB redirection stops working after client reconnect
bugs.symptoms: VMware View USB redirection stops working
bugs.conditions: VMware View client reconnects due to network interruptions
bugs.impact: VMware View USB redirection stops working
bugs.fix: VMware View USB redirection works after client reconnect

bugs.title: PEM: TMM core when deleting sessions not aware to PCRF
bugs.symptoms: TMM core.
bugs.conditions: When PCRF sends a CCA-T for a session with error code 5002 (UNKNOWN_SESSION_ID)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: If PCRF should just acknowledge CCA-T with success code 2001 even if its not aware of the session.

bugs.title: tmsh show gtm persist <filter option> does not filter correctly
bugs.symptoms: Following commands fail to return results even if there are matching records: # tmsh show gtm persist level wideip # tmsh show gtm persist target-type pool-member
bugs.conditions: This only happens when running the tmsh commands listed in the Symptoms.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to get a granular detail for persist stats.
bugs.workaround: Use GUI.
bugs.fix: Filters for the tmsh show gtm persist command now apply the filters correctly.

bugs.title: URLCAT stats cause crash without PEM URLCAT license
bugs.symptoms: URLCAT stats command causes TMM crash when urlcat license is not installed.
bugs.conditions: The system does not have PEM URLCAT license. The URLCAT stats command is invoked.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use PEM URLCAT stats if the license is not installed.
bugs.fix: License check is now performed before command is run.

bugs.title: SSL connections may fail with a handshake failure when the ClientHello is sent in multiple packets
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes BIG-IP system responds with a fatal-handshake alert and closes the SSL session for a new connection when a ClientHello record is split between two or more packets. If SSL debug logging is enabled, the system logs an error such as the following: 01260009:7: Connection error: ssl_hs_rxhello:6210: ClientHello contains extra data (47). Note: For information on SSL debug logging, see SOL15292: Troubleshooting SSL/TLS handshake failures at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/15000/200/sol15292.html.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a SSL ClientHello record is split across multiple TCP segments, and the last segment is relatively small.
bugs.impact: SSL connections fail to complete with a handshake failure.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: SSL handshakes no longer fails to complete when the ClientHello is split across multiple TCP segments, and the last segment is relatively small.

bugs.title: snmpd crashes when performing snmp query on ifXTable of ifMIB.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system performs a Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) query on the ifXtable object-specified in the interfaces management information base (ifMIB), the snmpd process stops responding.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: The BIG-IP system performs an SNMP query on the ifXTable of the ifMIB.
bugs.impact: snmpd crashes.
bugs.workaround: When problem occurs, snmpd automatically restarts.
bugs.fix: A problem of accessing null pointer in snmpd has been fixed.

bugs.title: PCCD Firewall compilation takes a long time
bugs.symptoms: PCCD Firewall compilation can take several minutes to complete if your config contains a lot of firewall contexts, even if they are relatively small (with very few rules per context, e.g., 5 or fewer rules per context).
bugs.conditions: 1. Your configuration contains a lot of firewall contexts (e.g., 1500 or more virtual servers with enforced policies configured.) 2. Very few rules per context, e.g., 5 or fewer rules per context.
bugs.impact: Compiling the firewall policies might take several minutes.
bugs.fix: Performance for compiling firewall policies containing a lot of firewall contexts has been restored.

bugs.title: tmm assert 'tcp_set_persist: retransmit pending'
bugs.symptoms: The tmm issues a 'tcp_set_persist: retransmit pending' assert.
bugs.conditions: Occurs in the TCP stack when the two internal timers, persistence timer and retransmission timer, are active simultaneously.
bugs.impact: TMM asserts 'tcp_set_persist: retransmit pending'. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use the performance TCP stack. This can be done by disabling all of the following profile parameters: - mptcp - rate-pace - congestion-control algorithms other than reno, newreno, scalable, highspeed, or none - tail-loss-probe
bugs.fix: TMM supports canceling of the zero window persistence timer.

bugs.title: Per VLAN/tmm based hardware SYN-cookie enhancement is a hardware-only feature
bugs.symptoms: The new feature of Per VLAN/TMM based HW SYN-Cookie enhancement to protect BIG-IP device and network is a hardware-only feature. It can only be turned on with hardware platforms that are installed with the supported FPGA firmware bitstreams, namely, BIG-IP 2000/4000/5000 family (v1.11.20.0+), VIPRION B2250 (v2.5.5.0+), and VIPRION B4450 (all), and BIG-IP i5000/i7000/i10000 family (all). For the hardware platforms without the firmware support, there will be no fall-back mechanism to turn on the feature in software only.
bugs.conditions: Configure the per VLAN/tmm hardware SYN-cookie feature
bugs.impact: The feature is unavailable on platforms with no firmware support.

bugs.title: Enforcer application might crash on XML traffic when out of memory
bugs.symptoms: Enforcer application might crash on XML traffic when out of memory.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system is out of memory.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system might temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a scenario where the system might crash when the XML parser ran out of memory.

bugs.title: In very fast transactions, some detection data is missing
bugs.symptoms: In very fast transactions, some automatic transaction detection data is missing.
bugs.conditions: Form submitted before page finishes loading.
bugs.impact: False positive automatic transaction alerts.
bugs.fix: Loss of data in the Automatic Transactions cookie can be prevented by initializing cookies earlier.

bugs.title: Older cli-tools unsupported by AWS
bugs.symptoms: Older EC2 tools stopped working in some AWS regions.
bugs.conditions: This can happen in some AWS regions.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP high availability configurations may stop working in some AWS regions.
bugs.fix: F5 Networks added the latest available version (1.7.5.1) of EC2 tools in this release/hotfix.

bugs.title: Bad actor quarantining
bugs.symptoms: An issue was found where bad actors could be released from quarantine due to a timing issue
bugs.conditions: This is a timing issue related to an having unusually high number of bad actors at the same time.
bugs.impact: Traffic can be removed from quarantine and passed to the web server
bugs.fix: An issue was fixed related to bad actor quarantining

bugs.title: Portal access should send request url with "/" in path to backend
bugs.symptoms: Backend server responds with HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request if target URI has empty path component.
bugs.conditions: Target URI has empty path component
bugs.impact: Backend server responds with HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
bugs.workaround: when HTTP_REQUEST { # Bug547332: [Portal Access] Send "/" in place of empty path in request URLs to backend if { [HTTP::path] contains "/2.0.0/link/" } { set bug547332 1 } elseif { [info exists bug547332] } { unset bug547332 } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { [info exists bug547332] && \ [HTTP::header exists Location] } { unset bug547332 HTTP::header replace Location [string map { {.com?} {.com/?} } [HTTP::header Location] ] } }
bugs.fix: Portal access should send request url with "/" in path to backend

bugs.title: Unexpected storage-format string causes asm restart
bugs.symptoms: ASM restarts and bd generates a core.
bugs.conditions: Logging Format : Comma-Separated Values Storage Format : User-Defined And give format string like what is mentioned in Splunk document - https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/AddOns/released/F5BIGIP/Setup "f5_asm=Splunk-F5-ASM,attack_type=%attack_type%,blocking_exception_reason=%blocking_exception_reason%,client_type=%client_type%,credential_stuffing_lookup_result=%credential_stuffing_lookup_result%,date_time=%date_time%,dest_ip=%dest_ip%,dest_port=%dest_port%,device_id=%device_id%,enforced_by=%enforced_by%,enforcement_action=%enforcement_action%,epoch_time=%epoch_time%,geo_info=%geo_location%,headers=%headers%,http_class=%http_class_name%,ip_addr_intelli=%ip_address_intelligence%,ip_client=%ip_client%,ip_route_domain=%ip_with_route_domain%,is_trunct=%is_truncated%,login_result=%login_result%,manage_ip_addr=%management_ip_address%,method=%method%,mobile_application_name=%mobile_application_name%,mobile_application_version=%mobile_application_version%,policy_apply_date=%policy_apply_date%,policy_name=%policy_name%,protocol=%protocol%,protocol_info=%protocol_info%,query_str=%query_string%,req=%request%,req_status=%request_status% ...snip..." Once the virtual server receives a request and bd tries to generate remote log message, bd crashes.
bugs.impact: ASM traffic disrupted while bd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use items available in "Available Items" only.

bugs.title: Under unknown circumstances sometimes a sessionDB subkey entry becomes corrupted
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a subkey that has master_record field set to true.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Monitor instances in a partition that uses a non-default route domain can fail validation on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: Error messages similar to this are present in the ltm log: -- err mcpd[9369]: 01020036:3: The requested monitor instance (/part10/test_mon 90.90.90.90%10 443 ltm-pool-member) was not found. -- err mcpd[9369]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020036:3: The requested monitor instance (/part10/test_mon 90.90.90.90%10 443 ltm-pool-member) was not found.
bugs.conditions: A chassis-based system with multiple blades. This can occur a few different ways: - A monitor is attached to an object that is configured in a partition that uses a non-default route domain, but the address of the monitor is explicitly using the default route domain (e.g. %0). - A monitor defined in the Common partition is attached to an object from a partition where the default route domain is different.
bugs.impact: Monitor instances in a partition that uses a non-default route domain can fail validation on secondary blades. mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Move the monitor to the /Common/ partition and do not specify %0 in the Alias Address. -- Do not use monitors from other partitions where the default route domain is different.
bugs.fix: The complete state for addresses on the primary blade is propagated to secondary blades.

bugs.title: TMM core due to iSession tunnel assertion failure
bugs.symptoms: TMM core due to "valid isession pcb" assertion failure in isession_dedup_admin.c.
bugs.conditions: Deduplication endpoint recovery occurs on a BIG-IP that has duplication is enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: An iSession tunnel initialization defect has been corrected.

bugs.title: Add support for auto-update of MachineCertService
bugs.symptoms: Auto-update of MachineCertService wasn't implemented. If APM contains newer MachineCertService EdgeClient doesn't pick it up automatically.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading existing APM install.
bugs.impact: Since MachineCertService is not auto-updatable service redeployment is required.
bugs.fix: Added support of auto-update to MachineCertService.

bugs.title: avrd reports incorrect stat values
bugs.symptoms: AVR has some uint32 counters for DoS statistics both in HW and SW. And these counters were getting overflowed with time.
bugs.impact: Impact would only be seen on some DoS stats but functionality wise everything works fine without any issue.
bugs.conditions: When the box is running under heavy DoS traffic for few hours, DoS counters can overflow.
bugs.workaround: There was no workaround.
bugs.fix: Counter overflow is now handled correctly for both HW and SW DoS.

bugs.title: iControl REST: Errors may occur when fetching large number of objects using iControl REST API
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST: Errors may occur when fetching a large number of objects using the iControl REST API. Symptoms may include a timeout error (typically after 60 seconds) or a Java OOM (out-of-memory) error.
bugs.conditions: This may happen when the control plane is stressed in terms of CPU and memory usage, for example, when trying to load 20 KB rules.
bugs.impact: iControl REST API is non-responsive or unusable.
bugs.workaround: Use pagination for getting a large number of objects, by using ODATA's $skip and $top query parameters. For example, to get the first 100 tm/ltm/pool objects: HTTP method - GET. URI - https://locahost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool?$skip=0&$top=100.

bugs.title: A TCL error in a DNS_RESPONSE iRule event can cause a tmm crash.
bugs.symptoms: A TCL error, such as referencing an undefined variable, in a DNS_RESPONSE iRule event can cause a tmm crash. This can occur on a UDP listener with a DNS profile without datagram load balancing enabled. A DNS_REQUEST event, with any content, on the same listener is also required.
bugs.conditions: All of the following: UDP listener with DNS profile without datagram load balancing. A TCL error, such as referencing an undefined variable, in a DNS_RESPONSE iRule event. A DNS_REQUEST iRule event with any content.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Either add datagram load balancing to the listener or correct the TCL errors that lead to the problem.
bugs.fix: The TCL error handling is now processed asynchronously which prevents the problem from occurring.

bugs.title: Firewall-blocked KPASSWD service does not cause domain join operation to fail
bugs.symptoms: KPASSWD service runs on tcp/464 and udp/464. If both of these ports were blocked, BIG-IP would not be able to properly set the machine account password for the created machine account. However, there is a bug on BIG-IP as well, which fails to report this failure back to the administrator. As the machine account itself was successfully created on ActiveDirectory side without the correct password, and BIG-IP's failure to report the KPASSWD failure problem, the domain join operation seems had worked perfectly. However, since the password information is never set on ActiveDirectory side, this causes this machine account effectively unusable because BIG-IP would never be able to establish a working SCHANNEL with ActiveDirectory server because of this password mismatch. creation is LDAP (+ Kerberos GSS-API with SASL binding), the machine account itself is generated.
