Furthermore, as password setting for machine account is not allowed to be performed by administrator, this situation obfuscate the fact the KPASSWD was failing as AD server never receives thus AD never logged any failure on this matter, while BIG-IP fails to detect the KPASSWD failure, and so as administrator's user experience goes, everything seems perfectly worked for domain join.
bugs.conditions: Out of DNS, LDAP, KERBEROS, KPASSWD services which are required for domain join operation, only KPASSWD is blocked.
bugs.impact: Created machine account is effectively unusable due to password mismatch, and BIG-IP would never be able to establish a working SCHANNEL, this renders NTLM authentication feature to be not working.
bugs.workaround: Allow KPASSWD to reach ActiveDirectory server

bugs.title: TMM may core on using SSL::disable on an already established serverside connection
bugs.symptoms: TMM process may crash if the SSL::disable iRule command is used on a serverside with a connection that has already established SSL.
bugs.conditions: Use of the 'SSL::disable serverside' iRule command on a serverside connection that has already established SSL
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use SSL::disable on an event where the serverside SSL connection is already established.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores on using SSL::disable on an already established serverside connection, it will now log a warning Connection error: hud_ssl_handler:605: disable profile (80)

bugs.title: Potential DNS Transparent Cache Memory Leak
bugs.symptoms: When a transparent cache is populated with messages where the DNSSEC OK-bit is true, and a query with that bit true, arrives at or after the expiration of the message TTL, the system leaks all subsequent queries with DNSSEC OK set to false, up through the TTL of that message.
bugs.conditions: Running a DNS transparent cache with clients requesting DNSSEC messages.
bugs.impact: A few hundred bytes can leak on each clientside query, leading to a massive leak over a short period of time.
bugs.workaround: Disable DNSSEC on all cached messages by disabling DNSSEC on pool members.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a potential DNS transparent cache memory leak.

bugs.title: SNMP ipAdEntAddr indicates floating vlan IP rather than local IP
bugs.symptoms: An SNMP query response for ipAdEntAddr would sometimes return floating IPs rather than local IPs. This was due to the supporting software returning the first found IP address for a given vlan.
bugs.conditions: Problem started after upgrading to v11.5.1 Eng-HF7, from v10.2.4. The same problem can happen on freshly installed 11.5.x as well.
bugs.impact: No impact to BIG-IP services, but the returned information to the SNMP query is sometimes incorrect.

bugs.title: Feeding empty username and password to the Logon Page followed by RadiusAuthAgent shows the session as Logged out
bugs.symptoms: Session logs out. No error messages or retry logon page. --------------------------------------------- Your session is finished. Logged out successfully. Thank you for using BIG-IP. To open a new session, please click here. ----------------------------------------------
bugs.conditions: Your environment has an access policy like the following Success Start -> Logon Page -> Radius Auth ----> Advanced resource assign (webtop) -> allow. | | failure -----------------------------------------------> Deny. If you connect to the virtual server with this access policy and provide an empty username and password, you are logged out of the session and asked to open a new session page.
bugs.impact: Without providing proper username and password, user is shown the error "Logged out successfully.", which is improper.
bugs.workaround: No mitigation observed.

bugs.title: GUI Network Map page runs out of memory and the GUI hangs indefinitely.
bugs.symptoms: GUI Network Map page runs out of memory and the GUI hangs indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: When a BIG-IP system is configured with a large number of Virtual Servers (3000+) and accompanying components (iRules, Pools, Pool Members, and Node Addresses), multiple users retrieving the Network Map might result in an Out of Memory Exception.
bugs.impact: GUI server becomes unresponsive and unable to process new requests. The GUI becomes unusable and requires a restart.
bugs.workaround: Use items in the filter bar (along the top of the screen) to reduce the result size to avoid an Out of Memory Exception. Also, increase the memory of the container server.
bugs.fix: Change how we retrieve data from the backend and move more logic to the client from the backend.

bugs.title: User with 'Application Editor' role set cannot modify 'Description' field using the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: User with 'Application Editor' role set cannot modify 'Description' field using the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Users with a role of Application Editor.
bugs.impact: Cannot modify 'Description' field using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: User with 'Application Editor' roles can modify 'Description' fields using tmsh.
bugs.fix: User with 'Application Editor' role can now modify 'Description' field using the GUI.

bugs.title: PCP and inbound-entry iRules command does not work with under-provisioned PBA LSN pool
bugs.symptoms: When an PBA LSN pool is under-provisioned, the LSN::inbound-entry iRule will not work. PCP will also not work with an under-provisioned PBA LSN pool.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when PCP or the iRules LSN::inbound-entry command is enabled on a PBA LSN pool that does not have many translation addresses.
bugs.impact: PCP or the LSN::inbound-entry iRule may not work. This would result in failing connections.

bugs.title: RAR for already deleted session returns RAA with 5012 error code
bugs.symptoms: Session already deleted forcefully by PEM, but when PCRF sends RAR with the same session ID then PEM responds with RAA with error code 5012 (unable to comply) instead of 5002(unknown session ID)
bugs.conditions: Session Deleted when Gx connection down and tmm.pem.session.endpointDeleteResponse and tmm.pem.session.FinalUsageRecord set to low value to trigger forced delete.
bugs.impact: PCRF still think session exists giving wrong signal to PCRF
bugs.workaround: Make sure tmm.pem.session.endpointDeleteResponse is set to high value to make sure session not deleted if Gx connection is down for a short period of time

bugs.title: Idle timeout may be tcp handshake timeout on CMP demoted Fast L4 virtual servers.
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances, CMP demoted Fast L4 virtual servers may intermittently and incorrectly use the tcp handshake timeout instead of the configured idle timeout.
bugs.conditions: - CMP demoted Fast L4 virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Connections may be reset earlier or closed at an unexpected time.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the virtual server is not CMP demoted. To do so, do one of the following: -- CMP-enable the virtual server. -- Ensure that any iRules that CMP-demotes the virtual server are corrected. See SOL13033: Constructing CMP-compatible iRules at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/000/sol13033.html

bugs.title: BGP routing using route-maps cannot match route tags
bugs.symptoms: When a route-map is used to redistribute routes into BGP, matching on the route tag fails.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing using BGP, redistribution into BGP using a route-map, route-map matches route tag.
bugs.impact: BGP may not get all prefixes from other routing protocols.
bugs.fix: Route-maps used with BGP now correctly match route tags.

bugs.title: Disabling an interface on a blade does not change media to NONE
bugs.symptoms: When an interface on a blade in a chassis is disabled, it's media does not get reported as NONE and the link on the other end stays UP.
bugs.conditions: Disabling an interface on a blade within a chassis.
bugs.impact: Media on the disabled interface is not reported as NONE and link on partner end is UP.
bugs.fix: fixed

bugs.title: External link status not displayed for VLAN/interfaces
bugs.symptoms: When you run tmsh show net interface on a Virtual Edition/Z100 BIG-Ip device, you see "Media None".
bugs.conditions: This occurs on devices that are not using SR-IOV
bugs.impact: External Link status cannot readily be determined from within the VE using usual interface status commands
bugs.workaround: check the link state on the hypervisor or connected devices check the results of higher layer protocols (ARP, ping, etc.)

bugs.title: Performance degradation when adding VDI profile to virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Performance degradation when adding VDI profile to virtual server
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the VDI profile
bugs.impact: 0.3s latency increase comparing with previous result
bugs.fix: Fixed 0.3s latency between client and server SSL hello if VDI profile is added to virtual server.

bugs.title: iControl calls that query key/cert from parent folder, and the name is missing the extension, result in incorrect results
bugs.symptoms: If the active folder is not same as the folder in which the query is being run, and the corresponding key/cert extension is not present in the name of the key/certificate file, the query result returns incorrect results.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when iControl calls that query key/cert from parent folder, and the name is missing the extension.
bugs.impact: The query result returns incorrect results.
bugs.workaround: You can use one of the following workarounds: -- Change the filename to include the extension. -- Change to the folder containing the iControl call you are executing.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly loads key/cert/csr/crl files without an extension, so iControl calls that query those files from parent folder, now return correct results.

bugs.title: Transparent Cache Messages Only Updated with DO-bit True
bugs.symptoms: When a transparent cache stores a message with DNSSEC OK (DO) bit TRUE and its TTL expires, the message is only updated when a new message arrives with DO-bit TRUE.
bugs.conditions: Running a DNS transparent cache with clients requesting DNSSEC messages.
bugs.impact: When the DO-bit TRUE's cached message TTL expires, the general impact is DO-bit FALSE queries will be proxied until the message cache is updated with DO-bit TRUE.
bugs.fix: The message cache is updated regardless of DO-bit state after TTL expiration. However, the cache prefers DO-bit TRUE messages, and will update the cached message if a newer one arrives with DNSSEC OK.

bugs.title: TMM crashes on standby device with re-mirrored SIP monitor flows.
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, the standby system with a SIP monitor crashes in a configuration where the active system contains a forwarding virtual server with a wildcard IP address and port, with connection mirroring enabled.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on an active-standby setup in which there is an L4 forwarding virtual server or SNAT listener configuration with a wildcard IP address and port, and with connection mirroring enabled. Also, the standby has a SIP monitor configured.
bugs.impact: Packets that are sent by the SIP monitor on the standby get routed back to the active unit (possibly due to a routing loop) and are then sent to the standby because of the wildcard mirrored configuration. tmm on standby might crash. When the crash occurs, the standby system posts the following assert and crashes: tmm failed assertion, non-zero ha_unit required for mirrored flow.
bugs.workaround: -- If a routing or switching loop is the reason the packets come back to the active unit, then the routing issues can be eliminated. -- The mirroring of the wildcard virtual server or SNAT listener can be disabled.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes on standby device with re-mirrored SIP monitor flows.

bugs.title: Memory protection strategies can conflict
bugs.symptoms: The TMM has three mechanisms to protect memory usage when under pressure: the sweeper responds to low memory with a variety of strategies such as killing idle flows; memory reaping is activated to restore memory to the system; and tcp random early drops are activated if configured. Since these are all targeting the same memory levels by default, it's possible that all three activate and victimize more flows than required. In addition, a flaw in the random early drop logic could cause unpredictable behavior.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under normal operating conditions.
bugs.impact: More flows are victimized than necessary when under memory pressure. One symptom is a large number of random early drops, and hovering right near the sweeper's low-water mark causing new flows to encounter the random early drop limits nearly immediately.
bugs.workaround: The sweeper's low-water mark can be adjusted, along with the tm.tcpmemorypressure.hiwater and tm.tcpmemorypressure.lowater variables so that they are not all at the same location; this can alleviate most symptoms of this issue.

bugs.title: ASM blocking page does not display when using SPDY profile
bugs.symptoms: The ASM blocking page will not be displayed when using the SPDY profile.
bugs.conditions: Virtual configured with ASM and spdy profile and request is blocked by ASM.
bugs.impact: Request blocked page is not displayed.
bugs.workaround: If possible, disable the SPDY profile on virtual servers configured to use ASM.
bugs.fix: ASM will now correctly display its blocking page when the SPDY profile is enabled and an ASM blocking rule is triggered.

bugs.title: TMM may core when reconfiguring iApps that make use of iRules with procedures.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core when reconfiguring iApps that make extensive use of iRules with procedures.
bugs.conditions: During the reconfiguration of more than one iApp by switching templates, prior and new templates to contain iRules with procedures of the same name. After the second or later reconfiguration TMM may core.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Modify iApp template to generate procedures that have a unique name per iApp.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when reconfiguring more than one iApp that contains iRule procedures of the same name.

bugs.title: Avrd is at CPU is 100%
bugs.symptoms: When the Application Visibility and Reporting (AVR) module is being used, the avrd daemon can consume all CPU. The avrd log will contain error messages similar to Semaphore DB_Publisher_ready is not set, for xxxx seconds
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using the AVR module.
bugs.impact: Avrd gets to 100% CPU and stays there even when no traffic is being passed, which will impact system performance
bugs.workaround: Restarting tmm will temporarily mitigate this problem
bugs.fix: Avrd is no longer susceptible to consuming all CPU indefinitely even when traffic is not being passed.

bugs.title: Tomcat might become unresponsive when the UI throws an Out of Memory Exception
bugs.symptoms: The UI might runs out of memory on a page that is memory heavy, such as on the Network Map page of a configuration with many Virtual Servers, Pools, iRules, Pool Members/Address Nodes, and the Tomcat UI server might become unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: Using the Network Map page to render the map with a large number of components and multiple consecutive users can cause the UI to run out of memory.
bugs.impact: The UI becomes unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Use the search filter to reduce the result set. When the UI becomes unresponsive, restart Tomcat. Also, consider increasing the memory allocation for Tomcat.

bugs.title: warning: Failed to find EUDs
bugs.symptoms: There are normal circumstances where the system does not yet have a diagnostics package installed. Even though it is normal, a warning log message is emitted for this condition.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on newly formatted installations prior to version 11.5.4.
bugs.impact: Even though this is logged at the warning level, lack of an EUD can indicate a normal condition on new installations.
bugs.workaround: ignore the warning
bugs.fix: If the system cannot find the EUD it will now be logged at the info level.

bugs.title: Windows 10 is not detected when Firefox is used
bugs.symptoms: Windows 10 is not detected when the Firefox browser is used.
bugs.conditions: Windows 10 and Firefox (at least versions 40 and 41).
bugs.impact: The Client OS agent chooses an incorrect branch. Network Access might be disabled for such a client.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Now Windows 10 is properly detected with the Firefox browser.

bugs.title: RDP resource 'Custom parameters' fail to accept parameters containing spaces or colon in the value
bugs.symptoms: Some RDP parameters may contain whitespaces or colon in the value, e.g.: loadbalanceinfo:s:tsv://MS Terminal Services Plugin.1.RDSFarm The configuration utility will throw a validation error "01070734:3: Configuration error: apm resource remote-desktop rdp: Parse error on line 0: <parameter>"
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using RDP parameters containing spaces or colon in the value.
bugs.impact: Administrator is unable to configure the RDP resource as desired.
bugs.fix: RDP parameters parsing has been refined to support values containing colons or whitespaces.

bugs.title: Add a log message to indicate transition in the state of Gx and Gy sessions.
bugs.symptoms: Without a state transition indicator, it is difficult to determine if the Gx and Gy session is active and UP on the BIG-IP device.
bugs.conditions: Gx or Gy state transitions need to occur.
bugs.impact: Difficult to identify and debug issues related to Gx and Gy state transitions.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is an improvement.
bugs.fix: Added a log message to indicate the state transitions for Gx and Gy sessions.

bugs.title: iSession remote endpoint connection not re-established
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently an iSession remote endpoint control connection may not be re-established.
bugs.conditions: This problem may occur in the following instances: -- Changing the deduplication cache mode. -- Terminating an iSession remote endpoint control connection.
bugs.impact: New iSession connections to the remote endpoint cannot be established.
bugs.fix: Reconnection of iSession remote endpoints is now successful.

bugs.title: L7 mirrored ACK from standby to active box can cause tmm core on active
bugs.symptoms: A spurious ACK sent to the standby unit will be mirrored over to the active unit for processing. If a matching connection on the active has not been fully initialized, tmm will crash.
bugs.conditions: HA active-standby pair setup for L7 packet mirroring.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Spurious ACK no longer causes outage, instead the packet is dropped.

bugs.title: SWG URL categorization may cause the /var/lib/mysql file system to fill.
bugs.symptoms: Secure Web Gateway (SWG) URL categorization may cause the /var file system to fill. This might manifest in the following ways. 1. The /var/lib/mysql file system is full or approaching 100% utilization, as shown in the following example: # df -h /var/lib/mysql Filesystem Size Used Avail Use% Mounted on /dev/mapper/vg--db--vda-app.ASWADB.set.1.mysqldb 12G 11G 576M 95% /var/lib/mysql 2. The database and index files for SWG URL categorization have grown very large, as shown in the following example: -- /var/lib/mysql/AVR/AVR_DIM_APM_SWG_URL.MYD: 8.1G <--- Database! -- /var/lib/mysql/AVR/AVR_DIM_APM_SWG_URL.MYI: 765M <--- Index!
bugs.conditions: SWG is provisioned and configured to perform URL classification, and a large amount of web traffic is being proxied by the SWG system.
bugs.impact: This results in the following impacts: - SWG-related operations dependent on MySQL may fail. - Once the /var/lib/mysql file system reaches 100% utilization, other BIG-IP system functions that are dependent on the MySQL system may also experience issues.
bugs.workaround: The issue can be worked around by resetting the AVR statistics. You can find information on how to reset AVR statistics in SOL14956: Resetting BIG-IP AVR statistics, available at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/900/sol14956.html. Impact of procedure: The procedure removes all Analytics data and resets the MySQL database.
bugs.fix: Secure Web Gateway (SWG) URL categorization no longer causes the /var file system to fill.

bugs.title: Destination route-domain specified in the SOCKS profile
bugs.symptoms: The SOCKS profile route-domain setting is supposed to control which route domain is used for destination addresses. It is currently used to identify the listener/tunnel interface to use when forwarding the traffic, but does not set the route domain on the destination address used by the proxy to determine how to forward the traffic.
bugs.conditions: When the virtual server receives a SOCKS request and the route-domain is not the default (0).
bugs.impact: SOCKS connection fails immediately and the system returns the following message to the client: Results(V5): General SOCKS server failure (1). Traffic is forwarded correctly only when the destination is route-domain 0. Other route domains might result in error messages and possible failed traffic.
bugs.workaround: Use a destination route-domain of 0 when working with the SOCKS profile.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the destination route-domain specified in the SOCKS profile. This allows the SOCKS profile to work correctly when the destination is not in route-domain 0.

bugs.title: DSR rejects return traffic for monitoring the server
bugs.symptoms: System DB variable 'tm.monitorencap' controls whether the server monitor traffic is encapsulated inside DSR tunnel. If it is set to 'enable', monitor traffic is encapsulated, and return traffic is without the tunnel encapsulation. In such a case, the return traffic is not mapped to the original monitor flow, and gets rejected/lost.
bugs.conditions: System DB variable 'tm.monitorencap' is set to 'enable', and DSR server pool is monitored.
bugs.impact: Monitor traffic gets lost, and server pool is marked down.
bugs.fix: The DSR tunnel flow now sets the correct underlying network interface, so that the return monitor flow can match the originating flow, which results in the DSR monitor working as expected.

bugs.title: tmm may crash in the case of mem alloc fails.
bugs.symptoms: tmm may crash in the case of mem alloc fails.
bugs.conditions: mem alloc that occurs with incompletely constructed RX queues.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now gracefully handles this mem alloc failure.

bugs.title: EAM memory leak when cookiemap is destroyed without deleting Cookie object in it
bugs.symptoms: EAM memory growing and OOM kills EAM process under memory pressure.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using access management such as Oracle Access Manager, when an authentication request is redirected to IDP (redirect URL is present) with cookies present, memory can grow unbounded.
bugs.impact: EAM memory usage increases and OOM kills EAM process if the system is under memory pressure.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround
bugs.fix: EAM memory usage no longer grows. Cookie objects are deleted prior to deleting cookieMap from obAction destructor.

bugs.title: postgres database configuration details are now captured by qkview
bugs.symptoms: The postgres database service provided on BIG-IP devices is largely ignored by the qkview diagnostic collection utility.
bugs.conditions: Using qkview.
bugs.impact: No postgres database configuration details.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Qkview now collects the new postgres items every time it executes. Qkview will now collect the following items: The files: /var/local/pgsql/postgresql.conf /var/local/pgsql/pg_hba.conf /var/local/pgsql/PG_VERSION A directory listing of: /var/local/pgsql/data and execute the following command: /usr/bin/pg_dump -h localhost -U postgres

bugs.title: Cannot launch Horizon RDS applications with the HTML5 client
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support launching Horizon RDS applications with the HTML5 client.
bugs.conditions: Accessing APM webtop with Horizon resources expanded into some RDS applications.
bugs.impact: Cannot launch Horizon RDS applications with the HTML5 client.
bugs.fix: Support for HTML5 client with Horizon RDS applications has been implemented.

bugs.title: XFV driver can leak memory
bugs.symptoms: When the interface goes down, memory is not correctly freed.
bugs.conditions: the leak happens when the interface goes down
bugs.impact: Over a long enough period of time the BIG-IP can go out of memory and TMM needs to be restarted.
bugs.fix: The driver was corrected so that when the interface is brought down, all the xfrags currently in the ring buffer are freed.

bugs.title: Renaming a virtual server with an attached plugin can cause buffer overflow
bugs.symptoms: Renaming a virtual server (essentially, moving one virtual server to a new location, which effectively renames it) might cause buffer overflow and potentially result in Failover.
bugs.conditions: The database variable 'mcpd.mvenabled' must be set to 'true'. Also, when moving a virtual server, the new name must be longer than the original name.
bugs.impact: Buffer overflow and potentially failover.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the move command. Instead, issue a delete followed by a create command in a transaction.
bugs.fix: Renaming a virtual server now works as expected, and does not results in buffer overflow or failover.

bugs.title: 10G interoperability issues reported following Cisco Nexus switch version upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: 10G link issues reported with VIPRION B2250, B4300 blades and BIG-IP 10x00 appliances connected to Cisco Nexus switches.
bugs.conditions: Issues reported after version upgrade on Cisco switch to version 7.0(5)N1(1).
bugs.impact: The links might not come up.
bugs.workaround: Toggling the SFP+ interfaces reportedly usually restores link.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system's 10G link now consistently becomes active when it is connected to other switches.

bugs.title: REST API command to create a new pool member on an existing pool returns a 404 error
bugs.symptoms: The following REST API command to create a new pool member on an existing pool works as expected in v11.5.2, but after upgrading to any v11.5.3 through v12.0.0 release returns a 404 error. curl -X POST -H "Content-Type:application/json" https://pt-f5-BIG-IP-1.pt-virt.exmple.com/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/~cldform_partition~test-cfme-pool/members -d '{"kind":"tm:ltm:pool:members:membersstate", "name":"test-eap-0.dev.example.com:80", "address":"192.168.1.1?}' --user testuser:$password --insecure However, pool member list in the GUI or TMSH shows the new member has been created.
bugs.conditions: - Setup a plain LTM system with normal set of objects including a pool. - Run the CURL command specified, adjusting the details to match what to use for that LTM and pool. (You can find reference information in the following DevCentral article, REST API Pool Member Creation: https://devcentral.f5.com/questions/rest-api-pool-member-creation.)
bugs.impact: Although the system presents a 404 error, the pool member is still created.
bugs.workaround: Ignore 404 error in REST command for creating a pool member.

bugs.title: iRule validation does not check RULE_INIT/virtual are disallowed in proc calling
bugs.symptoms: iRule validation does not check RULE_INIT/virtual are disallowed in proc calling
bugs.conditions: Under RULE_INIT event call a proc which has virtual command.
bugs.impact: Pass validation while it should not.
bugs.workaround: Do not call virtual command inside proc.
bugs.fix: Use the workaround.

bugs.title: Some changes to virtual servers' profile lists may cause secondary blades to restart
bugs.symptoms: If a virtual server's ip-protocol is not set, then some changes to the list of attached profiles may cause a validation error on secondary blades. This will cause those blades to restart.
bugs.conditions: This may happen in some cases when changing the list of profiles attached to a virtual server, but does not happen if 'ip-protocol' was explicitly set by the user.
bugs.impact: mcpd will restart on secondary blades. This will cause most other daemons on those blades to restart as well, including the TMM. Traffic will be lost.
bugs.workaround: You should explicitly set the ip-protocol when changing the profiles of a virtual server. Then this bug will not occur.
bugs.fix: If a virtual server's ip-protocol was not set, then some changes to the list of attached profiles would cause a validation error on secondary blades. This would cause those blades to restart. This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: VPN connection cannot be established from browser on MAC in some cases
bugs.symptoms: VPN connection cannot be established from browser on MAC if network access settings has huge number of split tunneling entries
bugs.conditions: -VPN is launched from the browser -Network access configuration is huge (around 200 split tunneling entries)
bugs.impact: User cannot launch VPN from browser
bugs.workaround: 1) Use Edge client or 2) reduce the size of network access configuration
bugs.fix: Now VPN can be established from browser even if Network Access configuration is big.

bugs.title: SSL has memory leak when peer sent a certificate chain but BIGIP SSL configured only Root certificate as trust CA.
bugs.symptoms: SSL has memory leak if during SSL negotiation peer sent a certificate chain but BIGIP configured only Root certificate as trusted CA. tmsh show sys memory: ssl_hs, ssl_hs_m and/or ssl memory usage will get bigger. The system may eventually out of memory and crash.
bugs.conditions: If peer sends certificate chain such as Root-Intermediate-Leaf certificates, but BIGIP SSL only configured Root cert as trusted CA, then there is SSL memory leak. If peer sends certificate chain such as Root-Intermediate-Leaf certificates, but BIGIP SSL configured Root-Intermediate certs as trusted CAs, then there is NOT memory leak.
bugs.impact: The BIGIP system will run out of memory, and eventually the BIGIP TMM may crash.
bugs.workaround: The workaround if applicable is to configure Root CA cert and all Intermediate CA certs in the trusted CA certs.

bugs.title: OPSWAT fails for Mac OS and Sophos AV version 9.4
bugs.symptoms: OPSWAT fails for Mac OS and Sophos AV version 9.4
bugs.conditions: Update Sophos Antivirus software to v9.4.0.
bugs.impact: AV Check fails.

bugs.title: Networking devices might block a packet that has a TTL value higher than 230.
bugs.symptoms: Some networking devices block a packet that has a TTL value higher than 230. The TTL value for the BIG-IP system is set to 255 internally and cannot be changed.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when traffic originates from the BIG-IP system (as a client).
bugs.impact: No access to the resources.
bugs.fix: The TTL value can now be changed from the hardcoded value of 255. This supports the requirement that some networking devices have to block a packet whose TTL value is higher than 230.

bugs.title: Changing ACL Order can cause General Database Error
bugs.symptoms: GUI showed 'General Database Error' when accessing the 'Change ACL Order' page and changing the ACL Order. It also happens when accessing 'Change ACL Order', making no changes, and selecting 'Finished.' However, adding or removing ACL entries reports no error.
bugs.conditions: -- Accessing the 'Change ACL Order' page and changing the ACL Order. -- Accessing 'Change ACL Order', making no changes, and selecting 'Finished.'
bugs.impact: User cannot change ACL order using the GUI.

bugs.title: Any AFM Management Port rules disappear from iptables upon 'bigstart restart iptables'
bugs.symptoms: Any AFM Management Port rules disappear from iptables upon 'bigstart restart iptables'.
bugs.conditions: -- Issuing the command: bigstart restart iptables. -- AFM configured.
bugs.impact: AFM Management Port rules disappear from iptables.
bugs.workaround: Before issuing the command 'bigstart restart iptables' issue the following command: /sbin/iptables-save > /etc/sysconfig/iptables

bugs.title: SNMP query response for sysPacketFilterStatHits is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: SNMP query response for sysPacketFilterStatHits return an inaccurate value. Typically a zero value.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at sysPacketFilterStatHits via snmp.
bugs.impact: Unable to view packet filter hits.
bugs.workaround: The tmctl command tmctl packet_filter_rule_stat can be used to show the filter statistics.

bugs.title: Diameter connection may stall if server closes connection before CER/CEA handshake completes
bugs.symptoms: Serverside connection stalls. Connection is not torn down and packets are not forwarded to serverside.
bugs.conditions: Selected pool member closes (via FIN) connection before sending CEA as part of Diameter handshake.
bugs.impact: Connection stalls until handshake timeout and then it is reset.
bugs.fix: Serverside diameter connections will be immediately reset if FIN is received before CEA (Capabilities-Exchange-Answer).

bugs.title: Some time zones prevent configuring trust with a peer device using the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: AEST, AEDT, ACDT, ACWST, ACWDT, AWST, Asia/Muscat, and AWDT time zones prevent configuring trust with a peer device using the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Setting a BIG-IP system timezone to AEST, AEDT, ACDT, ACWST, ACWDT, AWST, Asia/Muscat, or AWDT. -- Using the GUI to add a peer device to a trust configuration.
bugs.impact: Adding a peer device using the GUI fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds (you might find the first one easier): -- Temporarily set the device timezone to a non-affected timezone (e.g.; UTC), establish trust, and set it back: 1. Navigate to System :: Platform. 2. Under 'Time Zone', select 'UTC', and click 'Update' 3. Repeat steps one and two to change all devices that are to be part of the trust domain. 4. Establish device trust by navigating to Device Management :: Device Trust :: Add all peers to be part of the trust domain. 5. Once trust is established, navigate to System :: Platform, and change Time Zone back to preferred time zone. -- Use tmsh to add a peer device in these timezones: AEST, AEDT, ACDT, ACWST, ACWDT, AWST, Asia/Muscat, or AWDT.
bugs.fix: You can now use the GUI to add AEST, AEDT, ACDT, ACWST, ACWDT, AWST, Asia/Muscat, and AWDT when adding a peer device.

bugs.title: Incorrect information/text (in French) is displayed when the Edge Client is launched
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect information/text (in French) is displayed when the Edge Client is launched.
bugs.conditions: Edge client is used in French locale.
bugs.impact: User sees grammatically incorrect text in French. This is a cosmetic error that has no impact on system functionality.
bugs.fix: The correct information/text (in French) is now displayed when the Edge Client is launched.

bugs.title: URL including a "token" query fails results in a connection reset
bugs.symptoms: Per Request Policy access to URL containing a "token" query parameter fails and results in a connection reset with the following error: "ERR_NOT_FOUND: access2 token not found; subsession might be inactive"
bugs.conditions: Configure an Explicit SWG with a PRP that includes [protocol lookup (https) + category-lookup] It does not matter ntlm or basic auth. This is triggered on sites that have "token" in the query parameters.
bugs.impact: Clients receive this response: "ERR_NOT_FOUND: access2 token not found; subsession might be inactive"
bugs.workaround: Workaround iRule: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::query] contains "token" } { set fix 1 HTTP::query [string map "token aabbcc" [HTTP::query]] } } when HTTP_REQUEST_SEND { if { [info exists fix] && $fix equals 1 } { clientside { HTTP::query [string map "aabbcc token" [HTTP::query]] unset fix } } }
bugs.fix: Customization namespace for subsession state prefix with default value as "000fffff" has been added controlled via db variable "tmm.access.subsessionstateprefix" before state/token query param and validation is ensured to check for the prefix value before triggering serialize/deserialize code to avoid RST. In case if a UCS is being restored and used for a Hotfix, the newly added DB variable may not be present in /config/Bigdb.dat file. The following information needs to be added in /config/Bigdb.dat file followed by a "bigstart restart" to ensure proper working. # # This string is used as the prefix for the subsession state value that is sent as # part of the redirect URI being sent to the client. # [Tmm.Access.SubsessionStatePrefix] default=000fffff type=string realm=local display_name=Tmm.Access.SubsessionStatePrefix scf_config=true max=32

bugs.title: Errant DNS Express database log message.
bugs.symptoms: Upon initial system configuration or whenever the DNS Express database is recreated, the log message "Failed to reload dns-express db (Open)." may display in the ltm log for a short period of time. The message indicates that tmm attempted to load the database before it was written to disk. This error message is only of concern if it is persistent.
bugs.conditions: This error message may occur upon initial system configuration or if the DNS Express database has been regenerated.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to the system.

bugs.title: Monitors stop working - throttling monitor instance probe because file descriptor limit 65436 reached
bugs.symptoms: Monitor checks stop working. The ltm log file contains error messages similar to the following: 01060154:4: Bigd PID 7147, instance 0, throttling monitor instance probe because file descriptor limit 65436 reached.
bugs.conditions: - You have a monitor type configured that uses Tcl internally (for example, FTP, IMAP, POP3, SMTP monitors). - You have monitor logging enabled for the pool members or nodes. tmsh list ltm pool <pool_name> members { ... <member> { ... logging enabled tmsh list ltm node <node_ip> ... logging enabled
bugs.impact: Monitoring stops working; pool members are marked down when they are not.
bugs.workaround: No workaround if Tcl-using monitors are configured. If pool member or node level monitor logging is configured, cease logging and restart bigd. Disable monitor logging with appropriate commands on all pools and nodes necessary: tmsh modify ltm pool <pool-name> members modify { all { logging disabled }} tmsh modify ltm node <node-ip> logging disabled Restart bigd: tmsh restart sys service bigd
bugs.fix: Resolved resource leak so monitors continue to work properly.

bugs.title: Resolver H.ROOT-SERVERS.NET Address Change
bugs.symptoms: The IPv4 and IPv6 addresses for H.ROOT-SERVERS.NET are changing on December 1st 2015 from (128.63.2.53 / 2001:500:1::803f:235) to (198.97.190.53 / 2001:500:1::53). The old addresses will be good for 6 months after the change, and then the IPv4 address will go completely offline, and the IPv6 address is subject to go offline as well. More details http://h.root-servers.org/renumber.html
bugs.conditions: DNS Resolver uses hard-coded root hints for H.ROOT-SERVERS.NET.
bugs.impact: Incorrect address for a root-server means no response to that query.
bugs.workaround: There are 12 other root-servers that also provide answers to TLD queries, so this is cosmetic, but the addresses still need to be updated to respond to the change.
bugs.fix: Updated H.ROOT-SERVERS.NET to reflect the new IPv4 and IPv6 addresses taking effect December 1st, 2015 from (128.63.2.53 / 2001:500:1::803f:235) to (198.97.190.53 / 2001:500:1::53). For more information, see H-Root will change its addresses on 1 December 2015, available here: http://h.root-servers.org/renumber.html.

bugs.title: LCD display stops updating and Status LED turns/blinks Amber
bugs.symptoms: The LCD display may stop updating and the Status LED may turn Amber and begin blinking on BIG-IP 2000, 4000, 5000, 7000, or 10000-series appliances.
bugs.conditions: The Status LED turns Amber if the LED/LCD module stops receiving updates from the BIG-IP host, and begins blinking Amber if the LED/LCD module does not receive updates from the BIG-IP host for three minutes or longer. This condition may occur if data transfers between the BIG-IP host and the LED/LCD module over the connecting USB bus becomes stalled. Due to changes in BIG-IP v11.5.0 and later, the frequency and likelihood of this condition is greatly reduced, but may still occur under rare conditions.
bugs.impact: When this condition occurs, the front-panel LCD display does not display the current BIG-IP host status, and the Status LED blinks Amber. There is no impact to BIG-IP host operations, and no disruption to traffic.
bugs.workaround: This condition can be cleared by either of the following actions: 1. Press one of the buttons on the LCD display to navigate the LCD menus. 2. Issue the following command at the BIG-IP host console: /sbin/lsusb -v -d 0451:3410. Either action generates USB traffic, which triggers recovery from the USB stalled transfer condition.
bugs.fix: Auto-recovery from a USB stalled-transfer condition has been implemented, which prevents the Status LED from blinking Amber on BIG-IP 2000, 4000, 5000, 7000, 10000 or 12000-series appliances.

bugs.title: Renaming a virtual server will emit unnecessary '01010007:3: Config error: virtual_server_profile bad virtual' error messages in the ltm log.
bugs.symptoms: Renaming a virtual server will emit unnecessary error messages in the ltm log: 01010007:3: Config error: virtual_server_profile bad virtual.
bugs.conditions: Renaming a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The system emits an unnecessary error messages in the ltm log: 01010007:3: Config error: virtual_server_profile bad virtual. The virtual server is renamed and the configuration is correct. However, these spurious error messages are logged which, in this case, do not indicate a problem.

bugs.title: TMSH mv virtual command will cause iRules on the virtual to be dis-associated
bugs.symptoms: After renaming a virtual server that has attached iRules, the resulting virtual server configuration in tmm no longer has the iRules attached. The configuration in mcpd does not match the running configuration in tmm.
bugs.conditions: Must use the 'mv' command on an ltm virtual with iRules.
bugs.impact: Configuration is not as expected.
bugs.workaround: After moving the virtual, remove the iRules on it and re-add them.

bugs.title: Cache Lookups for Validating Resolvers ignore the query's DNSSEC OK (DO) bit
bugs.symptoms: RRSIG present when not asked for, and RRSIG and AD drop from response upon expiration from the cache.
bugs.conditions: If standard DNS requests are made against a Validating Resolver DNS cache that points to a second BIG-IP which in turn contains a wideip in a signed zone
bugs.impact: RRSIG present when not asked for, and RRSIG and AD drop from response upon expiration from the cache
bugs.fix: Update message encoding to depend on client DO bit.

bugs.title: AFM rule with "unknown" source Geo-entity stops functioning when another entity (geolocation or otherwise) is added to the same list of addresses in the rule
bugs.symptoms: When an AFM rule is configured to "unknown" geographic location, the rule stops functioning when another entity (geolocation or IP address) is added to the same list of addresses in the rule.
bugs.conditions: Configure an address list of AFM rule with "unknown" source Geo-entity and at least one other entity (geolocation or IP address).
bugs.impact: Confusing, inconsistent, and apparently broken behavior.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure "unknown" geographic locations as one of the entities in an address list. Known geographic locations work correctly.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing HTTP traffic with a FastL4 virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When a FastL4 virtual server with HTTP profile is used, certain traffic flows may cause excessive resource consumption.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 virtual server with HTTP profile.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a TMM crash and failover event.
bugs.workaround: -- If the HTTP profile is required, use a standard virtual server rather than performance (FastL4) type. -- If the HTTP profile is not required, you can remove the HTTP profile from the virtual server.
bugs.fix: TMM now process FastL4 HTTP traffic as expected

bugs.title: Crash on unexpected WAM storage queue state
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances WAM may enter an unexpected queue state and crash.
bugs.conditions: WAM configured on virtual with request queuing enabled
bugs.impact: Crash
bugs.fix: Gracefully recover from unexpected WAM storage queue state

bugs.title: Modifying an HTTP cookie value via the HTTP::cookie iRule API may yield to incorrect HTTP header data
bugs.symptoms: Upon repeatedly modifying the same HTTP cookie value (in the Set-Cookie header) within an iRule attached to a virtual server, the HTTP::cookie API may produce stale HTTP header data (e.g. HTTP Set-Cookie header and/or other HTTP headers).
bugs.conditions: LTM Virtual Server handling HTTP traffic, with iRule attached which modifies a given HTTP cookie value through the HTTP::cookie API, on ingress and/or egress traffic (through the HTTP_REQUEST and/or HTTP_RESPONSE events). An example use-case for producing the error would be encrypting and decrypting HTTP cookies via an iRule.
bugs.impact: Repeatedly altering the same HTTP cookie value in an iRule, via the HTTP::cookie API, may yield to an HTTP request/response with inconsistent HTTP header data, including but not limited to the Set-Cookie HTTP header.

bugs.title: Nokia alarms are not deleted due to the outdated alert_nokia.conf.
bugs.symptoms: Some of the log messages watched by alertd changed between BIG-IP software versions 10.x to versions 11.x/12.x. However, the /etc/alertd/alert_nokia.conf file has not been updated accordingly.
bugs.conditions: Running versions 11.x/12.x and receiving targeted messages that match the 10.x regex key fields. This occurs when the Nokia snmp alarms are enabled. See K15435 at https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K15435
bugs.impact: Matching the specific fields in the log message fails, so the corresponding alarm is not deleted from the nokia_alarm table. This might cause SNMP alerts to not be broadcast in Nokia-specific environments.
bugs.fix: The log messages watched by alertd and appearing in alert_nokia.conf now match each clear event key to its corresponding error definition, so alerts are recorded correctly.

bugs.title: SAML IdP requests may fail when Sharepoint is opened through Portal Access in the same browser
bugs.symptoms: SAML IdP resources can't be opened from webtop if there is a Sharepoint resource window opened from the same webtop. An attempt to open SAML IdP resource could result in 404 or connection reset. This was happening because Portal Access code processed special cookie for Sharepoint before checking if the request is internal for APM.
bugs.conditions: This exists when a SAML IdP resource exists on a full webtop and a user attempts to connect to a SharePoint Portal Access resource.
bugs.impact: SAML resources can't be accessed from webtop.
bugs.workaround: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::uri] starts_with "/saml" } { HTTP::cookie remove "MRHSHint" } }
bugs.fix: Addressed an issue where SAML IdP requests were failing because of the special Sharepoint handling code in Portal Access.

bugs.title: When SAML IdP-Connector Single Sign On Service URL contains ampersand, redirect URL may be truncated
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is used as SAML Service Provider, and IdP-Connectors Single Sign On Service URL contains ampersand (&), part of the URL may be truncated when user is redirected to IdP for authentication.
bugs.conditions: All conditions must be true: - BIG-IP is used as SAML Service Provider - Single Sign On Service URL property of IdP connector contains ampersand, e.g. https://idp.f5.com/saml/idp/profile/redirectorpost/sso?a=b&foo=bar - User performs SP initiated SSO
bugs.impact: The query part of the redirect URL after ampersand will be lost when user is redirected to SSO URL with Authentication Request.
bugs.fix: Redirect URL is no longer truncated after ampersand sign.

bugs.title: TMM may core during processing of a CCA-T.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core during processing of a CCA-T.
bugs.conditions: For every session there is Gx context and Main session Context. There are always stitched to same processing unit to have synchronous look ups when a flow arrives for the session. These contexts are mirrored on a different blades for high availability (HA). The issue occurs when the following events happen. 1. Main session moveds to a new processing unit (Failover) trigger. 2. This session is marked for deletion by RAR from PCRF or RADIUS Stop. 3. Session delete is initiated from main session by sending a local message. 4. Gx context has not yet moved to this processing unit. 5. CCR-T was sent for this session after asynchronous lookup for the Gx context and we freed the local message. This is the bug. (See explanation below) 6. Gx context moved 7. PCRF sends CCA-T came back and tried to look up local message queued to acknowledge to main session. 8. Local message was deleted at step 5 and TMM cored.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release prevents freeing of the Gx context when a CCR-T is sent out even if the Gx session is remote (present on another tmm), which prevents the TMM core.

bugs.title: Non-explicit (*) IPv4 monitor destination address is converted to IPv6 on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: A monitor destination address in the form of *:port (IPv4) is converted to *.port when upgrading from 10.2.4 to 11.5.x.
bugs.conditions: A monitor exists with a non-explicit address and explicit port on a BIG-IP system running 10.2.4. Then upgrade to 11.5.x (or install 10.2.4 ucs)
bugs.impact: Monitors appears to function normally but they will have the wrong format in the config file.
bugs.fix: Determine if non-explicit (*) address is ipv4 or ipv6 based on next character to be parsed.

bugs.title: Edge client sends repeated HTTP probe to captive portal probe URL for mis-configured server
bugs.symptoms: Edge client sends repeated HTTP probe to captive portal probe URL for mis-configured server. This has no functional impact on end user.
bugs.conditions: End user specifies incorrect VPN server URL in edge client
bugs.impact: None. This has no functional impact on end user.
bugs.workaround: Specify correct server URL in edge client
bugs.fix: No Edge client caches results of probe query reducing number of queries sent to probe URL.

bugs.title: 'tmsh show net cmetrics' reports bandwidth = 0
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh show net cmetrics' reports bandwidth = 0
bugs.conditions: tcp profile enables cmetrics-cache. connection involves at least 4 rtt updates.
bugs.impact: User cannot view cmetrics data.
bugs.workaround: For 12.0.0 and later, you can get this data using the ROUTE::bandwidth iRule. For earlier versions, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Properly compute bandwidth with the formula cwnd/rtt.

bugs.title: Status LED blinking Amber on BIG-IP 10000-series appliance
bugs.symptoms: The LCD display may stop updating and the Status LED may begin blinking Amber on BIG-IP 10000-series appliances.
bugs.conditions: The Status LED will blink Amber if the LED/LCD module does not receive updates from the BIG-IP host for 3 minutes or longer. This condition may occur if data transfers between the BIG-IP host and the LED/LCD module over the connecting USB bus becomes stalled.
bugs.impact: When this condition occurs, the front-panel LCD display will not display the current BIG-IP host status, and the Status LED will blink Amber. There is no impact to BIG-IP host operations, and no disruption to traffic.
bugs.workaround: This condition can be cleared by pressing one of the buttons on the LCD display to navigate the LCD menus. The button-press event generates USB traffic which will trigger recovery from the USB stalled transfer condition.

bugs.title: BIG-IP SSL does not support sending multiple certificate verification requests to the hardware accelerator at the same time in 11.6.0.
bugs.symptoms: When SSL sends multiple certificate verification requests at the same time, the handshake is disconnected with 'bad certificate'.
bugs.conditions: SSL simultaneously sends multiple certificate verification requests.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP SSL does not support this case and the SSL handshake is disconnected with "bad certificate".
bugs.fix: BIG-IP SSL now supports sending multiple certificate verification requests at the same time.

bugs.title: MTU Updates should erase all congestion metrics entries
bugs.symptoms: MTU updates erase cwnd cache entries, but not ssthresh or RTT, while an MTU update generally indicates a path change, meaning that these values might be invalid.
bugs.conditions: TCP cached congestion metrics from a previous connection, and subsequently receives an ICMP PMTU message.
bugs.impact: Connection might use invalid congestion metrics.
bugs.workaround: Disable cmetrics-cache, accept the suboptimal cached values, or write an iRule to purge the entry after path change.
bugs.fix: MTU updates now erase all congestion metrics entries, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: pccd crash when loading firewall config with mixed IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the same rule
bugs.symptoms: pccd crash when loading firewall config with mixed IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the same rule
bugs.conditions: If firewall config contains rules with mixed IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the same rule (either as source addresses or destination addresses), pccd may crash
bugs.impact: pccd crash.
bugs.workaround: Separate different address family addresses into separate rules. In other word, each firewall rule should contain only IPv4 or OPv6 addresses.

bugs.title: Monitor with send/receive string containing double-quote may fail to load.
bugs.symptoms: When a monitor string contains contains \" (backslash double-quote) but does not contain a character that requires quoting, one level of escaping is lost at each save/load. Note: Re-loading a config happens during licensing. If you decide to upgrade, first verify that you have an escaped quote in the monitor string. If you do, remove the re-licensing step from your MOP (Method of Procedure). The failure message for reloading the license with an escaped quote appears similar to the following example: Monitor monitor_1 parameter contains unescaped " escape with backslash.
bugs.conditions: If the string contains \" (backslash double-quote) but does not contain one of the following characters: ' (single quote), | (pipe), { (open brace), } (close brace), ; (semicolon), # (hashtag), literal newline, or literal space.
bugs.impact: Monitors are marked down due to expected string not matching or incorrect send string. Potential load failure.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Modify the content the BIG-IP system retrieves from the web server for the purposes of health monitoring, so that double quotes are not necessary. -- Use an external monitor instead.
bugs.fix: If the monitor send-recv strings contain a double-quote ", character, the system now adds quotes to the input. If a configuration contains '/"', does not reload the license before upgrade.

bugs.title: Hardware parity error mitigation for the SOURCE_VP table on 10000s/10200v/10250v platforms and B4300/B4340N and B2250 blades
bugs.symptoms: In rare occurrences, BIG-IP hardware is susceptible to parity errors due to unknown source. This bug mitigates parity errors that occur in the SOURCE_VP table of the switch hardware, indicated with the following message in the ltm log: Sep 15 12:12:12 info bcm56xxd[8066]: 012c0016:6: _soc_xgs3_mem_dma: SOURCE_VP.ipipe0 failed(NAK)
bugs.conditions: This occurs only on the BIG-IP 10000s/10200v/10250v platforms, and on the VIPRION B4300/B4340N and B2250 blades. The exact trigger of the parity error is unknown at this time.
bugs.impact: This impacts several series of BIG-IP products with hardware parity error mitigation capabilities.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting BIG-IP hardware should clear issues caused by hardware parity errors.
bugs.fix: A hardware parity error issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: [APM] HTTP status 500 response of successful Access Policy in clientless mode on chassis platform
bugs.symptoms: Successful execution of an Access Policy will result in the client receiving a HTTP status 500 error response when clientless mode is set. This error response is generated by APMD. This is a regression condition that occurs when the fix for bug 374067 is included.
bugs.conditions: -- The system has the fix for bug 374067. -- Clientless mode is enabled. -- BIG-IP platform is chassis platform. -- The administrator does not override the Access Policy response with iRule command.
bugs.impact: Client receives an invalid response.
bugs.fix: Upon successful execution of the Access Policy in clientless mode, the request is forwarded to the configured backend as needed.

bugs.title: GTM server 'Virtual Server Score' not showing correctly in TMSH stats
bugs.symptoms: GTM server 'Virtual Server Score' is not showing correct values in TMSH stats. Instead, stats shows zero value.
bugs.conditions: You have a virtual server configured with a non-zero score.
bugs.impact: tmsh show gtm server server-name detail lists 'Virtual Server Score' as zero. Note that there is no impact to actual load balancing decisions. Those decisions take into account the configured score. This is an issue only with showing the correct information and stats.
bugs.fix: TMSH now shows the correct value for 'Virtual Server Score' when you have a virtual server configured with a non-zero score.

bugs.title: Portal Access: corrections to CORS support for XMLHttpRequest
bugs.symptoms: XMLHttpRequest to external domain should fail if the server does not include 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header into response. Current implementation of CORS support in Portal Access does not enforce this failure. If XMLHttpRequest to same-origin resource is redirected to external one, it has to be treated as cross-domain request. Current implementation of CORS support in Portal Access does not handle this case correctly.
bugs.conditions: XMLHttpRequest to external domain via Portal Access succeeds even when the server response does not include 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header. XMLHttpRequest to same-origin resource succeeds via Portal Access in spite of response redirection.
bugs.impact: Web application may work incorrectly; some data access restrictions may not work.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access supports CORS in case of response redirection for XMLHttpRequest. CORS support enforces error in the case when 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is absent in server response.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Links targeting new window must not be rewritten as script
bugs.symptoms: Code for dynamic <base> handling tries to rewrite absolute-path references as a 'javascript:location=...'. This does not work for links with target='_blank', or other ways to open link in a new document.
bugs.conditions: A Ref link with target not rewritten correctly.
bugs.impact: Can end up with broken links.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround specific to the backend web application available upon request.
bugs.fix: Links with target must be correctly rewritten.

bugs.title: If 1 tmm gets more than 1 Mpps then the 1m stats in dos_stats can be wrong
bugs.symptoms: If 1 tmm with AFM DoS gets more than 1 Mpps then in the dos_stats, where stats_1m is calculated (previous 60s average pps) can be wrong. This can cause the DoS attack to be detected sooner than it should.
bugs.conditions: AFM DoS configured and provisioned. Any 1 tmm gets more than 1 Mpps of a certain kind for which we've configured DoS attack detection - and this could cause the 1 minute average stats to be wrong.
bugs.impact: The state will be wrong and AFM could detect a DoS attack before it actually reaches the configured threshold.

bugs.title: Alerts send from FPS plugin via HSL are sent in a malformed HTTP format
bugs.symptoms:
FPS alerts end with 

, HSL adds an extra 
.
bugs.conditions: FPS plugin send an alert via HSL.
bugs.impact: Alerts sent by FPS plugin via HSL are in malformed format with extra \n at the end.
bugs.fix:
One hard-coded 
 was removed from the end of the FPS alerts format, so that they now end with 
. When alerts are sent via HSL, an extra 
 is added and the final alert format is correct (

).

bugs.title: Misdirected UDP traffic with hardware acceleration
bugs.symptoms: UDP traffic might be forwarded to the wrong destination when using hardware acceleration.
bugs.conditions: If the UDP timeout is lower than the embedded Packet Velocity Acceleration (ePVA) aging timeout. This occurs because UDP connections are accelerated until the ePVA aging timeout expires for the connection. If the ePVA aging timeout is greater than the UDP timeout, then TMM removes the connection from software, but the connection is still accelerated in the ePVA. Subsequent traffic then matches to the original connection, causing it to be sent to the wrong destination.
bugs.impact: Traffic can be sent to the wrong destination.
bugs.workaround: You can use either or both of the following workarounds: -- Increase the UDP timeout (60s or more). -- Disable UDP hardware acceleration.

bugs.title: ePVA snoop header's transform vlan should be set properly under asymmetric routing condition
bugs.symptoms: On ePVA capable platform with fastl4 profile and asymetric routing on client side, ltm sends packets to the client with wrong vlan/correct mac address (or correct vlan and wrong mac-address) and undecremented ttl.
bugs.conditions: fastl4 profile and asymetric routing on client side
bugs.impact: Return traffic could use the wrong vlan
bugs.fix: Use the nexthop VLAN for ePVA transformation for offloaded flow when available, instead of the incoming VLAN

bugs.title: Edge client needs to re-authenticate after lost network connectivity is restored
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client restarts executing access policy after lost connectivity is restored. Usually that means Edge client will try to re-authenticate (if access policy is configured so) after lost network connectivity is restored.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client for Mac, APM with access policy with authentication configured.
bugs.impact: User needs to input credentials again.
bugs.workaround: Access policy can have "Save password" option enabled. In this case Edge Client caches the password based on password caching policy in connectivity profile and will not ask for password if cache is still valid.
bugs.fix: Edge Client for Mac now tries to restore session after lost network connectivity is restored.

bugs.title: ASM limitation in the pattern matching matrix builtup
bugs.symptoms: The signature configuration is not building up upon adding new signatures. This can look like a configuration change is not finishing, or if it does, it may result in crashes when the Enforcer starts up resulting in constant startups.
bugs.conditions: Too many signatures are configured with custom signatures. The exact number varies (depending on the signature) but hundreds of signatures may be enough to trigger it.
bugs.impact: Configuration change doesn't finish or crashes in the ASM startup (which results in constant startups of the system).
bugs.workaround: Workarounds are possible only in a custom signature scenario, only using fewer signatures or by removing unused signatures.
bugs.fix: Fixed a limitation in the attack signature engine.

bugs.title: Continuous error report in /dev/log/ltm: Device error: n3-compress0 Nitrox 3, Hang Detected
bugs.symptoms: Hardware compression slowly and progressively fails to handle compression operations. The system posts the following errors in ltm.log: crit tmm3[14130]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Nitrox 3.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system encounters errors during hardware compression handling. This occurs on the BIG-IP 5000-, 7000-, 10000-, and 12000-series platforms, and on VIPRION B22xx blades.
bugs.impact: Compression is (eventually) performed by software. This can result in high CPU utilization.
bugs.workaround: Disable compression if CPU usage is too high.
bugs.fix: Improved the device exception handling so that errors are correctly propagated to compression clients, thus preventing the progressive failure of the compression engine, and stopping the offload to software compression (which was driving up the CPU).

bugs.title: LTM v11.6.0 iControl REST transaction w/multiple commands don't work as expected
bugs.symptoms: An exception may be thrown during mcp transaction when processing a more than one delete request.
bugs.conditions: One of the objects being deleted must have a dependency on the other.
bugs.impact: A valid transaction may fail.

bugs.title: APM App Tunnel/AM iSession Connection Memory Leak
bugs.symptoms: A memory leak occurs when APM application tunnels or AM iSession connections are aborted while waiting to be reused.
bugs.conditions: The iSession profile reuse-connection attribute is true. A large number of iSession connections are aborted while waiting to be reused.
bugs.impact: Available memory might be significantly reduced when a large number of iSession connections waiting to be reused are aborted.
bugs.workaround: Disable the iSession profile reuse-connection attribute. Restart TMM.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an APM App Tunnel/AM iSession connection memory leak.

bugs.title: Inconsistent behavior on IP TTL handling between ePVA and tmm for Fast L4 flows.
bugs.symptoms: Fast L4 proxy operates in TTL decrement mode. That means that for Fast L4 software-transformed flows (that is, no PVA acceleration) the system decrements TTL by 1 during the transform. In comparison, for the ePVA assisted flows, the system operates in preserve mode (no TTL change).
bugs.conditions: For all ePVA assisted flows.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent behavior on IP TTL handling between ePVA and tmm for Fast L4 flows: TTL is not decremented for ePVA assisted flows, but TTL is decremented for flows without hardware acceleration.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware acceleration to see TTL decrements.

bugs.title: APMD logging at debug level may log passwords in clear text
bugs.symptoms: APMD logging at debug level logs all request headers in clear text. Some request types contain passwords in headers resulting in passwords logged in clear text.
bugs.conditions: APMD logging at debug level.
bugs.impact: Some passwords may be logged in clear text.
bugs.workaround: Do not log at debug level unless absolutely necessary.

bugs.title: tmsh list display incorrectly for default values of gtm listener translate-address/translate-port
bugs.symptoms: tmsh list displays incorrectly for default values of GTM listener translate-address/translate-port settings.
bugs.conditions: Using the tmsh list command to show translate-address/translate-port for GTM listener.
bugs.impact: tmsh list gtm listener does not display 'translate-address'/'translate-port' when it is set to enabled, but the command does show the values when it is set to disabled. The tmsh list gtm listener command should not show the default settings. This becomes an issue when used with the TMSH merge command, where the value gets set to the LTM virtual server default instead of maintained as the GTM Listener default. This might eventually result in failing traffic.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh list with 'all-properties' instead.
bugs.fix: GTM Listener's translate-address and translate-port field are now always displayed in TMSH commands. This is because there are different defaults in GTM Listeners than the LTM virtual servers. When used with the TMSH merge command, the value gets set to the LTM virtual server default instead of maintained as the GTM Listener default. By always displaying this attribute, no matter what the value is, the merge will always be handled appropriately.

bugs.title: Virtual servers using an SSL profile and two UDP profiles may not be accepted
bugs.symptoms: Error message: 01070711:3: Found disallowed profile: Not Profile profile_clientssl or 01070711:3: Found disallowed profile: Not Profile profile_serverssl
bugs.conditions: Create a virtual server with a client-ssl profile and/or a server-ssl profile and two different UDP profiles (one on the server side and one on the client side).
bugs.impact: When using either a client-ssl profile or a server-ssl profile, depending on the sort order of the UDP profiles, the configuration may not be accepted. When using both a client-ssl profile and a server-ssl profile, the configuration is not accepted.
bugs.workaround: When using either a client-ssl profile or a server-ssl profile, either use a common UDP profile for both client and server side or try renaming one of the UDP profiles to alter the sort order. When using both a client-ssl profile and a server-ssl profile, try using one UDP profile for both the client and server side.
bugs.fix: Virtual servers that utilize an SSL profile and a combination of UDP profiles are now accepted.

bugs.title: Dynamic drive mapping in network access may not work if path is received via session variable from LDAP/AD
bugs.symptoms: Dynamic drive mapping in network access may not work if mapping is configured to use session variable, and session variable is received from LDAP/AD.
bugs.conditions: Drive mapping is received from LDAP/AD and contains double slash in the path, e.g. "\\server\path"
bugs.impact: Dynamic drive mapping may not function.
bugs.workaround: For example using session.ad.last.attr.homeDirectory attribute value to drive map. Assign variable and escape the textra backslashes added by APM. homeDirectory = return [regsub -all {\\\\} [mcget {session.ad.last.attr.homeDirectory}] {\\}]

bugs.title: Use of JavaScript's 'eval' function may be prohibited by site's content security policy
bugs.symptoms: Websafe JavaScript does not run on sites that prohibit the use of 'eval' by using CSP headers.
bugs.conditions: CSP headers present that do not allow 'unsafe-eval'.
bugs.impact: Websafe JavaScript does not run and false positive 'component check' alerts are received in the dashboard.
bugs.fix: Websafe JavaScript now runs as expected, so no false positive 'component check' alerts are received in the dashboard.

bugs.title: Disk provisioning error after restarting ASM service.
bugs.symptoms: Disk provisioning error after restarting ASM service. In newer BIG-IP software versions ASM uses a different application volume name. Older BIG-IP software versions identify the application volume as being owned by ASM, and allows ASM to be provisioned and start. However, in the older versions, ASM create the application volume so there will be two ASM application volumes. If ASM is restarted with bigstart or tmsh, or if the BIG-IP system is rebooted, provisioning does not allow ASM to start.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned on both pre-v12.0.0 and post-v12.0.0 versions.
bugs.impact: ASM does not start, and bigstart status asm indicates a disk provisioning error.
bugs.workaround: Follow these steps: 1. Boot into the affected version of BIG-IP software. 2. If DoS profiles are applied, they need to be removed from the virtual servers before the provisioning can be carried out, for example: # tmsh modify ltm virtual all profiles delete { DoS-A-profile } # tmsh modify ltm virtual all profiles delete { DoS-B-profile } ..... 3. Run the command: tmsh modify sys provision asm level none. 4. Wait for unprovision to complete (do so by monitoring /var/log/asm). 5. Run the command: tmsh delete sys disk application-volume asmdata1. 6. Run the command: tmsh modify sys provision asm level nominal
bugs.fix: ASM starts successfully with no disk provisioning error after restarting ASM service using newer BIG-IP software.

bugs.title: Missing upgrade support for AFM Network DoS reports.
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading, the statistics of AFM Network DoS reports are not migrated correctly to the new version, leading to loss of data about the Client-IP addresses.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from versions 11.4.x or 11.5.x to versions 11.6.x or 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: The IP Addresses information of AFM Network DoS is lost. However, new activity is collected correctly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: This release provides upgrade support for AFM Network DoS reports.

bugs.title: APMD basic authentication cookie domains are not processed correctly
bugs.symptoms: 401 responses containing Set-Cookie headers might not be processed correctly. Domains that begin with a dot will be truncated and the cookies will not be sent to pool members.
bugs.conditions: An access policy needs to use Basic or NTLM authentication and one or more of the 401 responses must contain Set-Cookie headers. If a domain is specified and the domain begins with a dot, it will not be processed correctly.
bugs.impact: Cookies assigned during the authentication handshake might not be sent to pool members.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be used to process the 401 responses and remove any leading dots from domain fields of Set-Cookie headers.
bugs.fix: Domain fields in Set-Cookie headers found in 401 responses are processed correctly.

bugs.title: Oracle monitor fails with certain time zones.
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, the OJDBC driver reads a time zone file that it cannot understand, which causes Oracle monitors to fail.
bugs.conditions: - The system uses ojdbc6.jar for Oracle monitor functionality. - The UTC time zone is configured. - Contents of the /usr/share/zoneinfo directory are arranged so that the 'UTC' file is not the first in the list. (Versions prior to 10.2.4 use the 1.4-compatible ojdbc14.jar driver. The objdbc6.jar OJDBC driver, as supplied by Oracle for Java 6 (aka 1.6) auto-detects the local system's time zone name by scanning and comparing files under /usr/share/zoneinfo. The filenames are created during installation, and seem to depend on the 'Directory Hash Seed' of the /usr filesystem, so there is no predictable result.)
bugs.impact: Cannot use direct Oracle monitoring to ensure the backend is functionally operational. OJDBC driver seems to negotiate the time zone for the session, and instead of 'UTC', it attempts to change the time zone to: 'Universal', 'Zulu', 'Etc/Universal', 'Etc/Zulu', which will cause the monitor to fail, and not execute the actual monitoring. Note: Other time zones might be affected.For example, a similar issue might happen with the time zone set to GMT, which can become 'Greenwich' because of the same functionality.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no reliable workaround, reinstalling might resolve the issue, as may using another time zone.
bugs.fix: Oracle monitor functions now as expected with UTC and other time zones.

bugs.title: DWA 8.5 with Safari on MAC OS X 10.11 : check names not works
bugs.symptoms: For Domino Web Access 8.5 with Safari on Mac OS X 10.11, check names does not work.
bugs.conditions: Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create new message. 2. Enter the beginning of recipient name and press Check Names. 3. If there are some users whose names start with the same substring, a screen displays with possible names; select one of them. Steps 3 fail with APM reverse proxy. No windows pop up with possible name.
bugs.impact: User unable use 'check names' functionality.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: AAA pool member creation sets the port to 0.
bugs.symptoms: When the AAA server pool member is created (for Radius mode BOTH and for AD), the port is set to 0 (Any) as there are more than one ports for that pool member.
bugs.conditions: Create AAA pool member while creating an AAA RADIUS server or Active Directory server. The created pool member does not support the ability of having multiple port numbers and for that reason is updated with 0 (Any) as the port number for the pool member. If the user continues to modify using the Admin UI, the port changes made using tmsh will be overwritten again to 0.
bugs.impact: AAA pool member port is set to 0 (Any) rather than the port specified in the GUI. This is correct as the pool member does not support more and 1 port number.

bugs.title: Login/logout using Safari presents 'server drop connection' message.
bugs.symptoms: Logging in to the BIG-IP system using Safari browser and then click the "Logout" button, the system posts an error similar to the following: Safari can not open the page because server drop connection.
bugs.conditions: Logging in to the BIG-IP system using Safari browser and then click the "Logout" button.
bugs.impact: Minimal. The error stays for 30 seconds, and then the page refreshes, posting the expected logout page.

bugs.title: SSL client authentication should ignore invalid signed Certificate Verify message when PCM is set to 'request'.
bugs.symptoms: When peer certificate mode (PCM) is set to request, and the BIG-IP system client-ssl asks for the client certificate, handshake might fail if the client sends an invalid signed Certificate Verify message.
bugs.conditions: When SSL client certificate mode is request, and the client sends an invalid signed Certificate Verify message to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The handshake does not ignore the invalid signed certificate verify message, and handshake might fail. SSL client authentication should ignore invalid signed Certificate Verify message when PCM is set to 'request'. Regardless of whether the Certificate and Certificate Verify message is valid, the handshake should ignore the Certificate Verify signature error and let the handshake continue.
bugs.fix: When peer certificate mode (PCM) is set to request, and the BIG-IP system client-ssl asks for the client certificate, the handshake now ignores the Certificate Verify signature error and lets the handshake continue. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Configuration fails to load if DNS Express Zone name contains an underscore
bugs.symptoms: A configuration with a DNS Express Zone with an underscore in the name does not load, even though the gtm global-settings general domain-name-check is set to any of allow-underscore, svn-compatible, or none.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration setting gtm global-settings general domain-name-check is set to any of allow-underscore, svn-compatible, or none. -- DNS Express Zone exists with an underscore in the name.
bugs.impact: Cannot load the LTM configuration when restarting BIG-IP system when DNS Express Zones that have an underscore character in the name.
bugs.workaround: Force the GTM configuration to load by sequentially running the following commands: tmsh load sys config gtm-only. tmsh load sys config.
bugs.fix: All FQDNs may now contain underscore character. The BIG-IP system now correctly load configurations that contain DNS Express Zones with underscores in the name.

bugs.title: HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect in a non-HTTP iRule event can cause the next pipelined request to fail.
bugs.symptoms: An iRule that calls HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect in a non-HTTP iRule event can cause the TMM to core on the next pipelined request.
bugs.conditions: HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect used in a non-HTTP iRule event. A pipelined request follows the request that triggers the iRule response.
bugs.impact: TMM core.
bugs.workaround: Add the close header to the HTTP::response, and the connection will be automatically closed.
bugs.fix: The TMM will no longer core due to not being able to handle the next pipelined request after a HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect is used in a non-HTTP iRule event.
