bugs.title: Cannot enable MPTCP on some profiles in GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Version 12.1 Cannot enable MPTCP on some profiles in GUI. Get error message: 01070734:3: Configuration error: In profile /Common/proxy-client to enable MPTCP, Hardware SYN Cookie must be disabled.
bugs.conditions: Version 12.1 Enabling MPTCP on some profiles in GUI.
bugs.impact: Version 12.1 Cannot enable MPTCP.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to enable MPTCP on some profiles.
bugs.fix: Eliminate validation: it is reasonable to have MPTCP function until entering syncookie mode.

bugs.title: iOS Citrix Receiver web interface mode cannot launch the apps
bugs.symptoms: When a user clicks an app, a window displays with this message: "Cannot start the requested App. Select More info for further details."
bugs.conditions: An iOS Citrix Receiver in Web interface connection type and a BIG-IP system in Web interface configuration.
bugs.impact: Customer cannot launch app.
bugs.workaround: 1. In the Citrix Receiver, you can use the native GUI with Access-Gateway Enterprise edition type with this URI: https://<BIG-IP system virtual server FQDN>/ 2. Define an LTM data-group with FQDN set to /config/<storename>/pnagent/config.xml
bugs.fix: LaunchICA get request to be passed through VDI.

bugs.title: Epsec version rolls back to previous version on a reboot
bugs.symptoms: If administrator has installed multiple EPSEC packages, after a reboot the EPSEC version rolls back to the previously installed version.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system needs to be rebooted for this issue to be seen, and multiple EPSEC packages must have been installed on the system before the reboot.
bugs.impact: OPSWAT version rolls back without prompting or logging. This might open up the end-point security issues that are supposed to be fixed by the latest installed OPSWAT package.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to upload a dummy file in Sandbox. 1. Go to Access Policy :: Hosted Content :: Manage Files. 2. Upload any dummy file, even a 0 byte file. Change the security level to 'session'. After this change, even if you reboot or shutdown-restart, the EPSEC version does not revert.
bugs.fix: The most recently installed EPSEC version now remains configured, and does not roll back after reboot or shutdown-restart.

bugs.title: BD memory leak
bugs.symptoms: BD memory increases. May reach a kernel 'OOM killer' scenario.
bugs.conditions: Usually a policy with missing content profiles (XML, etc.) on a post request that causes the POST to be parsed incorrectly and issue many parameter violations.
bugs.impact: High memory consumption on the system, swap memory usage, potential crashes.
bugs.workaround: Apply the correct content profiles. Note: Valid requests typically do not have that many parameters in them. If you have requests that do, apply the 'apply value signature' on those big POSTs.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a memory leak in the Enforcer.

bugs.title: Unable to query admin IP via SNMP on VCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: The admin IP address is not returned via ipAdEntAddr.
bugs.conditions: Query admin IP via SNMP on VCMP guest via ipAdEntAddr.
bugs.impact: Unable to obtain admin IP address via SNMP for VCMP guests.
bugs.fix: ipAdEntAddr will now return the admin IP address on a VCMP guest.

bugs.title: Edge client shows "Invalid Cookies" message on third party IdP sites
bugs.symptoms: While authenticating with a third party IdP site, the site may show a message indicating that the cookie sent from client was invalid.
bugs.conditions: All of the following conditions should be met. - User connects using Edge Client, disconnects and then attempts to connect again. - APM is using SAML authentication with a third party IdP - IdP uses multiple cookies to identify user session
bugs.impact: Edge Client is redirected to IdP site and the site displays a message indicating that the cookie was invalid or that there was a problem with the cookie. User is not prompted for authentication credentials on the IdP.
bugs.workaround: Restart Edge Client before connecting again.

bugs.title: Route pool configuration may cause TMM to produce a core file
bugs.symptoms: TMM might produce a core file and take the action defined in configuration.
bugs.conditions: Client-side route pool configuration that configures a route pool to route back and has auto lasthop disabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using any route at client side (using auto lasthop or lasthop pool).
bugs.fix: The tmm crash caused by the route pool configuration is fixed.

bugs.title: Unable to create a new document with SharePoint 2010
bugs.symptoms: VPN users are unable to create a new document with SharePoint 2010 An error is given: "The Internet address https://ip:port/shared documents/forms/template.dotx" is not valid
bugs.conditions: Create a new document using the"New Document button".
bugs.impact: User cannot create a new document with SharePoint 2010.
bugs.fix: You can create a new document with Microsoft SharePoint 2010.

bugs.title: Interface bfd session does not appear in configuration file or in show running-config
bugs.symptoms: When a Bi-Directional Forwarding Detection (BFD) session is configured for an interface, the bfd session command does not appear in the show running config or in the configuration file. However, running show bfd session command shows that a session is configured.
bugs.conditions: Interface bfd session between two nodes.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine whether a bfd session is configured. Further, because it is not save in the configuration file, the bfd session configuration is lost when the system restarts the protocol.

bugs.title: Unable to sync events from SharePoint 2010 to local Outlook calendar
bugs.symptoms: Unable to sync events from SharePoint 2010 to local Outlook calendar.
bugs.conditions: Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a portal resource for SharePoint 2010 and assign it to webtop 2. Open VS and go to the SharePoint 2010 3. Create a calendar event 4. Sync the event to your local Outlook calendar Actual Results: Event is not synced to local Outlook calendar
bugs.impact: User unable sync events from SharePoint 2010 to local Outlook calendar.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: TMM crash when executing route lookup in tmsh for multicast destination
bugs.symptoms: Running 'tmsh show net route lookup 224.0.0.1' results in TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: Running the following command: tmsh show net route lookup 224.0.0.1
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than avoiding avoid route lookups of multicast destinations from tmsh. It should be possible to use 'ip route show' instead. tmsh still should work for unicast routes.
bugs.fix: Route lookup no longer results in a tmm crash.

bugs.title: Intermittent 'zero millivolt' reading from FND-850 PSU
bugs.symptoms: In rare instances, certain BIG-IP platforms may erroneously generate power supply error messages that indicate zero milli-voltage. Specific symptoms include: - SNMP alert 'BIG-IPSystemCheckAlertMilliVoltageLow' detected. - Front panel Alarm LED is blinking amber. - Errors such as the following are logged: emerg system_check[<#>]: 010d0017:0: Power supply #<x> meas. main outpu: milli-voltage (0) is too low. [where <x> is the power supply location (either 1 or 2)] - Errors such as the following may also be logged: -- err chmand[<#>]: 012a0003:3: Sensor read fault for Power supply #<x> meas. main outpu : File sensor/LopSensSvc.cpp Line 1453. -- notice chmand[<#>]: 012a0005:5: reinitialize tmstat sensors (num sensors:<#>). -- notice chmand[<#>]: 012a0005:5: reinitialize tmstat sensors (num sensors:<#>). Note that this condition may affect either PSU 1 or PSU 2.
bugs.conditions: This may occur intermittently on BIG-IP 10000-/12000-series appliances (including 10000s/10200v, 10050s/10250v, 10055/10255, 10350v and 12250v models) with FND850 model DC power supplies.
bugs.impact: There is no impact; these error messages are benign.
bugs.fix: Resolved intermittent erroneous "zero millivolt" reading from FND-850 PSU on BIG-IP 10000-/12000-series appliances.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes do not support session user-disable
bugs.symptoms: FQDN nodes do not support session user-disable.
bugs.conditions: Configure a monitor with recv-disable string, and set node to session user-disabled. Monitor does not mark the node down for draining persistent connections.
bugs.impact: Unable to use session drain.
bugs.fix: FQDN nodes now support session user-disable

bugs.title: Modification to parent clientssl CKC does not consistently reflected in the child clientssl profile
bugs.symptoms: If cert is modified in the parent client-ssl profile, and inherit-certkeychain is set TRUE in the child client-ssl profile, the system adds the parent CKC(cert-key-chain) to the client-ssl profile instead of changing it to the same value as the parents.
bugs.conditions: 1. Set inherit-certkeychain to TRUE in the child client-ssl profile. 2. Change the Parent CKC value.
bugs.impact: Parent cert-key-chain is added to the client-ssl profile instead of changing it to the same value as the parent's value. Certificate validation can fail if it is not in the chain.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Manually fix the CKC of child client-ssl profile. -- Set 'inherit-certkeychain = False' in the client-ssl profile.

bugs.title: The SNMP daemon might lock up and fail to respond to SNMP requests.
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP daemon might lock up and fail to respond to SNMP requests.
bugs.conditions: If the SNMP configuration on the BIG-IP changes and the SNMP daemon restarts. This is a timing issue that might appear intermittently.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system stops responding to SNMP requests. You then cannot monitor the BIG-IP system via SNMP.
bugs.workaround: If the SNMP daemon is locked up, restart it by issuing the following command: bigstart restart snmpd.
bugs.fix: The SNMP daemon no longer locks up and become unresponsive when it is restarted.

bugs.title: TMM can core due to memory corruption when using SPDY profile.
bugs.symptoms: TMM corefiles containing memory corruption within 112-byte memory cache.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server using a SPDY profile encounters an internal error while processing a SPDY packet.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release contains a fix that prevents a double free on error within the SPDY component.

bugs.title: Issue with assignment of non-string value to Form.action in javascript.
bugs.symptoms: Exception in javascript code.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to assign non-string value to a Form.action in javascript code.
bugs.impact: Web application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed for non string value types.

bugs.title: TMM core on HTTP response with steering action.
bugs.symptoms: TMM core on HTTP response with steering action.
bugs.conditions: HTTP profile is not attached to a PEM virtual server receiving the HTTP response. In this case, on receiving a connection request from the client, the BIG-IP system establishes server-side connection without waiting for the HTTP request from the client. Meanwhile, a steering policy got installed. The server responds with an HTTP request timeout message.
bugs.impact: TMM cores trying to steer the existing connection. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To avoid this issue, attach an HTTP profile to the PEM virtual server.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores on HTTP response with steering action.

bugs.title: BGP may advertise default route with bad parameters
bugs.symptoms: If a BGP neighbor is configured with 'default originate,' the nexthop advertised for the default route may be incorrect.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing using BGP configured, BGP neighbor configured with 'default originate'.
bugs.impact: The default route advertised via BGP is not acceptable to peers until the BGP session is cleared.
bugs.workaround: In imish, run the command: clear ip bgp <affected neighbor address>.
bugs.fix: BGP now always includes the correct nexthop on default route advertisements.

bugs.title: Differing certificate/key after successful config-sync
bugs.symptoms: 1) If you change a client-ssl profile to a different certificate/key, delete the original certificate/key, create a new certificate/key with the same name as the original one, associate the new certificate/key with the original client-ssl profile, then do a config-sync, the peer system(s)' FIPS chip will retain a copy of the original key. 2) If you change a client-ssl profile to a different certificate/key, delete the original certificate/key, create a new certificate/key with a different name from the original one, associate the new certificate/key with the original client-ssl profile, then do a config-sync, the peer's client-ssl profile will still use the original certificate/key instead of the new one.
bugs.conditions: 1) High Availability failover systems with FIPS configured with Manual Sync. 2) High Availability failover systems configured with Manual Sync.
bugs.impact: 1) An abandoned FIPS key is left behind. 2) The systems claim to be synced, but one system's client-ssl profile uses one certificate/key pair, while the other system(s)' same client-ssl profile uses a different certificate/key pair.
bugs.workaround: 1) Workaround #1: Run an extra config-sync before the second change of the client-ssl profile. Workaround #2: Delete the FIPS key by-handle on the peer system(s). 2) Workaround #1: Run an extra config-sync before the second change of the client-ssl profile. Workaround #2: Manually update the client-ssl profile then delete the old certificate/key on the peer system(s).
bugs.fix: Systems now have the same certificate/key after successful config-sync of High Availability configurations.

bugs.title: Use of OneConnect may result in stalled flows
bugs.symptoms: Stuck serverside flows that do not expire
bugs.conditions: Serverside flow expires while clientside is closing while OneConnect is being used.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory usage, tmm can crash.
bugs.workaround: Disable OneConnect. This can also be mitigated by ensuring the server-side idle timeout is not set lower than the client profile's fin-wait timeout while using OneConnect.

bugs.title: Manual upgrade of Edge Client fails in some cases on Windows
bugs.symptoms: Manual upgrade of BIG-IP Edge Client for Windows fails and this message displays "Newer version of this product is already installed."
bugs.conditions: Edge Client version 11.2.0. Version 12.0 is installed. User tries to upgrade Edge Client by running a newer installer package of Edge Client.
bugs.impact: Edge Client cannot be upgraded.
bugs.workaround: Uninstall and reinstall Edge Client or use the installer service component for automatic update of Edge Client.
bugs.fix: Fixed installer package.

bugs.title: AJAX File uploads don't work in IE (import policy doesn't work)
bugs.symptoms: You cannot import policies either XML or binary through the webui, but tmsh import works. When using the GUI you select the file and it gets stuck on "verifying". The issue occurs only in when uploading using Internet Explorer.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to upload a policy using Internet Explorer.
bugs.impact: You cannot import any policy from the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Other browsers such as FireFox or Chrome work.
bugs.fix: You can now import policies (XML and binary) using the Configuration utility in addition to the command line.

bugs.title: No connectivity inside enterprise network for "Always Connected" client if Network Location Awareness is enabled
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client loses all connectivity and an option to establish VPN is not available.
bugs.conditions: All of the following conditions must apply. 1) Edge Client is installed in "Always Connected" mode. 2) The Connectivity profile on server has location DNS list entries. 3) One of the DNS locations matches the DNS suffix set on the local network adapter.
bugs.impact: Client shows "LAN Detected" in the UI and does not try to connect to VPN. All traffic to and from the user's machine is blocked.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Edge Client now ignores DNS location settings in Always Connected mode and establishes VPN even inside enterprise networks.

bugs.title: If the user cancels a connection attempt, there may be a delay in estabilshing the next connection.
bugs.symptoms: Clicking on connect button does not trigger start of VPN connection immediately.
bugs.conditions: User cancelled previous connection attempt
bugs.impact: User must wait for ten seconds before attempting to reconnect.
bugs.fix: Fixed code to trigger VPN connection immediately even when user clicked cancel before.

bugs.title: OneConnect does not work when WEBSSO is enabled/configured.
bugs.symptoms: OneConnect is a feature that reuses server-side connections. When WEBSSO is enabled, it always creates a new server-side connection, and doesn't reuse pooled connections.
bugs.conditions: WEBSSO and OneConnect.
bugs.impact: Idle serverside connections that should be eligible for reuse by the virtual server are not used. This might lead to build-up of idle serverside connections, and may result in unexpected 'Inet port exhaustion' errors.
bugs.fix: OneConnect now works when WEBSSO is enabled/configured, so that the system reuses the pooled server side connections.

bugs.title: Upgrade from before 11.4.x fails due to Logging Profile Data Inconsistency
bugs.symptoms: In some rare cases a Logging Profile which had remote logging configuration and was then updated to only log locally may be left with the old remote logging data attached. This leads to an invalid state during upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from before 11.2.x, to 11.5.x, 11.6.x, or 12.0.0 through 12.1.1 A Logging Profile with the following attributes: 1) Anomaly logging enabled 2) Remote logging disabled 3) A row exists in LOGPROF_REMOTE_CONFIG for the Logging Profile
bugs.impact: All ASM configuration will not be upgraded and will be lost.
bugs.workaround: Make a spurious change to the problematic Logging Profile and save. This will remove the data inconsistency.
bugs.fix: Upgrade no longer fails due to the data inconsistency.

bugs.title: CMP disabled flows are not properly mirrored
bugs.symptoms: A client connection to a virtual server configured for 'cmp-enabled no' and 'mirror enabled' will be dropped if the standby unit is promoted to active.
bugs.conditions: The virtual server is configured for 'cmp-enabled no' and 'mirror enabled' on multiple BIG-IP appliances peered in a high availability configuration.
bugs.impact: Mirroring does not work as expected on BIG-IP appliances. Note: CMP is required on VIPRION chassis, so this expectation applies only to appliances.
bugs.workaround: Do not disable CMP on virtual servers that are mirrored.
bugs.fix: The system now supports mirroring connections between BIG-IP appliances in a high availability configuration on CMP-disabled virtual servers. Note: If CMP is disabled, hardware syn cookie must also be disabled for virtual servers to mirror connections. This is expected behavior.

bugs.title: Signatures cannot be updated after Signature Systems have become corrupted in database
bugs.symptoms: Signatures cannot be updated after signature systems have become corrupted in the configuration database.
bugs.conditions: Signature systems are corrupted in configuration database. This can occur after upgrading to v11.6.0, v11.6.1, or v12.0.0.
bugs.impact: Signatures cannot be updated.
bugs.workaround: Delete signature systems with an ID greater than 38, and re-add them by performing a signature update. You can delete these signature systems by running the following command: mysql -u root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e "DELETE FROM PLC.NEGSIG_SYSTEMS WHERE system_group = ''"
bugs.fix: Signature System data corruption is corrected upon upgrade, and Signatures can be subsequently upgraded.

bugs.title: IPsec tunnels fail when connection.vlankeyed db variable is disabled
bugs.symptoms: When connection.vlankeyed db variable is disabled, if the data traffic coming out of IKEv1 tunnels that needs to be secured using IKEv2 tunnels lands on tmm's other than tmm0, it will be dropped. The system establishes the IKEv2 tunnel but the data traffic will not be secured.
bugs.conditions: This issue is seen when the interesting data traffic lands on tmm's other than tmm0. The reason for this issue is due to incorrectly creating a flow on another TMM that is the owner of the outbound SA (IKEv2 tunnel).
bugs.impact: The system drops the data traffic to be secured using IPsec and connections fail.
bugs.workaround: Disable the cmp in the virtual server configuration.
bugs.fix: Flow creation at the TMM that owns the outbound SA for the IKEv2 tunnel is properly handled. TMM can handle the inner traffic from IKEv1 tunnel and secure it over another IKEv2 tunnel.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ ASM remote logger: Requests are not be logged.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IQ ASM does not log requests for the first remote logger configured on the system.
bugs.conditions: No remote logger has been previously configured for ASM.
bugs.impact: No requests are sent to remote logger that was just configured.
bugs.workaround: This issue resolves itself after a few seconds when the remote destination is responsive.
bugs.fix: An issue with requests not being logged after configuring a new remote logger for BIG-IQ ASM has been fixed.

bugs.title: Multiple log messages stating 'AdminIp fixed up with dhcp_enabled = false' are printed in /var/log/ltm after upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: /var/log/ltm shows multiple entries with this message: 'AdminIp fixed up with dhcp_enabled = false'.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading running BIG-IP with a newer version.
bugs.impact: This is a benign informational message about internal DHCP variable handling. The /var/log/ltm might contain repeated messages, but there is no functional impact.
bugs.fix: Multiple log messages stating 'AdminIp fixed up with dhcp_enabled = false' are no longer printed in /var/log/ltm after upgrade.

bugs.title: LTM Policy resets connection when removing non-existant HTTP header
bugs.symptoms: Customer might notice that certain HTTP requests would be prematurely terminated without seeing a response.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when an LTM Policy is defined to remove an HTTP header from a request or response, but the request or response does not contain the specified header.
bugs.impact: The connection gets reset, client does not see response.
bugs.workaround: As a possible mitigation, if the HTTP header to be removed has narrowly-defined expected value, it may be possible to add a condition that effectively tests for the existence of a header. For example, instead of unconditionally removing the Server: header from a response, a condition could be added to check whether the Server: header contains "Apache", or even if it contains the letter 'a', or even any letter or number.

bugs.title: No Session Variables displayed when click on "View Session Variables" link in APM "All Sessions" reports with reduced zeros in Session ID
bugs.symptoms: No Session Variables displayed when click on "View Session Variables" link in APM "All Sessions" reports
bugs.conditions: When Session ID has 1 or more leading zero
bugs.impact: Empty in the APM Session Variable report
bugs.workaround: Run "Session Variables" report. When enter session ID, prepend 0s if the session ID has less 8 chars. The total length of session ID is 8 chars.
bugs.fix: Session Variables report shows correctly.

bugs.title: Client OS version not logged in Browser/OS Reports for iOS client devices
bugs.symptoms: When an iOS device is used to login with APM, the client OS version is not logged and is not correctly reported in the Browser/OS Report.
bugs.conditions: Client device must run iOS.
bugs.impact: Devices running different versions of iOS are not differentiated in the Browser/OS Report.

bugs.title: PMTU discovery from the management interface does not work
bugs.symptoms: Network connectivity issues to the BIG-IP management interface. The management interface 'auto lasthop' feature (not to be confused with the auto lasthop setting on a virtual server) allows the BIG-IP to route responses to packets received on the management interface back to the MAC address of the layer-3 device that sent them, removing the need for static management-routes to be configured on the BIG-IP for communication beyond the management subnet. The operation of the lasthop module interferes with the management interface's ability to dynamically learn Path MTU (PTMU) through ICMP unreachable messages.
bugs.conditions: The MTU on one section of the network path between a client device and BIG-IP management interface is lower than the BIG-IP management interface's configured MTU (for example, part of the path passes through a tunnel), and an intermediary router is sending 'ICMP unreachable, fragmentation required' packets back to the BIG-IP to instruct it to send smaller datagrams.
bugs.impact: Unable to complete a TLS handshake to the management interface IP, or other similar operations that require large frames.
bugs.workaround: BIG-IP management interface auto lasthop functionality can be disabled to allow the interface to function normally. For more information see K52592992: Overview of the Auto Last Hop feature on the management interface, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K52592992.

bugs.title: Failed alerts on Internet Explorer
bugs.symptoms: Sending page data in alerts can cause alerts to fail.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions: -- 'attach HTML to alerts' enabled. -- Alert is sent from a large HTML page.
bugs.impact: Missed alerts
bugs.workaround: Disable 'attach HTML to alerts'.
bugs.fix: If page data overwhelms alert sending, only partial page data is sent, so the alert now completes as expected.

bugs.title: RAT detection failure
bugs.symptoms: When flash cookies are disabled, RAT detection fails.
bugs.conditions: Flash cookies disabled.
bugs.impact: RAT attacks are not reported to the alert server.
bugs.workaround: Enable flash cookie.
bugs.fix: RAT detection now works with regular cookies.

bugs.title: Only first entry in 'Mandatory Words' list is effective
bugs.symptoms: Despite adding two or more 'Mandatory Words' items, alerts are only sent on the first item.
bugs.conditions: Multiple 'Mandatory Words' items are configured. One of the items (not the top item) is injected into page.
bugs.impact: No 'Mandatory Words' alert sent (False negative).
bugs.fix: The entire 'Mandatory Words' list is now checked.

bugs.title: Error: Egress CoS queue packet drop counted against both Drops In and Drops Out statistics.
bugs.symptoms: Class of Service Queues (cosq) egress drop statistics are counted against both Drops In and Drops Out interface statistics.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for all cosq drops in response to excess egress traffic and MMU egress congestion.
bugs.impact: Any CoS queue egress drop is also counted against ingress drop stats, which could be interpreted incorrectly as doubled total drop stats.
bugs.fix: The Drops In interface statistics no longer includes Class of Service Queues (cosq) egress drop counts, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Kernel panics during boot when RAM spans multiple NUMA nodes.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) crashes in the kernel during early boot.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: * VE is running on Hyper-V. * VE RAM is configured in a such a way that it spans multiple NUMA nodes.
bugs.impact: Kernel panic during boot.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The kernel now properly aligns memory on multiple NUMA nodes, so there is no kernel panic during boot.

bugs.title: Datagroups have a large impact on configuration save times
bugs.symptoms: Configurations with a high number of datagroups result in an unexpected save time. When configuration contains 1000+ datagroups, then the save time is near 60 seconds.
bugs.conditions: This issues occurs when: - Configuration contains a significant number of datagroups - Running v11.0.0+
bugs.impact: Increased save time

bugs.title: Database logging truncates log values greater than 1024
bugs.symptoms: The Logging agent truncates log values greater than 1024. If the log value size is greater than 4060, the field is empty or null.
bugs.conditions: Logging into local database with log values (such as session variables) greater than 1024. If this size is too high (greater than 4060), the field displays as empty or null in reports.
bugs.impact: The reporting UI displays null or empty fields when the logged value is too large in size, such as a huge session variable.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: This release handles large single log values.

bugs.title: Configurable maximum message size limit for restjavad
bugs.symptoms: if the client issues a requests to iControl REST that results in a large amount of data (approx 200 MB), restjavad goes into an out-of-memory condition when attempting to serialize the response prior to returning it to the client.
bugs.conditions: A message is received by restjavad that is larger than the total free heap space. The most common cause is that the system sends a board query to icrd, which returns a very large response (approx 200 MB).
bugs.impact: restjavad becomes unresponsive until it is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: This fix exposes the maximum message size limit and allows a Network operator to change it by posting to a new configuration worker. An example is included below. The actual value varies by installation - load, average message size etc. Set it too low and the clients will receive 5xx errors even though there is sufficient memory. Set it too high and dangerously-large messages do not get dropped and might cause an out-of-memory exception. 5 MB is a recommended starting value. An example of setting the maximum message body size to 5kB (5000 bytes) on a machine called 'green.' The password needs to be changed appropriately. curl -s -k -u admin:PASSWORD -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H 'Connection: keep-alive' -X PUT "https://green/mgmt/shared/server/messaging/settings/8100" -d '{"maxMessageBodySize": "5000" }'.

bugs.title: VPN Server Module generates repeated Error Log "iface eth0 "... every 2 secs
bugs.symptoms: Chatty log messages seen in svpn.log file
bugs.conditions: Establish tunnel server and check svpn.log file (VPN server module) to see verbose logs
bugs.impact: Verbose logging having a general CPU and disk write impact.
bugs.fix: VPN Server Module doesn't generate repeated Error Log "iface eth0 (4)" every 2 secs

bugs.title: Deployment failed: Failed submitting iControl REST transaction
bugs.symptoms: When deploying an access control policy to a sync group, you notice the following error: Deployment failed: Failed submitting iControl REST transaction 1445978291443908: remoteSender:ip_address
bugs.conditions: This can happen on policy sync with a large number of ACLs.
bugs.impact: The system will function properly, but some transactions may take longer than expected. BIG-IQ deployment of APM access control lists is one known case to fail due to timeouts.
bugs.fix: The audit log contains every database modification request message sent to mcpd. Certain messages once took an unexpectedly long time to render, which has been fixed.

bugs.title: Unexpected handling of TCP timestamps under syncookie protection.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system experiences intermittent packet drops. Despite being negotiated during TCP handshake, the BIG-IP system fails to present timestamp option in subsequent segments. The BIG-IP system calculates invalid round trip time immediately after handshake, which might result in delayed retransmissions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - Virtual server configured with a TCP profile with timestamps enabled. - The syncookie mode has been activated. - Clients that support timestamps.
bugs.impact: Connection might be reset by remote TCP stack (e.g., NetBSD and FreeBSD), which requires timestamps to be maintained once negotiated. Retransmission timeout (RTO) value may be skewed. Segments that are subject to RTO might take up to 64 segments to retransmit.
bugs.workaround: Choose or create a TCP profile that has timestamps disabled.
bugs.fix: TCP Timestamps are now maintained on all negotiated flows.

bugs.title: CPM might crash when TCLRULE_HTTP_RESPONSE is triggered.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash if CONNFLOW_FLAG_L7_POLICY is not set in the connection flow flags, but the system still tries to call Centralized Policy Matching (CPM).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when TCLRULE_HTTP_RESPONSE is triggered from the server-side, if the server-side does not process the policy, and the connection flow flags do not have CONNFLOW_FLAG_L7_POLICY set.
bugs.impact: TMM/(CPM Module) might crash.
bugs.fix: The system now adds the flag check of CONNFLOW_FLAG_L7_POLICY if it is not already set, so there is no crash in TMM or Centralized Policy Matching (CPM).

bugs.title: Persist lookup across services might fail to return a matching record when multiple records exist.
bugs.symptoms: Persist lookup across services might fail to return a matching record when multiple records exist.
bugs.conditions: Persistence profile with 'match-across-services' enabled, and the configuration contains multiple records that correspond to the same pool.
bugs.impact: Connection routed to unexpected pool member.
bugs.fix: The operation now continues searching persistence records when 'match-across-services' is enabled until the operation finds a record that corresponds to the same pool.

bugs.title: TMM may crash with a SIGFPE panic if an AFM DOS profile is configured with Behavioral Analysis enabled
bugs.symptoms: If an AFM DoS profile with Behavioral Analysis enabled is applied to a virtual server configured for state mirroring, TMM may crash on the secondary device with a SIGFPE panic. The system may produce a panic message in /var/log/tmm* similar to the following: panic: ./local/net/packet.h:505: Assertion "l3hdr set" failed.
bugs.impact: TMM crash: Degraded HA. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: AFM is provisioned and an AFM profile with 'Behavioral Analysis' enabled is configured on a virtual server, and that virtual server is configured for mirroring.
bugs.workaround: Enabling the 'Behavioral Analysis' feature in an AFM profile is not completely functional at this time. Please do not enable the feature.

bugs.title: MCPD core with access policy macro during config sync in HA configuration
bugs.symptoms: In high availability config sync, the destination mcpd might crash if the user does the following steps: 1. Manually edit bigip.conf file at source to remove an access policy item (my-ap-1_mac_mymac1) that calls a macro, from the original access policy (my-ap-1) to another access policy (my-ap-2); 2. Load the modified config into running config; 3. Delete the original access policy (my-ap-1) before manually starting the config sync. The modified source configuration is sent to the destination during the manual incremental config sync, resulting in destination mcpd logging an error message: err mcpd[5441]: 01020036:3: The requested access_policy_name (/Common/my-ap-1) was not found. Immediately following the error message, the destination mcpd will crash and generate a core file.
bugs.conditions: Config sync is manual incremental, and the user manually edits /config/bigip.conf to modify the source configuration such that an access policy item with a macrocall is removed from the original access policy to another access policy, and then the original access policy is deleted, all before the manual config sync is started.
bugs.impact: During config sync, the destination BIG-IP system's mcpd crashes and restarts.
bugs.workaround: After removing the access policy item with a macrocall from the original access policy to another access policy and loading into the source running the configuration, do not delete the original access policy. Instead, start the config sync right away. After this first config sync is successful, delete the original access policy at the source, and then start the second config sync to finish the operation.
bugs.fix: MCPD no longer cores with access policy macro during config sync in high availability configuration.

bugs.title: tmm eventually crashes when Classification profile is configured on the virtual server
bugs.symptoms: tmm eventually crashes when Classification profile is configured on the virtual server
bugs.conditions: -- Classification profile configured on the virtual server. -- Many ssl/ftp/rtp/sip flows processed by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: remove Classification profile from the virtual
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes when Classification profile is configured on the virtual server

bugs.title: Small Client EDNS0 Limits can Sometimes Truncate DNSSEC or iRule DNS Packets
bugs.symptoms: A resolver sending a query with a small EDNS0 UDP buffer limit can lead to packet truncation. These response packets are flagged as truncated in the header, but the OPT record might be cut/missing leading some resolvers to consider the packet malformed.
bugs.conditions: Primarily via dynamic settings such as iRules on DNS_RESPONSE events adding new records, or DNSSEC record signing with responses over UDP.
bugs.impact: Some resolvers regard OPT-less truncated packets as malformed and cease follow-up requests via TCP or a larger EDNS0 UDP limit.
bugs.fix: Truncated DNSSEC or iRule DNS packets are RFC-compliant.

bugs.title: TMM might crash on failed SSL handshake
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake failures may crash in ssl_verify().
bugs.conditions: Certain types of failed SSL handshakes in versions 11.5.0 through 11.5.4.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Modifying serverssl cipher string to exclude ECDHE_RSA and ECDHE_ECDSA might help prevent the crash.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a TMM crash that might be encountered during the SSL handshake.

bugs.title: Multiple HTTP Host headers may circumvent SWG URL Filter Policy
bugs.symptoms: If an HTTP request contains multiple Host headers, the first one will be used to determine the destination IP when using an SWG Explicit Proxy. The last Host header is used by SWG to make a URL Filter policy decision. If the last Host header is allowed by the applied URL Filter policy, the request will be allowed. The request although will be send to the destination specified by the first Host header is blocked by the URL Filter policy, thereby circumventing the URL Filter Policy applied to the request.
bugs.conditions: An HTTP request is made to the an APM Explicit Proxy with 2 or more HTTP Host headers.
bugs.impact: A may send custom HTTP requests with multiple HTTP Host headers to gain access to a site that is being blocked by the applied URL Filter policy.

bugs.title: Profile Stats Not Updated After Standby Upgrade Followed By Failover
bugs.symptoms: 1. The current active sessions, current pending sessions, and current established sessions counts shown in commands 'tmsh show /apm profile access' and 'tmctl profile_access_stat' become zero after failover. 2. The system posts an error message to /var/log/apm: 01490559:3: 00000000: Access stats encountered error: SessionDB operation failed (ERR_NOT_FOUND).
bugs.conditions: This issue happens when the following conditions are met: 1. The HA configuration is running a release prior to 11.5.3 HF2, 11.6.0 HF6, or 12.0.0. 2. A standby unit is upgraded to version 11.5.3 HF2, 11.6.0 HF6, or 12.0.0. 3. Failover is triggered.
bugs.impact: The current active sessions, current pending sessions, and current established sessions counts of profile access stats remain zero after failover.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade all devices in the HA configuration to the same release and reboot them simultaneously.
bugs.fix: The current active sessions, current pending sessions, and current established sessions counts of profile access stats now report correctly after failover.

bugs.title: ASM REST: lastUpdateMicros is not updated when changing a Custom Signature
bugs.symptoms: The lastUpdateMicros field is meant to be updated if a user changes a custom signature, but it is not.
bugs.conditions: REST client is used to look at/filter the signatures collection (/mgmt/tm/asm/sigantures)
bugs.impact: Checking for updated signatures does not return the expected result.
bugs.fix: REST: The lastUpdateMicros field is now correctly updated after updating a user defined signature.

bugs.title: VIPRION B2100: Increase egress traffic burst tolerance for dual CoS queue configuration
bugs.symptoms: There is a high drop counts when running tmsh show net interface, and running tmctl -a drop_reason shows that a large number of drops are due to counters.rx_cosq_drop Smaller buffering alpha values are configured for egress buffering to allow an 8 HW CoS queue feature to correctly implement weight based egress dropping. This results in busy ports dropping more aggressively, although allowing more fair buffering amongst multiple active ports.
bugs.conditions: Higher traffic rates, which stress switch MMU buffering resources, might result in egress CoS queue drop on busy ports. This affects the BIG-IP 5000- and 7000 series platforms, and VIPRION B2100, B2150, and PB200 blades.
bugs.impact: This results in busy ports dropping more aggressively. Note that using smaller values allows more fair buffering amongst multiple active ports, whereas higher values allow better burst absorption but less fair buffering.
bugs.fix: This release uses a larger alpha value for better burst absorption when the 8 hardware CoS queue feature is not enabled.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Removing a Signature Set From One Security Policy Removes It From All Security Policies.
bugs.symptoms: When using ASM REST to remove a signature set association from a policy (DELETE), the set is removed from all policies in the system.
bugs.conditions: ASM REST is used to remove a signature set association from a policy. DELETE /mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/signature-sets/<ID>
bugs.impact: All policies will lose their association to that signature set. This may leave some policies not enforcing all the Attack Signatures that they are expected to.
bugs.workaround: A DELETE can be issued to the collection endpoint: /mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/signature-sets utilizing the $filter parameter to delete only the desired sets. Ex. DELETE /mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/signature-sets?$filter=id eq '<ID>'
bugs.fix: When using ASM REST to remove a signature set association from a policy (DELETE), the signature set association is removed only from the desired policy and not from all policies in the system.

bugs.title: Disk Serial number reported with incorrect formatting
bugs.symptoms: Depending on what operating system, and if the user is a normal user or an admin user - the serial number for the hard disk may be reported in the incorrect format
bugs.conditions: Customer is recording HDD.sn User changes between admin user and non-admin user
bugs.impact: SN may be reported byte swapped
bugs.workaround: Only record hdd.sn from one type of user (Admin/non-Admin)

bugs.title: Changing monitoring configuration stops health checks for FQDN nodes.
bugs.symptoms: When changing the monitoring configuration, the health checks never resume for FQDN node types.
bugs.conditions: Create a custom monitor, apply it to an FQDN node type. Change the monitor configuration, and health checks never resume.
bugs.impact: No health checking. (member status remains static as prior to change). - Traffic may be sent to unavailable pool members.
bugs.workaround: Restart bigd to force the change using the following command: bigstart restart bigd

bugs.title: Transactional PEM policies without an HTTP profile on the virtual server do not result in transactional classification.
bugs.symptoms: Transactional HTTP flows will be classified only on the first transaction.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with a PEM profile, classification profile, no HTTP profile, and transactional PEM policy.
bugs.impact: PEM actions that differ between transactions for a flow will not take effect. Instead, the flow adheres to the PEM actions against the first transaction.
bugs.workaround: Add an HTTP profile to the virtual server if transactional flows need to be evaluated for each transaction.

bugs.title: Endpoint Security client components (OPSWAT, EPSEC) may fail to upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Previously, F5 Client components were signed using SHA1 certificate. SHA1 is now considered insecure and Windows will reject components signed using a SHA1 certificate after March 31st 2016. To support this new requirement, F5 has changed the client component signing certificates to utilize a higher security validation algorithm. The result of this change is that clients utilizing client components built prior to these versions: Big-IP 12.0.0HF1 or earlier Big-IP 11.6.0 HF6 or earlier Big-IP 11.5.4 (base release) or earlier cannot Endpoint Security updates build 431 or greater. If you require updated Endpoint Security (OPSWAT / EPSEC) builds greater than 431 you must upgrade to these versions: Big-IP 12.1.0 or later Big-IP 12.0.0HF2 or later Big-IP 11.6.1 or later Big-IP 11.6.0 HF7 Big-IP 11.5.4 HF1 or later
bugs.conditions: Running incompatible BIG-IP version with EPSEC build 431 or later.
bugs.impact: User will see certificate warnings and installation of client component updates may fail. The failure may occur multiple times.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade BIG-IP to the correct version. Use the BIG-IP Web GUI's Software Management :: Antivirus Check Check Updates section to install an EPSEC build prior to 431.
bugs.fix: Updated signing certificate to a sha256 certificate. Client components and EPSEC binaries are now signed using the new, higher security certificate. Please note that upgrade to a HF in which client is signed using updated certificate is needed to install updated EPSEC releases. Please review the information carefully.

bugs.title: tmm may crash in fastl4 tcp virtual server
bugs.symptoms: tmm may crash if receives a fragmented packet in a fastl4 tcp virtual server.
bugs.conditions: fastl4 tcp virtual server fragmented packet arrives
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Enable option "Reassemble IP Fragments" in the fastl4 profile.

bugs.title: CGNAT memory leak when non-TCP/UDP traffic directed at public addresses
bugs.symptoms: When rejecting non-TCP/UDP inbound traffic a small amount of memory is leaked with each packet. Depending on the volume of such traffic this may be a slow or fast leak.
bugs.conditions: CGNAT configured with inbound connections enabled or hairpinning enabled Non-TCP/UDP traffic with a destination in the LSN Pool address space
bugs.impact: TMM might eventually run out of available memory. The aggressive mode sweeper might be triggered, causing connections to be killed. Eventually TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a memory leak that occurred When rejecting non-TCP/UDP inbound traffic.

bugs.title: "Data publisher not found or not implemented" messages in ltm log when running qkview
bugs.symptoms: When running a qkview, there are various "Data publisher not found or not implemented" messages in /var/log/ltm. This is benign and these messages can be safely ignored. The items are related to psu, cooling and chassis info.
bugs.conditions: Always present since the query is always made for these items that aren't available.
bugs.impact: A bit of concern by anybody monitoring /var/log/ltm and seeing these messages during a qkview which shouldn't have discernible impact on a system.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the messages as they are not caused by anything wrong in the system.
bugs.fix: Removed items from qkview, thus eliminating the messages. One still remains if there are various blades in a chassis caused "show sys memory" on the individual blade. A separate bug for this has been filed (bug 567330).

bugs.title: Large configuration files may go missing on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: bigip.conf or other configuration files may go missing on secondary blades once the configuration exceeds a certain size (approximately 8 MB).
bugs.conditions: This is only relevant on chassis.
bugs.impact: If the primary changes, then the configuration is at risk of being lost.
bugs.workaround: touch the relevant configuration file (usually bigip.conf) and the configuration file will reappear.
bugs.fix: bigip.conf or other configuration files would go missing on secondary blades once the configuration exceeded a certain size (approximately 8 MB). This has been fixed.

bugs.title: AD Query fails if cross-domain option is enabled and administrator's credentials are not specified
bugs.symptoms: AD Query fails in cross-domain environment, when AAA AD Server has no administrator credentials configured and user's logon name is different from pre-win2k name
bugs.conditions: - AD Query is configured in an Access Policy. - The administrator's credentials are not specified at AAA AD Server configuration page (that is in use by AD Query). - The domain logon name is different from pre-win2k name.
bugs.impact: AD Query fails
bugs.workaround: The administrator should provide AD administrator credentials at AAA AD Server configuration page.
bugs.fix: AD Query now completes as expected if cross-domain option is enabled and administrator's credentials are not specified.

bugs.title: Reboot is required, but not prompted after F5 Networks components have been uninstalled
bugs.symptoms: Attempt to establish a VPN connection from a Windows 10, Windows 8.1, Windows 7, or Vista desktop fails if F5 Networks components have been removed previously and the desktop was not rebooted. Typically this issue can be identified by these log records: <snip> DIALER, 48, \driverstatechecker.cpp, 10, dump, WAN Miniport (SSTP) DIALER, 48, \driverstatechecker.cpp, 10, dump, WAN Miniport (SSTP) DIALER, 48, \driverstatechecker.cpp, 10, dump, F5 Networks VPN Adapter <--- Two F5 Devices DIALER, 48, \driverstatechecker.cpp, 10, dump, F5 Networks VPN Adapter (7) <--- Two F5 Devices DIALER, 48, \driverstatechecker.cpp, 155, GetVPNDriverRASDeviceName, found device, F5 Networks VPN Adapter <snip> DIALER, 1, \urdialer.cpp, 1573, CURDialer::OnRasCallback(), RAS error (state=RASCS_OpenPort, error=633: The modem (or other connecting device) is already in use or is not configured properly.)
bugs.conditions: Windows desktop. Existing F5 components uninstalled. Reboot was not performed after uninstall.
bugs.impact: End users cannot establish a VPN connection from Windows-based clients.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the affected Windows desktop.
bugs.fix: After F5 Networks components have been uninstalled, the system does not require reboot, and uses the latest installed software-device for VPN, as expected.

bugs.title: HA channel flapping will cause SessionDB memory leak on standby due to unexpired entries
bugs.symptoms: SessionDB memory leak on a standby in the HA pair due to HA channel flapping causing failure of expiry messages.
bugs.conditions: SessionDB in use, HA channel errors
bugs.impact: Slow memory leakage on the standby
bugs.workaround: Alleviate the HA flapping and then restart the standby.

bugs.title: Extremely large number of SessionDB entries may cause HA flapping
bugs.symptoms: With enough SessionDB entries and a small enough high availability (HA) connections, the HA channel can become oversaturated.
bugs.conditions: -- Very large number of SessionDB entries. -- Small/inefficient HA channel.
bugs.impact: Mirroring and other HA-related TMM usage might be disrupted.
bugs.workaround: If this condition is occurring, the HA channel is continually being reset and then overflowing again when the SessionDB table is synced. You can mitigate by temporarily disabling session mirroring: 1. Disable session mirroring: tmsh modify sys db statemirror.mirrorsessions value disable 2. Wait a minute for HA connections to stabilize. 3. Sync the config changes. 4. Reboot the standby device. 5. Re-enable session mirroring: tmsh modify sys db statemirror.mirrorsessions value enable
bugs.fix: Added a new variable 'tmm.sessiondb.ha_mps_limit' to throttle the number of messages that SessionDB sends from the Active to Next Active after an HA state change. Note: Messages from CRUD operations are not throttled. The initial value is 0 for 'no throttling.' If set to a non-zero value N, SessionDB will ensure that, at most, N messages are sent per second. However, if the database is significantly larger than the configured limit, it will take more than 8 seconds to complete the sync. Example usage; to configure at most 1000 messages per second: tmsh modify sys db tmm.sessiondb.ha_mps_limit value 1000

bugs.title: Under certain conditions, SSO plugin can overrun memory not owned by the plugin.
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, SSO plugin can overrun memory not owned by the plugin. Symptoms could be different based on the owner of overrun memory.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1. The BIG-IP system is configured and used as SAML Identity Provider. 2. Single Logout (SLO) protocol is configured on an attached SP connector. 3. At least one user executed SAML WebSSO profile.
bugs.impact: Symptoms might differ based on the owner of overrun memory. Potentially, tmm could restart as a result of this issue.
bugs.workaround: Disable SAML SLO: remove SLO request and SLO response URLs from configuration in appropriate SAML SP connectors.
bugs.fix: SSO plugin no longer overruns memory not owned by the plugin, so the system supports the following configuration without memory issues: The BIG-IP system is configured and used as a SAML Identity Provider. Single Logout (SLO) protocol is configured on the attached Service Provider (SP) connector. At least one user executed SAML webSSO profile.

bugs.title: 'tmsh modify ltm node <ip_addr> state user-down' fails to bring pool member state offline.
bugs.symptoms: The command to set the ltm note state to user-down fails to bring pool member state offline. Running the command results in error messages similar to the following: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Invalid monitor rule instance identifier: 1137
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running the command to set the ltm node state to user-down, for example: tmsh modify ltm node 10.10.10.10 state user-down.
bugs.impact: Session status fails to update for pool member.
bugs.fix: The command to set the ltm node state to user-down now successfully brings pool member state offline.

bugs.title: Copper SFPs OPT-0015 on 10000-series appliance may cause interfaces to not come up and/or show corrupted serial numbers
bugs.symptoms: Some OPT-0015 copper small form-factor pluggable (SFP) transceiver might cause an internal bus to hang.
bugs.conditions: This happens only when the following conditions are met: -- 10000-series appliances. -- At reboot, at a restart of the bcm56xxd daemon, or when a copper SFP is enabled or disabled. -- There is at least one copper SFP present in the appliance. -- Interfaces are spread between hardware muxes. That means some SFPs are in ports 1.1-1.8 and other SFPs are in ports 1.9-1.16.
bugs.impact: Corrupted serial number information from SFPs, and fiber SFPs may not come up. Enable and disable of copper SFPs may not work.
bugs.fix: The system now ensures that the I2C bus muxes only enable a single interface, so the issue with interfaces on Copper SFPs OPT-0015 on 10000-series appliances no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Bait failure alerts do not give details of the cause of failure
bugs.symptoms: Bait fail alert details are always the same.
bugs.conditions: Honeypot mechanism failed due to http error, clientside error, timeout, etc.
bugs.impact: Difficult to find cause of failures due to poor granularity of error alert
bugs.fix: The following details were added to the Bait Failure alert: bf_malformed : Malformed bait response bf_jserror : Bait checks errored bf_timeout : Bait request timed out bf_<status_code> : Bait response was not 200 OK. Eg bf_404 bf_unknown : Other failure

bugs.title: No fallback for alerts.
bugs.symptoms: No fallback for alerts.
bugs.conditions: Alerts blocked by proxy.
bugs.impact: Alerts do not reach alert server.
bugs.workaround: When alert sending fails, other methods of contacting the alert server should be tried. In some scenarios, these fallbacks are not attempted.
bugs.fix: Use fallback methods when primary alert fails.

bugs.title: sod health logging inconsistent when device removed from failover group or device trust
bugs.symptoms: When a device is in a failover group, sod logs the state change messages indicating the reachability of other devices in the group. For example: Nov 2 11:34:54 BIGIP-1 notice sod[5716]: 010c007f:5: Receiving status updates from peer device /Common/BIGIP-3.localdomain (10.145.192.5) (Online). Nov 2 11:31:19 BIGIP-1 notice sod[5716]: 010c007f:5: Receiving status updates from peer device /Common/BIGIP-3.localdomain (10.145.192.5) (Offline). Nov 2 11:31:43 BIGIP-1 notice sod[5716]: 010c007e:5: Not receiving status updates from peer device /Common/BIGIP-3.localdomain (10.145.192.5) (Disconnected). If a reachable device is removed from the failover group, no "Disconnected" message is issued, so the last reported status will be inaccurate. When a device is part of a trust, sod logs messages indicating what unicast addresses it is monitoring on remote devices: Nov 2 11:34:29 BIGIP-1 info sod[5716]: 010c007a:6: Added unicast failover address 10.145.192.5 port 1026 for device /Common/BIGIP-3.localdomain. If devices are removed from the trust, sod does not log a message that those unicast addresses are no longer in use.
bugs.conditions: When a device is removed from a failover device group, or removed from a device trust.
bugs.impact: Inaccurate state reporting.
bugs.fix: When a device is removed from a failover device group, it is now reported as "Disconnected". When a device is removed from the device trust, sod on the other devices correctly reports that the unicast addresses belonging to the other devices have been deleted.

bugs.title: Brute Force Attack does not start from new entities
bugs.symptoms: An expected brute force attack does not start although the traffic pattern from an IP or to URL seems to be matching the configuration to start an attack.
bugs.conditions: Brute force attack is configured. Failed logins are happening that matches the configuration. The entity (IP/URL) is generating traffic less than 2 minutes.
bugs.impact: A brute force attack is not detected and not prevented.

bugs.title: iRule execution error under virtual server with adaptation profile can crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: tmm segv crash in tandem with log indicating "iRule execution error".
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with request-adapt or response-adapt profile and iRule which is capable of generating a Tcl runtime error.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Correct iRule to avoid runtime error.
bugs.fix: iRule execution error under virtual server with adaptation profile does not crash tmm

bugs.title: In a chassis system with APM provisioned mcpd daemon on secondary blade will restart.
bugs.symptoms: Uploading and installing an epsec/Opswat package on a chassis system will result in mcpd restart on the secondary blades.
bugs.conditions: Installing a new epsec package in a chassis system is the only condition under which this can happen.
bugs.impact: All daemons dependent on mcpd will restart
bugs.fix: Prevent validation of epsec package on secondary blades

bugs.title: Password copying in Variable Assign Agent may fail if user decides not to change password
bugs.symptoms: Copying password using "mcget -secure" command in Variable Assignment agent will fail if user decides not to change password when prompted.
bugs.conditions: The problem happens with these three conditions: 1. AD Query Agent is configured with "Prompt user to change password before expiration"; AND 2. User's password is about to expire and is prompted to change password by AD Query Agent; AND 3. User has chosen not to change password.
bugs.impact: New session variable will not be created by the Variable Assign Agent.
bugs.workaround: Moving the Variable Assign Agent before the AD Query Agent.
bugs.fix: after fix, password is always stored as secure session variable session.logon.last.password in encrypted form.

bugs.title: Abnormally high CPU utilization for external monitors
bugs.symptoms: High CPU utilization for external monitors that use SSL.
bugs.conditions: External monitor using SSL.
bugs.impact: Abnormally high CPU utilization.
bugs.fix: This release improves the handling of external monitors that use SSL so that CPU utilization no longer increases.

bugs.title: client-ssl profile is case-sensitive when checking server_name extension
bugs.symptoms: The client-ssl profile is Case-Sensitive when configuring server-name in the client-ssl profiles and checking server_name extension in the ClientHello Message.
bugs.conditions: When using mixed upper-lower case server-name in the client-ssl profile configuration and ClientHello messages.
bugs.impact: The system treats mixed upper-lower case server-name as different names which violate the RFC6066, which states: "Currently, the only server names supported are DNS hostnames. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive."
bugs.workaround: 1. Configure only one client-ssl profile with same server-name. 2. Use only lower-case server-name when configure the client-ssl profile. 3. Use lower-case server-name in the Client side.
bugs.fix: The system now treats mixed upper-lower case server-names as the same name, so server-name is no longer case sensitive.

bugs.title: Default obfuscator configuration causes very slow javascript in some browsers
bugs.symptoms: Slow javascript causes page to render with a slight delay.
bugs.conditions: Client on Explorer 8 on a slow machine or VM.
bugs.impact: Mainly on older browsers, a slight rendering delay (~1 second) may be noticed.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands on the BIG-IP system: echo "-x" > /shared/datasync/compiler_conf/cs_fpm/OBF_FLAGS chattr +i /shared/datasync/compiler_conf/cs_fpm/OBF_FLAGS
bugs.fix: Improved performance of obfuscated javascript.

bugs.title: sysGlobalTmmStatTmUsageRatio5s and sysGlobalTmmStatNpus in chassis
bugs.symptoms: The sysGlobalTmmStatTmUsageRatio5s and sysGlobalTmmStatNpus OIDs read lower than expected given the traffic on the system. The values suddenly increase when a non-running blade is powered down.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on a chassis where one or more of the blades are not in the cluster, but are not powered down. The usage ratios and Npus stats treat the blades as if they are in the cluster, and are factored into the calculation, making them appear lower than they actually are because non-working blades are in the calculation.
bugs.impact: Misleading, confusing statistics
bugs.workaround: You can completely power down the blade and it will be removed from the statistics calculation.
bugs.fix: sysGlobalTmmStatTmUsageRatio5s and sysGlobalTmmStatNpus are now calculated only against running blades.

bugs.title: Config Sync error after hotfix installation (chroot failed rsync error)
bugs.symptoms: Once an installation has been booted into, applying a hotfix over that installation does not change the SELinux policy, but instead uses the previously installed SELinux policy.
bugs.conditions: This affects installations of a later hotfix atop an earlier hotfix, or onto a base build of the same software version. Installation onto a new volume is unaffected. To determine whether the configuration will experience this issue, use md5sum to see whether the following have the same checksums: -- /etc/selinux/targeted/modules/active/modules/f5_mcpd.pp -- /usr/share/selinux/targeted/f5_mcpd.pp. If the checksums are the same, the system will use the SELinux policy installed with the previous hotfix, and this issue will occur.
bugs.impact: Sync of file objects might fail with an error similar to the following: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group [name] to commit id [number] failed with error 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), verify_sync_result:() :Failed to sync files. - sys/validation/FileObject.cpp, line 6276..
bugs.workaround: Instead of installing the hotfix over an existing installation of the base build of that version (or an earlier hotfix), install the base ISO (for example 11.5.4) into a volume, and then install the hotfix onto that volume, without booting the volume in between.
bugs.fix: Installing a hotfix over an existing base install now rebuilds the SELinux policy as expected.

bugs.title: iqsyncer: GTM/LC config sync failure with error from local mcpd Monitor parent not found
bugs.symptoms: GTM/LC config sync fails with error in /var/log/gtm and /var/log/ltm similar to the following: Monitor /Common/my_http_monitor parent not found
bugs.conditions: There is a customized GTM monitor on one member of a high availability configuration, but not on others.
bugs.impact: Config sync fails. On the device that does not have the monitor, the system logs a parent-not-found message into /var/log/gtm.
bugs.fix: GTM/LC sync now completes successfully even when the configuration being sync'd contains a custom GTM/LC monitor definition.

bugs.title: mcpd can assert on active connection deletion
bugs.symptoms: When all of the peers in an HA / DSC configuration are removed, then it is possible for the connection tear down to result in an assert.
bugs.conditions: Removal of all peers while a connection is handling a transaction.
bugs.impact: MCPD asserts and restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is necessary. MCPD restarts.
bugs.fix: Connection tear down checks for active connections and does not result in an assert when removing all peers while a connection is handling a transaction.

bugs.title: Load UCS failure for objects with unique IP address constraints.
bugs.symptoms: Loading a UCS on running configuration may fail on objects with unique IP address constraints (e.g., self IPs, pool member IPs, etc).
bugs.conditions: Loading a UCS on running configuration.
bugs.impact: UCS load failure.
bugs.workaround: Either load the UCS on a clean configuration (i.e., tmsh load sys config default), or run the load UCS command twice.

bugs.title: DNS messages may become malformed if the Additional section contains an OPT record followed by multiple records.
bugs.symptoms: A DNS message may become malformed when its Additional records section contains an OPT record followed by multiple other DNS records. As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom: The BIG-IP system receives properly formed DNS packets but after processing them sends them as malformed DNS packets.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP configuration contains a virtual server with an associated DNS profile. -- The BIG-IP system receives a DNS message that contains an OPT record. -- The DNS message's Additional records section contains multiple other DNS records.
bugs.impact: This issue impacts all DNS messages that contain an OPT record followed by more than one record. The DNS handling code expects a message containing an OPT record to have 0 or 1 TSIG record following the OPT record in the additional record section of a message. The RFCs permit the OPT record to be placed anywhere in the additional record section of a DNS message, with the exception of a TSIG record. If a TSIG record is present, it must always be last. If no TSIG record is present, then an OPT record can be last. The RFCs do not restrict a query from containing records in the additional record section of the message. When a DNS query or response is passed through the TMM DNS message handler, and that message contains an OPT record followed by more than one record, and those records that follow the OPT record contain compression pointers to other records that also follow the OPT record, then the message becomes mangled.
bugs.workaround: Disable DNS compression on the resolver, or configure the resolver to place OPT records at the end of the additional section (except TSIG records which must always be last).
bugs.fix: DNS messages which contain a record other than TSIG following an OPT record in the additional record section will be transformed in the message handler and the message inspection will be restarted. The transformation involves safely moving the OPT record to be last or second-to-last (in the presence of a TSIG record) position of the additional record section. 'Safely' means updating the relevant compression pointers. The subsequent code paths which depend on the OPT record's position now work as expected.

bugs.title: TMM can crash with ssl persistence and fragmented ssl records
bugs.symptoms: Unusual fragmented ssl records may be handled incorrectly resulting in tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: Ssl persistence and fragemented ssl records.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Possibly switch to different persistence type.
bugs.fix: The error in parsing fragmented ssl records has been resolved.

bugs.title: CertHelper may crash when performing Machine Cert Inspection
bugs.symptoms: CertHelper may crash while checking of machine certificate.
bugs.conditions: APM installed
bugs.impact: Authentication may fail.
bugs.fix: Fixed crash cause in CertHelper.

bugs.title: Unable to install from hotfix on platform with SSD via the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When using the GUI to install a hotfix on a platform with SSD drives, the system posts the following error message: No base image installed or compatible volume to install the Hotfix.
bugs.conditions: The hotfix's base software image is not installed on a non-active volume on a appliance with SSD drives. Current appliances shipping with SSD drives include the following: C109 - 5000 series (5250, 5050) D110 - 7000 series (7250, 7050, 7055) D111 - 12000 series (12050, 12250) D113 - 10000 series (10150N, 10350, 10350F, 10050, 10055) C119 - i5600/i5800 C118 - i7600/i7800 C116 - i10600/i10800 C121 - HRC-i5800 C122 - HRC-i10800 A113 - B2150 blade A112 - B2250 blade A114 - B4450N blade
bugs.impact: Cannot use the GUI to install a hotfix.
bugs.workaround: Using the CLI to install the hotfix.
bugs.fix: In this release, you can use the GUI to install a hotfix on platforms with SSD drives.

bugs.title: DoS Whitelist IPv6 addresses may "overmatch"
bugs.symptoms: When using the 8-entry "rich" DoS whitelist with IPv6 addresses, the HW matches only 32 bits of an incoming IPv6 address against the whitelist entry, meaning that if an incoming IPv6 address matches those 32 bits, the whitelist will result in "match", even if other bits of the IPv6 address do not match. Note that the configuration can select which set of bits (there are 4 choices -- 127:96, 95:64, 63:32, 31:0) to match against, via the db.tunable dos.wlipv6addrsel. Also, note that IPv4 matches are always perfect, and are not affected by this issue.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the 8-entry AFM DoS Whitelist is used to match against IPv6 addresses.
bugs.impact: In some cases, the Whitelist may overmatch, meaning some IPv6 addresses will be considered whitelist matches, when they do not match the whitelist.

bugs.title: EdgeClient cannot connect through captive portal
bugs.symptoms: EdgeClient cannot connect through captive portal.
bugs.conditions: 1) Install EdgeClient on a PC that connects to the APM through a captive portal. 2) Launch EdgeClient and try to connect to the APM. 3) System posts certificate warnings. Accept them. 4) Captive portal is not shown to the user. 5) EdgeClient just toggles between 'Waiting to connect to server' and 'Downloading server settings' messages.
bugs.impact: No captive portal displayed to the user. EdgeClient UI shows he user. 5) EdgeClient just toggles between 'Waiting to connect to server' and 'Downloading server settings' messages.
bugs.fix: Install EdgeClient on a PC that connects to the APM through a captive portal now opens as expected.

bugs.title: Portal Access should ignore incorrect IE-specific cookies with empty name and value
bugs.symptoms: IE-specific cookies with empty name and value are being sent to backend. Request header in a traffic dump between APM and backend could look like "Cookie: =;<other cookies>" for example.
bugs.conditions: This can occur with cookies being sent via Internet Explorer through Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Errors from backend applications which are unable to handle such cookies.
bugs.fix: Cookies with empty name and value will no longer be sent to backend application via Portal Access

bugs.title: Not all HTTP transactions make it through credits to iRule failures when FastL4 is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: Some HTTP transactions are dropped
bugs.conditions: Occurs in the following scenario - PEM configured on an HTTP virtual - Transactional policy configured - iRule triggered per transaction is attached to HTTP virtual and FastL4
bugs.impact: Can result in dropped flows.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this, issue can be avoided by not enabling FastL4 when iRules are present in this scenario.

bugs.title: When a virtual server has an Anti-Fraud Profile and a Web Acceleration profile, POST requests to non-protected URLs hang
bugs.symptoms: A POST request to a virtual will timeout and will not immediately return a response. After a timeout occurs, an HTTP 400 response status will be returned.
bugs.conditions: This issue is encountered when sending a POST request to a virtual server that is configured with an Anti-Fraud Profile and a Web Acceleration profile.
bugs.impact: The request times out and 400 HTTP response status is returned. The application will break.
bugs.fix: POST requests no longer time out when sent to a virtual server that has an Anti-Fraud Profile and a Web Acceleration profile.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP ASM configuration fails to load after an upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: A configuration load failure occurs after creating an ASM predefined report in a previous version - (11.3 or 11.4) and upgrading to a version prior to 12.1.0.
bugs.conditions: Define scheduled report with 'predefined-report-name: '/Common/Top alerted URLs' on version 11.3 or 11.4 upgrade the version.
bugs.impact: Version upgrade fails (the BIG-IP system becomes unusable).
bugs.workaround: Manually change predefined-report-name '/Common/Top alerted URLs' to predefined-report-name '/Common/Top alarmed URLs'.
bugs.fix: If an ASM predefined report was created in a previous version and the system was updated, it could have caused the configuration upgrade to fail. This failure no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Large compressed files can cause qkview to consume large amounts of memory.
bugs.symptoms: Large compressed files can cause qkview to consume large amounts of memory.
bugs.conditions: Less than 10% of system memory available or less than 96 KB of memory available. Large compressed files in qkview.
bugs.impact: Memory usage might be greater than 350200 kilobytes, which is the critical memory level. Might force other processes into swap. This can negatively impact performance.

bugs.title: 'gtmd' daemon is not visible in daemon-ha list command
bugs.symptoms: On the VIPRION B2250 blade, running tmsh list sys daemon-ha does not show gtmd even though gtmd is provisioned and running as confirmed by tmsh show sys service gtmd
bugs.conditions: This ocurs on VIPRION B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: gtmd not listed in daemon-ha table.

bugs.title: Correlation is continuously restarted with 'An instance with pid xxxx is already running' error in the ltm log
bugs.symptoms: correlation is continuously restarted with these errors: /var/log/asm: ---------- ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::NwdUtils::Nwd::log_failure): Watchdog detected failure for process. Process name: correlation, Failure: Insufficient number of threads (required: 1, found: 0). ---------- /var/log/ltm: ---------- err correlation[xxxx]: 01560000:3: An instance with pid yyyyy is already running ----------
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned.
bugs.impact: Correlation is continuously restarted.
bugs.workaround: Here is a workaround. All commands should be executed as root user, on the CLI of the affected BIG-IP system: 1) Create a backup of the file '/usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml' to '/usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml.orig': # cp /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml.orig 2) Patch the yaml file (Note: The spaces in the command are significant.): # perl -pi -e 's/correlation:/correlation:\n pid_file: \/shared\/tmp\/correlation.pid/' /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml 3) Diff the original file VS the patched file: # diff -C 1 /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml.orig /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml 4) Validate that the diff, which was generated in previous step, is exactly as follows (spaces are significant, timestamps will differ): *** /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml.orig 2015-11-09 10:12:06.000000000 -0500 --- /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml 2015-11-09 10:12:14.000000000 -0500 *************** *** 33,34 **** --- 33,35 ---- correlation: + pid_file: /shared/tmp/correlation.pid exec_method: system 5) Restart ASM: # bigstart restart asm 6) Make sure that the BIG-IP system is Active and that there are no 'Watchdog detected failure for process' errors in '/var/log/asm'. 7) Monitor logs for these errors, which should not appear: ----------------------------------------- /var/log/asm: ---------- ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::NwdUtils::Nwd::log_failure): Watchdog detected failure for process. Process name: correlation, Failure: Insufficient number of threads (required: 1, found: 0). ---------- /var/log/ltm: ---------- An instance with pid xxxx is already running ---------- ----------------------------------------- Note that step (5) is disruptive and will cause the BIG-IP system to go 'Offline' for a short period of time. In the case you need to revert the workaround: ----------------------------------------- # mv /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml.orig /usr/share/ts/config/asm_processes.yaml # bigstart restart asm -----------------------------------------
bugs.fix: We have resolved an issue with the correlation daemon startup sequence so that it does not go into a restart loop.

bugs.title: Dynamic route flapping may lead to tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: When dynamic routing is in use and routes are being actively added and removed, tmm may crash.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server configured with Dynamic Routing
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Flapping dynamic routes no longer trigger a tmm crash.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Virtual Edition becomes completely unresponsive under very heavy load.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition becomes completely unresponsive under very heavy load.
bugs.conditions: Sustained high packet rate with a very small payload.
bugs.impact: Traffic through the guest stops until the guest/BIG-IP system is reset. However, this issue is reproduced during a test that over provision a 2-vCPU guest and is unlikely to happen in normal operation.
