bugs.workaround: Try ones of the following workarounds (first on is the most preferred and so ): 1. Increase guest memory. 2. Significantly reduce the value of the content in '/sys/module/unic/rx_queue_size'. For example running the following command substantially decreases throughput: echo 1048576 > /sys/module/unic/rx_queue_size. 3. Set panic on OOM. Try this as the last option. sysctl vm.panic_on_oom=1
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Virtual Edition becomes unresponsive under extreme load test due to kernel memory exhaustion from over-provisioning.

bugs.title: Inbound ISP link load balancing will use pool members for only one ISP link per data center
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP Link Controller and GTM 11.5.3, 11.6.0 and prior versions, and BIG-IP DNS 12.0.0, the inbound ISP link load balancing functionality uses pool members for more than one ISP link per data center.
bugs.conditions: Using the inbound ISP link load balancing functionality in BIG-IP Link Controller and GTM 11.5.3, 11.6.0 and prior versions, and BIG-IP DNS 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: If a pool has multiple members that use different ISP links within a data center, the system uses only pool members associated with the ISP link of the first available pool member. The system marks pool members associated with subsequent ISP links as unavailable (grey).
bugs.fix: The inbound ISP link load balancing functionality will use pool members for only one ISP link per data center for each pool.
bugs.behavior: Beginning in BIG-IP Link Controller and GTM 11.5.4, 11.6.1, and BIG-IP DNS 12.1.0, the ISP link load balancing functionality will use pool members for only one ISP link per data center for each pool. The link that is associated with the first configured and available pool member within each data center will determine the link that will be used for the data center. The system will use only pool members associated with that link.
bugs.workaround: -- If you reside in the United States and used these EoL load balancing features prior to January 26, 2016: You might be eligible to re-enable the functionality by contacting F5 Support to determine eligibility for requesting a software patch. -- If you reside outside of the United States: Go to downloads.f5.com :: Non-US Patches for BIG-IP and download linkcost.im patch.

bugs.title: The audit_forwarder process fails to exit normally causing the process to consume CPU to near 100%
bugs.symptoms: audit_forwarder and mcpd consume almost 100% CPU. When syslog-ng restarts, it starts another audit_forwarder process, but it is the orphaned audit_forwarder process that will consume almost 100% CPU. When syslog-ng is restarted and audit_forwarder does not exit cleanly, the mcpd process will also begin consuming high CPU.
bugs.conditions: syslog-ng is stopped manually or sometimes (rarely) during a normal restart of syslog-ng.
bugs.impact: The audit_forwarder and mcpd processes consume excessive CPU.
bugs.workaround: Stop audit_forwarder manually (kill -9), once the orphaned audit_forwarder process is stopped, mcpd will return to normal CPU consumption.
bugs.fix: When syslog-ng is stopped manually (or when expected), audit_forwarder also exits, so the audit_forward process no longer consumes increasing CPU.

bugs.title: Sensitive monitor parameters recorded in bigd and monitor logs
bugs.symptoms: When bigd debug logging is enabled, the resulting bigd debug log may contain sensitive parameters from the monitor configuration. When monitor instance logging or monitor debug logging is enabled for certain monitor types, the resulting monitor instance logs may contain sensitive parameters from the monitor configuration. In each case, the monitor parameters logged may include: - user-account password - radius/diameter secret - snmp community string
bugs.conditions: This may occur under either of the following conditions: 1. bigd debug logging is enabled: tmsh modify sys db bigd.debug value enabled 2. Monitor instance logging is enabled for one of the following LTM monitor types: ftp imap pop3 smtp
bugs.impact: The user-account password, radius/diameter secret, or snmp community string configured in the LTM health monitor may appear in plain text form in the bigd debug log (/var/log/bigdlog) or in the monitor instance logs under /var/log/monitors.
bugs.workaround: 1. Do not enable bigd debug logging. 2. Do not enable monitor instance logging or monitor debug logging for affected LTM monitor types. 3. If it is necessary to enable monitor instance logging or monitor debug logging for troubleshooting purposes, remove the resulting log files from the BIG-IP system after troubleshooting is completed.
bugs.fix: The password, community and secret parameters will now be redacted by bigd and Tcl monitors when debugging is enabled.
bugs.behavior: The password, community and secret parameters will now be redacted by bigd and Tcl monitors when debugging is enabled. bigd will no longer log all of the monitor parameters every time that a Tcl monitor is scheduled and bigd debugging is enabled unless logging is specifically enabled for the monitor instance (e.g. a pool member has "logging enabled"). The Tcl worker process will no longer log all of the parameters of a monitor when the monitor is run and bigd debugging is enabled. If parameters information is needed for debugging purposes, this should be handled specifically in the Tcl monitor script.

bugs.title: TMM SIGSEGV and crash when memory allocation fails.
bugs.symptoms: TMM SIGSEGV and crash when memory allocation fails.
bugs.conditions: Although the specific conditions under which this occurs are not well understood, it appears that the issue occurs when the SSL operation detects an error and processes the connection for removal from the SSL queue. Before the connection is removed, another command attempts to remove the connection a second time, which causes the issue to occur.
bugs.impact: TMM SIGSEGV and crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None known at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM SIGSEGV and crash no longer occur when memory allocation fails due to a command attempting to remove the connection for removal from the SSL queue a second time.

bugs.title: Browser could become unresponsive when page with specific script constructions is accessed through Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: If user application code has an object with toString() method and property names similar to ones from Javascript builtin Location interface, our rewriting may cause an infinite loop while processing such object.
bugs.conditions: APM with Portal Access configured.
bugs.impact: Browser hangs or crashes when trying to access page through Portal Access.
bugs.fix: Resolved an issue in Portal Access where certain user-defined Javascript objects could cause a loop in F5 helper code and unresponsiveness of a browser.

bugs.title: Full Webtop resources appear overlapping in IE11 compatibility mode
bugs.symptoms: Full Webtop resources appear overlapping each other in MSIE 11 in compartibility mode
bugs.conditions: MSIE 11, compartibility mode. Full Webtop in use
bugs.impact: Everything is working but the icons overlap.
bugs.workaround: 1. modify advanced customization of apm.css #webtop_favorites_inner_container span.favorite span.caption{ ... <? if( $_GET['ctype'] == 'IE' && $_GET['cversion'] < 9){ ?> zoom: 1; <? }elseif( $_GET['ctype'] == 'IE' && $_GET['cversion'] == 11){ ?> zoom: 0; <? } ?> } 2. an irule that would change apm.css to #webtop_favorites_inner_container SPAN.favorite SPAN.caption { ... zoom: 1; /* <--- set 0 if msie 11 in compartibility mode */ }
bugs.fix: Everything is back to normal

bugs.title: After setting a Last Resort Pool on a Wide IP, cannot reset back to None
bugs.symptoms: After configuring a wide IP with a Last Resort Pool set to something other than None, you can no longer change the Last Resort Pool back to None.
bugs.conditions: Last Resort Pool is set to something other than None.
bugs.impact: There is no None option in TMSH or GUI.
bugs.workaround: Setting the Pool Name to an empty string via tmsh will set it to None. For example modify gtm wideip a wip.f5.com last-resort-pool a
bugs.fix: None options added to tmsh and GUI.

bugs.title: Messages logged when the CAN daemon (cand) receives unsolicited data
bugs.symptoms: When the log filter is configured to filter at the 'Informational' log level, the logs can get filled with 'request for unsolicated data' messages. These messages appear in the log every 20 seconds.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using a remote syslog logging filter with the 'Severity' field set to 'Informational'.
bugs.impact: Logs fill with messages. These messages are related to communication with the CAN daemon (cand), and are completely benign, so you can safely ignore them.
bugs.workaround: Change the remote syslog logging level to 'Notice'.

bugs.title: LTM Policy statistics showing zeros in GUI
bugs.symptoms: Statistics for LTM Policies, i.e. the total count of policy action invocations and number of successful policy action invocations, are not being updated in the GUI. The GUI shows zeros for both of these stats for every LTM Policy.
bugs.conditions: Occurs under all conditions.
bugs.impact: Through the GUI, Administrators cannot see invocation counts for general troubleshooting or to determine which policies are being used.
bugs.workaround: Accurate stats can be obtained from the command line using tmsh. Stats for all policies can be obtained by the following: # tmsh show ltm policy. Stats for a specific policy can be obtained by specifying the policy name. # tmsh show ltm policy <policy-name>.
bugs.fix: LTM Policy statistics now shows the correct values in the GUI.

bugs.title: "Expect 100-continue" support
bugs.symptoms: ASM supports "Expect 100-continue" behavior only for the POST method.
bugs.conditions: if for example, a client sends a request with PUT method, "Expect 100-continue" header, and a body.
bugs.impact: such a request will not be passed to server, instead it will hang and expire on a timeout.

bugs.title: Monitor description containing escape characters could get double-escaped
bugs.symptoms: When creating a monitor whose description contains escape characters, they get double-escaped. Example: root@(v11-5-01)(cfg-sync Disconnected)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# create ltm monitor http http_foobar description \@\#\$\@\#\$\@\#\$\@\#\$\@\#\$ root@(v11-5-01)(cfg-sync Disconnected)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list ltm monitor http http_foobar ltm monitor http http_foobar { defaults-from http description "@\\#\\$@\\#\\$@\\#\\$@\\#\\$@\\#\\$"
bugs.conditions: Creating monitors with escape characters in the description
bugs.impact: Description contains extra backslashes.

bugs.title: TMM may core when disabling HTTP in an iRule on a virtual server with HTTP and FastL4 profiles
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios TMM may core if disabling HTTP in CLIENT_ACCEPTED on a virtual server that is configured with FastL4 and HTTP profiles.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with HTTP and Fast L4 profiles. -- iRule attached to the VIP that disables HTTP in CLIENT_ACCEPTED event. -- Traffic is reset abruptly while passing through this VIP.
bugs.impact: TMM may core and the systems may failover.
bugs.workaround: Several options exist: - Use TCP and HTTP profiles instead of Fast L4. - Do not disable the HTTP profile via iRules.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when handling traffic on FastL4/HTTP virtual servers that disable HTTP via iRules.

bugs.title: Tcl monitors may not fire on their scheduled intervals
bugs.symptoms: Tcl monitors (FTP, IMAP, POP3, SMTP) might not fire on their scheduled intervals. If they are delayed long enough, it could trigger a false down condition even though the monitored object is up.
bugs.conditions: Multiple Tcl monitors are in use and several of the monitors are taking too long to complete. This could be caused monitored objects that are down and timing out or monitored objects that take too long to respond. This will cause the Tcl monitor work load to back up preventing other monitors (that might be up) from firing on time.
bugs.impact: An object might be marked down even though it is actually up.
bugs.workaround: If you are encountering this, and your environment requires you to use these types of monitors, and the condition is triggering only occasionally, you may be able to increase the monitor interval and timeout settings to avoid the false down situation.

bugs.title: TMM can continuously attempt to reset failing Nitrox
bugs.symptoms: If a Nitrox crypto accelerator chip fails, TMM will attempt to reset it to clear the failure condition. If the Nitrox failure is permanent, TMM will continuously attempt to reset the Nitrox, adversely impacting traffic flow. You will see errors in /var/log/ltm that say "crit tmm[12809]: 01010025:2: Device error: cn0 device soft resetting"
bugs.conditions: This occurs when one of the Nitrox crypto accelerator chips fails.
bugs.impact: Loss of traffic.

bugs.title: Charts: E-Mail sending doesn't work but no error is reported
bugs.symptoms: When trying to send a report via e-mail (using SMTP), user receives no indication of any problem but no e-mail is actually being sent.
bugs.conditions: Exporting a report via e-mail
bugs.impact: Unable to send reports

bugs.title: Manually created backend nodes should not be added to a pool that is managed by AWS Auto Scaling Group.
bugs.symptoms: Autoscale pool manager reports at every iteration in /var/log/ltm that it wants to delete a pool member but fails to do so.
bugs.conditions: Applies only to pool member autoscale in AWS. Happens only if you manually add a backend node to a pool that is managed by AWS Auto Scaling Group.
bugs.impact: /var/log/ltm is full of error messages. No actual impact on the traffic.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the pool member that has been manually added to the pool. Note: Manually created backend nodes should not be manually added to a pool that is managed by AWS Auto Scaling Group. Autoscale pool manager will detect that the offending pool member was not created by the AWS Auto Scaling Group. It will try to delete the pool member from the pool, an operation that will likely fail. This will be repeated at every iteration of the autoscale pool manager, which fills /var/log/ltm with error messages.

bugs.title: Communication between devices in a high availability (HA) configuration might occasionally fail on VIPRION 2200 and 2400 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: Communication between devices in a high availability (HA) configuration might occasionally fail on VIPRION 2200 and 2400 platforms.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION 2200 and 2400 platforms with more than one blade. Multiple devices in an HA configuration. TMM incorrectly identifies which TMM should handle host connections from an HA peer. The host connection will be reset after the SYN retransmits are exceeded between TMM and the host process.
bugs.impact: Periodic reported failures in host-to-host communication. This could affect config sync, and other HA related communication.
bugs.fix: Host communication on VIPRION 2200 and 2400 platforms behaves the same as host communication on non-VIPRION 2200 and 2400 platforms, as expected.

bugs.title: Some monitor types may fail to probe when the monitor definition is changed
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may fail to send monitor probes for FTP, IMAP, POP3, or SMTP monitors for monitored objects (pool member or nodes) after the configuration of the monitor is updated.
bugs.conditions: FTP, IMAP, POP3, or SMTP monitors are configured and a change is made to the monitor definition while the monitor is assigned to a pool member or node. The problem is more likely to occur if the monitor probe takes a long time to complete.
bugs.impact: Pool member or node status may no longer be updated and the BIG-IP system no longer properly tracks the health of the monitored object.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate this issue, avoid making changes to FTP, IMAP, POP3, or SMTP monitor definitions.
bugs.fix: Altering the configuration of an FTP, IMAP, POP3, or SMTP monitor no longer causes the BIG-IP system to stop monitoring the object.

bugs.title: Failover from PEM to PCRF can cause session lookup inconsistency
bugs.symptoms: A small number of PEM sessions can be looked up only by their session-ip, but not by their subscriber-id.
bugs.conditions: Using PEM, failover to PCRF.
bugs.impact: Fails to find sessions needed for traffic processing.
bugs.fix: The code change provides an internal fixup for incorrect sessions.

bugs.title: Fast successive MTU changes to IPsec tunnel interface crashes TMM
bugs.symptoms: Changing IPsec tunnel interface MTU attribute repeatedly in quick succession, TMM cores. This can occur whether or not traffic has flowed through the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when the IPsec tunnel interface attributes has its configuration modified quickly and repeatedly.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Change IPsec tunnel interface attributes at a rate of speed that allows each configuration modification to complete.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores if users quickly and repeatedly change interface attributes (for example, the MTU interface attribute).

bugs.title: TMM generated traffic to external IPv6 global-addr via ECMP routes might use link-local addr
bugs.symptoms: TMM might use a link-local IPv6 address when attempting to reach an external global address for traffic generated from TMM (for example, dns resolver, sideband connections, etc.).
bugs.conditions: - ECMP IPv6 routes to a remote destination where the next hop is a link local address. Typically this occurs with dynamic routing. - Have configured a virtual server that generates traffic from TMM (for example, dns resolver, sideband connections, etc.).
bugs.impact: Traffic might fail as its egresses from a link-local address instead of a global address.
bugs.workaround: It might be possible to work around if the dynamic routing peer can announce the route from a global address instead of a link local. Use of static routes might also work around the issue.
bugs.fix: TMM now uses the correct IPv6 global address when generating traffic to a remote address using ECMP routes via link-local next-hops.

bugs.title: Policy sync fails when adding host to AppTunnel on LSO resolve
bugs.symptoms: Policy sync fails when adding host to AppTunnel on LSO resolve. The system posts the following message: 01070712:3: String is not a valid IP address.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create AppTunnel resource on device1. 2. Sync APM policy with AppTunnel resource from device1 to device2. 3. On device2 policy sync, click Unresolve and resolve the conflict by adding another host (with a valid IP/hostname and port). 4. Click Finish.
bugs.impact: Policy sync fails.
bugs.fix: Policy sync is now successful when adding host to AppTunnel on LSO resolve.

bugs.title: bigd restart when DNS server returns 0 address
bugs.symptoms: bigd might restart if DNS server returns a 0 address on FQDN nodes.
bugs.conditions: DNS server returns a 0 address on FQDN nodes.
bugs.impact: bigd continually restarts.
bugs.workaround: Fix DNS configuration to not return 0 address.

bugs.title: Pool's 'active_member_cnt' attribute may not be updated as expected.
bugs.symptoms: If a pool has no associated monitors, new pool members added to the pool do not increment the active_member_cnt even if traffic will be passed to it. In other cases, for FQDN pool members, the active_member_cnt does not update in user-down scenarios, or other state transitions.
bugs.conditions: 1) Configure a pool without a monitor, and make use of an iRule that attempts to use the 'active_member_cnt' attribute. 2) Configure a pool with FQDN nodes and change the state to user-down, and check the active_member_cnt via an iRule or GUIshell.
bugs.impact: Although this does not impact load balancing and is not visible in the GUI or tmsh, it is exposed as a consumable attribute in iRules, which can impact your scripts.
bugs.workaround: member_count returns total members with no status information.
bugs.fix: Pool's 'active_member_cnt' attribute is now updated as expected, even for pools that have no assigned monitors.

bugs.title: Expanding large objects in Security - Network Firewall - Address Lists does not work for IE
bugs.symptoms: Expanding large address lists in Security - Network Firewall - Address Lists does not work on IE
bugs.conditions: Only happens when address lists are really big
bugs.impact: Address List page on Security-->firewall

bugs.title: No Audit logging on 'Clear Performance Data' from statistics page in GUI.
bugs.symptoms: There is no Audit logging on 'Clear Performance Data' from statistics page in GUI.
bugs.conditions: Clearing statistics in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Users can clear the performance data without leaving any trace.
bugs.fix: Logging is now provided in /var/log/webui.log when a user clicks 'Clear Performance Data' from statistics page in GUI.

bugs.title: Filtering encryption alerts
bugs.symptoms: There was no option in 11.6.0 or earlier to filter out encryption alerts.
bugs.conditions: Encryption is failing.
bugs.impact: There is always an alert sent, even if it comes from an unsupported browser.
bugs.fix: A new DB variable 'AntiFraud.EncryptionAlerts' has been added that controls whether or not the FPS plugin filters encryption alerts.

bugs.title: Show template javascript on Client initiated SSO v2
bugs.symptoms: On selection of Javascript injection with Custom, the template is blank.
bugs.conditions: With SSO - Forms client initiated, Selection of Injection method is Custom.
bugs.impact: On selection of Javascript injection with Custom, the template is blank, increasing the chance of creating errors with the custom Javascript.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Get the tcp dump of traffic. 2. From the dump, inspect the javascript used to submit the request. 3. Use it as the Custom script.
bugs.fix: Show default template javascript on user now chooses Javascript Injection - Custom, and the template is no longer blank.

bugs.title: Upgrading results in additional escaping for monitor send/recv strings in /config/bigip.conf.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading results in additional escaping for monitor send/recv strings in /config/bigip.conf. After upgrading the bigip.conf still has the old #TMSH-VERSION header. This is behavior is an intended behavior in 12.1.0, so it is not a bug; the configuration is still loaded in memory properly. The TMSH-VERSION string will be updated the next time a save sys config command is issued.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when upgrading BIG-IP software in the following situations: -- From 11.6.0 base version, or from 11.6.0 HF1 through 11.6.0 HF5 (or any engHF built on these versions) to final :11.6.0 HF6 through 11.6.0 HF8 -- From 11.5.3 base version, or from 11.5.3 HF1 or 11.5.3 HF2 (or any engHF for these versions) to 11.5.3 HF2 engHF2 or 11.5.3 HF2 engHF45.
bugs.impact: Monitors send/recv strings contain extra escape characters, for example: \\r, \\n etc. Post upgrade the monitors containing escaped characters will fail.
bugs.workaround: Manually/by script remove the additional escaping within the send/recv strings.
bugs.fix: The system no longer appends extra escape characters to monitor send/receive strings after upgrading.

bugs.title: The TMM may crash if http url rewrite is used with APM
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP uri rewrite feature depends on having a client-side to determine the ip address of that client. However, APM may use the HTTP filter without having a client-side. This can cause a TMM crash when the missing ip address is used by the HTTP uri rewrite feature.
bugs.conditions: APM + HTTP uri rewrite feature. (This is different to the "rewrite" profile.)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable the HTTP uri rewrite feature when using APM. An iRule may be used to safely implement its transformations.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes when the HTTP uri rewrite feature is used with APM.

bugs.title: MCPD restart on secondary blade after updating Pool via GUI
bugs.symptoms: If you use the LTM GUI in a clustered environment to add an IP Encapsulation profile to a Pool, then click Update, mcpd and other daemons may restart on secondary blades in the cluster. When this occurs, errors similar to the following will be logging from the secondary blades: -- err mcpd[22537]: 01020036:3: The requested pool profile (49825) was not found. -- err mcpd[22537]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020036:3: The requested pool profile (49825) was not found.
bugs.conditions: This problem may occur when operating BIG-IP in a clustered environment (VIPRION), and using the GUI to update the properties of an LTM pool with an IP Encapsulation profile defined.
bugs.impact: Daemon restarts, disruption of traffic passing on secondary blades.
bugs.workaround: Perform pool updates via the tmsh command-line utility.
bugs.fix: Pool profile update is performed by name rather than object ID, so MCPD no longer restarts on secondary blade after updating a pool using the GUI.

bugs.title: Active mode FTP data channel issue when using lasthop pool
bugs.symptoms: The data channel for active mode FTP may fail.
bugs.conditions: Active mode FTP through a virtual with ftp profile with port set to zero and configured to use a lasthop pool.
bugs.impact: Active mode FTP does not work.
bugs.workaround: Use auto-lasthop instead of lasthop pool. Use passive mode FTP.
bugs.fix: Active mode FTP now works correctly.

bugs.title: System may fail when syncookie mode is activated
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core when syncookie mode has been activated when under extreme memory pressure.
bugs.conditions: L7 VIP with certain TCP profile attributes enabled. Syncookies have been activated. System under memory pressure due to heavy load.
bugs.impact: tmm may core.
bugs.workaround: Use the default TCP profile for all L7 VIPs.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP will not encounter a system failure when syncookie mode has been activated.

bugs.title: APM Network Access VPN feature may leak memory
bugs.symptoms: VPN connections may cause memory usage to increase with the memory never being reclaimed.
bugs.conditions: -- APM Network Access feature is configured. -- VPN connections are being established.
bugs.impact: Slow memory leak over time with eventual out-of-memory condition, performance degradation, and traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: No workaround short of not using the APM Network Access feature.
bugs.fix: The APM Network Access VPN feature no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: Cannot create the same navigation parameter in two different policies
bugs.symptoms: Cannot create the same navigation parameter in two different policies. A validation issue blocks the user from adding a navigation parameter that is already defined in a different security policy.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after adding navigation parameter X to one policy, and then attempting to add the same parameter to another policy.
bugs.impact: Cannot add navigation parameter X to another policy after adding it to the first policy.
bugs.fix: The system now supports adding the same navigation parameter to different security policies.

bugs.title: "Show All" option for large no. of security objects can cause poor performance in some browsers
bugs.symptoms: Using "Show All" for showing a large number of security objects on GUI can be challenging for some browsers (especially IE)
bugs.conditions: Large number of security objects on GUI to display, use of particular browsers (especially IE)
bugs.impact: AFM Address List page and others may not render properly or responsively.
bugs.workaround: Use Chrome

bugs.title: SNMP dot3 stats occassionally unavailable
bugs.symptoms: SNMP would not provide values for some dot3 stats.
bugs.conditions: Always under affected version
bugs.impact: SNMP would not provide values for some dot3 stats. This is no impact actual traffic.
bugs.fix: The dot3 stats are now available.

bugs.title: Client can not connect to Windows 10 using ActiveX RDP client launched from the APM Webtop if "Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with Network level Authentication" is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: Client can not connect to Windows 10 using ActiveX RDP client launched from the APM Webtop if "Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with Network level Authentication" is disabled at the remote host. The user is shown an error message: "The connections cannot proceed because authentication is not enabled and the remote computer requires that authentication be enabled to connect."
bugs.conditions: Remote server is Windows 10, "Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with Network level Authentication" is not enabled on the server
bugs.impact: Client can not connect to remote server
bugs.workaround: Several workarounds are available here: 1) Enable "Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with Network level Authentication" on the remote server 2) Edit the registry on the remote or deploy as GPO to your desktop: [HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp] "SecurityLayer"=dword:00000001 "UserAuthentication"=dword:00000000 3) Using RDG may be considered as yet another possible workaround.

bugs.title: Unexpected loss of communication between slots of a vCMP Guest
bugs.symptoms: 1. Within the vCMP guest, the affected slot shows the other slot(s) to be offline. When logged into any other "offline" slot, the slot shows itself to be online. 2. Within the vCMP guest, on the affected slot, the log files (such as /var/log/ltm) have stopped recording log entries from the other slot(s). 3. Within the vCMP guest, on the affected slot, the eth1 interface shows TX increasing but RX not increasing. The eth1 interface on other slots shows both TX and RX increasing.
bugs.conditions: Only affects vCMP guests with 2 or more slots on VIPRION C2000-series chassis.
bugs.impact: The number of working slots in a vCMP guest is reduced to 1 slot. The effect on traffic may range from none to severe.
bugs.workaround: Within the vCMP guest, login to the command line (vconsole or SSH) of the affected slot and run the following: ifconfig eth1 down ; ifconfig eth1 up Alternatively, from the hypervisor, modify the vCMP guest to the Configured state, and wait to confirm the vCMP guest has stopped on all slots. Then return the vCMP guest to the Deployed state.
bugs.fix: This release no long exhibits loss of communication between slots of a vCMP Guest.

bugs.title: Control insertion to log_session_details table by Access policy logging level.
bugs.symptoms: Session records are always written to log_session_details table upon new session creation, regardless of access log level.
bugs.conditions: New sessions created
bugs.impact: CPU hogged when large numbers of sessions are created within short time period
bugs.fix: Control insertion to log_session_details table by Access policy logging level.

bugs.title: Overlapping of address are not allowed on firewall NAT policy match side
bugs.symptoms: Overlapping IP addresses (addresses and address-list) are not allowed in NAT policy rules.
bugs.conditions: Trying to configure overlapping IP addresses in NAT policy rules.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure overlapping IP addresses in NAT policy rules.
bugs.fix: The system now allows overlapping IP addresses (addresses and address-list) in a NAT policy rule. It logs a notice message in /var/log/ltm when there are overlapping IP addresses and includes detail address information.

bugs.title: Protected workspace does not work correctly with third party products
bugs.symptoms: 1) Internet Explorer and Firefox cannot be launched in Windows protected workspace if Norton Internet Security 22.x is present on user's machines. 2) Microsoft OneDrive does not work correctly inside protected workspace.
bugs.conditions: Norton Internet Security 22.x is installed on user's desktop. Protected workspace is used.
bugs.impact: User cannot launch Internet Explorer or Firefox inside protected workspace. Files cannot be synced to OneDrive.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: User can now launch Internet Explorer or Firefox inside protected workspace.

bugs.title: TMM may fail to forward FTP data connections when multiple PORT/EPRT commands are used in succession referring to the same IP/PORT
bugs.symptoms: TMM may fail to forward FTP data connections when PORT/EPRT commands are used in succession referring to the same IP/PORT.
bugs.conditions: FTP Virtual server configured with an FTP profile that does inherit-parent-profile disabled. A client to request EPRT and then PORT commands referring to the same IP/PORT.
bugs.impact: TMM may reset the connection in some cases.
bugs.workaround: Change the ftp profile to enable the inherit-parent-profile option.

bugs.title: HSB debug registers needed
bugs.symptoms: Some hardware platforms provide insufficient diagnostic information in the hsb_snapshot to determine the problem the system encounters. (The hsb_snapshot command gathers information from the high speed bridge (HSB) for diagnostic purposes.) Additional HSB debug registers are needed to perform full diagnostics.
bugs.conditions: Running the hsb_snapshot command in the qkview utility.
bugs.impact: Some HSB debug registers are needed to provide full diagnostics.
bugs.fix: The hsb_snapshot now supports all HSBE2 PDE/MGMT_RING, etc., debug and XLMAC registers, to support a more robust diagnostic operations.

bugs.title: TMM may core when APM is provisioned and access profile is attached to the virtual
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core when APM is provisioned and access profile is attached to the virtual.
bugs.conditions: This crash is most likely to occur when there are more than 1 ABORT events sent to a connection on a virtual with attached access profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: APM virtual server that can have multiple ABORTs events to a connection will no longer cause TMM to crash and restart.

bugs.title: Edge Mobile browser is recognized as Chrome
bugs.symptoms: Edge Mobile browser is recognized as Chrome causing a web page rendering issue.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP must have AAM module provisioned and have a policy with image optimization enabled attached to a virtual.
bugs.impact: When a user with Edge Mobile client accesses the website AAM can convert image to webp format not recognized by the client. It will cause incorrect rendering of the webpage.
bugs.workaround: Disable conversion to webp.

bugs.title: Optimization to JPEG-XR fails on Edge browsers
bugs.symptoms: When image optimization to convert to JPEG-XR is enabled and an Edge client connects to BIG-IP it doesn't receive optimized image according to configured policy and DB variable ccdb.allow.edge.jpegxr set to "true".
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has AAM provisioned and a policy with image optimization to convert to JPEG-XR option enabled is attached to a virtual. An Edge client connects via this virtual.
bugs.impact: JPEG-XR is expected to consume less throughput which may affect pages with multiple images rendering on it.

bugs.title: Improvement to cause tmm to core when mcpd exits
bugs.symptoms: When troubleshooting the tmm state when mcpd exits, it is not possible to generate a tmm core
bugs.conditions: Troubleshooting mcpd and tmm state at the same time
bugs.impact: Unable to force a tmm core when mcpd exits. There is no functional impact to this but it can make diagnosing issues more difficult.
bugs.fix: A new sys db variable has been added called tmm.mcp.disconnect.core to cause tmm to core when mcpd disconnects.
bugs.behavior: A new sys db variable has been added called tmm.mcp.disconnect.core. The default value is disabled. When enabled, tmm will core if mcpd exists. This can be useful for troubleshooting purposes.

bugs.title: Unable to clear LCD messages and Alarm LED state on non-iSeries platforms
bugs.symptoms: You cannot clear alert messages shown on the LCD display from the TMOS console. In addition, the Alarm LED may continue to reflect an elevated alert status (by display a steady or blinking Red or Amber state) after LCD alert messages are cleared.
bugs.conditions: -- This may occur when BIG-IP system is running on hardware platforms other than iSeries appliances. -- Specifically, affected platforms include: + VIPRION B4200, B4300-series, B4400-series blades + VIPRION C4400, C4480, C4800 chassis + VIPRION B2100, B2150, B2250 blades + VIPRION C2400, C2200 chassis + BIG-IP 2000-series, 4000-series, 5000-series, 7000-series, 10000-series, 12000-series appliances + BIG-IP 800, 1600, 1600 LC, 3600, 3900, 6900-series, 8900-series, 11000-series appliances + EM 4000 appliances -- Using the following commands to clear alerts from the LCD display or reset the Alarm LED: tmsh reset-stats sys alert lcd lcdwarn -c <level> [<blade>]
bugs.impact: The alarm state does not clear. The Alarm LED may indicate a previous alert state that has been acknowledged/cleared and is no longer accurate.
bugs.workaround: It may be possible to work around this issue using either of the following procedures: -- Clear the LCD alert messages by pressing the appropriate buttons on the front panel LCD display itself. -- Restart the fpdd daemon: bigstart restart fpdd Otherwise, rebooting the BIG-IP system restores the correct LED states.
bugs.fix: Clearing LCD alert messages from the TMOS console successfully clears alert messages from the LCD display and restores the Alarm LED to the correct status.

bugs.title: No support for server-side TLS SNI
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system is unable to perform server-side SNI without using an iRule.
bugs.conditions: -- Server-side pool members are configured to use TLS SNI. -- More than one valid server name exists.
bugs.impact: You must write an iRule that dynamically selects a server SSL profile based on the client host header.
bugs.fix: A new parameter has been added to the virtual server called 'serverssl-use-sni'. If multiple server SSL profiles are configured, and serverssl-use-sni is enabled, then the server SSL profile whose server-name matches the SNI extension in ClientHello will be selected. In the example below, server SSL profile s.1 will be used by default, unless the client connects using the SNI 'valid-client', in which case profile s.2 will be used. ltm profile server-ssl s.1 { app-service none cipher-group none ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 server-name none sni-default true } ltm profile server-ssl s.2 { app-service none cipher-group none ciphers DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 server-name valid-client session-ticket enabled } ltm virtual tls { destination 10.98.22.213:https ip-protocol tcp mask 255.255.255.255 pool ssl profiles { c.1 { context clientside } s.1 { context serverside } s.2 { context serverside } tcp { } } serverssl-use-sni enabled source 0.0.0.0/0 source-address-translation { type automap } }

bugs.title: TMM may core during ILX RPC activity if a connflow closes before the RPC returns
bugs.symptoms: TMM core with plugin context refcount error.
bugs.conditions: Using ILX RPC calls. Most likely to occur when using a low end box or virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: ILX plugin timeout no longer causes TMM core.

bugs.title: Mcpd core dump in the sync secondary during config sync
bugs.symptoms: mcpd will crash if certain files are missing from the file store during sync operations.
bugs.conditions: This can happen when files associated with file objects are removed from the file store. Users are not permitted to directly modify the contents of the file store.
bugs.impact: mcpd will crash
bugs.workaround: Users are not permitted to directly modify the contents of the file store. Use tmsh or the Configuration Utility to manage BIG-IP objects such certificates.
bugs.fix: Mcpd will no longer crash during a config sync if a file store object is missing.

bugs.title: "Request violation" details are blank in /var/log/asm
bugs.symptoms: "Request violation" details are blank in /var/log/asm
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: "Request violation" details are blank in /var/log/asm
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: Staging is not disabled on wildcard parameter "*" when Learn New Parameters is set to "Add All"
bugs.symptoms: Staging is not disabled on wildcard parameter "*" when Learn New Parameters is set to "Add All Entities".
bugs.conditions: Learn New Parameters is set to "Add All Entities".
bugs.impact: Staging on wildcard parameter "*" remains unchanged.
bugs.workaround: Disable staging on wildcard parameter "*" manually.
bugs.fix: Staging is now disabled correctly on wildcard parameter "*" when Learn New Parameters is set to "Add All Entities".

bugs.title: AVR reads BIG-IP system's cookie incorrectly in multiple BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.symptoms: AVR presents incorrect data in the GUI statistics (for example, unexpected pool members, and so on, with hitcount 0).
bugs.conditions: Multiple BIG-IP systems are configured, one is acting as server for the other and both have 'collect client latency' enabled.
bugs.impact: Invalid data is presented in the statistics.
bugs.workaround: Turn off 'collect client latency' in the AVR profile on the BIG-IP system that is acting as the server.
bugs.fix: Correct data is now presented in the statistics of a configuration in which one BIG-IP system is acting as the server in a multiple BIG-IP device configuration.

bugs.title: High Speed Logging to specific destinations stops from individual TMMs
bugs.symptoms: High Speed Logging to specific destinations stops from individual TMMs. The flows appear to have very large idle times. Attempts to delete the flows sets the idle time to zero, but does not kill the flow.
bugs.conditions: This appears to be the result of a failure on the part of the log destination (for example, a log server) wherein the server's TCP stack ACKs a FIN request from the TMM, but does not follow through with a matching FIN or RST. The logging code expects another timeout (essentially a FIN-WAIT2 timeout), but never receives one because the flow has already been marked as expired. As a result, the flow goes into a state in which it appears to be viable but is not actually delivering.
bugs.impact: Logs are silently lost.
bugs.workaround: Create an additional virtual server to act as a proxy for the log server, and sent the logs to this virtual server. This essentially uses the TMM itself as a sanitizing proxy.
bugs.fix: The system now resets the expire timer when it initiates the close. If the server fails to reset or complete the close, the flow is aborted on the next expiration event.

bugs.title: Tunnel details are not shown for MAC Edge client
bugs.symptoms: Tunnel details are not shown for MAC Edge client. Tunnel details are located in Edge client :: View details :: Connection :: Tunnel details
bugs.conditions: MAC Edge client and established network access connection.
bugs.impact: Minor. Only diagnostic information is missing, otherwise tunnel works fine.
bugs.fix: Tunnel details are now shown for MAC Edge client.

bugs.title: Unable to Import Certificate to a partition subfolder, message: Name cannot contain '/' nor '\'.
bugs.symptoms: UI prevents importing to sub-partitions a certificate with a forward slash in the name.
bugs.conditions: Create a sub-partition such as /Test/MyPartition and import a certificate with name /Test/MyPartition/myCertificate to target the /Test/MyPartition.
bugs.impact: Import operation fails. The system posts the following error: Name cannot contain '/' nor '\'. User cannot use the GUI to import a certificate in a sub partition.
bugs.workaround: For a certificate with a forward slash in the name, use tmsh to import it to a sub partition.

bugs.title: Luna FIPS request errors are logged as the same generic error.
bugs.symptoms: Whenever the Luna FIPS card firmware returns any error resulting from an asynchronous request, it sets the status to ERR_HSM_ERROR (0x40000116) and the FIPS driver logs the error. This behavior hides the true fault as there is no indication of the actual error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs whenever an error is returned as the result of an asynchronous FIPS request to the Luna FIPS device.
bugs.impact: The actual error reported by the Luna FIPS device firmware is never logged, preventing analysis of FIPS issues on Luna equipped platforms.
bugs.fix: Fixed FIPS module for Luna device to report HSM error when request completion status is ERR_HSM_ERROR and log non-fatal FIPS errors at warning level.

bugs.title: Update Generic Malware Signatures to detect new Dyre variant
bugs.symptoms: The generic malware signatures aren't detecting a new Dyre variant.
bugs.conditions: Dyre detection.
bugs.impact: Systems targeted by the new Dyre variant will not receive alerts from the FPS module when attacked.
bugs.fix: Detect the new Dyre variant with an updated generic malware signature.

bugs.title: Linux CLI VPN client fails to establish VPN connection on Ubuntu
bugs.symptoms: Linux client is unable to establish a VPN connection. An error is displayed which says that server certificate verification has failed.
bugs.conditions: CLI client used on Ubuntu to establish VPN connection.
bugs.impact: User cannot connect to VPN
bugs.workaround: Use web client.
bugs.fix: Fixed bug in certificate verification code.

bugs.title: [PORTAL] JavaScript errors when Application runs through Portal
bugs.symptoms: [Portal Access] Wrong rewriting for some nested conditional expressions at client side. For example, "x?w.location=y?a:b:c;"
bugs.conditions: Application running through Portal has javascript errors causing page not to load.
bugs.impact: Page not load.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround available upon request. iRule will specific to the wep application behind BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Iframes could be inaccessible to a parent window on a page accessed through Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: document.write from window to iframe could silently fail, if page is accessed by FQDN, and Same Origin Policy restrictions were relaxed with assignment to a document.domain. The code on the page will be executed without errors, but no content will appear in iframe.
bugs.impact: Some content could be not displayed on a page accessed through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround specific to a web application
bugs.conditions: This can occur with web applications that use heavy javascript including javascript across iFrames.
bugs.fix: Now iFrame with empty origin inherits origin value from parent window being accessed via Portal Access in the same manner as all browsers do.

bugs.title: Network Access fails on Windows platform
bugs.symptoms: Network Access fails on Windows platform when a Java AppTunnel resource has been assigned in Access Policy.
bugs.conditions: Windows clients connecting through Network Access VPN, and Java AppTunnel configured with local-ip setting
bugs.impact: Network Access fails on Windows platform, with the error message "Internal Error".
bugs.fix: Network Access works as expected on Windows platform even a Java AppTunnel resource has been assigned.

bugs.title: Subscriber ID type should be set to NAI over Diameter for DHCP discovered subscribers
bugs.symptoms: CCR-I requests from PEM to PCRF contain subscriber ID type is set to 6 (UNKNOWN) for DHCP subscribers instead of NAI.
bugs.conditions: Occurs for DHCP discovered subscribers on a BIG-IP system that uses a PCRF for policy determination.
bugs.impact: Might impact the way policies are provided from the PCRF.
bugs.fix: Subscrbier ID type is marked as NAI for DHCP discovered subscribers.

bugs.title: Client initiated form based SSO fails when username and password not replaced correctly while posting the form
bugs.symptoms: Client initiated form based SSO fails when the username and password are not replaced correctly in post request. The reason for this is that client initiated form based SSO and browser urlencode special character in username/password differently. and the case sensitive comparison fails to find match between both these urlencoded values. So sso module adds the username password to the token again. This results in password attribute/value pair appears twice with both the f5-sso-token and the real password and so it fails
bugs.conditions: When the password contains special charaters like [ or ]
bugs.impact: SSO fails with password attribute/value pair appears twice with both the f5-sso-token and the real password in the token and so it fails
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Not fixed yet.

bugs.title: ICAP anti virus tests are not initiated on XML with when should
bugs.symptoms: ICAP anti virus tests are not performed on XML with sensitive data.
bugs.conditions: ICAP and XML profile are configured on the policy, the ICAP configured to inspect the XML. The XML has sensitive data configured. The XML request contained sensitive data. The expectation was that XML with sensitive data would initiate ICAP tests.
bugs.impact: Virus tests will not be enabled on this request if the only reason for testing the ICAP was the existence of the sensitive XML data.
bugs.fix: ICAP tests are performed on XML with sensitive data.

bugs.title: CHD congestion control can have erroneous very large cwnd.
bugs.symptoms: At times, CHD congestion control can store a very large congestion window, resulting in release of data well beyond that warranted by network conditions.
bugs.conditions: The client advertises a receive window less than 1 MSS, and CHD tries to decrease the window.
bugs.impact: Possible network congestion.
bugs.workaround: Change congestion control algoirhtm from CHD.

bugs.title: Temporary negative bit-count on mgmt interface after LBH reset
bugs.symptoms: Temporary negative bit-count on mgmt interface after LBH reset.
bugs.conditions: Reset stats and an AOM reset.
bugs.impact: Minimal. After some traffic is passed via the mgmt interface, it comes back into the positive.

bugs.title: tmsh list/save configuration takes a long time when config contains nested objects.
bugs.symptoms: A configuration containing a number of nested objects takes a long time to list or save. For example, the tmsh listing time for a ~2 MB config can exceed 30 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Following is an example of nested objects in a config. If the config contains thousands of such virtual servers, it might take longer than 30 seconds to run either of the following commands: -- tmsh list ltm virtual. -- tmsh save config. ltm virtual vs { destination 10.10.10.10:http ip-protocol tcp mask 255.255.255.255 profiles { ::: nested object http { } http_security { } tcp { } } source 0.0.0.0/0 translate-address enabled translate-port enabled vs-index 26 } .
bugs.impact: When commands take longer than 30 seconds to complete, iControlREST times out.
bugs.fix: A configuration containing a number of nested objects no longer takes a long time to list or save, so iControlREST no longer times out. Note: You might still encounter this issue in configurations that have greater than ~6000 nested objects, which is the largest number tested.

bugs.title: Post RMA, system does not display correct platform name regardless of license
bugs.symptoms: When you get an RMA and you are licensed for a 4000 and the unit received has been licensed as a 4200, you will have a difference between hardware on site and the new hardware received, regardless of what license you have.
bugs.conditions: Take a 4000 from manufacturing and license it for a 4200 wipe system and rebuild and license for a 4000 and tmsh show sys hardware and device groups will indicate it to be a 4200 if you have a 4200 from manufacturing and license it as a 4000 it will still indicate that it is a 4200 Affected platforms is following 2000/2200 4000/4200 5000/5200 7000/7200 10000/10200
bugs.impact: Confusion as to what the actual platform is

bugs.title: DNS queries with OPT have no OPT in response for RFC 6891 compliance.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP DNS does not include an OPT record in responses to received requests that contain OPT records.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following condition is met: -- The query includes OPT.
bugs.impact: A resolver, not seeing an OPT, might interprets this as a lack of support and might send duplicate TCP requests.
bugs.fix: DNS queries with OPT now have OPT in response for RFC 6891 compliance. This fix also corrects other commonly found compliance issues with regard to EDNS handling as specified in clarifying RFC 6891.

bugs.title: Misleading error message in catalina.out when listing certificates.
bugs.symptoms: GUI logs 'Table not found' in catalina.out when some exceptions are returned before/at table creation. The exceptions are the actual cause of the failure. java.sql.SQLException: Table not found: SSL_CERTIFICATES_0_1652477104084229 in statement [DROP TABLE ssl_certificates_0_1652477104084229].
bugs.conditions: This occurs when listing certificates, and exceptions are returned.
bugs.impact: 1. Throws table creation exceptions when randomly generated table name contains invalid character ('-'). 2. Misleading 'Table not found" message in catalina.out.
bugs.workaround: Refreshing the page might fix the invalid table name issue because doing so generates a new table name. In some situations a restart of tomcat and httpd may be required.
bugs.fix: Errors occur when listing certificates that contain invalid characters from the randomly generated table names, so the GUI logs 'Table not found' in catalina.out when some exceptions are returned before/at table creation.

bugs.title: Device rename on standalone device will cause it to momentarily go offline
bugs.symptoms: If the DSC sync device object is renamed on a standalone configuration, the system posts a log message indicating that the device is going momentarily offline for traffic-group-1. That message looks like this: -- notice sod[...]: 010c0056:5: Deactivating traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1. -- notice sod[...]: 010c0057:5: Activating traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1. -- notice sod[...]: 010c0054:5: Offline for traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1. notice sod[...]: 010c006d:5: Leaving Offline for Active for dbvar not redundant. -- notice sod[...]: 010c0053:5: Active for traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1. This action is illegal if the device is part of a device trust group. On standalone configurations, setting the hostname through the GUI also implicitly renames the self device.
bugs.conditions: This happens only when the device is not in trust with any other devices. There is no impact unless it occurs on a vCMP hypervisor.
bugs.impact: If this happens on a vCMP hypervisor, then guests on that chassis may momentarily go offline due to an HA table entry tripping: warning chmand[...]: 012a0004:4: hypervisor_offline take action is set warning sod[...]: 01140029:4: HA hypervisor_offline_t chmand fails action is go offline. On devices that are not vCMP hypervisors, there is no impact to traffic. sod going offline for a traffic group does not stop traffic when the device is configured as standalone. The GUI shows this behavior only when the device is configured as standalone.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for renaming the self device. The hostname can be changed using tmsh ('modify sys global-settings hostname new-hostname.com'), which unlike the GUI does not rename the self device.

bugs.title: Nondescriptive error when an application template upload fails on iApp load.
bugs.symptoms: Nondescriptive error when an application template upload fails on iApp load. The system posts a message similar to the following: Loading configuration... /tmp/upload_template.tmpl Syntax Error:(/tmp/upload_template.tmpl at line: 1) "PK" unexpected argument
bugs.conditions: Uploading an incorrect file (e.g., a zip file instead of an iApp template).
bugs.impact: Difficult to determine the problem.

bugs.title: Corrupt MCP message causes crash in MCPConnection::sendMessage
bugs.symptoms: MCPd produces a core from both blades of 2 blade guest after running 'tmsh show sys conn' a few times.
bugs.conditions: Unknown
bugs.impact: Failover

bugs.title: tmm might leak memory on vCMP guest in SSL forward proxy
bugs.symptoms: In SSL forward proxy configuration on vCMP guest tmm might slowly leak memory when subjected to SSL Hello messages containing server name extension (SNI) that is not configured on the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with the following conditions are met: -- SSL forward proxy configuration. -- SSL hello with SNI extension.
bugs.impact: tmm might leak memory
bugs.fix: tmm no longer leaks leak memory on the vCMP guest in SSL forward proxy configurations.

bugs.title: Changing hostname on host sometimes causes blade to go RED / HA TABLE offline
bugs.symptoms: If the UI System::Platform screen is used to change the hostname on a Standalone VIPRION, the non-primary blades in the chassis may temporarily report an offline state.
bugs.conditions: This affects only multi-blade chassis systems in Standalone mode.
bugs.impact: If the system is hosting vCMP guests, it may cause unexpected failovers, and interruption of traffic.
bugs.workaround: To change the hostname on the VIPRION, use the tmsh command: 'modify sys global-settings hostname new-host-name'.
bugs.fix: Changing hostname on Standalone VIPRION no longer causes the non-primary blade to go RED / HA TABLE offline.

bugs.title: tmm core on long DIAMETER::host value
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes and restarts when an iRule is accessed that contains a large DIAMETER::host value.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with a DIAMETER::host iRule parameter set to a very large value (2000 characters).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Limit the length of the DIAMETER::host parameter to less than 1000 characters.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now limits the DIAMETER::host parameter to 1000 characters.

bugs.title: Session deleted and session statistics messages are logged with wrong partition
bugs.symptoms: For a user session in another partition, the session deleted and session statistics messages are logged with partition Common.
bugs.conditions: Access policy and virtual server in one partition, say "p1". User session is created on the p1 virtual server. Logs are turned on.
bugs.impact: Admin will see misleading information regarding the appropriate partition in the session deleted and session statistics messages.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Nitrox can hang on RSA verification
bugs.symptoms: With certain signatures, RSA verification can hang the Nitrox crypto accelerator chip. Errors in the ltm log show crit tmm[11041]: 01010260:2: Hardware Error(Co-Processor): n3-crypto2 request queue stuck
bugs.conditions: RSA verification with certain signatures.
bugs.impact: Nitrox crypto accelerator can hang.
bugs.fix: The Nitrox crypto accelerator will no longer hang when performing RSA verification.

bugs.title: Changing the username or password used for HTTP monitor basic auth may break HTTP basic auth
bugs.symptoms: HTTP basic authentication uses a base64 encoded string. When an HTTP monitor username or password is changed, the b64 string is regenerated and may become malformed.
bugs.conditions: When an http monitor username or password is changed, e.g. shortened, then the HTTP basic auth string may be mangled.
bugs.impact: An HTTP monitor may show its resource as unavailable after changing the username or password.
bugs.workaround: Restart big3d, or delete then recreate the monitor instead of modifying the existing monitor.
bugs.fix: HTTP monitors will now correctly handle a username or password change.

bugs.title: Change console baud rate requires reboot to take effect
bugs.symptoms: When you change the console baud rate, you will see garbage characters.
bugs.conditions: When you make modification to the console baud rate.
bugs.impact: The console display has garbage characters.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system.
bugs.fix: Console baud rate change now works.

bugs.title: Serverside nexthop info not available
bugs.symptoms: There is no info available for server nexthop (VLAN, MAC address).
bugs.conditions: Running the TMSH command: tmsh show sys conn all-properties
bugs.impact: No info regarding server nexthop. Troubleshooting asymmetric routing deployments is more difficult.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Command 'tmsh show sys conn all-properties' shows VLAN and MAC address of server nexthop.

bugs.title: Default obfuscator configuration causes very slow javascript in some browsers
bugs.symptoms: Slow javascript causes page to render with a slight delay.
bugs.conditions: FPS enabled on highly optimized web page
bugs.impact: Mainly on older browsers, a slight rendering delay (~1 second) may be noticed.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands on the BIG-IP system: echo "-x" > /shared/datasync/compiler_conf/cs_fpm/OBF_FLAGS chattr +i /shared/datasync/compiler_conf/cs_fpm/OBF_FLAGS
bugs.fix: Improved performance of obfuscated javascript.

bugs.title: Client capabilities failure
bugs.symptoms: In some cases client capabilities detection may fail, crashing TMM.
bugs.conditions: AVR and/or AAM provisioned and configured
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts
bugs.fix: Improve processing of client capabilities

bugs.title: Monpd is being affected by an I/O issue which makes some of its threads freeze
bugs.symptoms: When Monpd is restarted, it starts printing non-stop error message to logs. Analytics statistics may be lost, and new data cannot be loaded. The ltm log contains this error signature - err stat_bridge_thread[8278]: monpd`ERR`date`11285` [stat_bridge_thread::validateCorrectNumberOfPartitions, ] Too many partitions (44) defined for DB table AVR_STAT_DISK_T
bugs.conditions: A system I/O issue (maybe caused by /var/log being full).
bugs.impact: AVR statistics are lost. Monpd thread cannot load new data, and it prints non-stop error messages to the logs.
bugs.workaround: Run the following: find /var/avr/loader/ -mindepth 1 -name "*" -print0 | xargs -0 rm touch /var/avr/init_avrdb bigstart restart monpd

bugs.title: Missing partition and subPath fields for some objects in iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: When using iControl REST, the return output of some objects does not include the partition and subPath properties. Also the name property contains the full path instead of only the object name.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running BIG-IP systems with 11.6.0 HF6 installed.
bugs.impact: This breaks custom scripts that rely on those properties.
bugs.workaround: Do not use custom scripts to gather the partition and subPath properties of objects on BIG-IP systems with 11.6.0 HF6 installed.

bugs.title: Pipelined requests may result in a RST if the server disconnects
bugs.symptoms: If a HTTP client sends multiple pipelined requests before a full response is received, the HTTP filter will buffer them, and send them one at a time to the server. If the server ends via a "Connection: Close" the HTTP filter will ignore this, and continue to send the next buffered request. If the server then sends a FIN packet while that buffered request is in progress, the HTTP filter will send a RST packet to the client.
bugs.conditions: Multiple concurrent pipelined HTTP requests, and a back-end server that closes a connection while some requests are still buffered. Oneconnect is not used.
bugs.impact: The client will receive a RST instead of a FIN packet.
bugs.workaround: There are two work-arounds. 1) Enable one-connect. 2) via iRule. If a "Connection: close" header exists in the HTTP_RESPONSE event, then HTTP::close may be used to cleanly shut the connection down.

bugs.title: vCMP guest cluster may have two primaries due to partial partitioning of the management backplane network on one cluster member
bugs.symptoms: The management backplane network on one cluster member of a vCMP guest may partially malfunction in that multicast packets are able to be sent out of the cluster member but incoming multicast packets from the peer members are dropped. This results in the cluster becoming "split-brained" and having two primary members; the original primary remains so while the isolated member also elects itself as a primary.
bugs.conditions: This issue only occurs on vCMP guest clusters and has been found to only happen in extremely rare cases.
bugs.impact: Dataplane traffic remains unaffected. However, configuration changes will not propagated to the isolated cluster member, and stats will not be synced from the isolated cluster member. Furthermore, if the cluster is the active unit in an HA pair, this may result in a failover not occurring as expected due to the technical nature of the malfunction.
bugs.workaround: To resolve the issue, reboot the cluster member whose management backplane has malfunctioned.

bugs.title: Optional target IP address and port in the 'virtual' iRule API is not supported.
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios there is a need to redirect an HTTP request through a given virtual server to a another virtual server (or remote endpoint). Such an operation is also known as 'vip-to-vip' forwarding. The available iRule API (specifically, the 'virtual' command) does not currently support this functionality.
bugs.conditions: Using an iRule to forward a request through a given virtual server to another virtual server or remote endpoint.
bugs.impact: Cannot implement HTTP Forward Proxy plus Transparent redirection to Web-Cache Pool.
bugs.behavior: The 'virtual' iRule API has been changed to support a secondary target IP address and port to redirect the connection to, from a given virtual server. The new signature of the 'virtual' iRule API is: virtual [<name>] [<ipaddr> [<port>]] where: <name> = the name of the virtual server to redirect the connection from <ipaddr> = the target IP address of the remote endpoint to route the connection to, through the specified virtual server; <ipaddr> can also have a route-domain (%) <port> = the port of the remote endpoint to route the connection to, through the specified virtual server

bugs.title: VxLAN tunnel IP address modification is not supported
bugs.symptoms: VxLAN tunnel local and remote tunnel IP address change is not supported.
bugs.conditions: If a user tries to change the local and/or remote tunnel IP address, the configuration handler will fail the configuration change.
bugs.impact: The user must delete and recreate the VxLAN tunnel in order to change the tunnel local and/or remote address. Tunnel deletion also requires removing references to the tunnel, for example the tunnel self IP address and routes pointing to the tunnel, before the tunnel can be deleted. Those self IP addresses and routes must be re-added after recreating the tunnel with changed IP address parameters. This can be error-prone, especially if the number of tunnels is extremely large.
bugs.workaround: Delete existing VxLAN tunnel, and add a new tunnel with the modified tunnel IP address parameters.
bugs.fix: Modifying VxLAN tunnel IP addresses now works. Only tunnels that have been created with a multicast flooding type and have a multicast remote IP address are supported.

bugs.title: LTM iRule table set command cannot always set value of record with extremely short timeout
bugs.symptoms: If you have a record with an extremely low timeout value and you attempt to constantly set/reset the value, you may intermittently attempt to access the record while it is expired, in which case the value you attempt to set it to is not accepted.
bugs.conditions: Using table set command with a timeout of less than 8 seconds.
bugs.impact: iRule operates incorrectly
bugs.workaround: Refresh the timeout on the entry before attempting to set it, via table lookup.

bugs.title: Changing the monitor configuration of a pool can cause the virtual server to be briefly logged as down
bugs.symptoms: Changing the monitor configuration of a pool can cause the virtual server to be briefly logged as down.
bugs.conditions: Changing the monitor configuration of a pool. For example: tmsh modify ltm pool http-pool monitor http and tcp tmsh modify ltm pool http-pool monitor min 1 of { http tcp }
bugs.impact: Virtual server may be incorrectly marked down, when it should not be.
bugs.fix: Changing the monitor configuration of a pool no longer causes the virtual server to be marked as down.

bugs.title: Invalid /etc/resolv.conf when more than one DNS servers are set and MCPD is down.
bugs.symptoms: When MCPD is not in the running state, dhclient directly writes domain-name-server information into /etc/resolv.conf. If multiple domain-name-servers are given by DHCP server, they are written in the incorrect format with multiple domain-name-servers in a single line comma-separated. Each domain-name-servers entry should be written in a single line with "nameserver" prefix.
bugs.conditions: - MCPD is not in the running state. - DHCP is enabled. - DHCP server has provided multiple domain-name-server entries in the lease.
bugs.impact: Domain name resolution doesn't work.
bugs.workaround: Bring up MCPD which would write the resolv.conf in the correct format. Alternatively, user can manually modify /etc/resolv.conf to write multiple nameserver entry one per line.
bugs.fix: DHCP will now write a single nameserver per line in /etc/resolv.conf when multiple nameservers are configured in DHCP.

bugs.title: Disabling an IKE Peer sets all Common Settings values to default
bugs.symptoms: When an existing "Enabled" IKE Peer has its "State" attribute changed to "Disabled" the value of all of the attributes in the Common Settings table are set to their default values.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when setting the state of an IKE peer to Disabled.
bugs.impact: When an existing "Enabled" IKE Peer temporarily has its "State" attribute changed to "Disabled" then later reset to "Enabled", any non-default settings in the Common Settings table are lost.
bugs.workaround: Re-enter any non-default values in the Common Settings table when re-enabling and IKE Peer.

bugs.title: HTML5 File API and MediaSource URLs are blocked in Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Web Application is not working and a message similar to following is logged to the developer tools console in the browser: "Refused to load media from 'blob:https://...' because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: ..."
bugs.conditions: This occurs on web applications that are using the HTML5 file API
bugs.impact: Applications with usage of HTML5 File API could stop working when accessed via APM Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { if { [HTTP::header exists Content-Security-Policy] } { HTTP::header replace Content-Security-Policy \ [string map {"data:" "data: blob: mediasource: mediastream:"} [HTTP::header Content-Security-Policy]] } }
bugs.fix: blob: and mediasource: URL schemes are now allowed on pages accessed through APM Portal Access.

bugs.title: Resource Limitation error when removing predefined policy which has multiple rules
bugs.symptoms: Resource Limitation error when removing a predefined policy which has multiple rules referring to the same rating group.
bugs.conditions: - Gx and Gy are configured for the session - All rules refer to the same rating group
bugs.impact: Unable to remove an existing policy
bugs.fix: Policies can be removed and updated regardless of rules or rating group limitations.

bugs.title: The REST Framework no longer works when downgrading from BIG-IP version 12.x or 13.x to 11.6.x or 11.5.x
bugs.symptoms: After activating an earlier software version (by downgrading from a later version, or any other means) from BIG-IP version 12.x or 13.x to 11.6.x or 11.5.x, the REST Framework no longer works. At this time, iControl REST requests issued against the BIG-IP system return a 404 HTTP status code. Additionally, the BIG-IP system logs messages similar to the following example to the /var/log/httpd/httpd_errors file: Dec 3 15:57:51 localhost err httpd[14486]: [error] [client 192.168.94.48] File does not exist: /usr/local/www/mgmt
bugs.conditions: - Upgrading the BIG-IP system to version 12.x or 13.x and then activating a previous boot location containing 11.5.x or 11.6.x. - Utilizing iControl REST.
bugs.impact: iControl REST does not work on the older software version. Note: If you boot back into the version 12.x or 13.x slot, iControl REST functionality returns.
bugs.workaround: To recover from this issue and restore iControl REST functionality on the older software version, run the following command: rm -fv /shared/lib/rpm/* && reboot Note: On a VIPRION or vCMP system with multiple blades, you should run "clsh 'rm -fv /shared/lib/rpm/* && reboot'" instead, so that all blades are fixed and the system will work regardless of which blade becomes primary after the reboot.

bugs.title: HA IPSEC: tmm core/crash on standby in function ikev2_child_delete_outbound()
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash after a number of failovers (approximately two to four).
bugs.conditions: This occurs in a high availability (HA) configuration with IPSEC traffic and multiple failovers. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The intermittent tmm crash no longer occurs in a high availability (HA) configuration with IPSEC traffic and multiple failovers.

bugs.title: TMM may crash with 'tmsh show sys conn'.
bugs.symptoms: Although unlikely, the 'tmsh show sys conn' command may cause the tmm process to crash when displaying connections.
bugs.conditions: Although the conditions under which this occurs are not well understood, this is a rarely occurring issue.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to not issue the command: tmsh show sys conn.
bugs.fix: Running the command 'tmsh show sys conn' no longer causes TMM to crash when displaying connections.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ discovery fails
bugs.symptoms: After updating attack signatures, a Signature-system called "IBM WebSphere" may be created that does not contain a REST ID, and BIG-IQ will fail discovery. If you look at the REST output for this item at https://bigip_address/mgmt/tm/asm/signature-systems/ and look for "IBM WebSphere", you will see that the id field is empty.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when updating attack signatures, and when using BIG-IQ discovery.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ discovery fails.
bugs.workaround: On the affected device run the following: perl -MF5::Utils::Rest -MF5::DbUtils -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::SignatureSystem -e "F5::Utils::Rest::populate_uuids(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), rest_entities => ['F5::ASMConfig::Entity::SignatureSystem'])"
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with attack signature updates causing BIG-IQ discovery to fail.

bugs.title: FPS doesn't encrypt inputs of type "hidden"
bugs.symptoms: FPS doesn't encrypt inputs of type "hidden"
bugs.conditions: HTML input element of type "hidden" needs encrypting.
bugs.impact: Unable to support some applications
bugs.fix: FPS now encrypts all input types, including the 'hidden' type.

bugs.title: ICC may handle incorrectly when used with IEMobile client
bugs.symptoms: When IEMobile client connects to BIG-IP with AAM policy where ICC is enabled, the client may receive an incorrect response.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has AAM provisioned and a policy with ICC enabled is attached to a virtual. IEMobile client connects via this virtual.
bugs.impact: A page may be rendered incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: Disabled ICC.

bugs.title: TMM crash when deleting several thousands of address-list objects with address-list references on VE using the command 'tmsh delete security firewall address-list all'.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when deleting several thousands of address-list objects with address-list references on VE using the command 'tmsh delete security firewall address-list all'.
bugs.conditions: 1. This happens when there are a lot of address-lists to be deleted (3000 or more). 2. All the address lists need to be deleted in one shot using the command 'tmsh delete security firewall address-list all'.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Delete the address-lists in batches.

bugs.title: Some User-Agent strings are parsed incorrectly resulting in a wrong browser family
bugs.symptoms: When AM is configured for image optimization it may require to determine browser type to allow browser-specific optimizations. Incorrect browser family may result in using of an inapplicable optimization. For example, if Internet Explorer is recognized as Chrome, it may be served with an optimized image in WEBP format instead of JPEG.
bugs.conditions: An optimization is configured in AM policy requiring a browser specific optimization, e.g. image optimization.
bugs.impact: The client's browser may not render the page correctly.
bugs.workaround: Disable the appropriate optimization.

bugs.title: LTM policy is unable to disable SNAT
bugs.symptoms: The SNAT feature of an LTM policy used two keywords, 'automap' and 'none', to configure SNAT as automap or disabled, respectively. It turns out that the keyword 'none' has special meaning in tmsh, and is treated as an invalid value.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy with automap action. -- Attempt to disable SNAT from either GUI or tmsh using the value 'none'.
bugs.impact: Cannot disable SNAT using LTM policy.
bugs.workaround: Remove the SNAT action from LTM policy, and use an iRule instead.
bugs.fix: LTM policy can now successfully disable SNAT.

bugs.title: iControl can remove hardware SSL keys while in use
bugs.symptoms: When deleting SSL keys via iControl it is possible to delete keys from the Hardware Security Module even while they are configured in an active profile.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl to delete SSL key installed in hardware.
bugs.impact: Key is removed from HSM and must be reloaded.
bugs.workaround: Verify that keys are not in use before using iControl to delete them.

bugs.title: krb5.conf file is not synchronized between blades and not backed up
bugs.symptoms: krb5.conf file is not in sync across all blades. this may cause a feature (Kerberos SSO / Kerberos Auth) to not work as expected.
bugs.conditions: When administrator made changes to krb5.conf file manually, the configuration file is not synchronized to all blades or is lost upon upgrade.
bugs.impact: Kerberos Auth / Kerberos SSO does not work properly on all blades.
bugs.fix: The APM code now automatically synchronizes the changes to /etc/krb5.conf file to all devices in the Failover Device group. Any change made to this file either in Active Device or Standby device will be automatically synced to other device. In Chassis, all the Secondary blades will mirror the file on the Primary blade. Any manual change done on the Secondary blade(s) will be lost. The admin has to do the changes on Primary blade only and it will be synchronized with all others blades.
bugs.behavior: When admin modifies /etc/krb5.conf file, the changes are automatically updated on other devices in the same Failover Device group. When admin modifies the /etc/krb5.conf file on the primary blade of the chassis, the changes are automatically updated on all secondary blades.

bugs.title: TMM Packets can be dropped indiscriminately while under DoS attack
bugs.symptoms: When there is a loaded tmm that cannot consume packets fast enough, packets might be dropped while when AFM DoS flood mitigation is taking place.
