bugs.conditions: -- Loaded tmm that cannot consume packets fast enough. -- AFM DoS flood mitigation is taking place.
bugs.impact: Packets will be dropped indiscriminately.
bugs.fix: There is now a sys db tunable (sys db dos.scrubtime) which can be set to drop DoS attack packets in hardware more aggressively. This will prevent other non-attack packets from being dropped indiscriminately.

bugs.title: LCD might display incorrect output.
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect LCD display due to garbled messages received from LCD panel.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in various situations. Multiple messages sent to LCD and user interaction on LCD seem to reproduce the issue.
bugs.impact: LCD may display incorrect data.
bugs.workaround: The LCD usually corrects itself eventually, but to restore it immediately to a good state, run the following command: bigstart restart fpdd.
bugs.fix: The issue allowing garbled messages between the front panel display daemon (fpdd) and the LCD daemon (LCDd) is now prevented from happening.

bugs.title: ICAP Parsing improvement
bugs.symptoms: If a malformed ICAP message is sent to the Big-IP the ICAP parser can enter a state where it consumes an increasing amount of CPU and memory.
bugs.conditions: A request-adapt or response-adapt profile is configured. An ICAP message is received from an ICAP server lacking "ICAP/1.0" as initial header line.
bugs.impact: Memory and CPU usage increase. Eventually the TMM may crash causing Big-IP fail-over.
bugs.fix: ICAP parser checks for correct initial ICAP/1.0 header line and rejects message if missing.

bugs.title: [Upgrade] GTM pool member ratio setting to 0 is not honored when upgrading from v10.2.4 to v11.5.3.
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from 10.x to 11.x Wide IP pool member ratio value is changed from 0 to 1.
bugs.conditions: 1. Upgrade from v10.x to v11.x through 12.0.0 2. Have a Wide IP pool member ratio set to 0.
bugs.impact: Wide IP pool member ratio is changed to 1 (the default) from 0 after upgrading, potentially enabling selection of members that had been "disabled" with a ratio of 0.
bugs.workaround: Manually change ratio back to 0 after upgrade.

bugs.title: Hotfixes can update FPS engine file
bugs.symptoms: Previously, to receive a full solution that required changes on the FPS BIG-IP side and FPS client-side, both a hotfix and a live update were required.
bugs.conditions: FPS hotfix
bugs.impact: You have to install both the hotfix and the engine update
bugs.workaround: Install live update separately
bugs.fix: Hotfix can now update the FPS javascript engine

bugs.title: Guest user cannot see Event Correlation details
bugs.symptoms: Guest user cannot see Event Correlation details.
bugs.conditions: Log in as Guest
bugs.impact: Limited read access for guest users.
bugs.workaround: For guest user - there is no workaround, but if it is possible to log in as another user - then everything works.

bugs.title: Hotfixes can optionally update FPS engine file
bugs.symptoms: Previously, to receive a full solution that required changes on the FPS BIG-IP side and FPS client-side, both a hotfix and a live update were required.
bugs.conditions: FPS hotfix
bugs.impact: No ability to opt in/out of engine and signature changes from the hotfix
bugs.fix: Two new DB variables to enable/disabled taking update from hotfix: datasync.update_engine_from_factory datasync.update_signatures_from_factory

bugs.title: Realtime encryption causes high CPU usage in older browsers
bugs.symptoms: When encrypting using realtime encryption, CPU usage on the browser rises very high
bugs.conditions: Client: Internet Explorer 8 or below FPS: Configured to encrypt password using realtime encryption
bugs.impact: In extreme cases, browser may prompt user to stop the encryption script.
bugs.workaround: Disable realtime encryption in your anti-fraud policy.
bugs.fix: Improved performance of realtime encryption

bugs.title: Windows edge client may show scripting error on certain 3rd party authentication sites
bugs.symptoms: User sees JavaScript error on third party IDP sites.
bugs.conditions: Windows Edge client is used Access policy requires user to authenticate on a third party site
bugs.impact: Usability of Edge Client
bugs.fix: Edge Client now runs embedded browser in Internet Explorer 10 emulation mode, which has support for modern JavaScript.

bugs.title: HA: Failover during Radius Accounting On/Off bulk deletion not supported
bugs.symptoms: During a failover, PEM sessions that should be deleted are still enabled on the device that became active.
bugs.conditions: Failover occurs during bulk deletion of subscriber sessions.
bugs.impact: When the standby unit becomes active, un-deleted subscriber sessions that remained at the moment of failover will continue to be enabled until they time out.

bugs.title: TMM Core on Multi-Blade Chassis
bugs.symptoms: TMM core.
bugs.conditions: On a multi-blade chassis with WAM caching in use, where the datastor daemon is stopped and restarted, and where traffic is being cached by datastor.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The software defect has been found and fixed.

bugs.title: Floating IPv6 anycast address for HA results in intermittent communication loss
bugs.symptoms: When a floating IPV6 anycast address is used in an HA configuration, neighbor solicitation responses maybe sent by the standby box in the HA configuration. The mac masquerade address is not used for responses.
bugs.conditions: Floating IPV6 anycast address is used and packets are first received by the standby box.
bugs.impact: Communication issues between an IPv6 host and the traffic group floating IP address.
bugs.workaround: Use a regular IPv6 address instead of an anycast address for floating addresses.

bugs.title: kerberos cache is not cleared when Administrator password is changed in AAA AD Server
bugs.symptoms: when administrator's password is changed, the old ticket is still stored in kerberos cache, so AD Query failed
bugs.conditions: administrator's password is changed for AAA AD Server
bugs.impact: AD Query failed
bugs.workaround: as a workaround bigip administrator should remove kerberos cache files (krb5cc_0 and krb5cc_1) manually in /var/run/apmd/krb5cc/ and all subdirectories.
bugs.fix: after fix kerberos caches destroyed by apmd, if administrator's password is changed and access policy is applied

bugs.title: Values of high-water and low-water mark for 'apd' pending request queue might not handle requests completely.
bugs.symptoms: Under heavy authentication requests from tmm with a slow or down back-end authentication server, the apd accept connection queue could get full, resulting in apd logs: AD module: authentication with '1439805563539620' failed: Too many open files.
bugs.conditions: - Incoming authentication request to apd (from tmm) is very high. - Back-end authentication server is slow or down.
bugs.impact: Authentication failures; might bring authentication rate down to zero.
bugs.workaround: Adjust the value of connhwm, connlwm and soconnmax values using tmsh commands. - To set the value to 1024, use the following command: sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=1024. - Change Low water mark first using the following command: tmsh modify sys db apm.apd.connlwm value 480. - Change highwater mark next using the following command: tmsh modify sys db apm.apd.connhwm value 512.
bugs.fix: Values of high-water and low-water mark for the 'apd' pending request queue now handle requests as expected.

bugs.title: Statistics slow_merge option does not work
bugs.symptoms: When the statistics DB variable option 'merged.method' is set to 'slow_merge' then the merging of statistics stops working. This causes statistics to no longer appear to be updated.
bugs.conditions: The DB variable 'merged.method' is set to 'slow_merge'.
bugs.impact: Statistics no longer appear to be updated.
bugs.workaround: 1) Set "merged.method" to "fast_merge" which is the default. -or- 2) Create the /var/tmstat/cluster directory using mkdir. Please note the directory must be created on every blade in a chassis. Additionally, this directory needs to be re-created after reboots, so something like "/bin/mkdir /var/tmstat/cluster" should be added to "/config/startup"
bugs.fix: Statistics are now updated as expected when the statistics DB variable option 'merged.method' is set to 'slow_merge'.

bugs.title: Supported platforms for Event Correlation
bugs.symptoms: Event correlation is not supported on: 1. Any kind of multi slot/blade platform, physical or virtual, with multiple available slots/blades. But if cluster has only 1 active slot (green blade) - event correlation will run on it. This is relevant since version 11.3 2. A vCMP guest, that is hosted by a hypervisor, that runs on a platform which does not have an SSD drive. But if the disk is SSD on vCMP guest - event correlation will run on it. This is relevant since version 11.6
bugs.conditions: Clustered environment.
bugs.impact: Event Correlation daemon and GUI.
bugs.fix: Just documented exact platforms.

bugs.title: Adding a trunk might disable vCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: If a vCMP guest is running when a trunk is added, the guest might fail until vCMP is restarted.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP guest running -- Trunk added.
bugs.impact: Guest failure. vCMP restart required.
bugs.workaround: Restart vCMP.
bugs.fix: Adding a trunk no longer disables vCMP guests.

bugs.title: Route domain addresses can be selected when configuring device connectivity
bugs.symptoms: Route domain addresses can be selected when configuring a device connectivity. Doing so produces an error.
bugs.conditions: Having self IP addresses with a route domain.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. The system presents an error and does not use the IP address, even though the user can select it.
bugs.fix: The system now displays only relevant IP addresses that may be used as a device address, that is, those IP address that are in the default route domain, so the user cannot select an incorrect one.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes do not support monitor alias destinations.
bugs.symptoms: FQDN nodes do not support monitor alias destinations.
bugs.conditions: Configure a monitor with an alias address or port. The system will either prevent you from configuring, or the monitor will only be directed to the node address or port.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not send health checks to the configured monitor alias port. Monitor doesn't work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Depending on the functionality needed, you might be able to work around this by using an alternative configuration.
bugs.fix: FQDN nodes now support monitor alias destinations.

bugs.title: Nesting periodic after with parking command could crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule contains a periodic after command, and within this there is another periodic after command whose contents park, it can lead to tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: A periodic after command is used, and within this there is another periodic after command whose contents park.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not nest after commands with parking command.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with iRules that contain a periodic after command, which itself contains a periodic after command whose contents park. These iRules now complete as expected.

bugs.title: FQDN pool members do not support manual-resume
bugs.symptoms: FQDN pool members do not support manual-resume, but allow its configuration.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use manual-resume for FQDN pool members.
bugs.impact: FQDN pool members do not honor manual-resume setting.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure manual-resume on FQDN pool members.
bugs.fix: FQDN pool members do not support manual-resume, and BIG-IP no longer allows its configuration.

bugs.title: ASM config syncronization stops working
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, you might have ASM synchronization configured, but there is no evidence that the synchronization is occurring, and the policy changes are not synchronized. The following messages can be seen in '/var/log/ts/asm_config_server.log': ------------------------- F5::ASMConfig::Handler::SyncHandler::sync_general_ucs_request,,ASM is now entering sync recovery state. Requesting complete configuration from /Common/<peer_machine_name> F5::ASMConfig::Handler::send_to_relay,,Failed on sending sync_send_ucs to /Common/<peer_machine_name>: Can't call method "send" on an undefined value at /<path>/Handler.pm line <line_number>. F5::ASMConfig::Handler::spawn_relay_handler,,Sync recovery state timed out. State may be inconsistent with other peers ------------------------- Please notice the values in '<...>', in the log examples above, which may differ.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this, but it occurs when ASM is provisioned, ASM sync is enabled, and HA pair is configured. It is possible that it occurs when mcpd memory consumption becomes excessive.
bugs.impact: ASM sync does not occur
bugs.workaround: 1. Remove ASM sync from the device group (Under Security :: Options : Application Security : Synchronization : Application Security Synchronization). 2. Restart asm_config_server.pl on both devices and wait until they come back up. 3. Change the device group to a manual sync group . 4. On the device with the good configuration re-enable ASM sync for the device group. 5. Make a spurious ASM change, and push the configuration. 6. Change the sync type back to automatic.

bugs.title: SSL traffic stall with misconfigured mirroring configuration
bugs.symptoms: SSL traffic may be stalled if there is a mismatch in mirror setting on the SSL virtual server between the active and the standby unit.
bugs.conditions: SSL virtual server with mirroring enabled on the active unit and disabled on the standby unit.
bugs.impact: Connections on the active unit may be stalled up to "Handshake timeout" seconds
bugs.workaround: Configure both units to have the same mirror setting on the virtual server.

bugs.title: Total pva assisted connection counters are per acceleration.
bugs.symptoms: The total pva assisted connection counter is reported as the total number of times connections being accelerated by hardware. In the case of support dynamic hardware re-offloading, a connection might be offloaded to hardware multiple times, and therefore be counted in multiple time in this way.
bugs.conditions: Using pva-configured hardware.
bugs.impact: pva assisted connection counter reports higher-than-expected totals.

bugs.title: Trust domain changes do not persist on reboot.
bugs.symptoms: Some earlier releases saved only the internal binary database for trust domain changes (generally, changes to device group objects and device objects), rather than saving the text-based authoritative configuration in '/config/bigip*.conf'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when making changes to devices via the Device Management UI.
bugs.impact: Device Group configuration may not be correct after a reboot.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly run a command to save the configuration before rebooting devices.
bugs.fix: Trust domain changes do not persist on reboot.

bugs.title: Perpetual 'Loading...' banner when updating values in GUI System :: Preferences.
bugs.symptoms: The GUI banner 'Loading... Receiving configuration data from your device' does not disappear when updating changes in System :: Preferences page.
bugs.conditions: Use a BIG-IP system running 11.6.0 HF6. Make changes to System :: Preferences page.
bugs.impact: The GUI banner 'Loading... Receiving configuration data from your device' stays without showing the modified data. This is cosmetic. The changes are properly sent and stored. Reloading the page shows the new values.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is cosmetic.

bugs.title: Incorrect form action path may be used if it is changed inside 'onsubmit' event handler
bugs.symptoms: If HTML form has 'onsubmit' event handler which assigns absolute path to form action, then non-rewritten path is used for form submission.
bugs.conditions: HTML form with 'onsubmit' event handler
bugs.impact: HTML form can not be submitted.
bugs.workaround: Correction with application-specific iRule is possible
bugs.fix: Now action path assignment inside 'onsubmit' event handler is handled correctly.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ unable to license BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) instances in UDF/KVM Environments.
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to license a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in a UDF/KVM environment will fail; manually licensing the same BIG-IP with the same license regkey will work fine.
bugs.conditions: This issue affects systems that implement the SMBIOS specification in ambiguous ways. Differing mechanisms for reading the UUID can return different values.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IQ will incorrectly report that the license cannot be applied to the BIG-IP, and will fail the attempt.

bugs.title: Mirrored persistence entries retained after expiration
bugs.symptoms: Prior to expiration, the age of persistence entries is reset to 0, thus retaining the persistence entries forever.
bugs.conditions: -- Persistence is configured. -- A mirroring IP address is configured.
bugs.impact: Retention of persistence entries leads to eventual low memory conditions, performance degradation, and traffic outage or restarting of some daemons.
bugs.workaround: Although no reasonable workaround exists, you can clear the persistence table to reclaim leaked memory.
bugs.fix: Persistence entries are no longer retained beyond their expiration.

bugs.title: Possible memory exhaustion in access end-user interface pages for transparent proxy/SWG cases.
bugs.symptoms: When certain end user interface pages (e.g. 401 response) are served by the APM, these include a unique parameter in the URL. This results in the leak of objects representing caches for these pages, because their unique parameter renders caching ineffective.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Use of SWG in Transparent mode. -- One of the following: + Use a logon page agent, an external logon page agent, or a 401 agent in the access policy. + Trigger an access policy evaluation when one is already in progress or when accessing a page that requires an established session.
bugs.impact: A memory leak in the TMM.
bugs.workaround: None (when the triggering conditions are encountered).
bugs.fix: This release corrects the possible memory exhaustion issue in access end-user interface pages for transparent proxy/SWG cases.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when AAM receives a pipelining HTTP request while shutting down the connection
bugs.symptoms: In rare conditions when a client sends pipelining HTTP requests and AAM is configured it may incorrectly process a consequent request resulting in crashing of TMM.
bugs.conditions: AAM and ASM licensed and provisioned HTTP compression profile configured on a virtual server
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when AAM receives a pipelining HTTP request which while shutting down the connection

bugs.title: No virtual servers display on multi-page, multiple partition configurations.
bugs.symptoms: No virtual servers display on multi-page, multiple partition configurations.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the GUI on the virtual server list when there is more than one page of virtual server results in partition A and only one page in partition B, when you show page 2 in partition A and then switch to partition B.
bugs.impact: The list will be empty even though there are virtual servers configured on the system.
bugs.workaround: Switch to the partition you want to view before navigating to the virtual servers list page.

bugs.title: Memory leak in iprepd
bugs.symptoms: The IP reputation daemon (iprepd) has a small leak of around ~8 to ~16 bytes every 5 minutes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the BIG-IP box is licensed with IPI Subscription, and iprepd is running.
bugs.impact: Memory increases slowly until the kernel out-of-memory kills the iprepd process.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a memory leak in the IP reputation daemon (iprepd).

bugs.title: TMM might core when renaming an existing pool containing pool members
bugs.symptoms: TMM might produce a core dump if a pool containing poolmembers is renamed.
bugs.conditions: - Pool with pool members. - Move operation is enabled via sys db key. - Pool is renamed.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use move operation; fully delete and then recreate pools if renaming is needed.

bugs.title: TMM segfault in flow_find_opaque_ctx() caused by corrupt opaque ctx.
bugs.symptoms: A rare TMM segfault was encountered in flow_find_opaque_ctx() caused by corrupt opaque ctx. Log signature in /var/log/ltm: err tmm1[21114]: 01010276:3: Crypto codec error: sw_crypto Couldn't get ECDH other public value.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what conditions trigger this.

bugs.title: TMM cores in renew lease timer handler
bugs.symptoms: TMM generates core.
bugs.conditions: All three following conditions have to be met for this to trigger : 1) Both IPv4 and IPv6 network access connection has to be enabled for the same network access resource. 2) IPv4 address have to be statically assigned. 3) IPv6 address have to be dynamically assigned from the leasepool.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Workaround 1) Use IPv4 only network access connection. Workaround 2) While using both IPv4 and IPv6 network access connection, assign both IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint addresses from IPv4 and IPv6 leasepool respectively. Workaround 3) While using both IPv4 and IPv6 network access connection, assign both IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint statically.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores in renew lease timer handler

bugs.title: Cipher 3DES and iQuery encrypting traffic between BIG-IP systems
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems use the iQuery protocol to securely communicate with other BIG-IP systems. The BIG-IP system supports the AES/3DES ciphers for encrypting iQuery traffic. Some of these ciphers are now considered unsecure.
bugs.conditions: The value is hardcoded into the product. Note: This is completely independent of the TMM profiles or the httpd cipher values.
bugs.impact: There is no way to configure this; the value is hardcoded. Scanner operations performed on your configuration will report this as an unsecure cipher.
bugs.workaround: If you do not need iQuery at all, you can block port 4353 completely. For those who do need it, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The cipher list in use is now "AESGCM:AES:!ADH:!AECDH:!PSK:!aECDH:!DSS:!ECDSA:!AES128:-SHA1:AES256-SHA"

bugs.title: Curl connections with 'local-port' option fail sometimes over IPsec tunnels when connection.vlankeyed db variable is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Certain url connections with 'local-port' option fail sometimes over IPsec tunnels when connection.vlankeyed db variable is disabled with 'curl: (7) couldn't connect to host' error.
bugs.conditions: Using curl command with'--local-port' option causes the connections to fail on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: TCP connections do not complete the three way handshake and traffic does not pass.
bugs.workaround: Disabling 'cmp' option in virtual server secures the traffic over IPsec tunnels.
bugs.fix: Using curl command with'--local-port' option no longer causes the connections to fail on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: In some error scenarios, IPsec might send packets not intended for the IPsec over the tunnel.
bugs.symptoms: In some error scenarios, IPsec might send packets not intended for the IPsec over the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is some issue processing the packet going through IPsec tunnel.
bugs.impact: Tmm restart without core due to internal connection timeout.
bugs.fix: IPsec now only sends packets intended for IPsec over the tunnel.

bugs.title: TMM may leak memory when renaming pools
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue TMM may leak memory if a pool containing poolmembers is renamed.
bugs.conditions: - Pool with poolmembers. - Move operation is enabled via sys db key. - Pool is renamed.
bugs.impact: TMM may leak memory associated to pools and poolmembers
bugs.workaround: Do not use move operation; fully delete/recreate pools if renaming is needed.

bugs.title: Bringing up and tearing down an IPsec tunnel will slowly leak tmm memory
bugs.symptoms: Cipher memory initialized when an IPsec tunnel is created is not cleaned up when IPsec tunnel is removed.
bugs.conditions: Every time an IPsec tunnel is established and then removed will leave the allocated cipher memory in the system.
bugs.impact: Slowly leak TMM memory
bugs.fix: Cipher memory is freed when an IPsec tunnel is removed

bugs.title: SWG Explicit Proxy uses incorrect port after a 407 Authentication Attempt
bugs.symptoms: When the SWG Explicit Proxy is configured to perform a 407 Authentication Request, if the client accesses a non-standard HTTP port (e.g. http://www.example.com:8080) the first request after authentication will fail.
bugs.conditions: SWG Explicit Proxy configured HTTP 407 Authorization configured in Per-Request Policy for authentication Client requests a non-standard HTTP port in request
bugs.impact: The first request after authentication will fail.
bugs.workaround: If the user refreshes their browser request, subsequent requests will work as expected.

bugs.title: Changing the system's admin user causes many errors in the REST framework.
bugs.symptoms: The iControl REST log at /var/log/icrd will have entries similar to the following: notice icrd_child[32206]: 01420003:5: Cannot load user credentials for user "admin" Current session has been terminated.
bugs.conditions: Change the default admin user, for example, by following the steps in the Article K15632: Disabling the admin and root accounts using the BIG-IP Configuration utility or the Traffic Management Shell: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K15632.
bugs.impact: Many REST APIs do not function, and functionality that depends on REST fails.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround. You must use the default admin in order for iControl REST calls to work.
bugs.fix: You can now use iControl REST with alternate local admin usernames. Note: Depending on the software version you use, you might experience bug 754547, which requires a requires a manual restart of restjavad following a change to systemauth.primaryadminuser: tmsh restart sys service restjavad

bugs.title: New Diameter session event triggers registered for by the PCRF should not be appended to existing registered event triggers in PEM.
bugs.symptoms: PCRF may receive old event triggers it is not interested in.
bugs.conditions: PEM with a valid Gx interface should receive more than one set of event triggers that the PCRF needs to register for.
bugs.impact: Increase in Diameter traffic.
bugs.fix: Discard previously registered event triggers while registering a new set.

bugs.title: When a pool member goes down, persistence entries may vary among tmms
bugs.symptoms: When a pool member goes down, persistence entries may vary among tmms. The result will be that rather than persisting to a single pool member, the new connections may arrive on different pool members based on the number of tmms on the BIG-IP platform in use.
bugs.conditions: Using persistence with some connections persisted to a pool member that goes down, either administratively or due to a monitor. During this time, the client is issuing several new connections to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent persistence entries.
bugs.fix: The race conditions that involved dropping an offline pool member have been resolved.

bugs.title: FQDN pool in resource prevents Access Policy Sync.
bugs.symptoms: FQDN pool in resource causes Access Policy Sync to fail. You will see an error such as "PolicySyncMgr: Failed to create the policy /Common/ap_vdi" after making changes with the following error: "01070734:3: Configuration error: Cannot assign (/Common/myfqdnpool.example.com-10.10.10.10) as a pool member."
bugs.impact: Policy cannot sync to other devices.
bugs.conditions: - Create a pool with FQDN node - Add the pool to a resource such as remote-desktop - Add the resource to an access policy - Start a policy sync with the policy
bugs.fix: User can sync an access policy that include a resource with FQDN pool.

bugs.title: ASM REST: name for ipIntelligenceReference is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: The reference name for a Security Policy's ip-intelligence configuration is not consistent with F5 REST standards; which dictate that a reference name starts with a lower case letter. In the return for a policy resource the following is seen: ... 'IpIntelligenceReference': { 'link': 'https://localhost/mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<POLICY ID>/ip-intelligence' ... This should be 'ipIntelligenceReference' This has already been corrected in versions 12.0.0 and later.
bugs.conditions: ASM REST is used to access IP Intelligence for Security Policies.
bugs.impact: Reference names are inconsistent and confusing.
bugs.workaround: If an API client wishes to $expand the resource wanted in a way that works against all versions, the pre-expanded name can be used. ?$expand=ip-intelligence
bugs.fix: We corrected an inconsistent reference name. 'IpIntelligenceReference' is now 'ipIntelligenceReference'.

bugs.title: "pem classify" policy action parameters
bugs.symptoms: The "pem classify defer" and "pem classify" policy action logs an error when the application and protocol are not specified.
bugs.conditions: Create an LTM policy which has classification rules for which the application and protocol have not been specified and this policy is attached to a virtual.
bugs.impact: The configuration processing returns an error which is logged in /var/log/ltm and the erroneous policy is not used.
bugs.workaround: Fix the policy by specifying the application/classification and protocol.

bugs.title: On MAC, Network Access proxy settings are not applied to tun adapter after VPN is established
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, user may not be able to browse to external or internal web sites, Because the proxy settings won't be used.
bugs.conditions: User's machine has local proxy settings configured NA settings specify a proxy configuration
bugs.impact: User may not be able to browse some sites, or the connection would not take the proxy settings into account.

bugs.title: IPv6 packets containing extended trailer are dropped
bugs.symptoms: Some IPv6 packets are dropped
bugs.conditions: IPv6 packet contains trailing bytes after payload
bugs.impact: Packet loss
bugs.fix: IPv6 packets that exceed the size of the 'Payload Length' header will be trimmed and processed instead of being dropped.

bugs.title: WebSSO plugin core dumps under very rare conditions.
bugs.symptoms: WebSSO plugin core dumps under very rare conditions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs rarely when the WebSSO plugin is enabled.
bugs.impact: WebSSO plugin core dumps.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a rare core dump related to the Websso plugin.

bugs.title: vCMP guest cluster may have two primaries due to partial partitioning of the management backplane network on one cluster member
bugs.symptoms: The management backplane network on one cluster member of a vCMP guest may partially malfunction in that multicast packets are able to be sent out of the cluster member but incoming multicast packets from the peer members are dropped. This results in the cluster becoming "split-brained" and having two primary members; the original primary remains so while the isolated member also elects itself as a primary.
bugs.conditions: This issue only occurs on vCMP guest clusters and has been found to only happen in extremely rare cases.
bugs.impact: Dataplane traffic remains unaffected. However, configuration changes will not propagated to the isolated cluster member, and stats will not be synced from the isolated cluster member. Furthermore, if the cluster is the active unit in an HA pair, this may result in a failover not occurring as expected due to the technical nature of the malfunction.
bugs.workaround: To resolve the issue, reboot the cluster member whose management backplane has malfunctioned.

bugs.title: SNMP F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmPmStatConfigSyncState returns 0 for edited access profile
bugs.symptoms: F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmPmStatConfigSyncState returns a zero value for an APM access profile that has been edited but not yet applied, which should instead return a non-zero value. config # snmpwalk -v2c 127.0.0.1 -c public F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmPmStatConfigSyncState F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmPmStatConfigSyncState."/Common/my-test-access" = Counter64: 0
bugs.conditions: The access profile has been edited but not yet applied.
bugs.impact: SNMP users cannot discriminate the status of an APM access profile: applied or not applied.
bugs.workaround: None available.
bugs.fix: F5-BIGIP-APM-MIB::apmPmStatConfigSyncState now returns the correct non-zero value.

bugs.title: ePVA dynamic offloading can result in immediate eviction and re-offloading of flows.
bugs.symptoms: ePVA dynamic offloading can result in immediate eviction and re-offloading of flows. If dynamic offloading is enabled in the fastl4 profile, flows that collide in the ePVA will ping/pong in and out of the ePVA due to immediate eviction and re-offloading. Flows that are evicted due to collisions are reported in the epva_flowstat stats, tot.hash_evict.
bugs.conditions: A fastl4 profile with PVA Offload Dynamic enabled and two flows that result in a hash collision, resulting in an evicted flow.
bugs.impact: Flows that collide will be re-offloaded, evicted, and then re-offloaded again within a short time span. It is unknown if there is a direct impact, but in some cases a delay in processing packets on a connection may occur.
bugs.workaround: Disable PVA Offload Dynamic in the fastl4 profile. Another option would be to disable PVA Flow Evict in the fastl4 profile.
bugs.fix: The system now handles flows involved in hash collisions such that ePVA dynamic offloading no longer results in immediate eviction and re-offloading of flows.

bugs.title: Support Extended Master Secret Extension (RFC7627) for ProxySSL
bugs.symptoms: In ProxySSL, if a client and backend server negotiated and agreed to use Extended Master Secret, ProxySSL will not be able to finish the handshake successfully.
bugs.conditions: ProxySSL is enabled in BIG-IP and the client and server both support Extended Master Secret and successfully exchang the Extended Master Secret Extensions.
bugs.impact: ProxySSL will not work.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable Extended Master Secret features in client or server.
bugs.fix: ProxySSL now supports Extended Master Secret Extension (RFC7627) for ProxySSL.
bugs.behavior: If the client and the server exchanges extended master secret extension in its client hello or server hello, and agree to use extended master secret calculation, then BIGIP SSL will use the agreed calculation method. There is no hardware support for extended master secret computation, only software path.

bugs.title: BIG-IP SSL does not support Extended Master Secret Extension (RFC7627)
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP SSL cannot negotiate Extended Master Secret with client or server.
bugs.conditions: If a client or server tries to negotiate Extended Master Secret with BIG-IP SSL, the negotiation will only succeed in using the legacy master secret calculation.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP SSL and its peer can not successfully negotiate an Extended Master Secret calculation, instead can only negotiate a legacy master secret calculation. Note: The SSL handshake will continue to work.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP SSL now supports Extended Master Secret (RFC7627) for reverse/forward proxy.

bugs.title: Static RDP App Tunnel Resource connects to wrong backend server in some cases
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, user will get connected to wrong app tunnel resource.
bugs.conditions: One App tunnel resource host(or ip) is a substring of another app tuunel resource name or ip.
bugs.impact: User gets connected to wrong app tunnel resource once he clicks on resource icon on the webtop.
bugs.workaround: Don't create multiple resources where host name of one resource is substring of hostname of another resource.

bugs.title: Accept-language in alerts
bugs.symptoms: Accept-language header is not sent in alerts generated by FPS plugin.
bugs.conditions: Alerts generated by FPS plugin.
bugs.impact: Prevents analyzing the cause for plugin-generated alerts.
bugs.fix: The accept-language header is now sent in alerts generated by the FPS plugin.

bugs.title: Intermittent iStats reset
bugs.symptoms: iStats will intermittently be reset back to zero.
bugs.conditions: An event that causes iStats to be archive, such as removing an iStat, removing a configuration object that has an iStat or removing a custom-stat repeatedly may cause a reset.
bugs.impact: The iStat values will be reset to zero and then resume incrementing.
bugs.workaround: Avoid removing iStats or other events that trigger the resets.

bugs.title: Javascript error in Safari browser when working with framed Cross-Domains website
bugs.symptoms: ASM Client-Side Human User Indicator (CSHUI) script injected into a page with frames, and there are frames pointing to a domain that that is different from the top window frame, Safari browser throws out javascript error similar to the following: Blocked a frame with origin "http://172.16.32.64" from accessing a frame with origin "http://172.16.38.211". Protocols, domains, and ports must match.
bugs.conditions: -- CSHUI with framed Cross-Domains website in Safari. -- Frames on the page point to a domain that that is different from the top window frame.
bugs.impact: Javascript error in Safari browser.

bugs.title: reference to freed loop_nexthop may cause tmm crash.
bugs.symptoms: tmm may crash intermittently when there are cmp directed VIP (Virtual IP) to VIP traffic.
bugs.conditions: When CMP directed VIP to VIP traffic exists.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm should not crash on this condition any more

bugs.title: Content diagnostics and LCD
bugs.symptoms: While running platform_check, you notice this on the LCD: F5 LCD Server Clients: 0 Screens: 0
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running platform_check after running bigstart stop
bugs.impact: This is cosmetic, the LCD does not indicate that it is in diagnostic mode.
bugs.fix: When the LCD is unable to communicate with BIG-IP, such as during shutdown or platform_check, the LCD now displays the following: F5 LCD Server Host inaccessible or in diagnostic mode

bugs.title: Web application does not work/works intermittently via Portal Access after upgrading BIG-IP to any new version.
bugs.symptoms: Web application does not work/works intermittently via Portal Access after upgrading the BIG-IP system to any new software version.
bugs.conditions: -- Web application via Portal Access. -- Using any modern browser, for example Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari, Microsoft Internet Explorer 11 (IE11), or Microsoft Edge. -- Upgrading BIG-IP software. -- Web Application uses HTML5 features Local Storage or Session Storage.
bugs.impact: Various unexpected behaviors. For example, a custom intranet application link might experience intermittent failures through rewrite. This occurs because Portal Access does not support Storage areas (localStorage, sessionStorage). This might impact web-applications with content previously populated in Storage areas.
bugs.workaround: Possible workaround: -- Clear browser 'cookies and website data' or 'offline data' manually after upgrading (options to use depend on which browser you are using).

bugs.title: Datastor may crash
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases datastor may crash to protect the system from corruption. After datastor restarts, tmm may crash when attempting to communicate with datastor.
bugs.conditions: WAM provisioned and enabled
bugs.impact: Datastor and TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: [DNS] dns64 behavior does not comply with RFC about how to treat RCODEs other than 'NO ERROR'
bugs.symptoms: GTM/BIG-IP DNS forwards AAAA response with and RCODE other than 3 to the client, instead of sending an A query to the server.
bugs.conditions: dns64 profile configured.
bugs.impact: The client application fails even there is an A GTM/BIG-IP DNS server available.

bugs.title: ZebOS configuration cannot be loaded via imish when service password-encryption is set
bugs.symptoms: When "service password-encryption" is configured in ZebOS, encrypted passwords cannot be loaded through imish. imish will print "% Invalid input detected at '^' marker." and the password will not be loaded.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing is configured with "service password-encryption" in ZebOS config file or running config, run "imish -f <file>" or paste encrypted password into imish.
bugs.impact: ZebOS configuration will be incompletely loaded.
bugs.workaround: The config will be properly read if tmrouted is restarted. Restarting tmrouted will interrupt all dynamic routing. The config can also be loaded without restarting tmrouted by configuring the cleartext passwords manually. They will be encrypted when the configuration is saved.
bugs.fix: imish now correctly loads the ZebOS configuration when "service password-encryption" is set.

bugs.title: Issue a Body in Get sub violation for GET request with 'transfer-encoding: chunked'
bugs.symptoms: A GET request without payload but with payload indication doesn't issue the body in get violation.
bugs.conditions: A Get request without payload arrives. The request has a 'transfer-encoding: chunked' header although there is no payload.
bugs.impact: A suspicious request goes by undetected.
bugs.workaround: Add an iRule that removes this header from the ASM and issues a custom violation.
bugs.fix: A GET request without payload but with 'transfer-encoding: chunked' will issue the body in GET sub violation.

bugs.title: Consistently log the fragment in query_string and HTTP_QUERY for ASM/LTM
bugs.symptoms: ASM logging terminates the URL with the number sign '#' if it exists. The part after the '#' is logged as the query string.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP Request arrives into ASM. -- The URL contains a '#', for example: GET /something/something/dark/side#theforce HTTP/1.1 The full request URL needs to get logged in remote logging.
bugs.impact: The full HTTP Request line does not get logged as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A new remote logging field was added, 'fragment'. ASM is now logging the part after the '#' in this field.

bugs.title: vCMP guest fails to go Active after the host system is rebooted
bugs.symptoms: A vCMP guest fails to go Active after the host system is rebooted. When this occurs, the system posts the following message: confpp[9184]: rollback FAILED for 'unix_config_syslog'
bugs.conditions: The host of a vCMP guest is rebooted.
bugs.impact: The guest will not become active.
bugs.fix: vCMP guest now correctly goes Active after the host system is rebooted

bugs.title: [DNS] dns64-additional-section-rewrite v4-only does not rewrite v4 RRs
bugs.symptoms: A and AAAA RRsets in the additional section are dropped.
bugs.conditions: When dns64-additional-section-rewrite is 'v4-only' or 'v6-only'.
bugs.impact: Failure to include the additional RRs results in additional lookups by the client which could be glue records for a resolver.
bugs.workaround: Set dns64-additional-section-rewrite is 'any'.
bugs.fix: v4-only and v6-only options work as expected. Note that DNS64 prefix operations occur after all other DNS processing blocks -- including GTM.

bugs.title: WebSafe "Missing component" check gets applied on request with different referrer domain.
bugs.symptoms: The "Missing component" checker looks only looks at referrer header path and not the domain name. The result is a false positive alert indicating the cookie is missing.
bugs.conditions: The referrer is coming from a different domain and the system is still performing component validation check.
bugs.impact: False positive missing component alerts when redirecting from other sites to a WebSafe protected site.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure the same URL as a protected page.
bugs.fix: The Missing Component check now looks at the referrer header path as well as the domain name. This prevents false-positive Missing Component alerts when redirecting from other sites to a WebSafe protected site.

bugs.title: Differentiation of missing component alerts
bugs.symptoms: The alert reads as 'no cookie' while the actual situation is different.
bugs.conditions: The component check cookie exists, but it fails to be parsed by the plugin.
bugs.impact: False positive missing component no-cookie alerts.
bugs.fix: If the Component Check cookie exists and cookie parsing fails for different reasons, the system now sends different alert components (Unseal Failed or Cookie Malformed).

bugs.title: Actual attack detection threshold might be higher than configured one
bugs.symptoms: ASM brute force session based actual attack detection threshold might be higher than configured one.
bugs.conditions: 1. Failed logins are sent in high rate (more than 1 in 2 sec)
bugs.impact: Actual attack detection threshold is higher than configured one

bugs.title: AutoDoS daemon aborts intermittently after it's being up for several days
bugs.symptoms: AutoDoS daemon aborts intermittently when accessing session db api for memcache interface.
bugs.conditions: This happens in control plan AutoDoS daemon. This is an intermittent issue that occurs in few platforms under specific stress testing.
bugs.impact: Core will be seen, but the daemon will restart, and there is no loss of state.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: AutoDoS daemon no longer aborts intermittently when accessing session db api for memcache interface.

bugs.title: ArcSight gives error on specific transactions
bugs.symptoms: The Arcsight remote logger shows error messages when trying to parse messages from ASM.
bugs.conditions: An arcsight remote logger is configured. Specific transaction is coming out.
bugs.impact: Remote logging is not coming out.

bugs.title: VPN cannot be used in some cases when IP filtering engine is enabled
bugs.symptoms: NA connects and disconnects within 30 seconds in some cases if IP filtering engine is enabled in NA configuration
bugs.conditions: -IP filtering engine is enabled in NA configuration - Network Access virtual server connections are redirected to another internal virtual server in Big-IP connfiguration
bugs.impact: User cannot establish VPN
bugs.workaround: Do not redirect Virtual server connection or disable IP filtering engine. There are a couple of other workarounds: 1. Have the same port number for both the virtual servers. 2. If the port numbers need to be different for the 2 virtual servers, insert variable assignment agent which assigns value of client facing port (443 in this case) to variable session.server.network.port. Use custom variable and Text selections of agent. example: apm policy agent variable-assign /Common/na_act_variable_assign_ag { variables { { expression "return {443}" varname session.server.network.port } } }

bugs.title: Firefox signed plugin for VPN, Endpoint Check, etc
bugs.symptoms: Firefox v44.0 and later does not allow loading of Netscape Plugin Application Programming Interface (NPAPI) plugins, which are not signed by Firefox.
bugs.conditions: Using APM with Firefox v44.0 and later.
bugs.impact: Firefox v44.0 and later cannot establish network access or perform endpoint checking.
bugs.workaround: - Use Firefox v43.0 and earlier on all platforms. - Use Safari on Mac systems and Microsoft Internet Explorer on Microsoft Windows systems.
bugs.fix: Firefox v44.0 through v46.0 can now install F5 Network plugins, perform endpoint checking, and establish network access connections.

bugs.title: Network Access does not work if DNS cannot be resolved on client and PAC file contains DNS resolution code
bugs.symptoms: Tunnel server component of Edge client crashes, and user cannot establish VPN.
bugs.conditions: -DNS names cannot be resolved on client system. -PAC file used to determine proxy server uses JavaScript DNS resolution function.
bugs.impact: Tunnel server crashes and user cannot establish VPN.
bugs.workaround: Enable DNS resolution on client or do not use DNS resolution JavaScript functions in PAC file.
bugs.fix: Network Access now works as expected even when DNS cannot be resolved on client and PAC file contains DNS resolution code.

bugs.title: PEM: TMM asserts when Using Debug Image when Gy is being used
bugs.symptoms: TMM assert leading to restart.
bugs.conditions: When a policy P1 is installed over Gx with a reference to rating group R1 and later when an update is received over Gx to remove P1 and add policy P2 which also referring to same rating group R1 then TMM will core when Policy P2 is being removed.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and disruption of service.
bugs.workaround: PCRF should make sure add and remove policies are not done in single update.
bugs.fix: Issue has been fixed now.

bugs.title: [DNS] A query is not sent out in secondary mapping when no AAAA response.
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP DNS configured with DNS64 in Secondary mode receives no response for AAAA query, it does not attempt A query.
bugs.conditions: DNS64 configured in secondary mode.
bugs.impact: DNS64 secondary mode does not work as expected.

bugs.title: TMM (debug) assert seen during Failover with Gy
bugs.symptoms: When using the debug version of the tmm, HA fail over may cause the tmm to assert when Gy is configured.
bugs.conditions: Using PEM and Gy is configured.
bugs.impact: The TMM (debug version) may core and restart, resetting all connections.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the debug tmm with Gy.
bugs.fix: This debug assert has been changed to a debug log message.

bugs.title: ASM error prevents 4th-element version upgrades 'Invalid UCS. Cannot load configuration from newer version'
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade from any 11.6.x.y to 11.6.x.z, the following messages are logged to /var/log/asm: -- info tsconfig.pl[21395]: ASM initial configuration script launched -- info tsconfig.pl[21395]: ASM initial configuration script finished -- crit perl[19812]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::ConfigSync::upgrade_load): Invalid UCS. Cannot load configuration from newer version (0011.0006.0003.0001.0000.0000)
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Upgrade from any 11.6.x.y to 11.6.x.z (e.g., 11.6.3.1 to 11.6.3.2).
bugs.impact: ASM configuration is not loaded or upgraded. Errors in ASM log.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The upgrade in the case of 4th-element versions now works correctly.

bugs.title: ASM scripts can break applications
bugs.symptoms: ASM originated scripts are injected into places where they are not supposed to be, causing the script not to work and/or the application to break.
bugs.conditions: ASM is in front of a single page application, where injection is possible only for the main page. \ ASM has the CSRF or web scraping feature enabled.
bugs.impact: Application malfunctions, shows javascrip errors
bugs.workaround: Turn off the relevant feature that causes the injection.

bugs.title: FQDN node availability not reset after removing monitoring
bugs.symptoms: If you are using FQDN nodes that are being monitored, the node status will remain set to whatever it was before the monitor was removed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when removing monitoring from FQDN nodes
bugs.impact: The expected behavior is that the node status becomes 'unknown'. This could make it so FQDN nodes are permanently marked down or up.
bugs.fix: FQDN node status will now change to Unknown if monitoring is removed.

bugs.title: Use of iControl call get_certificate_list_v2() causes a memory leak.
bugs.symptoms: Use of iControl call get_certificate_list_v2() causes a memory leak.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the Management::KeyCertificate::get_certificate_list_v2 method in iControl.
bugs.impact: memory leak.
bugs.workaround: Restarting httpd helps reduce memory, but it must be restarted periodically to clear up the memory issues.
bugs.fix: Use of Management::KeyCertificate::get_certificate_list_v2 method in iControl no longer causes a memory leak.

bugs.title: Lines without EOL characters cause "tmsh load pem subscriber file" and GUI import to fail
bugs.symptoms: Subscriber lines terminated with an EOL that occur before the line without an EOL are loaded.
bugs.conditions: At least one line in the static subscriber file is not terminated with an EOL character.
bugs.impact: Impact to support staff in diagnosing the root cause for failure while importing a subscriber file.
bugs.workaround: Save the file in unix format that appends EOL characters to the each line. While editing the file make sure lines are terminated with an EOL character.

bugs.title: Kerberos SSO does not support AES256 encryption
bugs.symptoms: If the delegation account is enforced to use AES256 encryption, then APM Kerberos SSO will fail. Example error message: Dec 18 19:22:19 bigip8910mgmt err websso.7[31499]: 014d0005:3: Kerberos: can't decrypt S4U2Self ticket for user 'username' - Decrypt integrity check failed (-1765328353).
bugs.conditions: Delegation account is enforced to use AES256 encryption.
bugs.impact: Kerberos SSO will fail and user will be prompted to enter credential.
bugs.workaround: Disable the option to enforce AES256 encryption for the delegation account.
bugs.fix: Delegation account can be enforced to use AES256 encryption, provided the delegation account is configured as SPN format on the Kerberos SSO configuration.

bugs.title: Copying an access profile appends an _1 to the name.
bugs.symptoms: Copying an access profile appends an _1 to the name.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on every copy operation on an access profile.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue that does not impact system functionality.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this: 1. Copy the profile. 2. Edit bigip.conf to remove the _1 from the profile name. 3. Issue the command: tmsh load sys config.
bugs.fix: Copying an access profile no longer appends an _1 to the name unless it is needed, for example, when copying a profile whose name already exists.

bugs.title: Applying APM Add-on License Does Not Change Effective License Limit
bugs.symptoms: When an add-on license is applied on the active node, the effective license limit is not updated, even though telnet output shows that it is.
bugs.conditions: 1. Set up a high availability (HA) configuration with a base APM license. 2. Apply an APM add-on license to increase Access and CCU license limits.
bugs.impact: The actual number of sessions that can be established remains unchanged after adding an add-on license.
bugs.workaround: To make the add-on license effective, run the following command: bigstart restart tmm. For systems running v11.5.3, v11.5.4, and v11.6.0, use the following workaround: - Take one unit Offline. - Remove the HA configuration. - Reactivate license on the offline unit. - Take a peer unit Offline. - Release the first unit from Offline. - Reactivate license on the peer unit. - Rebuild HA configuration. - Release the peer unit from Offline.
bugs.fix: Applying APM add-on license now increases Access and CCU license limits, as expected.

bugs.title: JavaScript passed to ExternalInterface.call() may be erroneously unescaped
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript passed to ExternalInterface.call() may be erroneously unescaped.
bugs.conditions: Adobe ActionScript 3.0 version 24 or less.
bugs.impact: Adobe Flash application may crash.
bugs.fix: Completely fixed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: cron is configured with MAILTO=root but mailhost defaults to 'mail'
bugs.symptoms: The crontab and ssmtp configurations environment is MAILTO="", which means no email and it is difficult to find where the email went.
bugs.conditions: This exists in the default crontab and ssmtp configurations.
bugs.impact: - You may receive unexpected messages addressed to "root" at a host named "mail" on your network OR - You may encounter messages similar to the following in /var/log/maillog: Dec 10 03:25:24 BIG-IP-1 err sSMTP[8421]: Unable to connect to "mail" port 25. Dec 10 03:25:24 BIG-IP-1 err sSMTP[8421]: Cannot open mail:25
bugs.workaround: Change outbound-smtp mailhub to localhost with tmsh: tmsh modify /sys outbound-smtp mailhub localhost
bugs.fix: Default mailhub has been changed to localhost. Starting in 12.0.0, MAILTO is set to root instead of "" in /etc/crontab so that the output of cron jobs can be captured. However, ssmtp is configured by default with a mailhost of 'mail', which may result in either error messages logged to /var/log/maillog or unexpected messages received on another system.

bugs.title: Cron logs hourly email failure messages.
bugs.symptoms: Cron logs hourly email failure messages. When mailhub is configured, sends hourly email notifications containing the following message: Reports scheduling should not run on a machine with a failover state of inactive or standby at /usr/share/avr/bin/run_scheduled_reports.pl line 23.
bugs.conditions: Device is in standby or disabled.
bugs.impact: Log/email spam.
bugs.workaround: To avoid mail delivery attempts, change the third line of '/etc/cron.d/0hourly' to MAILTO="" .
bugs.fix: System no longer sends hourly reports when device is in standby or disabled.

bugs.title: Using the tmsh "edit" command to remove a monitor from a pool does not stop bigd from monitoring the pool
bugs.symptoms: Using the tmsh "edit" command to remove a monitor from a pool does not stop bigd from monitoring the pool.
bugs.conditions: Remove a monitor from a pool using tmsh edit commands.
bugs.impact: bigd still monitors the pool.

bugs.title: cron sends purge_mysql_logs.pl email error on LTM-only device
bugs.symptoms: On a device provisioned with LTM only, cron may log or send an email containing the following perl error: /etc/cron.hourly/purge_mysql_logs.pl: Usage: $class->connect([$dsn [,$user [,$passwd [,\%attr]]]]) at /etc/cron.hourly/purge_mysql_logs.pl line 27 This script was only intended to be run with AM, ASM, or ASM provisioned and it generates an error if it is not.
bugs.conditions: Any device with AM, ASM, and PSM not provisioned. LTM-only devices are impacted.
bugs.impact: If cron can send email, it will send the perl error in the email once per hour.

bugs.title: Compatibility issues with phishing detection and dosL7
bugs.symptoms: Alerts may not be sent by FPS if DOSL7 profile with proactive bot defense attached to the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Both FPS and DOSL7 profile with proactive bot defense is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Alerts will not be sent.
bugs.workaround: Disable proactive.
bugs.fix: Phishing Detection now works properly and phishing alerts are sent to the Dashboard by avoiding mitigation FPS reporting requests by DOSL7 PBD.

bugs.title: New DB variable log.lsn.comma changes CGNAT logs to CSV format
bugs.symptoms: New CSV format that does not use quotes as delimiters was not present prior to 12.1.2.
bugs.conditions: Setting the DB variable log.lsn.comma
bugs.impact: More control of logging format via the DB variable log.lsn.comma
bugs.fix: There is a new db variable log.lsn.comma that changes CGNAT logs to a CSV format that does not use quotes as delimiters between fields. Optional IP address fields appear as zero addresses, and optional numeric fields appear as zero. This new db variable applies to all LSN modes and to all ALG logs.
bugs.behavior: There is a new db variable log.lsn.comma that changes CGNAT logs to a CSV format that does not use quotes as delimiters between fields. Optional IP address fields appear as zero addresses, and optional numeric fields appear as zero. This new db variable applies to all LSN modes and to all ALG logs.

bugs.title: During shutdown, csyncd may dump core
bugs.symptoms: When csyncd exists during shutdown, it occasionally might leave a core dump.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during shutdown.
bugs.impact: None. csyncd is shutting down anyway; it just does so in an unclean manner. This is a cosmetic condition and does not indicate an issue with the system.

bugs.title: PCCD core and slow running SQL
bugs.symptoms: Search in network firewall log is very slow.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with large log files.
bugs.impact: Log searches could get really slow for very large log files.
bugs.workaround: Use custom search filters to speed up the search times.

bugs.title: Fail to update VPN correctly for non-admin user.
bugs.symptoms: VPN is not updated correctly for non-admin users.
bugs.conditions: Steps to Reproduce: 1. In BIG-IP 12.0, create Access Policy containing (Firewall Check, Machine Info, Machine Cert Auth, Cache and Session Control, Protected Workspace, VPN Resources with Optimized Applications.) 2. Login with a User without admin privileges 3. Run FF 4. Login to VS and install components 5. Click on NA resource on the webtop to start VPN tunnel => a user is asked for an admin password and VPN is successfully installed and established 6. Close FF and exit PWD

bugs.title: Analytics profile allows invalid combination of entities for Alerts setup
bugs.symptoms: When non cumulative metrics are selected for an Alert on a dimension that's other than a Virtual Server, errors appear in the log.
bugs.conditions: Analytics in use, and non-cumulative metrics such as the following are used on a time dimension: - Maximum TPS - Maximum Server Latency - Maximum Page Load Time - Maximum Request Throughput - Maximum Response Throughput
bugs.impact: You are able to configure invalid alerts but no warning is given and the metric does not work and generates errors in the /var/log/monpd.log file.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is Cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Invalid combination of entities for Alerts setup is no longer allowed. Validation is present both on UI side and the backend.

bugs.title: Pool licensing fails in some KVM/OpenStack environments.
bugs.symptoms: Licensing a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) from BIG-IQ, BIG-IQ can fail. The system posts the errors such as the following: -- In /var/log/ltm: Dossier error 16. -- In /var/log/restjavad: Dossier validation failed. error code: 5.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when BIG-IQ is used to license the BIG-IP VE instance.
bugs.impact: From BIG-IQ, the licensing operation will appear as a successful operation, however, BIG-IP VE will not be licensed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Licensing a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) from BIG-IQ in OpenStack and/or KVM environments completes with success on BIG-IQ and BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Additional garbage data being logged on user name and domain name for NTLM authentication
bugs.symptoms: ECA logs an error message in this format: Could not verify user (<Domain Name>\<User Name>) credential (<Reason>) Example: Could not verify user (mv4\test1) credential (STATUS_NO_LOGON_SERVERS) However, due to missing NUL termination, the user name and domain name may include garbage data such as follwing example: Could not verify user (mv413abfee\test1ewq12dsasd) credential (STATUS_NO_LOGON_SERVERS)
bugs.conditions: When NTLM front end authentication could not send the verification of the user's credential (e.g. ActiveDirectory server is down)
bugs.impact: BIG-IP could not send the verification to ActiveDirectory server for any reasons such as down ActiveDirectory server, incorrect machine account information between BIG-IP, and ActiveDirectory server, etc.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Now it properly logs the message with correct domain name and user name.

bugs.title: Improved Portal Access Log Message
bugs.symptoms: Portal access log message logs the failure to parse URL, but does not provide details on what URL failed to parse
bugs.conditions: Use Portal Access
bugs.impact: Portal Access Log messages will have incomplete information
bugs.fix: Improved Portal Access Log message to include URL that was failed to parse

bugs.title: Importing a previously exported policy which had two object names may fail
bugs.symptoms: If an exported access policy includes two object names profile_name-aaa and aaa, import that policy may fail or be incorrect.
bugs.conditions: For example: access policy name "test" access policy item name "test-empty" access policy item name "empty" For example: access policy name "test" access policy item name "test-empty" macro name "empty"
bugs.impact: Rare case, but the import of such a policy may fail.
bugs.workaround: One of the objects could be renamed in the bigip.conf file to avoid such a naming pattern.
bugs.fix: Objects are being exported correctly without error.

bugs.title: Rewrite engine behaves improperly in case of AS2 SWF with a badly formatted 'push' instruction
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite engine behaves improperly in case of AS2 SWF with a string in 'push' instruction longer than the instruction length itself.
bugs.conditions: Any AS2 SWF with a string in 'push' instruction longer than the instruction length.
bugs.impact: Rewrite coredump.
bugs.workaround: It can be worked around by adding an Portal Access profile resource item with Flash patcher turned off for improper SWF content.
bugs.fix: Completely fixed.

bugs.title: Invalid MSS with HW syncookies and flow forwarding
bugs.symptoms: A packet may have an MSS set to 65536 when using HW syncookies and flow forwarding.
bugs.conditions: The conditions which cause this are not fully known.
bugs.impact: TMM core/reboot.
bugs.workaround: Disable HW syncookies or TSO.

bugs.title: AVR reports device-level mitigation as "Device Level" and not as "Aggregated"
bugs.symptoms: When AVR gets a report on device-level mitigation, it reports it as "Aggregated" instead of "Device Level".
bugs.conditions: When AVR gets a report on device-level mitigation.
bugs.impact: The network reports was not clear or detailed enough.

bugs.title: ASM-config consumes 1.3GB RAM after repeated Policy Import via REST
bugs.symptoms: Multiple ASM-config processes are running (more than 10) and consuming more than a GB.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. Repeated policy import via REST.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system might run low on memory and post the following message in /var/log/kern.log: Out of memory: Kill process 22699.
bugs.workaround: Restart asm - disrupting Restart asm_config_server.pl - non disrupting
bugs.fix: We modified an operation to limit the number of ASM configuration processes. The operation now reuses processes instead of creating new ones, so the system no longer runs out of memory.

bugs.title: URL filter policy enforcement interprets "recommend to scan" as "uncategorized" all the time
bugs.symptoms: Previously the URL Filter Assign agent was always expected to be after Categorization and Response Analytics. In the case where Categorization returned only "recommend to scan" and Response Analytics returned nothing, "recommend to scan" would be treated as "uncategorized" before enforcing actions. BIG-IP now has Request Analytics. When this is used, there will be a URL Filter Assign agent after Request Analytics, and then another instance of this after Response Analytics. In such a situation, treating "recommend to scan" as "uncategorized" is incorrect in the instance of URL filter assign after Request Analytics.
bugs.conditions: Per request policy looks like: Category Lookup -> Request Analytics -> URL Filter -> Response Analytics -> URL Filter
bugs.impact: A "recommend to scan" categorization after Request Analytics is treated as "uncategorized". This is undesirable because the first URL Filter Assign instance deals with it as uncategorized instead of evaluating further by sending it to Response Analytics. If the first URL Filter allowed it through, Response Analytics would no longer see the "recommend to scan" classification and would not scan.
bugs.fix: Instead of switching "recommend to scan" to "uncategorized" in URL Filter, the system now leaves it as "recommend to scan" and takes the action of "uncategorized". Response Analytics was changed to strip the "recommend to scan" category if other categories exist, and to otherwise change it to "uncategorize". Because the system expects that Response Analytics is the last category evaluation agent in the policy, this is reasonable and safe to do.

bugs.title: Static proxy settings are not applied if NA configuration
bugs.symptoms: Applications that cannot evaluate PAC file cannot make use of static proxy configuration either.
bugs.conditions: - Network Access (NA) setting has static proxy configuration. - Application on user's system does not support proxy auto configuration, but does support static proxy configuration.
bugs.impact: Application cannot make connections if the proxy is required to connect to the destination. This could result in failed connection from that application
bugs.fix: Static proxy settings are now applied in Network Access configurations. This allow applications that do not support PAC files to work inside the VPN.

bugs.title: Some failover configuration items may fail to take effect
bugs.symptoms: These symptoms apply to version 12.0.0 and later: When only multicast failover is configured, traffic-groups are active on all devices in the device-group. If unicast failover is also configured, the traffic-group unexpectedly switches to a different device. These symptoms can occur on all versions: When the unicast address list is changed at the same time as other device properties, sod (the failover daemon) may fail to recognize one of the other changes.
bugs.conditions: For version 12.0.0 and later: Multicast failover is configured and the system loads the configuration from the configuration files. For example during the first boot of a new boot location, or after performing the procedure in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030. For all versions: A change is made to the cm device configuration that includes a unicast-address change along with something else.
bugs.impact: When only multicast failover is configured, traffic-groups may become active on all devices in the device-group. If unicast failover is also configured, the traffic-group might switch to a different device.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation for v12.0.0 (and later) symptom: To restore multicast failover, disable and re-enable multicast failover. To do so, perform the following procedure on the the local device. 1. Determine which interface is being used for multicast failover by running the following tmsh command: list cm device device1 multicast-interface. 3. Disable and re-enable multicast failover by running the following tmsh commands: modify cm device device1 { multicast-interface none }. modify cm device device1 { multicast-interface eth0 }. Mitigation for all versions symptoms: Do not make cm device unicast-address changes simultaneously with changes to other cm device properties.
bugs.fix: With the fix, sod now sends out multicast FO heartbeat datagrams under the same condition.

bugs.title: Policies on channel types "Other" and "Shell" may have implications on the remaining channel types as well
bugs.symptoms: For ssh proxy, if the admin has applied a Disallow or Terminate policy for a specific user or all users for "Other" and "Shell" channel types, it may disallow or terminate the remaining channel types. Currently disallowing “Other” and “Shell” will also block other channel types, namely shell, local and remote port forwarding, x11 forwarding and agent forwarding. For agent forwarding it is dependent on what kind of channel type the user uses with agent forwarding enabled. If it is shell or any forwarding type it will get disallowed, otherwise it will go through.
bugs.conditions: Disallow or Terminate policy for a specific user or all users for "Other" and "Shell" channel types needs to be applied.
bugs.impact: Usability is impacted. The admin has to be cautious of unintentionally blocking channel types when disallowing or terminating "Shell" and "Other" channels.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.

bugs.title: Large number of static arp entries on a BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: Many static arp entries for 127.20.X.X network are set for the 'tmm_bp' device on a running BIG-IP system. These will appear with any command that displays the kernel arp table, such as the 'arp' command.
bugs.conditions: -- Any platform with any set of modules provisioned. -- Running a command that displays the kernel arp table (for example, the 'arp' command).
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue only. 'arp -an' will return over 520 entries.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is cosmetic.

bugs.title: Keylogger Protection weakness in Internet Explorer
bugs.symptoms: Some types of malware can log keys using Javascript in Internet Explorer.
bugs.conditions: Endpoint infected with javascript keylogger malware. End user uses Internet Explorer.
bugs.impact: Product does not prevent keystroke logging.

bugs.title: PEM session usage via iRules immediate following PEM session creation via iRules may result in the usage not working as expected.
bugs.symptoms: PEM session usage via an iRule command may not work.
bugs.conditions: iRule that creates a PEM session and uses the session via iRule commands.
bugs.impact: iRule failure.
bugs.workaround: Add a small delay after PEM session creation via iRules

bugs.title: Route domain behavior is inconsistent
bugs.symptoms: In an APM configuration, if the route domain of the connectivity profile does not match the route domain of network access then egress traffic does not make it through even though ingress traffic does.
bugs.conditions: Network Access configuration. Route Domain Differing Route domains.
bugs.impact: Traffic is allowed (ingress traffic above) that should have been blocked.
bugs.workaround: Ensure everything is in the same route domain.

bugs.title: Dashboard does not work when custom port is used for management port.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP v12.0.0 introduced the ability to change the management port, but the dashboard was not changed to support that. Dashboard does not work when a port is used for management port other than the default port 443.
bugs.conditions: Using the dashboard when the management address is configured to use a port other than port 443.
bugs.impact: The dashboard reports a connection error and asks you to log back in.

bugs.title: kernel static route can become invalid in a SelfIp transaction
bugs.symptoms: kernel static route, default or otherwise, can become invalid, and be deleted from the kernel in a transaction, or loading configuration
bugs.conditions: Changing SelfIp address in a transaction where the address being change is the only address for a gateway or static route. Or loading a new configuration, where the SelfIp in the configuration and current SelfIp is the only address serving the static route
bugs.impact: Static route configured on the BIGIP, when loading configuration or changing SelfIp in a transaction or both add/delete is happening in the same transaction.
bugs.workaround: Delete all static routes before the transaction, or configuration load, and restore them after transaction, configuration load.
bugs.fix: SelfIp address changes in a transaction is ordered correctly to preserve affecting networking configurations.

bugs.title: Flow reporting does not occur for unclassified flows.
bugs.symptoms: Flow reports are missing for some of the flows.
bugs.conditions: Flow reporting action has been configured with no classification filter. This was observed for flows that remained unclassified until the very end.
bugs.impact: If you are using flow reports to track the data usage of the subscriber, the usage will not be accurate.
bugs.fix: For flows that do not get classified at all, the system now sends out flow reports at the end of the flow. The FLOW_INIT and FLOW_END reports are sent out in this case (that is, there are no FLOW_INTERIM reports). This is correct behavior

bugs.title: Qosmos classification result is not propagated for response-based classification.
bugs.symptoms: Qosmos classification result is not propagated for response-based classification.
bugs.conditions: No HTTP profile attached to the Virtual Server
bugs.impact: Classification result will not be propagated through the system. In the case of PEM, this issue leads to no enforcement of policy action.

bugs.symptoms: When using masquerade addresses, CPU usage increases. This can ultimately lead to a reduction in device capacity.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if one or more of your traffic groups is configured to use a MAC Masquerade address.
bugs.impact: Possible performance degradation or reduction in capacity

bugs.title: OneConnect profile with an idle or strict limit-type might lead to tmm core.
bugs.symptoms: OneConnect profile with an idle or strict limit-type might lead to tmm core.
bugs.conditions: OneConnect profile with a limit-type value of idle or strict.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use a limit-type of 'none'.
bugs.fix: A OneConnect profile using an idle or strict limit-type no longer causes the tmm to core when attempting to shutdown idle connections.

bugs.title: Subscriber info missing in flow report after subscriber has been deleted
bugs.symptoms: If we have a subscriber flow during which the subscriber gets deleted, then the flow reports begin to report subscriber id as "unknown". It becomes difficult to map the flow to that specific subscriber.
bugs.conditions: Flow reporting is enabled for a subscriber. And the subscriber gets deleted in the middle of a flow.
bugs.impact: If the customer is looking for subscriber id to match the flows, then they would miss out on these flows that get reported with unknown subscriber.
bugs.fix: We now save the subscriber id so that it can be accessed even after the subscriber has been deleted.

bugs.title: network-HSM may not be operational on secondary slots of a standby chassis.
bugs.symptoms: pkcs11d may not be running on secondary slots of a chassis.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when the following conditions are true: 1. Network-HSM installed on BIG-IP chassis. 2. Chassis is in standby state OR Secondary slots do not have management IP configured.
bugs.impact: If SSL profiles are configured with keys of security-type 'nethsm' when the specified conditions are true, traffic for such profiles will fail when the affected slots process traffic.
bugs.workaround: Manually install netHSM on each secondary slot.
bugs.fix: netHSM install no longer depends on management IP of secondary slots and also successfully installs on slots of a standby chassis.

bugs.title: Profile License May Be Missing After Failover or Blade Configuration Change In Chassis HA
bugs.symptoms: Some or all profile licenses may be missing after failover or, in a chassis high availability (HA) setup, if some blades in the standby chassis are removed, followed by failover. As a result, sessions cannot be established and the following error message will show up in the APM log. -- err tmm8[16609]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_FOUND. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_process_state_client_get_license, Line: 7135. -- err tmm8[16609]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_FOUND. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: hud_access_handler, Line: 2487.
