bugs.conditions: This failure may happen in a HA setup when 1. Failover happens, or 2. Changing multi-blade chassis HA blade configuration as follows: 2.1. Set mirroring to 'between'. 2.2. Leave the primary blade up and shut down the secondary blades in the standby chassis. 2.3 Change 'minimum numbers of blades up' to 1. 2.3. Force failover. The 1-blade chassis becomes active.
bugs.impact: Session will be terminated due to ERR_NOT_FOUND error when acquiring profile license.
bugs.workaround: For failover case: -- Disassociate and then re-associate the APM profile with the virtual server after failover. For blade configuration change, there are two options: 1. After failover, disassociate and then re-associate the APM profile with the virtual server after the 1-blade chassis becomes active 2. 2.1. Change mirroring to 'within'. 2.2. Shut down the secondary blades one by one, waiting a few minutes in between each shutdown (waiting is important because SessionDB needs some time to create backup copies). 2.3. Force failover. 2.4. Change mirroring back to 'between'.

bugs.title: Changing URL Filter logging configuration causes tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: When SWG is configured with URL filtering, changing the URL Filter log configuration while traffic is running can cause a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: Traffic is running through the box and logs are being collected while an admin simultaneously changes the configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: 1 tmm allocated per 2GB of RAM
bugs.symptoms: On Azure with 3.5GB 2vCPU configuration, only 1 tmm is started
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Virtual Edition in Public Clouds.
bugs.impact: Only allocating 1 tmm can cause under-utilized CPUs in VMs in public clouds when RAM is not multiple of 2GB/per CPU.
bugs.fix: The logic for determining number of CPUs to be used by BIGIP was changed to take into account different Cloud VE configurations like these: * 2 vCPU / 3.5 GB RAM * 4 vCPU / 7.0 GB RAM * 8 vCPU / 14.0 GB RAM Now BIG-IP will assume 1.5GB RAM/per CPU and better utilize above configuration using all available CPUs.

bugs.title: Cannot set 10T-FD or 10T-HD on management port
bugs.symptoms: When setting the B4450 or B4300 mgmt port to 10T-FD or 10T-HD, there is no link LED. However, the peer unit shows the correct link LED for this setting.
bugs.conditions: B4450 or B4300 blade and you want to set 10T-FD or 10T-HD media type
bugs.impact: Unable to set this media type.
bugs.fix: The management port of B4450 and B4300 blades can now be configured with 10T-FD or 10T-HD

bugs.title: RAM Cache Key Collision
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent tmm SIGSEGV when RAM Cache is enabled
bugs.conditions: This occurs when RAM cache is enabled in certain circumstances.
bugs.impact: Invalid response format, and/or serving the wrong object from cache, and/or tmm crash, interruption of service.
bugs.fix: The system now avoids RAM Cache Key collisions, the correct object and response format are delivered from the cache, and tmm no longer cores.

bugs.title: Too many annotations on dashboard line charts
bugs.symptoms: The dashboard lines charts are difficult to read because there are many annotations (red-filled circles on the bottom part of the diagram).
bugs.conditions: Reading any line chart with a time period other than the last five minutes reveals this issue.
bugs.impact: The user finds it difficult to read dashboard line charts.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic issue that does not indicate a problem.

bugs.title: Wrong advertised next-hop in BGP for a traffic group in Active-Active deployment
bugs.symptoms: The advertised next-hop is a floating-IP of the active traffic-group on a peer BIG-IP system, although it should be the floating-IP of the traffic-group active on the current BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- In a BIG-IP high availability (HA) configuration. -- The HA configuration is Active-Active topology. -- There are multiple traffic-groups, in which each device is active for one traffic-group.
bugs.impact: An incorrect next-hop in BGP is advertised for a traffic group in Active-Active deployment. Traffic for relevant advertised routes might go to a standby device.
bugs.workaround: Configure the floating address of a traffic group as the next-hop in its route-map.
bugs.fix: The advertised next-hop in BGP is now the smallest floating-IP active on the current BIG-IP system. Note: The ZebOS routing protocol suite available for BIG-IP configurations does not support traffic groups, so this issue might still be seen in certain circumstances.

bugs.title: Support two factor authentication for Citrix Receiver for Windows
bugs.symptoms: Two-factor authentication cannot be used with Citrix Receiver for Microsoft Windows.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP APM is configured in Citrix replacement mode configuration. -- Two-factor authentication is used in Access policy.
bugs.impact: Two-factor authentication does not work
bugs.fix: The system now supports two-factor authentication for Citrix Receiver for Windows.

bugs.title: ADAPT could time out during sending to IVS with no preview
bugs.symptoms: If ADAPT is sending a very long HTTP request or response to an internal virtual server (IVS), its timeout might expire before sending is complete, not giving a chance for the IVS to respond. This might occur in this following case: the IVS has an ICAP profile and the ICAP server waits for the entire ICAP request before responding, by which time the ADAPT timeout has fired.
bugs.conditions: A request-adapt or response-adapt profile has preview-size 0 and a timeout short enough to expire before the IVS has a chance to respond.
bugs.impact: The IVS transaction fails and ADAPT performs its service-down action. In this no-preview case, an 'ignore' (bypass) action is not possible, so the HTTP transaction fails.
bugs.workaround: Increase the timeout in the requestadapt or responseadapt profile, to cover the longest HTTP payload expected to be sent to the IVS.
bugs.fix: The ADAPT timeout begins after the entire payload has been sent to the IVS, so IVS has the full allowed time to respond.

bugs.title: ICAP/OneConnect reuses connection while previous response is in progress
bugs.symptoms: ICAP with OneConnect sometimes initiates a new ICAP request (REQMOD or RESPMOD) on the server connection while a previous response on the same connection is still being streamed from the ICAP server. This can cause the server to append the new response after the end of the previous response, in the same packet.
bugs.conditions: There is a 'oneconnect' profile on the internal virtual server along with the 'icap' profile. Triggered by a disconnection of the IVS by the parent HTTP virtual server, before the ICAP transaction is complete. This can happen for a number of reasons, such as an error in detected on the HTTP virtual server, or an HTTP::respond iRule that replaces an IVS response in progress.
bugs.impact: The connection used by the interrupted transaction is returned to the pool for reuse, potentially resulting in a new ICAP transaction beginning before the end of the interrupted one, and its response may be concatenated to the incomplete tail of the first one. OneConnect is unable to separate the contiguous ICAP responses whose boundary is within a packet. All the packet payload goes to the first ICAP transaction, and any payload after the terminating chunk is discarded. Thus the beginning of the second response is lost and its header parser gets confused. It keeps waiting for more data and rescanning the entire response, resulting in increasing CPU use up to 100% until the connection is aborted.
bugs.workaround: Remove OneConnect.
bugs.fix: Big-IP with ICAP and OneConnect never reuses a server connection while a previous ICAP transaction is still in progress. Whenever the IVS disconnects prior to completion of an ICAP transaction, the connection is not pooled for reuse.

bugs.title: Export button in EDGE client now creates a CTU report
bugs.symptoms: Export button created a Edge Client log, this log did not contain enough information for F5 to correctly diagnose many problems.
bugs.conditions: Open Edge Client, Open Details, Open view log -> Press Export
bugs.impact: F5 would have to ask customer to generate a CTU report from the Details page, delaying fixes
bugs.workaround: Use Generate CTU report button on the Details page
bugs.fix: Export button on View Logs page now generates CTU Log that contains full logging that F5 needs to diagnose problems.

bugs.title: Outbound ICAP request can double-chunk HTTP payload
bugs.symptoms: An outbound ICAP request body is double-chunked (has extra chunk headers inserted within the body chunks).
bugs.conditions: A primary virtual server has an HTTP profile and either request-adapt or response-adapt profiles, and a corresponding internal virtual server with an ICAP profile. Outbound ICAP request payload might be double-chunked if any of the following are true. Primary virtual server has a request-adapt profile and either: 1. HTTP client sends a POST request with chunked payload and the http profile has request chunking mode 'preserve' (default). 2. HTTP client sends POST request with chunked payload and the http profile has request chunking mode 'selective', unless certain other http related profiles are present on the http virtual server. Primary virtual server has a response-adapt profile and ICAP server responds with a body (200 ok), and: 3. HTTP server responds with chunked payload and the http profile has response chunking mode 'preserve'. If any of these conditions are true, the outbound ICAP request body might be double-chunked.
bugs.impact: The ICAP server receives corrupt payload and might malfunction and/or return corrupt payload to the receiving client or server.

bugs.title: Portal Access could respond very slowly for large text files when using IE < 11
bugs.symptoms: When accessing a large 'text/plain' file from server with Internet Explorer versions 7 through 10 client browsers, Portal Access sometimes holds the response until it fetches and processes the entire file contents. This can take several dozen seconds, or even minutes.
bugs.conditions: Internet Explorer version 7 through 10 with Portal Access
bugs.impact: Large text files can't be accessed or downloaded through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Irule that does any of following: a) Preferred: append F5CH=I to request uri in HTTP_REQUEST for affected requests. b) Call REWRITE::disable for affected requests.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue where Portal Access could try to buffer contents of some large files and respond with significant delay.

bugs.title: VCMP 4 cores on 3 blades : mcpd core when delete 255 dos profiles via tmsh command while machine is idle
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd crashes.
bugs.conditions: 1.create 4 cores vcmp guest on vic 1+ with 3 blades This platform has 15GB of mem 2. provision asm + ltm + AVR +FPS 3. create via script 255 dos profiles ( script attached) 4. delete it via tmsh command : delete security dos profile dos_* 5. result : Sometimes MCPD will crash
bugs.impact: Traffic and control plane disrupted while mcpd restarts.

bugs.title: Manual changes to policy imported as XML may introduce corruption for Login Pages
bugs.symptoms: Manual changes to policy imported as XML may introduce corruption for Login Pages. If the expiration period is omitted, the Login Page will be inaccessible.
bugs.conditions: Expiration period is omitted in hand-crafted XML policy file.
bugs.impact: The Login Page created as a result is inaccessible in GUI and REST.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that expiration period exists in XML policy file before import.
bugs.fix: A policy file, with a missing expiration field, imported as XML is now handled correctly.

bugs.title: TMSH allows RAN congestion and BWC to be enabled in the same policy rule.
bugs.symptoms: BWC actions will be applied while RAN congestion will not be applied.
bugs.conditions: A subscriber should be assigned a policy that has a rule with both BWC and RAN congestion enabled.
bugs.impact: RAN congestion will be disabled while BWC will be applied.
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI for policy rule configuration.

bugs.title: Webserver listening on local Wifi or ethernet IP cannot be accessed after VPN with proxy.pac file
bugs.symptoms: Webserver listening on local Wifi or ethernet IP cannot be accessed after VPN if proxy.pac is defined in a way that forwards all web traffic over VPN.
bugs.conditions: proxy.pac, network access, OS X system.
bugs.impact: Local web server is inaccessible if proxy.pac is defined in a way that forwards all traffic over VPN to corporate proxy server.
bugs.fix: Webserver listening on local Wifi or Ethernet IP can be accessed after VPN even if proxy.pac is defined in a way that forwards all web traffic over VPN to corporate proxy server.

bugs.title: Errors in IMsTscAxEvents::OnDisconnected doesn't have a text description
bugs.symptoms: The disconnect reason, extended disconnect reason are logged as numerical values. These values are not explained.
bugs.conditions: RDP session is disconnected
bugs.impact: Confusing logging, without any explanation given as to what is wrong
bugs.workaround: This (external) link to an MSDN page explaining the error codes may be helpful in interpreting the numerical values: https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa382170(v=vs.85).aspx
bugs.fix: The results from GetErrorDescription are logged

bugs.title: Periodic error "User login disallowed" messages logged referring to user "guest"
bugs.symptoms: In /var/log/ltm, the following may be seen periodically: Jan 11 14:40:43 slot1/test err mcpd[9432]: 01070827:3: User login disallowed: User (guest) is not an administrator, does not have a UID of zero, and has not been assigned a role on a partition.
bugs.conditions: Unknown
bugs.impact: Unknown, likely minimal, except extraneous logs

bugs.title: bgpd might crash in rare circumstances.
bugs.symptoms: Under unspecified conditions and in rare cases, bgpd might crash. Although bgpd restarts right away, routing table might be impacted.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are not known.
bugs.impact: This might impact routing table and reachability.
bugs.workaround: None known.

bugs.title: Edge client upgrade fails if client was configured in locked mode
bugs.symptoms: Edge client cannot be upgraded automatically to a newer version
bugs.conditions: Edge client package was downloaded with "Enable Always Connected mode" option checked Server contains a newer version of edge client
bugs.impact: Automatic upgrade of edge client will fail
bugs.workaround: Manually uninstall and re-install client

bugs.title: Staged signature false-positive violation
bugs.symptoms: False-positive blocking on staged signature.
bugs.conditions: -- A staged signature. -- A local logger is attached or the policy builder is in automatic or manual mode.
bugs.impact: A false-positive signature match.

bugs.title: Inaccurate message on missing request log record in Manual Traffic Learning
bugs.symptoms: A misleading message appears in Manual Traffic Learning screen if request log records have been deleted due to data rotation.
bugs.conditions: Request log records have been deleted due to data rotation.
bugs.impact: A misleading message may appear in Manual Traffic Learning screen.

bugs.title: Log all attempts of key export in ltm log
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to export keys are not logged.
bugs.conditions: -- Exporting keys. -- Viewing ltm log.
bugs.impact: No messages logged to indicate the export attempts.
bugs.fix: iControl: ====================== When any of the following iControl functions is called (either by the GUI or directly by a system user), the system logs it in ltm log. The log will include the iControl function name, key names, and BIG-IP user name. key_export_to_file key_export_to_pem export_all_to_archive_stream export_to_archive_stream export_all_to_archive_file export_to_archive_file ltm logs example: ====================== -- info iControlPortal.cgi[26687]: Management: private key export: keys (/Common/kc.key) in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::key_export_to_file() -- info iControlPortal.cgi[26687]: Management: private key export: keys (/Common/default.key, /Common/kc.key) in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::key_export_to_pem() -- info iControlPortal.cgi[26687]: Management: private key export: All keys in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::export_all_to_archive_stream() -- info iControlPortal.cgi[26687]: Management: private key export: keys (/Common/default.key) in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::export_to_archive_stream() -- info iControlPortal.cgi[26687]: Management: private key export: keys (/Common/default.key) in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::export_to_archive_file() -- info iControlPortal.cgi[4868]: Management: private key export: All keys in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::export_all_to_archive_file() -- info iControlPortal.cgi[4868]: Management: private key export: keys (/Common/kc.key, /Common/default.key) in Default mode are being exported by user "admin" via KeyCertificate_impl::export_to_archive_file() tmsh: ====================== The only possibility for using tmsh to export a key is saving a UCS file, so that will be logged. ltm logs example: ====================== notice tmsh[21886]: 01420012:5: private key export: All keys are being exported by user "admin" via UCS saving. GUI: ====================== There are 3 ways that a user can get key export from GUI: -- System :: Certificate Management : Traffic Certificate Management : SSL Certificate List :: default : Key Export -- System :: Certificate Management : Traffic Certificate Management : SSL Certificate List :: Archive... -- System :: Archives :: New Archive... These are internally implemented by using iControl and tmsh calls, so they will be automatically be logged in ltm log as iControl or tmsh users.
bugs.behavior: With this change, any attempt to export key will be logged in ltm log. Logged attempts include: save a UCS file, archive key files, or export key files, using tmsh/iControl/GUI.

bugs.title: NLA-awareness works incorrectly in "Always Connected Mode"
bugs.symptoms: Edge Clients configured with Network Location Awareness and Always Connected Mode will fail to connect if the client is outside of the enterprise LAN and "Allow traffic only in enterprise networks" is configured.
bugs.conditions: 1. Generate package which contains EdgeClient in always connected code, specify "Allow traffic only in enterprise networks" 2. Connect client to LAN which is not enterprise (without suffix) 3. Install and run EdgeClient
bugs.impact: Clients will be unable to connect to enterprise resources
bugs.fix: The Edge client will now pass through NLA Awareness events so that they can connect to enterprise resources.

bugs.title: tmsh show sys memory on secondaries will generate innocuous error
bugs.symptoms: The ltm log file contains these errors: err mcpd[9011]: 0107167d:3: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request (unknown request), tag (5130).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when logged into secondary member of a cluster (VIPRION blade or vCMP guest) and running the command: tmsh show sys memory.
bugs.impact: The error indicates that the secondary member cannot display information that is only presented on a primary. This is a spurious error, and you can safely ignore it.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the specific error with this signature: 0107167d:3: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request (unknown request), tag (5130).
bugs.fix: no longer displays 'Data publisher not found or not implemented' messages when running the command: tmsh show sys memory on secondary member of a cluster (VIPRION blade or vCMP guest).

bugs.title: Scheduled report lost after loading configuration
bugs.symptoms: Saved scheduled report will be lost after loading the system configuration.
bugs.conditions: Create scheduled report. Save the configuration. Load the configuration. The scheduled report wont be existing anymore.
bugs.impact: The scheduled report can be lost.
bugs.fix: A saved scheduled report is no longer lost after loading the system configuration.

bugs.title: Policy Diff/Merge Does Not Work Correctly For Session Awareness Login Pages
bugs.symptoms: When comparing Security Policies with Session Awareness enabled for specific Login Pages, false differences are shown in the Diff. Additionally, attempting to merge policies with these elements does not provide expected enforcement, as the Login Pages will not be enabled correctly in the target policy.
bugs.conditions: A Security Policy with Session Awareness Login Pages are compared with Policy Diff.
bugs.impact: False differences may appear, and merging them will not provide expected enforcement.
bugs.workaround: These elements can be ignored in the Diff Summary before an auto-merge, and handled manually.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when changing the IKE peer config.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash when changing the IKE peer config. It can happen with either IKEv1 or IKEv2 (TMM config crash).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when making changes to IPsec tunnels that causes the configuration to become invalid. For example, changing ISAKMP phase1 from SHA-1 to MD5 results in an invalid configuration. Note: This occurs in the GUI only. The tmsh 'create' command does not cause this core.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can use tmsh to make the affected configuration changes... this occurs in the GUI only. The tmsh 'create' command does not cause this core.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when changing the IKEv1 or IKEv2 peer config, even if the changes are not valid for the configuration.

bugs.title: db.proxy.__iter__ value is overwritten if it's manually set
bugs.symptoms: When setting the "BIND Forwarder Server List" on the "Configuration : Device : DNS" page, the system stores the values in the sysdb variable db.proxy.__iter__. When changing the value using tmsh or iControl, the db.proxy.__iter__ value is overwritten when subsequently viewing the value in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: When setting these values in sysdb via tmsh or REST, the values are set, but then upon re-visiting Configuration : Device : DNS in the GUI, the values in the sysdb variable are reset to their former values.
bugs.impact: BIND Forwarder Server List values do not persist.
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI to change the BIND Forwarder Server List values.

bugs.title: ACCESS::remove can result in confusing ERR_NOT_FOUND logs
bugs.symptoms: When using the iRule command ACCESS::remove, ERR_NOT_FOUND messages may appear in /var/log/apm. Theses are not real errors. ACCESS is trying to insert a session variable, but it is not able to find the session because the iRule already deleted the session. The logs in /var/log/apm look something like this: err tmm1[15932]: 01490514:3: 00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_FOUND. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_save_init_req_to_sessiondb, Line: 14823.
bugs.conditions: An iRule using the command ACCESS::remove, and the end-user does a POST.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, the iRule correctly deletes the session, and BIG-IP does not send a reset. But the log messages can be alarming or confusing.
bugs.fix: ACCESS::remove no longer results in confusing ERR_NOT_FOUND logs.

bugs.title: Erroneous syncookie flag in HSB return descriptor causes the BIG-IP system to pass through the ACK packets after the session is closed.
bugs.symptoms: In rare situations, a packet with ACK flag arriving shortly after the FIN packet is received on a flow might be marked by FPGA to be a valid syncookie response. The BIG-IP system creates a new connection for the ACK packet and passes the packet to the server side, causing a double transaction on the server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the unlikely event of an ACK packet accidentally matching the match hardware syncookie.
bugs.impact: Confusion on the client/server and double transaction on the server side.

bugs.title: Files with file names larger than 100 characters are omitted from qkview
bugs.symptoms: If the filename of a file being gathered by qkview happens to be larger than 100 characters, the qkview will simply not include it.
bugs.conditions: No conditions necessary. Any file with a name larger than 100 characters is automatically omitted.
bugs.impact: Files with names larger than 100 characters are being omitted from the qkview. Since UNIX files can be 256 characters long, this potentially could omit important files that could help diagnose problems.
bugs.workaround: One would have to rename any files with names larger than 100 characters to names with less than 100 characters.
bugs.fix: Qkview was fixed to not use POSIX as the tar format, but instead to use the "GNU" format which allows for up to 256 characters (the system limit). The fixed program now allows any length of characters possible.

bugs.title: Database Changes not Propagated to All Blades
bugs.symptoms: Using the TMSH interface to change a DB variable does not always result in propagating the value change to all blades.
bugs.conditions: In a clustered configuration, a change to the sys db wam.cache.range.maxranges value will be applied to the primary blade, but not to the secondary blades.
bugs.impact: Traffic could be processed differently on one blade vs another.

bugs.title: Disabling global Auto Last Hop setting breaks APM's Remote Desktop Gateway (RDG) feature
bugs.symptoms: Existing TCP connection is being sporadically disrupted by the BIG-IP virtual server sending out a SYN, ACK, causing existing connection to fail. The client and virtual server set up a good TCP connection, complete the SSL handshake, and start to pass application data. APM virtual server then sends SYN, ACK with sequence and ACK numbers that do not match the existing stream. The APM then tries three SYN-ACKs before giving up and sending out a RST-ACK, which drops the connection attempt, but as it shares the same ip:port number as the existing connection, resets the good connection.
bugs.conditions: Auto Last Hop setting is disabled.
bugs.impact: APM RDG feature does not work
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Enable Auto Last Hop. -- Set cmp_enabled to 'NO' on the virtual server.
bugs.fix: APM RDG feature now works as expected when Auto Last Hop is disabled.

bugs.title: SNMP TMM memory stats need to be presented per TMM process
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory stats presented by the enterprise MIB table sysTmmStatTable are presented per TmmId - which is defined as slot.cpu_number. However, a single TMM process can have multiple TmmIds with the number depending on the BIG-IP platform.
bugs.conditions: All
bugs.impact: No impact on services, but this places a burden on SNMP Monitors to summarize TmmId memory stats for a given TMM process.
bugs.workaround: The total memory allocated and used by a particular TMM process can be summarized at the SNMP Monitoring end using the sysTmmStatTmmPid to determine which TmmIds belong to the TMM process.
bugs.fix: A new enterprise MIB table, sysTmmProcStatTable, has been introduced that presents TMM memory statistics per TmmPid, where the TmmPid is the Linux Process Id for a TMM instance running on a specific slot.

bugs.title: Edge client uninstaller on windows leaves some client components on user's machine
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge client is not uninstalled completely from user's machine.
bugs.conditions: msiexec /x "f5fpclients.msi" is used to uninstall Edge Client.
bugs.impact: Edge Client is not uninstalled completely
bugs.workaround: Remove the remaining components using Windows "Add/Remove programs" or use the following command to remove the remaining components: "C:\%ProgramData%\\F5 Networks\f5unistall.exe" [/r] /uninstall"

bugs.title: Config verify may alter tacacs system-auth
bugs.symptoms: TACACS system-auth stops working after running config verify.
bugs.conditions: Running config verify where the tacacs system-auth does not match the running config (e.g., altered secret or server list).
bugs.impact: Unable to login to system with tacacs system-auth.
bugs.workaround: Reload the running configuration.

bugs.title: Possible gtmd crash under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: gtmd core leading to a SIGSEV due to a possible race condition.
bugs.conditions: Due to a possible race condition that occurs under certain conditions (such as a sync event), gtmd might core.
bugs.impact: This event could lead to an outage.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly processes this condition so that no race condition occurs.

bugs.title: ca-devices and non-ca-devices addition/deletion has been removed from restart cm trust-domain Root
bugs.symptoms: The properties 'ca-devices' and 'non-ca-device' are available in the 'restart' command but are not valid.
bugs.impact: You should not use the restart command with the properties 'ca-devices' and 'non-ca-device'. It has to be used similar to the delete command.
bugs.workaround: A new tmsh command to reset a device trust was added: 'restart cm trust-domain Root' which operates exactly like 'delete cm trust-domain Root'. The properties 'ca-devices' and 'non-ca-device' are available in the 'restart' command but are not valid. These properties are not available in the 'delete cm trust-domain'. Workaround for customer is to not use these two properties when running the 'restart cm trust-domain' command or to use the 'delete cm trust-domain'
bugs.fix: The 'ca-devices' and 'non-ca-devices' properties were removed from the tmsh command 'restart cm trust-domain' command because they are not valid.

bugs.title: IPsec GUI 'General database error' setting KBLifetime to max value
bugs.symptoms: Using the GUI, setting the Network : IPsec : IPsec Polices : KBLifetime attribute of a policy might trigger a 'General database error' for any KBLifetime value from 2147483648 to 4294967295.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI and setting KBLifetime values 2147483648 to 4294967295.
bugs.impact: Unable to set KBLifetime values 2147483648 to 4294967295 from the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Set the KBLifetime value using tmsh.

bugs.title: intermittent SSL traffic failure with Safenet HSM on BIG-IP chassis and appliance
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP intermittently has SSL traffic failures with HSM. This symptom happens on both chassis and appliance. The general error messages are logged with "FIPS acceleration device failure: fips_poll_completed_reqs: req: 44 status: 0x1 : Cancel"
bugs.conditions: When Safenet HSM is used with BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: SSL traffic is failing.
bugs.workaround: "bigstart restart pkcs11d" might mitigate this issue.
bugs.fix: Multiple issues are fixed including better sync-up between tmm and pkcs11d. Fixes are also included to deal with key handle changes at HSM.

bugs.title: IPsec does not send phase 2 delete.
bugs.symptoms: IPsec does not remove IKE-SA on change traffic selector. As result there are uneven SA status between IPsec devices and it can cause significant delay in communication.
bugs.conditions: Change traffic selector on one device, and force delete SA on the same device, but do not propagate to the other one.
bugs.impact: This might result in significant delays in communication.
bugs.workaround: Delete SA manually. Note: This workaround might not be possible.

bugs.title: [LTM][DNS] save-on-auto-sync with partitions fails for LTM DNS partition objects
bugs.symptoms: Even though 'auto-sync enabled' and 'save-on-auto-sync true' are set on a device group which has a partition assigned to it, creating an LTM DNS object in the partition is successfully transmitted to the running configuration of the peer device, but not written to bigip.conf.
bugs.conditions: 1. auto-sync and save-on-auto-sync enabled for device group. 2. The device group has a partition assigned to it. 3. Creating a ltm dns partition object.
bugs.impact: Changes are not written to conf files as expected.
bugs.workaround: Save configuration manually at regular intervals on peer box.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue where ltm dns objects are not being saved to their proper partition bigip.conf files when in a partition other than /Common/. This means that partitioned objects will be saved automatically when save-on-auto-sync is enabled for corresponding device groups. This affects ltm dns nameservers, zones, and tsig-keys.
bugs.behavior: LTM DNS objects (zones, tsig-keys, and nameservers) are now partitioned, so they will be saved to their corresponding partitons bigip_gtm.conf file under /config/partitions/. Because these objects are now partitioned, it also means user permissions to read / modify these objects will match the user permissions assigned to that partition.

bugs.title: BD Memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: An Enforcer crash occurs and UMU errors may appear in the bd.log file.
bugs.impact: Traffic goes down while the Enforcer goes back up.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory corruption issue.

bugs.title: Linux CLI client does not follow redirect response coming from APM
bugs.symptoms: If access policy on APM has redirect ending, Linux CLI client will fail to establish VPN.
bugs.conditions: Linux CLI client is used to establish VPN APM access policy has redirect ending.
bugs.impact: Cannot establish VPN.
bugs.workaround: Do not use redirection in access policy for Linux CLI client.
bugs.fix: Now Linux CLI client can follow redirect responses coming from APM.

bugs.title: User cannot perform endpoint check or launch VPN from Firefox on Windows 10
bugs.symptoms: If Firefox is used on Windows 10 to connect to APM, access policy may fail, or system fails to launch VPN.
bugs.conditions: Firefox is used to connect to APM on Windows 10. The following conditions are exclusive and have different impact: 1) Access policy requires client side inspection. 2) Attempt to launch VPN from WebTop.
bugs.impact: 1) Access policy will fail. 2) VPN cannot be launched from WebTop.
bugs.fix: User can now perform endpoint check or launch VPN from Firefox on Windows 10.

bugs.title: DoS vectors must be enabled in both DoS Profile and Device Configuration
bugs.symptoms: In order for a DoS vector in a DoS Profile to detect a you must enable that same vector in the DoS Device Configuration.
bugs.conditions: DoS vector configured at the per-virtual server level, but not at the device level.
bugs.impact: Might result in false negatives.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following workaround: 1. Enable the vector in Security : DoS Protection : DoS Profiles. To do so, click Network Protection, click Enabled, and enable the DoS Vector for the DoS Profile. 2. Enable the vector in the Device Configuration. To do so, go to Security : Dos Protection : Device Configuration, select the vector, and then configure the vector either manually, or with the auto-configuration option.

bugs.title: Syncookie mode is activated on wildcard virtuals
bugs.symptoms: Syncookie mode can be activated with a wildcard virtual, even in the case where there is no SYN flood.
bugs.conditions: The default number of connections per second before activating syncookie mode is 1993. This value can be increased to a max of 4093. After this threshold is reached, then syncookie mode is activated. This is an insufficient maximum for wildcard virtuals, since they can have 30k+ connections per second.
bugs.impact: Syncookie mode is activated with high connection rates to a wildcard virtual.
bugs.workaround: Break up the wildcard virtual into multiple virtuals to reduce the number of connections per virtual.
bugs.fix: It is now possible to set the PvaSynCookies.Virtual.MaxSynCache DB variable to 64K (previous max was 4093)

bugs.title: iRules commands that refer to a transport-config will fail validation
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule command refers to a transport-config, the iRule fails validation even if the object exists.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule command refers to a transport-config. -- iRule validation occurs. Example: create ltm pool p1 members add { 10.2.3.4:5060 } create ltm message-routing sip transport-config tc1 profiles add { udp sipsession } create ltm virtual vs1 destination 10.1.1.50:5060 profiles add { udp sipsession siprouter } create ltm rule r1 ltm rule r1 { when MR_INGRESS { MR::message route config tc1 pool p1 <==command refers to tc1 which is a transport-config object } }
bugs.impact: Validation fails even though object exists. Unable to directly refer to a transport-config from an iRule command.
bugs.workaround: If the name of the transport-config is loaded into a Tcl variable, the Tcl variable can be use to indirectly refer to the transport-config object.
bugs.fix: iRule validation logic has been improved to check for the existence of a transport config object.

bugs.title: Version Check fails when upgrading across a major version boundary
bugs.symptoms: The Edge client's version check is failing to check across a major version boundary, which causes the installer to not automatically update. F5InstServLog.txt reports the the following message service.cpp, 2015, VerifyPackage(), (0x64d) EXCEPTION - this is an old or same version - do not upgrade
bugs.conditions: Install EdgeClient from BIG-IP v12.0.0. Use EdgeClient to connect to a BIG-IP v12.1.0
bugs.impact: Edge Client auto-installer fails.
bugs.fix: The Edge client version check now properly detects new versions.

bugs.title: ASM fails to start with error - ndefined subroutine &F5::CRC::get_crc32
bugs.symptoms: ASM fails to start with error in ts_debug.log - Undefined subroutine &F5::CRC::get_crc32 called at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/RamCache.pm line 69
bugs.conditions: asm provisioned
bugs.impact: asm fails to start
bugs.fix: A rare condition in which asm fails to start has been fixed

bugs.title: Down IPsec traffic-selector shows as 'up' in 'show net ipsec traffic-selector' and in GUI
bugs.symptoms: After an SA goes down, 'show net ipsec traffic-selector' may report that the traffic-selector is up. The Web UI also reports up.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if a tunnel times out and goes to the down state.
bugs.impact: Confusion on the true state of the tunnel.
bugs.workaround: None needed.
bugs.fix: Now, when a tunnel times out and goes to the down state, the state is shown correctly.

bugs.title: Gy quota and end of session reporting does not work under certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: Gy quota and end of session reports are not sent for a session under certain conditions. The conditions include scenarios when classification is disabled on the virtual that handles the session or classification is enabled and no actions or classification filters under a session's policy. The other condition can be that classification is Enabled and there is no policy against a session.
bugs.conditions: 1. Classification Disabled on the virtual that handles the session 2. Classification Enabled AND no actions or classification filters under a session's policy 3. Classification Enabled AND no policy against a session
bugs.impact: Lack of Gy quota and end of session reports for a session
bugs.workaround: To workaround this, for the first two conditions, disable optimization where based on policies or actions and certain HUD nodes are removed.

bugs.title: TMM core when dnssec queries to dns-express zone exceed nethsm capacity
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes, and in /var/log/ltm you see entries indicating "Signature failed": err tmm1[16816]: 01010216:3: DNSSEC: Signature failed (signature creation) for RRSET (host0530.f5test.net, 1) with key /Common/myZSK2, generation 1.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when a dns-express zone generates more responses than the Thales can sign. The excess requests are queued and tmm can core.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer core when dnssec queries to dns-express zone exceed nethsm capacity.

bugs.title: CSR administrative Email attribute and Certificate Subjectâ€™s DN Email address
bugs.symptoms: The Email address entered in the GUI is also there in generated CSR certificate subject DN email address(without associated SAN rfc822name), thus generated CSR is not RFC5280 conforming. And there is no way to use different email for CSR administrative email address and certificate subject DN email address.
bugs.conditions: CSR generated though GUI by providing Email address is not RFC5280 conforming.
bugs.impact: GUI generates non RFC5280 conforming CSR.
bugs.workaround: Email address field in GUI can only be used for certificate subjects DN email address and when entered also enter rfc822name in subject alternative field. Example: If "test@test.com" entered in 'Email Address' field, then also include "email:test@test.com" in 'Subject Alternative Name' field.
bugs.fix: Should be able enter different email in certificate properties (SAN/subject), administrative email of the CSR and generated CSR is RFC5280 conforming

bugs.title: CSR attribute email and certificate Subject's DN email are not distinguished
bugs.symptoms: The email entered when creating a CSR is used as the CSR attribute email and the email in the certificate properties (SAN/subject)
bugs.conditions: Creating a CSR via iControl or TMSH
bugs.impact: Unable to generate a separate email attribute in the CSR as well as the certificate subject's DN email
bugs.behavior: With iControl or TMSH, When CSR with Subject's DN containing an EmailAddress created then a RFC822Name SAN entry with that EmailAddress is added automatically. For iControl or TMSH, If provided SAN is not short enough(current max length is 4095 chars) to automatically add RFC822Name SAN entry, then it will throw an error saying "Certificates with Subjectâ€™s DN containing an Email Address must also have a RFC822Name SAN entry with that Email Address and failed to automatically include as the length exceeded 4095 characters."

bugs.title: Dedup Cache Refresh may fail to re-initialize WOM endpoint
bugs.symptoms: WOM endpoints are not always re-initialized correctly when for dedup cache refresh operations: tmsh modify wom remote-endpoint all dedup-action cache-refresh
bugs.conditions: WOM
bugs.impact: iSession tunnels do not establish.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart

bugs.title: Some ZebOS daemons do not start on blade transition secondary to primary.
bugs.symptoms: In some specific cases the standby unit's secondary blade ZebOS daemons might not get started when it becomes active.
bugs.conditions: If the failover occurs as a result of the primary blade's mcpd restarting
bugs.impact: The new primary blade does not start some ZebOS daemons resulting in ospf not working as expected on the standby unit.
bugs.workaround: Run the following tmsh command on the new active unit: bigstart restart tmrouted.
bugs.fix: The BIG_IP system now correctly starts ZebOS daemons on the standby unit on a new blade that is starting up as a primary.

bugs.title: iControl query does not respect global cli settings when returning service values (number vs name).
bugs.symptoms: iControl queries that return a service value do not respect the global cli service setting. The iControl query always returns the service name even when the cli service setting is set to 'number'.
bugs.conditions: The cli global settings are configured to always display the service number using the following command: tmsh modify cli global-settings service number Using iControl queries that expect a service number.
bugs.impact: The iControl query always returns the service name.
bugs.fix: iControl query returns service name / port number based on global cli setting.

bugs.title: Virtual server using NTLM profile results in benign Tcl error
bugs.symptoms: Tcl error in /var/log/ltm. Tcl error: bad option "serverside": must be require or preclude while executing "constrain NTLM require clientside {HTTP} serverside {CONNPOOL} preclude FTP
bugs.conditions: Virtual server using the NTLM profile. Only logged when the first virtual server is created or when TMM restarts.
bugs.impact: If you are using TMSH to configure virtual server and NTLM profile, validation/constraint is not performed/enforced.
bugs.workaround: This is a benign, cosmetic error. There should be no functional impact to the system.
bugs.fix: Fixed the unexpected error message encountered and added validation when creating a virtual server with an NTLM profile.

bugs.title: Advanced Detection rate limiting can be incorrect in multi-blade clusters when rate limit is low
bugs.symptoms: If you have a large CMP configuration using Advanced Detection and rate limiting with a low rate limit applied, the per-core rate limit on attack traffic can end up being lower than the desired overall rate limit.
bugs.conditions: This was seen during internal testing with a large number of cores (3 blades / 24 cores) and a very low rate limit applied.
bugs.impact: Overall rate limit is lower than expected.
bugs.fix: Improvements were made to rate limiting in environments with a high number of tmms

bugs.title: A Set-Cookie for an existing ASM cookie without value change
bugs.symptoms: A Set-Cookie command appears for an ASM cookie (TS cookie) where the value has not changed and the set-cookie command is not needed.
bugs.conditions: -- The policy building is automatic or manual mode. -- Additional features may also cause TS cookie setting, but usually these will also include cookie changes.
bugs.impact: The unneeded cookie may disturb caching and cause additional unnecessary bandwidth consumption.
bugs.workaround: If possible, turn off the policy builder.
bugs.fix: Unneeded set cookie for an ASM cookie is not issued.

bugs.title: After connectivity loss and restoration between HSM and pkcs11d, SSL fails on some blades.
bugs.symptoms: After connectivity loss and restoration between HSM and pkcs11d, SSL fails on some blades.
bugs.conditions: Connectivity loss and restoration between HSM and pkcs11d.
bugs.impact: Sometimes, one or more blades have SSL failure consistently. Others are working fine after the network restoring.
bugs.workaround: None. This is an intermittent failure.
bugs.fix: All blades now recover the working condition after the network is restored.

bugs.title: BIG-IP logs INVALID-SPI messages but does not remove the associated SAs.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system logs INVALID-SPI messages but does not remove the associated Security Associations (SAs) corresponding to the message. Note: There are three parts to this issue, as recorded in the following bugs: 569236, 583285, and 662331.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if an IPsec peer deletes a phase2 (IPsec) SA and does not send a 'notify delete' message to the other peer. The INVALID-SPI message is most likely to be seen when the peer deletes an SA before the SA's agreed lifetime.
bugs.impact: If the BIG-IP is always the Initiator, the Responder will not initiate a new tunnel if the Responder only handles responses to the BIG-IP clients' traffic. The BIG-IP system continues to use the IPsec SA it believes to be still up. When an SA expires prematurely, some IPsec peers will reject an inbound SPI packet with an ISAKMP INVALID-SPI notify message. If the INVALID-SPI message does not cause new SAs to be created, there will be a tunnel outage until the SA lifetime expires on the defunct SA held on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Manually remove the invalid SA on the BIG-IP system by running the following command: delete /net ipsec ipsec-sa spi <invalid_spi>
bugs.fix: Now, when the BIG-IP system receives INVALID-SPI messages, it deletes the invalid Security Association as well as logging the INVALID-SPI message, so the tunnel can initiate again. Note: There is a three-part fix provided for this issue, as provided in the following bugs: 569236, 583285, and 662331.

bugs.title: Network Access incorrectly manipulates routing table when second adapter being connected if "Allow Local subnet access' is set to ON
bugs.symptoms: When Network Access is already established and a second network interface is being connected to client system, VPN quickly reconnects, which breaks existing TCP connections. Because reconnect occurs very quickly, it might appear to the user that nothing happened.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Allow Local subnet access' enabled. -- Client system is getting second network interface connected.
bugs.impact: Long-standing TCP connection may break, for example, VPN over Network Access.
bugs.workaround: Disable 'Allow Local subnet access'.
bugs.fix: Now Network Access remains stable when a second network interface is being connected, so any long-standing TCP connections (such as VPN over Network Access) continue as expected.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ CM 4.6 incompatible with BIG-IP 11.6.1.
bugs.symptoms: The restnoded process on the BIG-IP system continuously cycles after discovery by BIG-IQ CM 4.6.
bugs.conditions: Using BIG-IQ CM 4.6 to discover BIG-IP systems running 11.6.1.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ CM 4.6 cannot manage BIG-IP 11.6.1.
bugs.workaround: Do not use BIG-IQ CM 4.6 to discover BIG-IP systems running version 11.6.1.

bugs.title: Request to /my.policy.php3 will return 302 redirect to /vdesk/webtop.eui?webtop=... with rotated MRHSession.
bugs.symptoms: If access policy looks like following: Start --> Logon Page --> iRule event --> Full Resource assign --> Allow Request to /my.policy.php3 will return 302 redirect to /vdesk/webtop.eui?webtop=... with rotated MRHSession. In case when no iRule Event in AP it will return 200 code with rotated MRHSession.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create the following access policy. NOTE: iRule event can be created after following this link http://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/11000/200/sol11225 Start --> Logon Page --> iRule event --> Full Resource assign --> Allow 2. Use Edge Client to connect to the box with this access policy. It will fail. 3. Now remove iRule event agent from access policy and connect using Edge Client again. It will pass now.
bugs.impact: Connecting to the box with this access policy will fail.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not delete the SA on peer box after erase/modify ike-peer
bugs.symptoms: After erase/modify ike-peer command, phase 1-2 SA is deleted on one system, but is not deleted on the peer.
bugs.conditions: Run an erase/modify ike-peer command on one system in a peer configuration.
bugs.impact: Possible lost of connectivity (if initiator has SA but receiver does not).
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, delete SA manually on the peer system.

bugs.title: L2 loop on the BIG-IP system's management port network might cause VIPRION to reboot
bugs.symptoms: Several 'kernel: BUG: soft lockup' messages from kernel leading to TMM. Eventual blade reboot
bugs.conditions: -- Using vCMP. -- Network to which the BIG-IP management port is connected has a Layer 2 loop.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system is unusable and eventually reboots.
bugs.workaround: Avoid L2 loops in the network to which the BIG-IP management port is connected.

bugs.title: Different LACP key may be used in different blades in a chassis system causing trunking failures
bugs.symptoms: In rare conditions, different blades in a chassis system may use different LACP keys for the same trunk in the LACP control frames. This will cause some of the LACP trunk members not able to aggregate successfully with peer switch.
bugs.conditions: This only happens in a chassis based system when certain race condition causes trunk id being modified after initial trunk creation.
bugs.impact: Non aggregated trunk members won't be able to pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: Restart lacpd in all the blades in the chassis by running command "clsh bigstart restart lacpd"

bugs.title: Edge client does not use logon credentials even when "Reuse Windows Logon Credentials" is selected
bugs.symptoms: User is shown the logon page to connect to VPN after he logs on. Windows logon credentials are not used for VPN automatically.
bugs.conditions: Connectivity profile has "Reuse Windows Logon Credentials" selected
bugs.impact: User has to retype his credentials to connect to VPN
bugs.workaround: Enter the credentials again to connect to VPN
bugs.fix: Now logged on credentials are used automatically to connect to VPN

bugs.title: Clientside HTML parser does not recognize HTML event attributes without value
bugs.symptoms: Assignment of a specific HTML content to tag.innerHTML could lead to a JavaScript error. This happens when one or more of tags in HTML text contain html event attributes without value (such as <div onclick />) Following or similar error is logged in browser JavaScript console: Unable to get property 'charAt' of undefined or null reference
bugs.impact: Web application does not work when accessed through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: iRule could be provided for specific application.
bugs.fix: Now empty inline event handler attributes are not rewritten on client side.
bugs.conditions: Dynamically created HTML page with event attributes without values, for example: <div onclick />

bugs.title: Core occurs on standby in MRF when routing to a route using a transport config
bugs.symptoms: If routing a message to a route that uses a transport-config to define how to create an outgoing connection, the standby device will core.
bugs.conditions: routing a message to a route that uses a transport-config to define how to create an outgoing connection.
bugs.impact: The standby device will core.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Fix properly initializes a field on the standby.

bugs.title: Recovery from Amazon Network Failure may associate some virtual addresses to the standby BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Traffic will not pass to virtual servers of a traffic group
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP AWS High Availability AWS network outage
bugs.impact: Some of virtual addresses end up associated with the standby BIG-IP; traffic will not pass to their virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: If the desired BIG-IP is standby, failover to the BIG-IP. If the desired BIG-IP is already active, failover from this BIG-IP and then failover back to this BIG-IP.

bugs.title: TCP events are logged twice in a HA setup
bugs.symptoms: TCP log events are logged twice (if enabled in security log profile) with connection mirroring enabled on the virtual server in a HA setup (Active/Standby).
bugs.conditions: When there's a HA setup (Active/Standby) or both client side and server side connection flow.
bugs.impact: TCP log events are logged twice (duplicate events from active unit and standby unit or from both client side and server side of the connection flow).
bugs.fix: TCP log events are no longer logged twice when enabled in the security log profile with connection mirroring enabled on the virtual server in a HA setup (Active/Standby).

bugs.title: Packet's vlan priority is not preserved for CMP redirected flows when net cos feature is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When net cos (class of Service) feature is enabled, vlan priority for those cmp redirected packets are not being preserved from ingress to egress.
bugs.conditions: 1. net cos feature is enabled 2. packet is being cmp redirected from one tmm to another tmm for processing.
bugs.impact: Egress packets are not being processed according to the ingress vlan priority by BIG-IP and down stream router. Certain packets will be dropped by downstream router due to the wrong mark of vlan priority.

bugs.title: BGP ECMP learned routes may use incorrect VLAN for nexthop
bugs.symptoms: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) with Equal Cost Multipath (ECMP) may result in learned routes that use an incorrect nexthop Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN). As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: The system may randomly send the traffic using the incorrect nexthop.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP configuration with two or more VLANs configured with IPv6 global addresses. -- BGP with ECMP is peered with an active IPv6 BGP neighbor. -- BGP is configured with max-paths.
bugs.impact: The traffic randomly gets sent using the incorrect nexthop.
bugs.fix: Routes learned from the peer now have the correct nexthop VLANs.

bugs.title: Added --num_threads option to nethsm-thales-install.sh and nethsm-safenet-install.sh
bugs.symptoms: As part of the netHSM install, it is not possible to specify the number of threads for pkcs11d to use.
bugs.conditions: Using BIG-IP versions 11.x, 12.x, or 13.0.0.
bugs.impact: Cannot specify the number of threads for pkcs11d to use.
bugs.workaround: To set the number of threads, after install, run a separate tmsh command to set the number of threads and then restart pkcs11d.
bugs.fix: nethsm-thales-install.sh and nethsm-safenet-install.sh now have a --num_threads option to specify the number of threads pkcs11d will use. This simplifies the initial setup process for users that want to use a non-default number of threads.
bugs.behavior: nethsm-thales-install.sh and nethsm-safenet-install.sh now have a --num_threads option to specify the number of threads pkcs11d will use. This simplifies the initial setup process for users that want to use a non-default number of threads.

bugs.title: TMM segfault in lb_why_pmbr_str after GTM/BIG-IP DNS disables a GTM pool and LB why log is enabled
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores with sigsegv within lb_why_pmbr_str.
bugs.conditions: 1. Disable a GTM/BIG-IP DNS pool or pool member; 2. pool-member-selection is enabled for load-balancing-decision-log-verbosity.
bugs.impact: tmm cores.
bugs.workaround: Disable pool-member-selection for load-balancing-decision-log-verbosity.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer cores when disabling pool-member-selection for load-balancing-decision-log-verbosity.

bugs.title: Invalid WideIP name without dots crashes gtmd.
bugs.symptoms: If a user creates a WideIP or WideIP Alias with a name that does not contain a dot, gtmd crashes. The symptom is a crash and core dump from gtmd.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- FQDN validation is suppressed by the following setting: gtm global-settings general domain-name-check == 'none'. -- User attempts to create a WideIP with a name that does not contain a dot.
bugs.impact: gtmd crashes and WideIPs do not function.
bugs.workaround: When creating a WideIP or WideIP Alias while FQDN validation has been disabled (by setting gtm global-settings general domain-name-check == 'none'), make sure that the WideIP or WideIP Alias name contains at least one dot, and follows these rules: -- The name must not end with a dot. -- The name must not begin with a dot, unless '.' is the entire name. -- The name contains no consecutive dots.
bugs.fix: FQDN now validates to confirm that a WideIP or WideIP Alias name has at least one dot in an appropriate position, and has no consecutive dots, so there is no crash and core dump from gtmd. This validation occurs even when other FQDN validation has been suppressed by setting gtm globlal-settings general domain name check == 'none'.

bugs.title: After upgrade, user cannot upload APM Sandbox hosted-content file in a partition existing before upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade, an existing user-created partition will not be able to load any existing hosted-content file or upload a new one. The issue happens because the required APM Sandbox directory w.r.t. this partition is missing after the upgrade. 01070734:3: Configuration error: Cannot create symbolic link to sandbox. Error: No such file or directory. If you have access to bash shell, try to run command: ln -s /config/filestore/files_d/p1_file_d/sandbox_file_d /var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/p1_d/sandbox_file_d. Then try to upload file again. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. REPRODUCTION STEPS: 1) Before upgrade, create a partition (make sure APM is provisioned), say 'p1'. 2) Install the upgrade and reboot. 3) After upgrade, partition 'p1' is created but the required directory '/var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/p1_d' is not created. This can occur on upgrades from prior to 11.6.0 to 11.6.0 through 12.1.0.
bugs.conditions: Partition is created before the upgrade.
bugs.impact: Configuration load fails if the existing partition had any hosted-content file before upgrade. If it did not have any hosted-content file before upgrade, the configuration load will be successful, but the user cannot upload/create a new hosted-content file in this partition sandbox.
bugs.workaround: Workaround is manually create the required sandbox directory using bash command: mkdir -p /var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/p1_d

bugs.title: Sockets resource leak after loading complex policy
bugs.symptoms: File descriptors used by apmd remain unclosed (TCP and UDP) after loading a complex access policy. After some time, the APM process file descriptor table is exhausted and no more access policies are processed. The following error messages may be observed in the logs: err apmd[16013]: 01490000:3: HTTPParser.cpp func: "readFromSocket()" line: 86 Msg: epoll_create() failed [Too many open files].
bugs.conditions: This can happen at the initial stage after apmd starts, or later when policies are reloaded. Although this is not directly related to log-level, this problem is easier to observe when the access control log-level is Warning or lower (Notice, Info, Debug). File descriptors leak (remain unclosed) after loading complex policies that contain many agents.
bugs.impact: The APM process is unable to create new sessions, leading to an inability to process access policy operations.
bugs.workaround: This can happen at the initial stage after apmd starts, or later when policies are reloaded. Current preferred workaround is to set log level to ERROR or higher and restart apmd. When a large number of file descriptors has already been observed, the only way to close them other than disabling logging is to raise log levels to ERROR or above, and then issue the following command: bigstart restart apmd Note 1: Do not use sys db variables to change log level for versions 12.0.0 and later. Note 2: Double-check log levels using the following command: tmsh list apm log-setting all-properties Note 3: Opened file descriptors do not close until apmd is restarted. Note 4: When in doubt (about whether file descriptors are leaking), run the following command on the BIG-IP system: lsof -p `pidof apmd` | grep TCP; lsof -p `pidof apmd` | grep UDP. This gives you the number of open files. - Detailed steps to change logging-level to ERROR: Step 1. Modify access control log level using the following command: tmsh modify apm log-setting all access modify { all { log-level { access-control err } } } Step 2. Check the log levels using the following command: tmsh list apm log-setting all-properties Step 3. Manually restart apmd using the following command: bigstart restart apmd
bugs.fix: Sockets are now closed properly, so there is no longer file descriptor leakage when loading or reloading complex access policies.

bugs.title: Secondary Blade Rejects All Traffic after being added to the chassis
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade ends in errors, the device may be left in a state that it erroneously believes to still be in the middle of the upgrade.
bugs.conditions: A second blade is installed into a chassis and there are errors as it comes up. System configuration is never successfully loaded. This can occur during upgrades to versions prior to 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: Secondary blade blocks all ASM traffic.
bugs.workaround: 1) Delete the /var/ts/var/install/ucs_install.pid file on all blades 2) Push a fresh sync from a good device.
bugs.fix: The system correctly detects that it is no longer in the middle of an upgrade.

bugs.title: Aced process is not able to listen to port 6000
bugs.symptoms: When Aced process cannot listen to the port, it aborts and causes core dump to be produced.
bugs.conditions: In certain scenarios, an exiting instance of aced process does not perform a proper cleanup of the socket(listening of port 6000) and does not exit completely and the new instance of aced wont be able to listen to it.
bugs.impact: Aced process keeps crashing repeatedly.
bugs.fix: Aced process is fixed in order to explicitly close the socket file descriptor during exit. The new instance will be able to listen to that port.

bugs.title: Deleting all routes on a unit with a mirroring fastL4 Virtual may cause TMM to core
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances TMM may core if an HA pair configured with mirroring has all the routes to the server pool removed.
bugs.conditions: - HA pair. - FastL4 VIP with mirroring. - default route to pool via an intermediate router. - The active unit is handling traffic. - Active unit fails over and loses its mirroring connection. - Prior active unit comes back and HA connection is reestablished. - During the loss of HA and its recovery the now active unit loses its only route to the pool member.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not remove all routes to poolmembers. If this is needed please create other backup routes prior to the deletion.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores on deleting all routes on a unit with a mirroring fastL4 Virtual during HA connection loss and recovery.

bugs.title: Puffin browser is recognized as Chrome
bugs.symptoms: Puffin browser is recognized as Chrome that may cause a web page rendering issue.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP must have AAM module provisioned and have a policy with image optimization enabled attached to a virtual.
bugs.impact: When a user with Puffin client accesses the website AAM can convert image to webp format not recognized by the client. It will cause incorrect rendering of the webpage.
bugs.workaround: Disable conversion to webp.

bugs.title: Maxthon browser is recognized as Chrome
bugs.symptoms: Maxthon browser is recognized as Chrome that may cause a web page rendering issue.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP must have AAM module provisioned and have a policy with image optimization enabled attached to a virtual.
bugs.impact: When a user with Maxthon client accesses the website AAM can convert image to webp format not recognized by the client. It will cause incorrect rendering of the webpage.
bugs.workaround: Disable conversion to webp.

bugs.title: BOLT client browser is recognized incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: BOLT browser is recognized as Safari which may cause a web page rendering issue.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP must have AAM module provisioned and have a policy with ICC enabled attached to a virtual.
bugs.impact: When a user with BOLT client accesses the website AAM may use feature not supported by that client. It might cause an incorrect rendering of the webpage.
bugs.workaround: Disable ICC

bugs.title: Traffic not sent to default pool after pool selection from rule
bugs.symptoms: If you have an iRule configured to match a pattern in the HTTP::uri and send it to a non-default pool, subsequent requests in the HTTP keep-alive session will also be sent to the non-default pool even though they do not match the iRule.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after upgrading from 11.5.3 HF1 to 11.5.3 HF2.
bugs.impact: If the pool members are not configured to accept traffic that doesn't match the uri criterial, the server will not respond properly.
bugs.fix: Reverted a change that caused subsequent HTTP requests to go to the non-default pool after it was selected in an iRule.

bugs.title: iRule "nexthop IP_ADDR" rejected by validator
bugs.symptoms: The nexthop command allows an administrator the ability to specify a forwarding address in an iRule. The form which takes an IP address may be rejected by the validator with an error message of the form: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/irule_example] error: Unable to find vlan, vlangroup or tunnel (10.0.0.1) referenced at line 2: [nexthop 10.0.0.1]
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the nexthop command contains only the IP address, for example: when HTTP_REQUEST { nexthop 10.0.0.1 }
bugs.impact: The iRule containing the 'nexthop IP_ADDR' command cannot be associated with a virtual server.
bugs.workaround: The 'nexthop VLAN IP_ADDR' form of the command does pass the validator. Choose the named vlan on which IP_ADDR can be reached. For example: when HTTP_REQUEST { nexthop internal 10.0.0.1 }
bugs.fix: Validator now allows 'nexthop IP_ADDR' in iRules.

bugs.title: Password policy enforcement for root user when mcpd is not available
bugs.symptoms: When the mcpd configuration database is not available password policy is not enforced when changing passwords for the user 'root' using the command-line utility 'passwd' utility.
bugs.conditions: -- Advanced shell access -- mcpd is not available. -- Change root password with the 'passwd' utility.
bugs.impact: Root password may be set to a string that does not comply with the current password policy.
bugs.fix: The system now enforces the password policy for root user, even when mcpd is not available.

bugs.title: Upgrade for application security anomalies
bugs.symptoms: If upgrading to newer version, old statistics for application security anomalies are not shown.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from BIG-IP version older than 12.1.0 to newer version
bugs.impact: Losing old statistics for application security anomalies
bugs.fix: Upgrade to newer version and verify that old statistics are shown.

bugs.title: snmpd core during startup
bugs.symptoms: sod reanimates (with core dump) snmpd due to heartbeat timeout during BIG-IP system startup and configuration load.
bugs.conditions: During startup and configuration load, snmpd sometimes blocks while waiting for certain system resources to become available. If snmpd blocks longer than its configured heartbeat timeout, sod reanimates it (with a core dump).
bugs.impact: Only impact is the generation of a core file.
bugs.workaround: Increase the snmpd heartbeat timeout to 300 seconds or more. The 11.5.1 default timeout of 60 seconds might be too short for certain platforms and configurations. The default timeout for later releases is 300 seconds.

bugs.title: Unable to create gtm topology records using iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: The user is unable to create gtm topology records using iControl REST.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a user issues an iControl REST POST command for a gtm topology record.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST POST command fails with the following error: 'Topologies must specify both regions: ldns: server:'.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH, iControl SOAP, or the GUI to create gtm topology records.
bugs.fix: You can now create gtm topology records using iControl REST. Please be sure to format the gtm topology oid string using the following rules: 1) Use only a single space between each item in the topology string. 2) Use a fully-pathed name for datacenter, isp, region, and pool objects. For example: "ldns: subnet 11.11.11.0/24 server: datacenter /Common/DC".

bugs.title: TCP Analytics Profile section in virtual server UI has erroneous caption
bugs.symptoms: In TMUI: Local Traffic: Virtual Server:: Create: advanced, TCP Analytics profile section has a erroneous caption for HTTP Analytics profile.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when creating a TCP Analytics profile in the GUI when AVR is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: The screen posts a warning similar to the following: Warning: The Application Visibility and Reporting (AVR) module is not provisioned. Assigning an HTTP Analytics profile is not recommended. However, it should be TCP Analytics profile.
bugs.workaround: None. The message is correct the AVR is not provisioned. However, the warning should reference the TCP Analytics profile instead of the HTTP Analytics profile.

bugs.title: HA peer's certkeychain of clientssl profile is unexpectedly either removed or re-named after config sync.
bugs.symptoms: HA peer's certkeychain of clientssl profile is unexpectedly either removed or re-named after config sync.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen when all the below conditions are met. 1. When more than one certkeychains are configured in the clientSSL profile. 2. When the content of a certkeychain of the clientSSL profile is modified. For example, "modify ltm profile client-ssl a4 cert-key-chain modify { default { cert rsa.crt key rsa.key } }". 3. Performs config sync in HA setup.
bugs.impact: Missing certkeychain of a clientSSL profile can result in its inability to handle some kind of SSL traffic. For example, if the clientSSL originally has EC key/cert but loses it, then it is no longer able to handle SSL connection using EC cipher suites.
bugs.workaround: Basically reconfigure certkeychain but avoid modifying the content. 1. On any BIG-IP system, leave only the RSA certkeychain in the clientSSL profile, just like the default configuration. 2. Config sync, so that both systems have only the RSA certkeychain. 3. In any BIG-IP system, add certkeychains for other types (EC or DSA) you need. You can "add" or "delete" but do not "modify" any existing certkeychain. 4. Do config sync, so that both systems have the same certkeychains in the clientSSL profile.

bugs.title: Can't install more than 16 SafeNet HSMs in its HA group
bugs.symptoms: With installation script on the BIG-IP, you can't install more than 16 SafeNet HSMs in its high availability group with versions 5.2 and 5.4.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to install more than 16 SafeNet HSMs.
bugs.impact: Installer script failure.
bugs.workaround: The limit is set by SafeNet. Currently, with F5-supported 5.2 and 5.4 client software, SafeNet doesn't allow more than 16 HSMs in one high availability configuration.
bugs.fix: Updated SafeNet installation scripts by replacing "vtl" to "lunacm" for high availability group creation and member adding operations for version 6.2.

bugs.title: IE gives a security warning asking: "Do you want to run ... InstallerControll.cab"
bugs.symptoms: When logging into a VPN connection using Internet Explorer, Internet Explorer may prompt "Do you want to run ... InstallerControll.cab"
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM configured and is accessed by Internet Explorer. This can happen after an upgrade of BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: The prompt should not occur.
bugs.fix: Internet Explorer will no longer prompt to run InstallerControll.cab

bugs.title: Removed unused session ID from URL
bugs.symptoms: /vdesk/webtop/index.html URL includes the full session ID.
bugs.conditions: Use APM version older than v7.1.4.0 or older to establish VPN.
bugs.impact: Potential exposure of session ID via URL.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to newer version of APM client.
bugs.fix: Removed unused session ID from URL

bugs.title: BIG-IP APM now uses Airwatch v2 API to retreive device posture information
bugs.symptoms: Airwatch version 8.3 and above no longer use the v1 REST API. APM is not be able to retrieve device information from Airwatch MDM version 8.3 and higher and device posture checking in APM policies fails.
bugs.conditions: - Airwatch configured on APM - Airwatch is upgraded to version 8.3 or higher
bugs.impact: BIG-IP APM is unable to retrieve device information and device posture check will fail.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP APM now utilizes the Airwatch v2 API to access device posture information. Important: you must be using Airwatch release 8.3 and up because older releases do not support the v2 REST API end points.

bugs.title: SafeNet client not able to establish session to all HSMs on all blades.
bugs.symptoms: SafeNet client not able to establish session to all HSMs on all blades.
bugs.conditions: When the BIG-IP chassis is used with SafeNet HSM high availability (HA), and when BIG-IP tmm interface is used.
bugs.impact: SafeNet HSM HA is not being used at its maximal capacity.
bugs.workaround: Restart pkcs11d to mitigate this issue.
bugs.fix: We have adjusted the startup timing of pkcs11d to wait until tmm initialization finishes. Also we added retry for pkcs11d threads when connecting to HSM.

bugs.title: Cannot modify 'ip-address' attribute of static ARP / NDP entries
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to modify the 'ip-address' attribute of a static ARP / NDP entry results in the following error: Syntax Error: 'ip-address' may not be specified in the context of the 'modify' command. 'ip-address' may be specified using the following commands: create, list, show
bugs.conditions: Attempting to modify the 'ip-address' attribute of a static ARP / NDP entry.
bugs.impact: Note: Starting in 11.6.0, the 'ip-address' attribute of an ARP/NDP record can no longer be modified. This is as-designed functionality. However, the BIG-IQ SCVMM plugin fails to work properly as a result, which might impact some configurations. For example, when the LTM gateway device is running versions later than 11.5.3, it could fail because the syntax that worked in 11.5.3 no longer works in 11.6.0 and later.

bugs.title: Potential segfault when MRF messages cross from one TMM to another.
bugs.symptoms: Potential segfault when Message Routing Framework (MRF) messages cross from one TMM to another.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when MRF messages travel from one TMM to another, and an asynchronous operation also occurs (like persistence).
bugs.impact: It is possible for the message object to be removed before the asynchronous operation completes. If this occurs, a segfault may occur and the system might restart.
bugs.fix: This release corrects the issue of potential segfault occurring when MRF messages cross from one TMM to another.

bugs.title: Use of session DB on multi-process appliances and blades may core.
bugs.symptoms: On selected devices and blades, tmm runs multiple processes. When running multiple processes, the session DB may occasionally attempt an operation that will cause a tmm segfault.
bugs.conditions: In order to experience this failure, tmm must be running in multiple processes on the appliance or on the blade, and session DB usage is required with mirroring.
bugs.impact: Outage and restart of tmm. This applies when bringing up blades as well as bringing peers online.
bugs.fix: Use of session DB on multi-process appliances and blades no longer cores when bringing up blades as well as bringing peers online.

bugs.title: CRL is not being imported/exported properly
bugs.symptoms: CRL assigned as part of Machine Cert Auth is not being imported/exported properly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when importing SSL Certificates and Keys using the CRL type. Or when adding the Machine Cert Check agent to import an Access Profile in when creating a New Certificate Authority Profile.
bugs.impact: Prevents CRL from being exported. Might also impact the import/export of Certificate Authority Profiles.
bugs.workaround: 1. Copy and install the CRL to the other BIG-IP system separately. 2. Modify the exported configuration to use CRL from step 1
bugs.fix: Import and export of CRL is fully supported.

bugs.title: Default crypto failure action is now "go-offline-downlinks".
bugs.symptoms: Previously, if a crypto accelerator encountered a failure, the default action was "failover". Now, the default behavior is "go-offline-downlinks".
bugs.conditions: Failed crypto accelerator.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP with failing crypto accelerator on a chassis blade may remain in standby as primary blade.
bugs.workaround: Set the db variable crypto.ha.action to your desired value.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP will now default to "go-offline-downlinks".
bugs.behavior: The default value of the db variable crypto.ha.action has changed to 'go-offline-downlinks'. The only time this has an effect on the system is when a crypto accelerator fails. For a chassis, this value will cause the blade that had the failed crypto device to go offline, leaving the other blades to handle the load, while an appliance will failover to its standby peer.
