See https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K16951 for more details.

bugs.title: RESOLV::lookup against a TCP virtual will cause tmm core
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores when RESOLV::lookup hitting a TCP dns listener.
bugs.conditions: RESOLV::lookup points to a TCP virtual.
bugs.impact: tmm might crash with assert: 'Must be syncookie'. Traffic is interrupted.
bugs.fix: RESOLVE::lookup verifies that the listener is a UDP dns listener.

bugs.title: HTTP parses fragmented response versions incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: When a fragmented response is parsed by HTTP, the version field may be incorrectly bounded. HTTP correctly determines the version of the response. However, other filters that re-scan the version field might see a truncated value. The filters then miss-parse the HTTP version.
bugs.conditions: A fragmented response where the HTTP version field appears in multiple packets. Another filter, for example VDI, re-scans the HTTP version field.
bugs.impact: The detected version of HTTP may be incorrect. Typically, the response is detected as a HTTP/0.9 response rather than the 1.0 or 1.1 response it actually uses.
bugs.fix: HTTP correctly bounds the response version for other filters to parse.

bugs.title: APM Cannot create symbolic link to sandbox. Error: No such file or directory
bugs.symptoms: The user may encounter the following configuration error when adding a new APM sandbox-contained object in a non-default partition (other than /Common) if the user has ever attempted (but failed) to delete this partition (for example, couldn't delete it because it was not empty). 01070734:3: Configuration error: Cannot create symbolic link to sandbox. Error: No such file or directory. If you have access to bash shell, try to run command: ln -s /config/filestore/files_d/p1_d/sandbox_file_d /var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/p1_d/sandbox_file_d. Then try to upload file again. Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: The user has ever attempted (but failed) to delete the partition.
bugs.impact: No more APM sandbox object such as Hosted-Content can be added to the partition. Upgrade may fail to install configuration with the impacted sandbox object.
bugs.workaround: Manually use the shell command 'mkdir -p' to re-create the missing folder where the symbolic link is suppsed to be created as shown in the error message. Directories are: {to do mkdir -p) /config/filestore/files_d/OUTSIDE_PROD_d/sandbox_file_d /var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/OUTSIDE_PROD_d/sandbox_file_d After creating the directors sync to active unit.

bugs.title: Using iControl get_certificate_bundle_v2 causes a memory leak
bugs.symptoms: Using iControl call get_certificate_bundle_v2() causes a memory leak. iControlPortal memory use grows unbounded every time the method is called.
bugs.conditions: This occurs anytime the method is invoked; BIG-IP devices managed by Enterprise Manager can be especially impacted.
bugs.impact: Eventually iControlPortal will run out of memory and crash.
bugs.fix: The memory leak issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Default net ipsec ike-peer anonymous state disable
bugs.symptoms: The default of 'net ipsec ike-peer anonymous state' has been changed from enabled to disabled.
bugs.conditions: This applies to the 'net ipsec ike-peer anonymous state' setting.
bugs.impact: In order to use ike-peer anonymous, it must be explicitly enabled.
bugs.workaround: Set 'net ipsec ike-peer anonymous state' to enable if that is what is desired.
bugs.fix: The default 'net ipsec ike-peer anonymous state' is disable.
bugs.behavior: The default of 'net ipsec ike-peer anonymous state' has been changed from enabled to disabled.

bugs.title: Improved debug log for IKEv2 proposal transforms and payloads.
bugs.symptoms: IKEv2 logs insufficiently for debugging, for proposal transforms, especially when compared to IKEv1 logging of transforms during negotiation. Insufficient info is shown to explain why an IKEv2 negotiation fails.
bugs.conditions: If an IKEv2 negotiation fails due to proposal transform disagreement, examining /var/log/ipsec.log shows too few clues about what was wrong. When log-level is at least DEBUG, the log should give more debug info: tmsh modify net ipsec ike-daemon ikedaemon log-level debug. tmsh modify net ipsec ike-daemon ikedaemon log-level debug2.
bugs.impact: Diagnosing IKEv2 disagreement in transforms is hard without the new debug log info.
bugs.fix: Now /var/log/ipsec.log reveals clear detail about proposal transforms and payloads in /var/log/ipsec.log (and in tmm logs) when log level is at least DEBUG. Changing log level to debug works like this: tmsh modify net ipsec ike-daemon ikedaemon log-level debug. or tmsh modify net ipsec ike-daemon ikedaemon log-level debug2.

bugs.title: Address lease-pool in IKEv2 might interfere with IKEv2 negotiations.
bugs.symptoms: LTM IPsec IKEv2 does not support dynamic remote-address CONFIG option, but still might potentially process that information sent by third-party devices. The configuration changes from this option might affect traffic-selector selection in IKEv2 negotiations, leading to wrong matching results and failure in establishing IPsec SA.
bugs.conditions: Certain third-party vendor devices are the remote IKEv2 peer, for example, a CISCO APIC device.
bugs.impact: Failure in establishing IPsec SA.
bugs.fix: Address lease-pool in IKEv2 no longer interferes with IKEv2 negotiations.

bugs.title: IPsec IKE-v2 Peer UI does not prevent configuration of 'NONE' option using Microsoft Internet Explorer.
bugs.symptoms: The IPsec configuration utility (web UI) allows configuration of an invalid option "NONE" for Perfect Forward Secrecy when Internet Explorer browser is in use.
bugs.impact: The racoon daemon will fail to start and all tunnels may fail to work. The racoon.log file may contain messages like: 2016-09-14 16:32:16: INFO: Reading configuration from "/etc/racoon/racoon.conf" 2016-09-14 16:32:16: ERROR: /etc/racoon/racoon.conf.bigip:59: "}" DH group required. 2016-09-14 16:32:16: ERROR: fatal parse failure (1 errors) 2016-09-14 16:32:16: ERROR: failed to parse configuration file.
bugs.conditions: IPsec IKE-v2 Peer created with 'None' option for Perfect Forward Secrecy from GUI.
bugs.workaround: 'None' option for Perfect Forward Secrecy in IPsec IKE Peer creation page is an invalid option and should not be selected.
bugs.fix: Configuration utility (web UI): Removed 'None' option for Perfect Forward Secrecy in IPsec IKE Peer creation page.

bugs.title: Cannot create or edit a new document from SharePoint 2013 ribbon buttons via Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Cannot create or modify a new document from SharePoint 2013 ribbon buttons via Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: -- Attempting to create or edit a new document. -- Using SharePoint 2013 ribbon buttons via Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Cannot create or modify SharePoint 2013 documents via Portal Access. Document cannot be opened, edited, or saved to the server.
bugs.fix: Can now create and modify a new document from SharePoint 2013 ribbon buttons via Portal Access from Mac.

bugs.title: Configuration infrastructure should reject invalid 'None' option for IKE Peer Phase 1 Perfect Forward Secrecy
bugs.symptoms: The configuration infrastructure currently allows the invalid 'None' option to be configured on an IPsec IKE peer for phase 1 Perfect Forward Secrecy. Although the ability to configure the 'None' option is incorrect functionality which happens on specific browsers, the configuration infrastructure should have stronger checking and prevent the acceptance of an invalid 'None' option for configured IKE peers.
bugs.conditions: The ability to configure an IKE peer with an invalid 'None' option for Perfect Forward Secrecy occurs on Internet Explorer and Safari browsers, and the configuration infrastructure does not reject this invalid configuration for these cases.
bugs.impact: The racoon daemon will fail to start and all IPsec tunnels may fail to work. The racoon.log file may contain messages like: INFO: Reading configuration from "/etc/racoon/racoon.conf" ERROR: /etc/racoon/racoon.conf.bigip:59: "}" DH group required. ERROR: fatal parse failure (1 errors) ERROR: failed to parse configuration file.
bugs.workaround: Don't configure the 'None' option for Perfect Forward Secrecy in the IKE peer configuration section.
bugs.fix: Check for Perfect Forward Secrecy 'None' option in the configuration infrastructure and reject if this option is configured.

bugs.title: DB variable log.csyncd.level cannot be set to certain values
bugs.symptoms: The DB variable log.csyncd.level lists some values for tab completion, but validation prevents you from setting them. The error message looks like this: 01070911:3: The requested enumerated (alert) is invalid (critical, error, warning, notice, informational, debug) for loglevel in daemon_csyncd (/Common/daemon_csyncd)
bugs.conditions: You are trying to use the DB variable log.csyncd.level to increase the amount of information logged by csyncd. csyncd is a system service that on chassis mirrors certain portions of the filesystem between blades, and on all BIG-IP devices runs certain commands after detecting filesystem changes.
bugs.impact: You cannot set the log level to certain values.
bugs.workaround: If you want more debugging information, set the log level to 'debug', which is still accepted.
bugs.fix: The DB variable log.csyncd.level lists some values for tab completion, but validation formerly prevented you from setting them. This has now been resolved; all advertised values will now be accepted.

bugs.title: IPsec configuration mismatch in IKEv2 causes TMM crash in isakmp_parse_proposal ()
bugs.symptoms: crash (NULL pointer access)
bugs.conditions: IPsec configuration mismatch in IKEv2 (for initiator and responder)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: use correct configuration
bugs.fix: Proper reaction (connection reject) was added for improper configuration.

bugs.title: Provide a way to configure where in payload the CSPM JS is injected.
bugs.symptoms: This is an enhancement that allows you to choose where in the document the CSPM script will be injected.
bugs.conditions: You are using some application that can't read the document if something appears after closing the html tag.
bugs.impact: Today we append the CSPM payload (for client latency measurements) at the end of the HTML document (after the html tag). This works in browsers but it's not compliant to the HTML standard and may break some applications that rely on this standard (not browsers).
bugs.workaround: Un-checking "Page Load Time" in analytics profile.
bugs.fix: Verify that script was injected to the chosen location in the returned document.

bugs.title: L7 hardware syn cookie feature is broken in BIG-IP v12.0.0 hf1 and hf2
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP v12.0.0 hf1 and hf2 hardware syn cookie feature for L7 (e.g. Standard Virtual Server type or FastL4 with http profile) virtual server is broken due to HSB bitstream update with a new hardware syn cookie algorithm. It does not impact 12.0.0 base release.
bugs.conditions: Hardware syn cookie is enabled (which is the default setting) on L7 virtual server.
bugs.impact: When syncookie protection is triggered, ingress legitimate traffic may be dropped by BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware syn cookie on L7 virtual servers. Note: After this workaround you may encounter Bug ID 555020 SW syncookies and windowscaling will cause 3WHS to fail on L7 VIP in which case you would need to apply the workaround from that as well.
bugs.fix: This bug is fixed in 12.0.0-hf3 and 12.1.0.

bugs.title: TMM Restarts After Failover
bugs.symptoms: TMM generates core file and restarts.
bugs.conditions: 1. In a HA pair running pre 11.5.3-HF2 or 11.6.0-HF6, the standby is upgraded to 11.6.0-HF6 EHF 186, 241, 243, or 247. 2. Force failover. 3. A new session is established or an existing session terminated.
bugs.impact: Serivce is disrupted. All existing sessions are terminated.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer generates core file and restarts upon upgrade.

bugs.title: Extra log messages seen on optics removal.
bugs.symptoms: Following message may appear in /var/log/ltm when optics are removed: soc_phy_i2c_read_devtype - eeprom soc_phy_i2c_read_bytes failed port(28)
bugs.conditions: Optics removal.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic message and does not indicate a problem with the system.
bugs.workaround: None needed.
bugs.fix: This release eliminates the benign log messages that occurred when optics were removed.

bugs.title: Topology records can be ordered incorrectly.
bugs.symptoms: Topology records can contain missing order numbers, duplicate order numbers, and differences in the ordering of topology records on BIG-IP's in a sync group.
bugs.conditions: When adding or deleting topology records or modifying the order of existing topology records, the resulting ordering of the topology records can be inconsistent. This can lead to ordering issues including differences in the ordering of topology records on BIG-IP's in a sync group.
bugs.impact: It is difficult to manage the order of topology records. Topology records are evaluated in different orders on different BIG-IP's in a sync group.
bugs.fix: Topology records are now ordered consistently.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is used as SAML IdP, tmm may restart under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what the conditions are, but this occurs when BIG-IP is configured as SAML IdP.
bugs.impact: Tmm may restart.

bugs.title: Monitor probing to pool member stops after FQDN pool member with same IP address is deleted
bugs.symptoms: If an FQDN pool member resolves to the same IP address (node) as a non-FQDN (static) pool member, and the FQDN pool/member is deleted, no further monitor probes are sent to the remaining non-FQDN (static) pool member.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if an FQDN pool member resolves to the same IP address (node) as an existing non-FQDN (static) pool member.
bugs.impact: Loss of health monitoring to remaining non-FQDN (static) pool member.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than avoiding creating a static pool member with the same IP address that could be resolved to an FQDN name.
bugs.fix: An FQDN pool member and static (non-FQDN) pool member can no longer be created with the same IP address, preventing loss of monitoring of the static member of the conflicting FQDN pool member is deleted. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: Bundle-certificates Not Accessible via iControl REST.
bugs.symptoms: Bundle-certificates Not Accessible via iControl REST.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using iControl REST to look at bundle certificates via /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert/~Common~ca-bundle.crt/bundle-certificates
bugs.impact: Unable to get data from the command.
bugs.workaround: If you do not need to do it via iControl REST, you can view bundle certificates using the tmsh command tmsh list sys file ssl-cert ca-bundle.crt bundle-certificates
bugs.fix: The iControl rest command for viewing bundle-certificates now displays all of the certificates.

bugs.title: Upgrade, load config, or sync might fail on large configs with large objects.
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to load a large config with large objects may result in the following error message: err mcpd[7366]: 01070710:3: Database error (52), Can't write blob data, attribute:implementation status:52 - EdbBlobData.cpp, line 57 Attempting to synchronize a large change may result in the following error messages and a crash of the MCPD process: err mcpd[8210]: 01071693:3: Incremental sync: Caught an exception while adding a transaction to the incremental config sync cache: unexpected exception. err mcpd[8210]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: MCPProcessor::processRequestNow: Can't write blob data, attribute:msgs status:52 err mcpd[8210]: 01070596:3: An unexpected failure has occurred, request_group destroyed while processing, exiting...
bugs.conditions: The config must be approximately 19.75 MB (slightly less) prior to processing a large object in the config that exceeds 256 KB. Or, once config exceeds 19.75 MB and 2 MB of additional memory has been allocated, processing config objects that exceed 256 KB (the larger, the more likely to occur) lead to the error.
bugs.impact: Upgrade, load config, or sync might fail, and a system crash and restart might occur.
bugs.workaround: Stagger the load, or reduce the size of particularly large objects within a config.
bugs.fix: Memory handling is improved so that large configs with large objects now successfully complete upon upgrade, load config, or sync.

bugs.title: FastL4 TCP handshake timeout not honored for offloaded flows
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server is configured with a FastL4 profile that enables full acceleration and offload state set to 'embryonic', and if a flow is offloaded to be hardware accelerated, the connection idle timeout during the TCP handshake is set to the 'idle timeout' value of the FastL4 profile, but it should be set to the 'tcp handshake timeout' instead.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server is configured with a FastL4 profile that enables full acceleration and offload state of 'embryonic'. -- A flow is offloaded for hardware acceleration.
bugs.impact: The connection may remain in the half-open state longer than what is set in the TCP handshake timeout value.
bugs.workaround: Set the acceleration-offload state to establish. For example: tmsh modify ltm profile fastl4 fastl4_xyzzy pva-offload-state establish

bugs.title: SSL Certificate with special characters might cause exception when GUI retrieves items list page.
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading, unable to view certain certs from gui. Catalina.out file could contain the signature MalformedByteSequenceException: Invalid byte 2 of 3-byte UTF-8 sequence. iControl SOAP methods ==================== Management::KeyCertificate::get_certificate_list and get_certificate_list_v2 will return an exception if returning a certificate with special characters.
bugs.conditions: SSL Certificate with special characters might cause exception when GUI retrieves items list page. This has been observed on upgrades to BIG-IP version 11.5.4 through 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: The GUI does not display the page containing certificate information. iControl SOAP cannot return a list of certificates if they contain information with special characters.
bugs.fix: The GUI now correctly displays certificates with special characters, and iControl SOAP methods Management::KeyCertificate::get_certificate_list and get_certificate_list_v2 no longer return exceptions.

bugs.title: Step-Up Auth cannot validate SSL certificate revocations
bugs.symptoms: CRLDP Auth and OCSP Auth are not available in the subroutine policies.
bugs.conditions: The subroutines have On Demand Cert Auth, but do not have CRLDP Auth or OCSP Auth available.
bugs.impact: On Demand Cert Auth will validate that the certificate was validly signed by the certificate authority. But for full feature support, we should also be able to check if the certificate authority has revoked the certificate. That is the role of CRLDP Auth and OCSP Auth, but the agents are not currently available.
bugs.fix: The CRLDP Auth and OCSP Auth agents have been added to the subroutines.

bugs.title: Step-up auth with APM native Email OTP and SMS OTP
bugs.symptoms: APM now has support for step-up auth with APM native Email OTP and SMS OTP. The HTTP Auth agent can now be attached to a step-up policy.
bugs.conditions: N/A - this describes an improvement.
bugs.impact: N/A - this describes an improvement.

bugs.title: LocalDB Auth in subroutines
bugs.symptoms: LocalDB Auth is available in the session-based policy, but is not available in the subroutines.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered in APM when performing re-authentication at the virtual server level, e.g., to perform step-up auth on specific resources.
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure LocalDB Auth in subroutines.
bugs.fix: LocalDB Auth is now available in subroutines. Password reset is supported.

bugs.title: Topology Records: Longest Match Sorting in Unexpected Order
bugs.symptoms: The UI or TMSH only includes a create in a transaction. However, validation modifies an attribute (the order in this case) of another record, so both a create and a modify command is included in the transaction sent to TMM and other devices.
bugs.conditions: Create a GTM configuration with 3 topology regions. Create 3 topology records with the 'Request Source' (LDNS) as one of the regions. This results in 3 topology records with orders of 1, 2, and 3. Delete the topology record with the order of 2. Add another topology record with a region as the 'Request Source'. Note that while the UI or TMSH only includes a create in the transaction, a create and a modify is included in the transaction sent to TMM, etc.
bugs.impact: If there is another GTM in the sync group, it receives a transaction with both a create and a modify. This results in additional validation on the 2nd system.

bugs.title: Unbalanced double-quotes may merge lines upon config save-then-load
bugs.symptoms: Unbalanced double-quotes used in the configuration will cause load failure, or will merge subsequent configuration lines until a balancing double-quote character is found. For example, an improper expression may be used to configure a monitor 'recv' value that results in an unbalanced (odd number) of double-quote characters, such as "R\\"eceive" (note three double-quote characters, resulting in an unbalanced string). The string is considered unbalanced with an odd number of double-quote characters, regardless of escaping (such as double- or triple-backslash escaping).
bugs.conditions: An odd count of double-quotes are used for a configuration value, resulting in an unbalanced string. For example, configuring a monitor 'recv' value as "R\\"eceive" results in an unbalanced string (notice three double-quotes, an odd number).
bugs.impact: The configuration will fail to load, as it is improperly formed. In some cases the configuration may successfully load, but the unbalanced string will cause newline(s) to be implicitly escaped until a balancing double-quote is found; this will merge subsequent lines to the unbalanced line, resulting in the consumed lines to not be considered as configuration values, but as the merged continuation of the unbalanced line.
bugs.workaround: Modify configuration values that use double-quotes to be balanced (i.e., configuration items should have an even-number of double-quoted characters, even if they are escaped).

bugs.title: Windows Edge client cannot detect local LAN in some cases
bugs.symptoms: If Edge client is configured in Always Connected mode with option to "Allow Traffic" without VPN, it will continue to establish VPN even when location awareness is configured.
bugs.conditions: 1) Edge client was installed using a package that was created without setting DNS suffix list in connectivity profile 2) DNS suffix list to identify enterprise LAN was set in the connectivity profile after client package was created.
bugs.impact: Edge client will fail to detect Enterprise LAN and continue to establish VPN even when machine is connected to enterprise LAN.

bugs.title: "list sys crypto csr" output is not consistent
bugs.symptoms: "list sys crypto csr" prints the CSR file data along with the object information when there is only one CSR in the system. However, it only prints the object information when there exists multiple CSRs in the system.
bugs.conditions: 1. When there is only one CSR file in the system. 2. The csr name is not specified in the "list sys crypto csr" command.
bugs.impact: "list sys crypto csr" output is not consistent.
bugs.fix: With the fix, when the system contains only one CSR file, "list sys crypto csr" will no longer print the CSR file, and hence the output format is consistent in terms of the CSR count in the system. Note that if the csr name is specified in the comment, for example, "list sys crypto csr aaa.csr", the behavior is not changed, i.e., it will still prints the file content of the CSR.
bugs.behavior: With the fix, when the system contains only one CSR file, "list sys crypto csr" will no longer print the CSR file content (but will still display the CSR object information).

bugs.title: RBA may generate a core file when shutting down
bugs.symptoms: RBA core file is generated.
bugs.conditions: When RBA plugin is shutting down, which may be related to configuration changes, system instability, or Admin actions.
bugs.impact: No service impact except a core file is generated

bugs.title: icrd may crash on shutdown
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, icrd may crash and create a core file while shutting down.
bugs.conditions: icrd exiting, typically due to a system shutdown or reboot
bugs.impact: icrd crashes and generates a log file.
bugs.workaround: The crash of icrd during shutdown/reboot may be ignored; no services were impacted. Related core files can be deleted as desired.

bugs.title: Persistence may override node/pmbr connection limit
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances the BIG-IP system may load balance connections to a node or poolmember over the configured connection limit.
bugs.conditions: - Node or pool member configured with connection limit. - L4 or L7 virtual server. - Persistence configured on the Virtual Server. - Very high load on unit.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system may load balance connections to a node or pool member over the configured connection limit.
bugs.workaround: Remove persistence or use another method of limiting the connections (rate limiting or connection limit on the Virtual Server).
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly enforces the pool member/node connection limit.

bugs.title: A BD core on specific server behavior with a specific configuration
bugs.symptoms: A BD core.
bugs.conditions: -- A response that has many cookies. -- Many cookies are enforced, and are generating big cookies. -- Response logging is enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disturbance.
bugs.workaround: None. Note: In a typical configuration, enforcing that many cookies is not needed. You can reduce the list of enforced cookies only to the relevant ones, which can help reduce the likelihood of this issue occurring.
bugs.fix: BD no longer cores under these conditions.

bugs.title: 'Exceeding pool member limit' error with FQDN pool members and non-LTM license
bugs.symptoms: When configuring FQDN pool members on a BIG-IP system with a license that does not include the LTM module, an error similar to the following may be logged by mcpd: 01071732:3: Exceeding pool member limit (3). Cannot add pool member to pool:(/Common/pool_name).
bugs.conditions: This may occur if: 1. The active BIG-IP license does not include the LTM module. Specifically, the active license defines a pool member limit (ltm_lb_pool_member_limit) other than 'unlimited'. This applies to AFM, APM, and ASM licenses. 2. FQDN pool members are configured with 'autopopulate' set to 'enabled'.
bugs.impact: Under these conditions, the ephemeral FQDN pool members are counted against the pool member limit (ltm_lb_pool_member_limit) defined in the LTM license. Cannot configure FQDN pool members with autopopulate enabled on BIG-IP systems without an LTM license.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds for this issue: Workaround 1 ----------- 1. Configure FQDN pool members with autopopulate disabled. 2. Do not attempt to configure more pool members than are permitted by the active license. Workaround 2 ----------- Add the LTM module to the license configuration.

bugs.title: tmstat CPU values can be incorrect
bugs.symptoms: The CPU values returned by blades in a chassis may not be sorted correctly and so the returned values might appear confusing or invalid.
bugs.conditions: Retrieving values for a chassis using the following command: tmstat cpu.
bugs.impact: Incorrect reporting of TMM CPU utilization using tmstat command.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Values are now properly sorted and maintained.

bugs.title: VIPRION B2100 or B2150 blade Optic OPT-0016-00 is ON during BIG-IP system boot sequence causing errors with connected equipment
bugs.symptoms: When a VIPRION B2100 or B2150 blade boots, there is a brief window during which the transmitter on the optics module is enabled, but the accompanying initialization of the Broadcom switch has not yet occurred. during this window (~20 seconds) random data may be transmitted which may be reported as errors by the link partner.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION B2100 or B2150 blade is powered or rebooted or when the user performs a 'bigstart restart'.
bugs.impact: This has a minor impact. In most cases link is functional after the system fully initializes, although error counts may show up on the link partner.
bugs.workaround: If link fails to come up, attempt "bigstart restart bcm56xxd" to restart the Broadcom daemon. However, this will have no impact on errors seen by peer equipment. You can determine the type of hardware using the command: tmsh show sys hardware. 'Type' is A109 for VIPRION B2100 blades and A113 for VIPRION B2150 blades.

bugs.title: Reset Nitrox3 crypto accelerator queue if it becomes stuck.
bugs.symptoms: Certain configuration parameters used during an SSL handshake can elicit a 'queue stuck' message from the accelerator. When this happens, the /var/log/ltm log file will contain a message similar to the following: 'n3-cryptoX request queue stuck'.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system uses Nitrox 3 encryption hardware to perform SSL encryption. An SSL handshake sent to the BIG-IP system is incorrectly configured or contains bad information.
bugs.impact: In-flight and queued contexts for the specific accelerator are dropped. After device recovery, new requests will be accelerated.
bugs.workaround: Disable crypto acceleration.
bugs.fix: The crypto accelerator is gracefully reset when the accelerator stalls due to a misconfigured request. Note: This issue resolution is limited to SSL handshake issues, and is not a resolution for all possible causes of a 'queue stuck' event.

bugs.title: LocalDB auth logs new password in debug log on password change
bugs.symptoms: When the Local user changes the password, the Localdb component logs the new password in the Debug Level. Also, during the parsing of HTTP header, we log the content of the Parameter "_F5_challenge", which contains the Local user password.
bugs.impact: The password is plainly visible in the log file /var/log/apm
bugs.conditions: This occurs when local users are changing their passwords and Access logging is set to debug.

bugs.title: 'force-full-load-push' is not tab expandable
bugs.symptoms: The 'force-full-load-push' option for 'run cm config-sync' is not tab expandable unless it's the first option given.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when trying to use tab complete in tmsh for the 'run cm config-sync' command.
bugs.impact: The keyword 'force-full-load-push' has to be typed out in full or used as the first option.
bugs.workaround: Use 'force-full-load-push' as the first option, or type it out in full.

bugs.title: cert-key-chain drop-downs are not set to inherited values.
bugs.symptoms: When overriding the cert-key-chain in an SSL profile, the three drop-down menus are not set to the values specified in the parent profile.
bugs.conditions: When overriding the cert-key-chain in an SSL profile.
bugs.impact: The chain file might be inadvertently set to 'None' when creating a child profile just to override a Certificate and Key.
bugs.fix: When overriding the cert-key-chain in an SSL profile, the three drop-down menus are now set to the values specified in the parent profile.

bugs.title: HTTP Class profile is upgraded to a case-insensitive policy
bugs.symptoms: If you upgrade to version 11.4.0 through 12.0.0, and your configuration contains a HTTP Class profile, the generated policy will be case-insensitive.
bugs.conditions: HTTP Class profile
bugs.impact: Generated policy does not match on the same conditions as original HTTP Class profile.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit generated policy
bugs.fix: The case-sensitive attribute is added to generated policies during upgrade.

bugs.title: HTTP Class profile using a path selector upgrade to a policy that does not match the entire path
bugs.symptoms: If you upgrade to version 11.4.0 through 12.0.0, and your configuration contains a HTTP Class profile containing a paths selector, the generated policy does not match.
bugs.conditions: A HTTP Class profile containing a paths selector.
bugs.impact: The generated policy does not match the same paths as original HTTP Class profile.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit resulting policy
bugs.fix: The path selector specifier is no longer added to the generated policy allowing the entire http-uri to matched.

bugs.title: Using ECDSA Keys for User Public Key Auth or the Backend Server is configured to use ECDSA keys
bugs.symptoms: Using ecdsa keys for user public key auth will result in a connection hang. Using ecdsa keys on the backend server will result in the client receiving a TCP Reset.
bugs.conditions: Either of two conditions need to be satisfied: 1) Client has ecdsa keys, e.g ~/.ssh contains id_ecdsa.pub and id_ecdsa keys. 2) Backend server is using ecdsa. e.g. the sshd config contains the following where rsa and dsa are disabled and ecdsa is enabled: # HostKeys for protocol version 2 #HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key #HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key
bugs.impact: No ssh connection can be established through the ssh proxy
bugs.workaround: Please use RSA and DSA keys only for both User Public Key Auth and Server Key Exchange

bugs.title: Command history and audit logs add additional escaping
bugs.symptoms: The same command in TMSH command history contains extra slashes. When cut-n-paste is used, slashes are multiplying.
bugs.conditions: Command entered into tmsh includes escape (backslash) characters.
bugs.impact: Commands repeated from the history may not match what was entered and will be interpreted as displayed. The audit logs may contain additional quoting or escaping when compared to the command that was run.
bugs.workaround: When repeating commands from the history that contain escaping, remove the added escaping before running.
bugs.fix: Command history and audit logs no longer add additional escaping.

bugs.title: Unable to boot v11.6.0 on 7250 or 10250 platforms
bugs.symptoms: Unable to boot or system constantly rebooting.
bugs.conditions: Booting into v11.6.0 on 7250 or 10250 platform with RAID disk layout.
bugs.impact: Unable to boot.
bugs.fix: This version of the software boots boots correctly on 7250 or 10250 platforms with RAID disk layout. In version 11.6.1, the software would boot but would not start RAID.

bugs.title: Rate shaper drop policy sometimes show value is zero which is equivalent of default value
bugs.symptoms: The default values for a drop policy's elements max-threshold and min-threshold may show as '0' under certain circumstances, and their actual values under other circumstances. This can actually lead to the values being displayed differently between configsync devices despite the traffic group showing in-sync (internally, the actual non-zero default value is always used, and so no config mismatch is detected). This leads to confusion.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using rate-shaping drop policies.
bugs.impact: Confusion when you see the change in value from zero to something else when you change one value and see other value automatically changed.
bugs.workaround: No work around is needed.
bugs.fix: Ignore the parameter values when rate shaper drop policy changes automatically to the default value.

bugs.title: tmsh save /sys ucs command sends status messages to stderr
bugs.symptoms: When you run the tmsh save /sys ucs command, some normal status messages are being sent to stderr instead of stdout. This will be seen if a you are watching stderr for error messages.
bugs.conditions: There are no conditions, every time the command is run, it will send some status type messages to stderr.
bugs.impact: If a script runs the command it may report that the save failed because messages were send to stderr.
bugs.workaround: You can ignore the message "Saving active configuration..." being sent to stderr. It is not an error.
bugs.fix: The command will send the status messages to stdout.

bugs.title: Config sync peer may fail to monitor newly added pool member after it is added via sync
bugs.symptoms: If a pool member in a sync group is removed and another member added and then synced to the peer, the monitor state on the peer may be erroneous.
bugs.conditions: 2 or more devices in a device group A pool member is deleted, and another is added, then a full config sync is performed
bugs.impact: Monitoring does not happen. If the pool member should be marked down by the monitor, it may indicate as being up. You may need to do a system restart to get monitoring to resume properly.
bugs.workaround: Suggested workaround: Here’s a way that should avoid any possible downtime: 1. Do the node replacement on box A. Do not sync. 2. Do the node replacement on box B. Do not sync. 3. This will cause a sync conflict, and its resolution will require a full load. This is intentional. Force a sync. The result of that final sync will be that mcpd sends no changes to the relevant nodes on the receiving device.

bugs.title: httpclass containing escaped backslashes are stripped on migration to LTM policy
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading or installing a UCS file with http class profiles values containing escaped backslashes will have the escaped backslashes stripped from the value.
bugs.conditions: A http class profile with values containing escaped backslashes. This occurs on upgrades through 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: The escaped backslashes will be removed and then the policy will not correctly match.
bugs.workaround: Edit the policy and add backslashes back in.

bugs.title: Buffer error due to RADIUS::avp command when vendor IDs do not match
bugs.symptoms: Errors similar to the following in the ltm log: err tmm3[21915]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/RadiusTest CLIENT_DATA - Buffer error (line 1) (line 1) invoked from within 'RADIUS::avp 26 ip4 index 0 vendor-id 12345 vendor-type 6'.
bugs.conditions: The issue happens when there is a RADIUS::avp command for a vendor specific AVP and there's a RADIUS request that contains a different vendor-id than what was specified in the iRule command.
bugs.impact: You are unable to use vendor-specific RADIUS AVP commands
bugs.fix: Vendor-specific RADIUS AVP commands no longer generate errors.

bugs.title: When using a pool route, it is possible for TCP connections to emit packets onto the network that have a source MAC address of 00:98:76:54:32:10.
bugs.symptoms: When using a pool route, it is possible for TCP connections to emit packets onto the network that have a source MAC address of 00:98:76:54:32:10. This is the MAC address of Linux's tmm0 or tmm interface.
bugs.conditions: The traffic destination is the BIG-IP Linux host, e.g. big3d iQuery server. The traffic is proxied via fastL4, e.g. ConfigSync "Local Address" is set to None. The return route is a pool route. The traffic is interrupted, e.g. a router between the iQuery server and the client is switched off for several seconds.
bugs.impact: The traffic is sourced from invalid ethernet MAC 00:98:76:54:32:10. The iQuery connection cannot continue.
bugs.workaround: Increase the lasthop module's TCP idle timeout. echo 121 > /proc/sys/net/lasthop/idle_timeout/tcp
bugs.fix: TCP connections no longer emit packets that have a source MAC address of 00:98:76:54:32:10.

bugs.title: When a rewrite profile using the default settings is attached to a virtual server, all layer 3 connectivity will begin to fail.
bugs.symptoms: By default, the 'rewrite' profile is in APM portal mode. When enabling a 'rewrite' profile on a vCMP guest with ten cores allocated all layer 3 connectivity to the virtual IP will begin to fail. Errors similar to the following are seen in the TMM log (/var/log/tmm): notice share_mem: shmget(0x1304d8, 657664, 0x3b6): Invalid argument The system posts errors similar to the following in Local Traffic logs (/var/log/ltm): crit tmm1[17820]: 01000025:2: Device error: mpi failed to allocate shared memory err tmm1[17820]: 01480043:3: Failed to build plugin profile for /Common/rewriteplugin err tmm1[17820]: 01480002:3: Can't initialize plugin configuration crit tmm1[17820]: 01000203:2: Proxy failed to attach plugin rule err tmm1[17820]: 01000008:3: Proxy initialization failed for /Common/my_virtual
bugs.conditions: A 'rewrite' profile in portal mode (the default) on a vCMP guest with ten cores allocated. A 'rewrite' profile is required for rewriting content; this is required for APM Portal deployments and VDI deployments.
bugs.impact: When a 'rewrite' profile using the default settings is attached to a virtual server all layer 3 connectivity to the virtual IP will fail.
bugs.workaround: Use another core allocation configuration for the guest (such as two, four or eight). If the APM (portal) function is not required, create a custom 'rewrite' profile with the 'rewrite-mode' option of 'uri-translation'.

bugs.title: BIG-IP - Anonymous Certificate ID Enumeration
bugs.symptoms: Invalid requests to the BIG-IP mgmt API verify may reveal the specific cause of the failure to unauthenticated clients.
bugs.impact: Possible disclosure of the em_server_ip field of valid client certificates. This does not reveal the certificate needed for authentication.
bugs.fix: Error responses no longer indicates the specific cause. The cause is still logged in the apache logs for administrator review.
bugs.behavior: When communication first starts between BIG-IQ and BIG-IP, if communication fails the transmitted response no longer indicates the specific cause. Detailed error information is still logged in the apache logs.

bugs.title: Variable value in the nesting script of foreach command get reset when there is parking command in the script
bugs.symptoms: When there is something like the following script: foreach a [list 1 2 3 4] { set a 10 after 100 } There is parking command, after, in the script and it runs after "set a 10", when after command returns, the value of a goes back to the initial value set in the foreach, value of 10 is lost.
bugs.conditions: There is parking command in the nesting script of foreach. For more information on commands that park, see K12962: Some iRule commands temporarily suspend iRule processing at https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K12962
bugs.impact: Variable values get reset.
bugs.workaround: Set(or set again) the variable value after the parking command.
bugs.fix: Will fix in later release.

bugs.title: URL is not enforced correctly in some cases
bugs.symptoms: A URL is not enforced according to its configuration in the policy or the host name in the URL is not recognized when it exists. False positive or false negative happens.
bugs.conditions: A specific issue in the URL string.
bugs.impact: The URL is enforced incorrectly - false negative or false positive violations.
bugs.workaround: N.A
bugs.fix: The URL is now parsed correctly.
bugs.behavior: a slash is added to the beginning of the URL when it arrives without one. The modified URL will be enforced and reported as the URL.

bugs.title: Race condition in the terminate handler of the icrd_child process causes the process to become unresponsive, and generates a core file
bugs.symptoms: * In the /var/log/icrd log file, you may observe an error message similar to the following example: notice icrd: 5823,14414, RestServer, INFO,Connection idle too long fd:11. * The BIG-IP system may generate an icrd_child core file in the /var/core directory.
bugs.conditions: You use the iControl REST application programming interface (API) to obtain data from or modify the configuration of your BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: icrd_child experiences an intermittent segfault error and has to be restarted.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: Session ID is not shown for some messages in System-> Logs-> Access Policy
bugs.symptoms: Session ID is not shown (empty) for some messages in System :: Logs : Access Policy.
bugs.conditions: This is happening for all VDI messages and some APMD messages
bugs.impact: No session ID based report is available for these messages
bugs.workaround: For VDI it is by design not to print session ID, rather using a connection ID to track messages. For APMD it is known issue that some DEBUG messages don't have session IDs.
bugs.fix: This behavior is by design

bugs.title: More than one header name/value pair not accepted by ACCESS::respond
bugs.symptoms: An error is seen when ACCESS::respond command is used, for example, in an iRule with multiple header name/value pairs.
bugs.conditions: When ACCESS::respond command is used with multiple header name/value pairs.
bugs.impact: An error is generated when the command is used.
bugs.workaround: Let the command take only one name/value pair.
bugs.fix: The ACCESS::respond iRule event has been corrected to accept multiple HTTP header name/value pairs in a similar way to HTTP::respond. For example: ACCESS::respond 200 content "http body" header1 value1 header2 value2

bugs.title: User is prompted to install components repeatedly after client components are updated.
bugs.symptoms: After auto-update of client components from internet explorer, user will be prompted to install components again if he goes to VPN site again.
bugs.conditions: Administrator upgrades big-ip to 12.1. User has client components from a release older than 12.1
bugs.impact: User is prompted to install components again and again
bugs.workaround: Restart browser after components are updated the first time.

bugs.title: Assigning address list with 1000+ entries to 1000+ rules policy results in MCP errors
bugs.symptoms: If the size of an address list is too big, and that address list is used in 1000+ rules, it will cause MCP error when saving the config.
bugs.conditions: Assigning address list with 1000+ subnets to 1000+ rules
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to save.

bugs.title: iRule object with '{' ,'#', '}' in the same line not properly handled
bugs.symptoms: EM device discovery/device update fails with: Unexpected end of configuration...
bugs.conditions: iRule object with special characters in an expression may fail validation if they do not evenly match and are not escaped
bugs.impact: EM device discovery/device update fails or work but shows error archive diff feature on EM may fail with error
bugs.workaround: Escape the '#' with '\#'

bugs.title: Internet Explorer: incorrect handling of document.write() to closed document
bugs.symptoms: HTML page with document.write() operations inside event handlers may not be processed correctly. Internet Explorer may show error on this page.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with document.write() calls inside event handlers or another scripts executed after document loading. Strings passed to document.write() function contain HTML tags with URL or another re-writable content in attributes.
bugs.impact: HTML page is not shown at all or works incorrectly in Internet Explorer.
bugs.workaround: No workaround known
bugs.fix: Now HTML pages with document.write() calls for closed document are handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: PWS session does not launch on Internet Explorer
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer (IE) gets stuck entering Protected Work Space (PWS).
bugs.conditions: One of the DLLs provided by APM, vdeskctrl.dll, provides COM services. Internet Explorer (IE), consumes the COM services. The DLL is loaded by IE during upgrade of PWS components. For some reason (especially on slow systems), IE does not unload the the old DLL promptly after upgrading PWS. When COM services are invoked to initialize PWS after upgrade, old DLL provides the service. Due to the recent renewal of our signing certificate, old DLL can't certify the integrity of the new PWS components. We have researched the issue, but we have not found a way to instruct IE to unload the old DLL after upgrade.
bugs.impact: PWS session does not launch.
bugs.workaround: After upgrade, if Internet Explorer(IE) does not enter into PWS within 60 seconds, close IE and start a new session. This is an one time event.
bugs.fix: Internet Explorer can now launch a Protected Workspace session.

bugs.title: Portal Access: JavaScript errors accessing MS SharePoint 2010 / 2013 / 2016 in Internet Explorer 11
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft Internet Explorer version 11 (IE11) shows numerous JavaScript errors in debug console opening SharePoint pages with document lists via Portal Access. As a result, part of SharePoint functionality is unavailable (document submenus, for instance). System posts the following message: Export to database failed. To export a list, you must have a Microsoft SharePoint Foundation-compatible application.
bugs.conditions: - Using Portal Access in IE11. - Accessing SharePoint 2010 / 2013 / 2016. - Opening document library page in SharePoint.
bugs.impact: SharePoint application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: None, although you can successfully access the library directly using IE11.
bugs.fix: Now SharePoint pages with shared document lists can be opened correctly via Portal Access.

bugs.title: Gy CCR-i requests are not being re-sent after initial configured re-transmits
bugs.symptoms: For Gy interface, if OCS doesn't respond to the initial set of CCR-I requests as per the diameter-endpoint profile (1+ msg-max-retransmits <n>), the new set of CCR-I requests are not being generated, even after provisioning pending timeout happens.
bugs.conditions: This issues happens only for Gy interface and when initial set of CCR-I request doesn't get a CCA response.
bugs.impact: The subscriber will be left in Idle state till the default quota is breached and brought down or subscriber can reconnect once OCS CCA response is fixed.
bugs.workaround: Re-connect the subscriber once the CCA response is fixed in OCS
bugs.fix: The solution is to resend CCR-I requests once the provisioning timeout happens

bugs.title: mcpd can run out of file descriptors
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd crashes with the log message err mcpd[8835]: 01071070:3: Failed to open file /config/BigDB.dat.tmp with error 24
bugs.conditions: This can happen in multiple ways, in this case it was detected while running BIG-IQ policy sync.
bugs.impact: Mcpd can crash, rendering the system instable
bugs.fix: A crash related to mcpd running out of file descriptors has been fixed.

bugs.title: Request Logging profile Template textarea wrapping set to soft wrap
bugs.symptoms: The Template field in the Request Logging profile adds line break characters to long values.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a long string of text in the Template field for the Request Logging profile, for example, $DATE_NCSA [REQUEST] - [$HOST:$VIRTUAL_PORT] - $VIRTUAL_POOL_NAME - [SRC_PORT:$CLIENT_PORT] - $NCSA_COMBINED.
bugs.impact: The data stored has line break characters in it at every location where the text wraps inside the Template text box.
bugs.workaround: There is a partial workaround, depending on the length of the string and the width of your screen. Adjust the width of the Template field by clicking and dragging the lower-right corner of the field. The line breaks the system adds occur only when the text wraps inside the box when you save the profile (by pressing Finished on a new profile or Update on an existing one).

bugs.title: Standby TMM might overflow send buffer if out of sync with Active TMM
bugs.symptoms: Send buffer size is unlimited on a standby TMM. If sync is lost with the active TMM while a TCP client is advertising a zero receive buffer, the standby TMM might continue to use a zero send buffer indefinitely. This eventually leads to the send buffer overflowing on the standby TMM.
bugs.conditions: Standby TMM loses sync with active TMM while a TCP client's advertised receive window is zero.
bugs.impact: Standby TMM can accumulate too much data in the send buffer and overflow.
bugs.workaround: This issue is less likely with a low zero-window-timeout value in the TCP profile.

bugs.title: write to sessiondb fails for localdb password reset
bugs.symptoms: When the localdb instance name contains "." character, Apmd wont be able to store the memcache entry. The store operation will fail. You will see a log "notice apmd[15593]: 01490000:5: mc_set_mkey() failed with error [11]."
bugs.conditions: This can occur when doing a localdb password change and the localdb instance name has a period in it.
bugs.impact: The run time user information ( like login failure count ) is stored in memcache, if we are not able to store the entry in memcache, we will fail to authenticate the user.
bugs.workaround: Ensure your Localdb instance names do not contain a "." character.

bugs.title: TMM logs an incorrect error message when invalid regex pattern is used for LTM profiles
bugs.symptoms: When creating or editing LTM profiles with regex or GLOB-expression attributes using tmsh, if the regex or GLOB expression is invalid, the TMM logs an incorrect error message, similar to the following: Invalid command name.... The TMSH command line interface logs the correct message, similar to the following: Profile XYZ error - couldn't compile regular expression....
bugs.conditions: Specifying invalid regex or GLOB expressions in LTM profiles, using TMSH.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. This problem only affects the quality of diagnostics due to inaccurate TMM error logs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Policy automatic learning mode changes to manual after failover
bugs.symptoms: Policy automatic learning mode changes to manual when a failover occurs.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. Device group w/ ASM policy sync configured. ASM Policy is in automatic learning mode. A failover occurs.
bugs.impact: The policy changes from automatic learning mode to manual.
bugs.fix: Policy automatic learning mode no longer changes to manual when a failover occurs. Automatic learning mode will now be disabled only in active/active configurations.

bugs.title: DNS doesn't work properly on Ubuntu 15.10 when using f5fpc CLI client
bugs.symptoms: DNS doesn't work properly on Ubuntu 15.10 when using f5fpc CLI client. This happens because f5fpc fails to patch /etc/resolv.conf on Ubuntu 15.10 release.
bugs.conditions: /etc/resolv.conf, Ubuntu 15.10, f5fpc CLI client and network access establishment.
bugs.impact: DNS doesn't work properly on Ubuntu 15.10
bugs.fix: Now DNS works fine on Ubuntu 15.10 because /etc/resolv.conf can be patched correctly now by f5fpc command line client.

bugs.title: error "The modem (or other connecting device) is already in use or is not configured properly"
bugs.symptoms: Clients get an error: error "The modem (or other connecting device) is already in use or is not configured properly"
bugs.conditions: The exact reproduction steps are not known, but it was seen to occur on certain Windows 10 clients where the access components were removed and login was attempted afterward.
bugs.impact: Clients will be unable to connect to the VPN
bugs.workaround: Rebooting might correct the issue on the client machine.
bugs.fix: Network Access will no longer fail on client machines that first uninstall the components and then attempt to reconnect.

bugs.title: TCP forwarded flows are reset when time wait recycle of port happens
bugs.symptoms: You notice that port-reused connections are getting reset. When a flow is forwarded from one tmm to another, and the destination tmm finds that the client is reusing a port that is in time_wait, and time wait recycle is enabled, the source tmm terminates the connection with a RST sent to the SYN-ACK from the client.
bugs.conditions: Using time-wait recycle and a client reuses the port that is currently in time-wait, and the flow is forwarded to another tmm.
bugs.impact: Client flows are reset rather than accepted.

bugs.title: Two-factor auth not supported in step-up auth
bugs.symptoms: Two factor auth solutions like DuoProxy are not supported for step-up auth. The first logon page will render and accept credentials. In the observed setups, the second logon page will fail to render. It will result in a deny page or a reset.
bugs.conditions: In a subroutine (per-request policy), configure an authentication agent like AD Auth or RADIUS Auth that uses a two-factor authentication solution. An example is the DuoProxy.
bugs.impact: Two factor auth solutions are not supported in step-up auth
bugs.fix: Two factor auth solutions are supported now.

bugs.title: Upgrade causes an ASM subsystem error of PL_PARAM_ATTRIBUTES.
bugs.symptoms: The following error is produced in ASM log during upgrade: ----------- ASM subsystem error (ts_configsync.pl,F5::DbUtils::insert_data_to_table): Row <some_row_id> of table <some_db_table_name> is missing <some_field_name> (DDD) -- skipping F5::<some_package_name> -----------
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Upgrade performed.
bugs.impact: Different portions of the security policy may be incorrectly upgraded.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the root cause so that the security policy upgrades correctly, and the following error does not reproduce upon upgrading: ASM subsystem error (ts_configsync.pl,F5::DbUtils::insert_data_to_table): Row <some_row_id> of table <some_db_table_name> is missing <some_field_name> (DDD) -- skipping F5::<some_package_name>

bugs.title: qkview may not collect certain configuration files in their entirety
bugs.symptoms: If the following files exceed 5M in size, they will be truncated when collected by qkview: /config/partitions/*/bigip.conf /config/partitions/*/BIG-IP_base.conf /config/BIG-IP_gtm.conf
bugs.conditions: Any of the listed files exceeds 5 Mbytes.
bugs.impact: Fault diagnosis may be affected.
bugs.workaround: Create a qkview, and examine the qkview_run.data file. If this file indicates that any of the listed files has been truncated, manually copy that file from the BIG-IP device.

bugs.title: ADAPT recursive loop when handling successive iRule events
bugs.symptoms: After the first iRule resumes from being parked, ADAPT attempts to process the second iRule event repeatedly. The connection is aborted with RST cause "ADAPT unexpected state transition". The adapt profile statistic "records adapted" reaches a very high number as it counts every attempt.
bugs.conditions: A requestadapt or responseadapt profile is configured. An iRule is triggered on the ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT or ADAPT_RESPONSE_RESULT event, that parks. The modified headers (from an ICAP server) arrive at the ADAPT filter while the first event is parked. Any iRule on the ADAPT_REQUEST_HEADERS or ADAPT_RESPONSE_HEADERS event does not park.
bugs.impact: The connection is aborted with RST cause "ADAPT unexpected state transition". The statistic "records adapted" reaches a very high number. Eventually the TMM crashes and the Big-IP fails over.
bugs.workaround: If possible, arrange the iRules to avoid the conditions above. In particular, if there is no better way, it is possible to avoid this if there is an iRule on the ADAPT_REQUEST_HEADERS or ADAPT_RESPONSE_HEADERS event that parks.
bugs.fix: ADAPT correctly processes successive iRule events exactly once for each adaptation, and the "records adapted" statistic reports the correct number.

bugs.title: IPsec Phase 1 and Phase 2 authentication algorithms default to SHA-1 in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: IPsec Phase 1 and Phase 2 authentication algorithms default to SHA-1 in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: This happens when configuring IPsec via the GUI.
bugs.impact: The authentication algorithms may be configured as SHA-1 which may not be the best choice for the use case.
bugs.workaround: Select the appropriate level of authentication algorithm strength from the pull down menu for the use case.

bugs.title: IPsec Phase 1 and Phase 2 authentication algorithms now defaults to SHA-256.
bugs.symptoms: IPsec Phase 1 and Phase 2 authentication algorithms default to SHA-1.
bugs.conditions: When creating a 'net ipsec ipsec-policy' or creating a 'net ipsec ike-peer' and taking the defaults.
bugs.impact: Security is not as good as it could be.
bugs.workaround: Configure a higher level of security. e.g. SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512.
bugs.fix: IPsec Phase 1 and Phase 2 authentication algorithms now defaults to SHA-256.

bugs.title: GRE PPTP tunnels created via the relate_client and relate_server iRules commands may fail.
bugs.symptoms: For GRE PPTP flows, the local port and remote port in the clientflow and serverflow have changed from any (port 0) to the PPP ethertype (0x880b). This affects iRules commands related to flow creation such as relate_client and relate_server. Using port 0 with these commands will no longer match incoming GRE PPTP packets and the packets will be dropped. These drops can be seen in the no_handler_deny counter in the tmm_stat table.
bugs.conditions: iRule that uses the relate_client or relate_server commands to create flows to handle GRE (IP protocol 47) PPTP traffic.
bugs.impact: All GRE PPTP packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: The relate_client and relate_server commands in the iRule should be edited to use 34827 (0x880b) for the local and remote port.

bugs.title: Setting Encryption Algorithm for AH IPsec Policy is now ignored.
bugs.symptoms: Setting Encryption Algorithm for AH IPsec Policy is meaningless and is treated as a configuration error.
bugs.conditions: Creating a 'net ipsec ipsec-policy' with the 'ip protocol' set to AH.
bugs.impact: Configuration error.
bugs.workaround: Set the encryption algorithm to NULL with configuring IPsec protocol AH.
bugs.fix: The setting for encryption algorithm is ignored and defaults to NULL when configuring IPsec protocol AH.

bugs.title: FQDN pool member remains in disabled state after removing monitor
bugs.symptoms: If an FQDN pool member has been disabled by a monitor (for example, after the monitor receives the configured recv-disable string from the node) and the monitor is then removed from the pool or member configuration, the FQDN pool member remains in a 'disabled' state (state and session-status are 'disabled') instead of changing to an 'unknown' state.
bugs.conditions: -- FQDN pool member is marked 'disabled' by a monitor. -- The monitor is then removed.
bugs.impact: The FQDN pool member remains in a 'disabled' state and is unable to receive traffic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When an FQDN pool member is marked 'disabled' by a monitor, then the monitor is removed, the FQDN pool member is updated to an 'unknown' state. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: Object properties values containing spaces are prefixed by the partition name
bugs.symptoms: The object property values containing spaces are prefixed by the /Common partition name. The object property values not containing spaces are not prefixed by /Common partition. Example: post fix: (tmos)# list security dos bot-signature one-line ... security dos bot-signature "Nmap web server probe (nice ports Trinity)" { category "Network Scanner" rule "uricontent:\"nice ports,/Trinity.txt.bak\"; nocase;" } ... prior to fix: (tmos)# list security dos bot-signature one-line ... security dos bot-signature "Nmap web server probe (nice ports Trinity)" { category "/Common/Network Scanner" rule "uricontent:\"nice ports,/Trinity.txt.bak\"; nocase;" } security::dos::bot-signature is one example of this behavior. However, this may impact all property values that contain spaces in them.
bugs.conditions: Object property-values contain spaces in them.
bugs.impact: The tmsh list action or save config action will save the partition name /Common for property value of objects in /Common partition that contain spaces in them.
bugs.workaround: None, but this is a cosmetic issue. It does not lead to any incorrect configuration behavior. It is just a inconsistent listing depending upon whether the value contains the space character or not.
bugs.fix: The property values with or without spaces exhibit identical behavior. The listing of the property does not contain the /Common as a prefix.

bugs.title: parking command used in the nesting script of clientside and serverside command can cause tmm core
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores in configuration using certain iRules
bugs.conditions: An iRule that parks the interpreter is used in the nesting script of clientside and serverside command. (e.g. when doing a table lookup). For more information on iRule commands that park, see SOL12962: Some iRule commands temporarily suspend iRule processing, https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/12000/900/sol12962.html
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: move the parking command outside the nesting script.

bugs.title: 'C_GetAttributeValue error' with netHSM
bugs.symptoms: When netHSM is used with the BIG-IP system, there are intermittent messages containing text similar to the following: C_GetAttributeValue error.
bugs.conditions: When netHSM is used.
bugs.impact: C_GetAttributeValue error are posted. These messages are benign and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: This error message is not harmful. User can ignore them in the log.
bugs.fix: When netHSM is used, the benign 'C_GetAttributeValue error' messages are no longer posted.

bugs.title: ASU cannot be completed if license was last activated more than 18 months before
bugs.symptoms: Attack Signature Update (ASU) if license was last activated more than 18 months before.
bugs.conditions: The license was last activated more than 18 months before.
bugs.impact: Attack SIgnature Update (ASU) cannot be performed.
bugs.workaround: The license must be re-activated.
bugs.fix: Attack Signature Update (ASU) can now be completed based on a license retrieved from server.

bugs.title: APM Network Access IPv4/IPv6 virtual may leak memory
bugs.symptoms: Observation of performance graphs shows increasing TMM memory usage over time. Specifically, connflow and tunnel_nexthop caches grow over time.
bugs.conditions: APM virtual with Network Access configured with no SNAT and both IPV4 and IPV6 enabled.
bugs.impact: Memory leakage over time leads to performance degradation and possible traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: No workaround short of not enabling IPv6 support.
bugs.fix: Network Access now correctly manages its memory resources.

bugs.title: F-bit is not set in IPv6 OSPF Type-7 LSAs
bugs.symptoms: The forwarding address and the F-bit are not set in Type-7 LSAs sent out by the ASBR.
bugs.conditions: Virtual IP from a virtual server is redistributed as a Type-7 route by the ASBR.
bugs.impact: ABR routers are not able to propagate NSSA routes to other OSPF areas as External Type-5 routes. As a result, OSPF areas cannot reach external networks.
bugs.fix: ASBR sets the F-bit and forwarding address correctly.

bugs.title: DNS Search suffix are not restored properly in some cases after VPN establishment
bugs.symptoms: Modified DNS suffix after VPN establishment and closure may result in failure to resolve some DNS names
bugs.conditions: DNS Relay proxy service is stopped in the middle of VPN session. User's machine is rebooted.
bugs.impact: DNS suffixes are not restored properly which may lead to incorrect resolution of certain DNS names.
bugs.workaround: Any of the following workarounds 1) Do not stop DNS relay proxy service in the middle of a VPN session 2)Restore DNS search suffixes manually.

bugs.title: CPLD update success logs at the same error level as an update failure
bugs.symptoms: On booting after a successful CPLD update, you see an error in /var/log/ltm: "err chmand[4933]: 012a0003:3: CPLD not updated after previous power cycle."
bugs.conditions: This occurs during reboot after a successful firmware update
bugs.impact: The message is logged as an error, but it actually means that the CPLD version is as it is expected to be. This error can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: CPLD update not required is now logged at the info level, not error.

bugs.title: FQDN pool members not shown by tmsh show ltm monitor
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh 'show ltm monitor <monitor-type>' command does not display the status of FQDN pool members.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM monitor is assigned to FQDN pool members (including FQDN members of an LTM pool to which the monitor is assigned). -- Running the tmsh command: show ltm monitor <monitor-type>.
bugs.impact: Unable to view status of FQDN pool members via the tmsh 'show ltm monitor <monitor-type>' command.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The status of FQDN pool members is displayed by the tmsh 'show ltm monitor <monitor-type>' command. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: BIG-IP's Proxy-SSL is unable to handle fragmented SSL handshakes
bugs.symptoms: An SSL client can fragment a handshake message into multiple pieces (a fragmented set of handshakes). When BIG-IP receives such an SSL fragmented set of handshakes, it fails to recognize and reassemble the fragments. One of the ways in which this is happening is when Big-IP receives an SSL client certificate chain containing a large number of issuers. BIG-IP receives this as a fragmented set of handshakes and is unable to recognize as such. For RSA-4096, if the certificate chain contains at least 20 issuers, a handshake error is reported from BIG-IP and the connection is aborted.
bugs.conditions: The condition, below, is one among a few possible cases if the clientssl profile is configured with proxy-ssl enabled. - Client certificate chain has a depth of at least 20, for RSA-4096 client certificates and its issuers. (For RSA-2048, the depth is more. We don't know at the moment how much.) This assumes that all certificates (including issuers) possess the same key-length (4096 for RSA). If the key length differs in any one, the depth threshold may be more (if shorter key length) or less (if larger key length).
bugs.impact: When receiving fragmented ssl handshake message, the handshake fails, if tmm debug logging is enabled you will see "debug tmm1[10284]: 01260009:7: Connection error: ssl_hs_pxy_scan:9143: malformed ssl record (47)"
bugs.workaround: One of the ways in which the issue is triggered is with very large client certificates. This particular case can be mitigated. The workaround is to use client certificate chains that have a depth of up to 19 (for RSA-4096). The sub-case mentions the workaround through the removal of advertised certificates.

bugs.title: Erroneous error message Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_FOUND may appear in APM logs
bugs.symptoms: When a user session times out, then subsequently attempts access using the expired session ID, APM may log a log message at "err" level similar to this: Aug 15 14:54:25 bigip.hostname err tmm[10206]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_FOUND. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access_session.c, Function: access_session_delete, Line:
bugs.conditions: User is logged into APM and session times out.
bugs.impact: Error log messages may be confusing to BIG-IP APM administrators. The client is able to successfully reconnect.
bugs.fix: Erroneous messages of "Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_FOUND" are no longer logged in the APM log.

bugs.title: flash.utils.Proxy functionality is not negotiated
bugs.symptoms: Access to some field names of classes inherited from flash.utils.Proxy is broken.
bugs.conditions: Presence of flash.utils.Proxy descendants.
bugs.impact: Customer application malfunction.

bugs.title: New option to re-schedule datasync background tasks
bugs.symptoms: The datasync framework runs tasks in the background for use by the data plane. This is currently obfuscation of JavaScript for ASM and FPS, and generation of RSA keys for FPS. This happens during several hours every day in a low priority process.
bugs.conditions: The process starts every day at the same time, according to the time in which ASM or FPS were first provisioned. The time persists across upgrades, and is synced in the trust domain using the datasync-global-dg device-group.
bugs.impact: There is currently no simple way to reschedule these background tasks.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: There is now a simple method to reschedule the daily start time of the Datasync Background Tasks on GUI and TMSH/REST. In the GUI you can find this in Security :: Options : Background Tasks. In tmsh it is available via tmsh security datasync background-tasks.

bugs.title: Virtual servers configured with CMP enabled on a chassis can cause cascading primary blade failures when synced across a device group
bugs.symptoms: When a blade syncs its config with a peer device in a device group, an mcpd core dump triggers a new primary blade. If auto-sync is turned on the new primary will attempt to sync again, core dump, and cascade to the next primary.
bugs.conditions: There must be a virtual server synced in the device group configured with CMP enabled and an iRule. The chassis must also have a local non-synced virtual server referencing the same iRule. If that iRule is deleted on the peer device, it will cause a core dump on the chassis when the change is synced.
bugs.impact: If auto-sync is disabled on the device group and a user issues a manual sync, the primary blade will core and a new primary will come up out of sync but functional. If auto-sync is enabled on the device group, a cascading primary blade failure will occur. Every time a new primary is established, it will attempt to sync and core dump. This leaves the chassis in a state where the primary blade can't be established.
bugs.workaround: If auto-sync is turned on then disable it first to prevent cascading failures. One of several things can be done: 1. Remove the reference from the non-synced virtual server to the iRule that is in the device group. 3. Turn off CMP on the non-synced virtual server 2. Undo the delete of the iRule on the peer by either recreating it or loading a backup UCS. Attempt a manual sync and make sure it succeeds before turning auto-sync back on.

bugs.title: In some cases, only primary blade retains it's statistics after upgrade on multi bladed system
bugs.symptoms: Statistics from the primary blade remain after upgrade, but not from the other blades.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to new version in multi bladed system.
bugs.impact: Not all statistics are present after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: No workaround

bugs.title: Safenet HSM installation script fails to install successfully if partition password contains special metacharacters (!#{}')
bugs.symptoms: Safenet HSM installation script fails to install successfully if partition password contains special metacharacters (!#{}').
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Safenet HSM installation. -- Password contains special metacharacters (!#{}').
bugs.impact: Script fails to work properly, and fails to properly install/configure the HSMs, requiring manual intervention. Performing the operation manually is very complex, because the user must account for both tmsh and shell quoting, which the some user environments might not have.
bugs.workaround: Change password, or manually run tmsh command to define the /sys crypto fips external-hsm object (using proper shell quoting).
bugs.fix: Safenet HSM installation script install now completes successfully if partition password contains special metacharacters (!#{}'). Note: When using passwords with non-alphanumeric characters, make sure that they are escaped correctly, so that bash does not attempt to reinterpret or expand the password.

bugs.title: BGP may not accept attributes using extended length
bugs.symptoms: If a BGP peer sends a path attribute using the "extended length" flag and field, the attribute may be rejected and the BGP connection terminated.
bugs.conditions: Neighbor sends path attributes using extended length.
bugs.impact: The BGP adacency will repeatedly bounce and the RIB will never converge.
bugs.fix: Received BGP attributes using extended length are no longer rejected.

bugs.title: GTM autoconf can cause high CPU usage for gtmd
bugs.symptoms: The autoconf feature of GTM can cause high CPU utilization (~90%) under certain situations. In large configurations of LTM vses that contain "." (dot) in the name.
bugs.conditions: Large configuration of LTM VS that contain "." in the name have the name converted ("." is replaced by "_") and the LTM VS name is saved to the config. This causes the matching algorithm in autoconf to spend many CPU cycles walking the list of VS to find a match. This problem is caused by large numbers of VSes on a GTM Server. (10k VSes on 10k Server is less of an issue than 10k VSes on 1 GTM Server)
bugs.impact: CPU usage is high, which may impact monitoring and LB decisions.
bugs.workaround: There are some mitigations. The preferable (for performance and stability) are listed first. 1. Rename the virtual servers on the LTM to remove the "." This would require deleting the GTM configuration and rediscovering it and recreating pools. 2. Turn off autoconf. Run autoconf once to populate the config, then turn it off. 3. Reduce the frequency of autoconf. It will still cause a high CPU usage scenario, but it will be less frequent. Versions 12.0.0 and higher do not convert the "." to "_". So that problem is eliminated for new configurations. If a customer upgrades to 12.0.0 and the config still contains VS names that were previously converted, they still may run into high CPU usage. Upgrading to 12.0.0 alone does not fix this issue, a reconfig would be necessary.
bugs.fix: Change algorithm used to match LTM VS names to GTM VS to reduce linear walk of all VSes on a server.

bugs.title: TMM crash after changing raccoon log level
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes after changing the raccoon log level to debug2
bugs.conditions: Debug level is set to debug2 while tmm is passing traffic
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: set debug level to INFO
bugs.fix: A tmm crash related to changing the debug level while passing traffic has been fixed.

bugs.title: Support for New Platform: BIG-IP 10350 FIPS with NEBS support
bugs.symptoms: New platform introduction
bugs.conditions: New platform introduction
bugs.impact: New platform introduction

bugs.title: Network access webtop does not prompt the user if user closes browser window
bugs.symptoms: On Microsoft Windows, if VPN is launched from a network access webtop, and user closes the browser window, VPN is killed immediately without warning the user that VPN will be closed
bugs.conditions: User launches VPN from browser on Windows. Network access webtop is configured on APM.
bugs.impact: VPN session is closed without warning.
bugs.workaround: Do not use network access webtop. Use full webtop.
bugs.fix: Network access webtop now provides a prompt, if the user closes the browser window when VPN is launched from a network access webtop.

bugs.title: Add AES-GCM support for ssldump
bugs.symptoms: ssldump is unable to decrypt AES-GCM ciphers.
bugs.conditions: This applies only when the following SSL cipher suites are negotiated: AES128-GCM-SHA256 AES256-GCM-SHA384
bugs.impact: This makes it more difficult to analyze SSL related issue.
bugs.fix: Add AES-GCM cipher support.
