bugs.title: Invalid characters allowed in hostname
bugs.symptoms: The hostname not being RFC 952/RFC 1123 compliant.
bugs.conditions: Characters in the hostname making the hostname not RFC 952/RFC 1123 compliant.
bugs.impact: The hostname won't be RFC 952/RFC 1123 compliant.
bugs.workaround: Don't add characters to the hostname making the hostname not RFC 952/RFC 1123 compliant.

bugs.title: Block All - Session Tracking Status is not persisted across an auto-sync device group
bugs.symptoms: Users, IP addresses, and Sessions that are meant to be blocked due to their traffic patterns, are not being synchronized to the peer device in an auto-sync device group with ASM sync enabled. This can lead to bad actors becoming unblocked again after failover, or in an Active-Active configuration.
bugs.conditions: 1) Devices are in an auto-sync device group with ASM sync enabled. 2) Session Tracking is enabled.
bugs.impact: This can lead to bad actors becoming unblocked again after failover, or in an Active-Active configuration.
bugs.workaround: Force a full sync to propagate the session tracking information.

bugs.title: MCP may crash when syncing configuration between device groups
bugs.symptoms: mcpd on the sync target crashes when syncing configuration.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when a local non-synced object references an object that is synced (such as a local-only virtual server referencing a synced iRule), and a non-synced object on the target machine happens to be referencing the same synced object. In this condition, mcpd could crash if objects in a sync group are deleted and synced.
bugs.impact: Outage due to mcp crash which causes tmm to restart.
bugs.workaround: When you have devices with local-only resources that are referencing objects contained in a sync/failover group, avoid deleting any objects (such as iRules) that might be referenced by other local-only resources on other devices. Instead of a "this object is in use error", mcpd on the target machine will crash.
bugs.fix: Verify existence of rule objects when validating configuration.

bugs.title: If an SSL client disconnects while data is being sent to SSL client, the connection may stall until TCP timeout.
bugs.symptoms: If an SSL connection gracefully begins to disconnect at the same time as data is being encrypted by SSL acceleration hardware, the connection will remain open until the TCP profile timeout occurs instead of being closed immediately. This can cause unwanted higher memory usage, possibly causing crashes elsewhere.
bugs.conditions: * A virtual server with ClientSSL or ServerSSL profile. * BIG-IP SSL acceleration hardware. * While an SSL record is being encrypted by SSL accelerator hardware, the SSL connection begins to close by client TCP FIN or by any iRule command that closes the connection.
bugs.impact: There is a potential for higher memory usage, which in turn may cause TMM crash due to memory exhaustion resulting in service disruption.
bugs.workaround: If the affected SSL traffic does not include any long idle periods, memory consumption can be mitigated by reducing the idle timeout of the TCP or SCTP profile.
bugs.fix: SSL connections now disconnect normally if a disconnect attempt occurs while data is being encrypted by SSL acceleration hardware.

bugs.title: Publishing DNS statistics if only Global Traffic and AVR are provisioned
bugs.symptoms: AVR does not publish DNS statistics if LTM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: LTM is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: The DNS chart does not show statistics.
bugs.fix: We changed the condition when we published DNS statistic in this configuration.

bugs.title: Content Based Routing daemon (cbrd) logging control
bugs.symptoms: The cbrd logger might not produce enough useful output for troubleshooting purposes, and debug logging is not available.
bugs.conditions: Using xml profile, and you would like to see the xpath prints to a log file.
bugs.impact: Unable to see the xpath information
bugs.fix: It is now possible to enable xpath logging by adding these lines to /etc/cbr/logger.cfg: MODULE=CBR_PLUGIN; LOG_LEVEL=TS_INFO | TS_DEBUG; FILE = 2; Then: bigstart restart cbrd

bugs.title: Rarely encountered lockup for N3FIPS module when processing key management requests.
bugs.symptoms: The N3FIPS module does not respond to key management requests.
bugs.conditions: No specific condition has been identified for this failure.
bugs.impact: Existing data continues to forward, but new traffic keys fail. MGMT locks up. This is a rarely encountered issue.
bugs.workaround: A SNMP trap is generated when N3FIPS is locked up. The trap informs the user that the BIG-IP system must be rebooted. Rebooting clears the condition.
bugs.fix: The N3FIPS module no longer experiences occasional lockups when processing key management requests.

bugs.title: keys remain on FIPS card after deletion
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes when 'delete sys crypto key all' is executed with 5K fips keys, the keys are deleted from mcpd but still exist on the fips card. Subsequent key creation may fail with error 'max capacity reached'
bugs.conditions: It is not known what causes this.
bugs.impact: Keys may remain on the FIPS card, and may prevent the creation of additional keys

bugs.title: Hundreds of images are taking hours to import
bugs.symptoms: If access policy is linked to hundreds of images it might take hours to import. Import is possible only in shell, because gui is getting timeout with this.
bugs.conditions: Always with hundreds of images
bugs.impact: Unable to import images using the GUI. Only shell import is possible.

bugs.title: Unable to resume session when switching to Protected Workspace
bugs.symptoms: Clients logging into Protected Workspace are unable to view the page. The client's log file may have the following signature: HandlePwsCmd, detoured.dll signature validation error
bugs.conditions: This occurs infrequently on certain Windows clients logging into Protected Workspace
bugs.impact: Client browser cannot render the protected workspace
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue preventing Windows clients from using Protected Workspace

bugs.title: BIG-IP as a SAML Service Provider may fail to resolve Artifact for Assertion when route domains are configured
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP as a SAML Service Provider fails to resolve Artifact for Assertion when using a default route domain other than 0 in administrative partitions other than "Common".
bugs.conditions: - SAML Service Provider objects 'apm aaa saml' and 'apm aaa saml-idp-connector' are created in an administrative partition other than 'Common' - Default route domain other than 0 is used for a partition where objects are created. - BIG-IP used as a SAML Service Provider and is configured to use Artifact binding.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP can fail to resolve Artifact for an Assertion, which subsequently will fail SAML SSO.
bugs.workaround: Configure SAML Service Provider to use HTTP-POST binding instead of Artifact binding.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP as SAML Service Provider will use default route domain from administrative partition "Common" to resolve Artifact for Assertion.

bugs.title: ASM chassis sync occasionally fails to load on secondary slot
bugs.symptoms: ASM chassis sync occasionally fails to load on secondary slot when a new policy is created after a series of other configuration changes in quick succession.
bugs.conditions: A new policy is created after a series of other configuration changes in quick succession
bugs.impact: ASM chassis sync fails to load on secondary slot.
bugs.workaround: Make another system-wide configuration change, such as creating a user-defined signature, or wait until the hourly sync occurs.
bugs.fix: ASM chassis blades are now synchronized correctly after every policy creation.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 and SPDY do not parse the path for the location/existence of the query parameter
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 and SPDY do not parse the path for the location/existence of the query parameter.
bugs.conditions: when http/2 or spdy is configured and client query URI contains '?' (question mark).
bugs.impact: No query parameter will be returned.
bugs.fix: Issue fixed.

bugs.title: failed to load configuration, when cache_cleanup property is defined for AAA AD/LDAP server
bugs.symptoms: failure happens when loading configuration and creating AAA AD/LDAP server. cannot load configuration, until AAA AD/LDAP server is modified. the problem is indicated by error log message "Cannot cleanup cache while creating AAA AD Server" The same issue happens during creation of AAA AD/LDAP server if the option cache-cleanup is defined (not 0)
bugs.conditions: cache_cleanup property of AAA AD/LDAP server supposed to be set '0' all the time, except when cache cleanup is requested. if, by any reason, the property is not set to '0' when system starts up, then the system tries to cleanup non existing caches and fails to load configuration.
bugs.impact: Unable to start the system
bugs.workaround: using tmsh, modify object AAA AD/LDAP Server and set cache-cleanup propery to '0' when creating AAA AD/LDAP server, never set cache-cleanup property
bugs.fix: when creating an AAA AD/LDAP Server object and cache-cleanup property is specified (other than none), the property is not applied, as there is no cache yet. when modifying an AAA AD/LDAP Server object and cache-cleanup propery is speified along with any other setting, the cache-cleanup property is not applied, but other settings are modified as requested. error log message generated that cache was not cleaned this time.

bugs.title: Edge browser prompts user to install an application from Windows Store if Endpoint Inspection is configured
bugs.symptoms: When a user connects to an APM device configured with Endpoint Inspection for the first time using the Edge browser, the browser prompts the user to install an application from the Windows Store. This is confusing because there is no application in the store.
bugs.conditions: - Edge Browser is used - APM configured with Endpoint Inspection - No recent F5 Networks client components installed on the system
bugs.impact: Potential confusion, which might generate support calls.
bugs.workaround: Have the end user dismiss this dialog box and follow the prompts in the browser to download and install the F5 client components.

bugs.title: 'ACCESS::session exists' returns TCL error if there is no APM session associated with connflow
bugs.symptoms: 'ACCESS::session exists' returns TCL error if there is no APM session associated with connflow
bugs.conditions: There is no APM session associated with connflow
bugs.impact: Uncaught TCL errors result in connection termination and RST being sent to client or backend. Functionality that uses iRules with 'ACCESS::session exists' may be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Internal F5 iRules do not have workaround. Customer iRules can be modified to run 'ACCESS::session exists' inside catch {}. This will not lead to connection termination / RST.
bugs.fix: 'ACCESS::session exists' now returns false instead of TCL error when there is no APM session associated with connflow.

bugs.title: Forwarding flows leak when a routing update changes the egress vlan
bugs.symptoms: Forwarding flow doesn’t expire and leaks a connflow object.
bugs.conditions: Conditions to hit this are a route change on forwarded flows.
bugs.impact: Memory leak.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak with forwarding flows.

bugs.title: APM Network Access IPV4/IPV6 virtual may leak memory
bugs.symptoms: Observation of performance graphs shows increasing TMM memory usage over time. Specifically, xhead and xdata caches grow over time. Additionally, the ppp_npmode_errors in the ppp stat table will increment with each leak.
bugs.conditions: APM virtual with Network Access configured with IPV4 and IPv6.
bugs.impact: Memory leakage over time leads to performance degradation and possible traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: No workaround short of not enabling IPv6.
bugs.fix: APM Network Access now correctly manages its memory resources.

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator: Add the ability to dynamically update the CA bundles on the BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Maintaining CA bundle files on the BIG-IP system is a manual process, which can result in repeated overhead and potential mistakes.
bugs.conditions: Adding, deleting, merging, updating CA bundle files on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Incur administrative overhead for CA bundle file maintenance.
bugs.workaround: Manual process for adding, deleting and updating CA bundle files and configuration objects.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP users can now automate some of the CA bundle management processes, such as adding, deleting, or updating a CA bundle from local file systems or online sources, and merging, subtracting certificates from multiple CA bundle files.

bugs.title: HTTP request dropped when using ACCESS::disable from iRule and a Per-Request Policy
bugs.symptoms: When ACCESS::disable command is used in an iRule along with a Category Lookup agent in a per-request policy, the HTTP request we be incorrectly dropped and the connection reset. This error condition may also occur with other per-request policy agents.
bugs.conditions: APM deployed with a Per-Request policy using a Category-Lookup agent and an iRule which issues the ACCESS::disable command associated on the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: The HTTP request will be dropped or the HTTP connection will stall and timeout.

bugs.title: Excessive failures observed when connection rate limit is configured on a fastl4 virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: When connection rate limit is set on a fastL4 virtual server, client connections hang with high probability.
bugs.conditions: Set Connection Rate Limit on a fastL4 virtual server.
bugs.impact: Client connections hang with high probability.
bugs.workaround: Do rate limiting using iSession.
bugs.fix: Fixed Connection Rate Limiting on a fastL4 virtual server.

bugs.title: Fix memory leak.
bugs.symptoms: System exhausts available memory due to compression memory leak. Prior to running out of memory, repeatedly logs "Nitrox3 Hang Detected".
bugs.conditions: Compression device unavailable during creation of a new context.
bugs.impact: System can run out of memory.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware compression using tmsh: % tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy softwareonly
bugs.fix: Repaired memory leak.

bugs.title: Tagged VLAN configurations with a cmp-hash setting for the VLAN, might result in performance issues.
bugs.symptoms: Tagged VLAN configurations with a cmp-hash setting for the VLAN, might result in performance issues.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: 1. Use of tagged VLANs in the configuration. 2. Change cmp-hash of the tagged VLAN.
bugs.impact: Throughput is lower than expected. Packets are not being hashed using the hash set in config. (This can be verified by looking at 'tmm/flow_redir_stat'.)
bugs.workaround: Use untagged VLANs and hypervisor side tagging.
bugs.fix: You can now use tagged VLAN configurations along with a cmp-hash setting for the VLAN, without compromising performance.

bugs.title: Management DHCP settings do not take effect
bugs.symptoms: Modifications to /sys management-dhcp do not take effect.
bugs.conditions: Custom management-dhcp settings configured.
bugs.impact: DHCP for management interface does not function correctly.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following procedure: 1. Remount /usr to be read-write. # mount -o rw,remount /usr 2. Edit the following file, which is a symlink into /usr. # vi /defaults/config/templates/dhcp.tmpl 3. Change this line around line 7 to add escaped quotes print "interface \"$mgmt_interface\" {\n"; 4. Remount /usr back to read-only. # mount -o ro,remount /usr 5. Make a change to the list of DHCP requested options. # tmsh modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config request-options delete { ntp-servers } 6. Verify that "eth0" is quoted in this file: # grep interface /etc/dhclient.conf interface "eth0" { 7. Create a symbolic link to dhclient.conf # cd /etc/dhcp # ln -s ../dhclient.conf . 8. Restart DHCP on the management interface. # tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp disabled # tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp enabled No system reboot should be necessary.
bugs.fix: Management DHCP settings now take effect as expected when custom management-dhcp settings are configured.

bugs.title: asm_config_server_rpc_handler_async.pl SIGSEGV and core
bugs.symptoms: asm_config_server_rpc_handler_async.pl SIGSEGV and core
bugs.conditions: Import ASM XML security policy
bugs.impact: asm_config_server_rpc_handler_async.pl SIGSEGV and core. This occurs after the policy import completes.
bugs.fix: The asm_config_server_rpc_handler_async.pl no longer crashes upon import ASM XML security policy.

bugs.title: Analytics reports may not identify virtual servers correctly
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, Analytics statistics on virtual server activity may not be reported correctly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for virtual servers that are configured in one of these ways: 1. Two virtual servers have the same IP-Port-RouteDomain setting, but they use different protocols (such as TCP for one and UDP for the other) or different sources. 2. A virtual server is defined with a masked IP address rather than an explicit address (for example, 10.10.10.0/24).
bugs.impact: As a result, Analytics reports show an Aggregated Virtual Server or an incorrect one instead of displaying the correct virtual servers.
bugs.fix: Correct identification of the virtual server and the activity reported in the charts is displaying to the right virtual server.

bugs.title: Syn Cookie cache statistics on ePVA enabled devices is incremented with UDP traffic
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios UDP traffic can cause syncookie statistics to be incremented.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with fastL4 profile with ePVA offload enabled. Virtual server to handle UDP traffic.
bugs.impact: Statistics might be incorrectly incremented, and can lead to early syncookie activation if used in conjunction with TCP on the same virtual server.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer increases Syn Cookie cache statistics on ePVA enabled devices with UDP traffic.

bugs.title: DNS Relay proxy service does not respond to SCM commands in timely manner
bugs.symptoms: DNS relay proxy service may appear unresponsive when stopped/started through Service control manager and user may see a system dialog box saying "Service did not respond in a timely manner"
bugs.conditions: DNS relay services component of edge client is installed on user's machine
bugs.impact: Usability, User may think that service has failed.
bugs.workaround: Wait for service to respond proper status
bugs.fix: Service now reports correct status to service control manager immediately.

bugs.title: No violation details for illegal metachar violation when shift-jis is the web app language
bugs.symptoms: No violation details in the GUI for the illegal metachar violation.
bugs.conditions: 1. Web app language is shift-jis. 2. An illegal metachar violation (for example, %3b is semicolon ';', is illegal in the shift-jis encoding).
bugs.impact: There are no details to indicate which metachar caused the violation.
bugs.fix: There are now violation details in the GUI for the illegal metachar violation.

bugs.title: MCPd might leak memory in firewall stats.
bugs.symptoms: MCPd might leak memory in firewall stats.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at firewall stats.
bugs.impact: Unknown

bugs.title: Unexpected backslashes remain in monitor 'username' attribute after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: The monitor 'username' attribute contains unexpected backslashes.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from an earlier version with a configuration that contains a monitor 'username' attribute with at least one escaped backslash ('\\').
bugs.impact: Monitor probes contain excess backslashes which can lead to monitor failures.
bugs.workaround: Un-escape backslashes after upgrade by transforming '\\' sequences to '\'.
bugs.fix: Removed excess backslashes from monitor 'username' attribute during upgrade process.

bugs.title: Error is not posted when a UCS file with FIPS keys is loaded after re-initializing the FIPS card
bugs.symptoms: When a UCS with FIPS keys is loaded after re-initializing the FIPS card, errors should be posted that the FIPS keys in the configuration that are now invalid. Instead, the configuration loads without any errors, and SSL handshake failures are seen when a clientSSL profile uses the FIPS key.
bugs.conditions: UCS file with FIPS keys is loaded after re-initializing the FIPS card.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake failures are seen when a clientSSL profile uses the FIPS key.
bugs.workaround: You can delete the FIPS keys, re-initialize the FIPS card, then install the needed keys.

bugs.title: BIG-IQ Discovery may fail due to an invalid passphrase.

bugs.workaround: Run the following command on the BIG-IP system: bigstart restart restjavad

This can happen when there are multiple HTTP::request events attached to a virtual and each can invoke HTTP::respond. A new TCL command HTTP::has_response has been introduced that returns a boolean to indicate that HTTP::respond has already been invoked.

bugs.title: non-local static ARP entries are not recreated on tmm restart

bugs.conditions: Restarting TMM with non-local static ARP entry, or creating static ARP entry for address without a directly connected route.
bugs.impact: Creation of non-local static ARP entry
bugs.workaround: Re-create static arp entry after TMM restart. Or re-create static arp entry after adding a self-ip with network covering the static ARP address.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP will no longer allow creation of static arp entry that can not be resolved.

bugs.title: Apply Security Policies Only During Specified Times
bugs.symptoms: When in Automatic mode Policy Builder might apply policy changes at any time. There is no way to constrain changes to a specific time or schedule.
bugs.conditions: Policy Builder is used in automatic mode, and ramcache is being used.
bugs.impact: When changes to policy are applied the ramcache is flushed.
bugs.fix: A schedule can now be set for when to apply policy changes. This feature allows the option to apply changes to policies built by Policy Builder on scheduled interval/dates. This allows scheduling it during low traffic time, at night.

bugs.title: Traffic statistics on a SNAT object might not be updated if traffic is ePVA accelerated.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic statistics on a SNAT object might not be updated if traffic is ePVA accelerated.
bugs.conditions: SNAT object on a ePVA capable platform.
bugs.impact: Some traffic-related statistics (pkts/bytes in/out) are not updated.
bugs.workaround: To get these statistics, convert the global SNAT to an appropriate virtual server.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly updates traffic statistics on a SNAT object if traffic is ePVA accelerated.

bugs.title: Running concurrent TMSH instances can result in error in access to history file
bugs.symptoms: TMSH writes to the ~/.tmsh-history-username file whenever a command is issued. Running concurrent instances of TMSH can result in a race condition in writing this file.
bugs.conditions: Running multiple instances can cause one instance of TMSH to lock the history file while the other is trying to access it, resulting in an error.
bugs.impact: Updating the history file fails, so the file does not reflect the actual history of the commands that have been issued.
bugs.workaround: Only run a single instance of TMSH.
bugs.fix: Running concurrent TMSH instances no longer results in error in access to history file.

bugs.title: Rewrite can crash in some rare corner cases
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite can crash in some rare corner cases when some specific erroneous elements are present in an HTML content.

bugs.impact: Web application malfunction.
bugs.workaround: iRule or direct fix of improper HTML tag.
bugs.fix: Fixed.

bugs.title: ASM policies are created as inactive policies on the peer device
bugs.symptoms: ASM policies are created as inactive policies on the peer device.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- ASM Sync is enabled on a Sync-Only auto-sync Device Group. -- There is either no failover group, or the failover group is a manual sync group.
bugs.impact: ASM policies are created as inactive policies on the peer device, resulting in an inconsistency between peers.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Set the device group with ASM sync enabled to manual sync. -- Enable auto-sync for the failover group.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the ASM Synchronization mechanism so that ASM policies are correctly created on the peer device

bugs.title: NetHSM does not come back after TCP connection to device is reset
bugs.symptoms: NetHSM does not come back after TCP connection to device is reset.
bugs.conditions: TCP connection to NetHSM device is reset.
bugs.impact: NetHSM stops working.
bugs.fix: NetHSM connectivity is restored after TCP connection to device is reset.

bugs.title: MCPd might leak memory in SCTP profile stats query.

bugs.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) configuration error when no clientssl profile is present

bugs.conditions: Creating or modifying a virtual server with HTTP profile and HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) enabled, when no clientssl or derived profile is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Error while configuring a virtual server with HTTP profile and no "clientssl" (or derived) profile attached, when HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Add a "clientssl" (or derived) profile to the virtual server with HTTP profile and HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) enabled.
bugs.fix: The system now provides validation of HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) to require 'clientssl' (or derived) profile profile to a virtual server with HTTP profile and HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) enabled.

bugs.title: SNMP traps for FIPS device fault inconsistent among versions.
bugs.symptoms: The snmp traps bigipFipsDeviceError and bigipFipsFault are inconsistent among versions.
bugs.conditions: This trap is raised if the FIPS device firmware has stopped responding to requests and is no longer functional. The trap is different on the BIG-IP 10350 FIPS platform.
bugs.impact: The meaning of the trap is that the system is not able to perform any FIPS operations and process FIPS related traffic. You will need to be mindful of which version you are on to interpret the OIDs correctly.
bugs.fix: An SNMP trap is generated when the system has detected a FIPS device fault indicating that said device can no longer service FIPS operations. The OIDs are different across versions and one specific platform. Here is the OIDs and versions: BIGIP-COMMON-MIB::bigipFipsDeviceError .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.152 This trap means "Encountered error in the FIPS card operation" on all FIPS platforms BIGIP-COMMON-MIB::bigipFipsFault .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.156 (from v11.5.4-hf1 and 11.6.1, not 12.0.0) BIGIP-COMMON-MIB::bigipFipsFault .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.166 (from v12.1.0) These traps mean "The FIPS card is currently in faulty state" for the specific FIPS hardware included on the BIG-IP 10350

bugs.title: External input from client doesn't pass to policy agent if it is not the first in the chain.
bugs.symptoms: When client gets authenticated, and then the session is deleted (times out or is manually deleted from memcache), the browser still has its authorization token. If client refreshes the page, the browser passes the existing 'authorization' token, which gets deleted by the agent processing the existing task (a message box, in this case) for the targeted agent (HTTP_401_Response agent, in this case).
bugs.conditions: When a logon page is not the first agent in the access policy chain and it gets a pre-authenticated token from browser.
bugs.impact: Although client (browser) sends the pre-authenticated token, the browser still posts a challenge for credential (pop up window). This is unnecessary and should not occur.
bugs.fix: An HTTP_401_RESPONSE page can be placed anywhere in the access policy chain. Any pre-authenticated information for the targeted agent will not be consumed by another agent sitting in front.

bugs.title: Enable support for the Purpose-Built DDoS Hybrid Defender Platform
bugs.conditions: Requires new DoS License
bugs.fix: This fix adds support for recognition of a Purpose-Built DDoS Hybrid Defender license, and the necessary mechanisms to launch the DDoS Application.
bugs.behavior: There is no change in behavior to existing behavior and functionalities. However, when a DoS License is installed, the Big-IP platform takes on the role of a dedicated DoS protection device. Consequently most non-DoS related functionalities are either disabled or function in limited capacity.

bugs.title: If you have MSSQL proxy feature configured, you will lose it upon upgrading to v12.1.0 or later.
bugs.symptoms: MSSQL proxy is removed from BIG-IP product.
bugs.conditions: This will occur on the upgrade to 12.1.0 or higher if you had the MSSQL proxy configured.
bugs.impact: MSSQL proxy is no longer supported.
bugs.behavior: If you have MSSQL proxy feature configured, you will lose it upon upgrading to v13.0 or later.

bugs.title: Support for some future credit card number ranges
bugs.symptoms: ASM does not block or mask when a specific credit card number range (planned for the future) appears in the response.
bugs.conditions: The Data Guard feature is turned on and set to Block, Alarm or Mask. The responses contains credit card number with specific ranges.
bugs.impact: The traffic passes unmasked or unblocked to the end client.
bugs.workaround: A custom pattern is possible for these cases, but should be adjusted to each customer specifically.

bugs.title: Online help in the GUI missing details in description of "Bad multipart parameters parsing" HTTP validation
bugs.symptoms: Online help in the GUI missing details in description of "Bad multipart parameters parsing" HTTP validation
bugs.conditions: This is seen in the online help for Security :: Application Security : Blocking : Settings for Bad multipart parameters missing.
bugs.impact: This makes it difficult to properly configure this setting.
bugs.fix: Updated the online help in the GUI for the "Bad multipart parameters parsing" sub-violation in the HTTP protocol compliance failed Violations list.

bugs.title: ASM does not start up after TMM crash on a 3600 platform
bugs.symptoms: ASM does not start up after TMM crash on a 3600 platform. In the ASM log there are repeated insufficient thread messages. In the bd log there is a loop of restarts and SIGTERMs happening right after starting up.
bugs.conditions: tmm crashed or stopped causing the system to restart asm.
bugs.impact: ASM is not running. If bypass ASM is not configured, traffic is not getting through.
bugs.workaround: Run: bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: Default Session Summary reports are not present for new users with report access.
bugs.symptoms: Default Session Summary reports are not present for new users with report access.
bugs.conditions: Before you set the default report, the Default Session Summary report does not appear when you visit APM reports.
bugs.impact: Cannot see the session summary.
bugs.workaround: Run the Session Summary Report, and manualy set it as Default Report.
bugs.fix: Default Session Summary report now show when accessing the APM report.

bugs.title: Licensing Warning displays when CGNAT is licensed and LTM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: the CGNAT license allows the use of many features under the LTM UI tab. But in order to enable the LTM GUI tab, LTM must be provisioned. This causes a licensing warning to appear in the upper left corner of the GUI and on the command line.
bugs.conditions: -- CGNAT stand-alone license. -- LTM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Licensing Warning displays. User cannot confirm whether or not features are licensed features.
bugs.workaround: None. This is cosmetic only and has no effect on system operation.
bugs.fix: A Licensing Warning no longer displays when CGNAT is licensed and LTM is provisioned, which is correct functionality.

bugs.title: Firewall policies assigned to route domain may not sync across HA
bugs.symptoms: HA devices may report "in sync" even though the firewall policy assigned to the route domain is not being synced. The problem is sporadic.
bugs.conditions: Route domains are configured across HA peers, and the route domain has a firewall policy attached to it.
bugs.impact: Firewall policies not syncing correctly within a sync group can cause unexpected or unwanted traffic on the network.

bugs.title: Using snat/snatpool in related-rule results in crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash resulting in failover.
bugs.conditions: Using snat/snatpool command in related-rule.
bugs.impact: TMM crash resulting in failover.
bugs.workaround: Do not use snat/snatpool commands in related rule.

bugs.title: Invalid L4 packets might not match against AFM WhiteList properly
bugs.symptoms: If BIG-IP receives invalid L4 packets, they might not match against AFM whitelist properly and hence might detect an attack from a known whitelisted IP address.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM DoS configured. -- DoS "rich" whitelist configured with src IP address. -- Sweep/Flood vector configured with pkt-type "all-pkts". -- The BIG-IP system receives invalid Layer 4 pkts (i.e., IPv6 packets that don't have the correct next-header) specified
bugs.impact: The system could detect an attack, even though the packets are coming from a known whitelisted IP address. A false positive on a DoS attack could be triggered. There is no impact to the packet since if the packet is invalid it will be dropped anyway.
bugs.workaround: Instead of AFM DoS "rich" Whitelist, use the DoS AFM Address-List Whitelist to whitelist src IP addresses.

bugs.title: audit logs may show connection to hagel.mnet
bugs.symptoms: An iControl host header is improperly formatted with the name hagal.mnet The request is properly delivered to the correct host but contains a badly addressed host header that is ignored. If the authorization fails for the icontrol query then the audit log will contain this destination information which may be confusing.
bugs.conditions: Setting up device trust exercises this code path.
bugs.impact: No impact to functionality but is confusing for log interpretation.
bugs.workaround: There is not workaround
bugs.fix: When this bug is fixed then the host header is properly formatted with the destination of the iControl request.

bugs.title: Users with auditor role are unable to use tmsh list sys crypto cert
bugs.symptoms: The system returns error messages after running the following command: tmsh list sys crypto cert. Error messages appear similar to the following: -- Key management library returned bad status: -4, Invalid Parameter. -- Unexpected Error: Can't chmod key management directory: "/var/tmp/key_mgmt", error: [1] Operation not permitted".
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP user accounts configured with the auditor role. -- Running the command: tmsh list sys crypto cert.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP users with the auditor role cannot view certificates using the command: list sys crypto cert.
bugs.workaround: Use the following command: sys file ssl-cert For example, use either of the following: -- list sys file ssl-cert default.crt -- list sys file ssl-cert
bugs.fix: BIG-IP users with the auditor users can now see certificates using the following command: list sys crypto cert.

bugs.title: APM Sandbox configuration is missing if a partition was created before APM was provisioned
bugs.symptoms: Partition configuration is missing APM default Sandbox configuration objects if the partition was created before APM was provisioned. This may cause certain issues when APM Sandbox-related configuration is necessary in the new partition.
bugs.conditions: APM is not provisioned when the partition is being created, and the partition was created using tmsh create auth partition partition_name
bugs.impact: APM Sandbox related features may not work after APM is later provisioned.
bugs.workaround: Use the following command to create a partition: tmsh create sys folder /partition_name

bugs.title: The merged.state debugging file in qkview reports wrong method when input files are too volatile
bugs.symptoms: The /var/tmp/merged.state file produced by merged when it is sent SIGUSR2 including when qkview is taken can incorrectly report the merge method as slow in limited circumstances.
bugs.conditions: The input files to merged need to be in a steady state of churn (rows added or removed) so that merged cannot successfully complete a merge.
bugs.impact: It is harder to debug merged.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the churn on the input files, for example by not spawning a steady stream of processes recorded in the proc_pid_stat table.

bugs.title: Policy import, to inactive policies list, results in different policies on the sync-failover peers
bugs.symptoms: Having a standard Active/Standby setup, with a single Sync-Failover Device Group, Auto-Sync, with ASM enabled. When importing an ASM policy (named 'ddddd') into the inactive policies list, the following results in GUI screen, Security :: Application Security : Security Policies : Inactive Policies. On active device: Security Policy Name - Version ddddd - 2016-02-25 10:39:49 ddddd_2 - 2016-03-01 00:11:46 On standby device: Security Policy Name - Version ddddd - 2016-03-01 00:11:41 ddddd_2 - 2016-02-25 10:39:49 According to the 'Version' field (time stamps), the 'ddddd' on active is actually 'ddddd_2' on standby and then the other two policies are not the same. The group ends up with three different policies on the two devices.
bugs.conditions: -- Active/Standby configuration. -- ASM provisioned. -- Import security policy to the inactive policies list.
bugs.impact: Three different policies are created on the two devices.
bugs.fix: The import policy process now results in a consistent state on both devices in a device group.

bugs.title: ASM Remote logger doesn't log 64 KB request.
bugs.symptoms: A request longer than 10 KB is truncated to 10 KB in the ASM remote logger although the remote logger is configured to log up to 64 KB requests.
bugs.conditions: The remote logger is configured to max request size 64k . A request is longer than 10 KB.
bugs.impact: Incorrect request size in the log.
bugs.fix: ASM can now logs up to 64 KB requests. (Actual size depends on the total message size and the other fields in the message.)

bugs.title: WebSafe features do not support Non-UTF8 encodings.
bugs.symptoms: Encrypted ISO-8859-2 data is sent to the application server in UTF8 encoded form instead of ISO-8859-2 encoding.
bugs.conditions: Webpage using non-UTF8 encoding.
bugs.impact: Application server receives data in an unexpected encoding.
bugs.fix: Added support for ISO-8859-2 encoding

bugs.title: Loading sys config might fail after removing NICs for VE
bugs.symptoms: Loading sys config triggered by MCPD start might fail after removing NICs for VE if the given NICs have been configured as the data-plane interfaces in BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP VE. - Multi-NICs have been configured as the data-plane interfaces. - One or some of these NICs have been removed from the host side.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP VE stops working. BIG-IP VE cannot be in ready state since almost all other services depend on MCPD to be up running first.
bugs.workaround: Edit /config/bigip_base.conf to delete the net interfaces that have been removed on the host/hypervisor side.

bugs.title: SNMP sysObjectID OID reports ID of blade on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP v11.5.4, the behavior of the SNMP sysObjectID changed for VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms. On other BIG-IP 10.x and 11.x versions running on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID reports the ID of the Chassis (BIG-IPVprC2400 or BIG-IPVprC2200). In BIG-IP v11.5.4 and v12.0.0 and later running on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID reports the ID of the Blade (BIG-IPVprB2100, BIG-IPVprB2150, or BIG-IPVprB2250). In all versions of BIG-IP running on VIPRION 4xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID reports the ID of the Blade (BIG-IPPb100, BIG-IPPb100n, BIG-IPPb200, BIG-IPPb200N, BIG-IPVprB4300 or BIG-IPVprB4300N). In BIG-IP v12.0.0 and later running on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the BIG-IP design is changed such that the SNMP sysObjectID reports the ID of the Blade (BIG-IPVprB2100, BIG-IPVprB2150, or BIG-IPVprB2250), consistent with VIPRION 4xxx-series platforms. [See Solution article for ID 425331, when published.]
bugs.conditions: VIPRION C2400 and C2200 chassis VIPRION B2100, B2150 and B2250 blades BIG-IP v11.5.4 (release)
bugs.impact: SNMP queries to identify VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms return the Blade ID instead of the Chassis ID, requiring changes in how the returned sysObjectID is interpreted.
bugs.workaround: Identify a VIPRION 2xxx-series platform by the appropriate Blade ID (BIG-IPVprB2100, BIG-IPVprB2150, or BIG-IPVprB2250), instead of by the Chassis ID (BIG-IPVprC2400 or BIG-IPVprC2200).
bugs.fix: On VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID OID reports the ID of the Chassis, to match the behavior on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms with previous BIG-IP versions 10.2.x and 11.x.
bugs.behavior: On VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, the SNMP sysObjectID OID now reports the ID of the Chassis, to match the behavior on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms with previous BIG-IP versions 10.2.x and 11.x. Previously, SNMP sysObjectID reported the ID of the Blade on VIPRION 2xxx-series platforms, to match the behavior on VIPRION 4xxx-series platforms.

bugs.title: MCPd might leak memory in PEM stats queries.
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak may result in an "Out of Memory" condition causing functional issues in the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when a valid PEM stats query is issued by a UI (GUI TMSH, REST, etc.) and PEM is configured on the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: System may be unresponsive or crash due to being out of memory.
bugs.fix: Fixed the potential MCPd memory leak in PEM stats queries.

bugs.title: VE does not boot without a vga console
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Edition (VE) does not boot and no boot messages are displayed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is no video device present. This is an issue because by design VE grub and kernel configurations default to vga (tty0).
bugs.impact: VE does not boot.
bugs.workaround: Use a VGA console option when deploying the VE (via virt-admin, or the Xen configuration utility, etc.)

bugs.title: NPN configuration options are obsolete
bugs.symptoms: Next Protocol Negotiation (NPN) support is obsolete and will be removed from a future software version.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 configuration currently allows selection of NPN, ALPN or both.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 will only use ALPN, irrespective of the configuration referencing NPN.
bugs.workaround: Configure applicable profiles to use ALPN.

bugs.title: DHCP relay not forwarding server DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK message after sometime
bugs.symptoms: If routing table on DHCP server is mis-configured, so that DHCP server know how to send packets to BigIP selfIP(used by BigIP DHCP relay), but does not know how to send packets to DHCP clients, DCHP client will not receive DHCP reply for unicast request and will start to broadcast DHCP renewal. After a while, BigIP will stop to relay DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK back to DHCP clients all together.
bugs.conditions: DHCP server unicast reply back to client is not received by client, causing DHCP client to send broadcast DHCP packets(with client's IP as source IP).
bugs.impact: BigIP will stop to relay DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK back to DHCP clients
bugs.workaround: Fix the DHCP server routing table, so that DHCP server can deliver DHCP reply packet back to client successfully.
bugs.fix: DHCP relay now continues forwarding the server DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages under these conditions.

bugs.title: When a fips key is deleted, its corresponding public key is not deleted from fips card
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP does not delete the automatically-created public keys in FIPS cards when a FIPS keys is deleted
bugs.conditions: When the FIPS key is deleted, the corresponding public key is not deleted from the FIPS card.
bugs.impact: No functional impact.

bugs.title: Safari 9 and Safari 10 don't use autoconfig script from NA on OSX 10.11 and 10.12 if pac file is downloaded via tunnel
bugs.symptoms: Safari 9 and Safari 10 don't use autoconfig script from NA on OSX 10.11 and 10.12 if pac file is downloaded via tunnel
bugs.conditions: Safari 9 or 10 on El Capitan and Yosemite releases of macOS. Proxy.pac file configured on NA on BIG-IP. Proxy.pac file location is behind the corporate network
bugs.impact: Proxy.pac file is not applied when proxy.pac is behind corporate network. This may cause issues with accessing some of the internal websites.

bugs.title: DNS suffixes on user's machine may not be restored correctly in some cases
bugs.symptoms: DNS suffixes on user's may not be restored correctly if user reboots his machine without disconnecting VPN. This may result in incorrect or failed DNS resolution.
bugs.conditions: 1)DNS relay proxy components is installed on user's machine 2) User reboots the machine without disconnecting VPN first
bugs.impact: DNS suffixes are not restored correctly, which may lead to incorrect or failed DNS resolution
bugs.workaround: Disconnect VPN before rebooting machine
bugs.fix: DNS Suffixes are now restored properly.

bugs.title: incorrect crontab can cause large number of email alerts
bugs.symptoms: There is an incorrect crontab entry in /etc/cron.usbflush for /sbin/lsusb
bugs.conditions: This occurs for the usbflush entry.
bugs.impact: usbflush does not run, alert email is generated once per minute.
bugs.workaround: change /etc/cron.usbflush to use /usr/sbin/lsusb
bugs.fix: Fix /etc/cron.usbflush to use /usr/sbin/lsusb

bugs.title: The HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST iRule event can cause the TMM to crash if pipelined ingress occurs when the iRule parks
bugs.symptoms: The TMM crashes while resuming from a HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST event.
bugs.conditions: A HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST iRule event parks. Pipelined ingress occurs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Don't use parking iRule commands within the HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST event. If a parking command must be used, the following may work: Try using TCP::collect to disable ingress while a potentially parking iRule command executes. TCP::release can be used after the command completes to restore normal behavior. Another work-around is to set max-requests to 1. (Disabling pipelining.)

bugs.title: tmsh show sys hardwares show "unavailable" for hard disk manufacturer on B4400/B4450 blade
bugs.symptoms: tmsh show sys hardware show "unavailable" for hard disk manufacturer
bugs.conditions: In VIPRION B4400/B4450 blades, tmsh show sys hardware always shows "unavailable" for hard disk manufacturer.
bugs.impact: Can't get correct hard disk manufacturer information.
bugs.fix: Fixed

bugs.title: Enabling DNS resolver and proxy server pool at the same time by tmsh in OCSP Stapling Parameters (for clientSSL OCSP Stapling) might cause OCSP responder not reached
bugs.symptoms: OCSP Stapling uses either DNS resolver OR proxy server pool to connect to the OCSP responder. In GUI these two configuration options are selective but tmsh allows configuration of proxy-server-pool when use_proxy_server is set to false, and vice-versa.
bugs.conditions: DNS resolver and use_proxy_server are configured at the same time, but only one of these configurations is set to true.
bugs.impact: In following situation: -use_proxy_server: Enabled but incorrectly configured or external proxy server not working or down. -DNS resolver: Enabled and correctly configured. OCSP stapling will not work since device will try to connect to OCSP responder by using proxy regardless DNS resolver configuration. Since this 'double' configuration (DNS+use_proxy_server) only can be done by tmsh, you cannot see in GUI that you actually have both configurations at the same time.
bugs.workaround: Disable use_proxy_server configuration using tmsh, then device will use DNS resolver to reach OCSP responder.

bugs.title: Malware Guid is not reset at the end of the session
bugs.symptoms: The "Malware Guid" has an option to last for "session" only. This option does not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: "Malware Guid" expiration set to "session".
bugs.impact: User id does not change between sessions
bugs.fix: Cookie now expires at end of session

bugs.title: Policy Import (REST, inline XML import) in HA pair (CMI) fails on the peer device, remaining with a stub (default) policy.
bugs.symptoms: These errors are visible in asm log: -------------------- Mar 3 20:18:33 Bip_102 crit g_server.pl[29381]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl,F5::ImportExportPolicy::Base::fatal_error): no such file '/ts/var/sync/admin~t6jsI8OQtyjKrbs2Djpjng' Mar 3 20:18:33 Bip_102 info perl[29340]: 01310053:6: ASMConfig change: Import Policy Task Import Policy Task (1457029113.860000) [update]: Status was set to FAILURE. End Time was set to 1457029114. Message was set to Exported policy file not found!.. { audit: username = admin, client IP = 172.18.185.226 } -------------------- The policy created on the peer device is a stub - default policy.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned HA pair (CMI) Policy Import (REST, inline XML import)
bugs.impact: Policy Import (REST, inline XML import) in HA pair (CMI) fails on the peer device, remaining with a stub (default) policy on the peer device.
bugs.fix: We have fixed the import/export mechanism on HA pair (CMI).

bugs.title: Statistics data aggregation process is not optimized
bugs.symptoms: CPU spikes may occur every 5 minutes
bugs.conditions: Occurs all the time
bugs.impact: High CPU usage may be observed every 5 minutes
bugs.workaround: For versions based on 11.5.4 and 11.6.0 take the following steps: 1. Edit the entry 'AggregationMode' under the /etc/avr/monpd/monpd.cfg file and set it to be 'low' instead of 'medium' or 'high'. 2.Restart Monpd afterwards. For 12.0.0 and on: tmsh modify sys db avr.stats.aggregation value low
bugs.fix: The aggregation process of statistics in DB which is done using monpd should be optimized, and skip redundant updates of tables.

bugs.title: Adding an option for negative validation of occurence of a string in the header
bugs.symptoms: ASM doesn't have the option to filter a Login attempt according to a negative validation of occurrence of a header, which occurs in logins that issue a redirect.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for all Login Attempts if the login results in redirect
bugs.impact: It is not possible to filter redirect login pages
bugs.fix: ASM now has the ability to detect successful and failed logins when the result of login is a redirect.

bugs.title: Missing reference to customization-group from connectivity profile if created via portal access wizard
bugs.symptoms: An extra customization group is created for connectivity profile when the profile is created via portal access wizard and the configuration is reloaded.
bugs.conditions: Use portal access wizard to create configure objects.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact since customization is not actually used for connectivity group.
bugs.workaround: Create configure object manually rather than via wizard.
bugs.fix: There will be a reference to customization group from connectivity profile when the profile is created by wizard.

bugs.title: Support for hardware accelerated bulk crypto SHA256 missing
bugs.symptoms: Requests for bulk crypto SHA256 will be performed in software, not by the accelerator.
bugs.conditions: Any bulk crypto operation that uses SHA256 on the BIG-IP 1600, 3600, 5000, 6900, 7000, 8900, 10000, 11000, 11050, and 12000 platforms, and on VIPRION B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: The request will be completed in software which may result in increased CPU load.
bugs.fix: Requests for bulk crypto operations using SHA256 will be assigned to a hardware accelerator, and no longer serviced in software.

bugs.title: Priority group value of the AAA server pool members changed on change of monitor
bugs.symptoms: If you change or add a monitor to an AAA server priority group, the pool member priority may be changed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when changing the monitor or adding a new pool member.
bugs.impact: Priority order of pool members are changed.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to update the priority, to reset the value
bugs.fix: The priority order of pool members are preserved when a monitor is changed or pool members are added.

bugs.title: bop "network 0.0.0.0/0 route-map Default" configuration is lost after after restart/reboot
bugs.symptoms: network 0.0.0.0/0 route-map Default is missing in bgp after a restart/reboot
bugs.conditions: "network 0.0.0.0/0 route-map Default" is configured in bgp
bugs.impact: The bgp doesn't have the same configuration after a restart/reboot. persistence of bgp protocol is not maintained leading to unexpected behavior of bgp
bugs.fix: the persistence of "network 0.0.0.0/0 route-map Default" in bgp is maintained after a restart/reboot

bugs.title: ICAP: Client RST when HTTP::respond in HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE after ICAP REQMOD returned HTTP response
bugs.symptoms: Connection aborted with RST "ADAPT unexpected state transition (old_state 22 event 7)"
bugs.conditions: An HTTP virtual has a request-adapt profile. The ICAP server returns an HTTP response for REQMOD. An iRule executes HTTP::respond in the HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE event.
bugs.impact: HTTP::respond cannot be used to modify an HTTP response returned by an ICAP server that is modifying an HTTP request.
bugs.fix: HTTP::respond works as expected even on an HTTP response returned by an ICAP server after request adaption.

bugs.title: SSL Forward Proxy Forged Certificate Signature Algorithm
bugs.symptoms: In SSL Forward Proxy, the signature algorithm used by the CA certificate configured on the client SSL profile can change the signature algorithm used by the server certificate. For example, if the server certificate uses SHA1 but the CA certificate configured in client SSL profile uses SHA256, the forged certificate will use SHA256. If the server certificate uses SHA256 but the CA certificate configured in client SSL uses SHA1, the forged certificate will use SHA1. Both scenarios are a problem for a customer.
bugs.conditions: when the signature algorithm of the CA certificate configured in client SSL profile differs from the signature algorithm of the server certificate.
bugs.impact: The signature algorithm of forged certificate may differ from the signature algorithm of the server certificate.
bugs.workaround: Configure the CA certificate in client SSL profile so that the signature algorithm matches that in server certificate.

bugs.title: GUI strips out 0.0.0.0 masks from the SNMP Client Allow Lists.
bugs.symptoms: The GUI strips out 0.0.0.0 masks from the SNMP Client Allow List.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to specific SNMP Client Allow List containing 0.0.0.0 masks.
bugs.impact: The GUI strips the 0.0.0.0 masks.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to modify the SNMP Access if using 0.0.0.0 net masks.
bugs.fix: GUI no longer strips out 0.0.0.0 masks from the SNMP Client Allow Lists.

bugs.title: tmm cores when switching to IPv6 virtual server while connected to IPv4 virtual server with Edge Client.
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores when switching to IPv6 virtual server while connected to IPv4 virtual server with Edge Client.
bugs.conditions: NA resource with IPv4&IPv6 is used (SNAT pool in NA resource is set to None). User is connected to IPv4 Virtual server. While connected user clicks on 'Change server' and chooses an IPv6 virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: APM Webtop displays "Applications and Links" number is off by 1
bugs.symptoms: When "Applications and Links" section is collapsed on APM Webtop, the total number of items shown next to section name is off by 1.
bugs.conditions: "Applications and Links" section on APM Webtop is collapsed.
bugs.impact: "Applications and Links" number is off by 1
bugs.fix: Proper "Applications and Links" number is now shown on APM Webtop.

bugs.title: TCP Fast Open connection timeout during handshake does not decrement pre_established_connections
bugs.symptoms: If a TCP connection is started and contains a valid Fast Open cookie, then times out during the three-way handshake, the failure is not accounted for properly. If this occurs more than a threshold number of times, BIG-IP will stop performing TCP Fast Open.
bugs.conditions: A TCP connection using TCP Fast Open with a valid Fast Open cookie times out during the three-way handshake.
bugs.impact: Each connection that times out in this fashion decreases the number of valid pre-established connections that the BIG-IP can support. If the number of connections timed out in this fashion rises above a threshold, BIG-IP will act as if TCP Fast Open is disabled. This threshold cannot be changed.
bugs.fix: Decrement the pre-established connections counter when a TCP Fast Open connection times out during the initial handshake.

bugs.title: When mcpd is restarted on a blade, cluster members may be temporarily marked as failed
bugs.symptoms: When mcpd is restarted on a blade, the clusterd process on that blade may become blocked for some time. This may result in cluster member heartbeat timeouts, which are seen in the /var/log/ltm log file with messages that include: "Slot 1 suffered heartbeat timeout ..." This causes cluster members to be marked failed. The condition resolves itself within one minute, and the cluster fully recovers on its own.
bugs.conditions: Mcpd is restarted on a blade.
bugs.impact: Though all blades recover on their own, the cluster members being marked fail may result in a failover.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue. It is recommended to avoid restarting mcpd on any blade belonging to the active unit of an HA group. The issue resolves itself within about a minute, and all cluster members will be marked as up again.
bugs.fix: The clusterd daemon has been fixed to no longer become blocked when mcpd is restarted. This prevents the cluster member heartbeat timeouts from occurring, and thus no cluster members will be marked failed.

bugs.title: Whitelisted IPs of non-default DoS profile are ignored
bugs.symptoms: Only IP addresses included in the default DoS profile whitelist are treated as whitelisted. Transactions associated with a non-default DoS profile are put through DoS checks, even when their IP addresses are included in the non-default DoS profile's whitelist.
bugs.conditions: When configuring a DoS profile that is not used as the default profile, but rather is dynamically attached to certain transactions (via iRule or CPM), the IP addresses included in this DoS profile's whitelist are ignored and the IP addresses included in the default DoS profile's whitelist are implemented as whitelisted.
bugs.impact: IP addresses configured to be blocked or allowed may be processed differently than expected.
bugs.fix: When a transaction is dynamically attached to a non-default DoS profile, the IP addresses defined in the selected profile's whitelist are correctly allowed or blocked, as expected.

bugs.title: Maximum request body size is limited to 25 MB
bugs.symptoms: When a POST request with body size exceeds 25 MB is sent to APM virtual server, the request fails.
bugs.conditions: POST request body size exceeded 25 MB.
bugs.impact: The POST request fails. The maximum request body size is limited to 25 MB
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.behavior: Request body size is increased.

bugs.title: Config sync error when a key with passphrase is converted into FIPS.
bugs.symptoms: When a key with passphrase is converted to a FIPS key (that is, imported into the FIPS card) and a config sync is done, sync fails with an error saying that passphrase is specified but the key is not passphrase protected.
bugs.conditions: Converting a private key with a passphrase to FIPS key and then performing a config-sync.
bugs.impact: Config sync will fail.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that you only import FIPS keys that are not encrypted with a passphrase. For more information, see K15720: Certain tasks related to the management of SSL certificates do not support encrypted private keys (11.x) at https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K15720

bugs.title: Unable to update the default http-explicit profile using the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Trying to update default Local Traffic :: Profiles : Services : HTTP :: http-explicit profile, the system posts the following error: 'Some fields below contain errors. Correct them before continuing.' Under the 'Explicit Proxy' section for 'DNS Resolver' option, the system posts the following error: '010717e8:3: Invalid 'dns-resolver' value for profile /Common/http-explicit. The dns-resolver does not exist.'
bugs.conditions: Updating default http-explicit profile using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Error messages. Unable to update the default http-explicit profile using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to update the default http-explicit profile.
bugs.fix: You can now update the default http-explicit profile without error using the GUI.

bugs.title: TMM core due to wrong assert
bugs.symptoms: Under stress traffic tmm can core with the following backtrace: frame 3: in *__GI___assert_fail frame 4 will look like this: .... avr_alloc_segmempool_with_id .. mempool.c:278
bugs.conditions: AVR provision and collecting statistic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue that intermittently caused the TMM to core.

bugs.title: VIPRION B4400N blades might fail to go Active under rare conditions.
bugs.symptoms: Over extended periods of booting and rebooting a VIPRION system containing B4400N blades, a switch port connected to the HSB might fail to initialize properly. In some cases, logs indicate an occurrence of the problem in the following form: hgm_fcs_errs[higig mac #] exceeds 1000.
bugs.conditions: This happens under very rare conditions on B4400N blades; for example, after approximately 8-12 hours of continuous rebooting.
bugs.impact: When the problem is manifest, the HSB receives FCS errors at a high-frequency and does not receive any valid traffic from the port switch. The B4400N blade might be unable to go active and join the cluster.
bugs.workaround: To recover, reboot the system once.

bugs.title: Access keys missing from SessionDB after multi-blade reboot.
bugs.symptoms: Reboot a 4-blade vCMP guest. Now, only the master key for catalog remained. All subkeys are missing.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently during a reboot in a multi-blade vCMP guest configured with APM.
bugs.impact: Some Access subkeys may be missing after the reboot.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the primary blade.

bugs.title: GUI does not display the field for entering port number for pool members in 'use pool' mode for CRLDP AAA server configuration screen
bugs.symptoms: The field for entering the port number is not shown initially at the time of creation when you select the "use pool" option. Hoever, if you switch to direct mode and then comes back to use pool, you will be able to enter port
bugs.conditions: If you cannot enter the port for the pool member and save the AAA CRLDP server, the port number for that pool member is saved as 0 (*) any port.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent UI behavior
bugs.workaround: Switch to direct mode and then switch back to use pool mode. This will continue to display the port number field.

bugs.title: Traffic can be directed to a less specific virtual during virtual modification
bugs.symptoms: Traffic can be directed to an less specific virtual during virtual modification. It could also be dropped if there is no less specific virtual server.
bugs.conditions: net self external-ipv4 { address 10.124.0.19/16 traffic-group traffic-group-local-only vlan external } net self internal-ipv4 { address 10.125.0.19/16 traffic-group traffic-group-local-only vlan internal } ltm pool redirect-echo { members { 10.125.0.17:7 } } ltm virtual fw { description "less-specific virtual" destination 10.125.0.0:any ip-forward mask 255.255.255.0 profiles { fastL4 } translate-address disabled translate-port disabled vlans-disabled } ltm virtual redirect-echo { description "enable/disable this one" destination 10.125.0.20:echo ip-protocol udp mask 255.255.255.255 pool redirect-echo profiles { udp } vlans { external } vlans-enabled }
bugs.impact: Traffic can be directed to less specific virtual server
bugs.workaround: No known workaround at this time other than applying configuration changes in a manner that avoids doing them on a unit that is handling the traffic. Applying changes on the standby and then failing over and syncing or utilizing a maintenance window would be common schemes to achieve a separation between production traffic and configuration changes.
bugs.fix: No fix available at this time.

bugs.title: Potential memory corruption in MCPd
bugs.symptoms: Memory in mcpd could get corrupted. The effect of this is unpredictable.
bugs.conditions: Varies. One way (but not the only way) this could be seen is by cancelling a chunked stats query (e.g. hitting ctrl-c during "show sys connection").
bugs.impact: Varies. Sometimes nothing will happen; other times MCP could start acting unpredictably. In one case it closed its connection to TMM, which caused all TMMs to restart.
bugs.fix: Identified and fixed areas of potential memory corruption in MCP.

bugs.title: BigIP may generate ARPs after transition to standby
bugs.symptoms: tmm generates unexpected ARPs after entering standby
bugs.conditions: HA pair with a vlangroup with bridge-in-standby disabled ARP is received just before transition to standby
bugs.impact: Unexpected ARP requests that may result in packet loops
bugs.fix: ARPs will no longer be proxied on vlangroups with bridge-in-standby disabled after entering standby.

bugs.title: Error when loading Upgrade UCS
bugs.symptoms: When loading an older version UCS file while ASM is live an error may occur when processing the new configuration. You will see the following error in the asm log: Mar 9 07:16:06 dut30 err perl[22696]: 01310011:3: ASM configuration error: event code T1499 Failed to update configuration table CONFIG_TYPE_DYNAMIC_TABLES
bugs.conditions: Loading an older version UCS on a live system.
bugs.impact: Enforcement of Allowed Methods may be incorrect
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM
bugs.fix: Configuration is correctly processed when loading a UCS file for upgrade on a live device.

bugs.title: DBD::mysql::db do failed: Duplicate entry '/Common/xxx' for key 'name'
bugs.symptoms: Policy Import via iControl REST in an HA pair occasionally fails on the Standby device with - DBD::mysql::db do failed: Duplicate entry '/Common/xxx' for key 'name'
bugs.conditions: Active/Standby pair configured ASM provisioned Import a security policy, via iControl REST
bugs.impact: Policy import fails
bugs.fix: We have fixed the import policy via iControl REST so that it does not generate the database error

bugs.title: Stats file descriptors kept open in spawned child processes
bugs.symptoms: No known user visible impact.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in all multi-blade platforms where clusterd is running.
bugs.impact: No known user visible impact.
bugs.fix: Stats file descriptors are opened so that they are closed when a child process is spawned.

bugs.title: bd_agent and bd are suddenly restarted, while there is no traffic nor configuration being processed
bugs.symptoms: bd_agent and bd are suddenly restarted, while there is no traffic nor configuration being processed This log line appears in '/var/log/ts/nwd.log' ------------ asm_start|INFO|Feb 26 01:34:35.922|19639|F5::NwdUtils::Nwd::verify,,bd_agent: not enough threads, exceeded TimesThreadsFail (2)!! ------------
bugs.conditions: The conditions which trigger this are unknown.
bugs.impact: bd_agent and bd are suddenly restarted, while there is no traffic no configuration being processed
bugs.workaround: unknown

bugs.title: DTLS Networks Access may not work with some hardware platforms with Nitrox hardware acceleration
bugs.symptoms: Network Access always fallbacks to TLS connection even if DTLS is configured when connecting to some hardware platforms.
bugs.conditions: Network Access is configured to use DTLS Hardware BIG-IP with DTLS Nitrox acceleration is used
bugs.impact: Network Access connection always fallbacks to TLS connection
bugs.fix: Previously, Network Access always fell back to a TLS connection even if DTLS was configured when connecting to some hardware platforms. Network Access no longer falls back to TLS.

bugs.title: FIPS (ngfips) card-sync fails due to its lacking ability to properly handle "\" in the SO (security officer) password.
bugs.symptoms: When setting up SO (security officer) password using "tmsh run util fips-util -f init", it accepts the password containing "\" without showing problems. However, card-sync will fail since it can't properly log on the fips with the password.
bugs.impact: A password containing '\' will fail the card-sync process in FIPS HA setup.
bugs.workaround: Reset the password using command "tmsh run util fips-util -f init" and avoid the special character '\'.
bugs.conditions: FIPS card with a security officer that contains "\"
bugs.fix: The fix makes fips (ngfips) able to properly handle "\" in the SO (security officer) password so that card-sync won't fail due to it.

bugs.title: Multidomain SSO Access policy in progress with multiple tabs, landing URL set to the tab in which policy is completed.
bugs.symptoms: When URLs from multiple browser tabs start an access policy, the session is created with the landing URL from the first tab that started the session, not with URL the second tab that continued and finished establishing the access session. For example, an end user opens browser and sends GET to /first_url resource. Access initiates session, and renders logon page. Then end user opens another tab, and sends GET to /second_url resource. Access returns an error message "Access policy evaluation is already in progress for your current session." with a link to start new session. If the end user selects the "click here", the new session will start with /first_url, and not with /second_url as would be expected.
bugs.conditions: Using Multidomain SSO, and accessing two different resources before the access policy has been created. This causes the access policy to run from two different landing URLs
bugs.impact: This may cause BIG-IP as SAML SP unable to establish a session with IdP. In the case of LTM and APM, the user is always redirected to the URL from first tab after policy execution finishes.

bugs.title: Monitors may create invalid configuration files
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions monitors created or edited in the GUI may save an invalid configuration to disk, causing errors when the configuration is reloaded.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to create/edit monitors.
bugs.impact: tmsh load sys config will fail.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create or edit monitors. If your configuration file already has an offending backlash, please manually remove the backlash.

bugs.title: HSL::send may fail to resume after log server pool member goes down/up
bugs.symptoms: High speed logging (HSL): asymmetric bandwidth loss might result in no bandwidth tracking.
bugs.conditions: This will occur if the log server pool only has a single member in it, and that member goes down and up while HSL::send is occurring during traffic processing.
bugs.impact: For a period of time after the logging node comes back up, HSL::send events will not be sent to the log server. Sometimes it never recovers and tmm needs to be restarted.
bugs.workaround: If possible, configure log server pools with multiple members to avoid this condition.

bugs.title: Edge Client creates duplicate server list if cp has no alias
bugs.symptoms: If you don't specify an alias for a cp on the virtual server, a duplicate virtual server will appear in the server selection list
bugs.conditions: This occurs when copying virtual servers and an alias is not specified.
bugs.impact: Duplicate entry will appear in the server selection list
bugs.workaround: Supply an alias in the server list on the configuration page
bugs.fix: Configured server will automatically apply the host name as the alias and will not be duplicated in the server list

bugs.title: tmrouted may not re-announce routes after a specific succession of failover states
bugs.symptoms: tmrouted does not re-announce RHI routes in a specific transition of failover states within a HA pair using dynamic routing and HA pair.
bugs.conditions: - Active/Standby HA pair set up - Both units configured with a dynamic routing protocol and Route Health Injection enabled on one or more Virtual-Addresses. - Active unit has the following succession of failover states: Active->Offline->Online->Standby->Active
bugs.impact: Tmrouted may not announce the Virtual addresses when coming back to Active state after the mention succession.
bugs.workaround: A failover to Standby and back to Active works around the issue. Restarting tmrouted is also an alternative option.
bugs.fix: tmrouted now re-announces RHI routes in a specific transition of failover states within a HA pair using dynamic routing and HA pair.

bugs.title: Secondary MCPD exits for APM Sandbox warning improperly treated as configuration error
bugs.symptoms: Secondary blade MCPD exits if APM Sandbox intends to log a warning message when it fails to remove the corresponding sandbox directory /var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/<partition_name>_d while the user is removing the partition. There are multiple cases that can potentially log such kind of Sandbox warning message and cause an mcpd crash and/or tmm crash. APM can log the warning if it encounters a directory which is not empty, or if the directory does not exist. You will see this error signature in /var/log/ltm: Mar 11 11:36:49 slot2/viprion-3 warning mcpd[6022]: 010717ac:4: Configuration Warning: Cannot remove directory with symlink to sandbox for partition (p1). Error: Directory not empty. If you have access to bash shell, try to run command: rmdir /var/sam/www/webtop/sandbox/files_d/p1_d/
bugs.conditions: The sandbox directory corresponding to the partition that you are deleting cannot be removed due to any reason such as Not Existing, Not Empty, etc. on the secondary blade. This can occur on the secondary blades if you create a partition before provisioning APM, then delete the partition on the primary blade, and auto-sync is enabled in the device group.
bugs.impact: Secondary MCPD exits and blade restarts. Tmm can core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed such that Secondary MCP will not exit but only log the warning message as the partition is successfully deleted.

bugs.title: User-defined signature set cannot be created/updated with Signature Type = "All"
bugs.symptoms: When creating a User-Defined Signature Set the Signature Type cannot be set to "All". After saving the setting, it resets back to Request.
bugs.conditions: Creating a new signature set with Signature Type set to "All" (the dropdown defaults to "Request" when opening the create page).
bugs.impact: A Custom Signature Set cannot be created for with Request and Response Signatures
bugs.workaround: No workaround, but can be mitigated by creating two signature sets, or using manual sets.
bugs.fix: Signature Type can now successfully be set to "All" Signatures

bugs.title: TMM may core when LSN translation is enabled
bugs.symptoms: tmm core
bugs.conditions: Virtual uses LSN translation with a destination matching a pool-based route
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Virtual with LSN translation no longer leads tmm coring when destination matches a pool-based route.

bugs.title: HTTP starts dropping traffic for a half-closed connection when in passthrough mode
bugs.symptoms: HTTP starts dropping traffic for a half-closed connection when in passthrough mode.
bugs.conditions: HTTP is in passthrough mode. Traffic is flowing for a half-closed connection.
bugs.impact: Incomplete data transfer to end-point, when the connection is half-closed and HTTP is in passthrough mode.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] Web-applications can't set cookies with expiration date after 07 Feb 2106
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access silently discards cookies with expiration time after 07 Feb 2106
bugs.impact: Application is not able to set cookies. This could make it impossible to login or break other functionality of application when accessing it through Portal Access
bugs.workaround: when HTTP_RESPONSE { # Cookies from backend application may have expiration time after 07 Feb 2106. # This overflows 32-bit variable with timestamp ("Year 2038 problem"), therefore # such cookies are treated as expired and Portal Access code discards them. # The solution is to limit internal expiration time with some reasonable value: one month. foreach {cname} {affected_cookie_name} { if { [HTTP::cookie exists $cname]} { # log local0. "$cname=[HTTP::cookie $cname];expires=[HTTP::cookie expires $cname]" HTTP::cookie expires $cname 2592000 relative } } }
bugs.fix: Portal Access now correctly handles cookies from backend application with expiration date after 07 Feb 2106

bugs.title: Updated the list of Common Criteria ciphersuites
bugs.symptoms: This is a continuous maintenance of the default set per certification requirements
bugs.conditions: These changes are only in effect when ccmode script is executed.
bugs.impact: Current set of ciphersuites is the following, subject to change in future releases: AES{128,256}-{SHA,SHA256} ECDHE-RSA-AES128-CBC-{SHA,SHA256} ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-{SHA,SHA384} ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-{SHA256,SHA384} ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-{SHA,SHA256} ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-{SHA,SHA384 } ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-{SHA256,SHA384}

bugs.title: HSM logging error
bugs.symptoms: In some cases HSM logging does not function as designed.
bugs.conditions: Installing SafeNet HSM to BIG-IP chassis.
bugs.impact: Inaccurate HSM logs
bugs.fix: Improve HSM logging

bugs.title: Using OneConnect with forwarded flows might cause resets
bugs.symptoms: Using OneConnect with forwarded flows might cause resets. The first connection attempt from the client works properly and sets up the OneConnect flow pool on one tmm, and a forwarding flow on another tmm. Then, when the client attempts a second connection, the system tries to reuse the forwarding flow, which returns failure and resets the connection. The system might report a reset cause such as 'Unable to obtain local port' or 'Out of ports', or in some versions, there might not be a specific reset cause reported.
bugs.conditions: Using OneConnect and forwarding flows. The system uses forwarding flows when source-port preserve-strict is configured, when a virtual server is configured for 'cmp-enabled no', and in certain other circumstances. For example, this issue can be seen on 2000- and 4000-series platforms, when 'source-port preserve strict' is used with OneConnect.
bugs.impact: Client connections are reset.
bugs.workaround: Do not use preserve-strict and OneConnect together.

bugs.title: DNS Relay proxy component of edge client on windows consumes lot of CPU cycles
