bugs.symptoms: In certain conditions, DNS relay proxy component of edge clients goes in a state where it takes most of the CPU cycles and starts filling up the log file very quickly with messages of 'Unknown event signaled'
bugs.conditions: DNS Relay proxy is installed on user's machine
bugs.impact: User's machine will become very slow and appear to be unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Stop DNS Relay proxy service from service control manager.
bugs.fix: Fixed DNS relay proxy so it does not go in a state where it starts consuming huge CPU cycles.

bugs.title: AVR widgets are not synchronized in a HA configuration
bugs.symptoms: AVR widgets are not being synced between devices in a Sync-Failover Device Group.
bugs.conditions: Using a Sync-Failover Device Group and creating AVR widget.
bugs.impact: GUI widgets will not be available on all devices.
bugs.fix: MCP object for AVR-widgets is now set to be synced between devices.

bugs.title: Information missing from ASM event logs after a switchboot and switchboot back
bugs.symptoms: Information missing from ASM event logs after a switchboot and switchboot back
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned event logs available with violation details install/upgrade to another volume and switchboot to it wait for ASM to fully come up switchboot back event logs are still available but violation details are gone
bugs.impact: Information missing from ASM event logs after a switchboot and switchboot back

bugs.title: WEBSSO::select may crash tmm.
bugs.symptoms: The WEBSSO::select iRule command can cause TMM to crash if no arguments are passed in.
bugs.conditions: This occurs the command is used with no arguments.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: See the following DevCentral page related to WEBSSO::select - https://devcentral.f5.com/wiki/irules.websso__select.ashx

bugs.title: PCCD cored when running 'bigstart restart pccd' command in v11.6.1
bugs.symptoms: PCCD cores when running 'bigstart restart pccd' command in v11.6.1. The issue is intermittent.
bugs.conditions: Issue'bigstart restart pccd' command in v11.6.1.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. After pccd generates the core file it restarts and compiles the firewall rules successfully.

bugs.title: When going from active to offline, tmm might send a GARP for a floating address.
bugs.symptoms: When moving from active to offline, tmm might send one final GARP for a floating address from the device that is moving offline.
bugs.conditions: Using high availability, and switching a device from active to offline.
bugs.impact: The GARP from the offline device can arrive on upstream devices after the GARP from the newly active device, which might poison the address cache of the upstream device. The result is that failover takes longer, since the upstream devices must rediscover the active device.
bugs.workaround: Use MAC masquerading along with the floating address; the system sends a GARP for the MAC masqueraded address, which prevents the issue.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer sends a final GARP for a floating address immediately before going offline.

bugs.title: SNMP query shows stats for deleted access profiles
bugs.symptoms: After an access profile is deleted, running SNMP query will still return the stats for the delete access profile.
bugs.conditions: Deleting an existing access profile.
bugs.impact: You will continue to see those deleted access profile's SNMP stats.
bugs.workaround: Restarting apd/apmd will clear out the stats for the deleted access profiles.

bugs.title: Edge Client may not register DLLs correctly
bugs.symptoms: After an end-user confirms that they want to install InstallerControll.cab, the browser gets stuck in 'Checking client'.
bugs.conditions: Client is using Internet Explorer
bugs.impact: Clients are unable to install the Edge client components
bugs.fix: Edge client components are now getting properly registered.

bugs.title: CTU does not show second Class ID for InstallerControll.dll
bugs.symptoms: Client troubleshooting utility does not display the registered class id of Installer control.dll.
bugs.conditions: Client troubleshooting utility is used to display all installed edge client components.
bugs.impact: No impact to end user or administrator. Impacts F5 support.
bugs.fix: CTU now shows the class id of installer control.dll.

bugs.title: Client side integrity defense or proactive may break application
bugs.symptoms: A blank page is shown when client side integrity/proactive is turned on.
bugs.conditions: 1. Client side integrity/proactive is turned on 2. IE 11 in compatibility mode - version 8 or lower. IE6 and 7 work.
bugs.impact: Application is broken - blank page is shown

bugs.title: /var/log partition is full, sadf may crash
bugs.symptoms: the system activity report utility sadf may crash when /var/log partition is full
bugs.conditions: /var/log partition is full
bugs.impact: A core will be generated, but system activity report utility will continue to function.
bugs.fix: Update to latest version of software to address core

bugs.title: Configuring alternate admin user fails on multi-blade VIPRION chassis if default admin on primary is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: Configuring alternate admin user fails on multi-blade VIPRION chassis and will prevent newly added blades from being available to process traffic. If default admin on primary is disabled and you are on a chassis with at least two blades. After disabling the default admin on the primary and configuring an alternate, mcpd on secondary blades goes into a restart loop, and posts error messages similar to the following in /var/log/ltm: warning mcpd[26012]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : WARNING! Role no-access will lockout the user admin-primary2. warning mcpd[26012]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : WARNING! Role no-access will lockout the user admin-secondary1. warning mcpd[26012]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : WARNING! Role no-access will lockout the user admin-secondary2. err mcpd[26012]: 010718e7:3: The requested primary admin user (admin-primary1) must have a password set. err mcpd[26012]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 010718e7:3: The requested primary admin user (admin-primary1) must have a password set.... failed validation with error 17242343. In this example, admin-primary1 is the default admin user set in the GUI under System :: Platform :: Admin Account, admin-primary2, admin-secondary1 and admin-secondary2 are other admin users on the device, but they are not configured as the default admin user.
bugs.conditions: Chassis with multiple blades; alternate primary admin is set on the primary blade.
bugs.impact: mcpd in a restart loop on secondaries.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround that will allow you to use a different primary admin user on BIG-IP software versions affected by this issue. To stop secondary blades from restarting in a loop, issue the following commands on your primary blade, which should be stable at this time: # tmsh modify sys db systemauth.primaryadminuser value admin # tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: /etc/logrotate.d/sysstat's sadf fails to read /var/log/sa6 or fails to write to /var/log/sa6, disk space is not reclaimed.
bugs.symptoms: /etc/logrotate.d/sysstat fails to read /var/log/sa6 or fails to write to /var/log/sa6,, diskspace in /var/log/sa6 is not rotated and disk space reclaimed.
bugs.conditions: /var/log/sa6 becomes corrupt or disk space becomes full in /var/log/sa6
bugs.impact: Disk space is not reclaimed in /var/log/sa6
bugs.workaround: edit /etc/logrotate.d/sysstat Add "exit 0" after sadf line
bugs.fix: When /etc/logrotate.d/sysstat's sadf fails, exit cleanly so logrotate reclaims disk space

bugs.title: Sometimes launching RemoteApps from APM webtop fails after logout/login
bugs.symptoms: Due to the RemoteApp session termination logic employed by Microsoft and described in https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/rds/2007/09/27/terminal-services-remoteapp-session-termination-logic/ , it may happen that, if user logs out and then logs back in to the APM webtop, the subsequent attempts to launch RemoteApps would fail. This happens because of a bug in RDP client 8.1 that attempts to utilize the old authentication token although a new one is provided in the .rdp file.
bugs.conditions: User logs in to APM webtop, launches some RemoteApp, closes its window, logs out, logs in again and attempts to launch the same app or another app hosted at the same backend.
bugs.impact: Apps are not launched without any further notification.
bugs.fix: The fix has been implemented to make RDP client fail immediately on an attempt to use a wrong (expired) auth token. With this fix, it may only happen once to a user that RemoteApp launch would fail and an error will be shown immediately. The subsequent launches will succeed.

bugs.title: The GeoIP update script geoip_update_data cannot be used to install City2 GeoIP data
bugs.symptoms: The geoip_update_data script will not install a City2 GeoIP data.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to install the City2 GeoIP data.
bugs.impact: The City2 GeoIP data must be installed manually.
bugs.workaround: The City2 GeoIP data can be installed manually by extracting the contents of the RPM and updating the associated files. The commands are: rpm -U <full path to the City2 GeoIP RPM file> rm /shared/GeoIP/F5GeoIP.dat ln -s /shared/GeoIP/F5GeoIPCity2.dat /shared/GeoIP/F5GeoIP.dat rm /shared/GeoIP/v2/F5GeoIP.dat
bugs.fix: The geoip_update_data script was updated to support installing City2 GeoIP data.

bugs.title: Creating and immediately deleting an Access policy can cause APMD to crash
bugs.symptoms: If an Access Policy is created and deleted within a period of a few seconds, APMD can crash.
bugs.conditions: The new Access Policy must be deleted before APMD has finished creating the Access Policy.
bugs.impact: APMD restarts

bugs.title: LDAP Query agent failed to resolve nested group membership
bugs.symptoms: Not all of the nested group membership are resolved for a user
bugs.conditions: Several conditions need to be met: 1. LDAP Query agent is configured to connect to GC (Global Catalog) in AD environment; AND 2. There are sub domains in the AD environment; AND 3. A user who is a member of a group from one of the sub domains login in.
bugs.impact: User authentication might fail or not getting all the assigned resources due to missing nested group membership.
bugs.fix: after fix, LDAP agent retrieve group from server when talking to Global Catalog

bugs.title: HTTP monitor NTLM authentication requires domain to be uppercase
bugs.symptoms: NTLMv2 authentication support in the bigd monitor only works reliably with Microsoft servers if the (NetBIOS) domain part of the ("Down-Level Logon Name" format, https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa380525(v=vs.85).aspx#down_level_logon_name) username is either omitted or entered in uppercase (DOMAIN\user). However, if it entered in lowercase (domain\user), authentication fails.
bugs.conditions: Monitor using NTLM authentication with domain not uppercase.
bugs.impact: HTTP monitor marks member down.
bugs.workaround: Change domain in monitor user string to uppercase.

bugs.title: Configuration containing LTM nodes with IPv6 link-local addresses fail to load.
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue a configuration containing LTM nodes with IPv6 link-local addresses may fail to load.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to load a configuration containing a LTM node with a IPv6 link-local address.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Use IPv6 global addresses instead.
bugs.fix: Bigip now loads correctly a configuration containing a LTM node with a IPv6 linbk-local address.

bugs.title: Hostagentd might leak memory on vCMP hosts.
bugs.symptoms: hostagentd resident memory keeps leaking over time. Unexplained system instability. Health monitors might work intermittently.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when host uptime is two months or longer.
bugs.impact: hostagentd consumes more than 400 MB of resident memory. In some cases, the process consumes more than 1 GB. This might cause system instability and intensive usage of vCMP host swap memory.
bugs.workaround: Restart hostagentd on vCMP host.
bugs.fix: Many stability and other improvements have been made to hostagentd daemon and associated functionality, so that memory leaks on vCMP hosts no longer occur.

bugs.title: VIPRION 2200 platform might not pass traffic properly after FPGA firmware switch.
bugs.symptoms: After a FPGA firmware switch on VIPRION 2200 platforms without a system reboot, some internal higig ports might not operate properly.
bugs.conditions: Using tmsh or GUI to switch FPGA firmware on VIPRION 2200 platforms.
bugs.impact: This might result in the system not handling traffic properly.
bugs.workaround: After any FPGA firmware switch, reboot the entire chassis by running the following command: clsh reboot.

bugs.title: ASM is not sending 64 KB remote logs over UDP
bugs.symptoms: REmote logs are missing. The following log messages appears in bd.log and asm.log: ASM configuration error: event code L3350 Failed to write to remote logger vs_name_crc 1119927693 LoggingAccount.cpp:3348`remote log write FAILED res = -3 <Failed to send remote message (remote server not responding)> errno <Message too long>.
bugs.conditions: -- A remote logger configured for UDP. -- Max message length of 64 KB.
bugs.impact: Missing logs in the remote logger.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Change the remote logger to TCP. -- Reduce the message length to 1 KB.

bugs.title: License state information from REST worker is out of sync with device
bugs.symptoms: The license information returned from the REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/shared/licensing/registration does not match the information returned from tmsh show sys license
bugs.conditions: 1. Device has an expired license (for example, an expired Eval period) 2. That license is re-activated, so that inspecting the device manually shows it is no longer expired.
bugs.impact: The license state information returned from REST workers maybe be out of date with the information on the device.
bugs.workaround: Restart REST services on the BIG-IP device by typing bigstart restart restjavad

bugs.title: eventd might core on transition to secondary.
bugs.symptoms: Upon transition to secondary, eventd shuts down its consumer list. However, during this shutdown, there could still be queued events yet to be process. This leads to a race condition between processing the events and freeing the memory of the consumer.
bugs.conditions: This happens when eventd is being shutdown while processing events.
bugs.impact: Causes eventd segmentation fault and core dump
bugs.fix: eventd no longer cores on transition to secondary when eventd is being shutdown while processing events.

bugs.title: Edge Client may crash after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: The Edge client may crash after upgrading to 11.4.1 through 12.0.0.
bugs.conditions: Access Policy with Firewall Checker Update BIG-IP to 12.1.0
bugs.impact: Users are unable to use the Edge client
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash in the Edge client

bugs.title: mcpd core during config push from Enterprise Manager
bugs.symptoms: During a config push from EM to BIG-IP, mcpd and chmand core.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this, but it was seen during a config push of over 100 users from Enterprise Manager to an HA pair.
bugs.impact: mcpd cores, system restart.

bugs.title: Policy disabled after enabled with apply-policy via REST, asm-sync removal fixes
bugs.symptoms: After the Apply-policy task completes successfully, there is an LTM incremental sync back from the peer unit and the policy is deactivated.
bugs.conditions: High availability (HA) configuration with an auto-sync failover group with ASM sync enabled.
bugs.impact: ASM policy is erroneously deactivated several seconds after it has been activated via the Apply-policy task.
bugs.workaround: Temporarily disable ASM sync on the device group.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the Apply-policy task so that there is no erroneous deactivation after it has completed.

bugs.title: Support for Single FQDN usage with Citrix Storefront Integration mode
bugs.symptoms: Adding a new login account onto citrix receiver could enumerate the applications and desktop. But after logging off and trying to reconnect to the same account will start failing.
bugs.conditions: Citrix storefront integration mode with APM and using same FQDN for both accessing Storefront as well as APM virtual
bugs.impact: Clients are unable to connect.
bugs.workaround: No workaround other than using different FQDNs
bugs.fix: APM now does not modify the beacon urls when a single FQDN is used for internal as well as external beacons.

bugs.title: Connection canâ€™t be established when multiple clientssl profiles are attached if the default profile is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: Connection canâ€™t be established when multiple clientssl profiles are attached and the default clientssl profile Mode is set to disabled.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when configuring a virtual server to serve multiple HTTPS sites using the TLS SNI (see https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/400/sol13452.html), but you want the fallback to disable ssl processing if the client does not pass in a matching server name.
bugs.impact: Setting the default clientssl profile's Mode to disabled effectively disables all SNI processing that would be handled in the other clientssl profiles, which disables all SSL processing on the virtual server.
bugs.fix: HTTPS virtual servers will now properly inspect the SNI in ClientHello and match against existing clientssl profiles if the fallback clientssl profile Mode is set to Disabled.

bugs.title: non-admin user running list cmd: can't get object count
bugs.symptoms: Non-admin user running list cmd: can't get object count.
bugs.conditions: Login as non admin user
bugs.impact: Very minor non-admin user got some restrictions to view.
bugs.workaround: Use admin account.
bugs.fix: Non admin user rights fixed.

bugs.title: No enforcement for WebSocket Framing protocol RSV1, RSV2, RSV3 (Reserve) flags
bugs.symptoms: Enforcement is not present for RSV1, RSV2, RSV3 (Reserve) flags of WebSocket Framing protocol
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with WebSocket profile and ASM policy attached
bugs.impact: WebSocket Framing protocol do not work as expected
bugs.fix: WebSocket Framing protocol RSV1, RSV2, RSV3 (Reserve) flags are enforced accordingly

bugs.title: DNSRelay Proxy re-transmits DNS requests indefinitely every second if NA DNS servers do not respond
bugs.symptoms: DNS relay service will send lot of DNS requests inside the network access tunnel if the DNS server is unreachable or unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: DNS Relay proxy service is installed on user's machine One or more DNS servers are not reachable or unresponsive
bugs.impact: Will generate lot of DNS traffic from user's machine and may have an adverse impact on customer infrastructure.
bugs.workaround: Stop DNS Relay proxy service from service control manager.
bugs.fix: Excessive DNS queries are no longer being sent from the EDGE client if the DNS server is unreachable.

bugs.title: Selenium detection not blocked
bugs.symptoms: When selenium client webdriver is detected running the Chrome browser it is not being blocked due to low score being assigned by PBD (Suspicious Browsers) mechanism.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when ASM is provisioned with proactive bot defense enabled.
bugs.impact: A bot which running selenium Chrome webdriver isn't mitigated by DoSL7 PBD mechanism.
bugs.fix: Only for Desktop Google Chrome browsers, the PBD javascript code checks if a plugin called "Widevine Content Decryption Module" doesn't exists, the browser considered as running via the selenium tool and will be blocked by PBD.

bugs.title: SQL Error on Peer Device After Receiving ASM Sync in a Device Group
bugs.symptoms: When: 1) A "Block All" Session Tracking Status exists and 2) A full sync occurs in an ASM CMI device group (always the case in manual sync device group) Then upon loading the full sync in the peer an SQL error will appear during the load: "Failed on insert to PLC.PL_SESSION_AWARENESS_DATA_POINT (DBD::mysql::db do failed: Duplicate entry '<ID>' for key 'PRIMARY')"
bugs.conditions: 1) A "Block All" Session Tracking Status exists and 2) A full sync occurs in an ASM CMI device group (always the case in manual sync device group)
bugs.impact: Benign error which does not affect configuration or enforcement.
bugs.fix: SQL error no longer occurs on CMI Sync with Session Awareness

bugs.title: Allow more than 16 pool members to be chosen from a pool during a single load-balancing decision.
bugs.symptoms: Prior to this, only 16 pool members could be chosen during a single load-balancing decision.
bugs.impact: Cannot return more than 16 pool members in a DNS response.
bugs.fix: GTM now allows more than 16 pool members to be returned from a pool in a DNS response. Any amount from 1 to 500 can be selected.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP DNS GSLB now allows more than 16 pool members to be returned from a pool in a DNS response. Any amount from 1 to 500 can be selected.

bugs.title: F5_Invoke_replace() should accept more than 2 arguments
bugs.symptoms: Not rewritten request from web-application
bugs.conditions: web-application uses location.replace() with number of arguments > 2
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used to fix issue.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed

bugs.title: DNS/SIP whitelisted packets not reported
bugs.symptoms: If a DNS/SIP packet hits DOS whitelist then this packet is not being reported to AVR.
bugs.conditions: The packet has to be DNS or SIP packet and has to hit the whitelist.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact but AVR tables will not have the whitelisted packets in their count.

bugs.title: MPTCP or SSL traffic handling may cause a BIG-IP outage
bugs.symptoms: Occasional BIG-IP outages may occur when MPTCP or SSL traffic is being handled by a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP has been enabled on a TCP profile on a virtual server, or SSL is in use.
bugs.impact: A system outage may occur.
bugs.fix: An issue with handling of MPTCP and SSL traffic has been corrected.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable MPTCP on any TCP profile

bugs.title: Tooltip displayed in tray icon of Edge Client does not show text correctly in some cases
bugs.symptoms: In some languages (other than English), text displayed in tooltip created by Edge Client tray application is clipped.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client localized for Japanese language is used to establish VPN connection.
bugs.impact: Usability impact. Notifications are not visible completely.
bugs.workaround: View the notification by clicking on the Details buttons in the Edge Client application, and going to the Notification tab.
bugs.fix: Now tooltip displays localized text correctly.

bugs.title: Network Access traffic does not pass IPv6 traffic if a Network Access resource contains IPv4&IPv6
bugs.symptoms: Network Access clients are unable to pass IPv6 traffic
bugs.conditions: Network Access resource configured with IPv4&IPv6 Client attempts to pass IPv6 traffic
bugs.impact: IPv6 traffic is dropped
bugs.fix: APM will now pass IPv6 traffic through the tunnel if an IPv4&IPv6 resource is configured.

bugs.title: The blade alarm LED may not reflect the warning that non F5 optics is used.
bugs.symptoms: When non F5 optics is used for front switch ports, the LCD and /var/log/ltm will display some warning message. But the alarm LED may not reflect that.
bugs.conditions: This is caused by a race condition. When a blade comes up and decides its role as a primary blade or a secondary blade, it will clear the alarm LED. So the last blade coming up may have its alarm LED in the right state, but the blades that came up earlier may have their alarm LEDs cleared.
bugs.impact: The alarm LED may not reflect the warning.
bugs.fix: The problem is fixed in TMOS v12.1.1.

bugs.title: "Instance not found" error when viewing the properties of GSLB monitors gateway_icmp and bigip_link.
bugs.symptoms: When you attempt to view the monitors' properties, the page throws an "Instance not found" error.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the GSLB Monitors tcp_half_open, gateway_icmp and bigip_link's properties page.
bugs.impact: You cannot view some of their monitors' properties.
bugs.fix: Fixed the "Instance not found" error.

bugs.title: Traffic that uses a network HSM for crypto services can fail to recover.
bugs.symptoms: When the system is configured to use network HSM for FIPS crypto services, all FIPS-related traffic will cease to function after the tmm daemon gets restarted, and does not recover until a restart of both pkcs11d and tmm, or a reboot of the unit.
bugs.conditions: -- System is configured for network HSM for FIPS crypto services. -- tmm gets restarted.
bugs.impact: Traffic that relies on the network HSM for crypto services fails and does not recover.
bugs.workaround: Restart both pkcs11d and tmm by issuing the following command: On a standard BIG-IP appliance: bigstart restart pkcs11d tmm On a VIPRION system: clsh bigstart restart pkcs11d tmm
bugs.fix: Traffic that relies on the network HSM for FIPS crypto services now recovers as expected when tmm is restarted.

bugs.title: Firefox signed plugin for VPN, Endpoint Check, etc
bugs.symptoms: clients are unable to use the Firefox plugin on Firefox version 47 and above
bugs.conditions: Clients using Firefox v47 and above attempting to use the Firefox plugin
bugs.impact: Clients will be unable to use the plugin if they are using Firefox version 47 and above
bugs.fix: The Firefox plugin now supports all versions.

bugs.title: Command failing: tmsh show ltm virtual vs_name detail.
bugs.symptoms: The following command fails: tmsh show ltm virtual vs_name detail. The system posts the following error: 01020036:3: The requested profile exchange: virtual server object (exchange_profile_name:vs_name) was not found.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when an APM Access Profile has an Exchange Profile attached and the access profile is then assigned to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: No information is displayed by the tmsh show command.
bugs.fix: The tmsh show command now presents information, and 'tmsh show ltm virtual vs_name detail' shows the expected details without error.

bugs.title: Cannot use Administrator account other than 'admin' to manage BIG-IP systems through BIG-IQ.
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to use BIG-IQ to manage BIG-IP systems using an Administrator account named other than 'admin' can fail.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IQ managing BIG-IP systems. -- Using an Administrator account different from 'admin'
bugs.impact: You cannot manage BIG-IP systems through BIG-IQ.
bugs.workaround: Use the 'admin' account on BIG-IQ to manage BIG-IP devices.
bugs.fix: Can now use an Administrator account other than 'admin' to manage BIG-IP systems through BIG-IQ.
bugs.behavior: Local requests through iControl client are now made on port 80, instead of 443.

bugs.title: mcpd process on secondary blades unexpectedly restarts when the system processes multiple tmsh commands
bugs.symptoms: The Master Control Program Daemon (MCPD) on secondary blades may unexpectedly restart when the BIG-IP system processes multiple, concurrent TMOS Shell (tmsh) commands. Under these circumstances, a race condition may occur and cause the mcpd process on the secondary blades to fail to correctly process concurrent updates from the primary blade. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- The mcpd process on secondary blades unexpectedly restarts. -- You notice error messages in the /var/log/ltm file on the BIG-IP system that appears similar to the following example: + err mcpd[<PID>]: 01070823:3: Read Access Denied: The current update partition ([None]) does not match the object's partition (Common), stats not reset + err mcpd[<PID>]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01070823:3: Read Access Denied: The current update partition ([None]) does not match the object's partition (Common), stats not reset -- Depending on your high availability (HA) configuration, the device may unexpectedly fail over to another system in the device group.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have a VIPRION platform or Virtual Clustered Multiprocessing (vCMP) guest configuration that uses two or more blades. -- You attempt to run multiple, concurrent tmsh commands on the BIG-IP system. For example, you run a tmsh command to continually reset persistence records and at the same time run another tmsh command to continually reset the TCP statistics.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may experience performance degradation when the secondary blades become unavailable while the mcpd process restarts. Depending on your HA configuration, the device may fail over.
bugs.workaround: Issue commands as part of a transaction.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Rewrite option missing in TCP Window Scale Mode for FastL4 profiles
bugs.symptoms: The Rewrite option is missing in TCP Window Scale Mode for FastL4 profiles.
bugs.conditions: This is visible when modifying the TCP Window Scale Mode in the GUI. In tmsh the options are preserve, rewrite, or strip. In the GUI the only options are rewrite or strip.
bugs.impact: Unable to set this mode using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: The Rewrite option has been added to TCP Window Scale Mode for FastL4 profiles.

bugs.title: 6900, 8900, 8950, or 11050 platforms missing swap storage
bugs.symptoms: No swap is available; observable via 'cat /proc/swaps'.
bugs.conditions: A 6900, 8900, 8950, or 11050 platform with RAID LVM, directly upgraded from a pre-10.2.4 version to version 11.x/12.x.
bugs.impact: No swap space is created during upgrade. Multiple unexpected issues might occur because there is no swap space available.
bugs.workaround: Newer systems have the swap storage created during initial format. You might also be able to first upgrade to version 10.2.4. Then, when upgrading to version 11.x/12.x, the process creates the swap during upgrade.

bugs.title: Required files under /etc/ssh are not moved during a UCS restore
bugs.symptoms: The SSH files required for SSH sign on are not transferred when performing a UCS restore operation. Further, files are not transferred even during upgrade.
bugs.conditions: This can happen when performing a UCS restore operation, or when upgrading from one version to the next.
bugs.impact: This might impact SSH operations.
bugs.workaround: Add the /etc/ssh directory to the UCS backup configuration. This causes all subsequent UCS backup and restore operations will now include the /etc/ssh/ directory. To complete this procedure, refer to K4422: Viewing and modifying the files that are configured for inclusion in a UCS archive :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K4422.
bugs.fix: The correct folder is now present when performing a UCS restore operation, so that all of the files required for the operation of SSH are transferred.

bugs.title: Device-group "datasync-global-dg" becomes out-of-sync every hour
bugs.symptoms: The datasync-global-dg device-group may become out-of-sync unexpectedly without any user changes. When this happens, the user can manually sync the device-group, but after about an hour the device-group becomes out-of-sync again.
bugs.conditions: 1. This happens only in certain timezones, depending on the timezone configured on the BIG-IP. We have only seen this happening in the Europe/London timezone. 2. The problem will start happening about 3 days after the first installation of an ASM Signature Update (ASU) or FPS Engine/Signature Update.
bugs.impact: GUI/shell shows config-sync "possible change conflict" or "changes pending" in regards to the datasync-global-dg device-group.
bugs.fix: The datasync-global-dg device-group no longer becomes out-of-sync unexpectedly and repeatedly every hour.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than manually syncing the device-group approximately every hour.

bugs.title: Incorreect PMTU discovery causes unstable VPN tunnel on Linux and MAC
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, VPN connection will be unstable resulting in multiple disconnects and reconnects during the session.
bugs.conditions: MTU on local interface is configured lower than 1500
bugs.impact: VPN tunnel may disconnect and reconnect multiple times

bugs.title: Logging filter for remote loggers doesn't work correctly with more than one logging profile
bugs.symptoms: A logging message arrived at a remote logger while the remote logger's filter have a criteria that doesn't match.
bugs.conditions: More than one logging profile is attached to a virtual server, the logging profiles have different filters conditions.
bugs.impact: A non related messages will be presented at the remote logger
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with multiple remote logging with different filters.

bugs.title: BD crash on startup or on XML configuration change
bugs.symptoms: BD crash. out of memory XML message in the bd.log. The BD doesn't startup and keeps crashing upon startup.
bugs.conditions: Many XML profiles and relatively large XML configuration.
bugs.impact: ASM down, machine is offline.
bugs.workaround: Increase the XML available memory.
bugs.fix: Fixed an XML memory sanity test that caused a crash when out of XML memory upon reading XML configuration.

bugs.title: AVR might report incorrect statistics when used together with other modules.
bugs.symptoms: When AVR is assigned to a virtual server that also has APM or Behavioral DoS, it can lead to AVR getting false readings of the activity and as result report on unexpectedly large numbers.
bugs.impact: AVR reports incorrect statistics: unexpectedly large numbers.
bugs.conditions: AVR Module is used together with other modules, and these module affect the traffic flow.
bugs.fix: AVR now identifies the other modules' activity and collects the activity statistics accordingly.

bugs.title: BWC policy in device sync groups.
bugs.symptoms: When there is a BWC policy created in global sync group and also a local one, then the configuration displays an error.
bugs.conditions: If BWC policy is created both in global sync and local.
bugs.impact: Configuration error, BWC policies will not be synced due to errors.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that BWC policy is in global sync only.
bugs.fix: BWC policy is now configured for device group sync only in the global group and not local.

bugs.title: Configuring TCP/HTTP type iRules together has insufficient validation.
bugs.symptoms: The system allows configuration of BigTCP/FastL4 plus HTTP even though iRule validation does not prevent unusable iRules combinations. For example, the node/pool iRule command typically used for steering in L7 virtual servers do not make sense in a FastL4 environment, as there is no delayed binding and pool/node selection would occur too late. However the lack of specific validation for this configuration allows you to specify this combination without warning, resulting in a non-functional virtual server. The system allows node/pool commands in CLIENT_DATA or in HTTP_REQUEST, which is simply too late for them to execute correctly.
bugs.conditions: Configuration of BigTCP/FastL4 plus HTTP in iRules.
bugs.impact: Results in unusable iRules combinations. Connection will be aborted and dropped, and, depending on the configuration and version, the system might not send a RST.

bugs.title: VE OVA logrotate max-file-size too big for /var/log partition size
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Edition (VE) OVA logrotate max-file-size is too big for the /var/log partition size.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on 11.5.0 and later, where the partition size was reduced from 6 GB to 500 MB, to better manage disk space.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP VE system runs out of disk space due to increased logging. In this instance, logrotate should run and potentially free up space by rotating and compressing the actively written logs. With the current setting for max-file-size, however, that cannot happen, thus leading to increased likelihood of running out of space in /var/log.
bugs.workaround: You can extend the disk space for logs by performing the following procedure. (From K14952: Extending disk space on BIG-IP Virtual Edition, available here: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14952#proc3.) Impact of procedure: You need to shut down the BIG-IP VE system during the disk provisioning steps, and the system will not be available for traffic processing. You should perform this procedure during a suitable maintenance window. Increasing the disk size on the VE system is irreversible, since F5 does not support disk shrinking. 1. Log in to the command line on the BIG-IP VE system. 2. Shut down the system by typing the following command: shutdown -h now 3. Provision the desired disk space for the VE system on the hypervisor. For information about disk provisioning on the hypervisor, refer to the documentation from your hypervisor vendor. 4. Start up the BIG-IP VE guest instance on your hypervisor. For information about starting a guest instance on the hypervisor, refer to the documentation from your hypervisor vendor. 5. When the BIG-IP VE system is up, log in to the command line on the VE system. 6. Extend the /var/log directory by using the following command syntax: tmsh modify /sys disk directory /var/log new-size <desired value in KB>. --For example you would type the following command to extend the /var/log directory to 10 GB: tmsh modify /sys disk directory /var/log new-size 10485760. 7. Save the configuration by typing the following command: tmsh save /sys config. 8. Reboot the VE system by typing the following command: reboot. 9. When the BIG-IP VE system is up, log in to the command line on the VE system. 10. Verify that the /var/log directory is successfully extended to the size you have specified in step 6 by typing the following command: tmsh show /sys disk directory.
bugs.fix: In this release, the default /var/log partition size to prevent the issue that occurred because the log-rotate max-file-size was too big in VE.

bugs.title: Policy builder doesn't enable staging after policy change on "*" entities (file types, urls, etc.)
bugs.symptoms: When conditions of "Track Site Change" settings are met the staging flag on "*" entities is supposed to be turned ON in order to learn sub-sequences of site changes without blocking traffic. However it doesn't happen. The staging flag stays OFF.
bugs.conditions: Staging was set OFF on "*" entity. After that conditions of "Track Site Change" settings are met.
bugs.impact: in a situation when the protected Web application was changed, ASM can block traffic when it should not be blocked.
bugs.workaround: Staging flag can be changed manually via GUI
bugs.fix: The problem was a sub-sequence of other code changes. The code was fixed he way it should count for "Track Site Change" conditions and change Staging flag when it is needed.

bugs.title: MSS may exceed MTU when using HW syncookies
bugs.symptoms: Packets larger than the interface's MTU can be transmitted.
bugs.conditions: A SYN packet is received with an MSS that exceeds the interface's MTU.
bugs.impact: Potential packet loss.
bugs.workaround: Disable HW syncookie mode.

bugs.title: When using a config merge load to disable and then later re-enable a monitored pool member, monitor checking will not start up again.
bugs.symptoms: When using a config merge load to disable and then later re-enable a monitored pool member, monitor checking will not start up again.
bugs.conditions: A monitored pool member is initially disabled, and a config merge re-enables it
bugs.impact: Monitoring does not resume when pool member is re-enabled via config merge.
bugs.workaround: You can re-enable monitoring by running the following commands: tmsh save sys config tmsh load sys config

bugs.title: ospfd core dump when redistributing NSSA routes in a HA failover
bugs.symptoms: The ospfd is dumping a core when nssa routes are redistributed.
bugs.conditions: When a failover is initiated through the GUI on a BIG-IP high availability (HA) configuration, and a standby BIG-IP system cannot take the active role due to low HA score. The original active BIG-IP system takes back the active role.
bugs.impact: ospfd terminates on the BIG-IP system leading to connectivity issues until the ospfd comes up.
bugs.fix: ospfd no longer crashes when redistributing NSSA routes in a HA failover event.

bugs.title: Maximum connections is not accurate when TMM load is uneven
bugs.symptoms: Maximum connections is not accurate when TMM load is unevenly distributed. Maximum connection statistics report the sum of maximum connections per TMM, not the maximum connections per virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the load disaggregated to available TMMs is uneven.
bugs.impact: This causes the various TMMs to measure their individual maximum connections at significantly different times, resulting in lower-than-expected maximum connections.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the configuration matches traffic patterns, so the load of connections is evenly distributed across all TMMs.
bugs.fix: Maximum connections is now accurate when TMM load is uneven.

bugs.title: Multiple 'Loading state for virtual server' messages in admd.log
bugs.symptoms: When a dosl7d profile is configured on a BIG-IP that's in a device group and the BIG-IP is set to "Forced Offline" in the Device Management settings, admd will log multiple messages to admd.log similar to 47854390298368 Mar 22 02:38:50 [info] virtual bool CVirtualServerImpl::loadState() : Loading state for virtual server
bugs.conditions: - dosl7d profile attached to a virtual server - BIG-IP is part of a DSC cluster - a BIG-IP is forced offline in the cluster
bugs.impact: Excessive logging occurs to /var/log/adm/admd.log
bugs.fix: An issue with excessive logging to admd.log has been fixed.

bugs.title: Linux client does not restore route to the default GW on Ubuntu 15.10
bugs.symptoms: Default route may be deleted after network access connection is deleted on Linux Ubuntu 15.10 distribution.
bugs.conditions: Ubuntu 15.0, network access tunnel connect and then disconnect
bugs.impact: User will not be able to reach internet after disconnecting from network access.
bugs.workaround: If Wifi is in use then turn off and on again. If Ethernet is used then unplugging and plugging cable again should solve the problem.

bugs.title: Cannot generate key after SafeNet HSM is rebooted
bugs.symptoms: After the SafeNet Hardware Security Module (HSM) is restarted, users cannot generate a new key.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system uses the SafeNet HSM.
bugs.impact: HSM service is not usable even after restarting pkcs11d. Users must re-authenticate.
bugs.workaround: To generate a new key, after HSM finishes starting up, run the following commands: # /shared/safenet/toolkit/sautil -v -s 1 -i 10:11 -c # /shared/safenet/toolkit/sautil -v -s 1 -i 10:11 -o -p <hsm_partition_password> Or, you can reinstall SafeNet client.
bugs.fix: After the SafeNet Hardware Security Module (HSM) is restarted, users can now generate a new key.

bugs.title: 'merged.method' set to 'slow_merge,' does not update system stats
bugs.symptoms: When the statistics DB variable option 'merged.method' is set to 'slow_merge,' system stats is not updated and remains zero.
bugs.conditions: Merged.method is set to slow_merge.
bugs.impact: System stats such as overall CPU usage remain at zero.
bugs.workaround: Set Merged.method to fast_merge.
bugs.fix: When the statistics DB variable option 'merged.method' is set to 'slow_merge,' system stats are not updated as expected.

bugs.title: Unable to display and edit huge policies (more than 4000 elements)
bugs.symptoms: It takes a very long time or is not possible to display huge policies (more than 4000 elements). VPE returns server timeout error or simple halts.
bugs.impact: Unable to edit policy because VPE times out.
bugs.conditions: Huge Access Policy, for example, containing 4000 or more elements.
bugs.fix: VPE loading times for APM policies is greatly improved, so displaying very large policies (for example, 4000 elements) now completes successfully.

bugs.title: default-node-monitor is reset to none for HA configuration.
bugs.symptoms: default-node-monitor is reset to none for high availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.conditions: Scenario #1 Upgrading HA active/standby configuration, and reboot standby. Where configuration consists of the following: * ltm node with a monitor. * ltm default-node-monitor with a different monitor. Scenario #2 Given a HA active/standby configuration with an ltm default-node-monitor configured, set device-group sync-leader.
bugs.impact: Monitoring will stop after upgrading or setting sync-leader for all nodes that relied on the default-node-monitor.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure a default-node-monitor.

bugs.title: IPv6 downloads stall when NA IPv4&IPv6 is used.
bugs.symptoms: When downloading large files through network access, downloads can appear to stall for a period of time and then resume.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Network Access is configured with an IPv4&IPv6 resource
bugs.impact: Downloads occasionally stall with download speed going to 0, and then they resume.
bugs.workaround: It is possible that disabling large receive offload will work as a mitigation. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcplargereceiveoffload value disable.

bugs.title: User Sessions lookups are not cleared, session stats show marked as invalid
bugs.symptoms: AVR session statistics may be reported as excessively high, and when the sessions time out they get marked as invalid instead of being removed.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions which cause this in a production configuration are unknown, as this was discovered during internal testing.
bugs.impact: Session statistics will report incorrectly
bugs.fix: An issue with session statistics not clearing after session timeout has been fixed.

bugs.title: TMM spams ltm log with "01010235:2: Inet port find called for pg 1 with invalid cmp state 0"
bugs.symptoms: /var/log/ltm is spammed with below shown logs: Mar 23 08:21:52 slot2/technetium crit tmm[13305]: 01010235:2: Inet port find called for pg 1 with invalid cmp state 0 Mar 23 08:21:53 slot2/technetium crit tmm3[13305]: 01010235:2: Inet port find called for pg 1 with invalid cmp state 0 Mar 23 08:21:53 slot2/technetium crit tmm3[13305]: 01010235:2: Inet port find called for pg 1 with invalid cmp state 0
bugs.conditions: One or more blades are administratively disabled on a chassis system.
bugs.impact: Detrimental to TMM performance.
bugs.fix: /var/log/ltm should no longer be spammed with these critical logs.

bugs.title: xpath parser doesn't reset a namespace hash value between each and every scan
bugs.symptoms: After a while the iRule event stops firing until the cbrd daemon is restarted.
bugs.conditions: The customer has a virtual server configured with an XML, along with an iRule that triggers on the XML_CONTENT_BASED_ROUTING event.
bugs.impact: XML content based routing does not work dependably.
bugs.fix: fixing xpath parer -- Restoring namespace declaration each time the xpath parser finishes to parse the document.

bugs.title: Macrocall could be topologically not connected with the rest of policy.
bugs.symptoms: It is possible to create macrocall access policy item that: 1. Belongs to policy items list. 2. Correctly connected to ending. 3. Have no incoming rules (i.e., no items pointing at it).
bugs.conditions: 1. Create access policy with macrocall item in one of the branches. 2. Remove the item which refers to this macrocall item from AP As a result, macrocall item remains.
bugs.impact: VPE fails to render this access policy.
bugs.workaround: Delete macrocall access policy item manually using tmsh commands.
bugs.fix: Any modification of access policy is not allowed if it makes any access policy item non-referenced. At upgrade time, non-referenced access policy items are deleted. All subsequent access policy items are deleted as well. Resulting access policies can be rendered correctly by VPE. Note that only active configuration is corrected, saved configuration file (/config/bigip.conf) contains uncorrected version until any new configuration changes are done. Active configuration can be saved by explicit tmsh command ('tmsh save sys config partitions all").

bugs.title: WebSockets frames are not forwarded with Websocket profile and ASM enabled on virtual
bugs.symptoms: WebSockets frames are not forwarded with WebSocket profile and ASM enabled on virtual.
bugs.conditions: Virtual has WebSocket profile attached to it. ASM is enabled on the virtual. WebSockets server replies with a "Connection: upgrade" header. The issue is also seen if multiple header values are present in Connection header.
bugs.impact: WebSockets frames are not forwarded to the pool member
bugs.workaround: Use a simple iRule similar to the following: when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { [HTTP::status] == 101 } { HTTP::header replace "Connection" "Upgrade" } }
bugs.fix: The system now accepts "Connection: UPGRADE" or "Connection: upgrade" as valid header for WebSocket handshake, and supports a comma-separated list of values for the Connection response header.

bugs.title: DNS server for child zone can continue to resolve domain names after revoked from parent
bugs.symptoms: See. A domain name in a child server may continue to be resolved by the child server even after the parent server revokes the NS record for the child server.
bugs.conditions: A steady series of DNS queries for a domain name in the child. The TTL for the domain name A record is shorter than the TTL for the NS record for the child name server. The NS record is removed from the parent server.
bugs.impact: The revoked child server will still be used by a client after it is revoked.
bugs.workaround: Restart the TMM to clear out the cache.
bugs.fix: Do not update the NS record TTL to the value returned from the child server.

bugs.title: iRules are not updated in transactions through TMSH or iControl
bugs.symptoms: Updating an iRule in a transaction via TMSH or iControl results in the iRule not being updated, but there is no error indicating this.
bugs.conditions: Updating an iRule in a transaction using TMSH or iControl.
bugs.impact: iRule is not updated, and the user is not alerted of this fact.
bugs.fix: iRules modified through transactions are now updated properly.

bugs.title: Start Screen Guest List is not available
bugs.symptoms: Guest List is not available as a Start Screen.
bugs.conditions: vCMP is enabled.
bugs.impact: Cannot use Guest List as the Start Screen.
bugs.fix: Guest List option has been added for the Start Screen.

bugs.title: iControl REST unavailable after first boot
bugs.symptoms: After initial system start, you notice that iControl REST is unavailable.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on first boot.
bugs.impact: iControl REST is unavailable.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the BIG-IP clears this condition.

bugs.title: Sending a SIP invite with "tel" URI fails with a reset
bugs.symptoms: Using a "INVITE tel:" URI results in SIP error (Illegal value).
bugs.conditions: Sending a SIP "INVITE tel:" to BIG-IP does not work.
bugs.impact: "INVITE tel:" messages are not accepted by BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: An EHF will be released to address this issue. It will also be addressed in a future release.

bugs.title: TMM restart rarely during startup
bugs.symptoms: A TMM crashes with a core file during startup. It restarts then correctly.
bugs.conditions: The system starts up.
bugs.impact: The system startup takes longer. A core file appears. Traffic is not impacted and a failover usually doesn't occur since the system didn't reach the active state.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes during startup.

bugs.title: tmm segfault: ikev2_noncecmp (n1=0x0, n2=0x0)
bugs.symptoms: The tmm cores when using IPsec IKEv2.
bugs.conditions: A rare timing condition related to IPsec decryption and security association timeout.
bugs.impact: All connections reset.

bugs.title: iControl produces 404 error while creating records successfully
bugs.symptoms: iControl produces an HTTP 404 - Not Found error message while creating the BIG-IP DNS topology record successfully.
bugs.conditions: Creating GTM topology record without using full path via iControl.
bugs.impact: Resulting code/information is not compatible with actual result. For a post request, the create command and the list command are formed and executed, and the name in the curl request and the name in the list response are compared to verify whether or not it is the actual object. When a create command is executed with properties that are not fullPath (e.g., in iControl), it still creates the object with fullPath. So list returns the name with fullPath and compares it with the name that does not contain the fullPath, and the comparison fails because the names do not match.
bugs.workaround: Use the full path when creating BIG-IP DNS topology records using iControl.
bugs.fix: The system now compares both names, ignoring the partition '/Common' if the exact comparison fails.

bugs.title: ADAPT::result bypass after continue causes bad state transition
bugs.symptoms: Tcl command 'ADAPT::result bypass' does not work in ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT when the ICAP server has previously returned 100-continue.
bugs.conditions: iRules exist on a VS with an adapt profile, containing: when ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT { ADAPT::result bypass } or when ADAPT_RESPONSE_RESULT { ADAPT::result bypass }
bugs.impact: ADAPT logs an unexpected state transition and resets the connection, making it impossible for iRules to replace the ICAP response.
bugs.workaround: Avoid 'ADAPT::result bypass' commands in cases where there is no preview (either configured for no preview, or after the preview has been dropped due to a 100-continue or 200-ok ICAP response).
bugs.fix: Tcl command 'ADAPT::result bypass' is allowed in ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT and ADAPT_REPSONSE_RESULT at any time, even outside a preview (such as when the ICAP server has previously returned 100-continue and the preview has been dropped). No further payload is sent to the IVS, and further IVS response payload is ignored by ADAPT. The unmodified HTTP headers, any preview, and any future original payload bypass the IVS. A warning is logged in cases where some payload might have been lost (such as when there is no preview or it has been dropped, as is the case after ICAP 100-continue). The HTTP connections remain intact and amenable to user iRules replacing the content.

bugs.title: Zebos issue: No neighbor x.x.x.x activate in address-family IPv6 lost on reboot/restart.
bugs.symptoms: when a neighbor with ipv4 address is disabled in ipv6 address family, show running configuration displays that the neighbor is disabled. However, when we restart or reboot the tmrouted or bgp protocol, the neighbor is enabled again. The configuration persistence is not maintained.
bugs.conditions: 1. disable a neighbor with ipv4 address in ipv6 address family. 2. reboot/restart tmrouted or bgp protocol
bugs.impact: configuration persistence is not maintained. This impacts the BIGIP upgrades as the configuration loaded is not the same as it was before the upgrade. Similarly, a restart/reboot will also have different configuration loaded than originally used. This might alter the intended behavior of the protocol that the use expects to function.
bugs.workaround: disable the neighbor again.
bugs.fix: configuration persistence is maintained for the disabled neighbor with ipv4 address in the ipv6 address family.

bugs.title: BGP activated for IPv4 address family even when 'no bgp default ipv4-unicast' is configured
bugs.symptoms: When BGP is configured with 'no bgp default ipv4-unicast,' configuring a peer-group with IPv6 members adds 'neighbor <neighbor> activate' for the IPv6 neighbors under address-family ipv4.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- 'no bgp default ipv4-unicast' is configured in imish. -- 'neighbor <neighbor> peer-group <peergroup>' is configured.
bugs.impact: Despite disabling IPv4 unicast for BGP by default, neighbors in the peer group have the IPv4 unicast address family enabled.
bugs.workaround: Delete the line in the configuration that was automatically added in imish in the 'router bgp' section: no neighbor <neighbor> activate
bugs.fix: Configuring IPv6 members of a peer-group when 'no bgp default ipv4-unicast' no longer automatically enables IPv4 unicast for the peer-group members.

bugs.title: NTLM Auth cannot be disabled in HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST event
bugs.symptoms: The following iRule did not work as expected when the access profile had an NTLM auth. The client still received a 407 prompt to enter NTLM credentials. when HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::uri] contains "disable" } { ACCESS::disable } }
bugs.conditions: Access profile of an SWG type, with an NTLM auth profile attached.
bugs.impact: It was impossible to disable NTLM auth from the HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST event.
bugs.workaround: The following iRule works from HTTP_REQUEST when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::uri] contains "disable" } { ACCESS::disable ECA::disable } }
bugs.fix: When ACCESS filter is disabled, it still processes certain messages. The logic in one of those message handlers was "if NTLM configured, then wake up the ECA plugin" Fix changed the logic to "if NTLM configured and ACCESS filter is not disabled, then wake up the ECA plugin."

bugs.title: LCD text truncated by heartbeat icon on VIPRION
bugs.symptoms: while looking at informational text on the first line of the LCD display on a VIPRION, the end of the string is truncated by a heartbeat icon.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on platforms that display a heartbeat icon on the LCD display.
bugs.impact: The heartbeat icon is displayed over the last character of the string, this is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: In this release, longer messages on the LCD are now displayed on multiple lines.

bugs.title: "Corrupted Connect Error" when using IPv6 and On-Demand Cert Auth
bugs.symptoms: Browser shows a "corrupted connect error" when access policy runs On-Demand Cert Auth on an IPv6 virtual server. The root cause is that in packet capture, the APM sends an HTTP 302 with invalid brackets around the hostname, like this: Location: https://[login.example.com]/my.policy Brackets around IPv6 addresses are for raw IPv6 addresses. They are illegal for DNS names that represent an IPv6 address.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 virtual server, and On-Demand Cert Auth in the access policy. Only applies if a DNS hostname is used. Raw IPv6 addresses are not affected.
bugs.impact: Client is unable to authenticate.
bugs.fix: Clients connecting to an APM access policy with on-demand certificate authentication to an IPv6 virtual server now transmit the client certificate correctly when executing the access policy.

bugs.title: BIG-IP logs INVALID-SPI messages but does not remove the associated SAs.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system logs INVALID-SPI messages but does not remove the associated Security Associations (SAs) corresponding to the message. This is the second part of a fix provided for this issue. See fixes for bug 569236 for the first part.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if an IPsec peer deletes a phase2 (IPsec) SA and does not send a 'notify delete' message to the other peer. The INVALID-SPI message is most likely to be seen when the peer deletes an SA before the SA's agreed lifetime.
bugs.impact: If the BIG-IP is always the Initiator, the Responder will not initiate a new tunnel if the Responder only handles responses to the BIG-IP clients' traffic. The BIG-IP system continues to use the IPsec SA it believes to be still up. When an SA expires prematurely, some IPsec peers will reject an inbound SPI packet with an ISAKMP INVALID-SPI notify message. If the INVALID-SPI message does not cause new SAs to be created, there will be a tunnel outage until the SA lifetime expires on the defunct SA held on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Manually remove the invalid SA on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Now, when the BIG-IP system receives INVALID-SPI messages, it deletes the invalid Security Association as well as logging the INVALID-SPI message, so the tunnel can initiate again. This is part two of a two-part fix. Fixes for bug 569236 provide part one of the fix.

bugs.title: Using management port as config sync address might allow its deletion.
bugs.symptoms: If you assign the management port as a config sync address, it's possible to later delete the management port without error. This causes quite a few problems in multiple places (updating the sys_device, adding devices to trust, etc.)
bugs.conditions: management-ip while configured as a config sync address.
bugs.impact: Can delete management-ip.
bugs.workaround: None, other than do not delete management-ip when it's configured as a config sync address.

bugs.title: The TMM may crash when changing profiles associated with plugins
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may crash when changing profiles associated with plugins.
bugs.conditions: The must be a profile associated with a plugin already on a virtual server and traffic must be running. When the profile is removed or swapped for another, the crash may occur.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: A safe way to definitely avoid a crash is to stop the plugin before making changes to its profile.

bugs.title: AJAX encryption may send corrupted payload when configuration is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: AJAX encryption can fail when non-existent fields are configured.
bugs.conditions: Activate AJAX encryption and configure fields that don't exist in the page.
bugs.impact: Decryption of AJAX may fail.
bugs.fix: AJAX encryption now works as expected

bugs.title: ASM Policy Parameter's Filter: Search for at least 1 Override doesn't work
bugs.symptoms: The 'Overridden Characters in Value' and 'Overridden Attack Signatures' filter options on the Parameters List screen doesn't work correctly. These filter options appear after you set 'Parameter Value Type' to 'User-input value' and 'Data Type' to 'Alpha-Numeric'.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to filter parameters by settings the 'Value Type' to 'User-input value', 'Data Type' to 'Alpha-Numeric', and searching for 'At least one' signature override.
bugs.impact: Search fails.
bugs.fix: Searching for 'At least one' override now works correctly.

bugs.title: Alert dashboard does not correctly display Hebrew characters in alerts.
bugs.symptoms: Alert server cannot decrypt Hebrew characters in alerts.
bugs.conditions: Malicious script injection containing wide characters.
bugs.impact: Incorrectly displayed alerts in dashboard.
bugs.fix: Alerts are sent encoded and are decoded in the dashboard.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP may core while recompiling LTM policies
bugs.symptoms: In some rare and still unknown situations the BIG-IP Mcpd process may core when creating or modifying LTM policies. While the root cause of the crash is not fully understood at this time, one of the symptoms points to a nonexistent or invalid LTM policy.
bugs.conditions: Creating or modifying LTM policies.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP control plane services restart thus affecting both, control plane and data plane functionality.
bugs.workaround: A possible workaround could be to attempt re-creating the LTM policy producing the crash under a different name. Avoid any special characters (or spaces) in the name of the LTM policy.
bugs.fix: Not fixed yet.

bugs.title: In Multidomain SSO, primary auth virtual may fail as a resource
bugs.symptoms: Multidomain SSO use case with two virtuals: vs1 and vs2. Both virtuals are configured as APM+LTM pools. vs1 is designed as the primary auth virtual The expected result is that users can access resources on both virtuals. If they have not yet authenticated, they will be redirected to vs1 to authenticate. The reported result was that sometimes an already authenticated user would be able to access the resources on vs2. But their cookie would be rejected by vs1, and they would be asked to authenticate again.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what conditions cause this to occur.
bugs.impact: Users may be asked to re-authenticate, even though they just did so.
bugs.workaround: Use an independent auth virtual that is not also a resource.

bugs.title: Considerations for transferring files from F5 devices
bugs.symptoms: For more information, see K58243048: Considerations for transferring files from F5 devices, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.conditions: For more information, see K58243048: Considerations for transferring files from F5 devices, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.impact: For more information, see K58243048: Considerations for transferring files from F5 devices, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.fix: For more information, see K58243048: Considerations for transferring files from F5 devices, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048

bugs.title: tmm ASSERT's "valid node" on Active, after timer fire..
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on ASSERT's "valid node".
bugs.conditions: The cause is unknown, and this happens rarely.
bugs.impact: tmm crash
bugs.workaround: no
bugs.fix: TMM no longer asserts on 'valid node'

bugs.title: Portal Access could send to backend application wrong URL query separator
bugs.symptoms: If any query parameters were added into request URL after being processed with F5 rewriting code, backend application could receive URL with wrong query separator (';').
bugs.conditions: This occurs on Access Portal, some POST request parameters may have a semicolon as a query separator and not get rewritten.
bugs.impact: Applications expecting '&' as a query separator won't be able to parse query part of URL correctly and may return an error.
bugs.workaround: when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { # Replace parameter_name with actual name of parameter which is added after F5CH. if { [HTTP::query] contains {;parameter_name=} } { HTTP::query [string map {;parameter_name= &parameter_name=} [HTTP::query]] } }
bugs.fix: Now requests to back-end server with query parameters contain parameter delimiters from original web application request.

bugs.title: Portal Access code does not check if methods of XMLHttpRequest Javascript object are redefined by application
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access code does not check if wrapped methods of XMLHttpRequest Javascript object were redefined by web application. In the worst case this allows application code to read or modify mangled URL before sending AJAX request.
bugs.conditions: Application redefines 'open' method of XMLHttpRequest object or prototype.
bugs.impact: Application code can read and modify already rewritten URL and send unmangled AJAX requests.

bugs.title: ASM subsystem error appears in asm log after changing XML/JSON profile for parameter
bugs.symptoms: ASM subsystem error appears in asm log after changing XML/JSON profile for parameter ASM subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl,F5::ASMConfig::Handler::save_events_to_config_log): Couldn't save to config log (Attempt to bless into a reference at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/ASMConfig/Entity/Base.pm line 192. )
bugs.conditions: ASM rpovisioned change one XML/JSON profile, assigned to a parameter, to another XML/JSON profile.
bugs.impact: ASM subsystem error appears in asm log after changing XML/JSON profile for parameter
bugs.fix: We've prevented an error from occurring when changing XML/JSON profile for parameter

bugs.title: ServerSSL ClientHello does not encode lowest supported TLS version, which might result in alerts and closed connections on older Servers.
bugs.symptoms: Server SSL ClientHello does not encode lowest supported TLS version. The outer record for a ClientHello contains the same version as the ClientHello. If, for example, the ClientHello is TLS1.2, the outer record will contain TLS1.2. Older servers that do not support later TLS versions might generate an alert and close the connection.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system with a server SSL profile that supports a TLS version higher than that of the server to which it is connecting.
bugs.impact: The connection fails. The system might generate an alert.
bugs.workaround: Force the server SSL profile to use a lower TLS version number by selecting 'No TLSv1.2' or 'No TLSv1.1' in the `options' section of the Server SSL Profile.
bugs.fix: When enabled by setting the db variable, 'SSL.OuterRecordTls1_0,' to, 'enable,' the outer SSL record will always contain TLS1.0. This is the default. You can use this db variable to prevent an issue in older servers that do not support TLS versions later than 1.0, in which an alert might be generated closing the connection.
bugs.behavior: Formerly, the version present in the ClientHello and the version present in the outer record would match. Now, if the sys db variable, 'SSL.OuterRecordTls1_0,' is set to 'enable' the version present in the outer record will be TLS 1.0 regardless of the version in the ClientHello. This is the default.

bugs.title: High ASCII meta-characters can be disallowed on UTF-8 policy via XML import
bugs.symptoms: After importing an XML policy, you cannot view or edit policies containing high ASCII characters.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when importing XML policies containing high-ASCII meta-characters but high-ASCII is not allowed in a UTF-8 policy.
bugs.impact: Unable to view or edit the policy, and Illegal meta character in value violation is triggered

bugs.title: tmm core on out of memory
bugs.symptoms: tmm memory increases quickly, then crashes on out of memory condition
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this, but it was observed on a hardware platform processing a large number of ECDH ciphers.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None known.
bugs.fix: Cancel ongoing crypto requests when handshake is dropped.

bugs.title: When TMM is down, executing 'show ltm persist persist-records' results in a blank error message.
bugs.symptoms: Executing 'show ltm persist persist-records' results in a blank error message.
bugs.conditions: TMM must be down.
bugs.impact: Non-obvious / unhelpful error message is generated, leading to customer confusion.

bugs.title: [TMSH] sys crypto cert missing tab completion function
bugs.symptoms: When pressing the tab key for the tmsh command "sys crypto cert", it does not display existing certificate names. You must manually type the certificate name that you want to operate.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in tmsh: root@(big7)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list sys crypto cert <------- press <tab>. Options: all | <------------ nothing shows up. root@(big7)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# show sys crypto cert <------- press <tab>. Options: all | <------------ nothing shows up.
bugs.impact: Not possible to select a certificate using tab complete.
bugs.workaround: Manually type the certificate name.
bugs.fix: With the fix, you can now see the existing certificate names when pressing tab key for the tmsh command "sys crypto cert".

bugs.title: VE supports only 2 NUMA domains
bugs.symptoms: VMware ESX version 5.5 and greater can expose NUMA topology to guests, sometimes exposing more NUMA nodes than the two that Virtual Edition (VE) supports. This causes a TMM core, with the following error message in /var/log/tmm: sys_get_numa_info: <N> exceeds max nodes of 2
bugs.conditions: -- VE running on VMware ESX 5.5 or greater. -- 16 vCPUs configured.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: In VMware ESX, modify the guest hardware configuration to present a maximum of two sockets to the VE guest. For example, if you configure an 8 CPU VM, set Cores per Socket to 4.

bugs.title: Removing ECMP route from BGP does not clear route from NSM
bugs.symptoms: When configured to install multiple routes into the routing table, ZebOS does not withdraw BGP routes when a neighbor is shut down and it has more than two routes already installed for the same route prefix.
bugs.conditions: ECMP routing must be enabled and in-use.
bugs.impact: ECMP routes are not properly removed from the main routing table.
bugs.fix: Now properly removing ECMP routes from the routing table.

bugs.title: Forward proxy does not work when netHSM is configured on TMM interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Forward proxy feature does not always work when netHSM is configured on TMM interfaces.
bugs.conditions: When netHSM device is configured on TMM interface.
bugs.impact: The forward proxy feature does not work. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.fix: Forward proxy now works consistently when netHSM is configured on TMM interfaces.

bugs.title: The TMM may hang handling pipelined HTTP requests with certain iRule commands.
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, the TMM may hang during a HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect iRule command if it is part of a pipelined HTTP request.
bugs.conditions: A HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect iRule is used. The iRule command is in an event triggered on the client-side. A pipelined HTTP request is being handled.
bugs.impact: The TMM will be restarted by SOD.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer hangs in rare situations when processing a pipelined HTTP request and invoking a HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect iRule command.

bugs.title: Fragmented packets may cause tmm to core under heavy load
bugs.symptoms: tmm core due to assertion
bugs.conditions: tmm offloads a fragmented packet via an ffwd operation.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fragmented packets no longer cause tmm to core under heavy load.

bugs.title: forward slash '/' is used in the description field, admin user will be demoted to guest.
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new admin user, if a forward slash '/' is used in the description field, the user will be demoted to guest.
bugs.conditions: Creating a new admin user with a forward slash in the description text.
bugs.impact: mcp user's admin group demotion to guest.
bugs.workaround: Do not use forward slashes in the users description.
bugs.fix: System now allows forward slashes '/' in user description.

bugs.title: BD daemon crashes unexpectedly
bugs.symptoms: bd crashes, with the following log signature immediately before the crash in /var/log/bd.log: "IO_PLUGIN|ERR |Mar 29 20:48:02.217|17328|plugin_common.c:0085|plugin context doesn't match the argument which was originally set on it".
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this condition; it can occur intermittently during normal use of ASM.
bugs.impact: A bd crash, failover, traffic disturbance.
bugs.fix: Fix a bd crash scenario.

bugs.title: FPS periodic updates (cron) write errors to log
bugs.symptoms: FPS periodic updates (run via cron) write errors to log when FPS is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: FPS is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: Errors appears in FPS logs.

bugs.title: "Util% (last 10 sec)" Field in "tmsh show sys cpu" when 5 second average is computed
bugs.symptoms: When the command "tmsh show sys cpu" is executed, the output has "Util% (last 10 sec)" field displayed with incorrect information for the total column.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the command "tmsh show sys cpu" is invoked.
bugs.impact: The displayed data is not correct. Instead, the system is displaying the usage ratio which is calculated in an entirely different manner.
bugs.workaround: You can use the tmctl command to display the 5 sec average ratio which is what the output should be. The command is: tmctl cpu_info_stat -s five_sec_avg.ratio This provides the workaround to the output for the tmsh command "tmsh show sys cpu".
bugs.fix: "Util% (last 10 sec)" field output in "tmsh show sys cpu" when 5 second average is computed now displays the 5 seconds average data.

bugs.title: TMM may core when running two simultaneous WebSocket collect commands
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core with a SIGFPE when running two or more WebSocket collect commands in parallel.
bugs.conditions: -- WebSocket profile is attached to the virtual server. -- Multiple iRules with WebSocket collect commands are attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM may core with a SIGFPE resulting in loss of service.
bugs.workaround: Behavior is undefined when multiple collect commands are running at the same time. Rewrite iRules to have only one collect command executing at a time.
bugs.fix: iRule documentation was updated and WebSocket filter state machine was changed to reject multiple collect commands.

bugs.title: Transparent HTTP profiles cannot have iRules configured
bugs.symptoms: When an HTTP profile is configured in transparent mode, but has a nonexisting iRule attached to it, then tmm will crash.
bugs.conditions: There is irule but proxy is transparent when HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST { after 1000 } Change configuration from explicit->transparent while we were in the after command. We then attempt to use configuration that doesn't exist, and then crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This is incorrect configuration. Either detach the iRule or configure the profile in a mode other than transparent.
bugs.fix: Incorrectly configured proxy types from TMOS installations of earlier versions will be corrected at upgrade time. A warning will be logged that describes the change made.

bugs.title: tmm assert "wrong selector tag"
bugs.symptoms: The tmm will assert with "wrong selector tag."
bugs.conditions: This may happen with a high IPsec tunnel count, for example 24000 tunnels defined, and the system is out of memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Provision the system within working limits.
bugs.fix: The tmm assert has been corrected.

bugs.title: TCP:Collect ignores the 'skip' parameter when used in serverside events
bugs.symptoms: When TCP::Collect is used with 'skip' and 'length' arguments in SERVER_CONNECTED, the "skip' argument does not take effect and is ignored. The Collect works, but collects only the length bytes from start.
bugs.conditions: TCP:Collect on server side events like SERVER_CONNECTED used with the 'skip' parameter. This is an intermittent issue that have happen only with IIS server.
bugs.impact: TCP:Collect collects bytes without taking into account the skip, so the bytes collected are not the correct ones.
bugs.fix: The settings for TCP::Collect command skip and length arguments are now honored during packet processing.

bugs.title: AD/LDAP resource group mapping table controls are not accessible sometimes
bugs.symptoms: AD/LDAP resource group mapping In case of both lengthy group names and resource names edit link and control buttons could disapper under dialogue bounds
bugs.conditions: very long group names and resource names
bugs.impact: Impossible to delete and move rows in table - still possible to edit tho.
bugs.workaround: Spread one assign thru multiple rows
bugs.fix: Scroll bar is appearing when needed

bugs.title: iRule cmd: RESOLV::lookup causes tmm crash when resolving an IP address.
bugs.symptoms: iRule command RESOLV::lookup causes tmm crash when resolving an IP address.
bugs.conditions: Using the RESOLV::lookup iRule command to resolve an IP address.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the RESOLV::lookup command to resolve an IP address.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when the iRule command RESOLV::lookup is used.
