bugs.title: Deleting persistence-records via tmsh may result in persistence being created to different nodes
bugs.symptoms: After deleting the persistence records, a connection may use persistent records to two different nodes breaking persistence.
bugs.conditions: Deleting persistence records when there is high concurrency for particular persistence records (e.g., load testing).
bugs.impact: Client fails to persist to a particular node.
bugs.workaround: Avoid removing persistence records from tmsh or use iRules to remove persistence records.

bugs.title: Priority order of clientssl profile selection of virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: When a SSL connection with specified server name is received in a virtual server from the client side, the BIG-IP system selects one clientssl profile for this connection based on the given server name. Currently the system matches the server name using the following rules: (1) First try to match the server name with explicit server name configuration of the clientssl profiles. (2) If (1) has no match, then try to match the common names of the certificates used by the clientssl profiles. (3) If (2) has no match, then try to match the subject alternative names of the certificates used by the clientssl profiles. The issue is, based on RFC6125, common name should be used as a 'last resort'. In other words, the third rule should be the second rule.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met. (1) The incoming SSL request includes SNI (server name) extension in the clienthello, used to specify its desirable SSL server. (2) The given server name from the client side does not match any server name configured in all the clientssl profiles of the virtual server. (3) The certificates used by the clientssl profile of the virtual server have subject alternative names (note that every certificate has common name but not necessarily subject alternative names).
bugs.impact: The virtual server might select a clientssl profile that is not preferred by the client side.
bugs.fix: Priority order of clientssl profile selection of virtual server. The system now matches the server name using the following rules: (1) First try to match the server name with explicit server name configuration of the clientssl profiles. (2) If (1) has no match, then try to match the subject alternative names of the certificates used by the clientssl profiles. (3) If (2) has no match, then try to match the common names of the certificates used by the clientssl profiles. So the common-name match is last, which is correct according to RFC6125.
bugs.behavior: If server-name is not configured in the client SSL profile for SNI (server name) matching, SANs (subject alternative names) in the certificate will take precedence over CN (common name) in the certificate, for the SNI-matching process for client SSL profile selection.

bugs.title: Allowing non-English characters on login screen
bugs.symptoms: Passwords can contain non-English characters but it fails when logging in.
bugs.conditions: Passwords contain non-English characters.
bugs.impact: Users entering these characters on the login screen are unable to log in.
bugs.workaround: Make sure passwords contain only English characters.
bugs.fix: Usernames and passwords with non-English characters can be used to log in.

bugs.title: Failure to stabilize internal HiGig link will not trigger failover event
bugs.symptoms: The internal HiGig interface potentially and repeatedly report FCS errors or does not become stable in rare cases.
bugs.conditions: The internal HiGig interfaces experiences FCS or XLMAC link failures.
bugs.impact: Device is left in a state where it cannot receive or pass traffic or have frame checksum errors.
bugs.fix: HA failover mechanism is now activated when internal HSB ports on critical data path are consistently unstable.
bugs.behavior: There is a condition in which failures happen on the internal HiGig interfaces on the critical packet path between the HSB and the Broadcom switch, causing traffic interruption. Such failures can be inferred by HSB XLMAC instability or by observing increasing FCS errors. When these HSB XLMAC failures happened in the past, TMOS initiated a recovery mechanism by resetting the HSB MAC interface. However, if the failure persisted even after repeated recovery attempts, TMOS triggered a high availability (HA) failover event to prevent prolonged traffic disruption. The failover triggering condition is set as either the consecutive recovery attempts or consecutive FCS failure events that reach a configurable preset limit. After the HA failover was triggered, the original active unit will still keep trying to recover, and will mark itself ready if the failure condition is no longer observed. The XLMAC reset was existing behavior. The new behavior also applies to FCS failure events.

bugs.title: JavaScript: 'baseURI' property may be handled incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: If generic JavaScript object has 'baseURI' property, it may be handled incorrectly via Portal Access: web application may get 'undefined' value for this property.
bugs.conditions: User-defined JavaScript object with 'baseURI' property.
bugs.impact: Web application may work incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: iRule can be used to remove F5_Deflate_baseURI() calls from rewritten JavaScript code.
bugs.fix: Now JavaScript objects with 'baseURI' property are handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: Timeout error when attempting to retrieve large dataset.
bugs.symptoms: The Rest API can timeout when attempting to retrieve large dataset, such as a large GTM pool list. The error signature when using the Rest API looks like "errorStack":["java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException: remoteSender:127.0.0.1, uri:http://localhost:8110/tm/gtm/pool, method:GET "
bugs.conditions: Configuration containing a large number of GTM pools and pool members (thousands).
bugs.impact: If using the Rest API to retrieve the pool list, you may receive timeout errors.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMSH performance has been improved for this GTM case (improvement ~5-10 times), which is root case for REST failure. Timeout is no longer triggered for this amount of data.

bugs.title: Harden authentication infrastructure
bugs.symptoms: The authentication infrastructure for administrative interfaces does not implement all current recommended security practices.
bugs.impact: The authentication infrastructure for administrative interfaces does not implement all current recommended security practices.
bugs.fix: Implement all current recommended security practices in the administrative interfaces authentication infrastructure.

bugs.title: Response to -list iRules command gets truncated when dealing with MX type wide IP
bugs.symptoms: GTM iRule "members" with the "-list" flag will truncate MX-type WideIP pool members when printed out to a log.
bugs.conditions: Use the GTM iRule "members" with the "-list" flag to print out the members of an MX WideIP pool during a DNS event.
bugs.impact: WideIP MX-type pool members are truncated in the log.

bugs.title: Apply Policy Failure
bugs.symptoms: Some Policies cannot be successfully applied/activated
bugs.conditions: Signature overrides on Content Profiles are configured
bugs.impact: Policy cannot be applied
bugs.fix: Policies can be successfully applied.

bugs.title: platform-migrate won't import password protected master-keys from a 10.2.4 UCS file
bugs.symptoms: If you run the platform-migrate command to migrate from a UCS file generated on a platform running 10.2.4, the password protected master key won't import
bugs.conditions: You would encounter this when doing platform migration from an older platform running 10.2.4, and using the UCS file from that platform to platform-migrate to 12.1.1. This also only occurs if your 10.2.4 UCS contains secure attributes, such as clientssl or serverssl keys and profiles
bugs.impact: The platform-migrate command will fail if the 10.2.4 UCS contains a password protected master key.
bugs.fix: The 12.1.1 release can successfully platform-migrate UCS files from a 10.2.4 configuration if some steps are taken to generate a password protected master key on the 10.2.4 release. Without these steps, this impact exists. The 10.2.4-specific solution https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K9420

bugs.title: Last good master key
bugs.symptoms: When applying a UCS file to a platform that was different from the one the UCS was taken on, for example after RMA, you get a master key decrypt error because the master key is different.
bugs.conditions: This can occur either when applying a UCS file to an identical platform you received as an RMA exchange, or while performing the platform-migrate command.
bugs.impact: UCS load fails when extracting a UCS that came from another system.
bugs.fix: Secure Vault now stores the last good master key, which allows you to set the master key password to be the same as the other device you are importing from, then load the UCS from the other system. If master key decryption fails, the system will load the master key that was in effect before the UCS load was initiated. If that master key matched the master key from the system where the UCS was taken then encrypted attributes in the UCS can be loaded into the configuration.

bugs.title: Output of tmsh show sys crypto master-key
bugs.symptoms: In this release, tmsh show sys crypto master-key has changed and will now display its output as the base 64 encoded form of a SHA512 hash.
bugs.conditions: You will see this when running tmsh show sys crypto master-key, or f5mku -Z, or f5mku -U

bugs.title: MCP debug (/service/mcpd/debug), "Rule checker library has not been initialized"
bugs.symptoms: Running the command 'load sys config' fails with the following message: Rule checker library has not been initialized.
bugs.conditions: At least one of the following: -- The /service/mcpd/debug file is present. -- bigip_base.conf has the following config: sys daemon-log-settings mcpd { log-level debug }
bugs.impact: Cannot load config in debug mode.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, from the shell, call the following: setenforce 0
bugs.fix: Can now load config in debug mode.

bugs.title: SAML XML Canonicalization on BIG-IP as IdP may return invalid value if AuthnRequest is formed in a special way
bugs.symptoms: Signature validation fails on BIG-IP as IDP when AuthnRequest from external SP is signed, and contains a newline/linefeed character after '</Signature>' element
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP is used as IdP - External SP signs AuthnRequests - Signed AuthnRequest contains newline/linefeed character after '</Signature>' element
bugs.impact: WebSSO will fail
bugs.fix: Issue is now fixed.

bugs.title: TCP window scaling is not applied when SYN cookies are active
bugs.symptoms: TCP window scaling is not applied, which can be observed in transmitted packets containing small segments that are about the size of the unscaled window.
bugs.conditions: SYN cookies have been activated.
bugs.impact: Poor performance / throughput.
bugs.fix: The tmm now properly scales the TCP window upon SYN cookie activation.

bugs.title: After restarting bcm56xxd, 5.x interface might show as down.
bugs.symptoms: During internal testing, a very rare condition manifests in which the 5.x interfaces are down after a bcm56xxd restart. Signature in the log file is 01010031:4: Device warning: HSBe2 XLMAC initial recovery failed after 11 retries.
bugs.conditions: This has been seen very rarely and its causes are unknown.
bugs.impact: The 5.x interfaces connect the blades to the backplane so the blades cannot pass messages over the backplane.
bugs.workaround: The command bigstart restart bcm56xxd restarts all interfaces and should bring the 5.x interfaces back up.

bugs.title: ssldump may crash when decrypting bad records
bugs.symptoms: ssldump crashes while decrypting.
bugs.conditions: Using ssldump to decrypt SSL which contains bad records.
bugs.impact: ssldump crashes making it difficult to decrypt SSL data.

bugs.title: Directed failover of HA pair using only hardwire failover will fail
bugs.symptoms: Units configured in a HA pair using only hardwire failover will not be able to use a targeted failover.
bugs.conditions: HA pair configured without network failover but with a hardwire failover. Failover is attempted using one of the 2 following methods: Via GUI Device Management -> Traffic Groups check <traffic group> click "force to standby" again click "force to standby" via tmsh tmsh run sys failover standby device <peer device> traffic-group <traffic group name>
bugs.impact: Failover may fail with the following logs in /var/log/ltm Mar 15 10:27:57 <hostname> notice sod[8214]: 010c0044:5: Command: go standby <traffic group name> <device name> GUI. Mar 15 10:27:57 <hostname> notice sod[8214]: 010c002b:5: Traffic group <traffic group name> received a targeted failover command for <peer mgmt IP>. Mar 15 10:28:00 <hostname> notice sod[8214]: 010c004b:5: Target device <traffic group name> is not responding, cannot failover.
bugs.workaround: Use an alternative failover method: - Device Management > Devices > Force to Standby - Device Management > Traffic Groups > [traffic Group name] > Force to Standby - tmsh run sys failover standby # without device
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now fails over using targeted failover when hardwire failover is configured.

bugs.title: The "Maximum Line Length" violation is not detected in the last line of a websocket frame.
bugs.symptoms: The "Maximum Line Length" setting of the plain text profile does not inspect the last line sent in a web socket. This is true even if only a single line of text is sent to the web socket.
bugs.conditions: Plain text profile used, with Maximum Line Length set
bugs.impact: If a max-length violation occurs on the last line of text, ASM will not flag the violation.
bugs.fix: ASM now performs validation the length of all lines in a web socket when Maximum Line Length is specified in the profile.

bugs.title: Primary slot mismatch after primary cluster member leaves and then rejoins the cluster
bugs.symptoms: Secondary blades in a Viprion system can disagree about the identity of the Primary blade.
bugs.conditions: Viprion chassis with 3 or more blades. If the primary is temporarily isolated from the other blades, a new primary will be elected. When the primary rejoins, the non-primary blades do not correctly switch back to the newly re-elected primary.
bugs.impact: Configuration and status may not be kept properly in sync between blades.
bugs.fix: Secondary blades properly identify the Primary on changes.

bugs.title: Unsupported customization fields are shown for VMware View Logon Page policy agent
bugs.symptoms: The following customization text fields are shown to the user for VMWare View Logon Page policy agent: - Logon Page Input Field #1 - Logon Page Input Field #2 - Logon Page Original URL In fact, those cannot be customized and hence are misleading.
bugs.conditions: User configuring an access policy for native Horizon View clients access through APM.
bugs.impact: User may suppose these fields will affect the Horizon View client look'n'feel although they can't.
bugs.workaround: No workaround, these issues should just be ignored until hidden.
bugs.fix: These fields are to be hidden.

bugs.title: Inbound connections fail to keep port block alive
bugs.symptoms: Connections that use a PBA port block should keep the port block from expiring. However inbound connections to a client using a port block will fail to refresh the block, causing the block to expire pre-maturely. An inbound connection can remain active while the port block has been deleted.
bugs.conditions: An inbound connection with no outbound connections fails to keep a port block alive, resulting in an inbound connection to a client without a corresponding port block.
bugs.impact: When reverse mapping an inbound connection to a subscriber (e.g. trying to find who was using an ip address/port at a particular time), customers may find no corresponding port block, or a port block belonging to another client when the reverse map is performed at a time when the connection is closed.
bugs.workaround: When performing a reverse map, customers should use the start time of a connection to determine which port block was in use.
bugs.fix: Inbound connections properly refresh the port block, preventing premature expiration of the port block.

bugs.title: Accelerated compression segfault when devices are all in error state.
bugs.symptoms: TMM segfaults. Kernel log contains "Uncorrectable Error" and "icp_qa_al err" messages.
bugs.conditions: All physical or virtual devices concurrently enter error state.
bugs.impact: Tmm segfaults and restarts. May require a reboot.
bugs.workaround: Disable QAT compression using tmsh: tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy value softwareonly
bugs.fix: TMM QAT compression driver will not fail if all QAT devices concurrently go down.

bugs.title: Safenet HSM integration failing after it completes.
bugs.symptoms: tmm cannot load the Safenet library, and the following log entry is found in /var/log/auditd/audit.log: denied { read } for pid=4936 comm="tmm" name="libCryptoki2_64.so" dev=dm-1 ino=1441838 scontext=system_u:system_r:tmm_t:s0 tcontext=system_u:object_r:default_t:s0 tclass=lnk_file.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is at least one symlink in the shared/safenet/lunasa/lib/ directory. The safenet-sync.sh script (used to replicate a functioning Safenet HSM installation to a newly-inserted secondary blade) and csyncd conspire to improperly install/fix permissions on the secondary blade if there are symlinks, which results in the Safenet HSM integration failing after it completes, until the user takes appropriate actions.
bugs.impact: Upon failover to secondary blade, the BIG-IP system will be unable to communicate with the configured netHSM.
bugs.workaround: Use chcon and chcon -h to fix any permissions issues. The --reference option can be used on any properly permissioned file in the same directory to do this quickly. For example: chcon -h --reference=libcklog2.so libCryptoki2_64.so.

bugs.title: Question mark prevents TMSH from loading configuration file
bugs.symptoms: When loading system configuration for TMSH, if some properties have the value ? (question mark), TMSH fails to complete the loading.
bugs.conditions: -- Use TMSH to load configuration. -- string, vector of string properties have ? as value. -- ? is the stand-alone value. That is, ? has no characters before or after it and it is not part of a string.
bugs.impact: TMSH fails to load system configuration file
bugs.fix: TMSH now considers escaped question mark as a literal character if the question mark is explicitly escaped (i.e., using quotes, backslash, etc.). Loading system configuration succeeds if all question marks are properly escaped. Escaped question mark now stops displaying help messages in the TMSH, because a literal question mark should not have any special meaning attached to it. This fix does not affect the ways question marks are stored in the TMSH configuration files. Loading existing system configuration files should work properly.
bugs.behavior: TMSH now considers escaped question mark as a literal character if the question mark is explicitly escaped (i.e., using quotes, backslash, etc.), and will successfully load that system configuration if all question marks are properly escaped.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Missing 'gwt' support for urlContentProfiles
bugs.symptoms: A URL's header content profile cannot be set to 'gwt' via REST, and if such a configuration exists on the device, then REST will fail to retrieve the collection.
bugs.conditions: ASM REST is used to configure or inspect URLs on a Security Policy, and GWT profiles are used.
bugs.impact: Unusable REST for the collection.
bugs.fix: GWT profiles on URLs are now correctly supported via REST.

bugs.title: BIG-IP imports delay violations incorrectly, causing wrong policy enforcement
bugs.symptoms: When you import an XML file that contain references to violations in the delay blocking session tracking configuration, extra violations get added to the list.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when importing delay-type violations in ASM
bugs.impact: A very large subset of the violations is added to the policy
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now imports delay-type violations correctly.

bugs.title: tmm crash in FPS plugin
bugs.symptoms: Internal TMM message counter is not decreased correctly.
bugs.conditions: When FPS sources a response (like injected JavaScript). And at some specific circumstances inside TMM (order of traffic events). When there are many requests on a persistent HTTP connection.
bugs.impact: Possible TMM crash.
bugs.workaround: Limit the number of requests on a persistent HTTP connection (e.g. max-requests=64). This prevents the counter - which is 7 bits long - to overflow.

bugs.title: "Auto Apply New Signatures" is unchecked when there are no policies in current partition
bugs.symptoms: On Attack Signature Update page, "Auto Apply New Signatures" is unchecked by default when there are no policies in the currently selected partition.
bugs.conditions: There are no policies in the currently selected partition.
bugs.impact: On Attack Signature Update page, "Auto Apply New Signatures" is unchecked by default.

bugs.title: Traffic Group score formula does not result in unique values.
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, the Traffic Group score for a particular Traffic Group can be identical across devices in a device service cluster, resulting in the Traffic Group becoming Active on more than one device simultaneously.
bugs.conditions: The score is derived from the management-ip and other factors. If the device management-ips are not on the same /24 subnet, the score is not guaranteed to be unique. The score can be observed with the tmsh "run cm watch_trafficgroup_device" command, and in some versions of BIG-IP, the "show cm traffic-group" command.
bugs.impact: When the problem occurs, Traffic Groups will be Active on multiple devices simultaneously. The problem can affect all Traffic Groups.
bugs.workaround: The only solution is to change the management-ip on one of the colliding devices. The workaround is not practical with DHCP, and in many other situations.
bugs.fix: The Active device selection logic has been changed to deterministically choose the Active device location, even in cases with identical static scores.

bugs.title: Memory leak in bd under rare scenario
bugs.symptoms: Under high traffic, bd may leak memory and cause an ASM restart under certain rare conditions
bugs.conditions: ASM enabled and under high traffic
bugs.impact: Causes traffic abort while restart is happening. High swap and memory.
bugs.fix: A memory leak in the bd was fixed.

bugs.title: Resetting crypto client statistics can crash TMM and disrupt traffic handling.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when the statistics of the crypto client is reset when the External Crypto Offload feature is not licensed and the client configured with an unreachable crypto server. The command to reset the statistics of a crypto client is below: tmsh reset-stats sys crypto client [<client name>]
bugs.conditions: With a crypto client configured to target an invalid or unreachable crypto server and the External Crypto Offload (ECO) feature is not licensed, reset the statics of the crypto client.
bugs.impact: Traffic is temporarily disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the External Crypto Offload feature is licensed and/or target a valid crypto server when creating the crypto client.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition network settings aren't pinned correctly on startup
bugs.symptoms: You notice unusually high CPU utilization on Virtual Edition after upgrading to 12.1.0 when compared to a previous release (such as version 11.6.1).
bugs.conditions: This occurs after upgrading to 12.1.0. In Virtual Edition version 12.1.0, there is an issue where network interface IRQs don't get pinned correctly at startup.
bugs.impact: Since CPU0 is unusually high compared to previous releases, upgrading could put Virtual Edition into an overloaded state.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart tmm will start the network interfaces and pin them to the right IRQ.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where interfaces and their IRQs were not configured correctly during system boot.

bugs.title: ASM add_del_internal script does not sync across blades on the VIPRION platform.
bugs.symptoms: ASM add_del_internal script does not sync across blades on the VIPRION platform. The changes are not carried over to the secondary slots. The bd.log contains messages similar to the following: ---- BD_MISC|NOTICE|Apr 04 00:54:28.139|18395|temp_func.c:1899|CHANGED INTERNAL PARAM: [cookie_secure_attr][1] ----
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - Add the following internal parameter: 1.# /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add cookie_secure_attr 2. Run the following command on the primary slot: bigstart restart asm.
bugs.impact: This results in an inconsistent config and state between the primary blade and the secondary blades, which can cause inconsistent responses to the same traffic across blades.
bugs.workaround: Use clsh to set the value using the following command: # clsh /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add cookie_secure_attr 1.
bugs.fix: The VIPRION platform now syncs across blades the internal parameter 'add_del_internal add cookie_secure_attr' after running 'bigstart restart asm' on the primary blade, so inconsistent configurations and traffic handling no longer exist.

bugs.title: bruteForce record selfLink gets corrupted by change to brute force settings in GUI
bugs.symptoms: If you update the brute force settings in the GUI, rest_uuid is updated as well, which breaks the self-link in the iControl REST API
bugs.conditions: Update brute force settings in GUI
bugs.impact: Unique record part updated
bugs.workaround: Update brute force settings using the REST API
bugs.fix: GUI is not changing rest_uuid when brute force settings are updated

bugs.title: SMTPS virtual server with activation-mode allow will RST non-TLS connections with Email bodies with very long lines
bugs.symptoms: Connections to a virtual server that uses an SMTPS profile may be reset with a reset cause of 'Out of memory.'
bugs.conditions: This might occur under the following conditions: -- A virtual server that uses an SMTPS profile with activation-mode set to allow. -- A client connection which does not use TLS that sends a DATA section with a text line that is longer than approximately 8192 characters. 8192 characters is an approximation for the maximum line length. The actual problem length can be affected by the MSS value and the particular way that the TCP traffic is segmented.
bugs.impact: The TCP connection is reset with a reset-cause of Out of memory' and the email will not be delivered.
bugs.fix: A virtual server that uses an SMTPS profile with activation-mode set to allow no longer resets connections when the client does not use STARTTLS and the email body contains very long lines.

bugs.title: Provisioning APM to "none" creates a core file
bugs.symptoms: Provisioning APM level to "none" may result in apmd creating a core file.
bugs.conditions: When the APM service is shut down, the apmd daemon may create a core file.
bugs.impact: Harmless
bugs.workaround: There is no loss in functionality.
bugs.fix: Provisioning APM level to 'none' no longer results in apmd creating a core file.

bugs.title: inter-ability with "delete IPSEC-SA" between AZURE, ASA and BIGIP
bugs.symptoms: Some IKEv1 IPsec vendor implementations (for example Cisco ASA) send a delete SPI message for an IPsec-SA and expect that the sibling IPsec-SA (the SPI in the other direction) will also be deleted by the peer. BIG-IP sends and expect messages with two SPI's inside.
bugs.conditions: An IPsec tunnel between a BIG-IP system and some other vendor may experience this. Azure and Cisco ASA are two such vendors.
bugs.impact: An IPsec tunnel goes down and in some situations may not renegotiate while the BIG-IP believes that the outgoing SPI is still active. The tunnel will stay down until the lifetime of the outbound SA expires.
bugs.workaround: Delete the outbound SA from the BIG-IP using the tmsh command by specifying the related SA: (tmos)# delete net ipsec ipsec-sa ? Properties: "{" Optional delimiter dst-addr Specifies the destination address of the security associations spi Specifies the SPI of the security associations src-addr Specifies the source address of the security associations traffic-selector Specifies the name of the traffic selector
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system will remove both SAs associated with one traffic-selector (tunnel) when the peer sends a delete SPI message.

bugs.title: NTP configuration items are no longer collected by qkview
bugs.symptoms: qkview was collecting the file "/etc/ntp/keys" which in some cases, contains secret keys used for integrity verification of NTP messages.
bugs.conditions: Execute qkview to collect diagnostic information.
bugs.impact: Possibility for keys to be exposed.
bugs.workaround: 1. Do not execute qkview. 2. If executing qkview, do not share this file with untrusted parties.
bugs.fix: With this release, qkview no longer collects this file.

bugs.title: VMware View HTML5 client shipped with Horizon 7 does not work through BIG-IP APM in Chrome/Safari
bugs.symptoms: When using Google Chrome or Safari (WebKit-based) browser to launch VMware View HTML5 client for Horizon 7 from APM webtop, this attempt fails with a blank screen in place of remote desktop session.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP APM configured as PCoIP proxy for Horizon 7. -- APM webtop in which the HTML5 client is used to launch a remote desktop.
bugs.impact: Cannot use HTML5 client. Only native client (Horizon View client) is available.
bugs.workaround: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::header "Origin"] ne "" } { HTTP::header remove "Origin" } }
bugs.fix: VMware View HTML5 client shipped with Horizon 7 now work sthrough BIG-IP APM in Chrome/Safari.

bugs.title: SIP rport value not set in the BIG-IP system response to client RFC 3581
bugs.symptoms: Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) rport value not set in the BIG-IP system response to client.
bugs.conditions: Enabling SIP Via header insertion on the BIG-IP system on SIP MBLB profile or SIP MRF profile and client requests has Via header with rport set. RFC 3581 defines functionality of the rport parameter to request that the server send the response back to the source IP address and port from which the request originated.
bugs.impact: No rport value in the client response. SIP client/server or peer/peer communications do not work as expected. Connections might fail.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule similar to the following to insert the rport value into the header when client requests it: when SIP_REQUEST { set topvia [SIP::via 0] set replaceval ";rport=[UDP::remote_port];" if { $topvia contains ";rport;" } { set newtop [string map ";rport; $replaceval" $topvia] SIP::header insert Via $newtop 0 SIP::header remove Via 1 } }
bugs.fix: Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) rport value is now set as expected in the BIG-IP system response to client, as defined in RFC 3581.

bugs.title: Enhanced implementation of AES in Common Criteria mode
bugs.symptoms: Common Criteria (CC) mode disallows the use of dedicated BIG-IP accelerator. It can be observed that performance of the BIG-IP in CC mode may not be as fast as benchmarks for some implementations AES on CPU.
bugs.conditions: Common Criteria (CC) mode is enabled.
bugs.impact: Lower performance with CBC-based AES ciphersuites.
bugs.fix: Updated AES implementation may achieve higher performance of CBC-based AES ciphersuites.

bugs.title: sod core during upgrade from 10.x to 12.x.
bugs.symptoms: The failover daemon (sod) may core during an upgrade, when the peer device upgrade completes and rejoins the trust.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading a high availability configuration from 10.x to 12.x or later.
bugs.impact: Corefile generated, and system will temporarily go offline, resulting in an interruption of service.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade multiple devices in the high availability configuration from 10.x to a supported 11.x release, and then upgrade to the desired 12.x release.
bugs.fix: The failover daemon (sod) no longer cores during an upgrade, when the peer device upgrade completes and rejoins the trust.

bugs.title: BWC policy object retrieval through XConfig interface fails
bugs.symptoms: BWC policy object retrieval through XConfig interface fails. If the customer uses EM, device discovery failures are noticed as well.
bugs.conditions: BWC policy objects
bugs.impact: BWC policy object retrieval through XConfig interface fails. If the customer uses EM, device discovery failures are noticed as well.

bugs.title: 'ICAP::method <method>' iRule is documented but is read-only
bugs.symptoms: 'ICAP::method' iRule function is documented as 'ICAP::method <REQMOD|RESPMOD>' which is said to get as well as set (modify) the ICAP method type in the ICAP_REQUEST event. Validation has at times rejected an argument, and at times accepted it. In fact the argument is ignored even if validation accepts it: the method type cannot be changed by the iRule. When validation rejects it, the system posts an error similar to the following: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/icap_test] error: /Common/icap_test:2: error: [unexpected extra argument "REQMOD"][ICAP::method "REQMOD"]
bugs.conditions: iRule in ICAP_REQUEST event with 'ICAP::method REQMOD' or 'ICAP::method RESPMOD'.
bugs.impact: Users may attempt to change the method type. Usually the validator rejects it. In some versions the validator accepts it, but the methods only return the existing method type.
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to change the method type with 'ICAP::method <method>'.
bugs.fix: ICAP::method is now documented as simply 'ICAP::method' with no argument, and it simply returns the current method type 'REQMOD' or 'RESPMOD'.

bugs.title: SIP monitor with TLS mode fails to find cert and key files.
bugs.symptoms: SIP monitor with TLS enabled fails to find cert and key in filestore.
bugs.conditions: SIP monitor with TLS mode.
bugs.impact: Cannot create SIP monitor with TLS mode enabled and have the pool correctly checked.
bugs.workaround: Create an external monitor script to invoke the SIP monitor. Supply the correct arguments to the script.
bugs.fix: SIP monitor with TLS mode now finds cert and key files, so you can create SIP monitor with TLS mode enabled and have the pool correctly checked.

bugs.title: FW NAT translation fails if the matched FW NAT rule uses source address list and the source translation object in the rule is configured for dynamic-pat (with deterministic mode)
bugs.symptoms: Firewall NAT translation failures are observed if the pre-translation connection matches a Firewall NAT policy rule that uses source address list to match the incoming source address and the source translation object in the rule is configured to do 'dynamic-pat' with mode = deterministic
bugs.conditions: Following conditions suffice for the issue: a) FW NAT rule has source translation object of type 'dynamic-pat' and mode = deterministic AND b) FW NAT rule has match source address-list only (and no inline source addresses on the match side)
bugs.impact: Translation failure occurs as described resulting in the connection failures.
bugs.workaround: If a FW NAT rule has source translation object with dynamic-pat and deterministic mode, the source address(es) on the match side should be specified as inline address(es) instead of specifying the source address-list with such addresses.
bugs.fix: Fix involves using the addresses specified in the source address list of the FW NAT rule to match incoming connections and perform translation.

bugs.title: Qkview will abort if /shared partition has less than 2GB free space
bugs.symptoms: In order to inform the user that the /shared partition needed to be cleaned up, qkview was checking for at least 2GB of free space. This isn't a hard requirement to build a qkview which potentially could use much less than the 2GB limit. Additionally, some F5 VE systems are shipped with less than 2GB in /shared, thus qkviews cannot be produced.
bugs.conditions: The /shared partition is smaller than 2GB or has less than 2GB free.
bugs.impact: User is unable to create a qkview despite having enough room to build one.
bugs.workaround: Increase the size of /shared so that it has at least 2GB of free space. See https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K14952 for detailed instructions on resizing volumes.
bugs.fix: A warning about having less than 2GB will still be issued, but the qkview will continue to attempt to finish.

bugs.title: Updates to data groups fails with very large numbers of objects
bugs.symptoms: When modifying very large data groups(~33k objects) in the Configuration Utility, updates will fail with an error message: "Unknown Button Pressed."
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP contains a data group that exceeds roughly 33 thousand objects. Updates to particular object will fail.
bugs.impact: Updates to large data groups will fail in the Configuration Utility. Updates to smaller data groups are still possible.
bugs.workaround: Updates to large data groups must be made with tmsh.

bugs.title: Citrix Storefront integration mode with pass-through authentication fails
bugs.symptoms: Citrix Storefront integration mode with pass-through authentication fails. Client fails with error message saying "Authentication service is not reachable"
bugs.conditions: Citrix Storefront integration mode with only pass-through authentication enabled on the Storefront.
bugs.impact: Could not use pass through authentication on the storefront for remote access of the store.
bugs.fix: Passthrough authentication could be used for remote-access of the store.

bugs.title: ASM Disallowed Geolocations without a full country name known to BIG-IP are lost on update.
bugs.symptoms: The mapping of country codes to their names that ASM REST and GUI use is not updated when the GeoIP database is updated, and some values are missing. These country codes can still be added to the list of disallowed locations directly when viewing a request, but do not show up in the GUI or REST. On a subsequent update, country codes are then lost.
bugs.conditions: A country code whose full country name mapping is missing from ASM is added to the list of disallowed Geolocations from the Request Log. The GUI or REST interface is then used to update the list of disallowed geolocations.
bugs.impact: Traffic from the affected disallowed Geolocations are longer blocked.

bugs.title: LTM policy Tcl set-variable action can lead to tmm crash when the payload is synchronously released from below HTTP via an iRule.
bugs.symptoms: Customer may experience unexpected failover.
bugs.conditions: Issues has been found on a virtual server with both an attached iRule and LTM Policy. The iRule calls TCP::collect when connection is accepted, and calls TCP::release at the CLIENT_DATA event. The LTM Policy has a single action to set a tcl set-variable expression.
bugs.impact: Customer may experience unexpected failover
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: Failed to retrieve CRLDP list from client certificate if DirName type is present
bugs.symptoms: Client certification revocation check will fail.
bugs.conditions: Two conditions will trigger this problem: 1. A CRLDP agent is configured in the access policy without server hostname and port, which is needed for DirName type processing. AND 2. At least one DirName type CRLDP is present in the client certification and it is the first in the list.
bugs.impact: Users may fail access policy evaluation when client certification is used.
bugs.workaround: Configure an LDAP server for the CRLDP object. It need not return a valid CRL.

bugs.title: Configuration with LTM policy may fail to load
bugs.symptoms: Load may fail with an error similar to the following: 01070726:3: Policy /Common/Drafts/[name] in partition Common cannot reference policy reference /Common/Drafts/[name] /Common/[virtual server name] in partition [partition]. Note: The named object is in partition Common, but the message will incorrectly specify a different partition.
bugs.conditions: * An LTM policy has been published. * A draft has been created from this policy. * The LTM policy has been associated with a virtual server. * At least one partition other than Common has been created (the policy does not need to be in this partition). * The system is loading the configuration from the text config files (without a binary config file), e.g., as a result of performing a software upgrade or following the directions in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030).
bugs.impact: Configuration will fail to load.
bugs.workaround: Edit the configuration file to remove the draft policy (but not the published one).
bugs.fix: This defect has been resolved and the configuration will now load successfully.

bugs.title: Machine cert checker doesn't work as expected if issuer or AltName is specified
bugs.symptoms: Windows Machine cert checker doesn't work as expected if issuer or AltName is specified. User cannot pass access policy even with valid machine cert. Logs in client PC can be produced, such as: EXCEPTION - CCertCheckCtrl::Verify FindCertificateInStore failed with error code: and CCertCheckCtrl::Verify, Store name:"MY", Store location:"LocalMachine", Subject match FQDN:"1", Allow elevation UI:"0", Serial number(HEX):"", Issuer:"??????????????????????", SubjectAltName:""
bugs.conditions: Issuer or Subject AltName fields are populated. Site recently upgraded to 11.5.4.
bugs.impact: User may not pass policy as expected
bugs.fix: Now Machine Cert checker correctly processes issuer and SAN fields.

bugs.title: 'Enabed' typo in GUI under DoS Profiles --> Application Security --> General Settings
bugs.symptoms: 'Enabed' typo in GUI under DoS Profiles --> Application Security --> General Settings
bugs.conditions: 'Enabed' typo in GUI under DoS Profiles --> Application Security --> General Settings
bugs.impact: 'Enabed' typo in GUI under DoS Profiles --> Application Security --> General Settings
bugs.fix: Fixed a typo in GUI

bugs.title: APM attempts to launch VMware View Linux Desktop from the webtop using HTML5 client which is not supported
bugs.symptoms: VMware View Linux Desktops have been introduced along with the newer HTML5 client which is not supported with BIG-IP APM 11.5.x. However, if user gets entitled to a Linux Desktop when logging in to the APM webtop, they may attempt to launch it and APM will unsuccessfully try to use HTML5 client for it.
bugs.conditions: APM webtop configured for PCoIP Proxy case and VMware View Linux Desktop host assigned to the user.
bugs.impact: User may be confused being shown a desktop they cannot access.
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to connect to Linux Desktops hosts as they are not supported in 11.5.x versions.

bugs.title: Inconsistent display of route-domain information in administrative partitions.
bugs.symptoms: When IpAddress is displayed in GUI and TMSH, there exists some inconsistencies on how the route-domain of the address is displayed. This occurs for virtual servers and pool members.
bugs.conditions: IpAddresses configured for virtual servers and pool members outside the default-route-domain of the administrative partition.
bugs.impact: Although this is only a cosmetic issue, there might be confusion associated with the display inconsistencies.

bugs.title: RADIUS Auth Challenge message with Non-ASCII characters in it is rendered to users in hex-encoded form
bugs.symptoms: If RADIUS sends a challenge with a non-ASCII characters (e.g., from French/Spanish), the user is presented with a hex string in the challenge. For example, the result for the accented characters 'Ã¡, Ã©, Ã­, Ã³' is the hex-encoded string '0xe12c20e92c20ed2c20f3'.
bugs.conditions: Using APM with a RADIUS server that sends a challenge response with non-ASCII characters.
bugs.impact: End user sees a hex string instead of the challenge response.
bugs.workaround: 1. Navigate to Access Policy :: Customization :: Advanced. 2. Locate logon.inc (under Access Policy,Logon Pages, Logon Page in the Form Factor: Full/Mobile Browser frame of the screen. 3. Add code to logon.inc to decode the hex. 4. To do so, follow instructions for either BIG-IP v12.0.0 or for BIG-IP v11.6.0 HF6 to 12.0.0. Search for function OnLoad() in logon.inc. ---In BIG-IP v12.0.0 and later, beginning on line 302 --- 302 function OnLoad() 303 { 304 var header = document.getElementById("credentials_table_header"); 305 var softTokenHeaderStr = getSoftTokenPrompt(); 306 if ( softTokenHeaderStr ) { 307 header.innerHTML = softTokenHeaderStr; 308 } <? // ADD THE FOLLOWING CODE CHANGE INCLUDING THIS LINE if($challenge == 1){?> else if(header.innerHTML.substring(0,2) == "0x"){ var hex = header.innerHTML; var str = ''; var i=0; if (hex.charAt(0) == '0' && hex.charAt(1)== 'x') { i = 2; } var ret; for (; i < hex.length; i += 2) { ret = parseInt(hex.substr(i, 2), 16); if(isNaN(ret)){ break; } else { str += String.fromCharCode(ret); } } if(isNaN(ret)){ ret = hex; } else { ret = str; try{ ret = decodeURIComponent(escape(str)); } catch(e){}; } header.innerHTML =String(ret).replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>'); } <?}?> //END CHANGE --- In BIG-IP v11.6.0 HF6 to 12.0.0, beginning on line 260 --- 260 function OnLoad() 261 { 262 var header = document.getElementById("credentials_table_header"); 263 var softTokenHeaderStr = getSoftTokenPrompt(); 264 if ( softTokenFieldId != "" && softTokenHeaderStr && edgeClientSoftTokenSupport()) { 265 header.innerHTML = softTokenHeaderStr; 266 } <? // ADD THE FOLLOWING CODE CHANGE INCLUDING THIS LINE if($challenge == 1){?> else if(header.innerHTML.substring(0,2) == "0x"){ var hex = header.innerHTML; var str = ''; var i=0; if (hex.charAt(0) == '0' && hex.charAt(1)== 'x') { i = 2; } var ret; for (; i < hex.length; i += 2) { ret = parseInt(hex.substr(i, 2), 16); if(isNaN(ret)){ break; } else { str += String.fromCharCode(ret); } } if(isNaN(ret)){ ret = hex; } else { ret = str; try{ ret = decodeURIComponent(escape(str)); } catch(e){}; } header.innerHTML =String(ret).replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>'); } <?}?> //END CHANGE

bugs.title: No way to control how aborted iRules log messages are generated and sent to /var/log/ltm.
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to control the rate at which aborted iRules log messages are generated and sent to /var/log/ltm rule-aborted log messages similar to the following: info tmm[19392]: 01220009:6: Pending rule /Common/abort_rule <HTTP_REQUEST_SEND> aborted for <IP address>
bugs.conditions: Viewing ltm log messages.
bugs.impact: Many "pending rule aborted" messages in ltm log.
bugs.workaround: Syslog filter can be created to filter the unwanted log messages from /var/log/ltm. modify syslog { ... include " filter f_local0 { facility(local0) and not match (\"Pending rule /Common/_sys_APM_Exchange <HTTP_REQUEST> aborted for\"); }; " ... }
bugs.fix: This release adds a bigdb variable to control how aborted iRules log messages are generated and sent to /var/log/ltm. The new option can be configured either via a sys db or using tmsh: sys db: tmm.tcl.rule.aborted.log.ratio tmsh: ltm global-settings rule rule-aborted-log-ratio The options are as follows: - 0 Logging is disabled. - 1 (default) every aborted iRule occurrence is logged. - > 1 only one in N aborted execution is logged, in addition to a message indicating how many previous log messages were suppressed.
bugs.behavior: This release introduce a configuration option to control the rate at which aborted iRules log messages are generated and sent to /var/log/ltm. The option can be configured as follows: - 0 Logging is disabled - 1 (default) every aborted iRule occurrence is logged - > 1 only one in N aborted execution is logged, in addition to a message indicating how many previous log messages were suppressed. The new option can be configured either via a sys db or using tmsh: Sys db: tmm.tcl.rule.aborted.log.ratio tmsh: ltm global-settings rule rule-aborted-log-ratio

bugs.title: Network Map Pool Member Parent Node Name display and Pool Member hyperlink
bugs.symptoms: The Network Map was not displaying the correct node name and the link was taking you to an incorrect pool member.
bugs.conditions: Create a pool and pool member from a FQDN node. Add that pool to a virtual server. From the Network Map page the pool member link does not show the FQDN making it hard to tell what pool member it is. When you click on the pool member hyperlink it takes you to the incorrect pool member.
bugs.impact: This causes confusion because the pool members are difficult to identify without the FQDN and the link takes you to the incorrect pool member.

bugs.title: Permissions problem on /var/log/sa6
bugs.symptoms: Non-root users or processes cannot read or write from /var/log/sa6 directory because of not having the executable bit set (0755 permissions).
bugs.conditions: Non-root users attempting to read or write from /var/log/sa6 directory.
bugs.impact: Processes not run by root cannot read or write to this directory and permissions' errors abound.
bugs.workaround: As root, run the following command: chmod 755 /var/log/sa6 /var/log/sa. Once the directory has the correct permissions, the errors disappear.

bugs.title: BGP peer-group members address-family configuration not saved to configuration
bugs.symptoms: Deactivation of the ipv6 address-family for an IPv6 BGP neighbor that is a member of a peer group may be removed when the configuration is reloaded or the system restarts.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 BGP neighbors in a peer group Individual group members with different address-family configurations than the peer-group
bugs.impact: BGP behavior may change after reboot
bugs.workaround: If a neighbor must have different behavior than other peer group members it can be removed from the peer group and configured individually.
bugs.fix: BGP address-family configuration is now correctly saved and reloaded for neighbors belonging to a peer-group.

bugs.title: Incorrect error handling in HTTP cookie results in core when TMM runs out of memory
bugs.symptoms: If an under provisioned TMM runs out of memory, then this may result in allocation failures. Incorrect error handling of allocation failures in HTTP cookie code results in TMM core.
bugs.conditions: Cookie persistence with encryption required is enabled on the virtual. If an under provisioned TMM runs out of memory, then this may result in allocation failures.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fix error handling in HTTP cookie code. Allocation errors result in connection resets as opposed to core due to assert.

bugs.title: Malicious words alerts are sent with missing HTML.
bugs.symptoms: Malicious words alerts are sent with missing HTML.
bugs.conditions: Malicious words alert is sent.
bugs.impact: Difficult to investigate cause of alerts.
bugs.workaround: Implement beforeLoad function that attaches base64 encoded page HTML to all alert requests.

bugs.title: RatePaceMaxRate functionality does not work for the TCP flows where the round-trip time (RTT) is less than 6ms.
bugs.symptoms: RatePaceMaxRate functionality does not work for the TCP flows where the round-trip time (RTT) is less than 6ms. That results in sending data at higher rates than specified Max Rate.
bugs.conditions: RTT is less than 6ms.
bugs.impact: Packet loss might happen (queue overflow) due to sending at higher data rate than the specified max rate.
bugs.fix: RatePaceMaxRate works as expected, irrespective of latency.

bugs.title: SQL monitors 'count' config value does not work as expected.
bugs.symptoms: SQL monitors 'count' config value does not work as expected.
bugs.conditions: SQL monitor in use with the 'count' config value specified. The 'count' value is intended to record the number of times the connection to the back-end database is re-used before it is disconnected. However, the value is not correctly recording the number in this release.
bugs.impact: SQL monitor might use a 'count' value that is incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Add 101 to the desired value. For example, if the desired count is '5', use '106' instead.

bugs.title: PPTP log entries now includes route-domain information
bugs.symptoms: Log entries for PPTP does not include route-domain
bugs.conditions: Logging for PPTP
bugs.impact: Log entries for PPTP
bugs.fix: Log entries for PPTP now includes route-domain
bugs.behavior: HSL Log entries for PPTP now includes route-domain in from (client) and nat fields.

bugs.title: HTTP/ramcache2 and RAM Cache are not compatible.
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server fails some requests where the response is served from cache.
bugs.conditions: If a virtual server has either SPDY or HTTP/2 enabled, it might fail requests that would normally be served from RAM cache. Also, a normal HTTP virtual server that has an iRule attached that responds to the HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE event might give errors to Tcl commands that attempt to access the response headers. Certain filters and plugins that required access to the response headers might also fail in unexpected ways.
bugs.impact: Errors in certain TCL commands or failed requests.
bugs.workaround: Disable CACHE via an iRule: when HTTP_REQUEST { if {[HTTP2::active]} { CACHE::disable } }
bugs.fix: HTTP/ramcache2 and RAM Cache are now compatible, and documents served from cache always have accessible headers now. Note: This change introduces a formatting variance in the response headers. Now, certain header values are right justified, where previously, they were left justified. This includes the Age and Content-Length headers, though the Connection header remains left justified. Here is an iRule to remove this white space on cache service: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { set age_val [string trim [HTTP::header value Age]] set con_len [string trim [HTTP::header value Content-Length]] HTTP::header remove Age HTTP::header remove Content-Length HTTP::header insert Age "$age_val" HTTP::header insert Content-Length "$con_len" }

bugs.title: Session variable substitutions are logged
bugs.symptoms: With the log level set to debug, session variable substitutions are logged, including the encrypted password if you are substituting the password variable. You may see the following logs: debug apmd[3531]: 01490000:7: Util.cpp func: "ScanReplaceSessionVar()" line: 608 Msg: data: '%{session.logon.last.password}' start_pos: 0, count: 30 on 'session.logon.last.password' with the encrypted password logged
bugs.conditions: APM Access Policy log level set to debug, and session variable substitution is performed.
bugs.impact: Session variable substitution should not be logged, even if it is secure.
bugs.workaround: Set log level to informational or notice for normal operations. Logging at debug level is not recommended unless absolutely needed for specific troubleshooting as it adversely affects system performance.
bugs.fix: Session variable substitutions are no longer logged.

bugs.title: The tmm might crash with a segfault.
bugs.symptoms: The tmm might crash with a segfault.
bugs.conditions: Using IPsec with hardware encryption.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: IPsec is configured with hardware encryption error now returns an error code when appropriate, and manages the error as expected, so tmm no longer crashes with a segfault.

bugs.title: View HTML5 client doesn't work when APM is set to offload SSL from VCS
bugs.symptoms: For the new integration of VMware View HTML5 client applicable to HTML5 clients v2.6 or later, it does not work if APM was configured for SSL offloading to the View Connection Server.
bugs.conditions: APM configured for PCoIP proxy case using APM webtop and VMware View HTML5 client. Access to the VMware View backend is configured to take place over plain HTTP (SSL offloading mode) rather than HTTPS (SSL bridging mode).
bugs.impact: User cannot launch VMware View HTML5 client from APM webtop in case of SSL offloading mode.
bugs.workaround: Use SSL bridging mode to the backend.
bugs.fix: Now APM supports launching VMware View HTML5 client when SSL offloading mode is used.

bugs.title: Modifications to custom provisioning ratios via GUI are not saved in System :: Resource Provisioning.
bugs.symptoms: Modifications to custom provisioning ratios via GUI are not saved in System :: Resource Provisioning.
bugs.conditions: Use the GUI to customize any of the modules provisioned.
bugs.impact: Cannot customize provisioned ratios using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to change the ratios.
bugs.fix: Modifications to custom provisioning ratios via GUI are now saved in System :: Resource Provisioning.

bugs.title: Tcl evaluation outside of an iRule can lead to tmm crash when the payload is synchronously released from below HTTP via an iRule.
bugs.symptoms: Tcl expression evaluations (outside of an iRule) can lead to tmm crash when the payload is synchronously released from below HTTP via an iRule. A couple of examples where Tcl expressions are evaluated outside the context of an iRule include the tcl-setvar action of LTM Policy and the Request Header Insert feature of the HTTP profile.
bugs.conditions: Issue has been found on a virtual server with both an attached iRule and LTM Policy. The iRule calls TCP::collect when connection is accepted, and calls TCP::release at the CLIENT_DATA event. The LTM Policy has a single action to set a tcl set-variable expression.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tcl evaluation outside of an iRule no longer leads to tmm crash when the payload is synchronously released from below HTTP via an iRule.

bugs.title: During upgrade, configuration fails to load due to clientssl profile with empty cert/key configuration.
bugs.symptoms: During upgrade, configuration fails to load due to invalid clientssl profile cert/key configuration. The validation to verify whether at least one valid key/cert pair exists in clientssl profiles was enforced in software versions through 11.5.0. This validation was not in effect in versions 11.5.1, 11.5.2, and 11.5.3. The lack of validation resulted in invalid clientssl profiles (those containing empty key/certs or a cert/key of 'default'). When you upgrade such a configuration to 11.5.4 or later, you will receive a validation error, and the configuration will fail to load after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when all the below conditions are met. 1. You have a clientssl profile in a configuration from a version without validation (that is, 11.5.1, 11.5.2, or 11.5.3). 2. The clientssl profile in the configuration has an empty cert/key, or a cert/key of 'default'. 3. You upgrade to a version that has the cert/key validation (specifically, 11.5.4, 11.6.0, 11.6.1, and versions 12.1.0 and later).
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load. The system posts an error message that might appear similar to one of the following: -- 01070315:3: profile /Common/my_client_ssl requires a key Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. -- 01071ac9:3: Unable to load the certificate file () - error:2006D080:BIO routines:BIO_new_file:no such file. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this situation, modify the configuration file before upgrading: 1. Check the config file /config/bigip.conf. 2. Identify the clientssl profile without a cert/key. For example, it might look similar to the following: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/cssl_no-cert-key2 { app-service none cert none cert-key-chain { "" { } } chain none defaults-from /Common/clientssl inherit-certkeychain false key none passphrase none } Note: The profile might have cert-key-chain name but not the cert/key. In other words, it could also appear similar to the following example: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/cssl_no-cert-key2 { app-service none cert none cert-key-chain { default { } } chain none defaults-from /Common/clientssl inherit-certkeychain false key none passphrase none } 3. Remove the clientssl profile from /config/bigip.conf. 4. Run the command: tmsh load sys conf. 5. Re-create the clientssl profiles you need.

bugs.title: SCTP tmm crash with virtual server destination.
bugs.symptoms: Rare configuration with SCTP can cause TMM core.
bugs.conditions: Complex configurations including wildcards, virtual servers and SCTP profiles.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a rare SCTP tmm crash with virtual server destination when using complex configurations including wildcards, virtual servers and SCTP profiles.

bugs.title: Standby device will respond to the ARP of the SCTP multihoming alternate address
bugs.symptoms: When there is a SCTP connection established, the router will request the ARP for the client-side multi-homing alternate address, but the standby device will reply to the ARP request as well.
bugs.conditions: When an SCTP profile has at least one alternate-address configured, and is used in an high availability (HA) scenario, this issue will manifest.
bugs.impact: Traffic for the alternate-addresses may be directed to the wrong device in an HA group. The multi-homing function will fail as the alternate connection cannot established on the standby device.
bugs.workaround: Do not use a VLAN address as an alternate address. Use only routed addresses, and route those addresses to the floating Self-IP address of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: SCTP multihoming has been fixed to work correctly when used in a high availability setup with VLAN addresses

bugs.title: Dynamic toggling for HSB hardware checksum validation
bugs.symptoms: Disabling hardware checksum validation on BIG-IP requires manually editing a config tcl file and restarting TMM.
bugs.conditions: - Configuring HSB hardware checksum validation.
bugs.fix: HSB hardware checksum validation can now be configured by using the new DB variable "tmm.hsb.hwchecksumvalidation". When the value of this DB variable is changed, the HSB will be updated immediately without requiring a TMM restart.

bugs.title: SIP monitor in TLS mode marks pool member down after positive response.
bugs.symptoms: SIP monitor in TLS mode marks pool member down after positive response. The SIP monitor in TLS mode is constantly marked down.
bugs.conditions: SIP monitor configured in TLS mode. Server does not send close_notify alert in response to the monitor's close_notify request.
bugs.impact: Unable to monitor the status of the TLS SIP server.
bugs.fix: SIP monitor in TLS mode now marks pool member up after positive response. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Incorrect result returned from IP::tos iRule in the FLOW_INIT event.
bugs.symptoms: The result returned from the "IP::tos" iRule in the FLOW_INIT event is always zero (Normal-Service), even when the actual packet from the client has TOS set to a different value.
bugs.conditions: Calling the IP::tos iRule from within a FLOW_INIT event handler for a virtual server always returns zero. The following iRule demonstrates the issue: when FLOW_INIT { log local0. "TOS from [IP::client_addr] is [IP::tos]" } when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { log local0. "TOS from [IP::client_addr] is [IP::tos]" } The logs will show that the IP::tos value is always 0 at FLOW_INIT, and always correct at CLIENT_ACCEPTED.
bugs.impact: Cannot make the correct service or routing decision at FLOW_INIT, based on the TOS provided in the initial packet in the flow.
bugs.fix: The IP::tos iRule now correctly returns the TOS value from the initial client packet initiating a flow in the FLOW_INIT event handler.

bugs.title: Inbound connections are reset prematurely when zombie timeout is configured.
bugs.symptoms: When an LSN pool is configured in PBA mode with a non-zero zombie timeout, inbound connections are killed and reset prematurely, often in a matter of seconds.
bugs.conditions: PBA mode configured on the pool, and zombie_timeout set to a non-zero value.
bugs.impact: Inbound connections to PBA pools with a zombie timeout configured may not be usable.
bugs.fix: Inbound connections are no longer reset when zombie_timout is configured to a non-zero value.

bugs.title: Allow iQuery to negotiate up to version TLS1.2
bugs.symptoms: big3d accepts only TLS1.0, and gtmd offers only TLS1.0 during iQuery SSL handshake. iQuery does not negotiate up to TLS 1.2.
bugs.conditions: Establishing iQuery connections.
bugs.impact: The older, less secure TLS1.0 version is the only possible iQuery connection.
bugs.fix: big3d now accepts, and gtmd now offers up to, TLS1.2 in iQuery handshakes. TLS1 and TLS1.1 are still accepted by both ends of the iQuery connection (gtmd and big3d) to enable older clients (gtmd) to connect to newer servers (big3d) and vice versa.
bugs.behavior: big3d now accepts TLS1.2 in iQuery handshakes, and gtmd now offers up to TLS1.2.

bugs.title: Chassis Name and Type are blank in "tmsh show sys hardware"
bugs.symptoms: As of BIG-IP v12.1.0, the output of the "tmsh show sys hardware" command includes the "Chassis Name" and "Chassis Type" fields under the "Chassis Information" section. On VIPRION blades, these fields report the Marketing Name and Platform ID of the VIPRION chassis in which the blade is installed. On BIG-IP appliances, the "Chassis Name" and "Chassis Type" fields are not populated.
bugs.conditions: This affects the following BIG-IP appliances running BIG-IP v12.1.0 or later: BIG-IP 1600, 3600, 3900, 6900, 8900, 8950, 11000, 11050 BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series, 5000-/7000-series, 10000-/12000-series
bugs.impact: Cosmetic. Non-applicable fields contain no information.

bugs.title: TMM may restart when SAML SLO is performed after APM session is closed
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core when user performs SAML SLO on external to BIG-IP SP/IdP, and BIG-IP's APM session is no longer valid.
bugs.conditions: - User initiated SAML SLO on external SAML provider, and external provider redirect users to BIG-IP with SLO request. - User does not have a valid session on BIG-IP when SLO request is received.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable SAML SLO by removing SLO request/response URLs from configuration
bugs.fix: TMM will no longer restart in the case described above.

bugs.title: REST API does not allow modification of AFM address list
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to modify an existing address list with an API call. You can only overwrite the whole list.
bugs.conditions: You wish to modify an existing AFM address list using the REST API
bugs.impact: The only option is to replace the entire list.

bugs.title: MAC Edge client selects wrong network access resource if webtop contains multiple resources
bugs.symptoms: MAC edge client chooses last network access resource instead of first one, if multiple network access resources are configured on the webtop. Windows edge client selects the first resource. This may result in user confusion if multiple NA resources are configured
bugs.conditions: All conditions must be met -Multiple network access resources are configured on webtop -User uses MAC edge client to establish a network access connection
bugs.impact: User confusion and user may connect to incorrect network access resource
bugs.workaround: Any of the following workarounds would work 1) Do not configure multiple NA access resources 2) Create an access policy path which assigns correct NA resource based on client detection 3) Use Browser to establish NA connection

bugs.title: While adding GTM server, failure to configure new IP on existing server leads to gtmd core
bugs.symptoms: gtmd core with SIGSEGV in selfip_needs_xlation.
bugs.conditions: No GTM server object configured with existent selfip.
bugs.impact: gtmd cores. GTM unable to respond to DNS queries. DNS traffic disrupted while gtmd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure the GTM server object with an existent selfip. For more information, see K15671: The BIG-IP GTM system must use a local self IP address to define a server to represent the BIG-IP GTM system at https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K15671
bugs.fix: gtmd will not core.

bugs.title: IP exceptions may have issues with route domain
bugs.symptoms: The IP exception feature doesn't work as expected.
bugs.conditions: There are many defined same IPs but with different route domain. There were config changes to these IPs regarding their exception properties.
bugs.impact: An ignored IP is not ignored etc.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with IPs and route domain.

bugs.title: GTM auto discovery problem with EHF for ID574052
bugs.symptoms: After applying EHF9-685.88-ENG to CRCGTMCS101, many WideIPs such as CRT-LEGAL-SERVICE.gslb.global or OneEvent.gslb.global are unexpectedly status Checking instead of Available.
bugs.conditions: After applying EHF9-685.88-ENG
bugs.impact: Many WideIPs such as CRT-LEGAL-SERVICE.gslb.global or OneEvent.gslb.global are unexpectedly status Checking instead of Available.
bugs.workaround: Skip to the next Eng HF v11.4.1-hf10/hotfix/HF10-690.10-ENG
bugs.fix: This problem only occurs with the one faulty EHF9-685.88-ENG and does not occur anywhere else.

bugs.title: LCD Checkmark button does not always bring up clearing prompt on VIPRION blades.
bugs.symptoms: Pressing the LCD checkmark button does not always bring up clearing prompt on VIPRION blades.
bugs.conditions: Pressing the LCD's checkmark button to clear an alert on VIPRION blades.
bugs.impact: Cannot clear the alert using the LCD.
bugs.workaround: Press the checkmark button followed by the left or right arrow buttons.
bugs.fix: In this release, unneeded LCD updates that might have clogged the message channel have been optimized, and the keypress passed along at a later time, so it is not lost. So pressing the LCD checkmark button now correctly brings up clearing prompt on VIPRION blades.

bugs.title: SMB monitor fails due to internal configuration issue
bugs.symptoms: SMB monitor fails due to internal configuration issue
bugs.conditions: Configure the SMB monitor
bugs.impact: SMB monitor fails to execute
bugs.fix: Fixed an internal configuration issue so that the SMB monitor will load properly

bugs.title: LTM SSL should do a full handshake when peer attempts to resume a session with a different client TLS version.
bugs.symptoms: When client hello reuses a previous session ID, and changes the SSL version from TLS 1.0 to TLS 1.2 in the handshake layer, but keeps the TLS 1.0 in the record layer, LTM accepts the session resumption, but changes the version of the record layer to TLS 1.2 as well, and finishes the resumption. However, the client aborts the connection due to the record layer version change.
bugs.conditions: When SSL client attempts to resume a session, but the client_version has changed.
bugs.impact: LTM accepts the session resumption, but changes the version of the record layer to TLS 1.2, and finishes the resumption. However, the client aborts the connection due to the record layer version change.
bugs.fix: Instead of accept the session resumption, LTM SSL will do a SSL full handshake.

bugs.title: TMM crashes upon SSL handshake cancellation.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes upon SSL handshake cancellation.
bugs.conditions: SSL handshake cancellation.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when SSL handshake is canceled.

bugs.title: bgpd crashes when ip extcommunity-list standard with route target(rt) and Site-of-origin (soo) parameters are configured
bugs.symptoms: bgpd daemon crashes
bugs.conditions: bgp extended-asm-cap is configured before configuring ip extcommunity-list standard with rt and soo fields.
bugs.impact: bgpd daemon crashes leading to route loss and traffic loss.
bugs.fix: bgpd does not crash when both bgp extended-asm-cap and ip extcommunity-list standard with rt and soo parameters are configured.

bugs.title: Persist lookups fail for source_addr with match-across-virtuals when multiple entries exist with different pools.
bugs.symptoms: Persist lookups fail for source_addr with match-across-virtual servers when multiple entries exist for the client, but pointing to different pools.
bugs.conditions: 'Match_across_virtual' enabled. Multiple persistence entries for a client address exist, and some of these persistence entries point to poolmembers from different pools. Some of these poolmembers do not belong to any of the current virtual server's pools.
bugs.impact: Source address persistence fails for this client, even though there is a valid persistence entry that can be used.
bugs.fix: Persist lookups now succeed for source_addr with match-across-virtual servers when multiple entries exist with different pools.

bugs.title: Webtop doesn't notify user about ended session when F5 VPN application is used
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer based VPN solution will notify webtop window when APM session expires. New F5 VPN based solution (for Chrome and Firefox) has a technical limitation doing that, thus Webtop window still indicates webtop not a logout page like in case with Internet Explorer.
bugs.conditions: * Chrome or Firefox is used * Windows, Mac or Linux machine is used * User establishes VPN using F5 VPN application * Session expires on server
bugs.impact: When the session expires/killed by an admin F5 VPN app exists leaving Webtop untouched. This may confuse a user that the session is still valid
bugs.fix: Session validity is now performed when a user clicks on resource tile on webtop. If session is expired, webtop will redirect to logout page

bugs.title: False alarm on LCD indicating bad fan
bugs.symptoms: During some blade power ON conditions, a false alarm message is displayed on the LCD on the chassis bezel. This alarm indicates that several chassis fans are bad, however in reality the fans are not bad. Typically, the messages look like this: slot8/localhost emerg system_check[15535]: 010d0005:0: Chassis fan 2: status (0) is bad. slot8/localhost emerg system_check[15535]: 010d0005:0: Chassis fan 3: status (0) is bad. slot8/localhost emerg system_check[15535]: 010d0005:0: Chassis fan 4: status (0) is bad. slot8/localhost emerg system_check[15535]: 010d0005:0: Chassis fan 5: status (0) is bad.
bugs.conditions: Erroneous fan warnings may occur when a blade is inserted into a VIPRION 4800 chassis.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The user may experience concern over the false alarms.
bugs.workaround: Press green check button on the front of chassis bezel to clear the alarm.

bugs.title: Add support for Thales version 12.10.01
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP versions prior to 13.0 do not support Thales version 12.10.01
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP versions prior to 13.0
bugs.impact: If you have upgraded your Thales version, older versions of BIG-IP may not function correctly.
bugs.fix: This release adds support for Thales version 12.10.01.

bugs.title: warning: HSBe2 XLMAC initial recovery failed after 11 retries.
bugs.symptoms: ltm log contains multiple instances of the following message on VIPRION B4450 blades: warning: HSBe2 XLMAC initial recovery failed after 11 retries.
bugs.conditions: This often happens when VIPRION 4480 or 4800 chassis with B4450 blades is rebooting.
bugs.impact: No operation impact. This is a cosmetic message that you can safely ignore.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This message is cosmetic only.
bugs.fix: A more robust XLMAC recovery mechanism has been implemented which reduces the maximum retries to four. It does not completely eliminate this warning message (HSBe2 XLMAC initial recovery failed after 11 retries), but its frequency is greatly reduced.

bugs.title: Set execute permission on /var/lib/waagent
bugs.symptoms: Due to recent changes of the build process /var/lib/waagent didn't have proper execute permission set. This caused failure in executing user custom scripts during deploying.
bugs.conditions: First deployment of VM in Azure, which requires executing custom scripts.
bugs.impact: Custom scripts cannot be executed.
bugs.fix: Properly set execute permissions to /var/lib/waagent directory.

bugs.title: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt failure on base load
bugs.symptoms: On initial boot of VIPRION blade, before the blade is licensed, you may see the following error message in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[5015]: 010713d0:3: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt failure - decrypt failure
bugs.conditions: It is not yet known what the conditions are that trigger this error.
bugs.impact: This occurs on initial boot of the VIPRION blade, prior to licensing the device. After licensing, this error does not occur.
bugs.workaround: None. If this error is reported on first boot, but can otherwise be licensed, it can be safely ignored. If this occurred after loading a ucs file, see SOL13132: Backing up and restoring BIG-IP configuration files at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/13000/100/sol13132.html for more information on this error.

bugs.title: vCMP Guest VLAN traffic failure after MCPD restarts on hypervisor.
bugs.symptoms: On the affected slot, the vCMP guest is unable to pass traffic to or from the VLANs. If the guest has multiple slots, the CMP state logged in /var/log/tmm on that slot differs from the CMP state logged by other slots of the same guest. In the vCMP guest, 'tmsh show net interface -hidden' shows 0.x interfaces for the affected slot that differ from the 0.x interfaces shown by 'tmsh show vcmp guest all-properties' on the vCMP hypervisor for the same guest slot.
bugs.conditions: The MCPD daemon on one of the blades of the vCMP hypervisor crashes or restarts.
bugs.impact: The vCMP guests that are still running since before the MCPD daemon restarted may be unable to communicate to VLAN networks. Incoming traffic may also be affected, even though the vCMP guest has other functional slots to process traffic.
bugs.workaround: On the hypervisor, modify the vCMP guest configuration to not run on the affected slot. Wait to confirm the vCMP guest has stopped on the affected slot. Then modify the vCMP guest to run on the previously affected slot. Alternatively, modify the vCMP guest to the Configured state, and wait to confirm the vCMP guest has stopped on all slots. Then return the vCMP guest to the Deployed state.

bugs.title: Multiple iRule proc names might clash, causing the wrong rule to be executed.
bugs.symptoms: Multiple iRule proc names might clash, causing the wrong rule to be executed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is an iRule configured with more than one proc, which might cause the wrong proc to get executed.
bugs.impact: The call proc might execute the wrong proc.
bugs.fix: Multiple iRules configured with more than one proc no longer cause the wrong proc to get executed.

bugs.title: Improved SMTPS reset cause codes
bugs.symptoms: All SMTPS TCP resets issue the same message from the same code line, making determining the exact cause difficult, if not impossible.
bugs.conditions: An exceptional situation (such as out of memory, missing STARTTLS command, or other internal error) occurs that causes the SMTPS hudfilter to tear down a connection.
bugs.impact: Usability - the connection will be torn down with only a vague indication of why.
bugs.fix: Each connection teardown message is now unique, making it easier to determine the cause from the associated logs.
