bugs.title: LTM fastL4 DNS virtual server: first A query dropped when A and AAAA requested at the same time with same source IP:port
bugs.symptoms: LTM fastL4 DNS virtual server or SNAT: first A query dropped when A and AAAA requested at the same time with same source IP:port.
bugs.conditions: A and AAAA DNS Query requested at the same time with the same source IP and Port.
bugs.impact: A Type DNS Query dropped intermittently.
bugs.workaround: Configure a standard virtual server with UDP profile for the traffic instead of using fastl4 or snat.
bugs.fix: Type A requests no longer dropped when A and AAAA DNS Query requested at the same time with the same source IP and Port.

bugs.title: Clearing alerts from the LCD while the host is down will re-display the alerts on the LCD when the host comes up
bugs.symptoms: If the LCD visible alerts are cleared using the LCD menu while the Host is down, then when the host is brought back up the LCD will re-display any alerts that were generated after the host went down. Alerts generated after a the Host is down are persistent and when the host comes up it will harvest those alerts and re-display them on the LCD. Alarm LED may be re-initialized to an unexpected state.
bugs.conditions: Alerts generated while the host is down and alerts are cleared using the LCD menu interface.
bugs.impact: Alerts are re-displayed on the LCD when the host comes back up. And the alarm LED may indicate an alarm that was thought previously cleared.
bugs.workaround: Do not clear the alerts from the LCD interface while the host is down.

bugs.title: Improve detection of browser capabilities
bugs.symptoms: Browsers can override native functions, and manipulate the PBD capabilities test.
bugs.conditions: 1. Proactive Bot defense is on. 2. Attacker override its native functions.
bugs.impact: Malicious browsers can go undetected by PBD.
bugs.fix: Check that majority of browsers native functions are not overridden.

bugs.title: False positive "failed to unseal" Source Integrity alerts from old versions of Internet Explorer
bugs.symptoms: Large numbers of "failed to unseal" Source Integrity alerts.
bugs.conditions: Source integrity feature enabled. Clients using Internet Explorer 8 to 10.
bugs.impact: High number of false positive alerts in alert dashboard.
bugs.workaround: Create alert dashboard signature to ignore source integrity alerts containing "failed to unseal" and Internet Explorer 8 to 10 user agent.
bugs.fix: Fixed parsing in relevant browsers.

bugs.title: Attack prevention isn't escalating under some conditions in session opening mitigation
bugs.symptoms: Attack is detected and isn't escalating in session opening
bugs.conditions: A session opening attack, challenges are being answered by the attacker.
bugs.impact: The attack continues.
bugs.workaround: Configure the attack prevention as rate limit.
bugs.fix: Fixed attack escalation in some cases on session opening.

bugs.title: SSL resumed connections may fail during mirroring
bugs.symptoms: SSL resumed connections when using SSL mirroring may fail during mirroring. This could result in SSL connections being unable to recover after failover.
bugs.conditions: Mirroring enabled on virtual with an associated client-ssl profile.
bugs.impact: SSL connections unable to recover after failover.
bugs.workaround: Disable session cache to prevent connections from resuming.

bugs.title: TMM may crash with traffic to floating self-ip in range overlapping route via unreachable gw
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue TMM may crash in some specific scenarios if there is an overlapping and more specific route to the floating self-IP range configured on the unit.
bugs.conditions: - Unit configured with a floating self-IP and allow-service != none. - More specific route exists via GW to the self-IP. - Configured gateway for the overlapping route is unreachable. - Ingress traffic to the floating self-IP.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid the use of routes overlapping with configured floating self-IPs.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when floating self IPs are configured with more specific overlapping routes.

bugs.title: Pool licensing fails in some KVM/OpenStack environments
bugs.symptoms: Licensing a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) from BIG-IQ, BIG-IQ can fail. The system posts the following error in /var/log/ltm: Dossier error 16.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when BIG-IQ is used to license the BIG-IP VE instance.
bugs.impact: From BIG-IQ, the licensing operation will appear as a successful operation, however, BIG-IP VE will not be licensed.
bugs.fix: Licensing a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) from BIG-IQ in OpenStack and/or KVM environments completes with success on BIG-IQ and BIG-IP.

bugs.title: DNS protocol default profiles can be deleted after being modified.
bugs.symptoms: A protocol default profile can be deleted in some cases.
bugs.conditions: The protocol default profile is not a parent to any other profile and has been modified.
bugs.impact: Default protocol profile can be deleted. If a default profile has been deleted, the config might get into an invalid state, and a config reload might be necessary.
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to delete a protocol default profile.
bugs.fix: Default profiles are not deletable under any circumstances.

bugs.title: Monitor instances being deleted in peer unit after sync.
bugs.symptoms: Monitor instances being deleted in peer unit after sync.
bugs.impact: Unknown

bugs.title: GTM is Re-ordering pools when adding pool including order designation
bugs.symptoms: GTM re-orders, including the "0" order when adding the pool with specific order designation.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when adding pools with a specified order.
bugs.impact: This changes the pool order unexpectedly which will affect Load balancing using global-availability.

bugs.title: Observe "err bcm56xxd' liked log from /var/log/ltm
bugs.symptoms: Some "err bcm56xxd" log is observed from /var/log/ltm that read "err bcm56xxd[10968]: 012c0012:3: bs_module_do_precond:No preconditioning provided for module on port 3/5.0"
bugs.conditions: This occurs when during system start.
bugs.impact: The error is benign and can be ignored.
bugs.fix: The "No preconditioning provided for module" message is now logged at the info level.

bugs.title: IPv6 fragments are dropped when packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 fragments are dropped when packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Packet filtering is enabled and the system is processing IPv6 fragments.
bugs.impact: IPv6 fragments with a non-zero offset are lost.
bugs.workaround: Disable packet filtering.
bugs.fix: IPv6 fragments are no longer dropped when packet filtering is enabled.

bugs.title: BIG-IP CPU utilization can be high even when all bad actors are detected and mitigated
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP CPU utilization can be excessively high even after mitigating bad actors.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when Bad Actor detection is used
bugs.impact: CPU utilization will be higher than expected.
bugs.fix: An issue with referencing bad actors that have been detected and affecting CPU utilization has been fixed.

bugs.title: BADOS - BIG-IP Self-protection during (D)DOS attack
bugs.symptoms: Problem: 100% accurate detection may not help to prevent an attack It's necessary to protect BIG-IP CPU utilization during attack - for BAD actors (in addition to shunlist) and for unknown IPs. This mechanism should allow bad actors detection and keep CPU utilization in reasonable limits.
bugs.conditions: High BIG-IP CPU utilization during (D)DOS attack
bugs.impact: Service impact due to BIG-IP CPU high utilization
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Added additional CPU protection during a (D)DOS attack

bugs.title: Displaying application components reports an error
bugs.symptoms: Displaying an iApp which contains an iRule from an iLX workspace reports an error.
bugs.conditions: Displaying an iApp which contains an iRule from an iLX workspace.
bugs.impact: The components page reports an error.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: Displaying application components no longer reports an error.

bugs.title: TMM can core in a specific set of conditions.
bugs.symptoms: TMM can core and assert: 'ifc not set'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions: - A unit with license that ratelimits throughput performance to something other than max or 1. - One or more virtual IP addresses configured with DNS profiles with rapid-response enabled. - Something causing the listener to be disabled or a listener to not be found. - A DNS request sent to the disabled listener.
bugs.impact: TMM might core and assert: 'ifc not set'.

bugs.title: PEM deletes existing PEM Subscriber Session after lease time expires (DHCP renewal not processed).
bugs.symptoms: When the BigIp is in DHCP forwarding mode, if the giaddr field in the unicast DHCP renewal packet is set to DHCP relay agent IP address, the DHCP server sends the ACK to the renewal packet to the relay agent IP(giaddr) instead of ciaddr. Bigip DHCP module does not process the ACK and update the lease time, which causes PEM subscriber session to be aged out.
bugs.conditions: 1)BigIP in forwarding mode 2)giaddr field in unicast DHCP renewal packet is set to IP address of relay agent(Typically, it is set to 0 by DHCP client)
bugs.impact: PEM Subscriber Session will age out
bugs.fix: PEM no longer deletes existing PEM Subscriber Sessions after the lease time expires, so the DHCP renewal is now processed.

bugs.title: Soft lockup may occur when vCMP host TMMs run realtime without yielding.
bugs.symptoms: The host TMM is using 100% CPU.
bugs.conditions: There are no higher priority processes preempting the host TMMs.
bugs.impact: Soft lockup occurs, system may temporarily fail to process traffic.
bugs.workaround: Configure the vCMP host to run with a non-zero yield percentage and restart tmm. The yield value can be configured using a Tcl option in /config/tmm_init.tcl, for example: echo "realtime yield 10" >> /config/tmm_init.tcl.

bugs.title: Port/Protocol packet filter might fail to capture IPv6 fragments.
bugs.symptoms: Port/Protocol packet filter might fail to capture IPv6 fragments.
bugs.conditions: This can occur under the following conditions: - Virtual server is configured to use packet filters. - Packet filter is based on a port number. - Filter default action is discard. - IPv6 protocol is being used.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system will not be able to process IPv6 traffic.
bugs.workaround: For IPv6, instead of using a rule such as 'dst port 50000', filter based on raw fragments offsets, for example: '((udp dst port 50000) or (ip6[6]=44 and ip6[40]=17 and ip6[50]=50000)).

bugs.title: Don't include maximum TCP options length in calculating MSS on ICMP PMTU.
bugs.symptoms: TCP segment size is 40 bytes less.
bugs.conditions: ICMP implementation using Path MTU (PMTU). User enables MPTCP, Rate Pacing, or any of the following congestion controls: Vegas, Illinois, Woodside, CHD, CHG
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is less data per TCP segment.
bugs.workaround: Disable Path MTU Discovery by doing the following, "tmsh modify sys db tm.enforcepathmtu value disable"
bugs.fix: Don't include maximum TCP options length in calculating MSS on ICMP PMTU in the advanced TCP implementation.

bugs.title: Unnecessary re-transmission of packets on higher ICMP PMTU.
bugs.symptoms: LTM re-transmits TCP segments even when ICMP Path maximum transmission unit (PMTU) is higher than existing MTU.
bugs.conditions: ICMP PMTU is higher than existing MTU. User enables MPTCP, Rate Pacing, or any of the following congestion controls: Vegas, Illinois, Woodside, CHD, CHG
bugs.impact: Burst traffic generated.
bugs.workaround: Disable Path MTU Discovery by entering the command: tmsh modify sys db tm.enforcepathmtu value disable.
bugs.fix: Fixed unnecessary re-transmission of packets on higher ICMP Path maximum transmission unit (PMTU) in the advanced TCP implementation.

bugs.title: HTML_TAG_MATCHED fired for not matching tags.
bugs.symptoms: HTML_TAG_MATCHED might be raised for tags not configured in HTML profile rules. This issue only causes extra executions of iRule events and does not affect work of configured HTML tag-raise-event rules.
bugs.conditions: Erroneous extra match might happen in two situations: - When the last HTML tag in the current chunk of data (network packet) contains event handler attributes. - When the same tag in the current buffer has tag-remove and tag-raise-event HTML rules configured. The tag will be removed and HTML_TAG_MATCHED event will be raised for the last tag of current buffer instead.
bugs.impact: HTML_TAG_MATCHED might be executed with unexpected HTML::tag values. The event handler might fail if it does not verify tag and attribute values.
bugs.workaround: HTML_TAG_MATCHED event handler should contain checks for tag and attribute values. This is a recommended style for writing iRules with HTML_TAG_MATCHED, and DevCentral examples are already written this way.

bugs.title: Analytics alerts: Metric "Maximum TPS" can only be used with Virtual Servers (but not with a Pool Member).
bugs.symptoms: While configuring an alert for Maximum TPS on an Analytics profile, you get an error: Metric "Maximum TPS" can only be used with Virtual Servers (but not with a Pool Member)
bugs.conditions: This occurs when attempting to add an Analytics alert that triggers on Max TPS, and the alert is configured to run against a pool member or an application (the default is Virtual Server, not pool member or application).
bugs.impact: You cannot configure Max TPS alerts at the pool member level. The GUI appears to allow you to do this, but validation rules will prevent you from adding the alert. The full list of alerts that cannot be configured at the pool or application level include all rules with the word Maximum in them: - Maximum TPS - Maximum Server Latency - Maximum Page Load Time - Maximum Request Throughput - Maximum Response Throughput

bugs.title: Use of Standard access list remarks in imish may causes later entries to fail on add
bugs.symptoms: The use of remarks in standard access lists in dynamic routing shell causes subsequent filters in the same ACL to fail to load.
bugs.conditions: Create a standard access list with a remark. Add to the same list another entry to permit or deny a IP/range.
bugs.impact: The ACL does not load and error is returned.
bugs.workaround: No not use remarks in standard access lists or use an access list in the extended or named ranges.

bugs.title: High-speed logging to remote logging node stops sending logs after all logging nodes go down
bugs.symptoms: All logging to external logging nodes (such as BIG-IQ) suddenly stop.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the configured logging nodes go down. Even when they are brought back up, tmm will not send logs to the remote servers.
bugs.impact: Remote logging stops and will only resume if tmm is restarted.

bugs.title: Fast Forwarded UDP packets might be dropped if datagram-load-balancing is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: Fast Forwarded UDP packets might be dropped if datagram-load-balancing is enabled.
bugs.conditions: TMM is overloaded. UDP datagram load-balancing is used.
bugs.impact: UDP packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable datagram-load-balancing in the affected UDP profile. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify ltm profile udp <profile_name> datagram-load-balancing disabled
bugs.fix: The fast-forwarding mechanism now properly handle packets with invalidated flows. The packets are now sent back to the source tmm for reprocessing. The TCP and TCP4 filters were updated to properly work with the changed fast-forwarding implementation.

bugs.title: APM Login Performance may be degraded
bugs.symptoms: A high number of logins per second can cause increased latency. The actual login rate that can cause the increased latency depends on the Access Policy configuration and network characteristics. In a typical configuration and network setup, you should not observe noticeable latency if logins per second is less than a few hundred.
bugs.conditions: Very high rate of login requests. More noticeable if the login-per-second rate is more than several hundred.
bugs.impact: End users will experience slower login or login failure.

bugs.title: SCTP needs traffic-group validation for server-side client alternate addresses
bugs.symptoms: Addresses may be advertised in an SCTP INIT chunk even though they are not usable by the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: When an SCTP virtual server has server-side-multihoming enabled and the snatpool used by the virtual server contains addresses from other traffic groups, it will advertise all of the addresses from the snatpool in the INIT chunk.
bugs.impact: Some of the paths advertised in the SCTP association establishment creation process will be unusable. A conformant SCTP implementation on the server-side should test and disregard these paths, causing no impact to traffic.
bugs.fix: The SCTP filter in BIG-IP has been fixed so that all of the alternate addresses advertised during SCTP association establishment are in the same traffic group as the virtual server. Configured addresses are checked for the correct traffic group membership before being advertised.

bugs.title: Misconfigured SCTP alternate addresses may emit incorrect ARP advertisements
bugs.symptoms: SCTP alternate addresses may be advertised on the server-side that are in a route-domain that is different from that of the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Alternate-addresses are configured on an SCTP virtual server that aren't in the correct route domain.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to traffic processing. Alternate-addresses will be advertised even though they are not in the correct domain. Some addresses advertised may fail to respond to negotiation, but the SCTP association overall will be stable.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that all addresses for SCTP virtual servers are in the same route domain.
bugs.fix: The SCTP profile now screens alternate addresses for route domain membership before advertising them.

bugs.title: Windows integrated logon client take long time to log on in some case
bugs.symptoms: If Microsoft Windows integrated logon is used with the Edge client in locked mode, user login and logout takes more that three minutes to logon.
bugs.conditions: 1) Windows integrated logon (also known as credential provider) is used. 2) Edge client is configured in locked mode.
bugs.impact: Usability
bugs.fix: Microsoft Windows integrated logon client used when the Edge client is configured in locked mode no longer takes more than three minutes to logon.

bugs.title: apmd crash under rare conditions with LDAP in BIGIP 12.0 and beyond
bugs.symptoms: APM crashes during periods of high Active Directory lookups.
bugs.conditions: APM configured to use ldap. This was seen during stress testing of AD queries.
bugs.impact: APM crashes, clients unable to connect
bugs.fix: apmd no longer crashes during periods of high Active Directory (AD) lookups.

bugs.title: Empty URI rewriting is not done as required by browser.
bugs.symptoms: Empty URI must be rewritten at server side and client side rewriter in the same way: as empty URI (all browsers treat this type of URI in a specific way).
bugs.conditions: A tag with an empty 'src' or 'href' attribute.
bugs.impact: Web application malfunction, such as incorrect or unexpected behavior or error messages.
bugs.workaround: Use an application-specific iRule that modifies the empty URI. -- For example, for JavaScript methods such as setAttribute(), an iRule should change this: 'F5_Invoke_setAttribute(o, "src", uri)' to this: '(uri=="")?o.setAttribute("src", uri):F5_Invoke_setAttribute(o, "src", uri)'. -- As another example, for JavaScript methods such as write(str), writeln(str), innerHTML=str, outerHTML=str, and similar methods, if str contains , the iRule must remove the src attribute.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the issue of rewriting the empty URI the same way at the server side and client side: as empty URI (all browsers treat this type of URI in a specific way).

bugs.title: SCTP emits 'address conflict detected' log messages during failover
bugs.symptoms: The system may advertise, on the client-side, SCTP alternate addresses that are in a route-domain different from that of the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Configuring an SCTP virtual server with alternate-addresses that are not in the correct route domain.
bugs.impact: No impact to traffic processing. Some addresses advertised may fail to respond to negotiation, but the SCTP association overall will be stable.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that all addresses for SCTP virtual servers are in the same route domain.
bugs.fix: The SCTP profile now screens alternate addresses for route domain membership before advertising them.

bugs.title: BIG-IP v11.5.4 successfully installs on 12250v platform but is not supported.
bugs.symptoms: You can install v11.5.4 on the 12250v platform, but are unable to license BIG-IP. This is because v11.5.4 is not supported on the 12250v platform.
bugs.conditions: Install BIG-IP v11.5.4 on a 12250v platform.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP v11.5.4 is not supported on the 12250v platform. Even though installation succeeds, it is not possible to license BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Install a supported version of BIG-IP on the 12250v. Supported versions are 11.6.0 HF2 or later and 12.0.0 or later.

bugs.title: Standby box may crash or behave abnormally
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on the standby unit
bugs.conditions: It is not known the conditions that cause this, and has been seen very rarely.
bugs.impact: Tmm on the standby device crashes. Memory utilization before the crash can appear to be unusually high.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes in the rare case of WOM or Multipath TCP (MPTCP) virtual servers configured with mirroring.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE does not support live migration on Hyper-V
bugs.symptoms: Performing live migration of a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) from one Hyper-V host to another may result in non-functional virtual network devices, requiring a reboot of the guest to resolve. This behavior is unsupported.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE running on Hyper-V performing a live migration operation.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP VE guest may be unable to process network traffic requiring a reboot.
bugs.workaround: To work around this: 1. Fail over traffic to a VE instance running on another host. 2. Shut down the previously active BIG-IP guest. 3. Migrate it to the new host. 4. Bring it back up.

bugs.title: SSL does not cancel pending sign request before the handshake times out or is canceled.
bugs.symptoms: When TMM has many SSL handshake, for ephemeral key, SSL does not sign for ServerKeyExchange message. Then it is possible that sign request is pending on crypto SSL queue. Even the handshake is timeout or canceled, the sign request is still in the queue. This might cause memory accumulation.
bugs.conditions: When TMM has many SSL handshake, for ephermal key, SSL should sign for ServerKeyExchange message.
bugs.impact: Even if the handshake times out or canceled, the sign request is still in the queue. This might cause memory accumulation.
bugs.fix: SSL now cancels sign pending request before it times out or is canceled.

bugs.title: Clearing masquerade MAC results in unexpected link-local self IPs.
bugs.symptoms: BigIP advertises fe80::200:ff:fe00:0 as a selfip
bugs.conditions: masquerade MAC is from non-zero to zero
bugs.impact: May cause IP conflicts between HA devices
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm after setting masquerade MAC to none
bugs.fix: Do not advertise invalid selfip on clearing masquerade MAC

bugs.title: TMSH and iControl REST: When logged in as a remote user who has the admin role, cannot save config because of permission errors.
bugs.symptoms: When a remotely authenticated user who has the admin role uses TMSH or iControl to save the configuration, the operation fails because of permission errors. Using iControl, the system posts an error similar to the following: Error processing request for URI:http://localhost:8110/mgmt/tm/sys/config {code:400,message: Can't create tmsh temp directory \"/config/.config.backup\" Permission denied, errorStack:[]}. Using TMSH (e.g., running the command: tmsh save sys config), the system posts an error similar to the following: Can't create tmsh temp directory "/config/.config.backup" Permission denied
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Remote Authentication is configured. -- User is logged in as a remote user who has the admin role. -- Using TMSH or iControl for remotely authenticated user operations.
bugs.impact: Cannot save the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: -- Use the GUI to save the configuration. -- Have a locally authenticated user with admin role save the configuration.
bugs.fix: When a remotely authenticated user who has the admin role uses TMSH or iControl to save the configuration, the operation now completes as expected, without permission errors.

bugs.title: Horizon View client throws an exception when connecting to Horizon 7 VCS through APM.
bugs.symptoms: If APM is configured as PCoIP proxy against Horizon 7 VCS, the Horizon View client fails to retrieve the list of entitlements with an exception written in its logs.
bugs.conditions: APM as PCoIP proxy for Horizon 7 View Connection Server.
bugs.impact: Horizon View client cannot be used with APM to access Horizon 7.
bugs.fix: Horizon View client can now be used with APM to access Horizon 7.

bugs.title: CoS queue egress drop counts not reported in all drop counter stats.
bugs.symptoms: CoS queue egress packet drop counts are not exposed in the 'Drops' column for 'tmsh show net interface' for B2250, B4300 and 1x000 platforms. The CoS queue egress packet drop counts are however correctly reported via the 'drop_reason' and 'interface_stat' tmstat counters.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on B2250 and B4300 blades and on 1x000 platforms.
bugs.impact: CoS queue egress packet drop counts are not exposed via net interface reports, but are reported correctly via tmstat counters.
bugs.workaround: CoS queue egress packet drop counts can be viewed in tmsh using the following counters: -- tmctl interface_stat. -- tmctl drop_reason.

bugs.title: TMM crash and core dump when processing SSL protocol alert.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash and core dump when processing SSL protocol alert.
bugs.conditions: During SSL handshake, if the server sends protocol Alert to the BIG-IP system, TMM might crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: A problem of TMM restarting when processing SSL protocol alert has been fixed.

bugs.title: vCMPd may crash when processing bridged network traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions vCMPd may crash while processing bridged network traffic.
bugs.conditions: vCMP active in 'host-only' or 'bridged' mode.
bugs.impact: vCMPd may crash, resulting in a failure of guest instances on the same host hardware slot.
bugs.workaround: Deploy guests in isolated mode.
bugs.fix: vCMPd does not crash when processing bridged network traffic.

bugs.title: DNSSEC NSEC3 records with different type bitmap for same name.
bugs.symptoms: For a delegation from a secure zone to an insecure zone, BIG-IP returns different type bitmaps in the NSEC3 record depending on the query type. This causes BIND9's validator to reject the secure delegation to the insecure zone.
bugs.conditions: For insecure delegations, our DNSSEC implementation does not support the DS record. Those queries are forwarded to the backend, BIND if selected as fallback. Without ZSK/KSK for an insecure child zone, BIND responds SOA which we dynamically sign.
bugs.impact: DNS lookups may fail if BIND9's validator rejects the delegation.
bugs.fix: If response is a NODATA from either the proxy or a transparent cache, and the query is a DS, set the types bitmap to NS.

bugs.title: TMM crash with a core dump
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash with a core dump
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned Session Awareness enabled Mirroring is enabled HA (CMI) setup
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: We've fixed the handling of Session Awareness in HA (CMI) setup to prevent TMM crashes

bugs.title: Clicking 'Customize All' checkbox does not work.
bugs.symptoms: Clicking 'Customize All' in Safari browser does not check the checkboxes below, and the settings remain grayed out.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS.
bugs.impact: FPS child profile page.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: Clicking 'Customize All' checkbox in Safari browser now checks the checkboxes below and changes the state of the cosponsoring settings.

bugs.title: Linux host may lose dynamic routes on secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: The Linux host residing on a secondary blade might lose dynamic routes previously learned via a dynamic routing protocol.
bugs.conditions: - Multibladed chassis or vCMP guest. - Routes learned via dynamic routing. - Restart of services or reboot of secondary blade.
bugs.impact: Routes on Linux host of secondary blade are lost. This might affect host traffic, such as monitoring, remote logging, etc., due to the lack of routing information.
bugs.workaround: Modify the ZebOS maximum-paths setting on the primary blade to trigger a route update to the non-primary blades. Add a custom alert to the user_alert.conf to auto-mitigate this issue whenever a blade joins the cluster. # 11.5.x workaround for user_alert.conf alert BLADE_JOINED_CLUSTER "010719fc:5: Mate cluster member (.*) turned Green." { exec command="/usr/sbin/zebos -a cmd 'enable,conf t,maximum-paths 5,maximum-paths 4,exit,exit'" } Note: The Mate cluster log is not present in 11.6.x, so this an 11.5.x only workaround.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs, so there is consistency among blades.

bugs.title: Some Edge Client's German translations are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Some Edge Client's German translations are incorrect.
bugs.conditions: APM end-user's system using German locale.
bugs.impact: Conversion results in confusing text.
bugs.fix: Edge Client's German translations are now correct.

bugs.title: ZebOS adds and deletes an extraneous LSA after deleting a route that matches a summary suppression route.
bugs.symptoms: In a configuration with a summary route that is added to ZebOS and configured with 'not-advertise', when deleting the exactly matching route, ospfd sends LSA route with age 1, then immediately sends update with age 3600.
bugs.conditions: OSPF using route health injection for default route.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. The extraneous LSA is immediately aged out.
bugs.workaround: Configure a static default route in imish instead of using RHI for the default route.
bugs.fix: ZebOS no longer adds and deletes an extraneous LSA after deleting a route that matches a summary suppression route.

bugs.title: With Nagle disabled, TCP does not send all of xfrags with size greater than MSS.
bugs.symptoms: With Nagle disabled, TCP does not send all of xfrags with size greater than MSS.
bugs.conditions: Congestion window is small relative to message size; abc is enabled; also might manifest when serverside MTU is greater than clientside MTU.
bugs.impact: Additional connection latency.
bugs.workaround: Enabling proxy-mss on the serverside TCP profile significantly reduces incidence of this problem in observed cases. If init-cwnd is low, raising it might also help. Disabling abc can also reduce the problem, but might have other negative network implications.
bugs.fix: Incoming packets are now pulled more aggressively into the send buffer, if there are no negative implications for CPU performance.

bugs.title: CSRF enabled within iframe request causes to unpredictable behavior on a website.
bugs.symptoms: The csrf script changes the frame/iframe source attribute. When it happens the browser issue a request, as a result for each frame on a page 2 requests are being sent, the first is the original request when the frame is loaded and the second is when the csrf script changes the frame source attribute.
bugs.conditions: Enable ASM CSRF Request a page with an iframe or frameset
bugs.impact: Viewing the site causes some pages to show up blank.
bugs.workaround: Bypassing or disabling ASM for URL appears to fix the issue.

bugs.title: PS2 power supply status incorrect after removal
bugs.symptoms: After removing the second power supply (PS2), running system_check indicates that the power supply status is still good: system_check -d | grep power Chassis power supply 1: status FAN=good; VINPUT=good; VOUTPUT=good; STATUS=good Chassis power supply 2: status VINPUT=good; VOUTPUT=good; STATUS=not present
bugs.conditions: This occurs on 10000-series and 12000-series platforms when removing the PS2 power supply and running system_check
bugs.impact: Erroneous indication that the power supply is still good
bugs.fix: Power supply status for PS2 is now correctly indicated when the power supply is removed.

bugs.title: HSB lockup on B2100 (A109) blade with vCMP running v11.6.0 final
bugs.symptoms: An HSB lockup occurred on a B2100 (A109) blade running vCMP.
bugs.conditions: It is not yet known what triggers this.
bugs.impact: HSB lockup requires unit restart.

bugs.title: APD might crash if LDAP Query agent fails to retrieve primary group for a user
bugs.symptoms: APD crashes and generate a core file.
bugs.conditions: The problem can happen only when the following conditions are met: 1. LDAP Query is used with AD backend. 2. 'Fetch groups to which the user or group belong' is defined for a value other than None (e.g., direct/all). 3. There were previous logons to the BIG-IP system, so a group cache is built and valid. 4. There is a new group created in the domain and assigned as a primary group for the user trying to authenticate.
bugs.impact: Authentication service will be interrupted.
bugs.workaround: Administrator should reset the group cache using either GUI (AAA LDAP Server configuration page) or tmsh (apm aaa ldap object). After the cache is reset, the cache will be built from scratch at the time of the next request, and the new group will be added to the cache.
bugs.fix: APD no longer crashes if LDAP Query agent fails to retrieve primary group for a user.

bugs.title: iControl REST : possible to get duplicate transaction ids when transactions are created by multiple clients
bugs.symptoms: When 2 iControl REST clients using the same username create transactions simultaneously, they can potentially get the same transaction id. This completely messes up both the client code execution.
bugs.conditions: Client requests to create transaction are close to each other in time.
bugs.impact: Transaction semantics are not followed, and unintended errors may occur
bugs.fix: Under these conditions, transaction IDs are now unique, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: HA Grioup percent-up display value is truncated, not rounded
bugs.symptoms: The value displayed in "show sys ha-group detail" and "list sys ha-group" is shown as only the integer portion of the actual percent-up value.
bugs.conditions: When the number of "up" members in an HA Group results in a percent-up value that is not a whole number, the displayed value is truncated, not rounded.
bugs.impact: Incorrect display of the percent-up value. The score contribution is correct, and displayed rounded properly.
bugs.fix: The percent-up value is correctly rounded before display.

bugs.title: Wrong value for TCP connections closed measure
bugs.symptoms: In TCP analytics, the measure 'connections closed' displays the wrong value.
bugs.conditions: TMM_API debug enabled.
bugs.impact: Wrong value displayed.
bugs.workaround: Do not turn on debug printing.
bugs.fix: Memory corruption found and fixed. All debug printing organized together at the beginning of the function.

bugs.title: Single-line Via headers separated by single comma result in first character second header being stripped.
bugs.symptoms: Removing the first Via header strips the leading character from the second Via when headers are separated by a comma (',').
bugs.conditions: Multiple Via headers on single-line separated by a single comma (',').
bugs.impact: Leading character of 2nd Via header will be stripped e.g. 'SIP/2.0/TCP' becomes 'IP/2.0/TCP'.
bugs.fix: Removing the first Via header no longer strips the leading character from the second Via when headers are separated by a comma (',').

bugs.title: Standard TLS version rollback detection for TLSv1 or earlier might need to be relaxed to interoperate with clients that violate TLS specification.
bugs.symptoms: Standard TLS rollback detection for TLSv1 or earlier clients might be too strict for clients that do not comply with RFC 2246 and later. These clients may require 'tls-rollback-bug' option set.
bugs.conditions: Standard behaviour of TLS clients is to use ClientHello.client_version in pre-master secret (PMS). Some clients, incorrectly, might use negotiated version in PMS.
bugs.impact: Failed TLS handshake.
bugs.fix: Added support for tls-rollback-bug
bugs.behavior: This release provides improved support for "TLS rollback bug workaround" feature described in Managing SSL Traffic :: Configuring workarounds in the LTM documentation on AskF5. ([1] link below). The value is set by existing tls-rollback-bug option, using the command described in [2], below. This is an existing option. When this option is enabled in clientssl profile, RSA-only ciphersuites will have relaxed treatment of the version field set by the SSL/TLS client as part of the sequence of bytes encrypted to the server RSA key, called pre-master secret (PMS). With the option enabled, PMS can contain either ClientHello.client_version, or negotiated version. Standard behaviour of TLS clients is to use ClientHello.client_version in PMS. [1] https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/products/big-ip_ltm/manuals/product/ltm_configuration_guide_10_1/ltm_ssl_profiles.html. [2] create /ltm profile client-ssl xxx ciphers DEFAULT options { tls-rollback-bug }.
bugs.workaround: Configure the BIG-IP client SSL profile to include tls-rollback-bug, using a command similar to the following: create /ltm profile client-ssl xxx ciphers DEFAULT options { tls-rollback-bug }.

bugs.title: Connections to an APM virtual server may be reset and fail on appliance and VE platforms.
bugs.symptoms: APM connections failing when mac masquerade is in use and source-port preserve-strict is enabled on the APM virtual server.
bugs.conditions: The traffic-group has mac-masquerade configured and source-port preserve-strict is in use on the APM virtual server
bugs.impact: Connections to an APM virtual server may be reset and fail on appliance and VE platforms.
bugs.workaround: Disable either mac-masquerade or source-port preserve-strict (or both)

bugs.title: jitterentropy-rngd quietly fails to start
bugs.symptoms: If jitterentropy-rngd fails to start, it does so quietly during system start, causing init.d script [ OK ] when it should be [ FAILED ]. This can cause the system to hang indefinitely at boot time at the following step (the key name may vary, depending on what needs to be generated): Generating /var/named/config/rndc.key ( 09:08:10 ) ... Similarly, if jitterentropy-rngd fails to start but there are no keys to be generated at boot time, the system will boot successfully. However, the genkeys and genkeys-1024 processes invoked by crontab every hour might hang.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on any BIG-IP system if jitterentropy-rngd fails to start. The issue has been observed chiefly on vCMP guests running on VIPRION B21x0 blades.
bugs.impact: 1) The system may fail to boot (user intervention will be required at this point to recover the system). 2) As crontab invokes the genkeys and genkeys-1024 processes every hour, these may start but never terminate (any hung processes might eventually cause increased memory and CPU utilization, potentially leading to unpredictable system failures).
bugs.fix: jitterentropy-rngd now starts up as expected, so no failures occur.

bugs.title: False alert cn decryption failure log when peer (client) drops the TCP session during decryption.
bugs.symptoms: False alert cn decryption failure log when peer (client) drops the TCP session during decryption when crypto process is canceled intentionally. ERROR: ssl_cn_decrypt_fin_cb:1985: fin decryption failed
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: 1. Using a BIG-IP system with a Cavium Nitrox SSL accelerator card, and the handshake goes through the hardware path (Cavium Nitrox). Note: Not all the handshake instances are handled by the hardware; some run the software path. Whether the hardware path is used depends on the SSL protocol and cipher selection. 2. The client (usually the Chrome browser) connects to the BIG-IP system's virtual server but immediately drop the connection (for instance, pressingCtrl-f5 very quickly). The error appears when this termination happens to interrupt the hardware decryption process.
bugs.impact: The crypto process is canceled intentionally, so there should be no error.
bugs.workaround: This typically does not cause problem because the client (browsers) could have dropped the connection or restarted another session.
bugs.fix: The system no longer posts an error message that indicates an incomplete connection decryption if the connection decryption was already canceled. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Web clients (f5epi and f5vpn) require version 5.5 of QT package on all distributions of Linux
bugs.symptoms: The new web client depends on Qt library version 5.5. On some Linux distributions, this version may not be available in standard repositories. Web client installation fails on such distributions.
bugs.conditions: Qt library version 5.5 is not available on Linux distribution on which web client is being installed
bugs.impact: Web client cannot install.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, download and install the required qt library from the non-standard repository. Then build and install required Qt library on the distribution before installing the web client.

bugs.title: ACCESS policy running iRule event agent intermittently hangs
bugs.symptoms: If you are using iRule event agent on the 12.1.0 release, you may see an intermittent Access Policy execution hang. The hang occurs during the execution of ACCESS::policy agent_id.
bugs.conditions: iRule event agent is configured. iRule uses ACCESS_POLICY_EVENT_AGENT event Within this event, ACCESS::policy agent_id command is used.
bugs.impact: Policy execution intermittently hangs.
bugs.workaround: Please use this command: ACCESS::session data get {session.custom_event.id}
bugs.fix: A hang related to the use of ACCESS::policy agent_id has been fixed.

bugs.title: Changing the destination address of a virtual server when there is no other VIP with that same destination virtual address, the virtual address is not removed.
bugs.symptoms: When removing the last virtual server whose destination IP address matches a virtual address with auto-delete enabled the virtual address is also removed. However changing the destination address of a virtual server when there is no other VIP with that same destination virtual address, the virtual address is not removed.
bugs.conditions: -- Changing the destination address of a virtual server. -- There is no other virtual IP address with that same destination virtual address. -- Virtual address is configured with Route Health Injection (RHI) enabled.
bugs.impact: Virtual address with RHI enabled leaves routes injected into the routing process.
bugs.workaround: Remove the virtual address manually.

bugs.title: Unnecessary logging during startup: 'Unable to connect to MCPD' and Errdefsd is starting'.
bugs.symptoms: Unnecessary logging during startup: err errdefsd[5106]: 01940019:3: Unable to connect to MCPD, will try again in 30 seconds. err errdefsd[5106]: 0194001d:3: Errdefsd is starting. Old shared memory arena is now deprecated.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during system startup.
bugs.impact: No to low impact. This message is benign, and you can safely ignore it.
bugs.workaround: None needed.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the unnecessary benign error message logging that occurred during startup: 'Unable to connect to MCPD' and Errdefsd is starting'.

bugs.title: Partition can be removed when remote role info entries refer to it
bugs.symptoms: If you have a partition, and a remote-role info that mentions the partition, then you can delete the partition and the role info will not be modified. Once this configuration is saved, future loads will fail with an error like the following: 01070829:5: Input error: Invalid partition ID request, partition does not exist (your-partition-name)
bugs.conditions: A partition has been deleted, but the remote role configuration still names the partition.
bugs.impact: Load will fail.
bugs.workaround: Before removing a partition, ensure that any role-info entries mentioning the partition are also removed. If you already have encountered a failure to load such a configuration, edit /config/bigip.conf to remove the offending entries in "auth remote-role".
bugs.fix: It is no longer possible to enter this state. If a partition is referenced by a role-info entry, deleting that partition fails.

bugs.title: The "ACCESS::session create" iRule command does not work
bugs.symptoms: When the "ACCESS::session create" iRule command is used with an APM virtual, the command does not resume properly and causing the sessions to disconnect/hang.
bugs.conditions: APM virtual configured with an iRule that includes "ACCESS::session create" iRule command.
bugs.impact: APM virtual won't function correctly.
bugs.workaround: The "ACCESS::session create" iRule command should be removed from the iRule attached to the virtual.
bugs.fix: Updated the session DB calls to include req_id parameter so that the TCL context gets updated/saved and used upon resume.

bugs.title: False positive "URL error" alerts on URLs with GET parameters
bugs.symptoms: False-positive URL Error alerts are sometimes generated on URLs with GET parameters.
bugs.conditions: Use of URLs with GET parameters.
bugs.impact: Unwanted alerts in alert server.
bugs.fix: Hash calculation is done on slightly different URL inputs, causing mismatch.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as SAML SP does not redirect users to original request URI after authentication is completed
bugs.symptoms: After end-user successfully performs SP initiated SAML SSO with a original request URI other then "/", SP will redirect user back to '/' as landing URI.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as SAML SP and no relay state is configured on either SP or IdP
bugs.impact: User is not redirected to original request URI.
bugs.workaround: Workaround provided below works when first client request to BIG-IP as SP is 'GET'. This workaround is not applicable when first client request is 'POST'. SP object can be configured with relay state pointing to the landing URI: %{session.server.landinguri} After successful authentication, end-user will be redirected to the landing URI (reflected back by IdP in the relay-state).
bugs.fix: SAML SSO requests will now be redirected to the original request URI.

bugs.title: Alert is not redirected to alert server when unseal fails
bugs.symptoms: Alert is not redirected to the alert server when unseal fails and iRule is enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1. Unsealing alert failure. 2. iRule enabled.
bugs.impact: Alert is not redirected to the alert server and FPS returns 404 response.
bugs.workaround: Disable iRule.
bugs.fix: FPS now correctly redirects the alert.

bugs.title: Configuration of Timeout in AAA LDAP/AD Servers
bugs.symptoms: The Timeout configured in AAA LDAP/AD Servers controls only the network connection timeout and not operation timeout. The operation timeout is hardcoded to 180 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Configure a Timeout value in AAA LDAP/AD Servers.
bugs.impact: If the network connection has no issue, then it could take up to 180 seconds for the LDAP operation to fail.
bugs.workaround: No workaround. This is function as designed.

bugs.title: Rest API - log profile in json return does not include the partition but needs to
bugs.symptoms: When querying the log profile via the Rest API, the returned response does not include the partition name in FullPath. For example, for a log profile named mySample: https://bigip_ip/mgmt/tm/security/log/profile/~Common~mySample/application/mySample The JSON returned will contain "fullPath": "testProfile", It should contain "fullPath": "/Common/testProfile", This can cause BIG-IQ to fail to sync.
bugs.conditions: Log profile created. This is most visible when using BIG-IQ to sync.
bugs.impact: Applications relying on the folder path can fail
bugs.fix: The Rest API will now provide the full path to the log profile.

bugs.title: tmm crash when loading default signatures or updating classification signature
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading classification signatures or downgrading to the default signatures, tmm will crash.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when loading updated classification signatures on versions 12.1.0 and 12.1.1.
bugs.impact: tmm will crash during the load. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash when loading classification signatures.

bugs.title: Active Rules page displays a different time zone.
bugs.symptoms: Active Rules page displays a different time zone.
bugs.impact: GUI shows incorrect timezone.
bugs.conditions: When Active Rules page is loaded after the BIG-IP system timezone has changed.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command after changing BIG-IP timezone: bigstart restart tomcat.
bugs.fix: Active Rules page now shows the correct timezone after the BIG-IP system timezone has changed.

bugs.title: Applications that use appendChild() or similar JavaScript functions to build UI might experience slow performance in Microsoft Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.symptoms: Applications that use appendChild() or similar JavaScript functions to build UI might experience slow performance in Microsoft Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.conditions: Intense usage of JavaScript methods such as: appendChild(), insertBefore(), and other, similar JavaScript methods, in a customer's web application code.
bugs.impact: Very low web application performance when using Microsoft Internet Explorer.
bugs.fix: Applications that use appendChild() or similar JavaScript functions to build UI now experience expected performance in Microsoft Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.workaround: No workaround except to use another browser.

bugs.title: "never log" IPs are still reported to AVR
bugs.symptoms: IP addresses marked as "never log" are reported to AVR regardless of the flag
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Extra, unwanted logging for IP addresses flagged as "never log"

bugs.title: SSL resumption does not work with SSL::profile.
bugs.symptoms: SSL resumption does not work with SSL::profile.
bugs.impact: Unknown

bugs.title: New HA Pair created using serial cable failover only will remain Active/Active
bugs.symptoms: After creating a new sync-failover device group without network failover enabled, both devices remain Active.
bugs.conditions: Create a new sync-failover device-group without enabling network failover.
bugs.impact: Both device in the HA pair will be Active, which is unlikely to pass traffic successfully.
bugs.workaround: After adding the 2nd device to the sync-failover group, restart sod with "bigstart restart sod" on both devices.
bugs.fix: After creating the sync-failover group with without network failover configured, but a serial failover cable installed, one of the devices becomes Standby and the other remains Active.

bugs.title: The CMI rsync daemon may fail to start
bugs.symptoms: CMI starts an instance of the rsync daemon used for synchronizing file objects. If this daemon is not running, but left its PID file, then it will not restart.
bugs.conditions: The rsync daemon failed unexpectedly.
bugs.impact: Sync of file objects will fail with an error like this: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files...
bugs.workaround: Delete the PID file, "/var/run/rsyncd-cmi.pid". Then look up the configsync-ip of the local device and run "rsync-cmi start 1.2.3.4", replacing 1.2.3.4 with the current device's configsync-ip.

bugs.title: When DNS server node is flapping, FQDN Template Pool Member state might not update properly.
bugs.symptoms: When DNS server node is flapping, FQDN Template Pool Member state might not update properly. - The corresponding FQDN Template Node updates correctly. - FQDN Template Pool Members do not impact Pool health. - Does not impact traffic.
bugs.conditions: Trigger DNS server UP/DOWN, or change DNS configuration to point to an unreachable/reachable DNS server.
bugs.impact: Can be confusing for administrators.
bugs.workaround: tmsh modify ltm pool <name> members modify { <name> { state user-up } }

bugs.title: If IP address on network adapter changes but DNS remains unchanged, DNS resolution stops working
bugs.symptoms: - If an IP address on an interface changes after the connection to APM is established, DNS resolution stops working if the DNS on that adapter has not changed. - DNS resolution stops working until DNS relay proxy service is restarted or stopped.
bugs.conditions: - Using Microsoft Windows version 10. - Split tunneling configuration with split DNS scope. - IP address on the network adapter changes after the connection to APM is established, but the DNS on that adapter remains unchanged. - This might also occur when adapter 1 goes down and adapter 2 with same DNS as adapter 1 comes up.
bugs.impact: DNS resolution stops working until DNS relay proxy is stopped or restarted.
bugs.workaround: Stop or restart DNS relay proxy.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Unable to load configs from /usr/libexec/aws/.
bugs.symptoms: In 12.1.0, a new tmsh object 'sys global-settings file-whitelist-path-prefix' controls the path from which config can be loaded. To be allowed as a config storage location, the path must exist in file-whitelist-path-prefix. Because /usr/libexec/ is not part of the path, loading auto-scaling and CloudWatch iCall configuration files from /usr/libexec/aws/ fails.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs with AWS auto-scaling- and CloudWatch-related configuration files in TMOS v12.1.0.
bugs.impact: AWS auto-scaling-related automation and CloudFormation Templates (CFTs) for deploying BIG-IP will not work because 'sys global-settings file-whitelist-path-prefix' disallows /usr/libexec/aws/ is disallowed as legitimate config location.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, add /usr/libexec/aws/ into the 'sys global-settings file-whitelist-path-prefix'. To do so, run the following tmsh command: tmsh modify sys global-settings file-whitelist-path-prefix "{/var/local/scf} {/tmp/} {/shared/} {/config/} {/usr/libexec/aws}".
bugs.fix: Starting in 12.1.0-HF1, F5 Networks has changed the paths from which configuration files related to AWS autoscaling and CloudWatch can be loaded. This necessitates an extra step in the Custom AMI generation for Auto Scaling. Configuration files related to AWS auto scaling and CloudWatch have been moved to the /usr/share/aws/ directory. This change was made because the system no longer allows /usr/libexec/aws as a config file storage and load location. 12.1.0 and earlier Auto Scaling-related automation and CFT configurations must be modified to point to the new locations. The new locations for the Auto Scaling and CloudWatch config files are: The new locations for these config files are: -- /usr/share/aws/autoscale/aws-autoscale-icall-config. -- /usr/share/aws/metrics/aws-cloudwatch-icall-metrics-config.
bugs.behavior: Starting in 12.1.0-HF1, the system has changed the paths from which configuration files related to AWS autoscaling and CloudWatch can be loaded. This necessitates an extra step in the Custom AMI generation for Auto Scaling. Configuration files related to AWS auto scaling and CloudWatch have been moved to the /usr/share/aws/ directory. This change was made because the system no longer allows /usr/libexec/aws as a config file storage and load location. 12.1.0 and earlier Auto Scaling-related automation and CFT configurations must be modified to point to the new locations. The new locations for the Auto Scaling and CloudWatch config files are: The new locations for these config files are: -- /usr/share/aws/autoscale/aws-autoscale-icall-config. -- /usr/share/aws/metrics/aws-cloudwatch-icall-metrics-config.

bugs.title: DHCP lease is saved on the Custom AMI used for auto-scaling VE
bugs.symptoms: When configuring the instance for auto-scaling purpose and subsequently generating the Custom/Model AMI that is used for autoscaling VEs, the new instances generated from this image, might have the old DHCP lease acquired by the custom instance before an AMI was generated from it. This can collide with the new lease that the new instances get in their boot-up.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Auto-scaling VEs.
bugs.impact: Multiple valid DHClient leases exist, which could result dhclient in BIG-IP choosing wrong IP address for the management interface.
bugs.workaround: Delete the /var/lib/dhclient/dhclient.leases before shutting down the custom instance and generating a Custom/Model AMI out of it.
bugs.fix: Auto-scaling AMI will no longer contain a DHCP lease when they are saved.

bugs.title: APMD high CPU utilization
bugs.symptoms: APMD is running at unexpectedly high CPU.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when both of the following conditions are met: -- The connection between APMD and MCPD is lost due to MCPD restart. -- APMD keeps reading from the stale socket.
bugs.impact: -- High CPU utilization. -- Configuration cannot be pushed to APMD after MCPD restarts.

bugs.title: ospfd cores due to an incorrect debug statement.
bugs.symptoms: ospfd cores due to an incorrect debug statement.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in NSSA configs when ASE OSPF debugging enabled in imish (for example, by running the command: debug ospf route ase). Affected configuration commands are (in imish): debug ospf all. debug ospf route. debug ospf route ase.
bugs.impact: ospfd might crash, interrupting dynamic routing.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable debugging in ospf that includes 'route ase'.
bugs.fix: ospfd no longer crashes when debugging is enabled in imish.

bugs.title: CSRF injection leading to blank page
bugs.symptoms: When CSRF JS is injected, a blank page is seen.
bugs.conditions: When CSRF JS is injected. This page has has lots of iframes with the query parameters.
bugs.impact: Viewing the site causes some pages to show up blank.
bugs.workaround: Bypassing or disabling ASM for URL /apps/consumer/ITS/its_Lite/UpperFrame_Lite.jsp appears to fix the issue.
bugs.fix: Added new internal csrf_rewrite_frames_urls (default disabled) - if enabled bd will add the csrt token to the frame's src attributes when it has the query separator and will do it while response parsing.

bugs.title: APM ACL construction may cause TMM to core if TMM is out of memory
bugs.symptoms: During ACL construction, TMM send queries regarding assigned ACL information. If the reply message contains error message of out-of-memory, TMM was not handling this error message properly, and cause TMM to core.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is extremely loaded and out of memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: When handling the error reply message of out-of-memory during ACL construction, TMM can handle it without causing TMM to crash.

bugs.title: OOM with session messaging may result in TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Under out of memory conditions, session messaging may not initialize storage correctly, resulting in a later TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: Under out of memory conditions, memory allocation for session messaging fails, and storage is not initialized correctly.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Reduce load on box in order to avoid OOM conditions.
bugs.fix: Initialize storage on memory allocation failure.

bugs.title: gtmd core while adding a new GTM to an existing sync group.
bugs.symptoms: While adding a new GTM to an existing sync group, the new system's configuration conflicts with configurations on the other GTM systems in the sync group and causes gtmd to core on the unit being added.
bugs.conditions: Adding a new GTM to sync group. Other, more specific conditions are not known. That makes this rarely encountered, intermittent issue difficult to predict and reproduce.
bugs.impact: New GTM unit being added generated a gtmd core file. Configs on other production GTM devices in the network might also be compromised, and might need to be restored from backup. The system might produce a core dump at the moment of sync group corruption.
bugs.fix: Although the exact cause is unknown, the gtmd process has been modified to more gracefully handle the condition that generated the gtmd core while adding a new GTM to an existing sync group.

bugs.title: TMM QAT segfault after zlib/QAT compression conflation.
bugs.symptoms: TMM can segfault during prolonged mixture of software and hardware accelerated compression.
bugs.conditions: Continuous and prolonged mixture of software and hardware accelerated compression.
bugs.impact: TMM segfaults.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware accelerated compression with: tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy value speed
bugs.fix: TMM QAT compression added pointer-hardening for compression context.

bugs.title: Unable to launch View HTML5 connections in non-zero route domain virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Currently APM always attempts to uze the RTDom 0 when VMware View HTML5 client is launched. This doesn't work with the virtual servers in non-zero route domains.
bugs.conditions: APM configured as a PCoIP proxy on a VS in non-zero route domain.
bugs.impact: You cannot use virtuals in non-zero route domains if they need VMware View HTML5 client functionality
bugs.fix: APM now uses the proper route domain from the virtual server to handle VMware View HTML5 client connections.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VPR-B4450N shows "unknown" SNMP Object ID
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP VPR-B4450N blade does not show the correct Object ID for SNMP. An SNMP query will return "unknown".
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur on VIPRION B4450N blades running affected versions of BIG-IP software.
bugs.impact: Some network management applications may complain and fail.
bugs.fix: A new SNMP Object ID is added to TMOS v12.1.1 for VPR-B4450N.

bugs.title: VS hostname is not resolvable when DNS Relay proxy is installed and running under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: VS hostname is not resolvable when DNS Relay proxy is installed and running under certain conditions, it depends on client machine configuration. Symptom: negative record in windows DNS cache, can be verified by running ipconfig /displaydns
bugs.conditions: Specific client machine configuration
bugs.impact: VS hostname is not resolvable: - 'Refresh' of webtop causes unavailable webtop - Recurring check report may fail due to DNS resolve issue
bugs.workaround: * Clean windows DNS cache: ipconfig /flushdns or * Disable DNS Relay proxy service
bugs.fix: Now DNS Relay proxy service cleans up DNS cache after initialization mitigating issue described

bugs.title: Audit log messages with "user unknown" appear on install
bugs.symptoms: Multiple log entries in /var/log/audit similar to May 4 11:37:35 localhost notice mcpd[5488]: 01070417:5: AUDIT - client Unknown, user Unknown - transaction #33-1 - object 0 - create_if { db_variable { db_variable_name "version.edition" db_variable_value "<none>" db_variable_sync_type "private_internal" db_variable_data_type "string" db_variable_display_name "Version.Edition" } } [Status=Command OK]
bugs.conditions: This happens on initial install, it is not yet known what triggers it.
bugs.impact: This is the result of a daemon on the system not properly identifying itself to mcpd. The log messages can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: SSL::sessionid output is not consistent with the sessionid field of ServerHello message.
bugs.symptoms: SSL::sessionid output is not consistent with the sessionid field of ServerHello message. This is mostly cosmetic, but if an iRule depends upon the outcome, the result can be unexpected.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using an iRule to inspect the session ID on server-side SSL.
bugs.impact: The values do not match. SSL::sessionid outputs the wrong sessionid.
bugs.fix: The returned session ID in both the SERVERSSL_SERVERHELLO and SERVERSSL_HANDSHAKE events is the one presented by the SSL server.

bugs.title: False positive browser automation alert
bugs.symptoms: False positive browser automation alert containing details: "Cshui detected unknown (not human behavior)".
bugs.conditions: FPS automatic transaction detection feature activated.
bugs.impact: False positive browser automation alert containing details: "Cshui detected unknown (not human behavior)".
bugs.fix: Cshui result is now read correctly.

bugs.title: Unexpected/incorrect max CPU utilization statistics/performance values.
bugs.symptoms: CLI command 'tmsh show sys performance system' sometimes shows an incorrect (lower) 'Max CPU Utilization' value.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the BIG-IP system experiences occasional large spikes in CPU Utilization.
bugs.impact: Incorrect statistics reporting.
bugs.fix: CPU utilization data processing has been modified to more accurately report the maximum sampled value.

bugs.title: Stuck nitrox crypto queue can erroneously be reported
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, a stuck crypto queue can be erroneously detected on Nitrox systems (Nitrox PX and Nitrox 3). When the tmm/crypto stats are examined, they show no queued requests. The message "Device error: crypto codec cn-crypto-0 queue is stuck." will appear in the ltm log file.
bugs.conditions: Nitrox based system performing SSL under heavy load.
bugs.impact: Device errors reported in logs and crypto HA action is taken, possibly resulting in failing over.
bugs.workaround: Modify the crypto queue timeout value to 0 to prevent timeouts. tmsh modify sys db crypto.queue.timeout value 0
bugs.fix: The Nitrox crypto driver will now only examine requests in the hardware DMA ring to detect a stuck queue.

bugs.title: Pipeline reject in HTTP filter is not enforced in certain cases.
bugs.symptoms: Pipeline reject in HTTP filter is not enforced in certain cases.
bugs.conditions: A HTTP::respond or HTTP::redirect is currently sinking a request. The next request arrives within the same packet as part of the sunk request.
bugs.impact: Pipelined data incorrectly allowed as the next request.
bugs.fix: The passthrough_pipeline reject option will reject requests arriving within the same packet as a sunk request.

bugs.title: VCMP guests sflow agent can crash due to duplicate vlan interface indices
bugs.symptoms: When a VCMP guest uses sflow, the sflow agent will crash when it tries to add a row to its internal data structure and finds the key already exists for some other entry.
bugs.conditions: The problem is specific to BIG-IP i-Series platforms (i5200, i7200, i10200) with VCMP guests of 4 or more cores. 8 cores causes it all the time.
bugs.impact: sflow agent will crash.
bugs.fix: Make sure the allocated interface index for a vlan is not already taken by another interface object.

bugs.title: Policy may become unsyncable after changing contexts
bugs.symptoms: This is a known issue due to internal framework in MCPD which marks configurable objects as either synced and non-synced. If the user applies the policy to a non-syncing context (non-floating self-IP), then that policy won't be synced across HA devices anymore.
bugs.conditions: A config with standalone firewall policy applied to synced and non synced context.
bugs.impact: A policy that is assigned to otherwise non-syncing context, e.g. non-floating self-IP, the attached policy will no longer be synced even if attached to a syncing object later.
bugs.workaround: Create a "local" policy for non-floating self-IP only.

bugs.title: APM policy sync results are not persisted on target devices
bugs.symptoms: Policy sync results, including profile, sync folder, new partition, statuses, history are not persisted on target devices after sync, when there are no LSO resolution.
bugs.conditions: - Create an APM policy with no LSO to resolve, or have an APM policy that has LSO resolved by previous sync - Start a policy sync
bugs.impact: Sync results including the policy profiles won't be persisted so when the bigip restarts, all the sync data won't be lost.
bugs.workaround: Run tmsh command to save config: tmsh save sys config
bugs.fix: Policy sync result will be persisted on target devices so even when those devices restart, the data will still be there.

bugs.title: Failure to load config post upgrade: "Rate threshold cannot be set to 0."
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, configurations with DoS rate thresholds set may fail to load with a "Rate threshold cannot be set to 0" error message in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: DoS Protection configured with rate thresholds on a pre-12.0 installation. Upgrade to 12.0 and above.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP will fail to load the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit bigip.conf and remove all DoS rate threshold settings. Once the configuration successfully loads, apply the desired rate thresholds.

bugs.title: Server shutdown is propagated to client after X-Cnection: close transformation.
bugs.symptoms: Server shutdown is propagated to client after X-Cnection: close transformation.
bugs.conditions: In OneConnect configurations, when a server's maximum number of keep-alives is exceeded, the server closes the connection between itself and the BIG-IP system. This Connection: Close is transformed to an X-Cnection: close and sent to the Client along with a TCP FIN.
bugs.impact: Client side connections are closed by the BIG-IP system too early, causing subsequent requests to be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Set the OneConnect profile "Maximum Reuse" value to 2 below the value of the pool members max keep-alive setting. This forces OneConnect to close the connection before the pool member.
bugs.fix: Server shutdown is no longer propagated to client after X-Cnection: close transformation, so client side connections are now kept open by the BIG-IP system as expected, and subsequent requests are no longer dropped.

bugs.title: TMM crash in DNS processing on TCP virtual with no available pool members
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when processing requests to a DNS virtual server.
bugs.conditions: The issue can occur if a TCP DNS virtual receives a request when no pool members are available to service the request and a DNS iRule is suspended due to previous requests.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation is to ensure at least one pool member is available whenever the DNS virtual is processing traffic, or to avoid iRule commands that can suspend processing. Ensure datagram LB mode is enabled on UDP DNS virtuals.
bugs.fix: Product corrected to prevent crash when there are no available members.

bugs.title: Domain-name-strict has been deprecated, but is still present in GUI, GUI OLH, and TMSH CLI help.
bugs.symptoms: Domain-name-strict has been deprecated. The default is now domain-name-check allow-underscore. Upon loading a pre-existing configuration file, the following warning message will be logged in /var/log/ltm: -- Warning generated : value strict is deprecated. Forcing to allow-underscore. -- Configuration warning: value strict is deprecated. Forcing to allow-underscore. Upon loading a pre-existing configuration file, a warning will also be displayed in the console: value strict is deprecated. Forcing to allow-underscore.
bugs.conditions: Loading a pre-existing configuration file containing domain-name-strict.
bugs.impact: Although warnings are posted, the files are still loaded. However, GUI, GUI OLH, and TMSH CLI help have 'strict' as an option, and which is not accurate.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the 'strict' options, even though they are listed.

bugs.title: HSB may drop off of PCI bus
bugs.symptoms: The HSB may drop off of the PCI bus. This results failure to read the HSB registers, which is indicated by the following log entries in the tmm logfile: Device error: hsb_lbb1 hde1_crc_errs count 65535. Device error: hsb_lbb1 hde2_crc_errs count 65535. This is usually followed by SIGABRT. The subsequent TMM reload fails to load the HSB device. Querying the PCI bus (using lspci), shows that the HSB device is unavailable: 03:00.0 Ethernet controller: F5 Networks Inc. Device 0006 (rev ff) (prog-if ff) !!! Unknown header type 7f
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: Disruption of traffic. Request unit reboot.
bugs.workaround: Reboot unit.

bugs.title: Local password policy not enforced when auth source is set to a remote type.
bugs.symptoms: Local password policy not enforced when auth source is set to a remote type. Any non-default password policy change is not enforced for local users.
bugs.conditions: 1) Some part of the local password policy has been changed from the default values, for example, changing the password minimum-length to 12 where the default is 6. 2) The auth source is set to a remote source, such as LDAP, AD, TACACS.
bugs.impact: The system does not enforce any of the non-default local password policy options. For example, even if the minimum-length is set to 12, a local user's password can be set to something less than 12. Another example, even if the max-duration is set to 90 days, the password does not expire for 99999 days (the default).
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now honors the password policy settings for local accounts. However, this does not address complexity issues. That is tracked under ID 928161. For more information see https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID928161.html

bugs.title: Save on Auto-Sync is missing from the configuration utility.
bugs.symptoms: The option to configure save-on-auto-sync is missing in the Device Management GUI.
bugs.conditions: Devices configured in a DSC configuration. Automatic with Full or Incremental Sync is enabled. You attempt to configure the save-on-auto-sync option from the GUI.
bugs.impact: You will need to have TMSH access to the BIG-IP system to perform this task.
bugs.workaround: You will need to have TMSH access to the BIG-IP system to perform this task.
bugs.fix: This release adds per-device-group save_on_auto_sync flag to GUI: flag now shows in GUI and correctly saves. GUI: The "Sync Type" option in the GUI must be set to "Automatic with Full/Incremental Sync" in order for "Save on Auto-Sync" option to show.
bugs.behavior: Beginning in version 11.5.0, the /cm trust-domain 'save-on-auto-sync' attribute is no longer configured as part of the trust-domain, but is part of the configuration of a device group. With this change, the option to set that attribute becomes available in the GUI on the condition that the "Sync Type" option is set to "Automatic with Full/Incremental Sync".

bugs.title: IPv4 fragments are dropped when packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: IPv4 fragments are dropped when packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Packet filtering is enabled on version 11.5.4, 11.6.0 HF6, or 11.6.1.
bugs.impact: IPv4 fragments with a non-zero offset are lost.
bugs.workaround: Disable packet filtering.
bugs.fix: IPv4 fragments are no longer incorrectly dropped when packet filtering is enabled.

bugs.title: Upgrade script for SSO log-level
bugs.symptoms: In 12.1.0 and previous versions, SSO SAML and SSO FormBasedV2 object has log-level attribute, which has been replaced by an apm log config object.
bugs.conditions: If previous configuration contains SSO SAML objects or SSO FormBasedV2 objects upgraded to versions later than 12.1.0.
bugs.impact: After upgrade, no apm log config object is created for the SSO object.
bugs.fix: The upgrade script will now create apm log config object to replace log-level. The publisher's destination for it will be local-syslog. SSO log-level in the new apm log config object will remain the same. The new apm log config's name will be sso-log-setting-<log level>, <log level> can be Debug, Notice, Alert and so on. Warning Message 'apm log-setting is created as the log setting for sso objects. Access : ' will show in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.behavior: The Upgrade script for SSO log-level will create apm log config object to replace log-level. The publisher's destination for it will be local-syslog. SSO log-level in the new apm log config object will remain the same. The new apm log config's name will be sso-log-setting-<log level>, <log level> can be Debug, Notice, Alert and so on. Warning Message 'apm log-setting is created as the log setting for sso objects. Access : ' will show in /var/log/ltm. There is no impact to traffic; the upgrade will automatically create the necessary log config object for you.

bugs.title: For unmatched connection TCP RST may not be sent for data packet
bugs.symptoms: When AFM is enabled TCP RST will not be sent to client when client sends data packet to BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: When AFM is enabled and in TCP profile , timeout of reset is disabled, after connection times out RST wont be sent. But if BIG-IP receives data packet bigip does not send TCP RST.
bugs.impact: When client does not receive TCP RST for data packet sent for unmatched connection , generally timed out, Client keeps retrying, but BIG-IP shouldn't send TCP RST to all the packets received for unmatched connections.
bugs.workaround: Reset on timeout option can be enabled which will send TCP RST to client when connection times out. But if the BIG-IP reboots, client wont get TCP RST.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now sends a TCP RST for unknown connections so the clients and backend servers can start a new connection.

bugs.title: encryption_key in access config is NULL in whitelist
bugs.symptoms: encryption_key in access config is NULL sometime when applying 404 whitelist action and will result in TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: All the following must be true: - Access policy action resulted in a "not found". - The session corresponding to above action must be expired. - FIPS platform.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Data required to serve a "not found" action is retrieved and made available early so that such responses can be served correctly.

bugs.title: 10-core vCMP guest with ASM may not pass traffic
bugs.symptoms: The TMM plugin manager does not expect/support an ASM guest configuration of 10 cores, thus its calculations as to the number of devices required and numbering does not match the existing number of threads/devices.
bugs.conditions: 11.6.0 HF6 ASM provisioned on a vCMP guest 10 CPU cores allocated to an ASM guest
bugs.impact: System may not start or may exhibit intermittent failures.
bugs.workaround: Change the number of cores on the ASM guest to use either 8 CPU cores or 12 CPU cores.
bugs.fix: This issue was partially fixed in 11.6.0 HF6, but the tmplugin RPM was incorrect. This fix includes the proper RPM.

bugs.title: Modification to custom provisioning does not yield expected results.
bugs.symptoms: When a system is configured with one or more custom provisioning profiles, modifications to these profiles have no immediate effect. Moreover, there is no indication the system must be rebooted before these changes take effect.
