bugs.conditions: Modify one or more custom provisioning profiles.
bugs.impact: Provisioning modifications do not have any effect until the system is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: Reboot after provisioning changes.

bugs.title: DHCP server connFlow when created based on the DHCP client connFlow does not have the traffic group ID copied
bugs.symptoms: Variables in the flow context when stored in the sessionDB cannot be shared since the traffic groups of the server and client flows are different.
bugs.conditions: DHCP virtual created in a non-local traffic group.
bugs.impact: Variable sharing in the TCL context will not work.
bugs.workaround: Modify SysDb variable "Tmm.SessionDB.match_ha_unit" to disable the use of traffic-group ID while accessing the sessionDB.
bugs.fix: Copy the traffic group from client to server connFlows such that both connFlows have the same traffic group.

bugs.title: tmm core on the standby unit with dos vectors configured
bugs.symptoms: On the standby unit with mirrored connections configured, uninitialized dos_vectors may cause core dump
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: HA setup, mirroring enabled on a virtual that has dos vectors configured

bugs.title: iOS Edge Client Per-App VPN and MobileSDK connections should consume CCU license
bugs.symptoms: iOS Edge Client Per-App VPN and MobileSDK connections does not consume CCU license
bugs.conditions: iOS Edge Client Per-App VPN and MobileSDK
bugs.impact: CCU license not consumed

bugs.title: Rarely, an HSB transmitter failure occurs
bugs.symptoms: A very rare HSB transmitter failure occurs. This is indicated by the following message in the tmm logs: panic: hsb interface 1 DMA lockup on transmitter failure.
bugs.conditions: Although the exact conditions for this issue are unknown, this might be related to a 5250 platform or to a configuration containing a vCMP guest.
bugs.impact: Reboot of the unit.

bugs.title: Stress CPU on BIG-IP will also take into the packets dropped by hardware.
bugs.symptoms: Rate limit is directly proportional to CPU stress seen by the BIG-IP system. DoS will rate-limit traffic in hardware (HW) when the BIG-IP system is under stress (CPU is high), then if packets are dropped by HW and CPU of the system will come down and hence DOS will stop rate-limiting. SO this kind of behavior could result in toggling of DOS rate-limit state.
bugs.conditions: -- DoS in HW starts rate-limit in HW. -- DoS has autodos enabled.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may see that one second, DoS is rate-limiting packets and next second, it is allowing packets, and then next second it starts rate-limiting again, and so on. So there will be toggling of DoS vector mitigation state.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to disable autodosd for that vector.

bugs.title: RAT-Detection alerts sent with incorrect duration details
bugs.symptoms: If a remote access trojan (RAT) detection alert is thrown immediately upon initialization, the timestamp of the alert will be incorrect.
bugs.conditions: -- Enable RAT detection. -- RAT detection alert is countered within 5 seconds of initialization.
bugs.impact: False positives
bugs.fix: When generating RAT Detected alert within 5 seconds from page load, actualCounter in alert details is lower than 5 seconds for example: "timeToResetCounter":5000,"actualCounter":4296

bugs.title: ePVA does not offload UDP when pva-offload-state set to establish in BIG-IP 12.1.0 and 12.1.1
bugs.symptoms: When a fastL4 profile's pva-offload-state set to establish (default is embryonic), the corresponding UDP virtual server using that profile won't offload UDP traffic and causes performance degradation.
bugs.conditions: This issue is introduced during v12.0.0 development and only impacts v12.1.0 and v12.1.1 releases. A fastL4 UDP virtual server is using a fastL4 profile that has pva-offload-state set to establish.
bugs.impact: Performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: Use default setting for pva-offload-state of embryonic for fastL4 profile.
bugs.fix: With the fix in 12.1.2 and 13.0.0, ePVA will load UDP traffic when pva-offload-state set to establish.

bugs.title: NTP Security Updates
bugs.symptoms: It was found that the fix for was incomplete: three issues were found in the value length checks in NTP's ntp_crypto.c, where a packet with particular autokey operations that contained malicious data was not always being completely validated. A remote attacker could use a specially crafted NTP packet to crash ntpd. A memory leak flaw was found in ntpd's CRYPTO_ASSOC. If ntpd was configured to use autokey authentication, an attacker could send packets to ntpd that would, after several days of ongoing attack, cause it to run out of memory. An off-by-one flaw, leading to a buffer overflow, was found in cookedprint functionality of ntpq. A specially crafted NTP packet could potentially cause ntpq to crash. A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the way ntpd processed 'ntpdc reslist' commands that queried restriction lists with a large amount of entries. A remote attacker could potentially use this flaw to crash ntpd. A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in the way ntpd processed 'ntpdc reslist' commands that queried restriction lists with a large amount of entries. A remote attacker could use this flaw to crash ntpd. It was found that ntpd could crash due to an uninitialized variable when processing malformed logconfig configuration commands. It was found that ntpd would exit with a segmentation fault when a statistics type that was not enabled during compilation (e.g. timingstats) was referenced by the statistics or filegen configuration command. It was discovered that the sntp utility could become unresponsive due to being caught in an infinite loop when processing a crafted NTP packet. It was found that NTP's :config command could be used to set the pidfile and driftfile paths without any restrictions. A remote attacker could use this flaw to overwrite a file on the file system with a file containing the pid of the ntpd process (immediately) or the current estimated drift of the system clock (in hourly intervals).
bugs.conditions: NTP enabled.
bugs.impact: ntpd crash.
bugs.fix: NTP updates applied via RHSA-2016:0780.

bugs.title: Launching RDP resources of "Native" type requires downloading .rdp files which are not cleaned automatically
bugs.symptoms: For now, in order to launch a native RDP resource, user needs to download an automatically generated .rdp file which is later used for launching RDP client. Since MS RDP client doesn't support cleaning those files up automatically, users should bear in mind that those files may accrue in their "Downloads" folder over time.
bugs.conditions: Launching native RDP resource.
bugs.impact: Downloaded .rdp files are not automatically removed by RDP client.
bugs.workaround: Remove .rdp files manually from "Downloads" folder from time to time.

bugs.title: Javascript parser incompatible with ECMA6/7+
bugs.symptoms: A web application mis-functions on the client side
bugs.conditions: -- APM proxying a web application -- Web-application uses ES6/7 or higher javascript
bugs.impact: Web application mis-function
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with Javascript rewrite not occurring on ECMA6/7 Javascript.

bugs.title: Raw sockets are not enabled on Cloud platforms
bugs.symptoms: Cloud VMs come configured with UNIC driver instead of using raw sockets.
bugs.conditions: Cloud deployment - AWS and Azure.
bugs.impact: UNIC is used instead of raw sockets.
bugs.workaround: Manually disabling unic driver will force raw sockets to be used.
bugs.fix: Enabled raw sockets by default on Cloud deployments.

bugs.title: Remove debug output during first boot of VE
bugs.symptoms: There was unneeded debug output during 1st boot of VE on Cloud deployments.
bugs.conditions: Cloud deployment - AWS and Azure.
bugs.impact: Extra debug output on 1st boot.
bugs.fix: Debug output was removed.

bugs.title: TMM crashed with SIGSEGV and possible mr_proxy cores.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashed with SIGSEGV and possible mr_proxy cores.
bugs.impact: Unknown

bugs.title: libQt5WebKit.so.5 is required to install F5 web clients
bugs.symptoms: When installing web client packages downloaded from APM, installation may fail on certain Linux distributions with the following error message: nothing provides libQt5WebKit.so.5().
bugs.conditions: Installation is attempted on a Linux distribution running a pre-5.0 version of libQT.
bugs.impact: User cannot install F5 web clients for VPN and endpoint check on Linux.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, either use a distribution of Linux that has libQt5WebKit.so.5 or later installed, or install libQt5WebKit.so.5 or later before installing web clients.

bugs.title: IE11 and Chrome throw "Access denied" during access to any generic window property after document.write() into its parent has been performed
bugs.symptoms: IE11 and Chrome throw "Access denied" during access to any generic window property after document.write() into its parent has been performed from dynamically generated child.
bugs.conditions: Browsers: IE11 and Chrome When: After document.write() into its parent has been performed from dynamically generated child.
bugs.impact: Web application malfunction.
bugs.fix: Fixed.

bugs.title: Idle timeout ineffective for FIN_WAIT_2 when server-side expired and HTTP in fallback state.
bugs.symptoms: While passing normal traffic, CPU utilization of one or more tmms suddenly goes to 100% as viewed by top and remains there indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: Idle timeout for tcp flows in FIN_WAIT_2.
bugs.impact: There is a rare occurrence in which tmm might result in 100% CPU busy.
bugs.fix: This release honors the idle timeout in FIN_WAIT_2 when server-side expired and HTTP in fallback state.

bugs.title: TMM 'timer' device does not report 'busy' for non-priority timers.
bugs.symptoms: A discrepancy in CPU utilization reporting can observed when looking at different utilities or reporting systems (i.e. top, tmctl, SNMP, the performance graphs in the GUI, etc.). Specifically, certain utilities may report that TMM hyperthreads are 100% busy, while other utilities may indicate that TMM instances are only moderately busy. In this case, the utilities or systems reporting the higher CPU utilization are correct.
bugs.conditions: This issue has been seen extremely rarely, as it requires some other edge condition to also be occurring (TMM firing non-priority timers in a looping manner).
bugs.impact: A BIG-IP Administrator monitoring CPU utilization on the system may be confused about how busy TMM actually is. Although the main impacted system here is the tmm/stat tmctl table, these values are also exposed via the sysTmmStatTmUsageRatio5s MIB (which is more likely to be monitored by a BIG-IP Administrator).
bugs.workaround: Refer to utilities such as 'top' to monitor the CPU utilization of TMM hyperthreads.

bugs.title: False positive illegal length violation can appear
bugs.symptoms: A false positive illegal length violation.
bugs.conditions: A chunked request where the request length is more than half of the configured max request length.
bugs.impact: False positive illegal length violation.
bugs.workaround: Configure a higher max request length violation.
bugs.fix: Fixed a false positive request length violation.

bugs.title: Deleting access profile prompts for apply access policy for other untouched access profiles
bugs.symptoms: After deleting an access profile, the 'Apply Access Policy' link shows up and the status flags for some other untouched access profiles turn yellow. Also, there are APM log messages indicating that the configurations for those untouched access profile have been changed.
bugs.conditions: If an access profile containing macros is copied on the admin UI and is deleted subsequently.
bugs.impact: There is no change to the access profiles that are affected by the deletion. Admin can go ahead to click "Apply Access Policy" link to make the link disappear.
bugs.fix: The 'Apply Access Policy' link no longer appears when it is not applicable.

bugs.title: Some Access Policy sessions may not be sent over High Speed Logging destinations.
bugs.symptoms: At high APM (Access Policy) load, some sessions may fail to be reported through High Speed Logging destinations while these session logs can be found in other destinations, i.e., local-db or local-syslog.
bugs.conditions: -- APM configured to send logs over High Speed Logging. -- High APM load.
bugs.impact: Some Access session logs are not sent to High Speed Logging destinations.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for remote High Speed Logging destinations, however, to avoid losing logs, ensure that APM session logs are sent to local-db.
bugs.fix: Logs sent by the APM modules are delivered successfully over High Speed Logging.

bugs.title: An Application can fail to connect to a backend server in some cases if Optimized tunnels configured using hostnames ony
bugs.symptoms: If NA resource contains only Optimized tunnels, which uses hostnames only, application might fail to connect to a backend server if NA resource was manually reconnected and this application had already established a connection to this server before this reconnect.
bugs.conditions: - NA resource with Optimized Tunnels only - Optimized tunnel configured using hostname only - NA resource was manually reconnected or user created a new APM session - User application established the first connection before the NA was manually disconnected and connected again.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the configured network resources.
bugs.workaround: Several options can be considered Option #1 Add Optimised tunnels using IP address to this NA resource Option #2 Configure Network Tunnel with a proper IP Split Scope for this NA resource Option #3 Restarting the user application might help

bugs.title: iRule validation does not catch incorrect 'after' syntax
bugs.symptoms: iRule validation does not catch iRule with incorrect 'after' syntax, allowing an invalid iRule to be saved.
bugs.conditions: iRule with incorrect 'after' syntax. For example "after 5000 periodic" should be "after 5000 -periodic" (with a hyphen)
bugs.impact: Traffic handled by the iRule fails, generating the Tcl error 'invalid command name 'periodic' while executing 'periodic LB::reselect''.
bugs.workaround: Correct the syntax error.

bugs.title: Thales client install requires an SSH username, and always attempts to SSH into the RFS
bugs.symptoms: The Thales client installation operation always attempts to SSH into the RFS machine as part of the install script, and always requires an ssh-login.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP user installing Thales nethsm client software. -- The BIG-IP user does not have an SSH login to the RFS server.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP user must supply the script with an SSH login name, even if it is expected that the command will fail. Thales client installation fails otherwise.
bugs.workaround: As long as the RFS user can run the following command, the existing script will work, even if the user is non-root: /opt/nfast/bin/rfs-setup --force -g --write-noauth <BIG-IP IP address> If the BIG-IP system cannot log into the RFS at all, you must supply a dummy login for the RFS, because the unpatched script requires an SSH username, and will always attempt to log into the RFS. With a dummy login, although this step fails, the script attempts to recover as follows: -- Instructs the user to run the following command manually on the RFS: /opt/nfast/bin/rfs-setup --force -g --write-noauth <BIG-IP IP address> -- Asks whether the command completed successfully. As long as someone runs that command on the RFS before attempting or continuing Thales installation, the operation should complete without issue. Note: It is possible to run this command on the RFS before even attempting to run the Thales installation script on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Thales install now works with a non-root login to the RFS server or with no login at all.

bugs.title: TCP: connections may stall or be dropped
bugs.symptoms: TCP connections stall or get dropped.
bugs.conditions: Under some network conditions especially with rateshaper enabled TCP connection could stall and ultimately get reset.
bugs.impact: This usually happens with rateshaper or BWC enabled. Rarely could also happen with very lossy networks.
bugs.fix: Properly manage re-transmissions after a tail drop by not not doing the exponential back-off. Reset the re-transmit timer for every partial ack received after a tail drop.

bugs.title: IPv6 data pulled from the BIG-IP system via HTTPS, SCP, SSH, DNS or SMTP performance
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 data pulled from the BIG-IP system via HTTPS, SCP, SSH, DNS or SMTP might encounter significant performance impacts when initiated over a BIG-IP data port using IPv6.
bugs.conditions: -- Protocols: HTTPS, SCP, SSH, DNS, SMTP. -- IPv6. Note: Management port is not impacted.
bugs.impact: Performance impact pulling data over affected ports from the BIG-IP over IPv6. BIG-IQ performance is impacted trying to manage BIG-IP devices over IPv6.
bugs.workaround: Disable TSO for IPv6 at the command line by running the following command: ethtool -K tmm tso off. Note: This command must be run each time after reboot.
bugs.fix: The issue has been corrected, so that there is no performance impact pulling data over affected ports using HTTPS, SCP, SSH, DNS or SMTP from the BIG-IP over IPv6, and there is no BIG-IQ performance issue managing BIG-IP devices over IPv6.

bugs.title: iControl SOAP method System.Failover.get_peer_address might return incorrect value.
bugs.symptoms: iControl SOAP method System.Failover.get_peer_address returns no results. In DSC sync (11.0.0 or later), there is no longer a concept of a 'secondary peer address', and one can connect with more than one other device, so this method no longer can always return acceptable values. Therefore, the alternate method Management.Device.get_configsync_address is recommended.
bugs.conditions: Any 11.0.0 or higher platform with CMI configured.
bugs.impact: If the iControl SOAP method System.Failover.get_peer_address method is being used to determine whether sync is configured between two devices, the system might falsely treat the device as a standalone.
bugs.workaround: Use the the following method instead: Management.Device.get_configsync_address.
bugs.fix: The iControl SOAP method System.Failover.get_peer_address has been immediately deprecated. Use the method Management.Device.get_configsync_address instead.

bugs.title: Validation against routes where the network route-domain does not match VLAN route-domain
bugs.symptoms: Kernel ioctl error when creating static route, "ioctl failed: No such device"
bugs.conditions: When creating static route where the network route-domain is not the same as the VLAN route-domain
bugs.impact: Prevent the creation of the static route.
bugs.workaround: Use the correct route-domain when specifying the network for the static route entry.
bugs.fix: When creating static route using a VLAN that have non-default route-domain, validation will either correct the network route-domain - when it is unspecified, or throw validation error when specified route-domain did not match VLAN route-domain.

bugs.title: BMC timezone value was not being synchronized by BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: You notice that errors on the LCD have an incorrect timestamp compared to what is reported in BIG-IP
bugs.conditions: This can occur when running the 12.1.1 base release on the BIG-IP i-Series platforms.
bugs.impact: Timestamp is reported in the wrong time zone.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with incorrect timestamp reporting on the LCD display

bugs.title: Default value of device-request timeout factor might cause false alert: Hardware Error ni3-crypto request queue stuck.
bugs.symptoms: Default value of device-request timeout factor might cause false alert: Hardware Error ni3-crypto request queue stuck.
bugs.conditions: In case of heavy SSL traffic, Cavium Nitrox SSL hardware accelerator card might need more time than the default interval to complete the encryption or decryption.
bugs.impact: The /var/log/ltm log contains the following message: Hardware Error(Co-Processor): n3-crypto1 request queue stuck. tmm will be in failure state.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to increase the device.request.timeoutfactor db variable to allow more time for encryption or decryption to complete. For example, to increase device.request.timeoutfactor to 200, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db device.request.timeoutfactor value 200. To clear erroneously stuck queues, you must restart tmm or reboot the BIG-IP system. Note: Traffic is disrupted while during restarts.
bugs.fix: The default value of device.request.timeoutfactor is now sufficient to allow the Cavium Nitrox SSL hardware accelerator card to complete the encryption or decryption as expected.

bugs.title: Radius AVP parsing might get out of sync on Vendor-Specific AVP iRules.
bugs.symptoms: Radius AVP parsing might get out of sync on Vendor-Specific AVP iRules and produce a Tcl error: Buffer error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is an iRule looking for a specific Vendor-Specific AVP, and a Radius Packet that contains a different Vendor-Specific AVP, that comes alphabetically before the one in the iRule.
bugs.impact: Tcl Error and potentially a dropped request. The error is similar to the following: err tmm3[12353]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common <CLIENT_ACCEPTED> - Buffer error (line 1) (line 1) invoked from within "RADIUS::avp 26 string vendor-id 9 vendor-type 1.

bugs.title: Compression stalls, does not recover, and compression facilities cease.
bugs.symptoms: Compression stalls, does not recover, and compression facilities may cease.
bugs.conditions: A device error of any kind, or requests that result in the device reporting an error (for example, attempting to decompress an invalid compression stream).
bugs.impact: In general, compression stops altogether. Under some circumstances, compression requests may end up routed to zlib (software compression), but generally the SSL hardware accelerator card does not correctly report that it is unavailable when it stalls.
bugs.workaround: Select the softwareonly compression provider by running the following tmsh command: tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy value softwareonly.
bugs.fix: The compression device driver now attempts to recover after a failure. If it still cannot recover, new compression requests will be assigned to zlib (software) for compression.

bugs.title: Enabling of whitelists on a protected object requires disabling DoS protection support in hardware
bugs.symptoms: On certain platforms, DDoS protection support in hardware prevents configuration of a whitelist for a protected object.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration of a whitelist on a protected object. -- Hardware acceleration is configured on 5xxx/7xxx/10xxx/12xxx appliances, and all blades other than B2250/B4450.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure whitelist on a protected object.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware support for DDoS protection from the command line using the following command: modify sys db dos.forceswdos value true. Note: Disabling DDoS hardware support might impact the performance of the device because then, all DDoS protection mechanisms are managed in software.

bugs.title: Protocol version set incorrectly on serverssl renegotiation
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP serverssl profile sends a new ClientHello request to renegotiate SSL, the protocol version will be set to 0. This will cause renegotiation to fail.
bugs.conditions: ServerSSL profile configured on a virtual server, and BIG-IP initiates a renegotiation.
bugs.impact: Protocol field is invalid (0), and the server will reset the connection.
bugs.fix: Fixed a reset issue with SSL renegotiation in the serverssl profile.

bugs.title: Rewrite may crash processing HTML tag with HTML entity in attribute value
bugs.symptoms: If HTML page contains HTML entities in attribute values, rewrite may crash processing this page.
bugs.conditions:
HTML tag like this: <script src="
" type="text/javascript"></script>
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: In most cases HTML entities can be replaced by appropriate characters by iRule.
bugs.fix: Now rewrite correctly handles HTML entities in attribute values.

bugs.title: Syntax Error when reimporting exported content containing acl-order 0
bugs.symptoms: Syntax Error when reimporting exported content containing acl-order 0. The error message is similar to the following. Syntax Error: ... 'acl-order' may not be specified more than once; Validating configuration...
bugs.conditions: Exported config has apm resource with acl-order 0.
bugs.impact: Unable to import exported .conf.tar.gz.
bugs.fix: It is now possible to export and then import config that contains apm resource with acl-order 0.

bugs.title: Fast successive MTU changes to IPsec tunnel interface crashes TMM
bugs.symptoms: Changing IPsec tunnel interface MTU attribute repeatedly in quick succession, TMM cores. This can occur whether or not traffic has flowed through the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when quickly changing the IPsec tunnel interface MTU.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Change IPsec tunnel interface attributes at a rate of speed that allows each configuration modification to complete.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores if users quickly and repeatedly change interface attributes (for example, the MTU interface attribute).

bugs.title: Cavium Nitrox PX/III stuck queue diagnostics missing.
bugs.symptoms: Diagnostics tool to investigate rare issue where the Cavium Nitrox PX/III crypto chip gets into a "request queue stuck" situation.
bugs.conditions: System with Cavium Nitrox PX/III chip(s) which includes the BIG-IP 5xxx, 7xxx, 10xxx, and 12xxx platforms as well as the VIPRIOn B2200 blade, that hits a rare issue which logs a "request queue stuck" message in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.impact: This tool enables F5 engineers to obtain more data about this problem to help diagnose the issue.
bugs.fix: Provides a diagnostics tool. Does not directly mitigate the problem.

bugs.title: Configuring connection mirroring when using AFM send_to_virtual action
bugs.symptoms: Connection mirroring will not work if enabled only on the virtual server configured as send_to_virtual parameter.
bugs.conditions: Connection mirroring is only configured on the virtual server referenced by send_to_virtual parameter and not on the original virtual matched by traffic.
bugs.impact: Connection mirroring will not work
bugs.workaround: You must configure connection mirroring both on the original virtual server that would be matched by traffic and on the virtual referenced by send_to_virtual command
bugs.fix: User must configure connection mirroring both on the original virtual server that would be matched by traffic and on the virtual referenced by send_to_virtual command

bugs.title: TMM may crash with multiple IP addresses per session
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash
bugs.conditions: A session with multiple IP addresses with PCRF communication for dynamic policy management may have a crash credits to a race condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Check for timer expiration prior to processing the timer.

bugs.title: CATEGORY::filetype command may cause tmm to crash and restart
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule command is created using the CATEGORY::filetype command, the tmm may eventually suffer a failure, and restart.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using the CATEGORY::filetype iRule under normal operation.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash in CATEGORY::filetype

bugs.title: userDefined property for bot signatures is not shown in REST
bugs.symptoms: The user defined property of the signature is not exposed in iControl REST.
bugs.conditions: Attempting an iControl REST API call to see a signature.
bugs.impact: The userDefined field is not shown. Impacts external interfaces interacting with the BIG-IP configuration and expecting to see a field and a value there.
bugs.fix: The userDefined field exists now and has a true/false values.

bugs.title: FPS may erroneously flag missing cookie
bugs.symptoms: You see Missing Cookie errors for validation errors other than Missing Cookie.
bugs.conditions: Any component validation error.
bugs.impact: Missing Cookie errors counted when the validation error was not due to Missing Cookie
bugs.workaround: No.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with Missing Cookie error counting.

bugs.title: repeated failures on scheduled Signature Update (ASU)
bugs.symptoms: This produces errors similar to the following: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- asm_config_server.pl|INFO|Dec 11 04:02:03.697|9905|F5::Sigfile::AutoDownload::call_soap_server,,Calling 'https://10.10.10.10/esd/services/ASMUpdate' for new Signature version. asm_config_server.pl|ERR|Dec 11 04:02:08.199|9905|F5::Sigfile::AutoDownload::call_soap_server,,SOAP request failed: 500 read failed: ----------------------------------------------------------------------
bugs.conditions: ASM Provisoned
bugs.impact: repeated failures on scheduled Signature Update (ASU)
bugs.workaround: change the time the job runs daily and see if that resolves the issue. \\ First open up the cron job text file \\ # vi /etc/crontab Change this line - 02 4 * * * root run-parts /etc/cron.daily to - 10 4 * * * root run-parts /etc/cron.daily Save and quit. This will change the automatic updates to run @4:10 rather than 4:02.
bugs.fix: We've implemented a retry of a failed scheduled Signature Update (ASU).

bugs.title: The malformed MAC for inner pkt with dummy MAC for NSH with VXLAN-GPE.
bugs.symptoms: The target platform implementation need to be ensure that it is update to date with draft and additionally tested with other open sources and commercial implementations to deem stable. If not a stable and production version as in case below, sender packets can be with a dummy MAC which is not recognized by BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: Target platforms which may be unstable and untested in VXLAN-GPE.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP drop packets since it does not recognize inner pkt MAC.
bugs.workaround: Ensure target platform is stable, tested and production version wrt VXLAN-GPE and NSH.

bugs.title: Profile lookup when selected via iRule ('SSL::profile') might cause memory issues.
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule selects a profile using just its name, not the full path, the internal lookup might fail. This might cause a new version of the profile to be instantiated, leading to memory issues.
bugs.conditions: An iRule calls SSL::profile but does not supply the complete path (e.g., /Common/clientssl); rather, the iRule uses only the profile name.
bugs.impact: Higher memory usage than necessary.
bugs.workaround: Always have iRules select profiles using the complete path.
bugs.fix: If an iRule attempts to select a profile using only its name, the system now prepends the /Common path prior to looking it up, so there is no potential of instantiating another version of the profile, so no memory issue occurs.

bugs.title: Stateless virtual servers may not work correctly with route pools or ECMP routes
bugs.symptoms: Stateless virtual servers might not work correctly if the configured poolmember is reachable via a route pool or via several ECMP routes learned via dynamic routing.
bugs.conditions: - Stateless virtual server. - Pool reachable via route pool or via ECMP routes.
bugs.impact: Traffic might be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Use other virtual server types to process this traffic.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly handles traffic to a Stateless virtual server which makes use of route pools or ECMP routes to reach the poolmembers.

bugs.title: [Portal Access] URL normalization is required for some Javascript interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Several Javascript methods or properties should return normalized URL (i.e. without ports :80 for http: or :443 for https:, without /../ segments of path, etc.). Current code of Portal Access does not implement this.
bugs.impact: Web applications could fail with security or logic errors when they expect to get normalized URL from affected Javascript methods or properties.
bugs.behavior: Now not normalized URLs are not included in browser history (only in modern browsers).

bugs.title: In rare cases, connections may fail to expire
bugs.symptoms: Connections have an idle timeout of 4294967295 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Any IP (ipother) profile is assigned to virtual server.
bugs.impact: Connections may linger.
bugs.fix: Fixed idle initialization error when using Any IP (ipother) profile.

bugs.title: Device Group with incremental ConfigSync enabled might report 'In Sync' when devices have differing configurations
bugs.symptoms: Devices do not have matching configuration, but system reports device group as being 'In Sync'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Device Service Cluster Device Group with incremental sync is enabled. -- A ConfigSync operation occurs where a configuration transaction fails validation. -- A subsequent (or the final) configuration transaction is successful.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system incorrectly reports that the configuration is in-sync, despite the fact that it is not in sync. You might experience various, unexpected failures or unexplained behavior or traffic impact from this.
bugs.workaround: Turn off incremental sync (by enabling 'Full Sync' / 'full load on sync') for affected device groups. Once the systems are in sync, you can turn back on incremental sync, and it will work as expected.

bugs.title: iSession can't connect over default gateway pool
bugs.symptoms: iSession can't make wocd (and data) connections if the required route defined as pool.
bugs.conditions: define WOM BIGIP peer in different subnets with router(s) in the middle. If the route from one BIG-IP to the other is defined as POOL the WOM daemons will be unable to connect.
bugs.impact: WOM cannot establish an iSession tunnel
bugs.workaround: This issue can be mitigated if you can use a default gateway IP address instead of a default gateway pool.
bugs.fix: iSessions can now be established when using a default gateway pool

bugs.title: Dashboard displays incomplete alert details when Polish characters are included
bugs.symptoms: Polish alerts are not fully displayed fully in the dashboard.
bugs.conditions: Alert details contain Polish characters.
bugs.impact: Causes difficulty assigning alert severity.
bugs.fix: Alerts are now displayed correctly.

bugs.title: Improve access to localStorage
bugs.symptoms: In old FireFox version (19), exception is thrown when accessing local storage (nsIDOMStorage error).
bugs.conditions: access local-storage is ON in FireFox version (19)
bugs.impact: The Check Components feature is not working as expected.
bugs.fix: Protect access to local-storage.

bugs.title: CSRF doesn't look correctly into relative urls in the location header
bugs.symptoms: CSRF does not correctly look into relative URLs in the location header.
bugs.conditions: There is a relative URL in the location header.
bugs.impact: in some cases the location header is searched in the configuration as is, and is not found since it doesn't match the wildcard, which can trigger false positive CSRF violations.
bugs.fix: CSRF now correctly looks into relative URLs in the location header.

bugs.title: Sync fails when deleting an ssh profile
bugs.symptoms: After creating an ssh profile and successfully syncing it to the sync group, you later delete the profile and sync fails with this error on the target device: "err mcpd[5178]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/syncme to commit id 6 6285666289815053813 /Common/bigip2.mysite.com 0 failed with error 01071aaf:3: SSH profile: [/Common/ssh1] default actions is required and cannot be removed."
bugs.conditions: This is triggered when deleting an ssh profile that has been synced in a sync group. Sync group is configured for manual sync. It is not known if automatic sync also exhibits this behavior.
bugs.impact: Sync fails.

bugs.title: VE interface limit
bugs.symptoms: TMM fails to bootup successfully.
bugs.conditions: More than 10 interfaces assigned to Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.impact: BIG-IP fails to pass traffic as TMM fails to load successfully.
bugs.workaround: Make sure VE is assigned 10 or fewer interfaces.
bugs.fix: Added support for 32 interfaces on VE.

bugs.title: ssh profile should not contain rules that begin and end with spaces (cannot be deleted)
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to delete a rule for an ssh profile and committing the changes in the GUI, you get an error: "Operation is not supported on property /security/ssh/profile/~Common~ssh-test/rules."
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you previously created ssh profile rules that contain spaces in them, such as this example: create security ssh profile ssh-test actions add { " " } rules add { " " { actions add { " " } identity-users add { " "} identity-groups add { " " } } } auth-info add { " " }
bugs.impact: Unable to delete the rules
bugs.fix: You can now delete ssh profile rules that contain spaces for the rules.

bugs.title: tcpdump with :p misses first few packets on forwarding (UDP, FastL4) flows.
bugs.symptoms: When the tcpdump utility is used with the ':p' modifier, it appears that the first few serverside packets are not captured.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the ':p' modifier with the tcpdump utility to capture serverside flows associated with clientside flows that match a tcpdump filter. -- FastL4 or standard virtual server UDP flows are being captured.
bugs.impact: Typically, the peer flow will not be captured until the second packet is processed on the original flow that is captured by the tcpdump filter. Although there is no operational impact, it might cause confusion when looking for serverside traffic when capturing using a command similar to the following: tcpdump -i <vlan>:p host <client-ip> Typical examples of missing packets include: -- Serverside syn and syn-ack from FastL4 TCP traffic. -- All serverside packets for single packet request/reply traffic, e.g., dns request/reply.
bugs.workaround: Specify filter that includes serverside traffic (e.g., include pool member addresses as 'host <addr>').
bugs.fix: tcpdump now successfully captures the first serverside packets.

bugs.title: Sometimes when modifying the firewall rules, the blob does not compile and pccd restarts periodically
bugs.symptoms: With pccd.alwaysfromscratch set to true, the blob doesn't compile and pccd restarts periodically when firewall rules are modified.
bugs.conditions: 1. pccd.alwaysfromscratch is set to true (default value is false) 2. Modify some firewall rules.
bugs.impact: The blob doesn't compile and pccd keeps restarting without loading new rules.
bugs.workaround: Remove saved blob files in /var/pktclass/ (rm -f /var/pktclass/*) and restart pccd.

bugs.title: Pages using Angular may hang when Websafe is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Pages using angular may not load correctly when Websafe "inject Javascript into page" is enabled
bugs.conditions: Application using Angular.js Websafe: "inject Javascript into page" is enabled
bugs.impact: Page does not load fully
bugs.fix: Websafe no longer changes the page's "documentMode"

bugs.title: Resetting mgmt interface statistics doesn't work on VE or VCMP
bugs.symptoms: $ tmsh reset-stats net interface mgmt Doesn't reset mgmt interface statistics.
bugs.conditions: Only on VE or VCMP
bugs.impact: You cannot reset the management interface statistics, but this has no impact elsewhere in the system.
bugs.fix: This command $ tmsh reset-stats net interface mgmt resets mgmt interface statistics properly.

bugs.title: Pool members do not exit slow ramp when CARP persistence is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: Pool members do not exit slow ramp when CARP persistence is enabled and priority groups are configured.
bugs.conditions: Pool members using slow ramp with CARP persistence enabled and priority groups configured.
bugs.impact: Pool member selections shifts through decreasing priority, groups and the connection goes to an unexpected pool member, (that is, one not in the highest priority group), even though members in a higher priority group are active.
bugs.workaround: Disable the Slow Ramp Time setting on the pool.

bugs.title: Access profile configured with SWG Transparent results in memory leak.
bugs.symptoms: Access profile configured with SWG Transparent results in memory leak.
bugs.conditions: Create an access profile of type SWG Transparent, and assign to a virtual. Run traffic through this virtual.
bugs.impact: TMM leaks memory.
bugs.fix: Fixed the memory leak caused by access filter for SWG transparent use case.

bugs.title: Connection hangs when processing large compressed responses from server
bugs.symptoms: When large compressed responses are sent by the server, the connection hangs when trying to send decompressed content to the client.
bugs.conditions: An LTM policy which enforces decompression for responses is attached to the virtual server. The virtual server also has http compression profile attached to it. Server sends large compressed responses.
bugs.impact: Connection hangs when trying to process the compressed response in order to send decompressed content to client.
bugs.fix: The large compressed responses are successfully processed and no connection hangs are seen.

bugs.title: Occasional crash of icrd_child when BIG-IP restarts
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP restarts (bigstart restart), or when restjavad restarts (bigstart restart restjavad), there is an occasional crash of the icrd_child thread.
bugs.conditions: When BIG-IP restarts (bigstart restart), or when restjavad restarts. No other specific conditions.
bugs.impact: Occasional crash/SEGV exception.
bugs.workaround: Restart restjavad (bigstart restart restjavad). Impact of workaround: The iControl REST API for making queries or modifications is temporarily unavailable while the restjavad service restarts.
bugs.fix: Different approach of handling thread termination is implemented. New approach correctly terminates zombie processes and does not cause SEG fault.

bugs.title: Separate signature validation and encryption certificates used by SAML IdP
bugs.symptoms: In TMOS v.11.3 through v.11.6 releases there is only one certificate which can be configured for SAML SP connector ( apm sso saml-sp-connector, "sp-certificate" attribute). This certificate is used by Identity Provider both for verifying the signature of incoming ArtifactResolve request and encrypting (if encryption is enabled in IdP settings) of assertion and/or specified SAML attributes.
bugs.conditions: This restriction does not allow for supporting SP configurations where separate keys/certs are used for encryption and signing.
bugs.impact: Limited support for external Service Providers that require different certificates for signing/decryption.
bugs.fix: In version 12.0 it is now possible to configure SP connector objects with two certificates: sp-certificate < -- certificate used by IdP to validate signatures on messages received from SP. sp-encryption-certificate < -- certificate used by IdP to encrypt assertion/subject/attributes when encryption is enabled. =========== Similar symmetrical change was also implemented when BIG-IP is used as SAML SP. When BIG-IP is used as SAML SP, it is also possible to configure two certificates in AAA SAML object: sp-certificate < -- certificate used by SP to sign Authentication Requests. sp-decryption-cert < -- certificate used by SP to decrypt assertions/subject/attributes.

bugs.title: Audit forwarding Radius packets may be rejected by Radius server
bugs.symptoms: The Accounting-Request packets are missing two required AVPs (Attribute Value Pair), Acct-Session-ID and Acct-Status-Type. Some Radius servers drop Radius Accounting-Requests which are missing these AVPs.
bugs.conditions: Configured to use audit forwarding with radius and audit messages are not logged on the Radius server.
bugs.impact: Unable to log audit messages from BIG-IP using audit forwarding.

bugs.title: LTM policy TCP address selector offers only the condition 'match any of'
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, you can create a condition on a TCP address where a list of specified addresses are considered for a match. But the negated condition (i.e., 'do not match any of') is not available.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI, attempt to create an LTM policy condition that checks for addresses that do not match the specified list.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the GUI to specify conditions in a policy where the TCP address does-not-match a list of specified addresses.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create or modify a policy to negate a condition on TCP addresses, for example, in tmsh construct a command similar to the following: modify ltm policy my_policy rules modify { my_rule { conditions replace-all-with { 0 { tcp address not matches values { 10.10.4.0/0 } } } } }

bugs.title: Start to allow clientSSL profiles to be configured without RSA type key/cert pair
bugs.symptoms: RSA type cert/key pair is a mandatory property of a clientSSL profile.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when configuring a clientSSL profile.
bugs.impact: You are not allowed to assign cert/key pair that is not RSA.
bugs.fix: With this change, a clientSSL profile still requires at least one cert/key pair, but RSA type cert/key pair is no longer mandatory. For example, before this change, the below operation fails because it attempts to assign a clientSSL profile only an EC type cert/key. tmsh create ltm profile client-ssl cssl cert-key-chain replace-all-with { ec { cert ec key ec }} 010717e3:3: Client SSL profile (/Common/cssl): must have RSA Server certificate/key pair. After this change the above operation will be valid and hence the error message will no longer appear.
bugs.behavior: RSA type cert/key pair has been a mandatory configuration of a clientSSL profile. With this change, a clientSSL profile still requires at least one cert/key pair, but RSA type cert/key pair is no longer mandatory.

bugs.title: tmm crashes when ACL iRule with virtual command is triggered
bugs.symptoms: If an ACL iRule with virtual command is triggered and redirect the traffic back to the same virtual server, it can form a infinite recursion and cause tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: ACL uses an iRule that chooses a virtual server inside CLIENT_ACCEPTED.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: iRules should be self-limiting as following to avoid infinite recursion: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { if {[TCP::local_port] == 666 } { log "=== Redirection Port [TCP::local_port] client port [TCP::remote_port] " log local0. "virtual name is [virtual name]" set my_virtual_name "/Common/VS3" if { [virtual name] ne $my_virtual_name } { virtual $my_virtual_name } else { log local0. "preventing recursive call" } } }

bugs.title: No validation when delete iRule that is assigned to ACL policy
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule is deleted, BIG-IP does not throw error even when it is configured under ACL policy.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is provisioned -- iRule is configured under an ACL Policy. -- iRule is deleted
bugs.impact: iRule gets deleted without error. Later, the ACL policy won't be able to access the iRule.
bugs.fix: Added validation and an error message when an iRule is deleted which is configured under an ACL policy. "The irule (/Common/iRule1) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a fw_rule (rule1) in Policy (/Common/policy11)."

bugs.title: Stream filter may require large allocations by Tcl leading TMM to core on allocation failure.
bugs.symptoms: Stream filter may require large allocations by Tcl leading TMM to core on allocation failure.
bugs.conditions: Stream filter is active during low memory situations
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Stream may now be configured to parse xbufs in chunks. This limits the maximum amount of memory required and reduces the chance of an allocation failure.

bugs.title: No iControl functions to get and set master key.
bugs.symptoms: No iControl functions to get and set master key.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl with master key.
bugs.impact: Cannot get or set master key.
bugs.workaround: There is no iControl workaround.

bugs.title: LLDP VLAN Information not Transmitted to Neighbors When Interfaces are Added to a Trunk after the Trunk has Already Been Assigned to a VLAN
bugs.symptoms: Vlan Name and Vlan Tag values are not seen by the LLDP neighbors of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: 1. LLDP is enabled globally and per interface. 2. Interfaces are added to a trunk after it has already been assigned to a VLAN. For instance, assume the following protocol were followed for creating an LLDP trunk: tmsh modify net lldp-globals enabled tmsh modify net interface 1.1 lldp-admin txrx lldp-tlvmap 114680 tmsh modify net interface 1.2 lldp-admin txrx lldp-tlvmap 114680 tmsh create net trunk myTrunk tmsh create net vlan myVlan tmsh modify net trunk myTrunk interfaces add { 1.1 1.2 } tmsh modify net vlan myVlan interfaces add { myTrunk } The neighbor to this BIG-IP unit would not see the Vlan Name and Vlan Tag information of this trunk because the interfaces were added after the trunk was already assigned to a VLAN.
bugs.impact: LLDP Neighbors are unable to see VLAN information for the LLDP interfaces of the BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: If the configuration has not yet been performed, the issue can be prevented by assigning all the desired interfaces to a trunk before assigning the trunk to a VLAN. If the problem already exists, it can be remedied by performing a restart of the LLDP service. This should not impact dataplane services outside of LLDP. To do so, run the following command: bigstart restart lldpd
bugs.fix: VLANs are now properly applied to any interfaces added to a trunk if the trunk already belongs to any VLANs.

bugs.title: Include <AttributeConsumingService> in SP metadata
bugs.symptoms: Cannot include <AttributeConsumingService> in the Service Provider (SP) metadata to configure a BIG-IP system as an SP.
bugs.conditions: Configuring SAML federation as SP requires configuration of at least one <AttributeConsumingService>. This/these attribute/s along with the corresponding unique AttributeConsumingServiceIndex/s must be reported in the exported SP metadata.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure a BIG-IP system as an SP.
bugs.workaround: AttributeConsumingService is typically used together with AttributeConsumingServiceIndex in either of the following ways. 1. At configuration time, Service Providers export metadata and specify 'AttributeConsumingService' to describe the service and provide a list of requested attributes to be used by the service. 2. At run-time, Service Provider generates an authentication request to IdP and specifies 'AttributeConsumingServiceIndex', which is a reference to a particular AttributeConsumingService previously shared using metadata. This index is used by IdP to identify which AttributeConsumingService should be used to generate assertion with relevant attributes. For #1, the workaround is to manually edit the exported-by-SP metadata to include the AttributeConsumingService element. Note: In this case, exported metadata cannot be digitally signed. There is no workaround for #2, so even if metadata is edited, BIG-IP as SP will not include AttributeConsumingServiceIndex in authentication requests.
bugs.fix: Support for configuring Attribute Consuming Service(s) for SAML SP was added. On exporting SP metadata, the configured Attribute Consuming Service(s) along with corresponding unique Attribute Consuming Service Index(es) are part of the metadata. The metadata can be shared with an IdP, and the SP can generate an authentication request with an Attribute Consuming Service Index (reference to a particular Attribute Consuming Service). If the IdP supports Attribute Consuming Service, the index in the request is used by IdP to identify which AttributeConsumingService should be used to generate assertion with relevant attributes.

bugs.title: Active FTP data transfer via FTP AppTunnel is interrupted after 5 minutes.
bugs.symptoms: The connection is getting closed by the server. RST is being sent to the client from virtual server after 5 minutes of the download starting while data is flowing.
bugs.conditions: If the settings for the TCP profile are default on BIG-IP then this issue will be encountered for FTP transfer of files that take longer than 5 minutes to download. In a general case, if the idle timeout in the TCP profile is less than the keep-alive interval, and if FTP transfer takes more time than the specified TCP timeout, transfer gets interrupted.
bugs.impact: This affects FTP transfer of large-sized files that take more than 5 minutes (the default idle timeout in TCP profile on the BIG-IP system) to download.
bugs.workaround: Set the timeout to Indefinite or set the keep-alive interval to a value that is larger than idle timeout in the TCP profile. Then download does not get interrupted and completes as expected.

bugs.title: Ability to present a SHA1 certificate to clients that don't support SHA2
bugs.symptoms: Request to add ability to present SHA1 certificate (during SSL handshake) to SSL client that doesn't support SHA2 algorithms.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured to use certificate signed with SHA2 algorithm.
bugs.impact: Older SSL implementation that doesn't support SHA2 algorithm will fail when validating unsupported certificate.
bugs.workaround: These is no deterministic way to detect if a client supports SHA2 certificate; but heuristically, one can do the following using iRule: If client_hello contains TLS version >= 1.2, check for SHA2 support in client_hello's signature algorithm extension; if present, use clientssl profile configured with SHA2 certificate. Otherwise, use profile configured with SHA1 certificate.

bugs.title: AFM can log DoS attack against the internal mpi interface and not the actual interface
bugs.symptoms: While under an attack that matches a DoS profile, BIG-IP may indicate that the interface is the internal mpi interface and not the interface that the attack is happening on.
bugs.conditions: This can occur in CMP-enabled systems.
bugs.impact: A valid DoS attack will be misreported

bugs.title: FPS flags no cookie when length check fails
bugs.symptoms: You see No Cookie errors for validation errors other than No Cookie.
bugs.conditions: Malformed component validation cookie
bugs.impact: No Cookie errors counted when the validation error was not due to No Cookie
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with No Cookie error counting.

bugs.title: SWG Custom Category: unable to have a URL in multiple custom categories
bugs.symptoms: When configuring a url in multiple categories you receive a validation error message: May 19 16:13:44 bigip12 err mcpd[8992]: 010717f3:3: Custom category (/Common/category_allow_group2) has invalid URL (http://172.16.20.1/*). Reason: You cannot have the same URL in two or more custom categories. URL used in category (/Common/category_allow_group1).
bugs.conditions: Configuring the same URL in multiple custom categories.
bugs.impact: Unable to have the same URL in multiple custom categories, and therefore cannot configure the system to have a URL allowed for one group but not for another.
bugs.fix: Validation preventing the configuration of same URL for multiple custom categories has been fixed.

bugs.title: Memory leaks when session DB tables gets updated
bugs.symptoms: Memory usage stats indicate possible memory leaks.
bugs.conditions: When CEC flow bundling is used.
bugs.impact: Potential memory leaks.
bugs.workaround: Disable CEC flow bundling (tmm.gpa.cec.flow_bundling.enable = false).

bugs.title: Edge client may show a windows displaying plain text in some cases
bugs.symptoms: Under captive portal environment, sometimes edge client may show a windows with some plain text content.
bugs.conditions: Edge client is launched when users machine is inside captive portal network.
bugs.impact: User may not be able to establish VPN
bugs.workaround: Authenticate to captive portal using browser and Launch edge client again.

bugs.title: Virtual IP address change might cause VIP state to go from GREEN to RED to GREEN
bugs.symptoms: Virtual IP address change might cause VIP state to go from GREEN to RED to GREEN when pool goes empty.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the configuration contains a pool with only one FQDN pool member.
bugs.impact: VIP can go briefly RED and offline.
bugs.workaround: Configuring a fallback static IP node or multiple FQDN pool members removes this risk.

bugs.title: TCP Analytics reports huge goodput numbers
bugs.symptoms: TCP Analytics reports that 2^32 bytes have been delivered, rather than 0.
bugs.conditions: When the serverside connection attempt fails.
bugs.impact: TCP Analytics stats are inaccurate.
bugs.fix: Handle the failed connection case properly.

bugs.title: Deleting GTM links could cause gtm_add to fail on new devices.
bugs.symptoms: Once links are auto-discovered, if auto discovery is disabled and the links are deleted, they could become stuck in the Server > Virtual Server list, preventing new devices from joining the sync group. If gtm_add is run from a new device, the add will appear to succeed, but no GTM objects will show up on the unit.
bugs.conditions: Links are auto-discovered Auto discovery is disabled The links are deleted
bugs.impact: If gtm_add is run from a new device, the add will appear to succeed, but no GTM objects will show up on the unit.
bugs.fix: Cleanup all aspects of a GTM link when it is deleted.

bugs.title: "vcmp.vdisk.new_image_size" BigDB variable ignored when using virtual disk templates
bugs.symptoms: The "vcmp.vdisk.new_image_size" BigDB variable controls the size of newly create virtual disk images for vCMP guests. However, when vCMP Fast Provisioning is used (i.e., virtual disk templates), new virtual disk images created from a virtual disk template will have the same size as the template.
bugs.conditions: You may experience this issue if: * The vCMP host BIG-IP system is configured to use virtual disk templates, which is the case by default. * The "vcmp.vdisk.new_image_size" BigDB variable has been changed from its default value. * A new virtual disk image is created for a vCMP guest using a virtual disk template that was created before the "vcmp.vdisk.new_image_size" BigDB var was modified.
bugs.impact: The virtual disk image(s) created for a vCMP guest may have an unexpected and/or undesirable size.
bugs.workaround: To force the system to create a new virtual disk template using the size specified in the "vcmp.vdisk.new_image_size" BigDB variable, set the "vcmp.installer.use_vdisk_templates" to "disabled" using the following TMSH command: # tmsh modify sys db vcmp.installer.use_vdisk_templates value disabled Then set the vCMP guest to the provisioned or deployed state to initiate a new virtual disk image install for the guest. If a virtual disk image of the undesired size has already been created, it should be deleted first.

bugs.title: Forwarding address for Type 7 in ospfv3 is not updated in the database
bugs.symptoms: The ospf nssa-external database is not updated when the global address on an interface that is used as a forwarding address is changed
bugs.conditions: remove the global address on the forwarding interface
bugs.impact: the packets will be sent to an incorrect interface.
bugs.workaround: clear ipv6 ospf process
bugs.fix: The ospf nasa-external data shows correct forwarding address when the global address on the forwarding interface is changed.

bugs.title: HTTP:respond causes a keepalive connection to be RST after second request and "Invalid action" log.
bugs.symptoms: Clients experience connection resets when using HTTP keep-alives. LTM log contains 'Invalid action' messages in the log that look similar to the following: http_process_state_prepend - Invalid action:0x109010 (Server side: vip=/Common/myprofile=http pool=/Common/mypool server_ip=ip_address).
bugs.conditions: HTTP virtual server with an iRule attached. The invocation of the HTTP::respond API within the iRule's HTTP_REQUEST_SEND event for an HTTP keep-alive connection causes a reset of the keep-alive connection.
bugs.impact: HTTP keep-alive connections are being dropped when the iRule on the virtual server handling the HTTP traffic invokes the HTTP::respond API in the HTTP_REQUEST_SEND event.
bugs.workaround: Issue a HTTP::close before HTTP::respond Example: when HTTP_REQUEST_SEND { clientside { if {[HTTP::path] eq "/findex.html"} { HTTP::close HTTP::respond 200 content "This is my response" } } } Alternatively, issue HTTP::respond from a different event.

bugs.title: Upgrading 11.5.x/11.6.x hourly billing instances in AWS with multiple NICs to 12.1.x can result in instance becoming inaccessible.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading 11.5.x/11.6.x hourly billing instances in AWS with multiple NICs to 12.1.x can result in instance becoming inaccessible.
bugs.conditions: 11.5.x/11.6.x Hourly Billing instances with multiple NICs attached.
bugs.impact: User might not be able to log-in to the instance.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the instance corrects the problem.
bugs.fix: Upgrading 11.5.x/11.6.x hourly billing instances in AWS with multiple NICs to 12.1.x works with new Hourly billing licenses.

bugs.title: Upgrades from 11.6.1 or recent hotfix rollups to 12.0.0 may fail
bugs.symptoms: An upgrade to BIG-IP v12.0.0 will fail when all of the following conditions are met: - AVR provisioned - Upgrading to v12.0.0 from the following versions : - 11.6.1 Certain engineering hotfixes are also affected.
bugs.conditions: The following Engineering Hotfixes are affected. - 11.6.0-hf5 EHF index 110 (Hotfix-BIGIP-11.6.0.5.110.429-HF5-ENG.iso) - 11.6.0-hf5 EHF Index 214 - 11.6.0-hf5 EHF index 233 - 11.6.0-hf6 EHF index 240 11.6.1 is also affected.
bugs.impact: The upgrade to 12.0.0 will succeed but the configuration will fail to load. This can be detected by running tmsh load sys config verify. You will see the following signature: Unexpected Error: "Can't load keyword definition (analytics-report.device_group)"
bugs.workaround: 12.1.1 is schema compatible with 11.6.1, so upgrade to 12.1.1 instead.

bugs.title: Modifying an IPsec tunnel and IPsec plus IKE SA does not remove the remote SA.
bugs.symptoms: When modifying the ipsec-tunnel-profile, the BIG-IP system deletes the IKEv1 phase 2 SAs locally, but does not inform the remote IPsec peer.
bugs.conditions: - Configuration uses both IPsec 'interface' mode tunnel(s) and IKEv1. - A user modifies ipsec-tunnel-profile. Namely found here: -- web UI 'Network : Tunnels : Profiles : IPsec Interface : ipsec-tunnel-profile'. -- tmsh 'net tunnels ipsec ipsec-tunnel-profile'.
bugs.impact: A traffic outage on one tunnel when the remote IPsec peer is generally plays the role of Initiator. The remote system, will not attempt to establish a new tunnel because it believes that a valid SA exists.
bugs.workaround: Delete the defunct IPsec SA from the remote peer. If the remote IPsec peer is also a BIG-IP system, then restarting tmipsecd can be employed, however this will cause all IPsec tunnels to restart.

bugs.title: Incorrect PVA indication on B4450 blade
bugs.symptoms: When you run guishell -c "select HAS_PVA, PVA_VERSION from platform" on a B4450 blade (which includes PVA), the output indicates that it does not have PVA.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at platform information on B4450 blades.
bugs.impact: PVA acceleration is not detected properly
bugs.fix: PVA service is now indicated properly on the B4450 blade.

bugs.title: Not able to add remote user locally
bugs.symptoms: When a user has logged in remotely, using tmsh to add a user with the same name will fail: 01020066:3: The requested user role partition (raduser TestPartition) already exists in partition Common.
bugs.conditions: Remote authentication is configured and a remote user has logged in.
bugs.impact: Changing remote user to local fails.
bugs.workaround: Use "replace-all-with" for partition access: create auth user raduser password raduser1 partition-access replace-all-with { TestPartition {role manager }}

bugs.title: Cancellation requests for chunked stats queries do not propagate to secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: Canceling a request for a chunked stats query (e.g. hitting ctrl-c during "tmsh show sys connection") does not stop data flowing from secondary blades.
bugs.conditions: A chassis-based system with multiple blades. Users must execute a chunked stats query (e.g. "tmsh show sys connection") and then cancel it before it finishes (e.g. with ctrl-c in tmsh).
bugs.impact: Unnecessary data will be sent from TMM to secondary mcpd instances, as well as from secondary mcpd instances to the primary mcpd instance. This could cause mcpd to restart unexpectedly.
bugs.fix: Cancellations for chunked stats queries are now propagated to secondary blades.

bugs.title: Changing console baud rate for B2100, B2150 and B2250 blades does not work
bugs.symptoms: Changing the console baud rate does not take effect and leaves the setting unchanged.
bugs.conditions: Whenever the console baud rate is changed via tmsh, GUI, or iControl on the VIPRION B2100, B2150 and B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: Changing the console baud rate causes the front panel display manager to restart and does not actually modify the baud rate.
bugs.fix: Added needed object to global config map for VIPRION B2100, B2150 and B2250 blades so modify message no longer fail the object lookup.

bugs.title: Access session 'Bytes In' and 'Bytes Out' are not getting updated (stay at 0) when accessed with a http/2 enabled browser and HTTP/2 profile attached
bugs.symptoms: Access session 'Bytes In' and 'Bytes Out' are not getting updated (stay at 0) when accessed with a HTTP/2 enabled browser and HTTP/2 profile attached.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - An HTTP/2 enabled browser is in use. - APM and HTTP/2 are enabled on the same virtual.
bugs.impact: APM statistics for bytes in and out are not updated.
bugs.fix: Access session 'Bytes In' and 'Bytes Out' are now getting updated when accessed with a http/2 enabled browser and HTTP/2 profile attached

bugs.title: SSH Proxy profile visible in GUI available without AFM provision
bugs.symptoms: The SSH Proxy profile is visible in the virtual server configuration even if AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: This profile is visible in Security :: Protocol Security : Security Profiles : SSH Proxy in the configuration utility. It is also visible in the Virtual Server configuration page as an available profile.
bugs.impact: The SSH Proxy profile appears as if it is available for the virtual server, but the profile cannot be used without an AFM license.
bugs.workaround: License and provision AFM in order to use the SSH Proxy profile.
bugs.fix: If AFM is not provisioned, the virtual server configuration page does not show SSH Proxy profile selection options.

bugs.title: SSL forward proxy chaining does not work with next hop Transparent proxy mode without adding route
bugs.symptoms: SSL forward proxy chaining is not working for Explicit-Transparent and Transparent-Transparent proxy chaining modes if there is no route added for end destination network.
bugs.conditions: - Configure 1st Proxy as explicit or transparent and 2nd proxy as Transparent. - Have a direct connection between them with no router in between - Send SSL request
bugs.impact: SSL requests fail
bugs.workaround: Add a route in the bigip for the end destination network to know the nexthop for Explicit-Transparent or Transparent-Transparent proxy chaining modes.

bugs.title: An incorrect MSS can be sent in client SYN/ACK packet for an accelerated connection
bugs.symptoms: A client may receive an incorrect MSS value in the SYN/ACK packet for a connection that is hardware accelerated and the flow is accelerated during TCP three way handshake.
bugs.conditions: A fastl4 profile with Offload State set to SYN. This affects all platforms and versions of BIG-IP with HSB/ePVA hardware acceleration.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP advertises an MSS value that might be too large. This may cause problems if the server receives a packet that exceeds its MSS.
bugs.workaround: Configure the fastl4 profile's Offload State to EST.

bugs.title: Native RDP resource fails to SSO to backend if username contains Greek small letter final sigma (Ï‚)
bugs.symptoms: Native RDP resource fails to SSO to backend if username contains Greek small letter final sigma (Ï‚)
bugs.conditions: Non-ASCII username containing Greek letter Ï‚ (http://www.charbase.com/03c2-unicode-greek-small-letter-final-sigma) causes SSO to the backend to fail.
bugs.impact: User with Greek small final sigma in the username cannot logon automatically to the RDP backend.
bugs.workaround: Do not use SSO for this particular user, e.g., assign non-SSO resource instead.

bugs.title: HSB TX HGM lockup on 3900, 8900, and 10000-series platforms.
bugs.symptoms: HSB TX HGM lockup on 3900, 8900, and 10000-series platforms. Tmm cores with the following error message in /var/log/ltm: notice panic: hsb interface 2 DMA lockup on transmitter failure.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Upgrading 11.5.x/11.6.x hourly billing instances to 12.1.0 fails due to license SCD.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) instances that use the Amazon Web Services (AWS) hourly billing license model may fail when upgrading to version 12.1.0. As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom: After upgrading to version 12.1.0, the BIG-IP VE instance license is invalid.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have BIG-IP VE instances that use the hourly billing licensing model. -- Your BIG-IP VE instances are running 11.5.x or 11.6.x software versions. -- Your BIG-IP VE instances are running within the AWS EC2 environment. -- You upgrade the BIG-IP VE instance using the liveinstall method.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP VE instance licenses are not valid after upgrading to software version 12.1.0.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can use the liveinstall method on the hotfix image directly (instead of installing the base software image and then the hotfix image). To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure requires rebooting the system and should be performed only during a maintenance window. Download the BIGIP-12.1.0.0.0.1434.iso and Hotfix-BIGIP-12.1.0.1.1.1447-HF1-ENG.iso files to your workstation. For more information about downloading software, refer to SOL167: Downloading software and firmware from F5. Copy the downloaded files from your workstation to the /shared/images directory on the VE instance. To perform the installation by using the liveinstall method, and reboot the BIG-IP VE instance to the volume running the new software, use the following command syntax: tmsh install sys software hotfix Hotfix-BIGIP-12.1.0.1.1.1447-HF1-ENG.iso volume <volume-number> reboot For example, to install the hotfix to volume HD1.3 and reboot to the volume running the newly installed software, type the following command: tmsh install sys software hotfix Hotfix-BIGIP-12.1.0.1.1.1447-HF1-ENG.iso volume HD1.3 reboot Verify the installation progress by typing the following command: tmsh show sys software Output appears similar to the following example: Sys::Software Status Volume Product Version Build Active Status ---------------------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 BIG-IP 12.0.0 0.0.606 yes complete HD1.2 BIG-IP 12.1.0 0.0.1434 no complete HD1.3 BIG-IP 12.1.0 0.0.1434 no installing 6.000 pct
bugs.fix: BIG-IP VE instances that use the AWS hourly billing license model now complete successfully when upgrading to version 12.1.0.

bugs.title: Cookie Signature overrides may be ignored after Signature Update
bugs.symptoms: Cookie Signature overrides may be ignored after Attack Signature Update.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP ASM security policy is configured with an allowed cookie where Check attack signatures on this cookie is cleared (disabled). -- You install a Security Update Attack Signatures file. -- Your BIG-IP ASM system processes traffic that matches an attack signature for the URL or cookie that is configured with the attack signature override.
bugs.impact: The system detects an attack signature violation for the object.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can modify the security policy settings and override (disable) the ability to check attack signatures on cookies. To do so, perform the following procedure in accordance with the object that is affected in your security policy: Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedures should not have a negative impact on your system. Disabling Check attack signatures on cookies The following procedure disables checking of attack signatures for the allowed cookie. 1. Log in to the Configuration utility. 2. Navigate to Security :: Application Security :: Headers :: Cookie List. 2. Click the Allowed Cookies tab. 4. Click the name of the cookie. 5. Click the Attack Signatures tab. 6. Clear the Attack Signatures box. 7. Click Update. 8. Click Apply Policy.
bugs.fix: Cookie Signature overrides are observed correctly, even after Signature Update.

bugs.title: Aggregation issues in 'last day' and 'last month' data in AVR-related charts
bugs.symptoms: AVR aggregates data with the following resolutions: 1 Hour: every 5 minutes (12 data points). 4 Hours: every 1 hour (4 data points). 1 Day: every 4 hours (6 data points). 1 Week: every 1 day (7 data points). 1 Month: every 1 week (4 data points). Older: every 1 month. This can lead to situations in time-charts report a very limited number of data points, which results in data that is not useful.
bugs.conditions: Viewing 'last day' and 'last month' data in AVR-related charts.
bugs.impact: Data that is not useful.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Historical statistics are now shown in a better time resolution.
bugs.behavior: The intervals of 'last day' and 'last month' in all AVR-related charts has changed. -- 'last day' is represented by 24 points, each of which represents 1 hour (changed from 6 points that each represented 4 hours). -- 'last month' is now represented by 30 points, each of which represents 1 day (changed from 4 points that each represented a week). Immediately after upgrade, you might notice some data missing from the 'last day' and 'last month' reports. For example, you might see only the most recent 4 hours (represented by 4 points) in 'last day', but not the points that preceded those 4 hours, as you might expect when viewing data for the 'last day'. Similarly, you might see 7 points representing 1 week when selecting 'last month', but not the three weeks before that. In both cases the data is not lost (assuming you did not change the default db variable avr.stats.aggregation which is set to medium). You can view the data by selecting a different interval. For example, you can select 'last week' to see the last day (specifically, the day = 1 point), and you can select 'last year' to see the last month's data. After an interval (one week, or one month, depending on the type of chart), the time periods will sync up with the data, so the charts show a full representation of the data, as expected.

bugs.title: VLAN groups with no Self IP addresses defined might generate ICMP messages with loopback addresses.
bugs.symptoms: VLAN groups with no Self IP addresses defined might generate ICMP messages with loopback addresses.
bugs.conditions: Configuration of a virtual server on a VLAN group that does not have a Self-IP configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic destined for the virtual server might be rejected with an ICMP unreachable sourced from a loopback address.
bugs.workaround: Use a Self IP address on the VLAN group.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer sends ICMP from loopback addresses when in use with a VLAN group without a configured Self IP address.

bugs.title: Expired Timestamp violation is triggered too often
bugs.symptoms: Expired Timestamp violation is frequently encountered by benign traffic. This occurs whenever there is an interval of at least 10 minutes between requests by a particular browser.
bugs.conditions: The Expired Timestamp violation is enabled, and there is an interval of at least 10 minutes between requests by a particular browser.
bugs.impact: The Expired Timestamp violation is triggered and traffic may be blocked.
bugs.workaround: Disable Expired Timestamp violation.
bugs.fix: All predefined policy templates have Expired Timestamp disabled.

bugs.title: SSL hardware acceleration statistics might be incorrect.
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP device, hardware acceleration is still showing as 'Full' for some ciphersuites that employ a combination of software and hardware acceleration. It should be showing an acceleration type of 'Partial' in these cases.
bugs.conditions: When some operations (such as handshakes) happen in software while others (such as bulk encryption / decryption) are hardware-accelerated, for some ciphersuites.
bugs.impact: No impact to any other module
bugs.fix: Hardware acceleration statistics will be incremented as follows: 1. If all operations concerning the handshake and bulk encryption are done in hardware, the result is Full. 2. If some operations are done in software, while others are done in hardware the result is Partial. 3. If no operations are hardware accelerated the result is None (Software).

bugs.title: Devices in a device-group may report out-of-sync after one of the devices is rebooted
bugs.symptoms: Devices in a device-group may report out-of-sync after one of the devices is rebooted. As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptoms: - After the reboot, the config-sync originator reports 'Not All Devices Synced'. - After the reboot, the other devices in the device-group report 'Changes Pending'.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - You have a Sync or Sync-Failover device-group with multiple devices in it. - Using the Overwrite Configuration option in the GUI or command line tmsh, you manually initiate a synchronization of the configuration from the device where the configuration was modified, to the device-group. - The devices in the device-group display that they are in the synchronized state. - You reboot the config-sync originator device.
bugs.impact: After the reboot, the devices report out-of-sync. Note: This issue is purely cosmetic; no configuration is lost as result of this issue.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by not using the Overwrite Configuration option in the Configuration utility if you know you will have to reboot the device soon. Also note that once the issue occurs, you can restore normal config-sync status on the devices by performing a new config-sync operation.

bugs.title: GUI on VIPRION hangs on secondary blade reboot
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting a VIPRION chassis, the GUI suddenly becomes unresponsive several minutes after the reboot.
