bugs.title: BIG-IP ServerSSL connection may reset during rengotiation with some SSL/TLS servers due to ClientHello version
bugs.symptoms: During SSL/TLS renegotiation, the TLS standard requires that the new ClientHello version matches the first session. Usually, SSL/TLS servers require the new ClientHello version to match the previous negotiated (ServerHello) version. The BIG-IP ServerSSL default behavior is to match this requirement. The problem occurs if the SSL/TLS server requires the ClientHello (both in the Record layer and Handshake Protocol) in the new ClientHello to be exactly the same as the SSL/TLS version of the first ClientHello; that is: ************************************************************ 1st ClientHello record layer version == 2nd ClientHello record layer version; 1st ClientHello Handshake Protocol version == 2nd ClientHello Handshake Protocol version. ************************************************************ As a result, the SSL/TLS server will reject the renegotiation handshake, causing the connection to terminate.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using virtual servers configured with one or more ServerSSL profiles, and an SSL/TLS renegotiation occurs, and the server requires the new ClientHello version to match the first ClientHello instead of the previous ServerHello version.
bugs.impact: SSL/TLS renegotiation between BIG-IP ServerSSL profile and server may fail, resulting in an unexpected connection close or reset.
bugs.workaround: Manually setting the ciphers in the ServerSSL to TLS1.0 can solve the issue.
bugs.fix: A new db variable called ssl.RenegotiateWithInitialClientHello has been added to control the SSL/TLS version in the 2nd ClientHello: 1. The default is disable, which means that the 2nd ClientHello SSL/TLS version will be set to the negotiated version in the 1st round ServerHello. 2. If it is set to enable, both ClientHello versions will be exactly the same.

bugs.title: Add zLib compression
bugs.symptoms: Current driver supports only compress GZip and compress deflate.
bugs.conditions: APM Network Access tunnel has an option for compression. Compression is implemented in GZIP hudfilter which uses COMPRESS_ZLIB compression method. Currently only 'zlib' compression provider (software based) is implementing this method. None of the hardware providers (such as Coleto Creek) support it; they support COMPRESS_DEFLATE and COMPRESS_GZIP. GZIP hudfilter could use all 3 methods, but only ZLIB is compatible with current and older versions of the client. To preserve backward compatibility it must use ZLIB.
bugs.impact: Current compression hardware (such as Coleto Creek) is needed to support ZLIB method, otherwise compression in APM Network Access tunnel does not scale.
bugs.fix: zLib compression is now supported.

bugs.title: Inserted SIP VIA branch parameter not unique between INVITE and ACK

bugs.impact: SIP proxy servers which perform strict message validations may reject the call.
bugs.fix: Included a hash of the branch parameter of the received top-most via header into the branch parameter of the inserted via header. Thus is the received top-most via conforms to the spec and generates a different branch parameter between INVITE and ACK, the inserted via will have a different branch parameter.

bugs.title: [FW FQDN] RFE to address lower minimum allowed refresh interval (than current min of 10 mins)
bugs.symptoms: Firewall FQDN feature allowed the periodic refresh interval to be no less than 10 minutes. However, there are use cases where the FQDN -> IP mappings may change more frequently than 10 minutes. This would cause mis-match between the actual FQDN -> IP mappings and the mappings AFM/Firewall had learnt.
bugs.conditions: Firewall rules have been configured with FQDNs as one of the match dimensions (either source or destination or both). AFM DNS resolver refresh interval can be set to lowest possible allowed value of 10 minutes whereas the FQDN -> IP mappings change more frequently than 10 minutes.
bugs.impact: This would cause mis-match between the actual FQDN -> IP mappings and the mappings AFM/Firewall had learnt/cached.
bugs.fix: Firewall (AFM) now allows the minimum refresh interval for AFM DNS resolver to be set to as low as 5 seconds (and default is changed to 60 seconds).

bugs.title: Large ike-phase2-lifetime-kilobytes values in racoon ipsec-policy
bugs.symptoms: Setting max data limit transmitted (in kilobytes) to a very large limit results in a smaller limit, causing SAs to expire too quickly. Values for ike-phase2-lifetime-kilobytes inside ipsec-policy can reach 2^32-1 kilobytes, but will be processed incorrectly, as if the value were smaller.
bugs.conditions: When lifetime-kilobytes is large enough, it can act as though it were smaller.
bugs.impact: Negotiated SAs expire too quickly when size lifetime is calculated too small.
bugs.workaround: Before the fix, decrease lifetime-kilobytes until properly stable.
bugs.fix: The fix should make every value no more than 4294967295 kilobytes work correctly, without becoming some smaller value. (Note this value is 2^32-1.) If the size of ike-phase2-lifetime-kilobytes becomes 64-bit in the future, this will also work, causing a 64-bit value for kilobytes to occur in isakmp negotiation.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of L4 Dynamic ACL when it is processed together with L7 ACLs
bugs.symptoms: L4 Dynamic ACL is not applied to incoming traffic when assigned in combination with L7 ACL.
bugs.conditions: APM supports a combination of L7 ACL and L4 ACL to be assigned to one session. When L7 ACLs are assigned with higher priority than L4 ACLs, the processing of L4 ACLs is automatically deferred until L7 information is available. The issue here is that when none of L7 ACLs with higher priority match with the traffic, L4 ACL is incorrectly marked to be applied only to HTTP traffic. Therefore if the incoming traffic is not HTTP, for example, HTTPS, then this particular dynamic L4 ACL is bypassed.
bugs.impact: L4 Dynamic ACL is not applied correctly.
bugs.workaround: Reorder L4 ACLs with higher priority than L7 ACLs, if possible, or to prevent the issue from occurring, avoid assigning L7 ACLs if not needed.
bugs.fix: When L7 ACL is assigned in combination to L4 Dynamic ACL, L4 Dynamic ACL is correctly applied to all kinds of traffic, not only HTTP traffic.

bugs.title: Citrix Storefront integration mode gateway access reconnect fails
bugs.symptoms: After logging out from Citrix Receiver, clicking "Refresh Apps" and providing credentials gives an error: "Your logon has expired. Please logon again to continue."
bugs.conditions: BIGIP APM is configured in Storefront integration mode. Storefront remote access gateway configurations for APM leave the "Subnet IP address" as blank.

bugs.workaround: On the http profile of the virtual server, have this header (X-Citrix-Via:<single fqdn url>) for "Request Header Insert" configuration.

bugs.title: Very large number of log messages in /var/log/ltm with ICMP unreachable packets.
bugs.symptoms: When dns cache receives ICMP unreachable packets, or timeouts, related to outbound DNS requests, each one generates a log message in /var/log/ltm. Depending on DNS activity, this can result in a large number of log messages, which takes up space without providing additional information about the cause.
bugs.conditions: You have a DNS virtual server with DNS resolver cache configured. The virtual server receives ICMP unreachable in response to the DNS query. Note that DNS cache may send out multiple concurrent DNS queries, and only needs one to be successful in order to result a result, but it will still log these messages for any copies of the query that resulted in an ICMP unreachable response.
bugs.impact: You will see messages similar to the following in /var/log/ltm. err tmm[5021]: comm_point_tmm_recv_from failed: Software caused connection abort

bugs.title: tmm core on MRF when routing via MR::message route iRule command using a non-existant transport-config
bugs.symptoms: tmm will core if the transport config specified in a MR::message route iRule command does not exist.
bugs.conditions: the transport config specified in a MR::message route iRule command does not exist.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use the correct name for the trasnport-config object.
bugs.fix: fixed a tmm core.

bugs.title: "ASM starting" while it's already running, causing the restart of all ASM daemons
bugs.symptoms: ASM daemons suddenly restart, w/ the message "ASM Starting" in '/var/log/asm', while ASM is already running and without ASM stopping first.
bugs.conditions: Unknown
bugs.impact: ASM daemons restart
bugs.fix: We have prevented the ASM start script from being executed if it is already running. Thus, preventing the possibility of a spurious ASM Start while it's already running.

bugs.title: Virtual servers that use both FastL4 and HTTP profiles at same time will have incorrect syn cache stats.
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server remains in syncookie mode even after the syn flood stops. As a result of this issue, you might see the following symptoms: -- Virtual servers that use both FastL4 and HTTP profiles might show incorrect 'Current SYN Cache' stats. -- Virtual stats 'Current SYN Cache' does not decrease.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the configuration contains a virtual server that uses FastL4 as a filter (for example, has both the FastL4 profile and layer 7 profile (HTTP) syn flood to the virtual server).
bugs.impact: The virtual server stays stuck in syncookie mode after the synflood is over, and does not recover.
bugs.fix: Virtual servers that use both FastL4 and HTTP profiles will have correct syn cache stats.

bugs.title: big3d memory under extreme load conditions
bugs.symptoms: big3d memory consumption can grow if big3d is unable to process monitor requests in a timely fashion. This can be seen by monitoring the memory consumption of big3d using standard OS tools such as top.
bugs.conditions: big3d maintains a queue for monitor requests. Incoming monitor requests are first placed in the Pending queue. Requests are moved from the Pending queue to the Active queue, if there is room in the Active queue. When the Pending queue is full, there is no room for the Monitor Request. big3d attempts to clean up the Monitor request, but fails to completely free the memory. This might result in a significant memory leak. For this to happen, the Active queue must be full as well as the Pending queue. One possible condition that might cause this is if multiple Monitors time out. This results in Monitors having long life times, which keeps the Active queue full. Thus the Pending queue might become full and the memory leak can occur. In BIG-IP 11.1.0 versions of big3d, the Active queue has 256 slots and the Pending queue has 4096 slots. In BIG-IP 11.1.0-hf3, the queue sizes were expanded to 2048 for the Active queue and 16384 for the Pending queue. Since the queues were smaller n versions prior to 11.1.0-hf3, this leaks is more likely to manifest itself. In later versions, the leak is still possible, but is less likely to occur.
bugs.impact: big3d memory consumption grows unbounded. This might result in a big3d restart or memory starvation of other processes.
bugs.workaround: This can be partially mitigated by ensuring that monitors settings are reasonable and that big3d is not overloaded. This will minimize the chances that the Pending queue does not become full. There is no mechanism to resize the queues.
bugs.fix: When a monitor request is unable to be placed in the queue, the memory for the request is freed properly.

bugs.title: Cannot install DoS Hybrid Defender on standby device in HA pair if it's already installed on active
bugs.symptoms: After installation, the rpm on active device applications will be replicated to the standby. If standby does not have DHD installed, the installation page is never shown.
bugs.conditions: HA setup for DoS Hybrid Defender, with DHD only installed on Active.
bugs.impact: HA cannot be supported for DHD application on 12.1.0 and 12.1.1.
bugs.fix: Can now install DoS Hybrid Defender on standby device in HA pair if it's already installed on active.

bugs.title: tmm core
bugs.symptoms: A tmm core occurrs with the following log message: notice panic: ../kern/page_alloc.c:521: Assertion "vmem_hashlist_remove not found" failed.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Policy unable to match initial path segment when request-URI starts with "//"
bugs.symptoms: HTTP URI path policy does not match when request-URI starts with "//".
bugs.conditions: Policy unable to catch request when HTTP URI path configured to match value anywhere in path or in initial path segment when the request-URI starts with "//".
bugs.impact: The policy does not match in this case.
bugs.workaround: The policy could be modified to scan the full URI instead of just the path element however care should be taken to correctly handle potential matches with absolute URIs or in the query string.

bugs.title: AAM security hardening
bugs.symptoms: The wamd process, as used in AAM processing of images and PDFs, does not use current secure coding practices.
bugs.conditions: AAM active Image and/or PDF optimization enabled by policy
bugs.impact: wamd does not follow current secure coding practices.
bugs.fix: Update wamd to meet current secure coding standards.

bugs.title: TMM may leak or corrupt memory when configuration changes occur with plugins in use
bugs.symptoms: TMM may leak memory when plugins are in use and the plugin is re-initialized (typically due to configuration changes). In rare cases, memory corruption may occur causing TMM to restart.
bugs.conditions: Plugin-based functionality configured (ASM, APM, etc.) and configuration changes occur.
bugs.impact: The memory leakage generally occurs infrequently and at a rate that TMM operations are not affected. However, when memory corruption occurs, a traffic interruption may occur due to TMM restarting.
bugs.workaround: No workaround except disabling plugin-based functionality (such as ASM, APM, etc.).
bugs.fix: TMM now properly manages plugin memory, and no longer leaks or corrupts this memory.

bugs.title: Edge client does not log configuration parameters recieved from server
bugs.symptoms: Edge client does not log network access configuration parameters received from server. This makes troubleshooting of client issues difficult.
bugs.conditions: Edge client is used to establish VPN connection.
bugs.impact: Makes troubleshooting difficult
bugs.fix: Edge client now logs configuration parameters received from APM.

bugs.title: Updating pool members using iControl REST "PUT" resets monitors
bugs.symptoms: Issuing an iControl REST call using 'PUT' on a pool results in a "replace-all-with" behavior that deletes and recreates the pool members with the specified attributes, and uses system-defaults for unspecified attributes. This delete-and-replace behavior causes the monitor status to reset to 'unchecked' for the newly-created pool members; and if health monitors are applied to pool members, the status will eventually transition based on health checks (e.g., to "up" or "down"). This behavior may be surprising if the user expected the iControl REST call using 'PUT' on a pool to leave the monitor status unchanged for individual pool members.
bugs.conditions: Issuing an iControl REST call using 'PUT' to modify a pool.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST 'PUT' method on a collection overwrites all the members of that collection (e.g., all the members are deleted and re-created using the information provided). Because modifying a pool using 'PUT' causes all the pool members to be deleted and recreated, each pool member health status reverts to 'unchecked' (because the pool member is newly-created). If health monitor(s) are applied to pool members, then each pool member will eventually transition to a new status based on the result of subsequent health checks (e.g., to "up" or "down").
bugs.workaround: Use the iControl REST 'PATCH' method to individually modify members of a pool. This method is "safe" in that it will modify only that pool member, and the monitor health status will persist (based on its previous state and any associated health monitors). Note: You should generally prefer 'PATCH' over 'PUT' for iControl REST calls to modify collections. Using 'PATCH' will (safely) modify individual pool members, while using 'PUT' on the pool will cause "replace-all-with" to delete-and-recreate pool members (thereby resetting individual pool member health status).

bugs.title: CPU Saver option not working while the "latency" compression provider selection algorithm is in use.
bugs.symptoms: CPU Saver option not working while the "latency" compression provider selection algorithm is in use.
bugs.conditions: APM Edge Client over VPN tunnel. The issue tends to occur when CPR Saver is configured on the Edge Client on devices where hardware compression cannot perform the specific type of compression/decompression being requested.
bugs.impact: Edge Client shows the VPN tunnel as "Connected" but no traffic flow. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.workaround: #1 Enable CPU Saver in the secure connectivity profile: GUI: Access Policy :: Secure Connectivity :: profile_name :: Compression Settings :: Network Access :: CPU Saver [checkbox]. SHELL: tmsh modify apm profile connectivity dummy compress-cpu-saver true. #2 Configure compression strategy to "SPEED" (from LATENCY) SHELL: tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy value "speed".
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the CPU Saver option not working while the "latency" compression provider selection algorithm was in use. This mitigates a bottleneck when Software Compression is in use, correcting a problem with the tunnel stalling.

bugs.title: Brace matching in switch statement of iRules can fail if literal strings use braces
bugs.symptoms: In the TMUI on any iRule editing page, brace matching within a switch statement can fail if a literal string is surrounded with braces.
bugs.conditions: Use a literal string surrounded with curly braces for a case/pattern within a switch statement.
bugs.impact: Incorrect brace matching.
bugs.workaround: Instead of surrounding the literal string with braces, use double quotes.

bugs.title: tmm core on multiple SSL::disable calls
bugs.symptoms: tmm can crash if SSL::disable is called repeatedly in an iRule event.
bugs.conditions: Invoking SSL::disable multiple times in the same iRule event
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash related to multiple calls of SSL::disable

bugs.title: TLS v1.0 fallback can be triggered intermittently and fail with restrictive server setup
bugs.symptoms: HTTPS monitors mark a TLS v1.2-configured pool member down and never mark it back up again, even if the pool member is up. The monitor works normally until the SSL handshake fails for any reason. After the handshake fails, the monitor falls back to TLS v1.1, which the pool members reject, and the node remains marked down.
bugs.conditions: This might occur when the following conditions are met: -- Using HTTPS monitors. -- Pool members are configured to use TLS v1.2 only.
bugs.impact: Once the handshake fails, the monitor remains in fallback mode and sends TLS v1.0 or TLS v1.1 requests to the pool member. The pool member remains marked down.
bugs.fix: The system now successfully handles TLS v1.0 fallback when pool members are configured to use TLS v1.2 only, so pool members are correctly marked as being up.

bugs.title: DCDB security hardening
bugs.symptoms: The DCDB utility, as used in AAM processing, does not use current secure coding practices.
bugs.conditions: AAM active
bugs.impact: DCDB usage does not follow current secure coding practices.
bugs.fix: Update DCDB use to meet current secure coding standards.

bugs.title: dwbld core dump when Auto Blacklisting is configured, in a rare scenario
bugs.symptoms: The dynamic white/black daemon (dwbld) (a Control Plane daemon that supports the AFM IP intelligence feature) generates a core when processing an Auto Blacklisting Entry addition by TMM, when attack traffic causes a blacklist entry to be added. The problem happens in a rare scenario when dwbld and tmm are out of sync with respect to category names. This might happen for a very short window when configuration changes are made to Blacklist Categories (such as adding or removing a category).
bugs.conditions: -- DoS Auto Blacklisting feature enabled. -- Attack traffic generates an Auto Blacklist IP address entry. -- Configuration change to Blacklist Category occurs at the same time.
bugs.impact: dwbld crashes and restarts. No significant impact, as after restart, the dwbld should work properly.
bugs.fix: The release adds handling for the case in which dwbld is not up-to-date with configuration changes to Blacklist Categories when it simultaneously receives an Auto Blacklist Entry.

bugs.title: Big3D security hardening
bugs.symptoms: The Big3D utility, used in GTM, does not follow current secure coding best practices.
bugs.conditions: GTM active
bugs.impact: Big3D usage does not follow current secure coding best practices.
bugs.fix: Update Big3D use to use current secure coding best practices.

bugs.title: Floating tunnels with names more than 15 characters may cause issues during config-sync.
bugs.symptoms: Floating tunnels with names more than 15 characters may cause issues in config-sync, because such a long name is truncated when creating a corresponding Linux tunnel interface.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system consists of both floating and non-floating tunnels and their names are longer than 15 characters.
bugs.impact: When the config-sync happens, the following error may occur: Caught configuration exception (0), Cannot create tunnel 'g123456789abc~1' in rd0 - ioctl failed: File exists.
bugs.workaround: Some workarounds are available: - Make sure that tunnel names are less than 16 characters; or - Make sure that the names of floating and non-floating tunnels do not share a common prefix in the first 15 characters; or - Make sure that the BIG-IP system does not have a mixture of floating and non-floating tunnels.

bugs.title: Crash when a Gy update message is received by a debug TMM
bugs.symptoms: Debug TMM will crash when a Gy update message is received.
bugs.conditions: - Need a Debug TMM running - Gy update message must be received by the BIG-IP
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use non-debug TMM.
bugs.fix: Added checks to detect Gy udpate messages and handle them accordingly in the debug TMM. Thus, preventing a crash in the debug TMM.

bugs.title: The statistic ASM memory Utilization - bd swap size: stats are wrong
bugs.symptoms: AVR reports incorrect bd swap size statistics.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Viewing swap size statistics.
bugs.impact: Wrong value is displayed.
bugs.workaround: 1. Edit /etc/avr/tmstat_tables.xml 2. Change the following line: From: <value publishName="swap_size" columnName="swap_size" behavior="total" type="diff"/> To: <value publishName="swap_size" columnName="swap_size" behavior="average" type="status"/> 3. Run the following command: restart avrd.
bugs.fix: The statistic ASM memory Utilization - bd swap size: stats are now correct.

bugs.title: BD config update should be considered as config addition in case of update failure
bugs.symptoms: A configuration update fails when the system cannot find the item to update. Configuration failures are shown in bd.log.
bugs.conditions: The condition that leads to this scenario is not clear and is still under investigation.
bugs.impact: The update fails and the entity is not added.
bugs.workaround: Delete the faulty entity and re-add, and then issue the following command: restart asm. This fixes the issue in the cases in which it is a single entity.
bugs.fix: A configuration update no longer fails when the system cannot find the item to update. Now, the system adds the item with its updated value if the entity does not already exist. Otherwise, the operation updates the value of the existing entry.

bugs.title: Data transfer from the BIG-IP system self IP might be slow
bugs.symptoms: When a large amount of data needs to be transferred using a selp IP address, the BIG-IP system might send out fragmented IP packets with both the DF and MF bits set. Setting both bits is RFC compliant and valid, however some routers drop such packets. This might result in retransmissions and low throughput
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a self IP address processes large data transfers, and the router between the two endpoints does not process the IP fragments that have both the DF and MF bits set.
bugs.impact: Data transfer from the BIG-IP system's self IP might be slow.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command: ethtool -K tmm tso off. Note: This has a different effect from setting db key tm.tcpsegmentationoffload to "disable" (which will not workaround the issue). Note: To persist the effect of this command across reboots, use the solution specified in K14397: Running a command or custom script based on a syslog message, available here: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K14397. For example, alert tmmready "Tmm ready" { exec command="/sbin/ethtool -K tmm tso off" }
bugs.fix: Data transfer from the BIG-IP system self IP address has been improved.

bugs.title: Plugin should not inject nonce to CSP header with unsafe-inline
bugs.symptoms: When injecting CSP header values to enable FPS Plugin to work, unnecessary injections may break user's 'allow inline script' policy, since the more restrictive directive is always applied.
bugs.conditions: Server response contains either header from the "Content-Security-Policy" header.= family
bugs.impact: User's inline scripts will refuse to run since FPS Plugin injects nonce. This breaks user's application.
bugs.workaround: A fix has been deployed which makes 'unsafe-inline' and 'nonce' directives mutually exclusive. If user's CSP header allows inline scripts, we do not inject nonce.
bugs.fix: CSP header's 'unsafe-inline' and 'nonce' directive injection has been made mutually exclusive.

bugs.title: Sync fails when iRule or policy is in use
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading and attempting to sync to devices in a sync group, sync fails with the following error: Load failed from 119.big.ip 01070621:3: Rule priorities for virtual server (vs1) must be unique. Load failed from /Common/big152 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Values (/Common/vs1) specified for virtual server policy (/Common/vs1 /Common/asm_auto_l7_policy__vs1): foreign key index (vs_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database.
bugs.conditions: - A virtual address exists in the traffic-group-local-only group, meaning that it is not synced - A CPM policy or iRule is applied to that virtual server - Conduct a sync This was seen on an upgrade from 12.0.0 to 12.1.0 HF1 or beyond, but could be triggered on an upgrade from any version from 11.4.0 and beyond to 12.1.0 HF1.
bugs.impact: Config sync fails.
bugs.workaround: Disassociate the iRule or policy from the virtual server, then attempt to sync.

bugs.title: Failed to get master key (ERR_NOT_FOUND) in apm log on first boot
bugs.symptoms: After booting a new platform for the first time, you may see the following log entry in /var/log/apm: err tmm1[17340]: 01490563:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access stats encountered error: Failed to get master key (ERR_NOT_FOUND)
bugs.conditions: Viewing /var/log/ltm after first boot
bugs.impact: This is a residual log entry and is benign and can be safely ignored

bugs.title: Link Aggregation Control Protocol May Lose Synchronization after TMM Crash
bugs.symptoms: Traffic does not pass through a trunk interface and /var/log/ltm contains messages such as: lacpd[6636]: 01160011:6: Link 2.2 Actor Out of Sync lacpd[6636]: 01160012:6: Link 2.2 Partner Out of Sync
bugs.conditions: 1) BIG-IP 2000/4000 or similar platform where "qprop tmos.lacpd_depends_on_tmm == true" 2) Passive LACP trunk 3) tmm has crashed after box has come up 4) tmm startup delayed by dumping large core file 5) tmm startup delayed by large config or busy control plane
bugs.impact: Trunks created by LACP do not pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: Restart lacpd after tmm has come up again: "bigstart restart lacpd" Alternatively, modify /etc/bigstart/scripts/tmm.finish to restart lacpd on tmm going down Modify this line: for d in admd asm avrd dosl7d; do With these: for d in lacpd admd asm avrd dosl7d; do if [ `$BIGSTART singlestatus $d` = "run" ]; then $BIGSTART restart $d & fi done

bugs.title: Ramcache may leave the HTTP Cookie Cache in an inconsistent state
bugs.symptoms: Ramcache may re-use internal HTTP data without clearing the cookie cache. If other filters later inspect that cache they may read corrupted cookie information, or cause a TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: Ramcache + another filter or iRule inspecting/modifying cookies in a Ramcache response.
bugs.impact: The modifications of the corrupt cookie cache may cause HTTP headers to be malformed. Inspecting the cookie cache may cause the TMM to crash with an assert. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Ramcache clears the HTTP cookie cache in its responses.

bugs.title: AVR: Loading the configuration after upgrade might fail due to mishandling of scheduled-reports
bugs.symptoms: Loading the configuration after upgrade might fail due to mishandling of scheduled-reports, with an error similar to the following: err mcpd[5492]: 01071afc:3: Report scheduling requires specifying valid measures for entity asm_repev_ip.
bugs.conditions: -- AVR provisioned. -- Having scheduled report defined on a version earlier than v12.1.0, and upgrading to v12.1.0, v12.1.0, or v12.1.0.
bugs.impact: Loading the configuration after upgrade might fail.
bugs.fix: Loading the configuration after upgrade of scheduled-reports is now properly handled.

bugs.title: License not operational on Azure after upgrading from 12.0.0 HF1-EHF14 to 12.0.0-HF4 or 12.1.0-HF1 or 12.1.1.
bugs.symptoms: On Azure, after upgrading to any version other than 12.0.0 HF1-EHF14 or 12.1.0-HF1-EHF22, the system boots up as Not Licensed and Inoperative. Although certain cloud-specific 12.x EHFs such as BIG-IP Virtual Edition 12.1.0 HF1 EHF1 is intended for AWS only, BIG-IP does not prevent you from accidentally downloading and installing it into Azure environments. If you upgrade Azure from BIG-IP Virtual Edition 12.0.0 HF1 EHF14 to the 12.1.0 HF1 EHF1 or 12.0.0-hf4 or 12.1.1, the Azure license becomes nonoperational and gets invalidated.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading a BYOL instance on Azure to 12.1.0 HF1 EHF1 or 12.1.1. The Azure-specific versions are as follows: - 12.0.0-HF1-EHF14. - 12.1.0-HF1-EHF22.
bugs.impact: License becomes unusable. Re-licensing the instance gets an invalid license.
bugs.workaround: The workaround for this issue is to boot back into previous boot volume, and then upgrade to 12.1.0-HF1-EHF22 in Azure. To change default boot volume, choose one of the following methods: 1. tmsh reboot volume volume-name. 2. switchboot utility (interactive mode by default). 3. Admin UI. For more information about the switchboot utility, see SOL5658: Overview of the switchboot utility, available here: https://support.f5.com/csp/#/article/K5658
bugs.fix: This release fixes the issue that occurred when the Azure license become nonoperational after upgrading to BIG-IP Virtual Edition 12.1.0 HF1 EHF1 from 12.0.0 HF1 EHF14. Note: Do not use BIG-IP 12.1.0 HF1 EHF1 in the Azure environments.

bugs.title: pkcs11d signal handler improvement to turn off all threads at time of "SIGTERM"
bugs.symptoms: The current signal handler use 'exit' at time of 'SIGTERM'. This may result in a core under some abnormal situations.
bugs.conditions: When stopping pkcs11d using command like 'bigstart restart pkcs11d' or 'kill pkcs11d'.
bugs.impact: pkcs11d cores.
bugs.workaround: pkcs11d automatically comes up again after the core.
bugs.fix: The system now waits for all threads to finish before the pkcs11d program exits, so the core no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Vlan allowed mismatch found error in VCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: Your vCMP guests are unable to reach the network. You see in /var/log/ltm "mcpd[5503]: 01071322:4: Vlan allowed mismatch found: hypervisor "
bugs.conditions: When a VLAN exists in the vlan-allowed list contains a VLAN which matches the suffix of another VLAN in the list and both VLANs are configured on the VCMP guest. For example, xyz and abc_xyz will produce the error "warning mcpd[6374]: 01071322:4: Vlan allowed mismatch found: hypervisor (abc_xyz:1860), guest (/Common/xyz:1850)."
bugs.impact: Unable to use VLAN.
bugs.workaround: Rename the VLANs such that no VLAN matches suffix of any other VLAN.

bugs.title: SMTPS profile connections_current stat does not reflect actual connection count.
bugs.symptoms: SMTPS profile connections_current stat does not reflect actual connection count.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you have an SMTPS virtual server configured.
bugs.impact: profile_smtps_stat.connections_current rises over time and doesn't reflect actual number of SMTPS connections active.

bugs.title: Pagination controls missing for GSLB pool members
bugs.symptoms: The pagination controls for GSLB pool members do not appear when there are more items in the list than can be displayed (Record Per Screen)
bugs.conditions: Customer is running 12.1.0 or 12.1.1
bugs.impact: Unable to view the status of, or modify GSLB pool members beyond those displayed on the screen
bugs.workaround: Increase the number of Records Per Screen (System / Preferences / Records Per Screen) to a number larger than the number of items in your pool

bugs.title: On i5x00, i7x00 and i10x00 platforms, bcm56xxd may restart on power-up
bugs.symptoms: The following message appears on the console shortly after the system boots: emerg logger: Re-starting bcm56xxd.
bugs.conditions: This occurs as a result of a possible race condition on On i5x00, i7x00 and i10x00 platforms.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, bcm56xxd daemon restarts successfully.

bugs.title: Successive remote log operations trigger iRule Tcl error
bugs.symptoms: iRule terminates unexpectedly with error: 01220001:3: TCL error: ... Traffic rejected
bugs.conditions: iRule must perform multiple log operations, where log destination is a remote host. Example: log 192.0.2.1 "This will be sent to remote syslog" log 192.0.2.1 "This will trigger Tcl error"
bugs.impact: iRule may not operate as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use High Speed Logging (HSL) as an alternative.

bugs.title: SQL (Oracle) monitor daemon might hang.
bugs.symptoms: SQL (Oracle) monitor daemon might hang with high monitoring load (hundreds of monitors). DBDaemon debug log contains messages indicating hung connection aborting and that the address in use, unable to connect.
bugs.conditions: High number of SQL (Oracle, MSSQL, MySQL, PostgresSQL) monitors. Slow SQL responses might make the condition worse.
bugs.impact: Flapping pool members connected to SQL monitors. Frequent aborts and restarts of SQL monitor daemon.
bugs.workaround: You can mitigate this issue in the following ways: -- Reduce number of monitored pool members. -- Reduce frequency of monitor interval. -- Split monitors among multiple devices. -- Run monitors on bladed systems.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the address-in-use issue, and contains multiple monitor improvements to handle aborts and restarts of the SQL monitor daemon as well so that the system handles hung connections without aborting.

bugs.title: Unix daemon configuration may lost or not be updated upon reboot
bugs.symptoms: The confpp script is invoked to pass TMOS configuration information to other non-TMOS daemons running on a BIG-IP system. When a BIG-IP system is rebooted, if TMOS configuration elements are parsed or configuration changes or other events occur early in the boot process, the corresponding changes may not be propagated to the confpp.dat file and processed by the confpp script. As a result, configuration information may not be propagated as expected to non-TMOS daemons. A common symptom of this issue is that syslog-ng configuration is not updated to reflect the selection of the primary blade in a VIPRION chassis.
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur when booting an affected version of BIG-IP, such as: - Rebooting blades in a VIPRION chassis. - Rebooting a BIG-IP appliance or Virtual Edition instance.
bugs.impact: Expected configuration settings may not be applied to non-TMOS daemons upon a reboot. For example, syslog-ng configuration may not be updated to include expected logging on the primary blade in a VIPRION chassis.
bugs.workaround: On a running BIG-IP system that shows symptoms of this issue, changing a db variable will trigger the confpp script to run and update the relevant non-TMOS daemons with appropriate settings from the current configuration. To implement this workaround, use the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) to update a db variable. For example: tmsh modify sys db log.clusterd.level value "Informational" This issue can be avoided by forcing the MCP configuration to be reloaded from configuration files instead of from the MCP binary database (mcpdb.bin). For details, see: K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.fix: Configuration data/changes that occur early in the BIG-IP boot process are propagated successfully to non-TMOS daemons by the confpp script.

bugs.title: MPTCP connection not closed properly when the segment with DATA_FIN also DATA_ACKs data
bugs.symptoms: If a DATA_FIN is received with a DATA_ACK that acknowledges data, the BIG-IP will not process the DATA_ACK and will not shutdown the connection properly as it thinks there is still outstanding data to be acknowledged.
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile with Multipath TCP enabled is attached to a virtual server, and a DATA_FIN that DATA_ACKs data is received on an MPTCP connection.
bugs.impact: The connection is not closed properly and eventually times out.
bugs.fix: Fixed DATA_FIN handling.

bugs.title: Modified ASM cookie violation happens after upgrade to 12.1.x
bugs.symptoms: False positive modified ASM cookie violation. Perhaps other false positive cookie related violations.
bugs.conditions: System upgraded to 12.1.x. Existing end users are connected with their browsers to the site.
bugs.impact: False positive violations. A blocking page will be shown in case the modified ASM cookie is set to blocking (which is the default for this violation in case the policy is in blocking state).
bugs.workaround: There are three options: A. Set the modified ASM cookie violation to transparent after an upgrade for some time after the upgrade. B. Use the erase cookie blocking page as the default blocking page for some time after the upgrade. C. Use an iRule similar to the following: when ASM_REQUEST_DONE { if {[ASM::violation names] contains "VIOLATION_MOD_ASM_COOKIE"} { log local0. "remove TS01d2cce8 cookie" HTTP::respond 302 Location "http://sub.some_domain.com/index.html?[ASM::support_id]" "Set-Cookie" "TS01d2cce8=deleteOldTSCookie;expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT" }
bugs.fix: Modified ASM cookie violation no longer happens after upgrade to this version.

bugs.title: Upgrade from 10.2.4 to 12.1.x fails when SNMP trap exists in config from 10.2.4.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade from 10.2.4 to 12.1.x fails when SNMP trap exists in config from 10.2.4. After upgrade from 10.2.4 to 12.1.x, you are unable to use the GUI. The system posts the following message: The configuration has not yet loaded. CLI login works, and /var/log/ltm shows that the following message was recorded during the device bootup phase: emerg load_config_files: "/usr/libexec/bigpipe base daol" - failed. -- BIGpipe parsing error (/config/bigpipe/bigip_sys.conf Line 113): 012e0010:3: The requested value ({ i192_168_0_20_1) is invalid (<trapsess list> ` none) [add ` delete]) for 'trapsess' in 'snmpd'.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 10.2.4 to 12.1.x fails when SNMP trap exists in config from 10.2.4. The root cause is that the host parameter in the trap is encapsulated in quotation marks.
bugs.impact: The upgrade completes, but the configuration does not load when the system restarts.
bugs.workaround: After the configuration fails to load in this case, you can remove the SNMP trap destination configuration by editing the /config/bigpipe/bigip_sys.conf file, and performing a manual configuration conversion and reload to recover. Alternatively, to prevent the configuration load failure from occurring, you can remove the SNMP trap destination configuration before you upgrade to BIG-IP 12.1.x. Both procedures require that you re-create the SNMP trap destination configuration once the upgrade to BIG-IP 12.1.x and/or configuration load are complete.
bugs.fix: Upgrade from 10.2.4 now completes successfully when the host parameter exists in the 10.2.4 configuration includes SNMP traps.

bugs.title: Improvement for 'tmsh show ltm pool' command
bugs.symptoms: It is hard to determine which priority group is activated at any given time.
bugs.conditions: Using Priority Group Activation feature.
bugs.impact: Confusion on which members are actively handling traffic at any given time.
bugs.fix: 'tmsh show ltm pool' command displays additional row - 'Priority Groups' indicating which priority group is currently activated.
bugs.behavior: 'tmsh show ltm pool' command displays additional information regarding currently activated priority group in a new'Priority Groups' row.

bugs.title: Importing SAML IdP's metadata on BIG-IP as SP may result in not complete configuration of IdP connector object.
bugs.symptoms: When importing SAML IdP's metadata, certificate object might not be assigned as 'idp-certificate' value of saml-idp-connector object.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as SAML SP.
bugs.impact: Described behavior will result in misconfiguration. SAML WebSSO will subsequently fail.
bugs.workaround: Manually assign imported certificate as a 'idp-certificate' value of saml-idp-connector object.

bugs.title: ACCESS::session iRules did not work with IP-based sessions
bugs.symptoms: IP-based sessions rely on an internal IP to session mapping table. The ACCESS::session iRules were not using this table, so in IP-based session scenarios they never find the session. A simple iRule like this should generate a lot of logs. In an IP-based session scenario it would never log. when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [ACCESS::session exists] } { log local0. "Found Access Session" } }
bugs.conditions: SWG configuration with IP-based sessions. Attach an iRule to the virtual that includes ACCESS::session commands. They will not work as expected.
bugs.impact: ACCESS::session commands are essentially unavailable to IP-based sessions.
bugs.fix: All ACCESS::session commands were updated to read the IP to session mapping table when an access profile with IP-based sessions is attached to the virtual. ACCESS::session create has been updated, and it respects the 1-1 correspondence between IP addresses and sessions. If this IP address already has an associated session, APM returns that session. Otherwise we create a new session, and add it to the table.

bugs.title: Under certain conditions TMM may crash while processing OneConnect traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash while processing OneConnect traffic
bugs.conditions: Removing the OneConnect profile from a virtual server while passing traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM now processes profile removals as expected

bugs.title: TCP Analytics reports incorrectly reports entities as "Aggregated"
bugs.symptoms: Although the user has configured TCP Analytics to store statistics for a certain entity, it reports data for that entity in a single "Aggregated" row.
bugs.conditions: ALL of these conditions must be true: The TCP Analytics profile is attached to a virtual with both clientside or serverside collection turned off in the profile. TCP profile has mptcp, rate-pace, tail-loss-probe, fast-open, AND enhanced-loss-recovery all disabled. Also, Nagle, send-buffer, receive-window, proxy-buffer are not in AUTO mode. Finally, rexmt-thresh is 3 and the congestion control algorithm is not delay-based (NewReno, HighSpeed, Cubic). Regrettably, this matches the default TCP profile. An iRule enables TCP-Analytics when disabled by default in the tcp-analytics profile.
bugs.impact: Defect eliminates nearly all data granularity for TCP Analytics.
bugs.workaround: Change the TCP profile on the virtual to violate any of the conditions listed above. The easiest is probably to enable rate pace or mptcp. For all affected versions, this will result in a noticeable CPU performance penalty.
bugs.fix: Load entity information for both TCP stacks.

bugs.title: tmm assert "valid pcb" in tcp.c
bugs.symptoms: tmm panic tcp.c:2435: Assertion "valid pcb" failed
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Redirect/Route action doesn't work if there is an alert logging iRule
bugs.symptoms: When "Trigger iRule Events" is enabled in FPS profile and there are configured FPS rules with Route/Redirect actions, the actions will not be performed.
bugs.conditions: "Trigger iRule Events" is enabled in FPS profile and the virtual server has at least one iRule with ANTIFRAUD_ALERT or ANTIFRAUD_LOGIN events.
bugs.impact: Configured FPS rules with Route/Redirect actions will not be performed.
bugs.workaround: Disabling the "Trigger iRule Events" in FPS profile.
bugs.fix: "Trigger iRule Events" no longer breaks FPS rules with configured Route/Redirect actions.

bugs.title: ComplexType child elements in XML schema cannot have different values set in "fixed" attribute
bugs.symptoms: Within the XML schema definition, multiple child elements under a ComplexType cannot have different values set in "fixed" attribute.
bugs.conditions: Multiple child elements under a ComplexType in an XML schema are defined with different values set in "fixed" attribute.
bugs.impact: Subsequent elements are validated incorrectly with the initial element's definition.
bugs.workaround: Remove "fixed" attribute for subsequent elements in schema definition.
bugs.fix: Multiple child elements under a ComplexType may use different values set in "fixed" attribute.

bugs.title: REST id for Signatures change after update
bugs.symptoms: The REST id of existing signatures are unexpectedly modified after updating a User Defined Signature, or downloading an Attack Signature Update that modifies existing signatures.
bugs.conditions: A User-Defined Signature is updated, or an ASU containing updated signatures is downloaded.
bugs.impact: The REST id of the modified signatures is changed which may confuse REST clients.
bugs.workaround: Execution of the following script will repair an affected device: perl -MF5::Utils::Rest -MF5::DbUtils -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::Signature -e '$dbh = F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(); $dbh->begin_work(); $dbh->do("UPDATE PLC.NEGSIG_SIGNATURES SET rest_uuid = \"\" "); F5::Utils::Rest::populate_uuids(dbh => $dbh, rest_entities => ["F5::ASMConfig::Entity::Signature"]); $dbh->commit();'
bugs.fix: Updated Signatures now retain the correct REST id.

bugs.title: The TMM may become unresponsive when using SessionDB data larger than ~400K
bugs.symptoms: There is a hard limit on messages sizes sent on the backplane on chassis platforms. Messages larger than the limit (~400K) are refused from being sent at a lower layer but buffered for resending at a higher layer. The messages are never sent which cases backplane communication to lockup.
bugs.conditions: The BIGIP must be chassis with more than one blade and client traffic must trigger the creation of SessionDB data larger than ~400K.
bugs.impact: The TMM will become unresponsive to client traffic. If left running under load, the TMM may run out of memory from buffering SessionDB data and crash.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is the avoid sending large SessionDB data. The TMM may be restarted in the event it does get stuck.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a hard limit for sending SessionDB data on the backplane.

bugs.title: bgpd might core on restarting process with BGP debug enabled.
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP system configured with dynamic routing using the BGP routing protocol, when BGP debugging is enabled, the bgpd daemon may crash.
bugs.conditions: - BGP configured and peering established. - BGP debugging enabled. - BGP process is restarted gracefully.
bugs.impact: bgpd may crash.
bugs.workaround: Disable BGP debug.
bugs.fix: The bgpd might core on restarting process with BGP debug enabled.

bugs.title: Log IPsec tunnel up/down events
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to detect via logging that the IPsec tunnel state has changed.
bugs.conditions: When an IPsec tunnel becomes ready (up) or not ready (down).
bugs.impact: It is difficult to react to changing network conditions without notification.
bugs.fix: A log entry is made whenever the IPsec tunnel state changes. tmm IPsec: Tunnel up <source IP address> - <destination IP address> tmm IPsec: Tunnel down <source IP address> - <destination IP address>

bugs.title: Wrong alert when DTLS cookie size is 32
bugs.symptoms: When ServerSSL profile using DTLS receives cookie with length of 32 bytes it throws fatal alert.
bugs.conditions: Another LTM with ClientSSL profile issues 32byte long cookie.
bugs.impact: DTLS with cookie size 32 is not supported.
bugs.fix: DTLS now accepts cookies with a length of 32 bytes.

bugs.title: Thrift::TException error
bugs.symptoms: Trying to send a scheduled report might fail in some cases with the error "Thrift::TException=HASH(0x9a65410)".
bugs.conditions: This occurs when sending scheduled reports.
bugs.impact: Failure on sending scheduled-report.
bugs.workaround: Modify the script to use the explicit address instead of the 'localhost' value. This can be achieved with the following command: mount -o remount -rw /usr sed -i 's/localhost/127\.0\.0\.1/' /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/F5/AVReporter/Client.pm mount -o remount -r /usr
bugs.fix: Changing script to use explicit address instead of 'localhost'.

bugs.title: Citrix StoreFront integration mode with pass through authentication fails for browser access
bugs.symptoms: Citrix StoreFront integration mode with pass through authentication fails for browser access. After providing the credentials, browser access continuously asks for 'Can not complete the request', press 'OK'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - APM is configured in integration mode with StoreFront. - External access virtual server IP is used in Citrix gateway configuration 'Subnet IP address' column. - (Request Header Insert) :: [X-Citrix-Via-Vip:10.10.10.10], 10.10.10.10 is the virtual server IP address. Request Header Insert is configured on the HTTP profile of the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: No browser access to StoreFront.
bugs.workaround: StoreFront combines multiple headers of the same name and cannot use the resulting value. You can workaround this issue by stripping multiple headers of type x-citrix-via-vip. Make 10.10.10.10 the corresponding External access virtual IP address. when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::header count "X-Citrix-Via-Vip"] >= 2 } { HTTP::header remove "X-Citrix-Via-Vip" HTTP::header insert "X-Citrix-Via-Vip" "10.10.10.10" } }

bugs.title: IAppLX objects fail to sync after establishing HA in auto-sync mode
bugs.symptoms: IAppLX objects are part of REST Framework. REST Framework implements gossip based replication. This replication might not work when restFrameworkVersion in device-group device out of sync with actual restFrameworkVersion
bugs.conditions: DeviceInfoWorker detects and update the framework version after rest RPM upgrade. But device group device doesn't get updated correctly
bugs.impact: REST framework objects (Including iAppLX instances, templates, packages) fail to sync to HA peer
bugs.workaround: Mitigation is to run DeviceRefreshWorker and it is responsible for patching the localhost resource in all device groups with correct framework version on update. Workaround is to patch the restFrameworkVersion manually on the device-group device.
bugs.fix: Run the DeviceRefreshWorker and it is responsible for patching the localhost resource in all device groups with correct framework version on update.

bugs.title: Sometimes, passwords fields are readonly
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, passwords fields are readonly so the user won't be able to type any password.
bugs.conditions: WebSafe protection enabled on a site
bugs.impact: the user won't be able to type any password on the site.

bugs.title: No mirroring for TCP TIME-WAIT reconnections and new TCP flows after HA reconnections.
bugs.symptoms: New connections made when a BIG-IP flow is in TCP TIME-WAIT state are not mirrored. New TCP flows after high availability (HA) reconnections may not be mirrored correctly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a TCP profile is used, along with one of the following: -- A BIG-IP flow is in TCP TIME-WAIT state. -- HA connection is reestablished and a mirrored BIG-IP flow has lost some packets.
bugs.impact: The connections affected are not mirrored.
bugs.workaround: Disable TIME-WAIT for the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: Reconnections in TCP TIME-WAIT state are now mirrored correctly. New connections after HA reconnections are now mirrored correctly.

bugs.title: Backslashes in monitor send and receive strings
bugs.symptoms: After creating a monitor using the GUI containing a recv parameter with a backslash such as '\* OK', loading the configuration generates a validation error: 01070753:3: Monitor /Common/test recv parameter contains an invalid regular expression (Invalid preceding regular expression). Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. Attempting to configure the same monitor via tmsh throws the validation error before creating the monitor, but the GUI allows the single backslash. Two backslashes are required in this case.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to configure a monitor, whose receive string needs to look for a backslash, and only a single backslash is entered in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load after it is successfully created via the GUI. The GUI accepts this when it should throw a validation error: two backslashes are required.
bugs.workaround: When configuring the monitor via the GUI, use two backslashes instead of one.

bugs.title: [GUI] Changes can not be made to GTM listener in partition with default route domain <> 0
bugs.symptoms: When a listener is created in a partition that has a default route domain set, you cannot make changes to the listener in the GUI via DNS -> Delivery -> Listeners. It gives 'Instance not found' error when you try to save the change. Also, a listener in the /Common partition cannot even be viewed when a partition that has a default route domain other than 0 is selected.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using partitions that have default-route-domain set to something other than 0.
bugs.impact: You will be unable to make changes to the listener.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH or through LTM GUI: Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers.

bugs.title: On some platforms the SYN-Cookie status report is not accurate
bugs.symptoms: On a vCMP guest, after a ePVA-enabled virtual server enters SYN Cookie mode, the FPGA will never leave SYN Cookie mode even though BIG-IP has returned to normal mode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs intermittently on virtual servers with ePVA enabled on a vCMP instance where SYN Protection is triggered.
bugs.impact: Since this occurs very intermittently, the entire impact is not known. Initially this is an incorrect SYN Cookie status reporting issue for LTM Virtual statistics, but it is possible that if SYN Cookie mode is triggered again, hardware SYN might not be enabled properly.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade with new fixes for this.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP FPGAs now correctly report hardware SYN Cookie mode.

bugs.title: Injection of JS parts is not always working correctly together with Application CSS Injection
bugs.symptoms: JS part is not injected.
bugs.conditions: JS part is configured with the same tag as CSS Link and we inject into application CSS.
bugs.impact: Lacking WebSafe protection of page.
bugs.workaround: Configure different tags for JS parts and CSS Link.
bugs.fix: JS part is injected always when needed.

bugs.title: Requsts are dropped when custom captcha response page is longer than 1024 bytes
bugs.symptoms: When configuring custom Captcha response page bigger than 1024 bytes, requests are getting dropped instead of getting Captcha response. There is also no indication of error.
bugs.conditions: 1. During Captcha mitigation in DOSL7 2. Custom Captcha response page 3. Requests are getting dropped instead of getting Captcha response.
bugs.impact: Site availability decrease.
bugs.workaround: Change Captcha response to be smaller than 1024 bytes
bugs.fix: No limitation for Captcha page.

bugs.title: Mysqld and bcm56xxd seem to run at 100% on vCMP host.
bugs.symptoms: Mysqld and bcm56xxd seem to run at 100% on vCMP host.
bugs.conditions: When the hypervisor collects statistical data from itself and all hosted guests, too many system resources are used, leading to constant updates of data to mysql.
bugs.impact: This results in the hypervisor not functioning properly.
bugs.workaround: Execute the following command: bigstart stop monpd. Impact of this workaround: Although no statistical data will be collected, the hypervisor will perform all other functions.
bugs.fix: The sampling rate of statistical data was reduced, and samples only the required data for vCMP. As a result, collecting statistical data does not cause a serious impact to system performance, so the vCMP guest no longer experiences potential frequent failovers.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when adding and removing virtual servers with security log profiles
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances when virtual servers are configured with security log profiles TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: Creation, modification and deletion of many virtual servers with security log profiles attached.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash with the following log in /var/log/tmm: <13> Apr 18 13:23:04 <hostname> notice panic: ../base/fw_log_profile.c:3368: Assertion "fw_log_profile_protocol_sip_dos ref non-zero" failed. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with multiple creation, modification and deletion of many virtual servers with security log profiles attached.

bugs.title: Manager role should be allowed to create 'Custom Categories'
bugs.symptoms: When logged into the platform as a User with the role of "Manager" the user will be unable to create custom categories.
bugs.conditions: This only occurs within the GUI.
bugs.impact: GUI is unusable for the creation of new custom categories when user is of role type "Manager"
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH commands instead of GUI
bugs.fix: Now the users operating the GUI as role type "Manager" can create new custom categories.

bugs.title: statsd can core when reading corrupt stats files.
bugs.symptoms: -- The istatsd process produces a core file in the /shared/core directory.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: The istatsd process attempts to read a corrupt iStats segment file with duplicate FIDs. Under these conditions, the istatsd process continually consumes memory which produces a core causing the istatsd process to restart.
bugs.impact: iStatsd process will restart due to resource exhaustion.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can remove the iStats files and restart the istatsd processes. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: This workaround will cause all statistics in the iStats files to reset. 1. Log in to the BIG-IP command line. 2. To stop the istatsd and related processes, type the following command: tmsh stop sys service istatsd avrd merged. 3. To delete the iStats files, type the following command: find /var/tmstat2/ -depth -type f -delete. 4. To start the istatsd and related processes, type the following command: tmsh start sys service istatsd avrd merged.
bugs.fix: Added a fix to protect against a continually reading a segment file that is corrupted and has Duplicate Fids.

bugs.title: BIG-IP sends MP_FASTCLOSE after completing active close of MPTCP connection
bugs.symptoms: After completing an active close of an MPTCP connection, the BIG-IP sends MP_FASTCLOSE.
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile with Multipath TCP enabled is attached to a virtual server, and MPTCP performs an active close of a connection.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP retransmits MP_FASTCLOSE after the connection closing is complete until the maximum number of retransmissions is reached.
bugs.fix: Fixed sequence of events on connection closure.

bugs.title: No confirmation prompt for tmsh 'load sys config base' in command line mode
bugs.symptoms: TMSH 'load /sys config' command does not produce a confirmation prompt when run in the command line mode.
bugs.conditions: Run the TMSH 'load /sys config' command in command line mode.
bugs.impact: The 'load /sys config base' command does not produce confirmation prompt in command line mode. As a result, the operation could result in destructive configuration changes.
bugs.fix: TMSH 'load /sys config' command now produces the confirmation prompt in both the command line mode and interactive mode.

bugs.title: Deterministic NAT combined with NAT64 may cause a TMM core
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when a virtual is configured with nat64 enabled, and a deterministic NAT lsn-pool, and there is traffic.
bugs.conditions: lsn-pool in deterministic mode is attached to a virtual server with nat64 enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Deterministic NAT is not supported with nat64, and should not be configured.

bugs.title: Error when resetting statistics on GSLB Pool Members
bugs.symptoms: GUI error: "An error has occurred while trying to process your request." when attempting to reset the GSLB stats for DNS Pool Members.
bugs.conditions: -- In the GUI on the Statistics :: Module Statistics : DNS : GSLB :: Pool Members page. -- Attempting to reset statistics. Note: This occurs only on Pool Members Statistics. Other Types are unaffected.
bugs.impact: Inability to reset stats for BID-IP DNS Pool Members statistics from the GUI.
bugs.workaround: You can attempt to reset using a command line command similar to the following: $ tmsh reset-stats gtm pool <record> <pool> members { <server_obj>:<member> }. For example: $ tmsh reset-stats gtm pool a myPool1 members { LTM107:/Common/myFastL4VS }.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue on the GSLB Pool Member stats page.

bugs.title: Creating 256 Fundamental Security policies will result in an out of memory error
bugs.symptoms: ASM out of memory error will occur when 256 fundamental security policies are created.
bugs.conditions: Create 256 fundamental security policies.
bugs.impact: Out of memory error.
bugs.fix: Improved memory allocations for shared XML profiles to enable more than 256 fundamental security policies.

bugs.title: Selinux denial seen for apmd when it is being shutdown.
bugs.symptoms: When Apmd process is stopped, you observe a selinux related log which indicates that apmd process does not have the getattr permission for shared memory component owned by tmm.
bugs.conditions: When apmd is stopped or restarted.
bugs.impact: No Impact to APMD functionality. APMd stops and starts normally.

bugs.title: The cbrd daemon runs at 100% CPU utilization
bugs.symptoms: The cbrd daemon runs at 100% CPU utilization. You may notice this issue while inspecting: - The performance graphs for the BIG-IP device. - SNMP reports from the BIG-IP device. - The output of utilities such as top or ps. Note: The cbrd daemon performs XML Content-Based Routing on the BIG-IP system. However, the daemon runs regardless of provisioning and whether the feature is actually being utilized or not.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely occurring event whose cause is not known.
bugs.impact: The cbrd daemon may run inefficiently. Additionally, other control-plane processes running on the BIG-IP device may also be detrimentally affected (depending on the size of the BIG-IP device and its configuration).
bugs.workaround: You can try to work around this issue by restarting the cbrd daemon using the following command: bigstart restart cbrd As the issue occurs rarely, you may not experience this issue again for a long time. This is, however, only a temporary workaround, and will have to be repeated as needed.

bugs.title: Update TZ data
bugs.symptoms: Prior to this update, the data files provided by the tzdata package reflected the Egyptian government's plan to transition to daylight saving time (DST) on July 7, but the Egyptian government canceled the planned transition. This update provides tzdata data files that reflect the change of plans, and will thus provide correct time zone information. This update also includes a time zone transition for Asia/Novosibirsk from +06 to +07 on 2016-07-24 at 02:00.
bugs.conditions: Egyptian or Asia/Novosibirsk time zone active
bugs.impact: Timezone calculations do not reflect current standards
bugs.fix: Timezone data files updated to reflect current standards

bugs.title: Sync requests can be generated faster than they can be handled
bugs.symptoms: Configuration changes in quick succession might generate sync change messages faster than the receiving BIG-IP system can parse them. The sending BIG-IP system's queue for its peer connection fills up, mcp fails to allocate memory, and then the system generates a core file.
bugs.conditions: Configuration changes in quick succession that might generate sync-change messages.
bugs.impact: Core file and sync operation does not complete as expected. The possibility for this occurring depends on the size and complexity of the configuration, which impacts the time required to sync, and the traffic load occurring at the time of the sync operation.

bugs.title: With forward proxy enabled, sometimes the client connection will not complete.
bugs.symptoms: If forward proxy is enabled, and a required forged certificate is not in the cache, the connection might not complete.
bugs.conditions: Forward proxy is enabled, and a required forged certificate is not in the cache.
bugs.impact: Degraded service due to connections not completing.
bugs.fix: The stalling caused by a missing forged certificate no longer happens.

bugs.title: tmsh "ip-whitelist" field DOS application is deprecated
bugs.symptoms: tmsh "ip-whitelist" field DOS application is deprecated, but is still included for backward-compatibility. Since 13.x, it is not recommended to use the following tmsh command to add/modify white IP addresses for DOS application profiles. The "ip-whitelist" field is deprecated in 13.x. To configure the whitelist, use a generic global IP addresses list object. *NOT recommended usage* modify security dos profile dos application modify { all { ip-whitelist add { 8.8.8.8 } } }. *Recommended usage* create security shared-objects address-list dos_auto_http_white_ips_list addresses add { 8.8.8.8 } modify security dos profile dos http-whitelist dos_auto_http_white_ips_list
bugs.conditions: ASM or Purpose built DoS provisioned and a white IP address needs to be configured on the DOS application profile.
bugs.impact: When using the deprecated commands to configure a white IP address list for the DOS application profile. Although there is a warning displayed, the white IP address is added to the profile automatically via a generic global IPs list object, and the list is auto generated using the following name: dos_auto_http_white_ips_list.
bugs.workaround: Use the following commands: create security shared-objects address-list dos_auto_http_white_ips_list addresses add { 8.8.8.8 }. modify security dos profile dos http-whitelist dos_auto_http_white_ips_list.
bugs.fix: This version provides an option to configure a white IP address on the DOS application profile using a deprecated "ip-whitelist" field, the command works and creates a generic IP addresses list automatically, and attaches the list to the DOS profile.
bugs.behavior: When using the deprecated commands to configure a white IP address list for the DOS application profile. Although there is a warning displayed, the white IP address is added to the profile automatically via a generic global IPs list object, and the list is auto generated using the following name: dos_auto_http_white_ips_list.

bugs.title: Config sync fails after creating local user matching previously logged in remote user
bugs.symptoms: After a remote user logs in to a BIG-IP system that is a member of an HA group, if a local user account is created with a name that matches the remote user, config sync fails attempting to sync the local user account to other devices in the HA group.
bugs.conditions: 1. A remotely authenticated user logs in to a BIG-IP HA member. 2. An administrator user creates a local user account on the same BIG-IP HA member with a name that matches the previously logged-in remote user. This problem has been observed using TACACS remote authentication, but is expected to occur with other remote authentication methods as well.
bugs.impact: Unable to sync device groups.
bugs.workaround: 1. To avoid this error, create the local user on a different HA member, where the remote user has not previously logged in. 2. To recover from this error: (a) Delete the newly-created local user from the same HA member where it was created: tmsh del auth user <new-local-user-name> (b) Save current config: tmsh save sys config file <recovery-config-filename.scf> (c) Recover the device group sync status: tmsh run cm config-sync recover-sync (d) Restore the saved config: tmsh load sys config file <recovery-config-filename.scf>

bugs.title: Installing a new version changes the ownership of administrative users' files
bugs.symptoms: Installing a new version changes the ownership of administrative users' files to a different, nonzero UID.
bugs.conditions: A user is an administrative user who has advanced shell (bash) access and custom files in their home directory.
bugs.impact: Low in most cases, since the administrative user can still access most files. One exception is that SSH requires that the authorized_keys file be owned by the user ID in question. This is 0 when a user has an administrative role, so the authorized_keys file will be ignored and a password will still be required for login.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command, substituting a different filename as needed: chown 0 /home/theuser/.ssh/authorized_keys.
bugs.fix: Installing a new version changes the ownership of administrative users' files to a different, nonzero UID. This still happens by design, but no longer applies to the user's SSH configuration files, which stay at UID 0. Therefore, these users are no longer be prevented from using stored public keys in authorized_keys.

bugs.title: Web GUI submits changes to multiple pool members as separate transactions
bugs.symptoms: You notice an unusually high amount of sync traffic when changing many pool members at once. In extreme cases, mcpd may run out of memory and crash.
bugs.conditions: When looking at a list of pool members, it is possible to choose to view many pool members at once, and you can then select them all and enable or disable them with one press of a button. Rather than sending all of the operations in a single transaction, the GUI code updates each pool member one by one. When there are a lot of pool members and auto-sync is being used, this can cause race conditions that can generate a large number of transactions going from the local machine to the remote machine.
bugs.impact: This can cause an unusually high amount of sync traffic to occur between devices in the sync group with auto-sync enabled. In extreme cases this can cause mcpd to crash and traffic is disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: If you frequently need to enable/disable many pool members at once, there are a couple of options: 1. You can switch to manual sync during this operation. 2. You can minimize the number of pool members that are altered at once. The issue was observed when changing over 300 pool members at once.

bugs.title: HSB receive failure lockup due to unreceived loopback packets
bugs.symptoms: HSB reports a lockup due to a receive failure. Analysis of the HSB receive/transmit rings indicate that this is a false positive. Loopback packets were successfully transmitted, but not received, resulting in the receive failure. /var/log/ltm contains this signature: notice *** TMM 9 - PDE 19 - receive failure ***
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: The unit is rebooted.

bugs.title: Gx, Gy and Sd SessionIds have fixed prefixes
bugs.symptoms: All BIG-IP Gx, Gy and Sd end points use the same session ID prefix when communicating to a PCRF/OCS.
bugs.conditions: PEM configured with Gx, Gy or Sd.
bugs.impact: PCRF or DRA connected to multiple BIG-IPs cannot distinguish the Gx, Gy or Sd BIG-IP end-points using the session ID content.
bugs.fix: Gx, Gy or Sd session ID prefix has been made configurable.
bugs.behavior: Gx, Gy and Sd SessionIDs have configurable prefixes with the following default prefixes. Gx.BIG-IP.f5net.com Gy.BIG-IP.f5net.com Sd.BIG-IP.f5net.com

bugs.title: Debug TMM produces core on certain ICMP PMTUD packets
bugs.symptoms: The debug TMM will produce a core on the assert "cwnd or ssthresh too low" when receiving an ICMP PMTUD packet with an MTU larger than the current MTU. This does not affect the default TMM.
bugs.conditions: While using the debug TMM, an ICMP PMTUD packet is received with an MTU larger than the current MTU.
bugs.impact: Debug TMM crashes on assert "cwnd or ssthresh too low." Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Block incoming ICMP PMTUD packets. Note that this will cause Path MTU Discovery to fail, and IP packets sent by the BIG-IP system with the Don't Fragment (DF) bit set may be dropped silently if the MTUs of the devices on the path are configured incorrectly.
bugs.fix: The system now always updates TCP MSS after an ICMP PMTUD packet, so there is no debug TMM core.

bugs.title: Enable ASM option disappears from L7 policy actions
bugs.symptoms: ASM cannot be enabled if 'Application Security Manager' is used in the license string instead of 'ASM'.
bugs.conditions: 'Application Security Manager' is used in the license string instead of 'ASM'.
bugs.impact: The ASM module cannot be enabled using the GUI under certain licenses where ASM is licensed.
bugs.workaround: Enable ASM using tmsh instead of the GUI.
bugs.fix: The issue was caused by the license string used to check the licensing being 'Application Security Manager' instead of 'ASM'. iControl REST does not provide licensing info directly and the license string had to be parsed manually, unlike provisioning. The fix now checks for the spelled out version of the module as well.

bugs.title: Remote authentication for BIG-IP users can fail
bugs.symptoms: While trying to log into the command line of BIG-IP as a remotely authenticated user, login will intermittently fail. You may see the following in /var/log/secure: "err httpd[19596]: pam_ldap: ldap_simple_bind Can't contact LDAP server" but the LDAP server is up and is accessible by the BIG-IP
bugs.conditions: Remote authentication configured, users configured to use remote authentication, ssl-check-peer is enabled and one or more of these properties are different than "none": ssl-ca-cert-file, ssl-client-cert, ssl-client-key.
bugs.impact: The remote authentication service will fail to initiate a connection to the LDAP server with the ssl-check-peer setting enabled, even if the ssl-ca-cert-file is valid. It will terminate the connection and remote authentication will fail.
bugs.workaround: Disabling ssl-check-peer and setting ssl-ca-cert-file, ssl-client-cert and ssl-client-key to "none" can work around this issue.

bugs.title: tmsh list sys db non-default-properties, was listing db vars with default values.
bugs.symptoms: When running "tmsh list sys db non-default-properties", it lists results with default values when it should not.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you run tmsh list sys db non-default-properties.
bugs.impact: All db variables are displayed, not just the ones with no-default properties.
bugs.fix: The tmsh command "list sys db non-default-properties" now only returns results that are not equal to their default values.

bugs.title: scriptd and mcpd cores following multiple failovers due to bd (asm)
bugs.symptoms: You encounter multiple failovers due to BD (asm) failure and mcpd coring. the GUI is sluggish, then bd becomes unresponsive or mcpd cores.
bugs.conditions: Apply policies on a device at the same time that it becomes the Master Blade.
bugs.impact: A deadlock condition can occur when policies are being applied at the same time as a change arrives in the cluster config.
bugs.fix: Fixed a deadlock condition when applying policies.

bugs.title: BGP route-map changes may not immediately trigger route updates
bugs.symptoms: When a route-map is used to filter BGP advertisements, changes to the route-map that affect the filtered routes may not trigger an update to the affected routes.
bugs.conditions: BGP in use with a route-map filtering advertisements.
bugs.impact: BGP table may not reflect route-map changes until "clear ip bgp" is executed.
bugs.workaround: Run "clear ip bgp <neighbor>".
bugs.fix: Changing a route-map used with BGP updates affected routes without clearing the session.

bugs.title: Policy settings change during export/import
bugs.symptoms: Exporting a security policy from one device with specific learning and blocking settings selected, and then imports it to another device, the security policy does not load the expected learning and blocking settings on the target device, and is a mismatch from what is on the source device.
bugs.conditions: On device A: Security :: Application Security : Policy Building : Learning and Blocking Settings • Select 'Enable' and 'Learn' under HTTP protocol compliance failed for all the sub-violations. • Save and export the policy in XML format. • Import to device B.
bugs.impact: The loaded policy on device B does not have all the options checked for HTTP protocol compliance failed for all the sub-violations as expected. When exporting the policy from device B, the name of the exported file does not change to match device B's name, but still remains as device A's name.
bugs.workaround: For exporting a policy that has Policy Builder enabled, use either of the methods below: -- Use XML export: + On export: - Stop policy builder. - Export to XML policy. - Start policy builder. + On import: - Import the XML policy. - Start the policy builder on the newly imported policy. 2) Use binary export/import.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the XML Policy export/import processes so that there are no differences created in the 'HTTP protocol compliance' learning settings

bugs.title: tmrouted may crash when being restarted in debug mode
bugs.symptoms: tmrouted may restart after it being manually restarted with debug level equal or higher than 2.
bugs.conditions: tmrouted is manually restarted with debug level equal or higher than 2. Multi route-domain setup with independent routing processes enabled on several route-domains.
