bugs.impact: tmrouted may restart additional times which can add delay to getting back to service after manually restarting tmrouted. Any restart of tmrouted already causes loss of dynamic routing sessions.
bugs.workaround: Do not use equal or higher than 2 debug level for tmrouted. This should be carried out only under recommendation from F5 Support.
bugs.fix: tmrouted no longer crashes when being restarted in debug mode

bugs.title: Network Failover-based high availability (HA) in AWS may fail
bugs.symptoms: MCPD posts an error that network failover is not configurable: 01071ac2:3: Device-group (/Common/autoscale-group): network-failover property must be disabled in VE-1NIC.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to setup high availability (HA) in Amazon Web Services (AWS) with only 1 network interface.
bugs.impact: Configuration of high availability (HA) in AWS cannot be completed.
bugs.workaround: The current workaround is to configure high availability (HA) in AWS with at least 2 network interfaces.

bugs.title: csyncd crash
bugs.symptoms: csyncd crashes and dumps core under certain conditions. You might see messages such as the following: emerg logger: Re-starting csyncd.
bugs.conditions: csyncd handles filenames that contain certain exotic characters or symbols, or files with very long filenames.
bugs.impact: csyncd will crash and dump core. csyncd retarts continuously.
bugs.fix: csyncd now handles filenames that contain certain exotic characters or symbols, and files with very long filenames.

bugs.title: LSN_DELETE messages may be lost after HA failover
bugs.symptoms: After a failover, an LSN_DELETE message may be lost if the connection continued after the failover.
bugs.conditions: CGNAT configured as an HA pair, with session logging enabled.
bugs.impact: An LSN_DELETE message may be missing from the logs.
bugs.fix: After the fix, the LSN_DELETE message will not be lost.

bugs.title: User deletion doesn't delete tokens issued for that user at max 15 seconds
bugs.symptoms: REST Framework polls for any changes in user every 15 seconds. When user is removed from MCP directly using tmsh or BIG-IP GUI, for REST that user will be still valid for at most 15 seconds. So any authentication tokens issued will not be invalidated and all REST API requests will work as that user remains valid until user deletion is synced.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when users are deleted and the user is still using iControl REST.
bugs.impact: After user deletion from MCP, tokens issued for that user will not immediately deleted from REST
bugs.workaround: After user deletion, customer need to wait at most 15 seconds for change to take effect in REST API
bugs.fix: When user is removed from REST, all tokens issued for that user is invalidated immediately. If a user is removed from MCP either using TMUI or tmsh, that change will be synced to REST after 15 seconds in the worse case.
bugs.behavior: Auth token is removed upon user deletion.

bugs.title: Support launching multiple Horizon View client instances from APM webtop
bugs.symptoms: If there are two different virtuals with APM webtops and VMware View resources, launching the Horizon View client from one of them automatically closes the existing instance of Horizon View client.
bugs.conditions: Two different APM virtual servers with VMware View resources assigned to webtop.
bugs.impact: Cannot have multiple remote desktop sessions opened from different APM virtuals simultaneously.
bugs.fix: APM webtop now makes use of the "useExisting" flag supported by newer versions of Horizon View client, which allows multiple simultaneous instances to run.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE dataplane interfaces change to using UNIC modules instead of sockets.
bugs.symptoms: On AWS and Azure, dataplane interfaces use socket-based networking instead of UNIC modules. After upgrading a version later than 12.1.0, the default module for dataplane interfaces is UNIC modules instead of socket-based networking.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading BIG-IP VE on AWS or Azure running versions 12.0.0 or 12.1.0.
bugs.impact: The raw socket-based tmm driver is replaced by a UNIC driver. The socket-based driver eliminates kernel driver dependencies and provides better portability during kernel/driver upgrades.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP VE socket-based networking driver retained after upgrade on AWS or Azure.

bugs.title: TCP FIN sent with Connection: Keep-Alive header for webtop page resources
bugs.symptoms: When using customized webtops (for example, using custom images for the webtop links), sometimes a TCP FIN flag will be sent with a packet with an HTTP "Connection: Keep-Alive" header. Not all clients recover from this.
bugs.conditions: Use a customized webtop link.
bugs.impact: The webtop links page does not render correctly.
bugs.fix: Weptop page resources no longer send FIN flags with Keep-Alive headers.

bugs.title: HTTPS request to F5 licensing server fails
bugs.symptoms: Licensing BIG-IP systems through REST API fails.
bugs.conditions: Licensing BIG-IP systems using the REST API.
bugs.impact: Cannot use REST API to license BIG-IP systems.
bugs.workaround: Use TMUI or TMSH to license BIG-IP systems.
bugs.fix: Licensing BIG-IP systems through REST API now completes successfully.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system does not accept BGP connection requests when using peer-groups and no default address family.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not accept incoming or initiate outgoing BGP connections when using peer-groups and no default address family.
bugs.conditions: BGP configured with 'no bgp default ipv4-unicast' and neighbors configured using a peer group that's explicitly activated for IPv4.
bugs.impact: The BGP connection to any neighbor in the peer group will not come up until 'clear ip bgp' is run on the neighbor or tmrouted is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Clear the BGP neighbor after changing the configuration.
bugs.fix: BGP connections for neighbors in a peer group come up correctly when 'no bgp default ipv4-unicast' is configured.

bugs.title: apm client-packaging object missing in existing partitions after provisioning APM
bugs.symptoms: apm client packaging is missing for the partitions that are created before provisioning APM. This will prevent users customizing client package .
bugs.conditions: This happens to all the partitions that are created before APM is provisioned. Prevents users to customize the client package.
bugs.impact: User cannot customize the client packages
bugs.workaround: Create partition after APM is provisioned.
bugs.fix: Create apm client packaging object for all the partitions at the provisioning time.

bugs.title: coapi error on the shell, when user clicks on session in the manage sessions page
bugs.symptoms: Shows the error message similar to the following in console: err coapi: [error] [client 165.160.15.20] PHP Warning: date(): It is not safe to rely on the system's timezone settings. You are *required* to use the date.timezone setting or the date_default_timezone_set() function. In case you used any of those methods and you are still getting this warning, you most likely misspelled the timezone identifier. We selected the timezone 'UTC' for now, but please set date.timezone to select your timezone. in /var/sam/www/admin/reports/index.php on line 8, referer:
bugs.conditions: When you click on the GUI's session page, the error shows up in the console.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact to APM or the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: None. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the correct timezone, so no error occurs when clicking on the GUI's session page.

bugs.title: Incorrect process priority in vCMP guest results in low priority of the guest control-plane, which might cause high availability failover
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect process priority in vCMP guest results in low priority of the guest control-plane, which might cause high availability failover.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: * vCMP provisioned. * vCMP hypervisor (host) running 12.1.0 * vCMP guest with 2 or more cores deployed and running 11.5.0 or greater. * vCMP guest has HT-Split enabled (tmsh list sys db scheduler.splitplanes.ltm).
bugs.impact: vCMP guests may experience control-plane issues (such as failures to send or receive network failover traffic in an HA-pair, causing a failover).
bugs.fix: This release restores the process nice value of VCMP guest control-plane, so the vCMP guest no longer experiences potential frequent failovers.

bugs.title: iControl REST with 3rd party auth does not function as expected with '@' / email addresses as username.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use username containing an 'at' ( @ ) character, or specify the email address when requesting authentication token using iControl REST when 3rd party authentication provider being used.
bugs.conditions: Set-up the BIG-IP system to use 3rd party RADIUS or LDAP authentication and configure a username containing an 'at' ( @ ) character, or specify the email address.
bugs.impact: Cannot authenticate and get authentication token using iControl REST.
bugs.workaround: Do not use username with special characters, such as 'at' ( @ ), period ( . ), and so on).
bugs.fix: Updated logic to allow any special characters in username and password when 3rd party authentication system is used on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Policy with UTF-8 encoding retains disallowed high ASCII meta-characters after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Policy with UTF-8 encoding has disallowed high ASCII meta-characters even after upgrade, which results in suggestions for allowing meta-characters that cannot be accepted.
bugs.conditions: System with a policy with encoding set to UTF-8 (uppercase). Upgrading from v11.6.x/v12.x to v12.1.2 or 13.0.0.
bugs.impact: Suggestions for allowing high ASCII meta-characters cannot be accepted.
bugs.fix: The upgrade process now fixes policies that had their encoding stored in uppercase as well.

bugs.title: DB variable changed via GUI does not sync across HA group
bugs.symptoms: If a configuration change is made in the BIG-IP GUI which is backed by a DB variable, the change is not synced to other devices in the same sync-failover device group. If the same db variable change is made using the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh), the db variable change will be synced to other devices in the same sync-failover device group. Note that db variable changes are never synced to devices in sync-only device groups.
bugs.conditions: 1. BIG-IP systems in HA group, provisioned with modules (in addition to LTM) which create their own device groups (for example, ASM). 2. Original sync-failover device group replaced by a different sync-failover device group. 3. Using the GUI to change a configuration item which is backed by a DB variable. Examples include: failover.standby.linkdowntime (GUI: Device Management :: Device Groups : <fodg_name> : Failover : Link Down Time on Failover ) statemirror.clustermirroring (GUI: Device Management :: Devices : <device_name> : Cluster Options )
bugs.impact: Configuration of devices within a sync-failover device group may not be synchronized as expected.
bugs.workaround: To force synchronization of a db variable change made via the GUI, use a tmsh command of the following form: tmsh modify cm device-group <sync-failover device group name> devices modify { <device name> { set-sync-leader } } If the sync-failover device group is not automatically synced, manually sync the device group: tmsh run cm config-sync to-group <sync-failover device group name> To avoid creating a db variable change that will not be synchronized across sync-failover device group members, change the configuration or db variable using tmsh: tmsh modify sys db <variable name> value <new value> If the sync-failover device group is not automatically synced, manually sync the device group: tmsh run cm config-sync to-group <sync-failover device group name>
bugs.fix: DB variable changed via GUI now syncs across HA group as expected.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when /sys db tm.simultaneousopen is set to reset or drop_connection
bugs.symptoms: When the /sys db tm.simultaneousopen variable is set to 'reset' or 'drop_connection', TMM may crash during a TCP simultaneous 4 way handshake.
bugs.conditions: 1. The /sys db tm.simultaneousopen variable is set to 'reset' or 'drop_connection'. 2. A TCP 4 way handshake (simultaneous open) occurs as described in RFC 793.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: The crash can be avoided, while still mitigating TCP 4 way handshakes, by setting the /sys db tm.simultaneousopen variable to 'drop_pkt'.

bugs.title: FTP traffic does not work through SNAT when configured without Virtual Server
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to 12.1.0 or 12.1.1, FTP traffic no longer works correctly with SNAT, when SNAT is configured without a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system configured to allow FTP traffic through, and SNAT is configured without a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not SNAT port 21 traffic. In rare circumstances this can cause tmm to restart.
bugs.fix: FTP traffic now works through SNAT when SNAT is configured without a virtual server.

bugs.title: Request-oriented OneConnect load balancing ends when the server returns an error status code.
bugs.symptoms: Request-oriented OneConnect load balancing ends when the server returns an error status code.
bugs.conditions: OneConnect is enabled and the server responds with a HTTP error status code.
bugs.impact: The client remains connected to the server, and no further load-balancing decisions are made.
bugs.workaround: It may be possible to detect the HTTP status code in the response, and manually detach the client-side. To do so, use an iRule similar to the following: when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { [HTTP::status] == 200 } { return } if { [HTTP::status] == 401 } { set auth_header [string tolower [HTTP::header values "WWW-Authenticate"]] if { $auth_header contains "negotiate" || $auth_header contains "ntlm" } { # Connection-oriented auth. System should already be doing the right thing unset auth_header return } unset auth_header } catch { ONECONNECT::detach enable } }. Note: These workarounds should not be used when the backend server is using connection-oriented HTTP authentication (e.g., NTLM or Negotiate authentication).
bugs.fix: With OneConnect, the client-side remains detachable when the server-side returns an HTTP error status code.

bugs.title: False-positive header related violation
bugs.symptoms: The system reports a false-positive, header-related violation.
bugs.conditions: -- A custom header is added to the system. -- A header-related violation is turned on.
bugs.impact: The system reports a false-positive violation.

bugs.title: GUI total number of records not correctly initialized with search string on several pages.
bugs.symptoms: GUI total number of records not correctly initialized with search string on several pages.
bugs.conditions: Searching on the Data Group File List, iFile List, and lw4o6 File Object List pages.
bugs.impact: GUI shows that there are two pages, but advancing to the second page shows empty page.
bugs.workaround: Avoid searching in the Data Group File List, iFile List, and lw4o6 File Object List pages to view all items.
bugs.fix: Searching in the Data Group File List, iFile List, and lw4o6 File Object List pages works as expected.

bugs.title: i5x00, i7x00, i10x00 series appliances may use sensor number instead of name "LCD health" reporting communication error
bugs.symptoms: If the LCD is not communicating with BIG-IP when the chassis manager daemon starts occasionally LCD errors will be displayed using the sensor number rather than the name "LCD"
bugs.conditions: chmand restart and LCD unable to commuicate
bugs.impact: cosmetic
bugs.fix: LCD error will show name "LCD" rather than sensor number in communication error.

bugs.title: Multidomain SSO slave virtual cannot be reached
bugs.symptoms: One or multiple slave virtual servers cannot be reached in a Multidomain SSO use case. This happens due to a bug during the configuration of the SSO Auth Domains in the Access Profile. When a user attempts to access the virtual, it will not be reachable. The following message will appear on Warning level in the TMM logs: Multidomain SSO enabled for profile: <access-profile>. No matching domain found for request host: <host>.
bugs.conditions: This happens intermittently only after adding and deleting many auth domains.
bugs.impact: The virtual server is not reachable.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM
bugs.fix: The auth domain is added correctly when configured and can be found at runtime for proper execution of Multidomain SSO.

bugs.title: DoS Application - Block requests from suspicious browsers feature causes javascript latency for webapp first page
bugs.symptoms: When an end-user accesses a web-site's first page there is a noticeable latency until it gets the page content.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when ASM is provisioned with proactive bot defense enabled, when accessing the page for a first time.
bugs.impact: Bad user experience when accessing the website's first page.
bugs.fix: The javascript has improved as much as possible to reduce the time to get the website's first page.

bugs.title: Clustered Multiprocessing (CMP) peer connection may not be removed
bugs.symptoms: - High memory usage due to connflow allocations - conn_remove_cf_not_found stat is non-zero
bugs.conditions: CMP with multiple TMMs. CMP peer connection is removed before it has been established.
bugs.impact: Low memory may lead to allocation failures that may lead to tmm core
bugs.fix: Fix validation performed on parsed CMP flow keys that allows unknown CMP connections to be removed.

bugs.title: ASM errors during policy import
bugs.symptoms: Import failure when importing ASM policy with many Session Awareness Data Points. ASM logs errors similar to the following: -- crit g_server_rpc_handler_async.pl[10933]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl,F5::ASMConfig::Handler::log_error_and_rollback): Could not update the Export Policy Task 'Export Policy Task (1469519765.114479)'. DBD::mysql::db do failed: Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Session Awareness enabled. -- Many (more than 1000) active Session Awareness 'Block All' data points are present. -- Export a policy. -- Import the same policy.
bugs.impact: asm_config_server crash occurs. asm_config_server recovers automatically, within ~15-30 seconds.
bugs.workaround: Either release all Session Awareness Data Points before export, or remove them from the exported policy before importing it back.
bugs.fix: Import failure no longer occurs when importing ASM policy with more than 1000 Session Awareness Data Points. Now, there is a maximum of 1000 Session Awareness Data Points exported into an XML policy export.

bugs.title: ASM policy diff issue for HTTP method HEAD
bugs.symptoms: Policy diff erroneously indicates a difference with the HTTP HEAD method.
bugs.conditions: This always occurs for the HEAD method.
bugs.impact: Wrong results in policy diff.
bugs.fix: Policy diff no longer erroneously indicates a difference with the HTTP HEAD method.

bugs.title: REWRITE filter should enable INFLATE only when it is necessary for content detection and patching.
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite in 'uri-translation' mode and HTML profiles are requesting to decompress all responses from backend server. This could impact performance and cause extra memory usage.
bugs.conditions: -- Either rewrite profile in 'uri-translation' mode or HTML profile is attached to a virtual server. -- Backend responds with compressed data for any types other than HTML and CSS.
bugs.impact: Performance of Rewrite and HTML profiles is not optimal in case of compressed responses which should not be modified.

bugs.title: Large Websocket frames corrupted
bugs.symptoms: If large Websocket frames are being sent by the end-point and this transfer is interleaved with frames being sent by the other endpoint, corrupted frames could be sent by BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: Websocket profile is attached to the virtual. Large Websocket frames are sent by the end-point. This transfer is interleaved with frames being sent in the other direction.
bugs.impact: Connection reset because of corrupted frames being received by the end-point.

bugs.title: Hidden directories and files are not synchronized to secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: Hidden directories and files (those whose filenames start with '.') that are created on primary blade are not synced to secondary blades. Existing hidden files that are edited on the primary blade are not synced to secondaries.
bugs.conditions: Multi-bladed system.
bugs.impact: The most common uses of hidden files are per-user shell configuration and history.
bugs.workaround: Manually copy configuration files onto other blades.

bugs.title: Switch interfaces may seem up after bcm56xxd goes down
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh show net interface' may show that switch ports are still up after bcm56xxd is brought down. This is because bcm56xxd does not notify mcpd that bcm56xxd will go down.
bugs.conditions: If the switch ports are up and bcm56xxd is brought down, 'tmsh show net interface' will show that the switch ports are still up.
bugs.impact: The switch ports may seem up, but traffic can't be sent/received.
bugs.fix: Fix for bcm56xxd to notify mcpd that all ports become uninitialized before it goes down has already been implemented.

bugs.title: Encrypted cookie insert persistence with fallback may not honor cookie after fallback expires
bugs.symptoms: You notice erratic persistence behavior when you set cookie persistence to "required" in your cookie persistence profile
bugs.conditions: Encrypted cookie persistence with fallback where the fallback persistence has a reasonable short timer such that a request containing a valid cookie is handled after the fallback entry has expired.
bugs.impact: Persistence fails after fallback expired.
bugs.workaround: Change cookie-encryption to preferred which allows persistence on either encrypted or decrypted cookie.

bugs.title: TMM is killed by SOD (missing heartbeat) during geoip_reload performing munmap.
bugs.symptoms: TMM is killed by SOD (missing heartbeat) during geoip_reload performing munmap.
bugs.conditions: This can occur under normal operation, while running the geo_update command.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Running the geo_update command no longer causes this error.

bugs.title: Devices in sync group end up with differing configs after ucs restore.
bugs.symptoms: After a GTM UCS restore, Devices in sync group end up with differing configs.
bugs.conditions: Restoring an older UCS file in a GTM config, but the interface is marked down (not physically disconnected)
bugs.impact: Newer configuration objects will likely be deleted after the older configuration synchronizes to the sync group.
bugs.workaround: Ensure you disconnect the network interface before restoring an older UCS file as specified in SOL14083: Preventing synchronization when installing a UCS archive on a BIG-IP GTM system at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/solutions/public/14000/000/sol14083.html

bugs.title: Safenet 6.2 library missing after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading BIG-IP, a symbolic link is missing to the core Safenet library.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a BIG-IP installation with Safenet 6.2 already installed is upgraded.
bugs.impact: Safenet 6.2 is not functional.
bugs.workaround: Reinstall Safenet 6.2. Or, run this command at all blades of BIG-IP after the installation. ln -sf /shared/safenet/toolkit/libgem.so /usr/lib64/openssl/engines/libgem.so
bugs.fix: Add symbolic link to libgem at time of pkcs11d daemon start/restart.

bugs.title: In the iRule output of X509 Certificate's subject & issuer, the display is wrong.
bugs.symptoms: When using iRule to output X509 Certificate's subject & issuer, the display is wrong.
bugs.conditions: Using iRule command "X509::subject" & "X509::issuer" to get the Cert's subject &issuer, and then using log to display them.
bugs.impact: The iRule output of X509 Certificate's subject & issuer is wrong.
bugs.fix: In the iRule output of X509 Cert's subject & issuer, we should use the the more readable flag XN_FLAG_ONELINE in the X509_NAME_print_ex() as openssl used.
bugs.behavior: In this release the order of output is reversed for the X509::subject as compared to previous versions. This change was done to make the output of [X509::subject [SSL::cert 0]] OpenSSL-compatible. -- In prior versions without the fix the format is: CN=USERNAME,OU=CONTRACTOR,OU=PKI,OU=DEPT,O=COMPANY,C=US -- In versions with the fix the format now requires spaces between these attributes: C=US, O=COMPANY, OU=DEPT, OU=PKI, OU=CONTRACTOR, CN=USERNAME IMPORTANT: Depending on iRules you have configured, this change might impact application functionality that depends on the old format. If your application expects the output X509::subject to be in the old format, make sure to modify the iRules after upgrading. To use the new format in any iRules that use the old structure, change the output format of the X.509 certificate subject to use this format: C=US, O=COMPANY, OU=DEPT, OU=PKI, OU=CONTRACTOR, CN=USERNAME Additional note: Comma (,) is a valid character in X509::subject. In this release, the escaping method has changed. -- In prior versions, the subject string returned by X509::subject escapes comma with backslash (\): Rule /Common/rule_customer <CLIENTSSL_HANDSHAKE>: Subject DN: CN=user8,OU=DEPT,O=COMPANY\,,L=Tokyo,ST=Tokyo,C=JP When writing an iRule to validate the string, comma is already escaped by the backslash, but backslash should be escaped by another backslash as follows: set dn_validation "OU=DEPT,O=COMPANY\\,,L=Tokyo" -- In versions with the fix, the subject string returned by X509::subject wraps attributes with double quotation marks (""). Rule /Common/rule_customer <CLIENTSSL_HANDSHAKE>: Subject DN: C=JP, ST=Tokyo, L=Tokyo, O="COMPANY,", OU=DEPT, CN=user8 When writing an iRule to validate the string, the whole attribute should be enclosed with double quotation marks, and each double quotation mark should be escaped by a backslash: set dn_validation "L=Tokyo, O=\"COMPANY,\", OU=DEPT"

bugs.title: Analytics UI time format determined by System clock preferences
bugs.symptoms: Currently there is no consistent way to display timestamps. Some places use 12-hour notation while other 24-hour. Analytics UI has been using 24-hour historically. However, now that the BIG-IP system has a setting for this under System :: Preferences, Analytics will use this value to determine whether timestamps display in 12-hour or 24-hour format.
bugs.conditions: Viewing timestamps.
bugs.impact: Analytics pages will use 12-hour format on systems that are set to display 12-hour by default. This differs from the always-24-hour format that appeared in the past.
bugs.fix: Analytics pages use system preferences to determine whether 12-hour or 24-hour time formats are displayed.
bugs.behavior: Analytics UI time format is now determined by System clock preferences. Previously, there was no consistent way of displaying timestamps. Some places use 12-hour notation while other 24-hour. Analytics UI has been using 24-hour historically. However, now that the BIG-IP system has a setting for this under System :: Preferences, Analytics will use this value to determine whether timestamps display in 12-hour or 24-hour format.

bugs.title: False alert in daemon log (/var/log/daemon.log) when listing all certificates using iControl SOAP or GUI
bugs.symptoms: When calling get_certificate_list_v2 in iControl SOAP or browsing to "System ›› Certificate Management : Device Certificate Management : Device Certificate" in GUI, it prints the error message in the log: "big3 err iControlPortal.cgi[21270]: Could not find any crypto codecs supporting key management"
bugs.conditions: The false alert error appears when it is not a FIPS box.
bugs.impact: There is no impact. The message is supposed to be a neutral message instead of an error message.
bugs.fix: The message will only be displayed in the debug log, instead of appearing as an error message.

bugs.title: Send MSS on SYN,ACK when SYN does not have any options
bugs.symptoms: When the SYN does not have any options set, TCP does not set any options on the SYN-ACK.
bugs.conditions: TCP receives SYN without options.
bugs.impact: No options are set on SYN-ACK.
bugs.fix: You can now use a newly introduced sysdb variable TM.TcpSendSynAckMSSAlways to enable or disable this feature. If SYSdb TM.TcpSendSynAckMSSAlways is enabled and profile MSS is not equal to default MSS, TCP always sets the MSS option to the Profile MSS value on SYN-ACK.
bugs.behavior: In earlier versions, if SYN did not have any options set, the system did not set any options on the SYN-ACK. There is now a new sysdb variable TM.TcpSendSynAckMSSAlways, which you can use to enable or disable this feature. If SYSdb TM.TcpSendSynAckMSSAlways is enabled and profile MSS is not equal to default MSS, TCP always sets the MSS option to the Profile MSS value on SYN-ACK.

bugs.title: Memory leak when multiple DHCP servers are configured, and the last DHCP server configured is down.
bugs.symptoms: When the last member of a list of multiple DHCP servers is down, the original DHCP packet from client is not freed and memory is leaked.
bugs.conditions: Multiple DHCP servers are configured, and the last DHCP server configured is down.
bugs.impact: Packet memory is leaked.
bugs.workaround: Remove the last DHCP server that is down, or move it to the middle or front of the server member list.
bugs.fix: Free the original packet memory when last DHCP server is down.

bugs.title: GUI becomes unresponsive when managing GSLB Pool
bugs.symptoms: GUI Locks Up and becomes unresponsive. Most major web browsers will complain about slow javascript and prompt you to kill the script.
bugs.conditions: Managing an A type GSLB pool when hundereds of virtual servers exist. These virtual servers do not have to be associated with the pool you are attempting to manage.
bugs.impact: Page takes a significantly long time to load.
bugs.workaround: Manage pools through tmsh, or wait for it to load.

bugs.title: tmsh provides option to delete all URLs from a custom category, which is not possible
bugs.symptoms: tmsh provides a command option for admin to delete all URLs from a custom category. However, this is not a valid option, and an error will be displayed. The system presents the following error: Configuration error: Cannot delete url (http://www.example.com*). This occurs because because url-category (/Common/ex) is a custom category. A custom category must have at least one URL.
bugs.conditions: Running the following command: tmsh modify sys url-db url-category pattern urls delete { all }
bugs.impact: No URLs are deleted. Each URL must be deleted individually.
bugs.workaround: Delete URLs individually.

bugs.title: MTU values of range [9001-9198] is not supported in some Operating Systems.
bugs.symptoms: Some hypervisors don't support MTU value higher than 9000, thus modifying the MTU in [9001-9198] range is not supported.
bugs.conditions: Running on a hypervisor/host that doesn't support MTU value higher than 9000 for network interfaces.
bugs.impact: Trying to set MTU to a value within [9001-9198] will result in BIG-IP responding with "Invalid argument" error.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround to this issue as this is the issue on the hypervisor side. Customer should read hypervisor documentation to find out what range of values the given host supports.

bugs.title: Improve 407 based authentication to allow flexible support for Basic, NTLM and Kerberos
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP can only identify users based on NTLM Auth credentials, not combined with Kerberos and Basic. Not all clients are capable of NTLM authentication (or behave erratically when HTTPS comes on top like Apple Safari on MacOS) and not all are capable of Kerberos authentication. BIG-IP benefits from the speed and security of Kerberos authentication while leaving the option for the client to fall back to NTLM if the client is not able to present a Kerberos token instead of falling back directly to insecure Basic authentication.
bugs.conditions: In APM access policy, APM needs to have an option to authenticate user accounts with a 407 response and offer Kerberos, NTLM and Basic together.
bugs.impact: - performance lacks due to the regular authentications happening between the F5 SWG and the Active Directory. All requests for each element get a 407 back for another NTLM authentication that then leads to a communication between the SWG and the AD domain controller. If this were Kerberos the SWG would just need to verify if the Kerberos token is still valid. - If a client does not support NTLM it has no chance to authenticate although it might still support basic authentication.

bugs.title: SIP Parser fails header with multiple sequential separators inside quoted string.
bugs.symptoms: SIP Parser fails header with multiple sequential separators inside quoted string.
bugs.conditions: If a SIP header contains multiple attribute separators ',' or ';' in an attribute.
bugs.impact: The SIP parser flags the message as an error. If this occurs in a quote within the attribute, it should be allowed, but it will still fail, Valid SIP messages are failing to be parsed.
bugs.fix: The SIP parser has been improved to ignore multiple sequential separators if within quotes.

bugs.title: Licensing causes SELinux denied messages for mcpd
bugs.symptoms: After you apply a license, you see the following in /var/log/audit/auditd.log: type=AVC msg=audit(1469642592.548:489): avc: denied { relabelto } for pid=6908 comm="mcpd" name="bigip.license.chs600493s" dev=dm-10 ino=25 scontext=system_u:system_r:mcpd_t:s0 tcontext=system_u:object_r:tmp_t:s0 tclass=file.
bugs.conditions: This may be seen when licensing or during reactivation of a license.
bugs.impact: The errors are benign and can be safely ignored.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is a cosmetic error.
bugs.fix: Licensing no longer causes SELinux denied messages for mcpd.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when in Fallback state.
bugs.symptoms: There is a chance, when HTTP in Fallback mode, HTTP filter sends Abort event to TCP filter (causing tear down) prematurely while the Aborting triggered by upper filter/proxy is in flight. TMM may crash when this happens.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what conditions need to exist to trigger this, but it has been known to trigger when issuing HTTP::respond in the LB_FAILED event in an iRule, and it has been seen only rarely.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: no work around
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash

bugs.title: DTLS client (serverssl profile) fails to complete resumed handshake.
bugs.symptoms: DTLS client (serverssl profile) fails to complete resumed handshake.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the BIG-IP system acts as a DTLS client.
bugs.impact: Possible failed resumed handshake.
bugs.workaround: Disable session reuse.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a possible failed resumed DTLS handshake.

bugs.title: Some information displayed in "list net interface" will be stale for interfaces that change bundle state
bugs.symptoms: Changing the bundling on an interface does not clear the following fields in the previously configured interface: module-description, serial, vendor, vendor-oui, vendor-partnum, vendor-revision. That information will be correct for the active interface, it is just not cleared for the previously configured interface. Module description is not correctly reported on unbundled interfaces.
bugs.conditions: Bundling change on an interface
bugs.impact: "list net interface" on previously configured interfaces will show stale information. May be confusing. Module description is missing from "list net interface" on unbundled interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Stale data will clear on a reboot. This is purely a display issue, it does not affect the functionality of the currently configured interfaces.

bugs.title: Cannot delete partition when APM Sandbox configuration is present
bugs.symptoms: A partition cannot be removed when the APM Sandbox configuration is present and APM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: -- APM Sandbox configuration exists in partition other than Common. -- APM is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: Partition cannot be deleted.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can first provision APM and then delete the partition. This will require a restart of services. Another work around is to remove the bigip.conf file from under /config/partitions/<partition folder> and reload the full configuration. For example: 1) rm /config/partitions/<partition>/bigip.conf 2) tmsh load sys config 3) tmsh delete sys folder /<partition>
bugs.fix: Now, you can delete partition when APM Sandbox configuration is present.

bugs.title: Citrix Desktop/application name defined at broker is not correctly displayed.
bugs.symptoms: Title of the Citrix desktop or application resource is not displayed correctly.
bugs.conditions: Title parameter is absent in the ICA file.
bugs.impact: User-defined 'display name' of Citrix desktop is absent.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Title parameter is now inserted in the ICA file so that it is correctly displayed.

bugs.title: Secondary blades restart when modifying a virtual server's route domain in a different partition.
bugs.symptoms: Secondary blades restart when modifying a virtual server's route domain in a different partition. This log signature is in /var/log/ltm before the secondaries restart: err mcpd[1255]: 0107004d:3: Virtual address (/stef/1.1.1.1%0) encodes IP address (1.1.1.1) which differs from supplied IP address field (1.1.1.1%1).
bugs.conditions: - Multiple blades of vCMP guests in a sync-failover group. - Route domains created on each device. - Route domain assigned to a new partition after they were created.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while secondary blades restart.
bugs.fix: Secondary blades no longer restart when modifying a virtual server's route domain in a different partition.

bugs.title: DoS/Firewall GUI will not work with IE versions 10 or lower
bugs.symptoms: GUI pages may not be rendered at all (blank pages) or will show gibberish.
bugs.conditions: Using BIG-IP TMUI using IE 10 or lower.
bugs.impact: GUI pages may not be rendered at all (blank pages) or will show gibberish.
bugs.workaround: Use IE-11 or Microsoft Edge.

bugs.title: Crash: Tmm crashing when active system connections are deleted from cli
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP is in DHCP forwarding mode, if the giaddr field in the unicast DHCP renewal packet is set to DHCP relay agent IP address by relay agent, tmm may crash when active system connections are deleted from cli or via aging.
bugs.conditions: 1) BIG-IP in forwarding mode 2) giaddr field in unicast DHCP renewal packet is set to IP address of relay agent (Typically, it is set to 0 by the DHCP client)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This is not a typical network setup. Usually DHCP relay agent will not modify DHCP renewal packet to insert its own address as giaddr.

bugs.title: Unnecessary DTLS retransmissions occur during handshake.
bugs.symptoms: Unnecessary DTLS retransmissions occur during handshake.
bugs.conditions: During DTLS handshake, unnecessary retransmissions of handshake message may occur on VE platform.
bugs.impact: Possible DTLS handshake failure on VE platform.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a possible failed DTLS handshake on VE platforms.

bugs.title: Add the ability to modify cspm cache cookie name (currently "f5_cspm")
bugs.symptoms: AVR uses cspm cache cookie for page load time calculations. The cookie name is currently f5_cspm constantly
bugs.conditions: When page load time metric is requested, AVR injects the cspm cache cookie.
bugs.impact: The admin does not have the ability to change the cspm cache cookie name.
bugs.fix: Admins can now change the value of the default db variable, Avr.CspmCacheCookieName, and rename this cookie as required.

bugs.title: Reporting missing parameter details when attack signature is matched against parameter value
bugs.symptoms: A parameter is shown without parameters details or with garbled parameter details in the local logging GUI.
bugs.conditions: An attack signature was detected in a parameter value.
bugs.impact: Bad reporting

bugs.title: TMM crash on memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases tmm might crash on memory corruption.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what sequence of events triggers this condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes on memory corruption in rare cases.

bugs.title: iControl REST API sets non-default persistence profile prop to "none"; properties not present in iControl REST API responseiControl REST API, sets persistence profile's non-default property value as "none"; properties missing in iControl REST API response
bugs.symptoms: For persistence profiles, iControl REST does not provide visibility for property override when "none" is specified, including references, passwords, and array of strings.
bugs.conditions: -- Use iControl REST API with persistence profiles. -- string, enum, or vector of enum/string property explicitly set to "none" for a component within any REST API endpoint specialized in /etc/icrd.conf.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST API response skips these elements. iControl REST does not provide visibility for persistence profile property overrides.
bugs.fix: iControl REST API now returns persistence profile elements (i.e., string, enum , or vector of enum/string property that is explicitly set to "none" for a component within any REST API endpoint specialized in /etc/icrd.conf) with a value "none". The exclusion to this policy is the secured attributes. Secured attributes are always excluded from the iControl REST API response.

bugs.title: Config sync after deleting iApp f5.citrix_vdi.v2.3.0 could leave an extra tunnel object on synced system
bugs.symptoms: After deleting an iApp build from the f5.citrix_vdi.v2.3.0 template then running a config sync, the system that received the sync could have a tunnel object left over which should have been deleted. Running 'tmsh load sys config verify' after this sync would give the following error. 01070734:3: Configuration error: The object (Tunnel /Common/test-citrix-app-svc.app/test-citrix-app-svc_connect) is owned by a non-existent application (/Common/test-citrix-app-svc.app/test-citrix-app-svc). Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the iApp has been deployed in a sync group, then the iApp is deleted, then a config sync is initiated.
bugs.impact: Config validation fails, and you must delete the tunnel manually.
bugs.workaround: On the system that received the sync, edit /config/BIG-IP_base.conf to remove the following objects (replace "test-citrix-app-svc" with the name of the deleted iApp): a. vlan from net route-domain: /Common/test-citrix-app-svc.app/test-citrix-app-svc_connect b. net fdb tunnel /Common/test-citrix-app-svc.app/test-citrix-app-svc_connect c. net tunnels tunnel /Common/test-citrix-app-svc.app/test-citrix-app-svc_connect
bugs.fix: The autogenerated tunnel is now successfully removed on receiving devices.

bugs.title: Add extra decision logging for LTM load balancing (support only)
bugs.symptoms: It can be difficult to troubleshoot issues with LTM load balancing; existing logging is not detailed enough to troubleshoot some issues.
bugs.conditions: Support is troubleshooting issues with LTM load balancing.
bugs.impact: Support is unable to accurately determine why the system sends traffic to specific pool members.
bugs.fix: Added extra logging for load balancing. This logging is mainly for support to enable (it is not intended for use by the end-user at this stage).

bugs.title: Some iApp LX packages will not be saved during upgrade or UCS save/restore
bugs.symptoms: iApp LX packages that include dependencies on system utilities (like /bin/sh, /bin/bash, python etc.) cannot be imported to iApp LX RPM database.
bugs.conditions: oApp LX packages that depends on system utilities.
bugs.impact: iApp LX packages with dependencies will not be restored during upgrade or UCS restore process.
bugs.fix: iApp LX UCS save process is updated turn off automatic dependency generation by rpmbuild so iApp LX package can be imported during UCS restore or upgrade.

bugs.title: TMM may restart if SSO plugin configuration initialization fails due to internal error in tmconf library
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart when new SAML SSO configuration is created on BIG-IP systems as SAML IdP. This could also happen when BIG-IP is restarted, or a saved configuration containing SAML SSO objects is loaded on running BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: All of the following - The BIG-IP system is used as SAML IdP - New SAML SSO configuration is added on BIG-IP - Rarely occurring internal tmconf error happens when processing newly added configuration.
bugs.impact: TMM may restart.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer restarts when internal error happens upon adding new SAML SSO configurations. Instead, the system logs the following error in /var/log/apm to indicate problematic configuration object: Internal error processing sso config <name>.

bugs.title: Dynamic ACL agent error log message contains garbage data
bugs.symptoms: Starting in BIG-IP version 12.0.0, Dynamic ACL error log messages might contain garbage data.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Dynamic ACL detects incorrect syntax of an ACL entry.
bugs.impact: The system logs garbage data.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the ACL entry is correct.
bugs.fix: Dynamic ACL error log messages no longer contain garbage data when Dynamic ACL detects incorrect syntax of an ACL entry.

bugs.title: LocalDB auth agent is not available for APM based system auth
bugs.symptoms: LocalDB auth agent is not available for APM based system auth.
bugs.conditions: Try to add LocalDB auth agent to access profile for APM profile type of system auth. VPE does not show LocalDB auth agent for System auth access profiles.
bugs.impact: You are unable to assign a LocalDB auth agent for APM based system auth.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: LocalDB auth agent is now available for APM based system auth. LocalDB auth agent can be added in VPE for access profiles with type system auth.

bugs.title: Shrink/Expand imgs of Webtop Section is customizable
bugs.symptoms: Changing images for Shrink/Expand of Webtop Section in Webtop Customization does not actually change images on client; users see default images instead
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when using Webtop Customization.
bugs.impact: The default image is displayed instead of the customized image.
bugs.fix: Customization of Shrink/Expand images is working properly now in Webtop Section in Webtop Customization.

bugs.title: Policy learning is slow under high load
bugs.symptoms: On systems with high load, policy learning is slow and learning suggestions are slow to arrive.
bugs.conditions: Policy builder generates many learning suggestions on a system that processes intense traffic.
bugs.impact: Learning suggestions appear with considerable delay, policy learning speed goes down.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with slow policy learning on heavily loaded systems.

bugs.title: Message router profile is not inheriting the traffic-group from the parent folder
bugs.symptoms: The standby system sends gratuitous ARPs on the standby system for virtual servers configured with message router.
bugs.conditions: This symptom may occur if: -- The message router profile traffic-group is set to default (inherit from folder). -- The message router profile folder is also set to inherit from parent folder. -- A configuration change is made to the virtual server on the non-active unit.
bugs.impact: Traffic is routed to the standby system instead of the active one, causing connections to stall/fail until the neighbor table is updated.
bugs.workaround: Set traffic-group on the message router profile.

bugs.title: Half-closed congested SSL connections with unclean shutdown might stall.
bugs.symptoms: Half-closed congested SSL connections with unclean shutdown might stall.
bugs.conditions: If SSL egress is congested and the client FINs with no Close Notify, connection might stall as SSL does not request more egress data from HTTP.
bugs.impact: Possible stalled flow.
bugs.workaround: Use SSL client that sends clean shutdown.
bugs.fix: Resolved half-closed congested SSL connections with unclean shutdown, so connections no longer stall.

bugs.title: Configuring asymmetric routing with a VE rate limited license will result in tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Configuring asymmetric routing with a VE rate limited license results in tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: Asymmetric routing is configured (i.e., client and/or server ingress and egress travel on different VLANs), and a VE rate limited license is used.
bugs.impact: tmm might continually crash when passing traffic. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use asymmetric routing with a rate limited license.
bugs.fix: The VE rate shaper now works correctly when asymmetric routing is configured, tmm does not crash.

bugs.title: The reference count of NW dos log profile in tmm log is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances when virtual servers are configured with security log profiles, the log message in tmm log is showing incorrect reference cnt to the log profiles.
bugs.conditions: Creation, modification and deletion of many virtual servers with security log profiles attached.
bugs.impact: This may lead to issues such as TMM crash if the reference count is not calculated correctly
bugs.fix: The reference count now is showing correct number in the log message after the fix

bugs.title: Subscriber ID type should be set to NAI over Diameter for DHCP discovered subscribers
bugs.symptoms: CCR-I requests from PEM to PCRF have subscriber ID type set to 6 (UNKNOWN) for DHCP subscribers instead of 3 (NAI).
bugs.conditions: Occurs for DHCP discovered subscribers on a BIG-IP system that uses a PCRF for policy determination.
bugs.impact: Might impact the way policies are provided from the PCRF.
bugs.fix: Subscrbier ID type is marked as NAI for DHCP discovered subscribers.

bugs.title: SIP ALG not compatible with LSN PBA mode
bugs.symptoms: SIP Registrations cease to have incoming traffic delivered after a LSN PBA Block expires.
bugs.conditions: 1. SIP ALG is configured with a LSN pool in PBA mode with a block timeout configured 2. SIP registration requested with a longer expiry than then the remaining PBA lifetime 3. PBA block lifetime expires.
bugs.impact: SIP Registrations created with the associated LSN pool will not have inbound traffic after the PBA block expires.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure the LSN pool being used with SIP ALG into PBA mode with a block timeout; control SIP client behavior with SIP ALG profiles instead of PBA

bugs.title: DHCP: DHCP renew ack messages from server are getting dropped by BIGIP in Forward mode.
bugs.symptoms: When BIGIP is configured in Forwarding mode, renewal ack message from server in response to unicast renewal message from DHCP clients is getting dropped.
bugs.conditions: BIG IP in forwarding mode. DHCP clients sending unicast renewal message to DHCP server
bugs.impact: Unicast DHCP renewal requests are not acked. DHCP clients will send broadcast renewal messages and will be acked by servers.
bugs.workaround: After unable to receive acks from DHCP servers for unicast DHCP renewal messages, DHCP client will send broadcast DHCP renewal messages and will be acked by DHCP server and acks forwarded by BIGIP and received by DHCP clients.
bugs.fix: After being unable to receive ACK responses from DHCP servers for unicast DHCP renewal messages, the DHCP client will send broadcast DHCP renewal messages and receive an ACK from the DHCP server and ACKs forwarded by the BIG-IP system and received by DHCP clients.

bugs.title: Send HOST header in OCSP responder request
bugs.symptoms: HOST header not sent in OCSP responder request. APM OCSP responder object uses HTTP/1.0 to send a request to the OCSP responder and HTTP/1.0 does not have a host header.
bugs.conditions: OCSP configuration
bugs.impact: APM receives an invalid response because the OCSP Server didn't know which site to send the request to due to no HOST header.
bugs.workaround: Create a layer virtual server listening on the IP of the ocsp server and having an irule insert the host header. ltm rule ocsp_insert_http_host { when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::header insert Host <e.g. IP address> } }
bugs.fix: HOST header added in OCSP responder request for HTTP/1.1.

bugs.title: [GTM] [monitor] upgrade issue for monitor backslash '\'
bugs.symptoms: On upgrading to 11.6.1, extra backslashes are added to GTM monitor strings.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when upgrading BIG-IP software from from 11.6.0-HF5 to 11.6.1 with GTM configured.
bugs.impact: Extra backslashes in the monitor string will cause the monitor to fail.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit monitor to remove extra backslash(es) after upgrade.

bugs.title: Greylist (bad actors list) is not cleaned when attack ends
bugs.symptoms: When attack ends the greylist (detected bad actors) remains till the timeout expiration.
bugs.conditions: Detected bad actors and attack end.
bugs.impact: If new attack will start sooner than greylist expiration time, greylist member will be mitigated even if they are not related to the current attack.
bugs.workaround: It it's necessary it's possible to clear greylist manually using ipidr utility.
bugs.fix: Clear the greylist upon attack end.

bugs.title: CGNAT: LSN retries ignored in deterministic mode.
bugs.symptoms: You see CPU spikes on BIG-IP when LSN is enabled an set to deterministic mode with the sys db tm.lsn.retries variable.
bugs.conditions: LSN enabled
bugs.impact: BIG-IP will try all endpoints before failing regardless of the tm.lsn.retries setting.

bugs.title: Fastl4 drops ICMP fragmentation needed messages (no PVA).
bugs.symptoms: The fastl4 profile drops ICMP fragmentation needed messages.
bugs.conditions: Use of fastl4 profile
bugs.impact: Path MTU discovery fails, poor performance.

bugs.title: SIP Parser logging improvements
bugs.symptoms: The SIP parser logging and tracing can be vague and not helpful to field troubleshooting when SIP messages are unable to be parsed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when SIP logs an error due to a malformed or unsupported SIP message to the SIP parser.
bugs.impact: Isolating the specifc issue with a defective SIP message is difficult
bugs.workaround: Do not pass malformed or unsupported SIP messages into the BIGIP.
bugs.fix: Logging of SIP parser message rejection has been improved.

bugs.title: AAA RADIUS system authentication fails on IPv6 network
bugs.symptoms: APM supports RADIUS authentication to IPv6 servers for APM clients if the IPv6 servers are in a pool, but using RADIUS for system authentication directly to a RADIUS server fails on invalid IP address. The signature in the log file is as follows: err apmd[13481]: 01490108:3: /Common/profilename: RADIUS module: authentication with 'aa' failed: Invalid Server IP(0)/Port(0) (1)
bugs.conditions: RADIUS authentication configured for system authentication direct to a RADIUS server, and the RADIUS server is an IPv6 server.
bugs.impact: RADIUS is unable to connect directly to the IPv6 RADIUS server, clients unable to log into the system.

bugs.title: MSSQL health monitors fail when SQL server requires TLSv1.1 or TLSv1.2
bugs.symptoms: MSSQL health monitor always shows down.
bugs.conditions: The Microsoft SQL server that is being monitored has disabled support for legacy security protocols, and supports only versions TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2.
bugs.impact: MSSQL monitor is unable to perform health checking when SQL Server is configured to require TLSv1.1 or TLSv1.2.

bugs.title: Error when deleting multiple ASM Policies
bugs.symptoms: Error when attempting to delete multiple ASM policies at once.
bugs.conditions: Multiple ASM policies are selected for deletion that have multiple XML profiles configured on their URLs.
bugs.impact: Operation fails with ASM subsystem error messages in asm log.
bugs.workaround: Delete policies one at a time.
bugs.fix: Multiple ASM policy delete finishes successfully.

bugs.title: BIG-IP retransmits SYN/ACK on a subflow after an MPTCP connection is closed
bugs.symptoms: If a SYN with MP_JOIN is received on a new subflow during an MPTCP connection and the connection closes before the three-way handshake is complete, the BIG-IP will continue trying to complete the three-way handshake.
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile with Multipath TCP enabled is attached to a virtual server, and a SYN with MP_JOIN is received on another flow during an MPTCP connection.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP retransmits the SYN/ACK to the joining flow after the connection is closed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround
bugs.fix: Free joining connections when an MPTCP connection is closed.

bugs.title: Crash: tmm crashing when 2nd client (srcPort=68) sends a DHCP renew with giaddr (Relay Agent IP) in the packet after 1st client (srcPort=67).
bugs.symptoms: Two client side DHCP packets with giaddr field set, one with source port 67 and another client side packet with source port 68 (not conforming to RFC since giaddr set DHCP packet (from relay agent) should use 67 as source port per RFC), tmm will crash during err message logging.
bugs.conditions: 1) Two client side DHCP packets arrive one after another. 2) Both DHCP packets have giaddr fields set 3) One packet uses 67 as source port, the other uses 68
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: The conditions that cause the crash should not happen in a normal network setup. A DHCP relay agent should only use 67 as source port.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when SSL forward proxy is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when SSL forward proxy is enabled.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when SSL forward proxy is enabled and there is a server handshake done when client SSL handshake is not ongoing.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: SSL forward proxy now ignores server handshake done when client SSL handshake is not ongoing, so an intermittent TMM crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP processes SAML Single logout request/response, tmm cores intermittently.
bugs.symptoms: The tmm process crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system is configured as SAML IdP or SAML SP. -- BIG-IP processes SAML Single Logout Request/Response
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. All APM end users must log back in.

bugs.title: Max number of chunks not configurable above 1000 chunks
bugs.symptoms: If you want to support requests larger than 1000 chunks, the request is blocked and the system posts the following message in the ASM event log: Unparsable request content Chunks number exceeds request chunks limit: 1000.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the request exceeds 1000 chunks.
bugs.impact: Requests that are valid from the server side are being rejected.
bugs.fix: This release adds an internal parameter "request_max_chunks_number" to enable configuring a greater than 1000 max number of chunks. The default value is 1000
bugs.behavior: This release adds an internal parameter "request_max_chunks_number" to enable configuring a greater than 1000 max number of chunks. The default value is 1000

bugs.title: mcpd memory grows when updating firewall rules
bugs.symptoms: While updating firewall rules such as adding/deleting a blacklist, mcpd memory grows by a small amount with each update.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when making changes to firewall policies.
bugs.impact: mcpd memory grows unbounded; over a significant amount of time with many changes and no restarts, mcpd can run out of memory and oom killer can trigger a failover.

bugs.title: Improve details of ajax failure
bugs.symptoms: When AJAX request fails, insufficient information is provided to debug the failure.
bugs.conditions: AJAX failure
bugs.impact: Difficult to diagnose the failure.
bugs.workaround: Not relevant
bugs.fix: Add information to alert about AJAX failure.

bugs.title: mcpd does not properly validate missing 'sys folder' config in bigip_base.conf
bugs.symptoms: If a 'sys folder' is manually removed from bigip_base.conf, and the config is then reloaded, mcpd does not produce any warning or error messages, and allows the config to load.
bugs.conditions: A folder is removed from a previously valid configuration file.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent configuration between devices in the same device-group, shows in-sync when they are not, prevents config loading after mcpd has been reset.
bugs.workaround: Do not remove folders from the configuration file.
bugs.fix: mcpd now properly validates missing 'sys folder' config in bigip_base.conf, so the config performs as expected.

bugs.title: Add the ability to control dropping of alerts by before-load-function
bugs.symptoms: Too many alerts prevents you from enabling FPS. If it does get enabled, a large number of 'missing component' alerts are generated.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when enabling FPS will trigger a high number of alerts.
bugs.impact: FPS is disabled, or alerts are not categorized.
bugs.fix: Add before-load-function capability to drop alert on client.

bugs.title: Occasionally the logging system prints out a blank message: err mcpd[19114]: 01070711:3:
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the logging system prints out a blank message, similar to the following example: -- err mcpd[19114]: 01070711:3: For this log statement, there is text associated with the error in the bigip_mcpd_error_defs.in file, so something should be logged.
bugs.conditions: The problem is the result of an exception handler issue in mcpd's File Object validator. The damaged logs can come from anywhere in mcpd, but appear only after a File Object configuration change fails validation. If the problem occurs, it will happen only once per validation error. The damage caused by the exception handler is automatically corrected when the system rewrites the log.
bugs.impact: Except for the missing log text, the state and behavior of the BIG-IP system is unaffected.
bugs.workaround: None. The problem corrects automatically when the system rewrites the log.
bugs.fix: The logging system prints out a blank message in response to failed file object configuration change validations.

bugs.title: TMM or MCP might core while getting connections via iControl.
bugs.symptoms: When getting the connections list over iControl using System.Connections.get_list(), TMM or MCP cores or exits.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl to view all connections, and there is a very large number of connections (1 million or more) in the list.
bugs.impact: TMM or MCP may core or exit. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Debug TMM produces core when an MPTCP connection times out while a subflow is trying to join
bugs.symptoms: If an MPTCP connection times out while a subflow is still performing the three-way handshake, the TMM produces a core. This only affects the debug TMM, not the default one.
bugs.conditions: An MPTCP connection times out while a subflow is still performing the three-way handshake with MP_JOIN. This only affects the debug TMM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable MPTCP.
bugs.fix: Remove unestablished joining subflows when freeing the MPTCP connection structure.

bugs.title: Hotfix installation failure using certain version 11.x software to host incremental hotfix application of version 12.x software.
bugs.symptoms: Hotfix installation fails using certain version 11.x software to host incremental hotfix application of version 12.x software.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Active software is v11.x. -- Target software is v12.x. -- This is the first attempt install a hotfix to the installation target.
bugs.impact: Cannot install hotfix.
bugs.workaround: Delete the target location, and perform the hotfix installation again. Subsequent attempts to install the hotfix will automatically install the base release first, which includes the needed DB hash type, and the hotfix will succeed.

bugs.title: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records leaks memory
bugs.symptoms: A small memory leak is detected when running the following command: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records.
bugs.impact: The memory leak is small, however if the command is run constantly the memory growth can become large.
bugs.fix: tmsh show ltm persistence persist-records no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: Unsupported DDM F5 SFP modules do not write log message saying DDM is not supported
bugs.symptoms: QSFP modules that do not support DDM (Digital Diagnostic Monitoring), write messages to /var/log/ltm indicating DDM is not supported, however, there are certain unsupported DDM F5-branded SFP modules that do not write a message to the log.
bugs.conditions: Upon inserting the unsupported DDM SFP modules.
bugs.impact: DDM is not reporting information for the following optics: Unsupported DDM 1Gb-10GB SFP modules: OPT-0004 OPT-0007 OPT-0011 OPT-0015 OPT-0051 OPT-0033
bugs.fix: All DDM SFP 1Gb-10GB modules now log in /var/log/ltm that DDM is not supported with that optical transceiver.

bugs.title: SIP Parser incorrectly parsers empty header
bugs.symptoms: If a SIP message contains an empty header, the following header will be included as the value of the empty header.
bugs.conditions: A SIP header without any value will incorrectly cause the next header to be used as the value.
bugs.impact: If the following header is needed for processing the message, it will not be seen (since it is incorrectly considered the value of the previous header).
bugs.fix: Parser has been corrected to terminate an empty header when a line ending is seen.

bugs.title: IPsec tmm devbuf memory leak.
bugs.symptoms: A small memory leak was discovered during internal testing of IPsec tunnels. Over time tmm might run out of memory and crash.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: When upgrading from v10.2.4 to v11.5.x or v11.6.x, with fallback set to null in a wideip pool, the new pool will have fallback-ipv4 set to any6.
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from v10.2.4 to v11.5.x or v11.6.x, with fallback set to null in a wideip pool, the new pool will have fallback-ipv4 set to any6.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from v10.2.4 to v11.5.x or v11.6.x. -- Fallback set to null in a wideip pool.
bugs.impact: The fallback-ipv4 is incorrectly set to an IPv6 address rather than an IPv4 address.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to set Fallback to a different value before upgrading, and then set back after upgrade is complete.

bugs.title: Improved diagnostics in BD config update (bd_agent) added
bugs.symptoms: Improved diagnostics in BD config update (bd_agent) are needed.
bugs.conditions: Further troubleshooting of BD config update transmission is needed.
bugs.impact: No diagnostics are available.
bugs.fix: Improved diagnostics in BD config update (bd_agent) were added.

bugs.title: Compiled signature collections use more memory than prior versions
bugs.symptoms: Compiled signature collections use more memory than prior versions.
bugs.conditions: Different signature sets are used for different policies.
bugs.impact: BD memory usage for compiled signature collections is increased.
bugs.fix: Compiled signature collections memory usage was consolidated and reduced.

bugs.title: DNS cache local zone not properly copying recursion desired (RD) flag in response
bugs.symptoms: When a DNS query sets the RD flag, that setting is supposed to be copied to the response. When a DNS query is handled by a cache local zone, the RD flag is not set properly.
bugs.conditions: A DNS cache local zone must be configured and a DNS query with the RD flag set must be handled by this local zone.
bugs.impact: The flag is not set properly in the DNS response. This most likely will only be noticed by protocol validation tools as standard DNS clients generally do not check this bit.
bugs.workaround: Use an equivalent DNS Express configuration instead of the local zone.
bugs.fix: The fix is to properly check the RD flag on the query so that it can be copied to the response.

bugs.title: BIG-IP drops ACKs containing no max-forwards header
bugs.symptoms: When a sip profile is in use and receives an acknowledgment packet missing the Max-Forwards header, BIG-IP will treat the packet as un-forwardable and does not forward the ACK. This can be experienced as a specific cilent being unable to make a call.
bugs.conditions: This would only be seen when BIG-IP is connected to specific clients that fail to populate the Max-Forwards header on an ACK.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP treats packets with the missing header as having a value of 0, which means "Do not forward".

bugs.title: TMM crash, Invalid action
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and restarts. Before the crash, you may see this signature in /var/log/ltm: tmm1[21502]: 011f0007:3: http_process_state_prepend - Invalid action:0x109040.
bugs.conditions: This intermittent issue may be seen if you have an iRule that performs HTTP::disable, and there are network issues between the BIG-IP system and the pool members.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Yafuflash 4.25 for iSeries appliances
bugs.symptoms: Firmware on BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx needs to be upgraded to Yafuflash 4.25.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx. -- Yafuflash.
bugs.impact: This is a firmware upgrade.
bugs.fix: This release contains Yafuflash v4.25 for BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx.
bugs.behavior: This release contains Yafuflash v4.25 for BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx.

bugs.title: Portal Access: RSS XML files may contain non-rewritten URLs
bugs.symptoms: Some URLs in RSS XML files may not be rewritten if the file uses additional XML namespaces.
bugs.conditions: In the following example the content of <link> tag is not rewritten by Portal Access: <rss xmlns:a10="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" version="2.0"> <channel> <a10:author> author </a10:author> <link> http://domain.com </link>
bugs.impact: RSS pages may contain direct links if accessed via Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to replace non-rewritten URLs with rewritten ones.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access rewrites all necessary URLs in RSS XML pages with additional namespaces.

bugs.title: CLIENTSSL_SERVERHELLO_SEND event in SSL forward proxy is not raised when client reuses session
bugs.symptoms: When a client performs an abbreviated handshake by reusing the session from a previously established full handshake, the SSL forward proxy does not raise the CLIENTSSL_SERVERHELLO_SEND event.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- SSL forward proxy configured -- Session cache is enabled.
bugs.impact: iRule commands inside of the CLIENTSSL_SERVERHELLO_SEND are only executed for full handshakes but not for abbreviated handshakes; thus any logic that's applied per SSL connection should not run inside of CLIENTSSL_SERVERHELLO_SEND event since it is not reliably raised under all types of handshakes.
bugs.workaround: To make sure that the CLIENTSSL_SERVERHELLO_SEND event is reliably raised, disable session cache in the client SSL profile.

bugs.title: machine certificate check creates issuer string with DC with reverse order
bugs.symptoms: Machine certificate check on MAC creates issuer string with incorrect domain component (DC) order if it has any domain component in the certificate. For example, if DC in certificate says f5net.com, issuer DC string should look like "DC=f5net, DC=com" but instead, it's in reverse order (DC="com", DC="f5net").
bugs.conditions: Machine certificate check configured on BIG-IP systems, certificate contains DC components.
bugs.impact: Machine certificate check might fail.
bugs.workaround: For access policies with machine certificate check targeted towards MAC, the order of DC should be reversed (compared to access policy with machine certificate check targeted towards Microsoft Windows) in the regex configured in machine certificate check.
bugs.fix: DC order evaluated by MAC is correctly ordered now and matches with that of Microsoft Windows.
bugs.behavior: Previously, machine certificate check on MAC creates issuer string with incorrect domain component (DC) order if it has any domain component in the certificate. For example, if DC in certificate says f5net.com, issuer DC string should look like "DC=f5net, DC=com" but instead, it's in reverse order (DC="com", DC="f5net"). Now, DC order evaluated by MAC is correctly ordered now and matches with that of Microsoft Windows.

bugs.title: Dossier warning 14
bugs.symptoms: After each boot, the var/log/ltm log file contains messages similar to the following: warning mcpd[6296]: 01070267:4: Dossier warning 14.
bugs.conditions: This occurs upon reboot after licensing and management port configuration is complete on i5000/i7000/i10000-Series platforms.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. This is a benign message that can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: The var/log/ltm log file no longer contains the benign messages similar to the following: warning mcpd[6296]: 01070267:4: Dossier warning 14.

bugs.title: Error message on WSDL schema validation
bugs.symptoms: On upload, invalid WSDL schema validation file error message does not indicate the specific error in WSDL schema.
bugs.conditions: Upload invalid WSDL file.
bugs.impact: The system posts a vague error message: Validation failed. An error has occurred while processing the schema or WSDL document. (Can't use an undefined value as a SCALAR reference). In this case, the error message should similar to the following: Validation failed. An error has occurred while processing the schema or WSDL document. (Element ServerVersionInfo in namespace "http://schemas.microsoft.com/exchange/2010/Autodiscover" is not defined).
bugs.fix: The WSDL schema validation file error message now indicates the specific error in the WSDL schema.

bugs.title: Tilde character does not work on GET requests via iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: When issuing an iControl REST GET request to a URL that contains a tilde (~), for example when specifying a folder, the REST call will return an error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when performing an iControl REST GET request to any URL that contains contains a tilde character in the path name.
bugs.impact: iControl REST will respond with an error.

bugs.title: PCP may pick an endpoint outside the deterministic mapping
bugs.symptoms: When PCP is picking an endpoint for a LSN pool in deterministic mode and the initial pick fails due to an existing mapping, the subsequent picks are from the entire LSN pool translation port range. This may result in a mapping that violates the deterministic mapping algorithm.
bugs.conditions: With PCP configured and enabled with a lsn-pool in deterministic mode.
bugs.impact: Deterministic mapping restriction may be violated causing reverse mapping of public IP address to private IP address to not identify the correct subscriber.
bugs.workaround: Configure PCP with a NAPT pool (such as the DNAT mode's backup pool) and enable logging. Do not use an lsn-pool in deterministic mode.
bugs.fix: PCP no longer picks mappings outside of a client's DNAT range after the first mapping attempt fails.

bugs.title: HTTP header modify agent logs error message as it is disabled since it cannot modify headers/cookies in HTTP Response.
bugs.symptoms: HTTP Header Modify agent skips execution if it believes it is in the serverside chain, as the check is based on receipt of HUDEVT_REQ_DONE, which can be true on the clientside chain, causing HTTP header modify agent operations to log out with an error message.
bugs.conditions: Receipt of HUDEVT_REQ_DONE before execution of HTTP Header Modify agent.
bugs.impact: HTTP header modify agent cannot perform modification of headers/cookies.
bugs.fix: Appropriate check for disabling HTTP header agent only in serverside chain has been added and the check for the receipt of request has been processed has been removed.

bugs.title: Bad ACK Flood is not detected by AFM when loose-init is enabled on the virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When loose-init is set, which has the implicit semantics of "every ACK packet can create a connection". Hence, there is never a "Bad ACK" to drop. This behavior is expected as per design, so while enabling this option one should aware of the side effects it will cause.
bugs.conditions: This issue will be seen when loose-init is enabled on the fastL4 profile and when the box is flooded with asymmetric ACK packets (or) Bad-Acks.
bugs.impact: Enabling loose initiation may make it more vulnerable to denial of service attacks.
bugs.workaround: When loose-init is set in the fastL4 profile, also turn on connection-limits on the virtual and also Eviction Policy to prevent flow-table exhaustion.

bugs.title: Adding info about delete first 10000 out of XXX instead of showing alert
bugs.symptoms: When deleting requests by filter, delete is limited by 10K requests. Pop-up alert window is shown to explain this to user.
bugs.conditions: User tries to delete more than 10K requests by filter.
bugs.impact: Pop-up alert is shown, requiring user to click OK to continue.
bugs.workaround: Just click OK in alert window.
bugs.fix: Pop-up message eliminated, 10K limit explained in the action button itself.

bugs.title: qkview missing some HugePage memory data
bugs.symptoms: Some HugePage status data is missing from qkview, if the contents of /proc/meminfo does not list a units column for the Huge Page data.
bugs.conditions: /proc/meminfo file does not list units for HugePage data.
bugs.impact: HugePage data is missing from qkview diagnostics file.
bugs.workaround: Separately provide /proc/meminfo file.
bugs.fix: HugePage status data is now collected as expected.

bugs.title: Device Connectivity tabs not properly highlighted
bugs.symptoms: The Failover Network and Mirroring tabs in Device Connectivity aren't properly highlighted.
bugs.conditions: Clicking on "System :: High Availability :: Device Connectivity :: Failover Network" menu option and the "System :: High Availability :: Device Connectivity :: Mirroring" menu option.
bugs.impact: Displays the "Device Management :: Devices :: [device name]" page but doesn't highlight the tab. Highlighting works for ConfigSync tab only. "Failover Network and Mirroring" should be highlighted as well.
bugs.fix: The Failover Network and Mirroring tabs in Device Connectivity are now highlighted as expected.

bugs.title: Access Policy Manager CRL cache is locked out for CRLDP authentication
bugs.symptoms: A page protected by an Access Policy cannot be displayed after submitting credentials. Internally, on the BIG-IP device, apmd CPU utilization becomes very high.
bugs.conditions: 1. Access policy uses CRLDP authentication. 2. Cached CRL file(s) are expired.
bugs.impact: Unable to log on due to CRL cache lockout.
