When run in push mode (now the default), it is more efficient with the SASP protocol, only asking for changes from GWM, and pinging GWM infrequently if no traffic has been received. The improved monitor uses Pool name rather than Monitor name as the Workload name. This allows a single Monitor definition to be shared among many Pools, where previously a single unique Monitor was required for each SASP Pool.

bugs.title: Half-Open TCP Connections Not Discoverable
bugs.symptoms: New TCP connection requests are reset after a specific sequence of TCP packets.
bugs.conditions: A TCP connection in half-open state.
bugs.impact: Half-open TCP connections are not discoverable
bugs.fix: Properly acknowledge half-open TCP connections.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Access may be denied to users with Application Editor role when accessing SAML Authentication Context UI page
bugs.symptoms: When accessing the SAML Authentication Context UI page with application editor user role, the following error will be displayed: Read Access Denied: user (username) type (SAML authentication context classes list)
bugs.conditions: User attempting to view the page belongs to application editor group/role
bugs.impact: SAML Authentication Context UI page will not display existing objects
bugs.workaround: SAML Authentication Context UI page will still show existing object for users with administrative role.
bugs.fix: With the fix, no errors will be shown to users with Application Editor role when accessing SAML Authentication Context UI page

bugs.title: Invalid XML Policy Exported for Policies with Metachar Overrides on Websocket URLs
bugs.symptoms: Exported Policy in XML format cannot be imported.
bugs.conditions: Metacharacter overrides are defined on a Websocket URL in the policy.
bugs.impact: Exported XML policies cannot be imported back into the system without manual manipulation
bugs.workaround: If such a policy has already been exported only manual manipulation would allow it to be imported again.
bugs.fix: Policy export now correctly creates valid XML Policies for configurations with metachar overrides configured on Websocket URLs.

bugs.title: Memory leak in ospfd when distribute-list is used
bugs.symptoms: Memory might be leaked when a distribute-list is used to filter routes between OSPFv2 and the Routing Information Base (RIB). The leak may lead to a the daemon being terminated via the oom-killer.
bugs.conditions: OSPFv2 in use with a distribute-list, and Link State Advertisements (LSAs) in the database whose prefixes will be filtered by the distribute-list.
bugs.impact: ospfd may leak memory until the system terminates the process via the oom-killer.
bugs.workaround: Position the BIG-IP system in the network so there are no LSAs that need to be filtered using a distribute-list, such as in a stub area.
bugs.fix: ospfd no longer leaks memory when a distribute-list is configured.

bugs.title: Unable to assign wildcard wide IPs to various BIG-IP DNS objects.
bugs.symptoms: Assigning a wide IP with wildcard characters in the name to a DHS distributed application may not work properly when done via tmsh, and such configurations created via the GUI will result in configuration files that fail to load.
bugs.conditions: A wide IP with a wildcard character in its name.
bugs.impact: Unable to assign wide IP to BIG-IP DNS distributed-app.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue preventing wide IPs to be assigned to BIG-IP DNS distributed apps if those wide IPs have a wildcard character in their name.

bugs.title: Non-common browsers blocked by Proactive Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: Some non-common browsers may get blocked by the Proactive Bot Defense feature. This has been seen in rare cases, and causes these browsers to remain in a white page while the request is not being sent to the back-end server.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense enable on the DoS profile.
bugs.impact: In rare cases, some non-common browsers may get blocked.
bugs.fix: Non-common browsers no longer get blocked when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.

bugs.title: IKEv1 racoon daemon delayed timer use of ike-peer (rmconf) after deletion
bugs.symptoms: The IKEv1 racoon daemon can crash and restart when a v1 ike-peer is removed entirely from the config, or simply changed from v1 to v2.
bugs.conditions: When you remove an ike-peer whose version is v1, including any change from version v1 to v2 (since this has the effect of changing who handles that peer from the racoon daemon to tmm).
bugs.impact: IKEv1 racoon daemon restart that causes tunnel outage until re-established by future traffic.
bugs.fix: Validity of a v1 ike-peer inside the racoon daemon is more carefully checked. This release also prevents stale references from old security associations when a peer is removed. Note: A peer can be removed by complete erasure, or by changing the version to v2 so the IKEv1 racoon daemon no longer handles it.

bugs.title: Some SSL certificate SHA verification fails for different SHA prefix used by crypto codec.
bugs.symptoms: For PKCS#1, the SHA256 header should be: 30 31 30 0d 06 09 60 86 48 01 65 03 04 02 01 05 00 04 20. However, there might also be this alternate header: 30 2f 30 0b 06 09 60 86 48 01 65 03 04 02 01 04 20, Some implementation use the alternate. According to PKCS#1, the first one is used when producing signature, but both should be accepted when verifying signatures. In BIG-IP, SSL uses the 1st header: 30 31 30 0d 06 09 60 86 48 01 65 03 04 02 01 05 00 04 20, whereas crypto uses the 2nd header format for some cert verification: 30 2f 30 0b 06 09 60 86 48 01 65 03 04 02 01 04 20, which causes the inconsistent and signature verification fail.
bugs.conditions: For some particular certificates, crypto uses alternative SHA prefix for verification.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake fails because of certificate verification failure.
bugs.fix: Added crypto codec support for PKCS 1 RSA padding that adds hash DER encoding.

bugs.title: 2000/4000 platform reuses source port too fast when fastL4 virtual sets source-port preserve
bugs.symptoms: 2000/4000 platforms only support IPPORT hash due to the hardware nature of the platform. That means the source port has to change even if fastL4 virtual sets source-port preserve. A software defect causes fast source port reuse when fastL4 virtual sets source-port preserve.
bugs.conditions: fastL4 virtual sets source-port preserve.
bugs.impact: Can cause throughput degradation.
bugs.workaround: Set source-port to change.
bugs.fix: 2000/4000 platform now reuses source port at the correct rate when fastL4 virtual sets source-port preserve.

bugs.title: Add iRule support for no-padding RSA encryption
bugs.symptoms: There is no support for no-padding RSA encryption.
bugs.conditions: When CRYPTO::encrypt iRule is used.
bugs.impact: No option for no padding.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release adds a new option RSA_NO_PADDING to iRule CRYPTO. Note: RSA_NO_PADDING has weaker security. You should use it only if your implementation requires it.

bugs.title: TMM crash when call HTTP::respond twice in LB_FAILED
bugs.symptoms: TMM core-dumps when these conditions are met: - LB_FAILED event - irule script must use a "delay" (parked) statement together with two HTTP::respond statements.
bugs.conditions: - LB_FAILED event must be triggered by good IP address and bad port so that the serverside connflow is establish. you will not see this bug if no pool member is used or invalid IP address is used. - irule script must use a "delay" (parked) statement. the delay together with http response creates the right timing for the client side connflow to go away while proxy is pushing Abort event down to both clientside and serverside.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This fix rectifies the problem.

bugs.title: tmm core while running the iRule STATS:: command
bugs.symptoms: With an iRule that runs the STATS::set command inside the ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED event, tmm cores.
bugs.conditions: STATS:: command invoked inside the ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED event. This event does not have all of the connection information so invoking STATS:: to store data from the connection will fail and cause tmm to crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use STATS::set inside ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED

bugs.title: tmm core while running the iRule STATS:: command
bugs.symptoms: With an iRule that runs the STATS::set command inside the ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED event, tmm cores.
bugs.conditions: STATS:: command invoked inside the ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED event. This event does not have all of the connection information so invoking STATS:: to store data from the connection will fail and cause tmm to crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use STATS::set inside ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED

bugs.title: Snapshots may be kept longer than expected in the file store
bugs.symptoms: Files in /config/filestore/.snapshots_d may be kept longer than expected. This error message may be generated by mcpd later on: 01071350:3: subscriber(%icr_eventd): Snapshot for req_id(12345) getting removed due to timeout.
bugs.conditions: These will be generated on any creation of file objects, such as iFile objects, SSL keys, or certificates.
bugs.impact: A slight amount of additional disk space may be used. The error message may be ignored; it does not indicate a harmful state. Traffic is not at risk of being dropped.
bugs.workaround: A timer will automatically clean up these files after one hour. Alternately, run 'bigstart restart icr_eventd'.

bugs.title: QOS load balancing links display as gray
bugs.symptoms: All links in all data centers appear gray. After this patch all link appear to be green and the functional of load balancing to the first available link in each pool is restored.
bugs.conditions: This bug only affects devices licensed after 9/1/2016 which contain the gtm_lc: disabled field.
bugs.impact: Any GTM/LC devices licensed after 9/1/2016 and using links as part of their configuration will have the links reported as gray.
bugs.workaround: Remove all ilnks from configuration or install this hotfix.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of form that contains a tag with id=action
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, a form with an absolute path in the action is handled incorrectly in Internet Explorer (IE) versions 7, 8, and 9. The resulting action path is wrong and the form cannot be submitted.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under these conditions: -- HTML Form with absolute action path. -- A tag with id=action inside this form. -- A submit button in the form. -- IE versions 7 through 9.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue is that the web application can not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: This issue has no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Forms with absolute action paths and tag with id=action inside are handled correctly.

bugs.title: The TMM crashes in the websso plugin.
bugs.symptoms: The TMM core and plugins operate asynchronously. A connection may abort and the TMM may deallocate connection context before the plugin has finished processing asynchronous events. The TMM crashes when a plugin accesses deallocated connection context.
bugs.conditions: Events raised during normal use of the sessiondb store may be processed after the connection context has been deallocated.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM will no longer crash.

bugs.title: Error in the Console, when configured nonexistent parameter with Encryption and Obfuscation
bugs.symptoms: Wrong handling of nonexistent parameter configured with Encryption and Obfuscation
bugs.conditions: nonexistent parameter configured with Encryption and Obfuscation
bugs.impact: Error in console
bugs.fix: Ignore nonsexist parameter

bugs.title: Pool members may not be marked up and/or there might be a slight delay in monitors
bugs.symptoms: A UDP monitor might fail to mark a pool member up even when the pool member is up. Other monitor types may mark a pool member down. A slight delay (less than 0.1 seconds) might be noticed in monitor traffic sent by the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: To experience the incorrect pool member status issue, there is generally some other monitor on the system that is legitimately down. To experience the delay, run an affected version. The issue has been observed with TCP, HTTP, and HTTPS monitors.
bugs.impact: Incorrect pool member status or pool member flapping. Connections to monitored pool members might last slightly longer than necessary.
bugs.fix: In this release, the system now correctly sets pool member status and connections to monitored pool members no longer last longer than necessary.

bugs.title: Import/Activate Security policy with 'Replace policy associated with virtual server' option fails
bugs.symptoms: Visible errors in the BIG-IP Configuration utility: -- MCP Validation error - 01071abb:3: Cannot create/modify published policy '/Common/<ltm_policy_name>' directly, try specifying a draft folder like '/Common/Drafts/<ltm_policy_name>'. -- MCP Validation error - 01071726:3: Cannot deactivate policy action '/Common/<asm_policy_name>'. It is in use by ltm policy '/Common/<asm_policy_name>'.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Having an active Security policy 'A' assigned to an LTM L7 Policy 'L'. -- Import/Activate Security policy 'B' with the option 'Replace policy associated with virtual server' enabled, to replace security policy 'A'.
bugs.impact: Security Policy is activated but not assigned to the LTM policy.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command prior to the Import/Activate of a Security policy action: --------- # tmsh modify ltm policy L legacy ---------
bugs.fix: The process of importing/activating a Security policy now correctly replaces an existing policy, when the option 'Replace policy associated with virtual server' is enabled.

bugs.title: Creating 0.0.0.0:0 Virtual Server in TMUI results in slow-loading virtual server page and name resolution errors.
bugs.symptoms: Creating 0.0.0.0:0 Virtual Server in TMUI results in slow-loading virtual server page and name resolution errors.
bugs.conditions: When a virtual server with a destination address of 0.0.0.0:0 is in the list, sorting the list is slow because of extra name resolution performed.
bugs.impact: Degraded user experience waiting for the extra logic and misleading error in logs.
bugs.fix: Creating 0.0.0.0:0 Virtual Server in TMUI no longer results in slow-loading virtual server page and name resolution errors.

bugs.title: List GTM pools and wideips in a partition may result in objects from all partitions
bugs.symptoms: Listing GTM pools or wideips from the GUI, tmsh, iControl in a particular partition may return objects from all partitions.
bugs.conditions: GTM provisioned, multiple partitions configured, and GTM pools or wide IPs configuration in multiple partitions.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP users may be able to view objects that are in partitions they don't have access to.
bugs.workaround: No workaround other than don't use multiple partitions.
bugs.fix: This was an issue unique to GTM pools and wide IPs that resulted in the wrong set of objects being returned despite the partition context being given. The issue has been corrected, so that only valid objects are displayed for different users in different partitions.

bugs.title: DNS Resource Records for Wide-IPs are potentially missing when creating a large number of Wide-IPs
bugs.symptoms: When a Wide-IP is created, or a pool member is added/removed from a pool associated with the wideip, updates are sent to the on-box BIND to create/update/delete the matching resource records. Some of these updates could possibly be lost if there are a large number of changes happening rapidly.
bugs.conditions: If the BIG-IP is a member of a DNS/GTM sync-group and "synchronize-zone-files" is enabled.
bugs.impact: Not every wideip will have the appropriate resource records in bind. If the BIG-IP is functioning normally and answering DNS queries, then this is not a problem. If GTM is down but the on-box bind is still functioning, BIND could have answered DNS queries for the wideip. This situation could also come up right after the BIG-IP has rebooted where GTM is not fully initialized, but BIND is up.
bugs.workaround: There are some options: 1) Delete and recreate any affected wideips. Alternatively remove and re-add the pool members. 2) To avoid this condition if you know you will be adding many wideips, you could stop csyncd before and renable right after. "bigstart stop csyncd", create wips, "bigstart start csyncd".
bugs.fix: Eliminate race condition with creating BIND resource records when creating many Wide-IPs.
bugs.behavior: 1) Changes made directly to the BIND zone files in /var/named/config/namedb/ will not be automatically reloaded. The recommended steps provided by ISC for bind with dynamic zones should be used to freeze/thaw the zone to prevent conflicts. For example: a. Run 'rndc freeze example.com.' b. <edit the zone file in /var/named/config/namedb making sure to increment the zone serial number> c. Run 'rndc thaw example.com.' Note that BIND will reject dynamic updates while the zone is frozen so the zone should be left frozen only for the shortest amount of time possible. Resource records created by the BIG-IP for Wide-ips or using ZoneRunner will be refused and lost if the zone is frozen. 2) Changes made to /var/named/config/named.conf will not be reloaded automatically if DNS(GTM) is not provisioned. The 'rndc reconfig' or 'rndc reload' command should be used to load any changes made to the named.conf file.

bugs.title: Error message in ltm log when adding a DoS profile to virtual server in cluster setup
bugs.symptoms: In a cluster environment, when adding DoS profile to a virtual server, ltm log shows a configuration exception error message complaining about a file missing.
bugs.conditions: -- The setup is a cluster. -- DoS profile is created and attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but unnecessary error message is seen in ltm log.
bugs.fix: Unnecessary error message no longer occurs.

bugs.title: iApp may fail to install if AFM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: When you try to deploy the f5.microsoft_sharepoint_2016.v1.0.0rc1 iApp from the GUI, the install may fail when AFM is provisioned. A similar error occurs when deploying f5.http iApp. The failure to deploy might not be related to a specific iApp.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM provisioned. -- Using the GUI to deploy the iApp, f5.microsoft_sharepoint_2016.v1.0.0rc1, f5.http, and others.
bugs.impact: Deployment fails.

bugs.title: SSID filter may cause excessive buffering and high CPU
bugs.symptoms: CPU usage increases with excessive buffering of significant amount of data.
bugs.conditions: High CPU with huge amount of data buffered up, and SSL persistence is in use.
bugs.impact: Can slow down the system.

bugs.title: Source Address Translation to SNAT pool breaks SWG explicit use case for IP based session.
bugs.symptoms: All SWG session maps to SNAT pool IP and many requests will get stuck.
bugs.conditions: SWG virtual with Source Address Translation to SNAT pool, create session and send traffic for expired session
bugs.impact: Request will get stuck in ACCESS filter and browser will keep looping..
bugs.workaround: Change source address translation to AUTOMAP instead of SNAT Pool.
bugs.fix: Store client IP into scratch memory and use it to session lookup/creation instead of SNAT Pool IP.

bugs.title: HTTP Explicit proxy defect resolution
bugs.symptoms: Internal F5 code reviewed found potential errors.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with HTTP Explicit proxy.
bugs.impact: Erroneous behavior of HTTP Explicit proxy
bugs.fix: Resolved issues found in HTTP Explicit proxy.

bugs.title: SOCKS proxy defect resolution
bugs.symptoms: Internal F5 code review found potential errors.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with SOCKS proxy.
bugs.impact: Erroneous behavior of SOCKS proxy
bugs.fix: Resolved issues found in SOCKS proxy.

bugs.title: ASM is not available in LTM policy when ASM is licensed as the main active module
bugs.symptoms: ASM is not available in LTM policy rule creation when ASM is licensed as the main active module
bugs.conditions: ASM is licensed as the main active module
bugs.impact: ASM is not available in LTM policy rule creation
bugs.workaround: Use a license that has ASM as a sub-module. For example, LTM with Best Bundle.
bugs.fix: Fixed license data parsing so that the main module is also included in the license map used to determine whether a module is licensed or not.

bugs.title: Performance fix to not reset a data structure in the packet receive hotpath.
bugs.symptoms: No symptoms. This is a performance fix.
bugs.conditions: This will happen always in the packet receive hotpath.
bugs.impact: No impact. Without this fix BIG-IP could have 0.5% (hard to measure) performance impact.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Made an optimization to the packet receive hotpath.

bugs.title: Dynamic routing process ripd may core
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue the dynamic routing protocol daemon ripd, used for the RIP protocol may produce a core file when configuring it to use a interface configured with multiple self IP addresses on different subnets on the same VLAN.
bugs.conditions: - Use the RIP dynamic routing on an affected version. - Have multiple self IP addresses belonging to different subnets on the same VLAN - Add one of the subnets with the network command within the "router RIP" stanza.
bugs.impact: ripd will core and the configuration will not be allowed.
bugs.workaround: Configure one subnet/self IP address per VLAN.
bugs.fix: ripd no longer cores when configured with multiple subnets on the same VLAN.

bugs.title: TMM might crash during handling of RDG-RPC connection when APM is used as RD Gateway
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash during handling of RDG-RPC connection when APM is used as RD Gateway.
bugs.conditions: RDP client uses RDG-RPC protocol to connect via APM's RD Gateway implementation.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed TMM crash, which occurred during RDG-RPC protocol handling.

bugs.title: Linux client NA components cannot be installed neither using sudo password nor root password
bugs.symptoms: Linux client Network Access components cannot be installed neither using sudo password nor root password on firefox browser. Issue occurs because version reported is incorrect and post installation version on the machine still doesn't match with version reported by the server.
bugs.conditions: Firefox web browser, NPAPI plugins, Network Access on Linux distributions
bugs.impact: Installation and update of web browser plugin for network access fails

bugs.title: IPv6 configuration limitations
bugs.symptoms: When an Intel XL710 Ethernet 40 Gb interfaces interface is added to a VLAN, correct configuration procedure requires that all assigned IPv6 self ip addresses be reconfigured on the VLAN.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 self IP addresses. Intel XL710 Ethernet 40 Gb interface.
bugs.impact: Special configuration procedure is required.
bugs.workaround: Follow the defined procedure, by deleting and recreating any IPv6 self IP addresses.
bugs.fix: No special configuration procedures are required to configure the IPv6 self IP addresses for which a VIP is enabled.

bugs.title: Unexpected handling of TCP timestamps in HA configuration
bugs.symptoms: Despite TCP timestamps being configured, the BIG-IP system fails to present timestamp option during TCP negotiation. The BIG-IP system calculates invalid round trip time which might result in delayed retransmission.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: - Virtual server configured with a TCP profile with timestamps enabled. - Virtual server configured with connection mirroring.
bugs.impact: Retransmission timeout (RTO) value may be skewed. Segments that are subject to RTO might take up to 64 segments to retransmit.
bugs.fix: TCP timestamps are negotiated when connection mirroring is enabled.

bugs.title: False Positive for illegal method (GET)
bugs.symptoms: False Positive for illegal method (GET) and errors in BD log on Apply Policy: ---- ECARD|ERR |Sep 04 07:38:47.992|23835|table.h:0287|KEY_REMOVE: Failed to REMOVE data ----
bugs.conditions: This was seen after upgrade and/or failover.
bugs.impact: -- False positives. -- BD has the incorrect security configuration.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command: restart asm.

bugs.title: BGP community lower bytes of zero is not allowed to be set in route-map
bugs.symptoms: The bgpd process does not accept community attributes that contain values of the form ASN:0.
bugs.conditions: set the BGP community value to a value of form ASN:0
bugs.impact: if you attempt to configure a BGP daemon community attribute with a value of the form ASN:0, the system does not set the community value. This could also impact upgrading from the old versions to the version that doesn't support community values of the form ASN:0.
bugs.fix: BGP community can be set to values of the form ASN:0.

bugs.title: BIG-IP reset on ePVA accelerated flow may contain stale TCP window information.
bugs.symptoms: Reset sent by BIG-IP system on ePVA accelerated active flows might contain stale sequence number and ACK number, which might be out of the receiver's valid RST window.
bugs.conditions: For example, server side pool member down events lead to BIG-IP reset of all client flows on the pool member. If these flows are actively offloaded in ePVA with heavy traffic at the time of pool member down and reset sending out time, the SEQ/ACK number for the sending RST by BIG-IP SW might not be recent, and therefore a RST with most SW aware SEQ/ACK will be encoded.
bugs.impact: These RST might be ignored by the receiver if it is out of the valid window. The receiver must rely on the idle or alive timeout to clean this up. Although the receiver must rely on its TCP alive or idle timeout to activate in order to clean up these connections, this is the standard TCP stack behavior.

bugs.title: iRule use of 'all' keyword with 'class match' on large external datagroups may result in TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: When the 'all' keyword is used with 'class match' on large external datagroups, the results will be incorrect and may result in TMM restarting.
bugs.conditions: iRule utilizing 'all' keyword with 'class match' on large external datagroups. A more unusual case is external datagroups with the tmm.classallocatemetadata bigdb entry set to the non-default 'disable' value.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No reasonable workaround short of not using 'all' keyword with 'class match' in iRules.
bugs.fix: 'all' keyword with 'class match' now returns the correct results and TMM does not restart.

bugs.title: Dynamic ECMP routes missing from Linux host
bugs.symptoms: When an ECMP route is learned via dynamic routing, it is not added to the Linux host and local processes may not be able to reach the destination prefix. Load balanced traffic is not affected.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing in use, ECMP configured, ECMP route received from neighbors.
bugs.impact: Monitors may fail, other host-originated traffic may be sent out the wrong interface or nowhere at all.
bugs.workaround: Disable ECMP in ZebOS by setting "maximum-paths 1" in imish.
bugs.fix: ECMP routes are correctly added to the Linux host.

bugs.title: SSL session cache invalidations stat unused in TMM
bugs.symptoms: The statistic `session cache invalidations' is never updated.
bugs.conditions: client-ssl and/or server-ssl profiles are on a virtual
bugs.impact: none. this is only cosmetic.

bugs.title: AVR TPS calculation is inaccurate
bugs.symptoms: The TPS that AVR calculates for DoS is 11% more than the real TPS.
bugs.conditions: DoS profile attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Attack can wrongly be detected.
bugs.fix: TPS that AVR calculates for DoS now reflects the actual TPS.

bugs.title: tmm assert "invalid racoon2 block header prefix"
bugs.symptoms: tmm asserted and cored.
bugs.conditions: IPsec IKEv2 in use.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts and all connections are reset.
bugs.fix: The tmm will continue processing by logging and discarding the invalid memory block.

bugs.title: Raw markup in IPsec docs for ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm on tmsh command line
bugs.symptoms: Code that renders 'man page' docs for display on the tmsh command line appears to sometimes retain the original markup. In particular, the docs for ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm will show aes-gcm128 as 'B<aes-gcm128>' instead of removing the 'B<>' markup. This case seems to be an exception.
bugs.conditions: Docs display via tmsh command line: ...(tmos)# create net ipsec ipsec-policy ipsec-1-2-1 ?
bugs.impact: Extraneous markup characters appear in one displayed entry.

bugs.title: Unable to upload software image larger than 2GB using the GUI
bugs.symptoms: If you attempt to upload a software image at the System :: Software Management : Image List :: New Image screen, the following results may be observed: -- The Progress bar in the GUI never moves from 0%. -- A temporary file is created under /shared/images with a name in the form of: upload_###################.dat. -- The temporary file is never renamed to the correct image file name (as uploaded).
bugs.conditions: This may occur when the size of the software image to be uploaded is larger than 2 GB in size. Note: The BIG-IP v14.1.0 Upgrade ISO is 2.1 GB in size. Other BIG-IP v13.x and v14.x Recovery ISOs may also be larger than 2 GB in size.
bugs.impact: Unable to upload software image via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: 1. Use another method, such as SCP, to copy the BIG-IP software image to the target BIG-IP system. 2. After sufficient time has elapsed to allow the software image upload to complete, manually rename the temporary file under /shared/images to the final file name. Note: It is highly recommended to verify the md5sum of the temporary file to confirm that upload is complete, and that the temporary file is an accurate copy of the original software image uploaded.

bugs.title: GUI or iControl SOAP API call 'LocalLB::ProfileClientSSL::create_v2' creates invalid profile
bugs.symptoms: 1. Using the GUI or an iControl SOAP call can create invalid client SSL profile containing an empty cert-key-chain. This might occur after following these steps: -- Create new client-ssl cert from the GUI (the web-based UI). -- Check 'Custom' in 'Certificate Key Chain', but do not add anything. -- Click Finished. The system creates the following: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/cssl { app-service none cert none cert-key-chain { "" { } defualt_rsa_ckc { <=== a typo "defualt" cert /Common/default.crt key /Common/default.key } } <snip> } 2. Using the iControl function 'LocalLB::ProfileClientSSL::create_v2' creates a profile with two cert-key-chain objects containing identical cert and key values, but with different names: ltm profile client-ssl my_prof { app-service none cert mycert.crt cert-key-chain { "" { cert mycert.crt key mycert.key } defualt_rsa_ckc { <=== a typo "defualt" cert mycert.crt key mycert.key } } chain none inherit-certkeychain false key mycert.key passphrase none }
bugs.conditions: Creating client SSL profiles using the GUI or the iControl function create_v2().
bugs.impact: Cannot add the invalid client SSL profile to a virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Remove the invalid client SSL profile and re-create the profile using TMSH or the GUI.
bugs.fix: GUI or iControl SOAP API call 'LocalLB::ProfileClientSSL::create_v2' no longer creates an invalid profile when creating client SSL profiles using the iControl function create_v2(). In addition, 'defualt' has been changed to 'default', as expected.

bugs.title: Race condition when using SSL Orchestrator can cause TMM to core
bugs.symptoms: When running SSL Forward Proxy in the SSL Orchestrator environment, tmm may crash.
bugs.conditions: This race condition occurs only when running SSL Orchestrator with large numbers of connections.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the race condition so that TMM does not crash.

bugs.title: Session opening log shows incorrect number of challenged responses.
bugs.symptoms: Session opening log shows the incorrect number of challenged response.
bugs.conditions: Session opening is configured to mitigate session opening attack by client-side challenges.
bugs.impact: The log viewed contains incorrect values.
bugs.fix: Fixed a reporting issue with the session opening client-side challenges.

bugs.title: lsusb uses unknown ioctl and spams kernel logs
bugs.symptoms: RHEL6 version of lsusb and associated libusb1 libraries are using an ioctl that isn't properly supported by the kernel in the 32-bit syscall path.
bugs.conditions: RHEL6 version of lsusb and associated libusb1 libraries.
bugs.impact: Spamming of kernel logs.
bugs.fix: kernel.el6.5: fix missing ia32 compat mapping for USBDEVFS_GET_CAPABILITIES.

bugs.title: zxfrd crash due to lack of disk space
bugs.symptoms: It is possible that the zone transfer daemon (zxfrd) can crash if the /var disk partition fills up and zxfrd needs to increase the size of its database.
bugs.conditions: DNS Express configured Full /var partition Changes to the zone database require more space to be allocated for zxfrd.
bugs.impact: zxfrd may crash and restart. This process may repeat depending on the need for space on restart.
bugs.workaround: Free up space in the /var partition.
bugs.fix: zxfrd now correctly handles the out of space condition.

bugs.title: Running qkview with option -c (--complete) fails if there is an encrypted key
bugs.symptoms: When you run qkview -c, you are prompted for a password: Enter pass phrase for ./Common_d/certificate_key_d/:Common:f5_api_com.key_64768_1:
bugs.conditions: An OpenSSL key exists that is encrypted with a passphrase.
bugs.impact: qkview -c cannot be run because /bin/printcertmods requires a valid passphrase to finish.
bugs.workaround: Unless you can enter passphrases from the command line, assuming there are a small number of such keys and the passphrase is available, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The fix simply avoids the issue and skips computing the modulus for any encrypted key.

bugs.title: Overwrite flag in iControl functions key/certificate_import_from_pem functions is ignored and might result in errors.
bugs.symptoms: Overwrite flag in iControl functions key/certificate_import_from_pem functions is ignored and might result in errors. Specifically, the functions are: key_import_from_pem() certificate_import_from_pem() key_import_from_pem_v2() certificate_import_from_pem_v2()
bugs.conditions: When there is an existing key or certificate on the BIG-IP system, and you want to overwrite them using key_import_from_pem(), certificate_import_from_pem(), key_import_from_pem_v2(), or certificate_import_from_pem_v2() iControl calls, it results in errors stating that the key or certificate already exists on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Cannot overwrite the key/certificate file-objects using these iControl calls.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: - Delete and import the key/certificate using key_import_from_pem(), certificate_import_from_pem(), key_import_from_pem_v2(), or certificate_import_from_pem_v2() iControl calls. - Use key_import_from_file and certificate_import_from_file iControl calls as an alternative to import key/certificate from a file.
bugs.fix: Overwrite flag in iControl functions key/certificate_import_from_pem_v2() functions are now processed correctly and no longer produce errors.

bugs.title: large qkview files may not be uploadable to iHealth
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP device has a significantly complex configuration, this may cause the exported XML version of the configuration database to be significantly large, which might not be parsable by the iHealth service.
bugs.conditions: Very large configuration database, or very large core files exist.
bugs.impact: qkview files cannot be uploaded to iHealth diagnostic service.

bugs.title: Routing table doesn't get updated when EDGE client roams among wireless networks
bugs.symptoms: Clients using the EDGE client report that they are unable to reach the VPN when they switch wifi networks.
bugs.conditions: This is triggered when a device running the EDGE client is on a wifi network, then roams to another wifi network that has a different default route.
bugs.impact: Clients have an incorrect route to the VPN and are forced to re-connect.

bugs.title: Incorrect use of HTTP::collect leads to TMM core.
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect use of HTTP::collect leads to TMM hang. Watchdog kills TMM on timeout leading to core.
bugs.conditions: If the iRule requests non-incremental HTTP::collect or amount greater than content-length when the whole-body has already been received, then this leads to TMM hang.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Add an HTTP::release after the HTTP::payload instruction; Or Use incremental HTTP::collect commands.
bugs.fix: HTTP state machine was modified to handle non-incremental collects and condition where whole body has been received when the collect is issued.

bugs.title: Cannot SSH from AOM/SCCP to host without password (host-based authentication).
bugs.symptoms: Issuing commands from the AOM/SCCP menu to the host do not function, or password is required when SSH from AOM/SCCP to the host.
bugs.conditions: Presence of /etc/ssh directory on host.
bugs.impact: AOM/SCCP unable to connect to host without password.
bugs.fix: Can now SSH from AOM/SCCP to host without password (host-based authentication).

bugs.title: VDI plugin-initiated connections may select inappropriate SNAT address
bugs.symptoms: When the VDI plugin makes outgoing connections, the source address is selected from a SNAT pool. Should the connection pass through another matching virtual before reaching the external network, the selected SNAT address may be inappropriate for the egress vlan.
bugs.conditions: APM configuration with VDI functionality enabled and additional virtual matching the VDI-initiated connections.
bugs.impact: Return traffic from destination may not be able to return to the BIG-IP, thus breaking the VDI functionality.
bugs.workaround: No workaround short of removing the additional virtual matching the VDI traffic.
bugs.fix: Outgoing VDI connections now select an appropriate SNAT address even when passing through additional matching virtuals before reaching the external network.

bugs.title: Missing hyperlink to GSLB virtual servers and servers on the pool member page.
bugs.symptoms: Hyperlinks to to GSLB virtual servers and servers on the pool member page were removed in 11.x.
bugs.conditions: Have a GSLB pool with pool members set up.
bugs.impact: Must manually note of the member's virtual or server.
bugs.workaround: Manually take note of virtual or server and search for it.
bugs.fix: Added hyperlink to GSLB virtuals and servers on the pool member page.

bugs.title: GTM configuration fails to load when it has GSLB pool with members containing more than one colon character
bugs.symptoms: The user configuration set (UCS) configuration file may fail to load due to the global server load balancing (GSLB)-referenced virtual server name syntax. The system posts errors similar to the following: 01070226:3: Pool Member 20002 references a nonexistent Virtual Server.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have configured your BIG-IP DNS system (formerly known as BIG-IP GTM) with a virtual server name that includes the colon (:) character. -- The virtual server is included as a GSLB pool member. -- You save the configuration to a UCS file. -- You attempt to load the UCS configuration file.
bugs.impact: Unable to create GTM Pool Member from TMSH, or to load a configuration with this object in it.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue related to parsing of GTM Pool member names that prevents the use of GTM virtual servers or GTM servers with a colon (:) in the name from being used as a GTM pool member.

bugs.title: For the attributes that contain URI value in them, the passwords within the URI are stored in clear-text in the configuration file, audit file, tmsh history file
bugs.symptoms: The URI specification RFC 3986 allows the inclusion of the username and password in the URI string. example: http://username:password@example.com/resource There are a few attributes in the configuration objects that represent a URI example: sys/file/ssl-cert::source-path sys file ssl-cert /Common/dummy { cache-path /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/:Common:dummy_38971_1 revision 1 source-path http://admin:secret@10.154.128.224/dummy.crt } The usage of URI attribute similar to the example of sys/file/ssl-cert::source-path results in the password to be logged in clear-text in various locations. This possess a security risk as the log files could be available to unprivileged users. Currently the URI attributes are visible in the /var/log/audit, /config/<partition>/<folder>/BIG-IP*.conf, /<username>/.tmsh-history-<username> files.
bugs.conditions: Performing CRUD operation on a configuration object that contains a URI attribute. The TMSH, iControl REST interface are used for the CRUD operation. The username, passwords are present in the URI value.
bugs.impact: The clear-text passwords are exposed in the /var/log/audit, /config/<partition>/<folder>/BIG-IP*.conf, /<username>/.tmsh-history-<username> files.
bugs.fix: The passwords contained in URI are sanitized in the /var/log/audit, /<username>/.tmsh-history-<username> files. These are encrypted in the /config/<partition>/<folder>/BIG-IP*.conf file. excerpt from /config/bigip.conf sys file ssl-cert /Common/dummy1.crt { cache-path /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/:Common:dummy1.crt_64358_2 source-path http://:@10.154.128.224/dummy.crt source-path-password $M$mZ$WTgYeTHGVoo81Lw/fLJCBg== source-path-user admin } The password section within the URL field accepts these characters: You can ONLY use the following characters: "a-z", "A-Z", "0-9", "-", ".", "_", "~", "!", "$", "&", "'", "(", ")", "*", "+", ",", ";", "=", ":", percent-encoded for the entire UTF-8 character set.
bugs.behavior: Generally, the source-path attribute in the configuration objects represents URI fields. Pre-change the source-path attribute contained clear-text passwords. This can be seen in the TMSH list action, iControl REST POST/PATCH/PUT API. Post-change the source-path contains sanitized password [****] in the TMSH list, iControl REST API response.

bugs.title: Network Access Launch Application item fails to launch in some cases
bugs.symptoms: If multiple applications are configured to automatically launch on network access, only the first application will launch.
bugs.conditions: Network access resource has multiple applications configured
bugs.impact: Only the first application launches. Other applications won't launch automatically.
bugs.workaround: Launch applications manually after VPN is established.
bugs.fix: Multiple applications are now detected and launched correctly.

bugs.title: out of memory condition when URL categorization is configured to work with large feedlists
bugs.symptoms: out of memory condition when URL categorization is configured to work with large (millions of records) feedlists.
bugs.conditions: In order to hit this issue user would have to load and unload large feedlist multiple times
bugs.impact: SWAP memory will increase and will eventually lead the box to run out of memory
bugs.fix: This problem is fixed in v12.1

bugs.title: bigd crash with Tcl monitors
bugs.symptoms: bigd crashes after logging an error similar to the following: emerg bigd: PID: 38611 Received invalid magic '1213486160' in the stream
bugs.conditions: -- Tcl Monitors: FTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP. -- This issue might also occur if the Tcl worker is in a stuck state, due to pool member not responding within the configured timeout. -- May be particularly likely if the monitor is configured with an interval value of 1 second. Note: Although less frequent, this issue might still occur with proper monitor configurations (timeout: 3*interval + 1).
bugs.impact: bigd crashes and error messages. Possible interruption of monitoring status, pool members going down, interruption of traffic.
bugs.workaround: For the case where a Tcl monitor is configured with a 1-second interval value, increase the interval value to 2 seconds. Also increase the timeout value to 7 seconds (3*interval + 1). This reduces the chances of this issue occurring but does not eliminate it entirely.
bugs.fix: Monitor works as expected under the conditions described.

bugs.title: Special Virtual IP configuration required for IPv6 connectivity on some Virtual Edition interfaces
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 virtual servers may not be reachable on specific Virtual Edition (VE) instances, based on the interfaces used by that instance.
bugs.conditions: VE with IPv6 virtual servers configured. The VE instance must have SR-IOV interfaces, or KVM virtio interfaces backed by macvtap.
bugs.impact: Special configuration procedure is required.
bugs.workaround: Follow the defined configuration procedure by explicitly listing the VLANs for which this VIP is enabled. For example, in TMSH: 'modify ltm virtual <name> vlans-enabled' 'modify ltm virtual <name> vlans add { <vlans> }'

bugs.title: The value returned by "matchregion" in an iRule is inconsistent in some cases.
bugs.symptoms: The value returned by "matchregion" in an iRule is inconsistent when the GTM global setting, "cache-ldns-servers", is set to "yes" and the region contains a region, continent, country, state, or ISP.
bugs.conditions: The GTM global setting, "cache-ldns-servers" must be set to "yes" and the region must contain a region, continent, country, state, or ISP.
bugs.impact: The value returned by "matchregion" in an iRule is inconsistent and may lead to inconsistent behavior in the iRule.
bugs.workaround: Set the GTM global setting, "cache-ldns-servers" to "no".
bugs.fix: "Matchregion" returns the correct value under all conditions.

bugs.title: Occasional TCP resets during connection initiation (RST cause is "No local listener")
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, the BIG-IP will send a TCP RST in response to an initial SYN with the reset cause "No local listener". This does not affect subsequent connections from the client, so they are likely to succeed. The reset cause for a packet can be logged by setting the DB variable TM.rstcause.log to enable. The reset cause can be sent in the RST packet by setting the DB variable TM.rstcause.pkt to enable.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is configured to use TCP and a client initiates a connection.
bugs.impact: The attempted connection is reset. Subsequent attempts are likely to succeed.
bugs.fix: The icr_eventd daemon was updated to use TCP connections more efficiently.

bugs.title: Unexpected rate limiting of unreachable and ICMP messages for some addresses.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system might fail to send RSTs, ICMP unreachable, or ICMP echo responses for some addresses. /var/log/ltm might contain messages similar to the following: -- Limiting icmp unreach response from 251 to 250 packets/sec. -- Limiting icmp ping response from 251 to 250 packets/sec. -- Limiting closed port RST response from 251 to 250 packets/sec.
bugs.conditions: Certain traffic patterns to addresses in two or more different traffic-groups.
bugs.impact: Certain response messages from addresses in one or more traffic-groups (but not all) might be rate limited by the BIG-IP system even though the level of traffic has not exceeded the tm.maxrejectrate setting.
bugs.workaround: None known.
bugs.fix: The rate limiting messages in the ltm log will now include the name of the traffic group that is being rate limited. Example old log message: warning tmm[6167]: 011e0001:4: Limiting icmp ping response from 251 to 250 packets/sec. Example new log message: warning tmm[19109]: 011e0001:4: Limiting icmp ping response from 251 to 250 packets/sec for traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1.
bugs.behavior: The rate limiting messages in the ltm log will now include the name of the traffic group that is being rate limited. Example old log message: warning tmm[6167]: 011e0001:4: Limiting icmp ping response from 251 to 250 packets/sec. Example new log message: warning tmm[19109]: 011e0001:4: Limiting icmp ping response from 251 to 250 packets/sec for traffic group /Common/traffic-group-1.

bugs.title: L7 policies using normalized HTTP URI or Referrer operands may corrupt memory
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart when using a L7 policy that contains the 'normalized' keyword for HTTP URI or Referrer operands.
bugs.conditions: Normalized HTTP URI or Referrer operands used in L7 policies.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround short of removing use of normalization for HTTP URI and Referrer instances in L7 policies.
bugs.fix: Use of URI or Referrer normalization in L7 policies no longer results in memory corruption.

bugs.title: EAM core during shutdown
bugs.symptoms: During a graceful system shutdown, a core file eam.bld1.0.1447.core.gz may be created in /var/core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently during normal shutdown when Oracle Access Manager is configured.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to system operation, since this occurs on shutdown.
bugs.workaround: No workaround needed. There is no impact to system operation, since this occurs on shutdown.
bugs.fix: EAM no longer cores during shutdown.

bugs.title: Multiple TFTP data transfers cannot be initiated in a single session
bugs.symptoms: Multiple TFTP data transfers cannot be initiated in a single session.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with TFTP profile is configured to handle TFTP traffic.
bugs.impact: Multiple TFTP data transfers cannot be initiated in a single session.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Multiple TFTP data transfers can be initiated in a single session

bugs.title: HSL::send does not support handle of type string
bugs.symptoms: HSL::send performs no action when supplied with a logging handle which is a Tcl string.
bugs.conditions: Pass handle of type string to HSL::send.
bugs.impact: HSL::send does not perform intended action.
bugs.workaround: Use handle provided by HSL::open directly.

bugs.title: netHSM key creation with tmsh fails if CSR is also requested
bugs.symptoms: When using gen-csr option in tmsh to create a netHSM key, the operation fails.
bugs.conditions: gen-csr is used in the tmsh command when creating netHSM keys.
bugs.impact: Cannot create csr and key at the same tmsh command for netHSM.
bugs.workaround: Do not use gen-csr option when creating netHSM key.
bugs.fix: Implemented the underlying infrastructure to fully support PKCS #11 protocol. With this change, specifying gen-csr in tmsh works as expected for all netHSM, e.g., Safenet and Thales.

bugs.title: VDI crashes while responding to clients with multiple VDI threads running
bugs.symptoms: VDI crash dump is seen in bigip/var/core/ directory while accessing VDI resources.
bugs.conditions: VDI profile is attached to Virtual server and VDI resources are being used from webtop or from native client
bugs.impact: VDI access is interrupted

bugs.title: Reverse/transparent setting reverting to disabled on child monitor
bugs.symptoms: Child monitor failing. Reverse/transparent setting reverting back to disabled.
bugs.conditions: Parent monitor with reverse/transparent enabled and child monitor with reverse/transparent disabled.
bugs.impact: The child monitor begins to fail when the configuration is re-loaded.
bugs.workaround: Make sure child and parent monitors have the same reverse/transparent setting. Or don't use a custom monitor as a parent if you want to modify reverse/transparent settings.
bugs.fix: Parent monitor and child monitor with differing reverse/transparent now use the correct setting for that monitor configuration.

bugs.title: Fixes to bd and iprepd components not included in BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2
bugs.symptoms: The following bugs were documented as fixed in BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2: ID 531809: FTP/SMTP traffic related bd crash ID 559541: ICAP anti virus tests are not initiated on XML with when should ID 562775: Memory leak in iprepd However, the packages containing these fixes were not actually included in the BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2 ISO. Therefore, these bugs are not actually fixed in BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2
bugs.impact: Referenced bugs are not actually fixed in BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2.
bugs.fix: [BIG-IP v11.5.4 Hotfix Rollup containing this fix] includes the packages which contain the fixes for the following bugs: ID 531809: FTP/SMTP traffic related bd crash ID 559541: ICAP anti virus tests are not initiated on XML with when should ID 562775: Memory leak in iprepd

bugs.title: TMM crash during AVR data cleaning timer
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashed during data cleaning timer.
bugs.conditions: Root cause is not clear; cannot reproduce issue.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: APM session is terminated automatically if web based VPN client is running
bugs.symptoms: If user logs onto APM and launches the VPN client and then closes the browser, the VPN will continue to run and the session will not stop. This is a change in behavior from previous plugin-based web clients.
bugs.conditions: - VPN client is launched from the browser and is running when browser is closed.
bugs.impact: User will have to explicitly close VPN application as well as the browser to logout of session.
bugs.workaround: Close both the browser and the VPN client to stop the session.

bugs.title: REST API calls to invalid REST endpoint log level change
bugs.symptoms: In Big-IP 12.x versions before 12.1.2 invalid requests to a REST endpoint were being recorded in the FINE level logs, making it difficult to audit when an invalid request to a REST endpoint was coming in. In version 12.1.2, the log level was changed to INFO so that these messages are more easily consumed by users attempting to audit the log.
bugs.conditions: Any request made to an invalid REST endpoint will trigger a log message at the FINE level indicating that a request came in to an invalid REST endpoint.
bugs.impact: Auditing the REST Framework logs is more difficult, requiring you to look at messages logged at the FINE level.
bugs.workaround: Users can increase the log level of the REST Framework to FINE by making the following change to the file '/etc/restjavad.log.conf': Before: .level=FINE After: .level=INFO
bugs.fix: This message is included in the INFO log level on BIG-IP v12.1.2.

bugs.title: Overwrite flag in various iControl key/certificate management functions is ignored and might result in errors.
bugs.symptoms: Overwrite flag in key/certificate management iControl functions is ignored and might result in errors.
bugs.conditions: If there is an existing key/certificate, and the key/certificate management iControl/SOAP functions are used to overwrite the key/certificate by setting the overwrite flag, the flag is ignored, and an error is returned.
bugs.impact: Key/certificate overwrite using iControl operations might fail.
bugs.fix: The fix honors the overwrite flag, so that the key/certificate is overwritten when the flag is set to true.

bugs.title: SSO logging level may cause failover
bugs.symptoms: SSO logging level may cause failover.
bugs.conditions: SSO logging level set to "Debug".
bugs.impact: TMM may crash. Core file may be generated.
bugs.workaround: Lower the SSO log level from "Debug" to either "Info" or "Notice".
bugs.fix: The SSO logging level of "Debug" no longer causes failover.

bugs.title: TMM core may be seen when using an HSL format script for HSL reporting in PEM
bugs.symptoms: TMM core resulting in potential loss of service.
bugs.conditions: Requires a PEM HSL reporting action with an HSL format script against a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: In an iRule against the virtual server, set a Tcl variable in the first line after an iRule event. Unset the same Tcl variable in the last line of the iRule event.
bugs.fix: TMM core no longer occurs when using an HSL format script for HSL reporting in PEM.

bugs.title: Name Validation missing for some GTM objects
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system fails to prevent control characters from being embedded within GTM object names. Once the objects exist in the configuration, the BIG-IP system fails to load GTM configurations where objects containing control characters are referenced by other objects. The following GTM objects are susceptible to this control character issue: gtm datacenter gtm prober-pool gtm device gtm application gtm region entry gtm virtual server gtm server gtm link gtm pool
bugs.conditions: -- A GTM object with a control character in the name. -- That object is referenced by another object. Reproduction example: create gtm datacenter "start^Mend" create gtm server test datacenter "start^Mend" address add { 1.2.3.4 } save sys config gtm-only load sys config gtm-only
bugs.impact: Causes the config to fail to load.
bugs.workaround: Remove control characters prior to creating GTM objects.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP monitor process fails to process timeout conditions
bugs.symptoms: Pool members that are down are not marked down by the monitor. The BIG-IP system continues to attempt to monitor the object.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this condition. It was encountered on an https monitor.
bugs.impact: Incorrect monitor state. Pool members may not be marked down even though the target pool-member is down.
bugs.workaround: No known work-around
bugs.fix: The monitor process no longer inadvertently skips processing monitor timeouts and correctly marks monitored objects down.

bugs.title: Modifying license.maxcores Not Allowed Error
bugs.symptoms: Your sync-failover device group status says "Sync Failed" and reports the following error in Device Management :: Overview "- Sync error on <device name>: Load failed from /Common/BIG-IP1 0107178a:3: Modifying license.maxcores to a value other than 8 is not allowed."
bugs.conditions: Non-homogeneous Virtual Editions configured with different licenses in a device group, or with hardware-based BIG-IPs. If the license variable called perf_VE_cores is different among licenses, it will create this condition.
bugs.impact: The device group will fail to sync.
bugs.workaround: If you are using Virtual Editions in a Device Group, ensure that their licenses are the same.
bugs.fix: The variable doesn't sync so there is no error message.

bugs.title: VMware View connections to pool hit matching BIG-IP virtuals
bugs.symptoms: When a VMware View resource is configured to use a pool as a destination, for all the connections to this pool, except the very first one, a matching virtual lookup is performed. This doesn't align with the typical BIG-IP behavior on pool connections that should go directly to the chosen pool member and not hit matching virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: If a VMware View resource is configured to connect to a pool and there is a virtual server matching some or all the IP/port values of pool members, connections to those members will go through the matching virtual server, except for the very first one.
bugs.impact: If a matching virtual is not intended to pass the traffic through (e.g., a 'reject-all' virtual), those connections routed to this virtual server will fail.
bugs.fix: All the connections to VMWare View pool members now go directly without hitting matching BIG-IP virtual servers.

bugs.title: Client-type in access policy does not detect Edge Client after failing authentication.
bugs.symptoms: Users connecting to a virtual server using Edge Client and fails authentication are directed to the policy's deny page, which directs them to a new session link. Once the user clicks that link, the new session is launched, but the user is denied and keeps getting directed to the same Deny page with a link to new session.
bugs.conditions: Have an access policy that allows Client-Type Edge Client but denies Full Browser/Mobile. There is no Message Box on the Full Browser/Mobile branch in Client-Type.
bugs.impact: Once the user clicks new session link from the deny page, new session is launched but client-type gets detected as Full Browser/Mobile and user is denied. This continues until user cancels the external logon dialog.
bugs.workaround: In the "Full or Mobile Browser" branch, add a "Message Box".
bugs.fix: The new behavior is that on Edge Client, the new session link will not be shown. The user can click Cancel and then Connect to try to login to the VPN again. On browsers, the behavior is same. The link will be shown and user can click it to launch new session.
bugs.behavior: Older versions of client were being detected as Browser if user failed authentication the first time and created new session from the client UI. With this fix, Edge client will be detected as edge client in the above scenario.

bugs.title: BD process crash and restarts
bugs.symptoms: bd restarts and generates a core file. bd.log contains messages similar to the following: -- BD_MISC|ERR ... BD shrinking...,going down - BD will be right back. -- BD_MISC|CRIT ... Received SIGSEGV - Core Dumping.
bugs.conditions: The virtual server has a Security Policy and there is a heavy load of traffic. Note: This is a rare race condition case that might occur occasionally when the system is under heavy stress.
bugs.impact: bd restarts, causing a halt to traffic for few seconds.
bugs.fix: Race condition has been fixed.

bugs.title: ASM Policy Export returns HTML error file
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to export an ASM Policy the resulting file contains an HTML error page.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this condition.
bugs.impact: Unable to export ASM Policies.
bugs.workaround: Delete all files in /ts/dms/policy/upload_files/. All files are transient and can safely be deleted.
bugs.fix: Permissions are now explicitly set on exported ASM Policies so the GUI PHP process can successfully download it.

bugs.title: TMM can core when using LB::detach and TCP::notify commands in an iRule
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores when running an iRule that has the LB::detach command before the TCP::notify command.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server with an iRule that has the LB::detach command executed before the TCP::notify command.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid the combination of the TCP::notify and LB::detach commands.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores in this instance.

bugs.title: basic_string::compare error in encrypted SSL key file if the first line of the file is blank
bugs.symptoms: Trying to load a configuration that references an encrypted SSL key file may fail if the first line of the SSL key file is blank. When this occurs, the system will report a vague error message: 01070711:3: basic_string::compare If this happens during an upgrade, the system will not load the configuration under the new software version, and will remain inoperative.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if an affected configuration is present on a system running BIG-IP v11.3.0 or earlier, and is upgraded to BIG-IP v11.4.0 or later.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load on upgrade with extremely unhelpful error message, and absolutely no indication as to what file was being processed at the time (or that this relates to a filestore file).
bugs.workaround: Remove the newlines at the beginning of any SSL key files that begin with a newline. During an upgrade scenario, edit the files in the filestore.

bugs.title: Loading the configuration fails when a virtual server uses HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS).
bugs.symptoms: When loading the BIG-IP system's configuration by running the 'tmsh load sys config' command, the command fails and returns an error similar to the following example: 01071afb:3: With HSTS mode enabled in HTTP Profile '/Common/my-http', virtual server '/Common/my-vs' using this profile requires a 'clientssl' profile attached. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. This validation error should only be returned when a virtual server using HSTS was not assigned a client-ssl profile. This issue consists in the fact the BIG-IP system returns the error when your configuration is correct. Note this issue can also occur during an upgrade from an unaffected version (e.g., 12.1.4) to an affected version (e.g., 12.1.5).
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your configuration contains at least one virtual server making use of a HTTP profile with HSTS enabled. -- You attempt to reload the BIG-IP system's configuration (either explicitly via the tmsh utility, or implicitly during an upgrade).
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to load. This can have several consequences, depending on what you were doing: -- Upgrading from an unaffected version to an affected one: the configuration does not load after the upgrade and the system remains inoperative. -- Reloading the configuration to get rid of unsaved changes: you cannot do so, and the configuration elements you were trying to remove continue to exist in memory. -- Reloading the configuration to pick up manual changes you made to a configuration file (e.g., bigip.conf): you cannot do so, and the new configuration elements are not loaded into memory.
bugs.workaround: There is a temporary workaround. Potential impact of workaround: ideally, this workaround should not be performed on a unit that is already processing traffic, as the virtual servers will not operate in HSTS mode until the procedure is complete. As such, a small window will exist during which new clients will not immediately learn that the virtual servers wish to use HSTS. 1) Edit the /config/bigip.conf file (and all /config/partitions/*/bigip.conf files) and change the following section in HTTP profiles: From this: hsts { mode enabled } To this: hsts { mode disabled } 2) Load the configuration: tmsh load sys config partitions all 3) Re-apply HSTS to the appropriate HTTP profiles. However, note that the issue occurs again the next time a configuration load is attempted. If you are planning to upgrade to an affected version and you use HSTS, you can contact F5 Support to obtain an Engineering Hotfix for this issue for your software version.
bugs.fix: The configuration loads as expected.

bugs.title: Citrix Remote desktop resource custom parameter name does not accept hyphen character
bugs.symptoms: While adding the custom parameter in Citrix Resource would give parser error as following, 01070734:3: Configuration error: apm resource remote-desktop /Common/ctx_resource: Parse error on line 1: DesktopViewer-ForceFullScreenStartup=On"
bugs.conditions: Having Citrix resource with custom parameter name with hyphen character
bugs.impact: Custom parameter can not be used with hyphen character
bugs.fix: Accept custom parameter name with hyphen character

bugs.title: BMC version 2.50.3 for iSeries appliances
bugs.symptoms: Firmware on BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx needs to be upgraded to BMC version 2.50.3.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx. -- PXE boot.
bugs.impact: This is a firmware upgrade.
bugs.fix: This release contains BMC version 2.50.3 which includes support for PXE boot on the following BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx.
bugs.behavior: This release contains BMC version 2.50.3 which includes support for PXE boot on the following BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx.

bugs.title: SWG with Response Analytics agent in a Per-Request policy fails with some URLs
bugs.symptoms: SWG with Response Analytics agent in a Per-Request policy fails with some URLs
bugs.conditions: Response analytics agent is added to per-request policy and per-request policy is attached to the virtual. APM and SWG are provisioned and licensed.
bugs.impact: Client might receive resets for some URLs when response analytics doesn't function correctly.
bugs.workaround: Remove response analytics agent from the per-request policy and perform categorization based only on URLs.
bugs.fix: Correctly handle the response analytics for these URLs and dont send resets to client.

bugs.title: tmm core using PEM
bugs.symptoms: tmm core when using PEM with cloning monitored traffic
bugs.conditions: Using PEM with iRules and cloning traffic
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The problem with PEM and cloning traffic via iRule has been corrected.

bugs.title: After VPN tunnel established, if network is switched and a Captive Portal is present in the new network, EdgeClient fails to re-establish VPN tunnel
bugs.symptoms: After VPN tunnel is established, if network is switched and a Captive Portal is present in the new network, EdgeClient fails to re-establish VPN tunnel.
bugs.conditions: VPN tunnel is established. Place the computer in hibernation. Resume from hibernation and connect to a new network where a Captive Portal is present, e.g. Starbucks.
bugs.impact: EdgeClient may show an error page for captive portal or stay in Reconnecting state for extended period. Disconnect button may not be responsive.
bugs.fix: If captive portal is detected during reconnect, close VPN resources before showing captive portal authentication page.

bugs.title: NTLM Machine Account page fails when using an Admin password containing spaces
bugs.symptoms: Creating a new NTLM machine account under Access Policy :: Access Profiles : NTLM : Machine Account fails when admin password contains any number of white spaces in it.
bugs.conditions: -- NTLM Machine Account configuration. -- NTLM Machine Account admin password contains spaces.
bugs.impact: New NTLM Machine Account configuration cannot be created.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using white spaces in the NTLM Machine Account admin password.
bugs.fix: White space is now an allowed character in the NTLM Machine Account admin password.

bugs.title: Cannot map hardware type (12) to HardwareType enumeration
bugs.symptoms: iControl-SOAP throws an error whenever a method call to SystemInfo::get_hardware_information() is made.
bugs.conditions: This is reproducible in under all conditions.
bugs.impact: iControl-SOAP crashes when this call is made.
bugs.workaround: Don't call this SystemInfo::get_hardware_information().
bugs.fix: Call this method no longer leads to a crash.

bugs.title: Encryption and authentication keys for IKEv2 are not logged
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP provides no option to log the negotiated IKEv2 keys for debugging purposes.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered if you are trying to troubleshoot or debug IKEv2.
bugs.impact: Debugging protocol problems is impeded when encrypted packets cannot be examined for problems.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is known at this time.
bugs.fix: When ike-daemon log level is set to debug, and a log publisher is also attached, encryption and authentication keys are logged in tmm log files as well as ipsec.log. This mainly appears in the form of IKE protocol packets displayed in human readable form after decryption. This includes all negotiated keys, unless you have explicitly requested suppression of keys in logs by changing the value of sys db variable ipsec.debug.logkeys to prevent such display.
bugs.behavior: When ike-daemon log level is set to debug, and a log publisher is also attached, encryption and authentication keys are logged in tmm log files as well as ipsec.log. This mainly appears in the form of IKE protocol packets displayed in human readable form after decryption. This includes all negotiated keys, unless you have explicitly requested suppression of keys in logs by changing the value of sys db variable ipsec.debug.logkeys to prevent such display.

bugs.title: Cosmetic: duplicated partition names in the "Resource Management" window when assigning iRules to Virtual Servers.
bugs.symptoms: There is a cosmetic issue that results in duplicated partition names in the "Resource Management" window when assigning iRules to Virtual Servers (in Local Traffic â€ºâ€º Virtual Servers : Virtual Server List â€ºâ€º Virtual_Server_name).
bugs.conditions: 1) Go to Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers : Virtual Server List :: Virtual_Server_name --: Resources --: Manage iRules). 2) Move any 2 available iRules (created in Common partition) left to the "Enabled" column. 3) Select the bottom iRule from the "Enabled" column and click the "Up" button. 4) Add an additional iRule (created in Common partition) to the "Enabled" column.
bugs.impact: Instead of showing all iRules under one partition name (Common), the system is duplicating the partition name.
bugs.workaround: None. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: Partition names are no longer duplicated in the "Resource Management" window when assigning iRules to Virtual Servers.

bugs.title: Port misuse policies could be created if AFM is not provisioned
bugs.symptoms: You cannot select Port Misuse Policies from the menu but if you select Service Policies from the Network menu Port Misuse Policies, you can still create them from the upper horizontal Tabs. Changes are saved to the configuration file but are ignored.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is not provisioned. -- You select Service Policies in the GUI.
bugs.impact: The system indicates that a Port Misuse Policy is in effect when it is not.
bugs.workaround: When AFM is not provisioned Port Misuse Policy should not be available
bugs.fix: Removed Port Misuse Policy from upper Tabs if AFM is not provisioned, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: APM CustomDialer can't connect to APM server with invalid/untrusted SSL certificate
bugs.symptoms: If APM server uses untrusted SSL certificate/or it is accessed using IP address CustomDilaer, access is refused and there is no prompt to confirm the security warning.
bugs.conditions: APM has invalid certificate User uses CustomDialer to access VPN
bugs.impact: VPN connection can't be established
bugs.workaround: Use valid SSL certificate on APM or add particular invalid certificate to trusted store on Windows
bugs.fix: Now CustomDialer warns user about invalid certificate and allows to proceed with invalid certificate.

bugs.title: Local policy rule descriptions disappear when policy is re-saved
bugs.symptoms: Local policy rule descriptions disappear when policy is re-saved.
bugs.conditions: A rule with description exists, and the policy it's under is saved.
bugs.impact: An existing rule description disappears when the policy it's under is saved.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to modify the policy's properties.
bugs.fix: Local policy rule descriptions now remain visible when policy is re-saved.

bugs.title: Frequent DNS Express zone transfers can prevent updated zone data becoming available.
bugs.symptoms: If DNS Express performs a zone transfer more frequently than every 15 seconds, the new data will not become available until there is a 15 second period with no zone transfers.
bugs.conditions: DNS Express performs a zone transfer more frequently than every 15 seconds.
bugs.impact: Updated data in zone transfers is not available.
bugs.workaround: If possible, configure environment such that there is a 15 second window between zone updates. or If possible, disable notifies from the master dns server and lower the refresh time of the SOA record, forcing dnsX to check serial numbers of the zone at refresh interval and refresh the zone if needed.
bugs.fix: DNS Express no longer has the 15 second delay, so updated data in zone transfers is immediately available.

bugs.title: HTTPS Monitors Up Interval field cannot be disabled if enabled in parent monitor
bugs.symptoms: When the Up Interval of an HTTPS Monitor is enabled, all the children monitor of the same type will inherit the same setting and cannot disable it.
bugs.conditions: The parent https monitor has enabled the up interval.
bugs.impact: children monitors will also inherit the setting, and cannot disable the setting. They can, however, set a different value than the parent.

bugs.title: FastL4 with full PVA acceleration: Average connections per second decreased 5-7% since v12.1.1 on i5800 platforms
bugs.symptoms: Custom BIG-IP hardware provides a significant assist to the main CPU complex for FastL4 traffic with full PVA acceleration enabled; however, the main CPU still performs significant per-connection packet processing. Bug fixes and stability improvements in v12.1.1-HF1 and -HF2 have increased this load slightly. With a traffic profile that results in a high number of new connections and very little data exchanged per connection, if the CPU reaches 100% utilization, the average connections per second will be decreased.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP v12.1.1_HF1 and _HF2, with a virtual server configured for FastL4 traffic, and including a profile that enables Full PVA Acceleration is affected. The traffic includes an extreme number of new connections, with minimal data exchanged during each connection. i5800 appliances have shown a 5-7% decrease.
bugs.impact: The average CPS will decrease over the same configuration running v12.1.1 by approximately 5 percent, as observed with internal F5 traffic stress testing.

bugs.title: Edge client can fail to upgrade when Always Connected is selected
bugs.symptoms: Attempt to upgrade from an Edge client version to a current version fails when Always Connected is enabled
bugs.conditions: Always Connected is selected in BIG-IP when upgrading the client.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails. Must turn off Always Connected to upgrade client.
bugs.workaround: Turn off Always Connected before upgrading.
bugs.fix: Edge client now succeeds during upgrade when Always Connected is selected.

bugs.title: Desktop title is garbled for Citrix Storefront integration mode with non-sta configuration
bugs.symptoms: Desktop launched from browser or from native receiver has garbled title.
bugs.conditions: Citrix storefront integration mode through APM with no STA configured. Double byte language such as Japanese character set is used in the backend.
bugs.impact: Desktop title is not shown properly.
bugs.fix: Double byte character language title is shown properly

bugs.title: Service health calculation creates unjustified CPU utilization
bugs.symptoms: When ASM provisioned service health is calculated and published to all VSs with security profile, even if stress-based detection is not configured
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned and configured hundreds of VSs with security profile
bugs.impact: High CPU utilization
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Refactored internal infrastructure illuminated unnecessary server health calculation and CPU utilization

bugs.title: Deleting self IP prompting error with subnet network address
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect error message when attempting to delete the last non-floating self IP
bugs.conditions: Attempting to delete the last non-floating self IP
bugs.impact: Incorrect error message indicates that it includes the self IP being deleted but actually includes the network address of the self IP
bugs.workaround: Interpret the error message to indicate that one or more floating self IPs are configured in the specified network and that they must be removed before deleting the non-floating self IP.

bugs.title: Csyncd memory leak on multi-bladed systems
