bugs.symptoms: Csyncd memory use increases over time. It may fail due to large size (>2 to 3 GB), possibly leading to this ltm log: err csyncd[8258]: 013b0004:3: Fatal error: fork failed. Memory pressure may develop, leading to an increased use of swap, and the system may become sluggish and show other low-memory symptoms. If memory pressure is severe, the Linux oom killer will likely terminate csyncd. On systems with more free memory, csyncd will terminate with a core file when it is approaching 4GB in size. In both cases csyncd automatically restarts.
bugs.conditions: Multi-bladed vCMP guest or VIPRION.
bugs.impact: Low free memory may lead to system instability. If memory pressure is severe, the Linux oom killer will likely terminate csyncd. On systems with more free memory, csyncd will terminate with a core file when it is above ~2.2 GB in size. In both cases csyncd automatically restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restart csycnd on all blades to free the memory it has in use: clsh bigstart restart csyncd This is typically not service-affecting.
bugs.fix: Memory leak identified and fixed.

bugs.title: Device sync constantly showing Changes Pending when using custom ASM Search Engines
bugs.symptoms: The Device sync status will constantly show "Changes Pending" when a custom ASM Search Engine is added with a new Bot Name to an existing Search Engine name. For example, the Yandex search engine is a built-in search engine with Bot Name "Yandex". When adding a custom search engine with the same name "Yandex", but a different Bot Name, for example "yandexbot", the issue will happen. When the issue appears, the device sync status shows "Changes Pending". Running a config-sync will bring the status to "In Sync", but a few seconds later, the status will change back to "Changes Pending".
bugs.conditions: 1. Multiple devices are joined in sync-failover device-group and ASM sync is enabled. 2. (AND) A custom ASM Search Engine is added with a new Bot Name but an existing Search Engine Name.
bugs.impact: 1. Device sync status constantly showing Changes Pending 2. The custom ASM Search Engine may not be bypassed for JavaScript challenges which are sent as a result of either the Web Scraping Feature, or Device-ID. This applies also to standalone deployments.
bugs.workaround: Add the custom ASM Search Engine under a new name. For example, if adding the "yandexbox" search engine, then use the Search Engine name "Yandex-yandexbot" instead of simple "Yandex".
bugs.fix: The device sync status properly remains "In Sync" when custom ASM Search Engines are added.

bugs.title: TMM can crash when HTML minification is configured
bugs.symptoms: When AAM is provisioned and is used to cache dynamic pages, it can be configured to use HTML Minification to improve performance and optimize memory utilization. In some cases, HTML may incorrectly process the HTML code and cause TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: 1) AAM has to be provisioned and 2) AAM policy has to be configured and 3) has HTML minification enabled and 4) be applied to a virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disabling minification prevent TMM from crashing for this reason.

bugs.title: References to DTLS may show up in client logs even when DTLS is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Edge client logs contain entries that reference DTLS even when DTLS is disabled and is not used.
bugs.conditions: DTLS is disabled on APM and user establishes a VPN tunnel to APM using TLS.
bugs.impact: May cause confusion during troubleshooting connection issues; the log entries can be ignored if DTLS is not configured.
bugs.workaround: Ignore references to DTLS when DTLS is disabled.
bugs.fix: References to DTLS no longer show up in client logs even when DTLS is disabled.

bugs.title: Inconsistent info between tmsh and WebUI for profile radiusLB-subscriber-aware
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP provisioned with LTM only, the radius profile called radiusLB-subscriber-aware displays inconsistent information between tmsh and configuration utility
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at the radiusLB-subscriber-aware profile in both tmsh and the GUI.
bugs.impact: On a device that does not have PEM licensed: root@(v12)(cfg-sync Changes Pending)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list ltm profile radius radiusLB-subscriber-aware ltm profile radius radiusLB-subscriber-aware { app-service none defaults-from radiusLB } However, viewing the profile in the configuration utility Local Traffic :: Profiles : Services : RADIUS : radiusLB-subscriber-aware Settings field Custom checkbox Persist Attribute disabled Subscriber Discovery enabled Client Spec disabled Protocol Profile(_sys_radius_proto_imsi) enabled On a device which does not PEM licensed, the Protocol profile should be set to None but shows as enabled.

bugs.title: Firewall rule with Multicast/Link Local IPv6 addresses netmask bigger than 32 will not work
bugs.symptoms: For AFM firewall rule with IPV6 source or destination addresses matching multicast or link local pattern, if the netmask is set to greater than 32, the rule will not match.
bugs.conditions: IPV6 source or destination addresses matching patterns: FF02:xxxx:: FE08:xxxx::
bugs.impact: The firewall rule will not be applied if there's traffic matching the rule.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with AFM firewall rule netmasks

bugs.title: In TM Shell, saving the AAM configuration removes value from matching rule causing system configuration loading failure
bugs.symptoms: In TMSH, when trying to save the AAM configuration, TMSH removes value from matching rule. It corrupts bigip.conf and causes system loading configuration failure, with the following error in /var/log/ltm: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Policy "/Common/Drafts/<policy>", node "test_node", matching rule "path:Path": Must have a value. Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Use TM Shell to load configuration. -- AAM configuration is loaded on BIG-IP and it is saved
bugs.impact: TMSH fails to load system configuration file. Before the configuration save the policy would look like this: matching { path { values { / { } } } } After the save it is converted to matching { path { } }
bugs.fix: TMSH now saves AAM configuration without removing values from matching rules. Saving/loading system configuration succeeds.

bugs.title: SNMP reports incorrect value for sysBladeTempTemperature OID
bugs.symptoms: SNMP reports incorrect value for sysBladeTempTemperature OID, while TMSH reports the corresponding value correctly. # snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.1.3.2.4.2.1.2.8.1 F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysBladeTempTemperature.8.1 = Gauge32: 4294967245 # tmsh show sys hardware Sys::Hardware Blade Temperature Status Slot Index Lo Limit(C) Temp(degC) Hi Limit(C) Location ... 1 8 0 -48 0 Blade CPU #1 TControl Delta tem ... The negative "Blade CPU #1 TControl Delta" temperature is being incorrectly reported as a large positive temperature by SNMP.

bugs.title: Same report is downloaded repeatedly after user clicks on "export csv" and then click on another tab
bugs.symptoms: If you click on the "export csv" button and then switch to another report, the same csv file will be download again when you click on the tab of another report.
bugs.conditions: Creating multiple reports in Access Report page and clicking on the "export csv" button in one report.
bugs.impact: Same file will be downloaded repeatedly.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the page before switching to another report.

bugs.title: LTM v11.6.x Errors in F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.txt prevent its compilation in NMS (Network Management System)
bugs.symptoms: Error during compilation of MIB file F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.txt in NMS: Unexpected token: in /.../mibs/F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.mib line no: 27738. The above compilation error is caused by missing commas in F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.txt: ltmFwRuleStatRuleStatType OBJECT-TYPE SYNTAX INTEGER { enforced(1)staged(2), <===== comma missing here active(3), overlapper(4) } MAX-ACCESS read-only STATUS current DESCRIPTION "" ::= { ltmFwRuleStatEntry 6 } ltmFwPolicyRuleStatRuleStatType OBJECT-TYPE SYNTAX INTEGER { enforced(1)staged(2), <===== comma missing here active(3), overlapper(4) } MAX-ACCESS read-only STATUS current DESCRIPTION "" ::= { ltmFwPolicyRuleStatEntry 6 }
bugs.conditions: Compile F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.txt from 11.6.x versions in NMS.
bugs.impact: F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.txt fails to compile in NMS.
bugs.workaround: Correct syntax in the F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB.txt file, as follows: ltmFwRuleStatRuleStatType OBJECT-TYPE SYNTAX INTEGER { enforced(1), staged(2), active(3), overlapper(4) } MAX-ACCESS read-only STATUS current DESCRIPTION "" ::= { ltmFwRuleStatEntry 6 } ltmFwPolicyRuleStatRuleStatType OBJECT-TYPE SYNTAX INTEGER { enforced(1), staged(2), active(3), overlapper(4) } MAX-ACCESS read-only STATUS current DESCRIPTION "" ::= { ltmFwPolicyRuleStatEntry 6 }

bugs.title: iControl.ForceSessions enabled results in GUI error on certain pages
bugs.symptoms: GUI pages display "An error has occurred while trying to process your request."
bugs.conditions: Visiting pages related to PKI (cert/key), SNMP, AFM or licensing tasks when iControl.ForceSessions is enabled.
bugs.impact: Unable to use GUI for certain tasks when iControl.ForceSessions is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Use shell for related administrative tasks or if feature is not used, disable with the following command: tmsh# modify sys db icontrol.forcesessions value disable
bugs.fix: Enable GUI to adapt when the icontrol.forcesessions is set to 'enable'.

bugs.title: Surfing with IE8 sometimes results with script error
bugs.symptoms: Slow devices running Internet Explorer 8 can suffer performance issues on websafe protected sites.
bugs.conditions: Slow device running Internet Explorer 8. Large number of configured or updated malware signatures.
bugs.impact: Clientside slowness. In extreme cases, a popup asking the user whether to stop the script.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of malware signatures
bugs.fix: Compressed signatures

bugs.title: Attack Signature Update with only 1 active policy logs 'Please apply policy' error message
bugs.symptoms: Attack Signature Update on a device with only a single active policy logs the following error message: There are too many Security Policies using outdated attack signatures. Please apply policy on all Security Policies." This occurs even if 'Auto Apply New Signatures Configuration After Update' is checked.
bugs.conditions: Attack Signature Update on a device with only a single active policy.
bugs.impact: Benign error posted. The error message has no functional impact and can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: Encryption is not activated unless "real-time encryption" is selected
bugs.symptoms: Encryption is not activated as expected
bugs.conditions: Encryption enabled Real-time encryption disabled
bugs.impact: Encryption error alert received in alert server
bugs.workaround: Enable "real-time encryption"
bugs.fix: Encryption on submit is now supported better.

bugs.title: enable SIP::respond iRule command to operate during MR_FAILED event
bugs.symptoms: When an message fails to route, it is not possible to return an error status back to the client.
bugs.conditions: When a message fails to route, the MR_FAILED event is raised for the message.
bugs.impact: Without this change, it is not possible for the script author to generate a response message to the client based on the routing failure.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: SIP::respond command now works during MR_FAILED event.

bugs.title: Error message: subscriber id response; Subscription not found
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP restarts the icr_eventd process and generates a core file. You might see the following messages in the LTM log file: -- err icr_eventd[4589]: 01a10003:3: Receive MCP msg failed: could not get subscriber id response, status: 0x1020046 -- err mcpd[4206]: 01070069:3: Subscription not found in mcpd for subscriber Id %icr_eventd.
bugs.conditions: Might be related to restarting a BIG-IP Virtual Edition installation.
bugs.impact: The icr_eventd process restarts, and the system produces a core file.

bugs.title: Multi domain login support with Citrix logon prompt
bugs.symptoms: Domain session variable is not populated.
bugs.conditions: Only one domain can be supported by statically configuring the domain in access policy.
bugs.impact: Only single domain logon supported.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Support multiple domains using Citrix logon prompt for Citrix Receivers.

bugs.title: "SSL::disable/enable serverside" + oneconnect reuse is broken
bugs.symptoms: If "SSL::disable/enable serverside" is configured in an iRule and oneConnect is configured in the iRule or in the Virtual Server profile, BIG-IP may not receive the backend server's HTTP response for every client's HTTP Request.
bugs.conditions: 1. "SSL::disable/enable serverside" exists in the iRule 2. OneConnect is configured in the iRule or in the VS profile 3. apply the iRule and oneConnect Profile to the VS.
bugs.impact: The oneConnect behavior is unexpected, and may not get the backend Server's HTTP response for every client's HTTP Request.
bugs.workaround: You can work around the problem by disabling oneConnect.

bugs.title: Using iControl REST to create ucs archive results in a "500 internal server error" response when unit has ASM provisioned
bugs.symptoms: using iControl REST to create a ucs archive results in a "500 internal server error" response when unit has ASM provisioned. however, the UCS file does get created.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: BIG-IP returns a 500 internal server error; however, the UCS file does get created.

bugs.title: bigd core when using Tcl monitors
bugs.symptoms: If a Tcl monitor encounters an error, it may exit with an assert which causes bigd to core.
bugs.conditions: This can occur rarely when Tcl monitors are in use (specifically, SMTP, FTP, IMAP, POP3 monitors).
bugs.impact: bigd can core, which temporarily suspends monitoring while bigd restarts.
bugs.fix: Now, when a Tcl monitor encounters an error, it no longer exits with an assert, so bigd no longer cores.

bugs.title: Fastl4 handshake timeout is absolute instead of relative
bugs.symptoms: TCP connections that are pending completion of the three-way handshake are expired based on the absolute value of handshake timeout. For example, if handshake timeout is 5 seconds, then the connection is reset after 5 seconds of receiving the initial SYN from the client.
bugs.conditions: A TCP connection in three-way handshake.
bugs.impact: Connections are expired prematurely if they are still in three-way handshake.
bugs.workaround: Disable handshake timeout. Impact of workaround: Your TCP handshake will not prematurely timeout and connections remains open until the Idle Timeout expires.
bugs.fix: The handshake timeout now expires based on idleness of the connection, taking into consideration of any SYN retransmissions, etc., that might occur.

bugs.title: Missing health monitor information for FQDN members
bugs.symptoms: Health monitor information and status are both missing for FQDN nodes and pool members.
bugs.conditions: FQDN nodes and pool members configured.
bugs.impact: GUI does not show health monitors info/status in node properties page, pool member properties page, or monitor instances page. Difficulty checking health monitor info/status for FQDN members.
bugs.workaround: Check logs for this info.
bugs.fix: The system now exposes health monitors info/status and the GUI shows them in node properties page, pool member properties page, and monitor instances page.

bugs.title: vCMP guest may fail to start due to not enough hugepages
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, when there are many vCMP guests, the last one may fail to start because there are not enough hugepages. The shortfall is between 5 and 20 hugepages. Occasionally, that lack is sufficient to prevent the last guest from starting.
bugs.conditions: The circumstances under which this occurs are not known, but appears related to a race condition related to memory handling.
bugs.impact: vCMP guest fails to start.
bugs.workaround: Once in this state, restarting the host system clears the condition. Note: Restarting the vCMP guests does not clear the condition.
bugs.fix: Addressed by changes to the pagemap code.

bugs.title: GUI to handle file path manipulation to prevent GUI instability.
bugs.symptoms: Request file path may be incorrectly processed
bugs.conditions: Authenticated administrative user makes a GUI request
bugs.impact: The GUI becomes unstable because it cannot process the request.
bugs.fix: Redirect the user to a No Access page.

bugs.title: Support non-default route domains
bugs.symptoms: Some connections are reset
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the device is configured with non-default route domains when connecting to other tmms over the backplane
bugs.impact: Traffic processing failure
bugs.fix: The system now supports non-default route domains when connecting to other tmms over the backplane. Note: As a result of this fix, there is a behavior change: The iRule 'node' method now requires that you specify a route_domain to in order for the traffic to be sent to a node assigned to a route domain.
bugs.behavior: The iRule 'node' method now requires a route_domain to be specified in order for the traffic to be sent to a node that is assigned to a route domain.

bugs.title: IKEv2 VPN tunnels fail to establish
bugs.symptoms: IKEv2 VPN tunnels fail to establish.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with IKEv2 on a specific 12.1.2 HF1 engineering hotfix.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv2 VPN tunnels fail to establish.
bugs.workaround: Use IPsec IKEv1.
bugs.fix: IKEv2 VPN tunnels now establish as expected.

bugs.title: Memory leak in snmpd
bugs.symptoms: Memory usage in snmpd is increases until the OOM process kills snmpd.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured with virtual servers that have the same destination IP address
bugs.impact: snmp disrupted while snmp restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Fixed memory leaks.

bugs.title: software switched platforms accept traffic on lacp trunks even when the trunk is down
bugs.symptoms: On software switched platforms tmm owned LCAP trunks still accept traffic even though the trunk is down from the control plane ( LACP status down).
bugs.conditions: LACP trunk with status down
bugs.impact: VLAN failsafe timers are erroneous reset, VLAN failsafe is broken.
bugs.workaround: no workaround
bugs.fix: tmm now checks the link status on tmm owned lacp trunks before accepting traffic.

bugs.title: Connection Using TCP::collect iRule May Not Close
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP never sends a TCP FIN in response to a client FIN.
bugs.conditions: A finite TCP::collect iRule is in progress. This is repeatable in the debug kernel; in the default kernel, there has to be execution delay in a CLIENT_DATA iRule.
bugs.impact: The connection does not close until the sweeper causes a RST.
bugs.workaround: Adding a TCP::close command to a CLIENT_DATA iRule may work.
bugs.fix: Handle execution delay correctly.

bugs.title: bigd core due to memory leak, especially with FQDN nodes
bugs.symptoms: The bigd daemon may core due to excessive memory consumption caused by a slow memory leak that occurs when creating or updating an LTM node or pool member. This memory leak occurs much more quickly on BIG-IP v12.1.3.2 and earlier when using FQDN nodes/pool members with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled.
bugs.conditions: The bigd memory leak occurs slowly with non-FQDN nodes/pool members, but much more quickly on BIG-IP v12.1.3.2 and earlier when using FQDN nodes/pool members with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled. On BIG-IP v12.1.3.2 and earlier, an additional leak occurs each time an FQDN name is resolved for an FQDN node or pool member. The rate of the leak in this case is determined by the number of FQDN nodes/pool members configured with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled, and the FQDN name resolution interval (determined by the 'interval' setting of the 'fqdn' configuration for the FQDN node).
bugs.impact: The bigd daemon may core due to excessive memory consumption.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to work around this issue by one of the following methods: 1. Restart the bigd daemon before memory consumption becomes excessive. (Note that this may interrupt traffic to configured pool members.) On BIG-IP v12.1.3.2 and earlier: 2. Configure a longer 'interval' value in the 'fqdn' configuration for configured FQDN nodes. 3. Configure FQDN nodes/pool members without the 'autopopulate' setting enabled.
bugs.fix: The bigd daemon no longer leaks memory when configuring an LTM node or pool member.

bugs.title: "persist add" irule validation fails for RTSP_RESPONSE event on upgrade to v12.x.x
bugs.symptoms: "persist add" irule validation fails for RTSP_RESPONSE event on upgrade to v12.x.x
bugs.conditions: When the RTSP_RESPONSE event and "persist add" iRule are used and upgrade to v12.x.x.
bugs.impact: "persist add" iRule validation failed. The iRule will not be loaded.
bugs.workaround: possible workaround is to bypass validation when RULE_INIT { set static::persist_cmd { persist add uie $SessionID $static::persist_timeout } } when RTSP_RESPONSE { set SessionID [RTSP::header value "Session"] if { $SessionID != "" }{ #persist add uie $SessionID $static::persist_timeout eval $static::persist_cmd } }

bugs.title: Latency for Thales key population to the secondary slot after reboot
bugs.symptoms: It may take a significant amount of time for the Thales key to populate from the primary slot to the secondary slot after a reboot. The latency can be a few minutes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs for Thales netHSM installed on Chassis.
bugs.impact: The key can't be found at secondary slot and the ssl traffic may fail.
bugs.workaround: If SSL handshakes fail on secondary blades for newly created Thales keys, you may check secondary blades with nfkminfo -l to see if the file is there. If not the file can be synchronized with rfs-sync --U.

bugs.title: Native IXLV: New tagged VLAN does not work after several restarts of tmm
bugs.symptoms: Traffic does not pass for newly added tagged VLANs.
bugs.conditions: 1. Native IXLV devices (Intel X710/XL710/XXV710 family) NICs are in use. 2. Tagged VLAN in use. 3. TMM is restarted several times. 4. A new tagged VLAN is added.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not send/receive traffic for tagged VLANs.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, do the following: 1. Stop the BIG-IP guest. 2. Re-load the i40e driver on the hypervisor host using the following command: rmmod i40e; modprobe i40e. 3. Start the BIG-IP guest.
bugs.fix: Tagged VLANs now pass traffic as expected regardless of tmm restarts.

bugs.title: SSL handshake fails when clientssl uses softcard-protected key-certs.
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake fails when clientssl uses softcard-protected key-certs.
bugs.conditions: Softcard-protection is enabled and token protection is disabled.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake fails
bugs.workaround: None known.
bugs.fix: SSL handshake no longer fails when clientssl uses softcard-protected key-certs.

bugs.title: iControl REST transaction failure when specifying older schema version
bugs.symptoms: While performing iControl REST calls that specify 11.6.0 as the schema version, you get an error: {"code":400,"message":"Error on connection or connection was closed by peer:1114","errorStack":[]}r
bugs.conditions: Using iControl REST while specifying the 11.6.0 schema, for example: https://<ip_addr>/mgmt/tm/transaction/$trans_id?ver=11.6.0
bugs.impact: iControl REST call may fail intermittently.
bugs.workaround: Specify the current schema version.

bugs.title: Some URL unwrapping functions can behave bad
bugs.symptoms: Some URL unwrapping functions can behave incorrectly with different web application malfunctions as a result.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript with "location.pathname" like fields at the right side of an expression.
bugs.impact: Different web application malfunctions. One example is SharePoint 2010 using IE11, clicking the Edit button results in "Only secure content is displayed" at the bottom of the page.
bugs.fix: Fixed.

bugs.title: Mismatch in URL CRC32 calculation
bugs.symptoms: In some cases URL CRC32 calculated by JS does not match referrer CRC32 calculated by Plugin.
bugs.conditions: Each one of next conditions cause this problem: 1. CRC32 calculated for URL with path parameters while strip_path_parameters BigDB variable value is 'true'. 2. CRC32 calculated for URL with a fragment (hashmark '#') in query string.
bugs.impact: A component validation alert is triggered as a result of mismatch between URL CRC32 calculated by JS and referrer CRC32 calculated by Plugin.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: strip_path_parameters BigDB variable value is passed to JS and JS URL normalization before CRC32 calculation is now similar to the one Plugin does.

bugs.title: Loop detection implemention logic violates branch parameter compliance with RFC3261
bugs.symptoms: Branch parameter compliance with RFC3261 dictates that: ACK for a non-2xx response will have the same branch ID as the INVITE whose response it acknowledges. However in BIG-IP if loop detection is enabled, the branch parameter value differs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when loop detection flag is enabled in the sipsession object.
bugs.impact: Branch parameter value of INVITE and ACK for a non-2xx response even though its part of the same transaction. Violates RFC3261.
bugs.workaround: Disable loop detection flag in sipsession object.
bugs.fix: #tmsh modify ltm message-routing sip profile session sipsession loop-detection disabled

bugs.title: Non-zero Route domain is not always used in HTTP explicit proxy
bugs.symptoms: You may experience connectivity failure in certain situations where a sideband communications are required as part of the transaction.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has http-explicit configuration, where a sideband connection is required, say in the case of getting an OCSP response or a DNS resolver response when those services are associated with a different route domain.
bugs.impact: End-to-end connectivity failure.
bugs.workaround: Change configuration so that all services required are on the default route domain, 0.

bugs.title: HA pair will go Active/Active, and report peer as "offline" is network-failover service is blocked
bugs.symptoms: All members of a Sync/Failover Device Group report "Active" for all traffic-groups, and "Offline" for all peers. Configuration sync works appropriately.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if the network failover configuration is incorrect. Each device should have multiple network failover addresses (either unicast or multicast) configured, and any self-IPs configured as unicast addresses must not block the configured unicast UDP source-port (default value: 1026). If this port is blocked, the devices cannot exchange failover status information.
bugs.impact: When devices cannot reach the failover address of their peer devices, failover traffic will not be processed correctly and the device will become active for all traffic groups. This will result in duplicate IP addresses on the network for the objects in the traffic groups, which will cause a disruption of service.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the "allow-service" parameter for the self-IP includes the configured network-failover port. Normally this is done with "allow-service { default }" if using the default default-list, or an explicit entry can be used with "allow-service { udp:1026 }".
bugs.fix: The system has been changed to validate input of unicast self-IPs, and issue a TMSH warning and log a message if a unicast address is configured that does not have the correct allow-service attribute. "Unicast IP address x.x.x.x does not allow service on UDP port xxxx, network failover may not work."

bugs.title: Unknown/Undefined OPSWAT ID show up as 'Any' in APM Visual Policy Editor
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from OPSWAT SDK V3 to V4, opening Access Policy in VPE if one of the opswat checker (e.g. Anti-Virus checker) contains an Undefined (i.e. previously defined but out of support) ID it will display as "Any." The correct display should be "Unsupported" or "Invalid" product.
bugs.conditions: Wrongful information displayed.
bugs.impact: Wrongful information displayed.
bugs.fix: Correct (*** Invalid ***) information displayed.

bugs.title: No event triggered when the system receives a certificate message from the server.
bugs.symptoms: There is no event triggered when the system receives a certificate message from the server.
bugs.conditions: System receives a certificate message from the server.
bugs.impact: No event triggered.
bugs.fix: A new event SERVERSSL_SERVERCERT is raised after the server certificate is received and verified on the server side.
bugs.behavior: A new event SERVERSSL_SERVERCERT is raised after the server certificate is received and verified.

bugs.title: mkdisk utility fails if the USB device has a GUID partition table
bugs.symptoms: 'mkdisk' utility will fail under some circumstances, exiting with : Failed to add partition: Invalid argument Leaving
bugs.conditions: -- hosting system has 'sfdisk' version 2.26 or above -- USB device has a GUID partition table
bugs.impact: USB device formatting cannot proceed
bugs.workaround: convert the USB device partition table from GPT to MBR before using 'mkdisk' for example, use 'diskpart' in a Windows shell. run two commands on the disk: -- clean -- convert mbr Then use 'mkdisk' as usual.

bugs.title: qkview may cause tmm to restart or may take 30 or more minutes to run
bugs.symptoms: When taking a qkview on a heavily loaded BIG-IP device (with lots of connections) running 12.1.0 or 12.1.1, the qkview utility may take a very long time to complete (30+ minutes) or cause tmm to restart. This is due to a new qkview command that was added to gather a list of recent connections with the tmsh show sys connection command, which has a significant performance impact when run while the BIG-IP is heavily loaded.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on the following versions: - 12.1.0 including 12.1.0 HF1 and 12.1.0 HF2 - 12.1.1 including 12.1.1 HF1 This can occur when the BIG-IP is heavily loaded and while running the qkview command.
bugs.impact: Qkview command can take an exceedingly long time to run (30+ minutes). Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not run the qkview command if the device is heavily loaded.
bugs.fix: Removed offending "show sys connection" command from qkview utility.

bugs.title: Access Profile copying might end up in invalid way if series of names.
bugs.symptoms: After copying an access policy, you receive an error when trying to open the copy: "Unable to load accessPolicy '/Common/my_policy_access_1_1' from source."
bugs.conditions: When items with names ending with _#_#_1 and _#_#_2, _# reduction is working.
bugs.impact: Unable to copy policy properly.
bugs.workaround: Export policy, import with reuse.
bugs.fix: Copying is fixed for this conditions.

bugs.title: IE browser fails to establish VPN and throws error "Failed to initialize local Tunnel Server" sporadically
bugs.symptoms: IE browser fails to establish VPN with error "Failed to initialize local Tunnel Server" sporadically because of a race condition in the code.
bugs.conditions: IE, network access with DTLS connection, tunnel server
bugs.impact: IE cannot be established 100% of the times

bugs.title: Some mass storage is left un-used
bugs.symptoms: It is intended that all mass storage capacity be available for use by application data, site-local configuration, or sofwtare. In some conditions, about 10% of the mass storage capacity is not made available for application data.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the BIG-IP i-Series platforms.
bugs.impact: Applications that use a lot of storage may not function optimally.
bugs.fix: The storage is optimally reallocated.

bugs.title: iRules LX - Debug mode does not function in dedicated mode
bugs.symptoms: In case if the debug option is enabled in the dedicated mode, sometimes some of the nodejs process can be allocated a "in-use" port, which prevents it from starting successfully. By design every process is guaranteed a debug port in the configured range as long as there are enough ports available in the system. In-use ports are skipped, so consecutive port allocation is not guaranteed.
bugs.conditions: some of the ports in the range are busy.
bugs.impact: Some of the nodejs processes fail to start which prevents normal iRuleLX operation.
bugs.workaround: Consult with netstat output and set the debug-port-range-low to a higher value (eg. 10000+) to minimise the change of a port conflict.

bugs.title: iRules LX data not included in qkview
bugs.symptoms: Qkview does not contain any of the iRuleLX information.
bugs.impact: Support engineers will have to ask for the iRuleLX information separately. No iHealth heuristics possible at the moment.
bugs.fix: The following ILX information was added to the qkview: TMSH commands: list ilx workspace all-properties list ilx plugin all-properties list ilx global-settings (13.0.0+) list ltm profile ilx all-properties (13.0.0+) show ilx plugin all show ltm profile ilx all (13.0.0+) The files in the following folders: /var/ilx - master copies of workspaces /var/sdm - running files of the plugins /var/log/ilx - ILX specific logs

bugs.title: Minification is not applied to HTML when configured
bugs.symptoms: AAM policy has an option to minify JavaScript, CSS, and HTML content. When this option is turned on for a policy node matching HTML responses, BIG-IP no longer minifies the content.
bugs.conditions: AAM module is enabled and a virtual server has web acceleration profile with an AAM policy where HTML minification is enabled.
bugs.impact: Optimization for HTML content minification is not applied. Thus the size of a resulting response may be less optimal.

bugs.title: artificial low route mtu can cause SIGSEV core from monitor traffic
bugs.symptoms: When configuring a monitor instance targeting an address reachable via a route with an artificially low route mtu, tmm can crash repeatedly.
bugs.conditions: see above
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: configure correct MTU

bugs.title: Irrelevant fields visible in Logging profile
bugs.symptoms: When switching from logging format 'BIGIQ' to logging format 'Key-Value Pairs' in Application Security logging profiles, 'Maximum Request Size' and 'Maximum Query String Size' properties are not removed.
bugs.conditions: Switch from logging format 'BIGIQ' to logging format 'Key-Value Pairs' in Application Security logging profiles.
bugs.impact: Irrelevant fields visible.

bugs.title: TMM may core under certain conditions when APM is provisioned and access profile is attached to the virtual.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core under certain conditions when APM is provisioned and access profile is attached to the virtual.
bugs.conditions: APM is provisioned and access profile is attached to the virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Correctly handle session DB data in APM to prevent memory segmentation fault.

bugs.title: bigd may falsely complain of a file descriptor leak when it cannot open its debug log file
bugs.symptoms: - On 11.6.1, bigd will report erroneously mark pool members down and messags similar to the following will be seen in the ltm log file: Sep 23 10:45:59 bipve1 warning bigd[7413]: 01060154:4: Bigd PID 7413 throttling monitor instance probe because file descriptor limit 65436 reached. - On 12.1.x, this bug has negligible impact.
bugs.conditions: Monitoring must be in use, bigd debug logging must be enabled, and the bigd debug log file (/var/log/bigdlog) must be full.
bugs.impact: - On 11.6.1 this can cause bigd to stop monitoring, resulting in pool members being marked down erroneously. - In 12.1.x, some of the underlying logging code changed and there is no real impact.
bugs.workaround: You can rotate the log file, using the following command: logrotate -f bigdlog
bugs.fix: Stopped bigd from thinking it was out of file descriptors when it was unable to open its debug log file.

bugs.title: ClientSSL profile could incorrectly inherit cert-key-chain objects from parent profile
bugs.symptoms: Child clientSSL profile continues to inherit the cert-key-chain objects from parent clientSSL profile when it shouldn't.
bugs.conditions: Create a clientSSL profile is created by having cert/key field as defaults from parent profile, with a change in chain field. Make sure that no new cert-key-chain objects are added to the child profile. In this case, since chain field is changed, the child profile shouldn't inherit any cert-kay-chain objects from the parent, but it does.
bugs.impact: Child clientSSL profile continues to inherit the cert-key-chain objects from parent clientSSL profile when it shouldn't.

bugs.title: Duplicate SQL monitors updating pool member status incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: If you have two identical SQL monitors, this can cause pool members to be incorrectly marked down.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you have more than 1 identical SQL monitor for a pool.
bugs.impact: Pool members may be incorrectly marked down.
bugs.workaround: Ensure you only have one SQL monitor associated with a pool.

bugs.title: Sometimes f5fpc cannot establish Network Access connection and incorrectly reports 'Session timed out' error
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes f5fpc cannot establish Network Access connection. Successfully established Network Access connection and subsequent login retries will fail with 'Session timed out' error.
bugs.conditions: This intermittent issue might occur after there has been a successfully established Network Access connection, and a user retries to login once or multiple times.
bugs.impact: Network Access cannot be established and 'Session timed out' error is presented to the user.
bugs.workaround: 1) Find all processes with regex f5std, svpn and manually kill them. 2) Restart host OS.

bugs.title: In rare cases VDI plugin might leak memory or crash while processing client connections
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases VDI plugin might leak memory or crash while processing client connections.
bugs.conditions: APM is used for proxying VDI connections (e.g. Citrix Virtual Apps, VMware Horizon, MS RDP).
bugs.impact: Rarely, VDI plugin might leak memory or crash.
bugs.fix: Fixed rare VDI plugin memory leaks and crashes.

bugs.title: JavaScript challenge repeating in loop on Firefox when URL is longer than 1033 characters
bugs.symptoms: The JavaScript challenge is repeating in a loop on Firefox on URLs which are longer than 1033 characters. The request never reaches the back-end server. This happens in the following challenges: * Proactive Bot Defense with Suspicious Browsers enabled * Client-Side Integrity Defense In the rest of the challenges, the challenges will succeed, but POST requests will not be reconstructed correctly and sent as a multipart message to the back-end server.
bugs.conditions: URLs are longer than 1033 characters, AND: Users are using the Firefox browser, AND: Either: * Proactive Bot Defense with Suspicious Browsers enabled, OR * Client-Side Integrity Defense is enabled and is used as a DoSL7 mitigation during an attack.
bugs.impact: Requests to URLs longer than 1033 will be blocked on Firefox, and the browser will repeat the challenge in a loop.
bugs.fix: The JavaScript challenge no longer gets stuck in a loop on Firefox, on URLs which are longer than 1033 characters.

bugs.title: Bogus ICMP unreachable messages in PEM with ipother profile in use
bugs.symptoms: The ipother virtual server will send bogus ICMP unreachable messages caused by incorrect error handling in the PEM filter.
bugs.conditions: A VS with ipother profile configured together with the PEM profile. In the field defect the additional piece needed was the missing classification, but this is due to code ordering, so in non-fixed versions this can also happen with the classification profile present.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary ICMP traffic
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue related to unnecessary ICMP traffic in the PEM filter.

bugs.title: Web Scraping session_opening_anomaly reports the wrong route domain for the source IP
bugs.symptoms: When generating a web scraping attack of session opening anomaly type, there is an attack start/end event shown in the /var/log/asm and GUI: Security :: Event Logs : Application : Web Scraping Statistics. The event has a "source ip" field which should come along with the route domain. In the case of "session opening anomaly" the route domain is always zero. (For example: 127.0.0.1%0). Even there is a non-zero route domain configured.
bugs.conditions: Route domain is configured and a web scraping attack event triggers.
bugs.impact: Incorrect route domain field is shown in the GUI and /var/log/asm.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic error. The system uses the correct route domain
bugs.fix: The fix is to set the correct route domain for the "session opening anomaly" events shown in the GUI and /var/log/asm

bugs.title: Some Social Security Numbers are not being masked
bugs.symptoms: ASM does not block or mask some SSN numbers.
bugs.conditions: The Data Guard feature is turned on and set to Block, Alarm or Mask. The responses contains social security numbers with specific ranges.
bugs.impact: The traffic passes neither masked nor blocked to the end client.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly masks and/or blocks all relevant social security numbers.

bugs.title: Improve the detection of malicious browsers
bugs.symptoms: Some malicious browsers are not always detected.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.
bugs.impact: Some malicious browsers are not detected and not reported in the logs.
bugs.fix: Improved the detection of malicious browsers.

bugs.title: Route updates during IPsec tunnel setup can cause tmm to restart
bugs.symptoms: During the setup of IPsec tunnel flows, tmm depends on a valid route being available towards a remote peer to correctly create the IPsec inbound tunnel flows. The absence of the route at this stage, causes tmm to crash and restart. This is more likely to happen if the route towards the endpoint is dynamic.
bugs.conditions: IPsec tunnels are being set up with a given remote peer and the route towards that peer is not reliably present (as is in the case of dynamic route updates)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that there is always a valid route towards each of the remote peers.
bugs.fix: The tmm process no longer restarts if there is no valid route towards the remote peer during IPsec tunnel setup.

bugs.title: Behavior when using VLAN-Group and STP
bugs.symptoms: May not see ICMP response traffic when using Ping within the same VLAN when STP mode is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- STP mode is configured. -- Ping is issued in the same VLAN. Note: This issue is a constraint to soft switched platforms.
bugs.impact: May not see ICMP response traffic.

bugs.title: Clicking the policies list tab does not refresh the policies list on click.
bugs.symptoms: Clicking the policies list tab does not refresh the policies list on click.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the policy list page
bugs.impact: If the policy list changed, the updates will not be displayed.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the browser or click the menu Local Traffic > Policy List in order to refresh the page

bugs.title: PCCD memory usage increases on configuration changes and recompilation due to small amount of memory leak on each compilation
bugs.symptoms: Each time the Packet Classification Compiler Daemon (PCCD) process recompiles rules due to configuration changes, it loses approximately 20 bytes or more (depends on the rule complexity) due to small memory leak.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when making changes to the firewall configuration when AFM is configured.
bugs.impact: This can potentially lead to an out-of-memory situation if the system runs for a long time without reboot and PCCD continuously recompiles due to frequent configuration changes.
bugs.fix: The PCCD memory leak was identified and fixed.

bugs.title: tmm core while installing Safenet 6.2 client
bugs.symptoms: tmm core while installing Safenet 6.2 client.
bugs.conditions: Safenet 6.2 client installation
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm core related to Safenet 6.2 client installation.

bugs.title: AVR statistic is not save during the upgrade process
bugs.symptoms: All AVR statistics will be lost after upgrade from 12.1.0 or 12.1.1.
bugs.conditions: AVR statistic was collected on 12.1.0 or 12.1.1. The BIG-IP was upgraded.
bugs.impact: Old AVR statistics will be lost
bugs.workaround: 1. before upgrade edit the following file: ./usr/libdata/configsync/avr_save_pre 2. change the following line " [ $(is_provisioned avr) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned pem) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned afm) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned swg) -eq 1 $(is_provisioned asm) -eq 1 ] && " with " [ $(is_provisioned avr) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned pem) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned afm) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned swg) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned asm) -eq 1 ] && "
bugs.fix: AVR upgrade script fixed

bugs.title: Certificate objects are not properly imported from external SAML SP metadata when metadata contains both signing and encryption certificates
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP supports import of external SAML SP metadata to create SP-Connector objects. When such metadata file contains two certificates (one with 'signing' and one with 'encryption use) then BIG-IP will import certificate that is positioned 'second' in metadata twice.
bugs.conditions: Imported metadata contains two certificates with different use types: 'signing' and 'encryption'
bugs.impact: There is no impact if in metadata signing and encryption certificates are the same. If certificates are different - SAML SSO may not function properly due to incorrect certificate imported in configuration.
bugs.workaround: Import certificates manually, and assign them to created from metadata SAML SP connector
bugs.fix: Issue is now fixed: both certificates are imported correctly.

bugs.title: IPSEC + chassis behavior for case secondary blades on-off switch.
bugs.symptoms: After cmp_state change (secondary blade restart), some flows will fail
bugs.conditions: Adding-removing blades causes DAG flow redistribution and redistribution IKE/IPSEC SA's and IPSEC data flows between existing blades. It makes some flows interrupted and IPSEC peer disconnect.
bugs.impact: Some users may lose their connections and have difficulty restoring them.
bugs.fix: On HW configuration change BIG-IP need: 1. Graciously close affected IPSEC tunnels. 2. Update all involved IPSEC peers 3. Be ready to create the new tunnels upon requests.
bugs.behavior: Expected behavior: All IPSEC tunnels should be shutdown and restarted upon request.

bugs.title: Changing type on external data-group may cause issues with iRule
bugs.symptoms: When the type is changed on external data-group the iRule may improperly read the contents leading to iRule issues.
bugs.conditions: Type changed when re-loading external data-group.
bugs.impact: iRule issues while using contents of external data-group.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM (e.g., bigstart restart tmm). This will impact traffic running through the system so it is advised to perform this step during maintenance window.

bugs.title: Reduction in boot time in BIG-IP Virtual Edition platforms
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) version has experienced increased boot time.
bugs.conditions: The increased boot time occurs each time a VE is booted.
bugs.impact: Long boot time, longer than previous releases.
bugs.fix: Reduction in boot time in BIG-IP Virtual Edition platforms.

bugs.title: OneConnect with verified accept issues
bugs.symptoms: System may experience an outage.
bugs.conditions: Verified Accept enabled in TCP profile hardware syncookies enabled OneConnect profile on VIP Syncookie threshold crossed
bugs.impact: System outage.
bugs.workaround: Disabled verified accept when used with OneConnect on a VIP.
bugs.fix: Verified accept, OneConnect and hardware syncookies work correctly together.

bugs.title: iControl REST slow performace on GET request for virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Performing a GET request on a BIG-IP with a large number of virtual servers may result in slow performance and timeout errors.
bugs.conditions: When a significant number of virtual servers reference persistence profiles.
bugs.impact: Unable to perform large GET query on virtual servers.
bugs.fix: Improved iControl REST performance for Performing a GET request on a BIG-IP with a large number persistence profiles on virtual servers.

bugs.title: 'General Database Error' while changing the Admin UI authentication type
bugs.symptoms: Failed to choose Authentication type from Local to other BIG-IP-supported authentication type.
bugs.conditions: -- User Directory is Remote - APM Based. -- Authentication Type is RADIUS, AD, LDAP or TACACS+. -- All needed information about the AAA Server is specified.
bugs.impact: GUI error: 'General Database Error'.

bugs.title: Slow to delete URLs, CPU spikes with Automatic Policy Builder
bugs.symptoms: Deleting a URL causes an incorrect event to be generated and logged for every other URL in the Policy. When a policy has many URLs configured, deleting a URL takes a long time and consumes heavy CPU time.
bugs.conditions: Many URLs are configured in the Policy. This can be due to Policy Builder being set to "Always" learn new HTTP URLs. If Policy Builder is also configured to collapse common URLs to wildcards, then it deletes the collapsed urls and these calls can be resource intensive.
bugs.impact: 1) GUI is slow to delete URLs 2) Misleading (incorrect) logs are present in the audit log for each other URL in the system after a URL delete. 3) CPU can spike to 100%
bugs.workaround: A) Change "Learn New HTTP URLs" mode to "Selective" from "Always" B) Disable collapse URLS.
bugs.fix: URL delete no longer incorrectly generates an event for every other URL in the system.

bugs.title: iRule DNS request with trailing dot times out with empty response
bugs.symptoms: The DNS request takes about 20 seconds to respond and the response is empty.
bugs.conditions: An iRule uses RESOLV::lookup or NAME::lookup to resolve a domain name that ends with a dot.
bugs.impact: The request does not properly resolve to an IP address.
bugs.workaround: Strip the trailing dot from the domain name before calling RESOLV::lookup or NAME::lookup.
bugs.fix: Domain names with trailing dots are properly resolved from iRules. The trailing dot is stripped when the request is saved to later match with the response.

bugs.title: Two Delete buttons for records and main delete. Edit and Delete buttons are enabled when no record selected.
bugs.symptoms: There are two Delete buttons on the page. One Delete button is for the records and one for the overall Data Group.
bugs.conditions: The Data Group page had two "Delete" buttons, which causes confusion.
bugs.impact: Button confusion might result in clicking the incorrect button.
bugs.workaround: There is a confirmation message when deleting the Data Group. User must consider the warning before proceeding.
bugs.fix: Relabeled the buttons to "Delete Records" and "Delete Data Group". Also, disabled the Edit and Delete Records buttons until a record is selected.

bugs.title: [FIPS] High CPU usage (11.5.4) or memory error messages (11.6.1) during stress test using FIPS keys
bugs.symptoms: When running a stress test (for example, using Apache Bench tool) to aggressively connect virtual server whose clientSSL profile is using FIPS key; in 11.5.4, you may observe high CPU usage by using "top" command on the system and "Clock advanced" messages in the ltm logs; in 11.6.1, the above symptoms appeared in 11.5.4 are not seen, but ltm log prints a sequence of ERR_MEMORY_ALLOC_FAILURE at the beginning of the stress test.
bugs.conditions: 1. The connection to the virtual server is using a clientSSL profile whose SSL key is a FIPS key. 2. The connection that uses the FIPS key is triggered very frequently (such as in a stress test). For example, from the client side, it runs this Apache Bench command "ab -c 1000 -n 1000000 https://10.10.10.100/" to test the virtual server.
bugs.impact: When the connections occupy too much of the CPU's resource, it could impact the performance of other tasks of the system.
bugs.workaround: When this issue occurs, you can try to mitigate it by any methods that restricts FIPS key usage in the SSL connection, for example, do not configure the clientSSL profile with the FIPS key as the default clientSSL profile of the virtual server, and add more non-FIPS clientSSL profiles to the virtual server, so that the connections are not always handled by the FIPS key.

bugs.title: Returning to main menu from "RSS Feed" breaks ribbon
bugs.symptoms: When you go to "RSS Feed" configuration page for Document, Picture Library, List etc. and go back to SharePoint Dashboard using link at the top pointing to "RSS FEED for ..." and then click any option on the ribbon, you got "500 Internal Server Error" and ribbon stops working. When you use built-in browser button "go back" instead, everything works Ok.
bugs.conditions: "500 Internal Server Error" occurred. Ribbon stop working.
bugs.impact: Ribbon stop working.
bugs.workaround: Use built-in browser "go back" button instead.
bugs.fix: Returning to main menu from "RSS FEED for ...", ribbon continue to work. No more "500 Internal Server Error".

bugs.title: Web GUI keeps showing loader while updating security banner text
bugs.symptoms: When clicking Update after making changes in System :: Preferences, GUI may keep showing "Loading..." banner indefinitely. This is cosmetic: The changes are saved, and can be verified after refreshing the page.
bugs.conditions: Clicking Update after making changes to system preferences.
bugs.impact: No impact on functionality. The changes are saved. This is cosmetic.
bugs.workaround: Refreshing the page shows updated values.

bugs.title: LCD shows error screen on boot or after license expires
bugs.symptoms: The LCD on BIG-IP iSeries appliances may display an error screen.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if the appliance has just finished booting, or if the license has just expired.
bugs.impact: This may cause an unexpected error and subsequent navigation back to the LCD splash page.
bugs.workaround: Wait one minute and try to navigate the LCD screens again. If the system has already been licensed and is in the 'Active' state, subsequent attempts should work.
bugs.fix: The LCD on BIG-IP iSeries appliances no longer displays an error screen just after boot or license expiration.

bugs.title: TMM out of memory causes core in DNS cache
bugs.symptoms: The TMM crashes and service is lost until it restarts. You may see several "aggressive mode sweeper" messages in /var/log/ltm prior to the crash.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when the TMM memory is exhausted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Provision sufficient memory for the TMM or reduce load.
bugs.fix: The fix was to properly handle the failure allocating memory.

bugs.title: TMM hardware accelerated compression not registering for all compression levels.
bugs.symptoms: DEFLATE/gzip/zlib compression levels other than level 1 were bypassing the hardware accelerator and being serviced in software, resulting in higher CPU utilization and slower compression times.
bugs.conditions: Compression requests for DEFLATE/gzip/zlib levels other than level 1.
bugs.impact: Compression requests serviced by software are scheduled on local CPUs. During heavy compression traffic, overall system traffic flow may be reduced. Compression requests serviced in software may take significantly longer to complete.
bugs.fix: Hardware accelerator correctly registers for all DEFLATE/gzip/zlib compression levels, not just level 1.

bugs.title: Workaround for Software Installation Failures in TMUI
bugs.symptoms: A software installation fails for one of several reasons (unsupported software versions, lack of disk space, etc). This failure leaves the software volume in a state where future installations cannot be completed.
bugs.conditions: Software installation fails.
bugs.impact: You cannot install software on the failed volume. You will see "Previous installation not complete" message if you attempt to install software on this failed volume.
bugs.workaround: 1. Installation fails. 2. Navigate to System >> Disk Management. Click on HD1 (for example) 3. Under Contained Software Volumes, you can see the reason for failure on the failed volume. 4. Select the failed volume and click Delete. Confirm you want to delete the failed volume. 5. Once the volume is deleted successfully, return to System >> Software Management : Image List 6. Select a valid image and click the Install button. 7. Under Volume Set Name enter a valid name and click the Install button.

bugs.title: Edge browser prompts user to install f5-vpn from Windows Store
bugs.symptoms: When there are no components installed and user launches Network Access resource using Edge browser, Edge browser prompts user to install f5-vpn from Windows Store. This is confusing because there is no f5-vpn application in the Microsoft Store.
bugs.conditions: - No recent F5 Networks client components installed on the system. - APM configured. - Edge Browser is used.
bugs.impact: Potential confusion, which might generate support calls.
bugs.workaround: Have end users dismiss this dialog box and follow the prompts in the browser to download and install F5 client components.

bugs.title: Browser may hang at APM session logout
bugs.symptoms: Browser hangs at logout from APM session with RDP client and/or VMware View client.
bugs.conditions: - APM Virtual server with RDP client and/or VMware View client on webtop; - active session on this webtop with opened client.
bugs.impact: Logout from APM session may take a long time (several minutes). In some cases, it may be necessary to restart browser.
bugs.fix: Now browser does not hangs at logout from APM session with RDP client and/or VMvare View client.

bugs.title: Scripts on rewritten pages could fail with JavaScript exception if application code modifies window.self
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to call some JavaScript methods (such as XMLHttpRequest.open) on a page accessed through Portal Access could fail if application modifies window.self builtin object. As a result, the application will stop working and optionally log an undefined variable/reference exception into Developer Tools console. To verify that window.self is modified, run 'window.self == window' command in Developer Tools console of the page with error and check if it returns 'false'.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if a web application has javascript that modifies the value of window.self.
bugs.impact: Affected web-applications will not work when accessed through Portal Access.
bugs.fix: Scripts on pages accessed through Portal Access are no longer failing when web application code modifies window.self.

bugs.title: Inconsistencies in Automatic sync ASM Device Group
bugs.symptoms: Some ASM calls are not propagated correctly across an automatic sync device group.
bugs.conditions: Automatic Sync is configured for a Device Group with ASM enabled.
bugs.impact: This can cause any of the following depending on the change: -- Superfluous full sync operations. -- Updating the wrong element on the remote devices. -- Missing changes on the remote devices.
bugs.workaround: Disable automatic sync on the device group, and periodically push changes manually.
bugs.fix: Calls are correctly propagated across Automatic sync Device Groups with ASM enabled.

bugs.title: TMM may accumulate internal events resulting in TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: Under some uncommon circumstances, long-lived connections may cause internal events to be accumulated causing excessive memory usage potentially resulting in TMM restarting.
bugs.conditions: HTTP virtual with long-lived connections.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: The issue can be mitigated by setting the HTTP 'max-requests' profile option to a reasonably low value - this value will depend on application requirements.
bugs.fix: Internal events are no longer accumulated thus avoiding low memory conditions.

bugs.title: Provisioning page table cells overlap
bugs.symptoms: Cells in the provisioning page table overlap when they contain long strings.
bugs.conditions: Cells in the provisioning page table contain long strings.
bugs.impact: The cells will overlap.
bugs.fix: Cells in the provisioning page table no longer overlap when they contain long strings.

bugs.title: Unhelpful log message 'internal_cause' when the session is deleted due to accessing the root URI
bugs.symptoms: APM end users that are logged into an assigned webtop that open a new browser tab or new browser window, or otherwise visit '/' (the root URI), the existing session is deleted and a new one is created. The system posts a relatively ambiguous error message in /var/log/apm: notice tmm[20481]: 01490567:5: /Common/rdp_access:Common:9494c15a: Session deleted (internal_cause).
bugs.conditions: -- APM with full webtop assigned. -- Client visits the '/' URL.
bugs.impact: -- Previous session is halted and a new session is begun. -- Unhelpful and confusing log message.
bugs.fix: Log message now reads 'Session deleted (restarted)'. When you see this message, it indicates that the previous session was deleted and a new session started because the APM end user accessed the root URI when there was a webtop assigned to that APM end user. This might occur when the APM end user with the assigned webtop opens a new browser tab or new browser window, or otherwise visits '/' (the root URI).

bugs.title: Terminating of HTTP2 connection may cause a TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when an HTTP2 connection is being terminating on client and server sides concurrently.
bugs.conditions: HTTP2 profile is configured and assigned to a virtual. A client SSL profile is also used on the same virtual. Client interrupting a connection as well as server is also terminating a connection at the same time.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: A fix stops HTTP2 from further processing when a connection is terminating preventing TMM crash for this reason.

bugs.title: Allow Local DNS Servers is not honored on Mac OS X
bugs.symptoms: In some cases of split tunnel local DNS resolution on client does not work. Its "emulated" full tunnel mode i.e. split tunnel and IPv4 LAN address space of 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 and don't allow local subnet access.
bugs.conditions: Configure Allow Local DNS Servers is not honored on Mac OS X. Configure split tunnel and IPv4 LAN address space of 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0. Disable local subnet access. System has only one physical adapter (ethernet or wifi) available for networking.
bugs.impact: DNS resolution fails for some split tunnel deployment cases.
bugs.workaround: Specify "*" in DNS included address space to forward all DNS traffic over the tunnel.
bugs.fix: Allow local DNS configuration is honored on Mac OS X now.
bugs.behavior: Allow local DNS configuration is honored on Mac OS X now.

bugs.title: rate_limit can affect to iClient connectivity
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes iClient (using iSession) can't connect to server. In TMM log: iSession: Connection error: isession_handle_syn:3630: No peer
bugs.conditions: If a rate limit is set for an iClient virtual (with iSession defined) it can sometimes prevent iClient from connecting.
bugs.impact: iClient randomly can't connect
bugs.workaround: remove rate limit from virtual
bugs.fix: avoid rate_limit check for iSession control connection.

bugs.title: tmsh appears to allow password change for internal lcd admin user
bugs.symptoms: The 'tmsh modify auth password' command appears to allow the password to be changed for the f5hubblelcdadmin user.
bugs.conditions: Using the 'modify auth password' command under tmsh, and manually specifying the 'f5hubblelcdadmin' user (which does not appear among the list of available users, such as via tab-completion).
bugs.impact: This operation appears to succeed, but has no actual effect on BIG-IP operations. This is an internal user account which provides the context for communication with the lcd front panel display on newer BIG-IP appliances. Changing the stored password for this user account does not affect these operations.
bugs.fix: Removed the appearance of the ability to change the password for the internal lcd admin user.

bugs.title: GUI gives error when clicking "Update" making changes to VS in Security-Policies
bugs.symptoms: GUI times out and generates an error when ASM policy takes longer time to update (in Virtual Server Security page)
bugs.conditions: When the same ASM policy is attached to hundreds of virtual servers, it takes longer to update.
bugs.impact: GUI times out before the changes are saved. Users will be able to see the updated changes only after refreshing the page.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the page in the browser once the error shows up.
bugs.fix: GUI doesn't time out when ASM policy is updated.

bugs.title: iSession causes routing entry to be prematurely freed
bugs.symptoms: iSession may cause TMM to prematurely free a routing entry resulting in memory corruption and TMM restarting.
bugs.conditions: iSession-enabled virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: No reasonable workaround short of not using iSession functionality.
bugs.fix: iSession no longer causes routing entries to be prematurely freed.

bugs.title: Machine Cert OCSP check fails with multiple Issuer CA
bugs.symptoms: If there are multiple CAs in the CA bundle and issuing CA is not first in it, the OCSP responder returns "unauthorized" response.
bugs.conditions: This can only happen when issuing CA is not first in the CA file.
bugs.impact: OSCP check in machine cert will fail and user won't be able to follow successful branch in Access Policy. This might result in Authentication failure even though the machine cert is valid.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule Event and variable Assign agent in between Machine Cert and OCSP Auth agent. Follow these steps: iRule: 1) Loop through the CA bundle until you find matching issuer cert 2) Set this new issuer cert to "session.check_machinecert.last.cert.issuer.cert" Variable Assign: 3) Read this issuer cert from the session db and assign it back to the same session variable: session.check_machinecert.last.cert.issuer.cert = expr { [mcget -nocache {session.check_machinecert.last.cert.issuer.cert}] }
bugs.fix: Issuer cert is now looked up and set properly from the CA bundle. So there is no longer any failure response from OCSP responder.

bugs.title: Packet leak if reject command is used in FLOW_INIT rule
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory usage (packets) increases steadily over time.
bugs.conditions: 'reject' command is used in a FLOW_INIT rule
bugs.impact: Packet leak over time will consume TMM memory.
bugs.workaround: Do not use reject command in FLOW_INIT iRule

bugs.title: In rare cases, TMM will enter an infinite loop and be killed by sod when the system has TCP virtual servers with verified-accept enabled.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a SIGABRT (killed by sod)
bugs.conditions: TCP (full proxy) virtual servers with verified-accept enabled in the TCP profiles, that must be handling traffic. This issue occurs extremely rarely.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: disable verify accept.
bugs.fix: the loop is fixed.

bugs.title: Duplicate entry for bigipPb200 in F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB
bugs.symptoms: Duplicate error when loading F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB into the SNMP manager.
bugs.conditions: Loading F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB into the SNMP manager.
bugs.impact: F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB fails to load into the SNMP manager.
bugs.workaround: Changing bigipPb200 OBJECT IDENTIFIER ::= { sysDeviceModelOIDs 19 } to bigipViprion4 OBJECT IDENTIFIER ::= { sysDeviceModelOIDs 19 } in the F5-BIG-IP-SYSTEM-MIB.

bugs.title: BigIP upgrading doesn't carry over Thales configuration on the secondary slot
bugs.symptoms: After BIG-IP upgrading in the multi-blade platform configured with Thales, the secondary platform fails to carry over Thales configuration. When running enquiry at primary slot, you will get response about Thales config. At secondary slot, you will not be able to run "enquiry".
bugs.conditions: Thales installed on chassis.
bugs.impact: Secondary slot doesn't have Thales HSM configured.
bugs.workaround: Wait for csynced finish syncing /shared/nfast from primary slot to the secondary slot. Then run "clsh bigstart restart pkcs11d". While waiting, run this command to compare the folder size of /shared/nfast/. [root@localhost:/S1-green-P:Active:Standalone] config # clsh "du -sh /shared/nfast/" === slot 2 addr 127.3.0.2 color green === 220M /shared/nfast/ === slot 3 addr 127.3.0.3 color red === === slot 4 addr 127.3.0.4 color blue === === slot 1 addr 127.3.0.1 color green === 220M /shared/nfast/ Another workaround(maybe faster) is to reinstall Thales after upgrading. Csyncd could take 10+ minutes to finish sync'ing. A third workaround is to scp /shared/nfast/ from primary slot to secondary slot. After that, run "bigstart restart pkcs11d" e.g., [root@localhost:/S1-green-P:Active:Standalone]scp -r /shared/nfast/ slot2:/shared/

bugs.title: Secure Vault: Key cleanup for 5000- and 7000-series platforms
bugs.symptoms: Outdated and unused unit key is left on 5000- and 7000-series platforms after upgrade from an older version to v13.0.0.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on 5000- and 7000-series platforms. -- Upgrading from a version earlier than v13.0.0 to v13.0.0.
bugs.impact: 1) Unit key on disk is preferred over unit key in hardware. 2) Potential config load failures when upgrading from pre-v13.0.0 to v13.0.0, or installing v13.0.0 hotfixes on these devices.
bugs.workaround: NOTE: Impacts only 5000- and 7000-series platforms. On or before upgrade to v13.0.0 or its associated hotfixes, perform the following procedure: 1) Set master key to a known value: modify sys crypto master-key prompt-for-password 2) Save config: tmsh save sys config 3) Remove the old unit key: rm /config/bigip/kstore/.unitkey 4) Load config: tmsh load sys config 5) Save config: tmsh save sys config
bugs.fix: Unit key is no longer left on 5000- and 7000-series platforms after upgrade from an older version.

bugs.title: HTTP iRule commands could lead to WEBSSO plugin being invoked
bugs.symptoms: With SSO logs set to 'Debug' in Access log configuration, the following log messages are seen in '/var/log/apm': Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt debug websso.3[14520]: 014d0001:7: constructor Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt debug websso.3[14520]: 014d0001:7: webssoContext constructor ... Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt err websso.3[14520]: 014d0005:3: Unsupported SSO Method Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt debug websso.3[14520]: 014d0001:7: ctx: 0x914b510, SERVER: TMEVT_REQUEST Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt debug websso.3[14520]: 014d0001:7: ctx: 0x914a718, CLIENT: TMEVT_ABORT_PROXY Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt debug websso.3[14520]: 014d0001:7: webssoContext destructor ... Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt debug websso.3[14520]: 014d0001:7: webssoConfig destructor With 'rstcause' enabled, the following log message is seen in '/var/log/ltm': Sep 30 12:46:17 bigip3900mgmt err tmm2[13116]: 01230140:3: RST sent from 172.17.90.92:57611 to 127.0.0.1:10001, [0x24ccbbc:820] Internal error (APM::WEBSSO requested abort (Unsupported SSO Method))
bugs.conditions: HTTP::disable followed by HTTP::enable. when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { HTTP::disable // do some other stuff HTTP::enable }
bugs.impact: client receives a HTTP 503 reset
bugs.workaround: When the access profile is added to the virtual server, the websso plugin profile is automatically added. Manually removing the websso plugin fixes this bug.
bugs.fix: The server-side access hudfilter was mistakenly enabling the websso plugin. The logic has been updated so that this does not happen.

bugs.title: Thales HSM in HA with Failure can cause key creation delay for over 1 minute
bugs.symptoms: When an HSM goes offline in an HA HSM configuration, the switchover to the other HSM will not occur immediately. After the failover timeout, the switchover will occur, but in the meantime SSL handshakes will fail.
bugs.conditions: Whenever there is a disruption to a Thales HSM configured in HA with at least one other HSM.
bugs.impact: SSL handshakes fail between when the HSM goes down and when the failover timeout occurs.
bugs.workaround: Lower the relevant settings in /opt/nfast/kmdata/config/config file. The Thales User Guide has a detailed explanation of what each of the settings does. Thales recommends that in a production setup, unless there is a solid reason to modify these settings, they recommend that it is best to use the default values. Here are two example configs with lower timeouts: Very tight settings [server_settings] connect_retry=1 connect_keepalive=10 connect_broken=1 connect_command_block=0 Please note that this can cause a module to be marked as failed when there is just a short network glitch from which it may well recover. More relaxed settings [server_settings] connect_retry=3 connect_keepalive=4 connect_broken=10 connect_command_block=15 Following is more detailed information: In order to limit the time where SSL connections will fail, edit the Thales config settings in /opt/nfast/kmdata/config/config. The relevant settings are -- connect_retry: This field specifies the number of seconds to wait before retrying a remote connection to a client hardserver. The default is 10. -- connect_broken: This field specifies the number of seconds of inactivity allowed before a connection to a client hardserver is declared broken. The default is 90. -- connect_keepalive: This field specifies the number of seconds between keepalive packets for remote connections to a client hardserver. The default is 10. -- connect_command_block: When a netHSM has failed, this field specifies the number of seconds the hardserver should wait before failing commands directed to that netHSM with a NetworkError message. For commands to have a chance of succeeding after a netHSM has failed this value should be greater than that of connect_retry. If it is set to 0, commands to a netHSM are failed with NetworkError immediately, as soon as the netHSM fails. The default is 35. A slightly tighter setting than the default settings looks similar to the following: [server_settings] connect_retry=3 connect_keepalive=4 connect_broken=10 connect_command_block=15 A very tight setting looks similar to the following (Note: This can cause a module to be marked as failed when there is just a short network glitch from which it may well recover): [server_settings] connect_retry=1 connect_keepalive=10 connect_broken=1 connect_command_block=0 Thales recommends that in a production setup, unless there is a solid reason to modify these settings, it is best to use the default values.

bugs.title: Gratuitous ARPs may be transmitted by active unit being forced offline
bugs.symptoms: When cluster's active is forced offline, the non-primary blades may send gratuitous ARPs.
bugs.conditions: Cluster's active blade is forced offline.
bugs.impact: Potential impact to traffic if the gratuitous ARPs of the blade which goes offline is received before the unit taking over as primary, or if gratuitous ARPs are rate-limited on upstream or downstream devices.
bugs.workaround: Failover the cluster before forcing offline or configuring MAC masquerading.

bugs.title: Assert on deletion of paired in-and-out IPsec traffic selectors
bugs.symptoms: When two traffic-selectors, one in and one out, mirror each other by reversing source and destination addresses, then deleting one can miss-fire an assert, restarting tmm.
bugs.conditions: Defining two clearly related traffic selectors, one for in and one for out, can confuse a later check of their names.
bugs.impact: When a traffic selector is deleted, from such a pair, an assert can fail that restarts tmm processes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Using one traffic selector with direction=both would avoid the problem, before this change appears in a release.
bugs.fix: The confusion of over names for such paired traffic selectors is now fixed, so the assert cannot occur. Such traffic selectors -- just like each other execpt for reversed source and destination -- will work correctly for IKEv1 configs. For IKEv2 it is still best to use single TS insances with direction=both.

bugs.title: Removing route-domain may cause monitors to fail
bugs.symptoms: Removing route-domain may cause icmp and gateway-icmp monitors in unrelated route-domains to fail.
bugs.conditions: Route-domain is removed and icmp/gateway-icmp monitor is used.
bugs.impact: Monitor marking node down resulting in partial service outrage.
bugs.workaround: Restart bigd (bigstart restart bigd).
bugs.fix: Removing route-domain no longer causes monitors to fail.

bugs.title: TMM out of memory causes core in DNS cache
bugs.symptoms: The TMM crashes and service is lost until it restarts. You may see several "aggressive mode sweeper" messages in /var/log/ltm prior to the crash.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when the TMM memory is exhausted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Provision sufficient memory for the TMM or reduce load.
bugs.fix: The fix was to properly handle the failure allocating memory.

bugs.title: Some parts of Portal Access client may cause performance issues on rewritten pages
bugs.symptoms: Portal users complain that the page takes a lot of time to load and browser is unresponsive for most of this time. Top entries in the JavaScript profiler are any of following functions: F5_Deflate_index F5_Inflate_index F5_DomainCheck, F5_DomainCheck_IE or F5_DomainCheck_others
bugs.conditions: This can occur through the Access Portal under heavy load.
bugs.impact: Pages take a while to load and browser may show warnings about script execution time.
bugs.fix: Now the performance of F5 functions F5_Deflate_index, F5_inflate_index, and F5_DomainCheck is optimized to allow much better web app performance when delivered via Portal Access.

bugs.title: Policy import fails due to missing signature System in associated Signature Set
bugs.symptoms: ASM policy import fails due to a missing System, used in an associated Signature Set.
bugs.conditions: ASM policy is imported using an export file from a device with a more recent ASM Signature Update.
bugs.impact: The ASM policy import fails.
bugs.workaround: Update the ASM Signature on the target device before importing the policy.

bugs.title: GUI Failover Unicast Address information incorrect
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, the Failover Unicast Address information for the peer device shows the Management IP of the local device, instead of the peer's Management address.
bugs.conditions: Failover Device group with failover unicast addresses configured with management addresses.
bugs.impact: GUI displays incorrect address. *Mgmt addresses listed incorrectly show local mgmt addresses in the following locations: -- Device management :: Devices :: <peer device> -- Device Connectivity: Failover Unicast Configuration

bugs.title: When auto-refresh is enabled on the statistics screen for wideip / pools, it refreshes to the wrong screen.
