bugs.symptoms: When the page refreshes, it loads the wideip statistics screen, rather than the wideip pool statistics screen.
bugs.conditions: Have wide IP & pools and visit the stats page and click on view detail under the "Pools" column with refresh enabled.
bugs.impact: It makes it hard for the user to view updated stats for that particular stats page because it cannot be auto-refreshed.
bugs.workaround: Clicking the << Back button and "view detail" again would update the page stats.

bugs.title: Alertd can not open UDP socket upon restart
bugs.symptoms: alertd fails to restart due to the following error: Sep 29 18:29:44 B2200-R76-S19 err alertd[16882]: 01100009:3: Couldn't open file UDP listener
bugs.conditions: alertd has spawned a long-running process (e.g. ntpd) which does not close inherited file descriptors.
bugs.impact: alertd fails to restart
bugs.fix: Mark alertd file descriptors for automatic closure in child processes.

bugs.title: VCMP guest may temporarly fail to send information to the VCMP host
bugs.symptoms: Under CPU or memory pressure conditions, the guestagentd may log the following messages to /var/log/ltm: e.g. Sep 10 06:47:31 slot1/localhost info guestagentd[4858]: 01810007:6: Exit flags for PID 30469: 0x500
bugs.conditions: VCMP guest
bugs.impact: None as guestagentd keeps trying and recovers.

bugs.title: New SIP::persist keyword to set the timeout without changing key
bugs.symptoms: Setting the SIP persistence key's timeout using SIP::persist <new_key> <new_timeout> disables bidirectional persistence.
bugs.conditions: Setting the SIP persistence key's timeout using SIP::persist <new_key> <new_timeout>.
bugs.impact: Disables bidirectional persistence. Persistence entry only records destination (not source) of the session.
bugs.fix: New keyword, SIP::persist timeout <new_timeout> allows changing the timeout without changing the key.
bugs.behavior: There is a new keyword, SIP::persist timeout <new_timeout> allows changing the timeout without changing the key. Previously, if you changed the timeout, it disabled bidirectional persistence.

bugs.title: Some expected command output are missing in qkview
bugs.symptoms: Some commands are not executed and output are not collected by qkview.
bugs.conditions: If total execution time of all commands is exceeding 360 seconds.
bugs.impact: Missing command output in qkview tar file.
bugs.workaround: Missing commands need to be executed manually to share output with F5 support.
bugs.fix: Timeout can be passed as an arg to qkview command with -t option.

bugs.title: Changes to routing table are not prohibited even when access to local networks is disallowed in Network Access configuration
bugs.symptoms: When administrator disallows access to local networks in Network Access configuration, "Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection" is not enabled automatically.
bugs.conditions: Administrator disallows access to local networks in Network Access configuration.
bugs.impact: End user may gain access to local networks after VPN is established by either: 1) Modifying routing table OR 2) Roaming to a different network.
bugs.workaround: In network access configuration, make sure that "Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection" is checked if "Allow local subnet" option is unchecked.

bugs.title: Security Address Lists and Port Lists can't change Description field
bugs.symptoms: 'Description' doesn't get saved when a user tries to create a Address List, or Port List.
bugs.conditions: Create an Address List/Port List with a description, and hit 'Finished'. The Address/Port List will be created, but the object will not be saved.
bugs.impact: Users will not be able to save description when Address List/Port List gets created via GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create Address/Port List.
bugs.fix: 'Description' gets saved when a user tries to create a Address List, or Port List.

bugs.title: Fragmented packets on clone pool for L7 virtual server targeting another L7 virtual server through iRule
bugs.symptoms: Fragmented packets may be transmited to clone pool members of virtual server, which is also forwarding its traffic to another virtual server.
bugs.conditions: One virtual server should be configured to forward traffic to another one using iRule, i. e. when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { virtual another_virtual } This forwarding virtual should also have clone pool configured.
bugs.impact: Fragmented packet are transmitted to pool members, which affects performance and may trigger some intrusion detection systems.

bugs.title: HTTP to HTTPS TMUI redirection erroneously allows HTTP access to iControl SOAP and iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured to redirect HTTP to HTTPS, iControl SOAP and iControl REST API calls are erroneously accepted on port 80 (in addition to 443).
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP has 'Redirect HTTP to HTTPS' enabled.
bugs.impact: iControl SOAP and iControl REST calls are accepted on an unencrypted port. API calls still require authentication, but results are not encrypted.
bugs.fix: HTTP to HTTPS TMUI redirection no longer erroneously allows HTTP access to iControl SOAP and iControl REST.

bugs.title: Citrix PNAgent replacement mode: iOS Citrix receiver fails to add new store account
bugs.symptoms: iOS Citrix receiver fails to add new store account and touching on the Save option after providing the credentials displays "Loading" and comes back to previous save option. /var/log/apm displays "An exception is thrown: EVP_CipherFinal_ex failed: EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt" from VDI. The above error, otherwise, below error which deletes the session id abruptly. Oct 24 16:33:12 slot2/vip-guest7-test notice tmm[11547]: 01490567:5: /Common/mvdi-r_ap:Common:e19516fd: Session deleted (internal_cause).
bugs.conditions: APM is configured with Citrix replacement mode. Provide wrong passcode values for RSA SecurId auth for continuously three times which trigger the next token input for the fourth time entering the right passcode. APM rotate session is enabled.
bugs.impact: iOS Citrix receiver could not add the account after providing wrong token values for two factor auth
bugs.workaround: Kill the iOS Citrix receiver application and click on the receiver again to add the account.
bugs.fix: Use the right session id for decrypting the password.

bugs.title: Changes to the Connection.VlanKeyed DB key may not immediately apply
bugs.symptoms: Changes to the Connection.VlanKeyed DB key may not immediately apply to all TMMs
bugs.conditions: The Connection.VlanKeyed DB key is changed
bugs.impact: Asymmetrically routed connections may fail with Connection.VlanKeyed disabled
bugs.workaround: Restarting TMM will resolve the issue, though this will interrupt traffic so should be performed during a maintenance window. To do so, run one of the following tmsh commands: -- on an appliance (BIG-IP platform): bigstart restart tmm -- on a clustered system (a VIPRION or VIPRION-based vCMP guest): clsh bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: Asymmetrically routed connections no longer fail with Connection.VlanKeyed disabled.

bugs.title: Request having upper case JSON login parameter is not detected as a failed login attempt
bugs.symptoms: Not able to detect failed login attempt if ASM policy is case insensitive, and incoming JSON string contains upper case.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned ASM policy is case-insensitive JSON profile, w/ JSON login parameter with an upper-case character
bugs.impact: Not able to detect failed login attempt if ASM policy is case insensitive, and incoming JSON string contains upper case.
bugs.fix: We've made sure that JSON login parameter are always treated as case sensitive, regardless of the ASM policy case sensitivity setting.

bugs.title: Existence of /mprov_firstboot with vcmp can set improper tmmcount
bugs.symptoms: During start-up, tmm may go into a restart loop and never come up fully.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on both the vCMP host and guest, usually during the first or second boot of the upgraded software. The existence of /mprov_firstboot and a provision.tmmcountactual set to an incorrect value is an indication that this is occurring.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. tmm on the host goes into a restart loop due to lack of memory. Signature in the log files is similar to "notice Too small memsize (90) -- need at least 136 MB" tmm on the guests core with tmm log entries: notice panic: vdag failed to attach notice ** SIGFPE **

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system may unecessarily run provisioning on successive reboots
bugs.symptoms: After the first boot, the system runs provisioning and boots successfully, but there is a file left on the system /mprov_firstboot. This will appear in /var/log/ltm: info mprov:4614:: \'\'provision.initialized\' indicates force TMOS only provisioning - forcing.\' During a subsequent boot, provisioning will run again, potentially unnecessarily, due to the existence of this file. The following will appear in /var/log/ltm during the second boot: info mprov:4609:: \'Existence of file \'/mprov_firstboot\' indicates force TMOS only provisioning - forcing.\'
bugs.conditions: The memory size of the host changes and there is some other need for reprovisioning (for example a new configuration load).
bugs.impact: On a vCMP host, the second provisioning may not complete properly and guest systems will not pass traffic. The vCMP host will continually try to start more than one tmm and fail when there should only be one tmm running. The /var/log/tmm logfile on the vCMP host will contain: <13> Sep 25 01:33:28 vcmphost1 notice Too small memsize (60) -- need at least 136 MB The /var/log/tmm logfile on the vCMP guest will contain: <13> Sep 25 01:38:21 bigip1 notice Failed to write /var/run/libdag.so_2, err: -30 <13> Sep 25 01:38:21 bigip1 notice panic: vdag failed to attach <13> Sep 25 01:38:21 bigip1 notice ** SIGFPE **
bugs.workaround: If the vCMP host is in a tmm restart loop due to this issue, reboot the vCMP host to allow the system to come up properly.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP software now always removes the /mprov_firstboot file when the system is reprovisioned.

bugs.title: Added better search capabilities on the Pool Members Manage & Pool Create page.
bugs.symptoms: Large amount of virtual servers were hard to manage on the GSLB Pool Member Manage page.
bugs.conditions: Having large amount of virtual servers/wide ips
bugs.impact: Poor usability.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The GSLB Pool Member Manage page now has a new search feature in the form of a combo box to allow for better management of large amount of virtual servers.
bugs.behavior: The GSLB Pool Member Manage page now has the new search feature to allow for better management of large amount of virtual servers.

bugs.title: MCPD crash
bugs.symptoms: MCPD may crash while processing large requests.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are not yet defined.
bugs.impact: MCPD crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: MCPD now processes large requests as expected.

bugs.title: Persist timeout value gets truncated when added to the branch parameter.
bugs.symptoms: Persist timeout value gets truncated when added to the branch parameter due to difference in storage type.
bugs.conditions: If the persist timeout value was higher that 65535 then the value gets truncated.
bugs.impact: Incorrect persist timeout get into affect for the call other than the value set in the config.
bugs.fix: Persist timeout value no longer gets truncated when added to the branch parameter.

bugs.title: Azure cloud now supports hourly billing
bugs.symptoms: Prior to 12.1.2 hourly billing was not supported in Azure cloud.
bugs.conditions: Any version prior to 12.1.2 in Azure Cloud
bugs.impact: Hourly billing not possible
bugs.fix: With 12.1.2 hourly billing is now supported in Azure.

bugs.title: FQDN pool created with existing FQDN node has RED status
bugs.symptoms: After creating an FQDN pool using an existing FQDN node, the pool has RED status.
bugs.conditions: -- Existing FQDN node. -- Pool created with an existing FQDN node as a member.
bugs.impact: Traffic will not pass in this pool.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, follow these steps: 1. Delete the existing FQDN node. 2. Create a new one. 3. Create a pool that includes the new FQDN node.
bugs.fix: When creating an FQDN pool with an existing FQDN node, the pool status now reflects the actual monitor status.

bugs.title: Access Policy is not able to check device posture for Android 7 devices
bugs.symptoms: APM identifies Android devices based on their MAC address. With Android 7, it is not possible to retrieve device MAC address and hence APM is not able to check for device compliance against configured Endpoint Management System (EMS) using the Managed Endpoint Status Policy Item. If the Access Policy is configured to restrict access based on APM's Managed Endpoint Status, and the user attempts to connect to APM using an Android 7 device with the F5 Edge Client app, access will be disallowed.
bugs.conditions: - Access policy is configured to deny access on endpoint compliance failure with Managed Endpoint Status - User accesses APM from an Android 7 device using F5 Edge Client app.
bugs.impact: Connection is denied because F5 Edge Client is not able to determine the device MAC address to transmit to APM. The lookup for endpoint posture will result in a compliance check failure.
bugs.workaround: This workaround only applies to IBM Maas360: Add Variable Assign agent just before Managed Endpoint Status agent with the following variables: session.client.platform_tmp = expr {[mcget session.client.platform]} session.client.platform = expr {"iOS"} session.client.unique_id = expr {"Android[mcget session.client.unique_id]"} And add Variable Assign agent after Managed Endpoint Status agent to reset session.client.platform to its original state: session.client.platform = expr {[mcget session.client.platform_tmp]}
bugs.fix: Access policy now uses multiple fallback types to correlate the device identity with endpoint management systems: Device Serial Number, IMEI number, and MAC address, respectively.

bugs.title: Portal Access / JavaScript code which uses reserved keywords for field names in literal object definition may not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript code with literal object definition containing field names equal to reserved keywords is not handled correctly by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript code with literal object definition containing fields with reserved keywords as a name, for example: var a = { default: 1, continue: 2 };
bugs.impact: JavaScript code is not rewritten and may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Now JavaScript with literal object definition containing reserved keywords as field names is handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: DoS: tmm core after delete packet type from Device Sweep vector
bugs.symptoms: During the config change of Sweep vector, when all tmm threads delete the rate tracker, a race condition might occur that could prevent the tracker from being deleted. As a result, some tmm threads might see the new instance, which causes the tmm thread to abort.
bugs.conditions: This potential race condition occurs after delete packet type from Device Sweep vector.
bugs.impact: tmm thread might abort if a race condition occurs. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: mcpd failes to load configuration on upgrade if the transparent monitors are configured for FQDN nodes
bugs.symptoms: In /var/log/ltm the following errors will be logged Oct 6 07:01:11 localhost err tmsh[11209]: 01420006:3: Loading configuration process failed. Oct 6 07:01:12 localhost emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all" - failed. -- 01070734:3: Configuration error: Transparent monitors are not currently available for FQDN nodes. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Running 11.6.0 or prior with transparent monitors configured for FQDN nodes and then upgrading to 11.6.1 or higher.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP will stay INOPERATIVE until the configuration is changed and loaded.
bugs.workaround: After the upgrade, bigip.conf needs to be changed so that the transparent monitor is no longer configured for the FQDN node. After the edits are made, the config needs to be reloaded.

bugs.title: Decreased performance of ICMP attack mitigation.
bugs.symptoms: Decreased performance of ICMP attack mitigation.
bugs.conditions: A Big-Ip is under attack, for example a ICMP flood attack.
bugs.impact: Decreased performance of ICMP attack mitigation.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Increased performance of ICMP attack mitigation.

bugs.title: Online help for Network Access needs update
bugs.symptoms: Online help for advanced network settings does not tell users that if they fill in the DNS Address Space setting, they also need to install the DNS Relay Proxy service on Windows-based systems to get the desired result.
bugs.conditions: Split tunneling configured. Windows-based system in use. DNS Address Space setting filled in.
bugs.impact: Use of DNS Address Space setting does not provide the expected result.
bugs.workaround: Install the DNS Relay Proxy server on Windows-based systems.
bugs.fix: Network Access online help now states that for DNS Address Space to work properly on a Windows-based system, the DNS Relay Proxy service must be installed and running on the client.

bugs.title: New iRule command, MR::ignore_peer_port
bugs.symptoms: For incoming connections where the client used a ephemeral source port, subsequents connections from the same client may connect using a different ephemeral port. Without being able to identify the current connection as equivalents to other connections from the same IP, it will not be discoverable as an equivalent connection.
bugs.conditions: For incoming connections where the client used a ephemeral source port, subsequents connections from the same client may connect using a different ephemeral port.
bugs.impact: Without being able to identify the current connection as equivalents to other connections from the same IP, it will not be discoverable as an equivalent connection.
bugs.workaround: Without this change, a new connection would need to be created to the client.
bugs.fix: New iRule command allow script author to identify the current connection as equivalent to other connections of the IP and route domain ID matches.

bugs.title: qkview generation is slow due to 'ss -p' command
bugs.symptoms: qkview takes a significant amount of time to complete due to performance of 'ss -p' command.
bugs.conditions: Significant number of open sockets
bugs.impact: Slow qkview generation
bugs.fix: Decrease time of qkview generation by increasing performance of 'ss -p' command due to reduced complexity.

bugs.title: Rare problem in pam_tally; message: PAM Couldn't lock /var/log/pam/tallylog : Resource temporarily unavailable
bugs.symptoms: Contention for /var/log/tallylog lock might result in users failing to authenticate correctly. As a result of this issue, you might see the following message: PAM Couldn't lock /var/log/pam/tallylog : Resource temporarily unavailable.
bugs.conditions: High concurrent authentication attempts may trigger this issue. For example, open a connection, using basic authentication, performing a query (for example, get node list, get virtual address list, and set pool min active members), then close the connection. If done frequently enough, there is an occasional authentication failure.
bugs.impact: This intermittent authentication failure results in users not being able to login.
bugs.workaround: Since this is an intermittent authentication failure, wait a few seconds and then attempt to log in again.

bugs.title: TMM crash with assertion failure of pkt type not already ETHERTYPE_ARP
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes repeatedly on SIGSEGV during normal operation.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this, but the following log signature is seen in /var/log/ltm: arning tmm[6659]: 01190004:4: address conflict detected for <ip> (<mac>) on vlan <vlan> Where <ip> is the self IP, and <mac> is the mac from the peer BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: iControl doesn't give correct valid key sizes for FIPS keys on BIG-IP 5250, 7200F, 10200F, and 11050F platforms running the Cavium Nitrox XL FIPS cards.
bugs.symptoms: Using the get_valid_key_sizes() for querying the valid key sizes, 1024 is returned, which is not valid when the FIPS firmware is version 2.2 or above.
bugs.conditions: FIPS firmware is version 2.2 or above.
bugs.impact: Unsupported key-size is returned.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed to return the supported key-sizes in versions after 12.x.x.

bugs.title: IP/IPv6 TTL/hoplimit may not be preserved for host traffic
bugs.symptoms: Traffic to and from the Linux host has TTL set to 255 or hop limit set to 64. This may impact any protocols that scrutinize the TTL such as IGMP or BGP.
bugs.conditions: IP/IPv6 TTL/hoplimit for host traffic.
bugs.impact: IGMP packets will not be passed from TMM to the Linux host and remote routers may reject IGMP packets from the BIG-IP. BGP neighbors may reject packets from the BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Adjust TTL verification restrictions on peer devices.
bugs.fix: The IP/IPv6 TTL/hoplimit of host traffic is no longer modified when it traverses TMM.

bugs.title: Import of config with saml idp connector with reuse causes certificate not found error
bugs.symptoms: Export and then Import with reuse of config that has SAML Idp Connector as part of configuration would fail with Object not found or Certificate not found error: Import Error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: /Common/my_cert.crt certificate not found.
bugs.conditions: Exporting and then importing with "Reuse existing objects" checked. Normal import is ok.
bugs.impact: Importing fails.
bugs.workaround: On From box:Disconnect Idp configuration, export config. On To box:Recereate Idp configuration, import, reconnect it.
bugs.fix: Importing with reuse is fixed.

bugs.title: F5vpn does not close upon closing session
bugs.symptoms: F5vpn does not close upon closing session.
bugs.conditions: -- With Network Access started and connected to BIG-IP using browser. -- Clicking 'Logout' button on webtop.
bugs.impact: Session closes. Network Access window does not close, but instead remains in disconnected state.

bugs.title: Question mark prevents TMSH from loading configuration file
bugs.symptoms: When loading system configuration for TMSH, if some properties have value question mark, TMSH would fail to complete the loading.
bugs.conditions: -- Use TM Shell to load configuration. -- string, vector of string properties have ? as value
bugs.impact: TMSH fails to load system configuration file
bugs.fix: TMSH now considers escaped question mark as literal character if the question mark is explicitly escaped (i.e. using quotes, backslash, etc.) Loading system configuration succeeds if all question marks are properly escaped

bugs.title: Portal Access: document.write() with very long string as argument may be handled incorrectly.
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript code may include document.write() calls with very long strings (> 60K). In some cases these strings may be rewritten incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: - document.write() with very long string as argument. - argument string contains HTML tags with quoted attribute values which include '>' inside.
bugs.impact: rewritten HTML page may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Now document.write() calls with long HTML strings are handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: Policy sync shows as aborted even if it is completed
bugs.symptoms: After syncing a policy in a sync-only device group, the policy appears to be synced to the target successfully, however, the remote HA pair devices show status as canceled/aborted.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this condition. It was observed in a 4-device trust group consisting of 2 sync/failover groups and a single sync-only device group for all 4 devices. After the sync the status reported as cancelled/aborted.
bugs.impact: Sync status is displayed incorrectly, even after the sync was successful.
bugs.fix: Policy sync now shows as completed when it is completed.

bugs.title: LTM log contains misleading error messages for front panel interfaces, "PCI Device not found for Interface X.0"
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is initially booted or re-started, there are certain conditions under which the LTM log may report the following message for front panel interfaces, "PCI Device not found for Interface <X.0>", where X can be in the range of 1-6. These messages are misleading because the front panel interfaces do not have any PCI devices associated with them and should not have been flagged as errors.
bugs.conditions: i2600/i2800 products intermittently produce these messages upon power-up or BIG-IP re-start.
bugs.impact: They are false alarms in the log. The associated interfaces do not have said PCI devices.
bugs.fix: Removed the possibility of getting false alarm messages in the LTM log for front panel interfaces 1.0-6.0 that claim, "PCI Device not found for Interface X.0".

bugs.title: fastL4 + http profile with ip-protocol not set to tcp can crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: TMM will core when receiving a non-TCP datagram on a fastL4 + http profile virtual.
bugs.conditions: Create a virtual server that uses profiles fastL4 and http and is set to use an ip-protocol other than just tcp.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Set the virtual's ip-protocol to tcp.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when a virtual server with FastL4 and HTTP profiles, or FastL4 and hash persistence profiles, receives non-TCP traffic.

bugs.title: Certain DNS queries bypass DNS Cache RPZ filter.
bugs.symptoms: A DNS query with the DO-bit set to 1 will bypass the RPZ filter on a DNS Cache.
bugs.conditions: A DNS Cache configured with RPZ.
bugs.impact: Queries with DO-bit set to 1 will bypass the RPZ filter and be answered normally.
bugs.fix: The DO-bit is now ignored with respect to RPZ filtering.

bugs.title: Reserve enough space in the image for future upgrades.
bugs.symptoms: Increased the reserved free space in VM image from 15% to 30% to accommodate upgrades to future versions. Each next version tends to be bigger and require more disk space to install. The increased reserved space will allow upgrading to at least next 2 versions.
bugs.conditions: VE in local hypervisors and VE in the Cloud (AWS, Azure).
bugs.impact: Extends the disk image to reserve more disk space for upgrades.
bugs.fix: Increased the reserved free space on VE images.

bugs.title: Config save takes long time if there is a large number of data groups
bugs.symptoms: Config save takes a long time to complete
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a large number (~2000) of data-group objects in the configuration
bugs.impact: When take longer than 90 seconds soap iControl will time out. This make it impossible to manage via EM

bugs.title: mcpd core on iControl REST reference to non-existing pool
bugs.symptoms: MCPd cores when attempting to create a pool and a monitor reference by using a REST call such as: curl -u admin:admin -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST http://localhost:8100/tm/ltm/pool -d'{"name":"test_pool","monitor":" "}'
bugs.conditions: The monitor reference in the REST call must be comprised of a single space character.
bugs.impact: MCPd restarts, causing many of the system daemons to restart as well.
bugs.workaround: Don't use spaces in the monitor reference name.

bugs.title: DSR tunnels with transparent monitors may cause TMM crash.
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may crash if the BIG-IP system is configured with a DSR tunnel with a transparent monitor.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured with a DSR tunnel with a transparent monitor and the DB variable tm.monitorencap is set to "enable".
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM does not crash.

bugs.title: Incorrect TMSH help text for the 'max-response' RAMCACHE attribute
bugs.symptoms: The TMSH help text for the 'max-response' RAMCACHE attribute incorrectly states that for the default value of 0 (zero) unlimited cache entries are allowed. In reality the number of cache entries is limited to 10.
bugs.conditions: Invoking the TMSH man/help page on RAMCACHE.
bugs.impact: Incorrect TMSH help text
bugs.fix: max-response: Displays the maximum number of entries in the RAM cache. The default value is 0 (zero), which is equivalent with no max-response value being specified. Without the max-response option the system will limit the number of entries to 10 per Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM).

bugs.title: SCTP virtual server with mirroring may cause excessive memory use on standby device
bugs.symptoms: If a SCTP virtual server has high availability (HA) mirroring enabled, the send buffer on the standby may have extremely high memory usage until the connections close.
bugs.conditions: SCTP virtual server has mirroring enabled.
bugs.impact: TMMs will have high memory usage on standby device.
bugs.workaround: Disable mirroring on the SCTP virtual server.
bugs.fix: SCTP virtual server with mirroring no longer causes excessive memory use on standby device.

bugs.title: Output Errors in APM Event Log
bugs.symptoms: In some cases the HTML used to display APM event logs is generated incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: APM enabled Administrative user views APM event logs via WebUI
bugs.impact: Inaccurate HTML rendered in user browser.
bugs.fix: Corrected HTML errors when displaying APM event logs

bugs.title: "abbrev" argument in "whereis" iRule returns nothing
bugs.symptoms: The iRule [whereis <ip|ldns> abbrev] does not return a value.
bugs.conditions: iRule relying on whereis abbrev is used.
bugs.impact: The whereis iRule command will not return the expected value.

bugs.title: TCP Lossfilter not enforced after iRule changes TCP settings
bugs.symptoms: TCP Lossfilter function doesn't work properly, although the first few losses will be properly ignored.
bugs.conditions: TCP profile has ALL of the following settings: mptcp disabled; rate-pace disabled; tail-loss-probe disabled; fast-open disabled; cmetrics-cache-timeout = 0; congestion ctrl is reno, new-reno, high-speed, or scalable; nagle enabled or disabled; rtx_thresh = 3; loss-filter settings are both > 0. an iRule changes any of the above settings except loss-filter.
bugs.impact: Sending rate declines due to packet losses improperly interpreted as congestion.
bugs.workaround: Change any of the conditions above.
bugs.fix: Properly handle loss-filter state when switching TCP stacks.

bugs.title: restjavad spawns too many icrd_child instances
bugs.symptoms: icrd_child process keeps crashing and can lead to an out-of-memory condition.
bugs.conditions: This occurs due to a race condition while restarting the icrd daemon.
bugs.impact: icrd might crash.
bugs.fix: Fixed race condition that caused the system to run out of memory by spawning too many icrd_child processes.

bugs.title: When HA is configured on BIG-IPs managed by BIG-IQ, the AVR reporting from BIG-IQ may fail under the load
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IQ is monitoring more than 1 BIG-IP in a HA clustser, AVR reporting on the BIG-IQ may fail if one of the BIG-IPs is under heavy load.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IQ monitoring BIG-IPs in a HA cluster BIG-IPs running AFM and/or ASM BIG-IQ used to monitor AFM and/or ASM reporting. At least one of the BIG-IPs is under significant load so as to cause delays in responding to BIG-IQ requests.
bugs.impact: AVR reporting will stop functioning.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart restjavad

bugs.title: sys-icheck error for /usr/share/defaults/bigip_base.conf in AWS.
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP deployed in AWS cloud, sys-icheck reports size an md5 errors for /usr/share/defaults/BIG-IP_base.conf file as following: ERROR: S.5...... c /usr/share/defaults/BIG-IP_base.conf (no backup)
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP deployed in AWS cloud.
bugs.impact: sys-icheck reports "rpm --verify" size and md5 errors for /usr/share/defaults/BIG-IP_base.conf. This doesn't have any functional impact on the product but looks like factory config file was modified incorrectly by a user/application.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for this issue.
bugs.fix: sys-icheck error for /usr/share/defaults/BIG-IP_base.conf in AWS.

bugs.title: i2000 and i4000 series appliances do not warn when an incorrect optic is in a port
bugs.symptoms: A 1G optic is inserted in a port that only supports 10G optics, or a 10G optic is inserted in a port that only supports 1G optics. The invalid optic may show a link light, and no warning appears on the LCD.
bugs.conditions: i2000 or i4000 platforms ports do not auto-negotiate between 1G and 10G optics. Ports are assigned to one or the other speed.
bugs.impact: User may not understand why optic is not working correctly
bugs.workaround: Move the optic to the correct port.

bugs.title: sys-icheck reports error with /config/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key
bugs.symptoms: On Azure cloud, running sys-icheck may report an error with /config/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key and other files: ERROR: missing /config/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key ERROR: missing /config/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key.pub ERROR: missing /config/ssh/ssh_host_key ERROR: missing /config/ssh/ssh_host_key.pub
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP running on Azure cloud.
bugs.impact: sys-icheck utility indicates an error. The sys-icheck utility is used to find file system changes that have occurred since initial installation and provide information about their status.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with files in /config/ssh/ that was causing sys-icheck to report errors.

bugs.title: In some rare cases, VDI may crash
bugs.symptoms: VDI process crashes and connections to VDI resources are aborted.
bugs.conditions: VDI receives unexpected session variable result which is meant for some other VDI thread.
bugs.impact: Existing VDI connections are aborted and the user needs to login again.
bugs.fix: VDI should gracefully handle the error condition and should not crash

bugs.title: Connections can stall with TCP::collect iRule
bugs.symptoms: Connection does not complete
bugs.conditions: A TCP::collect command with two arguments defers collection beyond the first client message, which should be sufficient to produce a response. The Initial Sequence number in the SYN is < 2^31. The first received packet after the SYN carries data.
bugs.impact: Connection fails.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Properly set state variables associated with TCP::collect

bugs.title: The minimum IP packet fragment size is now 1 and not 24
bugs.symptoms: The minimum IP packet fragment size, set via DB Var [TM.MinIPfragSize], is 24 and that causes problems if you need to use smaller fragments in your network.
bugs.conditions: You are trying to configure TM.MinIPfragSize and need it to be set to a value smaller than 24.
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure fragment sizes smaller than 24 in your network.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Changed DB Var [TM.MinIPfragSize] minimum value from 24 to 1.

bugs.title: Processing Timeout When Viewing a Request with 300+ Violations
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to view a request that triggered hundreds or thousands of violations, a timeout is encountered.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to view a request that triggered hundreds or thousands of violations
bugs.impact: A timeout is encountered.
bugs.workaround: increase the "max_execution_time" timeout in /usr/loca/lib/php.ini from 30 to 240 seconds.
bugs.fix: Processing high violation requests is now more efficient.

bugs.title: Portal Access: problem with specific JavaScript code
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access does not rewrite JavaScript code with try...catch... operator followed by literal regular expression.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript code like follows: try {} catch (e) {} /aaa/.test(b)
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Now try / catch operator followed by literal regular expression in JavaScript code is handled correctly by Portal Access.

bugs.title: statsd does not handle SIGCHLD properly in all cases
bugs.symptoms: - Performance graphs are not updating or are not existant. - proc_pid_stat shows statsd time not increasing - Top also shows that statsd is not taking any processor time. Infact statsd is stuck on a wait in a signal handler.
bugs.conditions: If statsd receives a SIGCHLD signal it will get stuck and not process anything. The following can trigger the issue: rm -rf /shared/rrd.backup - sed -i "s/^#CRC.*$/#CRC $RANDOM/" /var/rrd/throughput.info - kill -HUP $(pgrep -f /usr/bin/statsd)
bugs.impact: No performance graphs are collected / generated
bugs.workaround: Restart statsd: - bigstart restart statsd
bugs.fix: statsd now handles SIGCHLD properly.

bugs.title: tmsh show sys tmm-info command shows low CPU Usage Ratio
bugs.symptoms: The CPU usage count is low as a result of including the the data from TMM's that are not active. This skews the numbers seen.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on any multi-tmm configuration.
bugs.impact: Numbers are not correct.
bugs.workaround: Use the top command to get a more correct reporting of the CPU Usage numbers.

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense failing in IE11 with Compatibility View enabled
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer 11 browsers which have "Compatibility View" enabled (under Compatibility View Settings IE menu), will fail the JavaScript challenge, when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled and the "Block requests from suspicious browsers" checkbox is checked. The challenged request will be blocked using a TCP_RST flag, and the browser will show "This page canâ€™t be displayed" is seen in the browser.
bugs.conditions: 1. DoS profile that is attached to the Virtual Server has Proactive Bot Defense is enabled and "Block requests from suspicious browsers" checkbox is checked. 2. Internet Explorer 11 browsers in which the site's domain is inserted to the "Compatibility View Settings" in the browser's menu.
bugs.impact: Legitimate browsers get blocked when accessing the site.
bugs.fix: Internet Explorer 11 browsers with "Compatibility View" enabled on the site no longer get blocked when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled on the DoS profile.

bugs.title: Alert Component and Malware values are reset when deleting unsaved user-defined alert
bugs.symptoms: When adding multiple user-defined alerts, Alert Component and Malware values are reset if deleting another alert from the list.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS.
bugs.impact: FPS GUI.
bugs.workaround: Add alerts without deleting.
bugs.fix: Alert Component and Malware values are no longer reset when deleting unsaved user-defined alert

bugs.title: the ipother proxy is sending icmp error messages to the wrong side
bugs.symptoms: the ipother proxy error handling sends ICMP error messages down the wrong side of the proxy. when a client-side error occurs, the error message is being sent to the server side
bugs.conditions: error handling of the ipother proxy
bugs.impact: ICMP error messages show up on the wrong side
bugs.workaround: no workaround
bugs.fix: fixed the error handling, messages are now sent to the correct side

bugs.title: TMM could use a lot of memory when an iRule calls parking command under AUTH events
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory usage keeps going and depending on the situation may eventually crash.
bugs.conditions: iRule calls parking commands under AUTH events.
bugs.impact: TMM memory usage keeps going up. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: The AUTH usage is replaced with APM module which is the preferred solution.

bugs.title: Outage may occur with VIP-VIP configurations
bugs.symptoms: In some VIP-VIP configurations, a system outage may occur while processing traffic.
bugs.conditions: VIP-VIP configuration
bugs.impact: System outage

bugs.title: Uneven egress trunk distribution on 5000/10000 platforms with odd number of trunk members
bugs.symptoms: When a trunk on the BigIP 5000 or 10000 platforms has an odd number of members, the traffic distribution to those interfaces will be unbalanced. Some interfaces will see more traffic than others.
bugs.conditions: This can occur for two reasons: Either purposefully configuring an odd number of members or a port goes down in a trunk that has an even number of members.
bugs.impact: Uneven traffic distribution.
bugs.fix: This release fixes uneven egress trunk distribution on the BIG-IP 5000 or 10000 platforms when there is an odd number of ports.

bugs.title: Timezone data on AOM not syncing with host
bugs.symptoms: Updating the timezone on the host does not sync to the AOM, because certain tzdata files are placed in the wrong directories.
bugs.conditions: A system using tzdata version v2016i-1 may encounter this problem. If the following files exist: /usr/share/zoneinfo/posix/zoneinfo/posix/F5zone.tab /usr/share/zoneinfo/right/zoneinfo/right/F5zone.tab /usr/share/zoneinfo/zoneinfo/F5zone.tab then the system has this problem.
bugs.impact: Time on the AOM is incorrect.
bugs.workaround: If the following files exist: /usr/share/zoneinfo/posix/zoneinfo/posix/F5zone.tab /usr/share/zoneinfo/right/zoneinfo/right/F5zone.tab /usr/share/zoneinfo/zoneinfo/F5zone.tab move them to: /usr/share/zoneinfo/F5zone.tab /usr/share/zoneinfo/posix/F5zone.tab /usr/share/zoneinfo/right/F5zone.tab
bugs.fix: Timezone data on AOM now syncs correctly with host again

bugs.title: Skype For Business thick client shows javascript errors when rendering APM logon page
bugs.symptoms: Skype For Business thick client shows javascript errors when rendering APM logon page
bugs.conditions: APM is used as federated auth provider for Microsoft Azure. User uses Skype For Business thick client to authenticate.
bugs.impact: User experience is impacted, however clicking thru javascript errors eventually leads to successful authentication and working Skype For Business app.
bugs.workaround: Click thru javascript error dialogs.
bugs.fix: Skype For Business thick client is now fully supported when authenticating against APM as federation provider for Microsoft Azure.

bugs.title: OneDrive for Business thick client shows javascript errors when rendering APM logon page
bugs.symptoms: OneDrive for Business thick client shows javascript errors when rendering APM logon page
bugs.conditions: APM is used as federated auth provider for Microsoft Azure. User uses OneDrive for Business thick client to authenticate.
bugs.impact: User experience is impacted, however clicking thru javascript errors eventually leads to successful authentication and working OneDrive for Business app.
bugs.workaround: Click thru javascript error dialogs.
bugs.fix: OneDrive for Business thick client is now fully supported when authenticating against APM as federation provider for Microsoft Azure.

bugs.title: RRD files are not backed up if the /shared/rrd.backup directory already exists
bugs.symptoms: Performance graphs do not display. rrdshim cpu time does not increase. Issuing "rrdtool dump /var/rrd/blade0cpu | grep lastupdate" shows a time in the past (prior to last system boot).
bugs.conditions: /shared/rrd.backup directory must not exist. incorrect info hash in /var/rrd/<filename>.info
bugs.impact: rrd files do not get backed up.
bugs.workaround: restart statsd "bigstart restart statsd"
bugs.fix: Corrupt performance graph RRD data is now backed up to the /shared/rrd.backup directory during startup even if the directory already exists.

bugs.title: VCMP guests may incorrectly obtain incorrect MAC addresses
bugs.symptoms: vCMP guests may be re-configured to use MAC addresses based off an all zero MAC address (00:00:00:00:00:00). The 'tmsh show net vlan' command will show the vlan interfaces having mostly 0's in the MAC address: ------------------------------------- Net::Vlan: external ------------------------------------- Interface Name external Mac Address (True) 00:00:00:00:00:01 MTU 1500 Tag 3702 Customer-Tag ------------------------------------- Net::Vlan: internal ------------------------------------- Interface Name internal Mac Address (True) 00:00:00:00:00:02 MTU 1500 Tag 3703 Customer-Tag
bugs.conditions: For this to manifest the vCMP host vcmpd process will have to have had a prior crash or be killed. In this scenario vcmpd on restart uses a default zero-base MAC address for the guests. The guests will not use the new zero-based MAC until services are restarted on the guest, on which the new MAC address will take effect.
bugs.impact: This can cause network issues and conflicts if occurring on multiple guests in the same VLAN as the same MAC addresses will be used.
bugs.workaround: Restart the guest from the hypervisor.
bugs.fix: vCMP no longer uses zero-based MACs on vcmpd crash/kill.

bugs.title: flow generated icmp error message need to consider which side of the proxy they are
bugs.symptoms: when generating an error message from a flow, the icmp6 code does not check which side the messages needs to be crafted for.
bugs.conditions: error handling
bugs.impact: As a result generated ICMP error message might contain the wrong addressing
bugs.workaround: no workaround
bugs.fix: now the code checks flow type before crafting the error message

bugs.title: ICMPv6 packets can have the wrong source IP if a IPv6 VIP has IPv4 pool members
bugs.symptoms: ICMPV6 packet has the source IP of IPv4 Mapped IPv6 selfIP address instead of the IPv6 selfIP address configured on the unit
bugs.conditions: IPv6 forwarding VIP with no translation references IPv4 poolmembers and the PMTU to the nexthop is less than the packet size sent by the server.
bugs.impact: ICMPv6 packets with wrong source IP addresses

bugs.title: HTTP GET requests with HTTP::cookie iRule command receive no response
bugs.symptoms: HTTP GET requests to virtual servers using the command "HTTP::cookie <name> <value>" in HTTP_REQUEST iRule event handlers do not get a response.
bugs.conditions: An LTM virtual server with an iRule including the HTTP::cookie command.
bugs.impact: No response is received by the client.
bugs.fix: HTTP GET requests to virtual servers using the command "HTTP::cookie <name> <value>" in HTTP_REQUEST iRule event handlers now get a response as expected.

bugs.title: Improve flow handling when Autolasthop is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Modifications made to improve flow handling in configurations which disabled Autolasthop.
bugs.conditions: Autolasthop disabled.
bugs.impact: Modifications made to improve flow handling in configurations which disabled Autolasthop.

bugs.title: The alert daemon should remove old log files but it does not.
bugs.symptoms: When the utilization of the log filesystem goes above the configuration setting 'sys db logcheck.alertthres' (default 90%), it is intended that the alert daemon should delete old log files. It does not.
bugs.conditions: System activity generates a high number of log messages, and/or a user puts large files in /var/log.
bugs.impact: The log filesystem may become completely full, and new log messages cannot be saved.
bugs.fix: The alert daemon will now remove old log files as intended.

bugs.title: sys-icheck reports error with ssh_host_rsa_key
bugs.symptoms: On Azure cloud, running sys-icheck may report an error with /config/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key and ssh_host_rsa_key.pub ERROR: SM5...... /config/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key ERROR: SM5...... /config/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key.pub
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP running on Azure cloud when running the sys-icheck utility.
bugs.impact: sys-icheck utility indicates an error. The sys-icheck utility is used to find file system changes that have occurred since initial installation and provide information about their status.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with ssh_host_rsa_key and ssh_host_rsa_key.pub that was causing sys-icheck to generate an error.

bugs.title: sys-icheck reports error with /var/lib/waagent
bugs.symptoms: On Azure cloud, running sys-icheck may report an error with /var/lib/waagent. On BIG-IP version 12.0.0: ERROR: ....L.... /var/lib/waagent L - readLink(2) path mismatch On BIG-IP version 12.1.0 and 12.1.1: ERROR: .M....... /var/lib/waagent M - Mode differs (includes permissions and file type)
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP running on Azure cloud.
bugs.impact: sys-icheck utility indicates an error. The sys-icheck utility is used to find file system changes that have occurred since initial installation and provide information about their status.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with waagent that was causing sys-icheck to fail.

bugs.title: If a virtual server's name has a "." in it then a DoS profile cannot be attached to it
bugs.symptoms: For virtual servers with a . (dot, or period) in the name and a DoS profile attached, a crash might occur when attacks are detected/stopped.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with a name that includes a . and an attached DoS profile, and then a DoS attack is detected.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove the . in the virtual server name.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now allows attaching a DoS profile to a virtual server that has a . in its name.

bugs.title: Disruption during manipulation of PEM data with suspected flow irregularity
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what conditions trigger this; it was observed with Policy Enforcement Manager configured. It may occur when a new blade is added or HA event occurs and flows get rebalanced before the session is established.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to manipulating Policy Enforcement Manager data.

bugs.title: Edge client can fail to upgrade when always connected is selected
bugs.symptoms: Attempt to upgrade an Edge client may fail if the Always Connected mode is enabled
bugs.conditions: Always Connected is selected in BIG-IP when upgrading the client
bugs.impact: Upgrade will fail
bugs.workaround: Disable the Always Connected mode
bugs.fix: Upgrade functions as intended regardless of connection mode

bugs.title: Some TCP connections do not work when hardware syncookies are being issued and certain options are enabled
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP 11.5.x, approximately 50% of TCP connections have all of their packets dropped when hardware syncookies are being issued and certain other features are enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- An 11.5.x version of the BIG-IP is in use on the system. -- The platform supports hardware syncookies. -- Hardware syncookies are being issued. -- The sys db TM.TCPProgressive is set to a value other than 'enable'. If the sys db TM.TCPProgressive is set to 'disable' or 'negotiate', the issue occurs when the previous conditions are met, and any one of the following conditions applies to the TCP profile attached to the virtual server: -- MPTCP is enabled. -- Rate pacing is enabled. -- Congestion control is set to vegas, illinois, woodside, chd (Caia-Hamilton Delay based) or cdg (Caia Delay-Gradient).
bugs.impact: Approximately 50% of connections will have all of their packets dropped when hardware syncookies are being issued.
bugs.workaround: Any of the following actions will mitigate this issue: 1. Disable hardware syncookies. 2. Set sys db TM.TCPProgressive to 'enable'. 3. If sys db TM.TCPProgressive is set to 'negotiate', set the following options on the TCP profile as follows: a. Disable MPTCP. b. Disable rate pacing. c. Set congestion control to reno, new-reno, high-speed, or scalable.

bugs.title: Network DoS logging configuration change can cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Whenever a DoS Network logging profile is assigned or removed from a Virtual Server, it could cause random TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: The problem happens only with runtime config change. Any logging profile config settings which was configured already and which gets loaded on TMM startup does not have this problem. Since this problem is a one time event on config change, TMM restart will pickup the config change and will work without any problem after the one time crash and TMM restart.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Invalid memory reference after free resulted in crash, which is fixed.

bugs.title: Windows command line client cannot connect if Edge client is running and disconnected
bugs.symptoms: Windows command line client cannot connect if Edge client is running and disconnected.
bugs.conditions: f5fpc.exe (Windows command line client) is used to establish VPN. Windows Edge client is running and is in disconnected state.
bugs.impact: VPN cannot be established using command line client.
bugs.workaround: Use Edge client to connect VPN.
bugs.fix: Now the Windows command line edge client (f5fpc.exe) works correctly if the full Edge Client is simultaneously running but disconnected.

bugs.title: Inconsistent hardware syncookie protection mode on B2100/B4300 blades and 5000/7000/10000 appliances
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP may enter a state where the software indicates it is not in syncookie protection mode for a virtual IP, but the FPGA is still in that mode.
bugs.conditions: This only occurs on the following platforms (B2100/B4300 blades, 5000/7000/10000 appliances) with Xilinx FPGA. It can be triggered if BIG-IP enters and exits syncookie protection frequently in a short interval as SYN traffic varies.
bugs.impact: This may lead to undesired behavior in processing traffic. For example it would cause the VIP to remain in hardware syncookie protection mode while SYN traffic is nominal.
bugs.workaround: Usually "bigstart restart tmm" would clear this error condition.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP hardware and software would have consistent syncookie protection state. However, this also introduces a behavior change on the following platforms (B2100/B4300 blades, 5000/7000/10000 appliances). When SYN traffic returns to nominal, it requires some legitimate traffic to trigger BIG-IP to exit syncookie protection mode.

bugs.title: Internet Explorer getting blocked when Web Scraping and Proactive Bot Defense are both enabled
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer browsers will get into an endless loop of requests, never reaching the back-end server, when accessing a Virtual Server which is enabled with both the Web Scraping feature, and the Proactive Bot Defense, if the mode of Proactive Bot Defense is set to During Attacks.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM Security Policy is attached to the Virtual Server, and has Web Scraping's Bot Detection set to Alarm & Block. 2. Within Web Scraping, both Fingerprint and Persistent Client Identification are disabled. 3. DoS profile is attached to the Virtual Server, and has Proactive Bot Defense set to During Attacks. 4. Users are using the Internet Explorer browser.
bugs.impact: Internet Explorer browser users are getting blocked from accessing the back-end server.
bugs.workaround: Two options for workaround: 1. Set Proactive Bot Defense to Always instead of During Attacks. 2. Enable either Fingerprint or Persistent Client Identification in the Web Scraping configuration.
bugs.fix: Internet Explorer users are no longer blocked when accessing a Virtual Server which has both Web Scraping enabled, and Proactive Bot Defense set to During Attacks.

bugs.title: Allowing Application Editor users to remove pool members
bugs.symptoms: Application Editors aren't allowed to remove pool members
bugs.conditions: This applies to the application editor user role.
bugs.impact: Application Editors cannot remove pool members using the web UI
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to remove pool members with an Application Editor user
bugs.fix: Application Editor users can now remove pool members

bugs.title: BIG-IP 11.6.1 - "tmsh show sys log <item> range" can kill MCPD
bugs.symptoms: MCPd cpu utilization is high and renders it unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: A ranged log query where the log files are excessively large, e.g., 1 GB uncompressed.
bugs.impact: MCPd is killed due to being unresponsive, which restarts multiple daemons.
bugs.workaround: Lower the logging level, thereby decreasing the size of the file which must be parsed.

bugs.title: TCP Analytics statistics does not list all virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: In "Statistics :: Analytics : TCP", displaying the stats by virtual server will only allow the option of "Aggregated".
bugs.conditions: This occurs on virtual servers with the TCP Analytics profile attached.
bugs.impact: GUI does not list all virtual servers that have the TCP Analytics profile attached.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with displaying TCP Analytics statistics for virtual servers.

bugs.title: Sync state remaining on 'Awaiting Initial Sync' when adding third device
bugs.symptoms: When adding a third device to the trust, the sync state might be show 'Awaiting Initial Sync' on the new device, while the other devices show 'In Sync'. Note: The sync status 'Awaiting Initial Sync' is related to a hidden device group (datasync-device-<devicename>-dg), which the system automatically creates and syncs. This device group does not appear in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM or FPS is provisioned. -- The link status of the third device is offline while adding it to the trust. (This is a rarely occurring condition.)
bugs.impact: When this occurs, the sync status will show 'Awaiting Initial Sync'. There is no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: 1. Identify the device group that is out of sync using the following command: tmsh show cm sync-status The out-of-sync device group returns a status similar to the following: datasync-device-bip2-dg (Awaiting Initial Sync): One or more devices awaiting initial config sync. 2. Find the device that owns the device-group that needs to be synced by looking at the status. For example, the device group in the previous example is 'datasync-device-bip2-dg', so the device is 'bip2'. 3. From that device, run a command similar to the following, replacing 'datasync-device-bip2-dg' with the device group that is out of sync: tmsh run cm config-sync force-full-load-push to-group datasync-device-bip2-dg Note: The GUI cannot be used because this is a hidden device group that does not appear in the GUI.
bugs.fix: The system now handles this condition, so there are no longer sync problems when adding a third device to the device trust when ASM or FPS are provisioned while the link is down.

bugs.title: EdgeClient disconnect may take a lot of time when machine is moved to network with no connectivity to BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Edge Client takes a lot of time to disconnect when machine is moved to network with no connectivity to BIG-IP
bugs.conditions: * VPN is established * Machine is moved to different network (with no BIG-IP) connectivity * EdgeClient stays in "Disconnecting..." state for few minutes
bugs.impact: User have to wait until Disconnect procedure is complete
bugs.fix: Now Edge Client uses 5000msec timeout in order to complete logout HTTP request. This is enough in normal conditions

bugs.title: LDAP type CRLDP is parsed incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to 11.6.1 HF1, CRLDP authentication stopped working. It can be seen from following sample log that the URL is not parsed correctly: warning apd[15314]: 0149015e:4: fc98d22d: CRLDP Auth agent: CRL lookup failed for LDAP url 'ldap::::389//crl.certificate.../..../certificaterevocationlist?certificateRevocationList' reason 'Invalid CRLDP URL.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs only when LDAP type CRLDP is available in the client certificate and it is used from the CRL Distribution Points list.
bugs.impact: Users may fail access policy evaluation when client certification is used.
bugs.workaround: Configure other than LDAP type distribution points in the Certificate or if multiple distribution points are present in the client certificate, make sure other than LDAP type scheme succeeds before hitting LDAP CRLDP.
bugs.fix: The system now parses LDAP type CRLDP URL correctly, so after upgrading, CRLDP authentication now works as expected.

bugs.title: Adding unlimited snaplen option to support page
bugs.symptoms: Qkviews with unlimited snaplen can only be created using the terminal.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to create qkviews with unlimited snaplen using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the GUI to create qkviews with unlimited snaplen.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create qkviews with unlimited snaplen.
bugs.fix: Qkviews with unlimited snaplen can be created using the terminal and the web UI.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may enter SYN cookie mode later than expected
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP entry to SYN cookie mode may not occur even though traffic pattern would dictate that it should.
bugs.conditions: Verified accept enabled on a Virtual IP. Large volume of traffic being processed by BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP does not enter SYN cookie mode at the expected time.
bugs.workaround: Disable verified accept on all VIP TCP profiles.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP correctly enters SYN cookie mode when traffic pattern dictates that it should.

bugs.title: When using a Thales key, SSL handshake failed after restarting pkcs11d
bugs.symptoms: With a Thales key, SSL handshake failed after restarting pkcs11d daemon.
bugs.conditions: Thales netHSM is used and pkcs11d daemon is restarted.
bugs.impact: SSL traffic is failed.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart tmm after bigstart restart pkcs11d

bugs.title: Certificate serial number is not displayed properly in OCSP Stapling logs.
bugs.symptoms: The certificate serial number is not displayed properly in OCSP Stapling logs.
bugs.conditions: These logs are seen when there are any errors when fetching and validating an OCSP response, and/or when SSL debug logs are enabled.
bugs.impact: Certificate serial number is not displayed properly.

bugs.title: i2000 and i4000 series appliances may show intermittent DDM alarms/warnings at powerup that clear right away
bugs.symptoms: Messages like the following in /var/log/ltm: Oct 14 12:22:26 localhost err pfmand[5637]: 01660011:3: DDM interface: 6.0 transmit power too low alarm. Transmit power:0.0515 mWatts Oct 14 12:22:26 localhost err pfmand[5637]: 01660011:3: DDM interface:6.0 receive power too low alarm. Received power:0.0000 mWatts Oct 14 12:23:29 localhost err pfmand[5637]: 01660013:3: DDM interface:6.0 transmit power too low alarm cleared Oct 14 12:23:29 localhost err pfmand[5637]: 01660013:3: DDM interface:6.0 receive power too low alarm cleared '
bugs.conditions: i2000 or i4000 series appliances with DDM enabled and a reboot or restart of the pfmand daemon
bugs.impact: No functional impact, these are not valid DDM alarms or warnings.
bugs.workaround: Ignore DDM errors that clear right away after powerup or pfmand restart.
bugs.fix: During DDM initialization clear any alarms or warnings cached in the hardware registers.

bugs.title: Audit Log filled with constant change messages
bugs.symptoms: Frequent changes by Policy Builder fill the audit log too quickly and can affect viewing the Security Logs: Error 502 Bad Gateway when clicking "Application Security" logs
bugs.conditions: Frequent Policy Builder changes occur and no ASM device group is configured.
bugs.impact: Disk space usage and errors viewing the Application Security logs
bugs.workaround: Workarounds: 1) Turn off "Recommend Sync when Policy is not applied". (Security â€ºâ€º Options : Application Security : Preferences) 2) Enable ASM sync on a device group.
bugs.fix: Updates to the audit log are throttled at max 1/minute.

bugs.title: Disabling an interface when DDM is enabled may result in transmit power too low DDM mesages
bugs.symptoms: messages in /var/log/ltm and their associated SNMP traps: Oct 21 08:22:40 localhost err bcm56xxd[21079]: 012c0017:3: DDM interface:1.1 transmit power too low warning. Transmit power:0.0211 mWatts or Oct 21 08:04:25 localhost err bcm56xxd[19986]: 012c0018:3: DDM interface: 1.1 transmit power too low alarm. Transmit power:0.0206 mWatt
bugs.conditions: 1 - DDM enabled 2 - optics that support DDM 3 - the interface is administratively disabled via tmsh or GUI
bugs.impact: cosmetic
bugs.workaround: Ignore DDM messages about transmit power on disabled ports. BIG-IP disables the transmit laser when interfaces are disabled to ensure the link does not come up. Some optics will consider that a DDM transmit power too low error.

bugs.title: Unable to set DNS Topology Continent to Unknown via GUI
bugs.symptoms: No option in dropdown menu to select Unknown Continent when configuring DNS Topology Record via GUI. Existing Topology Records will be displayed as "Continent is", instead of "Continent is Unknown".
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure a DNS Topology Record via the GUI.
bugs.impact: Unable to set the Continent field to 'Unknown' via GUI.
bugs.workaround: Set the continent via tmsh using the command `create gtm topology ldns: continent -- server: continent --`
bugs.fix: The dropdown menu now has an option to select an "Unknown" Continent.

bugs.title: delete of pem session attribute does not work after a update
bugs.symptoms: it will not be possible to delete the session attribute through rules.
bugs.conditions: rules with session attribute update & delete
bugs.impact: unable to delete session attribute

bugs.title: Kernel panic during unic initialization
bugs.symptoms: During system initialization, the kernel panics during unic initialization.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on BIG-IP Virtual Edition if an error (on memory allocation, io etc.) occurs during unic initialization.
bugs.impact: The kernel panics, system will not boot.
bugs.fix: Initialize resources to fail gracefully on error.

bugs.title: mcpd fails validation of dhcp type virtual servers if the configured profile is /Common/udp
bugs.symptoms: mcpd will fail to load the configuration if the pre 11.6.0 configuration had a dhcp virtual server is configured using any profile that is not /Common/udp.
bugs.conditions: In pre 11.6.0 having a dhcp type virtual server with a profile other than /Common/udp and then upgrading to 11.6.0 or above.
bugs.impact: mcpd fails to load the configuration. The BIGIP will not be operational until the configuration is changed and loaded.
bugs.workaround: Before the upgrade change the profile to /Common/udp. The same change can be made to the bigip.conf file after the upgrade. Then load the config with tmsh load /sys config

bugs.title: unused error messages for SecurID
bugs.symptoms: The following customization messages can be found at Access â€ºâ€º Profiles / Policies : Customization : General then on the left pane, click "text" and goto customization settings -> access profiles -> <someAP> -> error messages -> securid prompt messages SecurID authentication: unexpected error SecurID authentication: invalid username SecurID authentication: invalid passcode SecurID authentication: invalid PIN these messages can never be seen by end user, there is no need to customize them
bugs.conditions: some securid messages customized
bugs.impact: end user will never see messages regardless of customized the messages or default
bugs.workaround: workaround is not necessary, the module is functioning as designed. the only problem is - some extended error messages do not appear. end user only see "access denied" or "unknown error"
bugs.fix: messages are not available for customization

bugs.title: Single-page application AJAX does not work properly with synchronous ajax requests
bugs.symptoms: When single-page application is enabled and a synchronous Ajax request is sent, ASM responses such as CAPTCHA response may not work as expected.
bugs.conditions: -- Single-page application is enabled in ASM. -- The single-page application sends a synchronous AJAX request that needs to be mitigated.
bugs.impact: End users may not be able to pass the CAPTCHA challenge and therefore not we able to access the application.
bugs.workaround: Modify the backend application to use an asynchronous AJAX request.

bugs.title: UCS upgrade from v10.x to v11.4.x or later incorrectly retains v10.x ca-bundle.crt
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistent CA certificate chain creation, or certificate validation/verification when verification occurs against /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt.
bugs.conditions: A system is upgraded from v10.x to v11.x/v12.x, or a v10.x UCS is restored onto a v11.x/v12.x system.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent ca-bundle.crt upgrade/UCS load handling can lead to odd / non-deterministic behavior between devices, even an HA pair / cluster of devices. Non-determinism increases because ca-bundle.crt does not ConfigSync (and appears not to sync across blades in a chassis). For example, on one device, the BIG-IP system might construct and send a full certificate chain in an SSL Server Hello, when ca-bundle.crt is specified as a Client SSL profile's 'chain', but on its peer, if the peer is using an older/inconsistent ca-bundle, the peer might be unable to construct a full certificate chain.
bugs.workaround: On every device affected by this, or on every blade in a VIPRION system affected by this: 1. Update /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt with the version that ships with this software version: cp /usr/share/defaults/fs/config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt.rpmbackup /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt 2. Reboot the system and clear the MCPD binary database. Refer to AskF5 article K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030), but essentially: touch /service/mcpd/forceload && reboot 3. After reboot, verify that the two files match (they should have the same checksum): md5sum /usr/share/defaults/fs/config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt.rpmbackup /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt

bugs.title: After upgrade from 10.2.x, tmsh and GUI do not report the default SNMP community source if it's the default.
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade from 10.2.x, tmsh and GUI do not report the default SNMP community source if it's the default. For example, in response to the 'tmsh list sys snmp' command, output in 10.2.x contains the following strings: community-name public source default in 12.1.x, the output does not contain the string 'source default', only the string 'community-name public'.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 10.2.x.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine the SNMP community name if it is the default.

bugs.title: After an upgrade, the old installation's CA bundle may be used instead of the one that comes with the new version of TMOS
bugs.symptoms: When installing a new version of TMOS, the installer will choose the bundle by looking at the current installation and what came with the target version, choosing the newer one. This check is performed incorrectly, and the old bundle may accidentally be chosen.
bugs.conditions: This happens when /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt in the old version contains an RCS revision number near the top of the file, and the newer TMOS version does not contain a revision number. (This is a change in the format of the file generated by the organization providing F5 with this bundle.)
bugs.impact: Upgrades to versions that ship the "non-RCS" files will incorrectly retain the ca-bundle.crt from the previous version, instead of keeping the newer version that shipped with those versions. This can result in certificate verification failures (e.g. for an OCSP stapling profile), or a BIG-IP creating an inconsistent/incomplete certificate chain for a virtual server.
bugs.workaround: On every device affected by this, or on every blade in a VIPRION system affected by this: 1. Update /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt with the version that ships with this software version: cp /usr/share/defaults/fs/config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt.rpmbackup /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt 2. Reboot the system and clear the MCPD binary database. Refer to SOL13030, but essentially: touch /service/mcpd/forceload && reboot 3. After reboot, verify that the two files match (they should have the same checksum): md5sum /usr/share/defaults/fs/config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt.rpmbackup /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt
bugs.fix: When installing a new version of TMOS, the installer will choose the bundle by looking at the current installation and what came with the target version, choosing the newer one. This check was performed incorrectly, and the old bundle could accidentally have been chosen. This has been fixed, and the newer version of the file is correctly chosen.

bugs.title: Oversized pool member input
bugs.symptoms: In the System :: High Availability : Fail-safe : Gateway property page in the GUI, you are allowed to enter a pool member count higher than the maximum of 65535.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when entering a minimum pool member count. The limit is 0-65535 but the GUI allows you to enter a higher number.
bugs.impact: If you enter a higher number, a validation error will occur: "Value out of range. Correct Range: 0 - 65535"
bugs.fix: The pool member input is now 5 characters long.

bugs.title: When RADIUS remote authentication is enabled, a nonexistent user is able to ssh into the BIG-IP if they present the root's key.
bugs.symptoms: Able to login to BIG-IP using root's keypair as a user which does not exist on either the BIG-IP or the RADIUS server.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure SSH keypair for passwordless login on the BIG-IP system. 2. Enable RADIUS auth on the BIG-IP system. 3. Attempt to ssh in to the BIG-IP as a user which does not exist on either the BIG-IP or the RADIUS server, using the keypair.
bugs.impact: With root SSH keys, can login as nonexistent user.
bugs.workaround: Set the default remote role to something other than admin.

bugs.title: After changing from remote auth to local auth, if SSH keys are used, SSH attempts from nonexistent users result in a connection closed
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to ssh in as a nonexistent user using SSH keypair, the connection closes.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure SSH keypair for passwordless login. 2. Set auth source to a remote type such as RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, Active Directory. 3. Set auth source back to local. 4. Attempt to ssh to BIG-IP using keypair as a user that does not exist in the BIG-IP local user directory.
bugs.impact: User does not see expected password prompt. This can be used to check which usernames are valid on the BIG-IP system, but it requires SSH keys.
bugs.workaround: None known.

bugs.title: cpcfg cannot copy a UCS file to a volume set with a root filesystem that has less free space than the total UCS size
bugs.symptoms: cpcfg fails with errors similar to: Getting configuration from HD1.2 info: Copying configuration to HD1.1 info: Applying configuration to HD1.1 info: >++++ result: info: Extracting manifest: /var/local/ucs/config.ucs info: /: Not enough free space info: 739487744 bytes required info: 259965952 bytes available info: /var/local/ucs/config.ucs: Not enough free disk space to install! info: Operation aborted.
bugs.conditions: Use cpcfg for a UCS that is larger than free space on root filesystem of target volume set.
bugs.impact: You cannot use cpcfg to copy a UCS file to a volume set with a root filesystem that has less free space than the total UCS size
bugs.workaround: Run the below to fix /etc/mtab on target (HD1.3 is used in this example; substitute the correct target volume) before cpcfg: - volumeset -f mount HD1.3 - grep HD1.3 /proc/mounts | sed 's_/mnt/HD1.3_/_g;s_//_/_g' > /mnt/HD1.3/etc/mtab - volumeset -f umount HD1.3
bugs.fix: cpcfg could incorrectly calculate the amount of free space required, refusing to do the copy unless the / filesystem on the target volume had sufficient space to do the copy (not taking into account /config, /usr, /var, and other filesystems). This has been resolved and this free space calculation is done correctly.

bugs.title: Intermittent OCSP request failures due to non-optimal default TCP profile setting
bugs.symptoms: The connection between BIG-IP and OCSP responder is not reliable since it uses the default internal TCP configuration which doesn't fit the usage well.
bugs.conditions: When the OCSP stapling option is enabled in the clientSSL profile that is in use by a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP as a SSL server fails to staple the OCSP response to the SSL client. In other words, the certificate status messages are not added in the Server Hello message in the TLS handshakes to the SSL client.
bugs.workaround: The fix proposed an optimal TCP configuration used by the connection between BIG-IP and OCSP responder which makes the connection reliable now. Therefore the virtual server can now always correctly staple the certificate status in the Server Hello message to the SSL client.

bugs.title: Custom adaptive reaper settings may be lost at upgrade time
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in 11.6.0, the adaptive-reaper was changed to use the default-eviction policy. The configuration migration script does not migrate the adaptive-reaper settings, so after upgrade the reaper settings are reset to their default.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 10.x to 11.6.0 or later.
bugs.impact: Settings may be unexpectedly changed as part of upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Inspect the values after upgrade and reconfigure them.

bugs.title: After receiving the first Gx response from the PCRF, the BWC action against a rule is lost.
bugs.symptoms: The BWC action against a rule is lost and the traffic flow is capped at the maximum bandwidth configured in the BWC policy.
bugs.conditions: A flow should be associated with a PEM rule that has atleast a BWC action along with a Gx reporting action.
bugs.impact: The traffic flow is not capped by the correct BWC action, instead it is capped by the maximum configured bandwidth in the BWC policy.
bugs.fix: The BWC policy is restored correctly after a policy update.

bugs.title: Gx CCA with non-existent or non-pem policy does not trigger CCR-u reply
bugs.symptoms: If Gx interface, from the PCRF, receives a CCA with non-existent or non-pem policy, a CCR-u with 'Unknown rule name' is not being sent back to PCRF.
bugs.conditions: By default, for any CCR with a CCA having non-existent or non-pem policy.
bugs.impact: CCR-u with 'unknown rule name' is not being send back to PCRF.
bugs.workaround: Configure PCRF to send an existing policy on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Set the sys db variable tmm.pem.session.policy.InstallUnknown to FALSE to receive CCR-u with result code UNKNOWN_RULE_NAME, otherwise there will be no CCR-u sent back.
bugs.behavior: Before: If CCA with an unknown policy is received from Gx, the BIG-IP system replied with CCR-u with Result code set to UNKNOWN_RULE_NAME. Now: You can set a sys db variable tmm.pem.session.policy.InstallUnknown to FALSE to receive CCR-u with result code UNKNOWN_RULE_NAME. Otherwise, there will be no CCR-u sent back.

bugs.title: Duplicate ASM Policies Appear in GUI
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade multiple entries with the same policy name appeared in the ASM policy list.
bugs.conditions: A system where multiple Policy history entries exist with the same revision number for the same policy undergoes upgrade. It is not clear how a device gets into this state.
bugs.impact: This appears to be a display issue only, and does not affect enforcement or performance. There are no actual duplicate policies in the system, the GUI is only displaying two rows for the affected policies. REST is also affected, which will cause problems for BIG-IQ management of a device that encountered this error.
bugs.workaround: To repair the state for that policy, make a minor change in an affected policy (e.g., updating the Description), and then run Apply Policy.
bugs.fix: ASM now correctly displays one entry per policy.
