bugs.title: Unable to add users in User Enforcement list under user-defined partition. Update check fails in user-defined partition
bugs.symptoms: If a profile is assigned to a user-defined partition, it is not possible to add users to User Enforcement list. Also, if a user-defined partition is selected, the GUI will not display a message if a there are available signatures/engine updates.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS. Create user-defined partition.
bugs.impact: You are unable to manage the profile in the user-defined partition.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to add users.
bugs.fix: Users can be added to User Enforcement list and a message will be displayed if a new update is available.

bugs.title: SNMP traps for TCP resets sent due to maintenance mode enabled may not be sent
bugs.symptoms: Due to a syntax issue in /etc/alert/alertd.conf, SNMP traps sent for notifying RSTs sent due to maintenance mode on are not being sent.
bugs.conditions: Reset cause logging and maintenance mode are enabled Snmp trap destination is configured and routable
bugs.impact: snmp traps are not sent
bugs.workaround: Adding custom trap in /config/user_alert.conf with escaped characters will workaround the issue: alert BIGIP_IP_REJECT_MAINT_MODE_FIX "RST sent from (.*) Maintenance mode \(all VIP\/SNAT\/Proxy connections disabled\)" { snmptrap OID=".1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.34" }
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now correctly sends SNMP traps when configured to do so with TCP resets in maintenance mode.

bugs.title: Large POSTs rejected after policy already completed
bugs.symptoms: When the policy has already completed, access still rejects POSTs greater than 64k. Client will see a reset, and these error messages will appear on the BIG-IP: /var/log/ltm Oct 18 19:10:04 bigip6 err tmm[14242]: 01230140:3: RST sent from 10.2.61.80:8080 to 10.2.61.10:55280, [0x1d4cb2c:2863] APM HTTP body too big /var/log/apm Oct 19 09:42:37 bigip3922mgmt err tmm1[7636]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: hud_access_process_ingress, Line: 2960
bugs.conditions: Policy has already been fully evaluated to allow. Then the client sends a large POST. Only applies to POSTs made to '/'. Would not apply if the URL is something else like '/test'. Also does not apply to clientless modes, where the db key tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize can be used to increase the maximum POST body size allowed.
bugs.impact: Clients are unable to send POST bodies to '/' that are larger than 64kb, even though the policy has already been evaluated to allow.
bugs.workaround: Move the resource from '/' to another URL.
bugs.fix: The logic of '/' in this area was changed to be consistent with other URLs.

bugs.title: Adding a client side challenge whitelist URL wildcard list
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to tell that a URL wildcard is always qualified for client side challenges. Thus dynamic URLs system can't use the CS defense to dos attack or the proactive bot defense.
bugs.conditions: dynamic URLs are running in a dos attack and the system has cs mitigation enabled.
bugs.impact: the cs mitigation is not effective and the dos mitigation moves to the rate limit.

bugs.title: General DB error when select Profiles: Protocol: SCTP profile. Error due to 'read access denied type Virtual Address profile SCTP'
bugs.symptoms: When SCTP profile is selected, the system posts a general DB error due to 'read access denied type Virtual Address profile SCTP'.
bugs.conditions: -- Login to GUI with non-Admin user. -- Select SCTP profile from the GUI
bugs.impact: Cannot get the SCTP profile.
bugs.workaround: Login with Admin user.
bugs.fix: The non-Admin user is now be able to login to GUI, select the SCTP profile and retrieve SCTP profile information correctly.

bugs.title: Google Chrome may not launch F5 VPN app automatically in specific case
bugs.symptoms: Google Chrome may not launch F5 VPN app when an auto-launch is enabled for Network Access resource and previous agent in the Access Policy is some endpoint agent.
bugs.conditions: All conditions should be met: - Google chrome is used to access APM; - Webtop has configured auto-launch of Network Access resource or webtop has type 'Network Access'; - An endpoint agent check is last interactive agent before webtop in an Access Policy.
bugs.impact: Auto launch is not working
bugs.workaround: To launch application click on the tile To avoid issue in general: Add MessageBox agent between last Endpoint Agent and 'Allow' ending to allow Google Chrome get focus before showing webtop

bugs.title: TMM failure in PEM while processing Service-Provider Disaggregation
bugs.symptoms: TMM failure in PEM while processing Service-Provider Disaggregation.
bugs.conditions: System crashes when traffic flows and rules get executed on the flow.
bugs.impact: System crashes.
bugs.workaround: Set Service-Provider Disaggregation to sp as suggested by documentation.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a TMM failure in PEM while processing Service-Provider Disaggregation.

bugs.title: Flow entry memory leaked after DHCP DORA process
bugs.symptoms: After DHCP discover/offer/request/ack process (DORA), client side connection flow entry memory is not freed.
bugs.conditions: Run the DHCP DORA process through BIG-IP (in relay mode or forwarding mode, and wait for client connection flow entry ages out.
bugs.impact: The system leaks flow entry memory. Over a long period of time, system memory will eventually run out.
bugs.fix: After DHCP discover/offer/request/ack process (DORA), client side connection flow entry memory is now freed, so no memory leak occurs.

bugs.title: vCMP guests with vlangroups may loop packets internally
bugs.symptoms: If a vlangroup is configured within a vCMP guest, under some circumstances unicast packets may be looped between the switchboard and the BIG-IP guest. This is most likely to occur when the guest is part of an HA pair.
bugs.conditions: vCMP guest, vlangroups.
bugs.impact: High CPU utilization and potentially undelivered packets.
bugs.workaround: Correctly configure proxy ARP excludes on the vlangroup and increase the FDB timeout by setting the vlan.fdb.timeout database key to a larger value such as 3600.
bugs.fix: Packets are no longer looped between vlangroup children on vCMP guests.

bugs.title: SSL Handshake fails if client tries to negotiate EC ciphers but does not present ec_point_formats extension in ClientHello
bugs.symptoms: If client tries to negotiate EC ciphers but does not present ec_point_formats extension, SSL handshake fails. The ltm error log message looks like: ***************************************************** Oct 12 11:25:08 gtm2 warning tmm1[21167]: 01260009:4: Connection error: ssl_select_suite:6799: no shared ciphers (40) Oct 12 11:25:08 gtm2 warning tmm1[21167]: 01260026:4: No shared ciphers between SSL peers 10.1.6.50.36563:10.1.6.15.443. *****************************************************
bugs.conditions: If client tries to negotiate EC ciphers but does not present ec_point_formats extension, SSL handshake fails.
bugs.impact: SSL Handshake fails.

bugs.title: Traffic data stats get lost on hardware-accelerated flows when the flows are terminated earlier
bugs.symptoms: When the clients tend to reset HTTP keep alive connections immediately after data is received, instead of gracefully closing the connections per RFC, and because these flows were reset, the system loses these packet stats for the offloaded flows. This occurs because the BIG-IP system cannot determine the traffic direction without the connection flow information. FIN packets experience the same effect of closing the connection. If there are Flow Status Updates (FSUs) after the FIN packets, they are not counted either.
bugs.conditions: Clients that reset connection immediately after data is received.
bugs.impact: PVA traffic stats may not accurately show the packets/bytes counts for the offloaded flows.
bugs.workaround: One workaround is to consult with the hardware ePVA packet and byte forward counters in addition to the global PVA traffic stats. For verification purposes, you can use the following command: # tmctl -d blade -s name,active,bus,rqm_epva_fwd_pkts,rqm_epva_fwd_bytes tmm/hsbe2_internal_pde These rqm_epva_fwd_pkts/bytes counters are the current hardware counters from the ePVA registers, which are more up to date. Note: Make sure to associate the lbb_pde number to the individual PVA numbers in the output of 'tmsh show sys pva-traffic'. To get the global stats for all PDEs (as in 'tmsh show sys pva-traffic global'), you must use a script to add up these numbers.

bugs.title: TMM cores in iRule when accessing a SIP header that has no value
bugs.symptoms: When used an iRule to access a SIP header attribute with no value, TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: Use iRule to access the value of SIP message header attribute with no value. Eg: "Supported: " IEOL "Session-Expires:" IEOL
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.
bugs.fix: Fix includes adjusting the buffer offset properly to handle the empty header attributes while parsing the SIP message.

bugs.title: LTM Monitor custom recv/send/recv-disable parameters have backslash at the end may fail to load
bugs.symptoms: If LTM monitor configuration parameters have custom strings that end with backslash, the saved configuration will fail to load.
bugs.conditions: Any of the "recv", "send", or "recv-disable" parameters having a backslash at the end, and the configuration is saved.
bugs.impact: The new configuration fails upon reload.
bugs.workaround: Do not end custom strings with backslashes.

bugs.title: RSA authentication may fail on edge client on some older windows 10 builds
bugs.symptoms: Edge client on windows may fail to fetch passcode from RSA soft token even when user enters correct pin. Tis will result in authentication failure and client logs will contain the following log entry UWebBrowserParser::Invoke, GetPasscode failed: No tokens found!
bugs.conditions: - Windows 10 machine is not updated with latest update - RSA authentication is configured on server - Integrated soft token is used to get token information
bugs.impact: Client authentication will fail
bugs.workaround: -Install latest windows 10 update.

bugs.title: IE11 on Win10 after Anniversary update may break APM session
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer version 11 on Windows version 10 Anniversary update does not send session cookie when retrieving shortcut icons. For example: <link rel="shortcut icon" href="fav_resource.ico" type="image/x-icon"> This may break APM session. This behavior is described in Microsoft issue (https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/platform/issues/8748123/).
bugs.conditions: - Windows version 10 Anniversary update. - Internet Explorer version 11. - Any Web application with "shortcut icon" resource.
bugs.impact: Web Application might not work via APM.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to use iRule to send HTTP 404 response to such requests and to delete incorrect APM session; for example: when ACCESS_SESSION_STARTED { if { [HTTP::method] equals "GET" and ( [HTTP::path] ends_with ".ico" or [HTTP::path] ends_with ".ico?F5CH=I" ) and [HTTP::header "User-Agent"] contains "Trident/7.0; rv:11.0" }{ ACCESS::session remove HTTP::respond 404 } }

bugs.title: DHCP relay is not forwarding all of the DHCPOFFERS to clients
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from v11.5.3 to v11.6.1, DHCPOFFER packets got silently dropped.
bugs.conditions: If DHCP clients send broadcast DHCP packets with non-zero unicast source IP address via BIG-IP, and regular DHCP discovery packets(0.0.0.0 source IP addrees), multiple client connection flows are created, after some are aged out, BIG-IP may stop relay DHCP server replies back to clients.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP will stop to relay DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK back to DHCP clients
bugs.workaround: Manually delete all system connection flows by doing "delete sys conn" under tmsh.

bugs.title: MRF Per-Client mode connections unable to return responses if used by another client connection
bugs.symptoms: When an outgoing connection is created in per-client mode, that connection is exclusively for use by the client whose message was routed to the destination. All messages (response or requests) received by the server are automatically forwarded to the client. The messages received from the server are forwarded to the original connection from the client (even if it has been closed).
bugs.conditions: The connection from the client closes and the client connects again.
bugs.impact: Messages from the new client connection will be routed using the previously created outgoing connection. But messages received from the server will be forwarded to the original connection from the client which is closed. These message will fail to be delivered.
bugs.fix: When message arrive from a new client connection, the outgoing connection will be to forward messages received from the server to the new connection.

bugs.title: DATA_ACK and DATA_FIN ignored on a subflow not currently used for transmission
bugs.symptoms: During an MPTCP connection, if a DATA_ACK or DATA_FIN is received on a subflow that is not currently being used to transmit data, that DATA_ACK or DATA_FIN is ignored. Clients generally respond on the same subflow that they received data on, making this situation somewhat rare.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP is in use on a connection and a DATA_ACK or DATA_FIN is received on a subflow that is not currently being used to transmit data.
bugs.impact: The DATA_ACK or DATA_FIN is ignored. If the same information is not sent on other subflows, this can cause the connection to hang until the subflow times out.
bugs.fix: Accept DATA_ACK and DATA_FIN on any subflow.

bugs.title: Preserve original ownership of /etc/hosts file
bugs.symptoms: CLI VPN client changes ownership of /etc/hosts file to root. After disconnecting from VPN, ownership is not restored back to the original.
bugs.conditions: CLI VPN client is used to establish VPN connection on Mac/Linux.
bugs.impact: It breaks usability of /etc/resolv.conf for OS apps.
bugs.workaround: An administrator can restore ownership of /etc/hosts using system tools.
bugs.fix: Now the Mac / Linux CLI client preserves the original ownership of /etc/hosts after disconnecting from VPN.

bugs.title: Relocate TUC AVP to group AVP USU
bugs.symptoms: Current implementation sends Traffic Change Usage (TCU) in MSCC at the same level as USU.
bugs.conditions: Anytime there is a TCU.
bugs.impact: Interoperability with ZTE OCS, which requires it as a child USU (Used-Service-Unit)

bugs.title: Topology load balancing improvement
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, load balancing decisions can result in an unequal or unexpected distribution.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when topology load balancing is used for a wide IP and more than one pool share the highest assigned score for a particular load balancing decision.
bugs.impact: The resulting load balancing decisions can lead to an unequal or unexpected distribution of pool selections.
bugs.workaround: Topology records and pools can be configured to avoid the conditions which cause the condition.
bugs.fix: A system DB variable, gtm.wideiptoporandom, has been added. When this system DB variable is assigned the value of "enable" and more than one pool shares the highest assigned score for a given load balancing decision, a random pool is selected.

bugs.title: Unable to add multiple User-Defined alerts with the same search category
bugs.symptoms: Adding 2 or more User-Defined alerts causes to DB exception error.
bugs.conditions: Provision FPS Malware Detection license Add multiple User-Defined alerts with the same "Search In" category.
bugs.impact: Can impact detection of certain malware.
bugs.workaround: Adding single record each time. Use TMSH or Rest.
bugs.fix: GUI allows adding multiple User-Defined alerts of the same search category.

bugs.title: Memory leak when using insert action in pem rule and flow gets aborted
bugs.symptoms: Memory keeps increasing in PEM after several hours of live service.
bugs.conditions: Insert action in pem rule and response spawning multiple segments. Connection gets aborted midway.
bugs.impact: Connections can get reset once memory usage increases beyond threshold
bugs.fix: free xfrags when aborting flows

bugs.title: No flow control when using content-insertion with compression
bugs.symptoms: Packets can get queued in PEM and cause performance impact. It could cause memory corruptions in some cases
bugs.conditions: This issue can happen when system there is are a lot of connections with compression enabled, hardware offload is not enabled, and content insertion is enabled
bugs.impact: Performance impact to flows and possible system crash.
bugs.workaround: Enable hardware offload and use the pem throttle feature for content insertion

bugs.title: Hung tasks leading to system problems and lack of management access via ssh/GUI
bugs.symptoms: Problems with bigd, snmpd and other daemons. System becomes inaccessible via ssh and GUI. Hung tasks recorded in kern logs, typically snmpd, bigd, chmand, big3d hung. Caused by Centos kernel bug in netlink code where mutex is left locked on error path.
bugs.conditions: Seen when a system is handling heavy SNMP traffic and memory is low.
bugs.impact: SNMP traffic fails with hung tasks. Reboot required.
bugs.workaround: Apparently reducing SNMP load helps avoid/postpone the problem.

bugs.title: iControl REST API sets non-default profile prop to "none"; properties not present in iControl REST API responseiControl REST API, sets profile's non-default property value as "none"; properties missing in iControl REST API response
bugs.symptoms: For profiles, iControl REST does not provide visibility for profile property override when "none" is specified, including references, passwords, and array of strings.
bugs.conditions: -- Use iControl REST API. -- string, enum, or vector of enum/string property explicitly set to "none" for a component within any REST API endpoint specialized in /etc/icrd.conf.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST API response skips these elements. iControl REST does not provide visibility for profile property overrides.
bugs.fix: iControl REST API now returns elements (i.e., string, enum, or vector of enum/string property that is explicitly set to "none" for a component within any REST API endpoint specialized in /etc/icrd.conf) with a value "none". The exclusion to this policy is the secured attributes. Secured attributes are always excluded from the iControl REST API response.

bugs.title: AVR reports incorrect 'actions' in ACL reports
bugs.symptoms: AVR reports incorrect 'actions' in ACL reports: -- 'Default" reports as 'Drop'. -- 'Drop" reports as 'Reject'. -- 'Reject" reports as 'Accept'. -- 'Accept" reports as 'Accept decisively'. -- 'Accept decisively' reports as "Default'.
bugs.conditions: AVR reporting on ACL statistics.
bugs.impact: The system reports incorrect actions.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: AVR reports now shows correct actions.

bugs.title: Device error: crypto codec queue is stuck
bugs.symptoms: Under some stress conditions, the N3FIPS device in the 10350F platform may stop responding to requests and cause the following error logs to appear in /var/log/ltm.log: Oct 3 11:44:53 n3fips-1 crit tmm1[20259]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec fips-crypto0-1 queue is stuck. Oct 3 11:44:53 n3fips-1 crit tmm9[20259]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec fips-crypto0-9 queue is stuck. From this point on, the command "tmsh show sys crypto fips" will always return an error. As a result, the following SNMP trap will be generated: V2Trap(140) .1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0=12682 .1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.4.1.0=.1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.156 .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.1.1="Vendor init error: -36 FIPS device fault" .1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.4.3.0=.1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4
bugs.conditions: This is seen randomly under some stress conditions.
bugs.impact: The unit can no longer process any FIPS related traffic and all FIPS operations will fail. Rebooting the unit will cause the FIPS device to disappear from the system and it will not find any supported FIPS devices.
bugs.workaround: Power cycling the unit will recover full FIPS functionality. This can be done by selecting "P --- Power on/off host subsystem" in the AOM Command Menu and then toggling the power state.

bugs.title: Responses to some of the challenge JS are not zipped.
bugs.symptoms: Performance is affected on the JS challenge.
bugs.conditions: The following is turned on in the application dos configuration : CS challenge, or PBD challenge when Suspicious browsers are disabled or the Device-ID challenge.
bugs.impact: 1. These responses consume more CPU and more Bandwidth than needed. 2. Client-side latency is degraded. 3. More disk space is utilized than needed
bugs.fix: Some of the JS challenge have better performance now.

bugs.title: VCMP guest /shared file system growth due to /shared/tmp/guestagentd.out file
bugs.symptoms: /shared disk usage growth and the diskmonitor can alarm when percent of disk usage reaches the configured threshold.
bugs.conditions: VCMP guest, overtime /shared/tmp/guestagentd.out grows and not rotated.
bugs.impact: /shared filesystem can fill and cause alerting and inability to copy files such as .iso to /shared.
bugs.workaround: 1. periodically delete the non-critical file /shared/tmp/guestagentd.out OR, 2. bigstart stop guestagentd (this will disable vcmp health feature on the host)
bugs.fix: The guestagentd logs no longer fill the tmp file.

bugs.title: tmm crash during classification hitless upgrade if virtual server configuration is modified
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash
bugs.conditions: 1. classification hitless upgrade is triggered 2. pending (not saved) changes on any of the virtual servers
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Change of virtual server configuration triggers new library to be loaded during upgrade which wasn't expected by hitless upgrade mechanism and led to tmm crash. This is fixed in versions starting with 12.1.2.

bugs.title: Missing warning when typing current volume during a hotfix installation
bugs.symptoms: When installing a hotfix, typing the current volume throws no warning.
bugs.conditions: Typing the current volume.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic, the installation doesn't continue.
bugs.workaround: Do not select the current volume when installing a hotfix.
bugs.fix: A warning message is displayed when typing current volume during a hotfix installation.

bugs.title: Timestamps not available in bash history on non-login interactive shells
bugs.symptoms: There are no timestamps in bash history when bash is initiated from tmsh.
bugs.conditions: This issue arises when an Administrator or Resource Administrator with tmsh as the default shell runs bash from tmsh and then runs the 'history' command.
bugs.impact: Running 'history' in bash will not include timestamps of commands.
bugs.workaround: Timestamps can be added to bash history by running the following command in bash: export HISTTIMEFORMAT="%Y-%m-%d %T ".
bugs.fix: Added timestamps to bash history for non-login interactive shells.

bugs.title: TMM core in mptcp
bugs.symptoms: When MPTCP is enabled on a virtual server, TMM may generate a core file and restart.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP must be in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable MPTCP.
bugs.fix: Prevented TMM core.

bugs.title: AFM rules do not support the syntax ip_addr%vlan_tag in the address specification.
bugs.symptoms: AFM rules do not support the syntax ip_addr%vlan_tag in the address specification.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the syntax ip_addr%vlan_tag in the address specification.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the syntax to define source addresses.
bugs.workaround: The VLAN property is supported only on source address specification with a separate keyword 'vlan'.

bugs.title: BigDB.dat may become truncated
bugs.symptoms: BigDB.dat may become truncated.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are not well understood.
bugs.impact: Tomcat and possibly mcpd may restart due to having incorrectly generated configuration.
bugs.fix: A truncated BigDB.dat no longer causes Tomcat mcpd to restart.

bugs.title: Safenet uninstall is unable to remove libgem.so
bugs.symptoms: When uninstalling Safenet client 6.2 from a BIG-IP chassis, it can't remove libgem.so and generates the following error: rm: cannot remove `/usr/lib64/openssl/engines/libgem.so': Read-only file system.
bugs.conditions: This can be triggered when uninstalling the safenet client using the command safenet-sync.sh -u.
bugs.impact: Uninstall is unable to complete.
bugs.fix: When uninstalling Safenet client 6.2 from a BIG-IP chassis, the system can now remove libgem.so, so there is no error condition, and uninstall can complete as expected.

bugs.title: Cannot delete keys without extension .key (and certificates without .crt) using the Configuration utility
bugs.symptoms: You cannot delete keys without extension .key (and certificates without .crt) using the Configuration utility, which returns an error message similar to the following example: 01020036:3: The requested Certificate File (/Common/example.crt) was not found
bugs.conditions: The presence of SSL certificates and keys created without the .crt and .key extensions. This might have happened, for example, if the SSL certificates and keys were created using the tmsh utility.
bugs.impact: Cannot delete keys without extension .key (and certificates without .crt) using the Configuration utility.
bugs.workaround: You can use the tmsh utility to delete affected SSL certificates and keys. You would use commands similar to the following example: tmsh delete sys crypto cert example tmsh delete sys crypto key example
bugs.fix: You can now delete keys without extension .key (and certificates without .crt) using the Configuration utility.

bugs.title: BIG-IP doesn't support more than 4 NICs on Hyper-V on Windows Server 2012
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP doesn't support more than 4 NICs. As a result of this issue, you may encounter following symptoms: - BIG-IP boot time is increased. - Number of interfaces attached to tmm aren't more than 4 NICs. - In the /var/log/boot.log file, you observe messages similar to the following examples: + info plymouthd: udev still not settled. Waiting.udevd[367]: worker [380] unexpectedly returned with status 0x0100 + info plymouthd: udevd[367]: worker [380] failed while handling '/devices/LNXSYSTM:00/device:00/PNP0A03:00/device:08/VMBUS:01/vmbus_11' + info plymouthd: udevd[367]: worker [373] unexpectedly returned with status 0x0100 RHEL7.2 (or newer) guests are similarly affected, so this issue is not unique to BIG-IP 7.2 kernels. The issue isn't reproduced on Hyper-V on Window Server 2012 R2.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - Your hypervisor version is Hyper-V on Windows Server 2012. - You have more than 4 NIC attached to BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP doesn't support more than 4 NICs on Hyper-V on Windows Server 2012.

bugs.title: A route for /32 mask can't be added
bugs.symptoms: Adding a route for /32 mask will be allowed, with no error message, however, /32 route will not be populated into kernel.
bugs.conditions: Complex route overriding default routes and adding /32 mask route
bugs.impact: Route is not added to the routing table.
bugs.workaround: There will be error message like Feb 14 12:24:09 disc5 err chmand[2476]: 012a0003:3: Kernel returns error : Network is unreachable Feb 14 12:24:09 disc5 err chmand[2476]: 012a0003:3: Mgmt Operation:0 Dest:7.7.7.7 Feb 14 12:24:09 disc5 err chmand[2476]: 012a0003:3: Prefix Length:32 Gateway:10.255.0.1 mgmt:0 in /var/log/ltm until it's fixed properly.

bugs.title: Certificates with ISO/IEC 10646 encoded strings may prevent certificate list page from displaying
bugs.symptoms: SSL Certificate List page displays "An error has occurred while trying to process your request." or unable to view certificate information via iControl/REST.
bugs.conditions: Certificate with multi-byte encoded strings.
bugs.impact: Unable to view certificate list page or view certificate information via iControl/REST.

bugs.title: Potential crash in a multi-blade chassis during CMP state changes.
bugs.symptoms: Potential TMM crash resulting in flows being impacted.
bugs.conditions: A multi-blade chassis with PEM needs to undergo a CMP state change with flows on the active blade.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: NULL check has been added to facilitate a graceful failure during asynchronous handling.

bugs.title: Potential crash in a multi-blade chassis during CMP state changes.
bugs.symptoms: Potential TMM crash resulting in flows being impacted.
bugs.conditions: A multi-blade chassis with PEM needs to undergo a CMP state change with flows on the active blade.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: NULL check has been added prior to calling a callback for asynchronous handling.

bugs.title: Reducing the response time of the Device ID collection
bugs.symptoms: Device ID collection time being run on the browser needs to be faster.
bugs.conditions: Device ID collection is enabled on either the ASM Policy or DOS Profile.
bugs.impact: New sessions in the browser may take slightly longer to reach the website than necessary.
bugs.fix: Slightly reduced the response time of the Device ID collection.

bugs.title: AWS - Sometimes iid-document is not loaded on instance startup
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes iid-document is not loaded on instance startup.
bugs.conditions: VE in AWS (some of new regions). This can happen when network traffic is blocked during boot or if AWS metadata service is temporary not available.
bugs.impact: iid-document is missing and AWS Advanced HA functionality is not working as expected.
bugs.workaround: Manually execute the following script: /etc/vadc-init/aws-init.

bugs.title: ILX node.js process may be restarted if a single operation takes more than 15 seconds
bugs.symptoms: There is an ILX node.js process restart that occurs, conditional on the code and operations of the node.js process. The restart occurs when one specific operation (code path in your node.js app) takes longer than 15 seconds to complete.
bugs.conditions: -- Running ILX with a node.js RPC or streaming setup. -- A single operation takes more than 15 seconds.
bugs.impact: Connflow is dropped, traffic processing for the flows handled by that process stops until it restarts fully.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can time yourself in your node.js app, to either make sure operations complete within the timeframe, or determine where operations exceed the 15 second limit and rework the code so that operations complete within 15 seconds.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a time restriction on a single operation.

bugs.title: mgmt bridge takes HWADDR of guest vm's tap interface
bugs.symptoms: MGMT interface becomes unreachable and stops responding to traffic. Whenever guest is in provisioned state MAC address assigned to mgmt is correct (taken from base MAC). Whenever guest is in deployed state MAC address on host mgmt interface changes and is exactly the same as mgmt_vm_tap MAC.
bugs.conditions: The platform shipped with a "low" F5 base_mac A Linux bridge by default takes as its mac the lowest mac of its constituent interfaces. This did not cause a problem before because F5 Networks systems' baseMacs have historically been "low", e.g., with legacy_baseMacs in {00:01:D7, 00:0A:49, 00:23:E9}. When a guest tap interface is added to the mgmt bridge, the bridge takes its Linux default action, which is to take as its mac the lowest mac address of its constituent interfaces. With the comparison min(eth0's mac, guestTap's mac) returning guestTap's mac, the mgmt bridge incorrectly assumes a guestTapIntfc mac.
bugs.impact: Connectivity to the vCMP host platform is lost when the guest is deployed.
bugs.workaround: Use ifconfig to ensure that the mac address of the mgmt bridge never changes from eth0. For example, the following command sets as the mac of this bridge, the value passed in Mac. ifconfig <bridgeName= mgmt> hw ether <Mac of Eth0> Note: This assumes that eth0 will always be contained in the mgmt bridge.
bugs.fix: The system now uses ifconfig to assign the mac of interface eth0 to bridge mgmt.

bugs.title: BWC: tmm crash can occur if dynamic BWC policy is used at max-user-rate over 2gbps
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes while using Bandwidth Control (BWC) dynamic policies.
bugs.conditions: max-user-rate is set at 2gbps or higher.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use a maximum of 1gbps for dynamic BWC policy max-user-rate.
bugs.fix: tmm crashes while using Bandwidth Control (BWC) dynamic policies with max-user-rate set at 2gbps or higher.
bugs.behavior: no

bugs.title: TCP Fast Open does not work for Responses < 1 MSS
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP does not send the data until receiving the first client ACK.
bugs.conditions: TCP Fast Open requests an object of less than 1 MSS in size. Fast open and delayed acks enabled.
bugs.impact: Delayed completion of the connection.
bugs.workaround: Disable delayed acks.
bugs.fix: TCP sends SYN/ACK immediately after receiving the SYN, and the response as soon as it arrives from the server.

bugs.title: Response Policy Zones can trigger even after entry removed from zone
bugs.symptoms: If an entry (resource record) is removed from a response policy zone it is possible that it may still trigger as a match for RPZ.
bugs.conditions: -- An RPZ zone contains an entry, for example badzone.example.com. -- That entry is subsequently removed.
bugs.impact: The badzone.example.com entries will continue to be blocked by RPZ, even though the item has been removed.
bugs.workaround: Delete /var/db/zxfrd.bin and /var/db/tmmdns.bin and restart the system using the following command: bigstart restart zxfrd. This recreates the databases without the remnants of the deleted entries.
bugs.fix: The deleted entries are now properly handled and no longer trigger incorrect matches.

bugs.title: GUI LTM Virtual Server Connection Limit and Connection Rate Limit
bugs.symptoms: Depending on the Virtual Server Type selection the Connection Limit and Connection Rate Limit may or may not be supported. When changing the Virtual Server Type the GUI sometimes displays or hides the Connection Limit and/or Connection Rate Limit inconsistently.
bugs.conditions: When switching between Types, the Connection Limit and Connection Rate Limit may or may not be displayed or hidden correctly for the selected type.
bugs.impact: When updating the Virtual Server, if a value is persisted when it is not supported, the user will get an error. Or if a value is supported, but not visible, you cannot set the value through the GUI.
bugs.workaround: For values that are saved when they are not supported and the user gets an error, the user can set the value to 0. If the Connection Limit or Connection Rate Limit is not displayed in the GUI, the user can use tmsh to set the value.
bugs.fix: Ensure GUI is displaying and hiding Connection Limit and Connection Rate Limit correctly for each Virtual Server Type.

bugs.title: Zero length SSL records improperly processed with AES-GCM on 2000s/2200s, 4000s/4200v, B4450 platforms
bugs.symptoms: If a 2000s/2200s, 4000s/4200v, B4450 platform negotiates an AES-GCM SSL connection and is given an SSL record with a zero length plaintext payload, it will improperly process it, resulting in a bad record.
bugs.conditions: AES-GCM SSL record with a zero length plaintext payload on the BIG-IP 2000s/2200s, 4000s/4200v, B4450 platform.
bugs.impact: Bad record errors.
bugs.fix: AES-GCM SSL records with zero length plaintext will no longer result in a bad record.

bugs.title: Static route create validation is less stringent than static route delete validation
bugs.symptoms: When creating a static route the BIG-IP ensures that there is a self-IP on the same interface, but does not check to make sure that there is a self-IP on the same interface that uses the same IP protocol (IPv4 vs. IPv6). If the route is created with only self-IPs that use different IP protocols, then the system will not allow you to delete any self-IPs on the same interface as the static route.
bugs.conditions: Using a static route that has one IP protocol on a given interface along with self-IPs that, while on the same interface, use a different IP protocol.
bugs.impact: Unable to delete certain self-IPs.
bugs.workaround: In order to delete the self-IPs you can either: 1) Delete the static route. or 2) Create a self-IP on the same interface and using the IP protocol as the static route.
bugs.fix: Added validation to ensure that when a static route is created there is at least one self-IP that uses the same interface and IP protocol.

bugs.title: First few handshakes fail after chassis/appliance reboot when using HSM
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting with an HSM configured, you notice the first few handshakes fail, with the following error signature in /var/log/ltm: warning tmm3[13085]: 01260009:4: Connection error: info tmm3[13085]: 01260013:6: ssl_hs_vfy_sign_srvkeyxchg:9921: sign_srvkeyxchg (80) 1260013:6: SSL Handshake failed for TCP <src> -> <dest>
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the first few connections after reboot when an HSM is configured, and seems to occur if the device does not immediately pass traffic after reboot.
bugs.impact: The initial SSL connections will fail, then normal operation will resume.

bugs.title: getLopSensorData "sensor data reply too short" errors with FND300 DC PSU
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series or 5000-/7000-series appliances with FND300 DC power supplies running BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2, errors similar to the following are logged every 30+ seconds: warning chmand[8220]: 012a0004:4: getLopSensorData: LopHlprDev: sensor data reply too short, objId: 16d size: 39 warning chmand[8220]: 012a0004:4: getLopSensorData: LopHlprDev: sensor data reply too short, objId: 16e size: 39 In addition, the PSU status is reported as Not Present by the "tmsh show sys hardware" and "tmctl chassis_power_supply_status_stat" commands. tmsh show sys hardware: Chassis Power Supply Status Index Status Current 1 not-present NA 2 not-present NA tmctl chassis_power_supply_status_stat: name index status input_status output_status fan_status current_status ============================================================================== pwr1 1 2 2 2 2 0 pwr2 2 2 2 2 2 0 Totals 3 4 4 4 4 0 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ (Where a status value of 2 == Not Present)
bugs.conditions: This problem occurs when all of the following conditions are true: 1. BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series or 5000-/7000-series appliance 2. One or more FND300 DC power supplies installed 3. Running BIG-IP v11.5.4-HF2
bugs.impact: 1. Errors logged every 30+ seconds 2. PSU status is reported as Not Present
bugs.fix: The status of FND300 DC power supplies is reported correctly on BIG-IP 2000-/4000-series and 5000-/7000-series appliances.

bugs.title: DoSL7: total site TPS is lower than a single entity TPS
bugs.symptoms: A total site TPS is reported lower than a single TPS.
bugs.conditions: An entity is reported for the first time in the attack.
bugs.impact: Confusion in the reporting.

bugs.title: AVR: Changes to some entities on AVR DNS tmsh reports
bugs.symptoms: Some entities have been changed for AVR DNS reports on TMSH command. The attack-type entity is no longer available since DNS no longer provides this information to AVR, instead, there is attack-vector entity. The transaction-outcome entity was renamed to dns-transaction-outcome as part of clear separation for all transaction-outcomes.
bugs.conditions: Accessing AVR DNS reports using TMSH
bugs.impact: Old scripts that using the previous entities for DNS reports will break.
bugs.fix: The attack-type entity is no longer available on AVR reports for DNS. Instead, the attack-vector (vector) entity is provided to AVR. The transaction-outcome entity was renamed to dns-transaction-outcome on AVR reports.

bugs.title: Edge client starts new APM session when Captive portal session expire
bugs.symptoms: When a Captive portal session expires during Network Access, Edge-Client shows the Captive portal Authentication page. If the user doesn't authenticate for some amount of time (30-60sec) the Edge Client tries to disconnect the current session. When the user successfully authenticates, Edge Client starts new APM session instead of waiting until the user authenticates on Captive page.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when Captive portal is configured and the session expires.
bugs.impact: The Edge Client starts a new session when it should re-use the existing session.

bugs.title: LTM Configuration Found after Provisioning VCMP
bugs.symptoms: When provisioning VCMP on a previously enabled LTM unit, the existing LTM configuration is not automatically removed.
bugs.conditions: VCMP provisioned with LTM configuration.
bugs.impact: The behavior of the BIG-IP is undefined when VCMP is provisioned and LTM is configured. The impact can range from none to intermittent or total traffic loss.
bugs.workaround: Delete pool members, pools, and virtual servers before provisioning VCMP.
bugs.fix: Virtual servers will be disabled when VCMP is provisioned. If VCMP is already provisioned virtual servers can't be created unless they are created as a disabled virtual.

bugs.title: New APM client with hangup error code sent fail to terminate sessions on old version BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: There are no visible functional issues. But when the APM end user clicks the logout button or hangs up on the the client, the server (tmm) doesn't delete the session immediately. The session will later get deleted as part of the session timeout.
bugs.conditions: New APM client on an older BIG-IP release.
bugs.impact: Sessions won't get deleted immediately but will get deleted eventually depending on the access profile timeout. There might be memory pressure based on the load.
bugs.workaround: Write an iRule to delete sessions based on the uri/query param.

bugs.title: lasthop rmmod causes kernel panic
bugs.symptoms: If someone attempts to unload the lasthop kernel module, it will cause a kernel panic.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to unload the lasthop kernel module.
bugs.impact: The system reboots.
bugs.workaround: Avoid running the following command: # rmmod lasthop
bugs.fix: The lasthop kernel module should never be unloaded. The system now prevents the lasthop kernel module from being unloaded, so no kernel panic occurs.

bugs.title: SCTP::local_port iRule not supported in MRF events
bugs.symptoms: SCTP::local_port iRule not supported in MRF events
bugs.conditions: If MRF events are used, such as MR_INGRESS, MR_EGRESS and MR_FAILED events are used.
bugs.impact: SCTP::local_port won't work under MR events.
bugs.fix: After the fix, SCTP::local_port iRule will be supported in MRF events.

bugs.title: Policy Sync can fail over a lossy network
bugs.symptoms: Policy Sync fails.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IPs are connected over a lossy link.
bugs.impact: HA redundancy fails.
bugs.workaround: tmsh modify sys db TM.TCPProgressive.AutoBufferTuning value disabled
bugs.fix: Change configuration as described.

bugs.title: Learn flags of subviolations are incorrectly updated when all violations are updated by REST
bugs.symptoms: When the learn flags of all violations are updated by REST PATCH, the learn flags of all subviolations are incorrectly updated as well.
bugs.conditions: The learn flags of all violations are updated in a single REST PATCH operation.
bugs.impact: The learn flags of all subviolations are incorrectly updated as well.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Update violations in individual REST operations. -- Update the subviolations after the violation update.

bugs.title: Internal sync-change conflict after update to local users table
bugs.symptoms: User sync is initiated unexpectedly and automatically by the REST framework. To the internal sync system, this appears as if the same change is being made manually on all devices, causing a change conflict. In other words, 'show cm sync-status' returns output similar to the following: -------------------------------------------------------- CM::Sync Status -------------------------------------------------------- Color red Status Changes Pending Mode high-availability Summary There is a possible change conflict between device1 and device2. Details device1: connected mydg (Changes Pending): There is a possible change conflict between device1 and device2. - Recommended action: Synchronize device2 to group mydg In addition, users that were synchronized by the REST framework may not have the correct role and/or partition assigned to them.
bugs.conditions: -- A sync-failover device group exists. -- The REST framework's 'gossip' mechanism is set up correctly, which should happen automatically, but might not be ready. You can confirm that this is the case by running 'restcurl shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-bigips/devices'. The output must show all your devices, and show that they all have the same 'version' and the same 'restFrameworkVersion'.
bugs.impact: An unexpected change conflict between devices. In some cases, high CPU utilization by restjavad may be observed.
bugs.workaround: -- When you have the change conflict, force a sync to the device group from the device where the user was originally created. -- If the high CPU utilization by restjavad persists after a full sync, you can remediate the CPU utilization by restarting the restjavad service: restart sys service restjavad
bugs.fix: Internal sync-change conflict is no longer present after update to local users table.

bugs.title: Bigd memory leak
bugs.symptoms: The bigd process grows in size until one of two things happens: -- The Linux kernel runs out of memory and OOM kills the bigd process (or potentially some other large process) a few hours after the system starts up. -- On high-end platforms, the bigd process grows to just under 4GB in virtual size (vsize) and starts failing in unexpected ways, for example marking targets down that are not actually down, or failing to detect targets that are down.
bugs.conditions: -- You are running BIG-IP 12.1.5.3. -- You have HTTPS monitors configured.
bugs.impact: A memory leak occurs. Depending on the platform, process daemons might restart or fail. Monitored targets may be incorrectly marked down. Although restarting bigd is not traffic-impacting, it is possible that other daemon processes restart due to low memory conditions, and could disrupt traffic while they restart.
bugs.workaround: There is an engineering hotfix available HotFix-BIGIP-12.1.5.3.0.16.5-EHF16 :: https://downloads.f5.com/esd/product.jsp?sw=BIG-IP&pro=big-ip_v12.x&ver=12.1.5 To work around this, you can switch to non-HTTPS monitors until the engineering hotfix can be applied. Once you switch to non-HTTPS, restart bigd to release the leaked memory (restarting bigd should not be service impacting).

bugs.title: Policy sync status not shown on standby device in HA case
bugs.symptoms: After policy sync, policy sync statuses are not shown in admin GUI on standby device in a failover device group.
bugs.conditions: - Create a failover device group whose members are in a bigger sync-only device group for policy. - Initiate a policy sync from an active device - Check policy sync stats on standby device
bugs.impact: It does not affect sync functionality and user still can see the sync status on an active device.
bugs.workaround: Check sync status on an active device in the group.
bugs.fix: User will be able to see the sync statuses on a standby device, including itself as well as the list of devices in the whole sync-only group where sync is performed.

bugs.title: Routes added by 'Allow local DNS servers' are not removed even if these DNS servers are no longer among client's local DNS servers.
bugs.symptoms: -Routes to local DNS that get added due to 'allow local DNS' option in Network Access config do not get removed once network changes after VPN is established.
bugs.conditions: - 'Allow local DNS' option is selected in Network Access config. - BIG-IP administrator changes the network configuration after VPN is connected.
bugs.impact: If the BIG-IP administrator changes the network after a VPN is connected, and if DNS servers have changed, then routes to old DNS servers (which may or may not be reachable) will be left in the routing table.
bugs.fix: In Network Access, routes added by 'Allow local DNS servers' are now removed when they are no longer among a client's local DNS servers if the client's network properties change.

bugs.title: Suspended iRules cannot complete on aborted flows
bugs.symptoms: An suspended iRule does not resume if the connection aborts in the interim.
bugs.conditions: an iRule suspends, connection aborts.
bugs.impact: Not all business logic may execute.
bugs.fix: Keep the connflow alive if TCL operations are pending.

bugs.title: tmm crashes when classification is enabled and ftp traffic is flowing trough the box
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash
bugs.conditions: 1. classification profile attached to the virtual server 2. ftp traffic flows through the system 3. complex configuration with iRules and multiple modules enabled
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: remove classification profile from the virtual server
bugs.fix: Incorrect memory management in one of classification matching mechanisms led to a crash.

bugs.title: TMM might crash when TCP DSACK is enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes
bugs.conditions: All of the below are required to see this behavior: DSACK is enabled MPTCP, rate-pace, tail-loss-probe, and fast-open are disabled. cmetrics-cache-timeout is set to zero; congestion control is high-speed, new-reno, reno, or scalable; AND Nagle is not set to 'auto'. an iRule exists that changes any of the conditions above besides DSACK. various client packet combinations interact in certain ways with the iRule logic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Change any of the conditions above.
bugs.fix: TCP maintains state appropriately to avoid crash.

bugs.title: unic: flow redirects for non-default cmp-hash on untagged VLANs
bugs.symptoms: -- Low throughput. -- Flow re-directs in tmstat.
bugs.conditions: -- Untagged VLAN is in use -- A non-default cmp hash, such as src-ip or dst-ip, is in use.
bugs.impact: Performance degradation.

bugs.title: Support for overriding SPDAG address bit selection and L1 buckets on P8
bugs.symptoms: Traffic is highly imbalanced among TMMs in the chassis when using SPDAG (cmp-hash src-ip/dst-ip).
bugs.conditions: When using SPDAG (cmp-hash src-ip/dst-ip), the P8 DAG uses a subset of the bits of IPv4/IPv6 addresses. Traffic may not have enough entropy in the selected bits to be able to distribute evenly among the TMMs in the chassis.
bugs.impact: With traffic being imbalanced, a small group of TMMs in the entire chassis may be overloaded. The high load may cause a failover. The new active peer will be hit with the same traffic imbalance.
bugs.workaround: If the environment can control the allocation of remote IP addresses, allocate IP addresses with more entropy in the bottom 16 bits.
bugs.fix: The DB variable "dag.config" may be used to override the P8 DAG's address bit selection. The DB variable modifies low-level internals of the P8 DAG which are not published. This interface shouldn't be used generally by customers. The intention is that PD can craft a suitable config from sample traffic. Finding a good config is not straight forward.

bugs.title: Unable to add and modify URL parameters containing square brackets "[]" in FPS GUI
bugs.symptoms: When trying to add URL parameters containing square brackets "[]" in FPS GUI >> URL the parameters name become "0". If trying to modify, the parameters are not saved.
bugs.conditions: Provision FPS Create URL
bugs.impact: FPS GUI
bugs.workaround: via tmsh, an example: tmsh modify security anti-fraud profile criteria urls modify { /xml.php { parameters add { "mouse\[2]" } } }
bugs.fix: It is now possible to add parameters containing square brackets in FPS GUI.

bugs.title: dhclient doesn't honor 'interface-mtu' request-options
bugs.symptoms: Requesting MTU value from DHCP server is explicitly disabled using a configuration similar to the following: tmsh modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config request-options delete { interface-mtu }. But if DHCP send MTU value in its reply, this MTU will be configured on BIG-IP management interface.
bugs.conditions: DHCP server ignoring option sent by BIG-IP DHCP client.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP accepts the MTU value provided.
bugs.workaround: 1. Add supersede interface-mtu 1500; to interface "mgmt" section of the /etc/dhclient.conf file. 2. Restart dhclient.
bugs.fix: dhclient now honors 'interface-mtu' request-options.

bugs.title: In some cases, download of PAC file by edge client may fail
bugs.symptoms: Edge client may fail to download PAC file and incorrectly apply proxy configuration after VPN connection.
bugs.conditions: - User machine proxy configuration points to a proxy auto configuration file. - Network access proxy configuration points to a proxy auto configuration file. - PAC file URI in either case has uppercase characters. - PAC file is hosted on a server where resource names are case sensitive.
bugs.impact: PAC file download will fail and client will use incorrect proxy settings due to unavailability of PAC file.
bugs.workaround: Use only lowercase characters in PAC file URI.
bugs.fix: Now Edge client can download PAC files from URIs that have uppercase as well as lowercase characters.

bugs.title: SNMP reports incorrect values for F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolQueueOnConnectionLimit
bugs.symptoms: The F5 BIG-IP local mib has the wrong value definitions for F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolQueueOnConnectionLimit allowed(0),disallowed(1) instead of disabled(0),enabled(1)
bugs.conditions: This occurs on any platform that supports this MIB field and has LTM Pool configurations.
bugs.impact: Information mismatch

bugs.title: Pending sector utility may write repaired sector incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: When the pendsect process detects a pending sector and performs a repair of that sector, incorrect data may be written to an incorrect location on the hard disk. This may result in corruption of files on the BIG-IP volume that may not be detected for an indeterminate period of time after the pending sector was repaired. When a pending sector is repaired, a message similar to the following is logged to : warning pendsect[17377]: Recovered Pending LBA:######### (where ######### is the Logical Block Address of the repaired sector) For more information on the pendsect utility, see: SOL14426: Hard disk error detection and correction improvements
bugs.conditions: This may occur on BIG-IP appliances or VIPRION blades which contain hard disks which use 4096-byte physical sectors. Currently-known affected platforms include: BIG-IP 5000-/7000-series appliances BIG-IP 10000-series appliances VIPRION B4300 blades VIPRION B2100 blades Due to manufacturing changes and RMA replacements, additional platforms may potentially be affected. The smartctl utility can be used to identify hard disks using 4096-byte physical sectors: # smartctl --scan /dev/sda -d scsi # /dev/sda, SCSI device # smartctl -i /dev/sda | grep "Sector Size" Affected: Sector Sizes: 512 bytes logical, 4096 bytes physical Not Affected: Sector Size: 512 bytes logical/physical
bugs.impact: Potential corruption of unknown files on BIG-IP volumes.

bugs.title: POST request body is not saved in session variable by access when request is sent using edge client
bugs.symptoms: POST body sent by Edge Client is not saved in the session db session variable by access hudfilter.
bugs.conditions: - Configure BIG-IP as SAML Service Provider. To simplify reproduction change Access Policy execution timeout to few seconds. - Use Edge Client to connect to BIG-IP. - Saml Agent will redirect user for authentication to IdP - Wait for few seconds for access policy to time out on BIG-IP. - Enter credentials/complete authentication on IdP - User will be redirected back to BIG-IP as SP. At this moment APM will create a new session, and will evaluate access policy again.
bugs.impact: SAML Agent will now fail with the following error: SAML Agent: <AgentNameHere> cannot find assertion information in SAML request
bugs.workaround: Removing the â€˜Originâ€™ header from the request with iRule does fix the issue, and the POST body becomes available to access hudfilter.
bugs.fix: Check for receipt of HUDEVT_REQUEST_DONE before falling through from EV_ACCESS_TCL_COMPLETION to EV_ACCESS_REQUEST_DONE in client wait for request body to ensure proper storage of POST request body in sessiondb.

bugs.title: [RFE] - iApp modification request to add apm policy - f5.peoplesoft_9
bugs.symptoms: Currently its not possible to associate APM access policies to virtual servers created using the f5.peoplesoft_9 iApp template. This requires users to disable strict updates and then associate the policy with the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: When using f5.peoplesoft_9 iApp template and require an APM configuration.
bugs.impact: Cannot associate APM access policies to virtual servers created using the f5.peoplesoft_9 iApp template.
bugs.workaround: Disable strict updates and then associate the policy with the virtual server.
bugs.fix: The system now supports APM policies in f5.peoplesoft_9 iApp deployments.

bugs.title: CAPTCHA Challenge on Edge 14 Browser when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled
bugs.symptoms: The Edge 14 browser on Windows 10 will receive the CAPTCHA challenge when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled on the DoS profile and the "Block requests from suspicious browsers" checkbox is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense is enabled on the DoS profile and the "Block requests from suspicious browsers" checkbox is enabled.
bugs.impact: Edge 14 browser gets CAPTCHA challenge instead of passing through to the server.
bugs.fix: The Edge 14 Browser no longer gets the CAPTCHA challenge when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.

bugs.title: SIP ALG with Translation fails for REGISTER refresh.
bugs.symptoms: SIP-MBLB-ALG-Translation mode doesn't translate SIP REGISTER refresh message when arriving on the original flow.
bugs.conditions: 1. LSN Pool selected on CLIENT_ACCEPTED event. 2. SIP REGISTER request refresh happens on the original flow.
bugs.impact: SIP Register message egressed will not have translation applied i.e. the CONTACT and VIA header will not be translated.
bugs.fix: SIP REGISTER refresh processing identifies the translation used for the original SIP REGISTER and applies that translation to the SIP REGISTER refresh message.

bugs.title: SSL error message is missing important information
bugs.symptoms: If a SSL error occurs while running the iqsh utility or when BIG-IP DNS/GTM attempts to establish an SSL connection, then the system will dump certain pieces of information about the attempted connection but won't include the return code from OpenSSL (which indicates what the error actually was).
bugs.conditions: An SSL error occurs while running the iqsh utility or when BIG-IP DNS/GTM attempts to establish an ssl connection.
bugs.impact: The SSL connection has already failed by the time this error is displayed. Without the additional return code information it may be difficult to diagnose why the failure occurred.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The error code is output as a string indicating which of the defined errors occurred. See 'man SSL_get_error' for details on what each code means.

bugs.title: ASM Auto-Sync Device Group Does Not Sync
bugs.symptoms: Some messages that should be sent to peers in a device group are not successfully sent.
bugs.conditions: A series of create/delete ASM policies and multiple changes to the ASM sync Device Group (creation, deletion, joining devices, removing devices).
bugs.impact: ASM configuration does not sync properly
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the device group and restart asm_config_server using the following command: # pkill -f asm_config_server
bugs.fix: Communication over the ASM Device Group now works correctly after leaving/joining Device Groups.

bugs.title: The diagnostic tool dnsxdump may crash with non-standard DNS RR types.
bugs.symptoms: If the dnsxdump diagnostic tool is run when the DNS Express database has a DNS resource record using a non-standard type, the process may crash providing incomplete diagnostic output.
bugs.conditions: Running dnsxdump with a DNS Express database containing non-standard resource record types.
bugs.impact: dnsxdump provide incomplete diagnostic output, stopping on the zone containing the resource record with the non-standard type.
bugs.workaround: This is primarily known to be caused by non-standard RR types created for WINS records. Removing the WINS records from the master nameserver, will allow dnsxdump to work again after the next zone transfer.
bugs.fix: dnsxdump handles non-standard resource record types.

bugs.title: SELinux: snmpd is denied access to tmstat files
bugs.symptoms: When a custom SNMP MIB is created by using Tcl scripts or other methods, the snmpwalk will fail to access the created MIB data.
bugs.conditions: Custom created MIBs.
bugs.impact: Access to that MIB is denied.
bugs.fix: When a custom SNMP MIB is created by using a Tcl scripts or other methods, the snmpwalk no longer fails to access the created MIB data.

bugs.title: Chassis sync fails intermittently due to sync file backlog
bugs.symptoms: Chassis sync may fail intermittently if policies are changed and applied in a short interval.
bugs.conditions: Policies are changed and applied in a short interval on a chassis platform.
bugs.impact: Disk partition /var may fill up and synchronized changes may not appear on secondary blades.
bugs.fix: ASM configuration sync on chassis platform now works more reliably.

bugs.title: TMM crash on BigIP i4x00 and i2x00 with large ASM configuration.
bugs.symptoms: With large ASM configurations (50 virtual servers, 50 ASM policies), TMM will continuously crash on boot-up or restart.
bugs.conditions: Large ASM configurations (50 virtual servers, 50 ASM policies).
bugs.impact: TMM continuously crashes and restarts, system is unusable.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes on i4x00 and i2x00 platforms with large ASM configurations.

bugs.title: Tmm cores in bigproto_cookie_buffer_to_server
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores on SIGSEGV during normal operation. Although the exact triggering conditions are unknown, it might that when a connection is aborted in a client-side iRule, the reported log signature may indicate its occurrence: tmm3[11663]: 01220009:6: Pending rule <irule_name> <HTTP_REQUEST> aborted for <ip> -> <ip>.
bugs.conditions: Specific conditions that trigger this issue are unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: iControl calls related to key and certificate management (Management::KeyCertificate) might leak memory
bugs.symptoms: iControl calls related to Management::KeyCertificate might leak memory slowly, that causes swap space to increase continuously and might lead to exhaustion of swap space
bugs.conditions: This occurs with the iControl command bigip.Management.KeyCertificate.certificate_export_to_pem
bugs.impact: iControlPortal.cgi memory increases
bugs.workaround: Restart httpd to reload the iControl daemon.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak associated with iControl

bugs.title: A false positive modified domain cookie violation
bugs.symptoms: An unexpected modified domain cookie violation on system that has more than 127 policies configured.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when more than 127 policies are configured. The violation modified domain cookie is turned on and there are enforced cookies.
bugs.impact: A false positive violation.
bugs.workaround: Remove the modified domain cookie violation from blocking.
bugs.fix: Fixed a false positive modified domain cookie violation.

bugs.title: Nagle Algorithm Not Fully Enforced with TSO
bugs.symptoms: Sub MSS packets are more numerous than Nagle's algorithm would imply.
bugs.conditions: TCP Segmentation Offload is enabled.
bugs.impact: Sub-MSS packets increase overhead and client power consumption.
bugs.workaround: Disable TCP Segmentation Offload by running the following command: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcpsegmentationoffload value disable
bugs.fix: Deliver Integer Multiples of MSS to the TSO hardware when Nagle's algorithm applies.

bugs.title: SNAT pools allow members in different partitions to be assigned, but this causes a load failure
bugs.symptoms: SNAT pools allow members in different partitions to be assigned, but this is prohibited at load time.
bugs.conditions: The SNAT pool is in a partition different from that of the member you are trying to add to it.
bugs.impact: Load will fail with an error like the following: 01070726:3: SNAT pool translation address /p1/mysnatpool /p2/1.2.3.4%5 in partition PARE cannot reference SNAT Translation /p2/1.2.3.4%5 in partition p2
bugs.workaround: Use a SNAT pool member in the same partition.

bugs.title: TMM restart and failover.
bugs.symptoms: Under rare circumstances, an HSB-received failure can cause can cause TMM to restart
bugs.conditions: The conditions required for this issue to occur are unknown.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Apmd crashes when using iRule in clientless mode
bugs.symptoms: Apmd crashes when iRule is used in clientless mode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when following conditions are met: - iRule is used to evaluate the access policy. - If LDAP/AD query agent is configured in access policy to fetch many attributes. If the data is more than 64K, apmd will hit segfault (SIGSEGV) when trying to copy them.
bugs.impact: Apmd crashes or restarts.
bugs.workaround: Limit the number of attributes in Ldap/AD query agents. Apmd doesn't crash if the total data are less than 64K.
bugs.fix: Access Sessions with large amounts of session variable data are now created properly when called from the "ACCESS::policy evaluate" iRule command.

bugs.title: Memory Requirement for deploying Bot Signatures in DoS profiles
bugs.symptoms: When deploying large number of DoS profiles with Bot signatures enabled on low-end platforms, the memory spills over to the swap area. Each DoS profile consumes about 2 MB of memory per core for accommodating the complied bot signatures. For example, on VE with 2 cores and 8 GB of memory, deploying 1024 DoS profiles with bot signatures will consume 4 GB which together with the other memory requirements of ASM far exceeds the physical memory. The symptom is high utilization of swap memory.
bugs.conditions: Deploy large number (over 100) of DoS profiles with Bot signatures.
bugs.impact: Severe performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: On VE platforms, provision at least 4 GB more memory to the VM. On vCMP platform, assign this amount of memory to the guest machine. On physical machines, the only option is to upgrade to a larger memory platform. Consider using less profiles by reusing the same DoS profile on more than one Virtual Server.

bugs.title: LTM Policy with illegal rule name loses its conditions and actions during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP version 12.0.0 introduced more strict checking on the characters allowed in policy and rule names, and it also introduced an auto-migration feature to convert any disallowed characters to an underscore (_). Allowed characters in policy and rule names are: A-Z a-z 0-9 . / : % - Spaces are allowed between these characters. When there is a pre-v12.0 Policy that contains an illegal character, the rule has each illegal character converted to a legal one. But conditions and actions, which are joined to the rule by name were not similarly adjusted. After migration, LTM Policy rule does not have any conditions or actions referring to its new name.
bugs.conditions: - Pre-v12.0 BIG-IP - Policy and/or rule names contain illegal characters like: * < > ( ) [ ] - Upgrade to v12.0 or later
bugs.impact: Policy rule name is changed, illegal characters converted to benign underscore (_). The upgraded configuration will load successfully, but the Rule's associated conditions and actions are not changed, and still point to the policy by its former name, effectively becoming orphaned. Inspecting rule using UI or tmsh shows conditions and actions missing.
bugs.workaround: The bigip.conf file can be manually edited to fix illegal characters and configuration reloaded.

bugs.title: DNSX Performance Graphs are not displaying Requests/sec"
bugs.symptoms: The DNSX Performance graphs have a X and Y axis of Requests/second but the data actually shows total requests.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: The data displayed in the graph is not correct.

bugs.title: Large SSL certificate bundle export by GUI silently fails
bugs.symptoms: GUI SSL certificate bundle export silently fails if the size of the certificate bundle is greater than approximately 1824 KB.
bugs.conditions: 1. Import a certificate whose size is greater than 1823 KB. 2. Try to Export that certificate using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Unable to download large SSL certificate.
bugs.workaround: You can export the large SSL Certificate bundle as 'Archive' using the following procedure: 1. Navigate to System :: File Management : SSL Certificate List. 2. Click 'Archive. 3. Download the large SSL Certificate bundle.

bugs.title: After reboot LCD reports "unit going standby" even if it has gone active.
bugs.symptoms: After a reboot, the LCD and the tmsh show sys alert command reports "unit going standby" even though the device has become active.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently on system startup.
bugs.impact: LCD and tmsh show sys alert erroneously report "unit going standby". The /var/log/ltm log will have messages from sod indicating that it has become active.

bugs.title: Potential failure of DHCP relay functionality credits to incorrect route lookup.
bugs.symptoms: DHCP requests from client to server may not make it through.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system configured as a DHCP relay. -- Input variable (flow_key) incorrectly initialized.
bugs.impact: Clients might not get an IP address from the DHCP server.
bugs.fix: Input variable (flow_key) is initialized properly to prevent a potential route-lookup failure.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing HTTP2 traffic
bugs.symptoms: In some cases TMM may crash when processing HTTP2 traffic.
bugs.conditions: A virtual configured with HTTP2 and ClientSSL profiles
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Improve HTTP2 processing.

bugs.title: HA Groups sufficient threshold warns sufficient count=0 when sufficient count is set to all
bugs.symptoms: When the HA Health Monitor indicates that one or more objects do not meet the sufficient threshold, it is indicated by a yellow triangle icon in the System :: High Availability : HA Groups : Group screen. If the sufficient threshold is set to "All", then when you hover your mouse over the icon it will say the sufficient threshold of 0 is not met.
bugs.conditions: Device Cluster configured with HA Groups configured for one or more traffic groups. The HA Group has a sufficient threshold setting of "All".
bugs.impact: The text will indicate that the sufficient threshold of 0 is not met. This is a cosmetic display issue.

bugs.title: SSL may not be reassembling fragments correctly with a large-sized client certificate when SSL persistence is enabled
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP device, whenever a large-sized client certificate is sent by an SSL client to a virtual service, and SSL persistence is enabled, the SSID parser does not reassemble fragmented ClientKeyExchange messages correctly. It interprets the next incoming fragment - part of the CertificateVerify message - as a new record, incorrectly calculates its length and ends up waiting endlessly for more bytes to receive the record.
bugs.conditions: When SSL persistence is enabled and a large-sized client certificate is sent by the SSL client to the BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: Client connection hangs during the handshake. No impact to any other module.
bugs.workaround: Disable SSL persistence.
bugs.fix: SSL now reassembles fragments correctly with a large-sized client certificate when SSL persistence is enabled.

bugs.title: iOS receiver optional two factor auth slider is not displayed
bugs.symptoms: While adding a Citrix store account in iOS citrix receiver, it prompts for credentials based on access policy "Citrix logon prompt" agent. It does not display the slider option to have it as an optional.
bugs.conditions: Citrix APM is configured in replacement mode with "Citrix Logon Prompt" agent or "session.citrix.client_auth_type" variable assign is defined.
bugs.impact: Client auth type can not be optional. It is either be two factor or single auth type.
bugs.workaround: - Remove "Citrix Logon Prompt" and use regular "Logon Page". - Do not use "session.citrix.client_auth_type". - Add have the below irule attached to the Virtual server used for Store access. # optional two factor auth workaround. when HTTP_REQUEST { set uri_path [string tolower [HTTP::path]] if { $uri_path == "/vpn/index.html" } { HTTP::respond 200 -version auto content "/vpn/" noserver } elseif {$uri_path == "/agservices/discover"} { HTTP::respond 302 -version auto noserver Location "/vpn/index.html" } }

bugs.title: tmm may be killed by sod when a hardware accelerator does not work
bugs.symptoms: tmm may hang and crash (killed by the switchover daemon, sod), when the Cavium hardware accelerator does not come back after the reset from the driver.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely seen occurrence. It is triggered when the Cavium hardware accelerator stops working.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Power cycling the system might correct the error.
bugs.fix: The system now prints out an error message in the log file, improving the way tmm handles the failure.

bugs.title: Frame is not showing in the browser and/ or an error appears
bugs.symptoms: frame going blank when ASM policy enabled. this will trigger the following JS error in clients console: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property '3' of undefined
bugs.conditions: Asm policy enabled. Device id is enabled theough one of the supporting features
bugs.impact: Site not operating correctly.
bugs.fix: Fixed device id javascript issue that prevented a frame from being displayed .

bugs.title: Restjavad log messages: [ProcessManager] Maximum child processes of 3 has been reached
bugs.symptoms: Restjavad log file contains multiple messages similar to the following: -- [I][479][02 Nov 2016 00:38:51 UTC][ProcessManager] Maximum child processes of 3 has been reached. -- [I][480][02 Nov 2016 00:38:51 UTC][ProcessManager] Maximum child processes of 3 has been reached.
bugs.conditions: -- Restjavad startup. -- 100 or more devices discovered/managed.
bugs.impact: Potentially alarming/unnecessary error log messages.
bugs.workaround: None. Although the messages might be problematic, they do not indicate a serious condition.

bugs.title: Unable to set maxMessageBodySize in iControl REST after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading and attempting to set maxMessageBodySize via iControl REST, you get an error indicating the command is not implemented: {"code":400,"message":"onPut Not implemented","originalRequestBody":"{\"maxMessageBodySize\": \"111111111\"}","referer":"127.0.0.1","restOperationId":216941,"kind":":resterrorresponse"}
bugs.conditions: This occurs when upgrading from v11.6.1 to v12.1.0, v12.1.1,or v12.1.2, and applying the UCS from the 11.6.1 release. The error is generated because new defaults were added but they are not set on UCS restore.
bugs.impact: Command fails, unable to set maxMessageBodySize.
bugs.workaround: If you encounter this after an upgrade and UCS restore, you can run the following commands from the BIG-IP command line: 1. curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8100/shared/storage?key=shared/server/messaging/settings/8100. 2. bigstart restart restjavad.
bugs.fix: You can now set maxMessageBodySize via iControl REST after upgrading.

bugs.title: HTTP monitor log file is recreated after being deleted
bugs.symptoms: HTTP monitor log file is recreated after being deleted.
bugs.conditions: If the HTTP monitor log file is deleted during normal execution, it will be recreated, which is inconsistent with the behavior of other monitors. Normally the file is not recreated until the process is restarted.
bugs.impact: Deleted HTTP monitor log file is recreated. There is no impact to the system overall.

bugs.title: iControl-SOAP prints beyond log buffer
bugs.symptoms: When trace logging is turned on, iControl SOAP can potentially print text beyond its log buffer.
bugs.conditions: Logging for iControl SOAP is turned on with trace level.
bugs.impact: iControl-SOAP can print out garbage log to /var/log/ltm and can potentially lead to instability with reading beyond a buffer.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable logging with trace level, which is not turned on by default.
bugs.fix: Trim trace buffer to appropriate length to prevent printing garbage.

bugs.title: No way to perform a soft server certificate verification
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to perform a soft server certificate verification.
bugs.conditions: Server-side SSL forward proxy when 'server certificate is set to 'require' and 'untrusted CA response control' and 'expired certificate response control' are both set to 'ignore'.
bugs.impact: No way to perform a soft server certificate verification and continue the handshake as though the verification is OK, even if it is not OK.
bugs.fix: There is a new sys db variable: tmm.ssl.servercert_softval with default value 'disabled'. When this sys db variable is 'enabled', calling SSL::verify_result will return a soft verfiy_result value. Typical use case: It is used in the server-side SSL forward proxy when 'server certificate is set to 'require' and 'untrusted CA response control' and 'expired certificate response control' are both set to 'ignore' but would like to perform a soft server certificate verification.
bugs.behavior: There is a new sys db variable: tmm.ssl.servercert_softval with default value 'disabled'. When this sys db variable is 'enabled', calling SSL::verify_result will return a soft verfiy_result value. Typical use case: It is used in the server-side SSL forward proxy when 'server certificate is set to 'require' and 'untrusted CA response control' and 'expired certificate response control' are both set to 'ignore' but would like to perform a soft server certificate verification.

bugs.title: Statistics :: Analytics :: Hardware Acceleration menu contains misspelled menu item: 'Assited Connections'.
bugs.symptoms: Statistics :: Analytics :: Hardware Acceleration menu contains misspelled menu item: 'Assited Connections' instead of 'Assisted Connections'.
bugs.conditions: -- Running vCMP. -- System provides hardware acceleration. -- Statistics :: Analytics :: Hardware Acceleration menu.
bugs.impact: Spelling of 'Assited' instead of the expected 'Assisted'.
bugs.fix: Changed spelling of 'Assited' to 'Assisted'.
