bugs.title: CLI VPN client crashes when HOME environment variable is not defined
bugs.symptoms: CLI VPN client requires HOME environment variable for logging. If the variable is not set, CLI client crashes on Linux/Mac.
bugs.conditions: HOME environment variable is not defined.
bugs.impact: The VPN client crashes it is difficult to determine the cause.
bugs.workaround: Set HOME environment variable.
bugs.fix: Now the Linux command line client logs a message and exits gracefully rather than crashing when HOME variable is not set.

bugs.title: "reset-stats auth login-failures" command for unknown users causes secondary mcpd processes to restart
bugs.symptoms: Running the command "tmsh reset-stats auth login-failures <username>" on a bladed system can cause the mcpd process to restart on secondary blades if the <username> is not an actual user on the system. The /var/log/ltm log file will contain errors messages similar to: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020036:3: The requested username (username) was not found.... failed validation with error 16908342
bugs.conditions: This occurs on VIPRION systems when running the command for a user that doesn't exist on the other blades.
bugs.impact: mcpd processes on secondary blades restart, possibly causing loss of traffic and a failover (if in a device cluster).
bugs.workaround: Run the command "tmsh reset-stats auth login-failure <username>" using only valid usernames.
bugs.fix: Prevented the command "tmsh reset-stats auth login-failure <username>" from restarting mcpd instances on secondary blades when <username> is an unknown user. The bad command is intercepted at the primary blade and is dealt with there.

bugs.title: Provide a means to prevent QKView files from being uploaded to iHealth
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to prevent QKView files from being uploaded to iHealth unintentionally.
bugs.conditions: Running the qkview utility.
bugs.impact: QKView file might unintentionally be uploaded to iHealth.
bugs.fix: The qkview utility now supports a -i command line argument, which embeds a tag into the QKView file that instructs iHealth to ignore any QKView file containing that tag.
bugs.behavior: The qkview utility has a new -i argument that prevents unintentional upload of QKView files to iHealth. This argument can be configured to be persistent through the tmsh diagnostics setting: no-ihealth. For example: tmsh modify sys diagnostics ihealth no-ihealth true By default, this value is false. This causes the GUI to present options only for creating QKViews, and not for uploading to iHealth. When this config setting ('no_ihealth') is enabled, the qkview operation adds metadata to QKView files that prevent the files from being uploaded to iHealth.

bugs.title: Use of SPDY profile may crash tmm in rare conditions
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances, the SPDY profile might result in a tmm crash due to incorrect processing of allocated memory.
bugs.conditions: SPDY profile is configured and applied to a virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround other than to remove the SPDY filter.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin may crash if webtrace or debug log level is enabled for Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite plugin may crash on large rewritibale content when webtrace or debug log for Portal Access is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Portal Access log level is set to "Debug", or Web Application Trace feature of Portal Access is active.
bugs.impact: Portal Access is temporarily unavailable. Core file for 'rewrite' process is generated.
bugs.workaround: Fixed an issue where Rewrite plugin could crash when collecting webtrace or debug logs for Portal Access.

bugs.title: sys-icheck error for /var/lib/waagent in Azure.
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP deployed in Azure cloud, sys-icheck reports readlink error for /var/lib/waagent directory as following: ERROR: ....L.... /var/lib/waagent
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP deployed in Azure cloud.
bugs.impact: sys-icheck reports "rpm --verify" errors for /var/lib/waagent. This doesn't have any functional impact on the product but looks like factory RPM settings were modified externally and incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for this issue.
bugs.fix: sys-icheck error for /var/lib/waagent in Azure.

bugs.title: Potential crash in a multi-blade chassis during CMP state changes.
bugs.symptoms: CMP state change can result in a blade crash.
bugs.conditions: CMP state change with a PEM profile enabled on a virtual. The former can be triggered using a TMM restart/unrelated crash, blade insertion or blade administrative state change.
bugs.impact: Blade crash resulting in potential loss of service.
bugs.workaround: Deploy PEM in an HA-pair with a chassis fail over configured to occur if at most one blade on the active chassis fails.
bugs.fix: The system now gracefully handles sessionDB errors due to a CMP state change.

bugs.title: Ensure unique IKEv2 sequence numbers
bugs.symptoms: Although BIG-IP generates random sequence numbers for use in protocol negotiation, it is possible to allocate a new number already in use by a phase-one ike-SA or a phase-two child-SA.
bugs.conditions: When a sufficiently large number of tunnels are in use (e.g., numbering in thousands), odds of generating a duplicate sequence number is relatively high, given the number of random bits used to generate the number. More tunnels makes it more likely to occur.
bugs.impact: On sequence number collision, this might confuse an old SA, and probably never complete negotiation of a new SA. In addition, the system might crash if updating an old SA happened in a state where update is not expected.
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP uses more random bits in generated sequence numbers, and it always checks whether a new sequence number is currently in use anywhere else before proceeding. Thus collisions cannot be generated in sequence number allocation. New numbers should always be guaranteed unique now.

bugs.title: Portal Access: URLs in CSS image-set() function may not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access does not rewrite URLs in CSS function image-set() parameters. Browser cannot load corresponding resources.
bugs.conditions: CSS file with image-set() function or any of its variants, for example: .img { background-image: -webkit-image-set( "examples/images/image-384.jpg" 1x, "examples/images/image-768.jpg" 2x, ); }
bugs.impact: URLs in image-set() function are not rewritten; hence corresponding resources cannot be loaded by browser.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to replace non-rewritten URLs by rewritten ones.
bugs.fix: Now URLs in CSS image-set() function are rewritten correctly by Portal Access. Several browser-dependent modifications of this function are supported as well: '-webkit-image-set', '-moz-image-set', '-ms-image-set' and '-o-image-set'.

bugs.title: Portal Access may determine end of HTML SCRIPT tag incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: If HTML page contains SCRIPT tag with HTML comment inside, the end of this SCRIPT tag may be found incorrectly by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page with SCRIPT tag - HTML comment inside this tag - strings '<script>' and '</script>' inside this HTML comment Example: <script> <!-- var i=1; // <script> var line = "</script>"; //--> </script>
bugs.impact: The end of the SCRIPT tag is determined incorrectly by server-side HTML parser. In the example above, the end of SCRIPT tag is set at first '</script>' string. HTML page and scripts inside it may be handled incorrectly; web application may not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Split '</script>' string inside HTML comment into concatenation of two separate strings by iRule.
bugs.fix: Now interaction between HTML SCRIPT tag and HTML comment tag is handled correctly by server-side HTML parser in APM Portal Access.

bugs.title: Policy with assigned SAML Resource is exported with error
bugs.symptoms: If Access Profile's Access Policy has saml resource assigned export is failing with error.
bugs.conditions: 1. Access profile/access policy 2. Saml resource is assigned
bugs.impact: Unable to Export Policy
bugs.fix: Work order is restored

bugs.title: Heartbeat may be unavailable when viewing very large config via vconsole/serial console on bladed systems
bugs.symptoms: In a bladed vCMP system with guests spanning several blades, there is an issue when concatenating output from applications via blade console/virtual console. The timing issue is presumably that if the host is not processing fast enough to process the data sent by a guest application to the virtual console the host will suffer high load, causing the primary blade to clockadvance, miss its heartbeat, and be removed from the cluster.
bugs.conditions: -- In a large configuration (for example, 55 virtual servers with corresponding pools, persistence profiles, and iRules). -- Run the following tmsh command: tmsh show ltm virtual detail
bugs.impact: Blade may stop working after executing the command.
bugs.workaround: Upgrading hypervisor to 12.1.1 or later resolves the issue.

bugs.title: restjavad logs flooded with messages from ChildWrapper
bugs.symptoms: Running iControl REST under heavy load might result in restjavad logs being filled with multiple, repeating messages similar to the following: [WARNING][76559][13 Dec 2016 07:08:00 UTC][ChildWrapper] Exception found in child runner thread: null
bugs.conditions: -- Put iControl REST under a heavy load. -- View restjavad logs.
bugs.impact: Logs fill with messages and rotate out. Logs full of these error messages might cause other messages to be missed.
bugs.fix: iControl REST properly handles the exception described.

bugs.title: In some rare cases TMM may crash while handling VMware View client connection
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: VMware View client uses PCoIP to connect to backend via APM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed rare TMM crash during handling of VMware View client PCoIP connection

bugs.title: Browser will be stuck on 'checking endpoint status' in some cases
bugs.symptoms: If the APM end user selects 'No' in response to the prompt 'Allow this site to inspect your machine', the Firefox and Chrome browsers will hang on the 'checking endpoint status' page.
bugs.conditions: -- Firefox or Chrome browser is used to launch endpoint inspection helper app. -- The APM end user does not allow the app to perform endpoint check at launch time.
bugs.impact: Browser hangs on the 'checking endpoint status' page.
bugs.workaround: Use a different browser.
bugs.fix: End-User "no" responses to "Allow this site to inspect your machine" no longer results in a browser hang at "checking endpoint status" in Firefox.

bugs.title: crash with wrong ceritifcate in WSS
bugs.symptoms: BD crash.
bugs.conditions: Web services security is turned on. a bad / wrong / missing certificate is attached.
bugs.impact: Traffic drop until the BD is back (or failover).
bugs.workaround: The workaround would be to fix the attached certificate.
bugs.fix: Fix an issue with wrong certificates.

bugs.title: Two users cannot create policies at the same time.
bugs.symptoms: Two users cannot create policies at the same time.
bugs.conditions: -- Two users with admin authority are logged onto the GUI. -- Both begin creating separate ASM policies with distinct options. For instance: - User 'wafadmin1' logs in first. - User 'wafadmin2' logs in second. - Both are creating policies. - When wafadmin2 submits the policy, it's being overwritten by policy details given by wafadmin1. - Only user wafadmin1 can de-activate a policy; for other users the option itself is grayed out.
bugs.impact: Policy from one user can overwrite another's. Can also affect who can de-activate a policy.
bugs.workaround: Have only one user at a time create/modify/delete policies.

bugs.title: BGP ECMP recursive default route not redistributed to TMM
bugs.symptoms: ECMP recursive routes are not properly redistributed to TMM, resulting in an incorrect routing table.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing configured with multiple equal cost paths reachable through a recursive nexthop.
bugs.impact: Packets are not routed to all ECMP nexthops.
bugs.fix: ECMP routes with a recursive nexthop are now used correctly by TMM.

bugs.title: iControl SOAP doesn't support displaying all possible media options for interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Newer media options would erroneously be displayed as MT_AUTO from iControl SOAP. If the media option is considered internal; iControl SOAP will still display the specific type if available in its list. This has been changed to display MT_NONE for those options.
bugs.conditions: Platforms that support the missing interfaces in the iControl SOAP will not get the right info vi iControl SOAP. Specifically those that support MEDIA_40000_FDX and MEDIA_40000_LR4_FDX. Affected Platforms: A108 A112 D112 D113
bugs.impact: Information Mismatch
bugs.fix: iControl SOAP will display MT_NONE for media options that are considered internal. iControl SOAP has been extended to display newer media options matching the current list of supported BIG-IP media options.
bugs.behavior: iControl SOAP will return MT_NONE media options for INTERNAL interfaces.

bugs.title: TMM memory leak when ASM policy configured on virtual
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory leak in hud_oob when ASM policy configured on virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Memory leak could be observed via output of this TMSH command: tmctl -c memory_usage_stat | grep -P '^name|hud_oob' when ASM policy is configured on a virtual server. However this condition is not unique.
bugs.impact: TMM might run out of memory and eventually crash.
bugs.workaround: Try to disable ASM policy configuration on virtual server.
bugs.fix: A memory leak in hud_oob when ASM policy configured on virtual server has been fixed.

bugs.title: Potential PEM crash during a Gx operation
bugs.symptoms: Tmm may core during a Gx operation
bugs.conditions: Requires a PEM virtual with Gx, Sd or Gy enabled. This occurs when tmm starts.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Perform proper validation checks as part of API processing.

bugs.title: Potential crash in a multi-blade chassis during CMP state changes.
bugs.symptoms: tmm on a blade may crash during a CMP and PEM change.
bugs.conditions: Multi-blade chassis undergoing a CMP state change. Additionally requires PEM policy changes resulting in usage record updates.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use an HA pair and have the active chassis fail over during a CMP state change. Allow for the new stand by chassis to complete its CMP state change activity.
bugs.fix: Handle sessionDB failures gracefully.

bugs.title: TMUI loginProviderName is invalid when requesting a REST token
bugs.symptoms: Requests for X-F5-Auth-Token fail when a TMUI view is loaded that requires a X-F5-Auth-Token used for REST requests.
bugs.conditions: On startup if the tmos login provider takes too long to become available it will cause the login provider to be unavailable, and requests for auth tokens will fail. This is a race condition and happens intermittently. Typically on lower end devices.
bugs.impact: GUI cannot retrieve F5-Auth-Token for REST requests
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart restjavad
bugs.fix: Added retry to add login provider if unavailable.

bugs.title: Upgrade fails with "DBD::mysql::db do failed: Too many partitions (including subpartitions) were defined" errors in ASM log
bugs.symptoms: These errors come up in asm log, upon first start after upgrade: ------------------------- 2016-11-02T08:33:09-06:00 localhost notice boot_marker : ---===[ HD1.2 - BIG-IP 12.1.1 Build 0.0.184 <HD1.2> ]===--- Nov 2 08:35:34 c5af5ltm1b info set_ibdata1_size.pl[18523]: Setting ibdata1 size finished successfully, a new size is: 8466M Nov 2 08:36:03 c5af5ltm1b info tsconfig.pl[21351]: ASM initial configration script launched Nov 2 08:36:17 c5af5ltm1b info tsconfig.pl[21351]: ASM initial configration script finished Nov 2 08:36:23 c5af5ltm1b info asm_start[19802]: ASM config loaded Nov 2 08:37:40 c5af5ltm1b crit perl[19802]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::DbUpgrade::__ANON__): DBD::mysql::db do failed: Too many partitions (including subpartitions) were defined Nov 2 08:38:28 c5af5ltm1b crit perl[19802]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::DbUpgrade::__ANON__): DBD::mysql::db do failed: Cannot remove all partitions, use DROP TABLE instead Nov 2 08:38:28 c5af5ltm1b crit perl[19802]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::ConfigSync::load_traffic_data): Could not import table data PRX.REQUEST_LOG - ASM configuration save aborted Nov 2 08:38:33 c5af5ltm1b info perl[21860]: 01310053:6: ASM starting -------------------------
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned Local request logging enabled Upgrade of a maintenance release, HF or EHF
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails
bugs.workaround: Upgrade by the means of saving a UCS, performing a clean install and then loading the UCS. In the manual save/load UCS process, the upgrade of the Request Log can be disabled, which will workaround the error and the UCS will load fine. There are two options to disable the upgrade of the Request Log, when upgrading by the means of a UCS: ------------------- 1) do not load a Request Log, when loading a UCS: # tmsh modify sys db ucs.asm.traffic_data.load value never 2) do not save a Request Log, when saving a UCS: # tmsh modify sys db ucs.asm.traffic_data.save value disable -------------------

bugs.title: eamtest tool fails with Segmentation fault after initialization.
bugs.symptoms: Tests done with eamtest tool fail with Segmentation fault after initialization.
bugs.conditions: Run eamtest tool.
bugs.impact: eamtest tool fails, which affects troubleshooting using the tool.
bugs.workaround: Run eamtest with LD_PRELOAD=libeam_asdk_preload.so prefix.
bugs.fix: Wrapper script for eamtest tool now adds the =libeam_asdk_preload.so prefix automatically, so eamtest tool can be used to troubleshoot successfully.

bugs.title: Could not add new account in Citrix receiver for mac v12.3.0
bugs.symptoms: Could not add new account in Citrix receiver for mac version 12.3.0. It displays error as "Could not detect the specified account".
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM is used in either integration mode with Storefront or replacement mode. Add new account in Citrix receiver for mac v12.3.0
bugs.impact: Could not add new account
bugs.workaround: Attach this irule onto virtual server when HTTP_REQUEST { set uri_path [string tolower [HTTP::path]] if { $uri_path == "/vpn/index.html" } { set cookie "pwcount=0;Secure;HttpOnly;Path=/" HTTP::respond 200 -version auto content "/vpn/cgi/login" noserver "Set-Cookie" $cookie } }

bugs.title: HTTP2 can can crash tmm when stats is updated on aborting of a new connection
bugs.symptoms: HTTP2 allocates a block of memory for collecting stats on a connection. If the connection is aborted for any reason, tmm may try to update stats prior the memory is allocated.
bugs.conditions: HTTP2 profile is configured and assigned to a virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: A fix stops HTTP2 from accessing stats prior memory is allocated preventing TMM crash for this reason.

bugs.title: Adding a GUI option to set httponly atribute on ASM cookeis
bugs.symptoms: ASM cookies are set without the httponly attribute. Adding the attribute is allowed only using internal configuration.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: ASM cookies are not 'httponly', and changing this can only be done via the command line.
bugs.fix: Added a GUI option to set the 'httponly' attribute under Options : Application Security : Advanced Configuration : System Variables.

bugs.title: HSB transmitter failure on i2x00 and i4x00 platforms
bugs.symptoms: On the BIG-IP i2x00 and i4x00 platforms, tmm enters an infinite 'restart' loop after a 'bigstart restart' or 'bigstart restart tmm' command if traffic is actively flowing through the TMM. This is the result of an HSB transmitter failure.
bugs.conditions: Traffic actively flowing through the tmm and you issue 'bigstart restart' or 'bigstart restart tmm'. Another instance occurs when syncing the datasync-global-dg device-group for an HA configuration on iSeries platforms.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure all traffic is stopped before issuing the 'bigstart restart' or 'bigstart restart tmm' commands. Set HSB::failures_before_reset in /config/tmm_init.tcl to a high value, such as 1000 (default is 50) may resolve the issue, depending on the conditions this issue occurred.
bugs.fix: TMM restart loop no longer occurs following 'bigstart restart' on i2x00 and i4x00 platforms.

bugs.title: Sync fails after firewall policy deletion
bugs.symptoms: When deleting a firewall policy and then creating a new one, sync to standby fails.
bugs.conditions: Delete firewall policy then create a new one. Sync to Standby.
bugs.impact: Sync fails.

bugs.title: Trimming leading whitespaces at logging profile creation
bugs.symptoms: If a logging profile has a TAB character in its name, the name does not get double-quoted in bigip.conf, so configuration load fails.
bugs.conditions: Copy-pasting the logging profile name including a leading TAB character.
bugs.impact: Configuration loading failure upon next boot.
bugs.workaround: Copy-paste only the name (without the TAB character).
bugs.fix: Leading whitespaces (including TAB characters) are trimmed at profile creation, so the condition that caused the issue is eliminated.

bugs.title: Unable to change management-ip address
bugs.symptoms: After the management-ip address is changed, the BIG-IP system continues to use the old management-ip address. You might see the following error in /var/log/ltm: -- warning chmand[6584]: 012a0004:4: mcp_admin_ip_remove, delMgmtAddr() catch exception: Network Socket: Open Error [No such device], possibly nonexistent.
bugs.conditions: Running on platforms that use eth0 interface for management traffic. To determine whether the platform you have uses the eth0 interface for management traffic, run following command: ifconfig eth0.
bugs.impact: Unable to change management-ip address. After changing the management-ip, the old address will continue to be listed.
bugs.workaround: Save the change and reboot the system. After the changes have been saved, they will be applied after the unit is rebooted.

bugs.title: Partition of LTM policies is displayed in breadcrumb rather than properties table row
bugs.symptoms: There is no 'Partition/Path' row on LTM policies properties page. Instead the partition is displayed in the breadcrumb at the top of the page.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when selecting a LTM policy.
bugs.impact: Partition/Path not displayed.
bugs.fix: The partition was removed from the properties page breadcrumb and added as a 'Partition/Path' row to match the behavior of other LTM properties pages.

bugs.title: After upgrade to BIG-IP v12.1.x, Local Traffic Policies in partitions other than Common cannot be converted into a draft.
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP system has Local Traffic Policies defined in a non-Common partition, and the system is upgraded to version 12.1.0, 12.1.1, or 12.1.2, attempting to create a new draft of the policy by selecting "Create Draft" will fail and give an error message similar to: err mcpd[8140]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Can't associate policy rule (/Partition1/Drafts/policy_name policy_name_policy_rule) folder does not exist
bugs.conditions: A system is upgraded to version v12.1.x with Local Traffic Policies in a non-default partition.
bugs.impact: You cannot modify existing Local Traffic Policies.
bugs.workaround: Manually create a 'Drafts' folder in the appropriate partition, e.g.: tmsh create sys folder /Partition1/Drafts Alternately, create a new (different) policy in the specified partition, and then delete it. Doing this has a side-effect of creating the Drafts folder.

bugs.title: CCR-U missing upon VALIDITY TIMER expiry when quota is zero
bugs.symptoms: CCR-U is not sent upon VALIDITY TIMER experts.
bugs.conditions: If PCRF does not grant any GSU (no quota), but only specifies the VALIDITY timer.
bugs.impact: OCS does not get the CCR-U message and misses the information about quota.
bugs.workaround: Configure the quota deletion of depletion timeout to be non-zero.
bugs.fix: CCR-U is now sent upon VALIDITY TIMER experts.

bugs.title: TMM restart loop following 'bigstart restart' on i2x00 and i4x00 platforms
bugs.symptoms: On the BIG-IP i2x00 and i4x00 platforms, TMM enters an infinite 'restart' loop after a 'bigstart restart' or 'bigstart restart tmm' command if traffic is actively flowing through the TMM.
bugs.conditions: Traffic actively flowing through the TMM and you issue 'bigstart restart' or 'bigstart restart tmm'.
bugs.impact: System is unusable due to continuous TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure all traffic is stopped before issuing the 'bigstart restart' or 'bigstart restart tmm' commands.

bugs.title: Power on option in bladectl incorrectly resets already powered on blade
bugs.symptoms: If the power-on option via the bladectl command is issued against any B4100, B4200, B43xx, and B4450 blade that is already powered ON, it will cause the specified blade to reset similar to the reset option in bladectl.
bugs.conditions: Running any version of BIG-IP with 'bladectl -b X -p 1' on B4100, B4200, B43xx and B4450 blades where 'X' is the blade number.
bugs.impact: Blade resets unexpectedly if it is already powered ON.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the -p power on option against an already powered ON blade.
bugs.fix: B43xx and B4450 blades no longer reset when using the power on option in bladectl on an already powered on blade. Note: There is no fix for the B4100 or B4200 blades. The B4100 and B4200 blades are not supported in this release.

bugs.title: BIG-IP alerts contains proxy IP instead of client IP
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP alerts contains proxy IP address instead of client IP address.
bugs.conditions: 1. db var antifraud.uselastxff is disabled. 2. HTTP's 'accept xff' is enabled. 3. Request contains multiple XFF headers.
bugs.impact: WebSafe uses wrong IP address (proxy) as 'client IP' in alerts.
bugs.workaround: Use alternate XFF headers in HTTP profile.
bugs.fix: xff logic should consider multiple xff headers

bugs.title: [netHSM SafeNet] The 'Yes' and 'No' options to proceed or cancel the unisntall during "safenet-sync.sh -u " are not operational
bugs.symptoms: 'Yes' and 'No' options to proceed or cancel the uninstall operation are not operational.
bugs.conditions: Issue happens when running safenet-sync.sh -u.
bugs.impact: No impact.
bugs.fix: In this release, there is no Yes or No option for the SafeNet uninstall 'safenet-sync.sh -u.' command.

bugs.title: Improve cURL Usage
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, cURL usage within AFM does not comply with standards.
bugs.conditions: AFM active and configured to use external credentials
bugs.impact: Non-compliant cURL usage
bugs.fix: Improve cURL usage

bugs.title: gtm_add operation does not retain same-name DNSSEC keys after synchronize FIPS card
bugs.symptoms: When running gtm_add from one BIG-IP system to another, if the system being added already has the same DNSSEC key (dictated by DNSSEC key name), and you synchronize the FIPS card, then the FIPS card is wiped out (as expected), but the key is not re-added.
bugs.conditions: -- There is an existing DNSSEC key on one system. -- A second system has a DNSSEC key of the same name. -- Run gtm_add, with instructions to synchronize FIPS cards.
bugs.impact: No DNSSEC key of that name is present on FIPS card.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue prevent FIPS card synchronization through gtm_add when a DNSSEC key of the same name already exists on both GTMs.

bugs.title: Prevent sending a 2nd RST for a TCP connection
bugs.symptoms: After a specific sequence of packets resulting in sending a RST packet, TCP connection was kept alive and sent another RST when connection expired.
bugs.conditions: A specific sequence of packets (a second SYN segment within the TCP window) is received by a TCP connection.
bugs.impact: 2 RST segments is sent to the client instead of 1. In addition, the TCP connection was kept alive until the sweeper cleaned it.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TCP sends a single RST for specific sequence of packets

bugs.title: Buffer length check for quota bucket objects
bugs.symptoms: For quota bucket (Rating Groups) object, BIG-IP allocates a large buffer locally, and doesn't expect it to be over-run as the objects are expected to be smaller
bugs.conditions: Any quota bucket objects which are being inserted in PEM database
bugs.impact: For quota bucket objects which are in PEM database, the buffer is usually large enough, so there should not be any impact. But if the quota bucket ever gets larger, then potential corruption of the quota bucket information could occur. This could trigger a tmm core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: quota bucket with fewer rules

bugs.title: AVR HTTP/TCP: Only profiles from Common partition are displayed under All
bugs.symptoms: If you have HTTP Analytics profiles configured in multiple partitions, they will not be displayed when looking at all profiles from within the Common partition. Only the HTTP Analytics profiles from the Common partition are shown in the "All [Read Only]" view.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you are looking at the HTTP Analytics profiles from within the All [Read Only] partition.
bugs.impact: Analytics profiles from non-Common partition are not displayed, when viewing all partitions in read-only mode.
bugs.workaround: Workaround in UI: Switch to specific partition. Workaround in CLI: Display profiles using TMSH commands.

bugs.title: Connection queue limit is not properly enforced on bladed systems
bugs.symptoms: The connection queue depth may be larger than the configured limit.
bugs.conditions: Connection queues are enabled on bladed systems.
bugs.impact: Proper limits are not enforced, memory consumption may be larger than desired.
bugs.fix: The pool queue-depth-limit is now properly enforced chassis-wide, which may reduce the effective limit observed in previous versions.
bugs.behavior: The pool queue-depth-limit is now properly enforced chassis-wide, which may reduce the effective limit observed in previous versions.

bugs.title: TMM leaks memory in the ECM subsystem
bugs.symptoms: TMM leaks memory in the ECM subsystem.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the user has imported one or more SSL certificates onto the system and named them in such a way that the "ca-bundle.crt" string appears in their names. For example, "my-ca-bundle.crt". With this configuration in place, TMM leaks memory each time the configuration is modified.
bugs.impact: TMM will run out of free memory. This will initially impact traffic and could eventually lead to TMM crashing. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by renaming your SSL certificates so that their names don't contain the "ca-bundle.crt" string.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer leaks memory in the ECM subsystem.

bugs.title: Improve cURL usage
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, cURL usage within AFM does not comply with standards.
bugs.conditions: AFM active and configured to use external credentials.
bugs.impact: Non-compliant cURL usage.
bugs.fix: Improve cURL usage.

bugs.title: Unbundled 40GbE optics reporting as Unsupported Optic
bugs.symptoms: When a 40G interface is configured "bundle disabled" the optic module in use on the interface will be declared as an "Unsupported optic" module even though the optic module is F5 branded.
bugs.conditions: Using unbundled 40GbE optics.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic problem. The interface is able to function as intended.
bugs.workaround: No workaround, problem is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: The fix for the defect results in no longer declaring an otherwise supported optics module as unsupported when bundling is configured disabled on the interface.

bugs.title: iRule decryption does not work
bugs.symptoms: Retrieving the server-side SSL session ID using iRule does not work.
bugs.conditions: Retrieve server-side SSL Session ID using an iRule.
bugs.impact: Server-side traffic cannot be decrypted for non-RSA cipher suites.
bugs.fix: The server-side SSL session ID can now be retrieved with an iRule.

bugs.title: nic_failsafe reboot doesn't trigger if HSB fails to disable interface
bugs.symptoms: The HSB driver attempts a nic_failsafe in the case of failing to disable the interface.
bugs.conditions: The driver disables nic_failsafe prior to triggering the nic_failsafe. This is in hsb_ifdown_go_dead.
bugs.impact: TMM may restart continuously resulting in interfaces bouncing constantly.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the device.
bugs.fix: This release fixes issues where nic_failsafe reboot did not happen on HSB failures.

bugs.title: Unable to save advanced customization when using Exchange iApp
bugs.symptoms: When Policy created using Microsoft Exchange iApp script, Advanced Customization (usually of logon page) might fail with error similar to the following: 01020066:3: The requested Customization Template File (/Common/Exchange.app/exch_custom_logon_ag logon.inc) already exists in partition Common.
bugs.conditions: Usually: HA Pair, iApp exchange created profile, in general any advanced customization where name not equals customization_group_name:filename is affected.
bugs.impact: Unable to edit advanced customization, functionality is unaffected.
bugs.workaround: edit bigip.conf apm policy customization-group /Common/Exchange_2010.app/exch_custom_logon_ag { templates { logon.inc { name /Common/Exchange_2010.app/exch_custom_logon:logon.inc } } } change name /Common/Exchange_2010.app/exch_custom_logon:logon.inc to customizaton_group_name:filename i.e. name /Common/Exchange_2010.app/exch_custom_logon_ag:logon.inc
bugs.fix: Can now save advanced customization when using Microsoft Exchange iApp.

bugs.title: f5optics not enabled on Herculon iSeries variants HRC-i2800, HRC-i5800, HRC-i10800
bugs.symptoms: The f5optics functionality is not initialized on Herculon iSeries variants.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the following Herculon iSeries platforms: HRC-i2800, HRC-i5800, HRC-i10800.
bugs.impact: None. No f5optics optics module database is presently provided for Herculon platforms. Herculon uses no optics modules that require tuning (e.g., 100G).
bugs.fix: With the fix, if an optics module data base is provided via an f5optics install, f5optics will become operational on Herculon. An f5optics database will be provided if optics modules requiring tuning are ever used with Herculon.

bugs.title: MP_JOIN always fails if MPTCP never receives payload data
bugs.symptoms: MP_JOIN during an MPTCP connection always fails if the BIG-IP never receives payload data.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is configured with a TCP profile attached and "Multipath TCP" is enabled. An MPTCP connection is established where payload data is never sent to the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Unidirectional data connections receiving data from the BIG-IP (like with FTP) cannot join additional subflows.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Allow MP_JOIN after receiving a DATA_ACK that acknowledges data.

bugs.title: OSPF with multiple processes may incorrectly redistribute routes
bugs.symptoms: When OSPF is configured with multiple processes that each redistribute different type routes, LSAs may be created in a process for a route of the type other than the one configured for redistribution into that process.
bugs.conditions: OSPF routing with multiple processes configured. Each OSPF process configured with a different route type redistributed.
bugs.impact: Incorrect routing information in the network when OSPF converges.
bugs.workaround: Redistribute the leaked route type into the affected OSPF process and use a route map that filters out all routes.
bugs.fix: OSPF no longer leaks LSAs between processes redistributing different types of routes. OSPF routes are now created synchronously when the LSA database is updated. If routes are rapidly deleted and re-added, OSPF will send maxage LSAs followed by new LSAs. This is potentially a behavior change where, previously, only a single updated LSA would have been sent.

bugs.title: DNS Express may fail after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: TMM may not answer DNSX zones without TMM restart / DNSX zone refresh on upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from previous version.
bugs.impact: DNS Express may fail after TMM.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM, or force TMM to reload the DNS express database by running "tmsh load ltm dns dns-express-db".
bugs.fix: TMM now answers DNSX zones without requiring TMM restart / DNSX zone refresh on upgrade.

bugs.title: Audit-forwarder can take up an excessive amount of memory during a high volume of logging
bugs.symptoms: During a period where a lot of data is logged (such as the loading of a large configuration), audit_forwarder can use up a large amount of memory.
bugs.conditions: audit_forwarder is used with config.auditing.forward.type set to either "none" or "radius" and config.auditing set to "verbose" or "all".
bugs.impact: The excessive memory usage may result in processes getting restarted. Once the logging is done, audit_forwarder will not release all of the used memory.
bugs.workaround: Setting config.auditing value to "enable" or "disable" will slow or stop the excessive memory usage.
bugs.fix: Prevented audit_forwarder from using more memory than it needs.

bugs.title: Potential TMM crash due to duplicate installed PEM policies by the PCRF
bugs.symptoms: Potential TMM crash due to duplicate installed PEM policies by the PCRF.
bugs.conditions: - PEM enabled with Gx and Gy. - PEM policies configured with Gy quota management. - PCRF installs an already-installed policy against a subscriber.
bugs.impact: Loss of service. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure the PCRF to not install an already-installed policy against a subscriber.
bugs.fix: PEM now prevents PCRF from installing an already-installed policy against a subscriber.

bugs.title: Forcing a single injected tag configuration is restrictive
bugs.symptoms: Injected tags configuration in profile is globally controlled from the db variable antifraud.injecttags, and forces all protected pages to have a common set of HTML tags. If your web application has pages that do not work with the injected tags, then this will cause the application to work improperly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the injected tags db variable (antifraud.injecttags) is configured.
bugs.impact: Your web application may have pages that do not handle the tags properly and may malfunction.
bugs.workaround: Configure injected tags in a way which can applied to all URLs protected in a profile. If it is not possible due to some URL HTML structure, HTML must be modified.
bugs.fix: Injected tags configuration has been moved to the URL level.

bugs.title: Cannot configure any Mobile Security list having 11 records or more via the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Any item added to a list with more than 10 records in Mobile Security section is ignored.
bugs.conditions: Provision FPS License mobilesafe add 11 records to a list
bugs.impact: User configuration may not be saved.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH or Rest.
bugs.fix: GUI allows adding items to lists with more than 10 records.

bugs.title: Redirect loops on URLs with Path Parameters when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When Proactive Bot Defense is enabled, requests to URLs with Path Parameters (URLs containing a semicolon ;) may get stuck on a redirect loop. This typically applies to URLs which do not respond with HTML content or to URLs with low traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Proactive Bot Defense is enabled. -- URLs use Path Parameters (containing the semicolon ; character).
bugs.impact: Clients cannot access the web server, getting caught in an infinite redirect loop.
bugs.fix: Requests to URLs with ";" no longer get stuck in a redirect loop when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.

bugs.title: Operator users receive 'can't get object count from mcpd' error in response to certain commands
bugs.symptoms: Operator users receive the following error in response to certain commands: Unexpected Error: Can't display all items, can't get object count from mcpd.
bugs.conditions: -- The user is 'Operator' level. -- The command is a top-level list or show command, such as the 'show running-config' command.
bugs.impact: Operator-level users are unable to issue 'show' and 'list' commands on top-level objects, but can 'show' and 'list' specific configuration objects.
bugs.workaround: Issue commands for specific configuration objects.
bugs.fix: Operator-level users are now able to issue 'show' and 'list' commands on top-level objects without error.

bugs.title: Core happen when we try to delete PH2 struct does not have a proper PH1 reference.
bugs.symptoms: Racoon cored.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggered the core, it has been observed only once.
bugs.impact: Racoon crash and restore. Usually end user can't see it.
bugs.fix: Added protection from using an internal structure without proper tag.

bugs.title: tmm core with AFM provisioned
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores on the secondary blade while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently with AFM provisioned while passing traffic, even if AFM is not in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Classification signatures fails to update and there are no errors in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: The libcec.so library fails to update, and errors are no longer displayed in the GUI. Var/log/hitless_upgrade.log provides a hint that the upgrade is failing: update_dpi_sigfile.pl|DEBUG|Nov 01 20:39:33.305|19694|F5::DPI::Sigfile::AutoDownload::call_soap_server,,Timestamp: 2016-10-19 11:25:00, BigIP: 12.1.0 update_dpi_sigfile.pl|INFO|Nov 01 20:39:34.562|19694|F5::Sigfile::Update::update,,The most recent DPI Signatures file is already installed.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system is updated to the latest libcec.so, for example, using 'hitless upgrade' (Traffic Intelligence / Classification / Check for updates). -- Upgrade the software. By using "Check for updates"
bugs.impact: Classification signatures fail to update. There are no errors displayed in the GUI. Running the 'tmsh list ltm classification' command shows that the new version has not been installed. Additionally, in /var/log/hitless_upgrade.log: update_dpi_sigfile.pl|DEBUG|Nov 01 20:39:33.305|19694|F5::DPI::Sigfile::AutoDownload::call_soap_server,,Timestamp: 2016-10-19 11:25:00, BigIP: 12.1.0 update_dpi_sigfile.pl|INFO|Nov 01 20:39:34.562|19694|F5::Sigfile::Update::update,,The most recent DPI Signatures file is already installed.
bugs.workaround: Check /var/log/hitless_upgrade.log log
bugs.fix: The system now display error message on GUI correctly

bugs.title: Debug Messages for libcec.so library Hitless Upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Using 'hitless upgrade' (Traffic Intelligence :: Classification :: Signature Update :: Check for updates, or the tmsh command, tmsh list ltm classification signature-version) does not provide sufficient information in messages to indicate success or enable debugging of failure, nor do messages report the installed version of libcec.so. The system does not report the installed version of libcec, the classification library for PEM, in GUI or tmsh. The output shows the date that it last updated, but doesn't report the version of the library that it updated to.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system that was previously updated to a non-default libcec.so, for example, using 'hitless upgrade' (Traffic Intelligence / Classification / Signature Update / Check for updates). -- Upgrade the software. This reverts libcec.so to the original ISO distribution, as libcec is not part of the UCS file. -- Attempt to upgrade libcec again. The system responds as if the latest version is already running, despite it not existing on disk.
bugs.impact: There are no errors displayed in the GUI (or in tmsh). The only failure information available exists in /var/log/hitless_upgrade.log: update_dpi_sigfile.pl|DEBUG|Nov 01 20:39:33.305|19694|F5::DPI::Sigfile::AutoDownload::call_soap_server,,Timestamp: 2016-10-19 11:25:00, BigIP: 12.1.0 update_dpi_sigfile.pl|INFO|Nov 01 20:39:34.562|19694|F5::Sigfile::Update::update,,The most recent DPI Signatures file is already installed. This problem occurs because the decision on whether to to update is based on classification signature-version :: last-update-datetime, which is stored in the config, survives an upgrade, and is not tightly bound to the actual datetime of libcec on disk.
bugs.workaround: Before performing hitless upgrade, click 'Reset to Defaults' (under Traffic-Intelligence / Classification / Signature Update). This deletes the classification_signature_version object, which allows the hitless upgrade operation to succeed.
bugs.fix: The system now reports the installed version of libcec, the classification library for PEM in response to the following command: tmsh list ltm classification signature-version.

bugs.title: Edge Client shows several security warnings after roaming to a network with Captive Portal
bugs.symptoms: Network is blocked by a captive portal. Captive portal uses HTTPS. Periodic-session-check reports SSL certificate is not trusted because access to APM is redirected (to captive portal).
bugs.conditions: Create a VPN tunnel over WiFi. Place the computer in sleep/hibernate. Move to a new network with Captive Portal with SSL and resume from sleep/hibernate.
bugs.impact: Numerous security warnings.
bugs.fix: Edge Client no longer shows several security warnings after roaming to a network with Captive Portal.

bugs.title: Edge Client reconnection issues with captive portal
bugs.symptoms: Edge Client stuck at 'Reconnecting' when losing connection to Captive Portal with certificate warning.
bugs.conditions: Connect to APM through a captive portal.
bugs.impact: EdgeClient stuck at "Reconnecting".
bugs.fix: Edge Client no longer hangs at 'Reconnecting' when losing connection to Captive Portal with certificate warning.

bugs.title: Under rare circumstances, all blades in cluster claim not primary during start up
bugs.symptoms: All blades in cluster claim not primary during startup
bugs.conditions: during TMM startup
bugs.impact: The cluster (even if standalone) appears Standby, and ready-for-world is never reached.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm on primary blade

bugs.title: Multiple audit_forwarder processes cause the mcpd process to use a lot of CPU cycles
bugs.symptoms: Running multiple instances of syslog-ng causes multiple instances of audit_forwarder to be started up. Once more than one audit_forwarder process starts, mcpd CPU usage becomes excessive.
bugs.conditions: Running multiple instances of syslog-ng.
bugs.impact: The systems slows down significantly. /dev/log may be deleted and recreated with the wrong selinux contexts The GUI may become unresponsive and display a blank page.
bugs.workaround: Do not run more than one instance of syslog-ng.

bugs.title: Advanced customization doesn't work for Profiles in non-common partition with . (period) with name
bugs.symptoms: Advanced customization doesn't work for Profiles in non-common partition with . (period) with name. For example, when selecting logon.inc, it shows no source in the window.
bugs.conditions: Access Profile outside of Common partition.
bugs.impact: Unable to modify advanced customizaiton. Other functionality is not affected.
bugs.workaround: Rename profile and policy to non-period version or import profile and then reexport with no periods.
bugs.fix: Advanced customization now works for Profiles in non-Common partition with . (period) with name

bugs.title: In rare conditions, DNS cache resolver outbound TCP connections fail to expire.
bugs.symptoms: If a TCP connection is initiated by the DNS cache resolver but fails to be fully created, it may be leaked until the next restart of tmm.
bugs.conditions: This is only known to occur when other internal issues are affecting the tmm's functionality. If there are ongoing log messages in the tmm logs of the form: "hud_msg_queue is full," and a DNS cache resolver is attempting new outbound TCP connections, then it is possible to leak these connections.
bugs.impact: If enough connections are leaked, the tmm will not be able to create new connections even if the conditions causing the "hud_msg_queue" log messages resolve.
bugs.workaround: Restarting tmm will clear the leaked connections.
bugs.fix: The connections are now properly cleaned up if they are unsuccessfully created.

bugs.title: Displaying Hardware SYN Cookie Protection field in TCP/FastL4/FastHTTP profiles
bugs.symptoms: The Hardware SYN Cookie Protection field is not displayed in the GUI configuration screen for TCP/FastL4/FastHTTP profiles, despite hardware support for the feature existing on the platform.
bugs.conditions: Configuring TCP/FastL4/FastHTTP profiles in the BIG-IP GUI. This occurs on vCMP guests, on the 5000/5050, 5200/5250, 7000/7050/7055, 7200/7250/7255, 10000/100050/10055, 10200/10250/10255, 10350N, i5600, i5800, i7600, i7800, i10600, i10800 platforms, and on VIPRION systems using the B4450 or B4450N blades.
bugs.impact: The Hardware SYN Cookie Protection field is not displayed.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to set the Hardware SYN Cookie Protection field.
bugs.fix: The system no longer uses a static list of platforms that have an HSB as a basis for displaying the Hardware SYN Cookie Protection option in the GUI, so the field is shown as expected.

bugs.title: BIG-IP iSeries does not disallow configuring of management IP outside the management subnet using the LCD
bugs.symptoms: Configuring the management IP outside the management subnet succeeds without error.
bugs.conditions: On the LCD, navigate to the 'Setup' tab, and select 'Management'. 1. Set the default Gateway for the network. 2. Now set an IP address outside the Gateway subnet. 3. Notice no errors and commit is successful.
bugs.impact: Admin IP and Gateway for management route (/Common/default) not in a connected network.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure the IP and Gateway outside the management route.
bugs.fix: LCD no longer allows invalid configuration of mgmt IP (with gateway IP outside mgmt subnet).

bugs.title: CGNAT: Inbound NAT session logs may not log delete event after a blade failover
bugs.symptoms: After a blade failover, an existing inbound session may not have the delete event logged when it completes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- lsn-pool with NAPT. -- Inbound session logging enabled. -- HA configuration. -- After failover.
bugs.impact: The add event for the inbound session may not have a matching delete event.

bugs.title: Adding new item in VPE might end up with error
bugs.symptoms: Certain policies or macros can't be edited properly, usually after import. Errors like "Agent (XYZ) is already referenced by another access policy item" or "Access policy item type Action (XYZ) is already referenced by more than one access policy item."
bugs.conditions: When adding new item in certain (usually imported) policies where situation like %PROFILE%_logon_page_1 uses %PROFLE%_logon_page_2_ag might end up that %PROFILE%_logon_page_2 wouldn't be able to create agent
bugs.impact: VPE is unable to add action / create agent of certain types.
bugs.workaround: Editing bigip.conf and restoring enumeration for offending item (better for item rather than agent) would help to avoid this bug
bugs.fix: VPE now properly checks for existing agent names, so policies or macros can be edited properly.

bugs.title: TMM crash during request normalization
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash during request normalization
bugs.conditions: This could occur with APM virtual servers, or if an HTTP virtual server is configured with a local traffic policy or iRule that performs normalization.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Improve request normalization

bugs.title: Unconditional logs seen due to the presence of a PEM iRule.
bugs.symptoms: TMM log files will fill up.
bugs.conditions: Execution of an iRule with the following iRule command: PEM::subscriber config policy get <subscriber-id> <e164 | imsi | nai | private | mac-address | dhcp | mac-dhcp | dhcp-custom | sip-uri>.
bugs.impact: Limits the gathering and traversal of relevant data from the TMM logs if the condition is encountered several times.
bugs.workaround: Do not use an iRule containing the following iRule command: PEM::subscriber config policy get.
bugs.fix: Unconditional logs are no longer seen in response to the presence of a PEM iRule.

bugs.title: Memory leak when modifying large datagroups
bugs.symptoms: When modifying large external datagroups, a significant memory leak may occur.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when a large datagroup is in use and is modified.
bugs.impact: Memory is leaked, and the amount of memory leaked can be significant.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak related to modifying large datagroups.

bugs.title: Add Hyperlink to gslb server and vs on the Pool Member List Page
bugs.symptoms: Hyperlinks to the GSLB Server and Virtual-server are missing from the GSLB Pool Member list page.
bugs.conditions: This can be seen in the DNS :: GSLB : Pools : Pick a pool : Members tab
bugs.impact: You are unable to to quickly get to the server and virtual server from this page.
bugs.workaround: Manually navigate to associated server and Virtual Server.
bugs.fix: Hyperlinks for associated server and VS are not showing on the Pool Member list page.

bugs.title: BMC version 2.51.7 for iSeries appliances
bugs.symptoms: Firmware on BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx needs to be upgraded to BMC version 2.51.7.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx. -- Upgrading firmware.
bugs.impact: This is a firmware upgrade.
bugs.fix: This release contains BMC version 2.51.7 which includes the fix for a BMC firmware update failure on the following BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx.
bugs.behavior: This release contains BMC version 2.51.7 which includes the fix for a BMC firmware update failure on the following BIG-IP iSeries appliances: i2xx, i4xx, i5xx, i7xx.

bugs.title: Right pane displaying doesn't respect pin selected function when filter just applied
bugs.symptoms: When applying a filter when Pin Selected function is enabled, it doesn't work. If disabling and enabling it again, everything will be fine and filtered entities will be pinned.
bugs.workaround: Disable and re-enable Pin Selected option
bugs.fix: When changing filters from outside of the widget, the widget will update the position of its selected entities.

bugs.title: Comparison Charts are alive only during while staying on the page
bugs.symptoms: Comparison Charts are not persisted and if the page is reloaded or navigated away from in any other way, the charts will be lost.
bugs.conditions: Refreshing the page while looking at comparison charts.
bugs.impact: Settings are not preserved; you must reconfigure them to see the comparison.
bugs.fix: All charts configuration, including comparison charts will be persisted during navigation session (as long as the browser tab is open), even if the page is reloaded or being navigated away from.

bugs.title: BIG-IP should send SHA1 in supported signature hash algorithm last (clientside / Server Hello).
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP should send SHA1 in supported signature hash algorithm last (clientside / Server Hello). Instead, the BIG-IP system is sending SHA1 signature algorithms in the Server Hello first.
bugs.conditions: clientside / Server Hello.
bugs.impact: Minimal. SHA1 algorithms are listed first and they should be last.
bugs.fix: The system now reorders signature hash algorithms such that SHA1 is last.

bugs.title: Portal Access may delete scripts from HTML page in some cases
bugs.symptoms: If JavaScript uses Range.createContextualFragment() call to insert new scripts into HTML document, in some cases Portal Access may delete one of the scripts in the page.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript with Range.createContextualFragment() call which is used to add new scripts by subsequent insertBefore()/insertAfter() calls.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Now web apps delivered via APM Portal Access can use Range.createContextualFragment(), insertBefore(), and insertAfter() javascript properly.

bugs.title: Any CSS content truncated at a quoted value leads to a segfault
bugs.symptoms: Any CSS content truncated at a quoted value leads to a segfault. Example: ... .c1 {background-image: url('some
bugs.conditions: CSS ends without closing quote in value. Example: ... .c1 {background-image: url('some
bugs.impact: TMM or rewrite segfault. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use a particular iRule.
bugs.fix: CSS content truncated at a quoted value no longer leads to a segfault.

bugs.title: iControl keymanagment impory may fail when stale content exists in /config/ssl
bugs.symptoms: iControl returns fault similar to "Keys do not match" when respective key/cert does not exist in the filestore.
bugs.conditions: Stale cert/key in /config/ssl which matches the name of the cert/key being imported. For example, iControl attempting to import file as test.crt while /config/ssl/ssl.key contains test.key which does not match test.crt.
bugs.impact: Unable to import cert/key with particular name while /config/ssl contains stale content.
bugs.workaround: Remove the conflicting file from /config/ssl/ssl.{key,crt}.
bugs.fix: A certificate being imported is now checked against contents in filestore to determine whether the contents in /config/ssl are stale.

bugs.title: Parent profiles cannot be saved using FPS GUI
bugs.symptoms: Any parent profile (profile that has bee inherited) cannot be saved in FPS GUI.
bugs.conditions: Provision FPS License FPS. 1 or more child profiles.
bugs.impact: User configurations may not be saved.
bugs.workaround: Can use TMSH or REST.

bugs.title: External datagroups with no metadata can crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: If a large data group exists or the db variable tmm.classallocatemetadata is set to disabled, tmm may crash if the class match iRule matches 9 or more items in the datagroup.
bugs.conditions: External datagroups in use, a class match iRule will produce at least 9 matches, and the datagroup is extremely large or the db variable tmm.classallocatemetadata is set to disabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to large datagroups.

bugs.title: Incorrect initial size of connection flow-control window
bugs.symptoms: When a client establishes an HTTP2 connection, both endpoints can update their flow-control windows for the connection but their initial sizes of connection flow-control windows must be 65,535. BIG-IP erroneously sets it immediately to a configured value instead. Discrepancy in the window size calculation can result in cancelling of the client's requests.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server that has an HTTP2 profile with a custom value for receive-window exceeding 79 (Kilobytes).
bugs.impact: BIG-IP updates another endpoint with a WINDOW_UPDATE frame for the connection once it reaches a certain threshold. It doesn't happen when receive-window is set above 79 (Kilobytes). If a client has a large request (e.g., POST with a large amount of data), it resets the stream with HTTP2 RST_STREAM frame, canceling the request.
bugs.workaround: Configure receive-window attribute in HTTP2 profile to a value below 80 (Kilobytes).
bugs.fix: The fix in this release allows BIG-IP to behave according to RFC and send WINDOW_UPDATE frames, preventing the connection flow-control window from exhaustion on a remote endpoint.

bugs.title: TMSH output shows dtca.crt certificate-key-size is 1
bugs.symptoms: TMSH output shows dtca.crt certificate-key-size is 1, but the correct value should be 2048. This appears to be a cosmetic bug only, as OpenLLS shows the correct key size.
bugs.conditions: Running the command tmsh list cm cert dtca.crt.
bugs.impact: Shows dtca.crt certificate-key-size is 1, but the correct value should be 2048. This is a cosmetic issue only.
bugs.workaround: Use OpenLLS to see the correct key size.

bugs.title: Proxy configuration changes are not applied immediately by Firefox on OS X
bugs.symptoms: Once the VPN is established and F5 Access updates the proxy configuration on the client, the first request sent from the Firefox browser does not use the updated proxy configuration. Subsequent requests use the correct proxy configuration.
bugs.conditions: Firefox browser is used on Mac OS X.
bugs.impact: Proxy configuration changes are not applied immediately by Firefox on OS X. Wrong proxy configuration will be used for first request. Depending on setup, the client might not be able to reach the site, or the request won't go through intended proxy server.

bugs.title: Qkview now contains cloud metadata
bugs.symptoms: Qkview does not collect metadata about the host cloud instance in BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) configurations.
bugs.conditions: Anytime you run a qkview from a BIG-IP system running in a cloud environment
bugs.impact: No cloud metadata provided.
bugs.fix: When running a cloud instance of BIG-IP software, qkview now collects metadata about the cloud.
bugs.behavior: Qkview previously did not collect metadata about the host cloud instance in VE configurations. Qkview now collects host environment data when executed on VE.

bugs.title: Incorrect message logged when vCMP guest repartitions a host VLAN
bugs.symptoms: When you delete and re-create a VLAN on a vCMP guest using the same VLAN name, subsequent configuration loads will report a warning: Vlan allowed mismatch found: hypervisor (<hypervisor IP>), guest (/Common/<guest>:-1) and (/Common/<vlan>).
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you repartition a host VLAN on a vCMP guest.
bugs.impact: A warning is displayed, but the warning is benign and can be ignored.

bugs.title: Portal Access: JavaScript expressions in parentheses may be rewritten incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: In some cases Portal Access rewrites incorrectly JavaScript expressions enclosed into parentheses.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript code with the following constructions: - (a.b) (...) - (a[b]) (...) - (b) = ... Assuming 'b' is an element to be rewritten. Some examples: - (window.open) ("", "_blank"); - (form["submit"])(); - (location) = "http://some.org/";
bugs.impact: JavaScript code may not work correctly. In some cases, JavaScript code becomes syntactically incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to remove parentheses around JavaScript expressions where necessary.
bugs.fix: Now JavaScript expressions in parentheses are rewritten correctly.

bugs.title: GUI: virtual-address route-advertisement setting changed from 'selective' to 'disabled' after update
bugs.symptoms: Updating virtual-address setting route-advertisement via GUI setting to 'selective' does not reflect after update.
bugs.conditions: Updating virtual-address setting route-advertisement via the GUI, to 'selective'.
bugs.impact: Setting changes after update.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to update the virtual-address route-advertisement setting.
bugs.fix: Updating of the virtual-address setting route-advertisement via the GUI can be performed correctly now.

bugs.title: OAuth Client/RS and Authorization Server don't work together on the same BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: OAuth Client/RS and Authorization Server don't work together on the same BIG-IP system. These two features cannot be configured on the same BIG-IP system, and have to be configured on separate BIG-IP systems. Beginning with version 13.0.0, APM supports OAuth Client and RS functionality as one feature. APM also supports AS (an F5-specific implementation) as another feature. These two features are dependent on each other in that OAuth Client/RS communicate with AS for authorization decisions.
bugs.conditions: When APM OAuth client/RS and AS are configured on the same BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: APM OAuth Client/RS and AS cannot communicate each other when configured on the same BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Configure OAuth ClientRS on one BIG-IP system and AS on another BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Now OAuth Resource Server (RS), Authorization Server (AS), and Client role can be used simultaneously in the same BIG-IP.

bugs.title: BIG-IP closes a connection when a maximum size window is attempted
bugs.symptoms: HTTP2 provides flow control options which allow you to limit the amount of data on flight. A client can send an increment for a window size to an initial value set by standard to 65,535 bytes. BIG-IP used 64K value inherited from SPDY, causing overflow when the client tried to increment the value to its maximum.
bugs.conditions: HTTP2 profile is configured on a virtual, and client sends a WINDOW_UPDATE frame to increment the value to its maximum.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP considers the window size overflow as a protocol violation thus it shuts the connection down not serving any request.
bugs.fix: With a correct value for initial window size (for both a connection and a stream) BIG-IP correctly processes an increment request of the window size to its maximum.

bugs.title: Big3d memory leak when adding/removing Wide IPs in a GTM sync pair.
bugs.symptoms: The memory consumption of Big3d will slowly increase if a lot of Wide IPs are being created or deleted.
bugs.conditions: Adding or removing Wide IPs on a GTM sync pair.
bugs.impact: A few bytes of memory will be leaked by Big3d on sync.
bugs.workaround: there is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The leak has been eliminated.

bugs.title: No option to display time in 24-hour format at top of web-GUI
bugs.symptoms: There is no option in BIG IP system preferences that changes time format displayed on top of every web-GUI page to 24-hour format (for example, instead of '2:00 PM', time could be displayed as '14:00').
bugs.conditions: System Preferences options for GUI display.
bugs.impact: No way to configure for 24-hour time.
bugs.fix: There is now an option in BIG IP system preferences that controls how time format displays on top of every web-GUI page, 12- or 24-hour format (for example, '2:00 PM', or '14:00').

bugs.title: REST token storage improvement
bugs.symptoms: Under some conditions, it is possible to exceed the capacity of the REST token storage subsystem
bugs.conditions: REST interface in heavy use by authenticated users
bugs.impact: Unable to generate additional REST tokens
bugs.fix: Improve handling of REST tokens under high usage conditions

bugs.title: tmsh show sys perf command gives an error "011b030d:3: Graph 'dnsx' not found"
bugs.symptoms: When you run the command tmsh show sys perf, you get an error: 011b030d:3: Graph 'dnsx' not found This can also occur with other tmsh commands related to performance statistics, like show sys perf dnssec and show sys perf dnsexpress.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what exactly triggers this, it is caused by a timing issue that occurs during system initialization of multi-blade chassis.
bugs.impact: Certain tmsh sys perf commands fail to work and give an error.
bugs.workaround: Restart statsd on all blades once the chassis is up. e.g. "bigstart restart statsd" on each blade.
bugs.fix: statsd has been updated to reparse the statsd config file before rebuild it's config so that it doesn't lose the unsupported tables in it's list.

bugs.title: Under certain conditions, monitors do not time out.
bugs.symptoms: Some monitored resources are marked as "Unknown" when the actual status is "offline".
bugs.conditions: This can rarely occur when the monitor timeout period elapses when either no response has been received, or a response has been received indicating that the resource is "down" and the monitor is configured to ignore down responses. It is more likely to occur when many monitor timeout periods elapse at the same time, and the monitor timeout value is evenly divisible by the monitor's monitor interval.
bugs.impact: The status of the monitored resource is incorrect. This does not materially affect the operation of the system since resources marked "Unknown" will not be used.
bugs.workaround: Disable the affected resources, and then enable them again.
bugs.fix: The resource status is now correct under all monitor timeout conditions.

bugs.title: No drill-down filter for virtual-servers is mentioned on exported reports when using partition
bugs.symptoms: The selected filters will not appear in exported reports for virtual servers created under non 'Common' partitions.
bugs.conditions: When using virtual-servers and ASM policies under a non 'Common' partition, exported reports will not display the the selected drill-down filters.
bugs.impact: Exported reports will be displayed without the filters.
bugs.fix: Exported reports will take into consideration partitions which will make the drill-down filters appear as expected.

bugs.title: Corrupt policy history file causes UCS load to fail
bugs.symptoms: When a UCS containing a corrupted policy history is loaded from the CLI, the system posts an an error similar to the following: Can't call method "policy_name" on an undefined value at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/PolicyHistory.pm line 134. When the same UCS is loaded a second time, a message similar to the following is also reported: 01070710:3: Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:fw_log_profile status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127 Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when upgrading from v12.0.0 to v12.1.x if these files are empty (length 0), and cause UCS restore to fail because they cannot be read. The ASM configuration fails to upgrade properly, leaving all of the policies in transparent mode.
bugs.impact: Failed upgrade.
bugs.workaround: 1. Copy the last known valid versions of policies to replace the corrupted files. 2. Recreate the UCS. 3. Try the upgrade again.
bugs.fix: Corrupt policy history file no longer causes UCS load to fail.

bugs.title: ASM failures after upgrade due to empty file for most recent policy history
bugs.symptoms: ASM fails to start up correctly after roll-forward upgrade when the most recent policy history file for an active policy is empty. When this condition is encountered, the following messages are seen in /var/log/ts/ts_debug.log: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- asm|INFO|...Can't call method "policy_name" on an undefined value at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/PolicyHistory.pm line 134. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- ASM enforcer (BD) will fail with core dump on every repeated attempt to start.
bugs.conditions: The most recent policy history file for an active policy is empty. This may have occurred due to a full disk partition. However, if empty policy files were created on previous versions, ASM still fails following an aborted attempt to upgrade using these empty policy files.
bugs.impact: ASM fails to start up correctly. Errors appear in /var/log/ts/ts_debug.log and ASM enforcer (BD) fails with core dump repeatedly.
bugs.workaround: To correct this issue, the device configuration should be re-upgraded as follows: 1) Reboot to another installation location. 2) Delete the empty policy history file using a command similar to the following: rm /ts/dms/policy/policy_versions/8/57.plc 3) Save UCS file and Reboot. 4) Load UCS file saved in Step 3.
bugs.fix: Empty policy history files will not be written. Thus, subsequent roll-forward upgrades will complete successfully.

bugs.title: FPS Log Publisher is not grouped nor filtered by partition
bugs.symptoms: If there are several log publishers assigned to different partitions, it is not clear which log publisher is assigned to which partition. All log publishers are displayed regardless of the partition selected.
bugs.conditions: Provision FPS. Two or more partitions Two or more log publishers assigned to different partitions
bugs.impact: All log publishers are displayed regardless of partition.
bugs.fix: Log publishers are now grouped in GUI and filtered by the currently selected partition.

bugs.title: Request Events Missing Due to Policy Builder Restart
bugs.symptoms: Policy builder process restarts when it gets a UCS load event. As a result, request events are missing from the request log while policy builder is catching up on the policies.
bugs.conditions: -- In a high availability environment when devices require a full ASM sync from their peer. -- Learning is enabled for ASM policies.
bugs.impact: Any requests that needed to be logged due to a logging profile (e.g., Log All) will be lost during this time. This occurs because policy builder is responsible for logging these requests. These restarts are not particularly harmful.
bugs.fix: Policy builder now handles requests while catching up on the policies assuring no requests are lost due to the restart.

bugs.title: TMM may stall and not service queued connections on pool state transition
bugs.symptoms: In certain situations TMM may not process all connections queued in a configured connection queue if the relevant poolmember has been disabled/down, connection enqueued, and poolmember reenabled.
bugs.conditions: All of the following: - Persistence on VIP. - Slow ramp configured on pool. - Connection queueing on pool. - Connection limiting on poolmember. - Poolmember is disabled/down, connection is enqueued to poolmember, and poolmember is re-enabled/up.
bugs.impact: The queued connection to the VIP/poolmember on the specific TMM will remain in that state until the connection is either killed or client shuts down the connection. Any additional connections queued behind the prior queued connection will also stay queued. This will continue until all connections to the VIP/pmbr/tmm cease to connect/queue and are deleted.
bugs.workaround: You can use one of the following as a workaround: - Don't use persistence (or present via fallback) that makes cmp lookups, if a single poolmember is used in the pool. - Disable slow ramp If the situation has already occurred, delete all connections to the VIP/Affected TMM. After which new connections will work as expected.

bugs.title: CGNAT SIP ALG will drop SIP INVITE
bugs.symptoms: SIP INVITE message is dropped.
bugs.conditions: Subscriber registers and then attempts to call out.
bugs.impact: Subscriber not able to make calls.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the expiration value from the SIP message i.e. either from expires parameter or the Expire header to update the timeout of the registration record.

bugs.title: FastL4 virtual server with enabled loose-init option works differently with/without AFM provisioned
bugs.symptoms: If AFM provisioned, a FastL4 virtual server with enabled loose-init option drops all RST packets that do not relate to any existing flows. This behavior does not match the BIG-IP behavior when AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned. -- FastL4 virtual server. -- Loose-init option enabled.
bugs.impact: RST packets that do not relate to any existing flows are dropped, while they should not be dropped if the loose-init option enabled.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Fixed, so FastL4 virtual servers with enabled loose-init option will forward any RST packets.

bugs.title: A secondary mirroring address may be used when the primary address is available.
bugs.symptoms: TMM tries to establish a mirroring connection to both the primary and the secondary mirroring address. If the secondary mirroring address is connected faster, it will be used even when the primary address is available.
bugs.conditions: The secondary mirroring address is connected faster than the primary.
bugs.impact: The secondary mirroring address is used when the primary address is available.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The primary mirroring address takes priority over the secondary mirroring address.

bugs.title: Edge client stuck on "Initializing" state
bugs.symptoms: It takes a lot of time to reestablish the VPN connection when the Edge Client switches to network with Captive Portal authentication. Edge client freezes on "Initializing" state for around 1 minute.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on the Edge Client with Captive Portal configured.
bugs.impact: Edge client is stuck on "Initializing" for an excessive amount of time.

bugs.title: On DoS Visiblity pages, metrics from unprovisioned modules are displayed in the widgets
bugs.symptoms: When either ASM or AFM are not provisioned, Dimension Widgets are still showing metrics that belong to these modules.
bugs.conditions: Have either ASM or AFM provisioned, but not both
bugs.impact: We're showing metrics that aren't applicable to the given system
bugs.fix: Only metrics belonging to provisioned modules will be presented to the user.

bugs.title: the TCP::unused_port does erroneous accept IPV4_COMPAT addresses
bugs.symptoms: when calling TCP::unused_port command with a tcl ip addr object which represents the IPv4 address as IPv4-Compatible IPv6 address, the function searches for existing flows related to this address. IPv4-Compatible IPv6 addresses are deprecated, the flow table uses IPv4-Mapped IPv6 address
bugs.conditions: the IP::Addr object has been crafted with the following command [IP::addr <addr> mask ::ffff:ffff]
bugs.impact: The TCP::unused_port command is unable to return an unused port
bugs.workaround: use the string representation by forcing the object to be a string e.g. set ipv6_addr "fe80::250:56ff:0a1e:0101" set ipv4_from_ipv6 [ string tolower [IP::addr $ipv6_addr mask ::ffff:ffff] ] set free [TCP::unused_port $ipv4_from_ipv6 [TCP::local_port] 10.30.1.64 [TCP::client_port] 48000 48255]
bugs.fix: ID598860-5 fixes the IP::addr command to return IPV4 MAPPED addr

bugs.title: vCMP hypervisor version mismatch may cause connection mirroring problems.
bugs.symptoms: Connections may not be mirrored correctly when vCMP hypervisors use different software versions.
bugs.conditions: Mirroring for a pair of vCMP guest is enabled. vCMP hypervisors use different DAG software versions.
bugs.impact: Connections are mirrored incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: Use the same hypervisor software version when mirroring is configured for a pair of vCMP guests.
bugs.fix: Mirroring connection isn't established anymore when vCMP hypervisors use different DAG software versions.

bugs.title: IPsec: Traffic continues when the ike-peers are disabled
bugs.symptoms: Disabling an ike-peer has no effect.
bugs.conditions: Trying to disable an IPsec ike-peer using the following tmsh command: tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer <name> state disabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic continues when the ike-peers are disabled.
bugs.workaround: Delete the ike-peer instead of trying to disable it.

bugs.title: Access policy is applied automatically on target device after policy sync, when there is a also a FODG in the trust domain.
bugs.symptoms: After syncing an access policy, the access policy change on the other device should be prompting you to apply the policy, but instead it applies the policy automatically.
bugs.conditions: Two or more devices configured in a trust group, one device group is a failover device group, and one device group is a sync-only device group with automatic sync enabled.
