A key component that triggers this symptom is that the failover device group is listed first in the configuration. When this occurs, the policy will be applied automatically, which shouldn't occur.
bugs.impact: Policy changes are automatically applied, when they should only be synced with a prompt to apply after the sync.
bugs.fix: After syncing an access policy, the access policy change on the other device in the trust group now prompts you to apply the policy, which is correct behavior.

bugs.title: "HTTP 401 Response" agent reuses incorrect credentials
bugs.symptoms: In case of invalid credentials, user gets prompted less number of times than the 'Max Logon Attempts Allowed' count defined in auth agent.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs only when "HTTP 401 Response" agent is used before authentication agent in access policy.
bugs.impact: User won't get same number of logon attempts as defined in Auth Agent.
bugs.workaround: In auth agent, "Max Logon Attempts Allowed" should be set to 5 in order to get 3 logon attempts.
bugs.fix: UserÂ will get same number of logon attempts as defined in auth agent in case of invalid credentials.

bugs.title: Remote-logging where destination matches virtual will be sourced from loopback network
bugs.symptoms: Remote-logging traffic sent from the loopback network (e.g., 127.1.1.1).
bugs.conditions: Destination of remote-logging traffic matches virtual server.
bugs.impact: Remote-logging may be dropped due to sourced from non-routeable network.
bugs.workaround: Enable snat automap on the remote-logging virtual or create transparent host virtual (arp disable) which matches the remote-logging destination with snat automap enabled. Alternatively, an iRule could be associated with the virtual which snats traffic from the loopback network. Care must be taken to take route domains into consideration while writing the iRule. Example iRule for virtual in route-domain 38: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { # Work-around for ID629830. if { [IP::addr [getfield [IP::client_addr] "%" 38] equals 127.0.0.0/8] } { snat automap } }
bugs.fix: Remote-logging traffic is no longer sent from the loopback network (e.g., 127.1.1.1). This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: istatsd high CPU utilization with large number of entries
bugs.symptoms: With a large number of istats entries, statsd uses a large amount of CPU time to process istats.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a large number of istats entries in iRules.
bugs.impact: istats processing is slow. CPU utilization by istatsd is high.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of istats entries. Periodically purge the the istats entries if possible.

bugs.title: Disallowing TLSv1 connections to HTTP causes iControl/REST issues
bugs.symptoms: When HTTP disallows TLSv1 connections, UCS via iControl/REST fails with the following in the logs: [SEVERE][86][08 Nov 2016 16:47:20 UTC][com.f5.rest.icontrol.IControlRunnable] (iControl execution) AxisFault[; nested exception is: javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: Received fatal alert: handshake_failure]: [WARNING][87][08 Nov 2016 16:47:20 UTC][8100/tm/shared/sys/backup/52d67805-3aab-4260-8770-a690154c698e/worker UcsBackupTaskWorker] Failed to restore from backup: backup_test.ucs
bugs.conditions: This occurs when TLSv1 is explicitly disallowed in the HTTP profile.
bugs.impact: iControl REST clients are unable to connect.
bugs.fix: Explicitly disallowing TLSv1 in the HTTP profile no longer causes iControl/REST issues.

bugs.title: FTP ALG deployment should not rewrite PASV response 464 XLAT cases
bugs.symptoms: Deploying NAT64 part of a 464 XLAT solution may overwrite PASV response 464 XLAT cases.
bugs.conditions: FTP ALG deployment.
bugs.impact: PASV response 464 XLAT cases overwritten.
bugs.fix: Deploying NAT64 part of a 464 XLAT solution no longer overwrites PASV response 464 XLAT cases.

bugs.title: Cannot login with Firefox and IE after toggling between wireless and wired networks.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot log into BIG-IP's Web GUI on Firefox and Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) for the first 3-5 attempts after toggling the host computer's network between wireless and wired connections.
bugs.conditions: Using Firefox or IE browsers. Toggling between a wired and wireless network connections.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP shows a "login failed" page in the Web UI. The user cannot login with correct credentials for 3-5 attempts. Note: The number of attempts may be timing-dependent.
bugs.workaround: Use any of the following options: -- Use a Chrome browser. -- Do not toggle between different networks for internet access (i.e., wired and wireless). -- Keep trying to logon (i.e., try more than five times, or for a few minutes after toggling between networks). -- Restart the browser. -- Clear cookies.

bugs.title: [[SWG]-NTLM 407 based front end auth and passthrough 401 based NTLM backend auth does not work.
bugs.symptoms: With SWG client side NTLM auth configuration while doing the NTLM auth for backend, ECA plugin is trapping the Authorization credentials (NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE) sent by the client, it sinks the request and generates the 407 to the client to do proxy authentication.
bugs.conditions: Set-up SWG for auth with ntlm credentials Access a proxied resource which also requires ntlm auth
bugs.impact: Backend server access is restricted.
bugs.fix: Now when using SWG in explicit proxy mode with NTLM authentication with the Proxy-Authenticate header, BIG-IP allows NTLM authentication to proceed simultaneously to protected resource servers that also use NTLM authentication with the Authenticate header.

bugs.title: Microsoft Edge 14 on Windows 10 mobile device may collect incorrect Device ID
bugs.symptoms: In some cases of users using Microsoft Edge 14 on Microsoft Windows 10 mobile, the device ID may be collected incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: Device ID is enabled is ASM Policy or DOS Profile.
bugs.impact: Repeat ASM end users might be detected as new ones.
bugs.fix: Device ID is now collected correctly using Microsoft Edge 14 on Windows 10 mobile devices.

bugs.title: gnome-software throws error "This file is not supported" for F5EPI and F5VPN RPMs on Fedora 25
bugs.symptoms: gnome-software throws error "This file is not supported" for F5VPN and F5EPI RPMs on Fedora 25. Download F5EPI or F5VPN applications from chrome/firefox browsers. Once downloaded double clicking will launch gnome-software and it throws the specified error.
bugs.conditions: gnome-software, F5EPI and F5VPN RPM. This is specific to Fedora 25 and gnome-software version 3.22.1.
bugs.impact: F5EPI and F5VPN applications cannot be installed using OS native software installer GUI.
bugs.workaround: Open Terminal application and go to command line and run either one of the following commands: - pkgcon install-local -y -n /path/to/rpm/package. - dnf install /path/to/rpm/package.
bugs.fix: Versions of gnome-software 3.22.5 and later can now install F5EPI and F5VPN helper applications successfully.

bugs.title: AVR statistics is not saved during the upgrade process
bugs.symptoms: All AVR statistics will be reset after upgrade from 12.1.0 or 12.1.1.
bugs.conditions: AVR statistics collected on 12.1.0 or 12.1.1. The BIG-IP is upgraded.
bugs.impact: AVR statistics are reset.
bugs.workaround: 1. before upgrade edit the following file: ./usr/libdata/configsync/avr_save_pre 2. change the following line " [ $(is_provisioned avr) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned pem) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned afm) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned swg) -eq 1 $(is_provisioned asm) -eq 1 ] && " with " [ $(is_provisioned avr) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned pem) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned afm) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned swg) -eq 1 -o $(is_provisioned asm) -eq 1 ] && "
bugs.fix: AVR upgrade script is fixed, so AVR statistics are now saved during the upgrade process.

bugs.title: Dynamic Signatures feature can fill up /config partition impacting system stability
bugs.symptoms: When the AFM DoS Dynamic Signatures feature is enabled, inadequate file housekeeping results in the /config/filestore partition filling up. mcpd halts the other running daemons and the system becomes unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: AFM DoS Dynamic Signatures feature enabled Configuration changes made but not saved Device receives traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Make all configuration changes via Configuration Tool (UI) or issue a 'save sys config partitions all' command. If rolling back the configuration is a requirement, before making changes to the configuration, save a configuration snapshot to a file with the 'save sys config file <filename>' command. You can then load the previous configuration with a 'load sys config file <filename>' command.
bugs.fix: AFM DoS Dynamic Signatures file housekeeping improved, /config filestore no longer fills up.

bugs.title: Websockets processing error
bugs.symptoms: In some cases TMM may crash when processing Websockets traffic.
bugs.conditions: Websockets profile is attached to a virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Improve Websockets processing

bugs.title: Monitor send/receive strings cannot end with trailing single-backslash
bugs.symptoms: A monitor with a 'send' or 'receive' string is not supported with a single trailing backslash, such as "GET /\r\n\" (note the single-trailing backslash that "escapes" the trailing double-quotes).
bugs.conditions: A monitor 'send' or 'receive' string ends with a single trailing backslash; and the configuration is saved, and then a load is attempted.
bugs.impact: When configuration is saved and then loaded, the single-trailing backslash will escape the trailing double-quotes and the configuration will fail to load.
bugs.workaround: A double-trailing backslash is supported, where the trailing double-quotes will not be escaped, for example: "GET /\\r\\n"

bugs.title: Support Substitute value in ajax with application/x-www-form-urlencoded content-Type
bugs.symptoms: Substitute value feature does not support Ajax requests with application/x-www-form-urlencoded content-Type.
bugs.conditions: Send the credentials validation Ajax POST request with application/x-www-form-urlencoded content-Type.
bugs.impact: Page that uses Ajax requests with application/x-www-form-urlencoded content-Type won't be able to use Substitute value feature.

bugs.title: Top Traffic Learning Violations
bugs.symptoms: In v12.x, ASM unified manual learning and automatic policy building, which also caused significant changes in the GUI. There were only suggestions in Traffic Learning screen (both for manual and automatic mode). There were no more tables of manual traffic learning showing violating requests, ordered by violations or attack signatures.
bugs.conditions: When Policy Builder is enabled in ASM.
bugs.impact: In earlier versions, the 'manual traffic learning' feature showed violating requests, ordered by violations, making it possible to learn false positives and improve the policy. It also showed all violations ordered by violations or signature names, instead of the time-based order in the event logs. In later versions, instead of marking those as 'Unknown / Learnable Filetype' or something like 'New Entity Discovered: Filetype XYZ', traffic learning marks those as 'Illegal Filetype/URL <url>', which causes undue concern.
bugs.fix: Four triage sections were added to the Traffic Learning screen to speed up the traffic learning process: - Reduce Potential False-positive Alerts: Tables for the Top Violations, Top Matched Attack Signatures and Top Violating Meta-Characters. - Enforcement Readiness. - Add New Entities. - Delete Inactive Entities.

bugs.title: TMM crash in DNS processing on UDP virtual server with no available pool members
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when processing requests to a DNS virtual server.
bugs.conditions: The issue can occur if a UDP DNS virtual receives a request when no pool members are available to service the request and a DNS iRule is suspended due to previous requests.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation is to ensure at least one pool member is available whenever the DNS virtual is processing traffic, or to avoid iRule commands that can suspend processing. Ensure datagram LB mode is enabled on UDP DNS virtuals.
bugs.fix: This release prevents a crash in DNS processing on UDP virtual server with no available pool members.

bugs.title: Local Logs Missing Or Recorded Found For Incorrect Policy
bugs.symptoms: When loading a UCS (manually or due to a UCS sync) which has a the same ASM Policy names, but created in a differing order, the local logging daemon does not update its internal mappings.
bugs.conditions: The configuration is replaced by a UCS load that had a different list of ASM Policies.
bugs.impact: Local logs may be missing or listed for an incorrect ASM policy.
bugs.workaround: Restart asmlogd.

bugs.title: JavaScript challenge follow-up to POST is sent as GET in iframe from IE/Edge
bugs.symptoms: The JavaScript challenge that is sent to a POST request within an iframe will have a follow-up request of GET when coming from Microsoft Internet Explorer or Edge browser. The request reconstruction is incorrect, and the back-end server does not receive the request payload. This is relevant to all types JavaScript challenges: Proactive Bot Defense, DoSL7 Client-Side Integrity Defense, Device-ID Challenge, or CAPTCHA Challenge.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript challenge is used in a POST request, when one of the following features in enabled: Proactive Bot Defense, DoSL7 Client-Side Integrity Defense, Device-ID Challenge, or CAPTCHA Challenge.
bugs.impact: POST requests will be sent as GET and the request payload will not reach the back-end server.
bugs.fix: JavaScript challenges to POST requests are sent correctly to the back-end server when coming from iframe in Microsoft Internet Explorer/Edge browsers.

bugs.title: Client Side challenges and device ID doesn't work on a virtual server that has also APM
bugs.symptoms: Client side challenges do not work when APM is enabled in clientless mode.
bugs.conditions: APM is on the virtual server as ASM. APM is running in clientless mode.
bugs.impact: device ID related features doesn't work correctly.
bugs.workaround: N/S
bugs.fix: challenges are now sent in when APM in on the chain.

bugs.title: IPsec ALG: Traffic may not go through IPsec tunnel if ipsec.lookupspi is disabled and default DAG is used
bugs.symptoms: The connection table and IPsec ALG profile stats may indicate that the IPsec tunnel has been established, but traffic may not be passing through it.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on appliances when the IPsec ALG is used with default DAG and the sys db variable ipsec.lookupspi is disabled.
bugs.impact: Connections going through the IPsec tunnel may fail.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the db variable ipsec.lookupspi is enabled.

bugs.title: TMM Crash
bugs.symptoms: In some cases TMM may crash when processing TCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: In some cases TMM may crash when processing TCP traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Enable Verified Accept.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer produces a core.

bugs.title: Very large core files may cause corrupted qkviews
bugs.symptoms: If a large core file exists, the qkview command may generate a corrupted qkview.
bugs.conditions: qkview is run when core files greater than 2.4 GB exist in /var/core.
bugs.impact: qkview is unusable.
bugs.workaround: Copy the core files on the slave blade from /etc/core to a back up location and delete the original files before creating the qkview.
bugs.fix: qkview files run when core files greater than 2.4 GB exist in /var/core now complete as expected.

bugs.title: Edge Client on Mac OSX Sierra stuck in a reconnect loop
bugs.symptoms: Upon waking laptop Edge Client stuck in a reconnect loop.
bugs.conditions: Full-Tunnel, no Local LAN Access profile; when opening the device lid, which attempts to reconnect to the VPN service. This occurs only with MAC OS X 10.12.1.
bugs.impact: Cannot connect to VPN, and the Edge Client gets stuck in a reconnect loop.
bugs.workaround: Allow local subnet access set to enabled.
bugs.fix: In this release, using MAC OS X 10.12.1 now resumes a connection to VPN using the Edge Client.

bugs.title: BFD session interface configuration may not be stored on unit state transition
bugs.symptoms: 'bfd session' statements missing in ZebOS 'running-config'.
bugs.conditions: State transitions from online to offline.
bugs.impact: BFD configuration will become missing in ZebOS running config and no BFD sessions will be established.
bugs.workaround: Re-add statements manually.
bugs.fix: BFD session interface configuration is now stored on unit state transition.

bugs.title: PEM module crash when subscriber not fund
bugs.symptoms: Under rare circumstances, PEM usage reporting for a subscriber will cause a crash.
bugs.conditions: PEM subscriber info is missing for the current tmm, e.g., after a CMP state change.
bugs.impact: PEM/TMM SIGSEV.
bugs.fix: PEM usage reporting for a subscriber no longer causes a crash when PEM subscriber info is missing for the current tmm.

bugs.title: tmm crash possible if high-speed logging pool member is deleted and reused
bugs.symptoms: When deleting and then re-using a high-speed logging pool member that is in use, a rare tmm crash may occur.
bugs.conditions: High-speed logging profile configured, high-speed logging pool configured, and a pool member is removed and re-added while the pool is in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Rare tmm crash no longer occurs if high-speed logging pool member is deleted and reused.

bugs.title: WAM may leak memory when a WAM policy node has multiple variation header rules
bugs.symptoms: When a WAM policy node has multiple variation header rules, a memory leak occurs upon evaluation of each request.
bugs.conditions: WAM policy with node utilizing multiple variation header rules.
bugs.impact: Potential per-request memory leakage driven by client traffic.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to ensure that individual WAM policy nodes have fewer than two header variation rules.
bugs.fix: WAM no longer leaks memory when evaluation policy nodes which utilize two or more header variation rules.

bugs.title: Preserve original umask of /etc/hosts file
bugs.symptoms: CLI VPN client changes umask of /etc/hosts to 077. After disconnecting from VPN, the umask is not restored back to the original.
bugs.conditions: CLI VPN client is used to establish VPN connection on Mac/Linux.
bugs.impact: It breaks usability of /etc/resolv.conf for OS apps.
bugs.workaround: An administrator can restore umask of /etc/hosts using system tools.
bugs.fix: Now the Mac/Linux CLI VPN client preserves the original umask of /etc/hosts after disconnecting from VPN.

bugs.title: After provisioning change, Dimension Widgets on DoS Visibility pages are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Dimension Widgets list is defined upon first access to a DoS page during a browsing session. This means that if provisioning changes during that sessions, the widgets that are displayed may be incorrect. When un-provisioning modules it is not a problem since every widget goes through a licensing/provisioning validation before being added to the page. However, if adding a new module to provisioning, new widgets will not be added until the window/tab is closed and a new browsing session starts, or until "Reset Layout" is performed.
bugs.conditions: Change of provisioning modules during browsing session
bugs.impact: List of dimension widgets is not up to date with current provisioning
bugs.workaround: Workaround 1: closing and opening the window or tab. Workaround 2: choosing "Reset Layout" option from the cog menu.
bugs.fix: List of widgets is now determined by what's actually provisioned.

bugs.title: No guestagentd entry in merged.conf
bugs.symptoms: There is no entry in guestagentd in merged.conf. This results in this error in the ltm log whenever merged starts up: "Process managed by runsv is not in /config/merged.conf: guestagentd"
bugs.conditions: This is encountered whenever merged starts.
bugs.impact: In addition, for stats purposes, the proc_stat and plane_proc_stat tables are affected. If the pid changes (for whatever reason) BIG-IP will not have the assignments to the right process information.
bugs.workaround: Add guestagentd entry to merged.conf
bugs.fix: Add guestagentd entry to merged.conf

bugs.title: Network Access tunnel cannot be re-established after failover
bugs.symptoms: After failover, Network Access tunnel will not be able to be re-established.
bugs.conditions: 1. Network Access is used 2. Failover event occurred 3. Config snapshot was deleted before failover
bugs.impact: Application traffic through network access tunnel will stop.
bugs.workaround: End users need to logout and login again to create a new APM session. Then, Network Access tunnel will start up correctly.

bugs.title: Attack signature exception list upload times-out and fails
bugs.symptoms: httpd_errors log: ------------ err httpd[<PID>]: [error] [client <client_IP>] PHP Fatal error: Maximum execution time of 30 seconds exceeded in /var/ts/dms/common/classes/Thrift/packages/asmconfig/f5_thrift.php on line <line_ID>, referer: https://<BIG-IP_MGMT_IP>/dms/policy/pl_header_normalization.php ------------
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. Attack signature exception list uploaded.
bugs.impact: Attack signature exception list upload times-out and fails.
bugs.fix: Improved the Attack signature exception list upload process to take much less time.

bugs.title: Sorting Policy Sync's 'Static' or 'Dynamic' list of objects based on their 'LSO' or 'Dynamic' attribute, leads to unexpected behavior
bugs.symptoms: For the Policy Sync :: Static and Dynamic list of objects, clicking the Location Specific Column header does not sort the data, but instead toggles the checkboxes in the Location Specific column.
bugs.conditions: Clicking the Location Specific Column header on the Policy Sync's list of objects.
bugs.impact: Checkboxes are toggled in the Location Specific column.
bugs.fix: The ambiguity of the behavior when the LSO column header was clicked, was removed by providing a checkbox in the LSO Column header. This allows the user to select the LSO checkbox in multiple rows at a time.

bugs.title: 500 internal error on inline rule editor for certain firewall policies
bugs.symptoms: While attempting to use the inline rule editor on a firewall policy, the system returns a 500 internal error. Viewing and editing the same policy in tmsh works as expected.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when editing certain firewall policies in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Unable to view or edit the policy, page returns an error
bugs.workaround: You can view these rules in the GUI by disabling the inline rule editor.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with certain AFM rules generating a 500 internal error in the GUI.

bugs.title: Unable to generate a FIPS key using the GUI
bugs.symptoms: While generating a FIPS key from the BIG-IP GUI, you get the following error: Key management library returned bad status: -4, FIPS security is not licensed, FIPS key security type is not allowed. Generating a FIPS key from tmsh works properly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on FIPS-licensed 12.1.1 HF1 and HF2, when using the GUI to generate the FIPS key.
bugs.impact: Unable to generate a FIPS key using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use the following tmsh command to generate a FIPS key: tmsh create sys crypto key <key_object_name> security-type fips.

bugs.title: Portal Access [PeopleSoft] 'My Preferences' page does not have content
bugs.symptoms: IN PeopleSoft (PS) web-application 'My Preferences' page contains no content.
bugs.conditions: Steps to Reproduce: 1. Navigate and login to PS Portal through reverse proxy. 2. Click on 'My Preferences' item in 'Action list' button.
bugs.impact: Page contains no content. Web-application does not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use an iRule.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may incorrectly reject serverside connection when REQLOG is configured.
bugs.symptoms: Serverside connection can be reset when V2 plugin e.g. REQLOG is configured on virtual.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with REQLOG and SSL clientside and serverside profiles.
bugs.impact: Serverside connections can not be established due to early TCP RST and failing TCP handshake.
bugs.workaround: Remove REQLOG from configuration.
bugs.fix: V2 Plugins work correctly if clientside is disabled on the hudchain.

bugs.title: Some files in home directory are overwritten on password change
bugs.symptoms: The files .bash_logout .bash_profile .bashrc in a user's home directory are overwritten when that user's password is changed.
bugs.conditions: Change a user's password.
bugs.impact: Customizations to these files would be lost on password change. This only applies to users with advanced shell access.
bugs.workaround: Back up the files to a different location before making a password change.

bugs.title: Some tmstat-adapters based reports stats are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Stats are being collected in a wrong way for tmstat tables that are using partial-key. This leads to wrong values on reports.
bugs.conditions: Using partial key from tmstat-table on tmstat-adapter
bugs.impact: Wrong stats values for some reports.
bugs.fix: Tmstat-Adapters is now using the correct API from tmstat-framework which simulate a 'group-by' function on the query, and thus provide the correct result-set.

bugs.title: GUI user logged off when idle for 30 minutes, even when longer timeout is set
bugs.symptoms: GUI user is auto-logged off when idle for 30 minutes, even though the configured idle timeout is longer.
bugs.conditions: User logged in to gui and idle for 20-30 minutes
bugs.impact: User is logged out of the GUI.
bugs.fix: GUI user is no longer auto-logged off when idle for 30 minutes when the configured idle timeout is longer.

bugs.title: GeoIP lookups incorrectly parse IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, GeoIP lookups may not correctly parse IP addresses.
bugs.conditions: GeoIP lookups enabled
bugs.impact: Unintended responses to GeoIP lookups
bugs.fix: Improve parsing of IP address in GeoIP lookups

bugs.title: URI cache entries should be replaced /expired for euie hash table
bugs.symptoms: Tmctl stats for "access_uri_info" gradually grows and can lead to TMM memory exhaustion.
bugs.conditions: APM or SWG use case.
bugs.impact: TMM memory exhaustion.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm.
bugs.fix: A limit of how many entries will be stored in the URI cache is implemented. The default is 2048 entries, this DB variable can be set to control the max limit: access.max.euie_uri.cache.entries The DB variable allows a range of 2048 - 8192.

bugs.title: Unable to load config with client-SSL profile error
bugs.symptoms: Config loading fails with an error similar to the following: 'Client SSL profile cannot contain more than one set of same certificate/key type.'
bugs.conditions: This occurs when both of the following conditions are met: -- The system is loading config. -- The config contains a client SSL profile which has an RSA cert-key-chain whose key is default (/Common/default.key), but whose chain is non-empty, or the cert is different from /Common/default.crt. For example: cert-key-chain { cert /Common/default.crt <==== default cert chain /Common/chainCA.crt <==== non-empty key /Common/default.key <==== default key rsa { cert /Common/default.crt <==== default cert chain /Common/chainCA.crt <==== non-empty key /Common/default.key <==== default key } }
bugs.impact: Configuration can not be loaded.
bugs.workaround: Remove or adjust the problematic client SSL profile by editing the appropriate bigip.conf file (/config/bigip.conf or /config/partitions/<name>/bigip.conf, depending on the partition the profile resides in), and then load the configuration again. Steps: 1. Open the configuration file in a text editor. 2. Load the file /config/bigip.conf (or /config/partitions/<name>/bigip.conf, if the client SSL profile is in a partition). 3. Update the client SSL profile by setting .crt and .key to non-default, as shown in the following example: cert-key-chain { cert /Common/kc.crt <==== changed to non-default chain /Common/chainCA.crt key /Common/kc.key <==== changed to non-default rsa { cert /Common/kc.crt <==== changed to non-default chain /Common/chainCA.crt key /Common/kc.key <==== changed to non-default } } 4. Save your changes, and then run the following command: tmsh load sys conf

bugs.title: TMSH does not preserve \? for config save/load operations
bugs.symptoms: TMSH strips the escape characters for literal strings '\?' to be '?' or '\[' to be '[' in ltm monitor send/recv strings.
bugs.conditions: This condition manifests whenever the send/recv string in LTM monitor contains '\?' (backslash-question mark) or '\[' (backslash-open square bracket).
bugs.impact: This might cause the BIG-IP system to load incorrect monitor send/recv strings.
bugs.workaround: Use [] (open square bracket-close square bracket) in these cases, for example: [?] [[] Or simply avoid using '\' (backslash) in front of '?' (question mark) or in front of '[' (open square bracket) to indicate a literal string.

bugs.title: Empty external data-groups fail to load
bugs.symptoms: Config will fail to load after upgrade or ucs restore with error regarding an empty or missing data group: 01070630:3: The requested data group file (/config/filestore/.stage_d/130_d/Common_d/data_group_d/:Common:empty_48650_1) was not found or empty).
bugs.conditions: Config references an empty or missing datagroup.
bugs.impact: Config fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Remove references to empty or missing datagroups.
bugs.fix: You can now use an empty file as an external data-group, and it will simply behave as though it has 0 elements.

bugs.title: Packets dropped by HW grey list may not be counted toward AVR.
bugs.symptoms: If the system supports hardware grey list, packets dropped by HW grey list may not be counted toward AVR.
bugs.conditions: AFM license, HW grey list support.
bugs.impact: User visibility.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed.

bugs.title: Bot Name for ASM Search Engines is case sensitive
bugs.symptoms: CS challenge is returned for request with known search engine which is sent with different case than configured.
bugs.conditions: ASM profile is configured on the VS; DoS profile is not configured on the VS.
bugs.impact: Known search engines will get CS challenge.
bugs.workaround: Have DoS profile on the VS, in which the only feature turned on is Bot Signature, in report only, where only search engine category is turned on.
bugs.fix: making the ASM Search Engines case insensitive

bugs.title: Reseting classification signatures to default may result in non-working configuration
bugs.symptoms: Configuration will not load when running "tmsh load ltm classification signature default" or clicking Reset to Defaults button on Traffic Intelligence :: Applications : Signature Update page.
bugs.conditions: 1. You upgrade classification signatures to an IM package, and reference one of the newly added applications / categories in your configuration (e.g., PEM classification filter). 2. You reset classification signatures back to default by running "tmsh load ltm classification signature default" or selecting "Reset To Defaults" on the Traffic Intelligence :: Applications : Signature Update page.
bugs.impact: Configuration will not load.
bugs.workaround: Remove application that came with the new IM from the configuration.
bugs.fix: The release solves the problem of potentially non-working configurations after classification signatures were reset to default.

bugs.title: TAI offset not adjusted immediately during leap second
bugs.symptoms: When repeating a UTC time value during a leap second (when UTC time should be 23:59:60), the International Atomic Time (TAI) timescale should not stop, the kernel increments the TAI offset one second too late.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during an NTP leap second event, for example an event occurs on December 31, 2016, at 23:59:60 UTC
bugs.impact: Impact to applications unknown, system will stay stable and a timer may be fired off later than expected.
bugs.fix: International Atomic Time (TAI) offset during leap second has been corrected.

bugs.title: Cryptic error relating to the liveinstall.movelicense DB variable
bugs.symptoms: Unable to install, with an error containing, "Could not access license source".
bugs.conditions: liveinstall.movelicense needs to be disabled (with the config saved). lind may need to be restarted (or the system rebooted after the change). A new slot (nonexistent volume) needs to be chosen for the new installation.
bugs.impact: Installation fails when this DB variable is set.
bugs.workaround: Enable liveinstall.movelicense (or reset-to-default). Save the configuration. bigstart restart lind. Either the aborted installation will resume, or a new one will succeed.
bugs.fix: A more helpful message is now provided: failed (--nomovelicense specified, but target volume (1) does not exist.)

bugs.title: Administrative interface enhancement
bugs.symptoms: In some cases the administrative interface does not respond as designed
bugs.conditions: In some cases the administrative interface does not respond as designed
bugs.impact: In some cases the administrative interface does not respond as designed
bugs.fix: Enhance administrative interface

bugs.title: iRule does not re-enable AVR when in was disabled by LTM Policy
bugs.symptoms: When disabling AVR from an iRule, AVR HTTP statistics are not collected. When disabling AVR from LTM policy, you will still see AVR HTTP statistics.
bugs.conditions: LTM policy disables AVR, and an iRule running immediately after enables AVR.
bugs.impact: AVR HTTP statistic not available.

bugs.title: ASM Centralized Management Infrastructure Sync issues
bugs.symptoms: Devices in a multiple Automatic sync device-groups may extraneously request a full sync after initial device sync creation, or after a full sync event.
bugs.conditions: Devices are in an autosync failover group and an autosync sync-only group with ASM sync enabled.
bugs.impact: A device may extraneously request additional full syncs after receiving a full sync from its peer or after adding an ASM policy.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Extraneous full sync requests are no longer sent.

bugs.title: Unable to delete an access profile which contains a route domain agent
bugs.symptoms: If an Access profile contains a policy with a route domain agent, the policy cannot be copied or deleted from the GUI or command line tools. The GUI and CLI both fail with the following message: Operation error: getHash failed
bugs.conditions: Access profile contains a route domain agent.
bugs.impact: Cannot delete or copy the Access profile.
bugs.workaround: Delete the route domain agent from the VPE and then copy/delete the Access profile.
bugs.fix: You can now copy and delete Access profiles which contain a route domain agent.

bugs.title: Applying BWC over route domain sometimes results in tmm not becoming ready on system start
bugs.symptoms: Rebooting after applying BWC to route domain stops vlan traffic on VCMP guest. You will experience connection failures when bandwidth Controller (bwc) and Web Accelerator are enabled. Running the tmsh show sys ha-status all-properties command will indicate that tmm is in "ready-for-world", but the Fail status will read "Yes" when this is triggered.
bugs.conditions: BWC enabled and associated with a route domain, Web Accelerator is enabled, and the system is rebooted.
bugs.impact: The system does not comes up fully. TMM does not reach a ready state and will not pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: Remove BWC from route domain and then reapply the BWC back.
bugs.fix: BWC enabled and associated with a route domain, Web Accelerator enabled, and the system is rebooted, now results in the system and TMM coming up fully and passing traffic.

bugs.title: Attaching VDI profile to virtual server changes the default behavior of ACCESS::restrict_irule_events
bugs.symptoms: ACCESS::restrict_irule_events is enabled by default. But if you add the VDI profile to the virtual server, it changes this default behavior and disables this flag. Due to this, you will start seeing that iRule events are raised for internal APM requests as well. When this is happening, the system posts the following error signatures in /var/log/ltm: err tmm[20661]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/stream_vdi_debug <HTTP_RESPONSE> - Operation not supported (line 15) invoked from within STREAM::expression "@$matchstring@$replacestring@" ". err tmm[19745]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/stream_vdi <HTTP_REQUEST> - Operation not supported (line 1) invoked from within "STREAM::disable".
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with VDI profile attached. And any iRule implementation written with the assumption that restrict_irule_events are enabled by default.
bugs.impact: iRule implementation may not work as expected. For example: attaching the OFBA iRule (_sys_APM_MS_Office_OFBA_Support) to the virtual server which has VDI profile breaks OFBA functionality.
bugs.workaround: Enable the ACCESS::restrict_irule_events flag manually using syntax similar to the following: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { ACCESS::restrict_irule_events enable } Note: This impacts Citrix Wyse client RSA next-token change scenario.

bugs.title: sod may kill bcm56xxd under heavy load
bugs.symptoms: Under heavy load, bcm56xxd may not get enough CPU cycles to finish some of its operations and activate the watchdog process. In that case, sod will suspect that bcm56xxd has halted and terminate the process.
bugs.conditions: When the system is very busy, tmm has higher execute priority, and bcm56xxd does not have enough CPU cycles.
bugs.impact: The switch will not operate during the restart, and traffic might be interrupted.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the traffic to make the system less busy.
bugs.fix: The system now has bcm56xxd activate the watchdog so that sod does not terminate the bcm56xxd process.

bugs.title: ASM::disable does not disable client side challenges
bugs.symptoms: ASM::disable command was run but a challenge was still sent.
bugs.conditions: irule with ASM::disable. CS or DID challenge is configured.
bugs.impact: An unexpected JS challenge arrives
bugs.fix: Challenges are now not sent when ASM::disable command happens.

bugs.title: Some HTTP statistics not displayed after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Some statistics will disappear after upgrade due to bug in HTTP statistics backup.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading to newer version
bugs.impact: Not all statistics are shown.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where some ASM HTTP statistics would disappear after upgrade.

bugs.title: Analytics data is displayed per collection interval instead of per second.
bugs.symptoms: Analytics data is displayed as total number of events per selected interval (5 minutes by default) instead of average number of events per second in the selected interval.
bugs.conditions: Analytics data on the following pages is affected: Statistics :: Analytics :: IP (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Disk :: Disk Activity (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Disk :: Disk Sizes (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Bits (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Packets (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Connections::Client Side Connections. Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Connections::Server Side Connections. Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: TCP :: SynCookies (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: TCP :: Packets (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: TCP :: Connections (All *except* for 'Avg Active Connections'). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: UDP :: Datagrams (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: UDP :: Connections (All *except* for 'Avg Active Connections').
bugs.impact: Analytics data is accurate, but not displayed as expected, potentially leading to inaccurate interpretations.
bugs.workaround: The user can divide the displayed results by the number of seconds in the selected interval to get the average per second values.
bugs.fix: All Analytics data is displayed as average per second, and is not affected by changes to the selected collection interval.
bugs.behavior: Analytics data is displayed per collection interval instead of per second. Previously, the count of bytes/packets/new connections and so on, was displayed as total number of events that took place during a collection interval (5 minutes by default). This resulted in potential converting the 5 minute interval to "per second," which required dividing every displayed value by 300. Beginning with this release, metrics are displayed as average per second, and not total activity. Using a "per second" is much more intuitive rather than "per 5 minutes". Analytics data on the following pages is affected: Statistics :: Analytics :: IP (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Disk :: Disk Activity (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Disk :: Disk Sizes (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Bits (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Packets (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Connections::Client Side Connections. Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: Traffic Details :: Connections::Server Side Connections. Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: TCP :: SynCookies (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: TCP :: Packets (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: TCP :: Connections (All *except* for 'Avg Active Connections'). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: UDP :: Datagrams (All). Statistics :: Analytics :: Virtual Servers :: UDP :: Connections (All *except* for 'Avg Active Connections').

bugs.title: ArcSight cs4 (attack_type) is N/A for certain HTTP Compliance sub-violations
bugs.symptoms: ArcSight cs4 (attack_type) is reported as "N/A" for a violation whose sub-violation does not have a specific attack_type_code.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are HTTP Compliance sub-violations such as "Header name with no header value" that do not correlate to any attack_type. Other attack types are as follows: -- HTTP Protocol Compliance/ High ASCII characters in headers. -- HTTP Protocol Compliance/ Host header contains IP address. -- HTTP Protocol Compliance/ CRLF characters before request start. -- HTTP Protocol Compliance/ Header without header value. -- HTTP Protocol Compliance/ Body in GET/HEAD requests. -- Evasion technique/ directories traversals.
bugs.impact: When one of these violations occurs, the system does not assign the appropriate attack type to the logged request in the log or in the remote logger. The system reports the ArcSight remote logger message as attack_type="N/A". (If no other violation was found.)
bugs.fix: Now, when ArcSight cs4 (attack_type) HTTP Compliance sub-violations do not correlate to any attack_type, the system assigns the parent violation's attack type when reporting the violation.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may send oversized TCP segments on traffic it originates
bugs.symptoms: Traffic from the Linux host on BIG-IP may send TCP segments larger than the advertised TCP MSS of a remote host.
bugs.conditions: Received TCP MSS (plus protocol overhead) smaller than configured MTU of interface. Linux host sending large TCP segments, such as SNMP getbulk replies.
bugs.impact: TMM may send traffic to a TCP host that exceed the host's advertised MTU.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the interface MTU.

bugs.title: Stream is not finalized when OWS response has Transfer-Encoding header with zero-size chunk
bugs.symptoms: When OWS sends a chunked response and the only chunk has a zero size, HTTP2 profile receives neither the response's body nor indication that the response has zero size.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server must have HTTP2 profile, and OWS must serve a response with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a zero size chunk (empty body).
bugs.impact: On a stream with such response, BIG-IP doesn't generate a frame which would have END_STREAM flag. Some browsers may not handle the response properly. For example, a redirect may not be performed when the stream is not finalized. It results in incorrect page rendering on a client.
bugs.workaround: Use following iRule for broken URLs: when HTTP_RESPONSE { if {[HTTP::header exists "Transfer-Encoding"] && [HTTP::status] eq 301} { HTTP::respond 301 -version 1.1 noserver Location [HTTP::header Location] Date [HTTP::header Date] Content-Type [HTTP::header Content-Type] Connection [HTTP::header Connection] } } A condition may be changed to narrow the iRule for specific URLs. HTTP::respond may be modified to include other important headers and serve a proper status code.
bugs.fix: When OWS serves Transfer-Encoding chunked with zero size chuck, BIG-IP properly handles the response and sends END_STREAM flag finalizing the response.

bugs.title: Cannot access LTM policy rules in the web UI when the name contains certain characters
bugs.symptoms: Access LTM policy rules in the web UI when the name contains ampersand (%) or slash (/) displays an empty page.
bugs.conditions: The LTM policy rule name being accessed must contains the characters ampersand (%) or slash (/).
bugs.impact: The policy rule properties page displays an empty page.
bugs.workaround: Update the LTM policy rule using tmsh.
bugs.fix: LTM policy rules can be accessed as expected in the web UI regardless of their names.

bugs.title: Potential information leak of HTTP headers
bugs.symptoms: If a TRACE HTTP method is used, by default the BIG-IP system is transparent and will forward that request to the Origin Web Server (OWS). The OWS will reflect any headers seen in that request back in the response. If sensitive headers are added by the BIG-IP system, then the OWS will most likely cause those headers to be in the response. This may affect persistence cookies decrypted by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured to decrypt certain headers, or to insert 'private' headers passed to the OWS. A TRACE HTTP method is used. The OWS will reflect the headers it sees back to the client, leaking information.
bugs.impact: Any response from the origin web server will be forwarded to the client, including information added to that request by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: The HTTP filter by default will be transparent to TRACE requests. They may be rejected by changing the 'unknown method' option from 'allow' to 'reject'. If TRACE is removed from the list of known HTTP methods, then TRACE requests will be rejected. TRACE requests may also be rejected programmatically by iRules or by L7 Policies. Similar functionality for filtering HTTP methods exists in the PSM and ASM modules.

bugs.title: For Thales net-HSMs, fipskey.nethsm now defaults to module protected keys
bugs.symptoms: fipskey.nethsm uses a Thales utility to actually generate/export keys. This utility looks at files in .../kmdata/local to determine what type of protection to use. If there are any softcard or OCS files, then the key will be token protected. If there aren't any files then the key will be module protected. This can be a problem for BIG-IP since that entire folder is synced down to it, so OCS or softcard files unrelated to the BIG-IP operation will change fipskey.nethsm's behavior.
bugs.conditions: Use fipskey.nethsm to generate/export a nethsm-protected key while there are OCS or softcard files in the BIG-IP system's .../kmdata/localfolder.
bugs.impact: Key protection type changes based on the presence of softcard or OCS files in .../kmdata/local.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly use the -c or --protect option to define the protection type when generating/exporting keys.
bugs.fix: fipskey.nethsm will now default to making a module-protected key regardless of the presence of OCS or softcard files in .../kmdata/local. Scripts that export or generate token or softcard protected keys will now need to explicitly set the protection type via the -c or the --protect option in all situations.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as SAML SP: Objects created by IdP connector automation may not be updated when remote metadata changes
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is used as SAML Service provider (SP), IdP connector creation can be automated using list of URIs containing IdP metadata. Symptom for this issue: When remotely published metadata changes - BIG-IP will not be able to modify previously created idp-connector object(s) to reflect the changes. When issue happens, the error similar to following is logged in /var/log/saml_automation.log : "apm aaa saml-idp-connector *NAME* import-metadata only supports create operations."
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used as SP. IdP connector creation is automated. Metadata published on automation URIs changes.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP configuration will not contain the latest changes reflected in published IdP metadata. This may have different impact based on how metadata is changed. Impact can be from none to user authentication failure (e.g. when IdP signing certificate is changed).
bugs.workaround: When error is encountered: - Manually remove affected idp-connector configuration object - Restart samlidpd service : "bigstart restart samlidpd" As a result, SAML connector automation will re-create new idp-connector objects will current up-to-date metadata files.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP is able to modify previously created idp-connector object(s) to reflect the changes when connector automation is deployed.

bugs.title: restjavad is unable to read the dtca.key files resulting in Error: Failed to read key: invalid header
bugs.symptoms: when upgrading to 12.1.1, 12.1.2 or 13.0 releases, executing a command similar to curl -k -u admin:admin https://127.0.0.1:443/mgmt/shared/device-discovery-tasks causes the following error: "errorMessage": "Could not connect to host 10.0.0.160. Please ensure there are no licensing, firewall, port lockdown or network connectivity issues. Error: Failed to read key /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/trust_certificate_key_d/:Common:dtca.key_12100_2: invalid header"
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from releases prior to 12.1.1 to 12.1.1 or 12.1.2 or 13.0
bugs.impact: if your device has an iApps LX application, then that application sill not synchronize to the standby device. So if a failover occurs, then the iApps LX application will seem to disappear, and traffic will not pass through the application.
bugs.workaround: If you have upgraded and are in this condition, and you need to use iAppsLX, you can perform the following procedure to recover. Impact of procedure: this procedure disables HA and requires you to rebuild your HA environment. You only need to use this procedure if you absolutely need to run an iAppLX. 1. Reset device trust, then re-establish device trust, your device group(s), and your traffic group(s) 2. At the BIG-IP command line for each of the devices, run the following command: clear-rest-storage
bugs.fix: Upgrade to 13.1 or 13.0.x hot fix

bugs.title: A standby system can send gratuitous ARPs using both the VLAN and VLAN group MAC addresses
bugs.symptoms: The ltm logs show "address conflict" messages for one or more non-floating self IPs: warning tmm[16580]: 01190004:4: address conflict detected for 172.16.1.17 (00:01:d7:e3:c2:c3) on vlan 1326. The monitor traffic originated from those self IP addresses might be affected and pool member flapping symptoms might appear in the logs as well.
bugs.conditions: - The device has at least one non-floating self IP sitting in a VLAN group. - The device is a member of a Device Group. - The device's role is standby.
bugs.impact: Monitoring traffic from the standby unit might be affected, and pool member's status might not be tracked properly.

bugs.title: LDAP Query agent creates only two session variables when required attributes list is empty
bugs.symptoms: When required attributes list is empty, LDAP Query agent produces only two session variables. in previous releases, the default behavior was - to get all user's attributes and populate those as session variables
bugs.conditions: LDAP Query agent configured in an Access Policy. Required attributes list is empty (not any attr is configured)
bugs.impact: LDAP Query agent failed if branch rule expects to get user's attributes. any other agent in the policy that relies on user's LDAP attributes will also fail.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround you can configure required attributes to be retrieved by LDAP Query agent explicitly
bugs.fix: The default behavior is back; when the required attributes list is empty, the LDAP Query Agent will retrieve all user's attributes and populate them as session variables.

bugs.title: Local Traffic Policies rule page is incorrectly showing all partition's objects in 'Forward traffic' actions
bugs.symptoms: When creating an LTM policy rule action 'Forward Traffic' and selecting from a list of pools or virtual servers, objects from partitions other than the current partition and the Common partition show up.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the LTM policy rule creation page within a specific partition, and there are objects of the same type in other partitions.
bugs.impact: Users without access to the associated partition receive an error when selecting an object from that partition and clicking submit.
bugs.workaround: Do not select objects other than the ones in the current or Common partition from a dropdown.
bugs.fix: Local Traffic Policies rule page now shows only objects within the current partition or Common partition. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Configuring pvasyncookies db variable does not persist over reboots or to non-primary blades.
bugs.symptoms: pvasyncookies db variable does not disable/enable HW syn-cookies on secondary blades, and does not persist across MCPD restart/reboot.
bugs.conditions: Non-default setting for the pvasyncookies db variable.
bugs.impact: Setting does not persist across MCPD restart/reboot.

bugs.title: PVA stats does not show correct connection number
bugs.symptoms: do command tmsh show sys pva-traffic global The current connection number showed up may not be correct
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is PVA Traffic
bugs.impact: Wrong stats number for current PVA connections
bugs.fix: Fixed incorrect statistics for PVA Traffic

bugs.title: relax_unicode_in_xml/json internal may still trigger a false positive Malformed XML violation
bugs.symptoms: You observe Malformed XML violations on valid XML, even with the relax_unicode_in_xml flag set. The same can apply to JSON with the relax_unicode_in_json flag.
bugs.conditions: Valid XML containing unicode characters is passed through ASM, and the relax_unicode_in_xml flag is enabled.
bugs.impact: False positive Malformed XML violations may still be reported.
bugs.fix: XML and JSON unicode now operates as expected when using the relax_unicode_in_xml or relax_unicode_in_json internal parameter. To set these parameters, run the following commands: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add relax_unicode_in_xml 1. /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add relax_unicode_in_json 1. bigstart restart asm.

bugs.title: POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING causes false positive
bugs.symptoms: ASM reports false positive violation for the XML request.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using "%E2%80%AC" POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING as a input in the XML request.
bugs.impact: When one of the following 3 byte chars arrives to the XML parser, the payload considered as malformed XML: LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING (202a). RIGHT-TO-LEFT EMBEDDING (202b). POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING(202c).
bugs.fix: This release now supports the following 3 byte chars within the XML parser: LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING (202a). RIGHT-TO-LEFT EMBEDDING (202b). POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING(202c).

bugs.title: Prevent a spurious Broadcom switch driver failure.
bugs.symptoms: When a high volume traffic is sent to a BIG-IP system, the Broadcom network switch driver might fail. The failure occurs because the switch driver is preempted (by tmm) from completing a long chip reprogramming routine and touching a watchdog. Sod, which monitors the watchdog, thinks the switch driver has become nonfunctional and kills it.
bugs.conditions: A very high volume traffic is sent to a BIG-IP system under certain circumstances.
bugs.impact: Potential eventual system outage if the Broadcom switch driver fails.
bugs.fix: A spurious Broadcom switch driver failure is not possible anymore.

bugs.title: EdgeClient cannot establish iClient control connection to BIG-IP if another control connection exists
bugs.symptoms: When a iClient control connection, between Edge Client and BIG-IP, exists for a given session id, a new iClient control connection for the same session id cannot be established until the existing connection is torn down. When the client interface is down or the client changes networks, it takes time for the BIG-IP to detect that the existing control connection is down. During this time, if the client attempts to establish a new control connection (interface up or different network), BIG-IP rejects the new connection request.
bugs.conditions: EdgeClient attempts to open a new iClient control connection with the same session id as that of an existing control connection and without explicitly closing the current connection. This could happen when the client interface is down or clients changes the network it is on.
bugs.impact: Edge Client cannot establish a iClient control connection and hence a tunnel to the BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: When BIG-IP sees a new iClient control connection request for a session id for which another iClient control connection exists, the existing connection is closed and the new connection request is attempted to be accepted.

bugs.title: Sync all autodos history files from active to standby units every 5 mins
bugs.symptoms: In a high availability (HA) environment, MCP usage increases to 100% every 5 minutes on active devices and 65% on standby devices, which can negatively impact GUI performance. This occurs because the autodosd daemon individually syncs each autodos history file every 5 minutes. (The autodosd daemon is a control plane process which supports the BIG-IP AFM DoS Auto Threshold feature.)
bugs.conditions: -- AFM provisioned. -- HA configured.
bugs.impact: Performance of the BIG-IP system can temporarily be impacted.
bugs.fix: The system now uses one sync transaction to sync all autodos history files together from active to standby devices every five mins, so the performance impact is avoided.

bugs.title: tmm may get stuck in a core loop during a failover event
bugs.symptoms: During a failover event, it may be possible that the tmm cores on the newly active box causing another failover event where the next active box then cores again as well in a loop.
bugs.conditions: May occur during a failover event.
bugs.impact: Production traffic is no longer serviced or is severely hindered.
bugs.workaround: Restarting both active and standby units should stop core loop.

bugs.title: DNS::query can cause tmm crash if AXFR/IXFR types specified.
bugs.symptoms: Passing "AXFR" or "IXFR" as the type to the DNS::query iRule command can cause a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: DNS Express must be enabled when one of the XFR types is used in the DNS::query iRule command.
bugs.impact: tmm will crash and restart every time this command is issued. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not explicitly use AXFR or IXFR query types. If the [DNS::question type] command is being used to dynamically pass in the type, add a preceding check similar to the following: if { not [DNS::question type] ends_with "XFR" } { set rrs [DNS::query dnsx [DNS::question name] [DNS::question type]] }
bugs.fix: The iRule now provides an error message in /var/log/ltm indicating that AXFR and IXFR are not valid types to use with the DNS::query command, and no tmm crash occurs as a result.

bugs.title: Conditional compilation can be improperly rewritten in some cases
bugs.symptoms: Logically and syntactically improper JavaScript after rewriting if conditional compilation is present in some places.
bugs.conditions: Conditional compilation is present in some places.
bugs.impact: Web application misbehavior.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule. No general iRule exists.

bugs.title: Frequently logged "Silent flag set - fail" messages
bugs.symptoms: APM logs excessive messages similar to the following: 2016-12-07,21:46:10:864, 1740,884,APPCTRL, 2, \UBindSecurityMgr.h, 119, UBindSecurityMgrImpl::GetWindow, Silent flag set - fail
bugs.conditions: This can occur when connecting to APM via the Edge Client.
bugs.impact: Excessive messages are logged. These messages can be ignored.

bugs.title: APM Policy Sync: Resources under webtop section are not sync'ed automatically
bugs.symptoms: Resources put under webtop section such as webtop link, portal access requires to be included as dynamic resource or else sync will fail.
bugs.conditions: - Create a webtop section source such as portal access. - Create a webtop section and add the above-create portal access to it. - Create an access profile and add the webtop section resource via a resource assign agent in VPE. - Sync the profile.
bugs.impact: Sync will fail and some configured resources will not be available on the other devices.
bugs.workaround: Includes those resources as dynamic resources in Policy Sync advanced settings.
bugs.fix: Now administrators can sync access profiles with resources under webtop sections without including them manually as dynamic resources.

bugs.title: APM Policy Sync: Non-LSO resources such as webtop are listed under dynamic resource list
bugs.symptoms: Non-LSO resources such as webtop, even they are assigned via a normal resource assign agent, are listed under dynamic resource as opposed to static one.
bugs.conditions: - Create a webtop resource. - Create an access profile. - Launch VPE to assign webtop resource via a normal resource assign agent ("Advanced Resource Assign"). - Click on "Sync policy" button to bring up the policy sync dialog, click on "Advanced Settings" drop-down button and select "Static resources".
bugs.impact: No impact when default settings are configured for policy sync. Only in advanced setting is it confusing that a static resource is only listed in the dynamic resource list, with a prompt to include it as dynamic resource. Doing so does not cause any harm, but is unnecessary.
bugs.workaround: If it is a static resource, do not select it as dynamic resource.
bugs.fix: Static non-LSO resources such as webtop will be listed in static resource list in the advanced setting dialog for policy sync.

bugs.title: Window.error handler is called when alert size is too large
bugs.symptoms: When large HTML code is attached to alerts, the page's Window.error handler may be called.
bugs.conditions: "attach HTML to alerts" is enabled. The page's JavaScript assigns an "onError" listener on the window object.
bugs.impact: onError handler will be called.
bugs.workaround: Disable "attach HTML to alerts" on affected pages.
bugs.fix: onError handler is no longer triggered

bugs.title: tmm crashes when CLIENT_CLOSED or SERVER_CLOSED is used with parking command in another event
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: When CLIENT_CLOSED or SERVER_CLOSED is used with parking command in another event which is fired before either event.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Move the script in _CLOSED events to another events.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes when CLIENT_CLOSED or SERVER_CLOSED is used with parking command in another event.

bugs.title: DHCP: OFFER packets from server are intermittently dropped
bugs.symptoms: With a DHCP relay virtual server, OFFER packets from DHCP server are intermittently not forwarded to the client and dropped on BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: It is not known exactly what triggers this condition, but it occurs intermittently when the DHCP relay virtual server is in use.
bugs.impact: Client machines joining the network do not receive DHCP OFFER messages.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the serverside to force it to be recreated by the next DHCP request. For example, if the flow to the DHCP server 10.0.66.222 is broken, issue the following tmsh command: tmsh delete sys connection ss-server-addr 10.0.66.222 cs-server-port 67

bugs.title: SNAT creates duplicate snat-translation object - configuration load fails
bugs.symptoms: Loading a configuration file fails after creating a SNAT with the same translation address as an existing snat-translation object. The system posts the following error: Invalid SNAT Translation, the IP address 4.4.4.4 already exists. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: A SNAT is created with a translation address that is already used by a snat-translation object. This creates a new translation-address object with a duplicate translation address. Loading the configuration file results in a failure.
bugs.impact: Configuration files will be saved without error, but loading the configuration file will fail. Cannot load the configuration once saved, and must manually change the configuration files in order to get it to load.
bugs.workaround: Manually modify the configuration file to remove the duplicate snat-translation object. Make sure that the SNAT references the correct translation-object. Save and load the configuration file.
bugs.fix: The system no longer creates duplicate snat-translation objects that cause configuration load failure. Instead, the system now performs SNAT Validation that queries for existing trans_addr using address before creating a new one.

bugs.title: SSL::sessionid iRule command returns incorrect result
bugs.symptoms: SSL::sessionid iRule command returns incorrect result
bugs.conditions: An iRule is used to retrieve the session ID.
bugs.impact: The session ID might not be reliable.

bugs.title: APM - OAM login with ObSSOCookie results in error page instead of redirecting to login page, when session cookie (ObSSOCookie) is deleted from OAM server.
bugs.symptoms: APM - OAM login with invalid ObSSOCookie results in error page instead of redirecting to login page.
bugs.conditions: This happens occasionally if a session cookie (ObSSOCookie) is deleted from OAM server, or an OAM session is deleted from server.
bugs.impact: OAM login with invalid ObSSOCookie results in error page. However, expected behavior is that user is redirected to login page if login with ObSSOCokkie fails.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround
bugs.fix: Issue is fixed - On authenticate with ObSSOCookie, read getStatus() API call to check the ObSSOCookie status and redirect to IDP if it is not 1 (LOGGEDIN, AWAITINGLOGIN). With this fix user will be redirected to IDP on logging with cookie that is deleted manually from the OAM server.

bugs.title: Enable SIP::persist command to operate during SIP_RESPONSE event
bugs.symptoms: Without this change, it is not possible to change the timeout of a SIP persistence entry during SIP response message processing.
bugs.conditions: It is not possible to change the timeout of a SIP persistence entry during SIP response message processing.
bugs.impact: it is not possible to change the timeout of a SIP persistence entry during SIP response message processing.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: It is possible to change the timeout of a SIP persistence entry during SIP response message processing.

bugs.title: When a BIG-IP using BFD sessions is forced offline, the system continues to send "State Up" BFD packets for ~30 seconds
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP using statically configured BFD sessions (i.e. "bfd session <IP> <IP>" in the ZebOS configuration) is forced offline, it continues to send "State Up" BFD packets for an additional ~30 seconds.
bugs.conditions: System is using statically configured BFD sessions. System is forced offline.
bugs.impact: The BFD peer thinks the BIG-IP is still online and may send packets to it.
bugs.fix: Ensure BFD "State Up" packets are not sent when the BIG-IP is forced offline.

bugs.title: bigd memory leak for FQDN nodes on non-primary bigd instance
bugs.symptoms: On the non-primary blade with FQDN nodes configured, bigd.1 or bigd.2 (etc.) are consuming an unusually high amount of memory, and bigd cores may exist.
bugs.conditions: FQDN nodes configured on a VIPRION system. As configuration changes are made to FQDN nodes, bigd on the non-primary places memory consumption may be unusually high.
bugs.impact: bigd memory leak; possible bigd crash.

bugs.title: Non-default hold time restricts multiple IP case
bugs.symptoms: When the hold time variable is set to non-default value, a subscriber can not have multiple IP addresses.
bugs.conditions: Hold time value set to non-default by using sys db variable. a second IP address is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Cannot vary hold time for multiple-IP operation.
bugs.workaround: Use only the default hold time when using multiple IP addresses per subscriber.

bugs.title: tmm core with remote logging pool in non-zero route domain
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores every minute with a security log profile set to send log messages to pool members in a different route domain.
bugs.conditions: Remote logging pool configured, and the pool members are in a non-zero route domain that is different than that of the forwarding virtual.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the logging pool members are in the zero route domain.

bugs.title: specific external logging configuration can cause TMM service restart
bugs.symptoms: When external logging is configured for ACL rule hits, and the logging server connection is routed through a Forwarding Virtual, the ACL logging causes a TMM crash and service disruption.
bugs.conditions: The problem is seen when all the following conditions match: 1. External Logging server configured for ACL rule match. 2. External logging server is routed through a Forwarding Virtual (the destination IP of the external logging server matches a Forwarding Virtual's destination address/mask and hence gets routed through the Forwarding VIP). 3. The forwarded logging destination connection causes a crash in TMM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: --Avoid configuring remote logging to be forwarded through a Forwarding Virtual. -- Do not have logging enabled on the forwarding Virtual.
bugs.fix: Connections originated from the BIG-IP to the remote logging server are not subjected to ACL checks, which prevents generation of logs for log server connection, which prevents the error conditions.

bugs.title: Double-free may occur if Access initialization fails
bugs.symptoms: Double-free may occur if Access initialization fails.
bugs.conditions: Access initialization failure occurs, possibly due to license issues.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes and cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a double free condition so that the associated tmm crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: SSL TPS limit can be reached if the system clock is adjusted
bugs.symptoms: If you adjust the system clock you will occasionally get error messages of the form "SSL transaction (TPS) rate limit reached". (For the intended feature of this message, see K7747: Error Message: SSL transaction (TPS) rate limit reached https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K7747.)
bugs.conditions: Occurs when you adjust the system clock.
bugs.impact: When the message occurs, the connection and often several subsequent connections are dropped.
bugs.fix: The message no longer occurs when the system clock is changed and only occurs when system legitimately reaches the SSL TPS limit.

bugs.title: bcm56xxd crash following 'silent' port-mirror configuration failure
bugs.symptoms: A port-mirror configuration can fail 'silently', that is, no error from MCPD yet the following is logged in /var/log/ltm: err bcm56xxd: 012c0011:3: Trunk port trouble with bcm_mirror_port_set() Entry exists bs_mirror.c(598). err bcm56xxd: 012c0010:3: Trouble committing mirror settings to hardware: 0:21 bs_mirror.c(671). err bcm56xxd: 012c0010:3: Trouble setting port mirror from 2.1 to 2.6 bsx.c(5173). Once this happens, any subsequent port-mirror configuration will result in a deadlock condition and SOD will restart bcm56xxd. If the port-mirror interfaces are part of a trunk, any trunk configuration will cause this condition. For example, adding a vCMP guest.
bugs.conditions: Prior 'silent' port-mirror configuration error followed by a subsequent port-mirror configuration command.
bugs.impact: bcm56xxd continuously restarts until the bad port-mirror configuration is removed.

bugs.title: Deterministic NAT performance may be degraded
bugs.symptoms: Deterministic NAT performance may be degraded compared to performance in 12.1.x.
bugs.conditions: Deterministic NAT configuration in use in version 13.0.
bugs.impact: CPU utilization will be higher, and the system may pass traffic with less speed.
bugs.workaround: Enable the db variable pva.fwdaccel to see DNAT performance improve with a fastL4 profile.
bugs.fix: Deterministic NAT performance and scalability is improved relative to 13.0.0. Forward flow acceleration is always on for Deterministic NAT.

bugs.title: UDP Flood does not get detected if the vector limits are infinite
bugs.symptoms: If the UDP_flood AFM DoS vector is configured as 'infinite' for both detection-threshold-pps and default-internal-rate-limit then it will not get detected. Even per-virtual server and Sweep/Flood will not detect UDP_Flood. If they are not infinite, they should work as expected, and the default value for detection-threshold-pps is 400000.
bugs.conditions: -- Settings of 'infinite' for UDP_flood device-dos vector. -- Running v12.1.1, 12.1.2, or 12.1.3.
bugs.impact: You might expect UDP_flood vector to be detected at the per-virtual server and Sweep/Flood level, but if it is configured at infinite at the global device level, then it will not be detected at any level at all.
bugs.workaround: To enable the system to detect UDP_Flood at the various levels, set the global device-dos level for UDP_flood to be 4294967294 (1 less than MAX_UINT32). Note: With this workaround, the system still cannot detect UDP_flood vector still at the global device-level because the number is too high.

bugs.title: Non-Administrator TMSH users no longer allowed to run dig
bugs.symptoms: TMSH users without the Administrator role are allowed to run dig, which may allow access to files in the local filesystem.
bugs.conditions: Execute dig via TMSH
bugs.impact: File access restrictions for TMSH users without the Administrator role are not properly enforced when executing the dig command.
bugs.fix: TMSH users who are do not have Administrator roles can no longer run the dig utility through TMSH.
bugs.behavior: dig command is no longer allowed to be run through TMSH by non-admin users.

bugs.title: JET documentation incorrect for RESOLV::lookup
bugs.symptoms: JET documentation for the iRule command RESOLV::lookup contains a description of a bug where PTR records are not being cached. The documentation includes a workaround for this bug. However, the bug no longer exists.
bugs.conditions: tmsh help ltm rule command RESOLV::lookup | grep "Note: The results" -A6
bugs.impact: Jet documentation mentions a resolution to a bug that no longer exists.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic issue that you can safely ignore.
bugs.fix: The JET documentation has been updated.

bugs.title: APM MIB gauges not reset on standby device
bugs.symptoms: The following MIB gauges are not reset after the device transitions from active to standby: F5-BIG-IP-APM-MIB::apmAccessStatCurrentActiveSessions F5-BIG-IP-APM-MIB::apmAccessStatCurrentEndedSessions F5-BIG-IP-APM-MIB::apmPaStatCurrentActiveSessions F5-BIG-IP-APM-MIB::apmPaStatCurrentPendingSessions F5-BIG-IP-APM-MIB::apmPaStatCurrentCompletedSessions
bugs.conditions: After failover happens
bugs.impact: Since these gauges represent current session counts, administrator may not be able to identify the active device by looking at these gauges.
bugs.fix: Now the SNMP counters and statistics for APM sessions are reset to 0 when a device transitions from active to standby. This change impacts both SNMP and command "tmsh show apm profile access".

bugs.title: EAM warning message "failed to get host identifier"
bugs.symptoms: Seeing EAM warning message, "failed to get host identifier."
bugs.conditions: When starting EAM.
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure Access Management Service on OAM11g.

bugs.title: supported_signature_algorithms extension in CertificateRequest sent by a TLS server fails
bugs.symptoms: Clients are unable to establish an SSL session. If the backend server sends a Certificate Request with Signature Hash Algorithms set to SHA256, the serverssl profile responds with Certificate + Certificate Verify containing signature signed by SHA1 when ssl-sign-hash in that profile is set to 'ANY'. Since the backend server does not expect SHA1 the handshake fails.
bugs.conditions: * BIG-IP is communicating with a TLS server (applies to serverssl profile). * TLS server is requesting client authentication (this is less common). * TLS client using the supported_signature_algorithms extension (this is very common) * TLS 1.2 is likely needed. TLS 1.0 doesn't support extensions.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP will sign the TLS handshake with the SHA1 algorithm, which will fail on the server. Note that this issue is orthogonal to the issue of hash algorithm in X.509 certificates, e.g. "SHA1 in X.509 certificates".
bugs.workaround: No mitigation is known.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now properly parses the following extension in CertificateRequest by a TLS server.: SignatureAndHashAlgorithm supported_signature_algorithms<2^16-1>. This allows the existing logic to work, in particular, to learn that the server supports SHA2 family of hash algorithms and use them with the signature in the TLS handshake.

bugs.title: Sync Inconsistencies when using Autosync ASM Group between Chassis devices
bugs.symptoms: When at least two Bladed Devices are in two autosync device groups together, where one device group is the failover device group, and the other device group has ASM sync enabled on it, Devices may go out of sync and may end up with incorrect ASM configuration
bugs.conditions: At least two Bladed Devices are in two autosync device groups together, where one device group is the failover device group, and the other device group has ASM sync enabled on it. An ASM policy is created.
bugs.impact: Devices may go out of sync and may end up with incorrect ASM configuration
bugs.workaround: Enable ASM sync on the failover device group, or use manual sync for the ASM device group.
bugs.fix: Bladed devices (chassis) handle ASM autosync device groups correctly

bugs.title: Avr debug messages are printed to screen when saving/loading sys config
bugs.symptoms: Avr debug messages are printed to screen
bugs.conditions: When running: tmsh save sys ucs someUcs or tmsh load sys ucs someUcs
bugs.impact: You see debug messages, these can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
