bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Profile-level blacklist-words or whitelist-words lists from the previous version are not empty. -- The general malware appears in the antifraud.domainavailabilityurls db variable. -- Upgrade from pre-v13.0.0 software.
bugs.impact: Upgrade will fail.
bugs.fix: FPS now checks to determine whether the 'general' object already exists and modifies it instead of creating it.

bugs.title: Some metric terms are confusing.
bugs.symptoms: Metric names are unclear in the TCP Analytics profile ('Denied Accepts', 'Accepted Connections').
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the GUI, in tmsh, and when using REST.
bugs.impact: The terms are confusing. Denied Accepts is intended to mean that the connection was not accepted, and Accepted Connections was intended to mean that the connection was accepted.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.fix: The metric names are renamed as follows. On GUI: 1. 'Denied Accepts' is now 'Not Accepted'. 2. 'Accepted Connections' is now 'Accepted'. On tmsh: 1. 'accepts' is now 'accepted'. 2. 'accept_fails' is now 'not-accepted'. The changes appear in the following locations: 1. GUI: a. Statistics :: Analytics : Virtual Servers : TCP : Connections. b. Statistics :: Analytics : Virtual Servers : UDP : Connections. 2. tmsh: a. show analytics tcp report view-by <entity> measures { ... }. b. show analytics udp report view-by <entity> measures { ... }.

bugs.title: bd cores when persistent storage configuration and under some memory conditions.
bugs.symptoms: bd cores. Log signature in /var/log/bd looks similar to the following: BD_MISC|ERR |Jan 02 14:24:06.422|27867|io_manager_init.c:0395|internal_keep_alive: BD shrinking...,going down - BD will be right back. ptr BD_MISC|CRIT |Jan 02 14:24:06.422|27867|signals.c:0073|Received SIGSEGV - Core Dumping.
bugs.conditions: There is persistent storage configuration. There is high memory usage.
bugs.impact: bd crash. Traffic resets and/or failover
bugs.fix: This release fixes a bd crash due to specific memory conditions and persistent storage.

bugs.title: CPB (BIGIP->BIGIQ log node) Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Centralized Policy Builder (CPB) does not follow current best practices
bugs.conditions: Centralized Policy Building enabled
bugs.impact: Centralized Policy Builder (CPB) does not follow current best practices
bugs.fix: Centralized Policy Builder (CPB) now follows current best practices

bugs.title: ASM start process fail with 'Protobuf message exceeds max defined size' on machines with thousands of ASM configuration entities
bugs.symptoms: ASM start process fails on machines with thousands of ASM configuration entities. The log file contains error messages similar to the following: Protobuf message exceeds max defined size. Table: CONFIG_TYPE_DYNAMIC_TABLES.
bugs.conditions: Issue is very rarely reproducible and requires thousands of ASM policy entities on the machine.
bugs.impact: ASM may report legitimate request traffic as a violation.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Hyper-V VE image fails to boot, stuck on "monpd: - Running monpd bigstart script." displayed on console at startup
bugs.symptoms: The following message seen on the console "monpd: - Running monpd bigstart script." when starting BIG-IP. When booting in Hyper-V, this causes the VE to fail to fully boot.
bugs.conditions: AVR, SWG, APM, AFM, PEM or ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP VE fails to fully boot in Hyper-V
bugs.fix: Message removed.

bugs.title: Detail missing from power supply 'Bad' status log messages
bugs.symptoms: When an internal hardware sensor alert is received indicating a 'Bad' power supply status, no detail is included which indicates which characteristic of the power supply's state is resulting in a 'Bad' overall status for the power supply. In this scenario, the message logged at default logging level contains information similar to the following: ... crit chmand[...]: 012a0013:2: Blade 0 hardware sensor critical alarm: Power Supply 2 GPIO status(SPAFFIV03G): Bad
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system posts an internal hardware sensor alert.
bugs.impact: Unable to diagnose cause of 'Bad' power supply status at default logging level to determine whether the probable cause is due to a power supply hardware fault or a possible external power source issue.
bugs.workaround: If power supply errors continue to be logged: 1. Set the libhal logging level to 'Debug': tmsh mod sys db log.libhal.level { value "Debug" } 2. Let the system run in this configuration for at least a few minutes to collect a number of chmand error logs, such as: ... debug chmand[...]: 012a0007:7: Power Supply 1 alert objid:0x16f local:1 status:0x3 pin:0x2 action:0xd ... debug chmand[...]: 012a0007:7: Received Sensor Alert: sensor id 0x16f slot 0xff ... debug chmand[...]: 012a0007:7: Power Supply 1 alert objid:0x16f local:1 status:0x1 pin:0x2 action:0x3. 3. Set the libhal logging level back to 'Notice': tmsh mod sys db log.libhal.level { value "Notice" } 4. Take a qkview or an archive of /var/log/ltm, and engage F5 Professional Services for further analysis.
bugs.fix: When an internal hardware sensor alert is received indicating a 'Bad' power supply status, additional detail is now logged to help identify the cause of the 'Bad' overall status for the power supply.

bugs.title: HSB lockup in vCMP guest doesn't generate core file
bugs.symptoms: If an HSB lockup occurs in a vCMP guest, the system does not generate a core file.
bugs.conditions: HSB lockup, which occur rarely.
bugs.impact: Limited ability to diagnose failures due to HSB lockups.
bugs.fix: Whenever an HSB lockup occurs in a vCMP guest, the system generates a core file.

bugs.title: DNS Rapid Response filters large datagrams
bugs.symptoms: Assigning a profile with DNS rapid response enabled to a virtual server on a P8 chassis might result in problems with blades and the cluster. Depending on the timing of operations (config is loaded and tmm restarts), blades might never join the cluster properly and you will see errors similar to the following looping in /var/log/tmm: notice CDP: exceeded 1/2 timeout for PG 0 notice CDP: PG 0 timed out notice CDP: New pending state ff -> fe notice CDP: New pending state fe -> ff notice CDP: Selected DAG state from PG 0 for CMP state ff with clock 2445394 notice CDP: exceeded 1/2 timeout for PG 0 notice CDP: PG 0 timed out notice CDP: New pending state ff -> fe notice CDP: New pending state fe -> ff notice CDP: Selected DAG state from PG 0 for CMP state ff with clock 2445416
bugs.conditions: -- Assigning a profile with DNS rapid response enabled to a virtual server. -- P8 chassis. -- Large datagrams being passed.
bugs.impact: DNS Rapid Response filters large datagrams. Blades might never join the cluster.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now passes through any datagrams too big for DNS rapid response.

bugs.title: LTM: Rateshaper: For all rate shaper deployment use pfifo and fred as default.
bugs.symptoms: Using the SFQ Queue Method to create a rate class gives lower bandwidth than expected.
bugs.conditions: Rate shaper class created with SFQ.
bugs.impact: Lower bandwidth than configured.
bugs.workaround: Configure the rate shaper with pfifo instead of SFQ. Or, if the flow fairness is required, configure drop-policy to use fred.

bugs.title: After changing ike-peer change from IKEv2 to IKEv1 racoon does not get updated.
bugs.symptoms: 1. Two peers, one with IKEv2 ike-peer configured and the other with IKEv1 ike-peer configured. 2. Reboot IKEv2 peer. 3. Attempt to initiate tunnel from IKEv2 peer side. Won't work (that's expected). 4. Correct the IKEv2 peer to use IKEv1. 5. Attempt to initiate tunnel from 'new' IKEv1 peer side. Won't work (no policy found is logged). Still cannot initiate tunnel after switching from IKEv2 to IKEv1.
bugs.conditions: Changing IKE version from IKEv2 to IKEv1.
bugs.impact: IPsec does not work. You must reconfigure the two ike-peers from the start, or restart tmipsecd.
bugs.workaround: Configure the IKE peers to use IKEv1 at initial configuration, or restart tmipsecd after changing the configuration from IKEv2 to IKEv1.
bugs.fix: IPsec now supports changing the configuration from IKEv1 to IKEv2 after initial configuration setup.

bugs.title: GUI allows creating New client SSL profile in read-only partition
bugs.symptoms: Client SSL Profile Ciphers Group/String option is not grayed out when in a partition where editing is not allowed. This enables the option to click "Create New Cipher Group[+]" button, which is leads to the create client SSL profile page.
bugs.conditions: New client SSL profile creation page displayed in read-only partition when New Cipher Group(+) button clicked in any Client SSL profile properties page.
bugs.impact: GUI shows edit/create option when user is in read-only mode.
bugs.workaround: GUI just displays the create client SSL profile page, save will fail.
bugs.fix: Ciphers Group/String option should be grayed out in client SSL profile page. If Cipher Group is selected, [+] should be grayed out.

bugs.title: Whitespace is manipulated when using certificate export/import
bugs.symptoms: Whitespace is manipulated when using certificate export/import. This causes the certificates to have different checksums despite being functionally identical.
bugs.conditions: -- Export a certificate. -- Import the same certificate.
bugs.impact: Two certs are functionally identical, but whitespace differences not introduced by the user cause checksums to vary.

bugs.title: DHCP: DHCP PEM sessions are not cleared (until idle timeout) after ip release from client in some cases
bugs.symptoms: In some scenario, DHCP IP release messages received by BIG-IP do not trigger corresponding PEM sesssions to be removed from sessionDB. These sessions will removed after timeout.
bugs.conditions: 1)RUN DHCP DORA process to create PEM sessions via DHCP(relay or forwarding mode) 2)Wait for sometime (1-2 minutes) 3)Send DHCP renewal message to BigIP. 5)Send DHCP release message to BigIP. 6)Check sessionDb to see if the corresponcing PEM session is deleted. The problem only happens if the DHCP renewal/release did arrive at the tmm where sessionDB is located.
bugs.impact: Session deletion will not happen immediately. But client does not typically send DHCP release, so the chance for this to happen in real-world environments is small.
bugs.workaround: 1)Delete PEM session manually or 2)Wait for PEM session to timeout
bugs.fix: Remove PEM session from sessionDB regardless which tmm DHCP IP release is reveived

bugs.title: OAM Access gate init problem
bugs.symptoms: Access gates are not properly initialized after the first gate in the list initializes.
bugs.conditions: Configure more than one access gate.
bugs.impact: Other access gates are initialized with incorrect information, server initialization fails due to wring access gate ID.

bugs.title: "monpd: - Running monpd bigstart script." displayed on console at startup
bugs.symptoms: The following message seen on the console "monpd: - Running monpd bigstart script." when starting BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: AVR, SWG, APM, AFM, PEM or ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary message is seen on the console, it can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: Message removed.

bugs.title: New Threat Categories Identification in IP Intelligence Subscription Service
bugs.symptoms: There are two new threat categories detected by Webroot, but they are not supported in IP Intelligence service.
bugs.conditions: The system uses the Webroot SDK to download IP addresses with threats from Webroot server.
bugs.impact: Cannot block IP addresses from these new categories and cannot distinguish them from existing categories.
bugs.fix: Mobile threats and tor proxies are added to the IP Address Intelligence Categories options while illegal websites were removed.

bugs.title: bd log are full of 'Can't run patterns' messages
bugs.symptoms: The bd log are getting filled up with 'Can't run patterns' messages. A core might occur due to the i/o outage. General traffic disturbance/slowness might occur.
bugs.conditions: Configuration change that relates to attack patterns happens while there is heavy traffic.
bugs.impact: Potential traffic outage/slowness. 'Can't run patterns' messages filling up the bd log file.
bugs.fix: Fixed log throttling issue related to attack patterns configuration change.

bugs.title: It is impossible to open MS Word document in MS SharePoint 2013 using Internet Explorer 11 or MS Edge via Portal Access.
bugs.symptoms: It is impossible to open MS Word document in MS SharePoint 2013 using Internet Explorer 11 or MS Edge via Portal Access: the browser shows error message.
bugs.conditions: - MS SharePoint 2013 accessed via Portal Access session; - Internet Explorer 11 or MS Edge; - MS Word installed locally; - MS Word document in SharePoint library.
bugs.impact: User cannot edit/browse MS Word documents from SharePoint library in local MS Word application.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this bug.
bugs.fix: Now MS Word documents in SharePoint 2013 library can be opened in local MS Word application via Portal Access.

bugs.title: The WCCP client source-ip mask may now be configured.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system sends a source-ip mask of 0x0 which does not permit the Web Cache Communication Protocol (WCCP) server to load balance connections across multiple WCCP clients, i.e., BIG-IP systems.
bugs.conditions: Using WCCP on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system with the longest WCCP connection uptime will handle all traffic.
bugs.fix: The source-ip mask may now be configured via tmsh for WCCP.

bugs.title: IKEv1 phase 2 SAs not deleted
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system will not start phase 1 or phase 2 ISAKMP negotiation after an Active -> Standby -> Active failover within a short period of time.
bugs.conditions: The HA Active BIG-IP system goes Standby and then becomes Active again within the phase 2 lifetime.
bugs.impact: IPsec tunnel(s) is/are not initiated by the BIG-IP system. Network connectivity is broken between the private networks.
bugs.workaround: Option 1: Switch to IKEv2 and 12.x, which skips the problem altogether. This combination will mirror the SAs and so deleting existing SAs upon failover is not required. Option 2: Edit /config/failover/active and add the following two lines at the end: logger -p local0.notice "Employ ID636744 workaround. Purge IPsec phase2 SAs." tmsh delete net ipsec ipsec-sa

bugs.title: Potential TMM crash credits to BWC token distribution logic
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes at 'bwc_stb_static_recharge (stb_static=0x560086f501f0) at ../net/bwc_stb.c:364'.
bugs.conditions: Bandwidth Control (BWC) policies enabled with PEM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed a potential TMM crash credits to BWC token distribution logic.

bugs.title: Manager role has Create, Update, and Release access to Datacenter/links/servers/prober-pool/Topology objects but throws general error when complete.
bugs.symptoms: While logged in as a Manager role, if a user attempts to modify an object this role does not have access to, the GUI will post a validation error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when users in the Manager role make changes to Datacenter links/servers/prober-pool/Topology.
bugs.impact: The system posts generic validation errors when Create, Update, Delete actions are initiated by a user without proper permissions. These permissions are not allowed for the Manager, but the GUI makes it appear as if they are.
bugs.fix: The GUI now properly hides or disables the action buttons if a user does not have proper permissions to perform the action.

bugs.title: IKEv1 DELETE payload can use wrong source IP address for floating IPs
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system uses a floating IP to establish an IKEv1 IPsec tunnel, and then the Security Association (SA) is deleted, under rare conditions the ISAKMP notification will use a non-floating IP as the source address.
bugs.conditions: Define a tunnel with floating IP addresses, then toggle version between IKEv1 and IKEv2.
bugs.impact: The IKEv1 racoon daemon now deletes an SA without requiring the source IP to be the correct peer. It is possible that this will allow a random peer to delete another peer's security associations.

bugs.title: Node name and node address
bugs.symptoms: If you create a node with a name that is an IP address but the IP address is different than the name, it can produce an error when adding the node to a pool.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if the node name is, for example, /Common/10.10.10.10 and the IP address is 10.10.10.10%1
bugs.impact: When you attempt to add the node to a pool, an error will occur: Node name /Common/10.10.10.10 encodes IP address 10.10.10.10 which differs from supplied address field 10.10.10.10%1
bugs.workaround: If you set the node name to an IP address it must be identical to the actual IP address.

bugs.title: A FastL4 virtual server may drop a FIN packet when mirroring is enabled
bugs.symptoms: A FastL4 virtual server may drop a FIN packet when mirroring is enabled.
bugs.conditions: - The virtual server uses the FastL4 profile. - The virtual server performs mirroring. - The tm.fastl4_ack_mirror db key is enabled (default). - The client or the server sends a FIN packet, immediately followed by a RST packet.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system forwards the RST packet but not the FIN packet. As the RST sent by one of the TCP endpoints would have its sequence number increased by 1 to account for the FIN packet, the other TCP endpoint may not accept the RST as the FIN packet was never seen. This issue is exacerbated if the FIN packet also carries application data (for example, if it is actually a FIN,PSH,ACK packet). In this case, the other TCP endpoint never sees the application data contained within the packet, and the sequence number in the RST will be off by more than just 1. Ultimately this can cause application failures and also the two connection flows to stall for some time.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue you can either: 1) Disable mirroring for the virtual server (but this comes with a loss of functionality, which may not be acceptable). or 2) Disable the tm.fastl4_ack_mirror db key (but this would affect all FastL4 virtual servers performing mirroring on the box).
bugs.fix: A FastL4 virtual server no longer drops a FIN packet when mirroring is enabled.

bugs.title: Under some conditions, a change in the order of GTM topology records does not take effect.
bugs.symptoms: A change in the order of topology records does not take effect in GTM until the configuration is reloaded or a topology record is added or deleted.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when Longest Match is disabled and the order of topology records is changed without adding or deleting records.
bugs.impact: In certain configurations, the topology load balancing decision may not be made correctly.
bugs.workaround: Reload the GTM configuration or add/delete a topology record.
bugs.fix: Changes in the order of topology records now take effect immediately.

bugs.title: Access Policy with a secure attribute object can fail at runtime for users, if admins perform AP export/import at the same time
bugs.symptoms: When an access profile with a secure attribute (for example: AAA AD Auth agent, LDAP Auth agent, RADIUS Auth agent, etc.) is exported and then imported, secret attribute may not be imported properly. During run-time authentication error logs like below may be observed: Nov 30 12:12:12 hostname err apmd[8478]: 01490236:3: /Common/access-policy-name:Common:xxxxxxxx: LDAP Module: Failed to bind with 'cn=yyyy,dc=zzz,dc=xxx'. Invalid credentials.
bugs.conditions: APM access policy agent with a secure attribute (for example: AAA AD Auth agent, LDAP Auth agent, RADIUS Auth agent, etc.) exported and then imported.
bugs.impact: The APM agent imported in the access profile may not run properly and may end up in wrong branch.
bugs.workaround: After importing the access profile, manually re-configure agents with secure attributes.
bugs.fix: Now Per-request access policies that include objects with encrypted information such as client or resource server secrets, RADIUS secrets, and the like are imported and exported correctly.

bugs.title: Fix for crash when multiple tunnels use the same traffic selector
bugs.symptoms: Given multiple tunnels with the same traffic selector, a crash could sometimes occur.
bugs.conditions: Same traffic selector used with more than one tunnel.
bugs.impact: Possible tmm restart if problem happens. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use different traffic selectors for different tunnels.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to traffic selectors used with more than one tunnel.

bugs.title: big3d may crash
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, big3d may crash or malfunction while processing GTM data
bugs.conditions: GTM enabled
bugs.impact: iQuery connection may be reset
bugs.fix: big3d processes GTM data as expected

bugs.title: big3d may crash
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, big3d may crash or malfunction while processing GTM data
bugs.conditions: GTM enabled
bugs.impact: iQuery connection may be reset
bugs.fix: big3d processes GTM data as expected

bugs.conditions: GTM enabled
bugs.impact: iQuery connection may be reset
bugs.fix: big3d processes GTM data as expected

bugs.title: BIG-IP unstable when SCTP tx_chunks and rx_chunks configuration values are set incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP crashes repeatedly when attempting to establish an SCTP association.
bugs.conditions: When the values 'tx_chunks' or 'rx_chunks' in an SCTP profile are set to an integer multiple of 65,536, the BIG-IP will crash during traffic processing.
bugs.impact: Traffic processing will be disrupted as the BIG-IP restarts, and the SCTP virtual server may be unusable for the entire time that the profile misconfiguration is in place.
bugs.workaround: Set the tx_chunks and rx_chunks values in the SCTP profile to no more than 65,535 and no less than 1.
bugs.fix: Validation has been added so SCTP tx_chunks and rx_chunks configuration values cannot be set to more than 65,535 or less than 1.

bugs.title: The iRules LX streaming external data-group API may incorrectly not find a match.
bugs.symptoms: The iRules LX streaming data-group API for external data-groups may incorrectly not find a match when the following commands are used: - searchStartsWith (case insensitive search only) - matchEndsWith/searchEndsWith (any search types). - matchContains/searchContains (any search types). The following commands are not affected: - matchEquals/searchEquals. - matchStartsWith.
bugs.conditions: There are no conditions for the failure. Using the specified commands will most likely fail. Note: If the data-group is relatively small in size (e.g., approximately 10 records), it is possible that the issue will not happen.
bugs.impact: The specified commands will incorrectly not find a match when there is one.
bugs.fix: The iRules LX streaming external data-group API now correctly find a match when the following commands are used: - searchStartsWith (case insensitive search only). - matchEndsWith/searchEndsWith (any search types). - matchContains/searchContains (any search types). .

bugs.title: TMM core after deleting POLICY and executing command: show net ipsec ike-sa.
bugs.symptoms: TMM core after deleting POLICY and executing the following command: show net ipsec ike-sa.
bugs.conditions: -- IKEv1 configured and tunnel established. -- Traffic is running. -- IKEv1 peer reconfigured with proxy support as disabled.
bugs.impact: TMM cores after some hours, or immediately after running the command: show net ipsec ike-sa. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not delete a policy while an IPsec connection is active.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores after deleting POLICY and executing the following command: show net ipsec ike-sa.

bugs.title: VIP-on-VIP traffic may stall after routing updates
bugs.symptoms: After a routing update traffic for an existing connection sent to a VIP-on-VIP virtual server may be sent directly to the destination address instead of to the inner virtual server.
bugs.conditions: VIP-on-VIP configuration and static or dynamic routing changes.
bugs.impact: Existing connections to the outer VIP may stall.
bugs.fix: Connections to VIP-on-VIP virtual servers no longer stall after routing updates.

bugs.title: DNS Validating Resolver produces inconsistent results with DNS64 configurations.
bugs.symptoms: A DNS Validating Resolver incorrectly validates DNS responses received from A queries made as a result of a front-end AAAA query received on a profile with DNS64 configured. A SERVFAIL response may be sent to the client unless the Validating Resolver cache has previously successfully validated a front-end A query. In this scenario where the A records already exist in the cache, the expected DNS64 AAAA records are synthesized.
bugs.conditions: This issue may be observed with a DNS Validating Resolver configured on a DNS profile with DNS64 configured when processing AAAA queries.
bugs.impact: Incorrect SERVFAIL responses for AAAA queries that should get valid responses.
bugs.fix: DNS validation now occurs as expected, resulting in valid answers to AAAA queries.

bugs.title: Rest worker becomes unreliable after processing a call that generated an error
bugs.symptoms: Unreliable behavior from ASM REST API. 1) REST API tasks (like apply-policy) sometimes do not execute. 2) Calls that end in error are not correctly rolled back on the system.
bugs.conditions: A REST worker can enter this state if it processes specific calls that ended in error, such as creating a new active Policy. Note: Policies are meant to be created inactive and then activated through the apply-policy task.
bugs.impact: 1) REST API tasks (like apply-policy) sometimes do not execute. 2) Calls that end in error are not correctly rolled back on the system.
bugs.workaround: 1) Do not create 'active' policies. Create them with 'active': false, and then use the apply-policy task to set them active. 2) To recover a device that has reached this state, restart restjavad using the following command: bigstart restart restjavad
bugs.fix: REST workers maintain correct state and behavior after calls with errors.

bugs.title: Pool member discovery/autoscale does not work in eu-central-1 (Germany) region of AWS.
bugs.symptoms: Pool member discovery does not work and produces the following error: as-describe-auto-scaling-groups: Refused: The security token included in the request is invalid.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the eu-central-1 region only. Does not apply for failover. Note: This error might happen even when correct IAM credentials are specified.
bugs.impact: Pool member discovery cannot be run in eu-central-1 region.
bugs.workaround: Create autoscale configuration in regions other than eu-central-1.
bugs.fix: Pool member discovery/autoscale now works in eu-central-1 (Germany) region of AWS.

bugs.title: apmd may crash when HTTP Auth agent is used in an Access Policy
bugs.symptoms: apmd may crash when HTTP Auth agent is used in an Access Policy.
bugs.conditions: This might occur on heavy load, when AAA HTTP Server is configured in 'Form based' or 'Custom body' mode. The probability of occurrence is greater if there are session variables specified in the AAA HTTP Server configuration.
bugs.impact: apmd daemon crash. APM cannot process requests until apmd starts up again.
bugs.workaround: Use basic auth, or do not use HTTP Auth.
bugs.fix: apmd no longer crashes when HTTP Auth agent is used in an Access Policy.

bugs.title: Copying a Child Security Policy as a Parent Security Policy Leaves Elements Uneditable
bugs.symptoms: If a Parent copy is made Security Policy that had inherited elements, those elements may not be editable in the new Parent Policy.
bugs.conditions: A Parent copy is made Security Policy that had inherited elements.
bugs.impact: Elements may not be editable in the new Parent Policy.
bugs.workaround: Export the policy as XML and import it as a Parent Policy.
bugs.fix: Copying a Child Security Policy as a Parent Security Policy now allows editing of settings.

bugs.title: Modifying iRule online could cause TMM to be killed by SIGABRT
bugs.symptoms: If iRule is used by several virtual servers, and you edit the iRule online, it could cause TMM to be eventually killed by SOD (watchdog).
bugs.conditions: This can occur under the following conditions: 1. The iRule is used by large number of virtual servers. 2. You edit the iRule and save changes.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: If iRule is used by several virtual servers, and you edit the iRule online, it no longer causes TMM to be eventually killed by SOD (watchdog).

bugs.title: Wildcard wideips not handling matching queries after tmsh load sys from gtm conf file twice
bugs.symptoms: The wildcard wideip is not functioning as a wildcard wideip, but as a regular wideip.
bugs.conditions: Run tmsh load after the wildcard wideip is created: # tmsh load sys conf gtm-only.
bugs.impact: Wildcard wideips are not returning wildcard requests correctly.
bugs.workaround: reload mcpdb using commands: # touch /service/mcpd/forceload # bigstart restart mcpd
bugs.fix: Wildcard wideips now handle matching queries after tmsh load sys from gtm conf file twice.

bugs.title: Cluster blade status immediately returns to enabled/green after it is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios, disabling a blade will result in the blade immediately returning to online.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently under these conditions: - 2 chassis in an HA pair configured with min-up-members (for example, 2 chassis, 2 blades each, and min-up-members=2) - You disable a primary blade on the active unit, causing the cluster to failover due to insufficient min-up-members.
bugs.impact: Disabling the primary blade fails and it remains the primary blade with a status of online.
bugs.workaround: This is an intermittent issue, and re-trying may work. If it does not, you can configure min-up-members to a lower value or disable it completely while you are disabling the primary blade. The issue is triggered when the act of disabling the primary blade would cause the number of members to drop below min-up-members.

bugs.title: Vector (multi-options) lists values are not inherited if parent profile is changed.
bugs.symptoms: Vector (multi-options) lists values, (like "Application CSS Locations" or "Allow URLs from these external domains") are not inherited if parent profile is changed.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS. Create 2 or more Anti-Fraud profiles.
bugs.impact: Can cause a mismatched configuration.
bugs.workaround: Manually fill the appropriate values or use tmsh or Rest API to edit those values.
bugs.fix: Vectors now inherit values from parent profile.

bugs.title: relax_unicode_in_xml should become the default behavior
bugs.symptoms: You see "Malformed XML data - Malformed document, Input stream corrupt" violations on valid XML.
bugs.conditions: A character appears in the payload that is considered by the XML parser as illegal.
bugs.impact: A violation happens.
bugs.workaround: Use internal parameter relax_unicode_in_xml.

bugs.title: Edge client may terminate session sooner than what is specified in inactivity timeout
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, APM session may be terminated in 15 minutes even if inactivity timeout is much longer
bugs.conditions: - Inactivity timeout on APM is set to more than 15 minutes. - Edge client is unable to re-establish VPN session for 15 minutes.
bugs.impact: APM session will be terminated and user will be required to authenticate again.
bugs.fix: Now Edge Client will not blindly terminate the session in the face of 15 minutes of network connection failure. Instead, it will attempt to re-establish the VPN connection using the existing APM user session if that session's maximum timeout value is not yet reached.

bugs.title: Upgrade failure when Common Criteria Mode is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When the software is in "Common Criteria Mode", an upgrade via the Web UIis not possible, because the upgrade process automatically generates a UCS file, but Common Criteria requires that a password be supplied whenever a UCS is generated. The Web UI does not take this in to account, and never asks for a password for the UCS file.
bugs.conditions: Common criteria mode is enabled (i.e., the db variable security.commoncriteria is set to true).
bugs.impact: Software cannot be updated using the Web UI. The install fails with no indication as to why.
bugs.workaround: Disable Common Criteria Mode before upgrade by setting the db variable security.commoncriteria to false.

bugs.title: VADC: after re-deploying a single-nic VM with multiple nics, a load can fail due to stp member 1.0
bugs.symptoms: The configuration fails to load with the following message: 01070523:3: No Vlan association for STP Interface Member 1.0 Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: In single-nic mode, the interface 1.0 exists and can be saved as a VLAN member. Upon re-deploying the virtual-machine from single nic mode to multi-nic, the 1.0 interface becomes pending and should no longer impact any configuration. However, a condition exists after a VLAN delete, where the associated (automatically created) stp member is not removed from the running config and can cause a load error.
bugs.impact: Load fails and requires manual intervention. Otherwise, the STP member is benign because vADC does not support STP.
bugs.workaround: Remove the STP interface member 1.0 and reload.

bugs.title: Removed "(conn/s)" text from Average Concurrent Connections graph
bugs.symptoms: The unit of connections/sec is incorrect for the Average Concurrent Connections graph.
bugs.conditions: This is seen when looking at the Average Concurrent Connections graph.
bugs.impact: Potentially confusing information. The value is actually a general number of concurrent connections.
bugs.fix: Removed "(conn/s)" text from Average Concurrent Connections graph.

bugs.title: Do not manually create a sys management-ip on a clustered BIG-IP Platform through the admin_ip object.
bugs.symptoms: The cluster member's blade-specific mgmt ip is not modified you run tmsh modify sys management-ip <ipaddr/netmask>.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when trying to change the management IP using tmsh modify sys management-ip <ipaddr/netmask> on a blade.
bugs.impact: Although the command is successful, the cluster does not use this management IP, and the blade-specific management IP is unchanged.
bugs.workaround: Modify the blade-specific address of a cluster-member only through the sys cluster component. The correct command is tmsh modify sys cluster default members { <blade_number> { address <desired ipv4 addr> }}
bugs.fix: A configuration error message is emitted which instructs the user to use the sys cluster component to modify the blade-specific address of a cluster-member.
bugs.behavior: Administrators can no longer manually create a sys management-ip on any clustered BIG-IP Platform through the admin_ip object. Administrators are now guided to use the sys cluster component.

bugs.title: IPsec over isession not working
bugs.symptoms: User cannot send IPsec encrypted application data traffic through a secured iSession connection, just by configuring symmetric optimization to use IPsec for IP encapsulation.
bugs.conditions: Configure IPSec with iSession through the Quick Start screen and/or under the "Local Endpoint" configuration. Do not create any new IKE peers or traffic selectors.
bugs.impact: User is unable to send encrypted traffic using IPsec over the tunnel without additional configuration required for a typical IPSec setup.
bugs.workaround: Configuration needed for a typical IPsec setup should be made explicitly. isession encapsulation should be set to "none", and proper IKE-peer, IPsec policy, and traffic selectors should be configured to capture isession traffic between the isession endpoints. BIG-IP1 GUI: [Local Endpoint] Acceleration->Symmetric Optimization : Local Endpoint->Properties WAN Self IP Address: <BIG-IP1-local-endpoint-ipaddress> IP Encapsulation Type: None [Remote Endpoint] Acceleration > Symmetric Optimization : Remote Endpoints >New Remote Endpoint... IP Address: <BIG-IP2-local-endpoint-ipaddress> [IKE peer] Network->IPsec : IKE Peers->New IKE Peer... Remote Address: <BIG-IP2-local-endpoint-ipaddress> Version: Version1 Presented ID Value: <BIG-IP1-local-endpoint-ipaddress> Verified ID Value: <BIG-IP2-local-endpoint-ipaddress> [IPsec policy] Network->IPsec : IPsec Policies->New IPsec Policy… Name:<isession_policy_name> Mode: Tunnel Tunnel Local Address: <BIG-IP1-local-endpoint-ipaddress> Tunnel Remote Address: <BIG-IP2-local-endpoint-ipaddress> [Traffic selector] Network ->IPsec : Traffic Selectors ->New Traffic Selector... IPsec Policy Name: <isession_policy_name> Source IP Address: <BIG-IP1-local-endpoint-ipaddress> Destination IP Address: <BIG-IP2-local-endpoint-ipaddress> BIG-IP2 GUI: Analogous--just swap the local and remote endpoint addresses where they appear above

bugs.title: Safenet keys now use SHA-256 digest instead of SHA-1 digest.
bugs.symptoms: SafeNet keys originally defaulted to using a SHA-1 digest. Using SHA-1 is no longer recommended.
bugs.conditions: Make a SafeNet key using fipskey.nethsm.
bugs.impact: Keys use a less secure digest.
bugs.fix: SafeNet keys, when made via tmsh, now use sha-256 as the digest algorithm. Prior to this, SafeNet keys would use SHA-1 for the digest.

bugs.title: ASM end users blocked due to 'ASM Cookie Hijacking' violation after upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: ASM end users blocked due to 'ASM Cookie Hijacking' violation after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: - The ASM end user left the browser window open. - The ASM admin upgrades the BIG-IP version to 13.0.0 or later. - The previous software version was earlier than version 13.0.0.
bugs.impact: ASM end user is blocked for the first request. The next request will pass.
bugs.workaround: Alert ASM end users who encounter the 'ASM Cookie Hijacking' block to attempt their request an additional time.

bugs.title: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request
bugs.symptoms: The system logs the following message to /var/log/ltm with level 'warning: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a client requests information that is provided by a publisher via mcpd proxy before the publisher registers with mcpd.
bugs.impact: It may raise concerns that something is actually wrong when in fact it is a timing issue.
bugs.fix: The message is now logged with a notice level instead of a warning level.

bugs.title: LACP and CMP state simultaneously fail on 2150 or 2250 blades
bugs.symptoms: An internal traffic stoppage occurs and causes LACP ACTIVE trunk members to go down, and CMP state changes for the HOST and vCMP guests (if configured) on the impacted blade. The tmctl detailed statistics show sustained TX pause generated by HSB on one or more links and matching RX Pause received in interface_stat (on 4.1, 4.2, 4.3).
bugs.conditions: -- This happens when using 2150 or 2250 blades and an internal FPGA device gets into a bad state under heavy traffic load. -- The root cause of that is still under investigation. -- It happens extremely rarely.
bugs.impact: Traffic no longer functions on the blade where stoppage occurs.
bugs.workaround: Reboot blade.

bugs.title: Config sync after changing named pool members can cause mcpd on secondary blades to restart
bugs.symptoms: After performing a ConfigSync, mcpd restarts and the following error is seen in /var/log/ltm: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid mcpd context, folder not found <foldername>
bugs.conditions: - Chassis cluster with at least two blades - sync-failover device group set to full-sync and auto-sync disabled - Changing a named pool-member in non-default partition without syncing between delete and create
bugs.impact: Secondary blades do not process traffic as they restart
bugs.workaround: To prevent blade restart, follow the workaround in K16592: ConfigSync may fail when deleting and recreating a pool member with a node name set (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K16592). To work around this issue, you can synchronize the configuration just after deleting the pool member and node, before re-creating the pool member. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure may impact client connectivity to the node. You should perform this procedure only during a maintenance window. 1. Log in to the BIG-IP system Configuration utility. 2. Navigate to Local Traffic :: Pools, and select the Pool with the member you want to delete. 3. From the top of the menu, click Members. 4. Select the checkbox next to the pool member you want to delete, and click Remove. 5. Navigate to Local Traffic :: Nodes. 6. Select the checkbox next to the node with the same name, and click Delete. 7. Navigate to Device Management :: Overview. 8. Select the local device by hostname (self). 9. Click the Sync option. 10. If the ConfigSync was successful, you may now re-create the pool member.
bugs.fix: Config sync after changing named pool members no longer causes mcpd on secondary blades to restart.

bugs.title: DoS Visibility page on a system under stress can cause GUI timeouts and disconnections
bugs.symptoms: On a system with a lot of AVR related data for DoS Attacks, it might take a while to load the data needed for display on DoS Visibility pages. GUI queries the backend for all the required data simultaneously, which can cause the web server to attempt to handle too many open connections, and result high CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: Large amounts of data for DoS Attacks
bugs.impact: Instability in GUI usage. Performance degradation. Potential disconnections.
bugs.fix: Optimizations were done both on the back-end/database side and on the GUI side. GUI will now throttle its queries to the server.

bugs.title: Pagination broken or missing while viewing pool statistics for GTM wideip
bugs.symptoms: Error occurs while viewing pool statistics for GTM wideip if the number of pools are more than what can be displayed in a single screen.
bugs.conditions: When the number of pools are more than what can be displayed as specified in the System :: Preferences :: Record Per Screen setting.
bugs.impact: Unable to view the statistics of GTM wideip pools beyond those displayed on the screen.
bugs.workaround: Increase the number of Records Per Screen (System :: Preferences :: Records Per Screen) to a number larger than the number of pools in the GTM wideip.
bugs.fix: Can now view the statistics of GTM wideip pools beyond those displayed on the initial screen.

bugs.title: iHealth auto-upload script may get stuck in unusual circumstances
bugs.symptoms: If iHealth auto-upload is correctly configured, and an upload in progress is aborted due to power loss, or other such calamity, the state for future invocations will result in the iHealth script being non-functional, and displaying the message"ihealth is already executing (2). Exiting."
bugs.conditions: auto-upload to iHealth is correctly configured, and an upload in progress is aborted due to power loss. When the BIG-IP is restarted, iHealth is no longer reachable.
bugs.impact: the iHealth script is not usable, and the System-Support page cannot be used to create a qkview.
bugs.workaround: Execute the command, guishell -c "update diags_ihealth_request set ihealth_status=0"

bugs.title: L4 BDoS incorrectly learns traffic after learning period in learn-only mode
bugs.symptoms: L4 BDoS incorrectly learns traffic after learning period in learn-only mode.
bugs.conditions: -- L4 BDoS. -- Learn-only mode. -- Expired learning period.
bugs.impact: Traffic that has already been learned is learned again.
bugs.fix: The delayed threshold is now propagated (at least once) after the traffic stops and then delayed threshold is reset so that traffic is learned as expected.

bugs.title: Auto-thresholds are not applied for two vectors on per-VS DNS/SIP DoS profile
bugs.symptoms: Auto-thresholds are not applied for two vectors on per-VS DNS/SIP DoS profile.
bugs.conditions: DNS and SIP DoS profiles have enabled all vectors that have auto-thresholds support.
bugs.impact: No auto-threshold detection for SIP OTHER DOS, SIP PRACK method DOS, DNS IXFR query DOS, DNS OTHER DOS.
bugs.fix: Auto-thresholds now work for all expected vectors on per-VS DNS/SIP DoS profile.

bugs.title: "ACCESS::session remove" hangs in ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED
bugs.symptoms: When "ACCESS:session remove" can hang if it is used within the the ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED event. Other commands within the event may not execute.
bugs.conditions: when ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED { ACCESS::session remove } This iRule was also observed to hang, with the client not receiving the 401 response: when ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED { ACCESS::respond 401 content "Error denied..." ACCESS:session remove }
bugs.impact: ACCESS::session remove cannot be used in the ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED event, which may break some use cases. Some Access Exchange iRules are broken from this.
bugs.fix: Processing of "ACCESS::session remove" was reverted to an earlier version that does not exhibit this behavior.

bugs.title: SPM and Subscriber Management profile modifications are incorrectly allowed at the PEM Data plane listener level.
bugs.symptoms: While the PEM listener shows the modified profiles, the underyling listeners do not.
bugs.conditions: PEM Data plane listeners need to be present.
bugs.impact: Inconsistency between administrative and operational configuration.
bugs.workaround: Modify the profiles of the underyling virtuals to those of the PEM data plane listener.
bugs.fix: Modification of SPM and Subscriber Management profiles at the PEM Data plane listener level is now prevented.

bugs.title: Modified ASM Cookie violation is off by default
bugs.symptoms: Modified ASM Cookie violation is not active by default when creating a new policy.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when creating a new policy.
bugs.impact: The Modified ASM Cookie Violation isn't enabled.
bugs.workaround: Manually enable the Modified ASM Cookie Violation.
bugs.fix: Modified ASM Cookie violation will be activated in new Policy.

bugs.title: TMM crash when handling unknown Gx messages.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash resulting in potential loss of service.
bugs.conditions: PCRF sends unsupported Gx messages to PEM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Add support for identifying unknown messages types and handle them gracefully.

bugs.title: Bot can be classified as human
bugs.symptoms: A bot is classified as human in a rare case.
bugs.conditions: Web scraping is turned on. The CSHUI is tried on the user.
bugs.impact: Bot traffic gets classified as human by ASM.
bugs.fix: Fixed the CSHUI algorithm to have better bot detection.

bugs.title: DORA process fails when using "table" iRule command on DHCP virtual server in Relay Mode
bugs.symptoms: DORA process fails when using "table" iRule command on DHCP virtual server in Relay Mode.
bugs.conditions: 1) Config DHCP proxy in Relay mode. 2) Config a rule which uses "table" command and attaches the iRule to DHCP listener. 3) Run DHCP DORA process through DHCP proxy.
bugs.impact: DORA process failed.
bugs.workaround: Do not use "table" command in iRule.

bugs.title: Linux CLI client does not close connection immediately using fid/fname on SUSE Enterprise
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, VPN connection is not closed immediately using command line client on SUSE Enterprise Linux.
bugs.conditions: - CLI client is used on SUSE Linux Enterprise. - fid option is used.
bugs.impact: Connection is not closed immediately. As a result, the next attempt to establish a connection fails for a period of time.
bugs.workaround: Close connection without using fid option.

bugs.title: Multiple Diameter monitors to same server ip/port may race on PID file
bugs.symptoms: Two 'Diameter_monitor' instances probing the same server (IP/port) from different pools may interfere with each other, causing one of the monitor instances to fail. This is caused by a possible race in creating a PID file for this 'Diameter_monitor' configuration.
bugs.conditions: Configuration with multiple Diameter monitors probing the same server IP/port.
bugs.impact: One Diameter monitor may fail, while the other Diameter monitor to the same server IP/port succeeds. On subsequent probe-retry, the failed monitor may now succeed.
bugs.workaround: A possible work-around is to establish different monitor periods for the two pools (such as 28 seconds and 31 seconds), so a simultaneous probe-collision will fail one monitor once, which upon retry will succeed (as three monitor failures are required for a virtual server to be marked down).
bugs.fix: The fix includes the monitor-template name in the generation of the PID file, which ensures multiple Diameter monitor instances probing the same server (IP/port) do not interfere with each other.

bugs.title: Help file for MQTT profile is missing.
bugs.symptoms: Help file for MQTT profile is missing.
bugs.conditions: MQTT profile man page.
bugs.impact: MQTT profile man page contains no info.
bugs.fix: There is now man-page help for MQTT profile.

bugs.title: Handle 302 redirects for VMware Horizon View HTML5 client
bugs.symptoms: Starting from v4.4, Horizon View HTML5 client is using new URI for launching remote sessions, and supports 302 redirect from old URI for backward compatibility.
bugs.conditions: APM webtop with a VMware View resource assigned. HTML5 client installed on backend is of version 4.4 or later.
bugs.impact: This fix allows for VMware HTML5 clients v4.4 or later to work properly through APM.
bugs.workaround: For versions 11.6.x and 12.x: =============================== priority 2 when HTTP_REQUEST { regexp {(/f5vdifwd/vmview/[0-9a-f\-]{36})/} [HTTP::uri] vmview_html5_prefix dummy } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { ([HTTP::status] == "302") && ([HTTP::header exists "Location"]) } { if { [info exists vmview_html5_prefix] } { set location [HTTP::header "Location"] set location_path [URI::path $location] if { $location_path starts_with "/portal/" } { set path_index [string first $location_path $location] set new_location [substr $location $path_index] regsub "/portal/" $new_location $vmview_html5_prefix new_location HTTP::header replace "Location" $new_location } unset vmview_html5_prefix } } } ====================== For version 13.0: priority 2 when HTTP_REQUEST { regexp {(/f5vdifwd/vmview/[0-9a-f\-]{36})/} [HTTP::uri] dummy vmview_html5_prefix } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { ([HTTP::status] == "302") && ([HTTP::header exists "Location"]) } { if { [info exists vmview_html5_prefix] } { set location [HTTP::header "Location"] set location_path [URI::path $location] if { $location_path starts_with "/portal/" } { set path_index [string first $location_path $location] set new_location "$vmview_html5_prefix[substr $location $path_index]" HTTP::header replace "Location" $new_location } unset vmview_html5_prefix } } }
bugs.fix: Handle 302 redirects for VMware View HTML5 client are now handled properly.

bugs.title: Per-request policy branch expression evaluation fails
bugs.symptoms: Per-request policy branch expression evaluation fails and you see the following in /var/log/ltm: info tmm[20278]: 01870007:6: /Common/<policy>:Common:640446c9: Executed expression (expr { [mcget {perflow.category_lookup.failure}] == 1 || [mcget {perflow.response_analytics.failure}] == 1 }) from policy item (Category Lookup) with return value (Failed)
bugs.conditions: Per-request policy branch expression evaluation fails for any non-Access (non-APM) iRule events that are attached to the virtual server. The evaluation does not trigger for some requests when, in the same connection, the virtual server gets a request for an internal Access whitelisted URL, and then request for backend resource URIs.
bugs.impact: Per-request policy branch expression evaluation fails. If Access gets a request for whitelisted URL, the system disables all iRule events except the following: #define ACCESS_ALLOWED_IRULE_EVENTS ( \ ((UINT64)1 << TCLRULE_ACCESS_SESSION_STARTED) | \ ((UINT64)1 << TCLRULE_ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED) | \ ((UINT64)1 << TCLRULE_ACCESS_POLICY_AGENT_EVENT) | \ ((UINT64)1 << TCLRULE_ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED))
bugs.fix: Per-request policy branch expression evaluation now complete successfully for non-Access (non-APM) iRule events that are attached to the virtual server.

bugs.title: SNMP Get of sysInterfaceMediaActiveSpeed returns wrong value for 100000SR4-FD
bugs.symptoms: Value returned for sysInterfaceMediaActiveSpeed OID has value of 80 for interface with type 100000SR4-FD instead of value of 100000.
bugs.conditions: This always occurs for this type of interface.
bugs.impact: User sees wrong value for this interface in SNMP get. Value is correct in tmsh 'show net interface'.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to obtain the value by running the following command: show net interface. Note: There is no workaround in SNMP.

bugs.title: Dynamic Signatures are not copied to peers in a device group
bugs.symptoms: During a failover event, a newly active BIG-IP will generate its own Dynamic Signatures rather than use a copy of the previous Active unit's signatures.
bugs.conditions: HA configuration with Dynamic Signatures enabled.
bugs.impact: During failover events, there will be a lag of a few seconds while the Dynamic Signatures are generated and collated.
bugs.workaround: 1. Use the following command to verify that the device-group is set to none: list sys folder dos-common 2. If it is, you can associate dos-common to device group dos-global-dg using the following command: tmsh modify sys folder dos-common/ device-group dos-global-dg 3. Save the config using the following command: tmsh save sys config
bugs.fix: The system now explicitly adds folder and device group association, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Challenging AJAX-qualified requests cover only GET and POST HTTP methods
bugs.symptoms: When the Single Page Application flag enabled within DoS Application profile, and there is an AJAX request being sent using an HTTP method that is not a GET or POST (e.g., PATCH, PUT, DELETE), the Proactive Bot Defense does not display CAPTCHA pop-up.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- DoS Application profile assigned to a virtual server. -- Proactive Bot Defense enabled. -- Single Page Application flag enabled within DoS Application profile. -- HTTP method is not GET or POST.
bugs.impact: CAPTCHA or challenge does not work.
bugs.workaround: Disable Proactive Bot Defense, Single Page Application.
bugs.fix: Single Page Application (SpearHead) AJAX hook has been updated to support non-GET/POST HTTP methods.

bugs.title: Attack Signature Detected Keyword is not masked in the logs
bugs.symptoms: Attack Signature Detected Keyword is not masked in the logs
bugs.conditions: When the signature is matching a full request, and there is a sensitive keyword around the signature location, in some cases the signature appears in the logs and is not masked.
bugs.impact: Sensitive data may appear in the logs

bugs.title: Incorrect fan status displayed when fan tray is removed on BIG-IP iSeries appliances
bugs.symptoms: When the fan tray is removed, the fan status in tmctl tables and 'tmsh show sys hardware' are not updated correctly to reflect the current status of the fan tray i.e. not-present.
bugs.conditions: When the fan tray is physically removed.
bugs.impact: It is important to be aware of the fan status since malfunctioning of the fan tray can result in thermal shutdown when temperature thresholds are reached. Having incorrect/incomplete status would result in delayed corrective actions if a problem should arise.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Reference to SOL14556 instead of K14556 in tmsh modify net interface X.X media command
bugs.symptoms: Error message references solution number instead of Knowledgebase number: err mcpd[6492]: 01071ab6:3: The requested media 100TX-FD for interface 1.0 is invalid. Valid settings are: auto, 1000T-FD. Please see SOL14556 for details.
bugs.conditions: Incorrectly configure net interface media, e.g., modify net interface 1.0 media 100TX-FD.
bugs.impact: Posted message references SOL14556. The Ask F5 site now uses K numbers instead of SOL numbers. At some point, the previously used SOL numbers might no longer redirect, and the information originally in that article would be lost.
bugs.workaround: View knowledgebase article K14556: Copper 1 Gbps modules configured with media other than the 'auto' setting may not function, https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14556.
bugs.fix: Updated tmsh output to reference the new knowledgebase numbering.

bugs.title: Monitor with send/receive string containing double-quote may cause upgrade to fail.
bugs.symptoms: When you upgrade from an affected version, the config gets saved before moving to the new version, thus dropping the enclosing quotes and causing a load failure when booting into the new version.
bugs.conditions: Configuration where monitor string contains \" (backslash double-quote) but does not contain one of the following characters: ' (single quote), | (pipe), { (open brace), } (close brace), ; (semicolon), # (hashtag), literal newline, or literal space.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit each string in the bigip.conf to include enclosing quotes in order to get the config to load the first time.
bugs.fix: Configs load successfully after upgrade. Surrounding quotes, if missing, are added to strings in the bigip.conf file after upgrade. For example: \"service_status\":\"on\".+\"maintenance\":\"off\" in the recv, send recv-disable and username fields. Output of list ltm monitor and bigip.conf match. Reloading the same config via tmsh does not cause unintentional changes, wuch as losing a level of escape in monitor strings.

bugs.title: A subset of the BIG-IP default profiles can be incorrectly deleted
bugs.symptoms: On the BIG-IP system, default profiles should not be deletable. However, the system incorrectly allows a subset of them to be deleted. Known affected profiles include all default persistence and http profiles.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when someone attempts to delete a susceptible profile via TMSH, iControl SOAP or iControl REST. The issue does not occur when using the WebUI (where susceptible profiles are not selectable for deletion).
bugs.impact: If a default profile is missing from the configuration, several issues may arise. For instance, the configuration may fail to load or save, and the WebUI may fail to display certain screens.
bugs.fix: The system no longer allows certain default profiles to be deleted.

bugs.title: SSL Forward Proxy not to cache forged certificate if soft_vfyresult indicating an 'untrusted CA' or 'expired cert'
bugs.symptoms: The system caches a forged certificate when Forward Proxy (FWDP) server-side soft_vfyresult shows an untrusted CA or an expired cert. There is no method of overriding that behavior.
bugs.conditions: Using FWDP. Server-side soft_vfyresult shows an untrusted CA or an expired cert.
bugs.impact: No method to override the caching behavior.
bugs.fix: In this release, you can configure SSL forward proxy to not cache the forged certificate on the client side if the server-side SSL enables the sys db variable tmm.ssl.servercert_softval and the backend server certificate soft verify_result showing a 'untrusted CA' or 'expired certificate'.
bugs.behavior: In this release, you can configure SSL forward proxy to not cache the forged certificate on the client side if the server-side SSL enables the sys db variable tmm.ssl.servercert_softval and the backend server certificate soft verify_result showing a 'untrusted CA' or 'expired certificate'.

bugs.title: Webtop is displayed in English when viewed from a German Locale on Firefox Enterprise service release
bugs.symptoms: Webtop is not localized.
bugs.conditions: -- Firefox ESR is used to connect to APM. -- Viewing the APM webtop in a German Locale. Note: This is a Firefox issue that occurs only with the German language. Firefox sends uilang="en" (for English) instead of uilang="de" (for German).
bugs.impact: Webtop is displayed in English.

bugs.title: Reboot required after disk size modification in a running BIG-IP VE instance.
bugs.symptoms: - BIG-IP VE supports disk size modification during the lifetime of a running instance to expand or reduce the disk size that was allocated at the time of deployment. - A reboot is required after any such modification in the disk size for the changes to take effect. In previous versions, the reboot happened automatically but an affected BIG-IP VE will not have the reboot happening automatically. - Due to the lack of reboot, changes in disk size do not take effect on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Modifying disk size in a running BIG-IP VE instance.
bugs.impact: Changes in the disk size do not take effect till BIG-IP system is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: Manually reboot the running BIG-IP VE instance after making changes in disk size.
bugs.fix: Reboot required after disk size modification in a BIG-IP VE instance.

bugs.title: Reset of unsupported User Identifcation Methods for profiles of type OAuth-Resource-Server, SSL-VPN, System Authentication during upgrades
bugs.symptoms: In previous releases, some invalid combinations of Profile Type and User Identification Methods were allowed via either the UI or tmsh.
bugs.conditions: Use of invalid Profile types and User Identification methods is possible and they wont work.
bugs.impact: It is possible to create and use non-allowed profile type-user identification methods. Then, during upgrades, the following Profile types will have their user identification method automatically set to the corresponding values in the following table because other methods are not supported. Profile Type | User Identification Method --------------------------------------------- OAuth-Resource-Server| OAuth Token SSL-VPN | HTTP System Authentication| HTTP
bugs.workaround: You can reconfigure the user identification method to list of allowed ones: Profile Type | User Identification Method --------------------------------------------- All | HTTP LTM-APM | {HTTP | IP Address} OAuth-Resource-Server| OAuth Token SSL-VPN | HTTP SWG-Transparent | IP Address SWG-Explicit | {IP Address | Credentials} System Authentication| HTTP
bugs.fix: During upgrades, the following Profile types will have their user identification method automatically set to the corresponding values in the following tables because other methods are not supported. Warning message will be logged for each upgrade set required. In earlier releases, users were not prevented from selecting such user id methods. Profile Type | User Identification Method --------------------------------------------- OAuth-Resource-Server| OAuth Token SSL-VPN | HTTP System Authentication| HTTP

bugs.title: Changing the BIG-IP host name causes tmrouted to restart the dynamic routing daemons
bugs.symptoms: Changing the BIG-IP host name causes tmrouted to restart the dynamic routing daemons.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing in use, and you change the host name of the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing information is lost and must be relearned.
bugs.workaround: When using dynamic routing, only change the host name during a maintenance window.

bugs.title: Virtual Server creation ignores translate-address setting with wild card destination
bugs.symptoms: translate-address attribute ignored during virtual server creation, when destination is all zeroes and net mask is not specified.
bugs.conditions: Creating virtual server with wild card destination, no net mask, and translate-address set to enabled.
bugs.impact: translate-address can only be set to disabled during creation.
bugs.workaround: Either set translate-address after creation, or specify net mask for virtual server creation.
bugs.fix: Translate-address flag will now be honored when set while creating virtual server.

bugs.title: LSN pool client connection limit is not enforced when NAT64 and FTP is configured on the virtual
bugs.symptoms: LSN pool client connection limit is not enforced.
bugs.conditions: When NAT64 and FTP is configured on the virtual.
bugs.impact: LSN pool client connection limit is not enforced.

bugs.title: Access Policy Section Unexpectedly Shown
bugs.symptoms: When creating a Virtual Server, the Access Policy section is shown unexpectedly when Type is set to 'Internal' or Message Routing.'
bugs.conditions: Occurs when creating new Virtual Server and Type is set to 'Internal' or 'Message Routing.'
bugs.impact: Virtual Server properties will include "Access Policy" setting, which should not be allowed.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: The virtual server will now only show the "Access Policy" section when Type is set to 'Standard.'

bugs.title: BIG-IP devices configured with Manual Sync, deleting parent policy causes sync to fail.
bugs.symptoms: In high availability (HA) environment where BIG-IP devices are configured for Manual Sync, deleting parent policy causes sync to fail.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you delete the parent of a policy that was used as the parent of another policy. For example: 1. Clone Policy A and create Policy B. 2. Clone Policy B and create Policy C. 3. Delete Policy B.
bugs.impact: Manual sync operation fails.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following Workarounds: A. Enable automatic sync for HA configurations. B. Run the following commands: tmsh save sys config partitions all tmsh load sys config partitions all Sync
bugs.fix: In HA environments containing BIG-IP devices configured for Manual Sync, deleting parent policy no longer causes sync to fail.

bugs.title: Parser doesn't accept Contact header with expires value set to 0 that is not the last attribute
bugs.symptoms: Incoming SIP REGISTER messages are rejected by the SIP MRF parser when they contain Contact header expires value set to 0 that is not the last attribute
bugs.conditions: If the Contact header has an expires value of 0 and it's not the last attribute, for example: Contact: <sip:+414000400@10.0.0.42:5060>;expires=0;q=0.1.
bugs.impact: REGISTER is rejected with a '400 Bad request' error message
bugs.fix: Updated SIP parser to handle a Contact header with an expires value set to 0 that is not the last attribute.

bugs.title: Custom Dialer/Windows logon integration doesn't work against Virtual Server with untrusted SSL certificate
bugs.symptoms: Custom Dialer/Windows logon integration doesn't work against Virtual Server with untrusted SSL certificate
bugs.conditions: * Virtual Server has untrusted certificate * Using Custom Dialer or Windows logon integration features on client machine for establishing secure VPN
bugs.impact: Windows logon integration doesn't work. Cannot establish secure VPN connection before logging in to the machine. Custom dialer doesn't work. Cannot establish secure VPN using Dial-up entry.
bugs.workaround: - Install trusted certificate to Virtual Server or whitelist untrusted certificate on the client machine. or - Use Edge Client to establish secure VPN connection.
bugs.fix: The Custom Dialer/Windows Logon Integration feature now shows a certificate warning when the certificate is untrusted by the client. This allows the logon to proceed if the user accepts the certificate.

bugs.title: OAuth Authorization Server - OAuth Profile is not listing associated Access Profiles appropriately.
bugs.symptoms: OAuth Authorization Server - OAuth Profile is not listing associated Access Profiles appropriately. The Access Profiles list shows duplicate OAuth profile names.
bugs.conditions: An OAuth profile is associated with multiple Access Profile.
bugs.impact: Selection of Access Profile (i.e., clicking link) on OAuth Profiles list, doesn't show the expected Access Profile properties page.
bugs.workaround: Switch to Access profiles list page and select the profile directly.
bugs.fix: Now the GUI displays associated Access Profiles with the OAuth profile on OAuth Profiles list page correctly.

bugs.title: LTM 11.6.1 - Weblogic iApp inserts WL-Proxy-Client-IP header with route domain
bugs.symptoms: iApp incorrectly uses the entire IP address string, including route domain [IP::client_addr], when constructing the WL-ProxyClient-IP header via an iRule. Route domain suffix should be stripped.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you add a route domain to incoming client traffic and deploy the f5.bea_weblogic iApp template.
bugs.impact: Weblogic servers fail to parse the packet header.
bugs.workaround: Modify the irule to use [getfield [IP::client_addr] "%" 1]
bugs.fix: Fix builds the correct irule for handling route domains in Weblogic deployments.

bugs.title: ILX HTTP headerNames are not being properly treated as case insensitive
bugs.symptoms: ILX HTTP headerNames are treated as case-sensitive. They should be treated as case-insensitive.
bugs.conditions: Using an ILX plugin with a virtual server that has an HTTP profile.
bugs.impact: The ILX plugin must be written to be aware of case when handling HTTP headerNames.
bugs.fix: headerNames are now handled as case-insensitive.

bugs.title: AVR does not display 'Max read latency' units.
bugs.symptoms: AVR does not display units for 'Max Read Latency'.
bugs.conditions: AVR, ASM, DoS, or AFM are provisioned.
bugs.impact: No units are displayed.
bugs.workaround: 1. Edit the following file: /etc/avr/monpd/monp_disk_info_measures.cfg. 2. Add the following line at line 63: units=microsecond. 3. Restart monpd.
bugs.fix: Added units (microsecond) to AVR report.

bugs.title: On stress traffic wrong TPS reported to DOS
bugs.symptoms: Stress traffic sent to AVR reports higher TPS than actual to ASM.
bugs.conditions: ASM is been useed
bugs.impact: ASM can declares wrongly on attack.
bugs.fix: The real TPS reported to ASM

bugs.title: Explicit URLs are shown if Wildcard URLs Order is on.
bugs.symptoms: Explicit URLs are shown if Wildcard URLs Order is on.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS. Add several Explicit URLs and Wildcard URLs.
bugs.impact: Although only Wildcard URLs should show, the system also shows Explicit URLs in the FPS GUI.
bugs.workaround: This is a cosmetic issue that does not indicate an issue.
bugs.fix: Explicit URLs no longer appear if Wildcard URLs Order is on. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: TMM crash due to PEM usage reporting after a CMP state change.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash due to a code assertion resulting in potential loss of service.
bugs.conditions: A CMP state change due to a card reboot, disable, enable, insert or remove should have occurred while or right before a PEM usage reporting action.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Instead of asserting, handled the error condition gracefully.

bugs.title: BD crash fix
bugs.symptoms: A crash of the bd daemon.
bugs.conditions: Specific configuration and traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic resets and /or failover.
bugs.fix: BD crash scenario was fixed.

bugs.title: BGP may not send all configured aggregate routes
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, BGP may not send all configured Aggregate routes if one is a supernet of another.
bugs.conditions: - BGP established sessions. - BGP configuration contains several aggregate routes, one or more being a supernet of others.
bugs.impact: The smaller prefix aggregate (least specific), may not be sent to the BGP peer.
bugs.fix: BGP now sends all configured aggregates
bugs.behavior: BGP now sends all configured aggregates, even if one is supernetwork of another.

bugs.title: Improve traffic distribution on backplane links
bugs.symptoms: For chassis based platforms such as 2400 and 4800, there is a primary link and a secondary link from a blade to every other blade in the chassis. Both hidden links form a trunk. Sometimes the traffic is not divided between both links in a uniform way.
bugs.conditions: The exact condition under which this occurs is not well defined, but depends on the traffic.
bugs.impact: One link may be quite busy, while the other link is relatively idle.
bugs.fix: The fix improves the hashing algorithm such that traffic is distributed between both links in a more uniform way.

bugs.title: Configuring lots of Virtual IPs + stress traffic can cause avrd to crash
bugs.symptoms: Avrd crash.
bugs.conditions: lots of Virtual IPs + stress traffic
bugs.impact: Avrd restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: avrd no longer crashes under stress traffic with large numbers of virtual IPs.

bugs.title: Kernel.el7.2: Broadwell Home Agent devices have non-compliant BAR.
bugs.symptoms: Broadwell-EP CPUs have UNCORE devices known as the "Broadwell Home Agent" devices. For both single-socket and dual-socket platforms, this is pci 0000:ff:12.*. These devices have non-compliant BAR's and when the systems with the Broadwell-EP CPUs boot, dmesg output includes as part of early kernel booting messages similar to the following: [ 2.345303] pci 0000:ff:12.0: BAR 2: failed to assign [mem size 0x00000040] [ 2.345306] pci 0000:ff:12.0: BAR 4: failed to assign [mem size 0x00000040] [ 2.345309] pci 0000:ff:12.0: BAR 1: failed to assign [mem size 0x00000010] [ 2.345312] pci 0000:ff:12.0: BAR 3: failed to assign [mem size 0x00000010] [ 2.345315] pci 0000:ff:12.0: BAR 5: failed to assign [mem size 0x00000010] Not related, but also seen is the following: [ 20.123776] mei_me 0000:00:16.0: initialization failed. This is due to the bios configuration not permitting access to the ME (Management Engine). The kernel module for the ME should not be loaded as a result.
bugs.conditions: Affects the following platforms: - BIG-IP i10600/i10800 - BIG-IP i7600/i7800 - BIG-IP i5600/i5800 - BIG-IP i4600/i4800 - BIG-IP i2600/i2800 - HRC-i2800 - HRC-i5800 - HRC-i10800
bugs.impact: None. This is cosmetic and should not be cause for alarm. The Broadwell-EP Home Agent devices are not used by BIG-IP software, and appear only as part of the UNCORE devices associated with each physical socket.
bugs.workaround: None needed: this is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: This release includes RHEL7.3 kernels in the BIG-IP 7.2 kernels. RHEL7.3 kernels adds PCI handling for the Broadwell-EP Home Agent devices, which informs the kernel to not attempt to probe or configure the PCI BARs for such devices. Also, this release disables loading the MEI driver, which prevents the mei_me message posting.

bugs.title: Kernel.el7.2: xhci: off by one error in TRB DMA address boundary check
bugs.symptoms: Due to an off-by-one error in the xHCI driver, it is possible on BIG-IP platforms with xHCI controllers to see the following dmesg output when booting an affected platform: [ 164.552195] xhci_hcd 0000:00:14.0: ERROR Transfer event TRB DMA ptr not part of current TD ep_index 0 comp_code 1 [ 164.552200] xhci_hcd 0000:00:14.0: Looking for event-dma 00000000fffe6000 trb-start 00000000fffe7fe0 trb-end 00000000fffe8000 seg-start 00000000fffe7000 seg-end 00000000fffe7ff0
bugs.conditions: On any of the following BIG-IP platforms that have xHCI controllers and the system is booting normally: - BIG-IP 5000/7000 - BIG-IP i2800/i4800 - HRC-i2800 - BIG-IP VIPRION 4450
bugs.impact: It is not clear what the impact is if nothing is connected to the USB 3.0 ports, which are not accessible except on BIG-IP VIPRION 4450.
bugs.fix: Redhat integrated the fix for the off-by-one error from upstream kernel.org as part of the RHEL7.3 GA release, which is included in the BIG-IP 7.2 kernels in this release.

bugs.title: Core when accessing MQTT::Type after drop
bugs.symptoms: Core when accessing NULL MQTT::Type after drop.
bugs.conditions: iRule configured with NULL MQTT::Type and a MQTT::drop.
bugs.impact: tmm cores. Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now logs a Tcl error when accessing a NULL MQTT::Type after drop, and performs the drop as expected.

bugs.title: Using libtar with files larger than 2 GB will create an unusable tarball
bugs.symptoms: Programs such as qkview create a .tar file (tarball) using libtar. If any of the files collected are greater than 2 GB, the output tar file cannot be read by /bin/tar. This occurs due to a limitation of the file compression library employed by qkview command; the system cannot collect files larger than 2 GB in size in a Qkview. The qkview command may generate output that iHealth cannot parse, and that the tar command cannot extract.
bugs.conditions: -- The file collected via libtar (e.g., by qkview or other program dynamically linking with /usr/lib/libtar-1.2.11) is greater than 2 GB. -- A 2 GB or larger file exists in a directory that qkview normally collects.
bugs.impact: No qkview diagnostics file is created. Although you can extract the qkview tarball using /usr/bin/libtar, the file will be a zero-length file. Cannot submit a qkview to iHealth for analysis. Other applications using libtar will produce invalid tar files.
bugs.workaround: Remove the file larger than 2 GB from the system prior to running qkview or other program that uses libtar.
bugs.fix: With the fix to third party software, libtar, programs using libtar no longer create an unusable tarball when dealing with files larger than 2 GB.

bugs.title: If mcpd fails to load DNSSEC keys then signing does not happen and no error logged
bugs.symptoms: MCPD successfully loads configuration when it's not able to decrypt DNSSEC Key generation.
bugs.conditions: MCPD loads configuration with DNSSEC Key generation encrypted by master key which has been changed.
bugs.impact: The configuration successfully loads but BIG-IP is not able to sign Resource Records.
bugs.workaround: Whenever possible, you should try to avoid a master-key change when you may be affected by this issue. A common trigger for this issue is a BIG-IP Administrator running the "tmsh modify sys crypto master-key prompt-for-password" command prior to taking a UCS archive (see K9420/K82540512). Rather than doing this, simply read the current master-key on the source system, and apply the same key on the receiving system prior to restoring the UCS archive on said system. This can be achieved by running the following commands: # obtain the current master-key f5mku -K # install a new master-key f5mku -r <key_value> Important: If you have not performed this procedure before and require assistance, please contact F5 Support.
bugs.fix: MCPD throw error if not able to decrypt private text of DNSSEC Key generation with current master key.

bugs.title: When AVR collect Page load time and/or session data the Content-Length can be set incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: When the analytics profile with 'Page Load Time' and 'User Sessions' options is attached to a virtual server, sometimes it can incorrectly modify Content-Length for HTML responses. This might happen due to memory corruption.
bugs.conditions: AVR collect session and/or 'page load time' statistic.
bugs.impact: The response 'Content-Length' can be wrong.
bugs.workaround: Uncheck collect 'Page load time' and sessions on analytics profile.
bugs.fix: Potential memory corruption has been fixed. AVR sets the 'Content-Length' to the right value.
