bugs.title: UCS may fail to load due to Master key decryption failure on EEPROM-less systems
bugs.symptoms: The following error: 'Symmetric Unit Key decrypt failure - decrypt failure' is logged to /var/log/ltm when attempting to load a UCS. Configuration fails then to load due to a secure attribute decryption failure.
bugs.conditions: 1. UCS contains secure attributes. 2. UCS contains a '/config/bigip/kstore/.unitkey' file. 3. The current '/config/bigip/kstore/.unitkey' file does not match the '.unitkey' file within UCS. 4. System does not utilize an EEPROM for storing its unitkey. (For more information, see K73034260: Overview of the BIG-IP system Secure Vault feature :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K73034260.)
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following procedure: 1. Stop the system: # bigstart stop 2. Replace the '/config/bigip/kstore/.unitkey' file with the '.unitkey' file from the UCS 3. Replace the '/config/bigip/kstore/master' file with the 'master' file from the UCS 4. Remove the mcp db to forcibly reload the keys: # rm -f /var/db/mcpd.bin # rm -f /var/db/mcpd.info 5. Restart the system and reload the configuration: # bigstart start # tmsh load sys config or # reboot
bugs.fix: The system now always reload the .unitkey from storage when loading other keys, so the UCS loads as expected.

bugs.title: Searching for signatures with overrides in the policy returns incorrect results
bugs.symptoms: 1) Searching for Policy Attack Signatures with Overrides "On URLs" or "On HTTP headers" then all signatures are shown, regardless of whether they have overrides or not. 2) Searching for Policy Attack Signatures with Overrides "On XML profiles"/"On JSON profiles"/"On GWT profiles"/"On Plain Text profiles" then no signatures are shown, regardless of whether they have overrides or not.
bugs.conditions: Signature specific overrides are applied on URLs, Headers, or Content Profiles.
bugs.impact: No easy way to search for which signatures have overrides defined.
bugs.fix: Searching for signatures with overrides now works correctly.

bugs.title: Portal access page broken when accessed from Chrome and Firefox
bugs.symptoms: Portal access page broken when accessed from Chrome and Firefox, but loads in Internet Explorer. BLOB URLs refer to BLOB objects. These objects may contain arbitrary content including JavaScript code, CSS code, etc. In some cases, content of BLOB object should be rewritten before it is used by Web application.
bugs.conditions: Portal access page not load on Chrome & Firefox
bugs.impact: PA page does not load. Users cannot see the content of the page.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround available upon request

bugs.title: Blackhole management routes don't work
bugs.symptoms: When a management route of type blackhole is added, Linux does not end up with any blackhole routes. For the default route, nothing is created. For more specific routes, an interface route out the management interface is created.
bugs.conditions: Creating a blackhole management route.
bugs.impact: Management traffic will not be ignored and sent to the blackhole management route.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now allows blackhole management routes to be created.

bugs.title: Memory leak in STREAM::expression iRule
bugs.symptoms: If you are using the STREAM::expression iRule with APM, the stream filter can leak memory.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using the STREAM::expression iRule with an APM virtual.
bugs.impact: This causes a memory leak in tmm.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a memory leak in STREAM::expression iRule.

bugs.title: username aliases are not supported
bugs.symptoms: in is a common practice to use aliases for username. for example, an app might allow users to login with either their ID, cell number, or nickname. WebSafe doesn't support username aliases.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when your application uses username aliases.
bugs.impact: You are unable to use username aliases in your applications.
bugs.fix: providing new ANTIFRAUD irule command for setting username (replace username alias with the "real" username)

bugs.title: Crash when searching external data-groups with records that do not have values
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may crash when search through an external data-group that has at least one value with empty value.
bugs.conditions: For example, this occurs if data-group is defined as follows: the key for network 10.40.0.0/13 has no value: network 10.0.0.0/9 := "network 10.0.0.0/9", network 10.40.0.0/13, network 10.10.0.0/17 := "network 10.10.0.0/17", A search in the data-group above with -value or -element options where at least one of the result records has no value will most likely result in a TMM crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Make sure that every record in the external data-groups has a value.
bugs.fix: Searching values in an external data-group where result will contain at least one value with an empty value no longer results in a TMM crash. A -value search will yield an empty string for the records that do not have a value.

bugs.title: Policy with Session Awareness Statuses may fail to export
bugs.symptoms: ASM policy with many Session Awareness Statuses may fail to export.
bugs.conditions: There are many Session Awareness Statuses configured for the policy.
bugs.impact: ASM policy export will fail.
bugs.workaround: Remove all Session Awareness Statuses before export.
bugs.fix: ASM policy export only includes Session Awareness Statuses set to "Block All", and completes reliably.

bugs.title: mysqld.err rollover log files are not collected by qkview
bugs.symptoms: Only the file /var/lib/mysql/mysqld.err is collected in qkview without truncation rules normally used for log files. Also, the mysqld.err.1 and mysqld.err.2.gz, etc are not collected at all.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when generating a qkview.
bugs.impact: You cannot see other mysqld.err rollover files in the qkview, and since the one mysqld.err file might be huge (larger than 2 GB) the output of qkview will be unusable.
bugs.workaround: The missing files must be manually copied into the qkview output. If the mysqld.err is greater than 2 GB in size, it must first be truncated to smaller than 2 GB.
bugs.fix: With this fix, the files /usr/lib/mysql/mysqld.err and associated rollover files (up through .7.gz) will be collected by qkview. Also the truncation/transformation rules that are used for log files will also apply (using -s <size> to modify default behavior), meaning that files greater than 5 MB (by default) will be truncated and there is a maximum limit of 75 MB for any given log file (using -s0).

bugs.title: The CPU utilization of MCP can be high on standby box with autodos enabled
bugs.symptoms: In an active-standby HA setup, with autodos enabled, the CPU utilization of MCP on standby box is high in high stress scenario. For example, the CPU utilization of the standby can be at 80% with 100 virtuals configured.
bugs.conditions: 1. AFM Autodos enabled 2. Large number of virtuals configured
bugs.impact: Increase the CPU utilization by MCP on stand by box

bugs.title: Session variable replace with value containing these characters ' " & < > = may case tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash with session variable replace with value containing these characters ' " & < > =
bugs.conditions: Session variable replace with value containing these characters ' " & < > =
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: avoid session variable values containing ' " & < > = if possible. Otherwise, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Session variable overwrite operation with value containing special characters now works correctly

bugs.title: VADC: link status of a XL710 SR-IOV interface does not reflect the state of the physical link
bugs.symptoms: In VADC, link status always reports UP for one or more SR-IOV Intel XL710 virtual function interfaces (1.1, 1.2, etc.).
bugs.conditions: The VADC interfaces (1.1, 1.2, etc.) do not reflect the state of the physical link controlled by the hypervisor.
bugs.impact: This hinders troubleshooting traffic from the guest.

bugs.title: GUI - Client SSL profile certificate extensions names switch to numbers in case of validation error
bugs.symptoms: Client SSL profile certificate extensions names switch to numbers if there is any validation error in save.
bugs.conditions: Try to Create/Modify client ssl profile such that it results in a validation error and click 'Finished/Update'.
bugs.impact: No functional impact: certificate extensions names switch to their number representation, but if you correct the actual validation error and submit the change, the saved object will have the expected set of certificate extensions.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to create/update client SSL profile.
bugs.fix: GUI client SSL profile certificate extensions names are displayed even if there is a validation error.

bugs.title: Unable to add bait using the GUI if baits already added via tmsh
bugs.symptoms: Unable to add baits using the GUI if baits previously added via tmsh contain "bait_" in the name.
bugs.conditions: License and provision FPS. Use tmsh to add baits whose names contain "bait_".
bugs.impact: May affect detection of certain malware.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to add baits.
bugs.fix: GUI now allows adding baits even if existing bait names contain "bait_".

bugs.title: ORBit2 bug fix update - RHBA-2017-0033
bugs.symptoms: When logging in and out, linc socket files might accumulate in the /tmp/orbit-[username]/ directory. Consequently, the /tmp file system quickly becomes full, which in some cases causes processes running on the system to fail.
bugs.conditions: Logging in and out.
bugs.impact: The /tmp file system fills up, which might cause running processes to fail.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a Red Hat software issue.
bugs.fix: Linc socket files no longer accumulate in the /tmp/orbit-[username]/ directory when logging in and out, so any previously associated failures no longer occur.

bugs.title: db4 bug fix update - RHBA-2017-0035
bugs.symptoms: The db4 utility does not free unused mutexes properly when running the db_verify command, and can exit with an error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system internally runs the db_verify command.
bugs.impact: db4 utility might run out of resources for new mutexes.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a Red Hat software issue.
bugs.fix: With this update, the mutexes are properly freed and the db4 utility does not run out of resources for new mutexes.

bugs.title: RedHat: bash bug fix update - RHBA-2017-0038
bugs.symptoms: When bash expands a parameter stored in a string that exceeds the memory allocation limit for string expansion, it crashes with a segmentation fault error.
bugs.conditions: Bash expands a parameter stored in a string that exceeds the memory allocation limit for string expansion.
bugs.impact: Bash crashes with a segmentation fault error, and the command fails.
bugs.fix: With this update (bash-4.1.2-41.el6_8), the string expansion code has been updated, and bash now exits gracefully with an error message instead of crashing when a string is too long to expand.

bugs.title: Selective ICMP-echo behavior is inconsistent, depending on where the virtual address is disabled
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual address is using selective ICMP-echo and the virtual address is disabled, it will sometimes respond to ICMP echo requests, and sometimes not.
bugs.conditions: The difference appears to depend on where the virtual address is disabled. 1) If the virtual address is disabled in the virtual address settings page in the GUI: [Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers : Virtual Address List :: <address>] it stops responding to pings. 2) If the virtual address is disabled on the virtual address list page in the GUI: [Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers : Virtual Address List] it responds to pings. 3) If the virtual address is disabled with TMSH: 'modify ltm virtual-address <address> enabled no' it responds to pings. In addition, on a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE), case #1 also responds to pings.
bugs.impact: The ICMP echo behavior is different depending on where the virtual address is disabled.

bugs.title: Custom headers configuration issue
bugs.symptoms: Headers in the custom headers list are not seen as custom headers.
bugs.conditions: Configuration is updated by adding and removing custom headers.
bugs.impact: The incorrect XFF IP is reported. False positive geolocations and other violations.
bugs.workaround: Once the custom header table is updated, issue the following command: bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: Fixed custom header configuration issue.

bugs.title: iOS Edge Client is not able to establish per-app VPN connections with APM when it has VPE with iRule event agent without assigned webtop resource.
bugs.symptoms: iOS Edge Client is not able to establish per-app VPN connections with APM when it has VPE with iRule event agent without assigned webtop resource.
bugs.conditions: VPE with iRule event agent without assigned webtop resource.
bugs.impact: Cannot use iOS Edge Client to establish per-app VPN connections.
bugs.workaround: Add resource assignment agent with webtop resource.
bugs.fix: Now the iOS Edge Client can successfully connect to a per-session access policy that contains an iRule Event agent and not a Resource Assign agent.

bugs.title: Connflow can be leaked when DHCP proxy in forwarding mode with giaddr set in DHCP renewal packet
bugs.symptoms: Connflow entry memory are leaked when BIG-IP DHCP proxy is configured in forwarding mode and the DHCP relay agent between the DHCP client and the BIG-IP system sets giaddr field to itself after connflows created are aged out in a particular order.
bugs.conditions: 1) BIG-IP DHCP proxy is configured in forwarding mode. 2) DHCP relay agent sits between the DHCP client and the BIG-IP system sets giaddr field in DHCP renewal packet to itself (this has been observed in Cisco devices), so that DHCP renewal packet will be sent to a relay agent by DHCP servers. 3) Connflow created to giaddr(relay agent) ages out before connflows created to DHCP clients.
bugs.impact: Some connflows are not freed. Memory leak occurs. Eventually memory is exhausted.
bugs.fix: Ref count handing for giaddr connflows are now decremented when the client side connflow is removed, preventing the memory leak.

bugs.title: TMM may incorrectly respond to ICMPv6 echo via auto-lasthop when disabled on the vlan
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, TMM may respond to an ICMPv6 echo request using the auto-lasthop mechanism, when this has been disabled on the vlan.
bugs.conditions: - Auto-lasthop disabled on the ingress vlan - ICMPv6 echo request for a self-IP on the ingress vlan. - Route to the client IP address via a different vlan TMM may respond directly using the auto-lasthop feature and not via the route lookup.
bugs.impact: Traffic may not follow the expected path.
bugs.fix: TMM now correctly uses the configured option for auto-lashop and ICMPv6 traffic

bugs.title: DHCP statistics are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: DHCP statistics are incorrect if DHCP server is down while a new virtual server is created. And when the DHCP server comes back up, the current pending transactions are incorrect.
bugs.conditions: -- DHCP relay configured. -- DHCP server is down while the virtual server is created.
bugs.impact: The 'current pending transactions' for the DHCP server is incorrect if the DHCP server is down while a new virtual server is created.

bugs.title: STPD leaks memory on 2000/4000/i2000/i4000 series
bugs.symptoms: STPD process on any 2000/4000/i2000/i4000 series platform that sends BPDUs will grow in physical memory usage indefinitely so long as its role in the tree results in sending BPDU packets. The memory usage will be faster for each interface that is sending BPDUs.
bugs.conditions: Spanning tree is enabled on any 2000/4000/i2000/i4000 series platform and the device has a role in the tree that results in sending BPDUs on one or more interfaces. Memory can be seen to increase when tracking with Linux top commands. ex. top -b -n 1 | grep stpd The 5th and 6th columns 'VIRT' and 'RES' slowly increase over time, indicating the memory leak.
bugs.impact: Memory leak resulting in indefinite consumption of available physical memory over time.
bugs.workaround: While the memory leak itself cannot be mitigated without a hotfix, the problem can be avoided if the tree can be configured in such a way that the defect affected platforms don't generate BPDUs. This can be done by choosing a root such that the defect affected platforms will have its interfaces to be in blocking mode, or if possible, to be in passthrough mode.
bugs.fix: BPDU process source code fixed to release memory allocated for each BPDU packet created and sent.

bugs.title: New iRule options for MR::message route command
bugs.symptoms: When routing a message via the MR::message route command, the connection-mode and max-connections attributes are not settable.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when using the MR::message or MR::peer iRule commands and you wish to set the connection mode or max connections.
bugs.impact: For applications where other connection-modes are required (for example PER_CLIENT), it is not possible to implement via iRule.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: New keywords added to MR::message route command to allow specification of the connection-mode and max-connections attributes of the temporary route added to the message.

bugs.title: When upgrading from 10.x to a version that supports spanning VIPs, the virtual address spanning property may not be set properly
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading from 10.x to version 12.1.0 or later, a network virtual address that had ARP disabled will not have spanning automatically enabled.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from 10.x to 12.1.0 or later. Must have a network virtual address configured with ARP disabled when upgrading.
bugs.impact: If you are not actually using the spanning feature, there is no impact. If you are using the spanning feature, it will no longer work until it is explicitly enabled. This can result in the loss of traffic, as the upstream router will be sending packets to standby systems that will now refuse to process that traffic.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to an intermediate version that implements the explicit ICMP-Echo setting for virtual addresses (e.g. 11.x) and then upgrade to the desired version. Alternatively, you can manually set the spanning property on their virtual addresses as desired (after the upgrade).

bugs.title: New ICAP logging subset and messages
bugs.symptoms: Cannot turn on logging for the ICAP filter on the internal virtual server.
bugs.conditions: -- Internal virtual server. -- ICAP profile.
bugs.impact: You are unable to enable diagnostic logging for ICAP.
bugs.fix: New ICAP log messages are available to help with debugging. ICAP log messages appear in /var/log/ltm. The log level may be adjusted with the DB variable log.icap.level (default is 'notice').
bugs.behavior: A new logging subset 'icap' has been added. Some ICAP log messages have been added. ICAP log messages appear in /var/log/ltm. Log level is controlled by DB variable log.icap.level. Default is 'notice'.

bugs.title: Usage of iRule commands that try to get or set connection state during CLIENT_CLOSED iRule event may core with MRF
bugs.symptoms: A core may occur with message routing framework (MRF) virtuals or transport-config connections if trying to use certain iRule commands during CLIENT_CLOSED event.
bugs.conditions: Use of an iRule command that gets or sets state in a MRF protocol filter or MR proxy during CLIENT_CLOSED iRule event may core. This is because CLIENT_CLOSED event is raised after all state has been freed for the current connection.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use iRule command to get or set state during CLIENT_CLOSED iRule event.

bugs.title: tmsh command hangs when trust peer is deleted.
bugs.symptoms: When using tmsh to delete a peer, the command hangs, requiring your to CTRL-C to exit the command.
bugs.conditions: Using tmsh to remove a peer device from the trust group. For example: modify cm trust-domain Root ca-devices delete { 10.1.1.100 } name bigip.example.com
bugs.impact: The tmsh command will hang.
bugs.workaround: Use the correct syntax and arguments for the command: modify cm trust-domain Root ca-devices delete { device-name } Or you can use the GUI to remove devices from a trust group.

bugs.title: Session Creation failure after HA
bugs.symptoms: Under some HA scenarios, the subscriber session will be lost. If such a deleted session is added (the same subscriber-id), the addition attempt fails.
bugs.conditions: Intra-chassis HA is configured. One of the blades goes down & comes back up very rapidly & some subscriber sessions are lost. An attempt to add the lost subscriber again fails.
bugs.impact: A set of subscribers lost during HA will never be added back.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: iSeries LCD alerts screen returns to splash screen intermittently
bugs.symptoms: If there is a pending alert and the LCD remains on the alerts screen for an extended period of time, when you attempt to view the alerts for a particular severity (critical, error, warning, etc), the system re-directs to the splash screen instead of to the screen with a list of alerts.
bugs.conditions: -- An alert is pending. -- The LCD remains on the alerts screen for a long time (e.g., 1-2 minutes). -- Navigate to one of the alert levels to view the pending alerts. -- The LCD displays the splash screen instead of a list of alerts.
bugs.impact: The system returns to the splash screen instead of a list of alerts.
bugs.workaround: Navigate back to the alerts screen and select an alert severity to get a list of alerts.

bugs.title: BWC policy category attachment may fail during a PEM policy update for a subscriber.
bugs.symptoms: The correct BWC category is not applied resulting in incorrect BWC handling of subscriber traffic.
bugs.conditions: PEM policies against a subscriber should be modified such that the BWC policy stays the same while the BWC category changes.
bugs.impact: Use cases dependent on BWC can be impacted.
bugs.fix: Code changes were added such that BWC policy and category changes through PEM are handled correctly.

bugs.title: EdgeClient does not render Captive Portal login page which uses jQuery library for mobile devices
bugs.symptoms: Connect to a public network which has Captive Portal and the Captive Portal uses jQuery library for mobile devices. EdgeClient does not render login page for such Captive Portal.
bugs.conditions: Use public network with Captive Portal that uses jQuery library for mobile devices.
bugs.impact: EdgeClient can not establish VPN connection.
bugs.workaround: Use a browser to authenticate to Captive Portal. For locked client, there is no suitable workaround.
bugs.fix: Now Edge Client can successfully interact with a greater number of wifi captive portals.

bugs.title: In Gy delayed binding mode, CCR-Us triggered by concurrent flows are blocked.
bugs.symptoms: In Gy delayed binding mode, CCR-Us triggered by concurrent flows are blocked and PEM doesn't do re-try.
bugs.conditions: In Gy delayed binding mode, concurrent flows hits another rating group before the CCA-I for the first rating groups comes back.
bugs.impact: Quota management service will not be active for those concurrent flows.
bugs.fix: PEM now holds CCR-U requests for those concurrent flows and releases them after CCA-I comes back.

bugs.title: Incorrect packet size sent to clone pool member
bugs.symptoms: Cloned packets do not obey the egress interface MTU, and clone pool members may get traffic exceeding the link MTU.
bugs.conditions: Clone pool is configured on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Clone pool members may get traffic exceeding the link MTU.
bugs.workaround: Disable TSO using the following tmsh command: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcpsegmentationoffload value disable.

bugs.title: Added more error checking and reporting to RAM Cache TMSH commands
bugs.symptoms: Confusing results for some 'tmsh ramcache' commands.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in either of the following scenarios: -- There is more than one profile name when issuing a command. -- A profile name is not valid.
bugs.impact: Some commands do not execute as expected, or there is no indication that the command executed, but did nothing.
bugs.workaround: Use tab completion when entering a profile name, and never try to enter more than one profile name in a RAM cache command.
bugs.fix: The use of multiple profile names in a RAM cache command will now give an error message and do nothing. An invalid profile name will return an error, and again, do nothing.

bugs.title: F5 Optics seen as unsupported instead of misconfigured when inserted into wrong port on B4450 Blade
bugs.symptoms: Inserting a 40G optic into a 100G port, or inserting a 100G optic into a 40G shows the optic as "Unsuported Optic". That is not correct, it may be a supported optic, just inserted in the wrong port.
bugs.conditions: B4450 Blades with 100G or 40G optics inserted in a port that does not support that speed optic.
bugs.impact: The user may be confused on why the optic is not working, the error message is misleading when the optic is inserted in the wrong port.
bugs.workaround: If the optic shows up in "tmsh list net interface" as "Unsuported Optic" remove the optic and verify that the optic speed matches the port.
bugs.fix: The "tmsh list net interface" will now show: module-description "F5 Qualified Optic in invalid port" And the LCD warning message will show: Optic OPT-XXXX not valid in Interface <InterfaceNumber>.

bugs.title: iCRD 400 Error even though request succeeds
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is under a heavy load or is processing large TMSH files, the internal API returns a timeout error for processes that exceed 60 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Heavy traffic going through the BIG-IP system, processing large config files with save or merge command.
bugs.impact: If you have external workflow tools, this will signal a false failure.

bugs.title: A BIG-IP HA pair upgraded directly from 10.2.x to 12.1.x may lose the primary and secondary mirror IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading a BIG-IP HA pair directly from version 10.2.x to version 12.1.x, the devices may fail to retain their primary and secondary mirror IP addresses after the upgrade.
bugs.conditions: This will only occur during a direct upgrade from 10.2.x to 12.1.x. This will not occur, for instance, when upgrading to 12.0.x.
bugs.impact: The devices will not be performing any mirroring after the upgrade to version 12.1.x as a result of this issue.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by either: A) Performing an intermediate upgrade to BIG-IP version 12.0.x first. or B) Manually reconfiguring the mirror IP addresses after the devices have been upgraded to 12.1.x (for more information on how to do so, refer to K13478: Overview of connection and persistence mirroring (11.x - 12.x) https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13478).

bugs.title: No PCRE Validation Performed For Regular Expression Parameters
bugs.symptoms: If a Parameter is configured to match a specified regular expression, but the regular expression is misconfigured, there is no error presented to the user, and there is no regexp enforcement for the parameter. The following log can be observed in bd.log "PCRE compilation failed at offset 12: PCRE does not support \L, \l, \N, \U, or \u"
bugs.conditions: A non-PCRE regular expression is configured for a Parameter.
bugs.impact: No Regular Expression enforcement is performed.

bugs.title: Merged constantly restarts
bugs.symptoms: Merged constantly restarts. This may occur on upgrade or after merged restarts after enabling debug logging. The system logs the following error signature in /var/log/user.log: err merged[27984]: isc/libev evGetNext: Bad File Descriptor: 5, errno: 9 Bad file descriptor. notice logger: Started writing core file: /var/core/merged.bld0.0.249.core.gz for PID 27984.
bugs.conditions: log-config filter level is debug and merged restarts. Note: 'level debug' is the default for a log-config filter therefore the following would be debug logging: sys log-config filter myfilter { publisher mypub }
bugs.impact: Merged restarting may impact stats collection. This can also impact qkview generation, the statistics may be corrupt or missing, GUI might return "General database error retrieving information."
bugs.workaround: If you are encountering this, you can run the following tmsh commands to set the log level to the warning level. Impact of procedure: This will disable debug logging of merged. tmsh modify sys log-config filter <HSL-Filter-Name> level warn tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: Upgrade fails with "DBD::mysql::db do failed: Too many partitions (including subpartitions) were defined" errors in ASM log
bugs.symptoms: Upon first start after upgrade, the following error messages appear in asm log: ------------------------- notice boot_marker : ---===[ HD1.2 - BIG-IP 12.1.1 Build 0.0.184 <HD1.2> ]===--- info set_ibdata1_size.pl[18523]: Setting ibdata1 size finished successfully, a new size is: 8466M info tsconfig.pl[21351]: ASM initial configration script launched info tsconfig.pl[21351]: ASM initial configration script finished info asm_start[19802]: ASM config loaded crit perl[19802]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::DbUpgrade::__ANON__): DBD::mysql::db do failed: Too many partitions (including subpartitions) were defined crit perl[19802]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::DbUpgrade::__ANON__): DBD::mysql::db do failed: Cannot remove all partitions, use DROP TABLE instead crit perl[19802]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::ConfigSync::load_traffic_data): Could not import table data PRX.REQUEST_LOG - ASM configuration save aborted info perl[21860]: 01310053:6: ASM starting -------------------------
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Local request logging enabled. -- Upgrade of a maintenance release, hotfix, or engineering hotfix.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade by the means of saving a UCS, performing a clean install and then loading the UCS. In the manual save/load UCS process, the upgrade of the Request Log can be disabled, which will workaround the error and the UCS will load fine. There are two options to disable the upgrade of the Request Log, when upgrading by the means of a UCS: ------------------- 1) Do not load a Request Log, when loading a UCS: # tmsh modify sys db ucs.asm.traffic_data.load value never 2) Do not save a Request Log, when saving a UCS: # tmsh modify sys db ucs.asm.traffic_data.save value disable -------------------
bugs.fix: Roll-forward upgrade including traffic data now works correctly.

bugs.title: bd crash scenario
bugs.symptoms: The bd crashes, switch-over, some traffic outage.
bugs.conditions: A specific cross domain configuration exists. Specific traffic scenario happens.
bugs.impact: The bd crashes, switch-over, some traffic outage.
bugs.fix: Fixed a bd crash scenario.

bugs.title: ASM end user using mobile might be blocked when CSRF is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Users report their access is blocked; when you look at the error log, you see CSRF errors.
bugs.conditions: -- CSRF enabled on ASM. -- ASM client is using a mobile device.
bugs.impact: Client is blocked.
bugs.fix: Enabling access for specific mobile application.

bugs.title: Inject CSS link Tag "Customize" checkbox also check Inject CSS link Position
bugs.symptoms: Check/uncheck status of "Customize" in the "Tag" input field, and also check/uncheck status of "Customize" in the "Position" option.
bugs.conditions: -- Provision and license FPS. -- Add new profile.
bugs.impact: Inject CSS link Position may not inherit values from parent profile.
bugs.fix: "Customize" of Inject CSS link Position is not checked if "Customize" of Inject CSS link Tag is checked.

bugs.title: Disabling partition selector in DNS Resolver's Forward Zones
bugs.symptoms: The partition selector is enabled in DNS Resolver's Forward Zones.
bugs.conditions: Having Forward Zones in DNS Resolvers inside different partitions.
bugs.impact: Changing the partition in the Forward Zones page may error out.
bugs.workaround: Change the partition in the DNS Resolver List or use tmsh.
bugs.fix: The partition selector in DNS Resolver's Forward Zones has been disabled.

bugs.title: Inbound WideIP list page on Link Controller takes a long time to load when displaying 50+ records per screen
bugs.symptoms: Extremely long page load on Link Controller Inbound Wide IP list page.
bugs.conditions: The preference settings "Records per screen" must be a high value. 50 or more will start causing the page to load very slowly.
bugs.impact: Extremely long page load time.
bugs.workaround: Prior to the fix, the workaround is to set the preference settings "Records per screen" to a low value. The default value of 10 is fine.
bugs.fix: The page can now load hundreds of records on a single screen under 3 seconds.

bugs.title: On macOS Sierra (10.12) LED icons on Edge client's main UI buttons (connect, disconnect and auto-connect) are scaled incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: On macOS Sierra (10.12) LED icons on Edge client's main UI, the buttons (Auto-Connect, Connect, Disconnect) are scaled incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: macOS Sierra (10.12.x) and Edge client application.
bugs.impact: This is a display issue only. There is no functional impact to the system.
bugs.fix: On macOS Sierra (10.12) LED icons on Edge client's main UI buttons (connect, disconnect and auto-connect) are now scaled correctly.

bugs.title: BWC: dynamic policy category sees lower bandwidth than expected in Congested policies
bugs.symptoms: When BWC policy is configured with category that is configured at lower rate than max-user-rate, when the system is congested, the system might experience lower bandwidth and is not able to fill the pipe.
bugs.conditions: BWC dynamic policy configured with category. The number of sessions created is greater than max-rate/max-user-rate, utilizing all the policies. For example: max-rate=10mbps, max user rate=5mbps, cat rate=3mbps.
bugs.impact: Lower bandwidth is seen.
bugs.workaround: Configure categories at the same rate as that of max-user-rate.
bugs.fix: BWC: dynamic policy category now sees the same or better bandwidth.

bugs.title: GRE tunnel traffic pinned to one TMM
bugs.symptoms: GRE tunnel traffic can be sent to one TMM if BIG-IP doesn't proxy the GRE tunnel and uses forwarding virtual to handle GRE tunnel traffic.
bugs.conditions: Use forwarding virtual to handle GRE tunnel traffic.
bugs.impact: GRE tunnel traffic can overwhelm the one TMM and cause performance degradation.
bugs.fix: Improved GRE tunnel traffic handling so traffic does not overwhelm one TMM and cause performance degradation.

bugs.title: Use RDP URIs to launch MS RemoteApps from APM Webtop on Mac
bugs.symptoms: RDP client versions do not handle URI encoding properly.
bugs.conditions: APM using RDP files to launch Microsoft RemoteApps from the APM Webtop on Apple Macintosh computers.
bugs.impact: URI encoding improperly handled.
bugs.fix: APM now uses RDP URIs (instead of RDP files) to launch MS RemoteApps from APM Webtop on Mac. Mac MS RDP client 8.0.39 or later is required (as previous RDP client versions cannot handle URI encoding properly).

bugs.title: Policy Builder Persistence is not saved while config events are received
bugs.symptoms: Policy Builder Persistence is not saved while config events are received.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there are many changes made to the policy.
bugs.impact: Statistics are lost after pabnagd restarts.
bugs.fix: Persistence is now saved every 24 hours.

bugs.title: Displaying warning when Packet Filtering is disabled since Rules won't apply
bugs.symptoms: There is no visibility that, when Packet Filtering is disabled , Rules don't apply.
bugs.conditions: Packet Filtering is disabled.
bugs.impact: Rules can be managed but they won't apply.
bugs.fix: A warning is displayed when when Packet Filtering is disabled since Rules won't apply.

bugs.title: Edge Client now can launch administrator-defined script on session termination
bugs.symptoms: Cannot configure Edge Client to launch administrator-defined script on session termination.
bugs.conditions: -- EdgeClient is used (Mac/Windows). -- Administrator-configured script. -- Session termination.
bugs.impact: Edge Client cannot launch administrator-defined script on session termination.
bugs.fix: Edge Client on Apple Macintosh and Microsoft Windows now can launch administrator-defined script on session termination. Each time Edge Client closes an APM session, the configured script is invoked, except on Windows when a user logs in from Windows.

bugs.title: SSH Proxy does not correctly parse public keys containing comments
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP will RST the server side and client side connections upon connection initialization. If you have logging set up, log messages will inform you that the keys were mismatched.
bugs.conditions: Configuring the SSH Proxy feature's Real Server Auth public key field, using a public key that contains a comment, such as a trailing "root@myserver.local".
bugs.impact: SSH proxy fails.
bugs.workaround: Strip any comments from the Real Server Auth public key, such as "root@host.example.com".
bugs.fix: SSH Proxy now correctly parses public keys containing comments.

bugs.title: Role permissions for actions on the iRules LX Workspace editor page
bugs.symptoms: Mutable actions (delete, save, etc.) are available to roles with lower privilege than Manager.
bugs.conditions: Being logged in with a role with lower privileges than Manager allows access to mutable actions.
bugs.impact: The iRules LX filesystem can be modified by a non-privileged user.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly enforce roles on the iRules LX Workspace editor page.
bugs.behavior: The system now enforces roles on the iRules LX Workspace editor page, so that users cannot add, delete, or save edits unless they have a role of Manager or higher.

bugs.title: IPsec-related tmm segfault
bugs.symptoms: The tmm cores and all connections are reset.
bugs.conditions: Race condition during IPsec tunnel tear down.
bugs.impact: The tmm restarts and all connections reset. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The IPsec-related tmm segfault has been corrected.

bugs.title: port-fwd-mode mode configuration object value
bugs.symptoms: The port-fwd-mode object value of an interface object is not reset to the default value on loading a UCS.
bugs.conditions: Saved configuration / UCS must have port-fwd-mode in default (l3) state, and the current configuration must have port-fwd-mode set to "passive" mode.
bugs.impact: port-fwd-mode will continue to stay in the non-default state of "passive".
bugs.workaround: reconfigure the port-fwd-mode to the right value and save the configuration.

bugs.title: Response Page contents are corrupted by XML policy import for non-UTF-8 policies
bugs.symptoms: If non-UTF-8 policy has Response Pages configured with non-ASCII characters, the Response Page contents will be corrupted by an XML export/import.
bugs.conditions: 1) Response pages are configured with Non-ASCII characters in a non-UTF-8 Policy. 2) The Policy is exported via XML export.
bugs.impact: Response Page contents are corrupted
bugs.workaround: 1) Use binary policy export/import for non-UTF-8 policies. or 2) Encode the non-ascii characters using the html entities/code representations of them. (Example: 日本語 -> 日本語)
bugs.fix: Response Page contents are correctly exported.

bugs.title: SOCKS proxy protocol error
bugs.symptoms: In some cases the SOCKS proxy does not properly handle unexpected changes within a single connection
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with SOCKS Proxy profile
bugs.impact: SOCKS proxy does not function as designed
bugs.fix: Improved event handling in the SOCKS proxy

bugs.title: Backslash removal in LTM monitors after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading, BIG-IP fails to load the configuration and reports that a monitor failed to load.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on upgrade, with specific backslash escaping in LTM monitors. Note: This issue is specific to LTM monitors. It does not occur in BIG-IP DNS monitors. For example, to have two backslashes in the value, you specify three backslashes. The first backslash is the 'escape' character. ltm monitor https /Common/my_https { adaptive disabled cipherlist DEFAULT:+SHA:+3DES:+kEDH compatibility enabled defaults-from /Common/https destination *:* interval 5 ip-dscp 0 recv "Test string" recv-disable \\\"Test\\\"me\\\" <-- pertinent string value (can be in recv, send or username attributes too). send Test time-until-up 0 timeout 16 username test\\\"me }
bugs.impact: The monitor fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Manually correct the string to be the way it was before upgrade, then the configuration will load.
bugs.fix: Upgrade no longer results in incorrectly removing backslashes for some LTM monitor attributes.

bugs.title: A transaction that deletes and recreates a virtual may result in an invalid configuration
bugs.symptoms: Deleting and recreating a virtual server within a transaction (via tmsh or iControl REST) and trying to modify the profiles on the virtual server (e.g., changing from fastl4 to tcp) may result in an invalid in-memory configuration. This may also result in traffic failing to pass, because TMM rejects the invalid configuration. Config load error: 01070095:3: Virtual server /Common/vs_icr_test lists incompatible profiles. Configuration-change-time error in /var/log/ltm: err tmm[22370]: 01010007:3: Config error: Incomplete hud chain for listener: <name>
bugs.conditions: Deleting and recreating a virtual server within a transaction (via tmsh or iControl REST) and trying to modify the profiles on the virtual server (e.g., changing from fastl4 to tcp).
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load in the future. Traffic fails to pass, because TMM rejects the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Within tmsh, use the following command: profiles replace-all-with. Within iControl REST, use three separate calls: 1. Delete virtual server. 2. Create virtual server (with an empty profile list). 3. Modify the virtual server's profile list.

bugs.title: Subscriber remains in delete pending state until CCR-t ack has success as result code is received
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP subscriber session will remain in delete pending (stale) state if the Result-code received Acknowledgement from Gx or Gy and is marked as Failure for CCR-T request.
bugs.conditions: The stale session happens, during subscriber termination and if any CCR-T request for Gx or Gy receives an acknowledgement with non-SUCCESS in Result-code AVP
bugs.impact: The subscriber session in BIG-IP will stay in delete pending state (stale)
bugs.workaround: A tmm restart will cleanup all the stale sessions
bugs.fix: Fix will cleanup the session if a CCR-T acknowledgement is received irrespective of the Result-code AVP

bugs.title: TMM core while running iRule LB::status pool poolname member ip port
bugs.symptoms: An iRule response to a DNS request may trigger the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to produce a core file and restart. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- The BIG-IP system may temporarily fail to process traffic as it recovers from the TMM restart, and devices configured as an HA pair may fail over. -- The BIG-IP system generates a TMM core file to the /shared/core directory.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP DNS system is configured with a wide IP that utilizes an iRule. -- The iRule uses the DNS_REQUEST event command LB::status to check a pool member status. -- The iRule pool address and port are separated by white space. Example iRule syntax: gtm rule pool_member_selection { when DNS_REQUEST { LB::status pool pool-one member 10.0.0.10 80 } }
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use format 'ip:port' or vsname instead of 'ip port. Following are two examples: 1. gtm rule rule_crash_test { when DNS_REQUEST { LB::status pool pool-one member 10.2.108.100:80 } } 2. gtm rule rule_crash_test { when DNS_REQUEST { LB::status pool pool-one member pool_vs_name } }
bugs.fix: An iRule response to a DNS request no longer triggers TMM to produce a core file and restart.

bugs.title: DNSSEC key generations fail with lots of invalid SSL traffic
bugs.symptoms: DNSSEC keys can rollover periodically. This will fail, leading to no keys to sign DNSSEC queries (no RRSIG records) when the BIG-IP is handling a lot of SSL traffic with invalid certificates. The system posts the following log signature in /var/log/ltm: err tmm1[12393]: 01010228:3: DNSSEC: Could not initialize cipher context for key /Common/x1-zsk.
bugs.conditions: DNSSEC keys configured with periodic rollover. The certificate path queues an error (situations include but not limited to lots of SSL traffic with invalid certificates).
bugs.impact: DNSSEC key generations fail to be accepted by the TMM so that when the prior generation expires there is no valid certificate to sign DNSSEC queries.
bugs.workaround: Restart the TMM after the new key generation is created.
bugs.fix: DNSSEC key generations now complete successfully, even with a lot of SSL traffic with invalid certificates.

bugs.title: ePVA traffic stats are not accumulated for SNAT pool members
bugs.symptoms: SNAT pool members of a virtual server does not show any PVA related traffic stats after passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: A FastL4 virtual server using a SNAT pool for source address translation.
bugs.impact: Incomplete stats. No impact to traffic passing.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with ePVA statistics collection.

bugs.title: bindRequest timeout value for LDAP Authentication for remote users is set to 10s and cannot be controlled.
bugs.symptoms: If you have a custom bind-timeout value set for ldap system-auth, the custom value is honored for anonymous users but is ignored for explicit users.
bugs.conditions: ldap auth configured for remote authentication, and a custom bind timeout value is specified.
bugs.impact: The default timeout value of 10 seconds will be enforced for ldap auth.

bugs.title: Possible dead-lock on accept of multiple suggestions at once
bugs.symptoms: When accepting multiple suggestions at once it's possible that action fails
bugs.conditions: Accept of multiple suggestions for the same entities
bugs.impact: Action fails
bugs.workaround: One-by-one accept always works
bugs.fix: Multiple accept mechanism improve to prevent possible dead-locks

bugs.title: Session-based brute force resets failed logins counter upon successful login
bugs.symptoms: ASM counts failed login attempts per session (browser cookie) and blocks an end user if the number of failed exceeds a predefined threshold (default 5). If an ASM end user makes a successful login before the number of failed attempts reaches the threshold, the counter of failed attempts resets to zero.
bugs.conditions: ASM policy attached on the virtual server and brute force session-based feature is configured along with the login page.
bugs.impact: An ASM end user allowed to do a number of failed logins higher than threshold. This happens only in when that APM end user sent a successful login before number of failures hits the threshold.
bugs.fix: Session-based brute force now handles this issue.

bugs.title: AVR doesn't report on virtual and client IP in DNS statistics
bugs.symptoms: On the analytics DNS page, the virtual and client IP stats will be shown as "Aggregated".
bugs.conditions: This can be seen in DNS analytics, when view-by virtual or client-ip is selected.
bugs.impact: DNS statistics show incomplete results.
bugs.fix: AVR now provides the complete report results on virtual and client IP in DNS statistics.

bugs.title: Rarely, an HSB transmitter failure occurs
bugs.symptoms: A very rare HSB transmitter failure occurs. This is indicated by the following message in the tmm logs: panic: hsb interface 1 DMA lockup on transmitter failure.
bugs.conditions: Although the exact conditions for this issue are unknown, this might be related to a 5250 platform or to a configuration containing a vCMP guest.
bugs.impact: Reboot of the unit.
bugs.workaround: None. Note: Although there is no workaround, beginning in v13.0.0, there is an internal counter that tracks occurrences of these types of HSB transmitter failures, which enables better understanding of the issue and a more thorough investigation into its cause.
bugs.fix: The reboot of the unit occurs very rarely, and the conditions for this issue are not well understood. In this release, an internal counter has been added to track occurrences of HSB transmitter failures of this type, which will enable better understanding of the issue and a more thorough investigation into its cause.

bugs.title: request-adapt or response-adapt should be disabled by HTTP::disable
bugs.symptoms: When the HTTP profile is disabled by an iRule in events such as the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event, it is not possible to use ADAPT::enable to disable the adaptation. You might assume that because ADAPT depends on HTTP, it would naturally be disabled along with HTTP, but it is not.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with HTTP profile and also Request Adapt and/or Response Adapt profile. An iRule uses HTTP::disable to (for example) pass non-HTTP traffic.
bugs.impact: Despite HTTP being disabled, ADAPT attempts to handle ingress traffic, without parsed HTTP headers, so will fail. It is possible ADAPT will buffer ingress traffic indefinitely because it does not receive an expected message from the HTTP filter.
bugs.workaround: Disable request-adapt and/or response-adapt in the profile. When HTTP traffic is to be handled, have an iRule on the HTTP_REQUEST or HTTP_RESPONSE event call "ADAPT::enable true".
bugs.fix: The HTTP::disable command implicitly disables any corresponding request or response adaptation. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Always connected exclusion list does not support more than 10 entries.
bugs.symptoms: In locked client mode, APM provides a way to configure destinations that can still be reached by client, even in locked client mode. Number of entries is limited to 10.
bugs.conditions: Locked client mode is enabled
bugs.impact: More than 10 exclusions cannot be added

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE support for GCE
bugs.symptoms: There is no support for Google Compute Engine (GCE) in BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.conditions: Trying to use GCE with BIG-IP VE.
bugs.impact: No support for GCE.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) now supports Google Cloud infrastructure using BYOL licenses. F5's Good, Better and Best license bundles are supported up to 5 Gbps. This release supports single NIC configurations only.
bugs.behavior: The BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) now supports Google Cloud infrastructure using BYOL licenses. F5's Good, Better and Best license bundles are supported.

bugs.title: Syncookies activated on a genuine connection gets reset almost 30-50% of the time
bugs.symptoms: Syncookies activated on a genuine connection to a TCP-based virtual server gets reset almost 30%-50% of the time.
bugs.conditions: -- VADC platform when syncookie protection mode is configured and activated on a virtual server. Note: This issue might also occur on v12.x systems using the L7-intelligent-fpga HSB firmware.
bugs.impact: Potential performance impact.
bugs.fix: When syncookie protection mode is activated, all the genuine connections go through as expected, so there are no resets.

bugs.title: 3DES Ciphers have been removed from the SSL DEFAULT cipher list
bugs.symptoms: 3DES has been shown to be a weak cipher. As such, we removed it from the DEFAULT SSL cipher list (both clientssl and serverssl). On some older devices that can mean a connection is not possible.
bugs.conditions: Older SSL Clients and Servers might not be able to connect to the BIG-IP without a cipher list change.
bugs.impact: Service disruption
bugs.workaround: Not really a defect - the solution is to change the cipher string to "DEFAULT:3DES"

bugs.title: Assertion "vmem_hashlist_remove not found" failed.
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores with the following assertion: "vmem_hashlist_remove not found" failed.
bugs.conditions: It is unknown what leads to that situation directly.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The memory function fails the allocation gracefully.

bugs.title: 'SELinux targeted policy relabel is required' message
bugs.symptoms: 'SELinux targeted policy relabel is required' message appears at initial bootup. The system posts messages similar to the following: *** Warning -- SELinux targeted policy relabel is required. *** Relabeling could take a very long time, depending on file *** system size and speed of hard drives.
bugs.conditions: Install new software, reboot, watch the console.
bugs.impact: The indication of a 'warning' might be concerning. However, there is no impact to the functionality of the system. SELinux relabel always happens on first boot. It is a necessary and planned task and should be reported as an informational message instead of a warning.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is a cosmetic issue only.
bugs.fix: The SELinux relabel task message is now just an informational message.

bugs.title: Average CPU usage is calculated differently in DOS Visability page
bugs.symptoms: On systems with HT Split CPU the Average CPU usage shown in DOS Visibility page was calculated as average of all available CPU-s. On other hand, on other screens it is calculated as an average of maximum of data plane and control plane CPU-s. It causes inconsistency in displayed data.
bugs.conditions: HT Split is enabled on the system (tmsh list sys db scheduler.splitplanes.ltm results in "True")
bugs.impact: Inconsistency in CPU usage values displayed in DOS Visibility and other screens
bugs.fix: After the fix on systems with HT Split average CPU usage is calculated only for data plane CPU-s. The GUI title is changed correspondingly.

bugs.title: SSD Manufacturer "unavailable"
bugs.symptoms: On systems with an SSD, the manufacturer displayed in 'tmsh show sys hardware' may appear as "unavailable"..
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system with SSD installed.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, cosmetic only.
bugs.workaround: No workaround but the issue is only cosmetic and does not indicate an issue with the system.
bugs.fix: SSD Manufacturer now displays "Samsung" as expected.

bugs.title: 2nd Gy CCA-u is ignored by PEM if 2 CCR-u messages are sent before the 1st CCA-u is received.
bugs.symptoms: Quota provided by the 2nd Gy CCA-u is ignored which can result in limiting the effective quota provided to a subscriber. This in turn can result in additional control plane traffic as additional Gy CCR-u's outlining quota threshold/exhaustion will be sent by PEM.
bugs.conditions: PEM with Gx and Gy sessions. The threshold against the provided quota should be a large percentage of the quota which would result in quota exhaustion before additional quota is provided by the OCS.
bugs.impact: Potential service hit and increase in control plane traffic.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: Configure the threshold to be a smaller percentage of the provided quota.

bugs.title: TMM core when persist is enabled for wideip with certain iRule commands triggered.
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores with SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when persist is enabled for wideip, and an iRule with the following commands triggered: forward reject drop discard noerror host
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable persist on wideip. Note: Although this is not an ideal workaround, it provides a way that to use those iRule commands without causing a tmm core.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer coreswhen persist is enabled for wideip with certain iRule commands triggered.

bugs.title: CBL-0138-01 Active Copper does not work on i2000/i4000/HRC-i2800 Series appliances
bugs.symptoms: CBL-0138-01 will not come up or show link on i2000/i4000/HRC-i2800 series appliances. The following message will appear on the LCD: 0 01/30/17 09:02:59 error 0x1660016 Interface 5.0 detected a non 10GbE optic The following message will appear in /var/log/ltm: err pfmand[7630]: 01660016:3: Interface 5.0 detected a non 10GbE optic The interface will report in tmsh as down: tmsh show net interface 5.0 -------------------------------------------------------- Net::Interface Name Status Bits Bits Pkts Pkts Drops Errs Media In Out In Out -------------------------------------------------------- 5.0 down 0 0 0 0 0 0 none
bugs.conditions: i2000/i4000/HRC-i2800 series appliances and CBL-0138-01.
bugs.impact: The CBL-0138-01 will not work.
bugs.fix: CBL-0138-01 Active Copper now works correctly on i2000/i4000/HRC-i2800 Series appliances.

bugs.title: PEM: Gx sessions will stay in marked_for_delete state if CCR-T timeout happens
bugs.symptoms: PEM sessions stay in the marked-for-delete state if CCR-T times out.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if PCRF does not respond to CCR-T packets from the BIG-IP system during session termination.
bugs.impact: PEM sessions remain in the marked-for-delete state.
bugs.workaround: Configure the required timeout value in the sys db variable tmm.pem.session.timeout.endpointdeleteresponse. Note: The value must be greater than 0 (zero).
bugs.fix: PEM sessions no longer stay in the marked-for-delete state if CCR-T times out.

bugs.title: ILXFlow.lbSelect does not work inside 'requestStart' or 'requestComplete' events
bugs.symptoms: ILXFlow.lbSelect does not work inside the 'requestStart' or 'requestComplete' events.
bugs.conditions: Writing an ILX plugin that uses ILXFlow.lbSelect in the 'requestStart' or 'requestComplete' events.
bugs.impact: Load balancing selection fails. The plugin script fails.
bugs.fix: ILXFlow.lbSelect can now be called in the 'requestStart' and 'requestComplete' events.

bugs.title: Websocket URLs can't be explicitly excluded per attack signature
bugs.symptoms: A signature matches a websocket URL where it is defined as an excluded signature on the URL.
bugs.conditions: A websocket URL has a signature defined as excluded on this URL.
bugs.impact: A false positive signature match
bugs.workaround: disable the signature on the policy level when applicable.
bugs.fix: Signatures can now be excluded on the websocket URLs.

bugs.title: Cannot delete a SNAT pool and SNAT translation address in a single transaction.
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to delete an in-use SNAT translation and SNAT pool in a single transaction, tmsh will report that the SNAT translation object is in use, even though it is up for deletion in the current transaction. The system posts an error similar to the following: SNAT translation address <address> is still referenced by a snat pool
bugs.conditions: Attempt to delete a SNAT pool and SNAT translation object in the same transaction.
bugs.impact: Configuration scripts must order object deletion so that the SNAT translation object is removed before the SNAT pool.
bugs.workaround: Delete the SNAT translation first, then delete the SNAT pool.

bugs.title: mixed statistics between two intervals
bugs.symptoms: There are two collection intervals in AVR for collecting data: one every 10 sec for real time display and one every 5 min (or else set) for general statistics. The 5 min statistics is accumulated from the 30 intervals of 10 seconds. Sometimes, the last 10 seconds interval is missings the 5 min interval accumulation and entered the next 5 min interval resulting in an inaccurate accumulation of the 5 min interval.
bugs.conditions: This happens when the 10 seconds interval is taking too long to write it self
bugs.impact: Inaccurate accumulation of the 5 min interval statistics.
bugs.workaround: No workaround, some statistics will leak to next interval.
bugs.fix: The statistics for every 5 min interval will be display correctly (no leak between adjacent intervals).

bugs.title: Add support for IBM AppScan scanner schema changes
bugs.symptoms: IBM AppScan changed schema for its report file.
bugs.conditions: Using IBM AppScan for reporting.
bugs.impact: Data from new IBM AppScan scanner report file is not extracted properly for URL, parameters and cookies.
bugs.fix: Added support for IBM AppScan scanner schema changes.

bugs.title: Warning logged when GENERICMESSAGE::message drop iRule command used
bugs.symptoms: When submitting an iRule script using GENERICMESSAGE::message drop iRule command, a warning message is returned.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when saving an iRule that contains GENERICMESSAGE::message drop.
bugs.impact: A warning message is returned.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: iRule validation was improved to allow GENERICMESSAGE::message drop commands.

bugs.title: Incorrect entity is used when exporting TCP analytics from GUI
bugs.symptoms: When exporting statistics from the TCP Analytics page, the resulted data is for the default "view by" entity rather than the one that's actually selected
bugs.conditions: This occurs in Statistics :: Analytics : TCP, when you are viewing any dimension other than the default, and clicking Export.
bugs.impact: Incorrect data is being exported.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: The correct entity is now used when exporting TCP analytics from GUI, so the correct data is being exported.

bugs.title: Addition of new blade puts software management in a degraded state.
bugs.symptoms: When a new blade is inserted into a chassis that does not have HD1.1 populated, the software manager is sometimes unable to completely remove all logical volumes from the new blade's factory-installed HD1.1 volume set.
bugs.conditions: -- Adding a new blade in a chassis. -- The 'HD1.1' slot does not exist in the cluster.
bugs.impact: No immediate impact, but you will not be able to install to HD1.1 in the future due to the undeleted logical volume left in the volume set.
bugs.workaround: 1) Unmount the volume where the problem exists. 2) Remove the volume. 3) Restart the software manager. Example, in shell: First look in /var/log/liveinstall.log to find the name of the volume that still exists. You might see, for example: 'Can't remove open logical volume set.1._config'. Then use the following cleanup commands, substituting in the volume name, as follows: umount /dev/vg-db-sda/set.1._config lvremove /dev/vg-db-sda/set.1._config bigstart restart lind

bugs.title: Closing a PCP connection while an asynchronous mapping request is in progress may result in memory corruption.
bugs.symptoms: Memory corruption caused by closing a PCP connection while requests are being processed.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when a PCP client sends multiple requests and closes before receiving the replies. When the client OS receives a reply it will send an ICMP destination unreachable message which causes the BIG-IP to close the PCP connection. If the PCP connection is closed while a request is being processed, memory corruption may occur when the request completes.
bugs.impact: When memory corruption occurs, TMM may crash or assert. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Closing the PCP connection will not cause memory corruption.

bugs.title: Unable to create a bidirectional custom persistence record in MRF SIP
bugs.symptoms: Setting a persistence key via iRule sets the persistence entry as uni-directional
bugs.conditions: Setting a persistence key via iRule sets the persistence entry as uni-directional
bugs.impact: Custom SIP persistence entries cannot be bidirectional.
bugs.fix: This change adds a new SIP::persist key to set or reset the persistence entry as bidirectional.

bugs.title: CNAME ending with dot in pool causes validation problems after upgrade from 11.x to 12.x or v13.x
bugs.symptoms: gtm config load failure after upgrade from v11.x to v12.x or v13.x.
bugs.conditions: Create GTM pool with canonical-name ending with dot - for example "cname-with-dot.com." in v11.x and then upgrade to v12.x or v13.x.
bugs.impact: gtm config load failure after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Remove trailing dots or set "Domain Validation" to "none".
bugs.fix: Upgrading from 11.x to 12.x or 13.x with GTM Pool with canonical-name removes trailing FQDN dot.

bugs.title: GTM Monitor with send/receive string containing double-quote may cause upgrade to fail.
bugs.symptoms: When you upgrade from an affected version, the config gets saved before moving to the new version, thus dropping the enclosing quotes and causing a load failure when booting into the new version.
bugs.conditions: Configuration where monitor string contains \" (backslash double-quote) but does not contain one of the following characters: ' (single quote), | (pipe), { (open brace), } (close brace), ; (semicolon), # (hashtag), literal newline, or literal space.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit each string in the BIG-IP_gtm.conf to include enclosing quotes in order to get the config to load the first time.
bugs.fix: Configs load successfully after upgrade. Surrounding quotes, if missing, are added to strings in the BIG-IP_gtm.conf file after upgrade. For example: \"service_status\":\"on\".+\"maintenance\":\"off\" in the recv, send recv-disable and username fields. Output of list gtm monitor and bigip.conf match. Reloading the same config via tmsh does not cause unintentional changes, such as losing a level of escape in monitor strings.

bugs.title: Path MTU discovery occasionally fails
bugs.symptoms: Connections using a TCP profile that receive an ICMP needsfrag message may incorrectly ignore the message. This may cause Path MTU discovery to fail.
bugs.conditions: TCP profile assigned to VIP. Smaller MTU on data path than on TCP endpoints.
bugs.impact: The connection may stall as large TCP segments are continually retransmitted.
bugs.workaround: Configure the MSS in the TCP profile to match the lowest MSS. Use or disable Path MTU discovery with the tm.pathmtudiscovery database key.
bugs.fix: Path MTU discovery functions correctly with the TCP profile.

bugs.title: BFD may not remove dependant static routes when peer sends BFD Admin-Down
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, the BFD feature used in an Dynamic routing configuration, may not remove static routes when configured to be dependant on the liveliness of the BFD peer.
bugs.conditions: - BFD configured and up. - Static route configured and dependant on the BFD status of the BFD peer. - BFD peer enters maintenance mode by user configuration, setting the BFD session to admin-down.
bugs.impact: Static route may not be removed on BFD session configured by peer to be and traffic may still be routed.
bugs.fix: BFD now correctly removes dependant static routes on reception of BFD admin-down.

bugs.title: Standard deviation for Request Duration is calculated incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: In the HSL report, the Standard deviation for Request Duration is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: There are requests sent with delay reported in AVR reports.
bugs.impact: Wrong data in AVR reports. Standard deviation should be not 0 (zero), but it is reported as 0.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with standard deviaiton calculation.

bugs.title: TMM may crash with a very high number of concurrent TCP connections
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash with a very high number of concurrent connections (e.g., 30 million).
bugs.conditions: This happens if BIG-IP has a lot of concurrent connections and encounters HSB ring drops. At that time if ICMP monitors are configured, then LTM will QoS promote those ICMP monitor flows and if those are for the same endpoints, then tmm might crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with a very high number of concurrent TCP connections.

bugs.title: Configuration Utility shows 127.0.0.1 in the IP address field of the logon page and main page when using FQDN in browser
bugs.symptoms: Configuration Utility shows 127.0.0.1 in the IP address field of the logon page and main page.
bugs.conditions: -- Accessing Configuration Utility via Self IP. -- Using FQDN instead of Self IP in browser.
bugs.impact: 127.0.0.1 appears instead of SelfIP used on the mainpage

bugs.title: VPE endings/terminals incorrectly saved
bugs.symptoms: When a single transaction is used to create and move a terminal/ending, the move is not saved. When using macros, this can result in the terminal creation failing. Scenario 1: Click 'Edit Endings', click 'Add Ending', use the arrows to move the new ending, and click Save. Now open the 'Edit Endings' page again, the new ending is back at the top. Scenario 2: For a macro that is NOT currently being used, the same steps as scenario 1 apply for editing terminals. If you add a terminal and move it in the same transaction, the move is not saved. Scenario 3: For a macro that is being used, follow the same steps of creating a terminal and moving it within the same transaction. The save will fail with an error message that looks like this: Unable to execute transaction because of: 01071203:3: Caption (Out) of the rule in macrocall (/Common/alan-test_mac_empty) must be identical to the caption (Terminal 1) of terminalout.
bugs.conditions: Incorrect ordering occurs when the terminal/ending creation and move are done in the same transaction. MCPD error only occurs when these steps are done to a macro that is currently being used in the policy.
bugs.impact: Usability
bugs.workaround: Create the terminal/ending in one transaction. Then reopen the dialogue to move the terminal/ending.
bugs.fix: Fixed a calculation error in determining the ordering number for new terminals/endings.

bugs.title: Improve loading time when landing in dashboard page
bugs.symptoms: When data contains a very large number of different IP addresses, it can result in a long loading time for the dashboard page.
bugs.conditions: When opening Dashboard/Analysis page when DB contains a lot of data.
bugs.impact: Slow loading of the page.
bugs.fix: This release provides improved loading time when opening Dashboard/Analysis page with a very large number of different IP addresses.

bugs.title: Formatting installation using software v12.1.2 or v13.0.0 fails for i5000, i7000, i10000, i11000, i12000 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: Installation from external media (PXE or USB) fails with error: error: status 768 returned by command: /sbin/lvcreate -L -4719088K -n dat.share vg-db-cpmirror info: >++++ result: info: Negative size is invalid info: Run `lvcreate --help' for more information. info: >---- error: MultiVolume_add cpmirror.dat.share failed.
bugs.conditions: -- i5000, i7000, i10000, i11000, and i12000 platforms. -- Installation from external media (PXE or USB). -- Running software v12.1.2 or v13.0.0.
bugs.impact: System is non-functional. It will not work at all, until an 'installation from external media' is performed. There is no software on the system because the operation failed during the early stages of a formatting installation.
bugs.workaround: Use an earlier version for the formatting installation, such as 12.1.1, and then upgrade to the target version.
bugs.fix: The error no longer occurs; the formatting installation succeeds.

bugs.title: Western Digital WD1600YS-01SHB1 hard drives not recognized by pendsect
bugs.symptoms: In version 11.4.0, when pendsect was introduced, the Western Digital WD1600YS-01SHB1 hard drive was not supported. This drive was used in very early shipments of the 1600/3600 products. If you are running 11.4.0 and have a WD1600YS-01SHB1, you might see the following errors in /var/log/ltm: -- notice pendsect[1662]: skipping drive -- Model: WDC WD1600YS-01SHB1 -- notice pendsect[1662]: No known drives detected for pending sector check. Exiting
bugs.conditions: -- Running 11.4.0. -- Using WD1600YS-01SHB1 hard drives.
bugs.impact: The only impact is a pendsect notice in /var/log/ltm. The hard drive operates as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no mitigation or workaround for this issue.
bugs.fix: The WD1600YS-01SHB1 hard drive was added to the supported list of hard drives in versions 11.5.x, 11.6.x, and 12.1.3.

bugs.title: TMM may drop tunneled traffic when the sys db variable 'connection.vlankeyed' is set to 'disable'.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may drop tunneled traffic destined for it, even though the corresponding tunnel is created correctly.
bugs.conditions: The local-address of a tunnel is resided in a non-default route-domain and the sys db variable 'connection.vlankeyed' is set to 'disable'. Note that the default setting of that sys db variable is 'enable'.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may drop tunneled traffic.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer drops tunneled traffic.

bugs.title: Ready to be Enforced filter for Policy Signatures returns too many signatures
bugs.symptoms: Signatures that have not passed the staging period are shown when the filter is set to only show those that are ready to be enforced.
bugs.conditions: Signatures exist on a policy that have not passed their staging period and have no learning suggestions for them.
bugs.impact: Incorrect results are shown as a result of the filter.
bugs.workaround: The result should be inspected to see if the staging period has passed for each individual signature.
bugs.fix: The "Ready to be Enforced" filter works correctly.

bugs.title: MCP misses its heartbeat (and is killed by sod) if there are a large number of file objects on the system
bugs.symptoms: MCP may timeout and be killed by the sod watchdog, causing mcpd to restart.
bugs.conditions: Certain operations, under certain conditions, on certain platforms, may take longer to complete than the mcpd heartbeat timeout (300 seconds). When that happens, the system considers mcpd unresponsive, and will kill mcpd before it has finished its task, resulting in this issue. There are a number of ways that this issue may manifest. For example, the default mcpd heartbeat timeout might be reached when loading a configuration file with a large number* of file objects configured (e.g., SSL certificates and keys, data-groups, APM customizations, EPSEC file updates, external monitors, or other data present in the filestore (/config/filestore)). *Note: Depending the operations mcpd is performing, the performance of the hardware, the speed of disk access, and other potential factors, 3,000 is a relative estimate of the number of filestore objects that might cause this issue to occur.
bugs.impact: mcpd restarts, which causes a system to go offline and restart services.
bugs.workaround: To prevent the issue from occurring, you can temporarily disable the heartbeat timeout using the following command: modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat disable Important: Disabling the heartbeat timer means that, should the mcpd process legitimately become unresponsive, the system will not automatically restart mcpd to recover. Note: If you have a large number of objects (more than 3,000) in the filestore, and are able to reduce this by deleting their related configuration objects, you may be able to work around the issue. To determine the specific cause of the issue, you can open a support case with F5, to inspect the resulting mcpd core file.
bugs.fix: A possible case where mcpd goes too long without updating the heartbeat has been fixed by replacing one algorithm with a more efficient one.

bugs.title: Increased MySQL Memory usage when APM is provisioned on lower-end systems.
bugs.symptoms: You may notice mysql process continuously consuming high amount of CPU and memory resources when APM is provisioned. This can be seen in the results of 'top' command where mysql will be continuously listed. The issue applies to BIG-IP with 32 GB or less system memory available.
bugs.conditions: When APM module is provisioned, if either of the following is true: * logging configuration uses on-box publisher and log-level setting leads to high amount of logging data (e.g., DEBUG). * LocalDB or OAuth Authorization server is configured with a DB instance and traffic is being processed.
bugs.impact: You may notice general performance issues on BIG-IP systems with system memory 32 GB or lower when MySQL usage is high.
bugs.workaround: 1) Remove following 2 lines from file '/var/lib/mysql/cnf/apm.cnf' -- innodb_buffer_pool_size = 1G sort_buffer_size = 256M and save file before exiting. 2) Restart MySQL service using -- 'bigstart restart mysql'
bugs.fix: MySQL configuration when APM is provisioned now works as expected on lower-memory BIG-IP systems.

bugs.title: platform_check doesn't run PCI check on i11800
bugs.symptoms: When "platform_check misc" is run, it will return Miscellaneous Tests PCI: NOT RUN Test not available on this platform
bugs.conditions: This always happens.
bugs.impact: No platform check for PCI is executed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: It is fixed, platform check for PCI is executed.

bugs.title: tmrouted may continually restart after upgrade, adding or renaming an interface
bugs.symptoms: tmrouted continually restarts when it fails to resolve the interface index for a VLAN, VLAN group, or tunnel.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing configured. -- Non-default partition name or VLAN names greater than 15 characters.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing does not function. This may include monitors not functioning properly and marking pool members down incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: Shorten VLAN, VLAN group, or tunnel name, or move the interface into the Common partition.
bugs.fix: tmrouted no longer restarts when using long VLAN, VLAN group, or tunnel names in a non-default partition.

bugs.title: Update to max message size limit doesn't work sometimes
bugs.symptoms: There is a cap on all REST request/response message size. By default it is set to 32 MB, and you can modify it to higher limit using /mgmt/shared/server/messaging/settings/8100 REST endpoint. But the REST framework may not apply this change. When this occurs, you will see 501 Bad Gateway error from Apache and error message link "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: 47177925 is more than 33554432" in restjavad log (/var/log/restjavad.0.log).
bugs.conditions: This can occur when requesting or receiving more than 32 MB of data via iControl REST.
bugs.impact: REST framework applies message body limit only on incoming request and response. If incoming request results in requests to iControl REST or restnoded, the same settings (message body limit) are not applied.
bugs.fix: Messaging settings are applied on requests/responses, rather than on RestServer as forwarded outgoing requests/responses will not have server instance attached to request.

bugs.title: Processes started from interactive shells do not generate core files when they crash
bugs.symptoms: ulimit -c is set to 0 by default for login shells. This means that if a process crashes, and the process was started from an interactive session (e.g., via SSH or the console), it will not generate a core file. This behavior does not affect core system daemons such as TMM, MCPD, etc.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the default configuration.
bugs.impact: Processes run/started from an interactive session (e.g., via SSH or the console) that crash will not generate core files.
bugs.workaround: At a bash shell, set the core file limit for the current shell (and child processes) to "unlimited" by running the following command: ulimit -c unlimited
