Or you will see the following error messages in /var/log/apm. notice apmd[13086]: 01490000:5: memcache.c func: "mc_rcv_set_cmd()" line: 3501 Msg: Error: Invalid response to set command: SERVER_ERROR invalid command apmd[13086]: 01490000:5: memcache.c func: "mc_finish_set_pipeline()" line: 680 Msg: Error: Set pipeline: While receiving response to 0 cmd set
bugs.conditions: Rarely, when the system is in a transient state
bugs.impact: Unexpected responses

bugs.title: profile_clientssl should not be used with a transport-config
bugs.symptoms: transport-config objects define outgoing connections. Clientssl profile configures ssl compression for incoming connections. Thus adding a clientssl profile to a transport config has no effect
bugs.conditions: clientssl profile defined in a transport-config object
bugs.impact: The clientssl profile will not be used
bugs.workaround: do not include a clientssl profile in a transport-config object
bugs.fix: profile validation has been improved to not allow adding a clientssl profile to a transport-config object.

bugs.title: Password-less ssh access lost for non-admin users after tmsh load sys ucs
bugs.symptoms: During the load of ucs, the $HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys file is moved to /etc/ssh/<user> and then a symbolic link is pointed to that file in the $HOME/.ssh such that the ucs load modification of ownership won't break the password-less ssh access to the BIG-IP. The problem is that the /etc/ssh/<user> directory has no other-group read permissions and non-admin users can't read the file and hence the password-less access is denied and a password is requested.
bugs.conditions: Always happens as the permissions for /etc/ssh/<user> are 0700 (user read-write-execute only) and it is owned by root.
bugs.impact: Non-admin users lose password-less access to their BIG-IP after tmsh load sys ucs.
bugs.workaround: An admin user needs to manually change the permissions of the /etc/ssh and /etc/ssh/<user> permissions to be 0755. A non-admin user has no such capability and thus has no workaround.
bugs.fix: By simply setting the umask to 0022 prior to the call to mkpath (with 0755 permissions) makes the /usr/local/bin/install_ucs.pm script behave as expected. The override of the umask is then set back to previous value as to not affect the script elsewhere.

bugs.title: zxfrd may fail and restart after multiple failovers between blades in a chassis.
bugs.symptoms: zxfrd may fail and restart after multiple failovers between blades in a single chassis.
bugs.conditions: DNS Express must be configured in a multi-blade chassis. If a blade transitions from active to backup to active states and the DNS Express (tmmdns.bin) database has been re-created while the blade was in backup status, zxfrd may fail when attempting to reference old data.
bugs.impact: zxfrd will create a core file and restart, picking up where it left off.
bugs.fix: The cause of the failure is now addressed.

bugs.title: Sflow may use 0.0.0.0 as Agent Address in 2 core vCMP guests
bugs.symptoms: VCMP clusters without configured slot-specific management-ip addresses will report 0.0.0.0 for: sFlow (Agent Address), High Speed Logging (in certain log messages), and IPFIX (domain ID). When creating VCMP guests, the cluster's floating IP address is configured on the host using a command of the form: 'tmsh modify vcmp guest guest0 management-ip 10.1.2.3/24'; however, this will leave the slot-specific management IP address unconfigured. In this case, the affected services (sFlow, HSL, and IPFIX) will report 0.0.0.0 as their management IP address.
bugs.conditions: - vCMP guest deployed on a chassis with only Cluster IP set, and no individual blade IP addresses configured. - sflow and/or HSL and/or IPFIX configured.
bugs.impact: sflow, HSL, and IPFIX may incorrectly use 0.0.0.0 when identifying the BIG-IP system by management IP address. For sFlow, this is the default Agent Address. For HSL, certain log messages which identify the origin BIG-IP system by its management IP address will use this default value. For IPFIX, the domain ID will use this default value.
bugs.workaround: Configure cluster blade IP addresses. For example, to set the slot-specific management IP address on a VCMP guest which runs on a single slot, use a command similar to the following: tmsh modify sys cluster default members { 1 { address 10.1.2.3 } }

bugs.title: Crypto traffic failure for vCMP guests provisioned with more than 12 vcpus.
bugs.symptoms: Accelerated crypto and compression traffic may fail; stuck queue reports appear in logs.
bugs.conditions: Guests provisioned with more than 12 vcpus, and crypto or compression traffic passed through hardware acceleration.
bugs.impact: Can cause the hardware accelerator to fail and require host reboot.
bugs.workaround: Limit guest provisioning to 12 vcpus.
bugs.fix: Allow guests provisioned with more than 12 vcpus to operate without stalling hardware accelerators.

bugs.title: 'bigd' message send to 'mcpd' failure is not logged
bugs.symptoms: A bigd message to mcpd notifying of monitor status change may fail to be sent, without log notification, when the message is too large.
bugs.conditions: A message sent from bigd to mcpd that is too large (e.g., because of the unbounded accumulation of HTTP/1.1 200 codes with unique values).
bugs.impact: Mcpd is not notified of the monitor status change, and the missing message is not logged. The monitor reflects an incorrect status until a future status change triggers a successful notification-message to be sent from bigd to mcpd.
bugs.workaround: Diagnosis of an incorrect monitor status may identify this issue, but no direct workaround is available. The issue of the too-large bigd message is described in ID 645197, and involves the accumulation of unique HTTP/1.1 200 codes (indicating monitor success) without a monitor status-change for extended time (days or weeks). When a monitor status change finally occurs, bigd cannot notify mcpd because the message is too big. Thus, there is no indication of the monitor-status change. The secondary issue, here, is that there is no log message indicating the status-change-message-send failure.

bugs.title: Flash application components are loaded into wrong ApplicationDomain after Portal Access rewriting.
bugs.symptoms: Flash ActionScript3 application components are loaded into incorrect ApplicationDomain and in some rare cases this may cause errors in application.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when viewing Flash video while connected to APM.
bugs.impact: Flash applications might fail to render through Portal Access.
bugs.fix: Flash files accessed through Portal Access are now loading components into correct Application Domain. This improves compatibility with Flash apps.

bugs.title: UCS load does not set directory owner
bugs.symptoms: When loading a UCS file the directory /etc/ssh will become owned by the first user in the UCS with an .authorized_keys file.
bugs.conditions: UCS loaded that contains users with .authorized_key files
bugs.impact: Ownership of /etc/ssh is set to a non-root user after UCS load. This does not interfere with normal system operation or SSH authentication but does not follow secure coding practices
bugs.workaround: Ownership of on /etc/ssh can be restored with the command: chown root /etc/ssh
bugs.fix: UCS load now explicitly sets ownership of the /etc/ssh directory to root.

bugs.title: Dynamic routing update can delete admin ip route from the kernel
bugs.symptoms: Routes obtained from dynamic routing (BGP, etc.) can replace existing management route for the admin IP address, making the BIG-IP lose its management route. Static routes created via TMSH can replace management route.
bugs.conditions: Using TMSH to create "net route" that matches management network, or dynamic routing accepts a route that matches the management network.
bugs.impact: Losing the management network route, and potential loss of access to the BIG-IP via the management network.
bugs.workaround: Don't accept route updates for the management network. Don't create static routes for the management network.
bugs.fix: Management network admin IP address is now protected from being overwritten.

bugs.title: SSL connection is not mirrored if ssl session cache is cleared and resume attempted
bugs.symptoms: SSL connection is not mirrored if ssl session cache is cleared before attempting to resume the ssl connection.
bugs.conditions: A previous ssl session is attempting to resume the connection after the ssl session cache has been cleared.
bugs.impact: Connection is established but is not mirrored.
bugs.workaround: Could be avoided by disabling ssl session cache.
bugs.fix: SSL connection is not mirrored if ssl session cache is cleared before attempting to resume the ssl connection.

bugs.title: EdgeClient doesn't notify the user when it's time to interact with the logon page.
bugs.symptoms: EdgeClient doesn't notify the user when it's time to interact with the logon page.
bugs.conditions: When EdgeClient is minimized to the tray and the page requires user interaction no notification is shown.
bugs.impact: User may not know that EdgeClient is waiting for the input, hence VPN connection isn't established until user provides credentials
bugs.workaround: In the current Access Policy for each logon-page-and-language combination: * Go to advanced logon page customization. * Open the source code. * Find the following line: 'externalWebHost.webLogonNotifyUser();' * Replace it with the following line: 'externalWebHost.WebLogonNotifyUser();' Note the uppercase 'W' at the beginning of 'WebLogonNotifyUser' replace string.
bugs.fix: Now Edge Client correctly notifies the user when it's time to interact with the logon page to perform authentication.

bugs.title: MAC address must be configured on virtual function
bugs.symptoms: There may be a system outage if the virtual function device is not provided a MAC address from the hypervisor.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual Edition. -- Fortville virtual function device not provided a MAC address from the hypervisor.
bugs.impact: System outage.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that a MAC address is configured for each virtual function.

bugs.title: LACP PDUs generated by lacpd on i4x00/i2x00 platforms contain bad ethernet src mac address
bugs.symptoms: LACP PDUs generated by the 'lacpd' on the i4x00 & i2x00 platforms contain the wrong Ethernet source MAC address.
bugs.conditions: LACP configured on an trunk interface on i4x00 or i2x00 platforms.
bugs.impact: Some Cisco and Juniper switches discard these PDUs. They send PDUs as if the BIG-IP is not transmitting with a all-zeros 'Partner' section System ID. This renders LACP inoperable, and simply does nothing if the far end is configured for 'Passive'.
bugs.fix: Insure correct Source MAC address is inserted into the PDU.

bugs.title: TMSH allows mirror for persistence even when no mirroring configuration exists
bugs.symptoms: When Mirroring is not configured in a high-availability (HA) configuration, the Configuration Utility (GUI) correctly hides the 'mirror' option for Persistence profile. However, Persistence Mirroring can still be enabled via TMSH.
bugs.conditions: -- Mirroring is configured in an HA configuration. -- Persistence profile. -- Using TMSH.
bugs.impact: A memory leak and degraded performance can occur when: -- The Mirroring option of a Persistence profile is enabled. -- Mirroring in the HA environment is not configured.
bugs.workaround: Always use the Configuration Utility (GUI) to configure Persistence profiles. If you encounter this issue, complete the following procedure to locate Persistence profiles with Mirroring enabled, and then disable Mirroring for those profiles: 1. Access the BIG-IP Bash prompt. 2. List the Persistence profiles with the following command: tmsh list ltm persistence 3. Examine the Persistence profiles to identify the ones with 'mirror enabled'. 4. Disable Mirroring for each Persistence profile, using a command similar to the following: tmsh modify ltm persistence <persistence_type> <profile_name> mirror disabled 5. Save the changes to the Persistence profiles: tmsh save sys config
bugs.fix: TMSH no longer allows the configuration of mirroring of persistence profiles, which prevents any potential memory leak.

bugs.title: Ephemeral Node may be errantly created in bigd, causing crash
bugs.symptoms: When FQDN Ephemeral Nodes are being used at the same time as static Node objects, and there is change in those objects, either via DNS resolver changes or manual changes to static nodes, there exists a chance where one may be misidentified as the other during an update, causing a crash in bigd.
bugs.conditions: FQDN Nodes and Static Nodes being used. Change in node settings or creation/deletion of nodes.
bugs.impact: Bigd crashes, causing interruption in monitoring.
bugs.workaround: Avoid use of FQDN Nodes and Pool Members; use only static-IP Nodes/Members instead.
bugs.fix: Fixed case where misidentification may occur, resulting in bigd running without crashing.

bugs.title: GTM autodiscovery shows same status for tcp+udp virtuals using the same dest:port
bugs.symptoms: With GTM autodiscovery, when virtuals having same dest:port but different protocols from same ltm target, these virtuals have same status(both down or both up).
bugs.conditions: Virtual servers have same dest:port but different protocol from the same ltm target and GTM enables auto discovery.
bugs.impact: If you have two virtuals configured with the same IP:port, and you use those virtuals in gtm pools, you could have a virtual server down, and yet gtm would see it as still being up (or up, and seen as down), and there are no warnings, no messages to let them know anything is wrong.
bugs.workaround: Manually define the ltm-names, allowing gtmd to pass unambiguous requests to mcpd over iquery like this: modify gtm server gtm_myself virtual-servers modify { /Common/vs1_tcp { ltm-name vs1_tcp }} modify gtm server gtm_myself virtual-servers modify { /Common/vs1_udp { ltm-name vs1_udp }}

bugs.title: BIG-IP may send oversized TCP segments on traffic it originates
bugs.symptoms: Traffic from the Linux host on BIG-IP may send TCP segments larger than the advertised TCP MSS of a remote host.
bugs.conditions: Received TCP MSS (plus protocol overhead) smaller than configured MTU of interface. Linux host sending large TCP segments, such as SNMP getbulk replies.
bugs.impact: TMM may send traffic to a TCP host that exceeds the host's advertised MTU.
bugs.workaround: disable segmentation offload for the nvic
bugs.fix: BIG-IP no longer originates traffic to TCP hosts that exceed that host's advertised MTU.

bugs.title: System Log is not visible for ASM-related user roles
bugs.symptoms: System Log is not visible for ASM-related user roles, even though the ui.logaccess db key is already set to enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- User is logged in as security editor or security admin. -- The ui.logaccess key is enabled.
bugs.impact: Cannot access the system log from the GUI menu.
bugs.fix: The system log menu is now shown when ui.logaccess db key is enabled.

bugs.title: BD crashes repeatedly after interrupted roll-forward upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After roll-forward upgrade of version 12.1.x with ASM traffic data is interrupted, BD crashes repeatedly.
bugs.conditions: Roll-forward upgrade with ASM traffic data from version 12.1.x (with or without hotfixes) to any 12.1.x or later is interrupted by restart/reboot.
bugs.impact: BD crashes repeatedly on subsequent attempts to start ASM.
bugs.workaround: Disable roll-forward upgrade of ASM traffic data before upgrade: tmsh modify sys db ucs.asm.traffic_data.save value disable
bugs.fix: ASM completes roll-forward upgrade with traffic data correctly, even after upgrade process is interrupted.

bugs.title: AVR external log should have the option to start publishing at random time
bugs.symptoms: Every 5 minutes (or avrd interval), avrd sends entire external log. If you have many BIG-IP systems, this can cause a spike in the syslog server.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently when sending AVR data to external log servers.
bugs.impact: All logging is done at the same avrd interval, which can overload the external log servers.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A new DB variable was added: Avr.AddRandomDelayBeforeSnapshot. If the DB variable is set to 'enable', avrd will add a random interval before sending data to the external log server. The interval max value will be: ((avrd interval) / 2).

bugs.title: Multiple log messages 'Async process socket is full' written to asm_config_server.log
bugs.symptoms: While under CPU load, ASM policy adjustments by Automatic Policy Builder causes a flood of the following log message: Async process socket is full.
bugs.conditions: -- Device is under CPU load. -- Automatic Policy Builder requests ASM policy adjustments.
bugs.impact: A flood of 'Async process socket is full' messages are written to /var/log/ts/asm_config_server.log.
bugs.fix: 'Async process socket is full' log messages are now throttled.

bugs.title: Unnecessary disk monitor warnings for /var/asmdata1 on large platforms
bugs.symptoms: On large platforms, when you are logged into the console you see the following warning displayed frequently: "Disk partition /var/asmdata1 has less than 30% free"
bugs.conditions: ASM is installed with large platform configuration (such as on 6900).
bugs.impact: Disk usage warning is displayed frequently. Since ASM will likely reach expected disk utilization of greater than 70% during normal operation on large platforms, the threshold is set too low.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the percentage at which disk monitor alerts for /var/asmdata1: tmsh modify sys db platform.diskmonitor.limitwarn.var_asmdata1 value 15 tmsh modify sys db platform.diskmonitor.limitalert.var_asmdata1 value 10

bugs.title: LDAP search-timeout setting is not effective
bugs.symptoms: With LDAP remote auth, LDAP search does not timeout when search-timeout is set.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote authentication configured with LDAP or Active Directory. -- Search-timeout is set to some finite value.
bugs.impact: Login may be slow to fail when there is a problem with the LDAP server.

bugs.title: Client connection may hang when NTLM and OneConnect profiles used together
bugs.symptoms: In deployments where a NT LanManager (NTLM) authentication profile and a OneConnect profile are used together in a LTM virtual server to label an authenticated connection to a Domain Controller (DC); if the persisted connection to the DC is re-used, the connection may hang. A connection in this state may not be cleaned up by the sweeper, resulting in a memory leak.
bugs.conditions: The NTLM and OneConnect profiles are associated with a LTM virtual server.
bugs.impact: A client connection won't be serviced and TMM memory will leak. Over a long time period, this may result in more widespread service disruptions.
bugs.workaround: Avoid the use of OneConnect profiles on virtual servers that use NTLM profiles. The connections to the Domain Controller won't be pooled, but all other features will be retained.
bugs.fix: Fixed a problem that prevented NTLM and OneConnect profiles from working properly on the same LTM virtual server.

bugs.title: Improved default storage size for DNS Express database
bugs.symptoms: A tweak has been made to the DNS Express database to improve the initial database size.
bugs.conditions: DNS Express with configured zones.
bugs.impact: Possibly reduced database size.
bugs.workaround: N/A as this is an improvement.
bugs.fix: A tweak has been made to the DNS Express database to improve the initial database size.

bugs.title: HA standby virtual server with non-default lasthop settings may crash.
bugs.symptoms: A long-running high availability (HA) Standby Virtual Server with non-default lasthop settings may crash TMM.
bugs.conditions: -- HA standby virtual server is configured on the system with non-default lasthop configurations (e.g., lasthop pools or autolasthop disabled, etc). -- That virtual server receives more than 2 billion connections (2 billion is the maximum value of a 32-bit integer).
bugs.impact: TMM on the next-active device crashes. The Active device is not affected. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.symptoms: Changing the IKEv1 phase2 authentication algorithm to sha256, sha384, or sha512 does not work immediately, without a restart of the tmipsecd daemon.
bugs.conditions: If you change the ike-phase2-auth-algorithm attribute (inside an instance of ipsec-policy) to a value of sha256, sha384, or sha512, this causes a parse error when received by racoon. Thus the change does not take affect without a racoon restart.
bugs.impact: Cannot switch IKEv1 ipsec-policy to sha256, sha384, or sha512 authentication without either restarting BIG-IP or restarting tmipsecd.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the tmipsecd daemon causes a restart of all racoon processes, which causes the config to be re-read and then IKEv1 IPsec works correctly with SHA authentication algorithms.

bugs.title: Landing URI incorrect when changing URI
bugs.symptoms: User accesses resource1, and an access policy starts. Before the policy completes, the user changes to resource2. There is a warning page that the session already exists, and the user clicks to create a new session. After the policy completes, the user is directed to the landing URI of the resource1.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to change landing URI in the middle of an access policy
bugs.impact: End-user is inconveniently directed to the first resource instead of the second.
bugs.fix: Now the "To open a new session, please click here." link on the APM logout page reflects the last used landing URI rather than the first used landing URI.

bugs.title: Hide datasync-global-dg from the Device Group List page
bugs.symptoms: This device-group 'datasync-global-dg' is created and updated automatically, and should not be modified or deleted manually.
bugs.conditions: The 'datasync-global-dg' data-group gets deleted manually.
bugs.impact: The system may go offline, and errors may appear 'Can't associate Datasync Update Files'.
bugs.workaround: After accidentally deleting the datasync-global-dg device-group, the easiest way to resolve this issue is to perform the following procedure: 1. Run the following command: tmsh save sys config. 2. Run the following command: tmsh load sys config. 3. Wait a few seconds. If system is Offline, then wait about 3 minutes until the system is ACTIVE. 4. Run the following command: tmsh save sys config (for a second time). 5. Perform a force sync of datasync-global-dg: From the GUI of the same device (the device that was previously offline), select 'Sync Device to Group', making sure to check 'Overwrite Configuration', and click 'Sync'. 6. Wait until the devices are both ACTIVE and 'In Sync'.
bugs.fix: The device-group datasync-global-dg is now hidden from the Device Group List page, but still should appear in the 'Device Management Overview' page to allow controlling the sync.

bugs.title: Improve DNS TSIG Handling
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP software has long supported TSIG-style transaction security for zone transfers. It has not supported them for standard queries, however. A third-party DNS server requesting a zone transfer may first perform a standard SOA query to determine if a zone has changed prior to requesting a full transfer. This is vendor specific. When this request is TSIG signed, a BIG-IP system fails to properly respond.
bugs.conditions: A TSIG-signed DNS standard query arrives at a BIG-IP system, intended to be properly answered by the BIG-IP system itself, rather than being proxied to a pool member.
bugs.impact: This change affects DNS messages containing TSIG signatures. Those messages that do not contain these signatures are not affected. The handling of TSIG-signed messages has changed as described in the fix text.
bugs.workaround: This defect's workaround is limited to the case of a zone transfer client issuing a signed SOA query prior to conducting the actual transfer. In this case, it may be possible to configure the zone transfer client (DNS server requesting the transfer) to directly perform IXFR requests, rather than first issuing an SOA query first. If possible, this would avoid sending the BIG-IP a signed standard query (SOA), and thus allow transfers to occur.
bugs.fix: This fix corrects this defect, by adding support for properly handling queries of all types containing TSIG, as long as BIG-IP system possesses the correct TSIG key used to sign the received request. When the request is received, if the key is found, the signature validates, and the signature is within the validity timespan, the request is handled, and the response is properly signed with the key. If any of this fails, an error response (BADKEY, BADSIG, or BADTIME) is returned. The only exception to this behavior is: If the query contains a TSIG signature, and the key used is not found in the BIG-IP configuration, and the DNS profile's unhandled query action is 'allow', then the query is not touched, but rather simply proxied. This is done based on the possibility that some back-end server does have the needed key, and can therefore respond to the request. This fix also impacts the handling of zone transfer NOTIFY messages that lack a TSIG. In past versions, these messages were allowed and acted upon even if the zone setting 'Verify Notify TSIG' was enabled. NOTIFY messages lacking a TSIG are now dropped if this setting is enabled.

bugs.title: Stats for SNATs do not work when configured in a non-zero route domain
bugs.symptoms: When creating SNAT in a Route Domain different from 0, the command 'tmsh show ltm snat' does not report any statistics.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on all SNATs in a route domain other than 0.
bugs.impact: No statistics for the SNATs
bugs.fix: Stats for SNATs now work when configured in a non-zero route domain.

bugs.title: EPSEC installation failure reason is not logged in certain conditions.
bugs.symptoms: EPSEC installation fails with no specific reason provided in the error message.
bugs.conditions: This happens only when there is a version mismatch between the EPSEC RPM's database and the shared RPM database on the BIG-IP system. Often this happens if a switchboot is issued to activate an earlier version of BIG-IP software from a later version. The RPM database is shared, so on a switchboot, the RPM database version is not downgraded. This causes the subsequent EPSEC installation to fail. Although this is expected behavior, the reason for failure is not logged.
bugs.impact: Difficult to debug actual EPSEC installation failure reason.
bugs.fix: The system now logs the EPSEC installation failure reason.

bugs.title: Deletion of saml-idp-connector may fail depending on the order in which related objects are deleted within a transaction
bugs.symptoms: The system posts messages similar to the following even when the server associated to the connector is also being deleted in the same transaction: 01070734:3: Configuration error: apm aaa saml-idp-connector: Cannot delete saml-idp-connector /Common/saml_connector because it is being used by aaa-saml-server (/Common/saml_server_test1
bugs.conditions: When deleting saml-idp-connector first then the associated saml server.
bugs.impact: Cannot delete saml-idp-connector and associated server in that specific order.
bugs.workaround: Delete saml server first and then delete the saml connector.
bugs.fix: Now saml-idp-connector can be deleted with associated objects in any order from a transaction.

bugs.title: bigd/tmm con vCMP guests
bugs.symptoms: bigd/tmm con vCMP guests.
bugs.conditions: Set up vCMP guest on VIPRION B2100, B4200, or B4300 blades.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: This release corrects this issue so the crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: CPU overtemp condition threshold is 75C
bugs.symptoms: A CPU overtemp condition is logged when a B4450 CPU reaches 75C.
bugs.conditions: CPU temperature is only 75C and ambient temperature in the blade is in the normal range.
bugs.impact: Since the temperature threshold is set too low, the warning does not indicate an actual problem.
bugs.fix: The fix raises the CPU overtemp threshold to 88C for B4450. With the fix, the warning should be considered valid.

bugs.title: Internal virtual server inherits CMP hash mode from parent virtual server
bugs.symptoms: An internal virtual server might behave in unexpected ways, such as abort a client connection before connecting to the server.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with request-adapt or response-adapt profile and a vlan with 'cmp-hash' mode 'src-ip'. Internal virtual server without a VLAN or 'cmp-hash' setting.
bugs.impact: The internal virtual server might sometimes abort when attempting to make a connection to the server. This occurs after a successful load-balance pick indicated by the LB_SELECTED event, but before a TCP SYN packet is sent to the server. As a result the parent virtual performs the service-down-action configured in the request-adapt or response-adapt profile.
bugs.workaround: If possible, do not use the cmp-hash mode 'src-ip'.
bugs.fix: An internal virtual server is not affected by any 'cmp-hash' mode setting in the parent virtual server.

bugs.title: A monitor may unexpectedly transition from up to down and back to up.
bugs.symptoms: A pool member or node monitor may unexpectedly transition from up to down and back to up even though the pool member or node has not failed.
bugs.conditions: One or more of FTP, IMAP, POP3, or SMTP monitors are in use. This might also occur with monitor types other than those listed.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system might send a premature FIN on the connection. This might result in unexpected monitor flapping even though the monitored object has not failed.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP system no longer sends a premature FIN on the connection, so unexpected monitor flapping no longer occurs, in this case.

bugs.title: GUI to disable HEAD request
bugs.symptoms: Users are able to make HEAD HTTP request to GUI.
bugs.conditions: Users make an HEAD HTTP request and GUI allows it.
bugs.impact: GUI will allow HEAD HTTP request.
bugs.workaround: Configure the ssl.conf file to prevent HEAD HTTP request.
bugs.fix: Configure GUI to prevent HEAD HTTP request.

bugs.title: Apmd crashes with segmentation fault when trying to load access policy
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, apmd restarts when trying to re-load an access policy.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when some of the policy items are modified while apmd is trying to re-load the access policy.
bugs.impact: The apmd process restarts.

bugs.title: L7 Policy state may be corrupted in rare occasions
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may crash due to a conflict in L7 Policy state between the client and server-side connections.
bugs.conditions: When a virtual server configuration is changed together with policy configurations. One-Connect is used on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes due to the client-side and server-side L7 Policy state being out of sync after a configuration change.

bugs.title: Accessing SAML Resource may cause reset connection when SSO on access profile contains v1 (NTLM, form based) configuration
bugs.symptoms: Accessing SAML Resource causes RST when Single Sign-On (SSO) on access profile contains V1 configuration (NTLM, form based).
bugs.conditions: All of the following: - BIG-IP system is configured and used as SAML Identity Provider. - In-use access profile has both: 1) V1 SSL attached (NTLM, form based) and SAML resources assigned on access policy. - APM end user performs IdP-initiated SAML WebSSO by clicking published SAML resource on the webtop.
bugs.impact: TCP connection to the client is reset. As a result, APM end user is not able to perform IdP-initiated SAML WebSSO.
bugs.fix: Assigning V1 SSO profile on access policy no longer causes a connection reset when APM end user performs IdP-initiated SAML WebSSO by clicking published SAML resource on the webtop.

bugs.title: iOS RDP client fails to connect to RD Connection Broker via APM's Native RDP resource
bugs.symptoms: iOS RDP client fails to connect to Windows Server 2012/2016 with RD Connection Broker role installed via APM's Native RDP resource. When user launches Native RDP resource from APM Webtop, RDP client shows following error messages: -- Can't connect to the Remote Desktop Gateway. Contact your network administrator for assistance. (Error code: 0x03000008). -- Disconnected from server vpn.example.com with error code 0x00000003.
bugs.conditions: Using iOS client to connect to Windows Server 2012/2016 with RD Connection Broker role installed via APM's Native RDP resource.
bugs.impact: Connection from RD client to Terminal Server via BIG-IP APM fails.
bugs.workaround: iOS does not work in this case, but you can connect using a client device besides iOS such as Android.
bugs.fix: iOS RDP client now can connect to Windows Server 2012/2016 with RD Connection Broker role installed via APM's Native RDP resource.

bugs.title: ASM REST: POST disallowed to /mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/server-technologies endpoint
bugs.symptoms: POST was disallowed against the collection, but BIG-IQ needs this functionality to add the server technology with no side-effects.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IQ is used to manage a device, and a server technology is added to an ASM policy.
bugs.impact: BIG-IQ deployments that add a new server technologies on a policy will fail.
bugs.workaround: Non-BIG-IQ usage can and should be using mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/apply-server-technologies to add server technologies. For BIG-IQ there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Simple POST to /mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/server-technologies is now allowed.

bugs.title: RATE-SHAPER:Fred not properly initialized may halt traffic
bugs.symptoms: RATE-SHAPER:Fred is not properly initialized and might halt traffic.
bugs.conditions: Initialize RATE-SHAPER:Fred as the drop policy using its default properties.
bugs.impact: Traffic is halted.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Initialize the drop policy fred to the value of 9999 instead of default 0. -- Use RED as drop policy instead of fred.

bugs.title: Multiple requests from server may cause RTSP connection to stall
bugs.symptoms: When multiple requests are sent from the server before receiving response or further requests from the client, the RTSP connection may stall.
bugs.conditions: Virtual is configured with the RTSP profile and multiple requests are sent from the server before receiving response or further requests from the client.
bugs.impact: RTSP connection stalls.

bugs.title: /tmp/wccp.log file grows unbounded
bugs.symptoms: WCCP uses /tmp/wccp.log as output for Diagnostic information, independent of log level or db key. This file can grow unbounded if there are never any WCCP packets sent. If packets are sent the file is cleaned up automatically.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if WCCP is configured but never goes beyond negotiation.
bugs.impact: /tmp/wccp.log grows unbounded, filling up the disk.

bugs.title: Historical session data in db and inconsistent GUI info
bugs.symptoms: You notice a lot of session tracking data in your new ASM deployment, showing blocked requests, particularly on one of the high availability peers.
bugs.conditions: Enabling Session Tracking and setting "Block All Period" . Block All data points defaults to persist infinitely (with no expiration period).
bugs.impact: The records of session tracking are never cleaned up, which can present confusing session data.
bugs.workaround: Clear all session tracking data points (or as many as possible) and prevent them from accumulating. A) To prevent data points from accumulating, consider setting the blocking period to the default of 600 seconds (5 minutes) instead of 'infinite'. B) There is no option of clearing out all data points for a given policy in the GUI. This example provides one-line commands to do so. -- Run the following two commands sequentially, to clear out the data points of a specific policy. -- Apply that procedure for as many policies as possible. For example, given a policy id of 13, the following commands replace 13 (at '{ policy_id => 13 }') with the required policy id: ------------------ perl -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::Policy -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::SessionAwarenessDataPoint -e 'F5::ASMConfig::Entity::SessionAwarenessDataPoint->delete_many(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), policy => F5::ASMConfig::Entity::Policy->new(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), get_criteria => { policy_id => 13 }), master_keys => 1)' perl -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::Policy -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::SessionAwarenessDataPoint -e 'F5::ASMConfig::Entity::SessionAwarenessDataPoint->reload_session_db(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), policy => F5::ASMConfig::Entity::Policy->new(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), get_criteria => { policy_id => 13 }), delete_existing => 1)' ------------------
bugs.fix: Session Awareness Statuses are now cleaned after the expiration period, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Failover DB variables do not correctly implement 'reset-to-default'
bugs.symptoms: When the 'modify sys db' command option 'reset-to-default' is issued, the new value does not take effect, even though 'list sys db' displays the desired value.
bugs.conditions: This is known to affect at least the following failover-related DB variables: log.failover.level failover.nettimeoutsec failover.debug failover.usetty01 failover.rebootviasod failover.packetcheck failover.packetchecklog failover.secure mysqlhad.heartbeattimeout mysqlhad.debug mysqldfailure.enabled mysqldfailure.haaction.primary mysqldfailure.haaction.secondary
bugs.impact: The configuration change does not take effect.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly set the DB variable to the desired value.
bugs.fix: reset-to-default restores the default values.

bugs.title: bigd monitor stuck in fqdn-checking when DNS server unreliable
bugs.symptoms: FQDN monitors may be stuck in status 'fqdn-checking' in environments with an unreliable DNS server, such as when DNS queries frequently timeout.
bugs.conditions: FQDN monitors are configured; and the DNS server used to resolve FQDN nodes is intermittently available, leading to occasional timeouts to bigd from DNS queries.
bugs.impact: FQDN monitor status remains in 'fqdn-checking', even after the DNS server again becomes available. Monitors may eventually become "un-stuck", and monitors will (correctly) reset upon system restart.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, FQDN monitors are not recommended for use in environments where DNS servers are unreliable.

bugs.title: Android receiver 3.11 new store addition with auto discovery does not work
bugs.symptoms: Could not add a new account in auto discovery for Citrix receiver 3.11 version and getting error as "Citrix Receiver could not verify the server address"
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP virtual is configured for Citrix replacement mode in 11.5.x release Adding new account in Citrix Android receiver 3.11 in auto discover mode.
bugs.impact: Could not add new account in auto discover mode for Citrix Android receiver 3.11
bugs.workaround: Add this iRule to the virtual server. when HTTP_REQUEST { set uri_path [string tolower [HTTP::path]] if { $uri_path == "/vpn/index.html" } { set cookie "pwcount=0;Secure;HttpOnly;Path=/" HTTP::respond 200 -version auto content "/vpn/cgi/login" noserver "Set-Cookie" $cookie } elseif { $uri_path == "/agservices/discover" } { set cookie "X-Citrix-Session-Expired=true" HTTP::respond 403 noserver "X-Citrix-Session-Expired" "true" } }

bugs.title: MCP may crash when making specific changes to a FIX profile attached to more than one virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When a FIX profile is attached to more than one virtual server, making specific edits to the profile may result in MCP crashing and restarting.
bugs.conditions: A FIX profile is be in use and attached to more than one virtual server. You then edit the profile (and click "Update") in this order: - Change the Error Action from "Don't Forward" to "Drop Connection" - Add a new mapping to the Sender and Tag Substitution Data Group Mapping.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.fix: Prevented MCP from crashing when the FIX profile is edited.

bugs.title: B2250: Interface is dropping traffic in passive mode
bugs.symptoms: Passive mode is a new mode of operation introduced in BIG-IP version 13.0.0. In this mode of operation, the BIG-IP system processes data offline to detect DoS attacks and/or to collect HTTP analytics data, etc. The results are reported by the BIG-IP system might not be accurate.
bugs.conditions: -- Device is operating on passive mode data. -- VIPRION 2250 blade.
bugs.impact: This will impact BIG-IP system's ability to operate in passive mode.
bugs.fix: Passive mode is now fully supported on the B2250.

bugs.title: inconsistent attribute naming in sys connection
bugs.symptoms: The TMSH command "show sys connection" returns the idle time of a connection. However, its manpage refers to this as "age." Age is actually the minimum idle time.
bugs.conditions: Man page and TMSH command have different names for the same attribute.
bugs.impact: Different names in attribute might be confusing.
bugs.workaround: N/A.
bugs.fix: The "age" label is now "minimum idle time" in the man page.

bugs.title: HSL Balanced distribution to Two-member pool may not be balanced correctly.
bugs.symptoms: When configuring a two-member pool as HSL destination and using "balanced" distribution, logs from iRule HSL::send may end up balanced to a single pool member.
bugs.conditions: - Two-member pool configured as remote-high-speed-log destination. - The remote-high-speed-log distribution is set to "balanced" - Data-Plane logging using for example but not limited to: iRule HSL::send.
bugs.impact: Log message may not be distributed correctly resulting in more load on a single pool member.
bugs.fix: Logs are distributed more equally on pool members in "balanced" distribution HSL.

bugs.title: bd keeps coring after upgrade to 12.1.2 or later
bugs.symptoms: Pre-existing traffic data files from a previous attempt to perform a roll-forward/upgrade remain on the disk under /var/asmdata1/traffic_data, even after you set ucs.asm.traffic_data.save to disable. The qkview contains errors such as the following. -- ASM subsystem error (asm_start,F5::DbUpgrade::__ANON__): DBD::mysql::db do failed: Too many partitions (including subpartitions) were defined --
bugs.conditions: This can occur after upgrading ASM to 12.1.2 or later, and rolling forward the configuration.
bugs.impact: The ASM enforcer application continually fails, causing unit instability.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade by saving a UCS on 12.1.0, performing a clean install of 12.1.2, and then loading the UCS onto 12.1.2 (or later). In the manual save/load UCS process, the upgrade of the Request Log can be disabled, which works around the error, so the UCS can load without error. This can be set by: # tmsh modify sys db ucs.asm.traffic_data.load value never
bugs.fix: /var/asmdata1/traffic_data is now cleared as part of UCS load cleanup, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: LB::reselect iRule on a virtual with the HTTP profile can cause a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes after the LB::reselect iRule fails to connect to the server.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur when a virtual server is configured with HTTP and the LB::reselect iRule. If the LB::reselect fails to connect to the server and there is not a monitor on the pool, tmm will crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure a monitor for the pool.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to LB::reselect

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin may crash on some JavaScript files
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite plugin may crash parsing JavaScript files in US ASCII encoding.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript file in US ASCII encoding (not in UTF-8).
bugs.impact: Rewrite plugin may crash parsing this file. No response is sent to client.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to change/add 'charset' parameter in response header 'Content-type' to 'UTF-8' by iRule.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access rewrite correctly handles JavaScript data if the web page uses US ASCII encoding.

bugs.title: bcm56xxd core when configuring QinQ VLAN with vCMP provisioned.
bugs.symptoms: bcm56xxd constantly crashes, device goes off-line.
bugs.conditions: Reboot the system with QinQ VLANs configured and vCMP provisioned.
bugs.impact: Device goes off-line.
bugs.fix: bcm56xxd no longer crashes when QinQ VLANs are configured and vCMP provisioned.

bugs.title: EdgeClient locked mode exclusion list admin UI doesn't allow underscore character
bugs.symptoms: EdgeClient locked mode exclusion list admin UI doesn't allow underscore character
bugs.conditions: An administrator is trying to configure EdgeClient locked mode exclusion list with hostname containing underscore character ('_').
bugs.impact: Hostnames with underscore are not allowed in the list, and you can't whitelist them
bugs.workaround: Exclusion list feature for locked mode is also configurable using local registry on the client machine, registry configuration allows underscore characters. To add my_domain.com to the exclusion list please create registry key (key, not value) under key HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess\AlwaysConnected\Exclusions, e.g. HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess\AlwaysConnected\Exclusions\my_domain.com\
bugs.fix: Now admin UI allows you to specify underscore characters in Edge Client locked mode exclusion list

bugs.title: Argument of indirectly referenced eval() was not rewritten
bugs.symptoms: Errors indicated by web-application. Other potential symptoms include incorrect rendering for some pages and/or links not rewritten in web applications.
bugs.conditions: Using indirect references to native eval function in web-application code. For example. using a function in web-application's code similar to the following: function f(n) { var e = eval; return e(n); } f(some_text)
bugs.impact: Application does not work correctly via Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access supports calling eval() using indirect references. This improves web app compatibility.

bugs.title: Administrator users unable to access all partition via TMSH for AVR reports
bugs.symptoms: Using the TMSH for AVR reports can fail if it contains partition based entities, even with an administrator user (which should have permissions to all partitions).
bugs.conditions: Using the TMSH for querying partitioned based stats with an administrator user.
bugs.impact: AVR reports via TMSH will fail when using partition based entities.
bugs.fix: Allowing for administrator users to get all partitions available on query.

bugs.title: When using a route TMM may use a smaller MTU
bugs.symptoms: TMM uses a smaller MTU when connecting to a device via a configured route.
bugs.conditions: - Larger than 1500 bytes MTU configured on VLAN. - Static, or dynamically learned route, to a destination, with no specific MTU defined.
bugs.impact: Effective MTU when using the route will be limited to 1500 bytes. This includes derived MSS in TCP connections.
bugs.workaround: Specify the required MTU on routes.
bugs.fix: TMM now by default uses VLAN-configured MTU when using a route to a destination.

bugs.title: IPsec over iSession stops working after upgrading to 11.6.1 from 11.6.0
bugs.symptoms: IPsec over iSession stops working after upgrading from 11.6.0 to 11.6.1 or later.
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec over iSession configured. -- Upgrade from 11.6.0 to 11.6.1 or later.
bugs.impact: IPsec over iSession does not work. This occurs because beginning in 11.6.1, the anonymous IKE-peer is disabled by default. This prevents IPsec over iSession from working.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can configure the iSession configuration to use one sided iSession and IPsec to NAT traversal. For more information, refer to the Setting Up iSession and IPsec To Use NAT Traversal on One Side of the WAN chapter of the BIG-IP LTM BIG-IP TMOS: Tunneling and IPsec guide. Impact of workaround: Performing the suggested workaround should not have a negative impact on your system Note: The Quick Start : Symmetric Properties of the Configuration utility is considered obsolete due to the lack of support for IKEv2. Using the encapsulation option as outlined in the Setting Up iSession and IPsec To Use NAT Traversal on One Side of the WAN chapter of the BIG-IP LTM BIG-IP TMOS: Tunneling and IPsec guide is meant for demonstration purposes using low security defaults. This configuration is not recommended for use in production environments. Important: Configuring IPsec IKEv1 with the anonymous IKE-peer General Properties setting of State 'Enabled', can expose a known security vulnerability. This configuration should only be utilized when testing in a closed lab environment. For more information refer to: K10133477: BIG-IP IPsec IKE peer listener vulnerability

bugs.title: mcpd can crash if viewing a fast-growing log file through the GUI
bugs.symptoms: If the GUI tries to display a log file that is actively growing by thousands of log entries per second, the GUI might hang, and mcpd could run out of memory and crash.
bugs.conditions: The GUI tries to display a log file that is actively growing by thousands of log entries per second.
bugs.impact: mcpd crashes, and it and tmm restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the GUI to view a log file that is growing by thousands of log entries per second.

bugs.title: vCMP guest is unable to install a hotfix for block-device-images
bugs.symptoms: If a partial Hotfix image file is on the BIG-IP system, a vCMP guest may attempt to install that improper image file since that guest does not have access to a MD5 checksum verification. The most common error message encountered is 'Software compatibility tests failed.', which gives no indication of what actually went wrong. Other errors may be possible, depending on how the truncation/corruption affects installation.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP guest trying to install a hotfix image -- block-device-image installation started in vCMP guest -- Installing a hotfix when both a 'valid' hotfix image file and an 'invalid' hotfix image file exist on the system.
bugs.impact: Software installations might fail on vCMP guests with a confusing error.
bugs.workaround: Remove the corrupt image files from the BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Now, if a partial Hotfix image file exists on the BIG-IP system, a vCMP guest installs the correct software, or presents a meaningful error.

bugs.title: GSLB Pool Member Manage page fails to auto-select next available VS/WiP after pressing the add button.
bugs.symptoms: The combobox does not auto-select the next entry in the list of virtual servers/wide IPs after pressing the Add button and successfully adding an entry to the member list.
bugs.conditions: -- Have at least two entries in the combobox. -- Add one of the entries to the member list.
bugs.impact: The other entry is not selected automatically (as it was in BIG-IP versions 12.1 and earlier). Must manually select each entry to add to the member list. Loss of functionality from earlier releases.
bugs.workaround: Manually select each entry to add to the member list.
bugs.fix: Restored behavior that selects the next available entry in list after pressing the Add button on GSLB Pool's Member manage page.

bugs.title: Flows using DEFLATE decompresion can generate error message during flow tear-down.
bugs.symptoms: Repeated entries in the ltm log will show a completion-code error (comp_code=4) as in the following: Zip engine ctx eviction (comp_code=4): ctx dropped.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs when a flow that requests DEFLATE decompression is terminated when the compression engine is still in the middle of working on an incomplete DEFLATE block.
bugs.impact: False errors can appear: o In fields of tmctl rst_cause_stat table, false stats counters will increment for compression and packet errors. o Log entries with the "Zip engine... (comp_code=4)" appear in ltm log. Monitors observing the ltm log or stats in the tmctl rst_cause_stat table will see false positives.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware acceleration.
bugs.fix: A new tcl variable, nitrox::comp_suppress_itrunc, was added. It defaults to NO which yields legacy behavior. Setting it to YES causes comp_code=4 (ITRUNC) errors to not propagate as an error. To enable the feature, add the following line to /config/tmm_init.tcl: nitrox::comp_suppress_itrunc yes You will have to restart tmm for the change to take effect.

bugs.title: Upgrade to 13.0.0 on B2100/B2150 with IOMMU enabled prevents vCMP guests from starting
bugs.symptoms: vCMP guests will fail to start on B2100 and B2150 when the user had enabled the input/ output memory management unit (IOMMU) before upgrading.
bugs.conditions: * Run a pre-13.0.0 version of the software. * Run on a VIPRION B2100/B2150 blade. * Enable IOMMU before upgrading, using the following command: sys db kernel.iommu. * Upgrade to 13.0.0. * vCMP is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Cannot deploy vCMP guests.
bugs.workaround: Use the grub_open and grub_close commands to manually add "intel_iommu=on" to their kernel command line, as follows: ~$ grub_open /var/run/grub.conf.mdfy.24145 ~$ <edit the file above> ~$ grub_close
bugs.fix: Upgrade on VIPRION B2100/B2150 blades with IOMMU enabled no longer prevents vCMP guests from starting.

bugs.title: Downloading via APM tunnels could experience performance downgrade.
bugs.symptoms: Multiple DTLS records can be packed into one UDP packet. When packet size is too large, packet fragmentation is possible at IP layer. This causes high number of packet drops and therefore performance downgrade.
bugs.conditions: When downloading using APM tunnels.
bugs.impact: High number of packet drops and inferior performance.
bugs.fix: One DTLS record is now contained in each UDP packet to avoid packet fragmentation.

bugs.title: HSB transmitter failure may occur when global COS queues enabled
bugs.symptoms: An HSB transmitter failure may occur if global COS queues enabled. The HSB transmitter failure is logged in the TMM log files.
bugs.conditions: With global COS queues enabled, the HSB's watchdog loopback packets are sent on HSB ring 2, instead of ring 0. If HSB ring 2 is heavily utilized, this could cause the loopback packets to be dropped. If this occurs, then the watchdog may trigger an HSB transmitter failure.
bugs.impact: If this issue occurs then the BIG-IP is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: Do not use global COS queues.
bugs.fix: Loopback packet priority is now set during runtime to guarantee transmit on mgmt ring 0.

bugs.title: JavaScript challenge repeating in loop when URL has path parameters
bugs.symptoms: The JavaScript challenge is repeating in a loop on URLs which have path parameters (when the URL contains the ';' character). The request never reaches the back-end server. This happens in the following challenges: * Proactive Bot Defense with Suspicious Browsers enabled * Client-Side Integrity Defense In the rest of the challenges, the challenges will succeed, but POST requests will not be reconstructed correctly and sent as a multipart message to the back-end server.
bugs.conditions: URLs contain the ';' character, AND: Either: * Proactive Bot Defense with Suspicious Browsers enabled, OR * Client-Side Integrity Defense is enabled and is used as a DoSL7 mitigation during an attack.
bugs.impact: Requests with ';' character will be blocked and the browser will repeat the challenge in a loop.
bugs.fix: The JavaScript challenge no longer gets stuck in a loop on URLs which have path parameters.

bugs.title: SCTP: Multihome connections may not expire
bugs.symptoms: SCTP: Multihome connections may not expire when forcibly deleted.
bugs.conditions: When the multi-homing connections have been forcibly deleted from tmsh command.
bugs.impact: The multi-homing connections won't be expired.
bugs.workaround: Don't manually deleted the multi-homing connections.

bugs.title: TS cookie name contains NULL or other raw byte
bugs.symptoms: The TS cookie name may intermittently contain NULL.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently when ASM is provisioned and has a unique combination of security policy name and the server's cookie attributes (path and domain).
bugs.impact: False positives triggered on modified domain cookies.
bugs.workaround: To resolve this, change the policy security name.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the TS cookie name length.

bugs.title: Upgrade from 11.6.1 to 13.0.0 fails when two parameters in URL added to anti-fraud profile get 'identify-as-username enabled'.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade from 11.6.1 to 13.0.0 fails when two parameters in URL added to anti-fraud profile get 'identify-as-username enabled'. The system posts the following messages in /var/log/ltm: emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- 010719b4:3: URL can have only a single parameter identified as username in the Anti-Fraud profile '/Common/antifraud'. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Adding two parameters with 'identify-as-username enabled' using GUI.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails. Configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrade, check that every ANTIFRAUD URL has no more than one parameter with "identify as username" enabled. To do so, delete a parameter or disable "identify as username".

bugs.title: Verification of peer certificate chain may return incorrect result.
bugs.symptoms: When a certificate chain is made up of multiple certificates, the verification of the chain may be wrong.
bugs.conditions: This happens when the 'untrusted-cert-response-control' and 'expire-cert-response-control' are both set to 'ignore' on server SSL profile, and 'sys db tmm.ssl.servercert_softval' is 'enable'.
bugs.impact: When the condition matches, the 'SSL::verify_result' may return the wrong result.
bugs.fix: 'SSL::verify_result' returns the correct result.

bugs.title: BIG-IP i2x00 and ix4x00 platforms send LLDP, STP, and LACP PDUs with a VLAN tag of 0
bugs.symptoms: LACP, STP, and LLDP PDUs sent from either of the i2x00 or i4x00 platforms have a VLAN tag added to the PDU when they shouldn't.
bugs.conditions: Provision any of the three protocols: LLDP, STP, or LACP and the PDU sent by the BIG-IP will incorrectly have a VLAN tag with a tag-id of 0 added to the PDU.
bugs.impact: Some 3rd party devices may reject the packet. This will adversely affect operation of the affected protocol.
bugs.fix: This release ensures that the VLAN tag is stripped before the PDU is sent onto the wire.

bugs.title: DNS Express responses missing SOA record in NoData responses if CNAMEs present
bugs.symptoms: A valid NoData response can contain CNAMEs if a partial chase occurred without final resolution. DNS Express is not including the expected SOA record in this scenario.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS Express configured. -- Partial CNAME chase resulting in incomplete resolution.
bugs.impact: A valid DNS response with a a partial chase but missing the SOA record may not be considered authoritative due to the missing record.
bugs.fix: The SOA record is now included as appropriate.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when categorizing long URLs
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when categorizing long URLs.
bugs.conditions: URL categorization with long URLs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM now can handle really long URLs for URL categorization.

bugs.title: Required custom AVPs are not included in an RAA when reporting an error.
bugs.symptoms: Custom Attribute-Value-Pairs (AVPs) defined on the system will not be visible in a Re-Auth-Answer (RAA).
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- PEM enabled with Gx. -- Custom AVPs configured. -- PEM responds with an error code in an RAA against a Policy and Charging Rules Function (PCRF) triggered action.
bugs.impact: Lack of custom AVPs in such an RAA may result in loss of AVP dependent service.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Custom AVPs included regardless of an error code in an RAA.

bugs.title: Invalid "with the first highest ratio counter" logging for pool member ratio load balance
bugs.symptoms: Invalid value for "with the first highest ratio counter" for wideip load balancing decision is logged.
bugs.conditions: Enabled logging for wideip load balancing decision.
bugs.impact: Invalid value is logged for "with the first highest ratio counter".

bugs.title: Traffic-group failover-objects cannot be retrieved via iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: When issuing a GET you get the following error message: List property is not implemented! Detail [cm traffic-group failover-objects {...}]. (The ... represents the data that was presented as a list property.)
bugs.conditions: Trying to use iControl REST for getting failover-objects associated to floating traffic-groups
bugs.impact: No access to list of failover-objects associated to an specific floating traffic-group via the iControl REST interface
bugs.workaround: Use a different user interface (tmsh or GUI).
bugs.fix: Traffic-group failover-objects can now be retrieved via iControl REST

bugs.title: TMM crashes after changing VLAN tag to 'any'
bugs.symptoms: The VLAN tag cannot be modified to or from the value of 4096.
bugs.conditions: Modify VLAN tag from 4096 or to 4096.
bugs.impact: Cannot modify VLAN tag from 4096 or to 4096.
bugs.workaround: To modify the VLAN tag of an existing VLAN to or from the value of 4096, delete the VLAN and re-create it with the desired VLAN tag value.
bugs.fix: Validation now prevents changing to/from tag 'any' (4096) so this issue doesn't occur.

bugs.title: Need to re-provision vCMP after upgrading to 13.1.x or later on the BIG-IP 10350F platform
bugs.symptoms: With vCMP provisioned, upgrading to 13.1.x or later release will not enable IOMMU support after the upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading to 13.1.x or later. -- vCMP already provisioned. -- Running on the BIG-IP 10350F platform.
bugs.impact: Guests configured with FIPS functionality will fail to start until IOMMU is enabled.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Re-provision vCMP after the upgrade to enable IOMMU support. 1. Modify the value of the DB variable kernel.iommu to 'enable'. 2. Restart the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Oauth server is not registered in the map for HA addresses
bugs.symptoms: The same loopback address is assigned to two listeners.
bugs.conditions: -- AAA Servers with pool. -- OAuth Server.
bugs.impact: Traffic issues due loopback address that is assigned to OAuth Server, can be assigned to some other AAA Server that also uses pool.

bugs.title: Configuration validation (e.g., ConfigSync) may fail after an iRule is deleted, if the iRule made procedure calls
bugs.symptoms: Configuration validation fails spuriously, including potentially as a result of a ConfigSync or modifying an iRule, with an error similar to the following: 01020036:3: The requested rule (/Common/rule_uses_procs) was not found. Referencing an iRule that previously existed, but has been deleted (or is being deleted as a result of a ConfigSync).
bugs.conditions: -- iRule using procedures in a different iRule. -- iRule attached to virtual server.
bugs.impact: iRule procs are still referenced after deletion. Configuration validation fails spuriously.
bugs.workaround: Force reloading of the MCP binary database. For specific steps, see K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030).

bugs.title: Serverside SSL renegotiation does not occur after block cipher data limit is exceeded
bugs.symptoms: If you have a virtual server with a serverssl profile configured that serves large (>2GB) files, you may see these errors in /var/log/ltm: info tmm[17859]: 01260034:6: Block cipher data limit exceeded.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a serverssl profile is in use, and the server-side traffic exceeds 2GB.
bugs.impact: Serverssl renegotiation does not occur, log message is displayed.

bugs.title: SSLI statistic and Traffic classification statistic lost after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: If you upgrade from 13.0 to 13.1 (or above), SSLI and traffic classification statistis will be lost.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when upgrading SSLI from version 13.0.0
bugs.impact: SSLI and traffic classification statistic will be lost.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with statistics being lost during upgrade.

bugs.title: AVR caching mechanism not working properly
bugs.symptoms: The AVR caching mechanism fails to store dimension-based queries properly, which leads to incorrect reports.
bugs.conditions: Using AVR caching mechanism (turned-on by default).
bugs.impact: Reports will be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Using the following TMSH command should solve the problem: tmsh modify sys db avr.requestcache value disable * NOTE: the above might cause AVR to perform a bit slower.
bugs.fix: The system no longer stores the dimension-based queries in the AVR cache.

bugs.title: When tcp checksum set to software-only, automatically disable TCP Segmentation Offload
bugs.symptoms: TCP Segmentation Offload requires HW checksumming to be enabled. With HW checksum offload disabled, TSO needs to be disabled.
bugs.conditions: HW checksum disabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic might get lost
bugs.workaround: Manually disable TSO when disabling HW Checksum offload.
bugs.fix: Disabling HW checksum offload now disables TSO.

bugs.title: tmm core in iRule with unreachable remote address
bugs.symptoms: TCP::unused_port <remote_addr> <remote_port> <local_addr> [<hint_port>] with a non reachable remote_addr, tmm cores
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using TCP::unused_port in an iRule and the remote address is not reachable
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: create faux route for the destination address

bugs.title: Testing for connection to SMTP Server always returns "OK"
bugs.symptoms: When you click the SMTP GUI config "Test Connection" button it always gives green "OK" response, even if there is no network, or if the DNS response is NXDomain.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when testing the SMTP connection using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Validation of SMTP server availability is incorrect
bugs.workaround: You can test SMTP at the command line by attempting to send a test email, as in this example (substitute user@example.com with your valid email address): # echo "ssmtp test mail" | mail -vs "Test email" user@example.com
bugs.fix: The 'Test Connection' button for the SMTP server configuration reports errors as expected.

bugs.title: Attack Signatures do not mention 'Cookie' in Signature Scope field
bugs.symptoms: Attack Signatures that include Parameter/Cookies in their scope, do not mention 'Cookie' in Signature Scope field, on the Attack Signature Properties page.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the description of any Attack Signature that has Parameter/Cookie in its scope.
bugs.impact: The description lacks the word 'Cookie'. Because of this, you might be mislead and create faulty signatures.
bugs.fix: When filtering Attack Signature by Signature Scope that includes Parameter/Cookie property, The 'Cookie' property now appears.

bugs.title: Failure of mcpd during setup of HA communication
bugs.symptoms: -- The mcpd daemon exits and generates a core file. -- Communication fails between high availability (HA) peers.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while making configuration changes to HA configurations.
bugs.impact: The mcpd crashes and restarts. System operation pauses while mcpd restarts. HA (CMI) communication is not established.

bugs.title: Filterable rule's pools
bugs.symptoms: The list of pools on a policy rule cannot be filtered, and is unwieldy to use when there are a large number of pools.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when looking at the policy rule list and there are a large number of pools.
bugs.impact: Configurations containing many pools may result in time-consuming efforts to choose the appropriate pool.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is a cosmetic issue.
bugs.fix: Policy rule's pools can now be filtered.

bugs.title: TMM crash from a possible memory corruption.
bugs.symptoms: When APM resumes an iRule event from an asynchronous session data lookup, the resumption fails due to a bad memory access resulting in a crash.
bugs.conditions: The following must be true for this to happen: - APM provisioned and licensed. - Use of APM iRule events. - Session data lookup from iRule events.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None identified yet.
bugs.fix: Access to an invalid or stale Access session result from custom iRules no longer causes TMM crash.

bugs.title: RSASSA-PSS client certificates support in Client SSL
bugs.symptoms: Client certificate verification in BIG-IP v11.6.0 through 13.1.0 does not support client certificates that are signed using the RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm. Validation of such client certificates will fail.
bugs.conditions: - Client certificate signed with RSASSA-PSS algorithm. - Client Certificate is set to 'Required' in Client SSL profile. - Running any version from BIG-IP v11.6.0 through 13.1.0.
bugs.impact: SSL connections using client PSS certificates are rejected.
bugs.fix: Validation of client certificates that are signed using the RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm now completes successfully.

bugs.title: iControl REST query results in unexpected trailing space in a pool's monitor name
bugs.symptoms: When querying a pool's monitors via the REST API, there are unexpected trailing spaces in the monitor names.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the iControl REST command to look up a pool, e.g. GET /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/~Common~<poolname>
bugs.impact: The monitor contains a trailing a space in the result.

bugs.title: Display OCSP configuration change as warning message on the screen during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in v13.0.0, there is a configuration change that occurs on migration on OCSP stapling. The migration is gracefully handled during upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from older version (earlier than 13.0.0) to newer version (greater than, or equal to 13.0.0). -- There exists a clientSSL profile with OCSP stapling enabled.
bugs.impact: There are no warning messages, so you might not notice the configuration change during upgrade, which might lead to confusion.
bugs.fix: Instead of messages only in ltm.log, the system now displays the configuration changes as warning message during upgrade. These messages appear similar to the following warning mcpd[6094]: 0107185a:4: Warning generated, for version 13.1.0 or greater : Setting strict-responder-certificate-check to true in OCSP object (/Common/ocsp1) as its default value is changed to true. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading OCSP certificate validator (/Common/ocsp_https): Deprecating the OSCP certificate validator because its responder URL (https://responder.url) is not HTTP-based. notice mcpd[6094]: 01071bb6:5: Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl1) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_1.crt): successfully attached OCSP configuration (/Common/ocsp1) to the certificate (/Common/server_1.crt), and enabled OCSP stapling. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl2) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_2.crt): OCSP stapling is changed to disabled during upgrade - the certificate chain (/Common/c3d_ca.crt) is configured but is not a valid issuer of the certificate (/Common/server_2.crt). Please configure a valid issuer for the certificate or make sure that the certificate file contains its own issuer certificate. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl3) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_2.crt): OCSP stapling is changed to disabled during upgrade because the OCSP validator (/Common/ocsp_https) has been deprecated during upgrade. Please check previous warning messages or ltm logs for the deprecation reason. mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl4) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_1.crt): the clientSSL profile is now using /Common/ocsp1 for OCSP stapling instead of using /Common/ocsp3 because the certificate (/Common/server_1.crt) has been successfully associated with OCSP validator (/Common/ocsp1) during upgrade. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl5) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_2.crt): OCSP stapling is changed to disabled during upgrade - unable to find an HTTP-based OCSP responder's URL in the AIA (Authority Information Access) extension of the certificate (/Common/server_2.crt) or the configuration of the OCSP validator (/Common/ocsp3).
bugs.behavior: Instead of messages only in ltm.log, the system now displays the configuration changes as warning message during upgrade. These messages appear similar to the following warning mcpd[6094]: 0107185a:4: Warning generated, for version 13.1.0 or greater : Setting strict-responder-certificate-check to true in OCSP object (/Common/ocsp1) as its default value is changed to true. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading OCSP certificate validator (/Common/ocsp_https): Deprecating the OSCP certificate validator because its responder URL (https://responder.url) is not HTTP-based. notice mcpd[6094]: 01071bb6:5: Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl1) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_1.crt): successfully attached OCSP configuration (/Common/ocsp1) to the certificate (/Common/server_1.crt), and enabled OCSP stapling. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl2) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_2.crt): OCSP stapling is changed to disabled during upgrade - the certificate chain (/Common/c3d_ca.crt) is configured but is not a valid issuer of the certificate (/Common/server_2.crt). Please configure a valid issuer for the certificate or make sure that the certificate file contains its own issuer certificate. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl3) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_2.crt): OCSP stapling is changed to disabled during upgrade because the OCSP validator (/Common/ocsp_https) has been deprecated during upgrade. Please check previous warning messages or ltm logs for the deprecation reason. mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl4) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_1.crt): the clientSSL profile is now using /Common/ocsp1 for OCSP stapling instead of using /Common/ocsp3 because the certificate (/Common/server_1.crt) has been successfully associated with OCSP validator (/Common/ocsp1) during upgrade. warning mcpd[6094]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Upgrading ClientSSL (/Common/cssl5) CertKeyChain (/Common/server_2.crt): OCSP stapling is changed to disabled during upgrade - unable to find an HTTP-based OCSP responder's URL in the AIA (Authority Information Access) extension of the certificate (/Common/server_2.crt) or the configuration of the OCSP validator (/Common/ocsp3).

bugs.title: AVR doesn't display units for "Avg Read Latency" measurement
bugs.symptoms: AVR doesn't display units for 'Avg Read Latency'.
bugs.conditions: AVR, ASM, DoS, or AFM are provisioned.
bugs.impact: No units are displayed.
bugs.workaround: 1. edit the following file: /etc/avr/monpd/monp_disk_info_measures.cfg 2. add the following line at line 63: "units=microsecond" 3. restart monpd.
bugs.fix: Added units (microsecond) to AVR report.

bugs.title: No port configuration on the OAuth Client agent redirection uri
bugs.symptoms: Configuring port using number or session variable on the OAuth Client agent redirection URI is not allowed.
bugs.conditions: If HTTPS port is different from 443 then, redirection URI needs to specify port using port number or port session variable.
bugs.impact: OAuth Client redirection URI cannot be modified to contain custom HTTPS port number
bugs.workaround: Create a session variable containing both fqdn and custom port number and specify that in client redirection URI in OAuth Client agent.
bugs.fix: Now the OAuth Client agent redirection URI accepts session variables for configuration of hostname and port, for example: https://%{session.server.network.name}:%{session.server.network.port}/oauth/client/redirect’.

bugs.title: DES, 3DES and HIGH cipher string includes/excludes wrong ciphers
bugs.symptoms: When cipher string contains "DES", 3DES ciphers are also included. The keyword "3DES" does not impact the included/excluded ciphers. HIGH no longer includes 3DES ciphers.
bugs.conditions: Cipher string contains DES, 3DES and/or HIGH.
bugs.impact: Additional ciphers being offered to the client or ciphers not being omitted.
bugs.behavior: 3DES ciphers moved from "high" to "medium".

bugs.title: Classification memory allocation
bugs.symptoms: Classification library ('CE') allocates an extra 2 KB of memory per flow and never used it.
bugs.conditions: Classification and HTTP profile attached to Virtual Server.
bugs.impact: High memory footprint for heavily loaded systems.
bugs.workaround: Install latest Classification Update Package ('IM Package').
bugs.fix: The software now uses the latest Classification Update Package ('IM Package'), so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: SELinux warning messages regarding nsm daemon
bugs.symptoms: Receiving SELinux warning messages regarding nsm daemon when BFD is enabled, and deleting VLANs.
bugs.conditions: -- BFD enabled for any route-domain. -- Deleting VLANs.
bugs.impact: None. This warning message references actions that are extraneous for the nsm daemon.
bugs.fix: nsm no longer triggers SELinux warning messages with BFD enabled, and deleting VLANs

bugs.title: IP Intelligence: Policy diff doesn't work for categories
bugs.symptoms: no validation for existence of fields for a nested struct
bugs.conditions: create 2 policies. create difference in nested structs.
bugs.impact: compare policies with nested structs will not work as expected.
bugs.fix: add validation for existence of fields for a nested struct

bugs.title: MS RDP may not work thru native Application Tunnels on MacOS and Linux if user didn't specify credentials prior establishing the connection
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft Remote Desktop (MS RDP) may not work through native Application Tunnels on MacOS and Linux if there are no credentials specified prior to establishing the connection.
bugs.conditions: * Native applications tunnels are configured to use for MS RDP tunneling (MacOS and Linux). * Certificate of MS RDP backend is not always trusted by the keychain. * There are no credentials specified before establishing connection in remote desktop entry.
bugs.impact: MS RDP connection through Application Tunnels doesn't work.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: A. Specify credentials in the remote desktop entry. B. Mark the certificate of the remote backend as "always trust". C. Create a /etc/hosts entry alias for the required backend to point to localhost. Use this alias to access the remote backend to SSL layer accessible do not complain about certificate

bugs.title: Crash related to GTM monitors with long RECV strings
bugs.symptoms: gtmd core dump related to GTM monitors with long RECV strings.
bugs.conditions: Sufficiently large RECV (receive) string on a GTM Monitor.
