bugs.impact: Core dump. Traffic might be disrupted while gtmd restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue relating to a crash when a GTM monitor has a sufficiently large receive string configured.

bugs.title: Limits set in Server SSL Profile are not enforced if the server ignores BIG-IP's renegotiation ClientHello
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not act on the absence of renegotiation.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system acts as TLS client, a TLS server ignores renegotiation request. Finite TLS session data or time limits are configured in Server SSL Profile on the BIG-IP system. An example of such a TLS server is Apache/2.4.10 on Fedora Linux.
bugs.impact: Limits, such as data limits ("Renegotiate Size" in Server SSL) or time limits ("Renegotiate Period" in Server SSL) are not enforced with finite "Handshake Timeout".
bugs.fix: BIG-IP system acting as TLS client (Server SSL Profile) now shuts down the connection if a TLS server did not continue with TLS renegotiation within "Handshake Timeout" seconds after the ClientHello, corresponding to the renegotiation initiation, was sent by the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Multiple UDP/TCP packets packed into one DTLS Record
bugs.symptoms: The system converts the server provided packet into PPP buffers. These PPP packets are used to pack into DTLS records. Currently there is a limit of about 14 KB of DTLS records, such that the system can pack multiple PPP records into one DTLS record. However, creating bigger DTLS record can cause server IP Fragmentation. In the lossy environment, losing one IP fragment can cause the complete DTLS record to be lost, resulting in poor performance.
bugs.conditions: Multiple UDP/TCP packets packed into one DTLS Record.
bugs.impact: In networks with packet losses, the APM end-user application might suffer poor network performance.
bugs.fix: DTLS performance has been improved in lossy or high latency networks by optimizing the number of encoded ppp records inside of DTLS records.

bugs.title: qkview improvement for OVSDB management
bugs.symptoms: The user can configure ovsdb-server in the BIG-IP system to communicate with an OVSDB-capable controller. If the user wants the BIG-IP system to connect to an OVSDB-capable controller via a SSL connection, the user needs to configure a certificate and a certificate key in the TMSH command "sys management-ovsdb". Later on, if the user invokes qkview to collect system information, the configured certificate key can be collected in qkview.
bugs.conditions: The following conditions need to be met: - BIG-IP has the SDN services license. - The TMSH command "sys management-ovsdb" is set to "enabled". Note that this is set to "disabled" by default. - The TMSH command "sys management-ovsdb cert-key-file" is set to a certificate key. Note that this is set to "none" by default.
bugs.impact: If the user invokes qkview to collect system information, the certificate key configured in the command "sys management-ovsdb cert-key-file" will be collected in qkview.
bugs.workaround: If OVSDB management is currently set to "enabled" in the BIG-IP system, then the user can reset "sys management-ovsdb cert-file" and "sys management-ovsdb cert-key-file" to "none" before calling qkview to collect system information. In general, if OVSDB management has ever been set to "enabled", the user with the bash shell access can check if the file /var/run/openvswitch/BIG-IP_ovs_cert_key exists and delete it before calling qkview to collect system information.
bugs.fix: The certificate key configured in the "sys management-ovsdb" will not be collected when invoking qkview.

bugs.title: 'list cm device build' data is not synchronized correctly across a device trust group
bugs.symptoms: The output of 'tmsh list /cm device' shows different version/build numbers for different devices, although all devices in the device-group are running the same software version.
bugs.conditions: Running the following command to view build information on multiple devices: tmsh list /cm device.
bugs.impact: The output reports different version/build numbers for different devices, although all devices in the device-group are running the same software version. Shows different/misleading build information about hotfix/engineering hotfix status across the trust. Note: This information is displayed in the UI Device Management :: Devices screen.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Unsupported Power Supply Models Reported as 'Not-Present' When Inserted in 2xxx/4xxx/5xxx/7xxx/10xxx Series Platform
bugs.symptoms: Unsupported power supplies are misleadingly reported as "not-present" when inserted into the system even when power is actively supplied to them. For example, if a system had a valid AC PSU in slot #1 but an unsupported PSU in slot #2: #tmsh show sys hard|grep -A 4 Power Chassis Power Supply Status Index Status Current 1 up AC 2 not-present NA
bugs.conditions: -- A power supply unit that fits mechanically into the system but is not supported electrically is inserted and powered on. -- Inserted in 2xxx/4xxx/5xxx/7xxx/10xxx series platforms.
bugs.impact: Misleading information is given for the power supply as 'not-present' rather than 'unidentified'. System is in an unsupported electrical state and without power redundancy.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When an unsupported power supply is inserted into the system, it is now reported as 'unidentified'. In addition, a critical alarm will be raised to the LCD and written to the LTM log. For example, if a system had a valid AC PSU in slot #1 but an unsupported PSU in slot #2: # tmsh show sys hard|grep -A 4 Power Chassis Power Supply Status Index Status Current 1 up AC 2 unidentified NA The system reports the following critical alarm: critical 0x12a0059 Chassis power module 2 is unidentified.

bugs.title: 'mkdisk' utility can fail when creating bootable USBs on older running versions of BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Running the 'mkdisk' utility packaged with the BIG-IP ISO on older versions of BIG-IP (v11.4.X and earlier) fails with the following error: error: tm_install::RemovableDevice::FormatPartitioned - unable to parse version of 'sfdisk'
bugs.conditions: Run 'mkdisk' utility on v11.4.X or earlier, or any system where the output of '/sbin/sfdisk --version' has the form: sfdisk (util-linux <version>) rather than: sfdisk from util-linux <version>
bugs.impact: Unable to run 'mkdisk' utility on affected versions of BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Warning: This involves editing the contents of /sbin and remounting a system-critical read-only filesystem as read-write, so proceed with caution if you decide to try this. 1. Run 'mount -o remount,rw /usr' 2. Run 'mv /sbin/sfdisk /sbin/sfdisk.bin' 2. Create a shell wrapper script like this at /sbin/sfdisk: #!/bin/bash if [ "$1" == "--version" ]; then printf "sfdisk from util-linux 2.13.1" else /sbin/sfdisk.bin $@ fi
bugs.fix: 'mkdisk' utility no longer fails on older running versions of BIG-IP due to errors parsing 'sfdisk' version

bugs.title: ssmtp RewriteDomain setting is set to the empty string.
bugs.symptoms: The ssmtp RewriteDomain setting is set to the empty string. Therefore, the From address in any email sent by the BIG-IP has an empty domain.
bugs.conditions: This applies when the 'sys outbound-smtp rewrite-domain' setting is unset.
bugs.impact: It is difficult to determine the originating device for system email.
bugs.workaround: Set the 'sys outbound-smtp rewrite-domain' to the local hostname.
bugs.fix: The ssmtp RewriteDomain setting is no longer set to the empty string. If 'sys outbound-smtp rewrite-domain' is unset, no rewriting will occur and the From address will have the hostname as its domain.

bugs.title: fsck should not run during first boot on public clouds
bugs.symptoms: Although it is not needed, filesystem check runs during the first boot. This increases the boot time, especially for images that were created more than 180 days before the first boot, because twice year, booting up runs a more comprehensive fsck operation.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when booting up public cloud configurations of Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.impact: Potentially unacceptable long boot times.
bugs.fix: fsck does not run during first boot on public cloud configurations of VE. Running fsck is postponed until the second boot. If the more comprehensive fsck operation is required, it runs during the second boot as well.

bugs.title: DoS Visibility charts don't display information for dropped messages
bugs.symptoms: Collected information for dropped messages does not appear in the Security >> Reporting: DoS screens, and is not returned for REST-API queries.
bugs.conditions: When querying information about dropped messages, the returned value is '0', even when there were dropped messages.
bugs.impact: Dropped messages are not correctly reflected in the GUI and in the returned value for REST-API queries.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time

bugs.title: Using the REST API, making a change to an FQDN pool causes the pool member availability to become unknown.
bugs.symptoms: Using iControl REST, making a change to an FQDN pool member causes the pool member availability to become 'unknown'.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl REST, modify an existing pool member configured with an FQDN name. Note: This issue does not affect pool members configured to point directly at an IP address.
bugs.impact: The pool member status will show 'unknown'.

bugs.title: saml_sp_connector not properly deleted in a transaction that removes the saml resource and servers referring to it
bugs.symptoms: Cannot delete saml_sp_connector from a transaction even when all related objects are specified.
bugs.conditions: When deleting saml_sp_connector from a transaction along their associated objects.
bugs.impact: Cannot delete saml_sp_connector and associated objects.
bugs.workaround: Delete objects in the following order: SSOResource SSOSAMLConfig SPConnector
bugs.fix: The apm sso saml_sp_connector object can now be deleted from a transaction involving all the related objects regardless of the order in which the objects are specified.

bugs.title: The TCP autonagle feature is not supported in LTM Policy
bugs.symptoms: In the TCP profile, the auto-Nagle feature is not supported in LTM Traffic Policies.
bugs.conditions: -- Using auto-Nagle in the TCP profile. -- LTM Traffic Policies.
bugs.impact: The TCP auto-Nagle feature is not supported in LTM policies.
bugs.workaround: You can use iRules to enable or disable the TCP auto-Nagle feature.
bugs.fix: The TCP auto-Nagle feature is now supported in LTM Traffic Policies.
bugs.behavior: The TCP auto-Nagle feature is now supported in Traffic Policies.

bugs.title: Fragmented RADIUS messages may be dropped
bugs.symptoms: Large RADIUS messages may be dropped when processed by iRules.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a RADIUS message that exceeds 2048 bytes is processed by an iRule containing the RADIUS::avp command.
bugs.impact: The RADIUS message will be dropped, and an error will be logged that resembles: Illegal argument (line 1) (line 1) invoked from within "RADIUS::avp 61 "integer""
bugs.workaround: Remove RADIUS::avp commands from iRules processing large messages, or ensure that no RADIUS client or server will send large messages.

bugs.title: Intermittent failure to do a clean install on iSeries platforms from USB DVD-ROM
bugs.symptoms: Following the instructions at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13117 will occasionally fail on iSeries platforms, with the system being unable to find the installation media. If this happens, running the following command will fail. image2disk --instslot=HD1.1 --setdefault --nosaveconfig
bugs.conditions: This can occur on iSeries platforms while performing a clean installation.
bugs.impact: The /dev/cdrom softlink points to the virtual CD-ROM drive in iSeries platforms instead of the physical USB DVD-ROM drive. This prevents image2disk from automatically finding the installation media.
bugs.workaround: After the failure, while in MOS, determine USB CDROM device name, mount it, and tell image2disk specifically where it is: bash (try 'info') / > dmesg | grep "sr0\|sr1" sr0: scsi3-mmc drive: 62x/62x writer dvd-ram cd/rw xa/form2 cdda tray <-- cdrom name sr 6:0:0:0: Attached scsi CD-ROM sr0 sr1: scsi-1 drive sr 7:0:0:0: Attached scsi CD-ROM sr1 bash (try 'info') / > mount -r -t iso9660 /dev/srX /cdserver bash (try 'info') / > image2disk --instslot=HD1.1 --nosaveconfig /cdserver In the mount command, replace "/dev/srX" with whichever device is the physical drive.

bugs.title: buffer-max-packets default value is 0, not 10 as stated in tmsh documentation
bugs.symptoms: tmsh documentation of UDP profile option buffer-max-packets states: "Specifies ingress buffer packet limit. The default value is 10. Maximum allowed value is 255." Actual value by design is 0.
bugs.conditions: Viewing tmsh command line help for UDP profile option buffer-max-packets.
bugs.impact: Incorrect default value is stated.
bugs.workaround: The correct default value for UDP profile option buffer-max-packets is 0.
bugs.fix: Now, tmsh documentation of UDP profile option buffer-max-packets has been corrected to state: "Specifies ingress buffer packet limit. The default value is 0. Maximum allowed value is 255."

bugs.title: GUI LTM UDP profile missing Max Buffer Bytes and Max Buffer Packets setting
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to set the Max Buffer Bytes (buf_max_bytes) and Max Buffer Packets (buf_max_pkts) on a UDP profile.
bugs.conditions: Create/edit an LTM UDP profile via the GUI. The Max Buffer Bytes (buf_max_bytes) and Max Buffer Packets (buf_max_pkts) is not in the GUI.
bugs.impact: You cannot set the Max Buffer Bytes (buf_max_bytes) and Max Buffer Packets (buf_max_pkts) set in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: You need to use tmsh tool to set the Max Buffer Bytes (buf_max_bytes) and Max Buffer Packets (buf_max_pkts) values.
bugs.fix: Expose the Max Buffer Bytes (buf_max_bytes) and Max Buffer Packets (buf_max_pkts) values to be set in the GUI.

bugs.title: tzdata bug fix and enhancement update
bugs.symptoms: There have been changes to timezone data that impact tzdata packages: * Mongolia no longer observes Daylight Saving Time (DST). * The Magallanes Region of Chile has moved from a UTC-04/-03 scheme to UTC-03 all year. Starting 2017-05-13 at 23:00, the clocks for the Magallanes Region will differ from America/Santiago.
bugs.conditions: -- Mongolia during DST portion of the year. -- Comparing clock times in the America/Santiago zone with those in the Magallanes Region.
bugs.impact: Timezone data provided in tzdata will not match the area's time. Clocks for the Magallanes Region will differ from America/Santiago (its current timezone).
bugs.fix: To accommodate for Mongolia no longer observing DST, the new America/Punta_Arenas zone was created. Changes were also made to support other timezone changes. * The zone1970.tab file has been added to the list of files to be installed with the tzdata packages installation. Note: Users of tzdata are advised to upgrade tzdata to zdata-2017b-1.el6

bugs.title: Improve the detection of browsers used for web scraping
bugs.symptoms: Some browsers used for web scraping are not always detected.
bugs.conditions: This is when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.
bugs.impact: Some browsers used for web scraping are not detected and not reported in the logs.
bugs.fix: Improved the detection of browsers used for web scraping.

bugs.title: The commented-out sample functions in audit_forwarder.tcl are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: The commented-out sample "Transform" functions in audit_forwarder.tcl are not correct and should not be used.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to write your own Transform function in audit_forwarder.tcl using the examples.
bugs.impact: The Transform function may not work if the examples are followed.
bugs.workaround: Use the default Transform function as a starting point instead of one of the examples.
bugs.fix: Updated the example functions in audit_forwarder.tcl

bugs.title: tcp connect: errno and comm_point_tmm_recv_from messages
bugs.symptoms: When unbound (DNS cache) produces an error message, it's written to /var/log/ltm as a message from tmm. However, there is no indication that the message has anything to do with DNS caching. As a result of this issue, you might see errors similar to the following: -- err tmm5[14207]: tcp connect: errno 10 -- err tmm1[14244]: comm_point_tmm_recv_from failed: Software caused connection abort -- err tmm3[11846]: recvfrom failed
bugs.conditions: -- Unbound (DNS cache) produces an error message. -- Viewing these logged messages in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.impact: Some of these messages are benign, but there is no indication of that, or the associated functionality where the message was triggered. Difficulty troubleshooting the underlying issue.
bugs.fix: Logged messages now indicate their association with DNS cache. For example: -- info tmm4[19404]: DNScache: sending query -- info tmm4[19404]: DNScache: response for example.com. A IN

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing VPN traffic
bugs.symptoms: When processing certain types of VPN traffic TMM may crash
bugs.conditions: VPN connected
bugs.impact: TMM crash, resulting in a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when processing VPN traffic

bugs.title: iRule that uses ASM violation details may cause the system to reset the request
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule attempts to use the violation details such as attackSignature or MaliciousFingerprint, in some cases a legal request will be reset.
bugs.conditions: -- An ASM iRule that uses violation details is attached to the virtual server. -- The request contains the violation
bugs.impact: A legal request is being reset.
bugs.fix: iRule that uses ASM violation details no longer causes the system to reset the request.

bugs.title: Changed Format of RAM Cache REST Status output.
bugs.symptoms: The REST API returned cache contents in displayable form, not tagged field form.
bugs.conditions: Using REST API.
bugs.impact: Text must be parsed as if the caller plans to post-process it.
bugs.workaround: To present the data in some other format, the text can be displayed as is, but must be parsed as if the caller plans to post-process it.
bugs.fix: Now RAM Cache REST Status output is returned in field format, and must be parsed by a JSON parser and formatted for display. If you were using the previous format, you must now parse the JSON and re-format the data for display.
bugs.behavior: REST API calls for ramcache stats now returns data as formatted JSON.

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense JavaScript challenges may introduce high latencies and cause some browsers to display a blank page.
bugs.symptoms: When PBD and FP are both enabled, there is a very high client-side latency, especially on Microsoft Internet Explorer version 11 (IE11). On IE11, sometimes the challenge remains on a blank page, never moving on to the site from the back-end server.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP system has Proactive Bot Defense and fingerprinting enabled. -- The client is using IEll. Note: IE11 is known to be affected by this issue. However, other browsers may also be affected.
bugs.impact: Delay or blank page when clients access the page using IE11.
bugs.fix: Improved the client-side run-time of the JavaScript challenge and prevented it from getting stuck on Internet Explorer.

bugs.title: iApp LX app does not sync to standby in a HA pair
bugs.symptoms: Take two BIG-IPs. Install some iApp LX package individually on each device. Then, join the devices as an Active/Standby Device Services Clustering pair. The iApps that created with that package may not be synced from the Active to the Standby. You will see this error in restjavad.0.log: [WARNING] Failed to post to http://localhost:8100/shared/iapp/global-installed-packages: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Duplicate item. Key already exists
bugs.conditions: An iApp LX package was installed on two devices *before* those devices were joined into a Device Group.
bugs.impact: The standby device is missing critical iApp data.
bugs.workaround: To avoid this situation, join devices in a Device Group before installing packages. When the situation has not been avoided, to synchronize the standby device, run these two commands on it: 1. restcurl /shared/iapp/global-installed-packages -X DELETE 2. restcurl /shared/gossip -d '{"copyStateFrom":"1.2.3.4"}' For the IP address in command 2, use the Management address of the active device.

bugs.title: Support AES-GCM acceleration in Nitrox PX wlite VCMP platforms
bugs.symptoms: In Nitrox PX platforms, vCMP guests can't accelerate AES-GCM traffic, which might cause high CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: For those vCMP guests deployed on Nitrox PX-based platforms, and SSL cipher is configured to use AES-GCM. The following blades support the Nitrox PX and vCMP combination: VIPRION B4200, B4300, B2100, and B2150 blades.
bugs.impact: High CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Added AES-GCM hardware acceleration support for Nitrox PX-based vCMP.

bugs.title: iSession APM virtual server changes port if connection has forwarding virtual server with defined IP and wild card port
bugs.symptoms: iSession does not use the correct port when connecting to a specific (not-wildcard), layered virtual server listening on all ports.
bugs.conditions: -- Present forwarding virtual server after APM. -- A forwarding virtual server with a defined IP address and wildcard port.
bugs.impact: Connection is made using an unexpected port.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: -- Define a forwarding virtual server with a wildcard listener for IP address and wildcard port. -- Define a forwarding virtual server with a specific IP address and port.

bugs.title: REST asynchronous tasks permissions issues
bugs.symptoms: When running an asynchronous task via the iControl REST API (e.g., /mgmt/tm/task/sys/ucs), the task may get run as an incorrect user. This is not too problematic if both users have the same set of permissions. However, if one is a read-only user (for example a user named 'tmtstatus' that collects statistics), this results in the asynchronous task failing when one of these user-mixed problems appear. The system posts a message similar to the following: notice icrd_child[25185]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=29185 user=tmtstatus folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Syntax Error: "ucs" unexpected argument] cmd_data=save sys ucs
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently when running asynchronous tasks over REST.
bugs.impact: The task may get run as the wrong user and result in an error.
bugs.fix: Asynchronous tasks via the iControl REST API now handle these multiple user conditions.

bugs.title: DNS transparent cache can return non-recursive results for recursive queries
bugs.symptoms: If a non recursive query is cached by the DNS transparent cache, subsequent recursive queries provide the non-recursive answer.
bugs.conditions: DNS transparent cache that receives a non-recursive query whose result is stored in the cache.
bugs.impact: Non recursive responses for recursive requests.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be attached to the listener to disable the cache if the "rd bit" is not set in the DNS request.
bugs.fix: The RD bit is now handled as expected. If a recursive request is received, a non-recursive cached entry is ignored, and replaced, when the recursive request is answered.

bugs.title: The TMM on the next-active panics with message: "Missing oneconnect HA context"
bugs.symptoms: The next-active TMM panics with message: "Missing oneconnect HA context" on a virtual which doesn't have one-connect on the active.
bugs.conditions: A mirrored virtual is configured with one-connect on the next-active but no one-connect profile is present on the active. This can occur when the config-sync connection between peers is down or auto-sync on the device group is disabled. The next-active expects a one-connect HA context but the active does not send it.
bugs.impact: Connections on the active are not mirrored while the next-active restarts.
bugs.workaround: Resolving configuration differences between the active and next-active will prevent this panic.
bugs.fix: Mirrored connections which fail to find an HA context on the next-active are not established on the next-active.

bugs.title: pkcs11d restart due to the leakage of file descriptors with unsupported Thales client 11.5
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP is leaking file descriptors. After reaching the limit, one needs to restart pkcs11d to make it work again.
bugs.conditions: 1. Access to Thales netHSM changes from accepted to denied. 2. LTM uses Thales software version 11.50.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP is leaking file descriptors and after reaching the limit one needs to restart pkcs11d to make it working again.
bugs.workaround: Use the supported version combination as stated at https://support.f5.com/kb/en-us/products/big-ip_ltm/manuals/product/f5-thales-hsm-version-interoperability-matrix.html

bugs.title: Invalid Hash More setting hash persistence profile
bugs.symptoms: On the Hash persistence profile, there is an option 'Hash More' which is available in the GUI. This setting is not valid.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the Hash persistence profile in the GUI.
bugs.impact: This setting is not valid. There is no impact because the setting is non-functional, but might be confusing.
bugs.fix: The invalid option 'Hash More' has been removed from the Hash persistence profile.

bugs.title: Creation or reconfiguration of iApps will fail if logging is configured
bugs.symptoms: If logging destination of any type is configured (ArcSight, IPFIX, remote high speed logging, etc.), creation or reconfiguration of iApps will fail. The following error will be reported in /var/log/webui.log and displayed in the GUI: The connection to mcpd has been lost, try again.
bugs.conditions: Logging is configured: filter, destination, and publisher.
bugs.impact: Cannot create new iApps or reconfigure existing ones.
bugs.workaround: Remove logging configuration.
bugs.fix: Can now create or reconfigure iApps if logging is configured.

bugs.title: TMM core after a switchover involving GY quota reporting
bugs.symptoms: Core dump in the code path for async subscriber lookup causes core-dump.
bugs.conditions: This core happens in an intra-chassis HA configuration, if GY is configured & HA switchover is forced.
bugs.impact: An initial coredump (or HA switchover) forces multiple core dumps. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: After upgrade to v13.0.0, users may be met with a javascript error on the logon page or other APM pages
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP APM v13.0.0 has modified javascript to better handle more flexible session timeout parameters. This necessitated a modification in the timeout code in APM. Unfortunately, that means that after upgrade, your users may receive a script error: 'APMSessionTimeout is undefined' when using the F5 Edge Client, or when using a browser that has the old code cached.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to BIG-IP APM v13.0.0 with a login page or other Policy Item that presents a GUI to end users connecting using the F5 Edge Client or a browser with the previous version's timeout javascript code cached.
bugs.impact: Users receive confusing script errors in Edge Client or their web browser.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds. Note: If possible, use the first one. Only perform the manual workaround if the first one is not possible. -- Check the Knowledgebase Article (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K91200585) to determine available fix versions, and then contact F5 Networks Technical Support to obtain any available Engineering Hotfix or version Hotfix to address this issue. -- Perform this manual workaround: First, locate the items such as Logon Page and add a '?13' after the include for session_check.js. For example, the following steps: 1. Logon to the GUI as Admin. 2. Click Profiles/Policies :: Customization :: Advanced. 3. Navigate to your Access Policy. 4. Navigate to Access Policy, then to the page that has the issue, such as Logon Page. Note: The page is "logon.inc" for a logon page. 5. Locate the following line: <script language="JavaScript" src="/public/include/js/session_check.js" ></script>. 6. Insert ?13 after session_check.js in the script language line, for example: <script language="JavaScript" src="/public/include/js/session_check.js?13" ></script>. 7. Click Save Draft. 8. Click Save. Note: Using the specific text "13" in "?13" isn't critical; it just must be some text.
bugs.fix: End users with Edge Client or other browser no longer receive javascript errors.

bugs.title: massive prints in tmm log: "could not find conf for profile crc"
bugs.symptoms: Massive messages in tmm log: "could not find conf for profile crc" messages are shown while traffic is passing.
bugs.conditions: 1. Have dos profile attached to vs. dos profile does not have dos application enabled. 2. Have ASM policy attached to VS with Web Scraping on/session hijacking/session awarness with DID collection/brute force with DID collection.
bugs.impact: Massive prints in tmm log that can cause tmm to abort. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Have DOS application enabled (even if doing nothing).
bugs.fix: disable prints.

bugs.title: FTP data connection may use incorrect auto-lasthop settings.
bugs.symptoms: Due to known issue FTP data connection may fail to use auto-lasthop settings configured on the virtual server and use a value configured on VLAN level instead.
bugs.conditions: With the configuration below, FTP data connection will fail to use auto-lasthop: (1) - Global auto-lasthop set to 'disable' - VLAN auto-lasthop set to 'default' - Virtual server auto-lasthop set to 'enable' (2) - Global auto-lasthop set to 'disable' - VLAN auto-lasthop set to 'disable' - Virtual server auto-lasthop set to 'enable' With the configuration below, FTP data connection will improperly use the auto-lasthop: (1) - Global auto-lasthop set to 'enable' - VLAN auto-lasthop set to 'default' - Virtual server auto-lasthop set to 'disable' (2) - VLAN auto-lasthop set to 'enable' - Virtual server auto-lasthop set to 'disable'
bugs.impact: FTP data connection may fail to be established.
bugs.workaround: Use routing instead of auto-lasthop. (or) Enable auto-lasthop on VLAN level.

bugs.title: Sensitive information exposed during incremental sync
bugs.symptoms: A device group using incremental sync may not properly handle values that should be protected by Secure Vault.
bugs.conditions: A device group configured to use incremental sync.
bugs.impact: Some values that should be protected by Secure Vault are not encrypted as expected.
bugs.fix: Secure configuration values are encrypted as expected.

bugs.title: SSL/TLS-based monitors now use ServerSSL profiles
bugs.symptoms: The configuration of SSL/TLS-based monitors might differ from how SSL/TLS is configured for other objects, such as SSL/TLS-based virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: This applies to SSL/TLS-based monitors.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent configuration.
bugs.fix: In this release, instead of specifying ciphers, certificates, keys, and SSL options via explicit parameters, an SSL-based monitor (HTTPS/TCP plus SSL) is configured with a ServerSSL Profile. This profile contain all of the necessary settings. The ciphers, certificates, and keys are directly analogous to the those in the previous method of monitor configuration. SSL/TLS options may be specified in a more fine-grained fashion than the previous method, which enabled all compatibility options, or disabled all of them.
bugs.behavior: Previous versions of LTM monitors used explicit SSL/TLS settings for ciphers, certificates, and keys, as well as whether to enable compatibility options. In all prior releases, SSL options on HTTPS monitors were specified explicitly. With this change, HTTPS monitors get their SSL options from a named Server SSL Profile. The following options are retrieved from the profile: -- Cipher string or cipher group. -- Optional certificate and/or key. -- SSL Options. In prior releases, a compatibility flag could be enabled or disabled. When enabled, it turned on all SSL compatibility options; when disabled, all were turned off. With this change, individual SSL options can be specified in the profile.

bugs.title: 'tmsh show sys memory raw' command shows a slow build up of memory usage.
bugs.symptoms: The usage of istats_incr and istats_set commands do not release memory used during the processing of those commands. TMM might eventually core.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure SSL Orchestrator. -- Use istats_incr and istats_set commands.
bugs.impact: Heap memory usage goes up. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The usage of istats_incr and istats_set commands now release memory used during the processing of those commands, so TMM no longer cores.

bugs.title: memory leak on non-primary bigd with changing node IPs
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP systems with the multiple blades, or a BIG-IP system with multiple bigd processes running (bigd.1, bigd.2, etc.), if the system has FQDN nodes configured, all secondary bigd processes will consume an unusually high amount of memory, and bigd cores may exist when the FQDN node IP addresses change frequently.
bugs.conditions: FQDN nodes configured on a system, and the system (as a whole) has multiple bigd processes running, either across multiple blades or multiple bigd instances on a single blade. As configuration changes are made to FQDN nodes causing IP addresses to change, bigd on the non-primary places memory consumption may be unusually high.
bugs.impact: bigd memory leak; possible bigd crash.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: use static IP nodes and pool members rather than FQDN.

bugs.title: RFE to support AVR reporting for FW NAT translations
bugs.symptoms: Prior to 14.0 release, FW NAT translation events are logged (if enabled) but were not reported using AVR infrastructure (similar to CGNAT module)
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned and Firewall NAT configured.
bugs.impact: FW NAT users (new or migrating from CGNAT) would not have the ability to see AVR reports for various translation events. This may make NAT troubleshooting and/or NAT capacity planning difficult.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: AVR reporting is now available for AFM NAT feature.

bugs.title: LTM Policy error when rule names contain slash (/) character
bugs.symptoms: Beginning with v12.0.0, there has been additional validation for LTM Policy rule names to allow only certain valid characters. Prior to v13.1.0, the slash (/) character was included in the set of valid characters. But because the slash character is used as a delimiter in the BIG-IP virtual path hierarchy (e.g., /Common/my_policy/my_rule), extra slashes in a rule name causes validation problems because the rule appears to the system as having additional path segments.
bugs.conditions: LTM Policy rule contains the slash (/) character.
bugs.impact: Configuration will not load. Configuration may load, but admin GUI may not show policy rule.
bugs.workaround: In the bigip.conf file, the LTM Policy rule names can be manually edited to either remove the illegal character or to substitute a valid character. For example, the following policy won't load because the rule name contains a slash (/) character: ltm policy mypolicy { ... rules { /testperson/a { ... } But it will load when the slash (/) characters are changed to a legal character, such as underscores (_): ltm policy mypolicy { ... rules { _testperson_a { ... }
bugs.fix: For upgraded configurations, the roll-forward process will automatically translate slash (/) to underscore (_) in LTM Policy rule names. When creating new rules, validation will not succeed if a rule name contains an illegal character, such as a slash, so the issue will be prevented.

bugs.title: ReqLog profile on FTP virtual server with default profile can result in service disruption.
bugs.symptoms: When FTP's control channel and data channel arrive on different TMMs, ReqLog profile may fail to identify data channel's listener.
bugs.conditions: Default inherit FTP profile virtual server configured with ReqLog profile.
bugs.impact: Service disruption, fail-over event.
bugs.workaround: Create non-inheriting FTP profile for FTP virtual server with ReqLog profile.
bugs.fix: ReqLog now successfully finds appropriate listener.

bugs.title: HSB continually logs 'loopback ring 0 tx not active'
bugs.symptoms: In the TMM log files, HSB reports that 'loopback ring 0 tx not active'.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: Excessive logging. This may also cause an HSB lockup to not be detected.
bugs.fix: HSB no longer continually logs 'loopback ring 0 tx not active'.

bugs.title: The Dashboard does not show an alert when a power supply is unplugged
bugs.symptoms: The TMUI Dashboard's alert panel will not show any warning if the cord to one of the power supplies is unplugged.
bugs.conditions: One of the power supplies is unplugged.
bugs.impact: Watching the Dashboard will not alert the administrator to an unplugged power supply.

bugs.title: Security hardening of qkview
bugs.symptoms: qkview may collect sensitive information from BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Collecting qkview.
bugs.impact: qkview may collect sensitive information.
bugs.fix: qkview no longer collects sensitive information

bugs.title: Parsing certain URIs may cause the TMM to produce a core file.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may produce a core file while parsing URIs.
bugs.conditions: TMM may produce a core file while parsing URIs.
bugs.impact: TMM produces core file and failover.
bugs.fix: The TMM is more robust when parsing URIs.

bugs.title: tmm may restart when SAML SLO is initiated by SP using redirect binding
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured as SAML SP, there are two bindings supported for SLO profile: HTTP-Redirect and HTTP-POST (default option). If the BIG-IP system is configured to initiate SAML SP SLO profile with redirect binding - tmm may restart.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure the BIG-IP system as SAML SP. -- Configure HTTP-Redirect binding for SLO profile. -- Initiate SLO on SAML SP.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the BIG-IP system to use HTTP-POST binding for SLO profile. Configuration should be changed on IDP connector objects.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer restarts when SAML SLO is initiated by SP using redirect binding.

bugs.title: tmipsecd down after provisioning modules
bugs.symptoms: After provisioning a set of modules, tmipsecd may not be running.
bugs.conditions: After provisioning a set of modules.
bugs.impact: IPsec would not be operational.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmipsecd by running the following command: bigstart start tmipsecd.

bugs.title: eventd crashes during boot
bugs.symptoms: eventd may crash during boot due to heap corruption.
bugs.conditions: This happens during subscription and unsubscription of events.
bugs.impact: eventd crashes.
bugs.fix: Race condition has been resolved, so eventd no longer crashes.

bugs.title: Issues with Password Policy when expired passwords changed via command line
bugs.symptoms: Expired passwords when changed via command line caused certain password policy properties such as password expiration and password warning to get reset to zero.
bugs.conditions: -- Change expired password from command line (console or SSH)
bugs.impact: Certain password policy properties such as password expiration and password warning get reset to zero.
bugs.workaround: Subsequent password change via any of the management interfaces will set the affected password policy properties back to their correct values.
bugs.fix: Password properties are now handled consistency between the GUI and command line.

bugs.title: DoS Network, SIP and DNS logs in the GUI do not show destination address and port
bugs.symptoms: The destination address and port were not showing up on DoS Network, SIP and DNS logs the UI.
bugs.conditions: Viewing DoS Network, SIP and DNS logs in the GUI.
bugs.impact: The destination address and port do not show up in the GUI error logs.
bugs.fix: The destination address and port will now show up on the UI error logs for DoS DNS, SIP and Network.

bugs.title: tmsh list ltm node does not return an error when node does not exist
bugs.symptoms: TMSH does not post an error message in response to the tmsh command to list a specific, non-existent LTM node, or when listing a set of non-existent nodes using regular expressions.
bugs.conditions: -- Running the command: tmsh list ltm node. -- Running a regular expression to list a set of nodes. -- The specified node does not exist.
bugs.impact: The command produces no output or error message. No indication of why there is no output, nor is there a description of the possible error condition.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: TMSH now posts the appropriate, node-not-found error message when LTM nodes do not exist when running the command: tmsh list ltm node.

bugs.title: VCMP statistic for tmctl vcmp_stat n3_core_mask may be incorrect
bugs.symptoms: When switching a vCMP guest ssl-mode from dedicated to shared, the tmctl vcmp_stat n3_core_mask does not always reflect the change correctly. Note: Only the stat being reported by tmctl is wrong; the feature is still working properly.
bugs.conditions: vCMP system with one or more guests that the hypervisor admin switches the ssl-mode between shared and dedicated.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. This stat is used only for debugging.

bugs.title: When mcpd on a secondary blade crashes, after it comes back up, the virtual_disk entries are missing for that blade
bugs.symptoms: vCMP virtual disk images may appear to be missing according to the BIG-IP system (hypervisor), even though the disk images still exist.
bugs.conditions: MCPD on a secondary blade restarts, but vcmpd does not restart.
bugs.impact: This can cause confusion when looking at the hypervisor.
bugs.workaround: Restart vcmpd.

bugs.title: bigd may core on non-primary bigd when FQDN in use
bugs.symptoms: When using FQDN node/pool member resolution, a non-primary bigd process may core under certain circumstances. A non-primary bigd is any process instance other than zero in a multi-bigd scenario, or any bigd process on a non-primary blade in a chassis.
bugs.conditions: FQDN is in use.
bugs.impact: bigd may core and be restarted in a loop, causing some monitor instances to not be serviced. This may cause node/pool member flapping, or may cause certain nodes or pool members to be effectively not monitored.
bugs.workaround: Use static IPs instead of FQDN for node/pool member address assignment.
bugs.fix: Known causes of the bug have been fixed.

bugs.title: XML sensitive data masks the whole parameter value when it is in a parameter context
bugs.symptoms: When XML payload is in a parameter and a sensitive entity exists, the whole parameter value is masked.
bugs.conditions: -- Send XML request. -- The XML payload is in a parameter -- A sensitive entity exists.
bugs.impact: Cannot view the other information in the event logs apart from the sensitive entity.

bugs.title: Changes to the HTTP profile do not trigger validation for virtual servers using that profile
bugs.symptoms: Changing the HTTP profile does not trigger validation for virtual servers, so no inter-profile dependencies are checked.
bugs.conditions: Using an HTTP profile with a virtual server that uses other profiles that have settings that are mutually exclusive with those of the HTTP profile.
bugs.impact: The system will be in an invalid state. One immediate way this can be seen is when syncing to a peer. The sync operation does not complete as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use the error messages in the logs to determine how to change the configuration to return the system to a valid state.
bugs.fix: Changing the HTTP profile now triggers validation of all virtual servers using that profile.

bugs.title: ASM policy history GUI Validation Errors
bugs.symptoms: Empty extractions are not removed when deleting URL or filetype in ASM policies.
bugs.conditions: -- Create extraction with filetype. -- Remove filetype from allowed filetypes list.
bugs.impact: Empty extraction remains. This is benign, it does not affect enforcement on the policy.
bugs.fix: Empty extractions are now removed along with URL or filetype in ASM policies.

bugs.title: /shared/em/ssl.crt are not collected as part of qkview
bugs.symptoms: Enterprise Manager (EM) pushes certificates to /shared/em/ssl.crt on the BIG-IP system. In previous versions, qkview collected these certs. These certs are required to debug EM-related issues. In versions 12.x.x, these certs are not collected.
bugs.conditions: Running qkview on a BIG-IP system. Running versions 12.x.x.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Qkview does not include these additional certificates from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Qkview again collects the certificates that Enterprise Manager (EM) pushes to /shared/em/ssl.crt on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: IP addresses may appear "Aggregated" in "COMMON" section of dashboard but not Aggregated when applying module-specific filter
bugs.symptoms: Some IP addresses may appear as "Aggregated" in the "COMMON" section of the dashboard but not Aggregated when applying a module-specific filter. This occurs because lack of memory space causes information to be aggregated in the "COMMON" section before being aggregated in the module-specific DB.
bugs.conditions: A lot of diverse traffic (for some module) from many IP addresses (for example) on a system with a small amount of memory allocated for AVR.
bugs.impact: User sees a specific number (x) of IP addresses upon landing on the dashboard with "Aggregated" IP addresses, but when selecting a module-specific filter, statistics show a number plus another number (x+y) IP addresses (that is, essentially not aggregated).
bugs.workaround: Provision more memory to AVR.
bugs.fix: With this fix, aggregation does not happen in COMMON before it happens in the specific module. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: queue full dropped messages incorrectly counted as responses
bugs.symptoms: negative number of active response messages reported on sipsession profile stats
bugs.conditions: If a request message is dropped because the sip filter's ingress message queue is full, the wrong stats is incremented
bugs.impact: Counting the dropped request messages as response messages causes the calculation of the accepted response messages to be incorrectly calculated, thus producing a negative value.
bugs.fix: correct stats fields are incremented

bugs.title: bigd can crash when a DNS response does not match the expected value
bugs.symptoms: bigd can crash when a response returned from a DNS request does not match the expected value.
bugs.conditions: Monitoring DNS server(s), or using FQDN.
bugs.impact: Potential bigd core and restart; may cause endless restart loop as long as DNS monitor instance is configured.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Prevented bigd from crashing when a response returned from a DNS request does not match the expected value.

bugs.title: Orphaned bigd instances may exist (within multi-process bigd)
bugs.symptoms: When multi-process 'bigd' is configured, orphaned 'bigd' instances may be exit; such as an orphaned 'bigd.1' alongside the active 'bigd.1'.
bugs.conditions: -- db variable Bigd.NumProcs to 2 or higher. -- System monitors with long timeouts (such as ~183 seconds or longer), might also be relevant. When 'bigd' manages monitor configurations that results in no monitoring activity for a long time (such as due to long monitor timeouts), the operating system may temporarily suspend (and later resume) the 'bigd' process. The system might treat the 'bigd' process as if it were "hung", and start another 'bigd' instance without explicitly terminating the suspended 'bigd' process.
bugs.impact: The suspended 'bigd' process consumes process memory. The process might be suspended (consuming no CPU resources), or running, which might result in "double-monitoring" the resources assigned to that 'bigd' process. Note: If double-monitoring occurs, monitor status should be correct, but the double-monitoring unnecessarily consumes extra resources.
bugs.workaround: Configure 'bigd' to run as a single process. To do so, set the db variable Bigd.NumProcs to 1. Shortening monitor timeouts can reduce the possibility of a 'bigd' process being (temporarily) suspended by the operating system.
bugs.fix: Multi-process 'bigd' no longer produces orphaned (suspended) process instances.

bugs.title: Passive mode and untagged frames
bugs.symptoms: When port is configured in passive mode, to handle untagged frames, the system requires a VLAN to be configured on the system.
bugs.conditions: -- When port is operating in passive mode. -- Handling untagged frames.
bugs.impact: Must define a VLAN to process untagged data received on port operating in Passive mode. Might impact system performance.
bugs.workaround: Use the following procedure: 1. Create a VLAN. 2. Assign passive mode port as an untagged member of the VLAN.

bugs.title: IPv6 host traffic may use incorrect IPv6 and MAC address after route updates
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 traffic generated from the host, either from a host daemon, monitors, or from the command line, may use an MAC and IPv6 source address from a different VLAN.
bugs.conditions: - Multiple vlans with IPv6 configured addresses. - Multiple routes to the same destination, either the same or more specific, default routes, etc. that cover the traffic destination. - Changes in routes that will cause the traffic to the destination to shift from one vlan and gateway to another. This can be typically observed with dynamic routing updates.
bugs.impact: Traffic to the destination may fail due to using incorrect source IPv6/MAC address. This may cause monitor traffic to fail.
bugs.workaround: Continuous traffic to the IPv6 link-local nexthops can avoid this issue. This may be achieved by a script or an external monitor pinging the nexthop link-local address using the specific vlan.
bugs.fix: IPv6 host traffic no longer use incorrect IPv6 and MAC address after route updates.
bugs.behavior: Introduction of sys db ipv6.host.router_probe_interval, to control sysctl net.ipv6.conf.default.router_probe_interval value. This value is default to 5s.

bugs.title: SPI fields of IPsec ike-sa, byte order of displayed numbers rendered incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: When checking the SPI fields of an IKEv2 IPsec SA, the byte order of the displayed number is rendered incorrectly. The SPI details are seen in "tmsh show net ipsec ike-sa all-properties". For example, the BIG-IP will render this: Spi(local): 0x3c4742cab016098c Spi(Remote): 0x959f0a013581e25d When the actual SPIs viewed on the peer device are: Local spi: 5DE28135010A9F95 Remote spi: 8C0916B0CA42473C
bugs.conditions: IKEv2 IPsec SAs are established or attempting to be established.
bugs.impact: Can confuse a BIG-IP Administrator who is attempting to verify that IPsec peers have the same SAs.
bugs.workaround: Rearrange the SPI numbers manually or examine the ipsec.log to see the established SA SPI numbers.
bugs.fix: The correct SPI numbers are displayed when running the "tmsh show net ipsec ike-sa all-properties" command. Note that this command only shows IKEv2 SAs.

bugs.title: [Chrome] Web application's pop up window is blank
bugs.symptoms: Web application's pop up window is blank
bugs.conditions: Web application code opens new window and then populates it using document.write()
bugs.impact: Web application malfunction is likely
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used
bugs.fix: APM Portal Access now successfully handles document.write() in new open window.

bugs.title: GUI: When configuring Gx protocol profile message, not able to keep Subscriber Attribute value empty.
bugs.symptoms: User can not configure Gx protocol profile message from GUI with empty Subscriber Attribute.
bugs.conditions: When trying to create Subscription-Id-Type and specifying default value, there is no way in the GUI to keep Subscriber Attribute field empty when creating a new Gx Message. The field is always pre-filled with first subscriber attribute from the list - while there should be option of empty value. The help of default value says - The subscriber attribute has precedence over the default value. And indeed, the value of this attribute is influenced by the Subscriber Attribute chosen and default value is not used.
bugs.impact: User can not configure Gx protocol profile message from GUI with empty Subscriber Attribute. The subscriber attribute is always set to one of the attributes in the dropdown list.
bugs.workaround: User can configure Gx protocol profile message with empty Subscriber Attribute from CLI.
bugs.fix: 'None' option is added in the Subscriber Attribute dropdown which sets its value as empty.

bugs.title: GSLB Server properties page should show the iQuery section when type is BIG-IP System
bugs.symptoms: The iQuery section does not display on the GSLB Server properties page in the Web GUI.
bugs.conditions: There must be a GSLB Server created and configured to be of type BIG-IP System.
bugs.impact: The iQuery section does not display when it should on the properties page in the Web GUI.
bugs.workaround: the iQuery settings can be changed via TMSH.
bugs.fix: The iQuery section not properly display on a GSLB Server properties page.

bugs.title: Certain FIX messages are dropped
bugs.symptoms: When a FIX message is received with a length, checksum, or message type field containing leading zeros, the message may be dropped.
bugs.conditions: This bug affects all FIX messages having a length (tag 9), checksum (tag 10) or message type (tag 35) field that contains at least one leading zero. Certain third-party FIX protocol implementations are known to insert leading zeros in these fields.
bugs.impact: FIX messages from these products cannot be processed by the FIX profile in BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Valid Financial Information eXchange protocol messages are no longer rejected

bugs.title: persist record may be inconsistent after a virtual hit rate limit
bugs.symptoms: persist record may be inconsistent after a virtual hit rate limit
bugs.conditions: A virtual with rate limit set. persist is enabled.
bugs.impact: persist behavior will be impacted.
bugs.workaround: disable rate limit on virtual
bugs.fix: The problem is fixed.

bugs.title: Removed unnecessary ASSERTs in MPTCP code
bugs.symptoms: There are many scenarios that call ASSERT in the MPTCP code, many of which can be handled without using ASSERT.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is configured with a TCP profile with MPTCP enabled.
bugs.impact: If an ASSERT fails, traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Replaced many ASSERTs with other mitigations that allow TMM to continue running.

bugs.title: When we upgrade from 12.* to 13.0+ you cannot change the "Enable Access System Logs" and "Enable URL Request Logs" properties via the UI
bugs.symptoms: You cannot change the "Enable Access System Logs" and "Enable URL Request Logs" properties via the UI.
bugs.conditions: After upgrade from 12.* to 13.0+
bugs.impact: You cannot change the "Enable Access System Logs" and "Enable URL Request Logs" properties via the UI.
bugs.workaround: Manually add the properties via tmsh: (assuming affected log setting is abc) modify log-setting abc access add { general-log { publisher sys-db-access-publisher } } modify log-setting abc url-filters add { test_logsetting_swg { enabled true publisher sys-db-access-publisher }}
bugs.fix: Now it is possible to use the GUI to successfully use and configure log-setting objects that were created with tmsh.

bugs.title: Token validate response session variables created with no prefix might collide with other session variables.
bugs.symptoms: Token validate responses create session variables without any sub-prefix, which may result in collisions with other session variables.
bugs.conditions: Executing policy containing 'introspect' session variables such as 'authresult' and 'errMsg'.
bugs.impact: May collide with other session variables. If they collide with token introspect responses, one or the other will be overwritten, depending on the order in which the variables are executed.
bugs.fix: Now the APM OAuth Token validate response creates session variables with the prefix 'introspect' for introspect response specific session variables. This eliminates potential conflict with overwriting previous session variables. Upgrade Note: If you have existing access policy rules based on introspect response session variables, you must update the rule to use the new variable names.

bugs.title: Failure to use REST services on BIG-IP without 'admin' user
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use BIG-IP REST services such as BIG-IQ management and iApps LX, unless there is an administrator user named 'admin'.
bugs.conditions: The user name of the administrator account has been changed to anything other than 'admin'.
bugs.impact: Unable to use REST services such as BIG-IQ management and iApps LX.
bugs.workaround: Name the administrator 'admin'.
bugs.fix: REST services can now be used by admin users with names other than 'admin'.

bugs.title: Thales nethsm install script can configure BIG-IP for softcard/OCS keys
bugs.symptoms: The Thales nethsm installation script configures the BIG-IP only for using module protected keys. To use OCS keys or softcards instead (only one protection type can be used at one time), you must manually configure the BIG-IP system after the installation script finishes.
bugs.conditions: Want to use softcard or OCS protected keys in a BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.impact: Must take additional steps after installing the Thales HSM client software.
bugs.workaround: Manually configure the BIG-IP system to use OCS/softcard protected keys after installing the client software with the script.
bugs.fix: The Thales nethsm installation script can now configure the BIG-IP system to use OCS or softcard protected keys as part of installation, instead of requiring additional steps after the script completes.

bugs.title: AVR is not called for DNS packets when AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.symptoms: AVR DNS analytics are not available with avr-dnsstat-sample-rate setting to non-zero on the DNS profile when AFM is not provisioned. Note that in v13, when AFM is provisioned, the dns profile option "enable-dns-firewall" must also be set to yes (This is "DNS >> Delivery : Profiles : DNS ›› Properties : <profile name> in the GUI), and a DOS profile (security dos profile) must be associated with the virtual server. In addition, for all BigIP versions, the dns profile must have avr-dnsstat-sample-rate set to a non-zero value in order for AVR to collect statistics. Indications that no data was collected would be: In the GUI: Statistics :: Analytics :: DNS returns a message similar to the following: There is no data to display either due to the lack of relevant traffic, or due to the settings of the filter. In tmsh: # tmsh show analytics dns report view-by domain-name ---------------------- Analytics query result ---------------------- No data available
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is not provisioned (or AFM is provisioned, but enable-dns-firewall is not enabled in the DNS profile, and/or a security DOS profile is not associated with the gtm listener) -- DNS traffic is received by the BigIP
bugs.impact: No DNS analytics data available. Cannot see AVR data for DNS resolutions.
bugs.fix: AVR DNS analytics are now available with avr-dnsstat-sample-rate setting to non-zero on the DNS profile when AFM is not provisioned.

bugs.title: In Internet Explorer 6, encrypting ajax may cause significant slowdown for single page applications
bugs.symptoms: Browsing a single page application in Microsoft Internet Explorer 6 may become very slow if full ajax encryption is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Single page applications that support Internet Explorer 6 and activate full ajax encryption.
bugs.impact: Very slow browsing experience in Internet Explorer 6. Sometimes you cannot start using the page in browser stack, or it never loaded. In other cases, the page stops responding after sending request
bugs.workaround: Disabled ajax encryption in Internet Explorer 6 using a custom JavaScript function. Note: BIG-IP software does not support Internet Explorer 6.

bugs.title: Show /apm access-info all-properties causes memory leaks in tmm
bugs.symptoms: When tmsh is used to view session information, memory will leak on each request to pull the session information from tmm. This is a small leak but can be significant issue when all sessions are examined or the sessions are examined multiple times in a short time interval.
bugs.conditions: when using show /apm access-info all-properties
bugs.impact: Memory will leak in tmm daemons. This affects all modules that use tmm.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is not to use the mcp interface by tmm daemon, or to restart the tmms periodically after using the interface multiple times.
bugs.fix: Accessing APM session variables via tmsh (e.g., 'tmsh show /apm access-info all-properties') no longer causes a small TMM memory leak.

bugs.title: TMSH save sys config contains [api-status-warning] that do not correspond to any configuration instances
bugs.symptoms: There are multiple [api-status-warning] logs in /var/log/ltm present. Of these warnings the following do not correspond to existing configuration objects: warning tmsh[1598]: 01420013:4: [api-status-warning] ltm/classification/url-cat-policy is deprecated. warning tmsh[1598]: 01420013:4: [api-status-warning] sys/crypto/ca-bundle-manager is early_access. Logs were generated based off the type, even though there are no instances of that type present. For example: sys/crypto/ca-bundle-manager type is early-access, but there is no instance of this type; still the warning is generated. This is unexpected behavior. Similarly unexpected warning for ltm/classification/url-cat-policy. These [api-status-warning] messages should be created only for types that have been instantiated.
bugs.conditions: Issue a tmsh save sys config command. Look at the logs in /var/log/ltm corresponding to this operation.
bugs.impact: Excessive [api-status-warning] log message in /var/log/ltm file. The warnings can be ignored.
bugs.fix: Fixed generation of [api-status-warning] messages in /var/log/ltm. These logs were generated for tmsh save sys config operation.

bugs.title: PEM:sessions iRule made the order of parameters strict
bugs.symptoms: In the versions before 12.0, the order of parameters for "PEM::SESSIONS" rule was flexible. It was made strict because of the new validation infrastructure in 12.0. This breaks some existing iRules. The system will report a validation error such as: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/test_irule] error: /Common/test_irule:2: error: ["invalid argument subscriber-type"][PEM::session create $ip subscriber-type e164 user-name $user imsi $imsi subscriber-id $callingstationid]
bugs.conditions: Some parameters, for example, subscriber-id come before the parameter user-name.
bugs.impact: Configuration that was valid in earlier versions is not accepted in newer versions. This may result in the configuration failing to load during an upgrade and return an MCP validation error.
bugs.workaround: Change the order of the parameters.

bugs.title: [api-status-warning] are generated at stderr and /var/log/ltm when listing config in tmsh from top level namespace or at module level
bugs.symptoms: tmsh list at the top namespace or at module level or mode level generates unexpected [api-status-warning] messages. (tmos)# list << top namespace (tmos)# list ltm << ltm module (tmos)# list ltm profile << profile mode Each of the three illustrative examples generates unexpected [api-status-warning] messages at stderr and /var/log/ltm. The warnings are expected only at component level. The following example uses fastl4 as the component: (tmos)# list ltm profile fastl4 myfast [api-status-warning] ltm/profile/fastl4, properties : deprecated : software-syn-cookie <<— warning message; as expected ltm profile fastl4 myfast { app-service none software-syn-cookie enabled }
bugs.conditions: This occurs when typing "y" when being prompted to list all items: (tmos)# list Display all 155 items? (y/n) y [api-status-warning] ltm/profile/fastl4, properties : deprecated : software-syn-cookie <<< unexpected warnings These are displayed for several commands that give API warnings.
bugs.impact: Excessive [api-status-warning] at stderr and /var/log/ltm for tmsh list commands. These are spurious and can be ignored.
bugs.fix: [api-status-warning] messages will be generated at stderr and /var/log/ltm with tmsh list for the specific component.

bugs.title: LTM Policy blocks a URL containing pound/hash (#) character
bugs.symptoms: The issue occurs when user specifies a URL in an LTM Policy where the path contains the hash (#) character. This character was not considered to be valid, and so the valid-character checking logic treats the URL as invalid.
bugs.conditions: User specifies a URL, say for forwarding a redirect, that contains a hash (#) character. For example, defining a policy to redirect user connections to a URL like: http://www.example.com/path1/path2/#/otherpath
bugs.impact: User is unable to specify a URL containing the hash (#) character.
bugs.workaround: In some instances, it may be possible to substitute the hash character (#) with its URL-encoded equivalent (%23).
bugs.fix: URLs used in LTM Policies correctly treat the hash character (#) as an allowed character.

bugs.title: Improve traffic disaggregation for uncommon IP protocols
bugs.symptoms: The traffic of uncommon IP protocols on VLAN running default DAG is sent to one TMM by default.
bugs.conditions: Traffic of uncommon IP protocols on VLAN configured with default DAG.
bugs.impact: Traffic for uncommon IP protocols not distributed evenly among available processing units.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly distributes traffic for uncommon IP protocols based on src IP and dest IP.
bugs.behavior: The traffic of uncommon IP protocols on VLAN running default DAG is sent to one TMM by default. This DAG enhancement allows the default DAG to disaggregate traffic of uncommon IP protocols based on src IP and dest IP. Two more DB variables are added to control DAG behavior for uncommon IP protocols. ipproto.lookupip: enable/disable (default) ah.lookupip: enable/disable (default) Setting ipproto.lookupip to enable will disaggregate uncommon IP protocols based on src IP and dest IP. DB ipproto.lookupip applies to all IP protocols except for TCP, UDP, SCTP, IGMP, AH, ESP, GRE, ICMP, ICMPv6. Setting ah.lookupip to enable will disaggregate AH traffic based on src IP and dest IP.

bugs.title: Email agent does not send email if the remote server does not provide a 200 OK response to VRFY request.
bugs.symptoms: Access Policy Email Agent does not send email if the remote server does not provide a 200 OK response to VRFY request.
bugs.conditions: The version of CURL included in 13.0.0 uses VRFY requests to confirm recipients are valid before sending mail. Many servers consider VRFY a potential leak of information and will respond '252 - Not verified' and the BIG-IP system will not send the message.
bugs.impact: The Access Policy Email Agent does not send mail messages or log an error about mail not being sent.
bugs.fix: The APM Email agent (v13.0.0 and later) will: 1. Connect to SMTP server. 2. Based on SMTP server capability (EHLO response?) / or blindly (just send it) try to verify all the addresses configured (one by one). 3. If there is a positive response (2yz), send the mails. 4. If there is no positive response, simply don't send mails to configured address(es). 5. If there is no response (e.g., times out before getting a response), simply do not send mails to configured addresses.
bugs.behavior: The APM Email agent (v13.0.0 and later) will: 1. Connect to SMTP server. 2. Based on SMTP server capability (EHLO response?) / or blindly (just send it) try to verify all the addresses configured (one by one). 3. If there is a positive response (2yz), send the mails. 4. If there is no positive response, simply don't send mails to configured address(es). 5. If there is no response (e.g., times out before getting a response), simply do not send mails to configured addresses.

bugs.title: Failure to update ASM enforcer about account change.
bugs.symptoms: There is an error updating BD with the following information: Errors: ------------ bd_agent|ERR|...|F5::BdAgent::handle_bd_pipe_message,,Some records sent to enforcer were not handled ECARD|ERR |...|account_id_table_management.cpp:0222|Failed to PUT table ECARD|ERR |...|temp_func.c:0850|CONFIG_TYPE_ACCOUNTS message had errors in block_index: 0. status=9 -------------
bugs.conditions: In a high availability environment (with manual failover and ASM) with a UCS load that contains policies with the same names.
bugs.impact: Traffic is blocked due to Unknown HTTP selector
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following Workaround: A) Deactivate and reactivate the affected policy. B) Restart ASM on the affected device.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly handles a UCS containing policies with the same names in a high availability environment (with manual failover and ASM).

bugs.title: Sending scheduled-reports will fail due to lack of backend support
bugs.symptoms: Using the scheduled report from GUI fails and causes some orphan file descriptors every time scheduled report runs.
bugs.conditions: Using the scheduled report from GUI.
bugs.impact: Scheduled-reports won't work and cause the system to have more orphan opened file-descriptors every time it tries to send the report.

bugs.title: BWC: Non-TCP data going through Category can make policy active
bugs.symptoms: When category is set at lower rate than 100% of the user rate, and traffic going through the category is non-TCP, and the amount of data is 150% of the instance rate, then that can create policy to be active, lowering the overall bandwidth.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Category rate is less than max-user-rate -- Traffic is non-TCP data. -- Amount of data passing is 150% of max-user-rate.
bugs.impact: BWC dynamic policy cannot achieve 100% of max-rate.
bugs.workaround: Increase the max-rate of any dynamic policy, and add an additional static policy set to the max-rate expected from the dynamic policy. Note: There is no actual fix for this issue except for not using UDP traffic in categories, if the amount of traffic on that UDP category is expected to exceed 150%, or over to the maximum fair rate provided by the BWC instance. Note that the PEM subscriber and BWC instance have 1-1 relationship.

bugs.title: Enhanced data integrity alerts should not contain username value
bugs.symptoms: When the system detects modification of the username field, it sends the username value in the alert.
bugs.conditions: 1. Enhanced data integrity enabled. 2. There is parameter configured as 'Identify as username'.
bugs.impact: Username value will be sent in the alert.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now, when the system detects modification of the username field, it does not send the username value in the alert.

bugs.title: dwbld memory leak when AFM/ASM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: After many hours of system uptime, the dwbld process is consuming more memory than expected. dwbld is one of the service daemons started when AFM or ASM is provisioned.
bugs.conditions: AFM or ASM provisioning.
bugs.impact: Memory leak affects overall system performance. dwbld gradually leaks memory even when idle. This causes system going low on resident memory and affects performance of rest of the system.
bugs.workaround: Periodically run the following command: bigstart restart dwbld.
bugs.fix: The dwbld memory leak was identified and fixed.

bugs.title: The persist cookie insert iRule command may leak memory
bugs.symptoms: In some situations, the persist cookie insert iRule command may leak memory.
bugs.conditions: The persist cookie insert iRule command is used.
bugs.impact: Eventually, the TMM will run out of memory due to the leak.

bugs.title: During blade changes, PBA may cause a TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: TMM will restart, and an ASSERT will appear in the logs that there have been too many retries.
bugs.conditions: -- A port block allocation configuration with very high CPU utilization. -- The addition of a new blade. -- Running a version earlier than 12.0.0.
bugs.impact: TMM will restart, so existing blocks and connections will be lost. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Portal Access might incorrectly rewrite certain JavaScript constructor calls
bugs.symptoms: The Portal Access module transforms intranet web application code to make it accessible via an APM virtual server. One of these transformations might incorrectly rewrite certain JavaScript constructor calls, though you might not see any immediate visible effect.
bugs.conditions: The issue affects execution of expressions similar to 'new obj[property]' with certain property names in the web-application JavaScript code.
bugs.impact: When Portal Access accesses the intranet application containing such code, 'obj.property' might be called instead of being constructed. As a result, the application might fail with a very obscure and difficult to diagnose errors.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule for each specific case. There is no global workaround.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access rewrite has improved rewriting of certain JavaScript expressions.

bugs.title: SAN with uppercase names result in case-sensitive match or will not match
bugs.symptoms: SSL certificates with SAN domain names with uppercase characters will fail to match SNI requests for that domain name.
bugs.conditions: Multiple client-ssl profiles configured with SNI associated with a single virtual where the SAN (Subject Alternative Name) contains DNS names with uppercase characters.
bugs.impact: SNI does not match, resulting in the wrong certificate being returned to the client, which potentially results in a security warning in the client application due to a non-matching domain.
bugs.workaround: Use lowercase characters for SAN domain names in SSL certificates.
bugs.fix: SNI match is now case-insensitive.

bugs.title: Client-side JavaScript parser cannot recognize constructions like { if(a) break\n}
bugs.symptoms: javascript errors, web-application misfunction
bugs.conditions: dynamically created javascript at client side contains constructions like: { if(a) break\n}
bugs.impact: web-application malfunction
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used in some cases, but is not always possible.

bugs.title: C3D feature needs control plane support, SNMP, tmsh and iControl
bugs.symptoms: Client Certificate Constrained Delegation Support (C3D) feature needs control plane support, SNMP, TMSH, and iControl.
bugs.conditions: Using C3D.
bugs.impact: Needs iControl, SNMP and TMSH support.
bugs.fix: Client Certificate Constrained Delegation Support (C3D) is now supported from iControl, by SNMP, and in TMSH.

bugs.title: tmsh show net f5optics shows information for only 1 chassis slot in a cluster
bugs.symptoms: When you run tmsh show net f5optics, f5optics version information is displayed for one blade of a multi-blade chassis.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running the tmsh show net f5optics command on VIPRION.
bugs.impact: The f5optics version is not displayed for all of the blades.
bugs.fix: f5optics version information for all blades within a chsasis is displayed when the user issues tmsh show net f5optics from the primary blade.

bugs.title: snmpd returns 'No Such Object available' for ltm OIDs
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP starts with an expired license snmp queries for ltm related OIDs will return 'No Such Object available on this agent at this OID'. Even if you re-activate the license or install a new one snmpd will not be notified of the change in license and will stil return 'No Such Object available on this agent at this OID' until the snmpd process is restarted.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP starts with an expired licensed which is reactivated later.
bugs.impact: snmp queries to the ltm OIDs like ltmRst and ltmVirtual will not return any data.
bugs.workaround: A restart of snmpd (bigstart restart) after the license is re-activated or a new one is installed will resolve the issue.

bugs.title: TMM may restart while processing timers
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts during timer processing due to post-free memory usage.
bugs.conditions: Full-proxy TCP functionality in use. Additional conditions are not well defined, currently.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround available.

bugs.title: Parameter names are case sensitive in Internet Explorer 9 only
bugs.symptoms: Mis-configured parameter names with incorrect case will work as if they were configured correctly in all browsers except for Internet Explorer 9
bugs.conditions: Parameter names configured in the wrong case
bugs.impact: Encryption and data integrity features will appear to work as expected in all browsers except Internet Explorer 9. In Internet Explorer 9, encryption and data integrity will not be activated on the misconfigured parameter.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the parameter name to use the correct case.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 stream reset with PROTOCOL_ERROR when frame header is fragmented.
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 RST_STREAM is seen with PROTOCOL_ERROR when frame header is fragmented.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 profile is enabled on the virtual. The frame header gets fragmented because of TCP segmentation.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 stream is reset.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 parser changed to handle header splitting across multiple buffers.

bugs.title: Changes to MAC Masquerading may cause the Standby unit not reach the floating Self-IP address
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, changes to the MAC Masquerading setting of a traffic group may cause the Standby unit to be unable to reach the floating Self-IP.
bugs.conditions: - HA pair - Traffic-group with a MAC set in the MAC Masquerading setting. - Floating Self-IP using the above traffic-group - Make a change to the MAC Masquerading MAC address on the Active unit. - Run a config-sync from Active to Standby
bugs.impact: Standby unit is unable to reach the floating Self-IP address. No external or internet facing traffic will be affected.
bugs.workaround: Reboot or restart TMM.

bugs.title: BWC statistics include active and inactive policy counts.
bugs.symptoms: BWC statistics do not include active and inactive policy counts.
bugs.conditions: BWC is provisioned on the BIG-IP systems.
bugs.impact: Lack of statistics makes diagnostics more difficult.
bugs.fix: Additional statistics were added to highlight active and inactive BWC policies.

bugs.title: Provisioning mgmt plane to "large" and performing a config sync, might cause an outage on the peer unit.
bugs.symptoms: Provisioning mgmt plane to "large" and performing a config sync, might cause an outage on the peer unit. When provision.extramb is synced to the peer unit, mprov is called, which restarts tmm.
