bugs.conditions: -- Configure two devices in a sync group. -- tmsh modify sys db provision.extramb value 150. -- Sync to peer unit.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts on the peer unit. Traffic halted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the provision.extramb value is the same on all units in the device cluster before performing a config sync.
bugs.fix: The provision.extramb and provision.tomcat.extramb DB keys no longer ConfigSync, which prevents TMM restarting on peer devices after a change is made to the management subsystem provisioning and then performing a ConfigSync.
bugs.behavior: The provision.extramb and provision.tomcat.extramb DB keys no longer ConfigSync between devices.

bugs.title: Displaying 100G interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces' Active Media Type and Media Speed rows display none.
bugs.conditions: Having a server with 100G interfaces.
bugs.impact: Cannot use GUI to determine interfaces' Active Media Type and Media Speed.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to see the affected interface.
bugs.fix: 100G interfaces now display correctly.

bugs.title: Installation fails if only .iso.384.sig (new format signature file) is present
bugs.symptoms: Tab completion only will complete the names of ISO images that have an old style signature format ("BIG-IP-version-build.iso.sig"), not the new style ("BIG-IP-version-build.iso.384.sig"). Then, installation will fail even if you type out the full name.
bugs.conditions: This only happens when signature checking is enabled for ISO images. You can determine this by looking at the value of the DB variable "liveinstall.checksig".
bugs.impact: Tab completion will not show the ISO image, and even if you type out the full name, the installation will fail. An error message will appear in "show sys software status" and /var/log/liveinstall.log .
bugs.workaround: Put both types of signature file (.iso.sig and .iso.384.sig) on the device.
bugs.fix: Tab completion and installation will now work if the old signature file format (.iso.sig) is missing, and only the new signature format (.iso.384.sig) is present.

bugs.title: Learn from responses checkbox can appear checked and disabled in manual mode
bugs.symptoms: A security policy can get the 'Learn from responses' checkbox turned on in automatic mode. After moving to manual mode, the checkbox remains checked and it is not possible to uncheck it in manual mode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following actions are performed, in this order: 1. Have a policy in automatic mode 2. Check the learn from responses. 3. Move the policy to manual
bugs.impact: Cannot uncheck the 'Lean from responses' checkbox in manual mode.
bugs.workaround: Move to automatic, uncheck the checkbox, and move back to manual.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is used on an appliance with over 24 CPU cores (or VE on a HW platform with over 24 CPU cores) some processes may be constantly restarting until disabled.
bugs.symptoms: urldb may be constantly restarting on a BIG-IP appliance that has over 24 CPU cores.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP appliance has over 24 CPU cores or BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) platform has over 24 CPU cores. -- APM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: URLDB functionality will not be accessible to the users.
bugs.workaround: If URLDB functionality is not required - disable process by running 'bigstart stop urldb'. If urldb functionality is needed: 1. Stop urldb by running "bigstart stop urldb'. 2. Modify file '/etc/bigstart/scripts/urldb' as follows: a) Replace line: cpu_count=$(get_number_cpu) with line: tmm_count=$(get_tmm_count) b) Replace line: exec /usr/sbin/${service} -n ${cpu_count} with line: exec /usr/sbin/${service} -n ${tmm_count} 3. Save the file, and restart the process by running 'bigstart start urldb'.
bugs.fix: urldb no longer restarts when used on a platform with over 24 CPU cores and under 64 CPU cores.

bugs.title: "Signature Update Available" message is not cleared by UCS load/sync
bugs.symptoms: If the most recent Signature Update was loaded by device group sync or UCS load, the "Signature Update Available" message is never cleared out.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned and "Signature Update Available" was indicated prior to loading the most recent Signature Update by device group sync or UCS load.
bugs.impact: The "Signature Update Available" message is never cleared out.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM, or kill asmcrond ("pkill -f asmcrond").

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is used on an appliance with over 24 CPU cores (or VE on a HW platform with over 24 CPU cores) some processes may be constantly restarting until disabled.
bugs.symptoms: ECA may be constantly restarting on BIG-IP appliance that has over 24 CPU cores.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP appliance has over 24 CPU cores or BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) platform has over 24 CPU cores. -- APM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: ECA NTLM functionality will not be accessible to the users.
bugs.workaround: If ECA functionality is not required - disable process by running 'bigstart stop eca'. If ECA functionality is needed: 1. Stop eca by running "bigstart stop eca'. 2. Modify file '/etc/bigstart/scripts/eca' as follows: a) Replace line: cpu_count=$(get_number_cpu) with line: tmm_count=$(get_tmm_count) b) Replace line: exec /usr/sbin/${service} -n ${cpu_count} with line: exec /usr/sbin/${service} -n ${tmm_count} 3. Save the file, and restart the process by running 'bigstart start eca'.
bugs.fix: ECA no longer restarts when used on a platform with over 24 CPU cores and under 64 CPU cores.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is used on an appliance with over 24 CPU cores (or VE on a HW platform with over 24 CPU cores) some processes may be constantly restarting until disabled.
bugs.symptoms: ping_access_agent may be constantly restarting on BIG-IP appliance that has over 24 CPU cores.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP appliance has over 24 CPU cores or VE platform has over 24 CPU cores. -- APM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: PingAccess integration functionality will not be accessible to the users.
bugs.workaround: If PingAccess functionality is not required - disable process by running 'bigstart stop ping_access_agent'. If PingAccess functionality is needed: 1. Stop ping_access_agent by running "bigstart stop ping_access_agent'. 2. Modify file '/etc/bigstart/scripts/ping_access_agent' as follows: a) Replace line: cpu_count=$(get_number_cpu) with line: tmm_count=$(get_tmm_count) b) Replace line: exec /usr/sbin/${service} -n ${cpu_count} with line: exec /usr/sbin/${service} -n ${tmm_count} 3. Save the file, and restart the process by running 'bigstart start ping_access_agent'.

bugs.title: xdg-open fails to open custom protocol link (at first attempt) causing Google Chrome not to open F5 apps (f5vpn, f5epi) on Fedora 25
bugs.symptoms: F5's applications (f5vpn, f5epi) can't be launched from the webtop/webpage when Google Chrome is used on Fedora 25 or Fedora 26. This happens because of improper behavior of 'gio' utility which fails to process custom protocol link request ("f5-vpn://..."). gio utility is invoked by xdg-open script which, in turn, is invoked by Google Chrome. Firefox browser is not affected.
bugs.conditions: It happens when all conditions are met: * Fedora 25/26 Linux distribution. * Gnome as desktop manager. * Google Chrome.
bugs.impact: F5's application f5vpn and f5epi can't be launched from a web page by the first click. The second click within a short amount of time works fine.
bugs.workaround: * Click the second time on webtop resource icon or "Try again" link within the short amount of time (less than a minute). * Use Firefox browser on Fedora as it's not affected.

bugs.title: vCMP host avrd high CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: With high vCMP guest counts, the avrd shows sustained ~90% CPU usage on the HOST primary blade.
bugs.conditions: For example, 48 guests on B4300 8-blade P8, or 96 guests on B4450 8-blade P8.
bugs.impact: The avrd will compete with the control plane threads on the guest that share the same core. The guest dataplane runs at higher priority and not impacted. The avrd maintains a database of statistics available via the UI and 'tmsh show analytics vcmp ...'. When avrd is stopped, these statistics will not be available.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands on the HOSTprimary blade: clsh bigstart stop avrd clsh bigstart disable avrd
bugs.fix: The avrd no longer shows sustained ~90% CPU usage on the HOST primary blade with high vCMP guest counts.

bugs.title: TCP DNS profile may impact performance
bugs.symptoms: Under some conditions TCP DNS profiles may impact system performance
bugs.conditions: TCP DNS profiles
bugs.impact: Performance issues
bugs.fix: Improve performance while using TCP DNS profiles

bugs.title: The tmsh utility shows memory information only for the main thread of each TMM process.
bugs.symptoms: When running the 'tmsh show sys tmm-info' command from the command line, you may notice that the utility returns memory information only for the main thread of each TMM process. All the memory available to the TMM process is accounted for under its main thread, and all other threads appear as having no memory at all. For example: # tmsh show sys tmm-info --------------------------- Sys::TMM: 0.0 --------------------------- Global TMM Process Id 18228 Running TMM Id 0 TMM Count 1 CPU Id 0 Memory (bytes) Total 17.0G Used 522.9M CPU Usage Ratio (%) Last 5 Seconds 2 Last 1 Minute 2 Last 5 Minutes 2 -------------------------- Sys::TMM: 0.1 -------------------------- Global TMM Process Id 18228 Running TMM Id 1 TMM Count 1 CPU Id 1 Memory (bytes) Total 0 Used 0 CPU Usage Ratio (%) Last 5 Seconds 2 Last 1 Minute 2 Last 5 Minutes 2 [...]
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on any BIG-IP device running version 11.3.0 or later (provided that TMM threading has not been disabled for troubleshooting purposes).
bugs.impact: This issue is cosmetic, and there is no functional impact to the BIG-IP system. Whilst a BIG-IP Administrator may find the output confusing, all TMM threads have an equal share of the memory and are operating correctly.
bugs.workaround: Refer to memory information for the main thread.

bugs.title: Reactivating the license on a VIPRION system may cause MCPD process restart on all secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: All services on one or all secondary blades in a VIPRION chassis restart, and MCPD logs errors similar to the following: -- err mcpd[9063]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (sflow_vlan_data_source) object ID (1168). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:sflow_vlan_data_source status:13) -- err mcpd[9063]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01070734:3:Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (sflow_vlan_data_source) object ID (1168). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:sflow_vlan_data_source status:13)... failed validation with error 17237812. In versions prior to v11.6.0, the error is: 'Can't save/checkpoint DB object,' rather than 'Can't update_indexes/checkpoint DB object'.
bugs.conditions: Multi-bladed VIPRION system, where the 'if-index' value for VLANs differs between blades. You can check the 'if-index' value by running the following command on each blade: tmsh list net vlan all if-index.
bugs.impact: MCPD restart on all secondary blades results in partial service outage.
bugs.workaround: Reactivate the license only on a system that is standby/offline.
bugs.fix: Reactivating the license on a VIPRION system no longer causes MCPD process restart on one or all secondary blades.

bugs.title: Native RDP published on webtop does not connect if allowed vlans specified explicitly
bugs.symptoms: Native RDP hosts published on webtop does not connect if allowed vlans specified explicitly on the virtual server. It downloads the rdp file but opening the rdp file gets error message from rdp client something like "Your computer can't connect to remote computer".
bugs.conditions: - Native RDP host type published in webtop mode. - RDP Virtual server specified the allowed vlans explicitly. - MSRDP NTLM configuration is not specified in vdi profile.
bugs.impact: Could not connect to Native RDP host published on webtop
bugs.workaround: You can use either one of the below workarounds, - Have the virtual server with "All the vlans and tunnels" configuration. - Have MSRDP NTLM auth configuration in VDI profile which is attached to virtual server.
bugs.fix: Now Native Remote Desktop (RDP) resources can be delivered from APM virtual servers that have the "VLAN and Tunnel Traffic" set to a non-default value.

bugs.title: Exotic tmipsecd crash when internally the wrong path was used for racoon.
bugs.symptoms: Relaunching racoon might crash tmipsecd when internally the wrong path was used for racoon.
bugs.conditions: -- Racoon relaunch when tmipsecd had the wrong racoon path. -- Using IPsec tunnels.
bugs.impact: Core for tmipsecd.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a tmipsecd crash so it no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: IKEv2 PFS CREATE_CHILD_SA in rekey does not negotiate new keys
bugs.symptoms: During negotiations that use CREATE_CHILD_SA, IKEv2 will fail to send a KE in the payload when PFS (perfect forward security) is used in config. Rekey in IKEv2 does not negotiate new keys; the PFS value in phase1-perfect-forward-secrecy is used in the first exchange, then this first key is re-used in later rekey negotiation. Vendor interop problems exist when PFS is required by the other peer.
bugs.conditions: Define phase1-perfect-forward-secrecy with value other than none. After IPsec SAs expire or are manually deleted, the CREATE_CHILD_SA phase to negotiate new keys has no KEi payload from the BIG-IP Initiator and so no new encryption key.
bugs.impact: PFS settings apply only to first negotiation and not to subsequent SA rekeys. PFS is therefore absent. When the BIG-IP enters CREATE_CHILD_SA with a third party IPsec peer, negotiation will fail if the peer requires PFS. Under the same conditions, BIG-IP to BIG-IP tunnels will not fail.
bugs.workaround: To resolve vendor interop problems, disable PFS in the IPsec policy of both peers.
bugs.fix: When phase1-perfect-forward-secrecy is configured with a value other than none, the BIG-IP will now perform PFS negotiation correctly. Now rekey with CREATE_CHILD_SA generates a new key using the same DH Group as the first exchange that creates the first SA. Note: In the ipsec-policy configuration object, the ike-phase2-perfect-forward-secrecy option is relevant only to IKEv1 and has no influence on IKEv2 PFS rekeying.

bugs.title: Coredump observed at system bootup time when many DHCP packets arrived at BigIP
bugs.symptoms: During system bootup, system coredump is observed when many DHCP packets arrive before system is fully ready and many flow entry creation failures are observed
bugs.conditions: 1)BIG-IP DHCP proxy is in forwarding mode 2)DHCP relay agent in front of BIG-IP modifies giaddr field of DHCP packets to its own IP address 3)DHCP packets arrive during system bootup and before system is fully ready(some vlans, interfaces and routes are not fully up)
bugs.impact: System crash and coredump
bugs.workaround: Make sure system has come up completely before sending DHCP packets to the box
bugs.fix: Coredump no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: tmipsecd aborts
bugs.symptoms: tmipsecd aborts.
bugs.conditions: Conditions are unknown; this occurred once.
bugs.impact: IPsec-related operations halted while tmipsecd restarts.

bugs.title: Apply Policy failure if an custom Blocking Page is configured with an underscore in the header name
bugs.symptoms: An issue was introduced when dealing with custom Blocking pages containing an HTTP Header that has an underscore in the name.
bugs.conditions: A custom Blocking page is defined containing an HTTP Header that has an underscore in the name.
bugs.impact: Set Active fails
bugs.workaround: Use hyphens instead of underscores in the header name.
bugs.fix: Underscores in HTTP Headers in Blocking Response pages are handled correctly.

bugs.title: Bot signatures cannot be created after upgrade with DoS profile in non-Common partition
bugs.symptoms: Bot signatures cannot be created after roll-forward upgrade of configuration with only a DoS profile in non-Common partition.
bugs.conditions: A DoS profile in non-Common partition has Proactive Bot Defense enabled
bugs.impact: Bot signatures are not created.
bugs.workaround: Delete DoS Profile before upgrade, and re-create after upgrade is successful. Alternatively, another DoS Profile can be created in /Common, even if unused.

bugs.title: transaction capturing sends binary data without escaping
bugs.symptoms: If the transaction body contains binary data and transaction capturing is on. AVR will send to external log the binary data unescaping.
bugs.conditions: 1. Transaction capturing is on. 2. The transaction (response or request) contains binary data.
bugs.impact: AVR reports binary data unescaping.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After the fix AVR will send the binary data escaping.

bugs.title: Virtual flaps when FQDN node and pool configured with autopopulate
bugs.symptoms: Virtual address status flaps (RED :: BLUE :: DOWN :: UNCHECKED) when the FQDN node and pool are configured with autopopulate enabled, and the FQDN DNS response returns the same addresses.
bugs.conditions: -- FQDN node and pool are configured with autopopulate enabled. -- FQDN DNS response returns the same addresses.
bugs.impact: The virtual server becomes unavailable, and later switches to unchecked.

bugs.title: Support RSASSA-PSS-SIGN in F5 crypto APIs.
bugs.symptoms: Client certificate verification in BIG-IP v11.6.0 through v13.1.0 does not support client certificates that are signed using the RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm. Validation of such client certificates will fail.
bugs.conditions: - Client certificate signed with RSASSA-PSS algorithm. - Client Certificate is set to 'Required' in Client SSL profile. - Running any version of BIG-IP software from v11.6.0 through v13.1.0.
bugs.impact: SSL connections using client PSS certificates are rejected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Validation of client certificates that are signed using the RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm now completes successfully.

bugs.title: Update the default CA certificate bundle file to the latest version and remove expiring certificates from it
bugs.symptoms: The default CA certificate bundle file used by the system contains some older certificates, e.g., expired or soon-to-be expired.
bugs.conditions: If the default CA certificate bundle file is configured in SSL profiles, it is used as a set of built-in trusted certificates when verifying peer's certificate during SSL handshake.
bugs.impact: When the built-in trusted certificates are obsolete, i.e., containing a certain number of expired certificates, the systems might fail to verify peers certificate correctly.
bugs.workaround: You can either directly update the default CA certificate bundle file /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ca-bundle.crt with proper certificates and then 'bigstart restart tmm' Alternatively, you can use a separate certificate, for example: tmsh install sys crypto cert better_ca_bundle from-local-file /shared/better_ca_bundle.pem tmsh modify ltm profile client-ssl cssl ca-file better_ca_bundle.crt
bugs.fix: This release updates the default CA certificate bundle file by adding the latest certificates and removing the expired certificates.

bugs.title: Rare resets during the login process
bugs.symptoms: On rare occasions, the login process resets and a NULL sresult message will be logged in /var/log/apm: -- notice tmm[18397]: 01490505:5: /Common/ltm-apm_main_irules:Common:448568c9: Get license - Unexpected NULL session reply. Resetting connection.
bugs.conditions: A race condition allows license information to be processed out of order.
bugs.impact: The system resets the client connection attempt. The APM end user client must retry the login process.
bugs.workaround: Have the APM end user client retry the login operation.

bugs.title: coreutils security and bug fix update
bugs.symptoms: A race condition was found in the way su handled the management of child processes.
bugs.impact: A local authenticated attacker could use this flaw to kill other processes with root privileges under specific conditions.
bugs.workaround: install latest hotfix
bugs.fix: fixed in coreutils-8.4-46.el6

bugs.title: SNAT does not work properly on FTP VIP2VIP
bugs.symptoms: SNAT does not work properly on FTP VIP2VIP.
bugs.conditions: -- FTP communicates VIP2VIP to second virtual server. -- SNAT is configured on second virtual server.
bugs.impact: SNAT does not work properly on FTP VIP2VIP on data channel.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure SNAT on second virtual server.
bugs.fix: SNAT now works properly on FTP VIP2VIP.

bugs.title: Many objects must be reconfigured before use when loading a UCS from another device.
bugs.symptoms: Many objects are ignored by the platform-migrate option, and must be reconfigured before use when loading a UCS from another device.
bugs.conditions: UCS is being loaded from another device, using the platform-migrate option.
bugs.impact: Risk of configuration load failures.
bugs.workaround: None, other than reconfiguring for the destination device.
bugs.fix: The platform-migrate option for UCS loading has been modified so that nearly all configuration is loaded. Now, the only things you must configure are the management IP and license, then you can load the UCS. The end result should be a successfully loaded configuration, but with empty VLANs and trunks. You should be able to pass traffic once you reconnect these VLANs to interfaces.
bugs.behavior: The platform-migrate option for UCS loading has been modified so that nearly all configuration is loaded. Now, the only things you must configure are the management IP and license, then you can load the UCS. The end result should be a successfully loaded configuration, but with empty VLANs and trunks. You should be able to pass traffic once you reconnect these VLANs to interfaces.

bugs.title: "Unexpected Error" showing traffic-selector default-traffic-selector
bugs.symptoms: Running this tmsh command results in "Unexpected error": tmsh show net ipsec ipsec-sa traffic-selector default-traffic-selector-interface
bugs.conditions: This occurs when running tmsh show net ipsec ipsec-sa traffic-selector default-traffic-selector-interface
bugs.impact: The result is not return, the only output is "unexpected error".

bugs.title: PEM rule deletion with HSL reporting may cause tmm coredump
bugs.symptoms: tmm coredump caused by deletion of a PEM policy rule with HSL reporting configured and passing active traffic. tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: PEM policy rule with HSL reporting is deleted while passing subscriber traffic.
bugs.impact: tmm coredump causes traffic disruption and restart of tmm.
bugs.fix: PEM rule deletion with HSL reporting no longer causes tmm coredump.

bugs.title: MySQL does not initialize correctly on first system start
bugs.symptoms: MySQL is not yet setup, failed to initialize. Shutting down MySQL...... SUCCESS!
bugs.conditions: avr or asm are provisioned
bugs.impact: AVR, loadmanager etc dependent on mysql are down
bugs.workaround: Run of 'bigstart restart mysql' should solve the issue
bugs.fix: Allow MySQL enough time to properly initialize

bugs.title: On macOS Sierra (10.12), Edge client shows customized icon of size 48x48 pixels scaled incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: On macOS Sierra (10.12), Edge client shows customized icon of size 48x48 pixels scaled incorrectly; it appears very small.
bugs.conditions: On macOS Sierra (10.12), edge client, customized icon of size 48x48 pixels.
bugs.impact: This is a display issue only. There is no functional impact to the system.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom logo image with the pixel dimensions of 100x121 pixels.
bugs.fix: On macOS Sierra (10.12), Edge client now shows the customized icon of size 48x48 pixels that is now scaled correctly.

bugs.title: bgpd may crash on receiving a BGP update with >= 32 extended communities
bugs.symptoms: bgpd may crash when receiving a BGP update with >= 32 extended communities
bugs.conditions: A configured BGP peer sends a route update including and attribute containing 32 or more extended communities.
bugs.impact: bgpd may crash causing the BGP peering to reset
bugs.workaround: Ensure that peers do not send 32 or more extended communities to the BIG-IP in BGP routing updates.
bugs.fix: bgpd no longer crashes on receiving a BGP update with >= 32 extended communities

bugs.title: Host Processor Superuser keys in /root/.ssh/authorized_keys no longer necessary
bugs.symptoms: Keys with the name 'Host Processor Superuser' are still present in /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, but are no longer used by supported BIG-IP versions.
bugs.conditions: Running any currently supported version of BIG-IP software.
bugs.impact: The keys' presence is benign and there is no negative impact except for the confusion caused by wondering what these keys are for.
bugs.workaround: Keys with this label can be safely removed from the authorized_keys file manually.
bugs.fix: Host Processor Superuser keys have been removed from /root/.ssh/authorized_keys.

bugs.title: Warning message "Windows Media Player Extension" appears on some IE browsers
bugs.symptoms: On some rare cases of Internet Explorer users, the following warning message appears on the bottom of the page: The previous webpage wants to run the following add-on: 'Windows Media Player Extension' from 'Microsoft Corporation'. This happens when Device-ID is enabled in either the ASM policy or DOS profile.
bugs.conditions: This happens when Device-ID is enabled in either the ASM policy or DOS profile.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic: Warning message appears for first-time users, and not degrading performance.
bugs.workaround: Running the following command should prevent the warning message from appearing, without any side effects. tmsh modify security device-id attribute att22 { collect disabled }
bugs.fix: The warning message "Windows Media Player Extension" no longer appears on some Internet Explorer browsers when Device-ID is enabled.

bugs.title: ARP replies reach front panel port of the B4450 blade, but fail to reach TMMs.
bugs.symptoms: ARP replies reach the front panel port of the B4450 blade, but fail to reach TMMs. This is caused by a L2 defect in the Broadcom Trident2+ switch B4450 blade uses.
bugs.conditions: The switch learned a corrupted L2 FDB entry on internal HiGig trunk.
bugs.impact: The traffic hitting the corrupted L2 FDB entry will be dropped by the switch.
bugs.workaround: Identify the affected VLAN and flush L2 FDB entries on that VLAN using the following command: tmsh delete net fdb vlan {vlan_name}.
bugs.fix: Resolved an issue on Broadcom Trident2+ switch B4450 blades use in which ARP replies reached the front panel port, but failed to reach TMMs.
bugs.behavior: A new BigDB variable is added to control in which mode the l2xmsg module in Broadcom SDK should run. bcm56xxd.l2xmsg.mode: poll/fifo (default) The BIG-IP system used to always run l2xmsg module in poll mode. Now, the BIG-IP system will run l2xmsg mode in fifo by default.

bugs.title: Incorrect SNI hostname attached to serverside connections
bugs.symptoms: SNI hostname submitted to a virtual server on the client side is sent to server side, even if there is a different hostname specified in the server SSL profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Client side ClientHello contains SNI.
bugs.impact: SNI is sent from client to server without stripping or rewriting the SNI.
bugs.fix: SNI hostname submitted to a virtual server on the client side is no longer sent to server side unless specifically requested (for example when forward proxy is enabled). When there is a different hostname specified in the server SSL profile the SNI is also rewritten to the specified hostname.

bugs.title: Web UI: User not able to configure RADIUS profile for a Virtual Server when only LTM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS profile option is missing in Virtual server configuration page when PEM/AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: PEM/AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: You cannot attach RADIUS profile to a virtual server.
bugs.workaround: You can configure the same from TMSH.
bugs.fix: The dependency on PEM/AFM module is removed so that RADIUS profile option is available even if only LTM is provisioned.

bugs.title: Intermittent connection failure with SNAT/automap, SP-DAG and virtual server source-port=preserve
bugs.symptoms: Connections can fail intermittently when multiple clients use the same ephemeral port to connect to BIG-IP and are SNATted to the same address.
bugs.conditions: When SNAT/Automap is configured with SP-DAG and virtual server source-port setting is "preserve".
bugs.impact: Service interruption due to intermittent connection failures.
bugs.fix: Connections no longer fail intermittently with SNAT/automap, SP-DAG and virtual server source-port=preserve.

bugs.title: ADMd not cleaning up child rsync processes
bugs.symptoms: ADMd daemon on device is spinning up rsync processes and not cleaning them up properly, causing tons of this zombie processes
bugs.conditions: If rsync process ends via exit (in the case of some trouble)
bugs.impact: No technical impact, but there are many zombie processes
bugs.workaround: Restart admd (bigstart restart admd) to remove all existing rsync zombies.
bugs.fix: admd should handle SIGCHLD signal from rsync (in the case of some trouble)

bugs.title: Allowed Receiving Domain in SMTP Protocol Security is case sensitive
bugs.symptoms: False positive disallowed receiving domain violation in the SMTP security.
bugs.conditions: SMTP profile is attached to a virtual with security turned on. The SMTP security has an allowed domain list and the disallowed domain violation turned on. A transaction arrives from a domain that is in the list, but written in a different case.
bugs.impact: A false positive access from disallwed domain violation.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Virtual Edition may have minimal disk space for the /var software partition when deploying from the OVA file.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition does not have enough disk space for the /var software partition when deploying from OVA. The size of /var volume is 500 MB instead of 3 GB for BETTER and BEST license bundles.
bugs.conditions: Installing the scsi OVA vm bundle images.
bugs.impact: Not enough space in /var.

bugs.title: On VIPRION, iApps LX packages can take 10 minutes to synchronize
bugs.symptoms: Install a large iApps LX package on a VIPRION system, such as the "diameter" package, which installs roughly 20 MB of files. Then, within the next 10 minutes, remove or disable the new primary blade. The new primary blade may not have a complete copy of the package in /var/config/rest/iapps.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION is in use. -- Install a large iApps LX package. -- The VIPRION primary blade has been disabled.
bugs.impact: The new iApps LX package may be unusable with the new VIPRION primary blade.
bugs.workaround: After installing a large iApps LX package, allow the current primary blade to remain the primary for at least 10 minutes, so that it can synchronize the files to the other blades. If this is not possible, then re-install the iApps LX package on the new blade.

bugs.title: Support IP Uncommon Protocol
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP system can have CPU usage be non-uniformly distributed across the datapath (tmm) threads, such that the overall CPU usage is low, but individual datapath threads may show high usage of a subset of the CPUs on the system. This can be observed by viewing the per-CPU usage, and can manifest as spuriously dropped packets/flows.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system receives packets that have uncommon IP protocols – those not parsed by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The packets are eventually dropped but may drive a subset of the CPUs in the system to very high usage. As CPU increases, potentially reaching 100%, then the BIG-IP system will start dropping packets and the system might eventually fail.
bugs.fix: The system now supports packets that have uncommon IP protocols.
bugs.behavior: This change adds the capability of specifying various IP protocols as 'uncommon' protocols. Using this list of uncommon protocols can have the system mitigate an attack from uncommon protocols. To do so, perform the following procedure: 1. Set the sys db tunable dos.uncommon.replace.illegal to true (it is false by default). 2. Set the 8 sys db tunables dos.uncommon.protocols[0-7] to specify which protocols should be considered uncommon (by default all protocols except TCP/UDP/ICMPv4/ICMPv6/SCTP - bits 1/6/17/58/132 are uncommon). - dos.uncommon.protocols0 represents bits 31:0 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols1 represents bits 63:32 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols2 represents bits 95:64 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols3 represents bits 127:96 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols4 represents bits 159:128 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols5 represents bits 191:160 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols6 represents bits 223:192 of a 256-bit vector - dos.uncommon.protocols7 represents bits 255:224 of a 256-bit vector Setting the specific bit to '1' means that the specified protocol is considered 'uncommon', and setting the specific bit to '0' means that the specified protocol is not considered 'uncommon'. Then the DoS vector IP Unknown Protocol can be used to mitigate an attack from the above-specified 'Uncommon Protocols'.

bugs.title: ZebOS route-map set nexthop not being applied for neighbor outbound route-map
bugs.symptoms: BGP neighbor outbound route-map nexthop is not being applied
bugs.conditions: Advance routing configured with outbound route-map for BGP neighbor, and route-map have set nexthop entry.
bugs.impact: Incorrect nexthop advertised to peers when use with BGP neighbor outbound route-map
bugs.workaround: Use global redistribute route-map instead of neighbor specific outbound route-map.

bugs.title: Unable to display detailed CPU graphs if the number of CPU is too large
bugs.symptoms: Cannot display detail CPU graph. Go to Statistics :: Performance. Click 'View Detail Graph' under System CPU usage. Graph cannot display. System posts the message: Error trying to access the database.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION with 288 CPU cores or more totaled across all blades.
bugs.impact: Administrator is unable to view the detail CPU graphs.
bugs.fix: The GUI can now display detailed CPU graphs for 1024 cores with the default of 4 lines per graph.

bugs.title: Chassis Variant number is not specified in C2200/C2400 chassis after a firmware update
bugs.symptoms: Chassis Variant number is not specified when checking the log file /var/log/ltm, for example: #grep queryFDD /var/log/ltm ...debug chmand[12982]: 012a0007:7: queryFDD returned 1 items for: update|F100|||NONE|NONE|NONE|0x0 This should contain the Variant number 400-0028-04, as follows: ...debug chmand[32663]: 012a0007:7: queryFDD returned 1 items for: update|F100|400-0028-04||NONE|NONE|NONE|0x0
bugs.conditions: -- B2100/B2150/B2200 blade in C2200/C2400 chassis. -- Checking for the Chassis Variant number.
bugs.impact: This has no impact, since there are no Variants currently defined for the C2200/C2400 chassis.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Chassis Variant number is printed out as expected in the log file.

bugs.title: Cannot copy fields in Policy Rule section of LTM Policy rule overview page
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in version 13.0.0, on the LTM Policy rule overview, you cannot select and copy text. If you mouse down to click on a rule, the rule bar moves. This denotes new functionality where you can reorder rules in the list.
bugs.conditions: Go to Policy Rule overview and click a rule.
bugs.impact: Text cannot be highlighted in rule list. Copy/paste of text is not possible.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to select and copy text.

bugs.title: tmm crash after per-request policy error
bugs.symptoms: TMM core is seen when reject ending in per-request policy encounters error.
bugs.conditions: The conditions which trigger this are unknown at this time, it was seen once on a per-request policy error.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when reject ending encounters error in per-request policy

bugs.title: fastL4 fails to evict flows from the ePVA
bugs.symptoms: An accelerated flow is in the ePVA with no corresponding software connection.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4. -- ePVA. -- The other conditions under which this occurs are not well defined.
bugs.impact: ePVA can continuously send a packet. This might eventually result in a network outage.
bugs.workaround: Disable HW acceleration.
bugs.fix: There are now no unknown accelerated flows.
bugs.behavior: The default behavior is to ignore unknown HW accelerated flows (connections). This change will proactively evict unknown HW accelerated flows from the HW (ePVA).

bugs.title: Ampersand (&) in GTM synchronization group name causes synchronization failure.
bugs.symptoms: A GTM synchronization-group-name containing an ampersand (&) might cause an XML parsing failure and GTM sync groups would fail to sync.
bugs.conditions: A GTM synchronization group name with an ampersand (&) in the name.
bugs.impact: GTM sync groups does not synchronize.
bugs.workaround: Remove ampersand from sync group name.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue that prevented GTM sync groups with an ampersand (&) in the GTM synchronization-group-name from syncing.

bugs.title: OPSWAT inspect checks now supports privilege elevation
bugs.symptoms: If OPSWAT checks would require elevation or root rights for checking particular Antivirus, Firewall (or other security software) check fails.
bugs.conditions: * Windows/Mac client systems. * System has security software that requires privilege elevation/root access to check its status.
bugs.impact: OPSWAT checks fail completely or partially (e.g., some fields are not available).
bugs.workaround: Important note: This workaround is recommended only for troubleshooting purposes, as using it implies security issues. Run browser or EdgeClient on high integrity level (Windows)/under root (Mac).
bugs.fix: OPSWAT inspect checks now support privilege elevation via an optional F5 Inspector Service available in the Edge Client package. -- Windows: Introduced new component to provide on-demand elevation. -- Mac: Updated existing component to support such checks.

bugs.title: BGP advertisement-interval attribute ignored in peer group configuration
bugs.symptoms: BGP peer-group advertisement-interval attribute may be ignored with default settings set on individual peers belonging to the peer-group.
bugs.conditions: - BGP configured with peer-groups. - advertisement-interval configured with a non-default value
bugs.impact: The BGP peer will have an additional statement added indicating a default value of the advertisement-interval.
bugs.workaround: Manually set the advertisement-interval of the peer, instead of using the peer-group for this particular setting.
bugs.fix: BGP advertisement-interval attribute is no longer ignored in peer group configuration

bugs.title: Admin user cannot edit policy
bugs.symptoms: While logged into the active device, you are unable to edit a policy. The Save and Reconfigure buttons are grayed out. The standby device allows you to edit the policy and you can deploy the change to the active device, but you occasionally can't edit it from the active device.
bugs.conditions: It is not known what triggers this intermittent problem.
bugs.impact: Admin users are unable to edit a policy on the active device.
bugs.workaround: You can edit the policy on the standby device and deploy it to the active device.

bugs.title: On a BIG-IP system with DHCP enabled, 'tmsh load sys config default' consistently fails after 'tmsh load sys config' has failed with Conflicting configuration error.
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP system with DHCP enabled, 'tmsh load sys config default' consistently fails after 'tmsh load sys config' has failed due to an incorrect configuration. The system posts a Conflicting configuration message in response to the error.
bugs.conditions: There are multiple ways to encounter this: -- The BIG-IP system has a working configuration and is running normally. If the configuration becomes invalid, due to hardware configuration changes, a configuration mistake, or a typo in one of the configuration files, the MCPD never reaches the running state due to the configuration load error. -- If the BIG-IP system is managed by a BIG-IQ device, and the BIG-IQ device revokes the BIG-IP system's license, the configuration load might start failing if the BIG-IP system's configuration contains advanced features that require an active license.
bugs.impact: If the misconfiguration occurs during a upgrade from 10.2.4 to 12.1.x, the operation fails with the DHCP error. In these cases, when you try to load the default configuration through 'tmsh load sys config default', the configuration load fails with this error: /Common/management-ip: Conflicting configuration. Management-ip can't be created manually while DHCP is enabled. Within tmsh run 'modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp disabled' before manually changing the management-ip. MCPD never reaches the running state and the BIG-IP system does not function as expected.
bugs.workaround: Once this problem occurs, there is no way to force 'load sys config default' without first resolving the 'base config load failure' mcpd status, which requires repairing the configuration errors that caused the initial base configuration load failure. To do so, review the log files to determine the specific misconfiguration and remove it from the corresponding configuration file. Then try the configuration load operation again.

bugs.title: Monitor with description containing backslash may fail to load.
bugs.symptoms: When a monitor description contains a \ (backslash) character, the system adds another backslash for every save-load operation. After enough saves/loads, the description eventually hits the maximum length, causing an error message: '01020057:3: The string with more than 65535 characters cannot be stored in a message' upon loading the config.
bugs.conditions: Monitor with description containing backslash.
bugs.impact: Configuration changes without human intervention. Potential load failure.
bugs.workaround: Don't use backslashes in monitor descriptions.

bugs.title: SSL handshake fails if server certificate contains multiple CommonNames
bugs.symptoms: SSL server side handshake fails when the external server certificate's Subject field contains multiple CommonNames.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when both of the following conditions are met: -- The external server certificate's Subject field contains multiple CommonNames. -- The certificate does not contain subjAltName extension (or if it does, the same names are not included in the subjAltName's dNSName list).
bugs.impact: Connection with external server cannot be established. In case of forward proxy, bypass or intercept will fail.
bugs.workaround: In case of forward proxy bypass, configure IP address bypass instead of hostname bypass since IP address bypass check happens before SSL handshake. The second option is to update the external server's certificate to include the list of CommonNames in subjAltName extension as dNSName.
bugs.fix: The system now checks all CommonNames in a certificate's Subject field instead of checking only the longest one in length.

bugs.title: A specific sequence of packets to the HA listener may cause tmm to produce a core file
bugs.symptoms: A specific sequence of packets to the HA listener may cause tmm to produce a core file.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP is configured for HA.
bugs.impact: The TMM process may restart and produce a core file.

bugs.title: Portal Access incorrectly prefers charset from meta tag over the value from header
bugs.symptoms: If charset values in <meta> tag and Content-Type header are not equal, Portal Access prefers value from <meta> tag.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you have charset values in both the <meta> tag and in the HTTP header.
bugs.impact: This may result in unnecessary charset conversion of page content and corruption of some characters. Some characters in rewritten page may be garbled.
bugs.workaround: Remove <meta> tag from affected pages with iRule or modify its value to contain correct charset.
bugs.fix: Now, in Portal Access charset detection, the value from Content-Type header has precedence over value from <meta> tag.

bugs.title: Pool member's health monitors set to Member Specific does not display the active monitors
bugs.symptoms: When you configure a pool to have member-specific health monitoring, the active monitor no longer displays in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Have a pool member with Health Monitors set to Member Specific.
bugs.impact: The specified active monitors will be saved but won't be displayed as active.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to view a pool member's active monitors.
bugs.fix: Pool member's Health Monitors set to Member Specific now display active monitors.

bugs.title: No way to ensure the monitor works prior to applying the monitor to a pool
bugs.symptoms: There is no GUI method for ensuring that a monitor works prior to applying it to a pool.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a monitor to add to a pool.
bugs.impact: Monitor might fail. Requires external methods of determining source of failure.
bugs.workaround: Use tcpdump, curl, or other external method to determine why monitors are not functional.
bugs.fix: There is now a GUI method for ensuring that a monitor works prior to applying it to a pool.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as SAML IdP may fail to process signed authentication requests from some external SPs.
bugs.symptoms: When an external Service Provider (SP) canonicalizes authentication requests with the use of inclusive namespaces, a BIG-IP system used as SAML IdP may fail to process such requests. User's SSO will fail with following errors contained in /var/log/tmm: err tmm1[13063]: 014d0002:3: 9c7802e1: SSOv2 Digest from SAML message is invalid err tmm1[13063]: 014d0002:3: 9c7802e1: SSOv2 Error(12) Signature verification failed for SAML Authentication
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP is used as SAML IdP. - User performs SP-initiated SAML SSO. - External SAML SP sends signed authentication request, in which canonicalization was done with use of inclusive namespaces.
bugs.impact: Users are unable to perform SAML SSO with certain external service providers.
bugs.fix: Now BIG-IP APM as IdP SAML canonicalized authentication requests containing inclusive namespaces can be processed successfully.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of HTTP2 data frames larger than minimal frame size
bugs.symptoms: HTTP2 can vary frame size between 16K bytes (included) and 16 Mbytes (not included). When a client sends a data frame spawning more than one TCP segment, the BIG-IP system incorrectly decrements the frame size twice from the receive window. If the proxy flow control is disabled, this just creates an additional window update frame. If the proxy is in flow control, this causes a flow control error.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP2 profile is configured on a virtual server. -- Client sends a data frame larger than 16384 bytes, violating RFC. Note: The receiving maximum frame size of the BIG-IP is permanently set at 16384 bytes.
bugs.impact: HTTP2 resets the stream with FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When a client sends HTTP2 a data frame exceeding a negotiated maximum frame size, the BIG-IP system correctly resets the stream.

bugs.title: Configuration loading may fail when iRules calling procs in other iRules are deleted
bugs.symptoms: Loading of the configuration fail with a message indicating a previously deleted iRule cannot be found: 01020036:3: The requested rule (/Common/rule_uses_procs) was not found.
bugs.conditions: - iRule A is calling another iRule B using proc calls - iRule A is attached to a virtual server. - Detaching and deleting iRule A. - Loading the config (or performing config sync).
bugs.impact: iRules are still referenced after implicit deletion (via load). Configuration does not load.
bugs.workaround: Force reloading of the MCP binary database. For specific steps, see K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030).
bugs.fix: Configuration loading no longer fails when iRules calling procs in other iRules are deleted.

bugs.title: Active flows are aborted/torn down after PEM is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: Gradual memory leak or TMM crash may be observed.
bugs.conditions: Active flows passing through PEM are not aborted/torn down after PEM is disabled.
bugs.impact: Potential memory leak and TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Gradual memory leak or TMM crash no longer occurs if active flows are aborted/torn down after PEM is disabled.

bugs.title: Traffic Capturing is not reported to external log when "use-offbox" is set.
bugs.symptoms: When use-offbox is set in "analytics global-settings" transaction capturing is not send to the external log.
bugs.conditions: 1. use-offbox is set. 2. in analytics profile "Traffic Capturing Logging Type internal " is set.
bugs.impact: Traffic Capturing won't be reported to the external log.
bugs.workaround: Set Traffic Capturing Logging Type - external" in analytics profile.
bugs.fix: After the fix when use-offbox is set AVR will send traffic capturing data to the external log.

bugs.title: ClientSSL/ServerSSL profile does not report an error when a certain invalid CRL is associated with it when authentication is set to require
bugs.symptoms: Error is not reported if the profile is associated with an invalid Certificate Revocation List (CRL) that is not signed by trusted CAs, if the CRL issuer has the same subject name as one of the certs in trusted CA.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when associating CRLs with virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Error is not reported for invalid CRL.
bugs.workaround: OpenSSL command can be used to check if the CRL is signed by trusted CA.
bugs.fix: Error is reported in TMM logs if the CRL is not signed by trusted CA.

bugs.title: Unclear error string when setting invalid score values
bugs.symptoms: Setting invalid score value (for example, rule score or automatic transaction score) generates an unclear error in which the max value is printed as char (ASCII value of max, d is 100 in the following example): The value (144) is outside the acceptable value set [value equal to or less than d]. The message should read: The value (144) is outside the acceptable value set [value equal to or less than 100].
bugs.conditions: Setting invalid score value in tmsh (not in GUI).
bugs.impact: Misleading error message is posted. The impact is minimal. The correct value is used, it's just not displayed correctly in the error message.
bugs.workaround: Use GUI to get the appropriate error message.

bugs.title: Compatibility in bot defense iRules reasons from version 12.1.0 to version 13.0.0 or later
bugs.symptoms: Some specific iRules that use BOTDEFENSE::reason that worked in version 12.1.0 stop working after an upgrade to 13.0.0 or later.
bugs.conditions: An iRule exists that matches the string of a bot defense reason, for example: if {([BOTDEFENSE::reason] eq "passed browser challenge" ...
bugs.impact: The iRules that use the bot defense reason string may fail to match the new string.
bugs.workaround: You can manually update your iRules to use the correct bot defense reason string. Typically this is a matter of making the string case-insensitive. Here are some examples, but the list is extensive: From "Service to Other Module" to "Web-Scraping Detection". From "passed browser challenge" to "Passed Browser Challenge". From "passed captcha challenge" to "Passed CAPTCHA Challenge". From "whitelist" to "Whitelisted Transaction". For some of the reasons, a simple search and replace of: '[BOTDEFENSE::reason]' to '[string tolower [BOTDEFENSE::reason]]' would work

bugs.title: Portal Access: Same-origin AJAX rquest may fail if response contains non-wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin header
bugs.symptoms: Same-origin AJAX request fails via Portal Access if back-end response includes Access-Control-Allow-Origin header and its value differs from '*' and request origin.
bugs.conditions: - Same-origin AJAX request, for example: GET /some/file.ext HTTP/1.1 Host: http://example.com Origin: http://example.com - Back-end response with Access-Control-Allow-Origin header: HTTP/1.1 200 OK Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://another.com Without Portal Access, such a response is valid and accessible to client web application, if there were no redirects. But via Portal Access, the response is rejected.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to remove special query parameter 'F5_origin' from same-origin AJAX requests via Portal Access to disable CORS check emulation.
bugs.fix: Now same-origin AJAX requests are handled correctly in spite of Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.

bugs.title: SharePoint MS-OFBA browser window displays Javascript errors
bugs.symptoms: SharePoint MS-OFBA browser window displays Javascript errors while doing authentication.
bugs.conditions: -- SharePoint Access through LTM and APM. -- MS-OFBA iRule is used.
bugs.impact: JavaScript errors shown on the MS-OFBA browser window
bugs.fix: Now the SharePoint MS-OFBA browser window no longer displays Javascript errors while doing authentication from Microsoft applications.

bugs.title: APM daemon crashes when the LDAP query agent returns empty in its search results.
bugs.symptoms: APM daemon crashes when the LDAP query agent returns no search results.
bugs.conditions: APM provisioned with AD authentication setup.
bugs.impact: APM daemon crashes, need to restart RBA and WebSSO. This is a very rarely encountered issue.
bugs.workaround: Add LDAP Auth agent before the LDAP query to the existing policy. Note: Adding the extra agent, LDAP Auth agent, in the policy will preserve the functionality and features, enabling the policy to fail in LDAP Auth agent, instead of crash in LDAP Query agent.
bugs.fix: Now APM daemon no longer crashes when the LDAP query agent returns a specific type of null result from its search.

bugs.title: PVA support for uncommon protocols DoS vector
bugs.symptoms: A new HSB bitstream for VIPRION B4450 blades is needed to support IP uncommon protocols for DoS Vector.
bugs.conditions: Using the B4450 blade.
bugs.impact: No support for IP uncommon protocols for DoS Vector.
bugs.fix: HSB v3.2.13.0 bitsteam for VIPRION B4450 blades now provides support for IP uncommon protocols for DoS Vector.
bugs.behavior: This bitstream now supports IP uncommon protocols for DoS Vector. Any number of protocols with values between 0-255 can be simultaneously enabled.

bugs.title: Incomplete files still linked in /shared/vmisolinks
bugs.symptoms: If copying of an image file is interrupted and leaves a partial file with a .part or .filepart extension, it is still linked in /shared/vmisolinks and synced between blades.
bugs.conditions: Copy of an image to /shared/images is interrupted and a file with a .part or .filepart extension is left behind.
bugs.impact: The corrupted copy might appear valid when it is not.
bugs.workaround: Delete incomplete file copies with extension .part or .filepart.
bugs.fix: Csyncd ignores files with extensions .part or .filepart in /shared/images.

bugs.title: The GSLB Pool Member Manage page can cause Tomcat to drop the request when the Finished button is pressed
bugs.symptoms: Tomcat can potentially drop requests made by the client via the Web GUI on the GSLB Pool Members Manage page.
bugs.conditions: The config contains a large amount (in the thousands) of GSLB virtual servers or wide IP's, resulting in the action not being completed.
bugs.impact: The "Finished" button on that page does not save the changes made on that page.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with saving GSLB data via the GUI in large configurations.

bugs.title: FTP virtual server connections may rapidly reuse ephemeral ports
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system reuses ephemeral ports quickly, which might cause connections to fail, because those ports are in TIME-WAIT state on the server.
bugs.conditions: -- FTP active mode is used. -- Virtual server source-port change. -- Running on an affected platform: --- BIG-IP 5000 series (C109) --- BIG-IP 7000 series (D110) --- BIG-IP 10000s/10050s/10200v/10250v (D113, D112) --- B4300 / B4340N VIPRION blades (A108, A110)
bugs.impact: FTP active mode connections might fail.
bugs.workaround: There is no complete workaround. However, you can mitigate the issue using the default setting source-port=preserve on the virtual server. As alternatives, you can also try the following: -- Switching client traffic to Passive FTP. -- Enabling TIME_WAIT reuse on the FTP server, if the operating system supports it.

bugs.title: iCall script may log an error on execution
bugs.symptoms: An iCall script may log errors during execution while manipulating iStats. An example error is as follows: Failure in iCall script ${folder}/publish_stats while collecting application statistics. The error messages are due to file locking on the stats segment when multiple threads from multiple invocations of iCall scripts access the same file.
bugs.conditions: Multiple iCall scripts accessing the same data segment and log error messages.
bugs.impact: The script cannot record statistics for the interval during which it cannot access the data segment. Over time, the script daemon recovers and updates statistics. There is no impact on functionality.

bugs.title: iControl REST cannot stay in sync if /config/f5-rest-device-id is identical on each device
bugs.symptoms: When deploying an application such as an iAppLX application the LX-specific configuration is not synced, and you see a sync error in /var/log/restjavad.0.log.
bugs.conditions: This may occur if you have a device group established, but the /config/f5-rest-device-id contains an identical device ID on each of the devices. This could be triggered in a number of ways: - Cloning BIG-IP VMs - Extracting the same UCS file to each of the devices, then establishing a trust group
bugs.impact: Restjavad is unable to synchronize across the devices, as a result iAppLX applications fail to stay in sync.
bugs.workaround: The first test you should do is to look at the contents of /config/f5-rest-device-id on all devices. If any of the devices contain the same ID, you can perform the following procedure to reset iControl REST trust: Impact of procedure: the following procedure resets the rest storage which removes all iAppLX applications from your configuration. You will need to re-create and re-deploy any iAppLX applications that you had deployed. At the command prompt, run the following: rm /config/f5-rest-device-id; clear-rest-storage This will cause the f5-rest-device-id file to be re-generated and will clear the rest storage, at this point the application should stay in sync across devices once you re-install and re-deploy it.

bugs.title: After an upgrade, an URL from another policy's WSDL may be erroneously added after XML profile change
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, an URL from another policy's WSDL is erroneously added after modifying an XML profile.
bugs.conditions: An XML profile is modified following ASM upgrade.
bugs.impact: A URL from another policy is erroneously added to the policy.
bugs.workaround: The erroneously added URL should be deleted.
bugs.fix: URLs are added correctly as needed when XML profile is changed.

bugs.title: ASM Auto-Sync Device Group
bugs.symptoms: Some messages that were meant to be sent to peers in a device group are not successfully sent.
bugs.conditions: A mix of the following uses in GUI or REST API: 1) Creating/importing/deleting policies. 2) Accepting many suggestions at once. 3) Adjusting Policy Building Settings.
bugs.impact: 1) Overuse of full sync between devices. 2) Possible inconsistencies between devices. 3) Possibility of memory leak in rare cases.
bugs.workaround: Use manual sync groups for ASM sync.
bugs.fix: Communication for auto-sync groups repaired.

bugs.title: Traffic Capturing: Pool member that has a special name (internal activity) should be exported with its name, not an IP address
bugs.symptoms: For traffic capturing, if a pool member is assigned a special name (e.g., 'for internal activity'), the external AVR log will report the internal IP address instead of the pool member name.
bugs.conditions: 1. Assign name to internal pool member. 2. Enable HTTP traffic capturing. 3. Allow AVR to collect HTTP statistics. 4. View pool member name in external AVR log.
bugs.impact: External log reports internal IP address instead of pool member name.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The external AVR log now reports the pool member name as expected.

bugs.title: Memory Leak in ASM Sync Listener Process
bugs.symptoms: Following several sync errors, a memory leak occurs in the ASM sync listener process (asm_config_server.pl).
bugs.conditions: -- asm-sync is enabled on an auto-sync Device Group. -- Errors occur during attempts to sync, either due to full disk or in response to one or more of the following uses in GUI or REST API: + Creating/importing/deleting policies. + Accepting many suggestions at once. + Adjusting Policy Building Settings.
bugs.impact: RAM is increasing consumed leading to swap usage until the device reaches a panic state.
bugs.workaround: Restart asm_config_server on all devices using the following command: killall asm_config_server.pl
bugs.fix: Hard limits for memory size are now enforced for ASM processes. The sync listener process now shuts down and restarts after an hour of failed repeated attempts to synchronize the device group state.

bugs.title: Local Traffic Policies operating in First Match mode do not stop executing after the first matched rule if this has no action
bugs.symptoms: Local Traffic Policies configured for First Match mode may not stop executing after the first matched rule.
bugs.conditions: This happens when the first matched rule has no action (i.e. is set to ignore).
bugs.impact: This may cause Local Traffic Policies to execute an unintended action.
bugs.workaround: Rework the rules in your affected Local Traffic Policies so that every rule has at least one associated action.
bugs.fix: Execution of Local Traffic Policies now correctly stops after the first matched rule.

bugs.title: Closed connections remains in memory
bugs.symptoms: A connection remains open, which results in memory leaks in the tmm for the connections. The following command shows connections on traffic that was already closed: tmsh show sys conn.
bugs.conditions: A ASM_RESPONSE_VIOLATION iRule on the ASM-enabled virtual server. A request with connection: close.
bugs.impact: Memory increase due to connections left open. Incoming connections to the virtual server may fail and result in the BIG-IP sending a reset with a reset cause of "TCP closed".
bugs.workaround: If possible, remove this event from the iRule and/or add the OneConnect profile to the virtual server.

bugs.title: "Inherit traffic group from current partition / path" virtual-address setting is not synchronized during an incremental sync
bugs.symptoms: The "Inherit traffic group from current partition / path" virtual-address setting is not synchronized during an incremental sync.
bugs.conditions: Changing the "Inherit traffic group from current partition / path" setting and syncing to a peer unit using incremental sync.
bugs.impact: Peers in a Device Group will get out of sync.
bugs.workaround: Use a full sync instead.
bugs.fix: The "Inherit traffic group from current partition / path" virtual-address setting is now synchronized during an incremental sync.

bugs.title: TMM Crash
bugs.symptoms: Undisclosed conditions may cause TMM to crash
bugs.conditions: Undisclosed
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to HA failover
bugs.fix: Improve TMM reliability

bugs.title: While one chassis in a DSC is being rebooted, other members report spurious HA Group configuration errors
bugs.symptoms: Message of the form "notice sod[nnnn]: 010c006e:5: All devices in traffic group traffic-group-1(1 of 2) should have a HA group." is logged on peer devices when a Viprion chassis is being rebooted.
bugs.conditions: Multiple Viprion chassis are configured in a sync-failover device group, using HA Group scores.
bugs.impact: Log message indicates a configuration error that does not exist.
bugs.workaround: If these messages occur during a peer reboot, they should be ignored.
bugs.fix: Viprion chassis does not report HA Group configuration errors during peer reboot.

bugs.title: APM Profile access stats are not updated correctly
bugs.symptoms: The active and established sessions counts in the output of 'tmsh show apm profile access' command are not getting updated as sessions are established and terminated. At the same time, the following errors are showing up in the APM log: err tmm1[19902]: 01490574:3: (null):Common:00000000: Could not find tmstat. (/Common/Google_vsstats_key)
bugs.conditions: -- When session is established and terminated. -- Running the command: tmsh show apm profile access to view stats.
bugs.impact: APM profile access stats are not accurate.
bugs.fix: Now the tmsh command "tmsh show apm profile access" displays the correct profile access stats.

bugs.title: Wrong XML profile name Request Log details for XML violation
bugs.symptoms: After system upgrade, Request Log details for XML violation show XML profile name as 'N/A'.
bugs.conditions: System upgrade. Request Log details for XML violation.
bugs.impact: System upgrade does not synchronize properly between policy and already existing XML profiles. System functions properly on existing XML profiles, but violation report reference to the XML profile is wrong.
bugs.workaround: No workaround for already existing violation records. For new violation reports, run apply policy.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the correct XML profile name in the Request Log details for XML violation.

bugs.title: Automatically launched applications run with root permission on VPN establishment
bugs.symptoms: Configured applications are launched with root permissions on VPN establishment.
bugs.conditions: Network access rsource is configured to automatically launch application on VPN establishment.
bugs.impact: Application is launched as root. If application is interactive, user may be able to get root privilege
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround except not enabling automatic application launch in network access resource.
bugs.fix: Now application launches with the user privilege.

bugs.title: bigd crash (SIGSEGV) when running FQDN node monitors
bugs.symptoms: bigd processing FQDN node monitors may crash due to a timing issue when processing probe responses.
bugs.conditions: bigd is configured for FQDN node monitors.
bugs.impact: bigd crashes (SIGSEGV). The system restarts bigd automatically, and monitoring resumes. No other action is needed.
bugs.workaround: Although no workaround is available for bigd configured for FQDN node monitors, this crash occurs due to a timing issue, and should be rare.
bugs.fix: bigd no longer crashes (SIGSEGV) when running FQDN node monitors due to a timing issue.

bugs.title: DNS Express using wrong TTL for SOA RRSIG record in NoData response
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express returns an incorrect TTL for the SOA RRSIG record in a NoData response.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS Express configured. -- A query that results in a NoData response and DNSSEC signing requested.
bugs.impact: This brings the behavior in line with RFC2308. There is no known functional impact.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The TTL of the RRSIG record now matches the TTL of the covered SOA record.

bugs.title: When failing to load a UCS, the hostname is still changed, only in 12.1.2 or 13.0.0
bugs.symptoms: The platform-migrate option to the UCS load command is supposed to reject UCS archives generated on BIG-IP software v10.x. It does this; however, the hostname of the BIG-IP system changes to the one in the UCS.
bugs.conditions: You are trying to do a platform-migrate load to 12.1.2 or 13.0.0 of a UCS originating on a system running v10.x.
bugs.impact: The hostname is changed, but no other configuration is modified.
bugs.workaround: Set the hostname back to its old value.
bugs.fix: The hostname is now left unmodified.

bugs.title: Corrupted L2 FDB entries on B4450 blades might result in dropped traffic
bugs.symptoms: ARP replies reach front panel port of B4450 blades but fail to reach TMMs. This occurs because the switch in the B4450 blade has an L2 learning issue in the switch fabric that requires the system to correct the new L2 FDB entries learned on Higig trunks. The L2 module runs in poll mode by default, which is exposed to a 3-second race window in software, during which learning events in the switch hardware for a given L2 FDB entry can be lost. That can lead to corrupted L2 FDB entries and cause traffic hitting the corrupted L2 FDB entries to fail.
bugs.conditions: -- An L2 FDB entry is learned on Higig trunk. -- Multiple L2 learning events happen on the L2 FDB entry during the 3-second race window in software.
bugs.impact: The traffic hitting the corrupted L2 FDB entry will be dropped by the switch.
bugs.workaround: Delete the corrupted L2 FDB entries and cause the switch to re-learn them. To do so, identify the affected VLAN and flush L2 FDB entries on that VLAN using the following command: tmsh delete net fdb vlan {vlan_name}.
bugs.fix: A db variable switchboard.l2.mitigation was introduced to configure this feature. -- A value of "enable" allows packets to be forwarded in the case of corrupted L2 FDB entries. Packets will be hashed on source and destination addresses. Enabling forwarding this way is only a temporary measure. -- A value of "monitor" does not forward packets but will count packets which were affected by corrupted L2 FDB entries. The stat table switch/l2_mitgation, updated every 11 seconds, reports packet counts. Differences in packet counts are logged to /var/log/ltm. -- A value of "disable" disables both forwarding and packet counting. Packet counts are reset.

bugs.title: Portal access rewriting window.opener causes JS exception
bugs.symptoms: Portal access engine rewriting window.opener causes JavaScript exception error.
bugs.conditions: When rewriting window.opener.
bugs.impact: JavaScript exception error generated.
bugs.fix: The rewriting window.opener operation now completes with Message 'null', which is correct behavior. No JavaScript exception error is generated.

bugs.title: Failure to extend database continues to execute rather than halting because of fragmented state.
bugs.symptoms: Rarely occurring failure to extend database results in operations continuing to execute rather than halting because of fragmented state. Various behavior might occur, for example: unexpected traffic to disabled pool members, intermittent updated cert usage, receipt of messages such as 'MCP message handling failed' or 'Memory allocation failed: can't allocate memory to extend db size', and others.
bugs.conditions: TMM heap is fragmented such that memory allocation fails when extending the database.
bugs.impact: Operations continues to execute rather than halting, as might be expected. The system might report a variety of unexpected log messages and/or behaviors due to subsequent inconsistent state. Note: This is an extremely rare condition that occurs only when TMM is left in an inconsistent state. Although it is possible that this might eventually lead to bad behavior downstream, the event itself does not cause memory issues.

bugs.title: SSL renegotiation failed intermittently with AES-GCM cipher
bugs.symptoms: SSL failed to renegotiate intermittently with AES-GCM cipher because IV is not properly updated when a change cipher spec message is received.
bugs.conditions: This failure is more likely to occur during mutual authentication.
bugs.impact: Some servers authenticate client using renegotiation. This issue prevents their clients from properly connecting to the servers.
bugs.workaround: Disable AES-GCM cipher.
bugs.fix: The system now properly updates AES-GCM IV when a change cipher spec message is received.

bugs.title: Provide the ability to globally specifiy a DSCP value.
bugs.symptoms: The DSCP value is not configurable for some types of traffic, which can lead to dropped traffic during adverse network conditions.
bugs.conditions: Under adverse network conditions, monitor traffic can be dropped by the network.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP DNS incorrectly reports resources as unavailable because monitor traffic is dropped by the network due to congestion with unrelated traffic.
bugs.fix: Setting the new db variable tm.egressdscp to a value other than the default value of 0, results in the system setting the DSCP value for outgoing traffic to the configured value.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition Single-process requirement not enforced
bugs.symptoms: Although it is not a supported operation, a BIG-IP administrator can change the number of threads TMM runs per process by modifying the 'tmm.threads' db variable. Virtual Edition TMM code is written with the assumption that all TMMs run as threads in one TMM process, so modifying this variable can cause multi-process TMMs, which do not pass traffic. Running the following command doesn't display the dataplane interfaces for one or more TMMs: tmctl -f /var/tmstat/blade/tmm<x> -s name,if_index interface_stat
bugs.conditions: When tmm.threads db variable is set a value other than 0 (the default value).
bugs.impact: Some of the TMMs, though launched and running, do not pass traffic, resulting in degraded performance (throughput, CPS) for the assigned number of cores.
bugs.workaround: Do not change the tmm.threads db variable from its default value of 0.
bugs.fix: With this fix, any non-default value set to tmm.threads db variable is ignored.

bugs.title: Incorrect information about number of cores/guests on i11000 platforms
bugs.symptoms: -- Commands 'getconf _NPROCESSORS_CONF' and 'guishell -c 'select max_vcmp_guests from blade_info'' show different information. -- Command 'tmsh create vcmp guest <guest_name>' fails and reports an error: Could not allocate vCMP guest (<guest_name>) because fragmented resources.
bugs.conditions: -- i11000 hardware with 36 cores. -- vCMP guests are utilizing 32 cores of the system (4, 8-core guests are installed). -- Try to install a new guest.
bugs.impact: -- vCMP guest GUI page shows 36 cores are available, but only 32 cores are actually available for vCMP guests. -- After installation of 4, 8-core guests, the BIG-IP system should not allow new guest installations. If you try to install a new guest, the system reports an error that does not describe the real issue: Could not allocate vCMP guest (<guest_name>) because fragmented resources.
bugs.workaround: Limit the number of vCMP guests to the number reported by the command: guishell -c 'select max_vcmp_guests from blade_info'

bugs.title: IP Intelligence logging publisher removal can cause tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart immediately after removing global ip-intelligence logging publisher.
bugs.conditions: 1) Global IP Intelligence logging enabled. 2) While new incoming connections are handled by the system, delete the global logging publisher using the following command: modify security log profile global-network ip-intelligence { log-publisher none }
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. This is an intermittent, timing-related issue. Note: Because deleting the global ip-intelligence logging configuration publisher is uncommon, and might occur once, at setup, this issue is unlikely to manifest.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, other than to not delete the ip-intelligence global logging publisher when heavy traffic is being handled.
bugs.fix: Error handling now checks for NULL publisher and prevents the TMM restart.

bugs.title: GUI LTM Pool Statistics Page running out of memory with large number of Pools
bugs.symptoms: When there is a large number of configured Pools, it can adversely affect Pool Statistics Page display, causing an Out of Memory error.
bugs.conditions: Configure 2200 or more pools, and go to the Pool Statistics page.
bugs.impact: The page does not display because it causes Tomcat to run out of memory and restart automatically.
bugs.workaround: You can increase the memory allocated to Tomcat. For more information, see K9719: Error Message: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K9719

bugs.title: Rekey SSH sessions after one hour
bugs.symptoms: Common Criteria requires that SSH session be rekeyed at least every hour
bugs.conditions: SSH connections to or from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: SSH sessions are rekeyed in response to the quantity of data transferred, or on user demand, but not on the basis of elapsed time
bugs.workaround: If time-based rekeying is required in your environment, edit the SSH configuration to include a RekeyLimit with both data and time parameters using a command similar to the following: tmsh modify sys sshd include 'RekeyLimit 256M 3600s' Outbound SSH client connections can be modified by adding the same RekeyLimit configuration to /config/ssh/ssh_config or by including that option on the command line when calling the ssh client.
bugs.fix: SSH sessions are now rekeyed every hour regardless of the quantity of data transferred.

bugs.title: Guest configurations with mergeable buffers disabled are not supported.
bugs.symptoms: Guest configurations with mergeable buffers disabled are not supported.
bugs.conditions: Guest configuration explicitly disables mergeable buffers: <host mrg_rxbuf='off'/>.
bugs.impact: tmm core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. When mergeable buffers are disabled, the 13.0.0 virtio driver crashes and the 13.1.0 driver stops processing, i.e., it does not attach to the device.
bugs.workaround: Do not disable mergeable buffers.
bugs.fix: The system now logs an alert rather than enters a restart loop. Note: There is no plan to support disabled mergeable buffers.

bugs.title: Rewrite may crash on empty values in Headers list of Portal Access Resource Item configuration
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access rewrite process may crash when resource item configuration for the current request contains invalid value in Headers advanced option.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if the Headers options are empty, for example: tmsh modify apm resource portal-access <resource> items modify { <resource item> { headers { {} } } }
bugs.impact: Rewrite crashes.
bugs.workaround: Fix the configuration: 1. find resource and resource item names of configuration blocks containing 'headers none' using the following command: tmsh list apm resource portal-access. 2.
