For each affected resource and its item, run the following command: tmsh modify apm resource portal-access <resource> items modify { <resource item> { headers none } }
bugs.fix: APM Portal Access rewrite no longer crashes on invalid Custom Headers configuration.

bugs.title: On Linux, application launch parameter string may be truncated in some cases
bugs.symptoms: Application will be launched with truncated parameters if the parameter string specified in the UI contains the ampersand '&' character
bugs.conditions: Application tunnel feature is used on Linux. Application parameter string contains & character, and the string is unquoted.
bugs.impact: Application will be launched with incorrect parameters.
bugs.workaround: Encapsulate the parameter sting in double quotes.

bugs.title: PEM bigTCP optimization is wrongly selected in case of UNKNOWN subscriber policy.
bugs.symptoms: Some actions of PEM policy require full-proxy implementation. They do not work for bigTCP. BigTCP gets selected for those actions too.
bugs.conditions: PEM listener is configured with optimization. An UNKNOWN user policy gets applied with an action that cannot be used with bigTCP (HTTP redirect for example).
bugs.impact: Subscribers whose credentials are not known do not get correct remedial action.
bugs.workaround: Disable optimization in PEM profile. Create separate virtual servers with bigTCP to get the utility of optimization.

bugs.title: Safari, Firefox in incognito mode on iOS device cannot pass persistent client identification challenge
bugs.symptoms: When running Safari or Firefox in incognito mode on iOS devices, browser gets TCP RST and will not be able to pass client-side challenge. The system posts the following error in tmm log: failed parsing header 3.
bugs.conditions: 1. Web scraping is configured. 2. Persistent client identification is enabled. 3. Using Safari or Firefox on iOS devices.
bugs.impact: Browser cannot access the site.
bugs.workaround: Turn off persistent client identification.
bugs.fix: Safari, Firefox in incognito mode on iOS device can now pass persistent client identification challenge.

bugs.title: TCP analytics does not release resources under specific sequence of packets
bugs.symptoms: TCP analytics does not release memory when a specific sequence of packets is observed, and memory usage increases as more such flows occur.
bugs.conditions: -- A TCP analytics profile is configured to collect clientside/serverside analytics data. -- AVR is provisioned. -- FastL4 and HTTP profiles are configured. -- A specific sequence of packets (on the serverside) occurs.
bugs.impact: Main memory occupied by TCP analytics is not released which might lead to memory exhaustion on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Turn off collecting TCP analytics data for the virtual server.
bugs.fix: TCP analytics now releases resources properly.

bugs.title: BGP last update timer incorrectly resets to 0
bugs.symptoms: In ZebOS, every time the scan timer resets it also incorrectly resets the BGP last update timer as shown under the imish command 'sh ip route'. Output from 'sh ip route': 4054fdc0-3e51-4079-b52f-4a3b058a3f93#sh ip ro ... B 10.30.0.0/16 [20/0] via 10.10.1.2, eno33554952, 00:00:32 [20/0] via 10.10.1.6, eno33554952, 00:00:32 ... 4054fdc0-3e51-4079-b52f-4a3b058a3f93#sh ip ro ... B 10.30.0.0/16 [20/0] via 10.10.1.2, eno33554952, 00:00:33 [20/0] via 10.10.1.6, eno33554952, 00:00:33 ... 4054fdc0-3e51-4079-b52f-4a3b058a3f93#sh ip ro ... B 10.30.0.0/16 [20/0] via 10.10.1.2, eno33554952, 00:00:00 <<<< shouldn't reset [20/0] via 10.10.1.6, eno33554952, 00:00:00
bugs.conditions: Once ZebOS has learned a route from a BGP peer the route will show up under 'sh ip route' and the BGP last update timer will incorrectly reset.
bugs.impact: None. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP no longer resets the last update time of learned routes via BGP.

bugs.title: Polling time waiting for I2C bus transactions in the bcm56xxd daemon needs to be reduced
bugs.symptoms: On platforms that run the bcm56xxd daemon, the polling time that the system waits for I2C bus transactions to complete runs too long. On systems with I2C bus issues, this can lead to bcm56xxd core files, because the bcm56xxd daemon doesn't reset the watchdog so the watchdog timer kills the process.
bugs.conditions: This is an issue only when there is a stuck I2C bus, which occurs rarely.
bugs.impact: bcm56xxd process may core and restart. That typically resets the I2C bus, which resolves any issues.
bugs.workaround: None. Typically, the issue resolves itself.
bugs.fix: The number of times the bcm56xxd process polls for an I2C bus transaction to complete is reduced to prevent bcm56xxd core files.

bugs.title: GUI image list contains misleading 'MD5 Sum Verified' field
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, images in the Image List and Hotfix List contain a field called 'MD5 Sum Verified', which is misleading since no such verification is actually done.
bugs.conditions: Using BIG-IP GUI and viewing the Image List and Hotfix List.
bugs.impact: It appears that MD5 sums are being verified when in reality much more limited tests are done.
bugs.fix: Replace 'MD5 Sum Verified' with 'BIG-IP Image Verified' in Image List and Hotfix List in BIG-IP GUI to more accurately reflect our verification procedures.

bugs.title: MSRDP persistence does not work across route domains.
bugs.symptoms: MSRDP persistence doesn't work with non-default route domains.
bugs.conditions: Configure a virtual server with a MSRDP persistence profile and a pool using a non-default route domain.
bugs.impact: MSRDP persistence does not work.
bugs.workaround: Implement MSRDP persistence using iRules.
bugs.fix: MSRDP persistence with non-default route domains works correctly now.

bugs.title: TMM might crash while using SSL profiles on BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash while using SSL profiles on BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms.
bugs.conditions: -- TMOS v11.5.4 HF3. -- SSL profile active. -- BIG-IP 2000/4000 platform.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The cause of the crash was identified and removed.

bugs.title: MCPD does not prevent deleting an iRule that contains in-use procedures
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule that is attached to a virtual server makes a procedure call in a different iRule, it is possible to delete the different iRule with no error. MCPD contains validation that should prevent a user from deleting an iRule that is currently in use by a virtual server, e.g.: 01070265:3: The rule (/Common/rule_uses_procs) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a virtual server (/Common/vs_http). However, if an iRule attached to a virtual server makes a procedure call in a different iRule, it is possible to delete the different iRule with no error. This results in a configuration that will subsequently fail to load (during a config load, MCPD validation will catch this), or will fail if a full configuration sync is performed.
bugs.conditions: Must be using iRules that call into other iRules.
bugs.impact: System gets into a state where traffic may fail unexpectedly, and subsequent reboots, configuration loads, upgrades, or configuration sync operations will fail.
bugs.workaround: None. Use caution when deleting iRules, especially iRules that call into other iRules.

bugs.title: SSL persistence parsing issues due to SSL / TCP boundary mismatch
bugs.symptoms: When the SSL client or server system is set up to send SSL messages whose boundaries do not align with underlying TCP boundaries, the parser fails when SSL persistence is enabled. So, any SSL record spanning over multiple TCP segments (in this case it's ServerHello, Certificate, and ServerHelloDone) triggers the issue with the SSID error RST cause. This can also result from a message size exceeding the maximum configured size (default is 32K).
bugs.conditions: [1] SSL persistence is enabled. [2a] SSL message boundary does not align with underlying TCP segment boundary. One example of boundary mismatch is when the TCP MTU size is changed to a lower value (around 1200 bytes). Even then there may be specific values for which the boundaries match and parsing succeeds. [2b] The message size is greater than the maximum configured size (default 32k).
bugs.impact: When the parsing fails, the SSL client or server hangs and times out. In other words, SSL traffic is affected. The SSL parsing should succeed regardless of a match or mismatch between SSL message boundary and TCP segment boundary.
bugs.workaround: Disable SSL persistence.
bugs.fix: The system now switches the state of the SSL persistence to pass through all remaining messages, since no further parsing is needed.

bugs.title: With QoS LB, packet rate score is calculated incorrectly and dominates the QoS score
bugs.symptoms: When choosing QoS Load balance, packet rate is dominating the score.
bugs.conditions: QoS load balance.
bugs.impact: Load balance decision is mostly impacted by packet rate.
bugs.fix: Corrected a calculation error for QoS score involving packet rate.

bugs.title: Windows 10 Creators Update breaks RD Gateway functionality in BIG-IP APM
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to Windows 10 Creators Update (version 1703), when attempting to connect to a remote desktop through APM with the Remote Desktop Gateway (RDG) feature, the remote desktop client is not able to authenticate and connect. Windows 10 Version 1703 RDP client is using Negotiate HTTP authentication scheme, while APM requires NTLM scheme for RD Gateway.
bugs.conditions: - You are accessing Microsoft Remote Desktop through BIG-IP APM using Remote Desktop Gateway (RDG) feature. - You upgrade to Windows 10 Creators Update (version 1703).
bugs.impact: Remote desktop client is not able to authenticate and connect to the desktop.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Force the Windows RDP client to use NTLM authentication scheme (instead of Negotiate) by setting Group Policy 'User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Remote Desktop Services\RD Gateway\Set RD Gateway authentication method' to 'Ask for credentials, use NTLM protocol'. -- Use the following iRule to convert Negotiate to NTLM: when HTTP_REQUEST { set is_rdg_request [expr { [HTTP::method] starts_with "RDG_" }] if {!$is_rdg_request} { return; } set auth [HTTP::header Authorization] set is_nego_auth [expr { $auth contains "Negotiate" }] if { $is_nego_auth } { set auth [string map {"Negotiate" "NTLM"} $auth] HTTP::header replace Authorization $auth } } when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { if {!$is_rdg_request || !$is_nego_auth} { return; } catch { set auth [HTTP::header WWW-Authenticate] if { $auth contains "NTLM" } { set auth [string map {"NTLM" "Negotiate"} $auth] HTTP::header replace WWW-Authenticate $auth } } }
bugs.fix: After upgrading to Windows 10 Creators Update (version 1703), the RDP client can still authenticate and connect via APM used as RD Gateway.

bugs.title: APM Webtop max session timeout countdown reports incorrect value
bugs.symptoms: Max session timeout countdown timer on APM end user's webtop is reset when refreshing the webtop
bugs.conditions: 'Maximum Session Timeout' setting at Access :: Profiles/Policies is configured as less than default (7 days).
bugs.impact: End user's APM webtop can render incorrect value for Max session timeout countdown timer.
bugs.fix: Max session timeout countdown timer reflects correct value when APM webtop is refreshed.

bugs.title: iRule DNS::ttl does not allow 0 (zero)
bugs.symptoms: DNS::rr cannot set ttl to 0. The system returns the following message: error: [internal error "unexpected return code"][DNS::ttl $rr 0].
bugs.conditions: -- Using iRule DNS::ttl. -- Trying to set ttl to 0.
bugs.impact: DNS::rr cannot set ttl to 0, the resolver cache can't be disabled, and the system returns an error: error: [internal error "unexpected return code"][DNS::ttl $rr 0]
bugs.fix: iRule DNS::ttl now allows a 0 (zero) setting. iRule with ttl 0 can now be saved as expected.

bugs.title: Memory usage with MBLB SIP ingress buffer on standby
bugs.symptoms: Memory usage increases to high levels when the ingress-max profile setting is set to a large value.
bugs.conditions: Incoming SIP messages are mirrored to standby, then the flow is aborted on active.
bugs.impact: Degraded performance. With the built-in MBLB profile allocations will go up to 50 and stay there until the 'while' is killed on the client and the flow is allowed to expire. With a non-default MBLB profile, allocations will go as high as the ingress-max setting.
bugs.workaround: - Make sure there is at least one available pool member. - Use default MBLB profile, or at least ingress-max set close to the default (50).

bugs.title: Rolling forward with HTTPS monitors in the configuration with mismatched keys and certs
bugs.symptoms: If you roll forward, have HTTPS monitors in the configuration and use the monitor's attributes key and cert, make sure the key and cert are matching. Currently there is no validation in the HTTPS monitor for such mismatch. This feature will deprecate these attributes and move to SSL profile instead. If they are not matching, it will result in roll forward failure.
bugs.conditions: If you roll forward and have HTTPS monitors in the configuration and you are using attributes key and cert in the monitor
bugs.impact: If they are not matching, it will result in roll forward failure.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the key and cert of any HTTPS monitors are matching before you proceed to roll forward.

bugs.title: "oops" "bad transition" messages occur
bugs.symptoms: The /var/log/ltm log shows many "oops" "bad transition" messages.
bugs.conditions: These messages occur due to internal invariant violations on full proxy TCP virtual servers. Ramcache or SSL on these virtual servers are likely causes. There may be yet unknown causes.
bugs.impact: Connections encountering these errors are aborted.
bugs.workaround: The excess logging may be stopped by setting the DB variable tmm.oops to "silent". These errors won't be reported but connections will still be aborted.
bugs.fix: The conditions under which this error occurred have been resolved.

bugs.title: Blade family migration may fail
bugs.symptoms: Migrating the configuration from a B2100 blade to a newer variant, as documented in the "Migrating the Configuration on B2000 Series Blades" page in the "VIPRION Systems: Blade Migration" manual, may show output indicating a failure.
bugs.conditions: All such blade upgrades.
bugs.impact: The line 'load ucs failed!' should be ignored. If the line '/var/local/ucs/upgradeConfig-your-serial-number.ucs is loaded.' is present, then the UCS load was in fact successful and you can proceed with the instructions.
bugs.workaround: The line 'load ucs failed!' should be ignored. If the line '/var/local/ucs/upgradeConfig-your-serial-number.ucs is loaded.' is present, then the UCS load was in fact successful and you can proceed with the instructions.

bugs.title: MRF add 'existing_connection_only' and 'outgoing_connection_instance_seed' two iRule commands
bugs.symptoms: If the MRF 'existing_connection_only' is not there, then MRF will forward the new message to either the existing connection or creating a new connection. If the MRF 'outgoing_connection_instance_seed' is not there, then the generation of the connection's instance number will use some internal originating connection id. Same client IP with different src_port may end up to different outgoing connection.
bugs.conditions: If these two new iRule commands were not there.
bugs.impact: 1. Won't always reuse the existing connection. 2. The requests from same client IP with different src_port, the outgoing connection may be different.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: MR::message existing_connections_only <boolean> Gets or sets a flag that instructs the MRF to only forward the message using existing connections, and if a connection to the selected host does not exist then the route will fail. MR::message outgoing_connection_instance_seed <integer>Gets or if been set by this iRule then this seed will be used to generate the connection instance number instead of this generated by some internal originating connection id. (See MR::connection_instance iRule command). If the number received is larger than 32 bit then the 64 bit number will be hashed to 32 bit number.

bugs.title: Upgrade to 11.5.4 HF3 may remove valid cipher suite configuration from SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: During the upgrade to 11.5.4 HF3, the upgrade will remove the DHE-DSS from cipher suite, which will cause the cipher suites configured beginning with the characters '@', '+', '-', or '!' will be removed from the configuration.
bugs.conditions: clientssl/serverssl profile ciphers configuration contains keywords beginning with the characters '@', '+', '-', or '!'.
bugs.impact: Cipher suites are configured using keywords such as AES, AES-GCM, !DES, -ADH, @STRENGTH, etc. The issue causes keywords beginning with the characters '@', '+', '-', or '!' to be removed from the configuration. For example, if the cipher suite configuration before installing 11.5.4 HF3 was: 'NATIVE:!SSLV2:!SSLV3:!MD5:!EXPORT:!LOW:ECDHE+AES-GCM:ECDHE+AES:DHE+AES-GCM:DHE+AES:AES-GCM+RSA:RSA+AES:RSA+3DES:!RC4:!ADH:!ECDHE_ECDSA:!ECDH_ECDSA:!ECDH_RSA:!DHE-RSA-DES-CBC3-SHA:!ECDHE-RSA-DES-CBC3-SHA:!DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:+DES-CBC3-SHA' After installing 11.5.4 HF3 it would be reduced to: 'NATIVE:ECDHE+AES-GCM:ECDHE+AES:DHE+AES-GCM:DHE+AES:AES-GCM+RSA:RSA+AES:RSA+3DES'
bugs.workaround: Manually restore the clientssl/serverssl profile cipher configuration.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue that causes the cipher suites configured beginning with the characters '@', '+', '-', or '!' to be removed from the configuration on upgrade.

bugs.title: Tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes while passing traffic and generates core file.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: When triggered by a DHCP Lease query, subscriber ID with DHCP Option 37/38 is not supported.
bugs.symptoms: If configured to include DHCP Option 37/38, the subscriber ID field will be empty.
bugs.conditions: DHCP Lease query should use a DHCP virtual server with Option 37 or Option 38 configured to be part of the subscriber ID.
bugs.impact: Creation of subscribers with empty subscriber ID.
bugs.workaround: Do not use Option 37 or Option 38 as part of the subscriber ID in a DHCP virtual server that is to be used by a DHCP Lease query.

bugs.title: Single-NIC BIG-IP VE may erroneously revert to the default management httpd port after a configuration reload
bugs.symptoms: The single Network Interface Card (NIC) BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) may erroneously revert to the default management httpd port after you reload the configuration.
bugs.conditions: Management traffic port has been set to a value other than default port 8443.
bugs.impact: Management traffic port will revert to 8443 after any action which reloads configuration.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure port after each configuration reload using the following command: modify sys httpd ssl-port 443.

bugs.title: SSL sends HUDEVT_SENT to TCP in wrong state which causes HTTP disconnect the handshake.
bugs.symptoms: SSL sends HUDEVT_SENT to TCP in wrong state which causes HTTP disconnect the handshake.
bugs.conditions: SSL sends HUDEVT_SENT to TCP in wrong state.
bugs.impact: Then HTTP disconnects the handshake
bugs.fix: Don't allow SSL send HUDEVT_SENT event in the wrong state.

bugs.title: JS error when leaving page opened for several minutes
bugs.symptoms: Google Chrome delays JS execution when the tab is not active. Therefore anti-debug module acts as if someone is trying to debug JS code.
bugs.conditions: -- JS runs in hidden tab in Google Chrome. -- Anti-debug functionality is active. -- Page is left open for several minutes.
bugs.impact: Errors in console and JS logic is incorrectly executed.
bugs.workaround: Identify hidden tab and pause anti-debug functionality.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly handles JS code running in a hidden tab and pauses anti-debug check.

bugs.title: Transient error may appear in bd.log shortly after Signature Set is added to policy
bugs.symptoms: A transient error may appear in bd.log and asm.log shortly after a Signature Set is newly associated with a security policy. In bd.log, the messages appear similar to the following: ECARD_POLICY|ERR |Apr 09 01:00:23.205|24966|attack_patterns.cpp:0027|signature collection with id: 13 doesn't exist ATTACK_SIG|ERR |Apr 09 01:00:23.205|24966|attack_patterns_funcs.cpp:0083|Signature collection id: 13 Can't be acquired In asm.log, the messages appear similar to the following: info perl[20236]: 01310053:6: ASMConfig change: Policy Signature Set High Accuracy Detection Evasion Signatures [add]: Alarm was set to enabled. Policy Signature Set Name was set to High Accuracy Detection Evasion Signatures. Block was set to enabled. Learn was set to enabled. { audit: policy = /Common/policy2, username = admin, client IP = 192.168.188.44 } info perl[20236]: 01310053:6: ASMConfig change: Policy Signature Set High Accuracy Signatures [add]: Alarm was set to enabled. Policy Signature Set Name was set to High Accuracy Signatures. Block was set to enabled. Learn was set to enabled. { audit: policy = /Common/policy2, username = admin, client IP = 192.168.188.44 }
bugs.conditions: A Signature Set is newly associated with a security policy.
bugs.impact: A transient error may appear in bd.log and asm.log.
bugs.fix: No errors appear in in bd.log after a Signature Set change.

bugs.title: Rename Remote Logging format 'Key-Value Pairs' to 'Key-Value Pairs (Splunk)'
bugs.symptoms: 'Key-Value Pairs' logging format name does not mention 'Splunk', which makes it inconsistent with 'Common Event Format (ArcSight)'.
bugs.conditions: This is visible in Logging Profile :: Application Security, by choosing Storage Destination: Remote Storage, and then check Logging Format
bugs.impact: Remote Logging format is 'Common Event Format (ArcSight)' in one case, and 'Key-Value Pairs' in the other.
bugs.fix: Remote Logging format 'Key-Value Pairs' has been renamed to 'Key-Value Pairs (Splunk)'.

bugs.title: High memory usage when using the ICAP server
bugs.symptoms: High UMU memory when using the ICAP server.
bugs.conditions: -- ICAP is in use. -- There are long requests (requests longer than 128 KB) that should get to the ICAP server.
bugs.impact: UMU memory goes up.
bugs.workaround: -- Decrease the max concurrent long requests. -- Decrease the size for the long requests buffer size. -- Make sure the ICAP server is up and running and responding quickly (the issue will be more visible when the ICAP server is lagging).

bugs.title: User with role 'Manager' cannot delete/publish LTM policy.
bugs.symptoms: User with role 'Manager' cannot delete/publish LTM policy. audit.log contains a message similar to the following: notice icrd_child[18194]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=18194 user=Manager folder=/Manager module=(tmos)# status=[01070822:3: Access Denied: User (Manager) may not delete objects in partition (Common)] cmd_data=publish ltm policy /Manager/Drafts/draft-test.
bugs.conditions: -- User with 'Manager' role. -- Attempting to delete or publish an LTM policy.
bugs.impact: Operation does not complete, and system posts error.

bugs.title: Rarely if a subscriber delete is performed following HA switchover, tmm may crash
bugs.symptoms: If a subscriber delete is performed following a HA switchover, tmm may coredump. The probability of this scenario is rare, where a subscriber may have been freed during switchover and a subsequent forced delete command quickly follows.
bugs.conditions: -- A subscriber delete command followed by a HA switchover. -- During the switchover, the subscriber was freed.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now removes the subscriber index from the table if present in these cases.

bugs.title: Packet Tester is still available in the GUI when AFM is not provisioned
bugs.symptoms: The Packet Tester is an AFM-only tool, but is available in the GUI when AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system with AFM not licensed.
bugs.impact: The packet tester is available to use when it should not be.
bugs.fix: The Packet Tester is no longer available unless AFM is licensed. This is correct behavior

bugs.title: Gateway pool action may trigger the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to produce a core file and restart.
bugs.symptoms: As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- TMM generates a core file in the /shared/core directory. -- Your BIG-IP system logs a SIGFPE to the /var/log/tmm file at the same time TMM produces a core file and restarts. -- In one of the /var/log/tmm log files, you may observe error messages similar to the following example: notice panic: ../modules/hudfilter/hudfilter.c:1063: Assertion "valid node" failed. notice ** SIGFPE **
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP system is configured to route traffic using a gateway pool. -- The gateway pool is configured with Action On Service Down = Reject. -- The pool monitor marks all members of the gateway pool as unavailable. -- A connection is rejected by the gateway pool.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system temporarily fails to process traffic while the TMM process restarts. If the BIG-IP system is configured for high availability (HA), the system fails over to a peer system.
bugs.workaround: Set service-down-action to none or reselect.
bugs.fix: Gateway pool action no longer triggers TMM to produce a core file and restart.

bugs.title: Running tcpdump from TMSH cannot capture the local "tmm" interface
bugs.symptoms: Cannot run tcpdump against the "tmm" interface. System posts errors similar to the following: tcpdump: pcap_loop: Device /Common/tmm not found tcpdump: ioctl: No such device This occurs because the 'tmm0' interface was renamed to 'tmm' beginning in v12.1.0, but the libbigpacket conditional logic to handle "special device names" still references 'tmm0'.
bugs.conditions: -- When running tmsh, an environment variable ("TMOS_PATH") is set. -- The user logs in to the CLI with a default shell of tmsh (either as configured, or with a role assigned via remote-roles), or tries to run tcpdump via tmsh.
bugs.impact: Cannot run tcpdump on the 'tmm' internal interface.
bugs.workaround: Unset the 'TMOS_PATH' environment variable before running tcpdump.

bugs.title: AFM support of firewall rule UUID
bugs.symptoms: Currently UUID is generated on BIG-IQ, but it is not visible to BIG-IP/AFM, and it cannot be inserted back into the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- Firewall rules are read, modified, or deleted. -- Firewall rules are matched against firewall log.
bugs.impact: UUID cannot be used to identify firewall rules.
bugs.workaround: Policy/Rule-list Name and Rule Name pair can be used to identify firewall rule.
bugs.fix: UUID value is assigned to each firewall rule and can be used to identify the rule.

bugs.title: Possible performance impact on some SSL connections
bugs.symptoms: Some SSL connections may be delayed by almost exactly 5 seconds. The delay occurs between the SSL client hello and the server hello response from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL configured on a Virtual Server. Affects VIPRION/vCMP Guests. -- Client connects with an SSL session ID that is not in the cache, and in a very specific format that causes tmm to associate the session ID to a blade that does not exist.
bugs.impact: Performance may be impacted on those SSL connections.
bugs.workaround: Disable SSL session cache by setting cache-size to zero in the clientssl profile.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue that might cause performance impact on certain SSL connections.

bugs.title: SMB monitor marks node down
bugs.symptoms: Server Message Block (SMB) monitor marks node down after upgrading.
bugs.conditions: Samba server only accepts plaintext or lanman auth. SMB monitor begins to fail after upgrading.
bugs.impact: Monitor marked down, impairing services.
bugs.workaround: Modify the /etc/samba/smb.conf and in the [global] section, add the following lines: client ntlmv2 auth = No client lanman auth = Yes client plaintext auth = Yes

bugs.title: Extraneous OSPF retransmissions and ospfTxRetransmit traps can be sent
bugs.symptoms: When using OSPF with high load and network recalculation there is a possibility of a race condition that can lead to additional OSPF retransmissions being sent out. This might also cause SNMP traps to be sent, if configured on the system.
bugs.conditions: -- OSPF routing protocol configured. -- System configured to send SNMP traps. -- OSPF instability/networking flaps. Note: The greater the number of routes flapping, the more likely to see the condition.
bugs.impact: There is no impact on the OSPF processing itself. The additional traffic does not cause failing adjacencies or loss of routing information. However, this might cause many additional OSPF related traps to be sent, which might cause additional load on the external network monitoring system.
bugs.workaround: While this does not have a direct workaround, you may want to investigate the cause of the network/OSPF instability that causes the additional retransmissions.

bugs.title: TMM can restart when VLAN keyed connections are disabled.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may restart intermittently when VLAN-keyed connections are disabled.
bugs.conditions: VLAN-keyed connections are disabled. Several types of traffic can cause this, including FTP traffic and multicast traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: Disabling VLAN-keyed connections no longer causes TMM to restart.

bugs.title: Allow the system to retrieve a CRL from the CRLDP(CRL distribution point) and verify the SSL server's ceritificate status using the CRL.
bugs.symptoms: The system has no ability to download a CRL file from its CRLDP (which is usually a HTTP server).
bugs.conditions: -- SSL handshake. -- Receive a certificate from the SSL server, which contains a CRLDP URL (usually an HTTP URL) as a certificate extension.
bugs.impact: The system cannot check the SSL server's certificate status by checking its CRL file.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The system can now download the CRL file from the HTTP URL listed on SSL server's certificate and check the certificate's status against the CRL file.

bugs.title: tmm cache resolver should not cache response with TTL=0
bugs.symptoms: tmm cache resolver caches responses with TTL=0, and it shouldn't.
bugs.conditions: TTL is set to 0 on the BIG-IP DNS system, so TMM will see TTL=0 from the DNS answer.
bugs.impact: tmm cache resolver caches responses with TTL=0.
bugs.fix: The system no longer caches ttl=0 response for tmm cache resolver. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: PIM can be configured to use a floating self IP address
bugs.symptoms: Using PIM-Sparse Mode for multicast traffic with BGP for unicast routing/reverse path filtering may prevent PIM neighbor routers from switching from the RPT to the SPT.
bugs.conditions: -- PIM-Sparse Mode. -- BGP. -- Floating self IP address.
bugs.impact: Routers upstream and including BIG-IP will never receive PIM JOIN messages from the rendezvous point, which is required for traffic to switch from the RPT to the SPT. The sender's DR may continue to send traffic to the RP in register messages indefinitely.
bugs.workaround: Remove the floating self IP address from the traffic group or select a routing protocol that does not use it, such as OSPF.
bugs.fix: PIM can now send hello messages from a floating self IP address.
bugs.behavior: PIM can now send hello messages using a floating self IP address. Configure it in imish under the interface along with the PIM mode: #imish imish> enable imish# configure terminal imish(config)# interface external imish(config-if)# ip pim use-floating-address Upon failover, the previously active unit will send hellos from a non-floating self IP address, and the new active unit will begin sending hellos from the floating self IP address. No state is shared between the units; both will generate a new PIM generation ID, and the state of all multicast routes will be reset and need to reconverge.

bugs.title: Error when enabling ASM via iRule
bugs.symptoms: The following error occurs in tmm log err tmm3[26234]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/irule_switch <HTTP_REQUEST> - while executing "ASM::disable".
bugs.conditions: Enabling or disabling ASM using an iRule, for example, using an iRule similar to the following: when HTTP_REQUEST { ASM::disable if { ([IP::local_addr] equals "1.1.1.1") } { ASM::enable /Common/http_asm_policy log local0. "1 access" } elseif { ([IP::local_addr] equals "1.1.1.2") } { ASM::enable /Common/http_asm_policy_2 log local0. "2 access" } }
bugs.impact: Getting dropped request.
bugs.fix: Better handling of enable/disable ASM policy via an iRule.

bugs.title: The edit button on the GSLB Wide IP create page does not place the pool name back into the select dropdown
bugs.symptoms: The edit button in the Pools section of a Wide IP create page does not place the pool name entry back into the select dropdown.
bugs.conditions: There must be a pool in the selected list, that pool must be highlighted when the edit button is clicked.
bugs.impact: The edit button does not work as intended.
bugs.workaround: Use the delete button and find the pool in the select dropdown to edit its ratio.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue that caused the edit button on the Wide IP create page to not place the pool name back into the select dropdown.

bugs.title: Reassess encryption health after encrypted ajax is sent
bugs.symptoms: WebSafe application layer encryption fails to decrypt data sent by ajax multiple times for a single client.
bugs.conditions: Failure to decrypt data that was sent by AJAX
bugs.impact: Decryption is likely to continue failing until the page is refreshed.
bugs.fix: Encryption health status is reassessed after ajax response.

bugs.title: iControl REST: Unable to create valid iRule with symbol '{' via iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST throws an error when attempting to create an iRule where an event declaration is followed by a { on the next line. for example. when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { log local0. "Hello world" }
bugs.conditions: Creating iRule via iControl REST.
bugs.impact: User cannot create some iRules with iControl REST: some with "apiAnonymous" keyword.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH or GUI to create iRule

bugs.title: Honoring negotiated MSS for TCP segmentation
bugs.symptoms: Following are the symptoms: 1. When the BIG-IP system's MTUs are larger than the smallest MTU in the end-to-end path: -- The BIG-IP system does not mark coalesced packets larger than egress MSS but smaller than egress MTU in the BIG-IP system for segmentation. Therefore, the BIG-IP system receives 'ICMP fragmentation needed' messages from an intermediate router which drops the packets when the Don't Fragment (DF) bit is set in IP header. 2. When the BIG-IP system's MTUs are less than 1500: -- On ingress, the BIG-IP system rejects coalesced packets larger than ingress MTU and less than 1500 and having DF bit set in IP header. the BIG-IP system sends 'ICMP fragmentation needed' message to sender.
bugs.conditions: * Generic Receive Offload (GRO) and Large Receive Offload (LRO) for data plane interfaces are supported and enabled (both in host and guest). * Packets are sent with DF bit set. * For #1: -- FastL4 profile in use. -- The BIG-IP system's VLAN MTUs are larger than the smallest MTU in the end-to-end path. * For #2: -- The BIG-IP system's MTUs are set to a value that is less than 1500. -- The packets' DF bits are set.
bugs.impact: No traffic or very low throughput.
bugs.workaround: Disable LRO and GRO for data plane interfaces using the following command: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcplargereceiveoffload value disable. Note: For KVM virtio devices, LRO/GRO need to be turned off in host NIC.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system fastL4 stack now uses discovered MSS to determine whether TCP segmentation is required.

bugs.title: 'Default' plain text profile is created upon import policy with Disallowed WebSocket URLs
bugs.symptoms: A plain text profile named 'Default' is created upon import of a policy with Disallowed WebSocket URLs.
bugs.conditions: The user imports a policy with Disallowed WebSocket URLs.
bugs.impact: A plain text profile named 'Default' is created. It has no functional purpose.
bugs.workaround: Delete the plain text profile named 'Default' after import.
bugs.fix: No additional plain text profile is created upon import of policy with Disallowed WebSocket URLs.

bugs.title: TMM core while adding logging action to APM SWG
bugs.symptoms: TMM core while adding logging action to APM SWG.
bugs.conditions: -- Use of an application lookup perflow variable (perflow.application_lookup.result.*) in an SWG per-request Logging Agent. -- No Application Lookup Agent found prior in the chain. For example - The following example will crash: start : logging : allow - The following will succeed: start : application lookup : logging : allow
bugs.impact: TMM core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Remove the applicable perflow variables from the logging agent. -- Add an application lookup before trying to log application lookup perflow variables.

bugs.title: TMM core after intra-chassis failover for some instances of subscriber creation
bugs.symptoms: If intra-chassis failover is triggered in a loaded chassis, the tmm crashes in some cases of subscriber creation.
bugs.conditions: -- The chassis is loaded with many blades. -- The HA configuration is intra-chassis. -- RADIUS subscriber is added with custom attributes. -- The subscriber attributes are corrupted or erased.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. The slot reboots, potentially triggering further daglib hash changes. May result in cascading core under load. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: If intra-chassis failover is triggered in a loaded chassis, the tmm no longer crashes in some cases of subscriber creation.

bugs.title: TCP connection fail intermittently for mirrored fastl4 virtual server
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, a mirrored FastL4 virtual server may fail to forward the SYN on the server-side after receiving the context-ack from the peer. Note: This is a connection-failure through the active system, not simply a failure to mirror to the peer. Symptoms include: -- TCP connection failures. -- Possibly other packets lost.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 virtual server. -- Mirroring is enabled. -- Certain traffic interleaving might be necessary for this intermittent problem to occur.
bugs.impact: FastL4 mirroring does not always forward SYN to server after receiving context ACK. Connections fail.
bugs.workaround: Set the tm.fastl4_ack_mirror dv variable using the following command: tmsh modify sys db tm.fastl4_ack_mirror value disable.
bugs.fix: In this release, mirrored FastL4 virtual server now forward the SYN on the server-side after receiving the context-ack from the peer as expected.

bugs.title: Using variable substitution for Console attribute for remote-role always denies ssh access
bugs.symptoms: When using a remote role group to set a user's console by variable substitution from the RADIUS variable F5-LTM-User-Console, console access will be disabled no matter the value of the variable returned by the RADIUS server.
bugs.conditions: Remote auth using RADIUS. Remote role group configured to set console by variable substitution with F5-LTM-User-Console.
bugs.impact: Users who are expected to have tmsh access will not. These users will still have GUI access.
bugs.workaround: Use F5-LTM-User-Shell, and set the value to "tmsh" for users who need tmsh access.
bugs.fix: If console is set by variable substitution from F5-LTM-User-Console, and this variable is set to 1 (or Enabled), the user will have tmsh access.

bugs.title: TMM core after HA during GY reporting
bugs.symptoms: If intra-chassis failover is triggered in a loaded chassis, the tmm crashes in some cases of GY reporting
bugs.conditions: -- Failover is triggered, -- The daglib hash redistributes the subscriber DATA to different slots. -- Existing flows continue on the slots that were allocated using the old hash of daglib. Note: This is a rarely encountered issue that occurred in a setup with 8 slots and 750 thousand subscribers.
bugs.impact: Slot reboots. May trigger more hash rearrangement. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Network Access configuration with Layered-VS does not work with Edge Client
bugs.symptoms: When Network Access is configured in virtual server-to-virtual server targeting, the Edge client cannot connect.
bugs.conditions: Network Access is configured as follows : -- The external-client-facing virtual server has the SSL profile attached. -- The internal virtual server has the Access profile and connectivity profile attached. -- The external-client-facing virtual server has an iRule that forwards the HTTP requests to the internal virtual server.
bugs.impact: When Edge client connects, the external-client-facing virtual server issues a request for '/pre/config.php?version=2.0', and the Edge client hangs.
bugs.fix: Network Access configuration with Layered-VS now works with Edge Client.

bugs.title: SMB monitor marks node down when file not specified
bugs.symptoms: The smb monitor may always mark the node down when the file is not specified in the monitor config.
bugs.conditions: Pool member monitored with smb monitor.
bugs.impact: Service impact due to node being marked down.
bugs.workaround: Configure monitor to fetch file (authenticated).

bugs.title: WebSafe Login Validation may break response
bugs.symptoms: Response will be dropped, client will get an Err_Connection_Closed error
bugs.conditions: 1. WebSafe and APM are both provisioned and enabled 2. request for a WebSafe protected URL results in successful Login Validation
bugs.impact: response is dropped and application breaks
bugs.workaround: Do Not use WebSafe's Login-Validation, when a "connection terminating" filter (like APM) enabled
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with WebSafe Login Validation causing responses to be dropped.

bugs.title: Websafe features might break in IE8
bugs.symptoms: IE8 transform all custom HTTP headers names to lowercase in case header name configured with upper-case characters, WebSafe feature might break.
bugs.conditions: custom HTTP header configured with upper case characters client is IE8.
bugs.impact: FPS plugin will not find the header, as it received lower-case but configured with upper-case characters as a result, WebSafe functionality is broken (functionality which involve the custom HTTP header, e.g. ajax username header)
bugs.workaround: Set custom HTTP header name to lower case only.
bugs.fix: FPS now performs case-insensitive matches for custom HTTP headers.

bugs.title: AVR tcp-analytics: per-host RTT average may show incorrect values
bugs.symptoms: When viewing the Statistics :: Analytics :: TCP :: RTT, then selecting (in the table below the graph), View By: "Remote Host IP Address", the values presented RTT Avg (ms) may be incorrect (they could even be larger than the RTT Max column). As values are aggregated through the data tables, the reported rtt average value becomes larger and larger.
bugs.conditions: AVR is provisioned, and a tcp-analytics profile is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The values reported in the RTT Avg column when viewing by Remote Host IP Address may be incorrect.
bugs.fix: The rtt_count, rtt_max, rtt_avg, rtt_sum metrics after day aggregation and week aggregations are now correct in the day, week, month reports. The rtt_sum is now aggregated with correct value (exceed max int), as expected.

bugs.title: Large numbers of ERR_UNKNOWN appearing in the logs
bugs.symptoms: There are times when LTM Policy subsystem attempts to execute particular actions, which fail and result in LTM Policy writing an error to the logs with an error type of ERR_UNKNOWN.
bugs.conditions: This has been observed when plugins are active and experiencing high traffic volumes. The logging of ERR_UNKNOWN occurs when filters and plug-ins experience failures (such as out of memory) and react by initiating a reset of the connection. When these filters and plug-ins return an error to LTM Policy, LTM Policy logs ERR_UNKNOWN.
bugs.impact: This is a case of unnecessary logging, and there is no adverse effect other than a higher-than-normal amount of logging.

bugs.title: icrd_child generates a core when calling PUT on ltm/data-group/internal/
bugs.symptoms: icrd_child generates a core file when calling PUT on ltm/data-group/internal/.
bugs.conditions: Calling PUT on ltm/data-group/internal/.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST API is temporarily not available for configuration queries or modifications.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: icrd_child no longer cores when calling PUT on ltm/data-group/internal/.

bugs.title: REST: Failure to authenticate/renew user who is using expired password
bugs.symptoms: 1. Authentication failed for REST user, instead of prompt to renew the password. 2. Authentication is down briefly.
bugs.conditions: 1. REST API is used. 2. User password is expired.
bugs.impact: 1. Core log is dumped. 2. Authentication is down briefly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Request to /mgmt/shared/authn/login with a user with an expired password returns a 401 and a response asking the user to change their password using basic auth.

bugs.title: Portal Access: tmm may crash if web application uses long cookie names and/or values
bugs.symptoms: If JavaScript code sets a very long cookie value or uses very long cookie name (longer than 450 bytes), tmm may crash processing this cookie change.
bugs.conditions: -- JavaScript code sets/changes long cookie value or uses long cookie name; -- Chrome or MS Edge browser is used.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to remove 'Origin' header from any request to '/private/fm/volatile.html'. Note: This iRule has to enable events for internal requests using 'ACCESS::restrict_irule_events enable' command.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when an APM Portal Access web application uses long cookie values and/or names.

bugs.title: The snmpd daemon may leak memory when processing requests.
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the snmpd daemon may leak memory when processing requests.
bugs.conditions: A client allowed to send SNMP queries to the BIG-IP system, sends specially crafted requests.
bugs.impact: Once enough memory has leaked, the system may become unstable and fail unpredictably.
bugs.workaround: If the snmpd daemon is consuming excessive memory, restart it with the following command: bigstart restart snmpd
bugs.fix: The snmpd daemon no longer leaks memory when handling specially crafted requests.

bugs.title: An accelerated flow transmits packets to a stale (incorrect) destination MAC address.
bugs.symptoms: An accelerated flow can send to a stale destination MAC address after the ARP packet with the updated MAC address is received. Warning: disabling auto-lasthop is not enough when they want BIG-IP to use updated destination MAC address.
bugs.conditions: A flow is accelerated with a destination MAC address that changes while the flow is accelerated.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends packets to a stale (incorrect) destination MAC address. In this case, the new MAC address is not updated for the accelerated flow and the flow will continue to send traffic using the original MAC address.
bugs.workaround: Disable HW acceleration. Prevent the downstream destination MAC address from changing. For example, if the downstream unit is a BIG-IP active/standby configuration, then use MAC masquerading to prevent the MAC address from changing.

bugs.title: When creating LTM or DNS monitors through batch/transaction mode newlines are improperly escaped.
bugs.symptoms: - LTM/DNS monitors created via tmsh batch/transactions improperly escape newline characters. - Expected escaping: \r\n - Actual escaping: \\r\\n - Impact: The URI sent is not correct
bugs.conditions:
When creating LTM or DNS monitors through batch/transaction mode when strings contain newline characters. For example, using the following commands to batch-create: create gtm monitor http one_test_mon { send "GET / HTTP/1.0
Host: abc.example.com
User-Agent: slb-healthcheck
Connection: Close

" recv "200"} submit cli transaction list gtm monitor http one_test_mon The system creates the following monitor: gtm monitor http one_test_mon { defaults-from http destination *:* interval 30 probe-timeout 5 recv 200 send "GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: abc.example.com\r\nUser-Agent: slb-healthcheck\r\nConnection: Close\r\n\r\n"
bugs.impact: Cannot use batch/transaction mode in TMSH to create LTM or DNS monitors. Cannot use LTM or DNS monitors created using batch/transaction mode in tmsh.
bugs.workaround: Create the monitor directly in tmsh without using batch/transaction mode.
bugs.fix: When creating LTM or DNS monitors through batch/transaction mode newlines are now properly escaped.

bugs.title: VPN connection drops when 'prohibit routing table change' is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When there is a brief network outage and 'prohibit routing table change' is enabled, VPN gets disconnected and no further attempts are made to re-establish the VPN connection.
bugs.conditions: -- A brief network outage occurs. -- The 'prohibit routing table change' option is enabled.
bugs.impact: APM end users must click 'Connect' and re-authenticate in order to re-establish the VPN connection.
bugs.workaround: To re-establish the VPN connection, click 'Connect' and re-authenticate.
bugs.fix: Now the Windows Edge Client VPN connection stays active during a brief network outage, regardless of the state of the 'prohibit routing table changes' option.

bugs.title: A new tmsh command to flush all ePVA flow cache entries
bugs.symptoms: There is no command to flush all ePVA flow cache entries. The 'tmsh delete sys connection all' command causes tmm to send a ePVA flush command to HSB, but has the side effect of deleting all the connections inside tmm.
bugs.conditions: Traffic flows are offloaded to hardware for acceleration.
bugs.impact: Cannot flush the hardware flows into software.
bugs.fix: This release introduces a new tmsh command: tmsh modify sys connection flow-accel-type software-only. The command flushes all ePVA flows from hardware acceleration to software. Note: In order to keep the hardware accelerated flows out of the hardware after running the new flush command, the PVA Offload Dynamic/pva-offload-dynamic option of the FastL4 profile must be set to disabled. It is set to enabled by default. Important: Use this command judiciously. Flushing connections to software results in a performance impact to BIG-IP systems, as all the connections are evicted to software, so hardware offloaded connections must be reinserted.

bugs.title: Mcpd crash
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd crashes and generates a core file.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while making configuration changes to high availability (HA) configurations. This occurs rarely.
bugs.impact: The mcpd crashes and restarts. System operation paused while mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: MCPd SIGSEGV in boost::checked_delete
bugs.symptoms: MCPd SIGSEGV during tear down of DSC connections. System logs messages similar to the following to /var/log/ltm: warning mcpd[4822]: 01071aea:4: CMI heartbeat timer expired, status: 192.168.254.253.
bugs.conditions: During tear down of DSC connections, a heartbeat operation may be attempted on an already deleted connection.
bugs.impact: MCPd will be restarted, possibly resulting in other daemons restarting as well.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now handles this condition, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Loading UCS with the platform-migrate parameter could unexpectedly set or unset management DHCP
bugs.symptoms: When you load a UCS file using the platform-migrate parameter, the mgmt-dhcp value (enabled, disabled, or unset) will overwrite the value on the destination. Depending on the effect, this could change the destination's management IP and default management route. If the UCS does not have mgmt-dhcp explicitly written out, note that its value is treated as the default for the local system, which varies by the type of system. On Virtual Edition (VE) platforms, the default is to enable DHCP. On all other platforms, the default is to disable DHCP.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when loading a UCS using the platform-migrate parameter: tmsh load sys ucs <ucs_file_from_another_system> platform-migrate
bugs.impact: Changing the mgmt-dhcp value on the destination can result in management changing from statically configured to DHCP or DHCP to statically configured. This can result in loss of management access to the device, requiring in-band or console access.
bugs.workaround: There are a few ways to avoid this issue: 1. Specify the "keep-current-management-ip" parameter to the "load sys ucs" command, for instance: tmsh load sys ucs <ucs_file_from_another_system> platform-migrate keep-current-management-ip Note: The "keep-current-management-ip" parameter is undocumented and will not appear in context help or tab completion. 2. If you want to reset the target device to use a static IP, run the following commands after loading the UCS with the platform-migrate command: tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp disabled tmsh create sys management-ip <ip>/<mask> tmsh delete sys management-route default tmsh create sys management-route default gateway <ip>

bugs.title: Empty User-Agent in iSessions requests from APM client on Windows
bugs.symptoms: 'User-Agent' might be empty in some '/isession' requests from APM client on Microsoft Windows. Having empty User-Agent headers is not in RFC compliance and forces some firewall to block the connection. This might result in failure to establish a VPN tunnel.
bugs.conditions: '/isession' requests from APM client on Windows.
bugs.impact: Failure to establish a VPN tunnel.
bugs.fix: Now all connections from Windows APM VPN client contain 'User-Agent' headers, as expected.

bugs.title: Errors when platform migration process is loading UCS using trunks on vCMP guest/F5OS Tenants
bugs.symptoms: During the platform migration from a physical BIG-IP system to a BIG-IP vCMP guest/F5OS Tenant, the load fails with one of the following messages: 01070687:3: Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) is not supported on this platform. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. 01070338:3: Cannot create trunk [name of trunk], maximum limit reached Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- The source device is a physical BIG-IP device with one or more trunks with or without LACP in its configuration. -- The destination device is a vCMP guest/F5OS Tenant.
bugs.impact: The platform migration fails and the configuration does not load.
bugs.workaround: You can use one of the following workarounds: -- Remove all trunks from the source configuration prior to generation of the UCS. -- Before loading the UCS archive onto the target BIG-IP, edit the archive and remove the trunk configuration from ./config/bigip_base.conf, and then repack the UCS. -- After the UCS load fails, edit the configuration manually on the destination to remove trunk references, and then reload the configuration. -- K50152613

bugs.title: Memory leak when connection terminates in iRule process
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak eventually leading to alloc failure and TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: Connection is aborted/terminated when iRule processing is suspended for the current connection.
bugs.impact: Memory leak and eventual TMM restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid suspend/park commands in iRule processing.
bugs.fix: Memory no longer leaks when connection is aborted/terminated when iRule processing is suspended.

bugs.title: Some published externally AVR data can be corrupted when HTTP Traffic external publisher is on
bugs.symptoms: When publishing statistics to external destination (HSL or TCP) some messages contain wrong data. It happens only when HTTP traffic report is activated. One can see corrupted data also in debug output.
bugs.conditions: HTTP traffic report is activated. To activate it via GUI go to "Set up : Local Traffic ›› Profiles : Analytics : HTTP Analytics", choose or create analytics profile associated with VS that passes traffic, mark "External" checkbox next to "Traffic Capturing Logging Type".
bugs.impact: Some AVR data reported by HSL or TCP protocol to an external destination are corrupted.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Escaping and Base64 functions used in external message text processing turned to thread safe.

bugs.title: BIG-IP iSeries: Retrieving the gateway from the Host via REST through the LCD
bugs.symptoms: The LCD on BIG-IP iSeries appliances must detect whether the system is in IPv4 or IPv6 context before retrieving the gateway from the Host via REST. If two gateways are configured (IPv4 and IPv6) only whichever is first in the list is returned via REST and will be set on the Host.
bugs.conditions: If two gateways are configured (IPv4 and IPv6).
bugs.impact: Incorrect gateway retrieval can create bad configs which would impact traffic resulting in failed ping attempts, destination unreachable errors, request timeouts, etc.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: LCD code now retrieves the correct gateway when switching between IPV4 and IPV6 context.

bugs.title: Network access plugin message is not localized on Mac OS X
bugs.symptoms: During network access plugin installation, some text will always be displayed in English, even for non-English locales.
bugs.conditions: Running web client installation from Safari on Macintosh platforms running Mac OS X.
bugs.impact: Non-English-speaking APM end users installing the web client cannot read certain text.

bugs.title: Support tcpdump file has qkview extension
bugs.symptoms: The Support tcpdump file has a qkview extension.
bugs.conditions: On the Support page, generate a tcpdump file.
bugs.impact: The tcpdump file has a qkview extension. There is no functional issue with the system; only the file extension is incorrect.
bugs.fix: The Support tcpdump file now has a tcp extension.

bugs.title: Diameter Message Length Limit Changed from 1024 to 4096 Bytes
bugs.symptoms: Diameter messages longer than 1024 might cause core dumps.
bugs.conditions: Using Diameter messages longer than 1024.
bugs.impact: Diameter MRF virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Make sure messages are less than 1024 bytes.
bugs.fix: Messages of 4096 or fewer bytes now pass, and longer messages no longer cause core dumps.

bugs.title: "Severe critical" message after failed upgrade persists even after subsequent successful config load
bugs.symptoms: A critical message persists in the GUI after a failed upgrade: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- ASM Critical Warning An upgrade process was interrupted. It is very likely that ASM will start with a severe inconsistent interal state and critical errors ----------------------------------------------------------------------
bugs.conditions: ASM upgrade has failed.
bugs.impact: A critical message persists in GUI, even after a successful subsequent configuration load.
bugs.fix: Subsequent successful configuration load now clears failed upgrade message.

bugs.title: FPS should indicate live-update status (new content available/downloaded/auto-downloaded/download-failed)
bugs.symptoms: Snmp trap is not available for live-update status change because FPS doesn't report live-update content status via syslog.
bugs.conditions: Live update content status changed.
bugs.impact: There is no syslog indication about live-update content status change so snmp trap is not available for live-update status change.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: FPS will report status change via syslog.

bugs.title: apmd crashes executing iRule policy evaluate
bugs.symptoms: Following a restart, if apmd executes an iRule policy evaluate before its reinitialization is complete, apmd can crash.
bugs.conditions: If apmd restarts due to a crash or explicit restart command but tmm remains active, then iRule policy evaluate commands can reach apmd before it completes initialization and it will crash.
bugs.impact: apmd crashes and restarts, preventing end users from logging in.
bugs.fix: Now APMD has a more robust initialization process to ensure that it does not execute access policies from iRule commands before it is ready.

bugs.title: HTTPS monitors might share one SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: Each HTTPS monitor has its own cert, key, cipherlist, compatibility, and partition attributes for SSL-related functionality. Depending on the configuration, hardware, and number of HTTPS monitors, rolling forward a configuration with a number of HTTPS monitors might impact performance, memory usage, capacity, and compatibility.
bugs.conditions: These attributes of HTTPS monitors are of the same values: cert, key, cipherlist, compatibility, and partition, but occur in multiple HTTPS monitors.
bugs.impact: Potential impact on performance, memory usage, capacity, and compatibility as the roll-forward process creates each HTTPS monitor.
bugs.fix: To streamline the number of SSL profiles when rolling forward HTTPS monitors, if multiple HTTPS monitors contain attributes (cert, key, cipherlist, compatibility, and partition), with the same values, the monitors with same-value attributes will share one SSL profile, instead of having multiple sets of attributes, one for each HTTPS monitor. Note: Although there are fewer SSL profiles, if you want to change any of these attributes for one specific HTTPS monitor, you might have to add an SSL profile for it.
bugs.behavior: Original behavior: Each HTTPS monitor has its own cert, key, cipherlist, compatibility, and partition attributes for SSL-related functionality. New behavior: These SSL-related attributes are deprecated, and an SSL profile is created in lieu of those attributes. When rolling forward, instead of creating one SSL profile for each HTTPS monitor, one SSL profile will be shared by possibly many HTTPS monitors, if the specified attributes are of the same value.

bugs.title: URL encoded Authorization code does not work with APM OAuth client
bugs.symptoms: When the Authorization Server (AS) generates an authorization code which includes URL special character, in order to pass this code safely, AS encodes it with URL encoding. APM does not properly process this, and when OAuth client used it for retrieving an access token for a given code, OAuth client unnecessarily re-encode it, which causes the AS to reject the token request.
bugs.conditions: AS generates an OAuth Authorization code contains URL encoded characters.
bugs.impact: OAuth client fails to retrieve the token with the provided code.
bugs.workaround: Use the iRule to either decode the authorization code when APM receives it, or when APM sends it out.
bugs.fix: URL encoded authorization code now works with APM OAuth client.

bugs.title: Non-default header-table-size setting on HTTP2 profiles may cause issues
bugs.symptoms: HTTP2 connection sent RST_STREAM due to protocol error in response to headers frame.
bugs.conditions: HTTP2 profile configured with header-table-size with value exceeding 4096.
bugs.impact: Periodic HTTP2 connection failure to the virtual.
bugs.workaround: Restore the default header-table-size setting for the HTTP2 profile.

bugs.title: Support combination of real-time and on-submit encryption
bugs.symptoms: When real-time encryption is enabled and parameters that are configured with encryption are enabled, the system cannot encrypt the value populated by the script in real-time, so that parameter will be sent as plain text.
bugs.conditions: 1. Real-time encryption enabled. 2. Parameter configured with encryption enabled. 3. The encryption-enabled parameter is populated by the script.
bugs.impact: FPS cannot encrypt the encryption-enabled parameter in real-time, so that parameter will be sent as plain text.
bugs.fix: The system now supports the combination of real-time and on-submit encryption when using the Before Load Function: function(C){ C.XX.realTimeAndSubmitEnc = true;}. Note: You must configure the Before Load Function because this is not the default setting.

bugs.title: Custom Predefined Reports are not displayed in ASM Analytics Schedules
bugs.symptoms: When creating custom predefined filters, either via Requests page or via ASM Statistics, these custom reports are not displayed as part of the predefined reports list when creating/modifying an ASM Schedule.
bugs.conditions: Creating custom predefined filters, either via Requests page or via ASM Statistics.
bugs.impact: Reports created by user can not be easily used in GUI to create a scheduled report.
bugs.fix: ASM Requests/Stats pages now use the correct internal field name to store the reference to the report, thus it will be accessible by all screens.

bugs.title: iRule command PEM::session functions differently in 12.1.x and 13.0.0 than it did in prior versions
bugs.symptoms: When the RADIUS discovery virtual server and the traffic listener virtual server sit in two different route domains, the iRule command 'PEM::session info $sub subscriber-id' may not be able to fetch the subscriber-id.
bugs.conditions: -- Running v12.1.x or v13.0.0. -- RADIUS server. -- Use of iRule command PEM::session.
bugs.impact: 'PEM::session info state/subscriber-id' commands might not return the expected session info.
bugs.fix: iRule command PEM::session functions differently in 12.1.x and 13.0.0 than it did in prior versions. The commands now consider route domains.

bugs.title: Timestamps in icrd, restjavad, and restnoded logs are not synchronized with the system time
bugs.symptoms: Logs on icrd, restnoded, and restjavad are in the UTC time zone and are not aligned to the system time, which makes it difficult to determine the time during troubleshooting operations.
bugs.conditions: Checking the icrd, restnoded, and restjavad logs timestamps.
bugs.impact: Difficult to troubleshoot as the logs are not aligned with system time.

bugs.title: bigd not rotating DNS servers when ICMP packet is not received
bugs.symptoms: When the first DNS server becomes unavailable for FQDN node resolution, but no ICMP message is received, bigd does not rotate to the next DNS server. In the common case where a DNS server becomes unavailable, an ICMP message will notify bigd of server unavailability, and bigd will rotate to the next available DNS server. However, if network configuration fails to route this ICMP message back to bigd, the DNS server is assumed to remain available (and all subsequent DNS resolve operations will fail, as the DNS server is unavailable).
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple DNS servers are configured for FQDN resolution for 'bigd' monitors. -- The first DNS server becomes unavailable. -- ICMP messages are not received by 'bigd'. -- BIG-IP software versions earlier than 12.1.3.3 and 13.1.0.
bugs.impact: bigd continues to send FQDN node resolutions to the (now-unavailable) DNS server, which will fail to resolve (bigd will not rotate to the next configured DNS server). Existing resolved FQDN nodes and all associated monitors will continue to function normally.
bugs.workaround: Ensure network routes ICMP messages to bigd when the DNS server becomes unavailable.

bugs.title: LTM Policy rule name migration doesn't properly handle whitespace
bugs.symptoms: LTM Policy validation does not allow rule names to begin or end with whitespace characters. When migrating configuration to the next version, the migration process attempts to trim off any leading and trailing whitespace. However, this process does not handle leading and trailing whitespace when such characters occur within a double quoted string.
bugs.conditions: LTM policy with a rule name that contains leading and/or trailing whitespace characters. These will typically occur within a double-quoted string. Here is an example that one might find in bigip.conf: ltm policy example1 { rules { " leading and trailing spaces " { ... } ... }
bugs.impact: Policy rules are migrated incorrectly, then fail validation because there of remaining leading and/or trailing whitespace characters.
bugs.workaround: Prior to migration, LTM Policy rule name can be renamed to remove leading and trailing whitespace. After a failed migration, bigip.conf can be manually edited to remove offending characters and then the configuration can be manually loaded.
bugs.fix: LTM Policy migration properly handles whitespace in rule names in a quoted string.

bugs.title: Memory leak under rare conditions
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak
bugs.conditions: -- Mirrored flow. -- Persistence used. -- Another error condition such as high availability (HA) channel down.
bugs.impact: Memory leak.
bugs.fix: Memory leak is fixed.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can disable the Mirror Persistence option for the persistence profiles or make sure the mirroring channel is properly configured and operational. For information about troubleshooting the mirroring channel, refer to K54622241: Troubleshooting connection mirroring :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K54622241.

bugs.title: TFO and TLP could produce a core file under specific circumstances
bugs.symptoms: Sequence of packets sent to Virtual Server with TCP Fast Open and Tail Loss Probe enabled may cause TMM to produce a core file.
bugs.conditions: Tail Loss Probe and TCP Fast Open enabled on a virtual with undisclosed traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM may produce a core file.
bugs.workaround: Disable Tail Loss Probe from the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue related to an undesired interaction between TFO/TLP.

bugs.title: Profiles with names that contain percentage signs cannot be accessed in TMUI
bugs.symptoms: Clicking profiles on the list page in the Configuration Utility (GUI) with names that contain a percentage sign does not take you to the profile page.
bugs.conditions: -- Clicking profile names with percentage signs. -- The profiles list page in the GUI.
bugs.impact: The profile pages cannot be accessed from the profiles list page in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh or rename your profiles so their name does not include a percentage sign.

bugs.title: Rare, intermittent system instability observed in dynamic load-balancing modes
bugs.symptoms: The dynamic pool member load-balancing modes require a precision measurement of active connection counts and/or rates. Rare, intermittent system instability has been observed in dynamic pool member selection when a new connection arrives. TMM may restart, leaving a core file.
bugs.conditions: LTM pool configured to use a dynamic load-balancing mode ('ltm pool NAME load-balancing-mode MODE' where MODE is one of the dynamic load-balancing modes, such as dynamic-ratio-member, least-connections-node, predictive-node, etc.). The dynamic modes use the session database to share data among all TMM instances, and under extremely rare conditions, the session database may become unreliable.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts and leaves a core file. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The dynamic load-balancing modes are now more tolerant of errors from the underlying session database.

bugs.title: GSLB Pool Member Manage page display issues and error message
bugs.symptoms: The GSLB Pool Member Manage page displays an error message 'Entry could not be matched against existing objects' when using the static-target checkbox to add a member that does not exist on the BIG-IP config. Also when editing a pool member, the pool member's name will not be auto-selected in the combo box.
bugs.conditions: -- GSLB pool configured. -- Members available for addition to the pool. Note: This issue can happen when creating a pool in the members section as well as on the pool members manage page.
bugs.impact: Degraded usability.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to add a static-target and to edit pool members.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue with the edit button and issue that prevented adding as a static-target a GSLB pool member that was not part of the GTM config. Now, if static target is enabled, you can type the name of the target without the target being configured on the system.

bugs.title: Enterprise Manager may receive malformed data if there are multiple monitors on a pool
bugs.symptoms: Enterprise Manager (EM) may receive malformed data if there are multiple monitors on a pool. big3d returns malformed xml. Messages similar to the following appear in /var/log/em: Could not parse xml for device.
bugs.conditions: -- Flapping pool monitor has more than two HTTP-type monitors. -- iControl data returned from big3d LTM is malformed xml.
bugs.impact: Malformed data causes EM to not be able to gather stats from big3d.

bugs.title: statemirror.ipaddr db variable does not sync to peers
bugs.symptoms: Modifying /sys state-mirroring or db variable statemirror.ipaddr does not sync to peers.
bugs.conditions: -- Modify /sys state-mirroring or db variable statemirror.ipaddr. -- Sync to peers.
bugs.impact: Attempts to configure State Mirroring appear to have been successful, but the system does not state-mirror properly because the configuration is not properly synchronized
bugs.workaround: Update State Mirroring configuration via the 'cm device' object in tmsh, or via the GUI.

bugs.title: tmsh stats are not one-to-one mapping to tmctl
bugs.symptoms: tmsh stats doesn't have some stats while those stats exist at tmctl, such as fki_avg, fki_max, gk_avg, gk_max, dk_avg, and dk_max. At tmsh, 'find key by modulus' is shown as 'find_key', whereas it is shown as 'find_key_mod' at tmctl. This is because in tmsh it is not recommended to rename a stats item.
bugs.conditions: When tmsh stats command is used for pkcs11d.
bugs.impact: Some stats existing at tmctl are not showing up or showing differently at tmsh. 1. 'find_key' at tmsh is shown as 'find_key_mod' at tmctl. Also 'fk_*' is equivalent to 'fkm_*' 2. The following items are not as useful as the corresponding operation counts and error counts, so tmsh does not display them to keep tmsh table from being too wide. fki_avg fki_max gk_avg gk_max dk_avg dk_max.
bugs.workaround: Use tmctl if those stats not showing at tmsh are indeed needed.
bugs.fix: The statistics from tmctl pkcs11d_stat now matches the output of tmsh show sys nethsm pkcs11d-stat.

bugs.title: tmsh command for gtm-application disabled contexts does not work with none and replace-all-with
bugs.symptoms: The command for distributed-app's disabled-contexts does not work with the options 'none' and 'replace-all-with'.
bugs.conditions: Issuing gtm-application disabled contexts commands including the options 'none' and 'replace-all-with'.
bugs.impact: Command does not complete successfully. This is an internal validation issue.

bugs.title: support dynamic command line flags when executing a java process
bugs.symptoms: Java cored while running tasks for datasyncd.
bugs.conditions: unknown.
bugs.impact: datasync obfuscation process completed successfully. no impact.
bugs.workaround: there is no workaround at this time
bugs.fix: In order to improve our abilities to investigate such issues java command line flags can be configured during run-time.

bugs.title: Monitor configured with timeout large enough that the timeout plus interval is greater than 86400 seconds, the service may be incorrectly marked down.
bugs.symptoms: When the monitor is configured with a timeout large enough that the timeout plus interval is greater than 86400 seconds, the service may be incorrectly marked down.
bugs.conditions: Monitor configured with timeout plus interval larger than 86400.
bugs.impact: Periodically service taken offline which may result in persistence issues or impact service availability.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the monitor's timeout to less than (86400 - interval).

bugs.title: tmm may crash at ~75% of VLAN failsafe timeout expiration
bugs.symptoms: When VLAN failsafe is configured, and the VLAN failsafe timeout is 3/4 expired, tmm wants to generate ICMP traffic to evoke a network response. When this occurs, the system might experience a crash.
bugs.conditions: - VLAN failsafe is configured on a VLAN, for example with the recommended VLAN failsafe timeout of 90 sec. - The VLAN does not observe ARP/ndp traffic for 3/4 of the timeout, 67.5 seconds. - ICMP traffic generated to provoke a network response can under certain circumstances cause a TMM crash.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes, failover is triggered, as it would with a fully expired VLAN-failsafe-timeout condition (note that failover with a fully expired VLAN failsafe is correct behavior). Traffic on other VLANs might be disrupted while TMM restarts. (Traffic on the VLAN-failsafe-triggered VLAN is already disrupted, causing the timeout to expire.)
bugs.workaround: 1. To allow for VLAN failsafe to be updated for any frame, run the following command with VLAN failsafe enabled, run the following command: tmsh modify failover.vlanfailsafe.resettimeronanyframe enable This configuration increases the confidence that in the case of a timeout expiry a real traffic disruption is detected. 2. Set the timeout of VLAN failsafe to 4/3 of the setting you want, for example, to have a timeout setting of 90, specify 120. With this setting, failover occurs at 90 seconds for a fully quiescent network. Note: Having a fully quiescent network is a rare occurrence and likely indicates that another issue is occurring anyway.
bugs.fix: Generating ICMP traffic from TMM is no longer exposed to a potential crash in an invalid configuration or a completely quiet network, when generating ICMP traffic to provoke a network response on an expiring timer of VLAN failsafe, assuming the following configuration: - VLAN failsafe is configured. - VLAN failsafe expired 3/4 of the configured timeout (e.g., 67.5 seconds of 90 seconds ).

bugs.title: TMM core after intra-chassis failover for some instances of subscriber creation
bugs.symptoms: If intra-chassis failover is triggered in a loaded chassis, the tmm crashes in some cases of subscriber creation.
bugs.conditions: -- The chassis is loaded with many blades. -- The high availability (HA) configuration is intra-chassis. -- RADIUS subscriber is added with custom attributes. -- The subscriber attributes are corrupted or erased.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. The slot reboots, potentially triggering further daglib hash changes. May result in cascading core under load. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Verify the validity of the AVPs before copying the attributes

bugs.title: Sys connection behavior change
bugs.symptoms: tmm/mcpd might restart when retrieving a large number of flows in response to running the command 'show sys connection' without any connection specifiers.
bugs.conditions: -- Execution of command: show sys connection. -- Large number of flows.
bugs.impact: Possible disruption of traffic while tmm/mcps restarts.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed with the addition of the keyword: max-result-limit.
