bugs.conditions: This usually happen when a large certificate or certificate chain is configured for server or client authentication.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake will fail with client or server that properly checks the record size.
bugs.workaround: Use a certificate that is smaller in size.
bugs.fix: Properly fragment handshake data.

bugs.title: Diameter failure: load balancing fails when all pool members use same IP Address
bugs.symptoms: Case1: Run 2 Servers with same IP but different ports. Send 10 request from 1 client. Result: All 10 requests from client are delivered to 1 server. Same result when use-local-connection is disabled. Case2: Run 2 Servers with same IP but different ports but this time use MR::message route iRule command to route messages between hosts. Send 10 request from 1 client. Result: All 10 requests from client are delivered to 1 server.
bugs.conditions: Load balancing scenario with single client and two pool members. The servers use same IP, different ports.
bugs.impact: All the requests from the same client are delivered to 1 server only.
bugs.workaround: Use different IP address in the pool member. Or use different IP address as the client request.
bugs.fix: Load balancing scenario with single client and two pool members now completes successfully even when all pool members use same IP Address.

bugs.title: TMM restart while processing rewrite filter
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart and failover occurs while processing rewrite filter.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with rewrite-uri-translation profile. -- Serverside attempts to get data from clientside when connection flow does not exist.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM restart and failover no longer occurs while processing rewrite filter.

bugs.title: One LTM policy causes a different policy to not execute
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, the presence of one LTM policy will preclude another LTM policy from running.
bugs.conditions: Two policies present on a virtual server, one policy with a condition at HTTP_RESPONSE time will prevent a policy that unconditionally acts at HTTP_REQUEST time.
bugs.impact: Expected LTM policy does not run.

bugs.title: Protocol Security HTTP Protocol Check Maximum Number of Headers 'Alarm' mode results in 'Block'
bugs.symptoms: When using Protocol Security profiles for HTTP, the HTTP Protocol Checks 'Alarm' vs. 'Block' setting will not be honored for the 'Check maximum number of headers' check. If an HTTP response contains more than the configured maximum number of headers, the connection will be reset. Client traffic with more than the maximum allowed headers will be allowed through to the server, and an alert will be generated, as expected. The server response will also have too many headers, but the connection will be reset.
bugs.conditions: -- PSM HTTP Protocol Checks configured in 'Alarm' mode ('Block' disabled). -- The maximum number of headers is exceeded for server responses.
bugs.impact: Connections are reset, when only alerting is expected.
bugs.fix: Two threshold values are now available for monitoring the number of HTTP headers: -- Use the HTTP security profile and select 'alarm' (as opposed to 'block'). -- Use the HTTP service protocol profile. When the 'alarm' threshold is hit, the HTTP traffic remains intact, and logging can be seen in the PSM event logs. When the HTTP service protocol profile's threshold is hit, the HTTP traffic will be blocked, and logging to be seen in both LTM log and PSM event logs.

bugs.title: Connection resets on Virtual Server with APM Access Profile and ASM Security Policy
bugs.symptoms: Connections to a Virtual Server will be reset and not handled by the system.
bugs.conditions: This happens on Virtual Servers which have an APM Access Profile and an ASM Security Policy assigned to it.
bugs.impact: As a result, APM and ASM end users cannot access the site.
bugs.workaround: To prevent the problem from happening: Add a DoS profile with 'Application' enabled to the Virtual Server.
bugs.fix: Virtual Servers with APM Access Profile and ASM Security Policy no longer cause connection resets.

bugs.title: Real time encryption on non-password fields
bugs.symptoms: Real-time encryption for non-password field when full-AJAX encryption is enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure specific parameter with encryption enabled. 2. The page uses AJAX. 3. Change the configured parameter value in the page after it has been populated by the end user, and then submit the page.
bugs.impact: when malware changes input value with JS code, the system sends this value instead of the RTE one.
bugs.fix: The system now sends the real value from RTE in this case.

bugs.title: TMM memory leak when DoS profile is attached to VS
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory leak when DoS profile is attached to VS
bugs.conditions: 1. have DoS profile 2. traffic from search engine is coming to this VS 3. DNS resolver is configured
bugs.impact: TMM memory use increases over time.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Free memory periodically.

bugs.title: Client-side challenge is changing POST parameter value under some circumstances
bugs.symptoms: A parameter arrives with a different value to the server than was sent from the client. Happens while a brute force attack or web scraping challenge or web scraping session client-side mitigation is happening
bugs.conditions: -- POST request with URL-decoded parameters. -- A parameter is escaped. -- A client-side challenge is returned for this request.
bugs.impact: The wrong parameter arrives to the application. In response, the application may stop working or have other errors.
bugs.fix: Client-side challenge no longer changes POST parameter value under described circumstances.

bugs.title: AVR publishes tmstat statistics to internal store (SQL) when disable-all-internal-logging is set.
bugs.symptoms: AVR publishes tmstat statistics to the internal store (SQL) when disable-all-internal-logging is set. When disable-all-internal-logging is set (in analytics global-settings) AVR shouldn't publish any statistics to the internal storage.
bugs.conditions: Disable-all-internal-logging is set in the analytics global-settings.
bugs.impact: Statistics published to the database although it shouldn't.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After the fix, AVR doesn't publish any statistics to the database when disable-all-internal-logging is set.

bugs.title: Do not reboot on ctrl-alt-del
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP reboots on ctrl-alt-del keys
bugs.conditions: VE with ctrl-alt-del keys in the video console.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP reboots.
bugs.fix: prevent reboot on ctrl-alt-del

bugs.title: URLDB SIGFPE - 'urldb tcl result not overwritten'
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores with the the following notice: Assertion 'urldb tcl result not overwritten' failed.
bugs.conditions: Use of CATEGORY::lookup iRule in a case where the system fails to resume normal traffic flow after setting the result.
bugs.impact: Traffic flow is interrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: Added a check to ensure that upon failure to resume normal traffic flow, the result is cleared and reset so that the core does not occur.

bugs.title: TMM may restart when using SOCKS profile and an iRule
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts when sending traffic through a SOCKS virtual server that has an attached iRule that uses certain blocking commands.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server has a SOCKS profile, and an iRule which triggers on the SERVER_CONNECTED event. If the iRule uses commands that block, tmm might restart.
bugs.impact: Unexpected tmm restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid adding iRule on the SERVER_CONNECTED event, or avoid using certain iRule commands which do not complete immediately, such as 'after', 'table', 'session', and others.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when using SOCKS profile and serverside iRule parks.

bugs.title: Text in 'About BIG-IP Edge Client' cannot be copied using mouse or keyboard selection
bugs.symptoms: You cannot use the mouse or keyboard to select or copy the text in the BIG-IP Edge Client :: About BIG-IP Edge Client, window on MacOS. This text contains BIG-IP Edge Client version, which users sometimes need to provide for debugging.
bugs.conditions: Open BIG-IP Edge Client :: About BIG-IP Edge Client, and attempt to select or copy the text in this window
bugs.impact: Cannot copy/paste the BIG-IP Edge Client version for debugging. You must manually enter the version number.
bugs.workaround: Manually enter the version number.
bugs.fix: You can now select and copy the text in the BIG-IP Edge Client :: About BIG-IP Edge Client, window on MacOS.

bugs.title: The Neuron SDK rejects rule delete requests with -5 error
bugs.symptoms: Neurond cores if it receives an error while adding or deleting rules in neuron hardware.
bugs.conditions: Adding or deleting rules in neuron hardware
bugs.impact: Neurond cores

bugs.title: BIG-IP sometimes performs unnecessary reboot on first boot
bugs.symptoms: Some versions of the BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) software incorrectly determine that the size of its disk has changed, and re-sizes the partition table and causes a reboot to occur. This is likely to occur only on VE guests.
bugs.conditions: -- First boot of VE. -- Software version that exhibits this issue. Note: A specific software version for a specific cloud environment either always exhibit this, or never does.
bugs.impact: Additional, unnecessary minor filesystem size adjustment and additional time for a reboot to occur.
bugs.fix: An additional, unnecessary reboot of a BIG-IP Virtual Edition during its first boot-up should no longer occur.

bugs.title: Duplicate wildcard virtual server address creation
bugs.symptoms: You can create duplicate wildcard virtual servers using tmsh, but not in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Running v13.x. -- Creating duplicate wildcard virtual servers.
bugs.impact: You might experience unexpected behavior regarding routing of packets to virtual servers and their respective destinations.
bugs.workaround: -- Do not configure a second virtual server with identical attributes. -- Delete one of the identical virtual servers, if it has already been configured.

bugs.title: PEM sessions lost when new blade is inserted in chassis
bugs.symptoms: Inserting a blade into a chassis that is using high availability (HA) is configured for 'between clusters' can cause data loss in the SessionDB. This includes iRule table command as well as entries stored in the SessionDB from modules.
bugs.conditions: HA in use 'between clusters'.
bugs.impact: Data loss of some SessionDB entries.
bugs.workaround: In order to cleanly add a blade, put the setting from 'between clusters' to 'within cluster'; then add the new blade(s) to both clusters. Wait 60 seconds, then restore the HA connection to 'between clusters'
bugs.fix: PEM sessions are now retained when new blade is inserted in chassis when using 'between clusters'.

bugs.title: Policy automatic learning mode changes to manual after failover
bugs.symptoms: Policy automatic learning mode changes to manual when a failover occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Device group with ASM policy sync configured for multi-blade devices. -- ASM Policy is in automatic learning mode. -- A failover occurs.
bugs.impact: The policy changes from automatic learning mode to manual.
bugs.fix: Policy automatic learning mode no longer changes to manual when a failover occurs. Automatic learning mode will now be disabled only in active/active configurations.

bugs.title: tmsh show ltm virtual <vs-name> policies does not display policy-stats
bugs.symptoms: You are not able to view the policy stats when executing the tmsh show ltm virtual policy command.
bugs.conditions: Executing the command from cli tmsh show ltm virtual <vs-name> policies
bugs.impact: Policy stats are not displayed.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: tmsh show ltm virtual <vs-name> policies now displays policy stats.

bugs.title: Rateshaper stalls when TSO packet length exceeds max ceiling.
bugs.symptoms: If a TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) packet length exceeds the rateshaper's max ceiling, it causes the flow to stall.
bugs.conditions: Packet length exceeds rateshaper's configured max ceiling.
bugs.impact: The flow stalls.
bugs.workaround: Increase the configured rateshaper's max ceiling value to be larger than the largest packet length.
bugs.fix: Rateshaper no longer stalls when TSO packet length exceeds max ceiling.

bugs.title: F5 iRule signing certificate changed to SHA2
bugs.symptoms: Before this version, the F5 iRule signing certificate was SHA1.
bugs.conditions: Using signed iRules on a version before this.
bugs.impact: iRule signing less secure
bugs.fix: iRule signing certificate is now SHA2. No usage interruptions or specific upgrade actions should be necessary.

bugs.title: DNS configured with 2 Generic hosts for different DataCenters, with same monitors, servers status flapping
bugs.symptoms: DNS Server status flapping from red-green-red.
bugs.conditions: -- Two generic hosts in two different DataCenters; -- Two generic hosts are not available through DNS; -- Same monitor with available alias IP/port configured.
bugs.impact: Server status flaps from red to green and back.
bugs.workaround: Check Transparent for these monitors.

bugs.title: SSL handshake reference is not dropped if forward proxy certificate lookup failed
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, when forward-proxy certificate-lookup fails, the SSL handshake reference is not dropped, which can consume memory that is no longer needed.
bugs.conditions: Forward-proxy certificate-lookup fails; specifically, input string size is larger than maximum allowed.
bugs.impact: tmm memory use grows.
bugs.fix: The system now drops the SSL handshake reference when when forward-proxy certificate-lookup fails. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: MSIE 11 should avoid compatibility mode
bugs.symptoms: MSIE 11 in compatibility mode is causing JS errors because MSIE 7-9 are not good in javascript.
bugs.conditions: APM Client and MSIE 11 forced to compartibility mode.
bugs.impact: Certain pages on client UI are not being rendered or being rendered with errors.
bugs.workaround: Don't push MSIE 11 to compatibility mode with APM Use browsers that are good with javascript.
bugs.fix: We've added meta that sets MSIE in native mode. Although group policy in domain still can overwrite it, for most use cases it's enough.

bugs.title: The wrong profile name is used for the HTTP header limits
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP_PSM profile overrides the HTTP profile's limits for http headers. However, when the limit is exceeded, the HTTP profile name is used, rather than the HTTP_PSM profile name.
bugs.conditions: HTTP_PSM is used, together with differing limits between HTTP and HTTP_PSM on the maximum number of headers allowed.
bugs.impact: The log message generated when the header count is exceeded will be misleading.
bugs.fix: The HTTP header count limit now describes the correct profile that that limit came from.

bugs.title: GTM listener object cannot be created via tmsh while in non-Common partition
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use tmsh to create a GTM listener in a non-Common partition.
bugs.conditions: -- In a non-Common partition. -- Create a listener using a command similar to the following: (/Common/newpart)(tmos)# create gtm listener new address 10.2.2.2
bugs.impact: The listener will not be created. The system outputs an error similar to the following: 01020036:3: The requested profile (/Common/newpart/udp_gtm_dns) was not found.
bugs.fix: GTM Listener parser now correctly handles validation and selections of profiles for GTM listeners.

bugs.title: Silent reboot, identified with bad_tlp_status and completion_time_out in the sel log
bugs.symptoms: The most common symptom is a reboot of the unit without much detail in the normal tmm or ltm logs. From there, inspect the SEL logs. In the SEL logs, you will see a message about a bad_tlp_status, followed shortly by a message about completion_time_out_status. Those two messages together indicate this known issue.
bugs.conditions: -- There are empty 10 GB ports or 10 GB ports that have optics but are not connected to a proper link. -- Running on one of the following platforms: i2600, i2800, i4600, i4800.
bugs.impact: The unit intermittently reboots.
bugs.workaround: To prevent the issue from occurring, you must populate all 10 Gb ports with optic cables and ensure they are connecting to a working peer link. A single 10 Gb empty or improperly connected port can cause a system reboot. If that is not possible, however, there is no workaround, and you must contact F5 Technical Support to request a software update or engineering hotfix. Important: A device Return Materials Authorization (RMA) will not prevent this issue.
bugs.fix: There is a BIG-IP system software update to disable the 10 Gb FPGA mac receiver until a valid link is detected. This eliminates the issue and prevents the ultra jumbo packet from being sent to the FPGA datapath.

bugs.title: MCPD might crash if the AOM restarts
bugs.symptoms: In very rare circumstances, mcpd might crash when the AOM restarts.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while AOM is restarting.
bugs.impact: System goes offline for a few minutes.
bugs.fix: Added error handling to prevent crash. If this error occurs in the future it will not crash, but a restart of mcpd is required.

bugs.title: ltmVirtualServStatCurrentConnsPerSec statistic is maintained only for rate-limited virtuals
bugs.symptoms: When the LTM virtual server statistic table is accessed through SNMP, the CurrentConnsPerSec counter is meaningful only for virtual servers that have rate limiting configured.
bugs.conditions: When using SNMP to query virtual server statistics.
bugs.impact: The CurrentConnsPerSec counter will be 0 unless the virtual server has rate limiting enabled. This may be confusing because the statistic's MIB description does not explain the statistic's use.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The MIB description has been updated.

bugs.title: Old versions of APM configuration snapshots need to be reaped more aggressively if not used
bugs.symptoms: Currently, it takes 24 hrs for old versions of APM config snapshots that are not being used to time out and to release the memory. If access profiles are complex and are updated frequently within 24 hrs, memory resource is likely to be exhausted.
bugs.conditions: If access profiles are updated frequently within 24 hrs and each version of the configuration snapshot contains many variables.
bugs.impact: TMM may run out of memory and crash, causing service interruption.
bugs.fix: Per-session access policy snapshots are now deleted after 60 minutes instead of 24 hours.

bugs.title: AVR Max metrics shows wrong values
bugs.symptoms: In the AVR HTTP Page, metrics Max TPS and Max Throughput display incorrect values.
bugs.conditions: The root-cause is 32bit overflow, so the incorrect values are displayed when there are high volumes of traffic.
bugs.impact: Displayed metrics do not correctly show activity.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Represented values are now in 64bit instead of 32bit, and correct values are displayed.

bugs.title: Endless loop of requests when Fingerprint enabled on ASM Policy and client timezone is UTC+5 and east
bugs.symptoms: An endless loop of requests will be sent by browser when an ASM end user attempts to access a virtual server when Fingerprint is enabled on the ASM Policy. This happen only for client systems that are located in a timezone of UTC+5 or east from that.
bugs.conditions: -- Fingerprint is enabled on the ASM Policy. -- ASM end users are located in a timezone of UTC+5 or east from that.
bugs.impact: ASM end users are being blocked from accessing the back-end server.
bugs.fix: ASM end users in timezone UTC+5 and eastward no longer experience a request loop when Fingerprint is enabled on the ASM Policy.

bugs.title: Failed to load sample requests on the Traffic Learning page with VIOL_MALICIOUS_IP viol is raised
bugs.symptoms: Failed to Learn page malicious IP addresses in a specific case.
bugs.conditions: -- IP intelligence is turn on. -- Logging is turned off.
bugs.impact: Requests that should be learned are not.
bugs.workaround: Turn on logging.
bugs.fix: The system now Learns page malicious IP addresses when IP intelligence is turn on and logging is turned off.

bugs.title: Analytics based on tmstat-tables might cause high CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: High CPU usage on some configuration due to inefficient joining process for AVR statistics based on tmstat-tables.
bugs.conditions: Having any of the tmstat-based analytics available on machine.
bugs.impact: Might cause high CPU usage.
bugs.fix: Joining process for analytics based on tmstat tables was refactored to be more efficient.

bugs.title: Several factory policy templates have delayed blocking enabled
bugs.symptoms: Several factory Application Ready policy templates have delayed blocking in Session Tracking enabled by default.
bugs.conditions: Create a new policy using a factory Application Ready policy template.
bugs.impact: Delayed blocking in Session Tracking is enabled by default.
bugs.workaround: Disable delayed blocking in Session Tracking.
bugs.fix: Factory Application Ready policy templates have delayed blocking in Session Tracking correctly disabled by default.

bugs.title: Cannot create a Citrix or VMware View resource from Admin UI in a non-Common partition with a non-default route domain using pool as a destination
bugs.symptoms: Administrator cannot create a Citrix or VMware View resource from Admin UI in a non-Common partition with a non-default route domain using pool as a destination. The system posts a message similar to the following: 01070734:3: Configuration error: apm resource remote-desktop: /subpart/sec-vdi-desktop :only one destination type is supported.
bugs.conditions: 1) Non-default partition used (i.e., not the /Common partition). 2) This non-default partition uses a non-zero route domain. 3) A pool created in this partition.
bugs.impact: VDI resources (Citrix/VMware View) cannot be created using Admin UI in a non-default partition with a non-zero default route domain.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to create such a resource, using a set of commands similar to the following: In the /Common partition, run the following command: cd /subpart/ In subpart, run a command similar to the following: create apm resource remote-desktop vmware-view test_res_subpart pool /subpart/pool_subpart_partition
bugs.fix: You can now create a Citrix or VMware View resource from Admin UI in a non-Common partition with a non-default route domain using pool as a destination

bugs.title: Multicast traffic not forwarded to members of VLAN group
bugs.symptoms: Multicast traffic traversing through the BIG-IP system through a VLAN that is member of a VLAN group does not get forwarded to other members of the VLAN group.
bugs.conditions: Multicast traffic ingress from a VLAN in a VLAN group.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not forwarded to the other members of the VLAN group.
bugs.fix: Multicast traffic is now correctly forwarded to members of VLAN group.

bugs.title: BWC with iSession may memory leak
bugs.symptoms: A memory leak may occur when BWC is configured with iSession.
bugs.conditions: -- BWC is configured with iSession. -- The BWC policy is removed or reset.
bugs.impact: A memory leak.
bugs.fix: The memory leak is prevented when BWC and iSession are configured together and a BWC policy is removed or reset.

bugs.title: APM 11.x upgrade breaks 'log only message-id' workflow
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from APM 11.x, if you have the following filter in your config, it is ignored: sys log-config filter /Common/HSL_Splunk { level notice message-id 01490143 publisher /Common/HSL_Splunk source accesscontrol } In this case, the admin user will no longer get HSL messages of type 01490143. The only thing the filter is able do is negative filtering: sys log-config filter /Common/HSL_Splunk { level notice message-id 01490143 publisher none source accesscontrol } In this case, specifying publisher 'none' still drops log entries, so you can use this filter to send everything except message-id 01490143, but the previous workflow of sending only message-id 01490143 no longer works.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from 11.x. -- the log-config filter in 11.x is configured to filter only for message-id 01490143, for example: sys log-config filter /Common/HSL_Splunk { level notice message-id 01490143 publisher /Common/HSL_Splunk source accesscontrol } sys log-config publisher /Common/HSL_Splunk { destinations { /Common/HSL_Splunk { } } } sys log-config destination remote-high-speed-log /Common/HSL_Splunk { pool-name /Common/HSL_Splunk protocol udp } -- Upgrading to 12.x or 13.x.
bugs.impact: The previous workflow of sending only message-id 01490143 no longer works.

bugs.title: Second block device image install fails to install
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh install sys software block-device-image' fails in a vCMP guest after a previous, successful installation.
bugs.conditions: vCMP guest install using the command 'tmsh install sys software block-device-image' executed a second time in succession.
bugs.impact: After one block device install succeeds, subsequent installations will fail before rebooting.
bugs.workaround: Restart lind on all blades of the vCMP guest using the following command: clsh bigstart restart lind
bugs.fix: Block device image installs are now cleaned-up in vCMP guests, so the installation failure no longer occurs.

bugs.title: FastHTTP may crash when receiving a fragmented IP packet
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server configured to use FastHTTP may cause a TMM core if fragmented IP packets are received by the virtual. This can be observed by the following TMM log statement: panic: Assertion 'l4hdr set' failed.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server configured with a FastHTTP profile receiving fragmented IP packets.
bugs.impact: Intermittent TMM core, resulting in a TMM restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use a different profile than FastHTTP, such as a full proxy with TCP/HTTP filters.
bugs.fix: Force packet reassembly before packet is forwarded to a FastHTTP virtual.

bugs.title: TMM0 on the secondary blade sends out extra ARP replies
bugs.symptoms: TMM0 on the secondary blade can send out more than one ARP reply when it receives an ARP request.
bugs.conditions: ARP request is received by TMM0 on the secondary blade.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends out extra ARP replies.

bugs.title: Non-admin BIG-IP users can now view/re-deploy iApps through TMUI.
bugs.symptoms: Non-admin BIG-IP users cannot view deployed iApps, so they cannot redeploy the iApp. The system presents an error and does not allow access to the component view or the reconfiguration view. The error shown is 'An error has occurred while trying to process your request.'
bugs.conditions: -- Login to the BIG-IP system as a non-admin. -- Try to view components or reconfigure iApps.
bugs.impact: Cannot view/re-deploy iApps.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to view/re-deploy iApps. There are two TMUI workarounds to view/re-deploy iApps. Once you employ one of the workarounds, a Manager user can reconfigure the iApp successfully. Note: After successful submission, the system posts the error described, and the Manager still cannot access the Component list or iApps editing screens. -- Click on 'app_name' link anywhere in the system where iApp-related objects are listed. For example, if the iApp created a virtual server, click the Application column link on the 'Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers : Virtual Server List' page. -- Have an Admin user provide the direct link to app. To do so, perform the following procedure: 1. Login as Admin to the BIG-IP system. 2. Navigate to iApps :: Application Services : Applications :: <app_name>. 3. Get the direct link to the app reconfigure page by hovering over the Settings icon and then clicking 'Direct link to this page'. Note: This link will work as long as 'app_name' and template name have not been modified. The URL appears similar to the following: https://10.10.10.10/tmui/Control/jspmap/tmui/application/reenter.jsp?mode=app&name=/ptn1/abcd.app/abcd&template_name=/Common/f5.microsoft_exchange_2010_2013_cas.v1.6.1 4. Logout as Admin and login as Manager. 5. Paste the app direct link in the browser's address bar and press Enter.
bugs.fix: Non-admin BIG-IP users can now view/re-deploy iApps through TMUI.

bugs.title: Upgrade from v12.1.1, v12.1.2, v12.1.3, or v13.0.0 fails when DoS application profile has heavy URLs configured
bugs.symptoms: When heavy URLs are configured within a DoS application profile, an upgrade from v12.1.1, v12.1.2, v12.1.3, or v13.0.0 to a later version fails with an error: Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:dos_user_heavy_urls status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP v12.1.1, v12.1.2, v12.1.3, or v13.0.0 installed. -- Heavy URLs configured within DoS application profile. -- Upgrading to later version.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading from v12.1.1, v12.1.2, v12.1.3, or v13.0.0 to any later version, remove heavy URLs from all DoS profiles, and then re-add manually after successful upgrade.
bugs.fix: Upgrade now supports correct upgrading of DoS application heavy URLs.

bugs.title: Signature System corruption from specific ASU prevents ASU load after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After loading Attack Signature Update "ASM-SignatureFile_20170403_145743.im" on 11.5.4 HF2 (or later) and upgrading to certain software versions, attempts to perform Signature Update fail.
bugs.conditions: -- Loading Attack Signature Update "ASM-SignatureFile_20170403_145743.im". -- Using v11.5.4 HF2 (or later). -- Upgrading the device to 11.6.1, 12.1.0, 12.1.1, or 12.1.2.
bugs.impact: Attempts to perform Signature Update fail.
bugs.workaround: The mistaken Signature System can be deleted using the following SQL: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- UPDATE PLC.NEGSIG_SIGNATURE_SYSTEMS set system_id = 14 where system_id = (select system_id FROM PLC.NEGSIG_SYSTEMS where system_name = 'Apache'); DELETE FROM PLC.NEGSIG_SYSTEMS where system_name = 'Apache'; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
bugs.fix: Database corruption introduced by loading Attack Signature Update 'ASM-SignatureFile_20170403_145743.im' is now corrected upon upgrade.

bugs.title: tmm crash in free_bufctls
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes in free_bufctls.
bugs.conditions: Any double-free or use-after-free issue may cause this crash. Note: The component causing the issue may vary.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release provides improved memory handling.

bugs.title: The HTTP2 and SPDY filters may cause a TMM crash in complicated scenarios
bugs.symptoms: A TMM crash caused by a double-free of memory within the HTTP2 and SPDY filters. This crash could occur in other TMM sub-systems unrelated to HTTP2 or SPDY.
bugs.conditions: The HTTP2 or SPDY filter is used, together with many other TMM modules. This situation is difficult to trigger.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The HTTP2 and SPDY filters will no longer double-free memory in rare situations.

bugs.title: TFTP_DATA_SETUP/TFTP_DATA_TEARDOWN messages may not be logged if client and server reuse the ports
bugs.symptoms: TFTP_DATA_SETUP/TFTP_DATA_TEARDOWN messages may not be logged if client and server reuse the ports
bugs.conditions: Client and server must reuse the ports quickly for this to occur. When TFTP data transfer is started TMM creates a new flow for it and logs a "TFTP_DATA_SETUP" message if ALG logging is enabled. "TFTP_DATA_TEARDOWN" message is logged when the flow expires. The flow established to transfer the data expires after idletimeout configure in the TFTP profile. While the flow is alive if a new data transfer is initiated between the same client,server and if they use reuse the source,destination ports then TMM will not create a new for this data transfer. The existing flow will be reuse and the log messages will not be logged.
bugs.impact: Some TFTP data transfers are not logged.

bugs.title: Live Update via Proxy No Longer Works
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP devices that need to use a proxy server to communicate with callhome.f5.com, no longer receive, or check for, automatic updates.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP device is behind a network firewall and outbound communication must be through a proxy.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP will not be able to contact the callhome server to check for, or receive, updates.
bugs.workaround: Updates can be downloaded manually from the F5 Downloads server and installed directly on the BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Proxy settings are correctly used when contacting the F5 callhome server.

bugs.title: Secure renegotiation is set while data is not available.
bugs.symptoms: Secure renegotiation is set while data is not available, which causes a crash in certain connections.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when handling SSL secure renegotiation in certain connections.
bugs.impact: Crashes happen to certain SSL connections.
bugs.fix: Secure renegotiation is set while data is not available no longer causes a crash in certain connections.

bugs.title: Obscuring secrets in files collected by qkview
bugs.symptoms: Some config files collected by qkview may have clear text secrets.
bugs.conditions: Run qkview and extract to see files with cleartext secrets
bugs.impact: Plaintext secrets are uploaded to iHealth.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue, follow this procedure: 1. Untar qkview file. 2. Obfuscate secrets from the affected file. 3. Recreate qkview file to upload. For more information, see K55559493: Obfuscating sensitive data in a QKView file :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K55559493. Qkview obfuscation ================== -- Specific information from text files collected by qkview can be replaced/obscured. -- Configuration file is in JSON format and it requires regex search pattern and replacement text for given files. Config file =========== /etc/qkview_obfuscate.conf Config Template =============== { "filename_regex1": { "search_regex11": "replace_text11", "search_regex12": "replace_text12", "search_regex13": "replace_text13" <= No comma after the last element. }, "filename_regex2": { "search_regex21": "replace_text21", "search_regex22": "replace_text22", "search_regex23": "replace_text23" } <= No comma after the last node. } Notes ===== -- Search-and-replace rules are applied to the files that match the filename regex. -- Filename and search_pattern are the regex. JSON special characters need to be escaped in the regex. (JSON special chars list :: http://json.org/.) Example: search_pattern "bindpw\s+(\S+)" should be "bindpw\\s+(\\S+)". ('\' is escaped by '\\'.) -- If a filename matches multiple filename regexes, all rules of those files' regexes are applied to that file. Example: { "abc123\\.conf": { "password\\s+(\\S+)": "password ####", "passphrase\\s+(\\S+)": "passphrase ####" }, "abc\\w+\\.conf": { "bindpw\\s+(\\S+)": "bindpw dummypasswd" } } Because abc123.conf matches both filename regexes, all three rules are applied to abc123.conf. -- Obfuscation works only on text files. Compressed files are ignored. -- The qkview command fails if the config file is syntactically incorrect. Sample config ============= { "abc123\\.conf": { "password\\s+(\\S+)": "password ####", "passphrase\\s+(\\S+)": "passphrase ####" }, "myapp?\\w+\\.conf": { "bindpw\\s+(\\S+)": "bindpw dummypasswd" } } "abc123\\.conf" - matches abc123.conf "myapp?\\w+\\.conf - matches myapp*.conf

bugs.title: XenApp 6.5 published icons are not displayed on APM Webtop
bugs.symptoms: While publishing XenApp 6.5 resources through APM Webtop, some applications are not displaying the icons correctly. VDI Error logs are seen as follows: failed to handle '/f5vdi/citrix/icon/': Incorrect bitmap size"
bugs.conditions: -- XenApp 6.5 is used with their rollup hotfix 6 or 7. -- Some of the third-party applications more icon bitmap information than expected.
bugs.impact: Icons are not displayed on the APM Webtop
bugs.fix: Now APM Webtop correctly displays Citrix XenApp icons correctly regardless of the size of the bitmap data.

bugs.title: TMM 'DoS Layer 7' memory leak during config load
bugs.symptoms: Degraded performance; potential eventual out-of-memory. Note: The 'DoS Layer 7' allocations increase by 'TMM count * #domains' after each config load. Tip: You can watch the watch the 'DoS Layer 7' allocations increase on a shell on the BIG-IP system using the following command: # watch -n1 -- 'tmctl -s name,allocated,max_allocated,cur_allocs memory_usage_stat | grep -E "^name|---|^DoS Layer 7 "'
bugs.conditions: -- Provision ASM. -- Make sure the built-in 'security dos bot-signature' are added to the config. -- Load the config from another shell using the following command: tmsh load sys config
bugs.impact: Degraded performance; potential eventual out-of-memory.
bugs.fix: Fix memory leak after each config load.

bugs.title: Network failover without a management address causes active-active after unit1 reboot
bugs.symptoms: An appliance in a Device Service Cluster may erroneously claim Active status when it is rebooted. This results in an Active/Active situation, which may resolve itself by causing a failover.
bugs.conditions: Device Service Cluster with only self-ips configured for the failover network.
bugs.impact: Unexpected failover may cause traffic interruption.
bugs.workaround: Configuring multiple redundant network failover paths, including the management network will reduce the possibility of this problem.
bugs.fix: The failover daemon has been fixed to recognize that the self-IP communication paths are non-functional while the TMM is starting up, and will not go Active until sufficient time has elapsed to conclude that the peer is not present. Since the device cannot successfully process traffic until the TMM is functional, this does not result in a delay in restoring service.

bugs.title: High CPU usage from asm_config_server
bugs.symptoms: Use of Automatic policy builder might result in high CPU usage of asm_config_server (and ASM slowdown).
bugs.conditions: - Automatic policy builder. - Several entity types learning in 'Add all entities' configuration.
bugs.impact: ASM availability impacted.
bugs.workaround: - Switch to Manual policy builder. - Set entity types learning to compact / selective / never.
bugs.fix: prevented policy builder unnecessary load on asm config

bugs.title: Flows are incorrectly processed on a standby system.
bugs.symptoms: Standby system incorrectly processes flows, even if there is no other traffic group active on that system.
bugs.conditions: -- Spanning is enabled for a virtual address. -- No other traffic group active on a standby system.
bugs.impact: Flows are incorrectly processed.

bugs.title: L7 Policy reconfiguration causes a slow memory leak
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server with a L7 policy is reconfigured, a small amount of memory is leaked.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server with L7 policies has a configuration change.
bugs.impact: The memory leak will reduce the amount of resources for the TMM.
bugs.fix: L7 Policies no longer leak memory when a virtual server using them is reconfigured.

bugs.title: iApp - f5.forward_proxy + checksum - config error upgrading from v12 to v13
bugs.symptoms: v13.0.0 cli script f5.app_utils was released without a signature, causing signed iapps that refer to it to fail. 01070734:3: Configuration error: When updating status on AppTemplate ... signature verification of in Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: 1. Must be upgrading to 13.0.0. 2. Must have imported or created an iapp template that has a dependence, ie. tmsh::include. 3. Must have applied a checksum or signature to the imported template. Note: Deploying the iapp is not required. Config load will fail even if the iapp template is not used.
bugs.impact: Upgrade to v13.0.0 fails to load config.
bugs.workaround: Remove signatures and checksums from iApps that have script dependencies prior to upgrade.
bugs.fix: iApp templates and scripts are now signed.

bugs.title: tmm may crash from DoSL7
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server configured with the following: compression profile configuration, HTTP/DoSL7 with DoSL7 iRule, RamCache.
bugs.impact: SIGSEGV. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a possible tmm crash.

bugs.title: Localdbmgr process cores
bugs.symptoms: You see continuous "emerg logger: Re-starting localdbmgr" messages and localdbmgr continually cores.
bugs.conditions: When localdbmgr process tries to persist local user information to the MySQL Database.
bugs.impact: localdbmgr cores, APM local user database does not initialize.
bugs.fix: localdbmgr no longer crashes when trying to persist local user information to the MySQL Database.

bugs.title: GTM/DNS manual resume pool member not saved to config when disabled
bugs.symptoms: manual-resume disabled pool member becomes available after reboot.
bugs.conditions: GTM pool is configured with manual-resume enabled and its pool member was once unavailable.
bugs.impact: Unexpected available pool member which should be disabled.
bugs.workaround: After the pool member becomes disabled, manually run: # tmsh save sys config gtm-only

bugs.title: TIN cookie value is sent as a negative integer when Max session timeout and Inactivity timeout are set to more than 24 days in access policy.
bugs.symptoms: TIN cookie value is sent as a negative integer when Max Session Timeout and Inactivity Timeout are set to more than 24 days in access policy, or when Inactivity Timeout and Max Session Timeout are set to 0.
bugs.conditions: -- Access policy. -- Max session timeout and Inactivity timeout values are set to more than 24 days, or to 0 (zero).
bugs.impact: TIN cookie value is sent as a negative integer.
bugs.fix: Now the TIN cookie is properly set to a positive integer when Max Session Timeout and Inactivity Timeout are set to more than 24 days in access policy, or to 0 (zero).

bugs.title: Each save operation on the Policy Properties page records extra audit messages in the Audit Log.
bugs.symptoms: When changes are made to 'Security :: Application Security : Policy : Policy Properties' and then saved, some extra audit messages are recorded to 'Security :: Application Security : Policy : Audit : Log'
bugs.conditions: Click 'Save' button on the Policy Properties page.
bugs.impact: There are extra audit messages are recorded to the Audit Log. This is a cosmetic that has no impact on functionality.
bugs.fix: The previously used policy properties page has been replaced with a new one, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Global SNAT sets TTL to 255 instead of decrementing
bugs.symptoms: Global SNAT sets the TTL to 255 instead of decrementing.
bugs.conditions: Global SNAT configured.
bugs.impact: Possible routing loop.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: TTL for global SNAT now gets decremented.

bugs.title: A virtual server's connections per second (precision.last_value) is confusingly named.
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server's current connections-per-second statistic has a confusing name. The statistic is maintained when rate limiting is configured for a virtual server. The statistic is updated when the virtual hits a rate-limiting condition, and it stays at the last value it held when the limit was hit.
bugs.conditions: If the rate limit is never configured then the value is 0. If the rate limit is configured and is hit, then the value is the active count when the limit was hit. The value stays at that count until the limit is hit again.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact, but the statistic's meaning is confusing.
bugs.workaround: The MIB description should clarify the meaning of this statistic.

bugs.title: Memory might become corrupted when a Standby device transitions to Active during failover
bugs.symptoms: When a failover event occurs with connection mirroring enabled, it is possible for memory to be corrupted when the Standby device transitions to Active.
bugs.conditions: -- Active-Standby high availability configuration. -- Virtual server configured with the type set to 'Standard'. -- Connection mirroring enabled.
bugs.impact: Tmm might crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Memory is no longer corrupted.

bugs.title: rpcbind was removed from the BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: rpcbind was being installed on the BIG-IP and it is not being used.
bugs.conditions: normal install
bugs.impact: no impact. The daemon was removed so it wouldn't require maintenance and upgrades.
bugs.fix: since rpcbind is not being used on the BIG-IP it was removed.

bugs.title: Edge client on Macbook Pro with touch bar cannot connect to VPN after OS X v10.12.5 update
bugs.symptoms: Edge client running on Macbook Pro 2016 with a touch bar interface cannot connect to VPN in a full tunneling configuration with 'Prohibit routing table modification' option selected. Edge client's svpn.log shows an error entry similar to 2017-05-18,13:55:17:000, 16637,16638,svpn, 1, , 870, CMacOSXRouteTable::UpdateIpForwardEntry2(), EXCEPTION - write failed, 22, Invalid argument.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are met: 1) Edge client is running on Macbook Pro that has the iBridge interface (e.g., one with the touch bar). 2) VPN is configured in full tunneling configuration 3) Mac OS X version is v10.12.5. Note: You can find the interface on the Macbook Pro in the Network Utility under the Info tab.
bugs.impact: VPN connection will fail.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: - Disable 'Prohibit Routing table change' in the network access configuration. - Enable 'Allow access to local subnets'. - Enable a split tunneling configuration.

bugs.title: Refine PUSH flag settings for sub MSS packets
bugs.symptoms: Currently, in Auto mode, PUSH flag is set based on the application/network conditions. The system should instead append a PUSH flag to sub-MSS TCP segments (except 0 length pure ACK) to PUSH small segments faster to the receiving application in auto mode.
bugs.conditions: Non HTTP applications sending sub MSS packets.
bugs.impact: Non HTTP applications receive small segments slower if PUSH Flag is not present in sub-MSS TCP segments.
bugs.fix: In Auto Mode, last sub-MSS TCP segments are always appended with PUSH flag.

bugs.title: Some of the Korean translations in Windows Edge Client were incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Some of the Korean translations in Microsoft Windows Edge Client's main windows are incorrect.
bugs.conditions: User uses Edge Client application on Windows.
bugs.impact: Confusion due to inaccurate translation.

bugs.title: Gossip between Viprion blades
bugs.symptoms: Gossip does not appear to run between Viprion blades in a device service cluster.
bugs.conditions: Two BIG-IP systems running the latest build, configured with device service clustering and an HA group.
bugs.impact: Enabling Gossip on the non-primary Viprion blade interferes with communication between the primary and the remote peer.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable Gossip on the non-primary Viprion blade.
bugs.fix: The system no longer enables Gossip sync on non-primary VIPRION blades.
bugs.behavior: Previously, when The REST framework's 'gossip' mechanism was enabled on the non-primary VIPRION blade, it interfered with communication between the primary and the remote peer. Now, the 'gossip' mechanism is disabled on the non-primary blade, so communication between the primary and the remote peer is not impacted.

bugs.title: Added indication for requests that were logged only as sample request for the learning suggestion or were marked for delete
bugs.symptoms: Some requests are not part of Requests log, though they are saved in the same place. BIG-IP administrator user can get access to them using Support ID.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP administrator opens a request using its Support ID. -- The request being opened is marked for delete or it was logged as sample for learning suggestion, but it didn't answer to logging profile criteria.
bugs.impact: 1. A request is visible that the BIG-IP administrator expected to be deleted (till next request log cleanup) 2. A request is visible that doesn't answer to the logging profile criteria (e.g., request is Legal, while only Illegal are logged). 3. The request accessed using the Support ID is not visible when applying other filters, e.g., when filtering by time of that request.
bugs.workaround: None. This is an artifact of database functionality.
bugs.fix: Message added to the request details explaining that this request was marked for delete or logged for learning suggestion only.

bugs.title: KeyLogger fails to work properly with jQuery 1.11.1
bugs.symptoms: 'Invalid calling object' error message in the console.
bugs.conditions: - Edge Browser. - jQuery 1.11.1. - KeyLogger is enabled. - The BIG-IP user moves the cursor to a protected password field.
bugs.impact: 'Invalid calling object' error message in the console.
bugs.workaround: Disable KeyLogger in GUI.

bugs.title: Monitor node log fd leak by bigd instances not actively monitoring node
bugs.symptoms: Each instance of bigd running on the BIG-IP appliance or on each blade in a VIPRION chassis opens a file descriptor for each node or pool member that has monitor logging enabled. However, only one instance of bigd is actively monitoring each individual node, and actively logging health monitor events to the node log. When LTM health monitors are configured with node logging enabled, the bigd daemon may leak file descriptors for the node logs when the monitor is removed from the LTM node, pool, or pool member configuration. Note: This problem does not occur if node logging is disabled in the LTM node or pool member configuration ('logging' value set to 'disabled' in the LTM node or pool member configuration) prior to removing the monitor from the LTM node, pool or pool member configuration.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when the following conditions are met: 1. An LTM health monitor is assigned to an LTM node, pool or pool member with node logging enabled ('logging' value set to 'enabled' in the LTM node or pool member configuration). 2. The LTM health monitor is removed from the LTM node, pool or pool member configuration while logging is still enabled ('monitor' value set to 'none').
bugs.impact: When this problem occurs, the instance of bigd that is actively monitoring a particular node will close its file descriptor to that node's log file (under /var/log/monitors), but other instances of bigd running on the BIG-IP appliance or on each blade in a VIPRION chassis will leak their file descriptor to the node log. File descriptors that are opened by the bigd daemon and not closed will count against bigd's internal file descriptor limit. This may result in file descriptor exhaustion and failure of LTM health monitoring.
bugs.workaround: Disable node logging (set 'logging' value to 'disabled') in the LTM node or pool member configuration prior to removing the monitor from the LTM node, pool, or pool member configuration.
bugs.fix: The bigd daemon no longer leaks file descriptors for monitor node logs when multiple instances of bigd are running, LTM health monitors are configured with node logging enabled, and the monitor is then removed from the LTM node, pool, or pool member configuration.

bugs.title: Some HTTP iRule commands should always return results as Tcl lists, but do not.
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP iRule commands behave differently if they return only a single result. They will return a Tcl string rather than a Tcl list containing a string.
bugs.conditions: One or more of the following HTTP iRule commands are used, and the conditions exist such that a single result is returned: HTTP::cookie names HTTP::cookie attribute names HTTP::header names HTTP::header values
bugs.impact: A string is returned rather than a list. This may affect Tcl code that expects the result to be a list, leading to incorrect behavior.
bugs.workaround: If the result is not a list, this can be detected in a Tcl script, and the result handled as a special case.
bugs.fix: HTTP iRule commands that return a Tcl list will do so in all cases.

bugs.title: Occasional "profile not found" errors following activate access policy
bugs.symptoms: Immediately following the applying of a modified access policy it is possible for some profiles to disappear. It is transient and within a minute or two the profiles are available again.
bugs.conditions: Clicking "apply access policy" in the GUI or using tmsh to increment snapshot ids will clear the list of profiles and policies and then rebuild those lists. Authentication requests using profiles or policies not yet rebuilt returned the "profile not found" error.
bugs.impact: Some authentication attempts fail while the lists get rebuilt. Retrying the authentication a minute or two later succeeds.
bugs.workaround: Retry the authentication.
bugs.fix: Applying Access Policies in APM is improved to avoid a short dead time between when the old policies are removed and the new policies are activated.

bugs.title: svpn goes into a reconnect loop when another adapter is connected after VPN is connected.
bugs.symptoms: If you connect to VPN, and a previously disconnected network adapter (WiFi/ethernet) gets connected, then svpn goes into a reconnect loop due to routing table conflicts.
bugs.conditions: - Split tunnel configuration. - 'Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access' is enabled. - VPN is connected and a previously disconnected network adapter (WiFi/ethernet) gets connected.
bugs.impact: Reconnecting loop until you manually click Disconnect.
bugs.workaround: Disable the 'Prohibit routing table changes' option in Network Access.
bugs.fix: On the Mac VPN client, the svpn process no longer goes into a reconnect loop when another adapter is connected after VPN is connected.

bugs.title: Use HSB HiGig MAC reset to recover both FCS errors and link instability
bugs.symptoms: In addition to HiGig Link instability, FCS errors can be seen on internal switch and HSB Higig link. This is likely some PHY-related issues and can cause instability in communication links. One symptom associated with this might be that a blade cannot become active and join the cluster.
bugs.conditions: FCS errors reported in tmm/hsbe2_internal_lbb_hgm. Traffic failure observed on some VIPs or self IPs.
bugs.impact: Link unstable, frame loss. TMOS MPI and CDP packet loss and internal blade communication issues. HSB lockup and accumulated FCS errors observed from stats and log.
bugs.workaround: A switch port reset might be used to recover this failure. Note, however: that procedure might cause potential HSB lockups.
bugs.fix: FCS errors and link instability no longer occur.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin can accumulate memory used for patching very large files
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite plugin memory usage is significantly higher than normal (up to 200 MB RSS) and does not decrease.
bugs.conditions: This happens because the plugin caches and reuses already allocated chunks of memory instead of releasing them to the operating system.
bugs.impact: Out-of-memory crashes on systems with low amounts of memory.
bugs.workaround: Use one or both of the following workarounds: -- Restart rewrite when memory usage is too high. -- Disable patching for large (15-20 MB uncompressed) files.

bugs.title: cpcfg cannot copy a configuration on a chassis platform
bugs.symptoms: cpcfg fails with errors similar to: info: Getting configuration from HD1.3 info: Copying configuration to HD1.1 info: Applying configuration to HD1.1 error: status 256 returned by command: F5_INSTALL_MODE=install F5_INSTALL_SESSION_TYPE=hotfix chroot /mnt/tm_install/23102.e3MAZU /usr/local/bin/im -force /var/local/ucs/config.ucs info: >++++ result: info: Extracting manifest: /var/local/ucs/config.ucs info: /shared: Not enough free space info: 6144 bytes required info: 0 bytes available info: /var/local/ucs/config.ucs: Not enough free disk space to install! info: Operation aborted.
bugs.conditions: Only on a chassis platform running 13.0.x.
bugs.impact: You cannot use cpcfg on a chassis platform.
bugs.workaround: Save a UCS from the source volume, reboot to the destination volume, then load that UCS file.
bugs.fix: cpcfg could incorrectly calculate the amount of free space available, refusing to do the copy unless the /shared filesystem had sufficient space to do the copy. This has been resolved and this free space calculation is done correctly.

bugs.title: tcpdump may take several seconds to start capturing packets on vCMP guests
bugs.symptoms: Running a tcpdump may take 3 or more seconds to start capturing packets.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of these conditions are met: - tcpdump is being run within a vCMP guest on a VIPRION platform. - The guest has more than one blade in-use.
bugs.impact: tcpdump takes a slightly longer-than-expected time to start capturing traffic.
bugs.workaround: Wait several additional seconds to ensure that the tcpdump operation has a sufficient interval to start capturing packets.
bugs.fix: tcpdump now starts capturing packets sooner.

bugs.title: Deleting virtual server may cause tmm to segfault
bugs.symptoms: Deleting virtual server may cause tmm to segfault.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server is rate-limited. -- In-progress connections exist. -- Virtual server is deleted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Deleting virtual server no longer causes tmm to segfault.

bugs.title: Default GTM HTTPS monitor no longer supports EXPORT ciphers
bugs.symptoms: The default GTM https monitor (and its derivative built-in monitors like https_head_f5) supports EXPORT grade ciphers.
bugs.conditions: Default GTM HTTPS or its derivative built-in monitors like https_head_f5 are being used to monitor a node that only supports EXPORT ciphers.
bugs.impact: The node that GTM is monitoring is marked as GREEN/available.
bugs.fix: Default GTM HTTPS monitor no longer supports EXPORT ciphers.
bugs.behavior: The built-in GTM HTTPS monitor used to support EXPORT ciphers. This meant that monitoring a node that only supported EXPORT ciphers from GTM with the HTTPS monitor would result in the node being marked as GREEN/available. Now the built-in GTM HTTPS monitor (and its derivative built-in monitors like https_head_f5) no longer support EXPORT ciphers. If GTM is monitoring a node that only supports EXPORT ciphers with a default HTTPS monitor (or a derivative built-in like https_head_f5), then the node will be marked DOWN/offline. Note: If you want to continue monitoring a node from GTM that supports only EXPORT ciphers, you can create a custom HTTPS monitor and define the custom cipherlist field to allow EXPORT ciphers.

bugs.title: L2 Wire global syn cookie in HW floods SYN ACK packets to both the VLANs joined in a L2 VLAN group.
bugs.symptoms: Ports that are in L2 mode have learning disabled. So although HSB should tell the switch about the ingress port from which the packet came, it cannot do so in this release. That means that the SYN ACK packet will be flooded to both the VLANs. But only the client that sends that actual SYN will accept the SYN ACK, as the other interface contains the incorrect MAC addresses and will be dropped by the host connected to the second side of port.
bugs.conditions: Whenever AFM global syn cookie is triggered in hardware.
bugs.impact: Global syn-cookie does not work without a virtual server even if another global DoS vectors work without a virtual server. The system will send a spurious SYN ACK. There may or may not be any impact, as the spurious SYN ACK packet's MAC address will not be matched and should be dropped by the host. However, there is a possibility that it might lead to flooding of SYN ACK packets when a SYN attack is ongoing.

bugs.title: Filter by Support ID is not working in Request Log
bugs.symptoms: In some cases the Support ID of a request might be shorter than 19 digits. In this case filter by Support ID does not work in Request Logs.
bugs.conditions: -- Support ID is shorter than 19 digits. -- Trying to filter by Support ID.
bugs.impact: Filter by Support ID is not displayed in filter bar and does not affect the list.
bugs.workaround: You can try to filter by last 4 digits of Support ID. Although that does not replace filter by Support ID functionality, it might help.
bugs.fix: Filter by Support ID works for any length but 4 digits (in this case search uses the last 4 digits; also a 4-digit Support ID is not a realistic occurrence).

bugs.title: Wildcard URLs with identical wildcard order will have only one of them being enforced
bugs.symptoms: Enforcement is done on only one of the wildcards with an duplicate wildcard order.
bugs.conditions: There are several wildcard URLs simultaneously using REST, without specifying wildcardOrder.
bugs.impact: Not all wildcards will be enforced.
bugs.workaround: Update each wildcard with a specific wildcard order.
bugs.fix: Enforcement is now done on all wildcards, according to new enforcement wildcard order set when applying the policy.

bugs.title: DNS Express does not run on i11000 platforms with htsplit disabled.
bugs.symptoms: tmm processes enter a restart loop when trying to run DNS Express (DNSX) on i11000 platforms with htsplit disabled.
bugs.conditions: -- i11000 platform. -- htsplit disabled (sys db scheduler.splitplanes.ltm set to false). -- Trying to run DNSX.
bugs.impact: tmm processes enter a restart loop. In this condition, DNSX does not run, though other DNS functions are unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Enable htsplit using the following command: modify sys db scheduler.splitplanes.ltm value true
bugs.fix: tmm no longer cores under these conditions. However, you cannot use DNSX with htsplit disabled; htsplit must be enabled. Note: DNSX works as expected with htsplit enabled, both before and after the fix.

bugs.title: Keylogger protection is incompatible with the jQuery plugin "capslockstate".
bugs.symptoms: Keylogger protection generates random keypress events on the web page. If the jQuery plugin is in "Caps Lock" state and keylogger generates "a" (for example) then the jQuery plugin change its state back to "Caps Lock" off.
bugs.impact: Keylogger protection changes the state of the jQuery plugin ("Caps Lock" off ,"Caps Lock" on, unknown).
bugs.fix: The FPS code was aligned to the jQuery plugin so that the jQuery plugin and keylogger protection are now in sync.

bugs.title: WebSocket URLs over SSL don't match when differentiate HTTP/HTTPS is disabled
bugs.symptoms: A WebSocket URL is not detected as such in the switch-protocol request.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM policy with 'Differentiate between HTTP/WS and HTTPS/WSS URLs' disabled. -- Explicit WebSocket URLs, '/wss' configured. -- The ASM policy is attached to both a non-SSL virtual server and an SSL virtual server. -- Requests arrives, one from the SSL connection and one from the non-SSL connection.
bugs.impact: Over the SSL connection the request URL is not detected as '/wss' but as the wildcard URL. Over the non-SSL connection the request will be detected as '/wss' the WebSocket URL.
bugs.workaround: Enable 'Differentiate between HTTP/WS and HTTPS/WSS URLs'.
bugs.fix: A WebSocket URL is now detected as such in the switch-protocol request.

bugs.title: Dynamic Routing ZebOS using ip ospf <IP> message-digest-key command may fail.
bugs.symptoms: Failure occurs when attempting to configure or load OSPF configurations in imish using an interface-level command similar to the following: ip ospf <IP> message-digest-key <key index> md5 <password>.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the following command: ip ospf <IP> message-digest-key.
bugs.impact: The command causes an error and cannot be used or loaded. This may cause OSPFv2 adjacencies to fail.
bugs.workaround: If possible, use the non-IP version of the interface-level command, similar to the following: ip ospf message-digest-key <key index> md5 <password>.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly loads the ZebOS 'ip ospf <IP> message-digest-key' interface-level command.

bugs.title: iRule event after source pick is complete and before setting up the server side flow
bugs.symptoms: There is no iRule event after the source pick is complete and before setting up the server side flow.
bugs.conditions: Use iRule to modify the payload with source translation information.
bugs.impact: Cannot modify the payload with source translation information.
bugs.fix: You can now use the SA_PICKED event to affect operations after source translation is completed and before server side flow is established.

bugs.title: TCP flows going through the IP forwarding and L2 forwarding virtual server might get very low bandwidth.
bugs.symptoms: TCP flows going through the IP forwarding and L2 forwarding virtual server might get very low bandwidth.
bugs.conditions: -- BWC policy applied. -- TCP traffic passes through the IP forwarding or L2 forwarding virtual server.
bugs.impact: Lower throughput than expected.
bugs.workaround: When using BWC, use a proxy virtual server instead of IP forwarding or L2 forwarding virtual servers.
bugs.fix: TCP flows going through the IP forwarding and L2 forwarding virtual server no longer affect bandwidth.

bugs.title: LTM 12.1.2 HF1 - Upgrade to 12.1.2 HF1 fails with err "folder does not exist"

bugs.title: Indirect invocation for History object methods fails using Portal Access

bugs.title: 13.1.0 cannot join a device group with 13.1.0.1
bugs.symptoms: 13.1.0.1 cannot form device trust with a 13.1.0 device.
bugs.conditions: A device running 13.1.0 wanting to establish device trust with a device running 13.1.0.1 or vice versa.
bugs.impact: Cannot form Device Trust.
bugs.workaround: 13.1.0 cannot initially form device trust with a 13.1.0.1 device. However, if you establish trust from the 13.1.0.1 device and then bring in the 13.1.0 device from 13.1.0.1, you can mitigate this issue. Once trust is formed, there should be no issue.
bugs.fix: 13.1.0.1 now can form device trust with a 13.1.0 device.

bugs.title: The merge option for the tmsh load sys config command removes existing nested objects
bugs.symptoms: Nested objects are removed when newer objects are merged in. Configuration objects can contain nested objects. The merge option for tmsh load sys config command expects the nested-objects passed in to be merged alongside existing objects. example: Initial configuration [root@plate:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh list ltm pool ltm pool test-pool-mcconfig { members { test-mc1:http { address 10.13.14.15 priority-group 1 session monitor-enabled state checking } test-mc2:http { address 10.13.14.16 priority-group 4 session monitor-enabled state down } } monitor tcp } Run load merge command: [root@plate:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh -m root@(plate)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# load sys config merge from-terminal Enter configuration. Press CTRL-D to submit or CTRL-C to cancel. ltm pool test-pool-mcconfig { members { test-mc2:http { priority-group 0 } } } Loading configuration... root@(plate)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# ^D New configuration, not merged: [root@plate:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh list ltm pool ltm pool test-pool-mcconfig { members { test-mc2:http { address 10.13.14.16 session monitor-enabled state down } } monitor tcp }
bugs.conditions: Execute tmsh load sys config merge from-terminal command. The configuration contains nested objects. The configuration that is being merged in contains nested objects of the same type as the existing configuration.
bugs.impact: Configuration loss: Post merge the existing nested configuration objects are deleted.
bugs.fix: The behavior for the merge option of tmsh load sys config is corrected. The nested objects in the existing configuration are not deleted.

bugs.title: Edge Client logs the routing and IP tables repeatedly
bugs.symptoms: Edge Client logs the routing and IP tables repeatedly - in each reconnecting attempt.
bugs.conditions: Edge Client is in reconnecting state and gateway is reachable. However, APM server is not reachable/responding.
bugs.impact: It fills up the log file with information that is not useful.

bugs.title: Virtual server fails to process RD Gateway connections if 'Source Port' is set to 'Change'
bugs.symptoms: RDP client fails to connect via APM used as RD Gateway, if 'Source Port' is set to 'Change' on the virtual server. Native RDP resources on APM Webtop are also affected.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is used as RD Gateway. -- 'Source Port' is set to 'Change' on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: RDP client cannot connect via APM.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Set the virtual server'Source Port' setting to 'Preserve' (which is the default). -- Disable CMP on the virtual server. To do so, run the following commands: tmsh modify ltm virtual <VS-name> cmp-enabled no tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: CPU Usage Reaches 100% After Traffic Flowed Into CGNAT
bugs.symptoms: CPU usage reaches 100% after traffic flowed Into CGNAT. Issue with re-offloading to ePVA.
bugs.conditions: -- CGNAT configured. -- Most traffic is FastL4 forwarding deterministic LDNS. -- ePVA hardware is in use.
bugs.impact: Default configurations may suddenly show higher CPU performance profile usage after upgrade.
bugs.fix: The following db variables have been added to control re-offload behavior: sys db pva.reoffload.delay { value "5" } sys db pva.reoffload.exponential { value "true" } pva.reoffload.delay is in seconds. This is the amount of time that needs to expire before TMM attempts to re-offload the flow to the ePVA. If pva.reoffload.exponential is 'true', then if there is a collision, there is an exponential backoff (5 seconds, 10 seconds, 20 seconds, and so on), before the flow is re-offloaded). If pva.reoffload.exponential is 'false', then there is no backoff, and the flow is re-offloaded after the pva.reoffload.delay expires.
bugs.behavior: The following db variables have been added to control re-offload behavior: sys db pva.reoffload.delay { value "5" } sys db pva.reoffload.exponential { value "true" } pva.reoffload.delay is in seconds. This is the amount of time that needs to expire before TMM attempts to re-offload the flow to the ePVA. If pva.reoffload.exponential is 'true', then if there is a collision, there is an exponential backoff (5 seconds, 10 seconds, 20 seconds, and so on), before the flow is re-offloaded). If pva.reoffload.exponential is 'false', then there is no backoff, and the flow is re-offloaded after the pva.reoffload.delay expires.

bugs.title: Memory Leak in RAM Cache
bugs.symptoms: A slow increase in the magnitude of the value in the tm_header bucket of the memory_usage_stat table.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during a refresh of a cached document.
bugs.impact: A memory leak whose speed is relative to the life time of the documents in the cache, and the number of documents that can be refreshed.
bugs.workaround: If the document cannot be refreshed, the memory leak won't occur. A server configuration change or a response iRule that removes the Last-Modified, Expires, and Cache-Control headers will allow the BIG-IP system to cache documents and serve them from cache, but will not attempt to refresh them and thus avoid this leak. This workaround results in retrieving the whole document from the server when it has expired.
bugs.fix: Memory Leak in RAM Cache has been fixed.

bugs.title: DSC connections between BIG-IP units may fail to establish
bugs.symptoms: The device service clustering (DSC) connection between two BIG-IP units may fail to establish. One unit will log messages similar to the following example: -- err mcpd[7912]: 01071af4:3: Inbound CMI connection from IP (192.168.100.1) denied because it came from VLAN (v1542), not from expected VLAN (tmm). While the unit at the other end of the connection will log messages similar to the following example: -- notice mcpd[5730]: 01071432:5: CMI peer connection established to 192.168.200.1 port 6699 after 0 retries May 31 20:58:04 BIG-IP-c-sea notice mcpd[5730]: 0107143c:5: Connection to CMI peer 192.168.200.1 has been removed
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the Self-IP addresses used for Config-Sync by the two BIG-IP units are not in the same IP subnet, and special routing is configured between the BIG-IP units. Examples of special routing include a gateway pool or dynamic routing configurations with multiple routes to the same destination (i.e., ECMP routing).
bugs.impact: Config-Sync and device discovery operations will fail between affected units.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by using Self-IP addresses for Config-Sync that are on the same IP subnet or rely on simpler routing to achieve connectivity (i.e., a single route).
bugs.fix: Config-Sync and device discovery operations no longer fail.

bugs.title: Authentication statistics and logs added to Configuration Utility

bugs.workaround: Read logs in /var/log/security.
bugs.fix: New pages were created in the Configuration Utility that provide a view of successful and failed login attempts on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: 'RTSP::header exists' iRule command always returns True
bugs.symptoms: Using the 'RTSP::header exists' command in an iRule returns true even if the header is not present.
bugs.conditions: Using the 'RTSP::header exists' command in an iRule, e.g., [RTSP::header exists "Transmitting"].
bugs.impact: Returns 1 (TRUE) even if the header is not present. Should return 2 (ERR_NOT_FOUND) on failure.

bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP administrator tries to view the GTM link graphs in the GUI, the system reports 'General database error retrieving information'. statsd reports an error in /var/log/ltm err statsd[6318]: 011b030d:3: Graph '/Common/Link_AS394043' not found

bugs.title: Intermittent TMM crash when AFM dynamic (behavioral) signature is enabled and past attack signatures incorrectly exist in the correlation stats table
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent TMM crash when AFM dynamic (behavioral) signature is enabled and past attack signatures incorrectly exist in the correlation stats table - issue is due to TMM (self) abort due to memory corruption in one of the TMSTAT tables AFM uses for correlating dynamic signatures.
bugs.conditions: Following conditions suffice to trigger the TMM crash due to self abort in one of the TMSTAT tables: a) Generate a set of N dynamic signatures (few context). b) When attack stops, the current set of signatures are moved to 'past' attack state. c) If in between, TMM restarts (or receives MCP config again e.g via load), these past attack signatures are incorrectly created in tmstat table which is used only for the current attack signatures - this is the *cause* of the issue! d) New attack appears that somewhat overlap with the 'past' signatures and this causes the following TMSTAT table to be corrupted over period of time.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed, the past attack signatures are never created in the correlation stats table (even for conditions explicitly described above)

bugs.title: Unable to highlight and copy session ID from Active Sessions
bugs.symptoms: The session ID field in Active Session page cannot be selected or copied
bugs.conditions: This occurs on the Access Policy :: Manage Sessions :: Active Session page.
bugs.impact: Cannot select or copy session ID.

bugs.title: Fragmented IP over IPsec tunnels might capture mcp flows and provoke restarts
bugs.symptoms: If fragmented IP packets match an IPsec policy, then get forwarded to another tmm for actual processing, the flow lookup might accidentally grab a stale flow_key for another connflow, including internal MCP flows. When that happens, if IPsec does tunnel those flows, internal MCP heartbeats later miss and cause tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: -- Packet fragmentation. -- Packets are serviced by IPsec due to a matching policy for those packets.
bugs.impact: Tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can prevent this using either of the following methods: -- If you can, arrange that fragmented packets are re-assembled before reaching IPsec policy handling. -- Modify MTU configuration so fragmentation does not happen. Note: There is no mitigation when fragmented packets reach IPsec and need forwarding from one tmm to another.
bugs.fix: Now fragmented packets are handled correctly, and other flows cannot experience interference.

bugs.title: Fragemented IPsec encrypted packets with fragmented original payloads may cause memory leak in the TMM.

Modified config: ltm data-group internal /Common/sample_dg { records { entry1 { data "/BIG-IP BAD" ...

bugs.title: SSO Configurations update is failing from UI
