bugs.title: DNS Express does not correctly process multi-message DNS IXFR updates.
bugs.symptoms: If DNS Express sends an IXFR query to a DNS server, and that server responds with an IXFR update that is larger than one DNS message, DNS Express processes only the first message. DNS Express then updates the SOA serial number to match that of the IXFR, marks the IXFR as successful and the Zone as 'Green'. There is no indication that the IXFR was incomplete. DNS Express might then have, and might serve, incorrect data for that Zone.
bugs.conditions: An IXFR response from a DNS server spans multiple DNS messages. Note: This is not a common condition, but it is possible.
bugs.impact: This might result in incomplete or otherwise inaccurate Zone data, which DNS Express will serve.
bugs.workaround: Note: Although this does have a workaround, there is no way for you to determine that the Zone is complete other than to query the entire zone and compare it to the zone from the master DNS server. To workaround this issue: 1. Stop zxfrd. 2. Remove the database /var/db/zxfrd.bin. 3. Restart zxfrd. This triggers a full transfer (AXFR) of the zone, as well as all the other zones.
bugs.fix: The system now continues the processing of DNS messages until the closing SOA RR is encountered.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes: Pool members can become unknown (blue) after monitor configuration is changed
bugs.symptoms: A pool member configured through an FQDN node and which has multiple associated monitors may become unknown (blue) after a monitor rule change to one of its associated monitors. The expected behavior is that the node should remain 'green' if monitoring is successful with the new rule, but the node may become unknown (blue) until bigd is restarted.
bugs.conditions: A pool member is configured through an FQDN node, and has multiple associated monitors, and a monitor rule change is made to one of the associated monitors.
bugs.impact: The pool member status correctly reflects whether monitoring is successful (green) or the pool member is unknown (blue), but the changed monitor rule may not take effect until bigd is restarted.
bugs.workaround: When making changes to a monitor rule associated with a pool member configured through FQDN, verify the node remains monitored (green or checking), or restart bigd. Alternatively, change monitor rules within the configuration file, and reload the configuration.
bugs.fix: Pool members configured through FQDN nodes and with multiple associated monitors continue to be monitored after a monitor rule change to one of the associated monitors. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: Access profile 'Restrict to Single Client IP' setting not enforced with DTLS tunnel
bugs.symptoms: After APM end users establish a session from one client IP address, if they roam and get a different client IP address, the DTLS tunnel will still be able to establish, because the system does not enforce 'Restrict to Single Client IP'.
bugs.conditions: The client IP used to establish the session is different from the client IP used to establish DTLS tunnel and the 'Restrict to Single Client IP' setting is enabled.
bugs.impact: The DTLS tunnel will be established, which allows the client to access internal network resources from forbidden subnet.
bugs.workaround: Disable usage of DTLS tunnel.
bugs.fix: The 'Restrict to Single Client IP' setting is enforced correctly for DTLS tunnel.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin could crash on rewriting of some URLs in POST data
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite might crash on rewriting POST data with specific characters in the URL.
bugs.conditions: Rewrite of POST data with specific characters in the URL.
bugs.impact: Temporary outage of Portal Access services.

bugs.title: Edge client reevaluates access policy upon system wake up from sleep
bugs.symptoms: macOS edge client starts to re-evaluate access policy upon system wake up from sleep before access policy expires for any reason. Edge client should ideally reuse existing session but instead it requests for authentication again.
bugs.conditions: macOS edge client, macbook is put to sleep and is woken up before session expires.
bugs.impact: Usability. New request for authentication is shown.

bugs.title: Default 'enabled' value for 'request-based-authentication' of Kerberos Auth agent leads to various issues.
bugs.symptoms: The default value for 'request-based-authentication' property of Kerberos Auth agent is 'enabled'. This can lead to various issues, so most configurations require 'request-based-authentication' to be disabled.
bugs.conditions: Create a new Kerberos Auth agent in an Access Policy
bugs.impact: The 'request-based-authentication' property is 'enabled' by default, which can lead to various issues.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of these mitigations: -- Disable 'request-based-authentication' manually during creation of a Kerberos Auth agent. -- Modify the agent after it is created.
bugs.fix: The default value for 'request-based-authentication' property of Kerberos Auth agent is now 'disabled'. Previously, the default was 'enabled'.
bugs.behavior: The default value for 'request-based-authentication' property of Kerberos Auth agent is now 'disabled'. Previously, the default was 'enabled'. During upgrade, if you have any Kerberos Auth agents with RBA enabled, the value remains the same. However, when you create a new Kerberos Auth agent, 'request-based-authentication' is set to 'disabled' by default, and you must manually set it to 'enabled', if needed.

bugs.title: Hardware SYN Cookies may not deactivate after the SYN attack ends and valid TCP traffic starts
bugs.symptoms: Hardware SYN Cookies activated on a virtual server under a SYN attack may not deactivate after the SYN attack ends and valid TCP traffic starts. The non-supported TCP options under SYN Cookie protection will continue to be unsupported until the machine exit hardware SYN cookies.
bugs.conditions: A SYN flood attack or similar SYN attack where SYNs are flooded into the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: This can successfully cause hardware SYN cookies to be activated on the BIG-IP virtual server under attack. However, once the attack subsides and falls below the SYN check threshold, SYN cookies may not immediately deactivate. Because SYN cookie protection is still active, and because under SYN cookie protection some TCP options are not supported, the options will not be taken into account when processing traffic. For example, under SYN cookie protection, MSS is fixed to a few sizes. For traffic that arrives with a different MSS size, the system uses a supported size instead. Note that if no good traffic hits the virtual server, syncookies will also fail to deactivate, but will do so once both good traffic has been seen, and the attack has ended.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Hardware SYN Cookies now immediately deactivate after the SYN attack ends and valid TCP traffic starts.

bugs.title: sudo security update
bugs.symptoms: A flaw was found in the way sudo parsed tty information from the process status file in the proc filesystem.
bugs.conditions: A local user with privileges to execute commands via sudo could use this flaw to escalate their privileges to root.
bugs.impact: None. The sudo configuration on BIG-IP systems does not expose this vulnerability.

bugs.title: TMM can crash when it exits while still processing traffic

bugs.title: Autolasthop does not work for PPTP-GRE traffic.

bugs.title: SIGSEGV to tmm when performing multiple, repeated SSL profile updates, or during UCS restore

bugs.title: iRule commands may cause the TMM to crash in very rare situations.
bugs.symptoms: A TMM crash may occur in very rare situations.
bugs.conditions: A Tcl iRule command is used.
bugs.impact: A TMM Core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tcl iRule commands are more robust to extreme scenarios within the TMM.

bugs.title: System offline after deleting the datasync-global-dg device-group and manually re-creating it
bugs.symptoms: If the datasync-global-dg device-group is accidentally deleted and then manually re-created, other devices in the trust-domain might lose the datasync configuration, and go Offline until a workaround is applied or system is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: This might happen if the datasync-global-dg device-group is accidentally deleted and then manually re-created. Note: This device-group should never be deleted.
bugs.impact: The devices might go offline.
bugs.workaround: Perform this procedure from the device in the Offline state: 1. Run the following command: tmsh save sys config 2. Run the following command: tmsh load sys config 3. If system is Offline, wait approximately 3 minutes until the system is ACTIVE. Otherwise, wait a few seconds. 4. Run the following command again: tmsh save sys config 5. Perform a force sync of datasync-global-dg. To do so: a. From the GUI of the same device (the device that was previously Offline). b. Select 'Sync Device to Group'. c. Make sure 'Overwrite Configuration' is checked. d. Click 'Sync'. 6. Wait until the devices are ACTIVE and 'In Sync'.
bugs.fix: The system no longer allows deleting the datasync-global-dg device-group: a configuration exception is thrown in this case.

bugs.title: Websafe's 'Apply cookies to base domain' feature doesn't work for non standard ports
bugs.symptoms: 'Apply cookies to base domain' feature doesn't work for non standard ports.
bugs.conditions: 'Apply cookies to base domain' is enabled and connection is over non-standard ports (not 80, 443, etc.).
bugs.impact: Cookies won't be applied to base domain, thus WebSafe functionality will be broken and missing cookie alerts will be sent.
bugs.workaround: Use only standard ports.
bugs.fix: FPS now correctly parses base-domain, including port (if exists).

bugs.title: FPS: BLFN inheritance won't take effect until GUI refresh
bugs.symptoms: 1. Create fps profile with a "Additional function to be run before JavaScript load" (BLFN) configured. 2. Clone this profile. 3. In the cloned profile choose another profile to defaults from (where there is no BLFN). 4. Save configuration.
bugs.conditions: - Current profile has a BLFN configured. - New parent profile has no BLFN.
bugs.impact: The original BLFN is still configured on the profile (should have inherited the empty BLFN from parent profile).
bugs.workaround: 1. Use tmsh. 2. Refresh before save.
bugs.fix: Correct BLFN inheritance logic in GUI.

bugs.title: Alternative unicode encoding in JSON objects not being parsed correctly
bugs.symptoms: JSON content might be blocked when unicode encoding is used in one of the JSON nodes.
bugs.conditions: Configured ASM Policy with JSON profile.
bugs.impact: False positive blocked request.
bugs.workaround: Disable metachars checks in JSON profile.
bugs.fix: The JSON parser now handles unicode sequences correctly.

bugs.title: GUI: Allowed edit for NAT section in logging profile for users with Manager role
bugs.symptoms: NAT section cannot be edited by a user with Manager role.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP user account configured with the Manager role. -- Attempting to edit the NAT section in a logging profile.
bugs.impact: User with role Manager cannot edit related section in logging profile page
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to accomplish the task.
bugs.fix: Manager now has write access to NAT section only in logging profiles.

bugs.title: Suspended 'after' command leads to assertion if there are multiple pending events
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when an iRule has multi-parking commands including command after.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule has multi-parking commands. -- Command after is used multiple times in the iRule. Note: The exact condition of crashing tmm is not definitive, but when the above situation is met, it could trigger this crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Depending on the iRule, (e.g., script that uses command after very heavily, very often), the usages can be combined: after 100 after 200 { some script } can be combined to after 300 { the script }
bugs.fix: Suspended 'after' command no longer leads to assertion if there are multiple pending events

bugs.title: Config load fails when an iRule comment ends with backslash in a config where there is also a policy.
bugs.symptoms: Config load fails when an iRule contains a commented line that ends with an escape character (backslash), and the config also contains an LTM policy. Depending on the iRule, you might also see the following error: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 42078) double quotes are not balanced.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule contains commented line that ends with a backslash. -- The config also contains a policy. For example, an iRule similar to the first example, and a policy similar to the second: ltm rule /Common/log_info { when HTTP_RESPONSE { #log local0. "Original Location header value: [HTTP::header value Location],\ updated: [string map ":[TCP::remote_port]/ /" [HTTP::header value Location]]" } } ... ltm policy /Common/Test_Policy { controls { forwarding } requires { http tcp } rules { TestPol_Rule1 { actions { 0 { forward select node 10.2.10.20 } } conditions { 0 { tcp address matches values { 10.1.10.20 } } } } } strategy /Common/first-match }
bugs.impact: Config load fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use any of the following workarounds: -- Delete the line of code with the comment. -- Put the entire comment on one line of code. -- Divide lengthy comments into a series of smaller ones, so that each comment fits within one line of code. -- Move the iRule so that it is sequentially before the LTM policy in the config file.
bugs.fix: Config load no longer fails when an iRule comment ends with backslash in a config where there is also a policy.

bugs.title: TMM memory leak when manually enabling/disabling pool member used as HSL destination
bugs.symptoms: High Speed Logging fails to free an allocated cache memory resulting in memory leak. A small linear increase in mds_btree_nodes memory utilization may occur.
bugs.conditions: - Remote High Speed Logging configured. - Server-side connections dropped or closed. OR - High Speed Logging pool members removed.
bugs.impact: Increase in mds_btree_nodes memory utilization.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: High Speed Logging frees allocated memory correctly.

bugs.title: DNS Pool members do not show up in DNS statistics table
bugs.symptoms: In DNS statistics, the pool members list shows only type A members, even if there are non-A members.
bugs.conditions: DNS pools having non-A members
bugs.impact: Cannot see the stats for non-A members for pools in DNS Statistics. Misleading if pools have non-A members but do not show up.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to get stats information.
bugs.fix: Both new dashboard and legacy dashboard (Flash) have this issue. This fix addresses only the new dashboard, which will show all pool members no matter their types.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as SAML SP support for multiple signing certificates in SAML metadata from external identity providers.
bugs.symptoms: Certain SAML implementations support configuration of multiple signing certificates to be used for signing SAML messages. In these deployments different signing certificates could be used when certificate rotation takes place. Until now BIG-IP as SP only supported single signing certificate from external IdPs. When certificate rotation happens on external IdP, BIG-IP signing verification certificates have to be updated.
bugs.conditions: External IdP advertises multiple signing certificates in SAML metadata.
bugs.impact: When external IdP starts using new signing certificate previously advertised in metadata, authentication on BIG-IP as SAML SP will fail until administrator adjusts configuration to specify new signature validation certificate on appropriate SAML IdP connector object.
bugs.workaround: Signing certificates on BIG-IP as SAML SP can be reconfigured manually.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP as SP now supports multiple signing certificates advertised by external identity providers.

bugs.title: Policy automatic learning mode changes to manual after failover
bugs.symptoms: Policy automatic learning mode changes to manual when a failover occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Device group with ASM policy sync configured for multi-blade devices. -- ASM Policy is in automatic learning mode. -- A failover occurs.
bugs.impact: The policy changes from automatic learning mode to manual.
bugs.fix: Policy automatic learning mode no longer changes to manual when a failover occurs. Automatic learning mode will now be disabled only in active/active configurations.

bugs.title: Huge values are shown in the AVR statistics for ASM violations
bugs.symptoms: Huge values are shown in the AVR statistics for ASM violations.
bugs.conditions: Out-of memory-condition in the ASM. Some other extreme conditions might also cause this behavior.
bugs.impact: ASM violation numbers are incorrectly reported.
bugs.fix: An issue with bd sending wrong numbers to AVR was fixed.

bugs.title: Connection limit continues to be enforced with least-connections and pool member flap, member remains down
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances while using least-connections load balancing with a connection limit applied, if a pool member is at the connection limit and the node is stopped and restarted, the node will remain marked down.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following circumstances: - Least Connections (node or member). - Connection limit is set. - Then a pool member hits the connection limit. - The pool member is then marked down then up (e.g., manually).
bugs.impact: Pool member remains marked down.
bugs.workaround: This condition is very rare but if it occurs you can try removing the pool member or node and re-adding it.
bugs.fix: Connection limit is now correctly enforced with least-connections and pool member flap, so the member no longer incorrectly remains down.

bugs.title: Machine Certificate Checker service may not be used when UAC is disabled on windows machine
bugs.symptoms: Machine Certificate Checker service may not be used when UAC is disabled on windows machine causing Machine Cert Auth to either fail or go to 'Found' branch
bugs.conditions: Machine Certificate Checker is installed. Access Policy has Machine Cert Auth configured. Windows machine has UAC disabled.
bugs.impact: Machine Cert Auth agent either fails or goes to 'Found' branch
bugs.workaround: Enable UAC or Use elevation helper app (requires user to be an local admnistrator).
bugs.fix: Previously, on Windows, the Machine Certificate service was not used when UAC was disabled. Now, the Machine Certificate is used even when UAC is disabled.

bugs.title: TMM crash in PEM_DIAMETER component
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when the route to PCRF is lost.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM establishes connection with the diameter endpoint (Gx / Gy). -- The route to the diameter endpoint is lost (interface down / route deleted).
bugs.impact: TMM diameter module tries to communicate, does not handle the error, and crashes. Module reboot. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: Ensure that the network interface configuration routing diameter packet is not manually brought down. No workaround for externally triggered failures.
bugs.fix: The system now handles connections established with the diameter endpoint when the route to PCRF is lost.

bugs.title: Logout button not available in Configuration Utility when using Client Cert LDAP
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured to use the Client Cert LDAP for Remote Authorization, the Logout button is not available.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system is configured to use Client Cert LDAP for Remote Authorization.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system users cannot end the session on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Close all windows to end the session.
bugs.fix: Now, when the BIG-IP system is configured to use Client Cert LDAP as the Remote Auth method, there is a Logout button in the window, and when the Logout button is clicked, the system displays a modal window to instruct the user on how to end the session.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not display failed login attempts since last login in GUI
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP does not have a mechanism in the GUI to display information about login attempts.
bugs.impact: Administrators cannot use the GUI to evaluate login attempts to the BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Administrators can view the logs at /var/log/secure.
bugs.fix: New GUI pages were create to allow administrators, resource admins, and auditors to view information about login attempts to the BIG-IP. These pages are available at System >> Logins in the GUI. The user logins summary, available at System >> Logins : Summary can be set as the default start screen for BIG-IP users. However, this process is not as straightforward as other pages, as these pages are available only to users with a role of admin, resource admin, or auditor. Because of these restrictions, setting this page as default is accomplished by setting a DB variable, UI.Users.RedirectSuperUsersToAuthSummary, to true. When this DB variable is set to true, users with roles of admin, resource admin, or auditor will be redirected to the System >> Logins : Summary page. Users with other roles will be redirected to the Start Screen that is set in System >> Preferences.

bugs.title: High Speed Logging unbalance in log distribution for multiple pool destination.
bugs.symptoms: Remote High Speed Logging may send logs in an imbalance when configured to use multiple logging pools. The imbalance may occur if the logging destination remained idle for a while (no logs sent) after initial configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote High Speed Logging destination configured with multiple pools. -- The logging destination idle after initial configuration for more than 5 seconds.
bugs.impact: -- Log distribution imbalance.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Logs distributed equally on destination pools.

bugs.title: ClientHello sent in multiple packets results in TCP connection close
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system receives ClientHello messages in multiple fragments, and the first fragment length is smaller than 8 bytes, SSL might process it as a non-SSL packet.
bugs.conditions: -- The system receives ClientHello messages in multiple fragments. -- The first fragment length is smaller than 8 bytes.
bugs.impact: SSL might process the first fragment as a non-SSL packet, and discard it, and then tear down the TCP connection.
bugs.fix: Now, if the system receives the ClientHello message in multiple fragments, and the first fragment is smaller than 8 bytes, the system waits for the whole SSL packet to arrive before processing it.

bugs.title: Trap destination network option of 'default' is not valid
bugs.symptoms: The GUI and TMSH include an option for trap destination network that is not valid. The option 'default' can be entered in TMSH and selected in the GUI. In TMUI (the GUI), the system posts an error 'Required' when trying to save. In TMSH, the system posts the following error: 01070911:3: The requested enumerated (default) is invalid (, mgmt, other) for network. This is correct functionality.
bugs.conditions: Select 'default' from the dropdown menu in System :: SNMP :: Traps : Destination in the GUI. Or specify 'default' in the tmsh command: modify sys snmp traps modify.
bugs.impact: Selecting/specifying the 'default' option results in an error. The system rejects the selection in the GUI, so 'default' cannot be selected.
bugs.fix: The option 'default' was incorrectly included in TMUI, and has now been removed. Although you can still specify it in TMSH, the error message indicates that it is invalid, which is correct.

bugs.title: Asymmetric transparent nexthop traffic only updates ingress interface
bugs.symptoms: When transparent nexthop traffic from server to client uses a different VLAN group than client-to-server traffic, the server-to-client traffic is sent out the VLAN group that handles the client-to-server traffic. The destination MAC address on the server-to-client traffic is preserved even though the VLAN group is not.
bugs.conditions: -- Transparent nexthop virtual server configured. -- VLAN-keyed connections disabled. -- Asymmetric traffic between two VLAN groups.
bugs.impact: Return traffic may be transmitted on a VLAN group with a destination MAC that does not match any host on that group.
bugs.fix: When vlan-keyed connections is disabled and transparent nexthop is in use, each packet received will be sent the VLAN group which received it, even if this doesn't match the VLAN group passing traffic in the other direction. This is preferred behavior.

bugs.title: HTTP2 does not handle some URIs correctly
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances, the HTTP2 filter does not properly parse URIs
bugs.conditions: HTTP2 enabled
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: HTTP2 correctly parses URIs

bugs.title: Edge Client fails to reconnect to virtual server after disabling Network Adapter
bugs.symptoms: 1. Connect to an APM Virtual Server. 2. Disable Network Adapter. 3. Enable the Network Adapter. Edge Client fails to reconnect.
bugs.conditions: Network Adapter is disabled and re-enabled.
bugs.impact: Edge Client does not re-establish VPN when Network Adapter is re-enabled.
bugs.workaround: Disconnect and Connect Edge Client.
bugs.fix: Edge Client now successfully reconnects to virtual server after disabling and enabling Network Adapter.

bugs.title: csyncd does not handle an rsync stall
bugs.symptoms: An unknown event caused rsync to spin in a select(2) loop while the rsync socket was in TCP state CLOSE-WAIT with 1 byte remaining in the receive queue.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown, but might be related to VIPRION chassis, since that is the platform where this issue occurred.
bugs.impact: csyncd does not finish copying a file.

bugs.title: Bigd might stall while waiting for an external monitor process to exit
bugs.symptoms: The bigd process restarts due to a hearbeat failure. /var/log/ltm will contain a message similar to: warning sod[5444]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat bigd fails action is restart.
bugs.conditions: External monitors are in use. External monitors include user-defined external monitors as well as built-in external monitors (for example, SNMP, LDAP, etc.) High system load makes this more likely to occur.
bugs.impact: bigd will restart due to a heartbeat failure and monitoring will be interrupted.
bugs.workaround: Mitigations: -- If possible, reduce the system load on the BIG-IP system. -- If possible, use a built-in monitor type.
bugs.fix: bigd no longer stalls while waiting for an external monitor process to exit.

bugs.title: bigd might try to read from a file descriptor that is not ready for read
bugs.symptoms: The bigd process might consume excessive CPU resources or monitor probes might be erroneously marked as failed.
bugs.conditions: External monitors are in use. External monitors include user-defined external monitors as well as built-in external monitors (for example, SNMP, LDAP, etc.).
bugs.impact: The bigd process might consume excessive CPU resources for for various amounts of time. Single monitor probes might fail. Depending upon the timing of these failures, it might be possible to see monitor flapping when multiple probes for a specific monitored object happen to fail.
bugs.fix: An issue was resolved where the bigd process might consume excessive CPU resources or monitor probes might be erroneously marked as failed.

bugs.title: Cached stale Kerberos tickets can cause auth failures.
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, an attempt is made to update/renew an expired Kerberos ticket, and if that does not occur; it will result in stale/old Kerberos ticket causing APM end users to experience failures in authentication.
bugs.conditions: Kerberos tickets cannot be cleared and renewed.
bugs.impact: APM end users experience authentication failures and loss of connectivity.
bugs.workaround: Restart Kerberos Cache.
bugs.fix: A button is provided to be able to clear Kerberos cache from GUI. Similarly there is an option provided to clear cache using TMSH, using the following command: tmsh modify active-directory ad-auth-server cleanup-cache kerberos

bugs.title: macOS Edge client fails to detect correct system language for regions other than USA
bugs.symptoms: macOS Edge client fails to detect correct system language for regions other than USA.
bugs.conditions: -- macOS Sierra. -- Non-English language (e.g., Korean with different regions).
bugs.impact: Incorrect customization of Edge client for certain items, such as: logo, banner color, banner text color, and tray icon type.
bugs.workaround: Run one of the following command on the Terminal and re-launch Edge client: For English: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "en" "en-US" For German: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "de" "de-US" For Korean: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "ko" "ko-US" For Japanese: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "ja" "ja-US" For French: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "fr" "fr-US" For Spanish: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "es" "es-US" For Chinese traditional: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "zh-Hant" "zh-Hant-TW" "zh-Hant-US" For Chinese simplified: $ defaults write -globalDomain AppleLanguages -array "zh-Hans" "zh-Hans-US"
bugs.fix: Customization of the following items for Edge client now correctly reflect the region's language selection. -- Edge client logo. -- Banner color. -- Banner text color. -- Tray icon.

bugs.title: The Configuration Utility now disables the TLS 1.0 protocol by default
bugs.symptoms: The TLS 1.0 protocol was removed from the list of SSL protocols allowed by default in the management utility. This impacts the iControl REST API, and if you are using configuration management tools like Ansible (which uses Python) compiled with an older OpenSSL version, this will cause the client to suddenly fail to connect with an error similar to the following: SSLError: EOF occurred in violation of protocol. The protocol defaults can be seen with the following tmsh command: # tmsh list sys httpd ssl-protocol sys httpd { ssl-protocol "all -SSLv2 -SSLv3 -TLSv1" }
bugs.conditions: This can occur when connecting to the configuration utility, including using the iControl REST API, with an HTTPS client that is not compiled with TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 support.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP systems refuse to allow TLSv1 connections, so the client will be unable to connect. This will most likely be encountered as a sudden inability to connect after upgrading.
bugs.workaround: While TLS 1.0 can be re-enabled on BIG-IP systems via the 'tmsh modify sys httpd ssl-protocol' command, this is not advised because the protocol is past the end-of-life date. It is highly recommended to upgrade the OpenSSL version on all client devices that connect to the BIG-IP configuration utility.
bugs.fix: TLS 1.0 is no longer in the default SSL protocols list, and all SSL clients need to have support for TLS 1.1 or 1.2 or they will be unable to connect.
bugs.behavior: The configuration utility no longer allows the TLS 1.0 protocol by default. The following tmsh command shows the before and after settings: Prior to version 14.0.0: # tmsh list sys httpd ssl-protocol sys httpd { ssl-protocol "all -SSLv2 -SSLv3" } Beginning in version 14.0.0: # tmsh list sys httpd ssl-protocol sys httpd { ssl-protocol "all -SSLv2 -SSLv3 -TLSv1" } All clients connecting via SSL must have support for TLS 1.1 or 1.2 or they will be unable to connect.

bugs.title: Advisory color Yellow added to Configuration Utility
bugs.symptoms: Yellow is not available as a valid choice for advisory banners in the Configuration Utility.
bugs.conditions: When using the advisory banner in the Configuration Utility GUI, located at System :: Configuration.
bugs.impact: Cannot render the advisory message with a yellow color.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now supports Yellow as a valid option for the advisory banner.

bugs.title: GTM link graphs fail to display in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP administrator tries to view the GTM link graphs in the GUI, the system reports 'General database error retrieving information'. statsd reports an error in /var/log/ltm err statsd[6318]: 011b030d:3: Graph '/Common/Link_AS394043' not found
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP DNS/GTM is licensed and provisioned. -- BIG-IP DNS/GTM links are configured. -- Trying to view the GTM link graphs in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Unable to view BIG-IP DNS/GTM link graphs.
bugs.fix: The GTM graphs are available as expected.

bugs.title: dwbld service restarts randomly
bugs.symptoms: The service dwbld restarts without generating any core dump. This might happen randomly.
bugs.conditions: Certain dwbld socket operations can cause a signal to be issued.
bugs.impact: The signal is uncaught by the process. The signal itself is safe to ignore, but when left uncaught causes the process to restart. Service restart can disrupt ip-intelligence functionality, which the dwbld supports.

bugs.title: File named /root/.ssh/bigip.a.k.bak is present but should not be
bugs.symptoms: In AWS instances, a file /root/.ssh/bigip.a.k.bak is present which should not be. It is harmless to users other than that it is confusing.
bugs.conditions: After the first boot, this file should be deleted, but it is not.
bugs.impact: No real impact other than possibly confusion as this file isn't used in this environment. The file does not contain any sensitive data as it's a dangling symlink.
bugs.workaround: No need to workaround as the presence of the file is harmless. Users could manually remove this file if desired.
bugs.fix: This file is no longer present which is the correct state.

bugs.title: Upgrade failure for apm-log-setting objects
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade to 13.1.0, the configuration will fail to load with error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: In apm log-config (/p1/f1/sso-log-setting-Critical) there can only be one instance of access log configuration Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: If before upgrade, you have sso form-basedv2 object or saml sso config objects in your configuration
bugs.impact: mcpd will fail to start
bugs.workaround: manually edit the bigip.conf and remove all the sso form-basedv2 objects and saml sso config objects and then do tmsh load sys config
bugs.fix: After fix, upgrade will success

bugs.title: FQDN pool member status may become out-of-sync when enabled/disabled through GUI
bugs.symptoms: After toggling enable/disable on an FQDN pool member through the GUI, an FQDN pool member status may become 'out-of-sync', and the pool member might process connections opposite to its status. Specifically: 'disabled' might accept connections, and 'enabled' might not accept connections. In this state, the FQDN pool member appears to be exactly 'one-message-behind' for an enable/disable status change made in the GUI. The FQDN pool member status for enabled/disabled is always correctly displayed in the GUI and in tmsh, and behavior is correctly restored after a system reboot. Other pool members are unaffected.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP systems configured for high availability (HA). -- At least three members within an FQDN pool. -- Use the GUI to toggle enable/disable state on a FQDN pool member.
bugs.impact: The FQDN pool member does not correctly participate in receiving connections to the pool when in this error state. Other pool members remain unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Change FQDN pool to statically assign members.
bugs.fix: Toggling FQDN pool member between 'enable/disable' correctly changes that member's participation for accepting connections within its parent pool. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: 'bgp neighbor <peer -IP> update-source <IP>' command may apply change to all peers in peer-group
bugs.symptoms: When running the 'bgp neighbor <peer IP> update-source <IP>' command to a single peer, the changes may be applied to all peers in peer-group, if the peer IP belongs to a peer group.
bugs.conditions: - Using BGP with peer-groups. - Run 'bgp neighbor <peer IP> update-source <IP>', where <peer IP> is an IP of a peer in a peer-group.
bugs.impact: Changes may apply to all peers in the group.
bugs.workaround: Depending on the network setup, it may be possible to workaround the issue using the interface version of the command: bgp neighbor <peer IP> update-source <vlan name>.
bugs.fix: The command 'bgp neighbor <peer -IP> update-source <IP>' no longer applies the change to all peers in peer-group

bugs.title: Application Tunnel fails to start with the following message: Failed, Couldn't open proxy server.
bugs.symptoms: Application Tunnel fails to start, with the following message: Failed, Couldn't open proxy server. Also, logterminal.txt might contain multiple entries similar to the following: 2017-05-28,10:44:11:080, 2724,2500,HOST, 48, , 1801, CHostCtrl::OnTimer(), TUNNEL_SERVER_READY_CHECK - TunnelServer is ready 2017-05-28,10:44:11:095, 2724,2500,HOST, 48, , 1801, CHostCtrl::OnTimer(), TUNNEL_SERVER_READY_CHECK - TunnelServer is ready 2017-05-28,10:44:11:111, 2724,2500,HOST, 48, , 1801, CHostCtrl::OnTimer(), TUNNEL_SERVER_READY_CHECK - TunnelServer is ready
bugs.conditions: Conditions are undefined. If a thread running in F5 components gets blocked by something such as Anti-Virus, WM_TIMER events might cause the Microsoft Windows message queue to overfill, resulting in unexpected behavior. Note: This is an intermittent issue. Such instances of congestion happen when a thread, typically the main thread, is blocked by some long-standing (blocking) operation and does not happen in general use.
bugs.impact: Application Tunnel does not start.
bugs.fix: Application Tunnel client code has been improved to implement a queue overfill protection to prevent possible problems when starting the app tunnel.

bugs.title: Exclude the trusted anchor certificate in hash algorithm selection when Forward Proxy forges a certificate
bugs.symptoms: SSL Forward Proxy signs a forged certificate with a hash algorithm. This selected hash algorithm is the weakest algorithm from the certificates in the server certificate chain except the self-signed certificate. Some of the intermediate CA certificates in the cert chain use the SHA1 hash algorithm. This kind of intermediate CAs usually is are the BIG-IP system's ca-bundle. BIG-IP receives the cert chain including the intermediate CA and forges the cert with SHA1, which is rejected by some web clients.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is configured to use SSL Forward Proxy or SSL Intercept. -- Some intermediate CA in the web server's cert chain is using a weak algorithm like SHA1 to sign certificates. -- The web client rejects the weak-algorithm-signed certificate.
bugs.impact: Clients cannot access the web server due to SSL handshake failure.
bugs.fix: This fix excludes trusted CA certificates in hash algorithm selection. This may prevent forged certificate from using SHA1 hash algorithm.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Handling large replies to MCP audit_request messages
bugs.symptoms: When receiving very large replies to MCP messages (e.g., when viewing audit logs from the GUI), MCP can run out of memory and produce a core file. This is due in part to the amount of data returned, and also due in part to memory handling. In a production environment, fragmentation naturally occurs over the lifetime of MCP, thus increasing the odds of this happening. In addition, larger configurations cause more space to be consumed in MCPD and might more easily lead to the fragmentation, resulting in this issue.
bugs.conditions: Receiving very large replies to MCP messages (e.g., from audit_request messages, which occurs when you view audit logs from the GUI). Memory usage is already high.
bugs.impact: Allocation of memory for viewing the audit logs fails. MCP can run out of memory and produce a core file.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh/bash to view the audit logs instead of the GUI when audit logs are extremely large and memory usage is already high.
bugs.fix: Viewing audit logs in the GUI is now limited to 10,000 lines, so this issue no longer occurs.
bugs.behavior: The GUI is limited to viewing no more than 10,000 lines of the audit log. You can use tmsh/bash to view audit logs larger than 10,000 lines.

bugs.title: On demand cert authentication does not work with Linux CLI client
bugs.symptoms: If access policy is configured with on demand certificate authentication, Linux CLI client continually creates new sessions on APM until sessions are exhausted.
bugs.conditions: All conditions should be true 1) Linux CLI client is used 2) On demand certificate authentication is configured
bugs.impact: Client fails to establish connection. On APM, multiple sessions are created.
bugs.workaround: Use F5 helper apps client to launch VPN
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with on demand cert authentication not working with Linux CLI client

bugs.title: Creating new invalid SAML IdP configuration object may cause tmm restart in rare cases.
bugs.symptoms: Adding new SAML IdP configuration object containing empty attribute values via tmsh may cause tmm to restart.
bugs.conditions: New SSO SAML configuration contains one or more attribute values containing a session variable, following by another empty value "", for example: multi-values { "%{session.ad.last.attr.name}" "" } Note: This is not a valid configuration: empty values must not be provided in the list of SAML attributes.
bugs.impact: TMM may restart when new configuration is added. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove empty attribute values from configuration.
bugs.fix: SAML object validation has been improved so that empty SAML SSO object attribute values will no longer be accepted.

bugs.title: Cannot create stateless virtual servers with ip-protocol set to 'gre'.
bugs.symptoms: Stateless virtual servers can be used only for UDP traffic.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to create a stateless virtual server with ip-protocol set to 'gre'.
bugs.impact: Operation does not succeed. Cannot create stateless virtual servers with ip-protocol set to 'gre'.
bugs.fix: Can now create stateless virtual servers with ip-protocol set to 'gre'.
bugs.behavior: Previously, stateless virtual servers could only be used for UDP traffic. With this enhancement, you can configure stateless virtual servers with IP protocol set to 'gre'.

bugs.title: An enabled sFlow receiver can cause poor TMM performance on certain BIG-IP platforms
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP configuration includes at least one enabled sFlow receiver, certain platforms will experience poor TMM performance. Symptoms will include one or more of the following: - Higher than normal ping latency to the BIG-IP Self-IP addresses. - Higher than normal latency for applications flowing through BIG-IP virtual servers. - TMM clock advanced messages in the /var/log/ltm file. - Continuous activation and then quick deactivation of the idle enforcer for all TMM instances in the /var/log/kern.log file.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP configuration must include at least one enabled sFlow receiver (it doesn't matter whether this is reachable or not) and the platform type must be one of the following: - BIG-IP i10000 series - BIG-IP i7000 series - BIG-IP i5000 series - BIG-IP i4000 series - BIG-IP i2000 series - VIPRION B4450 blade
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system operates at a suboptimal performance level.
bugs.workaround: If the sFlow receiver is not strictly necessary for the correct functioning of your deployment, this can be disabled or removed to work around the issue.
bugs.fix: Performance is no longer degraded on certain platforms when the configuration includes enabled sFlow receivers.

bugs.title: [GUI][ZoneRunner] reverse zones should be treated case insensitive when creating resource record
bugs.symptoms: Creating a reverse zone in ZoneRunner ending not exactly as .arpa but with other case variations like .ARPA, resulting that zone is not treated as reverse zone. PTR is not available from the 'Type' dropbox menu when creating new resource record for that zone: DNS :: Zones : ZoneRunner : Resource Record List :: New Resource Record.
bugs.conditions: Creating a reverse zone in ZoneRunner ending not exactly as .arpa but with other case variations like .ARPA.
bugs.impact: Cannot create PTR resource record for the created reverse zones.
bugs.workaround: Create reverse zones exactly ending with .arpa.

bugs.title: Failover in the same availability zone of AWS may fail when AWS services are intermittently available.
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently available AWS services may lead to failure of curl requests to AWS or ec2 tools commands, resulting in failure of failover. As a result, public EIPs (for virtual servers) might remain pointing to the standby BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: AWS services are intermittently available.
bugs.impact: Failure of failover. Traffic will be routed to the standby BIG-IP system and lost.
bugs.workaround: Manually fail the systems over till failover succeeds at the desired BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Cannot run tmsh utils unix-* commands in Appliance mode when /shared/f5optics/images does not exist.
bugs.symptoms: From tmsh, running util unix-ls /var/log fails with the following error: exception: (Failed to canonicalize "/shared/f5optics/images") (util/RealpathHelper.cpp, line 49), continuing... Data Input Error: /var/log is not an accessible directory for the current mode.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system configured for Appliance mode. -- Upgrading from a pre-v12.x to v12.x or later. -- Using a platform that does not have a /shared/f5optics/images directory. These include the following BIG-IP blades and appliances: B4400, i4x00, i10x00, i2x00, i7x00, i5x00
bugs.impact: There is no shell access to the file system when the BIG-IP system is in Appliance mode. This is the intended purpose of Appliance mode. Therefore, unix-* commands are the only way to list directories, and perform other operations specific to the operating system.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, create the /shared/f5optics/images directory. To do so, do the following: 1. Boot the BIG-IP system into single-user mode. 2. Create the directory /shared/f5optics/images with the following command: mkdir -m 777 -p /shared/f5optics/images. 3. Reboot the BIG-IP system, and allow it to start up normally.
bugs.fix: The reported exception does not occur, and unix-* commands commands issued in Appliance mode run as expected.

bugs.title: The HTTP_DISABLE iRule event may cause a TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP_DISABLE iRule event is invoked when the HTTP filter is enabled or disabled. If this occurs before the first HTTP request is released, then the TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: -- The HTTP_DISABLE iRule event is used. -- HTTP is disabled before the first request reaches the HTTP filter. (This might occur if TCP::collect is used, or if HTTP::disable is invoked in CLIENT_ACCEPTED.)
bugs.impact: A TMM core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The HTTP_DISABLE event now works in the described case without causing a TMM crash.

bugs.title: Category Lookup by Subject.CN will result in a reset
bugs.symptoms: Category Lookup Agent is unable to find the Subject.CN, so it initiates an SSL Handshake failure. ==> /var/log/apm <== crit tmm[11181]: 01790602:2: [C] 10.20.100.1:11980 -> 10.11.10.101:443: (ERR_NOT_FOUND) Error processing URL Classification query from CatEngine
bugs.conditions: Category Lookup agent configured to use Subject.CN. May also apply if a Category Lookup agent is configured to use SNI, but the client does not send an SNI, resulting in the agent trying to use the Subject.CN.
bugs.impact: Cannot use Subject.CN as a data source for category lookup agent.
bugs.fix: The category lookup agent is now able to find the Subject.CN.

bugs.title: WebSafe might cause connections to hang
bugs.symptoms: In a loaded environment, FPS might free a connection context without cleaning up the state.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in a loaded environment (xoff events present).
bugs.impact: A connection might stall until abandoned by client.
bugs.fix: when freeing a connection context, FPS will clear internal egress state.

bugs.title: TMM core when server responds fast with server responses such as 404.
bugs.symptoms: TMM core when server responds fast with server responses such as 404.
bugs.conditions: -- FPS gets a request with a WebSafe URL (usually global URL - declared by signatures update). -- Server response is fast (based on URL/headers). -- FPS need to take some action on response.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: FPS now handles these conditions without a tmm crash.

bugs.title: CS redirects to incorrect URL
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP ASM system may redirect a client request to an incorrect URL after the client browser passes the client-side integrity defense JavaScript challenge.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have enabled the Client Side Integrity Defense feature in a DoS profile associated with a virtual server. -- A client request containing a certain structured URL is processed by the virtual server with the DoS profile. -- The client browser passes the client-side integrity defense JavaScript challenge issued by the BIG-IP ASM system.
bugs.impact: The client browser is redirected to an incorrect URL. If a malicious attacker triggers the DoS profile and then sends a maliciously crafted structured URL to unsuspecting users as part of a phishing attack, the users may be redirected to a malicious website.
bugs.fix: Client side code no longer redirects to an incorrect URL under these conditions.

bugs.title: Flow eviction for hardware-accelerated flow might fail
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, evicting a hardware-accelerated ePVA flow might fail. Under normal conditions, this flow eventually idles out of the ePVA, but if traffic happens to be generated over the flow, then it can stay in the ePVA indefinitely, even if there is no software connection context for this connection.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server using a FastL4 profile.
bugs.impact: A connection becomes stuck in the ePVA. Traffic might be disrupted if tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware acceleration.
bugs.fix: This release has updated the process for evicting a connection from the ePVA.

bugs.title: Use of more than 10 interfaces within AWS instances
bugs.symptoms: Within AWS, instances of type i3.16xlarge and r4.16xlarge allow for up to 15 network interfaces. Use of more than 10 interfaces on BIG-IP instances will result in the extra interfaces not functioning. Interfaces 1.10-1.14 will have the same MAC address as 1.1 and not function.
bugs.conditions: Use of i3.16xlarge or r4.16xlarge instances for BIG-IP with more than 10 network interfaces.
bugs.impact: The extra interfaces will not function.
bugs.workaround: Use multiple instances with fewer interfaces. Potentially use tunnels to separate traffic.

bugs.title: Efect of bad connection handle between APMD and memcachd
bugs.symptoms: When a connection handle (fd) between apmd and memcachd gets bad (someone else is using or already closed by memcachd), all worker threads gets locked out. A cleaner thread then restart APMD with an assert.
bugs.conditions: This is difficult to reproduce. It happens if one or more connection handle between apmd worker thread and memcachd gets misused.
bugs.impact: APMD gets locked down , eventually restart with a core.
bugs.fix: Communication between APMD and TMM has been improved to be more tolerant of error conditions.

bugs.title: Error adding /Common/WideIPs as members to GTM Pool in non-Common partition
bugs.symptoms: Unable to use Pool Members from /Common/ when outside of /Common/
bugs.conditions: Adding /Common/WideIPs as members in non-Common GTM Pool
bugs.impact: Unable to use pool-members from /Common/ when outside of /Common/
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue preventing users from using GTM pool-members within /Common/ on GTM Pools outside of /Common/

bugs.title: When network changes after VPN is established, network access tunnel is closed when network access configuration has 'Allow local DNS servers' and 'Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection' options enabled.
bugs.symptoms: - When network changes after VPN is established, network access tunnel is closed when network access configuration has 'Allow local DNS servers' and 'Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection' options enabled.
bugs.conditions: - Allow local DNS servers' option is enabled in Network Access configuration. - Prohibit routing table changes during Network Access connection option is enabled in Network Access configuration. - Network changes after VPN is established.
bugs.impact: - Network access tunnel is dropped due to routing table changes.
bugs.workaround: User needs to connect to VPN again.

bugs.title: The tmsh sys log filter is unable to display information in uncompressed log files.
bugs.symptoms: You notice missing log information when reviewing system logs using the tmsh show sys log command.
bugs.conditions: One or more of the BIG-IP sytem backup log files, designated with .1, .2, etc are not compressed. Note: Backup log files should end with the .gz extension. For example, ltm.1.gz. You use the tmsh show sys log command to view log information for one or more days in the past.
bugs.impact: Unable to view the full range of backup log information.
bugs.workaround: To log in to the Advanced shell (bash). To ensure all backup logs for a particular log type are compressed, use the following command syntax: gzip /var/log/<log>.* For example, to compress the full set of backup logs for the ltm log type, type the following command: Note: The following message is expected if the log file is already compressed: gzip: /var/log/<log>.gz already has .gz suffix -- unchanged' gzip /var/log/ltm.*
bugs.fix: Increased flexibility of log reading mechanism, to look for both compressed (ending in .gz) and uncompressed (ending in .#) log files.

bugs.title: tmm crashes after LSN pool member change
bugs.symptoms: Changing LSN pool members while processing traffic may cause tmm to crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Changing, using, or removing an LSN pool. -- Traffic is being processed.
bugs.impact: When tmm crashes, traffic processing will stop until tmm restarts. Note that this can occur, even if the change was on a high-availability peer unit and config-sync has taken place.
bugs.workaround: Recommend to change LSN pool members during a maintainence window with low traffic or ideally to use an HA pair with a standby unit for implementing configuration changes on live traffic.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes when changing LSN pool members while processing traffic.

bugs.title: Potential core when using MRF SIP with SCTP
bugs.symptoms: The system may core when using SCTP with MRF SIP if the outgoing connection receives more messages than it can process.
bugs.conditions: -- SCTP with MRF SIP configured. -- Outgoing connection receives more messages than it can process.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: With SCTP with MRF SIP, the system better handles conditions when the outgoing connection receives more messages than it can process, so the system does not core and restart.

bugs.title: Higher CPU usage for syslog-ng when a syslog server is down
bugs.symptoms: Higher CPU usage for syslog-ng when a syslog server is down.
bugs.conditions: A remote log server is added but it is not available.
bugs.impact: Potentially higher than expected CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate this issue, use either of the following: -- Ensure that the remote log server is available. -- Remove the remote log server from the configuration.

bugs.title: JSON encryption cannot be configured for URI's with custom ports
bugs.symptoms: JSON encryption does not encrypt Asynchronous JavaScript and XML (AJAX) request data that is being sent to a URI with a port number in it.
bugs.conditions: An API end-point that includes a port number.
bugs.impact: Request data not encrypted.
bugs.fix: WebSafe URL normalization now properly accounts for port numbers.

bugs.title: No distinction between IPv4 addresses and IPv6 subnet ::ffff:0:0/96
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP does not differentiate between IPv4 addresses (such as 1.2.3.4) and IPv6 addresses in the prefix ::ffff:0:0/96 (such as ::ffff:102:304, also written ::ffff:1.2.3.4). If you enter such an IPv6 address, the equivalent IPv4 address will be rendered and used.
bugs.conditions: Any attempt to use an IPv6 address in that subnet.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system will operate as if you entered the IPv4 address.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The differing addresses now are handled correctly. For most modules, this does not change the functionality at all. AFM is one exception; IPv6 traffic in the ::ffff:0:0/96 subnet will be treated differently than IPv4 traffic.

bugs.title: Upgrade failure at Client SSL profile "cannot contain more than one set of same certificate/key type."
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading the system, the clientssl profile /Common/crypto-server-default-clientssl might have contained a wrong structure, where it has two of RSA cert-key-chain and without cert and key outside of cert-key-chain block, and hence fails the validation during the upgrade. For example, below is the case of the wrong structure. ltm profile client-ssl /Common/crypto-server-default-clientssl { app-service none cache-size 0 cert-key-chain { default { <========== the 1st RSA cert-key-chain cert /Common/default.crt key /Common/default.key } default_SHA2 { <========== the 2nd RSA cert-key-chain cert /Common/default_SHA2.crt key /Common/default_SHA2.key } } ciphers DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 defaults-from /Common/clientssl inherit-certkeychain false renegotiate-period 21600 }
bugs.conditions: 1. The system is being upgraded from a version that is greater than or equal to 11.6.0, where the clientSSL profile /Common/crypto-server-default-clientssl was introduced. 2. The user has customized configuration on the clientSSL profile /Common/crypto-server-default-clientssl, i.e., /Common/crypto-server-default-clientssl appears in the /config/bigip.conf file.
bugs.impact: Upgrade failure at Client SSL profile "cannot contain more than one set of same certificate/key type."
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to remove the additional default certkeychain and manually add "cert xxxxxxxx" and "key xxxxxxxxx". In particular, modify /config/bigip.conf and change the profile to ltm profile client-ssl /Common/crypto-server-default-clientssl { app-service none cache-size 0 cert /Common/default_SHA2.crt <======== add this cert-key-chain { default_SHA2 { <=========== leave only one RSA certkeychin here cert /Common/default_SHA2.crt key /Common/default_SHA2.key } } ciphers DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 defaults-from /Common/clientssl inherit-certkeychain false key /Common/default_SHA2.key <========= add this renegotiate-period 21600 } and then do "tmsh load sys conf" again.

bugs.title: Session commands may not work correctly in FLOW_INIT event.
bugs.symptoms: Data read or write via session-related commands (e.g., table) in an iRule's FLOW_INIT event does not match that in other events.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using session-related commands from FLOW_INIT event.
bugs.impact: iRule does not function as expected.

bugs.title: Encoding binary data using ASN1::encode may truncate result
bugs.symptoms: When using ASN1::encode to encode one or more values, and where the encoding of any of these values results in a representation containing a NUL ('\x0') byte, the overall result that is presented to the iRule does not include the entire set of encoded values and is truncated at the first NUL byte.
bugs.conditions: -- Using ASN1::encode with binary values (e.g., INTEGER). -- Encoded results contain a NUL ('\x0') byte.
bugs.impact: Encoding results in the wrong/truncated value.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to encode the problematic values using an alternative method.
bugs.fix: ASN1::encode now correctly encodes binary values.

bugs.title: SIP monitor - Via header's branch parameter collision.
bugs.symptoms: When there is a failover in a high availability (HA) setup with SIP monitors, the SIP backend servers start flapping on both units. The reason this occurs is that after the failover, the two BIG-IP systems send SIP monitoring messages to the pool members with the same branch parameter on their Via headers. The backend server internal logic gets confused by the request coming from LB2 because it uses the same branch parameters of the request coming from LB1.
bugs.conditions: SIP branch hash string length is small enough that when sufficient SIP monitor messages were inundated, possible branch collision.
bugs.impact: This causes the backend server erroneously to send a response message to LB1 instead of LB2.
bugs.fix: Branch collisions no longer occur in this configuration.

bugs.title: SSL forward proxy does not create the server certchain when ignoring server certificates
bugs.symptoms: Forward proxy not working correctly when the server certificates are ignored. SSL forward proxy does not create the server certchain when ignoring server certificates, this prevents the client side from trusting the server cert and the SSL handshake hangs and fails after timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL forward proxy or SSL intercept is configured. -- Ignore server certificate configured in the server SSL profile.
bugs.impact: Client cannot establish SSL connection with server due to SSL handshake always timing out.
bugs.fix: The system now generates the server certchain (even when the server SSL profile ignores server certificates) and passes it to the client SSL, so that the client SSL can forge the cert and finish the SSL handshake.

bugs.title: High Speed Logging can crash TMM on TCP pool member down.
bugs.symptoms: In rare situations TMM can crash when pool member used in High Speed Logging is marked down by a monitor and pending TCP connection handshake completed shortly after.
bugs.conditions: -- High Speed Logging pool using TCP protocol. -- Pool marked down by monitor while pending TCP connection. -- TCP handshake completes after pool is marked down.
bugs.impact: Service disruption while tmm recovers. HA failover event. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Failure to retrieve large number of Bot Defense log records
bugs.symptoms: Due to resource limitations, when the device stores almost one million records of Bot Defense logs, attempting to review them in the GUI or in REST API fails.
bugs.conditions: -- One million records of Bot Defense log records on the device. -- Attempting to review them in the GUI or in REST API.
bugs.impact: Failure to view Bot Defense logs.
bugs.workaround: Send Bot logs to an external logger.

bugs.title: Rare tmm crash when changing the configuration of a FastL4 virtual server while passing traffic.
bugs.symptoms: Rare tmm crash when changing the configuration of a FastL4 virtual server while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 virtual server. -- Configuration change while passing traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a rarely occurring issue.

bugs.title: APMD debug messages about the file descriptor queue are not correct.
bugs.symptoms: When the file descriptor queue is logged, only the first entry is correct. The remainder are copies of the first entry.
bugs.conditions: You must run "kill -USR2 <pid of APMD>" on the command line on the BIG-IP to log the file descriptor queue.
bugs.impact: No functional or performance impact.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time

bugs.title: TMM may crash when a DHCP virtual server is used with an iRule involving SERVER_DATA event and TCL 'after' command.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured with a DHCP virtual server with an iRule, the TMM may crash when a DHCP server sends back multiple identical offers for a single request to the BIG-IP system within a certain period of time.
bugs.conditions: When the following conditions are met: - The BIG-IP system is configured with a virtual server with a DHCP profile and an iRule involving SERVER_DATA event and Tcl 'after' command. - A DHCP server sends back multiple identical offers for a single request to the BIG-IP system within a certain period of time.
bugs.impact: The TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes.

bugs.title: No way to query logins to BIG-IP in TMUI
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use the GUI to query logins to the BIG-IP system based on a time range or a specific user.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the GUI. -- Gather login information.
bugs.impact: No support for queries.
bugs.fix: Added support for using using the GUI to query logins to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.behavior: The ability to query logins on the BIG-IP, using the GUI, was added at System >> Logins : History. Users can query all available login data that is present on the BIG-IP. This information can be filtered by time, username, status, access method, and host.

bugs.title: IPsec: ASSERT 'BIG-IP_conn tag' failed
bugs.symptoms: When using IPsec, tmm assert with 'BIG-IP_conn tag' failed.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this assert occurs when using IPsec are unknown.
bugs.impact: The tmm restarts and all connections are reset. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: When using IPsec, tmm no longer asserts with 'BIG-IP_conn tag' failed.

bugs.title: TMM may crash due to wrong flow assigned to fragmented IPv4 packet
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash due to wrong flow assigned to fragmented IPv4 packet.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when either of the following conditions occur: -- The connection is re-accepted. -- The FLOW_INIT iRule event is used.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes, and the correct flow is assigned.

bugs.title: IP forwarding virtual server drops packets with TTL of 1 in TTL preserve mode
bugs.symptoms: FastL4/IP forwarding virtual server configured to preserve TTL on forwarding, drops ingress packets with a TTL of 1.
bugs.conditions: - FastL4 IP forwarding virtual server with a ip-ttl-mode configured to 'preserve'. - Packets with TTL of 1.
bugs.impact: Packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Change TTL mode on the FastL4 profile.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer drops packers with TTL of 1 when configured with TTL mode of 'preserve'.

bugs.title: Multicast pings not forwarded by TMM
bugs.symptoms: When multicast routing is configured, ICMP or ICMP6 pings are not forwarded by TMM even though UDP and other protocol traffic to the same group addresses works.
bugs.conditions: Multicast routing configured, VIP configured to forward ICMP traffic.
bugs.impact: Multicast group addresses cannot be reached with ICMP or ICMP6 echo requests.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer drops ping requests to multicast group addresses that should be forwarded.

bugs.title: Security Banner Text omits some non-English characters
bugs.symptoms: Some non-English characters in the Security Banner Text may be omitted when displaying them.
bugs.conditions: Entering some non-English characters in the Security Banner Text.
bugs.impact: Some of the non-English characters may be omitted when displaying the Security Banner Text.
bugs.workaround: Use only English characters in the Security Banner Text.
bugs.fix: The Security Banner Text no longer skips some non-English characters.

bugs.title: On large APM configurations (1000 Policies and a large number of Customization groups) mcpd gets killed before it can complete validation.
bugs.symptoms: On large APM configurations (1000 Policies and a large number of Customization groups) mcpd gets killed before it can complete validation. The limit of customization group object we can load(on bigip VE) is around 13K.
bugs.conditions: Large number of policies (thousands) and customization objects (tens of thousands).
bugs.impact: Unable to load configuration.
bugs.workaround: Turn off watchdog for mcpd via tmsh using the following command: tmsh modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat disabled Important! Remember to re-enable tmsh watchdog after the config loads successfully. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat enabled
bugs.fix: Large APM configurations no longer cause mcpd restart, so configurations load as expected.

bugs.title: SSH Proxy public key authentication can be circumvented in some cases
bugs.symptoms: SSH Proxy public key authentication might be circumvented in some cases, allowing a user without the appropriate private key in to the back-end end SSH server.
bugs.conditions: Public key authentication is being used to authenticate users. Note: This issue affects only public key authentication, so if additional forms of authentication are being used, the additional security that they provide will not be impacted.
bugs.impact: Unauthorized access.
bugs.workaround: A suggested workaround is to configure the back-end SSH server to require 2-factor authentication, or 3-factor authentication. This can be done by adding both publickey+password and publickey+keyboard-interactive as Required Authentications in the configuration file for the back-end SSH server. See the list below of supported client method orders. Also, keep in mind that the back-end server must support all 3 authentication methods (public-key, password, and keyboard-interactive), as an existing constraint of the current SSH proxy functionality. One cosmetic item to note is that, when multi-factor authentication is used, regardless of the result of the validity check of the public-key, the SSH proxy will report a 'failed' authentication to the client. However, the returned 'failed' code is merely cosmetic: the actual result of the validity check is what is used to determine whether or not the authentication succeeded. ------- Supported client method orders: publickey,keyboard-interactive publickey,password publickey,keyboard-interactive,password publickey,password,keyboard-interactive Any other combination of authentication methods will fail.
bugs.fix: Implemented stricter error handling in authentication checking.

bugs.title: Missing descriptions for SNMP OID ltmNodeAddrMonitorState and ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus values
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP OIDS ltmNodeAddrMonitorState and ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus may return integer values in the range of 25-29, for which descriptions are not provided in the MIB (/usr/share/snmp/mibs/F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB.txt).
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when doing an snmpwalk of these OIDs.
bugs.impact: Meanings of integer values in the range of 25-29 are unclear for SNMP OIDS ltmNodeAddrMonitorState and ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus.
bugs.workaround: For FQDN Ephemeral nodes, snmpwalk should return integer status with descriptions, such as the following: F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnChecking(26) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnDown(27) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnUp(28) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorStatus."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnUpNoAddress(29) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorState."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnChecking(26) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorState."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnDown(27) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorState."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnUp(28) F5-BIG-IP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrMonitorState."/Common/www.foo.com" = INTEGER: fqdnUpNoAddress(29)
