bugs.title: One extra mcpd AUDIT message logged after disabling mcpd audit logging
bugs.symptoms: By design, when mcpd audit logging is disabled, messages are logged to /var/log/audit, recording the fact that mcpd audit logging was disabled. After mcpd audit logging has been disabled via tmsh and the initial messages of this change are logged, the next command that modifies a configuration object will also be logged to the audit log. Afterwards, mcpd audit logging will be correctly disabled, so that no subsequent configuration changes will be logged by mcpd in the audit log.
bugs.conditions: Switching audit logging from enabled to disabled.
bugs.impact: Unexpected logging of potentially-sensitive information (such as a password in a user account object) in the audit log (/var/log/audit) may occur even though such logging has been disabled.
bugs.workaround: To avoid recording potentially-sensitive information in the audit log after disabling mcpd audit logging, before issuing any command that affects configuration objects containing sensitive information, issue one additional command to change a configuration object that does not contain sensitive information.
bugs.fix: Once mcpd audit logging is disabled, messages are no longer logged to /var/log/audit.

bugs.title: Debug image TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: If a debug TMM is being run and with PEM logging enabled. Under some subscriber addition cases, TMM crashes
bugs.conditions: -- TMM debug is used. -- PEM debug log is enabled. -- Many subscribers are added. -- The log message crashes subscribers.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts resulting in failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable PEM loggins in PEM debug image.

bugs.title: On i-Series platforms, HTTP/2 is limited to 10 streams
bugs.symptoms: On i-Series platforms, HTTP/2 is limited to 10 streams by licensing. "HTTP2 limited to 10 concurrent streams: Web Accelerator feature not licensed." appears in /var/log/ltm
bugs.conditions: Using an i-Series platform where WAM is unlicensable.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 performance may be less than desired
bugs.fix: It is possible to configure HTTP/2 with more than 10 streams on i-Series platforms.

bugs.title: SSL handshake failure with Session Ticket enabled on the backend server
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake failure occurs as a certificate is not issued (no certificate).
bugs.conditions: - Server SSL profile is enabled with the Session Ticket feature - Backend server also supports Session Ticket
bugs.impact: - Service is disrupted because of a handshake failure. - SSL handshake fails with no certificate issue.
bugs.workaround: Disable the Session Ticket feature on the Server SSL Profile or the backend server.

bugs.title: Reduced Issues for Monitors configured with FQDN
bugs.symptoms: Monitors configured using FQDN might experience several edge cases in some deployment environments. For example, you might experience issues with FQDN-configured monitors when used in environments with volatile/unstable DNS servers, or when network configuration causes ICMP packets from an unreachable DNS server to be non-routable back to 'bigd'. In such cases, the monitor may experiences delay in rotating to the next available DNS server. This is due to complex edge cases that exist within the initial FQDN monitor implementation, where anomalous behavior is aggravated through some network configurations.
bugs.conditions: Monitors are configured using FQDN, and one-or-more environment conditions exist such as: Unstable DNS servers (i.e., 'flapping' DNS), or the network configuration causes ICMP packets from an unreachable DNS server to be non-routable back to 'bigd'.
bugs.impact: The monitor will not be updated with information from the (new) DNS server when the previous DNS server becomes unavailable. Other monitor behavior will continue to function normally.
bugs.workaround: In some cases network configuration can be changed to avoid these edge cases, such as: Ensuring stable DNS servers with only periodic rollovers to backup DNS servers; ensure network ICMP packets are routable back to 'bigd'. Alternatively, monitors may be configured without using FQDN.
bugs.fix: Monitors configured using FQDN behave as expected in volatile environments, such as those with flapping DNS servers and where ICMP packets for unreachable DNS servers are non-routable back to 'bigd'.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing FastL4 traffic
bugs.symptoms: When processing certain types of traffic with a FastL4 profile, TMM may crash
bugs.conditions: FastL4 profile in use
bugs.impact: TMM crash, resulting in a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM not longer crashes when processing certain types of FastL4 traffic

bugs.title: Enhancing the error message for metadata import/export failure for SAML SP and IdP objects.
bugs.symptoms: When problems occur during the import or export of SAML metadata for SP or IdP, a message is logged, but the information is insufficient to help determine why the import/export failed. The system logs and error message similar to the following: MCP Error01070712:3: apm aaa saml-sp-connector <sp-connector> unable to parse metadata file /var/tmp/1498598319464.upload.
bugs.conditions: Metadata import/export failure for SAML SP and IdP.
bugs.impact: Generic message is logged. The message contains insufficient information for troubleshooting.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: This release enhances the error message logged during import/export failure of SAML SP or IdP metadata to provide additional info to help with troubleshooting. Examples: MCP Error01070712:3: apm aaa saml-sp-connector sp1 unable to parse metadata file /var/tmp/1506737815551.upload: invalid document structure . MCP Error01070712:3: apm aaa saml-sp-connector sp2 unable to parse metadata file /var/tmp/1506737894866.upload: unable to create converter for 'ABC' encoding. In addition, the SAX(XML parser) exception that is thrown is now modified to log the line number and column number of the location in the metadata file where exception occurred. Example: /var/tmp/mcpd.out - SAX Exception: line 1, char 40 message: invalid document structure.

bugs.title: Loading UCS with QinQ VLANs fails 'Can't free vlan entry, can't find vlan with oid'
bugs.symptoms: Unable to load a UCS due to a VLAN validation error.
bugs.conditions: QinQ VLANs saved in a UCS file.
bugs.impact: Unable to reload the saved config.
bugs.workaround: Before loading the config, use tmsh to delete all VLANs. Then config will load successfully.

bugs.title: New feature: revoke license
bugs.symptoms: A different license is required for each Virtual Edition (VE) instance.
bugs.conditions: Creating new instances of VE.
bugs.impact: Cannot reuse an existing VE license.
bugs.fix: For Virtual Edition (VE) BIG-IP systems, licenses can now reused by other VE instances by revoking an active license on one and installing it on another.
bugs.behavior: Revoke license is a new feature so that licenses can be reused for other virtual edition configurations. To revoke a license using tmsh, run the following command: tmsh revoke sys license registration-key <reg-key-number> The system responds with the following confirmation prompt: Revoking the license will return this BIG-IP to an unlicensed state. It will stop processing traffic. Are you sure? Y/N: When you type y, the system revokes the license and returns a response similar to the following: License successfully revoked [root@bigip11:LICENSE INOPERATIVE:Standalone] config # Jul 17 12:04:28 bigip11 emerg mcpd[5144]: 01070608:0: License is not operational (expired or digital signature does not match contents).

bugs.title: Virtual server configuration incorrectly allows mutually exclusive iSession and OneConnect profiles.
bugs.symptoms: The system does not prevent you from configuring a server-side iSession profile and a OneConnect profile on the same virtual server. This is not a valid configuration. Virtual server configuration should allow either a server-side iSession profile or a OneConnect profile, but not both. Although the virtual server configuration completes, three errors are logged to /var/log/tmm: 1) notice ISESSION: 172.27.114.10.443 ! 172.27.14.10.43321: connection error: isession_setup_ssl:1645: server-side SSL hudfilter replacement failed: ERR_NOT_FOUND 2) notice hudchain contains precluded serverside filter: CONNPOOL 3) notice MCP message handling failed in 0x898c80 (16977920): Jul 7 12:34:19 - MCP Message: notice create { notice virtual_server_profile { notice virtual_server_profile_vs_name "/Common/http_optimize_client" notice virtual_server_profile_profile_name "/Common/oneconnect" notice virtual_server_profile_object_id 159423 notice virtual_server_profile_profile_class_id profile_connpool notice virtual_server_profile_profile_type 13 notice virtual_server_profile_profile_context 0 notice virtual_server_profile_partition_id "Common" notice virtual_server_profile_leaf_name "http_optimize_client" notice virtual_server_profile_folder_name "/Common" notice virtual_server_profile_transaction_id 62 notice } notice } Loading a configuration containing a virtual server with both a server-side iSession profile and a OneConnect profile succeeds, but logs a mutually exclusive profile error: notice hudchain contains precluded serverside filter: CONNPOOL
bugs.conditions: Three conditions must be satisfied. 1) The BIG-IP has AAM licensed. 2) A server-side iSession profile is added to a virtual server. 3) A OneConnect profile is added to the same virtual server. Conditions 2 and 3 can be done in either order.
bugs.impact: OneConnect and iSession are mutually exclusive features, because both implement connection pooling. Configuring a virtual server with both server-side iSession and OneConnect profiles will break connection pooling, causing connections associated the virtual server to hang.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuring both server-side iSession and a OneConnect profiles on the same virtual server, as this is never a valid configuration.
bugs.fix: An error is now returned for attempts to configure both a server-side iSession profile and a OneConnect profile on the same virtual server. The error message text is: Configuration error: A virtual server (<vs name>) is not allowed to have both OneConnect and iSession profiles.

bugs.title: GUI Dashboard export history may have inconsistent time intervals
bugs.symptoms: When choosing to export a week-long report from the GUI Dashboard, the generated CSV history file may at times show statistics with a 26-minute interval between each row, and at other times show statistics with a 30-minute interval between rows.
bugs.conditions: This behavior depends on the time of day the report is generated.
bugs.impact: This is only a cosmetic issue. The statistics are still averaged out correctly over the interval returned in the CSV file.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Platform AC power supply faults when subjected to temperature above 50C (122F) at low input voltage.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP i15600, i15800 appliances utilizing a single 1500W AC power supply (PWR-0341-XX) shut down and trigger a fault.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- PWR-0341-XX Single Supply. -- input voltage is less than or equal to 100VAC. -- System is is drawing maximum power (greater than 1000W). -- Inlet temperature of the power supply is greater than 50C (122F).
bugs.impact: The power supply shuts down to protect itself. This results in appliance shutdown.
bugs.workaround: You can avoid this issue by doing any of the following: -- Installing two PSUs in the unit. -- Ensuring that input voltage is above 100VAC. -- Operating the system at a temperature lower than 50C (122F).

bugs.title: Search by "Signature ID is" does not return results for some signature IDs
bugs.symptoms: Search by "Signature ID is" does not return results for some signature IDs.
bugs.conditions: Request associated with signature that was previously enforced and is now in staging after the attack signature update.
bugs.impact: You are unable to filter requests by some signature IDs.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with searching by signature ID.

bugs.title: Username is reported in the session report after logout
bugs.symptoms: A username is reported after the user has logged out.
bugs.conditions: -- Session tracking with username is enabled. -- The logged-in user just logged out.
bugs.impact: Username is reported. This lasts for the time the session is still valid, 1200 seconds, by default. Note: The session expiration interval can be configured in the GUI.
bugs.fix: The sentence: 'User tracking does not expire when going through the logout page.' was added to the original note.

bugs.title: When 'Web Scraping Configuration' has 'Bot Detection' set to 'Alarm', the type=7 JavaScript challenge is sent.
bugs.symptoms: The JavaScript challenge type=7 is sent when it should not be. The challenge should be sent only when 'Bot Detection' is set to 'Alarm and Block' or when 'Fingerprint Usage' or 'Persistent Client Identification' is enabled in 'Web Scraping Configuration'.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM Policy. -- 'Bot Detection' set to 'Alarm' in 'Web Scraping Configuration'.
bugs.impact: After 10 requests to a qualified URL, the JavaScript challenge type=7 is sent back.
bugs.fix: Now, when using 'Web Scraping Configuration', JavaScript challenge type=7 is sent only when 'Bot Detection' is set to 'Alarm and Block' or when 'Fingerprint Usage' or 'Persistent Client Identification' is enabled in 'Web Scraping Configuration'.

bugs.title: Error when configuring a link local address as a default gateway
bugs.symptoms: When a link local address is configured as a default gateway there is an error when running the 'tmsh load sys config' command: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 1017) "default" unknown property. /config/bigip.config is incorrectly written with an empty interface value: cat bigip.conf|grep 'net route' -A4 net route /Common/External_default_GW { gw 169.254.200.1 interface network default }
bugs.conditions: -- config.allow.rfc3927 database key set to enable. -- Link local address is configured as a default gateway, as shown in the following example: cat bigip.conf|grep 'net route' -A4 net route /Common/External_default_GW { gw 169.254.200.1 interface <== This is the error network default }
bugs.impact: The default gateway works, but bigip.conf may not be loaded via tmsh with the command 'load sys config'.
bugs.workaround: Modify the bigip.conf file, adding the correct interface, as shown in the following example, which uses 'interface Ext': cat bigip.conf|grep 'net route' -A4 net route /Common/External_default_GW { gw 169.254.200.1 interface Ext network default }

bugs.title: SWG puts flow in intercept mode when session is not found
bugs.symptoms: In SWG, flows that should be getting bypassed are placed in intercept mode.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the per-request policy receives an https request and a session is not established.
bugs.impact: In some cases, the client sees certificate warning.
bugs.workaround: If the access policy is "start->allow"; following iRule can be used for workaround: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { if { [ACCESS::session exists] } { log local0. "Found Access Session" log local0. [ACCESS::session exists] } else { set sid [ACCESS::session create -lifetime 300 -timeout 300 -flow] log local0. "No Access Session found, creating $sid" ACCESS::session data set session.ui.mode "0" ACCESS::session data set session.policy.result "allow" } }

bugs.title: HTTP request dropped after a 401 exchange when a Websockets profile is attached to virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: The client sends a GET request with switching protocols and the server responds with a 401. Subsequent GET request from client is dropped.
bugs.conditions: HTTP and Websocket profiles are attached to the virtual server. The client sends a GET request with switching protocols indicating upgrade to Websockets, and the server responds with a 401. Subsequent GET request from client is dropped.
bugs.impact: Connection is reset.
bugs.workaround: Disable Websockets profile on the virtual server.
bugs.fix: We now check whether the Websockets filter is on the virtual server before attempting an insert.

bugs.title: SDD v3 symmetric deduplication may start performing poorly after a failover event
bugs.symptoms: In certain high availability (HA) configurations and after performing specific maintenance tasks involving failovers, SDD v3 symmetric deduplication may start performing poorly for some file transfers.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: 1) A BIG-IP HA configuration is deployed on each side of the WOM tunnel. 2) Symmetric deduplication is configured to use the SDD v3 codec. 3) The far side BIG-IP HA configuration (from the perspective of the client performing the download) is failed over. 4) Clients attempt to download files that had previously been transferred through the BIG-IP units.
bugs.impact: Symmetric deduplication is severely impacted (virtually no hits) for files that had previously been transferred through the units. This causes the amount of data transmitted over the WAN to increase. Files that were not transferred previously through the units are not affected by this issue.
bugs.workaround: To eliminate the impacted symmetric deduplication condition, restart the receiving (i.e., the near) side.
bugs.fix: SDD v3 symmetric deduplication no longer performs poorly after a failover event.

bugs.title: After classification rule is updated, first periodic Insert content action fails for existing subscriber
bugs.symptoms: Immediately after the classification rule associated with a static subscriber is updated and if the action list has Insert content, the first periodic insert content action fails for the subscribers. Subsequent Insert content action will proceed as expected
bugs.conditions: Update of the classification rule associated with the subscribers.
bugs.impact: First periodic Insert content action, immediately succeeding after the update of the classification rule will fail.
bugs.workaround: bigstart restart tmm, after updating the classification rule with insert content action will fix the issue
bugs.fix: Update the record count associated with the subscriber during eval.

bugs.title: IKEv2 does not support NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO
bugs.symptoms: IPsec IKEv2 tunnels cannot be established when the remote peer sends a NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO notification as part of the child Security Association (SA) establishment. This parameter is commonly sent by ASA devices.
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec IKEv2 with ASA peer. -- Remote peer sends a NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO notification as part of the child SA establishment.
bugs.impact: IKEv2 IPsec tunnels cannot be established with ASA peer.
bugs.workaround: Use IKEv1.
bugs.fix: During IPsec IKEv2 child SA establishment, the BIG-IP will ignore the NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO notification and will continue to establish the SA.

bugs.title: IKEv2: fewer logging format artifcacts with debug log-level
bugs.symptoms: When IPsec log-level is debug, sometimes logged payloads have line breaks in the middle, and most lines are missing a single character at line end, such as a closing parenthesis or quote.
bugs.conditions: Log level set to debug, then passing v2 IPsec traffic.
bugs.impact: Distracting imperfections in debug log output.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A larger buffer was used to reduce line breaks. Missing characters at line's end were due to incorrect swapping of one function for another that reserved a byte for a terminating null, when the size to copy was the line length; so the size to copy had to be increased to include an end null so it could be removed without shortening the line.

bugs.title: Portal Access: support of relative URLs in HTML tags <link rel=import ...>
bugs.symptoms: HTML components can be imported into HTML page via <link rel=import ...> tags. If the same HTML component is referenced by several such tags, only the first import is performed. But in the case of Portal Access, the browser cannot recognize identical URLs in some cases due to URL mangling. This may lead to unnecessary multiple loading of the same HTML component.
bugs.conditions: -- HTML page with several <link rel=import ...> tags referring to the same HTML component but using different representation of its URL, for example: <link rel=import href=/some/path/component.html> <link rel=import href=../component.html> -- '/some/path' and '../' refer to the same back-end path. -- Chrome browser.
bugs.impact: The component should be loaded once, but Portal Access rewrites both URLs. The browser cannot recognize its identity, so the component is loaded twice, and scripts inside are executed twice. Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access supports relative URLs in HTML import tags correctly.

bugs.title: RST when using Bot Defense profile and surfing to a long URL on related domain
bugs.symptoms: When surfing to a long URL of a related domain, and using "Cross Domain Requests : validate upon request" option in Bot Defense profile - Connection Aborts.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense Profile is attached to virtual server with 'Cross Domain Requests' option configured to 'Validate Upon Request'. -- Surfing to a non-HTML, long URL in a related domain.
bugs.impact: Connection Aborts.
bugs.workaround: Use another option of 'Cross Domain Requests': 'Validate in a Bulk' or 'Allow All'.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with connection resets when using a bot defense profile.

bugs.title: tmsh logs boost assertion when running child process and reaches idle-timeout
bugs.symptoms: An idle-timeout occurs while running a sub-process in interactive mode, resulting in a log message. tmsh logs a benign but ominous-looking critical error to the console and to /var/log/ltm if a tmsh command reaches idle timeout and a spawned sub-process is still running. The errors in /var/log/ltm begin with the following text: 'boost assertion failed'
bugs.conditions: -- tmsh command reaches idle timeout. -- Spawned sub-process is still running.
bugs.impact: Although the wording indicates a failure, the message is benign and you can safely ignore it.

bugs.title: Chain certificate is still being sent to the client, despite both ca-file and chain certificate being removed from the clientssl profile.
bugs.symptoms: Chain certificate is still being sent to the client, despite both ca-file and chain certificate being removed from the clientssl profile.
bugs.conditions: Set ca-file to 'none' in the clientssl profile.
bugs.impact: Chain is still sent.
bugs.fix: Chain certificate is no longer sent to the client when both ca-file and chain certificate are removed from the clientssl profile.

bugs.title: Log messages for virtual server status changes are not immediately logged.
bugs.symptoms: Log messages for virtual server status changes are not immediately logged.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server status due to lasthop-pool going down or coming back up. -- Viewing associated logs.
bugs.impact: No status-change messages are present.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when sys db Crypto.HwAcceleration is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when sys db Crypto.HwAcceleration is disabled.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when sys db Crypto.HwAcceleration is disabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Enable crypto hardware acceleration using the following command: tmsh modify sys db crypto.hwacceleration value enable

bugs.title: Periodic content insertion fails, if http request/response get interleaved by second subscriber http request
bugs.symptoms: Periodic content insertion for a subscriber may stop working after one or more insertions.
bugs.conditions: When a subscriber action list have Insert content added and if the request/response for that http transaction get interleaved by another subscriber request. This happens when more than one subscriber is using the same policy rule
bugs.impact: Periodic insert content action will fail to insert the content
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the subscriber for which insert content action no longer working
bugs.fix: For subscriber content insertion record lookup, use the correct session id storage associated with the subscriber.

bugs.title: Periodic content insertion fails, if pem and classification profile are detached and reattached to the Listener
bugs.symptoms: Periodic content insertion for a subscriber may stop working after one or more insertions.
bugs.conditions: When a subscriber action list have Insert content added and if pem and classification profiles are detached and re-attached to the Listener, periodic insertion may fail to insert the content. This happens when more than one subscriber is using the same policy rule and the listener.
bugs.impact: Periodic insert content action will fail to insert the content
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the subscriber for which insert content action no longer working
bugs.fix: For subscriber content insertion record lookup, use the right session id storage associated with the subscriber

bugs.title: DNSSEC Key Generation event failure during BIG-IP initialization can result in syncing empty DNSSEC keys to GTM sync group
bugs.symptoms: A DNSSEC key generation event is scheduled to occur (for example an expiration or rollover) while the Master Key is not yet initialized and mcpd is not in a full running state. The DNSSEC key generation fails because of the unavailablilty of the Master Key, but uninitialized mcpd may be unable to roll-back the transaction, resulting in syncing an empty DNSSEC key to the GTM sync group.
bugs.conditions: A DNSSEC key generation event is scheduled to occur (for example an expiration or rollover) during the time in which he Master Key is not yet initialized and mcpd is not in a full running state. This could be when a BIG-IP is being rebooted, performing a bigstart restart, or has been powered-off for some time and is being powered back up.
bugs.impact: It is possible that empty DNSSEC keys could be synced to the GTM sync group, over-writing previously valid key generations.
bugs.workaround: When powering off a GTM for an extended period of time, it is advisable to first remove the GTM from the sync group, so that whenever it is powered on again, it does not attempt sync before it is in a healthy state. You can also avoid this issue by performing reboot or bigstart restart during a window in which DNSSEC keys are not scheduled to expire or rollover.
bugs.fix: Now if a DNSSEC key generation event occurs (for example an expiration or rollover) while the Master Key is not yet initialized, we will delay all DNSSEC key generation events until the Master Key becomes available. A message will be logged in /var/log/ltm to inform the user we are delaying DNSSEC key generations for this reason.

bugs.title: qkview may take up to 90 seconds longer to execute on FIPS enabled systems
bugs.symptoms: When FIPS is enabled, qkview will execute the sys-eicheck.py script, which can take up to 90 seconds to execute.
bugs.conditions: FIPS is installed, or -c is specified on qkview command line.
bugs.impact: qkview takes longer to execute. Note: This extra time (90 seconds) is necessary when running qkview on a FIPS enabled system.
bugs.fix: This extra time (90 seconds) is necessary when running qkview on a FIPS enabled system.

bugs.title: 'tmsh show sys software' can erroneously show status 'installing hotfix' after inserting new blade
bugs.symptoms: After inserting a new blade into a chassis, it is possible that one of that blade's volumes will report status 'installing hotfix' instead of 'complete'. Example output of the command: tmsh show sys software: ----------------------------------------------------------- Sys::Software Status Volume Slot Product Version Build Active Status ----------------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 1 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no complete HD1.1 2 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no complete HD1.1 3 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no complete HD1.1 4 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no installing hotfix HD1.2 1 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete HD1.2 2 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete HD1.2 3 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete HD1.2 4 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete
bugs.conditions: This can occur after inserting a new blade into a chassis. The specifics conditions that result in the issue are unknown.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic. This has no effect on system behavior, only the display seen from 'tmsh show sys software'
bugs.workaround: Run 'bigstart restart lind' or reboot the new blade.

bugs.title: 'tmsh show sys software' can erroneously show status 'installing hotfix' after inserting new blade
bugs.symptoms: After inserting a new blade into a chassis, it is possible that one of that blade's volumes will report status 'installing hotfix' instead of 'complete'. Example output of the command: tmsh show sys software: ----------------------------------------------------------- Sys::Software Status Volume Slot Product Version Build Active Status ----------------------------------------------------------- HD1.1 1 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no complete HD1.1 2 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no complete HD1.1 3 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no complete HD1.1 4 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.0.196 no installing hotfix HD1.2 1 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete HD1.2 2 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete HD1.2 3 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete HD1.2 4 BIG-IP 11.5.3 2.234.196 yes complete
bugs.conditions: This can occur after inserting a new blade into a chassis. The specifics conditions that result in the issue are unknown.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic. This has no effect on system behavior, only the display seen from 'tmsh show sys software'
bugs.workaround: Run 'bigstart restart lind' or reboot the new blade.

bugs.title: VPE loading times can be very long
bugs.symptoms: When a configuration contains 2000-3000 Access Policy objects, the Visual Policy Editor (VPE) loading operations can take tens of seconds to load.
bugs.conditions: -- Access Policy configured with 2000-3000 Access Policy objects. -- Open in VPE.
bugs.impact: Policies with thousands of entries can take tens of seconds or more to load.
bugs.fix: Configuration load has been optimized, so VPE loading time is significantly shorter for these types of configurations.

bugs.title: ng_export, ng_import might leave security.configpassword in invalid state
bugs.symptoms: If import/export of Access Profile or Access Policy results in an error, security.configpassword may retain temporary not <null> state, which can cause problems when the config is saved or loaded using the sys save config or sys load config commands.
bugs.conditions: Import or export of Access Profile or Access Policy fails with an error.
bugs.impact: Passwords in .conf might get mangled.
bugs.workaround: Set the security.configpassword db variable using the following command: modify sys db security.configpassword value "<null>"
bugs.fix: Error handling for access policy import failures has been improved.

bugs.title: After an upgrade, IPsec tunnels may fail to start
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, the post-upgrade ipsec-policy or ike-peer configuration may be different to the pre-upgrade version.
bugs.conditions: -- ipsec-policy or ike-peer uses default setting(s). -- BIG-IP's software is upgraded.
bugs.impact: After an upgrade, tunnels may fail to establish or establish using a stronger cipher set.
bugs.workaround: After upgrade, set the configuration objects to the required values.
bugs.fix: The tmsh schema is improved to show IPsec values must be persisted by saving, even if they equal the default values. This way if software upgrade changes the defaults, the old default values will be used when explicitly saved in config. Thus users will not see default IPsec config values change.

bugs.title: Custom bidirectional persistence entries are not updated to the session timeout
bugs.symptoms: Custom bidirectional persistence entries will be created using the transaction timeout when processing the request, but will not be updated to the session timeout on a successful response.
bugs.conditions: -- Using custom bidirectional persistence. -- Successful response message is received.
bugs.impact: The persistence timeout will prematurely time out.
bugs.workaround: Set the transaction timeout to the session timeout value.
bugs.fix: The persistence timeout is correctly updated to the session timeout value when a successful response message is received.

bugs.title: Web UI: Unlicensed Configuration Warning for DHCP Relay configuration
bugs.symptoms: Unlicensed warning message 'The Unlicensed fields allow configuration on this page but does not take effect in the system' is displayed, even though the functionality works fine.
bugs.conditions: No PEM/AFM license.
bugs.impact: Incorrect information is provided in the message. Misleading message indicates that DHCP Relay functionality may not work, even though it does work. This is a cosmetic issue, and you can safely ignore the message.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is a cosmetic error. Note: Having a license for LTM is enough for DHCP Relay functionality to work. The GUI erroneously checks for the Subscriber Management license, which comes with PEM/AFM license, and displays warning message if not available. However, the lack of the Subscriber Management license is not required for DHCP Relay functionality to work, and the message should not be displayed.
bugs.fix: LTM license is enough for DHCP Relay functionality to work. But GUI checks for Subscriber Management license which comes with PEM/AFM license and displays warning message if not available.

bugs.title: Some FTP log messages may not be logged to /var/log/ltm
bugs.symptoms: Some FTP log messages may not be logged to /var/log/ltm
bugs.conditions: Virtual with FTP profile is configured
bugs.impact: Some FTP_SETUP/FTP_TEARDOWN and FTP_DATA_SETUP/FTP_DATA_TEARDOWN logs may not be logged to /var/log/ltm.
bugs.workaround: Use remote HSL logging

bugs.title: Performance impact for certain platforms after upgrading to 13.1.0.
bugs.symptoms: Performance impact for certain platforms after upgrading to 13.1.0.
bugs.conditions: The following platforms, with Fast HTTP/OneConnect/Full Proxy configured. -- i2800 -- i4800 -- i5800 -- i7800 -- i10800 -- i11800 -- B2250 -- B4450
bugs.impact: The performance impacts occur on the following platforms under the associated conditions: -- i2800 2%-3% Full Proxy traffic. -- i4800 2%-3% Full Proxy traffic. -- i5800 3%-8% Fast HTTP/Full Proxy traffic. -- i7800 3%-7% Fast HTTP/Full Proxy traffic. -- i10800 3%-7% Fast HTTP/Full Proxy traffic. -- i11800 2%-3% Fast HTTP traffic. -- B2250 3%-6% OneConnect/Full Proxy traffic. -- B4450 4%-10% Fast HTTP/OneConnect/Full Proxy traffic.
bugs.fix: Performance impact for certain platforms has been eliminated.

bugs.title: vCMP does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, vCMP may generate internal configuration data that does not comply with best security practices.
bugs.conditions: vCMP platform
bugs.impact: vCMP does not comply with best security practices.
bugs.fix: vCMP does now complies with best security practices.

bugs.title: App-service is not supported by import/export
bugs.symptoms: If Access Profile is created by an iApp and the configuration is grouped by app-service mechanism (i.e., it can be locked or managed via app-service filed in various objects), import/export does not work.
bugs.conditions: Access Profile that is created by iApp with app-service-based grouping.
bugs.impact: No import/export support. Difficult to backup and restore these types of profiles.
bugs.fix: There is no longer an import error in this instance.

bugs.title: ESXi host client fails to deploy a virtual machine from BIG-IP OVA file
bugs.symptoms: ESXi host client fails to deploy a virtual machine (VM) from the BIG-IP OVA file (probably because BIG-IP vmdk files are compressed).
bugs.conditions: Deploying BIG-IP OVA by ESXi.
bugs.impact: ESXi 6.5 does not support VMware vSphere Client, and failure to deploy via the ESXi host client leaves ovftool or booting off the product ISO as the only known viable options for ESXi 6.5.
bugs.workaround: Deploy the BIG-IP system by creating a new VM from the ISO file, and initially booting the VM off the official BIG-IP ISO to perform an installation.
bugs.fix: OVA image can now be deployed to a standalone host using the built-in web client.

bugs.title: Memory leak when using HTTP2 profile
bugs.symptoms: Memory continues to grow despite reduced volume of traffic. Large number of spdy_frame and xdata allocated.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with HTTP2 profile.
bugs.impact: Memory leak, which might eventually trigger aggressive sweeper and potential crash, resulting in failover.
bugs.fix: Virtual server configured with HTTP2 profile no longer leaks memory.

bugs.title: 1NIC VE in high availability (HA) device-group shows 'Changes Pending' after reboot
bugs.symptoms: When Virtual Edition (VE) is configured for 1NIC, you will see the following logs on reboot indicating that configuration has been loaded from file: notice tmsh[12232]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=12232 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=load sys config partitions all base notice tmsh[12392]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=12392 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=load sys config partitions all
bugs.conditions: - VE configured in 1NIC mode. - Unit booted either through reboot or power on.
bugs.impact: This is unlikely to have any impact if the VE is in standalone mode but could result in an unexpected config if the configuration files differ. If the VE is part of a device-group, then this will result in a commit id update and the units will show 'Changes pending'.

bugs.title: Potential memory issue in iprepd
bugs.symptoms: Potential memory issue in iprepd. No IP Intelligence reports in AVR.
bugs.conditions: This is caused by uninitialized variables.
bugs.impact: iprepd fails to download IP intelligence DB and subsequently AVR won't have IP Intelligence reports.
bugs.workaround: Restart iprepd.
bugs.fix: iprepd now downloads IP intelligence DB and subsequently AVR has the IP Intelligence reports.

bugs.title: agetty auto detects parity on console port incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: With a BIG-IP system configured for a console baud rate that is different from the baud rate of the serial terminal that is plugged in to the console port, he system returns garbled characters on the screen. Changing the terminal setting to match the console baud rate has no effect after that: the BIG-IP system continues to send garbage.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system with a console at certain baud rate. -- Plug in a serial terminal with a different baud rate. -- Press enter several times.
bugs.impact: The parity detection code selects the wrong setting, leaving the console port unusable until reboot of the BIG-IP system, or after killing and restarting agetty.
bugs.workaround: To recover from this condition, log on to the BIG-IP system via ssh, force parity off, and kill the agetty process (assuming the console is not logged in, and is therefore running agetty). via ssh: # stty -F /dev/ttyS0 -parenb ; killall agetty However, this is not an ideal workaround, as a frequent reason to use the serial console is lack of network access to the device. In that situation, you can log on by setting the terminal to Mark parity (8 data bits, Mark parity, 1 stop bit). Note: There is no way to mitigate the issue from the console connection itself, as agetty doesn't run while the console is logged in. You can also reboot the BIG-IP system, reset the terminal speed on the laptop to match the console speed set on the BIG-IP system, and reconnect the laptop.
bugs.fix: This issue has been corrected.

bugs.title: Unable to set 'media-fixed' on management port on BIG-IP i15000 platforms
bugs.symptoms: Changing 'media-fixed' on management port on BIG-IP i15000 platforms using tmsh command 'tmsh modify net interface mgmt media-fixed <speed>' does not take effect.
bugs.conditions: -- Connecting two BIG-IP i15000 units via management port. -- Changing the 'media-fixed' value.
bugs.impact: Changing the 'media-fixed' value does not work.
bugs.workaround: Pull the management cable out and plug it back in to get the link up at the respective speeds.
bugs.fix: Users can now change the 'media-fixed' value using tmsh commands.

bugs.title: Dhclient does not support standard supersede options on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: Dhclient supports the supersede option through which locally set value/values can supersede DHCP server-provided values in the lease for a given option. This is achieved by adding the supersede-option and value pair in dhclient.conf. In case of the BIG-IP system, the modifications in dhclient.conf are overwritten by MCPD, and MCPD does not support specifying supersede-options.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP configured with DHCP enabled. -- Attempt to supersede DHCP server-provided values in the lease for a given option by adding the supersede-option and value pair in dhclient.conf.
bugs.impact: The system overwrites the modifications. Cannot supersede DHCP server-provided values in the lease for a given option.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports the standard supersede options, so you can direct dhclient to use locally-configured values over the ones provided by the DHCP server for a given option.

bugs.title: tmm may crash when after deleting pool member in traffic
bugs.symptoms: tmm may crash when after deleting pool member that is processing traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Two or more pools share the same node as pool member. -- A pool member (with the shared node) is deleted while traffic is passing. -- Connpool is used.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes when after deleting pool member while traffic is passing.

bugs.title: iSeries AOM web UI update fails to complete.
bugs.symptoms: Upon upgrading a BIG-IP version, AOM web UI updates can sometimes fail.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when upgrading a BIG-IP system's software version on iSeries platforms.
bugs.impact: After booting to a new version, the AOM web UI update fails with an error message in /var/log/ltm similar to the following: err bmcuiupdate[20824]: Failed updated AOM web UI with return code 2
bugs.workaround: At the bash prompt run: /etc/lcdui/bmcuiupdate This triggers another upgrade attempt, and the result is logged in /var/log/ltm. This should not be service-affecting.
bugs.fix: AOM web UI update failures are now automatically corrected.

bugs.title: Allow multiple client SSL profiles on a virtual server with different security requirements
bugs.symptoms: When multiple client SSL profiles are attached to a virtual server, each must share the same ciphers, authenticate, authenticate depth, peer-cert mode, and, if peer-cert mode is require, CRL. Otherwise, the system posts an error similar to the following: 0107157c:3: Selected client SSL profiles do not match security policies for Virtual Server <vs-name>.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create two client SSL profiles, one of which requires client certificate and the other does not. 2. Try to assign these profile to the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: Error message. Cannot attach multiple, differing client SSL profile.
bugs.workaround: Assure that all client SSL profiles attached to a virtual share the same security attributes.
bugs.fix: Now, each client SSL profile attached to a single virtual server can have different security settings.

bugs.title: chmand error log message missing data
bugs.symptoms: When there is an error with communication between chmand and lopd, a message is logged giving information about the problem. That message is missing data useful to F5 for determining the cause of the communications error. Messages similar to: Jul 11 11:10:19 localhost warning chmand[7815]: 012a0004:4: getLopReg: lop response data does not match request, u16DataLen=0xb expected=0xb, u8Length=0x8 expected=0x, u8Page=0x28 expected=0x$, u8Register=0x50 expected=0xP The expected data values are missing in this message, making it more difficult for F5 engineers to determine what caused the original communications problem.
bugs.conditions: This issue only occurs when there is some problem with the communication channel between chmand and lopd.
bugs.impact: Added difficulty for F5 to determine what problem caused the error message to be logged.
bugs.fix: The expected data values are properly printed in the log message.

bugs.title: Unable to discover ASM policies with EM 3.1.1
bugs.symptoms: Enterprise Manager (EM) is unable to synchronize with the BIG-IP device with the error: 'Instance not found: ASM / Policy Template / <Policy Name>'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in response to either of the following conditions: -- The system has inactive ASM policies that have never been active. -- The system is affected by the following 11.5.x known issue: Policy history revision files in the /var/ts/dms/policy/policy_versions/* directories are erased after a device group sync.
bugs.impact: EM is unable to synchronize with the device.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1) Apply or Delete inactive policies. 2) Push another sync from the peer device or apply the affected policies.
bugs.fix: EM now successfully discovers devices with policies that have never been applied or are missing the latest policy history file.

bugs.title: False positive cookie hijacking violation
bugs.symptoms: A false positive cookie hijacking violation.
bugs.conditions: -- Several sites are configured on the policy, without subdomain. -- TS cookies are sent with the higher domain level then the configured. -- A single cookie from another host (that belongs to the same policy) arrives and is mistaken as the other site cookie.
bugs.impact: False positive violation / blocking.
bugs.workaround: Cookie hijacking violation when the device ID feature is turned off is almost never relevant, as it should be able to detect only cases where some of the TS cookies were taken. The suggestion is to turn off this violation.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes - monitor attribute doesn't reliably show in GUI
bugs.symptoms: When creating more than one node with FQDN configured with monitors, monitors are not displayed in the GUI properly.
bugs.conditions: Create more than one node with FQDN configured.
bugs.impact: The previously created FQDN node does not display monitors in the GUI. However, the subsequently created FQDN node does display the correct monitors.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to view monitors for Nodes with FQDN configured.
bugs.fix: Node page now displays the correct monitors for nodes configured with FQDN.

bugs.title: Upgrade to 13.1+ may fail for low resources platforms
bugs.symptoms: when upgrading a low resources platform (like vCMP guest with many provisioned modules) to 13.1 or higher, upgrade might fail
bugs.conditions: low resources platform
bugs.impact: upgrade failure
bugs.workaround: un-provision a few modules before upgrading (depends on platform resources)

bugs.title: Prevent login failure caused by user deleting cookies
bugs.symptoms: When deleting cookies immediately before attempting to log in to a protected website, the login operation may fail.
bugs.conditions: -- Delete cookies while on the login page. -- Attempt to log in immediately, without refreshing the page.
bugs.impact: Login failure.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system no longer fails login under these conditions.

bugs.title: Custom headers are removed on cross-origin requests
bugs.symptoms: Custom headers are removed on cross-origin requests.
bugs.conditions: A cross domain FPS request uses the FPS custom header. For example: AJAX encryption from one domain to another.
bugs.impact: The request will be blocked, FPS functionality breaks.
bugs.workaround: For HOST <HOST NAME> and FPS custom header <HEADER NAME>, a variant of the following iRule can be used: when HTTP_REQUEST { if {[HTTP::method] equals "OPTIONS" && [HTTP::host] equals "<HOST NAME>"} { set modify_allowed_headers 1 } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { [info exists modify_allowed_headers] && $modify_allowed_headers equals "1"} { if { [HTTP::header exists "Access-Control-Allow-Headers"] } { set hdr [HTTP::header value "Access-Control-Allow-Headers"] append hdr ", <HEADER NAME>" HTTP::header replace Access-Control-Allow-Headers $hdr } } }

bugs.title: The 'Illegal flow' violation occurs on requests to the same policy on non-synchronized devices
bugs.symptoms: The 'Illegal flow' violation occurs on requests to the same policy on non-synchronized devices when subsequent requests are handled by a different device.
bugs.conditions: Traffic is handled for the same policy by different devices that are not synchronized.
bugs.impact: 'Illegal flow' violation is triggered.
bugs.workaround: To workaround the issue, it is possible to align the differing account_id values by saving ASM configuration on one device, and loading on the other device. Important: This overwrites the full ASM configuration, and should be done only if all ASM policies are identical on both devices. No part of LTM configuration is changed by this action, however. This is the same mechanism used internally by ASM device group sync. To save the full ASM configuration: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- perl -MF5::ConfigSync -MF5::DbUtils -e 'F5::ConfigSync->new(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh())->save_to_file(filename => shift)' /var/tmp/full_asm_config.tgz ---------------------------------------------------------------------- To load the full ASM configuration: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- perl -MF5::ConfigSync -MF5::BigipVersionUtils -MF5::DbUtils -e 'F5::ConfigSync->new(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), ucs_version => F5::BigipVersionUtils::bigip_version())->load_from_file(filename => shift)' /var/tmp/full_asm_config.tgz ----------------------------------------------------------------------

bugs.title: BD crash upon startup
bugs.symptoms: System does not start up, bd restart while updating the geolocation database.
bugs.conditions: -- Traffic is running through the system. -- The geolocation database is being updated.
bugs.impact: The bd process restarts, which results in traffic disturbance and failover.
bugs.workaround: Update the geolocation database when there is no traffic.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly initializes the geolocation database before

bugs.title: Syncing a large number of folders can prevent the configuration getting saved on the peer systems
bugs.symptoms: When syncing a large number of folders (more than 56), the configuration on the peer systems fails to save. An error similar to the following appears in the audit log, possibly followed by garbage characters: notice tmsh[15819]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=15819 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Syntax Error: "}" is missing] cmd_data=save / sys config partitions { tf01 tf02 tf03 tf04 tf05 tf06 tf07 tf08 tf09 tf10 tf11 tf12 tf13 tf14 tf15 tf16 tf17 tf18 tf19 tf20 tf21 tf22 tf23 tf24 tf25 tf26 tf27 tf28 tf29 tf30 tf31 tf32 tf33 tf34 tf35 tf36 tf37 tf38 tf39 tf40 tf41 tf42 tf43 tf44 tf45 tf46 tf47 tf48 tf49 tf50 tf51 tf52 tf53 tf54 tf55 tf56 tf57 tf58 tf59 Note: These 'tfnn' folder names are examples. The audit log will contain a list of the actual folder names. (Folders are also called 'partitions'.)
bugs.conditions: -- System is in a device group. -- Sync operation occurs on the device group. -- There are a large number of folders (more than 56).
bugs.impact: Configuration on peer systems in a device group does not get saved after a sync.
bugs.workaround: Manually save the configuration on peer systems after a sync.
bugs.fix: The configuration on peer systems is now saved when a large number of folders are involved in the sync.

bugs.title: Multicast UDP from BIG-IP may have incorrect checksums
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP may transmit UDP datagrams with a bad checksum.
bugs.conditions: Outgoing link-local multicast UDP traffic from the Linux host, such as RIP.
bugs.impact: Packets may be dropped by adjacent devices.
bugs.workaround: Disable checksum offloading on the virtual NIC for affected VLANS, e.g. "ethtool --offload vlan1274 rx on tx off"
bugs.fix: Link-local multicast UDP packets are no longer sent with incorrect checksums.

bugs.title: PEM subscriber sessions are shown as '0' for blades that are not operationally UP.
bugs.symptoms: PEM subscriber sessions are shown as '0' for blades that are not operationally UP.
bugs.conditions: Execute 'tmsh show pem sessiondb blade x' on a blade that is DOWN.
bugs.impact: No impact to PEM-provided services. Potential questions related to why the the number of subscriber sessions on blade X is 0, when the operator is unaware that Blade X is operationally DOWN.

bugs.title: SDD v3 symmetric deduplication may stop working indefinitely
bugs.symptoms: In certain high availability (HA) configurations and after performing specific maintenance tasks involving failovers, SDD v3 symmetric deduplication may stop working indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: 1) A BIG-IP HA configuration is deployed on each side of the WOM tunnel. 2) Symmetric deduplication is configured to use the SDD v3 codec. 3) Applications configured to benefit from symmetric deduplication are actively passing traffic. 4) Both BIG-IP HA pairs (the near and far sides) are failed over concurrently (although in more rare cases, even failing over a single pair is sufficient to reproduce the issue).
bugs.impact: Applications no longer benefit from symmetric deduplication, increasing the amount of data transmitted over the WAN.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the services on all BIG-IP units involved in the topology (without performing additional failovers after they return on-line) restores symmetric deduplication functionality. This will cause some downtime.
bugs.fix: Performing failovers in AAM environment no longer breaks SDD v3 symmetric deduplication.

bugs.title: AD auth failures due to invalid Kerberos tickets
bugs.symptoms: User can not login.
bugs.conditions: - AAA AD server is configured on BIG-IP. - AD Auth/Query agent is used in Access Policy. - Cached Kerberos ticket is invalid or backend AD server is not reachable for some reason
bugs.impact: AD Auth/Query fails. APM end user won't be able to take successful branch in Access Policy.
bugs.fix: Invalid Kerberos tickets for AD Query are now automatically renegotiated by APM.

bugs.title: Serial console baud rate setting lost after running 'tmidiag -r' in Maintenance OS
bugs.symptoms: When booted into the Maintenance OS image from the grub boot menu, running tmidiag -r drops the serial console from the grub kernel line, which causes a loss of communication on the serial console after rebooting.
bugs.conditions: -- Booted into Maintenance OS. -- Running the command: tmidiag -r
bugs.impact: Serial console baud rate settings are incorrect. Uses the bios baud rate on the console.
bugs.workaround: When booting, edit the grub kernel line to include console=ttyS0. Note: The value is "tty", an uppercase "S" character, and zero, so ttyS0.
bugs.fix: tmidiag has been fixed to not strip out console=ttyS0.

bugs.title: Users are not expected to change security.commoncriteria DB variable through TMSH
bugs.symptoms: Changing the security.commoncriteria db variable to true, and then attempting to change it back to false through TMSH causes validation errors related to SSHD configuration. Users are not expected to change this value without using the ccmode script.
bugs.conditions: Changing the security.commoncriteria db variable to true, and then back to false.
bugs.impact: Validation errors. The BIG-IP system remains stuck in Common Criteria mode when it is not desired.

bugs.title: BD memory leak on specific configuration and specific traffic
bugs.symptoms: RSS memory of the bd grows.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote logger is configured. -- IP has ignore logging configured. -- Traffic is coming from the ignored logging IP.
bugs.impact: Potential memory exhaustion. The kernel might run out of memory and may kill bd, causing traffic disruption.
bugs.fix: Freeing up the remote loggers data when deciding not to log remotly.

bugs.title: New revoke license feature for VE only implemented
bugs.symptoms: Prior to this version, the license revoke feature was not implemented/available.
bugs.conditions: With out revoke implemented, the feature is simply not available.
bugs.impact: Licenses cannot be revoked and hence re-used.
bugs.fix: With this feature implemented, VE licenses can be revoked and then re-used on different VE.

bugs.title: TCL error in ltm log when server closes connection while ASM irules are running
bugs.symptoms: TCL error in ltm log, for example: TCL error: /Common/bug <ASM_REQUEST_DONE> - plugin_tcl_command_execute: Command error. invoked from within "ASM::severity"
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM irules are attached. 2. There was already one request passed to the web-server 3. Server closes connection.
bugs.impact: Error in ltm log.

bugs.title: TMM process fails
bugs.symptoms: TMM process fails with the following message: TMM SIGSEGV in hsb_fast_tx_pkt().
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that cause the process failure are not well understood. But failover may be generated using a command similar to the following: tmm.0 -T 10 --tmid 0 --npus 10 --platform A112 --split-planes -m -s 59028 '. Program terminated with signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
bugs.impact: Failover occurs. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Outage may occur with VIP-VIP configurations
bugs.symptoms: In some VIP-VIP configurations, TMM may produce a core with a 'no trailing data' assert.
bugs.conditions: VIP-VIP configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer produces a core with a 'no trailing data' assert.

bugs.title: Packets with payload smaller than MSS are being marked to be TSOed
bugs.symptoms: Packets with length less than the specified MSS are sent as TSO packets, and the Broadcom NIC drops those to degrade performance.
bugs.conditions: When TM.TcpSegmentationOffload is enabled, Packets with length less than MSS are sent as TSO packets.
bugs.impact: TCP Packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Disable TSO option by setting the following SYS DB variable to disable: TM.TcpSegmentationOffload.
bugs.fix: Packets less than MSS are not sent as TSO packets, so there is no performance degradation.

bugs.title: APM configuration snapshot takes a long time to create
bugs.symptoms: It takes a long time to create the configuration snapshot for a file. This may be accompanied by MEMCACHED related log message, as shown below. notice apmd[12928]: 0149016a:5: Initiating snapshot creation: tmm.session.10b9e255c7bb0_28oooooooooooooooo for access profile: /Common/workspace-acess notice apmd[12928]: 0149016f:5: Waiting for MEMCACHED to be ready notice apmd[12928]: 01490000:5: ApmD.cpp func: "wait_for_memcached_ready()" line: 1273 Msg: Unable to connect to tmm (sessiondb). Trying again... notice apmd[12928]: 01490000:5: ApmD.cpp func: "wait_for_memcached_ready()" line: 1280 Msg: Successfully connected to tmm (sessiondb)... notice apmd[12928]: 0149016b:5: Completed snapshot creation: tmm.session.10b9e255c7bb0_28oooooooooooooooo for access profile: /Common/workspace-acess notice apmd[12928]: 01490171:5: MEMCACHED is up
bugs.conditions: The issue happens if an access profile contains many resources, the resulting configuration snapshot will have even more configuration variables.
bugs.impact: TMM will run out of memory If the issue persists. User will not be able to log in due to profile not found error similar to the following: err apmd[13681]: 01490114:3: /Common/workspace-acess2:Common:a6b495ce: process_request(): Profile '/Common/workspace-acess2' was not found
bugs.fix: APM policy configuration snapshot generation performance for very large configurations has been improved.

bugs.title: Periodic content insertion of new flows fails, if an outstanding flow is a long flow
bugs.symptoms: If an outstanding flow with periodic insertion pem_action is very long, it prevents new flow matching the same rule from adding inert content pem_action even for a new periodic interval
bugs.conditions: If the outstanding flow with insert content pem_action spans multiple periodic interval.
bugs.impact: No content insertion during the time the long flow is outstanding for new flows matching the same rule as the long flow.
bugs.workaround: Long flows and short flows need to have separate rule configured
bugs.fix: New flows will add content insertion, if the new flow request falls in the new periodic interval.

bugs.title: ECDSA Key management support on BIG-IP using Thales and SafeNet external network HSM
bugs.symptoms: There is no support for ECDSA key management on BIG-IP systems using external network HSM on Thales and SafeNet.
bugs.conditions: Creating ECDSA keys and certificates using tmsh/GUI and iControl. e.g., tmsh create sys crypto key ec_nethsm key-type ec-private curve- name prime256v1 security-type nethsm tmsh create sys crypto cert ec_nethsm key ec_nethsm common-name www.ecdsa.com
bugs.impact: ECDSA Keys and Certificates cannot be created on external network HSM such as Thales and SafeNet on BIG-IP systems.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: ECDSA Key/cert management using external network HSM such as Thales and SafeNet is now supported on BIG-IP systems. The feature provides support on BIG-IP systems for external network HSM to create/list/delete/ operation for ECDSA keys and certificates along with using ECDSA sign operation during SSL handshake.

bugs.title: Ordering and OSPF configuration timing of IA routes on HA configuration can lead to differences in route table
bugs.symptoms: In some specific circumstances, the configuration ordering and activation timing in an HA configuration of OSPF inter-area (IA) routes might lead to one unit learning the route off the peer instead of learning it from the configuration.
bugs.conditions: - Two or more units using very close or identical OSPF configurations. - Announcement of IA summary routes that locally are blackholed. - One unit is configured before the others, in a way that the peers learn the route before the configuration is introduced locally.
bugs.impact: A unit may prefer a route to the peer instead of a locally configured blackhole.
bugs.workaround: Do any of the following: -- Restart the ospf process. -- Run the command: clear ip ospf process. -- Remove the ospf config and paste it back in.

bugs.title: sipdb cannot delete custom bidirectional persistence entries.
bugs.symptoms: Custom bidirectional SIP persistence entries cannot be deleted using the sipdb tool.
bugs.conditions: Rules and SIP messages created custom bidirectional SIP persistence entries.
bugs.impact: Custom bidirectional SIP persistence entries exist and can be viewed with the sipdb utility. They cannot be deleted, however.
bugs.fix: The sipdb tool now supports deletion of bidirectional SIP persistence entries.

bugs.title: ZoneRunner: GUI "Email Contact" field silently ignores invalid char '@' in Email Contact
bugs.symptoms: Changing the email address in ZoneRunner and using a '@' character does not work. System validation catches that the '@' is invalid, but the operation fails silently, and the new email address is not stored. Note. The '@' character is invalid for the email field because it has other uses in zone files. A dot should be used instead of '@'.
bugs.conditions: Zone already exists in ZoneRunner. Trying to update it with a new email address.
bugs.impact: Confusion as to why the GUI is ignoring the new email address they entered.
bugs.workaround: The '@' (at sign) character is invalid for ZoneRunner email fields because it has other uses in zone files. Use a '.' (dot, or period) character instead of '@'.

bugs.title: tmsh help/man page incorrectly state that the urldb feedlist polling interval is in seconds, when it should be hours.
bugs.symptoms: tmsh help/man page incorrectly state that the urldb feedlist polling interval is in seconds. In fact, it is in hours.
bugs.conditions: -- Viewing tmsh help/man page. -- Searching for urldb feedlist polling interval.
bugs.impact: Note that the interval described is in hours instead of seconds.
bugs.fix: tmsh help/man page now correctly states that the urldb feedlist polling interval is in hours.

bugs.title: DHCP virtuals need ALH set to Enabled for DHCP to function.
bugs.symptoms: DHCP packets from the client will not be forwarded to the server if auto-lasthop (ALH) is Disabled on the DHCP virtual server. While the ALH setting on a DHCP virtual server can be modified via TMSH, it cannot be modified via the GUI.
bugs.conditions: DHCP virtual created with the resulting ALH setting as 'Disabled'.
bugs.impact: DHCP packets from the client are not forwarded to the server. Loss of DHCP functionality.
bugs.workaround: Set ALH to enabled on the DHCP virtual server using TMSH.
bugs.fix: GUI sets AutoLastHop=Enabled in the background when creating DHCP virtual servers.

bugs.title: TMM halts and restarts in response to certain requests.
bugs.symptoms: TMM halts and restarts under certain conditions relating to Device ID or Fingerprinting.
bugs.conditions: Security policy or DoS Profile that uses Device ID or Fingerprinting.
bugs.impact: TMM halts and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Changing the Device ID matching mode to 'simple' will prevent this crash from happening. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db did.match_mode value simple

bugs.title: Application CSS injection might break when connection is congested
bugs.symptoms: Large CSS files configured for phishing protection injection in FPS (not fictive websafe CSS files) may be truncated upon response to client.
bugs.conditions: Inject into Application CSS enabled in Anti-Fraud Profile » Advanced » Phishing Detection Large CSS file such as bootstrap files configured for Application CSS Locations. Network congestion engaging TMM flow control.
bugs.impact: Pages may display incorrectly in client browser depending on application requirements with specific CSS. May break application functionality.
bugs.workaround: 1) Remove affected large files from Application CSS Locations. or 2) Disable Inject into Application CSS entirely.
bugs.fix: FPS now handles the case where injecting to application css was interrupted by congestion.

bugs.title: FPS modified responses/injections might result in a corrupted response
bugs.symptoms: in case a connection was congested and FPS tries to send additional egress (modifying the response, e.g. injections) the order of the response sending might break if this send is successful (i.e congestion just ended). instead of sending the buffered data first (response part that was buffered due to congestion), FPS tries to send the new data first and only than will send the buffered data.
bugs.conditions: - congested connection - FPS sends modified response (e.g. injections) - sending egress succeeded (congestion ended)
bugs.impact: response is corrupted - order of data has erroneously changed
bugs.fix: FPS will handle this case correctly, first sending buffered data then sending the new egress.

bugs.title: If a certificate is stored in DER format, exporting it using the GUI corrupts the output.
bugs.symptoms: When a certificate stored in DER format is exported, all bytes with values larger than 0x7E are replaced with 0x3F, and there is one more byte added (0x0a) at the end of the binary file.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to export a certificate stored in DER format.
bugs.impact: Corrupted certificate.
bugs.workaround: You will need to use openssl to create a copy of the certificate in .pem or .der format. For example, to export the der certificate myder.crt to a mycert.pem certificate in .pem format, run the following command: openssl x509 -out mycert.pem -in /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/\:Common\:myder.crt_75978_1 -inform der Note: This works for system users who can access the bash command, specifically, those with the administrator role.

bugs.title: AAM traffic report's time period doesn't always apply
bugs.symptoms: AAM traffic report's time period doesn't always apply.
bugs.conditions: Select a time period on the AAM traffic report page other than last hour.
bugs.impact: The table and graph still display last hour data.

bugs.title: It is not possible to use tmsh to change the password for 'admin' after configuring Remote-APM Based Auth on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: With APM-based system authentication, using tmsh to make changes to the password for user 'admin' will apparently succeed, but the password will be unchanged.
bugs.conditions: -- APM-based system authentication configured. -- Using tmsh to make changes to the password for user 'admin'.
bugs.impact: Unable to change password for default system account.
bugs.workaround: Switch to local system authentication, change the password for 'admin', then switch back to remote authentication.

bugs.title: Resource server failure message update
bugs.symptoms: Resource server failure response does not display the intended message
bugs.conditions: APM enabled
bugs.impact: When the resource server returns an failure response the intended diagnostic content is not included
bugs.fix: The resource server failure message has been updated

bugs.title: When BIG-IP as SAML IdP is configured to create large assertions, occasionally BIG-IP will not send entire assertion as part of the HTTP response to the client
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP as SAML IdP is configured to generate assertions larger than 32 KB, occasionally the BIG-IP system might not send the entire assertion as part of the HTTP response to the client, leaving the browser in a waiting state for the rest of the assertion to arrive.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is configured as SAML IdP. -- IdP is configured to include either list of (large) attributes, with assertion size exceeding 32 KB.
bugs.impact: Occasionally, APM end users will not be able to receive full SAML assertion, and therefore, authentication with SAML SP will fail.
bugs.workaround: When applicable, reconfigure SAML attributes to reduce the size of the generated assertion, i.e., remove unnecessary attributes from the SAML configuration.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports generating assertions larger than 32 KB.

bugs.title: The SAML IdP metadata automation periodic update of metadata file that has Certificate may cause 'Apply Access Policy' to show up even if no changes to the IdP connector object are made.
bugs.symptoms: On creating a SAML IdP metadata automation object with a metadata file that has Certificate, an IdP connector object is created and associated with SP object after the first timer expiry. If the SP is attached to an Access Policy, 'Apply Access Policy' shows up as expected. Next, if the metadata file in the automaton object changes such that no IdP connector object fields are impacted, 'Apply Access Policy' still shows up after next timer expiry. This is confusing because it should not show up when there is no update made to the IdP connector object or its association with SP object.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a SAML IdP connector automation object pointing to a metadata file that has Certificate, and the SP object is attached to an Access Policy. 2. Wait for the timer to expire the first time. 3. Make sure that the IdP connector object is created from the above metadata and associated to the SP object. Click on 'Apply Access Policy'. 4. Before the next timer event, change some field in the metadata that should not cause any update in the IdP connector object created above. 5. Next time the timer expires, notice that 'Apply Access Policy' still shows up, even though no IdP connector field was updated.
bugs.impact: 'Apply Access Policy' shows up when there was no update to the IdP connector or the SP-IdP connector join, which is misleading.

bugs.title: BWC priority groups cannot be shared across different BWC policies although the configuration allows it.
bugs.symptoms: BWC priority groups cannot be shared across different BWC policies, although the configuration allows it.
bugs.conditions: BWC categories are mapped in different BWC policies to a priority group.
bugs.impact: The system does not prevent the configuration, but the configuration has no effect. Configuration success is misleading.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system incorrectly allows clients through as part of SSL Client Certificate Authentication
bugs.symptoms: Under specific conditions, the BIG-IP system allows clients through (that otherwise should be rejected) as part of SSL Client Certificate Authentication.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the Trusted Certificate Authority specified in the Client-SSL profile is expired. Note: The client's certificate must be valid and trusted for the SSL handshake to continue. This issue purely deals with how the BIG-IP system treats the validity period of the signing Certificate Authority.
bugs.impact: F5 has reviewed this issue and has not classified it as a Vulnerability. However, F5 recognizes this issue may have a Security Exposure depending on how the BIG-IP system is utilized. Please observe that the issue here is not validation of the expiration time in the client's certificate. The issue here is handling of the expiration field in the certificate the BIG-IP system explicitly trusts, the so-called 'trust anchor'. In most cases, the trust anchor is a self-signed certificate. It is important to understand that the expiration field in trust anchors has no clear meaning, and even utilities such as OpenSSL historically treated this field in different ways. After completing its review, F5 has decided the correct and best behavior for the BIG-IP system is to reject the SSL handshake when the Trusted Certificate Authority has expired. The impact of this issue will vary greatly based on your deployment and type of business. In most cases, continuing to allow clients through past the validity of the Certificate Authority may be the behavior you expect or one that carries no negative consequences. However, if you obtained the Certificate Authority from a third party and expected the client certificates signed by that authority to stop working when its validity period expires, this will not happen because of this issue.
bugs.workaround: F5 recommends that you renew (or obtain renewed copies of) Certificate Authorities that are about to expire and that you want the BIG-IP system to continue trusting. F5 recommends that you remove from the BIG-IP system Certificate Authorities that are about to expire and that you do not plan to renew or continue trusting. This will ensure the BIG-IP system behaves optimally on versions affected by this issue.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly handles the validity period of Trusted Certificate Authorities used for SSL Client Certificate Authentication.

bugs.title: Cannot modify a newly created ASM policy within an iApp template implementation or TMSH CLI transaction
bugs.symptoms: Errors encountered - In TMSH CLI transaction: ---------------- transaction failed: 01020036:3: The requested ASM policy (/Common/<some_policy>) was not found. ---------------- In iApp template implementation: ---------------- script did not successfully complete: (01020036:3: The requested ASM policy (/Common/<some_policy>) was not found. ----------------
bugs.conditions: In an iApp template implementation or TMSH CLI transaction, create a new ASM policy and then try to modify it's active state.
bugs.impact: The policy is created but the modify action cannot find the policy.
bugs.workaround: iApps are built to work with ASM Policy Templates. A new ASM Policy Template can be created from the desired ASM Policy. That can be done via GUI and starting from from v13.0 via REST as well. Then, the newly created ASM Policy Template can be referenced in the iApp template implementation or TMSH CLI transaction as follows: ----------------- tmsh::create asm policy <some_policy> active policy-template NEWLY_CREATED_POLICY_TEMPLATE -----------------
bugs.fix: iApp template implementation and TMSH CLI transaction can now modify a newly created ASM policy.

bugs.title: 'Require consistent IP address' does not apply to some management GUI menu items
bugs.symptoms: The configuration setting 'System :: Preferences :: Require A Consistent Inbound IP For the Entire Web Session' ('sys http auth-pam-validate-ip' in tmsh) does not apply to some menu items, and acts as if the setting is enabled (that a consistent IP address is required) regardless of the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP administrator accesses the configuration utility from more than one source IP address, using the same session cookie.
bugs.impact: The 'sys http auth-pam-validate-ip' setting is ineffective on some menu items. These include ASM, AVR, and APM menu items.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the source IP address used when accessing the configuration utility does not change mid-session. This could happen if your management session is being load balanced across multiple HTTP proxies, for example.

bugs.title: New requests are not added to Request Log due to full disk partition
bugs.symptoms: New requests are not added to the Request Log due to full disk partition /var/asmdata1.
bugs.conditions: Disk partition /var/asmdata1 is completely filled.
bugs.impact: New requests are not added to Request Log.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you can safely delete all files under /var/asmdata1/request_log. Afterwards, kill the asmlogd process and allow it to restart automatically. Alternatively, ASM can be restarted.
bugs.fix: In cases where there is not enough free space on the filesystem, so a request will not be saved to Request Log, the system logs an error on failure. In addition, the system now detects and deletes unneeded files from /var/asmdata1 to reclaim some free disk space when the problem occurs.

bugs.title: F5 MIB value types changed to become RFC compliant
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP Version 12.1.2 several F5 MIB variables changed from 64-bit counter types to 32-bit gauge types. This change was made to make the MIBs RFC compliant. In a mixed environment, where some BIG-IPs are running 11.x and some running 12.x this can cause problems with the management station. If the management station cannot load MIBs dependent upon BIG-IP version then those variables can cause errors to be reported on the management station due to type mismatch.
bugs.conditions: An environment where a management station is managing BIG-IP systems with a mix of version 11.x and 12.x. The station may import a MIB version whose types do not match the MIBs on the BIG-IP system with regards to the type changes made in version 12.x.
bugs.impact: The management station reports errors due to type mismatch for some variables.

bugs.title: Introduce a user-input timeout to Vconsole
bugs.symptoms: Before this change, a user could idle a vconsole (telnet) connection to a guest, and that connection would remain active indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: A VCMP host administrator has connected to a guest using the vconsole program.
