bugs.workaround: In TMSH, after an upgrade to 13.0.0, run the following command: modify /ltm virtual-address /<partition>/<ip address> route-advertisement selective
bugs.fix: Route advertisement setting is now correctly upgraded.

bugs.title: Portal Access: handling of cssText property of CSSStyleSheet object has been corrected
bugs.symptoms: The cssText property of the CSSStyleSheet object is supported only by Internet Explorer 9 (IE9) or later. In other browsers this property is undefined. Testing of this property rises an error in Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox via Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when parsing JavaScript code similar to the following: var style = document.styleSheets[0]; if (style.cssText) { ... }
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Now the cssText property is handled correctly in all browsers via Portal Access.

bugs.title: Deleting an IKEv1 peer in current use could SEGV on race conditions.
bugs.symptoms: When either deleting a peer in IKEv1 or updating it, this problem causes the v1 racoon daemon to crash with a SIGSEGV under some race conditions, intermittently.
bugs.conditions: This requires a peer using IKEv1, which gets updated or deleted while the IKEv1 racoon daemon is performing operations related to this peer.
bugs.impact: If the problem occurs, the IKEv1 racoon daemon restarts and interrupts IPsec traffic.
bugs.fix: The system now checks whether the old peer definition is valid when navigating from phase-one SAs to the IKEv1 peer definition.

bugs.title: IKEv1 racoon daemon is not restarted when killed multiple times
bugs.symptoms: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels will fail and stay down indefinitely if the IKEv1 racoon daemon crashes. racoon does not get restarted by tmipsecd. This can occur if racoon has crashed more than once beforehand.
bugs.conditions: The IPsec IKEv1 racoon daemon crashes, or is killed manually, multiple times.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels cannot be established because the racoon daemon is dead. The user will receive no CLI or web UI clues to indicate that racoon is dead. Attempts to reconfigure IPsec while racoon is dead will not resolve the problem.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command to restart the IPsec IKEv1 racoon and tmipsecd daemons at the same time: tmsh restart sys service tmipsecd
bugs.fix: Fixed tmipsecd so it correctly tracks whether the IKEv1 racoon daemon is still running or needs a restart. This also covers odd timing, such as killing racoon right after it starts.

bugs.title: tmsh 'mv' command does not update the PostgreSQL database with new object name
bugs.symptoms: The 'tmsh mv' command causes an object to be momentarily removed from the 'tmm', but does not update the PostgreSQL database with the object's new name. This may cause issues when the configuration is reloaded. Note: The 'tmsh mv' command is not supported.
bugs.conditions: Issuing an 'tmsh mv' command to rename an object.
bugs.impact: PostgreSQL database is not updated with the object's new name. Potential issues when the configuration is reloaded.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the unsupported 'tmsh mv' command. You can rename an object using any of these methods: -- Using 'tmsh modify' commands. -- Running 'tmsh delete/create' commands. -- Through editing the configuration in the GUI. -- Executing REST API calls.

bugs.title: Some tmm/umem_usage_stat counters may be incorrect under memory pressure.
bugs.symptoms: After the BIG-IP system experiences severe memory pressure, the 'allocated' and 'max_allocated' counters from the tmm/umem_usage_stat table incorrectly show extremely high values.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system experiences enough memory pressure that slabs are transferred between threads.
bugs.impact: The 'allocated' and 'max_allocated' counters from the tmm/umem_usage_stat table do not reflect actual values. However, there is no functionality issue as a result. This is a cosmetic issue only.
bugs.fix: The system now manages better under memory pressure so that the tmm/umem_usage_stat counters correctly reflect actual values.

bugs.title: Safari 11 displays F5 EPI and F5 VPN launch confirmation dialogs twice
bugs.symptoms: Safari 11 displays confirmation dialogs to launch F5 EPI or F5 VPN app twice. Although functionality is not affected, the user experience might be confusing.
bugs.conditions: -- Safari 11, F5 EPI, or F5 VPN app installed. -- Endpoint check or VPN configured in access policy.
bugs.impact: None. The extra dialog box does not affect system functionality.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Confirmation dialog is now displayed only once.

bugs.title: No 'F5RST port in use' sent when new connection arrives to port in use with strict preserve.
bugs.symptoms: When 'Source Port: Preserve Strict' option is configured in performance L4 virtual servers, the 'F5RST port in use' packet is not sent, and connection hangs until timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- Connect to client and launch: # nc -p 8080 -v 10.10.10.40 80 -- Connect to client2 and launch: # nc -p 8080 -v 10.10.10.40 80 -- Modify virtual server vs_web type on LTM and repeat. When the virtual server is standard "F5RST port in use" is sent. When the virtual server is performance L4 is not.
bugs.impact: Connection hangs. No increase for port-in-use stats when using the following commands: tmsh show /net rst-cause.

bugs.title: ZebOS BGP peer-group configuration not fixed up on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: ZebOS BGP configuration failed to load from upgrade to 13.0.0.
bugs.conditions: When configuration specifies neighbor peer-group inside the address-family clause
bugs.impact: loading of ZebOS configuration after upgrade
bugs.workaround: Modify the ZebOS configuration to put the neighbor peer-group clause outside of the address-family clause
bugs.fix: The ZebOS configuration correctly orders the neighbor peer-group clause outside of the address-family clause, and loading of the BGP configuration after upgrade is successful.

bugs.title: HTTP 302 Redirect status text is HTTP-version dependent
bugs.symptoms: When using the HTTP::redirect iRule, it results in a response header beginning with the following string: HTTP/1.0 302 Found This could be considered non-RFC compliant, since the HTTP version is 1.0, but the status text is correct for HTTP/1.1. For strict RFC compliance -- HTTP/1.0 responses should specify status text 'Moved Temporarily' (RFC 1945 Section 9.3). -- HTTP/1.1 responses should specify 'Found' (RFC 7231 Section 6.4.3).
bugs.conditions: When using an iRule similar to the following HTTP::redirect redirect
bugs.impact: Clients should be relying upon the numeric HTTP status code, and not the status text that follows, so in theory, there should be no impact. However, those clients which use the status text for processing decisions must be ready to handle status text that doesn't match the specified HTTP version.
bugs.fix: HTTP::redirect status string is consistent for HTTP version.

bugs.title: after chassis failover: asmlogd CPU 100% on secondary
bugs.symptoms: After a failover in a chassis: - asmlogd CPU 0% on primary slot (which was secondary before the failover). - asmlogd CPU 100% on secondary (which was primary before the failover). Without traffic running through the chassis.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Chassis with at least two active slots. -- Chassis failover after some traffic was passed through the chassis.
bugs.impact: asmlogd CPU shows 100% on secondary (which was primary before the failover), and vice versa.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The asmlogd process now better handles chassis failovers during which the chassis slots change roles (primary/secondary), so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Incorrect alert details when XMLHttpRequest's timeout is smaller than timeout configured
bugs.symptoms: If XMLHttpRequest's timeout is less than the configured timeout, the system reports incorrect data in alerts.
bugs.conditions: Short timeout property in XMLHttpRequest's response.
bugs.impact: Wrong alert details.
bugs.fix: Alert details are no longer incorrect when XMLHttpRequest's timeout is smaller than the timeout configured.

bugs.title: BGP default-originate not announced to peers if several are peering over different VLANs
bugs.symptoms: BGP default-originate is not announced to peers if several are configured as peers over different VLANs.
bugs.conditions: -- default-originate is configured on four similar neighbors. -- The neighbors are reachable over different interfaces/subnets.
bugs.impact: Only some of the peered neighbors get the default route.
bugs.workaround: Add the following to the the BGP configuration: network 0.0.0.0/0
bugs.fix: All peered neighbors now get the default route.

bugs.title: Join FF02::2 multicast group when router-advertisement is configured
bugs.symptoms: MLD snooping switches may not deliver router solicitation packets to BIG-IP, which breaks BIG-IP's router advertisement functionality. MLD snooping switches may not deliver the packets because BIG-IP has not joined the FF02::2 multicast group.
bugs.conditions: router-advertisement configured, MLD snooping switches.
bugs.impact: IPv6 hosts never receive router advertisements from BIG-IP in response to their router solicitations.
bugs.workaround: Disable MLD snooping on switches.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now joins the FF02::2 multicast group when router-advertisements are configured.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP now joins the FF02::2 multicast group when router-advertisement is configured.

bugs.title: [APM] Usability: update tmsh error message to include access profile name
bugs.symptoms: The existing error message when deleting an access policy that is owned by an access profile is not descriptive: 01071111:3: Cannot delete access policy (/Common/delete_me_access_profile) because it is owned by a profile. It does not specify which profile owns the access policy.
bugs.conditions: When you try to delete an access policy owned by an access profile from tmsh using a command similar to the following: delete apm policy access-policy delete_me_access_profile
bugs.impact: This makes it difficult to debug, because the message does not state which access profile owns the access policy.
bugs.workaround: Manually check the access profiles to see which profile owns the access policy.
bugs.fix: The tmsh error message for deleting APM policy access-policy has been updated to include the name of the access profile that owns it.

bugs.title: In the GUI System :: High Availability : HA Groups edit page, pools created outside the Common partition cannot be modified
bugs.symptoms: In the HA Groups GUI edit page, only Pools created in the Common partition can be modified or deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- High Availability : HA Groups edit page. -- Pools created outside the Common partition.
bugs.impact: Devices must be paired to access HA Group configuration.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to modify or delete any non-Common pools attached to an HA Group.
bugs.fix: Now user can edit/delete non-Common pools in a preexisting HA Group.

bugs.title: After HA failover, subscriber data has stale session ID information
bugs.symptoms: After a failover in a high availability (HA) configuration, subscriber local data is populated with stale session id information
bugs.conditions: -- HA failover. -- PEM subscriber.
bugs.impact: Subscriber data with stale session ID information might cause invalid reference to incorrect subscriber data.
bugs.fix: Subscriber local data is now populated with new, generated session ID information.

bugs.title: Large volume of query result update to SessionDB fails and locks down ApmD
bugs.symptoms: While writing large query results from AD server to sessionDB using memcache API, write operation fails with partial write.
bugs.conditions: Large volumes of AD query (with Required 'All Attributes') results from AD server while writing to SessionDB.
bugs.impact: Operation fails with partial write. All worker threads performing authentication eventually gets locks down. Session watchdog thread eventually make a forced abort to recover from the situation. Apmd restarts in this situation.
bugs.workaround: Make query for specific attributes not the option 'All Attributes'.
bugs.fix: Partial write failure has been fixed, by writing remaining parts of the query results in several iterations, till the entire result is written.

bugs.title: GUI Unexpected changes to sFlow values when configuring using the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When configuring the sFlow values in the GUI, the value can unexpectedly change if you choose Default in the drop down.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuring an HTTP Profile, Interface, or VLAN with sFlow values. -- Select 'Default' from the drop down.
bugs.impact: The system might update the Global Settings value, which might cause confusion.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to independently update the sFlow values.
bugs.fix: The GUI now manages the sFlow values independently.

bugs.title: In SSL-O, TMM may core when SSL forward proxy cleanup certificate resources
bugs.symptoms: in SSL-O, due to race condition, TMM may core when SSL forward proxy tries to free up memory usage by releasing certificate resources.
bugs.conditions: This only happens in SSL-O with SSL forward proxy configured.
bugs.impact: TMM may restart due to using the wrong free function. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores under these conditions.

bugs.title: Slowness in IE when Removed Scripts Detection enabled
bugs.symptoms: Removed Scripts Detection feature can cause Microsoft Internet Explorer version 11 (IE11) slowness.
bugs.conditions: Enable Removed Scripts Detection and navigate to the protected page using IE11.
bugs.impact: IE11 browser is slow to display pages.

bugs.title: Encrypted field sometimes send the field value
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, in Microsoft Internet Explorer version 11 (IE11) mode 8, the encrypted parameter value sends only with the value, but without the name.
bugs.conditions: Using IE11 mode 8 with encrypted parameters.
bugs.impact: The application server will receive irrelevant data.
bugs.fix: Remove the name attribute of the encrypted field

bugs.title: WS::enabled returned empty string
bugs.symptoms: WS::enabled command returned empty string instead of 0 or 1 for status.
bugs.conditions: -- WS::enabled command is used to query the status of WebSocket processing. -- WebSocket and HTTP profiles are configured on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Unable to determine the status of WebSocket processing using iRule commands.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Invoke appropriate method via WebSocket Tcl code.

bugs.title: Potential memory leak if PEM Diameter sessions are not created successfully.
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak resulting in reduction in available memory.
bugs.conditions: 1. PEM configured with Gx. 2. PCRF Gx end point operationally DOWN 3. Subscriber creation attempt.
bugs.impact: Loss of service
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Diameter context is freed in case of a failed Diameter session creation.

bugs.title: Gx/Gy stats display provision pending sessions if there is no route to PCRF or the app is unlicensed
bugs.symptoms: If the PEM subscribers are brought up with diameter apps (Gx/Gy) configured and the PCRF is not reachable since there is no route or simply because there is no license configured for those apps. The Provision pending for sessions will get incremented and never rollback to zero even after the subscribers are cleaned up.
bugs.conditions: If the route to PCRF/OCS is missing or not reachable.
bugs.impact: Non-Zero stats for provision pending sessions
bugs.workaround: Disable the Gx/Gy profile if not required or configure the route.
bugs.fix: The system no longer increments the stats for diameter apps if the PCRF/OCS is not reachable, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: IPv6 prefix SPDAG causes packet drop
bugs.symptoms: If IPv6 prefix SPDAG is turned on, on systems running v12.1.2 HF1, v12.1.2 HF2, or 12.1.3, it can cause packet drops.
bugs.conditions: Turn on IPv6 prefix DAG. -- Assign a value other than 128 to sys db tmm.pem.session.ipv6.prefix.len. -- Running v12.1.2 HF1, v12.1.2 HF2, or 12.1.3.
bugs.impact: Packet drops.
bugs.workaround: Turn off IPv6 prefix SPDAG.

bugs.title: Portal Access produces incorrect Java bytecode when rewriting java.applet.AppletStub.getDocumentBase()
bugs.symptoms: Java applets containing call of getDocumentBase() through a reference to java.applet.AppletStub are incorrectly rewritten. Attempt to call incorrectly patched method causes following exception: java.lang.VerifyError: (...) Illegal type in constant pool
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using rewrite on Java applets that call getDocumentBase().
bugs.impact: Affected Java applets cannot be started through Portal Access.
bugs.fix: Rewritten applets with calls of java.applet.AppletStub interface methods are no longer causing java.lang.VerifyError exception during execution.

bugs.title: DNS:: namespace commands in procs cause upgrade failure when change from Link Controller license to other
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade fails with a message similar to the following. emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- 01070356:3: Link Controller feature not licensed. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Previously had Link Controller with DNS:: commands in an iRule proc.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: Remove DNS:: commands from procs before upgrade. Or use AFM instead of iRules.

bugs.title: Inconsistent behavior for virtual-address and selfip on the same ip-address
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistent ICMP/ARP behavior for self IP address or virtual-address when virtual-address and self IP address have the same IP address.
bugs.conditions: Virtual-address and self IP address have the same IP address. -- Virtual-address ICMP and ARP disabled.
bugs.impact: ICMP echo reply and ARP for the IP address might be inconsistent. Self IP address might override the ARP setting of a virtual address.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: This implements the initialization-order-independent set of rules of whether particular IP address should have ARP/ICMP enabled for multiple maching vaddrs. The lookup is performed from the most fine netmask to the most coarse netmask. If for particular netmask there is no maching vaddr then more coarse netmask is lookedup. Otherwise if any machnig vaddr for particular netmask have ARP/ICMP enabled then IP address will have ARP/ICMP enabled. If none of matching vaddrs for particular netmask have ARP/ICMP enabled the then IP address will have ARP/ICMP disabled. The rule above have one exception, due to the performance optimizations. If the vaddr have both ARP and ICMP disabled then the vaddr is considered deleted.

bugs.title: Using a multicast VXLAN tunnel without a proper route may cause a TMM crash.
bugs.symptoms: Using a multicast VXLAN tunnel without a proper route associated with the tunnel's local-address may cause a TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: When the following conditions are met: - No route is associated with the tunnel's local-address. - A selfip address is assigned to the tunnel. Then, a connection using the tunnel may cause a TMM crash. Note that the user can use the TMSH command "show net route lookup <address>" to check if there is a route associated with the tunnel's local-address.
bugs.impact: The TMM crashes and traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Make sure that there is a route associated with the tunnel's local-address, before using the tunnel.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes.

bugs.title: Do not print all HTTP headers to avoid printing user credentials to /var/log/apm.
bugs.symptoms: VDI debug logs print user credentials to /var/log/apm.
bugs.conditions: VDI debug logs are enabled and VDI functionality is used on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: User credentials are written to /var/log/apm.
bugs.workaround: Set VDI debug level to Notice.
bugs.fix: The system no longer prints user credentials to VDI debug logs.

bugs.title: Rare memory corruption in tmrouted while license is being reset
bugs.symptoms: tmrouted core due to memory corruption while license is being reset.
bugs.conditions: Rarely, when license file is being reset, tmrouted could core.
bugs.impact: restart of tmrouted daemon

bugs.title: LCD stuck at the loading spinner
bugs.symptoms: The LCD may become frozen at the loading spinner.
bugs.conditions: Occurs during the system start when the LCD is booting up.
bugs.impact: LCD display does not come up fully.

bugs.title: VPN tunnel cannot be established if allow local DNS is enabled and only one DNS is specified on client
bugs.symptoms: VPN tunnel cannot be established if 'allow local DNS' is enabled and only one DNS is specified on client on macOS High Sierra.
bugs.conditions: -- VPN tunnel. -- macOS High Sierra. -- Only one DNS configured (either manually or by DHCP) on client machine. -- Allow local DNS server configured in access policy.
bugs.impact: VPN tunnel cannot be established.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Configure two DNS servers. -- Disallow local DNS servers.

bugs.title: Avr reporting and analytics does not display statistics of many source regions
bugs.symptoms: 1. The network reporting does not show the statistics related to some Source Regions. 2. In the Security=>Reporting=>Network=>Enforced Rules dashboard are impossible to select or find some Source Region using filtering . For example, there are list of some missing Source Regions: France, Ile-de-France, Ukraine, Kyyiv,Russian Federation, Tambovskaya oblast, South Africa, Western Cape and Spain,Madrid
bugs.conditions: This occurs when attempting to filter on the affected source regions.
bugs.impact: The network reporting does not show the statistics related to some Source Regions.

bugs.title: Persistence record expires early if an error is returned for a BYE command
bugs.symptoms: When an error is returned for a SIP command, the persistence timeout is set to the transaction timeout.
bugs.conditions: An error is returned for a any SIP command.
bugs.impact: The persistence record will expire early when the call has not been ended.
bugs.fix: For BYE commands, the timeout is not set to transaction timeout on failure.

bugs.title: IKEv1 and IKEv2 cannot share common local address in tunnels
bugs.symptoms: When IKEv1 and IKEv2 IPsec tunnels are configured to use the same local IP address, either all the IKEv1 or all the IKEv2 tunnels will not establish. Note: This is as designed: the system does not support using the same local self IP to establish both IKEv1 and IKEv2 tunnels. However, the system does not prevent it, and there is no indication of the reason for the failure.
bugs.conditions: -- Use the same self IP as the local address of an IPsec tunnel for IKEv1, as well as the local address of a tunnel for IKEv2. -- Try to create competing listeners.
bugs.impact: Either the IKEv1 or IKEv2 tunnel will not work, because the listener for that tunnel fails to establish. Usually the IKEv1 tunnel will not work after tmm restart or BIG-IP reboot.
bugs.workaround: Use another self IP for the tunnel local address to keep IKEv1 and IKEv2 local tunnel addresses separate. Note: If IKEv1 tunnels use one local address, while IKEv2 tunnels use another, everything works as expected.
bugs.fix: Logging in /var/log/ltm now reveals failure to establish listener, along with a suggestion to avoid sharing one local address across IKEv1 and IKEv2 tunnels.

bugs.title: TMM may crash or LB::server returns unexpected result due to reused lb_result->pmbr[0]
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash or LB::server returns unexpected result.
bugs.conditions: GTM rule command LB::server is executed before a load balance decision is made or the decision is not to a real pool member.
bugs.impact: GTM rule command LB::server returns unexpected result. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: GTM rule command LB::server is now executed at the correct time, so TMM does not crash and LB::server returns expected results.

bugs.title: APMD may generate core file or appears locked up after APM configuration changed
bugs.symptoms: Right after clicking the 'Apply Access Policy' link, APMD may generate a core file and restart; or appears to be locked up.
bugs.conditions: -- Changing APM configuration, especially Per-Session and Per-Request Policy. -- Configured for AD or LDAP Auth Agent.
bugs.impact: If APMD restarts, then AAA service will be interrupted for a brief period of time. If APMD appears to be locked up, then AAA service will be stopped until manually restarted.
bugs.fix: APMD now processes the configuration changes correctly during 'modify apm profile access <profile name> generation-action increment' (TMSH) or 'Apply Access Policy' (GUI), and no service interruption occurs.

bugs.title: Inspection Host NPAPI Plugin for Safari can not be installed
bugs.symptoms: Inspection Host NPAPI Plugin for Safari on macOS High Sierra can not be installed.
bugs.conditions: macOS High Sierra, Inspection Host Plugin package installation triggered.
bugs.impact: Inspection Host plugin cannot be installed, therefore, endpoint checks will not work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Inspection Host NPAPI Plugin for Safari can now be installed successfully.

bugs.title: iQuery connections reset during SSL renegotiation
bugs.symptoms: Error in /var/log/gtm: err gtmd[14797]: 011ae0fa:3: iqmgmt_receive: SSL error: error:140940F5:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:unexpected record
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a system tries to send data over the iQuery connection while the two endpoints are performing SSL renegotiation. Note: iQuery connections automatically perform SSL renegotiation every 24 hours.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system is marked 'down' until the connection is reestablished. This usually takes no longer than one second. Note: This is a subtly different issue from the one (with a very similar error, 140940F5 virtual server 140940E5) described in ID 477240: iQuery connection resets every 24 hours :: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID477240.html (K16185: BIG-IP GTM iQuery connections may be reset during SSL key renegotiation :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K16185). This issue occurs even in versions where ID 477240 is fixed. There is no fix for this specific trigger of the same message. Note: The iQuery communication issue is fixed through ID 760471: GTM iQuery connections may be reset during SSL key renegotiation :: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID760471.html.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: ECP does not work for PFS in IKEv2 child SAs
bugs.symptoms: The original racoon2 code has no support for DH generate or compute using elliptic curve algorithms for (perfect forward security). Additionally, the original interfaces are synchronous, but the only ECP support present uses API with async organization and callbacks, so adding ECP does not work.
bugs.conditions: Changing an ike-peer definition from the default phase1-perfect-forward-secrecy value of modp1024 to something using ECP: ecp256, ecp384, or ecp512. Note: The first child SA is negotiated successfully.
bugs.impact: Once the first child SA expires (or is deleted), the IKEv2 tunnel goes down when another SA cannot be negotiated.
bugs.workaround: Use MODP for perfect-forward-secrecy instead of ECP.
bugs.fix: Full support for ECP as PFS has now been added, so a new child-SA negotiated in a IKEV2EXCH_CREATE_CHILD_SA exchange works as expected for ecp256, ecp384, and ecp512.

bugs.title: The policy builder is not getting updates about the newly added signatures.
bugs.symptoms: The policy builder is not getting updates about the newly added signatures.
bugs.conditions: When ASU is installed or user-defined signatures are added/updated.
bugs.impact: No learning suggestions for some of the newly added signatures.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- One workaround is restarting the policy builder. This will revert the learning progress made in the last 24 hours: killall -s SIGHUP pabnagd -- Manually change some Policy Attack Signature Set in Learning and Blocking Settings (e.g., disabling and re-enabling Learn checkbox).
bugs.fix: After the fix, Policy Builder will be aware of all newly added signatures.

bugs.title: Pool member port on AppIQ gives different number from port configured on the BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: Port numbers greater than 32767 are reported and displayed incorrectly on AppIQ.
bugs.conditions: Configure a port number that is greater than 32767.
bugs.impact: Ports are not displayed correctly on AppIQ. For example, port 60014 will be wrongly displayed as 4294961774

bugs.title: In routing module the 'sh ipv6 interface <interface> brief' command may not show header
bugs.symptoms: In the BIG-IP Advanced Routing module the 'sh ipv6 interface <interface> brief' command does not show header
bugs.conditions: - Advanced Routing module licensed and configured - From within imish shell, run the command 'sh ipv6 interface <interface> brief'.
bugs.impact: The header is not shown.
bugs.workaround: Run the equivalent command without indicating the interface: sh ipv6 interface brief
bugs.fix: The Advanced routing module 'sh ipv6 interface <interface> brief command now shows header.

bugs.title: MCPD Cores with SIGABRT
bugs.symptoms: MCPD cores with SIGABRT.
bugs.conditions: This occurs while the dynamic white/black daemon (dwbld) processes auto-blacklisted IP addresses.
bugs.impact: MCPD core.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command: tmsh modify sys db debug.afm.shun.notify_peers value disable
bugs.fix: MCPD no longer cores with SIGABRT if the auto-blacklisting feature is enabled.

bugs.title: User's timezone is not reflected when accessing Vmware Horizon desktop using Horizon HTML5 Client
bugs.symptoms: Target Horizon virtual desktop does not reflect the timezone of the client machine from which the user is connecting
bugs.conditions: User accesses a Horizon virtual desktop using Horizon HTML5 client
bugs.impact: Target View virtual desktop does not reflect the timezone of the client machine that is connecting to it. This causes confusion if the user's tizmeone differs from the timezone of the Horizon desktop.
bugs.fix: With VMWare Integration, the target Horizon virtual desktop now correctly reflects the timezone of the client machine from which the user is connecting.

bugs.title: AOM banner can appear after rebooting BIG-IP systems
bugs.symptoms: When performing multiple BIG-IP system reboots or host resets via the AOM menu, the AOM (BMC) device can become busy processing interrupts or other signals from the host and the AOM's IPMI main process will restart itself. As a result of this intermittent issue, you might encounter the following symptoms: 1. Showing the AOM Banner on the host serial console (if connected): --- Press <ESC>( for AOM Command Menu. 2. System Event Log entry in the '/var/log/sel' file: 0001 08/30/17 08:00:23 INF BMC boot marker. Note: It is normal to see a 'BMC boot marker' log entry if you power-cycle the device.
bugs.conditions: Perform multiple BIG-IP reboots or host resets via the AOM menu.
bugs.impact: Because this issue is intermittent, there is no way to predict the number of reboots required to expose the issue. It might appear after 10, 50, or 100 reboots, or you might not experience the issue regardless of the number of reboots. Note: If this situation occurs three times, the AOM will force a hard reset of itself by creating a watchdog timeout expiration.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround to this issue at this time.
bugs.fix: Improved handling of usb/scsi/hdisk commands when booting BIG-IP REL7 system have eliminated this issue.

bugs.title: User able to create node when an ephemeral with the same IP already exists
bugs.symptoms: If an FQDN ephemeral node exists for a given IP address, the user is still able to create a real node for the same IP address.
bugs.conditions: This can only be done by the GUI, not by tmsh or iControl REST.
bugs.impact: This should be prevented, but is allowed.
bugs.workaround: Avoid creating such a node.
bugs.fix: Validation now prevents this from happening.

bugs.title: LCD is unresponsive intermittently
bugs.symptoms: On tapping the LCD touchscreen, the screen lights up and the web page with the host IP address is displayed. However, the LCD is unresponsive to further taps and we cannot navigate through the LCD menu options. The 'LCD communication Error' critical alert is registered by alertd.
bugs.conditions: Exactly what condition gets the LCD to this state is still unknown. Investigations are underway on why/how the 'LCD communication Error' affect the system and LCD.
bugs.impact: The system cannot be configured using the LCD menu. It was reported that the traffic flow is not affected.

bugs.title: Change the default compression strategy to speed
bugs.symptoms: The current default compression.strategy is 'latency', which does not perform properly, i.e., the provider selection algorithm does not react to load change fast enough.
bugs.conditions: Using compression.strategy to distribute workload among hardware and software compression providers.
bugs.impact: The work load may not be distributed evenly among hardware and software compression providers when compression.strategy is 'latency'.
bugs.workaround: Modify the tmsh sys db variable compression.strategy to 'speed'.
bugs.fix: The default compression strategy is now set to 'speed'.

bugs.title: Add 'comp_req' to the output of 'tmctl compress'
bugs.symptoms: The output of 'tmctl compress' displays the total numbers of requests (tot_req), but does not distinguish between deflate (compression) requests and inflate (decompression) requests.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the output of the 'tmctl compress' command.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine the different types of requests.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release now distinguishes between deflate (compression) requests and inflate (decompression) requests, as follows: there is an indicator, 'comp_req', for compression requests. The number of decompression request is tot_req - comp_req.

bugs.title: Connections may fail when source-port=preserve-strict on the virtual, L4 mirroring is enabled and LSN pool/AFM dynamic-pat NAPT mode is configured with default DAG
bugs.symptoms: Connections may fail even when no colliding flows are present that use the same translation IP and port
bugs.conditions: Virtual server setting source-port=preserve-strict, L4 mirroring is enabled and LSN pool/AFM dynamic-pat NAPT mode is configured with default DAG
bugs.impact: Connections fail

bugs.title: bd core upon request, when profile has sensitive element configured.
bugs.symptoms: bd crash, system goes offline.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached on a virtual server. -- json profile configured with sensitive element.
bugs.impact: System goes offline/fails over.
bugs.workaround: Remove sensitive elements from the json profile in the ASM policy.
bugs.fix: ASM now handles this condition so the crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Device groups with no members will cause upgrade to fail
bugs.symptoms: An empty device group will fail upgrade with this error message: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip_base.conf at line: 37) "save-on-auto-sync" unexpected argument
bugs.conditions: This only affects systems with empty device groups.
bugs.impact: Configuration will fail to load after the upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Remove the empty device group before upgrading. An empty device group has no effect on the system, so this is a safe action to take.

bugs.title: i2000/i4000 Platforms Improperly Handle VLANs Created with a Value of '1'
bugs.symptoms: When an interface is associated with a VLAN whose tag value is '1', traffic is incorrectly sent out as untagged.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a VLAN with a tag value of '1'. 2. Associate an interface with the VLAN whose value is '1'. 3. Send traffic out that interface.
bugs.impact: Incorrect routing/switching of traffic.
bugs.workaround: Use VLANs with a tag value different from '1'.

bugs.title: LTM Policy applied to large number of virtual servers causes mcpd restart
bugs.symptoms: When a large policy (on the order of several dozen rules), is applied to a large number of virtual servers (on the order of hundreds), the mcpd process compiles the policy to an optimized, intermediate form for each virtual server. The compilation occurs in the mcpd process, and because it becomes so busy/non-responsive, a watchdog process intervenes and restarts the mcpd process.
bugs.conditions: -- Relatively large policy (~30 or more rules) applied to large number of virtual servers (~100 or more). -- Creating a draft of the policy that is currently applied to those virtual servers, when a similarly attached policy is published.
bugs.impact: The mcpd process becomes unresponsive and is reset by a watchdog process.
bugs.workaround: Two possible workarounds: -- Make copies of the policy and apply a different copy of policy to different subsets of virtual servers. -- Implement the policy using iRules.

bugs.title: Configuration sync failure involving self IP references
bugs.symptoms: Configuration sync fails, generating an error similar to the following: Caught configuration exception (0), Values (self-IP) specified for self IP (<name>): foreign key index (fw_enforced_policy_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database..
bugs.conditions: -- There is another object, such as a firewall policy, that references a self IP address. -- The self IP address is non-syncable; that is, its traffic group is set to 'traffic-group-local-only'.
bugs.impact: Sync operation fails.
bugs.workaround: Set the self IP address' traffic group to a value other than 'traffic-group-local-only', and then force a full load push from the first device.
bugs.fix: If a traffic group is non-syncable, modifying its traffic group to a syncable value (anything other than 'traffic-group-local-only') now causes the system to suggest synchronization.

bugs.title: Multidomain SSO infinite redirects from session ID parameters
bugs.symptoms: If an application uses a URL parameter of 'sid', 'sess', or 'S', the APM can enter an infinite redirect loop. In a packet capture, the policy completes on the auth virtual server. After policy completion, the client is redirected back to the resource virtual server. The resource virtual server cannot find the session, and redirects back to the auth virtual server. This begins the infinite loop of redirecting between resource and auth virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: Application with URL paramater containing 'sid', 'sess', or 'S' while using multidomain SSO.
bugs.impact: Applications that use 'sid', 'sess', or 'S' parameters cannot be fronted by an APM.
bugs.fix: Continue to lookup for token param to find session ID for multidomain SSO configuration even when the URI contains S/sess/sid query param to prevent infinite redirects.

bugs.title: Authorization header can cause a connection reset
bugs.symptoms: APM resets connections and reports an ERR_ARG from a simple web request.
bugs.conditions: -- APM profile with User Identification Method as HTTP. -- APM profile with User Identification Method as OauthToken. -- HTTP traffic arrives with certain types of Authorization headers.
bugs.impact: Connections are reset and APM logs ERR_ARG, which is not helpful for understanding the cause.
bugs.workaround: iRule workaround: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::header "Authorization"] contains "Bearer" && [string tolower [HTTP::header "User-Agent"]] contains "onenote" } { HTTP::header replace Authorization [string map {"Bearer" ""} [HTTP::header Authorization]] } }
bugs.fix: APM no longer resets connections and reports an ERR_ARG from a simple web request.

bugs.title: Connections may fail when iRule LSN::port is used, L4 mirroring is enabled and LSN pool/AFM dynamic-pat NAPT mode is configured with default DAG
bugs.symptoms: Connections may fail even when no colliding flows are present that use the same translation IP and port. /var/log/ltm contains tmm informational logs: "Requested Port busy"
bugs.conditions: LSN::port iRule command is used, L4 mirroring is enabled and LSN pool/AFM dynamic-pat NAPT modes is configured with default DAG.
bugs.impact: Connections fail, with log "Requested Port busy"
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Some requests or some request details may not be seen in exported request
bugs.symptoms: When you open an exported request is opened, you see a JavaScript error in the browser console, and some of the details are not visible, or the request itself is not visible at all.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while viewing an exported request when the request contains any illegal metacharacter violation.
bugs.impact: You are unable to view all the details for exported requests.

bugs.title: UIE persist may be inconsistent after a pool member is brought down
bugs.symptoms: For Universal Inspection Engine (UIE) persist, requests might be load balanced to different pool member after the original persisted pool member is brought down.
bugs.conditions: -- UIE persist. -- Original persisted pool member brought down.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent UIE persist.
bugs.fix: The system now provides consistent UIE persist after pool member down.

bugs.title: Weak Access Restrictions on the AVR Reporting Interface
bugs.symptoms: The AVR reporting interface does not follow best practices for access restrictions.
bugs.conditions: AVR provisioned
bugs.impact: If accessed the AVR reporting interface may disclose: - Client and server IP addresses - URIs from client requests - Metadata about attacks detected by BIG-IP
bugs.workaround: Ensure that network access to the management port is restricted and that Port Lockdown setting for Self-IPs is not set to "Allow All". The default port lockdown of "Allow Default" provides mitigation against access via Self-IP.
bugs.fix: Stronger access restrictions enforced on the AVR reporting interface.

bugs.title: When two BIG-IP virtual servers are configured with multi-domain SSO, under certain conditions user may encounter HTTP redirect loop.
bugs.symptoms: After successful authentication on the primary auth virtual, and and successful redirect to application virtual, the user may click the back button on the web browser which will re-request the multi-domain auth url. This may result in HTTP redirect loop.
bugs.conditions: When BIG-IP is configured with multi-domain authentication service for their web applications sitting behind LTM+APM virtual servers. APM multi-domain authentication service is configured with an access policy that does not contain a webtop and a "Primary Authentication URI" virtual server does not have an ltm pool assigned to it.
bugs.impact: User may encounter HTTP redirect loop
bugs.fix: User will not encounter HTTP redirect loops.

bugs.title: The iControl-REST timeout value is not configurable.
bugs.symptoms: Updating a large (75 KB or more records) data-group results in errors. This occurs because the communication between icrd_child and restjavad times out, and consequently the system raises errors. The default timeout is set to 60 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl Rest to update a data-group that contains 75 KB or more records.
bugs.impact: The operation times out and there is no way to configure the iControl Rest timeout value.
bugs.workaround: Options have been added to two config files to alter the timeouts of restjavad and iControl Rest. -- The config file for restjavad is /etc/rest.common.properties. The value that needs to be changed is 'rest.java.socket.timeout'. -- The file for iControlRest is /etc/icrd.conf. The value that needs to be changed is 'socketIdleSeconds'.
bugs.fix: The iControl-REST timeout value is now configurable. Options have been added to two config files to alter the timeouts of restjavad and iControl Rest. -- The config file for restjavad is /etc/rest.common.properties. The value that needs to be changed is 'rest.java.socket.timeout'. -- The file for iControlRest is /etc/icrd.conf. The value that needs to be changed is 'socketIdleSeconds'.

bugs.title: Unable to ping self IP of VCMP guest configured on i5000, i7000, or i10000
bugs.symptoms: Unable to the ping self IP of VCMP guests configured on i5000, i7000, or i10000.
bugs.conditions: Running TMOS v12.1.3 and VCMP guests configured on i5000, i7000 or i10000.
bugs.impact: Unable to process client traffic.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed.

bugs.title: False negative selenium is not detected in firefox browser
bugs.symptoms: Selenium is not detected in firefox browser by pbd.
bugs.conditions: PBD is enabled. Running selenium on firefox browser.
bugs.impact: False negative selenium is not blocked in firefox browser.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Better detect selenium on firefox.

bugs.title: IP ToS/QoS is not preserved in chained Virtual Servers when the second Virtual Server is FastL4.
bugs.symptoms: IP Type of Service (ToS) and/or Quality of Service (QoS) set by the server is not received by the client through the BIG-IP system when the BIG-IP system has two Virtual Servers chained together.
bugs.conditions: Two Virtual Servers in a chain with the second Virtual Server being a forwarding/performance (i.e., FastL4) rather than a Standard Virtual Server. IP ToS/QoS desired to be preserved from server to client.
bugs.impact: Client does not receive IP ToS/QoS from server via the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Change the second Virtual Server type to Standard with a TCP profile which has ToS/QoS set to Pass Through.

bugs.title: zxfrd core during transfer while network failure and DNS server removed from DNS zone config
bugs.symptoms: zxfrd cores and restarts.
bugs.conditions: While zone transfer is in progress, the network fails and the DNS server is removed from the DNS zone configuration.
bugs.impact: zxfrd cores.
bugs.fix: zxfrd no longer cores during transfer while network failure and DNS server removed from DNS zone config.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when serverssl cannot provide certificate to backend server.
bugs.symptoms: TMM halts and restarts when server SSL cannot provide a certificate to the backend server.
bugs.conditions: -- The backend server is configured to require a client certificate to complete the SSL handshake. -- The server SSL profile is not configured with a client certificate.
bugs.impact: TMM halts and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer halts and restarts when server SSL cannot provide a certificate to the backend server.

bugs.title: md5sum check on BMC firmware fails
bugs.symptoms: Checking the md5 sum of BMC firmware fails when issuing the command 'md5sum -c /usr/firmware/shuttle_x.x.xx.ima_enc.md5'. The command fails with the following message: (...) listed file could not be read".
bugs.conditions: iSeries appliances: - i2000 - i4000 - i5000 - i7000 - i10000 - i15000
bugs.impact: 'md5sum -c' does not work for BMC firmware checksums.
bugs.workaround: Indirectly check the md5sum by calculating it with 'md5sum /usr/firmware/shuttle*.ima_enc' and comparing it to 'cat /usr/firmware/shuttle*.ima_enc.md5'. Or use this command: diff -sy <(md5sum < /usr/firmware/shuttle*.ima_enc | awk '{ print $1 }') <(cat /usr/firmware/shuttle*.ima_enc.md5 | awk '{ print $1 }')
bugs.fix: Fixed 'md5sum -c' not working for BMC firmware checksums.

bugs.title: SWG-Explicit rejects large POST bodies during policy evaluation
bugs.symptoms: When an access profile of type SWG-Explicit is being used, there is a 64 KB limit on POST bodies while the policy is being evaluated. ==> /var/log/apm <== err tmm[13751]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: hud_access_process_ingress, Line: 3048
bugs.conditions: This applies only during the policy evaluation. After the policy has been set to 'Allow', there is no limit.
bugs.impact: Unable to start an SWG-Explicit policy with a large POST body.
bugs.fix: Modify the db variable 'tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize' with a value larger than the maximum post body size you would like to support. The maximum supported value is 25000000 (25 MB).

bugs.title: HA mirroring for flows without autolasthop cause a crash on the standby
bugs.symptoms: There is a tmm crash on a standby unit in a high availability (HA) configuration when fastL4 mirroring is configured and autolasthop is disabled.
bugs.conditions: FastL4 mirroring for flows without a lasthop, i.e. disabled autolasthop on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts on a standby device. No traffic is disrupted while tmm restarts on a standby device.
bugs.workaround: Enable autolasthop.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer restarts on a standby when fastL4 mirroring is configured and autolasthop is disabled.

bugs.title: f5.http iApp cannot add nodes with names containing four or fewer characters
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to deploy the f5.http iApp with node names of four or fewer characters that might already be used in other parts of the config.
bugs.conditions: Node name is short: four or fewer characters.
bugs.impact: iApp posts an error and does not deploy.
bugs.workaround: The bug is in uncompiled tcl code. The suggested workaround is to implement the fix. Edit /usr/share/tcl8.5/iapp/iapp*.tcl, and replace the 4 lines following the comment "# Detect a CIDR mask and pull it off the addr string" with these 5 lines: if { [regexp {/[0-9][0-9]?[0-9]?$} $addr] == 1 } { set loc [string first {/} $addr] set cidr_bits [string range $addr [expr {$loc + 1}] end] set addr [string range $addr 0 [expr {$loc - 1}]] }
bugs.fix: In this release, iApps now support very short node names (fewer than five characters).

bugs.title: Unable to force Bot Defense action to captcha_challenge in iRule for Suspicious Browsers
bugs.symptoms: When a request is being blocked (tcp_rst) due to being a suspicious browser, the action cannot be forced to captcha_challenge in the iRule.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a tcp_rst bot defense action is triggered on a suspicious browser, and you want to change the action to captcha_challenge.
bugs.impact: The bot defense action cannot be forced to 'captcha_challenge'. The TCP RST will still be sent.
bugs.workaround: Change the dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop db variable so that all suspicious browsers will be responded with the CAPTCHA challenge instead of getting blocked. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop value 999 Then, you can selectively block requests using the 'BOTDEFENSE::action tcp_rst' command in selected conditions.
bugs.fix: It is now possible to use BOTDEFENSE iRules to change the action of a Suspicious Browser from tcp_rst to captcha_challenge.

bugs.title: HTTP2 headers frame decoding may fail when the frame delivered in multiple xfrags
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently, HTTP2 experiences protocol resets.
bugs.conditions: -- xfrag is 2 bytes in length. -- The header length is greater than 128. -- xfrag starts. For example, the following returns the incorrect header length: (0xFF BYTE1) next byte, http2_arbint_read.
bugs.impact: Unexpected loss of HTTP2 frames due to protocol resets.
bugs.workaround: No effective workaround.
bugs.fix: HTTP2 now parses the request, regardless of its xfrags distribution.

bugs.title: FPS may introduce latency even for unprotected pages
bugs.symptoms: Depending on TCP profile parameters, FPS may introduce latency even for unprotected pages due to re-chunking of response. The latency introduction may arise when re-chunking causes a small TCP segment that the BIG-IP system's TCP stack or upstream device chooses to buffer (for example, due to Nagle's algorithm)
bugs.conditions: 1. FPS attached to virtual server. 2. TCP profile parameters (Nagle's Algorithm, MSS, etc.). 3. Chunked response from server.
bugs.impact: FPS unprotected pages may suffer 10's to 100's ms latency
bugs.workaround: Experience shows that disabling Nagle's Algorithm (for example) might overcome FPS latency, but it should be noted that this sort of mitigation should be carefully examined as it is influenced by many parameters (traffic patterns, other TCP profile parameters, SSL profile, etc.).

bugs.title: Change Captcha to be more flexible and dynamic
bugs.symptoms: The captcha image is limited to 6 characters, which must be digits or alphanumeric characters, and is case insensitive.
bugs.conditions: This is related to the captcha functionality.
bugs.impact: Limited flexibility configuring captcha.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: New Captcha image capture settings have been added.
bugs.behavior: New Captcha image capture settings have been added.

bugs.title: Brute force sourced based mitigation is not working as expected
bugs.symptoms: Brute force mitigations are not working by the configured order under some conditions - for example a captcha is arriving instead of a drop.
bugs.conditions: -- Brute force is configured. -- There is more than one source (for example, User and IP address).
bugs.impact: The incorrect mitigation is received.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with brute force mitigations.

bugs.title: f5optics should not show function name in non-debug log messages
bugs.symptoms: For logging thresholds other than debug, the function name appears in log messages created by f5optics.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP is running. -- Logging thresholds is set to a value other than debug.
bugs.impact: Log files contain unexpected data.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: With the fix, f5optics is not displaying function names in non-debug logging messages.

bugs.title: Under unknown circumstances sometimes a sessionDB subkey entry becomes corrupted
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a subkey that has master_record field set to true.
bugs.conditions: The specific conditions under which this occurs are not known.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Although the issue is not known, the system now handles the situation without necessarily restarting tmm.

bugs.title: "MCP Message:" seen on boot up with Best License
bugs.symptoms: This message can be seen in /var/log/tmm notice MCP message handling failed in 0x7aa640 (16973843): Aug 28 12:41:02 - MCP Message:
bugs.conditions: This occurs when booting BIG-IP that has a Best license applied.
bugs.impact: This message can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: Ignore message
bugs.fix: With fix, message goes away

bugs.title: Using iRule HTTP::redirect or HTTP::respond inside HTTP_REQUEST causes connection reset.
bugs.symptoms: When trying to run HTTP::redirect or HTTP::respond inside an HTTP_REQUEST event in which the destination host name is used (instead of an IP address), the HTTP connection is incorrectly reset.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule statement HTTP::redirect inside HTTP_REQUEST event. -- Use DNS name server to resolve the host name.
bugs.impact: HTTP connection is unexpectedly reset.
bugs.fix: Using HTTP::redirect or HTTP::respond inside HTTP_REQUEST event no longer causes a reset.

bugs.title: Support for Thales Security World version 12.40.2
bugs.symptoms: Support for Thales NetHSM client software "Thales Security World version 12.40.2".
bugs.conditions: Thales NetHSM client software "Security World version 12.40.2" is supported from BIG-IP release 14.1.0 onwards.
bugs.impact: Releases prior to BIG-IP version 14.1.0 do not support NetHSM client software "Thales Security World version 12.40.2".
bugs.workaround: Use BIG-IP release version 14.1.0 and above.
bugs.fix: Thales NetHSM client software "Thales Security World version 12.40.2" is supported from BIG-IP release 14.1.0 onwards.

bugs.title: The POP3 monitor used to send STAT command on v10.x, but now sends LIST command
bugs.symptoms: in BIG-IP version 10.x, the POP3 monitor sent STAT command (which returned a count of messages in the mailbox). Now, the monitor sends the LIST command (which returns a list of messages and their sizes).
bugs.conditions: POP3 monitor set up on a mailbox.
bugs.impact: If the polled mailbox used in the monitoring has a huge amount of messages, the STAT command might fail to return results in time.
bugs.workaround: 1. Create a mail account that does not receive many emails. 2. Make sure that the mailbox is nearly empty all the time (copy /dev/null periodically to the mailbox file).

bugs.title: DHCP Trace log incorrectly marked as an Error log.
bugs.symptoms: The following sample DHCP debug log may be found repeatedly in the TMM logs. <#> <date> <slot#> notice DHCP:dhcpv4_xh_timer_callback/1053: Entering: <mac-addr>
bugs.conditions: Send a DHCP request through a DHCP virtual and wait for 30 seconds for the DHCP callback to trigger.
bugs.impact: Possible clutter in the TMM logs.
bugs.workaround: Set the db variable to critical. To do so, run the following command: setdb tmm.dhcp.log.level critical
bugs.fix: The following log can be seen only when DHCP debug logs are set to enabled. <#> <date> <slot#> notice DHCP:dhcpv4_xh_timer_callback/1053: Entering: <mac-addr>

bugs.title: max-request enforcement no longer works outside of OneConnect
bugs.symptoms: max-request enforcement does not work when OneConnect is not configured.
bugs.conditions: -- The max-request enforcement option is configured. -- OneConnect is not configured.
bugs.impact: max-request enforcement does not work.
bugs.workaround: Always use OneConnect.
bugs.fix: max-request enforcement now works when OneConnect is not configured.

bugs.title: TMM restart due to delayed keep alives
bugs.symptoms: TMM killed with SIGABRT by the SOD process that monitors all process's health. TMM misses the keep alive, hence the restart. The stack trace shows that tmm was killed when it was waiting on a memory map (sys_mmap_obj) call.
bugs.conditions: The memory map call is known to take a long time to complete when the disk IO sub-system is very slow. High IO can also be a result of memory starvation accompanied by intensive paging
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: This problem is not likely to persist after a TMM service restart. So no user intervention is required. If this problem happens repeatedly, it would be required to take a look at IO Resources in use at time of the database load or reload, and see if a way to lower IO can be found.

bugs.title: qkview may not collect all data if there are deleted files in the filestore
bugs.symptoms: If files linked in /config/filestore/files_d/ are deleted or moved elsewhere in the filesystem, this will cause an error in mcpd, which will then cause qkview to abort collecting data from mcpd even if it has not finished.
bugs.conditions: files linked in /config/filestore/files_d/ are deleted or moved elsewhere in the filesystem
bugs.impact: Some data in the MCP database will be missing from qkview.
bugs.fix: qkview mcp module has been changed so that it will report errors from mcpd, but will continue processing.

bugs.title: IKEv2 able to fail assert for GETSPI_DONE when phase-one SA appears not to be initiator
bugs.symptoms: A tmm restart and corefile can occur in rare cases while negotiating an IKEv2 IPsec tunnel. A child_sa managed to process GETSPI_DONE once in the IDLING state, where the ike_sa was expected to be the initiator, but it appeared not to be -- failing an assert.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP is negotiating an IPsec tunnel as the Initiator, but an unexpected state change associated with being the Responder occurs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM will no longer restart due to assertion failure.

bugs.title: Reported Virtual Server CPU usage stats are slightly higher than actual
bugs.symptoms: The average CPU usage percentage reported per LTM Virtual Server is slightly higher than actual percentage of system CPU cycles used by each Virtual Server. The average CPU usage percentage per LTM Virtual Server is reported by the 'tmsh show ltm virtual' and 'tmctl virtual_server_cpu_stat' commands and in the GUI under Statistics :: Module Statistics : Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers. The average CPU usage values reported by these commands incorrectly include TMM Idle cycles in the calculations, which causes a slight over-reporting of average per-Virtual-Server CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when LTM Virtual Server CPU usage stats are observed via the 'tmsh show ltm virtual' or 'tmctl virtual_server_cpu_stat' commands or in the GUI under Statistics :: Module Statistics : Local Traffic :: Virtual Servers.
bugs.impact: Each LTM Virtual Server may appear to be using a greater percentage of system CPU cycles than they actually use.
bugs.workaround: Note: The values reported for 'tm_total_cycles' and 'tm_idle_cycles' represent a total value applied across the entire system: i.e., these are global values. The output from 'tmsh show ltm virtual', 'tmctl virtual_server_cpu_stat', or via the GUI report individual statistics for each virtual server. If you have multiple virtual servers, each with varying degrees of usage, you cannot use this workaround extract the per-virtual server information from a global stat. In the interest of extracting the information for a single virtual server, the following process might be useful. To determine the over-reporting value of the per-Virtual-Server CPU usage percentage ===================================== The instantaneous running count of TMM Idle cycles is displayed in the 'tm_idle_cycles' column displayed by the 'tmctl tmm_stat' command. You can compare this value to the 'tm_total_cycles' column to gain a general sense of the scale of the error. For a meaningful comparison of these values with the per-Virtual-Server CPU usage statistics (such as the 'avg_5sec' value reported by 'tmctl virtual_server_cpu_stat' or the 'Last 5 Seconds' value reported by 'tmsh show ltm virtual'), run the 'tmctl tmm_stat' command at intervals, such as every 5 seconds, and use the incremental changes in the 'tm_idle_cycles' and 'tm_total_cycles' values to estimate the degree to which the per-Virtual-Server CPU usage percentage is over-reported.

bugs.title: Setting zxfrd log level to debug can cause AXFR and/or IXFR failures due to high CPU and disk usage.
bugs.symptoms: Enabling debug logging on zxfrd (DNSX) can result in excessive CPU and disk usage, as well as errors during DNS AXFR or IXFR processing.
bugs.conditions: log.zxfrd.level is set to debug by running the following command: tmsh modify sys db log.zxfrd.level value debug
bugs.impact: IXFRs or AXFRs may fail and be rescheduled due to high CPU usage by zxfrd, which causes it to fail to process data packets during a transfer.
bugs.workaround: To avoid this issue, do not set log.zxfrd.level to debug.
bugs.fix: With this change, the dump to /var/tmp/zxfrd.out occurs only when a new db variable, dnsexpress.dumpastext, is set to true. This enables turning on logging for debug without consuming all the CPU and disk necessary to dump packets and zone contents. Note: Setting this value to true will cause the information to be dumped to stderr, which reveals the original issue, potentially causing transfer failures and high system resource usage. F5 recommends that you enable it only when directed to do so by F5 support staff.
bugs.behavior: Previously, setting the zxfrd log level to debug caused all AXFR and IXFR requests and responses to be logged to /var/tmp/zxfrd.out. Doing so also caused the contents of all zones to be dumped, as text, to /var/tmp/zxfrd.out when the database was saved. This was extremely CPU-, memory-, and disk-intensive. The CPU load could cause zxfrd to fail to process transfer data packets in a timely fashion, which could cause the master DNS server to close the connection. With this fix, setting log.zxfrd.level debug no longer outputs this information. Although it is not generally useful to output the contents of the transfer packets or the contents of the database, if this information is required for troubleshooting or information-verification purposes, you can set the new db variable: dnsexpress.dumpastext. Note: Setting this value to true will cause the information to be dumped to stderr, which reveals the original issue, potentially causing transfer failures and high system resource usage. F5 recommends that you enable it only when directed to do so by F5 support staff.

bugs.title: Safari 11 sometimes start more than one session
bugs.symptoms: In Safari 11 after session is finished and being restarted by "Click here to establish a new session" more than one session appears. It looks like Safari 11 beta and release bug.
bugs.conditions: Safari 11 beta and official release Policy with webtop Several passes from start to finish
bugs.impact: At certain point browser is reaching max sessions per IP and hangs on webtop.

bugs.title: IPsec config via REST scripts may require post-definition touch of both policy and traffic selector
bugs.symptoms: A new IPsec tunnel may not work after being configured over REST. While the configuration is correct, a log message similar to the following may appear in ipsec.log (IKEv2 example): info tmm[24203]: 017c0000 [0.0] [IKE] [INTERNAL_ERR]: selector index (/Common/Peer_172.16.4.1) does not have corresponding policy
bugs.conditions: A new IPsec tunnel is configured over REST.
bugs.impact: The newly configured IPsec tunnel does not start.
bugs.workaround: The following methods cause the traffic-selector and ipsec-policy to be correctly related to one another: -- Restart tmm. -- Change the configuration, for example the Description field, of both the policy and the traffic selector. This may also be done using REST.
bugs.fix: A traffic selector can no longer use a deleted policy by name, and if recreated after deletion, the policy is correctly constructed.

bugs.title: Edge client may try to reconnect even when session authentication fails due to policy violation
bugs.symptoms: Edge client on Microsoft Windows immediately attempts to reconnect if access policy ends in Deny ending.
bugs.conditions: -- Using Edge Client running on Windows. -- Access policy ends in Deny.
bugs.impact: Edge Client intermittently retries a new connection when logon is denied by policy violation instead of the reporting the policy violation.

bugs.title: Invalid monitor rule instance identifier
bugs.symptoms: iApp triggers an error while attempting to change server properties for pool members. The error reads "Invalid monitor rule instance identifier"
bugs.conditions: While changing the server properties associated with the pool members through iApp.
bugs.impact: Will not be able to change the server properties using iApp.

bugs.title: ePVA statistics are unrealistically high
bugs.symptoms: The embedded Packet Velocity Acceleration (ePVA) statistics are showing extremely high throughput and pps (much higher than the sum of all external interfaces). A relatively high amount of epva_connstat tot.snoop_dynamic is observed in comparison to other types of offloading.
bugs.conditions: Hardware traffic acceleration is activated.
bugs.impact: Some stats in the tmstat tables are incorrect, but these stats are primarily used for diagnostic purposes.
bugs.workaround: There is no good workaround for the stats issue.

bugs.title: mcpd emits an error message upon load when DER certificates are used
bugs.symptoms: mcpd may generate an error message of this format: 0107147f:3: Could not read certificate file (/Common/filename.crt).
bugs.conditions: Happens at load time when the configuration contains certificate file objects that were in DER format when they were imported.
bugs.impact: The error message is emitted, and the certificates are not verified, but the configuration loads successfully.
bugs.workaround: Use the PEM format instead of DER. This is more common, and the default in OpenSSL.
bugs.fix: Certificates in the DER format are now handled successfully.

bugs.title: Hidden newlines within monitor parameters may silently load without error
bugs.symptoms: Monitor parameters containing hidden newlines may silently load without error, when the configuration should fail to load. A conforming configuration requires each monitor parameter to comprise a single line; but manually editing the configuration file may insert a line-break within a single monitor parameter, thus breaking the parameter across two lines (resulting in a non-conforming definition). If the first line has an odd number of double-quotes (regardless of the presence of backslash-escaping), the hidden newline will not be detected and the monitor will load successfully.
bugs.conditions: A configuration file where a single monitor parameter is broken across two text lines (such as after manually editing the text file), and where the first line has an odd-number of double-quotes (regardless of the presence of backslash-escaping). For example, an improper text line break within a single monitor configuration that silently loads: 'send "GET http://path={\"checkDatabase\":\"true\"}<CR>\r\n"' ...where "<CR>" represents the hidden line break in the text file. This silently loads because the odd-number of double-quotes on the first line (before the <CR>) hides the newline in the text file, resulting in the first line being merged with the second line upon configuration load.
bugs.impact: The configuration loads successfully, when it should be rejected as non-conforming. The monitor will function normally, as the two lines separated by the hidden newline will be merged upon load. The configuration will behave correctly, even though the hidden line break implies the file is non-conforming.
bugs.workaround: Modify the configuration file so that each monitor parameter comprises a single text line (which is required for a conforming configuration).

bugs.title: Large configurations can cause memory exhaustion during live-install
bugs.symptoms: system memory can be exhausted and the kernel will kill processes as a result.
bugs.conditions: During live-install, if configuration roll-forward is enabled, and the compressed configuration size is of a similar order of magnitude as total system memory.
bugs.impact: The kernel will kill any number of processes; any/all critical applications could become non-functional.
bugs.workaround: Make sure there are no un-intended large files included in the configuration. Any file stored under /config is considered part of the configuration. If the configuration is, as intended, on the same order of magnitude as total system memory, do not roll it forward as part of live install. Instead, save it manually and restore it after rebooting to the new software. to turn off config roll forward; setdb liveinstall.saveconfig disable to save/restore configuration manually; see https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13132

bugs.title: 'Referer' is not masked when 'Query String' contains sensitive parameter
bugs.symptoms: While 'Query String' contains masked sensitive parameter value the 'Referer' header sensitive parameter value is exposed.
bugs.conditions: -- Sensitive parameter is defined in: 'Security :: Application Security : Parameters : Sensitive Parameters'. -- 'Query String' contains the defined sensitive parameter.
bugs.impact: "Referer" header contains unmasked value of the sensitive parameter.
bugs.workaround: Enable 'Mask Value in Logs' in: 'Security :: Application Security : Headers : HTTP Headers :: referer'.
bugs.fix: The 'Referer' header value is masked in case of sensitive parameter in 'Query String'.

bugs.title: NAT66 may fail if configured with a single translation address
bugs.symptoms: When the number of addresses configured on an lsn-pool or source-translation object is fewer than the number of tmms in the system, there a chance for the outbound connection's translation to fail.
bugs.conditions: NAT66 configured with a single translation address configured in the lsn-pool or source-translation object.
bugs.impact: Sub-optimal performance. May cause functional/validation tests to fail.
bugs.workaround: Configure at least as many translation addresses on your lsn-pool or source-translation object as there are tmms on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: NAT66 translations no longer fails when only a single translation address is configured.

bugs.title: Running tmsh show commands may cause mcpd memory leak
bugs.symptoms: mcpd memory utilization increases.
bugs.conditions: Periodically running tmsh show commands.
bugs.impact: Might cause mcpd memory leak, which might causes mcpd to restart, ultimately.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a memory leak when running tmsh show commands.

bugs.title: BD crash in a specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: BD crash occurs.
bugs.conditions: A specific, non-default configuration with specific traffic. The issue is much more likely to occur when the policy is not tuned correctly, in which case you might receive a potentially huge number of false positive attack signature matches on that payload. The crash might then occur if there is a subsequent 'Parameter value does not comply with regular expression' violation on that same payload. For example, nothing prevents you from incorrectly associating a Content-Type and <type-value> with a Request Body Handling parser that is not designed to parse that type of data, such as the following: Content-Type :: *xml* :: form-data This configuration is likely to result in a very long list of false-positive attack signatures. Because of the big message generated, The regex violation which is also likely to happen on the payload cannot be added to the filled message, which causes the crash.
bugs.impact: Failover, traffic disturbance.
bugs.workaround: In order to prevent this, correctly configure the header-based-content-profile property on URLs for cases where an unusual header requires a specific, potentially unexpected parsing mechanism. A correctly configured header-based-content-profile property on URLs appears as follows: In URL Properties, the Header-Based Content Profiles section of the wildcard URL is by default applying the value and content signature. Here, you can associate Content-Type with <type-value> with <parser-type>. By default, the correct definitions are as follows: Content-Type :: *form* :: Form Data Content-Type :: *json* :: JSON Content-Type :: *xml* :: XML
bugs.fix: Added a check to prevent a crash in a specific scenario.

bugs.title: TMM may crash during routing updates
bugs.symptoms: When dynamic routing is configured and ECMP routes are received, certain routing updates may lead to a TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing. -- ECMP routes.
