bugs.fix: The following list defines which log IDs are associated with which functional area in AFM: -- NETWORK_ACL = 23003137; -- DOS_NETWORK = 23003138; -- PROTOCOL_DNS = 23003139; -- DOS_APPLICATION = 23003140; -- DOS_PROTOCOL_DNS = 23003141; -- IP_INTELLIGENCE = 23003142; -- IPS_LOG = 27590657; -- //23003143 is not being used -- TRAFFIC_FLOW_STATS = 23003155; -- TRAFFIC_SYNCOOKIE_STATS = 23003156; -- THROTTLED_MESSAGES = 23003154; -- PROTOCOL_SIP = 23003144; -- DOS_PROTOCOL_SIP = 23003145; -- PROTOCOL_HTTP = 23003146; -- PEM_LOG = 24182785; -- CONFIG_CHANGE_LOG= 23003158; -- PORT_MISUSE_LOG = 23003157; -- RTBH_LOG = 23003163; -- SHUN_LOG = 23003159; -- NAT_LOG = 23003161; -- NAT_ERR_LOG = 23003162; -- NAT_PB_LOG = 23003168; -- DOS_THRESHOLD = 23003160; -- DYNAMIC_SIGNATURES = 23003173; -- BOTDEFENSE_REQUESTS = 23003147; -- SCRUBBER_LOG = 23003172; -- CLASSIFICATION_LOG = 27656193; -- PROTOCOL_SSH_AUTH = 23003164; -- PROTOCOL_SSH_ACTION = 23003165; -- PROTOCOL_SSH_TRAFFIC = 23003167; -- PROTOCOL_SSH_EVENTS = 23003166;

bugs.title: Error messages in Google Compute Engine that gateway is not in a connected network
bugs.symptoms: When running Virtual Edition (VE) in Google Compute Engine, some log messages are emitted of the form: -- err mcpd[31409]: 01071a95:3: Admin IP (10.128.0.5/255.255.255.255): Gateway (::) for management route (/Common/dhclient_route1) is not in a connected network. -- err mcpd[31409]: 01071a95:3: Admin IP (10.128.0.5/255.255.255.255): Gateway (10.128.0.1) for management route (/Common/default) is not in a connected network. These messages are benign and can be ignored.
bugs.conditions: -- Deploy BIG-IP VE in Google Compute Engine. -- Look at /var/log/ltm for the time period during startup.
bugs.impact: Spurious log messages.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: These log messages are no longer emitted.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition GTM DNS Query Performance Degradation
bugs.symptoms: The transaction rate for a DNS A record request synthetic test was up to fourteen percent lower for the BIG-IP Virtual Edition Release 13.1.0 compared to Release 13.0.0.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Virtual Edition 13.1.0 is deployed on a vSphere 6.0 or 6.5 system. Traffic consists solely of DNS A record requests at the rate of 700,000 requests per second. Ingress traffic is handled by an EXSi Intel ixgbe driver.
bugs.impact: The DNS transaction rate is up to fourteen percent lower on BIG-IP Virtual Edition 13.1.0 compared to 13.0.0.
bugs.workaround: DNS performance can be restored by altering the TMM scheduler maximum sleep duration to 250 usec. To do so, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db scheduler.maxsleepduration.ltm value 250000 The 250 usec value will improve DNS performance on a 10 GbE NIC, but reduce TCP performance on a 40 GbE NIC.
bugs.fix: Virtual Edition GTM DNS Query Performance Degradation has been addressed.

bugs.title: Performance of a client certificate validation with OCSP agent is degraded
bugs.symptoms: Performance is being degraded for OCSP agent. This can lead to Access Policy performance degradation if there are no more heavy agents configured.
bugs.conditions: OCSP agent is configured in an Access Policy.
bugs.impact: Fewer logons processed per second by the access policy that contains OCSP agent configured.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system sends out SYN/ACK with MSS 0 in VLAN syncookie protection mode on some platforms
bugs.symptoms: A firmware issue exists on certain platforms that will result in SYN/ACK packets with an MSS filed with a value of 0, even though TMOS sets it to a different value.
bugs.conditions: Hardware syncookie is enabled on a VLAN that is under SYN flood attack and the syncookie protection is triggered. This occurs on the following platforms: BIG-IP series 5000, 7000, and 10000 platforms, and VIPRION B2100, B2150, B2250, and B43x0 blades.
bugs.impact: Most TCP clients can handle these SYN/ACK packets gracefully, but some clients (such as Ixia traffic-test appliances) may not be able to handle them properly, thus impacting traffic.
bugs.workaround: Turn off hardware VLAN syncookie protection if regular TCP traffic is impacted.
bugs.fix: In 13.1.0, the per-VLAN-based syncookie protection will be disabled in the data plane BIG-IP series 5000, 7000, and 10000 platforms, and VIPRION B2100, B2150, B2250, and B43x0 blades.

bugs.title: Forward proxy forged cert lifespan can be configured from days into hours.
bugs.symptoms: Once support for OCSP in place, you may need to forge certificates in lifespan shorter than one day. Previously, there was no way to configure that.
bugs.conditions: Configure forward proxy forged cert lifespan shorter than a day.
bugs.impact: None. This is a request for enhancement.
bugs.fix: A new DB variable (tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours) is added to support specifying hours instead of days: [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh list sys db tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours sys db tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours { value "disable" } [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh modify sys db tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours value enable [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh list sys db tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours sys db tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours { value "enable" } When this variable is enabled, the configured lifespan is treated as hours. When this variable is disabled, the configured lifespan is treated as days.
bugs.behavior: Configured Forward proxy forged cert lifespan allows changing from days to hours using a new DB variable: tmm.ssl.certlifespaninhours.

bugs.title: Copying of profile with advanced customization or images might fail
bugs.symptoms: Copying a profile with advanced customization or images produces an error message similar to the following: 'Please specify language code' or similar
bugs.conditions: Access Profile has advanced customization group or customization image assigned to any of object connected to profile.
bugs.impact: Unable to copy policy.
bugs.fix: Copying of profile with advanced customization or images now succeeds as expected.

bugs.title: When from-nethsm option is specified, there is no error when 'security-type' is 'normal' or 'password'.
bugs.symptoms: The system posts an error when you specify 'security-type fips' along with 'from-nethsm', but ignores other, erroneous 'security-type' designations such as 'normal' and 'password'. In this case, when you specify 'security-type' as 'normal' or 'password', the system silently imports the 'from-nethsm' key as type 'nethsm'. Generally, as a best practice, when you should not specify 'security-type' when you use 'from-nethsm'. When you specify security-type fips', the system posts an error, for example: install sys crypto key key4___854f1568 from-nethsm security-type fips Syntax Error: Security type must be nethsm. This occurs because there is no way for the system to determine whether 'security-type normal' comes from 'default' (no 'security-type' specified) or from the manually specified 'security-type normal'.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the 'from-nethsm' option with the 'install sys crypto key' command. -- Specifying 'security-type normal' or 'security-type password'.
bugs.impact: Using 'from-nethsm' with 'normal' or 'password' as the 'security-type' are not compatible options.
bugs.workaround: The preferred usage is that when you specify 'from-nethsm', you should not also specify a 'security_type'. When you specify 'security-type' as 'normal' or 'password, the system ignores it, and imports the key as 'security-type' of 'nethsm'.

bugs.title: JS error "Failed to execute 'iterateNext' on 'XPathResult'...'"
bugs.symptoms: JS error "Failed to execute 'iterateNext' on 'XPathResult'...'"
bugs.conditions: Javascript access to Anchor.href within XPathResult.iterateNext() loop.
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used

bugs.title: Deleting and recreating a route-domain can cause ICMP monitors in that route-domain to permanently fail
bugs.symptoms: Pool members or nodes that utilize an ICMP monitor are marked down even though they are actually up. This issue only affects objects in route-domains that were removed and recreated.
bugs.conditions: The configuration utilizes ICMP monitors in a non-default route-domain and, at some point in the past, the route-domain was deleted and recreated while ICMP monitors were in use in that route-domain.
bugs.impact: Pool members or nodes are marked down incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: To avoid the issue, remove icmp monitors for pool-members and nodes before deleting the route-domain. Reapply the monitors after the route-domain is recreated. To correct the issue, restart the bigd process using the following command: tmsh restart sys service bigd.
bugs.fix: Pool-members and nodes that utilize an ICMP monitor are no longer incorrectly marked down after the route-domain containing them is deleted and recreated.

bugs.title: False positive WebSafe automatic transactions 'Bot' alerts
bugs.symptoms: 'Bot score alerts' on pages that use JavaScript to automate click events.
bugs.conditions: -- WebSafe automatic transactions alerts turned on. -- Non-zero score configured for 'bot score'. -- Pages that use JavaScript to automate click events.
bugs.impact: False positive automatic transaction alerts.
bugs.workaround: Set 'bot score' to zero for these pages
bugs.fix: Allow configuring the following custom JavaScript to disable this feature: function(C){C.XX.DFCD=true;}

bugs.title: iApp scripts that create ASM policies may stop working if the parent policy is mandated
bugs.symptoms: After enabling mandatory parent policies, iApp scripts that create ASM policies no longer work because no parent policy is assigned.
bugs.conditions: Mandatory parent ASM policy is enabled.
bugs.impact: iApp scripts for ASM do not function.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Add parent policy assignment to the script (this is the recommended workaround). -- Disable mandatory parent policies.
bugs.fix: iApp scripts that create ASM policies now work correctly if the parent policy is mandated.

bugs.title: tmsh modify FDB command permits multicast MAC addresses, which produces unexpected results
bugs.symptoms: TMSH does not block modify FDB commands that add a multicast MAC addresses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following is configured using tmsh commands when the mac-address is multicast: fdb vlan <vlan> records add {<mac-address> {interface <slot>/<port>}}.
bugs.impact: There is not enough information to map the outgoing MAC address to a multi-cast group, and therefore it gets a default entry added that has no ports mapped. The result is that the frame will not go out the interface indicated in the tmsh command yet no warning is provided.
bugs.fix: TMSH modify FDB command is no longer permitted to add multicast MAC addresses, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Malformed HTTP/2 requests may cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: Malformed HTTP/2 requests can cause TMM to crash
bugs.conditions: Specially crafted request is sent through an HTTP/2 configured virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 configured virtual server properly handles requests

bugs.title: Update iSeries LCD firmware to v2.03.085.00.0
bugs.symptoms: iSeries LCD firmware issues: -- LTM error logs contain the following rare errors: 1.35V_DDR3: Device or resource busy. -- There are cases when TMOS is under stress conditions that the LCD on iSeries devices can lock at red 'loading' screen.
bugs.conditions: -- This can occur if the ADC of the LCD microcontroller is busy updating counts when the request to read is issued. -- iSeries platforms under stress.
bugs.impact: -- A rare error message similar to the following, appears in the LTM log: 1.35V_DDR3: Device or resource busy. There is no system impact. -- LCD on iSeries devices can lock at red 'loading' screen. Appliance power cycle is required to correct the error.
bugs.fix: Issues are resolved with an updated iSeries LCD image. iSeries LCD firmware v2.03.085.00.0 fixes the following issues: -- LTM error logs contain the following rare errors: 1.35V_DDR3: Device or resource busy. -- There are cases when TMOS is under stress conditions that the LCD on iSeries devices can lock at red 'loading' screen.

bugs.title: Portal Access: support for JavaScript EventSource object
bugs.symptoms: Most modern browsers (e.g., Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, and macOS Safari) support the EventSource object, which allows receipt of server-generated messages via a permanent HTTP connection. The URL used to establish this connection should be rewritten; otherwise connection may not be used.
bugs.conditions: Web application uses EventSource object.
bugs.impact: No Portal Access support for EventSource object. Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to rewrite the URL used in the EventSource object, and to disable rewriting for corresponding server responses.
bugs.fix: Now the EventSource object is supported by Portal Access and can be used in Web applications.

bugs.title: Upgraded volume may fail to load if a Local Traffic Policy uses the forward parameter 'member'
bugs.symptoms: In response to this issue, you might see the following symptoms: -- System remains inoperative -- Screen alerts similar to the following are posted: 'Configuration has not yet loaded'. -- Configuration fails to load after upgrade to v12.1.0 or higher. The system records an error message similar to the following in the ltm log file: emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- 010716de:3: Policy '/Common/Policy', rule 'Policy-Rule'; target 'forward' action 'select' does not support parameter of type 'member'. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Local Traffic Policy with a forward action that selects a target of type 'member'.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load on upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Modify the local traffic policies to use a target type of 'node' before upgrading, or, after upgrading, edit the config file and modify 'member' to 'node' in the local traffic policy, and then reload the configuration.
bugs.fix: Upon upgrade to v12.1.0 or later, policies that perform the action 'forward - select - member' will be automatically changed to 'forward - select - node', and configuration will load successfully.

bugs.title: Unicast IP address can be configured in a failover multicast configuration
bugs.symptoms: Failover multicast configuration does not work when configured with a unicast IP address. Although this is an invalid configuration, the system does not prevent it.
bugs.conditions: Specify a unicast IP address under 'Failover Multicast Configuration' for network failover in high availability configurations.
bugs.impact: Failover multicast configuration does not work.
bugs.workaround: Specify a multicast IP address under 'Failover Multicast Configuration' for network failover.
bugs.fix: The system now prevents specifying a unicast IP address when configuring multicast failover.

bugs.title: Changes to a cipher group are not propagated to the ssl profiles until the configuration is reloaded
bugs.symptoms: Changes to a cipher group, even indirect changes such as changing an underlying cipher rule, will not be propagated to the ssl profiles until the configuration is reloaded.
bugs.conditions: An ssl profile is using cipher groups (instead of the cipher string) and some changes are made to that group.
bugs.impact: The available ciphers on an ssl profile might not be as expected.
bugs.workaround: Either always reload the configuration after changing a cipher group, or use the existing cipher string mechanism instead.
bugs.fix: With this change, changes to a cipher group will be correctly propagated to the ssl profiles.

bugs.title: Portal Access: JavaScript code may be corrupted in debug mode
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes Portal Access corrupts JavaScript code if it is running in debug mode.
bugs.conditions: - Portal Access in debug mode (i.e., with debug log setting). - JavaScript code.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Disable debug logging mode for Portal Access.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access does not corrupt JavaScript code in debug logging mode.

bugs.title: APMD process may fail to initialize on start either after upgrade or after adding certain configurations
bugs.symptoms: APMD process may fail at initialization time with errors similar to the following: -- createAgent - initInstance() failed for agent xxx_saml_auth_ag type (46) -- Exiting due to failure in loading access policy objects
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system is configured as SAML SP. -- Certificate used by configured SAML Agent was imported onto BIG-IP system in DER format.
bugs.impact: APMD service may become unresponsive, dropping all traffic protected by APM access policies.
bugs.workaround: Convert DER encoded certificate used by SAML SP agent into PEM format.
bugs.fix: DER certificate no longer cause APMD process errors at initialization time.

bugs.title: B2000 Series Blades Low Throughput With Two Member Trunk
bugs.symptoms: Trunk throughput is significantly less than twice the data rate of the individual interface members when combining them into a trunk.
bugs.conditions: B2000 Series blades with two interfaces configured together as a trunk with traffic exceeding the rate of the single interface capacity. Note that performance degradation can vary widely depending on source and destination IP and port combinations.
bugs.impact: Degraded Performance.

bugs.title: Chrome v60 and newer might incorrectly report that F5 VPN and F5 EPI status
bugs.symptoms: Chrome v60 and newer might incorrectly report that F5 VPN and F5 EPI applications have not provided any status update to the browser. However, both applications are being launched and function properly.
bugs.conditions: Chrome v60 and newer on Microsoft Windows, Apple Macintosh, or Linux-based systems.
bugs.impact: F5 VPN: the webtop displays the following message: Waiting for Network Access Application status. VPN or Application Tunnels work properly, and the APM end user may safely close the message box. F5 EPI: the webtop displays the following message: Waiting for Endpoint Inspection status. The latter message never goes away; however, F5 EPI applications are launched and function properly, and Security checks are performed in the background. Unless the APM end user refreshes the browser screen, the Access Policy never moves forward, causing browser never to refresh the page.
bugs.workaround: Use another browser: Internet Explorer 11, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, or Safari, as available. If using F5 EPI, refreshing the page after a one-minute since the check start should advance the position in the Access Policy, allowing the APM end user to properly log in.
bugs.fix: Now Chrome v60 and newer properly gets F5 VPN and F5 EPI application updates from the BIG-IP system, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: HTTP PSM leaks memory when looking up evasion descriptions
bugs.symptoms: http_psm_description_lookup leaks xfrags containing PSM evasion descriptions.
bugs.conditions: When PSM looks up evasion descriptions.
bugs.impact: Memory leaked each time might eventually cause out of memory to the TMM.
bugs.fix: This fix will stop the memory leakage.

bugs.title: Adding widget in Analytics Overview can cause measures list to empty out on Page change
bugs.symptoms: When adding a new widget on Analytics Overview page with multiple modules (e.g., vCMP, Security), it is possible to reach a state in which the list of available measures is empty.
bugs.conditions: -- All 'available measurements' is selected (moved left). -- A page should be changed.
bugs.impact: In some cases (like in vCMP when changing from Network to SynCookies), the list of available measurements will remain empty. Unable to select measures to display in new widget.
bugs.workaround: To reset the list of measures so that all measures are visible again, switch to another page and return to the previous one right away.

bugs.title: Live install from version 11.6.x to version 13.1.0 requires a manual step
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade (live install) to 13.1.0 never finishes due to the insufficient disk space because there is not enough memory allocated for /var filesystem. Therefore, upgrade/live install of BIG IP VE version 11.6.x to VE version 13.1.0 requires a manual step. File /shared/.tmi_config/global_attributes must be deleted before starting live install with the following command: tmsh install sys software image. Note: This applies only to images for VE/cloud that are 'Good'-model licenses.
bugs.conditions: -- Version 11.6.x VE/cloud images licensed for the 'Good' licensing model. -- Upgrade (live install) to version 13.1.0.
bugs.impact: Impossible to upgrade/live install from version 11.6.x to version 13.1.0.
bugs.workaround: 1. Delete the following file: /shared/.tmi_config/global_attributes. 2. Start upgrade/live install with the following command: tmsh install sys software image. After removing /shared/.tmi_config/global_attributes, upgrade/live install completes as expected.

bugs.title: Per Request Access Policy subroutine performance down by about 7%
bugs.symptoms: The performance of the per-request access policy with subroutines, even an empty one (in->out) is down by about 7%.
bugs.conditions: All of the following must be true for this issue to be exposed. 1) APM is provisioned. 2) An APM profile is attached to the virtual server. 3) A Per-Request access policy containing a subroutine is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Maximum RADIUS TPS is degraded (~7%).
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.

bugs.title: TLS v1.2 support in IP reputation daemon
bugs.symptoms: The IP reputation daemon opens SSL connections to the Webroot BrightCloud server using TLS 1.0 protocol.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using IP reputation.
bugs.impact: Because IP reputation services are used to accept/deny connections to critical business applications, there might be concerns about the service. Also some configurations might require that all transactions exfiltrating a PCI-controlled environment leverage secure protocols and ciphers, which won't be the case for IP reputation services.
bugs.fix: Webroot updated BrightCloud servers to support TLS 1.2. This is additional support. To preserve backward compatiblity, the servers support TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, TLS 1.2, SSL 2.0 and SSL 3.0. In addition, this software version supports TLS 1.2 on the client side by customizing the SDK used by the IP reputation daemon.

bugs.title: Escaped '#' is preserved in fields set through 'tmsh'
bugs.symptoms: Using 'tmsh' to set monitor fields containing an octothorp ('\#') preserves the included backslash, rather than "absorbing" the backslash into the special character '#'. For example, setting monitor 'username' or 'description' to "abc\#def" or "abc#def" will preserve the '\#' or '#' as provided. This may be surprising if it was assumed that the backslash (escape-character) would be implicitly "absorbed" into the octothorp ('#').
bugs.conditions: tmsh is used to set monitor parameters (such as 'username' or 'description') where the value includes an escaped octothorp ('\#).
bugs.impact: The backslash is preserved (and not implicitly absorbed as an escaped character preceding the octothorp).
bugs.workaround: Do not escape the octothorp with a backslash for monitor values if no backslash is desired; and wrap the value within double-quotes as necessary.

bugs.title: Cannot send messages to LCD if tmm or mcpd fail to come up.
bugs.symptoms: If either tmm or mcp fail to come up, alertd will not come up. Alertd is responsible for causing messages to appear on the LCD.
bugs.conditions: Abnormal startup on a system such that tmm or mcpd is prevented from coming up. For example: A configuration module is detected to be missing or unsupported on i5xxx-, i7xxx-, i10xxx-, and i15xxx-series platforms.
bugs.impact: Must view logs to determine what issues may have occurred during startup.
bugs.workaround: Examination of the system log files and/or qkview will likely contain any messages that would have been sent to the LCD.

bugs.title: Portal Access may handle JavaScript getter/setter definitions incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: In JavaScript, literal object definition may contain getter/setter definitions for some property, for example: var c = { get a() { return a; }, set a(v) { if (v) a = v; } }; The object 'c' has the property 'a' with explicit getter/setter functions. If name of such property is equal to any name to be rewritten, then Portal Access may generate incorrect JavaScript code.
bugs.conditions: - JavaScript code with literal object definition; - Property with getter/setter definition in this object; - Property name is one of rewritten names, like 'location' or 'onerror'.
bugs.impact: JavaScript code cannot be executed due to incorrect syntax after rewriting.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to replace rewritten property names by original ones.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access does not rewrite property names in getter/setter definitions for JavaScript objects.

bugs.title: Connection rate limit on a pool member can be exceeded
bugs.symptoms: The connection rate-limit to a pool member can exceeded.
bugs.conditions: When a virtual is configured with UDP, FastL4, and pva acceleration is enabled.
bugs.impact: The connection rate limit on the pool member can be exceeded.
bugs.workaround: Disable pva acceleration using the following command: "tmsh modify sys db pva.acceleration value none".

bugs.title: iSession tunnels are not reused and idle tunnels are not terminated by the sweeper
bugs.symptoms: When an iSession tunnel is created with certain iSession profile properties, the tunnel is not reused and the idle client-side (incoming) tunnel is not reset by the sweeper. TMM must be restarted to clean up the client-side iSession tunnels. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: An iSession tunnel is created with these three iSession profile properties: -- reuse-connection enabled -- deduplication disabled -- compression disabled
bugs.impact: Tunnel is not reused and the idle client-side (incoming) tunnel is not reset by the sweeper. TMM must be restarted to clean up the client-side iSession tunnels. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable the iSession profile reuse-connection property.
bugs.fix: iSession tunnels are reused and idle tunnels are terminated by the sweeper.

bugs.title: Malformed HTTP/2 request with invalid Content-Length value is served against RFC
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 request can include Content-Length header. When the value of a Content-Length header does not match the sum of lengths of all DATA frames from the stream, RFC requires that the system reset the stream.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server is configured with HTTP/2 profile. -- The value of Content-Length header does not match the sum of lengths of all DATA frames from the stream.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends a request to a server and serves a provided response, which is not in conformance with the RFC.
bugs.fix: Now, when a client sends a request over an HTTP/2 connection with a malformed HEADERS frame in which Content-Length does not match the payload size in DATA frames, the BIG-IP system correctly resets the stream with RST_STREAM frame.

bugs.title: Empty IP Address field of object created in a partition with route domain in GUI is auto-filled after save
bugs.symptoms: Config objects such as RADIUS server in APM or traffic class in LTM that contain the IP address field, when left empty and created in a partition that is associated with a route domain, the value is auto-changed to '::0.0.0.0' after save.
bugs.conditions: Configuring APM RADIUS authentication with an empty nas-ip-address.
bugs.impact: The value in the database does not change. This is a cosmetic issue only and represents on functional issue.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to see APM RADIUS authentication nas-ip-address using the following command: tmsh list apm aaa radius <name>
bugs.fix: Empty APM RADIUS authentication nas-ip-address is no longer automatically filled.

bugs.title: TMM can establish multiple connections to the same gtmd
bugs.symptoms: TMM can establish multiple connections to the same gtmd, and tmm may core.
bugs.conditions: This timing-related issue involves coordination between license blob arrival, gtmd connection teardown/establishment, and gtmd restart.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed, if there is an existing connflow, don't start another connection.

bugs.title: lindex does not recognize multi dimension array indexing
bugs.symptoms: lindex command reports failure when it is given multi indices, e.g. script "lindex $dnsServer 0 0" fails with error, wrong # args
bugs.conditions: lindex command is used with multi indices.
bugs.impact: Fails in validation and thus config load.
bugs.workaround: Use lindex command to each dimension separately.
bugs.fix: Will submit fix.

bugs.title: Inserting an un-powered PSU and then removing the un-powered PSU puts the BMC into an incorrect PSU status state.
bugs.symptoms: Inserting an un-powered PSU and then removing the un-powered PSU puts the BMC into an incorrect PSU status state. Once in this PSU incorrect status state, the BMC reports an input-lost alert on every subsequent host reboot until the PSU is re-installed, or the BMC is reset.
bugs.conditions: -- System is powered by a single PSU. -- A second un-powered PSU is inserted and then removed.
bugs.impact: On every subsequent host reboot the system reports an input-lost alert for the not-present PSU in the ltm log, the LCD posts a warning, and the system alarm LED turns yellow.
bugs.workaround: Re-install the second PSU, reboot the AOM via the console AOM menu, or power cycle the platform.

bugs.title: SNI support for GTM HTTPS monitors
bugs.symptoms: Some applications require that a TLS connection request include the Server Name Indication (SNI) extension to determine which server certificate should be used when negotiating a connection.
bugs.conditions: Monitoring HTTPS resources.
bugs.impact: GTM can now properly monitor resources that require SNI.
bugs.fix: GTM HTTPS monitoring allows the specification of the SNI value to use when monitoring a resource.

bugs.title: LTM Policy with 'requires {ssl-persistence}' load issue resolved in 13.1.0
bugs.symptoms: There was an LTM Policy with 'requires {ssl-persistence}' that was found and fixed during v13.1.0 project development. Note: Because this issue was fixed in v13.1.0 before release, you will not encounter this issue; this release note is included to track the Behavior Change.
bugs.conditions: LTM policy that has 'requires {ssl-persistence}'.
bugs.impact: Configuration load fails. Note: This occurs only in internal releases and was never included in an external release.
bugs.workaround: Change the configuration and load it manually. - If policy is active for the ssl-client-hello event, change ssl-persistence to client-ssl. - If policy is active for the ssl-server-handshake event, change ssl-persistence to server-ssl. - If policy is active for both ssl-client-hello and ssl-server-handshake events, change ssl-persistence to client-ssl - server-ssl.
bugs.fix: 13.1.0 configurations with policies that 'require {ssl-persistence}' are migrated successfully.
bugs.behavior: Beginning in v13.1.0, LTM Policy supports many more framework events than before, and certain 'requires' aspects had to be replaced. In previous releases, ssl-persistence was used for client-side and server-side events. Now policies that contain client SSL or server SSL will have specific 'requires' aspect for that side. Here are some examples of how the values changed: - If policy is active for the ssl-client-hello event, ssl-persistence should be client-ssl. - If policy is active for the ssl-server-handshake event, ssl-persistence should be server-ssl. - If policy is active for both ssl-client-hello and ssl-server-handshake events, ssl-persistence should be client-ssl - server-ssl. When updating LTM policies that already contain these values, the system changes them as follows: -- The system changes the 'requires' stanza to client-ssl, if policy condition or action references these events: - ssl-client-hello - ssl-client-serverhello-send -- The system changes the 'requires' stanza to server-ssl, if policy condition or action references these events: - ssl-server-hello - ssl-server-handshake -- The system changes the 'requires' stanza to reflect both client-ssl and server-ssl, if the policy condition or action references both a client and a server event: - client-ssl server-ssl

bugs.title: VDI Profile and Storefront Portal Access resource do not work together
bugs.symptoms: Accessing a Citrix Storefront portal access resource and clicking on the application does not work since VDI returns HTTP status 404.
bugs.conditions: -- VDI profile is attached to the Virtual server. -- Access policy has Citrix Storefront portal access resource. -- Citrix remote-desktop resource is attached.
bugs.impact: Citrix Storefront portal access resource cannot be used to launch applications.
bugs.fix: Citrix Storefront portal access resources can now be used with Citrix Remote desktop resources.

bugs.title: Event Correlation is disabled on vCMP even though all the prerequisites are met.
bugs.symptoms: The GUI screen Security :: Event Logs : Application : Event Correlation reports the message: Event Correlation is not supported on this platform.
bugs.conditions: Multi-bladed vCMP guest, running on a BIG-IP system with SSD drives, having only one available slot (other slots appear offline/unavailable).
bugs.impact: Under these conditions, Event Correlation is disabled.
bugs.workaround: The following workaround does not survive ASM restart. Thus, it has to be executed after every restart of ASM: ------------------------ # perl -MF5::ASMReady -MF5::Cfg -e 'while (! F5::ASMReady::is_asm_ready()) { print "Waiting for ASM to be ready.\n"; sleep 5; }; print "ASM is ready, patching Event Correlation cfg file\n"; F5::Cfg::cfg_set_config_item(qw{/etc/ts/correlation/correlation.cfg}, qw{General}, qw{Idle}, 0)' # pkill -f correlation ------------------------ Event Correlation should start with in ~15 seconds, after the execution of this workaround: ------------------------ # ps -elf | grep correlation 0 S root ... /usr/share/ts/bin/correlation ------------------------
bugs.fix: Event Correlation is now enabled on a multi-bladed SSD vCMP guest with only one active slot.

bugs.title: The username is updated in the alert dashboard even if login validation fails.
bugs.symptoms: The username is updated in the alert dashboard even if login validation fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- 'trigger iRule' is enabled on the FPS profile. -- ANTIFRAUD::username <user> command is used in the ANTIFRAUD_LOGIN Tcl event. -- 'login validation' is enabled on the FPS profile.
bugs.impact: The new username will be updated in previous alerts in the alert dashboard.
bugs.workaround: Use the ANTIFRAUD::username <user> command only if ANTIFRAUD::result is SUCCESS. Note: Reports to the risk engine will not contain the new username.
bugs.fix: FPS uses the new username but does not set the username cookie. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: tmm asserts on a virtual server-to-virtual server connection
bugs.symptoms: tmm might crash when using a virtual server-to-virtual server connection, and that connection has a TCP profile with keepalive configured.
bugs.conditions: -- L7 virtual server-to-virtual server connection (Virtual command, cpm rule, etc.). -- TCP profile with keepalive configured. -- (Deflate profile.) -- At the beginning of the connection, there is a stall for longer than the specified keepalive timer interval. -- The received response decompresses to a size that is greater than the advertised window size on the first virtual server's TCP stack.
bugs.impact: Shortly after the keepalive packet is received, which then is decompressed, the assert is triggered, and tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove keepalive from the TCP profiles of the two virtual servers involved.
bugs.fix: The system now honors the current receive window size when sending keepalives, so the tmm crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Kerberos keytab file content may be visible.
bugs.symptoms: Kerberos keytab file content may be visible.
bugs.conditions: Import a Kerberos keytab file. From the command line, check the file permissions. It is readable.
bugs.impact: keytab is similar to a private key file and should not be readable.
bugs.workaround: Use chmod to change the keytab file permission manually so that it is not world-readable.
bugs.fix: Kerberos keytab file content is no longer visible.

bugs.title: Compression watchdog period too brief.
bugs.symptoms: Compression TPS can be reduced on certain platforms when sustained, very high compression request traffic is present.
bugs.conditions: Very high sustained system-wide compression request traffic.
bugs.impact: Accelerated compression throughput can drop significantly; some flows dropped.
bugs.workaround: Switch to software compression.
bugs.fix: Compression request monitor tuned to account for systems with smaller bandwidth.

bugs.title: key-id missing for installed netHSM key for standby BIG-IP system in HA setup
bugs.symptoms: In a BIG-IP high availability (HA) configuration, the nethsm key installed has empty key-id string for the standby BIG-IP system. That is, the BIG-IP system that actually gets the key installed has the key-id string properly displayed. But its peer BIG-IP system does not display a key-id string associated with the installed key.
bugs.conditions: -- nethsm key installed. -- Standby BIG-IP system in an HA configuration.
bugs.impact: The peer BIG-IP system has no key-id string properly displayed.
bugs.workaround: Even though key-id does not display, the key is present on the peer BIG-IP system and can be used there.
bugs.fix: The netHSM key for standby BIG-IP system in HA configurations now shows up after a successful configsync.

bugs.title: Sync of virtual address and self IP traffic groups only happens in one direction
bugs.symptoms: If you have a virtual address and a self IP that both listen on the same IP address, changing the traffic group of the self IP will make an equivalent change to the traffic group of the virtual address. However, this does not work in reverse. Changing the traffic group of the virtual address will not cause a change of the traffic group of the self IP.
bugs.conditions: You have a virtual address and a self IP that both listen on the same IP address. (The subnet mask need not be the same.)
bugs.impact: This is by design, but is counterintuitive, and there is no warning message that this is the case. Setting the traffic group on both objects will always work properly.
bugs.workaround: Care should be taken to ensure that the desired traffic group is set on both objects.

bugs.title: Rapid creation/update/deletion of the same external datagroup may cause core
bugs.symptoms: -- notice tmm[15187]: 01010259:5: External Datagroup (/Common/Datagroup_1) queued. -- notice tmm[15187]: 01010259:5: External Datagroup (/Common/Datagroup_1) queued for update. -- err tmm[15187]: 01010258:3: External Datagroup (/Common/Datagroup_1) creation failed: initial load error, deleting.
bugs.conditions: Using external datagroup, rapidly creating updating and then deleting it.
bugs.impact: TMM fails
bugs.workaround: Allow TMM enough time to finish processing external data-group before starting another operation. Depending on the size of the datagroup anywhere from 1s to 10s or more may be needed. The LTM log can be examined for the create/finished message to help determine how much wait time is required.

bugs.title: APM client_packaging and sandbox objects are not handled when using tmsh auth partition to manage partition
bugs.symptoms: APM objects, client_packaging, and sandbox are not created and deleted along with partition folder if it is created and deleted using the command: tmsh auth partition.
bugs.conditions: - Create partition using the command: tmsh auth partition - Delete partition that is created by the command: tmsh sys folder command, or the GUI, by using the command: tmsh auth partition
bugs.impact: - Certain APM functions associated with client_packaging and sandbox are missing. - Deletion fails.
bugs.workaround: Use the 'tmsh sys folder; command or the GUI to create and delete partitions.
bugs.fix: Using 'tmsh auth partition' to create and delete partition can achieve the same result as using 'tmsh sys folder' or the GUI, e.g., create and delete client_packaging and sandbox along with the partition folder.

bugs.title: [KERBEROS SSO][KRB5] The performance of memory type Kerberos ticket cache in krb5 library drops gradually with the number of users
bugs.symptoms: APM performance of handling HTTP request drops gradually when Kerberos SSO is being used over a period of time. Websso CPU usage is very high. The BIG-IP system response can rate drop to the point that the clients disconnect after waiting for a response. The system logs error messages similar to the following: Failure occurred when processing the work item.
bugs.conditions: -- Running APM. -- A large number of APM end users (~20 KB) have logged on and are using Kerberos SSO.
bugs.impact: Increased latency of HTTP request processing.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of cached Kerberos user tickets by lowering the cache lifetime.
bugs.fix: Improvements to the krb5 library have been implemented for better scalability, so the latency of HTTP request processing has been significantly improved.

bugs.title: Need support for 4th element version in Update Check
bugs.symptoms: Previously, there was no 4th element version Update Check functionality.
bugs.conditions: Using Update Check.
bugs.impact: No 4th element version support provided.
bugs.fix: There is now 4th element version support in Update Check.

bugs.title: Hotfix install fails on vCMP guest when both guest and host have the same base version ISO present
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP software installations will fail and report a status of: waiting for cleanup; multiple base builds found (BIG-IP 13.0.0)
bugs.conditions: - Perform software installation in a vCMP guest when guest is running v13.0.0 or newer. - Ask the guest to install a hotfix (e.g. "tmsh install /sys software hotfix 13.0.0-hf2.iso volume HD1.2 create-volume") to a boot location that does not have a base software version installed. - Hypervisor has a valid copy of the the correct base image (e.g. v13.0.0 build 0.0.1645) - Guest has a valid copy of the correct base image (e.g. v13.0.0 build 0.0.1645)
bugs.impact: Software installation fails, and will not complete/continue.
bugs.workaround: Delete the base software image from either the hypervisor or guest's file system
bugs.fix: The condition no longer causes an error; the installation request successfully runs to completion.

bugs.title: Hardware syncookies number for virtual server stats is unrealistically high
bugs.symptoms: In some situations 'tmsh show ltm virtual' shows unrealistically high hardware (HW) syncookie numbers. These unrealistically high HW syncookie stats cause AFM DoS TCP synflood vector to have high numbers, and that can cause TCP synflood vector to drop packets in HW based on the configured rate-limit for that vector.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with hardware syncookie protection enabled.
bugs.impact: Stats issue. Can have impact to traffic if AFM TCP Synflood vector is enabled in mitigation mode.
bugs.workaround: Disable the TCP Synflood vector in mitigate mode. Since Syncookie is already providing protection, the TCP Synflood option should be enabled only in detect-only mode, if at all.
bugs.fix: Hardware syncookies number for virtual server now reports stats as expected.

bugs.title: Can't drilldown or filter by 'Client Countries'
bugs.symptoms: When drilling down or filtering by 'Client Countries' (Security :: Reporting : Application : Charts) there is an error in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM is provisioned. -- Attempt to drill down or filter by 'Client Countries'.
bugs.impact: Internal Error is displayed in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: 1. Edit file: /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_entities.cfg. 2. Delete line 171: (dim_authz_filter=vip_crc). 3. Issue the command: bigstart restart monpd.
bugs.fix: Drilling down or filtering results by 'Client Countries' works as expected.

bugs.title: Improve CSRF token handling
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, CSRF token handling does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: CSRF is configured.
bugs.impact: CSRF token handling does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: CSRF token handling now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: SNMP trap suppression should be based upon OID rather than trap text
bugs.symptoms: There are two db variables that allow trap suppression to be configured. They are snmp.bigiptraps.suppress.interval and snmp.bigiptraps.suppress.count. The suppression is cleared with each new trap issued so it does not successfully suppress traps when multiple traps are issued in the suppression interval.
bugs.conditions: Configuring SNMP trap suppression.
bugs.impact: It can appear that trap suppression is not working if multiple traps are being issued in the suppression interval.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The trap suppression processing has been improved to consider the full trap contents.

bugs.title: tcpdump option added to capture on 'all interfaces' from host side using the option '0.0:h'
bugs.symptoms: tcpdump can be used to capture packets to and from the host side, which means an administrator can see the packets that are sent from tmm to the Linux kernel (and vice-versa). However, this only could be done on a specific VLAN. Now, the '0.0:h' interface option to capture all host side traffic on all interfaces and VLANs works.
bugs.conditions: No specific conditions needed, interface option '0.0:h' never worked.
bugs.impact: The tcpdump interface option '0.0:h', to capture all host side traffic on all interfaces and VLANs, the operation captures no packets and will exit with the following message: tcpdump: Host modifier not supported on this interface.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: tcpdump now accepts the interface option '0.0:h' and will capture all host side traffic on all VLANs.

bugs.title: tcpdump optin added to capture on "all interfaces" from linux side using the option "any:l"
bugs.symptoms: tcpdump can be used to capture packets from the Linux side (using the Linux kernel's tcpdump instead of capturing from tmm). However this cannot be done on all interfaces and VLANs at the same time. The command needs to specify a particular VLAN for its Linux side capture.
bugs.conditions: Running tcpdump .
bugs.impact: Linux side tcpdump capture can be done on only one single vlan at a time.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: tcpdump now accepts the option 'any:l' which allows capture on all interfaces and VLANs at the same time from the Linux side.

bugs.title: Portal Access may use incorrect back-end for resources referenced by CSS
bugs.symptoms: If HTML page contains reference to external CSS file with URL beginning with '//', then host-less references in this CSS file are handled incorrectly by Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page at http://example.host/page.html: <link rel=stylesheet href=//another.host/some/path/my.css> - and this CSS contains reference with absolute path like this: html { background-image: url(/misc/image/some.png); } Portal Access uses 'http://example.host' as back-end for this image instead of correct 'http://another.host'.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to correct back-end host.
bugs.fix: Portal Access uses correct back-end host for references in CSS files included with scheme-less URL.

bugs.title: F5 APM webtop spawns a pop up windows with text 'webpage cannot be displayed' when running F5 VPN or F5 EPI first time
bugs.symptoms: Running F5 VPN or F5 EPI on the webtop page for the first time, Microsoft Internet Explorer v11 (IE11) spawns a pop-up window with text 'web page cannot be displayed' and does not close it automatically. The window must be closed manually.
bugs.conditions: The issue happens only when all of the following conditions are met: -- Microsoft Windows 7 operating system. -- IE11. -- F5 VPN/F5 EPI not installed. -- APM site is in trusted sites list.
bugs.impact: Window does not close on its own, and must be closed manually. Might cause confusion.
bugs.workaround: None. However, if any of the conditions are not met, the window closes automatically.

bugs.title: Error #2134 when attempting to create local flash.net::SharedObject in rewritten ActionScript 3 file
bugs.symptoms: Flash ActionScript3 application shows Error #2134 when trying to call flash.net::SharedObject.getLocal with localPath specified.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to create local SharedObject.
bugs.impact: Affected Flash applications are not working when accessed through Portal Access.
bugs.fix: Addressed an issue in Portal Access which caused rewritten Flash files to show Error #2134 on attempt to create local SharedObject.

bugs.title: HTTP::header command may crash TMM on an erroneous argument
bugs.symptoms: An iRule command 'HTTP::header insert' or 'HTTP::header remove' allows manipulation of HTTP headers. The iRule accepts arguments that might result in an error if they have an invalid format. TMM generates an internal Tcl error for the argument but continues to process the command. This might cause TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule is associated with a virtual server. -- The iRule contains either or both of the 'HTTP::header insert' and 'HTTP::header remove' commands. -- An argument in the command generates a Tcl error.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes causing failover and possible disruption in processing traffic.
bugs.workaround: Sanitize arguments for the command to prevent TCL error.

bugs.title: The case-sensitive problem during comparison of 2 Virtual Servers
bugs.symptoms: Failed to load "incident types volume graph" if incident was filtered by Virtual Server
bugs.impact: Chart of incident data will not be displayed.
bugs.workaround: Avoid to create virtual servers that have the same letters, differing only by capital letters verses small letters.
bugs.fix: monpd process uses a case-sensitive comparison of virtual servers

bugs.title: WebSockets: umu memory leak of binary frames when remote logger is configured
bugs.symptoms: ASM out of memory error messages in /var/log/asm.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with WebSocket profile. -- ASM remote logger configured and assigned to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: ASM out of memory, memory leak.
bugs.workaround: Remove ASM remote logging profile from a virtual server.
bugs.fix: This release correctly releases unused memory after WebSocket message is sent to the logging destination.

bugs.title: 'tmsh show sys connection' command prompt displaying 4 billion connections is misleading
bugs.symptoms: The 'tmsh show sys connection' may present a prompt asking you to confirm you want to display ~4 billion (4,294,967,295) connections: # show sys connection max-result-limit infinite Really display 4294967295 connections? (y/n)
bugs.conditions: -- The 'tmsh show sys connection' command is executed with max-result-limit option set to infinite.
bugs.impact: The value shown in the prompt (4294967295) is misleading, and does not reflect the actual number of connections being handled by the system. The 4294967295 number represents the maximum value the field can hold, not the number of actual connections.

bugs.title: PEM will optimize out classification if possible.
bugs.symptoms: This can occur with an unknown subscriber policy that doesn't have classification filters. Since applying classification may impede performance significantly, there is an optimization rule that if the first policy applied to a flow doesn't have classification filters, classification for that particular flow will be optimized out. When this occurs, flows will remain unclassified for their lifetime. As a result of remaining unclassified, if PEM pushes some classification match policies to this flow, the policies will not get applied.
bugs.conditions: Global/unknown policies doesn't include any classification filter.
bugs.impact: In this scenario, classification match policies may not be applied to existing flows.
bugs.workaround: A simple workaround would be, put a Any/Any classification filter in global or unknown subscriber policy to enabled classification for flow at its early stage.

bugs.title: Lack of meaningful information about 'codec alert' errors triggered by SSL traffic issues.
bugs.symptoms: Some problematic SSL traffic can cause the SSL processing engine to encounter errors and generate 'codec alert' errors in the LTM log. These errors do not convey any meaningful information about the actual problem that occurred.
bugs.conditions: Various SSL traffic issues seen by BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system Administrators cannot make any decisions if there is a lack of information about SSL traffic issues.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Added support to log the causes for 'codec alert' errors as debug logs.

bugs.title: Redeployment of SAML-SP app fails if HTTP-header-based SSO is configured
bugs.symptoms: Redeployment of SAML-SP app fails, and the app enters an error state.
bugs.conditions: -- Redeployment of SAML-SP app. -- HTTP-header-based SSO is configured.
bugs.impact: Redeployment fails; new configuration objects are not created.
bugs.workaround: Undeploy the app and then deploy it again.

bugs.title: TMM crashes during stress test
bugs.symptoms: During stress/load testing, with a large number of connections which triggers flow sweeping, TMM restarts.
bugs.conditions: A large number of connections are seen, which triggers an expansion of the connflow hash table at the same time the connflow sweeper is active.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Connflow removal from the internal hash table is deferred until the entire bucket is processed.

bugs.title: ASN1::encode returns wrong binary data
bugs.symptoms: ASN1::encode returns incorrect data for certain integer values. For example, for integer 49280, ASN1::encode returns 02030000.
bugs.conditions: The problem happens in an implicit UTF encoding/decoding, and it is not obvious what data triggers the error. This is because it implicitly converts the Tcl object type from byte array to string and later back to byte array, but because of the UTF de-coding algorithm, certain bytes get changed.
bugs.impact: The returned binary is wrong.
bugs.workaround: Use binary scan for the value that is incorrectly encoded by the command.
bugs.fix: ASN1::encode ENCODE mode now works so that it avoids the implicit type-conversion byte array to string back to byte array, which gets the original byte array changed during UTF-8 decoding.

bugs.title: SASP monitor may use the same UID for multiple HA device group members
bugs.symptoms: Under rare timing conditions, the SASP monitor running on one member of an HA group (failover device group) may use the same LB UID as another member of the device group. The LB UID used to connect to the Server/Application State Protocol (SASP) Group Workload Manager (GWM) is required to be unique for each client connecting to the GWM. As a result, only the first HA group member using the duplicated UID is able to successfully use the SASP monitor. The SASP monitor instance running on the HA group member using the duplicated UID will fail to connect to the SASP GWM.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under rare timing conditions when using the SASP monitor on a BIG-IP system that belongs to an HA group. It is possible that the necessary timing conditions may occur if the external SASP monitor daemon is forcibly restarted (such as for troubleshooting purposes).
bugs.impact: The SASP monitor is unable to monitor pool member availability on all members of the HA group.
bugs.workaround: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the configuration (as described in article K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030) allows recovery from this condition. It is possible that less-intrusive measures such as restarting the external SASP monitor daemon (such as by sending a SIGTERM to the SASPD_monitor process) may also allow recovery. Due to the rare occurrence of this symptom, this solution has not been confirmed.
bugs.fix: The SASP monitor reliably uses a unique UID across HA group members, allowing all HA group members to successfully connect to the SASP GWM.

bugs.title: Monitor status may show 'checking' after a pool member has been manually forced down
bugs.symptoms: Following certain sequences of actions, a pool member that is forced offline (e.g., '{session user-disabled state user-down}'), may have an associated monitor status (status of the associated monitor instance) that is shown as 'checking'.
bugs.conditions: This result may occur as the result of one of the following sequences of actions: 1. A pool member is created with an associated monitor, and that pool member is simultaneously forced offline. Example: tmsh create ltm pool test1 members add { 10.1.108.2:80 { session user-disabled state user-down } } monitor http 2. A pool member is disabled or forced offline, the configuration is saved, and the BIG-IP system is restarted (for example, by 'bigstart restart' or 'reboot' commands). Example: tmsh modify ltm pool test1 members modify 10.1.108.2:80 { session user-disabled state user-down } } tmsh save sys config bigstart restart
bugs.impact: The pool member remains offline as directed, but the associated monitor status (monitor instance status) indicates 'checking', which does not appear to match the pool member status. If the pool member is subsequently re-enabled, the associated monitor status (status of the associated monitor instance) will be updated to show the result of current monitor pings.
bugs.workaround: The 'checking' status of the monitor instance may be unexpected, in this context, but: - The monitor status (monitor instance status) does not affect the status of a disabled pool member. - This monitor status indicates that no monitor pings have been performed to update the initial state of the monitored object from 'checking' to a result determined by a monitor ping. The BIG-IP monitoring subsystem does not ping disabled pool members to update this status.

bugs.title: APM now supports VMware Workspace ONE integration with vIDM as ID Provider
bugs.symptoms: When VMware Horizon resources are behind APM, APM end user is able to see available desktops and application on VMware Workspace ONE portal but is not able to launch them.
bugs.conditions: -- VMware virtual desktops and applications are hosted on VMware Horizon behind APM. -- APM end user authenticates with VMware Identity Manager (IDM) and sees available virtual desktops and applications on Workspace ONE portal. -- APM end user attempts to launch a virtual desktop or application with VMware native client.
bugs.impact: Users authenticates but is not able to launch a desktop or application with View native client.
bugs.fix: APM now supports VMware Workspace ONE with VMware IDM as Identity Provider and APM as service provider, protecting VMware Horizon desktops and applications.

bugs.title: Users are not able to complete the sync using GUI
bugs.symptoms: A validation error occurred while syncing to a remote device Sync error on unitA.lab.local: Load failed from /Common/unitB.lab.local 01070080:3: The requested pool member is already in use as a self IP address (1.1.2.1) The above is expected as unit B is unable to validate the config for unit A. Incremental sync adds and removes configuration on unit A, hence the error.
bugs.conditions: 1.Units A and B in HA with manual incremental sync, unit B is active. 2.On unit B add a pool with a member having IP address matching the self IP of unit A. Then delete it. 3.create ltm pool p1 members add { 1.1.2.1:80 } 4.delete ltm pool p1 5.Try config-sync (using GUI). You will end up with a Sync Failed message: A validation error occurred while syncing to a remote device Sync error on unitA.lab.local: Load failed from /Common/unitB.lab.local 01070080:3: The requested pool member is already in use as a self IP address (1.1.2.1
bugs.impact: Users are not able to complete the sync using GUI
bugs.workaround: using tmsh to force a full sync

bugs.title: Web browsers may strip query parameters from the logout URL after completing SAML single logout profile.
bugs.symptoms: When user initiates SAML single logout (SLO) on BIG-IP (either SP or IdP), BIG-IP will attempt to log out user from all external SAML providers by following SLO profile. After SLO profile is completed, user will be redirected back to original URL that started SLO procedure. Newer versions of browsers are known to strip query parameters from this final URL. This may cause redirect to a URL with no query parameter.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used for SAML deployments as SP or IdP. Single logout profile is configured on BIG-IP. Single logout begins on BIG-IP with URL containing a query parameters.
bugs.impact: Final SLO redirect to original logout URL may be missing a query parameters. Behavior will differ based on the application behind BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Issue is now addressed in a way that browsers will no longer strip query parameters from the final SLO redirect.

bugs.title: FIX with PVA offload and late binding without flow release may not execute iRules on subsequent messages
bugs.symptoms: With a virtual server configured with a fastL4 profile and a FIX profile where the fast L4 profile is configured with late binding and explicit flow migration, the first connection after a setup or restart may not correctly execute FIX iRules if the flow is not handed off to ePVA after the first FIX message.
bugs.conditions: Configure a virtual server with a fastL4 profile and a FIX profile. Configure the FastL4 profile to have late binding and explicit flow migration. Place iRules on the virtual server that trigger on FIX_MESSAGE or FIX_HEADER. Restart the BIG-IP, connect to the virtual server and begin sending FIX messages.
bugs.impact: The iRules may not trigger on the second and further messages sent to the FIX virtual server on the first connection after the restart.

bugs.title: stats self-link might include the oid twice
bugs.symptoms: The object ID might be erroneously embedded in the self-link twice.
bugs.conditions: query for stats such as https://<host>/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/p1/stats
bugs.impact: incorrect self-link returned
bugs.workaround: be mindful when parsing the self-link

bugs.title: vADC 'live-install' Downgrade from v13.1.0 is not possible
bugs.symptoms: vADC v13.1.0 has a new storage format that is incompatible with earlier versions. It should be possible to use the '--format' option of 'image2disk' to downgrade a v13.1.0 vADC system, but it is not.
bugs.conditions: Running v13.1.0, attempt software downgrade to 11.5.4, for example: image2disk --format=volumes --nosaveconfig 11.5.4
bugs.impact: request is not allowed. no changes are made.
bugs.workaround: deploy a new 11.5.4 software image via the hypervisor environment

bugs.title: During Apply Policy action, bd agent crashes, causing the machine to go Offline

bugs.title: APMD Memory leak when applying a specific access profile
bugs.symptoms: Access profile having CheckMachineCert agent, while updating profile using 'Apply access policy', each time it leaks 12096 bytes of memory.

bugs.title: PEM session created by Gx may get deleted across HA multiple switchover with CLI command
bugs.symptoms: PEM sessions may get cleaned up with terminate cause of FATAL GRACE TIMEOUT, if multiple high availability (HA) failover is being performed using the following command: tmsh run sys failover standby.

bugs.title: AFM ACL Rule Policy applied on Standby device
bugs.symptoms: In a Active/Standby setup, with a Virtual Server configured to Mirror Connection State, the Standby Device is aware of the state of connections. The Standby device apart from maintaining the state of connections, need not apply ACL policy to the mirrored connections. But in a specific case where a ACL Policy happens to have Rule with Schedules attached, the Standby happens to apply policy on mirrored connections, which also generates ACL rule hit logs.
bugs.conditions: 1) Active/Standby device setup. 2) Virtual Server with Connection Mirroring enabled. 3) ACL Policy with a Rule having a Schedule attached, and during periods of transition when a Schedule may cause a Rule to be enforced or expired.
bugs.impact: Does not impact handling of traffic. Generation of ACL Rule hit logs from Standby is unexpected, and is not desirable.
bugs.workaround: Objective: - Disable sweeper applying ACL policy on Standby device. - Sys DB tunable must disable only on Standby device. Because sys db settings are auto-sync'd to Active device as well, you must do so using the following procedure. Steps to Apply Sys DB setting only on Standby device: 1. Turn off auto-sync for the device-group. 2. Apply settings just before Rule Schedule expiry on Standby device. 3. Wait till Rule Schedule change takes effect. 4. Revert the settings to normal, and enable auto-sync again. TMSH Command Sequence: root@(BIG-IP-primary)(cfg-sync In Sync)(Standby)(/Common)(tmos) # list sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl value sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl { value "enable" <<<< Set this to 'disable' } root@(BIG-IP-primary)(cfg-sync In Sync)(Standby)(/Common)(tmos) # modify cm device-group <device-group-for-failover> auto-sync disabled root@(BIG-IP-primary)(cfg-sync In Sync)(Standby)(/Common)(tmos) # modify sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl value disable root@(BIG-IP-primary)(cfg-sync Changes Pending)(Standby)(/Common)(tmos) # list sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl value sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl { value "disable" } On Active, it's still 'enable': root@(BIG-IP-secondary)(cfg-sync Changes Pending)(Active)(/Common)(tmos) # list sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl value sys db tm.sweeper.flow.acl { value "enable" } Enable auto-sync again: root@(BIG-IP-primary)(cfg-sync In Sync)(Standby)(/Common)(tmos) # modify cm device-group <device-group-for-failover> auto-sync enable Might have to issue this run command if the device is reported as 'requiring sync'. root@(BIG-IP-primary)(cfg-sync Changes Pending)(Standby)(/Common)(tmos) # run cm config-sync to-group <device-group-for-failover>

bugs.title: APM now supports VMware Workspace ONE integration with VIDM as ID Provider
bugs.symptoms: When VMware Horizon resources are behind APM, you can see available desktops and application on VMware Workspace One (WS1) portal, but you cannot launch them.
bugs.conditions: -- VMware virtual desktops and applications are hosted on VMware Horizon behind APM. -- Authenticate with VMware Identity Manager (VIDM) and see available virtual desktops and applications on WS1 portal. -- Attempt to launch a virtual desktop or application with VMware HTML5 client.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP users get authenticated with VIDM and can see available desktops and applications on the WS1 portal, but cannot launch a desktop or application with View HTML5 client.

bugs.title: Existing IPsec tunnels reload. tmipsecd creates a core file.
bugs.symptoms: Existing IPsec tunnels reload. tmipsecd creates a core file.
bugs.conditions: Although an exact replication of the issue has not been reliable, the one instance occurred after the following conditions: -- Remote peer repeatedly tries to establish a tunnel. -- The IPsec IKEv1 daemon 'racoon' is dead.

bugs.title: Retrieving too many groups is causing out of memory errors in TMUI and VPE
bugs.symptoms: Retrieving too many groups might cause out-of-memory errors in TMUI and VPE. TMUI might end up with HTTP 502 and VPE fails with HTTP 500
bugs.conditions: LDAP/AD server with over 20,000 groups.

bugs.title: Deferenced NULL object causes core

bugs.conditions: -- TMM low on memory. -- Category Lookup agent in Access Per-Request Policy.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Changed /var/log mount options

bugs.conditions: /var/log mount options.

bugs.title: Buitin Okta Scopes Request object uses client -id and client-secret
bugs.symptoms: Buitin Okta Scopes Request object uses client credentials instead of resource server credentials.
bugs.conditions: Buitin Okta Scopes Request object

bugs.title: Inconsistent DAGv2 state between B4400 blades after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: B4400 blades in the VIPRION chassis might encounter inconsistent DAGv2 state after upgrading from v12.1.x to v13.0.0 or v13.1.0. You might see messages similar to the following continuously logged into /var/log/tmm on the Standby unit: notice CDP: Selected DAG state from primary PG 0 for CMP state 03 with clock 6765
bugs.conditions: Upgrading VIPRION B4400 blades from v12.1.x to v13.0.0 or v13.1.0.
bugs.impact: There is no traffic impact on the Active BIG-IP system, but the issue causes the Standby BIG-IP system to constantly update its DAGv2 table.
bugs.workaround: Reboot one of the B4400 blades in the Active BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Signatures page includes columns supporting future enhancements
bugs.symptoms: The 'Shareability' and 'Approval State' columns are intended to support functionality that was not included in this release. There is no way to update status for either for any AFM Dynamic Signatures. tmsh will fail with the following message: Data Input Error: Can't modify 'shareability-state', 'approval-state', or 'predicates' for a DoS signature with 'network' or 'network' family. Signatures in the HTTP family can be modified via tmsh, but that requires ASM.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned, Dynamic Signatures enabled, DNS Dynamic Signatures enabled, at least one generated DNS Dynamic Signature.
bugs.impact: No impact on traffic.

bugs.title: APM eam process may be in restart loop with a core file generated each time when log level was changed from LOGLEVEL_DEBUG3 to LOGLEVEL_ERROR.
bugs.symptoms: APM eam process might go into a restart loop, with a core file generated at each restart, when log level is changed from LOGLEVEL_DEBUG3 to LOGLEVEL_ERROR.
bugs.conditions: Change log level from LOGLEVEL_DEBUG3 to LOGLEVEL_ERROR (which you might do to implement the workaround in K82304591: OAM ASDK log files may grow to consume excessive disk space, https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K82304591).
bugs.impact: eam restart loop, with a core file generated each time it restarts.
bugs.workaround: Delete any unwanted accessgate from APM. For every accessgate configured on the APM, you must also configure and enable a corresponding accessgate on the OAM server.

bugs.title: Obfuscator not producing deterministic output
bugs.symptoms: Proactive defense challenge is not passed.
bugs.conditions: The obfuscator does not produce the same output for the same pair of key and seed. Therefore, on multi-blade devices, or on active-active deployments, when the request to the page (url=/) and the request to the javascript (/TSPD/*?type=10) each go to a different blade or a different device. More frequently, it happens when the page and javascript are loaded from the same blade, but the javascript is stored in the cache. Then another refresh, and the request goes to the second blade. Because the javascript in the cache was received from the first blade, it does not match the page.
bugs.impact: Proactive defense challenge is not passed; challenge remains on blank page on chassis.
bugs.fix: Obfuscator now uses common Random object.

bugs.title: Malformed TLS1.2 records may result in TMM segmentation fault.
bugs.symptoms: TMM receives a malformed TLS1.2 record.
bugs.impact: TMM produces a core file and takes the configured HA failover action.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: [KERBEROS SSO] Performance of LRU cache for Kerberos tickets drops gradually with the number of users
bugs.symptoms: APM performance of handling HTTP request drops gradually when Kerberos SSO is being used over period of time. Websso process CPU usage is very high during this time. The latency can vary between APM end users.
bugs.conditions: -- A large number of APM end users have logged on and are using Kerberos SSO. -- Running APM.
bugs.impact: Increased latency of HTTP request processing.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the number of cached Kerberos user tickets by lowering the cache lifetime.
bugs.fix: LRU cache performance no longer drops linearly with the number of caches Kerberos tickets, the latency of HTTP request processing has been significantly improved.

bugs.title: Disabled PHP configuration option 'allow_url_fopen'
bugs.symptoms: PHP configuration option has allow_url_fopen set to 'On'.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system uses PHP for the Configuration Utility.
bugs.impact: System security improvement is needed to disable allow_url_fopen configuration option.
bugs.fix: Changed PHP configuration of allow_url_fopen from "On" to 'Off'.

bugs.title: Enhancement to SessionDB provides timeout
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, calls made to SessionDB never return from the remote TMM.
bugs.conditions: -- Using add, update, delete, and lookup commands to remote TMM. -- SessionDB request is not returned.
bugs.impact: Calls made to SessionDB never return from the remote TMM.
bugs.fix: The system initiates a timeout after 2 seconds. If a timeout occurs, the calling command receives a result of err==ERR_TIMEOUT. A new sys db variable was added to enable the timeout for the iRule table command. It defaults to false. Below is the new definition followed by the tmsh command to set the value. # Enable or disable iRule table cmd timeout override to cause all # requests to be 'remembered' so that we do not leak them # if subsystems fail. [Tmm.SessionDB.table_cmd_timeout_override] default=false type=enum realm=common enum=|true|false|
bugs.behavior: A new sys db variable was added to enable the timeout for the iRule table command. It defaults to false. Below is the new definition followed by the tmsh command to set the value. # Enable or disable iRule table cmd timeout override to cause all # requests to be 'remembered' so that we do not leak them # if subsystems fail. [Tmm.SessionDB.table_cmd_timeout_override] default=false type=enum realm=common enum=|true|false|

bugs.title: A cold faulted SSD drive may assert the BIOS causing a failure to boot
bugs.symptoms: A drive with a SMART failure of 202 when attempting to send the command to freeze lock the drive will cause a BIOS assert that will fail to continue to boot. This freeze lock is attempted at the end of BIOS operation just before passing off to the bootloader. The SMART attribute 202 is named as "SSD Mode Status" in the SM863A data sheet and is described as follows: "The raw value indicates the current status of tantal capacitor health." These particular cold temperature failures are caused by damage to the tantalum capacitor used by the power loss protection circuitry inside the SSD.
bugs.conditions: An SSD with a SMART failure of 202.
bugs.impact: Failure to boot OS until the offending drive is removed.
bugs.workaround: Remove the faulted drive. Presumes the remaining drive has an OS installed.
bugs.fix: BIOS has been updated to determine the SMART command failure type, if it is not a SMART 202 failure then the assert will maintain. If this is a SMART 202 failure then the BIOS will not assert and will continue to boot.

bugs.title: VE OVAs is not the supported platform to run VMware guest OS customization
bugs.symptoms: VMware vCenter fails to create customization specification wizard because the BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) OVA's OSType is set to 'Other 64-bit'.
bugs.conditions: When applying VMware guest OS customization on VMware BIG-IP VE.
bugs.impact: VMware guest OS customization fails (cannot create customization specification wizard).
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: - Apply VMware guest OS customization with 'ovftool'. - Manually set OSType to 'Other 3.x Linux 64-bit'.
bugs.fix: OS type embedded in .ovf file in VE OVAs has been changed from 'Other 64-bit' to 'Other 3.x Linux 64-bit' to enable VMware guest OS customization.
bugs.behavior: In this release, the OS type set in .ovf file in the BIG-IP VE SCSI OVA images for VMware has been changed from 'Other 64bit' to 'Other 3.x Linux 64bit'. This enables 'VMware Guest Customization' via VMware vCenter.

bugs.title: With a non-LTM license (ASM, APM, etc.), ephemeral nodes will not be created for FQDN nodes/pool members.
bugs.symptoms: 1. FQDN Node/pools fails to populate with members. 2. An error similar to the following is logged in /var/log/ltm when an FQDN node or pool member is created: err mcpd[####]: 01070356:3: Ratio load balancing feature not licensed.
bugs.conditions: 1. License a BIG-IP system with non-LTM license lacking the ltm_lb_ratio feature. Such licenses include APM and/or ASM licenses for certain newer platforms which do not support the AAM module. Affected platforms include certain iSeries and Virtual Edition (VE) releases. 2. Configure an FQDN node/pool member. Do not specify a 'ratio' value.
bugs.impact: Unable to use FDQN nodes/pool members with non-LTM license.
bugs.fix: Non-LTM license (ASM, APM, etc.), ephemeral nodes are now created for FQDN nodes/pool members.

bugs.title: In partitions with default route domain != 0 request log is not showing requests
bugs.symptoms: No requests in request log when partition selected, while they can be seen when 'All [Read Only]' is selected.
bugs.conditions: Select a partition whose default route domain is not 0 (zero).
bugs.impact: No requests in request log.
bugs.workaround: As a partial workaround, you can use [All], but it's read only.
bugs.fix: Fixed filter by Source IP, which worked incorrectly in partitions whose default route domain was not 0 (zero).

bugs.title: When script-src does not exist, FPS creates the script-src directive while ignoring the policy defined by default-src
bugs.symptoms: When script-src does not exist, FPS creates the script-src directive while ignoring the policy defined by default-src. This is also true for other directives such as img-src, style-src, etc.
bugs.conditions: Content-Security-Policy configured as follows: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'unsafe-inline' For example, for the following header: default-src 'unsafe-inline' FPS modifies it to: default-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-RANDOM-VAL'
bugs.impact: Application might not work because of FPS restricting inline script execution.
bugs.fix: The 'unsafe-inline' will not be injected into script-src or style-src directives if it is present in default-src directive.

bugs.title: If Inheritance is None in the Parent Policy and there are at least 1 child policy, the number of Comments shown in Inheritance Settings is equal to number of child policies
