bugs.symptoms: If Inheritance is None in the Parent Policy and there is at least one child policy, the number of Comments shown in Inheritance Settings is equal to number of child policies.
bugs.conditions: 1) Create Parent policy and set some section's Inheritance to None. 2) Create child policy and assign it to the parent created above. 3) Go to the Parent Policy Inheritance Setting tab, you will see that number of comments for sections with None will be equal to number of child policies.
bugs.impact: There is an incorrect number of Comments shown in Inheritance Settings
bugs.fix: The correct number of comments will be shown for each section in Inheritance Setting tab for Parent Policy. In case of None inheritance nothing will be shown.

bugs.title: DoS client side challenge does not encode the Referer header.
bugs.symptoms: XSS reflection when DoS client side is enabled as a mitigation, or a proactive bot defense is enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1. Login to the client IP address and send the ab request. 2. Once the DoS attack starts, sends the curl request hl=en&q=drpdrp'-alert(1)-'drpdrp". 3. Unencoded Referer header is visible.
bugs.impact: The XSS reflection occurs after triggering the DoS attack.
bugs.fix: DoS client side challenge now encodes the Referer header.

bugs.title: Send multiple fields as username identifier in phishing alert
bugs.symptoms: If a customer has more than one field representing the username, phishing users alerts cannot be configured for all the fields.
bugs.conditions: A customer has more than one field that represents the username.
bugs.impact: Customer won't be able to configure phishing users alerts for all the fields.
bugs.fix: FPS supports sending multiple fields as the username identifier in phishing users alerts.

bugs.title: When starting up, BIG-IP 4200 does not log 'Link: is DOWN/UP' message on some interfaces.
bugs.symptoms: During the boot sequence, the statuses of some of the interfaces are not logged in /var/log/ltm, presumably because of a race with modprobe. The issue happens only during the boot sequence and never after.
bugs.conditions: -- Reboot a BIG-IP 4200 platform. -- Observe the link status messages in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.impact: There may be some interfaces for which there are no status messages. Affects the system during boot.
bugs.workaround: Only happens during the boot, the log function is good afterwards.

bugs.title: memory leak on a specific server scenario
bugs.symptoms: The bd process memory increases.
bugs.conditions: A specific server scenario of handling the traffic.
bugs.impact: Swap may be used. The kernel OOM killer may be invoked. Possible traffic disturbance.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A memory leaked related to a specific server scenario was fixed.

bugs.title: tmctl -d blade command does not work in an SNMP custom MIB
bugs.symptoms: tmctl -d blade commands run in an SNMP custom MIB fail.
bugs.conditions: -- Using an SNMP custom MIB. -- Running tmctl -d blade commands.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure a custom MIB to gather data via a tmctl -d blade command.
bugs.workaround: Instead of tmctl -d blade, use the following command: tmctl -d /var/tmstat/blade.
bugs.fix: The blade command has been added to the set of commands that can be executed by snmpd.

bugs.title: RAM Cache Exceeding Watchdog Timeout in Header Field Search
bugs.symptoms: SOD halts TMM while RAM cache is processing a header.
bugs.conditions: When RAM cache is attempting to match an ETag and fails to find it in the header field.
bugs.impact: The search continues until a match is found in memory, or a NUL byte is encountered. If the search takes too long, sod kills RAM cache on a watchdog timeout violation.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: SOD no longer halts TMM while RAM cache is processing a header.

bugs.title: On an appliance IPv6 management IP config is not correctly preserved through an .iso install
bugs.symptoms: If an IPv6 management-ip is configured when an .iso is live-installed, the configuration in the new image will have an incorrect netmask for the IPv6 management IP. Note: This is true only for IPv6 management-IP configurations; IPv4 management-ip configurations work as expected.
bugs.conditions: -- On any appliance (i.e., not blades in a cluster). -- IPv6 management IP only.
bugs.impact: IPv6 management IP config is not correctly preserved through an .iso install. Configuration load fails.
bugs.workaround: Edit the /config/bigip_base.conf file and remove the extraneous netmask, and then load the config by running the command: tmsh load sys config. To do so, follow these steps: 1. Edit /config/bigip_base.conf: -- Change this: sys management-ip <IPv6_IP_address>/64/ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff::{} -- To this: sys management-ip <IPv6_IP_address>/64{} 2. If an IPv6 default-inet6 route is configured, that configuration also must be edited in /config/bigip_base.conf: -- Change this: sys management-route default { gateway <V6_gateway_IP_address> network default } -- To this: sys management-route default-inet6 { gateway <V6_gateway_IP_address> network default-inet6 } 3. After making and saving the changes, run the following command: tmsh load sys config

bugs.title: Monitor 'min 1 of' not working as expected with FQDN nodes/members
bugs.symptoms: A pool with a monitor configured as 'min 1 of {...}' may be unavailable when one or more members configured with FQDN are down, rather than remain available as long as at least one pool member remains up.
bugs.conditions: -- Pool nodes/members are configured with FQDN. -- At least one associated monitor is defined with the 'min 1 of {...}' feature.
bugs.impact: The pool may be seen as 'offline' when one or more members are down, rather than remaining available as long as a single pool member is 'UP'.
bugs.workaround: To configure a pool with 'min 1 of{...}', specify static pool members, do not use FQDN to configure pool members.
bugs.fix: A pool with FQDN configured nodes/members and specified with a monitor of 'min 1 of {...}' remains available as long as a single pool member remains up. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation.

bugs.title: Collect bigip.license files in qkview
bugs.symptoms: bigip.license files are not collected in qkview, which can make diagnostics difficult.
bugs.conditions: Collecting qkview in all conditions.
bugs.impact: F5 Support might have difficulty diagnosing an issue if the license information is not present.
bugs.workaround: Send license files separately from qkviews.
bugs.fix: bigip.license files are collected in qkview.

bugs.title: racoon daemon for IPsec IKEv1 listens on 0.0.0.0
bugs.symptoms: The racoon daemon binds to all addresses on the Linux host.
bugs.conditions: When the IKEv1 racoon daemon processes the config file written by tmipsecd.
bugs.impact: - IPsec tunnels may be established on unexpected IP addresses on the BIG-IP system. - Port scans or security audits may show the IPsec service on unexpected IP addresses.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The auto-generated racoon daemon config file no longer listens to 0.0.0.0 'any' addresses.
bugs.behavior: In previous releases, the racoon daemon would bind to all addresses on the Linux host. In this version, The IKEv1 racoon daemon no longer listens on 0.0.0.0.

bugs.title: merged fails merging a table when a table row has incomplete keys defined.
bugs.symptoms: There is as timing issue in merged where it will fail processing a table row with incomplete keys defined.
bugs.conditions: There are no specific conditions required, only that merged is running, which is true on every BIG-IP system, when the BIG-IP system is processing a table row with incomplete keys defined. Although this issue is not dependent on configuration or traffic, it appears that it is more prevalent on vCMP hosts.
bugs.impact: There will be a few second gap in available statistics during the time when a core is being created and merged restarts.
bugs.fix: merged now detect this scenario, a table row with incomplete keys defined, and does not fail.

bugs.title: Certain header manipulations in HTTP profile may result in losing connection.
bugs.symptoms: HTTP profile has an option 'Insert X-Forwarded-For' which adds a header when a request is forwarding to a pool member. When a virtual server has iRule with a collect command like SSL::collect, it is affected by the HTTP profile processing. Same issue has an option 'Request Header Erase' available in HTTP profile.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server meets the following conditions: -- ClientSSL profile. -- HTTP profile with option 'Insert X-Forwarded-For' enabled and/or configured option 'Request Header Erase'. -- iRule that has an 'SSL::collect' command in at least two events (e.g., CLIENTSSL_HANDSHAKE and CLIENTSSL_DATA).
bugs.impact: TCP connection is reset, and no response is provided to a client.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to insert X-Forwarded-For with an appropriate IP address and/or remove headers configured in 'Request Header Erase' option of HTTP profile.
bugs.fix: An issue of a resetting connections due to configuration options 'Insert X-Forwarded-For' and 'Request Header Erase' in HTTP profile no longer happens.

bugs.title: Unexpected error when applying hotfix
bugs.symptoms: Software 'install hotfix' commands fail with a message similar to the following: Image (BIGIP-11.6.1.0.0.317.iso) has a software image entry in MCP database but does not exist on the filesystem.
bugs.conditions: Before installing the hotfix, the necessary full (base) software image prerequisite was added to the images directory, but then was removed before issuing the hotfix command. For example, to apply 'Hotfix-BIGIP-11.6.1.2.0.338-HF2.iso', the system must have access to the base image; 'BIGIP-11.6.1.0.0.317.iso'.
bugs.impact: Cannot apply hotfix until the full base image is present.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following procedure: 1. Copy the base image to the images directory on the BIG-IP system. 2. Restart the 'lind' daemon. 3. Try the hotfix installation process again.
bugs.fix: Issuing a 'install hotfix' command when the base image is not available sends the system into a 'wait' state. The process status is 'waiting for base image', which should make clear what needs to be done. When the base image becomes available (in the images directory), the hotfix installation proceeds.

bugs.title: Mirrored connections ignore the handshake timeout
bugs.symptoms: Mirrored connections that do not complete the TCP 3-way-handshake do not honor the configured TCP handshake timeout on active and standby systems.
bugs.conditions: High availability mirroring enabled on virtual server with attached FastL4 profile.
bugs.impact: Unestablished TCP sessions in the connection table stay open for the duration of the TCP idle-timeout.
bugs.fix: Mirrored connections now honor the TCP handshake timeout.

bugs.title: Incorrect output of b64 unit key hash by command f5mku -f
bugs.symptoms: The output of the b64 unit key hash is inconsistent upon each 'f5mku -f' command, whereas the hex version of the unit key hash was always correct/consistent.
bugs.conditions: Viewing output of 'f5mku -f' command.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent output of the b64 unit key.
bugs.workaround: Adding the verbose option (v) to the f5mku command will print additional information. The following command prints the hex version of the unit key header hash, which will be stable and can be used to detect changes to the unit key: f5mku -vf For example: # f5mku -vf ... -- hdr.hash = c9:0d:13:2a:74:d4:7e:31:a4:78:5e:c8:3e:9c:b5:3d:7b:65:9c:7d ...
bugs.fix: The unit key hash is now the correct length and is consistent upon each 'f5mku -f' command.

bugs.title: Access session iRules can fail with error 'Illegal argument'
bugs.symptoms: Certain Access iRules can cause an argument error to occur. Errors in iRule logs appear similar to the following: session ID lookup failed - Illegal argument (line 1).
bugs.conditions: ACCESS::session iRules are used, for example: -- ACCESS::session sid. -- ACCESS::session data get {session.server.landinguri}. -- ACCESS::session data get {session.policy.result}.
bugs.impact: Tcl error occurs and the connection is reset. The system posts the 'Illegal argument" message in the iRules logs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue that would cause the error to occur.

bugs.title: Incorrect source mac for TCP Reset with vlangroup for host traffic
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP outbound host TCP RST packets have incorrect source-mac-address.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP host traffic is exiting via VLANs in a VLAN group.
bugs.impact: TCP Reset for traffic exiting the BIG-IP system with incorrect source-mac-address, which could include monitor traffic.
bugs.workaround: Use transparent mode on the VLAN group.
bugs.fix: source-mac-address for host traffic is correctly set.

bugs.title: iControl REST improper sanitisation of data
bugs.symptoms: A few values are not properly being sanitised by iControl REST.
bugs.conditions: When using iControl REST APIs
bugs.impact: Improper sanitisation of data
bugs.workaround: Limit access to management and self-ips to trusted networks and users to limit the exposure.
bugs.fix: iControl REST is now properly sanitising data.

bugs.title: Performance regression on B4450 blade
bugs.symptoms: Performance degradation may occur for certain types of traffic when the system is under heavy traffic load. L4 and L7 performance may be degraded by up to 5% compared to previous BIG-IP releases.
bugs.conditions: - L4 and L7 traffic when system is under heavy traffic load. - VIPRION B4450 blades.
bugs.impact: You may encounter a performance degradation for certain types of traffic upon upgrading.
bugs.fix: Performance regression on B4450 blade has been eliminated.

bugs.title: 'Failed to reload dns-express db (Version).' can be logged a few times a second if DNS Express was configured on a different partition but not the current one
bugs.symptoms: 'Failed to reload dns-express db (Version).' message can be logged a few times a second if DNS Express was configured on a different partition but not the current one.
bugs.conditions: This happens only if the following conditions are true: -- The reboot occurs between partitions. -- The previous partition had a DNS Express database with zones defined. -- The new partition has a newer version of DNS Express. -- There is no DNS Express configuration defined on the new partition.
bugs.impact: There is no negative impact to traffic flow or configuration. The logs simply fill with this message.
bugs.workaround: Remove the shared DNS Express database. Important: Perform this step only if you are sure you do not want the shared DNS Express database when you reboot back to the partition it was originally created on: rm /shared/zxfrd/* -f

bugs.title: APM AppTunnels memory leak
bugs.symptoms: Using APM AppTunnels causes a slow memory leak.
bugs.conditions: Use of APM AppTunnels.
bugs.impact: The slow memory leak exhaust tmm memory over time. Traffic disrupted when tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The memory leak has been corrected.

bugs.title: Routing via iRule to a host without providing a transport from a transport-config created connection cores
bugs.symptoms: Using MR::message route command without specifying a transport to use (virtual or config) will core if the connection receiving the request was created using a transport-config.
bugs.conditions: Using MR::message route command without specifying a transport to use (virtual or config) will core if the connection receiving the request was created using a transport-config.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Specify a transport to use for creating a new outgoing connection in the MR::message route command.
bugs.fix: The system will no longer core.

bugs.title: GEO dimension query failure
bugs.symptoms: In ASM reports, when adding a filter to 'Client Countries' the filter creation fails. The system writes the following error in monpd log: SELECT SQL_CALC_FOUND_ROWS ..., FACT.country_code `id` ... Because : Unknown column 'vip_crc' in 'where clause'.
bugs.conditions: Adding 'Client Countries' filter to ASM reports.
bugs.impact: The filter creation fails.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, perform the following procedure: 1. Edit /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_entities.cfg. 2. Remove the following line from section [asm_repev_geo]: dim_authz_filter=vip_crc. 3. Restart monpd.
bugs.fix: This release removes dim_authz_filter=vip_crc from [asm_repev_geo] in monp_asm_entities.cfg.

bugs.title: DoS Overview is very slow to load data, to the point of timeout
bugs.symptoms: When logs contains more than 1 million records, loading of attacks data is extremely slow and requires many SQL queries.
bugs.impact: DoS Overview page is unusable
bugs.fix: The fix revolved around combining all the required data into a couple of queries instead of sending distinct queries for every attack.

bugs.title: When changing internal parameter 'request_buffer_size' in large request violations might not be reported
bugs.symptoms: When the internal 'request_buffer_size' is set to a large value, long requests might be blocked, and no violation is reported.
bugs.conditions: -- Internal parameter 'request_buffer_size' is set to a large value (~50 KB or larger). -- Request is long (~50 KB or longer). -- Violations found.
bugs.impact: Requests might be blocked, and no reason is reported.
bugs.workaround: Reset internal 'request_buffer_size' to default.
bugs.fix: The system now handles the case in which the internal 'request_buffer_size' is set to a large value, so long requests are no longer blocked, and the violation is reported.

bugs.title: Policies cannot be created with SAP, OWA, or SharePoint templates
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to create a security policy using "OWA Exchange", "SAP NetWeaver", or "SharePoint" Policy Template fails.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to create a security policy using "OWA Exchange", "SAP NetWeaver", or "SharePoint" Policy Templates
bugs.impact: Policy creation fails.
bugs.fix: Policies can be created using these factory templates.

bugs.title: SMTP Profile: "Use Authentication" cannot be disabled using the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Once the "Use Authentication" option has been enabled in an SMTP profile, disabling this option using the GUI does not successfully disable this setting.
bugs.workaround: Disable the "Use Authentication" option using tmsh by running the following command: modify sys smtp-server <profile-name> authentication-disabled

bugs.title: Active connections are silently dropped after HA-failover if ASM licensed and provisioned but AFM is not
bugs.symptoms: If ASM licensed and provisioned, but AFM is not licensed/provisioned, active connections are silently dropped after HA-failover. In earlier versions, active connections were reset after HA-failover if only ASM was licensed/provisioned. When AFM is also licensed/provisioned, existing active connections were always silently dropped after HA-failover.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM licensed and provisioned, but AFM is not licensed/provisioned. -- HA-failover occurs.
bugs.impact: ASM client connections are not reset, but are silently dropped after HA-failover event.

bugs.title: Memory consumption of tmm slowly increases.
bugs.symptoms: Memory consumption of tmm slowly increases.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when a session is terminated in policy evaluation phase, e.g., a client lands on the logon page and lets it times out. You can determine whether this issue is occurring by checking for memory usage as 'session' is expanded to 4 GB.
bugs.impact: Device may fail over to another unit in the high-availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.workaround: To recover from this issue, restart tmm. Note: Traffic will be disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Memory consumption of tmm no longer increases when a client allows the logon page to time out.

bugs.title: Connection drops with Fast L4 profile that has loose init and syncookie enabled
bugs.symptoms: - Client connection failures - Traffic fails to get forwarded - TMM crashes
bugs.conditions: Following FastL4 features are simultaneously enabled: - Loose Initiation - Syncookies
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable Loose Initiation and/or Syncookies
bugs.fix: Added a warning message to TMSH and the FastL4 page of the GUI if Loose Initiation and Syncookies are both enabled.

bugs.title: BIG-IP as SAML IdP/SP may include last x509 certificate found in the configured bundle in signed SAML Response or single logout message
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is used as SAML IdP, and signing is configured, BIG-IP will sign the message by configured signing key, and include last certificate from the configured signing certificate chain in the SAML protocol message. Expected behavior is to include first certificate from the configured signing certificate chain. The same applies to SAML SP generating SLO request/response messages.
bugs.conditions: All of the following: - BIG-IP is used as SAML IdP or SAML as SP with SLO configured. - BIG-IP generates signed SAML response containing assertion or SLO request/response - Configured on BIG-IP signing certificate is a security chain and not a single certificate
bugs.impact: Impact is based on the SAML implementation on the receiving end of message sent by BIG-IP. Some implementation may drop signed SAML message if last certificate from the bundle is included in the message. Other implementations will accept such signed messages. Note that signing operation itself is performed correctly by BIG-IP using configured signing certificate, and digital signature will contain correct value.
bugs.workaround: Instead of using signing certificate chain, change BIG-IP SAML IdP/SP configured signing certificate to refer to a standalone signing certificate (single X509 object) by extracting first certificate from the chain.
bugs.fix: After the fix, BIG-IP will include first certificate found within configured signing certificate (chain).

bugs.title: OAuth client stores incorrectly escaped JSON values in session variables
bugs.symptoms: 1) The slash (/) is double escaped (\\/). The slash is common in URLs. 2) Unicode escaped characters (\uXXXX) are not correctly un-escaped into UTF-8 characters, ends up unrecognizable.
bugs.conditions: Occurs in 13.1 and earlier releases when OAuth servers response in JSON, such as the OIDC User Info.
bugs.impact: APM applications who read JSON node session variables may not get the correct values.
bugs.workaround: 1) For double escaped slash, workaround is like, session.oauth.client.last.UserInfo.picture = return [string map {{\\/} /} [ mcget {session.oauth.client.last.UserInfo.picture} ]] 2) For incorrect UTF-8 characters, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Unicode escaped characters are now correctly handled.

bugs.title: Firewall Rule hit counts are not auto updated after a Reset is done
bugs.symptoms: When a rule is selected and the "Reset Count" button is clicked, the command is executed but rule stats are not updated in the UI
bugs.conditions: This occurs when resetting rule hit count stats in the UI.
bugs.impact: Incorrect (stale) statistics are seen
bugs.workaround: Refresh the page
bugs.fix: Rule stats are now correctly updated in the UI after a 'Reset Count' is initiated.

bugs.title: Allow unsigned DNS notifies if a DNS express zone's target server has no TSIG key configured
bugs.symptoms: If a DNS Express zone that has Verify Notify TSIG checked gets a notify with no TSIG at all, unsigned notifies are not processed.
bugs.conditions: Unigned notify is received when Verify Notify TSIG is checked.
bugs.impact: Unsigned notifies are not processed
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This fix corrects an issue in TSIG handling when combined with NOTIFY messages for zone transfers

bugs.title: PEM Diameter stats may have errors when Diameter requests and responses are asynchronous
bugs.symptoms: Statistics provided by PEM Diameter applications may be in error.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM configured with Gx, Sd, or Gy. -- Diameter requests and responses processed asynchronously.
bugs.impact: May impact logic that is dependent on statistics.
bugs.workaround: Configure the Diameter solution such that requests and responses are synchronous.

bugs.title: TMM hud_message_ctx leak
bugs.symptoms: There is a TMM memory issue caused by leaked hud_message_ctx objects, each holding a websockets_frame.
bugs.conditions: Running WebSocket traffic that needs to be processed by a plugin like ASM.
bugs.impact: Increasing TMM memory usage leading to eventual service outage. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The memory leak in TMM has been fixed.

bugs.title: cs_qualified_urls bigdb does not cause configured URLs to be qualified.
bugs.symptoms: cs_qualified_urls is configured but is not functional.
bugs.conditions: -- cs_qualified_urls is configured. -- A request to the URL listed in the bigdb arrives. -- The URL is seen as non-qualified although configured.
bugs.impact: URLs that are not supposed to getting through configuration.
bugs.fix: Fixed a bigdb issue with cs_qualified_urls variable.

bugs.title: PEM Gx/Gy/Sd sessions ignore DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY result code from PCRF/OCS
bugs.symptoms: PEM session ignore DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY result code for any CCR request from PCRF/OCS
bugs.conditions: If PCRF/OCS respond with DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY result code
bugs.impact: PEM Gx/Gy/Sd sessions retries CCR requests towards PCRF/OCS
bugs.fix: PEM Gx/Gy/Sd sessions will not retry CCR request if DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY result code is received

bugs.title: A VLAN delete can result in unrelated VLAN FDB entries being flushed on shared VLAN member interfaces
bugs.symptoms: FDB flushing on VLAN deletes is performed by VLAN member interface reference only, without regard to VLAN tags. This can result in unrelated VLAN FDB entries also being flushed on shared VLAN member interfaces.
bugs.conditions: Issuing a VLAN delete with other VLANs using shared tagged member interfaces with the VLAN being deleted.
bugs.impact: FDB entries for unrelated VLANs will be flushed if they share the same tagged VLAN member interfaces as the VLAN being deleted.
bugs.fix: Correct FDB flushing on VLAN deletes, by limiting the scope to be VLAN specific.

bugs.title: dos.maxicmpframesize and dos.maxicmp6framesize sys db variables does not work for fragmented ICMP packets
bugs.symptoms: ICMP/ICMPv6 fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmpframesize is not counted in stats for 'ICMP frame too large' DoS vector.
bugs.conditions: -- ICMP fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmpframesize is received. -- ICMPv6 fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmpframesize is received.
bugs.impact: -- ICMP fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmpframesize is not dropped. -- ICMP fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmpframesize is not counted in stats for 'ICMP frame too large' DoS vector. -- ICMPv6 fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmp6framesize is not dropped. -- ICMPv6 fragmented packet with size larger than dos.maxicmp6framesize is not counted in stats for 'ICMP frame too large' DoS vector.
bugs.fix: ICMP/ICMPv6 fragmented packets are now dropped if their size is larger than dos.maxicmpframesize/dos.maxicmp6framesize. Drops are counted for 'ICMP frame too large' DoS vector stats.

bugs.title: TMM crash with SIGSEGV on update iclient conn_stats
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash with SIGSEGV on update iclient conn_stats
bugs.conditions: Connections are abandoned by external client. These connections might be suffering from connection closing in mid-conversation.
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. This is very rare event.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: The system now handles this condition, so the tmm crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: FDB entries for existing VLANs may be flushed when creating a new VLAN.
bugs.symptoms: FDB entries on existing VLAN trunk member interfaces may be flushed when creating a new VLAN.
bugs.conditions: - Creating a new VLAN with existing VLANs using trunk members. - STP is enabled on its trunk member.
bugs.impact: FDB entries on existing VLAN trunk member interfaces may be flushed when creating a new VLAN. This will result in potential network saturation.
bugs.workaround: To avoid the FDB flushing on trunk member interfaces of existing, unrelated VLANs, ensure that STP is disabled on its trunk member.

bugs.title: The dynconfd daemon uses UDP ports inefficiently
bugs.symptoms: When performing DNS queries to resolve FQDN node names to IP addresses, the dynconfd daemon may open UDP ports in excess of what is actually needed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using FQDN node names, with multiple system DNS name servers configured.
bugs.impact: The dynconfd daemon uses more UDP ports than is strictly necessary.
bugs.fix: The dynconfd daemon makes more efficient use of UDP ports when performing DNS queries to resolve FQDN node names to IP addresses.

bugs.title: RESOLV::lookup iRule command can trigger crash with slow resolver
bugs.symptoms: If thousands of connections are serviced by an iRule that performs a lookup for the same FQDN before the FQDN can be resolved, tmm may crash.
bugs.conditions: iRule with RESOLV::lookup. Slow DNS resolver. Thousand of connections triggering resolution of the same name.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove RESOLV::lookup from the workflow if it is not required.
bugs.fix: The scenario now works as expected and no longer results in a crash.

bugs.title: Log level change not saved to UCS.
bugs.symptoms: Changing the log level for an access policy using TMSH, and save this configuration into an UCS. Once restoring this UCS, you must to reload the Access :: Overview : Event Logs : Settings page in order to see the change in Admin UI.
bugs.conditions: -- Changing the log level for an access policy using TMSH. -- Saving this configuration into an UCS.. -- Restoring this UCS.
bugs.impact: Log level changes are lost. You must reload the Access :: Overview : Event Logs : Settings page in order to see the change in the GUI.

bugs.title: Creating a pool with a new node always assigns the partition of the pool to that node.
bugs.symptoms: When creating a node while creating a pool, the partition of the node is set to the one of the pool regardless of what was expected. For example, after running the command below, the new node will be assigned to differentpartition: root@(v13)(Active)(/differentpartition)(tmos)# create ltm pool my_pool2 members add { /Common/172.16.199.33:0 }
bugs.conditions: Creating a node while creating a pool in a partition different from the node.
bugs.impact: The node is displayed in the wrong partition.
bugs.workaround: Create a node separately and then add it to the pool.

bugs.title: User gets blocking page instead of captcha during brute force attack
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected blocking page while captcha is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Brute force configured with alarm and captcha mitigation. -- The only source configured is username. -- These are the first failed login requests after a system start up or after a login page configuration change.
bugs.impact: Unexpected blocking page mitigation where captcha mitigation was expected.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Access the login page at least 10 times within 5 minutes. -- Run the following command: tmsh modify sys db asm.cs_qualified_urls value <YOUR_LOGIN_URL>
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with unexpected blocking page while captcha is configured.

bugs.title: Searching and Reseting Audit Logs not working as expected
bugs.symptoms: Clicking the Search and Reset buttons on Audit Logs might post the following error message: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: Clicking the 'Search' or 'Reset' button on Audit Logs.
bugs.impact: Cannot search Audit Logs.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh or bash.
bugs.fix: Searching and Reseting Audit Logs now works as expected.

bugs.title: IPsec: invalid SPI notifications in IKEv1 can cause v1 racoon faults from dangling phase2 SA refs
bugs.symptoms: Deleting SAs on a remote peer can cause improper handling in the IKEv1 racoon daemon when invalid SPI notifications are processed.
bugs.conditions: Events causing deletion of phase one IKE SAs.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels will halt or restart. Connectivity between remote private networks will be interrupted.
bugs.fix: Phase one and phase two SA relationships are now more robust, tolerating operations that occur in any order, so tearing down old data structures will be done safely.

bugs.title: LRO performance impact with BWC and FastL4 virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Using Bandwidth controller (BWC) might result in a very large drop in performance of up to 75%. In this release, Large receive offload (LRO) is enabled by default.
bugs.conditions: -- BWC is configured. -- Virtual server has a FastL4 profile assigned. -- LRO is enabled (enabled by default in 13.1.0).
bugs.impact: Very large performance impact to the BWC policy (up to 75%). For example, if the BWC policy rate limit is set to 100Mb, the actual rate limit could be 25Mb.
bugs.workaround: Disabling LRO recaptures most of the performance degradation related to using FastL4. To disable LRO (this is a system-wide setting), run the following command: tmsh modify sys db tm.largereceiveoffload value disable Important note: Although you can disable LRO to recapture much of the 13.0.0-level performance, you will likely still experience some impact: 2-5% for small files, 17-22% degradation for the '10 requests per connection' benchmark. The only guaranteed way to avoid performance degradation is to remain on version 13.0.0.

bugs.title: Machine Info agent does not collect complete information on disconnected network adapters
bugs.symptoms: On Mac OS X, the BIG-IP APM Machine Info agent does not collect information for disconnected network adapters. On Microsoft Windows, the BIG-IP APM Machine Info agent does not collect the MAC address of disconnected network adapters.
bugs.conditions: Machine info agent is configured in the access policy.
bugs.impact: Access policy evaluation may yield incorrect results if a access policy node depends on this information.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: TMM may crash in some circumstances with VLAN failsafe
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when managing traffic in response to the VLAN failsafe traffic generating mechanisms
bugs.conditions: - VLAN failsafe is configured with low timers. - VLAN failsafe is triggered and multiple responses are received for traffic generating in fast succession.
bugs.impact: A TMM may core file may be produced. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Relax the timer to the default VLAN failsafe timer setting.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes in some circumstances with VLAN failsafe.

bugs.title: APMD intermittently crash when processing access policies
bugs.symptoms: APMD process may crash intermittently (rare) when processing access policies.
bugs.conditions: This rarely encountered issue occurs when any one of the following conditions exist: -- iRule is configured with 'ACCESS::policy evaluate'. -- NTLM authentication configured and ECA plugin is involved (for example VDI RDG). -- Kerberos authentication is configured with RBA enabled.
bugs.impact: APM end users cannot pass access policy, cannot login.
bugs.fix: APMD no longer intermittently crashes when processing access policies.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing SSL forward proxy traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing SSL forward proxy traffic
bugs.conditions: SSL forward proxy enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM now correctly processes SSL forward proxy traffic

bugs.title: Monitor Escaping is not changed when upgrading from 11.6.x to 12.x and later
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading, monitor attributes such as receive string and send string might contain escape sequences that must be processed after the upgrade. However, due to a problem introduced by the LTM policy upgrade script, this processing is not performed, resulting in monitors not functioning correctly after the upgrade. Note: Without LTM policies in the configuration, monitors upgrade without problem.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading and rolling forward monitor configuration data. -- LTM policy data present.
bugs.impact: Monitors may not work after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release addresses the underlying problem so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Inter TMM Caching Delay
bugs.symptoms: In some rare circumstances on VE instances, the transmission of updated cache information from TMM to TMM can be delayed.
bugs.conditions: VE instances.
bugs.impact: Different TMM hot content caches may serve different versions of the same document from cache.

bugs.title: Scheduled blob and current blob no longer work after restarting BIG-IP or PCCD daemon
bugs.symptoms: When there are scheduled firewall rules, and the BIG-IP system is restarted or PCCD daemon is restarted, new blob compilation succeeds, but TMM fails to activate the new blob. Both GUI and TMSH show error status: Firewall rules deployment failed. After the system gets in this state it cannot be fixed except by removing or disabling all scheduled firewall rules.
bugs.conditions: -- There are scheduled firewall rules. -- The BIG-IP system is restarted or the PCCD daemon is restarted.
bugs.impact: After this failure, firewall rules are not applied on data traffic.
bugs.workaround: Remove or disable all scheduled firewall rules.
bugs.fix: New blob deployed and new firewall rules applied successfully.

bugs.title: APM does not honor per-farm HTML5 client disabling at the View Connection Server
bugs.symptoms: Current logic for determining whether to offer HTML5 client option works for Horizon 6.x (and earlier) but it does not work for Horizon 7.x. With Horizon 7.x, VMware has enhanced the XML so that each resource includes a flag to indicate whether HTML5 client is enabled (absence of <html-access-disabled/> tag). APM does not honor this flag to show HTML5 client option to APM end user only if it has been enabled for that resource.
bugs.conditions: -- APM webtop with a VMware View resource assigned. -- HTML5 Access disabled for some of the RDS farms managed by the broker.
bugs.impact: APM offers HTML5 client launch option and actually runs it if requested, although it is disabled at the backend.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: For Horizon 7.x, the system now honors the <html5-access-disabled> flag in broker responses to disable HTML5 client for those RDS desktops and apps that have this flag set.
bugs.behavior: Before this fix, all the RDS desktops and apps were available for HTML5 client if it was installed on VCS. Now, for those desktops and apps where HTML5 access has been deliberately disabled at the broker, only the native client option will be available.

bugs.title: With DTLS version1, when client hello uses version1.2, handshake shall proceed
bugs.symptoms: With DTLS version1, when client hello uses version1.2, handshake fails with error of :unsupported version".
bugs.conditions: DTLS version1 handshake: Handshake version 1.0 . (0xfeff) Client hello version 1.2(0xfefd)
bugs.impact: DTLS functionalities.
bugs.fix: In this case, we shall still proceed to perform handshake instead of bailing out with "unsupported version" error.

bugs.title: URI reported in alert may not contain the actual traffic URI
bugs.symptoms: URI reported in alert may not contain the actual traffic URI.
bugs.conditions: The alert was triggered for a wildcard-configured URL.
bugs.impact: Request URI is not reported correctly. The reported URI will contain the configured URL instead of traffic URL. For example: -- A configured URL: /*. -- Traffic URI: /a/b/c?n=v. -- Reported URI: /*. -- Reported URI should be traffic URI: /a/b/c?n=v.
bugs.fix: FPS always normalizes traffic URI and reports that in the alert payload.

bugs.title: Loop of JS errors in Edge browser
bugs.symptoms: Loop of JS errors in console similar to the following: SCRIPT5007: Unable to get property 'timeStamp' of undefined or null reference 0844f74b58ab1800353ea6e389110166b33640975ab33f8c35b93e132e10aad2.js (839,290) SCRIPT5007: Unable to get property 'length' of undefined or null reference 0844f74b58ab1800353ea6e389110166b33640975ab33f8c35b93e132e10aad2.js (57,25)
bugs.conditions: -- Edge browser. -- Automatic transaction configured. -- Popup dialog box is waiting for FPS end user input. -- FPS end user inserts 1024 chars in password field.
bugs.impact: This might result in slowness of user environment. Errors are posted in the console.
bugs.workaround: Enable the -n flag to disable the anti-debug feature. To do so, add -n flag to /shared/datasync/compiler_conf/cs_fpm/OBF_FLAGS.

bugs.title: File Content Detection Formats are not exported in Policy XML
bugs.symptoms: If a policy is configured with Data Guard enabled with File Content Detection, the selected File Content Detection Formats are not correctly exported in the Policy XML. When the policy is then imported, the Data Guard settings will be invalid and cannot be changed until the File Content Detection Formats are configured again.
bugs.conditions: A policy is configured with Data Guard enabled with File Content Detection, and then exported in XML format.
bugs.impact: When the policy is then imported, the Data Guard settings will be invalid and cannot be changed until the File Content Detection Formats are configured again. The formerly selected file content formats will not be correctly identified.
bugs.workaround: Use Binary Policy import/export.
bugs.fix: File Content Detection Formats are correctly exported.

bugs.title: Enable AJAX Response Page or Single Page Application support causes the part of the web page failed to load.
bugs.symptoms: AJAX requests are not sent, JavaScript errors, AJAX-based web-app malfunctions.
bugs.conditions: 1a. Single page application enabled either via a DoS application profile or in an ASM policy. 1b. AJAX Response Page enabled via ASM policy. 2. Web Application client side code uses jQuery or any other AJAX clientside framework.
bugs.impact: AJAX request might not be sent, and the overall website's clientside functionality related to the AJAX requests might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Disable Single Page Application support.
bugs.fix: Fixed Single Page Application AJAX hook to support the AJAX response onload callback re-assignment.

bugs.title: Adding user defined signature on device with many policies is very slow
bugs.symptoms: Adding or modifying a user-defined signature on a device with many policies is very slow.
bugs.conditions: The user adds or modifies a user-defined signature.
bugs.impact: The process takes a long time.
bugs.fix: Adding or modifying a user-defined signature now takes a reasonable amount of time.

bugs.title: If tmm was restarted during an attack, the attack might appear ongoing in GUI
bugs.symptoms: Attack appears ongoing, even though it ended.
bugs.conditions: Rare condition of tmm restart during an attack.
bugs.impact: The GUI falsely shows the attack as ongoing, even though it ended.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Now, when tmm is restarted during an attack, this specific attack is shown as ended in DoS overview page after 15 minutes.

bugs.title: Changes to a parent policy that has no active children are not synced to the secondary chassis slots.
bugs.symptoms: Changes to a parent policy that has no active children are not synced to the secondary chassis slots.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Having a parent policy that has no active children.
bugs.impact: On a chassis failover, the new Primary slot will have an outdated version of the parent policy.
bugs.fix: Changes to a parent policy that has no active children are now synced to the secondary chassis slots.

bugs.title: WMI monitor sends logging data for credentials when no credentials specified
bugs.symptoms: A properly configured WMI monitor requires username and password credentials; but when these are omitted from the configuration, logging data is sent in place of the username and password (with the monitored object likely being marked 'down'). Because username/password credentials are required, the monitor should have been identified as wrongly configured before the monitor is marked down.
bugs.conditions: A WMI monitor is configured without including the required username/password credentials.
bugs.impact: The monitored object will be marked 'down'.
bugs.workaround: Configure the WMI monitor to include the username/password credentials.

bugs.title: WMI monitor on invalid node never transitions to DOWN
bugs.symptoms: A WMI monitor configured for an invalid node defaults to 'UP', and never transitions to 'DOWN'. Upon loading a configuration, a node defaults to 'UP' as an initial probe is sent based on the monitor configuration, and the node is then marked 'DOWN' as probes timeout or monitor responses indicate an error. However, an WMI monitor probe sent to a non-existent node is not detected as an error, and that node may persist in an 'UP' state (not transitioning to 'DOWN' as expected, such as after expiration of the configured monitor timeout).
bugs.conditions: WMI monitor is configured for an invalid node address, or for a node address on which no WMI service is running.
bugs.impact: The node persists in an 'UP' state, even though no WMI service is available, or that node does not exist.
bugs.workaround: An additional node monitor can be created to confirm the node is available (which may be a partial solution in some configurations). Using a non-WMI monitor (such as TCP) to probe availability of the WMI service on the target node may be possible in other scenarios.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system may connect to an OCSP server using an unexpected source IP address
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems configured to perform OCSP Stapling may connect to an OCSP server using an unexpected source IP address. The source IP address picked by the BIG-IP system may be something that doesn't exist at all in its configuration. Additionally, the source IP address picked by the BIG-IP system may appear corrupted or invalid to an Administrator (for example: 0.0.0.112).
bugs.conditions: Required configuration: 1) The BIG-IP system is running a version prior to 13.0.0. 2) The BIG-IP system is deployed as an IPv4/IPv6 multihoming device. 3) The DNS Resolver used by the OCSP Stapling configuration belongs to a non-0 route domain. 4) The virtual servers performing OCSP Stapling belong to a non-0 route domain different than the one used by the DNS Resolver. 5) Virtual servers using OCSP Stapling include both IPv4 and IPv6 destinations. 6) The OCSP server FQDN resolves to an A record. With these conditions in place, the issue occurs when a client attempts a connection to one of the OCSP Stapling-enabled IPv6 virtual servers, and this needs to connect to an IPv4 OCSP server. The source IP address used by the BIG-IP system will be an IPv4 address containing the last 4 bytes of an IPv6 Self-IP address configured on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails to perform OCSP Stapling, and the unusual traffic may trigger alarms on your network. The actual impact is limited, as clients who request validation of the certificate status and do not get it should be able to perform it on their own.
bugs.workaround: Where possible, you can work around this issue by re-configuring the BIG-IP system so that some of the conditions required for this issue to occur no longer apply.

bugs.title: Deselect a compression provider at the end of a job and reselect a provider for a new job
bugs.symptoms: The system might potentially retain a compression context, even though there is no data to be compressed or decompressed. This can affect the calculation of the load of the compression provider.
bugs.conditions: -- A connection is up. -- Compression context is active. -- There is no data for the compression provider.
bugs.impact: It affects the compression provider selection.
bugs.fix: The system now deselects a provider at the end of a compression/decompression operation, and reselects a provider at the beginning of another compression/decompression operation.

bugs.title: Monitor's adaptive-limit is not restricted to a minimum of the adaptive noise floor
bugs.symptoms: Setting an adaptive monitor's 'adaptive-limit' below the value of the db variable 'bigd.adaptive.default_noise_floor' behaves as though the limit is the same as the 'noise floor'. By default this is 100ms.
bugs.conditions: Setting an adaptive monitor's 'adaptive-limit' below the value of the db variable 'bigd.adaptive.default_noise_floor'.
bugs.impact: Monitor is still marked up even if the delay in the server's response is higher than the adaptive-limit configured for the monitor.
bugs.workaround: Change 'bigd.adaptive.default_noise_floor' to be less than the desired adaptive-limit, or use an adaptive-limit larger than 100ms.

bugs.title: LTM Policy internal compilation error
bugs.symptoms: To enable maximum performance, LTM Policies undergo a compilation process, where they are transformed to a compact binary representation. An issue was discovered where the transformation is being done incorrectly under certain circumstances.
bugs.conditions: While not common, certain LTM Policy combinations will be transformed to binary representation where certain internal parameters are incorrect.
bugs.impact: The tmm process may experience an unexpected restart, or a policy action may not run as expected.
bugs.fix: LTM Policies are correctly transformed to their high-performance, compact binary representations.

bugs.title: VPN tunnel adapter stays up in some cases
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, VPN tunnel adapter created by VPN client stays up even when tunnel is disconnected.
bugs.conditions: Application launch on VPN establishment is configured on APM and launched application is not closed
bugs.impact: Cosmetic. No functionality impact. Subsequent launch of VPN will create a new tunnel adapter
bugs.workaround: Close the launched application

bugs.title: When BIG-IP systems are deployed as SAML IdP, the Single Logout Request processing fails the optional field 'Name ID' is missing in the request.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is deployed as SAML Identity Provider (IdP), during the processing of the Single Logout Request, if NameID is empty in the request, the Single Logout Request fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the SAML Single Logout Request has empty NameID field in the request.
bugs.impact: The processing of the SAML Single Logout request fails.

bugs.title: asm_start is consuming too much memory
bugs.symptoms: asm_start is consuming too much memory.
bugs.conditions: Roll forward a device with a large ASM configuration.
bugs.impact: Increase memory pressure on the device.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command: restart asm
bugs.fix: asm_start no longer increases its memory footprint during upgrade.

bugs.title: Database cleaning failure may allow MySQL space to fill the disk entirely
bugs.symptoms: Database cleaning failure may allow MySQL space to fill the disk entirely, which prevents any modification of ASM policy configuration. In /var/log/ts/asm_config_server.log you might see these errors repeatedly: Jun 9 09:38:45 10gal-f5-5000-2 crit g_server_rpc_handler.pl[16654]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl,F5::ASMConfig::Handler::handle_error): Code: 999, Error message = DBD::mysql::db do failed: The table 'NEGSIG_SIGNATURES' is full
bugs.conditions: This occurs if database cleaning failures occur.
bugs.impact: Disk will fill up, and you will be unable to modify ASM policies.

bugs.title: UlrCat custom database feed list does not work when the URL contains a www prefix or capital letters.
bugs.symptoms: If a UrlCat custom database feed list has URLs containing a www prefix or capital letters, the URLs are not categorized when queried.
bugs.conditions: The UrlCat custom database feed list with URL containing www prefix or capital letters
bugs.impact: Improper classification
bugs.workaround: Using an iRule can help classify the URL.
bugs.fix: Normalized the URL before putting in the custom database.

bugs.title: Link from iApps Components page to Policy Rules invalid
bugs.symptoms: In an application that contains a Local Traffic policy, the link from the Components page to the Rule will not be valid.
bugs.conditions: -- Application creates or contains a Local Traffic Policy. -- Click the link from the iApps Components page to the Policy Rules page.
bugs.impact: Cannot navigate to the policy rule directly from the Components page.
bugs.workaround: Click on the Policy within the Components page to navigate to the Rule from that page.
bugs.fix: Link from iApps Components page to Policy Rules now navigates to the Rule, as expected.

bugs.title: X509_EXTENSION memory blocks leak when C3D forges the certificate.
bugs.symptoms: One X509_EXTENSION memory block leaks when C3D forges the certificate.
bugs.conditions: When C3D forges the certificate.
bugs.impact: X509_EXTENSION memory blocks leak when forged certificate is successful.
bugs.fix: The system now frees the leaked X509_EXTENSION when C3D forges the certificate.

bugs.title: Fragmented IPv6 packets not handled correctly on Virtual Edition
bugs.symptoms: Use of IP fragmentation with IPv6 packets might not be handled correctly by BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) platforms. The initial fragmented are received, but subsequent fragments are discarded.
bugs.conditions: VE with IPv6 packets and IP fragmentation.
bugs.impact: Traffic which depends upon fragmented IPv6 packets will not be successfully processed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: These fragments are now handled correctly in the same manner as IPv4.

bugs.title: IPsec: responder N(cookie) in SA_INIT response handled incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: IKEv2 negotiation fails when a responder uses N(cookie) in the SA_INIT response, because the BIG-IP system does not expect a second response with the same zero message_id always used by SA_INIT.
bugs.conditions: Any time a responder sends N(cookie) in the first response to SA_INIT from a BIG-IP initiator.
bugs.impact: The SA negotiation fails when a responder includes N(cookie) in a SA_INIT response, because a second response appears to have an out-of-order message ID when BIG-IP believe the first message_id of zero was already handled earlier.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly tracks a need to receive a SECOND response with message_id zero, to finish the SA_INIT exchange, whenever the first SA_INIT response caused the BIG-IP system to resend the first request with the cookie included.

bugs.title: The change of APM log settings will reset the SSL session cache.
bugs.symptoms: If you change the configuration of APM log settings, it might cause the SSL session cache to be reset. Also, subsequent resumption of SSL sessions may fail after such change causing a situation where full ssl handshakes may occur more frequently.
bugs.conditions: -- Change the configuration of APM log settings. -- SSL session cache is not empty.
bugs.impact: The change of APM log settings resets the SSL session cache, which causes the SSL session to initiate full-handshake instead of abbreviated re-negotiation.
bugs.workaround: Follow this procedure: 1. Change access policy. 2. The status of that access policy changes to 'Apply Access Policy'. 3. Re-apply that.
bugs.fix: The change of APM log settings now limits its effect on APM module instead of affecting other (SSL) module's data.

bugs.title: TMM core under heavy load with PEM
bugs.symptoms: An internal race condition when deleting stale PEM data may cause a TMM core due to a use after free.
bugs.conditions: PEM policies configured. The crash is more likely with CGNAT / FWNAT configured and after a CMP state change such as after a blade failure.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The race condition is eliminated. TMM does not core under heavy load with PEM.

bugs.title: Tcp-half-open monitors might mark a node up or down in error
bugs.symptoms: The tcp-half-open monitor might mark a node or pool member up when it is actually down, or down when it is actually up, when multiple transparent monitors within multiple 'bigd' processes probe the same IP-address/port.
bugs.conditions: All of the following are true: -- There are multiple bigd processes running on the BIG-IP system. -- There are multiple tcp-half-open monitors configured to monitor the same IP address. -- One or more of the monitored objects are up and one or more of the monitored objects are down.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system might occasionally have an incorrect node or pool-member status, where future probes may fix an incorrect status.
bugs.workaround: You can use any of the following workarounds: -- Configure bigd to run in single process mode by running the following command: tmsh modify sys db bigd.numprocs value 1 -- Use a tcp monitor in place of the tcp-half-open monitor. -- Configure each transparent monitor for different polling cycles to reduce the probability that an 'up' response from the IP address/port is mistakenly viewed as a response to another monitor that is currently 'down' (or vice-versa).

bugs.title: tmm ASSERT %s spdy pcb initialized
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when using SPDY with iClient over iSession. System logs a message similar to the following: notice panic: ../modules/hudfilter/spdy/spdy.c:4108: Assertion "spdy pcb initialized" failed.
bugs.conditions: Connections are abandoned by external client. These connections might be suffering from connection closing in mid-conversation.
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove SPDY.
bugs.fix: The system now handles this condition, so the tmm crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: IPv6 RADIUS servers not supported for remote authentication
bugs.symptoms: Authenticating against an IPv6 RADIUS server is not supported, only an IPv4 server.
bugs.conditions: This applies to remote authentication to log on to the BIG-IP system for management purposes.
bugs.impact: Logon operation will time out, as if the server did not respond.
bugs.workaround: Use an IPv4 server. If you have an IPv6 management IP, then you will need to have the IPv4 server reachable over a dataplane VLAN.
bugs.fix: Support for IPv6 RADIUS servers has been added.

bugs.title: SNMP performance can be impacted by a long list of allowed-addresses
bugs.symptoms: If the SNMP configuration includes a long list of allowed-addresses in the configuration then it can impact SNMP performance.
bugs.conditions: -- The SNMP daemon consults a system file to determine whether a request can be serviced. -- There is a long list of allowed addresses in the configuration.
bugs.impact: Potentially slow SNMP response.
bugs.workaround: Make the list of allowed addresses be the minimum set of your clients.
bugs.fix: The daemon code is now more efficient.

bugs.title: gtm::host iRule validation for ipv4 and ipv6 addresses
bugs.symptoms: gtm::host iRule isn't validating that the host given matches the type of WideIP it is attached to.
bugs.conditions: An AAAA-type wideip with a ipv4 gtm::host iRule, or A-type wideip with an ipv6 gtm::host iRUle.
bugs.impact: Incorrect host information was being returned.
bugs.workaround: Only attach gtm::host of IPv4 type to A-type WideIPs, and gtm::host rules of IPv6 to AAAA-type WideIPs.
bugs.fix: FIxed issue allowing incorrect gtm::host iRule commands to trigger on incorrect wideip types.

bugs.title: Pools do not appear as expected after deploying iApp via iWorkflow
bugs.symptoms: Only two of three pools are visible in the iApp view on the BIG-IP system after deploying via iWorflow 2.2, though the pool can be found as expected in the Pools view.
bugs.conditions: -- After deploying via iWorflow 2.2. -- Using iApp to view configured pools.
bugs.impact: Unreliable query response can result in unexpected behavior.
bugs.workaround: Do not rely on the iApps Component View, but inspect BIG-IP (management GUI) Local Traffic pages such as Local Traffic :: Pools : Pool List or examine the /config/bigip.conf file to ascertain whether a desired BIG-IP configuration has been created.

bugs.title: LTM Policy error message: Action occurs before conditions
bugs.symptoms: With LTM Policy now supporting more tmm events, you may experience an error when updating an LTM Policy and see one of the following error messages: -- Policy '<name>', rule '<name>'; defines an action which occurs before one of its conditions, or before a condition in an earlier rule with lower ID. -- Policy '<name>'; an action occurs before conditions in another rule. For best-match, all actions must happen later than all conditions.
bugs.conditions: You have defined a policy where at least one of the actions is set to fire at a time before the associated condition. For example, defining an action to occur at http-request time which depends on a condition that is evaluated at http-response time. For first-match policies, rules are validated in ID/ordinal order, and actions events on later rules must occur at or after condition events in the current and prior rules. For best-match policies, all actions must occur at or after than all conditions. For all-match policies, action and condition events need to be consistent with a rule, and there is no inter-rule dependence.
bugs.impact: Policy cannot be saved.
bugs.fix: LTM Policy supports more LTM framework events, so policy authors need to be aware of event ordering and ensure that actions occur at or after associated conditions.

bugs.title: TMM may leak memory when processing SSL Forward Proxy traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may leak memory when processing SSL Forward Proxy traffic.
bugs.conditions: SSL forward proxy enabled.
bugs.impact: Increasing memory consumption over time, potentially leading to a TMM crash and failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer leaks memory when processing SSL Forward Proxy traffic

bugs.title: Delivery of HUDEVT_SENT messages at shutdown by SSL may cause tmm restart
bugs.symptoms: During flow shutdown, SSL may deliver HUDEVT_SENT messages, causing additional messages to be queued by higher filters, which may result in a tmm crash and restart.
bugs.conditions: This happens in response to a relatively rare condition that occurs during shutdown, such as HUDEVT_SENT queued after HUDCTL_SHUTDOWN.
bugs.impact: Possible tmm restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: When access to APM is denied, system changes connection mode to ALWAYS_DISCONNECTED
bugs.symptoms: When access to APM is denied, Edge Client goes into ALWAYS_DISCONNECTED mode. Hence, it does not retry to establish VPN tunnel.
bugs.conditions: -- Edge Client installed in ALWAYS_CONNECTED mode (locked client). -- Access to APM is denied.
bugs.impact: No VPN tunnel is established, even if APM becomes accessible momentarily.

bugs.title: Running 'load sys config merge verify' will add new users to the PostGres database
bugs.symptoms: Running 'load sys config merge verify' will add new users to the PostGres database. The system posts an error similar to the following: 010719a2:3: PostgreSQL database error: ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "auth_user_pkey" DETAIL: Key (name)=(admin1) already exists.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs only under the following conditions: -- 'load config merge verify' of configurations including user definition. -- Attempt to create user with same name using 'load config merge', 'create user', or GUI options.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to use the verify argument when using 'load sys config merge' with configurations containing user definitions. 'verify' argument to 'load sys config' does not prevent or rollback side effects
bugs.workaround: Manually remove the user data from the PSQL database; from a bash prompt: psql -U postgres \c tmdb DELETE FROM auth_user WHERE name='admin1' DROP OWNED BY admin1 DROP ROLE admin1 DROP SCHEMA admin1 CASCADE \q

bugs.title: Qkview truncates tmstat snapshot files
bugs.symptoms: Qkview truncates the snapshot files it collects in /shared/tmstat/snapshots/.
bugs.conditions: Files are larger than 5 MiB, or the 'max file size' limit specified when running Qkview (the -s argument). Note: 5 MiB is qkview utility's default maximum file size value.
bugs.impact: Snapshot data may not be collected in qkview. This may result in data being lost if the issue is only identified once important data has rotated out of history.
bugs.workaround: To specify no file size limit when collecting qkviews, use the following tmsh command: qkview -s0

bugs.title: The Configuration utility may calculate and display an incorrect HA Group Score
bugs.symptoms: The Configuration utility may calculate and display a high availability (HA) Group Score of 0, while in reality the correct HA Group Score is greater than 0.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a particular HA Group object (for example, a Pool) has no available members, and the 'Minimum Member Count' option is not used (this is the default).
bugs.impact: This issue is cosmetic as it is limited to what the Configuration utility calculates and displays to the user. Internally, the system uses the correct HA Group Score to determine the role of the unit. However, it is possible for a BIG-IP Administrator to be mislead by this issue and take a wrong or unnecessary corrective action because of it.
bugs.workaround: You can use the TMSH utility from the command line to display the correct HA Group Score.
bugs.fix: The Configuration utility no longer calculates and displays an incorrect HA Group Score.

bugs.title: If a Pool contains ".." in the name, it is impossible to add a Member to this pool using the GUI Local Traffic > Pools : Member List page
bugs.symptoms: - Create a pool with name containing two dots (that is, the string '..') - Go to the GUI Local Traffic :: Pools : Member List page and click the Add button to add a member. - There is a No Access error preventing you from adding a member to the pool
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a pool name contains .. in the name.
bugs.impact: Cannot add a Member to the pool using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to add pool members to an existing pool using a command similar to the following. tmsh modify ltm pool <pool name> members add { <member info> }
bugs.fix: For pools with '..' in the name, it is now possible to add members after pool creation using the GUI Local Traffic :: Pools : Member List page.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while shutting down the BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Due to a race condition, tmm may crash while initializing the tma table (tma_table_uninit) and produce a core file.
bugs.conditions: Issue may happen in either of the following conditions - Restarting BIG-IP - Force offlining BIG-IP - TMM restart
bugs.impact: TMM crashes.

bugs.title: TMSH incorrectly allows settings snat-translation ip-idle-timeout to zero.
bugs.symptoms: The configuration setting ' ip-idle-timeout' on the snat-translation object allows zero as a possible value.
bugs.conditions: Entering the following tmsh command: tmsh create ltm snat-translation <snat-address> ip-idle-timeout 0
bugs.impact: The configuration will be invalid. This may cause issues with upgrades and the BIG-IP may not pass traffic correctly or as expected.
bugs.workaround: Do not set the snat-translation ip-idle-timeout to 0 using tmsh.

bugs.title: tmsh query for dns records may cause tmm to crash
bugs.symptoms: tmm experiences segmentation fault.
bugs.conditions: Run 'tmsh show ltm dns cache records key cache <cache>' query when dns cache contains malformed records.
bugs.impact: Core file / system outage. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm experiences segmentation fault when running the 'tmsh show ltm dns cache records key cache <cache>' query when dns cache contains malformed records.

bugs.title: DHCP request-options when set to "none" are reset to defaults when loading the config.
bugs.symptoms: Config load resets the request-option in "tmsh sys management-dhcp" to its default value when they are set to "none" in configuration.
bugs.conditions: - A config load in which request-option in "tmsh sys management-dhcp" is set to "none".
bugs.impact: User configuration is reverted as a side-effect of config load.
bugs.workaround: request-option specify the minimal set of configuration that DHCP server must provide as part of the lease. Setting it to "none" defeats the whole purpose of DHCP. It's better to set it to a minimal value like "routers, subnet-mask" in order to have management connectivity.
bugs.fix: DHCP request-options when set to "none" are reset to defaults when loading the config.

bugs.title: Tmm becomes unresponsive and might restart
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the tmm process can become unresponsive, and eventually be restarted by the watchdog process.
bugs.conditions: Problem occurs when there is an unexpected interaction between HTTP and SSL handlers during an abnormal connection shutdown.
bugs.impact: Tmm becomes unresponsive and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmm correctly shuts down HTTPS connection.

bugs.title: Monitor operations in transaction will cause it to stay unchecked
bugs.symptoms: If a monitored object is deleted and created or modified in the same transaction, and any of its monitor configuration is changed (either the monitor, or the state user-down), the monitor state will become unchecked.
bugs.conditions: This only happens within transactions. Note: Using the command 'modify ltm pool <name> members replace-all-with' is considered a transaction containing a delete and create of pool members.
bugs.impact: Monitor state never returns to its correct value.
bugs.workaround: Do not do these operations in transactions. For pool members, use 'modify ltm pool <name> members modify' instead of replace-all-with.

bugs.title: A SAML IdP connector causes a sync failure when created
bugs.symptoms: A SAML IdP connector causes a sync failure when created.
bugs.conditions: SAML IdP connector contains an embedded certificate.
bugs.impact: Sync fails.
bugs.workaround: Force a full load sync immediately after.

bugs.title: bd crash
bugs.symptoms: A bd crash.
bugs.conditions: -- A config change follows a bd crash. -- There is a policy that is misconfigured, for example, a form-data parsing is applied on a non-form-data payload (such as XML or JSON).
bugs.impact: bd crashes; system fails over; traffic disturbance occurs.
bugs.workaround: Set the following internal parameter to 0: max_converted_length_to_cache

bugs.title: iControl REST /mgmt/tm/sys/crypto/cert endpoint cannot be used to return the details of all SSL certificates present in the configuration at once.
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST /mgmt/tm/sys/crypto/cert endpoint cannot return the details of all SSL certificates present in the configuration at once. Requests to said endpoint may return a 400 HTTP status code and a stack trace indicating a timeout exception.
bugs.conditions: This issue is more likely to occur with configurations that include a large number of SSL certificates.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST /mgmt/tm/sys/crypto/cert endpoint cannot be used to return the details of all SSL certificates present in the configuration at once.
bugs.workaround: You can request the details of one SSL certificate at a time from that particular endpoint (for instance, /mgmt/tm/sys/crypto/cert/~Common~my1.crt). Or you can request the details of all SSL certificates present in the configuration at once by using the /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-cert endpoint (which is not affected by this issue).
bugs.fix: The efficiency of the iControl REST /mgmt/tm/sys/crypto/cert endpoint has been improved.

bugs.title: The presence of a file with the suffix '.crt.csr' in folder /config/ssl/ssl.csr/ causes a GUI exception
bugs.symptoms: When there is a file named *.crt.csr in folder /config/ssl/ssl.csr/, the GUI posts an error on page: System :: Device Certificates : Device Certificate :: Device Certificate: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: The presence of a file with the suffix '.crt.csr' in folder /config/ssl/ssl.csr/.
bugs.impact: -- Using iCRD with 'sys crypto' fails. -- The BIG-IP GUI exhibits the following behavior: + Inconsistently manages those files improperly. + May return errors on System :: Device Certificates : Device Certificate :: Device Certificate (e.g., 'An error has occurred while trying to process your request.'). + May confuse objects (e.g., 'web-server.crt' and 'web-server.crt.csr'). + GUI cannot create an archive (System :: File Management : SSL Certificate List :: Archive) containing these files, and reports an error.
bugs.workaround: Rename the csr file suffix from '.crt.csr' to '.csr'.
bugs.fix: The system now accepts csr files with any kind of suffix extension.

bugs.title: Unexpected result from multiple changes to a monitor-related object in a single transaction
bugs.symptoms: When a transaction attempts multiple commands (delete, create, modify) for the same object in the same transaction, the results can be unexpected or undefined. A common example is: 'transaction { delete key create_if key }' where the transaction will attempt to 'delete key', and then 'create_if key', which unmarks the delete operation on the key (so in this case the key remains unmodified). In other cases it is possible that monitoring stops for the associated object, such as for: pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor.
bugs.conditions: A user-initiated transaction attempts multiple commands for the same monitor-related object, such as (delete, create, modify).
bugs.impact: The monitor-related object may be unchanged; or monitoring may stop for that object.
bugs.workaround: Transactions modifying a monitor-related object (pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor) should perform a single command upon that object (such as one of: 'delete', 'create', 'modify').
bugs.fix: Behavior is as-expected when a transaction executes multiple commands (such as 'delete', 'create', 'modify') upon the same monitor-related object (pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor).

bugs.title: Unexpected result from multiple changes to a monitor-related object in a single transaction
bugs.symptoms: When a transaction attempts multiple commands (delete, create, modify) for the same object in the same transaction, the results can be unexpected or undefined. A common example is: 'transaction { delete key create_if key }' where the transaction will attempt to 'delete key', and then 'create_if key', which unmarks the delete operation on the key (so in this case the key remains unmodified). In other cases it is possible that monitoring stops for the associated object, such as for: pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor.
bugs.conditions: A user-initiated transaction attempts multiple commands for the same monitor-related object, such as (delete, create, modify).
bugs.impact: The monitor-related object may be unchanged; or monitoring may stop for that object.
bugs.workaround: Transactions modifying a monitor-related object (pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor) should perform a single command upon that object (such as one of: 'delete', 'create', 'modify').

bugs.title: Intermittent session-deletion error while performing Kerberos authentication
bugs.symptoms: When restrict_irule_events is disabled and rotatesessionid sys db variable is turned on, the following error is seen in /var/log/apm: debug apd[15051]: 01490000:7: AccessPolicyD.cpp func: "process_request()" line: 831 Msg: ** done with the request processing ** notice tmm[21212]: 01490567:5: 3b831892: Session deleted (security_check)
bugs.conditions: - Disable restrict_irule_events. - Turn on rotatesessionid (by default, it is on). - Kerberos Auth agent is included in access policy.
bugs.impact: APM end user cannot take successful branch in access policy.
bugs.workaround: Turn off rotatesessionid sys db variable.

bugs.title: OneConnect profile causes CMP redirected connections on the HA standby
bugs.symptoms: When virtual server uses OneConnect profile in HA setup, it can cause Clustered Multiprocessing (CMP) redirected connections and memory leak on high availability (HA) standby systems, including high memory usage on standby units.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server uses OneConnect profile in HA configuration. -- Mirroring is enabled. -- BIG-IP platform supports CMP.
bugs.impact: Redirected connections and memory leak on a standby device.
bugs.workaround: Remove OneConnect profile from the virtual server.

bugs.title: RDP URIs generated by APM Webtop are not properly encoded
bugs.symptoms: RDP URIs used to launch Native RDP resources form APM Webtop on Android/iOS/Mac are not properly encoded. As a result, RDP client might misinterpret the URI, in cases in which some RDP parameter contains the ampersand ( & ) symbol.
bugs.conditions: Native RDP resource is launched via RDP URI from APM Webtop. One of RDP parameters contains symbol that should be URI encoded, e.g., '&'.
bugs.impact: RDP client misinterprets URI, which may result in failure to open RDP resource.
bugs.fix: RDP URIs used to launch Native RDP resources from APM Webtop on Android/iOS/Mac are now properly encoded.

bugs.title: Attacks with randomization of HTTP headers parameters generates too many signatures
bugs.symptoms: When attackers randomize HTTP headers parameters, Behavioral DoS (BADoS) might generate too many signatures.
bugs.conditions: Attacks with randomization of HTTP headers parameters.
bugs.impact: The list of generated signatures is too long. It produces unnecessary CPU utilization for attack mitigation.
bugs.fix: Improved algorithm that detects a randomization.

bugs.title: High CPU consumption during signature generation, not limited number of signatures per virtual server
bugs.symptoms: The number of the signatures per virtual server is not limited. This can result in a very large number of generated signatures during sophisticated attacks that use changing patterns. After a time, when a system experiences a number of attacks, the list of generated signatures can be too long.
bugs.conditions: -- Sophisticated attacks that use changing patterns. -- System experiences a large number of attacks.
bugs.impact: High CPU utilization when mitigating. Overloaded GUI signatures screen.
bugs.workaround: Manually remove old / not-often-used signatures.
bugs.fix: The system now limits the number of signatures per virtual servers, and optimizes per-signatures operation.

bugs.title: Presentation of signatures in human-readable format
bugs.symptoms: When publishing signature with predicates such as http.referer and http.uri, the system presents the result of the hash operation as follows: http.uri_file_hashes-to 42
bugs.conditions: Always when publishing signature with predicates such as http.referer and http.uri.
bugs.impact: It is not clear what '42' means.
bugs.fix: When publishing signatures, the system now presents the hashes as follows: http.referer_hashes-like '/zzz' http.uri_file_hashes-like '/123'

bugs.title: The maximum-connection count doubles pva traffic counts for virtuals
