These conditions cause MCP validation to be skipped and thus, pktclass daemon (pccd) aborts when it receives an invalid address (or port) list configuration for a NAT policy rule.
bugs.impact: AFM pktclass daemon (or pccd) halts with following error message in /var/log/ltm: pccd[20954]: 015d0000:3: [NAT] commit failed.
bugs.workaround: No not modify AFM NAT policy rule configuration either by running the 'tmsh merge' command or by manually modifying bigip*.conf files. Use TMSH/GUI commands/options to manage AFM NAT configuration.
bugs.fix: MCP validation issue has been fixed to now detect the invalid address (or port) list condition in an AFM NAT policy rule when you attach a non-existent list either by running the 'tmsh merge' command or by manually modifying bigip*.conf files. MCP now catches the invalid configuration and posts an alert, preventing the pktclass daemon (pccd) from halting.

bugs.title: System posts error message: 01010054:3: tmrouted connection closed
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in BIG-IP 12.0.0, the tmrouted process pushes dynamic routes directly to the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM). This message indicates the system is shutting down and is expected behavior during the reboot or shutdown process. The appearance of this message on a stable running system may indicate an issue with tmrouted functionality. System posts the following message in /var/log/ltm: 01010054:3: tmrouted connection closed
bugs.conditions: This message occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have configured the BIG-IP system to use dynamic routing. -- The BIG-IP system is in the process of shutting down or rebooting.
bugs.impact: This message is benign, unless you view the message on a stable running system. In this case, the message may indicate an issue with the tmrouted process.

bugs.title: Validation missing when changing Syslog format from valid to invalid selection for DoS Application Protection
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP's High Speed Logging (HSL) configuration supports three syslog formats for log destinations: in TMUI syslog, in tmsh RFC5424 or leave blank as it is the default; TMUI BSD Syslog, tmsh RFC3164; and TMUI Legacy BIG-IP, tmsh legacy_bigip. The only supported format for DoS Application Protection is syslog/RFC5424. If you have not previously assigned a security logging profile to a Protected Object using a DoS Profile with the HTTP family of vectors enabled, configuration validation will prevent you from assigning a security logging profile with the incorrect syslog format. However, once the correct configuration has been made, no further validation takes place and a configuration with invalid syslog settings will be accepted. Log messages will not be sent.
bugs.conditions: You have a Protected Object with a DoS Protection profile with the HTTP family enabled. You have an HSL configuration using a remote-syslog destination using format syslog/RFC5424, and a Security Logging profile that references the publisher in that HSL configuration. You then update the remote-syslog destination to use another syslog format.
bugs.impact: Loss of logging data.
bugs.workaround: Continue using the supported syslog format: syslog/rfc5424.
bugs.fix: The system now validates that when using a Remote Syslog destination for Application DoS logs, only the Syslog/rfc5424 format is allowed.

bugs.title: Preventing ng_export hangs
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes ng_export is stuck while reading tmsh thru the pipe because of buffer issues. Export is trying to read more data from tmsh while data is lost in the middle of the read operation.
bugs.conditions: -- ng_export receives tmsh replies through buffer of constant size x. -- During the read operation, tmsh returns a buffer size of x minus k, where k is very small random number (less than 50). Note: K is very small random number, which makes this issue difficult to describe.
bugs.impact: The export operation hangs.
bugs.fix: ng_export is now using non-blocking socket and loops to wait for data or terminate gracefully
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Support DIAMETER Experimental-Result AVP response
bugs.symptoms: When the Diameter server returns an answer message with an Experimental-Result AVP, but doesn't have Result-Code AVP inside, then the server side flow is aborted.
bugs.conditions: Diameter answer message doesn't have Result-Code AVP available, but with Experimental-Result AVP.
bugs.impact: The server side flow is aborted.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to insert Result-Code AVP in all Diameter answer messages.
bugs.fix: This release supports DIAMETER Experimental-Result AVP response.

bugs.title: Incorrect BIGIP_GTMD_SERVER_NOIP_SNMP_STATUS_CHANGE_WHY_X SNMP message when deleting server with IP address.
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect BIGIP_GTMD_SERVER_NOIP_SNMP_STATUS_CHANGE_WHY_X SNMP message when deleting server with IP address.
bugs.conditions: When deleting a GTM server with 0 < num_boxes (HAS ip), the SNMP message sent was using the OID ".1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.157" corresponding to BIGIP_GTMD_SERVER_NOIP_SNMP_STATUS_CHANGE_WHY_X (meant for no ip), while it should have been using OID ".1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.57" which corresponds to BIGIP_GTMD_SERVER_SNMP_STATUS_CHANGE_WHY_X (for servers with ip).
bugs.impact: Incorrect OID - Status mapping causing incorrect SNMP messages.

bugs.title: CA bundle manager loses certificates in the CA bundle if the serial number is longer than 4 bytes
bugs.symptoms: CA certificates with long but different serial numbers are treated identical and duplicate, thus get lost in the CA certificate merge operation. Only one would be left.
bugs.conditions: - The CA bundle file is managed by the CA bundle manager. - The file contains certificates with large serial numbers.
bugs.impact: Certificates with large serial numbers are treated as duplicate, and removed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Large serial numbers are treated correctly.

bugs.title: static and dynamically learned blackhole route from ZebOS cannot be deleted
bugs.symptoms: -- Static route added via IMISH can not be deleted. -- Dynamically learned blackhole route can not be unlearned.
bugs.conditions: - Dynamic routing enabled. - Added static route via IMISH or learning blackhole route via dynamic routing.
bugs.impact: Unintended route remains.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmrouted.
bugs.fix: Static route from IMISH and dynamic blackhole route are now cleaned up correctly.

bugs.title: TMM core files might be truncated due to lack of space
bugs.symptoms: The /shared filesystem on a VIPRION 4450 blade might not have enough free space for large TMM core files.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on a VIPRION 4450 blade. -- /shared has less than approximately 250 GB of free space.
bugs.impact: If TMM cores, there may not be enough space to save the full core file. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: one Cisco NEXUS switch and 2 BIG-IP WCCP web caches do not work together
bugs.symptoms: The one Cisco CATALIST switch and 2 BIG-IP WCCP works perfect. The one Cisco NEXUSswitch and 2 BIG-IP WCCP does not work together. The difference is in the "WCCP Message Type: 2.0 I see you (11)" generated by NEXUS router. Existing code did not support offset (expect "Number of elements" always equal 0) as CATALIST and other switches set. But NEXUS use this element and it produce some offset in frames. As result BIG-IP can't understand it for case 1 NEXUS and two (or more) BIG-IP's This point is badly described in WCCP draft and investigation was based on WireShark dissector.
bugs.conditions: 1 NEXUS and two (or more) BIG-IP's have interability problem
bugs.impact: 1 NEXUS and two (or more) BIG-IP's can't work together.
bugs.workaround: avoid such configuration.
bugs.fix: Problem was fixed and it is working perfect now.

bugs.title: Traffic stops on tmm restart when guest VLAN tagging is used for BIG-IP VE.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic stops after tmm restart. BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) becomes unresponsive and requires power cycle.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Using VE. -- Data plane interfaces are SR-IOV VF. -- Guest VLAN tagging is used. -- tmm restart.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system stops working, and management connection may be lost, requiring power cycle.
bugs.workaround: Use VLAN tagging from host.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now continues to work after tmm restart when guest VLAN tagging is used with SR-IOV interfaces for BIG-IP VE.

bugs.title: Hardware syncookie mode is used when global auto last hop is disabled.
bugs.symptoms: When global auto last hop is disabled, for iSeries platforms (excluding i2xxx/i4xxx) and B4450 blades, hardware syncookie mode is used on SYN attack.
bugs.conditions: Global autohop is disabled. This setting is controlled by the following DB variable: # tmsh list sys db connection.autolasthop sys db connection.autolasthop { value "disable" } The default setting is enable.
bugs.impact: The virtual server can enter hardware syncookie mode, at which point responses will be routed using the incoming packet route. This can break configurations that are using asymmetric routing.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware syncookies by setting the following DB variable to false: tmsh modify sys db pvasyncookies.enabled value false

bugs.title: Fragmented SSL Client Hello message do not get properly reassembled when SSL Persistence is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Node Server rejects received-and-incomplete ClientHello message and connection terminates.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- SSL Persistence is enabled. -- There is no ClientSSL and ServerSSL profile. -- The BIG-IP device receives fragments of a ClientHello message (typically, 11 bytes each) from an SSL front-end client.
bugs.impact: With Session Persistence enabled -- The parser fails to reassemble fragmented ClientHello messages prior to passing it on to the backend server. -- As a result, the backend server responds as if it has received an incomplete ClientHello message, rejects the handshake, and terminates the connection.
bugs.workaround: The issue disappears when SSL Persistence is disabled.

bugs.title: Protocol Inspection custom signatures require that http_header keyword have a leading space character
bugs.symptoms: When using the term 'http_header' as an attribute of a content check, there must be a leading space between it and the content semicolon ';' delimiter. Also, 'http_header' cannot be applied for the second or subsequent content checks if preceding content checks do not have it. It also must be the first attribute of a content check. This example fails validation because there is no space between ';' and 'http_header': alert tcp any any -> any any (content:User-agent;http_header; content:"mortest"; distance:1; nocase; sig_id:100020;) This example fails validation because 'http_header' is first used for the second content check. It also fails because 'http_header' comes after 'distance' and 'nocase' for the second content check: alert tcp any any -> any any (content:User-agent; content:"mortest"; distance:1; nocase; http_header; sig_id:100020;)
bugs.conditions: This occurs when either of the following conditions are true: -- http_header is used for a content check that is not the first content check. -- http_header is used after other content parameters, such as 'distance' and 'nocase'.
bugs.impact: Custom signature fails validation.
bugs.workaround: Use the following workarounds: -- Use 'http_header' for initial content checks. -- Use 'http_header' before other content attributes, such as 'distance' and 'nocase'.
bugs.fix: Protocol Inspection no longer requires such unnecessarily restrictive constraints when using the http_header keyword.

bugs.title: tmm crashes on iRule with GTM pool command
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes with a SIGSEGV when a GTM iRule executes a 'pool' command against Tcl variables that have internal string representations, which can occur when a value is a result of (some) string commands (e.g., 'string tolower') or if the value comes from a built-in iRules command (such as 'class'). For example: when DNS_REQUEST { pool [string tolower "Test.com"] } or: when DNS_REQUEST { pool [class lookup pool-dg key-value] }
bugs.conditions: GTM iRule executes a 'pool' command against Tcl variables that have internal string representations.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Pass the 'pool' argument through 'string trim'. For instance: when DNS_REQUEST { pool [string trim [class lookup pool-dg key-value]] }
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes on GTM iRules that use the 'pool' command.

bugs.title: Using an iRule to change virtual servers prevents correct DAG detection for PBA and DNAT modes
bugs.symptoms: When redirecting the traffic by using iRule 'virtual <virtual_server>' on a PBA or DNAT LSN pool associated virtual server, the system resets the connection and logs errors similar to the following: err tmm2[19158]: 01670024:3: Unsupported DAG mode for LSN pool(/Common/session1_pool) mode PBA on interface _loopback err tmm2[19158]: 01670024:3: Unsupported DAG mode for LSN pool(/Common/dnat_pool) mode DNAT on interface _loopback This occurs because using an iRule to change virtual servers prevents correct DAG detection for PBA and DNAT modes.
bugs.conditions: -- LSN pool is configured in either PBA or DNAT mode. -- An iRule redirects traffic to a different virtual server.
bugs.impact: Connections fail using this iRule.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, configure the lsn-pools with NAPT mode.
bugs.fix: LSN can now detect the correct DAG mode after the virtual server is set using an iRule, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Attack-destination for a DoS vector was not predicting right thresholds in some cases
bugs.symptoms: When attack-destination is enabled for a vector, then thresholds predicted by attack-destination (bad dest ip) were not correct in some cases.
bugs.conditions: It can occur when attack-destination is enabled for a DoS vector in a config.
bugs.impact: Some times wrong threshold values could be predicted for the DoS vector if attack-destination is enabled.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This has been fixed in the code.

bugs.title: Bad actors detection might not work when signature mitigation blocks bad traffic
bugs.symptoms: When signature detected and mitigating no bad actors detection
bugs.conditions: 1. Signatures detected and mitigating 2. Attack traffic is not significantly higher than the good traffic
bugs.impact: No bad actors detected. Only signatures provides DoS protection. BIG-IP CPU utilization is higher than necessary
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The fix takes in account also SIGNATURES DROPS to decide when bad actors detection should be more agressive.

bugs.title: ASM standby unit showing future date and high version count for ASM Device Group
bugs.symptoms: Policy builder is changing configuration of standby unit.
bugs.conditions: The system state changes from active to standby (also when blade is changed from master to non-master).
bugs.impact: Unexpected changes are made to the policy on standby device (CID increment).
bugs.workaround: Restart pabnagd when switching device from active to standby (also when blade is changed from master no non-master): killall -s SIGHUP pabnagd
bugs.fix: Policy builder now updates its state correctly and doesn't make changes to a policy on a standby device.

bugs.title: System fails to boot when syslog-ng is not running.
bugs.symptoms: System hangs during boot while trying to start the httpd service.
bugs.conditions: syslog-ng is not running.
bugs.impact: System fails to boot
bugs.workaround: Correct the /etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf file if necessary and start the syslog-ng service using the following command: service syslog-ng start The system should continue to boot.

bugs.title: 2000/4000, 10000, i2000/i4000, i5000/i7000/i10000, i15000, B4000 platforms may return incorrect SNMP sysIfxStatHighSpeed values for 10G/40G/100G interfaces
bugs.symptoms: 2000/4000, 10000, i2000/i4000, i5000/i7000/i10000, i15000, B4000 platforms may return incorrect SNMP sysIfxStatHighSpeed values for 10G/40G/100G interfaces
bugs.conditions: -- 2000/4000, 10000, i2000/i4000, i5000/i7000/i10000, i15000, B4000 platforms. -- SNMP query of network interfaces via OID sysIfxStatHighSpeed.
bugs.impact: Value returned for 10G/40G/100G interfaces may be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Use OID sysInterfaceMediaActiveSpeed.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly returns SNMP sysIfxStatHighSpeed values for 10G/40G/100G interfaces.

bugs.title: tmsh save sys ucs <file> fails due to missing patch file in /config/.diffVersions
bugs.symptoms: The .diffVersions directory has config change-diffs saved into patch files every time tmsh saves the configs. This is used for diagnostic purposes only.
bugs.conditions: When doing a 'tmsh save sys ucs <file>', it is possible that a background 'tmsh save sys config' gets run at the same time, causing a patch file to be deleted that the ucs-save feature now expected to exist.
bugs.impact: The ucs-save feature complains about the missing patch file and exits.
bugs.workaround: Re-run the 'tmsh save sys ucs <file>' ignoring the missing patch file message. That missing file doesn't need to be restored.
bugs.fix: With this defect fixed, patch files that end up missing once 'tmsh load sys ucs <file>' is started will not be reported as an error, and the tmsh command will complete normally.

bugs.title: Connection failure during iRule DNS lookup can crash TMM
bugs.symptoms: The TMM crashes in the DNS response cache periodic sweep.
bugs.conditions: The DNS resolver connection fails after a successful lookup response is cached. This has been reproduced with a failure due to a lost route. Other failures such as down ports do not cause a crash.
bugs.impact: The TMM cores and automatically restarts, Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No known workaround.
bugs.fix: The reference counting of the resolver connection was fixed.

bugs.title: GTP::ie primitives in iRule to be certified
bugs.symptoms: The following commands in iRules are created and available but not officially tested and approved: GTP::ie set instance/value GTP::ie insert GTP::ie append GTP::ie remove
bugs.conditions: Using the following iRule commands: GTP::ie set instance/value GTP::ie insert GTP::ie append GTP::ie remove
bugs.impact: Although you can use these iRule commands, their functionality has not been tested and approved.
bugs.fix: GTP::ie primitives in iRule are now certified.
bugs.behavior: Certified pre-existing iRules: -- GTP::ie set instance <ie-path> <instance> Assigns <instance> to the information element (IE) instance at <ie-path>. -- GTP::ie set value <ie-path> <value> Assigns <value> to the IE value at <ie-path>. -- GTP::ie insert <ie-path> <type> <instance> <value> Inserts a new IE of type <type> and instance <instance> with value <value> at <ie-path> -- GTP::ie append [<ie-path>] <type> <instance> <value> Appends a new IE of type <type> and instance <instance> with value <value> to the end of embeded IE of grouped-IE specified by <ie-path> or to the end of message if the grouped-IE <ie-path> is absent. -- GTP::ie remove <ie-path> Removes IE specified by <ie-path>.

bugs.title: PEM content insertion in a compressed response may cause a crash.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash while processing a specially crafted page.
bugs.conditions: PEM enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash and failover event
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when processing specially crafted content via PEM.

bugs.title: tmsh show sys software doesn't show the correct HF version
bugs.symptoms: tmsh show sys software does not show the correct hotfix version. Instead, it shows the base 12.1.2 release, not the 12.1.2 HF1 hotfix version. However, selecting it boots the correct version. At the login prompt, in /VERSION and in tmsh show sys version the correct hotfix version is shown.
bugs.conditions: Using tmsh command: tmsh show sys software
bugs.impact: Hotfix version is not correct.
bugs.workaround: At the login prompt, using /VERSION or using tmsh show sys version, the correct hotfix version will be shown.

bugs.title: When using LDAP client auth, tamd may become stuck
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server uses an LDAP auth profile for client authentication, the system can get into a state where all authentications time out. This condition persists until tamd restarts. Traffic analysis between the BIG-IP system and the LDAP server shows that the BIG-IP system makes a TCP handshake with the server, then immediately sends FIN. Tamd cores may be seen.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server using LDAP auth profile. -- BIG-IP system makes a TCP handshake with the server, then immediately sends FIN.
bugs.impact: Authentication to the virtual server fails until tamd is restarted.
bugs.workaround: To recover, restart tamd by running the following command: bigstart restart tamd
bugs.fix: tamd no longer becomes stuck when using LDAP client auth.

bugs.title: 1NIC: Configuration error: Clearing IP on interface mgmt failed - Cannot assign requested address
bugs.symptoms: The error: Configuration error: Clearing IP on interface mgmt failed - Cannot assign requested add
bugs.conditions: Starting VE in 1NIC mode without a DHCP server and configuring the management interface.
bugs.impact: No management IP or Self IP.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Configuring the management IP in 1NIC mode now works.

bugs.title: MCPD crashes while fetching page Security :: Protocol Security : Inspection Profiles with 500 IPS profiles
bugs.symptoms: MCPD crashes while fetching page Security :: Protocol Security : Inspection Profiles with 500 IPS profiles
bugs.conditions: Adding more than 300,000 protocol inspection checks.
bugs.impact: mcpd crash.
bugs.fix: Added limitation in MCPD for creating profiles.

bugs.title: Violation rating is not exposed to the iRules
bugs.symptoms: Cannot create an iRule that relates to the violation rating.
bugs.conditions: An iRule that uses the violation rating.
bugs.impact: Missing iRule functionality.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release adds the violation_rating to the iRules.

bugs.title: Rare BD crash in a specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: BD crash or False reporting of signature ID 200023003.
bugs.conditions: JSON/XML/parameters traffic (should not happen with the enforce value signature).
bugs.impact: Failover, traffic disturbance in the core case. False positive violation or blocking in the other scenario.
bugs.workaround: Removing attack signature 200023003 from the security policy stops the issue.
bugs.fix: Fix a bug in the signatures engine that causes a false positive reporting of a signature. In some rare cases, this false reporting may cause a crash. A newly released attack signature update changes the signature in a way that it no longer causes the issue to happen.

bugs.title: HTTP2/SPDY profile can cause orphaned connections
bugs.symptoms: When tearing down a HTTP2 connection, which is composed of a clientside HTTP2 connection and 'n' serverside HTTP1.1 connections, the system might leave a subset of the 'n' serverside HTTP1.1 connection behind. Those left behind connections are still referencing the clientside PCB, which might result in a crash should they ever be expired, e.g., due to an AFM firewall policy change triggering the sweeper.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP2 leaves serverside connections behind. -- AFM firewall policy change occurs that triggers the sweeper.
bugs.impact: Orphaned connections might result in various behaviors, from a small memory leak to a tmm restart, which has the possibility of disrupting traffic.

bugs.title: Delete sys connection operations cannot be part of TMSH transactions
bugs.symptoms: TMSH operations that delete sys connection cannot be part of transactions. Once the TMSH transaction is submitted, TMSH freezes up if a 'delete sys connection ...' command is included.
bugs.conditions: Include delete sys connection operations in TMSH transactions.
bugs.impact: TMSH freezes up and transactions do not complete.
bugs.workaround: Only use tmsh delete sys connection outside of TMSH transactions.
bugs.fix: Delete sys connection operations can be part of TMSH transactions. TMSH no longer freezes up.

bugs.title: SNMP does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, SNMP does not follow best security practices when responding with specific MIBs.
bugs.conditions: SNMP access granted (no remote SNMP access is allowed in the default configuration).
bugs.impact: SNMP does not follow best security practices.
bugs.workaround: Restrict access to SNMP via IP and/or SNMPv3 authentication.
bugs.fix: SNMP now follows best security practices for all MIBs.

bugs.title: Protected Object "Add" and "Clone" buttons are hidden on screens with lower resolution
bugs.symptoms: When the inspector panel is opened, the buttons are not visible.
bugs.conditions: Screen resolutions lower than 1920x1080
bugs.impact: Cannot add or clone a new protected object
bugs.workaround: Collapse Inspector or scroll protected object list table to the left

bugs.title: The bcm570x driver can cause TMM to core when transmitting packets larger than 6144 bytes
bugs.symptoms: The bcm570x driver will cause TMM to core with the log message: panic: ifoutput: packet_data_compact failed to reduce pkt size below 4.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on a platform that uses the bcm570x driver (BIG-IP 800, 1600, 3600). -- A packet larger than 6144 bytes is transmitted from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: TMM core. Failover or outage. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Removed the panic statement that caused TMM to core. TMM will now log an error and drop the packet instead.

bugs.title: RFC 793 - behavior receiving FIN/ACK in SYN-RECEIVED state
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system resets connection with RST if it receives FIN/ACK in SYN-RECEIVED state.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system receives FIN/ACK when it is in SYN-RECEIVED state.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system resets connection with RST.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now responds with FIN/ACK to early FIN/ACK.

bugs.title: Names of the modified cookies do not appear in the event log
bugs.symptoms: A modified domain cookies violation happened. When trying to see additional details by clicking the violation link, the name and value of the modified cookie is empty.
bugs.conditions: A modified domain cookies violation happens. Note: This can happen only if there are also non-modified or staged cookies.
bugs.impact: Expected violation details are not displayed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Issue with modified domain cookie violation details is now fixed.

bugs.title: Security Policy Configuration Changes When Disabling Learning
bugs.symptoms: When Learning is enabled in either manual or automatic mode, and is then disabled. This was considered to be the end of the learning process, and so changes are automatically made to the default wildcard entities ("*" URL, Parameter, Filetype) such as removing the element from staging. The user is not notified of these changes, and they may not be expected, leading to undesired security enforcement.
bugs.conditions: -- Learning is enabled in Manual or Automatic mode. -- Learning is then disabled.
bugs.impact: Unexpected changes to the default wildcard elements in the policy can lead to undesired security enforcement.
bugs.workaround: The audit log shows all changes that were made to the policy, and undesired changes can be remedied before the policy changes are applied.
bugs.fix: No changes are made to the default wildcard entities upon disabling of learning.

bugs.title: MSTP: CIST bridge priority changes after adjusting the MSTI priority.
bugs.symptoms: Changing the priority of a non-zero region MSTP instance results in BPDUs advertising a change to the CIST Bridge Priority, but not for the expected MSTID instance.
bugs.conditions: Issue a STP MSTID priority modify request.
bugs.impact: Changing the MSTID priority for forcing the BIG-IP system to become the root bridge, does not work as expected. Note: F5 Networks recommends against having the BIG-IP system become the root bridge.
bugs.workaround: After modifying the MSTID priority, also restart the STP daemon (stpd) to have the BPDUs advertising the expected CIST/MSTID priorities.

bugs.title: bigd logs monitor status unknown for FQDN Node/Pool Member
bugs.symptoms: While monitoring FQDN nodes or pool members, bigd may log the current or previous monitor status of the node or pool member as 'unknown' in messages where that state internally could have been logged as 'checking' or 'no address' for FQDN template nodes. Other states for FQDN configured nodes or pool members log monitor status as expected. Messages are similar to the following: notice bigd[####]: 01060141:5: Node /Common/node_name monitor status unknown [ ip.address: unknown ] [ was up for ##hrs:##mins:##sec ] notice bigd[####]: 01060141:5: Node /Common/node_name monitor status up [ ip.address: unknown ] [ was unknown for ##hrs:##mins:##sec ] notice bigd[####]: 01060141:5: Node /Common/node_name monitor status up [ ip.address: up ] [ was unknown for ##hrs:##mins:##sec ] notice bigd[####]: 01060145:5: Pool /Common/pool_name member /Common/node_name monitor status unknown. [ ] [ was unchecked for ##hrs:##mins:##sec ] notice bigd[####]: 01060145:5: Pool /Common/pool_name member /Common/node_name monitor status up. [ ] [ was unknown for ##hrs:##mins:##sec ]
bugs.conditions: This may occur of the FQDN template node or pool member is in a 'checking' or 'no address' state. The 'checking' state may occur if the DNS resolution of the FQDN node or pool member name is in progress. The 'no address' state may occur if no IP addresses were returned by the DNS server for the configured FQDN node or pool member name.
bugs.impact: Unable to triage state of FQDN nodes or pool members identified in these log messages, to determine whether further troubleshooting is required, or what specific problem condition might require further investigation.
bugs.fix: An FQDN-configured node or pool member logs each internal monitor status, including for scenarios of 'checking' and 'no address' for FQDN template nodes which were previously logged as 'unknown'.

bugs.title: GET parameter is grayed out if MobileSafe is not licensed
bugs.symptoms: GET parameter is grayed out if MobileSafe is not licensed.
bugs.conditions: -- Provision FPS on a system whose license has at least one active feature. -- Do not license MobileSafe.
bugs.impact: In FPS Parameter's list, the GET method is always grayed out.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- License MobileSafe. -- Use TMSH or REST.
bugs.fix: The GET method is not grayed out if MobileSafe is not licensed.

bugs.title: iCall and CLI script memory leak when saving configuration
bugs.symptoms: Whenever an iCall script or CLI script saves the configuration, the scriptd process on the device leaks memory.
bugs.conditions: Use of iCall or CLI scripts to save the configuration.
bugs.impact: Repeated invocation might cause the system to run out of memory eventually, causing tmm to restart and disrupting traffic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not saving the configuration from iCall or CLI scripts.
bugs.fix: scriptd process on the device no longer leaks memory when iCall and CLI scripts are used to save the configuration.

bugs.title: A request-log profile may not log anything for the $VIRTUAL_POOL_NAME token
bugs.symptoms: For some HTTP requests, a request-log profile can log nothing for the $VIRTUAL_POOL_NAME token (which expands to an empty string in the resulting logs).
bugs.conditions: - The virtual server where the request-log profile is used also uses OneConnect. - The client uses HTTP Keep-Alive and sends multiple HTTP requests over the same TCP connection.
bugs.impact: For all HTTP requests the client sends except the first one, the $VIRTUAL_POOL_NAME token logs nothing. As a result, a BIG-IP Administrator may struggle to determine which pool serviced which request.
bugs.workaround: The $SERVER_IP and $SERVER_PORT tokens work for all requests, and so if those are also being logged it may be possible to deduce the pool name from that information. However, there is no workaround to make the $VIRTUAL_POOL_NAME token work all of the time.

bugs.title: rewrite profile causes "No available pool member" failures when connection limit reached
bugs.symptoms: ltm rewrite profile (with mode uri-translation) can cause connections on ltm forwarding virtual server to be terminated with reason "No available pool member".
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with ltm rewrite profile. Default pool has request queuing enabled and connection limits configured for all its nodes.
bugs.impact: When the connection limit is reached, further connections are terminated with "No available pool member" cause instead of being queued.
bugs.workaround: An iRule which selects default pool on HTTP_REQUEST: when HTTP_REQUEST priority 1000 { pool [LB::server pool] }

bugs.title: Potential high memory usage from errdefsd.
bugs.symptoms: errdefsd memory usage grows with each config-sync or config update.
bugs.conditions: Ever increasing errdefsd memory usage is visible when the following conditions are met: -- Config updates are frequent. -- management-port logging is not being used.
bugs.impact: In extreme cases, errdefsd memory usage might increase userland memory-pressure. Note, however, that it isn't actually using the extra memory, so while Virtual Memory Size (VSZ) might be high, Resident Set Size (RSS) need not be.
bugs.workaround: A workaround for this problem is to periodically send logs to a management-port destination. The destination may be as simple as a dummy UDP port on 127.0.0.1. Adding such a destination to the publisher for an existing, active log source will work. errdefsd just needs a reason to process and flush accumulating configurations.
bugs.fix: The changes in this bug force errdefsd to check for config changes once every second in addition to checking whenever management-port destination logs come in.

bugs.title: errdefsd fails to generate a core file on request.
bugs.symptoms: Should errdefsd crash or be manually cored for the purpose of gathering diagnostic information, no core file will be generated.
bugs.conditions: Forcing errdefsd to core for diagnostic purposes.
bugs.impact: Increased communication required with F5 Support when attempting to diagnose problems with errdefsd.
bugs.workaround: 1. Add the following lines to the official errdefsd script, /etc/bigstart/scripts/errdefsd: 16a17,19 > # set resource limits, affinity, etc > setproperties ${service} > 2. Run the following command: bigstart restart errdefsd
bugs.fix: errdefsd now generates a core file when forced to core.

bugs.title: Audit log messages sent from the primary blade to the secondaries should not be logged.
bugs.symptoms: Audit log messages sent from the primary blade to the secondaries are logged.
bugs.conditions: Multi-blade platform.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary messages in the log file.

bugs.title: AOM menu power off then on results in 'Host Power Cycle Event' SEL log entries posted every two seconds
bugs.symptoms: When using the AOM menu to power off then on the host CPU on i5600, i5800, i7600, i7800, i10600, i10800 platforms, the AOM creates a 'Host Power Cycle Event' SEL log entry every two seconds. The SEL log will continue to grow until external power to the appliance is fully power cycled.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on i5600, i5800, i7600, i7800, i10600, i10800 platforms. -- With an older version of CPLD code installed (e.g., CPLD 0x45), bring up the AOM menu using ESP shift-9, then select 'p' and '0' from the menu to power off the host CPU complex. -- Wait a few seconds, then select 'p' and '1' to power on the host CPU complex.
bugs.impact: This will result in ongoing 'Host Power Cycle Event' messages to post the the SEL log ( tail /var/log/sel ) every two seconds. The SEL log will continue to grow and wrap as this message continues to post to the SEL log every two seconds. This results in a very large number of SEL entry fetches by the host CPU to the AOM and can places a substantial load on the AOM interface.
bugs.workaround: The actual fix is to install a newer version of i5600, i5800, i7600, i7800, i10600, i10800 platform CPLD code (e.g., CPLD 0x54 or CPLD 0x55). Another workaround is to fully power cycle the appliance. However, every time AOM menu is used to power off then on the host, this SEL log entry will re-appear.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in newer versions of the i5600, i5800, i7600, i7800, i10600, i10800 platforms CPLD (e.g., v0x54 or 0x55).

bugs.title: Request logging is briefly suspended after policy re-assignment
bugs.symptoms: Requests are not logged locally
bugs.conditions: This can occur in either of these conditions -- Making changes to a policy and/or assigning it to a virtual server can cause the issue. -- A failover event moves the virtual server and policy to the other slot.
bugs.impact: Request logging is briefly suspended. Some log messages are not logged.
bugs.fix: Requests are logged to the local logger immediately after policy assignment.

bugs.title: User with 'operator' role may not be able to view some session variables
bugs.symptoms: When a user with 'operator' role tries to view the session variables, the GUI may show the following error: An error has occurred while trying to process you request.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is a huge blob of data associated with the user whose session variable is being viewed. For example Active Directory (AD) user accounts with thumbnailphoto and userCertificate user attributes containing binary data.
bugs.impact: User cannot view the session variables for those particular sessions. This data is available, however, via clicking on the Session ID.
bugs.workaround: Find this data via clicking on the session ID.
bugs.fix: User with 'operator' role can now view all expected session variables

bugs.title: ICAP modified HTTP 1.1 request/response without content-length gets "chunked" even with no body
bugs.symptoms: When a modified HTTP v1.1 request or response is returned from an ICAP server and has no body (and also no content-length), a 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' header is added and a zero-length chunk is appended.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile. -- Either request-adapt or response-adapt profile. -- Modified HTTP v1.1 request/response has no body (and no content-length header).
bugs.impact: The HTTP server or client to which the modified request or response is destined, receives invalid HTTP and might behave in an unexpected manner.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to detect the lack of a Content-Length header in the modified request or response, and insert 'Content-Length: 0'. For example with modified request: when ADAPT_REQUEST_HEADERS { if {([HTTP::method] eq "GET") and (not [HTTP::header exists 'Content-Length'])} { HTTP::header insert Content-Length 0 } } Similarly when ADAPT_RESPONSE_HEADERS {} for a response.
bugs.fix: A modified HTTP v1.1 request or response with no body is never 'chunked'.

bugs.title: Tmm core due to incorrect memory allocation
bugs.symptoms: In a rare condition after providing afm, we get a tmm core. You will see the following line in avrd.log /usr/bin/avrinstall -c20 -t10 -s2401000 --provisionAVR=0 --provisionASM=0 --provisionAFM=0 --provisionPBD=0 --provisionAPM=0 --provisionFPS=0 --provisionPEM=0 --provisionVCMP=0
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned. Attack started.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: We check that the shared memory was allocated correctly before reporting on an attack.

bugs.title: TMM crash caused by SSOv2 form based due to null config
bugs.symptoms: Service outage because of tmm restart.
bugs.conditions: When SSO V2 client initiated is configured and user sending a small POST request with a small payload (< 4K)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when executing with an invalid client-initiated forms SSO configuration.

bugs.title: Unexpected Octeon, Nitrox, and/or Super IO recovery warnings in LTM log
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected warnings in the LTM log indicating Octeon, Nitrox, and/or Super IO recovery happening in BIOS. Messages appear similar to the following: -- warning chmand[5972]: 012a0004:4: Nitrox recoveries: 1 -- warning chmand[5972]: 012a0004:4: Octeon recoveries: 1 -- warning chmand[6018]: 012a0004:4: Host CPU subsystem power-off event caused by Super IO
bugs.conditions: -- Currently released BIOS with error recovery enabled. -- VIPRION B2150 and B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact to the system. The BIOS shipping with the VIPRION B2150 and B2250 blades configures the PCIe interfaces in such an order that BIOS recovery may have to take over. These messages are generated as BIOS error recovery is implemented to correct the PCIe interfaces configuration issues after which the system will boot normally. These messages are then benign.
bugs.workaround: These are benign messages in the LTM and shows that BIOS error recovery is working. The messages may be ignored.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP as SAML IdP processes signed authentication requests from external SAML SP, a block of memory may become corrupted.
bugs.symptoms: After processing signed authentication requests from external SAML SP, SAML IdP may corrupt a block of tmm memory.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP system is configured as SAML IdP. - IdP is configured with external SP's signing certificate. - External SP sends signed authentication request.
bugs.impact: Various possible negative effects, including TMM core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP as SAML IdP no longer causes memory corruption when handling certain traffic.

bugs.title: Core with /usr/bin/tmm.debug at qa_device_mgr_uninit
bugs.symptoms: Running a debug version of tmm (/usr/bin/tmm.debug) on BIG-IP 2xxx and 4xxx platforms, crashes at qa_device_mgr_uninit when issuing either of the following commands: -- bigstart stop tmm -- bigstart restart tmm
bugs.conditions: Running a debug version of tmm. -- BIG-IP 2xxx and 4xxx platforms. -- Running either of the following commands: + bigstart stop tmm + bigstart restart tmm
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using a debug version of tmm on BIG-IP 2xxx and 4xxx platforms.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer halts and restarts under these conditions.

bugs.title: shutting down trap not sent when shutdown -r or shutdown -h issued from shell
bugs.symptoms: Shutting down trap not sent when shutdown -r or shutdown -h issued from shell.
bugs.conditions: When user access the linux shell and issues "shutdown -h" or "shutdown -r", the BIG-IP does not send shutting down trap.
bugs.impact: None. Since this is user triggered command, the user is aware of the shutdown event, so the lack of trap is not critical.
bugs.fix: The shutdown trap is sent when user issues "shutdown -r" or "shutdown -h" from the linux shell.

bugs.title: Adding support for BIG-IP 800 in 13.1.x

bugs.title: Using UDP port 67 for purposes other than DHCP might cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: DHCP relay presumes that a flow found via lookup is always a server-side flow of type DHCP relay. Hence TMM can crash when DHCP relay makes a server connection if UDP port 67 is used for another purpose, in which case a wrong DHCP server flow could be selected.
bugs.conditions: A UDP port 67 is configured for a purpose other than DHCP relay.
bugs.impact: TMM restart causes traffic interruption or failover.
bugs.workaround: Do not use UDP port 67 for other virtual servers, or configure a drop listener on certain VLANs that cannot avoid using UDP port 67.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with DHCP flow validation.

bugs.title: Modify b.root-servers.net IPv4 address 192.228.79.201 to 199.9.14.201 according to InterNIC
bugs.symptoms: The current IPv4 address for b.root-servers.net is 192.228.79.201. The IPv4 address for b.root-servers.net will be renumbered to 199.9.14.201, effective 2017-10-24. The older number will be invalid after that date.
bugs.conditions: Several profiles contain the b.root-servers.net IPv4 address as 192.228.79.201.
bugs.impact: The impact is likely minimal, at most a single timeout for pending TLD queries when they happen to round-robin onto an old IP address, probably not more often than the hint's TTL, which is more than a month, and even this should cause a timeout only when the old IP actually stops responding.
bugs.workaround: Update the root hints for all affected profiles manually except the hardwired ones.
bugs.fix: The IPv4 address for b.root-servers.net has been renumbered to 199.9.14.201, effective 2017-10-24.
bugs.behavior: The IPv4 address for b.root-servers.net has been renumbered to 199.9.14.201, effective 2017-10-24, according to InterNIC. The old IPv4 address (192.228.79.201) will continue to answer queries for at least 6 months.

bugs.title: Cannot SSH in with password after deploying Azure VE
bugs.symptoms: Password provided by user and accepted by Azure might be rejected by the BIG-IP. This results in the inability to immediately SSH-in with a password after successfully deploying Azure Virtual Edition (VE). This occurs because BIG-IP system applies its own password check for the password provided in the Azure user interface, such as Portal, ARM template, etc. The result is that Azure VE administrators cannot SSH-in immediately after deployment has succeeded. They must wait for 1-2 minutes, or no longer than 5 minutes, to let VE set the BIG-IP password after deployment. Weak passwords will be accepted, but you will be warned after SSH login that you need to change to use stronger passwords for both 'admin' and provided users as soon as possible. The message appears similar to the following: Warning: Password is too weak. Please set a stronger one for 'admin' and 'tester' users ASAP. Note: This is true only for password-based authentication. There is no impact on key-based authentication. VE Administrators can still SSH-in immediately after deployment has succeeded.
bugs.conditions: Azure VE with password-based authentication.
bugs.impact: There is no significant impact on interactive SSH into Azure VE, while automated deployments have no logic to retry or delay SSH-in attempts until the password is set.
bugs.workaround: Wait 1-2 minutes (no longer than 5 minutes) after successful deployment to let VE set the BIG-IP password.
bugs.fix: Behavior changes after applying a BIG-IP password check.

bugs.title: IKEv1 logging 'No need for ISAKMP mode config' event
bugs.symptoms: An unnecessary and distracting log line appears in /var/log/ltm when a IKEv1 security association is negotiated: No need for ISAKMP mode config. This is an internal mechanism related to dynamic IP address allocation at negotiation time, which the BIG-IP system does not support.
bugs.conditions: When a remote peer is configured for IKEv1.
bugs.impact: No impact beyond the message in /var/log/ltm for each SA negotiated.
bugs.fix: IKEv1 no longer sends the event involved, because the system does not depend on this event.

bugs.title: IKEv1 newest established phase-one SAs should be found first in a search
bugs.symptoms: Some IKEv1 implementations might delete "duplicate" phase one IKE SAs, even though not yet expired, keeping only the most recently negotiated IKE-SA. If this happens, and BIG-IP uses an older SA to negotiate, then phase two negotiation can fail. If at all possible, we want BIG-IP to prefer the newest SA for a given remote peer. If a peer deletes a second SA without notifying BigIP, preferring a newest SA may mitigate the problem.
bugs.conditions: The situation seems mostly easily arranged when two peers initiate a new IKE-SA at the same time, so that both are negotiated concurrently, since neither has yet been established. Afterward, there are two IKE-SAs for one remote peer, nearly the same age. If the other end deletes a duplicate without sending a DELETE message to BigIP, we might accidently use the older SA of a pair.
bugs.impact: If BIG-IP picks a mature IKE-SA for phase two negotiation that has been deleted by a peer, then BIG-IP's attempt to negotiate a new phase two SA will fail.
bugs.workaround: Try to configure other IPsec implementations to avoid deleting duplicate IKE-SAs.
bugs.fix: At the momenet a new IKE-SA is established, we now move that SA to the head of the hashmap bucket searched for that remote peer in the future. This makes us more likely to use the newest SA from the perspective of a remote peer, the next time we initiate another phase two negotiation ourselves.

bugs.title: Latest Opera Mini on Android is blocked by proactive bot defense
bugs.symptoms: Proactive bot defense blocks opera mini.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM or DoS Provisioned. 2. DoS Application profile assigned to a virtual server. 3. Proactive Bot Defense and Block suspicious browsers sections are enabled in the DoS Application profile configuration.
bugs.impact: End user cannot surf a website using Opera Mini browser on Android.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: CanIUse db has been updated to support opera mini.

bugs.title: iSeries LCD screen is frozen on a red spinning 'please wait' indicator
bugs.symptoms: There are conditions where the LCD looks frozen on a red spinning 'please wait' indicator. Known conditions include: power supply swaps, AC power cycles, or LCD connection issues to the host or AOM.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during power supply swaps, AC power cycles, or LCD connection issues to the host or AOM.
bugs.impact: iSeries LCD screen is frozen on a red spinning 'please wait' indicator. At this point the LCD screen is not usable until it is reset.
bugs.workaround: Using a command line prompt, from either the front panel management port or serial port, issue the following IPMI commands to reset the LCD module: ipmiutil cmd 00 20 e8 29 5 1 ipmiutil cmd 00 20 e8 29 5 0

bugs.title: BIG-IP not sending RST for SYN,ACK packets when ASM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP silently drop the serverside TCP flow, when it receives a client-side reset and the server-side flow is still in the SYN-SENT state.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP receives a client-side reset when client-side TCP flow is in ESTABLISHED state and server-side TCP flow is in SYN-SENT state, serverside flow is silently dropped.
bugs.impact: Since serverside pool member does not receive the RST, it remains in SYN-RECEIVED state until it runs out of syn retransmissions and eventually, due to timeout, it returns to LISTEN state.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP resets serverside TCP flow with RST when it receives a client-side reset and the server-side flow is still in the SYN-SENT state.

bugs.title: SOD may send SIGABRT to TMM when TMM has not reported its heartbeat for a long enough period of time.
bugs.symptoms: This seems to happen very infrequently. Symptoms vary from a simple TMM restart up to a blade reset. LTM log will show a sod message complaining about TMM heartbeats, followed later by SIGABRT messages from TMM.
bugs.conditions: TMM has not reported its heartbeat for a long enough period of time. The specific circumstances are unknown, but the issue has been seen with moderate-to-heavy system loads.
bugs.impact: Interruptions in data path processing. The interruption can be short for a simple TMM restart, longer for a full blade restart. Though these events altogether are rare, when they happen, it appears the simple TMM restart is more common than the blade restart.

bugs.title: Overriding Profile Max Age in RAM Cache
bugs.symptoms: The max age setting on the AAM profile sets the maximum age of every document in the cache. When a client request matches a document that has exceeded the profile max age, that document is verified with the origin web server before being served to the client.
bugs.conditions: When a document has a max-age that is larger than the max age of the profile.
bugs.impact: Documents with a max-age value greater than the max age setting of the profile are validated more often with the origin web server.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the f5-no-pma token list to tell RAM cache not to use the profile max age (pma) value to determine when to validate the document. Instead, the system uses the document's max-age, Expiration, or the HTTP heuristic value.

bugs.title: SSL Session Persistence hangs upon receipt of fragmented Client Certificate Chain
bugs.symptoms: When a very large Client Certificate Chain, typically exceeding 16,384 bytes, is received by BIG-IP on a virtual service, and Session Persistence is enabled, the handshake hangs.
bugs.conditions: [1] SSL client authentication is enabled on the backend server [2] No SSL profile is specified on the BIG-IP device for the virtual service, on both, client and server side [3] An SSL connection is initiated from the front-end client, via the BIG-IP's virtual service, to the backend server. [4] The client certificate chain is passed to the BIG-IP device as part of initiating the connection.
bugs.impact: The backend server will not be securely accessible via SSL because the connection hangs
bugs.workaround: Disable SSL Session Persistence.
bugs.fix: Whenever a fragmented message is received by a BIG-IP virtual service, subsequent messages contain a 5-byte header, each, which should be accounted for. Upon taking this into consideration, no more multiple-of-5 bytes are found missing while the message is being parsed by the Session Persistence parser, and the parser no longer hangs.

bugs.title: vCMPd may crash when processing bridged network traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions vCMPd may crash while processing bridged network traffic
bugs.conditions: vCMP active in 'host-only' or 'bridged' mode.
bugs.impact: vCMPd may crash, resulting in a failure of guest instances on the same host hardware slot.
bugs.workaround: Deploy guests in isolated mode.
bugs.fix: vCMPd does not crash when processing bridged network traffic.

bugs.title: AWS M5 and C5 instance families are supported
bugs.symptoms: AWS has announced support for M5 and C5 instance families. No previous BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) software supports these new AWS instance families.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to install pre-v14.0.0.1 VE software on M5 and C5 instance families.

bugs.fix: All necessary components are added to support AWS M5 and C5 instance families.
bugs.behavior: No previous BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) software supports the newly announced AWS M5 and C5 instance families. Version 14.0.0.1 officially supports the AWS M5 and C5 instance families.

bugs.title: A virtual server status changes to yellow while still available

bugs.title: Proxy host synchronization
bugs.symptoms: The DB variable proxy.host is not synced to the peer. The other related db variables (proxy.port, proxy.protocol, proxy.username, and proxy.password) are synced to the peer.
bugs.conditions: When using proxy in a high availability (HA) configuration.

bugs.title: Updating tests according to canIUse database

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense has false positive selenuim detection for UCBrowser
bugs.symptoms: Proactive Bot Defense reports about selenium detection and blocks legitimate users of UCBrowser.

bugs.title: The iRulesLX RPC completion can cause invalid or premature TCL rule resumption
bugs.symptoms: RPC completion will attempt to resume the RPC iRule execution when there is subsequent iRule activity on the flow - CLIENT/SERVER_CLOSED, for instance, which keeps the flow alive and blocks in an iRule event.
bugs.conditions: Blocking the iRule event When an RPC call is outstanding and the flow is aborted.
bugs.impact: It will cause the iRule event blocking when RPC call is outstanding and the flow is aborted
bugs.fix: Cancel ILX RPC TCL resumption if iRule event is aborted before resumption (reply or timeout) occurs.

bugs.title: ASM with Web Acceleration Profile can rarely cause TMM to core
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores after running web traffic. TMM stays down following the crash, even after traffic has stopped.
bugs.conditions: When ASM is provisioned with web acceleration profile.
bugs.impact: Data forwarding which causes tmm to core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.conditions: Configuration of '+' character in log profile name

bugs.impact: switch/color_policer tmctl table is not available in 12.1.0 - 13.1.0
bugs.fix: No fix.

bugs.title: Monitor node log not rotated for icmp monitor types
bugs.symptoms: When Monitor Logging is enabled for an LTM node or pool member using certain monitor types, the monitor node log under /var/log/monitors/ is not rotated or compressed when log rotation occurs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if Monitor Logging is enabled for an LTM node or pool member and the LTM node or pool member uses any of the following monitor types: - icmp - gateway-icmp
bugs.impact: Depending on the affected BIG-IP version in use, affects may include: 1. The active monitor node log is not rotated (not renamed from *.log to *.log.1). 2. The active monitor node log is rotated (renamed from *.log to *.log.1), but subsequent messages are logged to the rotated log file (*.log.1) instead of to the 'current' log file name (*.log). 3. The active monitor node log is not compressed (*.log.2.gz) when log rotation occurs.
bugs.workaround: To allow logging to the correct monitor node log file to occur, and for rotated monitor node log files to be compressed, disable Monitor Logging for the affected node or pool member(s). If symptom #1 (from Impact section above) occurs, Monitor Logging can be re-enabled after log rotation has occurred. To address symptom #2 or #3 (from Impact section above), Monitor Logging can be re-enabled immediately. For more information on Monitor Logging, see: K12531: Troubleshooting health monitors
bugs.fix: Monitor node logs are now rotated/compressed as expected.

bugs.title: IKEv2 ike-peer might crash on stats object during peer modification update
bugs.symptoms: A crash occurs upon passing traffic through the IPsec interface.
bugs.conditions: When an ike-peer is updated, or first defined at startup.

bugs.workaround: No workaround is known at this time.
bugs.fix: IKEv2 ike-peer no longer crashes on stats object during peer modification update.

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense sends CAPTCHA to the Firefox browser on iOS only in desktop mode
bugs.symptoms: When a request arrives from Firefox running on iOS in desktop mode and without TSPD_101 (proactive bot defense cookie). The big-ip respond with captcha challenge.

bugs.title: iHealth should show sfdisk info for vda for Z101 vcmp guests.
bugs.symptoms: After collecting a qkview, the data regarding the output from sfdisk doesn't show /dev/vd* devices since it is looking for /dev/sd* or /dev/hd* only.

bugs.title: tmsh::load within IApp template results in unpredicted behavior

One of the unexpected behavior seen is with the template having ASM policy and LTM policy. bugs.title: Substitute value support on change password pages

bugs.fix: BIG-IP will set the same value to fields only if their real value is equal.

bugs.title: HTML field obfuscation is not supported with SPA
bugs.symptoms: HTML field obfuscation feature is not supported on Single Page Application (SPA).
bugs.conditions: Configure WebSafe for SPA.
bugs.impact: HTML field obfuscation feature is not supported.

bugs.title: VPN cannot be established on macOS High Sierra 10.13.1 if full tunneling configuration is enabled
bugs.symptoms: For some Network Access configurations, VPN cannot establish a connection with client systems running macOS High Sierra 10.13.1 using F5 Edge client or Browser helper apps.
bugs.conditions: The following conditions must be true: -- The Network Access resource Traffic Options setting is configured for Force all Traffic Through Tunnel. -- The Network Access resource Allow Local Subnet setting is disabled. (Both of these options are defaults.) -- Client running macOS High Sierra 10.13.1.

bugs.title: High CPU Usage by the TMM Can Cause SOD to Kill vCMP Guests
bugs.symptoms: vCMP Guests restart or go offline.
bugs.conditions: In vCMP mode, when the TMM on the host uses too much CPU.
bugs.impact: vCMP Guests restart or go offline.
bugs.workaround: An adjustment to the scheduling can be made by this setting of the vCMP Host configuration: # echo "realtime yield 3" > /config/tmm_init.tcl # bigstart restart tmm (This setting must be performed individually on all blades.)

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense sends CAPTCHA to the Safari 5-6.2
bugs.symptoms: Safari 5-6.2 gets CAPTCHA when Proactive Bot Defense si enabled and a request arrives without valid Proactive Bot Defense cookie.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM or DoS Provisioned. 2. DoS Application profile assigned to a virtual server. 3. Proactive Bot Defense and Block suspicious browsers sections are enabled in the DoS Application profile configuration.
bugs.impact: Legitimate users of Safari 5-6.2 are challenged with captcha.
bugs.workaround: Disable Proactive Bot Defense or change browser_legit_min_score_drop sys db to be higher value. list sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop { value "120" }
bugs.fix: CanIUse db has been updated to support Safari 5-6.2

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense sends CAPTCHA to the UC browser on iOS devices
bugs.symptoms: When a request arrives from UCBrowser running on iOS and without TSPD_101 (proactive bot defense cookie). The big-ip respond with captcha challenge.
bugs.conditions: Dos profile attached to a virtual. Dos profile has application security enabled. Dos profile has proactive bot defense enabled.
bugs.impact: UC browser end-user presented with captcha challenge.
bugs.workaround: Increase proactive bot defense score. list sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_captcha sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_captcha { value "60" }
bugs.fix: User agent parser has been changed (adjusted) for the UC browser. The UC browser is detected as safari ios.

bugs.title: Mobile UC browser has been blocked by Proactive Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: A request from UC Browser installed on a mobile device is blocked (got RST packet or captcha).

To do so, use a configuration similar to the following: list sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop { value "120" }

bugs.title: Improved cases of legetimitae browsers getting captcha
bugs.symptoms: Some legitimate browsers may be detected as suspicious.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense, Block suspicious browsers is enabled.
bugs.impact: In some cases legit users might get Captcha.

bugs.title: Adaptive monitor feature does not mark pool member down when hard limit set on UDP monitors
bugs.symptoms: Member of pool is not marked down when response time exceeds hard limit.
bugs.conditions: Adaptive monitoring enabled for UDP monitor and server response time exceeds hard limit.
bugs.impact: Member remains in pool despite exceeding hard limit which may result in degraded services.

bugs.title: APMD may restart continuously and cannot come up
bugs.symptoms: apmd process cannot start correctly and restarts in an infinite loop. When apmd initializes the Allow Ending agent, the process tries to load all resources (including ACLs, the webtop, and all resources for every webtop, app tunnels, rdp, etc.). The most likely configuration to encounter this issue is with ACLs. For example, if you have thousands of ACL records, the Allow agent pulls them all at once. If the mcpd process is consumed with other operations, it might be that apmd cannot initialize the Allow agent in 30 secs, so it restarts, at which point the process tries to load all resources, cannot complete within the 30 seconds, and restarts in a loop.
bugs.conditions: Too many resources assigned in an Access Policy profile for example thousands of ACLs configured. apmd cannot initialize the Allow Ending agent in 30 seconds and decides it has stopped responding. Then it restarts by it's own, but problem is not solved, so it restarts in a loop
bugs.impact: APM end users cannot authenticate.
bugs.workaround: Reduce amount of resources so every agent can initialize within the 30-second timeframe.

bugs.title: ospfd core on secondary blade during network unstability
bugs.symptoms: ospfd core on secondary blade while network is unstable.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing configured with OSPF on a chassis. -- During a period of network instability.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing process ospfd core on secondary blade.

bugs.title: Active FTP data connection may change source port on client-side
bugs.symptoms: The active FTP data connection on the client-side may use source port other than what was configured in the 'Data Port' parameter of the FTP profile.
bugs.conditions: FTP profile is attached to a virtual server and the 'Data Port' parameter is either left as default (20) or defined as a specific value.
bugs.impact: Active FTP data connection may be blocked by firewalls that expect a pre-defined source port.
bugs.fix: Now strict preserve source port mode is applied for the active FTP data connection when the 'Data Port' parameter is defined. The source port mode of the control plane FTP virtual is used when the 'Data Port' parameter is set to 0.

bugs.title: Traffic Interruption for MAC Addresses Learned on Interfaces that Enter Blocked STP State (2000/4000/i2800/i4800 series)
bugs.symptoms: Some MAC addresses might experience delayed forwarding after the interface on which they are learned transition to a STP blocked state. This is because the FDB entries are not being flushed on these interfaces after they change to a block state. Traffic destined to these MAC addresses gets dropped until their associated entries in the FDB age out.
bugs.conditions: MAC addresses are learned on a STP forwarding interface that transitions to a blocked interface following a topology change.
bugs.impact: Traffic interruption for up to a few minutes for MAC addresses learned on the affected interface.
bugs.fix: FDB entries are now flushed by interface whenever an interface transitions to a STP block state.

bugs.title: Qkview utility may generate invalid XML in files contained in Qkview
bugs.symptoms: When Qkview runs, it may gather XML files that are not well-formed, and contain ASCII control characters. This is most commonly seen with mcp_module.xml. An XML validator may report an error such as: mcp_module.xml:536081: parser error : PCDATA invalid Char value 29 <msgs></msgs> ^
bugs.conditions: -- Running Qkview. -- An ASCII control character exists within a certain string field.
bugs.impact: The control character will be written verbatim into XML without encoding. Automated tools (e.g., iHealth) that attempt to process these files may fail.
bugs.workaround: iHealth automatically detects and corrects this issue in uploaded Qkviews. You can analyze the XML files with some other tool, a tar.gz, so it can be unpacked, the XML files edited to correct the formatting, and then repacked. The xmllint command-line tool (present on the BIG-IP system) can also recover valid XML by removing the invalid characters. To do so, you can run a command similar to the following: xmllint --recover mcp_module.xml --output mcp_module.xml
bugs.fix: Qkview no longer writes control characters in XML text, but instead processes them as expected.

bugs.title: TCP sndpack not reset along with other tcp profile stats
bugs.symptoms: TCP sndpack stat added is not being properly reset when a tmsh reset-stats command is issued.
bugs.conditions: When tmsh reset-stats command is issued. -- tmsh reset-stats /ltm profile tcp <profile-name>
bugs.impact: TCP sndpack stat doesn't reset when tmsh reset-stats command is issued.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: With this fix, TCP sndpack stat will reset when tmsh reset-stats command is issued.

bugs.title: Autoscale is not functional because of the change in file permission of the /shared/vadc/aws/iid-document document
bugs.symptoms: The /shared/vadc/aws/iid-document's file permission changed and as a result the autoscale feature was failing.
bugs.conditions: Whenever autoscale is triggered
bugs.impact: The autoscale feature does not work
bugs.workaround: The permission of /shared/vadc/aws/iid-document was never set explicitly. It inherited file permission flags from /shared/vadc/. We set the file permission explicitly.
bugs.fix: The autoscale feature is functional after changing file permissions of /shared/vadc/aws/iid-document.

bugs.title: F5 VPN or Edge Client may drop DTLS and use TLS if DTLS packet reordering happens
bugs.symptoms: F5 VPN or Edge Client may drop DTLS and use TLS if DTLS packet reordering happens. Only Mac and Linux clients are affected. Messages in svpn log indicate bad HTTP header, for example: 2017-10-18,20:20:37:764, 56666,2126506,svpn, 1, /UHTTPChannel.cpp, 414, UHTTPChannel::beginConnection(), EXCEPTION - Could not parse HTTP header.
bugs.conditions: -- F5 VPN or EdgeClient is used. -- Linux or Mac clients.
bugs.impact: UDP packet reordering happens at a specific point of PPP negotiation. TLS is used instead of DTLS.
bugs.fix: Previously, clients connecting via F5 VPN or Edge Client on Mac or Linux using DTLS might switch to TLS if DTLS packet reordering occurred. Now, Mac and Linux Edge Clients can handle UDP packet reordering and continue to use DTLS.

bugs.title: MCPD sync errors and restart after multiple modifications to file object in chassis
bugs.symptoms: Upon modifying file objects on a VIPRION chassis and synchronizing those changes to another VIPRION chassis in a device sync group, the following symptoms may occur: 1. Errors are logged to /var/log/ltm similar to the following: -- err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync: link_stat "/config/filestore/.snapshots_d/<_additional_path_to/_affected_file_object_>" (in csync) failed: No such file or directory (2) ) errno(0) errstr(). -- err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync error: some files could not be transferred (code 23) at main.c(1298) [receiver=2.6.8] syncer /usr/bin/rsync failed! (5888) () Couldn't rsync files for mcpd. ) errno(0) errstr(). -- err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync process failed.) errno(255) errstr(). -- err mcpd[<#>]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files.. 2. MCPD may restart on a secondary blade in a VIPRION chassis that is receiving the configuration sync from the chassis where the file object changes were made.
bugs.conditions: Making multiple changes to the same file objects on a VIPRION chassis and synchronizing those changes to another VIPRION chassis in a device sync group.
bugs.impact: Temporary loss of functionality, including interruption in traffic, on one or more secondary blades in one or more VIPRION chassis that are receiving the configuration sync.
bugs.workaround: After performing one set of file-object modifications and synchronizing those changes to the high availability (HA) group members, wait for one or more minutes to allow all changes to be synchronized to all blades in all member chassis before making and synchronizing changes to the same file-objects.

bugs.title: All signature update details are shown in 'View update history from previous BIG-IP versions' popup
bugs.symptoms: If you are running a BIG-IP release named with 4 digits (e.g., 12.1.3.1), all signature update details are shown only in 'View update history from previous BIG-IP versions' popup. The 'Latest update details' section is missing.
bugs.conditions: Running a BIG-IP software release named with 4 digits (e.g., 12.1.3.1).
bugs.impact: Low and incorrect visibility of signature update details.
bugs.workaround: Signature update details can be viewed in 'View update history from previous BIG-IP versions' popup.
bugs.fix: Signature updates are now shown correctly for all versions.

bugs.title: TMM core with APM
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent tmm core under load.
bugs.conditions: -- Provision at least APM. -- Additional required conditions are not well understood. -- Seems more likely to occur when APM is provisioned with other modules, especially ASM or AVR.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system stops processing traffic while the TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmm core no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Having multiple frames (window scopes) with specific names cause script failure.
bugs.symptoms: There are some variables that appear to be global. Therefore, when changing the 'window' scope, script ran into a logic error
bugs.conditions: Multiple frames (window scopes) with specific names.
bugs.impact: Having multiple frames (window scopes) with specific names cause script failure.
bugs.fix: Moved these global variables to be local and scope-independent.

bugs.title: VPE object names cannot contain special characters
bugs.symptoms: When a VPE object is created or renamed with one or more special characters, the characters are silently removed and the name of the object is saved without them. Special characters stripped from name of the VPE object when creating or renaming said VPE object
bugs.conditions: VPE object is created or renamed with one or more of the following special characters: `~!@#$%^&*={}|:"<>?\;',.?
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. This is working as expected even though it is not documented.
bugs.workaround: Do not include special characters when naming a VPE object.
bugs.fix: The system now posts the following message in this case: VPE objects, such as a message box or macro, cannot contain special characters such as brackets, exclamation points, or question marks. The VPE removes the special characters when saving the object. This is now documented. The following characters are not allowed in VPE object names: `~!@#$%^&*={}|:"<>?\;',.?

bugs.title: PEM subscriber sessions will not be deleted if a CCA-t contains a DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY return code and no request type AVP.
bugs.symptoms: Subscriber sessions in PEM will be stuck in a "Marked for Delete" state.
bugs.conditions: 1. PEM provisioned with Gx. 2. PCRF responds to a CCR-t with a DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY return code and no Request type AVP.
bugs.impact: Subscriber sessions stuck in delete pending resulting in a potential increase in memry consumption over a period of time.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: PCRF (remote Diameter end point) must send a CCA-t with a request type AVP in case a DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY return code is present.
bugs.fix: Handle the DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY return code on a CCA-t regardless of the request type AVP.

bugs.title: CCA without a request type AVP cannot be tracked in PEM.
bugs.symptoms: May cause diagnostic issues as not all CCA messages cannot be tracked.
bugs.conditions: 1. PEM with Gx/Gy configured 2. PCRF sends CCA's without a request type AVP
bugs.impact: May hamper effective diagnostics.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation: Configure the PCRF to always include a request type in its CCAs.
bugs.fix: Add a statistics counter to track CCA's that do not request type AVPs. Name of new counter:cca_unknown_type

bugs.title: With management ip is set as IPv6, the downgrade fails when loading the config because of trailing slash in BIG-IP_base.conf.
bugs.symptoms: Downgrading to older software that has IPv6 management support, when IPv6 management ip is configured, causes the configuration loading to fail due to extra slash in BIG-IP_base.conf (e.g. "2620:128:e008:4009::cafe/64/")
bugs.conditions: Management ip set to IPv6.
bugs.impact: The configuration load of BIG-IP_base.conf fails.
bugs.workaround: To address this issue the user has to edit the BIG-IP_base.conf and remove the extra slash from the management-ip field and re-load the configuration as instructed.

bugs.title: Configuration sync does not sync iControl LX or iApp LX objects
bugs.symptoms: Configuration sync operations do not sync iControl LX or iApp LX objects. In DHD DDos appliances, protected objects are essentially iApp LX blocks, and sometimes the system does not sync them to high availability (HA) peer.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when there are dtca.key and dtca.crt files under the /config/ssl/ssl.key/ and /config/ssl/ssl.crt/ directories that do not match the same files on a peer device.
bugs.impact: iControl LX or iApp LX objects do not sync to HA peer. The Config Sync indicator on the BIG-IP system will say 'in sync'.
bugs.workaround: One possible workaround is to manually discover other BIG-IP devices in the REST device group by providing usernames and passwords. To do so, you can use a curl command similar to the following: curl -X POST -d '{"address":"other_BIG-IP_mgmt_ip", "userName": "admin", "password":"admin_pw"}' http://localhost:8100/shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices
bugs.fix: dtca.key and dtca.crt are file objects that are managed by MCP. MCP keeps the correct copy of the these files in File Objects cache. iAppLX reads these from MCP and File objects cache rather than /config/ssl/ssl.key.

bugs.title: vCloud Director images not available
bugs.symptoms: There is no dedicated vCloud Director BIG-IP image of v13.0.0 HF3 to use for install/upgrade operations.
bugs.conditions: -- Installing BIG-IP v13.0.0 HF3. -- Upgrading to BIG-IP v13.0.0 HF3 from a prior release.
bugs.impact: Cannot use previously available method of installing/upgrading using a dedicated vCloud Director image. Note: Separate vCloud Director images are not available for BIG-IP v13.0.0 HF3. However, you can upgrade using the hotfix ISO or install using the general OVA images.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade a prior release using the hotfix ISO, or install using OVA for other VMware environments.

bugs.title: Errant log message appears as an error
bugs.symptoms: A log message similar to the following appears in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[]: 0107167d:3: Data publisher not found or not implemented when processing request (unknown request), tag (31624).
bugs.conditions: No specific conditions trigger this message. You might see this message when you inspect the LTM log after booting.
bugs.impact: There is no negative impact to the system. You can safely ignore this message.
bugs.workaround: No need for a workaround. The message can be ignored or filtered.

bugs.title: TMSH save sys config creates unneeded generate_config processes.
bugs.symptoms: When saving a configuration through TMSH or iControl REST, a process called generate_config is created.
bugs.conditions: Run tmsh save sys config, or the same command through iControl REST.
bugs.impact: One generate_config process will be generated per save operation. If config save occurs often, these extraneous processes can slowly fill up the process table.
bugs.workaround: There is no real workaround except to not save the config often enough to fill up process table with these extraneous processes. If the process table is full, to recover, you can restart tmsh, scriptd, or restjavad to clear out these unneeded processes.
bugs.fix: tmsh save sys config no longer generates generate_config processes.

bugs.title: Some process names may have last character truncated when viewing in iHealth
