bugs.symptoms: qkview reads the contents of the /proc directory to obtain details about running processes on a BIG-IP system. Occasionally, it will drop the last character of the process name. This is observable when displaying process information on the iHealth service after uploading a qkview.
bugs.conditions: Always
bugs.impact: Minimal
bugs.workaround: Don't assume that every process name is complete.
bugs.fix: This has been fixed.

bugs.title: SSO enabled Native RDP resources can't be accessed via hardware BIG-IP with "Intel Cave Creek" coprocessor
bugs.symptoms: APM Webtop's SSO enabled Native RDP resources can't be accessed via hardware BIG-IP with "Intel Cave Creek" coprocessor (e.g. BIG-IP 2000 (C112) or 4000 (C113)) from Mac, iOS and Android clients. Each launch attempt generates following errors in /var/log/apm: ... err vdi[123] ... {45.C} RsaDecryptData error: AsyncError:5: InvalidData ... err vdi[123] ... {45.C} An exception is thrown: handshake: decryption failed or bad record mac
bugs.conditions: Native RDP resource with enabled SSO is used on hardware BIG-IP with "Intel Cave Creek" coprocessor (e.g. BIG-IP 2000 (C112) or 4000 (C113)). The client OS is Mac, iOS or Android.
bugs.impact: RDP client can't launch requested resource (desktop/application).
bugs.workaround: Disable crypto HW acceleration with following command: tmsh modify sys db crypto.hwacceleration value disable
bugs.fix: SSO enabled Native RDP resources now can be accessed via hardware BIG-IP with "Intel Cave Creek" coprocessor (e.g. BIG-IP 2000 (C112) or 4000 (C113) platforms) from Mac, iOS and Android clients.

bugs.title: Routing changes may cause TMM to restart
bugs.symptoms: When routing changes are made while traffic is passing through the BIG-IP system, TMM might restart. This isn't a general issue, but can occur when other functionality is in use (such as Firewall NAT).
bugs.conditions: -- Routing changes occurring while BIG-IP is active and passing traffic. -- Dynamic routing, due to its nature, is likely increase the potential for the issue to occur. -- Usage of Firewall NAT functionality is one specific case known to contribute to the issue (there may be others).
bugs.impact: TMM restarts, resulting in a failover and/or traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: If dynamic routing is not in use, avoiding static route changes may avoid the issue. If dynamic routing is in use, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: TMM now properly manages routing information for active connections.

bugs.title: ASM GUI displaying inconsistent policy sync version information
bugs.symptoms: There is an inconsistency in how ASM-config derives the current policy revision, and in how it determines what is the 'latest' revision number for a policy. When upgrading machine the system attempts to restore the 'last active version' of each policy. The system determines the latest version by the highest revision number, which is now wrong. So an older version of the policy is restored.
bugs.conditions: Inactivate policy and activate again.
bugs.impact: The policy revision numbers start again, so the GUI appears to be displaying incorrect information, which can cause confusion.
bugs.fix: The system now ensures the correct revision sequence in Policy History, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: On multiblade Viprion, creating a new traffic-group causes the device to go Offline
bugs.symptoms: All devices in the failover device group will go offline, resulting in traffic disruption and possible failovers.
bugs.conditions: When a new traffic-group is created on a multiblade Viprion system that is a member of a sync-failover device group.
bugs.impact: Traffic to all other traffic-groups is disrupted for several seconds.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Creating a new traffic-group does not disrupt existing traffic-groups.

bugs.title: clusterd logs heartbeat check messages at log level info
bugs.symptoms: The system reports clusterd logs heartbeat check messages at log level info, similar to the following. -- info clusterd[6161]: 013a0007:6: Skipping heartbeat check on peer slot 3: Slot is DOWN. -- info clusterd[5705]: 013a0007:6: Checking heartbeat of peer slot: 2 (Last heartbeat 0 seconds ago)
bugs.conditions: log.clusterd.level set to info.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue: clusterd heartbeat messages will be logged at info to the /var/log/ltm.
bugs.workaround: Set log.clusterd.level to notice.
bugs.fix: The log level of clusterd logs heartbeat check messages has changed. For 'Skipping heartbeat check' messages, the log level is now debug, and 'Checking heartbeat of peer slot' messages log level is verbose and now reports on which bp the heartbeat was received.

bugs.title: Potential memory leak and TMM crash due to a PEM iRule command resulting in a remote lookup.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes
bugs.conditions: PEM iRule command that would result in an inter-TMM lookup on a long lived flow that would result in the PEM iRule command being hit several times. For example, a long lived flow with multiple HTTP transactions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Always release the connFlow reference associated with the TCL command to avoid a memory leak and potential crash.

bugs.title: BIG-IP reboot during a TMM core results in an incomplete core dump
bugs.symptoms: If an HSB lockup occurs on i10600 and i10800 platforms, then HSB panics and generates a core file for post-analysis. HSB also triggers a nic_failsafe reboot. On this platform, the reboot occurs before the core file is fully written, resulting in a truncated core.
bugs.conditions: An HSB lockup occurs, triggering a core dump and a nic_failsafe reboot.
bugs.impact: The reboot happens before the core dump completes, resulting in an incomplete core dump which is not useful for analyzing why the HSB lockup occurred. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround; does not hinder device operation, but does prevent post-crash analysis.
bugs.fix: Reboot is delayed until TMM core file is completed.

bugs.title: Changing the system's admin user causes vCMP host guest health info to be unavailable
bugs.symptoms: On the host, 'tmsh show vcmp health' does not display guest info. The iControl REST log at /var/log/icrd contains entries similar to the following: notice icrd_child[32206]: 01420003:5: Cannot load user credentials for user "admin" Current session has been terminated.
bugs.conditions: The default admin user "admin" has been changed. Note: You changed the default admin user by following the steps in the Article K15632: Disabling the admin and root accounts using the BIG-IP Configuration utility or the Traffic Management Shell: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K15632.
bugs.impact: Many REST APIs do not function, and functionality such as vCMP guest health that depend on REST fails.
bugs.workaround: Rename the default system admin back to 'admin': tmsh modify /sys db systemauth.primaryadminuser value admin Note: If you are using the default 'admin' account, make sure you change the password as well.

bugs.title: Certain Intel Crypto HW fails to decrypt data if the given output buffer size differs from RSA private key size
bugs.symptoms: SSO-enabled Native RDP resources cannot be accessed via hardware (HW) BIG-IP systems with 'Intel Cave Creek' coprocessor (i.e., SSL connection cannot be established with the db variable 'crypto.hwacceleration' enabled, and RSA key used).
bugs.conditions: The failure might occur in the following scenario: -- Running on Intel Cave Creek Engine (e.g., BIG-IP 2000 (C112) or 4000 (C113)). -- Client OS is Mac, iOS, or Android. -- HW crypto is enabled -- Using a virtual server with a client SSL profile and 2048 bit RSA key on. -- Native RDP resource with enabled SSO is used on hardware BIG-IP with 'Intel Cave Creek' coprocessor. -- Output buffer size differs from RSA private key size.
bugs.impact: -- SSL connection fails. -- RDP client cannot launch the requested resource (desktop/application).
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable crypto HW acceleration with following command: tmsh modify sys db crypto.hwacceleration value disable
bugs.fix: SSL connection can now be established as expected. SSO-enabled Native RDP resources now can now be accessed via hardware BIG-IP systems with 'Intel Cave Creek' coprocessor (e.g., BIG-IP 2000 (C112) or 4000 (C113) platforms) from Mac, iOS, and Android clients.

bugs.title: TMM crash when packet sampling is turned for DNS BDOS signatures.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes upon traffic matching a DNS BDOS signature if packet sampling is turned on by enabling db variable (l4bdos.signature.sample.packet.frequency).
bugs.conditions: DB variable l4bdos.signature.sample.packet.frequency is modified to a non-zero value (to collect DNS packet info upon matching a DNS dynamic signature).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable the packet sampling feature for BDOS signatures by setting the db variable l4bdos.signature.sample.packet.frequency to default value (0).
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when packet sampling is turned on and traffic matches DNS BDOS signature.

bugs.title: Unsupported Copper SFP can trigger a crash on i4x00 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: PFMAND can crash when an unsupported Proline Copper SFP is inserted in the 1G interfaces.
bugs.conditions: -- Using Proline CuSFP, Part number FCLF8521P2BTLTAA. -- Inserted into 1 GB interfaces. -- On i4x00 platforms.
bugs.impact: PFMAND cores.
bugs.workaround: Use only F5 branded Copper SFPs
bugs.fix: This release updates SFP string parsing in PFMAND to account for NULL terminated vendor information.

bugs.title: ASM Auto-Sync Device Group Does Not Sync
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances a device may enter an untrusted state and confuse the device group.
bugs.conditions: 1) ASM sync is enabled on an autosync device group 2) A new ASM entity is created on a device
bugs.impact: ASM configuration is not correctly synchronized between devices
bugs.workaround: 1) Remove ASM sync from the device group (Under Security ›› Options : Application Security : Synchronization : Application Security Synchronization) 2) Restart asm_config_server.pl on both devices and wait until they come back up 3) Change the device group to a manual sync group 4) On the device with the good configuration re-enable ASM sync for the device group 5) Make a spurious ASM change, and push the configuration. 6) Change the sync type back to automatic
bugs.fix: Devices no longer spuriously enter an untrusted state

bugs.title: bd crashes on a very specific and rare scenario
bugs.symptoms: When the system is configured in a specific way and the request sender responds incorrectly, bd crashes.
bugs.conditions: This rarely encountered crash occurs when there is a very specific BIG-IP system configuration, and ICAP is configured but not responding.
bugs.impact: bd crashes.
bugs.fix: The bd crash no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: bcm56xxd restart causes error logs from stpd, lldpd and lacpd.
bugs.symptoms: When bcm56xxd restarts as a result of an interface bundling change, other daemons (lldpd, stpd, lacpd) lose connectivity for the duration of the restart. This loss of connectivity results in the following errors being logged: -- err stpd[11965]: 01290003:3: HalmsgTerminalImpl_::sendMessage() Unable to send to any BCM56XXD address -- err stpd[11965]: 01280012:3: HAL packet request sendMessage failed (slot 0) -- err lacpd[10147]: 01290003:3: HalmsgTerminalImpl_::sendMessage() Unable to send to any BCM56XXD address -- err lacpd[10147]: 01160005:3: HalMsgHandler.cpp:125 - HAL send PDU request failed -- lldpd[11052]: 01290003:3: HalmsgTerminalImpl_::sendMessage() Unable to send to any BCM56XXD address -- err lldpd[11052]: 01570004:3: HAL send PDU request failed
bugs.conditions: Enabling or disabling bundling on 40 GB interface.
bugs.impact: Restart of bcm56xxd, which also results in restart of other daemons and logging of error messages to LTM log. Traffic disrupted while daemons restart.
bugs.fix: Enabling or disabling bundling on 40 GB interface now presents a message similar to the following: Are you sure? Y/N (changing the interface bundling will restart bcm56xxd, cause loss of connectivity to other daemons and impact traffic).

bugs.title: In rare situations hardware syncookies may be sent for a L7 virtual server when hardware syncookie protection is disabled
bugs.symptoms: In rare situations, hardware syncookies may be sent for the traffic received on a L7 virtual server even though hardware syncookie protection is disabled on the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: It is unknown what triggers this error condition at this point.
bugs.impact: Some of the TCP options are not supported under hardware syncookie protection mode.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Changes to fallback persistence profiles attached to a Virtual server are not effective
bugs.symptoms: Changes to fallback persistence profiles attached to a Virtual server may not be effective.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with persistence and a fallback persistence profile. -- Changes made to the fallback persistence profile.
bugs.impact: Changes to the fallback persistence profile are not effective with new connections until a change is made to the virtual server or TMM is restarted.
bugs.workaround: Make a simple change, for instance to the description field, to the virtual servers that have the changed fallback persistence profile configured.

bugs.title: bigd cores and sends corrupted MCP messages with many FQDN nodes
bugs.symptoms: When configured to monitor large numbers of nodes and/or pool members including FQDN nodes and/or pool members, the following symptoms may occur: - bigd may core (aborted by sod due to missed heartbeat). - bigd may produce corrupted MCP messages. - FQDN nodes and/or pool members may remain in a Checking state indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: These symptoms may occur on affected versions of BIG-IP when a large number of nodes and/or pool members including FQDN nodes and/or pool members are configured. Depending on the capabilities of the platform in use, approximately one thousand (1,000) or more total nodes and/or pool members may be required to produce these symptoms. FQDN nodes and/or pool members generate a more significant workload for the bigd daemon than nodes and/or pool members with statically-configured IP addresses. This additional load contributes to high CPU usage and the other observed symptoms.
bugs.impact: This issue produces the following impacts: - bigd may core. - nodes and/or pool members may remain in a Checking state indefinitely. - bigd may produce corrupted MCP messages, which generate error messages in the LTM log of the following form: ... err mcpd[####]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Can't parse MCP message, ... Examination of the corrupted MCP message shows objects at the point of corruption that have no hierarchical relationship with the objects referenced at the beginning of the message.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use the following approaches singly or in combination: 1. Reduce the number of nodes and/or pool members configured for a given BIG-IP system. 2. Configure nodes and/or pool members with statically-configured IP addresses.
bugs.fix: bigd no longer produces corrupted MCP messages, resulting in nodes and/or pool members remaining in a 'checking' state, with up to 2,000 nodes and/or pool members including FQDN nodes and/or pool members configured. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: If FIPS card goes bad and cannot initialize, the BIG-IP system will continuously reboot
bugs.symptoms: If FIPS card has a problem and cannot initialize, the BIG-IP system will continuously reboot with following message indicating failure to initialize FIPS device: Initializing FIPS device (n3fips): (Timeout) [FAILED]
bugs.conditions: FIPS card has a problem and cannot initialize.
bugs.impact: System will keep rebooting.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: QS user defined alerts may not be sent if there is no URL with qs configured on FPS profile
bugs.symptoms: when FPS signature update defines a URL with a query string, and defines a custom alert for that URL, the alert will not be sent if there is no URL with a query string configured on the FPS profile.
bugs.conditions: 1. Custom alert for a URL with query string. 2. There are. no URLs with query string configured on FPS profile
bugs.impact: System does not send alert.
bugs.workaround: Define a URL (potentially a placeholder URL) with query string on FPS profile.

bugs.title: Configuring two similar log filters with different destinations can result in undefined behavior
bugs.symptoms: The log destination used for logging is undefined.
bugs.conditions: If two or more log filters are created with the same log level, message ID, and source but with different log destinations.
bugs.impact: Only one filter will be used, so this can cause confusion when you expect logs to one or all of the log destinations.
bugs.workaround: Delete the duplicate filters.

bugs.title: Improve speed of ASM initialization on first startup
bugs.symptoms: ASM initialization on first startup takes a long time.
bugs.conditions: Provision ASM.
bugs.impact: ASM initialization takes a long time.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: ASM initialization on first startup is faster.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not retransmit DATA_FIN when closing an MPTCP connection
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP does not retransmit DATA_FIN when closing an MPTCP connection.
bugs.conditions: Close an MPTCP connection.
bugs.impact: If a DATA_ACK is not received for the DATA_FIN, the connection will stall until it times out.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Keep the retransmission timer running if an MPTCP connection can retransmit a DATA_FIN.

bugs.title: Changes in browsers tests for Device ID calculation
bugs.symptoms: Some browser tests are inaccurate.
bugs.conditions: Device ID collection is enabled on either the ASM Policy or DoS Profile.
bugs.impact: Device ID might be inaccurate in some cases.
bugs.fix: Removed some tests.

bugs.title: FPS: empty POST alert request may be forwarded to application server
bugs.symptoms: empty POST alert request forwarded to app server when trigger irule event is enabled
bugs.conditions: 1. empty POST alert request 2. trigger irule events is enabled in FPS profile
bugs.impact: alert is erroneously forwarded to the application server
bugs.workaround: drop the empty POST alert request with an irule
bugs.fix: FPS will not forward alerts to the application server

bugs.title: Entry for ssl key removed from tmsh causes tmsh load config to fail
bugs.symptoms: As part of phonehome, the licensing process uses an encrypted key which keeps it's passphrase securely in tmsh.
bugs.conditions: If the tmsh entry is deleted, then the key can no longer be used and issuing a new registration key will fail to create a new key and the bigip.conf will no longer load.
bugs.impact: The bigip.conf will not load without having to edit out the key and certificate entries. Also, phonehome will not work since there is no passphrase for the encrypted key.
bugs.workaround: Edit out the section for f5_api_com.key in /config/bigip.conf and run tmsh load sys config. Then remove the key: rm -f /config/ssl/ssl.key/f5_api_com.key and reinstall the license registration key.
bugs.fix: The fix will test if the tmsh has a reference to the f5_ap_com.key and delete the actual key during the license process which will then generate a new key and passphrase, thus updating tmsh.

bugs.title: Signature enforcement issue on specific requests
bugs.symptoms: Request payload does not get enforced by attack signatures on a certain policy configuration with specific traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- The violation 'Request exceeds max buffer size' is turned off. -- The request is longer than the max buffer size (i.e., a request is larger than the internal long_request_buffer_size).
bugs.impact: Attack signatures are not enforced on the payload of this request at all.
bugs.workaround: Turn on the violation in blocking 'Request exceed max buffer size'.
bugs.fix: The operation now looks into part of the payload for the attack signatures enforcement.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing ProxySSL data
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash will processing SSL/TLS data via ProxySSL
bugs.conditions: ProxySSL enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM processes SSL/TLS data via ProxySSL as expected

bugs.title: tmm crash when showing connections for a CMP disabled virtual server
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes when performing 'tmsh show sys connection' and there is a connection from a secondary blade to a CMP-disabled virtual server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- There is a CMP-disabled virtual server. -- There is a connection to that server from the control plane of a secondary blade (this can include monitoring traffic). -- Connections are displayed that include the connection from the secondary blade ('tmsh show sys connection').
bugs.impact: tmm crashes and restarts impacting traffic.
bugs.workaround: Do not use 'cmp-enabled no' virtual servers when there will be connections from the BIG-IP control plane to the virtual server. Avoid using tmsh show sys connection

bugs.title: Custom URL Filter object is missing after load sys config TMSH command
bugs.symptoms: The user will not be able to see the custom URL Filter object that is created either through TMSH/GUI. If the filter object is referred in Access Policy, the policy will fail to load during "load sys config" command. 01070712:3: Values (/Common/custurlfilter) specified for URL Filter Lookup Agent (/Common/prp_act_url_filter_lookup_ag): foreign key index (name_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: The custom URL Filter object is missing after the user does "load sys config" command in TMSH. Please note that SWG is not provisioned in this case.
bugs.impact: (1) The access policy will fail to load if it refers the URL Filter object. The user will not be able to use the URL Filter object in the policy.
bugs.workaround: (1) Provision SWG, and recreate the URL Filter or (2) Change bigip.conf to include the URL Filter object
bugs.fix: Fix is to make sure, during load sys config, custom URL filter gets saved properly and always visible, and usable in the policy.

bugs.title: Memory leak in case of a PEM Diameter session going down due to remote end point connectivity issues.
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak resulting in a potential OOM scenario.
bugs.conditions: 1. PEM configured with Gx 2. Flaky Diameter connection 3. Subscriber creation via PEM
bugs.impact: Potential loss of service.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Freed Diameter messages appropriately.

bugs.title: Access HUD filter has URL length limit (4096 bytes)
bugs.symptoms: Access HUD filter cannot process a URL if it is longer than 4096 bytes.
bugs.conditions: Any URL with a request consisting of more than 4096 bytes.
bugs.impact: The URL cannot be processed, and client gets a RST.
bugs.fix: In this release, the URL length limit increased to 8192 bytes.

bugs.title: High CPU load on generic message if multiple responses arrive while asynchronous Tcl command is running
bugs.symptoms: High CPU load on generic message if multiple responses arrive while asynchronous Tcl command is running.
bugs.conditions: Multiple response messages arrive on a connection while an asynchronous Tcl command is running on that connection.
bugs.impact: High CPU load might occur as multiple responses will be assigned the same request_sequence_number.
bugs.fix: Request_sequence_numbers are not assigned to response messages until the Tcl event is executed for that message. This avoids assigning the same number to multiple events.

bugs.title: Fix a race condition in ixlv driver which was causing a tmm panic
bugs.symptoms: TMM panic with "extract succeeded" error message
bugs.conditions: Ixlv driver is in use and number of TMMs are more than 4
bugs.impact: TMM restart
bugs.workaround: Reduce TMM count to 4 or less

bugs.title: BD core on a specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: bd process crashes, and core file created in the /shared/core/ directory.
bugs.conditions: Specific request and response characteristics that relates to CSP headers sent by the server.
bugs.impact: Failover in high availability units.
bugs.workaround: Disable CSP headers handling in ASM by running the following commands: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add csp_enabled 0 bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: The system now reinitializes the CSP headers before each response headers event, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Extra IPsec reference added per crypto operation overflows connflow refcount
bugs.symptoms: The size of the refcount field in connflow became smaller, making the length of some crypto queues in IPsec able to reach and exceed the maximum refcount value.
bugs.conditions: When a large data transfer under an IPsec SA creates a queue of crypto operations longer than the connflow's refcount can handle, the refcount can overflow.
bugs.impact: Unexpected tmm failover after refcount overflow.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: An object tracking crypto operations now adds a sole reference to the connflow as long as the count of crypto operation pending is nonzero.

bugs.title: AVR-related disk partitions can get full during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Disk is full during upgrade preparation when Application Visibility and Reporting (AVR) data exported from the MySQL DB to the disk.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from 13.1.x to a newer version. -- AVR is provisioned.
bugs.impact: If /shared/avr and /shared/avr_afm are full, the upgrade could fail.
bugs.workaround: Delete all data from AVR DB before upgrade: touch /var/avr/init_avrdb bigstart restart monpd As the upgrade can cause the disk to fill, here is an alternative workaround: 1. Save UCS file for backup purposes. 2. Manually move the contents from /shared/avr to /shared/tmp/avr: -------- # mkdir /shared/tmp/avr # mv /shared/avr/* /shared/tmp/avr -------- 3. Delete /shared/tmp/avr and files under this directory and check whether disk usage for /shared/avr has come down.
bugs.fix: AVR data compression has been introduced, single partition (/shared/avr) is used instead of two partitions (/shared/avr_afm, /shared/avr). As a result, a need for disk space is considerably reduced.

bugs.title: Anomaly threshold floor calculation (for bins with very low learnt threshold) during signature generation
bugs.symptoms: AFM might generate a dynamic signature for those bins that have a very low learnt threshold during the learning phase, if the current traffic rate spikes and increases above the anomaly threshold floor db variable value as specified by l4bdos.anomaly.threshold.floor
bugs.conditions: AFM dynamic signature feature is enabled.
bugs.impact: This might cause AFM to generate signatures with higher false positives. This is specifically due to incorrect application of db variable setting 'l4bdos.anomaly.threshold.floor' that should be interpreted as the 'floor' value of learnt thresholds for any bin. So, if the learnt threshold of a bin is lower than this db variable, the baseline threshold of the bin should be set to the db variable for anomaly detection phase.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed by making sure that db variable 'l4bdos.anomaly.threshold.floor' is used as the 'floor' value of baseline thresholds for those bins that have a learnt threshold lower than this db variable.

bugs.title: monpd does not return data for multi-dimension query
bugs.symptoms: When querying 'time-series' data for multiple-dimensions, most multi-dimension queries receive an empty response.
bugs.conditions: This occurs because the order of entities in the query is not sorted by priority.
bugs.impact: The corresponding dashboard displays incorrect statistics.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The monpd process now performs two queries in order to get the 'time-series' data for multi-dimensions: -- The first query gets the top entities. -- The second query gets data that is 'drilled down' by the top entities, the ones received from the first query.

bugs.title: GUI Network Map as Start Screen presents database error
bugs.symptoms: If the Network Map is set as the Preferences Start Screen, the GUI will display a database error page.
bugs.conditions: Set System :: Preferences : Start Screen to Network Map.
bugs.impact: Error page is displayed.
bugs.workaround: Navigate to the Network Map via the left navigation menu: Local Traffic :: Network Map.
bugs.fix: The Screen Start now launches successfully into the Network Map page.

bugs.title: BD crash
bugs.symptoms: BD crash.
bugs.conditions: ecard_max_http_req_uri_len is set to a value greater than 8 KB.
bugs.impact: Potential traffic disturbance and failover.
bugs.workaround: Change the value of ecard_max_http_req_uri_len to a size lower than 8 KB.
bugs.fix: Fixed a BD crash scenario.

bugs.title: TMM core may be seen when using Application reporting with flow filter in PEM
bugs.symptoms: TMM core with flow filter when Application reporting action is enabled
bugs.conditions: If Application reporting is enabled along with flow filter
bugs.impact: TMM restart causing service interruption
bugs.fix: Initialize the application start buffer so as to prevent the TMM core

bugs.title: Threat campaign filter does not return campaign if filter contains quotation marks
bugs.symptoms: A threat campaign is not displayed in the GUI on the Security :: Application Security : Threat Campaigns page.
bugs.conditions: Filtering for a campaign name that contains a quotation mark.
bugs.impact: Threat campaign filter by name does not work.
bugs.fix: REST escaping now supports this configuration..
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using quotation marks.

bugs.title: Import of objects from non-Common partitions linked to objects in Common partition may fail
bugs.symptoms: Export of objects from non Common partitions linked to objects in Common partition may fail with error like Import Error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: /Common/xyz is not found. Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Original object is in local partition have reference to object in Common partition
bugs.impact: Certain configurations become unexportable
bugs.workaround: Please use objects in the same partition while importing/exporting
bugs.fix: Now export and import working correctly

bugs.title: "GTP::ie insert" and "GTP::ie append" do not work without "-message" option
bugs.symptoms: When adding "GTP::ie insert" and "GTP::ie append" without "-message" option to iRule, there is warning message: [The following errors were not caught before. Please correct the script in order to avoid future disruption. "unexpected end of arguments;expected argument spec:VALUE"1290 38]
bugs.conditions: Using "GTP::ie insert" or "GTP::ie append" command without "-message" option
bugs.impact: The commands still be executed during runtime but the warning message may confuse user.
bugs.fix: There is no warning message when using "GTP::ie insert" and "GTP::ie append" without "-message" option.

bugs.title: Unable to create SNMP trap in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Trying to create a SNMP trap may fail in the GUI with the following error message: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: -- Trap destinations are configured using the GUI: When trap destinations are configured in the GUI, the trap name is generated using the destination IP address. -- Traps of the same destination address were previously created and deleted.
bugs.impact: GUI parameter checking does not work as expected. BIG-IP Administrator is unable to create a SNMP trap session.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue when using the GUI, remove all traps that have the same destination address as the new one that failed. Then re-add your destination. Tip: You can use tmsh to create/delete/modify SNMP traps, which enables viewing of the generated names, making it easier to understand what error has occurred.

bugs.title: Max in-progress sessions per client IP does not work correctly with Redirect ending
bugs.symptoms: Once the 'Max In Progress Sessions Per Client IP' limit is reached, new sessions cannot be established even after manually deleting few sessions.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is licensed and provisioned. -- Per-session policy is created with Redirect ending agent. -- 'Close session after redirect' setting is not checked in Redirect Ending agent.
bugs.impact: New sessions from client cannot be created after 'Max In Progress Sessions Per Client IP' limit is reached. End users may not be redirected to another internal or external URL.
bugs.workaround: If it's not required to keep the access session after redirecting to internal or external URL, check the 'Close session after redirect' setting in Redirect Ending agent of per-session policy.
bugs.fix: New sessions are created from same client after manually deleting the existing access sessions once 'Max In Progress Sessions Per Client IP' limit is reached.

bugs.title: PEM Diameter incomplete flow crashes when sweeped
bugs.symptoms: If a PEM Diameter flow is not fully created, for example suspended by an iRule, the sweeper may encounter a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM Diameter flow not fully created. -- The flow is suspended by an iRule. -- There is a CMP state change (likely) or a manual cluster-mirror change (less likely) while the flow is suspended.
bugs.impact: The tmm restarts and all flows reset. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The PEM diameter flow is now created in such a way to prevent any crash by the sweeper.

bugs.title: Running 'tmsh run /cm watch-devicegroup-device' does not work for IPv6 connections
bugs.symptoms: Running 'tmsh run /cm watch-devicegroup-device' where the BIG-IP systems config sync addresses are of type IPv6 does not work.
bugs.conditions: -- Running the command: tmsh run /cm watch-devicegroup-device. -- BIG-IP systems config sync addresses are of type IPv6.
bugs.impact: Functionality is not available.

bugs.title: Active compression requests can become starved from too many queued requests.
bugs.symptoms: From the "tmctl compress" table: the cur_ctx value for QAT is equal or higher than 512, and the cur_active remains at zero. CPU utilization per tmm in this condition may be quite high.
bugs.conditions: At least 512 contexts with no traffic wait in the compression queue and prevent new requests from getting compression service.
bugs.impact: Compression on a per-tmm basis can stop servicing new requests.
bugs.workaround: Switch to software compression.
bugs.fix: Soften the restriction so that accumulated contexts with no traffic cannot not prevent busy contexts from getting compression time.

bugs.title: B2250 blades experience degraded performance.
bugs.symptoms: B2250 blades have degraded performance by up to 17%. This is caused by connections not being offloaded to hardware as often as expected.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the FastL4 profile is configured to offload to hardware and the service provider DAG is configured and in use on B2250 blades.
bugs.impact: Performance will be degraded due to more connections being handled in software.
bugs.fix: The performance issue for the B2250 blades has been fixed.

bugs.title: APM end users can not change/reset password when auth agents are included in per-req policy
bugs.symptoms: Users cannot change password when AD, Radius or LocalDb auth agents are included in per-req policy.
bugs.conditions: - Per-req policy is attached to Virtual Server. - AD Auth, Radius Auth or LocalDB auth agents are included in per-req policy. - End user is challenged to change/reset the password.
bugs.impact: Users can not change password.
bugs.fix: Users now can successfully change or reset the password.

bugs.title: monpd core is sometimes created when the system is under heavy load.
bugs.symptoms: When system is under heavy load, aggregation of statistics tables in the database sometimes takes too much time and watchdog is triggered. When that happens, watchdog aborts the application and produces a core file.
bugs.conditions: -- System under heavy load. -- Setting and resetting DoS profile on virtual servers. -- Using AVR. -- Displaying aggregated statistics.
bugs.impact: System produces monpd core file, when no real crash occurs.
bugs.fix: Watchdog trigger no longer creates core by default under these conditions.

bugs.title: Users cannot change or reset RSA PIN
bugs.symptoms: User is not able to reset the PIN when RSA SecurID or RADIUS Auth agent is included in access policy.
bugs.conditions: - APM is licensed and provisioned. - RSA SecurID or RADIUS Auth agent is included in an access policy. - APM end user is challenged to reset the PIN or reenter the PIN/token.
bugs.impact: APM end users cannot reset the PIN or do not get authenticated.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: APM users can now successfully reset the PIN or reenter the token.

bugs.title: Monitor probes may fail to be sent to FQDN nodes when DNS responds with an increased number of nodes
bugs.symptoms: FQDN pool member monitor status is not updated and monitor probes are not sent to the FQDN pool member in the case where: FQDN-configured pools are populated with an initial set of nodes returned from a DNS query, and a subsequent DNS response includes a greater number of nodes that include the originally returned node-set. For example, if an initial DNS response populates an FQDN-configured pool with one node, and a subsequent DNS response returns two nodes (including the first node), then monitor probes may fail to be sent to the second FQDN-configured pool member.
bugs.conditions: -- The configuration has an FQDN-configured pool. -- The DNS server successfully returns one-or-more nodes. -- The DNS server later returns a greater number of nodes, including those nodes previously returned.
bugs.impact: Monitor probes may fail to be sent to the second FQDN-configured pool member. Incorrect FQDN pool member status.

bugs.title: The standard LinkUp/LinkDown traps may not be issued in all cases when an interface is administratively enabled/disabled
bugs.symptoms: The standard LinkUp/LinkDown traps are issued when a port's status changes; that is, the link goes up or down. Additionally, the network manager can administratively enable and disable ports. For some platforms, there is no reliably issued standard LinkUp/LinkDown trap when a port is administratively enabled/disabled.
bugs.conditions: Administrative disabling an interface on BIG-IP
bugs.impact: May issue only the F5 Link change trap and not the additional standard MIB trap. The standard LinkUp/LinkDown traps may not be issued.
bugs.workaround: Use the F5-proprietary MIB: 1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.4.0.37 F5-BIG-IP-COMMON-MIB::BIG-IPExternalLinkChange trap to track administrative changes to links.

bugs.title: tmm may crash in a compression provider
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash with the following panic message in the log files: panic: ../codec/compress/compress.c:1161: Assertion "context active" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on the following platforms: BIG-IP i-series or VIPRION 4400 blades. -- Virtual servers are performing compression.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes, Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use compression, or use software compression instead of hardware compression. To configure for software compression, run the following command: tmsh modify sys db compression.strategy value softwareonly

bugs.title: TCP ToS Passthrough mode does not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: For Standard virtual server with a TCP profile, when using ToS passthough, the ToS value is not passed from the server to the client-side. ip-tos-to-client pass-through link-qos-to-client pass-through
bugs.conditions: - Standard virtual server. - TCP profile configured with ToS passthrough.
bugs.impact: ToS is not passed to the client.
bugs.fix: ToS is now passed correctly from the server to the client-side.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 may truncate a response body when served from cache
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems provide a client-side HTTP/2 Gateway protocol implementation in conjunction with HTTP 1.x on a server side. A response can be cached on the BIG-IP system with a web acceleration profile. Sometimes a response served from cache is prematurely marked with END_STREAM flag, causing the client to ignore the rest of the response body.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system has a virtual server for which HTTP/2 and Web Acceleration profiles are configured.
bugs.impact: Some clients' browsers do not retry a resource, causing incorrect rendering of an HTML page.
bugs.workaround: Adding the following iRule causes the body to be displayed: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { set con_len [string trim [HTTP::header value Content-Length]] HTTP::header remove Content-Length HTTP::header insert Content-Length "$con_len" }
bugs.fix: With provided fix, HTTP/2 end users no longer experience the problem of incorrect page rendering due to this issue.

bugs.title: PEM Diameter incomplete flow crashes when TCL resumed
bugs.symptoms: If a PEM Diameter flow is not fully created, for example suspended by an iRule, and the irule is resumed because of timeout.
bugs.conditions: PEM Diameter flow not fully created, suspended by iRule, and the iRule is resumed by timeout.
bugs.impact: The tmm will restart and all flows will reset.
bugs.fix: The PEM diameter flow is now created in such a way to prevent any crash by iRule resumed by timeout.

bugs.title: Disabling a single pool member removes all GTM persistence records
bugs.symptoms: Disabling a single pool member removes all GTM persistence records.
bugs.conditions: 1. WideIP with persistence enabled. 2. drain-persistent-requests no. 3. GTM pool member toggled from enabled to disabled.
bugs.impact: All GTM persistence records are accidently cleared.
bugs.workaround: Set drain-persistent-requests yes.
bugs.fix: When drain-persistent-requests is set to no, only the persistence records associated with the affected pool members are cleared when a resource is disabled.

bugs.title: Secondary Authentication or SSO fail after changing AD or LDAP password
bugs.symptoms: APM end users cannot login, or single sign-on (SSO) can fail after changing AD or LDAP password
bugs.conditions: -- APM is licensed and provisioned. -- Active Directory or LDAP Auth agent is used in the policy for authenticating the users. -- When logging on to APM, user is asked to change the password.
bugs.impact: Authentication and SSO actions that rely on session.logon.last.password fail.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: APM SSO works fine after changing AD or LDAP password.

bugs.title: Updating iRule causes TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: A tmm core occurs when reloading an iRulesLX (iLX) Plugin. You might see error messages: notice ** SIGFPE ** pgo_use x86_64 vadc TMM Version 13.1.3.2.0.0.4 panic: Tcl Object 5600092578f8 is currently on free list
bugs.conditions: iRulesLXPlugin was reloaded into Workspace.
bugs.impact: Crash in TMM caused by updating an iLX instance. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Different versioned vCMP guests on the same chassis may crash.
bugs.symptoms: The vCMP guest TMM crashes soon after startup.
bugs.conditions: -- You are using BIG-IP software versions 12.1.0-12.1.2. -- vCMP guests are deployed in a chassis. -- You configure a new guest running unaffected software alongside an existing or new guest running affected software. In other words, the issue occurs if you mix guests running affected and non-affected versions in a single vCMP host.
bugs.impact: vCMP guests running older versions of the software might crash. Blades continuously crash and restart. Traffic cannot pass. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Different versioned vCMP guests on the same chassis no longer crash.

bugs.title: MCP cores when importing a configuration with 12000 nested address lists and auto-sync enabled.
bugs.symptoms: MCP cores when importing a configuration with 12000 nested address lists and auto-sync enabled. /var/log/ltm contains messages similar to the following: -- err clusterd[7274]: 013a0004:3: IO error on recv from mcpd - connection lost -- info sod[7953]: 010c0009:6: Lost connection to mcpd - reestablishing. -- notice chmand[7594]: 012a0005:5: resetting chmand services -- err snmpd[7952]: 010e0001:3: Cannot communicate with MCPD server. -- err mysqlhad[7596]: 014e0006:3: MCP Failure: 1. -- err zxfrd[7962]: 0153e0f7:3: Lost connection to mcpd. -- err tmrouted[6299]: 01910013:3: FATAL error: 6 irrecoverable MCP I/O error (Unknown error 16908291). -- err alertd[7280]: 01100042:3: Failed with MCPD at: MCP msg receive (16908291). -- err alertd[7280]: 01100042:3: Failed with MCPD at: Socket read (16908291).
bugs.conditions: -- AFM configuration. -- Devices in a device group trust configuration. -- Device group configured with Autosync enabled. -- Importing a configuration with a very large number of nested address lists (for example, 12000 nested address lists).
bugs.impact: mcpd cores.
bugs.workaround: Split the configuration into smaller chunks (e.g., 1000 address lists each) and load them one at a time.

bugs.title: Request logging is briefly suspended after policy creation
bugs.symptoms: Local request log is not showing some requests.
bugs.conditions: This can occur in either of these conditions -- Making changes to a policy and/or assigning it to a virtual server can cause the issue. -- A failover event moves the virtual server and policy to the other slot.
bugs.impact: Request logging is briefly suspended. Some log messages are not logged.
bugs.fix: All expected requests are present from the local log after policy creation.

bugs.title: BD crash
bugs.symptoms: BD crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- The internal parameter relax_unicode_in_json is set to 1. -- Specific traffic scenario.
bugs.impact: BD crash, failover, and traffic disturbance.
bugs.workaround: Turn off the internal parameter relax_unicode_in_json.
bugs.fix: BD no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: Warning message: get_db failed for is_provisioned wam - returning not-provisioned.
bugs.symptoms: There is a warning messages logged in ltm log: warning bigstart: get_db failed for is_provisioned wam - returning not-provisioned.
bugs.conditions: This occurs any time the BIG-IP system is started or services are restarted.
bugs.impact: This has no impact and is cosmetic. You can safely ignore these messages.

bugs.title: Some TMOS tools for querying various DBs fail when only a single TMM is running
bugs.symptoms: Command returns "No route to host" error.
bugs.conditions: Running diadb, sipdb, genericmsgdb or lsndb when only a single TMM is running.
bugs.impact: Unable to query SIP, Diameter, Generic-Message and LSN information from its corresponded DB query tool.
bugs.fix: Tools for querying various DBs now work regardless of the number of TMMs.

bugs.title: FPS should forward all XFF header values
bugs.symptoms: For BIG-IP alerts, FPS will insert a single XFF with the client IP and discard all XFF values/headers in the original request (the request which triggered the alert)
bugs.conditions: Alert generated on BIG-IP side.
bugs.impact: Original XFF information will be lost: only a single XFF header (containing client IP) will be present.
bugs.fix: FPS now copies all original XFF headers to the generated alert.

bugs.title: iRule URI::encode command does not follow RFC3986 for hexadecimal digits used in percent-encoded octets
bugs.symptoms: The iRule URI::encode command does not follow RFC3986 for hexadecimal digits used in percent-encoded octets. The URI::encode command always generates a lowercase hexadecimal number, so when uppercase is expected, the output of URI::encode does not work..
bugs.conditions: Using the iRule URI::encode command.
bugs.impact: When upper case is expected, the output of URI::encode does not work.
bugs.workaround: Use the Tcl toupper command to convert the output to uppercase.
bugs.fix: The iRule URI::encode command now generates RFC-compliant value.

bugs.title: Monpd core when trying to restart
bugs.symptoms: Monpd tries to restart and tries to access a non-initiated variable
bugs.conditions: Monpd tries to restart due to change of primary blade
bugs.impact: Monpd cores
bugs.fix: Adding sanity check to the non-initiated variable before trying to access it

bugs.title: iControl-REST crashes on /example for firewall address-lists
bugs.symptoms: Making a call to /example on firewall address-list crashes iControl-REST.
bugs.conditions: Making a call to /example on firewall address-list.
bugs.impact: The icrd_child process crashes.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not calling /example on firewall address-lists.

bugs.title: Websso crashes because of bad argument in logging
bugs.symptoms: Websso would crash because of bad argument in logging
bugs.conditions: Only when kerberos sso is configured
bugs.impact: Websso would crash and so single sign on may fail.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is not configure kerberos SSO
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Portal Access: Internet Explorer may encounter JavaScript error in multi-window Web application
bugs.symptoms: If Web application uses references to objects in different window, these references may become invalid after closing/reloading their window. In Internet Explorer, Portal Access may not work correctly if Web application uses references to forms or links in another window. This error appears if Web application uses emulation modes in Internet Explorer.
bugs.conditions: - Internet Explorer in any emulation mode - Multi-window Web application which uses inter-window object references
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly
bugs.fix: Now multi-window Web applications work correctly in Internet Explorer via Portal Access.

bugs.title: Upgrading using a ucs or scf file does not autogenerate uuids when current config has the uuid-default-autogenerate flag enabled
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading using a UCS or SCF file does not autogenerate uuids when the current config has the uuid-default-autogenerate flag enabled. This might cause issues when upgrading from older versions where uuids need to be quickly generated for existing firewall policies, rule lists, and management rules.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from an older version with an existing security policy which has no uuids configured.
bugs.impact: Requires manually configuration of uuids for rules that come in from the older config.
bugs.workaround: Generate uuids for all policies, rule-lists, and management rules using the following three tmsh commands: -- tmsh modify sec fire policy all rules modify { all { uuid auto-generate}} -- tmsh modify sec fire rule-list all rules modify { all { uuid auto-generate}} -- tmsh modify sec fire management-ip-rules rules modify { all { uuid auto-generate}} Optionally, to ensure rules created in the future have uuids autogenerated issue the following tmsh command: -- tmsh modify sec firewall uuid-default-autogenerate mode enabled
bugs.fix: No fix provided, Current behavior causes the uuid-default-autogenerate flag to be overwritten to disabled by the ucs load process. Workaround has been provided to mitigate against this behavior.

bugs.title: APM iRule ACCESS::session remove fails outside of Access events
bugs.symptoms: ACCESS::session remove fails
bugs.conditions: iRule calling ACCESS::session remove outside of Access events.
bugs.impact: APM iRule ACCESS::session remove fails to remove session
bugs.workaround: Use "ACCESS::session modify" and set the timeout/lifetime to something small, like 1 second. This should cause the session to be deleted due to timeout almost immediately, but note that it will show up in logs as timeout.

bugs.title: tmrouted connection closed messages logged on shutdown
bugs.symptoms: /var/log/ltm contains tmrouted connection closed messages. These are a normal part of system shutdown.
bugs.conditions: System is shut down.

bugs.title: Neurond may restart indefinitely after boot, with neurond_i2c_config message
bugs.symptoms: The neurond daemon may continually restart after a reboot. The problem may persist even after a reboot of the BIG-IP system. Manually stopping and starting neurond will not resolve the problem.
bugs.conditions: - This occurs only on BIG-IP platforms that contain a specific hardware part running v13.1.0. - The issue happens only after a reboot of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system constantly logs messages similar to the following: emerg logger: Re-starting neurond The /var/log/neurond logfile contains messages similar to the following: -- neurond_i2c_config_steps: STEP 20 Checking for Lane Alignment -- neurond_i2c_config_steps: Timeout waiting for good rx_align for ILK1 of NSP -- neurond_i2c_config: neurond_i2c_config_steps failed.
bugs.workaround: If you are not using FIX features, disabling the neurond service is a safe option. If your configuration relies on the FIX feature, a cold reboot by removing the BIG-IP system from the power may resolve the problem. However, multiple retries are sometimes necessary to get the part to initialize.
bugs.fix: This release increases the number of initialization retries to handle this condition, so continual restart no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Report Device error: crypto codec qat-crypto0-0 queue is stuck on vCMP guests
bugs.symptoms: Failure in SSL traffic in vCMP configurations. The system logs the following device error: -- crit tmm[17083]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec qat-crypto0-0 queue is stuck. -- warning sod[7759]: 01140029:4: high availability (HA) crypto_failsafe_t qat-crypto0-0 fails action is failover.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP guests when performing crypto operations. -- i5600, i5800, i7600, i7800, i10600, i10800, i12600, i12800, i15600, i15800 platforms.
bugs.impact: The 'crypto queue stuck' message is reported, and failover will be triggered.
bugs.fix: The 'crypto queue stuck' issue on vCMP platforms no longer occurs.

bugs.title: iRules LX: Cannot modify workspace imported by "Import From Workspace"
bugs.symptoms: The permissions of an iRules LX workspace copy created from the "Import..." "From Workspace" are set to 775 (drwxr-xr-x) for directories and 444 (-r--r--r--) for files including the node and tcl code files. This causes the "Could not save file: <file>" error upon modification of the code.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to modify imported workspace.
bugs.impact: Cannot save changes.
bugs.workaround: A. Create an "archive file" first and use it for importing. B. After creating a copy using "From Workspace", run chmod command to add +w to the group and others: e.g., chmod -R g+w,o+w <Workspacename>.

bugs.title: ACCESS is not replacing headers while replacing POST body
bugs.symptoms: If the first request for a session is a POST, APM will save the POST to replay after the policy completes. When the POST is restored after policy completion and released to the backend, the headers are the same as the most recent client request, not the original POST. In particular, the Content-Length header will not match the original POST.
bugs.conditions: First request for the session is a POST.
bugs.impact: Backend servers may complain of an incomplete HTTP POST due to a mismatching Content-Length header.
bugs.fix: Now, the system takes all headers from the original POST, except the Authorization header that Kerberos RBA needs, which is taken from the most recent client request.

bugs.title: Increase PEM HSL reporting buffer size to 4K.
bugs.symptoms: Before this fix, PEM HSL reporting buffer size is limited by 512 bytes.
bugs.conditions: If any PEM HSL flow reporting stream goes beyond 512 bytes, it will be truncated.
bugs.impact: Part of PEM HSL flow reporting information will be lost.
bugs.fix: We increase PEM HSL reporting buffer size to 4K, which should be enough for uses cases we currently know.

bugs.title: Login LDAP Attribute for Active Directory configurations incorrectly capitalizes sAMAccountName
bugs.symptoms: When configured for Active Directory remote authentication, the BIG-IP incorrectly modifies the sAMAccountName parameter with all lower-case letters.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP is configured for remote auth for Active Directory.
bugs.impact: Remote auth for Active Directory authentication failure.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to fix this attribute.
bugs.fix: Now use correct case for the sAMAccountName parameter.

bugs.title: Policy with CSRF URL parameter cannot be imported as binary policy file
bugs.symptoms: A policy with at least 1 CSRF URL parameter defined cannot be imported as a binary policy file.
bugs.conditions: A policy has at least 1 CSRF URL parameter defined.
bugs.impact: The policy cannot be imported as a binary policy file.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A policy with CSRF URL parameters defined can now be imported as a binary policy file.

bugs.title: Cisco IOS XR ISIS routers may report 'Authentication TLV not found'
bugs.symptoms: When peering with ISIS to Cisco IOS XR routers, messages similar to the following may be seen isis[1003]: %ROUTING-ISIS-5-AUTH_FAILURE_DROP : Dropped L2 LSP from TenGigE0/0/0/1 SNPA 0001.47fd.a801 due to authentication TLV not found.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system is configured for dynamic routing using the ISIS protocol, and is peered with an IOS XR router, or with another BIG-IP system running software older than than version 11.6.1. In addition, authentication needs to be configured, and a value needs to be set for lsp-refresh-interval, or for max-lsp-lifetime. For example: router isis isisrouter is-type level-2-only authentication mode md5 authentication key-chain keychain-isis lsp-refresh-interval 5 max-lsp-lifetime 65535 net 49.8002.00c1.0000.0000.f523.00
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. Routing is not impacted. LSPs containing actual routing information do contain the Auth TLV, as expected.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: ROM layout file missing for Blade B2250 in BIG-IP VIPRION 2400 chassis
bugs.symptoms: An error similar to the following is posted when blade B2250 is PXE-booted and an attempt is made to extract OPTN class data from the SPI flashrom: ERROR: Could not open ROM layout (/usr/firmware/victoria2-rom.layout). Please run "flashrom --help" for usage info.
bugs.conditions: When the ROM layout file is missing under the /usr/firmware/ directory in Maintenance OS (MOS).
bugs.impact: Failure to extract OPTN class data from the SPI flashrom results in failure to determine whether the system should be RAID formatted.

bugs.title: Profile from Common imported to other partition should still point to log-settings in Common
bugs.symptoms: If an access profile exported from the Common partition has log-settings in the Common partition, if the access profile is then imported to another partition, import fails with error that /partition/log-setting-name is not available.
bugs.conditions: If access profile is exported from Common partition and imported to non-common partition.
bugs.impact: There are no default log facilities (e.g., default-log-settings) in the partition. You must create them manually.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use the following procedure: 1. Create log objects with the proper name in the target partition. 2. Import the access profile.
bugs.fix: Now all policies exported from Common are expecting log objects to be presented in Common regardless of target partition.

bugs.title: High crypto request completion time under some workload patterns
bugs.symptoms: The tmctl tmm/crypto table shows heavily loaded bulk crypto queues backed up into associated waiting queue. The crypto requests continue to complete, but are significantly delayed.
bugs.conditions: High crypto usage often in conjunction with high compression usage.
bugs.impact: Crypto requests can be delayed as long as 1.5 seconds.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware crypto by setting the "crypto.hwacceleration" DB key to "disable": tmsh modify sys db crypto.hwacceleration value disable
bugs.fix: Improve accelerated crypto poll-timing calculation.

bugs.title: GUI does not show Device names with <> properly.
bugs.symptoms: When the Device Name has <> (left and right angle brackets) in the name, the GUI does not show the name properly.
bugs.conditions: Device Name contains <> characters.
bugs.impact: User is unable to see the device name in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to see the device name.
bugs.fix: Enable the GUI to show device name with <> characters.

bugs.title: admd might core under stress conditions
bugs.symptoms: admd might core when the system is under stress.
bugs.conditions: 1. Behavioral DoS and signatures are configured. 2. Heavy stress condition. 3. DHD licensed / AWAF licensed.
bugs.impact: admd daemon restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure signatures detection.

bugs.title: During config sync, if many client-ssl profiles are on a virtual server the CPU may briefly spike to 100%
bugs.symptoms: During config sync, if many (hundreds) of client-ssl profiles are attached to a virtual server, the CPU may spike to 100%.
bugs.conditions: -- Many (hundreds) of client-ssl profiles are attached to a virtual server. -- Config sync is executed.
bugs.impact: If enough client-ssl profiles are attached, the watchdog could fire, crashing tmm and causing service disruption. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not attaching hundreds of client-ssl profiles to a virtual server, or disabling config sync.
bugs.fix: Issue no longer occurs when there are 2000+ client-ssl profiles attached to a virtual server and config sync is executed.

bugs.title: Source client information not available in DOS DNS Protocol event logs
bugs.symptoms: In Security > Event Logs > DoS > DNS Protocol GUI, client/source information is not available to view
bugs.conditions: Source ip address and port can be used to filter logs and set conditions based on these logs.
bugs.impact: You are not able to view source/client ip-address and port in GUI but it can be viewed from CLI
bugs.fix: Source information is now available in GUI.

bugs.title: Connections may stop passing traffic after a route update
bugs.symptoms: When a pool is used with a non-translating virtual server, routing updates may lead to an incorrect lookup of the nexthop for the connection.
bugs.conditions: -- Pool on a non-translating virtual server. -- Routing update occurs.
bugs.impact: Connections may fail after routing updates. New connections will not be affected.
bugs.workaround: Use a route to direct traffic to the ultimate destination rather than using a pool to indicate the nexthop.
bugs.fix: Routing updates no longer interrupts traffic to connections using a pool member to reach the nexthop.

bugs.title: TACACS+ system auth and file descriptors leak
bugs.symptoms: Administrative access to the system with remote authenticated accounts fails, and the following is seen in the security log (/var/log/secure): -- httpd[###]: PAM [error: /lib/security/pam_bigip_authz.so: cannot open shared object file: Too many open files]. -- httpd[###]: PAM audit_open() failed: Too many open files -- Other errors that refer to 'Too many open files'. This might eventually lead to lack of HTTP-based access to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote system authentication configured to use TACACS+. -- Administrative access to the BIG-IP system using any HTTP-based results in leaked file descriptors. Relevant access methods include Web UI, iControl and iControl-REST. -- Repeated automated access using iControl is the fastest route.
bugs.impact: In some circumstances, the leak might accumulate to the point that no file descriptors are available and administrative access using remote authenticated accounts is no longer possible. This also includes access from SSH and console. The root account, which always uses local authentication, is not affected.
bugs.workaround: Workaround options: 1. Use only SSH for administrative access. 2. Restart httpd as needed.

bugs.title: SSID Persistence does not work with TLS v1.3. Warning message logged.
bugs.symptoms: In TLS v1.3, after initial handshake is established, the encrypted session ticket is encrypted by the back-end server. The SSL Session ID (SSID) parser, being only a passive listener, has no access to the decryption key required to decrypt the encrypted session ticket, and examine whether this is indeed a session ticket that needs to be cached for persistence.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a client-side virtual server meets all of the following conditions: -- No SSL profile is enabled. -- SSID Persistence is one of the resources (i.e., the SSID is enabled). -- TLS v1.3 traffic is negotiated between the SSL client and the back-end SSL server, with the BIG-IP device acting as a passive listener between the client and the back-end server.
bugs.impact: Configurations using SSID Persistence with TLS versions up to and including 1.2, will be impacted. Whenever TLS 1.3 traffic is processed and the SSID filter is enabled: -- The filter switches to pass-through. -- No session ID or session ticket is cached for persistence. As a result: + The CLI command 'tmsh show ltm persistence persist persist-records' does not show any of this information. + No SSID persistence is used to load-balance client traffic on to a back-end server (because there is no persistence record).
bugs.workaround: There is no solution possible with TLS v1.3. SSID does not work because of the very nature of the TLS v1.3 protocol. A TMM warning message is logged in the file "/var/log/ltm", in the following format: warning tmm[12729]: 01260044:4 SSID is not supported with TLS 1.3.
bugs.fix: A TMM warning message is logged in the file '/var/log/ltm', in the following format: warning tmm[12729]: 01260044:4 SSID is not supported with TLS 1.3.

bugs.title: PKCS12 file imported via Configuration utility into folder is placed at partition root
bugs.symptoms: When importing a certificate (cert) using the GUI Configuration utility, you can specify a partition folder, and the system imports the cert into that partition folder. However, specifying a partition folder when importing a PKCS12 cert imports it to the root partition folder, Common.
bugs.conditions: Login to GUI: - Navigate to: System :: Certificate Management : Traffic Certificate Management : SSL Certificate List. - Click Import: Select 'PKCS'. - Give the cert a name: sync_group/pk12gui
bugs.impact: PKCS12 files imported using the GUI Configuration utility are placed at root partition folder, Common, rather than the partition folder.
bugs.workaround: You can use either workaround: -- Once the PKCS12 file has been imported, export the cert and key, and then re-import into the partition folder. -- Import PKCS12 file using TMSH.

bugs.title: TACACS+ system auth file descriptor leaks when servers are unreachable
bugs.symptoms: Administrative access to the system with remote authenticated accounts fails, and the following is seen in the security log (/var/log/secure): -- httpd[###]: PAM [error: /lib/security/pam_bigip_authz.so: cannot open shared object file: Too many open files]. -- httpd[###]: PAM audit_open() failed: Too many open files -- Other errors that refer to 'Too many open files'. This might eventually lead to lack of HTTP-based access to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote system authentication configured to use TACACS+. -- Connections to one or more of the configured TACACS+ servers fails. -- Administrative access to the BIG-IP system using any HTTP-based results in leaked file descriptors. Relevant access methods include Web UI, iControl and iControl-REST. -- Repeated automated access using iControl is the fastest route.
bugs.impact: Depending on the number of connection failures, the open files limit of the web server process might be exceeded and new connections to the web server will fail. Administrative access using remote authenticated accounts is no longer possible. This also includes access from SSH and console. The root account, which always uses local authentication, is not affected.
bugs.workaround: To prevent the issue, remove unreachable TACACS+ servers from the tacacs configuration, or restart the httpd process as necessary. To recover if logins via remotely authenticated accounts are no longer possible, restart the httpd process.

bugs.title: Under certain extreme conditions, big3d may core
bugs.symptoms: While running at 100% CPU, big3d loses connection with mcpd. Instead of big3d attempting to reconnect, a core is created.
bugs.conditions: It has been determined that the likely cause of this crash is due to missing valid file descriptor/connection check.
bugs.impact: Lost iQuery connection.
bugs.fix: This fix adds a check so that big3d will retry the connection instead of creating a core.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing with PEM
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMM may consume an unusually large amount of system resources while processing compressed data with PEM
bugs.conditions: PEM enabled
bugs.impact: Reduced system capacity, potentially leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: Avoid excessive resource consumption while processing compressed data

bugs.title: IPsec log messages in /var/log/ltm missing module ID to reach bigiq logs
bugs.symptoms: Some groups of messages logged by tmipsecd are missing the errdefs annotation that identifies IPsec as the module. Messages reported when tunnels go up and down, or problems with listeners, go only to ltm logs, with no visibility to bigiq logs.
bugs.conditions: Missing the IPsec module subset ID.
bugs.impact: Missing IPsec messages in the bigiq logs.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The IPsec module subset ID has been added to tmipsecd log messages, so those messages will reach bigiq logs. Some log messages previously appearing only in /var/log/ltm now also appear in ipsec.log and also reach bigiq logs.

bugs.title: Transparent mode VLAN group may not work on vCMP guests
bugs.symptoms: Traffic not being passed through.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP guest with server-side and client-side VLANs mapped on the host to the vCMP guest. -- VLAN group configured in transparent mode and attached to the VLANs configured on the vCMP guest. -- VLAN group configured to bridge all traffic. -- Host configured on client side and on server side host, with corresponding VLANs attached. -- Self IP addresses configured in the same subnet on client, vCMP guest, and server. -- Send traffic from client to server or vice-versa.
bugs.impact: No traffic flow between client and server under this configuration.
bugs.workaround: Configure the network to use translucent mode.

bugs.title: STP interfaces remain in block state on 40G bundled interfaces after enabling STP
bugs.symptoms: STP interfaces are in a blocked state.
bugs.conditions: 40G bundled interface is enabled with STP.
bugs.impact: No STP BPDU gets send out and the STP state is blocked.

bugs.title: Upgrading from 13.1.1 to newer release might cause config to not be copied over
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading from 13.1.1 to newer release might cause config to not be copied over. This is due to the UUID being available on the older release but not on the newer one.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade or loading a UCS from 13.1.1 to newer release.
bugs.impact: Config cannot be loaded or fails.
bugs.workaround: Copy config and remove UUID-specific schema before loading the config.
bugs.fix: When upgrading to a version in which UUID is not supported, the system now automatically copies the config and removes UUID-specific schema before loading it.

bugs.title: DNS express response to non-existent record is NOERROR instead of NXDOMAIN.
bugs.symptoms: The DNS express response to a non-existent record is NOERROR instead of NXDOMAIN.
bugs.conditions: Delete a wildcard resource record to the related DNS express zone.
bugs.impact: DNS returns the incorrect response.
bugs.workaround: Delete the old db files: /var/db/tmmdns.bin and /var/db/zxfrd.bin, and then restart zxfrd.

bugs.title: Added RX latency with ixlv devices on VE after host reboot
bugs.symptoms: Received frames may be delivered in groups of four leading to added latency.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE using a ixlv virtual function (Intel X710/XL710/XXV710 NIC with SR-IOV) on the very first attach after a reboot of the underlying compute host (hypervisor). Packets will appear to arrive in groups of 4 to virtual servers and selfips via tmm.
bugs.impact: This will impact production traffic as extra latency will be introduced to incoming traffic before the tmm can process it.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm or reboot the guest at least once after starting it following a reboot of the physical compute host on which it runs.

bugs.title: Filters under Security :: Reports :: DoS :: URL Latencies work incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: When filtering data by a field in the 'Security :: Reports :: DoS :: URL Latencies' form, the filtering fails and the monpd process crashes.
bugs.conditions: There is some statistical data for DoS.
bugs.impact: Reports based on GUI filters are not complete.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The system now creates the correct query for this filter, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Datasafe: Fingerprinting code runs, but is not needed.
bugs.symptoms: When both datasafe and fingerprint are enabled, fingerprint collection code will be unnecessarily run on the clientside. The results of this collection are not used.
bugs.conditions: Both datasafe and fingerprint are enabled.
bugs.impact: Extra resources requested from the BIG-IP system by the client.
bugs.workaround: To turn off fingerprint, use the following syntax: tmsh modify security anti-fraud profile <PROFILE_NAME> { fingerprint { collect disabled} }
bugs.fix: Datasafe does not execute fingerprint collection unnecessarily.

bugs.title: TMM core upon matching a past (saved) dynamic signature of a specific family (network or dns) after the dynamic signature is disabled for that family on the parent context (but still enabled for other families)
bugs.symptoms: TMM would core upon matching a past (saved) dynamic signature of a specific family (network or dns) after the dynamic signature is disabled for that family on the parent context (but still enabled for other families).
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: -- Enable Network and DNS BDOS simultaneously (on DoS Device config). -- Generate dynamic signature that has both network and DNS metrics. -- Wait for signature to be moved to 'past' (persist) state. -- Disable either network or DNS BDOS (but not both). -- TMM cores if the traffic matches this signature.
bugs.impact: Traffic interruption due to TMM restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: In this release, if the dynamic signature is disabled for a specific family on a parent context (but not disabled for other family on that context), any past attack signature for the context is now deleted from the system.

bugs.title: Potential core in MRF occurs when pending egress messages are queued and an iRule error aborts the connection
bugs.symptoms: The system may core.
bugs.conditions: -- Egress messages are queued waiting for MR_EGRESS event to be raised. -- Current MR event exits with an error, thus aborting the connection.
bugs.impact: The system cores and will restart.
bugs.fix: The system now returns pending messages back to the originator if the connection aborts due to an iRule error.

bugs.title: The ASM-FPS fingerprint is not presented in dashboard
bugs.symptoms: The fingerprint is not presented in dashboard.
bugs.conditions: An iRule selects the FPS profile (by using ANTIFRAUD::enable).
bugs.impact: No fingerprint presented. Missing reporting.

bugs.title: Non-admin users have limited bash commands and can only write to certain directories
bugs.symptoms: TMSH access to Linux utilities does not follow best security practices.
bugs.conditions: Users without Advanced Shell Access running Linux utilities from inside TMSH.
bugs.impact: TMSH does not follow best security practices
bugs.fix: TMSH access to Linux utilities now follows best security practices.
bugs.behavior: Some tmsh util commands will be restricted to writing files to certain directories.

bugs.title: HTTP2 upload intermittently is aborted with HTTP2 error error_code=FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR(
bugs.symptoms: Uploads for the HTTP2 virtual server fail intermittently with HTTP2 error error_code=FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
bugs.conditions: HTTP2 virtual server configured.
bugs.impact: Uploads for the HTTP2 virtual server might fail intermittently.
bugs.fix: Uploads for the HTTP2 virtual server do not fail intermittently anymore.

bugs.title: Config load failed after upgrade from 12.1.2 to 13.x or 14.x
bugs.symptoms: Sys load fails with following errors, .... Loading schema version: 14.0.0 0107153e:3: Application id out of the valid range of [8192-16384). Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: When an CEC IM is applied to 12.1.2 and then when we upgrade to 13.x or 14.x, sys load will fail.
bugs.impact: System will fail to come to Active state after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: It can be fixed by manually deleting /var/libdata/dpi/conf/classification_update.conf

bugs.title: OSPF tag updates may not be propagated through process redistribution
bugs.symptoms: If BIG-IP receives an OSPF LSA with an external tag set and the ensuing route is redistributed into another protocol, including an OSPF process, updates to the tag may not be preserved.
bugs.conditions: -- Redistributing routes from OSPF process to another protocol or process. -- OSPF LSAs with external route tag != 0. -- External route tag changes to 0.
bugs.impact: Routing policy may not be executed correctly leading to misrouted or discarded traffic.
bugs.workaround: Clearing the affected route resolves the issue. This might require clearing the OSPF process. To do so, follow this process: In imish, run the following command: clear ip ospf This interrupts routing that relies on OSPF until the network reconverges.
bugs.fix: OSPF external tag updates are correctly propagated through redistribution.

bugs.title: SSL handshake fails for some servers if their root certificates are not in the configured CA bundle
bugs.symptoms: SSL code builds the chain only until it can find the first trust anchor. However, the OCSP and CRL code builds the chain all the way up to the root. In a case where the intermediate cert was found, but the root was not found in the CA bundle, the cert chain building fails and the handshake will be aborted.
bugs.conditions: Forward Proxy and OCSP are enabled on a serverssl profile
bugs.impact: SSL handshake fails for some servers if their root certificates are not in the configured CA bundle.
