bugs.workaround: Upgrade the ca bundle used to configure 'Trusted Certificate Authorities' on ServerSSL profile to include the root certificate for the server.

bugs.title: Traffic over a QinQ VLAN (double tagged) will not pass
bugs.symptoms: Traffic on a QinQ VLAN will not pass.
bugs.conditions: This issue exists when a VLAN is configured as a QinQ VLAN (i.e., a double-tagged VLAN).
bugs.impact: Traffic on a QinQ VLAN will not pass.
bugs.workaround: Disabling LRO may workaround this issue.
bugs.fix: Traffic on a QinQ VLAN now passes successfully.

bugs.title: Misleading log error message: Store Read invalid store addr 0x3800, len 10
bugs.symptoms: On rare occasions, messages like these can appear in /var/log/ltm: Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Loading keys from the file. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Read the unit key file if exists. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Unit key hash from key header: 9d:e6:90:... Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Unit key hash computed from read key:9d:e6:90:... Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost err mcpd[4139]: 010713d0:3: Symmetric Unit Key decrypt failure - decrypt failure Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071029:5: Symmmetric Unit Key decrypt Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071027:5: Master key OpenSSL error: 1506270960:error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt:evp_enc.c:587: Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Attempting Master Key migration to new unit key. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost warning chmand[5559]: 012a0004:4: Store Read invalid store addr 0x3800, len 10 Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost warning chmand[5559]: 012a0004:4: Store Read invalid store addr 0x3800, len 10 Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost warning mcpd[4139]: 012a0004:4: halStorageRead: unable to read storage on this platform. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071029:5: Cannot open unit key store Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Reloading the RSA unit to support config roll forward. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Loading keys from the file. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Read the unit key file if exists. Oct 20 14:21:04 localhost notice mcpd[4139]: 01071038:5: Unit key hash from key header: 9d:e6:90:... These messages are due to a transient failure reading the system's unit key from the virtual EEPROM on a vCMP guest. The error handling from this failure causes misleading messages, but it does successfully read the unit key during this error recovery.
bugs.conditions: These messages can only happen on a vCMP guest with SecureVault, and are very rare.
bugs.impact: None. These messages do not indicate an actual problem with the system.

bugs.title: Invalid error messages: warning chmand[5730]: 012a0004:4: Store Read invalid store addr 0x3800, len 10
bugs.symptoms: Loading a UCS in a vCMP guest which was taken from a different guest or a hardware device can produce the following error messages: warning mcpd[5953]: 012a0004:4: halStorageRead: unable to read storage on this platform. warning chmand[5730]: 012a0004:4: Store Read invalid store addr 0x3800, len 10 This is a cosmetic issue that occurs when the encrypted master key on a VCMP guest cannot be decrypted with the unit key of that system. This most often occurs when a UCS taken on a different guest is loaded.
bugs.conditions: Taking a UCS from one vCMP guest or hardware device and loading it onto a different vCMP guest. Note: F5 does not support this configuration.
bugs.impact: Although there is no adverse effect on the system, error messages will be logged.

bugs.title: Internal capacity increase
bugs.symptoms: tmm restarts unexpectely.
bugs.conditions: Internal to the tmm, a capacity limit is exceeded.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmm does not experience unexpected restart due to insufficient internal capacity.

bugs.title: tmm may crash in fastl4 TCP
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash and BIGIP fail over.
bugs.conditions: Virtual with fastl4 and TCP profile configured and used. LRO is used.
bugs.impact: tmm may crash
bugs.fix: the crash is fixed.

bugs.title: TCP timestamp rewrite mode not working on the client side of ePVA offloaded connections
bugs.symptoms: When the tcp-timestamp-mode is set to 'rewrite', not the default 'preserve', the client side TSecr is not set correctly for the FIN packets. When the flow is evicted due to FIN processing in ePVA, the process copies the timestamp from the server sending the FIN/ACK. This unexpected behavior causes the TCP client to halt at the FIN-WAIT-2 because the client thinks the FIN/ACK from the BIG-IP system includes illegitimate timestamp options, and drops it.
bugs.conditions: -- tcp-timestamp-mode is set to 'rewrite'. -- FastL4 profile. -- Systems with ePVA feature support.
bugs.impact: TCP client cannot handle the FIN packets properly, causing connection issues.
bugs.workaround: Use the default 'preserve' mode for FastL4 profiles.

bugs.title: bd core due to specific wrong configuration
bugs.symptoms: A bd core is encountered.
bugs.conditions: The redirect URL blocking response has the erase cookies JavaScript tag attached.
bugs.impact: A bd core, failover, traffic disturbance.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not putting JavaScript in the redirection URL.
bugs.fix: This bd core no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Cave Creek Crypto hardware reports a false positive of a stuck queue state
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, a stuck crypto queue may be erroneously detected on Cave Creek-based systems. This includes BIG-IP 2x00, 4x00, i850, i2x00, i4x00, and HRC-i2800. The system writes messages similar to the following example to the /var/log/ltm file: crit tmm3[11707]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec qa-crypto3-3 queue is stuck. warning sod[4949]: 01140029:4: HA crypto_failsafe_t qa-crypto3-3 fails action is failover.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - Your BIG-IP system uses the Cave Creek encryption hardware. - You are making use of hardware-based SSL encryption. - The BIG-IP system is under heavy load.
bugs.impact: The system reports device errors in logs, and takes crypto high availability (HA) action, possibly resulting in failover.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can modify the crypto queue timeout value. To do so, perform the following procedure. Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system. 1. Log in to the BIG-IP system as an administrative user. 2. Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by running the following command: tmsh 3. To change the crypto queue timeout value, run the following command: modify /sys db crypto.queue.timeout value 300 4. Save the change by running the following command: save sys config Increasing the crypto queue timeout gives the hardware enough time to process all queued request.

bugs.title: BIG-IP fails to go active after cryptographic hardware has recovered from a failure
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP system might not become active after a crypto-failsafe condition even after it has recovered from a cryptographic hardware failure. As a result of this issue, you might see output of the tmsh show sys ha-status command similar to the following example: Feature Key Action Fail Feature Take Client Proc Timeout crypto-failsafe qa-crypto3-3 failover yes yes yes 0 tmm3 0 The /var/log/ltm file contains messages similar to the following examples: -- crit tmm[9184]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec cn-crypto-0 queue is stuck. -- notice sod[8874]: 01140029:5: HA crypto_failsafe_t cn-crypto-0 fails action is failover.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Using BIG-IP 2000/2200, 4000/4200, or i2600/i2800 platforms. -- The crypto-failsafe action is set to failover. -- The failsafe condition is triggered. -- The cryptographic hardware has recovered from its failure.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system stays down, even after the cryptographic hardware has recovered. When the system is in this condition, traffic is not being processed.
bugs.workaround: When your BIG-IP system is in this state, you can recover by restarting the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) process. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Because so there is no traffic being passed, there is no traffic impact to performing this procedure. 1. Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by running the following command: tmsh 2. Restart TMM by running the following command: restart /sys service tmm Note: There is no way to easily determine whether the cryptographic hardware has recovered from the failure. Unfortunately, therefore, performing this mitigation step might not return the BIG-IP system to an active state. There are other issues with similar symptoms. If your system is experiencing one of those issues instead, this mitigation step will not produce successful results. Here are three other Known Issues that produce almost exactly the same error messages, but involve different configurations. You might find additional assistance here:: + K53752362: The BIG-IP system may erroneously detect a stuck crypto queue in Cave Creek devices :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K53752362 + K53220379: The BIG-IP system may erroneously detect a stuck crypto queue :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K53220379 + K16632: A vCMP host may stop processing SSL and HTTP compressed traffic for a vCMP guest due to a worker-lite system timeout :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K16632

bugs.title: Cave Creek Crypto HW accelerated SSL traffic may encounter errors and performance problems.
bugs.symptoms: Cave Creek Hardware-accelerated Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) traffic may encounter errors and performance problems. The BIG-IP system may experience SSL connection failures or reduced performance. Following logs show an example of errors seen: /var/log/ltm -- crit tmm3[11707]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec qa-crypto3-3 queue is stuck. -- warning tmm3[11707]: 01260009:4: Connection error: ssl_basic_rx:1015: decrypt request error (20)
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Your BIG-IP system uses Cave Creek SSL hardware acceleration. -- You are experiencing a high SSL traffic load.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may experience SSL connection failures or reduced performance.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can increase the crypto.queue.timeout database key. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system. This procedure will mitigate future occurrences. A reboot of the BIG-IP system is required to clear a currently occurring condition. 1. Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) as an administrative user. 2. Run the following command: modify /sys db crypto.queue.timeout value 300 3. Reboot the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Disable port bridging on HSB ports for non-vCMP systems
bugs.symptoms: Internal packets flooded on internal switch interfaces by the HSB can be bridged back to the HSB on BIG-IP 5000/7000 and VIPRION B2100 blades configured to enable port bridging by the switch.
bugs.conditions: -- Packets being flooded from the HSB to VLAN members when adding/deleting VLANs. -- Non-vCMP systems. -- Virtual server configured for Direct Server Return (DSR or nPath Routing).
bugs.impact: This triggers a FDB flush and can result in packet flooding back to the HSB and potential network saturation.
bugs.fix: Port bridging on HSB interfaces in the switch for non-vCMP systems is now disabled, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: HTTP::uri does not work after ACCESS::respond
bugs.symptoms: After evaluating the URI, the ACCESS::respond command deletes the old URI when creating the header block for the response. If HTTP::uri is used, an error is logged to /var/log/ltm: err tmm3[20848]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/myapp.app/myrule <ACCESS_ACL_ALLOWED> - ERR_ARG (line 7) invoked from within "HTTP::uri"
bugs.conditions: An iRule similar to the following example: when ACCESS_ACL_ALLOWED { if { [HTTP::uri] == "/" } { log local0. "Redirecting to /test/" ACCESS::respond 302 Location "https://[HTTP::host]/test/" } log local0. "Redirected [HTTP::uri]" }
bugs.impact: Connection is reset and an error is logged in /var/log/ltm. There is no documentation indicating this functionality.
bugs.fix: There is now documentation that HTTP::uri does not work after ACCESS::respond.

bugs.title: Standby system saves config and changes status after sync from peer
bugs.symptoms: After running config sync from an Active to a Standby device, the sync status is in SYNC for a short period time. After a while, it automatically goes to Changes Pending status.
bugs.conditions: -- Manual sync device-group configuration. -- Modify existing policy encoding to uppercase (via tmsh). -- ASM configuration.
bugs.impact: The high availability (HA) configuration goes out of SYNC.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Push the sync back from the Standby device to the Active device, and then again from the Active to Standby. -- Put the device group into auto-sync state and push the config from the Active to the Standby. After the Sync state resolves and the ASM configuration is finished loading, the device group can be put back to Manual sync.
bugs.fix: Change requested encoding to lowercase.

bugs.title: Firewall NAT Source Translation UI does not show the enabled VLAN on egress interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Egress Interfaces are not checked in the Source Translation page even if they are configured.
bugs.conditions: Create a source translation object with egress Interfaces set to 'Enabled on...', select Egress Interfaces from the list, and hit 'Finished'. Egress Interfaces will not be checked with the originally configured values.
bugs.impact: Egress Interfaces will not be checked even if they are configured.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to check if the object is actually configured with Egress Interfaces
bugs.fix: Egress Interfaces will be selected whenever a user tries to create a source Translation object with Egress Interfaces.

bugs.title: When processing DNSX transfers ZoneRunner does not enforce best practices
bugs.symptoms: When processing DNSX transfers ZoneRunner does not enforce best practices.
bugs.conditions: DNSX Zones enabled.
bugs.impact: Best practices not enforced.
bugs.fix: ZoneRunner now enforces best practices when processing DNSX transfers.

bugs.title: Increased APM session capacity is not available after installing an APM session count License
bugs.symptoms: Unable to use extra capacity after installing an APM add-on license with a larger session count.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the add-on License generated lacks the mod_apm license, meaning that no full APM license was previously installed, only the APM Light license (which constrains connections to a 10-session maximum). To determine whether this condition exists, check the bigip.license file, or execute the following command: tmsh show sys license details. If only mod_apml is present and session counts are higher than 10, then the system is in the condition that triggers the problem.
bugs.impact: Unable to use extra session capability; can use only the 10-session maximum provided by the APM Light license.
bugs.workaround: Contact your F5 sales representative to get the correct APM add-on license with mod_apm, as well as the additional session count capability.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP GUI now displays an error if an APM user count add-on license is used without a base APM license. The system reports such licenses as 'Licensed (Incomplete)'.

bugs.title: LCD splash screen may display incorrect platform name on iSeries appliance
bugs.symptoms: The LCD on an iSeries appliance may show the incorrect platform name after a license is applied.
bugs.conditions: The platform name may be incorrect on the LCD until the first reboot.
bugs.impact: Display only, no functional impact
bugs.workaround: Use "tmsh show sys hardware" to see the correct platform name.

bugs.title: Qkview Security Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Qkview does not follow best practices for sanitizing and anonymizing collected data
bugs.conditions: Qkview created
bugs.impact: Under certain conditions, Qkviews may include sensitive information, which may in turn be uploaded to iHealth
bugs.fix: Qkview now follows best practices for sanitizing and anonymizing collected data

bugs.title: Periodically SIP requests are not sent to the server
bugs.symptoms: When rate-limiting is configured on the virtual server and/or pool using a SIP profile, periodically SIP requests may not be forwarded to the server despite rate being under limit.
bugs.conditions: SIP profile associated with virtual server and rate-limit configured.
bugs.impact: SIP requests may not be forwarded to the server.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling rate-limiting.

bugs.title: TMM crash with HTTP/2 under specific condition
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when upgrading an HTTP/1.1 connection to an HTTP/2 connnection.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 gateway enabled. -- Pool member supports protocol switching.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than removing the HTTP/2 profile from the virtual server.
bugs.fix: TMM properly handles protocol upgrade requests from pool members when HTTP/2 is enabled, so no crash occurs.

bugs.title: Unexpected additional policy is created while creating a policy from a template via REST
bugs.symptoms: An unexpected additional policy is created while creating a policy from a template via REST while modifying other attributes.
bugs.conditions: The user creates a policy from a template via REST while modifying other attributes.
bugs.impact: An unexpected additional policy is created.
bugs.workaround: Use the import-policy task to create a new policy from a template in REST. Alternatively, if using the /policies endpoint, create the policy with just the name and template, and make any other changes as a separate update afterwards.

bugs.title: Anti virus false positive detection on long XML uploads
bugs.symptoms: A false positive virus-detected violation. The description of the violation explains that the ICAP server was not contacted.
bugs.conditions: -- A long XML upload or payload. -- The assigned XML profile is configured to be inspected by the ICAP server.
bugs.impact: Violation is detected where no violation has occurred (false positive violation).
bugs.workaround: Increase the internal parameter max_raw_request_len to the required length of the XML. Note: This workaround will affect the amount of logged data from ASM.
bugs.fix: Fixed a false positive virus-detected violation related to long XML uploads.

bugs.title: Corrupted SessionDB messages causes TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM SegFaults and restarts
bugs.conditions: This was reported once during normal tmm operation.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash related to sessiondb

bugs.title: Setting metric-type via ospf redistribute command may not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: When using a dynamic routing configuration, where an OSPF process redistributes routes setting a metric-type from another OSPF process the metric type is not changed.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing configuration with 2 or more OSPF processes redistributing routes using the "redistribute ospf <other process number> metric-type <type>"
bugs.impact: Metric type is not changed.
bugs.workaround: Change metric-type using a route-map applied to the redistribute command.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now correctly sets the metric-type on redistribution

bugs.title: Add new security policy template for API driven systems - "API Security"
bugs.symptoms: No security policy template for API Security for API driven systems.
bugs.conditions: -- Using API. -- Attempting to define REST API protection, Web Socket protection.
bugs.impact: No policy template.
bugs.fix: Added new security policy template for API driven systems - 'API Security'.

bugs.title: Incorrect serverside throughput stats observed when PVA disabled on virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Serverside throughput stats may be doubled when ingress and egress flows are split across two TMMs.
bugs.conditions: - Ingress and egress flows are split across different TMMs. - PVA is disabled on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The statistics reporting the volume of traffic being handled by the BIG-IP system may appear inconsistent.
bugs.workaround: Enable PVA on the virtual server.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may incorrectly drop packets from a GRE tunnel with auto-lasthop disabled.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may incorrectly drop packets from a GRE point-to-point tunnel with auto-lasthop disabled.
bugs.conditions: The auto-lasthop of a GRE point-to-point tunnel is disabled.
bugs.impact: The decapsulated packets may be dropped in the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system correctly processes decapsulated packets from a GRE point-to-point tunnel.

bugs.title: Auto-disable TMM.HTTP.TCL.Validation when APM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: The db variable Tmm.HTTP.TCL.Validation is enabled by default. This db variable should be disabled when APM is provisioned/enabled, and when ACCESS::restrict_irule_event is disabled and HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE events are detected with the assigned iRules.
bugs.conditions: Steps to Reproduce: 1. Define the following iRule in the virtual server. when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { ACCESS::restrict_irule_events disable } when HTTP_REQUEST { set u [ HTTP::uri ] log local0. "XXX: [ HTTP::uri ]" } when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { log local0. "XXX: [ HTTP::status ] [ HTTP::header Location ]" set l [ HTTP::header Location ] if { $l starts_with {/my.policy} } { append l {?modified_by_irule=1} HTTP::header replace Location $l } elseif { $l starts_with {/renderer/agent_logon_page_form.eui} } { # Next response will be the real response to the client. ACCESS::log "XXX: lp_seen" set lp_seen 1 } if { [ HTTP::status ] == 200 && [ info exists lp_seen ] && $lp_seen == 1 } { unset lp_seen HTTP::header insert X-MyAppSpecialHeader 1 } } 2. Configure START :: LOGON PAGE :: ALLOW policy. 3. Access the virtual server.
bugs.impact: TCP reset triggered when it should not. With respect to the specific condition described, the system should post the logon page.
bugs.workaround: Manually disable Tmm.HTTP.TCL.Validation.
bugs.fix: Tmm.HTTP.TCL.Validation is now disabled automatically when APM provisioned during the upgrades. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: CPU utilization on i850 is not a reliable indicator of system capacity
bugs.symptoms: Unlike previous platforms, the i850 may report between 50-70% CPU utilization when at full capacity. The specific number is workload dependent, and therefore should not be used as an indicator of system headroom for sizing purposes.
bugs.conditions: Running BIG-IP software on an i850.
bugs.impact: Confusion of actual capacity usage.
bugs.workaround: Refer to the BIG-IP stats and published capabilities to determine utilized capacity under a specific workload.

bugs.title: Performance degraded
bugs.symptoms: Portal access performance had a slight performance degradation. This was identified to be due to a new queuing strategy implemented to improve per-request policy auth use-case performance for higher end platforms in the 13.0 release. The nature of the problem is such that overall system degradation may be observed if APM is provisioned and per-request policy is not used.
bugs.conditions: APM is provisioned, but functionality is not related to per-request policy.
bugs.impact: Performance will be slightly lower under load.
bugs.fix: The queuing strategy was altered to take minimal CPU resources when idle.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing SSL/TLS data
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash will processing SSL/TLS data
bugs.conditions: TLS client authentication enabled
bugs.impact: TMM produces a core file and takes the configured HA failover action.
bugs.fix: TMM processes SSL/TLS data as expected

bugs.title: URI::path iRules command warns end and start values equal
bugs.symptoms: URI::path iRules command warns end and start values equal
bugs.conditions: The end and start values equal
bugs.impact: Warning message shows in console.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the warning.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed in 14.0 release.

bugs.title: SELinux denies console access for remote users.
bugs.symptoms: SELinux denies console access for remote users if they are attempting to log in for the first time. This occurs because the user has not logged in before, so no entries exist for them in the userrolepartitions file.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote authentication is enabled. -- BIG-IP system user attempts to log in to the console as their first login.
bugs.impact: Certain remote users may not be able to log in to the console.
bugs.workaround: Login as a remote user using SSH or the GUI.
bugs.fix: Allow login to connect to MCP to announce remote user login and set user role partition access.

bugs.title: tmm continuously restarts after provisioning AFM
bugs.symptoms: tmm continuously restarts when the Webroot database is getting downloaded to a BIG-IP system with less than 16 GB RAM and AFM provisioned.
bugs.conditions: -- Webroot URL categorization configured for Traffic Classification. -- BIG-IP system with less than 16 GB RAM. -- AFM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to ensure that more than 16 GB RAM is available when AFM is provisioned.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system with less than 16 GB RAM and AFM provisioned now prevents downloading the Webroot database or any updates if it is not already downloaded. Note: If the Webroot database already exists before upgrade to this release, Webroot lookup will continue to work.

bugs.title: Editing OAuth Client / Resource Server Request objects in the GUI results in invalid configuration
bugs.symptoms: APM offers OpenID Connect Client / Resource Server starting in BIG-IP 13.1. The configuration is composed of many objects necessary for the configuration to work correctly. One of the objects specifies the request data included in the authorization requests to 3rd party OpenID Connect Authorization Servers.
bugs.conditions: Administrator uses the GUI: Access => Federation => OAuth Client / Resource Server => Request to modify the request objects.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to create a valid configuration using the GUI. If attempted, an error will occur from the 3rd party as a result of the invalid request. The error may be similar to: "Some requested scopes were invalid."
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to create the request object configuration, with a command such as: create apm aaa oauth-request my_custom_GoogleAuthRedirectRequest description customized method get parameters replace-all-with { access_type { value offline } client_id { type client-id } include_granted_scopes { value true } redirect_uri { type redirect-uri } response_type { type response-type } scope { type scope } } type auth-redirect-request
bugs.fix: Using the GUI to create, copy, and modify APM OAuth Client / Resource Server Request objects will now result in a configuration that can function properly.

bugs.title: tmm cores with SIGSEGV in dns_rebuild_response while using host command for not A/AAAA wideip
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores with SIGSEGV in dns_rebuild_response.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a wideip of type other than A/AAAA. 2. Create a iRule with a host command for the previously created wideip. 3. Create a related zonerunner record with the same name and type. 4. Dig against the wideip with type any. 5. Observe that tmm cores.
bugs.impact: tmm cores.
bugs.workaround: Don't use host command for non type A/AAAA wideips.

bugs.title: Hourly billed cloud images are now pre-licensed
bugs.symptoms: Hourly billed images in cloud environments require outbound internet access to the F5 public license server in order to retrieve a license. This causes some sites with strict network access policies to fail to license.
bugs.conditions: Using hourly billing.
bugs.impact: Hourly instances do not receive licenses and thus could not pass traffic without outbound internet access.
bugs.workaround: Enable outbound internet access when the guest instance is created to allow it to license, then revoke it.
bugs.fix: Hourly billed cloud images are now pre-licensed and so do not require internet access to receive a license.

bugs.title: 'Can't associate Bot Defense ASM Profile' when creating iApp
bugs.symptoms: When creating an iApp, an error appears in the log: Configuration error: Can't associate Bot Defense ASM Profile (/Common/NEW_APP.app/ASM_NEW_APP_policy) folder does not exist.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while deploying certain iApps.
bugs.impact: The iApp successfully deploys, but an error is logged to /var/log/ltm. This is a cosmetic error message, and you can safely ignore it.
bugs.fix: The 'Can't associate Bot Defense ASM Profile' error no longer occurs when creating iApps.

bugs.title: Modifying a Netflow profile requires that there are zero connections on the virtual servers that it is attached to
bugs.symptoms: To change a Netflow profile that is attached to a virtual server, zero connections must be present on the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to change a Netflow profile that is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Cannot modify Netflow profile.
bugs.workaround: Either make sure that there are zero connections when modifying an attached Netflow profile, or detach the Netflow profile you wish to modify temporarily from all virtual servers that it is attached to. To make changes when the virtual server has active connections (ongoing stream of Netflow packets): 1. Change the Netflow profile in virtual server to none. 2. Change virtual server state to disabled (after this step, there will be 0 active connections for the virtual server). 3. Change Netflow profile in virtual server to new profile. 4. Change virtual server state to enabled.
bugs.fix: The system now disallows modifications to Netflow virtual servers with non-zero connection counts.

bugs.title: For HTTP statistic AVR collects Host Names only instead of the full URI
bugs.symptoms: AVR reports contain the "URI"s or the "Host Name + URI"s but for some scenarios, it is not needed and AVR should only report the "Host Name"s instead. The `:PORT` portion of the URL will be included in the hostname.
bugs.conditions: 1. AVR/ASM/DOS provisioned. 2. URLs flag is set in analytics profile
bugs.impact: No impact on current behavior.
bugs.fix: This option only available through the TMSH, so access to TMSH is desirable. To turn on Host Name only mode, run - "tmsh modify sys db avr.collectonlyhostnamefromuri value enable". To turn it off (the default behavior), run - "tmsh modify sys db avr.collectonlyhostnamefromuri value disable".

bugs.title: API errors can prevent access to login history in Configuration Utility
bugs.symptoms: Accessing the login history pages at System :: Logins, results in an error message similar to the following: Can't create temp directory, /var/system/tmp/tmsh/xxxxx, errno 13] Permission denied. The login history is not shown.
bugs.conditions: Accessing the login history pages at System :: Logins to view the login history.
bugs.impact: Cannot access login history in the Configuration Utility.
bugs.workaround: None at this time.

bugs.title: FQDN pool member status remains in 'checking' state after full config sync
bugs.symptoms: After performing a full config-sync (with overwrite config option checked) the sync target (peer) shows FQDN pool members stuck in the 'checking' state.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after a full config sync is forced between peers using FQDN pool members: tmsh modify cm device-group <dg_name> devices modify { <local_member> { set-sync-leader } }
bugs.impact: Affected pools show an Availability state of 'unknown', although pool members are available and can pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: Restart bigd on the affected peer after the config sync.
bugs.fix: After performing a full config-sync (with overwrite config option checked) the sync target (peer) no longer shows FQDN pool members stuck in the 'checking' state. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: LDAP Query may fail to resolve nested groups
bugs.symptoms: LDAP Query agent may fail to resolve nested groups for a user. /var/log/apm logfile contains the following error messages when 'debug' log level is enabled for Access Profile: err apmd[17159]: 014902bb:3: /Common/ldap_access:Common:254fdc14 Failed to process the LDAP search result while getting group membership down with error (No such object.). err apmd[17159]: 014902bb:3: /Common/ldap_access:Common:254fdc14 Failed to process the LDAP search result while querying LDAP with error (No such object.).
bugs.conditions: LDAP Query agent is configured in an Access Policy. 'Fetch groups to which the user or group belong' option is enabled
bugs.impact: LDAP Query agent fails. unable to get user identity. unable to finalize Access Policy.
bugs.fix: after fix, LDAP Query resolves all nested groups as expected and session.ldap.last.attr.memberOf attributes contains user's groups

bugs.title: TMM Core During FTP Monitor Use
bugs.symptoms: TMM Cores.
bugs.conditions: When the FTP monitor is used.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Turn off FTP monitoring.
bugs.fix: The tmm no longer cores when using a FTP monitor.

bugs.title: Version format of hypervisor bundle matches Version format of ISO
bugs.symptoms: Recently F5 incorporated 4th element into versioning scheme. 4th and 5th are separated by dash (instead of dot) in ISO name. This change/bug insures that names of hypervisor bundles also use dash between 4th and 5th elements.
bugs.conditions: Applies to hypervisor bundles (for example ova files for vmware).
bugs.impact: Version format in names of hypervisor bundles matches version format of ISO file
bugs.workaround: Version format in names of hypervisor bundles matches version format of ISO file
bugs.fix: Version format in names of hypervisor bundles matches version format of ISO file (usage of dash between 4th and 5th elements).

bugs.title: ICMP drop logs sometimes has wrong logging field values
bugs.symptoms: With ACL policy configured to allow a restricted set of traffic (say TCP packets) but disallowing ICMP, the client ICMP messages are being rightfully dropped. But the drops with ACL logging enabled, shows up wrong values. The values sometimes show up as TCP packet being dropped, instead of ICMP.
bugs.conditions: ICMP packet is configured to be dropped through ACL Rule policy, with logging enable on ACL Rule, the logs generated has wrong values. Sometimes, the field values for ICMP are totally wrong, and it could show up as a TCP connection being dropped (especially, when the most recent request was a TCP connection).
bugs.impact: Functionally, the ACL dropping behavior is correct. But with logging fields being displayed wrong, it appears as if a packet which was not supposed to be dropped is being wrongly rejected. No functional impact, the problem is only with logging information being wrong.

bugs.title: 13.0.0 Hotfix HF3 3.0.1679 TMM CORED due to SIGSEGV.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when woodside congestion-control is in use.
bugs.conditions: When woodside congestion-control is in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Other congestion control algorithms can be used as a workaround.
bugs.fix: This fix handles a rare TMM crash when woodside congestion-control is in use.

bugs.title: Geolocation upgrade files fail to replicate to secondary blades
bugs.symptoms: Geolocation upgrade files fail to replicate to secondary blades.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiblade VIPRION platforms/vCMP guests. -- Upgrading geolocation files on the primary blade. -- Viewing the geolocation files on the secondary blades.
bugs.impact: Geoip database is not updated to match primary blade.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Use the root account to manually create the /shared/GeoIP/v2 directory on secondary blades, and then run geoip_update_data on primary blade. -- On primary blade: 1. Edit /etc/csyncd.conf as shown below. 2. Restart csyncd. 3. Run geoip_update_data. To edit /etc/csyncd.conf: Merge the following two terms: monitor dir /shared/GeoIP {...) monitor dir /shared/GeoIP/v2 {...} into one term, as follows: monitor dir /shared/GeoIP { queue geoip pull pri2sec recurse yes defer no lnksync yes md5 no post "/usr/local/bin/geoip_reload_data" }
bugs.fix: Geolocation upgrade files now correctly replicate to secondary blades.

bugs.title: NetHSM capacity reduces when handling errors
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions NetHSM performance may be reduce while handling errors.
bugs.conditions: NetHSM enabled
bugs.impact: Reduced performance potentially leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: Process errors more efficiently when using NetHSM

bugs.title: RRD cpu files are not updated when statsd has no prior knowledge of blades joining a cluster.
bugs.symptoms: If a blade already known to statsd goes down, statsd continues to update the blade's /var/rrd/bladeXcpu file If a new blade joins and is announced to statsd, statsd stops updating all /var/rrd/bladeXcpu files especillay if it did not have prior knowledge of the blade.
bugs.conditions: If statsd is restarted after the blade is disabled, or goes down, and after that the blade rejoins the cluster, the /var/rrd/bladeXcpu files stop updating (where X is the blade number).
bugs.impact: Data of those files is not updated. This impacts the graphs generated from these files.
bugs.workaround: Execute the command "bigstart restart statsd" after the new blade has joined the cluster.

bugs.title: Possible memory leak in MRF under low memory
bugs.symptoms: MRF may leak a session db record when a memory allocation failure occurs when adding a connection to an internal table. In this the table entry will not be cleaned up when the connection closes.
bugs.conditions: MRF may leak a session db record when a memory allocation failure occurs when adding a connection to an internal table. In this the table entry will not be cleaned up when the connection closes.
bugs.impact: The table entry will be remain until the box resets.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The code has been fixed to remove the table entry when a memory allocation failure occurs while adding the record.

bugs.title: OAuth reports do not follow best practices
bugs.symptoms: The OAuth report does not follow current best practices
bugs.conditions: Authorized administrative user requests an OAuth report from the WebUI
bugs.impact: The OAuth report does not follow current best practices
bugs.fix: OAuth reports follow best practices

bugs.title: Web UI does not follow current best coding practices
bugs.symptoms: The web UI does not follow current best coding practices while processing PEM configuration updates.
bugs.conditions: PEM provisioned.
bugs.impact: UI does not respond as intended.
bugs.fix: The web UI now follows current best coding practices while processing PEM configuration updates.

bugs.title: Web UI does not follow current best coding practices
bugs.symptoms: The web UI does not follow current best coding practices while processing ASM configuration updates.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: UI does not respond as intended.
bugs.fix: The web UI now follows current best coding practices while processing ASM configuration updates.

bugs.title: Web UI does not follow current best coding practices
bugs.symptoms: The web UI does not follow current best coding practices while processing URL DB updates.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned.
bugs.impact: UI does not respond as intended.
bugs.fix: The web UI now follows current best coding practices while processing URL DB updates.

bugs.title: SAML export does not follow best practices
bugs.symptoms: Export of SAML data does not follow current best practices
bugs.conditions: SAML data exported by administrator
bugs.impact: Administrative request processing does not follow current best practices
bugs.fix: Update SAML export to follow current best practices

bugs.title: DNS request can be dropped when queued in parallel with another request
bugs.symptoms: DNS requests can be dropped.
bugs.conditions: 1. When two DNS requests are received in quick succession with matching IP/Port pairs. 2. The UDP DNS virtual does not use datagram LB mode.
bugs.impact: DNS requests may be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Configure the virtual server for UDP profile with datagram LB mode enabled.
bugs.fix: Added a new queue mechanism in IP proxy to handle datagram packets received in quick succession from same source/port.

bugs.title: nsm cores during update of nexthop for ECMP recursive route
bugs.symptoms: The Net­work Services Module daemon (nsm) cores while processing updates for ECMP recursive route nexthop.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing enabled. BGP peers provides ECMP routes with recursive nexthop.
bugs.impact: Failures passing traffic using the dynamic routes.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: nsm is able to process ECMP route updates without problem.

bugs.title: Potential TMM crash due to incorrect number of attributes in a PEM iRule command
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: An iRule with a PEM iRule command that does not have the minimum number of attributes.
bugs.impact: Loss of service. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the PEM iRule command is called with at least the minimum number of parameters. For example, make sure to call 'PEM::subscriber config policy referential set' with referential policies.
bugs.fix: The system now provides the correct number of attributes, preventing a NULL pointer dereference.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 requests with large body may result in RST_STREAM with FRAME_SIZE_ERROR
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 requests with a large body may result in the BIG-IP system sending RST_STREAM with FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 profile is configured on the virtual server. -- Request has body size greater than 16 KB.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 stream is reset with FRAME_SIZE_ERROR and transfer does not complete.
bugs.fix: Large HTTP/2 requests are now processed as expected.

bugs.title: Config with custom 'SIP' or 'Firepass' monitor fails to load after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: A configuration that contains custom 'SIP' or 'FirePass' monitors that is upgraded from a version earlier than v13.1.0 may either fail to load, or may result in a configuration that loads the first time after the upgrade, but cannot be re-loaded from the text config files. If the BIG-IP system has partitions other than 'Common', the initial configuration load may fail with an error such as: 01070726:3: monitor /Common/sip-monitor in partition Common cannot reference SSL profile monitor parameter /Common/sip-monitor 1 SSL_PROFILE_NAME= in partition name-of-other-partition If the BIG-IP system only has a 'Common' partition, the initial configuration load will succeed, but subsequent attempts to load the configuration (e.g., 'tmsh load sys config') may fail with this error: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 63) "user-defined" unknown property Which corresponds to a SIP or FirePass monitor in the configuration such as: ltm monitor sip /Common/test_sip_monitor { cipherlist DEFAULT:+SHA:+3DES:+kEDH compatibility enabled debug no defaults-from /Common/sip destination *:* filter 488 interval 5 mode tcp time-until-up 0 timeout 16 user-defined SSL_PROFILE_NAME /Common/test_sip_monitor_ssl_profile }
bugs.conditions: Custom 'SIP' or 'FirePass' monitor is configured, and the config is upgraded from a version earlier than v13.1.0 to version v13.1.0.
bugs.impact: After upgrade, the configuration fails to load with an error such as: 01070726:3: monitor /Common/sip-monitor in partition /Common cannot reference SSL profile monitor parameter /Common/sip-monitor 1 SSL_PROFILE_NAME= in partition name-of-other-partition. Alternatively, the configuration loads after upgrade, but the config file is corrupted, and will fail to load (such as after a system restart, or upon explicit 'tmsh load sys config'), with an error such as: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 63) "user-defined" unknown property
bugs.workaround: Remove custom 'SIP' and 'FirePass' monitors from the configuration, and re-create them manually after upgrade is complete.
bugs.fix: In this release, a configuration that contains a custom 'SIP' or 'FirePass ' monitor from a version earlier than v13.1.0 now loads correctly and continues to load as expected.

bugs.title: Additional logging for AVR mailer
bugs.symptoms: When AVR mailer fails due to server error, the exact error of failure is not reported anywhere and it is not possible to troubleshoot the issue.
bugs.conditions: Errors while sending out AVR e-mails
bugs.impact: Difficulty troubleshooting failures of mailer
bugs.workaround: It is possible to manually edit the mailer PHP script to increase debug level

bugs.title: localdbmgr can occasionally crash during shutdown
bugs.symptoms: When localdbmgr process is restarted, occasionally, the process crashes and a core file will be generated.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is provisioned. -- localdbmgr process is restarted.
bugs.impact: Although the process restarts, there is no impact to the APM functionality.
bugs.fix: localdbmgr no longer crashes during shutdown.

bugs.title: ASM crash when configuring remote logger for WebSocket traffic with response-logging:all
bugs.symptoms: ASM may crash when configuring remote logger for WebSocket traffic virtual server.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server handling WebSocket traffic. -- ASM remote logger on the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: ASM crash; system goes offline.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Remove remote logger. -- Have response logging for illegal requests only.
bugs.fix: The system now handles memory correctly and avoids crashing in this specific scenario.

bugs.title: DNS NOTIFY not sent to mgmt IP under Zone Transfer Clients list after DNS Express zone update
bugs.symptoms: When a DNS Express zone gets some zone entries updated, the BIG-IP system does not send DNS NOTIFY to nameserver with IP addresses from the mgmt subnet listed under Zone Transfer Clients.
bugs.conditions: * nameserver has IP address from mgmt subnet. * nameserver id listed under Zone Transfer Clients of DNS Express zone. * DNS Express zone gets entries updated.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system does not send NOTIFY request to the nameserver.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Content-Length is a valid HTTP/2 Header
bugs.symptoms: Content-Length header is not removed from response header blocks.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: None. This is correct behavior, as the Content-Length header is a valid one in HTTP/2 header blocks.
bugs.workaround: None needed. This is correct behavior.
bugs.fix: Removed unused configuration option.

bugs.title: TMSH not listing GTM Listener rules when listing all listeners
bugs.symptoms: TMSH does not show attached iRules on a GTM Listener when listing the listener via 'tmsh list gtm listener'.
bugs.conditions: A GTM Listener is configured with an iRule attached
bugs.impact: You would not see the iRule attached to the GTM Listeners when no name was provided
bugs.workaround: Specify the name of the listener to see

bugs.title: Intermittent connection resets are seen in HTTP/2 gateway when HTTP/2 preface is sent to server
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 connection in gateway scenario is reset when HTTP/2 preface makes it to the server instead of being consumed by the BIG-IP system. The backend connection to the server in gateway scenario is an HTTP/1 connection. The connection is reset when HTTP/2 preface is sent on the backend connection instead of being consumed by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 gateway is configured.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 connection reset is seen.

bugs.title: Chromebook legal browser detected as running selenium by Proactive Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: No real impact to the traffic, when selenium only is detected, but if the Proactive Bot Defense detects other headless browser properties in couple with the selenium detection it could lead to the headless browser detection score above limits and drop the request.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM or DoS Provisioned. 2. DoS Application profile assigned to a virtual server. 3. Proactive Bot Defense and Block suspicious browsers sections are enabled in the DoS Application profile configuration.
bugs.impact: No real impact to the traffic.
bugs.workaround: Disable Proactive Bot Defense or change browser_legit_min_score_drop sys db to be higher value. list sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop { value "120" }
bugs.fix: Selenium detection is changed for chromebooks

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing IPv6 traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may may crash while processing IPv6 traffic.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM processes IPv6 traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Filter by custom period is not working properly in some cases
bugs.symptoms: When in Requests (Event Correlation, Brute Force) page custom time period defined in filter - it is not working correctly, wrong dates filtered
bugs.conditions: Sever and client machines use different time zones
bugs.impact: User cannot filter effectively by custom time period
bugs.workaround: User can shift time period to compensate difference between server and his client machine
bugs.fix: Time range filter was fixed to work correctly and not depends from client machine timezone anymore

bugs.title: Wrong policy version time in policy created after synchronization between active and stand by machines.
bugs.symptoms: After synchronization, the policy version time in the policy created on the standby BIG-IP system is different from the policy version time on the original policy on the active BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Synchronizing the new policies on the active system with new policies on the standby system.
bugs.impact: Policy version timestamp on standby system is not synchronized properly.
bugs.workaround: Run full synchronization again from active system to the group.
bugs.fix: The policy version time in the policy created on the standby BIG-IP system now matches the policy version time on the original policy on the active BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Support for Safenet Client Software v7.x
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system is not compatible with SafeNet v7.x.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use a BIG-IP system with the Safenet v7.x client software.
bugs.impact: No support provided for the SafeNet network HSMs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than using an HSM with the supported SafeNet client software.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports SafeNet v7.x in the following configuration: -- Client software: 7.1. -- HSM software: 7.1. -- HSM firmware 7.0.2.

bugs.title: /var/log/avr/monpd.disk.provision not rotate
bugs.symptoms: the log file may fill-up /var partition
bugs.conditions: there is no special condition for this issue - if the log is big it won't rotate
bugs.impact: the log file may fill-up /var partition
bugs.workaround: 1. gzip /var/log/avr/monpd.disk.provision 2. touch /var/log/avr/monpd.disk.provision
bugs.fix: added /var/log/avr/monpd.disk.provision to the rotate mechanisem.

bugs.title: MCPD process may lock up and restart when applying Local Traffic Policy to virtual server
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd process becomes unresponsive while attempting to load the configuration, or attempting to apply a configuration change that associates a particular local traffic policy to a virtual server. The mcpd process may also periodically restart every 5 minutes.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual servers configured. - Specific policies configured and attached used by virtual servers. Only policies configured in a specific way will trigger this situation. The specifics are not well understood, however, the vast majority of Local Traffic Policies are unaffected by this issue.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: mcpd is responsive when an LTM Policy is attached to a virtual server, or when an already-attached policy is updated.

bugs.title: LDAP fails to initiate SSL negotiation because client cert and key associated file permissions are not preserved
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to an affected build, the default key will have incorrect group ownership.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade or load a .ucs with SSL keys configured.
bugs.impact: File permissions are not preserved in the .ucs file. The httpd process will not be able to use the default key, so anything using it will fail.
bugs.workaround: Run the following two commands: tmsh save /sys config tmsh load /sys config
bugs.fix: The system now preserves correct permissions for default.key across upgrade and ucs load.

bugs.title: Restarting service MCPD or rebooting BIG-IP device adds 'other' file read permissions to key file
bugs.symptoms: Restarting service MCPD or rebooting the BIG-IP device adds Unix 'other' read file permissions for key files. Key files Unix permission changes from '-rw-r-----' to '-rw-r--r--'
bugs.conditions: 1. Restarting the service MCPD 2. Rebooting BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: Key file Unix read permission changes from '-rw-r-----' to '-rw-r--r--'
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fix made sure restart of service MCPD and reboot of device does not change key files Unix read permissions from '-rw-r-----' to '-rw-r--r--'

bugs.title: A db var compression.zlibinflateratio.threshold is added to force stopping inflating
bugs.symptoms: A zip bomb can be sent to a BIG-IP system. When it is unzipped, its content can consume too much space.
bugs.conditions: This happens when the inflation ratio is very high.
bugs.impact: It can cause buffer overflow, or out of memory.

bugs.title: AWS C5/M5 Instances do not support BIG-IP VE
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) does not function on AWS C5/M5 instances.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE on AWS C5/M5 instances.
bugs.impact: Cannot use BIG-IP VE on AWS C5/M5 instances.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP VE now functions on AWS C5/M5 Instances.

bugs.title: tmm crash during execution of a per-request policy when modified during execution.
bugs.symptoms: Modify/delete of per-request policy during heavy traffic flow causes tmm to crash.
bugs.conditions: While a per-request policy (macro) is getting executed. Admin deletes the parent policy item (at the same time).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not modify per-request policy during heavy traffic flow.
bugs.fix: The situation is fixed, if the policy that is getting executed currently has been deleted, look for its continuation in the deleted policy list.

bugs.title: rrset statistics unavailable
bugs.symptoms: When cache entries of any kind are deleted, the rrset statistics for the cache may not be available
bugs.conditions: This occurs when dns cache entries are deleted
bugs.impact: Rrset statistics may not be available
bugs.fix: Update RRset ID when cached RRset is deleted

bugs.title: ASM Request Logs: Cannot delete second 10,000 records of filtered event log messages
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to delete request logs by a filter (10,000 at a time), only works once. Subsequent delete by filter actions do not remove additional earlier logs.
bugs.conditions: System has over 10,000 ASM request logs by a selected filter, and delete all by filter is used multiple times.
bugs.impact: Only the latest 10,000 events are deleted.
bugs.workaround: No work around for deleting by a filter. Delete all (without filter) works, and deleting selected requests works.
bugs.fix: Deletion by filter correctly deletes subsequent sets of 10,000 rows per action.

bugs.title: APM Client Software may be missing after doing fresh install of BIG-IP VE
bugs.symptoms: apm client software checks is broken in VM created with BIG-IP-13.1.0.1.0.0.8.ALL-scsi.ova.
bugs.conditions: Any software instance created by deployment of any OVA for the affected software versions.
bugs.impact: APM endpoint inspection feature (for Mac, windows and Linux clients). [Users affected] Configuration of APM client software check APM Visual policy editor. [Admin UI] APM Client package @ Connectivity / VPN : Connectivity : Profiles if you select "Web Browser Add-ons for BIG-IP Edge Client" option. [Admin UI]
bugs.workaround: Try the "epsec refresh" commands again after removing all environment locks on the shared RPM database using the following command: rm /shared/lib/rpm/__db.* epsec refresh
bugs.fix: After deployment of a new OVA for the fixed version(s), the problem no longer occurs.

bugs.title: qkviews for secondary blade appear to be corrupt
bugs.symptoms: Normally, a qkview created on a multi-blade system will include a qkview for every blade on the system. Those qkview files have an error that makes the tar-ball appear corrupt.
bugs.conditions: Running a qkview on a system with blades. Attempt to access the tar-ball using the following command: tar -tvzf 127.3.0.2.qkview | tail.
bugs.impact: The system posts the following messages: gzip: stdin: unexpected end of file tar: Child returned status 1 tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now Confuses troubleshooters into thinking that the blade qkview files are corrupt, which they are not.
bugs.fix: By not always writing an errant newline, the problem is solved.

bugs.title: SSL Forward Proxy not to cache expired server certificate
bugs.symptoms: In SSL Forward Proxy, the client side forges a server certificate and caches the forged cert for all server certificates passed the server side certificate validation including expired certificate.
bugs.conditions: In SSL Forward Proxy enabled server side profile, the 'server authentication' is set to required, and the 'expired certificate response control' is set to ignore. When the backend server certificate expired, the client side SSL will forge a certificate and cache the forged certificate.
bugs.impact: The caching of the expired certificate may cause the SSL to use the expired certificate even when the backend server renew the certificate.
bugs.fix: With this fix, SSL will no longer cache expired server certificate.

bugs.title: Ctrl+C does not terminate TShark
bugs.symptoms: A running TShark process on the BIG-IP system has problems exiting when the user is finished capturing and presses CTRL+C while listening on a tmm VLAN or 0.0.
bugs.conditions: -- Using TShark on a tmm VLAN or 0.0. -- Pressing Ctrl+C to exit.
bugs.impact: TShark does not exit as expected when pressing CTRL+C.
bugs.workaround: To recover, you can move the process to the background (CTRL+Z) and then halt the process, by running a command similar to the following: kill -9 'pidof tshark'
bugs.fix: Ctrl+C now terminates TShark as expected.

bugs.title: tmm core under stress when BADOS configured and attack signatures enabled
bugs.symptoms: Tmm core under stress. Note: This issue has a very low probability of occurring.
bugs.conditions: -- Out of memory. -- BADOS configured. -- Attack signatures enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None, except to not configure attack signatures.
bugs.fix: Added protection for the case when context adm_filters allocation is failed.

bugs.title: Upgrade may fail on a multi blade system when there are scheduled reports in configuration
bugs.symptoms: Unable to upgrade to newer version or hotfix fail. Secondary slot always fails upgrade with the following error in var/log/liveinstall.log: error: status 256 returned by command: F5_INSTALL_SESSION_TYPE=install tmsh -f save sys ucs /var/tmp/fbSBcyXrsz.ucs info: >++++ result: info: Saving active configuration... info: Thrift: Tue Dec 19 10:53:45 2017 TSocket::open() connect() <Host: localhost Port: 9090>Connection refused info: Error during config save. info: Unexpected Error: UCS saving process failed.
bugs.conditions: 1) System has two or more slots (multi-blade) 2) There are scheduled reports in configuration.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: 1) Save configuration for scheduled reports aside. 2) Remove all scheduled reports from configuration. 3) Perform upgrade. 4) Add scheduled reports back to configuration.
bugs.fix: On secondary blades monpd listens on slot-specific local address 127.0.3.X, so tmsh should use this address when it establishes connection to monpd (instead of 127.0.0.1)

bugs.title: AJAX blocking page isn't shown when a webpage uses jQuery framework.
bugs.symptoms: Request is blocked by an ASM policy, but the ASM end user does not see the blocking page with a unique support id for the blocked request.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM policy Asynchronous JavaScript and XML (AJAX) blocking page enabled. 2. ASM policy is working in blocking mode. 3. ASM policy attached to a virtual server. 4. AJAX request has been sent and blocked.
bugs.impact: ASM end user has no visual indication that there has been a blocked AJAX request.
bugs.fix: The system now handles Ajax requests being sent via the JQuery framework.

bugs.title: Allow param identification by arbitrary named attribute
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to configure an arbitrary selector. Only name/id is allowed.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when you want to configure alerts based on arbitrary selectors in the web page. - Create new antifraud profile. - Create new protected URL. - In parameters create new parameter and configure CSS selector (input[attr="custom"]). - Check 'Selector' checkbox.
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure an arbitrary selector.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is available.
bugs.fix: A selector can now use a protected parameter other than id/name.

bugs.title: Behavioral Clarification For Tcl After Command
bugs.symptoms: Flows with after commands accrue in the TMM due to not-yet-executed after scripts, causing memory pressure.
bugs.conditions: After command used in a Tcl script with a timeout beyond the connection lifetime.
bugs.impact: Potential memory pressure, leading to out of memory and TMM failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: If the after command does not need to execute after the flow has been expired, use one of the *_CLOSED events to cancel the after command.
bugs.fix: After commands on a closed or aborted flow will now be removed as soon as possible, rather than waiting for their timer to fire and detect they cannot be run, thereby significantly decreasing memory pressure.

bugs.title: mcpd may dump core on startup
bugs.symptoms: mcpd may generate a core file upon startup, with a message being logged that overdog restarted it because mcpd failed to send a heartbeat for five minutes.
bugs.conditions: This can happen only at startup.
bugs.impact: mcpd restarts, but resumes normal operation.
bugs.fix: mcpd no longer generates a core on startup.

bugs.title: Under certain circumstances, a stale HTTP/2 stream can cause a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Tmm might crash due to a stale/stalled HTTP/2 stream.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 profile in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Stale/stalled HTTP2 streams are handled correctly to prevent a tmm crash.

bugs.title: Disabling TCP segmentation offload can lead to a tmm assert
bugs.symptoms: If using vmxnet3 or virtio tmm drivers (not unic), if TCP segmentation offload is disabled while processing traffic, a tmm assert may be observed and tmm will restart. The tmm assert appears similar to the following: notice tso ioctl for member:0 of /Common/internal failed with value: 32tso ioctl for member:0 of /Common/external failed with value: 32panic: ./local/net/packet.h:328: Assertion "packet_ref: not free" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Deploy Virtual Edition (VE) using vmxnet3 or virtio tmm drivers. -- Continuously pass traffic through the system. -- Disable the DB variable tm.tcpsegmentationoffload.
bugs.impact: Sometimes tmm will restart, which will lead to traffic group failovers. This is a fairly rare situation, and disabling TCP segmentation offloading is not something routinely done, but if done while under load, this failure might occur.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Switching partitions while viewing objects in GUI can result in empty list
bugs.symptoms: In LTM Pool List, Node List, and Address Translations pages, switching partitions while viewing objects in the GUI can result in empty list.
bugs.conditions: This issue is present when all of the following conditions are met: -- One partition contains multiple pages of objects. -- The page count in one partition is greater than the page count in another. -- The active page number is greater than 1. -- You switch to a partition whose max number of pages is lower than the active page number. For example, in the GUI: 1. Create two non-Common partitions. 2. In one partition, create enough pools so that they do not fit on one page. 3. In the second partition, create only enough pools for one page. 4. On the Local Traffic :: Pools list page in the first partition, navigate to the second page of objects. 5. Switch to the other partition. 6. Note that the displayed page contains no objects.
bugs.impact: The list of pools is empty despite the fact that there are pools available.
bugs.workaround: Return to the first page of objects before switching to any other partition.
bugs.fix: The system now resets to the first page if the page number is greater than the page count, so the partition's objects display correctly.

bugs.title: Memory leak when attaching an LTM policy to a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: MCP's memory increases when deleting and adding an LTM policy attached to a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policies must be in use. -- A policy with at least one rule. (Note: A rule with actions or conditions will leak more memory.) -- Add the policy to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: MCP may run slower when memory is low. If all memory is used up, MCP will crash, which will cause a failover or outage.
bugs.fix: The system now prevents MCP from leaking memory when attaching an LTM policy to a virtual server.

bugs.title: Switch statements should be terminated with '--' to mark the end of the options
bugs.symptoms: Certain system iRules use tcl code that switches on the HTTP path string, taken from the [HTTP::path] command. It is possible to pass a string to it with a leading '-', and TCL interprets this as an option to the switch statement and will likely abort the connection.
bugs.conditions: Using system iRules: _sys_APM_ExchangeSupport_OA_BasicAuth _sys_APM_ExchangeSupport_OA_NtlmAuth _sys_APM_ExchangeSupport_main
bugs.impact: TCL will likely abort the connection if such a path is found.

bugs.title: APMD restarts when worker threads are stuck
bugs.symptoms: APMD restarts and logs a message about all threads being stuck.
bugs.conditions: A race condition allows the busy thread count to remain higher than the actual value. If it reaches the maximum thread count, APMD will restart.
bugs.impact: APMD can restart unexpectedly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The race condition is corrected and the restarts are eliminated.

bugs.title: cmp-hash change can hang iRule DNS lookup
bugs.symptoms: An iRule that uses RESOLV::lookup can hang repeatedly when cmp-hash configuration is changed.
bugs.conditions: An iRule must be in the middle of a call to RESOLV::lookup when a vlan cmp-hash configuration is changed.
bugs.impact: The iRule call can hang repeatedly.
bugs.workaround: Restart the TMM. This will interrupt client traffic.
bugs.fix: The iRule connection is reestablished when the pending query expires, so subsequent RESOLV::lookup calls do not hang per TMM.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing WebSockets data
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances, the Websockets filter does not properly parse certain request/response headers.
bugs.conditions: Websockets and HTTP profile attached to virtual.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to a failover event.

bugs.title: JavaScript errors shown when debugging a mobile device with ASM deviceID enabled
bugs.symptoms: When debugging a mobile device with ASM Device ID enabled, the Google Chrome browser console log contains JavaScript errors similar to the following: net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME. Note: In order to view the Chrome browser console log, you must use BrowserStack from a developer's console, or physically connect the phone by cable, enable 'usb debug', enable 'device discovery' on Chrome on the desktop, and view the console from there.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM policy is attached on a virtual server with deviceID enabled. -- Device ID collection request has been sent from a mobile device. -- Chrome browser console log is opened.
bugs.impact: Mobile device app developers might be concerned about the errors, potentially asking about why the ASM JavaScript code attempts to access UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME in a mobile device. The errors occur because Device ID enabled on an ASM policy uses the JavaScript request URI argument 'chrome-extension' to detect the existence of malicious browser extension. However, Chrome on Android/iOS does not support 'chrome-extension'.
bugs.workaround: Disable Device ID in ASM policy.
bugs.fix: The system now avoids checking Chrome extensions on mobile devices, so no UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME errors occur.

bugs.title: SIP MR profile, setting incorrect branch param for CANCEL to INVITE
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP SIP profile MR does not maintain the Via 'branch parameter' ID when the Via header insertion is enabled for INVITE and CANCEL for the same INVITE.
bugs.conditions: This happens only when the following conditions are both met: -- The transport connection that issued INVITE has been terminated. -- A new transport is used to issue CANCEL
bugs.impact: The result is different branch IDs for the BIG-IP system-generated Via header. INVITE is only cancelled on the calling side, while on the called side, the line will ring until time out.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.
bugs.fix: The branch parameter value calculation now remains consistent throughout the connection.

bugs.title: GUI - Server SSL Profile shows irrelevant options when "Server Certificate" is set to "Ignore"
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, the ServerSSL Profile options "Expire Certificate Response Control" and "Untrusted Certificate Response Control" are shown as stand alone options, yet those settings are not honored when the "Server Certificate" option is set to "Ignore" (default).
bugs.conditions: Create server SSL profile with "Server Certificate" option is set to "Ignore" (default). It shows "Expire Certificate Response Control" and "Untrusted Certificate Response Control" options, yet those settings are not honored.
bugs.impact: No functional Impact, it may cause confusion allowing view/modify for irrelevant options.
bugs.workaround: No functional Impact, Expire Certificate Response Control" and "Untrusted Certificate Response Control" options can be ignored when "Server Certificate" option is set to "Ignore" (default).
bugs.fix: "Expire Certificate Response Control" and "Untrusted Certificate Response Control" server SSL profile options are hidden when "Server Certificate" option is set to "Ignore" (default).

bugs.title: Local Traffic Policy on HTTP/2 virtual server no longer matches
bugs.symptoms: Local Traffic Policies may not match properly when a virtual server is handling HTTP/2 traffic.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with Local Traffic Policy and HTTP/2 profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic fails to pass through the virtual server, or fails to be processed as expected.
bugs.workaround: If able, use HTTP rather than HTTP/2. Or disable the policy. Otherwise there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Traffic now processed as expected.

bugs.title: The default value for the syncookie threshold is not set to the correct value
bugs.symptoms: The default value for connection.syncookies.threshold should be set to 64000. Instead, this value defaults to 16384.
bugs.conditions: This issue may be encountered when a virtual server uses syncookies.
bugs.impact: The connection.syncookies.threshold value will be lower than intended, possibly resulting in lower performance.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to manually set the threshold value: # tmsh modify sys db connection.syncookies.threshold value 64000

bugs.title: SSID does not cache fragmented Client Certificates correctly via iRule
bugs.symptoms: The last few bytes of a very large-sized Client Certificate (typically greater than 16,384 bytes) are not cached correctly if the certificate is received fragmented by the SSL Session ID (SSID) parser.
bugs.conditions: -- Client Authentication is enabled. -- A very large Client Certificate is supplied (typically greater than 16,384 bytes). -- SSL Session ID Persistence is enabled. -- The iRule CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT is enabled.
bugs.impact: The client certificate is not stored on the BIG-IP device correctly. The last few bytes are missing.
bugs.workaround: Disable the CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule when SSL Session ID (SSID) persistence is in use. Even though the Client Certificate does not get cached, that is preferable to caching an incorrect client certificate.
bugs.fix: This release supports caching of fragmented client certificates in the SSL Session ID (SSID) persistence feature to properly cache very large-size client certificates (typically exceeding 16,384 bytes).

bugs.title: TS cookie is set on a scenario when it is not needed
bugs.symptoms: A TS cookie arrives with the response.
bugs.conditions: A policy that doesn't have any cookie-related features turned on.
bugs.impact: An unneeded TS cookie arrives with the response. There is no particularly negative effect as a result; just a bit more throughput than might be expected.
bugs.workaround: Although you can remove the unneeded cookies using an iRule, this is not recommended because it is not always clear whether or not specific cookies are used.
bugs.fix: The system no longer issues cookies on a scenario where it is not needed.

bugs.title: MariaDB binary logging takes up disk space
bugs.symptoms: When there is a lot of traffic on BIG-IP machine the DB grows quite fast and reaches max disk partition size. Most of the disk space is occupied by mysqld-bin.00000X files.
bugs.conditions: -- A module that uses MariaDB is provisioned (examples: ASM or AVR). -- Traffic is heavy.
bugs.impact: -- Disk space: DB grows quite fast and reaches max disk partition size. -- Performance.
bugs.workaround: There is no workround at this time.
bugs.fix: MariaDB binary logging disabled.

bugs.title: Client connection with large number of HTTP requests may cause tmm to restart
bugs.symptoms: tmm may restart while processing client request
bugs.conditions: - PingAccess profile is configured on the virtual server. - Client connection sends over 64k HTTP requests that result in BIG-IP's connection to the PingAccess policy server.
bugs.impact: Traffic will be disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Modify HTTP profile used by affected virtual to specify the limit of HTTP requests per connection "maximum requests per connection" to be less then 64k, e.g. 63000 or less.
bugs.fix: Traffic will no longer be disrupted when client sends over 64k uncached requests on the same TCP connection.

bugs.title: Search engine list was updated, and fixing case of multiple entries
bugs.symptoms: Default search engine list does not identify current search engines, and blocks traffic unnecessarily. Part of the issue is that when adding custom search engines, there may be multiple search engines which match the User-Agent header, and this causes the match to fail.
bugs.conditions: Site accessed by search engines.
bugs.impact: Traffic from search engines is blocked unnecessarily.
bugs.workaround: Manually add search engines.
bugs.fix: Search engine list has been updated to reflect current common search engine usage. Also, this version removes the check of multiple search engines, so that now when multiple Search Engines are matched, the Search Engine bypasses the challenges.

bugs.title: Provide an internal parameter to configure allowed empty headers
bugs.symptoms: Some headers are expected to legitimately contain empty values. There is no option to configure this, which is required in order to define which headers may be sent with an empty value without triggering the empty-value violation, while continuing to enforce the violation on all other headers.
bugs.conditions: -- 'HTTP protocol compliance failed' violation: -- 'Header name with no header value' is enabled. -- A request arrives with a header that has no value.
bugs.impact: A legitimate request triggers a violation.
bugs.workaround: Disable 'HTTP protocol compliance failed' violation: 'Header name with no header value'. Important: This workaround reduces general security. An iRule workaround that uses custom violations and looks into empty headers is possible as well, for example: when ASM_REQUEST_DONE { foreach header_name [HTTP::header names] { if {([HTTP::header value $header_name] eq "") && !($header_name eq "my-allowed-empty-header-name")} { log local0.info "raising EMPTY_HEADER_VIOLATION for header $header_name" ASM::raise EMPTY_HEADER_VIOLATION } } }
bugs.fix: Added an internal parameter 'empty_header_value_allowed' that can be configured with a comma-separated list of headers for which an empty value is allowed.
bugs.behavior: This release introduces an internal parameter, 'empty_header_value_allowed', which can be configured with a comma-separated list of headers for which an empty value is allowed.

bugs.title: vcmpd may crash when it is exiting
bugs.symptoms: vcmpd may crash when it is exiting. The system logs an error message similar to the following in /var/log/ltm: err vcmpd[14604]: 01510000:3: Uncaught exception: basic_string::_S_create It's possible that vcmpd will then not start up, logging errors similar to the following in /var/log/ltm: umount(/var/tmstat-vcmp/<guest name>) failed: (16, Device or resource busy
bugs.conditions: vCMP must be in use.
bugs.impact: vcmpd cores, but does so when already exiting. It is possible that vcmpd will then be unable to restart itself, and will need to be manually restarted.
bugs.workaround: If vcmpd cannot restart itself, you can manually restart it by running the following command: tmsh restart sys service vcmpd
bugs.fix: Prevented vcmpd from crashing when exiting.

bugs.title: F5 DNS Relay Proxy service now warns about and clears truncated flag in proxied DNS responses
bugs.symptoms: F5 DNS Relay Proxy service does not support DNS-over-TCP requests, so if, in some configuration, the client resolver decides to use TCP for DNS resolution, this packet is not re-routed/proxied by the DNS Relay Proxy service, and may be causing DNS to be resolved using an incorrect DNS server (where the system decides to send it).
