Typically, if a client receives DNS response with the TC flag set, it retries using TCP. Clearing the TC flag makes client resolver not use TCP at all, preventing DNS packets leakage.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS server responds with TC flag set in DNS response packet. -- Windows only is affected.
bugs.impact: DNS resolution may not work as designed, as the system might send a packet to an incorrect DNS server.
bugs.fix: Now F5 DNS Relay Proxy service clears TC flag in all proxied packets, preventing client DNS resolvers from using TCP. An appropriate log entry is printed into the service's log.

bugs.title: Machine certificate check does not check against all FQDN hostnames
bugs.symptoms: macOS machine can be on multiple networks simultaneously, so it might have multiple hostnames. Machine certificate check does not check against all FQDN hostnames. This causes failure in certain scenarios.
bugs.conditions: -- macOS configuration with multiple hostnames. -- The 'match FQDN with subject alt name. option is specified for machine certificate check.
bugs.impact: Machine cert check might fail.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Previously, with a macOS system that had multiple hostnames, the machine certificate check could not check against all hostnames, causing failures in some scenarios. Now, the machine certificate check compares all hostnames on macOS devices.

bugs.title: Cannot replace a FIPS key with another FIPS key via tmsh
bugs.symptoms: If you try to replace an existing FIPS key using "tmsh install sys crypto key" the command fails with "is already FIPS". This can also occur when issuing the commands via the REST API.
bugs.conditions: If a FIPS key already created/installed via tmsh, it can not be replaced or overwritten via "tmsh install sys crypto" command.
bugs.impact: Fail to overwrite a FIPS key with another FIPS key via tmsh
bugs.fix: With the fix, the user can now use the command to replace or overwrite existing FIPS key with another key.

bugs.title: asmrepro recognizes a BIG-IP version of 13.1.0.1 as 13.1.0 and fails to load a qkview
bugs.symptoms: asmrepro recognizes a BIG-IP version of 13.1.0.1 as 13.1.0 and fails to load a qkview.
bugs.conditions: Try to deploy a qkview on a BIG-IP using the asmrepro tool while BIG-IP has a 4 element version like 13.1.0.1.
bugs.impact: Cannot deploy a 4 element version qkview on a BIG-IP using the asmrepro tool.
bugs.fix: asmrepro now handles the version number properly.

bugs.title: GUI slow with large number of entries in network firewall address list
bugs.symptoms: With 20,000 ip addresses in the network firewall address list, the GUI response(IE) when accessing the address list is slow to unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: When the network firewall address list has many entries eg.20000.
bugs.impact: Address list page becomes unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh
bugs.fix: Limit GUI view of address list to show first 100 entries, with a link at the bottom to go to a page to view all members of list.

bugs.title: B2250 blades may lose efficiency when source ports form an arithmetic sequence.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic imbalance between tmm threads. You might see the traffic imbalance by running the following command: tmsh show sys tmm-traffic
bugs.conditions: Source ports used to connect to B2250 blade form an arithmetic sequence. For example, some servers always use randomly selected even source port numbers. This means the 'stride' of the ports selected is '2'. Because a sorted list of the ports yields a list like 2, 4, 6, 8… 32002, 32004. It is 'striding' over the odd ports; thus, a port stride of 2.
bugs.impact: Traffic imbalance between tmm threads may result in sub-optimal performance.
bugs.workaround: Randomize source ports when connecting via a BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: This release introduces a new variable mhdag.pu.table.size.multiplier. Setting it to 2 or 3 mitigates the issue.
bugs.behavior: This release introduces a new variable to mitigate this issue: mhdag.pu.table.size.multiplier. You must set the variable to 2 or 3 on the host, and then restart tmm on all host blades and then all guests to mitigate the issue.

bugs.title: fipskey.nethsm is now deprecated
bugs.symptoms: Because tmsh commands for SafeNet HSMs have reached parity with fipskey.nethsm, the BIG-IP software is deprecating fipskey.nethsm beginning in this release. fipskey.nethsm no longer works on SafeNet HSMs. It continues to work on Thales HSMs, but with a warning that it will stop working soon.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure the BIG-IP system to work with an external nethsm. -- Use a workflow or script that references fipskey.nethsm with a SafeNet HSM or Thales HSM.
bugs.impact: Workflows and scripts that use fipskey.nethsm with a SafeNet HSM will no longer work, and workflows and user scripts with a Thales HSM will now receive a warning when they use fipskey.nethsm.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh instead of fipskey.nethsm.
bugs.fix: fipskey.nethsm is now deprecated because the tmsh commands have reached feature parity with it.
bugs.behavior: fipskey.nethsm no longer works with SafeNet HSMs, and warns that Thales will be deprecated very soon.

bugs.title: tmm SIGFPE 'valid node'
bugs.symptoms: A rare TMM crash with tmm SIGFPE 'valid node' may occur if the host is unreachable.
bugs.conditions: The host is unreachable.
bugs.impact: Lack of stability on the device. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This fix handles a rare TMM crash when the host is unreachable.

bugs.title: VDisk Migration Doesn't Log Information About Failures
bugs.symptoms: When a vdisk migration fails the cause is unknown.
bugs.conditions: When users choose to move a vdisk on a multi blade chassis running vcmp.
bugs.impact: The cause of the failure will be unknown and users won't know what to do.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Software syncookies without TCP TS improperly include TCP options that are not encoded
bugs.symptoms: When sending a software syncookie and there is no TCP timestamp option, tmm sends back TCP options like window scaling (WS), sackOK, etc. The values for these options are encoded in the timestamp field which is not sent. When the final ACK of the 3WHS arrives (without a timestamp), there is no way to know that the BIG-IP system negotiated the use of SACK, WS and other options that were encoded in the timestamp. This will leave the client believing that options are enabled and the BIG-IP believing that they are not.
bugs.conditions: TCP timestamps are disabled by the client, or in the TCP profile.
bugs.impact: In one known case, the client was Windows 7 which apparently disables timestamps by default. Users might experience poor connection performance because the client believed it was using WS, and that the BIG-IP system would scale up the advertised window. However, the BIG-IP system does not using WS in this case, and used the window size from the TCP header directly, causing the BIG-IP system to send small packets (believing it had filled the window) and wait for a response.
bugs.workaround: Specifically prevent the WS issue by lowering the send_buffer_size and receive_window_size to less than or equal to 65535.
bugs.fix: Added dependency between the window scale option and the timestamp option in a SYN/ACK response.

bugs.title: GUI Network Map objects in subfolders are not being shown
bugs.symptoms: Objects created in subfolders under a partition are not showing up in the GUI Network Map when selecting the partition.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a virtual server under a subfolder. -- View Network Map while /Common is the active partition. For example: 1. Create a subfolder such as /Common/subfolder. 2. In that subfolder, create a virtual server such as /Common/subfolder/virtualserver1. 3. Select /Common as the partition. 4. View the Network Map. The virtual server /Common/subfolder/virtualServer1 is not shown on the Network Map.
bugs.impact: Cannot see the objects in the subfolder.
bugs.workaround: Select the partition 'All[Read Only]' to see all objects in subfolders.

bugs.title: sod is unable to handle the maximum (127) allowable traffic groups if there are 8 devices in the DG
bugs.symptoms: sod consumes excessive amount of CPU time, and the traffic-group Active and Next-Active locations do not stabilize.
bugs.conditions: When the number of devices in the failover device group or the number of traffic groups is large. The limit varies by platform capacity, but any Device Service Cluster with more than 4 devices or more than 32 traffic groups can experience this issue.
bugs.impact: If the Active location is unstable, traffic will not be processed correctly. Excessive CPU consumption and network traffic interferes with other control plane functions including the UI.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: sod now handles network traffic more efficiently and limits network traffic to minimize interference with other components.

bugs.title: vADC: default gateway route required, lasthop kernel module removed
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE), connections to the management interface may fail if an explicit management route is not defined for it or was not learned from DHCP. This may prevent clients that previously managed VE from being able to do so after an upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- Inbound connections to VE over the management interface (SSH, SNMP, etc.). -- A suitable management route is not present.
bugs.impact: Clients that could previously connect to the management interface may be unable to do so after an upgrade if they never configured a suitable management route or one was not acquired by DHCP.
bugs.workaround: Configure suitable management routes or learn them via DHCP. VE will still be accessible via systems on its locally connected network segment and via the management console.
bugs.fix: Inbound connections using the management interface now require explicit route definitions.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP VE no longer supplies the 'lasthop' Linux kernel module. Inbound connections using the management interface now require explicit route definitions.

bugs.title: DNAT performance drops up to 50% when a second blade is added
bugs.symptoms: When a second blade is added to a chassis, excessive memory and CPU utilization may be observed.
bugs.conditions: A high number of concurrent connections using a LSN pool configured in deterministic mode.
bugs.impact: Fewer concurrent connections are supported in a two bladed system then when using a single blade.

bugs.title: Better detecting browser extentsions
bugs.symptoms: Browser extensions are not always detected
bugs.conditions: enabling "Web Scraping -> Suspicious Clients -> Detect browsers with Scraping Extensions", and choosing disallowed extensions.
bugs.impact: Browsers with disallowed extensions are not blocked.
bugs.fix: Improving browser extensions detection.

bugs.title: BD restart on a device where 'provision.tmmcountactual' is set to a non-default value
bugs.symptoms: BD restarts with this error: Plugin configuration load timeout. Exiting.
bugs.conditions: The db variable 'provision.tmmcountactual' is set to a number lower than the actual CPU count.
bugs.impact: BD restarts continuously.
bugs.workaround: You can use any of these workarounds: -- In the GUI, set 'RWThreads' under Security :: Options : Application Security : Advanced Configuration : System Variables. -- Use the 'add_del_internal' utility: ---------------------- # /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal USAGE: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add <param_name> <param_value> [--default <default_value>] /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal update <param_name> <param_value> [--default <default_value>] /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal delete <param_name> ---------------------- -- Set the bd internal parameter num_rw_threads to the amount of plugin channels that TMM expects. -- Revert 'provision.tmmcountactual' sys db to the default value.

bugs.title: Tcl actions not run if conditions have overlapping IP ranges
bugs.symptoms: Overlapping CIDR subnets in rule's condition cause unexpected result.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy with more than one IP-address-based condition. -- The IP address ranges overlap. -- An associated action that invokes a Tcl command.
bugs.impact: Tcl action is not run.

bugs.title: Requests do not appear in local logging due to rare file descriptor exhaustion
bugs.symptoms: In an extremely rare circumstance, requests do not appear in local logging due to file descriptor exhaustion in asmlogd.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM configured. -- ASM policy with an associated 'Log all requests' logging profile. -- Requests sent to virtual server. -- View Request Log.
bugs.impact: Requests do not appear in local logging.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM, or pkill -f asmlogd.
bugs.fix: Requests appear in local logging correctly.

bugs.title: SNMP memory leak may exhaust memory
bugs.symptoms: If an SNMP walk of the MIB causes any data to be leaked and is repeated continuously then it can exhaust memory. This is known to be an issue when the request-id issued by the client is 0. There may be other conditions in which the request/reply exchange leaks.
bugs.conditions: A configuration which when queried causes the snmpd subagent to leak PDU memory.
bugs.impact: The subagent will use too much memory and fail on an allocation and restart.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time. We have not been able to reproduce this failure and valgrind reports to date do not point to any specific code path errors except with 0 request ids.

bugs.title: User is not able to reset their Active Directory password
bugs.symptoms: When Active Directory is used for authenticating APM users and the user is required to change password on next APM logon, APM fails to update the password.
bugs.conditions: - APM is licensed and provisioned - Active Directory is used for authenticating the users - When logging on to APM, user is asked to change the password
bugs.impact: User is not able to change the password.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: APM end users can now successfully reset the password.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 now provides a way to inspect stream reset causes.
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP/2 protocol multiplexes multiple streams in a single connection. If a stream aborts, the connection might not. The HTTP/2 protocol condenses the reset cause into a single 4-byte integer, which is not enough to determine the real reason for the stream aborting. This makes debugging issues with HTTP/2 difficult.
bugs.conditions: A HTTP/2 stream aborts for any reason.
bugs.impact: The debugging of virtual servers that use HTTP/2 is more difficult.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When HTTP/2 streams abort, the reset cause may be recorded in the stats, if desired. This is configured using the normal rstcause configuration mechanisms. A BigDB var has been added: Tmm.HTTP2.sendrstwhy. If set to 'true' and an HTTP/2 stream aborts, the BIG-IP system sends an HTTP/2 frame containing reset cause information. The frame is of type '0xf5' = 245.

bugs.title: ProxySSL does not work properly with Extended Master Secret and OCSP
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake fails if the BIG-IP system is operating in ProxySSL mode, while client and server negotiate to use the Extended Master Secret and OCSP features together.
bugs.conditions: 1. Virtual server is configured to work in ProxySSL mode. 2. Client and server negotiate the SSL handshake with the Extended Master Secret. 3. Client and Server negotiate to use the OCSP.
bugs.impact: ProxySSL does not work properly with Extended Master Secret and OCSP simultaneously.
bugs.fix: Included the certificate status message in the calculation of Extended Master Secret.

bugs.title: With auto-lasthop enabled tmm accepts traffic from invalid addresses
bugs.symptoms: Tmm accepts traffic from incorrect source addresses: - 127.0.0.0/8 - 0.0.0.0/8
bugs.conditions: Auto-lasthop enabled.
bugs.impact: RFC6890 violation. Note: This is not a vulnerability, as traffic is getting returned to the lasthop populated via auto-lasthop. Therefore, no traffic is reaching the host; it is only an RFC violation.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate this issue, use the following packet filter: net packet-filter /Common/drop_local { action discard order 5 rule "( src net 0.0.0.0/8 or src net 127.0.0.0/8 )" }
bugs.fix: TMM drops traffic from incorrect source addresses: - 127.0.0.0/8 - 0.0.0.0/8

bugs.title: SSL memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: In some instances random memory can be corrupted causing TMM core.
bugs.conditions: SSL is configured (either client-ssl or server-ssl) and SNI is used to select a non-default profile.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, disrupting traffic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The memory corruption issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Two-way iQuery connections fail to get established between GTM devices with the same address on different networks connected through address translation
bugs.symptoms: Two GTM devices that have the same local IP address are not able to establish an iQuery connection, even when a translated address is configured.
bugs.conditions: This condition may occur if two GTM servers have the same self IP address on separate networks that are attempting to use address translation to establish a connection.
bugs.impact: When one or more GTM devices attempt to establish an iQuery connection to another device, it actually establishes a connection with itself instead of the other device.
bugs.workaround: To resolve the issue, 1. Configure the devices to have different self IP addresses. 2. Change the addresses and translated addresses of the corresponding GTM servers to match the new configuration using the following example command: tmsh modify gtm server <server_name> addresses ...
bugs.fix: You can now mitigate this issue by setting a variable to the name of the configured device that matches the local machine using a command similar to the following example: tmsh modify sys db gtm.selfdevicename value <device_name> If those values match and the two GTM servers are configured with different data centers, then a proper connection between devices can be established using address translation.

bugs.title: An incorrect data manipulation in cipher encrypt and decrypt could cause TMM crash with SIGABRT
bugs.symptoms: TMM receives SIGABRT from failover daemon, sod, due to heartbeat failure shortly after TMM starts up.
bugs.conditions: In some rare scenarios, TCP fast open encrypt/decrypt key may not be properly initialized when traffic comes into the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Multiple TMM threads can get into a loop, causing heartbeat failure. TMM restarts, Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The incorrect data manipulation in cipher encrypt and decrypt has been fixed.

bugs.title: RADIUS authentication requests erroneously specify NAS-IP-Address of 127.0.0.1
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS requests from BIG-IP have attribute NAS-IP-Address = 127.0.0.1, which might cause authentication to fail. The NAS-IP-Address is essentially the resource an end user client is trying to authenticate to. This is typically the management IP address of the BIG-IP system, but the BIG-IP system always sends 127.0.0.1 instead. That might fail or it might work, depending on how the server is configured.
bugs.conditions: This is an issue for all RADIUS authentication requests that use the attribute NAS-IP-Address. Note: This affects remote control plane authentication only, not APM or other uses of RADIUS.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system always sends 127.0.0.1 instead of the BIG-IP system's management IP address. RADIUS server might not service the request, so authentication fails.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: TMM core when using MPTCP
bugs.symptoms: When MPTCP is enabled on a virtual server, TMM may generate a core file and restart.
bugs.conditions: MPTCP must be in use.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: Disable MPTCP.
bugs.fix: Prevented TMM core.

bugs.title: Server health significantly increases during DoSL7 TPS prevention
bugs.symptoms: Mitigation of DoSL7 TPS affects server health value.
bugs.conditions: -- DoSL7 TPS configured together with BADOS. -- DoSL7 TPS is active.
bugs.impact: -- Incorrect Server Health reporting. -- Might activate Behavioral DoS (BADoS) false-attack detection when attacks mitigated by DoSL7 TPS are stopped.
bugs.fix: Server health now displays the actual backend server state, and does not incorrectly grow.

bugs.title: LTM v12.1.2: Static BFD with BIG-IP floating IP address
bugs.symptoms: In a HA configuration BFD session on both Active and Standby nodes can be configured with the same floating Self IP as a source IP address. This ends up with both Active and Standby nodes to actively send BFD Control packets to BFD neighbor. Responses from BFD neighbor are delivered to the Active node only. In effect not only the state of the session mismatches on Active and Standby node, also BFD Control packets send different information that disturbs the session.
bugs.conditions: - BFD sessions on HA Active and Standby have the same floating Self IP as a source IP address.
bugs.impact: BFD session gets disturbed both on HA Active node and BFD neighbor that might end up with invalidation of the route to the BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Workaround can be to manually disable BFD session on Standby node, however on failover the session would need to be manually restored. Other workaround can be to use non-floating Self IP as a source IP address of BFD Control packets, this however might require some additional logic on the BFD neighbor side.
bugs.fix: BFD session that uses a floating Self IP as a source IP address are now suspended on the Standby node in HA configuration. On failover the session is restored. In effect the BFD Control packets are sent only from one HA node - the Active one. On failover short flap might occur, as session states are not synchronized across HA pair.

bugs.title: failed configuration deletion may cause unwanted bd exit
bugs.symptoms: Immediately after the deletion of a configuration fails, bd exists.
bugs.conditions: When deleting a configuration fails.
bugs.impact: Unwanted bd restart.
bugs.fix: bd will exit upon a failed configuration only when configured to exit on failure.

bugs.title: If /config/BigDB.dat is empty or the file is corrupt, mcpd continuously restarts
bugs.symptoms: If an issue causes /config/BigDB.dat to be empty or its contents become corrupted, mcpd fails to start up. System commands report errors about being unable to read DB keys. 'bigstart' outputs errors: --dbval: Unable to find variable: [security.commoncriteria]
bugs.conditions: The event causing BigDB.dat to be truncated is unknown at this time.
bugs.impact: The system fails to start up, and mcpd continually restarts. The BIG-IP system fails to process traffic while the mcpd process is restarting.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can remove the empty or corrupted BigDB.dat file. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: Performing the following procedure should not have a negative impact on your system. 1. Log in to bash. 2. To remove the zero-byte or corrupted BigDB.dat file, type the following command: rm /config/BigDB.dat

bugs.title: qkview will not collect files greater than 2 GB
bugs.symptoms: Due to a limitation of the file compression library employed by qkview, it cannot collect files greater than 2 gb in size. qkview will abort when encountering such a file, and not produce a resulting qkview file.
bugs.conditions: A file exists in a directory that qkview normally collects.
bugs.impact: No qkview diagnostics file is created.
bugs.workaround: Remove the file greater than 2gb in size.

bugs.title: Configuration may not load or not accept vlan or tunnel names as "default" or "all"
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue, configurations containing vlan or tunnels named "default" or "all" are no longer accepted.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure this will result in a log message similar to the following: root@(f5-ve)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# create net tunnels tunnel default profile ppp 01070712:3: Cannot create tunnel 'default' in rd1 - ioctl failed: Invalid argument
bugs.impact: A configuration that contained this in earlier versions and upgraded to the affected version will fail to load.
bugs.workaround: Change or rename all instances of vlans and/or tunnels named "default" or "all"

bugs.title: HSB transmitter failure due to watchdog loopback failure
bugs.symptoms: An HSB transmitter failure is reported in the TMM logs. Under normal operation, software has an HSB watchdog that sends and receives a loopback packet. Under some unknown conditions, software fails to receive the loopback packet from the HSB. The following error messages are seen in the TMM logs: -- notice hsb0: failed to transmit loopback packet No.1 with error 2. (ERR_BUF) -- notice ring0: rx_prod_idx 00ba rx_cons_idx 00aa tx_prod_idx 0acf tx_cons_idx 0ace -- notice fsc_tx0: sw_cons 4acc hw_cons 6ace hw_prod_written 4acf hw_prod 4acf mask 0fff ... -- notice *** TMM 0 - PDE 0 - transmitter failure ***
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: An HSB lockup is detected, resulting in a nic_failsafe reboot.

bugs.title: SSL handshake fails for OCSP, TLS false start, and SSL hardware acceleration configured
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake fails if the client initiates the handshake with TLS false start (specifically, client SSL sends the SSL record data to the server before the Server sends out the CSS is FINISHED notification).
bugs.conditions: 1. Client initiates the SSL handshake with False Start. 2. The BIG-IP system has SSL hardware acceleration enabled (which is default for for non-virtual edition (VE) versions).
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends the RST to tear down the connection in TLS false start.
bugs.workaround: There are no true workarounds. You must disable one of the conditions to workaround the issue: -- Disable TLS False Start. (Note: this might not be feasible because it needs to be done on all clients.) -- Disable SSL acceleration. -- Disable AES-GCM ciphers in the client SSL profile. Without AES-GCM, clients do not try to use TLS false start and still be able to use (EC)DHE.
bugs.fix: The system no longer processes application data before verifying that the finished message arrives and handshake is complete.

bugs.title: DNS Security Logs report Drop action for unhandled rejected DNS queries
bugs.symptoms: DNS Security Logs report Drop action for unhandled rejected DNS queries.
bugs.conditions: DNS profile set unhandled-query-action reject.
bugs.impact: Incorrect event log. This is an incorrectly logged event and doe not indicate an issue with the system

bugs.title: Static member of pool with FQDN members may revert to user-disabled after being re-enabled
bugs.symptoms: Within an LTM pool containing both FQDN members and members configured with static IP addresses; a statically-configured member that had been disabled (session = user-disabled) and then re-enabled (session = user-enabled) may become disabled again after making other changes affecting the state of other FQDN members of the pool.
bugs.conditions: This may occur under the following conditions: - An LTM pool containing a mix of FQDN and statically-configured members. - A statically-configured pool member is disabled (session = user-disabled) and then re-enabled (session = user-enabled). - Other changes occur which affect the availability of FQDN pool members. For example, if a route to an FQDN pool member is deleted and recreated, a previously-disabled statically-configured member may revert to a disabled state. Depending on circumstances, the issue may only occur once after BIG-IP, TMM, bigd, or a related daemon restarts.
bugs.impact: A pool member may be unexpectedly disabled after being re-enabled, and thus would not receive traffic.
bugs.workaround: It may be possible to work around this issue by disabling and re-enabling the statically-configured pool member again.
bugs.fix: Statically-configured pool members of a pool that also contains FQDN members remain enabled after being manually disabled then re-enabled. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: GUI resets custom Certificate Key Chain in child client SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, editing a client SSL profile or selecting a different parent profile changes the Certificate Key Chain to default (i.e., /Common/default.crt and /Common/default.key).
bugs.conditions: This happens in the following scenario: 1. Using the GUI, create a client SSL profile. 2. Configure the new profile to inherit from a client SSL profile other than the default, clientssl. 3. Click the Custom box for Certificate Key Chain and select a different cert and key from the default. 4. Click Update. 5. In the GUI, change any setting in the newly created profile, or select a different parent profile (but not the clientssl profile). 6. Click Update again.
bugs.impact: The system resets Certificate Key Chain to default, even though the Custom box is checked.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue in the GUI, click the Custom checkbox next to the 'Certificate Key Chain' option in the parent profile. This will set the value of inherit-certkeychain to false , preventing the issue from occurring. You can also use tmsh to update parent profile settings to avoid the occurrence of this issue..
bugs.fix: GUI no longer resets custom Certificate Key Chain in child client SSL profiles.

bugs.title: Crash in bcm56xxd during TMM failover
bugs.symptoms: During a TMM failover, such as after an upgrade to a later version of software, bcm56xxd might crash.
bugs.conditions: TMM failover.
bugs.impact: Restart of bcm56xxd; temporary loss of network connectivity.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Bcm56xxd no longer crashes and restarts on a TMM failover.

bugs.title: Session variables in Requested Authentication Context Class in SP do not get resolved when Authentication Request is generated by BIG-IP as SP.
bugs.symptoms: Session variables in Requested Authentication Context Class in SP do not get resolved when Authentication Request is generated by the BIG-IP system as SP. They are sent as is. This is a behavior change from v12.1.2/v12.1.3/v13.0.0, where, the value gets substituted in the SP's AuthnRequest sent to IDP.
bugs.conditions: On configuring Requested Authentication Context Class in SP to define a session variable similar to the following: %{session.client.type}
bugs.impact: The generated Authentication Request does not have the session variable resolved. The string is sent as is. The Authentication Request fails and the session cannot be established.
bugs.fix: The system now resolves the session variable in the configured Authentication Context Class for SP while generating the Authentication Request.

bugs.title: Non-TCP and non-FastL4 virtual server with rate-limits may periodically stop sending packets to server when rate exceeded
bugs.symptoms: TMM may periodically stop sending packets to the server for a few seconds when the configured virtual server rate-limited value is exceeded.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual configured with rate-limit. -- Uses a UDP profile (i.e., not using TCP or FastL4). -- The idle-timeout is set to immediate.
bugs.impact: The virtual server might intermittently stop sending packets to the pool member server for a few seconds.
bugs.fix: UDP rate-limited virtual server now correctly sends packets to the server.

bugs.title: MBLB rate-limited virtual server periodically stops sending packets to the server for a few seconds
bugs.symptoms: Applying rate-limiting to MBLB SIP or Diameter virtual servers might cause the virtual server to periodically stop sending packets to the pool member server for a few seconds.
bugs.conditions: -- MBLB SIP or Diameter virtual server. -- Rate-limited is applied.
bugs.impact: The virtual server might intermittently stop sending packets to the pool member server for a few seconds.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: MBLB rate-limited virtual server now correctly sends packets to the server.

bugs.title: Fragmented ICMP forwarded with incorrect icmp checksum
bugs.symptoms: Large fragmented ICMP packets that traverse the BIG-IP might have their source or destination IP addresses changed and transmitted with the checksum incorrectly calculated.
bugs.conditions: A FastL4 virtual server able to transmit ICMP frames (ip-protocol ICMP or any), or SNAT/NAT only when a fragmented ICMP packet is received and is expected to be passed through the virtual server (or SNAT or NAT).
bugs.impact: Large ICMP echo packets (greater than MTU) will be dropped by the recipient due to the checksum error. No echo response will be seen.
bugs.workaround: Turn on IP fragment reassembly on the FastL4 profile associated with the virtual server.

bugs.title: Potential mcpd memory leak for signed iRules
bugs.symptoms: There is an MCP memory leak that occurs when th message "Signature encryption failed" is seen in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: Signing of iRules must be in use. Signature encryption must be problematic.
bugs.impact: MCP leak memory.
bugs.workaround: Resolve the signature encryption issue.
bugs.fix: Fixed memory leak.

bugs.title: memory leak in Machine Certificate Check agent of the apmd process
bugs.symptoms: apmd process leaks memory in Machine Certificate Check agent
bugs.conditions: Machine Certificate Check agent is configured in an Access Policy
bugs.impact: apmd may grow in size. this may lead to apmd process or some other processes at BIG-IP to be killed by OOM-killer
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The memory leak is fixed.

bugs.title: apmd may leak memory on destroying kerberos cache
bugs.symptoms: ampd leaks memory in AD Query agent.
bugs.conditions: The leak happens on either: 1. A kerberos cache reset is requested (any of the caches - GROUP/PSO/KERBEROS). OR 2. Any changes to associated AAA AD Server were made and new Access Policy is applied. OR 3. AD Query was not able to make ldap_bind to KDC and the error is NOT a timeout (e.g. invalid administrator password).
bugs.impact: The ampd leaks memory and may cause unstable behavior. The apmd process, or some other daemon may be killed by OOM killer when it tries to allocate memory.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After fix, there is no leak in AD Query agent of the apmd process.

bugs.title: apmd leaks memory when updating Access V2 policy
bugs.symptoms: A small leak occurs in the apmd process when processing mcp notifications about configuration updates.
bugs.conditions: -- Changing an Access Policy configurations. -- apmd receives a notification about it.
bugs.impact: apmd grows in size very slowly. The issue does not have any immediate and significant impact on BIG-IP system functionality.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: apmd no longer leaks a small amount when processing MCP notifications.

bugs.title: JS Injection into cached HTML response causes TCP RST on the fictive URLs
bugs.symptoms: TCP RST being sent when a browser requests a fictive URL that starts with either of the following strings: -- /TSPD/xxx...xxx?type=x -- /TSbd/xxx...xxx?type=x.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in either of the following scenarios: -- ASM policy is attached to a virtual server, and any of the following is enabled: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), Web Scraping/Single Page Application/AJAX Blocking internal. -- DoS profile with Single Page Application enabled is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: CSRF/Web Scraping/Single Page Application/AJAX Blocking page features might not work. This happens intermittently when the back-end server's HTML page (the one where the fictive URL is injected) is cached in the browser for more than two days.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to disable caching for HTML pages where a fictive URL is injected.
bugs.fix: The system now disables cached headers to HTML responses where a fictive URL is injected.

bugs.title: SSO-enabled native RDP resources cannot be launched from APM Webtop with Mac RDP client 10.x
bugs.symptoms: Mac RDP client 10.x shows credentials prompt when SSO-enabled native RDP resource is launched from the APM Webtop. If the user enters credentials manually, the RDP client will display an error message.
bugs.conditions: -- Mac RDP client is of version 10.x (e.g., 10.1.6). -- Native RDP resource is assigned to the webtop. -- SSO is enabled on the RDP Resource.
bugs.impact: RDP resource cannot be launched.
bugs.workaround: Add the following to 'Custom Parameters' of SSO-enabled RDP resources: full address:s:%{session.server.network.name} promptcredentialonce:i:1
bugs.fix: SSO-enabled native RDP resources now can be launched from APM Webtop with Mac RDP client 10.2.0.

bugs.title: qkview upload to ihealth fails or unable to untar qkview file
bugs.symptoms: qkview upload to ihealth fails unable to untar qkview file.
bugs.conditions: When qkview file is untarred, it creates a same directory name in loop as below and fails to untar successfully. .../dir1/ .../dir1/dir1/ .../dir1/dir1/dir1/ ... This happens due to dangling symlink dir1 which points to nothing. [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # ls -l /config/bigip/auth/pam.d/dir1 lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root 64 2018-01-30 08:56 /config/bigip/auth/pam.d/dir1 -> [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # stat /config/bigip/auth/pam.d/dir1 File: `/config/bigip/auth/pam.d/dir1' -> `' Size: 64 Blocks: 8 IO Block: 4096 symbolic link Device: fd16h/64790d Inode: 112045 Links: 1 Access: (0777/lrwxrwxrwx) Uid: ( 0/ root) Gid: ( 0/ root) Access: 2018-01-30 08:56:20.000000000 -0800 Modify: 2018-01-30 08:56:20.000000000 -0800 Change: 2018-01-31 08:39:35.000000000 -0800 [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config #
bugs.impact: Unable to untar qkview or qkview upload to ihealth fails.
bugs.workaround: Identify the dangling symlink and delete. Then generate qkview or use ihealth to generate qkview and upload to ihealth.
bugs.fix: Qkview tool will identify dangling symlink and handle safely to avoid looping.

bugs.title: Unnecessary file recovery_db/conf.tar.gz consumes /var disk space
bugs.symptoms: A file, /ts/var/install/recovery_db/conf.tar.gz ,is saved unnecessarily during UCS file save, and consumes /var disk space.
bugs.conditions: UCS file is saved.
bugs.impact: The /var filesystem can become full; this may degrade system performance over time, and can eventually lead to traffic disruptions.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete /ts/var/install/recovery_db/conf.tar.
bugs.fix: Unnecessary file recovery_db/conf.tar.gz is no longer written.

bugs.title: Memory leak in ASM-config Event Dispatcher upon continuous Policy Builder restart
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstance, when Policy Builder restarts continuously (in response to a different issue in which there are many shmem segments allocated and used by tmm), ASM-config Event Dispatcher memory usage grows uncontrollably.
bugs.conditions: In rare circumstances, Policy Builder restarts continuously (in response to a different issue in which there are many shmem segments allocated and used by tmm).
bugs.impact: ASM-config Event Dispatcher memory usage grows continuously until the device eventually fails over.
bugs.workaround: Restart asm_config_server on all devices using the following command: killall asm_config_server.pl
bugs.fix: ASM-config Event Dispatcher memory usage remains stable even upon multiple Policy Builder restarts.

bugs.title: new command-line tools (curl and nghttp) added
bugs.symptoms: This is an enhancement; new networking diagnostic tools are available.
bugs.impact: troubleshooting HTTP2 connectivity is easier
bugs.fix: Command-line tools have been updated to support HTTP/2. See 'man curl' and 'man nghttp' for details.

bugs.title: Setting log.ivs.level or log-config filter level to informational causes crash
bugs.symptoms: Certain log messages for internal virtual server (IVS) at 'informational' log level, cause TMM to crash when they are logged. The messages are logged at the end of an HTTP transaction to or from an IVS.
bugs.conditions: Information level logging enabled: - sys db log.ivs.level informational or - log-config filter level set to info A transaction that passes HTTP to/from an internal virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts, causing loss of connections.
bugs.workaround: Avoid setting log.ivs.level to 'informational' or higher level and/ log-config filter level to 'info' or higher. By default the level is 'error' which does not trigger the bug.
bugs.fix: Informational messages for internal virtual server (IVS) are logged as expected and TMM does not crash.

bugs.title: Certain virtual address route-advertisement settings break upgrades from 13.0.0 hotfix rollups
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading from a version of 13.0.0 other than the base build may result in failure depending on the values of the virtual address route-advertisement setting. If set to "selective", "any", or "all", the configuration will fail to load after the upgrade with an error similar to the following example in the /var/log/ltm file: load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- Loading schema version: 13.0.0 Syntax Error:(/config/bigip.conf at line: 1790) invalid property value "route-advertisement":"selective"
bugs.conditions: - Upgrading from a version of 13.0.0 other than the base (i.e. HF1 or later). - Upgrading to 13.1.0 or later. - At least one virtual address with its route-advertisement value set to "selective", "any", or "all".
bugs.impact: Configuration will not load. If the unit being upgraded is a stand-alone unit, this will result in a traffic outage.
bugs.workaround: If you become aware of this issue prior to upgrading: 1. Note any virtual address route-advertisement settings that are "selective", "any", or "all". 2. Change all of these values to either "enabled" or "disabled" (note that this will change their route advertisement behavior temporarily). 3. Perform the upgrade. The goal of this step is to have the BIG-IP system perform an installation while carrying forward the new, modified configuration. Note that if your chosen destination (i.e. HD1.3) already exists and contains the very software you want to install (i.e. 13.1.1.2), then you must first delete the destination before you can re-use it. This is because, by design, the BIG-IP system will not perform an installation if the desired software is already present in the destination boot location. Attempting such an installation would just result in the BIG-IP system immediately rebooting to activate that boot location, without performing any installation and thus defeating the point of this workaround. 4. Once the upgrade completes, change the route advertisement settings back to their original values. If you become aware of this issue after the upgrade has already failed: 1. Boot back into the old/working boot location. 2. Delete the boot location containing the failed installation. 3. Follow the procedure detailed under "If you become aware of this issue prior to upgrading".
bugs.fix: Upgrades from 13.0.0 hotfix rollups involving certain virtual address route-advertisement settings no longer fail.

bugs.title: DHCP configured domain-name-servers unavailable after reboot when there are more than two domain-name servers in the lease.
bugs.symptoms: DHCP-configured domain-name-servers (DNS) unavailable after reboot when there are more than two domain-name-servers in the lease.
bugs.conditions: - DHCP is enabled on the mgmt interface. - DHCP server provides more than 2 domain-name-servers in its lease.
bugs.impact: Name resolution on mgmt interface fails due to misconfiguration in DNS information for mgmt interface.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release corrects the handling of multiple DNS name-servers.

bugs.title: machine certificate check crash for 'match issuer' configuration on macOS Sierra 10.12.6
bugs.symptoms: Machine certificate check crashes a Mac BIG-IP Edge Client running on macOS Sierra 10.12.6 (16G29) when 'match issuer' is specified in the configuration.
bugs.conditions: - Machine certificate check configured for with 'match issuer' configuration. - macOS Sierra 10.12.6 (16G29). - BIG-IP Edge client. - F5 EPI.
bugs.impact: Machine certificate check does not pass because Edge client crashes.
bugs.fix: Machine certificate check now completes successfully using the Mac BIG-IP Edge Client running on macOS Sierra 10.12.6 (16G29) when 'match issuer' is specified in the configuration.

bugs.title: Non-URL encoded links to CSS files are not stripped from the response during concatenation
bugs.symptoms: Non-URL encoded links to CSS files are not stripped from the response during concatenation.
bugs.conditions: White space in the URLs.
bugs.impact: As above.
bugs.workaround: No workaround at this time.

bugs.title: ASM REST: Missing DB Cleanup for some tables
bugs.symptoms: Finished REST tasks that are not deleted by the client that initiated them are meant to be cleaned periodically. Certain tasks are not included in this cleanup job.
bugs.conditions: The following tasks are not reaped automatically if left uncleaned by the REST client that initiated them: From 13.0.x: -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/apply-server-technologies -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/bulk -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/export-policy-template -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/export-requests -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/import-policy-template From 13.1.0: -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/export-data-protection -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/import-data-protection -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/import-certificate -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/policy-diff -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/policy-merge -- /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/update-enforcer
bugs.impact: DB space usage grows with each ASM REST task that is not cleaned up.
bugs.workaround: REST Clients that initiate tasks can delete them after verifying the task has reached a final state.
bugs.fix: REST tasks left behind are now be pruned by the DB Cleanup process.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 can garble large headers
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP/2 filter may incorrectly encode large headers.
bugs.conditions: A header that encodes to larger than 2048 bytes may be incorrectly encoded.
bugs.impact: The garbled header may no longer conform to the HPACK spec, and cause the connection to be dropped. The garbled header may be correctly formed, but contain incorrect data.
bugs.fix: The HTTP/2 filter correctly encodes large HTTP headers.

bugs.title: RADIUS and SecurID Auth fails with empty password
bugs.symptoms: If password value is empty, the following error message will be logged in /var/log/apm: err apmd[14259]: 014902f0:3: /Common/profile_name:Common:eb69a5gd: RADIUS Agent: Failed to read Password Source session variable:
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when following conditions are met: - RADIUS or SecurID auth agent is included in the access policy. - Empty password value is used for authentication.
bugs.impact: User may not be authenticated.
bugs.workaround: - Add variable assignment agent before RADIUS/SecurID auth agent in the access policy. - Set 'session.logon.last.password' (or whatever password source is used for authentication) to a random value.
bugs.fix: RADIUS/SecurID auth agent allows empty password value for authentication.

bugs.title: Memory leak in TMSH load sys config
bugs.symptoms: When loading a configuration, either through tmsh load sys config or the corresponding iControl REST command, the TMSH or icrd_child processes can leak memory.
bugs.conditions: When configuration is loaded via TMSH or iControl REST.
bugs.impact: The TMSH process memory or icrd_child process memory continues to grow every time the config is loaded.
bugs.workaround: If memory consumption grows in the TMSH process, restart the TMSH process. If memory consumption grows in iControl REST, restart the REST service using the following command: bigstart restart restjavad.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a memory leak when loading configuration in TMSH or iControl REST.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing FastL4 TCP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing FastL4 TCP traffic
bugs.conditions: FastL4 profile enabled TCP profile enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM now processes FastL4 TCP traffic as expected

bugs.title: Cannot import local db user with multiple groups
bugs.symptoms: Importing of local user CSV file fails.
bugs.conditions: The CSV file contains the user-group field with multiple comma-separated values.
bugs.impact: Importing of local user record, which contains multiple comma separated values, fails.

bugs.title: An access profile with large number of SAML Resources (>200) causes APM error ERR_TOOBIG while loading.
bugs.symptoms: Using a SAML SP intiated use case (APM is IdP) and having a large Access Policy with 200 or more SAML resources assigned to users. Each time a new SAML resource is added to the above Access Policy, the whole SSO service becomes unusable. No new sessions can be established. We generate an internal metadata that consists of the names of all the SAML resources and the SSO name in our code. This has a limit of size 4K and these errors are seen on hitting this limit. Errors seen: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_TOOBIG. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_create_saml_meta_data, Line: 21001 014d1014:3: /Common/SAML_SSO_access:Common:7a34161c:SAML SSO: Error(16) Unable to find SAML SSO/SP Connector object matching SAML Authn Request
bugs.conditions: A SAML SSO Access policy has a large number of SAML Resources assigned to it (such that the combined length of their names >= 4K), we hit the hard limit of 4K in the code.
bugs.impact: We get error on running the Access Policy, the whole SSO service becomes unusable. No new sessions can be established.
bugs.workaround: Delete any unused SAML resources from SAML SSO access policy so that the combined length of the names of all SAML resources assigned to Access policy is < 4K.
bugs.fix: We removed the hard limit of 4K for the internal metadata we create so that we don't hit this issue.

bugs.title: Potential XSS security exposure on APM logon page.
bugs.symptoms: Potential XSS security exposure on APM logon page.
bugs.conditions: -- A LTM virtual server with an Access Policy assigned to it. -- The Access Policy is configured to use a 'Logon Page' VPE agent, followed by AAA agent with 'Max Logon Attempts Allowed' set to a value greater than 1.
bugs.impact: Potential XSS security exposure.
bugs.workaround: 1. Using APM Advance Customization UI, remove setOrigUriLink(); call in logon.inc from the next JS function: 369 function OnLoad() 370 { 371 var header = document.getElementById("credentials_table_header"); 372 var softTokenHeaderStr = getSoftTokenPrompt(); 373 if ( softTokenHeaderStr ) { 374 header.innerHTML = softTokenHeaderStr; 375 } 376 setFormAttributeByQueryParams("auth_form", "action", "/subsession_logon_submit.php3"); 377 setFormAttributeByQueryParams("v2_original_url", "href", "/subsession_logon_submit.php3"); 378 // ===> REMOVE THIS ONE setOrigUriLink(); ----
bugs.fix: Potential security exposure has been removed from APM logon page.

bugs.title: OneConnect header transformations may cause some Websocket connections to reset.
bugs.symptoms: During the Websocket handshake, if OneConnect is on, the Websocket header is set as "connection: close", then OneConnect will transform the header to be "X-Cnection: close". If the header is set as "connection: upgrade" as well as "connection: close", then OneConnect will transform both to be "X-Cnection: close" and "X-Cnection: upgrade", respectively. This causes some Websocket handshakes to fail.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server has HTTP and OneConnect profiles. The request has "Connection: close" and "Connection: upgrade" headers during the Websocket handshake.
bugs.impact: Websocket handshakes fail resulting in connection reset.
bugs.workaround: Remove OneConnect or use iRule to re-add "Connection: upgrade"

bugs.title: Importing the LocalDB csv file fails
bugs.symptoms: Using the Excel sheet to edit and save the LocalDB CSV breaks the Import functionality.
bugs.conditions: Admin Exports the LocalDB CSV file ( Access->Authentication->Local User DB->Users -> Export to CSV) Admin edits the file using Excel Sheet and saves it Admin Imports the CSV file
bugs.impact: File saved using Excel Sheet cannot be used for Import
bugs.workaround: Dont use excel sheet to edit the file. Use a simple text editor (like Textpad , vim) to edit and save the file.

bugs.title: The ':l' and ':h' options are not available on the tmm interface in tcpdump
bugs.symptoms: The ':l' and ':h' options are not available on the tmm interface in tcpdump.
bugs.conditions: Running tcpdump.
bugs.impact: Packet capture on the tmm interface from the Linux side or the host side of tmm interface is not possible.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The tmm interface now accepts ':l' and ':h' and packets on this interface can be captured from the Linux side or the host side.

bugs.title: FingerPrint JS might be injected although it is disabled in all ASM features, and no DoS
bugs.symptoms: Fingerprinting is injected while no ASM feature using it is asking for it.
bugs.conditions: -- Web-scraping is configured in the policy history. -- Policy iss configured using REST.
bugs.impact: FingerPrint JS is injected for each request.
bugs.workaround: 1. Turn on Bot detection and click Save. 2. Turn off Bot detection, FP flag, and suspicious clients detection, and click Save. 3. Apply Policy.

bugs.title: TCP handshake rejected if SYN cookies attack is detected
bugs.symptoms: TCP handshake rejected if SYN cookies attack is detected on platforms with some multiple HSB devices and BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) environments.
bugs.conditions: Enable syncookie protection in LTM global setting, and start SYN flood attacks.
bugs.impact: Regular traffic gets reset because of handshake failures.
bugs.workaround: Turn off syncookie protection.

bugs.title: Protocol Inspection needs add-on license to work
bugs.symptoms: Protocol Inspection does not work.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is licensed and provisioned through 'Good' or 'Better' license, but no add-on subscription license for Protocol Inspection. Alternately, AFM licensed as an add-on module to another module (typically LTM). -- Protocol Inspection profile configured and applied to a Virtual Server or referenced in a firewall rule in an active firewall policy. -- Upgrade to 13.1.0.3 or later. -- Attempt to use Protocol Inspection functionality.
bugs.impact: Protocol Inspection functions that used to work no longer work.
bugs.workaround: Activate an add-on subscription or obtain an AFM standalone license. Protocol Inspection functionality now requires one of these.
bugs.fix: Protocol Inspection now requires an add-on license to work. Note: If you previously had Protocol Inspection configured without an add-on license installed, the features are not applied to traffic until the add-on license is obtained, even though the interface allows you to configure them.
bugs.behavior: The Protocol Inspection (PI) Intrusion Detection and Prevention System functionality now requires either an add-on subscription or an AFM standalone license for any of the features to work. A 'Good' or 'Better' license no longer enables the PI features. Note: The Configuration Utility allows you to configure inspection profiles, compliance checks, and signatures, but they are not applied to traffic. There is no feedback that they are not applied. The operations simply fail silently.

bugs.title: Non-default HTTP/2 header_table_size causes HTTP/2 streams to be reset
bugs.symptoms: If the HTTP/2 configuration header_table_size is changed from the default value of 4096, then streams will be reset with a RST_STREAM error.
bugs.conditions: The header_table_size field in the HTTP/2 profile is changed from the default.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 connections will be unusable.
bugs.workaround: Set the header table size argument back to its default.
bugs.fix: The HTTP/2 filter correctly handles the dynamic header table resize notifications triggered by a non-default header table size. Streams will not be reset with a RST_STREAM error. Additionally, the BIG-IP system will now send the correct number of dynamic header table resize notifications when the table is resized by the client multiple times between header blocks.

bugs.title: A pool can be deleted despite being referenced as a clone-pool by an LTM policy action
bugs.symptoms: If a pool is being referenced as a clone-pool by a policy action, it can be deleted without any validation errors.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policies configured. -- At least one policy action forwards to the pool as a clone-pool. -- No other objects reference the pool. -- The referenced pool is deleted.
bugs.impact: The policy is deleted without error, but the reference to the pool remains. The policy will be referencing a pool that no longer exists. Config sync operations fail, and the configuration does not load.
bugs.workaround: Manually remove the reference to the pool from the policy action.
bugs.fix: Prevented pools from being deleted when they are referenced as clone-pools by policy actions.

bugs.title: The validation error message generated by deleting certain object types referenced by a policy action is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: When deleting certain objects that are referenced by policy actions, you may see a validation error like this: # tmsh delete ltm virtual test-vs 01071726:3: Cannot delete policy action '/Common/test-vs'. It is in use by ltm policy '/Common/test-policy'. The referenced object is not a "policy action" in this case, but is a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: LTM policies must be in use, and at least one policy action must forward to an object. The user must attempt to delete that object.
bugs.impact: Possible confusion at the error message.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Made the error message accurately reflect what the user was attempting to delete.

bugs.title: DNS Cache connections remain open indefinitely
bugs.symptoms: Resize / Clearing the DNS cache while a lot of traffic is running can cause numerous connections to remain open indefinitely. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: Resize / Clear the DNS Cache while it is resolving connections.
bugs.impact: Connections remain open forever, using up memory
bugs.workaround: If you are encountering this, you can remove these connections by restarting tmm: tmsh restart sys service tmm Impact of workaround: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where the DNS Cache kept connections open indefinitely when clearing or resizing a cache with active resolutions occurring.

bugs.title: Appliance mode hardening in scp
bugs.symptoms: When running in Appliance mode scp permits greater access than is required for administration tasks.
bugs.conditions: Appliance mode licensed.
bugs.impact: Appliance mode does not restrict scp access as strictly as possible.
bugs.workaround: N/A.
bugs.fix: Appliance mode functionality of scp now applies stronger restrictions.

bugs.title: Appliance Mode Security Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Appliance Mode does not follow best security practices for administrative users.
bugs.conditions: Appliance Mode licensed Administrative user access
bugs.impact: Appliance Mode does not follow best security practices.
bugs.fix: Appliance Mode now follows best security practices.

bugs.title: AD/LDAP admins with spaces in names are not supported
bugs.symptoms: If admin is imported from Active Directory (AD) or Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) and the name contains spaces, Visual Policy Editor (VPE), import/export/copy/delete, etc., fail, and post an error message similar to the following: sourceMCPD::loadDll User 'test user' have no access to partition 'Common'. Note: Names containing spaces are not supported on BIG-IP systems.
bugs.conditions: -- Admin name containing spaces is imported from AD or LDAP. -- Attempt to perform operations in VPE.
bugs.impact: VPE, import/export/copy/delete do not work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to not use admin names containing spaces.
bugs.fix: VPE and utilities operations are now supported, even for admins with spaces in names. However, F5 recommends against using spaces in admin names, and recommends that you modify the admin name to remove the spaces.

bugs.title: Windows Credential Reuse feature may not work
bugs.symptoms: Windows Credential Reuse feature may not work thus making a user to enter credentials in EdgeClient login window (as well as at Windows logon screen) instead of getting Single Sign-On. Next logs are observed in logterminal.txt when the issue happens: <Date and time>, 1312,1320,, 48, \certinfo.cpp, 926, CCertInfo::IsSignerTrusted(), the file is signed by 3rd party certificate <Date and time>, 1312,1320,, 1, \certinfo.cpp, 1004, CCertInfo::IsSignerTrusted(), EXCEPTION - CertFindCertificateInStore() failed, -2146885628 (0x80092004) Cannot find object or property. <Date and time>, 1312,1320,, 1, \certinfo.cpp, 1009, , EXCEPTION caught <Date and time>, 1312,1320,, 1, \CredMgrSrvImpl.cpp, 256, IsTrustedClient, EXCEPTION - File signed by untrusted certificate <Date and time>, 1312,1320,, 1, \CredMgrSrvImpl.cpp, 264, , EXCEPTION caught <Date and time>, 1312,1320,, 1, \CredMgrSrvImpl.cpp, 360, GetCredentials, EXCEPTION - Access Denied - client not trusted
bugs.conditions: A specific combination of versions of F5 Credential Manager Service and EdgeClient is being used on Windows operation system. Reuse Credential option is enabled in the Connectivity Profile.
bugs.impact: A user has to type credentials in EdgeClient login windows instead of smooth login with no credentials.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The issue causing feature not to work has been fixed.

bugs.title: Same AZ failover in AWS fails in some configurations with two or more objects sharing the same IP address.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP fails to reattach floating addresses to local interfaces during failover, when two or more objects are configured with the same IP address in a given traffic group. Failover fails with the following error in /var/log/ltm: err logger: /usr/libexec/aws/aws-failover-tgactive.sh (traffic-group-1): Failed to reassign some or all address(es): <IP address> <the same IP address> on interface <eni address>.
bugs.conditions: -- AZ AWS failover. -- Same IP address is used for two or more virtual addresses, self IPs, NAT, SNAT translation. Note: Having two virtual servers with the same IP address (but different ports) does not cause the problem. Also, there is no conflict when using the same IP address for different traffic groups.
bugs.impact: Failover will fail; some or all IP addresses will not be transferred to the active BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to change the configuration to use unique IP addresses for conflicting objects.
bugs.fix: This issue has been resolved.

bugs.title: During reboot to another volume, the GUI login page becomes prematurely available
bugs.symptoms: Less than a minute after a reboot to another volume is initiated from the GUI, the GUI reports that the reboot is complete and displays the login page. Normally, a reboot takes about 5 minutes.
bugs.conditions: User initiates a reboot to another volume from the GUI.
bugs.impact: Misleading information is shown in the GUI. The GUI reports that the reboot is completed and displays the login prompts. However this is not correct because the reboot is still in progress.
bugs.workaround: Check the reboot status from the console or simply wait about 5 minutes before attempting to login to the system again.

bugs.title: CGNAT translations fail when using Fastl4 + Default Dag + intra-chassis connection mirroring
bugs.symptoms: CGNAT translations fail with the error message 'LSN Pick took too long'. The error message can be observed in logs or with the command 'tmsh show ltm lsn-pool failure-cause'.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION 4450N blades when using default dag (net vlan cmp-hash default). -- FastL4 is configured -- Intra-chassis connection mirroring is configured.
bugs.impact: Some outbound translations are rejected.
bugs.workaround: You can use any of the following workarounds: -- Use SP Dag (net vlan cmp-hash src-ip/dst-ip). -- Disable connection mirroring. -- Configure a profile on the virtual server that is not FastL4.
bugs.fix: Translation attempts no longer fail in this configuration.

bugs.title: Core observed during lease query testing when RADIUS Authentication is configured in DHCP profile
bugs.symptoms: Tmm may halt and restart when RADIUS Authentication is configured in DHCP profile.
bugs.conditions: 1. RADIUS Authentication is configured in a DHCP profile. 2. DHCP response does not have proper info.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This version handles these conditions, so tmm does not halt and restart.

bugs.title: Tmm might crash activating new blob when changing firewall rules
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with core when changing firewall rules. TMM can enter a crash-loop, so it will crash again after restarting.
bugs.conditions: Updating, removing, or adding firewall rules. Specific characteristics of change that can cause this issue are unknown; this issue occurs rarely.
bugs.impact: Data traffic processing stops.
bugs.workaround: There are two workaround options: Option A 1. Delete all policies. 2. Create them again without allowing blob compilation. 3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 until all the policies have been created (enable on-demand-compilation). Option B Modify all the rules simultaneously. For example, the following steps will resolve this issue: 1. Enable on-demand-compilation 2. Select an IP address that is not used in any rules, e.g., 1.1.1.1. 3. Add that IP address to all the rules/source in all of the policies. To do so, run the following command for each policy: tmsh modify security firewall policy POLICY_NAME rules modify { all { source { addresses add { 1.1.1.1 } } } } 4. Delete the IP address (restore rules) in all of the policies. To do so, run the following command for each policy: tmsh modify security firewall policy POLICY_NAME rules modify { all { source { addresses delete { 1.1.1.1 } } } } 5. Disable on-demand-compilation. Doing so starts new blob compilation.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when changing firewall rules.

bugs.title: Upgrade creates Server SSL profiles with invalid cipher strings
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade of BIG-IP creates Server SSL profiles for custom HTTPS monitors that may have an invalid Ciphers attribute. This will not prevent the configuration from loading, but attempting to modify the existing SSL profile or create a new one with matching configuration will fail: 01070312:3: Invalid keyword 'kedh' in ciphers list for profile /Common/name-of-server-ssl-profile
bugs.conditions: Custom HTTPS monitors configured prior to an upgrade will result in these profiles being created during the upgrade. The default HTTPS cipherlist is 'DEFAULT:+SHA:+3DES:+kEDH', which is a valid OpenSSL cipher list, but is not a valid Client SSL / Server SSL cipher list.
bugs.impact: Upgrade creates configurations that are challenging to manage as a result of MCPD validation.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the cipher list to be valid according to both the OpenSSL cipher list and the Client SSL / Server SSL cipher list expectations. For instance, "DEFAULT:+SHA:+3DES:+EDH" instead of "DEFAULT:+SHA:+3DES:+kEDH".
bugs.fix: Upgrade no longer creates Server SSL profiles with invalid cipher strings.

bugs.title: bigd crash when processing monitor instance missing node name
bugs.symptoms: bigd crashes when processing a node monitor instance that is missing a node name. This behavior has been observed once, and the cause is unknown.
bugs.conditions: -- A node monitor instance is configured, but which is missing a node name. -- It is not currently known what other conditions lead to this state.
bugs.impact: bigd crashes and restarts when processing that node monitor instance that has no node name. Monitor probing from that bigd instance will not occur while bd restarts.
bugs.workaround: None. This behavior has been observed once, and the cause is unknown.

bugs.title: Device-info does not return some crucial fields
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IQ sometimes fails to license a BIG-IP and logs the following error: Unable to assign license; Cannot grant license to null device <host> (<ip>) because it's not a BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: -- Using BIG-IQ License Manager to activate a BIG-IP device. -- Activation is unsuccessful. This occurs intermittently after rebooting a BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP device does not get activated.
bugs.workaround: Restart restjavad daemon on the BIG-IP system: bigstart restart restjavad Once restjavad has been restarted, you can attempt to re-activate the BIG-IP device from the BIG-IQ.

bugs.title: Windows Logon Integration feature may cause Windows logon screen freeze
bugs.symptoms: Windows Logon Integration feature might cause a Microsoft Windows logon screen freeze, making Windows OS unresponsive to any client end user actions.
bugs.conditions: -- Client user putting laptop into sleep mode and waking it up multiple times. -- Possibly, only Windows 10 is affected.
bugs.impact: Logon screen may hang, not allowing client user to type in credentials.
bugs.workaround: Reinstall EdgeClient without the Windows Logon Integration Feature.
bugs.fix: Previously, the Windows Logon Integration feature sometimes caused the Windows Logon screen to freeze. Now, this issue has been fixed. As a side effect of the fix, the Logon screen now shows duplicates of the pre-logon VPN Entries, which might be confusing for client users. One duplicate comes from the Microsoft Credentials Provider. For information on how to disable the default Microsoft Credentials Provider, see the Microsoft Windows article: How to disable additional credential providers :: https://social.technet.microsoft.com/Forums/windows/en-US/9c23976a-3e2b-4b71-9f19-83ee3df0848b/how-to-disable-additional-credential-providers.

bugs.title: Fragmented icmpv6 packets are not displayed when using tcpdump with icmp6 filter
bugs.symptoms: When using tcpdump to display packets, and when the the icmp6 filter is used as an option to the tcpdump program, as below for example: tcpdump -nni 0.0 icmp6 -s0 tcpdump fails to display icmpv6 packets if they are fragmented. Non fragmented packets are displayed correctly. Using a different filter like: tcpdump -nni 0.0 host <ipv6> -s0 displays the fragmented icmpv6 packets correctly.
bugs.conditions: 1) icmpv6 packets need to be fragments ( likely because they exceeded MTU somewhere). 2) tcpdump has to be run with icmp6 specified as the filter
bugs.impact: Fragmented icmpv6 packets cannot be captured or displayed in tcpdump using the icmp6 filter
bugs.workaround: Don't use the icmp6 filter of tcpdump when you know that the packets could be fragmented. Use a host filter, or no filter ( if traffic is not too large)

bugs.title: Loading UCS with different provisioning can cause a single TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Saving a UCS file on one system and loading it on another that has different provisioning, can lead to TMM crash. Note: The crash will take place only once and the next process of TMM that will be automatically restarted will work without problems.
bugs.conditions: -- Save a UCS on a system that has AVR or ASM with DoS configured. -- Load the UCS on a system that does not have AVR nor ASM provisioned.
bugs.impact: When the system restarts after loading the UCS, TMM can crash but second process of TMM will work fine. There is no actual impact, since the system is not operational anyway during UCS load, it only takes more time to bring the system to active state after loading the UCS.
bugs.workaround: When loading a UCS that was saved on a system that had AVR or ASM, make sure the same modules are provisioned first, and then load the UCS.

bugs.title: TMM SIGSEGV under specific conditions.
bugs.symptoms: TMM SIGSEGV when running heavy traffic with LTM, ASM, AVR, and FPS provisioned when span port is enabled. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: -- LTM, ASM, AVR, and FPS are provisioned. -- Span port is enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Added option to reset staging period for signatures
bugs.symptoms: In cases where a staging period was started, but no traffic passed through security policy, you might want to reset the staging period when traffic starts, but there is no option to do so.
bugs.conditions: Staging enabled for signatures in policy.
bugs.impact: There is a suggestion to enforce the signature before any traffic can influence this decision.
bugs.workaround: If all signatures are staged, you can enforce them all, and then enable staging again. Note: Apply policy is required between actions.
bugs.fix: Added option to reset the staging period for all or specific signatures. In modal windows shown after clicking 'Change properties...' on the Policy Signatures screen, when 'No' is not selected for 'Perform Staging', the system presents a checkbox: Reset Staging Period.

bugs.title: OSPF summary address not re-announced on OSPF clear process
bugs.symptoms: When OSPFv2 is configured to make use of summary addresses englobing another more specific route, it is possible that the summary address is removed from the routing table if the routing process is cleared.
bugs.conditions: - Configure OSPFv2. - Configure summary-address within the OSPF routing configuration. - Configure an RHI address of another external route that is within the summary-address range to trigger the creation of the summary route. - Clear the OSPF routing process.
bugs.impact: The summary route may disappear after clearing the OSPF routing process.

bugs.title: Empty results on /tm/sys/config-diff/stats
bugs.symptoms: The /tm/sys/config-diff/stats REST API endpoint returns an empty response. This issue also causes the /tm/services endpoint to return a 400 response.
bugs.conditions: -- You have two scf files, e.g., f1 and f2, that you want to diff via the REST API. -- You diff the files via /tm/sys/config-diff/stats?options=f1,f2. -- This device is part of a Big-IQ DNS sync group.
bugs.impact: The endpoint returns an empty response.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the config-diff/stats endpoint

bugs.title: If using TMSH commands with deprecated attributes in iAPP, the upgrade will fail.
bugs.symptoms: TMSH commands with deprecated attributes will fail if used in iAPP.
bugs.conditions: TMSH commands with deprecated attributes will fail if used in iAPP. This is so whether the iAPP is activated during the upgrade process or simply run under iAPP service at the user display.
bugs.impact: TMSH commands will not execute like create command will result in no objects (eg monitor, virtual server etc) being created.
bugs.workaround: Try to avoid deprecated attributes of the object in the iAPP.
bugs.fix: All TMSH commands should handle deprecated attributes of objects consistently across TMSH command line, CLI Script and iAPP and like so: - run TMSH commands to full execution with only warning message. - full execution means objects action should be executed without error and no something amiss silently either.

bugs.title: Benign mc_delete_key notice message
bugs.symptoms: The /var/log/apm log contains a notice-level message similar to the following, where <RandomKey> is a random string: notice localdbmgr[13537]: 01490000:5: mc_delete_key() [<RandomKey>] failed with error [12]. For example: 01490000:5: mc_delete_key() [b] failed with error [12].
bugs.conditions: -- APM provisioned. -- Access policy is configured to create localdb dynamic user (i.e., uses LocalDB agent to create dynamic user).
bugs.impact: No specific action is required to cause the message to be written to the log. However, the message does not indicate an issue with the system, and does not impact functionality. The only impact is that the apm log file contains the messages. You can safely ignore these log messages.
bugs.fix: Benign mc_delete_key notice message is no longer logged.

bugs.title: With many iApps configured, scriptd may fail to start
bugs.symptoms: If many iApp instances are installed, scriptd may have issues starting up, including the log message: "script has exceeded its time to live, terminating the script"
bugs.conditions: This occurs when many iApp instances exist. F5's internal testing has been able to show that it occurs with 70 instances.
bugs.impact: The error message will show up, and some instances of the script will not run.
bugs.workaround: Restarting scriptd will resolve the issue.

bugs.title: False 'Web Rootkit detected' on UC browser for ChromeOS running on a mobile device
bugs.symptoms: When proactive bot defense, which provides headless browser detection, is enabled, a request from the UC Browser running on a mobile device, gets a high score and might be reset/CAPTCHA'd.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM or DOS provisioned. 2. Proactive bot defense (headless browsers detection) enabled in DoS Application profile and DoS profile assigned on a virtual server. 3. Request is sent without TSPD101 cookie.
bugs.impact: Potential reset/CAPTCHA in this case. In addition to the system presenting a false 'Web Rootkit detected' alert, there are other violations detected within the request.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Disable headless browser detection (under proactive bot defense). -- Raise reset/CAPTCHA score limits using the following commands: list sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_captcha sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_captcha { value "60" } list sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_drop { value "120" }
bugs.fix: Rootkit checks for UC Browser are improved.

bugs.title: shared memory leakage
bugs.symptoms: Processes that require shared memory to operate are failing (e.g. pabnagd).
bugs.conditions: Many shmem segments allocated and used by tmm.
bugs.impact: Potential failures in any process that requires shared memory segments, causing lack of services such as learning (bd+pabnagd), request logging (pabnagd+asm-config), etc.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: High CPU usage for apmd, localdbmgr and oauth processes
bugs.symptoms: High CPU Usage for apmd, localdbmgr, and oauthd with large configurations.
bugs.conditions: APM provisioned BIG-IP has Large configuration (i.e Large number of Virtual servers). A full config sync happens from one device-A(With large configuration) to device-B. The above said processes on Device-B will have high CPU usage. OR Same situation occurs when loading BIG-IP configuration with a large number of virtual servers.
bugs.impact: The user traffic may not be processed by APM until it is done processing all the config changes. The amount of time service is down depends on how large the configuration is.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.
bugs.fix: The software has been optimized to reduce the CPU Usage.
