bugs.title: Malformed HTTP/2 frame consumes excessive system resources
bugs.symptoms: Malformed HTTP/2 frame consumes excessive system resources.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with HTTP/2 profile enabled receives malformed frame.
bugs.impact: Excessive consumption of system resources.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 frames are processed without consuming excessive resources

bugs.title: Manual thresholds for DoS Protection Dynamic Signatures are not accepted via TMUI
bugs.symptoms: Manual thresholds for DoS Protection Dynamic Signatures are not accepted via TMUI. The 'Infinite' values for detection and mitigation are retained. No error message is returned.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure manual AFM detection and mitigation threshold for DoS Protection Dynamic Signatures using the Management GUI.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system Administrator is not aware that config change failed to be applied.
bugs.workaround: Manual thresholds for Dynamic Signatures can be configured using TMSH.
bugs.fix: You can now change manual detection and mitigation threshold via TMUI.

bugs.title: Machine Cert agent improperly matches hostname with CN and SAN
bugs.symptoms: MacOS Machine certificate agent matches the configured hostname with the actual hostname upon a beginning partial string match.
bugs.conditions: MacOS APM client using Machine Certificate Check agent.
bugs.impact: Hostname match may be incorrect in these cases.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The MacOS machine certificate check agent now matches on the whole host string rather than a sub string.

bugs.title: Repeated 'bad transition' OOPS logging may appear in /var/log/ltm and /var/log/tmm
bugs.symptoms: 'bad transition' OOPS messages may be repeatedly logged to /var/log/ltm and /var/log/tmm over time, polluting the log files.
bugs.conditions: Although there are no definitive user-discernible conditions, use of SSL functionality might increase the likelihood of logging.
bugs.impact: Log pollution and potential for performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: Suppress the logging using the following command: tmsh modify sys db tmm.oops value silent
bugs.fix: The 'bad transition' OOPS logging has been demoted to internal, debug builds only.

bugs.title: Request log shows Username N/A for the JSON authentication type Login page
bugs.symptoms: Login parameters in form of JSON parameters are not recognized for logging and protection.
bugs.conditions: The request log shows username N/A for JSON login parameters.
bugs.impact: The request log shows Username N/A and cannot track the username.
bugs.fix: JSON login parameters are now recognized in ASM logging and protection.

bugs.title: BD memory leak
bugs.symptoms: A BD memory leak.
bugs.conditions: websocket traffic with specific configuration
bugs.impact: Resident memory increases, swap getting used.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the web socket violations are not due to bad websocket URL configuration, that they are turned on in Learn/Alarm or block and that there is a local logger configured and attached.

bugs.title: Monitor instances may not get deleted during configuration merge load
bugs.symptoms: Orphaned monitor_instance records in mcpd. Secondary blade restarting in a loop. -- err mcpd[8982]: 01020036:3: The requested monitor instance (/Common/bigip 10.10.9.39 443 gtm-vs) was not found. -- err mcpd[8982]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020036:3: The requested monitor instance (/Common/bigip 10.10.9.39 443 gtm-vs) was not found.... failed validation with error 16908342.
bugs.conditions: Merge a GTM config file to update a virtual server's monitor.
bugs.impact: There is a leaked/extra monitor instance. Restarting secondary slot will result in a restart loop.
bugs.workaround: Remove the MCPD binary database on the Primary blade and restart services: # touch /service/mcpd/forceload # bigstart restart Note: This might change the primary slot.

bugs.title: Replace-all-with can leave orphaned monitor_rule, monitor_rule_instance, and monitor_instance
bugs.symptoms: Orphaned monitor_instance records in mcpd. Secondary blade restarting in a loop.
bugs.conditions: Modify the monitor for GTM objects using tmsh with replace-all-with.
bugs.impact: There is an leaked/extra monitor instance. Restarting the secondary slot results in a restart loop.
bugs.workaround: Impact of workaround: Might change the primary slot. Restart services using the following command: # bigstart restart

bugs.title: DNS query name is not showing up in DNS AVR reporting
bugs.symptoms: DNS query name is not showing up in DNS AVR reporting.
bugs.conditions: Sending traffic to Virtual with DNS profile.
bugs.impact: No query information for DNS is reported in AVR.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After fix, the query name is now showing up in AVR reporting.

bugs.title: Import/export is failing with lease pool
bugs.symptoms: Importing policy with lease pool might result in an error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when exporting a policy from /Common, or importing to a partition, and the route domain is not specified in the lease pool.
bugs.impact: Export does not work properly.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use the following procedure: 1. Detach the leasepool, 2. Export the policy. 3. Import the policy. 4. Create a new leasepool. 5. Attach to the newly imported policy
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue exporting and importing lease pools.

bugs.title: TMM crash when attaching FastL4 profile
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and generates a core file.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 profile is attached to a virtual server. -- L4 stats profile is defined.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: do not use fastl4 profile
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: BIG-IP software may fail to install if multiple copies of the same image are present and have been deleted
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP .iso images may fail to install if multiple copies of the same image are present and have been deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- Have multiple copies of the same image .iso in the /shared directory on a BIG-IP system. -- Delete one of them.
bugs.impact: Installation attempt of the remaining image(s) might fail.
bugs.workaround: Restart the lind process, so the installation can continue.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now installs an image if multiple copies of the same image are present and have been deleted

bugs.title: Reporting found forbidden words context
bugs.symptoms: When a forbidden word is found, its context may not be included in the sent HTML part of the alert.
bugs.conditions: A match of a forbidden word on the page.
bugs.impact: No context of a found forbidden word is shown.
bugs.fix: When a forbidden word is detected, HTML is now included in the “min” part of the alert to indicate the context of the forbidden word.

bugs.title: TMSH help missing for One-Connect limit-type property
bugs.symptoms: When One-Connect profile is created or modified in TMSH and help is invoked by typing the '?' character, description for the limit-type option is missing.
bugs.conditions: A One-Connect profile is created or modified in TMSH.
bugs.impact: Command line help missing.
bugs.workaround: TMSH help is similar to the following: limit-type: Connection limits with OneConnect are different from straight TCP connection limits. Three options are supported: 'none' (the default), 'idle', and 'strict'. -- When the limit is "none", simultaneous in-flight requests and responses over TCP connections to a pool member are counted toward the limit. There may be more TCP connections open to support new requests than there can be simultaneous in-flight requests and responses. This is particularly true when SNAT pools and narrow source address masks are used. -- When the limit is 'idle', idle connections are dropped as the TCP connection limit is reached. For short intervals, during the overlap of the idle connection being dropped and the new connection being established, the TCP connection limit may be exceeded. -- When the limit is 'strict', the TCP connection limit is honored with no exceptions. This means that idle connections prevent new TCP connections from being made until they expire, even if they might otherwise be reused. This is not a recommended configuration except in very special cases with short expiration timeouts.
bugs.fix: Missing help in TMSH added.

bugs.title: TMM halts and restarts when calculating BWC pass rate for dynamic bwc policy
bugs.symptoms: Rarely, TMM halts and restarts when calculating the BWC pass rate for dynamic bwc policy.
bugs.conditions: -- Using BWC dynamic bwc policy. -- Fair share rate is low. For this to happen, the fair share rate of the instance of dynamic policy has to be less than than 32 times the average packet size of the instance of policy. For example, if the average packet size is 1 KB, then the fair share would be under 32 KB.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: F5 does not recommend running the BWC under 64Kbps. Either decrease the number of subscribers or increase the max-rate of dynamic policy.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer halts and restarts when calculating the BWC pass rate for dynamic bwc policy when fair share rate is low.

bugs.title: Updating 3rd party device cert not copied correctly to trusted certificate store
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP admin updates the Device Certificate which also includes multiple CA intermediate and root certificates, it's expected that the new Device Certificate and its trust chain certificates are written to /config/big3d/client.crt and /config/gtm/server.crt. However, if the new Device Certificate is signed by a third party, only the Device Certificate is copied to client.crt and server.crt, even though root and intermediate certificates are written to /config/httpd/conf/ssl.crt/server.crt.
bugs.conditions: Updating Device certificate which also includes multiple intermediate and root certificates.
bugs.impact: The Trusted Device and Trusted server Certificates do not include intermediate CA and root certificates.
bugs.workaround: Manually copy/append the missing intermediate and root certificate to /config/big3d/client.crt and /config/gtm/server.crt.
bugs.fix: The fix will now add all the intermediate and root certificate including device certificate to Trusted Server and Trusted Device certificate bundle.

bugs.title: TMM on BIG-IP restarts if a dos profile is attached to a virtual with sip-routing enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts on a BIG-IP if a dos profile is attached to a virtual with sip-routing enabled
bugs.conditions: 1. A virtual with sip-routing enabled. 2. A dos profile is attached to this virtual
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: After fix, tmm is not restarting any more.

bugs.title: SSL/TLS handshake failures and terminations are logged at too low a level
bugs.symptoms: SSL/TLS handshake failures and terminations are being logged at too low of a level (INFO).
bugs.conditions: -- SSL/TLS connections are received or sent. -- Handshake failures are logged.
bugs.impact: Sometimes other errors are produced, and the cause is a SSL/TLS handshake failure, but this failure is not being logged.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: SSL/TLS handhake failures and terminations are now logged at a higher level (WARNING).

bugs.title: Client connection may hang when NTLM and OneConnect profiles used together
bugs.symptoms: In deployments where a NT LanManager (NTLM) authentication profile and a OneConnect profile are used together in a LTM virtual server to label an authenticated connection to a Domain Controller (DC); if the persisted connection to the DC is re-used, the connection may hang. A connection in this state may not be cleaned up by the sweeper, resulting in a memory leak.
bugs.conditions: The NTLM and OneConnect profiles are associated with a LTM virtual server.
bugs.impact: A client connection won't be serviced and TMM memory will leak. Over a long time period, this may result in more widespread service disruptions.
bugs.workaround: Avoid the use of OneConnect profiles on virtual servers that use NTLM profiles. The connections to the Domain Controller won't be pooled, but all other features will be retained.
bugs.fix: Fixed a problem that prevented NTLM and OneConnect profiles from working properly on the same LTM virtual server.

bugs.title: Orphaned tmsh processes might eventually lead to an out-of-memory condition
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, tmsh processes are orphaned when a user connects to the BIG-IP system via SSH, runs commands, and then quits the session or disconnects. An orphaned tmsh process will have a parent pid (PPID) of 1. You can check for orphaned tmsh processes using the following shell command: /bin/ps -o pid,ppid,comm -C tmsh PID PPID COMMAND 8255 1 tmsh If this issue occurs often enough, it might cause the BIG-IP system to run out of memory.
bugs.conditions: -- Using tmsh to connect to the BIG-IP system via SSH. -- Running commands. -- Quitting the session or disconnecting.
bugs.impact: Orphaned tmsh processes are created, which might eventually lead to an out-of-memory condition, if it occurs often enough.
bugs.workaround: There are several workarounds for this issue: -- Change the default shell to bash for users that are going to use the script. -- Use iControl. -- Halt orphaned tmsh processes.
bugs.fix: tmsh processes are no longer orphaned when a user connects to the BIG-IP system via SSH, runs commands, and then quits the session or disconnects under these conditions.

bugs.title: bigd may crash when the BIG-IP system is under extremely heavy load, due to running with incomplete configuration
bugs.symptoms: A rarely seen scenario exists where 'bigd' crashes when the BIG-IP system is under extremely heavy load, due to 'bigd' running with an incomplete configuration and attempting to interact with 'mcpd' prior to being fully configured by 'mcpd'. This may occur when 'mcpd' is sufficiently delayed in configuring 'bigd' upon 'bigd' process start (at system-start, or upon 'bigd' process re-start), such that 'bigd' attempts to report monitoring results to 'mcpd' prior to fully receiving its configuration (from 'mcpd').
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is under heavy load; and 'bigd' process is (re-)started; and 'mcpd' is delayed in relaying the full configuration to 'bigd'; and 'bigd' attempts to report monitoring results to 'mcpd'.
bugs.impact: Monitoring is delayed while bigd is restarting. If the load lasts for a long enough period of time, bigd might repeatedly fail to start and monitoring will not resume. In some cases 'bigd' may run with an incomplete configuration.
bugs.workaround: Reduce the load on the system.
bugs.fix: 'bigd' does not crash and runs with complete configuration when (re-)starting when BIG-IP runs under heavy configuration resulting in 'mcpd' delaying its configuration of 'bigd'.

bugs.title: Automated upload of qkview to iHealth can time out resulting in error
bugs.symptoms: The automated upload of qkview files to iHealth via the support page of the BIG-IP GUI can time out waiting for an analysis from iHealth. Sometimes, iHealth can take several minutes to complete analysis, and this is a realistic scenario. If the BIG-IP system times-out waiting for completion of the analysis, the link to the iHealth record is not stored.
bugs.conditions: iHealth takes longer than three minutes to complete analysis of a qkview file after uploading.
bugs.impact: Support history will not contain links to completed qkviews.
bugs.workaround: Run qkview from the command line and upload to iHealth manually.
bugs.fix: The iHealth link is now stored immediately after the qkview is successfully uploaded, and the timeout is not considered an error.

bugs.title: [Kerberos SSO] Support for EDNS for kerberos DNS SRV queries
bugs.symptoms: Kerberos DNS SRV requests do not contain EDNS headers. Without this header, DNS server truncates the UDP responses if it is greater than 512 bytes, causing the DNS request to be re-sent on TCP connections. This results in unnecessary round trips in order to resolve DNS SRV queries.
bugs.conditions: APM users using Kerberos SSO to access backend resources.
bugs.impact: Increased latency of HTTP request processing. If the number of APM users is large, then this issue is magnified.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Kerberos DNS SRV requests now support EDNS0 so that UDP responses greater than 512 bytes can be received correctly, eliminating delays caused by TCP retransmission.

bugs.title: tmm may run out of memory during IP shunning
bugs.symptoms: If no AppIQ is configured on an AFM-provisioned system, over time the system can run out of memory causing tmm to crash/restart.
bugs.conditions: -- Blacklist profile is configured with blacklist categories. -- AppIQ is not configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: If no AppIQ is configured, the system now handles the shunned IP's that are to be sent to ECM server.

bugs.title: Chrome v64.0.3282.119 changed way it launches custom protocol handlers causing F5 VPN and F5 EPI not to work properly on Windows
bugs.symptoms: Either of the following symptoms: -- F5 VPN and F5 EPI do not start from Google Chrome 64+ browser. -- Depending on the version of F5 VPN/F5 EPI, F5 VPN and F5 EPI do not update itself or other components when launched from F5 BIG-IP Webtop by Chrome 64+ browser.
bugs.conditions: -- Microsoft Windows clients connecting using Google Chrome 64.0.3282.119 or later. -- Launching from BIG-IP Webtop
bugs.impact: Either of the following outcomes: -- Cannot establish VPN or pass Endpoint Inspection. -- F5 Networks components are not updated properly.
bugs.workaround: You can use Firefox or Edge browser to launch F5 VPN/F5 EPI. There is no workaround for Chrome.
bugs.fix: F5 VPN and F5 EPI now properly consume data processed by Chrome 64+. Because earlier versions of F5 VPN or F5 EPI do not work properly with Chrome 64+ browser, you must launch applications out-of-band (by standalone installer), or by launching F5 VPN/F5 EPI from another browser (such as Firefox or Edge).

bugs.title: Occasionally, pkcs11d cores at Good, Better, Best license change on VE
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, pkcs11d restarts when changing a license's Good, Better, Best option.
bugs.conditions: -- When Safenet netHSM is used with BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- Changing an F5 license from or to Good, Better, Best.
bugs.impact: pkcs11d automatically restarts after the core. This is an occasional restart issue. Because this happens only when switching licenses, this does not affect normal BIG-IP system operation.

bugs.title: Monitor configuration with invalid 'key' and 'cert' not detected upon upgrade post v13.1.x
bugs.symptoms: A monitor configuration with invalid SSL-attributes for 'key' or 'cert' is not detected as invalid, and upon upgrade to on-or-after v13.1.0 may result in an invalid configuration; or may result in a config that loads with the pool 'up', but the monitor 'key' and 'cert' attributes must be added manually. The invalid configuration includes: 'key' and 'cert' attributes do not match, or are not supported. This affects the following monitors, which contain SSL attributes: 'https', 'SIP', 'Firepass'. In some cases this issue may present with valid and matching 'key' and 'cert', with the 'key' in the encrypted form.
bugs.conditions: -- A pre-v13.1.0 configuration containing monitors with invalid 'key' or 'cert' attributes (i.e., 'https', 'SIP', 'Firepass' monitors). -- In some cases the 'key' and 'cert' may be valid and match, with the 'key' in the encrypted form. -- Upgrading that configuration to v13.1.0 or later.
bugs.impact: After upgrade, the configuration does not load.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following workarounds: -- Repair configuration attributes so that 'key' and 'cert' attributes match, so upgrade may complete successfully. -- Remove the monitors before the upgrade, and re-add them after the upgrade is completed. -- In the case where the 'key' and 'cert' are valid and match, replace the encrypted key with the decrypted form. Note: Clearing the 'key' and 'cert' values properly resets the attributes to 'DEFAULT', which is a recommended practice.

bugs.title: Symlinks may be corrupted by upgrade
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases after a software version upgrade, a corrupted symbolic link that points to a nonexistent file may exist. Processes that try to use the file will fail, often generating the message 'No such file or directory'.
bugs.conditions: Happens after an upgrade. This rarely encountered issue occurs when the symlink points to an absolute path (/a/b/c/d) rather than a relative one (if you are in /a/b, then the target would be c/d).
bugs.impact: A symlink is broken, but it depends on whether the symlink is necessary to BIG-IP operation as to whether a problem will be immediately apparent.
bugs.workaround: If creating a symlink is necessary, use a relative path rather than an absolute one. If this condition is found, use the following command to rebuild the symlink: ln -fs <target> <symlink_name>

bugs.title: Support for ONAP site licensing
bugs.symptoms: ONAP site licensing not supported.
bugs.conditions: -- Attempting to use ONAP site licensing
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system does not license.
bugs.fix: Ported ONAP site licensing support to this version of the software.
bugs.behavior: This version of the software supports ONAP site licensing.

bugs.title: Core occurs if DIAMETER::persist reset is called if no persistence key is set.
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes and restarts.
bugs.conditions: The system is configured to use a custom persistence key, but no persistence key has been set and DIAMETER::persist reset command is used.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using DIAMETER::persist reset if a persistence key has not been set.
bugs.fix: System ignores the reset command if the key has not been set

bugs.title: apmd service may restart when BIG-IP is used as SAML SP while processing response from SAML IdP
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions apmd service may restart when processing response from SAML IdP.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured as SAML SP. BIG-IP is processing SAML message from IdP
bugs.impact: Temporarily users will not be able to authenticate agains BIG-IP until apmd service starts up.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: apmd service will no longer restart when processing messages from IdP.

bugs.title: Authentication with UTF-8 chars in password fails for ActiveSync users
bugs.symptoms: ActiveSync end users cannot login to the server.
bugs.conditions: -- ActiveSync end users. -- UTF-8 characters in the password.
bugs.impact: ActiveSync service is unavailable.
bugs.workaround: Put a Variable Assign agent after Logon Page with following assignment: (check the secure checkbox) session.logon.last.password = set pass [mcget -secure session.logon.last.password]; binary scan $pass c* chars; set newpass ""; foreach {ch} $chars { append newpass [format %c [expr $ch & 0xFF]] }; return $newpass
bugs.fix: Special UTF-8 characters in user passwords now work properly with ActiveSync.

bugs.title: Backslashes preceding a forward slash are mistakenly doubled in regular expression within Signature rule
bugs.symptoms: When adding or modifying a user-defined Attack Signature in Simple Edit Mode, backslashes preceding a forward slash are mistakenly doubled in regular expression keywords within the Signature.
bugs.conditions: -- Add or modify a user-defined Attack Signature with a regular expression keyword containing an escaped forward slash in Simple Edit Mode.
bugs.impact: The backslash escaping the forward slash is doubled, which changes the enforced signature rule.
bugs.workaround: Create or modify the Signature rule using Advanced Edit Mode.
bugs.fix: When adding or modifying a user-defined Attack Signature in Simple Edit Mode, backslashes preceding a forward slash are handled correctly in regular expression keywords within the Signature rule.

bugs.title: memory corruption can occur when using certain certificates
bugs.symptoms: If a certificate has an extremely long common name, or an extremely long alternative name and is attached to an SSL profile, memory corruption can occur when loading the profile.
bugs.conditions: An SSL profile is loaded with a certificate containing an extremely long common name or subject alternative name.
bugs.impact: TMM could crash.
bugs.workaround: Do not use certificates with extremely long common names
bugs.fix: A length check has been added to avoid corruption when using extremely long common names.

bugs.title: Kernel panic with mcpd or system shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Kernel panic possible when mcpd shutdown occurs. The mcpd shutdown may be explicit (bigstart stop), or as a side-effect of system shutdown.
bugs.conditions: Conditions are rare, and requires encountering a small timing window. -- vCMP on bare-metal systems. . -- Multiple admin domains defined. -- At least two admin domains have a default route interface called 'tmm'. -- The problem occurs when route-domains are cleaned up (via mcpd exit) and the kernel sees two interfaces with the same name (tmm) being moved back to the system default route domain.
bugs.impact: The system crashes when running the following command: bigstart stop. Otherwise, there is a kernel panic when the system shuts down.

bugs.title: HTML Field Obfuscation not working in IE7
bugs.symptoms: HTML Field Obfuscation does not work when using Microsoft Internet Explorer version 7 (IE7).
bugs.conditions: Open protected page using IE7.
bugs.impact: No HTML Field Obfuscation.
bugs.fix: HTML Field Obfuscation now works in IE7.

bugs.title: NAS-IP-Address is sent with the bytes in reverse order
bugs.symptoms: The NAS-IP-Address has the address of the local device sent with the bytes in reverse order (e.g., 78.56.30.172, where 172.30.56.78 is expected).
bugs.conditions: -- This affects IPv4 addresses only. -- BIG-IP system is configured for RADIUS authentication.
bugs.impact: The server may be configured to check the NAS-IP-Address before allowing logins, in which case it would fail.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This has been corrected.

bugs.title: Add virtual server name is recorded by the remote logging profile
bugs.symptoms: The virtual server name is not logged in remote logger.
bugs.conditions: Using remote logging.
bugs.impact: Missing detail about the virtual server in remote logging information.
bugs.fix: The virtual server name is now recorded by the remote logging profile.
bugs.behavior: The virtual server name is now recorded by the remote logging profile. Previously, it was not.

bugs.title: EUD_M package could not be installed on 800 platforms
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to install the EUD_M EUD package fail on 800 platforms even though they are supposed to be supported.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to install EUD_M package on 800 platforms.
bugs.impact: Cannot install EUD_M package on a platform that is claimed to support it.
bugs.fix: EUD_M package can now be installed on 800 platforms as expected.

bugs.title: SASP monitor marks members down with non-default route domains
bugs.symptoms: The LTM SASP monitor marks pool members down, whose address include non-default route domains.
bugs.conditions: 1. Using the SASP health monitor to monitor a pool or pool member. 2. The address of the pool member includes a non-default route domain, such as: ltm pool rd_test { members { test_1:http { address 12.34.56.78%99 } } monitor my_sasp }
bugs.impact: Pool members with non-default route domains will never be marked up by the SASP monitor.
bugs.workaround: Do not specify non-default route domains in the addresses of pool members monitored by the SASP health monitor. The SASP protocol does not support the use of route domains in member addresses. Thus, the SASP GWM (Global Workload Manager) will ignore route domain information included in the member addresses when registered by the SASP monitor in BIG-IP, and will report the status of members using addresses without route domains. Therefore, even with a fixed version of the SASP monitor, BIG-IP LTM administrators must be careful to avoid configuring multiple pool members with the same address except for different route domains, to be monitored by the SASP monitor. If case of such a configuration error, the status of the member reported by the SASP GWM may not accurately reflect the status of one or more of the pool members with matching IP addresses.
bugs.fix: The LTM SASP monitor will correctly report the status of pool members configured with addresses that include a non-default route domain, if the SASP GWM is monitoring members with matching addresses (minus route-domain information).

bugs.title: PEM does not use 'default' value configured for a custom Diameter-AVP
bugs.symptoms: -- PEM inserts custom AVP with the default value even if its parent AVP is not present in the incoming message. -- PEM does not respect the configured default value; instead it inserts a default value of 0 in custom AVPs. -- If multiple parent AVPs are present in the incoming message, the target AVP should be inserted only once for session-context-record purpose.
bugs.conditions: Configuring custom AVPs with the default value in the diameter application protocol profile.
bugs.impact: The default value functionality does not work properly.

bugs.title: The NAS-IP-Address in RADIUS remote authentication is unexpectedly set to the loopback address
bugs.symptoms: The NAS-IP-Address in RADIUS remote authentication requests is set to the loopback address, not the management IP.
bugs.conditions: This applies to remote authentication for the control plane, not APM.
bugs.impact: Login may be impacted.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: NAS-IP-Address Attribute is now set correctly when the the BIG-IP system is configured to use RADIUS authentication.

bugs.title: System may exhibit duplicate if_index, which in some cases lead to nsm daemon restart
bugs.symptoms: It is possible for the BIG-IP system to present duplicate if_index statistics of network objects, either viewed internally or polled via SNMP.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) configuration. -- Tunnels configured. -- If dynamic routing is configured, additional impact may be noted.
bugs.impact: -- Unreliable or confusing statistics via SNMP polling. -- If dynamic routing is also configured, possible nsm daemon restart, which may lead to loss of dynamic routes.
bugs.fix: System no longer exhibits duplicate if_index statistics.

bugs.title: DHCP server flows are not re-established after expiration
bugs.symptoms: DHCP relay agent does not have server flows connecting to all active DHCP servers after a while.
bugs.conditions: - More than one DHCP servers configured for a DHCP virtual. - Server flows timeout in 60 seconds
bugs.impact: DHCP server traffic not load balanced.
bugs.fix: A new logic to re-establish server flows is introduced to ensure a relay agent will have all DHCP servers connected.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing TCP DNS traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, when processing TCP DNS traffic, TMM may crash
bugs.conditions: DNS profile enabled TCP profile enabled AVR enabled ASM enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM processes TCP DNS traffic as expected

bugs.title: BWC stats for rates are published in bits per second instead of bytes per second
bugs.symptoms: Earlier rates are configured in bits/sec while the stats displayed the rates in bytes/second in both tmctl and tmsh tables. This can be confusing.
bugs.conditions: Get Bandwidth Controller stats, rates are obtained in bytes/sec.
bugs.impact: BWC stats rates (tmctl and tmsh) are now published in bits per second instead of bytes per second. this does not change the rest API's, iControl and SNMP. They still publish the stats in bytes per second.
bugs.workaround: You can change the bytes/sec to bits/sec manually.

bugs.title: Policy Audit Log should be cleaned by data size as well as number of rows
bugs.symptoms: When the Policy Audit Log row count is less than the maximum, but each row is very large, the total size causes errors in synchronization to the secondary blade of a chassis.
bugs.conditions: -- The Policy Audit Log row count is less than the maximum. -- Each row contains a lot of data.
bugs.impact: Errors in synchronization to the secondary blade of a chassis.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you can delete records from the Policy Audit Log (PL_CONFIG_LOG) using the following sql command: -------------------------------------------- CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE PROTECTED_CONFIG_LOG (config_log_id int); INSERT INTO PROTECTED_CONFIG_LOG SELECT MAX(config_log_id) AS max_config_log_id FROM PLC.PL_CONFIG_LOG config_log2 WHERE config_log2.is_policy_version_event = 1 GROUP BY policy_id; DELETE FROM PLC.PL_CONFIG_LOG where length(description) > 20000 and config_log_id not in (SELECT config_log_id from PROTECTED_CONFIG_LOG); ---------------------------------------------
bugs.fix: Now, in addition to cleaning the Policy Audit Log when the number of rows is greater than the maximum allowed, the table is also cleaned when its total size is greater than the maximum allowed.

bugs.title: Seperate ePVA offload timing configuration according to protocol
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP supports ePVA offloading feature on two protocols: TCP and UDP. The timing when they are offloaded is under the same fastl4 profile option: pva-offload-state. The available timings are defined in alignment with the TCP 3-way handshake. UDP, then, mimics the definition of the TCP 3-way handshake on the first few packets on both direction traffic.
bugs.conditions: On a ePVA supported platform. Some of the options will need UDP ePVA feature available.
bugs.impact: Separate the configuration of ePVA offload timing to TCP and UDP. The TCP offload timing uses the option "tcp-pva-whento-offload" to replace the old option "pva-offload-state", but still uses the 3-way handshake to determine the timing. The UDP ePVA offload timing is defined by packet counts. Options "other-pva-clientpkts-threshold" and "other-pva-serverpkts-threshold" is the user configurable threshold. Option "other-pva-whento-offload" allows user to decide whether each side of the traffic is offloaded once the side passes the threshold or BIG-IP waits for both side of the traffic to pass the threshold and offload together. New option "other-pva-offload-direction" allows user to set which direction of the traffic the user would like to allow offloading.
bugs.behavior: Deprecate DB variables: pva.udpest.clientpkts.threshold, pva.udpest.serverpkts.threshold, pva.offload.uniflow. Deprecate ltm profile fastl4 option: pva-offload-state. Add ltm profile fastl4 options: tcp-pva-whento-offload, other-pva-whento-offload, other-pva-offload-direction, other-pva-clientpkts-threshold, other-pva-serverpkts-threshold

bugs.title: HTTP/2, ALPN and SSL
bugs.symptoms: The SSL filter will not always add the ALPN extension.
bugs.conditions: If the negotiated cipher is not HTTP/2 compliant, the SSL filter may not add the ALPN extension.
bugs.impact: The failure to add the ALPN extension may result in the failure to negotiate the proper protocol.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: GUI Network Map objects search on Virtual Server IP Address and Port does not work
bugs.symptoms: Searching for a Virtual Server using the IP Address and Port of the Virtual Server does not work.
bugs.conditions: Create a Virtual Server with name vs1 and address.
bugs.impact: CAnnot search using an IP Address to filter Virtual Server results.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: We now include the Virtual Server's IP Address and Port as searchable values.

bugs.title: VCMP Guests unable to install block-device-image ISOs when http->https redirection is enabled
bugs.symptoms: ISOs of type block-device-image do not show up on VCMP Guests and are not available for installation when http->https redirection is enabled.
bugs.conditions: VCMP Guest has http->https redirection enabled.
bugs.impact: Not all available images are installable.
bugs.workaround: User must manually copy images to VCMP guest.
bugs.fix: Configured iControl REST to allow appropriate daemons access when http->https is enabled.

bugs.title: Appliance Mode does not follow design best practices
bugs.symptoms: Appliance Mode does not follow design best practices
bugs.conditions: Appliance Mode does not follow design best practices
bugs.impact: Appliance Mode does not follow design best practices
bugs.fix: Appliance Mode now follows design best practices

bugs.title: Create download URL for APM CLI client rpm/deb packages for x86_64 for armhf and Linux platforms
bugs.symptoms: APM CLI client rpm/deb packages are not available for download on the BIG-IP admin portal.
bugs.conditions: APM Client ISO v7181 includes APM CLI client rpm/deb packages, but they are not available for download on BIG-IP v14.0.x and v13.1.x
bugs.impact: APM CLI client rpm/deb packages are not available for download/install.
bugs.workaround: Use SSH to download the packages from BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Context leaked from iRule DNS lookup
bugs.symptoms: The memory usage increases, and stats are inaccurate.
bugs.conditions: Call RESOLV::lookup from an iRule.
bugs.impact: Memory leak that accumulates over time and inaccurate stats.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using RESOLV::lookup in an iRule.
bugs.fix: Memory leak no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Attempting to create GTM SIP monitor from GUI results in general database error
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to create GTM SIP monitor from GUI results in 'General database error'.
bugs.conditions: The user creates a SIP Monitor under DNS :: GSLB :: Monitors with 'mode' being 'TCP or 'UDP'.
bugs.impact: Some users are unable to create SIP monitors via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH or set the 'mode' to 'TLS' or 'SIPS'.
bugs.fix: SIP Monitors can now be created and modified via the web GUI without any issues.

bugs.title: FPS: false positive "no strong integrity param" when none of the configured data-integrity params are present in request
bugs.symptoms: A false positive "no strong integrity param" is sent when none of the configured data-integrity parameters are present in the request.
bugs.conditions: 1. a protected URL has at least one parameter configured with data0integrity check enabled 2. enhanced data manipulation is enabled 3. a request without any of the data-integrity parameters is sent to the protected URL
bugs.impact: A false positive "no strong integrity param" alert is sent.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: "No strong integrity param" alert should be suppressed in case that none of the data-integrity parameters were sent. In case that forcing all data-integrity parameters was enabled (tmsh modify sys db antifraud.autotransactions.parameternameintegrity value enable) - the alert will be sent.

bugs.title: The TMM may crash when under load when configuration changes occur when the HTTP/2 profile is used
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may later crash after a configuration change done under load if the HTTP/2 profile is used.
bugs.conditions: A configuration change occurs. The configuration change is large enough, or the TMM load large enough that the change is not synchronous. The change involves a HTTP/2 profile. Data traffic progresses through a partially initialized HTTP/2 virtual server, potentially causing a later crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Large configuration changes to the TMM involving a HTTP/2 profile will no longer potentially cause a TMM crash.

bugs.title: Async transaction may ignore polling requests
bugs.symptoms: Querying for the status of an asynchronous transaction by making a GET request may cause the query to block. The transaction will complete, even though the query may return an error status (400) to indicate that the GET request timed out.
bugs.conditions: A typical asynchronous transaction that returns a 202 status to indicate that you successfully created a transaction.
bugs.impact: The query returns an error.
bugs.workaround: To avoid having the query request block, refrain from querying the transaction for status.

bugs.title: Virtual address not responding to ICMP when ICMP Echo set to Selective
bugs.symptoms: If the virtual server's availability has taken the virtual address 'down', enabling the virtual server does not cause it to go 'up'.
bugs.conditions: -- ICMP Echo is set to Selective for the virtual address. -- Disable the virtual server. -- Enable the virtual server.
bugs.impact: The virtual address does not come up again. This affects the availability status of the virtual-address, and icmp-echo or route-advertisement for the virtual-address.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, do the following: 1. Set ICMP Echo to Always. 2. Disable the virtual-server. 3. Change virtual-address availability calculation back to the desired state.
bugs.fix: Virtual address now correctly responds to ICMP when ICMP Echo is set to Selective.

bugs.title: Virtual server in a non-default partition cannot select protocol inspection profile in the /Common partition
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server in a non-default partition is not able to select protocol inspection profile in the /Common partition. The system posts messages similar to the following: 01070726:3: Virtual Server /internal/vs-internalvs in partition internal cannot be referenced by Protocol Inspection Profile /Common/protocol_inspection in partition Common
bugs.conditions: -- Create a partition. -- Create a virtual server in that partition. -- Try and associate an IPS profile from /Common partition to the created virtual server.
bugs.impact: Cannot associate the profile.
bugs.fix: Profile is now associated with virtual server.

bugs.title: Config fails to load due to invalid SSL cipher after upgrade from v13.1.0
bugs.symptoms: Config with apparently invalid SSL cipher entry fails to load after upgrade from v13.1.0, and requires a manual config load after upgrade: 'tmsh load sys config' This occurs because starting in v13.1.0, 'https' monitors rely upon SSL-attributes configured through a 'serverssl' profile, which does not support the 'kEDH' cipher; but the 'kEDH' cipher was a default cipher for previous releases (where 'https' relied upon 'OpenSSL').
bugs.conditions: -- Config uses 'https' monitors. -- Upgrade occurs from v13.1.0 to a later version.
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to load, an error message is issued, and the device remains offline until a manual config load is performed.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- After upgrade from v13.1.0, perform manual config load by running the following command: tmsh load sys config (This works because upon a manual config load command ('tmsh load sys config'), the system replaces the existing 'https' ciphers with defaults appropriate for a 'serverssl' profile in the new version of the software. Even though the system posts an error referencing the invalid 'kEDH' cipher, the device will become 'Active' seconds later, and new default ciphers will be established for 'https' monitors.) -- Remove 'https' monitors prior to upgrade, and add again after upgrade.
bugs.fix: Config loads without error after upgrade from v13.1.0.

bugs.title: dynconfd may core and restart with multiple DNS name servers configured
bugs.symptoms: The dynconfd daemon may crash with a core and restart when processing a DNS query while multiple DNS name servers are configured or the list of DNS name servers is changed.
bugs.conditions: This may occur rarely when FQDN nodes are configured and multiple DNS name servers are configured, including when a name server is added to or removed from the system DNS configuration while a DNS query is active.
bugs.impact: Resolution of FQDN names for FQDN nodes and pool members may be briefly interrupted while the dynconfd daemon restarts. This may cause a delay in propagation of DNS zone changes to the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.workaround: This issue occurs rarely. There is currently no known workaround.
bugs.fix: The dynconfd process no longer cores and restarts with multiple DNS name servers configured.

bugs.title: TMM may core with a virtual server configured with fastl4, http, and persistence
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue TMM may crash when a specific traffic pattern is received on a virtual server configured with fastl4, http, and persistence.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server configured with fastl4, http, and persistence.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, disrupting traffic or causing failover.
bugs.workaround: Do not use fastl4 and http profiles along with persistence together.

bugs.title: Add a set of disallowed file types to RDP template
bugs.symptoms: Universally dangerous filetypes are not included in RDP policy template.
bugs.conditions: The user creates a new policy using the RDP template.
bugs.impact: Universally dangerous filetypes are not disallowed.
bugs.workaround: Dangerous filetypes can be added to policies created from RDP template.
bugs.fix: Universally dangerous filetypes are now included in RDP policy template.

bugs.title: Under certain circumstances a stale http2 stream can cause a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: A HTTP2 stream is getting overlooked when cleaning up a HTTP2 flow.
bugs.conditions: Currently only known is that the closing_stream is not empty. Exact entrance conditions not clear.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: HTTP2 flows are properly cleaned up to prevent a tmm crash.

bugs.title: TMSH improvements
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMSH usage, including via iControl, may lead to excessive resource consumption.
bugs.conditions: Authorized users making queries or updates via TMSH or iControl
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.

bugs.title: Internet Explorer does not offer F5 VPN or F5 EPI for installation when UAC is disabled
bugs.symptoms: When an APM end user first tries to open Network Access resources from webtop, or to pass Endpoint Inspection from a Microsoft Windows system with User Access Control (UAC) disabled, Internet Explorer 11 does not offer F5 VPN or F5 EPI for installation. Instead, it assumes that F5 VPN/F5 EPI is already installed.
bugs.conditions: -- Windows 7. -- UAC is disabled. -- F5 VPN/F5 EPI is not installed on the system.
bugs.impact: The APM end user has to click a 'download' link instead of having F5 VPN/F5 EPI automatically download.
bugs.workaround: Click the 'Download' link manually and install F5 VPN/F5 EPI.

bugs.title: GUI Network Map Policy with forward Rule to Pool, Pool does not show up
bugs.symptoms: When a Virtual Server has a Policy with a rule to forward request to a Pool, the Pool should be associated to the Virtual Server on the Network Map.
bugs.conditions: Create a Virtual Server with a Policy to forward requests to a Pool.
bugs.impact: The relationship of the Virtual Server to the Pool via the indirect Policy Rule is not visible in the network map.
bugs.workaround: No workaround to the visual.
bugs.fix: Associate Virtual Server with Policy that forwards requests to a Pool on the Network Map.

bugs.title: TMM crashes as a result of repeated loads of the GeoIP database
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash due to the repeated loading of the GeoIP database.
bugs.conditions: Repeatedly loading the GeoIP database in rapid succession.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid repeated loading of the GeoIP Database.

bugs.title: Websocket Message Type not displayed in Request Log
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to filter for websocket message types.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered on ASM when viewing the request log.
bugs.impact: Websocket Message Type not available to be displayed in Request Log.
bugs.fix: Websocket Message Type correctly displayed in Request Log

bugs.title: PAM RADIUS authentication subsystem hardening
bugs.symptoms: The RADIUS component of the PAM authentication subsystem does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: RADIUS authentication enabled
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: The RADIUS component of the PAM authentication subsystem now follows best practices.

bugs.title: Entry for SSL key replaced by config-sync causes tmsh load config to fail
bugs.symptoms: After config-sync, the secondary unit's key file does not match the passphrase stored for the key. This is a generic problem where config-sync is not synchronizing any differing file-objects on the secondary unit that happen to have the same cache_path as the primary.
bugs.conditions: If the cache_path of the encrypted key happens to be the same on the HA-pair, but the keys are different and have different passphrases.
bugs.impact: Secondary unit will fail to load the config during boot-up, so it will be offline. Other file-objects that had the same cache_path but where different files do not sync. The latter may not be noticed since nothing fails on the secondary unit.
bugs.workaround: Check if the cache_path of the encrypted key is the same on both systems prior to config-sync and that the sha1sum are different. If this is the case, remove the key on one of the systems and re-install the key and make sure the cache_path name is different.
bugs.fix: The key files (in the cache_path) will sync despite having the same name. The problem goes away. The same goes for any file-object that happened to have the same cache_path prior to sync.

bugs.title: SMTP monitor does not handle all multi-line banner use cases
bugs.symptoms: An SMTP monitor does not handle all multi-line banner use cases, such as when the banner is physically split across two packets. This issue is due to attempting to parse the banner value from the first packet without a portion of the banner value that may arrive in a second packet.
bugs.conditions: An SMTP monitor is configured; and uses a multi-line banner; and the SMTP monitor banner is split across two physical packets.
bugs.impact: The SMTP monitor sends an RST after the first packet, and marks the resource down.
bugs.workaround: Use an SMTP monitor with a single-line banner. Or, rather than using an SMTP monitor, instead use a TCP monitor with send/recv strings.
bugs.fix: An SMTP monitor handles all use cases that include a multi-line banner.

bugs.title: Dynamically advertised route may flap
bugs.symptoms: ZebOS may repeatedly add and delete the routes from protocol daemons. This may cause the protocol daemons to delete and re-advertise the default route.
bugs.conditions: - Dynamic routing in use - Kernel routes redistributed into a routing protocol - Static route configure in TMOS - Route advertisement enabled on the virtual-address that's the same as the static route
bugs.impact: Route flapping may cause instability in the network, including inability to reach the default network advertised by the BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Since the static route will be redistributed in the same way as the virtual-address, there is no need to enable route-advertisement on the VIP virtual-address. Disabling this will resolve the problem. The problem will also be resolved by moving the route from tmsh into ZebOS. - In imish config mode, "ip route <route> <gateway>" - In tmsh, "delete net route <route>"
bugs.fix: Configuring a static route in TMOS and enabling route-advertisement on the same virtual-address no longer causes route flapping in ZebOS.

bugs.title: PUT request sent to ltm/virtual failed because of ip-protocol property value any
bugs.symptoms: PUT request to ltm/virtual fails unexpectedly because ip-protocol property value any
bugs.conditions: When sending PUT request to ltm/virtual
bugs.impact: PUT request modifies properties that user includes in the request and resets the rest of property value to default. Default ip-protocol property value could be 'any', 'ip' or 'hopopt'
bugs.workaround: Using PATCH request

bugs.title: MCPD configuration load fails after reboot if user manually configures a static route while 1nic autoconfig is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: User has configured a single-nic BIG-IP VE with 1nic autoconfig enabled. The status of this DB variable can be seen through "tmsh list sys db provision.1nicautoconfig".
bugs.conditions: User configures a static net route through "tmsh create net route" that depends on the self-ip to reach out to the gateway associated with this static route.
bugs.impact: After reboot, MCPD never reaches "active" state as config load fails. This happens because the static route gateway becomes unreachable.
bugs.workaround: - User must disable "provision.1nicautoconfig" before creating net static routes with the following command: tmsh modify sys db provision.1nicautoconfig value disable
bugs.fix: In a single-nic configuration, disable "provision.1nicautoconfig" before manually creating net static routes.

bugs.title: DNSSEC Signed Zone Transfers Can Leak Memory
bugs.symptoms: TMM might leak memory when performing DNSSEC signed zone transfers. You can detect this issue by examining system memory before and after performing zone transfers. For example: tmsh show sys memory raw | grep dnssec
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic DNSSEC signing of zone transfers is configured for a given zone from an authoritative DNS Server (this could be on-box BIND, off-box BIND, etc) or from DNS Express.
bugs.impact: TMM leaks memory related to the signed zone transfer.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer leaks DNSSEC zone transfer related memory.

bugs.title: tmsh memory leak
bugs.symptoms: tmsh is leaking approximately 24 KB for every 'save sys config' call.
bugs.conditions: this occurs under the following conditions: -- In tmsh, run the following command repeatedly: save sys config -- In the GUI, modify the configuration and click Update, change pages, or otherwise cause a save to the configuration.
bugs.impact: This results in a memory leak, and a possible out-of-memory condition.
bugs.fix: tmsh no longer leaks memory when performing configuration-save operations.

bugs.title: TMM crash can occur when using LRO
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes under rare conditions when handling traffic with LRO enabled.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured to use LRO.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable LRO and/or syncookies.
bugs.fix: TMM processes traffic using LRO as expected

bugs.title: Disabling l7dos using LTM policy, and original DoS on the virtual server has no features enabled, connection hangs
bugs.symptoms: Using an LTM policy rule to disable l7dos when the DoS profile on the virtual server contains an application profile with no feature enabled, causes the transaction to hang instead of forwarding the request to server.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy with 'disable l7dos' rule. -- DoS profile on a virtual server contains an application profile without any features enabled.
bugs.impact: The connection hangs. Requests are not forwarded to server.
bugs.workaround: Enable any DoS application feature in the DoS profile attached to the virtual server (e.g., bot signatures, proactive bot defense, TPS-based DoS Detection, etc.). The profile can be disabled by default using the LTM rules.

bugs.title: Unnecessary pop-up appears
bugs.symptoms: A pop-up dialog box appears when 'Enhanced Data Integrity Check' is clicked.
bugs.conditions: -- Provision and license FPS. -- Add URL. -- Disable 'Check Full AJAX for Data Manipulation'.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary dialog box appears.
bugs.fix: The pop-up does not appear.

bugs.title: ASU and other Update Check services overload F5 download server
bugs.symptoms: ASM Signature Update (ASU) and other Update Check services may fail due to an overload on the F5 download server.
bugs.conditions: -- Automatic update attempt is initiated during specified schedule. -- F5 download server is overloaded by Update attempts.
bugs.impact: ASU and other Update Check services fail.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, run manual updates instead. To prevent this issue, change the time of the daily job run. To do so, follow these steps: 1. Open the cron job text file. # vi /etc/crontab 2. Change this line as follows: From: 02 4 * * * root run-parts /etc/cron.daily To: 10 4 * * * root run-parts /etc/cron.daily 3. Save the changes, and quit vi. This will change the automatic updates to run at 4:10 rather than 4:02.
bugs.fix: ASU and other Update Check services now stagger download attempts to prevent F5 download server overload.

bugs.title: bgpd may crash with overlapping aggregate addresses and extended-asn-cap enabled
bugs.symptoms: bgpd may crash on a BIG-IP system configured for dynamic routing announcing multiple overlapping aggregate-addresses with extended asn capabilities enabled.
bugs.conditions: - BGP enabled on route-domain - BGP configured to announce several overlapping aggregate-addresses - BGP configured with extended-asn-cap enabled.
bugs.impact: Inability for the unit to use BGP
bugs.workaround: Disabling extended-asn-cap or not announcing multiple overlapping aggregate addresses may allow to workaround this issue.
bugs.fix: bgpd no longer crashes with overlapping aggregate addresses and extended-asn-cap enabled

bugs.title: TMM crashes due to memory leaking while processing SSL forward proxy traffic
bugs.symptoms: SSL forward proxy can leak memory while forging the server certificate. TMM might eventually halt and restart when available memory is exhausted.
bugs.conditions: SSL forward proxy is enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted or failover event occurs while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed the memory leak in the SSL module.

bugs.title: OPT-0045 optic unable to link
bugs.symptoms: The OPT-0045 optical transceiver when inserted into a 40G port does not function. The following error appears in /var/log/ltm: Invalid module for bundle configuration of interface <portNumber>.0.
bugs.conditions: OPT-0045 in a 40G port.
bugs.impact: Optic does not work; interface does not come up.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release supports the OPT-0045 optical transceiver.

bugs.title: IPS stats tables are empty after upgrade from 13.1.0 to 14.0.0
bugs.symptoms: The IPS stats tables are empty after upgrade from 13.1.0 to 14.0.0.
bugs.impact: All statistics that relate to IPS are lost.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading, run the following SQL command: update AVR_CONF_FACT_TABLES set export_dir='/shared/avr_afm' where fact_name="AVR_STAT_IPS";
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrade from 13.1.0 to 14.0.0. -- AVR is NOT provisioned. -- Viewing IPS stats tables.
bugs.fix: The IPS stats tables are now saved in the '/shared_avr_afm' export directory.

bugs.title: Heavy use of APM Kerberos SSO can sometimes lead to memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: Kerberos SSO under high load can sometimes lead to system instability.
bugs.conditions: APM users using Kerberos SSO to access backend resources.
bugs.impact: This might result in unpredictable behavior such as memory corruption or core. However, the occurrence is rare since it only impacts concurrent DNS SRV requests to resolve different KDCs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Stability problems in DNS lookups in APM Kerberos SSO (S4U) have been corrected.

bugs.title: tmm may restart if an IKEv2 child SA expires during an async encryption or decryption
bugs.symptoms: TMM may discard an existing child-SA via timer during the moment it is in use for encryption or decryption. And in another spot, an error aborting negotiation can cause multiple timers associated with one child-SA, which fight one another.
bugs.conditions: Errors in IPsec config that fail negotiation can happen when a child-SA is in a state that does not manage timers correctly. A config with short SA lifetime, causing frequent re-keying, can have the effect of searching for a race condition when expire happens during active use in crypto.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts, disrupting traffic and causing HA failover.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the IPsec IKEv2 configuration in the IPsec policy is correct (the same) on both IPsec peers. Also, ensure SA lifetime has longer duration, instead of merely seconds. (The default is one day.)
bugs.fix: Now we ensure only one timer can be associated with a child-SA related to short-term progress toward maturity during negotiation, even if an error happens. Now we also ensure a child-SA is safe during async crypto operations, even if they expire while currently in use.

bugs.title: Multiple manual incremental sync operations might cause race condition in ASMConfig
bugs.symptoms: Numerous repeated sync recoveries by ASM after a manual incremental sync that contains many changes.
bugs.conditions: -- Delete/create many ASM policies. -- Issue a manual incremental sync repeatedly.
bugs.impact: High availability configuration goes out of sync and into 'Changes Pending' shortly after a manual incremental sync operation.
bugs.workaround: Use manual full sync.

bugs.title: VCMP guest, tmm continues to restart on Cavium Nitrox PX platform
bugs.symptoms: TMM continues to restart on vCMP guest. /var/log/tmm shows: <13> Feb 1 00:00:30 slot1/hostname notice ** SIGSEGV ** <13> Feb 1 00:00:30 slot1/hostname notice fault addr: 0x1d8 <13> Feb 1 00:00:30 slot1/hostname notice fault code: 0x1 . . .
bugs.conditions: -- Using the following platforms: + BIG-IP 800, 1600, 3600, 3900, 6900, 89xx, 11xxx. + VIPRION 42xx/43xx and B21xx blades. -- Configure vCMP host and guest. System has Common Criteria or FIPS mode enabled.
bugs.impact: vCMP guest can't become active.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: iRule table lookup command may crash tmm when used in FLOW_INIT
bugs.symptoms: iRule table lookup command may crash tmm when used in FLOW_INIT.
bugs.conditions: iRule table lookup command is used in FLOW_INIT.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use table lookup in the events after the flow is constructed.

bugs.title: The audit forwarding mechanism for TACACS+ uses an unencrypted db variable to store the password
bugs.symptoms: TACACS Shared Key is not encrypted in the DB key and is visible to admin and a read-only user.
bugs.conditions: Configure TACACS+ auditing forwarder.
bugs.impact: Exposes sensitive information.
bugs.fix: The sensitive data is not exposed, and this issue is fixed.

bugs.title: L7 connection mirroring may not be fully mirrored on standby BigIP
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue L7 connection mirroring may not be fully mirrored on standby BigIP
bugs.conditions: L7 VIP with mirroring configured Connections with transfer of substantial size.
bugs.impact: Connections may be mirrored initially but removed after some time. If there is a failover these connections may not be correctly handled.
bugs.workaround: Disabling LRO via tmsh modify sys db tm.tcplargereceiveoffload value disable May workaround this issue
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now fully mirrors all L7 connections

bugs.title: A remote TLS server certificate with a bad Subject Alternative Name should be rejected when Common Criteria mode is licensed and configured.
bugs.symptoms: According to RFC2818, if the certificate sent by the TLS server has a valid Common Name, but the Subject Alternative Name does not match the Authenticate Name in the server-ssl profile, the connection should be terminated.
bugs.conditions: -- A server-ssl profile is enabled on a virtual server and has the 'authenticate-name' property set. -- The TLS server presents a certificate in which the Subject Alternative Name does not match the configured authenticate-name. -- Common Criteria mode licensed and configured.
bugs.impact: A TLS connection succeeds which should fail.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A remote TLS server certificate with a bad Subject Alternative Name is now rejected when Common Criteria mode is licensed and configured.

bugs.title: Improving Single Page Application event handling
bugs.symptoms: When using Single Page Application, and registering to 'readystatechange' and 'load' events: The event is not forwarded to the original callback.
bugs.conditions: Single Page Application in enabled in ASM or DoS.
bugs.impact: Client page might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly calls the original callbacks when using Single Page Application, and registering to 'readystatechange' and 'load' events.

bugs.title: Improving Single Page Application event handling
bugs.symptoms: When using single page application, and registering to "readystatechange" and "load" events: The "remove event listener" does not apply.
bugs.conditions: Single Page Application in enabled in ASM or DoS.
bugs.impact: Client page might be broken.
bugs.fix: Correctly calling original callbacks.

bugs.title: wamd may leak memory during configuration changes and cluster events
bugs.symptoms: wamd memory consumption increases over time.
bugs.conditions: -- AAM is provisioned so wamd is running. -- User-initiated configuration change and/or other internal configuration or cluster events.
bugs.impact: wamd grows slowly over time, eventually crashing due to lack of memory. Temporary outage of services provided by wamd such as PDF linearization, invalidation, etc.
bugs.workaround: No workaround available.
bugs.fix: wamd n longer leaks memory during configuration changes and cluster events.

bugs.title: Cloning URL does not clone "Description" field
bugs.symptoms: When cloning URL using the "Clone URL" feature in FPS/DataSafe GUI, description field is not cloned to new URL.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license FPS/DataSafe.
bugs.impact: Not all expected configuration values of the URL are cloned.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Description field is now cloned to the new URL.

bugs.title: Improving Single Page Application event handling
bugs.symptoms: When using Single Page Application, and registering to 'readystatechange' and 'load' events: Callbacks are not called in ready state 1, and are called twice in ready state 4.
bugs.conditions: Single Page Application in enabled in ASM or DoS.
bugs.impact: Client page might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly calls the original callbacks when using Single Page Application, and registering to 'readystatechange' and 'load' events.

bugs.title: ASM policy is modified after pabnagd restart
bugs.symptoms: ASM policy modifications might occur after the the pabnagd daemon is restarted. Modifications include the following: -- Length attributes might change from 'any' to a low auto learning value. -- Check signature / metachars might change from unchecked to checked. This applies for the following entity types: filetypes, URLs, parameters, cookies, WS URLs, content profiles.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration containing a policy in which automatic learning mode is configured. -- Restart of pabnagd (the automated policy-building operations daemon).
bugs.impact: ASM policy is modified.
bugs.workaround: Switch policy builder to manual learning mode.
bugs.fix: Prevent unwanted adjust operations from being called on policy-catchup complete.

bugs.title: Unable to log into BIG-IP GUI after partition is deleted
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP GUI no longer presents a login dialog if a GUI's session becomes invalidated while it is viewing a partition that has subsequently been deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- A GUI session is logged in and a non-/Common partition is selected. -- The GUI session expires or is invalidated (producing the message 'Your login credentials are no longer valid'). -- While in that state, the selected partition is deleted via an SSH session. -- A subsequent attempt is made to log into the GUI (in any browser).
bugs.impact: Unable to log into the BIG-IP GUI. The UI consists of a grey backdrop colour with a partially drawn login field. There is no way to enter text into the field, so there is no way to log in. You must use SSH to log into the device and restart the tomcat process. In the browser's JavaScript console, the following message may be seen: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'style' of null at window.onload (login.jsp:35).
bugs.workaround: Use SSH to log into the device, and restart the tomcat process: tmsh restart sys service tomcat

bugs.title: Automatically add additional certificates to BIG-IP system in C2S and IC environments
bugs.symptoms: In order to function properly, the BIG-IP system's failover and autoscale features need extra certificates (which are used inside C2S environments) and endpoint URL. The extra certificates must be pointed to by the $AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable. The BIG-IP system's failover and autoscale feature use AWS CLI commands. Those AWS CLI commands need to have the $AWS_CA_BUNDLE pointing to the certificate files location and endpoint URL. These must be configured manually.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP is running in AWS C2S (Commercial Cloud Services) where the domain is either c2s.ic.gov or sc2c.sgov.gov. -- The BIG-IP system is configured to do failover or autoscale in those environments.
bugs.impact: Requires manual copying of the extra certificates, which are pointed to by AWS_CA_BUNDLE, to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: In this release, you can add all the needed certificates' URLs in the AWS user-data. The BIG-IP system then automatically downloads and stores the certificate and sets the $AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable and endpoint-url. To use the functionality, when launching the BIG-IP system from the AWS web console, specify the C2S certificate URL and test URL in the following format: c2s-keys-urls=url1,url2,url3;c2s-cert-test-url=ec2.us-iso-east-1.c2s.ic.gov:443; Where the syntax explanation is as follows: 1. The string literal : c2s-keys-urls= 2. List of comma separated URLs. 3. A semicolon (;). 4. The string literal : c2s-cert-test-url= 5. A URL which is of following format <A service name (e.g., ec2)>.<The region where it is running (e.g., us-iso-east-1)>.<the domain name :443 (e.g., c2s.ic.gov:443)> Example: ec2.us-iso-east-1.c2s.ic.gov:443;

bugs.title: TMM crashes when changing virtual server's profile to FastL4 profiles while traffic flows
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and creates core file when changing virtual server's profile from non-FastL4 to FastL4 profiles on-the-fly with traffic flowing.
bugs.conditions: Change the profile of the virtual server to FastL4 profiles while traffic is flowing.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not change the virtual server's profile while traffic is flowing.

bugs.title: APM SAML inline SSO documentation
bugs.symptoms: Internal multi-domain SSO does not work when the authentication cookie scope is host.
bugs.conditions: SSO configuration is assigned to an access profile for multi-domain SSO, and one of the following: -- There is no SSO configured for the requested authentication domain. -- The request does not map to configured authentication domains.
bugs.impact: Internal multi-domain SSO does not work.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Configure the application cookie scope as 'Domain'. -- Configure the SP-connector sp-location as 'External.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP APM can be configured as a SAML IdP to provide inline SSO for SPs not directly reachable by the client. For additional configuration details, see K06743491--Overview of BIG-IP APM SAML inline SSO :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K06743491.

bugs.title: Changing CGNAT SIP ALG profile log settings while handling traffic may cause tmm crash.
bugs.symptoms: Altering the router profile log settings (log publisher and logging profile) may cause the tmm to crash when handling traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- CGNAT SIP ALG. -- Changing log settings while handling traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Changing CGNAT SIP ALG profile log settings while handling traffic no longer causes tmm core.

bugs.title: FPS ajax-mapping property may be set even when it should be blocked
bugs.symptoms: Ajax mapping may be set only when 1) ajax-encryption is enabled OR 2) ajax-integrity AND strong-integrity are enabled. The bug allows to set ajax-mapping even for the following (invalid) configuration: ajax-encryption: disabled ajax-integrity: enabled strong-integrity: disabled
bugs.conditions: 1) ajax-encryption: disabled ajax-integrity: enabled strong-integrity: disabled 2) non-empty ajax-mapping
bugs.impact: System will set the ajax-mapping field when it should have been blocked.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: FPS should block ajax-mapping configuration when the pre-conditions weren't met.

bugs.title: Inefficient APM processing in large configurations.
bugs.symptoms: In configurations with large numbers of virtual servers or other entities, the apmd, oauth, and localdbmgr processes may consume large amounts of system resources.
bugs.conditions: -- Large configuration. -- APM provisioned. -- Multiple traffic groups exacerbate the effect.
bugs.impact: Heavy use of odd-numbered CPU cores may slow all control-plane operations, including user-interface response.
bugs.workaround: None known.

bugs.title: Portal Access: some multibyte characters in JavaScript code may not be handled correctly
bugs.symptoms: If JavaScript code contains multi-byte character which contains 0x0A in the last byte after conversion to UTF-32 form, then this character is handled as NEW LINE by Portal Access server-side JavaScript parser. If NEW LINE is not valid in this place, JavaScript code cannot be parsed.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript code with multi-byte character which contains 0x0A in the last byte after conversion to UTF-32 form, for example: //上 aa bb (上) gives (4E 0A) in UTF32 form. So this line is processed as the following TWO lines: // aa bb The second line is not a valid JavaScript code.
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access JavaScript parser handles multi-byte characters correctly.

bugs.title: SNMP trap destination configuration of network option is missing "default" keyword
bugs.symptoms: When SNMP trap destinations are configured, the user can specify the network that the traps are transmitted out from. By default, the routing table is consulted. Use the network keyword to overwrite this with either "management" or "other". There is also a "default" keyword, which was removed since it was confusing. However, this broke backward compatibility of the REST API; so, it was put back.
bugs.conditions: Including the "network default" keywords in trap configuration reports an error with version 13.0.0 where the "default" keyword was removed.
bugs.impact: Existing scripts may encounter errors if they used this keyword.
bugs.workaround: Don't use the "default" keyword with the snmp trap destination network configuration.
bugs.fix: The "default" keyword was put back.

bugs.title: When cloning a profile, URL parameters are not shown
bugs.symptoms: In Fraud Protection Service GUI, cloning a profile and then navigating to a URL, its parameters are not shown.
bugs.conditions: Provision and license Fraud Protection Service.
bugs.impact: Fraud Protection Service GUI.
bugs.workaround: Navigating again from Profiles will show the parameters.
bugs.fix: Parameters are now shown on first attempt after cloning a profile.

bugs.title: False positive illegal multipart violation
bugs.symptoms: A false positive multipart violation.
bugs.conditions: Uploading a file with a filename value that is encoded in non utf-8 encoding.
bugs.impact: A false positive violation, request rejected.
bugs.workaround: Might be workaround using an irule
bugs.fix: Corrected ASM multipart parsing.

bugs.title: i2000, i4000 i86 series platforms only - interface flow control not implemented
bugs.symptoms: On i2000, i4000 i86 series platforms the flow control field for an interface incorrectly displays the requested flow control, not what is actually programmed in the hardware. Hardware flow control support on these platforms was missing in BIG-IP. Bug 709869 tracks the problem that transmit flow-control on 1G interfaces was not implemented.
bugs.conditions: i2000, i4000 i86 series platforms Flow control on interfaces was set to something other than none.
bugs.impact: Flow control was not enabled on interfaces where it was requested.

bugs.title: "Enforce Ready" button has no effect for Signatures for Inactive Policy
bugs.symptoms: The "Enforce Ready" button has no effect for Signatures on Inactive Policies.
bugs.conditions: The user accesses "Enforcement Readiness" page for an Inactive Policy.
bugs.impact: Pressing "Enforce Ready" button has no effect.
bugs.workaround: Signature Staging can be disabled from "Application Security > Attack Signatures" page, or via REST.

bugs.title: Memory leak when OCSP is configured in clientSSL profile for C3D, or in serverSSL profile for server authentication
bugs.symptoms: There is a memory leak when OCSP is configured in the clientSSL profile for C3D feature, or in serverSSL profile for server certificate authentication.
bugs.conditions: OCSP is configured in the clientSSL profile for C3D feature, or in serverSSL profile for server certificate authentication.
bugs.impact: TMM will run out of memory.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Unexpected syntax error in TMSH AVR
bugs.symptoms: The following tmsh command does not work: tmsh show analytics http report view-by virtual measures { transactions } drilldown It fails with the following error message: 'Syntax Error: "drilldown" property requires at least one of (device device-list) to be specified before using.'
bugs.conditions: Whenever the affected tmsh command is run.
