bugs.title: vCMP host secondary member's cluster.conf file may replaced by that of vCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: -- clusterd restarts on secondary blade. -- Messages similar to the following are logged in each secondary blade's /var/log/ltm file as clusterd restarts: Management IP (<guest_management_ip>) already in use by (vcmp guest <guest_name>) -- Messages similar to the following are logged in the primary blade's /var/log/ltm file when clusterd restarts on a secondary blade: notice clusterd[3676]: 013a0006:5: Hello from slot 1. notice clusterd[3676]: 013a0006:5: Informing MCP about slot ID 1 member status. notice clusterd[3676]: 013a0006:5: Goodbye from slot 1.
bugs.conditions: -- Power-cycling a blade reproduces the issue most of the time. -- Possibly specific to platform: + This issue has been seen multiple hardware platforms, including B2100, B2150, B2250, and PB300. + Issue does not reproduce under the same conditions on a VIPRION 4800.
bugs.impact: Secondary slot on VIPRION hypervisor is in 'INOPERATIVE' state.
bugs.workaround: On the vCMP Host, copy the file /shared/db/cluster.conf from the primary to each secondary cluster members. For each secondary blade's slot, use a command similar to the following: scp /shared/db/cluster.conf slot<slot number>:/shared/db/cluster.conf Note: Implementing the workaround does not prevent the issue from recurring. An upgrade to an unaffected version is recommended.

bugs.title: Installs of 13.1.x on an MS800 fail
bugs.symptoms: Installing 13.1.x images on an MS800 fails with the message "Product has no root package for Mercury" in /var/log/liveinstall.log
bugs.conditions: Installing 13.1.x on an MS800
bugs.impact: Users can't install 13.1.x on a MS800 platform
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: SYN Cookie MSS for Fast L4 Profiles is limited to 256-9162
bugs.symptoms: User cannot configure SYN Cookie MSS values for Fast L4 Profiles outside of 256-9162.
bugs.conditions: Under syncookie activated condition, SYN Cookie MSS value is set to < 256.
bugs.impact: Under syncookie activated condition, server side MSS lower than SYN Cookie MSS lower limit cannot be honored on client side. As a result, server side MSS discards data segment if larger than SYN Cookie MSS lower limit.

bugs.title: Potentially fail to create user in AzureStack
bugs.symptoms: Using Microsoft Azure Stack on the BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) configured with password authentication, the system sometimes fails to create the provided user, which means that the VE admin cannot ssh in after deployment. bugs.title: Memory leak when using C3D
bugs.symptoms: When using the Client Certificate Constrained Delegation Support (C3D) feature, memory can leak.
bugs.conditions: Traffic passes through a virtual server with C3D enabled.
bugs.impact: Memory is leaked.

bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP/2 traffic

bugs.fix: TMM processes HTTP/2 traffic as expected

bugs.symptoms: If the system is upgraded from version 11.5.4-hf2, 11.6.0-hf4 and has more then 264 analytics profiles, the upgrade will fail.

bugs.impact: The upgrade will fail.

bugs.title: iRuleLx returning undefined value may cause TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: When an iRulesLX rule returns an undefined value, TMM may restart. An example of an undefined value is one where its jsonrpc v2.0 representation is missing required fields, such as "result".
bugs.conditions: iRulesLX is licensed, and a rule is run that returns an undefined value.
bugs.impact: Traffic is interrupted.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A TMM restart resulting from an iRulesLX rule returning an undefined value was fixed.

bugs.title: iRule command clientside and serverside may crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: Using clientside and serverside command in iRules may crash tmm.
bugs.conditions: Using such HTTP commands as HTTP::password in clientside and serverside nesting script.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this point.
bugs.fix: Fix clientside and serverside command do not work with certain HTTP commands.

bugs.title: TMM would crash if SSL Client profile could not load cert-key-chain successfully
bugs.symptoms: TMM would crash if SSL Client profile could not load cert-key-chain successfully, and SSL is working in the fwd-proxy-mode.
bugs.conditions: 1. SSL is working in the fwd-proxy-mode. 2. SSL could not load the cert-key-chain in the clientssl profile successfully. There could be couple of reasons: 2.1.We fail to configure the password required by the cert-key-chain. 2.2.Configured cert-key-chain type is not supported. 2.3.cert-key-chain name is incorrect.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure the cert-key-chain in the clientssl profile correctly.
bugs.fix: If we fail to load the cert-key-chain in the clientssl profile, and ssl is working in the fwd-proxy-mode, we will mark the corresponding ssl clientssl profile as invalid, then we will not accept the incoming SSL handshake destined to this profile.

bugs.title: If snmp disk-monitors minspace-type is percent then a 'load sys config default' fails
bugs.symptoms: The SNMP disk-monitors minspace-type default type is size. If you change it to percent, the 'load sys config default' command reports an error while loading the minspace value.
bugs.conditions: Loading default configuration when the disk-monitors minspace-type is percent.
bugs.impact: The 'load sys config default' fails.
bugs.workaround: First change the minspace-type to size and then issue the load defaults command.
bugs.fix: This bug has been fixed; the minspace-type size setting is included in the default configuration.

bugs.title: REST Framework HTTP header limit size increased to 8 KB
bugs.symptoms: HTTP Header size limit causing 'Error getting auth token from login provider' GUI messages.
bugs.conditions: A client uses an HTTP Header larger than 4 KB to make a request to the REST framework.
bugs.impact: Users cannot login or access certain pages in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Clear browser cookies, or otherwise reduce the size of the HTTP headers, so that the entire content HTTP headers is smaller than 4 KB.
bugs.fix: The HTTP header size limit for the REST Framework has been increased to 8 KB to match the limit set by Apache.

bugs.title: In-use, expired certificates now have a warning in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: If your BIG-IP device is using an expired certificate, you will now see a warning banner in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered if your device is using an expired certificate.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: You can see all expired certificates on the system by running the following tmsh command: tmsh run sys crypto check-cert
bugs.fix: System management GUI shows a prominent warning when an expired SSL certificate is in use.

You can configure this feature by using the following TMSH option: tmsh modify sys global-settings gui-expired-cert-alert enabled/disabled

bugs.title: When BIG-IP as OAuth AS has missing OAuth Profile in the Access profile, the error log is not clear
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system configured as OAuth AS has a missing OAuth Profile in the Access profile, the error log is not clear. It shows an error indicating 'OAuth mode is not set' instead of showing 'OAuth Profile is not configured'. In this case, the error 'OAuth mode is not set' means that the OAuth Profile is not associated in the Access profile of the virtual server acting as BIG-IP OAuth Authentication server.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is configured as OAuth AS. -- The Access profile is not configured with OAuth profile.
bugs.impact: Confusing error message that leads to delay in troubleshooting the OAuth configuration.
bugs.workaround: Configure an OAuth Profile in the Access profile of the virtual server acting as BIG-IP OAuth AS.

bugs.title: DNSSEC Signed Zone Transfers of Large Zones Can Be Incomplete (missing NSEC3s and RRSIGs)
bugs.symptoms: It is possible that when performing a sufficiently large DNSSEC signed zone transfer (e.g., ~1 KB records) that the final packet (or several packets) of NSEC3s and RRSIGs could be missing from the zone. This issue can be detected using a free third-party tool such as ldns-verify-zone or some other DNSSEC validating tool.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic DNSSEC signing of zone transfers is configured for a given zone from an authoritative DNS Server (this could be on-box BIND, off-box BIND, etc.), or from DNS Express.
bugs.impact: The DNSSEC signed zone transfer could be incomplete, that is missing some NSEC3s and RRSIGs. An incomplete DNSSEC zone is considered an invalid zone.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: DNSSEC signed zone transfers from general authoritative DNS Servers as well as from DNS Express are now complete regardless of the number of records in the zone.

bugs.title: Upgrades from pre-12.0.0 BIG-IPs to 12.0.0 with WideIPs with ipv6-no-error-response enabled will no longer delete AAAA-type WideIPs
bugs.symptoms: A pre-12.0.0 WideIP with ipv6-no-error-response enabled and a IPv4 last-resort-pool will only spawn an A-type WideIP after the upgrade
bugs.conditions: Pre-12.0.0 WideIP with an IPv4 last-resort-pool and ipv6-no-error-response enabled.
bugs.impact: Loss of the AAAA-type WideIP configuration item
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue where upgrading a Pre-12.0.0 WideIP with a last-resort-pool with only IPv4 pool members, and ipv6-no-error-respons enabled would only create an A-Type WideIP after the upgrade. Now, the AAAA-type WideIP will also be greated, with no-error-response enabled.

bugs.title: BGP may keep announcing routes after disabling route health injection
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue BIG-IP with BGP configured may continue to announce routes even after disabling the virtual address or disabling route announcement on the virtual address.
bugs.conditions: BGP configured with multiple routes announced via Virtual-address route announcements. Configuration changes made on the BGP configuration itself. Virtual address or its route health announcement disabled.
bugs.impact: Prefixes continue to exist in the BGP table even after disabling the virtual address (visible via imish with the "show ip bgp" command); which will continue to announce the prefix to configured peers.
bugs.workaround: Workaround would be to restart the dynamic routing process.
bugs.fix: BGP may no longer keeps announcing routes after disabling route health injection

bugs.title: Nitrox 3 compression hangs/unable to recover
bugs.symptoms: LTM logs show the following message: Nitrox 3, Hang Detected: compression device was reset When the error manifests, there will be three error messages sent to the log over a period of several seconds. The device is then considered unrecoverable and marked down, and will no longer accept compression requests.
bugs.conditions: This applies only to vCMP guests. Some compression requests can stall the device after a bad compression request is made. Note: Traffic volume and concurrence, along with the type of error have to occur together in order to result in this issue, so the issue is not easily reproduced.
bugs.impact: Once the device is marked down, compression will be sent to the software compression provider, until tmm on the device is restarted. This can cause local CPU utilization to climb.
bugs.workaround: There is no complete workaround without a software fix. However, compression will always default to the software compression provider when hardware cannot be recovered. There are three recovery options available if the TMM-internal reset fails to recover the compression device automatically. These should be employed in this order: A. Restart tmm using the command: bigstart restart tmm. B. Restart the vCMP guest. C. Restart the host (which restarts all guests). Note: Because of the traffic volume, timing, and error type that cause this condition, this error might recur. This issue appears to be caused by a particular compression request. So regardless of the recovery method you execute, the problem may recur in a short time, or months later.
bugs.fix: Compression device reset recovery made more robust for some compression failures.

bugs.title: Default SNI clientssl profile's sni_certsn_hash can be freed while in use by other profiles.
bugs.symptoms: SSL SNI mechanism creates a hash containing a mapping between SAN entries in a given profile's certificate and the profile. This hash is owned by the default NI profile, however is held by the other profiles on the VIP without a reference. If a connection utilizes SNI to use a non-default SNI profile *and* the default SNI profile reinitializes its state for any reason, the prf->sni_certsn_hash can be cleared and freed, leaving the existing connection(s) with profiles that refer to the freed hash. If then the connection attempts a renegotiation that causes the hash to be used, the freed hash can cause a fault should it have been reused in the meantime (i.e. the contents are invalid). The fix: When the default SNI profile is initializing, and SSL handshake is searching SAN/COMMON cert from non-default SNI profile, stop the search and return NULL.
bugs.conditions: SNI configured with one default SNI profile, one or multiple SNI profiles. The default SNI profile is changed and renegotiation with SNI(with non-default SNI profile) is issued.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When the default SNI profile is initializing, and SSL handshake is searching SAN/COMMON cert from non-default SNI profile, stop the search and return NULL.

bugs.title: ePVA hardware acceleration/offloading needs flow prioritization
bugs.symptoms: The system does not provide a prioritization mechanism that supports application-level control of which flows utilize the limited FPGA resources. As a result, higher priority flows might often be processed in software because the ePVA resources are consumed with lower priority flows.
bugs.conditions: Using ePVA hardware for processing flows.
bugs.impact: Higher priority flows might often be processed in software rather than hardware, which might be preferred.
bugs.fix: The system now provides a prioritization mechanism that supports application-level control of which flows utilize the limited FPGA resources.

bugs.title: Initial vCMP guest creations can fail if certain hotfixes are used
bugs.symptoms: vCMP guest fails to enter the 'provisioned' or 'deployed' states and similar messages can be seen in /var/log/ltm: -- vcmpd[14254]: 01510003:2: Guest (guest_name): Install failed. -- vcmpd[14254]: 01510004:3: Guest (guest_name): Install to VDisk /shared/vmdisks/guest_name.img FAILED: Child exited with non-zero exit code: 255
bugs.conditions: Creating vCMP guest using certain hotfix images, such as BIG-IP HF software released as partial .iso software images, and engineering hotfixes.
bugs.impact: vCMP guest cannot be created.
bugs.workaround: 1. Create and deploy the vCMP guest using the full .iso base software image. 2. Log in to the vCMP guest once it has finished starting up. 3. Apply the hotfix image or engineering hotfix.
bugs.fix: Guest creation succeeds.

bugs.title: bigd core due to memory leak, especially with FQDN nodes
bugs.symptoms: The bigd daemon may core due to excessive memory consumption caused by a slow memory leak that occurs when creating or updating an LTM node or pool member. This memory leak occurs much more quickly when using FQDN nodes/pool members with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled.
bugs.conditions: The bigd memory leak occurs slowly with non-FQDN nodes/pool members, but much more quickly when using FQDN nodes/pool members with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled. An additional leak occurs each time an FQDN name is resolved for an FQDN node or pool member. The rate of the leak in this case is determined by the number of FQDN nodes/pool members configured with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled, and the FQDN name resolution interval (determined by the 'interval' setting of the 'fqdn' configuration for the FQDN node).
bugs.impact: The bigd daemon may core due to excessive memory consumption.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to work around this issue by one of the following methods: 1. Configure a longer 'interval' value in the 'fqdn' configuration for configured FQDN nodes. 2. Configure FQDN nodes/pool members without the 'autopopulate' setting enabled. 3. Restart the bigd daemon before memory consumption becomes excessive. (Note that this may interrupt traffic to configured pool members.)

bugs.title: 'Export Suggestions' from Traffic Learning fails for suggestions that previously associated requests are no longer available.
bugs.symptoms: Export Suggestions operations fail when none of the previously associated requests are available.
bugs.conditions: There are suggestions for which associated requests are no longer available.
bugs.impact: 'Export Suggestions' fails.
bugs.fix: All suggestions can be successfully exported.

bugs.title: Enhance the GUI to handle large number of SSL profiles
bugs.symptoms: It is hard to manage large numbers of SSL profiles through GUI, and sometimes GUI crashes due to memory issues because of it.
bugs.conditions: Have large number of SSL profiles, certificates, and keys.
bugs.impact: It is hard to manage large number SSL objects through GUI and sometimes GUI crashes due to memory issues.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to manage large number of SSL objects.
bugs.fix: GUI user experience is enhanced to ease the management of large number SSL objects through GUI without crash.

bugs.title: Use native driver for 82599 NICs instead of UNIC
bugs.symptoms: -- Lower performance in TPS. -- Increased CPU consumption for throughput.
bugs.conditions: -- Running BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) (UNIC is the default Virtual Function Network Driver for VE). -- High data rates, perhaps particularly when connection mirroring is configured.
bugs.impact: Lower TPS performance numbers and higher CPU usage in throughput tests.
bugs.workaround: In case of UNIC, extra CPUs must be allocated to handle SoftIRQs for higher performance.
bugs.fix: This release provides a native driver based on F5's physical platforms.

bugs.title: Log Search option in GSLB similar to one in Logs:Audit:Search in Web GUI.
bugs.symptoms: This is an improvement for the logs search in the Web GUI under System:Logs:GSLB. The improvement offers more ways to search through the GSLB logs.
bugs.conditions: No specific conditions need to be met.
bugs.impact: No impact. The GSLB log search in the Web GUI will now offer more ways to search the logs.

bugs.title: The 'SYN Challenge Handling' setting of a TCP profile can revert to defaults when updating the profile using the GUI
bugs.symptoms: The 'SYN Challenge Handling' setting of a TCP profile can be reverted to defaults when a TCP profile is updated using the BIG-IP management GUI.
bugs.conditions: The SYN Challenge Handling settings of a TCP profile have previously been set to non-default values, and a configuration change is later made to the same TCP profile using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Loss of TCP profile syn challenge configuration settings
bugs.workaround: In the GUI, specifically set the SYN Challenge Handling fields after making an update to other TCP profile fields, or use tmsh to make the changes instead SYN Challenge GUI Setting: Nominal TMSH: syn-cookie-enable enabled syn-cookie-whitelist disabled GUI Setting: Challenge and Remember TMSH: syn-cookie-enable enabled syn-cookie-whitelist enabled GUI Setting: Disable Challenges: syn-cookie-enable disabled syn-cookie-whitelist disabled
bugs.fix: Now syn challenge handling setting isn't overwritten when tcp profile is updated

bugs.title: ASM Single page application causes JavaScript error when cross domain request is sent
bugs.symptoms: JavaScript error is reported to the browser developer's console: 'Refused to get unsafe header X-Security-Action', 'Refused to get unsafe header 'X-Security-Token'
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Bot defense/DoS Application/ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- Single page application enabled.
bugs.impact: Cross domain requests might be not handled properly.
bugs.workaround: Disable single page application using one of the following workarounds: -- Go to the bot defense profile in the GUI and disable single page application. -- Run the following tmsh command: tmsh modify security bot-defense profile all { single-page-application disabled } -- Go to DoS application profile in the GUI and disable single page application. -- Run the following tmsh command: tmsh modify security dos profile all { application modify { all { single-page-application disabled } } } -- To disable single page application for an ASM policy, run the following shell command: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal del single_page_application
bugs.fix: Single page application now handles cross domain requests for configured domains only.

bugs.title: FQDN nodes or pool members flap when DNS response received
bugs.symptoms: When an LTM pool is configured with FQDN nodes or pool members, the LTM pool and associated virtual server(s) may transition from an UP to DOWN state and back over a period of a few seconds. Such an event is accompanied by log messages similar to the following: -- notice mcpd[#]: 01071682:5: SNMP_TRAP: Virtual /Common/vs_test has become unavailable -- notice mcpd[#]: 010719e7:5: Virtual Address /Common/123.45.67.89 general status changed from GREEN to RED. -- notice mcpd[#]: 010719e8:5: Virtual Address /Common/123.45.67.89 monitor status changed from UP to DOWN. -- err mcpd[#]: 01020066:3: The requested Pool Member (/Common/Test_Pool /Common/test-dummy.com-12.34.56.78 443) already exists in partition Common. -- notice bigd[##]: 01060144:5: Pool /Common/Test_Pool member /Common/test-dummy.com-12.34.56.78 session status enabled by monitor -- notice bigd[##]: 01060145:5: Pool /Common/Test_Pool member /Common/test-dummy.com-12.34.56.78 monitor status up. [ /Common/mon_test_https: UP ] [ was checking for 0hr:0min:2sec ] -- notice mcpd[#]: 01071681:5: SNMP_TRAP: Virtual /Common/vs_test has become available -- notice mcpd[#]: 010719e7:5: Virtual Address /Common/123.45.67.89 general status changed from RED to GREEN. -- notice mcpd[#]: 010719e8:5: Virtual Address /Common/123.45.67.89 monitor status changed from DOWN to UP. This symptom repeats each time a DNS query is performed to resolve the FQDN node/pool-member name to its IP addresses, based on the 'interval' value configured for the FQDN node. This symptom occurs only when the 'autopopulate' value is set to 'enabled' for the FQDN node/pool-member.
bugs.impact: LTM pool and virtual server are briefly and periodically marked DOWN. Traffic may be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Either of the following methods can be used to work around this issue: -- Configure static IP addresses instead of FQDN nodes/pool-members. -- Set the 'autopopulate' value to 'disabled' for the FQDN node/pool-member, if possible (that is, if only one IP address is required/expected to be returned for the FQDN name, which means that the 'autopopulate' feature of FQDN nodes/pool-members is not required).
bugs.conditions: -- LTM pool is configured with FQDN nodes or pool members. -- The 'autopopulate' value is set to 'enabled' for the FQDN node/pool-member.
bugs.fix: FQDN node/pool-member and corresponding pool and virtual server are no longer briefly marked DOWN when the DNS server is queried to resolve the FQDN name, with the 'autopopulate' feature enabled for the FQDN node/pool-member. This issue is resolved by the FQDNv2 feature re-implementation in this version of the software.

bugs.title: memory leak in Machine Certificate Check agent of the apmd process
bugs.symptoms: apmd process leaks memory in Machine Certificate Check agent
bugs.conditions: - Machine Certificate Check agent is configured in an Access Policy - inspected machine certificate is revoked by CRL
bugs.impact: apmd may grow in size. this may lead to apmd process or some other processes at BIG-IP to be killed by OOM-killer
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround
bugs.fix: The memory leak is fixed.

bugs.title: BIG-IP handles some pathmtu messages incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 virtual servers incorrectly handle some pathmtu messages, such as ICMPv4 unreachable/fragmentation needed and ICMPv6 packet too big.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are true: -- The client sends a window scaling factor greater than 0 (zero). -- The server sends a window scaling factor equal to 0 (zero). -- The pmtu message is within the window, but does not reflect the exact expected sequence number. The delta is bigger than the advertised window scaled at a factor of 0 (zero).
bugs.impact: pmtu message is erroneously ignored.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Network Access cannot be established on Windows 10 RS4
bugs.symptoms: Network Access cannot be established on Microsoft Windows 10 RS4. Both EdgeClient and F5 VPN fails with the following error: An incorrect structure size was detected. Note: Custom Dial-up entry client is not affected. This is caused by Windows 10 RS4 regression in Remote Access System (RAS).
bugs.conditions: Networks Access connection fails when any of the following conditions are met: -- The Windows system is clean Windows 10 RS4 installation -- The Windows system has never connected to APM. -- The Windows system previously was connected to APM, but the BIG-IP Administrator modified Network Access resource settings When all of the following conditions are met, Network Access continues to work, unless the Administrator modifies the resource configuration or the user connects to a new APM server: -- The Windows system was previously connected to a specific virtual server on a particular APM. -- The Windows system was upgraded from previous Windows 10 version to Windows 10 RS4. -- The Windows system Administrator has not modified any settings of Network Access resource.
bugs.impact: Network Access connection cannot be established.
bugs.workaround: None. Note: This is caused by Windows 10 RS4 regression in RAS.
bugs.fix: Due to an issue introduced in Windows RS4, a VPN connection could not be established. This has been fixed.

bugs.title: Failure deleting GTM Monitors when used on mulitple Virtual Servers with the same ip:port combination
bugs.symptoms: User would get "monitor is in use" when attempting to delete a GTM Monitor, even after removing that monitor from all GTM Virtual Servers
bugs.conditions: Attach a gtm monitor to multiple gtm virtual servers in the same transaction, where both of the virtual servers are monitoring the same ip:port
bugs.impact: User will not be able to ever delete the un-used gtm monitor
bugs.workaround: Remove monitor from VSs Reload GTM configuration with tmsh load sys config gtm-only Delete monitor
bugs.fix: Fixed issue preventing users from deleting an unused GTM monitor, if that monitor was attached to two different GTM virtual servers of the same ip+port combination.

bugs.title: EPSEC package rolls back to previous version whenever the device is rebooted
bugs.symptoms: An old EPSEC package is made active during a reboot.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP has two epsec packages (one is default and one is latest). -- The epsec package marked as 'latest' is active EPSEC -- A reboot occurs.
bugs.impact: You must re-install the new epsec package after reboot.
bugs.workaround: Re-install the new EPSEC package after reboot.

bugs.title: Improper blade insertion can cause kernel panic
bugs.symptoms: An improperly inserted blade might cause a kernel panic due to unstable power and signals.
bugs.conditions: Improper blade insertion.
bugs.impact: Kernel panic or many other kinds of problems.
bugs.workaround: Reinsert the blade. Note: It is not possible to fix or handle unstable hardware signals caused by insecure contacts in the socket.

bugs.title: Some ASM operations delayed due to scheduled ASU update
bugs.symptoms: Some ASM operations (such as Apply Policy) are delayed while a scheduled ASU update is in progress. This issue affects only 12.1.3.x from 12.1.3.2 and later.
bugs.conditions: A scheduled ASM update is in progress on systems running v12.1.3.x.
bugs.impact: Some ASM operations, such as Apply Policy, are delayed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Other ASM operations are no longer blocked by scheduled ASU update.

bugs.title: Hundreds of cron-initiated ASM-config processes seem to be stuck
bugs.symptoms: In a very rare scenario, hundreds of cron-initiated ASM-config processes seem to be stuck waiting for a lock.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Hundreds of cron-initiated ASM-config processes seem to be stuck waiting for a lock.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM.
bugs.fix: Only a single cron-initiated ASM-config process runs at a time.

bugs.title: 2000/4000 series platform after applying performance upgrade license does not show correct name in show sys hardware
bugs.symptoms: Applying a performance upgrade license does not change the name shown in 'tmsh show sys hardware' when running BIG-IP versions 12.1.0 or earlier.
bugs.conditions: -- 2000 or 4000 series platform running with standard license. -- Apply a performance upgrade license. -- Running versions 12.1.0 or earlier.
bugs.impact: The name does not change, although the performance of the system is upgraded when the required reboot is complete after applying a performance upgrade license. This is a cosmetic issue only.
bugs.workaround: None. Rebooting does not update to the correct name.

bugs.title: Stalled mirrored flows on HA next-active when OneConnect is used.
bugs.symptoms: -- 'tmctl -d blade tmm/umem_usage_stat | grep xdata' may show increased memory usage. -- 'tmsh show sys connect' shows idle flows.
bugs.conditions: - OneConnect profile is configured. - High availability (HA) mirroring is enabled.
bugs.impact: - Some flows are mirrored incorrectly. - Stalled flows may occupy a lot of memory.
bugs.workaround: Disable OneConnect.
bugs.fix: Stalled mirrored flows no longer appear when OneConnect is used.

bugs.title: Users cannot distinguish between full APM and APM Lite License when looking at the provisioning page
bugs.symptoms: APM and APM Lite licenses are not distinguishable from the Provisioning UI: they both show as Licensed but APM lite only includes licenses for 10 sessions.
bugs.conditions: Viewing APM and APM Lite licenses in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Cannot distinguish the difference in types of licenses.
bugs.workaround: Check license file and verify what type of apm license is enabled: mod_apm (Full APM) or mod_apml (APM Lite).
bugs.fix: Change UI to state limited instead of licensed when only mod_apml is licensed.

bugs.title: Unable to add policy to virtual server; error = Failed to compile the combined policies
bugs.symptoms: LTM policy does not compile if it has more than one similar condition, and some of them refer to datagroup and others to non-datagroup types. The policy compiles if similar conditions all refer to datagroups or to non-datagroups. 010716d8:3: Compilation of ltm policies for virtual server /Common/vs_name failed; Failed to compile the combined policies.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy that has more than one similar condition. -- Some conditions refer to datagroup types. -- Some conditions refer to non-datagroup types. Following is an example of such an LTM policy (i.e., referring to both datagroup and non-datagroup types): ltm policy /Common/example_ltm_policy { published-copy /Common/block_URI requires { http } rules { example_Rule { conditions { 0 { http-host host datagroup /Common/example_datagroup <------ Datagroup } 1 { http-host host values { example.com } <------ Non-Datagroup } } } } strategy /Common/first-match }
bugs.impact: LTM policy does not compile. Cannot use the policy.
bugs.workaround: Create a datagroup for the non-datagroup type and use it in policy instead.
bugs.fix: LTM Policy compiles if it has more than one similar condition, and some of them refer to datagroup and others to non-datagroup types.

bugs.title: Unexpected TMUI output in SSL Certificate Instance page
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the TMUI for SSL Certificate Instances does not produce the expected HTML output.
bugs.conditions: Authenticated TMUI user browsing the SSL Certificate Instance page.
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output.
bugs.fix: SSL Certificate Instance now produces the expected HTML output.

bugs.title: Users cannot use Horizon View HTML5 client to launch Horizon 7.4 resources
bugs.symptoms: When using VMware View HTML5 client, end users are able to authenticate and see available View resources on the APM webtop. However, any attempt to launch the resource (desktop or application) in HTML5 mode momentarily appears to function, but then redirects to the initial APM login page.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- BIG-IP APM is protecting VMware Horizon View 7.4 resources. -- End user tries to launch a View resource from the APM webtop using the Horizon View HTML5 client.
bugs.impact: End user cannot launch VMware View resources with View HTML5 client.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following workarounds: -- If you are already running Horizon 7.4, use native View clients instead. -- If you have not upgraded to Horizon 7.4, stay on an older Horizon release until this issue is resolved. -- If you are running BIG-IP APM release 13.1.0, you can add the following iRule to the virtual server that handles HTML5 client connections: when HTTP_REQUEST { if { ([info exists tmm_apm_view_uuid]) && ([HTTP::method] == "GET") && ([HTTP::uri] ends_with "/portal/webclient/sessiondata")} { HTTP::cookie remove "sessionDataServiceId" } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { ([info exists tmm_apm_view_uuid]) } { set cookieNames [HTTP::cookie names] foreach aCookie $cookieNames { set path [HTTP::cookie path $aCookie] if {[string length $path] > 0} { HTTP::cookie path $aCookie "/f5vdifwd/vmview/$tmm_apm_view_uuid$path" } } } } Important: -- After applying the iRule and before attempting a connection, be sure to clear all cache and cookies from the client systems. Otherwise, the test operation may need to be executed before exhibiting successful behavior. -- The iRule workaround is for BIG-IP APM release 13.1.0. It is not supported for older BIG-IP releases.
bugs.fix: Horizon View version 7.4 in HTML5 mode now functions correctly with APM.

bugs.title: Phishing alert failed on IB login page
bugs.symptoms: Phishing alert won't be sent in phishing site which will be uploaded from NAB IB login page.
bugs.conditions: 1. Copy NAB IB login page and upload it as phishing site. 2. Navigate to the new phishing site.
bugs.impact: Phishing alert won't be sent.
bugs.fix: After that fix' the phishing alert will be sent.

bugs.title: Web Acceleration: TMM may crash on very large HTML files with conditional comments
bugs.symptoms: Web Acceleration feature may not handle big HTML file with improper conditional comments inside in some cases. TMM may crash processing such files if Web Acceleration profile is attached to VIP.
bugs.conditions: - HTML file with conditional comments inside: <!--[if condition...]> ... <![endif]--> - The size of "condition" from the pattern above is comparable with RAM size of BIG-IP box, i.e. ~8-10GB.
bugs.impact: TMM crash interrupts all active sessions.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now Web Acceleration feature can handle long HTML conditional comments correctly.

bugs.title: In older RAID BIG-IP systems, storage provisioning is not possible when a drive is missing.
bugs.symptoms: Any task requiring modification of application storage volumes does not succeed. This includes re-provisioning, which occurs automatically during software upgrades.
bugs.conditions: -- When a drive is not present in a drive bay on the following platforms: + BIG-IP 6900 + BIG-IP 8900 + BIG-IP 10000 + BIG-IP 11050 -- An application that requires storage volumes is provisioned, such as ASM.
bugs.impact: Tasks requiring modification of application storage volumes such as software upgrades or re-provisioning fails.
bugs.workaround: Check RAID status before software upgrades or re-provisioning. Address any degraded RAID issues, such as a missing drive, before upgrades and/or re-provisioning.

bugs.title: Tcl commands like "HTTP::path -normalize" do not return normalized path.
bugs.symptoms: When using HTTP::path with the -normalized parameter: "%2E%2E" is converted to ".." (expected) "/foo/../bar" is converted to "/bar" (expected) "/foo/%2E%2E/bar" is converted to "/foo/../bar" (unexpected)
bugs.conditions: The TCL command HTTP::path -normalize does not return normalized path as expected.
bugs.impact: Unexpected result.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The TCL command HTTP::path -normalize should return normalized path.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing the handshake message relating to OCSP, after the SSL connection is closed
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when receiving the HUDEVT_SSL_OCSP_RESUME_CLNT_HS after the SSL connection is closed.
bugs.conditions: -- The SSL connection has been closed. -- SSL receives the HUDEVT_SSL_OCSP_RESUME_CLNT_HS message.
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now ensures that SSL can still properly process the messages, even when the SSL connection is closed.

bugs.title: TMUI - Subject Alternative Name text box is not populated when renewing SAN-enabled cert
bugs.symptoms: GUI SSL Certificate renew does not auto populate Subject Alternative Name text box with the current certificates Subject Alternative Name.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create/Import a certificate with SAN in to the system. 2. Try to renew the same certificate 3. SAN text box in renew screen is not auto populated with certificate's SAN.
bugs.impact: GUI SSL certificate renew screen does not auto populate SAN text box with current certificate's SAN, user has to enter it manually.
bugs.workaround: Copy paste SAN from current certificate while renewing the certificate through GUI.
bugs.fix: GUI SSL certificate renew screen auto populates SAN text box with current certificate's SAN.

bugs.title: IP Intelligence categories documentation needs to be updated
bugs.symptoms: The AFM Manual topic "IP intelligence categories" does not match AFM GUI "Black List Categories".
bugs.conditions: Doc does not match GUI.
bugs.impact: Doc only
bugs.workaround: Look at GUI and Help for details.

bugs.title: SNMP OIDs (NA throughput) incorrect when compression is disable
bugs.symptoms: SNMP OIDs related to Network Access VPN tunnel or connectivity traffic are not updated if compression is not enabled. However, the definitions for connectivity traffic make it seem like they should be updated.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create an access policy with Network Access resource (no compression enabled). Also, connectivity profile with no compression. 2. Assign this to a virtual server. 3. Establish a VPN tunnel, and download a large file. 4. Compare the SNMP OID values before and after this large file download via VPN tunnel.
bugs.impact: Confusion and graphs that don't seem to show the expected traffic.
bugs.workaround: Turn on compression to see the stats updated.

bugs.title: OAuth Discovery Auto Pilot is implemented
bugs.symptoms: This now adds a new capability to allow user to select a period to have OAuth auto discovery automatically pull down JWT keys.
bugs.conditions: Follow the new added UI and configure frequency to start.
bugs.impact: No impact, it has usability improvement over manual discovery.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: New auto pilot capability is added for usability.

bugs.title: nitrox_diag utility generates QKView files with 5 MB maximum file size limit
bugs.symptoms: When nitrox_diag generates a QKView file, the utility does not use the -s0 flag for the qkview command. That means there is a 5 MB file-size limit for the resulting QKView file nitrox_diag generates.
bugs.conditions: Run the nitrox_diag command.
bugs.impact: QKView files generated in response to running the nitrox_diag command might not contain all necessary information, for example, the result might contain truncated log files.
bugs.workaround: After running nitrox_diag, run the following command to generate a complete QKView file: qkview -s0
bugs.fix: Nitrox_diag utility now uses the -s0 command to generate QKView files, so there is no longer a 5 MB maximum file size limit, and the full QKView file is created.

bugs.title: IPv6 NDP with vlan-groups: unexpected Neighbor Advertisement and ICMPv6 unreachable messages
bugs.symptoms: Stale NDP entries will generate an ICMPv6 Neighbor Advertisement (NA) if Neighbor Solicitations (NS) are received in rapid succession.
bugs.conditions: Neighbor entry being queried by the NS is in the probe state caused by the previous NS packet.
bugs.impact: Unexpected NA informs about the reachability of the neighbor that in fact might be not reachable.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Unexpected Neighbor Advertisement is no longer generated if Neighbor Solicitations are received in rapid succession.

bugs.title: iApp import immediately merges arbitrary configuration objects
bugs.symptoms: Using the 'iApp Template' import GUI to import a file that contains valid configuration objects results in immediate changes to BIG-IP system configuration. This is different from typical iApp workflows, which require an Application instance sourced from a Template. Instead, in this case, configuration changes are applied immediately upon import.
bugs.conditions: File that contains valid configuration objects is imported via iApp Template import functionality.
bugs.impact: Changes contained in the imported file are immediately applied to BIG-IP system configuration.
bugs.workaround: Audit all files imported to the BIG-IP system. If files contain valid configuration objects, expect configuration changes to occur immediately upon import to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: This release adds a confirmation message to the GUI iApp Template Upload, similar to the one for tmsh.

bugs.title: Discover task may get stuck in CHECK_IS_ACTIVE step
bugs.symptoms: The discover tasks is running periodically after user creates the task. But it may get stuck in the middle steps and fail to run periodically.
bugs.conditions: When HA failover group is set up and a discover task is created on one of the devices.
bugs.impact: The discover task will periodically pull the OpenID information and update oauth jwt and jwk configurations in MCP. If the task sticks, the jwt and jwk configuration will not sync to the latest version and may cause access policy fail.
bugs.workaround: If the task is stuck in any step that is not SLEEP_AND_RUN_AGAIN for more than one minute, manually cancel and delete the task and create the same task again.
bugs.fix: Discover task no longer gets stuck in CHECK_IS_ACTIVE step.

bugs.title: 'Apply Access Policy' light on for source profile after copying
bugs.symptoms: Copying Access Profile with advanced customization options might cause 'Apply Access Policy' light on the source profile.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: 1. Create an access profile. 2. Create a webtop resource and assign to the access policy via VPE's Advanced Resource Assign agent. 3. Go to customization, in advanced mode, change the item under webtop, e.g., webtop_help.inc and save it. 4. Apply the policy. 5. Make copy of the profile.
bugs.impact: 'Apply Access Policy' light is turned on (yellow) for the source access profile.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: No change to the source profile: the light is green.

bugs.title: Multiple TMM cores in http_cookie_decrypt
bugs.symptoms: Client/server SSL profiles, HTTP profile, and cookie persistence profile experiences multiple cores in http_cookie_decrypt.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with a virtual server configured as follows: -- Client/server SSL profiles. -- HTTP profile. -- Cookie persistence profile
bugs.impact: Device fails over. TMM cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This is likely a rarely occurring event. There is no workaround short of not using encryption for HTTP cookie persistence.

bugs.title: BADOS monitoring with Grafana requires admin privilege
bugs.symptoms: Current Grafana monitoring requires admin privilege. Grafana stores its internal database in unencrypted format, so the admin password can be extracted from a compromised computer.
bugs.conditions: Monitoring using Grafana.
bugs.impact: Guest user cannot access data needed for Grafana.
bugs.fix: There is now a REST call to pool the Grafana statistics. This allows any user (including guest), not just admin or root, to access data needed for Grafana.
bugs.behavior: This release introduces the following tmsh commands: -- tmsh run util admdb - for help + list-element path_folder - lists folder + view-element path_file - view file contents + list-metrics path vs + table-query base_path db sRate tsfiles ts metric_columns_aliases The path must be under /shared/admdb, for example: -- run util admdb list-element /shared/admdb/default/_a_l_l -- run util admdb view-element /shared/admdb/default/_a_l_l/info.sysinfo/1000/1522229248000.txt -- run util admdb table-query /shared/admdb default 1000 '[1522233344000]' '[1522234774492,1522235074492]' '[["info.attack",["v0"],"Attack"],["sig.health",["v0"],"Health"],["info.learning",["v0"],"Learning"],["info.learning",["v2"],"Learned samples"]]'

bugs.title: Interface Flow Control Status does not update when using copper SFPs and Link Partner Flow Control is disabled
bugs.symptoms: When setting the flow control value of an interface with a copper SFP to any value other than 'none' and the link partner has flow control disabled on their end, the interface stats will not reflect the configured flow control setting. This is because the interface stats reflect the negotiated link state rather than the advertised capabilities.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP device is using copper SFPs. -- Flow control is enabled on an interface. -- That interface is connected to another device where flow control has not been enabled. For example, an administrator might perform the following on a BIG-IP system with a copper SFP on interface 1.1: # modify net interface 1.1 flow-control tx-rx # show net interface 1.1 all-properties Under the 'Flow Ctrl' column of the interface properties, the value will indicate 'none' even though the interface was configured to enable transmit and receive flow control. This is because the column does not indicate the advertised capabilities but rather the negotiated property of the link.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact, as flow control cannot be performed until both link partners agree to support it.
bugs.workaround: Flow control must be enabled on the remote device and the link must be re-negotiated, in order for the flow control configuration to take effect and be reflected in the interface properties of the link.
bugs.fix: Interface Flow Control Status is now updated when using copper SFPs and Link Partner Flow Control is disabled. Note: The 'Flow Ctrl Req' label under 'tmsh show net interface all-properties' differs in previous versions: 'Flow Ctrl'. The value listed is the same, however, and represents the admin-requested value, and not the operational value.

bugs.title: DNS::question 'set' options are applied to packet, but not to already parsed dns_msg
bugs.symptoms: For certain types of iRules, using the DNS command DNS::question for type AAAA, when the DNS transparent cache is involved in the filter, the type can be reverted.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS transparent cache. -- Using an iRule similar to the following: when DNS_REQUEST { DNS::question type AAAA }
bugs.impact: When the packet goes to the pool, the type is reverted.
bugs.workaround: Enable gslb or dnsx on the profile.

bugs.title: Modify LTM client SSL or server SSL profile ciphers default-value does not work
bugs.symptoms: The value 'default-value for the ciphers attribute of client SSL or server SSL profiles does not set the ciphers attribute to inherited-from-parent, but instead copies the parent profile's current value. Additionally, it does not set the ciphers attribute to inherited if the attribute had previously been customized.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a child client SSL or server SSL profile. 2. Customize the child profile's ciphers value. 3. Modify the child profile's ciphers value via TMSH to 'default-value'
bugs.impact: Any subsequent changes to the parent profile's ciphers value are not inherited by the child profile because the ciphers attribute is considered to be customized, and has not been reset to inherited.
bugs.workaround: Any of the following workarounds work: 1. Simultaneously set both 'cipher-group' and 'ciphers' to 'default-value': tmsh modify ltm profile client-ssl child_clientssl cipher-group default-value ciphers default-value 2. In the Configuration Utility, uncheck the customization box for the ciphers attribute on the child profile.

bugs.title: Network Map might take a long time to load
bugs.symptoms: Network Map loading time is directly proportional to the number of profiles/policies associated with a virtual server. When there are a significant number, Network Map might take many tens of seconds to load; when there are fewer associated profiles/policies, loading time is shorter. For example, consider a configuration that contains virtual servers with a large number of associated profiles/policies. In the following example config, the virtual server has two associated profiles. The time to load the Network Map page increases with each additional profile/policy. # tmsh list ltm virtual vs ltm virtual vs { creation-time 2018-03-06:18:27:53 destination 0.0.0.0:any ip-protocol tcp last-modified-time 2018-03-06:18:27:53 mask any profiles { myhttp { } tcp { } } rules { myrule } source 0.0.0.0/0 translate-address disabled translate-port disabled vlans { socks-tunnel } vs-index 5 }
bugs.conditions: -- Navigate to Local Traffic :: Network Map in the BIG-IP Configuration Utility. -- The configuration contains a significantly large number of profiles/policies associated with the virtual server.
bugs.impact: It takes tens of seconds to load the Network Map page.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: The SNMP ipNetToMediaPhysAddress table is not supported in version 12.1.2 and forward
bugs.symptoms: If LTM pool node member's MAC addresses were being learned through the access to this table then, they must now be accessed through tmsh or the rest api.
bugs.conditions: The use of SNMP to learn the MAC addresses of LTM pool members.
bugs.impact: The SNMP ipNetToMediaPhysAddress table is no longer present.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to display node MAC addresses. "tmsh show net arp" and "tmsh show net ndp"

bugs.title: SNMP traps do not follow current best practices
bugs.symptoms: SNMP traps do not follow current best practices
bugs.conditions: SNMP v3 trap destinations configured
bugs.impact: SNMP traps do not follow current best practices
bugs.fix: SNMP traps now follow current best practices

bugs.title: SNMP traps do not follow current best practices
bugs.symptoms: SNMP traps do not follow current best practices
bugs.conditions: SNMP v3 trap destinations configured
bugs.impact: SNMP traps do not follow current best practices
bugs.fix: SNMP traps now follow current best practices

bugs.title: Errors related to dosl7d_tcpdumps_cleaner appearing in email every hour
bugs.symptoms: Errors may be sent in system emails once an hour due to a runtime error in the dosl7d_tcpdumps_cleaner which is run in an hourly cron job. Here is an example of such an email: From: root (Cron Daemon) To: root Subject: Cron <root@servername> run-parts /etc/cron.hourly Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Auto-Submitted: auto-generated X-Cron-Env: <LANG=en_US.UTF-8> X-Cron-Env: <SHELL=/bin/bash> X-Cron-Env: <PATH=/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin> X-Cron-Env: <MAILTO=root> X-Cron-Env: <HOME=/> X-Cron-Env: <LOGNAME=root> X-Cron-Env: <USER=root> /etc/cron.hourly/dosl7d_tcpdumps_cleaner: Use of uninitialized value $s in division (/) at /etc/cron.hourly/dosl7d_tcpdumps_cleaner line 111.
bugs.conditions: - The administrator configures the BIG-IP system to deliver locally generated email messages, or the administrator checks local emails to root, on the BIG-IP. - The hardware supports RAID, even if RAID is not configured.
bugs.impact: - Email messages with errors being sent once an hour. - DoSL7 tcpdump files may not be automatically cleaned if used in the DoS profile.
bugs.fix: The dosl7d_tcpdumps_cleaner cron job no longer sends error email messages every hour.

bugs.title: Display of Network Map is unreadable in browsers that cache old files
bugs.symptoms: Loading the GUI Network Map might display with code or garbage characters rather than the expected results.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from 12.x to later versions of BIG-IP software. -- The browser has cached resources to the Network Map.
bugs.impact: Network Map page display of Network Map is unreadable, or there is no data displayed.
bugs.workaround: You can recover from this using either of the following: -- Perform a 'hard refresh' on the page by holding down the Ctrl key and pressing F5 or the reload button on the browser to force a reload of the page and force download of the needed resource file. -- Clear the browser cache of Javascript files and reload the Network Map again.
bugs.fix: This version of the software ensures that Firefox retrieves the latest resource files.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing TCP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing TCP traffic
bugs.conditions: TCP profile enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM processes TCP traffic as expected

bugs.title: TMUI is unable to change the Alias Address of DNS/GTM Monitors
bugs.symptoms: TMUI (the GUI) is unable to change the Alias Address of DNS/GTM Monitors.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the GUI. -- DNS/GTM monitors with alias address. -- Attempting to change the Alias Address.
bugs.impact: Cannot change the Alias Address.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.

bugs.title: Not all ASM cookies are sent with 'secure' flag when turning on dosl7.use_secure_cookies
bugs.symptoms: When turning on dosl7.use_secure_cookies bigdb, all cookies set by DoSL7 are expected to be sent with the 'secure' flag. However, this is not the case for the TS_27 cookie: it is sent without the 'secure' flag.
bugs.conditions: 1. Efoxy (persistent client identification) is on. 2. dosl7.use_secure_cookies bigdb is on.
bugs.impact: TS_27 cookie is sent without the 'secure' flag.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to turn off efoxy.
bugs.fix: DoSL7 cookies are now sent with the correct 'secure' flag.

bugs.title: Remote admin user with misconfigured partition fallback to "All"
bugs.symptoms: When remote role groups are used to set user role and partition from the remote authentication server, and the server is configured to set a user to Administrator role with access to a particular partition, the user instead receives Administrator role on all partitions. Users with Administrator role on the BIG-IP are required to have all partition access.
bugs.conditions: Remote authentication with remote role groups. Remote authentication server configured to set a user to Administrator role with access to a particular partition.
bugs.impact: Administrator users have access to all partitions.
bugs.workaround: Change configuration on remote authentication server. Users with Administrator role need all partition access. Users who must be restricted to a particular partition should be given a more restrictive role.

bugs.title: Inbound or hairpin connections may get stuck consuming memory.
bugs.symptoms: When inbound or hairpin connections require a remote Session DB lookup and the lookup request or response messages get lost, the connections can get stuck in an embryonic state. They will be stuck in this state until they timeout and expire. In this state UDP connections will queue inbound packets. If the client application continues to send packets, the connection may never expire. The queued packets will accumulate consuming memory. If the memory consumption becomes excessive, connections may be killed and “TCP: Memory pressure activated” and “Aggressive mode activated” messages will appear in the logs.
bugs.conditions: A LSN pool with inbound and/or hairpin connections enabled. Lost Session DB messages due to heavy load or hardware failure. Remote lookups are more likely when using PBA mode or NAPT mode with default DAG.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory consumption that leads to dropped connections.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When Session DB messages are lost, the connection will be killed and any queued packets will be discarded. If the client application resends packets they will be treated as a new connection.

bugs.title: 13.0.0-to-13.1.0 upgrade operation on VIPRION 2250 blades might fail if global whitelist is configured
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading from 13.0.0 to 13.1.0 on VIPRION 2250 blades might fail if global whitelist is configured. After the upgrade, the system will stay offline.
bugs.conditions: -- Global whitelist configured. -- Running on VIPRION 2250 blades.
bugs.impact: System fails to run normally.
bugs.workaround: Remove global whitelist before upgrading to 13.1.0, add it back after upgrading.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs in fixed versions, so you can upgrade from 13.0.0 to a post-13.1.0 version of the software without encountering this issue.

bugs.title: Some DNS truncated responses may not be processed by BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: On 13.1.x DNS responses with truncated bit set are dropped when AFM DNS DoS is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM DNS DoS is enabled. -- Using 13.1.x.
bugs.impact: Clients do not receive truncated DNS responses.
bugs.workaround: Disable DNS DoS protection by changing the dos.dnsport variable to another port for which there is no valid traffic. For instance: tmsh modify sys db dos.dnsport value 54

bugs.title: During system boot, error message displays: 'Dataplane INOPERABLE - only 1 HSBes found on this platform'
bugs.symptoms: During system bootup, the system occasionally posts the following error message and the system does not come up: Dataplane INOPERABLE - only 1 HSBes found on this platform.
bugs.conditions: This occurs occasionally at system bootup. -- Using the following platforms: i4600, i4800, i10600, i10800, i2600, i2800, i7600, i7800, i5600, i5800, i15600, i15800, i12600, i12800, HERCULON i2800, HERCULON i5800, HERCULON i10800, i11600, i11800, i11800-DS, i5820-DF, i7820-DF.
bugs.impact: System does not come up.
bugs.workaround: Reboot system. Because this condition only happens occasionally, rebooting typically corrects the issue.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a race condition that might have occurred while reading FPGA firmware loading status.

bugs.title: OSPFv3 failure to create a route entry for IPv4-Mapped IPv6 Address
bugs.symptoms: Route entries for IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (::ffff:<IPv4>) are not created in TMM when passed from Dynamic Routing protocols like OSPFv3.
bugs.conditions: - Route entry is for IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, that is ::ffff:<IPv4>.
bugs.impact: - Route entry is not created in TMM, packets addressed to such a destination might not be delivered at all or might not be delivered using the most efficient route. - Connection between TMM and tmrouted is restarted that is a small performance overhead.
bugs.workaround: - If possible IPv4 address or IPv4-compatible IPv6 address should be passed instead of IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, however this depends on other routers.

bugs.title: Newly entered password is not remembered.
bugs.symptoms: - Upon enabling password remember feature and running 'tmsh load sys config default', the password history fails to verify and save the newly entered password. - Upon installing a BIG-IP image for the first time, the default password is not updated.
bugs.conditions: - Installing first time BIG-IP image. - Resetting the configuration using 'tmsh load sys config default'.
bugs.impact: The password is not remembered.
bugs.fix: Corrected selinux policy script of the file /etc/security/opasswd for access permission.

bugs.title: Deleting congestion metrics cache entries may result in TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Deleting congestion metrics cache entries using the TMSH command 'tmsh del net cmetrics' might result in TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: -- The congestion metrics cache has only one entry. -- Using the following TMSH command to delete congestion metrics cache entries: tmsh del net cmetrics
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not issuing the command: tmsh del net cmetrics

bugs.title: Localdb authentication may fail
bugs.symptoms: In Rare scenarios, localdb authentication may fail - due to thread synchronization issue in apmd deamon.
bugs.conditions: - APM is provisioned - Using localdb for authentication.
bugs.impact: Localdb authentication may fail
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Software has been upgraded to fix the race condition issue.

bugs.title: When the BigDB variable tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts is set a buffer overflow can occur
bugs.symptoms: When the BigDB variable tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts is set, a buffer overflow can occur.
bugs.conditions: -- The BigDB variable tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts is set. -- Forward proxy is being used. -- A malformed certificate with a serial number length equal to 256 bytes is parsed during forging.
bugs.impact: A off-by-one error causes one byte to write off the end of an array.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to not set tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts BigDB variable.
bugs.fix: Buffer no longer overflows.

bugs.title: When the BigDB variable tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts is set, a double-free error might occur
bugs.symptoms: When the BigDB variable tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts is set, a double-free error can occur.
bugs.conditions: -- The BigDB variable tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts is set. -- Forward proxy is being used. -- An error occurs when reading the certificate serial number.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not setting the tmm.ssl.loggingcreatedcerts BigDB variable.
bugs.fix: Double-free removed.

bugs.title: VLAN SYN cookies go into constant activated/deactivated cycle
bugs.symptoms: When VLAN SYN cookies are enabled on the BIG-IP client-side VLAN and per-virtual SYN cookies are disabled, and syn flood is running, VLAN SYN cookies can be observed activated as expected, but then BIG-IP falls into a never-ending cycle of VLAN SYN cookies activating/deactivating.
bugs.conditions: Hardware syncookie enabled on specific VLAN, and syn flood is run against that VLAN
bugs.impact: BIG-IP doesn't stay in hardware syncookie mode, diminishing the protection effect
bugs.workaround: Switch to VIP-based syncookie protection
bugs.fix: Use an estimated total per-VLAN syncookies generation count to determine if it is time to exit per-VLAN syncookie mode globally. The PDE register only reports the syncookie counts on the local PDE, and the number becomes lower with a platform with many PDEs assigned to tmms, which can easily fall below the fixed global exit threshold. By estimating the total syncookies count, we can make different platforms have similar exit condition.

bugs.title: GUI/iControl SOAP - KeyManagement export_all_to_archive_file failing immediately after HTTPD restart
bugs.symptoms: The export operation of SSL keys and certificate into a .tgz archive file fails when the httpd daemon is restarted.
bugs.conditions: -- Export SSL Keys and certificates into archive file. -- httpd is restarted.
bugs.impact: Export of SSL Keys and certificates into archive file does not work immediately after httpd restart via GUI/iControl.
bugs.workaround: After httpd restart, perform other operation like creating a key/cert before exporting archive file.
bugs.fix: The system allows exporting SSL keys and certificate to be archived into .tgz files after httpd restart.

bugs.title: RADIUS Accounting requests egress different self-IPs since upgrade to v13.1
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS Accounting requests egress different self-IPs since upgrade to v13.1 * START accounting message egresses floating self-IP * STOP accounting message egresses local self-IP Some radius messages will come from Floating address, some from Self IP address. The Radius server should be configured to accept all self and floating address of all the devices in the HA group, to ensure all messages are received.
bugs.conditions: RADIUS server configured with pool option.
bugs.impact: Causes RADIUS server to be unable to reconcile accounting messages.
bugs.workaround: In order to reconcile accounting messages they can be tracked through the Acct-Session-Id in RADIUS AVP's message which would be the same for the corresponding START and STOP messages to uniquely identify the session.
bugs.fix: RADIUS START and STOP messages now egress the same interface.

bugs.title: Post-login client-side alerts are missing username in bigIQ
bugs.symptoms: A client-side alert that contains a FPS-Username header with a value, but an empty fpm_username parameter - will be reported with "Unknown" username in bigIQ.
bugs.conditions: 1. post login (alert is sent after submitting username parameter) client side alerts 2. alert-pool points to bigIQ IP (not Alert-Server)
bugs.impact: Post login client side alerts are missing username (will show as "Unknown" in bigIQ, works well with Alert-Server).
bugs.workaround: Route all client-side alerts to another virtual server and strip of the empty fpm_username parameter from payload/query-string.
bugs.fix: FPS will always send username in the fpm_username parameter in case it was empty and FPS has username value.

bugs.title: Memory leak when SSL Forward proxy is used and ssl re-negotiates
bugs.symptoms: When looking at tmsh show sys memory you will see ssl_compat continue to grow and fails to release memory.
bugs.conditions: -SSL Forward Proxy In use -SSL Re-negotiations happening
bugs.impact: Eventually memory reaper will kick in.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: ssl_compat now properly releases connections on re-negotiation.

bugs.title: iRules LX plugin imported from a system with a different version does not properly run, and the associated iRule times out.
bugs.symptoms: An iRules LX plugin does not properly run and messages similar to the following example are logged to the /var/log/ltm file: err tmm[17616]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/my-plugin/my-rule <HTTP_REQUEST> - ILX timeout. invoked from within "ILX::call $ilx_handle -timeout 3000 my-function"
bugs.conditions: An iRules LX workspace archive is imported to BIG-IP version 13.1.0 or later from a previous software version. It should be noted this is what happens during a regular software upgrade. Therefore, you might encounter this issue when upgrading a system to BIG-IP version 13.1.0 or later.
bugs.impact: The affected iRules LX are not functional under the new software version, and the virtual servers utilizing them will experience various failures.
bugs.workaround: Change the node version from 0.12.15 to 6.9.1 and back.

bugs.title: DIAMETER::persist reset non-functional
bugs.symptoms: When the iRule DIAMETER::persist reset is called, it is meant to remove existing persistence records from diadb. Without this bug fix, calling DIAMETER::persist reset has no effect and the persistence record remains.
bugs.conditions: Diameter session profile has persistence enabled and an iRule attempts to remove a persistence record.
bugs.impact: not provided by ENE
bugs.fix: DIAMETER::persist reset now functions properly. You can delete diameter persistence records with this iRule.

bugs.title: "NTP not configured on device" warning seen when NTP symmetric key authentication is configured
bugs.symptoms: When NTP symmetric key authentication is configured, as per https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14120, and the BIG-IP is part of a device service cluster, then a warning similar to this will be seen periodically in /var/log/ltm: warning mcpd[6317]: 01071af0:4: NTP not configured on device 1.2.3.4 - within a trust
bugs.conditions: - NTP symmetric key authentication must be configured. - The BIG-IP must be part of a device service cluster. - Non-authenticated NTP servers must not be in-use.
bugs.impact: Incorrect NTP warnings are seen periodically in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Prevented this warning from being emitted when NTP symmetric key authentication is in-use in a device service cluster.

bugs.title: Azure: A failure to load mcpd configuration during the startup triggers "load sys config default" after an hour, if the config load failure is not corrected.
bugs.symptoms: - An "load sys config default" is reported in /var/log/ltm that wasn't initiated by the user manually. This can break password based SSH connectivity as the default config load wipes out the MCPD configuration.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP is running in Azure. - A mis-configuration in MCPD on-disk config in /config/*.conf files that fails "load sys config" during the startup. - The broken configuration stays that way for more than an hour. If the "load sys config" failure isn't corrected for an hour, the azure-init vadc startup script loads the default config to correct the problem, thus wiping out user configuration.
bugs.impact: User could lose the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.workaround: - If user has access to the BIG-IP, they should try to fix the "load sys config" failure manually by modifying the mcpd configuration in /config/*.conf files. This would prevent the eventual "load sys config default". - If user doesn't have access to the BIG-IP, there isn't really a workaround for this issue.

bugs.title: VCMP guests in HA configuration become Active/Active during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: When devices in a Device Service Cluster (DSC) are upgraded, multiple devices might become Active simultaneously. During upgrade, the process erroneously clears the management-ip during reboot, and then synchronizes to other members of the DSC. If the system is not performing an upgrade, the error is repaired as the device starts up, and has no visible effect. If an upgrade is being performed, the management-ip cannot be repaired, and the DSC members lose contact with each other, so they all become Active.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on VIPRION chassis systems, either natively, or as a vCMP guest. -- Upgrading from any affected versions (TMOS v12.1.3, TMOS v13.0.0, TMOS v13.0.1, TMOS v13.1.0), to any other version.
bugs.impact: When multiple devices become Active simultaneously, traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to remain in Active/Active state until upgrade is complete on all chassis in the DSC are finished. See K43990943: VIPRION systems configured for high availability may become active-active during the upgrade process :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K43990943 for more information on how to mitigate this issue.
bugs.fix: The erroneous management-ip change is not made, and the HA failover mechanism operates correctly across upgrade.

bugs.title: Memory leak when ACCESS::SESSION data get command is applied
bugs.symptoms: Slow memory leak occurs when ACCESS::SESSION data get command is used in iRule.
bugs.conditions: iRule contains an ACCESS::SESSION data get command.
bugs.impact: Memory leak eventually causes the BIG-IP system to fail over, interrupting traffic.

bugs.title: LTM v12.1.2 Upgrade fails if config contains "/Common/ssh" object name
bugs.symptoms: Loading configuration fails on upgrade
bugs.conditions: Must have a profile named "/Common/ssh" and must be upgrading to v12.1.2
bugs.impact: The system won't be functional
bugs.workaround: Delete or rename "/Common/ssh"

bugs.title: New blob compilation may fail with 'No Blobs available' error
bugs.symptoms: After modifying firewall configuration, the compilation of new blob may fail with 'No Blobs available' error.
bugs.conditions: Modifying firewall policies and rules.
bugs.impact: Firewall configuration changes are not applied. The previous configuration is used in data-path for processing data traffic.
bugs.workaround: Restart both tmm and pccd with the command: bigstart restart tmm pccd Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. Note: Versions 12.0.0 and later now better handle blob activation, so this is no longer an issue.

bugs.title: Subscriber session creation via PEM may fail due to a RADIUS-message-triggered race condition in PEM
bugs.symptoms: Session replacement fails as a result of a race condition between multiple RADIUS Accounting Start and Stop messages for the same subscriber.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- These SysDB variables are set as follows: sys db tmm.pem.session.radius.retransmit.timeout { value "0" } sys db tmm.pem.session.provisioning.continuous { value "disable" } -- Actions occur in the following order: 1. PEM receives RADIUS START with subscriber ID1 and IP1. 2. PEM receives RADIUS STOP with subscriber ID1 and IP1. 3. PEM receives RADIUS START with subscriber ID1 and IP2. 4. PEM receives RADIUS STOP with subscriber ID1 and IP2. -- The time interval between steps 1 and 2 is very small (less than ~1ms).
bugs.impact: Subscriber session creation via PEM may fail.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to leave SysDbs variables set to the default values.
bugs.fix: The system now handles PEM subscriber session updates properly, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: iRule triggered from RADIUS occasionally fails to create subscribers.
bugs.symptoms: The subscriber can not be added with the same IP address after retries. This is a rarely occurring issue: if the daily average of subscriber additions is ~30000 subscribers, 5 to 6 subscribers face this problem (0.02%).
bugs.conditions: Running iRule to create PEM sessions from RADIUS packets using the 'PEM::subscriber create' command.
bugs.impact: Intermittently (a few operations per day), the command silently fails. No session is created, and no TCL error is produced. Subscriber addition requires manual intervention.
bugs.workaround: Trigger a RADIUS START using a different IP address for the subscriber.

bugs.title: 'bandwidth utilization exceeded' log messages may not be output in all cases
bugs.symptoms: In certain cases log messages corresponding to 'bandwidth utilization exceeded' may not be output.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual Edition (VE) license with bandwidth limitations. -- Traffic exceeding the license limit.
bugs.impact: Logs are not output.
bugs.workaround: Modify tmsh sys DB variable log.alertbwthreshold with a value other than '0'.

bugs.title: fasthttp can crash with Large Receive Offload enabled
bugs.symptoms: fasthttp and lro can lead to a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: fasthttp and lro enabled. (lro is enabled by default >= 13.1.0)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use fasthttp
bugs.fix: fasthttp with lro enabled no longer causes tmm to crash.

bugs.title: Cookie persistence profile may be configured with invalid parameter combination.
bugs.symptoms: Configuring Cookie persistence profile via TMSH or iControl REST allows invalid parameter combinations.
bugs.conditions: Cookie persistence profile is configured via TMSH or iControl REST. TMUI is not affected.
bugs.impact: Invalid parameters for any method type of a Cookie persistence profile are ignored by TMM, no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: Use only the allowed parameters of each method type when Cookie persistence is configured via TMSH or iControl REST.

bugs.title: Multiple NTP server/domain-searches in the DHCP lease can cause missing DNS/NTP configuration.
bugs.symptoms: /var/log/boot.log has this error: dhcp_config: save error: 01070911:3: The requested host (ntp-servers-ip) is invalid for servers in ntp (/Common/ntp).
bugs.conditions: - The BIG-IP system has DHCP enabled for management interface. - Multiple NTP servers or domain-search are specified in the dhclient lease (stored at /var/lib/dhclient/dhclient.leases).
bugs.impact: - DNS and NTP servers are not configured in MCPD. - Name resolution can break.
bugs.fix: Multiple NTP server/domain-searches in the DHCP lease can cause missing DNS/NTP configuration.

bugs.title: Disallow DHCP relay traffic to traverse between route domains
bugs.symptoms: DHCP traffic can traverse between route domains, e.g., when working with a route domain with a parent. Under certain circumstances, this is not desired.
bugs.conditions: DHCP relay in use on a route domain with a parent relationship or strict isolation disabled.
bugs.impact: The DHCP server side flow might get established to the parent route domain, and will persist even after the route in its own route domain becomes available again.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A db key has been introduced, tmm.dhcp.routedomain.strictisolate, which allows enforcement of route domain traversal if desired/configured.

bugs.title: Unbalanced trunk distribution on i4x00 and 4000 platforms with odd number of members.
bugs.symptoms: For the i4x00 and 4000 platforms, egress trunk distribution will be unbalanced if the number of trunk members is not a power of 2.
bugs.conditions: A trunk is configured with an odd number of trunk interfaces or a trunk member goes down such that the number of working members is odd.
bugs.impact: Uneven traffic distribution. Some interfaces will see more traffic than others.
bugs.workaround: Insure the number of trunk interfaces is a power of 2: 2, 4, or 8.

bugs.title: iControl SOAP/GUI cannot generate SSL certificate or CSR for password-protected SSL key
bugs.symptoms: Cannot use iControl SOAP commands or the GUI to generate SSL certificate or CSR for a SSL key that is protected by password.
bugs.conditions: The SSL key is password-protected. That is, the key file has the below pattern as prefix. [root@big3:Active:Standalone] shared # head -2 test12345.key -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED
bugs.impact: Unable to generate a certificate or CSR for a key using iControl SOAP or the GUI.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following workarounds: Workaround A: Use tmsh to create the certificate or CSR. To do so, follow this procedure: 1. Run a command similar to the following: tmsh create sys crypto cert test12345 key test12345 common-name cn 2. Enter the PEM pass phrase: <<input the key's password>> 3. Run a command similar to the following: tmsh create sys crypto csr test12345 key test12345 common-name cn 4. Enter the PEM pass phrase: <<input the key's password>> Workaround B: Generate the certificate and CSR file using OpenSSL commands and then import them onto the BIG-IP system. 1.
