Run a command similar to the following: openssl req -x509 -sha256 -days 365 -key test12345.key -in test12345.csr -out test12345.crt 2. Enter the pass phrase for test12345.key: 12345 3. Run a command similar to the following: tmsh install sys crypto cert test12345 from-local-file /shared/test12345.crt 4. Run a command similar to the following: tmsh install sys crypto csr test12345 from-local-file /shared/test12345.csr
bugs.fix: Can now use iControl SOAP commands or the GUI to generate SSL certificate or CSR for a SSL key that is protected by password.

bugs.title: LTM SQL monitors may stop monitoring if multiple monitors querying same database
bugs.symptoms: When using an SQL monitor to monitor the health of SQL database pool members, one of the health monitors may stop actively monitoring one or more pool members. When this problem occurs, the following error messages may be logged in /var/log/DBDaemon-0.log: [if debug = yes in monitor configuration]: Using cached DB connection for connection string '<connection string>' then multiple, periodic instances of the following message, referencing the same connection string: Abandoning hung SQL query: '<query string>' for: '<connection string>' or: <connection string>(<thread-number>): Hung SQL query; abandoning
bugs.conditions: This may occur when all of the following conditions are met: -- Using one of the following LTM monitors: mssql, mysql, oracle, postgresql. -- Configuring multiple pool members for the same node (server). -- Configuring multiple SQL monitors that query the same server and database. And when one or both of the following conditions are met: Either: -- The SQL monitor is configured with a non-zero 'count' value. Or: -- An error occurs while querying a SQL database, such as [recorded in the DBDaemon log]: java.io.EOFException: Can not read response from server. Expected to read 4 bytes, read 0 bytes before connection was unexpectedly lost.
bugs.impact: When this problem occurs, the affected pool members are reported down, even though the database is actually up and responding correctly to traffic.
bugs.workaround: When this problem occurs, successful monitoring can be temporarily restored by disabling then re-enabling monitoring of affected pool members. To avoid one possible trigger for this issue (and thus reduce the likelihood of this issue occurring), configure the 'count' parameter in the SQL monitor configuration to a value of '0'.
bugs.fix: LTM SQL monitors continue monitoring when multiple monitors/ query the same server and database.

bugs.title: 'No Access' error when viewing GSLB Server's virtual server that has a name indicating a partition that does not exist on that BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system posts a 'No Access' error message instead of the virtual server's properties.
bugs.conditions: -- At least two BIG-IP systems in a sync group. -- One of the BIG-IP systems has a partition that does not exist on the other with an LTM virtual server on that partition. -- The issue occurs when a GSLB Server discovers that LTM virtual server and displays it on its virtual server page. Note: This same error message displays for GSLB pool member properties accessed by navigating to GSLB :: pools :: [pool] :: members :: Member : Address. The differing issues have been fixed in differing releases. You can find information about the similar issue in the AskF5 Bug Tracker article for 722734.
bugs.impact: It makes the GSLB Server's virtual server's properties page unavailable in this case.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workaroudns: -- Use TMSH to view or edit the properties of that virtual server. -- Create partitions on the GTM device to match those appearing to be referenced in the object names.
bugs.fix: Partition checking has been disabled for virtual servers on the GTM side, since a virtual server owned by a server is always in the partition of that server (/Common).

bugs.title: Merging config may not report syslog configuration errors
bugs.symptoms: A 'load sys config verify merge' may return successfully, but 'load sys config merge' without the 'verify' argument might fail.
bugs.conditions: Running the 'load sys config merge' without the 'verify' argument.
bugs.impact: False positive might be received in response to a successful config verify. However, the syslog system is not actually configured during a 'verify', so it does not report errors.

bugs.title: Portal Access: same-origin AJAX request may fail in some case.
bugs.symptoms: If base URL for current HTML page contains default port number, same-origin AJAX request from this page may fail via Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page with explicit default port in base URL, for example: <base href='https://some.com:443/path/'> - Same-origin AJAX request from this page, for example: var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest; xhr.open('GET', 'some.file');
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to use iRule to remove default port number from encoded back-end host definition in Portal Access requests, for example: when RULE_INIT { # hex-encoded string for 'https://some.com' set ::encoded_backend {68747470733a2f2f736f6d652e636f6d} # '3a343433' is hex-encoded form for ':443' set ::pattern "/f5-w-${encoded_backend}3a343433\$" set ::remove_end [ expr { [ string length $::pattern ] - 2 } ] set ::remove_start [ expr {$::remove_end - 7} ] } when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::path] starts_with "$::pattern" } { set path [ string replace [HTTP::path] $::remove_start $::remove_end "" ] HTTP::path "$path" } }
bugs.fix: Now same-origin AJAX requests are handled correctly if URL contains default port number.

bugs.title: AVR does not publish DNS statistics to external log when usr-offbox is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: AVR does not send DNS statistics to external logs when analytics global setting usr-offbox is enabled, if the following security analytics settings are set to disable: -- collected-stats-internal-logging. -- collected-stats-external-logging.
bugs.conditions: -- Security analytics settings collected-stats-internal-logging is disabled. -- Security analytics settings collected-stats-external-logging is disabled. -- Analytics global settings usr-offbox is enabled.
bugs.impact: DNS statistic are not sent to external log.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, perform the following procedure: 1. Provision ASM or AFM. 2. Run the tmsh command to set to enabled the security analytics setting collected-stats-external-logging. 2. Deprovision ASM/AFM.
bugs.fix: AVR now publishes DNS statistics to external logs when usr-offbox is enabled, as expected.

bugs.title: VPN clients experience packet loss/disconnection
bugs.symptoms: VPN clients experience packet loss/disconnection.
bugs.conditions: In certain scenarios, the tunnel establishment procedure might leak a small memory. If the tmm is running for a longer duration, this small leak can accumulate and result in out-of-memory condition
bugs.impact: Connections start to drop as tmm runs out of memory. TMM will eventually run out of memory and connections could be terminated. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: VPN clients no longer experience packet loss/disconnection, and TMM no longer restarts.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing SSL Intercept traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMM may consume excessive resources when processing SSL Intercept traffic via the Air Gap Egress Inspection feature.
bugs.conditions: Air Gap Egress Inspection with SSL Intercept enabled.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now process SSL Intercept traffic as expected.

bugs.title: TMSH dns-resolver allows route-domain from another partition
bugs.symptoms: User is able to modify a dns-resolver config object in the /Common partition such that TMSH accepts the route-domain name from another partition Subsequent import of the BIG-IP LTM config into the BIG-IQ fails on this partition validation check.
bugs.conditions: Import LTM config into BIG-IQ
bugs.impact: Incorrect dns-resolver configuration and BIG-IQ import failure

bugs.title: Cannot edit Terminals of Macro if one or more Macrocalls point to a given Macro.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot edit Terminals of Macro if one or more Macrocalls point to a given Macro. The system posts a message similar to the following: Unable to execute transaction because of: 01071203:3: Caption (XYZ1) of the rule in macrocall (/Common/abc_macro) must be identical to the caption (XYZ2) of terminalout.
bugs.conditions: -- Using Access Policy. -- Policy includes one or more macros. -- There is a macrocall on one of the macros. -- You attempt to add a new terminal to that macro.
bugs.impact: Cannot edit macro terminals.
bugs.fix: Can now edit Terminals of Macro if one or more Macrocalls point to a given Macro.

bugs.title: Ephemeral node stays Unavailable on 'standby' BIG-IP system after a forced-offline FQDN node is re-enabled
bugs.symptoms: In an high availability (HA) configuration where an FQDN template-node on the 'active' unit is 'Force Offline', and the configuration is synchronized to the 'standby' unit, upon 'Enable' on that FQDN template-node in the 'active' unit (and the configuration is synchronized to the 'standby' unit), the ephemeral nodes associated with that FQDN template node remain Unavailable on the 'standby' unit.
bugs.conditions: HA configuration is configured with 'active' sync. -- FQDN template-node is configured. -- After ephemeral nodes are refreshed on the 'active' unit, it transitions to the 'standby' unit. -- The FQDN template node on the (new-'active') unit is 'Force Offline' by the user. -- The user explicitly 'Enable' that FQDN template node on the 'active' unit.
bugs.impact: The ephemerals on the 'standby' unit remain unavailable, even though the associated FQDN template node is 'available'. However, as no traffic is routed to the 'standby' unit, traffic is unaffected. Upon transition from 'standby' to' active', the ephemeral nodes will be refreshed and traffic should continue.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of these configuration options to prevent this issue from occurring: -- Select 'Disabled' (rather than 'Force Offline') for the FQDN template node on the 'active' unit. -- Configure the node without using FQDN.
bugs.fix: Upon 'Force Offline' and then 'Enable' for an FQDN template node on an 'active' unit in an HA configuration, the ephemerals on the 'standby' unit will reflect the re-enabled status based on the associated FQDN template-node on the 'active' unit.

bugs.title: platform-migrate fails when LACP trunks are in use
bugs.symptoms: Use of the platform-migrate option might fail due to some configurations being invalid on the new system. The error message generated appears as follows: 01070687:3: Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) is not supported on this platform.
bugs.conditions: You have a trunk with LACP enabled. -- You are migrating from a hardware platform to a Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to migrate.
bugs.workaround: After taking the old system offline, but before saving the UCS, disable LACP on all trunks.

bugs.title: Memory Leak of access policy execution objects
bugs.symptoms: When per-request policy is configured, in some situations it fails to cleanup some temporary execution objects. There will be a small TMM memory leak in the access2 tag.
bugs.conditions: A per-request policy is in use. This can happen regardless of the content of the policy.
bugs.impact: TMM memory leak.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Temporary objects are cleaned up now, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: DNS-Express was not sending out NOTIFY messages on VE
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express is not sending out NOTIFY messages on BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.conditions: -- DNS Express configured to send out NOTIFY messages. -- Running on BIG-IP VE configuration.
bugs.impact: DNS secondary servers serving stale data.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: DNS Express now sends out NOTIFY messages on VE.

bugs.title: Firewall is not updated when adding new rules
bugs.symptoms: When adding new rules into existing firewall policies, firewall may be not updated, so new rules are not used in traffic processing. If on-demand-compilation mode is enabled, firewall may remain in quiescent state instead of compilation-pending state after adding rules.
bugs.conditions: -- Firewall rules are added into existing firewall policies. -- No rules are deleted or modified.
bugs.impact: Firewall is not updated and new rules do not affect data traffic. If on-demand-compilation mode is enabled, firewall remain in quiescent state instead of going to compilation-pending state after adding rules.
bugs.workaround: Make additional changes to firewall rules in order to start firewall update, for esample: -- Add a placeholder rule, and then delete it. -- Modify a rule (e.g. by adding an IP address), and then revert the modification by removing that IP address.
bugs.fix: When adding new rules, firewall is now always updated. If on-demand-compilation mode is enabled, firewall goes to the compilation-pending state after adding rules.

bugs.title: IKEv2 further child_sa validity checks
bugs.symptoms: A tmm restart can occur when a child_sa is rekeyed at expiration time, provided a race condition occurs.
bugs.conditions: Encountering the issue in which rekeying a child_sa might core when race conditions allowed that child_sa to be destroyed while in use.
bugs.impact: Restart of tmm and outage of IPsec tunnels until renegotiated.
bugs.fix: The validity of a child_sa and its traffic selector are checked now before use, to prevent failure when freed objects are accidentally used.

bugs.title: When ASM and APM are configured on the same virtual server, ASM could throw some errors in its logging.
bugs.symptoms: When ASM and APM WebSSO are on same virtual server, WebSSO might generate a new request. When that happens, ASM might see multiple requests with same support ID. This can cause issues with ASM and log errors.
bugs.conditions: When APM WebSSO is configured (only for Basic, NTLM, Kerberos).
bugs.impact: ASM stops processing the HTTP requests that have duplicate support IDs, causing an issue to ASM/APM end users.
bugs.fix: When ASM and APM WebSSO are on same virtual server, WebSSO no longer generates a new request, so duplicate support IDs are no longer created.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTML traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTML traffic
bugs.conditions: HTML profile enabled
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTML traffic as expected

bugs.title: AVR-profile might cause issues when loading a configuration or when using config sync
bugs.symptoms: Some fields in AVR-profile contain lists of items. Those lists can be set only if the relevant flag is set to 'true'. In case of a flag configuration change, the system must keep the lists as they were and not reset them, so they can be available in case the flag changes back again. Validation settings were created such that the lists flag is set to 'true' by default, but this can cause the load/merge process to break if the list was set, and afterwards the flag was set to 'false'.
bugs.conditions: Setting the relevant flag to 'false' after creating a list of items. The relevant fields in AVR-profile that have that logic are: -- IPs-list. -- Subnets-list. -- Countries-list. -- URLs-list.
bugs.impact: Management load and sync process may not work as expected.
bugs.fix: Validation for those fields when the associated flag is set to 'false' will be skipped in a load/merge scenario.

bugs.title: Remote logger message is truncated at NULL character.
bugs.symptoms: When a request including binary null character has been sent to an remote logger, configured for ASM, the request will arrive to the remote destination and will be truncated exactly at binary NULL character.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- ASM remote logger attached to a virtual server. -- Request including binary NULL character is sent to the remote logger destination.
bugs.impact: Partial request is logged at the remote logger destination.
bugs.fix: Binary NULL character is now escaped before being sent to the remote logger destination, so the request is no longer truncated.

bugs.title: High CPU when using HTTP::collect for large chunked payloads
bugs.symptoms: When collecting large amounts of chunked payload, approximately one million bytes, the processing to parse each chunk for the chunk headers and offsets results in large CPU utilization.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile is attached to virtual server. -- Server sends chunked response. -- An iRule on the virtual server uses the HTTP::collect command to collect and parse large chunked payloads.
bugs.impact: High CPU utilization.

bugs.title: F5 VPN and EPI apps quit on Linux distributions with Qt version 5.10.1 or higher
bugs.symptoms: F5 VPN and EPI apps quit on Linux distributions with Qt version 5.10.1 or higher.
bugs.conditions: -- Linux distributions with Qt version 5.10.0 or higher. -- F5 VPN and F5 EPI application.
bugs.impact: F5 VPN and F5 EPI apps quit.
bugs.workaround: Install Qt version 5.9.0 or lower, and make it the default installation.

bugs.title: TMM hardware accelerated compression not registering for all compression levels.
bugs.symptoms: DEFLATE/gzip compression levels other than level 1 bypass the hardware accelerator and are serviced in software, resulting in higher CPU utilization and slower compression times.
bugs.conditions: -- Compression requests for DEFLATE/gzip levels other than level 1. -- BIG-IP devices using Cave Creek SSL hardware acceleration.
bugs.impact: Compression requests serviced by software are scheduled on local CPUs. During heavy compression traffic, overall system traffic flow may be reduced. Compression requests serviced in software may take significantly longer to complete.
bugs.fix: Hardware accelerator correctly registers for all DEFLATE/gzip compression levels, not just level 1.

bugs.title: Possible SIGSEGV in GTMD when GTM persistence is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: When GTM persistence is enabled, GTMD may occasionally crash and restart.
bugs.conditions: GTM persistence is enabled.
bugs.impact: GTMD may occasionally restart.
bugs.workaround: Disable GTM persistence.
bugs.fix: GTMD will no longer crash and restart when persistence is enabled.

bugs.title: Nitrox PX recovery failure will not retry as it was designed to.
bugs.symptoms: The Nitrox PX encounters an error and proceeds to perform a soft reset, but if the soft reset fails, then there are no further attempts at recovery will be taken. The device will remain offline and no failsafe action will be triggered.
bugs.conditions: When a Nitrox PX device starts recovery and the soft reset procedure fails to complete successfully, the driver only logs the failure.
bugs.impact: Whenever a Nitrox PX soft reset fails, the device is left offline and remain unusable until TMM is restarted or the BIG-IP system is rebooted. No retries are attempted even though the driver is designed to retry three times before triggering the failsafe action.
bugs.workaround: to recover service to the Nitrox PX devices once this occurs, issue the following command to restart tmm: bigstart restart tmm Note: Traffic will be disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now triggers another reset sequence at the next opportunity when a soft reset fails.

bugs.title: DNS returns an erroneous invalidate response with EDNS0 CSUBNET Scope Netmask !=0
bugs.symptoms: The DNS filter returns an erroneous invalidate response with EDNS0 CSUBNET Scope Netmask !=0.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual Server configured with 'DNS Profile' set to 'dns' or a 'dns'-derived profile. - DNS queries with EDNS0 ECS option set.
bugs.impact: If the response ECS Scope Netmask has a value other than '0', LTM drops it, causing timeout and retry on client side.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: iCRD commands requiring 'root' user access fixed
bugs.symptoms: Some of the iCRD calls that run commands on the base operating system that require elevated permissions fail because iCRD was not correctly executing the commands in the right context.
bugs.conditions: Use an iCRD endpoint that requires elevated permissions to succeed.
bugs.impact: Only impacts iCRD endpoints which run commands that require root access.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This fix resolves this issue by running the commands with the correct user context.

bugs.title: Diameter and SIP profile statistics may require "Clear Statistics" button to be clicked twice to get the stats to zero out
bugs.symptoms: In UI, when navigate to the following profiles under "Statistics ›› Module Statistics : Local Traffic ›› Profiles Summary" - Diameter Router - Diameter Session - SIP Router - SIP Session "Clear Statistics" button may not work properly. You may need to click the button twice, or refresh the page, after clicking the button. Otherwise, stats may not be reset.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when trying to clear the statistics.
bugs.impact: Statistics are sometimes not cleared on the first attempt.
bugs.workaround: Click "Clear Statistics" button twice or refresh the UI after clicking "Clear Statistics" or use tmsh
bugs.fix: "Clear Statistics" button works properly.

bugs.title: In APM Citrix Storefront Integration mode ICA file returns duplicate TrasnportReconnectEnabled parameter
bugs.symptoms: In APM Citrix Storefront Integration mode, the ICA file returns a duplicate TransportReconnectEnabled parameter when Storefront is configured in Internal-only mode.
bugs.conditions: -- Citrix Storefront is configured with LTM and APM. -- Storefront is configured in Internal-only mode (i.e., no remote access enabled). -- While launching the application from the portal, ICA file returns a duplicate parameter for TransportReconnectEnabled.
bugs.impact: Citrix Receiver might misinterpret this ICA parameter. No immediate visible impact is seen.
bugs.fix: APM now properly returns the ICA parameter TransportReconnectEnabled.

bugs.title: VE with interface(s) marked down may report high cpu usage
bugs.symptoms: The "tmm" process may appear to be running at 90% or above in linux cpu reporting utilities such as "top" or "ps", even if the system is not handling a large amount of traffic. In this case, "tmsh show sys tmm-info" continues to report tmm's cpu usage accurately.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP Virtual Edition - One or more interfaces configured and used in the BIG-IP configuration is marked down
bugs.impact: tmm consumes cpu cycles even when idle. This may impact other guests running on the same hardware if the hypervisor has oversubscribed its cpu resources.
bugs.workaround: Disable any interface that is currently marked down. For example: tmsh modify net interface 1.1 disabled and then restart tmm: bigstart restart tmm

bugs.title: "Application Layer Encryption" option is not saved in DataSafe GUI
bugs.symptoms: "Application Layer Encryption" checkbox will remain enabled if un-checked via DataSafe GUI and will not be saved.
bugs.conditions: - Install DataSafe license - Provision FPS - Create URL
bugs.impact: Cannot enable/disable "Application Layer Encryption" via DataSafe GUI.
bugs.workaround: Application Layer Encryption can be enabled or disabled via TMSH command line or REST API.
bugs.fix: "Application Layer Encryption" option is saved if changed via DataSafe GUI.

bugs.title: Crash when cached route information becomes stale and the system accesses the information from it.
bugs.symptoms: The crash happens intermittently when the cached route information becomes stale and the system accesses the information from it.
bugs.conditions: Use stale cached route information.
bugs.impact: This condition can lead to a crash as the route information is no longer valid, and can lead to illegal memory access.
bugs.fix: The system now fetches the latest egress route/interface information before accessing it.

bugs.title: Restjavad hangs and causes GUI page timeouts
bugs.symptoms: Restjavad stops responding, causing GUI page timeouts.
bugs.conditions: The conditions behind this issue are not known.
bugs.impact: restjavad is active, but all endpoints are nonresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Restart restjavad.

bugs.title: TMUI dashboard daemon stability issue
bugs.symptoms: Some dashboard requests may cause a crash of TMUI dashboard daemons, affecting the TMUI dashboard.
bugs.conditions: Request sent to BIG-IP dashboard.
bugs.impact: Only the TMUI dashboard goes offline. Other TMUI functionality is not affected by this issue.
bugs.workaround: None available.
bugs.fix: Setup a correct exception handling prevented TMUI dashboard service failure.

bugs.title: 12.1.3.3 feature refinement might be lost after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: If you upgrade from 12.1.3.3 (or later) to 13.1.0 or 13.1.0.1, you will lose the VE-specific 12.1.3.3 feature refinements you gained.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 12.1.3.3 (or later) to 13.0.x, 13.1.0, or 13.1.0.1.
bugs.impact: Feature refinement provided in 12.1.3.3 will be lost after upgrade. Other functionality is unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Only upgrade from 12.1.3.3 or later to 13.1.0.2 or later.

bugs.title: iControl requests may cause excessive resource usage
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, iControl requests submitted by authenticated users may cause excessive resource usage.
bugs.conditions: Authenticated iControl user
bugs.impact: Excessive resource usage, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: iControl now processes requests as expected.

bugs.title: tmm crash due to a bad HA header

bugs.conditions: This can occur during normal tmm operation while Device Service Clustering is configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Temporary browser challenge failure after installing older ASU

bugs.conditions: -- Using BIG-IP version 13.1.0.5. -- Installing an ASU from before April 2018.
bugs.impact: Browsers remain on whitepage after receiving a browser challenge. Note: The problem should go away after 10-to-15 minutes of provisioning ASM, when more versions of JavaScript are generated.
bugs.workaround: Install the latest ASU.
bugs.fix: The browser challenges will succeed even after installing an older ASU.

bugs.title: Portal Access might omit some valid cookies when rewriting HTTP request.

bugs.title: Cannot filter Protocol Inspections display based on Action 'Don't Inspect'

bugs.conditions: Protocol Inspection provisioned and configured with at least one policy.

bugs.title: Enabling BigDB key bigd.tmm may cause SSL monitors to fail

bugs.impact: The cipher string will no longer be valid when bigd.tmm is enabled and the keywords will need to be modified or removed. SSL monitors begin to fail after modifying bigd.tmm.
bugs.workaround: Modify or remove incompatible keywords from the ciphers string; the in-tmm monitoring feature only allows ciphers that are allowed by SSL profiles.

bugs.title: AVR does not send errdef for entity DosIpLogReporting.
bugs.symptoms: AVR does not send errdef for entity DosIpLogReporting.
bugs.conditions: -- AVR is configured. -- View the DosIpLogReporting report.

bugs.fix: Added errdef for module DosIpLogReporting.

bugs.title: Network Map might take a long time to load
bugs.symptoms: Network Map loading time is directly proportional to the number of profiles/policies associated with a virtual server. When there are a significant number, Network Map might take many tens of seconds to load; when there are fewer associated profiles/policies, loading time is shorter. For example, consider a configuration that contains virtual servers with a large number of associated profiles/policies. In the following example config, the virtual server has two associated profiles. The time to load the Network Map page increases with each additional profile/policy. # tmsh list ltm virtual vs ltm virtual vs { creation-time 2018-03-06:18:27:53 destination 0.0.0.0:any ip-protocol tcp last-modified-time 2018-03-06:18:27:53 mask any profiles { myhttp { } tcp { } } rules { myrule } source 0.0.0.0/0 translate-address disabled translate-port disabled vlans { socks-tunnel } vs-index 5 }
bugs.conditions: -- Navigate to Local Traffic :: Network Map in the BIG-IP Configuration Utility. -- The configuration contains a significantly large number of profiles/policies associated with the virtual server.
bugs.impact: It takes tens of seconds to load the Network Map page.
bugs.fix: The data loading performance was improved to load the page faster.

bugs.title: VIPRION outgoing management IPv6 traffic from primary blade uses the cluster member IP
bugs.symptoms: The behavior of outgoing IPv6 management and IPv4 management traffic from the primary blade differs: IPv4 traffic is sourced from the cluster IP IPv6 traffic is sourced from the cluster member IP
bugs.conditions: IPv6 configured on the 'cluster' address and 'cluster member' address.
bugs.impact: The blade IP address, rather than the cluster floating IP, will be used as the source IP when querying the RADIUS server for remote-auth login against the management port.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: 'API Security' security policy template changes
bugs.symptoms: Parameter-related Learn/Alarm/Block settings in 'API Security' security policy template should be 'ON' by default.
bugs.conditions: Learn/Alarm/Block settings in 'API Security' security policy template.
bugs.impact: Settings not active.
bugs.fix: Parameter-related Learn/Alarm/Block settings in 'API Security' security policy template are now 'ON' by default.

bugs.title: License check VPE expression fails when access profile name contains dots
bugs.symptoms: License Check Agent always flows down fallback branch. Logs show the following pattern: -- err apmd[13738]: 01490190:3: /Common/my.profile.name:Common:2a392ccd: Key 'tmm.profilelicense./Common/my.profile.name#' was not found in MEMCACHED. -- err apmd[13738]: 01490086:3: /Common/my.profile.name:Common:2a392ccd: Rule evaluation failed with error: can't use empty string as operand of "-"
bugs.conditions: -- Access profile contains '.' (dot) characters in its name. -- License Check agent is used in the VPE to check against profile license.
bugs.impact: License check always fails, resulting in denied logon.
bugs.workaround: Use a different policy name without '.' characters.
bugs.fix: A new session variable named 'session.access.profileid' contains the profile name, with '.' characters being replaced with '_' characters, if any. If License agent branch rule uses profile license consumption as the criterion, do one of the following: -- If profile name is hard-coded, manually replace the '.' characters with '_' characters in the profile name. -- If the profile name is fetched from session variable, use 'session.access.profileid' instead of 'session.access.profile', as shown in the following example: expr {(([mcget -license "tmm.profilelicense.[mcget {session.access.profileid}]"] - [mcget -license "tmm.profilelicense.[mcget {session.access.profileid}]#"]) * 100) >= ([mcget -license "tmm.profilelicense.[mcget {session.access.profileid}]"] * 20)}
bugs.behavior: A new session variable named 'session.access.profileid' contains the profile name, with '.' characters being replaced with '_' characters, if any. If License agent branch rule uses profile license consumption as the criterion, do one of the following: -- If profile name is hard-coded, manually replace the '.' characters with '_' characters in the profile name. -- If the profile name is fetched from session variable, use 'session.access.profileid' instead of 'session.access.profile', as shown in the following example: expr {(([mcget -license "tmm.profilelicense.[mcget {session.access.profileid}]"] - [mcget -license "tmm.profilelicense.[mcget {session.access.profileid}]#"]) * 100) >= ([mcget -license "tmm.profilelicense.[mcget {session.access.profileid}]"] * 20)}

bugs.title: PEM sessions may stay in marked_for_delete state with Gx reporting and Gy enabled
bugs.symptoms: PEM sessions may stay in the marked-for-delete state after session deletion.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if Gx final usage reporting response comes before Gy delete response (CCA).
bugs.impact: PEM sessions remain in marked-for-delete state.
bugs.fix: PEM sessions no longer stay in the marked-for-delete state after session delete

bugs.title: Admin user roles automatically demoted to guest
bugs.symptoms: Newly created admin users are immediately demoted to guest.
bugs.conditions: -- A sync-failover device group exists. -- The REST framework's 'gossip' mechanism is configured. -- Create a new admin user using a command similar to the following examples: tmsh ----- tmsh create auth user test123 password **** partition-access add { all-partitions { role admin } } GUI ----- via WebUI System menu :: Users User Name: test123 Password: **** Confirm: **** Role: Administrator Partition: All Click Finish button Note: Correct REST framework 'gossip' mechanism configuration should occur automatically, but might not be ready. You can confirm whether this is the case by running the following command: restcurl shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices. The output must show all your devices, and show that they all have the same 'version' and the same 'restFrameworkVersion'.
bugs.impact: In a few seconds, the newly created admin user account reverts to a guest role. User does not have the expected admin access.
bugs.workaround: On the primary BIG-IP system, do the following: 1. Disable failover by running the following command: restcurl -X PATCH tm/shared/bigip-failover-state -d '{"isEnabled": false}' 2. Clear REST devices from the device group by running the following command: restcurl -X DELETE shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices

bugs.title: FQDN template nodes resolving to same IP address cannot be used in multiple non-Common partitions
bugs.symptoms: If an FQDN template node is created in a partition (not Common), then another FQDN template node is created in different partition but resolves to same IP address as the first FQDN template node, adding the second FQDN template node to a pool in the second partition will fail. An error message will be logged similar to the following: err mcpd[...]: 01020036:3: The requested Pool Member (/part1/pool_1 /part2/node2-192.168.172.246 80) was not found.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating FQDN template node in a partition other than Common. -- Creating another FQDN template node in different partition. -- Each node resolves to same IP address.
bugs.impact: Cannot add FQDN node to pool.
bugs.workaround: Create the first FQDN template node in the Common partition. Then, when FQDN template nodes are created on a different partition, they use the ephemeral node in Common.

bugs.title: After upgrade to 13.1.0 or later, mcpd fails to start due to syslog config parsing error.
bugs.symptoms: Prior to 13.1.0, the left square bracket character '[' was not treated as a special character and therefore did not have to be escaped with a '\'. 13.1.0 (and later) uses a newer version of syslog-ng, 3.8.1, where the left square bracket '[' is a special character and needs to be escaped. If you have a syslog filter that includes a match statement that formerly escaped only the right square bracket and not the left, when you upgrade to 13.1.0 or later, mcpd will fail to start with the following error: 01070920:3: Application error for confpp: Error parsing filter expression, error compiling search pattern, error=Error while compiling PCRE expression, error=missing terminating ] for character class, error_at=10 in /etc/syslog-ng/syslog-ng.conf.
bugs.conditions: -- The pre-v13.1.0 configuration contains a syslog filter that matches a string that contains a left and right square bracket. -- Only the right square bracket is escaped with 2 backslashes. For example: filter f_ssl_acc_req { not (facility(local6) and level(info) and match('[ssl_acc\\]')) or not (facility(local6) and level(info) and match('[ssl_req\\]')); };
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails to start.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Prior to upgrading, edit the syslog config with tmsh edit /sys syslog all-properties and escape the left square bracket with 4 backslashes '\', so for: [ssl_acc\\] change to \\\\[ssl_acc\\]. Example steps for vi editor =========================== Change from: filter f_ssl_acc_req { not (facility(local6) and level(info) and match('[ssl_acc\\]')) or not (facility(local6) and level(info) and match('[ssl_req\\]')); }; Change to: filter f_ssl_acc_req { not (facility(local6) and level(info) and match('\\\\[ssl_acc\\]')) or not (facility(local6) and level(info) and match('\\\\[ssl_req\\]')); }; For more detailed instructions see K96275603: The mcpd process may not start due to a syslog configuration parsing error after upgrading to BIG-IP 13.1.0 or later :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K96275603. -- You can prevent the issue from occurring altogether by defining filters using guidelines outlined in the following documents: -- K16932: Configuring the BIG-IP system to suppress sending SSL access and request messages to remote syslog servers :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K16932. -- Syslog-ng FAQ :: https://syslog-ng.com/wiki/syslog-ng-faq-filters.

bugs.title: NAS-IP-Address added to RADIUS packet unexpectedly
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS authentication request contains NAS-IP-Address attribute with value 127.0.0.1.
bugs.conditions: VIPRION (single or multiblade) with no cluster member IP addresses configured.
bugs.impact: Authentication does not work as it has invalid/unrecognized source NAS-IP-Address.
bugs.workaround: Configure cluster member IP address or define hostname and address via global-settings remote-host.

bugs.title: nitrox_diag may run out of space on /shared
bugs.symptoms: Running nitrox_diag may lose collected data if there is insufficient free space for the tar file to be created.
bugs.conditions: -- Running nitrox_diag. -- Insufficient free space available on /shared.
bugs.impact: Might lose data required to diagnose problems with Cavium Nitrox chips.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to ensure there is enough free space for the files to be created. In general, planning enough space for two copies of a tmm core file and two copies of a qkview works. That might require approximately one gigabyte. Though more might be needed for systems with a large amount of RAM.
bugs.fix: nitrox_diag now clears the older data before gathering new data, instead of after. Note, however, that if there is insufficient free space on /shared to collect the raw data, the operation still cannot succeed.

bugs.title: Custom dashboards do not upgrade from previous versions
bugs.symptoms: In previous releases, you could create customized dashboards using the Flash-based dashboard environment. This version of the software replaces the Flash-based dashboard with an HTML5-based dashboard. Because of the difference on dashboard widgets and technology differences, your customized Flash dashboards are not rolled forward during the upgrade to the new version.
bugs.conditions: -- Using pre-v14.0.0 software. -- Creating custom, Flash-based dashboards. -- Upgrading to v14.0.0 or later.
bugs.impact: You will not be able to see your previously saved, customized, Flash-based dashboards after upgrading to 14.0.0 or later. This occurs because of technological and framework differences between the old Flash-based dashboard and the new HTML5-based dashboard.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no direct workaround, the new dashboard lets you create customized dashboard views that do migrate with upgrades.

bugs.title: ASM GUI Fails to Display Policy List After Upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade to version 13.1.0 or later, ASM GUI fails to display the Policy List.
bugs.conditions: Using an 11.5.0 to 11.5.4-HF1 version that is affected by the issue of policies with duplicate REST IDs that occurred after restoring from policy history or using Policy Diff to compare policies.
bugs.impact: ASM GUI starting using the REST API from version 13.1.0, so any systems that have been affected by this issue on a previous version now cause the GUI to fail to display the Policy List.
bugs.workaround: On the device run the following script: --------------------------------- perl -MF5::DbUtils -MF5::Utils::Rest -MF5::ASMConfig::Entity::Policy -e '$dbh = F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(); $dbh->begin_work(); $dbh->do("UPDATE PLC.PL_POLICIES a SET a.rest_uuid = \"\" WHERE a.rest_uuid IN ( SELECT rest_uuid FROM (SELECT rest_uuid FROM PLC.PL_POLICIES GROUP BY rest_uuid having count(*) > 1) b)"); F5::Utils::Rest::populate_uuids(dbh => $dbh); $dbh->commit();' --------------------------------- Note: In a management environment, this change must be pushed to the peer as a full sync. The easiest way to do so is to ensure that the ASM sync device group is in manual sync mode, and to push the config to the peers from the device where the script was run.
bugs.fix: This data inconsistency is now repaired on upgrade, and the GUI loads the policy list successfully.

bugs.title: Edge Browser does not launch F5 VPN App
bugs.symptoms: On Microsoft Windows v10, use Edge Browser to establish VPN. Edge Browser does not launch F5 VPN App.
bugs.conditions: On Windows 10, use Edge Browser to establish VPN.
bugs.impact: APM end user cannot establish VPN tunnel using Edge Browser.
bugs.workaround: Use Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome.
bugs.fix: You can now use Windows 10 to launch Edge Browser to establish VPN connections.

bugs.title: Update cipher support for Common Criteria compliance
bugs.symptoms: Default cipher selection may not be compliant with Common Criteria requirements. Please see the Common Criteria guidance documentation for details about cipher strings in CC mode.
bugs.conditions: Common Criteria mode active
bugs.impact: Please see the Common Criteria guidance documentation for details about cipher strings in CC mode.
bugs.workaround: Please see the Common Criteria guidance documentation for details about cipher strings in CC mode.
bugs.fix: Improved Common Criteria compliance in default cipher strings.

bugs.title: TLS1.3 handshake fails for RSA PSS SHA512 with netHSM RSA 1024-bit key
bugs.symptoms: TLS1.3 handshake fails 1024-bit netHSM key with error message of "C_Sign with pss: pkcs11_rv=0x00000006, CKR_FUNCTION_FAILED".
bugs.conditions: netHSM 1024-bit RSA key is used
bugs.impact: C_Sign operation failed which leads to TLS1.3 handshake failed.
bugs.workaround: Don't use netHSM 1024-bit RSA key, it is not safe and should not be recommended.

bugs.title: PEM iRule subscriber policy name query using subscriber ID, may not return applied policies
bugs.symptoms: PEM::subscriber config policy get <subscriber id> does not return policy names
bugs.conditions: PEM iRule using subscriber ID to get policy name.
bugs.impact: Subscriber policy names are not returned.
bugs.workaround: Use PEM::subscriber config policy get <IP address> instead.
bugs.fix: Subscriber policy names are now returned when running PEM iRules using subscriber ID to get policy names.

bugs.title: MRF DIAMETER: Add log events to log when stale messages are removed from pending request queue
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to know when a stale pending request entry is removed from the pending request queue.
bugs.conditions: A stale pending request entry is removed from the pending request queue.
bugs.impact: There is no log message indicating that this has occurred, making it impossible to track which request did not receive an answer message.
bugs.fix: New log events have been added to account for these requests.

bugs.title: bcm56xxd crash with empty trunk in QinQ VLAN
bugs.symptoms: When an empty trunk (no members) is configured 'tagged' in a QinQ VLAN, bcm56xxd will continuously crash.
bugs.conditions: Trunk with no members, configured as 'tagged' in a QinQ VLAN.
bugs.impact: bcm56xxd continuously crashes.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Add members to the trunk. -- Remove the trunk from the QinQ VLAN.
bugs.fix: Do not program QinQ switch hardware if the trunk has no members.

bugs.title: Default disabled DoS profile cannot be attached to virtual server because of BADOS '2 virtual servers limitation'
bugs.symptoms: Configuration error: DoS profile with behavioral detection cannot be attached to a virtual server because use is limited to 2 virtual servers when the DoS profile does not have BADOS configuration.
bugs.conditions: Intermittent reproduction when more than 2 virtual servers and DoS profile pairs configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot assign DoS profile to virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Modify the DoS profile configuration: enable/disable BADOS features (bad actors/signatures) and try to reassign DoS profile to the virtual server.
bugs.fix: There is no 2-virtual server limitation when no BADOS is configured.

bugs.title: Vcmp_pde_state_memcpy core during http traffic and pfmand resets.
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts with core file available.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs intermittently under the following conditions: -- System uses pfmand. -- pfmand health monitoring enabled (sys db pfmand.healthstatus value enable, this is the default). -- The system is passing http traffic. -- pfmand is reset (tmsh modify sys pfman device 0/00:0c.5 status reset).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.

bugs.title: Connection might get reset when coming to virtual server with offload iRule
bugs.symptoms: When IN_DOSL7_ATTACK event is triggered, and iRule has an async command in it, events might be released out of order, causing connection RST.
bugs.conditions: 1. Have DoS profile with iRule turned on. 2. iRule is async (such as wait, DNS resolving, etc.). 3. Send POST request.
bugs.impact: Connection receives a RST.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Modified event ordering, which avoids connection RST.

bugs.title: Web GUI can sometime display the wrong cert and key for a GTM monitor that has the same name as some LTM monitor.
bugs.symptoms: The web GUI displays an incorrect value for cert and key for a GTM monitor.
bugs.conditions: The GTM monitor has the same name as an LTM monitor.
bugs.impact: Incorrect data can be presented regarding the GTM monitor's cert and key.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to display the correct cert and key.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing UDP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions BIG-IP systems may leak memory. Over time, the memory lost might affect performance/scalability as the unit approaches an out-of-memory condition. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: -- UDP profile configured. -- CLIENT_ACCEPTED iRule in use.
bugs.impact: Over time, this issue might lead to a BIG-IP system out-of-memory condition, which results in a TMM crash and failover event. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Run the following command: tmsh modify sys db tmm.sessiondb.table_cmd_timeout_override value true -- Enable 'resassemble-fragments' in the FastL4 profile.

bugs.title: The drops statistics in tmsh for LTM::DNS Profile Unhandled Query Action percentage column does not display the percentage
bugs.symptoms: The drops stat for LTM::DNS Profile Unhandled Query Action percentage column always displays as '-' in tmsh, regardless of the actual percentage.
bugs.conditions: LTM and DNS services provisioned, enabled, and configured.
bugs.impact: Incorrect drops stat for LTM::DNS Profile Unhandled Query Action percentage. Column always displays the value '-' instead of an actual percentage.
bugs.fix: The drops stat for LTM::DNS Profile Unhandled Query Action percentage column now displays the actual percentage.

bugs.title: AVR should not send statistic on hidden rows for module InterfaceTraffic and module InterfaceHealth
bugs.symptoms: AVR sends data on all interfaces, hidden and not hidden. It should send information only on not-hidden interfaces.
bugs.conditions: -- Tmstat table interface_stat exists. -- Viewing statistics for module InterfaceTraffic and module InterfaceHealth.
bugs.impact: Irrelevant data is sent.
bugs.fix: AVR now sends data only on not-hidden interfaces.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system accepts larger-than-egress MTU, PMTU update
bugs.symptoms: A Path MTU (PMTU) message can lead to the BIG-IP system to falsely assume an egress MTU on the related flow to be larger than the interface egress MTU.
bugs.conditions: A valid PMTU message.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP sends larger-than-configured interface egress MTU messages.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now limits the flow egress MTU to the interface egress MTU.

bugs.title: /proc/swaps is collected in qkview
bugs.symptoms: Not applicable. /proc/swaps is collected in qkview for getting additional information on system state for debugging purposes.
bugs.conditions: Not applicable.
bugs.workaround: collect /proc/swaps file manually and share with f5 for debugging if needed.
bugs.fix: /proc/swaps is collected in qkview for getting additional information on system state for debugging purposes.

bugs.title: When making a REST request to an object in /stats that is an association list, the selfLink has a duplicate name
bugs.symptoms: When you make a REST request to association list in /stats you get a duplicate name in the selfLink after members in both the entries and the selfLink, e.g.: # restcurl -X GET -u admin /tm/ltm/pool/~Common~pool1/members/~Common~node1:8105/stats { "kind": "tm:ltm:pool:members:membersstats", "generation": 3, "selfLink": "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/~Common~pool1/members/~Common~node1:8105/stats?ver\u003d14.0.0", "entries": { "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/~Common~pool1/members/~Common~node1:8105/~Common~node1:8105/stats": {
bugs.conditions: When making a REST request to an object in /stats that is an association list.
bugs.impact: The selfLink has a duplicate name. SelfLinks for associations do not work.
bugs.fix: This version uses the full path, so the issue no longer occurs, e.g.: # restcurl -X GET -u admin /tm/ltm/pool/~Common~pool1/members/~Common~node1:8103/stats

bugs.title: customizing or changing the HTTP Profile's IPv6 field hides the field or the row
bugs.symptoms: Customizing or changing the HTTP Profile's IPv6 field hides the field or the row.
bugs.conditions: Customizing or changing the HTTP Profile's IPv6 field.
bugs.impact: The HTTP Profile's IPv6 field cannot be customized or changed.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to set the HTTP Profile's IPv6 field.
bugs.fix: Customizing or changing the HTTP Profile's IPv6 field doesn't hide the field or the row.

bugs.title: AVR should report on all 'global tags' in external logs
bugs.symptoms: AVR reports only 'ssgName' from the global tags.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IQ operation configures the 'tag file' (/var/config/rest/downloads/app_mapping.json) on the BIG-IP system. -- Statistics are sent to the BIG-IQ system.
bugs.impact: Not all the tags are sent to the BIG-IQ system.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: AVR now reports statistics on all tags to the BIG-IQ system.

bugs.title: A vCMP guest may not provide guest health stats to the vCMP host
bugs.symptoms: A vCMP guest usually provides the vCMP host with some guest health statistics as a convenience to the vCMP host administrator. These stats are: -- mgmt/tm/sys/ha-status -- mgmt/tm/sys/software/status -- mgmt/tm/sys/software/provision These tables are created by the host when host vcmpd queries the guest over the vmchannel using REST. These RESTful queries may sometimes fail, causing the queried vCMP guest to be omitted in the display of the output of the following command: $ tmsh show vcmp guest
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP provisioned. -- Guests are deployed. -- Host vcmpd queries the guest over the vmchannel using REST.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact to the guests or to the host, other than these lost tables. -- Some vCMP guests may not show up in the output of the following command: tmsh show vcmp health -- Some guests may appear with the wrong status in the GUI. Such as being grey when it should be green. -- Files containing guest information, kept in: /var/run/vcmpd/<guestname>/json/(sys-ha-status.json|sys-provision.json|sys-software.json) may be missing from that directory. -- There might be files present there named using the following structure: /var/run/vcmpd/<guestname>/json/sys-(ha-status|provision|software).json.bad.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Decompression of large buffer might fail with comp_code=11 with Nitrox 3 hardware
bugs.symptoms: Messages like the following may show up in /var/log/ltm: -- crit tmm5[28908]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Zip engine ctx eviction (comp_code=11): ctx dropped. This occurs because the decompression of large compressed data failed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when compressed data cannot be decompressed in a single request to the Nitrox 3 hardware accelerator.
bugs.impact: Requests fail with a connection reset.
bugs.workaround: Use zlib software decompression.
bugs.fix: This release fixes this decompression issue in the Nitrox 3 driver.

bugs.title: Size of ibdata1 and DCC.CLIENT_SIDE_DROPPED_STAT
bugs.symptoms: MySQL partition size reaching 100%. The ASM log contains continuously reports 'Web scraping attack' being started/finished.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned -- A new attack starts every second or so.
bugs.impact: The 'DCC.CLIENT_SIDE_DROPPED_STAT' table exceeds the maximum of 20,000 rows, as defined in '/etc/ts/tools/clean_db.yaml' (a limit that should be imposed by the 'clean_db' process, which appears to be running without errors, verified by viewing the following log: /var/log/ts/clean_db.log). That ASM log is filled (~85% of it) with reports about 'Web scraping attacks' being started/finished. Most of the time, a new attack starts every second or so, indicating, perhaps, that the 'clean_db' process cannot keep up with cleaning that table.
bugs.workaround: Back up that single table and truncate it as follows: 1. To check how many records there are, run the following MySQL query: mysql -uasm -p`perl -MF5::Cfg -e 'print F5::Cfg::get_mysql_password()'` -e "Select count(*) from DCC.CLIENT_SIDE_DROPPED_STAT;" 2. To back up the records, run the following MySQL query: mysqldump --single-transaction -uasm -p`perl -MF5::Cfg -e 'print F5::Cfg::get_mysql_password()'` DCC CLIENT_SIDE_DROPPED_STAT >/shared/CLIENT_SIDE_DROPPED_STAT.sql Specify a target backup partition with at least 6 GB of available space. 3. To delete records, run the following MySQL query: mysql -uasm -p`perl -MF5::Cfg -e 'print F5::Cfg::get_mysql_password()'` -e "delete from DCC.CLIENT_SIDE_DROPPED_STAT;"

bugs.title: LDAP and AD Group Resource Assign are not displaying Static ACLs correctly
bugs.symptoms: In VPE LDAP and AD Group Resource Assign are not displaying static acls when they are configured.
bugs.conditions: While attempting to assign Static ACls via AD or LDAP Group Resource assign (aka Group Mapping) Static ACLs are not displayed.
bugs.impact: Users are not able to assign Static ACLs with AD and LDAP Group Mapping via VPE.
bugs.workaround: Static ACLs are assignable with TMSH.
bugs.fix: Functionality is restored and Static ACLs are being displayed in AD and Ldap Group Resource Assign aka Group Mapping use: tmsh modify apm policy agent resource-assign

bugs.title: Missing reference to customization-group from connectivity profile if created via network access wizard
bugs.symptoms: Connectivity profile generated from the use of network access wizard will not contain a reference to a customization-group.
bugs.conditions: Use network access wizard to create configure objects.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact since customization is not actually used for connectivity group.
bugs.workaround: Configure the connectivity profile object manually from tmui (GUI) or tmsh (command line) rather than via wizard. Replace the connectivity profile created from the virtual server within the virtual server with the manually created connectivity profile.

bugs.title: GTMD may intermittently crash under unusual conditions.
bugs.symptoms: GTMD may intermittently crash when an unexpected error occurs while creating a statistics row for a resource added to the configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- A pool member is added to the system. -- There is an unexpected failure to create the associated statistics row.
bugs.impact: GTMD restarts. Global traffic functionality is not available while GTMD is restarting.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: GTMD no longer intermittently crashes when a pool member is added to the system, but there is an unexpected failure to create the associated statistics row.

bugs.title: bd daemon restart loop
bugs.symptoms: Continuous BD restarts after period where /var was full and then cleaned
bugs.conditions: /var was full and then cleaned
bugs.impact: Continuous BD restarts
bugs.workaround: A) Make a spurious change in a policy and apply it. OR B) Restart ASM

bugs.title: ASM stalls WebSocket frames after legitimate websockets handshake with 101 status code, but without 'Switching Protocols' reason phrase
bugs.symptoms: When the WebSocket HTTP handshake response comes without 'Switching Protocols' reason phrase at the first line, the ASM does not follow up WebSocket frames on the WebSocket's connection. The system posts the following messages in /ts/log/bd.log: -- IO_PLUGIN|ERR |Mar 28 09:16:15.121|30539|websocket.c:0269|101 Switching Protocols HTTP status arrived, but the websocket hanshake failed. -- IO_PLUGIN|ERR |Mar 28 09:16:15.121|30539|websocket.c:0270|Possible reasons are websocket profile isn't assigned on a virtual server or handshake is illegal.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy and WebSocket profile attached to a virtual server. -- WebSocket backend server sends 101 response without the 'Switching Protocols' phrase.
bugs.impact: WebSocket frames stalls.
bugs.workaround: #1 Change the backend server: Change WebSocket backend server to return 101 response to include the 'Switching Protocols' reason phrase: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols #2 Use an irRule: when SERVER_CONNECTED { TCP::collect 15 } when SERVER_DATA { if { [TCP::payload 15] contains "HTTP/1.1 101 \r\n" } { TCP::payload replace 0 12 "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols" } }
bugs.fix: This release correctly handles 101 responses even without the 'Switching Protocols' reason phrase.

bugs.title: Permission is denied when accessing iRulesLX workspace
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to access the iRulesLX workspace page after a workspace has been created will result in an error similar to: General database error retrieving information.General error: 01070711:3: boost::filesystem::status: Permission denied: "/var/ilx/workspaces/Common/ilxtest_ws/rules/ilx-test-rule.tcl" in statement [SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dev_workspace WHERE name LIKE '%']
bugs.conditions: It happens after the workspace is created.
bugs.impact: Cannot access iRuleLX workspace.
bugs.workaround: running "setenforce 0" will allow you to access the GUI page and work normally.
bugs.fix: This problem is fixed in v14.1.0.

bugs.title: Enhanced administrator lock/unlock for Common Criteria compliance
bugs.symptoms: The Network Device and Firewall collaborative Protection Profiles v2.0 require certain behavior for locking and unlocking administrative-user accounts on the BIG-IP system. BIG-IP software needs to be enhanced for compliance with those requirements.
bugs.conditions: The ccmode script must be run to activate these enhancements. Also, see the Common Criteria Guidance document (published when the certificate is obtained) for more details.
bugs.impact: Without these enhancements activated, the BIG-IP system is not compliant with Common Criteria requirements.
bugs.workaround: Risk acceptance for Common Criteria non-compliance.
bugs.fix: To meet Common Criteria requirements, the BIG-IP system is enhanced in two areas: 1. The primary administrative user account (generally 'admin') can be locked out, as any other administrative-user account can be. However, it is never locked out when signing in from the serial console. 2. Locked out administrative-users are unlocked only after an administrator-specified time period has passed. The default is 10 minutes, and is set in the ccmode script.

bugs.title: Serverside packets excluded from DoS stats
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems configured with L4 DoS Protection might not provide sufficiently granular DDoS detection and mitigation to ensure that legitimate traffic is not impacted.
bugs.conditions: Configured for DDoS detection and mitigation.
bugs.impact: Legitimate traffic might be impacted.
bugs.fix: The following DoS vectors no longer count serverside packets. -- Single-Endpoint Flood -- Global-Device level aggregate vectors -- Bad-actor/attacked-dst for all vectors Additionally, hardware-accelerated, device-level (global) aggregate DoS vectors are now programmed dynamically when traffic is detected, rather than at configuration time. These behavior changes provide greater granularity in DDoS detection and mitigation to ensure that legitimate traffic is not impacted.
bugs.behavior: The following DoS vectors no longer count serverside packets. -- Single-Endpoint Flood -- Global-Device level aggregate vectors -- Bad-actor/attacked-dst for all vectors Additionally, hardware-accelerated, device-level (global) aggregate DoS vectors are now programmed dynamically when traffic is detected, rather than at configuration time. These behavior changes provide greater granularity in DDoS detection and mitigation to ensure that legitimate traffic is not impacted.

bugs.title: Records containing hyphens (-) will prevent child zone from loading correctly
bugs.symptoms: The dig command returns no record with SOA from the parent zone even though dnsxdump shows that the record exists.
bugs.conditions: -- Parent zone has a record containing - (a hyphen) and the preceding characters match the child zone. For example, myzone.com -- parent foo.myzone.com -- child -- In myzone.com, you have a record of the following form: foo-record.myzone.com
bugs.impact: DNS can not resolve records correctly.
bugs.fix: DNS now handles the case in which the parent zone has a record containing - (a hyphen) and the preceding characters match the child zone.

bugs.title: Exclude the trusted anchor certificate in hash algorithm selection when Forward Proxy forges a certificate
bugs.symptoms: SSL Forward Proxy signs a forged certificate with a hash algorithm. This selected hash algorithm is the weakest algorithm from the certificates in the server certificate chain except the self-signed certificate. Some of the intermediate CA certificates in the cert chain use the SHA1 hash algorithm. This kind of intermediate CAs is usually in the BIG-IP system's ca-bundle. BIG-IP receives the cert chain including the intermediate CA and forges the cert with SHA1, which is rejected by some web clients.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is configured to use SSL Forward Proxy or SSL Intercept. -- Some intermediate CA in the web server's cert chain is using a weak algorithm like SHA1 to sign certificates. -- The web client rejects the weak-algorithm-signed certificate.
bugs.impact: Clients cannot access the web server due to SSL handshake failure.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This fix excludes trusted CA certificates in hash algorithm selection. This may prevent forged certificate from using SHA1 hash algorithm.

bugs.title: DNS zones without servers will prevent DNS Express reading zone data
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express does not return dig requests.
bugs.conditions: DNS Express is configured a zone without a server.
bugs.impact: DNS Express does not return dig requests.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Remove the zone without the server. -- Configure a server for the zone.
bugs.fix: DNS zones without servers no longer prevent DNS Express reading zone data.

bugs.title: TMM crashes with message 'bad transition'
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes under a set of conditions in which the system detects an internal inconsistency. The system posts an error similar to the following in the LTM and TMM logs: crit tmm[18755]: 01010289:2: Oops @ 0x2285e10:5157: bad transition
bugs.conditions: Conditions that cause this to happen are not predictable, but these might make it more likely: -- FastL4 virtual server and HTTP are configured -- db variable tmm.oops set to 'panic'. -- Client sends three GET requests at once, and then closes the connection after a few seconds. -- The server sends a partial 'Connection: close' response.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Unhandled Query Action Drops Stat does not increment after transparent cache miss
bugs.symptoms: After a transparent cache miss, if the LTM DNS profile has Unhandled Query Action set to Drop, the request is dropped without incrementing the Unhandled Query Action Drops stat.
bugs.conditions: LTM DNS profile with a Transparent Cache and Unhandled Query Action set to Drop.
bugs.impact: Inaccurate statistics for the Unhandled Query Action Drops

bugs.title: DNSSEC keys are not generated when configured to use an external FIPS device
bugs.symptoms: DNSSEC keys that use an external FIPS device are not generated, and an SELinux denial is reported in /var/log/auditd/audit.log. The logged permission denial should indicate that a process running under the 'mcpd_t' SELinux context was denied the 'execmem' permission.
bugs.conditions: -- A device is configured with one or more DNSSEC keys that are configured to be generated by an external FIPS device (indicated by the 'use-fips' option being set to 'external'). -- An unpatched version of the Thales client software be in use on the device.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC keys will not be generated when configured to use the external FIPS device.
bugs.workaround: Update the version of the Thales client software that is in use on the device.

bugs.title: Network Access client caches the response for /pre/config.php
bugs.symptoms: The Network Access client caches the response for /pre/config.php.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is provisioned. -- Network Access is configured.
bugs.impact: Caching the response for /pre/config.php might reveal configuration information. However, a URL is public information by definition. The only sensitive information revealed are server names, which have to be revealed in order for the client to know where to connect.

bugs.title: PEM quota bucket gets deleted after receiving diameter too busy for max retry count
bugs.symptoms: PEM keeps retrying CCR-i even after reaching max retry count, in the case where OCS responds to CCR-i with DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY result code.
bugs.conditions: If OCS sends CCA DIAMETER_TOO_BUSY (result code 3004) for CCR-i messages
bugs.impact: PEM keeps retrying even after the max retry count is reached.

bugs.title: FTP with asymmetric routing and mirroring does not forward traffic or mirror on data connection
bugs.symptoms: FTP mirroring in an environment with asymmetrical routing on the clientside may fail to forward data connection traffic or correctly mirror the traffic to the peer unit.
bugs.conditions: With the following setup: - Asymmetric routing setup on the clientside. - The following db keys are disabled: + connection.autolasthop + connection.vlankeyed - Virtual server with FTP profile (inherit profile disabled). - Mirroring enabled.
bugs.impact: -- Passive data connection SYN is be forwarded. -- Mirroring of the data connection does not complete successfully.
bugs.workaround: Set a specific route to the client IP address to override asymmetric routing.

bugs.title: Host header persistence not implemented
bugs.symptoms: Online documentation describes a persistence mechanism which uses the HTTP Host: header. However, this mechanism is not implemented, and attempts to use it generates an error.
bugs.conditions: Online help for ltm persistence says that Host persistence can be enabled via iRule, but attempting to do so generates an error 'invalid argument host'.
bugs.impact: Although this does not impact any existing functionality, the documented function is not available.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: LTM Host: header persistence is implemented.

bugs.title: A GTM global variable has been added to "force invalid NS names" for all auto-generated zones for WideIPs.
bugs.symptoms: Fall back to BIND is enabled by default and if the use of the GTM hostname is misunderstood, the device could be exposed to potential DNS hijacking.
bugs.conditions: GTM automatically creates a zone file using the GTM hostname. If Fall back to BIND is tuned on and the Wide IP goes down, BIND will respond with an answer that has NS records in the authority section.
bugs.impact: If the device uses an unregistered hostname, a third party could register it and and hijack the domain.
bugs.workaround: Workaround A: - Change the hostnames on the GTMs to be a label within a domain you own. - Change the NS records in all the autogenerated zones that are not already pointing at a real domain to point at this hostname. Workaround B: - Turn off Fallback to BIND
bugs.fix: A GTM global variable has been added to "force invalid NS names" for all auto-generated zones for WideIPs. This variable is enabled by default for security purposes. This must be a gtm global so that it is synced. If this value is "true/enabled" then ".invalid." is appended to the BIG-IP's hostname. (See RFCs 6761 and 2606). This is the recommended way to build DNS names that should not escape into the public domain.

bugs.title: IPv6 NS dropped for hosts on transparent vlangroup with address equal to ARP disabled virtual-address
bugs.symptoms: As a result of a known issue IPv6 NS may be dropped if corresponds for host on remote VLAN of transparent vlangroup and matches a Virtual address with disabled ARP setting
bugs.conditions: - transparent vlan-group - Virtual Address with ARP disabled - Virtual Address corresponds to remote IPv6 host address
bugs.impact: NS for the host is dropped. Traffic will not reach the remote host as resolution does not complete.
bugs.workaround: Do not use overlapping Virtual-addresses with ARP disabled, or enable ARP.
bugs.fix: IPv6 NS is no longer dropped for hosts on transparent vlangroup with address equal to ARP disabled virtual-address.

bugs.title: TMM may halt and restart when threshold mode is set to stress-based mitigation
bugs.symptoms: When auto-DoS vector's threshold mode is set to stress-based mitigation, but the vector is in disabled state, TMM may halt and restart.
bugs.conditions: -- Threshold mode is set to stress-based mitigation. -- Vector is disabled.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts. Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not setting threshold mode to stress-based mitigation if the vector is disabled.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer restarts when threshold mode is set to stress-based mitigation and the vector is in disabled state.

bugs.title: fpdd may core dump when the system is going down
bugs.symptoms: fpdd may core dump when the system is going down. This is because the LED manager in the daemon cannot use the hal library to talk to other daemons.
bugs.conditions: The problem happens when the system is going down.
bugs.impact: This is a rarely occurring issue. When it happens, fpdd creates a core file. The LEDs may not reflect the status right before the shutdown. But the LEDs are reinitialized after the bootup.
bugs.fix: fpdd no longer core dumps when the system is going down.

bugs.title: 'HTTP::hsts preload' iRule command cannot be used
bugs.symptoms: Using the 'HTTP::hsts preload' iRule command in the GUI, you might see error message similar to the following: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/test] error: /Common/test:3: error: ["invalid argument preload; expected syntax spec: "][HTTP::hsts preload enable]. The message is incorrect: the command has the correct format. However, the system does not run it.
bugs.conditions: Using the 'HTTP::hsts preload' iRule command in the GUI.
bugs.impact: The command does not run. Cannot use the 'HTTP::hsts preload' iRule command in the GUI.
bugs.fix: 'HTTP::hsts preload' iRule command now works as expected.

bugs.title: SWG-Explicit rejects large POST bodies during policy evaluation
bugs.symptoms: When an access profile of type SWG-Explicit is being used, there is a 128 KB limit on POST bodies while the policy is being evaluated. The system posts an error message similar to the following in /var/log/apm: err tmm[13751]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: hud_access_process_ingress, Line: 3048
bugs.conditions: This applies only during policy evaluation. After the policy has been set to 'Allow', there is no limit to the POST body.
bugs.impact: Unable to start an SWG-Explicit policy with a large POST body.
bugs.fix: Now, you can resolve this issue by modifying db variable 'tmm.access.maxrequestbodysize' to use a value larger than the maximum request size you want to support.

bugs.title: Removing an iRule from a Virtual Server may prevent executing other iRules on the same Virtual Server.
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule is removed from a Virtual Server, especially one with explicitly specified high priority (with "priority" keyword), other iRules on the same Virtual Server may become "invisible" i.e. they are present but some of them are no longer executed. It may affect all the events or only certain types of them. Under certain conditions the defect may even disappear upon removing another iRule, particularly if it has low priority and handles the same event as the one which introduced the problem.
bugs.conditions: Removing an iRule from a Virtual Server.
bugs.impact: Some or all iRules on given Virtual Servers stop being executed.
bugs.workaround: Restart or reload the configuration. If removing iRules needs to be performed in run-time and it triggers the problem, it can be prevented by having any iRule (even an empty one) for the same event, as the iRule which is going to be removed, but with higher priority e.g. with attribute "priority 1".
bugs.fix: Corrected scanning of iRules stored behind the one which is being deleted.

bugs.title: In VPE SecurID servers list are not being displayed in SecurID authentication dialogue
bugs.symptoms: In VPE SecurID servers list are not being displayed in SecurID authentication dialogue. List is displaying only None.
bugs.conditions: Always when adding SecureID authentication action.
bugs.impact: Inability to (re)configure SecureId via VPE.
bugs.workaround: Manually modify RSA AAA server in SecurID Auth Agent via tmsh: tmsh modify apm policy agent aaa-securid <aaa agent> server <securid server name>

bugs.title: Unable to query a monitor status through iControl REST if the monitor is in a non-default partition
bugs.symptoms: It is not possible to query a monitor status through iControl REST if the monitor is in a non-default partition. If the monitor is in the /Common partition it is possible to obtain the monitor status with following command: [root@TEST_UNIT:Active:Disconnected] config # restcurl -u admin:admin /mgmt/tm/ltm/monitor/http/~Common~myHttpMonitor/stats { "kind": "tm:ltm:monitor:http:httpstats", "generation": 0, "selfLink": "https://<localhost path>", "apiRawValues": { "apiAnonymous": "------------------------------------＼n LTM::Monitor /Common/myHttpMonitor ＼n------------------------------------＼n Destination: <IP address:port>＼n State time: down for 113hrs:38mins:54sec＼n | Last error: No successful responses received before deadline. @2023.09.21 22:56:54＼n＼n" } } If the monitor is in a non-default partition, the iContol REST interface returns a "404 - Object not found" error: [root@TEST_UNIT:Active:Disconnected] config # restcurl -u admin:admin /mgmt/tm/ltm/monitor/http/~p1~myHttpMonitor/stats { "code": 404, "message": "Object not found - /p1/myHttpMonitor", "errorStack": [], "apiError": 1 }
bugs.conditions: - A monitor is configured in a non-default partition - Querying the status of the monitor in non-default partition using iControl REST
bugs.impact: It is not possible to query a monitor status through iControl REST if the monitor is in a non-default partition.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to query the status of the monitor. Following is an example: root@(TEST_UNIT)(cfg-sync Disconnected)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# cd /p1 root@(TEST_UNIT)(cfg-sync Disconnected)(Active)(/p1)(tmos)# show ltm monitor http myHttpMonitor ---------------------------------- LTM::Monitor /p1/myHttpMonitor ---------------------------------- Destination: <IP address:port> State time: down for 1hr:20mins:5sec | Last error: No successful responses received before deadline. @2023.09.26 15:21:17

bugs.title: GTM server device 'replace-all-with' reports error with specific server config
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to use a 'replace-all-with' action to replace the devices associated with a GTM/DNS server may fail with the message 'Server (<server_name>) must have at least one device.', if the new devices have the same names as the devices being replaced.
bugs.conditions: -- A 'replace-all-with' command is used to replace the devices associated with a GTM/DNS server. -- The names of all of the new devices match the names of existing devices.
bugs.impact: The 'replace-all-with' command fails. No changes are applied to the configuration.
bugs.workaround: When performing a 'replace-all-with' on the devices associated with a server, first run a 'replace-all-with' command with a placeholder device whose name does not match any of the devices being replaced or being applied. After this device is created, the intended command can be run.

bugs.title: Parameter handling and Ajax support for all HTTP request methods
bugs.symptoms: Parameters can be configured only for GET or POST HTTP request methods.
bugs.conditions: Need to protect parameters of HTTP request method that is not GET or POST.
bugs.impact: Parameters on HTTP requests that are not GET or POST cannot be configured.
bugs.fix: Parameter handling and Ajax support for all HTTP request methods are now available.

bugs.title: PB generates a suggestion to add a disallowed filtetype with empty name.
bugs.symptoms: Policy Builder (PB) generates a suggestion to add a disallowed filtetype with empty name. When trying to accept suggestion, you get a message 'action failed'.
bugs.conditions: This is a timing-related issue that occurs when trying to accept an incorrectly presented suggestion.
bugs.impact: An incorrect suggestion is issued that cannot be accepted. There is no specific impact on functionality.
bugs.workaround: Delete the suggestion, or mark it as ignored so it does not reappear.
bugs.fix: PB no longer issues the incorrect suggestion.

bugs.title: Connection failure during DNS lookup to disabled nameserver can crash TMM
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart as a result of a DNS lookup to disabled nameserver.
