bugs.conditions: DNS lookup that tries to connect to a nameserver that is not reachable for some reason. This could be an explicit 'RESOLV::lookup' command in iRule, or it could be DNS lookups internally triggered by APM or HTTP.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Verify connectivity to nameserver. As an alternative, refrain from using RESOLV::lookup in iRules.
bugs.fix: This issue is now fixed.

bugs.title: When ASM and APM are configured on the same virtual server, ASM might report some errors in its logging.
bugs.symptoms: When APM (SSO feature) and ASM are configured on the same virtual server, WebSSO recreates requests on 401 responses. Such requests have the same support ID, so ASM logs errors.
bugs.conditions: APM (WebSSO) and ASM are configured on same virtual server.
bugs.impact: ASM might potentially block such requests, so APM SSO functionality may not work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround except to not configure APM (WebSSO) and ASM on same virtual server.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: Portal Access: F5_isStyle() should be more selective
bugs.symptoms: Various web-application misfunctions are possible.
bugs.conditions: Web-application defined properties with names of style attributes that represent the subject for rewriting by Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Client-side web-application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule to handle this.

bugs.title: Small tmctl memory leak when viewing stats for snapshot files
bugs.symptoms: When viewing statistics for snapshot files, tmctl leaks a small amount of memory and displays the message: tmctl: BUG: tmstat_dealloc invoked on a handle with rows outstanding; release all rows before calling tmstat_dealloc at <address>
bugs.conditions: Using tmctl to view statistics of snapshot files, for example: tmctl -D /shared/tmstat/snapshots memory_usage_stat -s time,name,allocated,max_allocated name=access
bugs.impact: Errors written to output when running tmctl. The leak itself is very small and is only for tmctl (i.e., it does not have a cumulative, detrimental effect on the system that a TMM or MCP leak might).
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs when using tmctl to view statistics for snapshot files.

bugs.title: TMUI ILX Editor inserts an unnecessary linefeed
bugs.symptoms: If you use the TMUI edit for ILX, the system will append a linefeed character every time you save. This is not usually apparent, but if you edit the file, then delete your changes, and then save it, it will still register as changed. A message indicates the need to refresh the workspace, and the actual content of the file will change, but not the functionality.
bugs.conditions: Edit a workspace file in ILX via the TMUI editor (i.e., the GUI).
bugs.impact: File contents can change unexpectedly and have needless characters at the end.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH or a different editor, that is not TMUI, to change those files.
bugs.fix: TMUI no longer appends a linefeed character when saving.

bugs.title: Portal Access: correct processing of JavaScript code with template literals
bugs.symptoms: Modern JavaScript includes template literals, but Portal Access does not support them.
bugs.conditions: JavaScript code with template literals, for example: var a = Func `current location ${window.location}`;
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Portal Access can process JavaScript code with template literals.

bugs.title: AGC cannot do redeploy in Exchange and ADFS use cases
bugs.symptoms: In AGC exchanges or Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS) configurations, the system creates an SSL HTML form and SSO HTML form control object. Because of the limitation of ICRD, the system cannot directly delete SSO HTML form control objects.
bugs.conditions: -- Redeploy occurs in an AGC exchange ADFS configuration. -- Modifying existing configurations.
bugs.impact: Redeploy fails, configuration remain unmodified.
bugs.workaround: Do a undeploy, followed by a deploy.
bugs.fix: Redeploy now succeeds when using AGC with Exchange and ADFS use cases.

bugs.title: License String 'ASM-VE' was not recognized by the UI in the policy rule page
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system is licensed with the license string that includes 'ASM-VE' instead of the standard 'ASM', the policy page does not recognize it and does not provide the 'Enable ASM' option.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system is licensed with the license string that includes 'ASM-VE' instead of the standard 'ASM'.
bugs.impact: The policy page does not recognize it and does not provide the 'Enable ASM' option.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to create policy.

bugs.title: Malformed JSON files may be present on vCMP host
bugs.symptoms: -- Many error messages such as the following may appear in the /var/log/ltm file: warning vcmpd[7457]: 01510005:4: Failed to update guest stats from JSON file. -- The output of 'tmsh show vcmp health' may omit some guests.
bugs.conditions: All needed conditions are not yet defined. - vCMP is provisioned. - Guests are deployed.
bugs.impact: Some vCMP guests may not show up in the output of the command: tmsh show vcmp health In addition, there might be files present named using the following structure: /var/run/vcmpd/<guestname>/json/sys-(ha-status|provision|software).json.bad. There is no functional impact to the guests or to the host, other than these lost tables, which are provided as a convenience to the vCMP host administrator.
bugs.workaround: In some cases, the condition can be cleared by taking these actions in the guest instance: 1. clsh touch /service/mcpd/forceload 2. clsh reboot Otherwise, superfluous log messages may be filtered out of local logging by use of a sys syslog 'include' filter. You can filter messages related to remote/external logging using the procedure in K13333: Filtering log messages sent to remote syslog servers :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13333.

bugs.title: BIG-IP sys db variable avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable resets back to default value on services restart
bugs.symptoms: After a BIG-IP system reset, a modified setting for the BIG-IP sys db variable avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable returns to the default value.
bugs.conditions: 1. avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable value is modified from the default. 2. The BIG-IP system restarts.
bugs.impact: avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable returns to its default value.
bugs.workaround: After BIG-IP system reset, specify the value of avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable again.
bugs.fix: A modified avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable value no longer returns to the default value after BIG-IP system restart.

bugs.title: Remote logger violation_details field does not appear when virtual server has more than one remote logger
bugs.symptoms: Remote logger violation_details field appears empty.
bugs.conditions: -- More than one remote logger is attached to the virtual server. -- A violation occurs. -- Viewing the associated log.
bugs.impact: Violation_details field appears empty in logs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Remote logger violation_details field is now populated as expected when the virtual server has more than one remote logger.

bugs.title: Missing transaction count in = application security report under view by IP Intelligence
bugs.symptoms: Transactions without an IP reputation threat are not listed on application security reports under viewed by IP Intelligence.
bugs.conditions: -- All transactions without an IP reputation threat. -- Application security reports.
bugs.impact: Transaction count statistics are missing.
bugs.fix: A new category for IP reputation has been added, 'No Threat', for these transactions from an IP address that has no bad reputation, and will be listed under 'No Threat'.

bugs.title: slot1/whitebird-4800 notice Not supported protocol log message
bugs.symptoms: When ASM or AFM are licensed and provisioned, creating a FastL4 virtual server with a protocol other than TCP or UDP causes TMM to produce unnecessary log messages in the per-TMM log files (/var/log/tmm*) Redundant prints in tmm log. E.g., <13> Mar 21 21:17:19 slot1/whitebird-4800 notice Not supported protocol
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM or AFM are licensed and provisioned 2. Create a FastL4 virtual server with a protocol other than TCP or UDP
bugs.impact: Cosmetic, no functionality is affected.
bugs.fix: Remove this unnecessary print from tmm log

bugs.title: GUI iRule Data Group properties: when viewing object with IPv4-mapped IPv6 address get 'An error has occurred while trying to process your request.'
bugs.symptoms: In GUI iRule Data Group properties, when viewing an object with an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address get the following error: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule Data Group configured with an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address in tmsh. -- Attempting to view that Data Group in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Cannot view or modify iRule Data Groups with these IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to view and modify iRule Data Groups with IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses.

bugs.title: Multiple B4450 blades in the same chassis run into inconsistent DAG state
bugs.symptoms: Multiple B4450 blades in the same chassis can run into inconsistent DAGv2 state.
bugs.conditions: More than one B4450 blade in the same chassis.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent DAG state can cause traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm on one blade in the chassis and force the blades to reform the cluster in data plane.
bugs.fix: Multiple B4450 blades in the same chassis no longer experiences an inconsistent DAG state.

bugs.title: SSL handshake fails for OCSP + TLS false start + SSL hardware acceleration
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake will fail if Client initiate the handshake with TLS false start(Client SSL send the SSL record data to server before Server send out the CCS + FINISHED).
bugs.conditions: 1. Client initiates the SSL handshake with False Start. 2. BIG-IP has SSL hardware acceleration enabled（which is default for for non-VE version).
bugs.impact: BIG-IP will send the RST to tear down the connection in TLS false start.
bugs.workaround: 1. Disable TLS False Start - that needs to be done on all clients so might not be feasible; 2. Disable SSL acceleration. 3. Disable AES-GCM ciphers in clientssl profile. Without AES-GCM clients will not try to use TLS false start and still be able to use (EC)DHE.

bugs.title: TMSH/REST API does not honor access-info client ip or username filter
bugs.symptoms: TMSH/REST API does not filter Username or Client IP for access-info command. The user gives the input as Username or Client IP; still, the tmsh/rest API output does not filter correctly and produces the entire output.
bugs.conditions: The user gives Username or Client IP for tmsh "show apm access-info" command expecting the filtering will occur based on that given input.
bugs.impact: TMSH and REST API command produces more output.
bugs.workaround: Client Side script in REST API can ignore the empty session in the output and honor the values only when Client IP presents in case of Username as input. Similarly, the script can ignore the values when Username presents in case of Client IP as input.
bugs.fix: Filtering should be based on the given input either Username or Client IP based in TMSH and the corresponding REST output.

bugs.title: ASM Signature Update cannot be performed on hourly billing cloud instance
bugs.symptoms: ASM Signature Update cannot be performed on hourly billing cloud (AWS) instance. Licenses on these devices cannot be updated and have a fixed Service Check Date (SCD), which must be more recent to allow ASM Signature Update.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to perform ASM Signature Update on hourly billing cloud (AWS) instance.
bugs.impact: Performing ASM Signature Update fails.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: ASM Signature Update can now be performed on hourly billing cloud instance.

bugs.title: IKEv1 logging shows spi of deleted SA with opposite endianess
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes the IKEv1 racoon daemon logs a 32-bit child-SA spi with octets in backwards order (reversing the endianness).
bugs.conditions: When an SA is deleted.
bugs.impact: Logging typically shows a network byte order spi in the wrong order. Cosmetic interference with logging interpretation.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The spi values are shown in the correct endianness now.

bugs.title: Manually changing a device to standby will cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: When you change the set the HA state of a device to Standby when it's already in standby, tmm may crash.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when both devices are in Standby, and you run tmsh run /sys failover standby
bugs.impact: tmm crashes and restarts. Since the device was already in standby, traffic is not disrupted.

bugs.title: Enabling MCP Audit logging does not produce log entry for audit logging change
bugs.symptoms: When you enable MCP audit logging, the action of changing the audit logging entry is not logged. All actions after the configuration change are logged.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when enabling MCP audit logging.
bugs.impact: The audit logging change itself is not logged in the audit logs.

bugs.title: list self-ip with queries does not work
bugs.symptoms: "list net self" command always returns all Self IPs, regardless of the regex patterns.
bugs.conditions: list net self always returns all Self IPs
bugs.impact: You are unable to filter the Self IP list using a regex pattern.
bugs.fix: You can now use pattern matching to list Self IPs

bugs.title: When the system config has many iRules and they are installed on many virtual servers, the config loading time is significantly long
bugs.symptoms: Config load could be very long and CPU usage very high.
bugs.conditions: There are many iRule and they are installed on many virtual servers.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system performance could be degraded during the load and may cause system lock up.
bugs.workaround: Run "tmsh modify sys db rule.validation value syntax", this causes iRule validation to check iRule syntax only; the semantic checks will not be performed.
bugs.fix: In this release, the config loading time is cut significantly.

bugs.title: Failed attempt to resize 'appdata' leaves volume unmounted.
bugs.symptoms: If attempts at resizing the /appdata partition fail (due to insufficient free space), /appdata is left unmounted on boot.
bugs.conditions: Physical volume is too full to accommodate /appdata resizing. The typical case is when there are already many other software volumes before the resize task has been able to run.
bugs.impact: /appdata is not mounted after the system comes up.
bugs.workaround: Manually remount the appdata partition.
bugs.fix: Failed attempt to resize 'appdata' no longer leaves volume unmounted.

bugs.title: tmm might restart if the HTTP passthrough on pipeline option is used
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may crash if the HTTP profile's 'passthrough_pipeline' field is set to 'passthrough'.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile is configured as a transparent proxy. -- HTTP profile has the 'passthrough_pipeline' field is set to 'passthrough'.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes when HTTP switches to passthrough mode in some cases.

bugs.title: Virtual address (/Common/10.10.10.10) shares address with floating self IP (/Common/10.10.10.10), so traffic-group is being kept at (/Common/traffic-group-local-only)
bugs.symptoms: Warning similar to below, referencing a non-floating self IP: Virtual address (/Common/10.10.10.10) shares address with floating self IP (/Common/10.10.10.10), so traffic-group is being kept at (/Common/traffic-group-local-only)
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server is defined using the same IP address as a non-floating self IP.
bugs.impact: Virtual Server does not fail over with floating traffic group as expected.

bugs.title: Applying firewall policy to self-ip can cause tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Applying a firewall policy to a self-ip can cause a tmm crash. This is due to an uninitialized local variable that cause memory corruption on a stat memory location.
bugs.conditions: No specific condition for this to happen. This can happen in any config. However, it should be a vary rare occurrence.
bugs.impact: Temporary traffic disruption while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround. Tmm should recover automatically and function normally.

bugs.title: RouteDomainSelectionAgent might fail under heavy control plane traffic/activities
bugs.symptoms: If per-session access policy requests route domain selection during policy evaluation, the agent might hang and fail to retrieve route domain information. APMD might restart and produce a core file.
bugs.conditions: -- Policy sync operation. -- System receives a query for route domain information. -- There is a heavy load of control plane traffic to process.
bugs.impact: Poor performance and/or APMD restarts with a core file, causing brief disruption of the authentication service.
bugs.fix: Route domain selection operations no longer fail under heavy control-plane traffic/activities.

bugs.title: IPv6 cache route metrics are locked
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances IPv6 route metrics are locked for the lifetime of a route metrics cache entry.
bugs.conditions: Under certain circumstances IPv6 route metrics cache entries are created locked.
bugs.impact: IPV6 route metrics are locked for the lifetime of a route metrics cache entry. When receiving subsequent icmpv6 packet to big messages with a larger MTU, the value does not get updated.
bugs.fix: IPv6 route metrics are not locked anymore.

bugs.title: SELinux issue related to URLDB functionality
bugs.symptoms: When moving from a partition running v13.0.0 or later software to a partition containing pre-v13.0.0 software, the files under /var/urldb will have incorrect SELinux labeling. The BIG-IP system reports SELinux errors in /var/log/auditd/audit.log similar to the following: -- emerg logger: Re-starting bigd type=AVC msg=audit(1523996911.786:104): avc: denied { associate } for pid=32553 comm="python" name="incoming" scontext=system_u:object_r:unlabeled_t:s0 tcontext=system_u:object_r:fs_t:s0 tclass=filesystem
bugs.conditions: -- System is running pre-v13.0.0 software. -- Has URLDB functionality. -- Upgrade performed to v13.0.0 or later. -- Switch back to the partition that contains the pre-v13.0.0 software.
bugs.impact: The URLDB functionality does not work.
bugs.workaround: Change the SELinux label on /var/urldb (and all files under this directory) using the following command. chcon -R -t file_t /var/urldb

bugs.title: ix600 platforms will now have DoS Enforcement in Software Mode enabled automatically
bugs.symptoms: The sys db variable dos.forceswdos controls DoS enforcement in software mode. ix600 platforms with TurboFlex licenses restrict DoS enforcement to software mode. The default for dos.forceswdos is 'disable', so DoS enforcement does not work on those platforms until this setting is changed to 'enabled'.
bugs.conditions: -- ix600 platforms, as detailed in the following list: + BIG-IP i2600 + BIG-IP i4600 + BIG-IP i5600 + BIG-IP i7600 + BIG-IP i10600 + BIG-IP i12600 + BIG-IP i15600 + BIG-IP i11600 -- TurboFlex license. -- Using software versions 13.1.x-14.0.0.
bugs.impact: The dos.forceswdos db variable is set to false by default in the configuration, meaning that DoS works in Hardware mode on capable hardware platforms. However, due to licensing restrictions for ix600 platforms, DoS enforcement can run only in software mode. For ix600, if the dos.forceswdos setting is not changed to true, DoS enforcement does not work at all.
bugs.workaround: Manually set the sys db variable dos.forceswdos to true to enable DoS enforcement in software mode. Note: In its default value 'false', DoS enforcement is in hardware mode, which is not supported by ix600. If you upgrade the license from ix600 to ix800, this db variable is still set to 'true', meaning DoS is operating in software mode. To run DoS in hardware mode on ix800 platforms, set the db variable to false.
bugs.fix: This change supports licensing behavior on ix600 platforms with Turboflex licenses, and enables DoS enforcement in supported software mode automatically (sets db variable to true). To have DoS enforcement in hardware mode requires ix800 or higher licenses, whenever available, and requires that the sys db variable dos.forceswdos be set to false.

bugs.title: Update Check for EPSEC shows OPSWAT description without EPSEC version on GUI
bugs.symptoms: On the BIG-IP GUI, under System :: Software Management :: Update Check, after pressing 'Check now', the 'Available Update' shows a long string 'OPSWAT Endpoint Security Integration Update. See readme_minimum_version.txt before install' instead of the EPSEC version, e.g.: epsec-1.0.0-679.0.
bugs.conditions: -- Under System :: Software Management :: Update Check. -- Press 'Check now'.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine what version is available by viewing 'Available Update'. Although this is how all the other updates work, it can result in a confusing BIG-IP user experience.
bugs.workaround: To have the browser show the link's destination address, view the browser's status fields while hovering the cursor over the following link text: OPSWAT Endpoint Security Integration Update. See readme_minimum_version.txt before install.
bugs.fix: The output now shows the version, e.g.: epsec-1.0.0-679.0.

bugs.title: GUI SSL Certificate does not display correct expiration dates
bugs.symptoms: GUI SSL Certificate bundle (Including ca-bundle), the expiration date displayed on the certificates list page shows the date of the first certificate in the bundle, and the highest expiration date in the bundle.
bugs.conditions: Have a SSL certificate bundle containing certificates with different expiration dates.
bugs.impact: This is a GUI display issue; there is no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: GUI SSL Certificate bundle expiration dates on the certificates list page shows the expiration date of the first certificate within the bundle to expire and the highest expiration date in the bundle.

bugs.title: VLAN failsafe failover may not occur
bugs.symptoms: VLAN failsafe may not take effect and cause failover.
bugs.conditions: If the VLAN failsafe is disabled, and then re-enabled, it might not properly take effect.
bugs.impact: System will not fail over when it should.
bugs.workaround: The failure condition is cleared by the next reboot following the disable/enable.
bugs.fix: Failover occurs as expected.

bugs.title: Loading sys config using merge does not work for client SSL profiles with passphrase-protected key
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP system posts an error similar to the following when merging configuration of a client SSL profile: 010717e7:3: Client SSL profile (/Common/test): cert-key-chain and profile cert, key or chain options cannot be specified together.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the SSL key of the client SSL profile is passphrase-protected.
bugs.impact: Unable to merge configuration.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, remove the cert/key/chain/passprase outside of the cert-key-chain block before issuing the following command: load sys config from-terminal merge. In particular, use the following text as the configuration: root@(big4)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# load sys config from-terminal merge Enter configuration. Press CTRL-D to submit or CTRL-C to cancel. ltm profile client-ssl test { app-service none cert-key-chain { test12345 { cert test12345 key test12345 passphrase $M$SIwDQYJKoZIhvcNAQEBBQABOC== } } inherit-certkeychain false } In this example, this is the text to replace:: root@(big4)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# load sys config from-terminal merge Enter configuration. Press CTRL-D to submit or CTRL-C to cancel. ltm profile client-ssl test { app-service none cert test12345 cert-key-chain { test12345 { cert test12345 key test12345 passphrase $M$EAAaOBsTCBrjAzBggrBgEFBQc== } } chain none inherit-certkeychain false key test12345 passphrase $M$S/4S5uRf8leryRGv5MX9DAAvK== } Loading configuration... 010717e7:3: Client SSL profile (/Common/test): cert-key-chain and profile cert, key or chain options cannot be specified together. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.

bugs.title: Node monitor instances not showing up in GUI
bugs.symptoms: Navigating to Local Traffic :: Monitors :: <some_monitor> should show a list of nodes with some_monitor assigned to them. GUI does not list related nodes under Instances tab.
bugs.conditions: -- At Local Traffic :: Monitors :: <some_monitor>. -- Under the Instances tab.
bugs.impact: No instances listed. Cannot use the GUI to determine which nodes are associated with a monitor.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to list nodes associated with a monitor.
bugs.fix: The GUI now lists all associated nodes under Local Traffic :: Monitors :: <some_monitor> :: Instances tab.

bugs.title: BIG-IP images are available in Alibaba Cloud
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) images are now available in the Alibaba International Cloud Marketplace.
bugs.conditions: Create virtual server instance within Alibaba International Cloud environment and select BIG-IP from the list of available images.
bugs.impact: New offerings for BYOL and PAYG for BIG-IP VE are now available in the Alibaba International Cloud Marketplace.
bugs.workaround: BIG-IP VE images are now available in Alibaba Cloud.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP VE images are now available in Alibaba Cloud.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP VE now supports the Alibaba International Cloud Marketplace.

bugs.title: Pass in IP to urldb categorization engine
bugs.symptoms: Category lookup results might be less accurate. In some cases, the system returns 'uncategorized' when the reference (Forcepoint) returns a specific category.
bugs.conditions: Category Lookup agent is in per-request policy using the categorization engine to lookup up a website's classification.
bugs.impact: Actions leveraging categorization results will be applied incorrectly.
bugs.fix: This release can now pass in more information to the urldb categorization engine, which supports finger-grained categorization.

bugs.title: Commands are replicated to PostgreSQL even when not in use.
bugs.symptoms: In MCP, PostgreSQL is used only by AFM. Even when AFM is not provisioned, however, commands are being replicated to PostgreSQL.
bugs.conditions: AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary CPU cycles spent by MCP replicating commands to PostgreSQL.
bugs.fix: Prevented replication of commands to PostgreSQL when it is not in use.

bugs.title: Using iRule 'DNS::question name' to shorten the name in DNS_REQUEST may result malformed TC response
bugs.symptoms: Received malformed Truncated DNS response.
bugs.conditions: -- Using iRule 'DNS::question name' to shorten the name. -- DNS response is longer than 4096 UDP limit.
bugs.impact: DNS request might not be resolved correctly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: In this release, when DNS::query name changes the query name, the software ensures that the request is updated with proper lengths.

bugs.title: stpd repeatedly logs "hal sendMessage failed"
bugs.symptoms: On non-primary clustered blades in a BIG-IP chassis environment, stpd may repeatedly log "hal sendMessage failed"
bugs.conditions: Two or more blades clustered in a chassis with STP enabled on one or more ports.
bugs.impact: All BIG-IP blades
bugs.workaround: No workaround except to ignore log messages - they are spurious and have no ill effect on the system besides log spam.

bugs.title: tmm core files produced by nitrox_diag may be missing data
bugs.symptoms: When the nitrox_diag utility generates a tmm core file, that file might include data for only one tmm thread instead of all tmm threads.
bugs.conditions: -- Running the nitrox_diag utility. -- Using devices with the Cavium Nitrox crypto card. -- The nitrox_diag utility generates a tmm core file.
bugs.impact: The resulting core file might include data for only one tmm thread instead of all tmm threads, making it more difficult for F5 to diagnose reported problems with the Cavium Nitrox crypto card. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When the nitrox_diag utility generates a tmm core file, that file now includes data for all tmm threads instead of only one.

bugs.title: NPAPI inspection host plugin does not work with latest epsec image on macOS
bugs.symptoms: NPAPI inspection host plugin on macOS does not work with the latest Endpoint Security (EPSEC) image because the policy server is bundled with individual applications and is not a part of OESIS package. There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.conditions: -- NPAPI plugin. -- One of the recent EPSIC image 684.0, AV/FW endpoint inspection. -- Safari web browser
bugs.impact: NPAPI plugin does not work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: REST filter on nested entities has no effect
bugs.symptoms: REST filter on nested entities has no effect, and all results are returned.
bugs.conditions: A REST GET request is issued using a filter on a nested entity, such as filtering URLs on CORS originName.
bugs.impact: The filter is ignored and all results are returned.
bugs.fix: REST filter on nested entities is applied correctly and only returns the matching entities.

bugs.title: UCS restore may fail with: Decryption of the field (privatekey) for object (9717) failed
bugs.symptoms: -- UCS archive restore fails -- The Traffic Management Shell (TMSH) and/or /var/log/ltm file show following error message: 01071769:3: Decryption of the field (privatekey) for object (9717) failed. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: - Restoring configuration from UCS. - The UCS is being restored on a different BIG-IP system with a different master key.
bugs.impact: -- The UCS configuration is not applied. -- The BIG-IP is not in a fully operational state.
bugs.workaround: If you encounter this error and dynad is not in use (dynamic debug) you can manually edit bigip_base.conf. 1. Locate the dynad config in /config/bigip_base.conf file: For example, the dynad config will look like: sys dynad key { key $M$jV$VX7HMp5q346nsTYDYFPnYdJLrBPyQSCrDTJYAz4je7KXJAC38fxtDJL35KtF66bq } 2. Modify the dynad configuration lines to: sys dynad key { key "test" } 3, Save the updated bigip_base.conf file 4. Load the configuration with command: tmsh load sys config
bugs.fix: The log message is improved to provide the BIG-IP administrator with more specific detail that the dynad key failed to be decrypted.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing TCP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMM may crash while processing TCP data
bugs.conditions: TCP profile enabled TCP Segment Offload enabled
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes TCP traffic as expected

bugs.title: Changing console Baud-rate to a supported value requires reboot
bugs.symptoms: Unable to modify console Baud-rate.
bugs.conditions: Running BIG-IP release 11.6.0 or later.
bugs.impact: System instability.
bugs.workaround: Reboot system after modification of console Baud-rate.

bugs.title: Mcpd is blocked when executing the tmsh command 'tmsh -a show net arp all'
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd/tmm stops responding to the query sent from tmsh for 'tmsh -a show net arp all'.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when executing the command 'tmsh -a show net arp all'.
bugs.impact: Mcpd becomes blocked and you are unable to run other commands, such as qkview.

bugs.title: Folder in a partition may result in load sys config error
bugs.symptoms: If you run the command 'tmsh load sys config current-partition' in a partition that includes a folder, the command may return an error.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: -- Create a partition. -- Create a folder in that partition. -- In the newly-created partition. -- Save the configuration with the command 'save sys conf'. -- In the same partition, run the following command to load the configuration: 'tmsh load sys config current-partition'.
bugs.impact: The load configuration process fails with an error that the folder does not exist.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: NSH tunnel reject inner packet from other vendor
bugs.symptoms: NSH does not interoperate between BIG-IP systems and some external NSH vendors.
bugs.conditions: -- NSH tunnel. -- The external NSH vendor cannot configure inner packet MAC destination.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system rejects the packet. Lost connectivity with some of the vendors.
bugs.workaround: To work around this limitation, you can do either of the following: -- Use an external vendor that does support configuration of inner packet MAC destination. -- Avoid use NSH for external vendors without such ability.
bugs.fix: The system can now passes NSH packets as expected in this scenario.

bugs.title: Transparent forwarding mode across multiple VLAN groups or virtual-wire
bugs.symptoms: This is a virtual-wire or vlan-group deployment scenario in which there is a BIG-IP system connecting two networks with more than one link. This scenario is referred as 'asymmetric deployment'. In this case. the outgoing packet does not have the correct VLAN configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual-wire or vlan-group configured. -- BIG-IP system is connecting two networks with more than one link. -- There is more than one virtual-wire/vlan-group to handle the traffic across multiple links. -- Packets belonging to a flow arrive on any link with a valid VLAN.
bugs.impact: The connectivity between the endpoints fails.
bugs.fix: Transparent forwarding mode now works across multiple VLAN groups or virtual-wire.
bugs.behavior: Transparent forwarding mode now works across multiple VLAN groups or virtual-wire.

bugs.title: X520 virtual functions do not support MAC masquerading
bugs.symptoms: MAC masquerading is not supported when using X520 virtual functions via SR-IOV in Virtual Edition (VE). This is due to a lack of functionality in the underlying hardware.
bugs.conditions: -- Use SR-IOV virtual functions as interfaces within VE. -- Configure MAC masquerading with a shared MAC that should follow the active system after traffic group failovers.
bugs.impact: MAC masquerading will not function in this environment.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not to use MAC masquerading, as conventional failover works for this environment.
bugs.fix: MAC masquerading is now supported when using X520 virtual functions via SR-IOV in Virtual Edition (VE).

bugs.title: admd stops responding and generates a core while under stress.
bugs.symptoms: admd stops responding and generates a core while under stress.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is under stress. -- CPU starvation is occurring.
bugs.impact: admd core and restart. Note: The admd process provides stress-based DoS detection and mitigation control. When admd is not running, there is no stress-based anomaly detection or behavioral statistics aggregation.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: BADOS mitigation may fail
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions BADOS mitigation may fail
bugs.conditions: BADOS enabled
bugs.impact: BADOS does not function as intended =
bugs.fix: BADOS now functions as intended

bugs.title: CSP headers block additional JavaScript in Chrome 65
bugs.symptoms: The FPS option 'Additional JavaScript' does not run in recent versions of Google Chrome when CSP blocks inline scripts.
bugs.conditions: -- Site using the FPS 'Additional JavaScript' feature. -- CSP is enabled.
bugs.impact: Configured JavaScript does not run in the browser.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than installing the most recent FPS engine file.
bugs.fix: CSP headers no longer block 'Additional JavaScript' in Google Chrome when CSP blocks inline scripts.

bugs.title: ADM may fail when processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, ADM may fail when processing HTTP traffic
bugs.conditions: ASM enabled
bugs.impact: ADM does not function as intended
bugs.fix: ADM processes HTTP traffic as expected

bugs.title: Non-standard HTTP header Keep-Alive causes RST_STREAM in Safari
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system has a web-acceleration which provides a number of caching and optimization options suitable for HTTP/1.1. It uses 'Connection: Keep-Alive' header on a server side, which results in appearance of 'Keep-Alive' header in a response. Such a HTTP header was adopted by the industry but not standardized. When a web-acceleration profile is configured and provides a response, Safari clients do not accept responses with a such header and reject those with a RST_STREAM message.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP has a virtual server with HTTP/2 profile and a web-acceleration profile. -- A pool member responds with 'Keep-Alive' header in the following format: Keep-Alive: timeout=<number>, max=<number>.
bugs.impact: A response to a request is rejected, which might cause incorrect rendering of HTTP page.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to remove the Keep-Alive header: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { HTTP::header remove keep-alive } Alternatively use an LTM Policy where this header is removed from a server's response.

bugs.title: DHCP traffic may not be forwarded when BWC is configured
bugs.symptoms: DHCP traffic may not be forwarded when BWC is configured on the system.
bugs.conditions: -- DHCP virtual server configured. -- BWC policy configured and attached to the route-domain.
bugs.impact: DHCP traffic may not be forwarded.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to remove the BWC policy.
bugs.fix: DHCP traffic is now forwarded when BWC is configured

bugs.title: When creating a new iRulesLX rule, TMSH appends ".tcl" to rule filenames that already end in ".tcl"
bugs.symptoms: When using TMSH to create a new iRulesLX rule with the extension '.tcl' as part of the rule name, TMSH will append another '.tcl' at the end of the file. This is problematic when attempting to view the iRule in the GUI (in the iRulesLX workspace at Local Traffic :: iRules : LX Workspaces :: <workspace name>).
bugs.conditions: Creating a new iRulesLX iRule in TMSH.
bugs.impact: Cannot view or delete the iRule from the iRulesLX GUI.
bugs.workaround: Do not name rules with the '.tcl' extension.

bugs.title: bigd restarts after loading a UCS for the first time
bugs.symptoms: bigd restarts when loading a UCS for the first time, where the load succeeds; and no related messages are reported in /var/log/ltm; and no bigd core file is produced.
bugs.conditions: bigd loads a UCS file for the first time, such as after the command: tmsh load sys ucs no-license keep-current-management-ip no-platform-check
bugs.impact: The UCS file is correctly reloaded, and bigd restarts with the loaded configuration. No bigd core is produced, and no related messages are found in /var/log/ltm. After restart, bigd performs all system functions as expected.
bugs.workaround: System runs as expected after the bigd restart, and the user need not take any action.

bugs.title: When creating a new iRulesLX rule, the GUI appends .tcl to rule filenames that already end in .tcl
bugs.symptoms: When using the GUI to create a new iRulesLX rule with the extension .tcl as part of the rule name, the GUI will append another .tcl at the end of the file. This is problematic when attempting to view the iRule in the iRulesLX workspace (at Local Traffic :: iRules : LX Workspaces :: <workspace name>).
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a new iRulesLX iRule in the GUI. -- Adding the extension .tcl.
bugs.impact: Cannot view or delete the iRule from the iRulesLX GUI.
bugs.workaround: Do not name rules with the .tcl extension. The system will do that for you.

bugs.title: [tmsh] list gtm pool show does not list pool member depends-on if there is virtual server dependency in GTM server
bugs.symptoms: GTM pool member dependency cannot be listed correctly using the following command: # tmsh list gtm pool
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server dependency in GTM server. -- Running the command: tmsh list gtm pool.
bugs.impact: 1. Pool member dependencies are not listed. 2. Pool member dependency information is missing when saving config: # tmsh save sys config gtm-only
bugs.workaround: List specific gtm pools instead by running a command similar to the following: # tmsh list gtm pool a p1

bugs.title: 'Always Connected Mode' text is missing in EdgeClient tray
bugs.symptoms: When right-clicking the EdgeClient tray icon, the pop-up menu shows a grey box instead of the 'Always Connected Mode' text.
bugs.conditions: EdgeClient installed in 'Always Connected Mode' with 'Allow' traffic when VPN is disconnected.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Previously, the message appeared only for blocked mode.
bugs.fix: Now, when a user right-clicks the Edge Client tray icon in Always Connected mode, the <uicontrol>Always Connected Mode</uicontrol> text is displayed on the tray icon pop-up menu.

bugs.title: Removal of HTTP hash persistence cookie when a pool member goes down.
bugs.symptoms: When HTTP cookie hash persistence is configured the cookie is removed when a pool member goes down. This is incorrect if pool members are using session replication.
bugs.conditions: - Cookie hash persistence is configured. - A pool member that the persistence record points to goes down. - Pool members are using session replication.
bugs.impact: Connected clients must establish a new session.
bugs.workaround: To configure HTTP cookie hash persistence, use an iRule similar to the following: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { persist cookie hash JSESSIONID }
bugs.fix: HTTP hash persistence cookie is no longer removed when a pool member goes down. If you need to remove the cookie, use an iRule similar to the following: when PERSIST_DOWN { HTTP::cookie remove JSESSIONID }

bugs.title: Removing a Copper SFP on certain platforms incorrectly retains info about the SFP
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP displays a stale SFP serial number after removing a copper SFP. A fiber SFP inserted into an interface after removing a copper SFP will not come up.
bugs.conditions: 800, 1600, and 3600 platforms with copper SFPs.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic display of stale serial number of copper SFP. Fiber SFP will not work when inserted after a copper SFP is removed.
bugs.workaround: Restart bcm56xxd.

bugs.title: When licensing through a proxy, setting the db variables for proxy.host, proxy.port, etc., has no effect.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is behind a proxy server, the licensing process does not work, despite having set the db variables for proxy.host, proxy.port, proxy.protocol, etc.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is behind a proxy server that gates internet access. -- Attempting to license (or revoke the license of) the BIG-IP system is not possible using GUI or tmsh since communications with the license server will fail.
bugs.impact: Cannot license, reactivate license, or revoke the license of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Instead of using GUI or tmsh, run the following command, substituting your proxy specification for <proxy> and your license registration key for <reg-key>: /usr/local/bin/SOAPLicenseClient --proxy <proxy> --basekey <reg-key> --certupdatecheck
bugs.fix: Licensing/revoke licensing works as expected by simply setting the tmsh sys db variables proxy.host, proxy.port, etc.

bugs.title: Ephemeral pool-member state on the standby is down
bugs.symptoms: On a standby BIG-IP system, an ephemeral pool-members state remains user-down after re-enabling an FQDN node on the primary system.
bugs.conditions: Re-enabling a forced-down FQDN node on the primary system.
bugs.impact: On the standby system, the ephemeral pool-members are in state: user-down, (forced-down in GUI).

bugs.title: Creating static route for advertised dynamic route might result in dropping the tmrouted connection to TMM
bugs.symptoms: While creating a static route, tmrouted disconnects with error: existing entry is not a dynamic.
bugs.conditions: Creating a static route for a network that already has an advertised dynamic route.
bugs.impact: TMM's connection to tmrouted goes down, which results in loss of the dynamic route for TMM.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not creating a static route for routes received through dynamic routing.
bugs.fix: Creating static routes for advertised dynamic route no longer causes the tmrouted-to-TMM connection to drop.

bugs.title: SSO for native RDP resources is not compatible with the 'Force Updated Clients' setting of 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' Group Policy
bugs.symptoms: To address a vulnerability in their CredSSP implementation Microsoft released set of updates for all versions of Windows (https://aka.ms/credssp). Although the APM implementation is not affected by this vulnerability, the Microsoft Windows Server fix introduces compatibility issues. The update adds new Group Policy 'Encryption Oracle Remediation', which, if set to 'Force Updated Clients' on the server might break SSO for APM's native RDP resources.
bugs.conditions: -- RDP server has https://aka.ms/credssp update installed. -- 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' Group Policy on the RDP server is set to 'Force Updated Clients'.
bugs.impact: SSO for native RDP resources does not work.
bugs.workaround: Set 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' Group Policy on the RDP server to 'Mitigated'.
bugs.fix: SSO for native RDP resources is now compatible with the 'Force Updated Clients' setting of 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' Group Policy.

bugs.title: ICMP unreachable messages sent only from active to standby
bugs.symptoms: When the self IP has a firewall rule to reject ICMP unreachable, the system will be sent from active to standby and not from standby to active. This is correct behavior, but v13.x might show ICMP unreachable messages sent from standby to active along with those from active to standby.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM firewall rule is applied to the self IP as reject ICMP unreachable messages. -- Active/standby high availability (HA) cluster.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. ICMP unreachable messages not showing has no effect on BIG-IP system functionality. Note: If there is a firewall to block traffic on self IPs, but still want ICMP unreachable messages, that configuration is not valid, and HA will not work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Excessive 'The Service Check Date check was skipped' log messages.
bugs.symptoms: Large numbers of these warnings are logged into the "ltm" file: warning httpd[12345]: 0118000a:4: The Service Check Date check was skipped. The message appears whenever a new "httpd" instance is launched.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP instance has been installed with a "no service check" license. These licenses are sometimes provided with cloud pre-licensed VE software images.
bugs.impact: Log files are saturated with many useless warnings. This can hide actual problems and impede their diagnosis.
bugs.workaround: During manual troubleshooting, commands such as the following may be used to filter the excess warnings: # grep -v 'Service Check Date check was skipped' ltm | less The syslog-ng 'include' filter mechanism is another possibility, but this should be attempted only with assistance of the F5 Support team.

bugs.title: Apmd logs password for acp messages when in debug mode
bugs.symptoms: Apmd logs password when executing policy via iRule.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is licensed and provisioned -- Executing policy via iRule using iRule command 'ACCESS::policy evaluate'. -- Clear text password is supplied for authentication -- Debug mode active
bugs.impact: Apmd logs clear text password
bugs.workaround: Use '-secure' option when providing/setting password session variable in iRule, for example: -- ACCESS::session data get [-sid <sid>] [-secure] <key> -ssid <session_id> -- ACCESS::session data set [-sid <sid>] [-secure] <key> [<value>]
bugs.fix: Apmd now no longer logs password in debug mode when evaluating policy via iRule.

bugs.title: ospfd cores when configured with 'area 0 range 0.0.0.0/0'
bugs.symptoms: ospfd core. Loss of dynamic routing functionality.
bugs.conditions: - Enable dynamic routing with OSPFv2. - Configure OSPF with the following value: area 0 range 0.0.0.0/0.
bugs.impact: Loss of dynamic routing functionality.
bugs.fix: ospfd no longer cores when configured with "area 0 range 0.0.0.0/0"

bugs.title: Message delivered to the wrong peer if bidirectional persistence is used.
bugs.symptoms: A message may be delivered to the wrong peer if bidirectional persistence is used. The existing algorithm for selecting the direction to forward a message that matches a bidirectional persistence entry may send the message to the wrong peer.
bugs.conditions: -- Bidirectional persistence is configured. -- A pool of server devices is sharing the same state. -- One server is down. -- The other server uses the same session to send the message to another peer.
bugs.impact: LTM may send the message to the wrong peer.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to route/deliver the message, or don't share the state between servers.

bugs.title: OPT-0031 and OPT-0036 log DDM warning every minute when interface disabled and DDM enabled
bugs.symptoms: DDM transmit power too low warning continually appear in /var/log/ltm, and in SNMP traps. Messages appear similar to the following: DDM interface:3/1.0 transmit power too low warning. Transmit power(mWatts) 0.0001 0.0001 0.0001 0.0001 A single warning message is expected, not repeating messages.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The interface is disabled. -- DDM is enabled. -- OPT-0031 or OPT-0036.
bugs.impact: There are multiple messages in /var/log/ltm, and SNMP DDM traps. There is no impact on traffic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to enable the interface or disable DDM.
bugs.fix: DDM errors no longer continually appear on disabled interfaces containing OPT-0031 or OPT-0036.

bugs.title: APM CRLDP Auth passes all certs
bugs.symptoms: In some situations, a failure to download a new CRL may result in the CRLDP Auth agent treating revoked certs as valid.
bugs.conditions: Non-zero value for the update-interval in the CRLDP AAA object, and a download failure occurs while trying to update the CRL.
bugs.impact: Revoked users may regain access.
bugs.fix: Failure to download a CRL will now revert to the cached CRL, if that CRL is still valid under its nextUpdate time. If there is no valid cached CRL, APM reverts to the action specified in the AAA CRLDP setting of 'Null CRL Allowed'.

bugs.title: Restjavad may hang if discover task fails and the interval is 0
bugs.symptoms: If a discover task fails because of a network issue, the system tries to run the task again at the next scheduled time. If the discover interval is set to 0, the system retries immediately, which may cause restjavad hang.
bugs.conditions: If a provider has configured discover interval 0 and the discover task failed because of network issues.
bugs.impact: The discover task tries to use a lot CPU when restjavad continuously retries the task.
bugs.workaround: Change the discover interval to 1 hour or more.
bugs.fix: Now, if the discover interval is 0 and the discover task fails because of a network issue, the system sends the task to the finished state and does not retry anymore.

bugs.title: Errors in chmand
bugs.symptoms: VIPRION cluster does not form; only primary blade stays online. Chassis manager chmand generated a core file. System logs the following error in ltm log: err clusterd[11162]: 013a0004:3: Error adding cluster mgmt addr, HAL error 7.
bugs.conditions: -- Restoring UCS. -- Chassis starting up. -- System in stressed condition, where there is very little or no memory available.
bugs.impact: Cluster does not form.
bugs.fix: These errors in chmand are fixed.

bugs.title: antserver creates large temporary file in /tmp directory
bugs.symptoms: SWG Analytics (running through the antserver daemon) creates a large temporary file in the /tmp directory due to a lack of write permissions on the appropriate directory.
bugs.conditions: -- SWG provisioned. -- Viewing SWG Analytics.
bugs.impact: /tmp is temporarily populated with a large file that might fill up the directory if it is already close to capacity.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: System now writes to /shared/tmp/ant_server so that it no longer writes to /tmp, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Platform-migrate of UCS containing QinQ fails on VE
bugs.symptoms: If you are doing platform-migrate from a hardware device to a Virtual Edition (VE) guest, and the UCS that came from the hardware device has a QinQ VLAN configuration, then the upgrade will fail.
bugs.conditions: -- VLAN with a QinQ configuration exists on the hardware configuration. -- UCS file is saved on the hardware device. -- UCS is copied to a VE guest. -- Attempt to load the configuration using the following command: load sys ucs <UCS filename> no-license platform-migrate.
bugs.impact: The UCS load will fail and generate an error: 01071bd8:3: The tag-mode for requested member <VLAN name> has to be 'none' on platforms that do not support QinQ. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.fix: The configuration now loads successfully, disables QinQ on the associated VLAN, and warns that this action was automatically taken.

bugs.title: Serial Console Baud Rate Loses Modified Values with New Logins on iSeries Platforms Without Reboot
bugs.symptoms: On an iSeries platform, when the console baud rate is changed through TMSH, new terminal sessions revert back to the previous baud rate instead of adopting the new setting unless the unit is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: 1. Modify the console baud rate in BIG-IP through TMSH on an iSeries platform (i2xxx, i4xxx, i5xxx, i7xxx, i10xxx, i15xxx), for example: tmsh modify sys console baud-rate 9600. 2. Exit from the login prompt in the current terminal session, or kill it and start a new session.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system reverts to the previous baud rate instead of the new setting. Inability to create any new serial console connections with the modified baud-rate without a reboot.
bugs.workaround: The problem can be mitigated by manually reprogramming the TTY device and restarting the agetty process and bash login sessions. This closes any existing console connections, but newly established connections will connect at the modified baud rate. 1. Use TMSH to modify the baud rate to the desired speed by running a command similar to the following: tmsh modify sys console baud-rate 9600 2. Re-program the TTY device with the desired speed by running a command similar to the following: stty -F /dev/ttyS0 9600 3. Kill the existing agetty process so it will re-start at the new baud rate by running the following command: /usr/bin/killall -q agetty 4. Restart bash logins by running the following command: /bin/kill -HUP `/bin/ps -A | /bin/grep ttyS0 | /bin/grep -v grep | /bin/grep bash | /bin/awk '{print $1}'` >/dev/null 2>&1
bugs.fix: In addition to reprogramming the UART with the new baud rate, the BIG-IP system now re-initializes the TTY device and agetty process with the correct speed so that new terminal sessions reflect the change.

bugs.title: iRulesLX Hardening
bugs.symptoms: iRulesLX does not follow current best practices and should be updated to ensure layered protections.
bugs.conditions: -iRulesLX in use
bugs.impact: iRulesLX does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: iRulesLX now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: vCMP: tmm core in guest when stopping vCMP guest from host
bugs.symptoms: A tmm core in the guest on the primary blade, not the secondary blade, after the guest is disabled on the hypervisor.
bugs.conditions: -- A cross-blade vCMP guest. -- Guest is disabled on the hypervisor.
bugs.impact: Because the guest is in the process of being disabled, there is no impact on traffic, however, the core file may take up space on the guest on the primary blade.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate the disk problem, manually delete the core file.

bugs.title: Changing WebSocket payload protocol profile from mqtt back to none causes TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: When WebSocket profile's payload protocol profile configuration value is modified from 'mqtt' to 'None', TMM restarts once upon receiving traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- The WebSocket profile is attached to a virtual server. -- Protocol profile configuration value is modified from 'mqtt' to 'None'.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts when traffic is processed by the virtual server to which the WebSocket profile is attached.
bugs.workaround: After changing WebSocket profile's payload protocol profile configuration value from 'mqtt' to 'None', issue the following command in BIG-IP system shell, before processing any traffic. # bigstart restart tmm

bugs.title: PEM policy actions obtained via a PCRF are not applied for traffic generated subscribers
bugs.symptoms: Policy and Charging Rules Function (PCRF) policy actions will have no effect on the subscribers' traffic.

bugs.title: AVR should report 'resolutions' in module GtmWideip

bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: AVR now reports 'resolutions' in GtmWideip module.

bugs.title: Application Security roles are not showing all accessible objects in GUI
bugs.symptoms: Not all configuration objects are exposed to users of type Application Security Administrator and Application Security Editor that are technically accessible by the user role.
bugs.conditions: -- Users exist with roles of Application Security Administrator and Application Security Editor. -- Attempting to work with certain configuration objects.
bugs.impact: Users configured with these roles cannot view all object types using the GUI. Certain pages cannot be reached from the menu, as the software hides most of the configuration pages for these roles.
bugs.workaround: Users can use TMSH.

bugs.title: Simple mode Signature edit does not escape semicolon

bugs.conditions: -- Using a user-defined ASM Signature in Simple mode. -- There is a semicolon followed by a space in a keyword.
bugs.impact: The signature cannot be created.
bugs.workaround: The signature can be created in Advanced Mode by escaping semicolon as "|3B|".

bugs.title: AVR can generate many files in /var/avr/loader folder, which might cause disk-usage problem
bugs.symptoms: -- The folder /var/avr/loader contains many files (e.g., more than 1500 files). -- monpd is not running.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Avrd is running. -- monpd is down.
bugs.impact: AVR writes many files to /var/avr/loader. Depending on disk usage, this might cause disk-usage problems.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Restart monpd. When monpd starts up, it deletes the files under /var/avr/loader. -- Delete all files under /var/avr/loader.
bugs.fix: There is now a limit for the /var/avr/loader folder, so that it can contain no more than 1100 files. This prevents disk-usage problems.

bugs.title: IPS only works over UDP or TCP virtual server
bugs.symptoms: For Standard or FastL4 virtual, Protocol Inspection does notwork over SCTP/IPsec/Other protocols.
bugs.conditions: -- Standard virtual server with protocol configured as SCTP or IPsec. -- Performance L4 virtual servers with protocol configured as Other.
bugs.impact: Protocol Inspection does not work.
bugs.workaround: Configure TCP/UDP virtual servers.

bugs.title: VE with only hda drive does not report disk statistics
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) setup, there are no disk stats. The system logs error messages similar to the following: err chmand[7946]: 012a0003:3: Disk Latency Monitor: No disks found.
bugs.conditions: -- VE with only an hda drive. -- Navigate to inspector pages Monitoring :: Dashboards :: Device :: Health to view the statistics.
bugs.impact: Disk usage statistics are all zeroes. 'No Data' on Inspector pages charts: 'Disk Operations', 'Disk Throughput', and 'Disk Merges' The system reports that no disks are found.
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure the VE hypervisor so the virtual disk is named sda or vda instead of hda.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the hda disk when it is the only available disk, so the statistics are correctly reported.

bugs.title: coapi errors while modifying per-request policy in VPE
bugs.symptoms: System reports errors about coapi in /var/log/ltm when modifying a per-request policy in the Visual Policy Editor (VPE). err coapi: PHP: requested conversion of uninitialized member.
bugs.conditions: -- The per-request policy being modified is attached to the virtual server. -- Using VPE.
bugs.impact: The impact can vary by version. -- In some versions it represents a stray error log. -- In other versions the 'Accepted Languages' in the Logon Page agent does not have the full list. -- In other versions, there are server 500 errors when modifying agents.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, perform the following procedure: 1. Remove the per-request policy from the virtual server. 2. Modify the policy. 3. Add the policy back to the virtual server.
bugs.fix: Now per-request access policies can be simultaneously used and edited without causing spurious 'coapi' log errors.

bugs.title: TMM crash when RPC resumes TCL event ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED

bugs.conditions: Plugin RPC call has iRule event ACCESS_SESSION_CLOSED configured.
bugs.impact: System instability, failover, traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: iControl SOAP attribute ssl_profile not supported for in-tmm https monitor
bugs.symptoms: iControl SOAP cannot be used to modify the 'ssl_profile' attribute on an 'https' monitor when 'in-tmm' monitoring is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- 'https' monitor is configured. -- 'in-tmm' monitors are enabled. -- Use iControl SOAP to set/get the 'ssl_profile' attribute for an 'https' monitor.
bugs.impact: 'ssl_profile' attribute on an 'https' monitor cannot be modified through iControl SOAP.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use a different mechanism, such as through the GUI or tmsh, to modify the 'ssl_profile' attribute associated with an 'https' monitor. -- Disable 'in-tmm' monitors.

bugs.title: IKEv2 logs peers_id comparisons and cert verfication failures
bugs.symptoms: Insufficient information is logged when a certificate fails verification, or when ID_I in an IKE_AUTH request does not match configuration for peers_id in the ike-peer description.
bugs.conditions: When IKE_AUTH fails due to either certificate verification failure or mismatch of ID_I and peers_id.
bugs.impact: Hard to diagnose proximate cause of IKE negotiation failure during IKE_AUTH exchange.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When log level is at least debug, each ID_I and peers_id comparison is logged, so both config and IKE_AUTH payload content is clearly revealed. When certificate verification occurs, failure is now always logged with PROTO_ERR level, and success is also logged with INFO level when log level is at least debug.

bugs.title: IKEv2 accepts asn1dn for peers-id only as file path of certificate file
bugs.symptoms: IKEv2 only has a very inconvenient way to specify ID for an ike-peer when using peers-id-type asn1dn. The string value of peers-id-value was understood only as a file path, and not as a representation of the asn1dn value itself. The file had to be a certificate, whose subject happened to be the ID of the remote peer as a distinguished name (DN), so this could be extracted as binary DER for asn1dn. This was both awkward and error prone, requiring what amounts to a copy of a peer's certificate before it is sent during negotiation.
bugs.conditions: -- Using certificate based authentication in IPsec IKEv2. -- Configuring an ike-peer with peers-id-type as asn1dn.
bugs.impact: Very difficult to use asn1dn as the ID of a peer, impeding inter-operation with other vendors.
bugs.workaround: If you can install a local copy of the peer's certificate, with an asn1dn value inside matching what that peer will actually send in an IKE_AUTH exchange, IKEv2 can extract the asn1dn provided the value of peers-id-value is an absolute file system path to this local certificate copy.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP now understands three different ways to express asn1dn inside the peers-id-value string: hexadecimal, distinguished name (DN), and (as a fallback default only) the literal content of the peers-id-value string unchanged. This last is not recommended since it will not be valid asn1dn. Parsing rules are the following: * A string containing equal sign ('=') is assumed a DN. * Otherwise a string is hexadecimal, if it contains only hex digits as well as any number of optional spaces and octothorpes ('#'). Spaces and '#' bytes are ignored, so only hex digits get converted to binary. * Any string parsed as neither DN nor hex is kept as is. Note: An example DN (distinguished name) from rfc1779 is "CN=Steve Kille, O=ISODE Consortium, C=GB". This is the sort of input converted to asn1dn when the value contains at least one equal sign.

bugs.title: Providing LB::status with a GTM Pool name in a variable caused validation issues
bugs.symptoms: When utilizing an LB::status iRule where the GTM Pool name was provided in a variable, instead of directly written into the command, the system posts the following error message: Can't read 'monkey': no such variable.
bugs.conditions: LB::status pool a <Variable containing string>.
bugs.impact: Unable to use LB::status iRule.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Can now use LB::status iRule command to display the status of a GTM Pool when the name of the pool is provided in a variable.

bugs.title: tmm restarts under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: tmm restarts in certain cases; no traffic goes through the BIG-IP system.

bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
