An FQDN node is created with autopopulate disabled, for an address which may resolve to the same address as one of the static nodes. 3. This FQDN node is added (as a pool member) with autopopulate disabled, to a pool with no other non-FQDN members. 4. The DNS server resolves the FQDN name to an IP address that matches one of the static nodes. 5. A subsequent DNS query resolves the FQDN name to a different IP address that matches a different static node. Note: This symptom can occur only if the statically-configured node is created prior to creating an ephemeral pool member for the same IP address. If an ephemeral pool member and node are created first, it is not possible to create a statically-configured node or pool member using the same IP address.
bugs.impact: Traffic for the affected pool is not sent to the correct pool member (new ephemeral address), and is instead sent to incorrect pool member (old ephemeral address).
bugs.workaround: This issue can be prevented by either of these methods: -- Avoid configuring a static (non-FQDN) node with an IP address that matches any address that might be returned by the DNS server when resolving the FQDN. -- Add a statically-configured pool member to the pool in addition to the FQDN template member. Once this symptom occurs, You can recover by performing one of the following actions: -- Delete the statically-configured node with the conflicting IP address. -- Delete the FQDN pool member from the pool, then re-adding the FQDN pool member to the pool. -- Delete and recreating the pool.

bugs.title: UDP flows are not deleted after subscriber deletion
bugs.symptoms: UDP flows continue to live till UDP idle time occurs, even after the subscriber is gone and the option for immediate deletion of the flow is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- The option to delete flows upon subscriber deletion is enabled. -- The UDP flow is established with an idle time greater than the re-evaluate timeout.
bugs.impact: The UDP flows continue to be alive after the required time, but only act to drop the traffic.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Modify the UDP idle timer to a suitable value. 2. Force delete the UDP flow from CLI.
bugs.fix: UDP flows are now deleted after subscriber deletion.

bugs.title: LONG_REQUEST notice print incorrect in BD log
bugs.symptoms: LONG_REQUEST notice print shows incorrect memory usage.
bugs.conditions: -- A long request is received. -- View the LONG_REQUEST notice in the BD log.
bugs.impact: LONG_REQUEST notice is seen in BD logs containing an incorrect value for total memory used by long request buffers. Incorrect logging of total memory used by long request buffers.
bugs.fix: LONG_REQUEST notice print in BD log now shows correct amount of memory used by long request buffers.

bugs.title: CPU stats are not correctly recorded when snapshot files have timestamps in the future
bugs.symptoms: One symptom is that a message similar to the following comes out in the log files frequently. May 24 16:31:53 lusia_60.F5.COM warning merged[6940]: 011b0914:4: No individual CPU information is available. Merged CPU stats will be 0.
bugs.conditions: If all of the snapshot stats files have timestamps in the future, CPU stats will not be correctly merged.
bugs.impact: Frequent error messages in the logs, and incorrect merged CPU stats.
bugs.workaround: Remove all of the stats snapshot files that have timestamps in the future and restart merged.
bugs.fix: Merged has been update to correctly deal with the case where all of the stats snapshot file have timestamps in the future, and will correctly merge the CPU stats.

bugs.title: BD and BD_Agent out-of-sync for IP Address Exception, false positive/negative
bugs.symptoms: bd log spits this error. ------- ECARD_POLICY|NOTICE|May 24 04:49:42.035|4143|table.h:2408|IPTableList::del_object key not found in table ECARD|ERR |May 24 04:49:42.035|4143|table.h:0398|KEY_UPDATE: Failed to REMOVE data will continue to add -------
bugs.conditions: Configuring IP Address Exceptions in certain order - w/ and w/o route domain.
bugs.impact: BD and BD_Agent out-of-sync for IP Address Exception, causes false positives / false negatives
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: System no longer generates these false positive/negative log entries.

bugs.title: Null char returned in REST for Suggestion with more than MAX_INT occurrences
bugs.symptoms: Unable to view ASM event log details for a majority of violations.
bugs.conditions: Suggestion with more than MAX_INT (2,147,483,647) occurrences.
bugs.impact: Null char returned in REST for Suggestion with more than MAX_INT occurrences.
bugs.workaround: Use the following sql command: UPDATE PLC.PL_SUGGESTIONS set occurrence_count = 2147483647 where occurrence_count < 0;
bugs.fix: Null char is no longer returned in REST for Suggestion with more than MAX_INT occurrences.

bugs.title: Traffic Policy edit to datagroup errors on adding ASM disable action
bugs.symptoms: Adding an ASM disable action will trigger a message similar to the following: transaction failed:010716de:3: Policy '/Common/Drafts/TD180420-07', rule 'test'; target 'asm' action 'disable' does not support parameter of type 'policy'.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to submit a rule with a 'disable asm' action and a condition with datagroup.
bugs.impact: Cannot create a 'disable asm' action.
bugs.workaround: Create the rule using tmsh.
bugs.fix: You can now use the GUI to submit a rule with a 'disable asm' action and a condition with datagroup.

bugs.title: Traffic Policy edit to datagroup errors on adding ASM disable action
bugs.symptoms: Adding an ASM disable action triggers an error when the rule is submitted. The system posts a message similar to the following: transaction failed:010716de:3: Policy '/Common/Drafts/TD180420-07', rule 'test'; target 'asm' action 'disable' does not support parameter of type 'policy'.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to submit a rule with a 'disable asm' action and a condition with datagroup configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot create a 'disable asm' action.
bugs.workaround: Create the rule using tmsh.

bugs.title: Protocol Lookup agent has been removed
bugs.symptoms: The Protocol Lookup agent has been removed from the product.
bugs.conditions: Trying to use the Protocol Lookup agent.
bugs.impact: No Protocol Lookup agent is present.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround. The Protocol Lookup agent has been removed in this release.
bugs.fix: In this release, you can use the SSL Check agent instead.

bugs.title: Pfmand on vCMP guests does not recover after service interruption
bugs.symptoms: If pfmand on a vCMP host shuts down and starts back up, pfmand running on any of the vCMP guests loses connection and does not recover.
bugs.conditions: - vCMP host and guest(s) both have pfmand.healthstatus set to "enable" - pfmand on the host shuts down and starts up again. This can sometimes occur due to re-licensing on the host.
bugs.impact: Pfmand on vCMP guests loses connection: warning pfmand[20332]: 01660005:4: No connection to hypervisor.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the vCMP host will allow the pfmand connection to be be re-established.

bugs.title: Add functionality to configure the minimum TLS version advertised and accepted by big3d (iQuery)
bugs.symptoms: big3d advertises a TLSv1.0 version. Even though big3d requires previously exchanged certificates to validate a connection request, the TLSv1.0 advertisement triggers various vulnerability scanners and is flagged.
bugs.conditions: Running a vulnerability scanner or other SSL test tool.
bugs.impact: The scanner or tool reports that big3d might potentially accept a TLSv1.0 connection request (which is considered insecure). Vulnerability scanners then flag the BIG-IP system as vulnerable.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, because big3d accepts connections only from clients that match the certificates on the BIG-IP system, the risk is minimal. In addition, you can deploy firewall rules to accept connections only on port 4353 from know BIG-IP systems.
bugs.fix: This version adds a db variable for the big3d big3d.minimum.tls.version. By default the value is 'TLSv1'. You can also specify TLSV1.1 or TLSV1.2 (the setting is case insensitive). After changing the DB variable, restart big3d. Change the value on all BIG-IP systems that are subject to scans. This includes GTM as well as LTM configurations.

bugs.title: bgpd may crash processing extended ASNs
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions bgpd may crash while processing extended ASNs.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing enabled. Extended ASP capabilities enabled: bgp extended-asn-cap enabled
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing disrupted while bgpd restarts.
bugs.fix: bgpd now processes extended ASNs as expected.

bugs.title: SSL key files that have world-read permission are created during device trust reset
bugs.symptoms: After a reset of device trust, there are some SSL key files that are created and have world-read permission. These files should be protected or not exist.
bugs.conditions: Using either tmsh or GUI, the issue a reset to an existing device trust.
bugs.impact: Unauthorized user is given access to SSL key files in the file store.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Automatically disable Nagle's Algorithm for RD Gateway connections
bugs.symptoms: When APM's RD Gateway virtual server has Nagle's Algorithm enabled in the client TCP profile, it might severely degrade responsiveness of RDP client, to the point when it becomes unusable.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is used as RD Gateway. -- Nagle's Algorithm is enabled in client TCP profile.
bugs.impact: RDP client becomes unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Disable Nagle's Algorithm in the client TCP profile.
bugs.fix: The system now automatically disables Nagle's Algorithm for RD Gateway connections.

bugs.title: PAYG License remains inactive as dossier verification fails.
bugs.symptoms: - BIG-IP is deployed in a cloud environment (AWS/Azure/GCE) with PAYG licenses. The license won't activate on the startup.
bugs.conditions: - There are multiple ways this can happen but all of those come down to user networking issue where the http calls to the cloud metadata service fails. - This can be a simple routing issue to the metadata service or a firewall issue.
bugs.impact: As license activation fails, the instance becomes unusable.
bugs.workaround: User should look at /var/log/ltm to determine the networking issue that is causing the dossier verification failure. This would be typically printed in the following way: Curl request to metadata service failed with error(<error-code>): '<error-message>' By resolving this networking error, license activation should succeed.
bugs.fix: PAYG License remains inactive as dossier verification fails.

bugs.title: open-vm-tools now reports selfips in addition to management IP
bugs.symptoms: open-vm-tools (VMware Tools) only reports IP addresses for the management interface. Thus, IP addresses for self IP addresses on VLANs are not visible to automation tools that act on the IP addresses reported through VMware Tools.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in VMware environments.
bugs.impact: The VMware Tools report only their management IP addresses. Any processes, such as automation, that want to discover self IP addresses on VLANs cannot do so using VMware Tools. Note: This does not represent functionality provided in BIG-IP software. Rather, it is descriptive of how the VMware Tools work. This information is provided here for those whose automation or other tasks might depend on IP addresses reported by VMware Tools.
bugs.workaround: Connect automation tools to the management interface learned via open-vm-tools. You can then use tmsh or iControl to discover the self IP addresses for further orchestration or automation.

bugs.title: MCPD restarts on all secondary blades post config-sync involving APM customization group
bugs.symptoms: After performing a series of specific config-sync operations between multi-blade systems, the MCPD daemon restarts on all secondary blades of one of the systems. Each affected blade will log an error message similar to the following example: -- err mcpd[5038]: 01070711:3: Caught runtime exception, Failed to collect files (snapshot path () req (7853) pmgr (7853) not valid msg (create_if { customization_group { customization_group_name "/Common/Test-A_secure_access_client_customization" customization_group_app_id "" customization_group_config_source 0 customization_group_cache_path "/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/customization_group_d/:Common:Test-A_secure_access_client_customization_66596_1" customization_group_system_path "" customization_group_is_system 0 customization_group_access 3 customization_group_is_dynamic 0 customization_group_checksum "SHA1:62:fd61541c1097d460e42c50904684def2794ba70d" customization_group_create_time 1524643393 customization_group_last_update_time 1524643393 customization_group_created_by "admin" customization_group_last_updated_by "admin" customization_group_size 62 customization_group_mode 33188 customization_group_update_revision 1
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - You have configured a device-group consisting of multi-blade systems (such as VIPRION devices or vCMP guests). - Systems are provisioned for APM. - The device-group is configured for incremental manual synchronizations. - On one system (for example, source_system), you create an APM configuration object (for example, a connectivity profile) that causes the automatic creation of an associated customization group. - You synchronize the configuration from the source_system to the device-group. - On the source_system, you create a new configuration object of any kind (for example, an LTM node). - Instead of synchronizing the newest configuration to the device-group, you synchronize the configuration from another device in the device-group to the source_system (which effectively undoes your recent change). - The MCPD daemon restarts on all secondary blades of the source_system.
bugs.impact: While the MCPD daemon restarts, the blade is offline, and many other BIG-IP daemons need to restart along with MCPD. -- If the source_system is Active, the load capacity of the system temporarily decreases proportionally to the number of blades restarting. Additionally, if the systems use the min-up-members or HA-Group features, losing a certain number of secondary blades may trigger a failover. -- If the source_system is Standby, some of the previously mirrored information may become lost as TMM on secondary blades restarts along with MCPD. Should this system later become the Active system, traffic may be impacted by the lack of previously mirrored information.
bugs.fix: The MCPD daemon no longer restarts on secondary blades after config-sync of APM.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic
bugs.conditions: Use of HTTP iRules and/or LTM policies utilizing HTTP features.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: SWG URL Filters does not show the Filter Action for the Category but instead shows the Filter Action of its Sub-Categories
bugs.symptoms: SWG Parent URL Filter does not show the Filtering Action of self; instead it shows the accumulated status of the sub-categories
bugs.conditions: If default Filtering action is different from the Sub-categories filtering action.
bugs.impact: From the traffic filter and the GUI showing status of the URL filter is different

bugs.title: Private SSL key file access is too permissive
bugs.symptoms: The following private key files are world readable so anyone logged onto the BIG-IP system can read them: /config/ssl/ssl.key/.tmp1024rsa.pem /config/ssl/ssl.key/.tmp512rsa.pem These files are regenerated hourly so the any potential impact is very minimal.
bugs.conditions: Any standard BIG-IP installation exhibits this.
bugs.impact: Non-root users can read SSL private keys.
bugs.fix: The listed files are now only readable by the root user.

bugs.title: Cannot delete FQDN template node if another FQDN node resolves to same IP address
bugs.symptoms: If multiple FQDN nodes and corresponding pool members are created, with FQDN names that resolve to the same (or a common) IP address, you may not be able to delete any of the affected FQDN nodes even after its corresponding FQDN pool member has been deleted.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions -- Multiple FQDN template nodes exist with FQDN names that resolve to the same (or a common) IP address. -- FQDN pool members exist for each FQDN template node, with corresponding ephemeral pool members for each which share the same IP address. -- One of the FQDN pool members is removed from its pool. -- You attempt to delete the corresponding FQDN template node.
bugs.impact: The FQDN template node remains in the configuration and cannot be deleted, while an ephemeral node or pool member exists with an IP address corresponding to that FQDN name.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Remove all remaining conflicting FQDN pool members (with FQDN names that resolve to the shared/conflicting IP address). 2. Delete the desired FQDN node. 3. Re-create the remaining FQDN pool members to replace those removed in step 1.

bugs.title: Cannot delete FQDN template node if another FQDN node resolves to same IP address
bugs.symptoms: If multiple FQDN nodes and corresponding pool members are created, with FQDN names that resolve to the same (or a common) IP address, you may not be able to delete any of the affected FQDN nodes even after its corresponding FQDN pool member has been deleted.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions: -- Multiple FQDN template nodes exist with FQDN names that resolve to the same (or a common) IP address. -- FQDN pool members exist for each FQDN template node, with corresponding ephemeral pool members for each which share the same IP address. -- One of the FQDN pool members is removed from its pool. -- You attempt to delete the corresponding FQDN template node.
bugs.impact: The FQDN template node remains in the configuration and cannot be deleted, while an ephemeral node or pool member exists with an IP address corresponding to that FQDN name.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Remove all remaining conflicting FQDN pool members (with FQDN names that resolve to the shared/conflicting IP address). 2. Delete the desired FQDN node. 3. Re-create the remaining FQDN pool members to replace those removed in step 1.

bugs.title: Reported session ID keeps changing for the same user session when ASM doesn't track sessions
bugs.symptoms: A reported session ID is not maintained for the same user session.
bugs.conditions: -- Simple, feature-less policy (i.e., policy contains only attack signatures). -- There are no cookies coming in from the server.
bugs.impact: The TS cookie is not created since there is no cookie-enforcing feature that is turned on (such as session tracking). Although this is correct behavior, it might result in confusion when there is a different, random session ID on each request.
bugs.workaround: Turn on a cookie-related feature (such as session tracking).
bugs.fix: session_id is no longer shown in request log when TS cookie does not exist. This prevents any potential confusion when viewing the logs in this situation.

bugs.title: Always show violations in request log when post request is large
bugs.symptoms: The system does not always show violations in request log when post request is large.
bugs.conditions: A large post request with many parameters is sent.
bugs.impact: Although the violations is handled correctly, it is not reported.
bugs.workaround: Disable learning mode. The internal parameter pb_sampling_high_cpu_load can define what is seen as high CPU load above which sampling does not take place. The default is 60. -- Using a lower value reduces the chances of sampling data. -- Using 0 makes sampling never happen and thus this issue does not occur (this slows down automatic policy building).

bugs.title: Client fails to connect to server when using PVA offload at Established
bugs.symptoms: A client can fail to connect to the server on subsequent attempts if using FastL4 with hardware (HW) acceleration. When this issue occurs, the profile_bigproto_stat/rxsynatestablished stat is non-zero.
bugs.conditions: A FastL4 virtual server is configured with offload_state = EST.
bugs.impact: Clients fail to connect to the server.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable PVA acceleration.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system reboots while TMM is still writing a core file, thus producing a truncated core.
bugs.symptoms: If an HSB lockup occurs on i10600 and i10800 platforms, then TMM panics and generates a core file for post-analysis. HSB also triggers a nic_failsafe reboot. On these platforms, the reboot occurs before the core file is fully written, resulting in a truncated core.
bugs.conditions: An HSB lockup occurs on an i10600 or i10800 platform, triggering a core dump and a nic_failsafe reboot.
bugs.impact: The reboot happens after the core dump begins before it completes, resulting in a truncated core dump, which is not useful for analyzing why the HSB lockup occurred. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Reboot is delayed until TMM core file is completed.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing APM DTLS traffic
bugs.symptoms: When processing DTLS traffic for APM, TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: APM provisioned and configured. DTLS enabled in APM configuration.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: DTLS traffic is now processed as expected.

bugs.title: AVR: analytics statistics are displayed even if they are disabled
bugs.symptoms: Some entities are being collected for AVR internal (DB based) reports, even though they are set as disabled on AVR profile.
bugs.conditions: -- DoS profile enabled on a virtual server. -- IP/URLs are disabled on AVR profile for that virtual server.
bugs.impact: AVR does not adhere to its own settings for some entities.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP checks all conditions prior publishing the entities, and if an entity should not be collected for AVR, it will be published as "Aggregated" on internal (DB based) reports.

bugs.title: Forward Error Correction missing Auto option
bugs.symptoms: 100 GB Interfaces lack the Forward Error Correction Auto option in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP systems with 100 GB interfaces.
bugs.impact: Cannot Forward Error Correction to Auto using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to set Forward Error Correction to Auto.
bugs.fix: Forward Error Correction now has an Auto option in the GUI.

bugs.title: Analytics agent always resets when Category Lookup is of type custom only
bugs.symptoms: Analytics errors out with a log that says you cannot use custom lookup only along with analytics (/var/log/apm). Even if the Analytics agent is set to disable RST on failure, the agent will send a RST.
bugs.conditions: In the per-request policy, Category Lookup agent is set to custom lookup only.
bugs.impact: This configuration leads to an Analytics agent with 'RST on Failure' disabled. The BIG-IP Admin cannot make the choice to disable RST on failure for this particular setup (even though it is a misconfiguration).
bugs.workaround: You can avoid the RST and error by modifying the configuration to use a standard category lookup before the analytics agent. Using a custom-only 'Category Lookup' immediately followed by 'Response Analytics' is not a valid configuration. In this configuration, Analytics cannot run the way it is supposed to because it does not have the right information. 'Response Analytics' gives the option to choose what to do on error: RST, or continue on, implying that the non-RST option is valid. If the admin chooses to not reset, the system should log the error and continue. In this case, the system actually does send a RST, even though the RST is not what the BIG-IP admin intended to configure.
bugs.fix: Disabling RST on failure now works properly in this scenario now. The configuration is still technically incorrect, but now the system takes the correct specified action-upon-error.

bugs.title: load sys config merge not supported for iRulesLX
bugs.symptoms: iRulesLX configurations are (for the most part) contained in the file system, rather than the 'traditional' BIG-IP config files. An attempt to merge configurations containing iRulesLX using the tmsh command 'load sys config merge' options fails with an error similar to the following: # load sys config merge from-terminal Enter configuration. Press CTRL-D to submit or CTRL-C to cancel. ilx plugin test-plugin { from-workspace test-ws } Validating configuration... Unexpected Error: "basic_string::at"
bugs.conditions: The configuration being merged contains iRulesLX.
bugs.impact: The merge will fail with the error: Unexpected Error: "basic_string::at". The previous configuration will continue to work.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time for merging iRulesLX configuration. If the iRulesLX configuration is removed from the configuration to be merged, the merge will work.

bugs.title: The configuration may fail to load if a pool-type route is created that does not reference a pool
bugs.symptoms: The configuration may fail to load if a pool-type route is created that does not reference a pool.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in either of the following situations: -- A route is created via tmsh specifying 'pool none'. -- No pool is selected in the configuration utility when 'Use Pool' is selected. Note: It is possible to not select a pool only if there are no pools configured on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The configuration is accepted, but the resulting configuration does not load.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not creating a pool-type route with no pool.
bugs.behavior: pool for static route object can no longer be set to "none"

bugs.title: TCP flow may not work as expected if double tagging is used
bugs.symptoms: TCP flow may have an incorrect ACK number, and the flow may stall or reset. The BIG-IP system sends an ACK that is higher than it should be based on the data received from the client.
bugs.conditions: Double tagging is used.
bugs.impact: TCP connection fails.
bugs.workaround: Change the db variable tm.tcplargereceiveoffload value to disable.
bugs.fix: TCP flow now has the correct ACK number when double tagging is used.

bugs.title: New Chrome version is blocked when using Proactive Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: Mozilla Chrome versions 67 and later, selenium is false-detected. The system posts a message similar to the following: -- info tmm1[24434]: Rule /Common/UBOT_PRINT <BOTDEFENSE_ACTION>: client_anomaly {Selenium WebDriver Detected}.
bugs.conditions: -- Proactive Bot Defense. -- Block suspicious browsers is enabled.
bugs.impact: Legitimate users using Chrome 67 and later might get blocked/captcha.
bugs.fix: This version fixes the selenium test for new Chrome versions.

bugs.title: The configuration of some of the Nokia alerts is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: The categories for perceived severity in the alert_nokia.conf file are 0-4, 10-11, but there is an entry in the file with a value of 6.
bugs.conditions: -- Traps are enabled to support SNMP alerts in the Nokia NetAct format, e.g., using the following command: tmsh modify sys db alertd.nokia.alarm value enable -- The values in the alert_nokia.conf file are applied.
bugs.impact: Some of the values are incorrect. Handling of the trap/clear for the mislabeled trap is incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Edit the alert_nokia.conf file and restart the alert daemon.
bugs.fix: All OIDs that clear a Specific Problem (SP) now have a perceived severity of 5.

bugs.title: Mcpd and bigd monitor states are intermittently out-of-sync
bugs.symptoms: Bigd only informs mcpd of the state of a node on a state change. If the pool member status happens to be incorrect, this can cause the following symptoms. -- Pool member status may be incorrect for a long time -- Traffic may be directed to a pool member that is actually down.
bugs.conditions: -- Monitor is attached to pool member and bigd does not inform the state change event for a long time in certain corner cases. -- No periodic events from bigd to mcpd.
bugs.impact: -- False monitor status in UI/CLI. -- Large number of RST connections as traffic is directed to a pool member that is actually DOWN
bugs.fix: Added new db variable, bigd.stateupdateinterval, to create additional messages that correct the pool member status in certain conditions.
bugs.behavior: The bigd daemon can now create additional messages to inform mcpd of the status change for a monitored node or pool member, in case the message indicating the initial status change is not received or processed successfully by mcpd. This feature for a BIG-IP system by configuring the following sys db variable to a non-zero value: sys db bigd.stateupdateinterval { default-value "0" scf-config "true" value "0" value-range "integer min:0 max:600" } This value represents the number of seconds after an initial status change that bigd will wait before beginning to send additional status-change messages to mcpd. The first such additional message will be sent approximately the configured number of seconds after the initial message triggered by the monitored object's initial status change. Subsequent such messages will be sent at intervals approximately equal to two (2) times and four (4) the initial delay. This sequence of messages restarts after each change in the monitored object's status detected by bigd as a result of monitor pings. Since the processing of such messages triggers a modest amount of additional processing by mcpd, this value can be tuned for the desired balance between quick response and recovery from such conditions, and acceptable mcpd processing overhead.

bugs.title: High-Speed Bridge may lock up
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, hardware systems with a High-Speed Bridge and using Layer 2 forwarding configurations may experience a lockup of the High-Speed Bridge.
bugs.conditions: Hardware platform with High-Speed Bridge. Layer 2 forwarding enabled. vlangroup.flow.allocate disabled.
bugs.impact: High-Speed Bridge lockup, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: The vlangroup.flow.allocate DB variable is enabled by default. Ensure that vlangroup.flow.allocate is enabled with the command: modify /sys db vlangroup.flow.allocate value enable

bugs.title: Fix of ID 615222 results in upgrade issue for GTM pool member whose name contains a colon; config failed to load
bugs.symptoms: Loading configuration process failed after upgrade when pool member names contain colons. The system posts errors similar to the following: 01070226:3: Pool Member 443:10.10.10.10 references a nonexistent Virtual Server Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- GTM pool member has colon in its name. -- Upgrade to any of the following versions: + 12.1.3.x + Any 13.0.x + All 13.1.x earlier than 13.1.1.2 + 14.0.x earlier than 14.0.0.3
bugs.impact: The system removes the part of the pool member name that precedes the colon, and configuration load fails. For example, when the configuration contains a pool member named example_pm:443:10:10:10:10, the system removes the part of the pool member name that precedes the first colon, in this case, example_pm, leaving the pool member name 443:10.10.10.10.
bugs.workaround: After upgrade, add two backslash characters, \\ before the first colon, : character. 1. Upgrade the BIG-IP DNS system to the new version of software. 2. SSH to log into the bash prompt of the BIG-IP DNS system. 3. Run the following command to add the string \\ in front of the first colon character, : in the name of each affected GTM pool member: for j in $(find /config/ -name bigip_gtm.conf); do for i in $(awk '$0 ~ /^gtm server.*:/ {gsub("[/:]"," ",$0); print $4}' ${j}); do sed -i "s, /Common/${i}, /Common/${i}\\\\\\\,g" ${j} | grep " /Common/${i}"; done; done 4. Run the following command: load sys config gtm-only
bugs.fix: Configuration load no longer fails when upgrading with a configuration that contains BIG-IP DNS pools with members whose names contain colon characters.

bugs.title: Available datagroup list does not contain datagroups with the correct type.
bugs.symptoms: Available datagroup list contains only datagroups with type string and is not repopulated with datagroups that have a different type to match when the operand/selector changes.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the GUI. -- Operand or selector in a condition is changed to a combination that is not compatible with string-type datagroups.
bugs.impact: Cannot assign a non string-type datagroup to a condition.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to configure the policy rule condition.
bugs.fix: Datagroups list is repopulated with datagroups of the appropriate type when its rule condition's operand or selector is changed.

bugs.title: mysql monitor debug logs incorrectly report responses from 'DB' when packets dropped by firewall
bugs.symptoms: The 'debug' log for a 'mysql' monitor may incorrectly report data being received from the database when network routing is configured to drop packets from that database, causing confusion when diagnosing packet traffic. This might be stimulated by configuring the firewall to enable traffic to/from the 'mysql' database, and then (after the 'mysql' monitor successfully connecting with the database) changing firewall rules to drop packets returned *from* the database.
bugs.conditions: -- A 'mysql' monitor successfully connects to the 'MySql' database. 2. Once connection is established, firewall rules are changed to 'DROP' packets returned from the 'MySQL' database, resulting in several entries in the 'mysql' monitor 'debug' log that incorrectly suggest packets were received from the 'MySQL' database.
bugs.impact: Several log entries may be made in the 'mysql' debug log suggesting packets were received from the 'MySQL' database (after a previous successful database probe connection), when in fact those packets were dropped due to changes in the firewall rules. These log entries may confuse debugging scenarios, but will typically self-correct (such as after three log message entries).
bugs.workaround: When configuring network traffic for 'MySQL' database resources, ensure symmetry for traffic handling (either bi-directional packet routing between 'bigd' and the 'MySQL' database is supported, or neither 'send' nor 'receive' packet routing to the 'MySQL' database is supported).

bugs.title: 'No Access' error when viewing properties page of a GTM Pool member whose name includes a partition that does not exist on that BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system posts a 'No Access' error message instead of the GTM Pool member's properties.
bugs.conditions: -- At least two BIG-IP systems in a sync group. -- One of the BIG-IP systems has a partition that does not exist on the other, with a GTM Pool member on that partition. -- The issue occurs when a GSLB Server discovers that GTM Pool member and displays it on its properties page. Note: This same error message displays for GSLB Server's virtual server properties accessed by navigating to GSLB :: servers :: [server] :: virtual servers :: [virtual server]. The differing issues have been fixed in differing releases. You can find information about the similar issue in the AskF5 Bug Tracker article for 710032.
bugs.impact: It makes the GSLB pool member's properties page unavailable in this case.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workaroudns: -- Use TMSH to view or edit the properties of that GTM Pool member. -- Create partitions on the GTM device to match those appearing to be referenced in the object names.
bugs.fix: Partition checking has been disabled on the GTM side, since a pool member owned by a server is always in the partition of that server (/Common).

bugs.title: Damaged tmm dns db file causes zxfrd/tmm core
bugs.symptoms: zxfrd/tmm cores on startup.
bugs.conditions: Damaged tmm dns db file.
bugs.impact: System remains in a tmm-restart loop caused by tmm opening a corrupted tmmdns.bin on startup and segfaulting. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue for versions 12.1.3.1 and 13.1.0.2 and later, perform the following steps: # rm -rf /shared/zxfrd/* # bigstart restart zxfrd To work around this issue for versions prior to 12.1.3.1 or 13.1.0.2 perform the following steps: # rm -rf /var/db/* # bigstart restart zxfrd

bugs.title: VLAN group does not pass OSPF traffic till first unicast packet is passed
bugs.symptoms: Vlan group does not pass OSPF traffic till first unicast packet is passed.
bugs.conditions: -- VLAN group configured on the BIG-IP system. -- Routers are attached to BIG-IP interfaces.
bugs.impact: OSPF traffic is interrupted. OSPF router adjacency is not set.

bugs.title: ASM CAPTCHA sends non url-encoded payload when captcha is submitted by pressing 'Enter'
bugs.symptoms: When an APM end-user gets the ASM CAPTCHA page, types the correct CAPTCHA letters and presses the 'Enter' key, rather than clicking the Submit button. The CAPTCHA letters are sent to the BIG-IP system along with other request parameters, these additional parameters are forwarded to the backend server incorrectly as non-url-encoded, they should be url-encoded.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- ASM provisioned. -- DoS application or ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- DoS application or ASM policy has CAPTCHA enabled. -- User submits the CAPTCHA form using the 'Enter' key.
bugs.impact: Application receives unexpected content, which might cause the backend server's application business logic to not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Disable CAPTCHA within the DoS application or ASM policy.

bugs.title: The TMM - host interface may stall when the kernel memory is fragmented
bugs.symptoms: MCP logs 'Removed publication with publisher id TMMx' and the affected TMM restarts.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Linux kernel memory fragmentation exists. -- Another operation is occurring, including (among others): + Config-sync with full reload is initiated. + Running tcpdump.
bugs.impact: Degraded performance and unexpected failover when tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: If TMM fails to properly start for a prolonged period of time as a result of this issue, you can try to recover the system by restarting TMM (bigstart restart tmm), restarting the services (bigstart restart), or rebooting the system (reboot). IMPORTANT: This is not a permanent workaround, just a way to temporarily recover the system until you can upgrade to a version of the software that contains a fix for this issue.
bugs.fix: The internal driver has been improved, allowing it to work in low- and/or fragmented-memory conditions.

bugs.title: Memory leak when using SP-DAG and a small LSN pool.
bugs.symptoms: High memory usage by objects of type cmp. Using SP-DAG and a small Large Scale NAT (LSN) pool, some TMMs may not have any local translation addresses. If connections are routed out a VLAN that has cmp-hash src-ip, a small amount of memory may be leaked.
bugs.conditions: -- Using SP-DAG. -- Using small LSN pools. -- Having TMMs that do not not have any local translation addresses. -- Connections are routed out a VLAN that has cmp-hash src-ip.
bugs.impact: A small amount of memory may be leaked. The aggressive sweeper might kill connections. TMM may crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Using the default DAG with small LSN Pools gives all TMMs local translation endpoints. To prevent the leak, allow only VLANs with cmp-hash dst-ip in the LSN pool egress interface list.

bugs.title: Access Policy import with 'reuse' enabled instead rewrites shared objects
bugs.symptoms: If a policy is exported and then imported with 'reuse' it rewrites objects on the server instead of simply reusing them.
bugs.conditions: -- Exporting profile A. -- Importing profile B, with 'reuse' configured. -- The objects in both profiles are named the same and are the same type.
bugs.impact: -- 'Reused' objects on the system are modified. -- Policy A requires 'apply', because objects shared with Policy B are overwritten.
bugs.fix: Access policy import with 'reuse' option enabled no longer rewrites shared objects

bugs.title: File "dead.letter" may show up in /root directory
bugs.symptoms: In /root directory, there is a file named "dead.letter" with /etc/cron.daily/cleanup_sync_files: ls: cannot access /config/filestore/sync_file_request_d: No such file or directory
bugs.conditions: If your device does not use LocalDB feature or there is no local user created.
bugs.impact: The file /root/dead.letter grows daily by 5 lines regarding missing sync_file_request_d directory.
bugs.workaround: Having MAILTO="" in /etc/crontab will stop this from happening.
bugs.fix: The "dead.letter" will not be generated anymore.

bugs.title: Possible tmm core during high load, or when an ASM policy is enabled by other modules
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash if other modules enable ASM conditionally (e.g., 'ASM::enable' in an iRule) or if the BIG-IP system is under heavy memory load.
bugs.conditions: -- DoSL7 profile or Bot Defense profile is attached to a virtual server. Along with either of the following: -- The BIG-IP system is experiencing high load (low memory). -- An ASM policy is enabled by another module or configuration, such as an APM Access policy or an ASM::enable iRule command.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use 'ASM::enable' (or similar) to enable an ASM policy, when using DoSL7 or Bot Defense profiles attached to virtual servers.
bugs.fix: No tmm core occurs during high load or when an ASM policy is enabled by other modules

bugs.title: Add record type breaks commands 'modify gtm pool type all'; errors on nonexistent pool
bugs.symptoms: tmsh command returns an error similar to the following message: 01070227:3: Pool Member references a nonexistent Pool (/Common/poolname of type NAPTR)
bugs.conditions: Changing the record type on GTM pool members by running the following command: tmsh modify gtm pool type all members add.
bugs.impact: Unable to add pool members quickly to all pools of the same type.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: FIPS HSM: SO login failing when trying to update firmware
bugs.symptoms: After FIPS device initialization when trying to update the FIPS firmware. It may fail on SO login.
bugs.conditions: When trying to update FIPS firmware.
bugs.impact: This will not be able to upgrade the FIPS firmware.

bugs.title: mailx is blocked by SELinux Policy
bugs.symptoms: The mail command is not functional with the SELinux Policy.
bugs.conditions: Using mailx to send mail.
bugs.impact: Cannot use mailx to send mail. This is a function of the SELinux Policy, which does not allow execution of the mailx commands.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can configure the BIG-IP system to communicate with an SMTP mail server using the method appropriate for your BIG-IP version. For specific procedures, see K3667: Configuring alerts to send email notifications :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K3667.

bugs.title: LTM policies does not work if a condition has more than 127 matches
bugs.symptoms: LTM policies do not work if number of matches for a particular condition exceeds 127.
bugs.conditions: LTM policy that has a condition with more than 127 matches.
bugs.impact: LTM policy does not match the expected condition.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: LTM policy now works for a condition with more than 127 matches.

bugs.title: Invalid-certificate warning displayed when deploying BIG-IP VE OVA file
bugs.symptoms: The OVA signing certificate that signs BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) OVA files expired. When deploying a BIG-IP VE from an OVA file, an invalid-certificate warning might be displayed due to the expired OVA signing certificate.
bugs.conditions: This issue may be encountered during the creation of new instances of BIG-IP VE in clients that check the validity of the OVA signing certificate (e.g., VMware). Note: Existing BIG-IP VE instances are not subject to this issue.
bugs.impact: There might be questions about the integrity of the OVA file, and in some cases, might not be able to deploy a new instance from an OVA file.
bugs.workaround: The expired OVA signing certificate has been replaced with a valid signing certificate.
bugs.fix: The expired OVA signing certificate has been replaced with a valid signing certificate.

bugs.title: Radius Accounting-Request (STOP) always includes AVP Framed-IP-Address=0.16.0.0 when Network Access rescource configured with IPv4 & IPv6
bugs.symptoms: When VPN tunnel is terminated, 'Radius Accounting-Request (STOP)' always includes AVP Framed-IP-Address=0.16.0.0 instead of the assigned IPv4 addr to the PPP tunnel.
bugs.conditions: -- Network Access resource is configured with both IPv4 and IPv6. -- PPP IP address can be either static (obtained from RADIUS) or dynamic (obtained from the lease pool). -- Using an Edge client or a browser. -- VPN tunnel is terminated.
bugs.impact: APM sends 'Radius Accounting-Request (STOP)' that includes the AVP Framed-IP-Address=0.16.0.0 value instead of the assigned IPv4 client IP address.
bugs.workaround: Configure only IPv4 IP addresses for the Network Access resource.
bugs.fix: Include Framed IP Address in RADIUS Acct STOP message only when it is a valid IPv4 address.

bugs.title: DNS cache replication between TMMs does not always work for net dns-resolver
bugs.symptoms: System DNS resolvers (net dns-resolver objects) do not share DNS reply information between the dns resolver instances across TMMs, which can result in separate TMMs performing seemingly-unnecessary DNS lookups.
bugs.conditions: There are no LTM DNS *cache* objects present in the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.impact: A performance impact resulting from each TMM having to perform unnecessary DNS lookups.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create a placeholder LTM DNS cache resolver object. The object does not need to be used anywhere, just present in the config. Note: This workaround is effective even without a DNS license (although in that case, the placeholder object must be created using tmsh, as the GUI menu would not be available without a DNS license.)

bugs.title: BIND upgrade to version 9.11.4
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system is running BIND version 9.9.9.
bugs.conditions: BIND on BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: BIND 9.9 Extended Support Version was supported until June, 2018.
bugs.fix: BIND version has been upgraded to 9.11.4.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when tracing iRules containing nameless listeners on internal virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when tracing iRules containing nameless listeners on internal virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: -- Using iRule tracing. -- Internal virtual servers. -- Listener iRule, where the listener has no name.
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when tracing iRules containing nameless listeners on internal virtual servers.

bugs.title: Performance degrades when no inspections are enabled in IPS
bugs.symptoms: When protocol inspection is attached to a virtual server, but the profile contains no inspections, there is a performance degradation of around 15%.
bugs.conditions: -- Protocol inspection profile is defined and attached to a virtual server. -- The profile contains no inspections.
bugs.impact: Performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: Enable at least one inspection in the profile.
bugs.fix: If no inspections are enabled, there is no performance degradation when attaching the protocol-inspection profile.

bugs.title: Error in creating internal virtual servers, when address 0.0.0.0 exists on different partition
bugs.symptoms: Loading correct configuration with 'tmsh load /sys config' fails. The error message appears similar to the following: 01070726:3: Virtual Address /test/0.0.0.0 in partition test cannot be referenced by Virtual Server /Common/test-internal in partition Common. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Creating internal virtual server, when 0.0.0.0 address exists on another partition.
bugs.impact: Inability to load config, with created internal virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Create internal virtual server first; then create the 0.0.0.0 address on a different partition.
bugs.fix: 'tmsh load /sys config' no longer reports incorrect errors.

bugs.title: Apmd crashes running command: tmsh restart sys service all
bugs.symptoms: Rarely occurring apmd crash.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is licensed and provisioned. -- Running the command: tmsh restart sys service all.
bugs.impact: Apmd crashes and cenerates a core file. Traffic may be disrupted while apmd restarts.
bugs.fix: Apmd no longer crashes during tmsh restart sys service all.

bugs.title: tmsh does not automatically add websso and rba information when access profile associated to a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: After an access profile is associated with a virtual server via tmsh connections get reset with this error signature in /var/log/ltm: err tmm1[7894]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_process_state_client_enforce_acl, Line: 11058
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using tmsh to add an access profile to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: The access profile is added, but its dependent profiles are not, and connections resets.
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI to add the access profile.

bugs.title: BIG-IP installations on RAID systems (old style) may not boot
bugs.symptoms: Kernel panic at boot time with specific message similar to the following: mdadm: Devices UUID-<...> and UUID-<...> have the same name: /dev/md<X>.
bugs.conditions: -- System is a RAID platform, with an an earlier style RAID configuration such as the following: + 10000s / 10200v + 10050s / 10250v + 10055s / 10255v -- System has been upgraded through v14.1.0 and then downgraded to v14.0.0 or earlier. Note: For RAID platforms such as i15600 / i15800 and newer, this is not an issue.
bugs.impact: The downgraded v14.0.0 or earlier version does not boot.
bugs.workaround: To downgrade, boot and install the desired software version from external media.
bugs.fix: The duplicate device error no longer occurs during installation; the failure no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Factory default reset procedure does not remove AGC deployments
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP software has a procedure to reset the configuration to factory defaults: load sys config defaults This command clears most of the BIG-IP configuration, but does not delete objects inside of the Access Guided Config (AGC) configuration database.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration containing AGC deployments. -- Use the following command to reset the configuration to factory defaults: tmsh load sys config default
bugs.impact: Configurations made with AGC (iApps LX) are not removed. There is no particular functional impact, but these customization deployment objects remain on the system.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, use the following procedure: 1. Run the command 'load sys config default'. 2. Wait until the BIG-IP system has been reset. 3. Navigate to iApps :: Application Services :: Applications LX. 4. Use the GUI to delete all apps.

bugs.title: OSPF routes missing
bugs.symptoms: When newer link-state advertisement (LSA) (with greater seq) comes in, the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) discards the old one by marking it DISCARD. The SPF calculation function suspends the calculation every 100 vertexes. If the discard happens during such a suspend, then after the calculation resumes, the discarded LSAs are ignored,n which can cause route unreachable, and eventually route withdraws.
bugs.conditions: A very large number (~500, beyond best practices) of routers in a single OSPF area.
bugs.impact: Intermittent route flaps occur that might cause unreachable destination or increased network traffic due to the non-optimal route choice.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The 'vertex threshold' IMISH parameter is now provided for OSPF/OSPF6, and it is meant to control the amount of vertexes calculated in one bunch (the default value is 100). This value can be increased to prevent LSA discards. The value of 0 means that SPF calculation is not suspended at all, and in case of large areas this may cause slow responsiveness of OSPF and LSA drops, eventually.

bugs.title: Crypto traffic such as SSL may stop working in certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: Crypto traffic such as SSL traffic processing stopped.
bugs.conditions: This issues may occur in following condition: - After configuring SSL profiles on the platforms where crypto hardware such as Intel QAT crypto SSL is present and due to unknown issues if the crypto hardware fails.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP device cannot pass crypto traffic.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the SSL profiles or delete/re-create SSL profiles which process SSL traffic. Crypto traffic will be processed by software codec, it will impact the system performance as crypto traffic will be processed by software codec. To recover the crypto hardware, reboot the system, if it is a VE/vCMP guest, then reboot host/hypervisor.

bugs.title: TMM core when processing an unexpected remote session DB response.
bugs.symptoms: Using CGNAT or FW-NAT on a cluster may cause a TMM core if there are intra-cluster communication issues that cause CMP state transitions. The system writes messages to /var/log/tmm* similar to the following: notice CDP: exceeded 1/2 timeout for PG 1 notice CDP: PG 1 timed out notice CDP: New pending state 0f -> 0d notice Immediately transitioning dissaggregator to state 0xd notice cmp state: 0xd notice CDP: New pending state 0d -> 0f ... notice cmp state: 0xf notice CDP: exceeded 1/2 timeout for PG 1
bugs.conditions: -- A LSN pool or FW-NAT source translation that has persistence enabled. -- Intra-cluster communication issues that cause CMP state transitions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM does not crash when an unexpected remote session DB response is received.

bugs.title: Address lists and port lists used for AFM firewall rules cannot be created unless AFM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: Address lists and port lists used for AFM firewall rules cannot be created unless AFM is provisioned. This makes it impossible to create these items to share with LTM virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: Trying to create shared address lists and port lists for AFM firewall rules and LTM virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Cannot create address lists and port lists to share between AFM firewall rules and LTM virtual servers.
bugs.behavior: There is now a top-level TMUI menu entry named 'Shared Objects' containing address lists and port lists. AFM firewall rules already used these; now LTM can too, specifically virtual servers.

bugs.title: IPsec keys are once again logged when db variable ipsec.debug.logkeys equals 1
bugs.symptoms: Logging of keys when debug mode was "debug" or higher in IKEv1's /var/log/racoon.log was disabled in an earlier release. IKEv2's logging of keys in other log files was disabled as well.
bugs.conditions: -- When negotiating any IKEv1 security association. -- When negotiating any IKEv2 security association when ikedaemon log level has been set to debug or debug2.
bugs.impact: Keys, nonces, and several other "sensitive" values are no longer logged for either IKEv1 or IKEv2, making it hard to decrypt test traffic when debugging in the aftermath of problems.
bugs.workaround: There is no work around on the BIG-IP. However, debug logs on the remote peer, if not a BIG-IP, may provide the desired key information.
bugs.fix: The previous default logging of keys and other values have been restored, if db variable ipsec.debug.logkeys is set equal to one instead of zero. The new default value of ipsec.debug.logkeys is one. But this only logs IKEv2 keys when ikedaemon log level is debug or debug2.

bugs.title: MCPD crashes if several thousand files are created between config syncs.
bugs.symptoms: If more than several thousand (typically 20,000, but number varies by platform) files, for example SSL certificates or keys, are created between config syncs, the next config sync operation will take too long and mcpd will be killed by sod.
bugs.conditions: Creation of several thousand SSL certificates or keys followed by a config sync operation.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while the MCPD process restarts.
bugs.workaround: Run a config sync operation after every ~5000 files created.
bugs.fix: MCPD no longer crashes if several thousand files are created between config sync operations.

bugs.title: Improving Proactive Bot Defense Detection
bugs.symptoms: As part of Proactive Bot Defense tests, 2 webrootkit function are falsely detected.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.
bugs.impact: The limit allowed from those functions lowered by 2 (limit can be configurable using a bigDB).
bugs.workaround: Raise the required webrootkit function threshold by 2. (Using bigDB dosl7.web_rootkit_report_min_score)
bugs.fix: Correctly detecting functions.

bugs.title: Idle asm_config_server handlers consumes a lot of memory
bugs.symptoms: Idle asm_config_server handlers needlessly uses a large amount of memory.
bugs.conditions: This issue might result from several sets of conditions. Here is one: Exporting a big XML ASM policy and then leaving the BIG-IP system idle. Relevant asm_config_server handler process increases its memory consumption and stays that way, holding on to the memory until it is released with a restart.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary memory consumption.
bugs.workaround: 1) Lower the MaxMemorySize threshold from 450 MB to 250 MB, per process of asm_config_server: --------------- # perl -pi.bak -e 's/MaxMemorySize=471859200/MaxMemorySize=262144000/' /etc/ts/tools/asm_config_server.cfg --------------- 2) Restart asm_config_server, to free up all the memory that is currently taken by all asm_config_server processes and to impose the new MaxMemorySize threshold: --------------- # pkill -f asm_config_server --------------- Notes: -- The provided workaround does not permanently fix the issue. Instead it alleviates the symptoms of memory pressure, by (1) lowering the MaxMemorySize threshold from 450 MB to 250 MB, per process of asm_config_server, and (2) freeing up all the memory that is currently taken by all asm_config_server processes. -- This workaround does not cause any down time; the asm_config_server processes automatically start within ~30 seconds.

bugs.title: GTM regex handling of some escape characters renders it invalid
bugs.symptoms: The memory footprint of big3d increases.
bugs.conditions: GTM monitor recv string such as the following: ^http\/\d\.\d[23]\d\d
bugs.impact: Escaped characters are mishandled. This causes the regex compilation to fail and leak memory. The monitor marks the server it is monitoring UP as long as the server returns any response.
bugs.workaround: If you notice big3d memory footprint increase and you have a monitor recv string that has escaped characters such as '^http\/\d\.\d[23]\d\d', try changing the recv string to something similar to the following: ^HTTP/[0-9][.][0-9] [23][0-9]{2}
bugs.fix: Fixed handling of escape characters. Recv strings that previously failed to compile will now compile.

bugs.title: PTI (Meltdown) mitigation should be disabled on AMD-based platforms
bugs.symptoms: Platforms with AMD processors freeze when the PTI (Page Table Isolation) mitigation is enabled, after a period ranging from several hours to several days. You can find information about which versions have the PTI (Meltdown) mitigations enabled in the AskF5 Article: Bug ID 707226: DB variables to disable Meltdown/PTI mitigations :: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID707226.html.
bugs.conditions: -- AMD-based platforms: + BIG-IP B4100 blades + BIG-IP B4200 blades + BIG-IP 6900 and NEBS appliances + BIG-IP 89x0 appliances + BIG-IP 6400 FIPS and NEBS platforms + BIG-IP 110x0 appliances -- The database variable kernel.pti is set to enable (to address PTI (Meltdown)).
bugs.impact: System locks up and is rebooted by the watchdog timer.
bugs.workaround: Set the database variable kernel.pti to disable by running the following command: tmsh modify sys db kernel.pti value disable According to AMD, these AMD processors are not vulnerable to PTI (Meltdown), so there is no reason to leave the db variable enabled.
bugs.fix: PTI (Page Table Isolation) mitigation is no longer enabled on AMD-based platforms.

bugs.title: IPsec related routing changes can misfire, like changing tunnel mode to interface mode
bugs.symptoms: IPsec config changes that rely upon interface mode tunnels, which are driven by routes with associated tunnel VLANs, can sometimes fail to pass traffic after a config change altering routes, or altering the number of tunnels involved.
bugs.conditions: - Changing tunnel mode to interface mode. - Adding or removing routes for interface mode IPsec tunnels. - Deleting an IPsec tunnel object.
bugs.impact: An IPsec tunnel outage may occur before a system restart, which looks like absence of proper routing config, but which is due to inconsistent update when changes affect routing used by IPsec tunnels in interface mode. In some cases, a tmm core can occur which interrupts service briefly until restarted.
bugs.workaround: Typically saving before bigstart restart gets routing config related to IPsec back into working order.
bugs.fix: Tunnel and nexthop dependencies are now managed more exactly for routing changes that affect IPsec.

bugs.title: Disable flow if no protocol inspection profile is attached.
bugs.symptoms: If protocol inspection profile is attached with no compliance checking or signatures enabled, the system still processes all the packets through the IPS library.
bugs.conditions: -- Protocol inspection profile is defined and attached to a virtual server. -- The profile contains no inspections.
bugs.impact: Potential performance degradation.
bugs.workaround: If no inspections are needed, then remove the protocol inspection profile from the virtual server. Otherwise, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: If no inspections are enabled, there is no performance degradation when attaching the protocol-inspection profile.

bugs.title: Exists selector is added to L7 traffic policies
bugs.symptoms: It is difficult to detect whether a string exists in an L7 policy traffic operand.
bugs.conditions: -- L7 traffic policies are used. -- A rule requires a condition result string to either exist or not exist.
bugs.impact: The required rule cannot be written.
bugs.workaround: Using tmsh, it is possible to specify 'starts-with' an empty string to emulate a string 'exists' behavior. The GUI does not support this.
bugs.fix: The 'exists' selector has been added to L7 traffic policies to enable the detection of whether an output operand string exists.
bugs.behavior: There is now an 'exists' selector in L7 traffic policies to enable the detection of whether an output operand string exists.

bugs.title: Log message to GTM logs if an invalid regular expression is given to a monitor.
bugs.symptoms: Memory consumption of big3d increases due to the regular expression failing to compile and leaking memory.
bugs.conditions: The regex passed contains some combination of escape characters such as "^ http\/\d\.\d [23]\d\d"
bugs.impact: Big3d memory consumption increases.
bugs.workaround: Use a different regular expression. For example "^ http\/\d\.\d [23]\d\d" can be replaced with "^HTTP/[0-9].[0-9] [23][0-9][0-9]".
bugs.fix: Extra validation was added for regular expressions. A better escaping of certain characters was implemented. An error message will be logged to the GTM logs when a regular expression fails to compile. Also glibc's regcomp() was fixed to not leak memory when failing to compile.

bugs.title: IKEv1 phase2 key length can be changed during SA negotiation
bugs.symptoms: Using IKEv1, if phase2 key length does not agree on both sides, a responder accepts whatever the initiator proposes as key length, but only after an initiator is authenticated. This results in key length downgrade or upgrade at a trusted peer's request, because the IKEv1 daemon was configured to obey the other peer's key length request.
bugs.conditions: The value of the ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm on both sides agree on the encryption algorithm, but differ in key length. For example, if the initiator picks AES128 when the responder expects AES256.
bugs.impact: The responder accepts AES128 anyway. Although phase1 key length must be an exact match, when phase2 key length does not match, this allows an initiating peer to change the key length a responder uses, thus changing the strength configured by that responder.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is known at this time.
bugs.fix: Policy in phase2 negotiation is now changed to require exact match in key length for both initiator and responder, so both sides get the strength explicitly configured for that peer. Now config must be identical on both sides for ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm inside ipsec-policy.

bugs.title: Searching Request Log for value containing backslash does not return expected result
bugs.symptoms: Searching within Request Log for a value containing backslash does not return the expected result. This happens because escaping of backslashes in REST API access is handled differently with 'eq' and 'contains' filters.
bugs.conditions: Searching within Request Log for a value containing backslash.
bugs.impact: Search within Request Log record containing backslash does not return the expected result.
bugs.workaround: Backslashes in REST API requests should be doubled when searching using 'contains' filter, but must not be doubled when searching with 'eq' filter.
bugs.fix: Searching within Request Log for a value containing backslash returns the expected result.

bugs.title: Manual config-sync fails after pool with FQDN pool members is deleted
bugs.symptoms: If a user, deletes a fqdn pool on one BIG-IP in a cluster and then run a manual config sync with another BIG-IP, the change fails to sync with the other BIG-IPs in the cluster.
bugs.conditions: - Create fqdn pool in one BIG-IP - Save sys config - Run config sync - Delete fqdn pool - Save sys config - Run config sync manually Result: After deleting fqdn pool in BIG-IP and config sync with another BIG-IP, Manual config sync failed. Still, we can see the deleted fqdn pool in another BIG-IP
bugs.impact: FQDN pool delete failed in another BIG-IP and manual config sync operation is failed.
bugs.workaround: The workaround for this issue is to use auto-sync.

bugs.title: IKEv2 connflow expiration upon ike-peer change
bugs.symptoms: Altering the definition of an ike-peer does not expire the connflow used for the tunnel, so it remains in use for the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: -- Making any change to an IKEv2 ike-peer, even insignificant changes such as a description change. -- Running a system version that has new attribute auth-rule inside ike-peer. Note: This is not likely to occur in older system versions where no ike-peer state exists inside a connflow, because any ike-peer changes do replace the associated objects. In those cases, even though the same connflow is used, the system uses new algorithms for the ike-peer.
bugs.impact: In effect, you cannot change the configuration of the flow by changing the peer definition.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Changes in ike-peer now expire any existing connflow for that ike-peer. This affects only a system version that has new attribute auth-rule inside ike-peer.

bugs.title: Virtual server is not accessible from internal host when Traffic Matching Criteria is configured as address subnet
bugs.symptoms: When a Traffic Matching Criteria address-range uses subnet, the related virtual address is created with arp=disabled, icmp=disabled. This means that the address (any addr in the subnet) will not respond to arp or icmp, and hence the vs will be unreachable. If the flags are manually enabled then the virtual becomes reachable from client, however, it is still not reachable from the internal host.
bugs.conditions: When a Traffic Matching Criteria address-range uses subnet, this problem happens.
bugs.impact: Virtual server is not accessible from internal host.
bugs.workaround: Use specific address range in Traffic Matching Criteria.

bugs.title: Modified ssl_profile monitor param not synced correctly
bugs.symptoms: After modifying the ssl_profile attribute on an HTTPS monitor on a device in a high availability (HA) configuration, and after performing a full ConfigSync, the corresponding monitor on the peer-sync unit does not have the updated value.
bugs.conditions: -- An HTTPS monitor is used on BIG-IP systems in an HA configuration. -- The ssl_profile field is modified on an HTTPS monitor. -- A sync-to-peer (full ConfigSync, not incremental sync) is attempted to propagate the modified ssl_profile value to the peer units.
bugs.impact: The ssl_profile value for the HTTPS monitor on the peer unit is set to none, resulting in the two devices reporting themselves as in-sync, but having potentially different HTTPS monitor configurations.
bugs.workaround: -- Do not run HTTPS monitors using in-tmm monitors, -- Use the traditional HTTPS monitor configuration for SSL-attributes (cipherlist, key, cert, and compatibility attributes on HTTPS monitor). Note: Using these attributes generates deprecation warnings, but the configuration still takes effect.
bugs.fix: After modifying the ssl_profile attribute on an HTTPS monitor on a system within an HA configuration, and after performing a full ConfigSync, the corresponding monitor on the peer unit now receives the updated monitor attribute, as expected.

bugs.title: TMM core when using Multipath TCP
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, TMM might crash when processing MPTCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile with 'Multipath TCP' enabled is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic interrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable MPTCP.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer produces a core.

bugs.title: RRSIG might expire without incrementing external-facing zone SOA serial
bugs.symptoms: When a zone that is DNSSEC signed is copied to a slave via AXFR, each RRSET gets an RRSIG that has an expiration time. If the zone is otherwise static and the default expiration and publication times are configured, the RRSIGs on the slave will expire before the xfr-soa-serial gets updated by a key rollover event.
bugs.conditions: xfr-soa-serial is updated when RRSIGs expire, so that slave servers get a new copy of the zone when the RRSIG expires.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC signed zones fail verification if any clients use a slave DNS server for a static zone.
bugs.workaround: Set RRSIG validity time equal to or greater than the ZSK rollover time.

bugs.title: BIG-IP versions 11.6.3.x show 'Edition' as 'Final', not 'Point Release'
bugs.symptoms: When issuing the command 'tmsh show sys version' or viewing the /VERSION file, BIG-IP versions 11.6.3.x show the 'Edition' element as 'Final', not the expected 'Point Release'. For example, on BIG-IP v11.6.3.2, the 'tmsh show sys version' command shows: # tmsh show sys version Sys::Version Main Package Product BIG-IP Version 11.6.3.2 Build 0.0.2 Edition Final Date Wed May 23 19:39:10 PDT 2018
bugs.conditions: This occurs on all Point Release versions of BIG-IP v11.6.3.x.
bugs.impact: Possibly misleading indication of whether the installed BIG-IP v11.6.3.x version is a Point Release or not.
bugs.workaround: The final numeric element in the Version string indicates the Point Release number.
bugs.fix: When issuing the command 'tmsh show sys version' or viewing the /VERSION file, BIG-IP versions 11.6.3.x show the 'Edition' element as the expected 'Point Release'.

bugs.title: Changes to a cipher rule do not immediately have an effect
bugs.symptoms: If a cipher rule is changed, and a cipher group that uses the rule is attached to an SSL profile, the change does not take effect until something else on the SSL profile changes.
bugs.conditions: -- A cipher group is used by an SSL profile. -- One of its cipher rules changes.
bugs.impact: Unexpected behavior occurs because the cipher rule change does not take effect immediately.
bugs.workaround: After changing the cipher rule that's used by a cipher group, make a change to any SSL profile that uses the associated cipher group.
bugs.fix: Any changes to a cipher rule or cipher group now takes immediate effect.

bugs.title: Unexpected TMUI output in AFM
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the TMUI for AFM does not produce the expected HTML output.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned and active.
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output.

bugs.title: Unexpected TMUI output in AFM
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the TMUI for AFM does not produce the expected HTML output.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned and active.
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output.

bugs.title: Import of Access Profile with Machine Cert Checker and default CA Profile is failing
bugs.symptoms: Export and then reimport of Access Profile with Machine Cert Checker agent configured with default CA Profile is failing the following error: The requested profile_certificateauthority (Common/certificateauthority) was not found. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Any Profile/Policy with Machine cert and default settings
bugs.impact: Low: affecting only import/export.
bugs.workaround: Use non-default CA Profile at the export time.
bugs.fix: Export and import of Profile with default CA Profile works properly.

bugs.title: ASM UMU memory leak when WebSocket url has json profile with parse parameters enabled
bugs.symptoms: When ASM inspects WebSocket frames, the bd daemon memory is leaking; eventually ASM stops inspecting traffic and sends resets or bypass requests.
bugs.conditions: ASM module is provisioned. -- ASM policy and WebSocket profile are attached to a virtual server. -- WebSocket URL has JSON profile attached to it. -- JSON profile has parse parameters flag enabled (this is the default).
bugs.impact: ASM may reset connections; failover might occur.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Remove JSON profile from WebSocket URL in the ASM policy. -- Disable parse parameters flag in the json profile.
bugs.fix: The system now frees the allocated memory when it finishes the inspect of a WebSocket frame.

bugs.title: Enabling EDI protection by 'id' attribute configuration
bugs.symptoms: When protecting a field with EDI by its 'id' attribute, no protection is applied.
bugs.conditions: Protect with EDI a form field by its 'id' attribute.
bugs.impact: No protection provided.
bugs.fix: This release now supports this feature.

bugs.title: SIG SEGV during IP intelligence category match in TMM
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart while matching traffic from source IP to IP Intelligence category.
bugs.conditions: Multiple configuration changes that include deleting the custom IP intelligence categories.
bugs.impact: TMM restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer restarts while matching traffic from source IP to IP Intelligence category.

bugs.title: icrd_child spawns more than maximum allowed times (zombie processes)
bugs.symptoms: icrd_child is issued a SIGTERM. The SIGTERM might not succeed in destroying the process, especially if the system is under a lot of load. This leads to zombie processes.
bugs.conditions: -- The icrd_child process is issued a SIGTERM that does not successfully destroy the icrd_child process. -- System under heavy load.
bugs.impact: There are zombie icrd_child processes consuming memory.
bugs.workaround: Restart the system.
bugs.fix: Introduced the following configuration in /etc/icrd.conf: sigkillDelaySeconds If set to 0, or if missing from icrd.conf, SIGKILL will not be issued after SIGTERM is issued to the icrd_child process. If set to greater than 0, after the specified delay, SIGKILL will be issued after SIGTERM is issued to the icrd_child process if icrd_child process is not terminated. A 'safe' number for the delay may be 3 seconds, but will depend on your configuration.
bugs.behavior: Introduced the following configuration in /etc/icrd.conf: sigkillDelaySeconds If set to 0, or if missing from icrd.conf, SIGKILL will not be issued after SIGTERM is issued to the icrd_child process. If set to greater than 0, after the specified delay, SIGKILL will be issued after SIGTERM is issued to the icrd_child process if icrd_child process is not terminated. A 'safe' number for the delay may be 3 seconds, but will depend on your configuration.

bugs.title: A FastL4 connection can fail with loose-init and hash persistence enabled
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system fails to create a connection after 3WHS when using loose-init and hash persistence. This can happen if traffic is redirected from one BIG-IP system to another, with the second BIG-IP system failing to create the connection, causing an interruption of traffic on that connection.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with hash persistence. -- FastL4 profile with loose-init enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic fails when redirected from one BIG-IP system to another.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable hash persistence.
bugs.fix: A FastL4 connection no longer fails with loose-init and hash persistence enabled.

bugs.title: Importing access profile takes a long time
bugs.symptoms: It takes a long time for the 'Apply Access Policy' link to show up on the admin UI after importing an access profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Access policy with many macros. -- Import exported profile multiple times with Reuse Existing Objects checked -- As the number of imports increases, so does the latency.
bugs.impact: The imported access policy takes a long time to be imported and ready to use.

bugs.title: In a device-group configuration, a non-empty partition can be deleted by a peer device during a config-sync.
bugs.symptoms: In a device-group configuration, a BIG-IP administrator can add a non-synced object to a partition on one device, then delete that partition on a peer device, syncing the delete (this is assuming the partition is empty on the peer). Although the config-sync operation will report as having completed successfully on both devices, and no errors will be visible in the /var/log/ltm file of either device, a number of issues can manifest at a later time.
