For instance, assuming the non-synced object was a VLAN, listing all VLANs across all partitions will return the following error: root@(bigip-ntr-d)(cfg-sync In Sync)(Active)(/)(tmos)# list net vlan recursive 01070712:3: Internal error, can't load folder or nested folder for: /test/my_vlan And reloading the config will return the following error (as the partition has been deleted, including its flat config files): root@(bigip-ntr-d)(cfg-sync In Sync)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# load sys config Loading system configuration... /defaults/asm_base.conf /defaults/config_base.conf /defaults/ipfix_ie_base.conf /defaults/ipfix_ie_f5base.conf /defaults/low_profile_base.conf /defaults/low_security_base.conf /defaults/policy_base.conf /defaults/wam_base.conf /defaults/analytics_base.conf /defaults/apm_base.conf /defaults/apm_saml_base.conf /defaults/app_template_base.conf /defaults/classification_base.conf /var/libdata/dpi/conf/classification_update.conf /defaults/urlcat_base.conf /defaults/daemon.conf /defaults/pem_base.conf /defaults/profile_base.conf /defaults/sandbox_base.conf /defaults/security_base.conf /defaults/urldb_base.conf /usr/share/monitors/base_monitors.conf Loading configuration... /config/bigip_base.conf /config/bigip_user.conf /config/bigip.conf 01070523:3: No Vlan association for STP Interface Member 1.2. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. These are just examples, and the exact failures will depend on the type of non-synced object and its use within your configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- Two or more devices in a device-group configuration. -- Using partitions that contain non-synced objects. -- Deleting the partition on a device and syncing the changes to the other devices.
bugs.impact: The partition is deleted on the peer device, even though it still contains non-synced objects. A number of config issues can arise at a later time as a result of this.
bugs.workaround: In some cases, if you need to define non-synced objects, you can do so in partitions or folders that are associated with 'device-group none' and 'traffic-group none'. This would prevent the partition or folder from synchronizing to other devices in the first place.
bugs.fix: Validation has been added that will make a config-sync receiver reject the operation if this includes the deletion of a non-empty partition. In this case, the config-sync will fail and report an error message similar to the following example: 0107082a:3: All objects from local device and all HA peer devices must be removed from a partition (test) before the partition may be removed, type ID (467), text ID (60706)

bugs.title: Non-attacking IP addresses could be logged along with attacking IP addresses when DoS detects an attack
bugs.symptoms: During an attack, MySQL might log IP addresses that are not part of an attack along with the IP addresses that are part of the attack.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the system detects a BadEndpoint attack.
bugs.impact: The system might log messages related to IP addresses that are not part of the attack. These IP addresses are not part of the attack and may be ignored.
bugs.fix: The system now tracks a special state that detects which Endpoints are bad, so it ignores the IP addresses that are not part of the attack.

bugs.title: iControl REST statistics request causes CPU spike
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IQ makes iControl REST requests to BIG-IP systems to get statistics. Regardless of the page size setting, the request causes the CPU to spike to 100% utilization.
bugs.conditions: An iControl REST API request from a BIG-IQ device for a few stats for an object on a BIG-IP system. Note: A request for a single statistic usually does not cause a spike.
bugs.impact: Frequent requests by BIG-IQ for stats causes repeated spikes.

bugs.title: Incorrect RST message after 'reject' command
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP sends RST containing "Internal error in tcpproxy invalid state for repick" instead of correct "iRule execution (reject command)".
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server with a HTTP profile, and an iRule using 'reject' command.
bugs.impact: Investigating RST causes may be confusing.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM sends correct RST message.

bugs.title: Ephemeral nodes on peer devices report as unknown and unchecked after full config sync
bugs.symptoms: After a Full Configuration Sync is performed in a device cluster, Ephemeral (FQDN) nodes on peers to the device initiating the Configuration Sync will report their status as Unknown with monitor status of Unchecked. Note: The nodes are still monitored properly by the peer devices even though they are not reported as such.
bugs.conditions: -- Full configuration sync performed in a device cluster. -- Ephemeral (FQDN) nodes configured.
bugs.impact: Monitor status on the peer devices is reported incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: Any of the following three options will correct reporting status on the peer devices: -- Restart bigd -- Cause monitoring to the FQDN nodes to fail for at least one probing interval, and then restore monitoring accessibility. -- Disable and then re-enable the FQDN node Each of these workarounds results in the reported status of the FQDN node on the peer reporting correctly again. The workarounds do not prevent a subsequent configuration sync from placing the FQDN nodes back into Unknown status on peers, however.

bugs.title: DNS traffic does not get classified for AFM port misuse case
bugs.symptoms: When DNS query name has a label length of greater than 23 bytes, it does not get classified as DNS.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM provisioned. -- A port misuse policy for DNS and a service policy configured. -- DNS query name with label length of greater than 23 bytes.
bugs.impact: DNS does not get classified properly for some cases.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Allowed DNS label length is now 64 bytes, so any DNS query name where each label name is fewer than 64 byes is now properly classified.

bugs.title: dynconfd memory usage increases over time
bugs.symptoms: dynconfd memory usage slowly increases over time as it processes various state-related messages.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions as dynconfd is a core LTM process. Large numbers of pool members combined with flapping might increase the rate of memory usage increase.
bugs.impact: dynconfd grows over time and eventually the system is pushed into swap. Once swap is exhausted, the Linux OOM killer might terminate critical system processes, disrupting operation.
bugs.workaround: Periodic restarts of dynconfd avoids the growth affecting the system.
bugs.fix: dynconfd no longer leaks memory when processing messages.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Virtual Edition in AWS does not failover NATs in same availability zone
bugs.symptoms: If BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in AWS is configured with a traffic group to failover and its peer is in the same AWS availability zone, NAT objects will not fail over during high availability (HA) events.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in AWS, configured to failover with a peer that's in the same availability zone. -- NAT in the configuration. -- Failover event occurs.
bugs.impact: The NAT object will not failover and the newly active system for the traffic group will not receive traffic for it.

bugs.title: sasp_gwm monitor leaks memory over time
bugs.symptoms: The Server/Application State Protocol (SASP) monitor, sasp_gwm memory usage slowly increases over time.
bugs.conditions: The Server/Application State Protocol (SASP) monitor is configured. The leakage occurs during normal operation of the monitor and is not tied to any specific user or traffic action.
bugs.impact: sasp_gwm grows over time and eventually the system may be pushed into swap. Once swap is exhausted, the Linux OOM killer might terminate critical system processes, disrupting operation.
bugs.workaround: Periodic restarts of sasp_gwm processes avoids the growth affecting the system.
bugs.fix: The sasp_gwm monitor no longer leaks memory when processing messages.

bugs.title: API requests with 'expandSubcollections=true' are very slow
bugs.symptoms: Submitting an iControl REST query using the option 'expandedSubcollections=true' takes significantly longer to return than one without that option. For example, the command 'https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/virtual?expandSubcollections=true' takes significantly longer than the command 'https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/virtual'.
bugs.conditions: Submitting a query using expandedSubcollections=true.
bugs.impact: The response takes significantly longer to return
bugs.workaround: The additional processing time occurs because the 'expandedSubCollections' parameter fetches all the related associated elements. You can use the following alternative to retrieve the virtual configuration: 1. Run the following query: GET mgmt/tm/ltm/virtual 2. Obtain the list of virtual servers by: 2a. parsing either the selfLink or the fullPath properties in the response items array, where the response is from step 1. 2b. writing an iControlLX worker that does this. Note: Writing a worker abstracts the parsing logic into a user-defined endpoint. It provides API access to the data. 3. Iterate over the virtual servers querying each with the option 'expandSubcollections=true'.

bugs.title: IKEv1 has unused CRL-File in GUI that does nothing at runtime
bugs.symptoms: The CRL File in config for an IKEv1 ike-peer does not actually do anything, so it should not be presented in the web GUI. It also appears in the tmsh command line.
bugs.conditions: When using the configuration utility (web UI), the config for an IKEv1 ike-peer allows you to specify a CRL file that is not actually used for anything.
bugs.impact: The CRL file is not used in certificate checking.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not configuring the unused file.

bugs.title: Auto-update fails for F5 Helper Applications on Linux
bugs.symptoms: A pop-up error message is displayed for failed auto-update for F5 Helper Applications on Linux.
bugs.conditions: Linux users using F5 Helper Applications (f5epi and f5vpn) to establish a VPN tunnel.
bugs.impact: Linux users are not updated to the new releases.
bugs.workaround: Reinstall F5 Helper Applications manually.
bugs.fix: Auto-update succeeds for F5 Helper Applications on Linux

bugs.title: APM does not follow current best practices for HTTP headers
bugs.symptoms: APM does not follow current best practices for HTTP headers
bugs.conditions: APM enabled
bugs.impact: HTTP headers not generated as intended
bugs.fix: APM now follows current best practices for HTTP headers

bugs.title: OPT-0036-01 does not report DDM tx power alarms or tx power warnings
bugs.symptoms: The OPT-0036 optic does not report Tx alarms or warnings. The optic does report transmit power readings, but does not generate warnings or alarms if the transmit readings are outside the threshold ranges. OPT-0036-01 does not support SFF-8636.
bugs.conditions: -- Hardware using this optic: - vendor-oui 00176a - vendor-partnum OPT-0036 - vendor-revision 01 -- DDM is enabled.
bugs.impact: OPT-0036-01 does not report DDM transmit alarms or warnings.
bugs.workaround: DDM Receive power alarms and warnings are correctly reported. You can view the transmit power readings and thresholds to manually determine if the power is outside the DDM transmit threshold values. Note: When the OPT-0036 is disabled, the transmit laser is disabled and the transmit power is 0mW.

bugs.title: Updating tests according to canIUse database
bugs.symptoms: Some browser capabilities are changed.
bugs.conditions: Proactive Bot Defense, Block suspicious browsers is enabled.
bugs.impact: Browsers might get scored wrongly, and therefore get captcha/tcp rst when they shouldn't (Or not get when they should).
bugs.fix: Updating internal database according to CanIUse DB.

bugs.title: SNAT settings in network resource are not applied after FastL4 profile is updated
bugs.symptoms: When the admin updates a FastL4 profile, the iRule associated with the internal virtual server (the APM forward virtual server) is removed. This iRule sets up the SNAT setting, however, since the iRule is removed, the SNAT setting is not applied to new network access connections.
bugs.conditions: -- Using network access. -- FastL4 profile is updated.
bugs.impact: When accessing the backend resource, the BIG-IP system uses the self IP address as the source IP address instead of the IP address configured under the network access resource. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm. Restarting tmm re-creates the forward virtual servers and attach the relevant iRule.

bugs.title: management IP address change in device-groups
bugs.symptoms: When only the management ip address is changed on a BIG-IP, the rest resource /shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices/<uuid> is not updated with the new ip address. This affects the deployment of the SSLO iApp, which relies on the management address.
bugs.conditions: Management IP address is changed on a BIG-IP
bugs.impact: SSLO iApp fails to deploy on a standalone BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to update the managementAddress by sending a PATCH request to the device in tm-shared-all-big-ips device group. restcurl -X PATCH -d '{"managementAddress":"10.80.99.157"}' /shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices/6911da3d-e3a5-4503-a42f-0ed80440638f
bugs.fix: The code is fixed to support a scenario in which only the management IP address is changed. The restjavad daemon must be restarted after the management address was changed.

bugs.title: Ephemeral listener might not be set up correctly
bugs.symptoms: When ephemeral listeners are set up across a cluster, the transaction might fail.
bugs.conditions: When using Network Access tunnel with proxy ARP and no SNAT.
bugs.impact: The client-assigned IP address might intermittently fail to be resolved via ARP on the serverside/leasepool VLAN.
bugs.fix: The ephemeral listener is now set up correctly.

bugs.title: ASM may consume excessive resources
bugs.symptoms: While processing certain types of responses, ASM may consume excessive resources.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned and enabled. -- Response-side features are enabled (e.g., the default learn from responses and learn server tech or data guard is Enforced, etc.).
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a delay in traffic processing or a failover event.
bugs.fix: ASM now processes traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Changing the management IP of an Active device in Device Service Cluster will cause Active/Active
bugs.symptoms: The Device Service Clustering software uses the management IP as the primary key to identify the nodes in the cluster. When the Active device begins using a new management IP, the Next-Active device cannot reach the Active device, and becomes Active. Once the configuration change has propagated to all devices, a new Active device is chosen.
bugs.conditions: Changing the Management IP of an Active device in Device Service Cluster.
bugs.impact: Device Service Cluster has multiple Active devices for several seconds.
bugs.workaround: Do not change the management IP of the Active device. Force the device to Standby, and then change the IP.

bugs.title: Outgoing RIP advertisements may have incorrect source port
bugs.symptoms: TMM may change the source port of Routing Information Protocol (RIP) packets sent by ripd to something other than port 520. Neighbor routers will not accept these packets and RIP routing will not work. If the TMM instance handling the outgoing packet would not be selected to handle return traffic by the hashing algorithm in use, the source port of the traffic will be modified so the hashing algorithm returns the same TMM instance.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple TMM instances. -- RIP routing configured. -- After reboot.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing using RIP does not work if the traffic hash of the packets does not match the TMM handling the outgoing traffic.
bugs.workaround: Delete the sys connection for RIP; the new connection is expected to use the correct port.

bugs.title: syslog-ng does not send any messages to the remote servers after reconfiguration
bugs.symptoms: Changing syslog remote server IP address (tmsh sys syslog remote-servers) requires a syslog-ng process restart to take effect. Syslog operations do not use the new remote destination address on syslog service reconfiguration.
bugs.conditions: 1. Add a Remote Syslog server (Server A) using System :: Logs :: Configuration :: Remote Syslog. 2. Click Update (Syslog messages go out toward Server A). 3. Remove Server A from configuration. 4. Add new Server B (different IP address). 5. Click Update.
bugs.impact: After reconfiguring remote syslog host IP addresses, syslog messages continue to be sent to the previously configured addresses.
bugs.workaround: Restart the syslog service using the following command: bigstart restart syslog-ng Messages will now properly be sent toward Server B (the new IP address).
bugs.fix: Syslog operations now use the new remote destination address on syslog service reconfiguration.

bugs.title: Corrupted HSB RQM configuration causes HSB receive failures on 5000s/5200v, 5050s/5250v/5250v-F platforms
bugs.symptoms: In rarely occurring cases, HSB RQM queues configuration becomes corrupted, which leads to HSB receive failures. In some cases, all queues above 64 are all disabled, although the lower queues are configured and enabled with no packet drop. In some other cases, all queues are disabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Using 5000s/5200v, 5050s/5250v/5250v-F platforms. -- Specific conditions under which this occurs have not been reproduced.
bugs.impact: The receive failure leads to HSB lockup, and will impact traffic.
bugs.workaround: Reboot to recover, or disable ePVA to avoid lockup at the cost of some performance degradation.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE Cryptographic Offload updated to Intel QAT 1.7 v4.4.0 SDK
bugs.symptoms: Data compression offload to QuickAssist devices is now enabled as part of BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) Cryptographic Offload feature. BIG-IP VE Cryptographic Offload uses the Intel QAT 1.7 SDK. A newer QAT 1.7 SDK v4.4.0 provides code and firmware that fixes several known QAT defects, including a compression defect specific to Lewisburg/Lewis Hill QuickAssist devices.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP VE SSL Offload is licensed -- The BIG-IP VE VM has been assigned QAT Virtual Functions.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP VE Cryptographic and Compression offload are more reliable. The QAT 1.7 v4.4.0 SDK should be installed on the hypervisor host.
bugs.fix: Several Intel QuickAssist defects have been fixed for BIG-IP VE Cryptographic and Compression Offload by upgrading BIG-IP VE to the Intel QAT 1.7 v4.4.0 SDK. This newer QAT SDK introduces code and firmware support to fix several defects. A new Compress and Verify mode is introduced to work around a compression defect specific to Lewisburg/Lewis Hill QuickAssist devices. See Intel's QuickAssist Release Notes for additional details: https://01.org/sites/default/files/downloads//336211-009qatrelnotes.pdf.

bugs.title: The tmsh utility cores when multiple tmsh instances are spawned and terminated quickly
bugs.symptoms: A tmsh core occurs when multiple tmsh instances are spawned and terminated quickly /var/log/kern.log: info kernel: tmsh[19017]: segfault ... system messages in /var/log/messages: notice logger: Started writing core file: /var/core/-tmsh ... /var/log/audit: notice -tmsh[19010]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=19010 ...
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs intermittently in the following scenario: 1. Open multiple instances of tmsh using the following command pattern: tmsh run util bash tmsh run util bash tmsh run util bash tmsh run util bash ... 2. Quickly terminate them using Ctrl-D or by closing terminal.
bugs.impact: The tmsh utility crashes and produces a core file in the /shared/core directory. The BIG-IP system remains operational.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmsh if the problem occurs. To prevent the issue from occurring: Do not quickly terminate tmsh instances using Ctrl-D.

bugs.title: Licensing fails on a single-NIC device if a VLAN name other than 'internal' is used for the dataplane.
bugs.symptoms: Licensing fails with the following error in /var/log/ltm: Curl request to metadata service failed with error(45): 'Failed binding local connection end'
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) has provision.1nic enabled. -- The default 'internal' VLAN for the dataplane has been given a different name.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails to activate and cannot pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: Use 'internal' as the name for the 1nic dataplane VLAN interface.

bugs.title: A timer loop might occur when OCSP Stapling is enabled resulting in tmm getting aborted
bugs.symptoms: When OCSP Stapling is enabled on a client SSL profile, certain uncommon operations might result in a tmm timer queue getting into a loop, which results in tmm being aborted by sod. tmm restart
bugs.conditions: -- There are SSL handshakes waiting for an OCSP response, and one of the following: + There is a CMP transition. + There are changes made to the OCSP object.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts. Traffic interrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling OCSP stapling.
bugs.fix: The timer issue has been corrected.

bugs.title: Client's scripts trigger alerts while changing fields' values legally
bugs.symptoms: When a client's script manipulates EDI-protected fields, an EDI alert is triggered, even though the script is trusted.
bugs.conditions: Protected field manipulation by a trusted script.
bugs.impact: Alerts are triggered for trusted scripts.
bugs.fix: This release allows trusted scripts to manipulate protected fields if a trusted (user-triggered) event has occurred.

bugs.title: Potential HW/HSB issue detected
bugs.symptoms: There are a number of High-Speed Bridge (HSB) stats registers that monitor the errors in HSB SRAM that are critical for passing traffic, for example, RQM_CRC_ERROR Count 0, RQM_CRC_ERROR count 1, RQM_CRC_ERROR Count 2, etc. Any errors in any of these registers may indicate a hardware error in the HSB SRAM that impedes traffic through embedded Packet Velocity Acceleration (ePVA). In that case, ePVA-accelerated flow might fail. With a burst of CRC errors in the SRAM for ePVA transformation cache, it won't trigger a failover and causes a silent traffic outage on the FastL4 VIP with hardware traffic acceleration. This is because the health check watchdog packets are still functioning correctly, and the current TMOS software primarily monitors watchdog packets tx/rx failures to trigger failover. In these cases, there might be the following messages in /var/log/tmm*: Device error: hsb_lbb* tre2_crc_errs count *
bugs.conditions: Traffic is offloaded to HSB hardware for acceleration.
bugs.impact: Hardware accelerated traffic drop.
bugs.workaround: Switch traffic to software acceleration.
bugs.fix: Including traffic-critical registers in failover triggers, helps failover happen quickly with minimum disruption to traffic in the case of SRAM hardware failures.

bugs.title: BWC: Measure log-publisher if used might result in memory leak
bugs.symptoms: When Measure is used in BWC with log publisher defined, it might result in a memory leak in tmm.
bugs.conditions: -- BWC dynamic policy is configured. -- Measure is enabled. -- Log-publisher is defined.
bugs.impact: Memory leak in errdef.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not to enable Measure in the BWC dynamic policy.
bugs.fix: Configuring Measure in the BWC dynamic policy no longer results in a memory leak.

bugs.title: vlangroup usage may cause a excessive resource consumption
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, systems using vlangroup functionality may consume excessive resources.
bugs.conditions: Vlangroups with child vlans with Self-IPs Self-IPs that have restricted allow lists
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a crash and failover event.
bugs.workaround: Alter configuration. Contact support for instructions.
bugs.fix: Resource consumption is normalized.

bugs.title: Customization group object is not deleted when SAML resource object is deleted
bugs.symptoms: Customization group object for the corresponding SAMLResource object is in the configuration store, even after SAMLResource is deleted in GUI/TMSH.
bugs.conditions: -- Customization Object is in the configuration store. -- Delete the SAMLResource.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact, but additional configuration objects exist in the configuration store.
bugs.workaround: Delete the customization group object manually in TMSH. The BIG-IP system administrator can delete those customization groups if the corresponding SAML resources are deleted or do not exist in the configuration. The command 'list apm policy customization-group' lists all the customization groups. The SAML-specific customization groups end with '_resource_saml_customization' and are prefixed with the SAML resource name (SAML resource name concatenated with literal 'resource_saml_customization').
bugs.fix: Customization group objects are now deleted when the SAML Resource object is deleted.

bugs.title: ADFS proxy does not fetch configuration for non-floating virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: If the virtual address of a virtual server has a non-floating traffic group (e.g., traffic-group-local-only), ADFS proxy does not perform periodic configuration updates, including listing allowed URIs from ADFS, and thus blocks all the requests (by responding with 404).
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual address of virtual server has non-floating traffic group. -- ADFS proxy feature is enabled on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: All the requests to ADFS are blocked.
bugs.workaround: Set floating traffic group for virtual address (e.g., traffic-group-1).
bugs.fix: ADFS proxy now fetches configuration from ADFS for non-floating virtual servers.

bugs.title: AOM update occurs at every boot up
bugs.symptoms: Due to a corrupted AOM image loaded in Manufacturing between 5/15/2018 and 5/31/2018 on certain platforms, TMOS attempts to update the AOM every time TMOS boots. After the update, the system runs normally.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under the following conditions: -- Using AOM/BMC version 4.06 (4.6.17). -- Using BIG-IP i2000 or i4000 platforms. -- The hardware was manufactured between 2018-05-15 and 2018-05-31.
bugs.impact: Systems that are in this state attempt to update the AOM on every boot, after which they proceed to boot normally. Note: The AOM-update attempt is not an indication of a functional issue. Although the AOM-update attempt occurs at each bootup, once the attempt complete, the system functions normally.
bugs.workaround: Manually update the firmware using a later AOM image.

bugs.title: AVR does not collect all of APM TMStats
bugs.symptoms: AVR does not collect all of APM TMStats
bugs.conditions: Using AVR to view APM stats.
bugs.impact: Cannot view all values.
bugs.fix: This release now provides stats for the following: -- License Stats :: show apm license -- Session Stats (ACL Stats) :: show apm acl -- Access Profile Stats :: show apm profile access -- OAuth Client Stats :: show apm aaa oauth-server -- OAuth Profile Stats :: show apm profile oauth -- Network Access Stats :: show net tunnels ppp
bugs.behavior: This release now provides stats for the following: -- License Stats :: show apm license -- Session Stats (ACL Stats) :: show apm acl -- Access Profile Stats :: show apm profile access -- OAuth Client Stats :: show apm aaa oauth-server -- OAuth Profile Stats :: show apm profile oauth -- Network Access Stats :: show net tunnels ppp

bugs.title: Internet Explorer running on Windows phone 8.1 gets CAPTCHA during legitimate browsing
bugs.symptoms: Internet Explorer (IE) running on Microsoft Windows phone v8.1 gets CAPTCHA during legitimate browsing.
bugs.conditions: -- Proactive Bot Defense is enabled on a DoS profile attached to a virtual server. -- A client connects using IE on Windows phone v8.1.
bugs.impact: CAPTCHA occurs during legitimate browsing.
bugs.fix: A CAPTCHA event is no longer inadvertently enabled for Internet Explorer browsers on Windows Phone 8.1.

bugs.title: BD crash on specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: BD crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- Specific traffic conditions. -- A loaded system.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.

bugs.title: ASM Support for BITW
bugs.symptoms: Missing ASM support for bump-in-the-wire (BITW), Layer 2 Transparent bridge mode on the same VLAN.
bugs.conditions: -- Deployment of ASM. -- VLAN operating with Layer 2 Transparency.
bugs.impact: ASM deployment in bridge mode is not supported.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: ASM now supports deployment in same VLAN operating with Layer 2 Transparency.

bugs.title: Regcomp() leaks memory if passed an invalid regex.
bugs.symptoms: Because of memory leak, big3d's memory usage increased over time
bugs.conditions: Pass invalid expression to regcomp.
bugs.impact: Escaped characters are mishandled. This causes the regex compilation to fail and leak memory.
bugs.workaround: If you notice big3d memory footprint increase and you have a monitor recv string that has escaped characters such as '^http\/\d\.\d[23]\d\d', try changing the recv string to something similar to the following: ^HTTP/[0-9][.][0-9] [23][0-9]{2}
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak in big3d

bugs.title: REST API takes more than 20 seconds when 1000+ virtual servers with SNAT-Pool configured
bugs.symptoms: REST API takes more than 20 seconds to complete the GET request when there are 1000+ virtual servers configured with the same SNAT-Pool.
bugs.conditions: -- A large number (1000+) of virtual servers. -- Configured with the same SNAT pool.
bugs.impact: REST API takes more than 20 seconds to response to the GET request.
bugs.fix: Under these conditions, now the response time is approximately 5 seconds.

bugs.title: Rapid datagroup updates can cause type corruption
bugs.symptoms: 'invalid class type" error message in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: Using external datagroups and updating them before the previous update has finished, such as with: -- Executing config-sync. -- echo "create sys file data-group dg-test source-path file:///var/tmp/dg_test type string separator :=; create ltm data-group external dg-test external-file-name dg-test; modify sys file data-group dg-test source-path file:///var/tmp/dg_test" | tmsh -a
bugs.impact: iRule fails.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that changes to a datagroup are done processing (by looking for the 'finished' message in the LTM logs) before updating them again.
bugs.fix: Rapid updates no longer cause type corruption.

bugs.title: PEM transaction-enabled policy action lookup optimization to be controlled by a sys db
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to disable optimization if time-based actions are enabled in the PEM policy and a statistical transaction-based action enforcement is desired.
bugs.conditions: If the PEM classification tokens do not change.
bugs.impact: Time-based actions such as insert content may not get applied to such flows.
bugs.fix: There is now a sys db tmm.pem.actions.lookup.optimize variable to disable optimization if time-based actions are enabled in the policy and a statistical transaction based action enforcement is desired over per-flow enforcement

bugs.title: Information is not updated after installing FPS live update via GUI
bugs.symptoms: The GUI does not display the updated information after installing an update.
bugs.conditions: FPS is licensed and provisioned.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic only.
bugs.workaround: Refreshing the page.
bugs.fix: The information is updated after installing an update.

bugs.title: DHCP in forwarding mode decrements the received DHCP client side IP TTL prior to forwarding the packets towards the DHCP server
bugs.symptoms: DHCP packet dropped by the DHCP relay agent after the BIG-IP system, if the DHCP clientside packet received by the BIG-IP system has a TTL of 1.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system configured as a DHCP forwarder. -- DHCP client side packet received with a TTL of 1.
bugs.impact: Loss of DHCP service via the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate this issue, have the DHCP client send a DHCP request with an IP TTL greater than or equal to 2.

bugs.title: Modifications to AVR metrics page
bugs.symptoms: AVR metrics page does not use current best practices
bugs.conditions: AVR enabled
bugs.impact: Unexpected output when displaying the AVR metrics page
bugs.fix: AVR metrics page now follows best practices

bugs.title: No Bot Defense Logs when ASM Policy is used without Proactive Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: Device ID challenges are not logged in the Bot Defense Request Log (local and remote) when associating the Bot Defense logging profile to the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: -- Device ID is enabled on the ASM Policy. -- DoS profile with Proactive Bot Defense is not associated with the virtual server.
bugs.impact: There are no logs to show the browser challenges and the requests from clients that do not support JavaScript.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Requests are now logged to the Bot Defense Request Log with Device ID enabled on the ASM Policy and no associated DoS profile.

bugs.title: TMM restart when there are virtual server and route-domains with the same names and attached firewall or NAT policies
bugs.symptoms: TMM might restart when changing firewall or NAT configurations on a virtual server with the same name as a route-domain.
bugs.conditions: - There is a virtual server and a route-domain that have the same name in the configuration. - A firewall or NAT policy is being attached or removed from one or both of the virtual server or route-domain.
bugs.impact: TMM might halt and traffic processing temporarily ceases. TMM restarts and traffic processing resumes.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not to use the same name for virtual server and route-domain objects.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes under the conditions described. Firewall and NAT configurations are applied correctly on virtual servers with the same names as route-domains.

bugs.title: Rolling DNSSEC Keys can stop regenerating after a length of time on the standby system
bugs.symptoms: Rolling DNSSEC Keys may stop generating when a BIG-IP system is on standby for a length of time
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system is on standby for a length of time, in general, longer than twelve hours.
bugs.impact: Rolling DNSSEC keys can stop regenerating.
bugs.fix: Rolling DNSSEC Keys no longer stop regenerating after a length of time on the standby system.

bugs.title: Users may get blocked on Web Scraping or CAPTCHA
bugs.symptoms: Users using touchscreen or touchpad may get falsely blocked under the Web Scraping violation. Similarly, some users may fail to pass the CAPTCHA challenge when triggered by Brute Force Mitigation, DoSL7 Mitigation, or Proactive Bot Defense.
bugs.conditions: Either: - Web Scraping is enabled with Bot Detection set to alarm or to block (13.1.x/14.0.x). - CAPTCHA mitigation is in use due to another suspicious activity, triggered by Brute Force Mitigation, DoSL7 Mitigation, or Proactive Bot Defense (14.0.x). And: User is using touchscreen or touchpad.
bugs.impact: Some legitimate users may get blocked.
bugs.fix: Fixed false detection of some users as bots causing them to be blocked by Web Scraping or CAPTCHA.

bugs.title: Slow response times when expandSubcollections set to true
bugs.symptoms: A query for virtual servers with expandSubcollections set to true may exhibit slow response to the caller.
bugs.conditions: -- icrd logging enabled. -- Using the 'expandSubcollections=true' option in the REST query.
bugs.impact: Slow response times may impact usability, and the query may time out.
bugs.workaround: A refined query for specific entities may improve the performance time.

bugs.title: platforms using RSS DAG hash reuse source port too rapidly when the FastL4 virtual server is set to source-port preserve
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system running RSS DAG hash attempts to reuse ports while pool members remain in a TIME_WAIT state and are unable to process new connections.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You are running on a BIG-IP platform using RSS DAG hash, for instance, z100 and 2000 or 4000 series hardware platform. -- You have the FastL4 profile associated with a virtual server. -- The virtual server is configured with source-port preserve.
bugs.impact: Traffic throughput may be degraded.
bugs.workaround: Set source-port to change.
bugs.fix: Platforms running RSS DAG hash now reuse source port at the correct rate when virtual server sets source-port preserve.

bugs.title: iRule drop/discard may crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash after an iRule attempts to drop packet.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with UDP profile, and following iRule: when LB_SELECTED { drop # discard - drop is the same as discard }
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM correctly handles 'drop' command in 'LB_SELECTED' event.

bugs.title: interruption of traffic handling as sod daemon restarts TMM
bugs.symptoms: When the receiving host in a TCP connection has set its send window to zero (stopping the flow of data), following certain unusual protocol sequences, the logic in the TMM that persists in probing the zero window may enter an endless loop.
bugs.conditions: When the TCP implementation is probing a zero-window connection under control of a persist timer.
bugs.impact: Lack of stability on the device. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This fix handles a rare TMM crash when TCP persist timer is active.

bugs.title: 'Cannot find disk information' message when running Configuration Utility
bugs.symptoms: When running the Configuration Utility in the GUI, after clicking Next on the License screen, the GUI reports an error and you are unable to proceed: Cannot find disk information.
bugs.conditions: The conditions that trigger this are unknown; in one scenario, it was observed after running 'tmsh load sys config default', suspending the BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) guest, and then restarting it and running the Configuration Utility.
bugs.impact: You are unable to proceed through the configuration utility.
bugs.workaround: If this occurs, reboot the device, and the error will fix itself.

bugs.title: dns_path lingering in memory with last_access 0 causing high memory usage
bugs.symptoms: dns_path not released after exceeding the inactive path ttl.
bugs.conditions: 1. Multiple tmm's in sync group 2. Multiple dns paths per GTM needed for load balancing.
bugs.impact: High memory usage.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: dns_path memory will be released after ttl.

bugs.title: Mobile Firefox in Desktop Mode may be falsely detected
bugs.symptoms: Clients running Firefox on an Android device and selecting 'Request Desktop Site' may have a falsely detected user agent.
bugs.conditions: -- Proactive Bot Defense or Device ID features are enabled. -- Client uses Firefox on an Android device and selects 'Request Desktop Site'.
bugs.impact: Client may possibly get the CAPTCHA challenge, or Device ID functionality may not work correctly.
bugs.fix: Mobile Firefox in Desktop Mode now functions correctly.

bugs.title: Virtual-wire is not supported on un-tagged VLANs.
bugs.symptoms: Virtual-wire is not supported on un-tagged packets. When configuring a virtual-wire on un-tagged VLANs, the BIG-IP system does not forward packets in virtual-wire.
bugs.conditions: A virtual-wire configured on un-tagged VLANs.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not forwarded in virtual-wire.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than using virtual-wire only with tagged VLANs.

bugs.title: Unlock 10 million custom db entry limit
bugs.symptoms: Cannot add more than 10 million custom db entries.
bugs.conditions: This happens when you try to add more than 10 million custom db entries.
bugs.impact: Not able to add more than 10 million entries.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release provides a sys db var, tmm.urlcat.no_db_limit, to allow growth beyond the existing limit of 10 million custom db entries.

bugs.title: Improved debugging output for mcpd
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, mcpd debugging output is insufficient for diagnosing a problem.
bugs.conditions: Using debugging in mcpd, specifically, setting log.mcpd.level to debug.
bugs.impact: None. Has no effect without log.mcpd.level set to debug.
bugs.fix: New output helps F5 engineers diagnose mcpd problems more easily.

bugs.title: 'The requested Pool Member ... already exists' logged when FQDN resolves to different IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: When FQDN nodes and pool members are used in LTM pools, a message similar to the following may be logged if the DNS server returns a different set of IP address records to resolve the FQDN name: err mcpd[20479]: 01020066:3: The requested Pool Member (****) already exists in partition ****.
bugs.conditions: This message may be logged when the DNS server returns a different set of IP address records to resolve the FQDN name, and new ephemeral pool members are created corresponding to the new IP addresses. This may occur intermittently depending on timing conditions.
bugs.impact: These log messages are cosmetic and do not indicate any impact to traffic or BIG-IP operations.
bugs.fix: 'The requested Pool Member ... already exists' messages are no longer logged occasionally when an FQDN pool member name resolves to different IP addresses.

bugs.title: NodeJS debugger accepts connections from any host
bugs.symptoms: The NodeJS debugger accepts connections from any host. Note: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine. This issue exists in Node.js, not in BIG-IP software.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under either of the following conditions: -- iRuleLX plugin configured. -- Administrator starts node-inspector.
bugs.impact: NodeJS Debugger exposed to remote access. Important: Enabling the NodeJS debugger should only be part of active troubleshooting; it is not a recommended configuration for a production system.
bugs.workaround: Specify an authorized host for remote access using the following command: --debug=<host>:<port>

bugs.title: False-positive cookie hijacking violation
bugs.symptoms: A false-positive cookie hijacking violation.
bugs.conditions: -- Several sites are configured on the policy, without subdomains. -- TS cookies are sent with the higher domain level then the configured. -- A single cookie from another host (that belongs to the same policy) arrives and is mistaken as the other site cookie.
bugs.impact: False positive violation / blocking.
bugs.workaround: Cookie hijacking violation when the device ID feature is turned off is almost never relevant, as it should be able to detect only cases where some of the TS cookies were taken. The suggestion is to turn off this violation.
bugs.fix: False-positive cookie hijacking violation no longer happens working with multiple domains on some scenarios.

bugs.title: DHCPRELAY6 can lead to a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: tmm can crash when handling a DHCPv6 request via the DHCPv6 relay.
bugs.conditions: tmm handling a DHCPv6 request.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to DHCPv6 request via the DHCPv6 relay.

bugs.title: ASM cannot complete initial startup with modified management interface on VE
bugs.symptoms: The management interface is needed during initial ASM config and startup. This value is hardcoded in an ASM config file as the default 'eth0' instead of being discovered dynamically based on the device configuration. So if the management interface is configured to be on a different interface than eth0 and this config file is not changed to reflect that, ASM fails to start.
bugs.conditions: -- Running BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- The management interface is configured to be on a different interface than eth0. -- The config file (/etc/ts/common/image.cfg) does not reflect that change.
bugs.impact: ASM fails to start.
bugs.workaround: Modify the config file (/etc/ts/common/image.cfg) to match the non-default interface (e.g., eth1 instead of eth0).
bugs.fix: The management interface is now discovered dynamically during startup instead of relying on a hardcoded default.

bugs.title: Virtual server drop down missing objects on pool creation
bugs.symptoms: Available virtual servers are not populated in the drop down list during Pool creation.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server names containing single quote, backslash, or greater-than and less-than signs: ' \ < >.
bugs.impact: Unable to add available virtual servers to pools.
bugs.workaround: After pool creation, go into that newly created pool, click 'Members', and then click 'Manage', and use the Virtual Server drop-down list to add any virtual servers.
bugs.fix: Fixed the drop down for virtual servers. Now virtual servers get loaded in the drop-down list during pool creation.

bugs.title: Physical disk HD1 not found for logical disk create
bugs.symptoms: The blade error 'Physical disk HD1 not found for logical disk create' occurred preceding a CPU reboot on a VIPRION 2250 blade. /var/log/ltm shows messages similar to the following: -- debug chmand[3370]: 012a0007:7: mcp_logical_disk mcp_create received -- debug chmand[3370]: 012a0007:7: logical_disk create received: name[HD1] media[general_use_ssd] -- err chmand[3370]: 012a0003:3: Physical disk HD1 not found for logical disk create -- debug chmand[3370]: 012a0007:7: other mcp_create (tag=8124) messages -- debug chmand[3370]: 012a0007:7: mcp_physical_disk mcp_create received -- debug chmand[3370]: 012a0007:7: physical_disk create received: serial number[BTDV466121NK840JVN] name[HD1] Notice that physical_disk HD1 was created right after logical_disk HD1 was created. BIG-IP system operations expect the reverse, i.e., physical_disk HD1 should be created first. Note: These messages are visible only when you have the sys db log.libhal.level set to DEBUG and run the following command: tmsh modify sys db log.libhal.level value "Debug"
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that result in this issue are still being investigated.
bugs.impact: This occurs because the Logical disk was created before the physical one. The system posts the following error: err chmand[3370]: 012a0003:3: Physical disk HD1 not found for logical disk create. The system is forced to reboot. Traffic disrupted while the system restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The message is not printed anymore

bugs.title: Two ACL BLOBs saved in /var/pktclass/ directory use too much disk space there
bugs.symptoms: Two ACL BLOB files are saved in /var/pktclass/ directory in order to provide ACL persistence in the case of BIG-IP system restart. For large ACL configurations, these files can require more space than available on some platforms.
bugs.conditions: Large ACL configuration.
bugs.impact: Blob compilation fails.
bugs.workaround: Reallocate filesystem, so /var volume can accommodate two large BLOB files. This workaround may be not available on some platforms.
bugs.fix: Only one BLOB file is saved in /var/pktclass/ directory. Filesystem reallocation is never required.

bugs.title: MCPD on secondary VIPRION or vCMP blades may restart after making a configuration change.
bugs.symptoms: The MCPD daemon on secondary VIPRION or vCMP blades exits and restarts, logging errors similar to the following: -- err mcpd[11869]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Node name /group1/5.5.5.5 encodes IP address 5.5.5.5%18 which differs from supplied address field 5.5.5.5. -- err mcpd[11869]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Node name /group1/5.5.5.5 encodes IP address 5.5.5.5%18 which differs from supplied address field 5.5.5.5... failed validation with error 17237812. Or: --- err mcpd[8320]: 0107003b:3: Pool member IP address (5.5.5.5%999) cannot be assigned to node (/group1/node1). The node already has IP address (5.5.5.5). --- err mcpd[8320]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 0107003b:3: Pool member IP address (5.5.5.5%999) cannot be assigned to node (/group1/node1). The node already has IP address (5.5.5.5).... failed validation with error 17236027.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- VIPRION or vCMP platform with more than one blade. -- A partition with a non-default route domain. -- Creating a pool member in the aforementioned partition while a configuration save is taking place at the same time (either system or user initiated).
bugs.impact: If the system is Active, traffic will be disrupted as the secondary blades restart. The capacity of the system will be reduced until all blades are on-line again. Additionally, depending on the system configuration, the system may fail over to its peer (if one exists).
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not to create pool members from a different client while saving configuration changes in another client. However, this does not help if the configuration save operation was system-initiated.
bugs.fix: MCPD on secondary blades no longer restarts if a pool member is created in a partition that uses a non-default route domain at the same as the configuration is being saved.

bugs.title: Tmsh show command terminated with CTRL-C can cause TMM to crash.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash when running show ltm clientssl-proxy cached-certs virtual [name] clientssl-profile [name]
bugs.conditions: -- Running the command: show ltm clientssl-proxy cached-certs virtual [name] clientssl-profile [name]. - The command is terminated by the client connection, aborting with CTRL-C.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not terminate tmsh show commands with CTRL-C.

bugs.title: False-positive DATA IS MALFORMED alert when request is redirected to a protected URL
bugs.symptoms: There is a false-positive DATA IS MALFORMED alert sent when a request is redirected to a protected URL.
bugs.conditions: A request is redirected to a FPS-protected URL.
bugs.impact: False-positive DATA IS MALFORMED alert is sent.

bugs.title: Rare TMM crash when Single Page Application is enabled on DoSL7
bugs.symptoms: There is a rare TMM crash that may happen when Single Page Application is enabled on the DoS Application profile.
bugs.conditions: Single Page Application is enabled on the DoS Application profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Rare TMM crash no longer occurs when Single Page Application is enabled on DoSL7.

bugs.title: Invalid logsetting config messaging between our daemons could send apmd, apm_websso, localdbmgr into infinite loop
bugs.symptoms: Invalid logsetting config messaging between our daemons could send apmd, apm_websso, localdbmgr into infinite loop. This could be triggered by invalid state of our control plane daemons.
bugs.conditions: This is an extremely rare situation that can be caused by invalid logsetting config messaging between our daemons. However, once it happens it can impact multiple daemons at the same time causing all of them to hang.
bugs.impact: Once this happens it can impact multiple daemons (apmd, apm_websso, localdbmgr) at the same time causing all of them to hang.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time, you can recover by restarting the daemons that hang.
bugs.fix: We have fixed a memory corruption that can break the linkages in our data structure which would cause certain traversals to loop indefinitely.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when a session is terminated
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when it is releasing the memory used by a session that is terminated. Either one of the following error messages might appear in the TMM log: -- notice panic: ../kern/umem.c:4166: Assertion "valid type" failed. -- notice panic: ../kern/page_alloc.c:705: Assertion "vmem_hashlist_remove not found" failed.
bugs.conditions: The memory used by a session is corrupted during the lifetime of the session. This issue happens infrequently.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts, causing service interruption if the BIG-IP system is not part of a high-availability setup.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when removing an access session.

bugs.title: Entropy start-up sentinel file is not cleared on successful start
bugs.symptoms: When the entropy start-up fails, a file is created that will prevent a reboot loop. However, if the entropy start-up succeeds, the file remains.
bugs.conditions: Entropy start-up fails and then succeeds.
bugs.impact: The entropy start-up sentinel file is not cleared as it should be. If an entropy failure happens again, then all subsequent rebooting for a failed entropy is disabled. Should the entropy succeed and then later fail, the reboot to handle the failed entropy start-up will not happen.
bugs.workaround: User can manually remove the start-up failure sentinel file using the following command: /bin/rm -f /.entropy_failure_sentinal_file
bugs.fix: Now, if the entropy start-up succeeds, the system removes that file, so that subsequent failures reboot at least once. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: PEM content insertion in a compressed response may truncate some data
bugs.symptoms: HTTP compressed response with content insert action can truncate data.
bugs.conditions: PEM content insertion action with compressed HTTP response.
bugs.impact: Data might be truncated.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling compression accept-encoding attribute in the HTTP request.
bugs.fix: HTTP compressed response with content insert action no longer truncates data.

bugs.title: tmm core dump due to SEGFAULT
bugs.symptoms: tmm core dump due to SEGFAULT.
bugs.conditions: System under load in network. Other conditions required to recreate this are unknown, but indicated a potential memory-handling issue.
bugs.impact: The blade reboots resulting in failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The apparent memory-handling issue leading to the SEGFAULT has been corrected, so the tmm core and failover no longer occur.

bugs.title: DAGv2 port lookup stringent may fail
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances tmm might not be able to find a local port, and the connection may fail. This happens, for example, for active FTP with mirroring enabled.
bugs.conditions: Active FTP with mirroring enabled.
bugs.impact: Connection cannot get established.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable mirroring.
bugs.fix: TMM is now always able to find a local port.

bugs.title: AVR inject CSPM event when there is no analytics profile on the virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When there is a request for page load time in the analytics profile, and changes to the configuration remove the analytics profile, AVR will continue to inject the Client Side Performance Monitoring (CSPM) cookie.
bugs.conditions: -- Request for page-load-time statistic. -- The analytics profile has been removed from the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Page-load-time cookie is injected when it should not be.
bugs.workaround: Uncheck the page-load-time checkbox before removing the profile from the virtual server.
bugs.fix: AVR now injects CSPM cookie only when it needed.

bugs.title: IApp LX directory disappears after upgrade or restoring from ucs
bugs.symptoms: After BIG-IP version upgrade or restoring from UCS, iApps/Application Services/Applications LX screen displays instances of iApps LX, but their UI is not functional. That is caused by the software defect causing iApp LX directory to disappear from /var/config/rest/iapps.
bugs.conditions: This issue can only happen during initial start after BIG-IP version upgrade or restoring from UCS. The more iApps LX instances and the more configuration they use, the more likely this issue to happen. We observed this issue with 90+ instances of f5-ddos-hybrid-defender iApp LX.
bugs.impact: The code of iAppLX is removed from the system because of the defect. That makes iAppLX UI unusable. The configuration deployed by the iApp LX instances remains in effect. The iApp LX configuration data remain intact and UI can be completely restored after manual installation of iApp LX code.
bugs.workaround: 1. Copy iAppLX code from an unaffected BIG-IP to the BIG-IP impacted by this defect. For example, /var/config/rest/iapps/f5-ddos-hybrid-defender. 2. Create a symlink to UI code for UI to work. For example, ln -sfvn /var/config/rest/iapps/f5-ddos-hybrid-defender/presentation /var/iapps/www/f5-ddos-hybrid-defender 3. Restart restjavad: bigstart restart restjavad 4. Restart restnoded: bigstart restart restnoded
bugs.fix: The issue should not happen when upgrading to the BIG-IP version with the fix or restoring from UCS on the BIG-IP version with the fix.

bugs.title: VPE cannot modify subroutine settings
bugs.symptoms: Open per-request policy in Visual Policy Editor (VPE) that has a subroutine. Click 'Subroutine Settings / Rename. Numeric values like the inactivity timeout are displayed as 'NaN. Attempts to modify the values results in MCP validation errors such as one of these: - Unable to execute transaction because of: - Unable to execute transaction because of: 01020036:3: The requested user role partition (admin Common) was not found.
bugs.conditions: -- Per-request policy in the VPE. -- Subroutine in the per-request policy. -- Attempt to change the values.
bugs.impact: All fields say 'NaN', and error when trying to modify properties. Subroutine settings like the Inactivity Timeout and Gating Criteria cannot be modified through the VPE
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to modify these values, for example: tmsh modify apm policy access-policy <policy_name> subroutine properties modify { all { inactivity-timeout 301 } }
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed; it is now possible to view and modify subroutine settings in the VPE.

bugs.title: Switching from FastL4 or TCP profiles to an ipother profile may leave a virtual server with stale TCP syncookie parameters
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server may attempt to use syncookies on first SYN packet rather than allowing the connection to pass through to the real server.
bugs.conditions: Modifying a virtual server (CLI/iControl/GUI) to switch from FastL4 or TCP profiles to an 'ip-other' profile.
bugs.impact: The configured 'ip-other' virtual server will fail to accept all traffic. For example, a TCP or a UDP flow which should have been accepted and processed by the 'ip-other' virtual server will be dropped incorrectly, trying to enforce 'Syn Cookie' validation.
bugs.workaround: When switching a virtual server profile from FastL4/TCP to the 'ip-other' profile, delete the virtual server and then re-add it with the 'ip-other' profile.

bugs.title: Device management and GUI can be configured using different crt/key
bugs.symptoms: Device management and GUI using different crt/key Device Certificates : Device Certificate ›› Device Certificate" displays different certificate than the GUI uses.
bugs.conditions: modified default httpd crt/key file locations using tmsh command: tmsh modify sys httpd ssl-certkeyfile /config/httpd/conf/ssl.key/new-server.key ssl-certfile /config/httpd/conf/ssl.crt/new-server.crt
bugs.impact: "Device Certificates : Device Certificate ›› Device Certificate" will not display the correct certificate.
bugs.workaround: keep sys httpd ssl-* pointing at default locations: tmsh modify sys httpd ssl-certkeyfile /config/httpd/conf/ssl.key/server.key ssl-certfile /config/httpd/conf/ssl.crt/server.crt
bugs.fix: GUI will now allow you to configure device certificate and Device key which pointed to non-default cert/key file location. Default cert/key file locations are: /config/httpd/conf/ssl.crt/server.crt /config/httpd/conf/ssl.key/server.key

bugs.title: Inserting multi-line HTTP header not handled correctly
bugs.symptoms: Using an iRule to insert an HTTP header that contains an embedded newline followed by whitespace is not parsed properly. It can result in the new header being incorrectly split into multiple headers.
bugs.conditions: iRule which adds a header containing embedded newline followed by whitespace: HTTP::header insert X-Multi "This is a\n multi-line header"
bugs.impact: New header does not get parsed properly, and its values are treated like new header values. In some cases the tmm may be restarted.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the trailing whitespace text is not present (if not legitimately there). For manipulation of HTTP Cookie headers, use the HTTP::cookie API rather than directly via HTTP::header.
bugs.fix: Inserting multi-line HTTP header parsed correctly

bugs.title: HTTP::header names might damage HTTP cookie cache due to stale xcursor
bugs.symptoms: HTTP::header names can damage HTTP cookie cache due to stale xcursor, and subsequently causes tmm to core dump on failing to validate the internal data structure.
bugs.conditions: Using Tcl HTTP::header names that change the internal data structure of the HTTP cookie cache.
bugs.impact: Tmm might core dump, resulting in device failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: This is likely a rarely occurring event. There is no workaround, short of using HTTP::header only as read-only mode.

bugs.title: TMM restart in B2250 vCMP systems, and ping/monitor failures in non-B2250 vCMP systems.
bugs.symptoms: -- On B2250 blades the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) may experience a series of panics and restarts. The system reports a related message in /var/log/tmm: vdag failed to attach -- On other types of BIG-IP systems (e.g., iSeries) ICMP monitors (or manual pings from the command line) may fail, indicating incorrectly that a node which is known to be up is down, and a packet capture will show ICMP echo reply packets arriving, but being ignored.
bugs.conditions: -- Guest BIG-IP instance in a vCMP configuration. -- Guest is running BIG-IP v13.1.3.5. -- Host is running a software version other than BIG-IP v13.1.3.5. -- For the tmm panic issue, the host is a B2250 blade.
bugs.impact: -- For B2250 configurations, tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. -- For non-B2250 configurations, ICMP monitors are incorrectly marked down.
bugs.workaround: None. Note: If installing 13.1.3.5 on a vCMP host or guest, please contact F5 Support and ask for an engineering hotfix with the fix for this issue. Install it on the vCMP host and all guests on that host running 13.1.3.5.
bugs.fix: TMM disruption no longer occurs from disaggregation in vCMP systems.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing compressed data
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing compressed data.
bugs.conditions: Compression enabled Hardware compression disabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: TMM now correctly processes compressed traffic

bugs.title: Request Logs are not stored locally due to shmem pipe blockage
bugs.symptoms: An unknown issue causes the communication layer between pabnagd and asmlogd to be become stuck. Messages similar to the following appear in pabnagd.log: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- account |NOTICE|... src/Account.cpp:183|Skipped 36 repeated messages. Request Log protobuf subscription queue is full. Message dropped. rqlgwriter |WARNIN|... src/RequestLogWriter.cpp:137|Skipped 599 repeated messages. No space to write in shmem. Messages similar to the following appear in pabnagd.log:
bugs.conditions: Request Logs are not stored locally due to shmem pipe blockage.
bugs.impact: Event logs stop logging locally.
bugs.workaround: Restart policy builder with: killall -s SIGHUP pabnagd
bugs.fix: The policy builder now detects the blockage, and restarts the connection with the request logger.

bugs.title: One dataset contains large number of variations of TLS hello messages on Chrome
bugs.symptoms: Dataset of TLS fingerprints of clients of a site can consume significantly more space than needed.
bugs.conditions: -- BADOS with TLS signatures. -- AFM end user clients using the Mozilla Chrome browser.
bugs.impact: Dataset is full, so it does not contain a full TLS fingerprints set. As result there is a risk of creating false-positive TLS signatures.
bugs.workaround: Turn off TLS signatures.
bugs.fix: Dataset of TLS fingerprints contains unique TLC fingerprints regardless GREASE ciphers.

bugs.title: Invalid arguments to run sys failover do not return an error
bugs.symptoms: If an invalid device name is used in the sys failover command, the device name reject is logged in /var/log/ltm and failover does not occur. No error or failure message is displayed on the command line. Note: In prior versions, the system incorrectly performed a force-to-standby operation (no 'device' specified), rather than a directed failover operation (failover to specified 'device'). Although this resulted in the active device becoming standby, it did not cause the system to choose the (nonexistent) device specified.
bugs.conditions: Run a tmsh command similar to the following: sys failover standby traffic-group traffic-group-1 device invalid_name
bugs.impact: Since no failover occurs and no error/warning is returned, this may result in some confusion.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Memory corruption when using SSL Forward Proxy on certain platforms
bugs.symptoms: When using SSL Forward proxy, memory corruption can occur, which can eventually lead to a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: Client SSL profile on a virtual server with SSL Forward proxy enabled. -- Using the following platforms: - vCMP host - 2000s / 2200s - 5000s / 5200v - 5050s / 5250v / 5250v-F - 10350V-F
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: Subscriber-id query using full length IPv6 address fails.
bugs.symptoms: FW NAT / CGNAT modules query the subscriber ID using IPv6 address. If the query is done using the IPv6 mask, under some circumstances the query fails.
bugs.conditions: The network is using an IPv6 mask other than 128. Subscribers are created using the masked IP address as the key. If NAT module uses the complete IP address as the query key, the subscriber will not be found.
bugs.impact: Logs contain UNKNOWN subscriber-id.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Subscriber ID queries using IPv6 address are now returning the subscriber-id.

bugs.title: 206 Partial Content responses from ramcache have malformed Content-Range header
bugs.symptoms: When ramcache serves a 206 Partial Content response from cache, the Content-Range header repeats the name: Content-Range: Content-Range: bytes 0-5/28
bugs.conditions: Request from client for partial document (Range header) against a virtual server with a web-acceleration profile having no applications (ramcache), where the requested document is present in ramcache.
bugs.impact: The client may mishandle the response, as the Content-Range header is malformed. This may cause additional traffic as the client may retrieve the entire document in a subsequent request due to the malformed response.
bugs.workaround: Remove the duplicate portion of the Content-Range header using an iRule at HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE time.
bugs.fix: The Content-Range header is now correctly formed for 206 Partial Content responses served from ramcache.

bugs.title: ICMP monitors may be marked down if packet-filter is set to discard or reject
bugs.symptoms: ICMP monitors may incorrectly mark pool members down if packet filters are used
bugs.conditions: 1. If an ICMP monitor is configured, as well as packet filters, and the default packet-filter action is Discard or Reject, and no rule exists to specifically allow the reply traffic, then the ICMP echo reply packets may be dropped, and the monitor will be marked down. 2. This can also be encountered by simply pinging the target from the BIG-IP command line.
bugs.impact: Monitors incorrectly mark the pool member down.
bugs.workaround: Either add a packet filter rule specifically allowing the return traffic, change the default packet filter behaviour to 'accept', or use a different type (non ICMP) of monitor.

bugs.title: Diameter MRF CER/DWR e2e=0, h2h=0 does not comply with RFC
bugs.symptoms: Diameter message routing framework sends Capabilities-Exchange-Request (CER)/Device-Watchdog-Request (DWR) with hop-by-hop (h2h) ID and end-to-end (e2e) ID set to 0 as the server.
bugs.conditions: Diameter Message Routing Framework (MRF) in use
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends CER and DWR to remote peers. However, the BIG-IP system sends e2e=0 and h2h=0 as the server ID in the CER and DWR requests. This does not comply with RFC 6733 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6733).
bugs.workaround: Use an DIAMETER_EGRESS iRule event to change the hop-by-hop ID and end-to-end server ID.

bugs.title: SSL in proxy shutdown case does not deliver server TCP FIN
bugs.symptoms: Connection is not torn down.
bugs.conditions: HTTPS server disconnects connection when in handshake.
bugs.impact: Potential resource exhaustion.
bugs.workaround: You can mitigate this condition in either of the following ways: -- Wait for system to clean up lingering connections. -- Use tmsh to clean up connections. (Note: Sometimes this might not work as expected depending on conditions.)
bugs.fix: SSL server side handles this error situation by sending out all remaining egress data and sending a shutdown signal to lower filters.

bugs.title: GUI TACACS+ remote server list should accept hostname
bugs.symptoms: Cannot add hostnames to the Remote - TACACS+ server list in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- On the System :: Users : Authentication page with Remote - TACACS+ specified. -- Add hostname to the server list.
bugs.impact: Validation does not accept a hostname. Cannot add hostname as a server.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to add a hostname.
bugs.fix: The system now allows hostname to be added with proper validation in this case.

bugs.title: Exporting profile/policy with pools from Common and importing to non-Common partitions might not work
bugs.symptoms: Exporting profile/policy with pools from the Common partition and importing to non-Common partitions might result in an error.
bugs.conditions: -- Profile/policy is in Common partition and has either: + A pool assigned to it directly via pool assign. + Uses an object that uses a pool (e.g., an Active Directory Server that has a pool configured pool). -- Importing to a non-Common partition configured with a Route Domain ID other than 0.
bugs.impact: Import operation does not complete. Cannot import profile/policy.
bugs.fix: %0 rd is added to IP addresses so when the policy is exported it explicitly refers to 0 RD, which allows for correct export and import of the profile/policy.

bugs.title: Some iSeries appliances can experience traffic disruption when the HA peer is upgraded from 12.1.3 and earlier to 13.1.0 or later.
bugs.symptoms: -- CPU core 0 can be seen utilizing 100% CPU. -- Other even cores may show a 40% increase in CPU usage. -- Pool monitors are seen flapping in /var/log/ltm. -- System posts the following messages: + In /var/log/ltm: - err tmm4[21025]: 01340004:3: HA Connection detected dissimilar peer: local npgs 1, remote npgs 1, local npus 8, remote npus 8, local pg 0, remote pg 0, local pu 4, remote pu 0. Connection will be aborted. + In /var/log/tmm: - notice DAGLIB: Invalid table size 12 - notice DAG: Failed to consume DAG data
bugs.conditions: -- Active unit on a pre-12.1.3.1 release. -- Standby peer upgraded to a 13.1.0 or later release. -- Device is an iSeries device (i5600 or later). Important: This issue may also affect iSeries HA peers on the same software version if the devices do not share the same model number. Note: Although this also occurs when upgrading to 12.1.3.8 and 13.0.x, the issue is not as severe.
bugs.impact: - High CPU usage. - Traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: Minimize impact on affected active devices by keeping the upgraded post-13.1.0 unit offline as long as possible before going directly to Active. For example, on a 12.1.3 unit to be upgraded (pre-upgrade): -- Run the following command: tmsh run sys failover offline persist -- Run the following command: tmsh save sys config -- Upgrade to 13.1.0.8. -- Unit comes back up on 13.1.0.8 as 'Forced Offline' and does not communicate with the active unit running 12.1.3 at all. -- Set up HA group and make sure the 12.1.3 Active unit's HA score is lower than 13.1.0.8. -- To cause the 13.1.0.8 unit to go directly to Active and take over traffic, run the following command on the unit running 13.1.0.8: tmsh run sys failover online At this point, the 12.1.3 unit starts to show symptoms of this issue, however, because it is no longer processing traffic, there is no cause for concern.
bugs.fix: This release introduces a new bigdb variable DAG.OverrideTableSize. To prevent the issue on an upgraded post-13.1.0 unit, set DAG.OverrideTableSize to 3. In order to return the system to typical CPU usage, you must set the db variable, and then restart tmm by running the following command: bigstart restart tmm (Restarting tmm is required for 13.1.1.2 and newer 13.1.1.x releases.) Note: Because the restart is occurring on the Standby unit, no traffic is disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: iSession hudfilter initialization fails when apm-forwarding-server-tcp profile is used.
bugs.symptoms: When either apm-forwarding-client-tcp or apm-forwarding-server-tcp profile is used on virtual server, which includes connectivity profile, traffic hitting the virtual server may be reset.
bugs.conditions: -- Using apm-forwarding-client-tcp or apm-forwarding-server-tcp profiles. -- Virtual server that also includes connectivity profile.
bugs.impact: When the virtual server processes traffic, the traffic is reset.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the these TCP profiles on virtual servers that also include a connectivity profile. In general using these profiles is not recommended, since these are intended to be used on APM internal virtual servers.

bugs.title: ProxySSL leaks profile reference
bugs.symptoms: Proxy SSL leaks server SSL profile references whenever a virtual server is uninitialized or reinitialized.
bugs.conditions: -- One or more Client SSL profiles are in use -- SSL profile has the 'Proxy SSL' (proxy-ssl) setting enabled. -- The profile is re-initialized; this can occur when a profile is modified.
bugs.impact: Memory leaks. Tmm can crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: The tmrouted repeatedly crashes and produces core when new peer device is added
bugs.symptoms: There is a tmrouted crash when new peer device is added.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Core produced. Tmrouted crashes repeatedly. Dynamic routing for all route domains is temporarily disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Have MCP force load as described in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030).

bugs.title: BIG-IP may attempt to write to an out of bounds memory location, causing the bd daemon to crash.
bugs.symptoms: The bd daemon crashes
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned and passing traffic -- Other conditions are unknown
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.
bugs.fix: A possible out of bounds write was fixed.

bugs.title: Merged can use %100 of CPU if all stats snapshot files are in the future
bugs.symptoms: Merged uses %100 of CPU if it cannot remove the oldest snapshot file, due to all snapshot files having timestamps in the future.
bugs.conditions: All stats snapshot file having timestamps in the future, release has the fix for issue 721740, but not this issue.
bugs.impact: Merged using %100 of the CPU.
bugs.workaround: Remove snapshot stats files that have timestamps in the future and restart merged.
bugs.fix: Correctly exit cleanup logic when all stats snapshot files have timestamps in the future.

bugs.title: False-positive illegal-length violation can appear
bugs.symptoms: A false-positive illegal-length violation.
bugs.conditions: A chunked request where the request length is more than half of the configured max-request length.
bugs.impact: False-positive illegal-length violation.
bugs.workaround: Configure a higher max request length violation.
bugs.fix: Fixed a false-positive request-length violation.

bugs.title: 'Detection Evasion' violations might not report violation details in their reports or in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Evasion technique details are not presented in the request log.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in either of the following scenarios: -- Many evasion techniques occur in a single request. -- The evasion techniques that occur are not set as enabled in the policy configuration.
bugs.impact: 'Detection Evasion' attacks are reported the logs, but there are no violation details to help clarify what actually triggered.

bugs.title: Difficulty in selection from large numbers of iRules for Virtual Server configuration
bugs.symptoms: Users who wish to select large numbers of iRules for an individual virtual server may find difficulty in locating and selecting iRules because of the relatively small size of the control on the page.
bugs.conditions: A user has a large number of iRules configured and wishes to select one or more iRules for an individual virtual server.
bugs.impact: A user may have difficulty finding their desired iRule(s).
bugs.workaround: iControl REST or TMSH

bugs.title: TMM may leak memory when SSL certificates with VDI or EAM in use
bugs.symptoms: TMM 'method' memory usage grows over time when VDI and serverssl *or* EAM and clientssl are configured on the same VIP.
bugs.conditions: One or both of the following: -- VDI and serverssl are configured on the same VIP -- EAM and clientssl are configured on the same VIP
bugs.impact: TMM memory usage grows over time leading to eventual performance degradation and potential traffic outage if TMM cores.
bugs.workaround: No workaround short of not using these combinations of features.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer leaks memory when VDI and serverssl *or* EAM and clientssl are configured together on the same VIP.

bugs.title: Logon page modification fails to sync to standby
bugs.symptoms: Changes in the login page of VPE do not sync to standby.
bugs.conditions: 1. You make changes to the logon page on the active device, making changes to the username or any other field on the login page of VPE. 2. You sync to standby, and it succeeds.
bugs.impact: When you access in standby device, the customization error failure message appears, and the dialog fails to open in VPE. You cannot see the changes made on the active device from standby device.
bugs.workaround: Do not make changes to fields on the login page.
bugs.fix: Changes in the login page of VPE now sync to standby.

bugs.title: "tmsh show sys hardware" shows blade part number instead of chassis part number
