bugs.symptoms: Near the end of the output of "tmsh show sys hardware", it will display "System Information" like the following: System Information Type A112 Chassis Serial chs500264s Level 200/400 Part 400-0039-03 REV B For a chassis based platform, the "Level 200/400 Part" will display the blade part number instead of the chassis part number.
bugs.conditions: This always happens on a chassis based platform. It does not affect appliance.
bugs.impact: It is cosmetic. This does not affect regular traffic at all.
bugs.fix: The root cause has been identified, and will be fixed in the future.

bugs.title: Per-Request Policy may require enabling SSL Forward Proxy Bypass
bugs.symptoms: For some SSL/TLS traffic, the per-request policy does not complete, leading to hanging connections and/or connection resets.
bugs.conditions: Reproducible with any forward proxy configuration involving per-request policies. This includes Secure Web Gateway (SWG) and SSL Orchestrator (SSLO). To reproduce, the SSL Forward Proxy Bypass feature must be disabled in the client and server SSL profiles. This is equivalent to 'always intercept'.
bugs.impact: Policy execution may stall. Clients may experience hanging connections and/or connection resets.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following procedure: 1. Enable the SSL Forward Proxy Bypass feature in the client and server SSL profiles. 2. Set the default action to 'Intercept'.
bugs.fix: Now policy execution for per-request policies in SWG and SSLO use cases work properly when SSL Forward Proxy Bypass is not enabled.

bugs.title: SIP Response routing fails under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: SIP Response is not sent to the client.
bugs.conditions: -- 'honor-via' is enabled. -- SIP Client sends a SIP Request. -- SIP client connection is closed.
bugs.impact: Honor via results in routing the message to the next VIA entry but does not have enough information to route the message. SIP Response is not forwarded to the client.
bugs.fix: Now, the information needed to connect to the originating device is available, so the SIP Response can be forwarded to the client. There is a small CPU performance penalty with this fix and throughput may be affected if CPU usage is already near 100%.

bugs.title: No "Loading..." feedback when updating DoS Application profile
bugs.symptoms: When updating a DoS Application profile or cancelling changes, the GUI does not print the "Loading..." graphic at the top of the page. No feedback is provided.
bugs.conditions: Working with the DoS Application profile when ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: No feedback is provided possibly causing the administrator's confusion when updating the profile.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The DoS Application profile GUI now shows the "Loading..." message at the top of the page when updating the profile or cancelling changes.

bugs.title: TMM crash after changing LSN pool mode from PBA to NAPT
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes after changing LSN pool mode from PBA to NAPT when long lived connections are killed due to the PBA block lifetime and zombie timeout expiring.
bugs.conditions: An LSN pool using PBA mode with a block lifetime and zombie timeout set and long lived connections.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Instead of changing the LSN pool mode from PBA to NAPT, create a new LSN pool configured for NAPT and change the source-address-translation pool on the virtual servers that use the PBA pool. The PBA pool can be deleted after the virtual servers are no longer using it.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes after changing LSN pool mode from PBA to NAPT.

bugs.title: Standby device goes active during UCS restore after default config is loaded and a serial cable is used for failover
bugs.symptoms: Standby device goes active during UCS restore after default config is loaded.
bugs.conditions: High-availability-configured BIG-IP devices that use a serial cable for failover. On the standby device: -- The default config is loaded. -- A UCS is subsequently loaded.
bugs.impact: Traffic erroneously fails over to the BIG-IP device that has the UCS loaded. Traffic subsequently fails back to the original BIG-IP device after the device that erroneously went Active senses the serial cable being asserted from the other device.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: BGP 'capability graceful-restart' for peer-group not properly advertised when configured
bugs.symptoms: BGP neighbor using peer-group with 'capability graceful-restart' enabled (which is the default). However, on the system, peer-group defaults to disable. Because there is no config statement to enable 'capability graceful-restart' after restart, it gets turned off after config load, which also turns it off for any BGP neighbor using it.
bugs.conditions: - Neighbor configured to use peer-group. - Peer-group configured with capability graceful-restart, but with the default: disabled.
bugs.impact: Because peer-group is set to disable by default, and there is no operation to enable it after restart, 'capability graceful-restart' gets turned off after config load, and neighbors using it from peer-group get turned off as well.
bugs.workaround: Re-issue the commands to set peer-group 'capability graceful-restart' and 'clear ip bgp *' to reset BGP neighbors.
bugs.fix: The peer-group now has 'capability graceful-restart' enabled by default, so this issue no longer occurs.
bugs.behavior: In this release, peer-group has 'capability graceful-restart' enabled by default.

bugs.title: The IKEv1 racoon daemon can crash on multiple INVALID-SPI payloads
bugs.symptoms: When an IKEv1 peer sends an INVALID-SPI payload, and BIG-IP system cannot find the phase-two Security Association (SA) for that SPI but can find phase-one SA involved; the racoon daemon may crash if there are additional INVALID-SPI payloads afterward.
bugs.conditions: -- An INVALID-SPI notification is received. -- That phase-two SA is already gone. -- The phase-one parent SA is still around. -- Subsequent notification INVALID-SPI payloads involve the same phase-one SA.
bugs.impact: The v1 racoon daemon cores, interrupting traffic until new tunnels can be established after racoon restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The system no longer destroys the parent phase-one SA when an INVALID-SPI notification cannot find the target phase-two SA, so this issue does not occur.

bugs.title: Suggest breaking up the API protection profile into multiple in case large number of paths like 12k in the OpenAPI specification file
bugs.symptoms: Restjavad runs out of heap and reports an out-of-memory exception while parsing a large number of paths in the OpenAPI specification file.
bugs.conditions: A large number of paths (e.g., 12 KB) in the OpenAPI Specification File.
bugs.impact: Cannot upload a large number of paths in a OpenAPI specification file. restjavad reports an out-of-memory exception.
bugs.workaround: Break the specification file into multiple, create multiple profiles.
bugs.fix: Break OpenAPI Specification File into multiple files, and create multiple profiles.

bugs.title: L2 transparent VLAN group based deployments require configuration of a transparent next hop per virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Configuration overhead that requires configuration of a virtual server per VLAN group.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system deployed in an L2 transparent mode using VLAN groups.
bugs.impact: Configuration overhead to configure virtual server per VLAN group.
bugs.fix: Prevent the need to configure a virtual server per VLAN group.

bugs.title: BIG-IP fails to load MCPD due to empty bigip.conf after the UCS save/load and reboot ???
bugs.symptoms: After saving/loading the UCS and rebooting, the BIG-IP system may end up in a state where the bigip.conf file is empty. This can cause MCPD to fail to load. Error logs have shown that MCPD is waiting without receiving a response, and the system configuration cannot be loaded due to the missed user configuration.
bugs.conditions: Occurs intermittently after UCS save/load operations followed by reboots or toggling the BIG-IP. The bigip.conf file ends up empty, while the bigip.conf.bak remains intact.
bugs.impact: MCPD fails to load, causing the BIG-IP system inoperative until the configuration is restored from backup (bigip.conf.bak), resulting in downtime

bugs.title: sp-connector is not being deleted together with profile
bugs.symptoms: If a profile is connected to an SSO SAML IdP configuration with an SP connector, the sp-connector is not available for delete when the profile is deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- Profile is connected to an SSO SAML IdP configuration with an SP connector. -- Deleting the profile and attempting to delete the sp-connector.
bugs.impact: The SP connector is not listed for delete when the profile is deleted.
bugs.workaround: To delete the SP connector, run the following command: tmsh delete apm sso saml-sp-connector NAME
bugs.fix: SP connectors are now available for delete when profile is deleted.

bugs.title: Policy change with newly enforced signatures causes sig collection failure in other policies
bugs.symptoms: An ASM policy change with newly enforced signatures causes a signature collection failure in all other policies.
bugs.conditions: An ASM policy is changed by adding newly enforced signatures.
bugs.impact: Signature collection failures are logged for all other policies.
bugs.workaround: For each other policy on the device, make a spurious change (such as modifying policy description and saving) and apply the policy. Alternatively, a new user-defined signature which would be included in enforcement can be spuriously added and then immediately removed.

bugs.title: AFM TCP Half Open vector might show mitigation when that is not happening
bugs.symptoms: In AFM, it is possible that the device-level TCP Half Open vector will show int_drops when actually LTM per-vlan syncookie is mitigating the attack.
bugs.conditions: When AFM is enabled and LTM per-vlan syncookie is doing HW syncookies.
bugs.impact: Stats could be misleading.
bugs.workaround: You can turn off the AFM TCP half Open vector.
bugs.fix: Now, we will only show the TCP half Open stats when we are actually mitigating through TCP half Open vector.

bugs.title: The autodosd process does not support multiple traffic-group
bugs.symptoms: The autodosd process supports only the default traffic-group 'traffic-group-1'.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when there are multiple traffic-groups in high availability (HA) environment.
bugs.impact: The autodosd process works only for the default traffic-group traffic-group-1.
bugs.fix: The autodosd process now supports multiple traffic-group in high availability (HA) environment.

bugs.title: Incorrect prefix of ICMP error messages in NAT64
bugs.symptoms: When ICMPv4 error messages are returned for NAT64 connections, the source address of the ICMPv6-translated error message uses ::ffff as the IPv6 prefix, creating an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address.
bugs.conditions: -- NAT64 enabled. -- ICMPv4 error messages are returned from IPv4 hosts and routers.
bugs.impact: The ICMP error messages cannot be routed to the client and are dropped by intermediate routers. This can prevent clients from properly detecting errors such as unreachable hosts and networks. This causes failures in utilities such as ping and traceroute.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The ICMPv4 error messages are correctly translated to ICMPv6.

bugs.title: HTTP monitors fail to be persisted if Alias Address includes a route domain
bugs.symptoms: HTTP monitors fail to be persisted.
bugs.conditions: -- The monitor is of HTTP type. -- Its Alias Address includes a route domain.
bugs.impact: Saving the monitor returns an 'Invalid IP' error message.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create and update an HTTP monitor whose address includes a route domain.
bugs.fix: HTTP monitors with an Alias Address that includes a route domain are persisted as expected.

bugs.title: Users may get blocked on Web Scraping or CAPTCHA
bugs.symptoms: Some users may get falsely blocked under the Web Scraping violation. Similarly, some users may fail to pass the CAPTCHA challenge when triggered by Brute Force Mitigation, DoSL7 Mitigation, or Proactive Bot Defense.
bugs.conditions: Either: - Web Scraping is enabled with Bot Detection set to alarm or to block (13.1.x/14.0.x). - CAPTCHA mitigation is in use due to another suspicious activity, triggered by Brute Force Mitigation, DoSL7 Mitigation, or Proactive Bot Defense (14.0.x).
bugs.impact: Some legitimate users may get blocked.
bugs.workaround: Running these commands may prevent these browsers from getting blocked: -- /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ws_cshui_susp_event_bot_score 0 -- bigstart restart asm This disables one of the tests that cause the false positive.
bugs.fix: Fixed false detection of some users as bots causing them to be blocked by Web Scraping or CAPTCHA.

bugs.title: Automatic policy learning is slower when there are thousands of policies
bugs.symptoms: Policy learning takes longer than previous versions when there are thousands of policies.
bugs.conditions: -- Specific load over thousands of policies. -- Automatic policy building. -- Requests do not have violations.
bugs.impact: It takes longer for the system learn all the policies.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, set the following variable to 100: pb_sampling_high_cpu_load Note: The default is 10, which gets 10 sampled requests. Setting the value to 100 impacts performance. (Note: The parameter name is misleading, as the variable does not relate to CPU load.)
bugs.fix: Issue is mitigated in this release. The policies get learned slower in 14.0.x and later, on systems with a high load of legal traffic and many policies. What took an hour to learn in previous versions might take several hours. You can use the internal parameter, pb_sampling_high_cpu_load, to adjust this. (Note: The parameter name is misleading, as the variable does not relate to CPU load.)

bugs.title: URL suggestion is still explicit though it should be *.[Jj][Ss]
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected URL suggestion populated for explicit URL even though URL's Filetype is defined in list: 'File types for which wildcard HTTP URLs will be configured (e.g. *.jpg)'.
bugs.conditions: Adding a Filetype to the 'File types for which wildcard HTTP URLs will be configured (e.g. *.jpg)' list after first traffic for specific URL with that Filetype arrived (problem persists even if suggestions is deleted).
bugs.impact: Unexpected URL suggestion populated for explicit URL when it should not.
bugs.workaround: - Ignore the suggestion (use the ignore button). - Restart policy builder (run the command pabnagd).
bugs.fix: When adding a new Filetype to the 'File types for which wildcard HTTP URLs will be configured (e.g. *.jpg)' list, once the first traffic for an explicit URL with a suggestion arrives, the explicit URL suggestion will be deleted and a wildcard URL suggestion for matching Filetype will be created.

bugs.title: TMSH improvements
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMSH usage, including via iControl, may lead to excessive resource consumption.
bugs.conditions: Authorized users making queries or updates via TMSH or iControl
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.

bugs.title: Network Map summary counts pool members more than once if they are shared across pools
bugs.symptoms: On the page at Local Traffic :: Network Map, in the summary view, the total number of pool members shows a larger number if there are pool members referenced by multiple pools.
bugs.conditions: -- Network Map summary view. -- Pool members referenced by multiple pools.
bugs.impact: The number of pools value is higher than the actual number of pools because of how the system tracks a single pool member referenced in multiple pools.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Redirection to logon summary page does not occur after session timeout
bugs.symptoms: After a BIG-IP Administrator user session times out, the user is not automatically redirected to the logon summary page, despite being configured to do so.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is configured to redirect to the logon summary page immediately after logging in, using the following db variable: ui.users.redirectsuperuserstoauthsummary = true -- The BIG-IP Administrator users' session automatically times out.
bugs.impact: The system does not comply with government security requirements that BIG-IP Administrator users be sent automatically to the logon summary. BIG-IP Administrator users must manually navigate to the logon summary page
bugs.workaround: Manually navigate to the logon summary page.

bugs.title: BGP neighbor peer-group config element not persisting
bugs.symptoms: neighbor peer-group configuration element not persisting after restart
bugs.conditions: - dynamic routing enabled - BGP neighbor configured with peer-group - BIG-IP or tmrouted daemon restart
bugs.impact: BGP peer-group configuration elements don't persist
bugs.workaround: Reconfigure BGP neighbor peer-group after restart
bugs.fix: BGP neighbor peer-group configuration is properly save to configuration, and persists after restart

bugs.title: RAM Cache traffic fails on B2150
bugs.symptoms: Rendering pages from RAM Cache fails. System does not pass RAM Cache traffic on B2150 platform.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION B2150 blade. -- Attempting to pass traffic from RAM Cache.
bugs.impact: B2150 does not pass any RAM Cache traffic.
bugs.fix: RAM Cache traffic now succeeds on B2150.

bugs.title: New and improved infrastructure for BDoS to share learned traffic characteristics within the device group/cluster setup.
bugs.symptoms: BDoS feature (AFM/DHD) needs to share learned traffic characteristics across nodes (within a cluster) and across devices (within the device group). Previous infrastructure used by BDOS could cause spikes in disk usage due to a large number of snapshot files being saved under /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d partition.
bugs.conditions: BDOS feature is enabled on at least 1 context (either at global context or at least 1 virtual server).
bugs.impact: The /config partition on the BIG-IP system consistently fills up with large numbers of directories/files under /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d, eventually causing system to run out of disk space under /config partition.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, manually delete files/directories filling up under /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d partition to free up disk space.
bugs.fix: BDOS now uses a new (and improved) infrastructure for sharing data across nodes/devices (within device group/cluster setup) that does not require snapshot files to be maintained under /config/filestore/ partition.

bugs.title: Unable to access BIG-IP Configuration Utility when BIG-IP system is behind a Reverse proxy
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP management interface is accessed through a Reverse Proxy, you cannot login to the Configuration Utility. Instead the system presents a blank page, as the Reverse Proxy IP/hostname is in the Referer header instead of that of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: You are accessing the BIG-IP Configuration Utility through a Reverse Proxy.
bugs.impact: You are unable to login to the Configuration Utility.
bugs.workaround: Configure their Reverse Proxy to place the IP address of the BIG-IP system in the Referer header.

bugs.title: ACCESS::session iRule commands may not work in serverside events
bugs.symptoms: -- 'ACCESS::session sid' will returns empty. -- 'ACCESS::session data get <varname>' returns empty.
bugs.conditions: -- Using IP-based sessions -- ACCESS::session iRule commands in a serverside iRule event, such as HTTP_PROXY_CONNECT. -- Using SSL Bypass. Note: This issue is known to occur when using SSL Bypass, but this is not the only configuration that exhibits the problem.
bugs.impact: iRules may not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The ACCESS::session iRules now work in serverside events when doing IP-based sessions.

bugs.title: Reduce the impact of the Dynamic Script Removal Detection loading time
bugs.symptoms: In some specific cases, Dynamic Script Removal Detection loading times impact can be meaningful.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic Script Removal Detection enabled.
bugs.impact: Loading times might be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Remove the problematic methods using the FPS GUI.

bugs.title: ASM Sync does not work when the configsync IP address is an IPv6 address
bugs.symptoms: If the configsync IP address of the device is configured to be an IPv6 address, changes in ASM configuration do not synchronize across the cluster.
bugs.conditions: Devices in a Device Group have an IPv6 address set as their configsync IP address.
bugs.impact: ASM configuration does not synchronize across the Device Group.
bugs.workaround: Set the configsync IP address to be an IPv4 address and restart the asm_config_server process. To restart the asm_config_server process, run the following command: pkill -f asm_config_server

bugs.title: Key creation on Thales fails with thales 12.40 on tmm interface
bugs.symptoms: The key creation is failing for Thales 12.40 installed on tmm interface on BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when creating keys using tmsh on Thales 12.40 via the tmm interface on BIG-IP
bugs.impact: You cannot create any keys/certs on Thales.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: The fix is included which fixes this intermittent key creation failure on Thales 12.40.

bugs.title: v11.x versions GTM VS status depends on the ltm vs iRule pool availability
bugs.symptoms: GTM VS status should depend on default pool status only. But v11.x versions GTM VS status depends on the availability of the pool used in the ltm VS iRule.
bugs.conditions: LTM VS having a iRule which contains a pool command.
bugs.impact: GTM VS status is marked incorrectly.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using pool command in the iRule.

bugs.title: bd crash.
bugs.symptoms: bd might crash when enabling a specific internal parameter used for debugging.
bugs.conditions: The internal param pb_force_sampling is enabled. Note: This internal parameter is used to debug the system and is not needed for use in production environments.
bugs.impact: bd crashes.
bugs.workaround: Do not enable pb_force_sampling. There is no need for it in normal operations.
bugs.fix: Fixed a possible crash scenario with an internal parameter.

bugs.title: tmm may crash at startup if the configuration load fails
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, tmm may crash at startup if the configuration load fails.
bugs.conditions: This might occur after a configuration loading failure during startup, when TMM might take longer than usual to be ready.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes at startup if the configuration load fails.

bugs.title: It is possible for DNSX to serve partial zone information for a short period of time
bugs.symptoms: During zone transfers into DNS Express, partial zone data may be available until the transfer completes.
bugs.conditions: -- Two zones being transferred during the same time period + zone1.example.net + zone2.example.net -- Transfer of zone1 has started, but not finished. -- zone2 starts a transfer and finishes before zone1 finishes, meaning that the database might be updated with all of the zone2 data, and only part of the zone1 data.
bugs.impact: Partial zone data will be served, including possible NXDOMAIN or NODATA messages. This happens until zone1 finishes and saves to the database, at which time both zones' data will be complete and correct.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to limit the number of concurrent transfers to 1. However this severely limits the ability of DNS Express to update zones in a timely fashion if there are many zones and many updates.
bugs.fix: All zone transfers are now staged until they are complete. The zone transfer data is then saved to the database. Only when the zone data has completed updating to the database will the data be available to queries.

bugs.title: After entering username and before password, the logging on user's failure count is incremented.
bugs.symptoms: Listing login failures (i.e., using the following command: 'tmsh show auth login-failures') shows a failed login for the user who is currently logging in via console or SSH.
bugs.conditions: -- A user is logging in via console or SSH. -- Between the time the system presents the password prompt and the user enters the password. Note: This does not apply to GUI or iControl REST logins.
bugs.impact: If many logins for the same user get to this state simultaneously, it may be enough to exceed a specified lockout threshold, locking the user out.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than using the GUI or iControl REST to log in to the system.

bugs.title: HTTP Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) headers not being added to all APM generated files
bugs.symptoms: HTTP Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) headers are missing for some APM-generated files.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- HTTP profile is configured with HSTS enabled. -- HTTP GET requests for APM renderer files, including CSS, JS, and image files from the webtop.
bugs.impact: Without these headers, the user agent (browser) may switch to non-secure communication.
bugs.fix: When the HTTP profile is configured with HSTS enabled, all APM renderer files are now sent with HSTS headers.

bugs.title: Fingerprint cookie large value may result in tmm core.
bugs.symptoms: The JavaScript component calculates part of the fingerprint cookie value. In some rare cases, large values are generated and may result in tmm core.
bugs.conditions: A large value (more than 35 characters) inside the fingerprint cookie.
bugs.impact: Memory overrun, tmm core in some cases.
bugs.fix: FPS will check the value and truncate it if it exceeds the maximum length.

bugs.title: local-db PEM Subscriber Activity log missing
bugs.symptoms: PEM subscriber activity log is empty when published to local database.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM subscriber activity log is configured. -- The endpoint is local-db.
bugs.impact: Missing activity logs for external server.
bugs.workaround: Configure the destination as local-syslog publisher.
bugs.fix: PEM Subscriber Activity log is now populated.

bugs.title: URLCAT doesn't work when we have uppercase characters in feedlist
bugs.symptoms: A URL does not get classified when there are uppercase characters in the feedlist.
bugs.conditions: Using uppercase characters in the feedlist.
bugs.impact: URL is not classified as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Kern.log contains many messages: warning kernel: Tracklist initialized; Tracklist destroyed
bugs.symptoms: There may be a large number of messages in /var/log/kern.log similar to the following: Tracklist initialized Tracklist destroyed
bugs.conditions: This can happen when vCMP is provisioned, which enables SR-IOV mode.
bugs.impact: It causes messages to show up in /var/log/kern.log, but does not affect traffic. This is a cosmetic issue and does not indicate a functionality issue.
bugs.fix: Tracklist is now disabled, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: User with Certificate Manager role is unable to archive certificates using GUI and iControlSOAP
bugs.symptoms: Unable to archive certificates or keys using GUI and iControlSOAP.
bugs.conditions: When the user is in Certificate Manager role.
bugs.impact: Unable to backup certificates or keys.
bugs.workaround: The user in Certificate Manager role is still be able to export the key and see its PEM string. So you can manually create an archive file by copying the PEM string into a file.
bugs.fix: User with Certificate Manager role is now able to archive certificates using GUI and iControlSOAP

bugs.title: IKEv1: The 4-byte 'Non-ESP Marker' may be missing in some IKE messages
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system might fail to re-establish an IKEv1 phase 1 security association (ISAKMP-SA) when the Initiator starts the exchange using UDP port 4500. The exchange progresses to the point of NAT detection, whereupon the BIG-IP system stops using the Non-ESP marker and sends malformatted ISAKMP.
bugs.conditions: All of the following must be true: -- The BIG-IP system is an IKEv1 Responder. -- ISAKMP phase 1 negotiation starts on UDP port 4500. -- NAT is detected on only one side during the phase 1 exchange.
bugs.impact: -- Establishment of an ISAKMP-SA will fail until the peer device switches to UDP port 500. -- The remote peer may send INVALID-SPI messages quoting SPI numbers that do not exist.
bugs.workaround: To help workaround this issue, you can try the following: -- Make sure the BIG-IP system is always the Initiator. -- Bypass NAT. -- Configure both the BIG-IP system and remote peer to use address IDs that are not the same as the IP addresses used in the ISAKMP exchange, thus causing the BIG-IP system to think there is NAT on both sides.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now keeps the Non-ESP marker when NAT is detected.

bugs.title: Disallow hard links to svpn log files
bugs.symptoms: svpn log files may not be created with the expected access restrictions.
bugs.conditions: File system access to svpn log file destinations.
bugs.impact: svpn log files are not restricted as expected.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that only authorized users have filesystem access to svpn log file destinations, such as a user's home directory.
bugs.fix: Ensure that log files are created with the desired restrictions.

bugs.title: Error in APM Hosted Content when set to public access
bugs.symptoms: Error when rendering APM Hosted content when set to public access.
bugs.conditions: APM enabled Hosted content enabled Hosted content set to public access
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output in webtop pages
bugs.workaround: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { ACCESS::restrict_irule_events disable } when HTTP_REQUEST { if {[HTTP::uri] starts_with "/vdesk/resource_info_v2.xml?" && [URI::decode [HTTP::query]] contains "<"} { HTTP::uri [HTTP::path] } }

bugs.title: Use of TCP Verified Accept can disable server-side flow control
bugs.symptoms: Unexpectedly high memory usage, aggressive sweeper messages, TCP memory pressure messages in logs.
bugs.conditions: Verified Accept is enabled in TCP profiles that are associated with virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory usage.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling Verified Accept.
bugs.fix: Fixed server-side flow control.

bugs.title: End users using virtual keyboard might be blocked during clientside features
bugs.symptoms: End users using a virtual keyboard may be blocked when being challenge with CAPTCHA or when Web Scraping or Bot Defense profile are enabled.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when end users use virtual keyboard, and one of the following: -- End users are being challenged with CAPTCHA mitigation on ASM policy or DoS profile (v14.0.0 or later). -- Web Scraping with Bot Detection is configured (v13.1.0 or later).
bugs.impact: User using a virtual keyboard might be blocked.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: sticky_id in fingerprint cookie sometimes contains large value
bugs.symptoms: Fingerprint cookie contains a large value. Intermittently, when the cookie is not sync, the fingerprint cookie might contain a larger number of characters than 13.
bugs.conditions: The cookie is not sync.
bugs.impact: Fingerprint cookie contains a value larger than the expected 13 characters.
bugs.fix: fingerprint cookie always contains 13 characters.

bugs.title: Apply Policy and Upgrade time degradation when there are previous enforced rules
bugs.symptoms: When there are previously enforced rules present in the system, the time to apply changes made to a policy, and the time to upgrade the configuration to a new version suffers.
bugs.conditions: -- Signature Staging is enabled. -- Updated Signature Enforcement is set to 'Retain previous rule enforcement and place updated rule in staging'. -- Signatures are enforced on a policy. -- A new ASM Signature Update is installed, which modifies the matching rule for some enforced signatures.
bugs.impact: The time to apply changes made to a policy, and the time to upgrade the configuration to a new version, suffers from a inefficiently performing query related to the existence of previously enforced rules.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Query indexing and performance is fixed: Apply Policy executes in the same time whether there are previously enforced rules in the system or not. Enforcing all signatures in a set now correctly removes the previously enforced rule from the signature.

bugs.title: [GTM] load or save configs removes backslash \ from GTM pool member name
bugs.symptoms: GTM config fails to load, and posts an error similar to the following: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip_gtm.conf at line: 47) the "create" command does not accept wildcard configuration identifiers
bugs.conditions: GTM server virtual server name contains a backslash (\) character.
bugs.impact: GTM config fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Edit bigip_gtm.conf manually and add the \ character. Important: The system removes the \ (which results in further validation failures) in response to any of the following actions: -- Load the GTM config. -- Make changes to the GTM config, and you or the system saves it. -- cpcfg operation. -- Upgrade the system.

bugs.title: Enabling 'default-information originate' on one of the several OSPF processes does not inject a default route into others.
bugs.symptoms: The use case is the following: |OSPF 1|---|Network1|------[|OSPF process 1|---BIG-IP system---|OSPF process 2|]-----|Network2|---|OSPF 2| Attempting to redistribute default route received from OSPF process that is peering with the Internet to OSPF process 2. However, if that route is removed (e.g., an Internet link goes down), OSPF process 2 removes the associated route and the 'default-information originate' command is the ideal choice, because as long as the OSPF process 1 default route is in the routing table, the default route is redistributed into OSPF process 2. If that route is gone, OSPF process 2 immediately removes it from routing table. Enabling 'default-information originate' on OSPF process 2 does not affect the outcome, and a default route is not injected like it should be.
bugs.conditions: -- On the BIG-IP system, OSPF routing protocol is enabled on a route-domain. -- Routing configuration example: OSPF router config examples: *** OSPF 1: !router ospf 1 ospf router-id 10.13.0.7 redistribute ospf network 10.13.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 default-information originate OSPF 2: router ospf 1 ospf router-id 10.14.0.5 redistribute ospf network 10.14.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 BIG-IP system: router ospf 1 ospf router-id 10.13.0.2 network 10.13.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 router ospf 2 ospf router-id 10.14.0.9 network 10.14.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 *** -- Enable 'default-information originate' on BIG-IP OSPF process 2 should allow OSPF process 2 to receive advertised default route from BIG-IP OSPF process 1 if such exists. # expected OSPF routers configuration on the BIG-IP system: router ospf 1 ospf router-id 10.13.0.2 network 10.13.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 router ospf 2 ospf router-id 10.14.0.9 network 10.14.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 default-information originate
bugs.impact: A default route from OSPF process 1 is not advertised into OSPF process 2 routing table.
bugs.fix: Enabling 'default-information originate' on OSPF process 2 forces OSPF process 2 to receive a default route from OSPF process 1 if such exists.

bugs.title: State Mirroring between BIG-IP 13.0.x and 13.1.x systems may cause TMM core on standby system during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP devices running 13.0.x (13.0.x or a 13.0.x point release) and 13.1.x software versions in a High-Availability (HA) configuration with state mirroring enabled may cause a standby system to produce a TMM core file.
bugs.conditions: -- State mirroring configured on two or more BIG-IP systems (state mirroring is enabled by default). -- For VIPRION clusters or VIPRION-based vCMP guests, the systems are configured to mirror 'Between Clusters'. -- The active system is running v13.0.x, and the standby system is running v13.1.x, e.g., as a result of an in-progress upgrade.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash on a standby system during upgrade. This issue should not disrupt traffic, because the TMM is coring only on the standby unit.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue, disable State Mirroring prior to upgrading, and re-enable it once both devices are running v13.1.x, or complete the upgrade of both devices to v13.1.x. 1. You can disable mirroring using either the GUI or the command line. 1a. In the GUI: -- Set the Primary and Secondary Local Mirror Address configurations to 'None' under Device Management :: Devices :: [Self] device :: Mirroring Configuration. 1b. From the command-line: -- Run the following command: tmsh modify cm device <name-of-self-device> mirror-ip any6 mirror-secondary-ip any6 && tmsh save sys config Important: This action results in connection state loss on failover. 2. Once all devices are running the same software version, re-enable state mirroring by re-adding the device mirror IPs removed previously. Note: F5 recommends that BIG-IP systems run with the same software version on all devices.
bugs.fix: TMM on standby no longer cores during upgrade.

bugs.title: Protocol Inspection user interface elements are active but do not work
bugs.symptoms: Protocol Inspection (PI) user interface options are present, but are not applied to traffic. Protocol Inspection (PI) now requires the presence of either an add-on subscription or an AFM standalone license for any of the features to work. A 'Good' or 'Better' license does not activate the PI features. The Configuration Utility still allows you to configure inspection profiles, compliance checks, and signatures, but they are not applied to traffic. There is no feedback that they are not applied.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM licensed and provisioned through 'Good' or 'Better' license, but no add-on subscription license for Protocol Inspection. Alternately, AFM licensed as an add-on module to another module (typically LTM). -- PI profile configured and applied to a virtual server or referenced in a firewall rule in an active firewall policy.
bugs.impact: If you previously had Protocol Inspection configured without the add-on license installed, the features are no longer applied to traffic until the add-on license is obtained. However, the GUI options remain active.

bugs.title: iControl REST input sanitization
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST worker input sanitization issue.
bugs.conditions: iControl REST worker service running on BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: iControl REST and tmsh
bugs.fix: Improved iControl REST worker input sanitization.

bugs.title: iControl REST input sanitization
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST worker input sanitization issue.
bugs.conditions: iControl REST worker service running on BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: iControl REST and TMSH
bugs.fix: Improved iControl REST worker input sanitization.

bugs.title: AVR DoS Attack report misses virtual server name in a specific config
bugs.symptoms: DoS AVR Report GUI page is under: Navigate to Security :: Reporting : DoS : Network The report shows the attack, but categorizes the attack under 'Aggregated' in the Virtual Server name value, rather than the actual name of the Virtual Server on which the attack is happening.
bugs.conditions: -- A Virtual Server is configured with a IP/Subnet range. For example, -- Virtual Server with Destination Address: 10.10.10.0/27 (meaning the destination range is 10.10.10.32 - 10.10.10.63). -- Destination Address of the Client Traffic and Attack: 10.10.10.63 View AVR Reporting, which does not resolve the to any specific Virtual Server, but instead categorizes the attack as 'Aggregate'.
bugs.impact: AVR report missing the Virtual Server information.

bugs.title: Apmd leaks memory when executing per-session policy via iRule
bugs.symptoms: Apmd leaks memory when executing per-session policy via iRule.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is licensed and provisioned. -- Per-session policy is executed via iRules or APM-based System Authentication is used.
bugs.impact: Apmd leaks memory.
bugs.fix: Apmd no longer leaks memory when per-session policy is executed via Rules.

bugs.title: Handle x520 PF DOWN/UP sequence automatically by VE
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP VE is running on a host, there is the host interface's Physical Function (PF, i.e. the actual interface on the host device), and Virtual Function (VF, a virtual PCI device that the BIG-IP VE can use). If an x520 device's PF is marked down and then up, tmm does not recover traffic on that interface.
bugs.conditions: -- VE is using a VF from a PF. -- The PF is set down and then up.
bugs.impact: VE does not process any traffic on that VF.
bugs.workaround: Reboot VE.
bugs.fix: Tmm now restarts automatically when the PF comes back up after going down.
bugs.behavior: Tmm now restarts automatically when the PF comes back up after going down.

bugs.title: If named is restarted and zrd is not restarted, ZoneRunner can lose contact with the DNS server daemon
bugs.symptoms: ZoneRunner displays the following error message when attempting to list resource records: No route to host.
bugs.conditions: -- named is restarted outside of the normal start up procedure. -- zrd is not restarted.
bugs.impact: ZoneRunner cannot communicate with named, and thus cannot display resource records. There are temporary addresses created on the loopback address to facilitate communication between the zrd and named processes. When named is restarted, these temporary address are inadvertently removed.
bugs.workaround: Restart the zrd process using the following command: bigstart restart zrd
bugs.fix: The system no longer removes loopback addresses when named is restarted, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: iControl REST input sanitization
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST worker input sanitization issue.
bugs.conditions: iControl REST worker service running on BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: iControl REST
bugs.fix: Improved iControl REST worker input sanitization.

bugs.title: Bash shell still accessible for admin even if disabled
bugs.symptoms: With the administrator role, you have an option in TMUI to disable or restrict terminal access. If you disable or restrict access, the corresponding REST endpoint is neither disabled nor restricted.
bugs.conditions: Use TMUI as the admin, or as a user with the administrator role, and either of the following: -- Disable terminal access. -- Restrict access to TMSH.
bugs.impact: Users with the Administrator role can obtain shell access via REST. With terminal access disabled: -- If you attempt to login using SSH, you will not be to do so. -- If you make a POST request to the /mgmt/tm/util/bash endpoint with a body that includes a command to run, that command will be run. With access to TMSH restricted: -- A POST request to the /mgmt/tm/util/bash endpoint that includes a body with a command to run will be run.

bugs.title: MPTCP Passthrough and VIP-on-VIP can lead to TMM core
bugs.symptoms: If a FastL4 virtual server has an iRule that uses the 'virtual' command to direct traffic to a virtual server with MPTCP passthrough enabled, TMM may produce a core upon receiving certain traffic.
bugs.conditions: A FastL4 virtual server has an iRule that uses the 'virtual' command to direct traffic to a virtual server with a TCP profile attached that has MPTCP passthrough enabled, and certain traffic is received.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using an iRule with the 'virtual' command to direct traffic to a virtual server with MPTCP passthrough enabled.
bugs.fix: If MPTCP passthrough is enabled, the system now processes incoming MPTCP connections coming from the loop device as if MPTCP is disabled.

bugs.title: Too many branches in agents may cause request process slow down
bugs.symptoms: When a policy has an agent with a lot of branches, and many requests are routed to the branches near the bottom of the agent, those requests may take significantly longer to process.
bugs.conditions: A policy that has an agent with a lot of branches, and many requests are routed to the branches near the bottom of the agent.
bugs.impact: Requests may take a significantly longer time to process. For example, a policy with 10 branches might experience twice the processing time (from 5.7 microseconds (the baseline) to 12.9 microseconds. Depending on the number of requests that are routed to the branches near the bottom of the agent, you might even experience a lag in which the BIG-IP system appears to have stopped responding.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not configuring too many branches on a single agent. You can use layered / cascaded agents to limit the number of branches per agent.

bugs.title: BIG-IP is unable to send statistics to BIG-IQ DCD node using IPv6 address
bugs.symptoms: When IPv6 is used for transferring data from BIG-IP systems to BIG-IQ DCD nodes, no traffic arrives to the BIG-IQ.
bugs.conditions: -- DCD node uses IPv6 interface for collecting data from BIG-IP systems. -- BIG-IP is registered on BIG-IQ as 'BIG-IP device' the regular way (not necessary via IPv6 management interface).
bugs.impact: No statistics from BIG-IP systems are collected.
bugs.workaround: Use IPv4 addresses instead.
bugs.fix: You can now use IPv6 addresses in BIG-IP systems, and statistics arrive to the BIG-IQ.

bugs.title: Advanced Filters for Captured Transactions not working on Multi-Blade Platforms
bugs.symptoms: On multi-blade systems, when you navigates to System :: Logs : Captured Transactions, click on Expand Advanced Filters, choose something, and click Update, the GUI reports a 'Could not get captured events' message.
bugs.conditions: -- Multi-blade systems. -- AVR provisioned. -- AVR HTTP Analytics Profile configured with 'Internal Traffic Capturing Logging Type' option enabled.
bugs.impact: The Captured Transactions filter does not work.
bugs.fix: The Captured Transactions filter now works as expected.

bugs.title: Rare condition memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: BD dameon core
bugs.conditions: Slow server and slow offload services.
bugs.impact: A bd crash, traffic distrubance
bugs.fix: A memory corruption condition was solved.

bugs.title: Scheduled reports are being incorrectly displayed in different partitions
bugs.symptoms: Scheduled analytics reports are being displayed in the list regardless of selected partition. However, you can only open reports belonging to the selected partition, even if they belong to 'Common'.
bugs.conditions: System configured with multiple partitions.
bugs.impact: It makes it difficult to modify reports from different partitions.
bugs.workaround: Switch to the report's partition before editing it.
bugs.fix: Report's partition is now indicated in the list and correct handling is performed according to standard partition rules.

bugs.title: mcpd might crash on an unlicensed system
bugs.symptoms: On an unlicensed system with a built-in iRule attached to a virtual server, mcpd might crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Unlicensed system (including as a result of the service agreement check date validation treating a license as invalid). -- At least one built-in, system-supplied iRule is attached to a virtual server. -- mcpd loads from the config files, such as when having just upgraded.
bugs.impact: On an unlicensed system, mcpd might crash repeatedly.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following procedure: 1. Reactivate the license on the system from the command-line, following the instructions in K2595: Activating and installing a license file from the command line :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K2595. 2. License the system. Note: Running commands (e.g., tmsh show /sys hardware) on VIPRION systems while mcpd is down might fail or otherwise not work as expected.

bugs.title: Management MAC address and host VLAN MAC address is the same on iSeries platforms when in vCMP mode
bugs.symptoms: On iSeries platforms, when a VLAN is attached to a vCMP guest, the management MAC address and the host VLAN MAC address will be the same.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a VLAN on the host and attaching it to a vCMP guest. -- iSeries platforms.
bugs.impact: The management MAC address is the same as the Host VLAN MAC address, resulting in the same MAC being used for the VLAN traffic originating from the vCMP Host along with the Host's mgmt Interface traffic, potentially resulting in issues relating to the inability to differentiate traffic to mgmt port or traffic ports.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The management MAC address and Host VLAN MAC address are now different on iSeries platforms, so the system can differentiate traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Security hardening on the following platforms
bugs.symptoms: Improve hardware security on the following platforms (i850, i2000, i4000, i5000, i7000, i10000, i15000, HRC-xxx)
bugs.conditions: Using the following platforms: i850, i2000, i4000, i5000, i7000, i10000, i15000, HRC-xxx.
bugs.impact: These platforms do not use all available hardware security enhancements.
bugs.fix: Specified platforms now use hardware security enhancements.

bugs.title: Portal Access: fix F5_isXMLHttpObject predicate
bugs.symptoms: Various web-application misfunctions are possible.
bugs.conditions: Web-application defined object with properties which are subject to be rewritten by Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Client-side web-application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule is possible to remove unwanted rewriting.

bugs.title: Applications that use getResponseHeader or getAllResponseHeaders do not work properly
bugs.symptoms: Various web-application misfunctions are possible.
bugs.conditions: Web-application defined properties getResponseHeader() or getAllResponseHeaders.
bugs.impact: Client-side web-application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule is possible.

bugs.title: BIG-IP systems cannot be deployed in an L2 transparent mode with VLAN groups in Standard Proxy mode.
bugs.symptoms: Services that require Standard Proxy mode cannot be availed of.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system deployed in an L2 transparent mode using VLAN groups.
bugs.impact: Prevents services that require Standard Proxy mode from being leveraged in an L2 transparent deployment.
bugs.fix: Support standard proxy mode.

bugs.title: Brute Force end attack condition isn't satisfied for successful logins only
bugs.symptoms: When brute force attack is detected and prevented by asm, asm continue to prevent login attempts even the attacking traffic has stopped 5 minutes ago.
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual server - ASM Brute Force protection enabled in the asm policy - There is an ongoing brute force attack on the backend server.
bugs.impact: ASM doesn't report that brute force attack is finished and logins mitigation continues to occur.
bugs.workaround: While ongoing endless brute force attack, change an arbitrary field in brute force configuration and apply policy. Brute force attack end event will be triggered and the system will stop brute force prevention, if the attacking traffic still being sent, new brute force attack event will be raised and the mitigation will reoccur.
bugs.fix: Fix brute force end condition check for a case when only successful logins are sent.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system reuses cached session-id after SSL properties of the monitor has been changed.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system maintains an SSL session cache for SSL (https) monitors. After changing the properties of an SSL monitor that might affect the operation of SSL, the BIG-IP continues to reuse an existing SSL session ID.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has cached session ID from previous SSL session. -- SSL properties of monitor that might affect the operation of SSL are changed. -- Monitor is using bigd.
bugs.impact: Sessions still use cached session ID. If session continues to succeed, session uses cached session ID till expiry.
bugs.workaround: -- Restart bigd. -- Remove the monitor from the object and re-apply. -- Use in-tmm monitors.

bugs.title: HTTP filter complains about invalid action in the LTM log file.
bugs.symptoms: Payload data is collected at the HTTP_REQUEST event and finishes collecting (HTTP::release) when the NAME_RESOLVED event occurs. On releasing, data is forwarded to the serverside, triggering the HTTP_REQUEST_SEND event. When trying to raise HTTP_REQUEST_SEND, the iRule queues it and returns IN_PROGRESS, because the system is already in the process of running TCLRULE_NAME_RESOLVED. (Nested iRules: TCLRULE_NAME_RESOLVED -> TCLRULE_HTTP_REQUEST_SEND) Due to the IN_PROGRESS status, tcp_proxy skips forwarding HUDCTL_REQUEST to the serverside, but not the subsequent payload. So the HTTP filter considers this an invalid action.
bugs.conditions: -- Standard virtual server with iRules attached (for example, using the following configuration for a virtual server): when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::collect NAME::lookup @10.0.66.222 'f5.com' } when NAME_RESOLVED { HTTP::release } when HTTP_REQUEST_SEND { log local0. "Entering HTTP_REQUEST_SEND" } -- Client sends two HTTP Post requests. -- After the first request, the second connection is kept alive (for example, by using HTTP header Connection) so that the second request can reuse the same connection.
bugs.impact: The second request gets reset, and the system logs errors in the LTM log file.
bugs.workaround: To avoid nested iRules in this instance, simply remove the HTTP_REQUEST_SEND from the iRule.

bugs.title: SERVER_CONNECTED fires at wrong time for FastL4 mirrored connections on standby
bugs.symptoms: For FastL4 connections, SERVER_CONNECTED currently doesn't fire on the standby device. If the standby device then becomes active, the first packet from the server on an existing FastL4 connection causes SERVER_CONNECTED to fire. Depending on what the iRule does in SERVER_CONNECTED, a variety of results can occur, including TMM coring due to commands being executed in unexpected states.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability configuration. -- Mirrored FastL4 virtual server. -- Attached iRule contains a SERVER_CONNECTED event.
bugs.impact: SERVER_CONNECTED does not fire when expected on standby device. When the standby device becomes active, the SERVER_CONNECTED iRule may cause TMM to core with traffic being disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.fix: SERVER_CONNECTED now fires when expected on the standby device.

bugs.title: Persist value for the RADIUS Framed-IP-Address attribute is not correct
bugs.symptoms: Using the RADIUS Framed-IP-Address attribute as a persistence value does not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: Using RADIUS and persisting on the Framed-IP Address attribute (RADIUS AVP 8).
bugs.impact: RADIUS requests may not get persisted to the servers they should be.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to persist instead, e.g.: ltm rule radius-persistence { when CLIENT_DATA { persist uie [RADIUS::avp 8] } }
bugs.fix: We now use the correct value for persistence.

bugs.title: SCTP multi-homing INIT address parameter doesn't include association's primary address
bugs.symptoms: When multihoming is enabled in an SCTP profile, the source-address of the INIT chunk was not added as an Address parameter in that INIT chunk.
bugs.conditions: Any SCTP profile where multi-homing is enabled.
bugs.impact: No impact for peers that implement SCTP in accordance with RFC 4960. RFC does not require that the address either should or should not be included in the INIT chunk, but does require that an entity receiving an INIT chunk include the source-address in its list regardless of whether that is included in the INIT chunk.
bugs.workaround: No known workaround.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now includes all relevant addresses in the INIT chunk.
bugs.behavior: When multihoming is enabled, the local address will now be added to the INIT chunk. Previously the local address (that is, the address that the datagram is sent from) was not listed as an Address parameter. This is permitted, but not required, by RFC 4960 section 3.3.2.1.

bugs.title: SIP routing UI does not follow best practices
bugs.symptoms: The SIP routing UI does not follow best practices.
bugs.conditions: Administrative access to the SIP Profile web UI.
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output.
bugs.fix: The SIP routing UI does now follows best practices.

bugs.title: Misleading 'Invalid Nonce' error message
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs during access policy evaluation, resulting in a redirect to /my.logout.php3?errorcode=21 The end-user receives a logout/deny page that displays an error message of 'Invalid Nonce', which is an inaccurate and confusing log message.
bugs.conditions: 'Invalid Nonce' is normally reserved for On-Demand Cert Auth nonce failures. It is also being mistakenly shown for some cases of invalid APM session IDs, especially a sessionID that fails any security checks. This can sometimes be the symptom of the 'retry-after-reset' scenario. In this scenario, there is an unrelated failure in the access policy evaluation resulting in a reset being sent to the client. The client then tries to retry the original request. If the APM system has already rotated the sessionID (a security defense against session hijacking), then the retry has a stale sessionID. This invalid session ID results in displaying 'Invalid Nonce'.
bugs.impact: The error message of 'Invalid Nonce' is partially correct, since sessionID rotation is a form of cryptographic nonce. But the message is very confusing for end-users. It is also confusing for admins who do not think they have configured any nonce-based protocols. The error message should be more related to the real problem of invalid sessionID.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: IP address from XFF header is not taken into account when there are trailing spaces after IP address
bugs.symptoms: X-FORWARDED-FOR (XFF) header is ignored by BIG-IP ASM even though usage of XFF is enabled in HTTP profile. In DoS statistics, the original source IP is reported (instead of one taken from XFF).
bugs.conditions: There are spaces after IP address in the XFF header.
bugs.impact: Source IP is not reported as expected in all BIG-IP reports.
bugs.workaround: Configure the proxy server to not add trailing spaces after the IP address in the XFF header.
bugs.fix: Trailing spaces are now ignored when extracting IP addresses from XFF headers in AVR.

bugs.title: pabnagd core when centralized learning is turned on
bugs.symptoms: pabnagd (the process responsible for automated and manual policy building operations) restarts and generates a core file. This might result in a loss of learning progress. Note: This is a very rarely occurring issue.
bugs.conditions: Centralized learning is enabled for a policy.
bugs.impact: If there are locally learned policies, the system might lose some number of hours of learning progress. How many hours might be lost depends on the version, as follows: -- For 13.1.0: 24 hours (12 hours, on average). -- For 14.0.0: 1 hour (1/2 hour, on average).
bugs.fix: The pabnagd process no longer restarts/cores when centralized learning is enabled.

bugs.title: UCS does not follow current best practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions
bugs.conditions: Administrative access to system status data
bugs.impact: UCS save operations do not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: UCS save operations now follow current best practices.

bugs.title: F5_Inflate_onevent() issue when it assign value to user-defined object
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected undefined value retrieved from user-defined object property whose name matches the name of an event handler (e.g., onreadystatechange).
bugs.conditions: Assigning values to the property of user-defined object whose name matches the name of an event (e.g., onreadystatechange).
bugs.impact: Retrieved value from that property is undefined. Web-application might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to work around this issue.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly handles values retrieved from a user-defined object property whose name matches the name of an event handler.

bugs.title: Creating or deleting rule list results in warning message: Schema object encode failed
bugs.symptoms: "Schema object encode failed: No foreign keys found for nested object" warning message is logged into /var/log/ltm while creating or deleting the rule list. Jul 25 05:44:49 localhost.localdomain warning icr_eventd[4778]: 01a10008:4: Schema object encode failed: No foreign keys found for nested object with tag 17547
bugs.conditions: Observed when creating or deleting rule list in /var/log/ltm tmsh create security firewall rule-list rule-list1 tmsh delete security firewall rule-list rule-list1
bugs.impact: The warning message has no impact on functionality and can be ignored.
bugs.fix: Log message has been changed to log at the debug level.

bugs.title: /mgmt/toc endpoint issue after configuring remote authentication
bugs.symptoms: 'Invalid username or password.' error on the /mgmt/toc page after configuring remote authentication.
bugs.conditions: When remote auth is configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure remote authentication. After configuring remote authentication, you can login to the mgmt/toc area with the admin user, but using a remote auth user ended up with 'You are not authorized to use this resource'.
bugs.workaround: On BIG-IP versions since 14.1.0.6 and 13.1.1.5: Enable 'Fallback to Local' in the remote auth config section on the BIG-IP system: tmsh modify auth source fallback true. Both local BIG-IP user 'admin' and LDAP user are now able to authenticate and access https://XX.XX.XX.XX/mgmt/toc. On other versions of BIG-IP software, there is no workaround.
bugs.fix: When source type is set to a remote auth method, login now succeeds. If the remote server is unavailable, authentication now falls back to local authentication, if authentication source fallback is set to true.
bugs.behavior: This release allows fallback to local authentication. When the authentication source type is set to a remote authentication source, if the remote server is unavailable, authentication now falls back to local authentication, if authentication source fallback is set to true.

bugs.title: Log output does not reflect BIG-IP system timezone setting
bugs.symptoms: Running the command 'tmsh show sys log' for any module in a specified range displays results according to the UTC timezone, despite the setting on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- Run the following command: tmsh show sys log <any_module> range <range options> -- View the output.
bugs.impact: Log filtering may not return results because of the difference between timezone settings.
bugs.workaround: Set timezone to UTC setting.

bugs.title: SAML -IdP-initiated case that has a per-request policy with a logon page in a subroutine fails.
bugs.symptoms: For a BIG-IP system configured as IdP, in the SAML-IdP-initiated case: If the IdP has a Per-Request policy (in addition to a V1 policy), such that the Per-Request policy has a subroutine or a subroutine macro with a logon page, the system reports access failure on running the policy. The error logged is similar to the following: '/Common/sso_access:Common:218f759e: Authorization failure: Denied request for SAML resource /Common/saml_resource_obj1&state=000fffff032db022'.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system configured as IdP. -- SAML IdP initiated case in which the following is true: + The IdP has a Per-Request policy (in addition to a V1 policy). + That Per-Request policy has a subroutine or a subroutine macro with a logon page.
bugs.impact: Access is denied. The request URI has '&state=<per-flow-id>' appended to the SAML Resource name.
bugs.fix: The system now checks for additional query parameters in the request_uri while extracting Resource name so it is not incorrectly set to 'ResourceName&state=<per-flow-id>' which causes the access failure.

bugs.title: APM is not able to do compliance check on iOS devices running F5 Access VPN client
bugs.symptoms: Compliance check against Microsoft Intune fails when an APM end user attempts a VPN connection from a managed iOS device running the F5 Access VPN client.
bugs.conditions: -- APM policy is configured to use Microsoft Intune for device compliance check. -- APM end user is attempting VPN connection using the F5 Access VPN client on an iOS device.
bugs.impact: APM is not able to do compliance checks on the device, and VPN connection fails.
bugs.fix: APM can now check iOS devices for compliance against Microsoft Intune.

bugs.title: IKEv1 handles INVALID-SPI incorrectly in parsing SPI and in phase 2 lookup
bugs.symptoms: INVALID_SPI notification does not delete the IPsec-SA with the SPI value that appears in the notify payload. This occurs because the handler of INVALID-SPI notifications performs the following incorrect actions: -- Fetches SPI from payload as if it's a string, rather than the network byte order integer it actually is. -- Attempts phase 2 lookup via selector ID (reqid) rather than SPI. Either alone prevents finding the SA to delete.
bugs.conditions: An IKEv1 IPsec peer sends an INVALID-SPI notification to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The IPsec-SA with that SPI cannot be found and is not deleted.
bugs.workaround: From the BIG-IP command line, you can still manually delete any IPsec-SA, including the invalid SPI, using the following command: # tmsh delete net ipsec ipsec-sa spi <spi number>
bugs.fix: SPI is now extracted correctly from the payload as a binary integer, and the phase 2 SA lookup is done with a proper SPI search, which also requires a match in the peer address.

bugs.title: Parsing pool members as variables with IP tuple syntax
bugs.symptoms: There is a config loading warning at tmsh similar to the following: unexpected end of arguments;expected argument spec:PORT.
bugs.conditions: Tcl variable is used for the IP tuple instead of a plain value.
bugs.impact: iRule LB::reselect command may not recognize an IP tuple when it is a variable. tmsh warning shows. Note: There is no warning in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use plain value instead of variable.

bugs.title: TLS1.2 and earlier 'do not advertise' signature algorithm RSA-PSS
bugs.symptoms: 'Do not advertise' support for RSA-PSS signature algorithms in TLS1.2 and earlier versions. This is advertised by the default cipher group.
bugs.conditions: -- TLS1.2 and earlier. -- Attempting to use 'Do not advertise.'
bugs.impact: No support for 'Do not advertise.' Possible handshake failure with unsupported signature algorithm.
bugs.workaround: Use a cipher group with RSA-PSS removed from the signature algorithms. Switch to using the cipher string from cipher groups.
bugs.fix: There is now 'Do not advertise' support for RSA-PSS signature algorithms in TLS1.2 and earlier versions.

bugs.title: i4x00/i2x00 platforms transmit LACP PDUs with a VLAN Tag.
bugs.symptoms: A trunk configured between a BIG-IP i4x00/i2x00 platform and an upstream switch may go down due to the presence of the VLAN tag.
bugs.conditions: LACP configured between a BIG-IP i4x00/i2x00 platform and an upstream switch.
bugs.impact: Trunks are brought down by upstream switch.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling LACP.
bugs.fix: The system no longer transmits a VLAN tag for LACP PDUs, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: SMTP monitor fails to handle multi-line '250' responses to 'HELO' messages
bugs.symptoms: When monitoring an SMTP server that emits multi-line '250' responses to the initial 'HELO' message, the monitor fails. If monitor logging is enabled on the pool member, the system posts an error similar to the following in the monitor log: 09:50:08.580145:(_Tcl /Common/mysmtp): ERROR: failed to complete the transfer, Failed to identify domain.
bugs.conditions: -- Monitoring an SMTP server. -- SMTP server is configured to return a multi-line '250' response to the initial 'HELO' message.
bugs.impact: The pool member is marked down even though it is actually up.
bugs.fix: The system now handles multi-line '250' responses to the initial 'HELO' message.

bugs.title: Dynamic route with recursive nexthop might cause tmrouted restart
bugs.symptoms: tmrouted restart.
bugs.conditions: - Dynamic routing enabled. - Routing update with recursive nexthop.
bugs.impact: Stability of the dynamic routing daemons. TMM cannot learn or advertise routes while the daemon restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not exporting routes with recursive nexthop.
bugs.fix: Dynamic routes with recursive nexthop no longer cause tmrouted restart.

bugs.title: SAML Sax Parser returns error when importing metadata file that contains certain UTF-8 encoded characters other than ASCII
bugs.symptoms: When SAML metadata file that contains certain UTF-8 characters other than ASCII is imported, SAML SAX Parser returns error
bugs.conditions: When SAML metadata file contains certain UTF-8 characters other than the ASCII set
bugs.impact: SAML metadata file is not imported, and the system reports an error. SAML configuration on BIG-IP systems is impacted.
bugs.workaround: Remove the non-ASCII UTF-8 characters, and try the import operation again.

bugs.title: Ping Access Agent Module leaks memory in TMM.
bugs.symptoms: While handling Ping Access Request, if the internal events passing between modules fail, it might cause a memory leak inside TMM.
bugs.conditions: Internal events passing between Ping Access Request processing modules fail.
bugs.impact: Ping Access Agent Module leaks memory in TMM.

bugs.title: Vmware Horizon session collaboration (shadow session) feature does not work through APM.
bugs.symptoms: When the VMware virtual desktop interface (VDI) is configured, session collaboration or shadow session does not work.
bugs.conditions: -- VMware VDI configured and Desktop resource is accessed with native client or browser. -- Shadow session is enabled in desktop.
bugs.impact: Desktop's Shadow session resource icon is not showed on webtop or native client.
bugs.fix: Users should see Desktop's shadow session icon when resources are loaded on to webtop or native client.

bugs.title: 'Internal error' appears on Goodput GUI page
bugs.symptoms: The Statistics :: Analytics : TCP : Goodput GUI page displays 'Internal Error', and data does not display.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on multi-blade VIPRION systems.
bugs.impact: You are unable to see statistics for TCP Goodput on a multi-blade system.
bugs.workaround: 1. Edit /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tcp_measures.cfg file: -- In [cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m] section replace existing value of merge_formula parameter with the following one: merge_formula=IF(SUM(cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m)=0,"N/A",ROUND(SUM(cs_numendings_m*cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m)/SUM(cs_numendings_m),2)) -- In [cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m]section replace existing value of merge_formula parameter with the following one: merge_formula=IF(SUM(cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m)=0,"N/A",ROUND(SUM(cs_numendings_m*cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m)/SUM(cs_numendings_m),2)) -- In both aforementioned sections add the following parameter: merge_deps=cs_numendings_m 2. Restart the monpd daemon: tmsh restart sys service monpd
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with Goodput statistics on multi-blade systems.

bugs.title: Add the login detection criteria of 'status code is not X'
bugs.symptoms: There is a criterion needed to detect successful login.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to detect successful login when the response code is not X (where 'x' = some code).
bugs.impact: Cannot configure login criteria.
bugs.fix: This release adds a new criterion to the login criteria.

bugs.title: Login validation may fail for a large request with early server response
bugs.symptoms: in case of large request/response, if FPS needs to store ingress and ingress chunks in buffer for additional processing (ingress :: for parameter parsing, egress :: for login validation's banned/mandatory strings check or scripts injection), if the server responds fast enough, the buffer may contain mixed parts of request/response. This may have several effects, from incorrectly performing login-validation to generating a tmm core file.
bugs.conditions: -- Login validation is enabled and configured to check for banned/mandatory string. -- A username parameter is configured. -- There are no parameters configured for encrypt/HTML Field Obfuscation (HFO), and no decoy parameters. -- There is a large request and response. -- The system response very quickly.
bugs.impact: This results in one or more of the following: -- Login validation failure/skip. -- Bad response/script injection. -- tmm core. In this case, traffic is disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: FPS now handles ingress/egress buffers separately, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Ajax blocking page breaks ajax based applications
bugs.symptoms: When ajax blocking page is enabled within ASM policy it interferes with the web-app's ajax API's by hooking ajax responses. As a result ajax response isn't passed to a native response handler. The symptoms are ajax requests stuck or not being fired.
bugs.conditions: - ASM Provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual - Ajax Blocking page enabled within asm policy
bugs.impact: Ajax based web-app won't work properly.
bugs.workaround: Disable Ajax Blocking page feature in asm policy.
bugs.fix: ASM Ajax blocking response hooks are fixed to address the issue.

bugs.title: Errors when trying to delete all bot requests from Security :: Event Logs : Bot Defense : Bot Requests
bugs.symptoms: When trying to delete all bot requests from Security :: Event Logs : Bot Defense : Bot Requests Delete fails with error and exceptions in restjavad.log: [WARNING][593][30 Jul 2018 14:42:26 UTC][8100/mgmt ForwarderPassThroughWorker] URI:http://localhost:8100/mgmt/tm/asm/events/bot-defense-events?$top=200000, Referrer:https://<local_IP>/dms/bot_defense/bot_requests.php, Method:DELETE, Exception:java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException: remoteSender:<remote_IP>, method:DELETE
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered when deleting all bot requests while traffic is passing.
bugs.impact: Delete fails, and there is significant memory consumption in asm_config_server.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the bot-requests deletion process to not fail with errors and not cause substantial memory consumption in asm_config_server.

bugs.title: Configured name of wildcard parameter is not sent in data integrity alerts
bugs.symptoms: FPS sends a data integrity alert when a parameter is configured with 'Check Data Manipulation' enabled. the alert includes parameter's actual-name, actual-val-crc, and expected-val-crc. For wildcard parameters, it is difficult to tell which parameter was found and triggered the data integrity alert, since FPS sends only the actual name that was found in the request.
bugs.conditions: Wildcard parameter defined for integrity check.
bugs.impact: Alert analysis is more difficult, as the actual matched parameter is not obvious.
bugs.fix: FPS now includes wildcard parameter's configured-name in the data integrity alert.

bugs.title: Update to global list of disallowed filetypes not propagated to the policies
bugs.symptoms: Existing policies do not get updates to the global list of disallowed filetypes.
bugs.conditions: A disallowed filetype is added or removed from the global list of disallowed filetypes
bugs.impact: Existing policies are not 'informed' of changes to the global list of disallowed filetypes. The policies keep using the disallowed filetypes list that existed on startup (or if the policy was created after startup, then its the list that existed when the policy was created).
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM by running the command: restart asm Upon restart all policies get the updated list of disallowed filetypes.
bugs.fix: All policies are now updated with changes to the global disallowed filetypes list.

bugs.title: APM client does not support untrusted SSL certificate
bugs.symptoms: When connecting to APM server configured with untrusted SSL certificate, the Windows Logon integration / Custom dialup entry displays a security warning and asks users for confirmation.
bugs.conditions: APM Virtual Server configured with untrusted SSL certificate (self-signed certificate or SSL Certificate issued by an untrusted CA).
bugs.impact: Custom dialup does not establish VPN Tunnel.
bugs.workaround: Configure APM server with a trusted SSL Certificate.
bugs.fix: Now with this release, any connection to the APM server configured with untrusted SSL certificate is denied. To override this default, perform the following steps: 1. In Registry Editor, locate the following registry folder: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\F5 Networks\RemoteAccess 2. Set the following registry key: "AskAboutUntrustedSSLCert"=dword:00000001

bugs.title: Add support for "Restart Desktop" setting in View clients, native as well as HTML5 clients
bugs.symptoms: When VMware resources are accessed through APM VMware VDI, the "Restart Desktop" setting is not seen on enumerated for Desktop resource. The same issue is observed with HTML5 clients.
bugs.conditions: - VMware Native or HTML5 client is used - APM VMware VDI is used - Desktop resources should be enumerated - Right click on resource
bugs.impact: Unable to restart desktop from native and HTML5 clients.
bugs.fix: Restart desktop is successful and it works as expected.

bugs.title: IPv6 SCTP traffic not passing after CMP-hash reconfiguration.
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 SCTP traffic not passing after CMP-hash reconfiguration.
bugs.conditions: When the CMP hash is changed in certain ways, SCTP traffic may stop passing.
bugs.impact: After changing the configuration, SCTP traffic will not pass.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM to pick up the configuration change. If existing connections are cleared using "tmsh del sys conn" _before_ the configuration is changed, traffic may continue to pass.

bugs.title: Encrypted field lost reference when adding input element to parentElement
bugs.symptoms: A config parameter is not encrypted in real time
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using innerHTML to add input before the encrypted input.
bugs.impact: Parameter is not encrypted

bugs.title: ASM/XML family parser does not support us-ascii encoding when it appears in the document prolog
bugs.symptoms: ASM blocks requests when a request payload is an xml document with a prolog line at the begging with encoding="us-ascii"
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual server - ASM handles xml traffic with encoding="us-ascii" (this is very unlikely, the common case is encoding="utf-8")
bugs.impact: Blocked xml requests
bugs.workaround: Remove xml profile from a url in asm policy or disable XML malformed document detection via asm policy blocking settings
bugs.fix: xml parser is fixed and now allows encoding="us-ascii"

bugs.title: javascript functions in href are learned from response as new URLs
bugs.symptoms: New urls representing javascript functions are learned from response.
bugs.conditions: Learn from response is turned on and URLs learning set to 'Always'
