bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: 1. Edit the following file: /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_cpu_info_measures.cfg 2. Remove all division by 100 on 'formula' of each entity. 3. Save the change and restart monpd (bigstart restart monpd).
bugs.fix: Scale is now fixed and is not pre-divided by 100.

bugs.title: Auto Last Hop for management connections cannot be disabled/enabled
bugs.symptoms: Disabling/Enabling Auto Last Hop for management connections does not take effect. By default, it is enabled and stays enabled after a change.
bugs.conditions: -- Manual BIG-IP Management Port Configuration is configured. IP address and Network Mask is set, but Management Route is empty. -- Auto Last Hop for management connections is disabled. # tmsh mod ltm global-settings general mgmt-auto-last-hop disable -- BIG-IP system is rebooted. # full_box_reboot
bugs.impact: Auto Last Hop for management connections is still enabled on management interface and the BIG-IP system is still accessible outside local management network.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use the following commands to move the lasthop.modules script to the /etc/sysconfig/sysinit directory: # mv -v /etc/sysconfig/modules/lasthop.modules /etc/sysconfig/sysinit/00activate-early-lasthop.sysinit 2. Reboot the BIG-IP system. # full_box_reboot
bugs.fix: The lasthop.modules lasthop.modules script has been moved to the /etc/sysconfig/sysinit directory, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing Portal Access requests
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, TMM may crash while processing Portal Access requests.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server with Portal Access.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes Portal Access requests correctly.

bugs.title: DNS GUI may generate error or display names with special characters incorrectly.
bugs.symptoms: -- If a DNS object name (such as a Server or Link) contains a special character, the name may be truncated after the special character when displayed in the GUI. For example: DNS -> GSLB -> Server : - Select a server with name containing a special character (such as # or &). - Go to Devices, Virtual Servers or Links tab. - Click on the tab again or go to another tab. DNS -> GSLB -> Links : - Select a link with name containing special character (such as # or &). - Go to Servers or Virtual servers tab, click on the tab again or go to other tab. In such cases, the characters after the special character disappear in the Server and/or Link name. -- Certain DNS GUI operations may generate an error such as: "An error has occurred while trying to process your request." For example: DNS -> GSLB -> Pools -> Pool List : - Select a Pool - Go to Members tab - Click Manage
bugs.conditions: -- The DNS object name may be displayed incorrectly if it contains a special character such as: # & -- An error can occur on BIG-IP versions prior to 15.0.0 that contain the fix for ID1045421 (such as Engineering Hotfixes on versions 14.1.x or 13.1.x with a fix for ID1045421).
bugs.impact: -- DNS object names display incorrectly and may not be selectable for subsequent operations in the GUI. -- You may not be able to manage DNS objects in certain contexts in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use the Command Line Interface (tmsh) to manage DNS objects.
bugs.fix: -- DNS object names containing special characters are displayed properly in the GUI. -- GUI operations to manage DNS objects do not generate errors in the presence of the fix for ID1045421 on BIG-IP versions prior to 15.0.0.

bugs.title: Enable SysDb variable 'Connection.VgL2Transparent' prior to operating the BIG-IP in L2 transparent mode using VLAN groups.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic is not passed across the VLAN group.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system configured to operate in L2 transparent mode using VLAN groups.
bugs.impact: Packets are not forwarded.
bugs.workaround: Configure a transparent next hop on the virtual server.
bugs.fix: SysDb variable 'Connection.VgL2Transparent' has been added to enable this functionality.
bugs.behavior: A new SysDb variable called 'Connection.VgL2Transparent has been added. It can be enabled to enable L2 transparent forwarding in a VLAN group without needing to configure a transparent next hop on the virtual server. Usage: tmsh modify sys db Connection.VgL2Transparent value <enable|disable> It is disabled by default, and needs to be set prior to configuring the VLAN group.

bugs.title: sod does not validate message length vs. received packet length
bugs.symptoms: sod may crash or produce unexpected behavior.
bugs.conditions: If a malformed network failover packet is received by sod, it may cause an invalid memory access.
bugs.impact: sod may crash, causing a failover.
bugs.fix: sod validates the received packet length and does not reference invalid memory.

bugs.title: HTTP response may be dropped following a 100 continue message.
bugs.symptoms: When a 100 response a quickly followed by another HTTP response (2xx/4xx), the second response might be dropped.
bugs.conditions: When a 100 response is quickly followed by another HTTP response (i.e., a 2xx/4xx response arrives within a few microseconds).
bugs.impact: The second response might be dropped, so the end user client might not receive all the HTTP responses coming from the server. Note: This does not happen all the time, and depends on how the underlying data packets are formed and delivered to the HTTP filter.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use an iRule to disable the HTTP filter in the HTTP_REQUEST event. -- Disable LRO by running the following command: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcplargereceiveoffload value disable

bugs.title: 'route domain' messages appear in console connections
bugs.symptoms: When logged into a console connections, you may see messages similar to the following in the terminal. 'route domain 0:'
bugs.conditions: -- Using a console connection. -- Rebooting the system, or restarting TMM.
bugs.impact: No impact other than the unwanted messages. These messages are benign and do not indicate functional issues.
bugs.workaround: You can prevent the messages from displaying in the console by modifying /etc/bigstart/scripts/tmrouted.finish to redirect the output from /usr/bin/rdip to /dev/null. Note: This change may not survive an upgrade.

bugs.title: Multiple extensions in SIP NOTIFY request cause message to be dropped.
bugs.symptoms: When SIP NOTIFY messages are sent with a request URI that contains multiple client extensions, the system does not forward the message as expected.
bugs.conditions: SIP NOTIFY messages sent with a request URI that contains multiple client extensions.
bugs.impact: NOTIFY message is not forwarded.
bugs.fix: Improved SIP URI parser now correctly handles multiple extensions in a URI.

bugs.title: APM custom report with active field failed on vcmp
bugs.symptoms: APM custom report, when including active field, fail to run on VCMP platform.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create an APM custom report (Access :: Overview :: Access Reports, click on "Custom Reports" panel, then "create". Select fields for the report, make sure check "Active" under "Session") 2. Run the report
bugs.impact: Unable to run the report with the specific field.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Admin can run APM custom report with active field without problem on vcmp.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system does not answer the request matching L7 policy that disabled DOSL7 when BADOS configured.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not answer the request matching the L7 policy that disabled DOSL7 when BADOS is configured. The connection hangs.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a DoS profile Behavioral & Stress-based (D)DoS Detection. 2. Create an L7 policy to disable DoS profile (even on all URLs). 3. Attach both to a virtual server. 4. Send a request to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Connection hangs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling the Behavioral & Stress-based (D)DoS Detection from the DoS profile.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly handles a disabled DOSL7 policy.

bugs.title: Cleanup Webroot database files when database fail to download
bugs.symptoms: /var partition gets full when the temporary files are not deleted.
bugs.conditions: When the update process of the wr_urldb encounters errors, the temporary (downloaded/created) files do not appear to be deleted, and /var directory fills with them.
bugs.impact: /var partition may get full.
bugs.workaround: Empty /var/wr_urldb/bcdatabase, and restart wr_urldbd to re-download the new database file.
bugs.fix: With this release, the temp files downloaded during the database download process get deleted when the download fails.

bugs.title: FPS live updates do not install when minor version is different
bugs.symptoms: Install update file with a different minor version. For example, install update file versioned 13.1.1 on BIG-IP version 13.1.0.
bugs.conditions: FPS is licensed and provisioned.
bugs.impact: FPS engine and signature cannot be updated.
bugs.fix: The minor version in update file is now ignored and only the major version is validated.

bugs.title: Known Swap Usage Leak by iCRD Child
bugs.symptoms: A leak in iCRD Child is causing excessive use of SWAP memory.
bugs.conditions: Heavy use of BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: SWAP Memory will eventually run out causing system reboot.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the BIG-IP to clear SWAP Memory.

bugs.title: Incoming SYNs are dropped and the connection does not time out.
bugs.symptoms: There is a hard-coded limit on the number of SYNs forwarded on a FastL4 connection. This might cause a problem when a connection is reused, for example, if a connection is not correctly closed.
bugs.conditions: -- SYN forwarding on FastL4 connections. -- The number of SYNs on a single connection reaches the hard-coded limit.
bugs.impact: If the number of SYNs on a single connection reaches this limit, subsequent incoming SYNs are dropped and the connection might not time out.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The following command enables the forwarding of an an unlimited number of SYNs: tmsh modify sys db tm.dupsynenforce value disable

bugs.title: do not count resumed connections against SSL TPS
bugs.symptoms: The SSL TPS limit is based on the time complexity of the operations needed to create a new session. A resumed session does not have this complexity, and therefore should not count against the licensed TPS limit.
bugs.conditions: SSL is licensed with a limit other than `unlimited'
bugs.impact: Not as many new SSL connections/second as expected.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround
bugs.fix: Resumed SSL sessions no longer count against the TPS limit.

bugs.title: False positive in SFTP policy enforcement
bugs.symptoms: In some rare cases, SFTP policy enforcement may detect a false positive. This will only have an effect if the SSH Proxy profile in place has actions in place for SFTP enforcement.
bugs.conditions: SFTP file transfers.
bugs.impact: Either a disconnect to the user, a log being generated, or no effect at all, depending on the SSH Proxy profile.

bugs.title: Displaying network map with virtual servers is slow
bugs.symptoms: The network map loads slowly when it contains lots of objects.
bugs.conditions: Load the network map in a configuration that contains 1000 or more objects.
bugs.impact: The network map loads very slowly.

bugs.title: MCPd crash seen during load sys config
bugs.symptoms: If the system is gathering IP intelligence category stats (e.g., by issuing the following command: show security ip-intelligence global-policy ip-intelligence-categories) and simultaneously you issue the command 'load sys config', MCPd might crash while fetching the stats.
bugs.conditions: -- IP intelligence category stats are being fetched. -- The command 'load sys config' is executed.
bugs.impact: MCPd restarts.Traffic disrupted while the daemon restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not gathering IP intelligence category stats while the load sys config operation is being performed.
bugs.fix: MCPd no longer crashes during load sys config while the system is gathering IP intelligence category stats.

bugs.title: Errors in browser console in browser verification challenge
bugs.symptoms: When enabling Browser Verification on the Bot Defense profile, or Suspicious Clients on the Web Scraping feature of the ASM Policy, the following error messages may be shown in the console of the end users' (clients) browsers that are accessing the virtual server. These messages are cosmetic-only, and do not indicate any functional problem. They are displayed only when the end user opens the browser's Developer Tools to look at the Browser Console. The messages are: -- Not allowed to load local resource: chrome://rumola/content/rumola48.png -- GET chrome-extension://invalid/ 0 () -- [Violation] Added synchronous DOM mutation listener to a 'DOMNodeInserted' event. Consider using MutationObserver to make the page more responsive. -- [Deprecation] 'webkitURL' is deprecated. Please use 'URL' instead. -- The Web Audio autoplay policy will be re-enabled in Chrome 70 (October 2018). Please check that your website is compatible with it.
bugs.conditions: -- Browser Verification is enabled on the Bot Defense profile, or Suspicious Clients on the Web Scraping feature of the ASM Policy -- End user client accesses the virtual server and opens the Developer Tools of the browser.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic error messages appear in the browser's console when opened.

bugs.title: REST PUT command fails for data-group internal
bugs.symptoms: Cannot change content of existing data-group internal using REST PUT command.
bugs.conditions: -- Using REST API. -- Creating and updating data-group in a single transaction.
bugs.impact: Cannot modify data-group internal via the REST API.
bugs.workaround: Add 'type' in the content. Note: This change in behavior occurred as the result of a different change in the software. Previously, you could not create and update data-group in a single transaction. Now you can, but you must also specify 'type'.

bugs.title: /32 self ip addresses display invalid mask
bugs.symptoms: tmos routing table (show net route) displays an invalid mask for the self ip's with a 32/128 bitmask
bugs.conditions: Self IPs configured an address with 32/128 bitmasks.
bugs.impact: Routing table displays an invalid mask.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround

bugs.title: TMM memory leak
bugs.symptoms: -- High TMM memory utilization; -- Aggressive sweeper activated; -- the 'packet', 'xdata' and 'xhead' caches in the memory_usage_stat tmstat table have high 'allocated' and 'curr_allocs' numbers with a steadily increasing profile.
bugs.conditions: A fastL4 and a L7 profile (e.g. HTTP) are assigned to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Degraded performance, possible TMM crash due to out-of-memory condition.
bugs.workaround: Do not add a L7 profile to a fastL4 virtual server.
bugs.fix: No memory leak in the TMM.

bugs.title: TMSH platform_check utility does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: No functional issues.
bugs.conditions: TMSH access to the platform_check command
bugs.fix: Security violation removed

bugs.title: CPU spikes appear wider than actual in graphs
bugs.symptoms: Graphs of CPU usage show spikes that are wider than actual CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: CPU usage has spikes.
bugs.impact: Graphs of CPU spikes appear to last longer than they actually last.
bugs.workaround: Perform the following procedure: 1. Run the following command to record the 5-second average rather than the 1-second average: sed -i.bak 's/TMCOLNAME "ratio"/TMCOLNAME "five_sec_avg.ratio"/;s/TMCOLNAME "cpu_ratio_curr"/TMCOLNAME "cpu_ratio_5sec"/g' /config/statsd.conf 2. Restart statsd to load the new configuration: bigstart restart statsd
bugs.fix: CPU samples for graphs are averaged over longer time to more closely represent actual time between samples.

bugs.title: Add Alibaba Cloud support to Qkview
bugs.symptoms: Qkview has been updated to support obtaining files relevant to the Alibaba Cloud.
bugs.conditions: Run Qkview.
bugs.impact: Files related to the Alibaba Cloud were not collected.
bugs.fix: Files related to Alibaba Cloud are now collected.

bugs.title: BIG-IP NIC teaming of SR-IOV interfaces does not work under VMware ESXi
bugs.symptoms: Configuring multiple SR-IOV interfaces into a trunk does not function correctly when running BIG-IP as a guest under VMware ESXi. The interface will show as uninitialized.
bugs.conditions: A system that passes SR-IOV virtual functions directly to a BIG-IP guest when running on VMware ESXi.
bugs.impact: The trunk will fail to initialize.

bugs.title: Cannot create non-ASCII entities in non-UTF ASM policy using REST
bugs.symptoms: You cannot create non-ASCII entities (such as URLs and parameters) in a non-UTF-8 policy using REST.
bugs.conditions: -- The policy is configured for an encoding other than UTF-8. -- Attempting to create non-ASCII entries using REST.
bugs.impact: You cannot create an entity (such as a URL or parameter) which contains non-ASCII characters using REST.
bugs.workaround: Use UTF-8.

bugs.title: Request Log export document fails to show some UTF-8 characters
bugs.symptoms: After exporting an ASM security event log, the log file exists but the characters are not visible.
bugs.conditions: Decoding of UTF-8 characters fails in Request Log export on small range of characters.
bugs.impact: The contents of the log are not human readable.
bugs.fix: Request Log export document now shows UTF-8 characters correctly.

bugs.title: WebSocket Statistics are updated to differentiate between client and server sides
bugs.symptoms: The WebSocket feature has statistics that records the number of each type of frame seen. These statistics do not differentiate between client and server sides.
bugs.conditions: The WebSocket profile is used to add WebSocket protocol parsing.
bugs.impact: WebSocket Traffic Statistics may be misleading
bugs.fix: WebSocket statistics now differentiate between client and server side.

bugs.title: SSL session mirroring may cause memory leakage if HA channel is down
bugs.symptoms: If SSL session mirroring is enabled, but the HA channel is down, attempts to mirror may result in memory leakage.
bugs.conditions: - SSL session mirroring enabled - HA channel is down
bugs.impact: Memory leakage over time resulting in eventual memory pressure leading to performance degradation and possible TMOS restart.
bugs.workaround: Ensuring that the HA peer is present and connected will avoid the leakage. Otherwise, no reasonable workaround exists short of disabling SSL session mirroring.
bugs.fix: SSL session mirroring no longer leaks memory when the HA channel is down.

bugs.title: Tmsh session initiation adds increased control plane pressure
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) can consume more system memory than expected.
bugs.conditions: Multiple users or remote processes connecting to the BIG-IP administrative command-line interface.
bugs.impact: Increased control plane pressure. Various delays may occur in both command-line and GUI response. Extreme instances may cause one or more processes to terminate, with potential disruptive effect. Risk of impact from this issue is increased when a large number of automated tmsh sessions are created.
bugs.workaround: For users with administrative privilege (who are permitted to use the 'bash' shell), the login shell can be changed to avoid invoking tmsh when it may not be needed: tmsh modify /auth user ADMINUSERNAME shell bash
bugs.fix: This issue is fixed in the following releases: -- 12.1.5.3 and later -- 13.1.3.4 and later -- 14.1.2.6 -- 14.1.4 and later -- 15.0.1.2 and later -- 15.1.0.4 and later -- 16.0.0 and later

bugs.title: Origin header is not reconstructed after Bot defense challenge
bugs.symptoms: Origin header is not reconstructed after Bot defense challenge. It is shown as 'null' after cross site redirect, and is incorrect after browser or device ID challenge.
bugs.conditions: - Bot defense profile is attached to a virtual server. - Origin header is present in POST request. - Cross site redirect, Browser, or DID challenge during POST request.
bugs.impact: Servers might block requests from unknown origins.
bugs.fix: Origin header is now correctly reconstructed after Bot challenge

bugs.title: Accessing the BIG-IP system's WebUI via special proxy solutions may fail
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system's WebUI is accessed via certain special proxy solutions, logging on to the system may fail.
bugs.conditions: This issue is known to happen with special proxy solutions that do one of the following things: - Remove the Referer header. - Modify the HTTP request in such a way that the Referer and Host headers no longer tally with one another.
bugs.impact: Users cannot log on to the BIG-IP system's WebUI.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you can do any of the following things: - Access the BIG-IP system's WebUI directly (i.e., bypassing the problematic proxy solution). - Modify the proxy solution so that it does not remove the Referer header (this is only viable if the proxy does not alter the Host header). - Modify the proxy solution so that it inserts compatible Referer and Host headers.
bugs.fix: CSRF checks based on HTTP headers pre-logon have been improved.

bugs.title: EDI alert on autofill of multiple fields
bugs.symptoms: When browser autofills more than one EDI protected field, a false-positive alert is triggered.
bugs.conditions: Protect multiple input fields with EDI
bugs.impact: False-positive EDI alert is thrown
bugs.fix: Support for multiple autofill was added to JS engine

bugs.title: If two racoon daemon are spawned on startup, one fails and cores.
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system becomes Active, tmipsecd starts a racoon daemon for each route domain, including the default RD 0. If for any reason racoon fails to fully start, tmipsecd will start another instance of racoon. When this occurs, one or both of them may crash and create a core file.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP becomes Active or racoon is (re)started. -- IPsec does not have to be configured for this failure to occur.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels might delay starting while racoon restarts.

bugs.title: SIP ALG: Do not translate and create media channels if RTP port is defined in the SIP message is 0
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system incorrectly handles SDP media ports. UAC sends SDP message body publishing capable of handling voice, text, and video. UAS responds, publishing voice, text and video not desired by setting video port to '0'. The BIG-IP system does not honor the fact that UAS does not want video, and translates video port '0' to an ephemeral port, causing the UAC to believe it must open a video channel. When the UAC sends a video connection request, the BIG-IP system sends the request to the wrong port, i.e., to the media port for text, which causes the connection to fail.
bugs.conditions: RTP media port defined in the SIP message is set to 0.
bugs.impact: Improper media channel creation.
bugs.workaround: You can use an iRule workaround to remove the media attributes with ports set to 0 at the ingress, and update the message body size accordingly.

bugs.title: A draft policy of an existing published policy cannot be modified if it is in /Common and an used by a virtual server in a different partition
bugs.symptoms: If you have a published policy in /Common that is in use by a virtual server in a different partition, if you try to create and modify a draft of the existing policy, you will get an error like this: "01070726:3: Policy /Common/Drafts/test-policy in partition Common cannot reference policy reference /Common/Drafts/test-policy /test/test-vs in partition test" This happens in both the GUI and TMSH.
bugs.conditions: -- A published policy exists in /Common. -- The published policy is attached to a virtual server in a different partition. -- Attempt to create and modify a draft of the policy.
bugs.impact: Inability to edit the published policy.

bugs.title: Bot Defense protection blocks Safari browser requests while using cross site redirect protection by 'Location' header
bugs.symptoms: Bot defense blocks a request containing a TSPD101 cookie in query string. TSPD101 is sent when using the Safari browser, and cross-site redirect protection is applied on a request.
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned. - Bot Defense profile attached to a virtual server. - Cross-site redirection is applied on a request. - Using the Safari browser.
bugs.impact: Cross-site requests are blocked during the grace period configured on the bot defense profile.
bugs.workaround: Disable browser verification in the bot defense profile.
bugs.fix: Cross-site redirect protection now works as expected when cookie is sent via query string.

bugs.title: VE: Predictable NIC ordering based on PCI coordinates until ordering is saved.
bugs.symptoms: The order of interfaces in BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) is determined by the Linux kernel. The order of interfaces on BIG-IP systems tmm does not match the one determined by the Linux.
bugs.conditions: -- Repeatedly deploy BIG-IP configurations within KVM with many (e.g., 6 or more) interfaces. -- Observe the order of devices on the PCI bus and the order that they are enumerated within tmm (1.1, 1.2, 1.3, etc.).
bugs.impact: Sometimes the order between the two does not match. This makes it difficult to reliably use the order with automation to ensure the right devices belong to the correct VLANs, and other operations.
bugs.workaround: Interrogate the MAC addresses of interfaces to map them against NIC definitions to determine the order.
bugs.fix: There is now a predictable NIC ordering based on PCI coordinates until ordering is saved.
bugs.behavior: The NIC ordering is now based on PCI co-ordinates, so you no longer need to interrogate the MAC addresses of interfaces to map them against NIC definitions to determine the order.

bugs.title: Tmm may fail a heartbeat on VE if unscheduled by busy hypervisor
bugs.symptoms: Tmm is killed by sod and restarts after failing to send a heartbeat message.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) running on a busy host system.
bugs.impact: Tmm restarts and recovers. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Upgrades to 13.1.1.2, 14.0.0, 14.0.0.1, or 14.0.0.2 from pre-12.1.3 can cause configurations to fail with GTM Pool Members
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading to 13.1.1.2, 14.0.0, 14.0.0.1, or 14.0.0.2 might result a configuration that fails to load due to a stray colon-character that gets added to the configuration file.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrade from pre-12.1.3 to 13.1.1.2, 14.0.0, 14.0.0.1, or 14.0.0.2. -- GTM Pool Members.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Remove stray colon-character from bigip_gtm.conf.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue preventing configurations from loading into 13.1.1.2, 14.0.0, 14.0.0.1, or 14.0.0.2 from a version before 12.1.3.

bugs.title: IP-related agents in Per-Request Policy do not work correctly when APM and SWG are configured
bugs.symptoms: IP-related agents fail.
bugs.conditions: 1. APM and SWG configured. 2. Any of the following IP related agents is added to the Per-Request Policy: a. Client IP Subnet Match b. Client Port Match c. IP Geolocation Lookup d. IP Reputation Lookup e. Server IP Subnet Match f. Server Port Match
bugs.impact: Agent fails to work properly and will take the fallback branch.
bugs.fix: IP-related agents in Per-Request policy now work correctly when APM and SWG are configured.

bugs.title: Chunked responses may be incorrectly handled by HTTP/2
bugs.symptoms: When a chunked HTTP response is serialized by HTTP/2, the chunking headers should be removed. This does not occur in some cases.
bugs.conditions: The HTTP/2 filter is used. Some other profiles are used on the same virtual. (In particular, the request logging profile triggers this issue.)
bugs.impact: The HTTP/2 payload will include chunking headers, corrupting it.
bugs.workaround: An iRule may be used to detect a HTTP/2 client, and forcibly turn on unchunking in the HTTP_RESPONSE event. Example: ltm rule unchunk_http2 { when HTTP_REQUEST { set is_http2 [HTTP2::active] } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { $is_http2 } { HTTP::payload unchunk } } }

bugs.title: mcpd might restart on secondary blades after modify sys httpd ssl-certchainfile
bugs.symptoms: On a chassis platform, if 'tmsh modify sys httpd ssl-certificate' is run immediately after creating a new certificate file, it's possible for mcpd to restart on the secondary blades. This happens when it takes longer for csyncd to copy the new certificate file to the other blades than it takes mcpd to send the modify message to the other blades.
bugs.conditions: Chassis platform with multiple blades. Setting the httpd ssl-certificate to a new file.
bugs.impact: mcpd stops on secondary blades, causing those blades to go offline for a short time while mcpd and other daemons restart.
bugs.workaround: When setting the httpd ssl-certificate to a new file, wait a few seconds after creating the file before issuing the tmsh modify command.

bugs.title: Some regions in Spain are returned with incorrect locations using the 'GeolocationCheck' agent
bugs.symptoms: Using the 'GeolocationCheck' agent exposes database inaccuracies. IP Address 213.60.113.177 is located in 'Galicia (Spain)', but geoip_lookup tool indicates 'Islas Baleares (Spain)'.
bugs.conditions: Using geoip_lookup tool to locate regions in Spain.
bugs.impact: Some regions in Spain are returned with incorrect locations.

bugs.title: Increase the limit of the maximum allowed timestamp for OAuth token processing for OAuth Client
bugs.symptoms: During OAuth token processing for OAuth Client, if the timestamp is set to a value greater than INT32_MAX (2147483647), the BIG-IP system posts an error message, but the error is not descriptive enough to assist in troubleshooting. The error message appears similar to the following: err apmd[14229]: 01490290:3: /Internet/Oauth_OpenAM_Preprod:Internet:46ea50d9:/Internet/server_act_oauth_client_ag: OAuth Client: failed for server '/Internet/server1' using 'authorization_code' grant type (client_id=oidc), error: stoi
bugs.conditions: -- OAuth token processing for OAuth Client. -- Timestamp value greater than INT32_MAX.
bugs.impact: The APM end user is not granted access because the the policy does not complete successfully.
bugs.fix: The maximum allowed timestamp is increased from INT32_MAX (2147483647) to 6249223209600, and now includes more descriptive error messages for better troubleshooting when the BIG-IP system receives invalid timestamps.

bugs.title: Default engineID may have different lengths
bugs.symptoms: The initial engineIDType on an unconfigured system is NETSNMP_RND. If the snmpd configuration file is read and there is no stored engine ID then one is generated based on current system time (and some other bits) to produce a random engineID. When randomly generated engineID changed length in release 14.0.0 of the BIG-IP to include some trailing zeros.
bugs.conditions: Use of unconfigured engineID on a clean install with version 14.0.0 or later. Note the engineIDType of NETSNMP_RND cannot be user configured.
bugs.impact: This can be confusing because the alert daemon and the snmp agent both issue traps and the alert daemon traps did not include the trailing zeros.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The bug has been fixed and the trailing zeros are no longer included in the randomly generated engine ID.

bugs.title: Configuring EngineID for SNMPv3 requires restart of the SNMP and Alert daemons
bugs.symptoms: Configuring EngineID for SNMPv3 does not take effect until the SNMP and Alert daemons are restarted.
bugs.conditions: Configure the EngineID for SNMPv3 using the tmsh command: modify sys snmp include 'EngineType n'
bugs.impact: The SNMPv3 value does not take effect.
bugs.workaround: Restart the daemons after changing the EngineID: restart /sys service snmpd restart /sys service alertd Note: The SNMP daemon should be restarted before the Alert daemon.
bugs.fix: The new EngineID is used after being configured, and no longer requires daemon restart.

bugs.title: TSO in software re-segments L3 fragments.
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 does not re-assemble fragments by default, but on a system with software-enabled TSO (sys db tm.tcpsegmentationoffload value disable), those fragments are erroneously re-segmented.
bugs.conditions: The behavior is encountered on BIG-IP Virtual Edition when setting sys db tm.tcpsegmentationoffload value disable, but does not cause a tmm core on Virtual Edition.
bugs.impact: Already-fragmented traffic is fragmented again.

bugs.title: Fix block size insecurity init and assign
bugs.symptoms: After an HA failover the block size insecurity checks were creating conditions for an infinite loop. This causes tmm to be killed by sod daemon via SIGABRT.
bugs.conditions: Rare not reproducible.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: The init and assign of block size insecurity were modified and debug checks added. A possible loop condition in ssl renegotiation was removed.

bugs.title: Querying vCMP Health Status May Show Stale Statistics
bugs.symptoms: Stale statistics collected while the guest was running a pre-13.1.0 version may periodically be seen when querying vCMP health status in the Configuration Utility or via tmsh show vcmp health commands.
bugs.conditions: This issue may be seen when all of the following conditions are met: - the vCMP guest is deployed on more than one blade - the vCMP guest is upgraded from a pre-13.1.0 release to 13.1.0 or above
bugs.impact: Health status is not always accurately reported
bugs.workaround: The issue may be resolved by setting the guest status temporarily to configured and then back to deployed.

bugs.title: External references in XML Profiles are not retrieved via defined HTTP proxy
bugs.symptoms: Externally referenced XML schema files in a XML Profile cannot be retrieved using a defined HTTP proxy.
bugs.conditions: -- An XML profile has externally referenced XML schema files. -- Outbound access from the device is only available using a HTTP proxy.
bugs.impact: The XML profile cannot be saved or enforced.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, the external referenced files can be uploaded to the XML Profile with the appropriate Import URL.

bugs.title: Portal Access: Issue with long 'data:' URL
bugs.symptoms: HTML page may contain a very long 'data:' URL. Portal Access cannot handle such URLs correctly.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with very long 'data:' similar to the following example: data:image/png;base64,... Such URLs might be several megabytes long.
bugs.impact: The rewrite plugin cannot process HTML pages with very long URLs and restarts. The page is not sent to the end user client; web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access handles very long 'data:' URLs correctly.

bugs.title: Changing monitor config with SASP monitor causes Virtual to flap
bugs.symptoms: If you change the monitor configuration for a pool or pool member to include the SASP monitor and add or remove an additional monitor (e.g., TCP), the pool members affected by this configuration change will be marked Down/Unavailable (RED) for some period of time (e.g., 5 seconds) after the change. During this time, if all pool members are marked down, any virtual servers associated with the pool are also marked down, interrupting traffic.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when changing the configured monitor for a pool or pool member in one of the following ways: 1. From a SASP monitor to a SASP plus another monitor. 2. From a SASP monitor plus another monitor, to a SASP monitor. 3. From a SASP monitor plus another monitor, to a SASP monitor plus a different monitor.
bugs.impact: Pool members affected by the monitor change are marked down by the SASP monitor until the SASP monitor receives member weights from the SASP GWM. If the monitor configuration change affects all pool members in a pool, any virtual servers configured to use that pool are also marked down during this period.
bugs.workaround: If some members of the pool are configured to use a different monitor than the other pool members, only a subset of pool members are marked down as the result of the monitor configuration change, and the corresponding virtual servers are not marked down due to the monitor configuration change.

bugs.title: DoSL7 attack is not detected when using multiple profiles with Behavioral Detection
bugs.symptoms: Setting up multiple DoS Application Profiles on the same Virtual Server via either iRules or LTM Policies causes DoSL7 attacks to not be detected or mitigated, if one of the profiles has Behavioral Detection enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple DoS profiles are configured on a single Virtual Server, either using the iRule DOSL7::enable command, or LTM Policies controlling the DoS profile. -- One of the DoS profiles on the Virtual Server has Behavioral Detection enabled, even if the Stress-Based Operation Mode is set to Off.
bugs.impact: DoSL7 attacks are not detected and not mitigated, with no indication that they are not.
bugs.workaround: Disable Behavioral Detection on all of the DoS profiles that are directly or indirectly associated with the Virtual Server. If Stress-Based Operation Mode is set to Off, then you might need to temporarily set Stress-Based to Transparent, disable the Behavioral checkboxes, and then set Stress-Based Operation mode back to Off.

bugs.title: PEM Gx/Sd session will support Redirect-Information AVP with URL address type and enforce HTTP Redirect
bugs.symptoms: HTTP Redirect action need to get enforced when Redirect-Information AVP with URL address type is received via Gx/Sd interface
bugs.conditions: When Redirect-Information AVP with URL address type is received via Gx/Sd interface
bugs.impact: HTTP Redirect action need to get applied
bugs.fix: PEM will support Redirect-Information AVP with URL address type and enforce HTTP redirect action
bugs.behavior: For Gx/Sd session, if dynamic rules with Redirect-Information AVP of type URL address is received PEM will enforce HTTP Redirect action.

bugs.title: Upgrades from releases earlier than 13.1.1 may fail when AD servers are invalid
bugs.symptoms: If an invalid Active Directory (AD) server is configured, upgrades to releases 13.1.1 and later might fail due to MCP validation that validates the AD server. The system reports an error in audit log (/var/log/audit): -- 01071d05:3: <domain-controller> is not a valid IP address or hostname.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade to 13.1.1 or later with invalid AD server configured.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Boot back into the previous volume and modify the Authentication AD domain controller to ensure that 'Hostname' under Domain Controllers is defined using FQDN. -- Alternatively, edit the bigip.conf configuration file within the upgraded volume to correct the issue, save the file, and reload the configuration. apm aaa active-directory /Common/ad-controller { admin-encrypted-password <xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx> admin-name admin domain example.local domain-controller <xxxxxx> <----------- Must be defined using FQDN domain-controllers { example { ip 192.168.1.50 } } use-pool disabled }

bugs.title: GTM virtual server status shows incorrect monitor IP address
bugs.symptoms: If a prober pool is assigned to a datacenter/server/virtual server after the monitor for that virtual server has already run on a non-prober-pool-member, the virtual server status (tooltip or 'tmsh show') does not update to show that probes are being sent from a prober-pool-member.
bugs.conditions: -- Prober pool assigned to a datacenter/server/virtual server. -- Assignment occurs after that virtual server's monitor has already run on a non-prober-pool-member.
bugs.impact: The virtual server tooltip and results from the 'tmsh show' command display possibly stale information.
bugs.workaround: Remove and re-add monitor to the virtual server.
bugs.fix: Not updating this information is intentional as an optimization. Therefore, the fix is to remove the IP info from virtual server status to avoid potential stale information being presented. The information is still preserved in debug log messages, etc.
bugs.behavior: Previously, the virtual server tooltip and results from the 'tmsh show' command did not update to show that probes were being sent from a prober-pool-member, if the monitor was assigned after the monitor already ran on a non-prober-pool-member. In this release, the tooltip and 'tmsh show' command do not report the IP info, so there is no possibility for presenting stale information or creating BIG-IP user confusion. Not updating this information is intentional as an optimization. The information is still preserved in debug log messages, etc.

bugs.title: Support dynamic CRL check for clientSSL profile
bugs.symptoms: Although dynamic CRL checks for server SSL profile are supported in earlier releases, CRL checks for client SSL profiles are not. The operation fails if you try to assign a CRL validator object to a client SSL profile: tmsh modify ltm profile client-ssl cssl crl my_crl
bugs.conditions: When trying to assign a CRL validator to a client SSL profile.
bugs.impact: Unable to dynamically verify the revocation status of the SSL certificate from the client side. Note: The static CRL file configuration still works. But without the (dynamic) CRL validator configuration, it cannot automatically fetch, check, and cache CRL files for certificates received.
bugs.workaround: You can partially work around this by developing scripts to keep changing the static CRL file configuration, for example: tmsh modify ltm profile client-ssl cssl crl-file /shared/xxx.crl
bugs.fix: Now you can configure a CRL validator object for a client SSL profile. The object automatically fetches, checks, caches, updates, and manages the CRL files, based on the CRL URLs on the SSL certificates whenever a certificate is received, so you no longer need to download, manage, and change the CRL files yourself.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system should trigger a HA failover event when expected HSB device is missing from PCI bus
bugs.symptoms: In some rare circumstances, the HSB device might drop off the PCI bus, resulting in the BIG-IP system not being able to pass traffic. However, no high availability (HA) failover condition is triggered, so the BIG-IP system stays active.
bugs.conditions: HSB drops off the PCI bus. This is caused in response to certain traffic patterns (FPGA issue) that are yet to be determined.
bugs.impact: No failover to standby unit after this error condition, causing site outage.
bugs.fix: Now the active BIG-IP system fails over to the standby when HSB on the active unit drops off the PCI bus.

bugs.title: IKEv2 potential double free of object when async request queueing fails
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core during an IPsec cleanup of a failed async operation.
bugs.conditions: When an async IPsec crypto operation fails to queue.
bugs.impact: Restart of tmm. All tunnels lost must be re-established.
bugs.workaround: No workaround known at this time.

bugs.title: AWS: Disk resizing in m5/c5 instances fails silently.
bugs.symptoms: Resizing the disk in an m5/c5 instance in AWS has no impact on the disk size, and this operation fails silently.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system deployed in AWS with m5/c5 instance type that uses NVME disks instead of the usual native paravirt disks.
bugs.impact: Disk resizing fails; administrators cannot grow the instance disk in response to their requirements and instance utilization post-deployment.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: AWS: Disk resizing now works as expected.

bugs.title: vCMP guest observes connflow reset when a CMP state change occurs.
bugs.symptoms: There is a connflow reset when a CMP state change occurs on a vCMP guest. The system posts log messages similar to the following: CMP Forwarder expiration.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP configured. -- Associated virtual server has a FastL4 profile with loose init and loose close enabled.
bugs.impact: This might interrupt a long-lived flow and eventually cause an outage.
bugs.fix: The system now drops the connflow instead of resetting it.

bugs.title: In LTM Policy Rule page, replacing 'forward node' action with 'forward pool' does not delete the node property
bugs.symptoms: On the LTM Policy Rule page, replacing 'forward node' action with 'forward pool' does not delete the node property.
bugs.conditions: An LTM policy rule exists, where the action is forward and the object type is node, and the node field is filled out.
bugs.impact: The modified rule shows the new configuration with the pool, while it still uses the old configuration with the node.
bugs.workaround: Delete the existing action and add a new action with the correct pool.
bugs.fix: Changing the object type from node to pool now clears the existing node or virtual server property in the forward action.

bugs.title: Incorrect error message: "Can't find pool []: Pool was not found" even though Pool member is defined with port any(0)
bugs.symptoms: When a pool member is defined with port any(0), calling the GetPoolMember() function, gives an incorrect error message that the pool member was not found.
bugs.conditions: Pool member with port any(0)
bugs.impact: Wrong error message printed to avrd.log
bugs.fix: Added a flag that indicates whether or not to print an error message to the GetPoolMember() function.

bugs.title: Clientssl accepts non-SSL traffic when cipher-group is configured
bugs.symptoms: Clientssl accepts Non-SSL traffic even when "Non-SSL Connections" is disabled.
bugs.conditions: In clientssl profile, Cipher Group is configured and one of the "No SSL/TLS/DTLS" option is enabled.
bugs.impact: Connections to VIP with clientssl profile are not encrypted. If SSL client authentication is enabled, plaintext request is successful meaning that client can get access to resources otherwise requiring a valid client certificate.
bugs.workaround: Use Cipher String instead of Cipher Group when configuring clientssl profile.
bugs.fix: Properly validate cipher suites in a cipher group before use.

bugs.title: Upgrades from 10.2.x fail due to empty virtual address lines in the configuration
bugs.symptoms: In 10.2.x it is possible to have 'empty' virtual address lines in the configuration like this: virtual address 10.10.10.10 {} Lines such as these cause failures when upgrading to any version of BIG-IP software that includes the functionality to to add 'arp disable' to virtual addresses that do not have an explicit configuration for their ARP setting. This functionality is present beginning with software version 11.5.0.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Empty' virtual address lines in the configuration. -- Upgrading to a version of BIG-IP software that includes the functionality to to add 'arp disable' to virtual addresses that do not have an explicit configuration for their ARP setting.
bugs.impact: The upgrade fails without a clear error message.
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to 11.5.0 first, and then upgrade to the desired version.

bugs.title: Gratuitous ARP not sent on interface up
bugs.symptoms: Gratuitous ARP not seen when an interface comes up: different behavior depending on software version. On BIG-IP software version 11.6.x and on BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE), version 13.1.x, when interface is UP, after 3 seconds, the BIG-IP system sends GARP out. On version 12.1.2，the BIG-IP system does not send GARP upon interface UP.
bugs.conditions: The interface transition from DOWN to UP state.
bugs.impact: No GARP for self-ip addresses on interfaces.

bugs.title: Custom DIAMETER monitor requests do not have their 'request' flag set
bugs.symptoms: Using the technique detailed in the Article: K14536: Customizing the BIG-IP Diameter monitor https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14536 to create custom DIAMETER monitor requests fails for any request that uses the numeric form of a DIAMETER command code, because the 'request' flag is not set in the DIAMETER packet.
bugs.conditions: -- Using custom DIAMETER monitor requests. -- Using numeric DIAMETER command codes.
bugs.impact: The monitor probes fail because the BIG-IP system does not set the DIAMETER 'request' flag for requests it sends when using a numeric value for the command code, so the DIAMETER server thinks it is a response
bugs.fix: Ensured that the 'request' flag is set for all DIAMETER monitor requests.

bugs.title: Tmsh loads schema versions 12.x and earlier which are no longer supported
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems support directly upgrading to a new version from the previous two major BIG-IP versions. Thus, upgrading to BIG-IP version 15.x from BIG-IP version 13.x, 14.x or 15.x is supported. Similarly, tmsh and iControl REST interfaces allow a previous version to be specified, to interpret commands and format responses according to the specified schema versions. Thus, schema versions 13.x, 14.x and 15.x are supported by tmsh and iControlREST. However: Affected versions of BIG-IP version 15.x still load unsupported 12.x and 11.x tmsh schema versions. Affected versions of BIG-IP version 14.x still load unsupported 11.x tmsh schema versions.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on affected versions of BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Instances of tmsh consume more memory (averaging approximately 16MB per instance on BIG-IP version 15.1.0) due to loading unsupported 12.x and 11.x schemas. If a large number of tmsh instances are loaded (due to a large number of users logged in, and particularly a large number of remotely-authenticated users), tmsh memory consumption can contribute to out-of-memory conditions.
bugs.fix: Schema versions 12.x and 11.x are no longer loaded by tmsh or available via iControlREST, except for the following versions: 11.5.0, 11.5.4, 11.5.5, 12.0.0, 12.1.0
bugs.behavior: This may impact you if you are running BIG-IP version 15.1.0 or later and attempting to use tmsh schema versions or iControl REST API versions 12.x or 11.x, such as: -- Setting the current tmsh version to a 12.x or 11.x version: tmsh modify cli version active 12.1.3 -- Attempting to load a configuration saved in a Single Configuration File (SCF) from a 12.x or 11.x version: tmsh load sys config file my_saved_12.1.3_config.scf -- Specifying a 12.x or 11.x version when making iControl REST API calls: curl -sk -u admin:admin GET https://<mgmt.ip.address>/mgmt/tm/sys/console?ver=12.1.3 Note: This restriction does not affect upgrading from 12.x or 11.x versions, or loading configuration from a UCS file for such versions: tmsh load sys ucs my_saved_12.1.3_config.ucs This is because UCS files include a backup of the tmsh schema version under which they were saved, which is then imported as needed when loading the configuration from the UCS file.

bugs.title: TMM crashes due to memory leak found during SSL OCSP with C3D feature enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM raises a segmentation violation and restarts.
bugs.conditions: -- Set up client-side and server-side SSL with: + Client Certificate Constrained Delegation (C3D) enabled. + OCSP enabled. -- Supply SSL traffic.
bugs.impact: Memory leaks when traffic is supplied. When traffic intensifies, more memory leaks occur, and eventually, tmm raises a segmentation fault, crashes, and restarts itself. All SSL connections get terminated. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable C3D.
bugs.fix: Memory no longer leaks when C3D and OCSP are both enabled with client SSL and server SSL set up.

bugs.title: QOE module is deprecated and upgrade causes QOE config to be removed
bugs.symptoms: When upgrade happens to 15.0.0, some QOE related configuration will be removed. 1. Virtual server will not have QOE profile and QOE iRule. 2. PEM rule will not have QOE reporting.
bugs.conditions: When upgrade happens to 15.0.0, some QOE related configuration will be removed.
bugs.impact: QOE reporting and iRules will not work as intended.
bugs.fix: QOE related configuration will be removed and following warnings will be logged in ltm.log file to inform the user of change in configuration: 1. Virtual Server containing QOE profile and iRule: Removing QOE profile (<ProfileName>) from the virtual server (<VirtualServerName>) because QOE module is deprecated. The ltm rule (<iRuleName>) assigned to the virtual server (<VirtualServerName>) contains at least one 'QOE::*' command. Detaching ltm rule from virtual server because QOE module is deprecated. 2. PEM rule containing QOE reporting: PEM Rule '<PEMRuleName>' : Disabling QOE reporting action because QOE module is deprecated.

bugs.title: Signature Overrides for Content Profiles do not work after signature update
bugs.symptoms: JSON profile signature override does not include legacy signature after Automatic Signature Update (ASU).
bugs.conditions: Signature override on content profile ASU with major update to targeted sig.
bugs.impact: -- Unexpected block on a previously white-listed signature. -- Confusing logging for why the signature was blocked (should indicate it was due to using an old signature version).
bugs.workaround: -- Create the signature override at higher context, e.g., the URL. Removing the URL context override again keeps it fixed. -- Enforce new version of sig globally.
bugs.fix: Signature Overrides for Content Profiles now work after signature update.

bugs.title: Ensure 8 GB RAM vCMP guests have no more than three modules provisioned before upgrading
bugs.symptoms: On earlier builds of BIG-IP software (specifically, version 14.0.0 and earlier), TMSH might allow vCMP Guests with 8 GB or less to provision more than three modules, even though the recommended practice counsels against doing so. Upgrading a system with a vCMP guest configured with more than three modules results in a 'failed load,' as returned in 'tmsh show sys mcp' command results. This configuration might potentially cause out-of-memory problems once traffic is passed.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP guests with 8 GB RAM or less. -- Four or more modules provisioned. -- Upgrade the system.
bugs.impact: Possible out-of-memory errors on BIG-IP systems once traffic gets passed.
bugs.workaround: Provision no more than three modules on 8 GB RAM vCMP guests before upgrading. If more than three modules are already provisioned, before upgrading vCMP guests with 8 GB or less of RAM, remove provisioning on some modules to ensure that there are no more than three modules provisioned before upgrading.
bugs.fix: The process halts with an error when attempting to provision more than three modules on vCMP guests with 8 GB or less of RAM.
bugs.behavior: In earlier releases, you could provision more than three modules on vCMP guests with 8 GB or less of RAM. Now, the provisioning process halts with an error when attempting to do so.

bugs.title: TMM crash (SIGFPE) when starting on a vCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: A log message in /var/log/tmm similar to the following: Assertion 'Hash type successfully set' failed.
bugs.conditions: A vCMP guest running either: - v13.x release of 13.1.3.6 or later - v12.x release of 12.1.5.3 or later A vCMP hypervisor that is running: - v13.x release of 13.1.3.4 or lower - v12.x release or 12.1.5.2 or lower - v11.x release Any vCMP guests running v14.x or later are not affected.
bugs.impact: Tmm may initially fail to start, log an SIGFPE, and then might or might not start normally afterwards. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Either: -- Upgrade the vCMP Hypervisor to the latest release. -- Upgrade the guest to v14.1.0 or later. It may also help to remove the cached libdag on the guest, and restart tmm by running the following commands on the guest: rm -f /var/run/libdag.so_* && bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes during startup with SIGFPE

bugs.title: DNSX can no longer receive DNS NOTIFY messages on self ips
bugs.symptoms: DNSX can no longer receive DNS NOTIFY messages on self ips.
bugs.conditions: User has configured DNSX as a DNS slave/secondary server that listens for DNS NOTIFY messages from a master DNS server.
bugs.impact: DNSX acting as slave/secondary can no longer receive or process DNS NOTIFY messages via self ips.
bugs.workaround: If your infrastructure relies on DNS NOTIFY messages being sent to DNSX slave/seconadry servers via self ips, you will need to modify the configuration on their Master DNS server(s) and also on the BIG-IP with DNSX acting as a slave secondary. The Master needs to be configured to send DNS NOTIFY messages to either to a BIG-IP Virtual (UDP & TCP) with DNSX enabled on the associated DNS profile or configured to send to the management ip of the BIG-IP, or both. Note if using the management ip to recieve DNS NOTIFY for DNSX, you must enable this behavior by setting the dnsexpress.notifyport db variable to a port number besides zero.

bugs.title: VMware Horizon PCoIP transport is not supported for IPv6 targets
bugs.symptoms: When APM is configured as a proxy for Vmware Horizon and the Horizon backends are accessible only via IPv6 address, user is not able to access resources over PCoIP protocol.
bugs.conditions: - APM is configured as proxy for Vmware Horizon - A virtual desktop host (Horizon backend) can only be accessed via IPv6 - Vmware VCS (View Connection Server) is configured with Virtual "HTTP(s) Secure Tunnel" option disabled - User tries to open a desktop via APM with native Horizon client using PCoIP protocol.
bugs.impact: User is not able to access the desktop. Instead, this error is displayed: "This desktop is not addressable with your current settings. Please contact your system administrator"
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: The HTTP URI is not always parsed correctly
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP URI exposed by the HTTP::uri iRule command, Traffic Policies, or used by ASM is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile is configured. -- The URI is inspected.
bugs.impact: If the URI is used for security checks, then those checks might be bypassed.
bugs.fix: The HTTP URI is parsed in a more robust manner.

bugs.title: VMware Horizon HTML5 client launch results in certificate mismatch warning
bugs.symptoms: VMware Horizon HTML5 client launch from APM Webtop results in certificate mismatch warning, as browser is redirected to IP address instead of host name due to use of "view.proxy_addr" session variable.
bugs.conditions: VMware Horizon HTML5 client is used. "view.proxy_addr" session variable is set to external IP address.
bugs.impact: Certificate mismatch warning is shown.
bugs.workaround: Unset "view.proxy_addr" session variable, it's required only for PCoIP clients and HTML5 client uses Blast protocol.
bugs.fix: "view.proxy_addr" session variable is now ignored for Blast protocol, which lets VMware Horizon HTML5 client to launch without warnings, even when this session variable is configured.

bugs.title: First successful auth iControl REST requests will now be logged in audit and secure log files
bugs.symptoms: Previously, when making a REST request from a client for the first time and it is successful, this action was not logged. Just subsequent REST calls were logged or initial failed REST calls from a client were logged.
bugs.conditions: Making a successfully auth-ed initial REST request from a new client to BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP admins would not know when a new client first made a successful REST call to BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Now on the first successful REST call, these actions are logged in /var/log/audit and /var/log/secure log files. Here's an example of what shows in audit log: -- info httpd(pam_audit)[26561]: 01070417:6: AUDIT - user bart2 - RAW: httpd(pam_audit): user=bart2(bart2) partition=[All] level=Guest tty=(unknown) host=10.10.10.10 attempts=1 start="Fri Oct 12 17:07:53 2018" end="Fri Oct 12 17:07:53 2018". Here's an example of what shows in secure log: -- info httpd(pam_audit)[26561]: user=bart2(bart2) partition=[All] level=Guest tty=(unknown) host=10.10.10.10 attempts=1 start="Fri Oct 12 17:07:53 2018" end="Fri Oct 12 17:07:53 2018". -- info httpd(pam_audit)[26561]: 01070417:6: AUDIT - user usr2 - RAW: httpd(pam_audit): user=usr2(usr2) partition=[All] level=Guest tty=(unknown) host=10.10.10.10 attempts=1 start="Fri Oct 12 17:07:53 2018" end="Fri Oct 12 17:07:53 2018". Subsequent REST calls will continue to be logged normally.
bugs.behavior: Now on the first successful REST call, these actions are logged in /var/log/audit and /var/log/secure log files. Subsequent REST calls will continue to be logged normally.

bugs.title: PCCD may exhaust system memory when compiling
bugs.symptoms: PCCD will endlessly allocate memory during some compilations, causing the device to become unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: Certain rare configurations, such as having a single rule with 4095 vlans in Zone configurations.
bugs.impact: Device becomes unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Remove the offending configuration change. In order to do this, first run "bigstart stop pccd" in order to reclaim the memory that PCCD has consumed, and then edit the configuration.

bugs.title: DHCPv6 does not have the ability to override the hop limit from the client.
bugs.symptoms: DHCPv6 packet may be dropped by a device after the DHCP relay if the client provided hop limit is 1.
bugs.conditions: DHCPv6 Relay configured on the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Loss of DHCPv6 service.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Configurable hop limit over-ride capabilities provided for client sent DHCPv6 packets.

bugs.title: DoSL7-related logs are not throttled
bugs.symptoms: The tmm log has lots of DoSL7-related messages.
bugs.conditions: The system encounters a condition that may lead to notice messages.
bugs.impact: tmm log is flooding with messages.
bugs.fix: The DoSL7 module is no longer floods the tmm logs.

bugs.title: SNMP MIBs and docs are included in two RPMs
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP .iso file includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of net-snmp (the alert daemon uses 32bit and the snmp daemon uses 64 bit). Both the net-snmp-libs x86_64 and i686 RPMs include the MIBs and the docs.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the SNMP MIBs and docs in the RPMs.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. net-snmp documentation is provided by two files when it should be provided by just one.
bugs.fix: SNMP MIBs and docs are included in only one RPM now.

bugs.title: BGP route map community value: either component cannot be set to 65535
bugs.symptoms: The community value for BGP route map entries should allow values of 1-65535 for both components, but it is not allowing 65535 for either component.
bugs.conditions: -- Using BGP route map community values. -- Attempting to set one or both components to 65535.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the full range of BGP route map community values
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: This release allows the usage of 65535 for either (or both) BGP route map community values.

bugs.title: dynconfd restarts if FQDN template node deleted while IP address change in progress
bugs.symptoms: The dynconfd daemon may crash and restart if an FQDN template node is deleted (by user action or config sync) while ephemeral nodes are in the process of being created, and deleted as the result of new IP addresses being returned by a recent DNS query.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on BIG-IP version 14.0.0.3 (and BIG-IP versions 13.1.x or v12.1.x with engineering hotfixes for ID 720799, ID 721621 and ID 726319), under the following conditions: 1. A DNS query returns a different set of IP addresses for one or more FQDN names. 2. While new ephemeral node(s) are being created (for new IP addresses and deleted (for old IP addresses), an FQDN template node is deleted (either by user action or config sync).
bugs.impact: The dynconfd daemon crashes and restarts. Ephemeral nodes may not be updated in a timely manner while the dynconfd daemon is restarting.
bugs.fix: The dynconfd daemon does not crash and restart if an FQDN template node is deleted while ephemeral nodes are in the process of being created and deleted as the result of new IP addresses being returned by a recent DNS query.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system sends Product-Name AVP in CER with Mandatory bit set
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system always sets the Mandatory bit flag for Product-Name AVPs in DIAMETER Capabilities Exchange Request messages.
bugs.conditions: Using DIAMETER to send a Capabilities Exchange Request message with the Product-Name AVP.
bugs.impact: If the DIAMETER peer is intolerant of this Mandatory bit being set, it will reset the DIAMETER connection.
bugs.workaround: Configure an iRule in the MRF transport-config, for example: ltm rule workaround { when DIAMETER_EGRESS { if {[serverside] && [DIAMETER::command] == "257" } { DIAMETER::avp flags set 269 0 } } }
bugs.fix: This release always clears the Mandatory bit for Product-Name AVPs in DIAMETER Capabilities Exchange Request messages.

bugs.title: Enabling or disabling a Distributed Application results in a small memory leak
bugs.symptoms: Enabling or disabling a Distributed Application results in an 8 byte memory leak.
bugs.conditions: Enabling or disabling a Distributed Application.
bugs.impact: 8 bytes of memory are leaked every time a Distributed Application is enabled or disabled. If Distributed Applications are repeatedly programmatically enabled and disabled, over time, the system might eventually exhaust all available memory.
bugs.fix: Enabling or disabling a Distributed Application no longer results in a memory leak.

bugs.title: Config sync of APM policy fails with Cannot update_indexes validation error.
bugs.symptoms: Config sync operation fails for APM policy when policy item of same name points to different agent on source and target The system posts errors similar to the following: Sync error on rfang-vemgmt.lab.labnet.com: Load failed from /Common/rfang-ve-3mgmt.lab.labnet.com 01070734:3: Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (access_policy_item_agent) object ID (/Common/resm_act_message_box_1 /Common/resm_act_message_box_ag_1). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:access_policy_item_agent status:13)"
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: 1. Configure a failover device group containing two BIG-IP systems. 2. Create an APM access profile on one unit. + Launch VPE for the policy. + Add a macro. + In macro add an agent, e.g., Message box. + Add macro to the main policy. 3. Initiate config sync to another device. 4. On one BIG-IP system, add another Message box agent using the same macro. On the other BIG-IP system, make a copy of the access profile. 5. On either BIG-IP system, initiate another config sync operation.
bugs.impact: Unable to sync configuration in a failover device group.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this using the following procedure: 1. On the device receiving the config sync, delete the APM policies that contain the referenced APM policy items. 2. Perform an overwrite-config-sync operation from the sending device to this device.

bugs.title: OpenSSH hardening
bugs.symptoms: The default OpenSSH configuration does not follow best practices for security hardening.
bugs.conditions: Administrative SSH access enabled.
bugs.impact: OpenSSH does not follow best practices.
bugs.fix: The default OpenSSH configuration includes best practices for security hardening.

bugs.title: Protocol Security logging profiles cause slow ASM upgrade and apply policy
bugs.symptoms: ASM upgrade and apply policy are delayed by an additional 3 seconds for each virtual server associated with a Protocol Security logging profile (regardless of whether ASM is active on that virtual server). During upgrade, all active policies are applied, which leads to multiple delays for each policy.
bugs.conditions: There are multiple virtual servers associated with Protocol Security logging profiles.
bugs.impact: ASM upgrade and apply policy are delayed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: While the client has been closed, iRule function should not try to check on a closed session
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores. System posts a message: access::session exists is used during CLIENT_CLOSED iRule event.
bugs.conditions: -- Client has closed the connection. -- iRule function tries to check on a closed session. -- An 'access session::exists' command is used inside the iRule event CLIENT_CLOSED.
bugs.impact: tmm may core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the iRule command 'access session::exists' inside CLIENT_CLOSED.
bugs.fix: Command execution of 'access::session exists' is now prevented in the iRule event CLIENT_CLOSED.

bugs.title: APM iRule events intermittently fail to execute
bugs.symptoms: ACCESS_PER_REQUEST_AGENT_EVENT iRule event intermittently fails to execute.
bugs.conditions: No particular sequence of events that reliably triggers this. Initially thought to be happening when modifying iRules while running traffic.
bugs.impact: ACCESS_PER_REQUEST_AGENT_EVENT iRule event will not run and the iRule commands in it will not be executed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Some SSO methods may work inappropriately when using OTP Generate agent
bugs.symptoms: Password-based single sign-on (SSO) methods (such as HTTP basic, NTLM, Form Based) may not work because the OTP Generate agent overwrites the session.logon.last.password session variable with the one-time password.
bugs.conditions: Access policy contains 'OTP Generate' agent and the Access Profile has an assigned SSO method.
bugs.impact: Some SSO methods may not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: 1. Use a 'Variable Assign' agent to store the APM end user's password in a temporary session variable. 2. Use that as the source in the SSO credential mapping agent.
bugs.fix: This release adds an 'OTP Source' field in the v1 (per-session) OTP verify agent.

bugs.title: TMM panics after a large number of LSN remote picks
bugs.symptoms: TMM panics with the assertion "nexthop ref valid" failed. This occurs after a large number of remote picks cause the nexthop reference count to overflow.
bugs.conditions: A LSN Pool and remote picks. Remote picks occur when the local TMM does not have any addresses or port blocks available. Remote picks are more likely when inbound and hairpin connections are enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM restarts. Traffic is interrupted.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer panics regardless of the number of remote picks.

bugs.title: virtual server with perm profile drops traffic received from Vxlan-GRE tunnel interface
bugs.symptoms: virtual server with perm profile drops traffic received from Vxlan-GRE tunnel interface.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with pem profile and Vxlan-GRE tunnel interface.
bugs.impact: Traffic drop.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Websso fails to decrypt secured session variables
bugs.symptoms: Whenever websso tries to decrypt secure session variables, the following error is seen /var/log/apm: Aug 15 21:36:25 abcd err websso.0[20421]: 014d0028:3: /Common/Test_PRP:Common:2b8e7abc: Master Decrypt failed for user test with error 'ckDecrypt: invalid ciphertext' Aug 15 21:36:25 abcd info websso.0[20421]: 014d0009:6: /Common/Test_PRP:Common:2b8e7abc: Websso basic authentication for user 'test' using config '/Common/sso_test_obj'
bugs.conditions: - Per-req policy is attached to virtual server. - Secure subsession variables are assigned to session variables using Variable Assign Agent in per-req policy. - SSO Configuration Select agent is used in per-req policy.
bugs.impact: Single Sign-On (SSO) won't work correctly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 may garble large headers
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP/2 filter may incorrectly encode large headers.
bugs.conditions: A header that encodes to larger than 2048 bytes.
bugs.impact: Application functionality may be disrupted because large header values, such as for cookies, may be truncated when passed to the endpoint.
bugs.fix: The HTTP/2 filter now correctly encodes large HTTP headers.

bugs.title: Upgrade PingAccess SDK used by BIG-IP APM to v1.1.3
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading PingAccess SDK from v1.0.0 to v1.1.3
bugs.conditions: The SDK is upgraded during system upgrade.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP APM will internally use PingAccess SDK v1.1.3 when interacting with PingAccess servers.
bugs.workaround: Not Applicable.
bugs.fix: Upgraded PingAccess SDK used by BIG-IP APM to the v1.1.3, applicable when BIG-IP APM interacts with PingAccess servers.

bugs.title: Missing data for Firewall Events Statistics
bugs.symptoms: Statistical information that is collected for Firewall event, has some data that is getting lost and not reported. When this is taking place, the following message appears at avrd log: Some rows of load_stat_firewall_events_<some number> not loaded
bugs.conditions: AFM is used, no particular condition that leads to this situation of losing some of the stats, usually takes place under heavy activity.
bugs.impact: Statistical reports of Firewall Events are missing some the the activity that actually took place.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Issue with missing data was fixed.

bugs.title: DoS-related reports might not contain some of the activity that took place
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, some telemetry data of DoS related activity is lost.
bugs.conditions: No specific condition other than using the BIG-IP system anti-DDoS feature.
bugs.impact: DoS related reports might not contain some of the activity that takes place.
bugs.fix: Issue was fixed, all telemetry data is collected without errors.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not throw error when intermediate CA is missing the "Basic Constraints" and "CA:True" in its extension
bugs.symptoms: An intermediate CA certificate should be considered invalid if the certificate does not contain both 'Basic Constraints: critical' and 'CA:TRUE' in its extension. The BIG-IP system does not enforce this.
bugs.conditions: The SSL profile has peer-cert-mode set to require and untrusted-cert-response-control set to drop.
bugs.impact: The system might unexpectedly accept the SSL connection while the peer is using an inappropriate certificate.
bugs.fix: With this fix, if the SSL profile has peer-cert-mode set to require and untrusted-cert-response-control set to drop, the system drops the SSL handshake if the peer's CA certificate does not contain both 'Basic Constraints: critical' and 'CA:TRUE' in its extension.
bugs.behavior: When authenticating a peer's SSL certificate, the system requires a CA certificate to have the 'Basic Constraints' and 'CA:True' in its extension, like this: X509v3 Basic Constraints: critical CA:TRUE If an SSL profile has peer-cert-mode set to require and untrusted-cert-response-control set to drop, the system drops the handshake if the peer's CA certificate does not satisfy this requirement.

bugs.title: Wrong certificate can be chosen during SSL handshake
bugs.symptoms: If two certificates of the same type are configured in an SSL profile, one marked `usage CA' and the other not, the wrong one could be chosen during the handshake.
bugs.conditions: Two certificates of the same type are configured in an SSL profile.
bugs.impact: The wrong certificate could be chosen during the handshake.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure two certificates of the same type on an SSL profile.

bugs.title: Fixed crash related to DNSSEC key rollover
bugs.symptoms: When running out of memory, a DNSSKEY rollover event can cause a tmm core dump.
bugs.conditions: System low/out of memory. DNSSKEY rollover event.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue in DNSSEC Key Rollover event that can cause a crash.

bugs.title: Specifying a larger system disk during VE launch requires manual reboot for the increase to go into effect
bugs.symptoms: It is allowed to specify larger system disk size during VE launch. The larger disk will be allocated, but VE will not be able to use the extra space initially. Manual reboot will allow VE to use the extra space. Desired behavior for VE is to reboot by itself.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you launch VE with a larger system disk in the initial version of 14.1
bugs.impact: BIG-IP cannot use the extra space
bugs.workaround: Reboot VE
bugs.fix: If a larger system disk size is specified during VE launch, it will be allocated. But VE will not be able to use the extra space initially. Manual reboot will allow VE to use the extra space.

bugs.title: After upgrade, dhclient overwrites configured hostname, even when 'sys management-dhcp' does not contain the 'host-name' in the request-options.
bugs.symptoms: The configured hostname is overwritten by dhclient after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- DHCP enabled. -- Custom hostname configured using the procedure described in K45728203: AWS generates the BIG-IP VE instance host name to include the host name's private IP address :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K45728203, instead of using the one provided by the DHCP server.
bugs.impact: Incorrect hostname assigned to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Change the DHCP settings, and issue the following command to correct the name without losing connectivity to management: # tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp disabled; tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp enabled
bugs.fix: Disable and reenable dhclient to fix the dhclient overwritten hostname after upgrade when 'sys management-dhcp' does not contain the 'host-name' in the request-options.

bugs.title: Rolling DNSSEC Keys may stop generating after BIG-IP restart
bugs.symptoms: Rolling DNSSEC Keys may stop generating when a BIG-IP system restart.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system gets restarted by calling 'bigstart restart' command.
bugs.impact: Rolling DNSSEC keys can stop generating.
bugs.fix: Rolling DNSSEC Keys no longer stop regenerating after BIG-IP restart

bugs.title: The name of the ltmPoolMemberStatCurrentConnsPerSec statistic is confusing
bugs.symptoms: The ltmPoolMemberStatCurrentConnsPerSec statistic is maintained only when rate limiting is configured for the LTM pool member. The statistic records the last value when the rate limit was hit.
bugs.conditions: When accessing SNMP statistics for pool members, and viewing the values for CurrentConns.
bugs.impact: Values might be confusing when using SNMP to monitor LTM pool members.
bugs.fix: The description text has been updated as follows: snmptranslate -Td F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmVirtualServStatCurrentConnsPerSec snmptranslate -Td F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmNodeAddrStatCurrentConnsPerSec snmptranslate -Td F5-BIGIP-LOCAL-MIB::ltmPoolMemberStatCurrentConnsPerSec

bugs.title: Adding alias for a WideIP with the same name as an alias from another WideIP will replace the previous alias
bugs.symptoms: WideIP alias will be replaced.
bugs.conditions: There is an existing alias for a WideIP and adding the same alias for another WideIP.
bugs.impact: The previous WideIP will be replaced.
bugs.workaround: Avoid adding existing WideIP for other WideIP.

bugs.title: GUI does not reflect updates made to a peer device's pool monitor
