bugs.symptoms: In a sync-failover configuration with a gateway fail-safe pool and a peer member monitored by the peer device, when updating a peer-owned health monitor, the change is not automatically shown in the GUI. For example: BIG-IP A and BIG-IP B are in a sync-failover configuration. BIG-IP A has a gateway pool Pool_A configured with monitor Monitor_A. Using the BIG-IP B GUI to change the monitor for Pool_A, the updated monitor is not reflected in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Sync-failover configuration with a gateway fail-safe pool and a peer member monitored by the peer device. -- Update the peer-owned health monitor.
bugs.impact: The change is successfully made but is not reflected in the GUI status.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the GUI or reload the configuration after making the update.

bugs.title: Tmm may be killed during snapshot creation on VMware ESXi
bugs.symptoms: tmm is sometimes killed by sod during snapshot creation when running on VMware ESXi.
bugs.conditions: An attempt to snapshot a running BIG-IP guest is made. This can cause the instance to be descheduled by the host upon which it is running which prevents tmm from touching its watchdog. Upon being scheduled to run, if sod runs before tmm can update the watchdog, it will kill tmm. A message indicating that tmm did not run for an extended period of time may be logged such as: 01010029:5: Clock advanced by 40124 ticks This message indicates generally that tmm did not run and can indicate other types of issues as well.
bugs.impact: Traffic processing can be severely impacted while the snapshot operation is proceeding regardless of whether tmm restarts or not. If tmm is restarted, production traffic will not be processed until it is finished restarting.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Traffic Intelligence system-generated presets are not saved to config file, and GUI allows them to be deleted
bugs.symptoms: Traffic Intelligence system-generated presets (those with name ce_*) are not saved to the config file. As a result, changes are lost on mcpd restart. In addition, the GUI allows them to be deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM license with Traffic Classification feature flag enabled. --Create ltm policy and attach system preset, save sys config and run the command: bigstart restart. -- Use the GUI to try to delete system-generated presets.
bugs.impact: GUI allows system-generated presets to be deleted. Changes made to those presets are lost upon bigstart restart.
bugs.workaround: None. Or use custom profile.

bugs.title: Traffic intelligence hitless upgrade uses load sys config
bugs.symptoms: Traffic intelligence (cec) uses load sys config on each hitless upgrade. This may cause configuration load to fail if the configuration has some errors, and hence virtual servers may go down.
bugs.conditions: When the system triggers manual or automatic hitless upgrade for traffic classification.
bugs.impact: System may go offline if the configuration has errors.
bugs.workaround: Disable automatic hitless upgrade for traffic intelligence.
bugs.fix: Update the hitless upgrade scripts to avoid load sys config while loading new IM package. Now, IM will load only the new classification_update.conf file as a part of hitless upgrade.

bugs.title: Bladed unit goes offline after UCS install
bugs.symptoms: Unit goes offline after UCS install. Secondary blades go offline. This lasts about a minute, and then the system goes back online.
bugs.conditions: After UCS install.
bugs.impact: -- Limited high availability (HA) capabilities (failover, sync, mirroring, etc.). -- Cluster reduced to a single blade immediately after UCS install, which might impact performance.

bugs.title: Adding a default tmm gateway in AWS breaks failover between two instances if the default tmm gateway can't provide route to the ec2 metadata service at 169.254.169.254.
bugs.symptoms: Instance failover breaks with the following messages in /var/log/ltm: /usr/libexec/aws/aws-failover-tgactive.sh (traffic-group-1): Instance sanity check failed with error: /usr/libexec/aws/aws-failover-tgactive.sh (traffic-group-1): ('Connection aborted.', error(111, 'Connection refused'))
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP is deployed in AWS with multiple NICs. - Also, the BIG-IP is part of a failover group. - The Failover/HA in AWS depends on access to the instance metadata provided by the EC2 cloud via the http endpoint at 169.254.169.254. - The default gateway provided by AWS through DHCP ensures access to this metadata endpoint without any additional configuration. However, when using a custom default gateway, the access to the instance metadata endpoint might not work.
bugs.impact: As moving the elastic-ip between the Active and Stand-by instances breaks, the failover can't complete and the new Active instance can't takeover the BIG-IP operations.
bugs.workaround: Add the ip rule for the link local address 169.254.169.254 as following: ip rule add to 169.254.169.254 lookup 245

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS and GTM DNSSEC security exposure
bugs.symptoms: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K00724442
bugs.conditions: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K00724442
bugs.impact: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K00724442
bugs.fix: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K00724442
bugs.behavior: Note: After installing a version of the software that includes the fix for this issue, you must set the following db variables: -- dnssec.nsec3apextypesbitmap -- dnssec.nsec3underapextypesbitmap. These two db variables are used globally (i.e., not per-DNSSEC zone) to configure the NSEC3 types bitmap returned in one-off NODATA responses for apex and under-apex responses, respectively. When the BIG-IP system is queried for a DNS name in which the DNS name exists and is not of the RR type requested, the NSEC3 types bitmap on the response reflects what you configure for the db variable, minus the queried-for type. When using these variables: -- Configure type values as all lowercase. -- Enclose multiple types in quotation marks (e.g., "txt rrsig"). -- Understand that there is likely no need to change the apex type setting; do so with extreme care. The under-apex settings are what you will find helpful in addressing the negative caching issue.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT may restore incorrect client identity if client IP does not match NAT64 prefix
bugs.symptoms: SIP response messages have the wrong IP address in the FROM header when using NAT64.
bugs.conditions: If the client's IPv6 address does not match the virtual server's configured IPv6 prefix, the FROM header on a response message will have a different IP address that the request message.
bugs.impact: The SIP ALG with SNAT system will be unable to establish a call for the client.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The FROM header will now contain the client's IP address.

bugs.title: Non-utf8 characters in resource descriptions causes malfunction of Resource Assign Dialogue
bugs.symptoms: APM resource that has 0xfc (u-umlaut) from 8859-15 in description field is causing error in the Visual Policy Editor resource assignment.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you manually edit an APM resource (hex edit of bigip.conf) and replaces u-umlaut with 0xfc
bugs.impact: Error on Visual Policy Editor while trying to edit advanced resource assign agent: "Unable to find rootNode 'message' in Load response for 'editActionDialogue'... Dialogue loading has failed."
bugs.workaround: Do not manually change utf8 characters in APM resource descriptions of of bigip.conf
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed

bugs.title: High disk utilization when unused files or file objects grow in the file store folder
bugs.symptoms: When duplicate file store objects are created in the filestore folder, this results in high disk space utilization.
bugs.conditions: -- Create an LTM virtual profile and save the configuration. -- Delete the profile -- The same profiles are created shortly thereafter -- Mcpd is restarted
bugs.impact: Duplicate file objects may be created in /config/filestore/files_d. Hard disk utilization increases.
bugs.workaround: Identify the duplicate file store objects which are not in use and delete them.

bugs.title: SNMP OID for sysLsnPoolStatTotal not incremented in stats
bugs.symptoms: SNMP OID for sysLsnPoolStatTotal is not incremented in stats totals.
bugs.conditions: This affects all of the global port block allocation (PBA) counters.
bugs.impact: SNMP OID for sysLsnPoolStatTotal is not incremented when it should be. Stats are not accurate.
bugs.fix: SNMP OID for sysLsnPoolStatTotal is now incremented in stats totals.

bugs.title: AVR is doing extra activity of DNS data collection even when it should not
bugs.symptoms: When collecting DNS data, AVR generates data that is used only for BIG-IQ, even if not connected to BIG-IQ.
bugs.conditions: DNS Statistics collection or DNS-DoS is configured.
bugs.impact: avrd process is taking more CPU cycles for activity that is not needed. There is no impact to functionality.
bugs.fix: The system no longer performs extra computation that is not needed in this case.

bugs.title: gtmd crash
bugs.symptoms: gtmd crashes
bugs.conditions: This rarely occurs when an iQuery connection is abnormally terminated.
bugs.impact: Under rare circumstances, gtmd may crash and restart.

bugs.title: ASM tsconfig log message mispellings
bugs.symptoms: error logged in /var/log/asm: Sep 19 19:57:10 f5-ha-ltm1 info tsconfig.pl[3955]: ASM initial configration script launched Sep 19 19:57:25 f5-ha-ltm1 err tsconfig.pl[3955]: initial configuration script encountered a fatal error: Failed To Retrive Self Mac Address First line, "configration" should be configuration (missing u) Second line, "Retrive" should be Retrieve (missing second e"
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: ASM tsconfig log message mispellings

bugs.title: Network Map page Virtual Servers with associated Address/Port List have a blank address.
bugs.symptoms: On the Local Traffic > Network Map page, some virtual servers have a blank address.
bugs.conditions: An address list or port list is associated with the virtual server
bugs.impact: The Network Map will display a blank address field.

bugs.title: If style attribute contains HTML entities, it may not be rewritten correctly on client side.
bugs.symptoms: Wrong styling of web-application page, direct links to scc resources from web-application.
bugs.conditions: HTML entities within style attribute in some tags. For example: url('some.jpg')
bugs.impact: User experience may suffer.
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule can be used.
bugs.fix: The issue with html entities in style attribute is fixed.

bugs.title: Users without Advanced Shell Access are not allowed SFTP access
bugs.symptoms: Users that do not have Advanced Shell Access can access BIG-IP via SFTP.
bugs.conditions: User without Advanced Shell Access.
bugs.impact: Users that do not have Advanced Shell Access cannot access BIG-IP via SFTP.
bugs.fix: Users that do not have Advanced Shell Access can no longer sftp into BIG-IP. Such users can still use scp for file transfers.

bugs.title: The TMM process may crash in some tunnel cases
bugs.symptoms: When Direct Server Return (DSR) or asymmetric routing with a tunnel is deployed, the TMM process may crash.
bugs.conditions: There are two scenarios that may lead to this issue: Scenario 1: DSR - DSR is deployed. Scenario 2: Asymmetric routing - The sys db variable connection.vlankeyed is set to 'disable'. - A VLAN and a tunnel are used to handle asymmetric routing.
bugs.impact: The TMM process crashes.Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM process no longer crashes.

bugs.title: Error encountered when performing a policy sync on an access profile of SSO type
bugs.symptoms: When performing a policy sync on an access profile of SSO type, it fails with an error message: "PolicySyncMgr: Internal error while collecting objects for policy /Common/MySSOProf. Exception: PolicySyncMgr: MCP query queryallincludereferencetree failed for macros. Encountered MCP exception 01020036:3: The requested Access Policy (/Common/MySSOProf) was not found"
bugs.conditions: - Create an access profile of type SSO - Start a policy sync on the profile
bugs.impact: Access profile cannot be sync'ed to other devices.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Access profile of SSO type won't be in the list of policy sync windows so that user won't be able to perform the operation on this type of access profile.

bugs.title: Virtual server configured with destination address list may not respond to ARP and ICMP echo
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server configured with destination address list, some of the address ranges within the list may be configured as a subnet virtual address. Subnet virtual addresses do not respond to ARP and ICMP echo. This is in line with the traditional subnet listeners.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is configured with destination address list, that contains address ranges.
bugs.impact: Addresses may behave differently in a destination address list depending on whether the address is configured as a host or as part of a range.
bugs.workaround: If the addresses of a destination address list are desired to behave as hosts, then do not add address ranges to the list, but add them as a list of individual addresses.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP HTTP2 filter makes inappropriate assumptions about requests and responses without content lengths
bugs.symptoms: HTTP2 differs from HTTP1 in that it is possible to have a request or response without a Content-Length header, and have the connection remain open afterwards. The HTTP2 framing allows the end of such a request or response to be detected. This difference can cause the HTTP framework within the BIG-IP system to become confused in certain HTTP2 scenarios. This can lead to inappropriate traffic handling of HTTP2 requests and responses.
bugs.conditions: -- An HTTP2 request or response is seen without a Content-Length header. -- The HTTP2 request is either sent in multiple frames, or single frame + followed by one or more Data frames. -- That request or response would require a Content-Length (or Transfer-Encoding: Chunked) in HTTP 1.x.
bugs.impact: -- HTTP2 traffic handling can fail if no Content-Length header exists, and one is expected in HTTP 1.x. -- The Data Frames are not sent to the HTTP1 server side. -- In certain scenarios, the HTTP1 side sends the pool member response back to the pool member . That will result in RST of the backend side connection with the following message in /var/log/ltm " [F5RST(peer): HTTP2 internal error (bad state transition in egress_complete)]

bugs.title: Self IP route is not updated in a routing table if there is more than one route with the same destination signature
bugs.symptoms: When Self IP address is added/updated via tmsh, Configuration utility, or "tmsh load sys config merge" command, BIG-IP routing daemon updates routing information in the routing table. If Dynamic Routing is configured on BIG-IP and affected Self IP route has the same destination as routes, gathered from routing protocols, then on adding or changing this Self IP address, the corresponding route from routing table has to be updated, usually it means that a new route is added to the routing table and the old one is removed, but a new route is added and then gets deleted from the routing table instead of old one.
bugs.conditions: 1) There is a route in the routing table with the same destination signature as a Self IP address' route we are planning to add or update. Usually this situation occurs when Dynamic Routing is configured on BIG-IP and a dynamic route is added to the routing table. 2) The Self IP is added or updated.
bugs.impact: The routing information isn't updated. The Self IP route isn't involved in routing decisions and therefore traffic, which has to use Self IP route for routing, uses out of date, incorrect routing information and is sent to a wrong destination.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: MCP crash or blocked for a long time when loading configuration
bugs.symptoms: Configuration loading crashes while loading hundreds or thousands of bot-defense profiles at once. The system logs messages in /var/log/ltm: -- err mcpd[8967]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), MCP call 'mcpmsg_set_ulong_item(msg, CID2TAG(cid), val)' failed with error: 16908292, 01020036:3: The requested user role partition (admin Common) was not found. -- err mcpd[8967]: 01070001:3: Failed to allocate memory for size 66256896 at framework/MCPProcessor.cpp:1041. -- crit tmsh[640]: 01420001:2: The connection to mcpd has been lost, try again. : framework/RemoteMcpConn.cpp, line 74.
bugs.conditions: Loading configuration with hundreds or thousands of bot-defense profiles.
bugs.impact: MCP might crash or be blocked for a long time. The system cannot perform traffic management operations, report system status, or allow reconfiguration, and other daemons are also affected.
bugs.workaround: Create bot-defense profiles one at a time rather than loading a configuration with hundreds or thousands of bot-defense profiles at once.
bugs.fix: The configuration load no longer crashes while loading hundreds or thousands of bot-defense profiles at once.

bugs.title: ASM GUI does not follow best practices
bugs.symptoms: When processing requests to the administrative webUI, ASM does not follow best practices.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned and enabled. Authenticated user with Administrator, Resource Administrator, or ASM Administrator roles.
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output.
bugs.fix: When processing webUI requests ASM now follows best practices.

bugs.title: AFM GUI does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: AFM GUI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.conditions: AFM provisioned Authenticated administrative user
bugs.impact: AFM GUI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.fix: AFM GUI now follows best security practices.

bugs.title: Resource-admin user roles can no longer get bash access
bugs.symptoms: Resource-admin users with bash access may write to system files beyond the scope of their assigned access.
bugs.conditions: Resource-admin users configured with bash shell access.
bugs.impact: Resource-admin users with bash access may write to system files causing security risks.
bugs.workaround: Do not assign bash access for resource-admin users.
bugs.fix: Resource-admin users restricted to tmsh access now. If a resource-admin user had bash access in a prior version and upgrades to this version, that user will get converted to tmsh access automatically after the upgrade process.
bugs.behavior: Resource-admin roles can no longer have bash shell access. And upon upgrade, resource-admin users with bash access will get converted to tmsh shell access.

bugs.title: Virtual server configured with FIX profile can leak memory.
bugs.symptoms: System memory increases with each transmitted FIX message. tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with a FIX profile. -- FIX profile specifies a message-log-publisher.
bugs.impact: Memory leak. Specifically, in the xdata cache. Potential traffic disruption while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: If possible, discontinue use of message logging functionality. Removing the message-log-publisher from the FIX profile stops xdata growth.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG does not reparse SDP payload if replaced
bugs.symptoms: When a SIP message is loaded, the SDP is parsed. If modified or replaced, the system does not reparse the modified payload.
bugs.conditions: This occurs internally while processing SDP in a SIP message.
bugs.impact: Changes to the SDP are ignored when creating media pinhole flows
bugs.fix: The SDP payload is now reparsed if modified or replaced.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Under heavy SSL traffic, sw crypto codec queue is stuck and taken out of service without failover
bugs.symptoms: Under heavy SSL traffic, it is observed that sw crypto codec queue is stuck and taken out of service, but no failover happened
bugs.conditions: Heavy SSL traffic
bugs.impact: Traffic is impacted and a large number of SSL handshakes to the BIG-IP are failing.
bugs.workaround: Increase crypto.queue.timeout to a much larger number(from 100 to 500 for example). Restart tmms for the change to take effect.

bugs.title: The tcpdump file does not provide the correct extension
bugs.symptoms: The output file from tcpdump generation is named support.tcpdump even though it is a compressed file.
bugs.conditions: Whenever tcpdump is generated and downloaded.
bugs.impact: You must rename the file with the correct file extension and then decompress it to access the .dmp files.
bugs.workaround: Rename the downloaded file from support.tcpdump to <filename>.tar.gz and decompress it.
bugs.fix: File name changed to support.tcpdump.tar.gz.
bugs.behavior: The tcpdump file has a different name and file extension - support.tcpdump.tar.gz

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT does not translate media addresses in SDP after SUBSCRIBE message
bugs.symptoms: The media addresses in the SDP payload are not translated by MRF SIP ALD with SNAT after a SUBSCRIBE message has been processed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs because the SUBSCRIBE message has has the TO and FROM headers with the same value causing the ALG to enter hairpin mode.
bugs.impact: Media addresses in the SDP payload are not translated.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Hairpin mode is not entered when processing SUBSCRIBE messages

bugs.title: Puffin Browser gets blocked by Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: Users using the Puffin Browser are blocked when accessing the Virtual Server when it is protected with either Proactive Bot Defense (within DoSL7 profile) or with the Bot Defense profile. This applies to all version of the Puffin Browsers: Desktop, Android, iOS.
bugs.conditions: - Users using the Puffin Browser on Desktop, Android, iOS - Bot Defense Profile, or: DoSL7 profile with Proactive Bot Defense is used while the "Block Suspicious Browsers" checkbox is enabled
bugs.impact: Users of the Puffin Browser cannot access the website
bugs.fix: Users of the Puffin Browser can now access the website that is protected by Bot Defense without getting blocked. For the fix to be applied, both BIG-IP Release and ASU must be installed which contain the fix. Also, it is recommended to enable the following DB variables: tmsh modify sys db dosl7.proactive_defense_validate_ip value disable tmsh modify sys db dosl7.cs_validate_ip value disable

bugs.title: CMP forwarded LRO host packets do not restore LRO flag
bugs.symptoms: When packets are being CMP forwarded for the host (e.g., related connection), the LRO flag is not being restored. As a result, these packets do not go through TSO which results in PMTU response and the connection hangs.
bugs.conditions: This issue is particular to CMP forwarded host connections which are going over the TMM interface due to explicit LRO and large MTU.
bugs.impact: The connection hangs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: URL is not removed from custom category when deleted
bugs.symptoms: When the admin goes to delete a certain URL from a custom category, it should be removed from the category and not be matched anymore with that category. In certain cases, the URL is not removed effectively.
bugs.conditions: This only occurs when the syntax "http*://" is used at the beginning of the URL when inserted into custom categories.
bugs.impact: When the URL with syntax "http*://" is deleted from the custom category, it will not take effect for SSL matches. For example, if "http*://www.f5.com/" was inserted and then deleted, and the user passed traffic for http://www.f5.com/ and https://www.f5.com/, the SSL traffic would still be categorized with the custom category even though it was deleted. The HTTP traffic would be categorized correctly.
bugs.workaround: "bigstart restart tmm" will resolve the issue.
bugs.fix: Made sure that the deletion takes effect properly and SSL traffic is no longer miscategorized after removal of the URL from the custom category.

bugs.title: In very rare situations, some filters may cause data-corruption.
bugs.symptoms: In very rare situations, an internal data-moving function may cause corruption. Filters that use the affected functionality are: HTTP2, Sip, Sipmsg, MQTTsession, serdes_diameter, FTP.
bugs.conditions: The affected filters are used, and some very rare situation occurs.
bugs.impact: This may cause silent data corruption, or a TMM crash.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The data-moving function has been fixed to correctly notify its callers about its behavior in rare situations.

bugs.title: SIPALG::hairpin and SIPALG::hairpin_default iRule commands to enable or disable hairpin mode added
bugs.symptoms: In MRF SIP ALG, the hairpin flag is part of the translation_details structure. Because a connection/translation might be used for multiple simultaneous calls, if any call is hairpinned, subsequent calls on the same connection will not translate SDP addresses.
bugs.conditions: -- A connection/translation using multiple simultaneous calls -- A call is hairpinned.
bugs.impact: Subsequent calls on the same connection do not translate SDP addresses.
bugs.fix: SIPALG::hairpin and SIPALG::hairpin_default iRule commands to enable or disable hairpin mode added.

bugs.title: Removal of timer object from tmm timer-ring when a tcl context is released.
bugs.symptoms: If a tcl context is associated with a tmm-timer (while creating access session) using iRule, the timer object is removed during tcl context release but its association remains. When the timer fires, it tries to access a memory which is already freed, causing tmm to crash and generate a core.
bugs.conditions: Creating access session using iRule.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Now the timer object created under tcl context is tied with tcl command context and a callback function. This function will be called every time a tcl context is released. This will allow any additional cleanup (e.g. removal of timer from timer ring) and freeing the tcl command context.

bugs.title: Bot Defense : Bot Traffic - 3 month/last year filter not displayed correctly
bugs.symptoms: 3 month/last year filters are not displayed correctly in the applied filter.
bugs.conditions: 3 month/last year filter applied in Bot Defense : Bot Traffic.
bugs.impact: You cannot see which filter is currently applied.
bugs.fix: 3 month/last year filter is now displayed correctly in applied filter.

bugs.title: Tooltips for OWASP Bot Categories and Anomalies were added
bugs.symptoms: Tooltips for some OWASP Bot Categories and Anomalies are 'N/A' in GUI/REST.
bugs.conditions: - GUI page: Event Logs:: Bot Defense :: Bot Traffic. - Bot classification is 'OWASP Automated Threat'.
bugs.impact: Tooltip shows 'N/A' instead of detailed description. You cannot see detailed description of Bot classification of traffic.
bugs.fix: Tooltips for OWASP Bot Categories and Anomalies were added.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT does not translate media addresses in SDP after NOTIFY message
bugs.symptoms: The media addresses in the SDP payload are not translated by MRF SIP ALD with SNAT after a NOTIFY message has been processed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs because the NOTIFY message has has the TO and FROM headers with the same value causing the ALG to enter hairpin mode.
bugs.impact: Media addresses in the SDP payload are not translated.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Hairpin mode is not entered when processing NOTIFY messages

bugs.title: Ordering Symantec and Comodo certificates from BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: This new feature enables ordering Symantec and Comodo certificates from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: You must have a Symantec or Comodo CA account to make certificate orders from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: This new feature enables ordering of certificates from CAs Symantec and Comodo. CA-Approved certificates are automatically fetched and installed on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a new feature.
bugs.fix: This release adds the capability to order/fetch and install certificates from CAs Symantec and Comodo.
bugs.behavior: You can now order/fetch and install certificates from the Symantec and Comodo Certificate Authorities.

bugs.title: Portal Access does not rewrite the script element with textNode children
bugs.symptoms: Web-application defining script element with textNode children are not rewritten by Portal Access. This can cause the web application to fail to load.
bugs.conditions: Web-application defining script element with textNode children which requires client-side dynamic script rewriting
bugs.impact: - Web application may fail to load. - Non-rewritten HTTP request
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule to rewrite the content of textNode. There is no generic iRule but it can be implemented depending on the web application requirement.

bugs.title: Added comments which elaborated not to use any ACL that includes the reserved address range 127.10.x.x if multiple Views are defined.
bugs.symptoms: Based on ZoneRunner's design, each view has a unique client acl such as zrd-acl-000-xxx from 127.10.x.x address range. ZoneRunner communicates with bind using the unique IP address, so that bind knows which View ZoneRunner is querying for. If using 'any' for a View's match-clients attribute, bind always returns information from that View, because 127.10.x.x also belongs to any. Added comments to caution against using any ACL that includes the 127.10.x.x address range the configuration needs to have multiple Views.
bugs.conditions: If using 'any' for a View's match-clients attribute, bind will always return information from that View as 127.10.x.x also belongs to any.
bugs.impact: Documentation enhancement. No direct impact.
bugs.workaround: Added comments which elaborated not to use any ACL that includes the reserved address range 127.10.x.x if multiple Views are defined.
bugs.fix: The comment section now provides a much clearer description when creating a new View.

bugs.title: Heavy use of APM Kerberos SSO can sometimes lead to slowness of Virtual Server
bugs.symptoms: When there are a lot of tcp connections that needs new kerberos ticket to be fetched from kdc, then the websso processes requests slower than the incoming requests. This could lead to low throughput and virtual server is very slow to respond to requests.
bugs.conditions: Large number of APM users using Kerberos SSO to access backend resources and all the tickets expire at the same time.
bugs.impact: Low throughput and slow responses from Virtual server.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Increase the size of websso worker queue, so that tmm and websso process can communicate effectively. This eliminates VS slowness and hence increase throughput.

bugs.title: During CMP forward, nexthop data may miss at large packet split
bugs.symptoms: At splitting large package, nexthop data is used for the first small packet but missed in the subsequent packets.
bugs.conditions: CMP forward of host LRO packet (e.g., FTP data-channel)
bugs.impact: heavy packet loss, re-transmissions and delays
bugs.fix: Transmission time is now relatively consistent and there is no significant packet loss or delay.

bugs.title: Failed to parse X-Forwarded-For header in HTTP requests
bugs.symptoms: Failed to parse X-Forwarded-For header. This results in failure when extracting proper values in DOSL7.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Accept XFF' is enabled in HTTP profile. HTTP profile is added to the virtual server. -- Bot Defense profile is added to the virtual sever. -- HTTP request contains 'X-Forwarded-For' header.
bugs.impact: DOSL7 does not receive the proper values for X-Forwarded-For.
bugs.fix: DOSL7 now receives the correct value under these conditions.

bugs.title: Portal Access Web Page does not render properly
bugs.symptoms: Some of the Microsoft hosted cloud sites, including dynamics, use a logon process that goes through secure.aadcdn.microsoftonline-p.com. This might result in a number of different kinds of problems: -- iOS devices do not send the MRHSession cookie, so are denied when requesting CSS and JavaScript. -- Android devices might 'fail to load'.
bugs.conditions: Using Portal Access (PA) on a Microsoft-hosted cloud site.
bugs.impact: -- The PA Web Page does not load correctly. -- Script errors appear on the browser console. -- Intended functionality on the web page is not provided.
bugs.workaround: You can use an iRule to work around this.
bugs.fix: Portal Access Web Page now renders properly under these conditions.

bugs.title: GUI - SSL Certificate Instances section to include Monitor Instances
bugs.symptoms: The GUI SSL Certificate Instances section was enhanced to include Monitor Instances
bugs.conditions: Use SSL certificate and key in monitor instances.
bugs.impact: It's now easier to view all referencing monitors will make certificate management easier.
bugs.fix: GUI SSL Certificate Instances section now include Monitor Instances.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing HTTP/2 traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash when processing HTTP/2 traffic
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 profile enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP/2 traffic as expected.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG now supports reading SDP from a mime multipart payload
bugs.symptoms: Previously all non-SDP SIP payloads were ignored. This would cause media pinhole flows to not be created.
bugs.conditions: An INVITE message or its response contained a SDP section in a mime multipart payload.
bugs.impact: Media pinhole flows were not created
bugs.fix: The SIP ALG functions can now extract and process the SDP section of a mime multipart payload.

bugs.title: TMSH command "tmsh show ltm urlcat-query" not performing cloud lookup
bugs.symptoms: TMSH command "tmsh show ltm urcat-query" does not perform cloud lookup when there is no entry in the local database.
bugs.conditions: - TMSH command "show ltm urlcat-query abc.com" is executed. - abc.com does not have an entry in the local webroot database.
bugs.impact: - Cloud lookup is not executed for unknown URL entries.
bugs.fix: Now the "tmsh show ltm ulcat-query" command performs cloud lookup when there is no entry in the local database.

bugs.title: Creating EC-only client SSL profile for forward-proxy without RSA key certs defined results in invalid profile
bugs.symptoms: When you create an EC-key-cert-only client SSL profile and attach it to the virtual server, TMM marks the profile as invalid and reports an error in /var/log/ltm: -- crit tmm[16024]: 01260000:2: Profile /Common/c.f: could not load default key file; invalidating profile.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen when the following conditions are met: -- An EC-type cert/key pair is configured on the client SSL profile. -- Forward proxy is enabled in the client SSL profile. -- No RSA key cert is configured on the client SSL profile.
bugs.impact: The system marks that client SSL profile invalid, rendering it unusable.
bugs.workaround: Also configure an RSA-type key cert on the client SSL profile.
bugs.fix: The client SSL profile no longer has the restriction for key/cert type when forward proxy is enabled.

bugs.title: Anti-fraud: remote logging of login attempts
bugs.symptoms: There is no support for logging of login attempts to a remote service.
bugs.conditions: Using high speed logging (HSL) to log login attempts.
bugs.impact: There is no support for logging of login attempts.
bugs.fix: FPS now uses HSL to report login attempts using configured templates, rate-limit, and publisher to a remote service. To enable this feature: # via tmsh only tmsh modify sys db antifraud.riskengine.reportlogins value enable # via tmsh or GUI tmsh modify sys db antifraud.internalconfig.string1 value "<login attempt log template>" tmsh modify sys db antifraud.internalconfig.string2 value "<log-rate-exceeded log template>" tmsh modify sys db antifraud.internalconfig.number1 value "<log-rate-exceeded threshold>" tmsh modify security anti-fraud profile <fps profile> risk-engine-publisher <publisher> It is recommended that you use encoding when composing an HTTP template. The default encoding level is 0, meaning 'never encode'. To change encoding level: tmsh modify sys db antifraud.internalconfig.number2 value <0/1/2>
bugs.behavior: FPS now includes the ability to perform High Speed Logging (HSL) of all login attempts to specific protected URLs. These events can be forwarded to remote services (e.g. SIEM Server), and, when enabled, can help indicate whether applications are under attack.

bugs.title: Brute Force CAPTCHA response page truncates last digit in the support id
bugs.symptoms: Brute Force CAPTCHA response page shown to an end-user has a support id and the last digit is truncated.
bugs.conditions: - ASM Provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual server - ASM Brute Force Protection enabled in the asm policy - ASM Brute Force sends captcha mitigation page when a website is under brute force attack.
bugs.impact: The support id presented to an end-user won't be matched to the one shown in the asm logs
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: The code is fixed, correct support id is shown in the captcha response page.

bugs.title: The /var partition may become 100% full requiring manual intervention to clear space
bugs.symptoms: The /var partition might become completely full on the disk due to files being written to /var/config/rest. This condition may be accompanied by console error messages similar to the following: 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var (slot #) has only 0% free Additionally, there may be periodic restjavad and bigd daemons restarts related to disk space exhaustion.
bugs.conditions: Process traffic while DoS Dashboard is open.
bugs.impact: The partition housing /var/config/rest may become 100% full, impacting future disk IO to the partition
bugs.workaround: This workaround is temporary in nature, should the conditions of this bug still be met, and may need to be periodically performed either manually or from a script. While these steps are performed, the BIG-IP REST API will be temporarily inaccessible, and higher disk IO may be seen. Run the following commands, in sequence: bigstart stop restjavad rm -rf /var/config/rest/storage*.zip rm -rf /var/config/rest/*.tmp bigstart start restjavad Manual application of these workaround steps clears the 100% utilized space condition and allows the partition to resume normal operation.
bugs.fix: The system deletes all Zip files in the REST root directory so that the partition-full condition no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Requests are reported to local log even if only Bot Defense remote log is configured
bugs.symptoms: Requests are logged locally on the BIG-IP system while they supposed to be sent only to the remote logger.
bugs.conditions: - Bot Defense profile attached to a virtual server. - Bot Defense remote logger profile attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Requests logged locally on the BIG-IP system when they are not supposed to be.
bugs.fix: Logging profile filter mechanism now honors remote and local logging configurations.

bugs.title: The "audit_forwarder is disabled as the configuration is incomplete" message can be confusing if logged when the configuration is loading
bugs.symptoms: This message may be logged while the audit_forwarder is loading the configuration: audit_forwarder is disabled as the configuration is incomplete. Please define the following db variables: config.auditing.forward.sharedsecret, config.auditing.forward.destination and config.auditing.forward.type. And make sure config.auditing.forward.destination is not set to "::". These DB variables may all be actually configured correctly, but since the configuration has not loaded yet this message may be logged multiple times.
bugs.conditions: The audit_forwarder process is starting up and loading the configuration.
bugs.impact: Confusing error messages in /var/log/ltm. Logging will still work as configured.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Message has been modified to indicate the possibility of loading the configuration. Message is now logged only once. A new messages is logged indicating when audit_forwarder is enabled.

bugs.title: Changed Default Cloud-Init log level to INFO from DEBUG
bugs.symptoms: Cloud-Init services generate too many debug log lines that populate their systemd journal.
bugs.conditions: Any BIG-IP VE release with Cloud-Init enabled and using "systemd".
bugs.impact: There're too many debug log lines that might make VE admin miss any more important information and severe errors when reading it.
bugs.workaround: Manually change all Cloud-Init's log levels to INFO from DEBUG.
bugs.fix: Cloud-Init's log default levels have been changed to INFO from DEBUG.

bugs.title: DNSSEC: gtmd leaks memory when dnssec keys on a dnssec zone are auto-rolling
bugs.symptoms: gtmd leaks memory every time an auto-rolling DNSSEC Key on a DNSSEC Zone expires or rolls-over.
bugs.conditions: Auto-rolling DNSSEC Keys are associated with a DNSSEC Zone.
bugs.impact: gtmd leaks memory every time an auto-rolling DNSSEC Key on a DNSSEC Zone expires or rolls-over.
bugs.workaround: The user can modify their DNSSEC Keys to be non-rolling/static dnssec keys. Also gtmd can be restarted to temporarily correct the memory leak. But this workaround is not recommended except during a scheduled maintenance window or unless traffic processing seems to be impacted by gtmd memory usage (unlikely scenario).

bugs.title: Improve WebRootKit alert details
bugs.symptoms: WebRootKit alert is not informative in some cases.
bugs.conditions: Script override native function and the native function toString.
bugs.impact: The overwritten native method toString will look like real native method toString in the alert
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.

bugs.title: Virtual server may reset a connection with port zero when client sends ACK after a 4-way close
bugs.symptoms: Virtual sends a reset of port zero.
bugs.conditions: Here is an observed sequence for the problem to happen: 1. Three way handshake initiated by client to VIP. 2. Client actively closing the connection - 4 way close 3. Client continues to send ACK after 4 way close
bugs.impact: Virtual does a wrong reset.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Connection flow collision no longer causes packets to be sent from source port 0.

bugs.title: Add log events for MRF SIP registration/deregistration and media flow creation/deletion
bugs.symptoms: Generally only error conditions are logged for SIP. More logging is needed around SIP registration/deregistration, media flow creation/deletion, to help debug in the field.
bugs.conditions: log.mrsip.level notice or above.
bugs.impact: Only error conditions are logged. Events helpful for debugging are not available in the logs.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Log information logging is available around SIP registration/deregistration and media flow creation/deletion.

bugs.title: If the 'giaddr' field contains a non-zero value, the 'giaddr' field must not be modified
bugs.symptoms: DHCP-RELAY overwrites the 'giaddr' field containing a non-zero value. This violates RFC 1542.
bugs.conditions: DHCP-RELAY processing a message with the 'giaddr' field containing a non-zero value
bugs.impact: RFC 1542 violation
bugs.fix: DHCP-RELAY no longer overwrites the 'giaddr' field containing a non-zero value.

bugs.title: Upgrades break existing iRulesLX workspaces that use node version 6
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading a BIG-IP with iRulesLX plugins, if those plugins are based on workspaces that use node version 6 (instead of version 0.12) they will fail to work properly after the upgrade once the plugin is reloaded from the workspace. Errors like this will be seen in /var/log/ltm: Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 info sdmd[17582]: 018e0017:6: pid[26853] plugin[/Common/test-jt-plugin.test-jt-extension] Starting the server.....jt...after upgrade... Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 err sdmd[17582]: 018e0018:3: Resuming log processing at this invocation; held 233 messages. Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 err sdmd[17582]: 018e0018:3: pid[26850] plugin[/Common/test-jt-plugin.test-jt-extension] /var/sdm/plugin_store/plugins/:Common:test-jt-plugin_62858_3/extensions/test-jt-extension/node_modules/f5-nodejs/lib/ilx_server.js:30 Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 err sdmd[17582]: 018e0018:3: pid[26850] plugin[/Common/test-jt-plugin.test-jt-extension] ILXServerWrap = process.binding('ILXServerWrap').ILXServerWrap; Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 err sdmd[17582]: 018e0018:3: pid[26850] plugin[/Common/test-jt-plugin.test-jt-extension] ^ Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 err sdmd[17582]: 018e0018:3: pid[26850] plugin[/Common/test-jt-plugin.test-jt-extension] Error: No such module: ILXServerWrap Oct 5 06:37:12 B7200-R14-S36 err sdmd[17582]: 018e0018:3: pid[26850] plugin[/Common/test-jt-plugin.test-jt-extension] at Error (native)
bugs.conditions: Upgrading a version of BIG-IP that is using iRulesLX that has a workspace based on node version 6. Later reloading the iRulesLX plugin from the workspace.
bugs.impact: The iRulesLX plugin no longer works.
bugs.workaround: - Navigate to the workspace folder on the BIG-IP (/var/ilx/workspaces/<partition>/<workspace name>. - Make the file "node_version" writable (chmod +w node_version). - Edit the node_version file: change "0.12" to "6" - Save the node_version file. - Make the file "node_version" read-only (chmod -w node_version). - Reload the iRulesLX plugin from the workspace.
bugs.fix: Prevented the node version from getting reverted to default during an upgrade.

bugs.title: 'load sys config verify' resets the active master key to the on-disk master key value
bugs.symptoms: Master key is reset to an older value which may differ from the 'active' value.
bugs.conditions: Configuration is validated via 'tmsh load sys config verify'.
bugs.impact: Configuration elements may be encrypted with a different key leading to a corrupt configuration state. If the configuration is saved, future loads will fail.
bugs.fix: Verification loads do not override the 'active' master-key.

bugs.title: DNSSEC: Creating a new DNSSEC Zone can result in gtmd attempting to sync every 10 seconds
bugs.symptoms: Creating a new DNSSEC Zone can result in gtmd attempting to sync every 10 seconds even though the configuration appears to be the same on each GTM in the sync group. This will last until another change is committed to the database (for example: create a new un-related object like a gtm wideip)
bugs.conditions: The user creates a new DNSSEC Zone.
bugs.impact: gtmd may attempt to sync every 10 seconds until another configuration change is made.
bugs.workaround: If the user makes another un-realted configuration change, like creating a gtm datacenter or wideip, the attempt to sync every 10 seconds will stop.

bugs.title: AVRD can crash with core when disconnecting/reconnecting on HTTPS connection
bugs.symptoms: AVRD crashes repeatedly when the BIG-IP system is configured to work with BIG-IQ.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system is connected to BIG-IQ. -- Disconnecting/reconnecting on HTTPS connection.
bugs.impact: Statistics collection is unstable : some stats data are lost during avrd crash.
bugs.fix: Object associated with HTTPS connection was deleted before the last event on this connection arrived. Object deletion is now deferred, so this issue no longer occurs..

bugs.title: Bogus numbers in hsbe2_internal_pde_ring table's rqm_dma_drp_pkts column
bugs.symptoms: The DMA drop packet and bytes registers (rqm_dma_drp_pkts and rqm_dma_drp_bytes in tmm/hsbe2_internal_pde_ring table) can have huge numbers, which appear to be close to multiples of 4G (2^32). The count reported in the register from hsb_snapshot shows very small number: from tmm/hsbe2_internal_pde_ring name active bus rqm_dma_drp_pkts rqm_dma_drp_bytes ---------------- ------ --- ---------------- ----------------- lbb0_pde1_ring2 1 2 17179869185 4398046511186 lbb0_pde1_ring3 1 2 8589934597 2199023256108 lbb0_pde2_ring0 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde2_ring1 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde2_ring2 1 2 8589934592 2199023255552 lbb0_pde2_ring3 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde3_ring0 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde3_ring1 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde3_ring2 1 2 8589934592 2199023255552 lbb0_pde3_ring3 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde4_ring0 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde4_ring1 1 2 0 0 lbb0_pde4_ring2 1 2 8589934592 2199023255552 lbb0_pde4_ring3 1 2 0 0 lbb1_pde1_ring1 1 3 0 0 lbb1_pde1_ring2 1 3 4294967298 1099511627952 From hsb_snapshot for pde1's ring 0 to ring 3: 50430: 00000000 rqm_dma_drp_pkt_cnt_4 50530: 00000000 rqm_dma_drp_pkt_cnt_5 50630: 00000001 rqm_dma_drp_pkt_cnt_6 50730: 00000005 rqm_dma_drp_pkt_cnt_7
bugs.conditions: The register reads sometimes return a 0 value.
bugs.impact: The DMA drop stats are not accurate
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm can reset the stats, but it will disrupt traffic.
bugs.fix: Add the protection in register reads to avoid occasional read errors.

bugs.title: Memory pressure from nsyncd
bugs.symptoms: The nsyncd process may reserve large pages of memory. This can impact the performance of other processes.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Degraded GUI or tmm performance.
bugs.workaround: Restart nsyncd.
bugs.fix: Nsyncd no longer reserves large pages of memory.

bugs.title: DNSSEC: Initial Key Generations may take up to 5 seconds to appear when a new DNSSEC Key is created
bugs.symptoms: Initial Key Generations may take up to 5 seconds to appear when a new DNSSEC Key is created.
bugs.conditions: The user creates a new DNSSEC Key.
bugs.impact: The initial DNSSEC Key Generation may take up to 5 seconds to appear in the configuration
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Usage of whitelist in DoS profile is not clear
bugs.symptoms: - When adding an fqdn to the address list in a DoS profile or shared objects, we can get this message if an FQDN policy is not configured: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Please configure a dns-resolver under global-fqdn-policy. However, if AFM is not provisioned, then an fqdn policy cannot even be configured. - HTTP (DoSL7) section of the DoS profile only supports single IP addresses, and IP with netmask. - DNS/SIP/Network sections of the DoS profile only support single IP addresses, IP ranges, and FQDN.
bugs.conditions: DoS profile is configured and IP whitelist contains IP ranges, netmasks, or FQDN.
bugs.impact: - Some of the entries in the address whitelist may not be applied in the DoS profile. - Confusing error messages
bugs.workaround: - For HTTP (DoSL7) section of the DoS profile, use only Single IP addresses, or IP network + netmask. - For DNS/SIP/Network sections of the DoS profile, use only Single IP addresses, IP ranges, or FQDN.

bugs.title: Attack status is not updated when Protected Objects Details Panel is refreshed
bugs.symptoms: The Protected Objects Attack Status in the Protected Objects list table row is not updated when the details panel is refreshed
bugs.conditions: For Protected Objects that show "Attack Detected...", it is possible that the initial loading or subsequent refresh of the details panel may not show any attacks because the attack has come to an end.
bugs.impact: Detail Panel Attack info and Row data could be out of sync
bugs.workaround: Reload Protected Objects page

bugs.title: HA-Status changes to "Changes Pending" after Edge Client download
bugs.symptoms: In a HA device group, trying to download edge client on one device cause the "changes pending" indicator to turn on.
bugs.conditions: - Create a failover device group and put at et least two devices in it. - Navigate to Access Profile > Connectivity / VPN > Connectivity > Profiles - Choose a connectivity profile (create one if there is not already one). - Click on drop down button "Customize Package" and select either of them ("Windows" or "Mac) - Click Download
bugs.impact: Give user a false sense of config being changed.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: "Changes Pending" indicator won't turn on with Edge Client download

bugs.title: Vcmp guest vlan mac mismatch across blades.
bugs.symptoms: Guests running on blades in a single chassis report different MAC addresses on a single vlan upon host reboot for vcmp guest.
bugs.conditions: This issue may be seen when all of the following conditions are met: - One (or more) blade(s) are turned off completely via AOM. - Create two vlans. - Deploy a multi-slot guest with the higher lexicographic vlan. - Now, assign the smaller vlan to the guest. - Reboot the host
bugs.impact: Incorrect MAC addresses are reported by some blades.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a vCMP guest VLAN MAC mismatch across blades under these conditions.

bugs.title: Server Technologies logos all appear as default icon
bugs.symptoms: Server Technologies logos all appear as the default icon.
bugs.conditions: Browsing the list of available Server Technologies in an ASM policy.
bugs.impact: Server Technologies logos all appear as the default icon.
bugs.workaround: Install the most recent Server Technologies update file.
bugs.fix: Server Technology-specific logos appear correctly.

bugs.title: Setting the hostname to non-FQDN value prevents upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade of the BIG-IP system fails.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP systems that contain hostnames that do not meet FQDN standards. For instance, this could be due to the use of invalid characters, such as asterisk '*'. An example of an invalid hostname is as follows: test***.example.com.
bugs.impact: Inability to upgrade. Note: Setting hostname in tmsh CLI does not validate FQDN like the GUI does, so when you use tmsh to set hostnames, make sure to use an FQDN-compliant one.
bugs.workaround: When attempting to upgrade you must make sure all hostnames are FQDN compliant.

bugs.title: Virtual server page is blank when SSLO is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: When SSLO is provisioned and trying to create a new virtual server, the virtual server page is blank.
bugs.conditions: SSLO is provisioned
bugs.impact: Cannot create a new virtual server when SSLO is provisioned.
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed in this release.

bugs.title: PEM may not re-establish diameter connection after HA switchover
bugs.symptoms: PEM diameter may not establish diameter connection after a failover, if more than 25 days have elapsed between failovers
bugs.conditions: If 25 days have elapsed between failovers
bugs.impact: Diameter connection may not happen
bugs.workaround: tmm restart
bugs.fix: Allow establishment of diameter connection by resetting the reconnect timer

bugs.title: On rare occasions, gtmd fails to process probe responses originating from the same system.
bugs.symptoms: On rare occasions, some resources are marked 'unavailable', with a reason of 'big3d: timed out' because gtmd fails to process some probe responses sent by the instance of big3d that is running on the same BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: The monitor response from big3d sent to the gtmd on the same device is being lost. Monitor responses sent to other gtmds are sent without issue. The conditions under which this occurs have not been identified.
bugs.impact: Some resources are marked 'unavailable' on the affected BIG-IP system, while the other BIG-IP systems in the sync group mark the resource as 'available'.
bugs.workaround: Restart gtmd on the affected BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: A client SSL handshake fails when client hello extension contains only unsupported groups
bugs.symptoms: If the supported groups extension in the client hello contains only groups that are not supported by the BIG-IP system, the handshake fails.
bugs.conditions: -- (ec)dhe ciphers are used. -- The supported groups extension does not contain any groups supported by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Client connections to the BIG-IP system fail.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not configuring (ec)dhe ciphers.

bugs.title: With ASM CORS set to 'Disabled' it strips all CORS headers in response.
bugs.symptoms: All access-control-* headers are removed by ASM, including Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) headers. This causes CORS-related JavaScript errors on the browser console, and blocks cross-domain requests that should be allowed.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- Backend server sends CORS headers access-control-*.
bugs.impact: Any webapp that sends cross origin AJAX requests might not work.
bugs.workaround: Set up an iRule on a virtual server, for example: when HTTP_RESPONSE { array set header_list { } foreach header_name [HTTP::header names] { if { [string tolower $header_name] starts_with "access-control-" } { set header_list($header_name) [HTTP::header $header_name] } } } when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { foreach header_name [array names header_list] { if {!([HTTP::header exists $header_name])} { HTTP::header insert $header_name $header_list($header_name) } } }
bugs.fix: ASM no longer removes CORS headers when the feature is set to set to 'Disabled'. This is correct behavior.

bugs.title: Patched Cloud-Init to support AliYun Datasource
bugs.symptoms: Shipped Cloud-Init in this version of VE has no support of Alibaba Cloud metadata service for having no support of AliYun Datasource.
bugs.conditions: VE for Alibaba Cloud
bugs.impact: Provisioning VE through Cloud-Init won't work on Alibaba cloud
bugs.fix: Patched Cloud-Init to support AliYun Datasource

bugs.title: SCTP profiles have been modified to advertise one stream unless configured otherwise
bugs.symptoms: SCTP profiles used to default to two streams. When a client connects, the profile negotiates assuming that the server can accept two streams. When a server connection is established later, if the server advertises only one stream, the connection resets. This scenario results in a difficult-to-diagnose condition.
bugs.conditions: If not configured, the default for SCTP profiles is now to advertise and accept only one stream in each direction.
bugs.impact: Unless otherwise explicitly configured, SCTP profiles advertises one stream only.
bugs.workaround: If more than one stream is required, configure the SCTP profile for a greater number.
bugs.fix: The SCTP profile has been modified to default to a more-reliable and easier-to-understand configuration.
bugs.behavior: The BIG-IP SCTP profile has been modified so that the default configuration for SCTP profiles supports 1 (one) stream.

bugs.title: MCPD sync errors and restart after multiple modifications to file object in chassis
bugs.symptoms: Upon modifying file objects on a VIPRION chassis and synchronizing those changes to another VIPRION chassis in a device sync group, the following symptoms may occur: 1. Errors are logged to /var/log/ltm similar to the following: -- err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync: link_stat "/config/filestore/.snapshots_d/<_additional_path_to/_affected_file_object_>" (in csync) failed: No such file or directory (2) ) errno(0) errstr(). -- err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync error: some files could not be transferred (code 23) at main.c(1298) [receiver=2.6.8] syncer /usr/bin/rsync failed! (5888) () Couldn't rsync files for mcpd. ) errno(0) errstr(). -- err mcpd[<#>]: 0107134b:3: (rsync process failed.) errno(255) errstr(). -- err mcpd[<#>]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Failed to sync files.. 2. MCPD may restart on a secondary blade in a VIPRION chassis that is receiving the configuration sync from the chassis where the file object changes were made.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered when rapidly making changes to files such as creating and then deleting them while the config sync of the file creation is still in progress.
bugs.impact: Temporary loss of functionality, including interruption in traffic, on one or more secondary blades in one or more VIPRION chassis that are receiving the configuration sync.
bugs.workaround: After performing one set of file-object modifications and synchronizing those changes to the high availability (HA) group members, wait for one or more minutes to allow all changes to be synchronized to all blades in all member chassis before making and synchronizing changes to the same file-objects.

bugs.title: The autodosd process consumes a lot of memory and continuously restarts.
bugs.symptoms: The autodosd process consumes a lot of memory and continuously restarts. (The autodosd process is a control plane process which supports the BIG-IP AFM DoS Auto Threshold feature.)
bugs.conditions: Many virtual servers (e.g., 1,020) with dos-profiles attached, even there is no DoS vector enabled.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system continuously restarts.
bugs.workaround: Set sys db dos.auto.threshold.learnalways to false. This sys db variable controls whether the BIG-IP system should learn/store traffic history and calculate the auto-thresholds when we are in manual-threshold mode also. The default is on (always learn).
bugs.fix: The autodosd process allocates memory only when the DoS vector is enabled, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Do not provision both GTM and LC modules when upgrading on C117 BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: On C117 BIG-IP, before upgrading to this version, make sure if you are using GTM or LC module, do not provision both modules. Provision one or the other.
bugs.conditions: C117 BIG-IP provisioned with GTM and LC modules, among others.
bugs.impact: Upgrade may fail if you have GTM and LC modules both provisioned, due to memory constraints.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading, if you are using GTM or LC, make sure only provision one or the other, and not both.
bugs.fix: Provision either GTM or LC as needed, but not both.

bugs.title: "source-port preserve" does not work on BIG-IP Virtual Edition
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition uses RSS hashing for selecting TMMs which has the side effect of causing "source-port preserve" to reuse ports aggressively. This can ultimately lead to connection failures.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP virtual edition with "source-port preserve" configured on a fastl4 virtual server and VE configures RSS hash. VE will configure RSS hash if both the below conditions are met 1. VE supports RSS hash on the NIC. Currently, RSS is supported on ixlv and vmxnet3 NICs 2. The number of TMMs <= maximum number of queues supported by the NIC. For ixlv this is 4 and for vmxnet3 this is 8
bugs.impact: Connections may fail due to reusing ports too quickly.
bugs.workaround: On the Virtual Server, set source-port to "change".

bugs.title: Stale packets in HSB transmit queue causes HSB DMA lockup
bugs.symptoms: A stale packet in the HSB transmit queue without the packet_ending flag set might cause HSB transmission failure and DMA lockup.
bugs.conditions: Conditions under which this occurs have not been reproduced.
bugs.impact: The HSB transmit failures leads to HSB DMA lockup and impacts traffic.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the unit to recover from the HSB DMA lockup.

bugs.title: tmsh help for FQDN node or pool member shows incorrect default for fqdn interval
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh help text for LTM nodes and pools shows the incorrect default for the fqdn 'interval' value. The default is indicated as the TTL, whereas the actual default value is 3600 seconds (1 hour). The configured value is displayed correctly if the node or pool is displayed using the 'all-properties' keyword.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: FQDN nodes and pool members may be created with a different fqdn refresh interval than intended.
bugs.workaround: When creating an FQDN node or pool member, specify the desired fqdn 'interval' value (either TTL, or the desired number of seconds).
bugs.fix: The tmsh help text for LTM nodes and pools correctly shows the default value of 3600 seconds for the fqdn 'interval' value.

bugs.title: ASM unable to display *any* event logs, unless they are searched for by support ID
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, ASM is unable to display *any* event logs, unless they are searched for by support ID.
bugs.conditions: Either the numerical value returned from this query: mysql> SELECT request_log_id FROM PRX.REQUEST_LOG_CLEARED; Or the numerical value returned from this query: mysql> SELECT MAX(request_log_id) FROM PRX.REQUEST_LOG_PROPERTIES WHERE flg_is_deleted = 1; Are larger than the numerical value returned from this query: mysql> SELECT MAX(id) FROM PRX.REQUEST_LOG;
bugs.impact: ASM is unable to display *any* event logs, unless they are searched for by support ID.
bugs.workaround: mysql> UPDATE PRX.REQUEST_LOG_CLEARED SET PRX.REQUEST_LOG_CLEARED.request_log_id = (SELECT MAX(PRX.REQUEST_LOG.id) FROM PRX.REQUEST_LOG); mysql> DELETE FROM PRX.REQUEST_LOG_PROPERTIES WHERE PRX.REQUEST_LOG_PROPERTIES.request_log_id NOT IN (SELECT PRX.REQUEST_LOG.id FROM PRX.REQUEST_LOG);

bugs.title: Syslog-ng Memory Leak
bugs.symptoms: After a long uptime (almost a year) syslog-ng had consumed 1.1G of virtual memory on BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: Memory leak when syslog-ng handles continuous SIGHUP signals.
bugs.impact: Memory necessary for optimal operation is constrained.
bugs.workaround: Run this command once a month: service syslog-ng restart

bugs.title: Use of HTTP::cookie after HTTP:disable causes TMM core
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule disables HTTP with HTTP:disable, subsequent use of HTTP::cookie for that request will cause a TMM core dump.
bugs.conditions: 1) HTTP profile is configured on the virtual. 2) HTTP:disable is called on request. 3) HTTP:cookie is then called on that request.
bugs.impact: Use of iRules in the above mentioned order will result in a TMM core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not call HTTP:cookie on requests that have had HTTP disabled by HTTP:disable

bugs.title: SERVFAIL when attempting to view or edit NS resource records in zonerunner
bugs.symptoms: While attempting to use ZoneRunner to edit NS resource records, getting error: 01150b21:3: RCODE returned from query: 'SERVFAIL'.
bugs.conditions: - An NS resource record is selected using the zonerunner GUI - The NS record points to a zone that bind is not authoritative for. - Recursion is enabled on the zone in question - The bind process is not able to reach the nameserver referenced in the NS record.
bugs.impact: Administrator is unable to use ZoneRunner to edit NS records.
bugs.workaround: Set recursion to no for the appropriate zone, perform the change, set recursion back to yes. Note: This will be impacting to any clients expecting recursion for the duration of the change.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system sends Firmware-Revision AVP in CER with Mandatory bit set
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system always sets the Mandatory bit flag for Firmware-Revision AVPs in DIAMETER Capabilities Exchange Request messages.
bugs.conditions: Using DIAMETER to send a Capabilities Exchange Request message with the Firmware-Revision AVP.
bugs.impact: If the DIAMETER peer is intolerant of this Mandatory bit being set, it will reset the DIAMETER connection.
bugs.workaround: Configure an iRule in the MRF transport-config, for example: ltm rule workaround { when DIAMETER_EGRESS { if {[serverside] && [DIAMETER::command] == "257" } { DIAMETER::avp flags set 267 0 } } }
bugs.fix: This release always clears the Mandatory bit for Firmware-Revision AVPs in DIAMETER Capabilities Exchange Request messages.

bugs.title: syn-cookies incorrectly enabled in f5.ip_forwarding iApp template
bugs.symptoms: The f5.ip_fowarding iApp template disables loose-init and loose-close but does not disable syn-cookie protection in the fastL4 profile, causing traffic degradation.
bugs.conditions: Any deployment of the f5.ip_forwarding template will trigger this issue.
bugs.impact: Dropped packets.
bugs.workaround: Disable app-service strict-updates and then disable syn-cookie-enable on the appropriate fastL4 profile.
bugs.fix: SYN cookie protection is now correctly disabled in the fastL4 profile created during deployments of the f5.ip_forwarding iApp template.

bugs.title: Search Engine get Device ID challenge when using the predefined profiles
bugs.symptoms: When using one of the pre-defined profiles, "bot-defense-device-id-generate-after-access" and "bot-defense-device-id-generate-after-access", Search Engines might get Device ID challenges (and will most likely get blocked since cannot run JS)
bugs.conditions: One of the pre-defined profiles ("bot-defense-device-id-generate-after-access" or "bot-defense-device-id-generate-after-access") are attached to vs, and a valid search engine sends requests.
bugs.impact: Search Engines may be blocked.
bugs.workaround: Change mitigation of "Trusted Bot" in the attached profile to "Alarm": 1. Go to Security ›› Bot Defense : Bot Defense Profiles ›› bot-defense-device-id-generate-after-access or Security ›› Bot Defense : Bot Defense Profiles ›› bot-defense-device-id-generate-before-access 2. Go to tab "Mitigation Settings" 3. For "Trusted Bot" choose "Alarm". 4. Save profile.

bugs.title: Qkview produces core file if interrupted while exiting
bugs.symptoms: If, during qkview operation's exit stage, it is interrupted (with Ctrl-C for example), it produces a core file.
bugs.conditions: -- Qkview is exiting. -- The qkview operation receives an interrupt.
bugs.impact: A core file is produced.
bugs.workaround: When closing qkview, or if it is closing, do not interrupt it; wait for it to exit.

bugs.title: APMD leaks memory if access policy policy contains variable/resource assign policy items
bugs.symptoms: If an access policy contains variable/resource assign policy items, APMD will leak memory every time the policy is modified and applied.
bugs.conditions: 1. Access policy has variable/resource assign policy items. 2. The access policy is modified and applied.
bugs.impact: APMD's memory footprint will increase whenever the access policy is applied.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Memory growth has been addressed.

bugs.title: APMD recreates config snapshots for all access profiles every minute
bugs.symptoms: When the access profile configurations in APMD and MCPD are out of sync, APMD will detect the config snapshot for one access profile is missing. This triggers AMPD to recreates the config snapshots for all access profiles. The detect-recreate cycle will repeat every minute. Sep 11 17:57:39 BIG-IP err apmd[18013]: 01490259:3: Exception occurred for memcache operation: AccessPolicyProcessor/ProfileAccess.cpp line:492 function: resetTimeout - Config snapshot for profile /Common/ap could not be found using key tmm.session.a9735a75704_0ooooooooooooooooooo ... Sep 11 17:57:59 BIG-IP notice apmd[18013]: 014902f3:5: (null):Common:00000000: Successfully created config snapshots for all access profiles. ... Sep 11 17:58:39 BIG-IP err apmd[18013]: 01490259:3: Exception occurred for memcache operation: AccessPolicyProcessor/ProfileAccess.cpp line:492 function: resetTimeout - Config snapshot for profile /Common/ap could not be found using key tmm.session.a9735a75704_0ooooooooooooooooooo ... Sep 11 17:59:00 BIG-IP notice apmd[18013]: 014902f3:5: (null):Common:00000000: Successfully created config snapshots for all access profiles.
bugs.conditions: The condition under which the access profile configurations in APMD and MCPD become out of sync is unknown.
bugs.impact: TMM memory usage will increase due to excessive config snapshots created.
bugs.workaround: Restart APMD to clear the APMD and MCPD out of sync condition.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: AVRD crash when configured to send data externally, and there are large number of virtuals/pool-members
bugs.symptoms: In a configuration that AVR is set to send telemetry data to external source (like connection with BIG-IQ), and there is large number of config objects in the system, such as virtual servers and pool-members. AVRD is constantly crashing.
bugs.conditions: 1. AVR is set to send telemetry data to external source (like connection with BIG-IQ). 2. Large number of config objects in the system, such as virtual servers and pool-members.
bugs.impact: AVRD process is crashing and telemetry data is not collected.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed, AVR can handle any number of virtuals/pool-members when sending its telemetry.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT: Ephemeral listeners not created for unsubscribed outgoing calls
bugs.symptoms: When a temporary registration is created for an unsubscribed user making an outgoing call, an ephemeral listener to receive incoming messages is not created.
bugs.conditions: -- If nonregister-subscriber-callout attribute is enabled in the siprouter-alg profile. -- An unregistered client device places an outgoing call. At this point, a temporary registration is created. This temporary registration lives for the life of the call. -- During the lifetime of the temporary registration, if the connection from the client is closed, it is not possible for an external device to reach the client device.
bugs.impact: The callee of an outgoing call initiated by an unregistered SIP device cannot end the call.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: When a temporary registration is created, an ephemeral listener is created to receive SIP commands to be forwarded to the client device.

bugs.title: AVR JS injection can cause error on page if the JS was not injected
bugs.symptoms: If page-load-time is enabled in the AVR profile, and the response is small enough to not be chunked, AVR 'promises' to the client a JS injection in the response by adding the expected length of the JS to the Content-length header. If later, it is identified that the response contains no HTML tag, AVR does not inject the JS; instead it wraps the response with spaces. This can lead to errors in cases where the change in response size is not supported.
bugs.conditions: AVR is configured to collect 'Page Load Time' and the response from the web server has these conditions: -- The response is uncompressed. -- The context-type header is text/html. -- The response is not chunked (Context-length header exists). -- The payload does not include the HTML head tag.
bugs.impact: White Spaces at the end of the page can cause it to be invalid for some applications.
bugs.workaround: To avoid trying to inject to pages where the JS does not fit, use iRules to control which pages should get the JS injection. For detailed information, see K13859: Disabling CSPM injection with iRules :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13859.

bugs.title: SFP interfaces fail to come up on BIG-IP 2x00/4x00, usually when both SFP interfaces are populated
bugs.symptoms: The SFP interfaces do not come up or flap up and down repeatedly on BIG-IP 2000/4000 on boot up when both SFP interfaces are populated. When interface flaps state changes such as those below are logged in ltm log: info pfmand[PID]: 01660009:6: Link: 2.1 is UP info pfmand[PID]: 01660009:6: Link: 2.1 is DOWN
bugs.conditions: Both SFP interfaces, 2.1 and 2.2, on BIG-IP 2000/4000 are populated. This is typically observed after an upgrade to an affected version.
bugs.impact: Traffic cannot be sent/received from these interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Disconnect and reconnect the cable.
bugs.fix: The interfaces now come up successfully. Occasional link bounce may be seen on reboot.

bugs.title: memory leakage when "apply to base domain" is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Memory leakage when "apply to base domain" is enabled. this can result in a crash or aggressive sweeper mode.
bugs.conditions: "apply to base domain" is enabled in the anti-fraud profile
bugs.impact: Aggressive connections sweeper mode, and traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Non-admin users are not able to run the tmsh list command due to permissions error for LTM message-routing
bugs.symptoms: Any non-admin cannot use tmsh list commands. Running the command gives the following error: Unexpected Error: Can't display all items, can't get object count from mcpd.
bugs.conditions: Run a tmsh list command when logged in as non-admin user.
bugs.impact: Error is posted. Non-admin users cannot use the tmsh list commands.
bugs.workaround: Log in as admin to execute the tmsh list command.
bugs.fix: Non-admin users can now run tmsh list commands, as appropriate for the Role associated with the type of user account.

bugs.title: When the rate-limit setting is configured to a low value, sampled attack log messages are not logged
bugs.symptoms: On hardware platforms, with the default-internal-rate-limit of a DoS vector being set to a low number, there is no sampled attack message in the log, even the attack is being detected.
bugs.conditions: -- Setting the default-internal-rate-limit of the targeted DoS vector to a low number, e.g., 2. -- Detect attack.
bugs.impact: No visibility of the attack after being detected.
bugs.workaround: Use a higher number for the default-internal-rate-limit of the targeted DoS vector.
bugs.fix: A low default-internal-rate-limit value does not create problem. The sampled attack log message is being shown.

bugs.title: Omitted check for success of memory allocation for DNSsec resource record
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may panic from SIGABRT while logging this message: ./rdata.c:25: ldns_rdf_size: Assertion `rd != ((void *)0)' failed.
bugs.conditions: During memory stress while handling DNSsec traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM panic and subsequent interruption of network traffic.
bugs.workaround: Keeping the workload within normal ranges reduces the probability of encounter.
bugs.fix: The system now checks for success of memory allocation for DNSSEC resource record, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: When there is more than one route domain in a parent-child relationship, outdated routing entry selected from the parent route domain may not be invalidated on routing table changes in child route domain.
bugs.symptoms: In a situation when a routing entity belonging to the child route domain is searching for an egress point for a traffic flow, it's searching for a routing entry in the child domain first, then if nothing is found, it searches for it in the parent route domain and returns the best found routing entry. If the best routing entry from the parent route domain is selected, then it is held by a routing entity and is used to forward a traffic flow. Later, a new route entry is added to the child route domain's routing table and this route entry might be better than the current, previously selected, routing entry. But the previously selected entry doesn't get invalidated, thus the routing entity that is holding this entry is forwarding traffic to a less-preferable egress point. #Example: RD0(parent) -> RD1(child) routing table: default gw for RD0 is 0.0.0.0/0%0 pool member is 1.1.1.1/32%1 - Pool member searches for the best egress point and finds nothing in the routing table for route domain 1, and then later finds a routing entry, but from the parent route domain - 0.0.0.0/0%0. Later a new gw for RD1 was added - 0.0.0.0/0%1, it's preferable for the 1.1.1.1/32%1 pool member. 0.0.0.0/0%0 should be (but is not) invalidated to force the pool member to search for a new routing entry and find a better one if it exists, as in this case, with - 0.0.0.0/0%1.
