bugs.conditions: 1. There is more than one route domain in the parent-child relationship. 2. There are routing entries for the parent route-domain good enough to be selected as an egress point for the routing object (for instance, pool member) which is from child route domain. 3. The routing entry from a parent route domain is selected as an egress point for the object from the child route domain. 4. New routing entry for child route domain is added.
bugs.impact: If a new added route is preferable to an existing one in a different route domain, the new, preferable, route is not going to be used by a routing object that has previously selected a route. Thus, traffic flows through these routing objects to an unexpected/incorrect egress point. This might result in undesirable behavior: -- The route might be unreachable, and all traffic for a specific pool member is dropped. -- The virtual server cannot find an available SNAT address. -- Simply, the wrong egress interface is being used.
bugs.workaround: Use either of these workaround after a new route in child domain is added. -- Recreate a route. Recreate a parent route domain's routes. Restart tmrouted daemon if routes are gathered via routing protocols. -- Recreate a routing object. - If a pool member is affected, recreate the pool member. - If a SNAT pool list is affected, recreate it. - And so on.
bugs.fix: Routing objects are now forced to reselect a routing entry after a new route is added to the child route domain's routing table.

bugs.title: Pattern match in profile configuration may cause excessive memory and CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: tmm has abnormally high memory and CPU usage
bugs.conditions: In profile configuration, a pattern match such as "glob" is used, e.g. ltm profile http-compression my_httpcompression { uri-include { .* "(\?#glob)*" } }
bugs.impact: Excessive memory and CPU usage can drag system performance.

bugs.title: avrd memory leak when BIG-IQ fails to receive stats information
bugs.symptoms: AVRD has memory leak when it is failing to send statistical information to BIG-IQ.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is used by BIG-IQ version 6.0.0 or higher, and stats collection is enabled. Plus, BIG-IQ has some malfunction that prevents it from receiving the statistical information that BIG-IP is sending (for example: all DCDs are down, or not network connection between BIG-IP and BIG-IQ).
bugs.impact: avrd memory is increased over time, leading to avrd restart when it is getting too large
bugs.workaround: Connectivity issue between BIG-IP and BIG-IQ should be fixed, not just in order to prevent this memory leak, but for more important functionality such as visibility and alerts features in BIG-IQ.
bugs.fix: Memory leak is fixed.

bugs.title: False positive evasion violation
bugs.symptoms: When Referer header contains a backslash character ('\') in query string portion, 'IIS backslashes' evasion technique violation is raised.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Url Normalization' is turned on and 'Evasion Techniques Violations' is enabled. -- Referer header contains a backslash character ('\') in query string part.
bugs.impact: False positive evasion technique violation is raised for Referer header.
bugs.workaround: Turn off 'Url Normalization' on the 'Normalization Settings' section of the 'referer' property on the HTTP Header Properties screen.
bugs.fix: Fixed Referer value normalization to be done on the URL part only.

bugs.title: Add OCSP server support to IKEv2 negotiation for IPsec peer authentication
bugs.symptoms: There is no support for OCSP in IPsec.
bugs.conditions: When and IPsec ike-peer uses certificates, the name of a locally defined OCSP cert-validator object can be specified in new attribute ocsp-cert-validator, so the OCSP server is contacted during IKE negotiation, to authenticate the peer's certificate.
bugs.impact: If a peer is not using certificates, nothing happens. But if using certificates, the ike-peer's certificate is authenticated with the OCSP server, using asynchronous HTTP request during the middle of the IKE_AUTH exchange in IKEv2. Success permits new SA (security association) creation, while failure causes IKEv2 negotiation failure, denying an SA.
bugs.workaround: None, this is a code improvement.
bugs.fix: IKEv2 negotiation of SAs in IPsec now supports OCSP for certificate authentication. This requires the definition of and OCSP cert-validator in configuration, followed by adding the name of this object to attribute ocsp-cert-validator in the ike-peer configuration definition. Note: You can use this feature with IKEv2 but not IKEv1.
bugs.behavior: You can now add the name of an OCSP cert-validator to ike-peer in IPsec, to make a peer's certificate require authentication by OCSP before IKE negotiation succeeds and an SA (security association) is created. For docs on the new ocsp-cert-validator attribute see this help info: tmsh help net ipsec ike-peer For docs on how to create an instance of the OCSP object, see this help info: tmsh help sys crypto cert-validator ocsp The name must include the partition prefix. For example, If you create an instance named 'my_ocsp_srv' in the Common partition, then set ocsp-cert-validator like this: tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer peer_ocsp ocsp-cert-validator /Common/my_ocsp_srv This new attribute is only used when 1) the ike-peer also uses certificates, and 2) an instance of OCSP cert-validator with that name is found in configuration. When creating the OCSP object instance, you likely want a shorter timeout in order to minimize the effect of caching responses from the OCSP server. For example: tmsh create sys crypto cert-validator ocsp my_ocsp_srv dns-resolver my_dns timeout 4 cache-timeout 5 cache-error-timeout 5 responder-url http://10.100.145.64:8888 clock-skew 900 The cache-timeout and cache-error-timeout values cannot be smaller than timeout, so adding one second to the timeout value is suggested. Note if the responder-url has and explicit IP address, as shown above in the example, then a DNS resolver will not actually be used, so you can provide a dummy: tmsh create net dns-resolver my_dns forward-zones add { net { nameservers add { 10.20.20.100:53 } } } route-domain 0 The IP address given for my_dns above does not matter, because it will not be used. So my_dns merely serves to satisfy OCSP cert-validator creation, which requires either a dns-resolver or a proxy-server-pool in the command line. If an ike-peer uses certificates, and attribute ocsp-cert-validator is the name of a configured OCSP cert-validator instance, then during IKEv2 negotiation, the OCSP server will be contacted to authenticate the remote peer's certificate, during the IKE_AUTH exchange. This happens right after the AUTH signature payload is authenticated. If the OCSP server returns good status, negotiation succeeds and a new SA is created. Otherwise, for example if the OCSP says the peer's certificate has been revoked, then negotiation fails because the peer is not authenticated. Note: IKEv1 is not supported in this behavior change.

bugs.title: Requests that evaluate to same subsession can be processed concurrently
bugs.symptoms: Requests that evaluate to the same subsession can be processed concurrently in some cases
bugs.conditions: -- Per-Request policy with subroutines. -- Duplicate requests are sent that match existing subsession gating criteria.
bugs.impact: The request gets aborted with error messages in /var/log/apm: apmd_plugin.cpp func: "serialize_apmd_reply()" line: 495 Msg: AccessV2 agent execution error 4.

bugs.title: Potential mcpd crash in tmstat library
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases, the tmstat library might cause mcpd to crash.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that trigger this are unknown, but it is very rare.
bugs.impact: Mcpd crashes, causing a failover or outage.
bugs.fix: Prevented possible crash in tmstat library.

bugs.title: PEM iRule burst of session ADDs leads to missing sessions
bugs.symptoms: Some PEM sessions that were originally added, later disappear and cannot be added back.
bugs.conditions: -- Subscriber addition is done by iRule on UDP virtual servers. -- The sessions are added in a burst. -- A small fraction of such sessions cannot be added back after delete.
bugs.impact: Policies available in the missing session cannot be accessed.
bugs.workaround: Add a delay of at least a few milliseconds between adding multiple session with same subscriber-id and IP address.
bugs.fix: The release handles the issue that prevented the addition of the new subscriber. Now, even after the bursts of iRule additions, no re-additions fail.

bugs.title: Potential crash in TMM when updating pool members
bugs.symptoms: In very rare cases, TMM can crash while updating pool members.
bugs.conditions: The conditions that lead to this are not known.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes, which can cause a failover or outage.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Prevent TMM from crashing when updating a pool member.

bugs.title: A blade may occasionally get stuck and never be ready due to shared_random_data not ready
bugs.symptoms: A blade may occasionally get stuck and never be ready due to shared_random_data not ready.
bugs.conditions: Very occasionally shows up when a new blade is inserted.
bugs.impact: The blade cannot start properly.
bugs.fix: There is now reliable communication for shared_random_data to guarantee a non-primary node gets a copy of shared_random data.

bugs.title: AWS Cloud VE instance cannot connect to the metadata server to obtain licensing details.
bugs.symptoms: After booting BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in AWS, the device reports being unlicensed and does not pass traffic. The following chmand errors are visible in the logs: Curl request to metadata service failed with error(28): 'Timeout was reached' DossierReq exception: VirtDossier Service: Instance identity retrieval from the metadata failed. Check network connectivity to the instance metadata before retrying /var/log/kern.log contains error messages: kernel: [ 47.261935] VF could not set VLAN 1 kernel: [ 47.269080] ixgbevf 0000:00:03.0 eth0: failed to initialize vlan filtering on this port
bugs.conditions: -- VE in AWS cloud -- Single NIC configuration -- Intel ixgbevf NIC driver -- BIG-IP v13.1.3.3
bugs.impact: BIG-IP boots into an unlicensed state and does not pass traffic.
bugs.fix: VE can now communicate with the metadata server.

bugs.title: ARP table may not be updated properly by some TMMs
bugs.symptoms: When receiving ARP request coming from the client, some TMMs may not update the ARP table properly, leading to connectivity failures.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP with autolasthop disabled. - Client blocking ARP responses. - BIG-IP relies only on ARP requests coming from the client for sending the traffic back.
bugs.impact: This will have no impact in most of configurations, since BIG-IP will perform it's own resolution for client's MAC addresses. In a case where client is not responding to ARP probes sent by Big-IP, the problem may lead to connectivity failures for particular clients.
bugs.workaround: Configure static ARP entries OR enable autolasthop.

bugs.title: CSRF fires Javascript error in IE7 or IE11 Compatibility View to IE7
bugs.symptoms: When csrf enabled in asm policy, it fires javascript errors in IE7
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual - ASM csrf protection configured - An HTML page accessed via IE7 or IE11 Compatibility View to IE7
bugs.impact: csrf doesn't work in IE7, POST requests being sent from IE7 will be blocked.
bugs.workaround: Disable CSRF protection in asm policy
bugs.fix: csrf code is fixed and now have basic support for IE7

bugs.title: SIP falsely detects media flow collision when SDP is in both 183 and 200 response
bugs.symptoms: A spurious error message is logged ("MR SIP: Media flow creation (...) failed due to collision") and media does not flow.
bugs.conditions: A SIP server responds to an INVITE with both a 183 "Session Progress" and later a "200 OK" for a single SIP call, and both responses contain an SDP with the same media info.
bugs.impact: Media does not flow on pinholes for which a collision was detected and reported.
bugs.fix: No collision is detected or logged when multiple messages with SDP recreate the same flows in the same call.

bugs.title: Small memory leak while creating Access Policy items
bugs.symptoms: Memory slowly leaks for every access policy item added: 32 + 80 bytes for each item.
bugs.conditions: The leak occurs while creating new policy items in Access.
bugs.impact: After long uptime mcpd may crash due to lack of memory.
bugs.workaround: restart mcpd periodically if you modify Access policies frequently by adding or deleting policy items.
bugs.fix: Leak was fixed by clearing the leaked objects.

bugs.title: Fragile NATT IKEv2 interface mode tunnel suffers RST after flow-not-found after forwarding
bugs.symptoms: -- SYN/ACK packets arriving on a tunnel fail to be matched to an existing flow followed by a RST issued by the BIG-IP system. -- The BIG-IP system reports 'no flow found'. -- MAC addresses can contain random values, or fe:fe:fe:fe:fe:fe.
bugs.conditions: -- Using IKEv2 with both NAT-T and interface mode. -- The BIG-IP is configured to use several tmm instances. -- The combination of IP addresses and port numbers result in distributing legs of processing one flow across several tmm instances.
bugs.impact: NATT/ESP tunnel flows can end with a RST reset.
bugs.fix: In the ESP proxy, The system now clears a bit in packet metainformation related to forwarding, so a decrypted packet such as SYN/ACK can reach the last tmm needed.

bugs.title: PCCD may get into crash-loop after BIG-IP upgrade or after BIG-IP restart
bugs.symptoms: When there are scheduled firewall rules, and per-policy compilation optimization enabled, PCCD may enter crash-loop after installing new build. In very rare cases this can happen after regular BIG-IP restart. Per-policy compilation optimization is enabled by default, the sys db variable pccd.perpolicycompilation is true.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is licensed and provisioned. -- There are scheduled firewall rules. -- Per-policy compilation optimization enabled (sys db variable pccd.perpolicycompilation is true) -- The BIG-IP system is upgraded or restarted
bugs.impact: After this failure, an rare problem is that PCCD is continuously crashing. New firewall config is not applied on data traffic. The pre-upgrade firewall config is still applied on data traffic.
bugs.workaround: Set sys db variable pccd.perpolicycompilation to false.
bugs.fix: PCCD works correctly in these conditions.

bugs.title: Macro policy does not find corresponding access-profile directly
bugs.symptoms: The discovery task runs but does not apply the 'Access Access Policy' for the access policy for which the Provider is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Auto-discovery is enabled for a provider. -- Discovery occurs.
bugs.impact: The Access Policy is not applied after successful auto-discovery. The policy must be applied manually.
bugs.workaround: Apply the Access Policy manually after auto-discovery.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with not automatically applying the access policy after discovery.

bugs.title: TMM SIGABRT seen in HTTP/2 gateway scenario when shutting down connection
bugs.symptoms: TMM SIGABRT seen in HTTP/2 gateway scenario when shutting down connection.
bugs.conditions: This might occur rarely when the HTTP/2 gateway is configured on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: TMM SIGABRT no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: AAA CRLDP configurations configured using the 'No Server' option may be rendered incorrectly while using IE v11
bugs.symptoms: When a user tries to see a AAA CRLP server which has been configured with a 'No Server' option, the server connection shows up as Direct when it is in fact 'No Server'. This is not the case in other browsers, such as Google Chrome v69 or Mozilla Firefox v57. They show the configured object value correctly for the AAA CRLP Server, which is 'No Server'.
bugs.conditions: Using the Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) browser v11.
bugs.impact: Inaccurate configuration information shown for the server connection.
bugs.workaround: Use Firefox version 57 or Chrome version 69. Alternatively, view the correct value using the following tmsh command: tmsh list apm aaa crldp all-properties

bugs.title: Error 'This Logout URL already exists!' when updating logout page via GUI
bugs.symptoms: When you try to update the Logout Page, you get an error about the URL existence: Error 'This Logout URL already exists!'
bugs.conditions: 1. Create any Logout page. 2. Try to update it.
bugs.impact: The properties of the Logout Page cannot be updated.
bugs.workaround: Delete the logout page and create a new one.
bugs.fix: This release addresses the issue, so that no error is reported when updating the Logout Page.

bugs.title: IPv6 Duplicate Address Detection may fail.
bugs.symptoms: When a new Self IP address is added, the BIG-IP system sends Neighbor Solicitation messages to the solicited-node multicast address corresponding to the new address but does not send Neighbor Solicitation messages to the solicited-node multicast address corresponding to the link local address.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 Strict Compliance is enabled.
bugs.impact: Duplicate link-local addresses may not get detected.

bugs.title: TCP Analytics supports ANY protocol number
bugs.symptoms: No TCP analytics data is collected for an ANY virtual server.
bugs.conditions: 1. Provision AVR 2. Create a FastL4 server that accepts all protocols. 3. Attach a TCP Analytics profile 4. Try to run UDP traffic through it.
bugs.impact: No TCP analytics data is collected for TCP flows when a virtual server's protocol number is ANY.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround this time.
bugs.fix: TCP analytics now supports both ANY and TCP protocol numbers and would collect analytics for TCP flows if protocol number is ANY or TCP.

bugs.title: TMM core when processing invalid timer
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes while processing an SSLO iRules that enables the SSL filter on an aborted flow.
bugs.conditions: SSLO is configured and passing traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: SSL filter will no longer be enabled after connection close.

bugs.title: Native VMware Horizon client fails to authenticate against APM if RADIUS challenge is used
bugs.symptoms: Native VMware Horizon client fails to authenticate against APM if RADIUS challenge is used, e.g. RADIUS server performs two factor authentication.
bugs.conditions: 1. Native VMware Horizon client is used to connect via APM. 2. RADIUS authentication agent is present in Access Policy. 3. RADIUS server asks for challenge response (e.g. 2FA).
bugs.impact: Authentication fails. User can't get access to VMware Horizon resources.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue preventing native VMware Horizon client to authenticate with RADIUS challenge.

bugs.title: RADIUS Authentication over RSA SecureID is not working in challenge mode
bugs.symptoms: Cannot change/reset RSA PIN.
bugs.conditions: Using RADIUS Auth Agent to communicate with RSA SecurID server for user authentication.
bugs.impact: Users cannot change or reset RSA PIN.
bugs.fix: RADIUS Authentication over RSA SecurID now works in challenge mode.

bugs.title: BIG-IP sends spurious ICMP PMTU message to server
bugs.symptoms: After negotiating an MSS in the TCP handshake, the BIG-IP system then sends an ICMP PMTU message because the packet is too large.
bugs.conditions: -- The server side allows timestamps and the client side does not negotiate them. -- The client-side MTU is lower than the server-side MTU. -- There is no ICMP message on the client-side connection.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary retransmission by server; suboptimal xfrag sizes (and possibly packet sizes).
bugs.workaround: Disable timestamps or proxy-mss on the server-side TCP profile.

bugs.title: Paging controller changed
bugs.symptoms: Old paging controller allowed you jump to the last page or to any custom page you wanted. This could result in really long load time.
bugs.conditions: Lots of entries in split view pages (e.g. Request Log)
bugs.impact: Very long load time or event timeout.
bugs.workaround: instead of going to the last page - you can just change sorting order. jump to specific page out of the first 3-5 - is not a common scenario and can be replaced by applying filter.
bugs.fix: paging controller changed to more modern one which doesn't allow jump to the last/custom page - only 3-4 pages in each direction.

bugs.title: Remote logging needs 'localip' to set source IP properly
bugs.symptoms: The source ip of log entries sometimes uses the system's self IP address.
bugs.conditions: This occurs during system start-up if syslog-ng starts before the management IP and route are up. This issue can also occur in a high availability (HA) environment.
bugs.impact: Remote log entry has the wrong source IP address.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to set the local-ip parameter as per: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13080#localip For example, to configure the BIG-IP syslog to bind to 10.10.10.10 when sending logs to the remote syslog server mysyslogB, enter the following command: modify /sys syslog remote-servers modify { mysyslogB { local-ip 10.10.10.10 }} Note: For BIG-IP systems in a HA configuration, the non-floating self IP address is recommended if using a TMM-based IP address. Note: In case a nonexistent localip is configured in include option, configure a unique persist-name per https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID740589.html.

bugs.title: Phishing detection is loaded without being licensed
bugs.symptoms: When client has phishing detection enabled but not licensed, phishing enable still loaded even though it's not supposed to.
bugs.conditions: Phishing Detection is enabled but not licensed.
bugs.impact: Phishing Detection is loaded even though it's not licensed
bugs.workaround: Configure as BLFN: function(C){C.repeat=1;C.A.B.B=0;}
bugs.fix: Phishing Detection now will no longer be loaded when module is not licensed.

bugs.title: Kerberos Auth agent may override settings that manually made to krb5.conf
bugs.symptoms: when apmd starts up, it can override settings in krb5.conf file with those required for Kerberos Auth agent
bugs.conditions: - Kerberos Auth is configured in an Access Policy, - administrator made changes to krb5.conf manually to the section [realms] of the configured realm
bugs.impact: Kerberos Auth agent behavior is not what administrator expects with the changes. it may also affect websso(kerberos) to behave properly
bugs.fix: after fix, the configuration file changes are merged. Kerberos Auth agent adds the lines it requires and does not override existing settings

bugs.title: HTTP Profile Request Header Insert Tcl error
bugs.symptoms: A TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: When the HTTP profile Request Header Insert field contains a Tcl interpreted string, Tcl is executed to expand the string before the header is inserted into the request header block. If a Tcl error occurs
bugs.impact: In some cases this can cause TMM to crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following to mitigate this: -- Verify that your Tcl executes correctly in all cases. -- Use a static string.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: Virtual server with access profile in local traffic group is disabled after upgrade from pre-13.1
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server is disabled, error message: Oct 3 16:03:00 istc-sslvpn warning mcpd[6831]: 0107185a:4: Warning generated, for version 13.1.0 or greater : Disable virtual server /Common/VPN_vs because it has access profile attached and its associated traffic group (/Common/traffic-group-local-only) is different from another one () that is also associated with a virtual server with access profile attached
bugs.conditions: Standalone device with a VS using the same IP address as the Self-IP.
bugs.impact: Virtual server with access profile is disabled.
bugs.workaround: Manually re-enable virtual server.
bugs.fix: Virtual server state is kept the same after upgrade.

bugs.title: Attack Signatures page: filter applied by another user may replace currently applied filter
bugs.symptoms: If user switches between different policies in the Policy Attack Signature page, and at the same time another user changes Policy Attack Signature properties on the same page, after policy is changes - filter applied by second user is applied for the first user.
bugs.conditions: 2 different users work on the Policy Attack Signature page simultaneously
bugs.impact: Incorrect filter applied at some scenarios, which may be confusing for user

bugs.title: Extractions are learned in manual learning mode
bugs.symptoms: - BIG-IP reports "Changes pending" frequently - Errors in pabnagd.log: "Missing Parameter Rule1 attribute element"
bugs.conditions: Direct cause: Policy contains parameters with dynamic type Indirect cause: Policy Builder is configured to classify parameters as dynamic (related to bug 717525)
bugs.impact: - BIG-IP reports "Changes pending" frequently - Errors in pabnagd.log: "Missing Parameter Rule1 attribute element"
bugs.workaround: - Change all dynamic parameters value types to User Input with Alpha Numeric data type - Unset parameters' dynamic value type (or uncheck all parameters' dynamic classification options in 'Learning And Blocking Settings').
bugs.fix: Policy Builder does not set extractions for dynamic parameters in manual mode

bugs.title: 'Unable to load the certificate file' error and configuration-load failure upgrading from 11.5.4-HF2 to a later version, due to empty cert/key in client SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: During upgrade, the configuration fails to load due to an invalid client SSL profile cert/key configuration. The system posts an error: Unable to load the certificate file. This occurs as a result of an invalid configuration that can be created as a result of a bug (614675) that exists in 11.5.4-HF2 (and only in 11.5.4-HF2). Because of the bug, it is possible to create a client SSL profile with an empty cert-key-chain, as shown in the following example: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/cssl { app-service none cert none cert-key-chain { "" { } <=============== empty cert-key-chain defualt_rsa_ckc { <==== typo: 'defualt' cert /Common/default.crt key /Common/default.key } } key none } Note: This upgrade failure has an unique symptom: the typo 'defualt_rsa_ckc'. However, the name has no specific negative impact; the issue is with the empty cert-key-chain. After upgrading such a configuration from 11.5.4-HF2 to any later version of the software, the system posts a validation error, and the configuration fails to load.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when all the following conditions are met: -- You are using 11.5.4-HF2. -- The 11.5.4-HF2 configuration contains an invalid client SSL profile (i.e., a client SSL profile containing an empty cert-key-chain). -- You upgrade to any software version later than 11.5.4-HF2.
bugs.impact: After upgrade, the configuration fails to load. The system posts an error message similar to the following: -- "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- Loading schema version: 11.5.4 Loading schema version: 13.1.0.8 01071ac9:3: Unable to load the certificate file () - error:2006D080:BIO routines:BIO_new_file:no such file. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: You can fix the profile configuration in /config/bigip.conf either before the upgrade (in 11.5.4-HF2), or after the upgrade failure. To do so: 1. Replace 'cert none' with a cert name, such as /Common/default.crt. 2. Replace 'key none' with a key name, such as /Common/default.key. 3. Remove the entire line containing the following: "" { }. 4. Correct the spelling of 'defualt' to 'default'. Although there are no negative consequences of this typo, it is still a good idea. The new profile should appear similar to the following: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/cssl { app-service none cert /Common/default.crt chain none cert-key-chain { default_rsa_ckc { cert /Common/default.crt key /Common/default.key } } key /Common/default.key }

bugs.title: Drd utility can hang when generating qkview
bugs.symptoms: "qkview -v" shows qkview generation got stuck on qkafm.so module while executing /usr/sbin/drd: Executing Module: [qkafm.so] Executing /usr/bin/du -h /var/lib/mysql/logdb/ ... Result: [0] Elapsed: 0.064386 Executing /usr/sbin/drd --readlong=/usr/sbin/readlong --all ...
bugs.conditions: AFM module is provisioned
bugs.impact: Impossible to create qkview.
bugs.workaround: # mount -o remount,rw /usr # sed -i '/output.wait()/d; s/return output.stdout.readlines()/return output.communicate()[0].splitlines(True)/g' /usr/sbin/drd # mount -o remount,ro /usr

bugs.title: OSPF packets are duplicated in the BIG-IP in L2 transparent mode using virtual wires
bugs.symptoms: OSPF packets are duplicated while traversing a virtual wire.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured in L2 transparent mode using a virtual wire.
bugs.impact: OSPF unreliability can impact the overall routing domain and in turn impact services dependent on it.
bugs.fix: Handle multicast packets through a virtual wire correctly.

bugs.title: 'Illegal Query String Length' violation displays wrong length
bugs.symptoms: When the system decodes a query string that exceeds the allowed query string length, the system reports the incorrect 'Illegal Query String Length' violation string length.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Illegal Query String Length' violation is encountered. -- The query string is decoded and reported.
bugs.impact: The system reports the decoded character count rather than bytes. For example, for a Detected Query String Length = 3391, the system posts a Detected Query String Length = 1995.

bugs.title: Persistence records leak while the HA mirror connection is down
bugs.symptoms: Memory might leak on the active unit while the high availability (HA) mirror connection is down.
bugs.conditions: -- The persistence configured that requires its state to be stored stored on the BIG-IP system. -- Mirroring is configured on the persistence profile or the virtual server. -- Mirror connection is down, for example, next active is down/offline/unavailable.
bugs.impact: Memory leak until the HA mirror connection is up. Once mirror connection is up, the system releases the memory.
bugs.workaround: -- Disable persistence while HA mirror connection is down (e.g., performing maintenance). -- Disable session mirroring for iRules. -- Use persistence that does not requires its state to be stored on the BIG-IP system. -- Restore HA connection.
bugs.fix: Persistence records no longer leak memory while the HA mirror connection is down.

bugs.title: GTPv2 MEI and Serving-Network fields decoded incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: MEI and Serving-Network vales obtained with GTP::ie get iRule command contains digits swapped in pairs, first digit missing and a random digit added at the back.
bugs.conditions: Processing GTP traffic with iRules.
bugs.impact: It is impossible to obtain correct value of MEI and Serving-Network fields of the GTPv2 packets when processing with iRules.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Decoding of GTPv2 MEI and Serving-Network fields corrected.

bugs.title: With AFM enabled, during bootup, there is a small possibility of a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: During bootup, with AFM enabled, there is a small possibility of a tmm crash. The tmm process generates a core file and then automatically restart.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM enabled. -- sPVA-capable hardware platform. -- Boot up the system.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes, coredumps, and then restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The race-condition has been fixed, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Rare TMM restart due to NULL pointer access during AFM ACL logging
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes while performing log ACL match logging.
bugs.conditions: The problem can happen only with the following configuration: 1) AFM Logging for ACLs enabled. 2) Security Network Logging profile has the property "log-translation-fields enabled" The problem happens under extremely rare circumstances.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Defensive error handling to avoid the scenario of NULL pointer access.

bugs.title: iApp: f5.ldap fails when monitor pw contains '$'
bugs.symptoms: The f5.ldap iApp posts an error and fails to deploy when the user enters a monitor password containing the '$' (dollar/peso currency) character.
bugs.conditions: LDAP monitor password contains '$'.
bugs.impact: iApp does not deploy.
bugs.workaround: There are two workaround: -- Create the monitor prior to deploying the iApp, and then select it from a dropdown list in the iApp to deploy. -- The iApp deploys normally for passwords that do not contain $ characters.
bugs.fix: This version supports the use of monitor passwords containing '$' in the f5.ldap iApp template.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE with 1nic does not handle fragmented traffic to webui or ssh properly
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to send fragmented packets destined for SSH or the webui of BIG-IP VE running with 1 NIC will fail. This is a rare situation generally, but one noted area where we have seen it is when BIG-IQ attempts to discover the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE configured with 1 network interface. Send IP fragmented traffic to either SSH or the web interface (TCP/8443 for 1nic).
bugs.impact: The IP fragments will not be properly reassembled and the connection will ultimately fail. This is only an issue for IP fragmented traffic sent with 1nic destined for SSH or the webui.
bugs.workaround: Prevent IP fragmentation, or configure multiple network interfaces.

bugs.title: DNS64 stats not increasing when requests go through dns cache resolver
bugs.symptoms: DNS64 stats are not incrementing when running the tmsh show ltm profile dns or in tmctl profile_dns_stat commands if responses are coming from dns cache resolver.
bugs.conditions: DNS responses are coming from dns cache resolver.
bugs.impact: DNS64 stats not correct.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: File manually uploaded information is not synced correctly between blades
bugs.symptoms: When you upload a file, the file is marked internally as manually uploaded. When the system downloads a file, it is marked as not being manually uploaded. This information is not passed and handled correctly on chassis.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration is deployed on multiple blades -- Fail over has occurred. -- New update file is downloaded from ESDM on the primary blade.
bugs.impact: Security updates are not automatically installed on the new primary blade after failover.
bugs.workaround: Manually install security updates on new primary blade.
bugs.fix: Corrected sync/handle information about file files, whether they are manually uploaded or downloaded from ESDM.

bugs.title: MBLB SIP dropping packets with unknown methods
bugs.symptoms: Traffic sent to a MBLB SIP LB is dropped if the SIP method is unknown.
bugs.conditions: Packets encountered SIP methods not already known to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Packet is dropped.
bugs.workaround: Include the SIP method in sip.perf

bugs.title: Modifying datagroup type at runtime is not supported
bugs.symptoms: After a hand-edit of BIG-IP configuration to modify a datagroup's type, "tmsh load sys config" appears to succeed without error. However, the datagroup type change does not take effect.
bugs.conditions: Edit datagroup type by hand.
bugs.impact: Datagroup and the rules which reference it do not behave as expected.
bugs.workaround: If feasible, create a new datagroup with the desired type.

bugs.title: Invalidation trigger parameter containing reserved XML characters does not create invalidation rule
bugs.symptoms: If a parameter value for an invalidation trigger contains reserved XML characters, compilation of the resulting invalidation rule fails due to the reserved characters not being escaped.
bugs.conditions: - AAM policy with invalidation trigger defined - trigger request with parameter value(s) containing reserved XML characters
bugs.impact: The invalidation rule requested by the trigger request is not created. Content is not invalidated as expected.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists.
bugs.fix: The reserved XML characters are now properly escaped and the invalidation rule is created as expected.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not support Azure D2_V3 or D4_V3 instance types
bugs.symptoms: If BIG-IP images are run on Azure D2_V3 or D4_V3 instance types, mcpd may fail to start correctly and be killed either by the kernel's hung process watchdog, or from a SIGABRT from sod. This prevents the instance from being able to operate normally. Support for these instance types has not been added yet.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP running within Azure cloud environment utilizing D2_V3 or D2_V4 instances.
bugs.impact: The system may run fine, but in some cases it has been observed that mcpd will fail to start properly and be killed. If this occurs, the system will fail to operate normally.
bugs.workaround: Run on a V2 instance.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT: SIP Response message not forwarded by BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: SIP Server sends SIP Request to the client. The SIP Server inserts a different port, so that response are received on a different port. The Client sends the response on the new requested port. BIG-IP drops the packet
bugs.conditions: SIP Server wants the SIP Response to be coming on a different port.
bugs.impact: SIP Request will not receive the SIP Response
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: Fix BIG-IP to process the SIP Response and send it to the SIP Server

bugs.title: RAID status in tmsh is not updated when disk is removed or rebuild finishes
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh show sys raid' shows stale information When the RAID status changes because a disk fails, is pulled without being removed from the RAID, or when RAID rebuild completes, the new status is not updated to be visible in tmsh. Log messages, SNMP traps and alerts associated with the change in RAID status do not appear.
bugs.conditions: -- Platforms that support RAID running 14.0.0 or later. -- Running the command: tmsh show sys raid.
bugs.impact: 'tmsh show sys raid' output might show disk as ok when it has actually failed, or may show the disk as rebuilding when it is actually ok.
bugs.workaround: From a bash shell run the command 'array' to see the correct state of the RAID. If a disk has failed or been removed, the following tmsh commands remove the disk from the RAID: tmsh mod sys raid array <arrayName> remove <DiskName>

bugs.title: pkcs11 test utility is failing when running nethsm-test on BIG-IP systems configured for AWS CloudHSM
bugs.symptoms: When using the nethsm-test tool to validate netHSM installation and configuration on the BIG-IP system, running the command 'tmsh run sys crypto nethsm-test' fails.
bugs.conditions: -- AWS CloudHSM installed and configured as BIG-IP netHSM. -- Running nethsm-test.
bugs.impact: Failure to run command: tmsh run sys crypto nethsm-test. pkcs11 test utility fails.

bugs.title: API Protection feature inadvertently allows editing of associated access policy
bugs.symptoms: This release contains a feature called API Protection. API Protection access policies are hidden from the user interface in most areas except the log settings area.
bugs.conditions: Modifying API Protection access policy from Access :: Overview :: Event Logs :: Settings.
bugs.impact: If the API protection policy / profile is modified outside of API Protection GUI, the 'Apply Access Policy' may become activated with no way to deactivate it.
bugs.workaround: Navigate to the API Protection area and modify any part of the API Protection profile. This causes it to re-deploy, at which time the system clears the 'Apply Access Policy' prompt.

bugs.title: Memory leak in BDoS module
bugs.symptoms: TMM runs out of memory and restarts. The memory usage as shown in "tmctl memory_usage_stat", under module line tag "session" is noticed to be high, and keeps growing.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen when BDoS feature is configured, and if there exits Custom or Auto Generated BDoS Signatures. When such signatures exist, the BDoS one second timer callback leaks memory.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable BDoS feature. Disable all configured and auto generated BDoS signatures using TMSH command: modify security dos dos-signature all { state disabled }

bugs.title: admd livelock under CPU starvation
bugs.symptoms: Due to the resources starvation the worker thread of admd does not get CPU for more than two minutes. At the same time, the configuration thread does get CPU. The admd heartbeat failure occurs at 120 seconds. The SOD daemon kills admd. The system posts messages similar to the following: -- notice sod[6783]: 01140041:5: Killing /usr/bin/admd pid 6732 -- warning sod[6783]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat ADMD.Anomaly0 fails action is restart. -- warning sod[6783]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat ADMD.Publisher0 fails action is restart.
bugs.conditions: -- High CPU / memory utilization, -- Very large configuration. Note: There are no known special configuration requirements to have this occur.
bugs.impact: admd restarts. Behavioral DoS does not work.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: admd livelock event no longer occurs in response to CPU starvation in very large configurations.

bugs.title: BDoS Signature can wrongly match a DNS packet
bugs.symptoms: When using BDoS feature for DNS protocol, and when there are auto-generated DNS Signatures or if Custom DNS signatures are configured manually, it is found that at times, a valid DNS request is dropped because it wrongly matches the configured/dynamically generated DNS Signature when the box is under load, and BDoS mitigation is ongoing.
bugs.conditions: Configured DNS Signature (Or) there exists a Dynamically generated DNS Signature. Such a DNS signature is found to match a DNS packet wrongly, even though the signature match criteria is different from the matched DNS packet.
bugs.impact: When box is under load, the configured DNS signature gets into Attack Mitigation mode (which is normal), but may wrongly drop a DNS packet that does not match the signature.
bugs.workaround: Disable BDoS for protocol DNS. Also, do not use Manually configured DNS Signatures.
bugs.fix: The parsed DNS information is cached and re-used wrongly as a performance optimization, which is corrected.

bugs.title: Multiple wildcards not matched to most specific WideIP when two wildcard WideIPs differ on a '?' and a non-wildcard character
bugs.symptoms: Multiple wildcards not matched to the most specific WideIP.
bugs.conditions: Two wildcard WideIPs differ on a '?' and a non-wildcard character.
bugs.impact: DNS request will get wrong answer.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Multiple wildcards are now matched to the most specific WideIP when two wildcard WideIPs differ on a '?' and a non-wildcard character.

bugs.title: pkcs11d error code not logged in logs
bugs.symptoms: When NetHSM debug logging is turned on, pkcs11d does not log the return codes it receives via PKCS11 API from the Safenet Luna and Thales.
bugs.conditions: It occurs when any pkcs11 api fails for some reason.
bugs.impact: Makes it more difficult to debug the root cause of pkcs11 failure.
bugs.workaround: Engage F5 Support when this level of diagnostic information is required.

bugs.title: 'Transaction Not Found' Error on PATCH after Transaction has been Created
bugs.symptoms: In systems under heavy load of transactions with multiple icrd_child processes, the system might post an erroneous 'Transaction Not Found' response after the transaction has definitely been created.
bugs.conditions: Systems under heavy load of transactions with multiple icrd_child processes.
bugs.impact: Failure to provide PATCH to a transaction whose ID has been created and logged as created.
bugs.workaround: If transaction is not very large, configure icrd_child to only run single-threaded.
bugs.fix: Erroneous 'Transaction Not Found' messages no longer occur under these conditions.

bugs.title: SSD bay identification incorrect for RAID drive replacement
bugs.symptoms: On iSeries platforms with dual SSDs, the 'bay' of a given SSD indicated in the 'tmsh show sys raid' command may be incorrect. If a drive fails, or for some other reason it is intended to be replaced, and you are using the bay number listed from the tmsh command, the wrong drive could be removed from the system resulting in system failure to operate or boot.
bugs.conditions: iSeries platform with dual SSDs.
bugs.impact: Removal of the one working drive could result in system failure and subsequent failure to boot
bugs.workaround: If you discover that you removed the incorrect drive, you can attempt to recover by re-inserting the drive into the bay that it was in, and powering on the device. The following steps will help to avoid inadvertently removing the wrong drive: As a rule for systems with this issue: -- Power should be off when you remove a drive. This makes it possible to safely check the serial number of the removed drive. -- Power should be on, and the system should be completely 'up' before you add a new drive. Here are some steps to follow to prevent this issue from occurring. 1. Identify the failed drive, taking careful note of its serial number (SN). You can use any of the following commands to get the serial number: • tmsh show sys raid • tmsh show sys raid array • array 2. Logically remove the failed drive using the following command: tmsh modify sys raid array MD1 remove HD<> 3. Power down the unit. 4. Remove the fan tray and physically remove the failed drive. 5. Manually inspect the SN on the failed drive to ensure that the correct drive was removed. 6. Replace the fan tray. 7. Power on the unit with the remaining, single drive. 8. Once booted, wait for the system to identify the remaining (good) drive. You can confirm that this has happened when it appears in the 'array' command output. 9. Remove fan tray again (with the system running). 10. Install the new drive. 11. Use the 'array' command to determine that the new drive is recognized (Note: the tmsh commands do not show new drive at this stage.) 12. Logically add the new drive using the command command: tmsh modify sys raid array MD1 add HD<> 13. Monitor the rebuild using any of the commands shown in step 1. Note: You must follow these steps exactly. If you insert the new drive while the system is off, and you then boot the system with the previously existing working drive and the new blank drive present, the system recognizes the blank drive as the working Array member, and you cannot add it to the array. That means system responds and replicates as if 'HD already exists'.

bugs.title: Browser becomes unresponsive when loading the network map with a virtual server that contains a forwarding rule policy in the second position
bugs.symptoms: Browser becomes unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: Loading the network map with a virtual server that contains a forwarding rule policy in the second position.
bugs.impact: Browser becomes unresponsive and must be restarted.
bugs.workaround: Change the position of the forwarding rule policy.
bugs.fix: The browser now behaves as expected when loading the network map with a virtual server that contains a forwarding rule policy in the second position.

bugs.title: [PA] Client side HTML patcher does not handle the case when both newlines and HTML tags are present in attribute value
bugs.symptoms: Broken HTML on the page. This occurs because of there are both both newlines and HTML tags specified in the attribute value definition.
bugs.conditions: document.write with newlines in attribute value. For example: document.write("");
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than not using this construction.
bugs.fix: You can now use both newlines and HTML tags specified in the attribute value definition.

bugs.title: Connection reset seen with SSL bypass on a L2 wire setup
bugs.symptoms: A connection reset occurs when trying to bypass SSL forward proxy on a L2 Wire setup.
bugs.conditions: -- configure an SSL policy to bypass the SSL forward proxy in an L2 Wire setup. -- Attempt to pass traffic that matches the policy.
bugs.impact: Traffic that matches the policy experiences a reset when attempting to do the bypass. Cannot bypass SSL forward proxy on a L2 wire setup
bugs.fix: The system now recognizes that it is doing a bypass in a L2 Wire setup, and handles the bypass to avoid the reset.

bugs.title: Race condition between clustered DIAMETER devices can cause the standby to disconnect its mirror connection
bugs.symptoms: Depending on the DIAMETER settings of the BIG-IP system, there can be a race condition in a mirrored device cluster where the standby BIG-IP system resets its mirror connection to the active device.
bugs.conditions: -- MRF DIAMETER in use. -- The DIAMETER session profile on the BIG-IP system is configured to use a non-zero watchdog timeout. -- The DIAMETER session profile on the BIG-IP system is configured to use Reset on Timeout. -- This is more likely to happen if (in the DIAMETER session profile) the Maximum Watchdog Failures is set to 1, and the Watchdog Timeout is configured to be the same value as the remote DIAMETER system.
bugs.impact: The standby is no longer mirroring the active system, and gets out of sync with it. There may be connections lost if a failover occurs.
bugs.workaround: To mitigate this issue: 1. Configure the Maximum Watchdog Failures to a value greater than 1. 2. Configure the Watchdog Timeout as something different from the same timeout on the remote peer, preferably to something that will have little overlap (i.e., the two timers should fire at the exact same time very infrequently).
bugs.fix: Prevented the standby from sending DWR packets to the active device, so that it no longer expects DWA responses that never arrive.

bugs.title: Portal Access: IE: not rewritten content produced by rewritten document.write() targeted to parent window.
bugs.symptoms: With Portal Access and the Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) browser, all links are not rewritten on the page of a web application.
bugs.conditions: -- Portal Access and IE browser. -- On content not rewritten dynamically, created by JavaScript, which uses document.write() targeted to the parent window.
bugs.impact: Web-application does not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: You can use a custom iRule to work around this issue.
bugs.fix: With Portal Access and the Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) browser, all links are now rewritten on the page of a web application.

bugs.title: TMM crashes on shutdown when using virtio NICs for dataplane
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash on stop or restart.
bugs.conditions: 1. Put the virtio NIC in a bad state while TMM is running (for example, detach the NIC from the host). 2. Run the following command: bigstart stop tmm
bugs.impact: TMM crash generates a core file. However, there is no impact on traffic as the device is already in a bad state before the crash.
bugs.fix: TMM does not crash on stop/restart regardless of NICs state.

bugs.title: bd crash with specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: BD crash
bugs.conditions: A specific scenario may cause bd crash.
bugs.impact: Failover, traffic disturbance.

bugs.title: It is possible for the archive.tm2 file to not get cleaned up
bugs.symptoms: The istats daemon maintains a file (/var/tmstat2/blade/archive.tm2) that is used to track the addition and deletion of dynamic statistics. It is possible for this file to grow so large that it causes the istats daemon to use too much CPU.
bugs.conditions: This rarely happens, but it is due to loss of state, such that stale statistics are maintained when they should have been deleted.
bugs.impact: The istats daemon can use too much of the control plane CPU in this error condition.
bugs.workaround: Remove the /var/tmstat2/archive.tm2 file. The system recovers after one cycle of processing the archive file.

bugs.title: DHCP Relay does not retain client source IP address for chained relay mode
bugs.symptoms: The second relay in a DHCP relay chain modifies the src-address. This is not correct.
bugs.conditions: Using DHCP chained relay mode.
bugs.impact: The src-address is changed when it should not be.
bugs.fix: For chained relay mode there is now an option to preserve the src-ip, controllable by 'sys db tmm.dhcp.relay.change.src'.

bugs.title: MRF SIP curr_pending_calls statistic can show negative values.
bugs.symptoms: Certain irregular SIP message patterns may produce an erroneous curr_pending_calls value that can drop below zero and underflow.
bugs.conditions: Uncommon message flows like re-transmitted INVITE or OK responses can trigger the issue, which may be brought about at times by lost packets when using UDP.
bugs.impact: SIP curr_pending_calls may show incorrect values.

bugs.title: Illegal parameter violation when json parsing a parameter on a case-insensitive policy
bugs.symptoms: An illegal parameter violation is raised although the parameter is configured
bugs.conditions: The policy is configured as case insensitive, and a parameter is configured with capital letters
bugs.impact: False positive illegal parameter violation
bugs.workaround: Configure violation as case sensitive

bugs.title: FPS to splunk logging is confusing
bugs.symptoms: When using a splunk destination for the risk-engine publisher, the log message template is ignored. instead all available fields are logged in a splunk formatted way. On the other hand, FPS requires a non-empty log message for actually sending the logs, this means that the user must assign a dummy value in the log message template.
bugs.conditions: 1. splunk destination 2. non empty log message (sys db antifraud.internalconfig.strin1 or antifraud.internalconfig.strin2)
bugs.impact: User must set a dummy content for the log messages in order to be able to send the logs. However, the actual content will be not as expected in case of a splunk formatted destination.
bugs.workaround: Set a dummy value (a single space will do) in the log messages template.

bugs.title: SafeNet purchased by Gemalto -- impacting links to support
bugs.symptoms: safenet was purchased by Gemalto and the safenet-inc.com site links no longer work. Docs need updates for support links.
bugs.conditions: User tries to use the old safenet links in the old docs and does not use the new links in the new doc pointing toward gemalto.
bugs.impact: User goes to a non-working link.
bugs.workaround: Docs updated to reflect that SafeNet was purchased by Gemalto -- impacting support links/urls in docs. New support link user should use is: https://supportportal.gemalto.com
bugs.fix: Changed SafeNet support link/url to Gemalto support link/url.

bugs.title: Higig MAC recovery mechanism may fail continuously during run time
bugs.symptoms: At runtime, the Higig MAC recovery mechanism might be triggered due to FCS errors. Normally, the recovery mechanism will recover from the issue. However, if it does not recover, the mechanism will continue to run over and over again.
bugs.conditions: May related to the traffic pattern the blade is processing.
bugs.impact: The blade will stay at Inoperative state and not able to pass traffic
bugs.workaround: Manually reboot the blade.
bugs.fix: The blade will now reboot if fcs recovery is not able to fix the link. The reboot can be disabled by DB variable tmm.hsb.hgmfcsresetaction

bugs.title: Manager users cannot perform changes in per-request policy properties
bugs.symptoms: Users with Admin role can edit and administer per-request policy properties. Users with Manager role, which can manage most APM objects, cannot manage this specific one.
bugs.conditions: User with Manager role tries to modify or change per-request policies properties.
bugs.impact: Cannot manage per-request policy properties if user role is Manager.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than having an Admin user manage these objects.
bugs.fix: Added per-request policy objects to the list of objects that can be managed by users with Manager role/

bugs.title: Unable to edit Per-Request Policies logged in as a user account configured with the Manager role.
bugs.symptoms: If you navigate in the GUI to Access :: Profiles :: Policies :: Per-Request Policies and try to edit a per request policy logged in with a user with the role of Manager, you get an error message as follows: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: -- Logged in as a user whose role is Manager. -- Trying to edit per-request policy.
bugs.impact: Cannot edit per-request policies with user accounts whose role is Manager.
bugs.workaround: Log in with a user configured with the Admin role to edit in this case.
bugs.fix: You can now edit per-request policies from the GUI and tmsh while logged in as a user configured with a Manager role.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing iSession traffic
bugs.symptoms: The TMM process may crash when processing traffic with an iSession virtual server.
bugs.conditions: iSession virtual server enabled
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes iSession traffic as expected.

bugs.title: BIG-IP with physical/cloud HSM integration needs to restart tmm after a fresh install
bugs.symptoms: Immediately following a fresh BIG-IP install to a BIG-IP system with physical/cloudhsm integration, a nethsm key/cert-enabled SSL client profile cannot be applied to a virtual server. The system reports the following error messages: Profile /Common/c.1 - cannot load key/cert/chain: /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_key_d/:Common:k1_61411_1//config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/:Common:k1_61414_1/: Not found. warning tmm1[19027]: 01260009:4: Connection error: hud_ssl_handler:1149: invalid profile (40)
bugs.conditions: Apply a client SSL profile with cloud/physical HSM key/cert.
bugs.impact: Virtual server enabled with cloud/physical HSM key/cert cannot be configured.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm after the fresh install: bigstart restart tmm

bugs.title: Remove 'sys-unconfig' and 'rhel-configure' binaries and related systemd service
bugs.symptoms: The RHEL-related binaries 'sys-unconfig' and 'rhel-configure' are shipped with BIG-IP when they are not relevant.
bugs.conditions: Running a BIG-IP v14.1.x release
bugs.impact: Binaries with RHEL branding are installed on system which are not used in BIG-IP and generate superfluous files.
bugs.fix: Removed 'sys-unconfig' and 'rhel-configure' binaries and related systemd service

bugs.title: Under unlikely circumstances, TMM hangs and is terminated by the failover daemon
bugs.symptoms: TMM hangs and subsequently is terminated by sod.
bugs.conditions: -- Payload manager is used. -- Another profile (e.g., rewrite) on an HTTP virtual server needs unchunked payload for processing. Note: Although this is an unlikely set of conditions, it can occur, depending on the traffic you have.
bugs.impact: Failover occurs. TMM goes into a loop, and after 10 seconds, it's killed by sod. After it restarts, the system comes back online and can pass traffic. However, if the same conditions recur, the failover happens again. The frequency of the failover recurrence depends on the traffic.

bugs.title: Network Firewall : Active Rules page does not list active rule entries for firewall policies associated with any context
bugs.symptoms: In Security :: Network Firewall :: Active Rules, when selecting any context (Global, Route Domain, Virtual Server, or SelfIP), the policy associated with the Virtual Server is listed, but not the rules within that policy.
bugs.conditions: Applies to any context policies.
bugs.impact: You cannot manage rules from the Active Rules page. This is GUI display issue and does not affect functionality.
bugs.workaround: In Security :: Options :: Network Firewall :: Firewall Options: Disable Inline Rules. This reverts to the legacy editor and displays the policy details.
bugs.fix: Network Firewall : Active Rules page now lists active rule entries for firewall policies associated with any context.

bugs.title: Occasionally ramcache might crash when data is sent without the corresponding event.
bugs.symptoms: Ramcache filter causes crash when sending data without HUDCTL_RESPONSE while in CACHE_COLLECT event.
bugs.conditions: When the access_policy_trace db variable is enabled, failure in insertion of policy path cookie in the header while sending a redirect to the client might cause the ramcache filter to SIGSEGV.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Turn off the access_policy_trace db variable.
bugs.fix: The system now handles this scenario, so there is no longer a ramcache crash.

bugs.title: IPsec / ESP traffic pinned to TMM 0 for SP-Dag on 4000s/4200v, 2000s/2200v platforms
bugs.symptoms: Traffic pinned to TMM 0 using Source/Destination Disaggregation (SP-DAG) on 4000s/4200v, 2000s/2200v platforms.
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec / ESP packets. -- SP-DAG configured. -- Using 4000s/4200v, 2000s/2200v platforms.
bugs.impact: Traffic disaggregation does not operate as expected. Traffic pinned to TMM 0.

bugs.title: APM Endpoint inspection fails on macOS Mojave
bugs.symptoms: When there are two or more endpoint checks that require OPSWAT libraries, the endpoint checks fail on macOS Mojave.
bugs.conditions: Access Policy profile with two or more endpoint checks such as AntVirus, Firewall, System Patch.
bugs.impact: Network Access (VPN) is denied.

bugs.title: Key logging chrome extension can bypass Websafe KeyLogger
bugs.symptoms: When installed, JSLogger extension can bypass password field protection and get the real password input
bugs.conditions: JSLogger extension installed
bugs.impact: Password value is captured
bugs.fix: Code adjustment for better event faking

bugs.title: tmm cores under stress test on virtual server with DoS profile with admd enabled
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores
bugs.conditions: -- Systems under stress testing. -- Virtual server with DoS profile with admd enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Turn off Behavioral DOS.
bugs.fix: This tmm core no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: Anti-Bot Mobile SDK cookie name change to support identical cookies for multiple virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Multiple virtual servers are each using different cookie names for cookies 72, 74, and 76. This occurred because these cookie names are dependent on virtual server properties.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple subdomains are configured to resolve to different virtual servers with different ASM policies. -- Anti-Bot Mobile SDK attempts to connect to these virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Anti-Bot Mobile SDK is not able to connect to multiple virtual servers using the same cookie.
bugs.fix: The relevant cookie names were changed. The format TS00000000_7x (prefix/suffix may change according to configuration) is now used for cookies 72, 74, and 76, which results in identical cookie names for all configured virtual servers. This will allow Anti-Bot Mobile SDK to connect to multiple virtual servers using the same cookie.

bugs.title: Bot Detection injection include tags which may cause faulty display of application
bugs.symptoms: The Bot Detection feature / Bot Defense profile includes JavaScript which is injected within <APM_DO_NOT_TOUCH> tags. Some web applications may be displayed incorrectly due to these tags.
bugs.conditions: - Your application includes JavaScript which dynamically adds HTML elements and expects a certain set of tags in the <head> section of the HTML. - Bot Detection / Bot Defense are enabled.
bugs.impact: Some web applications may be displayed incorrectly.
bugs.fix: There is now an ASM Internal Parameter 'inject_apm_do_not_touch' and a db variable 'asm.inject_apm_do_not_touch', which can be disabled (modify sys db asm.inject_apm_do_not_touch value false) to prevent the <APM_DO_NOT_TOUCH> tag from being injected, thus allowing the application to be displayed correctly.
bugs.behavior: This release provides an ASM Internal Parameter 'inject_apm_do_not_touch', and a db variable 'asm.inject_apm_do_not_touch', which can be disabled (the default is enabled) to prevent the <APM_DO_NOT_TOUCH> tag from being injected, thus allowing the application to be displayed correctly. To disable db variable, run the following command: modify sys db asm.inject_apm_do_not_touch value false

bugs.title: Virtual server stops passing traffic after modification
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server stops passing traffic after changes are made to it.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server is using a port-list or address-list -- High availability (HA) environment with multiple traffic groups -- A change is made to the virtual server
bugs.impact: Every time you make changes to the virtual server, the traffic-group for the virtual address is changed, and traffic goes down.

bugs.title: Traffic bridged between VLANs in virtual-wire setups may have the wrong destination MAC in packets that egress from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.symptoms: Potential MAC relearning at the switches the BIG-IP system is connected to.
bugs.conditions: -- DB variable connection.vlankeyed set to disabled. -- Multiple virtual-wires configured on the BIG-IP system. -- Client to server and server to client traffic using different virtual wires on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Packets reach their L3 destination using an unexpected L2 path.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than re-enabling sys db connection.vlankeyed.
bugs.fix: Connflow next hop and previous hop updates are now done in the correct order for virtual wires.

bugs.title: Incorrect handling of memory allocations while processing DNSSEC queries
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- Heavy DNS traffic using DNS security signatures. -- Use of external HSM may aggravate the problem.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release corrects the handling of memory allocations while processing DNSSEC queries.

bugs.title: iControl REST cert creation not working for non-Common folder
bugs.symptoms: Certificate creation under a non-Common folder using iControl REST doesn't work. For example, the user sends the iControl REST message and gets the error message return: curl -sk -u admin:f5site02 https://10.192.84.16/mgmt/tm/sys/crypto/cert/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST -d '{"name":"/my_dir/mmmmm", "common-name":"cn","key":"/my_dir/mmmmm"}' | ~/bin/json-parser-linux64 { "code": 400, "message": "Unable to extract key information from \"/config/filestore/files_d/my_dir_d/certificate_key_d/:my_dir:mmmmm_166121_1\"to \"/var/system/tmp/tmsh/87bOS1/ssl.key//my_dir/mmmmm\"", "errorStack": [], "apiError": 26214401 }
bugs.conditions: The user attempts to create an SSL certificate under a non-Common folder using iControl REST.
bugs.impact: Unable to create an SSL certificate in non-Common folder.
bugs.workaround: Create the SSL certificate using tmsh.
bugs.fix: With the fix, certificate can be created under non-Common folder using iControl REST.

bugs.title: Import is failing for APM SSO Config Saml object
bugs.symptoms: Import of policy is failing with Syntax Error: '[api-status-warning]' unexpected argument.
bugs.conditions: Imported policy has APM SSO Config Saml object.
bugs.impact: Unable to import policy.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue, follow this procedure: 1. Unpack conf.tar.gz. 2. Edit the ng-export.conf file to find and remove the line containing [api-status-warning]. 3. Packup conf.tar.gz again.
bugs.fix: [api-status-warning] are being handled so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: DataSafe Logging Settings page is missing when DataSafe license is active
bugs.symptoms: DataSafe Logging Settings page is missing when DataSafe license is active
bugs.conditions: 1. DataSafe license is active 2. Logging of Login attempts feature enabled
bugs.impact: DataSafe Logging Settings page is missing in GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to configure the logging of Login attempts feature.
bugs.fix: FPS GUI should display Logging Settings page also when DataSafe license is active.

bugs.title: FastHTTP insert XFF header can be incorrect
bugs.symptoms: When using the FastHTTP profile to insert an XFF header, the value can be incorrect.
bugs.conditions: FastHTTP profile to insert a XFF header
bugs.impact: The value can be incorrect.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with XFF header insertion in the FastHTTP profile.

bugs.title: invalid inactivity timeout suggestion for cookies
bugs.symptoms: ASM will report "invalid inactivity timeout" suggestions to delete a cookie, even though the cookies are being sent and are valid.
bugs.conditions: - Inactivity timeout feature is configured in Policy Builder - Cookie entity is configured in the policy - Valid, non-violating traffic containing cookies is passed
bugs.impact: Since non-violating traffic is not sent to the policy engine, the inactivity timeout timer is never reset, which will eventually lead to suggestions to delete the inactive cookie entities. These suggestions are erroneous because valid cookies are being sent in the traffic.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the inactive entity suggestions for cookies
bugs.fix: Inactivity learning for cookies has been deprecated, the feature does not cover cookies anymore.

bugs.title: South Sudan, Sint Maarten, and Curacao country missing in GTM region list
bugs.symptoms: South Sudan, Sint Maarten, and Curacao countries are missing from the region list.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a GTM region record. -- Create a GTM any region of Country South Sudan, Sint Maarten, or Curacao.
bugs.impact: Cannot select South Sudan county from GTM country list.
bugs.fix: South Sudan, Sint Maarten, and Curacao are now present in the GTM country list.

bugs.title: Datasync may start background tasks during high disk IO utilization
bugs.symptoms: Datasync daemon runs background tasks only when CPU and RAM resources are available. However, there is no check for when the disk IO is busy. When the disk IO is heavily used but CPU and RAM are available, the background tasks may start causing the disk IO to be used even heavier, affecting performance.
bugs.conditions: - Client-side ASM/FPS features are enabled. - Other conditions causing high disk IO usage on the device.
bugs.impact: - High disk IO causing occasional performance degradation - On extreme cases, datasyncd may miss its heartbeat and cause a failover

bugs.title: Some tmsh list commands may fail with message 'Password could not be retrieved' when SSLO is provisioned but not APM
bugs.symptoms: Some tmsh list commands may fail while SSLO is provisioned but no urldb or APM modules are provisioned with the following message: 'Password could not be retrieved'.
bugs.conditions: -- SSLO is provisioned. -- Neither APM or URLDB are provisioned. -- Run the generic tmsh list command.
bugs.impact: tmsh command fails and posts the error: Unexpected Error: Password could not be retrieved. Note: Some 'tmsh list' commands with arguments do run. For example, 'tmsh list net vlan' provides correct output, but 'tmsh list' does not.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than provisioning APM or URLDB. Note: You can provision APM or URLDB even if they are not licensed. Although the full feature set is not available without a license, provisioning loads the daemons needed to support the generic 'tmsh list' command.
bugs.fix: We hide the oath options when only SSLO is provisioned so that we do not require SQL to be up with SSLO. Oauth is not needed under SSLO.

bugs.title: MRSIP log of subscriber deletion outputs '(null)" for subscriber URI
bugs.symptoms: New logging was added for SIP subscriber registration and deletion. The deletion log MRSIPERR_SUBSCRIBER_DELETION_LOG() fails to show the subscriber URI, and instead, /var/log/ltm shows messages similar to the following: MR_SIP: Subscriber registration deleted (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:5060 -> yyy.yyy.yyy.yyy:5060) subscriber URI: (null)
bugs.conditions: -- A SIP subscriber registration is deleted. -- The log level DB variable log.mrsip.level is 'notice' or above.
bugs.impact: Prevents correlation of the deletion with the corresponding registration of the subscriber URI.
bugs.fix: The /var/log/ltm shows the subscriber URI, (for example): MR_SIP: Subscriber registration deleted (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:5060 -> yyy.yyy.yyy.yyy:5060) subscriber URI: 100028@example.com

bugs.title: VMware Horizon idle timeout is ignored when connecting via APM
bugs.symptoms: VMware Horizon has an option to set idle timeout under "View Configuration\Global Settings\General\Client-dependent settings\For clients that support applications". When there is no keyboard or mouse activity for the given time, application sessions should be disconnected (desktop sessions are staying, though). This settings has no effect when connecting via APM.
bugs.conditions: VMware Horizon idle timeout setting for applications is configured and remote application is launched via APM.
bugs.impact: VMware Horizon idle timeout setting for applications has no effect.
bugs.fix: VMware Horizon idle timeout "For clients that support applications" is now honored when connecting via APM.

bugs.title: TMUI does not provide option to enable BADOS TLS fingerprint signatures
bugs.symptoms: TMUI does not provide option to enable BADOS TLS fingerprint signatures.
bugs.conditions: ASM licensed
bugs.impact: You can't enable BADOS TLS fingerprint signatures via TMUI.
bugs.workaround: tmsh is available to enable TLS fingerprint BADOS signatures.

bugs.title: CSRF situation on BIGIP-ASM GUI
bugs.symptoms: CSRF situation on the BIG-IP ASM GUI that might potentially lead to resource exhaustion on the device for the moment it is being run.
bugs.conditions: The following URL accepts a wildcard in the parameter id, making it a heavy URL: https://BIG-IP/dms/policy/pl_negsig.php?id=*
bugs.impact: Once multiple requests are sent to the target GUI, it is possible to see httpd process spiking even in core 0 (VMWare).
bugs.fix: If the query string parameter has a string value the query is not executed.

bugs.title: Disk partition /var/log is low on free disk space
bugs.symptoms: Warning messages, such as these on system CLI: -------------- Broadcast message from root@bigip1.test.net (Wed Nov 7 09:01:01 2018): 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var/log (slot 1) has only 0% free --------------
bugs.conditions: ASM or DoS is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Disk partition /var/log is low on free disk space.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete nsyncd logs from /var/log.
bugs.fix: There is now stricter log rotation for nsyncd.

bugs.title: Portal Access: rewriting for Worker.postMessage(msg,transfer) should not rewrite 2nd argument
bugs.symptoms: Using Portal AQccess the browser posts an error message in it's console similar to the following: Failed to execute 'postMessage' on 'Worker': No function was found that matched the signature provided.
bugs.conditions: Web-application contains javascript code which in turn contains postMessage() to worker with second argument which is array.
bugs.impact: Web-application misfunction
bugs.workaround: Custom iRule workaround is possible. For example: # custom workaround for BZs 749142 for specific page when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { # path to html page where postMessage is used: if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "/custom_path" } { REWRITE::post_process 1 set sw 2222 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { if {[info exists sw] && $sw == 2222} { unset sw set strt [string first {</head>} [REWRITE::payload]] if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt 0 { <script> (function(){ var old_f5_ipm = F5_Invoke_postMessage; // BZ 749142: fix F5_Invoke_postMessage F5_Invoke_postMessage = function () { if ('string' === typeof arguments[2]) { return old_f5_ipm.apply(this, arguments) }else{ return Function.prototype.call.apply(arguments[0].postMessage,arguments); // call source function } } // just a hack to enable unzipped content of Worker for iRule processing (this is impossible for F5CH=I) F5_Invoke_Worker = function () { arguments[1] = F5_WrapURL(arguments[1],"h"); return new Worker(arguments[1]) } })(); </script> } } } }
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed.

bugs.title: Cannot create LTM policy from GUI using iControl
bugs.symptoms: LTM policy cannot be created from GUI using iControl REST.
bugs.conditions: Using iControl to create an LTM policy.
bugs.impact: LTM policy cannot be created from the GUI
bugs.workaround: Create LTM policy using TMSH.
bugs.fix: Can now create LTM policy from GUI using iControl.

bugs.title: Problem sync policy contains non-ASCII characters
bugs.symptoms: When access policy contain non-ASCII characters, policy sync either fails or the characters are not sync'ed properly on the target.
bugs.conditions: -- Using an access profile. -- Access profile contains non-ASCII characters (code point greater than 0x7f), e.g.,in VPE, add an 'Advanced Resource Assign' agent and specify an expression similar to the following in addition to the resource: expr { [string tolower [mcget -decode {session.ad.last.attr.memberOf}]] contains [string tolower "CN=Suporte_TransmissãČo,"] || [string tolower [mcget -decodde {session.ad.last.attr.memberOf}]] contains [string tolower "CN=suporte_tx,"]} -- Start policy sync on the profile.
bugs.impact: Policy sync fails or does not complete properly for the non-ASCII characters.
bugs.fix: Policy sync now works properly when the policy contains non-ASCII characters.

bugs.title: DataSafe: Cannot lower secure-channel-lifetime through GUI
bugs.symptoms: A secure channel cookie lifetime must be greater than or equal to other cookies lifetime. The BIG-IP system GUI does not show non-DataSafe cookies, so there is no way to change their lifetime setting, if needed.
bugs.conditions: -- In tmsh, specify a secure-channel cookie lifetime value. -- In the GUI, set the non-DataSafe cookie lifetime to a value that is greater than the secure-channel cookie lifetime. -- Save the configuration.
bugs.impact: The save operation fails with the error message: Results in an error: Save Failed: 01071a07:3: The lifetime of Malware forensics cookie should be less than or equal to the lifetime of Secure channel cookie in the Anti-Fraud profile '/Common/test'. The secure-channel cookie lifetime cannot be lowered using the GUI; you must use tmsh to do so.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to change the cookie's lifetime value.

bugs.title: Added description of subviolation for the suggestions that enabled/disabled them
bugs.symptoms: Missing description of subviolation for the suggestions that enabled/disabled them.
bugs.conditions: There are suggestions that enabled/disabled subviolations in the security policy.
bugs.impact: Cannot determine the subviolation for the suggestions that enabled/disabled them.
bugs.workaround: Open Description in an additional tab in Learning and Blocking settings screen.
bugs.fix: Added description of subviolation for the suggestions that enabled/disabled them.

bugs.title: New Application Ready Templates
bugs.symptoms: Application Ready Templates do not support current versions of their applications.
bugs.conditions: Using Application Ready Templates.
bugs.impact: F5-tuned templates are not available to fully secure the latest version of some applications.
