bugs.fix: The following Application Ready Templates have been updated to newer versions: - Drupal 8 - OWA 2016 - Sharepoint 2016 - Wordpress 4 Reference: F5DevCentral/f5-asm-policy-template-v13 :: https://github.com/f5devcentral/f5-asm-policy-template-v13/tree/master/application_ready_template_v13

bugs.title: dname compression offset overflow causes bad compression pointer
bugs.symptoms: DNS requests receive error response: - Got bad packet: bad compression pointer - Got bad packet: bad label type
bugs.conditions: When dns response is large enough so that dname redirect to an offset larger than 0x3f ff.
bugs.impact: DNS response is malformed.
bugs.fix: dname compression offset overflow no longer causes bad compression pointer.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT: Temporary registration not extended by subsequent INVITE
bugs.symptoms: INVITE message being processed operation creates a temporary registration entry for a unregistered subscriber, this registration entry is not extended if a subsequent invite occurs. This could cause the registration to expire during a call, thus allowing the reserved translated addresses to be provided to a different subscriber.
bugs.conditions: An INVITE message is received when unregistered-subscriber-callout attribute in the siprouter-alg profile
bugs.impact: The system adds a temporary registration entry to the registration table. The lifetime for this entry is the max-session-timeout value from the siprouter-alg profile. Subsequent INVITES will not extend the lifetime. This could cause the registration to expire during a call, allowing the reserved translated addresses to be provided to a different subscriber.
bugs.fix: Subsequent INVITEs now extend the lifetime by another max-session-timeout value.

bugs.title: IPsec tunnels fail to establish and 100% cpu on multi-blade BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: IPsec tunnels fail to establish and CPUs go to 100%.
bugs.conditions: - IPsec tunnels configured. - System has multiple blades.
bugs.impact: The CPU exhaustion may cause system instability. The tmm logs may contain large numbers of messages similar to the following: -- notice SA is not in LARVAL state when receives PFKEY UPDATE: src=50.1.1.53 dst=40.1.1.50 spi=0xc9cd688 proto=0x32 dir=0x1:IN reqid=0.0:0:0x10c81 state=1
bugs.workaround: For vCMP systems, provision the Guest on one blade only. There is no workaround for bare-metal systems.
bugs.fix: An internal control-plane messaging loop has been fixed.

bugs.title: TMM cores when query session index is out of boundary
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores when the queried session index is out of boundary. This is not a usual case. It is most likely caused by the memory corrupted issue.
bugs.conditions: When session index equals the size of session caches.
bugs.impact: TMM cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The index boundary check now operates correctly in this situation, so tmm no longer cores.

bugs.title: Global DNS DoS vector does not work in certain cases
bugs.symptoms: Global DNS DoS vector stops working under certain conditions.
bugs.conditions: Packets are not made to go through its entirety.
bugs.impact: Global DNS data structures are overwritten by subsequent incoming packets. Global DNS DoS vector does not rate-limit the packets.
bugs.fix: Global DNS DoS vector checks now prevent this issue, so rate-limiting works as expected.

bugs.title: Client-SSL Object's description can be updated using CLI and with REST PATCH operation
bugs.symptoms: REST PUT fails to update the object description when proxy-ca-cert and proxy-ca-key are not configured, and triggers an error: SSL forward proxy RSA CA key is missing.
bugs.conditions: Issue is seen only with REST PUT operation, and when proxy-ca-cert and proxy-ca-key are not configured.
bugs.impact: REST PUT operation cannot be used to update/modify the description.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following: -- You can use TMSH to update/modify the description, even if proxy-ca-cert and proxy-ca-key are not configured. -- You can also use PATCH operation and send only the required field which need modification.

bugs.title: Bare-metal installs via 'image2disk' may fail in v14.1.0 or greater
bugs.symptoms: Running a bare-metal installation via image2disk (IE, 'image2disk --format=volumes <ISO>') may fail due to a missing command in the maintenance OS.
bugs.conditions: The version of MOS installed on the system is from a v14.1.0 or newer ISO, and a user attempts a bare-metal installation via the 'image2disk' command.
bugs.impact: Unable to perform bare-metal installations/installations from MOS in affected versions.
bugs.workaround: The installed version of MOS can be removed with the command '/usr/lib/bpdiag -a mos'. After doing this, installing a version older than 14.1.0 will re-install an older version of MOS without this issue. You can then reboot to MOS and manually run the installation using 'image2disk' from there.
bugs.fix: Fix issues with bare-metal installations via 'image2disk' failing.

bugs.title: Audit Log: 'cmd_data=list cm device recursive' are being generated continuously even the command has not been executed
bugs.symptoms: The system generates and logs the following message continuously, at the rate of 3 times a minute: user=root folder=/ module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=list cm device recursive:.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in normal operation.
bugs.impact: All tmsh commands are logged including the command which executed by a internal cron job. So, messages of 'cmd_data=list cm device recursive' are logged in /var/log/audit even the command has not been executed by a user. This is designed behavior.

bugs.title: 'table delete' iRule command can cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM SegFaults and restarts.
bugs.conditions: 'table delete' gets called after another iRule command.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Call 'table lookup' on any key before performing a 'table delete'. Whether or not the key was added into the database beforehand does not matter.
bugs.fix: Fixed code to prevent invalid use of internal data structure.

bugs.title: AFM ACL Rule with Redirect to Virtual action can on rare occasions cause TMM restart
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart when Traffic hits AFM Policy Rule having Redirect to Virtual Action, and when the Redirected to Virtual is being modified or when traffic hits the box immediately on TMM service being up. During the time when the TMM has just started, some of the Virtual Server could be in the process of being Ready. When traffic hits the TMM right after TMM startup, and if the Redirect to Virtual is not yet Ready is when this crash is likely. Virtual Server can also be in a not yet Ready state during configuration change of the Virtual Server.
bugs.conditions: AFM Rule with Redirect to Virtual configured Traffic Matching the Redirect to Virtual rule The Redirect to Virtual Server is not Ready. When a Virtual Server goes through configuration change, or when TMM has just started and not all Virtual Servers are in Ready state yet, this problem can be hit.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and service disruption. Since the issue can happen when TMM is just up after initialization, when the Virtual Servers are in the process of being initialized one by one, a restart of TMM could cause repeated such TMM crash and restarts.

bugs.title: Modifying nodes/pool-member can lose monitor_instance and monitor_rule_instances for unrelated objects
bugs.symptoms: There are two symptoms: -- Modifying the monitor for a node or pool-member might remove monitor rule instances and monitor instances for other nodes/pool-members. -- After those unrelated monitor rule instances and monitor instances are removed, if you try to alter the state of the pool-member/node, the system posts the following message: Invalid monitor rule instance identifier.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system is configured with nodes, pool-members, and pools with monitors. -- Modify one of the nodes that is not in a pool. -- Run the following command: tmsh load /sys config -- Loading ucs/scf file can trigger the issue also.
bugs.impact: The system might delete monitor rule instances for unrelated nodes/pool-members. Pool members are incorrectly marked down.
bugs.workaround: Failover or failback traffic to the affected device.

bugs.title: Race condition while modifying analytics global-settings
bugs.symptoms: Updating the analytics global-settings might cause a core for avrd. The avrd.log contains the following record: AVRD_CONFIG|NOTICE... 13931|lib/avrpublisher/infrastructure/avr_mcp_msg_parser.cpp:2985| Modified Analytics Global Settings, added "0" offbox TCP addresses
bugs.conditions: Analytics global-settings are updated either explicitly, using a tmsh command, or implicitly, by internal process script.
bugs.impact: Might cause a core for avrd. After coring once, avrd is expected to start normally without any additional cores. The configuration change is expected to be applied correctly after restart is complete.
bugs.fix: Race condition no longer occurs while modifying analytics global-settings.

bugs.title: Race condition while BIG-IQ updates common file
bugs.symptoms: The file /var/config/rest/downloads/app_mapping.json is being used by two processes: BIG-IQ and avrd. This can cause a race-condition between the two and in some rare cases can cause avrd to crash.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IQ updating /var/config/rest/downloads/app_mapping.json while avrd is reading it.
bugs.impact: avrd might read incomplete data, and can even core in some rare cases.
bugs.fix: This race condition no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Unable to issue iControl rest API to perform 'tmsh show running-config' command
bugs.symptoms: Cannot mimic a tmsh show or list command using iControl REST.
bugs.conditions: Referred to the iControl REST User Guide, version 13.
bugs.impact: Not able to replace a tmsh show or list command with an iControl REST request.
bugs.workaround: There are no hard and fast rules to mimic the show or list command in iControl REST, other than to make a GET request to an endpoint. This information is stated in the user guide. Based on the tmsh man page, running-config is an option and a suggestion is to try: /mgmt/tm/sys/proc-info/stats?options=running-config

bugs.title: Provisioning URLDB and SWG simultaneously produces a confusing error message if neither module was originally provisioned
bugs.symptoms: If you have URLDB or SWG provisioned and try to provision the other, you will get an error message: The requested provision module (%s) is not compatible with already provisioned module (%s). This same error message is displayed if neither module was provisioned to start with, and can be confusing.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to provision SWG and URLDB without either module being originally provisioned
bugs.impact: You can safely ignore the benign error message.
bugs.fix: New message makes sense regardless of the starting state (i.e. SWG or URLB or neither originally provisioned): Module (%s) is not compatible with module (%s). These modules can't be provisioned simultaneously.

bugs.title: Improved visibility for Accept on Microservice action in Traffic Learning
bugs.symptoms: Low visibility for accepted on microservice action.
bugs.conditions: There are suggestions that can be accepted on microservice.
bugs.fix: Improved visibility for Accept on Microservice action and microservice-related details of suggestions.
bugs.impact: The system does not show Accept on Microservice in a suggestion.

bugs.title: LDNS and DNSSEC: Various OOM conditions need to be handled properly
bugs.symptoms: Some LDNS and DNSSEC out-of-memory (OOM) conditions are not handled properly.
bugs.conditions: LDNS and DNSSEC OOM conditions.
bugs.impact: Various traffic-processing issue, for example, TMM panic during processing of DNSSEC activity.
bugs.fix: The system contains improvements for handling OOM conditions properly.

bugs.title: Error messages seen while running "run sys crypto nethsm-test" tool
bugs.symptoms: Error messages seen while running nethsm-test tool with command "run sys crypto nethsm-test" Invalid req_id 1073741841 actual 1073741842 in Message Header: Ignoring the Message
bugs.conditions: Install and Configure AWS cloudHSM as BIG-IP netHSM. Run command "tmsh run sys crypto nethsm-test.
bugs.impact: Error messages seen while running "tmsh run sys crypto nethsm-test" with AWS cloudHSM.
bugs.workaround: You may use aws cloudhsm client 1.0.18 or 1.1.0 to work around this issue.

bugs.title: IVS connection on VLAN with no floating self-IP can select wrong self-IP for the source-address using SNAT automap
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions the wrong self-IP can be selected as a source address for connections from an Internal Virtual Server to remote servers.
bugs.conditions: - Using an Internal Virtual Server (IVS). - The VLAN being used to connect from the IVS to the server does not have a floating self-IP configured. - At least one other VLAN has a floating self-IP configured. - The primary virtual server that connects to the IVS is using SNAT automap.
bugs.impact: IVS traffic might not be routed properly.
bugs.workaround: - Configure a floating self-IP on the IVS server side VLAN. or - Use a SNAT pool instead of automap.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG: Potential to end wrong call when BYE received
bugs.symptoms: When a BYE is received, the media flows for a different call might be closed in error.
bugs.conditions: If the hash of the call-id (masked to 12 bits) matches the hash of another's call-id.
bugs.impact: The media flows for both calls will be closed when one receives a BYE command. A call may be incorrectly terminated early.
bugs.fix: Entire call-id checked before terminating media flows.

bugs.title: HTTP Persistence cookies erroneously sent when cookie persistence turned off
bugs.symptoms: Traffic may appear to not be load balancing among a pool correctly. Because clients are receiving persistence cookies when they should not be, a client can be routed back to the same pool member for subsequent requests when this is not necessary, instead of being assigned a pool member through load balancing.
bugs.conditions: To encounter this bug, two conditions must be met 1) - The always_send option must be on with HTTP persistence cookies or - Cookies are configured with an expiry 2) Later, persistence is change to 'persist none' (by an iRule, for example).
bugs.impact: The system erroneously sends persistence cookies with responses. Undesired routing might occur, where a client is not load balanced, and instead is always directed back to the same pool member.
bugs.workaround: Turn off the always-send option, and disable the HTTP persistence cookie expiry. If you need the expiry function, use an iRule to re-add it after the cookie has been inserted.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Installation on MOS shell throws 'getenforce command not found' error
bugs.symptoms: When the local installation of the BIG-IP image via MOS is attempted, you may observe the error below. error: tm_install::TMOS::TMOS_getenforce -- Command not found: /usr/sbin/getenforce
bugs.conditions: -- When installing the BIG-IP image via the MOS shell
bugs.impact: -- Installation will be a success but you may observe the getenforce command not found error which is benign.
bugs.fix: Added the getenforce command for the MOS shell

bugs.title: In-TMM monitor agent log message enhancement
bugs.symptoms: Log message TMALOG_PROBE_SEND_FAIL reports only the TMM and MID of the monitoring activity, but gives no information on the monitor configuration to help track down the monitor that is failing. At the default TMA log level there is no way to correlate that with the monitor configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- In-TMM monitoring is enabled (the db variable bigd.tmm is set to 'enable'). -- A monitor of a protocol for which in-TMM monitoring is supported is active.
bugs.impact: Difficult to determine which configured monitor is failing to send probes.
bugs.fix: Log message TMALOG_PROBE_SEND_FAIL reports the monitor name from the BIG-IP configuration in addition to the MID. Log message TMALOG_ACTY_CREATE reports the MID in addition to the monitor name and other information. TMALOG_ACTY_DELETE reports the MID in addition to the monitor name. At log levels 'notice' and above the MID can be used along with the information from TMALOG_ACTY_CREATE to correlate other TMALOG messages by the reported TMM and MID.

bugs.title: DNS cache resolver may return a malformed truncated response with multiple OPT records
bugs.symptoms: A configured DNS resolving cache returns a response with two OPT records when the response is truncated and not in the cache.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when: -- A DNS resolving cache is configured. -- The DNS query being handled is not already cached. -- The response for the query must be truncated because it is larger than the size the client can handle (either 512 bytes or the buffer size indicated by an OPT record in the query).
bugs.impact: A DNS message with multiple OPT records is considered malformed and will likely be dropped by the client.
bugs.workaround: A second query will return the cached record, which will only have one OPT record.
bugs.fix: DNS cache resolver now returns the correct response under these conditions.

bugs.title: Install All Updates button is active when it should not be
bugs.symptoms: The Install All Updates button is active when there are updates only for non-licensed/non-provisioned sections.
bugs.conditions: -- Viewing the Live Updates page. -- There is an update in the non-licensed/non-provisioned section, and nowhere else.
bugs.impact: The Install All Updates button is active and can be clicked, but nothing happens and there are no warnings.

bugs.title: HTTPS monitor sends different number of cipher suites in client hello after config load and bigd restart
bugs.symptoms: HTTPS monitor sends different amount of cipher suites in client hello during SSL handshake and sometimes back end server fails to find a desired cipher suite from client hello. As a result, sometimes SSL handshake fails and monitor wrongly marks pool member down.
bugs.conditions: -- Have an SSL profile to be used by an HTTPS monitor. -- Load the same config more than once.
bugs.impact: HTTPS monitor might incorrectly mark pool member down because of a failed SSL handshake.
bugs.workaround: Restart bigd using the following command: bigstart restart bigd
bugs.fix: HTTPS monitor now sends a consistent number of cipher suites in the client hello message during the SSL handshake.

bugs.title: MOS_Image2Disk_Installation- kjournald service error
bugs.symptoms: Attempted local installation of BIG_IP software image via MOS. During installation, there is a procedure error: tm_install::TMOS::TMOS_getenforce -- Command not found: /usr/sbin/getenforce. Installation is successful, even with this error.
bugs.conditions: Attempted installation of a copied .iso image: image2disk --nosaveconfig --instslot=MD1.2 BIGIP-15.0.0-0.0.1248.iso
bugs.impact: When the installation of packages starts, the system reports the message. Installation completes successfully. There is no functional impact on the system, so you can safely ignore this message.
bugs.fix: The 'Command not found: /usr/sbin/getenforce' error no longer occurs.

bugs.title: GTPv2 Serving-Network field with mixed MNC digits
bugs.symptoms: iRules command 'GTP::ie get value' incorrectly decodes Serving-Network field, putting the least significant digit of mobile network codes (MNC) value before the other two.
bugs.conditions: Using the iRule command 'GTP::ie get value' to retrieve the Serving-Network field from a GTP message (the iRule construction: GTP::ie get value -message $gtp_message 83).
bugs.impact: The operation returns results in which the least significant digit is inserted before the other two, resulting in incorrect data being returned.
bugs.fix: The iRule command 'GTP::ie get -message $gtp_message 83' that retrieves the Serving-Network now returns the correctly ordered, three-digit values for mobile country codes (MCC) and mobile network codes (MNC) as a two-element list: {{<MCC> <MNC>} <optional data>}, where the first element is another list containing actual MCC and MNC values, while the second element is optional binary data which follows MCC and MNC. It is the same format as used for ULI field decoding.
bugs.behavior: The iRule command 'GTP::ie get -message $gtp_message 83' that retrieves the Serving-Network now returns the correctly ordered, three-digit values for mobile country codes (MCC) and mobile network codes (MNC) as a two-element list: {{<MCC> <MNC>} <optional data>}, where the first element is another list containing actual MCC and MNC values, while the second element is optional binary data which follows MCC and MNC. It is the same format as used for ULI field decoding.

bugs.title: After upgrade to 13.1.3.3 or 13.1.3.4, B2250 blades may fail to detect HSB and have restarting chmand
bugs.symptoms: When booting after upgrade, BIG-IP system software may not fully start up, preventing normal service -- In early boot messages in /var/log/ltm: + warning chmand[xxxxx]: 012a0004:4: No FPGA HSB LBB PCI device found. + emerg chmand[xxxxx]: 012a0000:0: Dataplane INOPERABLE - No HSBe2_v2 found on the platform (A112) -- In later ltm logs, chmand may be seen restarting every few seconds with these lines, among others, logged each time it starts: + notice chmand[xxxxx]: 012a0005:5: Starting ChassisManager (chmand). + info chmand[xxxxx]: 012a0006:6: Found platform 'A112' in /PLATFORM. -- The chmand process may create core in /var/core when it restarts.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrade B2250 (A112) blade to software version 13.1.3.3 or 13.1.3.4. -- This issue occurs on affected BIG-IP versions running directly on the indicated hardware platforms, or running as a vCMP host on the indicated hardware platforms.
bugs.impact: No service after upgrade. Note: This might not occur in every configuration. Some multi-blade configurations might encounter this issue where others do not.
bugs.workaround: If possible, roll back to a previous version and contact F5 Support to get an engineering hotfix containing a fix for this issue.
bugs.fix: Upgrading BIG-IP software on B2250 blades completes successfully, when BIG-IP software is running directly on the hardware or is running as a vCMP host. For vCMP deployments, the vCMP host must be running the fixed BIG-IP software in order to resolve this issue.

bugs.title: -s option in qkview help does not indicate maximum size
bugs.symptoms: When running qkview with the -h option to obtain help, the -s (size) option is incorrectly rendered. It should read: [ -s <max file size> range:0-104857600 Bytes ]
bugs.conditions: -- Running qkview -h. -- Viewing the -s (size) option help.
bugs.impact: The measurement size, bytes, is missing, which might result in confusion.
bugs.workaround: Use the -s option as normal, but be advised that the number should be in bytes, and that the maximum number is 104857600.

bugs.title: AFM Policy with Send to Virtual and TMM crash in a specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart in a specific scenario when AFM Policy is configured in multiple contexts (Global, Route Domain, Virtual Server), with Log Translations enabled, and Send-To-VS feature configured in at least one of the rules in the Security Policy.
bugs.conditions: -- When using Firewall ACL Policy in more than one context, i.e., more than one of the following context has ACL Security Policy applied: + Global Context + Route Domain + Virtual Server Context -- Send To Virtual Server is configured on any Rule on the Security policy. -- Traffic matching a Rule (with logging enabled) in more than one context. -- AFM Security Logging Profile has log Translation Field Enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM restart causes service disruption. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable Logging of Translation Fields in Security Logging Profile.
bugs.fix: Invalid memory access when ACL classification is done second time, to support Send to Virtual feature in a specific scenario.

bugs.title: EDNS0 client subnet behavior inconsistent when DNS Caching is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When EDNS0 client subnet information is included in a DNS request, and DNS caching is enabled, the responses differ in their inclusion of EDNS0 client subnet information based on whether the response was supplied by the cache or not.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when EDNS0 client subnet information is included in a DNS request, and DNS caching is enabled.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent behavior.
bugs.fix: In this release, responses are now consistent when caching is enabled.
bugs.workaround: To allow consistent processing of any EDNS0 queries with ECS information, use a DNS profile where DNS caching is disabled by default, and selectively use the DNS cache only for non-EDNS0 queries.

bugs.title: nsm can become unresponsive when processing recursive routes
bugs.symptoms: imish hangs, and the BIG-IP Network Services Module (nsm) daemon consuming 100% CPU.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing enabled -- Processing recursive routes from a BGP peer with different prefixlen values.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing, and services using dynamic routes do not operate. nsm does not recover and must be restarted.
bugs.fix: nsm now processes recursive route without issues.

bugs.title: Possible interruption while processing VPN traffic
bugs.symptoms: When processing certain rare data sequences occurring in VPN traffic, the Traffic Management Microkernel may execute incorrect logic, triggering a TMM restart.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs only with the CGNAT feature provisioned and when at least one virtual server is configured with certain profiles.
bugs.impact: The restart of the TMM disrupts network traffic until either an HA-configured partner TMM assumes processing or the TMM restart has completed.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.
bugs.fix: Improved handling of PPTP messages in PPTP profile.

bugs.title: [BIG-IQ Integration] Deadlock occurs when adding multiple hostnames with transparent enforcement
bugs.symptoms: Transparent enforcement by hostname has been moved from the Host Name configuration to the Microservice configuration. REST API Clients that use the backwards-compatible, old endpoint, and send multiple requests in parallel may encounter a deadlock when configuring this element.
bugs.conditions: 1) REST API Clients configure policy enforcement transparency by hostname. 2) They use the backwards-compatible, old endpoint to do so. 3) Multiple requests are sent in parallel. Note: This is the case for BIG-IQ managing the BIG-IP system and configuring multiple domain names.
bugs.impact: Configuration calls fail due to internal DB deadlocks
bugs.workaround: Retry the API calls (or BIG-IQ deployment)
bugs.fix: Deadlocks during configuration calls are retried automatically and do not interrupt deployments.

bugs.title: SP Connector config changes causes BIG-IP tmm core sometimes during handling of SAML SLO request
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when BIG-IP handles SAML SLO requests, and SP Configuration is changed by the admin around the same time.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: When SP configuration is changed by the admin, and when BIG-IP handles SLO requests correctly without any BIG-IP tmm core.

bugs.title: ASM REST may consume excessive resources
bugs.symptoms: While processing ASM REST calls from authorized users ASM may consume excessive resources.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned and licensed REST calls from an authorized user
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: ASM REST now consumes resources as expected.

bugs.title: Moderate: net-snmp security update
bugs.symptoms: SNMP crashes due to a specially crafted UDP packet by an authenticated user, resulting in Denial of Service.
bugs.conditions: SNMP traffic enabled
bugs.impact: SNMP crashes resulting in a denial of service.
bugs.fix: Patched net-snmp to properly validate input data.

bugs.title: DHCP requests are not sent to all DHCP servers in the pool when the BIG-IP system is in DHCP Relay mode
bugs.symptoms: DHCP requests from the client are sent only to the first member in the DHCP server pool.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP system configured as a DHCP Relay. - DHCP server pool contains more than one DHCP server.
bugs.impact: - DHCP server load balancing is not achieved. - If the first DHCP server in the DHCP server pool does not respond or is unreachable, the DHCP client will not be assigned an IP address.

bugs.title: Add support for P-521 curve in the X.509 chain to SSL LTM
bugs.symptoms: SSL is unable to verify certificate signed with EC P-521 key.
bugs.impact: Client/server authentication (X.509 signature verification) will failed when using certificate signed with EC P-521 key.
bugs.workaround: Client/server has to use certificate signed with supported EC curve (P-256/P-384).
bugs.fix: Add P-521 curve support in X.509 chain verification.

bugs.title: DNS FPGA Hardware-accelerated Cache can improperly respond to DNS queries that contain EDNS OPT Records.
bugs.symptoms: FPGA hardware-accelerated DNS Cache can respond improperly to DNS queries that contain EDNS OPT Records. This improper response can take several forms, ranging from not responding with an OPT record, to a query timeout, to a badvers response.
bugs.conditions: -- Using VIPRION B2250 blades. -- This may occur if a client sends a query with an EDNS OPT record that has an unknown version or other values that the Hardware-accelerated Cache does not understand. These errors only occur when matching the query to a hardware cached response. Note: If the response is not in the hardware cache, then the query should be properly handled.
bugs.impact: Hardware-accelerated DNS Cache drops the request. Clients will experience a timeout for that query. This is occurring now because of the changes coming to software from certain DNS software vendors that remove specific workarounds on February 1st, 2019. This is known as DNS Flag Day.

bugs.title: A sub-second timeout for the SSL alert-timeout option may be desirable in certain cases
bugs.symptoms: For certain high-throughput applications running over SSL (for instance, video streaming), it may be desirable for the BIG-IP system to reset both flows as soon as possible once one side has sent a FIN but the peer side is continuing to send data. This situation can be undesirable (as it is wastes bandwidth) given that at this point the BIG-IP system is no longer proxying data but just dropping all remaining ingress packets (as SSL does not support half-closed TCP connections).
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: - A standard virtual server with the client SSL and server SSL profiles in use. - As part of a connection handled by the virtual server, one side sends a FIN midstream to the BIG-IP system. - The peer side ignores the FIN and continues to send data.
bugs.impact: Even if the SSL alert-timeout option was set to its lowest allowed value (1 second), given a large number of connections in this specific state, the wasted bandwidth can reach considerable levels.
bugs.fix: The SSL alert-timeout option now supports the 'Immediate' value, which makes the BIG-IP system reset both flows after 1/1000 second.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing TLS traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when processing client-side certificates in TLS traffic.
bugs.conditions: Client certificate authentication is enabled (client-side SSL).
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes TLS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: iControl REST may fail while processing requests
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, iControl REST may stop processing requests.
bugs.conditions: AVR provisioned. Authenticated REST user.
bugs.impact: iControl REST stops responding.
bugs.fix: iControl REST now processes requests as expected.

bugs.title: Need generic name for upgraded HTTPS monitor configured with SSL options
bugs.symptoms: When you upgrade a BIG-IP system to BIG-IP 13.1.0 or later and roll forward a configuration that contains an HTTPS monitor configured with SSL options, the configured SSL options are converted and saved in a new custom Server SSL profile named <HTTPS_monitor_name>_ssl_profile. Additionally, the new HTTPS monitor is configured to use the new custom Server SSL profile. For example, if the previous, earlier BIG-IP version has an HTTPS monitor named example_https_monitor, the configuration has a new Server SSL profile named example_https_monitor_ssl_profile. This new Server SSL profile is visible with any other configured Server SSL profiles by navigating in the Configuration utility to Local Traffic :: Profiles :: SSL :: Server.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade a BIG-IP system to BIG-IP 13.1.0 or later and roll forward a configuration that contains an HTTPS monitor configured with SSL options.
bugs.impact: All HTTPS monitors now use the same SSL profile created during the upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Recreate the monitors and specify the name you want.

bugs.title: HTTPS monitor does not appear to be using cert from server-ssl profile
bugs.symptoms: An HTTPS monitor using a client certificate configured in the server-ssl profile fails to send the certificate during the SSL handshake. A tcpdump shows a 0-byte certificate being sent.
bugs.conditions: -- In-tmm monitoring is disabled (default). -- The server-ssl profile has been modified but without changing the configured certificate or key. The resulting message passed from mcpd to bigd will contain only the incremental modification to the profile, which bigd treats as a complete profile, meaning that it is possible for the certificate and key parameters to be lost.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake might fail to complete and the HTTPS monitor fails.
bugs.workaround: Restart bigd process by running the following command: bigstart restart bigd
bugs.fix: mcpd now sends the full profile configuration to bigd upon modification.

bugs.title: Config sync status is always "Changes Pending"
bugs.symptoms: You see constant or nearly constant "Changes Pending" config sync status for a sync group
bugs.conditions: ASM configured in a sync group with manual sync. Session Tracking is configured, and is configured to Block All Thresholds.
bugs.impact: Config sync status of the sync group is almost always at "Changes Pending".
bugs.fix: If you attempt to enable Block All Thresholds, the GUI will report a warning: Manual Sync Group is configured for this device. Enabling any of the Block All Thresholds may result in constant "Changes Pending" state for the group

bugs.title: Manual Device Group Put in Pending State With No Indication
bugs.symptoms: When Session Tracking is enabled on devices in a Manual Sync ASM-enabled device group, the device group can be put into 'Pending' state with no indication as to what changed in the system. This is because Audit Log Messages are not written for changes due to Session Tracking.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM Sync is enabled on a Manual Sync Device Group. -- Session Tracking is enabled on an ASM Security Policy.
bugs.impact: It is unclear why the device group is in Pending State and what the impact is if the configuration is pushed to a peer.
bugs.fix: When in a high availability (HA) environment, changes to Session Tracking are now written to the Audit log as batched events, similar to the following example: x Sessions were set to 'Block All'

bugs.title: Split View pages: if user-defined filter removed right after creation - all user-defined filters are deleted
bugs.symptoms: In any Split View page (Request Log, Learning, etc.): All user-defined filters are removed if you delete a newly created filter without reloading the page first.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a new filter. -- Remove the new filter.
bugs.impact: The system removes all user-defined filters.
bugs.workaround: Before you delete a newly created filter, reload the page.
bugs.fix: Filter removal now completes successfully for all scenarios.

bugs.title: When parameters with special characters are obfuscated they are not url-encoded
bugs.symptoms: Applying obfuscation on parameters with special characters, like "$", are not URL-encoded. Hence, they are delivered incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: Obfuscated parameter includes special characters
bugs.impact: These paramters are sent incorrectly (not URL-encoded)
bugs.fix: Code fixed to resolve this issue

bugs.title: UTF-8 character in subject of a certificate used for iQuery cannot be removed
bugs.symptoms: If certificate subject which is added to 'Trusted Device Certificates' or 'Trusted Server Certificates' contains UTF-8 characters, it cannot be removed via GUI or edited via TMSH. When removing such a certificate GUI posts the following error: Key management library returned bad status: -2, Not Found.
bugs.conditions: -- Using a certificate with UTF-8 character in its subject. -- The cert is in 'Trusted Device Certificates' or 'Trusted Server Certificates'. -- Try to remove this certificate.
bugs.impact: Certificates from 'Trusted Device Certificates' or 'Trusted Server Certificates' are not editable via TMSH. The only way of removing them is to edit /config/big3d/client.crt or /config/gtm/server.crt
bugs.workaround: Edit /config/big3d/client.crt or /config/gtm/server.crt to remove the certificates containing the UTF-8 character in subject of a certificate.

bugs.title: Persistence record is deleted in MRF SIP after updating timeout value with the iRule 'SIP::persist timeout'
bugs.symptoms: MRF SIP persistence records are deleted after updating the timeout value with the iRule 'SIP::persist timeout'.
bugs.conditions: -- MRF SIP configured with a persistence mode enabled. -- Persistence timeout value is modified with iRule 'SIP::persist timeout'.
bugs.impact: Connections are not persisted as expected, causing additional processing, load balancing, and potential for misrouted messages.
bugs.workaround: Do not use 'SIP::persist timeout' to update timeouts. Increase initial timeout values when using custom persistence mode or switch to a non-custom persistence mode that updates timeouts automatically without iRules.
bugs.fix: The iRule 'SIP::persist timeout' no longer causes the persistence record to be deleted when updating the timeout value.

bugs.title: GUI VLAN list page loading slowly with 50 records per screen
bugs.symptoms: GUI VLAN list page is loading slowly with there are 3200+ VLANs with the Records Per Screen Preference set to 50.
bugs.conditions: -- Using a VIPRION system. -- Configuration containing 3200 or more VLANs. -- System Preferences Records Per Screen set to 50.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the page.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh or guishell tool to see the VLANs. You can also try using a smaller value for the Records Per Screen option in System :: Preferences.
bugs.fix: Improved data retrieval and rendering for the VLAN list page.

bugs.title: Certain BIG-IP DNS configurations improperly respond to DNS queries that contain EDNS OPT Records
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express does not always include an EDNS OPT Record in responses to queries that contain an EDNS OPT Record.
bugs.conditions: Queries to DNS Express containing an ENDS0 record it does not understand.
bugs.impact: DNS Express responses might not contain the RFC-required ENDS0 record. Some compliance tools and upstream DNS servers may consider the BIG-IP non-compliant, and report it as such. This is occurring now because of the changes coming that remove certain workarounds on February 1st, 2019. This is known as DNS Flag Day. All network configurations on the internet will be affected by this change, but only some DNS servers will be negatively impacted. Fixes for this issue handle the conditions that were once handled by those workarounds.
bugs.fix: Corrected EDNS OPT record handling in DNS Express. Note: The EDNS Compliance Tester should produce output similar to the following when run against DNS Express: example1.com. @10.10.10.125 (ns.example1.com.): dns=ok edns=ok edns1=ok edns@512=ok ednsopt=ok edns1opt=ok do=ok ednsflags=ok optlist=ok signed=ok ednstcp=ok

bugs.title: Subscriber management configuration GUI
bugs.symptoms: Subscriber management configuration GUI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.conditions: PEM provisioned Authenticated user accesses Subscriber Management->Activity Log->Log Configuration page.
bugs.impact: Subscriber management configuration GUI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.fix: Subscriber management configuration GUI now follows best security practices.

bugs.title: Certain BIG-IP DNS configurations improperly respond to DNS queries that contain EDNS OPT Records
bugs.symptoms: DNS Express drops a DNS query that contains an EDNS OPT Record that it does not understand.
bugs.conditions: If a client (such as a DNS Flag Day compliance tool) or upstream DNS Server sends an invalid ENDS OPT record.
bugs.impact: DNS Express drops the request. Clients (such as a DNS Flag Day compliance tool) or upstream DNS server will experience a timeout for that query. This is occurring now because of the changes coming that remove certain workarounds on February 1st, 2019. This is known as DNS Flag Day. All network configurations on the internet will be affected by this change, but only some DNS servers will be negatively impacted. Fixes for this issue handle the conditions that were once handled by those workarounds.
bugs.fix: When a query with an invalid EDNS OPT version is received by DNS Express, send a response with the BADVERS error code as stipulated by the RFC. Note: The EDNS Compliance Tester should produce output similar to the following when run against DNS Express: example1.com. @10.10.10.125 (ns.example1.com.): dns=ok edns=ok edns1=ok edns@512=ok ednsopt=ok edns1opt=ok do=ok ednsflags=ok optlist=ok signed=ok ednstcp=ok

bugs.title: VA status change while 'disabled' are not taken into account after being 'enabled' again
bugs.symptoms: The virtual-address network is not advertised with route-advertisement enabled.
bugs.conditions: 1. Using a virtual-address with route advertisement enabled. 2. Disable virtual-address while state is down. 3. Enable virtual-address after state comes up.
bugs.impact: No route-advertisement of the virtual-address.
bugs.workaround: Toggle the route-advertisement for virtual-address.
bugs.fix: The virtual-address now operations as expected when disabled.

bugs.title: LTM NAT does not forward ICMP traffic
bugs.symptoms: ICMP traffic that matches LTM NAT object on a BIG-IP system, is not forwarded through but instead is dropped on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM NAT object is configured on the BIG-IP system. -- The BIG-IP system receives ICMP traffic matching the LTM NAT object.
bugs.impact: Client ICMP traffic (matching LTM NAT) is not forwarded to the destination causing traffic disruption.
bugs.fix: ICMP traffic matching an LTM NAT object is now forwarded to the destination as expected.

bugs.title: Certain BIG-IP DNS configurations improperly respond to DNS queries that contain EDNS OPT Records
bugs.symptoms: DNS Cache drops a DNS query that contains an EDNS OPT Record that it does not understand.
bugs.conditions: If a client (such as a DNS Flag Day compliance tool) or upstream DNS Server sends an invalid ENDS OPT record.
bugs.impact: DNS Cache drops the request. Clients (such as a DNS Flag Day compliance tool) or upstream DNS server will experience a timeout for that query. This is occurring now because of the changes coming that remove certain workarounds on February 1st, 2019. This is known as DNS Flag Day. All network configurations on the internet will be affected by this change, but only some DNS servers will be negatively impacted. Fixes for this issue handle the conditions that were once handled by those workarounds.
bugs.fix: When a query with an invalid EDNS OPT version is received by DNS Cache, the system now sends a response with the BADVERS error code, as stipulated by the RFC. Note: Any NOSOA and NOAA results from the EDNS Compliance Tester used for DNS Flag Day are false positives and are expected when testing against DNS Cache. The EDNS Compliance Tester assumes an authoritative server, and makes non-recursive queries. For example, you might see a Resolver response similar to the following: example1.com. @10.10.10.126 (ns.example1.com.): dns=nosoa,noaa edns=nosoa,noaa edns1=ok edns@512=noaa ednsopt=nosoa,noaa edns1opt=ok do=nosoa,noaa ednsflags=nosoa,noaa optlist=nosoa,noaa,subnet signed=nosoa,noaa,yes ednstcp=noaa These types of responses are expected when running the validation tool against DNS Cache.

bugs.title: Certain BIG-IP DNS configurations improperly respond to DNS queries that contain EDNS OPT Records
bugs.symptoms: DNS Cache does not always include an EDNS OPT Record in responses to queries that contain an EDNS OPT Record.
bugs.conditions: Responses to queries with EDNS0 record to DNS Cache do not contain the RFC-required EDNS0 record.
bugs.impact: Some compliance tools and upstream DNS servers may consider the BIG-IP non-compliant, and report it as such. This is occurring now because of the changes coming that remove certain workarounds on February 1st, 2019. This is known as DNS Flag Day. All network configurations on the internet will be affected by this change, but only some DNS servers will be negatively impacted. Fixes for this issue handle the conditions that were once handled by those workarounds.
bugs.fix: Corrected EDNS OPT record handling in DNS Cache. Note: Any NOSOA and NOAA results from the EDNS Compliance Tester used for DNS Flag Day are false positives and are expected when testing against DNS Cache. The EDNS Compliance Tester assumes an authoritative server, and makes non-recursive queries. For example, you might see a Resolver response similar to the following: example1.com. @10.10.10.126 (ns.example1.com.): dns=nosoa,noaa edns=nosoa,noaa edns1=ok edns@512=noaa ednsopt=nosoa,noaa edns1opt=ok do=nosoa,noaa ednsflags=nosoa,noaa optlist=nosoa,noaa,subnet signed=nosoa,noaa,yes ednstcp=noaa These types of responses are expected when running the validation tool against DNS Cache.

bugs.title: PEM content insertion action may insert more than once with Once-Every method
bugs.symptoms: PEM content insertion action data is being reset even if there is no PEM policy update.
bugs.conditions: During re-evaluation to update the existing flow.
bugs.impact: More than expected Insert content action with Once-Every method of insert content action.

bugs.title: PEM Once-Every content insertion action may insert more than once during an interval
bugs.symptoms: Successful PEM content insertion accounting is lost during re-evaluation, resulting in more insertions per insertion interval.
bugs.conditions: During re-evaluation to update the existing flow.
bugs.impact: More than expected Insert content action with Once-Every method of insert content action
bugs.fix: Update the insertion content accounting data during re-evaluation.

bugs.title: TMM crashes on traffic passthrough when SSO Config object is deleted while being used in SSO Configuration Select Agent in PRP
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on traffic passthrough when SSO Config object is deleted while being used in SSO Configuration Select Agent in PRP.
bugs.conditions: Create a basic SSO item. Create a PRP that has the SSO Assign in it and select the basic SSO item. Create a PSP that is Start->Allow Create a VS that uses the PRP, PSP, and an pool. Delete the SSO item in the UI. Run traffic through the VS
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not delete the SSO config object referenced by SSO Configuration Select agent in PRP.
bugs.fix: SSO Configuration Select agent should fail with error code when sso_config cannot be found (i.e. NULL).

bugs.title: MCP validation to prevent sso config object deletion when referenced by SSO Configuration Select agent in PRP
bugs.symptoms: SSO config object can be deleted even when it is referenced by SSO configuration select agent in PRP.
bugs.conditions: Create a basic SSO item. Create a PRP that has the SSO Assign in it and select the basic SSO item. Create a PSP that is Start->Allow Create a VS that uses the PRP, PSP, and an pool. Delete the SSO item in the UI.
bugs.impact: Traffic flow for SSO configuration select agent fails since the sso config object is deleted.
bugs.fix: MCP validation needs to be added in sso config object deletion validation. When an sso object is deleted, we need to make sure it is not referenced by V2 policy agent.

bugs.title: Installation using image2disk --format may fail after TMOS v14.1.0 is installed
bugs.symptoms: When v14.1.0 is installed, subsequent installations of software performed using image2disk with the --format=volumes option from within a TMOS installation slot. The failure occurs after the disks have been formatted, but before the TMOS installation slot is bootable, and the system is left without a TMOS installation slot. While performing the installation, the system posts messages similar to the following in the serial console: -- info: tm_install::RPM::rpm_db_find_by_namearch -- not found : MySQL-shared/i686 ... -- info: tm_install::VolumeSet::VolumeSet_install_packages -- installing package MySQL-shared (i686) -- info: tm_install::RPM::rpm_db_find_by_namearch -- not found : openssl/x86_64 ... -- info: tm_install::VolumeSet::VolumeSet_install_packages -- installing package openssl (x86_64) -- info: capture: status 32512 returned by command: chroot /mnt/tm_install/1258.DHwcwN rpm --rebuilddb ... -- info: chroot: failed to run command 'rpm': No such file or directory
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- Version 14.1.0 is installed on the system, even if the system never boots into the 14.1.0 installation slot. -- Using image2disk with the --format=volumes option specified from TMOS. -- Installing another version of the software. In particular, this issue affects MOS version 2.12.0-140.0, which can be checked by running this command from a bash shell on the BIG-IP system: grub_default -d | grep -A6 'TMOS maintenance' | grep 'TIC_STATIC_VERSION'
bugs.impact: The installation fails, and the system is left in a state where it is not accessible on the network and has no configuration. You must use the console to access the system.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following workarounds: -- Use the Software Management screens in the GUI to perform installations -- Use the tmsh 'sys software' commands to perform software installations. -- Do not use the image2disk --format command to install software.

bugs.title: HSL may incorrectly handle pending TCP connections with elongated handshake time.
bugs.symptoms: HSL may incorrectly handle TCP connections that are pending 3-way handshake completion that exceed default handshake timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- HSL or ReqLog configured to send logging data to pool via TCP protocol. -- TCP 3-way handshake takes longer than 20 seconds (the default handshake timeout) to complete.
bugs.impact: -- Service interruption while TMM restarts. -- Failover event.
bugs.fix: HSL handles unusually long pending TCP handshakes gracefully and does not cause outage.

bugs.title: While loading large configurations on BIG-IP systems, some daemons may core intermittently.
bugs.symptoms: When manually copying a large config file and running 'tmsh load sys config' on specific hardware BIG-IP platforms, multiple cores may be observed from different daemons.
bugs.conditions: This has been observed on i4800 platforms when the 'management' provisioning (corresponding to the provision.extramb DB key) is set to 500 MB or less.
bugs.impact: The mcp daemon may core and all daemons on the BIG-IP system may be restarted.
bugs.workaround: Set db key 'provision.extramb' to 1024 or greater.

bugs.title: There may be a latency between session termination and deletion of its associated IP address mapping
bugs.symptoms: In SWG, if a new request from a client executes iRule command "ACCESS::session exists" when the session has expired previously, the command will return false. However, if command "ACCESS::session create" is executed following the exist command, the session ID of the previous session may be returned.
bugs.conditions: In SWG, if a new request from a client IP comes into the system right after its previous session has expired.
bugs.impact: The Access filter will determine that the session ID is stale and, therefore, will redirect the client to /my.policy

bugs.title: TMM cores with SIGFPE after NAT object modification, posting error" panic: ../base/listener.c:1292: Assertion 'bound listener' failed
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores with SIGFPE after NAT object modification, posting error" panic: ../base/listener.c:1292: Assertion 'bound listener' failed
bugs.conditions: Create and then delete and recreate NAT objects in a single transaction.
bugs.impact: Causes TMM to restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Perform the delete operation and the create operation in separate transactions. TMM does not fail when the delete and create (with swapped originating-address) operations are done in separate transactions.

bugs.title: Windows Logon Integration does not work
bugs.symptoms: Windows Logon Integration, the network logon using dial-up connection failed with error message and VPN could not be established: Connecting - Error 1471: Unable to finish the requested operation because the specified process is not a GUI process.
bugs.conditions: Windows Logon Integration is used for dial-up / establish VPN.
bugs.impact: APM end user cannot establish a VPN tunnel via Windows Logon Integration.
bugs.fix: The system now handles Windows Logon Integration as expected, so APM end users can establish a VPN tunnel.

bugs.title: URI translation rules defined in Rewrite profile with type 'uri-translation' are not applied.
bugs.symptoms: A regression in configuration processing causes LTM Rewrite profile to ignore configured URI translation rules.
bugs.conditions: Using LTM Rewrite profiles to ignore configured URI translation rules.
bugs.impact: URI translation rules defined in Rewrite profile with type 'uri-translation' are not applied.
bugs.fix: Restored functionality of LTM Rewrite URI translation rules.

bugs.title: Impossible to create Bot Signature/Bot Category Signature in user partition different from 'Common'
bugs.symptoms: For any partition other than 'Common'(i.e., a user-defined partition), cannot create a new Bot Signature or Bot Category Signature via GUI, because the form fields and buttons are disabled (grayed out).
bugs.conditions: -- Creating Bot Signature/Bot Category Signature. -- The partition is set to a user-defined partition.
bugs.impact: No creation of Bot Signature/Bot Category Signature can be completed through GUI in a user-defined partition.

bugs.title: Impossible to remove Bot profiles, Logging profiles, and Cloud Security Service profiles from a user-defined partition
bugs.symptoms: Removing Bot/Logging/Security Service profiles that were created in a user-defined partition fails via GUI.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to delete Bot/Logging/Security Service profiles that were created in a user-defined partition.
bugs.impact: The Bot/Logging/Security Service Profile cannot be deleted via GUI.
bugs.workaround: Remove Bot/Logging/Cloud Security Service profiles via TMSH.
bugs.fix: You can now remove Bot profiles, Logging profiles, and Cloud Security Service profiles from user-defined partition.

bugs.title: Tmm crash on standby device and Diameter stats issues
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes on the standby device. Prior to the crash, Diameter stats are not updating on the standby device.
bugs.conditions: Diameter is configured in a high availability (HA) environment.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Stats on standby device are now updated properly, and tmm does not crash.

bugs.title: Trying to remove a user-created 'Bot Signature' on IE11 fails
bugs.symptoms: Trying to remove a user-created 'Bot Signature' on Microsoft Internet Explorer v11 (IE11) fails with the following message: To continue, please select one or more items from the list!
bugs.conditions: -- Using IE11. -- Attempting to remove a user-created 'Bot Signature'.
bugs.impact: The operation fails.
bugs.workaround: Use Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox browsers.

bugs.title: REST Backwards Compatibility: Cannot modify enforcementMode of host-name
bugs.symptoms: Modifying the enforcementMode value fails with the following message: Valid Host Name already exists in this policy. In 14.1.0, the capability to treat specific domains as Transparent while the rest of the policy is in Blocking moved from Host Names to the new Microservices feature. The REST endpoint for Host Names (/mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/host-names) is meant to still support setting and modifying this attribute. However, this is not happening successfully.
bugs.conditions: -- Running version 14.1.0 software. -- Using a pre-14.1.0 REST API to modify the enforcementMode of a host name (/mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/host-names).
bugs.impact: The value change fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use either workaround: -- Change the value using the GUI. -- Use the newer endpoint: (/mgmt/tm/asm/policies/<ID>/microservices).
bugs.fix: Using the backwards compatible REST to update the enforcementMode of a host name now succeeds.

bugs.title: ASE user cannot create or modify a bot signature.
bugs.symptoms: Application Security Editor user role gets a validation exception while trying to create or modify bot defense signature either via GUI, tmsh, or REST.
bugs.conditions: The logged on user account is configured with an Application Security Editor role.

bugs.workaround: Change user role to Administrator or Web Application Security Administrator to create or modify bot defense signatures.

bugs.title: Request Log: Accept Request button available when not needed
bugs.symptoms: There are several violations that make request unlearnable, but the Accept Request Button is still enabled.
bugs.conditions: Request log has requests with following violations that make requests unlearnable: - Threat Campaign detected - Null character found in WebSocket text message - Access from disallowed User/Session/IP/Device ID - Failed to convert character + 2 subviolations of HTTP protocol compliance failed violation: - Unparsable request content - Null in request - Bad HTTP version or only following violations were detected: - Access from malicious IP address - IP is blacklisted - CSRF attack detected - Brute Force: Maximum login attempts are exceeded

bugs.title: TMM crashes while making changes to virtual wire configuration
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when deleting a virtual-wire configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: LTM logs are filled with error messages while creating/deleting virtual wire configuration
bugs.symptoms: LTM logs are filled with error messages when creating/deleting virtual wire config.
bugs.conditions: Virtual wire is created and then deleted.
bugs.impact: Error messages are getting logged to ltm.
bugs.fix: Log messages for virtual wire interfaces are not being seen.

bugs.title: Incorrect bad-actor stats for IGMP fragment flood vector
bugs.symptoms: For incorrect fragments, the bad actor stats for the IGMP fragment flood vector are displayed incorrectly.
bugs.conditions: When a DoS attack is sent for IGMP fragment flood vectors with incorrect fragments.
bugs.impact: Incorrect stats
bugs.fix: With this change, the stats are displayed correctly.

bugs.title: Impossible to remove Bot profiles, Logging profiles, and Cloud Security Service profiles from a user-defined partition
bugs.symptoms: Removing Bot/Logging/Security Service profiles that were created in a user-defined partition fails via GUI.

bugs.title: Potential memory leaks in TMM when Access::policy evaluate command failed to send the request to APMD
bugs.symptoms: Memory usage in TMM keeps going up.
bugs.conditions: Access::policy evaluate command fails with error message in /var/log/ltm: TCL error: ... - Failed to forward request to apmd.

bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances tmm can reorder or omit HTTP data segments when they are received while processing an iRule which is parked.

bugs.title: BD crash when content profile used for login page has no parse parameters set
bugs.symptoms: Bd crashes. No traffic goes through ASM.

bugs.title: Import XML policy error

bugs.title: Generating Qkviews or tcpdumps via GUI or running the 'ihealth' command removes /var/tmp/mcpd.out
bugs.symptoms: After generating a Qkview or collecting a tcpdump via the BIG-IP GUI, or using the 'tmsh run util ihealth' command to do the equivalent, the /var/tmp/mcpd.out file is missing.
bugs.conditions: -- Generating a Qkview or collecting a tcpdump via the BIG-IP GUI. -- Using the 'tmsh run util ihealth' command to do the equivalent operation.
bugs.impact: The file /var/tmp/mpcd.out is a debug file used by mcpd, primarily for collecting debug-level log information from MCPD. The file being deleted causes challenges with trying to collect diagnostic information from a BIG-IP system (turning on mcpd debug logging), because it now requires a service impact (restarting mcpd). Additionally, may cause challenges in managing disk space on /shared filesystem, as mcpd keeps writing to a deleted file, and it cannot be truncated.
bugs.workaround: Generating Qkviews by invoking the 'qkview' command directly avoids this issue. Edit the /usr/bin/ihealth.sh script to remove the corresponding line. From a bash shell: 1. mount -o remount,rw /usr 2. /bin/cp /usr/bin/ihealth.sh{,751009.bak} 3. sed -i '/\/bin\/rm -f \/var\/tmp\/mcpd.out/d' /usr/bin/ihealth.sh 4. mount -o remount,ro /usr Note: This workaround does not persist across software installs/upgrades, nor does it ConfigSync or replicate across blades in a VIPRION chassis.
bugs.fix: The problem line has been removed from the script, so this mcpd debug file is left alone (not deleted) after running ihealth.sh. Note that the GUI version of running qkview uses ihealth.sh script.

bugs.title: ihealth.sh script and qkview locking mechanism not working
bugs.symptoms: Two qkviews can be started up on a system at the same time, which results in conflicts for each.
bugs.conditions: Running qkview on one terminal and then ihealth.sh in another.
bugs.impact: Running of two qkviews at the same time breaks both qkviews since they compete for the same files.
bugs.workaround: Run either qkview or ihealth.sh, not both simultaneously.
bugs.fix: Starting a qkview and then running ihealth.sh halts immediately as the system detects that qkview is running.

bugs.title: One or more TMM instances may be left without dynamic routes.
bugs.symptoms: Inspecting the BIG-IP's routing table (for instance, using tmsh or ZebOS commands) shows that dynamic routes have been learnt correctly and should be in effect. However, while passing traffic through the system, you experience intermittent failures. Further investigation reveals that the failures are limited to one or more TMM instances (all other TMM instances are processing traffic correctly). The situation does not self-recover and the system remains in this state indefinitely. An example of a traffic failure can be a client connection reset with cause 'No route to host'. If the client retries the same request, and this hits a different TMM instance, the request might succeed.
bugs.conditions: This issue is known to occur when all of the following conditions are met: - The system is a multi-blade VIPRION or vCMP cluster. - The system just underwent an event such as a software upgrade, a reboot of one or more blades, a restart of the services on one or more blades, etc.
bugs.impact: Traffic fails intermittently, with errors that point to lack of routes to certain destinations.
bugs.workaround: You can try to temporarily resolve the issue by restarting the tmrouted daemon on all blades. To do so, run the following command: # clsh "bigstart restart tmrouted" However, there is no strict guarantee this will resolve the issue, given the nature of the issue. Alternatively, you could temporarily replace the dynamic routes with static routes.
bugs.fix: All TMM instances across all blades now properly learn dynamic routes.

bugs.title: i5000/i7000/i10000 platforms: SFP/QSFP I2C problems may not be cleared by bcm56xxd
bugs.symptoms: Messages similar to the following appear in /var/log/ltm: info bcm56xxd: 012c0012:6: I2C muxes are not cleared. Problem with mux 224:
bugs.conditions: -- i5000/i7000/i10000 platforms. -- May be caused by a defective optic, rebooting/upgrading BIG-IP, removing and reinserting optics.
bugs.impact: Changes in optic state may be ignored while I2C bus is unavailable.
bugs.workaround: For each SFP, perform the following procedure: 1. Unplug the optic. 2. Wait 10 seconds. 3. Plug optic back in. Note: This message might be caused by a defective optic. If error messages stop when one optic is removed, and error messages resume when the optic is inserted, replace that optic.
bugs.fix: The I2C bus on i5000/i7000/i10000 platforms now resets the Mux controlling the I2C bus connected to the front panel optics.

bugs.title: TCP receive window may open too slowly after zero-window
bugs.symptoms: After a zero-window, TCP reopens its receive window with init-rwnd * mss bytes if sys db tm.tcpinitwinafterxon is enabled and grows it as data is received. For a TCP connection with a large receive window, reaching the receive window limit might take some RTTs due to init-rwnd is limited to 64.
bugs.conditions: -- A TCP profile with large receive window size. -- A zero-window is sent. -- TCP receive window is reopened when data is drained.
bugs.impact: TCP does not have the functionality to reopen it's receive window more aggressively if needed which might result in longer transfer times.
bugs.fix: A new sys db (tm.tcpinitwinmultiplierafterxon) is introduced to provide TCP the functionality to reopen it's receive window more aggressively after zero-window.
bugs.behavior: A new sys db (tm.tcpinitwinmultiplierafterxon) has been introduced to provide TCP the functionality to reopen it's receive window more aggressively after zero-window. It has a default minimum value of 1 and can be increased to a maximum of 100.

bugs.title: Virtual server status stays unavailable even after all the over-the-rate-limit connections are gone
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server status becomes unavailable when the connections are over the rate limit, and stays unavailable when the number of connections fall below the limit.
bugs.conditions: -- The connections are over the rate limit, making the virtual server status unavailable. -- The number of connections fall below the limit.
bugs.impact: Virtual server status reports unavailable, even though it should be available.
bugs.workaround: This problem does not impact virtual server processing traffic. It simply reports the wrong status.

bugs.title: HTTP iRule event HTTP_REJECT broken
bugs.symptoms: When an action causes an HTTP_REJECT event to be triggered, the content isn't executed, and BIG-IP logs an error log message that the event aborted: info tmm[16852]: 01220009:6: Pending rule (null) <HTTP_REJECT> aborted
bugs.conditions: Any actions that cause an HTTP_REJECT event to be triggered.
bugs.impact: iRule content is not executed and the iRule action is aborted.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the HTTP_REJECT event

bugs.title: Ability to search the active access sessions by virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: There is no ability to search access session by virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: Find/search of active sessions per virtual server
bugs.impact: Cannot complete the operation.
bugs.fix: This release supports the searching active access sessions by virtual servers.

bugs.title: TMSH: 'tmsh save sys config' prompts question when display threshold is configured which is causing scripts to stop
bugs.symptoms: Issuing the command 'tmsh save sys config' results in a question when display threshold is set and when management routes are configured. There is no prompt when no management routes are configured. This question is posted only when management-routes are configured, and does not appear when other provisioning commands are issued and the config is saved.
bugs.conditions: 1. Set the cli preference display-threshold to a smaller value than the default. 2. Create management routes. 3. Issue the following command: tmsh save sys config
bugs.impact: When there are more items configured than the threshold, the system presents a question: Display all <number> items? (y/n) Scripts are stopped until the prompt is answered.
bugs.workaround: To prevent the question from popping up, set display threshold to 0 (zero). In the case of this script, you can also delete the management route definitions to prevent the question from being asked.

bugs.title: DNS or Network protocol DoS attacks reported as mitigating when configured as monitoring
bugs.symptoms: The DoS visibility screens (Monitoring :: Security :: Reporting : DoS) may display DNS and Network protocol DoS attacks with the incorrect mitigation details.
bugs.conditions: An attacked object assigned to a DoS profile with either DNS or Network security protocols that are configured to have detect-only or learn-only states for DoS attacks.
bugs.impact: Network or DNS DoS attacks, detected by a DoS profile with detect-only or learn-only protection, display mitigation as Blocking instead of the configured Transparent protection. This does not affect the reported traffic data found in the DoS visibility dimensions and charts.

bugs.title: MRF: Race condition may create to many outgoing connections to a peer
bugs.symptoms: If two different connections attempt to create an outgoing connection to a peer at the same time, multiple connections may be created, even if the peer object is configured for one connection per peer. This is due to a race condition in message routing framework during connection creation.
bugs.conditions: -- Two different connections attempt to create an outgoing connection to a peer at the same time. -- The peer is configured for one connection per peer.
bugs.impact: More than one connection to a peer is created.
bugs.fix: Only one connection is created under these conditions.

bugs.title: LSN pool real-time stats are not persisted over reboot
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting a VIPRION device or blade for which Port Block Allocation (PBA) is done, the PBA allocation is persisted, but the stats are not.
bugs.conditions: Reboot the VIPRION device or a blade
bugs.impact: LSN pool real-time stats are not persisted over reboot. The stats are not consistent with the connection DB.
bugs.workaround: There is no direct workaround, but you can make the stats consistent by deleting the PBA allocation or wait for it to age out of the LSN DB. Subsequent PBA allocations will be reflected correctly in the stats and will be consistent with the LSN DB.

bugs.title: mcpd core after changing parent netflow to use version9
bugs.symptoms: When making changes to netflow profile (changing between v9 and v5), mcpd CPU usage on one core goes high, and a core file is written. The problem occurs only when modifying root netflow profile that is referenced by a child netflow. Modifying the root netflow profile works as expected when it is not being referred to by any child netflow. When the issue occurs, mcpd gets into a loop and hangs there for a long time.
bugs.conditions: The problem occurs only when modifying root netflow profile that is referenced by a child netflow.
bugs.impact: The config changes appear to have been made. However, mcpd processes the config and stops responding. While mcpd restarts, there is no traffic management functionality (e.g., cannot retrieve or update system status, cannot reconfigure system, other daemons are not functional).
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: Invalidation trigger parameter values are limited to 256 bytes
bugs.symptoms: Invalidation trigger parameter values are limited to a internal representation of 256 bytes. The values are escaped for regex matching, so the effective value size from the user perspective can be somewhat smaller than 256 bytes. Oversize values result in invalidation of all content on the target policy node.
bugs.conditions: -- AAM policy with invalidation trigger. -- Invalidation trigger request with parameter value larger than 256 bytes.
bugs.impact: All content on target policy node is invalidated rather than the specific content targeted.
bugs.fix: Invalidation trigger parameter values can now be up to 8K bytes in size.

bugs.title: MCP Validation does not detect when virtual servers differ only by overlapping VLANs
bugs.symptoms: It is possible to configure two virtual servers with the same address, port, and route domain, and have them overlap only in VLANs. MCP does not detect the overlap. Errors like this may be seen in the ltm log: err tmm1[29243]: 01010009:3: Failed to bind to address
bugs.conditions: Two (or more) virtual servers with the same address, port, and route domain, and have them overlap only in VLANs
bugs.impact: Traffic does not get routed properly.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than ensuring that virtual servers that have the same address, port, and route domain have no overlap of VLANs.

bugs.title: HTTP Connect Category Lookup not working properly
bugs.symptoms: 1. HTTP Connect Category Lookup does not return the correct category. 2. HTTP Connect Category Lookup cannot attach the service chain correctly.
bugs.conditions: -- Using SSLO iApp to configure a security policy. -- Choose conditions 'Category Lookup (All)' and '"Category Lookup (HTTP Connect)'.
bugs.impact: Service chain is not correctly triggered based on the SSLO iApp policy selection when HTTP Connect traffic is passed.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: 1. The Access Per-request Policy HTTP Connect Category Lookup agent now returns the correct category ID. 2. Service connector is now inserted correctly, which ensures the correct behavior when dealing with HTTP Connect tunnel traffic.

bugs.title: LTM policy rule condition does not match server-name in ssl-extension
bugs.symptoms: An LTM policy that attempts to match the server name of an SSL extension does not get executed, even though the server name in the client hello packet is a match for the condition.
bugs.conditions: Using an LTM policy that has a rule which has a condition that attempts to match on the server name of the an SSL extension.
bugs.impact: The LTM policy is not executed.
bugs.workaround: An iRule may be used instead.

bugs.title: Unnecessary reporting of errors with complex denial-of-service policies
bugs.symptoms: In the tmm log files, messages are reported: 016e0002:3: Execution of action 'l7dos enable from-profile=/dos-xyzzy' failed, error ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- At least one virtual server configured with a complex L7DoS policy.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system continually logs erroneous errors to /var/log/ltm.
bugs.workaround: Attach another 'bot' profile to the virtual server associated with the error.
bugs.fix: The system no longer prints unnecessary errors

bugs.title: TMM, ZebOS, and Linux routing table may lose dynamic routes on a tmm restart
bugs.symptoms: There are three major routing participants on a BIG-IP system: TMM, ZebOS, and Linux routing tables. Each of them replicates routes between the other. The 'bigstart restart tmm' command restarts tmm, and a part of the restart process is to mark VLAN interfaces DOWN and later UP. Another part the same process is to restart the ZebOS daemons. There is a race condition between these two events, so the following might happen: 1) tmm marks interface named vlan1 as DOWN, and a bit later marks as UP, but not UP and RUNNING. 2) The ZebOS daemons are restarted and ready to update interface status. They request a current status and mark interface UP, not UP and RUNNING. 3) tmm is fully restarted and marks vlan1 UP and RUNNING. 4) The ZebOS daemons reject dynamic routes because interface vlan1 is UP, but not RUNNING.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). - Dynamic routing is configured and there is a decide with some dynamic routes. - You run the 'bigstart restart tmm' command.
bugs.impact: Traffic which relays on dynamic routes is interrupted. Because this is a race condition, it depends on configuration and timing.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmrouted daemon using the following command: bigstart restart tmrouted
bugs.fix: Dynamic routes are not rejected and are successfully inserted into routing tables.

bugs.title: Ability to select both IKEv1 and IKEv2 in ike-peer config deprecated
bugs.symptoms: Multiple values (v1/v2) for the IKE version attribute can lead to inconsistent handling of IPsec tunnel negotiation and can lead to unexpected errors, depending on which peer is the Initiator. Additionally, setting both values has lead to an indeterminate state in the BIG-IP system internal configuration.
bugs.conditions: Both v1 and v2 are selected as the IKE version in the ike-peer configuration object.
bugs.impact: An indeterminate configuration state can exist after changing from both versions to just one.
bugs.workaround: An indeterminate configuration state after changing from both versions to just one can normally be cleared by restarting tmipsecd (bigstart restart tmipsecd) but may require a reboot the BIG-IP system in order to clear the TMM state.
bugs.fix: Ike peer version can take only one value now: -- In the GUI, you can set the version by selecting one option through radio buttons (either v1 or v2). -- In TMSH, You can specify the the version using the 'replace-all-with' option. When trying to set more than one value, an error message is displayed.

bugs.title: When upgrading to v14.0.0 or later, the 'no-tlsv1.3' option is missing from HTTPS monitors automatically created server SSL profiles
bugs.symptoms: If there are HTTPS monitor objects that were created using BIG-IP software v12.x, when the BIG-IP is upgraded directly to v14.0.0 or later, the operation automatically creates server SSL profiles for the HTTPS monitors as needed. Those server SSL profile objects do not have 'no-tlsv1.3' included in their 'options' configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- Having HTTPS monitors configured in v12.x before upgrading. -- Directly upgrading from v12.x to v14.0.0 or later
bugs.impact: TLSv1.3 gets enabled on the server SSL profiles.
bugs.workaround: -- To avoid this issue, upgrade from v12.x to v13.x, and then upgrade to v14.0.0 or later -- To mitigate this issue, modify the affected profile to disable TLSv1.3.

bugs.title: CGN Inbound connections should not bypass AFM firewall rules
bugs.symptoms: CGNAT inbound connections to an lsn-pool member IP address that are supposed to match a AFM firewall rule do not trigger a policy action.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM Provisioned. -- Inbound connection matches firewall rule.
bugs.impact: Inbound connection's packet always bypass firewall rules.
bugs.fix: AFM Firewall policy is now enforced on inbound connections as default behavior. Added sys db variable afm.inbound_conn.enforce_policies to disable AFM policy enforcement on inbound connection.
