bugs.behavior: A new sys db variable has been added, afm.inbound_conn.enforce_policies, to disable AFM policy enforcement on inbound connections. It can be set to enable or disable, and the default is enable.

bugs.title: Incorrect eps rate for ICMP fragmented DoS vector
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect pps (eps) rate in the GUI interface (and tmctl dos_stats) for ICMP fragmented DoS vector.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM deployed. -- ICMP fragments received by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Incorrect statistics for ICMP fragmented DoS vector

bugs.title: GTM Sync group not syncing properly with multiple self IP addresses configured on one VLAN but not all configured for GTM server
bugs.symptoms: GTM changes in some devices are not synced to other GTM-configured devices in the same syncgroup.
bugs.conditions: -- There are multiple self IP addresses configured on one VLAN. -- Some, but not all, self IP addresses are configured for GTM server.
bugs.impact: GTM Sync group not syncing properly.
bugs.workaround: Configure all self IP addresses in the syncgroup for GTM server.

bugs.title: Updates to HSL pool members may not take effect
bugs.symptoms: High Speed Logging (HSL) does not respect the configured pool's changes and continues to send logs to the previous state of the pool. For example, consider the following configuration: -- HSL configured to send logs to pool (pool-HSL) where pool-HSL has 2 members: pm-1, and pm-2. -- There is a manual update to pool-HSL to remove pm-2, or a monitor marks pm-2 down. -- That change is not honored, and HSL continues to send logs to pm-2.
bugs.conditions: -- High Speed Logging configured to log to a pool of multiple members. -- Pool members change manually or due to a monitoring probe. -- Running one of the known affected TMOS versions.
bugs.impact: HSL logs continue being forwarded according to the previous state of the configured pool. The new state is not reflected.
bugs.fix: Updates to pool members used as HSL destination are correctly reflected in HSL log forwarding.

bugs.title: REST API Timeout while queriying large number of persistence profiles
bugs.symptoms: When you have a large number of collections in BIG-IP, REST API seems to be timed out without any response from BIG-IP
bugs.conditions: When BIG-IP has large number of persistence profiles.
bugs.impact: REST API gets timed out when REST API queries the BIG-IP for persistence profiles. There is no response sent for given REST API.
bugs.workaround: When you have a large number of collections, you are recommended to use paging mechanism. Please refer https://devcentral.f5.com/d/icontrol-rest-user-guide-version-131-246. "iControl ® REST supports pagination options for large collections.

bugs.title: Custom MIB actions can be blocked by SELINUX permissions
bugs.symptoms: When creating custom MIBs you can execute commands, but you may run into SELINUX permissions issues that prevent the tmctl command from executing.
bugs.conditions: Executing tmctl calls inside custom MIB procedures
bugs.impact: Statistics are not collected for the MIB objects
bugs.fix: The SNMPD LINUX permissions have been expanded to cover this case.

bugs.title: Http2 virtual does not honour translate-address disabled
bugs.symptoms: Translate-address disabled on an HTTP/2 virtual server is ignored.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 virtual server configured. -- Translate-address disabled.
bugs.impact: The traffic is still translated to the destination address to the pool member.
bugs.fix: Translate-address disabled is working correctly now.

bugs.title: In BIG-IP VE, some IP rules may not be created during the first boot up.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) system might not be able to install some IP rules in the host during the first boot up. As a result, some types of traffic (e.g., ssh) destined for the BIG-IP system via the data path (not via the management interface) might not be able to respond back to a sender. This issue exists only during the first boot into a new BIG-IP partition after installation.
bugs.conditions: This issue exists if the following conditions are met: -- The BIG-IP system is VE. -- Before installing a new BIG-IP image, the sys db variables 'liveinstall.saveconfig' and 'liveinstall.moveconfig' are both set to 'disable'. By default, both variables are set to 'enable'. -- First boot into a new BIG-IP partition after installation.
bugs.impact: Some types of traffic (e.g., ssh) destined for the BIG-IP system via the data path (not via the management interface) might not be able to respond back to a sender.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Restart mcpd using the following command: bigstart restart mcpd -- After the first boot into a new BIG-IP partition, you can simply reboot the BIG-IP system again, and then the necessary IP rules are created correctly.
bugs.fix: The necessary IP rules are created correctly in the first boot into a new BIG-IP partition after installation.

bugs.title: Downgrading from v14.1.0 to a previous release leaves two directories with improper ownership
bugs.symptoms: Downgrading from BIG-IP version 14.1.0 to an earlier version, the group ID of /var/lock and /var/spool/mail are incorrect. This can be encountered after you boot into the earlier-versioned software image. /var/log/liveinstall.log contains the following messages: -- info: RPM: filesystem-2.4.30-3.el6.0.0.10.i686 -- info: RPM: warning: group lock does not exist - using root -- info: RPM: warning: group mail does not exist - using root When running the following command: config # rpm -V filesystem ......G.. /var/lock ......G.. /var/spool/mail The expected results are as follows: config # rpm -V filesystem config # stat -c %G /var/lock lock config # stat -c %G /var/spool/mail mail In this version, the results are as follows: config # rpm -V filesystem config # stat -c %G /var/lock root config # stat -c %G /var/spool/mail root
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP version 14.1.0 is running. -- An earlier software version is installed. -- The system is then booted into that earlier version.
bugs.impact: There is no known impact to the system if this occurs; however, running rpm -V will report these two discrepancies. This occurs because rpm versions 4.8 and earlier have built-in recognition of exactly three group names; 'root', 'mail', and 'lock'. In v4.8, these special names appear in <src>/lib/misc.c:gnameToGid. To use the group names 'mail' and 'lock' as intended, all BIG-IP releases earlier than BIG-IP v14.1.0 rely on this special feature of rpm. BIG-IP v14.1.0 moved to rpm version 4.11, in which the function no longer exists.
bugs.workaround: Using a shell command, correct the group ID of the two directories that are incorrect using the following two commands: config # chgrp lock /var/lock config # chgrp mail /var/spool/mail

bugs.title: False positive cookie hijacking violation
bugs.symptoms: A false positive cookie hijacking violation.
bugs.conditions: -- Several sites are configured on the policy, without subdomain. -- TS cookies are sent with the higher domain level then the configured. -- A single cookie from another host (that belongs to the same policy) arrives and is mistaken as the other site cookie.
bugs.impact: False positive violation / blocking.

bugs.title: Connection tear down takes longer when using FastL4 profiles and connection mirroring.
bugs.symptoms: Connection tear down takes longer when using FastL4 profiles and connection mirroring.
bugs.conditions: FastL4 profile with connection mirroring.
bugs.impact: Delay during TCP connection tear down.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than disabling the db variable tm.fastl4_ack_mirror to disable mirroring when using FastL4.

bugs.title: UDP::hold/UDP::release does not work correctly
bugs.symptoms: UDP::hold/UDP::release do not work properly. Connections cannot be deleted and tmm logs an error: crit tmm14[38818]: 01010289:2: Oops @ 0x2b6b31b:7903: Flow already has peer. Tried to overwrite.
bugs.conditions: iRule with UDP::hold/UDP::release
bugs.impact: UDP::hold/UDP::release does not work correctly
bugs.fix: UDP::hold/UDP::release now works correctly

bugs.title: Downgrading from BIG-IP version 14.1.0 to an earlier version, the mode of /sys is incorrect.
bugs.symptoms: rpm is used to check current file states versus expected file states in the 'filesystem' package; changes are detected: [root@localhost:NO LICENSE:Standalone] config # rpm -V filesystem .M....... /sys
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP version 14.1.0 is running. -- An earlier software version is installed. -- The system is then booted into that earlier version.
bugs.impact: There is no known impact to the system if this occurs, but running 'rpm -V filesystem' reports the discrepancy.
bugs.workaround: Using a shell command, run the following command to correct the mode of the directory that is incorrect: chmod u+w /sys

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator may not activate service connectors if traffic is an HTTP tunnel
bugs.symptoms: Decrypted traffic is not forwarded to services despite even though a matching rule action in security policy selects a service chain.
bugs.conditions: -- Matching rule action in security policy selects a service chain. -- Traffic is an HTTP tunnel (CONNECT method) is accepted by an outbound transparent proxy created by SSL Orchestrator.
bugs.impact: No visibility to decrypted traffic if it is an HTTP tunnel through SSL Orchestrator.
bugs.fix: Decrypted traffic is forwarded as expected to services, when matching rule action in security policy selects a service chain, for HTTP tunnel traffic sent through SSL Orchestrator.

bugs.title: Restore old 'merge' functionally with new tmsh verb 'replace'
bugs.symptoms: Prior to v12.1.3.4, the 'merge' command merged a specified config with the existing config, replacing certain conflicting values. In this release, the merge command operates differently, so there is a new command, 'replace', to now perform the operation previously accomplished with 'merge'.
bugs.conditions: Running the following command: tmsh load /sys config file <scf-filename> merge
bugs.impact: Operation does not work like it did in previous releases.
bugs.fix: This release restores the merge functionally from v12.x and earlier with a new tmsh verb: replace. The new TMSH command is as follows: tmsh load sys config file <filepath> replace
bugs.behavior: This release restores the merge functionally from v12.x and earlier with a new tmsh verb: replace. The new TMSH command is as follows: tmsh load sys config file <filepath> replace The merge command now operates as follows: -- Previously: if a top-level object (virtual server) existed in the config and also in the merge file, the top-level object was replaced. -- Now: if a top-level object (virtual server) exists in both, the top-level object is recursively merged. (Pool members are merged together. LTM virtual server profiles are merged together (appended vs. replace-all-with)).

bugs.title: Possible tmm crash when using manual mode mitigation in DoS Profile
bugs.symptoms: tmm crash and restart is possible when using manual mode mitigation in DoS Profile.
bugs.conditions: When manual mode mitigation is used for any vector that is enabled in the DoS Profile that is attached to a Protected Object.
bugs.impact: tmm crash and restart is possible. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm crash and restart no longer occurs when using manual mode mitigation in DoS Profile.

bugs.title: TSO packet bit fails IPsec during ESP encryption
bugs.symptoms: Internal error when an unexpected packet bit for TCP segment offload manages to reach crypto code for ESP in IPsec, when this is not expected.
bugs.conditions: Traffic passing through ESP encapsulation for an IPsec tunnel when the TSO bit (for TcpSegmentationOffload) is set on the packet involved.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Now we ensure the TSO bit is cleared, so it doesn't cause ESP crypto code to fail, when it cannot be handled correctly.

bugs.title: BIOS update fails with "flashrom not safe for BIOS updates yet" log message
bugs.symptoms: Upon installing a version of BIG-IP that contains an updated version of the system BIOS onto an F5 hardware platform, the BIOS update may fail. Messages similar to the following may be seen at the console: Updating BIOS to /usr/firmware/<filename>.bin Using layout file /usr/firmware/<filename>.layout to update bios region Updating BIOS... DO NOT POWER DOWN Updating BIOS... DO NOT POWER DOWN (elapsed seconds:1) ... Updating BIOS... DO NOT POWER DOWN (elapsed seconds:##) BIOS update failed. Check /var/log/ltm for errors Broadcast message from systemd-journald@localhost (<date & time string>): chmand[####]: 012a0000:0: BIOS update failed. Check /var/log/ltm for errors A message similar to the following will be seen in the /var/log/ltm file: info chmand[####]: 012a0006:6: /bin/bios_update: flashrom not safe for BIOS updates yet.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on F5 hardware platforms running affected versions of BIG-IP based on RHEL 7.x, when booting into an affected version that includes a newer BIOS image than the system is currently using. The "tmsh show sys hardware" command can be used to see the currently-used BIOS version. The /var/log/ltm file contains messages from chmand when BIOS (and other firmware) updates are attempted, which display the version found currently installed and the newer version for which the update was attempted.
bugs.impact: Affected F5 hardware platforms may continue to run a non-current version of system BIOS, which may compromise system stability and/or performance.
bugs.workaround: It is possible to work around this issue by installing a later, non-affected version of BIG-IP into a different volume, booting into that version to perform firmware updates, then booting back into the affected BIG-IP version.
bugs.fix: BIOS updates are now successfully performed on versions of BIG-IP based on RHEL 7.x.

bugs.title: iRule running reject in CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED event can cause core
bugs.symptoms: The CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED iRule event can run very early when classification happens in the classification database (srdb). If the iRule then issues a reject command, tmm cores.
bugs.conditions: CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED on L4 executing reject command.
bugs.impact: tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: iRule running reject in CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED event no longer causes tmm core.

bugs.title: False positive CSRF violation for the URL with semicolon with explicit CSRF URL configuration
bugs.symptoms: Requests containing semicolon ';' characters are blocked by an ASM policy that has explicit CSRF URL configured. An ASM blocking page listing a support ID is presented to the ASM end user.
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned. - ASM configured on a virtual server. - ASM CSRF enabled and explicit URL configured.
bugs.impact: Web application do not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use a wildcard CSRF URL.
bugs.fix: CSRF JavaScript code now handles the semicolon ';' character, as a path parameter separator, when it is at the end of the request URL.

bugs.title: Kerberos replay cache leaks file descriptors
bugs.symptoms: APMD reports 'too many open files' error when reading HTTP requests: -- err apmd[15293]: 01490000:3: HTTPParser.cpp func: "readFromSocket()" line: 113 Msg: epoll_create() failed [Too many open files]. -- err apmd[15293]: 01490000:3: ApmD.cpp func: "process_apd_request()" line: 1801 Msg: Error 3 reading/parsing response from socket 1498. strerror: Too many open files, queue size 0, time since accept There are file descriptor dumps in /var/log/apm showing many deleted files with name krb5_RCXXXXXX: -- err apmd[15293]: 01490264:3: 1492 (/shared/tmp/krb5_RCx8EN5y (deleted)) : cloexec, Fflags[0x8002], read-write -- err apmd[15293]: 01490264:3: 1493 (/shared/tmp/krb5_RCnHclFz (deleted)) : cloexec, Fflags[0x8002], read-write -- err apmd[15293]: 01490264:3: 1494 (/shared/tmp/krb5_RCKGW8ia (deleted)) : cloexec, Fflags[0x8002], read-write
bugs.conditions: This failure may happen if the access policy uses Kerberos authentication, Active Directory authentication, or Active Directory query. The conditions under which the Kerberos replay cache leaks is unknown.
bugs.impact: APM end users experience intermittent log on issues.

bugs.title: Header Field Value String Corruption
bugs.symptoms: This is specific to HTTP/2. In some rare cases, the header field value string can have one or more of its prefix characters removed by the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: If the header field value string is exceptionally long, and has embedded white space characters, this bug may occur.
bugs.impact: A header such as: x-info: very_long_string that has white space characters may be sent to the client thus: x-info: ery_long_string that has white space characters
bugs.fix: Fixed.

bugs.title: In SSL forward proxy, forged untrusted server certs are no longer cached.
bugs.symptoms: Previously, SSL forward proxy cached forged server certs on the client side even if the server cert was untrusted. Now, SSL forward proxy does not cache the forged cert if the server cert is untrusted.
bugs.conditions: SSL forward proxy is enabled and server cert is untrusted.
bugs.impact: You might notice a performance impact compared with previous releases.
bugs.fix: There is a behavior change: the system does not cache forged server certs if the cert is not trusted.
bugs.behavior: Previously, SSL forward proxy cached forged server certs on the client side even if the server cert was untrusted. Now, SSL forward proxy does not cache the forged cert if the server cert is untrusted. As a result, you might notice slower performance in this release under these conditions.

bugs.title: Fake keystrokes are not generated in some browsers
bugs.symptoms: When Keylogger protection is enabled, some browsers (e.g., Microsoft Internet Explorer v11) may show the 'caps lock is on' warning on the password field of a login page.
bugs.conditions: Keylogger protection is enabled on a protected URL.
bugs.impact: Capslock warning is displayed, even when caps lock is off, or it may not be displayed when caps lock is on.
bugs.fix: The 'caps lock' indicator now shows correctly.

bugs.title: PEM::session info cannot set subscriber type and ID
bugs.symptoms: Cannot set the subscriber type and ID with iRule PEM::session info <subs-id | subs-type | subscriber-type | subscriber-id > <value>.
bugs.conditions: Trying to set a subscriber type and ID attributes using the following iRules returns error. PEM::session info <ip> subscriber-id <value> PEM::session info <ip> subscriber-type <value> PEM::session info <ip> subs-id <value> PEM::session info <ip> subs-type <value>
bugs.impact: Cannot set subscriber type and ID using PEM:session info iRule.
bugs.workaround: Set the subscriber type and ID together using the following iRule. PEM::session info <ip addr> subscriber subscriber-id> <subscriber-type>

bugs.title: DNS queries without the RD bit set may generate responses with the RD bit set
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system is configured to use forward zones, responses to DNS queries may include the RD bit, even if RD bit is not set on the query.
bugs.conditions: -- Forward zone is configured. -- Processing a query without the RD bit.
bugs.impact: Some responses to DNS queries may include the RD bit, even thought the RD bit is not set on the query. This is cosmetic, but some DNS tools may report this as an RFC violation.
bugs.fix: If a query does not have the RD bit set and is forwarded, the system now clears the RD bit on the response from the forward, if it is set.

bugs.title: Invalid Bot Defense Cookie might be raised when browser is open for too long
bugs.symptoms: When using Bot Defense profile, if a browser page remains open too long (more then 24 hours) without surfing the webserver, BIG-IP raises an Anomaly "Invalid Bot Defense Cookie" and mitigate the request.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense Profile is attached to VS. -- Browser remains open for more then 24 hours without surfing the site (after first surfing to the site)
bugs.impact: Clients are mitigated by this anomaly.
bugs.workaround: Add Exception for "Invalid Bot Defense Cookie" to "Captcha" - clients will have to solve captcha, but cookies will renew and issue would be solved (no more Captchas)

bugs.title: GUI Network Map to account for objects in a Disabled By Parent state
bugs.symptoms: When an object has a Disabled By Parent state, it is counted in the Unknown status instead of evaluating its actual Availability status.
bugs.conditions: Viewing objects with Disabled By Parent state in Network Map.
bugs.impact: The status shown in the map and summary view does not reflect the correct status.
bugs.workaround: Use the object list views to filter by status to see the correct status.

bugs.title: Out-of-order packet arrival may cause incorrect Fast L4 goodput calculation
bugs.symptoms: When Fast L4 receives out of order TCP packets, TCP analytics may compute wrong goodput value.
bugs.conditions: When FAST L4 receives out-of-order packets.
bugs.impact: Fast L4 reports an incorrect goodput value for the connection.
bugs.fix: Out-of-order packet arrival no longer causes incorrect Fast L4 goodput calculation

bugs.title: Internally forwarded flows can get dropped with AFM L4 BDoS feature enabled
bugs.symptoms: Client request fails, due to being dropped on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP AFM L4 BDoS feature is enabled. -- Virtual server setup is such that the client-facing virtual server's destination is forwarded through another virtual server, which is an internally forwarded flow.
bugs.impact: Client request gets dropped due to BIG-IP AFM dropping the flow.
bugs.workaround: Disable BDoS feature. The feature can be disabled using the following commands: -- To disable BDoS globally, run the following command: modify security dos device-config dos-device-config dynamic-signatures { network { detection disabled mitigation none }} To disable BDoS globally per-profile, run the following command: modify security dos profile <profile-name> dos-network modify { test { dynamic-signatures { detection disabled mitigation none } } } modify security dos profile test protocol-dns modify { test { dynamic-signatures { detection disabled mitigation none } } }
bugs.fix: The system now handles the looped flows properly, so the BDoS module does not incorrectly cause the packet to be dropped.

bugs.title: Firefox v52 or earlier getting CAPTCHA by Bot Defense
bugs.symptoms: ASM end users connecting using Firefox v52 or earlier might get the CAPTCHA challenge by Bot Defense when the browser is running on virtual machine or Remote Desktop.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense is enabled. -- Detect Suspicious Browsers is turned on. -- Using a pre-v52 version of Firefox. -- Running Firefox on a virtual machine or Remote Desktop.
bugs.impact: Firefox users can access the page only after passing the CAPTCHA challenge.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command to work around the issue: tmsh modify sys db dosl7.browser_legit_min_score_captcha value 70
bugs.fix: The system no longer presents a CAPTCHA challenge CAPTCHA by Bot Defense for ASM users connecting using Firefox v52 or earlier.

bugs.title: TCP Analytics: Fast L4 TCP Analytics reports incorrect goodput.
bugs.symptoms: Fast L4 TCP Analytics reports incorrect goodput when server sequence number and the TMM generated sequence number are different.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when either of the following conditions are met: -- tcp-generate-isn is set in the Fast L4 profile. -- SYN cookie is active.
bugs.impact: The GUI page Statistics :: Analytics :: TCP :: Goodput page displays incorrect goodput values.
bugs.fix: Fast L4 TCP Analytics now shows correct goodput values when server sequence number and the TMM generated sequence number are different.

bugs.title: Automatic eviction of PEM URLCAT cloud cache
bugs.symptoms: PEM URLCAT looks up the URL in the local webroot database of 20 million entries. If an entry is not found in the webroot local DB, a message is sent to webroot website. The results from the web lookup are stored in a per tmm local cache, which can hold 128K entries (by default). If the local cache fills up, the cloud query no longer happens. It is required to clear up some space in the cloud cache to accommodate the new entries.
bugs.conditions: If the local cache fills up, the cloud query no longer happens.
bugs.impact: Cloud query no longer happens for new requests.
bugs.fix: 10% of the per tmm local cache will be cleared and new entries will be added in this space only. The last 10% of memory will always be cleared if the local cache is full.
bugs.behavior: The entries in the cloud cache will be evicted, if the cache becomes full. Prior to this change, the cloud lookup would stop altogether once the cache was full.

bugs.title: VMware Horizon PCoIP clients may fail to connect shortly after logout
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes if user closes opened PCoIP desktop and logs out and then logs in again, he can't launch the same desktop anymore.
bugs.conditions: PCoIP UDP VS has "vdi" profile assigned.
bugs.impact: User can't open PCoIP remote desktop during short time period (1 minute).
bugs.workaround: Remove "vdi" profile and assign "remotedesktop" profile to the PCoIP UDP VS: # tmsh modify ltm virtual <PCoIP UDP VS> profiles delete { vdi } # tmsh modify ltm virtual <PCoIP UDP VS> profiles add { remotedesktop } In admin UI the assignment of "remotedesktop" profile can be controlled via "Application Tunnels (Java & Per-App VPN)" checkbox (right under "VDI Profile" dropdown).
bugs.fix: Assignment of "vdi" profile to PCoIP UDP VS does not cause intermittent connection problems anymore.

bugs.title: Duplicate entries in dos_stat table
bugs.symptoms: The dos_stats table shows duplicate entries with one being in learning status and the other in ready status.
bugs.conditions: - Deploy BIG-IP - Provision DDoS modules - After attack and learning period is over
bugs.impact: Duplicate entry is shown in the statistics table, leading to confusion.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system might fail to read SFPs after a reboot
bugs.symptoms: SFP interfaces are reported as missing: # tmsh show net interface 2.0 -------------------------------------------------------- Net::Interface Name Status Bits Bits Pkts Pkts Drops Errs Media In Out In Out -------------------------------------------------------- 2.0 miss 0 0 0 0 0 0 none sys ha-status will report tmm ready-for-world as failed: # tmsh show sys ha-status ------------------------------------------------------------------------- Sys::HA Status Feature Key Action Fail ------------------------------------------------------------------------- ready-for-world tmm none yes ready-for-world tmm1 none yes ready-for-world tmm2 none yes ready-for-world tmm3 none yes ready-for-world tmm4 none yes ready-for-world tmm5 none yes
bugs.conditions: This has been seen on the i15800 and i11000 series BIG-IP platforms immediately after the system boots.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not become ready after a reboot.
bugs.workaround: Mitigation if the system is in this state, restart tmm: # tmsh restart sys service tmm

bugs.title: 'DataSafe Profiles' menu has changed to 'BIG-IP DataSafe'
bugs.symptoms: The 'DataSafe Profiles' menu has changed to 'BIG-IP DataSafe'.
bugs.conditions: FPS Provisioning and a DataSafe license.
bugs.impact: The menu name has changed in this release.
bugs.fix: 'DataSafe Profiles' menu has changed to 'BIG-IP DataSafe'.

bugs.title: BD is not correctly closing a shared memory segment
bugs.symptoms: Number shared memory segments is increasing.
bugs.conditions: There are many ASM restarts.
bugs.impact: Memory increases on the system.
bugs.fix: Fixed a possible shared memory leak issue.

bugs.title: CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED running reject can lead to a tmm core
bugs.symptoms: When the CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED event is run on a serverside flow, and then an iRule command (e.g., to reject a flow) is run, tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- CLASSIFICATION_DETECTED event runs on a serverside flow. -- An iRule command runs (e.g., reject a flow).
bugs.impact: tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: SIP MRF INGRESS_ALG_TRANSLATION_FAIL state has incorrect state_type
bugs.symptoms: SIP ALG calls that fail translation during ingress are not cleaned up by the system, which might result in memory being leaked inside the TMM processes.
bugs.conditions: SIP ALG calls that fail translation during ingress.
bugs.impact: TMM leaks memory, which can slow down performance and eventually cause TMM to run out of memory and restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now cleans up SIP ALG calls that fail translation during ingress, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Mitigate mcpd out of memory error with auto-sync enabled.
bugs.symptoms: If auto-sync is enabled and many configuration changes are sent quickly, it is possible for a peer system to fall behind in syncs. Once it does, it will exponentially get further behind due to extra sync data, leading to the sending mcpd running out of memory and core dumping.
bugs.conditions: -- Auto-sync enabled in an HA pair. -- High volume of configuration changes made in rapid succession. Typically, this requires hundreds or thousands of changes per minute for several minutes to encounter this condition.
bugs.impact: mcpd crashes.
bugs.workaround: There are no workarounds other than not using auto-sync, or reducing the frequency of system configuration changes.
bugs.fix: This is not a complete fix. It is still possible for mcpd to run out of memory due to a peer not processing sync messages quickly enough. It does, however, make it more difficult for this scenario to happen, so configuration changes with auto-sync on can be sent somewhat more quickly without crashing mcpd as often.

bugs.title: GUI - Provide search capability for Keys, Certificates and SSL Profile select boxes
bugs.symptoms: It is hard to select options when there are a large number of options in select boxes for Keys, Certificates, and SSL Profiles.
bugs.conditions: Have large number of Keys, Certificates, and SSL Profiles, which is common in case of virtual hosting.
bugs.impact: It is hard to search and select required options when there are large number of options in select boxes. In addition, the GUI may restart due to java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space when a large number of SSL key/cert/profiles. This applies to all GUI screens with large number of SSL key/cert/profiles.
bugs.workaround: To work around the out-of memory issue, 1. Allocate appropriate extramb to tomcat using the following command: tmsh modify sys db provision.tomcat.extramb value 256 2. Restart tomcat: bigstart restart tomcat
bugs.fix: Improved selection experience when there are number of options in select boxes for Keys, Certificates, and SSL Profiles. GUI no longer restarts.

bugs.title: HTTP commands do not return an error when called from an invalid state
bugs.symptoms: HTTP commands do not return an error when called from an invalid state, such as after HTTP::disable has been called, or from an 'after' script. TMM might crash and report a message in one of the TMM logs: notice panic: ../modules/hudfilter/http/http_cookie.c:489: Assertion "cookie name exists" failed.
bugs.conditions: Executing HTTP commands in an iRule from an invalid state.
bugs.impact: TMM might restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Change iRule so that it is not calling HTTP commands from an invalid state.

bugs.title: tmm core while using service chaining for SSLO
bugs.symptoms: tmm cores when using security services (service connect agent in per-request policies) for SSLO deployment.
bugs.conditions: -- Service connect agent in per-request policy. -- SSLO deployment.
bugs.impact: tmm cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer cores when using security services (service connect agent in per-request policies) for SSLO deployment.

bugs.title: Changing route-domain on partitions leads to Secondary blade reboot loop and virtual servers left in unusual state
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Servers left in unknown state. Blade keeps restarting.
bugs.conditions: Change default route domain (RD) of partition with wildcard Virtual Servers.
bugs.impact: -- Cannot persist the wildcard virtual server RD configuration. -- Changing virtual server description after moving route-domain fails. -- Secondary blade in constant reboot loop.
bugs.workaround: 1. Delete wildcard virtual servers before changing default route-domain on partition. 2. Execute the following commands, in sequence, substituting your values for the configuration-specific ones in this example: # ssh slot2 bigstart stop # modify auth partition pa-1098-blkbbsi0000csa21ad1142 default-route-domain 109 # save sys config # clsh rm -f /var/db/mcpdb.bin # ssh slot2 bigstart start Note: This recovery method might have to be executed multiple times to restore a working setup.

bugs.title: False positive illegal meta char violation in param name
bugs.symptoms: false positive illegal meta char violation in param name.
bugs.conditions: -- There is a definition for an illegal meta char. -- That meta char arrives escaped.
bugs.impact: False positive violation.
bugs.workaround: Change the parameter name meta illegal meta chars.

bugs.title: Live Update cannot be used by Administrator users other than 'admin' and 'root'
bugs.symptoms: When users configured with the Administrator role log into the system, they are not allowed to install security update files on the new live-update page: System :: Software Management : Live Update
bugs.conditions: Logged in BIG-IP user is not 'admin' (the built-in Administrator account for the TMUI) or 'root' (the built-in Administrator account for the TMSH).
bugs.impact: Cannot apply security updates.
bugs.workaround: To install the security updates, log in as 'admin' or a BIG-IP user configured as a web-application-security-administrator or web-application-security-editor (role must be configured on all partitions or at least on the Common partition).
bugs.fix: Any BIG-IP user configured as Administrator can now apply security updates.

bugs.title: ACL-related reports might not contain some of the activity that takes place
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, some telemetry data of ACL-related activity is lost. You might see messages similar to the following: ../src/loader/monpd_stat.cc:load_file:0571| Some rows of load_stat_enforced_acl_154392960.1 not loaded (1597 rows affected).
bugs.conditions: No specific condition other than using the AFM Rules feature.
bugs.impact: ACL-related reports might not contain some of the activity that takes place.

bugs.title: Many nested client SSL profiles can take a lot of time to process and cause MCP to be killed by sod
bugs.symptoms: With a large number of client SSL profiles, combined with shallow nesting of these profiles, all referring to a single SSL certificate file object, mcpd can take a lot of time to process an update to that certificate. It is possible this amount of time will be longer than sod's threshold, and cause it to kill mcpd.
bugs.conditions: - A large number (hundreds or thousands) of client SSL profiles that have a shallow nesting structure and all point back to a single SSL certificate file object. - Happens when the SSL certificate is updated.
bugs.impact: sod kills mcpd, which causes a failover (when high availability (HA) is configured) or an outage (when there is no HA configured).
bugs.fix: Prevented sod from killing mcpd in this scenario.

bugs.title: mcpd can be killed if the configuration contains a very high number of nested references
bugs.symptoms: mcpd can be killed by sod if the configuration contains a very high number of nested references. This results in a core file due to a SIGABRT signal.
bugs.conditions: A very high number of nested configuration references (such as SSL certificate file objects).
bugs.impact: Failover or outage (if not HA). The system sends no traffic or status while mcpd restarts.

bugs.title: PEM iRule action with RULE_INIT event fails to attach to PEM policy
bugs.symptoms: PEM iRule action with RULE_INIT event fails to attach to PEM policy.
bugs.conditions: Attaching PEM policy with PEM iRule action that contains a RULE_INIT event.
bugs.impact: PEM fails to update the new iRule action.
bugs.workaround: Force mcpd to reload the BIG-IP configuration. To do so, follow the steps in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030.
bugs.fix: The system now continues processing PEM iRule actions if RULE_INIT event is present, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: AFM drops forwarding ICMP traffic matching FW NAT rule for Dest NAT that also has Proxy ARP enabled for destination addresses in the rule
bugs.symptoms: When Proxy ARP is enabled for destination addresses in an FW NAT rule performing destination NAT (static-nat/static-pat), forwarding ICMP traffic matching that rule is incorrectly dropped by AFM instead of being forwarded through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- Proxy ARP is enabled for destination addresses in an FW NAT rule. -- The BIG-IP system (AFM) receives forwarding ICMP traffic for these (untranslated) destination addresses.
bugs.impact: Forwarding ICMP traffic is dropped by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: You can disable Proxy ARP functionality for FW NAT rules to cause the BIG-IP system (AFM) to handle forwarding ICMP traffic correctly and pass it through the system to the backend. However, this causes the BIG-IP system to not respond to ARP requests anymore for destination addresses in such rules. As a further mitigation action, you can configure static ARP entries to handle this.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system (AFM) now correctly forwards ICMP traffic through to the backend when Proxy ARP is enabled on destination addresses in the matching FW NAT rule.

bugs.title: Hardware returning incorrect type of entry when notifying software might cause tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Potential tmm crash when hardware returns incorrect type of entry when notifying software.
bugs.conditions: -- sPVA is not programmed with blacklist or greylist entries. -- Hardware returns an incorrect blacklist or greylist entry to the software.
bugs.impact: tmm crashes and restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release provides a defensive check in software to not crash, and to dump the hardware registers when this happens. This will help to debug the hardware better in the future.

bugs.title: Kerberos SSO: Improve the logging of the error msg when Kerberos requests are not processed.
bugs.symptoms: Currently, when the client system closes the TCP connection, associated Kerberos requests are not processed. The error msg logged is generic, and does not include the reason Kerberos requests were not processed. err websso.3[25121]: 014d0048:3: /Common/test_access_sso:Common:074d1914: failure occurred when processing the work item: Kerberos failed
bugs.conditions: This occurs when Kerberos requests are not processed because the client closed the TCP connection.
bugs.impact: The error msg logged is generic and does not indicate the reason for the failure, which makes it difficult to debug scenarios in which the BIG-IP system handles a large number of Kerberos SSO requests that lead to system instability.
bugs.fix: When Kerberos SSO requests are not processed due to client or server-side issues, the system logs an error msg containing the corresponding reason.

bugs.title: Support some AAA agents relevant to oauth-resource-server type policy
bugs.symptoms: AD query, LDAP query, RADIUS Auth, RADIUS Acct, TACACS+ Auth and TACACS+ Acct cannot be used in an access policy of type oauth-resource-server.
bugs.conditions: Access policy is of type oauth-resource-server.
bugs.impact: The agents cannot be used.
bugs.fix: These agents have now been made visible for access policy of type oauth-resource-server.

bugs.title: Pool IP ToS/QoS settings are not preserved on mirrored FastL4 connections
bugs.symptoms: Mirrored serverside FastL4 connections do not inherit the IP ToS/QoS values from the selected pool or values set via iRule IP::tos/LINK::qos commands.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 virtual server with mirroring. -- Pool with non-zero IP ToS/QoS values. or -- iRule with IP::tos/LINK::qos serverside commands
bugs.impact: IP ToS/QoS values are not set on mirrored connection after failover.
bugs.workaround: Configure desired IP ToS/QoS values in FastL4 profile
bugs.fix: Mirrored FastL4 serverside connections now inherit the IP ToS/QoS values specified in the associated pool configuration or values set via iRule IP::tos/LINK::qos commands.

bugs.title: PEM does not initiate connection request with PCRF/OCS if failover occurs after 26 days
bugs.symptoms: No connection request with PCRF/OCS if high availability (HA) failover occurs after 26 days. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: -- Using PEM. -- HA failover occurs after 26 days.
bugs.impact: PEM does send the reconnect request within the configured reconnect, so there is no connection initiated with PCRF/OCS.
bugs.workaround: To restart the connection, restart tmm restart using the following command: tmm restart Note: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: PEM now initiates the connection with PCRF/OCS under these conditions.

bugs.title: Possible memory leak in nlad deamon
bugs.symptoms: nlad grows in size. The system posts the log message NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE in the apm logfile.
bugs.conditions: - NTLM auth configured. - The BIG-IP system cannot connect to the configured backend KDC.
bugs.impact: nlad may be killed by OOM killer if it grows significantly.
bugs.workaround: Correct configuration issues, so that the BIG-IP system can connect to the configured domain controllers.

bugs.title: ASM REST: All signatures being returned for policy Signatures regardless of signature sets
bugs.symptoms: By default, only signatures that are included in the Security Policy enforcement via the Policy's Signature Sets are included in the response to /tm/asm/policies/<ID>/signatures. Additionally, there should be the capability to $filter for either signatures that are in the policy or not in the policy. These filters are not working
bugs.conditions: ASM REST/GUI is used to determine the number of signatures enabled on a Security Policy
bugs.impact: More data that expected will be returned to REST clients which may cause confusion. Learning statistics/graphs may have confusing/incorrect numbers.
bugs.fix: inPolicy $filter works again, and the default behavior only returns the signatures that are in the policy.

bugs.title: Deprecated Fields in Bot Defense Request Log
bugs.symptoms: Some fields in the Bot Defense request log have been supplanted by new ones that add more information reflecting new features. There are duplicated fields for Bot Defense request log. The previous fields are being kept for backward compatibility so that existing code reading the remote logs do not break. Their presence might introduce confusion as to their significance and use.
bugs.conditions: Using the Bot Defense remote logger.
bugs.impact: Redundant fields that may create confusion.
bugs.workaround: You can safely ignore these fields and use the new ones.

bugs.title: Unable to import access policy with pool
bugs.symptoms: If your exported policy contains a pool object (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or LDAP Auth object) import of such a policy fails.
bugs.conditions: -- Exported policy contains a pool. -- Attempt to import that policy.
bugs.impact: Unable to import certain configurations.
bugs.fix: Policies with pools are imported successfully.

bugs.title: RADIUS auth might not be working as configured when there is change in RADIUS auth config name.
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS auth might not be working as configured when there is change in RADIUS auth config name. You might also see an error: err apmd[14182]: 01490108:3: /Common/:Common:cc55b9e2: RADIUS module: authentication with 'testuser@example' failed: no response from server (0).
bugs.conditions: In an LTM pool that uses APM AAA RADIUS to authenticate, change (modify/delete) the name of the RADIUS authentication server in config file.
bugs.impact: When using tmm.default version, intermittently MCP error messages in tmm logs indicate that the RADIUS server cannot be found, and RADIUS authentication does not work as expected.

bugs.title: Deadlock While Attaching NDAL Devices
bugs.symptoms: A potential deadlock may occur while Network Device Abstraction Layer (NDAL) Interfaces are being attached.
bugs.conditions: -- Using BIG-IP Virtual Edition. -- Attaching NDAL devices. -- The tmm has not yet established a connection with mcpd.
bugs.impact: TMM is unable to connect to mcpd. The tmm process cannot reconnect to mcpd in retries, if a connection is not established on tmm startup.
bugs.fix: Deadlock no longer occurs while NDAL devices are being attached.

bugs.title: Disabling and immediately re-enabling the slot resulting interfaces from the slot permanently removed from aggregation
bugs.symptoms: Working-mbr-count not showing correct number of interfaces.
bugs.conditions: Slot got disabled and re-enabled immediately.
bugs.impact: Interfaces may be removed from an aggregation permanently.
bugs.workaround: Disable and re-enable the slot with time gap of one second.

bugs.title: AJAX encryption feature ignores encoded parameters names
bugs.symptoms: AJAX encryption feature does not encrypt parameters configured with encryption enabled in the application AJAX request. This is done in case the parameters are sent with encoded names.
bugs.conditions: -- Parameter is configured with encryption enabled. -- AJAX encryption feature is enabled and the application sends the configured parameter using AJAX. -- The application sends the configured name encoded. -- The parameter-encoded name and the parameter-unencoded name are different.
bugs.impact: The configured parameter is sent as plain text.
bugs.workaround: You v14.0.x and later, once the parameter is configured, configure the 'Name in request' option to the parameter encoded name. For example, if you have a field called 'password', and you want to send an AJAX request using '%24password', you must configure AJAX Mapping like this: password -> %24password
bugs.fix: In v14.0.x and later, continue to use the solution suggested in the Workaround section. In 13.1.x versions, the encrypt AJAX feature now encrypts parameters with encoded names as well.

bugs.title: avrd process crash during shutdown if connected to BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: During shutdown of BIG-IP, if it is connected to BIG-IQ then avrd might crash.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is set to shutdown and configured to send statistics to BIG-IQ.
bugs.impact: No serious impact, since the BIG-IP is already instructed to shutdown, so the process crash is not causing any damage.
bugs.fix: Issue is fixed, avrd does not crash during shutdown

bugs.title: TimeoutException when filtering request logs
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to view filtered request logs and you see a TimeoutException in /var/log/restjavad.0.log.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while viewing filtered request log entries.
bugs.impact: After 30 seconds, a restjavad timeout occurs.

bugs.title: RST cause logging is improved for a specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: A RST with an 'Unknown reason' is logged for a specific sequence of packets.
bugs.conditions: - TCP, SSL, HTTP, HTTP/2, and HTTPROUTER are configured on the virtual server.
bugs.impact: The RST does not indicate the root cause of the issue.
bugs.fix: A descriptive RST cause message is appended to the log/pcap.

bugs.title: Proxy initialization fails/port denied when excessively large max header size is set in the HTTP/1 profile
bugs.symptoms: If the configuration has an excessively large 'Maximum Header Size' value in the HTTP/1 profile on a virtual server that also has HTTP/2, initialization fails. The tmm log file contains messages similar to the following: notice Proxy initialization failed for /Common/https_virtual1. Defaulting to DENY. The ltm log file contains messages that indicate that the virtual server is not accepting traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Large max_header_size (e.g., 4294967295) is configured in HTTP profile. -- The system does not have enough free memory.
bugs.impact: -- As a result, the initialization fails. -- Browsing via the virtual server does not work.
bugs.workaround: To prevent this issue from occurring, if a virtual server has an HTTP/2 profile on it, the max_header_size value inside the HTTP profile should be between 0 and 131072.

bugs.title: AVR global settings are being overridden by HA peers
bugs.symptoms: Configuration of AVR global settings is being overridden by high availability (HA) peers, and thus report incorrectly to BIG-IQ Data Collection Devices (DCDs).
bugs.conditions: Configuring HA for systems connected to BIG-IQ.
bugs.impact: Configuration of BIG-IP systems in HA configuration can override each other. This might result in the following behavior: -- A common symptom is the 'Stats Last Collection Date' shows up as Dec 31, 1969 or Jan 01, 1970, depending the timezone configuration of the device -- The 'Stats Last Collection Date' shows up as '--' -- The BIG-IP systems incorrectly identify themselves to BIG-IQ. -- The BIG-IP systems report to the wrong DCD. -- The BIG-IP systems report to DCD, even if they are not configured to report at all. -- The BIG-IP systems do not report at all, even if they are configured to report. Note: This bug is tightly related to BIG-IQ Bug ID 757423.
bugs.fix: Synchronization of relevant fields on AVR global settings are disabled, so this issue no longer occurs.
bugs.workaround: Refer to the procedure in K50285521: BIG-IQ system may cause out-of-sync condition between the managed BIG-IP HA pair :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K50285521.

bugs.title: iRule commands (such as relate_server) do not work with MRP SIP
bugs.symptoms: Some iRule commands (such as relate_server) fail when used in conjunction with Message Routing Protocol (MRP) SIP configurations using message routing transport.
bugs.conditions: -- MRP SIP configuration uses transport-config. -- iRule command 'relate_server' is configured on the corresponding virtual server.
bugs.impact: iRule commands such as relate_server cannot be used with MRF SIP.

bugs.title: Portal Access: Resource with '?' in query part of URL cannot be created.
bugs.symptoms: If a Portal Access resource URL contains '?' (a question mark) inside the query part, it cannot be created. The URL is reported to be invalid.
bugs.conditions: Portal Access resource with URL containing a '?' inside query part, like this: http://example.com/some/path?aaa=?&b=vvv
bugs.impact: Portal Access resource cannot be used.
bugs.workaround: Replace '?' with '%3F' inside the query part of the URL.
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access resource URL can contain '?' inside query part.

bugs.title: Large configurations containing LTM Policies load slowly
bugs.symptoms: Very slow performance when loading a configuration, for example, at system start up. During this time, the tmsh process shows high CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: Big IP 13.1.x, 14.x. Large configuration (1 MB or larger) and at least one, but more likely tens or hundreds of LTM policies defined in the configuration.
bugs.impact: Slow configuration loading, or in cases with very large configurations, full config load may fail after a long wait. Slowness increases with overall configuration size and number of LTM policies defined.
bugs.fix: Large configurations containing LTM Policies load normally.

bugs.title: IP::addr iRule command does not allow single digit mask
bugs.symptoms: When plain literal IP address and mask are used in IP::addr command, the validation fails if the mask is single digit.
bugs.conditions: The address mask is single digit.
bugs.impact: Validation fails.
bugs.workaround: Assign address/mask to a variable and use the variable in the command.

bugs.title: iControl REST incorrectly allows remotely-authenticated users to use basic authentication
bugs.symptoms: Configurations that previously used TACACS for authentication in order to make REST requests are no longer required to use a token for remote authentication. You can simply use username and password via basic authentication.
bugs.conditions: Use of remote authentication using TACACS.
bugs.impact: iControl REST traffic using Basic authentication with valid credentials succeeds, when it should not.
bugs.fix: REST no longer requires a token to login for TACACS authorization.
bugs.behavior: REST Requests previously required a token for remote, TACACS authentication. Now, you can authenticate remotely with only username/password. Note: If you previously used scripts that automatically requested tokens, you should remove them from use.

bugs.title: Attempt to change password using /bin/passwd fails
bugs.symptoms: When we run /bin/passwd as root: passwd.bin: unable to start pam: Critical error - immediate abort Failed to change user's password. Exiting. If we then do /bin/ausearch -m avc -ts recent, we see a lot of selinux denials for passwd.bin.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions needed
bugs.impact: Root/admin user cannot change password using the standard /bin/passwd executable.
bugs.workaround: The workaround would be to disable selinux, change the password and re-enable selinux: # setenforce Permissive # passwd # setenforce Enforcing Alternatively, one can use the tmsh commands to change the passwords: tmsh modify auth password root Lastly, if one wishes to modify the selinux policy, there is the standard way of doing this # ausearch -c passwd.bin --raw | audit2allow -M mypasswd # semoduile -i mypasswd.pp
bugs.fix: With fix, we have no issues with /bin/passwd.bin being denied by selinux and /bin/passwd works as expected.

bugs.title: In-TMM monitors may have duplicate instances or stop monitoring
bugs.symptoms: Most monitored resources (such as pools) report messages similar to the following: Availability : unknown Reason : The children pool member(s) either don't have service checking enabled, or service check results are not available yet. A fraction of the monitored resources report the correct status based on the state of the resource. Enabling bigdlog may show instances of messaging containing 'tmm_mid=x:0' (where x can be values like 0, 1, 2 etc.), for example, it is tmm_mid=1:0 in the following example: [0][11288] 2019-03-08 10:03:04.608: ID 10859 :(_do_ping): post ping, status=UNKNOWN [ tmm?=true td=true tr=false tmm_mid=1:0 addr=::ffff:1.2.37.44:443 mon=/Common/https fd=-1 pend=0 #conn=0 up_intvl=5 dn_intvl=5 timeout=16 time_until_up=0 immed=0 next_ping=[1552068189.684126][2019-03-08 10:03:09] last_ping=[1552068184.684909][2019-03-08 10:03:04] deadline=[1552067610.048558][2019-03-08 09:53:30] on_service_list=True snd_cnt=119 rcv_cnt=0 ] The following error might appear in /var/log/ltm: -- failed to handle TMA_MSG_DELETE message: MID 0, error TMA_ERR_INVALID_MID(Monitor ID is invalid or unused)
bugs.conditions: -- Configure In-TMM monitoring with a sufficiently large number of monitored objects. -- Modify monitors while pool members are in an offline state or perform rapid modification of In-TMM monitors.
bugs.impact: Some monitors may be executed multiple times per configured interval on a resource, and some monitors may not be executed at all against resources.
bugs.workaround: Switch to traditional bigd monitoring instead of In-TMM: tmsh modify sys db bigd.tmm value disable
bugs.fix: Rapid modification of in-TMM monitors no longer leaves old monitor instances behind.

bugs.title: Diameter MBLB profile does not change the hop-by-hop ID by default
bugs.symptoms: The Diameter MBLB profile does not change the hop-by-hop ID.
bugs.conditions: Diameter MBLB virtual server.
bugs.impact: The hop-by-hop ID is not changed.
bugs.workaround: no workaround
bugs.fix: The Diameter MBLB profile can now change the hop-by-hop id when enabled by the db key Diameter.mblb.hopid_replace to enable.
bugs.behavior: There is a new db key 'Diameter.mblb.hopid_replace' that you can enable to automatically set the hop-by-hop ID.

bugs.title: iHealth may report false positive for Critical Malware
bugs.symptoms: A minor change in the way qkview reports executable filenames may cause iHealth to interpret the presence of malware.
bugs.conditions: qkview files produced by 14.1.0 when uploaded to ihealth.f5.com
bugs.impact: iHealth may report a false positive for malware.
bugs.workaround: Ignore critical errors for malware reported by iHealth for version 14.1.0 only.
bugs.fix: This is fixed in 14.1.0.1

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system reports frequent kernel page allocation failures.
bugs.symptoms: Despite having free memory, the BIG-IP system frequently logs kernel page allocation failures to the /var/log/kern.log file. The first line of the output appears similar to the following example: swapper/16: page allocation failure: order:2, mode:0x104020 After that, a stack trace follows. Note that the process name in the line ('swapper/16', in this example) varies. You may see generic Linux processes or processes specific to F5 in that line.
bugs.conditions: This issue is known to occur on the following VIPRION blade models: - B2250 (A112) - B4450 (A114) Please note the issue is known to occur regardless of whether the system is running in vCMP mode or not, and regardless of whether the system is Active or Standby.
bugs.impact: As different processes can experience this issue, the system may behave unpredictably. For example, it is possible for a TMOS installation to fail as a result of this issue. Other processes may not exhibit any side effect as a result of this issue. The exact impact depends on which process becomes affected and how this process is designed to handle such a failure to allocate memory.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by increasing the value of the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter. This controls the amount of memory that is kept free for use by special reserves. It is recommend to increase this to either 64 MB (65536 KB) or 128 MB (131072 KB). You must do this on all blades installed in the system. When instantiating this workaround, you must consider whether you want the workaround to only survive reboots, or to survive reboots, upgrades, RMAs, etc. This is an important consideration to make, as you should stop using this workaround when this issue is fixed in a future version of BIG-IP software. So consider the pros and cons of each approach before choosing one. -- If you want the workaround to survive reboots only, perform the following procedure: 1) Log on to the advanced shell (BASH) of the primary blade of the affected VIPRION system. 2) Run the following commands (with the desired amount in KB): # clsh "sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072" # clsh "echo -e '\n# Workaround for ID753650' >> /etc/sysctl.conf" # clsh "echo 'vm.min_free_kbytes = 131072' >> /etc/sysctl.conf" -- If you want the workaround to survive reboots, upgrades, RMAs, etc., perform the following procedure: 1) Log on to the advanced shell (BASH) of the primary blade of the affected VIPRION system. 2) Run the following commands (with the desired amount in KB): # clsh "sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072" # echo -e '\n# Workaround for ID753650' >> /config/startup # echo 'sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072' >> /config/startup Note that the last two commands are not wrapped inside 'clsh' because the /config/startup file is already automatically synchronized across all blades. Once the issue is fixed in a future BIG-IP version, remove the workarounds: -- To remove the first workaround: 1) Edit the /etc/sysctl.conf file on all blades and remove the added lines at the bottom. 2) Reboot the system by running 'clsh reboot'. This will restore the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter to its default value for the BIG-IP version you are running. -- To remove the second workaround: 1) Edit the /config/startup file on the primary blade only and remove the extra lines at the bottom. 2) Reboot the system by running 'clsh reboot'. This restores the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter to its default value for the BIG-IP version you are running. To verify the workaround is in place, run the following command (this should return the desired amount in KB): # clsh "cat /proc/sys/vm/min_free_kbytes"
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer experiences kernel page allocation failures.

bugs.title: Copied policy does not retain signature staging
bugs.symptoms: When copying a modified policy or a policy that has never been applied, all signatures are set to staging enabled.
bugs.conditions: Copying a modified policy or policy that has never been applied.
bugs.impact: All signatures in the copied policy are set to staging enabled.
bugs.workaround: Export the policy (either as binary or XML) and re-import.
bugs.fix: Signature staging settings are retained correctly after the policy is copied.

bugs.title: Incorrect warning: Traffic Matching Criteria's inline source address has been set to any4 from any6 to match inline destination address' address family.
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect warning message is given when the inline source/dest address is changed: -- warning mcpd[6927]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Traffic Matching Criteria's inline source address has been set to any4 from any6 to match inline destination address' address family.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after you create a traffic-matching-criteria (port-list, address-list) with different source and destination addresses.
bugs.impact: An incorrect and confusing warning message is given. This warning does not affect traffic processing. It is inadvertently triggered when reading the configuration of the traffic matching profile. Virtual servers should continue to work, and the config should load as expected, despite the warning.

bugs.title: False positive JSON max array length violation
bugs.symptoms: False-positive JSON max array length violation is reported.
bugs.conditions: -- JSON profile is used. -- The violation is coming for non-array under certain conditions.
bugs.impact: The system reports a false-positive violation.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing UDP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources while processing UDP traffic.
bugs.conditions: Enabled virtual server with a UDP profile. datagram_lb mode enabled.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes UDP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Allow 'DIAMETER::persist reset' command in EGRESS events
bugs.symptoms: The 'DIAMETER::persist reset' command is not allowed in EGRESS events; it is blocked by validation.
bugs.conditions: In an iRule, attempt to use 'DIAMETER::persist reset' in an EGRESS event for DIAMETER.
bugs.impact: Unable to reset persistence records on an EGRESS event in DIAMETER through iRules.
bugs.fix: Fixed iRule validation to allow 'DIAMETER::persist reset' on EGRESS events for DIAMETER.

bugs.title: SNMP does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, SNMP does not follow best security practices when responding with specific MIBs.
bugs.conditions: SNMP access granted (no remote SNMP access is allowed in the default configuration).
bugs.impact: SNMP does not follow best security practices.
bugs.workaround: Restrict access to SNMP via IP and/or SNMPv3 authentication.
bugs.fix: SNMP now follows best security practices for all MIBs.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system failed to advertise virtual address even after the virtual address was in Available state.
bugs.symptoms: After failover, a longer time than expected for the virtual server to become available.
bugs.conditions: -- There is a configuration difference in the pool members before and after the configuration synchronization. -- Probe status is also different.
bugs.impact: Virtual server takes longer than expected to become available.
bugs.workaround: Run full sync (force-full-load-push) from the active BIG-IP system to solve this issue.

bugs.title: Log messages 'TCP RST from remote system' messages logged if GTM/DNS is licensed but not provisioned
bugs.symptoms: When GTM/DNS is licensed but not provisioned, there are potentially numerous reset messages every 10 secs in the gtm/logs: err tmm[29412]: 01230140:3: RST sent from <IP-address:port> to <IP-address:port>, [n] TCP RST from remote system
bugs.conditions: GTM/DNS is licensed but not provisioned.
bugs.impact: A message is logged in gtm/logs. This is an informational message, and can be safely ignored.
bugs.fix: The tmm process no longer attempts to attempt to connect to gtmd if GTM/DNS is not provisioned, so this message no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Virtual server config changes causing incorrect route injection.
bugs.symptoms: Updating the virtual server to use a different virtual address (VADDR) does not work as expected. The old VADDR route should remove and inject the new route for the new virtual address. Instead, it injects incorrect routes into the routing protocols.
bugs.conditions: -- Change the VADDR on a virtual server. -- Set route-advertisement on both VADDRs.
bugs.impact: Incorrect routes are injected into routing protocols.

bugs.title: Inconsistent validation for firewall address-list's nested address-list causes load failure
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistent validation for firewall address-list's nested address-lists causes load failure. The operation validates 'addresses' in the address-list but misses the case of modifying the address-list nested in the address-list. The system posts a message similar to the following: 01071a5a:3: Cannot configure mix of IPv4 and IPv6 address(es) in this object. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Modify an address-list's address-lists to contain mixed IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. -- Save the configuration. -- Load the configuration.
bugs.impact: Missing validation for nested address-list modification allows an invalid configuration to be specified and saved into bigip*.conf, which causes load failure. Note: This might cause upgrade from v12.1.x to fail when the configuration contains a mix of IPv4 and IPv6 within an address-list.
bugs.workaround: Edit the bigip*.conf file to remove the mix of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the nested address-lists.
bugs.fix: This release contains validation to nested address-lists to check for overlapping IP addresses in the same address family.

bugs.title: UDP flows may not be swept
bugs.symptoms: Some UDP connection flows do not show in connection table but do show up in stats. This might occur with datagram_lb mode is enabled on the UDP profile under heavy load.
bugs.conditions: -- UDP profile with datagram_lb mode enabled. -- System under heavy load.
bugs.impact: Increased memory utilization of TMM.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly manages all expired flows.

bugs.title: CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may not be triggered on TLSv1.3 connections
bugs.symptoms: The CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may not be triggered on TLSv1.3 connections.
bugs.conditions: -- TLSv1.3 connection. -- Client SSL profile is configured with client certificate authentication (either 'request' or 'require'). -- An iRule depends upon the CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT event.
bugs.impact: The CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event may not be triggered on TLSv1.3 connections.
bugs.fix: The system now sends CLIENTSSL_CLIENTCERT iRule event when client certificate authentication is configured on client SSL profiles TLS 1.3.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic with AAM
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic with AAM.
bugs.conditions: An active virtual server with an AAM profile and RAM cache enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes AAM traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Proactive Bot Defense : unable to modify existing allow list entry attributes in GUI - 'This whitelist item already exists' pop-up is shown
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to modify existing bot defense allow list item. For example, you attempt to change Mitigation Action to Enabled from Disabled or vice versa. The system posts a popup error: This whitelist item already exists.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you try to commit a change to a Mitigation Action or Browser Verification and Device ID Challenge on an existing allow list. Note: This does not occur if you modify other parts of the allow list item (Source or Specified URL).
bugs.impact: Updating existing whitelist item requires additional steps.
bugs.workaround: If you want to update Mitigation Action of an existing item, you can change Source or Specified URL together to bypass the error.

bugs.title: Configuring SSL Forward Proxy and an OCSP stapling profile may allow a connection to a website with a revoked certificate
bugs.symptoms: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K73202036
bugs.conditions: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K73202036
bugs.impact: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K73202036
bugs.fix: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K73202036

bugs.title: Dynamic Script Removal Detection fires false-positive alerts on Firefox add-ons and Chrome extensions
bugs.symptoms: In some Firefox add-ons and Chrome extensions there are Dynamic Script Removal Detection false-positive alerts when this feature is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic Script Removal Detection enabled. -- Using Firefox with add-ons or Chrome with extensions.
bugs.impact: Dynamic Script Removal Detection false-positive alerts.
bugs.fix: Dynamic Script Removal Detection being enabled no longer causes false-positive alerts on Firefox add-ons and Chrome extensions

bugs.title: Newly added Systems are not added as part of installing a Server Technologies update file
bugs.symptoms: Newly added Systems are not added as part of installing a Server Technologies update file, which prevents acceptance of Server Technology suggestion.
bugs.conditions: A Server Technology update file contained newly added Systems is installed.
bugs.impact: A suggestion to add a Server Technology using a newly added System cannot be accepted.
bugs.workaround: The corresponding ASM Signature update file must be loaded first.
bugs.fix: Newly added Systems are added correctly after installing Server Technology update file.

bugs.title: iRule event info command does not return proper error codes
bugs.symptoms: Some iterations of the DevCentral iRules API documentation describing the 'event' command state that the [event info] command returns one of the ERR_xxxx error codes when LB_FAILED is emitted. However, the return is not according to the API doc, e.g.: -- When the pool is marked down, [event info] returns a empty string. -- When the pool is marked up but all the members are available, it returns 'connection limit'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when comparing the documented iRule event error codes to the actual error codes.
bugs.impact: Misleading information.

bugs.title: iRulesLX NodeJS daemon does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: The iRulesLX NodeJS daemon, if explicitly launched with the --debug command-line option, does not follow best security practices.
bugs.conditions: Launch an iRulesLX plugin:extension with debug command line option (--debug).
bugs.impact: NodeJS daemon does not follow best security practices.
bugs.fix: NodeJS daemon now follows best security practices.

bugs.title: ASM content-security-policy header modification violates Content Security Policy directive
bugs.symptoms: When the backend server sends a content-security-policy header where source-src and default-src directives are missing, ASM will modify the header when it does its own JavaScript injection, which might cause a csp policy violation for inline JavaScript code.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached on a virtual server. -- ASM policy has CSRF or AJAX Blocking page enabled.
bugs.impact: Inline JavaScript does not run. The Browser reports a content-security-policy violation.
bugs.workaround: Disable csp in ASM by running the following commands: -- /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add csp_enabled 0 -- bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: ASM no longer modifies the csp header when both source-src and default-src directives are missing.

bugs.title: A NLRI with a default route information is not propagated on 'clear ip bgp <neighbor router-id> soft out' command
bugs.symptoms: A default route is not propagated in Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) by a routing framework on a command: 'clear ip bgp <neighbor router-id> soft out'. -- Enter to imi(Integrated Management Interface) shell. [root@hostname:Active:Standalone] config # imish hostname[0]> -- Issue a command inside imish. 10.0.0.4 is neighbor BGP router-id. hostname[0]>clear ip bgp 10.0.0.4 soft out
bugs.conditions: -- There is a BIG-IP system with the following routing configuration: imish output: hostname[0]#sh run ! no service password-encryption ! interface lo ! ... <skip other default information, like interfaces.> ! router bgp 1 bgp router-id 10.17.0.3 bgp graceful-restart restart-time 120 neighbor 10.17.0.4 remote-as 1 ! -- There is a default route, which is advertised by this BGP configuration. Here is one way to check it: hostname[0]:sh ip ospf database ... <skip less important info> AS External Link States Link ID ADV Router Age Seq# CkSum Route Tag 0.0.0.0 10.17.0.3 273 0x80000002 0x5c4e E2 0.0.0.0/0 0 The 'clear ip bgp 10.17.0.4 soft out' command is issued, and there is no NLRI with a default route generated. You can confirm that by running tcpdump and reading what is in the generated Link-state advertisement (LSA), messages or by watching OSPF debug logs. Note: The source from which you gather the default route and advertise it to the neighbors does not matter. It might be the usual BGP route learned from another router, a locally created route, or it might be configured by 'neighbor <neighbor router-id> default-originate'.
bugs.impact: A default-route is not propagated in NLRI by 'soft out' request, even with default-originate configured.
bugs.workaround: There is no specific workaround for 'clear ip bgp <neighbor router-id> soft out' command, but if you want to make routing protocol propagate a NLRI with a default route, you can do either of the following: -- Remove the default route from advertised routes. This workaround is configuration-specific, so there there are no common steps. + If you have default-originate configured for your neighbor, then delete that part of the configuration and re-add it. + If you create a default route as a static route, recreate it. + And so on. The idea is to remove a root of default route generation and then add it back. -- Run a 'soft in' command from your neighbor. If a neighbor you want to propagate a NLRI is a BIG-IP device, or is capable of running this type of command, you can issue a imish command on the neighbor: # neighbor-hostname[0]: clear ip bgp <neighbor router-id> soft in Note: This time, the 'soft in' command requests the NLRIs.
bugs.fix: A NLRI with default route information is successfully propagated on 'clear ip bgp <neighbor router-id> soft out' command.

bugs.title: TCP connection may hang after finished
bugs.symptoms: TCP connections hang. Memory usage increases. TMM restarts. Numerous hanging connections reported similar to the following: -- config # tmsh show sys conn protocol tcp Sys::Connections 165.160.21.1:5854 195.245.21.252:443 any6.any any6.any tcp 449 (tmm: 0) none none 165.160.21.1:5847 195.245.21.252:443 any6.any any6.any tcp 449 (tmm: 0) none none 165.160.21.1:5890 195.245.21.252:443 any6.any any6.any tcp 449 (tmm: 0) none none 165.160.21.1:5855 195.245.21.252:443 any6.any any6.any tcp 449 (tmm: 0) none none 165.160.21.1:5891 195.245.21.252:443 any6.any any6.any tcp 449 (tmm: 0) none none
bugs.conditions: Pool member fails to respond with an ACK to BIG-IP system serverside FIN. The BIG-IP system serverside connection eventually times out, and the clientside connection is orphaned.
bugs.impact: Those connections hang indefinitely (even past the idle timeout). Memory increases, eventually leading to a possible TMM out-of-memory condition, requiring a TMM restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TCP connections no longer hang under these conditions.
bugs.workaround: To delete the orphaned connections, you must restart the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) or restart the BIG-IP system. To restart the BIG-IP system, you can use either of the following procedures: Impact of either workaround: Service will be interrupted. If configured for high availability (HA), the BIG-IP system fails over to another device in the device group. Rebooting the BIG-IP system =========================== 1. Log in to the Advanced Shell (bash). 2. To restart the system, type the following command: reboot Restarting all blades on a VIPRION system ========================================= 1. Log in to bash. 2. To restart all the blades on the VIPRION system, type the following command: clsh shutdown -r now

bugs.title: Windows Logon Integration throws Invalid Handle error
bugs.symptoms: Previously, with Windows Logon Integration, the network logon using dial-up connection failed with invalid handle error: Connecting Error 6: The handle is invalid.
bugs.conditions: Windows Logon Integration is used for dial-up / establish VPN.
bugs.impact: APM end user cannot establish VPN tunnel via Windows Logon Integration.
bugs.fix: The system now handles Windows Logon Integration as expected, so APM end users can establish a VPN tunnel.

bugs.title: Dashboard and tmctl shows incorrect new connections
bugs.symptoms: tmctl, pcap, and dashboard shows incorrect new connections.
bugs.conditions: -- TCP time wait is greater than one second. -- New connections counter on dashboard is a higher number than actual connections.
bugs.impact: A spike occurs that shows twice as many connections than are actually present.
bugs.workaround: Change tcp time_wait to less than one second and new connections increment behavior is intermittent.

bugs.title: Stateless virtual servers does not work for non-standard load-balancing methods
bugs.symptoms: Load-balancing does not work properly for stateless virtual servers with ratio-member load balancing, least-connection methods.
bugs.conditions: Stateless virtual server with ratio-member load balancing or least-connection load balancing method.
bugs.impact: Traffic is processed only with a single pool member. Ratio-load balancing does not work properly.
bugs.workaround: Use the default round-robin load balancing method.

bugs.title: URL lookup queries not working
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, there is no response to a url-categorization query.
bugs.conditions: This might occur under the following conditions: -- When there are duplicate requests using tmsh. -- When the connection is partially closed by the server.
bugs.impact: URL does not get classified. Cannot take any actions against those URLs.
bugs.fix: URL lookup queries now work as expected.

bugs.title: Monpd might load many CSV files such that stats for AVR are not loaded to the database as quickly as expected
