bugs.symptoms: Monpd attempts to load a batch of CSV files that exceed the partition threshold. This might cause Monpd to falsely detect a corrupted database.
bugs.conditions: -- Monpd is down for a given interval, and needs to load a batch of CSV files. -- Monpd gets lower priority for CPU and does not manage loading CSV files within a specific timeframe. -- Some of the reports are more demanding than others, and create CSV files more often, which makes it harder for Monpd to load efficiently.
bugs.impact: Stats for AVR might not be loaded to the database within an expected interval.
bugs.fix: Monpd now checks whether a new partition is required after each CSV file load. When needed, it creates one and aggregates data in the database to avoid this issue.

bugs.title: Install ISO does not boot on BIG-IP VE
bugs.symptoms: The install ISO does not boot on BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.conditions: Attempting to boot a BIG-IP VE from a virtual DVD-ROM drive loaded with an affected ISO file.
bugs.impact: The system does not fully boot and hangs, preventing you from performing an installation or using the live environment for other recovery purposes.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, boot the BIG-IP VE from an ISO file earlier than 14.1.0. If necessary, install that version, and then upgrade to 14.1.0 using the live installer.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with iso images not booting.
bugs.behavior: The fix introduces a behavioral change in the serial console prompt when compared to the legacy console. During DVD, USB, PXE installations, MOS reboots on hardware platforms: The login prompt will read 'localhost login:' before changing to the 'switch_root' prompt. After logging in as root, the prompt changes to 'switch_root'.

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE cannot use MOS for reimaging with 4 GB of memory or less
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to perform a clean installation on a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) using the Maintenance Operating system (MOS) may fail with 'no space left on device'.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The device is a BIG-IP VE with 4 GB of RAM or less. -- You perform a clean installation of BIG-IP 14.1.0, or a clean installation of any earlier version after the system was previously upgraded to BIG-IP 14.1.0. Note: An example of a clean installation is one initiated by the "image2disk --format=volumes" command.
bugs.impact: The installation fails. Once that has occurred, the system automatically reboots into the previously active boot location.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Temporarily assign at least 5 GB of memory to the VE instance for the duration of the installation. You can then lower it after installation is complete. -- Create a fresh image from one of the pre-populated images such as OVA or QCOW2 and migrate a previous configuration to it.

bugs.title: WebUI does not follow best security practices
bugs.symptoms: WebUI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.conditions: Authenticated administrative user access to WebUI.
bugs.impact: WebUI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.fix: WebUI now follows best security practices.

bugs.title: Access policy was not found while creating configuration snapshot.
bugs.symptoms: APMD fails to create configuration snapshot with the following error: --err apmd[16675]: 01490000:3: AccessPolicyProcessor/AccessPolicyProcessor.cpp func: "dispatchEvent()" line: 1195 Msg: EXCEPTION AccessPolicyProcessor/ProfileAccess.cpp line:234 function: snapshotConfigVariables - AccessPolicy ("/Common/myPolicy") not found while creating configuration snapshot!!!! If you attempt to modify the policy in question, the system reports a second error: -- err apmd[16675]: 01490089:3: 00000000: Configuration change notification received for an unknown access profile: /Common/myPolicy
bugs.conditions: If TMM restarts and new access policy is added before TMM is fully up and running.
bugs.impact: Configuration snapshot is not created, and users cannot log on.
bugs.workaround: Recreate the access profile when TMM is stable.

bugs.title: FTP connections to virtual server drop when both sides of data channel are offloaded via FastL4
bugs.symptoms: FTP uploads that are offloaded on both sides drop after the idle timeout period, even though data is flowing.
bugs.conditions: -- FTP virtual server set up with a standard profile and FastL4 offloading. -- Attempt a file upload to the virtual server where both client and server side of the data channel are offloaded.
bugs.impact: Dropped connections; data loss.
bugs.workaround: You can do either of the following: -- Enable Inherit Parent Profile on the FTP profile. -- Turn off FastL4 offloading.
bugs.fix: -- FTP connections to virtual servers no longer drop when both sides of data channel are offloaded via FastL4. -- The output of the following command displays the correct acceleration state: tmsh show sys conn all-properties.

bugs.title: Updated flags for countries that changed their flags since 2010
bugs.symptoms: Old flags for countries that changed their flags since 2010.
bugs.conditions: Requests from one of the following counties: -- Myanmar -- Iraq -- Libya
bugs.impact: Old flag is shown.
bugs.fix: The three flags are now updated in ASM.

bugs.title: Security Policy's Attack Signatures put back into staging after Export/Import in Binary format
bugs.symptoms: Exporting an ASM Security Policy in binary format retains the last updated time of each Attack Signature in the Security Policy. If the Security Policy is then imported into a system where the Attack Signatures have been subsequently updated, any signature that was updated is put back into staging for that Policy.
bugs.conditions: 1) An ASM Security Policy has Attack Signatures that have been removed from staging (enforced). 2) The Policy is exported in binary format. 3) The Policy is imported to a system where the enforced Attack Signatures have been updated by a subsequent ASM Attack Signatures update..
bugs.impact: Any attack signature that has been updated since the policy was exported is be put back into staging.
bugs.workaround: A) Export in XML format instead of binary or B) Re-enforce any staged signatures after import. (The GUI might show signatures as not in staging, but the actual signatures' status are in staging after import of binary.)
bugs.fix: Signatures retain the same enforcement state they had when they were exported even if they were updated on the system.

bugs.title: Missing policy name in exported ASM request details
bugs.symptoms: No Policy name in exported ASM Request details.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when viewing the Security Events Report.
bugs.impact: Missing policy name in request details.
bugs.fix: Policy name is now displayed in exported ASM request details.

bugs.title: Exported requests cannot be opened in Internet Explorer or Edge browser
bugs.symptoms: Any exported report (requests/correlation/learning) cannot be opened in Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE) or Edge brower due to javascript error
bugs.conditions: Viewing an exported report using IE or Edge.
bugs.impact: Unable to view the exported report.
bugs.workaround: Use a different browser.
bugs.fix: Exported files are now visible in all officially supported browsers.

bugs.title: No failover on HA Dual Chassis setup using HA score
bugs.symptoms: On a high availability (HA) set up of two chassis, an HA failover does not occur, despite HA score on Standby being greater than Active.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple blades disabled. -- Both active and standby chassis have same HA score. -- Enabling blades on standby chassis.
bugs.impact: Although enabling blades on the standby chassis causes a higher HA score on the standby (which should cause a failover to occur), HA state remains the same on both chassis. HA failover is not occurring using HA score calculation.

bugs.title: Proactive bot defense falsely detects Selenium on Firefox version 64.x
bugs.symptoms: Proactive bot defense falsely detects Selenium on FireFox version 64.x. ASM end users first have to solve captcha before reaching the website.
bugs.conditions: -- Proactive bot defense is enabled. -- Detect suspicious browsers is configured.
bugs.impact: End users need to solve captcha before reaching the website.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule that overrides proactive action for Firefox version 64.x.
bugs.fix: The system no longer detects Firefox 64.x as if it driven by Selenium.

bugs.title: GUI LTM Policy options disappearing
bugs.symptoms: Listed policies disappear under 'Do the following when traffic is matched' in Local Traffic :: Policies : Policy List :: {Rule Name} when pressing Cancel or Save and opening the list again.
bugs.conditions: Click the Cancel or Save button on the Local Traffic :: Policies : Policy List :: /Common/policy1:rule1 properties page. Here are some specific steps to reproduce this issue (this procedure assumes you have at least one policy with at least one rule defined): 1. Navigate to Local Traffic :: Policies : Policy List :: /Common/policy1:rule1 to open the rule1 properties page. 2. In the section 'Do the following when the traffic is matched', click to open the first dropdown menu. - The system lists all of the items. 3. Click Cancel. 4. Click to reopen the properties page, and click the first dropdown menu. - The system lists fewer of the options. 5. Repeat steps 3 and 4.
bugs.impact: Options disappear from the list each time you click Cancel or Save. Cannot select options because they are no longer visible in the list.
bugs.workaround: To return all options to the list, use the refresh button in the browser. You can also use the following the tmsh command: modify ltm policy Drafts/<policy name> modify { <rule name> { actions add { ...
bugs.fix: Policies no longer disappear under these conditions.

bugs.title: Disabled virtual server accepts and serves traffic after restart
bugs.symptoms: Disabled virtual servers accept traffic after being upgraded to an affected version, or after restarting.
bugs.conditions: 1. A virtual server is configured on pre-v14.1.0. 2. Disable the virtual server. 3. Either upgrade to an affected version, or restart the system.
bugs.impact: The virtual server remains 'Disabled', but it accepts and processes traffic.
bugs.workaround: To correct the behavior, manually enable/disable the virtual server.
bugs.fix: Disabled virtual servers no longer process traffic after a restart.

bugs.title: Reconfiguring an iApp that uses a client SSL profile fails
bugs.symptoms: As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- A virtual server is created but no client SSL profile is applied. -- In the /var/log/ltm file, the system logs messages similar to the following example: err mcpd[6434]: 01b4002b:3: Client SSL profile (/Common/Example.app/Example_client-ssl): the profile has no RSA cert/key pair that can be modified. To add RSA cert/key, please use [cert-key-chain add]
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Attempting to reconfigure an iApp. -- The iApp contains a client SSL profile.
bugs.impact: The system fails to create and apply the client SSL profile to the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, you can temporarily disable SSL in the iApp, and then enable it again. Impact of workaround: Reconfiguring your iApp reconfigures all BIG-IP objects associated with the iApp. This might cause service disruptions to the application the iApp has been deployed for. 1. Navigate to the impacted iApp in GUI: iApps :: Application Services : Applications :: Example. 2. Find the setting associated with the client SSL profile, often titled "How should the BIG-IP system handle SSL traffic?" 3. Change the associated setting to one that does not imply the use of SSL, for example: "Plain text to and from both clients and servers." 4. Press the Reconfigure button. 5. Return to the same question and change the field back to its original setting. 6. Press the Reconfigure button once more.
bugs.fix: Reconfiguring an iApp that uses a client SSL profile now succeeds as expected.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when using RADIUS Accounting agent
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when using RADIUS Accounting agent in either per-session or per-request policy.
bugs.conditions: - APM is provisioned and licensed. - RADIUS Accounting agent is used in either per-session or per-request policy.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when RADIUS Accounting agent is used in the access policy.

bugs.title: STP fails when passed through a BIG-IP system in VLAN group L2 transparent mode with bridge mode enabled
bugs.symptoms: STP error at the STP-enabled switch ports results in the switch ports being blocked.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system configured in VLAN group L2 transparent mode with bridge mode enabled. -- STP traffic between source and sink switch ports passing through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Traffic does not pass through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: -- Disable STP on the switch ports. -- Disable bridge mode on the VLAN group.

bugs.title: Child clientSSL profile's inherit-certkeychain can be unexpectedly set to false after updating the certificate file
bugs.symptoms: Child client SSL profile's inherit-certkeychain can be unexpectedly set to false after updating the certificate file used by the profile.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen intermittently when all of the following conditions are met. -- The client SSL profile is a child client SSL profile profile, i.e., it has a parent client SSL profile. -- The child and the parent profile are using the same certificate. -- The certificate file is updated, for example, by using a command similar to the following: tmsh modify sys file ssl-cert child.crt { source-path file:///config/ssl/ssl.crt/default.crt app-service none cert-validation-options { } issuer-cert none }
bugs.impact: The child client SSL profile may unexpectedly end up using a different cert-key-chain from its parent profile.
bugs.workaround: The inherit-certkeychain flag can be set only in the GUI location: Local Traffic :: Profiles : SSL : Client :: child_profile. In the row 'Configuration: \ Certificate Key Chain', uncheck the checkbox on the right side. That sets inherit-certkeychain to true (or does not customize the cert-key-chain for the child profile). Once the box is unchecked, the Certificate Key Chain field appears greyed out and filled with parent profile's cert-key-chain.
bugs.fix: The child profile's inherit-certkeychain flag is no longer unexpectedly set to false after updating the certificate file.

bugs.title: Portal Access: Image HTML element with source URL like '//some.domain?a=b' cannot be loaded.
bugs.symptoms: Image HTML element with source URL like '//some.domain?a=b' (i.e., no slash following the doman) cannot be loaded via Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with the IMG tag like this:
bugs.impact: Image cannot be loaded.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to add trailing slash to domain name in source URL:

bugs.title: Saving configuration by tmsh is taking a long time and it is being called frequently
bugs.symptoms: -- The system is randomly running auto 'save sys config'. -- Completion of the save operation is taking a longer time than expected.
bugs.conditions: -- No specific steps. This occurs in the course of normal operations. -- The system has a very large configuration.
bugs.impact: The 'tmsh save sys config' command is being called frequently and saving the configuration takes a long time. The length of time it takes to save depends on the size of the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Stop the auto update by running the following command: bigstart stop httpd

bugs.title: iRule : [string first] returns incorrect results when string2 contains null
bugs.symptoms: In an iRule such as 'string first $string1 $string2' returns incorrect results when $string2 contains a null byte and $string1 is not found within $string2. Performing the same search in tclsh, the expected -1 (not found) result is returned.
bugs.conditions: -- 'string first $string1 $string2' iRule. -- string2 in an iRule contains a null byte.
bugs.impact: Operation does not return the expected -1 (not found) result, but instead returns an unexpected, random result.

bugs.title: Tmm crash (assert) during SIP message processing on MRF-SIP-ALG setup.
bugs.symptoms: tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- SIP calls under load. -- MRF-SIP-ALG setup. -- Most of the calls re-use the conn flow.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: If connections reach a threshold value of 64500, the connection is dropped, drop stats are updated, and a log message is reported: Message handling threshold reached on flow.

bugs.title: iRule 'DIAMETER::avp read' command does not work with 'source' option
bugs.symptoms: Configuring a 'source' option with the iRule 'DIAMETER::avp read' command does not work. The operation posts a TCL error in /var/log/ltm logs: err tmm3[11998]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/part1 <MR_INGRESS> - Illegal value (line 1) error Illegal value invoked from within "DIAMETER::avp read 444 source [DIAMETER::avp data get 443 grouped]".
bugs.conditions: Using the 'DIAMETER::avp read' iRule command with a 'source' option.
bugs.impact: 'DIAMETER::avp read' does not work with the 'source' option.
bugs.workaround: Use 'DIAMETER::avp get data' with the 'source' option, and re-create the header part when needed.

bugs.title: When SSL persistence enabled, session cache size cannot be zero.
bugs.symptoms: LTM will reset the connection if SSL persistence enabled + session cache size is set to zero.
bugs.conditions: User can set the session cache size to zero when SSL persistence is enabled.
bugs.impact: LTM will reset the connection is no session ID sent when SSL persistence is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Do not set the session cache size to zero when SSL persistence is enabled.
bugs.fix: The profile validation should validate the session cache size setting when SSL persistence is enabled.

bugs.title: Improved matching of response messages uses end-to-end ID
bugs.symptoms: Some responses incorrectly match requests when their hop-by-hop IDs match. This causes the response to be dropped.
bugs.conditions: Matching hop-by-hop ID.
bugs.impact: Responses rarely match the wrong request, but when they do, they will be dropped.
bugs.fix: Responses are now matched to requests using end-to-end ID as well as hop-by-hop ID. There should be no more incorrect matches.

bugs.title: During failover, an OSPF routing daemon may crash.
bugs.symptoms: With a specific OSPF configuration, during a failover, a peer which is changed from standby to active may experience an ospfd daemon crash.
bugs.conditions: High availability configuration with a routing configuration: 1) access-list with 0.0.0.0/0 filtering: access-list 199 remark test access-list 199 deny ip host 0.0.0.0 host 0.0.0.0 access-list 199 permit ip any any 2) OSPF router with this access-list: router ospf 1 ospf router-id 10.14.0.11 bfd all-interfaces network 10.14.0.0/16 area 0.0.0.1 distribute-list 199 in ! -- The device with this configuration is in the standby state. -- A failover occurs.
bugs.impact: An OSPF daemon crashes, losing routing information and OSPF dynamic routes for a moment while ospfd daemon restarts.
bugs.fix: An ospfd daemon no longer crashes during a failover.

bugs.title: Policy validation error 'All blocking flags are unset' appears even when a violation is set to block
bugs.symptoms: The following policy validation error appears after a policy is applied if no signature sets are set to block (even when a violation is set to block): "All blocking flags are unset while policy is in blocking enforcement mode."
bugs.conditions: -- A policy is applied. -- No signature sets are set to block.
bugs.impact: A policy validation error occurs: 'All blocking flags are unset while policy is in blocking enforcement mode.' This is a cosmetic error and does not indicate an issue with the system.

bugs.title: L2 Transparent mode: Asynchronous mode packet MAC address is changed for certain VLANs
bugs.symptoms: In L2 transparent mode when used in asynchronous mode, the packet gets tagged with the wrong VLAN.
bugs.conditions: -- L2 wire / L2 transparent mode configuration. -- Asynchronous mode.
bugs.impact: The client user receives data with the wrong tag.
bugs.workaround: Do not use async mode for L2 transparent mode.

bugs.title: Possible tmm crash when AFM DoS badactor or attacked-dst or endpoint vector configured
bugs.symptoms: tmm might crash and restart.
bugs.conditions: When AFM DoS badactor or attacked dst is configured on a vector, there is a race condition which can cause tmm to crash. The same race condition is present when single endpoint vectors are configured.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The race condition is now fixed.

bugs.title: Portal Access: Weak F5_isAttr and other predicates
bugs.symptoms: Various web-application misfunctions are possible.
bugs.conditions: User-defined properties with names that are subject to rewriting by Portal Access.
bugs.impact: Client-side web-application misfunction.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule to remove unwanted rewriting.

bugs.title: Policy updates stall and never complete
bugs.symptoms: When applying new or updated ASM policies, the update process stalls and never returns. This error is logged in /var/log/asm: crit perl[7333]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (bd_agent,F5::BdAgent::start): No ack received from BD after 600 seconds -- aborting.
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently when making policy updates.
bugs.impact: The policy update is not applied, and you are unable to make configuration changes.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM: bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: The system now handles the application of new or updated ASM policies so that the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Incompatible libcec may sync from standby to active with automatic hitless upgrade.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may enter a restart loop after an upgrade if automatic hitless upgrade enabled for classification. Example: A standby system is upgraded to v13.1.x while the active is running v12.1.x. Due to automatic hitless upgrade, a standby device might download the latest classification IM signature file on the standby and then sync it with active, which is still running older BIG-IP system software. This results in a library incompatibility on active device.
bugs.conditions: This may happen if the following conditions are true: -- The configuration has Traffic Intelligence automatic classification signature update turned on -- A standby unit in the device group is temporarily booted to a different software version than other units in the group. -- The BIG-IP system is running an AFM or PEM, or PEM Custom DB license.
bugs.impact: Active system may enter a tmm restart loop. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Turn off automatic hitless upgrade for the LTM classification signature-update-schedule during maintenance upgrades that cause a device to run a different software version than other device-group members.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing FastL4 traffic with the Protocol Inspection Profile
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing traffic with a FastL4 virtual with the Protocol Inspection Profile attached.
bugs.conditions: -FastL4 Virtual -Protocol Inspection Profile
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes FastL4 traffic with the Protocol Inspection Profile as expected.

bugs.title: Missing indication when client fails connecting to Security Cloud Services
bugs.symptoms: When Security Cloud Services and Centralized Device ID are enabled, the clients may be blocked from accessing the site if there is no connectivity to the Cloud Services. There is no indication of these failures.
bugs.conditions: -- Security Cloud Services are enabled. -- Centralized Device ID is enabled. -- Device ID is enabled on a Bot Defense profile. -- There is no connectivity between clients and the Cloud Services.
bugs.impact: Connectivity fails with no indication of the failure. Administrators cannot monitor users getting blocked due to connectivity failures with the Cloud Services.
bugs.fix: There is now an indication in the Bot Defense Request Log when clients are blocked due to 'Cloud connectivity failure'. This appears in the 'Challenge Failure Reason' field.

bugs.title: Enable FIPS in prelicensed VE images without requiring a reboot
bugs.symptoms: Must reboot a FIPS-enabled PAYG-Best BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) image to see the FIPS prompt.
bugs.conditions: -- Using FIPS. -- Using PAYG-Best. -- Using VE.
bugs.impact: Must reboot the system to see the FIPS prompt.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system to see the FIPS prompt.
bugs.fix: This release enables FIPS in prelicensed VE images without requiring a reboot.
bugs.behavior: You no longer need to reboot a FIPS-enabled PAYG-Best VE image to see the FIPS prompt.

bugs.title: Frequent zone update notifications may cause TMM to restart
bugs.symptoms: When there are frequent zone update notifications, the watchdog for TMM may trip and TMM crash/restarts. There may also be 'clock advanced' messages in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: - Using DNS express. - DNS zone with allow notify. - Frequent zone NOTIFY messages resulting in zone transfers.
bugs.impact: TMM restart potentially resulting in failing or impacting services. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Frequent zone update notifications no longer cause TMM to restart.

bugs.title: New vlan statistics added.
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh command 'show net vlan' only displays statistics for each VLAN's interface, and not each VLAN's statistics.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when running the command 'tmsh show net vlan'
bugs.impact: You are unable to view PVA statistics.
bugs.fix: The tmsh command 'show net vlan' now displays each vlan's statistics, including PVA statistics.
bugs.behavior: Starting in v16.0.0, the command 'tmsh show net vlan' now outputs each vlan's stats retreived from TMM, including PVA stats, immediately following 'customer-tag' and right before the list of interfaces. Example: [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh sho net vlan ------------------------------------- Net::Vlan: external ------------------------------------- Interface Name external Mac bugs.title: New SNMP MIB, sysVlanIfcStat, for vlan statistics.
bugs.symptoms: V16.0.0 and v15.1.2 have a new SNMP MIB, sysVlanIfcStat, for VLAN statistics. Previously there were no ways to retrieve PVA statistics for each VLAN.
bugs.conditions: Viewing VLAN statistics through SNMP queries.
bugs.impact: PVA stats are not displayed.
bugs.fix: SysVlanIfcStat includes many of the same fields from the ifXTable, with a few additions. Notably, the new MIB includes PVA statistics.

bugs.title: Packet data may fail CRC checks due to hardware (HSB) issue
bugs.symptoms: Issues in the HSB may cause packet data to fail CRC (TCP checksums). This can be confirmed by observing the CRC error rate reported by the HSB, along with confirming that the packet data was correct when it arrived at the BIG-IP system by using a tcpdump capture. This issue persists until the HSB is rebooted, which appears to clear the condition.
bugs.conditions: Network traffic is received by the BIG-IP system. It is unknown what causes the issue in the HSB.
bugs.impact: Incoming packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Reboot to clear the state of the HSB.

bugs.title: AVR reporting UI does not follow best practices
bugs.symptoms: The AVR reporting UI does not follow best practices.
bugs.conditions: Administrative access to the AVR reporting web UI.
bugs.impact: Unexpected HTML output.
bugs.workaround: The AVR reporting UI does not follow best practices.
bugs.fix: The AVR reporting UI now follows best practices.

bugs.title: OSPF inter-process redistribution might break OSPF route redistribution of various types.
bugs.symptoms: Enabling inter-process OSPF route redistribution might cause overall problems with OSPF route redistribution.
bugs.conditions: OSPF is configured with inter-process OSPF route redistribution, for example: router ospf network 0.0.0.0/0 area 0 redistribute kernel redistribute ospf 1234 <--- !
bugs.impact: Routes might not be redistributed and will not be present in OSPF database. This affects all redistribution types (kernel, static, etc..)
bugs.workaround: Do not use inter-process OSPF route redistribution.
bugs.fix: Inter-process OSPF route redistribution is working properly.

bugs.title: Standby TMM my crash while processing mirrored TLS traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the standby TMM may crash while processing mirrored TLS traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with server-side SSL -- Connection mirroring enabled.
bugs.impact: High availability (HA) connection mirroring fails. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes TLS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: iControl REST API adds unnecessary escape character (\) to URL if the URL contains a wildcard character
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST API adds unnecessary escaping to URL if it contains a wildcard character.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating configuration using iControl REST API. -- Configuration includes a URL containing wildcard character.
bugs.impact: iControl REST API adds unnecessary escape character (\) to URL. The resulting configuration may not be interpreted correctly by the data plane because the request URL does not match with the configuration. -- One specific example: # restcurl -u admin:<password> -d '{"name":"/vdesk/test*","type":"wildcard"}' "https://host.mgmt.siterequest.com/mgmt/tm/security/anti-fraud/profile/fps_logonpage_wildcard/urls" -- Results in this: urls { /vdesk/test\\* { priority 2 type wildcard } } -- Instead of the expected: urls { /vdesk/test* { priority 2 type wildcard } }
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to add the configuration.

bugs.title: Request Log: wrong titles in details for Illegal Request Length and Illegal Query String Length violations
bugs.symptoms: Illegal Request Length uses Illegal Query String Length template and vice versa, so the incorrect titles are shown in violation details.
bugs.conditions: Open details of Illegal Request Length or Illegal Query String Length violation in request log.
bugs.impact: Illegal Request Length uses Illegal Query String Length template and vice versa. Only the titles are wrong. The actual requests are recorded correctly.
bugs.fix: Correct templates are now used for Illegal Request Length and Illegal Query String Length violations, so the correct titles show.

bugs.title: Traffic processing may be stopped on VE trunk after tmm restart
bugs.symptoms: Trunk interface members might be missing from tmm after tmm restart on BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.conditions: -- Using trunks on VE. -- tmm restarts.
bugs.impact: No traffic processing after tmm restart.
bugs.workaround: Remove the interfaces from the trunk and re-add them: # tmsh modify net trunk <trunk name> interfaces none # tmsh modify net trunk <trunk name> interfaces add { <interface1> <interface2> }
bugs.fix: Traffic processing on trunks is stable after tmm restart.

bugs.title: Timer processing taking too long
bugs.symptoms: The SFP status process takes too long, causing the timer to fire too infrequently.
bugs.conditions: On i15xxx platforms the timer interval is too long due to processing inside the timer.
bugs.impact: It will take the system longer to notice changes to SFP status.
bugs.fix: The timer processing has been fixed so the timer interval is now correct.

bugs.title: Dynamic Routes stats row does not appear in the UI
bugs.symptoms: From UI, when navigate to the following path: Statistics ›› Module Statistics : Local Traffic ›› Profiles Summary : Diameter Router. The stat for 'Current number of dynamic routes' does not appear.
bugs.conditions: Any condition
bugs.impact: Unable to view dynamic routes statistics in the GUI
bugs.workaround: Look at the statistics from tmsh
bugs.fix: Dynamic Routes stats row is displayed properly in the UI

bugs.title: Category lookup returns wrong category on CONNECT traffic through SSLO
bugs.symptoms: Category lookup returns wrong category on CONNECT traffic through F5 SSL Orchestrator (SSLO).
bugs.conditions: -- Outbound deployment configured in SSLO, where SSLO behaves as a transparent proxy. -- A policy has a branch to lookup category using HTTP Connect. -- An HTTPS client generates HTTPS traffic via an explicit proxy on local network with private address through SSLO as the gateway.
bugs.impact: Category Match is not performed, resulting in fallback branch to be taken.
bugs.fix: Category lookup now works correctly in this scenario.

bugs.title: iRule audit logs may be written to separate files
bugs.symptoms: Only the first line of an iRule audit log is written into /var/log/audit. The rest of the iRule is logged to /var/log/messages.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when iRule audit logging is enabled and iRule events are triggered.
bugs.impact: Snippets of iRules appear in unexpected locations.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, if you have sensitive information in your iRules and want to prevent it from appearing in audit logs, you can disable audit logging.

bugs.title: Typo in named errdefs
bugs.symptoms: The errdefs string for NAMED_CANCEL_ERR has a typo in it - says "chages" instead of "changes"
bugs.conditions: Whenever the error condition occurred and the error message was shown.
bugs.impact: Misspelling in error output.
bugs.workaround: NA.
bugs.fix: Fixed a typo.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 connections may leak memory if server-side connection not established
bugs.symptoms: Xhead and xdata memory caches grow over time when HTTP/2 traffic is present. Eventual performance degradation and potential traffic outage due to memory exhaustion.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 configured with HTTP Router profile. -- Configuration or network issues which prevent server-side connection from being established.
bugs.impact: Memory leakage over time may result in performance degradation and eventual traffic outage if TMM restarts due to memory exhaustion.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 connections no longer leak memory when server-side connection establishment fails.

bugs.title: UCS creation might fail during frequent config save transactions
bugs.symptoms: If 'tmsh save sys config' is run simultaneously with 'tmsh save sys ucs <file>', there is the possibility of a race condition where a file gets scheduled to be added to the UCS file, but gets deleted by the save-config before it actually gets saved.
bugs.conditions: -- Run 'save sys config' at the same time as 'save sys ucs <file>' in tmsh. -- Files are getting added by one tmsh command, yet deleted by the other. For example, when deleting a file that has not been saved to the configuration, while the system tried to create a UCS that contains that to-be-deleted file. Note: There are many operations in which 'save sys config' is performed internally, so running the 'save sys ucs <file>' operation might encounter the timing error any time, even when you are not manually running 'save sys config'.
bugs.impact: The UCS is not created, and system posts messages similar to the following: -- config/bigip_base.conf/: Cannot stat: No such file or directory. -- Exiting with failure status due to previous errors. -- Operation aborted. This is a rare, timing-related occurrence. Even though the 'save sys ucs <file>' aborts and logs errors, simply re-running the command is likely to succeed.
bugs.workaround: Re-run the 'save sys ucs <file>' after it aborts. Nothing else needs to be changed or restored.
bugs.fix: The race condition is avoided and the 'save sys ucs <file>' now succeeds due to files removed by 'save sys config'.

bugs.title: Large packets silently dropped on VE mlxvf5 devices
bugs.symptoms: Jumbo frames are disabled by default for Mellanox ConnectX-4 and ConnectX-5 devices using the mlxvf5 driver (i.e., many BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) configurations). Packets larger than 1500 bytes are silently dropped. Only packets up to 1500 bytes are supported when jumbo framers are disabled.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE with SR-IOV using Mellanox ConnectX-4 or ConnectX-5 NICs. Typically this represents VE configurations running on private Cloud environments such as VMware, KVM, OpenStack, and others. Note: You can determine your environment by running the following commands: # tmctl -d blade tmm/device_probed # tmctl -d blade xnet/device_probed Configurations exhibiting this issue either: 1. reports a value of 'mlxvf5' in the driver_in_use column in tmm/device_probed, and possibly reports 'tmctl: xnet/device_probed: No such table.' 2. reports a value of 'xnet' in the driver_in_use column in tmm/device_probed, and a value of 'mlxvf5' in the driver_in_use column in xnet/device_probed.
bugs.impact: Packets larger than 1500 bytes are dropped without a warning.
bugs.workaround: Enable jumbo frames and then restart tmm. 1. Add the following line to /config/xnet_init.tcl: drvcfg mlxvf5 jumbo_support 1 2. Restart tmm: bigstart restart tmm Important: There are two possible mlxvf5 drivers. It is possible to enable jumbo frames only for the xnet-based driver. Important: Enabling jumbo frames causes a performance loss for 1500-byte-size packet, but offers higher throughput at lower CPU usage for larger packets. Note that 1500 bytes is the most common size for internet packets.

bugs.title: TMM cores in certain scenarios with HTTP/2 virtual server
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores when attempting to reset a stream. Parent connection may be resetting and going away, race conditions may lead to TMM core in HTTP MR proxy.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with HTTP/2, HTTP, TCP, SSL and httprouter profiles. Race conditions when resetting connections.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Clock advanced messages when modifying a virtual server with 1000 SSL profiles
bugs.symptoms: The system posts clock advanced messages when modifying a virtual server. You might also experience an Active/Active situation because tmm might be too busy to send high availability (HA) packets. The messages appear similar to the following: notice tmm1[12549]: 01010029:5: Clock advanced by 556 ticks
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server has 1000 or more SSL profiles defined. -- A client SSL profile gets its defaults from another profile. -- You change the cipher settings in that other profile.
bugs.impact: The system logs clock advanced messages, and sod kills tmm when you run the following command: tmsh load sys config Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, do the following: -- Remove some of the SSL profiles from the virtual server. -- Reset the cipher settings to default.

bugs.title: Remote auth: PAM_LDAP buffer too small errors
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to log into the BIG-IP system using an LDAP account. The system might log the following message in /var/log/secure: -- crit httpd[28010]: pam_ldap(httpd:account): buffer 'buffer_size' too small. Note: This message might not be logged for all occurrences of this issue.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- Remote-LDAP authentication is configured. -- There is a user account with attributes longer than 255 characters in length. -- That user attempts a logon to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: LDAP authentication not working properly.
bugs.workaround: Configure user accounts with attributes shorter than 255 characters.
bugs.fix: LDAP authentication and authorization now succeeds for users under these conditions.

bugs.title: [GTM] bigip_add password prompt for IPv4-mapped IPv6 address
bugs.symptoms: After running the big_ip add script without a specifying a server address, the host address posted in the ssh password prompt is an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address for IPv4 servers. For example: Enter root password for 0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:FFFF:0A3C:010A
bugs.conditions: Run bigip_add without a server address, when the host address is an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address.
bugs.impact: There is no way to tell what the actual server name is without converting the IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses back to an IPv4 to find which password to enter, for example: 0A3C:010A to 10.60.1.10
bugs.workaround:
To workaround this, edit the bigip_add script. IMPORTANT: Make sure to back up the bigip_add script before making modifications. 1. Make /usr folder writable # mount -o rw,remount /usr 2. Backup bigip_add: # cp /usr/local/bin/bigip_add /shared/tmp/bigip_add.backup 3. Edit bigip_add by adding different 'print' output for IPv4 servers. Replace this: < print "Enter $ruser password for $ip if prompted
"; With something similar to this: > if ($ip =~ /0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:FFFF:/) { > my $display_ipv4 = ipv6_to_ipv4($ip); > print "Enter $ruser password for $display_ipv4 if prompted
"; > } else { > print "Enter $ruser password for $ip if prompted
"; > } NOTE: Do not modify the actual value for $ip. Below is an example diff: # diff /shared/tmp/bigip_add.backup /usr/local/bin/bigip_add 18a19 > 43a45,51 > sub ipv6_to_ipv4 > { > my $in_addr = $_[0]; > my @ipv6 = split /:/, $in_addr; > > my $ipv6_part1 = hex ($ipv6[6]); > my $ipv6_part2 = hex($ipv6[7]); 44a53,60 > my $ipv4_1=scalar($ipv6_part1>>8); > my $ipv4_2=scalar($ipv6_part1&0xff); > my $ipv4_3=scalar($ipv6_part2>>8); > my $ipv4_4=scalar($ipv6_part2&0xff); > > my $ipv4 = "${ipv4_1}.${ipv4_2}.${ipv4_3}.${ipv4_4}"; > return $ipv4; > } 75d90 < 152c167,173 < print "Enter $ruser password for $ip if prompted
"; --- > > if ($ip =~ /0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:FFFF:/) { > my $display_ipv4 = ipv6_to_ipv4($ip); > print "Enter $ruser password for $display_ipv4 if prompted
"; > } else { > print "Enter $ruser password for $ip if prompted
"; > } 179d199 <

bugs.title: No DIAMETER Disconnect-Peer-Request message sent when TMM is shutting down
bugs.symptoms: When TMM is shutting down with active DIAMETER connections, it does not send out any Disconnect-Peer-Request messages to its DIAMETER pool members.
bugs.conditions: - DIAMETER in use. - Active connections from the BIG-IP system to its DIAMETER pool members. - TMM is shutting down.
bugs.impact: The remote server is not notified of the change in DIAMETER peer status.

bugs.title: /var/log logical volume may run out of space due to agetty error message in /var/log/secure
bugs.symptoms: An agetty error message is output to the /var/log/secure log fil every 10 seconds while the instance remains on: agetty[<process_id>]: /dev/tty0 ttyS0: No such file or directory.
bugs.conditions: This agetty error message is an issue on all BIG-IP Virtual Edition and Cloud instances. It is not configuration-dependent.
bugs.impact: This may fill the /var/log/secure log file. When /var/log is full, certain system services may degrade or become unresponsive (e.g., DNS).
bugs.workaround: Manually extend the /var/log logical volume. For more information, see Increase disk space for BIG-IP VE :: https://clouddocs.f5.com/cloud/public/v1/shared/disk_space.html.
bugs.fix: The issue causing the agetty error message in /var/log/secure has been resolved.

bugs.title: Phonehome_upload crashes when Automatic Phone Home is disabled
bugs.symptoms: When Automatic Phone Home is disabled (this is not the default), the process will crash when it is invoked by the system once-a-month.
bugs.conditions: -- Automatic Phone Home is disabled (the default is "enabled")
bugs.impact: The process crashes and generates a core file.
bugs.workaround: Edit root's crontab file using "crontab -e" and add a '#' at the beginning of the line for "/usr/bin/phonehome_upload" Note that this workaround: -- needs to be applied to each device in a device group separately -- needs to be applied to each blade in a VIPRION (or VIPRION-based vCMP guest) separately -- needs to be reapplied after software installations

bugs.title: HTTPS connection error from Chrome when BADOS TLS signatures configured
bugs.symptoms: HTTPS connection error occurs. The system posts the following ltm.log warnings: -- warning tmm1[25112]: 01260009:4: Connection error: ssl_basic_crypto_cb:694: Decryption error (20) -- warning tmm1[25112]: 01260009:4: Connection error: hud_ssl_handler:1941: codec alert (20)
bugs.conditions: -- BADOS TLS signatures configured. -- DoS profile is attached to a virtual server. -- Using Google Chrome browser.
bugs.impact: HTTPS virtual server is not responsive.
bugs.workaround: Turn off TLS signatures flag.
bugs.fix: HTTPS connection error no longer occurs when connecting from Chrome to virtual server with TLS signature BADOS protection.

bugs.title: SSLO does not deliver content generated/originated from inline device
bugs.symptoms: If any inline service acting as a proxy generates content for the client while resetting the server side connection, then the client might not see the content, and will instead see a reset.
bugs.conditions: -- F5 SSL Orchestrator (SSLO) with inline services intercepting requests and replying without letting the content go to back-end server. -- Inline services resetting the back-end connection
bugs.impact: Client receives a reset instead of a redirect or error page.
bugs.fix: Clients now receive the content that the inline device generates.

bugs.title: Memory leak when using lots of iApps
bugs.symptoms: Scriptd creates open files that are never closed by improperly closing sockets before exiting. This eventually results in errors that there are too many open files which can overload the system.
bugs.conditions: Run a large number of iApps on a system for a long period of time. You can determine if you are affected by this by using the following command: lsof | grep scriptd |grep socket |wc -l After it has run for a while you will notice that this number is slowly growing as scriptd processes exit without closing their sockets appropriately.
bugs.impact: Constantly increasing use of system resources.

bugs.title: Corrupted customization group on target after updating logon page agent field on source device and config sync
bugs.symptoms: After making changes to the logon page agent field, performing config sync to another device and opening the logon agent in VPE on the sync target device encounters an error.
bugs.conditions: 1. Form a failover device group with two devices. 2. On one device, create an access policy with logon page agent. Initiate config sync to sync the policy to other devices. Verify everything is correct on target device (specifically: open VPE for the policy, Logon Page is in the policy, click on the agent, and edit box appears without issue). 3. On source device, launch VPE for the policy, click on Logon Page agent, make changes to Agent (e.g., choose 'password' type for field3. Save the change and make a config sync again. 4. Go to target device, open VPE for the policy, and click on Logon Page is in the policy.
bugs.impact: Config is not synced properly to another device in the device group.
bugs.workaround: In addition to changing the logon page field, also make a change in the 'Customization' section (e.g., update the text for Logon Page Input Field).
bugs.fix: Target device receives identical configuration as source one after config sync after user updates logon page field in logon agent editing dialog.

bugs.title: [App Tunnel] 'URI sanitization' error
bugs.symptoms: URI sanitization error with app tunnel (application tunnel). The system posts messages similar to the following: -- APM log: warning tmm[19703]: 01490586:4: /Common/AP-AD:Common:ff776e4a: Invalid Resource Access For RESOURCENAME. RST due to URI sanitization -- LTM log: err tmm[19703]: 01230140:3: RST sent from 10.0.0.1:80 to 10.0.0.1:228, [0x2263e2c:7382] Unrecognized resource access (RESOURCENAME)
bugs.conditions: Access Policy that includes a 'Logon Page' and 'Advanced Resource Assign' (full webtop and app tunnel).
bugs.impact: APM does not send a response after receiving a request to 'GET /vdesk/resource_app_tunnels_info.xml'.

bugs.title: TMM crash and core
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and generates a core file under unknown conditions.
bugs.conditions: The conditions required for this issue to occur are not well understood, but might be related to a MCP message handling failure (during virtual server creation) in an AAM with LTM configuration. The issue might be related to an unsupported configuration, as follows: The BIG-IP system does not prevent you from configuring a server-side iSession profile and a OneConnect profile on the same virtual server. This is not a valid configuration, however. Virtual server configuration should allow either a server-side iSession profile or a OneConnect profile, but not both.
bugs.impact: TMM crash and core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Correct the misconfiguration (specifically, OneConnect and iSession being mutually exclusive features), and try the operation again.

bugs.title: No support of TMUI (GUI) in 1 or 2 CORE 2GB VE instance
bugs.symptoms: Cannot execute TMUI functions (such as activate license, configure net and LTM items etc.) because Tomcat has insufficient memory. TMUI shows the following error message: Internal Server Error. The server encountered an internal error or misconfiguration and was unable to complete your request. ...
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Virtual Edition deployed with 1 or 2 virtual CPUs and 2 GB memory.
bugs.impact: You are unable to manage BIG-IP Virtual Edition using TMUI.
bugs.workaround: Configure more memory using the following command: setdb Provision.Tomcat.extraMB 100 Note: Less or more extra memory might work too.

bugs.title: In MOS, the 'image2disk' utility with the '-format' option does not function properly
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system boots, mcpd continually restarts.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you issue the 'image2disk' command with the '-format' option in the MOS (Maintenance Operating System) shell.
bugs.impact: When the system boots, it cannot become active.
bugs.workaround: In the MOS shell, do not issue the 'image2disk' utility with the '-format' option. You can achieve the same result by following the shell guidance. To begin, type 'start<enter>'. If the system is already in the defective state, use this shell command, and then reboot: touch /.tmos.platform.init The problem should be resolved.
bugs.fix: In MOS, running 'image2disk' with the '-format' option no longer causes continuous mcpd restarts.

bugs.title: mcpd can restart on secondary blades if a policy is created, published, and attached to a vs in a single transaction
bugs.symptoms: On a VIPRION cluster, if a single transaction creates a policy with the name Drafts/NAME, publishes the policy, and attaches the policy to a virtual server, mcpd restarts on the secondary blades.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION chassis with more than one blade. -- Single mcp transaction that: * Creates a policy with 'Drafts/' as part of the policy name. * Publishes that policy. * Attaches that policy to a virtual server, either in the same transaction or a later transaction.
bugs.impact: mcpd restarts on all secondary blades of a cluster.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Do not create policies with 'Drafts/' in the name. -- Do not create and publish a policy in the same transaction.

bugs.title: peer-cert-mode set to 'always' does not work when client-ssl is enabled with session-ticket
bugs.symptoms: When a session is restored using a session-ticket, the peer-cert-mode setting is not acknowledged.
bugs.conditions: -- Session tickets are enabled. -- The peer-cert-mode in the client SSL profile is set to 'always'. -- A session is restored using a ticket.
bugs.impact: The SSL client is validated only once, instead of each time.
bugs.workaround: Disable session ticket.
bugs.fix: If peer-cert-mode is set to always, session tickets are not issued. This is the same behavior as is seen with session ID resumption.

bugs.title: Deleted APM cookies missing 'secure' and 'HttpOnly' flags
bugs.symptoms: Returned deleted cookies are missing 'secure' and/or 'HttpOnly' flags.
bugs.conditions: When APM cookies with 'secure' and 'HttpOnly' flags are deleted, those flags are missing in response Set-Cookie: headers.
bugs.impact: Some vulnerability scanners may detect that as security issue.
bugs.workaround: iRule like the next: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { foreach mycookie [HTTP::cookie names] { HTTP::cookie secure $mycookie enable HTTP::cookie httponly $mycookie enable } }
bugs.fix: Preserved the flags 'secure' and 'HttpOnly' for deleted APM cookies

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG: Mirrored media flows timeout on standby after 2 minutes
bugs.symptoms: The media flows get terminated after the UDP idle timeout expires on a Standby device.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) configuration. -- SIP media calls on a SIP-ALG with SNAT feature enabled.
bugs.impact: SIP calls fail to deliver media when HA failover occurs.
bugs.workaround: Partial mitigation is to set the UDP idle timeout to a higher value.
bugs.fix: Properly set SIP ALG media pinhole connection flags so that to not time out due to inactivity on the next active device.

bugs.title: UDP / DNS monitor marking node down
bugs.symptoms: The UDP / DNS monitor marks nodes down.
bugs.conditions: -- UDP or DNS monitor configured. -- Interval is multiple of timeout. -- The response is delayed by over one interval.
bugs.impact: Pool member is marked down.
bugs.workaround: Increase the interval to be greater than the response time of the server.

bugs.title: Unstable asm_config_server after upgrade, 'Event dispatcher aborted'
bugs.symptoms: Ignored suggestions for Multiple decoding or HTTP Protocol Settings present after upgrading a unit to 14.1.0 can cause the asm_config_server and pabnagd processes to enter restart loops.
bugs.conditions: 1) On a 13.1.x system send traffic that will generate suggestions for Max Decoding Passes, Maximum Headers, and/or Maximum Parameters. 2) Set those Suggestions to be Ignored. 3) Upgrade to 14.1.0.
bugs.impact: -- Multiple asm_config_server restarts. -- System instability, including inability to manage ASM settings or use traffic learning. -- No local logging.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: A) Delete any such ignored suggestions using the following SQL command: > DELETE FROM PL_SUGGESTIONS WHERE element_type IN (7,193,75); B) Delete any such ignored suggestions before upgrade using the GUI/REST/SQL.
bugs.fix: The system now handles removed Entity types during upgrade for Ignored Suggestions: Ignored suggestions for Multiple decoding or HTTP Protocol Settings are removed during upgrade. You must reconfigure the Ignore settings after upgrade.
bugs.behavior: Refactoring in 14.1.0 modified the functionality of the following Entity types: Max Decoding Passes, Maximum Headers, and/or Maximum Parameters. Ignored suggestions for Multiple decoding or HTTP Protocol Settings are removed during upgrade, so you must reconfigure the Ignore settings after upgrade.

bugs.title: IPsec connection can fail if connflow expiration happens before IKE encryption
bugs.symptoms: IKEv2 negotiation fails, and tmm log shows the following error: notice [INTERNAL_ERR]: ikev2....: Invalid BIG-IP flow context
bugs.conditions: Unusual timing that results in connflow expiration immediately preceding Diffie Hellman generation.
bugs.impact: IKE Negotiation fails, so an SA cannot be established.
bugs.fix: Missing connection context is now replaced, so IKE negotiation can continue.

bugs.title: A UDP DNS packet may incorrectly match a BDoS signature if such a packet was queued up due to ingress shaper
bugs.symptoms: A UDP DNS packet may incorrectly match a BDoS signature if such a packet was queued up due to ingress shaper. In the worst case, this incorrect signature match might drop the packet.
bugs.conditions: AFM is enabled and it receives multiple (back-to-back-to-back) UDP DNS packets, which (due to ingress shaper) might cause queueing for some of the packets in the same data path thread.
bugs.impact: In this case, when the queued packet is later picked up for further processing, it may incorrectly match a BDoS signature (that would not have otherwise matched if this packet was not queued). A UDP DNS packet may match an incorrect signature and thus might be incorrectly dropped by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: UDP DNS packets never match an incorrect BDoS signature, even if such packets are queued due to ingress shaper.

bugs.title: Ephemeral pool members not created after DNS flap and address record changes
bugs.symptoms: When using FQDN node/pool members, ephemeral pool members may not be created for one or more pools after address records change on the DNS server. Once this condition occurs, ephemeral pool members are no longer created for a given FQDN name in the affected pool.
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur under rare timing conditions when the following factors are present: -- Using FQDN nodes/pool members. -- Changes occur in the address records on the DNS server, causing new ephemeral nodes/pool members to be created and old ephemeral nodes/pool members to be deleted. -- There is a temporary loss of connectivity to/responsiveness from the DNS server.
bugs.impact: When this issue occurs, the affected pool may be left with no active pool members. In that case, virtual servers targeting the affected pool become unavailable and stop passing traffic.
bugs.workaround: When this issue occurs, the ability to create ephemeral pool members can be restored by either of the following actions: 1. Restart the dynconfd daemon: bigstart restart dynconfd 2. Delete and re-create the FQDN template pool member using the following two commands: tmsh mod ltm pool affected_pool members del { fqdn_pool_member:port } tmsh mod ltm pool affected_pool members add { fqdn_pool_member:port { additional field values } } To ensure that a pool contains active members even if this issue occurs, populate each pool with more than one FQDN pool member, or with an additional non-FQDN pool member.

bugs.title: SAML metadata import (SP or IdP) fails if the metadata file has both SPSSODescriptor and IdPSSODescriptor
bugs.symptoms: If the SAML SP or IDP metadata has both SPSSODescriptor and IdPSSODescriptor tags, the import fails with errors like this: The metadata file '/var/tmp/1547120861955.upload' being used to create SAML IdP connector 'Kismet' is an SP metadata file.
bugs.conditions: -- SP or IDP metadata file has both SPSSODescriptor and IdPSSODescriptor tags and -- Attempt to import them to create SP or IdP connector objects.
bugs.impact: Metadata import is not successful.
bugs.workaround: Use the following workarounds, as appropriate: -- When importing SP metadata, remove all IDPSSODescriptor tags from the metadata file. -- When importing IDP metadata, remove all SPSSODescriptor tags from the metadata file.
bugs.fix: Metadata import is now successful when both SPSSODescriptor and IdPSSODescriptor tags are present, and the connector object is created.

bugs.title: UDP monitor not behaving properly on different ICMP reject codes.
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected or improper pool/node member status.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system receives the ICMP rejection code as icmp-net/host-unreachable.
bugs.impact: The monitor might consider a server available when some type of ICMP rejection has been received that is not port unreachable.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use UDP monitors configured with a receive string. -- Do not use UDP monitors.

bugs.title: v14.1.0.5 includes Guided Configuration 4.1
bugs.symptoms: Guided Configuration is not upgraded automatically with each release; it must be manually upgraded between versions. It should be bundled into the release. Version 14.1.0.5 includes Guided Configuration 4.1.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading Guided Configuration.
bugs.impact: Have to manually upgrade Guided Configuration.
bugs.workaround: Manually upgrade Guided Configuration.
bugs.fix: Guided Configuration v4.1 is bundled into BIG-IP software v14.1.0.5 and no longer requires manual upgrade.
bugs.behavior: Guided Configuration v4.1 is bundled into BIG-IP software v14.1.0.5. For versions earlier than 14.1.0.5 (e.g., 14.1.0.0), you had to upgrade Guided Configuration manually. That is no longer necessary.

bugs.title: TMM crash due to missing classification category
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when 'Thin_Client' category is used. The tmm2 log contains messages: -- notice panic: ../modules/hudfilter/gpa/gpa_config.c:507: Assertion "Category does not exist" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- TMM is configured for debug mode (which might occur in cases described in K11490: Configuring the Traffic Management Microkernel to use debug mode :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K11490). -- There is a classification configured with a category that does not exist.
bugs.impact: TMM restart loop. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Change the category to something that exists to load tmm.debug.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with 'Thin_client' category.

bugs.title: ZebOS might miss kernel routes after mcpd deamon restart
bugs.symptoms: After an mcpd daemon restart, sometimes (in ~30% of cases) ZebOS is missing some of kernel routes (virtual addresses). One of the most common scenario is a device reboot.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing is configured. -- Virtual address is created and Route Advertisement is configured: imish -e 'sh ip route kernel' -- mcpd daemon is restarted or device is rebooted.
bugs.impact: The kernel route (virtual address) is not added to the ZebOS routing table and cannot be advertised.
bugs.workaround: There are several workarounds; here are two: -- Restart the tmrouted daemon: bigstart restart tmrouted -- Recreate the affected virtual address.
bugs.fix: The kernel route is now present in the ZebOS routing table after mcpd daemon restart.

bugs.title: Non-IPsec listener traffic, i.e. monitoring traffic, can be translated to incorrect source address
bugs.symptoms: When IPsec traffic is processed by a FastL4 profile, which is not related to an IPsec listener, and is send out via a gateway pool or a dynamic route, the source address of this traffic can be erroneously changed to 127.0.0.x.
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec traffic is processed by a FastL4 profile, which is not related to an IPSEC listener. -- The traffic is sent out via a gateway pool or a dynamic route.
bugs.impact: The incorrect source address is used.
bugs.fix: The IPsec traffic uses now the correct IP source-address.

bugs.title: Individual policy that cannot be deleted, can be if part of multi-policy delete
bugs.symptoms: A policy that cannot be deleted individually can be deleted in a multiple-policy delete operation.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM policies with dependencies that cannot be deleted (LTM dependencies, parent policies with children, etc.). -- Attempt to delete the policies individually. -- Attempt to delete the policies as part of a multiple-policy delete operation.
bugs.impact: Policies with dependencies are deleted.
bugs.workaround: Delete policies one at a time.
bugs.fix: A policy that should not be deleted individually now cannot be deleted in a multiple-policy delete operation.

bugs.title: OAuth JWT Issuer claim requires URI format
bugs.symptoms: APM currently expects the OAuth JSON web tokens (JWT) Issuer claim to be in the URI format: -- JWT-Config does not allow Issuer setting unless it is in the URI format. -- The issuer value in the incoming token is expected to be in the URI format and should match with the Issuer setting in the JWT-Config.
bugs.conditions: OAuth JWT Issuer claim in the URI format for JWT access token and ID token.
bugs.impact: As per RFC 7519, 'iss' claim value is a case-sensitive string containing a StringOrURI value. To comply with RFC 7519, basically allowing any string value in the Issuer claim, APM should ease this validation.
bugs.fix: JWT config issuer Validation is removed to allow a string or URI value for the JWT issuer.

bugs.title: MCPD crash
bugs.symptoms: mcpd crashes on out of memory.
bugs.conditions: A memory leak occurs when the following tmsh command is run: tmsh reset-stats ltm virtual
bugs.impact: MCPD can run out of memory and crash. Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Try to use the reset-stats tmsh command sparingly.
bugs.fix: A memory leak that occurred when running the command 'tmsh reset-stats ltm virtual' has been fixed.

bugs.title: [api-status-warning] ltm/classification/signature-update-schedule is deprecated
bugs.symptoms: A tmsh warning is logged to /var/log/ltm: warning tmsh[29177]: 01420013:4: [api-status-warning] ltm/classification/signature-update-schedule is deprecated.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs when system is booting and when config is saved.
bugs.impact: The benign message is reported. This warning is benign, so you can safely ignore it.
bugs.fix: Fixed an erroneous warning that signature-update-schedule is deprecated that was occurring on system start.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP might respond incorrectly to ICMP echo requests or incorrectly add/remove dynamic routes to a virtual-address
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system unexpectedly responds to ICMP echo requests to a virtual-address that is unavailable, or unexpectedly does not respond to ICMP echo requests to a virtual-address that is available. The BIG-IP system fails to remove a dynamic route for a virtual-address that is unavailable or fails to add a dynamic route for a virtual-address that is available.
bugs.conditions: -- There are multiple virtual servers associated with a virtual address. -- The virtual-address icmp-echo is set to 'all' or 'any'. -- The virtual-address route-advertisement is set to 'all' or 'any'.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP might respond incorrectly to ICMP echo requests sent to a virtual-address. -- If the virtual-address icmp-echo is set to 'all' or 'any', the BIG-IP may not respond correctly after a virtual-address availability change. -- If the virtual-address route-advertisement is set to 'all' or 'any', the route for the virtual-address may not advertise properly after a virtual-address availability change. The BIG-IP might fail to insert or remove a dynamic route for a virtual-address. This might cause the network to direct traffic to a down virtual-address or alternatively, not direct traffic to an up virtual-address.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now responds correctly to ICMP echo requests and correctly adds/removes dynamic routes to a virtual-address, as appropriate.

bugs.title: DNS express in restart loop, 'Error writing scratch database' in ltm log
bugs.symptoms: DNS express (zxfrd) daemon gets stuck in a restart loop with the messages: -- In /var/log/ltm: Error writing scratch database (no error information available), serving database is unchanged. zxfrd will exit and restart. -- The system posts the following message on the command line every few seconds: emerg logger: Re-starting zxfrd
bugs.conditions: An update to an SOA record (and only an SOA) is received through a incremental zone transfer update (IXFR).
bugs.impact: Zone updates from the DNS master servers are not processed.
bugs.workaround: As a partial workaround, the DNS express cache files can be removed, forcing zxfrd to pull the entire zone using an AXFR request. To do so, use the following commands, in sequence: bigstart stop zxfrd rm /shared/zxfrd/* bigstart start zxfrd Note: DNS express will not be able to service DNS responses until the zone transfers have completed. For this reason, this procedure should be carried out on the standby device, if possible.
bugs.fix: The system now properly handles IXFRs that contain only starting and ending SOA RRs, and no other RRs.

bugs.title: Incorrect stream HTTP statistic values are reported for the TTFB (Time to first byte) fields
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect stream HTTP statistic values are reported for TTFB (Time to first byte), which includes the Avg Client TTFB, Min Client TTFB, and Max Client TTFB. This displays incorrect values for the statistics graphs and tables containing these fields.
bugs.conditions: -- An HTTP Analytics profile is attached to the virtual server. -- Basic HTTP/2 traffic is sent to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Incorrect values for the TTFB statistic graphs and tables within the HTTP Analytics profile are seen.
bugs.fix: The correct stream HTTP statistic values are now reported for the TTFB (Time to first byte) fields.

bugs.title: TMM can crash with core on ABORT signal due to non-responsive AVR code
bugs.symptoms: ABORT signal is sent to TMM by SOD; TMM aborts with a core.
bugs.conditions: Non-responsive AVR code. No other special conditions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: BD crash on specific cases
bugs.symptoms: BD crash on specific cases.
bugs.conditions: Have a feature that requires Captcha/ Client side Integrity in ASM.
bugs.impact: No traffic to app.
bugs.fix: This release fixes the specific crash scenario.

bugs.title: Inconsistent logging of hostname files when hostname contains periods
bugs.symptoms: Some logs write the hostname with periods (eg, say for FQDN. For example, /var/log/user.log and /var/log/messages files log just the hostname portion: -- user.log:Aug 5 17:05:01 bigip1 ). -- messages:Aug 5 16:57:32 bigip1 notice syslog-ng[2502]: Configuration reload request received, reloading configuration. Whereas other log files write the full name: -- daemon.log:Aug 5 16:58:34 bigip1.example.com info systemd[1]: Reloaded System Logger Daemon. -- maillog:Aug 5 16:55:01 bigip1.example.com err sSMTP[12924]: Unable to connect to "localhost" port 25. -- secure:Aug 5 17:02:54 bigip1.example.com info sshd(pam_audit)[2147]: 01070417:6: AUDIT - user root - RAW: sshd(pam_audit): user=root(root) partition=[All] level=Administrator tty=ssh host=10.14.13.20 attempts=1 start="Mon Aug 5 17:02:30 2019" end="Mon Aug 5 17:02:54 2019". -- ltm:Aug 5 17:02:42 bigip1.example.com warning tmsh[2200]: 01420013:4: Per-invocation log rate exceeded; throttling.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP hostname contains periods or an FQDN: [root@bigip1:Active:Standalone] log # tmsh list sys global-settings hostname sys global-settings { hostname bigip1.example.com }
bugs.impact: Hostname is logged inconsistently. Some logs write the full hostname (FQDN), while other log files write only the hostname portion. This can make searching on hostname more complicated.
bugs.fix: Hostnames are now written consistently for all log files in /var/log directory.
bugs.behavior: Syslog-ng was using truncated hostname (without FQDN) while logging. This release adds fqdn use_fqdn(yes) in the syslog-ng template, so the system now logs the full hostname (FQDN).

bugs.title: Add diskmonitor support for MySQL /var/lib/mysql
bugs.symptoms: If the disk partition /var/lib/mysql is filled to 100%, diskmonitor does not notify that the partition is nearly exhausted.
bugs.conditions: The disk partition /var/lib/mysql is filled to 100%.
bugs.impact: diskmonitor does not notify that disk partition /var/lib/mysql is nearly exhausted.

bugs.title: Add SNMP trap support for MySQL /var/lib/mysql
bugs.symptoms: If the disk partition /var/lib/mysql is filled to 100%, SNMP trap does not notify that the partition is nearly exhausted.
bugs.conditions: The disk partition /var/lib/mysql is filled to 100%.
bugs.impact: SNMP trap does not notify that disk partition /var/lib/mysql is nearly exhausted.

bugs.title: No URL category data on SSL Orchestrator dashboard and on SSL Orchestrator statistics page after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade, the "Top 10 URL Category" tab on SSL Orchestrator dashboard shows "No data". URL data are also missing on "SSL Orchestrator orchestrator-> Analytics->General Statistics" page. The data collected before upgrade disappears.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade any version of BIG-IP when SSL Orchestrator is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Some analytics data for SSL Orchestrator is missing.
bugs.fix: Fixed SELinux issues on backup of url category data.

bugs.title: GTM marks pool members down across datacenters
bugs.symptoms: GTM pool members are marked down even though the monitored resource is available. GTM debug logs indicate that each GTM is relying on the other GTM to conduct probing: debug gtmd[13166]: 011ae039:7: Check probing of IP:Port in DC /Common/dc1. debug gtmd[13166]: 011ae03a:7: Will not probe in DC /Common/dc1 because will be done by other GTM (/Common/gtm2). --- debug gtmd[7991]: 011ae039:7: Check probing of IP:Port in DC /Common/dc2. debug gtmd[7991]: 011ae03a:7: Will not probe in DC /Common/dc2 because will be done by other GTM (/Common/gtm1).
bugs.conditions: -- GTM configured in different data centers. -- GTM pool configured with a single monitor, and the monitor uses an alias address that can be pinged from both data centers. -- GTM pool members configured from different data centers.
bugs.impact: Pool members are marked down.
bugs.workaround: Instead of a single monitor, use a monitor created specifically for each data center.

bugs.title: TMSTAT offbox statistics are not continuous
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP systems are manged by BIG-IQ, the device health statistics have gaps (missing samples).
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP systems managed by BIG-IQ
bugs.impact: Missing data on device health, such as CPU load and memory occupancy.
bugs.fix: Functionality restored - BIG-IP systems send all the data as expected.

bugs.title: No support of injection into XHTML pages
bugs.symptoms: FPS does not inject the JS engine into pages with 'application/xhtml+xml' content-type.
bugs.conditions: The content-type of the response is 'application/xhtml+xml'.
bugs.impact: DataSafe features (e.g., encryption and obfuscation) are not working on XHTML pages.
bugs.fix: FPS now injects JS engine into 'application/xhtml+xml' pages. Note: JS removal detection does not work in this case (but it does work for HTML pages).

bugs.title: Improve default management port firewall
bugs.symptoms: Certain invalid packets are permitted to pass the default firewall on the management interface.
bugs.conditions: Invalid packets generated by adjacent hosts on the management interface.
bugs.impact: Invalid packets delivered to linux kernel.
bugs.fix: The default management port firewall now blocks invalid packets.

bugs.title: In SSL forward proxy, forged untrusted server certs are no longer cached.
bugs.symptoms: Previously, SSL forward proxy cached forged server certs on the client side even if the server cert was untrusted. Now, SSL forward proxy does not cache the forged cert if the server cert is untrusted.
bugs.conditions: SSL forward proxy is enabled and server cert is untrusted.
bugs.impact: You might notice a performance impact compared with previous releases.

bugs.title: Navigation parameters arriving with post payload causing problems
bugs.symptoms: False-positive illegal URL violation reported.
bugs.conditions: -- Navigation parameters are defined, and are arriving in the payload. -- A wildcard URL is not defined.
bugs.impact: False-positive violation.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, configure a navigation parameter in the following order: 1. Create navigation parameter for a URL. 2. Create the URL. There is now a checkbox in the URL where you can specify value to check navigation parameters).

bugs.title: On Demand Cert Auth Mode option set to Require in Per-Request Policy
bugs.symptoms: Setting the On Demand Cert Auth Modeoption to 'Require' in a per-request policy causes the browser to spin if no certificate is provided.
bugs.conditions: -- In a Per Request Policy, set On Demand Cert Auth to Require. -- Client SSL Profile as: -- LTM client SSL profile configured similar to the following: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/test_clientssl_ignore { ca-file /Common/BACKEND_ROOT client-cert-ca /Common/BACKEND_ROOT inherit-ca-certkeychain true inherit-certkeychain true peer-cert-mode ignore } -- Virtual server containing the client SSL profile and Per Request Policy. -- Navigate to the virtual server using a browser that has no client certificate. -- Press F5 (Refresh) after receiving the RST.
bugs.impact: The browser does not receive a response for one or more minutes, until you get RST. tmm logs shows messages similar to the following: [C] 172.31.68.130:582 -> 172.31.73.74:443:ERR_NOT_FOUND: access2 token not found; subsession might be inactive
bugs.workaround: The client browser must have a valid SSL certificate for the BIG-IP system to pass on demand certificate authentication in a per-request policy and avoid a delayed RST. Setting the Auth Mode to Require should only be used if the client provides a client certificate.

bugs.title: A new CLI command added to retrieve DoS vector stats
bugs.symptoms: Given a attack vector name or partial name, CLI command is not able to query matched attack vector information.
bugs.conditions: This is a description of missing functionality. It happens under all conditions.
bugs.impact: There is no CLI command to query for matched attack vector information.
bugs.workaround: All attack vector information for a given context (virtual server) can be queried using existing tmsh commands, then they need to filter out the specific attack vectors by writing scripts or filtering program.
bugs.fix: Given a attack vector name or partial name, there is now a CLI command provided to query matched attack vector information directly: list security presentation tmui attack-list XXXX XXXX is vector name or partial name.
bugs.behavior: This release introduces a new tmsh command: list security presentation tmui attack-list XXXX This command enables you to query attack information based on attack vector full name (or partial name). Existing CLI commands are not impacted by this change.

bugs.title: SSL profile: CRL signature verification does not check for multiple certificates with the same name as the issuer in the trusted CA bundle
bugs.symptoms: If there are multiple certificates in the trusted CA bundle with the same common name, CRL signature verification checks only one of them while looking for CRL issuer.
bugs.conditions: Multiple certificates with the same subject name as the CRL issuer in the trusted CA bundle used for authentication in SSL profiles.
bugs.impact: Handshake failure.
bugs.fix: This has been fixed to check for the issuer among all certificates that have the same subject name as the CRL issuer.

bugs.title: "Illegal parameter location" violation is reported for array parameter and for each item
bugs.symptoms: When OpenApi2 (Swagger) array parameter receives an illegal location, the violation is reported both for the array parameter, and for each element of array.
bugs.conditions: - API security policy has an array parameter configured - The array parameter is sent in location different from expected
bugs.impact: Excessive "illegal location" violations are reported in log.
bugs.fix: ASM code was fixed to report the "illegal location" violation only on the array parameter, not on each element.

bugs.title: High CPU during erroneous deletion
bugs.symptoms: The utilization of some CPUs in the system starts going up and remains so for a long time.
