Might see messages similar tot he following in tmm logs: -- notice PEM: spm_subs_id_consistency_check_cb: Session 10.1.10.10%0-4a89723e; Instance ID mismatch ERR_OK for subscriber id 310012348494 with 10.1.10.10-0-4a8987ea. -- notice PEM: spm_subs_id_consistency_check_cb: Session 10.1.18.10%0-4a8b850c; Look up returned err ERR_OK for subscriber id 3101512411557
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions under which this occurs are unknown. One potential trigger is CDP flap.
bugs.impact: TMM may need to be restarted if the CPU usage does not subside. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Try deleting all subscribers from the CLI.

bugs.title: SSL monitor continues to mark pool member down after restoring services
bugs.symptoms: After an HTTPS monitor fails, it never resumes probing. No ClientHello is sent, just 3WHS and then 4-way closure. The pool member remains down.
bugs.conditions: -- The cipherlist for the monitor is not using TLSv1 (e.g., contains -TLSv1 or !TLSv1). -- The pool member is marked down.
bugs.impact: Services are not automatically restored by the health monitor.
bugs.workaround: -- To restore the state of the member, remove it and add it back to the pool. -- Remove !TLSv1 and -TLSv1 from the cipher string, if possible.

bugs.title: External datagroups of type string cannot use iRule command 'class match equals' for entries > 32 characters long
bugs.symptoms: iRules using the command 'class match' with the 'equals' operator on long entries fail to return a positive match, even if they are in the datagroup, for example: my_datagroup: "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456" := "value1" class match "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456" equals my_datagroup
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when all of the following conditions are met: - Using an external datagroup of type string with keys longer than 32 characters. - Using an iRule with the 'class match' command and the 'equals' operator on the external datagroup. - Trying to match keys that are longer than 32 characters.
bugs.impact: iRules will act incorrectly
bugs.workaround: If none of the keys in the datagroup are prefixes of each other, the 'equals' operator can be changed to 'starts_with' or 'ends_with' (if none are suffixes of each other).
bugs.fix: iRules using the command 'class match' with the 'equals' operator on long entries now correctly matches external datagroup string entries which are longer than 32 characters.

bugs.title: SSLO or SWG connections using proxy chaining to Explicit Proxy can get reset
bugs.symptoms: Connections get reset with reset cause "repick failed"
bugs.conditions: SSLO with proxy chaining to Explicit Proxy or SWG per-request policy using proxy select agent with No URI rewrite
bugs.impact: Connections get reset with reset cause "repick failed"
bugs.fix: Connections no longer get reset.

bugs.title: Residual folders after uninstalling the cloudhsm from BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: After uninstalling cloudhsm from the BIG-IP system, you can still see /etc and /run in the installing path - /shared/cloudhsm or /opt/cloudhsm. Inside /etc, there are some old cloudhsm config file backups, which may take disk space, depending on how many times you configure cloudhsm.
bugs.conditions: When uninstalling AWS cloudhsm from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The leftover folders may take some disk space.
bugs.workaround: You can manually delete these folders to free up space if you do not need them. However, keep in mind these old configuration backup files are intentionally kept by AWS cloudhsm.

bugs.title: Portal Access: client-side URL rewriter incorrectly replaces '..' with 'f5-w-doubledot' in query
bugs.symptoms: Via Portal Access, web-application generates requests on which '..' in the query portion of URL is replaced by 'f5-w-doubledot'.
bugs.conditions: Client-side JavaScript code produces a URL with '..' in query part.
bugs.impact: Web-application does not function as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule to workaround this issue.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed.

bugs.title: IKEv2 debug logging often omits SPI values that would identify the SAs involved
bugs.symptoms: Debug logging for IPsec often has no clear identification of which SA was involved during some logged events.
bugs.conditions: When you examine logs in either /var/log/tmm or /var/log/ipsec.log to debug IPsec activity.
bugs.impact: You might have trouble analyzing what happened from logs when the SA involved in an event is not identified.
bugs.fix: More logged lines now include SPI values to identify the SA involved, especially in error cases.

bugs.title: Re-transmitted IPsec packets can have garbled contents
bugs.symptoms: Before re-transmitting a packet, it is discovered to be garbled, mainly in the form of having physical length that no longer matches the logical length recorded inside the packet.
bugs.conditions: Possibly rare condition that might cause packet freeing while still in use.
bugs.impact: Likely tunnel outage until re-established.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is known at this time.
bugs.fix: This release adds checksums to verify IPsec packets are not altered between first creation and later re-transmission.

bugs.title: Live Update does not authenticate remote users
bugs.symptoms: Remote users with Administrator or Application Security Administrator roles cannot run Live Update.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote user (LDAP/RADIUS). -- Remote user logged in. -- New installation is available.
bugs.impact: -- Remote users cannot manually check for updates. -- Remote users cannot manually upload new files. -- Remote users cannot install new update files.
bugs.workaround: Log in with a local user like admin, application security editor, or application security administrator.
bugs.fix: Authentication is directly done from MCP. Remote users are not treated like local users, so only the role of the user determines the ability to perform operations such as Live Update.

bugs.title: ASM XMLHTTPRequest wrapper attempts to access responseText for non text respnseType
bugs.symptoms: A website that uses non-text values for XMLHTTPRequest.responseType experiences issues, and JavaScript errors are shown in the browser console. Failed to read the 'responseText' property from 'XMLHttpRequest': The value is only accessible if the object's 'responseType' is '' or 'text' (was 'blob').
bugs.conditions: This occurs under either set of conditions: 1. -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- AJAX blocking page enabled in the ASM policy. 2. -- Bot Defense or DoS Application profile attached to a virtual server. -- Single page application enabled in the Bot Defense or DoS Application profile.
bugs.impact: End-user experience might be affected; website functionality might malfunction.
bugs.workaround: For Conditions set 1: Disable AJAX blocking page. For Conditions set 2: Disable Single page application.
bugs.fix: ASM XMLHTTPRequest wrapper now avoid illegal access to XMLHTTPRequest.responseText.

bugs.title: GUI cannot edit ILX workspace/extension objects with certain non-alphanumeric characters.
bugs.symptoms: iRules LX (ILX) Object names including non alpha-numeric characters are not handled by the GUI.
bugs.conditions: ILX workspaces or extensions with names that include non alpha-numeric characters. $ (USD symbol) are prohibited in BIG-IP object names. However, they are allowed in the iRules LX workspace and extension names. This applies to both tmsh and iControl REST.
bugs.impact: These ILX workspaces or extensions are inaccessible in the GUI. Cannot use the GUI to edit them.
bugs.workaround: Rename your workspaces and extensions.

bugs.title: Traffic using route entry that's more specific than existing blackhole route can cause core
bugs.symptoms: TMM asserts with 'Attempting to free loopback interface'message.
bugs.conditions: - Using blackhole routes. - Have a route entry that is more specific than the existing blackhole route.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use /32 blackhole routes.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when using blackhole routes that are less specific than non-blackhole routes.

bugs.title: Tmm crash when per-request policies are in use
bugs.symptoms: Per-req-policies may intermittently leak memory, leading to a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: -- APM enabled -- Per-request policy enabled and passing traffic
bugs.impact: Memory can leak. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: tmsh command 'show security' returning a parsing error
bugs.symptoms: Running the tmsh command 'tmsh -m show security' returns a parsing error similar to the following: Unexpected Error: Chunked data did not start with start_message.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is provisioned. -- Running the command: 'tmsh -m show security'.
bugs.impact: -- the 'show security' commands return a parsing error. -- Some show commands might not work.
bugs.fix: Ensured that the system handles the 'tmsh -m show security' command without a parsing error.

bugs.title: Additional logging added to detect when monitoring operations in the configuration exceeds capabilities.
bugs.symptoms: GTM logs 'no reply from big3d: timed out' messages when the configuration results in more runtime monitoring operations than can be supported in a given environment, but the same message also appears in the log for other reasons.
bugs.conditions: The GTM configuration results in more runtime monitoring operations than can be supported in a given environment.
bugs.impact: It is not possible to detect when there are more runtime monitoring operations than can be supported in a given environment without enabling debug logging and performing a complex analysis of the resulting log files.
bugs.workaround: Enable debug logging and conduct a detailed analysis to determine if monitor requests are scheduled at the configured intervals.
bugs.fix: There is now a warning message that provides a much clearer indication of the condition: The list processing time (14 seconds) exceeded the interval value. There may be too many monitor instances configured with a 7 second interval.

bugs.title: AFM Flow Inspector filter doesn't indicate src-ip/dst-ip filters filters as clientside.
bugs.symptoms: In AFM debug tool, flow inspector, for IP address filtering, the GUI describes fields as 'Source' and 'Destination', and provides no indication that this means the client-side source and client-side destination.
bugs.conditions: Using the 'Source' and 'Destination' fields in the AFM debug tool, flow inspector, for IP address filtering.
bugs.impact: GUI does not indicate what sort of data it expects. Confusion determining which IP address should be used.
bugs.workaround: Specify 'Source' as the client-side source and 'Destination' as the client-side destination.
bugs.fix: Labels are added to indicate that these are client-side fields.

bugs.title: Packet tester tool in command line does not support tab completion on vlan name. Vlan name without partition is not supported either
bugs.symptoms: Packet tester tool does not support tab completion and partition for VLAN name.
bugs.conditions: -- Run the tmsh packet tester tool with no partition on the VLAN name. -- Try tab completion for the VLAN name in the tmsh command.
bugs.impact: If partition is not entered, the result from packet tester is wrong. Tab completion does not work.
bugs.workaround: Add the partition name to the VLAN name when running the tool.
bugs.fix: VLAN name without partition is now supported. Tab completion works as expected.

bugs.title: Drop Redirect tab incorrectly named as 'Redirect Drop'
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect naming on navigation tabs Security :: Debug :: Drop Redirect.
bugs.conditions: Navigating to Security :: Debug :: Drop Redirect.
bugs.impact: The page name is Drop Redirect instead of Redirect Drop.
bugs.fix: Drop Redirect tab is now correctly named as 'Drop Redirect'

bugs.title: Added ability in the Flow Inspector to search on serverside src/dst ip addresses
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to search on serverside source/destination IP addresses using Flow Inspector.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using Flow Inspector, a debug tool in AFM.
bugs.impact: You are unable to search server-side source/destination IP addresses.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh: tmsh show sys connection
bugs.fix: Added ability in the Flow Inspector to search on serverside src/dst IP addresses.

bugs.title: For in-tmm monitoring: multiple instances of the same agent are running on the Standby device
bugs.symptoms: The standby device is sending monitor requests at a more frequent interval than what is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- In-tmm monitoring configured. -- High availability (HA) configured. There is no explicit way to reproduce this and it does not occur every time.
bugs.impact: Multiple instances of in-tmm monitoring may be created and the BIG-IP device may be sending monitoring traffic more frequently than what is configured.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing multiple monitoring instances to be created.

bugs.title: Improve log message when an SSL invalid profile is found
bugs.symptoms: When an SSL alert is sent, the profile name is printed but not the name of the virtual. If this is a heavily used profile, it makes tracing difficult.
bugs.conditions: An SSL alert is sent and logged.
bugs.impact: Difficult to identify which virtual server / profile combination was used.
bugs.fix: When an SSL alert is sent, the name of the associated profile and virtual server are included in the log.

bugs.title: Failure to open data channel for active FTP connections mirrored across an HA pair.
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally, attempting to actively open a data channel from an FTP session that is mirrored across a BIG-IP high availability pair will fail. This is due to aggressive port reuse on the active BIG-IP system, causing ports that are still in a TIME_WAIT state to be used for the data connection.
bugs.conditions: -- Have a BIG-IP HA pair configured. -- Create an FTP virtual server with mirroring enabled. -- Have the pool member(s) of the virtual server be either 3CDaemon or IIS servers (this issue has been confirmed only for 3CDaemon and IIS, but it could affect other servers as well). -- Client attempts to download data through the virtual server via active FTP.
bugs.impact: Data connections fail to open; data transfer is unsuccessful.
bugs.workaround: Use passive FTP, or do not use mirroring for FTP virtual servers.
bugs.fix: Mirrored, active FTP connections no longer fail to open data channels, and now successfully transmit data.

bugs.title: End-user may not be able to connect to VPN.
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server without a connectivity profile is accessed with the request for a file pre/config.php, an invalid file is cached in the BIG-IP system's HTTP cache. When the same request is later sent to a virtual server that does contain a connectivity profile, the invalid file from the cache is returned, which results in VPN connection failure.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is configured. -- Virtual server without connectivity profile is configured. -- Another Virtual server with connectivity profile is configured. -- The first virtual server is accessed with an HTTP request for pre/config.php?version=2.0. -- Then second virtual server is accessed with same request.
bugs.impact: End-user may not be able to use the VPN.
bugs.workaround: When the issue occurs, run the following command on the BIG-IP command line in order to clear the cache: tmsh delete ltm profile ramcache all
bugs.fix: The caching functionality has been updated to ignore the caching of invalid files.

bugs.title: Browser might get stuck when SPA is enabled
bugs.symptoms: The browser might get stuck when enabling ASM SPA feature.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM SPA is enabled. -- The application page is hooking native JavaScript AJAX calls.
bugs.impact: The browser gets stuck. The page is not displayed.
bugs.fix: Avoid infinite recursion loop for AJAX callbacks.

bugs.title: Adding a tighter protection to fictive url
bugs.symptoms: fictive url are not identified tight enough
bugs.conditions: outdated fictive urls are sent to BIG-IP
bugs.impact: in some cases wrong behavior of bot-defense handling fictive outdated fictive urls

bugs.title: Fetching non-configured 3GPP-RAT-TYPE subscriber attribute using iRule can crash tmm.
bugs.symptoms: A TMM crash occurs while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: Fetching a non-configured 3GPP-RAT-TYPE subscriber attribute using an iRule.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Dont use an iRule to fetch 3GPP-RAT-TYPE subscriber attribute if 3GPP-RAT-TYPE is not set.

bugs.title: Traffic redirection to an internal virtual server may fail.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic sent by a first virtual server to a second internal virtual server may fail. Traffic is silently dropped.
bugs.conditions: One of the following configurations: - A virtual server configured with a pem policy rule that targets an internal radius virtual server that sends traffic statistics to a radius server. - A virtual server configured with an iRule that opens a sideband connection to a second internal virtual server using the iRule command "connect". - A virtual server configured with an iRule that forwards traffic to a second internal virtual server using the iRule command "virtual", where the second virtual server performs source address translation with an LSN pool or with AFM NAT.
bugs.impact: The traffic sent to the internal virtual server is silently dropped.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using a PEM policy rule that targets an internal radius virtual server. Avoid traffic forwarding to an internal virtual server with the iRule commands "connect" or "virtual".
bugs.fix: The traffic is now successfully sent or redirected to the internal virtual server without any drops.

bugs.title: iRule Command TCP::release does not work correctly with argument 0.
bugs.symptoms: When using the iRule command TCP::release with argument 0, the command does not work correctly.
bugs.conditions: TCP::release is used with argument 0.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP configuration might not load correctly.

bugs.title: Autodos daemon history file is created even there is no vector enabled in a DoS profile
bugs.symptoms: Autodos daemon history file is created even when there is no vector enabled in a DoS profile.
bugs.conditions: An empty DoS profile is attached to a virtual server without enabling any vector in the profile.
bugs.impact: Disk space is being unnecessarily used.
bugs.workaround: Make sure each DoS profile attached to virtual server has at least one vector enabled.
bugs.fix: Attaching an empty DoS profile without an enabled vector does not create a history file for that virtual server in the autodos daemon.

bugs.title: HSB error causes TMM core and failover
bugs.symptoms: The HSB device reports a transmitter failure, which can be observed in the ltm/tmm logs: Error in /var/log/ltm similar to:crit tmm[17788]: 01010025:2: Device error: hsb hsb interface 0 DMA lockup on transmitter failure This results in a TMM core, a failover, and a unit reboot.
bugs.conditions: It's unknown under what conditions this occurs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Global SNAT connections do not reset upon timeout.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not send reset packets when a connection times out.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured with global SNAT.
bugs.impact: Client or server might unnecessarily keep the connection open.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use forwarding virtual server with snatpool instead of global SNAT. -- Modify tmm_base.tcl as follows: profile bigproto _bigproto { reset_on_timeout enable }

bugs.title: After upgrade, nlad may not create an schannel to a domain controller
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading to v14.1.0 or later, the nlad daemon cannot create Microsoft Secure Channel (Schannel) connections to configured domain controllers after reboot. The system posts errors in the /var/log/apm logfile similar to the following: err eca[5290]: 0162000e:3: Failed to resolve DC FQDN (example.example.com), Name or service not known (-2).
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading the BIG-IP system to v14.1.0 or later. -- NTLM front-end authentication is configured.
bugs.impact: NTLM authentication might fail for APM end users. No NTLM communication to back-end Domain Controller while nlad restarts.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command to restart nlad: bigstart restart nlad eca

bugs.title: UIDs on /home directory are scrambled after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: UIDs of /home/$USER files and /home file are scrambled after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from 12.1.3.7 to 13.1.0.8.
bugs.impact: Low in most cases, since the administrative user can still access most files. One exception is that SSH requires that the authorized_keys file be owned by the user ID in question. This is 0 when a user has an administrative role, so the authorized_keys file will be ignored and a password will still be required for login.

bugs.title: Aborted DNS queries to a cache may cause a TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash if an attempt is made to send a response to a TCP connection that has already been torn down.
bugs.conditions: TCP connections that are aborted before receiving a RESPONSE from a cache.
bugs.impact: Loss of service until TMM is restarted. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Aborted DNS queries to a cache no longer cause a TMM crash.

bugs.title: VDI plugin might crash on process shutdown during RDG connections handling
bugs.symptoms: VDI plugin might crash on process shutdown if it is stopped during handling of RDG connections.
bugs.conditions: VDI plugin process is stopped while new RDG connection is established via APM.
bugs.impact: The process will be shutdown, but generated core file might cause unnecessary confusion.
bugs.fix: Fixed VDI plugin crash on process shutdown during RDG connections handling.

bugs.title: TMM cores when receiving HTTP/2 request if mirroring is configured
bugs.symptoms: TMM on active unit cores when it receives an HTTP/2 request when mirroring is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) configuration. -- Active unit received an HTTP/2 request. -- Mirroring is enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM cores. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable mirroring. Note: Connection mirroring is not supported in combination with the HTTP/2 profile. The system now checks for this combination and prevents it from being configured.
bugs.fix: This release adds connection mirroring validation for the HTTP/2 profile. HTTP/2 virtual server validation fails if connection mirroring is enabled, and the system posts an error similar to the following: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Error configuring Virtual Server (/Common/vs1). Connection mirroring is not supported in combination with HTTP2 profile.
bugs.behavior: Previously, TMM cored on the active system when it received an HTTP/2 request and connection mirroring was enabled. Now, HTTP/2 Virtual Server validation fails if connection mirroring is enabled, and the system reports the following message in the LTM log: err mcpd[25742]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Error configuring Virtual Server (/Common/vs_http). Connection mirroring is not supported in combination with HTTP2 profile. This is correct behavior, as connection mirroring is not supported in combination with the HTTP/2 profile.

bugs.title: Nitrox 3 instruction/request logger may fail due to SELinux permission error
bugs.symptoms: When the tmm Nitrox 3 queue stuck problem is encountered, the Nitrox 3 code tries to log the instruction/request, but it may fail due to SELinux permissions error. The system posts messages in /var/log/ltm similar to the following: -- crit tmm1[21300]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Nitrox 3, Hang Detected: compression device was reset (pci 00:09.7, discarded 54). -- crit tmm1[21300]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Failed to open instruction log file '/shared/nitroxdiag/instrlog/tmm01_00:09.7_inst.log' err=2.
bugs.conditions: -- tmm Nitrox 3 queue stuck problem is encountered. -- The Nitrox 3 code tries to log the instruction/request.
bugs.impact: Error messages occur, and the tmm Nitrox 3 code cannot log the instruction/request.
bugs.fix: Nitrox 3 queue stuck occurrences are now logged as expected.

bugs.title: In rare cases tmm crash is observed when using APM as RDG proxy
bugs.symptoms: Tmm may crash when APM is configured as an RDG proxy to access Microsoft remote desktops and applications.
bugs.conditions: APM is used as RDG proxy
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: ZebOS addresses blocks do not reflect RFC5735 changes to reserved address blocks.
bugs.symptoms: Special IP address handling as per RFC6890 is done correctly in the routing protocols. There is a possibility of martian addresses getting announced or allowed addresses restricted (e.g., 128.0.0.0/16 and 191.255.0.0/16). This impacts all components using dynamic routing.
bugs.conditions: -- Network advertisements in BGP, etc., allow martian addresses and restrict allowed network-space as per RFC6890, for example, 128.0.0.0/16 and 191.255.0.0/16, 223.255.255.0/24 are blocked. -- In IPv6 loopback addressed are allowed, so ::/128 (unspec) and ::1/128 (loopback) addresses are allowed. -- Some DSlite address ranges are not handled correctly.
bugs.impact: Martian addresses are allowed. Non-martian addresses are blocked.
bugs.fix: Ensure that martian addresses like IPv6 (::/128 - unspec, ::1/128 - loopback) are not used. Note: Although 128.0.0.0/16, 191.255.0.0/16, 223.255.255.0/24 are no longer martian addresses, they still cannot be used.

bugs.title: Non-UTF8 characters returned from /bin/createmanifest
bugs.symptoms: /bin/createmanifest reads from mcpd values stored for items that are obtained from firmware. These might contain non-UTF8 characters. This program is called in qkview, which then gets updated to iHealth. If any non-UTF8 character is present, the output is omitted (because XML cannot handle non-UTF8 characters).
bugs.conditions: Data stored in mcpd obtained from firmware contain non-UTF8 characters.
bugs.impact: The upload to iHealth will not contain any of the manifest data set obtained via createmanifest.
bugs.workaround: The values can be obtained from the qkview by reading the qkview_run.data, but the convenience of reading these in iHealth is not possible.
bugs.fix: The corrected program converts any non-UTF8 characters into '%xx', thus outputting compliant UTF8 strings. These do not negatively impact the XML requirement, and the modified string can be uploaded to iHealth (and the non-UTF8 characters can be examined as hexadecimal values).

bugs.title: BIG-IP may fail source translation for connections when connection mirroring is enabled on a virtual server that also has source port set to 'preserve strict'
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system may fail source translation for connections matching a virtual server that has connection mirroring enabled and source port selection set to 'preserve strict'.
bugs.conditions: Connections match a virtual server that has following settings: - Connection mirroring is enabled. - Source Port set to 'Preserve Strict'. In addition, CMP hash selection (DAG mode) on the corresponding VLANs is set to 'Default DAG'.
bugs.impact: Source translation may fail on BIG-IP system, leading to client connection failures.
bugs.workaround: You can try either of the following: -- Do not use the Source Port setting of 'Preserve Strict'. -- Disable connection mirroring on the virtual server.

bugs.title: No disallowed Geolocation violation detail entry
bugs.symptoms: The disallowed geolocation does not have an entry for violation details in remote logging.
bugs.conditions: While blocking requests from disallowed geolocation and viewing remote logger for details.
bugs.impact: No details for geolocation violation in the remote logger.
bugs.fix: Now geolocation violation shares details in the remote logger.

bugs.title: Ajax encryption feature may cause high CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: Ajax encryption may cause high CPU usage on the client side.
bugs.conditions: Ajax Encryption feature is enabled.
bugs.impact: High CPU usage on the client side.
bugs.fix: Ajax encryption logic no longer causes high CPU usage.

bugs.title: Virtual server created with Guided Configuration is not visible in Grafana
bugs.symptoms: The traffic of Virtual Server created with the Guided Configuration is not visible with Grafana monitoring tool. Statistics of this virtual server are not included in the admdb part of qkview.
bugs.conditions: -- Create virtual server using Guided Configuration. -- Use the Grafana monitoring tool to view virtual server statistics. -- Create a qkview.
bugs.impact: Cannot view virtual server using the Grafana monitoring tool. The resulting qkview contains no statistics for this virtual server. Lack of information for debugging and troubleshooting
bugs.workaround: Configure virtual server manually, without the Guided Configuration
bugs.fix: Virtual server created with Guided Configuration is visible in Grafana and its statistics present in qkview.

bugs.title: Engineering Hotfix ISOs may be nearly as large as full Release ISOs
bugs.symptoms: Engineering Hotfix ISO images might be unexpectedly large.
bugs.conditions: This might occur with certain Engineering Hotfix builds.
bugs.impact: Engineering Hotfixes are unnecessarily large.
bugs.fix: Engineering Hotfix ISO images are no longer created with a size that may occasionally exceed 2 GB, and no longer contain a complete set of packages replacing all packages installed by the original BIG-IP release upon which the Engineering Hotfix is based.

bugs.title: GUI creates a policy even if there were errors
bugs.symptoms: Creating Policy in the GUI shows an error even when the Policy is created successfully.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while creating a Policy in the GUI.
bugs.impact: It might appear that the Policy is not created (even though it was) because the GUI displays an error message.
bugs.workaround: Refresh the Policy List page. The created Policy displays.
bugs.fix: Prevent Policy creation if there are any errors.

bugs.title: iRule command 'ACCESS::session data get -secure' can fail when evaluating empty variables
bugs.symptoms: Use of the iRule command 'ACCESS::session data get -secure <empty variable>' might fail intermittently, which might result in BIG-IP traffic processing failures and a Tcl error logged in /var/log/ltm: err tmm2[22011]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/sp_irule <HTTP_REQUEST> - variable lookup failed (line 1)Illegal argument (line 1) (line 1) invoked from within "ACCESS::session data get -secure "session.saml.last.attr.name.foo"".
bugs.conditions: Use of -secure flag to get data from an empty variable from ACCESS::session inside iRules.
bugs.impact: Connection drop.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule catch statement.
bugs.fix: The system now checks for empty variable value before attempting decryption.

bugs.title: DoSL7 Record Traffic feature is not recording traffic
bugs.symptoms: Enabling 'Record Traffic During Attacks' in the DoS Application Profile does not record traffic during attacks: TCP Dump files are not being created in the /shared/dosl7/tcpdumps/ directory as expected.
bugs.conditions: -- Enabling 'Record Traffic During Attacks' in the DoS Application Profile. -- DoSL7 Attacks are detected.
bugs.impact: Attack traffic is not being recorded as expected.
bugs.fix: Enabling 'Record Traffic During Attacks' in the DoS Application Profile correctly records traffic during attacks.

bugs.title: BIND Update
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade BIND to 9.11.5-P4 per recommendation from ISC
bugs.conditions: GTM provisioned.
bugs.impact: BIND not up-to-date
bugs.fix: Upgrade to BIND 9.11.5-P4

bugs.title: BIND Update
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade BIND to 9.11.5-P4 per recommendation from ISC
bugs.conditions: GTM provisioned.
bugs.impact: BIND not up-to-date
bugs.fix: Upgrade to BIND 9.11.5-P4

bugs.title: BIND Update
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade BIND to 9.11.5-P4 per recommendation from ISC
bugs.conditions: GTM provisioned.
bugs.impact: BIND not up-to-date
bugs.fix: Upgrade to BIND 9.11.5-P4

bugs.title: Ephemeral pool members may not be created after config load or reboot
bugs.symptoms: When using FQDN nodes and pool members, ephemeral pool members may not be created as expected immediately after a configuration-load or BIG-IP system reboot operation.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on affected BIG-IP versions when: -- Multiple FQDN names (configured for FQDN nodes/pool members) resolve to the same IP address. -- DNS queries to resolve these FQDN names occur almost simultaneously. The occurrence of this issue is very sensitive to timing conditions, and is more likely to occur when there are larger numbers of FQDN names resolving to a common IP address.
bugs.impact: When this issue occurs, some subset of ephemeral pool members may not be created as expected. As a result, some pools may not have any active pool members, and do not pass traffic. This issue, when it occurs, may persist until the next DNS queries occur for each FQDN name, at which point the missing ephemeral pool members are typically created as expected. Using the default FQDN interval value of 3600 seconds, such downtime lasts approximately one hour.
bugs.workaround: To minimize the duration of time when pools may be missing ephemeral pool members, configure a shorter FQDN interval value for the FQDN nodes: tmsh mod ltm node fqdn-node-name { fqdn { interval ## } } Where ## is the desired number of seconds between successive DNS queries to resolve the configure FQDN name.

bugs.title: Bypassing SSL interception in SSL Orchestrator may crash TMM if virtual server is SNAT enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM daemon crashes with segmentation fault signal (SIGSEGV).
bugs.conditions: On rare occasions specific to a certain race condition, when SSL forward proxy enforces the bypass action on a flow that's handled by a SSLO transparent virtual server that has SNAT enabled, TMM may crash.
bugs.impact: Failover or network outage. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when SSL forward proxy enforces the bypass action on a flow that's handled by a SSLO transparent virtual server that has SNAT enabled.

bugs.title: TMM clock advances and cluster failover happens during webroot db nightly updates
bugs.symptoms: Webroot database mapping and unmapping takes a very long amount of time on TMM, so you might see clock advances occur. The long interval might result in a failover/state-transition in clustered environment.
bugs.conditions: -- Webroot database is downloaded. -- TMM needs to swap to the new instance.
bugs.impact: TMM does not process traffic because of the long delay in mapping and unmapping, and failover might happen in a clustered environment.
bugs.workaround: You can avoid this issue by disabling BrightCloud updates, however, your environments will miss the latest updates as a result. #vi /etc/wr_urldbd/bcsdk.cfg DoBcap=true DoRtu=false DownloadDatabase=false
bugs.fix: Mapping/Unmapping the database is done asynchronously and the delay is reduced so that the CDP failover doesn't happen.

bugs.title: TMM logs 'MSIX is not supported' error on vCMP guests
bugs.symptoms: On vCMP guests, logs of 'MSIX is not supported' messages apppear in /var/log/tmm.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only on vCMP guests.
bugs.impact: MSIX is not supported on vCMP guests, but system operation and traffic passing are not impacted otherwise.

bugs.title: LDAP authenticated Firewall Manager role cannot edit firewall policies
bugs.symptoms: The system posts the following message when the LDAP authenticated Firewall Manager role creates/modifies a firewall policy with rules or upgrading existing firewall policy: User does not have modify access to object (fw_uuid_config).
bugs.conditions: -- Log in using an account with the Firewall Manager role. -- Create/modify firewall policy with rules or upgrade existing firewall policy.
bugs.impact: Firewall modification operations fail with access to object (fw_uuid_config) error.
bugs.fix: Firewall manager can now edit firewall policies.

bugs.title: SNMP MIBS for AFM NAT do not yet exist
bugs.symptoms: SNMP MIBS for AFM NAT do not yet exist.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in normal operation.
bugs.impact: Unable to read values that do not exist in SNMP, meaning that you cannot access information that you need.

bugs.title: Bot defense anomaly 'Invalid Mouse Events Sequence' false positive raised and request is blocked
bugs.symptoms: Request is blocked. The message 'Invalid Mouse Events Sequence' anomaly appears in the bot defense requests log.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Bot defense assigned to a virtual server. -- End user clicks on a checkbox or an HTML radio button.
bugs.impact: Requests are blocked.
bugs.workaround: Disable bot defense human detection negative checks. For versions earlier than v14.1.0: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ws_cshui_susp_event_bot_score 0 bigstart restart asm For v14.1.0 and higher Disable anomaly 'Invalid Mouse Events Sequence' in bot defense profile
bugs.fix: This release no longer checks events sequences for checkboxes and radio buttons, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: TMCTL stats counters are still available for QoE module which is deprecated
bugs.symptoms: QoE module is deprecated from 15.0.0. But TMCTL stats counters are still available for QoE module.
bugs.conditions: View PEM action and High Speed Logging (HSL) stats using the tmctl command, for example: -- tmctl -w120 pem_actions_stat -- tmctl -w120 pem_hsl_stat
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. Because QoE cannot be configured, it cannot be used, the stats will never be updated. The values for the stats will always be zero and can be ignored.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) using virtio interfaces with direct descriptors.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use this procedure: 1a. For BIG-IP systems running versions earlier than 14.1.0, add the following line to /config/tmm_init.tcl: device driver vendor_dev 1af4:1000 unic 1b. For BIG-IP systems running v14.1.0 and later, add the following line to /config/tmm_init.tcl: device driver vendor_dev 1d0f:ec20 sock 2. Restart tmm using the following command: bigstart restart tmm Note: You might need to manually remove that line from /config/tmm_init.tcl after upgrading.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes traffic as expected.

bugs.title: pccd crashes when deleting a nested Address List
bugs.symptoms: When removing a nested Address List or Port List, the pccd process might crash.
bugs.conditions: This might occur under the following conditions: -- Removing a nested Address List or Port List using a tmsh transaction with an incorrect tmsh command order consistently results in this crash. -- A high availability (HA) setup with config-sync enabled and there are intermittent problems with HA-connections, or out-of-memory system state, might intermittently result in this crash.
bugs.impact: pccd crashes with core, restarts, and correctly compiles the new configuration. There is a resulting, small delay in applying the new configuration due to the pccd restart.
bugs.workaround: -- If the crash occurs as a result of incorrect tmsh commands in a transaction, reorder commands to the parent list is modified or deleted before deleting the nested list. -- If the crash is an intermittent issue due to problems with HA-connections, or an out-of-memory system state, no action is necessary; pccd correctly compiles new configuration after it restarts.
bugs.fix: pccd no longer crashes under these conditions, and correctly compiles the new configuration.

bugs.title: Category lookup returns wrong category on subsequent traffic following initial HTTP CONNECT traffic through SSLO
bugs.symptoms: Category lookup returns the wrong category on subsequent traffic following initial HTTP CONNECT traffic through F5 SSL Orchestrator (SSLO).
bugs.conditions: -- Outbound deployment configured in SSLO, where SSLO behaves as a transparent proxy. -- A policy has a branch to lookup category using HTTP Connect. -- An HTTPS client generates HTTPS traffic via an explicit proxy on the local network with a private address through SSLO as the gateway.
bugs.impact: Category Match is not performed on subsequent requests, resulting in fallback branch to be taken.
bugs.fix: Category lookup now works correctly in this scenario.

bugs.title: HTTP monitor with a configured username/password fails when in-tmm monitoring is enabled
bugs.symptoms: http monitor using a username/password fails to send an authorization header. If the webserver is configured for basic authentication, it may reject the request.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP monitor is configured with a username and password. -- In-tmm monitoring is enabled (bigd.tmm enabled).
bugs.impact: HTTP monitor is marked down.
bugs.workaround:
There is change of behavior with in-tmm monitors: -- In-tmm monitors treat the send string in a more strict manner: send "GET /monitor HTTP/1.0
Host: test.com

" Because the string is terminated with 

, the monitor treats this as the end of the HTTP request, and Authorization gets omitted. To workaround this issue, omit the final 
, as follows: send "GET /monitor HTTP/1.0
Host: test.com
"

bugs.title: Datagroup iRule command class can lead to memory corruption
bugs.symptoms: When using the iRule command to access datagroups within a foreach loop, memory can be corrupted and tmm can crash.
bugs.conditions: A [class] command used within a foreach loop.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: No workaround aside from removing that iRule.
bugs.fix: tmm no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: Error reading RRD file may induce processes to mutually wait for each other forever
bugs.symptoms: If an error occurs while statsd is reading a file that contains performance data, certain control-plane processes may wait for each other indefinitely. In some instances, error messages about files in the /var/rrd directory may appear in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: Errors occur when performance-monitoring processes attempt to read files in the BIG-IP's internal Round-Robin Database.
bugs.impact: Attempts to issue commands using "tmsh" may hang up. No "qkview" datasets can be successfully generated.
bugs.workaround: If damaged data files in /var/rrd can be identified, delete them and run "bigstart restart statsd".

bugs.title: GUI Network Map slow page load with large configuration
bugs.symptoms: Network Map loads very slowly when displaying large configurations.
bugs.conditions: Open Network Map page with a large configuration, for example, 2500 or more virtual servers, pools, and pool members.
bugs.impact: The Network Map page loads too slowly to be usable.
bugs.fix: Network Map no longer loads very slowly when displaying large configurations.

bugs.title: mcpd process killed after upgrade from 12.1.3
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP appliance fails to become available after upgrade, and the mcpd process keeps restarting.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system is upgraded from 12.1.3 to 14.1.0, with a very large configuration. For example, this was encountered with more than 8,000 virtual servers and more than 600 monitor instances.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails to become operational.
bugs.workaround: If you are encountering this, you can disable the mcpd heartbeat with the following command to complete the upgrade: tmsh modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat disable Once the upgrade is complete, enable the heartbeat: tmsh modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat enable

bugs.title: Specific sequence of packets causes Fast Open to be effectively disabled
bugs.symptoms: You see this warning in the logs: warning tmm[21063]: 01010055:4: Syncookie embryonic connection counter -1 exceeded sys threshold 64000.
bugs.conditions: -- TCP Fast Open and ECN are both enabled. -- There are multiple RST segments from the receive window received in SYN_RECEIVED state.
bugs.impact: TCP Fast open is disabled, as the pre_established_connections becomes very large (greater than a threshold).
bugs.workaround: TCP ECN option can be disabled.
bugs.fix: TCP Fast Open is prevented from being disabled when some conditions are met.

bugs.title: A missed SYN cookie check causes crash at the standby TMM in HA mirroring system
bugs.symptoms: In a high availability (HA) mirroring configuration, an L7 packet SYN cookie check may be skipped on the standby unit and eventually causes TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: -- L7 traffic being passed to an HA configuration that is configured for mirroring traffic. -- Failover occurs.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes on the standby device. No connections shown on the standby unit even when mirroring isenabled.
bugs.workaround: Do not use HA mirroring.
bugs.fix: The system now provides SYN cookie checks for L7 mirrored packets on the standby system.

bugs.title: Invoking the HTTP::respond iRule command when the HTTP2 profile is present can cause stalled or malformed responses.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system stalls a connection instead of sending the intended HTTP response, or sends a malformed response.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- The virtual server uses the http2 profile. -- The virtual server uses an iRule that invokes the HTTP::respond command under the HTTP_REQUEST or HTTP_RESPONSE event.
bugs.impact: Clients do not get the expected responses, leading to application failures.
bugs.fix: The HTTP::respond iRule command works as expected under these conditions.

bugs.title: Excessive resource consumption when processing REST requests
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, REST requests may consume excessive system resources
bugs.conditions: -- Advanced Shell on the BIG-IP system. -- REST usage.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now handles REST requests as expected.

bugs.title: DNS Validating Resolver Cache 'Key' Cache records not deleted correctly when using TMSH command to delete the record
bugs.symptoms: Attempt to delete a DNS Validating Resolver cache record from the 'Key' cache does not remove the record. Also displays a negative TTL for that record. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: -- Populate the DNS Validating Resolver Cache. -- Attempt to delete a record from the 'Key' cache.
bugs.impact: Undesired behavior due to records not being deleted as instructed. Also negative TTL.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to restart tmm to generate a completely empty DNS cache. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue preventing records from a DNS Validating Resolver's 'Key' sub-cache from being deleted when utilizing the TMSH command: delete ltm dns cache records key cache

bugs.title: Case insensitive flag is ignored on regular expression keywords in simplified Signature editor
bugs.symptoms: The case insensitive flag is not applied on regular expression keywords created using the simplified Signature editor.
bugs.conditions: A regular expression signature keyword is created and set to be case insensitive.
bugs.impact: The signature keyword is enforced as case sensitive.
bugs.workaround: The regular expression can be specified as case insensitive by prepending with "(?i)".
bugs.fix: The case insensitive flag takes effect correctly on regular expression keywords in simplified Signature editor.

bugs.title: Errors in IE11 console appearing with Bot Defense profile
bugs.symptoms: When Bot Defense profile is used and has Browser Verification enabled to either Verify Before Access, or Verify After Access, Microsoft Internet Explorer v11 (IE11) Browsers may display the following errors in the browser console: HTML1512: Unmatched end tag. a.html (26,1) HTML1514: Extra "<body>" tag found. Only one "<body>" tag should exist per document. a.html (28,1)
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is enabled with Browser Verification. -- End user clients are using the IE11 browser.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic error messages appear in an end user's browser console.
bugs.workaround: In order to work around this issue, inject the scripts to the '<body>' tag instead of the '<head>' tag. This can be done using this tmsh command: tmsh mod sys db dosl7.parse_html_inject_tags value after,body,before,/body`

bugs.title: Deleting policies using select all feature on non-Common partition attempts to delete all policies across all partitions
bugs.symptoms: Deleting policies using select all feature on non-Common partition attempts to delete all policies across all partitions, not just in the active partition.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple partitions, each with at least one policy. -- In one of the non-Common partitions, check the box next to 'Name' to select all the polices under that partition, and click delete.
bugs.impact: The system posts a confirmation message to deletes all policies across all partitions rather than all policies on that specific partition.
bugs.workaround: Do not click the 'Name' check box, select each policy individually to delete.

bugs.title: peer-cert-mode set to 'always' does not work when client-ssl is enabled with session-ticket
bugs.symptoms: When a session is restored using a session-ticket, the peer-cert-mode setting is not acknowledged.
bugs.conditions: -- Session tickets are enabled. -- The peer-cert-mode in the client SSL profile is set to `always'. -- A session is restored using a ticket.
bugs.impact: The SSL client is validated only once, instead of each time.
bugs.workaround: Disable session ticket.

bugs.title: Class name mismatch is not caught
bugs.symptoms: The datagroup referenced in irule is different from data group definition and the error is not caught at validation. During config load, you see this error: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/myrule] error: Unable to find value_list
bugs.conditions: The datagroup referenced in an iRule is different from data group definition.
bugs.impact: The error is not caught at validation, and TMM errors out at run time.
bugs.workaround: Use the right name. Note: The name is case sensitive.

bugs.title: Unable to login using LDAP authentication with a user-template
bugs.symptoms: User cannot login using remote LDAP authentication. This occurs because LDAP with user-template uses user-template username as DN for search.
bugs.conditions: LDAP authentication configuration includes user-template, which is not a valid DN.
bugs.impact: Remote LDAP authentication users are unable to login.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Create a specific user for bind by configuring bind-dn and bind-pw and remove user-template. -- Switch to local authentication.

bugs.title: After a software upgrade, the BIG-IP system does not use the correct hostname for logging.
bugs.symptoms: After performing a regular software upgrade during which the configuration was rolled forward, the log messages for all daemons except tmm on the upgraded unit, report the default hostname (i.e., localhost) instead of the hostname assigned to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Performing a software upgrade to BIG-IP version 11.5.6, 11.5.7, 11.5.8, or 12.1.4 while rolling forward the existing configuration. This can also happen when you first set up remote syslog on a new LTM on an affected version.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to the BIG-IP system itself. However, a BIG-IP Administrator may wrongly assume that the configuration failed to load the configuration due to the default hostname being visible in the logs. This is not the case; the BIG-IP system correctly loads the configuration post-upgrade. If you are concentrating logs to an external server this may make it difficult to determine where some logs originated.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, run the following command: bigstart restart syslog-ng Note: This issue occurs only the very first time one of the affected versions is booted. Once the issue has been worked around once, the issue does not recur. Therefore, this workaround can be considered permanent.
bugs.fix: After software upgrade, the BIG-IP system now uses the intended hostname for logging.

bugs.title: Data operation attempt on object that has not been loaded
bugs.symptoms: While assigning VLANs to Traffic Matching Criteria, you get an error: 01070712:3: Data operation attempt on object that has not been loaded.
bugs.conditions: This occurs while trying to add or modify VLANs on a Traffic Matching Criteria.
bugs.impact: Error is reported; unable to add or modify VLAN assignment to Traffic Matching Criteria.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue to allow configuration of VLANs to Traffic Matching Criteria object.

bugs.title: Rewrite plugin can crash during initial configuration load
bugs.symptoms: Rewrite plugin can crash if the configuration is large enough to block mcpd from responding for more than 60 seconds. Following messages appear in /var/log/ltm: warning sod[6200]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat rewrite0 fails action is restart.
bugs.conditions: -- Very large configuration that takes time to load (observed with ~100 virtual servers). -- Low performance platform.
bugs.impact: Rewrite operation crashes, writes core file, and restarts normally. This happen only during initial config load and does not affect traffic.

bugs.title: Network DoS Logging Profile does not work with other logging profiles together
bugs.symptoms: When the network DoS logging profile is configured with other logging profiles, such as AFM ACL logging profile, on the same virtual server, DoS logging does not occur.
bugs.conditions: Configure DoS logging profile on a virtual server with other logging profiles, such as AFM ACL logging profile.
bugs.impact: When DoS attack happens, no DoS attack is being logged.
bugs.workaround: Configure one general log profile for all DoS and AFM logging.
bugs.fix: Both logging profiles now work together.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition doesn't support forging MAC addresses with Mellanox ConnectX-3 virtual functions
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) does not support forging MAC addresses when using virtual functions from Mellanox ConnectX-3 adapters. Without this, features like MAC Masquerading and VLAN groups do not function.
bugs.conditions: -- VE with a Mellanox ConnectX-3 virtual function. -- Configuration requiring the use of non-default MAC addresses.
bugs.impact: Attempts to use these features with these NICs will not succeed, and traffic that relies on this configuration will not function.

bugs.title: RAM cache is not compatible with verify-accept
bugs.symptoms: The TCP profile's verify-accept option is not compatible with the RAM cache feature
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile is used with the 'verify-accept' option enabled, together with a Web Acceleration via RAM cache.
bugs.impact: There may be a log message in /var/log/tmm# describing an 'Invalid Proxy Transition'. The RAM cache feature may not handle later pipelined requests due to the proxy shutting down the connection.
bugs.workaround: Do not use TCP's verify-accept option together with RAM cache.
bugs.fix: RAM cache now works correctly when the TCP profile enables the verify-accept option.

bugs.title: Using TCP::close with ASM may cause a crash.
bugs.symptoms: ASM may hold HTTP requests, which prevents connection establishment to the backend. When ASM prevents connection establishment this way, it also prevents TCP::close from terminating the connection to the client. Repeated calls to TCP::close on a pipelined connection while ASM holds connection establishment may cause a counter to overflow, which triggers an assertion failure.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server is configured with ASM. -- An iRule which calls HTTP::respond and TCP::close for some requests.
bugs.impact: ASM blocks HTTP requests that are not responded to from the iRule. The client sends pipelined HTTP requests. Traffic is interrupted while the TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: TCP::close should be called once per connection, not once per HTTP request. A workaround is to guard the TCP::close call this way within the HTTP_REQUEST event: if {![info exists closed]} { set closed 1 TCP::close }

bugs.title: TMM crashes in certain situations of which iRule execution interleaves client side and server side flows
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes in certain situations in which iRule execution interleaves client-side and server-side flows.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that cause this issue are unknown, although appear to happen in at least one configuration: OneConnect with an iRule whose execution leads to that, inside TMM, the client-side and server-side flow operations interleave.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: iRule clears the right side data after execution.

bugs.title: Routing daemon NSM cores if any of interface indexes of VLANs, Tunnels or VLAN Groups are identical to loopback and tmm interfaces of Route Domains where these VLANs, Tunnels or VLAN Groups are located
bugs.symptoms: Routing daemon NSM crashes and generates a core file, then the watchdog daemon, tmrouted notices that NSM is down and restarts it, then NSM crashes and generates a core file and everything starts all over again.
bugs.conditions: This very rare situation occurs when there is a BIG-IP system with the following routing configuration: -- At least one Route Domain on a BIG-IP has the tmm and loopback interfaces generated (when Route Domain was created) in such way that one of their internal interface indexes (ifindex) is the same as the ifindex of the suspected object, in this example, it's a VLAN. -- The suspected Route Domain has a routing protocol enabled. -- The suspected object, VLAN, is added to the suspected Route Domain. In general, this rarely occurring issue occurs in response to the way route domains and VLANs are organized on the BIG-IP system and how they interact with each other in NSM, and how a collision occurs.
bugs.impact: Routing Daemon NSM crashes and generates a core file.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the BIG-IP system. If this does not resolve the issue, you must re-create all VLANs.

bugs.title: Unknown notify message types unsupported in IKEv2
bugs.symptoms: IKE negotiation fails when an unrecognized notify payload type is seen in a message processed by IKEv2.
bugs.conditions: Receiving an IKE message that contains a notify payload whose numeric type value is unrecognized by IKEv2.
bugs.impact: Negotiation fails with an aborted connection, preventing tunnel creation.
bugs.workaround: A peer can suppress notification payloads with advisory values that get rejected by IKEv2 within the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: All unknown notify types are now logged and then ignored.

bugs.title: IKEv2 ignores passive=true setting in ike-peer
bugs.symptoms: An IKEv2 ike-peer object can be configured in passive mode, but passive mode does not work.
bugs.conditions: An ike-peer has passive set to true.
bugs.impact: The ike-peer can still initiate an IKE tunnel negotiation. Passive mode does not work, and the BIG-IP system is the initiator.

bugs.title: Added DB variable to force setting RA bit in response from cache
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, a response from Transparent cache may not have the RA (Recursion Available) bit set.
bugs.conditions: The issue takes place under the following conditions: -- Response going from a transparent cache. -- The msg sub-cache does not contain the query. -- The rrset sub-cache does contain the query.
bugs.impact: A response from Transparent cache does not have RA bit set.
bugs.workaround: The following iRule resolves the issue: When DNS_RESPONSE { DNS::header ra 1 }
bugs.fix: Added new DB variable dnscache.forcerecursionavailablebit which, when enabled, forces setting the RA bit in responses coming from any type of cache.

bugs.title: bigtcp does not issue a RST in all circumstances
bugs.symptoms: bigtcp does not issue a TCP reset, e.g. when using the iRule reject command on CLIENT_ACCEPTED
bugs.conditions: bigtcp in use, tcp connection, connection ungracefully shut down via a 'reject' command in an iRule
bugs.impact: TCP RST is not sent, and the SYN is silently dropped.
bugs.fix: bigtcp virtuals send now a TCP RST if needed.

bugs.title: Portal Access: cookie exchange may be broken sometimes
bugs.symptoms: Portal Access uses special HTTP request with URL '/private/fm/volatile.html' to exchange cookie data between client and BIG-IP. Sometimes the BIG-IP system might send an invalid response to such a request. As a result, no cookie data can be sent from the backend server to the client.
bugs.conditions: Invalid response to HTTP requests with the following URL: /private/fm/volatile.html.
bugs.impact: Portal Access client cannot see cookies set by the backend server. Backend server does not send cookie data to the client.
bugs.fix: Portal Access now sends correct HTTP responses with backend cookie data to the client.

bugs.title: OAuth Authorization Server returns an invalid 'sub' claim in JWT access token when 'subject' field is configured to be a session variable other than the default
bugs.symptoms: Invalid 'sub' claim in JWT access token that is generated by OAuth Authorization Server.
bugs.conditions: -- OAuth Authorization Server is configured to return JWT access token. -- Subject field is configured to be a session variable other than the default '%{session.assigned.uuid}'.
bugs.impact: Invalid value in 'sub' claim in JWT access token. If OAuth resource server depends on the value of 'sub' claim, then that functionality does not work.
bugs.workaround: Add Variable assign agent after OAuth Authorization agent, and assign session.assigned.oauth.authz.token.subject with the session variable name such as the following: session.logon.last.logonname.
bugs.fix: OAuth Authorization Server sends valid value in 'sub' claim in the generated JWT token when subject is configured to use a session variable.

bugs.title: Unable to edit LTM/AFM Policies that belong to an Application Service (iApp) using the WebUI.
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new rule or modifying an existing rule in a LTM/AFM Policy policy using the WebUI, the operation fails and an error similar to the following example is returned: Transaction failed:010715bd:3: The parent folder is owned by application service (/Common/MyPolicy.app/MyPolicy), the object ownership cannot be changed to ().
bugs.conditions: -- The LTM/AFM Policy belongs to an Application Service (iApp). -- The modification is attempted via the WebUI.
bugs.impact: Unable to make changes to existing LTM/AFM Policies.
bugs.workaround: Use the tmsh utility to make the necessary modifications to the LTM/AFM Policy. For example, the following command modifies an existing rule: tmsh modify ltm policy myapp.app/Drafts/myapp_l7policy rules modify { 0 { conditions modify { 0 { http-method equals values { GET POST } } } } }

bugs.title: Unable to use an iRule to classify traffic that has already been classified.
bugs.symptoms: If network has already been classified (for example as icmp), then re-classifying it in an iRule will fail.
bugs.conditions: -- CLASSIFY::application used in CLIENT_ACCEPTED iRule -- Traffic arrives that has already been classified
bugs.impact: iRule fails to re-classify the traffic.
bugs.fix: A bigdb variable has been added, tmm.gpa.srdb.defer_finalization. The default value is false. If set to true, it will allow an iRule to reclassify traffic that has already been classified.
bugs.behavior: A new bigdb variable has been added, called tmm.gpa.srdb.defer_finalization. The default value is false. If set to true, it will allow you to reclassify traffic that has already been classified.

bugs.title: Strings in APM GUI: Do not use 'none' to mean 'empty value'
bugs.symptoms: In TMSH, 'none' is a special keyword for attributes of type string that is interpreted as an empty value. However, in the APM user interface, if you type 'none' for any field expecting a string value, it is not considered empty.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when typing 'none' as a string value throughout the APM GUI.
bugs.impact: The configuration does not operate as expected.
bugs.workaround: Leave fields blank if you want them to be empty in the APM GUI. Do not use 'none' to mean 'empty' for any field requiring a string in the APM GUI.

bugs.title: Subroutine name should use partition name and policy name
bugs.symptoms: When you create API per-request policy using the same name as a policy from another partition, BIG-IP generates an error similar to the following: java.net.ProtocolException: status:400, body:{"code":400,"message":"transaction failed:01070734:3: Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (subroutine_properties) object ID (/TST/svc1-my_auth svc1-my_prp). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:subroutine_properties status:13)","errorStack":[],"apiError":2}.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure an API protection per-request policy in one partition with the same name as a policy in another partition. -- Attempt to import or export the policy.
bugs.impact: Import / export functionality fails.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that names for API protection per-request policies are unique.
bugs.fix: The name generated for API protection per-request policies now uses partition name combined with the policy name, so the issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Allow duplicate FQDN ephemeral create/delete for more reliable FQDN resolution
bugs.symptoms: When using FQDN nodes and pool members, ephemeral pool members may not be created as expected immediately after a configuration-load or BIG-IP reboot operation.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on affected BIG-IP versions when: 1. Multiple FQDN names (configured for FQDN nodes/pool members) resolve to the same IP address. 2. DNS queries to resolve these FQDN names occur almost simultaneously. 3. The BIG-IP version in use contains the fix for ID 726319. The occurrence of this issue is very sensitive to timing conditions, and is more likely to occur when there are larger numbers of FQDN names resolving to a common IP address.
bugs.impact: When this issue occurs, some subset of ephemeral pool members may not be created as expected. As a result, some pools may not have any active pool members, and will not pass traffic. This issue, when it occurs, may persist until the next DNS queries occur for each FQDN name, at which point the missing ephemeral pool members are typically created as expected. Using the default fqdn interval value of 3600 seconds, such downtime would last approximately one hour.
bugs.workaround: To minimize the duration of time when pools may be missing ephemeral pool members, configure a shorter fqdn interval value for the FQDN nodes: tmsh mod ltm node fqdn-node-name { fqdn { interval ## } } Where ## is the desired number of seconds between successive DNS queries to resolve the configure FQDN name.
bugs.fix: When using FQDN nodes and pool members, ephemeral pool members will be created as expected following a configuration-load or BIG-IP reboot operation. However, messages similar to the following may be logged when the DNS server returns a different set of IP address records to resolve the FQDN name: err mcpd[20479]: 01020066:3: The requested Node (****) already exists in partition ****. err mcpd[20479]: 01020066:3: The requested Pool Member (****) already exists in partition ****.

bugs.title: F5 Adaptive Authentication feature has been removed
bugs.symptoms: F5 Adaptive Authentication feature has been removed from the product beginning with the v15.0.0 release. This version removed: -- Adaptive auth configuration from admin UI (Authentication : F5 Adaptive Authentication (MFA)). -- Corresponding online help. -- Adaptive Auth agents from the list of agents in VPE (F5 MFA Device Registration, F5 MFA User Verification under Authentication tab). -- The reports from admin UI Access :: Overview :: F5 Adaptive Auth (MFA).
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use the F5 Adaptive Authentication feature from BIG-IP Admin UI.
bugs.impact: No F5 Adaptive Authentication-related features exist in this release.

bugs.title: IKEv2 debug logging an uninitialized variable leading to core
bugs.symptoms: Logging an internal error might result in core.
bugs.conditions: When ike_sa variable is uninitialized.
bugs.impact: Loss of tunnels due to core.
bugs.fix: Ike_sa is now initialized to hold a valid value before logging takes place.

bugs.title: TMM memory leak
bugs.symptoms: -- TMM memory utilization baseline is slowly increasing. -- The 'allocated' column of the 'tcl' row in the memory_usage_stat tmctl table is high and is close to the 'max_allocated' value.
bugs.conditions: -- The header-insert option in a custom HTTP profile is configured. -- The profile is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Degraded performance, and eventual out-of-memory condition that may trigger a TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Instead of the profile header-insert, use HTTP::header iRule commands.
bugs.fix: The header-insert option can now be configured in HTTP profiles without causing a TMM memory leak.

bugs.title: RADIUS Acct STOP message is not being sent when configured with route domain for HA Pool setup
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS Acct STOP message is not being sent when configured with route domain for HA Pool setup
bugs.conditions: -- Configure Floating IP with route domain. -- Configure RADIUS accounting server with Pool Setup. -- Configure the virtual server containing the access policy to use the RADIUS Accounting server. -- Access the virtual server.
bugs.impact: -- START message is being sent through proper egress floating IP address. -- STOP message is not sent, and the system logs the following error message: -- err tmm1[11193]: 01490586:3: (null):Common:8a505e8c: Processing radius acct stop message failed, connection failure. -- err tmm1[11193]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_RTE. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access_session.c, Function: access_session_final_callback, Line: 4439.
bugs.workaround: This issue is present only when the floating IP address is configured with a non-default route domain. It works fine with the default route domain. Use of default route domain is recommended.
bugs.fix: RADIUS Acct STOP message is now sent as expected.

bugs.title: Thales nethsm-thales-rfs-install.sh script failing with / partition full
bugs.symptoms: nethsm-thales-rfs-install.sh fails with errors / partition full or /shared/nfast/bin/anonkneti: No such file or directory
bugs.conditions: Installing Thales RFS using the script: nethsm-thales-rfs-install.sh.
bugs.impact: Failed Thales RFS installation.
bugs.workaround: Modify nethsm-thales-rfs-install.sh script as follows. Replace: mkdir -p /shared/nfast for tar_file in $nfast_agg_tar $nfast_ctls_tar $nfast_user_tar $nfast_pkcs11_tar do tar -C / -xvf $nfast_path$tar_file with mkdir -p /shared/nfast for tar_file in $nfast_agg_tar $nfast_ctls_tar $nfast_user_tar $nfast_pkcs11_tar do tar -C /shared/nfast -xvf $nfast_path$tar_file --strip-components=2

bugs.title: APD/APMD may consume excessive resources
bugs.symptoms: APD/APMD may consume excessive resources when processing certain requests
bugs.conditions: -- APM provisioned and enabled. -- The service type is either SWG Explicit or Clientless Mode 3.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially degrading overall throughput or leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: For Clientless Mode 3, replace with Clientless Mode 1 to work around the issue.
bugs.fix: APD/APMD now consumes the expected resources when processing requests

bugs.title: Addition of receive status code to DNS HTTP/HTTPS monitors
bugs.symptoms: This feature adds an additional status code match option for the DNS HTTP/HTTPS monitors to act as a gating check for the current receive-string-match functionality.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure a DNS HTTP/HTTPS monitor with receive status code and receive string parameter selected. -- Assign this monitor to a DNS resource, either pool member or virtual server.
bugs.impact: Resource becomes available or unavailable depending on whether the server response contains the status code or receive string defined in the monitor.
bugs.workaround: This is a new feature.
bugs.fix: Receive status code feature adds an additional status code match option for DNS HTTP/HTTPS monitors to act as a gating check for the current receive-string-match functionality. This is a new parameter in these monitors and is used to mark a virtual server or pool member available or not available.

bugs.title: Pool Members may not be updated accurately when multiple identical database monitors configured
bugs.symptoms: When two or more database monitors (MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle) with identical 'send' and 'recv' strings are configured and applied to different pools (with at least one pool member in each), the monitor status of some pool members may not be updated accurately. Other parameters of the affected monitors that differ (such as 'recv row' or 'recv column' indicating where the specified 'recv' string should be found in the result set) may cause pool members using one of the affected monitors to connect to the same database to be marked UP, while pool members using another affected monitor may be marked DOWN. As a result of this issue, pool members that should be marked UP or DOWN by the configured monitor may instead be marked according to another affected monitor's configuration, resulting in the affected pool members being intermittently marked with an incorrect state. After the next monitor ping interval, affected pool members members may be marked with the correct state.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when multiple database monitors (MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle) are configured with identical 'send' and 'recv' parameters, and applied to different pools/members. For example: ltm monitor mysql mysql_monitor1 { ... recv none send "select version();" ... } ltm monitor mysql mysql_monitor2 { ... recv none send "select version();" ... }
bugs.impact: Monitored pool members using a database monitor (MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle) randomly go offline/online.
bugs.workaround: To avoid this issue, configure each database monitor with some unique value within the 'send' and 'recv' parameters. For example: ltm monitor mysql mysql_monitor1 { ... recv none send "select version();" ... } ltm monitor mysql mysql_monitor2 { ... recv 5.7 send "select version();" ... }
bugs.fix: The system now correctly updates pool members when multiple identical database monitors are configured.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources while processing FIX traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the TMM may consume excessive resources when processing traffic for a Virtual Server with FIX profile applied.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server with FIX profile.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes FIX traffic as expected.

bugs.title: CAPTCHA Custom Response fails when using certain characters
bugs.symptoms:
When setting the CAPTCHA Custom Response in the Bot Defense GUI, saving the profile fails when using certain characters. For example, using the following response will return the error: 'black' unknown property This question is for testing whether you are a human visitor and to prevent automated spam submission.


%BOTDEFENSE.captcha.image% %BOTDEFENSE.captcha.change%
What code is in the image\? %BOTDEFENSE.captcha.solution%
%BOTDEFENSE.captcha.submit%

Your support ID is: %BOTDEFENSE.captcha.support_id%.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to configure custom CAPTCHA response in the Bot Defense profile GUI.
bugs.impact: Cannot configure custom CAPTCHA response in the Bot Defense Profile GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH or REST API to configure the CAPTCHA Custom Response.
bugs.fix: Configuring custom CAPTCHA response page in the Bot Defense Profile no longer fails when using certain characters.

bugs.title: Refreshing sessions fails with 'All[Read Only]' partitions
bugs.symptoms: While trying to refresh Access :: Overview : Active Sessions in the GUI, you get an error 'No Access'.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a user with operator level or higher attempts to refresh the Overview tab under Access in the GUI while in the 'All[Read Only]' partition.
bugs.impact: 'No Access' page error after clicking on Refresh button.
bugs.workaround: Use the Refresh button of the browser to refresh the entire page.
bugs.fix: When logged in as operator/admin, you can now refresh the page in 'All' partition without error.

bugs.title: TMM may crash in busy environment when handling HTTP responses
bugs.symptoms: When load balancing HTTP requests, the BIG-IP system matches client-side and server-side connections. When connections are shutting down, a race condition may occur on a busy system and peer connection reference can be lost.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has a standard virtual with HTTP profile and HTTP router. -- The BIG-IP system has high CPU utilization.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes causing failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The race condition has been corrected, so TMM no longer crashes in a busy environment when handling HTTP responses.

bugs.title: Drive model WDC WD1005FBYZ-01YCBB2 must be added to pendsect drives.xml
bugs.symptoms: Below messages get logged to /var/log/messages -- notice syslog-ng[15662]: Configuration reload request received, reloading configuration; -- warning pendsect[31898]: skipping drive -- Model: WDC WD1005FBYZ-01YCBB2 -- warning pendsect[31898]: No known drives detected for pending sector check. Exiting
bugs.conditions: Using hardware containing drive model WDC WD1005FBYZ-01YCBB2.
bugs.impact: The system logs the messages because the drive model is not listed in /etc/pendsect/drives.xml.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit /etc/pendsect/drives.xml as follows: 1. Give write permissions to modify file: chmod u+w /etc/pendsect/drives.xml 2. Open the file and add the following at the end of the file, before default: <snip> <WD1005FBYZ> <offset firmware="RR07">0</offset> <offset firmware="default">0</offset> <family> "wd_Gold"</family> <wd_name>"Gold"</wd_name> </WD1005FBYZ> <DEFAULT> <firmware version="default"> <offset>0</offset> </firmware> <name> "UNKNOWN"</name> <family> "UNKNOWN"</family> <wd_name>"UNKNOWN"</wd_name> </DEFAULT> </model> </drives> 3. Save and close the file. 4. Remove write permissions so that no one accidentally modifies this file: chmod u-w /etc/pendsect/drives.xml 5. Run the following command and check /var/log/messages to verify no errors are seen: /etc/cron.daily/pendsect

bugs.title: qkview may contain sensitive information
bugs.symptoms: For more information see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.conditions: For more information see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.impact: For more information see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.workaround: For more information see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.fix: For more information see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048

bugs.title: Large user database size
