bugs.impact: A particular live update attempt may skip a day.
bugs.workaround: Perform the live update manually.

bugs.title: Continual mcpd process restarts after removing big logs when /var/log is full
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP device suddenly stops passing traffic. You might see errors similar to the following: err mcpd[15230]: 01070596:3: An unexpected failure has occurred, TAP creation failed (tmm): Permission denied - net/validation/routing.cpp, line 168, exiting...
bugs.conditions: This might occur when when /var/log is full and then you remove big logs.
bugs.impact: The mcpd process restarts continuously. This occurs because tmm blocks mcpd from restarting after /var/log fills up.
bugs.workaround: Empty the contents of big size log files under /var/log and reboot the BIG-IP system. If that does not resolve the problem, restart all processes (bigstart restart) or reboot the box.

bugs.title: Firewall rule to block ICMP/DHCP moved from 'required' to 'default' to allow mgmt interface ICMP to be blocked by user configuration
bugs.symptoms: If a firewall is configured on the management port with an ICMP rule, after upgrading to v14.1.x or later, the ICMP rule does not work. This is because the iptables INPUT chain calls f5required, f5acl, and f5default rules in that order, and ICMP is explicitly allowed in the f5required chain, meaning ICMP never reaches the f5acl chain which is where user defined filters for the mgmt interface are placed.
bugs.conditions: - Firewall rules are configured on the management port (System >> Platform >> Security) - One or more of those rules are configured to block ICMP traffic (of any type)
bugs.impact: ICMP packets cannot be blocked with a firewall rule to drop on the management port. ICMP packets are allowed from the management port and will not increase the packet 'Count' reported under System >> Platform >> Security, even if explicitly allowed by a rule.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands after upgrading to v14.1.x or later from earlier versions, to any version where this fix for this ID is not present. ' # Create a new file : /config/id760355.sh #----------------------------------------- #!/bin/bash # Moves the ICMP allow rule from f5required to f5default, replicating the fix in ID760355 # logmsg() { echo "$(realpath $0): $1" | logger -p local0.info } logmsg "Running - waiting for pccd to start" if timeout 180 bash -c 'until pgrep -x "pccd" > /dev/null ; do sleep 2; done' ; then logmsg "pccd has started - applying iptables fix for ID760355" sleep 2 /sbin/iptables -D f5required -p icmp -j ACCEPT 2> /dev/null if [ "$?" == 0 ] ; then logmsg "Moved iptables ICMP accept rule from f5required to f5default" /sbin/iptables -I f5default -p icmp -j ACCEPT else logmsg "No existing iptables ICMP allow rule to move - no changes made" fi else logmsg "pccd did not start - fix for ID760355 has not been applied" fi #----------------------------------------------- # Append these lines to the existing file /config/startup (note the need to use :w! to save the file in vim due to it being read-only) echo Executing $0 | logger -p local0.info timeout 600 /config/id760355.sh&
bugs.fix: ICMP firewall rule has been moved from the f5-required to f5-default.

bugs.title: Users with Application Security Administrator role cannot delete Scheduled Reports
bugs.symptoms: User accounts configured with the Application Security Administrator role cannot delete scheduled reports, while they can create/view/edit them.
bugs.conditions: -- Logged on with a user account configured as an Application Security Administrator. -- Attempting to delete a scheduled report.
bugs.impact: Cannot complete the delete operation. Deleting scheduled reports requires root/admin intervention.
bugs.workaround: Use root or a user account configured as Administrator to delete scheduled reports.
bugs.fix: User accounts configured with the Application Security Administrator role can now delete Scheduled Reports

bugs.title: Update Alias Address field with default placeholder text
bugs.symptoms: Unable to update Alias Address field with the default value under Local Traffic :: Monitors :: [MonitorName] after removing everything from the input field and updating again with the placeholder text.
bugs.conditions: -- Using a system running software in which the GUI supports Chinese characters. -- Remove content from the Alias Address field under Local Traffic :: Monitors:: [MonitorName]. -- Enter the default placeholder text.
bugs.impact: Unable to update the Alias Address input field with default placeholder text after replacing the said field with blank text or a valid value.
bugs.workaround: Pass empty value or ::
bugs.fix: Allow monitors to update with default placeholder text for Alias Address

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT: Next active ingress queue filling
bugs.symptoms: When running MRF SIP ALG with SNAT, the ingress queue may fill, causing messages to be dropped on the next-active device.
bugs.conditions: -- The active device determines that an operation can be skipped because the details are already discovered processing a previous message. -- The next-active device has not yet processed the previous message and is not able to skip the operation.
bugs.impact: Mirroring state is lost for the connection.
bugs.fix: When the connection is mirrored, the processing operation is not skipped on either the active or next-active device.

bugs.title: GARP is not sent from newly active device after failover for FW NAT policy rule's dest prefixes
bugs.symptoms: After failover, there is no GARP from the newly active device for FW NAT policy rule's dest prefixes.
bugs.conditions: Configure FW NAT policy rules with proxy arp enabled for destination prefixes. After failover no GARP is sent for those destinations prefixes.
bugs.impact: After failover traffic can fail/degrade.
bugs.workaround: No workaround other than forcing the initial active HA device to be active again.
bugs.fix: The system now sets the high availability (HA) unit correctly for FW NAT policy.

bugs.title: High number of vcmp guests on clusters and discovery appliances may result in retries for guest deployment
bugs.symptoms: - Guests coming up with retries and - Messages like below in the LTM log Guest (XXX): Killing VM process.
bugs.conditions: - Clusters or discovery appliances host - High number of vcmp guests being deployed
bugs.impact: VCMP guests may become unable to pass traffic.

bugs.title: HA connection might stall on Active device when the SSL session cache becomes out-of-sync
bugs.symptoms: You see 'SSL handshake timeout' error messages in LTM log, and high availability (HA) system performance becomes degraded.
bugs.conditions: This might occur in either of the following scenarios: Scenario 1 -- Manual sync operations are performed during while traffic is being passed. -- SSL Connection mirroring is enabled. Scenario 2 -- Saving configuration on an HA Standby node during while traffic is being passed. -- SSL Connection mirroring is enabled.
bugs.impact: -- In Scenario 1, the sync operations causes the session cache to be out-of-sync between active and standby nodes. -- In Scenario 2, the save operation clears the session cache on the standby node. As a result, the session cache might be out-of-sync between active and standby nodes. In either Scenario: -- SSL Connection mirroring fails and posts the timeout message. -- The HA system performance becomes degraded due to SSL connection timeout.
bugs.workaround: -- Disable SSL session caching by setting 'Cache Size' in the client SSL profile option to 0. -- Set device management sync type to Automatic with incremental sync.

bugs.title: System Integrity Status: Invalid after BIOS update
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP system boots, it performs a System Integrity Check. The System Integrity Status may return one of three states: Valid, Unavailable, or Invalid. This issue causes the System Integrity Status to return a value of 'Invalid'.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP systems that have been manufactured using a earlier BIOS version. -- Updating to a newer BIOS version.
bugs.impact: The System Integrity Status returns a status of Invalid, which may falsely indicate that the system BIOS or OS has been compromised.
bugs.workaround: Install the new BIOS, which fixes the issue that causes the 'Invalid' status to be reported, and, on systems where the BIOS and OS have not been compromised, returns a status of 'Valid'.
bugs.fix: The System Integrity Status check now return 'Valid' for systems that have not been compromised.

bugs.title: Connection reset is seen when Category lookup agent is used in per-req policy
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system sends reset to client when Category Lookup agent is used in per-req policy.
bugs.conditions: -- APM or SSLO is licensed and provisioned. -- URLDB and SWG are not provisioned. -- Category Lookup agent is used in the policy to process custom categories.
bugs.impact: Connection reset is seen on client from APM/SSLO box.
bugs.workaround: Modify Category Lookup agent 'lookup-type' property to 'custom-only' via TMSH, for example, by using a command similar to the following: modify apm policy agent category-lookup example_prp_act_category_lookup_ag lookup-type custom-only
bugs.fix: Category lookup agent in per-req policy now successfully processes custom categories, so the reset no longer occurs.

bugs.title: PEM iRule to set policy in rigorous loop may crash tmm due to rare timing conditions
bugs.symptoms: tmm coredump
bugs.conditions: -- Using an iRule to apply a referential policy in a rigorous loop. -- This is a rarely occurring timing issue.
bugs.impact: Traffic impact due to tmm coredump. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now validates session presence before applying the policy.

bugs.title: After installing a UCS that was taken in forced-offline state, the unit may release forced-offline status
bugs.symptoms: After installing a UCS that was taken in forced-offline state, the unit may release forced-offline status (e.g., transitions to standby or active).
bugs.conditions: Installing UCS that was taken in forced-offline state on clean installed unit.
bugs.impact: Unit may become active/standby before intended (e.g., during maintenance).
bugs.workaround: After installing the UCS, ensure that the unit is in forced-offline state as intended. If not in forced-offline state, force the unit offline before proceeding.

bugs.title: Enabling user to configure nonce disabled/enabled from Mgmt GUI login as well as CLI
bugs.symptoms: When Remote client cert-ldap authentication is enabled in BIG-IP and ocsp-responder is configured. By default nonce was always added in ocsp request
bugs.conditions: -- Remote client cert-ldap authentication is enabled in BIG-IP and ocsp-responder is configured.
bugs.impact: A new configurable parameter "ssl-ocsp-use-request-nonce" is introduced in httpd, to configure whether to send the nonce in ocsp request. Default value is On
bugs.fix: 1.Configure BIG-IP for Remote-cert-ldap authentication 2.Set httpd ssl-ocsp-use-request-nonce on in httpd profile 3.Capture the ocsp packet 4.When httpd ssl-ocsp-use-request-nonce is on, ocsp request should contain OCSP nonce in the extensions

bugs.title: Live update notification is shown only for provisioned/licensed modules
bugs.symptoms: Live update notification in the left top corner of the screen was shown even when you cannot install updates, e.g., no permissions or no license/provisioning.
bugs.conditions: -- There is update for non-provisioned/licensed module. -- Attempt to install the update.
bugs.impact: A notification appears and it cannot be removed.
bugs.fix: Live update notification is now shown only for provisioned/licensed modules.

bugs.title: Configuring a route-domain causes diskmonitor error in logs
bugs.symptoms: Configuring a non-default route-domain results in a diskmonitor error in logs: warning diskmonitor[14972]: 011d0002:4: Skipping net:[4026532306]. Stat returned message: /usr/bin/stat: cannot read file system information for net:[4026532306]: No such file or directory.
bugs.conditions: -- Install or upgrade to v14.1.0 or v15.0.0. -- Non-default route-domain configured on VLAN.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact. The message logged does not indicate functional issues.
bugs.workaround: This issue can be worked around with two methods. The first is by creating a syslog-ng filter. 1. Log in to the TMOS shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: ----- tmsh ----- 2. To edit syslog, type the following command: ----- edit /sys syslog ----- 3. When syslog configuration opens in the vi text editor, copy and paste the entire entries below: ============ CUT BELOW ============== modify syslog { include " # Workaround for ID760468 to remove diskmonitor messages filter f_no_audit { not message(＼"AUDIT|diskmonitor.*Skipping net:＼"); };" } ============ CUT ABOVE ============== 4. Exit the text editor by typing the following key sequence: ----- :wq! ----- 5a. At the following prompt, type y to save the changes to the file: Save changes? (y/n/e) The tmsh utility prompt returns. 5b. If the syslog filter contains syntax errors, the tmsh utility returns the following prompt: There were errors. Continue editing (y) or discard changes (n) (y/n) Correct the errors until there are no more errors flagged. 6. Save the configuration by typing the following command: ----- save /sys config ----- The second is by modifying the diskmonitor script as follows. Note: This change does not replicate between blades, does not ConfigSync, is not preserved as part of a UCS archive, and is not preserved across software installs on a system. 1. Mount /usr as rw (read-write). 2. Open /usr/bin/diskmonitor in an editor, locate the line that references '/shared/em', and add this immediately above it: || substr($mountline[1], 0, 4) eq 'net:' 3. Mount /usr as ro (read-only). Here is a one-line command string you can use: mount /usr -o remount,rw && if [ ! -f /usr/bin/diskmonitor.id760468 ]; then /bin/cp /usr/bin/diskmonitor{,.id760468}; fi && sed -ie "/^.*shared＼/em.*＼$/i＼ || substr(＼$mountline[1], 0, 4) eq 'net:'" /usr/bin/diskmonitor && (perl -c /usr/bin/diskmonitor || echo "WARNING: DISKMONITOR SCRIPT IS NO LONGER VALID PERL") && mount /usr -o remount,ro
bugs.fix: Configuring a non-default route-domain no longer results in diskmonitor errors in the LTM log.

bugs.title: GTM iQuery connections may be reset during SSL key renegotiation.
bugs.symptoms: During routine iQuery SSL renegotiation, the iQuery connection will occasionally be reset.
bugs.conditions: This occurs occasionally during routine renegotiation.
bugs.impact: The affected iQuery connection is briefly marked down as the connection is marked down before the connection is immediately re-established.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround.
bugs.fix: GTM iQuery renegotiations no longer cause the error that reset the connection.

bugs.title: Apache spawns more processes than the configured limit, causing system low memory condition
bugs.symptoms: Apache (httpd) process count MaxClients on BIG-IP systems is set to '10' in the configuration. When more requests are received, Apache spawns more processes than 10, consuming more memory.
bugs.conditions: Numerous clients trying to connect simultaneously to the BIG-IP GUI.
bugs.impact: System low memory condition can severely impact application/system performance, and sometimes triggers Out-Of-Memory (OOM) Killer, so critical applications might be terminated.
bugs.workaround: Complete the following procedure: 1. Modify /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf to have the following configuration outside of the prefork module (global): MaxClients 10 2. Run the following command: bigstart restart httpd

bugs.title: Traffic processing interrupted by PF reset
bugs.symptoms: CPU usage increases after PF reset. Traffic between client and server is interrupted.
bugs.conditions: -- E710 NICs are used. -- Reset PF.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP instance requires a restart after PF reset to resume traffic processing.
bugs.workaround: Restart the BIG-IP device.
bugs.fix: A TMSH db variable ve.ndal.exit_on_ue, is introduced to enable/disable device restart on PF reset. On restart, a new error message within /var/log/tmm is written. Error message: "Restarting TMM on unrecoverable error."

bugs.title: Invalid configuration parameters are visible when Dos Vector is in "Auto Detection/Multiplier Based Mitigation"
bugs.symptoms: Configure Dos Vector to use "Threshold Mode" -> "Auto Detection/Multiplier Based Mitigation" 1. Enable "Bad Actor Detection -Parameters Per Source IP Detection/Mitigation Threshold EPS are visible. 2. Enable "Attacked Destination Detection" -Parameters Per Destination IP Detection/Mitigation Threshold EPS are visible.
bugs.conditions: Dos Profile Vector "Threshold Mode" -> "Auto Detection/Multiplier Based Mitigation"
bugs.impact: Some parameters are visible that should not be. There is no negative system behavior.
bugs.fix: Check for Threshold Mode, before enabling or disabling fields

bugs.title: On systems with multiple versions of BIG-IP in use, the 'invalid' System Integrity Status may persist
bugs.symptoms: The system security state reported by the shell utility 'tpm-state' may report 'Invalid'.
bugs.conditions: -- The system contains a volume running BIG-IP software version that does not support Trusted Platform Module (TPM). -- You install a version that does support TPM. -- The system is rebooted, from the old (non-TPM-capable) BIG-IP version to the new, TPM-capable version.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system reports an invalid TPM status upon the first boot of the upgraded BIG-IP 14.1.0 slot.
bugs.workaround: Rebooting the system again into 14.1.0 after initially booting into 14.1.0 resolves the issue.

bugs.title: PEM flow filter with DSCP attribute optimizes traffic resulting in some PEM action enforcement
bugs.symptoms: Some PEM action enforcement does not work with flow filter with PEM attribute set.
bugs.conditions: Flow filter has the Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) attribute set
bugs.impact: Some PEM actions such as http-redirect do not perform as expected.
bugs.workaround: Set the DSCP to the default value
bugs.fix: The operation now includes the packet DSCP value while evaluating the flow filter.

bugs.title: Retransmitted TCP packet has FIN bit set
bugs.symptoms: After TCP sends a packet with FIN, retransmitted data earlier in the sequence space might also have the FIN bit set.
bugs.conditions: -- Nagle is enabled. -- TCP has already sent a FIN. -- A packet is retransmitted with less than MSS bytes in the send queue.
bugs.impact: The retransmitted packet has the FIN bit set even if it does not contain the end of the data stream. This might cause the connection to stall near the end.
bugs.workaround: Set Nagle to disabled in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: The incorrect FIN bit is removed.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP installer fails to automatically detect installation media.
bugs.symptoms: Image2disk command does not automatically detect repository. As a result, installation with image2disk command may not work. Here is an example of the affected image2disk command syntax. switch_root:/# image2disk --format=volumes --nosaveconfig --nosavelicense
bugs.conditions: -- 14.1.0 clean install using DVD-ROM or USB thumb drive. -- Using a command that does not specify a repository.
bugs.impact: Installer cannot start unless you explicitly specify the repository.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Manually specify repository while running image2disk command. For example, the following command successfully starts installation with DVD-ROM (/cdserver) or USB thumb drive (/mnt/thumb/<ISO>): switch_root:/# image2disk --format=volumes --nosaveconfig --nosavelicense /cdserver switch_root:/# image2disk --format=volumes --nosaveconfig --nosavelicense /mnt/thumb/<ISO> -- At the command line, type 'start', and the interactive software installation starts.

bugs.title: TPM system integrity check may return invalid status when booting into BIG-IP 14.1.0
bugs.symptoms: The Trusted Platform Module (TPM) system integrity check may return an invalid status. As a result of this issue, you may encounter one or more of the following symptoms: -- While the system boots to BIG-IP 14.1.0, you observe an error message that appears similar to the following example: tpm-status-check[5025]: System Integrity Status: Invalid -- After rebooting the system to different volumes, you continue to observe the previous error message.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following condition is met: You reboot a system running either BIG-IP 13.1.x or 14.0.0 (including their point releases) to BIG-IP 14.1.0.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system reports an invalid TPM status and TPM is non-functional.
bugs.workaround: To recover from this issue, you must delete the grub configuration file and reboot the system twice for an automatic repair to occur. To do so, perform the following procedure: Impact of workaround: The system will not be available while performing multiple reboots. F5 recommends that you perform this procedure during an appropriate maintenance window. 1. Log in to the command line of the affected system. 2. Mount the boot partition by typing the following command: mkdir -p /mnt/boot; mount /dev/mapper/$(ls /dev/mapper | grep boot) /mnt/boot 3. Delete the grub.multiboot.cfg file by typing the following command: rm -f /mnt/boot/grub2/grub.multiboot.cfg 4. Reboot the system by typing the following command: reboot Note: The system software fixes the grub.multiboot.cfg file automatically upon booting. 5. When the system has completed booting, log in to the command line and reboot the system again by typing the following command: reboot This final step properly boots the system with TPM enabled.
bugs.fix: Rebooting a system no longer returns the TPM error.

bugs.title: Updating BIG-IP 14.1.x Linux kernel to RHEL7.5
bugs.symptoms: The kernel for the BIG-IP 14.1.x Linux kernel needs updating to RHEL7.5.
bugs.conditions: Using the most current version of the BIG-IP software.
bugs.impact: The Linux kernel update is a typical function of ongoing BIG-IP software development.
bugs.fix: Below are the advantages of kernel update: -- Ease of maintenance. -- Security fixes part of RHEL 7.5. -- New / Enhanced feature support.

bugs.title: TCP Verified-Accept with proxy-mss enabled does not honor the route-metrics cache when sending the SYN to the server
bugs.symptoms: TCP Verified-Accept with proxy-mss enabled does not honor the route-metrics cache when sending the SYN to the server
bugs.conditions: -- TCP Verified-Accept option is used. -- The proxy-mss is enabled. -- The route-metrics cache entry is enabled.
bugs.impact: Route-metrics cache entry does not get used.

bugs.title: On BIG-IP VE, 'snmpwalk -v 2c -c public localhost .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.1.7.3' returns only /appdata details.
bugs.symptoms: Executing 'snmpwalk -v 2c -c public localhost .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.1.7.3' returns only /appdata details.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Virtual Edition
bugs.impact: The snmpwalk command shows the details of all partitions on previous versions. It now shows only the '/appdata' details.
bugs.workaround: No workaround exists for this issue currently.

bugs.title: System integrity messages not logged
bugs.symptoms: On TPM-equipped platforms, log messages indicating recovery from a very rarely triggered condition, where the TPM chip needs to be cleared, are not being recorded in the logs on boot.
bugs.conditions: -- TPM-equipped platforms. -- Rarely triggered condition in which the TPM chip needs to be cleared.
bugs.impact: No message indicating the need to clear the TPM. Note: The need to clear the TPM does not affect the subsequent operation of system integrity checks.
bugs.workaround: None. The TPM is automatically cleared on boot. Once cleared, it operates normally. Using remote attestation by submitting a QKview file to iHealth and checking the System Integrity status in the resulting report will reliably indicate any tampering in the BIOS or system startup files.
bugs.fix: TPM needing to be cleared message is now logged.

bugs.title: Virtual Server discovery may not work after a GTM device is removed from the sync group
bugs.symptoms: LTM configuration does not auto-discover GTM-configured virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: -- GTM is deprovisioned on one or more GTM sync group members, or the sync group is reconfigured on one or more members. -- Those devices remain present in the GTM configuration as 'gtm server' objects. -- iQuery is connected to those members.
bugs.impact: Virtual servers are not discovered or added automatically.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Manually add the desired GTM server virtual servers. -- Delete the 'gtm server' objects that represent the devices that are no longer part of the GTM sync group. These can then be recreated if the devices are operating as LTM-configured devices. Note that deleting a gtm server object will also remove any of its virtual servers from gtm pools.

bugs.title: Allow Device Certificate renewal from BIG-IP Configuration Utility
bugs.symptoms: Unable to renew Device Certificate from System :: Certificate Management : Device Certificate Management : Device Certificate :: server.crt in non-English BIG-IP configurations.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to renew a device certificate on the System :: Certificate Management : Device Certificate Management : Device Certificate :: using the server.crt-equivalent on a non-English BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Unable to renew Device Certificate from the BIG-IP Configuration Utility.
bugs.workaround: Use a command of the following syntax, replacing key name, cert name, and # of days with your values: openssl req -new -x509 -key ../ssl.key/server.key -days <# of days> -out server.crt For example, to renew the siteserver.key and siteserver.crt for 90 days, use the following command: openssl req -new -x509 -key ../ssl.key/siteserver.key -days 90 -out siteserver.crt
bugs.fix: The system now allows Device Certificate renewal from BIG-IP Configuration Utility.

bugs.title: MSIE logon page form alignment right might not get displayed correctly
bugs.symptoms: In Microsoft Internet Explorer, the logon page form is not aligned properly.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following settings are configured: -- In General Page Style Settings :: Page Alignment, and choose Right -- In Layout Settings :: Page layout, choose Form Right. -- In Form Settings :: Form alignment, choose Right.
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic issue. There is no functional impact.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by modifying the following selector in apm_full.css: table#main_table table#interaction_table Add following lines at the end: <? if(($_GET['ctype'] == 'IE' || $_GET['ctype'] == '') && getCssCustiomizationVar("form_alignment") == "right" ) { ?> float: %[form_alignment]; <? } ?>
bugs.fix: In Microsoft Internet Explorer, the logon page form is now aligned properly.

bugs.title: Remove Obsolete APM keys in BigDB
bugs.symptoms: Several APM/Access BigDB keys are obsolete
bugs.conditions: This is encountered on BIG-IP software installations.
bugs.impact: The db keys are obsolete and can be safely ignored.
bugs.workaround: Remove those keys from BigDB and control plane side as those are not being used. But don't remove the keys which has still dependancies with other modules and also don/'t remove those keys used in upgrade
bugs.fix: The following db keys have been removed from the system: Log.AccessControl.Level Log.ApmAcl.Level Log.SSO.Level Log.swg.Level Log.AccessPerRequest.Level Log.access.syslog Log.access.db

bugs.title: Memory corruption when using C3D on certain platforms
bugs.symptoms: When using Client Certificate Constrained Delegation (C3D), memory corruption can occur, which can eventually lead to a tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: C3D is enabled on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: TMSH may utilize 100% CPU (single core worth) when set to be a process group leader and SSH session is closed.
bugs.symptoms: TMSH does not correctly handle absence of input stream after closing interactive SSH session and remains active in an infinite loop using 100% CPU.
bugs.conditions: If TMSH is a process group leader, it will not be killed when the parent shell is terminated upon SSH session close. This is a rare case, as TMSH must be deliberately promoted to a process group leader, e.g., with the 'setsid' command. Usually the shell process is a group leader and, when it is terminated upon SSH session close, it kills its child processes, including TMSH.
bugs.impact: The equivalent of one CPU core is utilized to 100% by the TMSH process. It may be mostly scheduled on one core or spread over multiple control plane cores.
bugs.workaround: TMSH should not be intentionally promoted to a process group leader. You can kill all TMSH processes using the command: killall -9 tmsh Warning: This command kills both abandoned and in-use TMSH processes. The latter can include other users' TMSH shells, and even system-level processes invoking the TMSH utility internally. Killing all TMSH processes can lead to various unexpected failures. You can use the 'top' command to see which TMSH process is using high CPU (e.g., 90% or more), and kill just those, as those are the likely zombie processes. You can kill specific TMSH processes using the command: kill -9 <pid> Where <pid> is the process ID of the TMSH instance to kill.
bugs.fix: I/O error handling in TMSH has been corrected, so it no longer ignores absence of input stream which led to infinite loop.

bugs.title: RST from non-floating self-ip may use floating self-ip source mac-address
bugs.symptoms: A RST from non-floating self-ip may use floating self-ip source mac-address when AFM or ASM is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM or ASM is enabled. -- RST generated from non-floating self-ip address.
bugs.impact: An L2 switch may update the fwd table incorrectly.
bugs.fix: The system now uses the correct source mac-address under these conditions.

bugs.title: FastL4 might drop invalid PMTU (ICMP) message
bugs.symptoms: In an n-path deployment, FastL4 might drop invalid PMTU (ICMP) messages.
bugs.conditions: N-path (Direct Server Return) is configured.
bugs.impact: FastL4 might drop invalid PMTU (ICMP) message. As BIG-IP does not see the full handshake, this is expected.
bugs.fix: The db key TM.FastL4_invalid_pmtu_passthrough was added to allow for this situation.

bugs.title: The Nokia alert configuration is not correct for all clearing events
bugs.symptoms: Alarms may not get correctly entered or cleared from the Nokia Alarm database.
bugs.conditions: A Nokia alarm is generated and then the alert condition clears.
bugs.impact: The alarm is not cleared when it should be. This can lead to confusion about error conditions.
bugs.fix: The values have been corrected.

bugs.title: Mysql error is displayed when saving UCS configuration on BIG-IP system when MySQL is not running
bugs.symptoms: When saving the configuration to a UCS file, the process tries save the IPS learning information stored in the MySQL database. MySQL runs only when particular modules are provisioned. If MySQL was previously running as a result of different provisioning, but is not currently running, saving the configuration to a UCS file succeeds, but the system reports a spurious message during the operation: Can't connect to local MySQL server through socket '/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock.
bugs.conditions: -- Saving the configuration to a UCS file. -- BIG-IP system provisioning only includes modules that do not require MySQL. These modules may include: + LTM + FPS + GTM (DNS) + LC + SWG + iLX + SSLo -- BIG-IP system was previously provisioned with a module that starts MySQL, which results in the creation of the file /var/db/mysqlpw. These modules may include: + APM + ASM + AVR + PEM + AFM + vCMP
bugs.impact: The error message is cosmetic and has no impact on the UCS save process.

bugs.title: Internal sync-change conflict after update to local users table
bugs.symptoms: -- The 'top' command shows Java and mcpd becoming CPU intensive. -- /var/log/audit shows many 'modify { user_role_partition { user_role_partition_user ...' -- /var/log/restjavad-audit.0.log shows many REST API calls to 'http://localhost:8100/mgmt/shared/gossip' from the peer.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a new admin user with bash access on a device.
bugs.impact: High CPU usage (Java and mcpd) on control and analysis plane.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, follow these steps: 1. Sync from the device where the user was created. 2. Run the following command on all devices: tmsh restart sys service restjavad Although Java and mcpd will still show high CPU usage even after restart, waiting a few minutes enables the processes to return to normal.

bugs.title: FastL4-steered traffic might cause SSL resume handshake delay
bugs.symptoms: When a FastL4 virtual server steers traffic to another SSL-enabled virtual server, there can be a delay on SSL session resumption because SSL is unable to identify the connection flow. Additionally, it has been observed that if fallback persistence is configured, the BIG-IP system might fail to start the connection serverside.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 virtual server. -- iRule is used to steer traffic to another virtual server with client SSL enabled. -- Multiple tmm's.
bugs.impact: -- Potential impact to SSL performance. -- Possible connection failure.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue: -- Disable FastL4. -- Enable OneConnect.
bugs.fix: FastL4-steered traffic no longer causes SSL resume handshake delay.

bugs.title: BIG-IP GTM might not always sync a generation of a DNSSEC key from its partner
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP GTM might not always sync a generation of a DNSSEC key from its partner.
bugs.conditions: Generating a DNSSEC key. Note: This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC keys may not be synced.

bugs.title: Static generation of rolling DNSSEC keys may be missing when the key generator is changed
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP system may lose DNSSEC keys if the key generator is changed from rolling keys to static keys
bugs.conditions: DNSSEC key generation is changed from rolling to static.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC keys may be lost.

bugs.title: Incorrect enforcement of explicit global parameters
bugs.symptoms: A false positive or false negative enforcement of explicit global parameter.
bugs.conditions: -- A configuration with more than 255 security policies. -- Policies configured with an explicit parameter that is unique (for example, 'static', a disabled signature, etc.). -- Attempt to enforce that parameter.
bugs.impact: Wrong blocking/violations. The parameter is not found, and the wildcard * parameter is enforced instead.
bugs.workaround: Make the explicit parameters a wildcard parameter.
bugs.fix: Explicit parameters are enforced correctly on all parameters.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT: Added additional details to log events
bugs.symptoms: Subscriber name is not included in debug log events for temporary subscriber registration creation and deletion.
bugs.conditions: debug log events for temporary subscriber registration creation and deletion.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but the associated MRF SIP ALG with SNAT issue might be difficult to debug.
bugs.fix: Subscriber ID is now included in the log events.

bugs.title: Part of audit log messages are also in other logs when strings are long
bugs.symptoms: Parts of audit logs are found also in other logs like /var/log/user.log and /var/log/messages.
bugs.conditions: -- When audit log message strings are long.
bugs.impact: Log messages are duplicated. There is no indication of system functionality, and you can safely ignore them.
bugs.workaround: Modify the syslog-ng maximum length of incoming log messages from 8192 to 16384 bytes: tmsh modify sys syslog include "options { log-msg-size(16384); };"

bugs.title: Empty hostname in remote log after modification
bugs.symptoms: The hostname is empty in ASM remote log after certain modifications to hostname.
bugs.conditions: Device hostname is modified such that the new value precedes the old value alphabetically.
bugs.impact: The hostname is empty in ASM remote log.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM after modifying hostname.

bugs.title: Incorrect advertised next-hop in BGP for a traffic group in Active-Active deployment
bugs.symptoms: The advertised next-hop is a floating-IP of the active traffic-group on a peer BIG-IP system, although it should be the floating-IP of the traffic-group active on the current BIG-IP system. Note: A previous bug had this same symptom, but was due to a different root cause.
bugs.conditions: -- In a BIG-IP high availability (HA) configuration. -- The HA configuration is Active-Active topology. -- There are multiple traffic-groups, in which each device is active for one traffic-group.
bugs.impact: An incorrect next-hop in BGP is advertised for a traffic group in Active-Active deployment. Traffic for relevant advertised routes might go to a standby device.
bugs.workaround: Configure the floating address of a traffic group as the next-hop in its route-map.
bugs.fix: The advertised next-hop in BGP is now the smallest floating-IP active on the current BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: TMM crashes due to webroot database shared memory channel corruption when wr_urldbd daemon restarts
bugs.symptoms: Webroot daemon (wr_urldbd) crashes because of a socket handler issue that occurs when sending the URI categorization request to the BrightCloud server. Wr_urldbd daemon restarts, and during startup, it loads the downloaded database to the shared memory channel. This shared memory channel is being used by the TMM, which has no information about the wr_urldbd restart, so tmm restarts.
bugs.conditions: -- Wr_urldbd restarts (which occurs due to an issue in socket handler when sending URL categorization requests to the BrightCloud server). -- During wr_urldbd startup, the daemon starts loading the downloaded webroot database to the shared memory channel set up between the wr_urldbd and TMM. -- TMM accesses this shared memory channel to perform a URL category lookup (due to traffic).
bugs.impact: TMM restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes under these conditions.

bugs.title: TMM SIGABRT while evaluating access policy
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores while evaluating access policy.
bugs.conditions: -- Secure Web Gateway is configured and in use. -- An access policy is being evaluated.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule similar to the following: when ACCESS_POLICY_COMPLETED { set res [ACCESS::session data get "session.policy.result"] if {[string compare $res "in_progress"] == 0} { log local0.notice "rejecting" reject } log local0.notice "result :$res" }
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores under these conditions.

bugs.title: An NLRI with a default route information is not propagated on 'clear ip bgp <neighbor router-id> soft out' command in some scenarios
bugs.symptoms: Soft out reset does not work for the default route.
bugs.conditions: -- BGP enabled -- A route configuration change is made and 'clear ip bgp <IP-addr> soft in/out' is executed
bugs.impact: A default-route is not propagated in Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) by 'soft out' request.
bugs.fix: The 'clear ip bgp <IP-addr> soft in/out' command now sends all the known routes.

bugs.title: DataSafe GUI is displayed when invalid FPS licenses keys are configured
bugs.symptoms: When DataSafe license is installed and invalid FPS license keys are configured, DataSafe GUI is displayed instead of FPS GUI with a license error message.
bugs.conditions: - License DataSafe. - Configure invalid FPS license keys (license.antifraud.*).
bugs.impact: The incorrect GUI is displayed. This is a cosmetic error. The system functions as expected.
bugs.workaround: Setting database variable: license.antifraud.id = "<null>"
bugs.fix: The correct GUI is displayed.

bugs.title: F5.ip_forwarding iAPP fails to deploy
bugs.symptoms: F5.ip_forwarding iApp fails to deploy due to a syntax error in the tmsh command for syn-cookie-enable.
bugs.conditions: Deployment of the f5.ip_forwarding iApp fails unless you specify an existing FastL4 profile.
bugs.impact: Cannot deploy the f5.ip_forwarding iApp template.
bugs.workaround: To deploy the f5.ip_forwarding iApp, select 'Advanced' configuration mode and choose an existing FastL4 profile for the question 'What Fast L4 profile do you want to use?'
bugs.fix: The f5.ip_forwarding iApp template deploys the recommended FastL4 profile without error.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing local traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing local network traffic.
bugs.conditions: Multi-blade chassis, including multi-blade vCMP guests.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes local network traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Web Browser Hang on Reading Compressed Data from BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: Reading an object from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: The virtual server has both a web acceleration profile with an active application and the HTTP compression filter on it. When reading a compressible object from the web acceleration small object cache, the HTTP compression filter may compress the data, but not rewrite the Content-Length header.
bugs.impact: The client will wait for the BIG-IP to deliver the amount of data specified by the Content-Length header, but since the object was compressed, there isn't that much data to deliver.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Remove the HTTP compression filter from the virtual server. -- Mark objects smaller than 4,000 bytes as no-store.

bugs.title: tmsh show net route lookup is not showing for IPv4-mapped IPv6 address route
bugs.symptoms: Route entries for IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (::ffff:<IPv4>) are not shown using the show net route lookup command.
bugs.conditions: -- Route entry is for IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, that is ::ffff:<IPv4>. -- Dynamic Routing protocols such as OSPFv3 configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot see any dynamic routes added while IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are configured.
bugs.fix: The query for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses now shows dynamic routes added while IPv4-mapped IPv6 is configured.

bugs.title: TMSH displays TSIG keys
bugs.symptoms: TSIG key is displayed when related configuration is listed in TMSH.
bugs.conditions: Authenticated administrative user. Listing TSIG keys using TMSH.
bugs.impact: Displaying TSIG keys is a security exposure.
bugs.fix: TMSH no longer displays TSIG keys when listing configuration.

bugs.title: APM does not support adding SameSite cookie attribute to APM cookies.
bugs.symptoms: The Chrome browser version 80 changes the way it treats the SameSite cookie attribute to be complaint, according to https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-west-cookie-incrementalism-00. In this case, if the server does not set the SameSite cookie attribute, the browser treats the cookie attribute as equivalent to "samesite=Lax", which changes the behavior of how the cookie is shared with the domain, which did not originally set the cookie.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured.
bugs.impact: The latest browser (e.g., Chrome 80) stops sending the APM cookie back to the different domain, if it does not find the SameSite cookie attribute for APM cookies.
bugs.workaround: Use a customer iRule to add the SameSite cookie attribute to the APM cookies in HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE.

bugs.title: Custom monitor fields appear editable for Auditor, Operator, or Guest
bugs.symptoms: Mozilla Firefox browser shows custom monitor fields editable for Auditor, Operator, or Guest role users.
bugs.conditions: You can experience this issue by following these steps: 1. Create custom monitor (e.g., http, mysql, tcp). 2. Use FireFox browser to logon to the BIG-IP system Configuration utility with a user role that is Auditor, Operator, or Guest. 3. Access the custom monitor. Note that Send String, Receive String, and Receive Disable String are all grayed out. 4. Click the browser Back button. 5. Click the browser Forward button.
bugs.impact: Send String, Receive String, and Receive Disable String are now editable fields. Although the Auditor, Operator, or Guest. user can edit the fields, the Update button is still grayed out, so any entry is not saved.

bugs.title: Remove policy editing restriction in the GUI while auto-detect language is set
bugs.symptoms: While policy language was set to auto-detect, the policy editing was not allowed.
bugs.conditions: Create a new policy and set the language to auto-detect.
bugs.impact: While policy language was set to auto-detect, the policy editing was not allowed.
bugs.workaround: The policy language must be set to something other than auto-detect to allow user to edit the policy from GUI. However, policy editing is possible using REST API.
bugs.fix: The GUI restriction was removed. User can modify the policy while the language is set to auto-detect.

bugs.title: Missing charset specification in response page after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Blocking response pages are missing charset specification after upgrade, and appear garbled for non-UTF-8 policies.
bugs.conditions: -- A blocking response page is configured with non-UTF-8 characters. -- ASM is upgraded.
bugs.impact: Blocking response pages appear garbled.
bugs.workaround: To workaround this issue, follow this procedure: 1. Change the policy to transparent and save. 2. Change it back to blocking and save. 4. Apply policy. Now the response page now appears correctly.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing FastL4 traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources when processing FastL4 traffic
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 profile enabled. -- loose-init enabled.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: Disable loose-init in environments where it is not needed.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes FastL4 traffic as expected

bugs.title: Broadcast frames may be dropped
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, broadcast Ethernet frames may be dropped.
bugs.conditions: Multi-blade systems. Stand-alone appliances and VE systems are not affected. Single-blade vCMP guests are not affected.
bugs.impact: Dropped Ethernet frames.
bugs.fix: Broadcast frames are now processed as expected.

bugs.title: tmm crash after extended whitelist modification
bugs.symptoms: tmm might crash and restart.
bugs.conditions: Modifying the whitelist extended entry in tmsh.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The tmm process no longer crashes when modifying the whitelist extended entry in tmsh.

bugs.title: Specifically crafted requests may lead the BIG-IP system to pass malformed HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K50375550
bugs.conditions: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K50375550
bugs.impact: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K50375550
bugs.workaround: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K50375550
bugs.fix: For more information please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K50375550

bugs.title: param data type violation on an Integer parameter, if an integer value is sent via websocket JSON
bugs.symptoms: A false positive occurs with 'Illegal parameter data type' violation on an integer parameter, on websocket messages
bugs.conditions: An explicit parameter with type integer is configured.
bugs.impact: A false positive can occur, 'Illegal parameter data type' is reported.
bugs.fix: Fixed a false positive with integer values

bugs.title: Wr_urldbd might crash while system is in a restarting loop.
bugs.symptoms: Webroot daemon (wr_urldbd) crashes if it gets back to back SIGTERM signals. Subsequent SIGTERM is handled by default signal handler instead of registered one. As a result wr_urldbd's threads are not prevented from starting if wr_urldbd is in the process of shutting down.
bugs.conditions: -- System configuration is changing -- wr_urldbd is restarting continuously at the same time
bugs.impact: Wr_urldbd crashes during restart and generates core file.
bugs.fix: Wr_urldbd handles all signals with registered handler and does not crash.

bugs.title: Bot Defense Search Engines getting blocked after configuring DNS correctly
bugs.symptoms: Bot Defense performs a reverse DNS for requests with User-Agents of known Search Engines. A cache is stored for legal / illegal requests to prevent querying the DNS again. This cache never expires, so in case of an initial misconfiguration, after fixing the DNS configuration, or routing or networking issue, the Search Engines may still be blocked until TMM is restarted.
bugs.conditions: -- Initial misconfiguration of DNS or routing or networking issue. -- Cache stores requests to prevent future queries to DNS. -- Correct the misconfiguration.
bugs.impact: Cache does not expire and is never updated, so it retains the misconfigured requests. As a result, valid Search Engines are getting blocked by Bot Defense.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM by running the following command: bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: The internal DNS cache within Bot Defense and DoSL7 now expires after five minutes.

bugs.title: Changing a virtual server to use an address list should be prevented if the virtual server has a security policy with a logging profile attached
bugs.symptoms: If you create a virtual server with a single address ('Host' in the GUI) for both its source and destination, then configure the virtual server's security policy with a logging profile, and then (after creating the virtual server) modify the source or destination to use a traffic matching condition, the system reports no error when updating the configuration.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use a virtual server with a security policy attached that uses a logging profile with an address list as the virtual server's source or destination.
bugs.impact: An invalid configuration is not caught. When later loading the configuration, the system reports a validation error, and the configuration does not load.
bugs.fix: An error is now generated under these conditions.

bugs.title: wr_urldbd creates sparse log files by writing from the previous position after logrotate.
bugs.symptoms: After log rotation, the wr_urldbd daemon continues to write at the pre-rotate offset into the file, so the next message is written at offset N, making the file sparse, with all characters prior to position being read as nulls.
bugs.conditions: System rotates log files.
bugs.impact: Some automated systems might not be able to read log file.
bugs.fix: Log file preserves text file type after log rotation.

bugs.title: SNAT pool may use wrong address after self addresses are added/modified
bugs.symptoms: Traffic sent on different networks using a SNAT pool may select a SNAT IP address that is not on the local network.
bugs.conditions: -- SNAT pool configured with two or more addresses on different networks. -- Self IP addresses are added/modified such that: - Before the modification, two or more addresses in the SNAT pool are on the same network. - After the modification, the addresses in the SNAT pool are on different networks.
bugs.impact: The incorrect source address might impact network traffic.
bugs.workaround: Remove and re-add the members in the SNAT pool.

bugs.title: Errors in REST token requests may log sensitive data
bugs.symptoms: When requests for REST tokens generate a parsing error the logged message may contain sensitive data present in the request, including passwords.
bugs.conditions: Error in token request parsing. Typically causes include a typo or other JSON syntax error in the POST body of the REST request.
bugs.impact: Restlogs record sensitive data. Properly formatted requests do not generate this error logging and do not record sensitive data.
bugs.fix: Sensitive data is now filtered from logging.

bugs.title: Upgrade of standby BIG-IP system results in empty Local Database
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade of standby BIG-IP system results in empty Local Database.
bugs.conditions: This happens on standby device in a high availability (HA) setup.
bugs.impact: All previously existing local users disappear from the standby device. If a failover happens, then none of the local users will be able to login now.
bugs.workaround: To trigger a full database dump from the active BIG-IP system that returns the standby device's database to its original state, on the standby device, do the following: 1. Reboot. 2. Switch to a new installation volume. 3. Force stop the localdbmgr process: bigstart stop localdbmgr 4. Wait at least 15 minutes. 5. Restart the localdbmgr: bigstart restart localdbmgr

bugs.title: OSPF Hello does not work for L2 wire
bugs.symptoms: OSPF Hello does not work for L2 wire.
bugs.conditions: This always occurs for L2 wire configurations.
bugs.impact: OSPF does not perform connection.
bugs.workaround: Set the vlangroup.forwarding.override flag to enable: tmsh modify sys db vlangroup.forwarding.override value enable
bugs.fix: The problem is fixed by propagating some flags from parent to dynamic VLAN groups.

bugs.title: Opening libcryptoki-6.2.2-11.x86_64.rpm fails during SafeNet 6.2.2 client install
bugs.symptoms: When using verbose mode, SafeNet installation script emits the following benign error message: error: open of libcryptoki-6.2.2-11.x86_64.rpm failed. Even though the error is harmless, it is disturbing to have the false negative.
bugs.conditions: Install SafeNet 6.2.2 on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: This error message is benign, so you can safely ignore it.
bugs.workaround: You can either ignore this error message or turn off the verbose option of SafeNet installation script.
bugs.fix: There is now a new SafeNet client tar ball to replace the Luna_6.2.2_Client_Software.tar, so this error message no longer occurs..

bugs.title: 'Connection Rate Limit' is hidden, but 'Connection Rate Limit Mode' is not
bugs.symptoms: 'Connection Rate Limit' setting is hidden when it is appropriate to do so. However, the 'Connection Rate Limit Mode' setting is still visible, even when 'Connection Rate Limit' is hidden.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a Virtual Server with type Standard. 2. Click Configuration 'Advanced'. 3. Enter values for 'Connection Rate Limit" and "Connection Rate Limit Mode'. 4. Save the configuration. 5. Change the virtual server type to Forwarding (Layer 2).
bugs.impact: 'Connection Rate Limit' is hidden -- which it should be, but 'Connection Rate Limit Mode' is not -- which it should be as well. Although 'Connection Rate Limit Mode' is available, the system ignores any setting specified.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure 'Connection Rate Limit Mode', as it has no effect.

bugs.title: APM per-request policy variable assign agent does not support secure variable assignment
bugs.symptoms: APM per-request policy variable assign agent does not support secure assignment of variable(s).
bugs.conditions: Variable assignment agent is used in APM per-request policy and Secure option is selected from dropdown in variable assignment entry.
bugs.impact: Variables are not saved securely and are seen in plaintext.
bugs.fix: Variable assign agent in APM per-request policy can securely assign variables after fix.

bugs.title: Additional config-sync may be required after blob compilation on a HA setup in manual config-sync mode
bugs.symptoms: When manual config-sync mode is enabled for a HA setup, additional config-sync may be required after firewall blob compilation.
bugs.conditions: Firewall rule configuration modified on a high availability (HA) setup with manual config-sync mode enabled.
bugs.impact: Additional config-sync may be required after compilation completion. A warning may be given: "There is a possible change conflict between <device1> and <device2>.", and full sync may be forced.
bugs.workaround: Enable auto config-sync instead of manual config-sync.
bugs.fix: Additional config-sync is not required in these conditions.

bugs.title: Hyperv SR-IOV: MTU more than 1500 is not supported
bugs.symptoms: Packet length observed (using tcpdump or any other tool) is 1514 bytes.
bugs.conditions: 1. Hyper-V SR-IOV NICs are in use on the BIG-IP system. 2. VLAN MTU is greater than 1500 on the BIG-IP system, and MTU is greater than 1500 on client and server NICs.
bugs.impact: Jumbo frames do not work. Note: This is a limitation in the drivers themselves, and is not unique to BIG-IP systems. The same issue occurs if the MTU change is attempted from the Linux command line instead.

bugs.title: Debug information logged to stdout
bugs.symptoms: There is debug information logged to stdout -- err mcpd[6943]: 01071392:3: Background command '/usr/libexec/mdmsyncmgr -o restore' failed. -- err mcpd[6943]: 01071703:3: Postprocess action (/usr/libexec/mdmsyncmgr -o restore) failed with exit code (9).
bugs.conditions: Whenever logging config is changed.
bugs.impact: Log messages are seen when logged in via a terminal.
bugs.fix: These redundant message no longer occur.

bugs.title: Incorrect MAC Address observed in L2 asymmetric virtual wire
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect MAC Address observed in L2 asymmetric virtual wire for ICMP unreachable on UDP traffic.
bugs.conditions: L2 asymmetric virtual wire is configured.
bugs.impact: Incorrect MAC Address in teh packet when the BIG-IP system sends ICMP unreachable on UDP traffic
bugs.fix: The correct MAC address is seen in the packet that is flowing from the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Without a virtual server, responses from server to client are dropped in a BIG-IP system when the latter is deployed in L2 transparent mode using virtual wire.
bugs.symptoms: Responses from a server are not received by the client.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system deployed in L2 transparent mode using virtual wire. -- No virtual server is configured.
bugs.impact: Responses from server to client are dropped. Loss of service.
bugs.fix: Set the L2 transparent flag for the server-side flow if the client-side flow has this flag set.

bugs.title: Disabled Virtual Server Dropping the Virtual Wire traffic
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server is disabled, it drops the traffic on the virtual wire.
bugs.conditions: Virtual wire is configured and corresponding virtual server is disabled.
bugs.impact: Virtual wire traffic which is matching the disabled virtual wire is dropped.
bugs.fix: If the virtual server is blocked, virtual wire traffic ignores the configured virtual server and uses the default virtual wire server(_vlangroup). Traffic will not be dropped.

bugs.title: TMM core after long run of high volumes of traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM core, failover.
bugs.conditions: -- Running on a vCMP guest with 4 cores and 2 VIPRION B4300 Blades. -- ASM provisioned. -- Bot-defense profile attached to a virtual server. -- DoS profile attached to a virtual server. -- Antifraud profile attached to a virtual server. -- Different types of traffic running for hours. Note: This is a description of the hardware and software configuration on which this occurred; the issue has not been reproduced, so some triggering factors have not yet been identified.
bugs.impact: Failover. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Client authentication performance when large CRL is used
bugs.symptoms: Search for revoked certificate is done serially on the BIG-IP system. This causes performance impact when a large CRL (e.g., one with ~60 KB entries) is used.
bugs.conditions: -- Client authentication configured with a CRL containing a large number of entries (~60 KB). -- Associated with virtual server. -- Client connection requests arrive to be authenticated.
bugs.impact: CRL checking spikes up TMM CPU usage. Performance may be impacted.

bugs.title: nat64 and ltm pool conflict
bugs.symptoms: When a pool is assigned to a virtual server with nat64, the destination address is changed to the one of the pool, regardless if address translation is enabled or not.
bugs.conditions: vs with nat64 and pool configured.
bugs.impact: nat64 does not happen, even if the translate-address option is set to disable.
bugs.fix: When a nat64 virtual server has a pool and translate-address is disabled, the pool is utilized but nat64 is performed.

bugs.title: Traffic Learning: Accept and Stage action is shown only in case entity is not in staging
bugs.symptoms: Accept and Stage action is available, even for entities that are in staging already.
bugs.conditions: Create suggestion for the entity (e.g., Attack signature on parameter) that is in staging.
bugs.impact: Action that is not relevant is shown.
bugs.fix: Accept and Stage action is available only for suggestions on entities that are not in staging

bugs.title: Text for analyzed requests improved for suggestions that were created as result of absence of violations in traffic
bugs.symptoms: Text for analyzed requests might be misleading for suggestions that are created as result of an absence of violations in traffic: X requests triggered this suggestion from date:time until date:time. Actually: -- 'X requests' did not trigger a violation, and no sampled are requests provided. -- The format of the time in 'from date:time until date:time' is difficult to parse.
bugs.conditions: There are suggestions that were created as result of an absence of violations in traffic in the policy.
bugs.impact: Text might be misleading.
bugs.fix: Improved text for analyzed requests for suggestions that were created as result of absence of violations in traffic

bugs.title: ASM BD core when custom captcha page configured size more than 45K with %ASM.captcha.support_id% placeholder is at the end
bugs.symptoms: ASM BD crash when custom captcha page configured size is 45K
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned. - ASM policy attached to a virtual server. - CAPTCHA page size is bigger than 45 KB. - CAPTCHA protection is enabled via brute force or ASM::captcha iRule.
bugs.impact: There is an ASM BD crash that occurs upon a request protection by CAPTCHA mitigation. If configured for high availability (HA), failover occurs.
bugs.workaround: Define CAPTCHA page sizes smaller than 45 KB.
bugs.fix: ASM BD core is fixed; BD no longer crashes, even when the CAPTCHA page size is larger than 45 KM.

bugs.title: Ephemeral FQDN pool members in Partition shown as Common under Local Traffic > Pools > "Members"
bugs.symptoms: When Ephemeral FQDL pool members exist in non-Common partition, they are shown to be in the /Common partition on the Local Traffic : Pools : Members page. In the statistics view of the same object, they are shown appropriately with their non-Common partition.
bugs.conditions: -- Ephemeral FQDL pool members exist in a non-Common partition. -- View the FQDL pool members on Local Traffic : Pools : Members page.
bugs.impact: No impact to configuration, however, the display is confusing and shows contradictory partition information.

bugs.title: Connections routed to a virtual server lose per-client connection mode if preserve-strict source port mode is set
bugs.symptoms: Systems desiring to create a unique connection per connection client may silently end up with clients sharing an outgoing connection if routing uses a virtual server as the outgoing connection transport definition, and the virtual server has the source-port attribute set to preserve-strict.
bugs.conditions: -- Routing using a virtual server as the transport definition for the outgoing connection. -- The virtual server has the source-port attribute set to preserve-strict.
bugs.impact: Systems desiring to create a unique connection per connection client may silently end up sharing an outgoing connection.
bugs.fix: Per-client mode is now maintained when routing to a virtual server, even when preserve-strict is selected.

bugs.title: Security pages unavailable after switching RT mode on off few times
bugs.symptoms: Security dashboard and analytics pages display "Unable to load application" and no statistics available.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP configured to collect statistics from security modules and new statistics are generated periodically. The problem may appear when a user switches real-time mode on off few times.
bugs.impact: Security dashboard and analytics pages unavailable for at least few hours and some real-time statistics are lost.
bugs.fix: Added timeout for fetching data from statistics module.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system incorrectly flags UDP checksum as failed on x520 NICs
bugs.symptoms: When UDP checksum is 0 (zero), a BIG-IP device with an x520 NIC causes the packets to be marked as 'checksum failed'.
bugs.conditions: -- Using BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- VE is using x520 VF.
bugs.impact: UDP Packets with 0 checksum are dropped.
bugs.fix: UDP checksum failed packets are marked by the ixvf driver as 'not checksummed by hardware'. This makes software re-verify checksum instead of relying on hardware-indicated checksum pass/fail.

bugs.title: PostgreSQL database disk usage over 2 GB without AFM provisioned
bugs.symptoms: PostgreSQL uses a large amount of disk when AFM is licensed.
bugs.conditions: AFM being licensed but not in use.
bugs.impact: Increase in database file size.
bugs.workaround: Follow the procedure to dump/load the database. The dump-load procedure used as follows: 1. pg_dumpall -U postgres |gzip -1v >/shared/tmp/pgdump$(date +%s).gz 2. bigstart stop pgadmind 3. rm -rf /var/local/pgsql/ 4. bigstart start pgadmind 5. sleep 3; while pidof initdb; do sleep 1; done; sleep 3 6. zcat /shared/tmp/pgdump$(date +%s).gz|psql -U postgres template1 7. bigstart restart pgadmind

bugs.title: Send HOST header in OCSP responder request
bugs.symptoms: As per the Digicert documentation, the OCSP/CRL connections require either HTTP1.1 or HTTP1.0 with host header. (Digicert). LTM uses HTTP1.1 without the host header in OCSP responder request
bugs.conditions: OCSP and CRL Authentication uses HTTP1.0 for OCSP responder requests
bugs.impact: OCSP in the current BIG-IP relies on OpenSSL for its operations and current version of OpenSSL that is available in BIG-IP is 1.0.2za OpenSSL 1.0.2 is only capable of generating HTTP/1.0 requests for OCSP and CRL fetches; it does not support HTTP/1.1. This limitation prevents clients from communicating with OCSP/CRL endpoints that require HTTP/1.1, resulting in failures for revocation checks in environments where modern protocols are mandated.
bugs.workaround: Add either of these iRules to the Virtual Server Modify HTTP 1.0 to HTTP1.1 when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::version "1.1" } Add Host header when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::host "[HTTP::host]” }
bugs.fix: Support for HTTP1.1 is added. The OCSP requests for auth should now use HTTP1.1 version

bugs.title: WMI monitor may return negative values
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect or unexpected load balancing results. If you have enabled snmp.snmpdca.log then you will see negative values logged to /shared/tmp/WMIHttpAgent.log
bugs.conditions: -- Load Balancing Method is set to either Dynamic Ratio (member) or Dynamic Ratio (node) -- Metric monitored on server returns very large value For example: when monitored server has more then 4GB memory allocated
bugs.impact: WMI monitor returns negative value and incorrect Dynamic Ratio score is calculated.

bugs.title: iRule checksum created in GUI might cause config load failure in tmsh
bugs.symptoms: tmsh config load may fail and issue the message indicating mismatching checksum, similar to the following: 01071493:3: iRule (/Common/pool_select_rule) content does not match the checksum. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Select a new or existing iRule on the Local Traffic :: iRules :: iRules List page, and click 'Add Checksum". -- SSH into the BIG-IP system and run the following command: tmsh load sys config
bugs.impact: tmsh config load fails.
bugs.workaround: Do not add checksums to iRules you create in the GUI.

bugs.title: avrd high CPU utilization due to perpetual connection attempts
bugs.symptoms: avrd shows high CPU utilization. Repeated retries on auth token client failed connection attempts.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IQ system is not available (even though it is configured). -- Frequent connection retries.
bugs.impact: avrd consumes a large amount of CPU.
bugs.workaround: Correct BIG-IQ availability and restart avrd.
bugs.fix: avrd now waits between connection retries, so this issue does not occur.

bugs.title: Reboot with 'tmsh reboot' does not log message in /var/log/audit
bugs.symptoms: The tmsh reboot command is missing from /var/log/audit.
bugs.conditions: -- Reboot a system using the command 'tmsh reboot'. -- View the /var/log/audit log.
bugs.impact: The system does not log the tmsh reboot operation in the /var/log/audit log. A message similar to the following should be reported: notice tmsh[19115]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=19115 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=reboot.

bugs.title: ASM does not remove CSRT token query parameter before forwarding a request to the backend server
bugs.symptoms: CSRT query parameter observed in tcpdump on the BIG-IP system's server side.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- CSRF enabled in ASM policy.
bugs.impact: Backend app gets CSRT parameter, which might impact its business logic.
bugs.workaround: You can remove a CSRT query parameter using a URI modification iRule on the server side.
bugs.fix: The system now removes the csrt query parameter before forwarding a request to the backend server

bugs.title: Information in snmpd.conf files may be overwritten causing SNMP v3 queries to recieve 'Unsupported security level' errors
bugs.symptoms: During daemon startup, the snmpd daemon zeroes out sensitive data in the snmpd.conf files. This is done so that passwords are not available to be read on disk. This can cause problems when other daemons using the net-snmp shared libraries access snmpd.conf files for data that they need during startup. If you have 'zeroed out' data under /config/net-snmp/snmpd.conf, the system reports 'Unsupported security level' errors in response to SNMP v3 query, for example: snmpget -v 3 -u testuser -a SHA -A "testuser" -x AES -X "testuser" -l authPriv localhost sysSystemUptime.0. snmpget: Unsupported security level (Sub-id not found: (top) -> sysSystemUptime).
bugs.conditions: Custom SNMP v3 users created and exist in /config/net-snmp/snmpd.conf 'zeroed out' data: Example from /config/net-snmp/snmpd.conf where user 'testuser' has some data that is 'zeroed out' (0x 0x): usmUser 1 3 0x80001f88808047605278d46d5b "testuser" "testuser" NULL .1.3.6.1.6.3.10.1.1.1 0x .1.3.6.1.6.3.10.1.2.1 0x 0x
bugs.impact: Daemons usually start in an orderly fashion and usually do not conflict with each other. However, it is possible that they might fail to load correctly due to the zeroing out of data. For example this can cause SNMP v3 access errors for users with 'zeroed out' data under /config/net-snmp/snmpd.conf: snmpget -v 3 -u testuser -a SHA -A "testuser" -x AES -X "f5testuser" -l authPriv localhost sysSystemUptime.0. snmpget: Unsupported security level (Sub-id not found: (top) -> sysSystemUptime).
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to configure SNMP users.

bugs.title: The nsm process may crash if it detects a nexthop mismatch
bugs.symptoms: If there is a mismatch between tmrouted and nsm for the interface index or gateway of a nexthop, nsm may crash and restart.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing is in use. -- A mismatch between tmrouted and nsm for the interface index or gateway of a nexthop exists.
bugs.impact: There is a temporary interruption to dynamic routing while nsm is restarted.
bugs.fix: Prevented nsm crashing when there is a mismatch between tmrouted and nsm for the interface index or gateway of a nexthop.

bugs.title: Continuous TMM restarts when HSB drops off the PCI bus
bugs.symptoms: In the unlikely event that HSB drops off the PCI bus, TMM continuously restarts until the BIG-IP system is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which the issue occurs are unknown, but it is a rarely occurring issue.
bugs.impact: Repeated TMM restarts. Traffic disrupted until you reboot the BIG-IP system. The HSB reappears and is functional after reboot.
bugs.workaround: Manually reboot the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer gets stuck in a restart loop, as a reboot is now automatic in this scenario.

bugs.title: No swap memory available after upgrading to v14.1.0 and above
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade to v14.1.0 or higher, swap memory may not be mounted. TMM or other host processes may restart due to lack of memory.
bugs.conditions: -- System is upgraded to v14.1.0 or above. -- System has RAID storage.
bugs.impact: May lead to low or out-of-memory condition. The Linux oom killer may terminate processes, possibly affecting service. Typically management activities may be impacted, for example, a sluggish GUI (config utility) or tmsh sessions.
bugs.workaround: Mount the swap volume with correct ID representing the swap device. Perform the following steps on the system after booting into the affected software version: 1. Get the correct ID (RAID device number (/dev/md<number>)): blkid | grep swap Note: If there is no RAID device number, perform the procedure detailed in the following section. 2. Check the device or UUID representing swap in /etc/fstab. 3. If swap is not represented with the correct ID, modify the /etc/fstab swap entry to point to the correct device. 4. Enable the swap: swapon -a 5. Check swap volume size: swapon -s If the blkid command shows there is no UUID associated with the swap RAID device, use the following procedure: 1. Generate a random UUID: uuidgen 2. Make sure swap is turned off: swapoff -a 3. Recreate the swap partition with UUID generated in step 1: mkswap -U <uuid_from_step_1> <raid_device_from_step_1> 4. Run blkid again to make sure that you now have a UUID associated with the raid device: blkid | grep swap 5. edit fstab and find the line <old_value> swap swap defaults 0 0 6. Replace the old value, whether it was an incorrect UUID or a device name, with the UUID generated in step 1, for example: UUID=8b35b30b-1076-42bb-8d3f-02acd494f2c8 swap swap defaults 0 0

bugs.title: Ping6 with correctly populated NDP entry fails
bugs.symptoms: TMM NDP entries show correct info with neighbor discovery protocol (NDP) resolved but ping6 fails
bugs.conditions: This occurs only on a cluster setup. Other conditions that cause the issue are unknown.
bugs.impact: Ping6 fails for that address.

bugs.title: IKEv2 rekey fails to recognize VENDOR_ID payload when it appears
bugs.symptoms: Rekey with non BIG-IP systems can fail when a response contains a VENDOR_ID payload.
bugs.conditions: - IKEv2 Responder sends VENDOR_ID payload in rekey response. - The ipsec.log misleadingly reports: [I] [PROTO_ERR]: unexpected critical payload (type 43) Note: This message may be correctly present under other conditions, with different type constants not equal to 43.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP as the initiator of rekey drops the rekey negotiation without making further progress when the responder included a VENDOR_ID payload in a response. This will result in deleting the SA for good when the hard lifetime expires, causing a tunnel outage.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is known at this time.
bugs.fix: Handling of payload types during rekey will now ignore VENDOR_ID when it appears, the same way we ignore VENDOR_ID in other messages during IKE negotiation.

bugs.title: 'exclusiveMaximum' and 'exclusiveMinimum' from swagger are not taken into account in param creation
bugs.symptoms: Parameters generated from swagger with "exclusiveMaximum" or 'exclusiveMinimum' may not have accurate min/max setting when added to policy
bugs.conditions: Parameters in swagger file specifies numeric values for 'exclusiveMaximum' or 'exclusiveMinimum' instead of true/false.
bugs.impact: Min/max value enforcement for parameter may be incorrect when it is loaded.
bugs.workaround: Manually update the min/max values.

bugs.title: Wrong remote-role assigned using LDAP authentication after upgrade to 14.1.x and later
bugs.symptoms: When multiple attributes in a list match multiple roles, the wrong role may be assigned. Alternatively, authentication may fail when check-roles-group is disabled.
bugs.conditions: LDAP server replies with a list of attributes (e.g., list of memberOf) where more than one match existing role.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP assigns the user to the last attribute in the list that matches a role, potentially yielding a more restrictive set of permissions. Authentication may fail when check-roles-group is disabled.
bugs.fix: The correct remote-role is now assigned using LDAP authentication after upgrade to 15.1.x.

bugs.title: Hardware cryptography acceleration may fail
bugs.symptoms: Host reports the following error message: Device error: crypto codec qat-cryptoXX-Y queue is stuck.
bugs.conditions: Platform with access to Intel QAT cryptography hardware Hardware cryptography acceleration enabled
bugs.impact: Hardware cryptography acceleration failure, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware crypto acceleration for impacted device.
bugs.fix: Platforms with QAT accelerators now function as expected.

bugs.title: Web-socket enforcement might lead to a false negative
bugs.symptoms: A request that should be blocked will be passed to server.
bugs.conditions: Parse parameters flag in json profile is enabled. Requests are sent in json websocket.
bugs.impact: Bad requests may be passed to the server
bugs.workaround: Disable parse parameters flag in json profile
bugs.fix: Web-socket enforcement now filters requests as expected.

bugs.title: Aggregated Domain Names in DNS statistics are shown as random domain name
bugs.symptoms: Many DNS queries (e.g., 50000) with different query domain names are sent and AVR aggregates data it shows aggregated names using a random name taken from the first lookup table record.
bugs.conditions: -- Run 50000 DNS queries, all with different domain names. -- View Statistics :: Analytics :: DNS, and choose View By : Domain Names.
bugs.impact: There is one random domain name with a high counter value, other domains are shown with counter 1.

bugs.title: The monitor probing frequency has been adjusted because more than 20 synchronous monitors were detected.
bugs.symptoms: You see the following logged to /var/log/ltm: notice gtmd[23555]: 011ae106:5: The monitor probing frequency has been adjusted because more than 20 synchronous monitors were detected.
bugs.conditions: This can occur during normal operation of GTM.
bugs.impact: There is no impact and the system is operating normally; this is a debug message that is logged at the Notice level.
bugs.fix: Log message has been changed to log at the debug log level.
bugs.behavior: Change the log level from notice to debug for log "The monitor probing frequency has been adjusted because more than %d synchronous monitors were detected."

bugs.title: LRO packets are not taken into account for ifc_stats (VLAN stats)
bugs.symptoms: The ifc_stats do not correctly reflect the number of incoming octets/packets. There is a discrepancy between octets/packets in/out in the ifc_stats table, which tracks per-VLAN stats.
