bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION chassis provisioned in vCMP mode with more than one blade in it. -- Large configuration with many guests. -- The VIPRION chassis is rebooted. -- A different issue, of type 'Configuration from primary failed validation' occurs during startup on one or more Secondary blades. By design, MCPD restarts once on affected Secondary blades, which is the trigger for this issue. An example of such a trigger issue is ID 563905: Upon rebooting a multi-blade VIPRION or vCMP guest, MCPD can restart once on Secondary blades.
bugs.impact: -- Loss of entire configuration on previously working vCMP guests. -- The /shared/vmdisks directory, in its unmounted state, may not have sufficient disk space to accommodate all the virtual disks for the vCMP guests designated to run on that blade. As such, some guests may fail to start. -- If you continue using the affected guests by re-deploying configuration to them, further configuration loss may occur after a new chassis reboot during which this issue does not happen. This occurs because the guests would then be using the original virtual disk files; however, their configuration may have changed since then, and so some recently created objects may be missing.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround to prevent this issue. However, you can minimize the risk of hitting this issue by ensuring you are running a software version (on the host system) where all known 'Configuration from primary failed validation' issues have been resolved. If you believe you are currently affected by this issue, please contact F5 Networks Technical Support for assistance in recovering the original virtual disk files.

bugs.title: SCP file transfer hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the SCP file transfer system does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: Administrative user with SCP access.
bugs.impact: Under certain conditions, the SCP file transfer system does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: The SCP file transfer system now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: TMSH allows creation of duplicate community strings for SNMP v1/v2 access
bugs.symptoms: TMSH allows you to create multiple access records with the same IP protocol, same Source IP network, and same community string.
bugs.conditions: Duplicate access records are created in TMSH.
bugs.impact: Unintended permissions can be provided when an undesired access record with the correct community string is matched to a request instead of the desired access record.
bugs.workaround: Use the Configuration Utility to manage SNMP v1/2c access records. (The GUI properly flags the error with the message: The specified SNMP community already exists in the database. If you use tmsh, ensure that community strings remain unique within each Source IP Network for each IP protocol.

bugs.title: TMM can crash on certain vCMP hosts after modifications to VLANs and guests.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and produces a core file. TMM logs show the crash was of type SIGFPE, with the following panic message: notice panic: ../base/vcmp.c:608: Assertion "guest has vlan ref" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- The vCMP host is a platform with more than one tmm process per blade or appliance. + VIPRION B4300, B4340, and B44xx blades. + BIG-IP iSeries i15x00 platforms -- A VLAN is assigned to a vCMP guest. -- The TAG of the VLAN is modified. -- The VLAN is removed from the vCMP guest.
bugs.impact: While TMM crashes and restarts on the host, traffic is disrupted on all the guests running on that system. Guests part of a redundant pair may fail over.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes on certain vCMP hosts after modifications to VLANs and guests.

bugs.title: Firewall rule list configuration causes config load failure
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh load sys config' reports a syntax error. The syntax error is reported on 'security firewall rule-list rule' configuration.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only if any of the rule-list rule ip-protocol contains one of the following protocols: Note: You can see the mismatched protocol names in the /etc/protocols listing file (column 1 and column 3 differ): bbn-rcc 10 BBN-RCC-MON # BBN RCC Monitoring nvp 11 NVP-II # Network Voice Protocol dcn 19 DCN-MEAS # DCN Measurement Subsystems ospf 89 OSPFIGP # Open Shortest Path First IGP crdup 127 CRUDP # Combat Radio User Datagram
bugs.impact: The system fails to load the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the configuration file: /config/bigip_base.conf 1. Replace the ip-protocol name from rule-list configuration: -- Change BBN-RCC-MON to bbn-rcc. -- Change NVP-II to nvp. -- Change DCN-MEAS to dcn. -- Change OSPFIGP to ospf. -- Change CRUDP to crudp. 2. Save the file. 3. Issue the command: tmsh load sys config. The configuration now loads without syntax errors.

bugs.title: HA failover network disruption when cluster management IP is not in the list of unicast addresses
bugs.symptoms: If the cluster management IP address is not in the list of failover network unicast addresses, the blade management IP addresses in the unicast mesh will not be able to receive failover messages from peer devices.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION chassis or vCMP guest on a VIPRION chassis. -- Per-blade management IP addresses listed in the failover network unicast mesh. -- No cluster management IP address listed.
bugs.impact: The blade management IP addresses in the failover network unicast mesh stop functioning: [root@VIP2200-R75-S5:/S1-green-P::Standby:In Sync] config # tmctl -w 200 -S sod_tg_conn_stat entry_key local_failover_addr remote_device_name pkts_received transitions last_msg status ----------------------------- ------------------- ------------------------------ ------------- ----------- ---------- ------ 10.200.75.8->10.10.10.1:1026 10.10.10.1:1026 VIP2200-R75-S8.sin.pslab.local 3249 3 1555399271 1 10.200.75.8->10.200.75.3:1026 10.200.75.3:1026 VIP2200-R75-S8.sin.pslab.local 0 1 0 0 <-- 10.200.75.8->10.200.75.4:1026 10.200.75.4:1026 VIP2200-R75-S8.sin.pslab.local 0 1 0 0 <--
bugs.workaround: You can add an explicit management IP firewall rule to allow this traffic: tmsh modify security firewall management-ip-rules rules add { accept_udp_1026 { place-before first ip-protocol udp destination { ports add { 1026 } } action accept } } This will add a firewall policy so port 1026 is no longer locked down, and the blade management IP addresses in the unicast mesh should begin to function properly.

bugs.title: ASM modifies cookie header causing it to be non-compliant with RFC6265
bugs.symptoms: When ASM strips the cookie header from the ASM cookies, it leaves the cookie header in a way that is not compliant with RFC6265 on two aspects: 1. No space after the semicolon 2. A cookie with no value is sent without the equals sign
bugs.conditions: -- ASM Security Policy is used -- Request includes an ASM cookie
bugs.impact: Some web servers may refuse to handle non-compliant Cookie headers, causing the application flow to break.
bugs.workaround: Disable the cookie stripping by modifying the DB variable as follows: tmsh modify sys db asm.strip_asm_cookies value false
bugs.fix: ASM now strips the ASM cookies from the request in a way that is compliant with RFC6265.

bugs.title: SIP monitor in non default route domain is not working.
bugs.symptoms: SIP pool members in non-default route domain are being marked as unavailable even though they are available.
bugs.conditions: SIP pool members in non default route domain.
bugs.impact: SIP service unavailable.

bugs.title: Bot Defense challenge blocks requests with long Referer headers
bugs.symptoms: The Bot Defense challenge may block the client if the Referer header is between about 1400 characters and 3072 characters long. This client may get blocked by TCP RST, or suffer from a challenge loop.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense with Verify before Access, or Proactive Bot Defense are configured -- Request has a Referer header that is between ~1400 and 3072 characters long
bugs.impact: Legitimate browsers may get blocked or suffer from a challenge loop
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to override the Referer header from the HTTP_REQUEST event, to make it shorter.
bugs.fix: Challenges with long Referer headers no longer block legitimate clients.

bugs.title: Support to enable/disable reusing serverside TIME_WAIT connections
bugs.symptoms: Currently, the serverside connections in TIME_WAIT state are reused for new serverside connections (by default) before TIME_WAIT expires. A mechanism is required to disable reusing the TIME_WAIT connections if needed.
bugs.conditions: A new serverside connection request is made that matches an existing TIME_WAIT connection and connection is reused.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system behavior on reusing TIME_WAIT connections is configurable based on the tmm.reuse.ss.timewaitconns sys db. tmm.reuse.ss.timewaitconns: enabled (the default) -- A new serverside connection request comes for a TIME_WAIT serverside connection. -- Connection is reused. tmm.reuse.ss.timewaitconns: disabled - A new serverside connection request comes for a TIME_WAIT serverside connection - "Port in use" error is returned
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: A mechanism to enable/disable reusing TIME_WAIT connections on serverside is provided via a sys db.

bugs.title: HTTP profile Response Size stats incorrect for keep-alive connections
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP profile Response Size static is incorrectly updated per-response using the cumulative number of response bytes seen for the lifetime of the connection, rather than the bytes seen per-response.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile configured -- HTTP connection reused for multiple requests/responses
bugs.impact: The HTTP profile Response Size statistics may be incorrectly reported and do not correlate to actual traffic seen.
bugs.fix: The HTTP Response Size statistics are correctly updated using per-response values.

bugs.title: AVR dashboard displays incorrect client/server bytes-in/bytes-out stats
bugs.symptoms: AVR dashboard for SSL Orchestrator shows incorrect bytes-in and bytes-out stats for both client and server.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL Orchestrator licensed and provisioned. -- Application Visibility and Reporting (AVR) is licensed and provisioned.
bugs.impact: AVR does not report correct stats.
bugs.fix: AVR dashboard for SSL Orchestrator now shows correct bytes-in and bytes-out stats for both client and server.

bugs.title: tmrouted may crash while processing Multicast Forwarding Cache messages
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, tmrouted may crash while processing Multicast Forwarding Cache (MFC) messages.
bugs.conditions: tmrouted processing MFC messages.
bugs.impact: tmrouted crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: tmrouted now processes MFC messages as expected.

bugs.title: 'License expired' message not specific
bugs.symptoms: When booting into a 14.0.0 version on which restricted license mode is not enabled, the license-expired message shows the generic 'license expired' message, but does not list the specific modules.
bugs.conditions: Modules with license not enabled. Note: This occurs in a specific scenario in which you upgrade to an unlicensed version, revert to the previous version, don't change the license, and upgrade back to the original version. This fails as it is designed to, but reports the general 'invalid license' failure rather than the more specific one.
bugs.impact: License expired message is generic, and does not list the specific modules which are not enabled on 14.0.0.
bugs.workaround: None. Specific modules not enabled for 14.0.0 may show 'generic' license expired. You can cross-check if there are any modules which are not enabled for 14.0.0.

bugs.title: Firewall rule list configuration causes config load failure
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh load sys config' has a syntax error. The syntax error is reported on 'security firewall rule-list rule' configuration.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only if any of the rule-list rule ip-protocol contains one of the following protocols: -- BBN-RCC-MON -- NVP-II -- DCN-MEAS -- OSPFIGP -- CRUDP
bugs.impact: The system fails to load the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the configuration file: /config/bigip_base.conf 1. Replace the ip-protocol name from rule-list configuration: -- Change BBN-RCC-MON to bbn-rcc. -- Change NVP-II to nvp. -- Change DCN-MEAS to dcn. -- Change OSPFIGP to ospf. -- Change CRUDP to crudp. 2. Save the file. 3. Issue the command: tmsh load sys config. The configuration now loads without syntax errors.

bugs.title: named or dnscached cannot bind to IPv6 address
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios, the named process cannot bind to IPv6 addresses. This occurs because the dnscached process listens to the wildcard IPv6 address port 53 (i.e., :::53) so it cannot respond to queries sent to IPv6 addresses. Following message is reported in ltm log: err named[16593]: binding TCP socket: address in use.
bugs.conditions: -- The named and dnscached processes are not running. -- The dnscached process is started first. -- The named process is started later.
bugs.impact: The named process does not respond to the queries that are sent to IPv6 addresses at port 53.
bugs.workaround: 1) Stop both named and dnscached process. 2) Edit the startup script for dnscached to start in IPv4-only mode. 2a) On BIG-IP system, open the file /etc/bigstart/startup/dnscached. 2b) Add "-4" to the command line option of dnscached. 3) Restart the processes: bigstart restart named dnscached
bugs.fix: The dnscached startup script has been modified to start in IPv4-only mode, so it does not listen on any IPv6 address.

bugs.title: Increase efficiency of sPVA DoS protection on wildcard virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Certain characteristics of received packets can reduce the efficiency of filtering during a denial-of-service attack
bugs.conditions: -- AFM using hardware-based sPVA DoS protection. -- bad-actor filtering configured on a wildcard virtual server.
bugs.impact: CPU usage increases, which might result in legitimate packets being dropped or delayed.
bugs.workaround: Configure bad-actor at the global-level instead of at the wildcard-virtual-server level.
bugs.fix: This release provides increased efficiency of sPVA DoS protection on wildcard virtual servers.

bugs.title: PEM with traffic group can lead to local cache leaks on STANDBY if there is an ACTIVE-ACTIVE transition
bugs.symptoms: PEM spm_local_cache could get leaked on the STANDBY chassis.
bugs.conditions: -- If the high availability (HA) cluster switches to ACTIVE-ACTIVE mode during its lifetime. -- PEM running in a Traffic-group configuration.
bugs.impact: Memory on the STANDBY chassis get leaked.
bugs.fix: Fixed a potential PEM spm_local_cache leak on the STANDBY chassis.

bugs.title: Monpd uses excessive memory on requests for network_log data
bugs.symptoms: Monpd allocates excessive memory on multi-blade devices, and in some cases the kernel may kill monpd. The following log signature may be encountered in /var/log/kern.log: err kernel: : [1537424.588160] Out of memory: Kill process 28371 (monpd) score 117 or sacrifice child
bugs.conditions: This can occur in a multi-blade BIG-IP environment when you are displaying pages that query for network_log data, for example Bot Defense requests in the event log, or realtime AVR data.
bugs.impact: Large fluctuations in host memory usage, occasionally leading to OOM events.
bugs.fix: A db variable has been added: avr.eventlogsreportrownumber, which controls the number of logs displayed. The db variable default is 10000, and supports a range from 100 through 1000000. Note: Using the maximum value may trigger the behavior described here. The system behavior depends on the specific machine hardware.

bugs.title: Fix RFC issue with the multipart parser
bugs.symptoms: false positive or false negative attack signature match on multipart payload.
bugs.conditions: very specific parsing issue.
bugs.impact: A parameter specific excluded signature may be matched or un-matched.
bugs.fix: Multi part parser issue was fixed.

bugs.title: ASM brute force counts unnecessary failed logins for NTLM
bugs.symptoms: False positive brute force violation raised and login request is blocked
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- ASM Brute force protection enabled for NTLM login type
bugs.impact: login request blocked by asm policy
bugs.workaround: Define higher thresholds in brute force protection settings
bugs.fix: asm code has been fixed and do not count unnecessary failed logins for NTLM

bugs.title: BSD HSL remote logging does not log FQDN from BIG-IP 12.0.0 and later
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP systems configured to send remote syslogging via HSL using BSD format, if the configuration of use_fqdn (yes), only the simple HOSTNAME is logged instead of the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN).
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP version 12.0.0 or later is installed. -- System configured for BSD HSL remote syslogging with use_fqdn (yes).
bugs.impact: BSD HSL remote logging does not log FQDN; it logs the HOSTNAME instead. Note: This also occurs for SNMP, i.e., with pre-v12.x software, the whole fqdn is retrieved, and with v12.x and later, only the hostname is retrieved.

bugs.title: BIG-IP systems might not complete a short ICAP request with a body beyond the preview
bugs.symptoms: An ICAP request (REQMOD or RESPMOD) body goes out to the ICAP server as far as a preview. If the server responds 100-continue, only a single chunk of the remaining payload might be sent to the server. Eventually the connection times out.
bugs.conditions: -- An ICAP profile is configured with a preview. -- The HTTP request or response to be modified has a body that is more than one chunk longer than the preview length, yet short enough to be completely buffered in BIG-IP system before the preview is sent to the ICAP server. -- The ICAP server responds with 100-continue.
bugs.impact: Only the first chunk of payload is sent after the preview, and eventually the connection times out.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now sends the complete ICAP request to the server, and the transaction completes normally.

bugs.title: SNMPv3 user name configuration allows illegal names to be entered
bugs.symptoms: The validation of SNMPv3 user names is not strict, and allows users of both the GUI and TMSH to enter badly formed user names. When the SNMP daemon reads these user names from the snmpd.conf file, validation rejects the names.
bugs.conditions: Poorly formed SNMPv3 user names can be entered into configuration, for example, names with embedded spaces.
bugs.impact: The user names are not accepted by the SNMP daemon when it reads the configuration from the snmpd.conf file.
bugs.workaround: Use alphanumeric characters for SNMPv3 user names, and do not include embedded spaces in the names.

bugs.title: WebSocket traffic is transmitted with unknown opcodes
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not preserve WebSocket frames. Frame headers and payload may be reordered such that a header for a second frame may be sent out in the middle of a first frame's payload. Frame boundaries get skewed and payload gets interpreted as headers.
bugs.conditions: A request logging profile is configured on a WebSocket virtual server.
bugs.impact: WebSocket frames are not preserved such that traffic appears to be garbage. -- If request logging is enabled, client frames may not be preserved. -- If response logging is enabled, server frames may not be preserved.
bugs.workaround: Remove the request logging profile.

bugs.title: BIG-IP allows enabling deprecated Network Access compression, causing intermittent tunnel traffic drops with Edge Client
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent tunnel traffic drops when Network Access compression is enabled. Tunnel stability is restored when Compression is disabled. No client-side errors clearly indicating unsupported configuration.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP APM with Network Access resource configured -- Compression enabled on Network Access resource -- Edge Client version 7.2.6 or later -- VPN tunnel established -- Intermittent traffic flow over the tunnel
bugs.impact: -- Intermittent VPN tunnel instability -- Hard-to-diagnose issues, potentially leading to unknowingly enabling unsupported configurations
bugs.workaround: Disable compression in the BIG-IP Network Access config and connectivity profile config.
bugs.fix: Compression settings is now removed in Network access page in Admin webUI.

bugs.title: GTM TCP monitor does not check the RECV string if server response string not ending with \n
bugs.symptoms: GTM TCP monitor marks resource down.
bugs.conditions: TCP server respond string not ending with '\n'.
bugs.impact: Available resources are marked down.
bugs.workaround: If the TCP server is sending a text response, reconfigure the server to make sure it terminates the output with '\n'. If the TCP server can not be changed (for example if it produces binary output), it may be possible to create an external gtm monitor instead.

bugs.title: [CPM] 'Use case sensitive string comparison' has no effect on datagroup match
bugs.symptoms: The 'Use case sensitive string comparison' setting in Policy options does not have any effect on policy matching when used in combination with a datagroup.
bugs.conditions: Policy's datagroup and case sensitivity options are used together.
bugs.impact: Datagroup matching cannot be toggled using the case sensitivity matching.
bugs.workaround: Add matched strings directly into the traffic policy rule condition to perform case insensitive matching. Note: Datagroup matching using case insensitivity is not supported.
bugs.fix: The GUI is changed to reflect that case sensitivity is not supported with datagroups. A warning is also issued in /var/log/ltm if such a configuration is still selected.

bugs.title: On-Demand Certificate Authentication agent for Per-Request Policy does not work with multiple Client SSL profiles that have the 'Default SSL Profile for SNI' option disabled and assigned to a single Virtual Server
bugs.symptoms: After the client certificate has been provided, the browser waits for a response within a few minutes and then displays the error 'Page cannot be displayed'. At the same time you can watch the following informational messages in the /var/log/apm events log file: info tmm[12245]: 01870000:6: /Common/app1.example.com:Common:dd1d4e4f: Executed agent (/Common/app1.example.com_On-Demand-CRLDP_ondemand_cert_auth_act_ondemand_cert_auth_ag) with return status (Need more data)
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system is configured as Identity Aware Application Proxy for multiple application access, that may require On-Demand Client Certificate Authentication by using different Client SSL profiles. The following is a sample scenario: -- There are 3 web-application (app1.example.com, app2.example.com, app3.example.com) that are located behind the BIG-IP system configured as Identity Aware Application Proxy (by means of using Per-Request Access policy). -- app1.example.com and app2.example.com are configured to require On-Demand Client Certificate Authentication as primary authentication method. -- Each application requires a separate Client SSL profile with separate Client Authentication options specified. -- Client SSL profile for app1.example.com application has 'Default for SNI' option enabled. In this case, all authentication requests to app2.example.com fail, even if a trusted certificate is provided.
bugs.impact: On-Demand Certificate Authentication fail, even if a trusted client certificate is provided.
bugs.workaround: Use a single Client SSL profile with a single certificate, where the Subject Alternative Name extension lists fully qualified domain names of all applications, protected by Identity Aware Application Proxy.

bugs.title: Issues in IE8 when using bot defense browser JavaScript verification and SPA
bugs.symptoms: When using JavaScript verification with a Single Page Application (SPA) on Microsoft Internet Explorer version 8 (IE8) on Windows 7, there is an error message in the browser console which can cause whitepage or crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot defense profile is attached. -- Browser Verification is 'Verify Before Access' or 'Verify After Access' (Blocking and Detection Only). -- Single Page Application is enabled -- Navigating to an HTML page using IE8 over Windows 7 OS, and sending ajax requests.
bugs.impact: Browser gets whitepage or crashes.
bugs.fix: IE8 is no longer supported in Single Page Application mode. whitepage and crashes are fixed, but the SPA mechanism will not work.

bugs.title: DNSSEC zone SEPS records may be wiped out from running configuration
bugs.symptoms: Under certain circumstances, DNSSEC zone SEPS records may be wiped out from running configuration.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only with GTM configurations loaded by the command: tmsh load sys config gtm-only.
bugs.impact: SEPS records may be lost after a configuration reload.
bugs.fix: DNSSEC zone SEPS records are no longer lost from running configuration in response to the command: tmsh load sys config gtm-only.

bugs.title: Cannot save UCS with a passphrase when unused EPSEC files are available
bugs.symptoms: Error during config save: Unexpected Error: UCS saving process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Unused EPSEC files files exist in: /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/epsec_package_d/ -- Try to save UCS file using passphrase. -- Issue the command: tmsh save /sys ucs /var/tmp/MyUCS.ucs passphrase password
bugs.impact: The save operation fails with the following error: Saving active configuration... /var/tmp/configsync.spec: Error creating package WARNING:There are error(s) during saving. Not everything was saved. Be very careful when using this saved file! Error creating package Error during config save. Unexpected Error: UCS saving process failed.
bugs.workaround: Delete unused EPSEC files, UCS gets saved successfully.

bugs.title: SIP MRF via header shows TCP Transport when TLS is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When an SSL Client Profile (TLS) is enabled on a SIP Message-Routing Virtual Server, the via header shows an incorrect transport protocol when SIP messages are sent out the client side of MRF. For example, the via header contains 'SIP/2.0/TCP' or 'SIP/2.0/UDP', when it should read 'SIP/2.0/TLS'.
bugs.conditions: Sending SIP messages from the client side of the SIP MRF when an SSL client profile is enabled on the SIP Message-Routing virtual server.
bugs.impact: The via header is not correct and violates the SIP RFC.
bugs.workaround: Create an iRule that replaces the incorrect via header with a correct one, for example: when SIP_REQUEST_SEND { if { [clientside] } { SIP::header replace Via [string map [list "SIP/2.0/TCP " "SIP/2.0/TLS " "SIP/2.0/UDP " "SIP/2.0/TLS "] [SIP::header Via 0]] 0 } }
bugs.fix: The via headers show the correct text (e.g., SIP/2.0/TLS) when an SSL Client Profile is enabled on a SIP Message-Routing virtual server.

bugs.title: GTM fails to log MCPD error in GTM log and logs it in LTM log instead.
bugs.symptoms: When using BIG-IP link monitors with the mentioned conditions, the system logs MCPD error messages (GTM config sync result from local mcpd: result) in the LTM instead of GTM. # tail /var/log/gtm May 15 11:58:54 gtm1a.test.net err iqsyncer[2684]: 011ae104:3: Gtm config sync result from local mcpd: result { May 15 11:58:54 gtm1a.test.net notice gtmd[15881]: 011a0006:5: hookOnChild: SYNC syncer exited with status == 0.(success) # tail /var/log/ltm May 15 11:58:14 gtm1a.test.net err mcpd[9833]: 0107082c:3: Cannot modify the destination address of monitor /Common/my_bigi_link. May 15 11:58:14 gtm1a.test.net err mcpd[9833]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/gtm to commit id 1 6691325118043697493 /Common/bigip1 0 failed with error 0107082c:3: Cannot modify the destination address of monitor /Common/my_bigi_link.. May 15 11:58:24 gtm1a.test.net err mcpd[9833]: 0107082c:3: Cannot modify the destination address of monitor /Common/my_bigi_link. May 15 11:58:24 gtm1a.test.net err mcpd[9833]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/gtm to commit id 1 6691325118043697493 /Common/bigip1 0 failed with error 0107082c:3: Cannot modify the destination address of monitor /Common/my_bigi_link.. Expected logs: # tail /var/log/gtm -f May 7 13:39:21 gtm1a err iqsyncer[27803]: 011ae104:3: Gtm config sync result from local mcpd: result { result_code 17238060 result_message "0107082c:3: Cannot modify the destination address of monitor /Common/my_bigip_link." result_attribute monitor }
bugs.conditions: -- A bigip_link monitor with destination * written in bigip_gtm.conf. -- That monitor is associated with a link. -- The following command is run on one of the sync group peers: tmsh load /sys config gtm-only.
bugs.impact: GTM log is missing MCPD error text, which instead gets logged in LTM log.

bugs.title: Importing CSV reports error message, though operation is successful
bugs.symptoms: Importing CSV of users into the APM localdb reports an exception in both theG UI and /var/log/webui.log: ERROR common.Facade:error - com.f5.tmui.util.ajax.cli.CliHandlerException: CliHandler: Local User Database: CliHandler: Command failed with error: However, the system actually creates the users, and they are visible on refresh.
bugs.conditions: CSV import of users into the APM localdb via the GUI.
bugs.impact: GUI suggests failure even thought localdbmgr actually creates the users. The users are visible on refresh, so although the error appears, there is no impact to functionality.
bugs.workaround: None. This is cosmetic.
bugs.fix: The error message for TMUI and in the logs has been improved to show both the return code and the error message printed by the CLI command. If there is no output, the message reports that instead of leaving the reason blank. This should help with debugging.

bugs.title: Portal Access: F5_Invoke_load() infinite recursion in special case
bugs.symptoms: Web-application page is frozen.
bugs.conditions: This can occur with certain JavaScript functions in the web application.
bugs.impact: Client-side web-application page is not usable.

bugs.title: iRules does not follow current design best practices
bugs.symptoms: iRules does not follow current design best practices.
bugs.conditions: iRules does not follow current design best practices.
bugs.impact: iRules does not follow current design best practices.
bugs.fix: iRules now follows current design best practices.
bugs.behavior: Database variable 'tmm.tcl.rule.connect.allow_loopback_addresses' was created to toggle whether or not to allow loopback addresses; TRUE will restore previous behavior and enable loopback connections. Default value is FALSE.

bugs.title: SWG limited session limits on SSLO deployments
bugs.symptoms: SWG limited session limits are enforced on SSLO deployments that enable Explicit proxy authentication.
bugs.conditions: -- SSLO with Explicit proxy authentication is deployed. -- Many concurrent SSLO connections that use custom category lookup (beyond the SWG limited session limit).
bugs.impact: SSLO fails to connect when the SWG limited session limit is reached.
bugs.fix: If there is an SSLO profile paired with either an APM or SSLO per-request policy on a virtual server, and the operation has done a custom category only lookup, an SWG limited license is no longer consumed. This answers the case where there is auth (APM) on one virtual server, and the transparent virtual server is SSLO with custom category lookup only.

bugs.title: Security firewall policy in an iApp not deleted on config sync peer with the rest of a deleted iApp
bugs.symptoms: If a security firewall policy is part of an iApp inside a folder created by that iApp, then when the iApp is deleted, any config sync peer will not delete the policy when it deletes the rest of the iApp.
bugs.conditions: -- iApp with folder and security firewall policy is deleted. -- High availability (HA) config sync configuration.
bugs.impact: The security policy is gone on the system where the iApp was initially deleted, but the peer still has that object, and it can't be deleted because it's part of an iApp.

bugs.title: Importing local users CSV via UI shows a redundant error
bugs.symptoms: Importing a local user CSV via the GUI generates an error ERROR common.Facade:error - com.f5.tmui.util.ajax.cli.CliHandlerException: CliHandler: Local User Database: CliHandler: Command failed with error:
bugs.conditions: -- Importing a local user CSV file via the GUI -- CSV file is missing a linefeed on the last line
bugs.impact: Import is successful, but an error is shown on the UI
bugs.fix: Fixed an error when processing the CSV file from the GUI

bugs.title: Cookie Persistence profile is not showing up in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Cookie Persistence profile is not showing up in the GUI; also missing from the GUI is persistence type cookie.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to view the Cookie Persistence profile.
bugs.impact: User cannot configure persistence profile at GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to configure the profile.

bugs.title: IPv6 host defined via static route unreachable after BIG-IP reboot
bugs.symptoms: Static route unreachable after BIG-IP system reboot.
bugs.conditions: -- Add a static route. -- Issue a ping (works fine). -- Reboot the BIG-IP system. -- Issue a ping (cannot pint the route).
bugs.impact: Static route exists in both kernel and LTM routing table but unable to ping the route after rebooting the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Workaround-1: Delete the IPv6 route entry and recreate the route by issuing the following commands in sequence: tmsh delete net route IPv6 tmsh create net route IPv6 network 2a05:d01c:959:8408::b/128 gw fe80::250:56ff:fe86:2065 interface internal Workaround-2: net route /Common/IPv6 { gw fe80::456:54ff:fea1:ee02 <-- Change this address to unicast address from 2a05:d01c:959:8409::/64 network interface /Common/Internal mtu 1500 network 2a05:d01c:959:8408::b/128 }

bugs.title: BGP sessions remain down upon new primary slot election
bugs.symptoms: BGP flapping after new primary slot election.
bugs.conditions: --- A BFD session is processed on a secondary blade. (It can be identified by running tcpdump.) -- After a primary blade reset/reboot, the BFD session should be processed by the same tmm on the same blade, which was secondary before the primary blade reset/reboot. -- The BFD session creation should happens approximately in 30 seconds after the reset/reboot.
bugs.impact: BGP goes down. BGP flaps cause route-dampening to kick-in on the BGP neighbors.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, but you can stabilize the BIG-IP system after the issue occurs by restarting the tmrouted daemon. To do so, issue the following command: bigstart restart tmrouted
bugs.fix: BFD no longer remains DOWN after a blade reset/reboot. There is a convergence period caused by blade changes(blade reset/reboot, new blade installed, blade comes up), which may take a few moments, but after that BFD sessions show correct status.

bugs.title: iRule drop command on DNS traffic without Datagram-LB may cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may crash and restart when an iRule on a DNS virtual server performs the 'drop' command while the BIG-IP system is handling both a DNS request and DNS response at the same time for the same DNS client IP and port without UDP Datagram-LB.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP instance has two or more TMM processes as a result of having two or more physical cores or virtual CPUs. -- A virtual server with both DNS and UDP profiles and one or more iRules. -- The UDP profile has Datagram LB disabled. -- The iRules have a 'drop' command. -- The iRules have a DNS_REQUEST and/or DNS_RESPONSE event with an iRule command that require coordinating data with another TMM on the system, such as the 'table' command.
bugs.impact: TMM crash or restart. Traffic impacted. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: F5 strongly recommends using a UDP profile with Datagram-LB enabled for DNS UDP virtual servers. Alternatively, replace the 'drop' command with DNS::drop in DNS_REQUEST and DNS_RESPONSE events, or with UDP::drop in other iRule events. See the respective references pages for DNS::drop and UDP::drop for the Valid Events each iRule command is available in: https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/DNS__drop.html https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/UDP__drop.html

bugs.title: Pool gets disabled when one of its pool member with monitor session is disabled
bugs.symptoms: A pool which has at least two pool members and one of its pool members associated with a monitor is disabled, the entire pool gets marked disabled-by-parent.
bugs.conditions: -- Monitor assigned to a single pool member. -- That member is manually disabled.
bugs.impact: The pool status for the entire pool is marked disabled-by-parent.

bugs.title: Bot Defense whitelists does not apply for url "Any" after modifying the Bot Defense profile
bugs.symptoms: When creating a whitelist in the Bot Defense profile with url "Any" - after modifying the Bot Defense log profile, the whitelist does not apply anymore.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is attached to the Virtual Server -- Adding a whitelist to the Bot Defense profile with url "Any" -- Modifying the Bot Defense profile afterwards.
bugs.impact: Whitelist does not apply - users from the defined IP/GEO location might be blocked.
bugs.workaround: Delete and add the whitelist after modifying the profile.
bugs.fix: Keep the whitelist as is when updating bot profile.

bugs.title: Negative numbers of received packets in DoS-sampled log messages for bad actor and attacked destination attacks
bugs.symptoms: There are negative values for the number of received packets in DoS-sampled log messages for bad actor and attacked destination attacks.
bugs.conditions: Running the reset-stats command.
bugs.impact: Incorrect log messages.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. Do not run reset-stats command.
bugs.fix: Internal counter is now initialized properly after running the reset-stats command.

bugs.title: OAuth puts quotation marks around claim values that are not string type
bugs.symptoms: When you define a claim to use with OAuth, and the claim-type setting is set to something other than String, the claim value is treated as a string anyway and encapsulated in quotation marks.
bugs.conditions: -- OAuth is configured. -- The oauth claim value being used is not of type string (i.e. array, or boolean, or number)
bugs.impact: The claim value is encapsulated in quotation marks and processed as a string.
bugs.fix: OAuth no longer puts quotation marks around claim values that are not string type.

bugs.title: PEM actions not applied in VE bigTCP.
bugs.symptoms: If PEM virtual server is configured using bigTCP, the return traffic from the server may not return to the same TMM. PEM policies do not get applied.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition. -- bigTCP is configured (FastL4 with PEM/GPA hudfilters). -- Virtual server uses Source-NAT.
bugs.impact: PEM policies do not get applied.
bugs.workaround: To work around this, do the following: -- Configure bigTCP virtual server not to use source-NAT. -- Configure destination-IP for hashing in server-vlan (the external VLAN that has the virtual server).

bugs.title: Special chars < > & displayed incorrectly in BIG-IP GUI logon banner window
bugs.symptoms: If you try to enter any of these three characters: < > & (greater than, less than, ampersand) into GUI Preference page or TMSH sys global-settings configuration, they are displayed as escape chars in the GUI window correspondingly as: < > &.
bugs.conditions: Entering one of these three characters into GUI banner text settings: < > &.
bugs.impact: At GUI Logon page, the page displays with the following characters: < > & instead of the specified characters: < > &.
bugs.fix: You can now use < > & characters for GUI logon banner text, and the system displays those characters in the GUI logon window.

bugs.title: ASM CAPTCHA preview pages don't display the page properly
bugs.symptoms: The CAPTCHA image and corresponding icons are not shown in the window showing CAPTCHA message.
bugs.conditions: 1. Go to Security ›› Application Security : Policy : Response Pages. 2. Go to CAPTCHA section. 3. Press on 'show' button. 4. Preview of the CAPTCHA is not displayed properly. 5. Go To CAPTCHA Fail section. 6. Press on 'show' button. 7. Preview of the CAPTCHA Fail is also not displayed properly
bugs.impact: The CAPTCHA preview cannot be seen properly by the user.
bugs.workaround: This only affects the preview.
bugs.fix: Images are shown properly after fix.

bugs.title: ASU is very slow on device with hundreds of policies due to table checksums
bugs.symptoms: ASU is very slow on devices with hundreds of policies due to table checksums.
bugs.conditions: -- There are hundreds of ASM policies on the device. -- ASU is performed. -- 'DoTableChecksums' is set to 1.
bugs.impact: The ASU process takes hours to complete.
bugs.workaround: In the configuration file /etc/ts/dcc/prepare_policy.cfg, set 'DoTableChecksums' to 0.

bugs.title: ASU is very slow on device with hundreds of policies due to logging profile handling
bugs.symptoms: Signature Update (ASU) is very slow on devices with hundreds of policies due to logging profile handling.
bugs.conditions: -- There are hundreds of ASM policies on the device. -- ASU is performed. -- The BIG-IP is configured for logging profile handling.
bugs.impact: The ASU process takes hours to complete.

bugs.title: Upgrade support for DB variable to attach AJAX payload to vToken cookie should be consistent with config in MCP
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade support for DB variable to attach AJAX payload to vToken cookie sets 'send in alerts' flag configured on parameters without checking whether automatic transaction detection is turned on on the URL.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP version 13.1.x or 14.0.x -- A protected URL is configured with automatic transaction detection turned off. -- A parameter on that URL is configured with all flags turned off. -- The DB variable antifraud.internalconfig.flag1 is set to 'enabled' value. -- Upgrade to 13.1.x or later (with load config) started.
bugs.impact: After upgrade, the configuration fails to load due to an error during schema change validation
bugs.workaround: -- Set the DB variable antifraud.internalconfig.flag1 value to 'disabled' before the upgrade. -- Configure 'send in alerts' flag on the parameters manually.
bugs.fix: Now upgrade support takes into consideration the automatic transaction detection flag on URL and sets 'send in alerts' flag on URL parameters only for URLs with automatic transaction detection turned on.

bugs.title: No option to filter out bots with N/A anomaly category
bugs.symptoms: Some of the bots has N/A for anomaly category. There is no way to filter them in Bot Traffic or on Bot Requests screens.
bugs.conditions: There are bot requests/bots with N/A for the anomaly category.
bugs.impact: No way to filter them in Bot Traffic or on Bot Requests screens.
bugs.fix: Added option to filter by the N/A anomaly category.

bugs.title: Virtual Server resets connections when all pool members are marked disabled
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system immediately responds with a RST against a SYN when all pool members are marked disabled by a monitor.
bugs.conditions: All the pool members are marked disabled by a monitor or administratively.
bugs.impact: Cannot use iRules to respond with an HTTP 503 error to incoming traffic.
bugs.workaround: Use Forced offline instead of disabled to prevent this issue.
bugs.fix: Virtual server no longer resets connections when all pool members are marked disabled.

bugs.title: Increase vCPU amount guests can use on i11800-DS platforms.
bugs.symptoms: Users are unable to configure guests with 12 or 16 CPUs on the i11800-DS platforms.
bugs.conditions: i11800-DS platforms in vCMP mode.
bugs.impact: Cannot assign 12 or 16 CPUs to guests on i11800-DS platforms.
bugs.fix: 12 or 16 CPUs can now be assigned to guests on i11800-DS platforms.

bugs.title: Portal Access: property 'background-image' should be processed
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect background image in web-application page.
bugs.conditions: Web-applications use the 'background-image' property of a style.
bugs.impact: Incorrect client-side web-application rendering.
bugs.workaround: You can create an iRule using the following template. # Note: Replace PAGE_URL (below) with the actual page URL. # # Use this custom iRule for pages where # the issue exists, it adds an entry for # background-image into F5_Deflate table. # when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "PAGE_URL" } { log local0. "URI=([HTTP::path])" # Found the file we wanted to modify REWRITE::post_process 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { set rewrite_data [REWRITE::payload] set rewrite_start [string first {<script id='F5_helperVersionCheck} $rewrite_data] log local0. "Found </script> at $rewrite_start" if {$rewrite_start > -1} { REWRITE::payload replace $rewrite_start 0 { <script> (function () { Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call = function (o) { o['background-image']=o.backgroundImage; return false; } F5_Deflate_index({},'a') delete Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call })() </script> } } }

bugs.title: APM cannot handle HTTP requests with very long URLs
bugs.symptoms: If a very long URL (longer than 8KB) is used in APM session, such a request would fail.
bugs.conditions: - APM session established. - HTTP request with very long URL (longer than 8 KB).
bugs.impact: There is no response for such HTTP request. Web application cannot work correctly.

bugs.title: UI becomes unresponsive when accessing Access active session information
bugs.symptoms: When accessing Admin UI Access :: Overview :: Active Sessions page, the page status is stuck in 'Receiving configuration data from your device'. TMSH command 'show apm access-info' also hangs. The following error messages shows up in TMM log: -- notice mcp error: 0x1020002 at ../mcp/db_access.c:831 -- notice mcp error: 0x1020031 at ../mcp/mcp_config.c:588
bugs.conditions: -- Two vCMP guests or two chassis are set up in high availability mode. -- If Network Mirroring is toggled between 'Within Cluster' and 'Between Cluster' while traffic is going through the device.
bugs.impact: Some session variables may be lost, which results in UI hang. Admin UI becomes unusable.
bugs.workaround: Do not toggle between 'Within Cluster' and 'Between Cluster' while traffic is going through the device.

bugs.title: DNSSEC Key Generations are not imported to secondary FIPS card
bugs.symptoms: When new DNSSEC Key Generations are generated by FIPS card, the Generation is not imported to secondary FIPS card.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has a GTM sync group with FIPS cards in sync. New DNSSEC Key Generation is created.
bugs.impact: New DNSSEC Key Generation is not imported to secondary FIPS card, but the generation is synced within GTM sync group.
bugs.fix: DNSSEC Key Generation is not imported to secondary FIPS card over creation

bugs.title: An invalid SSL close_notify might be sent in some cases.
bugs.symptoms: If a clienthello is not fully received and parsed, any alert sent might be invalid (show an invalid version number).
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server has a client-ssl profile. -- The 'unclean-shutdown' option is disabled. -- The virtual server receives an incomplete clienthello before shutting down.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact, although alerts sent might show an invalid version number.
bugs.workaround: Enable unclean-shutdown (which is enabled by default).

bugs.title: Grub boot entries not updated on i2600 from iControl SOAP set_boot_location call
bugs.symptoms: After calling iControl SOAP System::SoftwareManagement::set_boot_location, the switchboot information correctly shows that the volume should be changed, but grub still shows the current active volume to be unchanged. Upon reboot, the system boots into the unchanged default volume. The system records the following when the iControl call is made/var/log/messages : warning grub_default: unkeyed boot entry found (BIG-IP 12.1.2 Build 0.0.249 <HD1.1>); assigning st.u0 M
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP iSeries platforms: 1. iControl SOAP system::SoftwareManagement::set_boot_location 2. Check grub_default -l
bugs.impact: Unable to upgrade systems via iControl SOAP due to the inability to reboot into the newly installed software.
bugs.workaround: The following iControlREST call works correctly: curl -k -u<username>:<passwd> https://<IP-addr>/mgmt/tm/sys -X POST -H "Content-type: application/json" -d '{"command":"reboot", "volume":"<volume>"}' {"kind":"tm:sys:rebootstate","command":"reboot","volume":"<volume>"}

bugs.title: False positive header related violation
bugs.symptoms: The system reports a false-positive, header-related violation.
bugs.conditions: -- A custom header is added to the system. -- A header related violation is turned on.
bugs.impact: The system reports a false-positive violation.

bugs.title: VLAN groups are incompatible with fast-forwarded flows
bugs.symptoms: Traffic flowing through VLAN groups may get fast-forwarded to another TMM, which might cause that connection to be reset with reason 'Unable to select local port'.
bugs.conditions: -- Using VLAN groups. -- Flows are fast-forwarded to other TMMs.
bugs.impact: Some connections may fail.
bugs.fix: The system now prevents flows on VLAN groups from being fast-forwarded to other TMMs.

bugs.title: When SSL forward proxy is enabled, AKID extension of the OCSP signer certificate on the clientside is not correct
bugs.symptoms: When SSL forward proxy is configured, or for SSLO, if OCSP or CRL is set on the serverside, the certificate that signs the OCSP response on the clientside does not have the correct Authority Key Identifier (AKID).
bugs.conditions: Configure SSL forward proxy or enable SSLO and enable OCSP or CRL on serverside/server SSL profiles.
bugs.impact: Incorrect AKID X509 extension for the OCSP signer certificate on the clientside. Depending on browsers/clients, this may result in the browsers/clients to not be able to use the stapled OCSP response.
bugs.fix: After the fix, the OCSP signer certificate has the correct AKID X509 extension.

bugs.title: GUI LTM Stats page freezes for large number of pools
bugs.symptoms: When a configuration has approximately 5400 pools and 40,000 pool members, navigating to the GUI page to look at stats for all or one pool, the GUI page may freeze indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: Configurations with large number of pools and pool members, e.g., 5400 pools and/or 40,000 pool members.
bugs.impact: Cannot view pool or pool member stats in GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use iControl REST or TMSH to retrieve stats for such a large number of pools or pool members.
bugs.fix: The stats page now returns data for configurations of large numbers of pools and pool members, though a Timeout window may pop up after 30-seconds for big queries. You can dismiss that Timeout window, and the stats display as expected.

bugs.title: Modifying 'local-ip' for a remote syslog requires restarting syslog-ng
bugs.symptoms: Modified the local IP address takes effect only after restart of the syslog-ng.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure the remote syslogs and allow some time to pass. -- Change the local IP address.
bugs.impact: Change does not occur until you reboot or restart syslog-ng.
bugs.workaround: To cause the change to occur, restart syslog-ng: bigstart restart syslog-ng

bugs.title: TMM may crash with panic message: Assertion 'cookie name exists' failed
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with SIGFPE panic panic: ../modules/hudfilter/http/http_cookie.c:489: Assertion 'cookie name exists' failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with remote desktop or VDI profile attached. -- VDI logging level is set to Debug. -- iRule that modifies/reads HTTP cookies.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Increase the log-level for VDI from 'Debug' to a higher level.
bugs.fix: Fixed TMM crash, which occurred when remotedesktop/VDI profile was used together with custom iRule and Debug level logging.

bugs.title: Binary policy import fails with a user-defined Signature Set containing only non-existent signatures
bugs.symptoms: Binary policy import fails if the policy contains a user-defined Signature Set which contains only non-existent Signatures (such as user-defined Signatures). The error in the GUI: Failed to insert to PLC.PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS (DBD::mysql::db do failed: Cannot add or update a child row: a foreign key constraint fails (`PLC`.`PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS`, CONSTRAINT `PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`set_id`) REFERENCES `NEGSIG_SETS` (`set_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE) at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/BatchInsert.pm line 223. ) The error in /var/log/asm: crit g_server_rpc_handler_async.pl[26870]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl,F5::ASMConfig::Handler::log_error_and_rollback): Failed to insert to PLC.PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS (DBD::mysql::db do failed: Cannot add or update a child row: a foreign key constraint fails (`PLC`.`PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS`, CONSTRAINT `PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`set_id`) REFERENCES `NEGSIG_SETS` (`set_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE) at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/BatchInsert.pm line 223.
bugs.conditions: A binary policy file contains a user-defined Signature Set which contains only signatures that don't exist on the target device (such as user-defined Signatures).
bugs.impact: Policy import fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following Workarounds: -- Re-export the policy as XML. -- Create the missing user-defined Signatures.
bugs.fix: Binary policy import succeeds even with empty user-defined Signature Sets.

bugs.title: Secondary blades go offline after new primary is elected
bugs.symptoms: Secondary active blades go offline.
bugs.conditions: -- Cluster with three or more active blades. -- Primary blade is rebooted. For example, on a 4-bladed system, after slot 1 (primary blade) was rebooted and slot 2 (secondary blade) takes over as primary, slots 3 and 4 both go offline due to high availability (HA) table, with the logs showing reason as 'waiting for configuration load'.
bugs.impact: Cluster reduced to a single blade, which may impact performance.

bugs.title: Problems in reporting of disallowed URL
bugs.symptoms: Parameters that were configured to be sensitive, are not masked
bugs.conditions: -- Disallowed URL is configured -- A request is sent with sensitive parameters in post data.
bugs.impact: Sensitive data is not masked.
bugs.fix: When a disallowed URL is configured and a request is sent with sensitive parameters in post data, the sensitive data is now masked.

bugs.title: In L2wire mode packets from srcIP 0.0.0.0 will be silently dropped
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system is configured in L2Wire mode, packets from srcIP 0.0.0.0 are dropped.
bugs.conditions: L2Wire mode.
bugs.impact: All srcIP 0.0.0.0 packets are dropped silently.
bugs.workaround: Configure the virtual server to be in L2-forward mode.
bugs.fix: The system no longer drops srcIP 0.0.0.0 packets when in L2Wire mode.

bugs.title: A tm.rejectunmatched value of 'false' will prevent connection resets in cases where the connection limit has been reached
bugs.symptoms: Setting the DB variable tm.rejectunmatched to 'false' causes the BIG-IP system to not send RSTs when there is a match but the connection is rejected due to connection limits.
bugs.conditions: - tm.rejectunmatched is set to 'false'. - A packet is matching a BIG-IP object. - The packet is to be rejected because of connection limits.
bugs.impact: Reset packets are not sent back to clients when they should be.
bugs.fix: Packets that match a BIG-IP object but fail due to connection limits will now be rejected with an RST.

bugs.title: Modifying fields such as chain, trusted certificate authorities in client SSL profile, and/or chain in cert-key-chain belonging to the same client SSL profile might not be reflected in TMM
bugs.symptoms: Modifying fields such as chain, trusted certificate authorities, and others, in client SSL profile, or chain in cert-key-chain belonging to the same client SSL profile, might not be reflected in TMM.
bugs.conditions: Modifying fields such as chain, trusted certificate authorities in client SSL profile or chain in cert-key-chain belonging to the same client SSL profile.
bugs.impact: Even after modifying trusted certificate authorities, chain, or other fields, those changes might not be reflected in the actual configuration in TMM.
bugs.workaround: Following workarounds may be applied: 1. Update the client SSL profile again. 2. Restart TMM. 3. Restart mcpd.

bugs.title: ASM unable to handle ICAP responses which length is greater then 10K
bugs.symptoms: ASM drops ICAP and HTTP connections when a multipart request arrives to the ASM enforcer and then forwarded to the ICAP server for virus inspection, and the ICAP server replies with a large (greater then 10 KB) response.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- Antivirus service IP and port defined in the BIG-IP GUI under Options :: Integrated Services. -- Antivirus protection enabled in the ASM policy.
bugs.impact: ASM drops ICAP and HTTP connections.
bugs.workaround: Configure the ICAP server to send back responses smaller than 10 KB.
bugs.fix: There is new ASM internal parameter introduced to make the ICAP response buffer size configurable within the ASM enforcer. The maximum response buffer size is 250 KB. To set the variable, issue the following commands, in sequence: -- /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add icap_response_buff_size 250000 -- bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: Traffic Intelligence Feed Lists are not usable if created on Standby unit in Traffic Group
bugs.symptoms: If Feed List is created on Standby unit, it will not be synchronized to other units in Traffic Group, and will become unusable.
bugs.conditions: -- Create Feed List on a Standby unit. -- Attempt to use URLCAT with Custom DB.
bugs.impact: URL Categorization based on Custom DB does not work.
bugs.workaround: Create Feed List on the Active unit and synchronize to Standby.
bugs.fix: Feed Lists can now be used if created on a Standby unit.

bugs.title: Changes to a Web Acceleration profile are not instantly applied to virtual servers using the profile
bugs.symptoms: Changing parameters in a Web Acceleration profile does not change the behavior of virtual servers already using the profile.
bugs.conditions: This issue is encountered after changing the settings of a Web Acceleration profile already in use by one or more virtual servers.
bugs.impact: The changes are saved correctly and are visible in the Web UI and tmsh; however, virtual servers already using the profile are not affected by the changes. This may result in some confusion and in the BIG-IP Administrator being unable to apply their desired changes.
bugs.workaround: After modifying the profile, remove the profile from all virtual servers and then re-add it.

bugs.title: Unable to login using LDAP with 'user-template' configuration
bugs.symptoms: Unable to login as remote-user.
bugs.conditions: When the following are true: -- LDAP remote-auth configured with user-template. -- Remote-user configured to permit login.
bugs.impact: Unable to login with remote-user.
bugs.workaround: Use bind-dn for authentication.

bugs.title: ASM should treat 'Authorization: Negotiate TlR' as NTLM
bugs.symptoms: When an authentication request with Authorization: Negotiate arrives to ASM. ASM does not count it as a login attempt. As a result brute force protection isn't applied.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual sever. -- Login URL configured in ASM policy. -- Brute force protection enabled in ASM policy.
bugs.impact: Brute force attack checking can be skipped if the backend server authorization type is NTLM but the client sends 'Authorization: Negotiate TlR'.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule which changes 'Authorization: Negotiate TlR' to NTLM on the client side (before ASM) and sets is back to the original value on the server side (after ASM)
bugs.fix: After the fix ASM treats 'Authorization: Negotiate TlR' as NTLM, while the 'TlR' is a sign of NTLM usage.

bugs.title: VLAN groups do not bridge non-link-local multicast traffic.
bugs.symptoms: VLAN groups do not bridge non-link-local multicast traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- VLAN groups configured. -- Using non-link-local multicast traffic.
bugs.impact: Non-link-local multicast traffic does not get forwarded.
bugs.fix: VLAN groups now bridge non-link-local multicast traffic.

bugs.title: PKCE support for BIG-IP as a Client
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not support PKCE for OAuth clients.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP APM configured as an OAuth Authorization Server. -- The environment requires PKCE
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure PKCE not the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: When BIG-IP requests access to the system as a client, a code challenge is sent along with authorization details to the authorization server to obtain the authorization code. In the token request, a code verifier is sent to the token endpoint along with the authorization code. Therefore, the server compares the code verifier to the code challenge and performs the proof of possession.

bugs.title: UI becomes unresponsive when accessing Access active session information
bugs.symptoms: When accessing Admin UI Access :: Overview :: Active Sessions page, the page status is stuck in 'Receiving configuration data from your device'. TMSH command 'show apm access-info' also hangs.
bugs.conditions: -- Two vCMP guests or two chassis are set up in high availability mode. -- If Network Mirroring is toggled between 'Within Cluster' and 'Between Cluster' while traffic is going through the device.
bugs.impact: Some session variables may be lost, which results in the GUI becoming unresponsive. The Access :: Overview :: Active Sessions page in the Admin UI becomes unusable.
bugs.workaround: Do not toggle between 'Within Cluster' and 'Between Cluster' while traffic is going through the device.
bugs.fix: The solution for the reported issue is handled by the fix provided for ID 783817. ID 786173 fixes a null pointer exception that might occur in the specific case of a certain missing session variable, which is relevant only in BIG-IP releases 14.1.0 or later.

bugs.title: Modifying a monitor Alias Address from the TMUI might cause failed config loads and send monitors to an incorrect address
bugs.symptoms: - Monitors are firing and are being sent to a pool-member or node address rather than a monitor's alias address. - Running the command 'tmsh load /sys config' reports an error: 01070038:3: Monitor /Common/a-tcp address type requires a port.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a monitor without an alias address. -- Modify the monitor later in the TMUI to specify an alias address.
bugs.impact: Monitors are sent to an incorrect IP address. tmsh load /sys config will fail to load the configuration.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Delete and recreate the monitor and specify the correct alias address at creation time. -- Fix the monitor definition using tmsh.

bugs.title: MRF Generic Message: unaccepted packets received by GENERIC MESSAGE filter causes subsequent messages to not be forwarded
bugs.symptoms: When a message is created using the GENERICMESSAGE::message create iRule command during the CLIENT_DATA event, if the TCP payload buffer is not cleared before the event completes, the data in the payload buffer is forwarded to the generic message filter disrupting its statemachine.
bugs.conditions: -- A message is created using GENERICMESSAGE::message create iRule command during CLIENT_DATA event. -- TCP payload buffer is not cleared before the event completes.
bugs.impact: The data in the payload buffer is forwarded to the generic message filter disrupting its statemachine. Subsequent messages are not forwarded.
bugs.workaround: To fix the problem, add the following to CLIENT_DATA: TCP::payload replace 0 [TCP::payload length] ""
bugs.fix: Data left in the TCP payload buffer is now ignored and does not negatively impact the filter.

bugs.title: Debug-level messages are being logged even when the system is not set up for debug logging
bugs.symptoms: With certain modules provisioned, the following debug apmd log events are reported to the logging server: -- slot1/systemname debug apmd[14204]: GSSAPI client step 2. -- err apmd[14204]: 01490107:3: ...: Local error, SASL(-1): generic failure: GSSAPI Error: Unspecified GSS failure. Minor code may provide more information (Ticket expired) (-2)
bugs.conditions: -- APM, APML, ASM, AVR, iRulesLX, LTM provisioned. -- Configured to use Generic Security Service Application Program Interface (GSSAPI, also GSS-API).
bugs.impact: Debug-level messages are logged even when the BIG-IP system is not configured to use debug logging: debug apmd[14204]: GSSAPI client step 2.

bugs.title: Rename of 'AMF Body' context to 'HTTP request body - unparsed payload' in request log
bugs.symptoms: Current context name of 'AMF Body' does not clearly describe the log issue.
bugs.conditions: When a violation is raised in the context of an unparsed body.
bugs.impact: 'AMF Body' in the log message does not clearly indicate the associated context.
bugs.fix: Confusing context name 'AMF Body' has been changed to 'HTTP request body - unparsed payload' to more accurately describe the context.

bugs.title: Upgrade failure from 13.0.x or earlier when using LTM Policies with DOSL7
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade fails when upgrading from 13.0.x or under if the config includes an LTM Policy (CPM) which modifies a DoS Application Profile.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM Policy is configured to specify a DoSL7 profile name. -- Upgrade is from version 13.0.x or earlier.
bugs.impact: Upgrade failure.
bugs.workaround: 1. Manually edit the /config/bigip.conf file, and place all of the 'security dos profile' objects before any 'ltm policy' objects. 2. Load the config.
bugs.fix: Upgrade no longer fails when using an LTM Policy which specifies a DoSL7 profile name.

bugs.title: Wrong Data Manipulation titles
bugs.symptoms: The Data Manipulation labels in Automatic Transactions say 'Request Data Manipulation Score' and 'Request Data Manipulation Maximum Score', but they should say 'Data Manipulation Score' and 'Data Manipulation Maximum Score'.
bugs.conditions: -- FPS is licensed and provisioned. -- Viewing Automatic Transactions.
bugs.impact: Labels are misleading. Here are the proper definitions: Data Manipulation Score: The score added to the total alert score if the system detects data manipulation in parameter values or in the Ajax payload. See the online help for more details. Data Manipulation Maximum Score: The value entered here limits the total combined score that can be added to an alert when the BIG-IP system detects that data manipulation occurred on two or more parameters. See the online help for more details.
bugs.fix: Modified titles: removed the word 'Request'.

bugs.title: Pending GTP iRule operation maybe aborted when connection is expired
bugs.symptoms: When there is a suspended iRule operation (such as the table or after command) in GTP iRule event, the operation may be intermittently aborted when the connection is expired.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a connection times out while there is still a pending iRule operation. For example, in one use case, there is a table command in GTP_SIGNALLING_INGRESS event, and the immediate idle timeout is configured in the UDP profile.
bugs.impact: GTP iRule may not be completely executed.
bugs.workaround: For the specific use case when immediate idle timeout is used, change idle timeout to some positive value. Then use the iRule to expire the connection after the GTP iRule event is done, for example, by setting 'IP::idle_timeout 0' in SERVER_CONNECTED event.
bugs.fix: When connection is expired, pending iRule operations in GTP iRule events are now completed.

bugs.title: Configuration fails to load after install of v14.1.0 on BIG-IP 800
bugs.symptoms: When performing an installation of 14.1.0 on the BIG-IP 800 platform, the configuration fails to load after booting and reports an error: 01070920:3: Application error for confpp: iptables-restore v1.4.21: Couldn't load target `ha_multicast':No such file or directory
bugs.conditions: -- Install or upgrade to 14.1.0. -- BIG-IP 800 platform.
bugs.impact: Unable to load configuration.

bugs.title: SSL forward proxy: OCSP signer certificate isn't refreshed or regenerated when forward proxy CA key/cert is changed
bugs.symptoms: When stapling the OCSP response (and hence OCSP certificate) to the SSL client, the issuer that appears on the OCSP certificate mismatches with what is configured in the client SSL profile as the forward proxy CA cert.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen when all the below conditions are met. -- The BIG-IP system is using SSLO or SSL forward proxy. -- The client hello sent from the SSL client includes the status request extension. This means that it requests BIG-IP system to staple the OCSP response. -- The forward proxy CA cert in the client SSL profile is modified.
bugs.impact: In SSLO or SSL forward proxy mode, the server cert and the OCSP response the BIG-IP system sends to the SSL client should be both signed (issued) by the forward proxy CA cert configured at the client SSL profile. If they are signed by different issuers, it may not pass some of the validation check performed by the SSL client and might lead to SSL client's terminating the SSL handshake.
bugs.workaround: To updates and regenerates the OCSP signer information, after modifying the forward proxy CA cert, run the command: bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: The issuer appearing on the OCSP response always matches the forward proxy CA cert configured at the client SSL profile.

bugs.title: Export fails from partitions with '-' as second character
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to export a profile/policy from partition using the hyphen/dash (-) as the second character results in error message: 'Incorrect arguments: <partition> is not specified' error.
bugs.conditions: Partition with '-' as second character in the name.
bugs.impact: Unable to export policy from given partition
bugs.workaround: Rename partition without '-' as the second character.
bugs.fix: Export is working as expected in this scenario.

bugs.title: Unable to add 'Enforce' parameter if already configured in different URL
bugs.symptoms: If two or more URLs are configured with 'Application Type = Mobile', is is not possible to add the 'Enforce' parameter to more than one URL. Also, the 'Mobile Encryption Parameter' option is automatically checked if already checked in another URL.
bugs.conditions: 1. License FPS and MobileSafe. 2. Add two or more URLs with 'Application Type = Mobile'.
bugs.impact: Data sent from MobileSafe SDK may not be encrypted.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to configure these settings.
bugs.fix: The 'Enforce' parameter is now added correctly, and the 'Mobile Encryption Parameter' is not checked automatically, which is correct functionality.

bugs.title: AVRD stays at 100% CPU constantly on some systems
bugs.symptoms: One thread of the avrd process spontaneously starts to consume 100% CPU.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions under which this occurs are unknown, but might occur only on vCMP configurations.
bugs.impact: System performance degrades.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM: bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: Added processing that prevents AVRD from entering endless loops.

bugs.title: httprouter may deadlock
bugs.symptoms: The httprouter proxy may get into a state where it closes the TCP window, and never reopens it.
bugs.conditions: The HTTP MRF Router is used. This configuration is typically used with the HTTP2 Full Proxy when you use the httprouter profile. A very large amount of data arrives from the server in a short amount of time after connection setup.
bugs.impact: Traffic on a HTTP2 stream, or HTTP 1 connection blocks. Eventually, the connection will be killed by the sweeper.
bugs.fix: The HTTP MRF Router will not get into a state where the TCP window is permanently closed.

bugs.title: Database monitors debug logs have plaintext password printed in the log file
bugs.symptoms: When monitor instance is in "debug" logging enabled mode for certain monitor types, the resulting monitor instance logs may contain sensitive details like password
bugs.conditions: When debug mode is enabled for following monitoring types 1. mssql 2. mysql 3. oracle 4. postgresql
bugs.impact: The user-account password configured in the health monitor may appear in plain text form in the monitor instance logs under /var/log/monitors/.
bugs.workaround: 1. Do not enable monitor instance logging or monitor debug logging for affected monitor types. 2. If it is necessary to enable monitor instance logging or monitor debug logging for troubleshooting purposes , remove the resulting log files from the BIG-IP system after troubleshooting is completed.
bugs.fix: The password filed for monitor will now be redacted by external monitors when monitor debugging is enabled.

bugs.title: Tmsh command 'show running-config' fails when Protocol Inspection is not licensed.
bugs.symptoms: If the Protocol Inspection feature is not licensed then tmsh command 'show running-config' fails with 'Protocol Inspection feature not licensed.' message.
bugs.conditions: - AFM Protocol Inspection feature is not licensed.
bugs.impact: 'tmsh show running-config' command returns an error: 'Protocol Inspection feature not licensed.'
bugs.fix: 'tmsh show running-config' command works as expected.

bugs.title: BIG-IP responds incorrectly to ICMP echo requests when virtual server flaps.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system unexpectedly responds to ICMP echo requests to a virtual-address that is unavailable, or unexpectedly does not respond to ICMP echo requests to a virtual-address that is available. The BIG-IP system fails to remove a dynamic route for a virtual-address that is unavailable or fails to add a dynamic route for a virtual-address that is available.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create two virtual servers with multiple nodes. Set ICMP echo as all or selective/all. 2. Ping from client to virtual address. 3. Bring down nodes. 4. ping fails from client to virtual address as expected 5. Bring up nodes and make sure all virtual servers are online. 6. Start ping from client to virtual address.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system might respond incorrectly to ICMP echo requests sent to a virtual-address. -- If the virtual-address icmp-echo is set to 'all' or 'any', the BIG-IP system may not respond correctly after a virtual-address availability change. -- If the virtual-address route-advertisement is set to 'all' or 'any', the route for the virtual-address may not advertise properly after a virtual-address availability change. The BIG-IP system might fail to insert or remove a dynamic route for a virtual-address. This might cause the network to direct traffic to a down virtual-address or alternatively, not direct traffic to an up virtual-address.
bugs.workaround: Update virtual address ICMP setting to any or selective/any.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed.

bugs.title: TMSH displays TSIG keys
bugs.symptoms: TSIG key is displayed when related configuration is listed in TMSH.
bugs.conditions: -- Authenticated administrative user. -- Listing TSIG keys using TMSH.
bugs.impact: TSIG keys are listed when they should not be.
bugs.fix: TMSH no longer displays TSIG keys when listing configuration.

bugs.title: The device status is falsely showing as forced offline on the network map while actual device status is not.
bugs.symptoms: Network Map in GUI shows incorrect [Forced Offline] status.
bugs.conditions: -- Multi-blade system The device status in the network map is falsely shown [Forced Offline] when actual device status is something else other than [Forced Offline]. In other words, it is always shown as [Forced Offline]. -- Non multi-blade system The device status in the network map is falsely shown [Forced Offline] when actual device status is something else other than [Active] or [Forced Offline]. In other words, it displays fine only for [Active] and [Forced Offline].
bugs.impact: The device status in the network map is not reliable

bugs.title: While deleting a DoS profile, tmm might core in sPVA
bugs.symptoms: When trying to delete a DoS profile attached to a virtual server, it is possible that tmm might core and restart.
bugs.conditions: -- An AFM DoS profile is attached to a virtual server. -- Some of the DoS attacks are programmed into hardware (HW) through sPVA. -- That DoS profile is deleted.
bugs.impact: tmm might generate a core and restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use software (SW) DoS only.
bugs.fix: The tmm process no longer generates a core and restarts when deleting a profile that is attached to a virtual server.

bugs.title: Improve initializing TCP analytics for FastL4
bugs.symptoms: TCP analytics for FastL4 might stay uninitialized under specific circumstances.
bugs.conditions: System clock advances while initializing TCP analytics for FastL4.
bugs.impact: TCP analytics for FastL4 might stay uninitialized for a while and miss some analytics data.
bugs.fix: Initialization of TCP analytics for FastL4 is improved.

bugs.title: IVSERR_SENT_RESULT_LOG displays incorrect IVS name
bugs.symptoms: Internal virtual server (IVS) logs an incorrect name when it sends a result code back to the primary virtual server.
bugs.conditions: -- DB variable log.ivs.level value of 'notice' or above. -- IVS configured with a service that sends a result callback (such as ICAP).
bugs.impact: Log message can be confusing, and prevents filtering logs based on IVS name.
bugs.fix: Log message displays correct IVS name.

bugs.title: URLCAT by URI does not work if it contains port number
bugs.symptoms: If absolute URI contains port number then URLCAT returns the result: Uncategorized.
bugs.conditions: Create new connection using CONNECT <absolute_uri> method.
bugs.impact: AFM rules configured with use of categorization do not work as intended.
bugs.workaround: Add URI with port number to custom Feed List.
bugs.fix: URLCAT works if request URI contains port number.

bugs.title: Validation error regarding disabling DoS Software Mode is unclear
bugs.symptoms: You encounter an error message: This platform does not support DoS hardware capability, which is needed to disable this sys db variable.
bugs.conditions: -- This can be encountered during system start, or when loading a UCS file. -- The error is logged if the DB variable Dos.ForceSWDos is set to false on a platform that does not support hardware DoS capability.
bugs.impact: Error is logged but it is unclear that the error means that the db variable Dos.ForceSWDos is set to false, but the device does not have hardware DoS capability.
bugs.fix: The validation message has been revised to include db variable in question.

bugs.title: Potential memory leak when software crypto request is canceled.
bugs.symptoms: Memory may occasionally leak when a software crypto request is cancelled before it has completed.
bugs.conditions: There are a number of reasons why a software crypto request may be canceled.
bugs.impact: Memory may leak.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.

bugs.title: Bypass MRF SIP LB restriction of conversion from reliable transport (TCP) to unreliable transport (UDP)
