bugs.workaround: -- If you are experiencing slow response time, it can help to use SNMP client options of long timeouts and less retries so that SNMP requests do not keep restarting each time the previous request times out. -- If you are querying statistics information, it is more efficient to just query the specific table you are interested in rather than doing a full snmpwalk of multiple tables. -- If you are making bulk requests, you should avoid requesting from multiple different tables in the same request. -- Avoid having multiple different clients querying different tables simultaneously.

bugs.title: tmm memory growth if high availability (HA) peer is unavailable
bugs.symptoms: tmm memory utilization growth.
bugs.conditions: The next-active device in the high availability (HA) configuration is down, and either of the following: -- Persistence mirroring is configured. -- Connection mirroring of a virtual server with a persistence profile is configured.
bugs.impact: Connection limits due to memory tmm memory pressure or possible tmm out-of-memory failure.
bugs.workaround: Disable persistence and/or connection mirroring if the standby device will be down for an extended period of time.
bugs.fix: tmm memory no longer grows if high availability (HA) peer is unavailable.

bugs.title: Tmm memory utilization growth.
bugs.symptoms: Tmm memory growth with improper high availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.conditions: - The device mirror-ip is not configured properly, along with either of the following: + Persistence mirroring is configured. + Connection mirroring of a virtual server with a persistence profile.
bugs.impact: Connection limits due to memory tmm memory pressure or possible tmm out-of-memory failure.
bugs.workaround: - Properly configure the cm device mirror-ip and/or mirror-secondary-ip. After doing this, the memory utilization should drop. - Disable mirroring on the persistence profiles and/or virtual servers. After doing this, the memory utilization will not drop until tmm is restarted.

bugs.title: Cmp_dest on C2200 platform may give incorrect results
bugs.symptoms: Cmp_dest on C2200 platform may give incorrect results.
bugs.conditions: Run cmp_dest.
bugs.impact: Incorrect results from cmp_dest.
bugs.fix: Cmp_dest now gives correct results.

bugs.title: When inserting a cookie or a cookie attribute, BIG-IP does not add a leading space, required by RFC
bugs.symptoms: The 'HTTP::cookie attribute' irule command allows manipulation of Cookie or Set-Cookie headers in HTTP requests or responses. When this command is used to insert a cookie attribute, it appends the attribute (and a possible value) to the header without a leading space character. A leading space character is a requirement per RFC 6265. When such a header is formed with iRule command 'HTTP::cookie insert' or 'HTTP::cookie attribute insert', the leading space is not provided, violating the RFC.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server with HTTP profile is configured. -- There is an iRule generating or updating a cookie header with 'HTTP::cookie insert' or 'HTTP::cookie attribute insert' command.
bugs.impact: There is no space preceding the attribute. RFC is violated.
bugs.workaround: When inserting a cookie attribute with iRule command, add a leading space to the name of attribute to be inserted.

bugs.title: iApp Templates are now marked as Deprecated
bugs.symptoms: All iApp templates have been marked as deprecated.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered in the iApps :: Application Services : New Application Service screen.
bugs.impact: If you wish to use these deprecated templates, select the "Show deprecated templates" checkbox.
bugs.behavior: In this release, all iApp templates have been marked as deprecated. They are still accessible in the GUI in the iApps tab, but you will need to choose "Show deprecated templates" in order to see them.

bugs.title: iApps: Calling 'Package Require <PKG>' in a template with a manager role is not supported
bugs.symptoms: With the Manager role, when calling 'package require <PKG>' in an iApp template, following exception occurs: Error parsing template:can't eval proc: "script::run" invalid command name "file" while executing "file join $dir $f".
bugs.conditions: Users can not use Manager Role when importing iApps that contain a 'package require' call.
bugs.impact: Cannot use Manager Role when importing iApps that contain a 'package require' call.
bugs.workaround: Use the Admin role to import new templates.

bugs.title: When HTTP/2 is negotiated, if the provided cipher suite list cannot be matched, then the last one will be selected.
bugs.symptoms: The last provided cipher suite in the list is chosen if HTTP/2 is negotiated and not matched.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 negotiation is enabled. -- The provided cipher suites are not matched.
bugs.impact: The lest secure cipher suite would be selected.
bugs.workaround: Put the most secure cipher suite in the end of the list.
bugs.fix: Now the most secure cipher suite is selected regardless of the order in the list.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing SSL traffic via an HTTP/2 full-proxy
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing SSL traffic with an HTTP/2 full-proxy.
bugs.conditions: -HTTP/2 enabled -MRF enabled -SSL profile enabled
bugs.impact: Potential TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes SSL traffic via an HTTP/2 full-proxy as expected.

bugs.title: Gossip shows active even when devices are missing
bugs.symptoms: Gossip appears Active even when one or more devices go missing from device group. 'restcurl shared/gossip' shows active on both devices, even when the devices are not listed in 'restcurl shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-allBIG-IPs/devices'.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this issue occurs are unknown. This is an intermittent issue.
bugs.impact: Gossip reports that it is working when it is not.
bugs.workaround: -- If the missing device is the active device, run the following command on the Active DSC Device: restcurl -X POST -d '{}' tm/shared/bigip-failover-state -- If the missing device is the standby device, reboot the device, make it active, and then run the following command: restcurl -X POST -d '{}' tm/shared/bigip-failover-state

bugs.title: Localdb authentication fails
bugs.symptoms: In Active / Standby setup, user authentication fails after failover occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- APM configured in Active / Standby setup. -- Per-session policy configured with Localdb Auth . -- Failover occurs.
bugs.impact: APM end users are unable to authenticate.
bugs.workaround: Restart localdbmgr on the new active device, using the following command: # bigstart restart localdbmgr
bugs.fix: In Active / Standby setup, user authentication no longer fails after failover occurs, so APM end users are able to authenticate.

bugs.title: The /var partition may become 100% full requiring manual intervention to clear space
bugs.symptoms: The /var partition might become completely full on the disk due to files being written to /var/config/rest. This condition may be accompanied by console error messages similar to the following: 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var (slot #) has only 0% free on secondary blade. Additionally, there may be periodic restjavad and bigd daemons restarts related to disk space exhaustion.
bugs.conditions: Process traffic while DoS Dashboard is open
bugs.impact: The partition housing /var/config/rest may become 100% full, impacting future disk IO to the partition.
bugs.workaround: Important: This workaround is temporary, and may need to be periodically performed either manually or from a script. Impact of Workaround: While these steps are performed, the BIG-IP REST API will be temporarily inaccessible, and higher disk IO may be seen. Run the following commands, in sequence: bigstart stop restjavad rm -rf /var/config/rest/storage*.zip rm -rf /var/config/rest/*.tmp bigstart start restjavad Manual application of these workaround steps clears the 100% utilized space condition and allows the partition to resume normal operation.

bugs.title: Valid GTP-C traffic may cause buffer overflow
bugs.symptoms: Valid GTP-C traffic may cause buffer overflow with incrementing sequence numbers.
bugs.conditions: Valid GTP traffic with incrementing sequence number will cause memory corruption/core when processed through IPS library.
bugs.impact: TMM Crash/core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: The only workaround is to disable protocol inspection or remove GTP service from all protocol-inspection profiles.

bugs.title: Hardware syncookies on some hardware platforms may retrieve the wrong mss
bugs.symptoms: When hardware syncookie is activated, the system may retrieve the wrong MSS (TCP maximum segment size) value for the flow. This impacts all BIG-IP hardware platforms except BIG-IP 2000/4000.
bugs.conditions: -- Using any BIG-IP platform except BIG-IP 2000/4000. -- Hardware syncookies used.
bugs.impact: Connection failures and/or excessive TCP segment retransmissions.
bugs.workaround: Use software syncookies and disable hardware syncookie protection.

bugs.title: Unable to configure performance HTTP virtual server via GUI
bugs.symptoms: When creating 'performance HTTP' virtual servers via GUI, the following error is reported: 01070734:3: Configuration error: A Virtual Server(/Common/vfasthttp) cannot be associated with both fasthttp and L4 profile.
bugs.conditions: Use the GUI to create a virtual server of type Performance (HTTP).
bugs.impact: Failed to create a 'performance HTTP' virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to configure the performance HTTP virtual server: tmsh create ltm virtual vfasthttp destination 1.1.1.1:80 ip-protocol tcp profiles add { fasthttp }

bugs.title: Virtual Server iRule does not match an External Data Group key that's 128 characters long
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server iRule does not match an External Data Group key that is 128 characters long.
bugs.conditions: -- A string type External Data Group with a key/value pair whose key is 128 characters long. -- An iRule using [class match] to get the value from the Data Group.
bugs.impact: The call to [class match] returns an empty string ("").

bugs.title: The iControl REST query request returning empty list for DoS Protected Objects
bugs.symptoms: DoS Protection profiles are not displayed in the GUI, but they are visible when using the tmsh command: tmsh list security dos profile | grep "security dos profile"
bugs.conditions: This is encountered in Security :: DoS Protection : Protection Profiles.
bugs.impact: DoS Protected Objects are not included in the REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/security/presentation/tmui/virtual-list, so the GUI cannot display the DoS Protected Objects
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh.
bugs.fix: DoS Protected Objects are now visible in the GUI

bugs.title: Manual changes to policy imported as XML may introduce corruption for Login Pages
bugs.symptoms: Manual changes to a policy imported as XML may introduce corruption for Response Pages. The following log appears: ASM subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl ,F5::PrepareConf::Policy::prepare_alternate_response_file_tbl): failed to parse response headers - please check response page.
bugs.conditions: -- XML policy file is missing a response header. -- Import the policy.
bugs.impact: The affected reponse page is not returned for traffic as expected, and an error is reported instead.
bugs.workaround: Go to the affected policy's Response Pages: Login Page, click Save and then click Apply Policy.
bugs.fix: The system now gracefully ignores empty header for Login Page response page.

bugs.title: Escaped slash in Parameter regular expression value fails regex validation
bugs.symptoms: A Parameter with a backslash-escaped slash in regular expression cannot be created.
bugs.conditions: You attempt to create a Parameter with a backslash-escaped slash in a regular expression, for example, "aaaa\/bbb".
bugs.impact: The parameter fails to be created due to regular expression validation.
bugs.workaround: Specify the regular expression for the Parameter with slash unescaped (without the preceding backslash).
bugs.fix: A Parameter with a backslash-escaped slash in regular expression can be created successfully.

bugs.title: Problems establishing HA connections on DAGv2 chassis platforms
bugs.symptoms: High availability (HA) mirroring does not work correctly on VIPRION B4400 blades.
bugs.conditions: - VIPRION B4400 chassis platform with multiple blades. - HA mirroring is enabled.
bugs.impact: HA mirroring does not work
bugs.fix: HA connections on VIPRION B4400 chassis platforms are correctly established.

bugs.title: The 'any-available' prober selection is not as random as in earlier versions
bugs.symptoms: Some big3d instances can be periodically busier than other big3d instances.
bugs.conditions: -- When 'any-available' is selected for either the prober-preference or prober-fallback options. -- A large number of monitors are defined.
bugs.impact: When the 'any-available' prober option is used, the selection of big3d probers may not be as random as in BIG-IP software versions prior to v13.0.0.

bugs.title: PEM iRule crashes when more than 10 policies are tried to be set for a subscriber
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: Using an iRule to apply more than 10 referential policies for a subscriber.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system validates the number of policies before setting them to a subscriber. In this release, iRule behavior does not result in a tmm core dump, but the number of policies that can be simultaneously applied to a subscriber through an iRule is limited to 7.
bugs.behavior: In previous releases, the system did not prevent using an iRule to apply more than 10 referential policies for a subscriber. In those cases, however, tmm crashed and generated a core. In this release, the BIG-IP system validates the number of policies before setting them to a subscriber. iRule behavior does not result in a tmm core dump, but the number of policies that can be simultaneously applied to a subscriber through an iRule is limited to 7.

bugs.title: Certain configuration may result in zombie forwarding flows
bugs.symptoms: OneConnect profile in conjunction with 'Source-port preserve-strict' or cmp-hash setting of 'dst-ip' or 'src-ip' on the server-side VLAN may result in zombie forwarding flows. On the server-side the incoming traffic hits a different TMM from the one that handles the outgoing traffic. Unexpected 'Inet port exhaustion' messages may be logged in the LTM log file.
bugs.conditions: -- OneConnect configured. And one of the following: -- Source-port is set to preserve-strict. -- The cmp-hash setting on the server-side VLAN is set to 'dst-ip' or 'src-ip'.
bugs.impact: Zombie forwarding flows. Over time, the current allocation count grows and does not return to its prior level when traffic stops. The current allocation can be checked with this command: # tmctl memory_usage_stat name=connflow -s name,cur_allocs
bugs.workaround: You can use any of the following workarounds: -- Remove the OneConnect profile from the Virtual Server. -- Do not use 'source-port preserve-strict' setting on the Virtual Server. -- Set the 'cmp-hash default' on the server-side VLAN if it is set to 'cmp-hash src-ip' or 'cmp-hash dst-ip'. Note: After making this change, it may be necessary to run the command 'tmsh restart sys service tmm', which will clear the old flows but also impact traffic. Traffic interrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Flow Inspector cannot filter on IP address with non-default route_domain
bugs.symptoms: Flow Inspector cannot filter on IP address with non-default route_domain.
bugs.conditions: -- In Flow Inspector. -- Attempting to filter results. -- Some results use IP addresses with non-default route domains.
bugs.impact: Filter does not return results as expected.
bugs.fix: You can now filter on IP address with non default route_domain In Flow Inspector.

bugs.title: LTM log contains shutdown sequence logs after boot_marker as logs are buffered until BIG-IP reboots
bugs.symptoms: In reboot case, the BIG-IP system buffers the shutdown sequence log messages and writes them to disk once the syslog service starts during the boot process. The boot_marker message is written before shutdown messages sync to disk. This leads to out-of-sequence log messages, making it difficult to determine when the service stop occurred.
bugs.conditions: Reboot the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Log messages appear out of order. It is difficult to tell whether service stop happened as part of reboot, or any error during the subsequent boot process.

bugs.title: Pool may temporarily become empty and any virtual server that uses that pool may temporarily become unavailable
bugs.symptoms: Intermittently (depending the timing of operations that keep MCP busy): 1. Messages similar to the following may be logged in the LTM log, indicating that the virtual server associated with a pool became temporarily unavailable: -- notice mcpd[4815]: 01071682:5: SNMP_TRAP: Virtual /Common/test_vs has become unavailable. -- notice mcpd[4815]: 01071681:5: SNMP_TRAP: Virtual /Common/test_vs has become available. 2. Optionally, if a 'min-up-members' value is configured for the pool, a message similar to the following may be logged in the LTM log, indicating that the number of available pool members became less than the configured value: -- notice mcpd[4815]: 01070282:3: Number of pool members 2 less than min up members 3.
bugs.conditions: 1. The pool members are all FQDN pool members. 2. The DNS query to resolve pool member FQDNs returns a completely new (non-overlapping) set of IP addresses. (This causes all existing Ephemeral pool members to be removed and replaced with new Ephemeral pool members.) 3. MCP is very busy and slow to process messages.
bugs.impact: Under these conditions, existing Ephemeral pool members may be removed before new Ephemeral pool members can be created to replace them, causing the pool member to become temporarily empty. This can result in intermittent loss of availability of the virtual server if all records returned by the DNS server for the referenced FQDN change from the previous response.
bugs.fix: FQDN ephemeral pool members are created in a more timely manner when FQDN resolution via DNS returns new address records.

bugs.title: PVA does not validate interface MTU when setting MSS
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect MSS value might be used when hardware (HW) syncookies are used, and the MTU is smaller than the MSS.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system sends TCP segments, fragmented across multiple IP packets, that exceed the size of the local interface MTU. -- This occurs when HW Syncookies are enabled.
bugs.impact: TCP segments larger than the local interface MTU sent towards the client. These TCP segments are transmitted as IP fragments.
bugs.workaround: Increase MTU size.

bugs.title: When adding several mitigation exceptions, the previously configured actions revert to the default action
bugs.symptoms: After adding a new item to the mitigation exception list, you can also change its mitigation action. If you do not save the changes and then add more new exception items, the mitigation actions of the previously added items return to their default value actions.
bugs.conditions: -- Add mitigation exception to the Bot Configuration. -- Change mitigation action on that new exception. -- Add new items to exception list without first saving.
bugs.impact: Mitigation action exceptions might be saved with their default value actions instead of the actions you configured.
bugs.workaround: After adding a group of exception items and editing their actions, save the Bot Configuration properties before adding any new mitigation exception items.
bugs.fix: When adding several mitigation exceptions, the previously configured actions no longer revert to the default action.

bugs.title: SNMP custom stats cannot access iStats
bugs.symptoms: While doing an snmpwalk, you encounter the following error: -- tcl callback Default return string: istats: tmstat_open_read: open: /var/tmstat/istats: Permission denied. -- istats: tmstat_read: open: /var/tmstat/istats: Permission denied. -- ERROR opening iStats read segment '/var/tmstat/istats': Permission denied.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using SNMP to access iStats.
bugs.impact: iStats cannot be accessed through SNMP and generates an error.

bugs.title: BaDoS State file load failure when signature protection is off
bugs.symptoms: Behavioral DoS (BADoS) loses its learned thresholds.
bugs.conditions: Restart of admd when signature protection is off.
bugs.impact: The system must relearn the thresholds, BADoS protection is not available during the learning time.
bugs.workaround: Turn on signatures detection.
bugs.fix: BADoS State file successfully loads after admd restart, even without signatures detection.

bugs.title: MCPD memory leak on standby BIG-IP with APM license
bugs.symptoms: MCPD may leak memory on the standby BIG-IP system in a high availability (HA) configuration if there are many updates for customization groups.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP HA configuration. - APM-enabled configuration. - Many APM configuration changes related to customization, such as creation / modification of interactive Access Policy agents (message boxes, logon pages, etc.).
bugs.impact: MCPD may leak memory and may be restarted by system monitoring process. This may affect all active sessions.

bugs.title: SQL monitor fails with 'Analyze Response failure' message even if recv string is correct
bugs.symptoms: For a database (mssql, mysql, postgresql or oracle) monitor type, with a 'recv' string configured, a pool member configured to use the DB monitor may be marked down even if the server is working and includes the configured response string among the response data. Debug logging of the SQL monitor indicates the following: ... [DBPinger-3778] - Response from server: Database: 'db1'Database: 'information_schema' ... [DBPinger-3778] - Checking for recv string: information_schema ... [DBPinger-3778] - Analyze Response failure The log shows 'Analyze Response failure' error message even when the configured 'recv' string appears within the response message from the DB server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the string matching the configured 'recv' string value does not appear in the response from the DB server in the row indicated by the 'recv-row' value configured for the monitor. The default value of 'none' for the 'recv-row' monitor configuration value is actually interpreted as 'row 1' by the DB monitor core implementation. Therefore, with the default configuration, any 'recv' string configured must appear in the first row of the DB server response in order to be recognized as a match.
bugs.impact: The DB monitor fails, and the DB server (node) is marked as down even though it is reachable and responding correctly per the configured 'recv' string.
bugs.workaround: You may use one of the following methods to work around this issue: 1. Configure the DB monitor's 'recv' string to match on the first row in the server response message. 2. Configure the 'recv-row' value in the DB monitor to match the row of the DB server's response which contains the configured 'recv' string. 3. Do not configure 'send' or 'recv' string for the DB monitor.

bugs.title: GTMD daemon crashes
bugs.symptoms: The gtmd process crashes in response to a call triggered by its own timer event.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this causes this intermittent issue are difficult to reproduce, but it might occur when the system is under heavy load when gtmd is starved of CPU cycles.
bugs.impact: The gtmd process restarts and produces a core file.

bugs.title: 'Prevent Password Auto-Complete' feature does not work on newer versions of Chrome browser
bugs.symptoms: Newer versions of Chrome browser (v75+) show the 'Save Password' dialog, even though the 'Prevent Password Auto-Complete' option is enabled.
bugs.conditions: - Provision 'Fraud Protection Service'. - License 'Application Layer Encryption'. - Create a parameter with 'Substitute Value' enabled. - Enable 'Prevent Password Auto-Complete'.
bugs.impact: The browser saves the masked password, which prevents the end-user from logging in to the protected page.
bugs.workaround: No workaround is available.
bugs.fix: The browser will no longer ask to save the end-user's password and he will be able to log in to the protected page.

bugs.title: BGP Peer-group route-maps are not applied to newly configured address-family ipv6 peers
bugs.symptoms: Inbound or outbound route-map configuration may not be applied properly to address-family ipv6 members of peer-group
bugs.conditions: This happens when route-map is applied to a peer-group before the neighbor gets configured as a peer-group member. For example: conf t no route-map test no router bgp 64512 route-map test permit 10 match ipv6 address 2001::1/128 router bgp 64512 neighbor pg1 peer-group neighbor pg1 remote-as 64512 address-family ipv6 neighbor pg1 activate neighbor pg1 route-map test out end conf t router bgp 64512 neighbor 2001::2 peer-group pg1 end
bugs.impact: route-map configuration inherited from the peer-group (in or out) may not be applied to the BGP neighbor
bugs.workaround: After a peer is added: - Remove peer-group route-map configuration. - Re-add peer-group route-map configuration. - Clear BGP sessions to apply new config.

bugs.title: SIP messages fail to forward in MRF SIP when preserve-strict source port is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: When MRF SIP is configured in per-client mode and preserve-strict source port is enabled on a virtual server, messages may fail to forward due to port collisions when multiple clients try to use the same port (which is expected/accepted behavior with this configuration). After the port has been freed or the configuration changed, messages continue to fail for clients that had previous port collisions.
bugs.conditions: -- MRF SIP configured with: Per-Client connection mode and virtual server with preserve-strict source port enabled. -- Multiple clients try to connect using the same local port. -- Previously failed client connections attempt to connect again after the port has been freed or configuration changed.
bugs.impact: Calls from one or more clients are unable to be completed.
bugs.workaround: You can prevent this behavior using either workaround: -- Configure a different connection mode (Per-TMM, for example). -- Disable preserve-strict source port on the virtual server.
bugs.fix: Clients with previous connection failures are now able to connect when the port is no longer in use or the configuration has been changed.

bugs.title: TMM may experience high latency when processing WebSocket traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may experience higher than usual latency when processing WebSocket traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- WebSocket traffic. -- Very long connections or large amounts traffic. -- Platforms with many CPUs.
bugs.impact: Increased latency in WebSocket traffic.
bugs.fix: Fix an issue that could cause a latency with WebSocket traffic.

bugs.title: WebSSO does not support large NTLM target info length
bugs.symptoms: WebSSO crashes.
bugs.conditions: When the optional field of the target info is about 1000 bytes or larger.
bugs.impact: WebSSO crashes and loss of service.
bugs.workaround: Config NTLM not to have large target info, recommend < 800.

bugs.title: On Upgrade or UCS Restore Decryption of the vCMP Guest sym-unit-key Field Fails on the Host
bugs.symptoms: An upgrade or UCS restore fails on the host with an error message: err mcpd[1001]: 01071769:3: Decryption of the field (sym_unit_key) for object (<guest name>) failed.
bugs.conditions: -- An upgrade or UCS restore of the vCMP host. -- Having a vCMP guest's sym-unit-key field populated. -- Having changed the host's master key.
bugs.impact: The upgrade or UCS restore fails with an MCPD error.
bugs.workaround: Comment out the sym-unit-key field and load the configuration.

bugs.title: When in HA, the Standby device is forwarding traffic causing a loop and subsequent network shutdown
bugs.symptoms: Standby is passing traffic when a virtual wire is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual wire configured in high availability (HA).
bugs.impact: Standby device is forwarding traffic traffic when it should not, causing a loop and subsequent network shutdown.
bugs.fix: The Standby device no longer passes traffic through virtual wire when it should not.

bugs.title: Cannot process empty ltcfg field value: class name
bugs.symptoms: You see the following in /var/log/ltm: bigip1.localdomain notice mcpd[8154]: 01b00001:5: Cannot process empty ltcfg field value: class name (trapsess) field name () This message is issued when snmp trap destinations are configured without pass phrases. It is not an error and the log message can be ignored.
bugs.conditions: Configuring SNMP trap destinations.
bugs.impact: Meaningless logs.
bugs.fix: The log message has been removed.

bugs.title: iRules LX Streaming Extension dies with Uncaught, unspecified error event
bugs.symptoms: You are using a virtual with an ilx profile generated from an iRules LX Streaming extension and observed the following error or similar. Sep 05 09:16:52 pid[5850] Error: Uncaught, unspecified "error" event. (ETIMEDOUT) Sep 05 09:16:52 pid[5850] at ILXFlow.emit (events.js:163:17) Sep 05 09:16:52 pid[5850] at ILXFlowWrap.ilxFlowErrorCb [as onIlxError] (/var/sdm/plugin_store/plugins/<pluginName>/extensions/<workspaceName>/node_modules/f5-nodejs/lib/ilx_flow.js:108:10)
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with an ilx profile generated from an iRules LX Streaming extension. The problem is aggravated if a web-acceleration profile is configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic may be disrupted until the sdmd daemon has respawned another node.js process.

bugs.title: ICMP replies are forwarded with incorrect checksums causing them to be dropped
bugs.symptoms: If a FastL4 virtual server receives an ICMP response without first receiving an ICMP request, the checksum on the ICMP response that is egressed by tmm will not be calculated correctly.
bugs.conditions: An ICMP response without a corresponding ICMP request, such as in non-symmetric routing scenarios.
bugs.impact: ICMP replies are forwarded with the incorrect checksum and likely will be dropped by the recipient or other devices on the network.
bugs.workaround: Ensure symmetric routing. Configure L7 virtual servers for use with ipother profiles.

bugs.title: Some WebSafe request signatures may not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: Request signatures are part of the WebSafe signature mechanism. The request signature is achieved by configuring an FPS-protected URL and a corresponding custom-alert. If the URL is a wildcard, a priority must be assigned to determine the order of matching. URL matching by priority is not working properly. As a result, the signature do not work as expected
bugs.conditions: There is at least one wildcard URL configured by the request signature update file.
bugs.impact: A portion of WebSafe request signature do not work as expected: -- An alert is sent, though it should not be (false-positive). -- An alert was not sent, though it should be (false-negative).
bugs.workaround: Configure the same signature manually in the BIG-IP system's GUI/tmsh.
bugs.fix: FPS now correctly handles signature-based wildcard URL's priority.

bugs.title: TMM is unable to redirect RRDAG'd traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM cannot redirect RRDAG traffic in vCMP guest. This can affect GTP traffic.
bugs.conditions: Send UDP traffic to vCMP guest using RRDAG cmp-hash.
bugs.impact: Traffic is pinned to tmm.0.
bugs.fix: A new db variable has been added: dag.rrdag.redirect enable|disable The default value is disable. Enabling this db variable allows the BIG-IP system to evenly disaggregate UDP traffic that has low entropy in ports in hardware in vCMP mode. In vCMP guests, the BIG-IP system can redirect UDP traffic using non-default cmp hash.
bugs.behavior: A new db variable has been added: dag.rrdag.redirect enable|disable The default value is disable. Enabling this db variable allows the BIG-IP system to evenly disaggregate UDP traffic that has low entropy in ports in hardware in vCMP mode. In vCMP guests, the BIG-IP system can redirect UDP traffic using non-default cmp hash.

bugs.title: [api-status-warning] are generated at stderr and /var/log/ltm when listing config with all-properties argument
bugs.symptoms: Running the command 'tmsh list' on a pool or virtual server with the 'all-properties' argument generates a warning: [api-status-warning] ltm/virtual, properties : deprecated : urldb-feed-policy
bugs.conditions: Including the 'all-properties' argument with the 'tmsh list' command.
bugs.impact: There is no impact to the system. The excessive [api-status-warning] at stderr and /var/log/ltm for tmsh list commands are spurious, benign, and can be ignored.
bugs.workaround: tmsh modify /mgmt shared settings api-status log resource-property deprecatedApiAllowed false tmsh modify /mgmt shared settings api-status log resource deprecatedApiAllowed false

bugs.title: MRF SIP, Diameter, Generic MSG, high availability (HA) - mirrored-message-sweeper-interval not loaded.
bugs.symptoms: The mirrored-message-sweeper-interval configuration option has no effect on the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: MRF in use, high availability configured, and a SIP profile is configured to use a specific Mirrored Message Sweeper Interval setting.
bugs.impact: On a system under high load, the next active device in a high availability (HA) pair could run out of memory.
bugs.fix: Message sweeper interval value now loads correctly.

bugs.title: SAML attribute value when supplied with quotes "" around it causes error while displaying the list of SAML IDPs
bugs.symptoms: When you create a new or edit an existing SAML IDP and provide SAML attribute value surrounded by quotation marks ("" ), the existing list of SAML IDPs will not be displayed.
bugs.conditions: SAML IDP attribute value provided is surrounded by "".
bugs.impact: GUI does not display the list of existing SAML IDPs.
bugs.workaround: Do not provide SAML attributes with "" surrounding the attribute values. If there are any attributes with "" surrounding, delete them using TMSH.

bugs.title: Log HSB registers when parts of the device becomes unresponsive
bugs.symptoms: Part of the HSB becomes unresponsive and there is no logging of additional registers to assist in diagnosing the failure.
bugs.conditions: It is unknown under what conditions the HSB becomes unresponsive.
bugs.impact: Limited visibility into the HSB state when it becomes unresponsive.
bugs.fix: Additional logging of HSB register states has been added whenever parts of the HSB become unresponsive.

bugs.title: REST API to /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/stats/<specific pool> will fail for some pools
bugs.symptoms: The GET requests to REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/stats for a specific pool may fail with Error 404.
bugs.conditions: Pools that start with the letter 'm'. This is because those endpoints contain objects with incorrect selflinks. For example: - Query to the below pool that starts with the letter 'm' will work as it contains the right selflink. - Pool: "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/~Common~m/stats" - selfLink: "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/~Common~m/stats?ver=x.x.x.x" - Query to the below pool that does not start with the letter 'm' may not work as it contains the wrong selflink. - Pool: "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/~Common~a/stats" - selfLink: "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/~Common~a/stats?ver=x.x.x.x" In the above example, the word 'members' is displayed in selflink.
bugs.impact: Errors are observed with GET requests to REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/stats.
bugs.workaround: The following workarounds are available: 1. Use /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/stats without a specific pool, which does return the pool member stats for every pool. 2. For each pool member in /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool, issue a GET for: /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/<pool>/members/<member>/stats
bugs.fix: The REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool/members/stats/<specific pool> will have the working endpoints returned.

bugs.title: Check SAs in context callbacks
bugs.symptoms: Crypto operations can crash.
bugs.conditions: Any crypto operation involving an ike-sa or a child-sa.
bugs.impact: Tunnel outage due to core, lasting until restart and renegotiation.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash related to crypto operations and SAs.

bugs.title: DB monitor marks pool member down if no send/recv strings are configured
bugs.symptoms: If an LTM database monitor type (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle or PostgreSQL database monitor type) is configured without a 'send' string to issue a user-specified database query, pool members using this monitor are marked DOWN, even though a connection to the configured database completed successfully.
bugs.conditions: -- AnLTM pool or pool members are configured to us an LTM database (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle or PostgreSQL) monitor type. -- No send string is configured for the monitor.
bugs.impact: With this configuration, the monitor connects to the configured database, but does not issue a query or check for a specific response. Pool members are always marked DOWN when using a database monitor with no 'send' string configured.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, configure 'send' and 'recv' strings for the database monitor that will always succeed when successfully connected to the specified database (with the configured username and password, if applicable).

bugs.title: JavaScript challenges fail when using LTM Rules which disable DoSL7, Bot Defense, or ASM by default
bugs.symptoms: When using complex CPM rules (LTM Policy), and the default rule is to disable DoSL7, Bot Defense, or ASM, the special URLs cannot reach the DoSL7 hudfilter or BD, and are getting blocked. These cause any JavaScript challenges to not pass, and block the users. Example of l7dos disabled by default: default { actions { 0 { l7dos disable } } ordinal 3 } In this case, the following error is observed in /var/log/ltm if ASM Policy is also used: [2aeadec:931] Internal error (ASM requested abort (trans begin error)) The request reaches ASM but without the policy identifier and the error is seen.
bugs.conditions: Using complex CPM rules (LTM Policies) in which the default rule is to disable DoSL7, Bot Defense, or ASM.
bugs.impact: JavaScript challenges fail and block traffic from browsers.
bugs.workaround: -- If l7dos or bot-defense is disabled on the default rule, then add a rule for enabling l7dos or bot-defense on requests to /TSPD/* URLs. -- If asm is disabled on the default rule, then add a rule for enabling asm on requests to /TSbd/* URLs.

bugs.title: tmsh help text contains a reference to bigpipe, which is no longer supported
bugs.symptoms: The 'sys httpd ssl-certkeyfile' tmsh help text contains a reference to bigpipe, which is no longer supported.
bugs.conditions: Viewing tmsh help for 'sys httpd ssl-certkeyfile'.
bugs.impact: Incorrect reference to bigpipe.
bugs.workaround: You can use the following command sequence to change the key: modify httpd { ssl-certfile [string] ssl-certkeyfile [string] }

bugs.title: ASM reporting for WebSocket frames has empty username field
bugs.symptoms: When using ASM to inspect and report WebSocket frames, the username field is always reported as empty or absent.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- WebSocket profile attached to a virtual server. -- ASM logging profile attached to a virtual server. -- WebSocket traffic inspected by ASM and logged as event log message or remote logger message.
bugs.impact: Poor visibility of current logged-in user in the event log for WebSocket frames.
bugs.fix: ASM populates username field for logged WebSocket frames

bugs.title: Unable to enable LDAP system auth profile debug logging
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in version 14.1.0, LDAP debugging must be performed on nslcd logs and not pam_ldap logs; however, it is not possible to enable debug logging on nslcd via the configuration file.
bugs.conditions: This would be encountered only if you (or F5 Support) wanted to do troubleshooting of LDAP connections by enabling debug logging.
bugs.impact: LDAP system authentication 'debug' parameter does not provide sufficient levels of debug logs, but there is no functional impact to normal system operation.
bugs.workaround: To enable debug logging and have the system post log messages to the SSH/console window, start the nslcd process with -d option, which causes nslcd to run in the foreground until you press control-c to stop it: systemctl stop nslcd nslcd -d Note: The -d setting does not persist, so each time you want to log debug output, you must complete this procedure. You can increase the amount of debug output by specifying additional -d options (up to 3), e.g., '-ddd' or '-d -d -d'. When done, stop nslcd with control-c, and then restart it with the default options via the normal systemctl daemon: systemctl start nslcd
bugs.fix: The nslcd logs are now visible on /var/log/secure file.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing crypto data
bugs.symptoms: While processing cryptographic data using Intel QAT hardware, TMM may crash with a SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: Intel QAT hardware present Hardware acceleration enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash resulting in a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes QAT-accelerated cryptographic traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Change of pool configuration in OneConnect environment can impact active traffic
bugs.symptoms: In OneConnect environments, when the default pool is updated for the first time, active connections reconnect to new pool members. Further update to pool configuration has no impact on traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with OneConnect profile. -- Default pool is updated when active connections are present.
bugs.impact: Active traffic disrupted.

bugs.title: Distributed reports fail when management address is used for config sync in a device group
bugs.symptoms: In system where a device group uses the management interface, reporting statistics for device group does not work. The following error appears in /var/log/avr/monpd.log: REPORTER|ERROR|Nov 04 14:24:38.017|32640|../src/reporter/handlers/distributed/DistributedReportRunnerHandler.cpp:processCallStatusMessage:1921| Map reduce call failed. Can't collect report data from the cluster members..
bugs.conditions: -- Device group is used. -- The configsync.allowmanagement DB variable is set to 'enable'. -- Management IP address is used as the config sync address of the device group.
bugs.impact: AVR statistics report for device group does not work.
bugs.workaround: Use a self IP address for device groups instead of the management IP address.
bugs.fix: AVR statistics are now reported for device groups under these conditions.

bugs.title: GTP log message contains no useful information
bugs.symptoms: GTP profile and GTP iRules provide no useful information in order to proceed with troubleshooting.
bugs.conditions: GTP profile or iRules fails to process message
bugs.impact: User lacks of information for troubleshooting
bugs.fix: GTP error log has been replaced with a more useful message. The new log message provides more intuitive information including the reason and, in some messages, location of data that causes the failure.

bugs.title: REST does not follow current design best practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, REST endpoints do not follow current design best practices.
bugs.conditions: Authenticated REST request with malicious content.
bugs.impact: REST endpoints do not follow current design best practices.
bugs.fix: REST endpoints now follow current design best practices.

bugs.title: Cannot 'Reset Count' or search logs for firewall global policy in different partition
bugs.symptoms: In GUI Firewall active policy page, 'Reset Count' and 'search logs' buttons are disabled when you are in a different partition then the rule's source partition.
bugs.conditions: -- An active policy is in a different partition from the one you are in. -- Security :: Network Firewall : Active Rules. -- Select a rule. -- Attempt to reset count.
bugs.impact: Count cannot be reset; the button is grayed out.
bugs.workaround: To enable the buttons, change to the partition used for creating that specific policy.
bugs.fix: You can now reset the count or search logs even if they are in a different partition.

bugs.title: MySQL monitor fails to connect to MySQL Server v8.0
bugs.symptoms: The LTM MySQL health monitor fails to connect to a MySQL server running MySQL Server v8.0. A pool member configured for a MySQL server running MySQL Server v8.0 and using the MySQL health monitor will be marked DOWN.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the LTM MySQL health monitor to monitor a MySQL server running MySQL Server v8.0.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP cannot monitor the health of a MySQL server running MySQL Server v8.0 using the MySQL health monitor.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP can monitor the health of a MySQL server running MySQL Server v8.0 using the MySQL health monitor.

bugs.title: In-TMM MQTT monitor is not working as expected
bugs.symptoms: The monitoring probes are not being sent out to the network. Regardless of the monitor config and sys db variable.
bugs.conditions: Configuring the in-TMM MQTT monitor.
bugs.impact: Pool members with attached MQTT monitor state is incorrectly shown as DOWN.
bugs.fix: In-TMM MQTT monitor now works as expected.

bugs.title: Unwanted LDAP referrals slow or prevent administrative login
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP system configured with remote LDAP/Active Directory authentication, attempting to login to the Configuration Utility or to the command-line interface may proceed very slowly or fail.
bugs.conditions: -- LDAP/Active Directory 'system-auth' authentication configured. -- The Active Directory enables LDAP referrals (the default). -- There are a large number of Active Directory servers in the enterprise, or the BIG-IP system does not have complete network connectivity to all Active Directory servers (caused by firewalls or special routes).
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system may accept LDAP referrals that it is unable to process, resulting in authentication timeouts/failures.
bugs.workaround: To temporarily disable the referrals, edit one of the configuration files /etc/nslcd.conf or /config/bigip/auth/pam.d/ldap/system-auth.conf, and add the following line: referrals no Restart nslcd service to apply change: systemctl restart nslcd Note: This change is not persistent and will be lost whenever MCPD re-loads the configuration, or when other changes are made to system-auth configuration values.
bugs.fix: Changes to LDAP referrals value in configuration are now saved, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: JWT Claim value without quotes is invalid
bugs.symptoms: JSON payload is invalid since claims are generated without quotes(")
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP creates JWT claim value without quotes when scope is not openid.
bugs.impact: Token is invalid.
bugs.workaround: Replace claim type 'string' with 'custom' adding quotes after backslash. apm oauth oauth-claim /Common/uid { claim-name uid claim-type custom claim-value "\"%{session.custom.name:noconv}\"" }

bugs.title: Align the behavior of NAT44 and NAT64 when translate-address is disabled under Virtual Configuration with LTM Pool and LSN Pool
bugs.symptoms: Configure translate-address disabled under Virtual with LTM pool configured. In the NAT44 case, LTM pool is used as next-hop and packets are L2 forwarded to LTM pool members without destination address translated. In NAT64 case, packets are dropped if there is no route available to reach the IPv4 destinations (derived from original IPv6 destination). Packets are not L2 forwarded to LTM pool members.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with LTM pool configured. -- CGNAT LSN pool configured. -- Translate-address disabled.
bugs.impact: If there is no route available to reach the destination, NAT64 packets are dropped.
bugs.workaround: Configure default gateways/routes to reach the IPv4 destination in NAT64 case.
bugs.fix: Aligned the behavior of NAT44 and NAT64 when translate-address is disabled under Virtual Configuration with LTM Pool and LSN Pool. Use LTM pool as next hop for L2 forwarding the NAT64 packets when translate-address is disabled.

bugs.title: Segmentation fault when pem_sessiondump --detail with special character in session attribute
bugs.symptoms: Segmentation fault. No impact to traffic.
bugs.conditions: Configure session with special character in its attribute. Pem_sessiondump --detail of the session causes it to crash.
bugs.impact: pem_sessiondump --detail returns segmentation fault.
bugs.fix: Allocated stack space for variable in the required function.

bugs.title: Loading the configuration may not set the virtual server enabled status correctly
bugs.symptoms: When loading the configuration, if the virtual address is disabled but the virtual server is enabled, the virtual server may still pass traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Loading the configuration. -- A virtual server's virtual address is disabled.
bugs.impact: Virtual servers unexpectedly process traffic.
bugs.workaround: Manually re-enable and disable the virtual address.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when using AFM with sPVA and DoS vectors enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when using AFM/sPVA with Network and DNS Security vectors.
bugs.conditions: AFM is configured with hardware DoS (sPVA) enabled, along with Network and DNS security vectors.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: -- Use only DNS security vectors. -- Disable hardware DoS (sPVA): tmsh modify sys db dos.forceswdos value true

bugs.title: TMM may produce a core on a standby device
bugs.symptoms: Tmm cores on the standby device.
bugs.conditions: Detailed condition is still unknown. So far, this issue is observed under the following configuration. -- Connection mirroring is enabled on Standard type of virtual server. -- High availability (HA) configured.
bugs.impact: On a Standby BIG-IP unit, traffic is disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: CPM policy stops matching after adding rule
bugs.symptoms: LTM Centralized Policy Matching (CPM) policy conditions stop matching some traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Very specific LTM policy configuration. -- Adding a matching rule. For this case, an example scenario might involve a rule with two conditions and two actions. The two conditions check for one of two HTTP hosts, and checking that the HTTP URI path starts with some substring. The two actions are typically disabling server SSL, and forwarding to a specific pool. The last rule is called DropAll and matches all traffic.
bugs.impact: This might cause the policy to stop matching for nearly all rules, including the rule that check for 'All Traffic'.

bugs.title: Installation issues when adding new blade v12.1.3 to VPR cluster v14.1.0.1 EHF
bugs.symptoms: A newly inserted blade fails to upgrade on a Viprion system.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen only on VIPRION chassis when the primary blade is running engineering hotfix (EHF) v14.1.0.1 EHF 0.17.7 and newly inserted blade is configured with v12.1.3.
bugs.impact: Unable to upgrade the new blade in VIPRION chassis.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the active volume on the primary blade contains a version other than an EHF, and the other volume is installed with the EHF, then insert the new blade in the chassis.
bugs.fix: A software image containing an Engineering Hotfix which includes an updated nash-initrd package may be successfully installed into blades in VIPRION chassis.

bugs.title: Save-on-auto-sync is not working as expected with large configuration objects
bugs.symptoms: In device group has enabled 'save sys config' for all auto-sync operations using the following command: modify cm device-group name save-on-auto-sync true Warning: Enabling the save-on-auto-sync option can unexpectedly impact system performance when the BIG-IP system automatically saves a large configuration change to each device.
bugs.conditions: -- The save-on-auto-sync option is enabled. -- Device has large configuration, such as 2,100 virtual servers and ~1100 partitions
bugs.impact: Configuration it not saved, which leads to out-of-sync condition.
bugs.workaround: You can avoid this issue by using manual sync instead of auto-sync, or by not enabling 'save-on-auto-sync'.

bugs.title: DNSSEC Key Generation expires if creation of new Generation failed
bugs.symptoms: DNSSEC Key generation expires when new generation failed to be created.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured with rolling DNSSEC Key and following conditions are met: 1. New DNSSEC Key generation not created due to failure, so only one generation remains for the DNSSEC Key. 2. The old DNSSEC Key generation is nearly expired.
bugs.impact: The last DNSSEC Key generation expires and the Key does not have any generation. As a result, BIG-IP fails to sign RRs with the DNSSEC Key.
bugs.workaround: New DNSSEC Key can be created to trigger creation of new generation.
bugs.fix: DNSSEC Key generation never expires if that generation is the last one for the DNSSEC Key.

bugs.title: HTTPS monitoring is not caching SSL sessions correctly
bugs.symptoms: In situations where a cached SSL session cannot be used, there are conditions where the information for old and new SSL sessions are not properly updated, and valid SSL sessions are not terminated in an orderly fashion.
bugs.conditions: When using GTM HTTPS monitoring.
bugs.impact: Information for old and new SSL sessions are not properly updated, and valid SSL sessions are not terminated in an orderly fashion.
bugs.workaround: Restart big3d by running the following command: bigstart restart big3d

bugs.title: Incorrect Active/Standby status in CLI Prompt after failover test
bugs.symptoms: After running 'promptstatusd -y' to check current failover status, it displays an incorrect Active/Standby status in the CLI prompt.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions: 1. Modify the db variable: bigdb failover.state. 2. Check that /var/prompt/ps1 and CLI prompt reflect the setting. 2. Reboot the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Status shown in the prompt does not change.
bugs.workaround: Do not run 'promptstatusd -y' command manually. The db variable 'failover.state is a status-reporting variable. The system does not report status manually set to something other than the actual status. Note: 'promptstatusd' is not a BIG-IP user command, it is a daemon. It is highly unlikely that manually running this command will produce information that is useful or relevant to the status being sought.

bugs.title: Encountering apmd out of memory events and process getting halted
bugs.symptoms: The kernel logs out-of-memory errors and halts apmd: err kernel: : [70076.639026] Killed process 16095 (apmd) total-vm:7054192kB, anon-rss:2759164kB, file-rss:4724kB, shmem-rss:156kB.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered when APM is provisioned and running.
bugs.impact: APM process is halted and restarted. APM traffic disrupted while apmd restarts.

bugs.title: Config utility (web UI) output differs between tmsh and AS3 when the pool monitor is changed.
bugs.symptoms: When a transaction attempts multiple commands (delete, create, modify) for the same object in the same transaction, the results can be unexpected or undefined. A common example is: 'transaction { delete key create_if key }' where the transaction attempts 'delete key', and then 'create_if key', which unmarks the delete operation on the key (so in this case the key remains unmodified). In other cases it is possible that monitoring stops for the associated object, such as for: pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor.
bugs.conditions: A user-initiated transaction attempts multiple commands for the same monitor-related object (such as delete, create, modify).
bugs.impact: The GUI shows misleading info about the pool monitor.The monitor-related object may be unchanged, or monitoring may stop for that object.
bugs.workaround: Transactions modifying a monitor-related object (pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor) should perform a single command upon that object (such as one of: 'delete', 'create', 'modify').
bugs.fix: Behavior is as-expected when a transaction executes multiple commands (such as 'delete', 'create', 'modify') upon the same monitor-related object (pool, pool_member, node_address, monitor).

bugs.title: IRules ending with a comment cause config verification to fail
bugs.symptoms: 'tmsh load sys config verify' reports error messages for a signed iRule: -- 01071485:3: iRule (/Common/example) content does not match the signature. -- Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Have an iRule which ends in a comment. -- iRule is signed. -- Run the command: tmsh load sys config verify
bugs.impact: 'tmsh load sys config verify' reports an error when there should be none. Configuration validation fails.
bugs.workaround: Delete or move any comments that are at the end of the iRule, and validate the configuration again.

bugs.title: Replaced ISC_TRUE and ISC_FALSE with true and false
bugs.symptoms: Updated the zrd code to remove references to ISC_TRUE and ISC_FALSE since the software is upgraded BIND to 9.11.8 and those macros do not exist anymore.
bugs.conditions: BIND version is earlier than 9.11.8.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact.
bugs.fix: Removed references to ISC_TRUE and ISC_FALSE zrd since the software has been upgraded to BIND to 9.11.8 and those macros do not exist anymore.
bugs.behavior: Removed references to ISC_TRUE and ISC_FALSE zrd since the software has been upgraded to BIND to 9.11.8 and those macros do not exist anymore.

bugs.title: IPsec works inefficiently with a second blade in one chassis
bugs.symptoms: Under high availability (HA) configurations, a secondary blade does not receive mirrored updates for security associations (SAs). When a new ike-peer is created, if that peer's IP address is handled by a secondary blade, all IKE negotiation packets are dropped after forwarding between primary and secondary blades. But an ike-peer that is present from the start is mistakenly assigned to a primary blade, and thus works correctly.
bugs.conditions: -- More than one blade: a secondary blade in addition to a primary blade. -- Remote ike-peer IP addresses that happen to hash to a secondary blade by the BIG-IP system disaggregation (DAG) mechanism. -- Configuration for Active-Standby, which works on Active but fails to mirror SAs to Standby, when the IP address would be handled by a secondary blade.
bugs.impact: After failover from Active to Standby, missing SAs that could not be mirrored are renegotiated, causing tunnel outage until new negotiation concludes. After adding a new ike-peer that should negotiate on a secondary blade, all IKE packets vanish, so no tunnel is ever created for such an ike-peer. In high availability (HA) configurations, tunnels re-establish after renegotiation, for tunnels that would be assigned to a secondary blade. This works, but undercuts the benefit of high availability (HA) for tunnels other than those on a primary blade.
bugs.workaround: For a new ike-peer assigned to a secondary blade, restart tmm or the blade, and when the system comes back up, this peer is handled on the primary blade. Note: Although this peer can then create a tunnel, any secondary blade is unused by IPsec.
bugs.fix: Assignment of blade ownership is now correct after a restart, even when blades are slowly discovered incrementally, or added dynamically after a system has come up. HA mirroring works, and SAs are present after failover. Tunnels are negotiated on secondary blades, so ike-peer instances with IP addresses handled on a secondary blade function as well as those on a primary blade.

bugs.title: ConfigSync Hardening
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, ConfigSync does not apply design best practices.
bugs.conditions: Clustered device is used.
bugs.impact: ConfigSync does not apply design best practices.
bugs.fix: ConfigSync now applies design best practices.

bugs.title: SWG license does not get released for sessions created through iRules
bugs.symptoms: Requests get blocked/reset as SWG license does not get released for sessions created through iRules
bugs.conditions: SWG iRules is used to create APM/SWG session with per-request policy having category lookup agent.
bugs.impact: Requests get blocked/reset.
bugs.fix: SWG license gets released for sessions created through irules.

bugs.title: Requests fail to load when backend server overrides request cookies and Bot Defense is used
bugs.symptoms: When Bot Defense is used on the backend server that overrides request cookies, requests to non-HTML resources may fail, or may receive the whitepage JavaScript challenge. An example is when a back-end server responds with a Set-Cookie header containing empty values for each cookie request cookie it does not recognize.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense is enabled. -- Backend server is overriding the Bot Defense cookies with the TS prefix.
bugs.impact: Some URLs fail to load following the JavaScript challenge.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to strip the TSPD_101 cookie from the request before forwarding it to the backend: when HTTP_REQUEST_RELEASE { HTTP::cookie remove "TSPD_101" }

bugs.title: ICMP echo requests occasionally go unanswered
bugs.symptoms: ARP entry get stuck at state NEXTHOP_INCOMPLETE for several seconds.
bugs.conditions: -- There is no ARP entry for the return-route router. -- The 'remote' BIG-IP system receives ICMP echo request.
bugs.impact: Possible traffic failures.
bugs.fix: ICMP echo replies are always sent for a valid ICMP echo request.

bugs.title: Upgrade fails when client-ssl inherits proxy-ca-key/cert with error message: Client SSL profile (/Common/child): must have at least one set of CA type cert-key-chain.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade failure when loading configuration file or ucs from older version, with the below error message against child client-ssl profile: Client SSL profile (/Common/child): must have at least one set of CA type cert-key-chain.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- When upgrading from an older version (earlier than 14.0.0) to a newer version (14.1.0 or later). -- The configuration has a child client SSL profile that inherits from a parent client SSL profile. -- The parent SSL profile has SSL forward proxy enabled and proxy-ca-cert/proxy-ca-key configured.
bugs.impact: Unable to upgrade the system with old configuration.
bugs.workaround: You can workaround this issue using the following procedure: 1. Manually edit /config/bigip.conf to add the following lines: proxy-ca-cert /Common/rsa.crt proxy-ca-key /Common/rsa.key 2. Reload the configuration using the following command: tmsh load sys config Here is an example: ltm profile client-ssl /Common/child { app-service none cert /Common/default.crt cert-key-chain { default { cert /Common/default.crt key /Common/default.key } } chain none defaults-from /Common/parent inherit-certkeychain true key /Common/default.key passphrase none proxy-ca-cert /Common/rsa.crt <===== add this line proxy-ca-key /Common/rsa.key <===== add this line }

bugs.title: TMM can leak memory under specific traffic and iRule configurations.
bugs.symptoms: -- TMM leaks memory in the 'bigip_connection' component. -- Depending on the specific iRule configuration, other components, such as 'tcl' and 'tclrule_pcb', may also leak. -- A 'double flow removal Oops' message may be visible in the tmm and ltm log files. -- 'TCL error' messages may be visible in the ltm log file.
bugs.conditions: This issue is known to occur only under rare circumstances in conjunction with specific traffic and iRule configurations.
bugs.impact: After a prolonged amount of time spent leaking memory, TMM may not be able to fulfill new memory allocations and crash. This results in a traffic interruption, a core file, and a failover on redundant units. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: The word 'ceritifcate' is misspelled in an error message
bugs.symptoms: The word 'ceritifcate' should be spelled 'certificate' in the error message: err big3d[5725]: 12b10000:3: Could not list the ceritifcate directory '/shared/em/ssl.crt' in function EmCertsModified: Permission denied.
bugs.conditions: This message is produced by big3d when attempting to re-read the certificate file after it realises the timestamp of the file has changed.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact to the system. This is an error message that needs updating. In addition, the inclusion of the term 'EM' is erroneous, and you can ignore it.

bugs.title: Loading UCS file on VIPRION not updating interface flow-control settings on non-primary blades.
bugs.symptoms: Interface flow-control settings on non-primary blades are not updated after loading a UCS file.
bugs.conditions: 1. Save UCS with 'flow-control' default value 'tx-rx'. 2. Modify the value from 'rx-tx' to 'none'. 3. Save another UCS with modified value. 4. Load the UCS with default value, everything works fine here. 5. Load the UCS with the modified value.
bugs.impact: The 'flow-control' setting gets changed. The functionality does not work after the first UCS load.
bugs.workaround: Load the same UCS file again.

bugs.title: Link Up status should clear Link Down in Nokia Alarm database
bugs.symptoms: When using Nokia NetAct (the alertd.nokia.alarm DB variable has the value "enable"), the LINK STATUS traps are the same for down/disable and up/enable. That has the side effect of leaving entries in the Nokia Alarm database.
bugs.conditions: Enable Nokia NetAct and see that the alarm database has uncleared entries for link status changes.
bugs.impact: This is confusing because entries in the database that do not clear.
bugs.fix: A new DB variable has been implemented (alertd.nokia.linktraps). The default value is disabled and the variable only takes effect when alertd.nokia.alarm is enabled. Note that the first time these variables are enabled you must restart the alert daemon and the nokiasnmp daemon. With these variables enabled (and the daemons restarted) the link status traps are broken out into two separate traps. The LINK UP/ENABLED trap clears the LINK DOWN/DISABLED trap.

bugs.title: When using a variable as the only parameter to the iRule persist command, the iRule validation fails
bugs.symptoms: When using a variable as the only parameter to the iRule persist command, for example: when HTTP_REQUEST { set persistence none persist $persistence } The iRule validation fails with the message: Persistence mode (Cookie) called out in rule <rule name> requires a corresponding persistence profile for virtual server
bugs.conditions: Using a variable as the only parameter to the iRule persist command.
bugs.impact: Validation fails and hence the system config cannot be loaded.
bugs.workaround: The first parameter is one of pre-defined action keywords, so use plain text.

bugs.title: Cannot use BIG-IQ to license BIG-IP 14.1.0.3 on AWS.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP 14.1.0.3 on AWS license does not complete from BIG-IQ.
bugs.conditions: -- Using BIG-IQ. -- Attempting to license BIG-IP 14.1.0.3 on AWS.
bugs.impact: Cannot use BIG-IQ to license BIG-IP 14.1.0.3 on AWS.
bugs.workaround: Restart restjavad on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Can now use BIG-IQ to license BIG-IP 14.1.0.3 on AWS.

bugs.title: Tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: When the tunnel count is high, tmm can crash.
bugs.conditions: This issue was not reproducible and steps are unknown as it occurs randomly.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: APM per-request policy continues evaluation even if variable assign agent is created with bad expression.
bugs.symptoms: APM per-request policy contains variable assign agent with an incorrect expression, e.g., 'return {aa}}}'. When traffic is passed through a virtual server containing such a per-request policy, traffic processing continues past the variable assign agent, and the client connection is reset later.
bugs.conditions: -- APM per-request policy contains a variable assign agent with an incorrect expression, e.g.,'return {aa}}}'. -- Traffic is passed through a virtual server containing such a per-request policy.
bugs.impact: APM per-request policy continues evaluation past variable assign agent and fails at random events, resulting in a RST sent to client.
bugs.workaround: Fix the expression in variable assign agent used in APM per-request policy attached to virtual server.
bugs.fix: APM per-request policy does not evaluate past the variable assign agent, if the expression in the variable assign agent is incorrect.

bugs.title: Change in Default password policy for number of characters different between passwords
bugs.symptoms: DoD STIG requires that there be an 8-character difference between old and new passwords; the current default is 5.
bugs.conditions: Changing passwords.
bugs.impact: When you change a BIG-IP password, the new password must have 8 characters different from the old.
bugs.fix: Default is changed from 5 to 8.
bugs.behavior: Change in Default password policy for number of characters that must be different from previous passwords. The default number of characters that must differ has changed from 5 to 8.

bugs.title: Root's crontab file may become empty
bugs.symptoms: Under low-disk conditions for the /var/ filesystem, BIG-IP system processes may incorrectly update root's crontab file (/var/spool/cron/root). This results in the file contents being removed; i.e., the file is empty.
bugs.conditions: Low disk space on the /var filesystem.
bugs.impact: System and user entries in root's crontab file stop executing.

bugs.title: OVA/Azure template sets '/var' partition with not enough space
bugs.symptoms: After booting a new BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) image from OVA or Azure, you see errors on the console: Broadcast message from root@localhost.localdomain: 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var has only 19% free.
bugs.conditions: Installing BIG-IP software via the OVA template or Azure image.
bugs.impact: System is generally un-usable; applications cannot operate without space in /var. Diskmonitor reports console errors and errors in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.workaround: Remove unused APM binaries in /var/sam/images.

bugs.title: AVR statistics are lost when performing an upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After performing an upgrade on an offline/standby machine, AVR statistics were gone. This was done on a device-group configuration in this way: 1. sync configuration 2. take UCS backup 3. make the standby unit forced offline. 4. install a new boot location on the standby unit. 5. Switchboot the standby unit from the newly installed location. 6. The standby unit comes online with the new version. 7. Release the standby from offline, becoming standby. 8. Make a failover, now the standby running on the new version becomes active. 9. Force new standby (previously active and on the old version) offline 10. Install the new version on the current standby unit 11. Switchboot the current standby. 12. Release offline the current standby. 13. Now both units are on the new version
bugs.conditions: Using AVR statistics and performing an upgrade on a machine that is not in the state of 'active' and 'online'.
bugs.impact: AVR statistics are not being backed-up and/or restored when performing an upgrade on a machine.
bugs.workaround: On the 'from' version (i.e., before starting the upgrade process), do the following: $ cp /usr/share/avr/bin/avr_db_backup.sh /shared/avr_db_backup.sh.orig $ cp /usr/share/avr/bin/avr_db_restore.sh /shared/avr_db_restore.sh.orig $ mount -o remount -rw /usr $ sed -i 's/clsh/clsh --color=all/g' /usr/share/avr/bin/avr_db_backup.sh $ sed -i 's/clsh/clsh --color=all/g' /usr/share/avr/bin/avr_db_restore.sh $ mount -o remount -r /usr ** Before proceeding with the upgrade, double check that the only difference between the original files (/shared/avr_db_backup.sh.orig & /shared/avr_db_restore.sh.orig) and the modified versions is 'clsh --color=all'. If this is the only change, you may proceed and start with the upgrade process.
bugs.fix: Fixed the scripts that do the backup process.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing IP traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash with 'Assertion "l4hdr set" failed' panic message in /var/log/tmm* log.
bugs.conditions: Packet filter is enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: Disable the packet filter.
bugs.fix: TMM handles IP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Unable to specify if giaddr will be modified in DHCP relay chain
bugs.symptoms: ID746077 changed the dhcprelay behavior in order to comply with RFC 1542 Clarifications and Extensions for BOOTP. However, as the change also encompasses the DHCP-to-DHCP relay scope, the behavior cannot be configurable with a db key.
bugs.conditions: DHCP Relay deployments where the giaddr needs to be changed.
bugs.impact: You are unable to specify whether giaddr will be changed.
bugs.fix: A new sys db tmm.dhcp.relay.giaddr.overwrite is introduced The default is : sys db tmm.dhcp.relay.giaddr.overwrite { value "enable" } On versions with a fix to 746077, the sys db DOES NOT exist and BIG-IP will always retain the source IP On versions with both this fix and ID748333 fix, this fix overrides the fix for 746077. To change the default, set to "disable" to retain

bugs.title: Hertfordshire county missing from GTM Region list
bugs.symptoms: Hertfordshire county is missing from Regions in the United Kingdom Country/State list.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a GTM region record. -- Attempting to select Hertfordshire county for the United Kingdom.
bugs.impact: Cannot select Hertfordshire county from United Kingdom Country/State list.

bugs.title: Add 'virtual-server' argument to 'tmsh help sys connection' for version 14.x
bugs.symptoms: Virtual-server argument is not available in tmsh in versions prior to 14.x.
bugs.conditions: Running the command 'tmsh show sys connection'.
bugs.impact: Inability to filter for virtual server.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing Diameter traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing Diameter traffic.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with Diameter profile enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes Diameter traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Duplicate user-defined Signature Set based on Attack Type is created upon policy import
bugs.symptoms: A duplicate user-defined Signature Set is created upon policy import when the Set has a filter using Attack Type.
bugs.conditions: A policy using a user-defined Signature Set with a filter using Attack Type is exported.
bugs.impact: A duplicate user-defined Signature Set is created upon policy import.
bugs.workaround: The policy can be modified to use the original Set, and the duplicated set can then be deleted.
bugs.fix: Duplicate user-defined Signature Set based on Attack Type is no longer created upon policy import.

bugs.title: AVRD crash when configured to send data externally
bugs.symptoms: AVRD can crash repeatedly when configured to send telemetry data externally.
bugs.conditions: -- AVR is configured to send telemetry data to an external source (like connection with BIG-IQ). -- Large number of config objects in the system, such as virtual servers and pool members.
bugs.impact: AVRD process crashes, and telemetry data is not collected.
bugs.workaround: Split the configuration updates into smaller batches

bugs.title: Avrd crashes upon configuration change.
bugs.symptoms: AVRD crashes upon configuration change.
bugs.conditions: A change in virtual server configuration is made. No special conditions.
bugs.impact: AVRD crashes and there can be gaps in statistics data.

bugs.title: When 'Monitor Disabled Objects' is set to 'no', GSLB should cease monitoring disabled pool members.
bugs.symptoms: When the 'Monitor Disabled Objects' option is set to 'no', the monitors assigned to a disabled pool member continue monitoring the associated object.
bugs.conditions: When the 'Monitor Disabled Objects' option is set to 'no' and the configuration for a disabled pool member includes a monitor or the pool member inherits a monitor from the pool.
bugs.impact: Disabled pool members are always monitored regardless of the 'Monitor Disabled Objects' setting. This prevents using 'Monitor Disabled Objects' set to 'no' as a way to reduce monitoring load by only monitoring active objects.
bugs.workaround: Remove the monitor from the disabled pool member.
bugs.fix: GSLB no longer monitors disabled pool members when the pool member configuration includes a monitor and the 'Monitor Disabled Objects' option is set to 'no'.

bugs.title: Can't load keyword definition (ips-inspection-compliance.subscription) on upgrade from v14.1.0.5 to v15.0.0
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade fails from v14.1.0.5 to v15.0.0: Can't load keyword definition (ips-inspection-compliance.subscription) can't find parse node (ips::inspection::compl::subscription).
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from v14.1.0.5 to v15.0.0.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails.
bugs.fix: You can now upgrade from v14.1.0.5 to 15.0.1 or later.

bugs.title: DoS vector or signature stays hardware-accelerated even when traffic rate is lower than mitigation threshold
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect hw_offload status for DoS vector or signature in tmctl dos_stat after the attack has stopped.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system with DoS-accelerated vectors support (SPVA support).
bugs.impact: DoS vector/signature stays hardware-accelerated.
bugs.workaround: After attack, change the state for DoS vector/signature to detect-only. Then return vector state to mitigate.
bugs.fix: Hardware-acceleration status for vector/signature status is updated based on observed traffic.

bugs.title: DNS DoS profile vectors do not function correctly &start;
bugs.symptoms: Clients report that DNS TXT queries are not working. In /var/log/ltm, you see the following error: DOS attack start was detected for vector TXT query DOS.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when DNS profile DoS vectors are enabled. It can be encountered after upgrading.
bugs.impact: DNS DoS detection and mitigation is not functioning correctly.
bugs.fix: DNS DoS profile vectors are now detected correctly.

bugs.title: Big3d cannot log the full XML buffer data
bugs.symptoms: Big3d cannot log the full XML buffer data: -- notice big3d[12212]: 012b600d:5: Probe from ::ffff:11.11.1.21:45011: len 883/buffer = <vip>.
bugs.conditions: The gtm.debugprobelogging variable is enabled.
bugs.impact: Not able to debug big3d monitoring issues efficiently.

bugs.title: TMM crash after sessiondb ref_cnt overflow
bugs.symptoms: Log message that indicates this issue may happen: session_reply_multi: ERROR: unable to send session reply: ERR_BOUNDS [...] valid s_entry->ref_cnt
bugs.conditions: -- Specific MRF configuration where a single router is configured and shared by ~500 virtual servers -- also the traffic is routed by iRules similar to the following iRule: MR::message route peer "peer-[IP::local_addr]-[TCP::local_port]" that sends traffic to the same destination IP, 500 destination ports that could lead to a huge number of session entries owned by a single tmm. -- High rate of session lookups with a lot of entries returned. Note: This issue does not affect HTTP/2 MRF configurations.
