bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: - Create unique MRF routers and assign a different MRF router to each virtual server - Use different destination IP address Note: while this issue seems to be a generic sessionDB issue, above provided workaround is when it is only evident that MRF config seems to be causing the issue.

bugs.title: CSRF false positive
bugs.symptoms: A CSRF false-positive violation.
bugs.conditions: CSRF enforcing security policy. This is a very rare scenario, but it happens due to a specific parameter in the request, so the false-positive might repeat itself many times for the same configuration.
bugs.impact: False-positive Blocking / Violation
bugs.workaround: If this happens change the csrf parameter and restart the asm daemon: 1. Change the csrf parameter name internal parameter: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add csrf_token_name <string different than csrt> 2. Restart the asm daemon: restart asm

bugs.title: TMM may crash will processing connector traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions TMM may crash will processing connector traffic.
bugs.conditions: Virtual service with Connector profile enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now handles connector traffic as expected.

bugs.title: AFM ConfigSync Hardening
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, AFM ConfigSync does not apply design best practices.
bugs.conditions: ConfigSync enabled. AFM provisioned.
bugs.impact: ConfigSync does not apply design best practices.
bugs.fix: ConfigSync now applies design best practices.

bugs.title: Support PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) in BIG-IP APM OAuth Authorization Server.
bugs.symptoms: APM does not support PKCE in the OAuth Authorization Server scenario.
bugs.conditions: -- APM provisioned and an APM policy is configured to use OAuth as an Authorization Server.
bugs.impact: PKCE is not supported.
bugs.fix: APM OAuth Authorization Server mode now supports PKCE Authorization flow defined in RFC7636.

bugs.title: Resource Admin User unable to download UCS using Rest API.
bugs.symptoms: Resource Admin User cannot download UCS file using REST API. The system returns a message: Authorization failed
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP user with Resource Administrator role. -- Try to Download UCS file using REST API.
bugs.impact: Resource Administrator user cannot download UCS file using REST API.
bugs.workaround: The Resource Administrator user can use the GUI to download the file.

bugs.title: ONAP Licensing - Cipher negotiation fails
bugs.symptoms: Cipher negotiation fails between the BIG-IP and a third-party license server.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when BIG-IP is deployed in a custom ONAP environment that uses a third-party license server.
bugs.impact: TLS negotiation fails.
bugs.workaround: Change the order of ciphers. Enable only ECDHE ciphers.

bugs.title: Memory leak in icrd_child observed during REST usage
bugs.symptoms: When multiple users are issuing REST commands, memory may leak slowly in icrd_child.
bugs.conditions: -- THe icrd_child process is running. -- There are multiple users accessing device via REST.
bugs.impact: The memory leak is very progressive. Eventually, the icrd_child process runs out of memory.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak in icrd_child.

bugs.title: APM Portal Access resource URI might not be re-written for some scenarios involving APM per-request policy.
bugs.symptoms: APM Portal Access resource URI might not be re-written for some scenarios involving APM per-request policy.
bugs.conditions: Two connections from same client IP are executing simultaneously in APM per-request policy subroutine and trying to access APM portal access resource.
bugs.impact: The client session that first finishes the APM per-request policy subroutine will be redirected a re-written resource URI for portal access resource. All other sessions that simultaneously entered the subroutine will not be redirected to a re-written resource URI for portal access resource and instead will be redirected to the backend server URI.
bugs.fix: All client IP based sessions that are simultaneously executing inside the subroutine, will see a re-written URI when trying to access APM portal access resource.

bugs.title: The Native client and the HTML5 View Client version are now logged at info level.
bugs.symptoms: You can now see the VMware Native Client and HTML5 versions logged at info level.
bugs.conditions: -- Open VMware Native Client and connect to the virtual server. -- At info log level, the Native Client version is logged. -- Open browser and connect to virtual server (APM webtop). -- At info log level, the HTML client version is logged.
bugs.impact: You can now see the version of the client at info level. This is helpful if the APM end users use an older version or a vulnerable client.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: You can now see the VMware Native Client and HTML5 versions logged at info level. The version might not be printed if the end user uses an older version of client (earlier than or equal to v4.5).

bugs.title: HA Group score not computed correctly for an unmonitored pool when mcpd starts
bugs.symptoms: When mcpd starts up, unmonitored pools in an high availability (HA) group do not contribute to the HA group's score.
bugs.conditions: -- HA group configured with at least one pool. -- At least one of the pools assigned to the HA group is not using monitoring. -- mcpd is starting up (due to bigstart restart, or a reboot, etc.).
bugs.impact: Incorrect HA Group score.
bugs.workaround: Remove the unmonitored pools from the HA group and re-add them.

bugs.title: Documentation for HTTP::proxy is incorrect: 'HTTP::proxy dest' does not exist
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP GUI iRule definitions, when hovering over HTTP::proxy, the help text mentions 'HTTP::proxy dest', which is an invalid command.
bugs.conditions: The system displays incorrect information when the iRule help text is visible.
bugs.impact: The help text mentions 'HTTP::proxy dest', which is an invalid command option.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the invalid 'HTTP::proxy dest' command.
bugs.fix: The help text now shows 'HTTP::proxy', which is correct.

bugs.title: When HTTP/2 stream is reset by a client, BIG-IP may not respond properly
bugs.symptoms: When a client resets the HTTP/2 stream, the BIG-IP system may have several DATA frames ready to send. It drops these frames but does not account back those in a connection-send window. It can reduce this window to the value when no DATA frames are sent over this connection until the client updates the send window.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system has a virtual server. -- HTTP/2 profile is assigned to it.
bugs.impact: For any subsequent request after the send window loses enough size, DATA frames with payload are not sent to the client over the affected HTTP/2 connection.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP systems correctly handle dropping DATA frames accounting back their lengths in a connection-send window.

bugs.title: Errors running 'config' command
bugs.symptoms: Running the 'config' command reports errors: coapi_query failed at /usr/local/lib/perl5/F5/COAPI.pm line 215, <FH> line 3.
bugs.conditions: This might occur under either of the following conditions: -- The BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) instance has low memory. -- Running the command occurs before mcpd is in a running state.
bugs.impact: Failure to configure the management IP address.
bugs.workaround: Wait for the VE instance to start up and fully stabilize and have mcpd in the running state before running the config command.

bugs.title: Provide a full reset to factory defaults, as if the device was just out-of-the-box
bugs.symptoms: The image2disk(--format) command can be used to reset the BIG-IP to factory defaults; however, executing the image2disk directly against a /shared/images ISO (e.g. image2disk --nvlicenseok --nosaveconfig --setdefault --reboot --format=volumes /shared/images/BIGIP-11.5.0.iso), has resulted in an appliance or a blade requiring a USB installation.
bugs.conditions: Resizing logical volumes from their installed defaults, increasing the disk space for /usr) can prevent the installation of the software upon reboot.
bugs.impact: Sometimes running image2disk directly against a /shared/images ISO resulted in an appliance or a blade requiring a USB installation.
bugs.workaround: create a logical volume and copy the iso to the newly created logical volume and run the image2disk against the newly created logical volume. # lvcreate -L 2g -n install vg-db-hda # mkfs.ext3 /dev/vg-db-hda/install # mkdir /install # mount -t ext3 /dev/vg-db-hda/install /install # cp /shared/images/BIGIP-11.5.0.iso /install # image2disk --nvlicenseok --nosaveconfig --setdefault --reboot --format=volumes /install/BIGIP-11.5.0.iso

bugs.title: The SNMP max message size check is being incorrectly applied.
bugs.symptoms: If the SNMP server receives an SNMPv3 request with a small max message size then, it applies that check to all requests. This can cause SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c requests time out if they are too long or if their responses are too long, for example, large get bulk requests.
bugs.conditions: An SNMPv3 small max message size received while processing large SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c requests.
bugs.impact: Responses time out.
bugs.workaround: Do not send SNMPv3 requests to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: SNMPv3 requests no longer impact SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c requests.

bugs.title: PEM: ftp-data not classified or reported
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server is configured with an FTP profile, and also a PEM or classification profile, the traffic associated with the FTP data stream is not correctly classified or reported.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server is configured with an FTP profile. -- There is also PEM or classification profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic associated with ftp-data (i.e., file transfers using FTP) may not be classified or reported.
bugs.fix: Ftp-data is now correctly classified and reported. Note that the 'inherit-parent-profile' in the FTP profile must be enabled.

bugs.title: Pabnagd cores during device group settings changes
bugs.symptoms: Pabnagd crashes with core
bugs.conditions: This can occur intermittently when device group settings are changed.
bugs.impact: Due to pabnagd restart, up to 1 hour of policy builder learning progress is lost.
bugs.fix: Fixed a pabnagd crash.

bugs.title: SSL Handshakes may fail with valid SNI when SNI required is true but no Server Name is specified in the profile
bugs.symptoms: When the client attempts to connect, even when sending the proper SNI extension, the BIG-IP system resets the connection after the client hello.
bugs.conditions: -- SNI Required set to true. -- No Server Name configured in the client SSL profile.
bugs.impact: SSL connections with valid SNI are closed, and the client cannot connect. With generic alerts enabled, you will see 'SSL alert number 40'. This is because the system does not read the server names from the SAN extension within the certificate.
bugs.workaround: Specify a valid server name in the server name field of the client SSL profile.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources while processing iRules
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources while processing iRules.
bugs.conditions: HTTP VS enabled. iRule using HTTP_PROXY_REQUEST configured.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now consumes resources as expected.

bugs.title: ASM ConfigSync Hardening
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, ASM ConfigSync does not apply design best practices.
bugs.conditions: ConfigSync enabled. ASM provisioned.
bugs.impact: ASM ConfigSync does not apply design best practices.
bugs.fix: ConfigSync now applies design best practices.

bugs.title: Unencoded sym-unit-key causes guests to go 'INOPERATIVE' after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: VCMP guests go to 'INOPERATIVE' after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading the host from v12.1.4.1. -- Upgrading the host from v13.1.1.5 and all intervening versions up to, but not including, v13.1.3, to any higher version
bugs.impact: VCMP guests at state 'INOPERATIVE' and do not pass traffic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround. You must upgrade to a Fixed version, for example, 15.1.0.

bugs.title: GUI Login History hides informative message about max number of lines exceeded
bugs.symptoms: When there are more than 10000 lines in /var/log/secure* files, visiting System :: Logins :: [History|Summary] in the GUI shows 'No Entries' instead of the actual error message about the large number of lines.
bugs.conditions: If there are more than 10000 lines in /var/log/secure* files.
bugs.impact: GUI displays 'No Entries' instead of the actual error message.
bugs.workaround: -- Via the CLI by specifying the number of lines: tmsh show sys log security lines 15000 | less -- Delete the large amount of secure files from /var/log/.

bugs.title: Tmm core while using service chaining for SSLO
bugs.symptoms: Tmm cores.
bugs.conditions: Service chaining is used in SSLO; Service resets server side and keeps client side open.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmm no longer cores

bugs.title: TMM may core in a rare condition when tearing down a connection
bugs.symptoms: HTTP or HTTP2 virtual server receives a request and tries to create a connection to the server. If this connection establishment fails, the connection to the client is torn down. This core occurs when trying to abort the clientside connection.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server with HTTP profile is created. -- HTTP2 profile may or may not be present on the virtual server. -- An httprouter profile is present on the virtual server. -- Connection establishment with the server fails.
bugs.impact: TMM cores, failover condition occurs, and traffic processing can be interrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: A TMM core no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: IE11 with CSRF Object does not support property or method 'addEventListener'
bugs.symptoms: Application displays an "unable to connect" overlay. Browser console errors noted.
bugs.conditions: CSRF enabled. IE11
bugs.impact: Site is inaccessible for IE11 users when ASM CSRF protection is enabled on the site.

bugs.title: Management interface flaps after rebooting the device
bugs.symptoms: The Management interface flaps after rebooting the device, which may cause a momentary active-active condition in a high availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.conditions: This can occur after rebooting the active or standby device in an HA configuration if the final management port configuration completes late in the startup sequence. This can be due to network conditions for the network the management port is connected to. This problem has been observed only on hardware platforms.
bugs.impact: Devices go active-active for a few seconds and then resume normal operation.
bugs.workaround: You may be able to work around this by changing the management port speed to 100/Fixed Duplex. For more information on changing the interface, see K14107: Configuring the media speed and duplex settings for network interfaces (11.x - 13.x), available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14107.
bugs.fix: The startup sequence has been changed to confirm that management port configuration is complete before proceeding with HA processing.

bugs.title: Export, then import of pool outside of a default route domain may fail
bugs.symptoms: While importing a policy, you get an error: Syntax Error:(/shared/tmp/apmom/import/abc.conf at line ###) invalid IP address: "1.1.1.1%0%1"
bugs.conditions: -- Importing a previously exported policy -- The policy was from a partition with a non-zero route domain
bugs.impact: Importing the policy fails on syntax error.
bugs.workaround: You can manually edit the file and then attempt the import again. For example if a pool member was supposed to exist in route domain 1 with port 1812, the erroneous policy might look like this: ltm pool /@partition/@name-safenet-radius-pool { members { prod/1.1.1.1%1:radius { address 1.1.1.1%0%1 <===== priority-group 1 state up } } min-active-members 1 } It can be manually fixed by removing the erroneous %0 in the string. ltm pool /@partition/@name-safenet-radius-pool { members { prod/1.1.1.1%1:radius { address 1.1.1.1%1 priority-group 1 state up } } min-active-members 1 }

bugs.title: OWASP Compliance score is shown for parent and child policies that are not applicable.
bugs.symptoms: OWASP score for a parent policy or child policy is shown as 0. The more accurate value should be 'N/A' since these policies are not configurable for OWASP.
bugs.conditions: Create either child policy or parent policy. On Security ›› Application Security : Security Policies : Policies List page you will see in the OWASP Compliance score the value 0, and when going to OWASP page configuration (Security ›› Overview : OWASP Compliance) the user will see a note that the policy is not configurable for OWASP.
bugs.impact: When looking on the policies list, the user may get the impression that the parent or child policies can be configured to comply with OWASP.
bugs.workaround: Ignore OWASP Compliance score for child and parent policies.

bugs.title: Changing a virtual server's destination address from IPv6 to IPv4 can cause tmrouted to core
bugs.symptoms: When using dynamic routing, changing a virtual server's address from IPv6 to IPv4 can cause tmrouted to core.
bugs.conditions: -- Using dynamic routing. -- Changing a virtual server's destination address from IPv6 to IPv4. -- The virtual server's state changes.
bugs.impact: Tmrouted cores and restarts, which causes a temporary interruption of dynamic routing services.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to modify both the destination address and the netmask at the same time, e.g.: tmsh modify ltm virtual <virtual server name> destination <destination address> mask <netmask>
bugs.fix: Now preventing tmrouted from coring when a virtual server's address is changed from IPv6 to IPv4.

bugs.title: Reset stuck request queue errors
bugs.symptoms: Logs indicate that a device reset has taken place due to a stuck crypto queue operation. In /var/log/ltm: crit tmm[15650]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-crypto1 reset stuck request queue, retried 1/3 crit tmm[15650]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-crypto1 device soft resetting
bugs.conditions: This can occur with hardware SSL acceleration.
bugs.impact: The device can undergo a reset. It will recover, but there can be several seconds of lag during the recovery period.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware acceleration.

bugs.title: The nitrox_diag utility may not include register dump values for crypto accelerators
bugs.symptoms: Running the nitrox_diag may not include Nitrox3 register values when gathering device diagnostic information from guest.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the host is running 11.6.x, when the guest is running 14.1.0.1, and when the guest runs nitrox_diag. Running nitrox_diag on the host still works. Running nitrox_diag in older guests still works.
bugs.impact: Not all available debugging information will be included for diagnosis. This makes investigating hardware-related issues involving Nitrox3 more difficult.
bugs.workaround: You can still run nitrox_diag, but it will not include register dumps. In some cases this is okay: the other information gathered by nitrox_diag may be sufficient to resolve issues under investigation.

bugs.title: MRF: BiDirectional pesistence does not work in reverse direction if different transport protocols are used
bugs.symptoms: If a message is routed from one transport protocol (for example TCP) to another transport protocol (for example UDP), messages traveling from the destination to the source of the persistence entry are incorrectly delivered to the destination.
bugs.conditions: -- A message is routed from one transport protocol (for example TCP) to another transport protocol (for example UDP). -- Messages are traveling from the destination to the source of the persistence entry.
bugs.impact: Messages are forwarded to an incorrect endpoint.
bugs.fix: For all bi-directional persistence records the transport protocol of the connection is not used in the key used to store the record.

bugs.title: Out of shmem, increment amount in /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf
bugs.symptoms: System logs error: err sod[8444]: 01140003:3: Out of shmem, increment amount in /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf.
bugs.conditions: -- Large number of traffic groups. -- A number of devices in the device cluster. -- Heavy traffic resulting in numerous configsync or config save operations.
bugs.impact: Memory leak. Future changes to the high availability (HA) table may fail or be ignored. This could result in HA events not being tracked correctly.
bugs.fix: The HA table no longer leaks memory if an entry is reinitialized.

bugs.title: Tmsh load sys config from-terminal merge: error for config embedded sub profile can have only a single object of any part enabled
bugs.symptoms: When merging a network sub profile using 'tmsh load sys config from-terminal merge", tmsh reports a config error. 010715e4:3: Security log profile '/Common/logpartition01' can have only a single object of any part enabled. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is provisioned. -- Using TMSH terminal merge. -- Specifying an existing network log profile name that does not match the name in the configuration. Following is a detailed example: -- TMSH terminal merge works when you provide an existing name under network log profile. For example, if a BIG-IP has the following config in bigip.conf: "security log profile pf-log-01 { network { /Common/logpartition01 { <--- name contains /Common/ filter { log-acl-match-accept enabled } format { type user-defined user-defined "${date_time},${bigip_hostname},${management_ip_address},${src_ip},${src_port},${dest_ip},${dest_port},${translated_src_ip},${translated_dest_ip},${translated_src_port},${translated_dest_port},${date_time},,${protocol},${action}" } publisher lp-hsl-01 } } }" -- Terminal merge does not work, if you specify a different name under network when compared to name in the config. In this case, the name of the log profile under network stored for logpartition01 is '/Common/logpartition01'. When merging a config under network, the following config reports an error: "security log profile pf-log-01 { network { logpartition01 { <--- name is logpartition01, but not '/Common/logpartition01' filter { log-acl-match-accept enabled } format { type user-defined user-defined "${date_time},${bigip_hostname},${management_ip_address},${src_ip},${src_port},${dest_ip},${dest_port},${translated_src_ip},${translated_dest_ip},${translated_src_port},${translated_dest_port},${date_time},,${protocol},${action}" } publisher lp-hsl-01 } } }"
bugs.impact: New config is not applied. Error is posted.
bugs.workaround: While merging the config, specify the exact name of the profile that is already present in the config files. Note: The name of the sub-profile can be found in /config/bigip.conf file on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: REBOOT REQUIRED prompt appears after failover and clsh reboot
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances, when a reboot immediately follows a VIPRION blade failover, a REBOOT REQUIRED prompt will appear on one blade after the system starts up again.
bugs.conditions: This issue can be created by doing the following: - using a VIPRION system with at least 2 blades running - AAM is not provisioned - reset the primary blade - immediately following the blade reset, run 'clsh reboot' on a secondary blade.
bugs.impact: Following the clsh reboot, the REBOOT REQUIRED prompt appears on one blade: [root@vip4480-r44-s18:/S2-yellow-S::REBOOT REQUIRED:Standalone] config # Any blade with this prompt must be rebooted again.
bugs.workaround: None currently known.

bugs.title: Message Routing Framework Improvement: Added source port mode to transport config
bugs.symptoms: A source port mode is not configurable for the source port of a transport config in Message Routing Framework (MRF), but is configurable for the source port of a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Set the source port in a transport config for an MRF profile.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent configuration options for similar connection settings in MRF.
bugs.fix: Added a source port mode to the transport config configurations settings.
bugs.behavior: A source-port-mode attribute has been added to transport-config containing the same enum fields of the virtual server's source-port attribute: change, preserve, and preserve-strict

bugs.title: MRF SIP-ALG drops SIP 183 and 200 OK messages
bugs.symptoms: SIP 183 and 200 OK messages are dropped after an INVITE in MRF SIP-ALG when media info is present in the Session Description Protocol.
bugs.conditions: - MRF SIP-ALG default configuration - INVITE sent with media info in SDP - Media info contains an rtcp without an IP address
bugs.impact: SIP calls are unable to establish media connections.
bugs.workaround: Ensure all RTCP attributes in the SDP have IP addresses. Example: Change "a=rtcp:29974\r\n" to "a=rtcp:29974 IN IP4 10.10.10.10\r\n"
bugs.fix: Calls are able to establish media connections in MRF SIP-ALG when media info contains an RTCP with no IP information.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when RAM Cache is employed for HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: RAM Cache is an LTM feature to accelerate HTTP traffic. In some cases ramcache incorrectly optimizes storing data which results in memory errors.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has a virtual with webacceleration profile without a policy (RAM Cache is used).
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and causes failover event which may interrupt to process traffic.
bugs.workaround: Remove webacceleration profile.
bugs.fix: TMM works as expected when a RAM Cache-enabled webacceleration profile is configured on a virtual.

bugs.title: VMware View resources with SAML SSO are not working
bugs.symptoms: Connections to SAML-enabled VMware View resources fail with following error in /var/log/apm: err vdi[18581]: 019cffff:3: /pathname: {a7.C} Failed to handle View request: Can't find 'artifact' parameter.
bugs.conditions: VMware View resource is configured with SAML SSO method.
bugs.impact: Users cannot launch VMware View apps/desktops via SAML-enabled resource.
bugs.fix: Can now successfully use VMware View resources with SAML SSO.

bugs.title: Remote users are unable to authenticate via serial console.
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to login to the serial console with remote user credentials (e.g., RADIUS, LDAP, TACACS remote auth) fail with one of the following error messages: -- 'Cannot load user credentials for user' (v13.1.1.2) -- 'Session setup problem, abort.' (v14.1.0.1)
bugs.conditions: Configure system for remote authentication and attempt authentication via serial console.
bugs.impact: Remote authentication users are unable to login via serial console.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds: -- Remote authentication users can login using an SSH connection to the BIG-IP system's management IP address. -- Use the credentials of a local user account to login to the serial console.
bugs.fix: Fixed in BIG-IQ 8.3.0 Release

bugs.title: Global Staged Default Action is logged for ICMP traffic targeted to BIG-IP itself
bugs.symptoms: "Global Staged Default Action" message is logged into the firewall log for ICMP traffic targeted to Self-IP or Virtual Server destination address, even though this traffic can never be affected by Global Default Actions. The "Global Staged Default Action" counter is also incremented.
bugs.conditions: Logging is enabled for Global Staged Default Action by setting the sys db tm.fw.stagedglobaldefaultrule.log to value "enabled" (this sys db has value "disabled" by default). There are no special conditions for the "Global Staged Default Action" counter increment.
bugs.impact: Misleading messages are logged into the firewall log. The "Global Staged Default Action" counter is incorrectly incremented. The traffic itself is not affected and there are no other negative effects except the incorrect log message and counter update.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround regarding the "Global Staged Default Action" counter increment. For preventing the misleading log message disable logging of Global Staged Default Action by setting the sys db tm.fw.stagedglobaldefaultrule.log to value "disabled".
bugs.fix: The "Global Staged Default Action" message is not logged and corresponding counter is not incremented for ICMP traffic targeted to Self-IP or Virtual Server destination address.

bugs.title: Tmm crash SIGSEGV - virtual_address_update() in ../mcp/db_vip.c:1992
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores when creating a virtual server.
bugs.conditions: ISO build that includes the fix for ID 718790 or ID 783617.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Handle case where mcp virtual address tags come in different orders.

bugs.title: Upgrade fails when SSLv2 cipher is in the cipher list of an SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade, configuration load fails and the following error is present in /var/log/ltm log: 01070312:3: Invalid keyword 'sslv2' in ciphers list for profile /Common/serverssl-insecure-compatible Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system with SSLv2 as ciphers option in SSL profile running software v12.x/v13.x. -- Upgrading to a version that reports an error when using SSLv2, such as v14.x/v15.x.
bugs.impact: The config is not loaded, and upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: If you are encountering this after upgrading, run the following commands from the bash prompt: 1. Backup the configuration: #cp /config/bigip.conf /config/bigip_backup.conf 2. List the occurrences of 'sslv2' in the bigip.conf: #more bigip.conf | grep -i sslv2 3. Remove the SSLv2 references: #sed -i "s/\!SSLv2://g" /config/bigip.conf 4. Check to ensure there are no 'sslv2' references: #more bigip.conf | grep -i sslv2 5. Verify the configuration: #tmsh load sys config verify 6. Try loading the configuration: #tmsh load sys config
bugs.fix: SSLv2 validation is removed from the configuration and upgrade succeeds.

bugs.title: On a vCMP host VIPRION chassis, running vCMP guests may adopt an incorrect identity following simultaneous mcpd restarts on multiple blades
bugs.symptoms: On a VIPRION chassis provisioned as a vCMP host, mcpd on the secondary blades may restart and log errors similar to the following in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[43273]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (trunk_virtual_mbr) object ID (<guest_name> <PDE_interface>). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:trunk_virtual_mbr status:13)... failed validation with error 17237812 Post-mcpd starts on secondaries, guests that were involved in the above error might adopt each other's identity and answer at a different mgmt address than their own
bugs.conditions: All of the following conditions must be met: - The VIPRION system is provisioned as a vCMP host with one or more deployed guests. - An abrupt loss of inter-blade connectivity occurs without a graceful secondary disconnect. - A secondary blade subsequently reconnects to the primary.
bugs.impact: All services on the affected secondary blades restart. vCMP guests running on those blades are disrupted until MCPD recovers After MCPD recovers, some guests have corrupted identity and are now essentially unusable
bugs.workaround: No workaround, the guests that are corrupted once (when a different identity was taken) have to be deleted+recreated

bugs.title: Export of variable-assign is failing if 'error:' is part of expression
bugs.symptoms: Export of variable-assign with 'error:' string as part of expression is failing.
bugs.conditions: -- Exported Profile or Policy has variable assign -- Variable assign contains 'error:' (any capitalization) in string.
bugs.impact: Unable to export policy.
bugs.workaround: Use 'error :' (with space) instead of (error:)

bugs.title: AWS instance using xnet driver not receiving packets on an interface.
bugs.symptoms: Packets are being sent to the AWS instance but no packets are seen on interface.
bugs.conditions: -- AWS instance using xnet driver. -- Occurs when the instances are idle and then suddenly passes traffic again. -- Other, more specific conditions are unknown at this time.
bugs.impact: Loss of packets in the interface, in turn, causing data loss.
bugs.workaround: A temporary way to avoid the problem is to configure BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) to use an alternative network driver in place of the default 'xnet' driver. In releases 14.1.0 and later, this would be the 'sock' driver. Use The following command sequences from the BIG-IP instance's 'bash' prompt to configure the alternative driver. (Note the use of the 'greater-than' symbol.) # echo "device driver vendor_dev 1d0f:ec20 sock" > /config/tmm_init.tcl [check that the file's contents are correct] # cat /config/tmm_init.tcl [restart the BIG-IP's TMM processes] # bigstart restart tmm [make certain that the 'driver_in_use' is 'sock'] # tmctl -dblade -i tmm/device_probed

bugs.title: Failover between clustered DIAMETER devices can cause mirror connections to be disconnected
bugs.symptoms: When using DIAMETER with certain settings, a failover might cause mirror connections to get disconnected.
bugs.conditions: -- Two or more BIG-IP systems in a high availability (HA) configuration. -- Aggressive settings for the DIAMETER watchdog timeout and max failures.
bugs.impact: Loss of mirroring between BIG-IP systems.
bugs.fix: Mirror connections no longer disconnect during a failover.

bugs.title: Device trust UI hardening
bugs.symptoms: Improved device trust UI input sanitization
bugs.conditions: -ConfigSync in use
bugs.impact: Improved device trust UI input sanitization
bugs.fix: Improved device trust UI input sanitization

bugs.title: BIG-IP as Authorization server: OAuth Report GUI display expired token as active
bugs.symptoms: Expired tokens status is shown as ACTIVE in the GUI whereas it is shown AS EXPIRED in the CLI via tmsh list apm oauth token-details
bugs.conditions: -- Access tokens/Refresh tokens should be expired
bugs.impact: Misleading information regarding the token status
bugs.workaround: Uuse 'tmsh list apm oauth token-details' but this shows only the first 100 tokens
bugs.fix: Made GUI changes to match the tmsh functionality

bugs.title: Some VDI use cases can cause excessive resource consumption
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, APM may consume excessive resources while processing VDI traffic.
bugs.conditions: APM is used as VDI proxy.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource usage, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: APM now processes VDI traffic as expected.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when shutting down
bugs.symptoms: When the TMM is shutting down, a driver may be in a partially initialized state. When a buffered packet is flushed, the driver may crash.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition. -- The TMM is shutting down while traffic is being processed.
bugs.impact: A TMM restart may be delayed while the TMM writes a core file. Traffic disrupted while the tmm process restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM shuts down properly without crashing.

bugs.title: i10000 series appliances with HDVC part number 505-0030 missing name in show sys hardware and on LCD
bugs.symptoms: "tmsh show sys hardware" will not display a "Name" for the Platform on i100000 series appliances with part number 505-0030. The LCD will not display the system name.
bugs.conditions: i10000 series appliances with part number 505-0030 with HDVC (high voltage DC) power supplies.
bugs.impact: Display only. No functional impact. The LCD and "tmsh show sys hardware" will not display the product name of i10600 or i10800 as expected.
bugs.fix: Display correct F5 marketing name for i10000 series appliances with high voltage DC power supplies.

bugs.title: TMM might crash with traffic while deleting a pool member
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash during an operation of deleting a pool member.
bugs.conditions: -- Deleting a pool member from a pool -- The BIG-IP system is in the middle of processing a request. One potential scenarios is running a large iRule that inserts a delay in the processing of a request. This makes it more likely to satisfy the condition.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Patch or Delete commands take a long time to complete when modifying an ASM signature set.
bugs.symptoms: When modifying an ASM signature set that is not attached to any security policy using iControl REST Patch or Delete commands, the command takes a long time to complete.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Using REST API Patch or Delete command to modify an ASM signature set.
bugs.impact: Command takes longer (several seconds) to process on detached ASM signature sets than it takes to complete on attached signature sets.
bugs.fix: Changes to signatures and signatures sets now only recompile policies that are affected by the change.

bugs.title: The rate class feature does not honor the Burst Size setting.
bugs.symptoms: The Burst Size setting is intended to specify the maximum number of bytes that traffic is allowed to burst beyond the base rate configured for the rate class. When the burst rate is set to zero, no bursting is allowed. In this release, the Burst Size setting has no effect, even though neither the GUI nor tmsh prevent you from configuring.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when attempting to use the burst setting in the following BIG-IP software versions, and later: -- 13.0.0 through 13.1.1.5 -- 12.1.2 through 12.1.4.1 -- 11.5.5 through 11.5.9 -- 11.6.3.2 through 11.6.3.4
bugs.impact: Traffic does not burst beyond the base rate configured for the rate class. In the case of hierarchical rate classes, the BIG-IP may temporarily fail to process traffic.

bugs.title: HSL logging may work unreliably for Management-IP firewall rules
bugs.symptoms: HSL logging related to Management-IP firewall rules can periodically freeze and corresponding log messages can be lost.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions, this can happen intermittently on any setup.
bugs.impact: HSL log messages related to Management-IP firewall rules are missed.
bugs.fix: HSL logging related to Management-IP firewall rules no longer halts intermittently, and all corresponding log messages are present in the log.

bugs.title: When engineID is reconfigured, snmp and alert daemons must be restarted
bugs.symptoms: The engineID, engineBoots, engineTime values in SNMPv3 traps are shared by both the SNMP and the Alert daemons and are included in traps raised by both daemons. When the engineID is reconfigured then both daemons must be restarted in order to resynchronize the new values.
bugs.conditions: Traps issued by the SNMP and Alert daemons may not have engine values that are in sync when the EngineID is first reconfigured. This can happen both with a configuration change and an upgrade.
bugs.impact: This may confuse the SNMP client receiving the trap.
bugs.workaround: Restart the snmp daemon and then the alert daemon when the engine ID is reconfigured for the first time and the first time after a software upgrade tmsh restart sys service snmpd alertd

bugs.title: VE rate limit should not count packet that does not have a matched vlan or matched MAC address
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Edition (VE) Rate limit counts packets that are not intended for BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: -- Rate-limited license in BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) -- Promiscuous mode is enabled
bugs.impact: If you do not have an unlimited license for a Virtual Edition device, you cannot use VLAN tags or MAC Masquerading without a greatly increased risk of running out of licensed bandwidth. Even if you are not using any service, BIG-IP counts all traffic seen on the interface against the license. Due to VMWare's switch design you have to expose the device to all of the traffic to use those two features.

bugs.title: HTTP parsing restrictions
bugs.symptoms: When parsing HTTP the following non-compliant behavior was accepted: White-space before a colon in a header name. Bad characters in HTTP/2 URIs
bugs.conditions: HTTP profile enabled.
bugs.impact: Non-compliant HTTP traffic is accepted and forwarded to pool members.
bugs.fix: HTTP parsing was more lenient than that required by the RFC. HTTP parsing now is more strict. In addition, version handling of non-HTTP protocols like RTSP/2.0 is now somewhat altered.

bugs.title: Connection in FIN_WAIT_2 state may fail to be removed
bugs.symptoms: If a connection that has a fully closed client-side, but a server-side still in FIN_WAIT_2, receives a SYN matching the same connflow, the idle time is reset. This can result in the fin-wait-2-timeout never being reached. The SYN will be responded to with a RST - 'TCP Closed'
bugs.conditions: - Client side connection has been fully closed. This may occur if a client SSL profile is in use and an 'Encrypted Alert' has been received. - Server side has sent a FIN which has been ACK'd, but no FIN has been received from the server. - SYN received matching the existing connflow before the FIN-WAIT-2-timeout has been reached (300 default).
bugs.impact: Connection may fail to be removed in a timely manner. New connection attempts are RST with 'TCP Closed'
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following: -- Ensure servers are sending FIN's so as not to leave the connection in a FIN_WAIT_2 state. -- Mitigate the issue by lowering the FIN-WAIT-2-timeout to a smaller value, e.g., FIN-WAIT-2-timeout 10.

bugs.title: 'translate-address disabled' setting for LTM virtual server does not have any effect with iRules for NAT64 traffic
bugs.symptoms: IPv4 Packets are forwarded to server-side with destination address changed to LTM pool member address even when 'translate-address disabled' is configured on a NAT64 virtual server.
bugs.conditions: -- Create iRules for LTM pool selection. -- Configure the NAT64 virtual server with 'translate-address disabled'. -- Send IPv6 client request accessing the NAT64 virtual server.
bugs.impact: Server-side IPv4 packets are forwarded with destination address modified. The server-side packets do not reach the intended destination, resulting in connection failures.
bugs.workaround: Use normal LTM pool selection instead of iRules-based, LTM pool selection.

bugs.title: Add option to insert security headers for fictive URL responses
bugs.symptoms: When ASM blocks any of the HTTP requests, then the HTTP security headers are missed in ASM internal response. (e.g. blocking page, captcha, and all other fictive url's of ASM, including BOT Defense, and L7DOS).
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned and configured with a policy. - Traffic arrives which violates the ASM policy
bugs.impact: ASM internal responses are anomalous for penetration testing and vulnerability assessment tools.
bugs.workaround: Create iRules to insert needed security headers into ASM blocked/internal responses

bugs.title: mcpd may core when resetting a DSC connection
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances mcpd may core when resetting its DSC connection.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions are not known for this to occur. The BIG-IP system must be in a Device Service Cluster, and must have configuration sync enabled. It might be related to when an Administrative BIG-IP user makes manual changes to the device trust group that would cause the trust to be broken (and optionally, re-established).
bugs.impact: mcpd cores and restarts. This results in a failover to the next active peer.
bugs.fix: The system now prevents mcpd from coring when it resets it DSC connection.

bugs.title: P2P failure while connecting with Cisco router when firewall is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: When P2P is configured and a firewall policy is set, OSPF status is set to 'exstart' when AFM is provisioned and tm.fw.defaultaction is set to 'drop'/'reject'.
bugs.conditions: P2P is configured and a firewall policy is set.
bugs.impact: OSPFv3 does not work.
bugs.workaround: Set tm.fw.defaultaction to allow: tmsh modify sys db tm.fw.defaultaction value allow

bugs.title: MCPD: memory leak on standby BIG-IP device
bugs.symptoms: MCPD memory consumption may increase on standby BIG-IP device if APM configuration is updated. Some of the allocated memory is not freed after configuration update.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP high availability (HA) pair is installed and configured -- APM is provisioned -- Access Policy is configured and updated periodically
bugs.impact: MCPD may take a lot of memory on the standby device. Normal functionality of standby device may be stopped; reboot of the device is required.
bugs.fix: MCPD on standby BIG-IP device does not take more memory than the same daemon on active BIG-IP device.

bugs.title: Queries with TSIG signatures not matching BIG-IP result in malformed BADSIG answer
bugs.symptoms: In certain circumstances, it is possible that queries to the BIG-IP system with a TSIG key name, which matches a TSIG key on the BIG-IP system, but carries a different signature, the the BIG-IP system responds with a malformed BADSIG answer
bugs.conditions: -- Queries to the BIG-IP system are made with a TSIG key name matching a TSIG key on the BIG-IP system, -- The signature on the TSIG key differs.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system answers with a malformed BADSIG warning; this is an example from the dig command: ;; Warning: Message parser reports malformed message packet. ;; Couldn't verify signature: tsig indicates error.
bugs.fix: Delete TSIG info after the TSIG error is detected and processed.

bugs.title: Monpd process consumes considerable amount of RAM on systems with many virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Monpd process consumes a considerable amount of RAM (several gigabytes). The RAM usage grows constantly within the first 24 hours. This occurs because of the collection of ADM (BADOS) real-time statistics in monpd memory for last 24 hours per virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Many virtual servers are defined in the system. The memory consumption depends on the number of virtual servers.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory consumption reduces available RAM for other system daemons.
bugs.fix: AVR now reports ADM (BADOS) real-time statistics only for virtual servers with BADOS profiles enabled.

bugs.title: False positive attack detection on DoS profile vectors for unbalanced traffic
bugs.symptoms: DoS attack is detected on a profile vector when attack Packets Per Second (PPS) is lower than the threshold.
bugs.conditions: Unbalanced traffic between tmms for DoS profile vector.
bugs.impact: False positive attack detection.

bugs.title: P2P failure on BIG-IP system while connecting with Cisco router
bugs.symptoms: P2P connection is stuck when AFM basic firewall is enabled.
bugs.conditions: The db variable tm.fw.defaultaction is set to drop/reject. (The default is 'accept'.)
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system cannot establish a connection with Cisco in P2P configurations.
bugs.workaround: Set the value of tm.fw.defaultaction to 'allow': tmsh modify sys db tm.fw.defaultaction value allow

bugs.title: Autoconf continually changes a virtual IP object when virtual IP/port on LTM is not in sync
bugs.symptoms: The virtual server for an LTM redundant peer is continually updated with its IP/Port changing back and forth between two values, leading to perpetual GTM configuration syncs.
bugs.conditions: The destination IP:port of the virtual server on the LTM is not in sync between the LTM devices in the device-group.
bugs.impact: The virtual server is flapping status between "blue" and 'green', and its destination IP:port is changing between a correct value and an incorrect one. Traffic will be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Perform a configsync on the LTM device-group that owns the virtual server.

bugs.title: LSN_PB_UPDATE logs are not generated when subscriber info changes
bugs.symptoms: LSN_PB_UPDATE logs are not generated when subscriber info changes.
bugs.conditions: Logging profile indicates that LSN_PB_UPDATE events should be logged.
bugs.impact: The expected logs are not generated.

bugs.title: TMM Crashes upon failure in Bot Defense Client-Side code
bugs.symptoms: On some cases, when Bot Defense Client-Side code is running on the browser, it causes TMM to crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense is enabled with any JS browser verification (before or after access). -- Surfing using a browser to an html page.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Adding sanity test so TMM will not crash.

bugs.title: BD crash under certain circumstances
bugs.symptoms: BD crashes with an error message: 01230140:3: RST sent from 10.0.1.101:83 to 10.0.1.1:464, [0x2911514:1148] Internal error (ASM requested abort (open error)).
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption / failover.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a bd crash scenario.

bugs.title: The cron daemon not running after upgrade from pre-v14.1.0 versions to 15.0.x
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to v15.0.x, the system cron daemon is not running, which causes periodic system operations not to run. This includes, but is not limited to: -- SSL/TLS ephemeral key generation. -- Log rotation. -- SSL certificate.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade BIG-IP system from pre-v14.1.0 to 15.0.x.
bugs.impact: The crond daemon is down, making any process dependent on crond to not work on the system: -- The SSL connection mirroring does not work as expected. -- Script scheduling does not work.
bugs.workaround: Enable and start crond: 1. systemctl enable crond 2. systemctl start crond
bugs.fix: The system now ensures that the cron daemon (crond) is running consistently after upgrades.

bugs.title: MCPD crashes when assigning an iRule that uses a proc
bugs.symptoms: MCPD crashes when assigning an iRule to a Virtual Server or loading a config with an iRule assigned.
bugs.conditions: The iRule must uses a proc that contains three statements associated with different feature flags.
bugs.impact: MCPD will crash, unable to use a desired iRule.
bugs.fix: iRules using proc can be assigned to a Virtual Server without crashing MCPD.

bugs.title: Multpile process consumer more memory with multiple components provisioned and causing RAM usage grow during traffic testing.
bugs.symptoms: Different process (in this case avrd) on the BIG-IP system are killed due to OOM when most of components are provisioned and traffic testing encompasses more than 100 users. This occurs because the amount of memory is not sufficient for the provisioning of APM plus SWG, which requires 16 GB alone.
bugs.conditions: -- Many virtual servers configured. -- Large number of client end users sending a lage amount of traffic. -- Less than 16 GB, which is not sufficient with many modules provisioned.
bugs.impact: Excessive memory consumption reduces available RAM for other system daemons.

bugs.title: SSLO connection hang when bypass is enabled
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake may hang due to a race condition.
bugs.conditions: SSL dynamic bypass is enabled, but verified-handshake is disabled, or is using VHF version of profiles.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake hangs.
bugs.workaround: When dynamic bypass is enabled, be sure to enable verified-handshake or use the VHT version of SSL profiles.

bugs.title: MRF SIP ALG with SNAT incorrectly detects ingress queue full
bugs.symptoms: When SIP ALG processes a non-registered subscriber SIP outbound call, the ingress queue counter may underflow. This is interpreted as ingress queue full and the rest of message will be dropped.
bugs.conditions: SIP ALG processes non registered subscriber SIP outbound calls (nonregister-subscriber-callout option is enabled in SIP session profile).
bugs.impact: SIP ALG incorrectly detects the ingress queue is full and stops processing the rest of SIP ALG traffic.
bugs.fix: When SIP ALG processes non registered subscriber SIP call, the ingress queue counter is handled correctly.

bugs.title: The HTTP Explicit proxy does not work correctly with IPv6 clients connecting to IPv4 destinations over CONNECT
bugs.symptoms: A typical configuration of the HTTP Explicit Proxy includes four virtual servers: -- Two virtual servers for the Explicit Proxy, one IPv4, one IPv6. -- Two general-purpose virtual servers: one IPv4, one IPv6. The general-purpose virtual servers allow handling of CONNECT tunneling over the HTTP-tunnel interface. Unfortunately, if an IPv6 client tries to CONNECT to an IPv4 destination, it fails, returning a 503 status error. This is due to the IPv6 general-purpose virtual server not being found when performing the destination lookup.
bugs.conditions: -- The HTTP explicit proxy is used on an IPv6 address. -- 'default-connect-handling deny' is configured on the explicit proxy HTTP profile. -- IPv4 and IPv6 general-purpose virtual servers exist on the HTTP-tunnel interface. -- The client connects, and uses CONNECT to proxy to an IPv4 address.
bugs.impact: The client will not be able to CONNECT through the explicit proxy to an IPv4 address.
bugs.fix: Mismatched IPv6 to IPv4 scenarios are supported with the HTTP Explicit Proxy.

bugs.title: Proxy ARP failure
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, and when the BIG-IP system does not have a directly connected route to the request sender, proxy ARP may fail, leading to dropped ARP replies.
bugs.conditions: -- Running v12.1.4.1 or 12.1.3.7 with engineering hotfix 0.89.2. -- ARP requests and replies are processed by different TMMs. -- A directly connected route to the request sender is not available.
bugs.impact: ARP replies are dropped, leading to connection failures.
bugs.workaround: Create a self IP in the same subnet as the ARP request senders. This creates the necessary directly connected route.

bugs.title: PB core dump while processing many entities
bugs.symptoms: PB core dump.
bugs.conditions: This may happen when the system is strained and PB is processing large policies (updating many entities may happen during periodic processing, response analysis). This is a very rarely occurring scenario.
bugs.impact: PB core dump and restart.
bugs.fix: PB core dump no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Network DoS reporting events as 'not dropped' while in fact, events are dropped
bugs.symptoms: Logs/Tmctl shows packet dropped whereas AVR shows Action as 'Allowed' and not 'Dropped'.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM configured. -- AFM passes the message to AVR for reporting.
bugs.impact: The operation does not update the drop flag. It appears from AVR Reporting that packets are allowed, but actually they are dropped
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: AVR Reporting now shows proper value.

bugs.title: No virtual server name in Hardware Syncookie activation logs.
bugs.symptoms: Missing virtual server name in Hardware Syncookie activation logs. ltm/logs contains error messages: notice tmm2[1150]: 01010240:5: Syncookie HW mode activated, server = 0.0.0.0:0, HSB modId = 2.
bugs.conditions: -- More than one virtual server with same Destination IP e.g., 'x.x.x.x'. -- Port 'y' configured. -- Hardware Syncookie activated.
bugs.impact: Difficult to determine which virtual server actually got the Syncookie activated.

bugs.title: Under heavy load, bcm56xxd can be killed by the watchdog
bugs.symptoms: bcm56xxd crashes, and the device fails over on heartbeat error: warning sod[7244]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat bcm56xxd fails action is restart. notice sod[7244]: 010c006c:5: proc stat: [0] pid:12482 comm:(bcm56xxd) state:S utime:16612520 stime:879057 cutime:11 cstime:21 starttime:1601425044 vsize:2189299712 rss:527927 wchan:18446744073709551615 blkio_ticks:0 [-1] pid:12482 comm:(bcm56xxd) state:S
bugs.conditions: -- HA configured. -- Programming the DAG while it is under heavy load (i.e., a large number of objects that have to be programmed into the switches).
bugs.impact: The bcm56xxd daemon may restart and produce a core file. It then continues trying to program the DAG. This causes a system to go offline and stop processing traffic.
bugs.fix: The bcm56xxd daemon no longer crashes while the DAG is being programmed.

bugs.title: Using Generic Message router to convert a SIP message from TCP to UDP fails to fire SERVER_CONNECTED iRule event.
bugs.symptoms: When using the Generic Message router to convert SIP messages from TCP to UDP, BIG-IP fails to raise the SERVER_CONNECTED iRule event.
bugs.conditions: Converting the transport of SIP messages with the Generic Message router.
bugs.impact: Any code that waits for the SERVER_CONNECTED event will not run.
bugs.fix: SERVER_CONNECTED event is raised.

bugs.title: GUI SIP monitor fails to create/update when status code is empty
bugs.symptoms: GUI reports 'General database error.', and SIP monitor is not created/updated.
bugs.conditions: -- Select a status code list value for additional status codes option. -- Do not add any status codes or remove all existing status codes.
bugs.impact: GUI reports an error. Unable to create/update SIP monitor using GUI.
bugs.workaround: Change the value of Additional status code options to 'None' if you do not want to add any status codes.
bugs.fix: The system now presents an Alert Message when trying to create or update a SIP monitor without a Status Code when the Status Code List is selected.

bugs.title: Multicast route entries are not populating to tmm after failover
bugs.symptoms: Multicast route entries are not populating in tmm after failover. ZebOS has the multicast entries, but tmm does not.
bugs.conditions: -- High Availability (HA) configured, with multicast traffic. -- A failover occurs.
bugs.impact: Multicast traffic does not pass through properly
bugs.workaround: Clear the multicast entries in ZebOS manually: > clear ip mroute * > clear ip igmp group

bugs.title: Pool member silently changed to user-disabled from monitor-disabled
bugs.symptoms: When a node (Disabled by Monitor) is updated via the member screen (no change to configuration required), the status changes from: 'Available (Disabled) pool members is available, monitor disabled'. To: 'Available (Disabled), pool member is available, user disabled'.
bugs.conditions: -- A node disabled by Monitor. -- Go to GUI LTM pool member and navigate into the monitor disabled member, then update without any configuration change.
bugs.impact: Pool member goes to 'user-disabled'.
bugs.workaround: To recover, re-enable the pool member.

bugs.title: PPTP profile option not available when creating or modifying virtual servers in GUI
bugs.symptoms: There is no option to configure a PPTP profile for a virtual server in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Creating or modifying a virtual server in the GUI.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure the PPTP profile for a virtual server using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to add a PPTP profile to the virtual server.

bugs.title: PostgreSQL monitor fails on second ping with count != 1
bugs.symptoms: When using one of the DB monitors (Oracle, MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL) to monitor the health of a server, the pool member may initially be marked UP, but then will be marked DOWN on the next and all subsequent pings. When this occurs, an error message similar to the following appears in the monitor-instance log under /var/log/monitors: Database down, see /var/log/DBDaemon.log for details. Exception in thread "DBPinger-##" java.lang.AbstractMethodError: org.postgresql.jdbc3.Jdbc3Connection.isValid(I)Z at com.f5.eav.DB_Pinger.db_Connect(DBDaemon.java:1474) at com.f5.eav.DB_Pinger.db_Ping(DBDaemon.java:1428) at com.f5.eav.MonitorWorker.run(DBDaemon.java:772) at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:748)
bugs.conditions: This may occur if all of the following conditions are true: 1. You are using a DB monitor (Oracle, MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL) configured with a 'count' value of either '0' or a value of '2' or higher. 2. You are using a version of BIG-IP (including an Engineering Hotfix) which contains the fix for ID 775901.
bugs.impact: Unable to monitor the health of postgresql server pool members accurately.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, configure a 'count' value of '1' in the postgresql monitor configuration.
bugs.fix: The DB monitor reports the health of a DB server pool member accurately in conjunction with the fix for ID 775901.

bugs.title: PEM drops new subscriber creation if historical aggregate creation count reaches the max limit
bugs.symptoms: PEM subscriber create fails, usually seen across multiple high availability (HA) failover events
bugs.conditions: When the aggregate subscriber create reaches the maximum subscriber limit per tmm which is configured using sys db, sys db statemirror.mirrorsessions
bugs.impact: Unable to bringup any more subscribers
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm when the limits are reached
bugs.fix: PEM subscriber creation no longer fails after multiple failover events.

bugs.title: TMUI dashboard hardening
bugs.symptoms: The TMUI dashboard does not comply with current best practices.
bugs.conditions: TMUI dashboard accessed by authenticated administrative user.
bugs.impact: The TMUI dashboard does not comply with current best practices.
bugs.fix: The TMUI dashboard now complies with current best practices.

bugs.title: TMM Crash with inbound traffic during high availability (HA) failover
bugs.symptoms: New standby device's tmm crashes and generates a core after high availability (HA) failover.
bugs.conditions: 1. Enable inbound mode Endpoint Independent Filtering (EIF) in the source translation object. 2. Outbound traffic hits the source translation creating inbound entries. 3. Inbound traffic matches the inbound entry, and this connection stays alive. 4. high availability (HA) failover occurs. 5. Inbound connection closes, and the connection free comes from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: New standby device's tmm may crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes with inbound traffic during high availability (HA) failover.

bugs.title: On a system with no VLANs, you can create virtual servers or SNATs that have identical address/port combinations
bugs.symptoms: If you have a system with no VLANs configured, and you attempt to create virtual servers or SNATs that have the same address/port combinations, you will be able to do so without validation errors.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system with no VLANs configured. -- Creating virtual servers or SNATs that have identical address/port combinations.
bugs.impact: An invalid configuration is allowed.
bugs.fix: The system now prevents this invalid configuration.

bugs.title: GUI update of Child FastL4 profile overwrites CLI-only customized settings (options that are not available in GUI)
bugs.symptoms: Child FastL4 profile is being reset after clicking Update from GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Create child SSL FastL4, profile inheriting settings from a parent FastL4 profile. -- From the command line, change any of the CLI-only visible settings in the child FastL4 profile (e.g., pva-acceleration, explicit-flow-migration, etc.), and save the changes. -- In the GUI, click the Update button in the child FastL4 profile without making any change.
bugs.impact: The operation overwrites the CLI changes made in the child profile, and inherits those values from the parent settings instead.

bugs.title: RAID status is shown <undefined> after upgrade from 12.1.3.5 to 13.1.1.5
bugs.symptoms: On RAID supported BIG-IP platforms, upgrade from BIG-IP v12.1.3.5 to BIG-IP v13.1.1.5, RAID array member state is shown as 'undefined' in below commands, though actual RAID status is 'up'. - array - tmsh show sys raid
bugs.conditions: On RAID supported platforms, clean install of BIG-IP 12.1.x version followed by upgrade to BIG-IP 13.1.x version.
bugs.impact: RAID information is reported wrongly.
bugs.fix: RAID information is retrieved and parsed according to the new mdadm supported in BIG-IP 13.1.x version.

bugs.title: BIG-IP closes connection when an unsized response is served to a HEAD request
bugs.symptoms: When HTTP response has neither Content-Length nor Transfer-Encoding and has a body, BIG-IP closes a connection to designate end of the response body. HTTP protocol allows to send HEAD request instead of GET request to obtain a response headers only (without). BIG-IP erroneously closes a connection when a response to HEAD request lacks both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP has a virtual server configured to use an HTTP profile. The server response does not include the Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding headers in response to a HEAD request, and both client and server sides expects the communication to continue over the same connection.
bugs.impact: Connection closes and a client may not repeat the corresponding GET request on another connection.
bugs.fix: Connection keeps opened when an unsized response provided to a HEAD request.

bugs.title: MRF outbound messages are dropped in per-peer mode
bugs.symptoms: When a Message Routing profile is configured with a peer consisting of an outbound virtual server, transport config, no pool, and per-peer mode, messages may be dropped when the outgoing connection is persisted to a different tmm than the message was received on.
bugs.conditions: -- Message Routing Profile. -- A peer configured for outbound traffic with a virtual server and transport config in per-peer mode, no pool. -- Persistence is enabled. -- Multiple outbound messages with the same destination address.
bugs.impact: Outbound traffic with the same destination address may be dropped at random.
bugs.workaround: Change the peer connection mode to 'Per TMM'.
bugs.fix: Multiple outbound messages to the same destination address are no longer randomly dropped.

bugs.title: Named.config entry getting overwriting on SSL Orchestrator deployment
bugs.symptoms: When topology or general settings are re-deployed, named.config is modified, and entries which do not belong to SSL Orchestrator are overwritten.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when topology or system settings are re-deployed.
bugs.impact: Content of named.conf file is lost/overwritten.
bugs.workaround: Modify named.conf manually or using zoneRunner (DNS :: Zones : ZoneRunner : named Configuration) after SSL orchestrator deployment.

bugs.title: Azure walinuxagent has been updated to v2.2.42.
bugs.symptoms: Some onboarding features are not available in the current version of walinuxagent.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use a feature that is not available in the current version of the Azure walinuxagent that is included in the BIG-IP release.
bugs.impact: Cannot use new features in the Azure walinuxagent until the Azure walinuxagent is updated.
bugs.fix: The Azure walinuxagent has been updated to v2.2.42.

bugs.title: TMM leaks memory when explicit SWG is configured with Kerberos authentication
bugs.symptoms: Memory usage of filter keeps increasing over time and becomes one of major consumers of the TMM memory.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens if the following conditions are met: 1. Access profile type is SWG-explicit. 2. Access policy contains HTTP 407 Response policy item with HTTP Auth Level being Negotiate. 3. Kerberos is used to authenticate a user.
bugs.impact: TMM sweeper enters aggressive mode and reaps connections.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may stop responding to ARP requests after TMM restarts or the system reboots
bugs.symptoms: After a reboot or TMM restart, BIG-IP may stop responding to ARP requests for configured virtual-servers.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy with external datagroup configured on virtual server.
bugs.impact: Unable to establish connections to the affected virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Delete and re-add the affected virtual-server.

bugs.title: Information Elements with zero-length value are rejected by the GTP parser
bugs.symptoms: When processing a GTP message containing zero-length IEs (which are allowed by the 3GPP Technical Specification), the message might get rejected.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with GTP profile enabled processing GTP traffic.
bugs.impact: Well-formed GTP messages might get rejected.
bugs.workaround: Avoid sending GTP messages containing zero-length IEs.
bugs.fix: Zero-length IEs are now processed correctly.

bugs.title: Add rule to the disabled pem policy is not allowed
bugs.symptoms: Adding rule to PEM policy is not allowed
bugs.conditions: A PEM policy is disabled
bugs.impact: You are unable to add rules to a PEM policy if it is disabled.
bugs.fix: Allow adding rules to disabled PEM policy

bugs.title: Fix martian addresses as per RFC6890
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP LTM v14.1.0 does not update the route for 128.0.0.0/1 network via BGP UPDATE message
bugs.conditions: Send BGP UPDATE message for 128.0.0.0/1 network to the BIG-IP
bugs.impact: BIG-IP does not update the route
bugs.workaround: Incorporate martian address compliance as per RFC6890
bugs.fix: BGP routing UPDATES works with 128.0.0.0/1 network and similar ones as allowed by RFC6890

bugs.title: IPsec passthrough scenario may not forward ICMP unreachable messages from the server-side
bugs.symptoms: ICMP protocol 50 unreachable messages are not forwarded from the server-side to the client-side when a SNAT Virtual Server handles ESP flows that are not encapsulated in UDP port 4500 (RFC 3948). Other ICMP messages related to the server-side ESP flow may be similarly affected.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system is forwarding ESP (protocol 50) packets. -- Virtual Server is configured with a SNAT pool or automap. -- The server-side IPsec peer sends ICMP protocol errors in response to the ESP packets.
bugs.impact: ICMP packets arriving on the server-side are not forwarded to the client-side.
bugs.workaround: Option 1: -- Enable NAT Detection (RFC 3947) on the IPsec peers. NOTE: NAT Detection (RFC 3947) is the correct way to implement IPsec peers when network address translation occurs between the two IPsec peers. Option 2: -- Remove NAT from the Virtual Server. -- Set the following sys db values: # tmsh modify sys db ipsec.lookupip value "enable" # tmsh modify sys db ipsec.lookupspi value "disable" NOTE: The sys db settings in option 2 do not resolve the ICMP issue if NAT is configured on the Virtual Server.
bugs.fix: ICMP protocol 50 unreachable messages from the server-side are forwarded to the client-side.

bugs.title: Kernel Log Messages Logged Twice
bugs.symptoms: You see duplicate log messages in /var/log/kern.log
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered when viewing /var/log/kern.log right after startup in BIG-IP versions dating back to 14.1.0
bugs.impact: Viewing ('cat'ing) kern.log results in duplicated log messages in the buffer.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with duplicated log messages in /var/log/kern.log.

bugs.title: Session and authentication cookies should use larger character set
bugs.symptoms: The session and authentication cookies are created using a limited character set.
bugs.conditions: Creating session and authentication cookies.
bugs.impact: Cookies are created with a less broad character set than they could be.
bugs.fix: JSESSIONIDs and AuthCookies are created using a wider character set.
bugs.behavior: This release changes the format of the BIGIPAuthCookie and JSESSIONID cookies to use a larger alphabet during encoding (case sensitive alphanumeric).

bugs.title: L7 Policies may execute CONTAINS operands incorrectly.
bugs.symptoms: L7 Policies involving CONTAINS operands may execute incorrectly in some cases. The policy compiler may incorrectly combine some internal states, 'forgetting' degrees of partial evaluation of a CONTAINS operation.
bugs.conditions: Multiple CONTAINS conditions are used on the same virtual server.
bugs.impact: The wrong policy actions may be triggered.
bugs.workaround: It may be possible to reorder the rules in a policy to restore correct operation. However, the more complex the policy, the less likely this is.
bugs.fix: L7 Policy CONTAINS operations are compiled correctly. Policies with CONTAINS operations no longer trigger the wrong rule actions.

bugs.title: Extremely long nameserver name causes GUI Error
bugs.symptoms: Extremely long nameserver and tsig key name gives an error in the GUI while viewing: -- Bad Request. Your browser sent a request that this server could not understand. -- Request-URI Too Long. The requested URL's length exceeds the capacity limit for this server.
bugs.conditions: When nameserver and tsig key name length exceeds 3300 characters.
bugs.impact: The GUI reports an error when you try to view them. Youa re unable to view nameserver and tsig keys having extremely long names.
bugs.workaround: Create nameserver and tsig keys with shorter names, preferably fewer than 255 characters.
bugs.fix: Nameserver and tsig key names are now validated, so this error no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Per-request Policy customization is used for 'URL blocked' page
bugs.symptoms: When per-request Access Policy includes Reject Ending agent, it may show 'URL blocked' page to client. It is expected that this page uses customization settings from corresponding per-request Access Policy, but it uses customization settings from Access Profile.
bugs.conditions: Per-request Access Policy with Reject Ending agent and customized 'logout' page.
bugs.impact: Incorrect customization settings may be used.
bugs.fix: Now 'URL blocked' page shown for Reject Ending agent in per-request Access Policy uses customization settings from this per-request Access Policy.

bugs.title: Unknown trap OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.47.2.0.1.0.1
bugs.symptoms: During re-licensing or license reload, an unknown trap OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.47.2.0.1.0.1 may be sent.
bugs.conditions: Occurs during license reload or reactivation.
bugs.impact: After a license reload, the unknown trap can be seen like the following: run "tcpdump -ni mgmt port 162 -vvvv &": 12:01:59.883331 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 47411, offset 0, flags [DF], proto UDP (17), length 101) 10.248.136.179.55540 > 172.28.8.68.snmptrap: [bad udp cksum 0x486e -> 0xd7b8!] { SNMPv2c { V2Trap(58) R=1205683810 .1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0=1775555 .1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.4.1.0=.1.3.6.1.2.1.47.2.0.1.0.1 } }

bugs.title: If wr_urldbd is restarted while queries are being run against Custom DB then further lookups can not be made after wr_urldbd comes back up from restart.
bugs.symptoms: URLCAT lookups to Custom DB return Unknown result.
bugs.conditions: -- URL is being looked up against Custom DB -- wr_urldbd is restarted at the same time
bugs.impact: Queries will likely fail in highly loaded environments if wr_urldbd is restarted for any reason.
bugs.fix: Wr_urldbd restores connection to Custom DB after restart.

bugs.title: The TMM may crash in a rare scenario involving HTTP unchunking, and plugins.
bugs.symptoms: The TMM crashes while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: This occurs rarely on a Virtual Server configured with HTTP profile that has HTTP response chunking enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes in a rare scenario involving HTTP unchunking and plugins.

bugs.title: Serverside conection may use wrong VLAN when virtual wire is configured
bugs.symptoms: Server syn is flowing on the wrong VLAN, when tmm tries to establish a server connection. The BIG-IP system sends RST packets of unmatched VLAN/MAC combination
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual wire is configured . -- Clientside data and handshake come in on different VLANs.
bugs.impact: Some client connections fail to establish

bugs.title: RST_STREAM is sent in closed state on a serverside stream in HTTP/2 full proxy
bugs.symptoms: RST_STREAM is sent on a serverside stream in closing state in HTTP/2 full proxy.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 clientside and serverside profiles are attached to the virtual server. -- HTTP and httprouter profiles are attached to the virtual server. -- Race between clientside and serverside closing, where clientside closes faster.
bugs.impact: RST_STREAM is sent on a stream in closed state.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with RST_STREAM being sent incorrectly.

bugs.title: LB::detach iRule command may trigger TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM SIGSEGV crash.
bugs.conditions: LB::detach is run during a HTTP transaction.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not write iRules that may execute LB::detach while a HTTP transaction is in progress.
bugs.fix: TMM does not crash even if LB::detach is run during HTTP transaction.

bugs.title: Avrinstall crashes and admd restarts in endless loop when APM provision is Minimal
bugs.symptoms: During upgrade, avrinstall crashes, and then admd restarts repeatedly.
bugs.conditions: This occurred with the following provisioning: -- APM: Minimal -- ASM: Minimal
bugs.impact: Avrinstall crashes, and admd restarts in an endless loop. No stress-based anomaly detection or behavioral statistics aggregation.
bugs.workaround: Increase the APM provision to Nominal.
bugs.fix: Fixed an avrinstall crash related to low memory.

bugs.title: Multicast Flood Can Cause the Host TMM to Restart
bugs.symptoms: A vCMP host tmm is restarted.
bugs.conditions: The vCMP host is processing heavy multicast traffic.
bugs.impact: The host TMM restarts and traffic stops for the guests.
bugs.workaround: An adjustment to the scheduling can be made by this setting of the vCMP Host configuration: # echo "realtime yield 90" > /config/tmm_init.tcl # bigstart restart tmm The bigstart restart tmm must be performed individually on all blades on the vCMP host. These changes also must be done on all vCMP hosts with guests in a high availability (HA) setup.
bugs.fix: The host TMM no longer restarts.

bugs.title: Incorrect source MAC address with hardware acceleration (ePVA) and asymmetric routing
bugs.symptoms: Connections that are hardware accelerated and that use asymmetric routing may use the wrong MAC address for return traffic. This can be observed by looking at a packet capture.
bugs.conditions: Hardware acceleration is enabled (ePVA/fastL4) with asymmetric routing.
bugs.impact: The return traffic has the wrong source MAC address. This may affect packet forwarding depending on the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Disable HW acceleration.

bugs.title: SSO setting for Portal Access resources in webtop sections cannot be updated.
bugs.symptoms: SSO setting for Portal Access (PA) resource assigned to any webtop section cannot be updated due to the following error: No such atomic attribute:name in class:webtop_section_webtop_section_resource Configuration with such a resource cannot be transferred to another BIG-IP system due to the same error.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system configuration with the following objects: -- SSO configuration (any type). -- PA resource with resource item. -- The webtop section with the PA resource. -- Full webtop. -- Per-session access policy with resource assignment agent which assigns webtop, webtop section, and PA resource.
bugs.impact: Configuration cannot be updated or transferred.
bugs.workaround: Delete webtop sections from the configuration and re-create them after transfer / upgrade / update process.
bugs.fix: Now APM configuration with Portal Access resources in webtop sections can be transferred or upgraded.

bugs.title: TCP, UDP, and SCTP proxy converts to GEO proxy when georedundancy profile is attached with virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: When a georedundancy profile is attached to a TCP, UDP, and SCTP virtual server, proxy does not convert to GEO proxy.
bugs.conditions: Attach georedundancy profile to a standard TCP, UDP, or SCTP virtual server.
