bugs.impact: Unable to convert proxy to GEO proxy when georedundancy profile is attached with TCP, UDP and SCTP virtual

bugs.title: Blade software installation stalled at Waiting for product image
bugs.symptoms: On a chassis system where the active/primary blade is running version 14.1.0 or later and a new blade is inserted that has version 14.0.0 or lower, the secondary blades fail to receive the updated images and the installation stalls. The primary blade reports 'Waiting for product image' when running the tmsh show sys software status command.
bugs.conditions: Primary blade running version 14.1.0 or above. Secondary running an earlier version is inserted.
bugs.impact: Newly inserted blade does not synchronize volumes with the primary blade and cannot be used. The tmsh show sys software status command reports that one or more blades are in 'waiting for product image' status indefinitely.
bugs.workaround: Ensure all blades are running the same version. This can be accomplished manually by running the following command at the command prompt (this example is for new blade inserted at slot #3): scp /shared/images/* slot3:/shared/images

bugs.title: AVR statistics for NAT cannot be shown on multi-bladed machine
bugs.symptoms: The system presents an error messagewhen trying to get AVR statistics for NAT: Data Input Error: Database is unavailable.
bugs.conditions: Using AVR reports for NAT on a multi-bladed BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: Cannot view AVR statistics for NAT.
bugs.workaround: 1. Back up the file /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tmstat_fw_nat_entities.cfg 2. Run the following command: sed -i 's/measures=/measures=period,/' /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tmstat_fw_nat_entities.cfg 3. Verify that the only change made to 'sed -i 's/measures=/measures=period,/' /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tmstat_fw_nat_entities.cfg' was adding a 'period,' to the list of measures (can be compared against the backup file). 4. Restart monpd (to pick up the changes): bigstart restart monpd
bugs.fix: Fixed formula for statistics to allow using it on a multi-bladed BIG-IP device.

bugs.title: IPsec: TMM cored with SIGFPE in racoon2
bugs.symptoms: TMM asserted and cored in racoon2 with this panic message: panic: iked/ikev2_child.c:2858: Assertion "Invalid Child SA proposal" failed.
bugs.conditions: When IKEv2 Phase 2 SA has no peer proposal associated with it.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Bcm56xxd does not always generate a core file
bugs.symptoms: Certain 'assertion' failures in the bcm56xxd software will exit cleanly instead of generating a core file.
bugs.conditions: Assertion failures in the Broadcom SDK library.
bugs.impact: No core file generated.
bugs.fix: Modify assertion code to always produce a core file.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when sending TCP packets
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and produces a core file. TMM logs show the crash being type SIGFPE, with the following panic message: Failed assert: xnet_lib.c:795: Valid tx packet
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual Edition
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: A temporary way to avoid the problem is to configure BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) to use an alternative network driver in place of the default 'xnet' driver. In releases 14.1.0 and later, this is the 'sock' driver; in releases 13.1.0 through 14.0.x, the 'unic' driver is the alternative. Use one of the following command sequences from the BIG-IP instance's 'bash' prompt to configure the alternative driver. (Note the use of the 'greater-than' symbol.) -- Commands for Releases 14.1.0 and later: # echo "device driver vendor_dev 1d0f:ec20 sock" > /config/tmm_init.tcl [check that the file's contents are correct] # cat /config/tmm_init.tcl [restart the BIG-IP's TMM processes] # bigstart restart tmm [make certain that the 'driver_in_use' is 'sock'] # tmctl -dblade -i tmm/device_probed -- Commands for releases 13.1.0 through 14.0.0: # echo "device driver vendor_dev 1af4:1000 unic" > /config/tmm_init.tcl [check that the file's contents are correct] # cat /config/tmm_init.tcl [restart the BIG-IP's TMM processes] # bigstart restart tmm [make certain that the 'driver_in_use' is 'unic'] # tmctl -dblade -i tmm/device_probed
bugs.fix: TMM processes large packets as expected.

bugs.title: Cannot change managemnet IP from GUI
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to change the management IP from the GUI
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when using the GUI to change the management IP address via the System :: Platform page.
bugs.impact: The GUI indicates that it will redirect you to the new IP address. You will eventually be redirected but the management IP address is not changed on the BIG-IP device.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create the management IP. This will overwrite the old one. Example: create /sys management-ip [ip address/prefixlen] To view the management IP configurations tmsh list /sys management-ip
bugs.fix: Should be able to set the Management IP from GUI as below 1. Go to System->Platform page. 2. Choose Configuration -> Manual and set some other IPv4 address 3. Press the Update button.

bugs.title: GUI hangs when iApp produces error message
bugs.symptoms: If lengthy Tcl errors are displayed in the GUI while creating an iApp, the GUI can hang.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating an iApp that contains a syntax error. -- A large error message is emitted.
bugs.impact: GUI hangs.
bugs.workaround: Restart the tomcat process: tmsh restart sys service tomcat

bugs.title: Plane CPU stats too high after primary blade failover in multi-blade chassis
bugs.symptoms: The data, control, and analysis plane stats are too high as reported by tmsh show sys performance system detail.
bugs.conditions: The primary blade in a multi-blade chassis fails over to another blade.
bugs.impact: The plane CPU stats are too high.
bugs.workaround: Remove the /var/tmstat/blade/statsd file on the previous primary blade and restart merged on that blade.
bugs.fix: The plane CPU stats are now cleared on a secondary blade after failover.

bugs.title: English instead of Japanese in messages for BIG-IP Edge Client
bugs.symptoms: Untranslated text for BIG-IP Edge Client in the Japanese environment: If you see a prompt to look for an app in Store, press 'Esc' key.<br/>If you see a prompt to switch apps, click 'Yes' button.
bugs.conditions: APM Access Policy : Start :: Antivirus :: Logon and configured with only the single language Japanese.
bugs.impact: Some of the warning messages are shown in English rather than Japanese.

bugs.title: Certain plaintext traffic may cause SSL Orchestrator to hang
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading SSL Orchestrator to version 5.x, traffic gets reset, SSL Orchestrator hangs, and tcpdump analysis indicates that connections are being reset due to SSL handshake timeout exceeded.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL Orchestrator configured. -- Initial plaintext traffic resembles SSLv2 hello message or has less-than-enough bytes for SSL to process.
bugs.impact: SSL Orchestrator hangs on that connection, unable to bypass traffic until the connection times out. Other connections handle traffic during this interval.
bugs.fix: This release adds a db variable to enable/disable SSLv2 hello parsing. It is called tmm.ssl.v2compatibility and is disabled by default.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing DNS profiles with DNS queing enabled
bugs.symptoms: TMM may consume excessive resources while processing traffic with a DNS profile.
bugs.conditions: A DNS listener is configured with DNS queuing enabled. DNS queuing is enabled by default.
bugs.impact: Excessive resources consumption potentially leading to a TMM crash and failover event.
bugs.workaround: Disable DNS queuing.
bugs.fix: Resource limits for DNS queuing are introduced with the help of DB variables. modify /sys db dns.ingress.queue.high value <value> modify /sys db dns.ingress.queue.low value <value> This change also exposes following variables to ensure that the paths to the DNSX database are resilient in the face of a temporarily unavailable DNSX database: modify /sys db dns.action.queue.max value <value> modify /sys db dns.actions.poll value <value> modify /sys db dns.contexts.poll value <value> Modify the value to default to reset any of the above variables.
bugs.behavior: Resource limits for DNS queuing are introduced with the help of DB variables. modify /sys db dns.ingress.queue.high value <value> modify /sys db dns.ingress.queue.low value <value> This change also exposes following variables to ensure that the paths to the DNSX database are resilient in the face of a temporarily unavailable DNSX database: modify /sys db dns.action.queue.max value <value> modify /sys db dns.actions.poll value <value> modify /sys db dns.contexts.poll value <value> Modify the value to default to reset any of the above variables.

bugs.title: Generate signature files for logs
bugs.symptoms: To achieve DoDIN APL certification, the BIG-IP system must guarantee the integrity of log files using the standards' recommendation of encrypting those files on the local store. The BIG-IP system does not generate signature files for logs. As a result, the system stores the audit information (i.e., the log files stored in /var/log folder and other subfolders) without creating integrity files.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the audit information stored in /var/log and other locations.
bugs.impact: Audit log files are stored without integrity files on the local system.
bugs.workaround: Disable local logging for audit logs and send them to remote syslog, for example: tmsh modify sys syslog include "filter f_audit { facility(local0) and not message(AUDIT); }; "
bugs.fix: There is now a LogIntegrity utility provided to generate signature files for logs. -- To enable the feature: tmsh modify sys db logintegrity.support value enable -- To set the LogIntegrity loglevel: tmsh modify sys db logintegrity.loglevel value debug You must create private key and store it in SecureVault before enabling this feature. To do so: 1. Generate a private key with the name logfile_integrity.key, for example: tmsh create sys crypto key logfile_integrity.key key-type rsa-private key-size 2048 gen-certificate security-type password country US city Seattle state WA organization "Example, Inc." ou "Example-Creation Team" common-name www.example.com email-address admin@example.com lifetime 365 2. Generate RSA encrypted private SSL keys: 2a. Go to the filestore location on the BIG-IP system: cd /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_key_d/ ls | grep logfile_integrity:Common:logfile_integrity.key_63031_2 openssl rsa -aes256 -in :Common:logfile_integrity.key_63031_2 -out logfile_integrity_secure.key 2b. Specify the PEM password/passphrase (e.g., root0101) to use to protect the SSL private key (in this example, logfile_integrity_secure.key is the password protected private key): 2c. run command to list the generated files ls | grep logfile_integrity :Common:logfile_integrity.key_63031_2 logfile_integrity_secure.key 3. Install the generated password protected SSL private key with the same password (e.g., root0101) used in step 2 to store in 'secure vault' on the BIG-IP system: tmsh install sys crypto key logfile_integrity.key passphrase example root0101 from-local-file logfile_integrity_secure.key Once the feature is enabled and the private key installed, The signature files are generated under /var/log/digest whenever log files get rotated. If you want to verify Signatures, follow these steps: 1. Go to the filestore location on the BIG-IP system : cd /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d 2. Execute the following command to generate the public key. openssl x509 -in :Common:logfile_integrity.key_63031_2 -noout -pubkey > certificatefile.pub.cer 3.Verify the signature file using public key: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/certificatefile.pub.cer -signature /var/log/digest/audit.1.sig /var/log/audit.1

bugs.title: OVSDB-server daemon lost permission to certs due to SELinux issue, causing SSL connection failure
bugs.symptoms: OVSDB-server fails to make SSL connections when Selinux is enforced. In /var/log/openvswitch/ovsdb-server.log: ...|00012|stream_ssl|ERR|/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/:Common:myCert_2468_1: stat failed (Permission denied).
bugs.conditions: -- Navigate to System :: Configuration : OVSDB. -- Add cert and keys.
bugs.impact: Permission denied, SSL connection failure.
bugs.workaround: Step 1: Check openvswitch SELinux denial: # audit2allow -w -a Example output: type=AVC msg=audit(1566915298.607:32958): avc: denied { search } for pid=18966 comm="ovsdb-server" name="/" dev="dm-7" ino=2 scontext=system_u:system_r:openvswitch_t:s0 tcontext=system_u:object_r:f5config_t:s0 tclass=dir Was caused by: Missing type enforcement (TE) allow rule. You can use audit2allow to generate a loadable module to allow this access. Step 2: Find openvswitch components that need Linux policy additions: # audit2allow -a Example output: #============= openvswitch_t ============== allow openvswitch_t f5config_t:dir search; allow openvswitch_t f5filestore_t:dir search; allow openvswitch_t f5filestore_t:file { getattr open read }; Step 3: Modify the policy to allow access to the component openvswitch_t: # audit2allow -a -M openvswitch_t Step 4: Apply the policy: # semodule -i openvswitch_t.pp
bugs.fix: SELinux policy rules for openvswitch module have been added.

bugs.title: 'tmsh list' / 'tmsh list security' hangs when AFM / Herculon DDoS Hybrid Defender are not provisioned
bugs.symptoms: The 'tmsh list security' command hangs when ASM is provisioned and AFM or Herculon DDoS Hybrid Defender are licensed, but not provisioned.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when AFM and/or Herculon DDoS Hybrid Defender are licensed but not provisioned.
bugs.impact: The tmsh command hangs when running any of following commands: - tmsh show running-config - tmsh show running-config security - tmsh show running-config security presentation tmui virtual-list - tmsh list - tmsh list security - tmsh list security presentation tmui virtual-list
bugs.fix: The tmsh list security command no longer hangs when ASM is provisioned and AFM/Herculon DDoS Hybrid Defender is not provisioned.

bugs.title: Flowspecd starts with message: Shm segment not found in /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf.
bugs.symptoms: During system boot, the flowspecd daemon emits a message 'Shm segment not found in /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf', and heartbeat monitoring is disabled for flowspecd.
bugs.conditions: Flowspecd daemon is running.
bugs.impact: No heartbeat monitoring for flowspecd daemon.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the file /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf and insert a line at the end: ha segment path: /flowspecd
bugs.fix: Missing line in /etc/ha_table/ha_table.conf added causing flowspecd to start cleanly and undergo a heartbeat monitoring.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic.
bugs.conditions: HTTP profile active.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Unnecessary memory allocation in AVR module
bugs.symptoms: Internal Bados indicator is not updated correctly, creating unnecessary memory allocation in AVR module.
bugs.conditions: Using AVR.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary memory consumption

bugs.title: Modifying a virtual address with an iControl PUT command causes the netmask to always change to IPv6 ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff
bugs.symptoms: Using an iControl PUT command to modify a virtual address will change that address's netmask to ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff.
bugs.conditions: Modifying a virtual address using an iControl PUT command.
bugs.impact: An unintentional change to the virtual address's netmask.
bugs.workaround: Two options: -- Use a PATCH command instead of a PUT command. -- Always specify the netmask explicitly when making changes.

bugs.title: F5 APM modules added capability to pull user group membership information from Kerberos authentication tickets
bugs.symptoms: F5 APM Kerberos Auth agent is unable to extract the user group membership info from the Kerberos authentication ticket.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered while using the Kerberos Auth agent
bugs.impact: APM is unable to extract user group membership info directly from Kerberos tickets.
bugs.workaround: Use Active Directory query module to query on user group membership info from backend AD server during every request. Impact of workaround: this has a negative performance impact
bugs.fix: F5 APM modules added capability in Kerberos Authentication module to pull user group membership IDs from Kerberos authentication tickets, and added new AD Group SID Resolver module to resolve group IDs to memorable group names using group cache.

bugs.title: afm_cmi.py daemon can cause very high BIG-IP CPU utilization(>90%)
bugs.symptoms: The AFM Auto threshold and behavioral dos historical data synchronization process consumes greater than 90% CPU. This affects TMM performance and some outages may occur.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in both high availability (HA) and standalone configurations. In both cases "MCPD" issues were reported. (Delay in response or the daemon crashed)
bugs.impact: TMM performance is affected and outages may occur.
bugs.workaround: Kill the AFM data synchronization process: kill -9 afm_cmi.py
bugs.fix: If the connection to MCP is non responsive, the script will attempt to reinitialize MCP connection every second until successful. The script will be blocked until mcp connection is established.

bugs.title: TMSH does not follow current best practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMSH does not follow current best practices when processing come commands.
bugs.conditions: Administrative user with TMSH access
bugs.impact: TMSH does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: TMSH now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: Virtual address can be deleted while it is in use by an address-list.
bugs.symptoms: -- The virtual-address (and virtual server) will no longer work. -- The BIG-IP won't answer ARP requests for it. -- Loading the config again or performing similar operations will not re-create the virtual-address.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual address is deleted while it is in use by an address list and virtual server. -- MCPD is restarted (or the unit rebooted, etc.).
bugs.impact: Traffic processing is disrupted

bugs.title: Improve error message if user did not select a address-list or port list in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, the Virtual Server screen displays the available address-lists or port lists for source address, but there is no clarity on whether the options are selected or available.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server's source address section.
bugs.impact: If you do not make a selection and try to create the Virtual Server, an error occurs: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.workaround: Click to select the address-list of port-list displayed as source address for Virtual Server.

bugs.title: MCPD error - Trouble allocating MAC address for VLAN object
bugs.symptoms: You see the following errors in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[8985]: 0107071c:3: Trouble allocating mac address for vlan object /Common/external.
bugs.conditions: Conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: There is no known impact to the system as a result of this log message.
bugs.workaround: If this reoccurs, you can try force reloading mcpd. For more information, see K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030.

bugs.title: Setting ssl profile to none in https monitor, not setting Ciphers to DEFAULT as in serverssl Profile
bugs.symptoms: With in-tmm monitoring enabled (or sys db bigd tmm set to enable) and with https monitor's ssl-profile set to none, the expected behavior is to send ciphers in ClientHello based on default serverssl profile as mentioned in GUI help for https monitor.
bugs.conditions: Configure HTTPS Monitor with ssl-profile "None".
bugs.impact: Ciphers are not exchanged as expected in the ClientHello Packets
bugs.workaround: Configure HTTPS Monitor without ssl-profile option, default serverssl profile will be used

bugs.title: TCP re-transmission during SYN Cookie activation results in high latency
bugs.symptoms: Issue is reported at the following system setup: client <-> BIG-IP <-> concentrator <-> proxy <-> BIG-IP nat gateway <-> Internet -- SYN Cookie got activated on F5 nat gateway. -- Latency from 'Internet' (public host) is observed at 'Proxy' device sitting before F5 nat gw. -- During the latency issue, SYN Cookie was active and evicting connections. -- When SYN Cookie is enabled, it switches to l7 delayed binding as expected but it is not sending ACK for HTTP request so the client sends it again and again.
bugs.conditions: Haredware SYN Cookie is enabled on FastL4 profile
bugs.impact: High latency is observed.
bugs.workaround: Disable the SYN Cookie on the FastL4 profile

bugs.title: Duplicate MAC entries in FDB
bugs.symptoms: Forwarding DataBase (FDB) not updated when a MAC moves among interfaces.
bugs.conditions: -- Having multiple paths to a MAC in a given configuration.
bugs.impact: There are duplicate MAC address entries which come from multiple interfaces.

bugs.title: False positive malformed json or xml violation.
bugs.symptoms: A false positive malformed XML or JSON violation occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- A stream profile is attached (or the http profile is set to rechunk on the request side). -- A json/XML profile attached to the virtual.
bugs.impact: A false positive violation.
bugs.workaround: Modify the http profile to work in preserve mode for request chunking (this workaround is not possible in 16.1).

bugs.title: Dynamic routing daemon mribd crashes if 'mrib debug all' is enabled in high availability (HA) config with Floating Self IP configured for PIM protocol.
bugs.symptoms: The multicast routing protocols are implemented by pimd and mribd daemons. mribd daemon crashes in a specific configuration when debug logging is enabled for this daemon.
bugs.conditions: 1) Dynamic Routing bundle is enabled and PIM protocol is enabled on a route domain. 2) High availability (HA) group/pair with floating self IP address is configured. 3) PIM neighbors are configured for each peer in high availability (HA) group/pair. 4) One of the peers in high availability (HA) is configured to use floating self IP address as an IP address for PIM protocol. This is done using the 'ip pim use-floating-address' command in the PIM configuration in imish: # ip pim use-floating-address 5) Multicast routing is configured in imish: # ip multicast-routing 6) Debug logging for mribd is enabled: # debug ip mrib all # debug ipv6 mrib all --- Note: Although steps 3 and 4 are optional, a practical configuration makes no sense without them.
bugs.impact: Dynamic routing daemon mribd crashes. Advanced routing not available while mribd restarts.
bugs.fix: Dynamic routing daemon mribd no longer crashes when mribd debug logging is enabled.

bugs.title: Manually licensing a versioned VE license through the GUI fails to activate the license
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not activate a versioned BIG-IP VE (VE) license using the manual licensing process through the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Any VE license installed using the manual method that contains Exclusive_version for versioning.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not go active, as the license does not activate properly.
bugs.workaround: Use the CLI to paste the license file into /config/bigip.license then reload the license using 'reloadlic' in the bash shell.
bugs.fix: The system prevents using manual license installs through the GUI for versioned VE licenses.

bugs.title: Ldbutil utility ignores '--instance' option if '--list' option is specified
bugs.symptoms: When running ldbutil utility, if the '--list' option is specified, then the '--instance' option has no effect. All the local users will be listed.
bugs.conditions: When both '--list' and '--instance' options are specified.
bugs.impact: The output lists all the local users and not limiting to the '--instance' option given.

bugs.title: Log HSB registers when parts of the device becomes unresponsive
bugs.symptoms: Part of the HSB becomes unresponsive, and there is no logging of additional registers to assist in diagnosing the failure.
bugs.conditions: It is unknown under what conditions the HSB becomes unresponsive.
bugs.impact: Limited visibility into the HSB state when it becomes unresponsive.

bugs.title: HSB and switch interface pause frames
bugs.symptoms: The interface between the HSB and switch may experience a high number of pause frames, which can be observed in the switch interface stats counters.rx_pause value. This may also be seen by impacted traffic in the ltm logs, such as lacpd errors: info lacpd[8992]: 01160010:6: Link 2.3 removed from aggregation info lacpd[8992]: 01160011:6: Link 2.3 Actor Out of Sync info lacpd[8992]: 01160012:6: Link 2.3 Partner Out of Sync
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur if there are hardware-accelerated flows and IPv6 traffic.
bugs.impact: Network traffic is dropped.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, the fix for this issue has been added to HSB firmware images for BIG-IP v14.1.x. This includes the B4450N and iSeries platforms.

bugs.title: Incorrect values in REST response for dos-l3 table
bugs.symptoms: Some of the calculations in the AVR publisher are not performed, and incorrect values are shown in the REST response.
bugs.conditions: -- Device vector detection and mitigation thresholds are set to 10 -- The attack vector is triggered
bugs.impact: Wrong values appear in REST reponse
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with incorrect values for mitigated attacks.

bugs.title: DoS stats table shows drops count on tcp-half-open global vector for packets dropped by ltm syn cookie
bugs.symptoms: DoS stats table shows drops count on tcp-half-open global vector for packets dropped by ltm syn cookie, even when the tcp-half-open vector mitigation threshold is not reached on the vector
bugs.conditions: -- Device DoS tcp-half-open vector is in detect-only mode or mitigate with 64000 limit. -- LTM SYN cookies are enabled.
bugs.impact: DoS stats table show inaccurate result
bugs.fix: After fix, the packets dropped by LTM SYN cookie is not counted against device dos tcp-half-open vector

bugs.title: Specific FIPS device errors will not trigger failover
bugs.symptoms: When the FIPS device experiences a hardware failure during idle-time, the device may not fail over.
bugs.conditions: -- FIPS hardware failure occurs, but the device is idle
bugs.impact: The device may not fail over on FIPS hardware failure.
bugs.fix: Interpret rare FIPS card failure as failover event.

bugs.title: TMM does not enforce RFC compliance when processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM does not require RFC compliance when processing HTTP traffic. This does not impact the performance or security of BIG-IP systems, but may impact connected systems if they expect only compliant traffic to be forwarded.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP virtual server -- Non-compliant HTTP request from client
bugs.impact: Pool members may be exposed to non-compliant HTTP requests.
bugs.fix: The HTTP filter now optionally performs basic RFC compliance checks. If a request fails these checks, then the connection is reset.
bugs.behavior: A new BigDB variable has been added. The new 'Tmm.HTTP.RFC.Enforcement' option may be enabled or disabled. It is disabled by default. If enabled, the HTTP filter performs basic RFC compliance checks. If a request fails these checks, then the connection is reset. The checks performed are a subset of those described within the HTTP PSM module. If a blocking page is required, or more detailed control over which checks are performed, configure HTTP PSM or ASM on the virtual server. If either HTTP PSM or ASM are configured on a virtual server, the state of the 'Tmm.HTTP.RFC.Enforcement' BigDB variable is ignored on that virtual server.

bugs.title: Unable to scp/sftp to device after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Users with numeric usernames are unable to log in via scp.
bugs.conditions: -- Logging in via scp/sftp. -- User account with a numeric username.
bugs.impact: Unable to log in via scp.
bugs.workaround: Include alpha characters in username.

bugs.title: Unable to scp to device after upgrade: path not allowed
bugs.symptoms: SCP of file to the BIG-IP system results in error: path not allowed
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs when both conditions are present: -- The BIG-IP user has shell tmsh or shell none access. -- The scp operation is performed on a non-symlink location present under scp whitelist (/config/ssh/scp.whitelist). For example: scp to /var/tmp succeeds scp to /shared/tmp fails with 'path not allowed'.
bugs.impact: Cannot copy files to symlinks present under whitelist.
bugs.workaround: Use the explicitly listed (symlink) path as the scp destination.
bugs.fix: You can now scp copy files to a path present under whitelist without error.

bugs.title: LTM high availability (HA) sync should not sync GTM zone configuration
bugs.symptoms: LTM high availability (HA) sync group are syncing GTM zone configuration changes.
bugs.conditions: 1. BIG-IPs has both LTM and GTM provisioned. 2. The two BIG-IPs are inside one LTM sync group.
bugs.impact: GTM zone files are accidentally modified.

bugs.title: Reset Horizon View application does not work when accessing through F5 APM
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to reset VMware applications from a Windows VM client, Android VM client or HTML5 client.
bugs.conditions: -- VMware Horizon Proxy configured via an iApp on APM -- Access the VM applications via APM webtop through native client /HTML5 client for windows or access applications via native client on android
bugs.impact: Impaired reset option functionality

bugs.title: 'Application Service List' empty after UCS restore
bugs.symptoms: The iApps :: Applications LX list does not display anything after restoring a UCS that was taken from a different device.
bugs.conditions: -- Restoring a UCS from a different device. -- UCS includes the iAppLX package.
bugs.impact: Cannot see anything on 'Application Service List', and you are unable to configure the application.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command before restoring the UCS file: clear-rest-storage

bugs.title: LACP working member state may be inconsistent when blade is forced offline
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistent (out-of-sync) LACP working member state. Incorrect trunk high availability (HA) score.
bugs.conditions: LACP updates while blade is going offline.
bugs.impact: Incorrect high availability (HA) score may prevent the unit from automatically failing over.

bugs.title: Self-IP does not respond to ( ARP / Neighbour Discovery ) when EtherIP tunnels in use.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems might not respond to ( ARP / Neighbour Discovery ) requests received via EtherIP tunnels on a multi-blade system.
bugs.conditions: Decapsulated ( ARP / Neighbour Discovery ) requests for an address owned by the BIG-IP system is processed by a secondary blade.
bugs.impact: Some endpoints may not be able to resolve ( ARP / Neighbour protocol ) via EtherIP tunnel.
bugs.workaround: Create static ARP entries on affected endpoints.

bugs.title: Wrong wildcard URL matching when none of the configured URLS include QS
bugs.symptoms: Wildcard URLs has a flag (include_query_string) which indicates if the matching should include traffic URL's QS or not For example, if the traffic URL is '/path?a=b' and configured URL is '/path*b': 1. if include QS enabled, URL is matched 2. otherwise, no match (since matching against '/path' only) if there are no configured URLs with "Include Query String" enabled, matching may be wrong
bugs.conditions: 1. Wildcard URL configured in anti-fraud profile (URL name contains an asterisk) 2. None of the configured URLs has "Include Query String" enabled 3. Traffic URL contains a query-string
bugs.impact: URL is incorrectly matched (when it either shouldn't be matched at all or should match another configured URL). Features/signatures might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Configure at least one URL with "Include Query String" enabled
bugs.fix: FPS should match query string correctly (according to configuration)

bugs.title: After an initial boot, mcpd has a defunct child "systemctl" process
bugs.symptoms: Zombie "systemctl" process, as a child of mcpd.
bugs.conditions: Reboot of the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Minimal; a single zombie process is created.
bugs.workaround: To get rid of the process, you can restart mcpd.

bugs.title: Incomplete Action 'Deny' does not take effect for HTTP-Connect
bugs.symptoms: Per-request policy's incomplete-action 'Deny' does not take effect for HTTP-Connect request.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL Orchestrator (SSLO) or APM is licensed and provisioned. -- Per-request policy is created and attached to a virtual server. -- Incomplete Action value of per-request policy is set to 'Deny'.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system does not reject the HTTP-Connect request when incomplete-action is set to 'Deny'.
bugs.fix: Incomplete Action 'Deny' now takes effect for HTTP-Connect request.

bugs.title: DNSSEC does not insert NSEC3 records for NXDOMAIN responses
bugs.symptoms: DNSSEC does not insert NSEC3 records for NXDOMAIN responses.
bugs.conditions: -- "process-xfr yes" is set for the dns profile associated with the listener; And -- There is no "Zone Transfer Clients" nameserver configured for that zone. And -- There is no wideip configured.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC does not respond NSEC3 for non-existent domain.
bugs.workaround: 1. Change this setting for dns profile from "process-xfr yes" to "process-xfr no"; Or 2. Add a nameserver for "Zone Transfer Clients" of that zone. Or 3. Add a wideip.

bugs.title: Mcpd core when changing password for BIG-IP remote user
bugs.symptoms: While changing a BIG-IP remote password, mcpd hangs during the LDAP authentication process, and crashes.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that trigger this are unknown; it occurred while changing the password for a remote user on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Mcpd stops responding, then crashes. Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.

bugs.title: HTTP response not forwarded to client during an early response
bugs.symptoms: In early server responses, the client does not receive the intended response from the HTTP::respond iRule. The client instead receives an unexpected 500 internal server error.
bugs.conditions: -- A slow client. -- early server response with the HTTP::respond iRule.
bugs.impact: A client does not receive the redirect from the HTTP::respond iRule.
bugs.fix: The client now receives the redirect from the HTTP:respond iRule.

bugs.title: Large number of in-TMM monitors results in some monitors being marked down
bugs.symptoms: Pool members are marked down from the in-TMM monitor.
bugs.conditions: Device has a large number of in-TMM monitors.
bugs.impact: Monitor target may appear down when it is actually up.
bugs.workaround: Disable in-tmm monitors: tmsh modify sys db bigd.tmm value disable

bugs.title: Throughput degradation while uploading when using TAP device in service chain for SSL Orchestrator
bugs.symptoms: When the TAP service is configured for SSL Orchestrator, upload throughput is degraded.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when a TAP service is configured in the deployment.
bugs.impact: Upload speed through the device is degraded.
bugs.workaround: Modify the PUSH flag on TAP service TCP wan profile from Default to Auto...

bugs.title: After starting up, mcpd may have defunct child "run" and "xargs" processes
bugs.symptoms: After starting up, mcpd may have defunct child "run" and "xargs" processes
bugs.conditions: Slow disk storage or large configuration files.
bugs.impact: Minimal; some zombie processes are created.

bugs.title: Prober pool selected on server or data center not being displayed after selection in Internet Explorer
bugs.symptoms: Selected prober pool not visible on server or data center in Internet Explorer or Edge
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you have a prober pool configured for a data center or server, and you are viewing them in the GUI using Internet Explorer or Edge.
bugs.impact: The prober pool is not displayed.
bugs.workaround: Use Chrome or Firefox as browser

bugs.title: Renaming HA VLAN can disrupt state-mirror connection
bugs.symptoms: If the VLAN that services the state mirror connection between BIG-IP systems is renamed, it can cause a disruption of the state mirror connection. It can also lead to an eventual crash.
bugs.conditions: Renaming the VLAN that services the state mirror connection between BIG-IP systems in an high availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.impact: System might crash eventually.
bugs.workaround: Do not rename the VLAN that services the state mirror connection between BIG-IP systems in an HA configuration.

bugs.title: Qkview may fail to completely sanitize LDAP bind credentials
bugs.symptoms: Qkview snapshots may contain a portion of the LDAP bind password.
bugs.conditions: LDAP bindpw attribute contains whitespace.
bugs.impact: As stated.
bugs.workaround: Remove nslcd.conf from qkview tarball.
bugs.fix: Qkview will detect and remove an LDAP bindpw containing whitespace.

bugs.title: FTP profile causes memory leak
bugs.symptoms: When a FTP profile is added to a virtual server, TMM runs with memory leak and eventually system has to terminate connections.
bugs.conditions: A FTP profile is installed on virtual server and the inherit-parent-profile parameter is enabled or isession is also included on the FTP virtual.
bugs.impact: TMM runs with memory leak and eventually system has to terminate connections.
bugs.workaround: Disable the inherit-parent-profile option if fastL4 data-channel is adequate.
bugs.fix: Fix the internal memory cleanup function bug.

bugs.title: Bot Defense whitelists do not apply for IP 'Any' when using route domains
bugs.symptoms: When defining whitelists in bot defense profiles, when the IP is set to 'Any' and route domains are in use, whitelists are not applied.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is enabled. -- Whitelist is configured for IP 'Any' (for URL or GEO), -- Sending a request that matches the whitelist using route domains.
bugs.impact: Request will be mitigated.
bugs.workaround: For url whitelist only: Add micro service to the bot defense profile, configure: 1. Add required URL. 2. Specify service type 'Custom Microservice Protection'. 3. Set the 'Mitigation and Verification' setting as required (relevant for logging only). 4. In 'Automated Threat Detection', set 'Mitigation Action' to 'None'. 5. Set the microservice 'Enforcement Mode' to 'Transparent'. This causes the associated URL to never be blocked (but no 'whitelist' will be seen in reporting).
bugs.fix: Enabling IP 'Any' on route domains now works as expected.

bugs.title: Incorrect error message when uploading OpenAPI 3.0 file
bugs.symptoms: When trying to upload OpenAPI 3.0 file through Access ›› API Protection : Profile ›› New, an error message is displays that the file is not a valid OpenAPI specification file.
bugs.conditions: - Upload OpenAPI 3.0 or newer specification files.
bugs.impact: Cannot use OpenAPI 3.0 or newer specification files to create profiles.
bugs.workaround: The BIG-IP 15.1.x does not support OpenAPI 3.0 specification files. OpenAPI 3.0 is supported from BIG-IP 16.1.x, this functionality is moved from TMUI to AGC.
bugs.fix: Updated error message to show supported OpenAPI specification file version.

bugs.title: Parameters payload parser issue
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect parameter parsing occurs under some conditions. For example, in a signature violation, the 'Actual Parameter Name' value appears as 'attachment; filename'.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM in use. -- Request contains multipart headers.
bugs.impact: Incorrect policy enforcement.
bugs.fix: This release fixes an issue related to multipart requests.

bugs.title: Request Log export file is not visible for requests including binary data
bugs.symptoms: Request Log export file is not visible.
bugs.conditions: Request Log export file contain request with binary data
bugs.impact: Cannot get data from Request Log export file.

bugs.title: Using the Websocket profile prevents mouse wheel scroll function
bugs.symptoms: Mouse wheel function does not work.
bugs.conditions: WebSSO and Websocket profiles are configured on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Although there is no product functionality impact, it is an inconvenience to the BIG-IP administrator using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use an iRule that disables SSO for the Websocket request. For example, for remotespark (https://www.remotespark.com/html5.html) you can use the following iRule: ltm rule sso_disable_ws { when HTTP_REQUEST { if {[HTTP::uri] starts_with "/RDP?" and [HTTP::header exists "Upgrade"] and [HTTP::header "Upgrade"] == "websocket" } { log "DISABLING WEBSSO" WEBSSO::disable } } }

bugs.title: SIP ALG virtual with source-nat-policy cores if traffic does not match the source-nat-policy or matches the source-nat-policy which does not have source-translation configured
bugs.symptoms: In SIP ALG virtual with source-nat-policy assigned, if traffic processed by the virtual server does not match source-nat-policy, or if it matches source-nat-policy that does not have source-translation configured, tmm cores and restarts.
bugs.conditions: -- SIP ALG virtual server with an assigned source-nat-policy. -- Traffic does not match the source-nat-policy, or traffic matches a source-nat-policy that has no source-translation configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure SIP ALG virtual so that the condition never happens. For example, apply a source attribute to the virtual server that filters out traffic that will not match the source-nat-policy. Never use a source-nat-policy that has no source-translation.

bugs.title: GUI displays error when a virtual server is modified if it is using an address-list
bugs.symptoms: When you modify a virtual server, the GUI returns an error similar to the following: 01b90011:3: Virtual Server /Common/vs2_udp's Traffic Matching Criteria /Common/vs2_udp_VS_TMC_OBJ illegally shares destination address, source address, service port, and ip-protocol with Virtual Server /Common/vs1_tcp destination address, source address, service port.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when either of the following occur: -- When renaming the virtual server. -- When changing the address-list attribute.
bugs.impact: Cannot update virtual configuration with new value.

bugs.title: Need informative messages for HTTP iRule runtime validation errors
bugs.symptoms: For HTTP iRule runtime validation errors, an ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED error message is appended (with rule name and event) to /var/log/ltm, but the message is not informative about the cause of the validation error: err tmm1[20445]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/example <HTTP_REQUEST> - ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED (line 1) invoked from within "HTTP::uri". The system should post a more informative message, in this case: err tmm[10662]: 01220001:3: TCL error: /Common/example <HTTP_REQUEST> - can't call after responding - ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED (line 1) invoked from within "HTTP::uri"
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP filter and HTTP iRules are used by a virtual server. -- An HTTP iRule runtime validation error happens. For example, HTTP::uri is called after HTTP::respond () which is not supported.
bugs.impact: With no informative error messages, it is difficult to identify the validation error.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Informative messages are provided for HTTP iRule runtime validation errors.

bugs.title: Added HTTP2 and HTTP3 request/response statistic fields to the HTTP profile
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP/1.1 request/response statistic fields in the HTTP profile are incremented incorrectly when HTTP2 traffic is encountered. There is not currently a way to view the HTTP2 and HTTP3 request/response stats on the HTTP profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Client or server sends HTTP2 request/response. -- Using GUI, TMSH, iControl (SOAP), or SNMP.
bugs.impact: Incorrect HTTP/1.1 request/response statistic values are present in the HTTP profile when HTTP2 traffic is encountered.
bugs.fix: New HTTP2 and HTTP3 request/response statistic fields have been added to the HTTP profile. These report the correct request/response stats from the GUI, TMSH, iControl (SOAP), and SNMP components.

bugs.title: Chaining a standard virtual server and an ipother virtual server together can crash TMM.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a SIGFPE and restarts. The TMM logs contain the following panic message: Assertion "xbuf_delete_until successful" failed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: -- The system has been configured with a standard virtual server and an Any IP (ipother) virtual server chained together. This can be done explicitly using an iRule that features the 'virtual' command to connect the two virtual servers, or implicitly with certain APM configurations. -- The pool member on the server-side asks this specific virtual server configuration on the BIG-IP system to retransmit data.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the target virtual server in the chain configuration does not use the ipother profile.

bugs.title: Invalid volume name, clusterd error at boot time
bugs.symptoms: In certain cases, booting a new blade or upgrading can result in HD1.0 being created and the following error on startup in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[6426]: 01070945:3: Invalid volume name (HD1.0) err clusterd[8217]: 013a0004:3: result { err clusterd[8217]: 013a0004:3: result.code 17238341 err clusterd[8217]: 013a0004:3: result.message 01070945:3: Invalid volume name (HD1.0) err clusterd[8217]: 013a0004:3: result.attribute volume err clusterd[8217]: 013a0004:3: }
bugs.conditions: Conditions are not yet fully understood, but it has been documented only to occur on VIPRION systems, and specifically when booting to a newly upgraded volume or installing a new blade.
bugs.impact: Clusterd keeps restarting, BIG-IP system is unusable.
bugs.workaround: Workarounds include: -- Deleting volume HD1.0. -- Replacing volume HD1.0 with the name of the desired boot volume in /shared/db/cluster.conf.

bugs.title: SSL traffic fails with Equinix netHSM on device restart
bugs.symptoms: SSL traffic with Equinix netHSM keys fails if TMM process is restarted or device is restarted.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when following conditions are met: 1. Virtual server configured with SSL profile containing Equinix netHSM keys. 2. Device or TMM process is restarted
bugs.impact: SSL traffic fails.
bugs.workaround: Manually restart the pkcs11d process: tmsh restart sys service pkcs11d
bugs.fix: SSL traffic with Equinix netHSM keys no longer fails if TMM process is restarted or device is restarted.

bugs.title: bcm56xxd watchdog restart
bugs.symptoms: During initialization of very large configurations it is possible that the watchdog timer will fire and reset the bcm56xxd driver.
bugs.conditions: System configuration with very large number of objects being loaded.
bugs.impact: The driver restarts.

bugs.title: A rare TMM crash cause by the fix for ID 816625
bugs.symptoms: In rare scenarios involving HTTP unchunking and plugins, the TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: The fix for ID 816625 fixed HTTP unchunking and some plugins, dynamically removing the unchunking logic when required. Other plugin behavior may in addition abort the unchunking logic in an unexpected way. This causes a double-abort, and triggers a TMM crash.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The TMM no longer crashes in a rare scenario involving HTTP unchunking and plugins.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP is deployed as SAML SP, it cannot decrypt assertion it receives from IdP if it is signed using AES-GCM algorithm
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP as SAML Service Provider (SP) fails to decrypt an assertion and report an error when the assertion is encrypted using AES-GCM: err apmd[13452]: 01490202:3: session: SAML Agent: ag failed to process encrypted assertion, error: Unsupported encryption algorithm.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when BIG-IP SP receives an encrypted assertion from an IdP which is encrypted using AES-GCM.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP as SAML SP fails to verify assertion, so the access policy execution may fail if BIG-IP as SAML SP is configured for client end user authentication.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP as SAML Service Provider can now successfully decrypt assertion that is encrypted using AES GCM protocol family: AES 128 GCM, AES 192 GCM, and AES 256 GCM

bugs.title: Behavioral DoS dashboard disregards user access rights to virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: For users that have access to particular partition(s) only, the Behavioral DoS dashboard shows data for all virtual servers, including virtual servers in partitions that this user does not have access to.
bugs.conditions: -- logged into the GUI as a user which only has access to one partition -- viewing the Behavioral DoS dashboard -- The device has virtual servers on partitions to which the current user has no access.
bugs.impact: User can see BADOS statistics data related to restricted partitions.
bugs.fix: Added a mechanism for getting ADM real time data only for virtual servers accessible by the user.

bugs.title: The sFlow sample collection for VLAN does not work with VLAN groups
bugs.symptoms: The sFlow FLOW packets containing traffic samples for a VLAN are not generated and not sent to the receiver, although CNTR telemetry packets are sent.
bugs.conditions: -- The VLAN is a member of a VLAN group. -- The VLAN has sFlow packet sampling configured and enabled.
bugs.impact: No traffic samples are available from the VLANs that are part of VLAN groups.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround for VLANs that are part of VLAN groups, the sFlow traffic samples work with VLANs that are not part of VLAN groups.

bugs.title: GENERICMESSAGE::message's src and dst may get cleared in certain scenarios
bugs.symptoms: The "GENERICMESSAGE::message src" and "GENERICMESSAGE::message dst" iRule commands may not work properly if iRule processing changes to a different TMM. These commands may return an empty string rather than correct data.
bugs.conditions: -- Using "GENERICMESSAGE::message src" and/or "GENERICMESSAGE::message dst" iRule commands. -- iRule processing moves from one TMM to another TMM.
bugs.impact: Incorrect data returned from "GENERICMESSAGE::message src" and "GENERICMESSAGE::message dst" iRule commands.
bugs.fix: The "GENERICMESSAGE::message src" and "GENERICMESSAGE::message dst" iRule commands now return correct data.

bugs.title: Windows code signing certificate update 2019
bugs.symptoms: The certificate for APM Edge Client (v7.1.8.1) expires on 12 Dec. 2019
bugs.conditions: Code signing certificate expired on December 11,2019.
bugs.impact: Certificate is expired.
bugs.fix: Update APM client with the certificate attributes and use the new code singing certificate.

bugs.title: SSL::enable does not work for server side ssl
bugs.symptoms: When SSL::enable is issued in an iRule, for example in the HTTP Request event, it will not enable the server side profile if the server side profile is disabled.
bugs.conditions: An HTTP profile is configured on a virtual, and the server-ssl profile on the same virtual is disabled.
bugs.impact: The connection will close instead of completing.
bugs.workaround: Do not use a disabled server-ssl profile in this situation.
bugs.fix: The SSL::enable iRule works as expected in the above scenario.

bugs.title: /var/lib/mysql disk is full
bugs.symptoms: PRX.BRUTE_FORCE_* db tables do not have a row_limit, so they can grow to consume all available disk space in /var/lib/mysql.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: /var/lib/mysql can run out of disk space
bugs.workaround: 1. Truncate the two large tables. This clears all the row in those table and should make disk space. Note that existing brute force username and IPs reporting data will be lost. # mysql -u root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e "TRUNCATE TABLE PRX.BRUTE_FORCE_MITIGATED_USERNAMES" # mysql -u root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e "TRUNCATE TABLE PRX.BRUTE_FORCE_MITIGATED_IPS" 2. Add row_limit for the two tables to avoid the same issue in the future. Add following lines in the bottom of this file, /etc/ts/tools/clean_db.yaml PRX.BRUTE_FORCE_MITIGATED_USERNAMES: row_limit: 100000 order_by: brute_force_mitigated_username_id PRX.BRUTE_FORCE_MITIGATED_IPS: row_limit: 100000 order_by: brute_force_mitigated_ip_id Restart clean_db process (there is no impact of restarting this process) # pkill -f clean_db Wait 30 sec, and make sure the process came back # ps aux | grep clean_db
bugs.fix: ASM now processes matching signatures as expected.

bugs.title: Using broadcast or subnet address as self IP may cause interruption during config sync
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd daemon exits with -1 exit code, triggering restart of mcpd and some other system services. You might see messages in ltm.log: -- err mcpd[21618]: 0107142f:3: Can't connect to CMI peer 192.168.1.136, TMM outbound listener not yet created. -- err mcpd[21618]: 01070596:3: An unexpected failure has occurred, Cannot get route for dest 192.168.1.136 in rd0 Invalid entry type: 3 - net/validation/routing.cpp, line 1231, exiting.
bugs.conditions: -- Device has been configured to use a non-unicast address as its self IP. -- There are attempts to establish device trust with it.
bugs.impact: This triggers interruption during config sync on the device initiating the exchange. Restart of mcpd and other important system services may cause temporary interruption in device operation.
bugs.workaround: Do not use non-unicast addresses for self IP configuration.

bugs.title: State mirroring default does not require TLS
bugs.symptoms: By default, state mirroring information in an HA pair may not be protected while in transit between peers.
bugs.conditions: HA pair of BIG-IP systems. "statemirror.secure" db key set to "false"
bugs.impact: State mirroring data is not protected while in transit between peers.
bugs.workaround: Set the sys db variable "statemirror.secure" to true.
bugs.fix: statemirror.secure is set to "true" by default.
bugs.behavior: statemirror.secure is set to "true" by default

bugs.title: JWT token verification failure
bugs.symptoms: JSON Web Token (JWT) verification failure with error -1.
bugs.conditions: Token size larger than 4080.
bugs.impact: Request is rejected.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with JWT token verificaton.

bugs.title: IPS IM package version is inconsistent on slot if it was installed or loaded when a slot was offline.
bugs.symptoms: If the IPS IM package is installed on a multi-slot device, and one slot is offline, the IM package version might be different on the offline slot when it comes back online. It also shows different versions of the Active IM package on different slots.
bugs.conditions: -- Multi-bladed clustered system. -- One of the blades is offline. -- The IPS IM package is installed to the primary blade.
bugs.impact: The primary blade syncs the IM package to all of the secondary blades that are online; however, when the offline blade comes back online, it does not have the updated IM package. As a result, traffic being processed by different blades will be using different IPS libraries and might cause inconsistency in the functionality
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, you can prevent the issue by ensuring that all blades are online when you install an IPS IM package.

bugs.title: TMM may core in a rare condition serving an HTTP response
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes when HTTP server receives a POST request, it can serve a response prior the whole request payload is arrived. When a response is chunked in some occasions TMM may fail to process it correctly.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has a virtual server configured with HTTP profile. -- POST request is processing. -- A chunked response is served before the whole request is received. -- A Security Policy is applied to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM cores, failover condition occurs, and traffic processing can be interrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now properly handles early chunked responses and does not allow TMM to core for this reason.

bugs.title: Cloud Security Services do not apply current best practices
bugs.symptoms: The built-in endpoint configuration does not apply current best practices.
bugs.conditions: Default endpoint configuration.
bugs.impact: CSC do not apply current best practices.
bugs.fix: The built-in endpoint configuration now applies current best practices.

bugs.title: Enhance FIPS crypto-user storage
bugs.symptoms: Existing TMOS releases use legacy storage and generation facilities that have been supplanted in newer TMOS releases.
bugs.conditions: Crypto-officer access to TMSH / fipsutil.
bugs.impact: Sensitive crypto-user information was not secured properly
bugs.fix: FIPS crypto-user storage now uses proper security practices.

bugs.title: NTLM Auth may fail due to incorrect handling of EPM response
bugs.symptoms: NTLM passthrough authentication may stop working after upgrade.
bugs.conditions: -- NTLM authentication configured. -- Upgraded to a BIG-IP software version that contains the implementation for the Microsoft Internet Explorer feature, 'Enhanced protected mode' (EPM). -- There are more than two protocol sequence towers included in the EPM response.
bugs.impact: APM end users cannot login.
bugs.fix: The system can now parse EPM response as expected.

bugs.title: Notarize APM Clients to support macOS Catalina
bugs.symptoms: MacOS Catalina requires an installation package be notarized.
bugs.conditions: Installing EdgeClient on MacOS Catalina.
bugs.impact: EdgeClient cannot be installed on MacOS Catalina without notarization.

bugs.title: French language spelling error in BIG-IP Edge Client message window
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Edge Client message window contains spelling error while displaying in French language: En cour de Réinstallation du
bugs.conditions: Using the BIG-IP Edge Client in a French environment.
bugs.impact: The message should be: En cours de Réinstallation du

bugs.title: The WebUI incorrectly allows the dns64-prefix option found in DNS profiles to include a subnet mask.
bugs.symptoms: The input validation performed by the BIG-IP system WebUI incorrectly allows the dns64-prefix option found in DNS profiles to include a subnet mask. The WebUI should allow users to specify only a prefix (for example, 2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:0 or 2001:db8::); however, it incorrectly allows users to specify a subnet mask too (for example, 2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:0/96 or 2001:db8::/96). In contrast, the TMSH utility correctly enforces values for this option.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP Administrator creates or modifies a DNS profile using the WebUI, and specifies an IP/SM value for the dns64-prefix option.
bugs.impact: Upon performing DNS64, TMM returns incorrect DNS answers that do not use the specified prefix. For example, if the Administrator specifies 2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:0/96 as the prefix, and if the IPv4 address of the requested resource is 198.51.100.1, DNS64 returns ::198.51.100.1 instead of 2001:db8::c633:6401. This prevents end-user clients from reaching the intended resource. The impact described in this section only applies to BIG-IP versions 14.1.0 and later. Previous BIG-IP versions also had this WebUI validation issue, but despite this TMM still returned the correct DNS answer.
bugs.workaround: When configuring this option using the WebUI, do not specify a subnet mask.

bugs.title: The SNMPv3 engineBoots value restarts at 1 after an upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Many SNMPv3 clients pay attention to the engineBoots value as part of server authentication. When the BIG-IP system is upgraded, the engineBoots value is not retained, so it restarts at 1.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading a BIG-IP system whose engineBoots value is greater than 1.
bugs.impact: The engineBoots value is reset to 1. This may look like an error condition for the SNMPv3 client.
bugs.workaround: 1. Run the following command (where n = the value at which you want to start the engineBoots): tmsh modify sys snmp include 'engineBoots n' 2. Restart SNMPD.
bugs.fix: This issue has been fixed: the engineBoots value is now kept as part of the configuration.

bugs.title: Address list as source/destination for virtual server cannot be changed from tmsh
bugs.symptoms: Address list as source/destination for virtual server cannot be changed from tmsh as it is applicable from GUI.
bugs.conditions: For an address created in tmsh: # list security shared-objects address-list security shared-objects address-list testAddressList { addresses { 1.1.1.1/32 { } 2.2.2.2/32 { } } } There is no Address list option shown in virtual server config: # modify ltm virtual test source Configuration Items: [enter address or address/prefixlen] <==!!
bugs.impact: Address list as source/destination for virtual server cannot be changed from tmsh.
bugs.workaround: Use the GUI to make changes to the Address list as source/destination for virtual server.

bugs.title: Error: Media type is incompatible with other trunk members
bugs.symptoms: Loading system configuration is failing after upgrade with an error message 01070619:3: Interface 5.0 media type is incompatible with other trunk members
bugs.conditions: -- Trunk interface created in BIG-IP version 12.3.4. -- Trunk interfaces have different speeds (e.g. 100Mb interfaces and 1Gb interfaces) -- Load the configuration after upgrading from v12.1.3.4 to v12.1.3.5.
bugs.impact: The system configuration is failing to load.
bugs.workaround: If you encounter this error, manually fix all trunks to only use interfaces of the same speed, and then load the configuration.

bugs.title: VXLAN tunnel might fail due to misbehaving NIC checksum offload
bugs.symptoms: Some NICs, e.g., on BIG-IP 2000/4000 platforms, perform checksum offloading for UDP, and erroneously mark a 0 (zero) checksum as a checksum failure, even though the UDP header includes an optional, 16-bit one's complement checksum that provides an integrity check. If the computed checksum is 0, it is transmitted as all ones. In this case the NIC should accept the checksum, but it does not.
bugs.conditions: NIC offload checksum of 0.
bugs.impact: VXLAN tunnel fails.
bugs.fix: The VXLAN tunnel now ignores invalid checksums if the checksum is 0.

bugs.title: CSR subject fields with comma(,) are truncated during certificate renewal via the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: CSR subject fields getting truncated during certificate renewal via the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Certificate subject field contains comma(,) -- Renewing the certificate via the GUI.
bugs.impact: Invalid certificate signing requests are created. This may not be apparent until certificate validation occurs, or when the certificate authority denies the certificate signing request.
bugs.workaround: TMSH command line interface can be used to create the CSR when commas are present in subject field.

bugs.title: Prevent receive window shrinkage for looped flows that use a SYN cookie
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: -- VIP to VIP (looped flow) configuration. -- SYN cookie is used. -- Initial receive window is greater than 3.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: -- Set the initial receive window value of the VIP to 3.
bugs.fix: Receive window shrinkage is prevented for looped flows using SYN cookies.

bugs.title: Host traffic via IPv6 route pool uses incorrect source address
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 route pool uses an incorrect source address rather than the self IP address. As a side symptom, if there are an even number of members in the pool, only half of the pool members are attempted during load balancing.
bugs.conditions: --IPv6 route pool is configured.
bugs.impact: Failed connections from the BIG-IP host that uses an IPv6 pool route.
bugs.fix: IPv6 route pool uses the correct self IP address.

bugs.title: MCP update message may be lost when primary blade changes in chassis
bugs.symptoms: In a VIPRION chassis, when the Primary blade is disabled (intentionally or due to an unexpected loss of functionality) and a new Primary blade is selected, there is a brief window of time during which status messages forwarded from MCPD on a Secondary blade to MCPD on the Primary blade might be dropped, possibly resulting in an incorrect view of the state of configured objects.
bugs.conditions: This problem may occur under the following conditions: -- The state of a blade-local object/resources (such as a network interface or trunk) changes. -- There is a high load on MCPD (for example, due to configuration reload on the new Primary blade) which delays processing of some MCPD actions.
bugs.impact: This problem may result in the state of blade-local objects (such as interfaces or trunks) being seen and reported incorrectly across the blades in the chassis, or on one or more specific blades (Primary, Secondary) in the chassis. For example, if loss of the Primary blade results in one or more interfaces in a trunk being marked down by LACPD on a specific blade, resulting changes in trunk/member status may not be propagated correctly to the Primary blade, and from there to other Secondary blades.

bugs.title: Boot marker is being logged before shutdown logs
bugs.symptoms: When rebooting the BIG-IP, the boot marker appears before the shutdown logs localhost notice boot_marker : ---===[ HD1.1 - BIG-IP 14.1.2 Build 0.0.37 ]===--- localhost.localdomain err logger[29153]: shutting down for system shutdown on behalf of root localhost.localdomain notice mcpd[4645]: 01070406:5: Removed publication with publisher id shell_publish
bugs.conditions: Issue is observed while rebooting the device
bugs.impact: Creates confusion when trying to debug an issue using log files.

bugs.title: When a SSL Orchestrator app is deployed, tmm errors are logged in /var/log/apm
bugs.symptoms: If you deploy a layer 3 outbound or inbound app, the deployment will go fine but some errors will be logged in /var/log/apm: err tmm[21184]: 0187005b:3: Access Policy(/Common/ssloP_myTest01.app/ssloP_myTest01_per_req_policy) update: Customization group set can be only assigned to Access policy of type per-request or api-protection notice tmm3[21184]: 01490562:5: /Common/sslo_myTest01.app/sslo_myTest01_end_allow_ag: /Common/sslo_myTest01.app/sslo_myTest01_end_allow agent update can not be resolved.
bugs.conditions: Provision SSL Orchestrator, deploy l3 outbound or l3 inbound
bugs.impact: The app deploys successfully, but you will see some ambiguous errors in the log. These log messages can be ignored.
bugs.fix: Add new condition check, if access policy type is SSL Orchestrator policy, access-per-request cgs wrong assign exception will not be printed in log.

bugs.title: TMM crash due to failed assertion "sp->slab_cache == ((umem_cache_t *)(((char *)(&(ccp)[-((ccp)->cc_td)])) - __builtin_offsetof(umem_cache_t, cache_cpu)))"
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: Exact conditions are not yet known. It is suspected it is related to using APM and/or SAML authentication protocol.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Reconnection timeout values for the CMI channel differs between versions 12.1.x and 14.1.x
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP devices are part of a device group they are connected. This connection is called the 'CMI channel'. If network disruptions occur, the connection is re-established. The timeout intervals for reconnecting are not consistent among all releases of BIG-IP software.
bugs.conditions: -- When the CMI channel goes down and is reconnecting. -- Comparing the intervals in 12.1.x with those in 14.1.x.
bugs.impact: The timeout interval may not be the expected length of 5 seconds or 12 seconds, or another value. The behavior of the reconnection does not match documented behavior in K13946: Troubleshooting ConfigSync and device service clustering issues :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13946.

bugs.title: HSB transmit lockup on i4600
bugs.symptoms: TMM shows HSB transmit lockup message and cored.
bugs.conditions: -- Using an i4600 platform. -- Other conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Disruption to processing traffic on the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: TMM may crash running remote tcpdump
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- Tcpdump is run with the --remote-dest parameter. -- The destination address is routed via a VLAN, whose cmp-hash setting has been changed from default to src-ip.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not route remote tcpdump operations via a VLAN with non-default cmp-hash settings.
bugs.fix: Remote tcpdump now works via VLANs with any cmp-hash setting.

bugs.title: JWT token verification failure
bugs.symptoms: JWT token verification failure with error -1.
bugs.conditions: Token size larger than 4080.
bugs.impact: Request rejected and the log message simply says 'unknown error -1.'
bugs.fix: The 4080 token size limitation is removed.

bugs.title: In rare cases tmm crash is observed when using APM as RDG proxy.
bugs.symptoms: Tmm may crash when APM is configured as an RDG proxy to access Microsoft remote desktops and applications.
bugs.conditions: APM is used as RDG proxy
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmm does not crash when APM is configured as RDG proxy.

bugs.title: Changing a UDP virtual server with an immediate timeout to a TCP virtual server can cause connections to fail
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system sends a TCP SYN to the back-end server, but ignores the server's SYN-ACK response.
bugs.conditions: A virtual server that contains a UDP profile with idle-timeout immediate is modified to replace the UDP profiles with TCP profiles.
bugs.impact: Connections from the BIG-IP system to backend servers fails.
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the virtual server.

bugs.title: IPv6 Management route is preferred over IPv6 tmm route
bugs.symptoms: The IPv6 Management route has lower metrics than the static IPv6 tmm route. As a result, traffic that matches the default route goes to the management interface.
bugs.conditions: -- Create an IPv6 management route, which is going to be a default gateway. -- Receive another default gateway from a configured peer using any of dynamic routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, etc.)
bugs.impact: The incorrect routing table sends the traffic that matches the default route to the management interface.
bugs.fix: IPv6 routes now prioritize TMM interfaces.

bugs.title: User shouldn't be able to configure two identical traffic selectors
bugs.symptoms: Config load fails by issuing "tmsh load sys config verify" 01070734:3: Configuration error: Duplicate traffic selector is not allowed Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Duplicate IP addresses on multiple traffic-selectors attached to different ipsec-policies.
bugs.impact: Config load will fail after a reboot
bugs.workaround: Delete duplicate traffic-selectors.

bugs.title: APM OAuth - Auth Server attached iRule works inconsistently
bugs.symptoms: The iRule attached to the OAuth Resource Server (RS) is not triggered when the traffic hits the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs during a reboot of the BIG-IP device containing an OAuth server config and an attached iRule, or when the iRule is initially assigned to the OAuth Server.
bugs.impact: OAuth scope check agent fails with 'HTTP error 503': as the iRule attached to the RS virtual server is not triggered.
bugs.workaround: For existing OAuth servers with the iRule attached, modify the iRule, for example, adding a log. This makes the iRule trigger when it is initially attached or loaded.
bugs.fix: The iRule is triggered when a request comes to the OAuth RS virtual server.

bugs.title: Incomplete response to an internal request by Portal Access
bugs.symptoms: HTTP request to /private/fm/volatile.html may return a truncated response.
bugs.conditions: - Portal Access configured for some resource - The resource uses cookies
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly
bugs.fix: Now Portal Access handles internal requests correctly.

bugs.title: Display of Certificate Subject Alternative Name (SAN) limited to 1023 characters
bugs.symptoms: Certificate Subject Alternative Names are limited to 1023 characters.
bugs.conditions: Using a certificate with a Subject Alternative Name longer than 1023 characters.
bugs.impact: A certificate's Subject Alternative Name is not correct in the BIG-IP configuration. This does not impact the BIG-IP system's ability to select the proper Client SSL profile on a virtual server that uses SNI matching to provide distinct certificates.
bugs.workaround: Specify fewer than 1023 character for the Certificate Subject Alternative Names.

bugs.title: Unable to successfully deploy BIG-IP 15.0.0 on Nutanix AHV Hypervisor
bugs.symptoms: In the deployment of BIG-IP 15.0.0 on Nutanix AHV Hypervisor, f5-label service is failing with inappropriate input device error.
bugs.conditions: Deployment of BIG-IP v15.0.0 on Nutanix AHV Hypervisor.
bugs.impact: Deployment of BIG-IP v15.0.0 is not stable to log into GUI or terminal on Nutanix AHV Hypervisor.
bugs.workaround: Steps: 1. Mount the drive: mount -o rw,remount /usr 2. Add a comment below the line in the '/usr/lib/systemd/system/f5-label.service' service file: #StandardInput=tty 3. Reload the daemon: systemctl daemon-reload 4. Restart the service: systemctl restart f5-label
bugs.fix: The I/O device has been changed to the default input device '/dev/null' to resolve the issue.

bugs.title: Some systems can experience periodic high IO wait due to AVR data aggregation
bugs.symptoms: Systems with a large amount of statistics data collected in the local database (i.e., systems not working with BIG-IQ) can have high IO Wait CPU usage, peaking at 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 24 hours. This is caused by the data aggregation process that is running on the local database. Notice that large memory footprints, particularly for avrd might be a symptom for the phenomenon.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is collecting statistics locally (i.e., not sending data to BIG-IQ or another external device). -- There is a large amount of statistics data. -- May occur even if AVR is not explicitly provisioned.
bugs.impact: High IO can impact various processes on BIG-IP systems. Some of them can experience timeouts and might restart.
bugs.workaround: The most effective workaround is to lower the amount of data collected by setting the 'avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable' DB variable to a lower value. The recommended values are 20000 (on larger, more powerful systems with more than 16 cores) or 2148 (on smaller systems). Note: After you lower the database value, continue to monitor the BIG-IP system for long I/O wait times and high CPU usage. If symptoms persist and the system continues to experience resource issues, you may need to reset the BIG-IP AVR statistics. For information about resetting BIG-IP AVR statistics, refer to K14956: Resetting BIG-IP AVR statistics :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14956.
bugs.fix: Set default value of avr.stats.internal.maxentitiespertable DB variable to 20000. Set it to 2148 on systems with fewer than or equal to CPU 16 cores.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not account a presence of http2 profile when response payload is modified
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system might close a connection when the HTTP response payload is modified and sent without chunking encoding. If communication goes over an HTTP connection, the BIG-IP system closes a connection to tell a client that a response is served. With HTTP/2 connections, an unsized response is marked with the END_STREAM flag. This case is not accounted for, and the BIG-IP system closes HTTP communication with a server anyway.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server has an http/2 profile configured on the client side. -- There are other profiles configured which can modify the HTTP response payload.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system wastes resources not reusing a server side HTTP connection when an unsized response is sent over an HTTP/2 connection to a client.

bugs.title: Adding multiple user-defined Signatures via REST in quick succession may end with duplicate key database error
bugs.symptoms: Adding multiple user-defined Signatures via REST in quick succession may end with duplicate key database error.
bugs.conditions: At least two REST calls adding Attack Signatures and/or Attack Signature Sets which are sent in quick succession to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: REST calls after the first may not be successful, resulting in failure to modify configuration as desired.
bugs.workaround: Retry the subsequent REST calls.

bugs.title: State mirroring default does not require TLS
bugs.symptoms: By default, state mirroring information in an HA pair may not be protected while in transit between peers.
bugs.conditions: HA pair of BIG-IP systems. "statemirror.secure" db key set to "false". No profiles or virtuals having session-mirroring or connection mirroring with ssl enabled.
bugs.impact: State mirroring data is not protected while in transit between peers.
bugs.workaround: Set the sys db variable "statemirror.secure" to true.
bugs.fix: Ensure no sensitive data is mirrored unless the HA peer connection is secure.

bugs.title: State mirroring default does not require TLS
bugs.symptoms: By default, state mirroring information in an HA pair may not be protected while in transit between peers.
bugs.conditions: HA pair of BIG-IP systems. "statemirror.secure" db key set to "false". No profiles or virtuals having session-mirroring or connection mirroring with ssl enabled.
bugs.impact: State mirroring data is not protected while in transit between peers.
bugs.workaround: Set the sys db variable "statemirror.secure" to true.
bugs.fix: Ensure no sensitive data is mirrored unless the HA peer connection is secure.

bugs.title: REST system unavailable due to disk corruption
bugs.symptoms: -- The iControl REST commands respond with the following: [INFO] Text: u'{"code":200,"message":"REST system unavailable due to disk corruption! See /var/log/restjavad.*.log for errors.","restOperationId":1472895,"kind":":resterrorresponse"}' -- The GUI indicates that iAppLX sub-system is unresponsive. -- On the BIG-IP device, /var/config/rest/storage/LOST-STORAGE.txt exists.
bugs.conditions: The conditions that trigger this are unknown. It might be due to a previous catastrophic event such as power loss or out-of-memory errors. Manually creating the file /var/config/rest/storage/LOST-STORAGE.txt can also trigger this error.
bugs.impact: The iControl REST system is unavailable.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands at the BIG-IP command prompt: bigstart stop restjavad restnoded rm -rf /var/config/rest/storage rm -rf /var/config/rest/index bigstart start restjavad restnoded rm -f /var/config/rest/downloads/*.rpm rm -f /var/config/rest/iapps/RPMS/*.rpm tmsh restart sys service tomcat Then, reinstall any iAppLX packages that were installed.
