bugs.title: A Large /config folder can cause memory exhaustion during live-install
bugs.symptoms: - live install can fail at around 96% - system memory can be exhausted and the kernel will kill processes as a result.
bugs.conditions: During live-install, if configuration roll-forward is enabled, and the uncompressed ucs size is larger than the available memory.
bugs.impact: The kernel will kill any number of processes; any/all critical applications could become non-functional.
bugs.workaround: Make sure there are no un-intended large files included in the configuration. Any file stored under /config is considered part of the configuration. If the configuration is, as intended, on the same order of magnitude as total system memory, do not roll it forward as part of live install. Instead, save it manually and restore it after rebooting to the new software. to turn off config roll forward; setdb liveinstall.saveconfig disable to save/restore configuration manually; see https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13132

bugs.title: Memory leak in icrd_child due to concurrent REST usage
bugs.symptoms: When multiple users are issuing REST commands, memory may leak slowly in icrd_child.
bugs.conditions: -- The icrd_child process is running. -- There are multiple users accessing device via REST.
bugs.impact: Memory slowly leaks in icrd_child.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory leak in icrd_child.

bugs.title: Memory leak due to session context not freed
bugs.symptoms: Memory increases slowly
bugs.conditions: A PEM iRule times out
bugs.impact: Memory could be exhausted depending on the frequency of the command timeouts

bugs.title: Possible TMM crash with a multi-IP PEM subscriber configured with more than 16 IP addresses
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: PEM configured with a multi-IP subscriber with more than 16 IP addresses.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not create a PEM subscriber with more than 16 IP addresses.

bugs.title: TCP connection fails to establish when an SFC policy is enabled
bugs.symptoms: TCP Connections fail to establish. Data transfer does not happen.
bugs.conditions: -- SFC chain is configured on the system. -- The configured SFC chain contains legacy servers (non-SFC) as part of the chain. -- A source port changes from one hop of the SFC chain to next hop.
bugs.impact: TCP Connections fail to establish. Data transfer does not happen.

bugs.title: .tmp files in /var/config/rest/ may cause /var directory exhaustion
bugs.symptoms: The /var partition might become completely full on the disk due to tmp files being written to /var/config/rest. This condition may be accompanied by console error messages similar to the following: 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var (slot #) has only 0% free on secondary blade. Additionally, there may be periodic restjavad and bigd daemon restarts related to disk space exhaustion.
bugs.conditions: Process traffic while DoS Dashboard is open. This issue is happening because a VIPRION process is not available because of a REST timeout.
bugs.impact: The partition housing /var/config/rest may become 100% full, impacting future disk IO to the partition.
bugs.workaround: Manually run the following commands, in sequence: bigstart stop restjavad rm -rf /var/config/rest/*.tmp bigstart start restjavad
bugs.fix: Increased the rest socket timeout value and shellexecutor timeout value to 6 min to fix the timeout issue of viprion worker ﻿The fix also includes automatic removal of unused tmp files.

bugs.title: Mcpd may miss its high availability (HA) heartbeat if a very large amount of pool members are configured
bugs.symptoms: If a very large amount of pool members are configured (tens of thousands), mcpd may miss its high availability (HA) heartbeat and be killed by sod.
bugs.conditions: -- A large number of pool members. -- Pool member validation occurs (such as when loading a configuration or doing a configsync operation).
bugs.impact: Mcpd is killed by sod. This causes a failover (when the BIG-IP is in a DSC) or outage (if standalone).

bugs.title: iApp UI broken when referencing to iApp profile /Common/_sys_radius_proto_imsi
bugs.symptoms: When deploying a custom iApp template, the GUI says "An error has occurred while trying to process your request"
bugs.conditions: A custom iApp template is deployed that is derived from _sys_radius_proto_imsi
bugs.impact: UI display is impacted for the affected iApp.

bugs.title: Invalid opcode: kernel BUG at mm/shmem.c:556!
bugs.symptoms: A blade reboots due to a kernel panic with the following message: crit kernel: kernel BUG at mm/shmem.c:556!
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that trigger this are unknown.
bugs.impact: Kernel panic followed by blade reboot.

bugs.title: AVRD may core when restarting due to data collection device connection timeout
bugs.symptoms: Avrd crashes, one or more core avrd files exist in /var/core
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system is managed by BIG-IQ via secure channel -- Avrd is restarted.
bugs.impact: Avrd cores as it is shutting down. During avrd shutdown, the BIG-IQ data collection device (DCD) is unreachable for 10 minutes
bugs.fix: The AVRD HTTPS module now stops any connection attempts when shutdown sequence is in progress, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: FPS does not serve configuration script in gzip format
bugs.symptoms: When FPS is attached to a virtual server with http-compression profile, website page loading occasionally hangs.
bugs.conditions: -- http-compression profile is attached to FPS virtual server. -- The compression profile is configured to compress js files (this is the default).
bugs.impact: Site loads slowly / hangs, or appears to hang.
bugs.workaround: Exclude 'JavaScript Configuration Directory' from http-compression profiles.

bugs.title: False positives Mismatched message key on ASM TS cookie
bugs.symptoms: ASM system triggers false positives for ASM Cookie Hijacking violation with reason "Mismatched message key"
bugs.conditions: -- An HTTP request containing an old frame cookie with a different message key from the main ts cookie is rejected -- The cookie is left intact
bugs.impact: All subsequent requests are rejected on ASM Cookie Hijacking violation
bugs.workaround: 1. Disable "Learn Host Names" flag all policies. If the policy builder is on manual mode, they need to change it back to Auto mode, disable "Learn Host Names", then change to manual mode. OR 2. Delete the mismatched cookie. This will cause the violations to stop occurring if the request comes from a legit endpoint
bugs.fix: In order to activate the changed functionality, set internal parameter ignore_cookies_msg_key to 1 and restart asm by executing following commands in CLI: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ignore_cookies_msg_key 1 bigstart restart asm Once enabled, ASM system does not trigger false positives.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing TCP traffic with iRules
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing TCP traffic with iRules
bugs.conditions: iRule with FLOW_INIT event TCP connection
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes TCP traffic with iRules as expected.

bugs.title: Intermittent Virtual Edition deployment failure due to inability to access the ssh host key in Azure
bugs.symptoms: Deployment of BIG-IP Virtual Edition may result in an error "Failed to generate ssh host key".
bugs.conditions: Azure only. Observed for instances with password-based authentication.
bugs.impact: A timing issues exists with host key generation. The Virtual Machine is likely to be deployed, but users and automation tools might be unable to communicate with the instance.
bugs.workaround: BIG-IP may still be accessible despite the error.

bugs.title: SSL TMUI hardening
bugs.symptoms: The SSL TMUI does not implement current best practices.
bugs.conditions: -Authenticated administrative user accessing SSL TMUI
bugs.impact: The SSL TMUI does not implement current best practices.
bugs.fix: The SSL TMUI now implements current best practices.

bugs.title: Appdata logical volume cannot be resized for some cloud images
bugs.symptoms: When resizing the appdata logical volume, the change may not be honored. This is because sometimes the disk metadata does not support the change without unmounting and remounting the disk.
bugs.conditions: This issue applies to deployments that provision multiple modules requiring a large appdata logical volume.
bugs.impact: The appdata logical volume cannot be resized, so you must reduce the number of modules and the associated provisioning level so that the existing appdata logical volume size does support them.
bugs.fix: Logic was added to disk resizing to account for scenarios where the disk must be unmounted and then remounted to make the change. If the disk must be unmounted and remounted, this also requires a reboot (automatic).

bugs.title: Standby high availability (HA) device passes traffic through virtual wire
bugs.symptoms: Virtual wire is forwarding traffic on standby resulting in traffic loops and potential network outage.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) configured. -- Virtual wire configured.
bugs.impact: Standby device is passing traffic, which may create traffic loops and bring down the network.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure virtual wire on standby devices.
bugs.fix: Although you can create this configuration, the standby no longer forwards any traffic, which prevents the traffic loop and potential network outage.

bugs.title: HTTP PSM blocking resets should have better log messages
bugs.symptoms: When reset-cause logging is turned on, or when RST packet logging is used, the reset reason used when rejecting bad HTTP PSM traffic is not descriptive.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under either of these conditions: -- HTTP PSM is used, and a request is blocked. -- Reset cause or RST packet logging is enabled.
bugs.impact: The reset reason given is not descriptive, making troubleshooting difficult.
bugs.fix: The reset reason used when rejecting HTTP PSM traffic is more descriptive.

bugs.title: Session timeout in diadb entry is updated to 180 on unsuccessful transaction
bugs.symptoms: Diameter MRF persist records are not deleted at session timeout.
bugs.conditions: -- Diameter MRF in use -- An unsuccessful CCR transaction occurs
bugs.impact: Unsuccessful transaction attempts do not time out and remain in the session database.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be used to reset session timeout in diadb upon an unsuccessful transaction through MR_FAILED by executing DIAMETER::persist reset.

bugs.title: An iRule before HTTP_REQUEST calling persist none can crash tmm
bugs.symptoms: During an iRule event before HTTP_RQUEST, e.g. on FLOW_INIT/CLIENT_ACCEPTED disabling persistence with 'persist none' can crash tmm.
bugs.conditions: An iRule event before HTTP_RQUEST, e.g., on FLOW_INIT/CLIENT_ACCEPTED disabling persistence with 'persist none'.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash.

bugs.title: SNMP address-related GET requests slow to respond.
bugs.symptoms: SNMP get requests for ipAddr, ipAddress, ipAddressPrefix and ipNetToPhysical are slow to respond.
bugs.conditions: Using SNMP get requests for ipAddr, ipAddress, ipAddressPrefix and ipNetToPhysical.
bugs.impact: Slow performance.

bugs.title: HTTP PSM detects more issues with Transfer-Encoding headers
bugs.symptoms: HTTP PSM may not detect some invalid Transfer-Encoding headers.
bugs.conditions: HTTP PSM is used to detect HTTP RFC violations. A request with an invalid Transfer-Encoding header is sent.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not alarmed/blocked as expected.
bugs.fix: HTTP PSM detects new cases of invalid Transfer-Encoding headers.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when Network Access tunnel is used
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: -- APM session is established. -- Network Access tunnel is established and used;
bugs.impact: APM end users experience Network Access tunnel disconnected. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: This release fixes a tmm crash.

bugs.title: Marketing name does not display properly for BIG-IP i10010 (C127)
bugs.symptoms: The /var/log/ltm log includes error messages about the marketing names errors: Invalid marketing name.
bugs.conditions: -- Running BIG-IP software version 13.1.3.1. -- Using BIG-IP i10010 (C127) platform.
bugs.impact: This causes errors in the logs, and affects the tmsh and LCD displays. The LCD displays C127 for the Platform Name instead of the actual platform name. The TMSH command, tmsh show sys hw, displays C127 for the Platform Name instead of the actual platform name.
bugs.fix: This is fixed in version 13.1.3.2.

bugs.title: ASMConfig Handler undergoes frequent restarts
bugs.symptoms: Under some settings and load the RPC handler for the Policy Builder process restarts frequently, causing unnecessary churn and slower learning performance.
bugs.conditions: Configure one or more policies with automatic policy building enabled and learn traffic with violations
bugs.impact: Control Plane instability and poor learning performance on the device.
bugs.fix: The Policy Builder handler is now restored to a more robust process lifecycle.

bugs.title: Upgrading EUD in certain conditions may lead to missing software volumes
bugs.symptoms: -- Software volumes no longer appear in the grub menu after reboot and are not available to boot into. -- Software volumes no longer reported by 'tmsh show sys software' if further upgrades are made.
bugs.conditions: You may encounter this issue in the following scenario: -- You install an EUD package. -- You previously booted into a slot running v13.1.x or later. -- You downgraded to a pre-v13.1.x to perform the EUD installation.
bugs.impact: Loss of software volumes.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to install the EUD package from the v13.1.x (multiboot software) volume or before installing EUD from v12.1.x (non-multiboot software). 1. Boot into the multiboot software volume (this syncs the grub.multiboot.cfg file and the legacy grub cfg file). 2. Boot back to 12.1.x (non-multiboot software) and install the EUD.

bugs.title: Memory Leak when using Ping Access profile
bugs.symptoms: The memory usage by pingaccess keeps going up when sending request with expired session cookie to a virtual server with PingAccess Profile.
bugs.conditions: 1. BIG-IP virtual server that contains PingAccess Profile. 2. Request sent with expired session cookie.
bugs.impact: Memory leak occurs in which ping access memory usage increases.
bugs.fix: Fixed a memory link with the Ping Access profile.

bugs.title: Tmm crash in Ping access use case
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: Ping access use case.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Properly handle ping traffic.

bugs.title: AD Query and LDAP Auth/Query fails with IPv6 server address in Direct mode
bugs.symptoms: Both AD Query and LDAP Auth/Query fails.
bugs.conditions: -- AD Query Agent, LDAP Auth Agent, or LDAP Query Agent is configured in Per-Session or Per-Request Policy. -- These agents are configured in Direct mode. -- The AD and LDAP server address is configured as IPv6 address.
bugs.impact: Users may not be able to login to APM, and hence service is disrupted.
bugs.fix: Users are now able to login to APM.

bugs.title: Improve handling of HTTP/2 GOAWAY frame
bugs.symptoms: After an HTTP/2 transaction, HTTP/2 'Out Of Memory Error"' stat 'Goaway reason' is incremented even though no GOAWAY frames were sent.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 configured on the client side and server side. - HTTPROUTER configured.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 stats incorrectly imply that GOAWAY frames are sent due to memory issues.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 GOAWAY frame handling is improved.

bugs.title: Corrupted DAG packets causes bcm56xxd core on VCMP host
bugs.symptoms: On VCMP host, bcm56xxd crashes when it receives a corrupted DAG packets.
bugs.conditions: Unknown.
bugs.impact: Device goes offline, traffic disruption.

bugs.title: Port lockdown settings may not be enforced as configured
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions port lockdown settings may not be enforced as configured.
bugs.conditions: -Virtual Edition. -Virtual server with http explicit proxy enabled.
bugs.impact: Port lockdown settings not enforced as configured.
bugs.fix: Port lockdown settings are now enforced as configured.

bugs.title: Port lockdown settings may not be enforced as configured
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions port lockdown settings may not be enforced as configured.
bugs.conditions: -Virtual Edition. -Virtual server with http explicit proxy enabled.
bugs.impact: Port lockdown settings not enforced as configured.
bugs.fix: Port lockdown settings are now enforced as configured.

bugs.title: In-TMM monitors fail to match certain binary data in the response from the server
bugs.symptoms: Pool members are incorrectly marked DOWN by a monitor. The pool members send the expected response to the probe, but the BIG-IP system marks them DOWN.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - In-TMM monitoring is enabled on the system (the 'bigd.tmm' db key is set to 'enable'; note this is set to 'disable' by default). - One or more TCP or HTTP monitors specify a receive string using HEX encoding, in order to match binary data in the server's response. - Depending on the HEX values specified (currently values in the range of 0x80-0xBF are believed to be affected), response matching fails.
bugs.impact: Objects that are meant to be marked UP are marked DOWN. As a result, no load balancing occurs to affected resources.
bugs.workaround: Either one of the following workarounds can be used: - Disable in-TMM monitoring by setting 'bigd.tmm' to 'disable'. - Do not monitor the application through a binary response (if the application allows it).
bugs.fix: The monitor finds the recv string and shows the pool or member as available.

bugs.title: Crash due to incorrect format specifiers is fixed.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes
bugs.conditions: This is handled internally in the code. Currently, the scenario is not possible, and the existing logic ensures that this issue is not triggered.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Corrected the format specifiers in the affected log statement to align with the actual data types being passed. This fix prevents potential TMM crashes.

bugs.title: ASU cannot be completed after Signature Systems database corruption following binary Policy import
bugs.symptoms: Signatures cannot be updated after signature systems have become corrupted in the configuration database, after a binary policy containing a user-defined Signature Set using an unknown System was imported.
bugs.conditions: Signature systems are corrupted in configuration database, because a binary policy containing a user-defined Signature Set using an unknown System was imported.
bugs.impact: Signatures cannot be updated.
bugs.workaround: Delete signature systems with an ID greater than 38, and re-add them by performing a signature update. You can delete these signature systems by running the following command: mysql -u root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e "DELETE FROM PLC.NEGSIG_SYSTEMS WHERE system_group = ''"

bugs.title: The iRule regexp command issues an incorrect warning
bugs.symptoms: At validation time, mcpd issues a warning similar to the following: warning mcpd[7175]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : /Common/test1:2: warning: ["＼1" has no meaning. Did you mean "＼＼1" or "1"?][{(test) (＼1)}]
bugs.conditions: Use arguments such as "＼1", "＼2", "＼3" etc., in command regexp.
bugs.impact: A warning is generated, "＼1" has no meaning, even though it is valid.
bugs.workaround: Ignore the warning.

bugs.title: APM end-user connection reset
bugs.symptoms: When the URL being accessed exceeds a length of 8 KB, the BIG-IP resets the connection.
bugs.conditions: -- APM deployed with a per-request policy. -- The per-request policy includes a category lookup.
bugs.impact: The APM end-user connection is reset, and the system posts an error message in /var/log/apm: -- crit tmm[23363]: 01790601:2: [C] 10.62.118.27:65343 -> 65.5.55.254:443: Maximum URL size exceeded.
bugs.fix: The URL length limit has been increased from 8 KB to 32 KB.

bugs.title: Azure scan table warnings can be ignored.
bugs.symptoms: When running BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in the Azure cloud environment, you may see warnings in daemon and user log files: -- warning: tm_install::DosPtable::scan_table -- identification of /dev/sdb1 failed; ID is 7. -- warning: tm_install::DosPtable::scan_table -- identification of /dev/sdb1 failed; ID is 7. This warning is due to installer code that expects to be running on official F5 hardware. This warning can be ignored.
bugs.conditions: This warning may be seen when running BIG-IP VE in the Azure cloud environment.
bugs.impact: These are benigh warning messages that can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: Default provisioning for all instances is LTM nominal
bugs.symptoms: Prior to configuring an AWS WAF (AWAF) PAYG cloud instance, you may see errors related to an unlicensed LTM module. This occurs because the default provisioning for all instances is LTM nominal. However, the license associated with an AWAF PAYG cloud instance does not enable the LTM feature. As a result, the default provisioning for an unconfigured AWAF PAYG cloud instance will be incompatible with the PAYG license.
bugs.conditions: -- This issue relates only to AWAF PAYG cloud instances. -- Not using the onboarding/templates to configure/provision the instance prior to use.
bugs.impact: Licensing error messages may be observed before the AWAF cloud instance is configured/provisioned. The functionality works as expected, however, so you can ignore these messages.
bugs.workaround: The recommended workflow for all cloud instances is to use onboarding/templates to configure/provision the instance prior to use. If this workflow is followed, any provisioning errors associated with the default provisioning are cleared prior to usage.

bugs.title: The version of open-vm-tools included with BIG-IP Virtual Edition is 10.0.5
bugs.symptoms: Features supported in newer versions of open-vm-tools will not be available.
bugs.conditions: This issue may be seen when running in VMware environments.
bugs.impact: Features that require a later version of open-vm-tools will not be available.
bugs.fix: The version of open-vm-tools has been updated to 10.1.5.

bugs.title: AVR should make sure file permissions are correct (tmstat_tables.xml)
bugs.symptoms: By building rpm of avrd, few cfg files get wrong set of permissions (executable)
bugs.conditions: Any build of avrd rpm
bugs.impact: Apparently not having the right set of permissions can lead to system half
bugs.workaround: Change permissions on file: # chmod -x /etc/avr/tmstat_tables.xml
bugs.fix: AVR build the rpm cfg files with the right set of permissions, instead of building them as executable file, building them in 644 mode.

bugs.title: Support ID on AJAX CAPTCHA popup (SPA) does not match the Support ID in log
bugs.symptoms: The Support ID shown to the ASM end user does not appear in the logs.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Bot Defense profile attached to a virtual server. -- Single Page Application (SPA) is enabled in the Bot Defense profile. -- AJAX request is blocked by bot defense, and CAPTCHA is shown to the ASM end user.
bugs.impact: ASM end user might complain about CAPTCHA and provide their Support ID to the BIG-IP administrator, but the BIG-IP administrator will not be able to find the Support ID in the logs.
bugs.fix: Bot defense has been fixed so that the Support ID shown to the ASM end user matches the Support ID in the logs.

bugs.title: F5 Endpoint Inspection helper app is not updated
bugs.symptoms: F5 Endpoint Inspection helper app is not updated, but other components such as F5 VPN helper App is auto updated.
bugs.conditions: Use a browser to establish VPN
bugs.impact: End users cannot to receive bug fixe or feature enhancement updates.
bugs.workaround: Download and install F5 Endpoint Inspection helper from BIG-IP. https://APM_SERVER/public/download/f5epi_setup.exe
bugs.fix: F5 Endpoint Inspection helper app is auto updated.

bugs.title: Self-IP hardening
bugs.symptoms: Self-IP handling for IPv6 link-local addresses does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: Self-IP with IPv6 link-local address.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP does not implement current best practices for IPv6 link-local addresses.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now implements current best practices for IPv6 link-local addresses.

bugs.title: Category lookup tool in GUI may not match actual traffic categorization
bugs.symptoms: Category Lookup agent has changed to include the IP in the categorization query. The BIG-IP TMUI does not do the same (Access Policy :: Secure Web Gateway : Database Settings : URL Category Lookup).
bugs.conditions: -- SWG or URLDB provisioned. -- Run traffic with category lookup in the PRP and note the category produced. -- Run the same URL through the GUI lookup tool or the command line tool.
bugs.impact: Some websites may be categorized differently depending on if the IP address is passed in or not.

bugs.title: Avrd core when sending large messages via https
bugs.symptoms: When sending large messages (>4KB) via HTTPs may cause avrd to core.
bugs.conditions: This typically happens when BIG-IP is managed by BIG-IQ and configuration is large and complex or traffic capturing is enabled.
bugs.impact: Messages to BIG-IQ are lost. In severe cases, analytics functionality may be unavailable due contiguous AVRD cores.
bugs.fix: Fixed an avrd crash

bugs.title: SFP interfaces are flapping on 2xxx/4xxx on version 15.0.x
bugs.symptoms: SFP interfaces start flapping immediately after booting up 2xxx/4xxx platforms, and it takes some time to goes into an up/running state.
bugs.conditions: Happens on the following platforms with BIG-IP 15.0.x using the SFP interface: 2000s/2200v 4000s/4400v
bugs.impact: Interface are unusable until it stops flapping and goes into an up/running state.
bugs.workaround: There is no known mitigation except to wait for the interface to go into the up/running state.
bugs.fix: Enough time is provided for the SFP interface to complete initialization and go into the up/running state.

bugs.title: Conditional requests are served incorrectly with AAM policy in webacceleration profile
bugs.symptoms: HTTP 1.1 allows a conditional request with header If-Modified-Since or If-Unmodified-Since to determine whether a resource changed since a specified date and time. If AAM is provisioned and its policy is assigned to a virtual server, it may incorrectly respond with 304 Not Modified, even after the resource was updated.
bugs.conditions: -- AAM is provisioned and webacceleration policy is attached to a virtual server. -- Client sends a conditional request with If-Modified-Since or If-Unmodified-Since header. -- The BIG-IP system responds from AAM cache.
bugs.impact: Client does not receive an updated resource.
bugs.workaround: Use webacceleration profile without AAM policy for resources that require conditional checks falling back into Ramcache.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now respects If-Modified-Since or If-Unmodified-Since header and provides an appropriate response for the requested resource when compared to the date supplied in either header.

bugs.title: Idle async handlers can remain loaded for a long time doing nothing
bugs.symptoms: Idle async handlers can remain loaded for a long time doing nothing because they do not have an idle timer. The sum of such idle async handlers can add unnecessary memory pressure.
bugs.conditions: This issue might result from several sets of conditions. Here is one: Exporting a large XML ASM policy and then leaving the BIG-IP system idle. The relevant asm_config_server handler process increases its memory consumption and remains that way, holding on to the memory until it is released with a restart.
bugs.impact: Depletion of memory by lingering idle async handlers may deprive other processes of sufficient memory, triggering out-of-memory conditions and process failures.
bugs.workaround: -- Restart asm_config_server, to free up all the memory that is currently taken by all asm_config_server processes and to impose the new MaxMemorySize threshold: --------------- # pkill -f asm_config_server --------------- -- Restart asm_config_server periodically using cron, as idle handlers are soon created again.
bugs.fix: Idle async handlers now exit after 5 minutes of not receiving any new calls.

bugs.title: Some init-rwnd and client-mss combinations may result in sub-optimal advertised TCP window.
bugs.symptoms: Due to a known issue BIG-IP may advertise sub-optimal window size.
bugs.conditions: Result of (init-rwnd * client-mss) is greater than maximum window size (65,535).
bugs.impact: Degraded TCP performance.
bugs.workaround: Do not use init-rwnd values that might result in values higher than maximum window size (65,535). Assuming MSS of 1480, the maximum value of init-rwnd is: 65535/1480 = 44.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic.
bugs.conditions: A virtual with standard HTTP profile is configured.
bugs.impact: When TMM crashes it causes a failover event and may interrupt traffic processing.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Possible handshake failure with TLS 1.3 early data
bugs.symptoms: During TLS 1.3 early data handshake, a code alert and handshake failure may occur
bugs.conditions: TLS 1.3 with early data resumption.
bugs.impact: Handshake failure.
bugs.workaround: Turn off early data.
bugs.fix: Fixes a possible TLS 1.3 early data handshake failure and code alert.

bugs.title: Unable to upload swagger files with a pattern in description
bugs.symptoms: While uploading a swagger file, you get an error: java.net.ProtocolException: status:400, body:{"code":400,"message":"transaction failed:\"-\" unknown property","errorStack":[],"apiError":2}
bugs.conditions: A description field in the swagger file contains a hyphen with a space on each side, for example: "description" : "{\n\"documentTypeName\": \"problem - here\"}
bugs.impact: BIG-IP reports the error that the pattern is not accepted.
bugs.fix: Fixed an error loading swagger files.

bugs.title: Azure walinuxagent has been updated to v2.2.42
bugs.symptoms: Some onboarding features are not available in the current version of walinuxagent.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use a feature that is not available in the current version of the Azure walinuxagent that is included in the BIG-IP release.
bugs.impact: Cannot use new features in the Azure walinuxagent until the Azure walinuxagent is updated.
bugs.fix: The Azure walinuxagent has been updated to v2.2.42

bugs.title: Azure walinuxagent has been updated to v2.2.42.
bugs.symptoms: Some onboarding features are not available in the current version of walinuxagent.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use a feature that is not available in the current version of the Azure walinuxagent that is included in the BIG-IP release.
bugs.impact: Cannot use new features in the Azure walinuxagent until the Azure walinuxagent is updated.
bugs.fix: The Azure walinuxagent has been updated to v2.2.42.

bugs.title: The liveupdate.log file is not gzipped
bugs.symptoms: After installing BIG-IP the following error messages is observed: 1. Broadcast message from root@localhost.localdomain (Mon Oct 7 16:10:02 2019): 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var/log has only 6% free 2. Broadcast message from systemd-journald@localhost.localdomain (Mon 2019-10-07 16:01:03 IDT): alertd[8975]: 01100048:0: Log disk usage still higher than 80% after logrotate and 24 times log deletion
bugs.conditions: Liveupdate logs.
bugs.impact: Liveupdate logs are increasing in size and old logs are not gzipped, log disk usage is higher than 80%.
bugs.workaround: The logs can be manually gzipped or deleted.
bugs.fix: The liveupdate logs are rotated and gzipped.

bugs.title: After UCS restore the restnoded or restjavad is not active
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, after restoring a UCS, either restnoded or restjavad is not restarted and you see the following message in the GUI: The iApp LX sub-system is currently unresponsive. The JavaScript sub-system is currently unavailable. Please open TMSH or a ssh shell and try restarting restnoded. Also look for errors in /var/log/restnoded/restnoded.log.
bugs.conditions: -- After restoring a UCS. -- Other conditions that trigger this are unknown; this is an intermittent error.
bugs.impact: You may be unable to use iAppLX apps such as the SSL Orchestrator (SSLO) UI.
bugs.workaround: Use the following procedure to recover: 1. Create an SSH connection to the unit using the management IP address. 2. Execute the following command: bigstart restart restnoded restjavad 3. Wait for restnoded and restjavad to come up, and then try to access the SSL Orchestrator UI.

bugs.title: External monitors mark objects down
bugs.symptoms: Object to which the external monitor is attached is marked down.
bugs.conditions: Executing external monitors trying to access something without appropriate permissions.
bugs.impact: Object to which the external monitor is attached is marked down.
bugs.fix: This issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Client browser traffic through APM SWG transparent proxy using captive portal might get reset.
bugs.symptoms: Client browser traffic through APM Secure Web Gateway is being reset by APM SWG.
bugs.conditions: -- APM SWG transparent proxy is configured with captive portal. -- Client browser sends redirect to original URI on a TCP connection that was opened before access policy completion on captive portal.
bugs.impact: The connection is reset.
bugs.fix: Client browser sending redirect traffic on a TCP connection opened before access policy completion on captive portal will not get RST and traffic will be processed successfully by the BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Some strings on BIG-IP APM Server pages are not localized
bugs.symptoms: Some text in APM Server pages, such as the logout page, are presented in English even when using a different language.
bugs.conditions: Use APM with a localized language, and certain strings for pages like logout, Webtop, or EPS, would still be in English.
bugs.impact: Some strings are displayed in English instead of localized language.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP APM Server pages have been updated to include translations for all the affected strings.

bugs.title: HTTP custom analytics profile 'not found' when default profile is modified
bugs.symptoms: Adding SMTP config to default HTTP analytics profile results in config parsing failures for child profiles that are assigned to virtual servers. Removing SMTP config resolves the issue. The 'tmsh load sys config' command fails with the following error: -- 01020036:3: The requested profile (/Common/child-analytics) was not found. -- Unexpected Error: Validating configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Child analytics profile applied to virtual server. -- Parent analytics profile contains SMTP config.
bugs.impact: Loading configuration might fail.
bugs.fix: The system now avoids setting SMTP field for child profiles on MCP validation when in load/merge phase.

bugs.title: Tmsh crash potentially related to NGFIPS SDK
bugs.symptoms: Tmsh crash occurs rarely. The NGFIPS SDK may generate a core as well.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions that trigger this are unknown. It can be encountered when running the following tmsh command: tmsh -a show sys crypto fips key field-fmt include-public-keys all-properties
bugs.impact: Tmsh may crash. You are exited from tmsh if you were using it as a shell.

bugs.title: After upgrading BIG-IP software and resetting HA, gossip may show 'UNPAIRED'
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading BIG-IP software and reconfiguring high availability (HA), gossip may show 'UNPAIRED' and the REST endpoint /resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices/ may show only one device.
bugs.conditions: -- This has been observed during upgrade from 14.x.x to 15.x.x. -- Reconfigure HA. -- View gossip results and REST endpoint output.
bugs.impact: The gossip output shows 'UNPAIRED', and the REST endpoint reports only one decide. SSL Orchestrator does not work as expected
bugs.workaround: If gossip shows 'UNPAIRED' after upgrade, you may need to do following at both devices: 1. Delete existing device information: restcurl -X DELETE shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices 2. Force update: bigstart restart restjavad restcurl -X POST -d '{}' tm/shared/bigip-failover-state

bugs.title: When BGP recursive nexthop is down, network is down, logs show Type: 0 messages without nexthop.
bugs.symptoms: While BGP is configured to use recursive routes and OSPF is used to provide a route to the recursive routes, you see repeated messages 'Type: 0'.
bugs.conditions: Due to network unreachable issue, ZebOS is shown all type :0 message. 1. BGP recursive routes are configured. 2. OSPF is configured to provide routing to the recursive routes. 3. OSPF flaps, or the network connection to the next hop is lost somehow.
bugs.impact: BGP logs do not contain helpful diagnostic information.

bugs.title: [SIP-MRF] Transport-config source port behavior changed needs after upgrading to version with new source-port-mode attribute
bugs.symptoms: A new parameter "source-port-mode" was added in MRF transport-config in V16.0.0; its default setting is "Change". Users who upgrade from an older configuration version and have a value set in source-port will experience a change in behavior after updating. To achieve equivalent behavior when upgrading to the new config, the source-port should retain its value, but IF it is non-zero, the source-port-mode should be set to preserve-strict.
bugs.conditions: When BIG-IP is upgraded from a version without the Transport-Config:source-port-mode setting to a version (v16.0.0 or later) that includes it. Transport-Config with non-zero source-port configured.
bugs.impact: After BIG-IP upgrading, with the same transport-config, BIG-IP changed the source-port when connecting to a pool member, and caused SIP responses to be unable to be sent back to the client.
bugs.workaround: Manually change "source-port-mode" to "preserve-strict" after upgrade.

bugs.title: Profile name over 64 characters in length will cause ACCESS::session create to fail
bugs.symptoms: TMM resets ACCESS::session create iRule commands after assigning an access profile to it.
bugs.conditions: -- Access profile name is longer than 64 characters (including partition and app name if applicable) -- ACCESS::session create iRule used
bugs.impact: ACCESS:session create iRule will fail; connection will reset.
bugs.workaround: Make sure the Access profile name is less than 64 characters when using ACCESS::session create iRule command.
bugs.fix: Buffer used to store Access profile name has been increased. Max is now 1024.

bugs.title: ZRD process restarts observed due to stale files in /var/zrd/zrd-undo/ when UCS file is loaded or any modifications in wide IP configurations.
bugs.symptoms: Due to stale files in /var/zrd/zrd-undo, UCS loading is failing. Stale files are causing differences in zone information between named.conf and /var/zrd/zrd-undo files which is leading to restart of the zrd process (the ZoneRunner daemon).
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a wide IP with one or more aliases. -- Deleting the configurations along with the ZoneRunner file. -- Loading the UCS file.
bugs.impact: UCS configuration load fails, resulting in zrd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Note: Before loading the UCS file, remove stale files in /var/zrd/zrd-undo/: 1. Halt the zrd and named processes: bigstart stop zrd named 2. Delete the GTM wide IP: tmsh delete gtm wideip a all 3. Remove the stale zrd files: \rm /var/zrd/zrd-undo/* 4. Edit named.conf (vi /var/named/config/named.conf) and remove all the zones. 5. Remove the stale named files: \rm /var/named/config/namedb/db.* /var/named/config/dummy 6. Restart the zrd and named processes: bigstart start zrd named

bugs.title: SIP MBLB incorrectly initiates new flow from virtual IP to client when existing flow is in FIN-wait2
bugs.symptoms: In MBLB/SIP, if the BIG-IP system attempts to send messages to the destination over a TCP connection that is in FIN-wait2 stage, instead of returning a failure and silently dropping the message, the BIG-IP system attempts to create a new TCP connection by sending a SYN. Eventually, the attempt fails and causes the connection to be aborted.
bugs.conditions: -- This happens on MBLB/SIP deployment with TCP. -- There is message sent from the server to the BIG-IP system. -- The BIG-IP system forwards the message from the server-side to client-side. -- The destination flow (for the BIG-IP system to forward the message to) is controlled by 'node <ip> <port>' and 'snat <ip> <port>' iRules command. -- The destination flow is in the FIN-wait2 stage.
bugs.impact: This causes the BIG-IP system to abort the flow that originates the message.
bugs.fix: SIP MBLB correctly initiates a new flow from a virtual IP to the client when an existing flow is in the FIN-wait2 stage.

bugs.title: Incorrect source MAC used when the BIG-IP system in L2 transparent mode generates a TCP RST packet.
bugs.symptoms: Packet with unexpected source MAC is seen on the adjacent node to the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is configured in an L2 transparent mode using virtual wires. -- Traffic forwarded between client and server in an asymmetric manner across virtual wires.
bugs.impact: Incorrect source MAC is used. Possible impacts to services on nodes adjacent to the BIG-IP system if policy decisions on those nodes are made with the source MAC of the received packet as input.

bugs.title: AVR and BIG-IQ stats show N/A bar for Source IP and domain name on DNS query packet
bugs.symptoms: AVR and BIG-IQ stats show an N/A bar for Source IP and domain name fields on DNS query packets, while the correct IP and domain name is shown in other bars.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is provisioned. -- DNS traffic is processed.
bugs.impact: No functional impact, but incorrect and redundant results are shown in AVR.
bugs.fix: Incorrect and redundant N/A bar has been removed.

bugs.title: "Application Security Administrator" user role cannot manage Dos Profile GUI
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP GUI users in "Application Security Administrator" role are not allowed to manage DoS profile page and settings.
bugs.conditions: This affects users logged in with the "Application Security Administrator" role
bugs.impact: DoS profiles cannot be edited from GUI
bugs.workaround: Either change user role to allow managing DoS profile or edit profiles from tmsh
bugs.fix: The roles Application Security Operations Administrator and Application Security Administrator can now manage DoS profiles in the GUI.

bugs.title: Processing ICMP unreachable packets causes FWNAT/CGNAT persistence issues with UDP traffic
bugs.symptoms: When hosts send ICMP unreachable error messages and processed by the BIG-IP system, subsequent good UDP packets do not get the persistence LSN translation address.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with FW NAT or CGNAT configuration to accept UDP traffic. -- Client or/and server randomly sends ICMP unreachable messages.
bugs.impact: LSN persistence issues. UDP packets from the same client IP address may not get the same translation address every time, even though there exists a persistence entry in the table
bugs.fix: Processing ICMP unreachable packets no longer causes FWNAT/CGNAT persistence issues with UDP traffic.

bugs.title: User cannot update blocking response pages after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Response Pages screen is stuck after user tries to save changes
bugs.conditions: The device is upgraded from a pre-15.1 release to a newer version
bugs.impact: Impossible to update blocking response pages using the GUI
bugs.workaround: Blocking pages can be updated using the REST API
bugs.fix: Database upgrade script was fixed to preserve correct Server Technology settings that lead to errors in Response Pages screen

bugs.title: Response and Blocking Pages page: Deception Response pages should not be shown in parent policy
bugs.symptoms: Deception Response pages shown and editable in parent policy.
bugs.conditions: -- Deception Response Pages feature is licensed and enabled. -- You are editing the parent policy.
bugs.impact: Deception Response pages cannot be updated from the parent policy, thus any update of response pages fails with error.
bugs.fix: Deception Response pages not shown in parent policy.

bugs.title: SNMPv3 pass phrases should not be synced between high availability (HA) devices as that are based on each devices unique engineID
bugs.symptoms: SNMPv3 fails to read authenticated or encrypted messages to all but one of the members of a Config Sync group.
bugs.conditions: Using SNMPv3 to read or receive Traps from high availability (HA) pairs.
bugs.impact: SNMPv3 can only work for one member of a configsync group. Configuring passwords on one device, makes that device work, but other members of the config sync group will now fail.
bugs.workaround: - check "Authoritative (security) engineID for SNMPv3" is not synced (mostly code released since 2019) engineID needs to be unique per device - Modify /defaults/config_base.conf to set sync to "no" and check that these do not sync We must NOT sync these parameters as they need to match the individual device engineID display-name "Authoritative (security) engineID for SNMPv3" display-name "Authentication pass phrase for SNMPv3 messages" display-name "Privacy pass phrase used for encrypted SNMPV3 messages" display-name "User's passphrase" display-name "Privacy passphrase" ### Mount usr as rw see see K11302 mount -o remount,rw /usr pico /defaults/config_base.conf # use Control-w to search for the display names above # change "configsyncd yes" to "configsyncd no" if necessary in each location # use Control-x y to exit with saving # Restore usr as ro mount -o remount,ro /usr tmsh load sys config Then once they are not syncing over, you can create v3 on each device using the same pass phrase as your SNMPv3 manager is using tmsh modify sys snmp users add { v3snmp { auth-protocol sha privacy-protocol aes username mikev3 auth-password password3 privacy-password password3} } tmsh modify sys snmp users modify { v3snmp { security-level auth-privacy access rw } } Then each device should respond OK to query for that same pass phrase snmpwalk -v 3 localhost -a sha -x aes -A password3 -X password3 -u mikev3 -l authpriv For more information about SNMP, see the following articles. K15681: Customizing the SNMP v3 engineID K6821: SNMP v3 fails if the SNMP engine ID is not unique K3727: Configuring custom SNMP traps

bugs.title: Tmm may crash while processing a compression context
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes on segfault.
bugs.conditions: Conditions are unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Orphaned bigip_gtm.conf can cause config load failure after upgrading
bugs.symptoms: Configuration fails to load after upgrade with a message: 01420006:3: Can't find specified cli schema data for x.x.x.x Where x.x.x.x indicates an older version of BIG-IP software than is currently running.
bugs.conditions: -- Orphaned bigip_gtm.conf from an older-version. This can occur if GTM/DNS is provisioned, then deprovisioned before upgrade, leaving behind a bigip_gtm.conf with the old schema. -- Upgrading to a new version that does not contain the schema for the old version that the bigip_gtm.conf uses.
bugs.impact: Configuration fails to load after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading: If the configuration in bigip_gtm.conf is not needed, then it can be renamed (or deleted) before upgrading: mv /config/bigip_gtm.conf /config/bigip_gtm.conf.id837637 tmsh load sys config gtm-only After upgrading (i.e., with the system in the Offline state) services must be restarted to pick up the change: mv /config/bigip_gtm.conf /config/bigip_gtm.conf.id837637 tmsh restart sys service all

bugs.title: Restjavad Storage and Configuration Hardening
bugs.symptoms: The restjavad component does not follow current best coding practices.
bugs.conditions: -REST endpoints in use
bugs.impact: The restjavad component does not follow current best coding practices.
bugs.fix: The restjavad component now follows current best coding practices.

bugs.title: Per-request policy using Client-Initiated Form-based SSO cannot access the resource, and configured as SAML-IdP, fails to process SAML Requests/Responses.
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system contains a per-request policy and is deployed to use Client-Initiated Form-based SSO for a resource, you cannot access the resource. When the BIG-IP system is deployed as SAML-IdP, it fails to process SAML Requests/Responses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs only when per-request policy is also associated in the BIG-IP virtual server.
bugs.impact: For BIG-IP systems deployed with Client-Initiated Form-based SSO on a resource, you cannot access the resource. For BIG-IP systems deployed as SAML IdP, SAML functionality does not work.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure the per-request policy in the virtual server.

bugs.title: SSH Client Requirements Hardening
bugs.symptoms: In some configurations, BIG-IP systems allow the use of DSA keys for SSH authentication.
bugs.conditions: Terminal Access (SSH) enabled for users with DSA keys.
bugs.impact: DSA keys are allowed for authentication, exposing BIG-IP to the limitations of this key format, including potential compromise of the authenticated session.
bugs.workaround: For ssh key based authentications, DSA keys should not be used.
bugs.fix: ssh-dss is disabled from supported authentication methods. It can be enabled under BIGIP using command tmsh modify sys sshd { include '"HostKeyAlgorithms +ssh-dss"' }
bugs.behavior: ssh-dss is now disabled by default from supported SSH authentication methods. It can be explicitly enabled under BIG-IP using command: tmsh modify sys sshd { include '"HostKeyAlgorithms +ssh-dss"' }

bugs.title: Error message: Unable to parse availability log.
bugs.symptoms: The execution of command 'tmsh show sys availablility' fails with the following output: Unexpected Error: Error: unable to parse availability log
bugs.conditions: When the binary log - /var/log/availability.0 file gets corrupted.
bugs.impact: Cannot view system uptime from tmsh.
bugs.workaround: Execute 'tmsh reset-stats sys availability' to reset the binary log file.

bugs.title: Duplicate traffic-selectors may result in failure while reloading the configuration or during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Configuring duplicate net ipsec traffic-selectors with one having interface mode ipsec-policy and another having non-interface mode ipsec-policy is allowed, but results in an error on reloading the config, and may fail during upgrades.
bugs.conditions: -- Adding a second traffic-selector that has the same values for all these five attributes: - destination-address - destination-port - source-address - source-port - ip-protocol. -- The second traffic-selector ipsec-policy is in interface mode, i.e., has its 'mode' field set to 'interface'. -- The first traffic-selector has a non-interface ipsec-policy. Example of two duplicate traffic-sectors (trafsel1 and trafsel2): net ipsec ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy { ike-phase2-auth-algorithm aes-gcm128 ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm aes-gcm128 } net ipsec ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface { ike-phase2-auth-algorithm aes-gcm128 ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm aes-gcm128 mode interface } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel1 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy source-address 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel2 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface source-address 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar }
bugs.impact: The configuration is allowed, but fails config reload and upgrade, giving the following error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Duplicate traffic selector is not allowed.
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading: Ensure all pairs of duplicate traffic-selectors have an ipsec-policy configured and that, this ipsec-policy is in interface mode, i.e., has its 'mode' field set to 'interface', or ensure any one of the five attributes listed above is unique. This can be done in multiple ways: 1. Change the ipsec-policy of the traffic-selector to take an interace mode ipsec-policy: Example: net ipsec ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy { ike-phase2-auth-algorithm aes-gcm128 ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm aes-gcm128 } net ipsec ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface { ike-phase2-auth-algorithm aes-gcm128 ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm aes-gcm128 mode interface } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel1 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface source-address 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel2 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface source-address 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar } 2. Change the mode of ipsec-policy (used by any duplicate traffic-selector) to 'interface'. Example: net ipsec ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy { ike-phase2-auth-algorithm aes-gcm128 ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm aes-gcm128 mode interface } net ipsec ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface { ike-phase2-auth-algorithm aes-gcm128 ike-phase2-encrypt-algorithm aes-gcm128 mode interface } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel1 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy source-address 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel2 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy source-address 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar } 3. Change any one of the five attributes to be unique, (e.g., source-address): net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel1 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy source-address 1.1.2.2/32 source-port texar } net ipsec traffic-selector trafsel2 { ipsec-policy temp-ipsec-policy-interface source-texar 1.1.1.1/32 source-port texar }
bugs.fix: Modify the config of duplicate traffic-selectors to have their ipsec-policy set to "interace" mode or make any one of the five attributes noted above unique.

bugs.title: ASM cannot save sync file after MySQL corruption following forcible restart
bugs.symptoms: ASM cannot save sync file after MySQL corruption following forcible restart.
bugs.conditions: MySQL was restarted forcibly, possibly following /var disk partition exhaustion.
bugs.impact: ASM cannot save sync files. This prevents saving UCS and high availability (HA) sync.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, it may be possible to delete all files under /var/lib/mysql/PLC_ucs and restart MySQL. However, in our experience, once MySQL has been corrupted by forcible restarts and/or disk exhaustion, it is more advisable to reinstall the device from scratch and load the saved configuration.

bugs.title: Remote ActiveDirectory users are unable to login to the BIG-IP using remote LDAP authentication
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the BIG-IP system requires you to change your password on every login. Furthermore, the login then fails, and loops endlessly asking for the password, even though the password has not expired.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP 14.0.0 and later. -- LDAP authentication is used for remote users. -- Active Directory (AD) user account has shadowLastChange attribute with a value of 0 (or anything lower than the number of days since 1-1-1970).
bugs.impact: Remote AD BIG-IP users are unable to login to the BIG-IP system using remote LDAP authentication
bugs.workaround: Clear the value of shadowLastChange within AD.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may create multiple connections for packets that should belong to a single flow.
bugs.symptoms: Due to a known issue, BIG-IP may create multiple connections for packets that should belong to a single flow. These connections will stay in the connection table until the idle timeout is reached. These connections can be used for forwarding the traffic.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP may create multiple connections for packets that should belong to a single flow when both following conditions are true: - Packets are coming at a very high rate from the network. - Flow handling these packets is torn down.
bugs.impact: This might result in packets from the client being handled by one flow and packets from the server being handled by a different flow.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system's time zone database does not reflect recent changes implemented by Brazil in regard to DST.
bugs.symptoms: In 2019, Brazil cancelled DST (Daylight Saving Time) and is now on standard time indefinitely. The BIG-IP system's time zone database needs to be updated to reflect this change.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP systems configured to use "America/Sao_Paul" (or other applicable Brazilian localities) will still apply DST. Hence time will spring forward and backward on previously designated dates. This will have no impact to application traffic handled by the BIG-IP system. However, logs, alerts, reports, cron jobs, etc. will use incorrect time. Note: You can inspect the time changes your system is due to apply by running the following command from the BIG-IP system's advanced shell (bash): zdump -v <timezone> For example: zdump -v America/Sao_Paulo
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you can set the BIG-IP system's time zone to that of a different country with the same UTC offset and already not observing DST. For example, instead of using "America/Sao_Paul", you could use "America/Buenos_Aires" to obtain the same result.

bugs.title: MQTT monitor is not working in route domain.
bugs.symptoms: MQTT monitor fails when non-default route domains are used.
bugs.conditions: -When a non-default route domain is configured for a pool member -mqtt monitor in use
bugs.impact: Mqtt monitor does not work in route domain.

bugs.title: Listener traffic-group may not be updated when spanning is in use
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP may fail to update configuration of a virtual server when disabling or enabling spanning on the virtual address.
bugs.conditions: Spanning is disabled or enabled on a virtual address.
bugs.impact: Disabling or enabling spanning on a virtual address has no effect on the virtual-server configuration. Depending on the configuration, virtual server may or may not forward the traffic when expected.
bugs.workaround: Enable/Disable spanning together with changing a traffic-group (both options have to be changed simultaneously): > modify ltm virtual-address 0.0.0.0 traffic-group traffic-group-2 spanning disabled > modify ltm virtual-address 0.0.0.0 traffic-group traffic-group-1 spanning enabled

bugs.title: Tmrouted on a multi-blade system might generate a core during system shutdown
bugs.symptoms: A tmrouted core is generated during system shutdown.
bugs.conditions: -- The system is a multi-blade system. Note: This has only been seen on a multi-blade, vCMP guest. -- The system is shutting down.
bugs.impact: Tmrouted core is generated. There are no other known impacts.

bugs.title: Unable to load license/dossier when going down for vCMP
bugs.symptoms: After provisioning vCMP on the BIG-IP system and rebooting, vcmpd might core during the shutdown with a log message in /var/log/ltm "Unable to load license/dossier: Failed to connect to HAL via halmsg".
bugs.conditions: This occurs when rebooting the BIG-IP system after provisioning vCMP.
bugs.impact: This crash does not impact any functionality - system is shutting down anyway

bugs.title: DoS report exist in per-widget but not under individual virtual
bugs.symptoms: 'Undefined entity dosl7_vip was used' error message is reported on widgets whenever a 'Virtual Server' filter is selected on the 'Security :: Reporting : DoS : Custom Page' GUI page.
bugs.conditions: -- Navigate to Security :: Reporting : DoS : Custom Page in the GUI. -- Filter widgets results with specific 'Virtual Server'.
bugs.impact: GUI widgets report errors and cannot show stats.
bugs.workaround: This GUI fix requires modifying a single PHP file in one location, which you can do directly on your BIG-IP system with a few bash commands: 1. Backup the file '/var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php': $ cp /var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php /shared/ 2. Change permissions to allow modifying it: $ chmod +w /var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php 3. Change the file to include the fix: $ sed -i 's/dosl7_vip/vip/g' /var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php $ sed -i "s/ANALYTICS_MOD_DNS_DOS => 'vip'/ANALYTICS_MOD_DNS_DOS => 'dns_vip'/g" /var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php 4. Verify that the fix is as expected: $ vimdiff /var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php /shared/dos_custom_overview_commons.php (** You should see two lines modified: 1. ANALYTICS_MOD_DOSL7 => 'dosl7_vip' to ANALYTICS_MOD_DOSL7 => 'vip'. 2. ANALYTICS_MOD_DNS_DOS => 'vip' to ANALYTICS_MOD_DNS_DOS => 'dns_vip') 5. Revert permissions of the file: $ chmod -w /var/ts/dms/amm/common/ovw/dos_custom_overview_commons.php 6. Log out and log back into the GUI, so that the new version of the file loads.
bugs.fix: GUI configuration for the 'Virtual Server' filter is fixed with the correct dimension name.

bugs.title: Enabling DoS stats also enables page-load-time
bugs.symptoms: If collect-all-dos-statistic is enabled, AVR 'promises' to the client a JavaScript injection in the response by adding the expected length of the JavaScript to the Content-length header.
bugs.conditions: Security :: reporting : settings : collect-all-dos-statistic is enabled.
bugs.impact: In addition to collecting DoS statistics, JavaScript injection also occurs.
bugs.workaround: Can use iRules to control which pages should get the JavaScript injection. For detailed information, see K13859: Disabling CSPM injection with iRules :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13859.
bugs.fix: Changed the condition that insert the JavaScript injection in case that "collect all dos stats" is enabled.

bugs.title: LCD buttons are not responsive during End User Diagnostics 'Front Port LED Test'
bugs.symptoms: During EUDSF3.9.1 Front Port LED Test on BIG-IP iSeries platforms, the LCD buttons are unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: -- Running the EUDSF3.9.1 Front Port LED Test. -- Using BIG-IP iSeries platforms.
bugs.impact: Cannot execute the EUDSF3.9.1 Front Port LED Test on BIG-IP iSeries platforms..
bugs.workaround: Continue to use EUDSF 3.7.0. EUDSF3.9.1 is required only for iSeries i10010, where the test does not have this issue.
bugs.fix: The version EUD3.9.2 release contains a fix for this issus.

bugs.title: TMM might crash once after upgrading SSL Orchestrator
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash due to SIGABRT.
bugs.conditions: -- Session check agent is present in APM per-request policy. -- APM Access Profile scope changes during SSL Orchestrator upgrade. -- This issue can occur for SSL Orchestrator upgrades from 14.x to 15.x and above.
bugs.impact: TMM might crash once. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Session check agent now exits and terminates the flow.

bugs.title: TMM receives invalid rx descriptor from HSB hardware
bugs.symptoms: The HSB hardware returns an invalid receive (rx) descriptor to TMM. This results in a TMM core and can be seen as a SIGSEGV in the TMM logs. This also might result in continuous restarts of TMM, resulting in subsequent SIGSEGVs reported in the TMM logs until the unit is manually recovered.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. This may result in continuous TMM restarts until the BIG-IP system is rebooted.

bugs.title: Rewrite URI translation profile can cause connection reset while processing malformed CSS content
bugs.symptoms: Malformed CSS where one of the style rules is missing a closing brace could cause LTM Rewrite profile to stop processing file or reset connection.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM Rewrite (URI translation) profile is attached to virtual server. -- Content rewriting is enabled in Rewrite profile settings. -- CSS file contains style rule with missing closing brace.
bugs.impact: URLs are not modified within affected files, starting from the missing closing brace. Intermittent connection resets occur.
bugs.workaround: Before rewriting, insert the missing symbol into CSS content either directly on the backend server or with an iRule.

bugs.title: A modified default profile that contains SSLv2, COMPAT, or RC2 cipher will cause the configuration to fail to load on upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading, the configuration fails to load and throws an error about a profile that is located in profile_base.conf using SSLv2. However, upon inspection you will notice that there is no SSLv2 cipher in use.
bugs.conditions: The upgrade failure is seen when all the following conditions are met: -- BIG-IP system with SSLv2 as the ciphers option in an SSL profile running software v12.x/v13.x. -- Upgrading to a version that reports an error when using SSLv2, such as v14.x/v15.x. (1) Modified root SSL profile (such as /Common/clientssl or /Common/serverssl) is present in bigip.conf. (2) The modified root SSL profile contains an invalid keyword 'COMPAT', 'SSLv2', or 'RC2' in its ciphers (3) The default profiles whose ciphers inherited from the root profile are not present in bigip.conf. The error for invalid ciphers is reported against these profiles.
bugs.impact: Beginning in version 14.x, SSLv2 has been changed from being a warning condition, and now prevents the configuration from loading. In most cases the upgrade script properly removes this, so there is no issue. However, if this issue is encountered, the configuration fails to load after upgrading.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- The easiest way to work around this is to comment out the modified base profile from bigip.conf and then run the command: tmsh load sys config. -- If you are post upgrade, you can use sed to remove the !SSLv2 entries. To do so, perform these steps on the standby device: 1. cp /config/bigip.conf /config/backup_bigip.conf 2. Run: sed -i "s/\(\!SSLv2:\|:\!SSLv2\)//g" /config/bigip.conf 3. tmsh load /sys config

bugs.title: Issue with 'Multiple of' validation of numeric values
bugs.symptoms: 'Multiple of' validation of numeric values may not be correct in some scenarios.
bugs.conditions: -- Create default policy from API Security template. -- Create default decimal parameter with 'Multiple of'=5. -- Send request to /index.php?param=0.
bugs.impact: 'Multiple of' validation of numeric values does not block as expected.

bugs.title: IPother profile with SNAT sets egress TTL to 255

bugs.conditions: Virtual-server with ipother profile and SNAT configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic leaves with egress TTL set to 255.
bugs.fix: TTL is now decremented by 1 on forwarded packets.

bugs.title: iRule 'drop' command does not drop packets when used in DNS_RESPONSE
bugs.symptoms: The iRule 'drop' command may not drop a DNS response when called under DNS_RESPONSE event.
bugs.conditions: iRule drop is used under DNS_RESPONSE event.
bugs.impact: DNS response may be improperly forwarded to the client.
bugs.workaround: Use DNS::drop instead.

bugs.title: TMM can crash when connecting to IVS under extreme overload
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash while attempting to connect internally to an internal virtual server (IVS) and the connection setup cannot be completed due to internal factors.
bugs.conditions: -- Extreme overload such that TMM is out of memory, or some other internal condition that prevents connection setup. -- Connection to an internal virtual server is attempted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM does not crash while connecting to an IVS under extreme overload.

bugs.title: Moving a virtual-address from one floating traffic-group to another does not send GARPs out.
bugs.symptoms: Gratuitous ARPs (GARPs) are not sent out when moving a virtual-address from one floating traffic-group to another (e.g., from traffic-group-1 to traffic-group-2).
bugs.conditions: -- Moving a virtual-address from one floating traffic-group to another. -- The traffic-groups are active on different devices.
bugs.impact: Application traffic does not immediately resume after the virtual-address is moved. Instead, the surrounding network devices have to ARP out for the IP address after reaching a timeout condition.
bugs.workaround: After moving the virtual-address, disable and then re-enable the ARP setting for the virtual-address. This forces GARPs to be sent out.
bugs.fix: GARPs are sent out as expected.

bugs.title: Incorrect inheritance treatment in Response and Blocking Pages page
bugs.symptoms: Deception Response Pages is not inherited, but if common response pages are inherited, you are unable to save changes.
bugs.conditions: -- Deception Response Pages features licensed. -- Parent policy selected with inheritance of response pages.
bugs.impact: Deception Response Pages cannot be modified.
bugs.fix: Inheritance is treated correctly in Response and Blocking Pages page.

bugs.title: Restjavad fails to start if provision.extramb has large value
bugs.symptoms: Rolling restarts of restjavad every few seconds typically due to failure to start and reports messages in daemon log: daemon.log: emerg logger: Re-starting restjavad The system reports similar message at the command line. No obvious cause is logged in rest logs.
bugs.conditions: -- System DB variable provision.extramb has an unusually high value*: + above ~2700-2800MB for v12.1.0 and earlier. + above ~2900-3000MB for v13.0.0 and later. -- On v13.0.0 and later, sys db variable restjavad.useextramb needs to have the value 'true' *A range of values is shown. When the value is above the approximate range specified, constant restarts are extremely likely, and within tens of MB below that point may be less frequent. To check the values of these system DB varaiables use: tmsh list sys db provision.extramb tmsh list sys db restjavad.useextramb
bugs.impact: This impacts the ability to use the REST API to manage the system
bugs.workaround: If needing sys db restjavad.useextramb to have the value 'true', keep sys db provision.extramb well below the values listed (e.g., 2000 MB work without issue). To set that at command line: tmsh modify sys db provision.extrammb value 2000 If continual restarts of restjavad are causing difficulties managing the unit on the command line: 1. Stop restjavad (you can copy this string and paste it into the command line on the BIG-IP system): tmsh stop sys service restjavad 2. Reduce the large value of provision.extramb if necessary. 3. Restart the restjavad service: tmsh start sys service restjavad
bugs.fix: Restjavad memory is now capped at a sensible maximum. If provision.extramb is set to a value higher than 2500 MB it will be considered to be 2500 MB for the purposes of restjavad, and the system logs a message similar to the following in /var/log/ltm, where XXXX is the value of provision.extramb: notice restjavad: JVM heap limit exceeded. Using maximum supported value of 2500 instead of provision.extramb XXXX.

bugs.title: Portal Access: HTML iframe sandbox attribute is not supported

bugs.conditions: Using an iframe with the sandbox attribute in a web application.
bugs.impact: The web application does not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule as a workaround. Although the exact content of the iRule is strongly dependent on the web application, you can use the following iRule as a good example that can be customized: when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { HTTP::path] ends_with "/CUSOM_PATH_TO_JS_FILE" } { REWRITE::post_process 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { while {true} { set str { sandbox="} set strt [string first $str [REWRITE::payload]] set str_len [string length $str] if { $strt > 0 and $strt < [expr [REWRITE::payload length] - $str_len] } { REWRITE::payload replace $strt $str_len { sandbo1="} } else { break } } }

bugs.title: Application traffic may fail after an internal interface failure on a VIPRION system.
bugs.symptoms: Blades in a VIPRION system connect with one another over a data backplane and a management backplane. For more information on the manner in which blades interconnect over the data backplane, please refer to K13306: Overview of the manner in which the VIPRION chassis and blades interconnect :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13306. Should an internal interface fail and thus block communication over the data backplane between two distinct blades, an unusual situation arises where different blades compute different CMP states. For example, if on a 4-slot chassis, blades 2 and 3 become disconnected with one another, the following is TMM's computation of which slots are on-line: slot1: slots 1, 2, 3, and 4 on-line (cmp state 0xf / 15) slot2: slots 1, 2, and 4 on-line (cmp state 0xb / 11) slot3: slots 1, 3, and 4 on-line (cmp state 0xd / 13) slot4: slots 1, 2, 3, and 4 on-line (cmp state 0xf / 15) As different slots are effectively operating under different assumptions of the state of the cluster, application traffic does not flow as expected. Some connections time out or are reset. You can run the following command to inspect the CMP state of each slot: clsh 'tmctl -d blade -s cmp_state tmm/cmp' All slots should report the same state, for instance: # clsh 'tmctl -d blade -s cmp_state tmm/cmp' === slot 2 addr 127.3.0.2 color green === cmp_state --------- 15 === slot 3 addr 127.3.0.3 color green === cmp_state --------- 15 === slot 4 addr 127.3.0.4 color green === cmp_state --------- 15 === slot 1 addr 127.3.0.1 color green === cmp_state --------- 15 When this issue occurs, logs similar to the following example can be expected in the /var/log/ltm file: -- info bcm56xxd[4276]: 012c0015:6: Link: 2/5.3 is DOWN -- info bcm56xxd[4296]: 012c0015:6: Link: 3/5.1 is DOWN -- info bcm56xxd[4296]: 012c0012:6: Trunk default member mod 13 port 0 slot 2; CMP state changed from 0xf to 0xd -- info bcm56xxd[4339]: 012c0012:6: Trunk default member mod 13 port 0 slot 2; CMP state changed from 0xf to 0xd -- info bcm56xxd[4214]: 012c0012:6: Trunk default member mod 13 port 0 slot 2; CMP state changed from 0xf to 0xd And a CMP transition will be visible in the /var/log/tmm file similar to the following example: -- notice CDP: PG 2 timed out -- notice CDP: New pending state 0f -> 0b -- notice Immediately transitioning dissaggregator to state 0xb -- notice cmp state: 0xb For more information on troubleshooting VIPRION backplane hardware issues, please refer to K14764: Troubleshooting possible hardware issues on the VIPRION backplane :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14764.
bugs.conditions: This issue arises after a very specific type of hardware failure. The condition is very unlikely to occur and is impossible to predict in advance.
bugs.impact: Application traffic is impacted and fails sporadically due to a mismatch in CMP states between the blades. Failures are likely to manifest as timeouts or resets from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: F5 recommends the following to minimize the impact of this potential issue: 1) For all highly available configurations (e.g., A/S, A/A, A/A/S, etc.). The BIG-IP system has functionality, in all software versions, to enact a fast failover when the conditions described occur. To ensure this functionality will trigger, the following configuration requirements must be met: a) The mirroring strategy must be set to 'between'. b) A mirroring channel to the next-active unit must be up. c) The min-up-members option must be set to the number of blades in the chassis (e.g., 4 if there are 4 blades in the chassis). Note: It is not required to actually configure connection mirroring on any virtual server; simply choosing the aforementioned strategy and ensuring a channel is up to the next-active unit will suffice. However, note that some configurations will benefit by also configuring connection mirroring on some virtual servers, as that can greatly reduce the number of affected connections during a failover. 2) For 'regular' standalone units. If a VIPRION system is truly standalone (no kind of redundancy whatsoever), there is no applicable failsafe action, as you will want to keep that chassis online even if some traffic is impaired. Ensure suitable monitoring of the system is in place (e.g., remote syslog servers, SNMP traps, etc.), so that a BIG-IP Administrator can react quickly in the unlikely event this issue does occur. 3) For a standalone chassis which belongs to a pool on an upstream load-balancer. If the virtual servers of a standalone VIPRION system are pool members on an upstream load-balancer, it makes sense for the virtual servers to report unavailable (e.g., by resetting all new connection attempts) so that the upstream load-balancer can select different pool members. An Engineering Hotfix can be provided which introduces an enhancement for this particular use-case. A new DB key is made available under the Engineering Hotfix: tmm.cdp.requirematchingstates, which takes values 'enable' and 'disable'. The default is 'disable', which makes the VIPRION system behave as in versions without the enhancement. When set to 'enable', the VIPRION system attempts to detect this failure and, if it does, resets all new connections. This should trigger some monitor failures on the upstream load-balancer and allow it to select different pool members. Please note you should only request the Engineering Hotfix and enable this DB key when this specific use-case applies: a standalone VIPRION system which belongs to a pool on an upstream load-balancer. When the new feature is enabled, the following log messages in the /var/log/ltm file indicate when this begins and stops triggering: -- crit tmm[13733]: 01010366:2: CMP state discrepancy between blades detected, forcing maintenance mode. Unable to relinquish maintenance mode until event clears or feature (tmm.cdp.requirematchingstates) is disabled. -- crit tmm[13262]: 01010367:2: CMP state discrepancy between blades cleared or feature (tmm.cdp.requirematchingstates) disabled, relinquishing maintenance mode.
bugs.fix: The system now includes the enhancement for the 'standalone chassis which belongs to a pool' use-case, as discussed under the Workaround section.

bugs.title: Client OS agent in Access Policy added iPadOS categorization option
bugs.symptoms: iPadOS is categorized as iOS.
bugs.conditions: Use F5 Access for iPadOS to access webtop or establish VPN.
bugs.impact: Client OS agent in Access Policy does have an iPadOS categorization option
bugs.fix: iPadOS option is added to Client OS agent in Access Policy.

bugs.title: iControl REST hardening
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST does not implement current best practices.
bugs.conditions: -Authenticated administrative users of iControl REST.
bugs.impact: iControl REST does not implement current best practices.
bugs.fix: iControl REST now implements current best practices.

bugs.title: License activation takes a long time to complete on Google GCE platform
bugs.symptoms: The license installation and activation process takes a very long time to complete.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP Virtual Edition running on Google Compute Engine (GCE) Platform. - Activating the BIG-IP license.
bugs.impact: It can take 2-3 minutes to report the device is licensed and 3-4 minutes for BIG-IP system to become Active after that.

bugs.title: Hardware accelerated connection mismatch resulting in tmm core
