bugs.conditions: HTTP virtual server performing decompression of response data from a server, e.g. because a rewrite profile is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable compression on the server.

bugs.title: Improperly configured NTP server can result in an undisciplined clock stanza
bugs.symptoms: There can be an undisciplined clock stanza in /etc/ntp.conf, resulting in an undisciplined clock. NTP documentation: http://support.ntp.org/bin/view/Support/UndisciplinedLocalClock
bugs.conditions: This might occur in at least the following ways: -- No server is specified in 'sys ntp servers {}'. -- A server does exist, but an improper method was used to configure the NTP server.
bugs.impact: When the LOCAL undisciplined clock is left as a valid time-source, it delays the system synchronizing time to a real NTP server. It can also result in time being adjusted incorrectly if the the remote time-source becomes unreachable.
bugs.workaround: Configure a dummy server via 'ntp servers {}' that does not respond. While this removes the undisciplined local clock, it does result in ntpd having an unreachable time source, and could be flagged in diagnostics, misdirect other troubleshooting, generate unnecessary traffic, etc. However, if the 'dummy' source starts responding, it could become a rogue time source.

bugs.title: Using non-standard HTTPS and SSH ports fails under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: On all versions 12.1.0 or later, if you change the HTTPS port (e.g., to 8443, as is required for '1NIC' BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) deployments) and then expose the management UI via a self IP in a non-zero route domain, you cannot access the system via the GUI or CLI, and the system does not pass traffic as expected. In versions 14.1.0 and later on VE installations, attempting to manage a BIG-IP system over a self IP can fail if all these conditions are met: -- Non-standard HTTPS port used. -- No TMM default route configured. -- No route to the client IP address configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Modify the default HTTPS and/or default SSH ports. And either of the following: On 12.1.0 and above: -- Expose the management UI and/or CLI via a self IP in a non-zero route domain. On 14.1.0 and above: -- No TMM default route configured. -- No route to the client IP address configured.
bugs.impact: -- Unable to access BIG-IP GUI on non-standard HTTPS port. -- Unable to access BIG-IP CLI on non-standard SSH port.

bugs.title: Message Routing Diameter profile fails to forward messages with zero length AVPs
bugs.symptoms: Message Routing Diameter profile does not forward diameter messages that include an AVP with a zero (0) length data field.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server with an Message Routing Diameter Profile. -- A diameter message containing an AVP with a zero length data field.
bugs.impact: Diameter messages with zero length AVPs are not forwarded as expected.
bugs.fix: Message Routing Diameter now forwards diameter messages containing zero length AVPs.

bugs.title: File size of asm_modules.xml can exceed the file size limit of iHealth
bugs.symptoms: ASM policies and LTM objects are not uploaded to iHealth.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM is provisioned -- A qkview is generated from a unit with a large number of policies -- The qkview is uploaded to iHealth
bugs.impact: -- iHealth does not load part of the qkview. -- Downloading qkview file from iHealth, the asm_modules.xml file has been stripped in the fetched qkview data file. This occurs because of the 500 MB file size limit in iHealth. The file size of asm_module.xml can be huge because of per-policy/account signature tables, DCC.ACCOUNT_NEGSIG_SIGNATURE_PROPERTIES and PLC.PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SIGNATURES. Files that are not included in the qkview data because they are too larger are reported in the 'skipped_files' report in the root directory of the qkview data.

bugs.title: Broken layout in Threat Campaigns and Brute Force Attacks pages
bugs.symptoms: Horizontal scroll added to the page unnecessarily.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when viewing the Threat Campaigns or Brute Force Attacks page in any browser
bugs.impact: The horizontal scroll bar breaks the intended page layout.
bugs.fix: Layout fixed

bugs.title: GUI Browser Cache Timeout option is not available via tmsh
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP v10.x it was possible to change the browser cache timeout from bigpipe using the command: bigpipe httpd browsercachetimeout In 14.1.2.1 and newer, it is still possible to change the value in the GUI using "System :: Preferences :: Time To Cache Static Files. However there is no tmsh equivalent in any version.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when you try to configure the GUI browser cache timeout setting using tmsh.
bugs.impact: Unable to modify browser cache timeout except from GUI
bugs.workaround: Using GUI to configure this field. GUI System :: Preferences :: Time To Cache Static Files.

bugs.title: Client-ssl profiles derived from clientssl-quic fail validation
bugs.symptoms: After configuring a clientssl-quic profile, you get a validation error: 01b40001:3: A cipher group must be configured when TLS 1.3 is enabled (validation failed for profile /Common/clientssl-f5quic-udp).
bugs.conditions: This can occur when using the clientssl-quic built-in profile to build a profile that can serve HTTP/3 over QUIC.
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure a clientssl profile to work with HTTP/3 + QUIC that is also customized to serve the right certificate, etc.
bugs.workaround: Modify the clientssl-quic profile to have the following properties: cipher-group quic ciphers none This requires the following additional config objects: ltm cipher group quic { allow { quic { } } } ltm cipher rule quic { cipher TLS13-AES128-GCM-SHA256,TLS13-AES256-GCM-SHA384 description "Ciphers usable by QUIC" }
bugs.fix: Update the built-in configuration to pass validation.

bugs.title: Improve MPTCP's SYN/ACK retransmission handling
bugs.symptoms: - MPTCP enabled TCP connection is in SYN_RECEIVED state. - TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: - MPTCP is enabled. - SYN/ACK (with MP_JOIN or MP_CAPABLE) sent by the BIG-IP is not ACKed and needs to be retransmitted.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable MPTCP option in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: MPTCP's SYN/ACK retransmission handling is improved.

bugs.title: PAM_RHOST not set when authenticating BIG-IP using iControl REST
bugs.symptoms: The missing PAM_RHOST setting causes the radius packet to go out without the calling-station-id avp
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure radius server and add it to BIG-IP tmsh create auth radius system-auth servers add { myrad } 2. modify auth source type to radius tmsh modify auth source { type radius } 3. try to authenticate to BIG-IP using iControl REST
bugs.impact: Remote authentication using iControl REST is not allowed based on calling-station-id

bugs.title: ASM replies with JS-Challenge instead of blocking page upon "Virus detected" violation
bugs.symptoms: When ASM detects "virus" (with help of external icap server), the response page will be JS-Challenge instead of blocking.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy attached to a virtual server. -- Anti-Virus protection enabled in ASM policy. -- ASM finds a virus in a request.
bugs.impact: -- End user client gets JS-Challenge response instead of blocking page. -- End user does not see ASM support ID. -- Browser can run the JavaScript and resend the request to ASM, which is then forwarded to the backend server.
bugs.fix: The software now replies with the blocking page, including the ASM support ID.

bugs.title: Virtual server-to-virtual server with 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled can result in 'no trailing data' error
bugs.symptoms: A configuration with a virtual server-to-virtual server flow established, for example by the 'virtual' iRule command, and using a TCP stack with 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled, might encounter a race between the delayed ACK and the tail loss probe, which can lead to a tmm_panic or an OOPs message: no trailing data.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server-to-virtual server flow established. -- TCP profile with 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled. -- Certain timing related traffic scenario.
bugs.impact: TMM generates a core and reports an OOPs message: no trailing data.
bugs.workaround: Do not use a TCP stack with 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled in conjunction with a virtual server-to-virtual server flow configuration.
bugs.fix: Virtual server-to-virtual server with 'Tail Loss Probe' enabled can now be used without error.

bugs.title: Running cpcfg after first boot can result in daemons stuck in restart loop
bugs.symptoms: After running cpcfg and booting into the volume, daemons such as named and gtmd are stuck restarting. Additionally the SELinux audit log contains denial messages about gtmd and named being unable to read unlabeled_t files.
bugs.conditions: Running cpcfg on a volume that has already been booted into.
bugs.impact: Services do not come up.
bugs.workaround: In the bash shell, force SELinux to relabel at boot time. Then reboot: # touch /.autorelabel # reboot

bugs.title: ZoneRunner GUI is unable to display CAA records
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to manage a CAA record via the GUI shows an error: Resolver returned no such record.
bugs.conditions: -- Navigate to DNS :: Zones :: ZoneRunner :: Resource Record List :: Search All Records. -- Click on record of type CAA.
bugs.impact: Unable to update CAA records via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Manually edit the BIND configuration. -- Delete the record and create a new one with the desired changes.

bugs.title: Avrmail timeout is too small
bugs.symptoms: AVR report mailer times out prematurely and reports errors: AVRExpMail|ERROR|2019-11-26 21:01:08 ECT|avrmail.php:325| PHPMailer exception while trying to send the report: SMTP Error: data not accepted.
bugs.conditions: Configure reports, which will be sent to e-mail
bugs.impact: Error response from SMTP server, and the report is not sent
bugs.workaround: Increase timeout in avrmail.php via bash commands
bugs.fix: The timeout was increased in avrmail.php

bugs.title: Scheduled reports are sent via TLS even if configured as non encrypted
bugs.symptoms: The scheduled report email is sent from BIG-IP using TLS even if configured to not use encryption. When the mail server TLS is outdated it may lead to failure of the mail delivery.
bugs.conditions: The scheduled reports are enabled and configured to use a mail server which reports TLS capability.
bugs.impact: The minor impact is unexpected behaviour. In rare cases it may lead to malfunction of the scheduled reports.
bugs.fix: The automatic TLS connection was introduced via udate of the phpmailer module. The current fix disables automatic behaviour such that encryption will be used according to BIG-IP configuration.

bugs.title: Unbalanced trunk distribution on i4x00 and 4000 platforms with odd number of members.
bugs.symptoms: For the i4x00 and 4000 platforms, egress trunk distribution will be unbalanced if the number of trunk members is not a power of 2.
bugs.conditions: A trunk is configured with an odd number of trunk interfaces or a trunk member goes down such that the number of working members is odd.
bugs.impact: Uneven traffic distribution. Some interfaces will see more traffic than others.
bugs.workaround: Insure the number of trunk interfaces is a power of 2: 2, 4, or 8.

bugs.title: Incorrect value (icmpv6) is used when RuleList/Rule/Protocol is set to ICMPv6 via UI.
bugs.symptoms: /config/bigip_base.conf fails with following error Syntax Error:(/config/bigip_base.conf at line: 619) "ip-protocol" unknown protocol "icmpv6"
bugs.conditions: From WebUI, user configures Rule List -> Rule -> Protocol and selects "icmpv6" from drop down
bugs.impact: Failure to load configuration during upgrade or discovery by BIG-IQ
bugs.workaround: Set the protocol attribute via tmsh modify security firewall rule-list test rules modify { test { ip-protocol ipv6-icmp } }
bugs.fix: The correct value is ipv6-icmp. This value is now set.

bugs.title: QUIC congestion window sometimes increases inappropriately
bugs.symptoms: When QUIC is discovering the link bandwidth, it sometimes increases the congestion window when there is not enough available data to use the existing congestion window.
bugs.conditions: When the application is not generating enough data, or any streams with data are stream flow control limited.
bugs.impact: In some cases, the congestion window can be too large for the path and cause packet losses if it is later fully utilized.
bugs.fix: Correctly check for data limitations before increasing congestion window.

bugs.title: Internet Explorer restart is required after VPN plugin is upgraded to 12.1.5
bugs.symptoms: After browser components are updated and user tries to establish VPN from Internet Explorer, user sees an error message saying 'Failed to initialize local Tunnel Server'.
bugs.conditions: - User established VPN from Internet Explorer before using older F5 Internet Explorer browser plugin - The same instance of Internet Explorer is used to establish VPN after BIG-IP was upgraded to 12.1.5
bugs.impact: VPN cannot be established until user restarts browser.
bugs.workaround: Restart browser.

bugs.title: Panic in TMM due to internal mirroring interactions
bugs.symptoms: The Traffic Management Microkernel suddenly restarts due to a SIGSEGV segmentation fault.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is being used. -- Connection mirroring is being used.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuring connection mirroring when APM is being used.

bugs.title: Unexpected differences in child policies when using BIG-IQ to change learning mode on parent policies
bugs.symptoms: After changing a parent policy's learning mode or other learning attributes in policy-builder settings, deploying the policy will result in differences in the child policies.
bugs.conditions: On BIG-IP and BIG-IQ: 1. Parent policy has a policy-building section that is inherited. 2. Child policy has wildcard default (*) elements such as urls. On BIG-IQ: 3. Change parent learning mode from manual to disabled or vice versa 4. Deploy changes
bugs.impact: There are differences after deploy.
bugs.workaround: Discover and deploy again from BIG-IQ
bugs.fix: Changes are deployed from BIG-IQ without causing unexpected changes.

bugs.title: The list processing time (xx seconds) exceeded the interval value. There may be too many monitor instances configured with a xx second interval.
bugs.symptoms: Messages similar to the following may be seen in the DNS (GTM) logs: The list processing time (32 seconds) exceeded the interval value. There may be too many monitor instances configured with a 30 second interval. This message was introduced in 15.0.0 as an aid to help identifying overloaded DNS (GTM) systems, but it triggers too easily and can be logged when the device is not overloaded.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS (GTM) servers are present. -- Virtual servers are configured on those DNS (GTM) servers. -- A monitor is applied to the DNS (GTM) server.
bugs.impact: Messages are logged that imply the system is overloaded when it is not.
bugs.workaround: Create a log filter to suppress the messages sys log-config filter gtm-warn { level warn message-id 011ae116 source gtmd }

bugs.title: APM Portal Access: Base URL may be set to incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, Portal Access may set an incorrect value for the Base URL used in rewritten JavaScript code.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page - JavaScript code inside the page
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to correct Base URL value inside rewritten page.
bugs.fix: APM Portal Access now sets the correct Base URL value.

bugs.title: Default Apache testing page is reachable at <mgmt-ip>/noindex
bugs.symptoms: For BIG-IP v14.1.x and later, the default testing page of the Apache web-server is accessible at <mgmt-ip>/noindex.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when navigating to the /noindex page from the web browser.
bugs.impact: Limited information about the Apache web server and its operating system is available to users with access to the mgmt port interface.
bugs.fix: /noindex now returns a 403 Forbidden Error Response.

bugs.title: Client port reuse causes RST when the backend server-side connection is open
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system or SSL Orchestrator does not close server-side connections when the security service closes the connection with the BIG-IP or SSL Orchestrator. So if client reuses the port, SSL Orchestrator rejects new connections by sending RST.
bugs.conditions: -- Service profile is attached to virtual server. or -- SSL Orchestrator is licensed and provisioned and Service chain is added in the security policy. -- Security service closes the server-side connection with SSL Orchestrator. -- Client reuses the source port.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system or SSL Orchestrator rejects new connection from clients when a client reuses the port.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system or SSL Orchestrator no longer rejects the client connection when the client reuses the port.

bugs.title: Upgrading from versions 11.5.x or 11.6.x to 13.1.0 or later breaks trust with BIG-IQ
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system running versions 11.5.x or 11.6.x is upgraded to 13.1.0 or later, if the system is being managed by BIG-IQ, the device can no longer be managed by BIG-IQ (including re-discovery), and reports an error: Error getting resource provisioning from /mgmt/tm/sys/provision on x.y (n.n.n.n), Authorization failure - you may need to remove the device from BIG-IQ and add it again to reestablish trust.
bugs.conditions: -- Adding a BIG-IP system running software versions 11.5.x or 11.6.x to BIG-IQ and upgrading the device to 13.1.0 or later. Note: This issue occurs only on BIG-IP devices running software versions 11.5.x, regardless of BIG-IQ version. BIG-IP devices running versions 12.0.0 or higher are not expected to result in lost trust on upgrade to 13.1.x.
bugs.impact: The device is no longer manageable by BIG-IQ. This occurs because of the underlying mechanism for the issue: when establishing trust with a BIG-IQ device, the BIG-IP keeps a record of that establishment in its REST storage. Upon upgrade from 11.5.x to a higher version, the BIG-IP system does not preserve that piece of information; preserving the information became a part of the upgrade process for 12.0.0 and later. At version 13.1.0, BIG-IP configurations began stricter enforcement of preauthorized devices, as a purposeful security measure. Information vital to 13.1.x authorization requirements is no longer present for BIG-IP devices added to BIG-IQ while at 11.5.x and subsequently upgraded. The end result is that a BIG-IQ device managing a 13.1.x device for which trust was established in the 11.5.x version now is unable to fully validate the trust credentials.
bugs.workaround: The workaround for this issue is to preemptively remove and re-add a problematic BIG-IP device while at version 12.x or 13.0.x prior to the upgrade to version 13.1.x or later. The method for reestablishing trust after upgrade is to remove the device from BIG-IQ and then add it back. In this case, the entire BIG-IP configuration, including all the previously deployed apps, are preserved on upgrade. Once the device is re-added/rediscovered, the BIG-IQ will import its configuration, including the apps.

bugs.title: ASM policies may not load after upgrading to 14.x or later from a previous major version
bugs.symptoms: ASM policies may not load immediately after upgrade due to SELinux policies issues relating to the upgrade process.
bugs.conditions: 1. ASM is provisioned. 2. One or more ASM Security Policies is attached to one or more virtual servers. 3. Upgrade from v12.x or v13.x to v14.x or later.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not processed properly after upgrade due to failure to load ASM policies.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds. -- Remove ASM Policies while upgrading: 1. Prior to upgrade, remove all ASM Security Policies from all virtual servers. 2. Upgrade. 3. Reassociate each ASM Security Policy with its original virtual server. -- Restore the UCS on a new boot location after upgrade: 1. Prior to upgrade, create a UCS. 2. Upgrade or create a new instance of the software version at the target location. 3. Restore the UCS at the new location.
bugs.fix: ASM policies now load as expected after upgrading to 14.x or later from a previous major version.

bugs.title: Violation Occurrences section of event logs missing info
bugs.symptoms: There is information missing in the Violation Occurrences section of the event logs.
bugs.conditions: Viewing event logs in an ASM configuration with multiple Attack Types (e.g., Detection Evasion, HTTP Parser Attack).
bugs.impact: The Violation Occurrences section of the event log reports only the following: HTTP protocol compliance failed [1]. There should also be the following: Evasion technique detected [1]

bugs.title: The client-side connection of a dhcpv4_fwd profile on Broadcast DHCP-Relay Virtual Server never expires from the connection table
bugs.symptoms: The client-side connection of the dhcpv4_fwd profile on Broadcast DHCP-Relay Virtual Server never expires from the connection table.
bugs.conditions: Configure dhcpv4_fwd profile on Broadcast DHCP-Relay Virtual Server.
bugs.impact: Even after correcting the listener to use dhcpv4 (relay) instead of dhcpv4_fwd (forwarding) profile, the client-side connection from the dhcpv4_fwd profile remains.
bugs.workaround: Delete the long-standing connection from the connection table.

bugs.title: ASM causes high mcpd CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: -- CPU utilization is high on the odd-numbered cores. -- Messages appear at 60-second intervals in /var/log/ts/asm_start.log: update_GTM_score
bugs.conditions: -- One or more virtual servers have FTP/SMTP/WEBSEC profiles attached to it. -- ASM configured.
bugs.impact: Elevated CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: -- On the BIG-IP system, edit the file /etc/ts/tools/nwd.cfg to change the value EnforcerCpuReportTimeInterval from 60 to a higher value, e.g., 3600 for once an hour, or even larger. -- Restart ASM: bigstart restart asm
bugs.fix: This issue has been resolved so that CPU usage is no longer elevated under these conditions.

bugs.title: Traps that were disabled are enabled after configuration save
bugs.symptoms: The ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable setting is not saved to config files nor UCS. If you have disabled 'link up/down' traps for an interface, save the config, and then load the config files or UCS, all interfaces will have traps enabled, even the ones that were explicitly disabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Disable 'link up/down' traps for an interface. -- Save the configuration or UCS. -- Reload the configuration or load the UCS.
bugs.impact: All interfaces have traps enabled, even the ones that were explicitly disabled.

bugs.title: GUI: virtual server from NOT Common partition can be selected during creation policy in Common partition
bugs.symptoms: If you create a policy in the Common partition, then virtual servers from the other non-Common partitions are visible and can be selected when they should not be visible.
bugs.conditions: 1)Create partition First 2)Create default policy with virtual server in partition First 3)Switch partition to Common 4)Go to "Security ›› Application Security : Security Policies : Policies List" 5)Create new policy and look at list of available virtual servers to select
bugs.impact: Virtual server from non-Common partitions can be selected during creation of a policy in the Common partition
bugs.fix: Only virtual servers from Common partition can be selected during creation policy in Common partition.

bugs.title: Cached results for a record are sent following region modification
bugs.symptoms: Changing the contents of a topology region record may result in DNS queries temporarily being directed as if the change had not happened for queries from the IP address of the last end user client to use topology load balancing.
bugs.conditions: -- A client at a single IP address makes multiple queries that are load balanced using topology, both before and after a change to a topology region record, where that change also modifies the result the single client receives. -- If a query from a different client IP address is received and load balanced using topology, then the issue is corrected until the next change to a topology region record.
bugs.impact: After changing the contents of a topology region record, the last end user client to send a query before the change may receive the wrong load balancing decision if the change affected that decision. Queries from other end user clients are load balanced correctly and cause the issue to go away until the next topology region record change.
bugs.workaround: This issue can be temporarily corrected by sending a DNS query that is load balanced using topology after making changes to region records.
bugs.fix: The system now handles regions item changes as expected, so this issue no longer occurs.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when using "SSL::extensions insert"
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: iRule with "SSL::extensions insert"
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Remote logger violation_details field content appears as "N/A" when violations field is not selected.
bugs.symptoms: When remote logger is enabled and violation_details field is selected for output, but violations field is not selected - content of violation_details field appears as "N/A".
bugs.conditions: - Remote logger is enabled; - violation_details field is selected for output; - violations field is not selected for output; - violation is detected and reported to remote logger.
bugs.impact: Remote logger will not contain violation_details in report.
bugs.workaround: Enable violations field for remote logging.
bugs.fix: ASM code was fixed to report violation_details field independently of violations field.

bugs.title: AVRD core due to a try to load vip lookup when AVRD is down
bugs.symptoms: AVRD cores during startup.
bugs.conditions: Avrd receives a SIGTERM while it is starting.
bugs.impact: This can lead to an AVRD core.
bugs.fix: Added some more checks while loading new configuration. Suppose to reduce the frequent of these occurrences. Still can happen in very rare occasions.

bugs.title: Bot Defense "User Agent Spoofing" Anomaly False Positive using Firefox on Fedora
bugs.symptoms: Firefox browser, when running on Fedora Distribution, which accesses the Virtual Server which has Bot Defense profile could trigger a false positive of the "User Agent Spoofing" anomaly.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is associated with the Virtual Server -- Client uses Firefox running on Fedora GNU/Linux
bugs.impact: The client may get blocked.
bugs.workaround: On the Bot Defense Profile, add an exception to "User Agent Spoofing" with the action set to Alarm or None.
bugs.fix: Firefox browsers running on Fedora GNU/Linux no longer trigger the User Agent Spoofing anomaly.

bugs.title: Cert-LDAP returning only first entry in the sequence that matches san-other oid
bugs.symptoms: Certificate-ldap only returns the first matching oid from the certificate file even though multiple matching san-other entries exists
bugs.conditions: When Certificate-ladp attribute ssl-cname-field set to san-other and certificate with multiple san-other oids
bugs.impact: Only the first matching oid is returned.

bugs.title: 100G modules may not work properly in i15000 and i15800 platforms
bugs.symptoms: The tuning values programmed in the switch are not correct for 100G OPT-0039 and OPT-0031 SFP modules.
bugs.conditions: -- Using OPT-0039 or OPT-0031 modules. -- Running on i15000 and i15800 platforms. Note: Use 'tmsh list net interface vendor-partnum', to identify the optic modules installed.
bugs.impact: You might see traffic drop. Note: Potential issues related to incorrect tuning values come from F5-internal sources and have not been reported in production configurations.

bugs.title: Bgpd might crash when outputting the results of a tmsh show command: "sh bgp ipv6 ::/0"
bugs.symptoms: When BGP tries to print the address of the default route's peer but there is no matching address for IPv4 or IPv6 so the system returns a NULL and attempting to print results in a crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Running the show command: sh bgp ipv6 ::/0. -- There is no matching IPv4 or IPv6 address for the peer. The conditions that cause this to occur are unknown.
bugs.impact: Bgdp crashes. Routing may be affected while bgpd restarts.

bugs.title: TMM crash following DNS resolve with Bot Defense profile
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when Bot Defense is enabled and network DNS is configured.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when is Bot Defense enabled and network DNS is configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when Bot Defense is enabled and network DNS is configured.

bugs.title: Validation of monitor field fails in transaction
bugs.symptoms: Validation of monitor destination/address fails if used with transactions. The transaction consists of two operations: a delete and a create (with a new destination). This passes validation on the BIG-IP system where the change was made. However when the change is synced to the peer, it fails validation on the peer.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create monitor destination/address in transaction. -- Delete monitor. -- Create monitor with destination as *:80 and *:*. 2. Sync to peer.
bugs.impact: It passes validation on BIG-IP but fails on config sync to the peer.
bugs.workaround: In order to get the devices back in sync, run config sync with force-full-load-push.

bugs.title: WCCP crashes on "ServiceGroup size exceeded" exception
bugs.symptoms: Under general usage; WCCP crashes with a "ServiceGroup size exceeded" exception.
bugs.conditions: Have WCCP service groups configured.
bugs.impact: WCCP throws an exception and crashes.

bugs.title: SSL::collect and SSL::release in an iRule causes connection reset
bugs.symptoms: Using SSL::collect and SSL::release in an iRule alongside a policy with a 'Set Variable' action resets the connection, and reports an error: 01220001:3: TCL error: no connection established SSL::collect needs an established connection! (line 1) invoked from within "SSL::collect".
bugs.conditions: -- SSL::collect and SSL::release in an iRule. -- Policy with a 'Set Variable' action.
bugs.impact: The system resets the connection.

bugs.title: BD crash on specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: BD crash on specific scenario
bugs.conditions: A brute force attack mitigation using captcha or client side challenge.
bugs.impact: BD crash, failover.
bugs.workaround: Add an iRule that removes the query string from the referrer header only for the login page POSTs.

bugs.title: Wrong FDB table entries with same MAC and wrong VLAN combination
bugs.symptoms: Forwarding DataBase (FDB) table has duplicate MAC entries with the incorrect VLANs. MAC entries are correct in the switch but not in the control plane.
bugs.conditions: Enable L2Wire.
bugs.impact: Duplicate MAC entries with incorrect VLANs in FDB table.
bugs.workaround: Restart bcm56xxd: bigstart restart bcm56xxd Note: You can use tmsh to see the table: tmsh -m show net fdb

bugs.title: AFM FQDN Resolver does not honor Refresh Interval during or after disruption
bugs.symptoms: Unbound uses default host-ttl (900) and it cannot be customized.
bugs.conditions: Always.
bugs.impact: DNS queries can take up to 15 minutes to fail (default host-ttl time) if the server is down.
bugs.fix: "host-ttl" is now configurable via TMSH.

bugs.title: Unexpected reset upon long requests when ip is whitelisted
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected reset upon big requests when ip is whitelisted
bugs.conditions: The request exceeds max buffer size violation is turned on. The source IP is set to never block.
bugs.impact: The request is answered with a reset.
bugs.workaround: A workaround is to turn on session tracking on the same policy. You may turn off all the other properties for the session tracking (so it won't do anything).
bugs.fix: Added more scenarios where unblock can't actually happen and the long request will be enforced only in the headers.

bugs.title: ASM GUI and REST become unresponsive upon license change
bugs.symptoms: When there is a license change at the same time as a security update (ex. Threat Campaigns or Attack Signatures), the system can reach a deadlock which blocks some operations, eventually leading to all the REST threads becoming blocked and unresponsive.
bugs.conditions: A license change occurs at the same time as a security update (ex. Threat Campaigns or Attack Signatures).
bugs.impact: ASM user interfaces are unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Kill asm_config_server.pl or restart ASM
bugs.fix: Fixed the deadlock race condition.

bugs.title: Diameter Mirror connection lost on the standby due to "process ingress error"
bugs.symptoms: In MRF/Diameter deployment, mirrored connections on the standby may be lost when the "process ingress error" log is observed only on the standby, and there is no matching log on the active.
bugs.conditions: This can happen when there is a large amount of mirror traffic, this includes the traffic processed by the active that requires mirroring and the high availability (HA) context synchronization such as persistence information, message state, etc.
bugs.impact: Diameter mirror connections are lost on the standby. When failover occurs, these connections may need to reconnect.
bugs.fix: Diameter mirror connection no longer lost due to "process ingress error" when there is high mirror traffic.

bugs.title: Add option to exclude stats collection in qkview to avoid very large data files
bugs.symptoms: Statistics collection may cause qkview files to be too large for the iHealth service to parse, or may cause memory allocation errors: qkview: tmstat_map_file: mmap: Cannot allocate memory qkview: tmstat_subscribe: /var/tmstat/blade/tmm5: Cannot allocate memory at 0xa08a938
bugs.conditions: Qkview is executed on an appliance or chassis that has a very large configuration.
bugs.impact: Qkview files may not be able to be parsed by the iHealth service. Also, memory allocation error messages may be displayed when generating qkview.
bugs.fix: Qkview now has a -x option that can be used to exclude statistics collection in the stat_module.xml file.
bugs.behavior: Qkview now has a -x option that can be used to exclude statistics collection.

bugs.title: JWK keys frequency does not support fewer than 60 minutes
bugs.symptoms: When configuring the OAuth provider and trying to set the task frequency to fewer than 60 minutes, the BIG-IP reports an error: 01b70003:3: Discovery interval (10) for OAuth provider must be greater than (60) minutes.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when configuring the frequency interval of an OAuth provider to a value lower than 60 minutes.
bugs.impact: You are unable to create a provider with a frequency interval of fewer than 60 minutes.
bugs.workaround: Use a value of 60 minutes or higher.
bugs.fix: Auto discovery frequency now supported values lower than 60 minutes.

bugs.title: Client port reuse causes RST when the security service attempts server connection reuse.
bugs.symptoms: If the security service attempts server connection reuse, client port reuse causes RST on new connections.
bugs.conditions: -- Service profile is attached to virtual server. or -- SSL Orchestrator (SSLO) is licensed and provisioned and Service chain is added in the security policy. -- Security service reuses server-side connection. -- Client reuses the source port.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system or SSLO rejects new connection from clients when a client reuses the port.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system or SSLO no longer rejects the client connection when the service tries to the reuse server connection and the client reuses the port.

bugs.title: Improvement to MRF DIAMETER to select automatic removal of a persistence entry on completion of a transaction
bugs.symptoms: MRF DIAMETER is not DIAMETER-application aware. It does not have application-specific business logic. When creating a DIAMETER solution, BIG-IP operators often need to write iRule scripts that remove a session persistence entry at the end of a transaction.
bugs.conditions: Some applications require removal of the persistence entry upon successful completion of a transaction. Other applications require removal upon unsuccessful completion of a transaction.
bugs.impact: iRule script is required.
bugs.workaround: Systems requiring automatic removal of a session persistence entry must write iRule scripts that inspect the answer message for its success and then use the DIAMETER::persist reset iRule command.
bugs.fix: It is not possible to instruct the system to automatically remove a persistence entry based on the result status of a answer message.

bugs.title: TMM may sometimes core when HTTP-MR proxy attempts to go into passthrough mode
bugs.symptoms: TMM may sometimes core when HTTPMR proxy attempts to go into passthrough mode
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile is attached to the virtual. -- httprouter profile is attached to the virtual. -- HTTP goes into passthrough mode for any of the variety of reasons.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer cores when HTTP-MR proxy attempts goes into passthrough mode.

bugs.title: Missing MaxMemory Attribute
bugs.symptoms: The MaxMemory Attribute is not reported in the System Monitor statistics report.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when viewing the System Monitor report.
bugs.impact: No 'MaxMemory' value label appears in System Monitor statistics. Instead, there are duplicate AvgMemory fields, for example: ...(AvgMemory='3818',AvgMemory='3818').
bugs.workaround: Use the AvgMemory value that is the higher of the two to represent MaxMemory. Note: Sometimes, the AvgMemory and MaxMemory values are the same. In that case, use the second value.
bugs.fix: The MaxMemory attribute is now reported in System Monitor statistics.

bugs.title: Empty HSTS headers when HSTS mode for HTTP profile is disabled
bugs.symptoms: HTTP Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) headers have an empty value for some APM Access Policy-generated responses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- HTTP profile is configured with HSTS mode=disabled (which it is by default). -- HTTP requests for APM renderer content, including CSS, JS, and image files from the webtop.
bugs.impact: Some audit scanners can consider the empty value of Strict-Transport-Security headers as a vulnerability. For browsers, the empty HSTS value equals no HSTS in response.
bugs.workaround: 1. Enable HSTS mode for the HTTP profile. 2. Use an iRule to remove the empty HSTS header from responses: when HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE { if { [HTTP::header value "Strict-Transport-Security"] eq "" } { HTTP::header remove "Strict-Transport-Security" } }
bugs.fix: When the HTTP profile is configured with HSTS mode=disabled, responses from APM renderer content are now sent without an HSTS header.

bugs.title: The TMM pages used and available can be viewed in the F5 system stats MIB
bugs.symptoms: The memory pages available and in use are tracked with system statistics. Previously those statistics were available only with the tmctl command in the shell.
bugs.conditions: When system resource decisions are being made, the information about memory usage is important.
bugs.impact: It is not feasible to query each BIG-IP device separately.
bugs.fix: You can query these statistics with SNMP through the F5-BIGIP-SYSTEM-MIB::sysTmmPagesStat table.

bugs.title: Portal Access: F5_Inflate_onclick wrapper functionality needs refining
bugs.symptoms: Event handler defined on DOM elements is not executed properly, and some events on a page like onClick() are not executed properly.
bugs.conditions: -- Portal access enabled. -- Rewrite enabled. -- New value of event handler is equal to inline handler already set for the element.
bugs.impact: Web application does not operate as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule, for example, an iRule that redefines F5_Inflate_onclick: Note: In the following iRule, substitute <PATH_TO_PAGE> with the page in your web application. when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "<PATH_TO_PAGE>" } { # log "URI=([HTTP::path])" # Found the file to modify REWRITE::post_process 1 set do_it 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { if {[info exists do_it]} { unset do_it set strt [string first {<script>try} [REWRITE::payload]] if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt 0 { <script> (function(){ var ioc = F5_Inflate_onclick; F5_Inflate_onclick = function(o, incr, v) { if (v === o.onclick && typeof v === 'function') { return v; } return ioc.call(this,o,incr,v); } })(); </script> } } } }

bugs.title: Load balancing IPsec tunnels
bugs.symptoms: IPsec can experience packet loss on oversubscribed TMM instances (reaching 100% CPU transiently or consistently) and other TMM instances do not share the load.
bugs.conditions: -- A large number of IPsec tunnels. -- The Security Associations (SAs) associated with IPsec tunnels are not balanced across TMMs. -- Other TMMs are less busy.
bugs.impact: If random assignment of IPsec tunnels to TMM instances results in one TMM needing more than 100% CPU to handle all the traffic, packets are lost. When packets are lost, they are retransmitted, and BIG-IP network performance drops in proportion to the packet loss.
bugs.fix: The following sys db variables offer better tmm load balancing for IPsec tunnels. By default these variables are zero. tmsh modify sys db ipsec.sp.owner value 1 tmsh modify sys db ipsec.sp.migrate value 1 tmsh modify sys db ipsec.pfkey.load value 2 F5 strongly recommends that these values only be set under the direction of F5 Support, Consultants or Pre-Sales engineers. This issue occurs only in extreme cases. TMM instances can be CPU pinned by other traffic outside of IPsec, so it is critical to first ascertain that IPsec traffic is resulting in poor TMM performance before implementing the variables. Notation "sp" refers to an IPsec object where tunnel SAs live. Variable ipsec.sp.owner controls whether these have a tmm owner that can be assigned. Variable ipsec.sp.migrate controls whether tunnels can migrate automatically based on CPU load. Variable ipsec.pfkey.load controls frequency of inter-TMM messages about CPU load to enable load-balancing decisions. The value of ipsec.pfkey.load is seconds between CPU load update messages. The highest possible frequency is once a second, for value "1". Any value larger than 4 or 5 seconds runs a risk of using CPU load information too out-of-date to accurately balance load.

bugs.title: Fetching ASM policy list from the GUI (in LTM policy rule creation) occasionally causes REST timeout
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to associate new ASM policies to LTM policies, due to REST timeout.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered when there are a large number of policies configured in ASM.
bugs.impact: Unable to associate new ASM policies to LTM policies, due to rest timeout.
bugs.fix: Modified REST query to get only fullPath to display the list of policies, so the timeout no longer occurs.

bugs.title: Outbound TFTP and Active FTP no longer work by default over the management port
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use TFTP or Active FTP at the BIG-IP management port to transfer files to a remote system, the connection eventually times out and the file is not transferred. This is expected behavior resulting from the enhancement made in BIG-IP v14.1.0: "Support for network firewall rules on the management port" :: https://techdocs.f5.com/kb/en-us/products/BIG-IP_ltm/releasenotes/product/relnote-bigip-14-1-0.html#rn_ltm-tmos_1410_new. When attempting to use TFTP and Active FTP via tmm interfaces will work as it has the necessary Algorithm capabilities to set up return listeners.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP v14.1.0 or greater. - Attempt to initiate TFTP or Active FTP from the BIG-IP management port through command line.
bugs.impact: Unable to use TFTP or Active FTP to transfer files to/from the BIG-IP system over management port
bugs.workaround: Consider using encrypted transport (sftp, scp, etc.) in order to avoid the exposure of sensitive data, including passwords. Manually load connection tracking for the necessary protocol(s) from the command line with: modprobe nf_conntrack_ftp modprobe nf_conntrack_tftp

bugs.title: ixlv: double tagging is not working
bugs.symptoms: If a VLAN tag is configured on the Virtual Function in the host, and the BIG-IP guest is configured to use a tagged VLAN, packets that egress the host on this VLAN contain only the VLAN tag configured on the host (i.e. the BIG-IP's VLAN tag is lost).
bugs.conditions: - Using a BIG-IP VE. - A VLAN tag is configured on both the host VF and on the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP's VLAN tag is lost.
bugs.fix: Both VLAN tags are now present in packets.

bugs.title: New SNMP authentication type and privacy protocol algorithms not available in UI
bugs.symptoms: Unable to configure the new SNMP authentication type and privacy protocol algorithms from the BIG-IP Configuration utility.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP with Net-SNMP libraries version 5.8.
bugs.impact: The new authentication type and privacy protocol algorithms cannot be configured through the BIG-IP Configuration Utility.
bugs.workaround: Specify the auth-protocol and privacy-protocol values using TMSH, following is an example: modify /sys snmp users add { <user> { access rw security-level auth-privacy auth-protocol sha256 auth-password defaultPassword privacy-protocol aes-192 privacy-password defaultPassword username <user> } }

bugs.title: Systemd not deleting user journals
bugs.symptoms: When setting 'SystemMaxUse' to any value, systemd does not honor this limit, and the specified size is exceeded.
bugs.conditions: Using a non-TMOS user account with external authentication permission. Note: Systemd-journald is configured to create a user journal for every remote user that logs into the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Journald filling up the file system. These journals are allocated with a minimum size of 4MiB and are not removed when the log entries age-out.
bugs.workaround: Option 1: To immediately free up space, manually remove per-user journal logs from the following location: /var/log/journal/*/user-* Option 2: To prevent the system from creating these journal files going forward: 1. Edit /etc/systemd/journald.conf and add the following at the bottom of the file: SplitMode=none 2. Restart systemd-journal service # systemctl restart systemd-journald 3. Delete the existing user journal files from /var/log # rm /var/log/journal/*/user-* Note: -- You must apply this workaround separately to each blade of a VIPRION or vCMP guest running on a VIPRION. -- You must reapply this workaround after performing software installations.

bugs.title: CONNECT_RESET_ERROR is reported when Subroutine Timeout is reached for HTTP connections
bugs.symptoms: The system reports a CONNECT_RESET_ERROR when the Subroutine Timeout is reached for HTTP connections.
bugs.conditions: You do not proceed with a policy action within a subroutine until the subroutine timeout interval is reached.
bugs.impact: You cannot complete Per-Request Policy definition after a long period of inactivity.
bugs.fix: You can now restart the Per-Request Policy Subroutine for a certain period after Subroutine Timeout is reached. The previous behavior was to reject requests for expired subroutine with CONNECTION_RESET_ERROR.
bugs.behavior: You can now restart the Per-Request Policy Subroutine for a certain period after the subroutine timeout interval passes. The previous behavior was to reject requests when the expired Subroutine Timeout was reached for HTTP connections, at which point the system reported the CONNECTION_RESET_ERROR.

bugs.title: Error: Invalid self IP, the IP address already exists.
bugs.symptoms: When loading a configuration, the config load fails with an error: Invalid self IP, the IP address <ip_addr> already exists.
bugs.conditions: -- Config contains an IPv4 SelfIP -- Config contains an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address that is assigned to the same vlan BIG-IP does not prevent you from creating this condition and will allow you to save it.
bugs.impact: During configuration load will fail: 0107176c:3: Invalid self IP, the IP address <ip_addr> already exists. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: Delete one of the SelfIP addresses and load the configuration.

bugs.title: Methods Missing From ASM Policy
bugs.symptoms: If the ASM http-methods are missing from the MCP configuration, importing an XML ASM policy creates a policy that has no allowed methods and will block all traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system configuration is loaded without the required asm_base.conf. -- An XML ASM policy is loaded.
bugs.impact: All traffic is blocked for the policy.
bugs.workaround: Recreate the required methods (GET, POST, etc.) in the policy.
bugs.fix: Lack of defined ASM http-methods in MCP no longer affects policy loading.

bugs.title: The allow-only-in-enterprise LAN feature on Mac OS not working after reboot
bugs.symptoms: Firewall feature on Mac devices does not work after reboot, if the device connects to a hotspot network immediately after reboot
bugs.conditions: -- End user client is using a Mac device. -- Edge Client is in 'Always Connected' mode. -- allow-only-in-enterprise LAN is enabled. -- The Mac device is rebooted.
bugs.impact: The device is able to connect to the Internet after reboot, but not to the internal network.
bugs.fix: The allow-only-in-enterprise LAN feature now works correctly on a Mac device after a reboot.

bugs.title: LCD touch panel reports "Firmware update in progress" indefinitely
bugs.symptoms: After a software upgrade that includes an LCD firmware update, the LCD touch panel may remain stuck reporting an error indefinitely / for longer than 30 minutes: Firmware update in Progress may take up to 30 minutes.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: -- You have one of the following BIG-IP platforms: * i850 * i2x00 * i4x00 * i5x00 * i7x00 * i10x00 * i11x00 * i15x00 * HRC-i2x00 * HRC-i5x00 * HRC-i10x00 -- You perform a software upgrade that updates the firmware on the LCD touch panel, e.g. upgrading from BIG-IP v13.1.x to BIG-IP v14.1.x or newer.
bugs.impact: The system is functional, but the LCD displays the firmware update screen indefinitely. The LCD cannot be used while it is frozen on the firmware update warning screen.
bugs.workaround: Important: Before attempting this workaround, check that there are no indications the system is still performing a firmware update (such as a terminal prompt), and that the following messages can be found in /var/log/ltm after the most recent boot: notice chmand[6302]: 012a0005:5: firmware update succeeded. notice chmand[6302]: 012a0005:5: Firmware check finished. These messages indicates that the firmware update has finished, and the LCD is displaying the warning screen in error, so it is safe to perform the workaround. Reboot the BIG-IP system to return the LCD to normal operation. After a reboot of the BIG-IP operating system, the LCD touch panel should be responsive.

bugs.title: Need to be able to set a higher Subroutine timeout value
bugs.symptoms: The Subroutine Timeout value for a Per-Request Access Policy cannot be set higher than 300 seconds (5 minutes).
bugs.conditions: This is encountered while configuring per-request access policies.
bugs.impact: You are unable to set a subroutine timeout value longer than five minutes.
bugs.fix: Maximum allowed value for Subroutine Timeout in Per-Request Access Policy was increased to 900 seconds (15 minutes).
bugs.behavior: The maximum allowed value for Subroutine Timeout in a Per-Request Access Policy is now 900 seconds (15 minutes). In previous releases, it was 300 seconds (5 minutes).

bugs.title: URL for IFRAME element may not be normalized in some cases
bugs.symptoms: Client JavaScript may see a non-normalized URL for the IFRAME HTML element in Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: - Original HTML page contains IFRAME element with relative URL - JavaScript code reads this URL from the IFRAME element
bugs.impact: The URL for IFRAME element is not normalized and the web application may not work correctly in Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to correct the returned IFRAME URL in rewritten JavaScript code. There is no generic iRule pattern; the correction depends on actual JavaScript code, but you can use the following example as a template: when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] ... } { # use appropriate selection for URI set correct_location 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { if {[info exists correct_location]} { unset correct_location # look for the piece of code to be corrected set str2find {...} # use appropriate pattern for rewritten code set str_len [string length $str2find] set strt [string first $str2find [REWRITE::payload]] # make replacement using appropriate corrected code if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt $str_len {...} } } }

bugs.title: Active Rules for Route Domain are not listed in GUI inline editor
bugs.symptoms: Route domain does not show attached policies.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the foloowjg scenario: 1. Configure Route domain with Firewall policy. 2. In Security :: Network Firewall :: Active rules, select specified Route Domain to view policy details. 3. Set the Inline Rule Editor option in Security :: Options :: Network Firewall :: Firewall Options Inline Rule Editor to Enabled.
bugs.impact: Cannot see policy information for Route Domains.
bugs.workaround: Use legacy Active rules editor. To do so, set the Security :: Options :: Network Firewall :: Firewall Options Inline Rule Editor option to Disabled.

bugs.title: Route Domain Active Rules stats are cleared when a rule list is modified
bugs.symptoms: In the Active Rules page, when you select a Route Domain context, then modify this policy to add a new rule and then cancel the new rule, the new rule is removed, but the count values of the other rules are reset to 0.
bugs.conditions: New rule is canceled before addition.
bugs.impact: Active Rules stats are cleared when a rule list is modified. Incorrect stats are reported.

bugs.title: Remote syslog server cannot parse violation detail buffers as UTF-8.
bugs.symptoms: Remote syslog server is unable to properly parse the violation detail buffers as UTF-8.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the violation detail buffers contain double-byte/non-UTF characters, due to requests that contain non-ASCII UTF-8 characters.
bugs.impact: The syslog server cannot parse violation detail buffers as UTF-8.

bugs.title: BIG-IP sending the wrong trap code for BGP peer state
bugs.symptoms: When BGP peer is going down, the BIG-IP system sends the wrong 'bgpPeerState: 6(established)' with its SNMP trap.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG IP system is connected with a Cisco router to verify the traps. -- BGP peer between the BIG-IP system and the Cisco router is going down. -- Both devices release an SNMP trap.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends the wrong code with its SNMP trap. It should be 'bgpPeerState: idle(1)' when the peer is not connected.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now sends the correct trap code for BGP peer state.
bugs.behavior: The bgpPeerState for bgpBackwardTransNotification now reports the state after the state machine transition, i.e., the state that is being transition into. In earlier releases, it reported the state prior to the state machine transition, which would always report idle because all backwards state transitions are into idle.

bugs.title: Export/Import on a parent policy leaves children in an inconsistent state
bugs.symptoms: When overwriting a parent policy with import/replace, elements from the parent policy that were deleted remain in the child policies.
bugs.conditions: -- A parent policy exists with a child policy that inherits a section in which new configuration elements can be created in the parent policy (like ip address exceptions). -- An element is deleted from the parent policy, and then the parent policy is exported. -- The parent policy is then imported to replace a parent policy on a different device to perform the same changes on its children.
bugs.impact: The children on the different devices are left unexpectedly in different states.
bugs.fix: Import/Replace for a parent policy for sections that remain inherited will now delete elements that were removed from the parent policy instead of disinheriting them.

bugs.title: LTM policy with a 'shutdown' action incorrectly allows iRule execution
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems provide manipulation tools over a connection with an LTM policy and/or iRule. LTM policy takes precedence over iRules and has an option to shutdown a connection based on satisfied conditions. When a connection is closing, an iRule should not be executed under the same conditions.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has a virtual server with an LTM policy and an iRule. -- The LTM policy has action 'shutdown connection' under certain conditions. -- The iRule has an event which is triggered under the same conditions.
bugs.impact: The iRule is executed before the connection is being reset.

bugs.title: SSL option "passive-close" option is unused and should be removed
bugs.symptoms: The SSL profile "passive-close" option is available in TMSH (but not the GUI), but is not actually used. A side-effect of this issue is: when the "passive-close" option is configured in TMSH, if the profile is later modified in the GUI, the "passive-close" option will be removed from the profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Modifying a client or server SSL profile in TMSH.
bugs.impact: The "passive-close" option is not actually used.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the "passive-close" option.

bugs.title: Live Update service indicates update available when the latest update was already installed
bugs.symptoms: When downloading and installing the latest ASU file manually the Live Update indicator located at the top left of the screen still indicates that there is a new update available.
bugs.conditions: -- The Live Update scheduler is not in auto mode (System :: Software Management :: Live Update :: Installation of Automatically Downloaded Updates = Disabled). -- Upload and update the latest ASU file manually.
bugs.impact: The Live Update indicator continues to indicate on a new update though the latest file was installed.
bugs.fix: The Live Update service no longer displays a false message regarding updates available.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTTP/2 traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP/2 traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 is enabled on the server side. -- Fallback-host option is specified on client-side HTTP virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: -- Disable HTTP/2 on the serverside profile. or -- Do not use fallback-host option on the clientside.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP/2 traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Transparent vlan-group with standard virtual-server does L2 forwarding instead of pool selection
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is configured with transparent vlan-group and traffic is matching a standard or fastl4 virtual-server and traffic hitting BIG-IP does not have a destination MAC address that belongs to BIG-IP - traffic will be L2 forwarded and pool member selection will not happen. This defect will also cause active FTP data connections over vlan-group to fail.
bugs.conditions: All conditions must be met: - Traffic over transparent vlan-group. - Standard or fastl4 virtual-server. - Traffic has a destination MAC address that does not belong to BIG-IP. OR - Standard virtual server with FTP profile is configured. - Active FTP session is in use. - Traffic flows over vlan-group.
bugs.impact: Server-side connections will fail.
bugs.workaround: Use opaque vlan-group instead. OR disable db variable connection.vgl2transparent (15.0+)

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing iRules with MQTT commands
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing iRules for MQTT profiles.
bugs.conditions: -MQTT profile. -MQTT iRule.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes MQTT iRules as expected.

bugs.title: MRF DIAMETER: Retransmission queue unable to delete stale entries
bugs.symptoms: DIAMETER messages queued for retransmission that do not receive answer responses may be missed by the sweeper logic and not be deleted until the connection closes.
bugs.conditions: -- A DIAMETER message is queued for retransmission without a timeout to tigger retransmission. -- No answer response is received.
bugs.impact: The memory used to hold the copy of the message in the retransmission queue is leaked.
bugs.fix: The retransmission queue has been fixes so all stale messages are deleted as expected.

bugs.title: Unable to initiate SWG database download from Admin UI when management network has no direct internet connectivity.
bugs.symptoms: If the management network is not directly connected to the internet, 'Download Now' action on 'Access ›› Secure Web Gateway : Database Settings : Database Download' fails the connectivity check and refuses to start database download.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure proxy in the same subnet and block BIG-IP management traffic on the gateway -- Remove default routes from linux routing table and add route to the proxy server if necessary.
bugs.impact: Database download fails and you see an error message: "Database download server (download.websense.com) could not be reached. Please verify the correctness of the DNS lookup server configured on this BIG-IP system."
bugs.workaround: -- Run the following tmsh command: tmsh modify sys url-db download-schedule urldb download-now true -or- -- Configure download settings and wait until the scheduled database download.

bugs.title: Possible TMM crash when disabling bot profile for the entire connection
bugs.symptoms: When using an iRule to disable bot profile, and causing it to be disabled (for the entire connection) during a CAPTCHA challenge -- TMM will crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is attached to the Virtual Server, with a CAPTCHA mitigation. -- An iRule is attached to the virtual server, which disables bot profile. -- Sending a request that is responded with a CAPTCHA, then sending (in the same connection), a request that disable the bot profile, and then answering the CAPTCHA.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: When using an iRule to disable bot defense profile on certain conditions, add an "else" clause for re-enabling the profile, taking note that all ::disable iRule commands are effective for the entire connection, and not just the transaction.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes when disabling bot defense profile for the entire connection.

bugs.title: Transactions are held for a long time on specific server related conditions
bugs.symptoms: Long request buffers are kept around for a long time in bd.
bugs.conditions: -- The answer_100_continue internal parameter is turned off (non default) or the version is pre 15.1 -- The server closes the connection while request packets are accumulated.
bugs.impact: The long request buffers are consumed. You may see a "Too many concurrent long requests" log message and requests with large content lengths will get reset.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround that can be done from ASM configuration. If possible, change the server application settings to wait longer for the request payload in 100-continue request or change the client side application to not work with 100-continue.
bugs.fix: Add a check for this scenario so transactions will be released correctly.

bugs.title: TMM crashes while processing MRF traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM panic occurs when processing overflowed the MPI messages due to incorrectly calculated master key length: ../dev/mpi/mpi_mem.c:1129: Assertion "tail not past head" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Message Routing Framework (MRF) traffic of type Diameter and SIP. -- Auto-initialization enabled on peer, but can happen without auto-initialization enabled, just at a less-predictable rate.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM crash no longer occurs under these conditions.

bugs.title: BIG-IP still sends STARTTLS if the 'No encryption' SNMP option is enabled
bugs.symptoms: The SMTP 'No Encryption' configuration option is not honored by the BIG-IP device.
bugs.conditions: The 'No Encryption' option is selected under the SMTP configuration object.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP disregards its SMTP configuration and attempts to initiate TLS.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may reset a stream with an empty DATA frame as END_STREAM
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 defines END_STREAM flag in a frame as an end of a stream. A peer can send an empty (with no payload) DATA frame to designate a last one in a stream. When BIG-IP receives an empty DATA frame, it handles it incorrectly, sending RST_STREAM to a client.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has a virtual server configured with an HTTP/2 profile on the client side. -- The client sends a request containing a payload over a stream, ending the stream with empty DATA frame.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system may reset the stream.
bugs.workaround: A client should resend the request handling more data.
bugs.fix: When empty DATA frame with END_STREAM flag is handled by the BIG-IP system, it terminates the stream accordingly.

bugs.title: Charts discrepancy in AVR reports
bugs.symptoms: Discrepancy in AVR reports. When filtering on the 'last month' interval, a specific number of total requests per virtual server is shown. Then when filtering to the present day from a date that encompasses that month, a lower number is reported.
bugs.conditions: -- Number of records in database exceeds the maximum mount of data that AVR can aggregate between different table-resolutions. -- There are metrics on the report other than the default one (hits-count).
bugs.impact: Stats on DB get corrupted and incorrect.
bugs.fix: Aggregation store-procedure is now fixed.

bugs.title: Logon Page configured after OAuth client in access policy VPE, get error message Access policy evaluation is already in progress for your current session
bugs.symptoms: When 'Logon Page' agent is configured after 'OAuth client' in access policy VPE, you see an error message that says 'Access policy evaluation is already in progress for your current session'
bugs.conditions: In access VPE, Logon page after OAuth client agent in standard customization type.
bugs.impact: Cannot process further to reach resources.
bugs.workaround: Use a 'Logon Page' agent instead of the 'Message Box' agent and configure it such as: all fields Type will be set to 'none' message for the users will be mentioned in the 'Form Header text' field Logon Button value will be changed from 'Logon' to 'Continue' This should simulate exactly the look and feel of a message box but will prevent the issue from happening.

bugs.title: Management interface might become unreachable when alternating between DHCP/static address assignment.
bugs.symptoms: When the Management IP address assignment is changed and the IP address obtained from DHCP lease is used for static interface configuration, the management port might become unreachable after the DHCP lease expiration time, even though interface has a static IP configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Management IP assignment is changed from dynamic (DHCP) to static. -- The static IP address that is configured is identical to the DHCP address that was assigned.
bugs.impact: Remote management access is lost after the DHCP lease expires.
bugs.workaround: When changing the management interface configuration from DHCP to static, first delete the old configuration, then create new configuration. This can be done with TMSH: (tmos)# modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp disabled (tmos)# del sys management-ip 10.14.30.111/24 (tmos)# create sys management-ip 10.14.30.111/24 { description configured-statically }

bugs.title: Link Controller inbound wide IP load balancing method incorrectly presented in GUI when updated
bugs.symptoms: Load balance methods for Link Controller inbound wide IP are always set to default values when the load balancing method is updated through GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple inbound wide IPs are configured; -- Load balancing methods are updated through GUI once.
bugs.impact: Unable to manage wide IPs through the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to manage Inbound WideIPs.

bugs.title: With virtual-wire, lldpd warns 'Received LLDPDU from an unknown interface :12.1'
bugs.symptoms: Erroneous warning messages from lldpd about internal system interfaces: hostname warning lldpd[12345]: 01570005:4: Received LLDPDU from an unknown interface :11.1
bugs.conditions: -- Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) is enabled. -- Virtual-wire configured.
bugs.impact: Continual warning messages from lldpd.
bugs.fix: This error conditions has been corrected.

bugs.title: Series of unexpected <aborted> requests to same URL
bugs.symptoms: Series of unexpected <aborted> requests to same URL
bugs.conditions: Web-app using special code pattern in JavaScript. For example: loc = window.location; obj = {} for (i in loc) { obj[i] = loc[i]; }
bugs.impact: Page load is aborted
bugs.workaround: Following iRule can be used with customized SPECIFIC PAGE_URL value: when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "SPECIFIC_PAGE_URL" } { # log "URI=([HTTP::path])" # Found the file we wanted to modify REWRITE::post_process 1 set do_fix 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { if {[info exists do_fix]} { unset do_fix set strt [string first {<script>try} [REWRITE::payload]] if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt 0 { <script> (function () { var dl = F5_Deflate_location; F5_Deflate_location = function (o) { if (o.F5_Location) Object.preventExtensions(o.F5_Location) return dl(o); } })() </script> } } } }

bugs.title: HTTP2::disable fails for server side allowing HTTP/2 traffic
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system provides an iRule command 'HTTP2::disable serverside' to put http2 in passthrough mode. When the command is called during the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event, it should completely disable http2 until the end of TCP connection, or until the HTTP2::enable command is executed.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server has an HTTP/2 profile configured on the server side. -- An iRule with an the command 'HTTP2::disable serverside' command is attached to the virtual server in the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system continues to send HTTP/2 traffic to a server.

bugs.title: Disabling of HTTP/2 profile on server side does not prevent h2 in ALPN
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 protocol can be negotiated with the Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) on the Transport Layer Security (TLS) level of communication. When an iRule disables HTTP/2 on a server side, it is assumed that the BIG-IP system no longer offers h2 to a server as an option.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server has an HTTP/2 profile configured on both the client and server sides. -- A server SSL profile is configured on the virtual server. -- An iRule using the 'HTTP2::disable serverside' command is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system offers h2 as an option in ALPN when the HTTP/2 profile is disabled on a server side. If h2 is accepted by the server, communication fails since HTTP/2 is disabled and does not decode HTTP/2 traffic.
bugs.fix: When a command 'HTTP2::disable serverside' is executed, the BIG-IP system correctly disables the HTTP/2 profile on a server side, and no longer offers h2 when negotiating a protocol over ALPN.

bugs.title: VCMP guest secondary blade restarts when creating multiple APM profiles in a single transaction
bugs.symptoms: VCMP secondary blade restarts when creating more than one access profile in a transaction.
bugs.conditions: - In one transaction - Create more than one access profiles
bugs.impact: Blade restarts and traffic is disrupted.
bugs.fix: All VCMP blades will continue to work when creating more than one access profile in a transaction.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing SSL traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources when processing SSL traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Client authentication is enabled on client-side SSL.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes SSL traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Ephemeral pool member not created when FQDN resolves to new IP address
bugs.symptoms: On rare occasions, when using FQDN nodes/pool members and the FQDN name resolves to a different IP address, the ephemeral pool member for the old IP address may be removed, but a new ephemeral pool member for the new IP address may not be created. Under normal operation, the following sequence of messages is logged in /var/log/dynconfd.log when dynconfd logging is set to 'debug' level: [D]: setFQDNPoolMembersModified: pool /Common/my_fqdn_pool node /Common/my_fqdn_node fqdn my.fqdn.com [D]: PoolMember::scan: pool /Common/my_fqdn_pool member /Common/my_fqdn_node fqdn my.fqdn.com But when this problem occurs, the 'setFQDNPoolMembersModified' log message is not followed by a 'PoolMember::scan' log message: [D]: setFQDNPoolMembersModified: pool /Common/my_fqdn_pool node /Common/my_fqdn_node fqdn my.fqdn.com
bugs.conditions: This may occur under rare timing conditions while using using FQDN nodes/pool members, when the DNS server resolves the FQDN name to a different IP address.
bugs.impact: Pools configured with FQDN-based pool members may become empty, in which case no traffic will be processed by that pool.
bugs.workaround: To recover from this condition once it occurs, perform either of the following actions: -- Restart the dynconfd daemon: bigstart restart dynconfd This temporarily interrupts queries for FQDN name resolution and updates (deletion/creation) of ephemeral nodes/pool members in response to FQDN resolution changes. This action is not otherwise expected to affect traffic currently flowing to pools. -- Remove the FQDN pool member, then re-add the FQDN pool member back to the pool: tmsh modify ltm pool my_fqdn_pool { members delete { my_fqdn_node:port } } tmsh modify ltm pool my_fqdn_pool { members add { my_fqdn_node:port <other parameters> } } If the pool already has no ephemeral pool members, this has no effect on traffic (which is already not flowing to this pool). If the pool has some ephemeral pool members but not the complete list of expected ephemeral members, this will interrupt traffic flowing to this pool while there are no pool members present. In that case, temporarily adding at least one pool member with a statically-configured IP address before removing the FQDN pool member, then removing the same temporary pool members after replacing the FQDN pool member, allow straffic to continue flowing to the pool while this action is performed.

bugs.title: Continuous restart of ntlmconnpool after the license reinstallation
bugs.symptoms: The ntlmconnpool process continuously restarts after reinstalling the license. The system reports a message in the BIG-IP console: Re-starting ntlmconnpool. The BIG-IP may show as 'Disconnected', and 'TMM outbound listener not yet created' messages may be present in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when you upgrade your license such that the new license changes the number of available TMMs.
bugs.impact: The system requires a reboot and reports a ‘Re-starting ntlmconnpool’ message continuously in the BIG-IP console.
bugs.workaround: To resolve the issue, it is necessary to reboot. Once the system restarts, it operates as expected.

bugs.title: Network Firewall Active Rule page does lot load
bugs.symptoms: The page (content frame) is blank and nothing is visible
bugs.conditions: This occurs when viewing the Active Rule page.
bugs.impact: You are unable to view active Rules in UI
bugs.fix: Network Firewall Active Rule page is now visible in the GUI.

bugs.title: TMM may restart under large amount traffic load
bugs.symptoms: TMM occasionally restarts when running heavy workload. The crash is a timing based issue between different tmm threads, and thus happens only occasionally.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is provisioned with dos functionality -- When BIG-IP is under heavy workload
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: After fix, no more tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Increase size of /var logical volume to 1.5 GiB for LTM-only VE images
bugs.symptoms: The /var logical volume size of 950 MiB for LTM-only BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) images may be too small for some deployments. This can result in result in loss of SSH access.
bugs.conditions: This applies to deployments that use declarative onboarding for configuration.
bugs.impact: Complex declarative onboarding configurations may fill the /var logical volume. You are locked out because of the too-small volume.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to manually extend the /var logical volume. For more information, see K14952: Extending disk space on BIG-IP VE :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14952.
bugs.fix: The size of the /var logical volume was increased from 950 MiB to 1.5 GiB for LTM-only VE images.
bugs.behavior: The size of the /var logical volume was increased from 950MiB to 1.5GiB for LTM-only Virtual Edition images.

bugs.title: "Security ›› Reporting : ASM Resources : CPU Utilization" shows TMM has 100% CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: TMM CPU utilization around 100 percent under Security ›› Reporting : ASM Resources : CPU Utilization.
bugs.conditions: No special conditions. Only viewing at the stats of TMM CPU in 'Security ›› Reporting : ASM Resources : CPU Utilization'. They will always be in wrong scale, but when the TMM has ~1% CPU usage, it will be presented as 100% CPU usage.
bugs.impact: Wrong scale is presented and might cause machine's state to be interpreted wrongly.
bugs.workaround: 1. Backup /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_cpu_info_measures.cfg file. 2. Run the following: $ sed -i 's|tmm_avg_cpu_util)/(count(distinct time_stamp)|tmm_avg_cpu_util)/(count(distinct time_stamp)*100|g' /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_cpu_info_measures.cfg 3. Compare the backup file to /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_cpu_info_measures.cfg: Make sure that there are two lines modified, and that the modification is multiplying with 100 the denominator (i.e., actually dividing the TMM value with 100). 4. To make those changes take affect, run the following command: $ bigstart restart monpd
bugs.fix: Dividing the TMM value with 100 to fit correct scale.

bugs.title: IP fragments are disaggregated to separate TMMs with hardware syncookies enabled
bugs.symptoms: With hardware syncookies enabled, HTTP POST requests that are fragmented into separate segments are processed by different TMMs. Connection is subsequently reset with a TCP RST cause reported as: No flow found for ACK.
bugs.conditions: -- Hardware syncookies triggered. -- IP fragmented HTTP POST request.
bugs.impact: Connection is subsequently reset with TCP RST, cause 'No flow found for ACK'.
