bugs.title: Cannot enable logging for management firewall with LTM only provisioned
bugs.symptoms: You cannot enable firewall logging via tmsh or the GUI when only LTM is provisioned. AFM must be licensed and provisioned in order to configure firewall logging with tmsh or the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- No AFM Provisioned -- v14.1.0 or newer. -- Using firewall rules to protect the management interface.
bugs.impact: You cannot enable firewall logging to help with tracking or to aid in troubleshooting.
bugs.workaround: You can run the following command to view the counters from F5 rules easily with this command (output is very verbose): # /sbin/iptables -vL f5acl If you want to enable logging (output is very verbose), you can run the following command: /sbin/iptables -I f5acl -j LOG --log-prefix "IPTables-Dropped: " This will then log to /var/log/kern.log. To remove this change: /sbin/iptables -D f5acl -j LOG --log-prefix "IPTables-Dropped: "

bugs.title: Update default anti-fraud profile with new per-request policy logon page URL
bugs.symptoms: Cannot access an application that is protected by APM and FPS.
bugs.conditions: When DataSafe logon protection is enabled with per-request policy added on virtual server.
bugs.impact: You cannot get access to the application.
bugs.workaround: Add the URL /subsession_logon_submit.php3* to the access-logonpage-protection-datasafe profile.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with per-request logon policy.

bugs.title: Software installation on vCMP guest fails with '(Software compatibility tests failed.)' or '(The requested product/version/build is not in the media.)'
bugs.symptoms: Software upgrades to an Engineering Hotfix on a vCMP guest might fail with one of the following messages: failed (Software compatibility tests failed.) failed (The requested product/version/build is not in the media.) The failed installation is also indicated by log messages in /var/log/ltm similar to: -- info lind[5500]: 013c0007:6: Install complete for volume=HD1.2: status=failed (Software compatibility tests failed.) -- info lind[5500]: 013c0007:6: Install complete for volume=HD1.2: status=failed (The requested product/version/build is not in the media.)
bugs.conditions: This may occur when performing a software upgrade to an engineering hotfix on a vCMP guest running affected versions of BIG-IP software, when the software images are present on the vCMP host. This can be accomplished by running the following command from the vCMP guest console: tmsh install sys software block-device-hotfix <hotfix-image-name> volume <volume.name>
bugs.impact: Unable to perform software installations on vCMP guests using installation media located on the vCMP host.
bugs.workaround: Option 1: =========== Make sure that the .iso files for both base image and engineering hotfix are copied to the vCMP guest (under /shared/images) before starting the installation. If installing the software from the command line, use syntax similar to the following: tmsh install sys software hotfix <hotfix-image-name> volume <volume.name> Option 2: =========== Even if the engineering hotfix installation has failed, the base image should still have been installed properly. You can restart the vCMP guest and perform a hotfix installation on top of already installed base image, using syntax similar to the following: tmsh install sys software hotfix <hotfix-image-name> volume <volume.name> Option 3: =========== Even if the engineering hotfix installation has failed, the base image should still have been installed properly. Ensure there is copy of the engineering hotfix image locally within the vCMP Guest. Then restart the lind service on the vCMP Guest: tmsh restart sys service lind If running the vCMP Guest on multiple slots, you may need to restart lind on all slots. From the primary slot on the vCMP Guest, run: clsh tmsh restart sys service lind The hotfix installation should begin again, this time using the hotfix from within the /shared/images/ location on the vCMP Guest. Option 4: =========== Manually eject the CD from the vCMP guest's virtual CD drive, and then restart lind. On the vCMP Guest: 1. Confirm the wrong ISO image is still locked (inserted in the CD drive): isoinfo -d -i /dev/cdrom Note: Pay attention to the volume ID in the output from within the vCMP guest. 2. Unlock (eject) the image: eject -r -F /dev/cdrom && vcmphc_tool -e 3. Verify the CD drive is now empty: isoinfo -d -i /dev/cdrom The output should report an error that includes: <...> Sense Code: 0x3A Qual 0x00 (medium not present) Fru 0x0 <…> 4. Restart lind: tmsh restart sys service lind If running the vCMP Guest on multiple slots, you may need to restart lind on all vCMP Guest slots. From the primary slot on the vCMP Guest, run: clsh tmsh restart sys service lind
bugs.fix: Software upgrades on a vCMP guest complete successfully even when the software images are present on the vCMP hypervisor.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTTP/3 traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP/3 traffic.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/3 profile enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP/3 traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Access Policy cannot be created with 'modern' customization
bugs.symptoms: Per-Request Policy (PRP) Access Policy with Customization Type set to Modern cannot be created due to internal error.
bugs.conditions: Creating a PRP Access Policy with Customization Type set to Modern.
bugs.impact: Administrator cannot use modern customization.
bugs.workaround: 1. In bigip.conf find the following line: apm policy customization-source /Common/standard { } 2. Add the following line: apm policy customization-source /Common/modern { } 3. Save the changes. 4. Load the config: tmsh load sys config
bugs.fix: Now modern customization can be used for any Access Policy.

bugs.title: Mcpd crash when adding NAPTR GTM pool member with a flag of uppercase A or S
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd restarts and produces a core file.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while adding a pool member to a NAPTR GTM pool where the flag used is an uppercase 'A' or 'S' character.
bugs.impact: Mcpd crash and restart results in high availability (HA) failover.
bugs.workaround: Use a lowercase 'a' or 's' as the flag value.
bugs.fix: Mcpd no longer crashes under these conditions. The flag value is always stored in lowercase regardless of the case used as input in the REST call or tmsh command, etc.

bugs.title: Restarting bigstart shuts down the system
bugs.symptoms: The 'bigstart restart bigstart' command shuts down the system without displaying or informing the BIG-IP system user that this command can interrupt service. The system goes directly to the inoperative state as soon as the command is run.
bugs.conditions: -- Running the command bigstart restart bigstart. -- Running 'systemctl restart systemd-bigstart' twice.
bugs.impact: Different versions appear to have different behavior: -- v12.1.5: shell hangs on bigstart command, but the BIG-IP system stays Active. -- v13.1.0.7: The BIG-IP system goes inoperative upon 'bigstart restart bigstart'. -- 1v4.1.2.3: The 'bigstart restart bigstart' command cannot find the 'bigstart' service, but 'systemctl restart systemd-bigstart' shows this behavior.

bugs.title: Unexpected FIN from APM virtual server during Access Policy evaluation if XML profile is configured for VS
bugs.symptoms: APM virtual server user's GUI (e.g., 'Logon page') cannot be rendered by browsers.
bugs.conditions: This issue is encountered when an XML profile is configured for the APM virtual server.
bugs.impact: APM end users are unable to get a logon page.
bugs.workaround: Disable the XML profile for the APM virtual server.
bugs.fix: There is no unexpected traffic interruption from the APM virtual server when the XML profile is configured for the virtual server.

bugs.title: Apply Policy action is not synchronized after making bulk signature changes
bugs.symptoms: After an action that affects thousands of objects, a subsequent Apply Policy may be missed by a peer.
bugs.conditions: -- Devices are in an auto-sync device group with ASM sync enabled. -- A bulk action that affects thousands of objects is performed (e.g., enforcing or disabling all signatures). -- An Apply Policy action is taken immediately afterwards.
bugs.impact: Peer devices that are still busy processing the large request miss the Apply Policy action, and it is never sent again.
bugs.workaround: Make a spurious change and reapply the policy.

bugs.title: Incorrect masking of parameters in event log
bugs.symptoms: When using CSRF protection, sensitive parameters values can be masked incorrectly in the event log.
bugs.conditions: The request contains a CSRF token and sensitive parameters.
bugs.impact: Sensitive parameters values can be masked incorrectly in the event log.
bugs.fix: Sensitive parameters values are now correctly masked in the event log when request contains CSRF token.

bugs.title: No hardware mitigation for DoS attacks in auto-threshold mode with enabled attacked destinations detection
bugs.symptoms: There are no hardware mitigation for DoS attacks
bugs.conditions: Auto-threshold mode and detection for attacked destinations should be activate for DoS static vector
bugs.impact: DoS attack mitigation performed only by software
bugs.fix: Improved search in already hardware offloaded entities

bugs.title: DNS::header rd does not set the Recursion desired
bugs.symptoms: iRule command DNS::header rd not working as expected.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server configured with an iRule command to set DNS::header rd.
bugs.impact: The DNS::header rd iRule command does not set the Recursion Desired flag in DNS headers.

bugs.title: Incorrect DoS static vectors mitigation threshold in multiplier based mode after run relearn thresholds command
bugs.symptoms: Value in mitigation thresholds are above infinite value (4294967295)
bugs.conditions: Multiplier based mitigation mode for Dos static vectors after run relearn thresholds command
bugs.impact: Incorrect display value for DoS thresholds in GUI and tmctl
bugs.fix: Do not apply multiplayer for infinite threshold value (4294967295).

bugs.title: APM Hosted Content feature incorrectly guesses content type for CSS files
bugs.symptoms: APM has a hosted content feature where files can be uploaded for serving out to end users. This is typically used for Edge Client hosting, CSS, and Images. When you upload a CSS file with Hosted Content enabled, BIG-IP classifies it as 'text/x-asm' when it should be 'text/css'.
bugs.conditions: APM Hosted Content feature serving CSS files.
bugs.impact: Incorrect content type used for CSS may confuse some web clients.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use the Hosted Content GUI to change the file type from 'text/x-asm' to 'text/css'.

bugs.title: LDAP remote authentication for REST API calls may fail during authorization
bugs.symptoms: LDAP (or Active Directory) remote authentication fails during authorization for REST API calls. Clients receive 401 Unauthorized messages and /var/log/restjavad.x.log may report messages similar to the following: -- [I][1978][26 Mar 2021 13:23:36 UTC][8100/shared/authn/login AuthnWorker] User remoteuser failed to login from 192.0.2.1 using the tmos authentication provider -- [WARNING][807][26 Mar 2021 14:43:24 UTC][RestOperationIdentifier] Failed to validate Authentication failed.
bugs.conditions: LDAP (or Active Directory) remote authentication configured with a User Template instead of a Bind Account.
bugs.impact: Unable to authenticate as remote-user for access that uses authorization, like REST API calls.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Configure LDAP/AD remote authentication to utilize a Bind account instead of the User Template. -- Create a local user account for each remote user, allowing local authorization (authentication remains remote).

bugs.title: Dynamic server config on OAuth Client/RS agent in Per-Session-Policy
bugs.symptoms: Session config on OAuth Client/RS agent is applied once and used for all APM sessions.
bugs.conditions: OAuth is configured
bugs.impact: You are unable to provision OAuth Authorization Servers per group of APM session(s)
bugs.workaround: Create OAuth Client/RS agent with each server object applicable
bugs.fix: You can now configure a "DynamicServer" session variable for OAuth so that one agent can be applied to multiple sessions.

bugs.title: Protected Object Aggregate stats are causing elevated CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: Due to a large number of tables containing 'Protected Object Aggregate stats', the merged daemon might cause elevated CPU usage on odd-numbered CPU cores.
bugs.conditions: AFM, ASM, or DoS features are provisioned.
bugs.impact: Elevated CPU usage on odd-numbered cores caused by merged daemon.
bugs.fix: Protected Object Aggregate stats no longer cause elevated CPU usage.

bugs.title: TMM can crash when processing SCTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing SCTP traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- SCTP listener enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes SCTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Some HTTP/3 streams terminate early
bugs.symptoms: Some HTTP/3 streams are terminated with a FIN before all the requested data is delivered.
bugs.conditions: -- Send multiple HTTP3 requests on different streams simultaneously. -- The back-end in server is NGINX. Note: This might happen with other web servers as well.
bugs.impact: Data transfer is incomplete.
bugs.workaround: Update the server-side connection to HTTP/2.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where some HTTP/3 streams were being terminated early.

bugs.title: SSL connection mirroring intermittent failure with TLS1.3
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent failure of standby connection mirroring TLS1.3 handshake.
bugs.conditions: TLS1.3 and connection mirroring. More easily reproduces with ecdsa signature.
bugs.impact: Standby device fails tls handshake, active success so connection succeeds but not mirrored.
bugs.fix: Standby device now uses correct signature size if it differs from active device.

bugs.title: HTTP/3 does not support draft-25
bugs.symptoms: Clients attempting to connect with QUIC version 25 and ALPN h3-25 are unable to connect.
bugs.conditions: An end user client attempts to connect using QUIC version 25 and ALPN h3-25.
bugs.impact: Attempts to use HTTP/3 with some clients may fail.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports draft-24 and draft-25.

bugs.title: MCP crashes when deleting a virtual server and its traffic-matching-criteria in the same transaction
bugs.symptoms: MCPD crashes when deleting a virtual server and traffic-matching-criteria in the same transaction. This can happen when explicitly using a transaction, or when using a feature that uses transactions, such as when deleting an iApp instance that created these objects.
bugs.conditions: -- Using a virtual server that has traffic-matching-criteria (e.g., port lists or address lists) attached. -- Deleting the virtual server and its traffic-matching-criteria in the same transaction.
bugs.impact: MCP cores, which causes a failover (in a high availability (HA) system) or temporary outage.
bugs.workaround: Delete the traffic-matching-criteria object separately from the virtual server.

bugs.title: Alertd could leak memory if nokia alarm is enabled and nokiasnmpd is not running
bugs.symptoms: If the nokiasnmp daemon has not started running when the nokia alarm configuration is enabled then the alert daemon leaks memory when issuing traps.
bugs.conditions: Enabling nokia alarm handling and not starting the nokiasnmp daemon. The first time the alarm handling is configured, the alert and nokiasnmp daemons must be restarted.
bugs.impact: Memory is leaked when traps are issued in this configuration.
bugs.fix: The code has been fixed to properly handle this error condition and not leak memory.

bugs.title: Switching from fast_merge to slow_merge can result in incorrect tmm stats
bugs.symptoms: TMM stats are reported incorrectly. For example, the system may report double the number of running TMMs or an incorrect amount of available memory.
bugs.conditions: Changing the DB key merged.method from fast_merge to slow_merge.
bugs.impact: Incorrect reporting for TMM stats.
bugs.workaround: Remove the file /var/tmstat/cluster/blade0-performance. These files are roll-ups and will be re-created as necessary.

bugs.title: APM Portal Access: Base URL may be set to incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, Portal Access may set an incorrect value for the Base URL used in rewritten JavaScript code.
bugs.conditions: - HTML page - JavaScript code inside the page
bugs.impact: Web application may not work correctly.
bugs.workaround: Use iRule to correct Base URL value inside rewritten page.
bugs.fix: APM Portal Access now sets the correct Base URL value.

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator Configuration GUI freezes after management IP change.
bugs.symptoms: Changing the management IP address of the SSL Orchestrator BIG-IP device can result in an unresponsive SSL Orchestrator configuration interface in the TMUI. All other menus continue to work fine.
bugs.conditions: Change the management IP address of the SSL Orchestrator BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: The SSL Orchestrator configuration interface in the TMUI becomes unresponsive and the BIG-IP SSL Orchestrator device administrator is not able to perform SSL Orchestrator management and configuration tasks.
bugs.workaround: After the SSL Orchestrator BIG-IP device management IP address change, use the following steps to get the SSL Orchestrator user interface to render correctly: 1. Wait for the management IP address change to become effective: (That is, the BIG-IP admin/user can log in to the BIG-IP console using the new management IP address). 2. In the BIG-IP terminal run the following commands: restcurl -X DELETE shared/resolver/device-groups/tm-shared-all-big-ips/devices restcurl -X POST -d '{}' tm/shared/bigip-failover-state 3. The SSL Orchestrator UI/topology should become available in approximately 30 - 60 seconds (subject to topology size, etc.)
bugs.fix: SSL Orchestrator Configuration GUI freezes after management IP change.

bugs.title: DataSafe is not available with AWAF license after BIG-IP startup or MCP restart.
bugs.symptoms: DataSafe is not available with an AWAF license.
bugs.conditions: -- AWAF license -- BIG-IP startup or MCP restart
bugs.impact: DataSafe is not available.
bugs.workaround: Reset to default license.antifraud.id variable. tmsh modify sys db license.antifraud.id reset-to-default.
bugs.fix: Additional DataSafe license validation during MCP startup after license information is loaded.

bugs.title: Re-offloading of TCP flows to hardware does not work
bugs.symptoms: Once Hardware evicts the EPVA TCP flows due to Idle timeout, tmm does not reinsert the flows back when it receives a packet belonging to that flow.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the TCP connection is kept idle for ~20 seconds.
bugs.impact: Performance can be impacted. Hardware acceleration will be disabled for the flows once the flow is removed from hardware due to Idle timeout.
bugs.fix: Fix will re-offload the flows to HW once SW starts receiving packets due to HW eviction of flows by Idle timeout.

bugs.title: LTM policy matching does not work as expected
bugs.symptoms: Policy matching may fail to work as expected
bugs.conditions: Having many conditions with the same operand may trigger an issue where the wrong transition is taken. This may also be triggered by very complex policies with large numbers of rules.
bugs.impact: LTM policy matching does not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use fewer than 30 values in an LTM policy rule.
bugs.fix: LTM Policy matching now works correctly with large complex policies containing many rules or conditions.

bugs.title: Kernel page allocation failure seen on VIPRION blades
bugs.symptoms: Despite having free memory, the BIG-IP system frequently logs kernel page allocation failures to the /var/log/kern.log file: warning kernel: : [7673174.106142] swapper/6: page allocation failure: order:2, mode:0x104020
bugs.conditions: This issue is known to occur on the following VIPRION blade models: - B2250 (A112) - B4300 (A108) - B4340N (A110) - B4450 (A114)
bugs.impact: As different processes can experience this issue, the system may behave unpredictably. For example, it is possible for installation to fail as a result of this issue. Other processes may not exhibit any side effect as a result of this issue. The exact impact depends on which process becomes affected and how this process is designed to handle such a failure to allocate memory.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by increasing the value of the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter. This controls the amount of memory that is kept free for use by special reserves. It is recommend to increase this as follows: -- 64 MB (65536 KB for B2250 blades). -- 48 MB (49152 KB for B4300 blades). -- 128 MB (131072 KB forB4450 blades). You must do this on each blade installed in the system. When instantiating this workaround, you must consider whether you want the workaround to survive only reboots, or to survive reboots, upgrades, RMAs, etc. This is an important consideration to make, as you should stop using this workaround when this issue is fixed in a future version of BIG-IP software. So consider the pros and cons of each approach before choosing one. -- If you want the workaround to survive reboots only, perform the following procedure: 1) Log on to the advanced shell (BASH) of the primary blade of the affected VIPRION system. 2) Run the following commands (with the desired amount in KB): # clsh "sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072" # clsh "echo -e '＼n# Workaround for ID753650' >> /etc/sysctl.conf" # clsh "echo 'vm.min_free_kbytes = 131072' >> /etc/sysctl.conf" -- If you want the workaround to survive reboots, upgrades, RMAs, etc., perform the following procedure: 1) Log on to the advanced shell (BASH) of the primary blade of the affected VIPRION system. 2) Run the following commands (with the desired amount in KB): # clsh "sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072" # echo -e '＼n# Workaround for ID753650' >> /config/startup # echo 'sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072' >> /config/startup Note that the last two commands are not wrapped inside 'clsh' because the /config/startup file is already automatically synchronized across all blades. Once the issue is fixed in a future BIG-IP version, remove the workarounds: -- To remove the first workaround: 1) Edit the /etc/sysctl.conf file on all blades and remove the added lines at the bottom. 2) Reboot the system by running 'clsh reboot'. This will restore the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter to its default value for the BIG-IP version you are running. -- To remove the second workaround: 1) Edit the /config/startup file on the primary blade only, and remove the extra lines at the bottom. 2) Reboot the system by running 'clsh reboot'. This restores the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter to its default value for the BIG-IP version you are running. To verify the workaround is in place, run the following command (this should return the desired amount in KB): # clsh "cat /proc/sys/vm/min_free_kbytes"

bugs.title: Bot Defense 'Web RootKit' Anomaly False Positive using Seznam.cz Browser on iOS
bugs.symptoms: When using Bot Defense profile with browser verification, and sending a request using Seznam.cz Browser - 'Web RootKit' anomaly is detected and the client is blocked.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is used, with a 'Verify After Access' or 'Verify Before Access' Browser Validation. -- Request is sent using Seznam.cz browser on iOS.
bugs.impact: The client is blocked.
bugs.workaround: Change the bigDB variable for minimum web rootkit allowed to a higher value. This allows all web rootkited browsers. tmsh modify sys db botdefense.min_rootkit_functions value 100
bugs.fix: Disable Web Rootkit tests for Seznam.cz browser on iOS. Note: Fix is valid only when not using Device ID Collection.

bugs.title: Incorrect Alarm/Block flags displayed for Signature with previously enforced rule
bugs.symptoms: When Signature Staging is disabled globally, signatures containing previously enforced rules are displayed with Alarm/Block flags set to 'No'. This occurs even if the signature is fully enabled and the associated Set is set to Learn/Alarm/Block.
bugs.conditions: -- Signature Staging is disabled globally. -- A signature has a previously enforced rule. This occurs when an F5-provided signature is taken out of staging, and the signature is then updated by ASU.
bugs.impact: The signature appears in the Attack Signature GUI page as having alarm and blocking disabled, although the signature does block correctly.

bugs.title: DNS response recursion desired (rd) flag does not match DNS query when using iRule command DNS::header rd
bugs.symptoms: DNS response recursion desired (rd) flag does not match the DNS query when using the iRule command DNS::header rd.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule command DNS::header rd is used to set DNS query rd bit to a different value. -- At least one wide IP is configured.
bugs.impact: DNS response rd flag does not match the DNS query. This is not RFC compliant.
bugs.workaround: Do not configure any wide IPs.

bugs.title: Client-side asymmetric routing could lead to SYN and SYN-ACK on different VLAN
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is configured with at least two VLANs/interfaces, and a virtual server with auto-lasthop disabled, then when that virtual server receives a SYN from a client and sends the SYN/ACK directly back to the client on a different VLAN/interface, it currently expects the ACK to be received on the outgoing interface unless the client is not directly connected and the connection is using a default gateway.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP is configured with two VLANs/interfaces for a client (one for incoming packets, one for outgoing packets, i.e. asymmetric routing). -- The client using asymmetric routing is connecting to a virtual server with auto-lasthop disabled. -- The outgoing route to the client (from the BIG-IP) is directly connected to the client (i.e. on the same network; not going through a gateway). -- The DB variable connection.vlankeyed has the value "enabled" (which is the default).
bugs.impact: The mismatch could lead to connections failing to establish.
bugs.workaround: Use only a single VLAN on the client side, or disable the DB variable "connection.vlankeyed".

bugs.title: APM does not support adding samesite cookie attribute to APM cookies.
bugs.symptoms: The Chrome browser (i.e version 80 ) changes the way it treats the samesite cookie attribute to be complaint, according to https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-west-cookie-incrementalism-00 In this case, if the server does not set the samesite cookie attribute, the browser will treat the cookie attribute as equivalent to "samesite=Lax", which changes the behavior of how the cookie is shared with the domain, which did not originally set the cookie.
bugs.conditions: APM is configured.
bugs.impact: The latest browser (eg : chrome80 ) will stop sending the APM cookie back to the different domain, if it does not find the samesite cookie attribute for APM cookies.
bugs.workaround: Custom irule to add samesite cookie attribute to the APM cookies in HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE.

bugs.title: APM: Incorrect messages on logout page
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, the customized APM logout page is shown without messages substituted. Internal template names are shown instead, for example: %[message]
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server with APM access policy and full webtop. - Normal logout from user session.

bugs.title: iControl API calls with remote user auth cannot create/update SYS iFiles with 600 permission
bugs.symptoms: Curl called from iControl REST cannot access files with 600 permission The call fails with the following error. { "apiError": 26214401, "code": 400, "errorStack": [], "message": "Failed! exit_code (37).\n" } The exist code comes from curl. The code 37 is: CURLE_FILE_COULDNT_READ_FILE (37) A file given with FILE:// couldn't be opened. Most likely because the file path does not identify an existing file. Did you check file permissions? (see https://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/libcurl-errors.html)
bugs.conditions: -- Using Curl to call an iFile from iControl REST. -- iFile has 600 permission.
bugs.impact: Cannot create/modify iFile objects from source files even the remote user account is granted administrator rights.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Change the file permission to 644. -- Change the user from a remote to local account (with the Administrator role).

bugs.title: Traffic Classification auto signature update fails from GUI
bugs.symptoms: Beginning in BIG-IP software v14.1.0, Traffic Classification auto signature update fails when performed using the GUI. The system reports an error: Error: Exception caught in the script. Check logs (/var/log/hitless_upgrade.log) for details.

bugs.impact: Fails to update the classification signature automatically.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following: -- Perform Traffic Classification auto signature update operations from the CLI. -- Use the GUI to manually update Traffic Classification signatures.

bugs.title: Filtering by Bot Categories on Bot Requests Log shows 0 events
bugs.symptoms: A log that has 'Browser Automation’ as the ‘Bot Category’ exists. When filtering for only Bot Category: Browser Automation, nothing Shows up.

bugs.title: Hardware-accelerated connections might not be removed from ePVA on transition to standby
bugs.symptoms: This issue only affects certain platforms, such as the B4450. For affected platforms, when the active BIG-IP unit in a redundant configuration becomes the standby unit after a failover event, the traffic sent to the virtual servers with hardware acceleration enabled continues to be accelerated by the ePVA hardware on the original active unit (now the standby unit). These entries should be flushed on transition to standby if PVA standby flush is enabled.
bugs.conditions: When a failover event occurs on a device with hardware-accelerated virtual servers and PVA standby flush is enabled.
bugs.impact: Hardware-accelerated entries may stay active on the standby unit, processing network traffic.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware-accelerated (ePVA) connections.

bugs.title: The bigd monitor reports misleading error messages
bugs.symptoms: When a recv string is used with an HTTP/HTTP2/HTTPS/TCP monitor, the HTTP status code is collected and in the event of failure, the most recent value (from before the failure) is retrieved and used as part of the log output. This can result in a message that is misleading.
bugs.conditions: - The BIG-IP system configured to monitor an HTTP/HTTP2 server. - The BIG-IP system configured to monitor an HTTPS/TCP monitor.
bugs.impact: Generates a misleading log messages, difficulty in identifying the actual cause of the monitor failure. This occurs because the system stores the 'last error' string for these monitors. This can be misleading, especially when a receive string is used. Following is an example: -- A BIG-IP system is monitoring an HTTP server that is returning proper data (i.e., matching the receive string). -- The HTTP server goes down. Now the BIG-IP system will have a last error string of 'No successful responses received before deadline' or 'Unable to connect'. -- The HTTP server goes back up and works for a while. -- For some reason, the HTTP server's responses no longer match the receive string. In this case, a message is logged on the BIG-IP system: notice mcpd[6060]: 01070638:5: Pool /Common/http member /Common/n.n.n.n:n monitor status down. [ /Common/my_http_monitor: down; last error: /Common/my_http_monitor: Unable to connect @2020/01/09 04:18:20. ] [ was up for 4hr:18mins:46sec ] The 'Unable to connect' last error reason is not correct: the BIG-IP system can connect to the HTTP server and gets responses back, but they do not match the received string.

bugs.title: HTTP authentication in the access policy times out after 60 seconds
bugs.symptoms: HTTP authentication in the access policy times out after 60 seconds, where previously, the timeout was 90 seconds.
bugs.conditions: Encountering the timeout of HTTP authentication in the access policy in this version of the software.
bugs.impact: HTTP authentication times out 30 seconds earlier than it did in previous versions. There is no way to configure this timeout value, so authentication fails for operations that require greater than 60 seconds to complete.
bugs.fix: Added options to configure the HTTP connection and request timeouts in HTTP authentication. 1. A db key to configure Connection Timeout for HTTP Server configuration: +[APM.HTTP.ConnectionTimeout] +default=10 +type=integer +min=0 +max=300 +realm=common +scf_config=true +display_name=APM.HTTP.ConnectionTimeout 2. A db key to configure Request Timeout for HTTP Server configuration: +[APM.HTTP.RequestTimeout] +default=60 +type=integer +min=0 +max=600 +realm=common +scf_config=true +display_name=APM.HTTP.RequestTimeout
bugs.behavior: Added db variables APM.HTTP.ConnectionTimeout and APM.HTTP.RequestTimeout as options to configure the HTTP connection and request timeouts in HTTP authentication. The APM.HTTP.ConnectionTimeout defaults to 10 seconds, and the APM.HTTP.RequestTimeout defaults to 60 seconds. Note: These defaults are the same as the values in earlier releases, so there is no effective functional change in behavior.

bugs.title: Added internal parameter to address Chrome samesite default change
bugs.symptoms: False-positive violations related to domain cookies enforcement (such as modified domain cookies, dynamic parameters extractions).
bugs.conditions: -- Using Google Chrome browser. -- The ASM protected site is sending cookies (that are configured as enforced) with resources that are accessible through third party sites.
bugs.impact: False-positive violations.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can add the SameSite=None attribute to ASM generated cookies with the Set-cookie command.
bugs.fix: Added an internal parameter, ts_cookie_add_attrs, that allows the BIG-IP system administrator to add a string at the end of the ASM Set-Cookie HTTP response header. Using this internal parameter, the administrator can add the SameSite=None string to opt-out from the Chrome browser modification and have the ASM cookie behave as before. This change is global and affects all ASM system cookies, except those set via JavaScript.

bugs.title: QAT compression codec produces gzip stream with CRC error
bugs.symptoms: When an HTTP compression profile is enabled on BIG-IP platforms with Intel QuickAssist Technology (Intel QAT) compression accelerators, gzip errors are produced.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the following conditions are met: -- The following platforms with Intel QAT are affected: + 4450 blades + i4600/i4800 + i10600/i10800 + i7600/i7800 + i5600/i5800 + i11600/i11800 + i11400/i11600/i11800 + i15600/i15800 -- The compression.qat.dispatchsize variable is set to any of the following values: + 65535 + 32768 + 16384 + 8192 -- The size of the file being compressed is a multiple of the compression.qat.dispatchsize value, for exampld: + 65355*32768 + 8192*32768
bugs.impact: Clients cannot decompress the compressed file because there is an invalid gzip footer.
bugs.workaround: Disable hardware compression and use software compression.
bugs.fix: The system now handles gzip errors seen with QAT compression.

bugs.title: JavaScript engine file is empty if the original HTML page cached for too long

bugs.conditions: Original HTML page with FPS injected content is cached for too long due to some caching headers (e.g., ETag), so the JavaScript engine link becomes invalid.

bugs.workaround: You can use either workaround: -- Use an iRule to disable caching for protected HTML pages. -- Set caching time for protected HTML pages to the same value as the datasync tables regeneration timer according to the active datasync profile (default value is two 2 days).

bugs.title: When running the debug version of TMM, an assertion may be triggered due to an expired DNS lookup.

bugs.impact: TMM crashes and, in redundant configurations, the unit fails over.

bugs.fix: The debug assert was removed and replaced by a debug log.

bugs.title: Tmm crash: invalid route type
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes. /var/log/tmm contains the log entries: tmm1: notice panic: invalid route type tmm1: notice ** SIGFPE **
bugs.conditions: The issue is intermittent. 1. There is more than one route domain in the parent-child relationship. 2. There are routing entries for the parent route-domain good enough to be selected as an egress point for the routing object (for instance, pool member) which is from child route domain. 3. The routing entry from a parent route domain is selected as an egress point for the object from the child route domain. 4. A new routing entry for child route domain is added.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no way to workaround a problem, but there is a safe way to add and delete routes without putting a BIG-IP into a state where it could encounter this issue. Safe way to add/delete a route. 1) Add routes to child route domains first, then to parent route domain. 2) Delete routes from parent route domain first, then from child route domain.
bugs.fix: Routing objects are now forced to reselect a routing entry after a new route is added to the child route domain's routing table and it's not causing a TMM crash anymore.

bugs.title: Modifying address-list resets the route advertisement on virtual servers.
bugs.symptoms: If you modify an address list associated with a virtual server, any modifications done to virtual addresses are lost when the address list is modified. This issue has also been shown to cause inconsistent ICMP response behavior when 'selective' mode is used.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: -- Create an address list. -- Assign it to a Virtual Server. -- Modify some or all virtual addresses. -- Modify the address list.
bugs.impact: -- Modifications made to virtual addresses are lost. -- Possible ICMP response issues when 'selective' mode is used (e.g., responses when all pool members are disabled, or no responses when pool members are enabled).
bugs.fix: Virtual address properties are now preserved when an address list is modified.

bugs.title: GUI cannot delete a cert with a name that contains with * or ＼ or [ ] within the cert name that ends with .crt
bugs.symptoms: If a cert is created with a name that contains * (asterisk) or ＼ (backslash) or [] (square braces) anywhere within the cert (has the file extension .crt), the cert cannot be deleted using the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Certificate names containing * or ＼ or [] for example: *example.crt example*e.crt eaxmple*.crt ＼example.crt exampl＼e.crt example＼.crt [e]xample.crt e[x]ample.crt exampl[e].crt -- Select the checkbox in the GUI and click Delete.
bugs.impact: The certificate is still present. The GUI displays the message: No records to display.
bugs.workaround: You can use TMSH to delete these certs: Note: The following characters must be escaped in the tmsh command: * ＼ [ ] For example: tmsh delete sys file ssl-cert '＼*example'

bugs.title: DNS Cache not functioning
bugs.symptoms: DNS queries are not being cached on the BIG-IP device.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS cache is enabled (System :: Configuration : Device : DNS Cache). -- Device receives DNS queries.
bugs.impact: DNS queries are forwarded, but the BIG-IP system does not cache them.
bugs.fix: DNS queries are now cached when DNS Cache is enabled.
bugs.behavior: Full DNS cache functionality has been restored. This results in performance degradation. You might notice it in OCSP performance, when compared to releases in which full DNS cache functionality is not present. By default, DNS cache is disabled. To recapture performance, enable DNS cache.

bugs.title: Tmm crash while passing diameter traffic

bugs.title: Reboot after tmsh load sys config changes sys FPGA firmware-config value
bugs.symptoms: As a part of FPGA firmware update, "tmsh load sys config" fails. Chmand reports errors: chmand[19052]: FPGA firmware mismatch - auto update, No Interruption! chmand[19052]: 012a0006:6: FPGA HSB firmware uploading now...use caution! Reloading fw_update_post configuration (via systemctl): [FAILED]
bugs.conditions: Running either of the following commands: tmsh load sys config /etc/init.d/fw_update_post reload
bugs.impact: Firmware update fails.
bugs.workaround: Use this procedure: 1. Mount /usr: mount -o rw,remount /usr 2. Add the following line to the '/usr/lib/systemd/system/fw_update_post.service' file: ExecReload=/etc/init.d/fw_update_post reload 3. Reload systemctl: systemctl daemon-reload 4. Reload the file: /etc/init.d/fw_update_post reload
bugs.fix: Added the reload option in fw_update_post service file.

bugs.impact: Erroneous reporting of live update availability: reports 'true'; should report 'false'. For example, the message might report that three modules have updates when only one module does.
