bugs.impact: LDAP data is not updated consistently, and authentication might fail.

bugs.title: When processing server-side TLS traffic, LTM may not enforce certificate chain restrictions
bugs.symptoms: When processing server-side TLS traffic, LTM may not enforce certificate chain restrictions as expected. TLS traffic is encrypted as expected but under certain conditions certificate authentication restrictions are not enforced
bugs.conditions: -Server-side SSL profile. -Certificate chain validation enabled.
bugs.impact: LTM may not enforce TLS certificate chain restrictions as expected.
bugs.fix: LTM now processes server-side TLS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: RESOLV::lookup @<virtual server name> may not work
bugs.symptoms: In v13 later, iRule command RESOLV::lookup @<vs name> does not work
bugs.conditions: The virtual server targeted by the RESOLV::lookup command is not configured with IP protocol UDP ("ip-protocol udp" in TMSH)
bugs.impact: The DNS virtual is working while iRule RESOVE::lookup does not send request to the virtual.
bugs.workaround: Either of these: 1. Modify the target virtual server to specify an IP protocol of UDP 2. Replace the name with IP address to workaround the issue. set hostip [RESOLV::lookup @198.51.100.1 -a $hostname]

bugs.title: Network map shows 'One or more profiles are inactive due to unprovisioned modules' in Profiles section
bugs.symptoms: Network map shows error message: One or more profiles are inactive due to unprovisioned modules.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- A profile is attached to a virtual server, but the module supporting the profile is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: The Network Map shows an error message.
bugs.workaround: Provision the module that supports the profile.
bugs.fix: The button text has been modified to be more informative.

bugs.title: When importing a BIND zone file, SRV/DNAME/NAPTR RRs do not have correct $ORIGIN appended
bugs.symptoms: When importing a BIND zone file, $ORIGIN is appended for rdata from SRV and NAPTR RRs, also not appended for DNAME's owner label.
bugs.conditions: $ORIGIN is used in original zone files and use zone runner to import.
bugs.impact: Zone files are not generated correctly.
bugs.workaround: Do not use $ORIGIN.

bugs.title: Memory corruption during APM SAML SSO
bugs.symptoms: During processing of SAML SSO single logout (SLO) requests, a block of tmm memory may become corrupted.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP system is configured as SAML SP. - External SAML IdP sends SLO request.
bugs.impact: Various possible negative effects, including TMM core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP as SAML SP no longer causes memory corruption when handling certain traffic.

bugs.title: Incorrect value in Transparent Nexthop property
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect value in Transparent Nexthop property on virtual server page with assigned VLAN.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server configured with with transparent next-hop bychecking 'Transparent Nexthop' in the GUI on the LTM Virtual Server page: Transparent Nexthop = None Works fine with:
bugs.impact: Incorrect value shown in Transparent Nexthop property field.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to complete the action successfully.

bugs.title: TMM core with mirroring traffic due to unexpected interface name length
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: -- Platform: B4400 Blade (BIG-IP VPR-B4450N). -- High availability (HA) mirroring is set up. -- Provisioned modules: LTM, AFM. -- HA mirroring messages are received with unexpected interface name length.
bugs.impact: Processing of invalid length can cause memory corruption. The tmm process generates a core. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now validates the length of the interface name before processing the HA message at the receiver side and ignores the HA message if the interface name length is wrong.

bugs.title: Statsd fails to start if one or more of its *.info files becomes corrupted
bugs.symptoms: If one of the *.info files in /var/rrd becomes corrupted, statsd fails to load it and ends up restarting continuously. You see the following messages in /var/log/ltm: -- err statsd[766]: 011b020b:3: Error 'Success' scanning buffer '' from file '/var/rrd/throughput.info'. -- err statsd[766]: 011b0826:3: Cluster collection start error.Exitting.
bugs.conditions: Corrupted *.info file in /var/rrd.
bugs.impact: Stats are no longer accurate.
bugs.workaround: It might take multiple attempts to repair the *.info files. You might have to run the following command several times for different .info files, where <filename> is the actual name of the file (e.g., 'throughput.info'): found=0;while [ $found != 1 ]; do filetype=`file throughput.info | cut -d " " -f2`;if [[ $filetype != "ASCII" ]]; then rm -f <filename>.info; else grep CRC <filename>.info;found=1;fi; done
bugs.fix: The system now detects corrupt *.info files and deletes and recreates them.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing Diameter traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing Diameter traffic
bugs.conditions: -Diameter profile enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes Diameter traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Retreive browser cookie from related domain instead of performing another Bot Defense browser verification challenge
bugs.symptoms: After configuring the "validate upon request" option in "Cross Domain Requests" in a Bot Defense profile, JS challenges continue to be sent.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is enabled -- "Cross Domain Request":"validate upon request" option is enabled -- A browser navigates to a qualified (HTML) page from a related domain.
bugs.impact: Browser receives another JS challenge, instead of retrieving the cookie from the related domain. This causes extra latency for the client.
bugs.workaround: Use "validate in a bulk" option.
bugs.fix: Retrieving the cookie from the related domain even if the page is qualified.

bugs.title: HA daemon sod cannot bind to ports numbered lower than 1024
bugs.symptoms: If the network high availability (HA) daemon sod is configured to use a port number that is lower than 1024, the binding fails with a permission-denied error. This affects binding to ports on both management and self IP addresses. Example log messages: /var/log/ltm err sod[2922]: 010c003b:3: bind fails on recv_sock_fd addr 1.2.3.4 port 1023 error Permission denied. notice sod[2992]: 010c0078:5: Not listening for unicast failover packets on address 1.2.3.4 port 1023. /var/log/auditd/audit.log type=AVC msg=audit(1578067041.047:17108): avc: denied { net_bind_service } for pid=2922 comm="sod" capability=10 scontext=system_u:system_r:f5sod_t:s0 tcontext=system_u:system_r:f5sod_t:s0 tclass=capability
bugs.conditions: -- high availability (HA) daemon sod is configured to use a port lower than 1024 for network high availability (HA) operations. -- Version 13.1.0 or later.
bugs.impact: A network high availability (HA) connection configured to use a port number lower than 1024 on an affected version does not function.
bugs.workaround: Change the port number to 1024 or higher. Note: UDP port 1026 is the default.

bugs.title: Domain cookie same-site option is missing the "None" as value in GUI and rest
bugs.symptoms: There isn't an option to add to a domain cookie with the attribute "SameSite=None". The value "None" which appears as an option is used will not add the attribute at all.
bugs.conditions: You want to have SameSite=none attribute added to a domain cookie.
bugs.impact: You are unable to set SameSite=None
bugs.workaround: Set the SameSite=None cookie value in the application. An iRule could also be added that inserts the cookie. For more information on the iRule, see the following DevCentral article: https://devcentral.f5.com/s/articles/iRule-to-set-SameSite-for-compatible-clients-and-remove-it-for-incompatible-clients-LTM-ASM-APM

bugs.title: FQDN node resolution fails if DNS response latency >5 seconds
bugs.symptoms: When resolving FQDN names for FQDN nodes/pool members, pending DNS requests are timed out after 5 seconds with no response from the DNS server. If there is a persistent latency of 5 seconds or greater in the DNS server responses, FQDN name resolution will fail and ephemeral nodes/pool members will not be created.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP using FQDN nodes/pool members - Persistent latency of 5 seconds or greater in the DNS server responses
bugs.impact: Ephemeral pool members may not be created, thus no traffic will be sent to the intended pool members.
bugs.workaround: Resolve any persistent latency issues that might cause delays of 5 seconds or more in DNS server responses.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing L4 behavioral DoS traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing L4 behavioral DoS traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Enable L4 behavioral DoS.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: Disable L4 behavioral DoS.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes L4 behavioral DoS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Tcpdump does not export the TLS1.3 early secret
bugs.symptoms: Users running tcpdump with the 'ssl:v' flag to obtain the early traffic secret are given the early master secret instead.
bugs.conditions: Run tcpdump with the 'ssl:v' flag.
bugs.impact: Users cannot decrypt TLS1.3 early data packets.
bugs.fix: Tcpdump will now output the early traffic secret with the 'ssl' flag. The 'ssl:v' flag will continue to be used for outputting the early master secret.

bugs.title: Config load fails after changing the BIG-IP Master key which has an encrypted key in it's configuration
bugs.symptoms: Config load fails with an error: 01071769:3: Decryption of the field (privatekey) for object (12004) failed. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP configuration has a secured attribute, for example an encrypted dynad key -- The master key password is changed -- The configuration is loaded before saving the changes
bugs.impact: "tmsh load sys config" fails.
bugs.workaround: After modifying the master key password, save the configuration and then perform the tmsh load sys configuration.

bugs.title: Memory leak on every DNS query made for "HTTP Connector" agent
bugs.symptoms: 'plugin' subsystem of TMM leaks memory, when "HTTP Connector" agent performs DNS query.
bugs.conditions: Access Policy contains "HTTP Connector" agent.
bugs.impact: Roughly 500 KB is leaked for every 10000 requests.
bugs.fix: Fixed memory leak in 'plugin' subsystem of TMM.

bugs.title: WideIP (A) created together with aliases (CNAME) causes missing A records in ZoneRunner
bugs.symptoms: Creating WideIP with aliases at the same time causes ZoneRunner to create CNAME RRset without matching A RRset on the peer.
bugs.conditions: Creating WideIP with aliases at the same time(using GUI or tmsh) causes ZoneRunner to create CNAME RRset without matching A RRset on the peer.
bugs.impact: GTM peer will not respond with correct answer for DNS request.
bugs.workaround: Create wideip with two steps.

bugs.title: During BIG-IP boot, hyper-v driver installation throws error messages on console
bugs.symptoms: Early in the BIG-IP boot, the following error messages are seen on the console: insmod: error inserting '/lib/hv_vmbus.ko': -1 No such device insmod: error inserting '/lib/hv_storvsc.ko': -1 Unknown symbol in module
bugs.conditions: Hyper-V drivers are included in initrd for Microsoft platforms, as the initrd is common for all platforms, The Hyper-v drivers when loaded, resulted in errors below. insmod: error inserting '/lib/hv_vmbus.ko': -1 No such device insmod: error inserting '/lib/hv_storvsc.ko': -1 Unknown symbol in module These errors are seen on Physical BIG-IPs
bugs.impact: No impact to BIG-IP functionality

bugs.title: Unable to set SameSite attribute for AVR session cookie
bugs.symptoms: When trying to set the 'Samesite' attribute using a Local traffic policy according to https://devcentral.f5.com/s/articles/increased-security-with-first-party-cookies-30715, you are able to set the SameSite attribute for all cookies except for the AVR user session cookie.
bugs.conditions: -- Use Google Chrome browser. -- Page load time or user sessions collecting in HTTP Analytics profile is checked for the related virtual server.
bugs.impact: Can't add SameSite attribute to AVR cookies.
bugs.fix: Added an internal parameter, avr_cookie_add_attributes, that allows the BIG-IP system administrator to add a string at the end of the AVR Set-Cookie HTTP response header. Using this internal parameter, the administrator can add the SameSite=None string to opt-out from the Chrome browser modificatio, allowing the AVR cookie behave as before. This change is global and affects all AVR system cookies (page load time & user sessions).

bugs.title: Auto classification signature update fails
bugs.symptoms: During classification update, you get an error: "Error: Exception caught in script. Check logs (/var/log/hitless_upgrade.log) for details" An additional diagnostic is that running the command "/usr/bin/crt_cache_path" reports "none".
bugs.conditions: This is encountered while updating the classification signatures or the protocol inspection updates. It can occur when something goes wrong during license activation, but license activation ultimately succeeds.
bugs.impact: When this issue occurs, auto classification signature update will fail.
bugs.workaround: You may be able to recover by re-activating the BIG-IP license via tmsh.

bugs.title: FPGA firmware changes during configuration loads
bugs.symptoms: FPGA firmware on DDoS Hybrid Defender products might be changed unexpectedly during a configuration load or license update.
bugs.conditions: Configuration load or license update.
bugs.impact: FPGA firmware changes unexpectedly, reboot might be required to stabilize.
bugs.fix: A race condition to select the correct Turboflex profile has been eliminated.

bugs.title: Change help text for Untrusted Cert Response Control and Expired Cert Response Control in ServerSSL OLH
bugs.symptoms: Help text for Untrusted Cert Response Control and Expired Cert Response Control in ServerSSL OLH needs updating.
bugs.conditions: 1. Go to Local Traffic >> Profiles >> SSL >> Server. 2. Create new or edit existing profile and see help text.
bugs.impact: Incorrect content.
bugs.fix: For both Create and Properties help, updated ignore and mask content for both Expired and Untrusted Certificate Response Control fields.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing iRules LX commands
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing iRules LX commands
bugs.conditions: -iRules LX in use
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes iRules LX commands as expected.

bugs.title: Under certain conditions, the virtio driver may core during shutdown
bugs.symptoms: If the virtio driver fails to initialize, it may core during shutdown.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the virtio VE driver. -- The virtio driver fails initialization and shuts down instead.
bugs.impact: TMM cores during driver shutdown.

bugs.title: Audit Log: "cmd_data=list cm device recursive" is been generated continuously
bugs.symptoms: The system generates and logs the following message continuously every 30 seconds, in /var/log/audit: -- bigip1 notice tmsh[47755]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=47755 user=root folder=/ module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=cd / ; -- bigip1 notice tmsh[47755]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=47755 user=root folder=/ module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=list cm device recursive
bugs.conditions: This occurs during normal operation.
bugs.impact: Audit log file contains numerous 'cmd_data=list cm device recursive' messages.
bugs.workaround: -- To prevent the two messages from being logged to /var/log/audit: 1. Edit the 'include' section of syslog configuration to suppress audit logs of 'cmd_data=cd /' and 'cmd_data=list cm device recursive': # tmsh # edit /sys syslog all-properties 2. Replace 'include none' with the following syntax: === sys syslog { - snip - include " filter f_audit { facility(local0) and message(＼"AUDIT＼") and not message(＼"cmd_data=list cm device recursive|cmd_data=cd /＼"); };" - snip - } -- To filter the messages sent to remote syslog servers only, do the following: 1. Set sys syslog remote-servers none: # tmsh modify sys syslog remote-servers none 2. Edit the 'include' section of syslog configuration to suppress audit logs of 'cmd_data=cd /' and 'cmd_data=list cm device recursive': # tmsh # edit /sys syslog all-properties 3. Add the following filter: filter f_remote_loghost { not (facility(local0) and message(＼"AUDIT.*cmd_data=list cm device recursive|cmd_data=cd /＼")); }; Result: The system sends all messages that match the filter to the remote syslog server. It uses the "not" operand to filter the messages out. 4. Add destination and log directives. Below is a sample configuration, with the filter in step 3: sys syslog { include " filter f_remote_loghost { not (facility(local0) and message(＼"AUDIT.*cmd_data=list cm device recursive|cmd_data=cd /＼")); }; destination d_remote_loghost { udp(＼"10.0.0.1＼" port(514)); }; log { source(s_syslog_pipe); filter(f_remote_loghost); destination(d_remote_loghost); }; " }

bugs.title: Check-host-attr enabled in LDAP system-auth creates unusable config
bugs.symptoms: When configuring system auth to use LDAP, if you set check-host-attr to enabled, the resulting /config/bigip/pam.d/ldap/system-auth.conf that is generated cannot be parsed by nslcd.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuring system auth to use LDAP. -- Setting check-host-attr to enabled.
bugs.impact: LDAP-based auth does not function.

bugs.title: Update oprofile tools for compatibility with current architecture
bugs.symptoms: Current operf as shipped with BIG-IP is out of date and will not work. Per the oprofile page (https://oprofile.sourceforge.io/news/) the version included in our systems (0.9.9) was released in 2013.
bugs.conditions: Opcontrol still works but operf will not load. # operf --version use the opcontrol command instead of operf.
bugs.impact: Outdated operf means that it cannot be used for troubleshooting purposes.

bugs.title: URI::query command returning fragment part, instead of query part
bugs.symptoms: The iRule URI commands are designed to parse a given URI string to each components such as scheme (URI::protocol) or authority (URI::host). The URI::query command is designed to return the query part of an URI, but the returned string contains the fragment part. For example, for the URI "foo://example.com:8042/over/there?name=ferret#nose" (an example from Section 3, RFC 3986), URI::query returns "name=ferret#nose". The "#nose" part should not be present in the return value
bugs.conditions: Create a test rule with URI having '#' like this. when HTTP_REQUEST { # from RFC 3986 Section 3 set url "foo://example.com:8042/over/there?name=ferret#nose" log local0. "query: [URI::query $url]" }
bugs.impact: URI operations that involve #fragments may fail.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Possible issues when using DoSL7 and Bot Defense profile on the same virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When DoSL7 and Bot Defense profiles are configured together on the same Virtual Server, some requests might not be handled by the Bot Defense profile.
bugs.conditions: -- DoSL7 profile is attached to the virtual server (with Application). -- Bot Defense profile is attached to the virtual server. -- Another security module is attached to the virtual server (WebSafe, MobileSafe, ASM).
bugs.impact: Some requests might not be processed by the Bot Defense profile.
bugs.workaround: Disable dosl7.idle_fast_path: tmsh modify sys db dosl7.idle_fast_path value disable
bugs.fix: The mechanism which caused this issue is now correctly enabled.

bugs.title: ASMConfig Handler undergoes frequent restarts
bugs.symptoms: Under some settings and load, the RPC handler for the botd process restarts frequently, causing unnecessary churn and message-cluttered logs.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot protection is enabled. -- A high volume of bot attacks are handled.
bugs.impact: The RPC handler for the botd process restarts frequently, causing unnecessary churn and noisy logs
bugs.fix: The botd handler is now restored to a more robust process lifecycle.

bugs.title: A BD memory leak
bugs.symptoms: A memory leak is observed in the bd process. The bd process memory increases over time.
bugs.conditions: A few bytes leak on every request under specific conditions.
bugs.impact: Slowly the bd memory increases until OOM killer is invoked by the kernel.
bugs.fix: The memory leak in the bd process was fixed.

bugs.title: BIG-IP system may forward IP broadcast packets back to the incoming VLAN interface via a forwarding virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: Some received packets are retransmitted back on the incoming VLAN interface.
bugs.conditions: The symptom is found with the following conditions: 1. A forwarding virtual server is configured. 2. A packet is received whose destination MAC address is its unicast VLAN MAC address and the destination IP address is the broadcast address of that subnet.
bugs.impact: Broadcast packets are forwarded back to the incoming VLAN interface might result in loops if there are multiple gateways on the network.
bugs.workaround: Apply an iRule to network-forwarding virtual servers that drops packets destined to the broadcast IP address of local vlans. For example: ltm data-group internal /Common/local_broadcast_ips { records { 10.1.1.255/32 { } 10.1.2.255/32 { } } type ip } ltm rule do_not_fwd_to_bcast_addrs { priority 5 when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { if { [class match [IP::local_addr] equals local_broadcast_ips ] } { drop } } }
bugs.fix: Should not see packets retransmitted on the incoming vlan interface with forwarding virtual server is configured.

bugs.title: Adding port-list to Virtual Server changes the route domain to 0
bugs.symptoms: When attaching the port-list to virtual server dest:port-list, the route domain of the virtual server is changed to the default value of 0, and the port-list is not correctly applied. This is encountered in the GUI but not in the CLI.
bugs.conditions: Using port-list along with virtual server in non default route domain using the GUI.
bugs.impact: You are unable to use the GUI to attach a port-list that uses a non-default route domain to a virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to attach a port-list to a virtual server if the port-list uses a non-default route domain.

bugs.title: Intermittent auth failures with remote LDAP auth for BIG-IP managment
bugs.symptoms: There are intermittent auth failures when accessing the BIG-IP administration interfaces via SSH or the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote LDAP auth is configured. -- An idle timeout RST is received on the LDAP connection before the configured auth LDAP idle-timeout expires. This RST might be generated by tmm (if the connection to the LDAP server is via a defined VLAN), some other intervening device on the network, or from the LDAP server itself (depending on its connection time limit).
bugs.impact: There might be intermittent remote-auth failures.
bugs.workaround: Set the auth ldap idle-timeout to a smaller value, for example, via tmsh: modify auth ldap system-auth idle-timeout 299

bugs.title: TMM crash at Tcl_AfterCancelByUF() while deleting connections.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashed while deleting connections.
bugs.conditions: 1.There are a high volume of connections remaining (those connections born from a virtual server which has iRule with "after XXX -periodic" iRule command) and connections are deleted. 2. A huge number of DNS requests are sent from the same source IP/port to a datagram_LB enabled UDP listener, which results in a huge number of flows in the same bucket and connections are deleted.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.

bugs.title: Errors on VPN client status window in non-English environment
bugs.symptoms: If Network Access resource is being accessed using user interface language other than English, JavaScript errors may be shown in VPN client status window.
bugs.conditions: - Access Policy with languages other than English - Network Access resource assigned to this Access Policy - standalone VPN client in non-English environment
bugs.impact: VPN connection cannot be established.
bugs.fix: Now standalone VPN client can work correctly in non-English environment

bugs.title: Unnecessary HTML response parsing and response payload is not compressed
bugs.symptoms: When either DoS Application Profile or Bot Defense profile are used, or ASM Policy with complex LTM Policy, the Accept-Encoding request header is removed by the BIG-IP system, which causes the backend server to respond with uncompressed payload.
bugs.conditions: One of these options: -- Bot Defense Profile is associated with the Virtual Server. -- DoS Profile is associated with the Virtual Server and has Application (L7) enabled. -- ASM Policy is associated with the Virtual Server and has complex LTM Policy: multiple ASM Policies, or additional rules.
bugs.impact: -- Response payload sent by the backend server is uncompressed. -- Performance impact caused by response parsing.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to disable the option for modification of Referer header: tmsh modify sys db asm.inject_referrer_hook value false Note: Using this brings back the impact of bug 792341.
bugs.fix: The system no longer removes the Accept-Encoding header and no longer parses response payload if not needed based on configuration.

bugs.title: serverssl profile hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the serverssl profile does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: - serverssl profile in use - Intel QAT HW accelerator in use - AES-GCM/AES-CCM encryption in use
bugs.impact: serverssl profile does not process traffic as expected, potentially leading to dropped connections.
bugs.workaround: Use the AES(-CBC) cipher instead of AES-GCM and AES-CCM
bugs.fix: The serverssl profile now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: TMM and the kernel choose different VLANs as source IPs when using IPv6.
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 traffic generated from the host, either from a host daemon, monitors, or from the command line, can use a MAC and IPv6 source address from different VLANs.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple VLANs configured with IPv6 addresses. -- Multiple routes to the same destination, either the same or more specific, default routes, etc., that cover the traffic destination. -- Changes are made to routes that cause the traffic to the destination to shift from one VLAN and gateway to another. This can be typically observed with dynamic routing updates. - The db key snat.hosttraffic is set to disable.
bugs.impact: Traffic to the destination may fail because the incorrect source IPv6/MAC address is used, which might cause monitor traffic to fail.
bugs.workaround: Tmsh list sys db snat.hosttraffic tmsh modify sys db snat.hosttraffic value enable tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: AFM FQDN rule matching is broken when multiple FQDN's in firewall policies resolve to the same IP address
bugs.symptoms: AFM FQDN rule matching is broken when multiple FQDN's in firewall policies resolve to the same IP address
bugs.conditions: -- A firewall policy contains multiple rules -- Two or more rules point to different fully qualified domain names (FQDNs). -- Both FQDNs resolve to the same IP address
bugs.impact: Firewall rule action won't be correctly applied to traffic, causing some traffic to be processed incorrectly by BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Configure FQDN's in such way that no two FQDN's will resolve to the same IP address. If you need to use multiple FQDNs with the same IP address in a policy, configure one as FQDN and the other as a resolved IP address.

bugs.title: One thread of pkcs11d consumes 100% without any traffic.
bugs.symptoms: One thread of pkcs11d consumes 100% without any traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is licensed with NetHSM, and service pkcs11d is running. -- The MCDP service is restarted.
bugs.impact: NetHSM configurations and statistics updates are not updated.
bugs.workaround: Restart the pkcs11d service: tmsh restart sys service pkcs11d
bugs.fix: The system now watches for errors and prevents this error from occurring.

bugs.title: MRF Diameter: memory leak during server down and reconnect attempt which leads to tmm crash and memory usage grow
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak can cause tmm to crash and memory usage to grow.
bugs.conditions: -- Diameter transmission setting is enabled and action should be retrans. -- auto-init should be enabled. -- And server is down.
bugs.impact: Memory corruption will lead to tmm crash in longer run and memory leak make memory usage to grow in linear order. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: When server is down BIG-IP keeps creating new connection to it. there is memory leak need to be fixed.

bugs.title: Could not configure FQDN in DoS Profile DNS NXDOMAIN QUERY Vector
bugs.symptoms: GUI configuration for Dos Profile vector is missing functionality to Check, add and delete FQDN's
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the GUI while creating a new DoS Profile that uses a a DNS NXDOMAIN query vector.
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure a valid FQDN list
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to set configuration

bugs.title: ASM Application Security Editor Role User can update/install ASU
bugs.symptoms: Live Update modifications are allowed for Application Security Editor Role.
bugs.conditions: Login as Application Security Editor user and try to install ASU.
bugs.impact: Application Security Editor Role role is permitted to update Attack Signatures when it shouldn't be.

bugs.title: Multiple rate-limiting agents sharing the same rate-limiting key config may not function properly
bugs.symptoms: When multiple rate-limiting agents share the same rate-limiting key config, removing one agent may cause other agents to not function properly. In case of using tmm.debug, it may generate a core.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple rate-limiting agents sharing the same rate-limiting key config. -- Removing one agent.
bugs.impact: Tmm restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not share the same rate-limiting key config among multiple agents.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm core related to multiple rate-limiting agents.

bugs.title: Sock driver does not use multiple queues in unsupported environments
bugs.symptoms: In some unsupported environments, the underlying sock driver uses only only 1 queue. You can confirm whether it does so by executing the tmctl command to check the rxq column (which shows 0): tmctl -d blade -i tmm/ndal_rx_stats' and You can verify this on the tx side as well.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in certain unsupported environments. Note: When you run 'ethtool -l', you can see: 'command not supported'.
bugs.impact: When multi-q is present, the use of single queue can impact performance when using the sock driver.
bugs.workaround: Use other available drivers. You can check the available drivers by executing the tmctl command: tmctl -d blade -i tmm/device_probed
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the sock driver.

bugs.title: TMM restart loop if virtio platform specifies RX or TX queue sizes that are too large (4096 or higher)
bugs.symptoms: If the underlying virtio platform specifies RX and/or TX queue sizes that are 4096 or larger, the BIG-IP system cannot allocate enough contiguous memory space to accommodate this. Errors similar to these are seen in the tmm log files: ndal Error: Failed to allocate 2232336 (2228224 + 4096 + 16) bytes virtio[0:7.0]: Error: Failed to allocate descriptor chain virtio[0:7.0]: Error: Failed allocate indirect rx buffers
bugs.conditions: -- Using a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) with virtio drivers. -- The underlying platform specifies RX and/or TX queue sizes of 4096 or larger.
bugs.impact: TMM continually restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use the sock driver instead of virtio. In your BIG-IP VE VM execute the lspci command to determine which virtio driver is present: # lspci -nn | grep -i eth | grep -i virtio 00:03.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: Red Hat, Inc Virtio network device [1af4:1000] 00:04.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: Red Hat, Inc Virtio network device [1af4:1000] 00:0b.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: Red Hat, Inc Virtio network device [1af4:1000] Configure a socket driver: echo "device driver vendor_dev 1af4:1000 sock" > /config/tmm_init.tcl Reboot the instance

bugs.title: ConfigSync status remains 'Disconnected' after setting ConfigSync IP to 'none' and back
bugs.symptoms: After setting a device's ConfigSync IP to 'none' and then back to an actual IP address, the device remains in a disconnected state, and cannot establish ConfigSync connections to other BIG-IP systems in its trust domain. MCPD periodically logs messages in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[27610]: 0107142f:3: Can't connect to CMI peer a.b.c.d, TMM outbound listener not yet created.
bugs.conditions: --- BIG-IP system is in a trust domain with other BIG-IP systems. --- Local device's ConfigSync IP is set to 'none', and then back to an actual IP address.
bugs.impact: Devices unable to ConfigSync.
bugs.workaround: This workaround will disrupt traffic while TMM restarts: 1. Ensure the local ConfigSync IP is set to an IP address. 2. Restart TMM: bigstart restart tmm This workaround should not disrupt traffic: Copy and paste the following command into the Advanced Shell (bash) on a BIG-IP system, and then run it. This sets the ConfigSync IP for all device objects to 'none', and then back to their correct values. TMPFILE=$(mktemp -p /var/tmp/ ID882609.XXXXXXX); tmsh -q list cm device configsync-ip > "$TMPFILE"; sed 's/configsync-ip .*$/configsync-ip none/g' "$TMPFILE" > "$TMPFILE.none"; tmsh load sys config merge file "$TMPFILE.none"; echo "reverting back to current"; tmsh load sys config merge file "$TMPFILE"

bugs.title: Active Directory authentication does not follow current best practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, Active Directory authentication does not follow the current best practices.
bugs.conditions: When ADAuth agent is used in VPE
bugs.impact: ADAuth agent is not following best practices
bugs.fix: Active Directory authentication now follows the current best practices.

bugs.title: Traffic does not pass on tagged VLANs on VE configured on Hyper-V hypervisors &start;
bugs.symptoms: Traffic does not pass on tagged VLANs when a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) is deployed on a Hyper-V hypervisor. This may manifest as traffic failing after an upgrade from earlier (unaffected) software versions. Note: This functionality worked as expected in v13.x and earlier, and if the same VE is downgraded to v13.x, VLAN tagging functionality is restored. This is due to an interoperability issue between RedHat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and Microsoft Hyper-V, which seems to affect RHEL v7.3 and RHEL v7.5. Hyper-V on Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2012 do not seem to identify the version of the built-in LIS correctly on Centos 7.3 or Centos 7.5 (which are built on RHEL 7.3 and RHEL 7.5 respectively). Although there is a statement of support by Microsoft for VLAN tagging on RHEL 7.3 and 7.5 when running on Hyper-V, that functionality does not appear to work at present: Supported CentOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux virtual machines on Hyper-V :: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/Supported-CentOS-and-Red-Hat-Enterprise-Linux-virtual-machines-on-Hyper-V.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP VE is deployed on a Hyper-V hypervisor. -- VLAN configured in BIG-IP VE with tagged interfaces, e.g.: net vlan external { interfaces { 1.1 { tagged } } tag 4000 } -- At present, VLAN tagging on the v14.x and v15.x releases does not work because those releases are running on CentOS 7.3 and 7.5 respectively, which both are affected by the MS/RHEL interoperability issue. -- BIG-IP v12.x and v13.x use a different (older) CentOS version, so VLAN tagging works without issue on those releases.
bugs.impact: -- The system does not prevent you from configuring tagged VLANs, even though they do not pass traffic. -- Although upgrades complete and you can reboot into the new boot location (or you can set up on Hyper-V from scratch), traffic does not pass (into the guest) across VLANs that are tagged. Important: If using tagged VLANs on VE setups on Hyper-V is critical to your configuration, you might want to elect to postpone upgrading from a working, v12.x and v13.x release.
bugs.workaround: Essentially, there is no workaround in this release; you must reconfigure the virtual machine to use separate, untagged interfaces for each VLAN. Note: Although this is technically a problem between Hyper-V and the built-in LIS on RHEL 7.3/7.5, this issue is being tracked internally in this bug.
bugs.behavior: In this release, traffic does not pass on tagged VLANs when a BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) is deployed on a Hyper-V hypervisor. This functionality worked as expected in v13.x and earlier, and if the same VE is downgraded to v13.x, VLAN tagging functionality is restored. Important: If using tagged VLANs on VE setups on Hyper-V is critical to your configuration, you might want to elect to postpone upgrading from a working, v12.x and v13.x release.

bugs.title: BGP SNMP trap has the wrong sysUpTime value
bugs.symptoms: The timestamp value of sysUpTime in SNMP traps reported by BGP is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: BGP connection with a peer flaps, and sends traps for the following: bgpSnmpNotifyEstablished bgpSnmpNotifyBackwardTransition
bugs.impact: The sysUpTime in the trap generated by BGP is incorrect.
bugs.fix: Fixed an incorrect calculation of sysUpTime.

bugs.title: Mirroring not working properly when default route vlan names not match.
bugs.symptoms: When using two BIG-IP systems to mirror traffic, mirroring occurs when the default gateway VLAN names match; however, if the default gateway VLAN names don't match, then the BIG-IP system does not mirror client-side packets to the peer, which causes the standby BIG-IP system to reset all client-side flows on failover.
bugs.conditions: -- Two BIG-IP LTM systems configured as a high availability (HA) pair. -- Default gateway VLAN names don't match between them.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system does not mirror client-side packets to the peer, which causes the next-active device to reset all client-side flows on failover. Upon failover all flows are being RST just like a typical failover scenario without mirroring implemented.
bugs.workaround: Use same VLAN name on all external VLANs that might be used for mirroring.

bugs.title: Applied Blocking Masks discrepancy between local/remote event log
bugs.symptoms: Applied Blocking Masks discrepancy between local/remote event log, ASM logging event logs both locally and remotely to BIG-IQ has discrepancy.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when "Applied Blocking Masks" logs are emitted on a device where local and remove event logging is configured.
bugs.impact: This is cosmetic but can lead to confusion.

bugs.title: sflow_agent crash SIGABRT in the cleanup flow
bugs.symptoms: Disabling DHCP on the management port causes sflow_agent to crash.
bugs.conditions: This does not always occur, but when it does occur, it crashes when disabling DHCP on the management port.
bugs.impact: sflow_agent crashes.
bugs.workaround: Do not disable DHCP on the management port
bugs.fix: Placed the NULL check to in sflow agent admin IP handling code

bugs.title: Request Log: wrong filter applied when searching by Response contains or Response does not contain
bugs.symptoms: When searching by "Response contains" or "Response does not contain", an incorrect filter is applied and displayed
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the GUI when selecting "Response contains" or "Response does not contain" filter
bugs.impact: You are unable to search by response in the GUI
bugs.workaround: There is no way to search in GUI, but you can search using REST API
bugs.fix: Correct filter applied and displayed for Response contains or Response does not contain filters

bugs.title: SELinux issue cause zrd down
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading BIG-IP software, zrd fails to start. There are errors in /var/log/daemon.log: err named[19356]: open: /config/named.conf: permission denied
bugs.conditions: This can occur after upgrading, for example, when upgrading from version 14.1.0.6 to 15.0.1.1.
bugs.impact: DNS service disrupted as zrd fails to start after reboot.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command after upgrading: restorecon -rF /var/named/

bugs.title: Nslookup might generate a core during system restart
bugs.symptoms: Nslookup generates a core file. The core file name might start with "nslookup", "isc-worker", "isc-timer" or "isc-socket".
bugs.conditions: Multiple instances of nslookup are running when the system shuts down.
bugs.impact: A core file is generated. However, since this is during system shutdown, the impact should be minimal.

bugs.title: Statsd can deadlock with rrdshim if an rrd file is invalid
bugs.symptoms: -- RRD graphs are not updated. -- System statistics are stale. -- Commands such as 'tmsh show sys memory' may not complete. -- qkview does not complete, as it runs "tmsh show sys memory'. You may see errors: -- err statsd[5005]: 011b0600:3: Error ''/var/rrd/endpisession' is too small (should be 15923224 bytes)' during rrd_update for rrd file '/var/rrd/endpisession'. -- err statsd[5005]: 011b0600:3: Error '-1' during rrd_update for rrd file '/var/rrd/endpisession'.
bugs.conditions: Truncation of a binary file in /var/rrd.
bugs.impact: Stats are no longer collected. Statsd and rrdshim deadlock.
bugs.workaround: Remove the truncated file and restart statsd: bigstart restart statsd
bugs.fix: Now detecting and rectifying truncation of RRD files.

bugs.title: Excessive TMM memory consumption by "Anti-Replay" protection for TLS 1.3 0-RTT/Early Data
bugs.symptoms: Incoming packets are dropped, connections are dropped. "Aggressive mode sweeper" messages recorded in "ltm" log, such as: warning tmm[457]: 011e0003:3: Aggressive mode sweeper: /Common/default-eviction-policy (1cf1) (global memory) 99 Connections killed The output of the following command shows a value of 2.3G for "Alloc (bytes)": # tmsh show sys memory | grep -E "SubSystem|EB.Tree"
bugs.conditions: -- At least one virtual server has a clientssl profile configured to enable the TLS 1.3 protocol, along with the advanced option setting "0-RTT/Early Data with Anti-Replay". (In the Configuration Utility, the field in Profile Properties is "Data 0-RTT" and the value would be "Enabled with Anti-Replay".)
bugs.impact: Dropping packets and connections impedes handling of network traffic. In extreme cases, the shortage of available TMM memory may trigger a greater disruption.
bugs.workaround: In the "clientssl" profile, set the TLS 1.3 option "Data 0-RTT" to "Disabled".

bugs.title: Radius authentication may consume excessive resources
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, radius authentication may consume excessive resources.
bugs.conditions: -Radius authentication enabled.
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: Radius authentication is now processed as expected.

bugs.title: HTTP/2-to-HTTP/2 virtual server with translate-address disabled does not connect
bugs.symptoms: If a virtual server is configured with both client-side and server-side using HTTP/2, and with translate-address disabled, the connection to the server-side does not succeed.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 profiles on both client-side and server-side, using an http-router profile. -- Translate-address is disabled.
bugs.impact: Connections fail.

bugs.title: TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV with TLS1.3
bugs.symptoms: Possible handshake failure with some combinations of TLS Fallback Signaling Cipher Suite Value (SCSV) and SSL profile protocol versions.
bugs.conditions: -- Using fallback SCSV suites. -- Using certain client SSL profile protocol versions (e.g., the virtual server is configured for TLS1.3, and the client is configured for TLS1.0 - TLS1.2).
bugs.impact: Possible handshake failure.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now correctly handles all combinations of fallback SCSV and supported protocol versions.

bugs.title: The fix for ID 439539 can cause mcpd to core.
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd cores during config sync.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on rare occasions when the device transitions from standby to active, and the connection between the BIG-IP peers stalls out.
bugs.impact: Mcpd cores. Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Support for QUIC and HTTP/3 draft-27
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system supports QUIC and HTTP/3 draft-24 and draft-25. IETF released draft-27 in February 2020, and major browser vendors have announced they intend to widely deploy support for it, unlike previous drafts.
bugs.conditions: Browser requests draft-27.
bugs.impact: Connection downgrades to an older version, or fails if the browser cannot downgrade.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports draft-27. (The QUIC community skipped draft-26), has deleted draft-24 support from the implementation, and deprecates support for draft-25.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 Method OPTIONS allows "*" (asterisk) as an only value for :path
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 request is not forwarded and RST_STREAM with PROTOCOL_ERROR is sent back to the client.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 request with method OPTIONS and pseudo header :path value equal to something other than "*" (asterisk).
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 request with Method OPTIONS is limited to :path "*" only. Any other URIs are not forwarded to the server but rejected with RST_STREAM with PROTOCOL_ERROR.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 request with Method OPTIONS now allows the URI to be something other than "*". This request is not rejected, but is forwarded to the server.

bugs.title: ACCESS::session irule command does not work in HTTP_RESPONSE event
bugs.symptoms: When ACCESS::session irule is used in HTTP_RESPONSE event, the APM session creation fails with the following log in /var/log/ltm No HTTP data available - command unsupported in event (line XX)session creation failed - Operation not supported (line XX)
bugs.conditions: Using ACCESS::session create command under HTTP_RESPONSE.
bugs.impact: Cannot create APM session using the ACCESS::session irule command.
bugs.workaround: The same irule ACCESS::session can be used under HTTP_REQUEST to create the APM session.

bugs.title: Flow will abruptly get dropped if "PVA Offload Initial Priority" is set to High/Low
bugs.symptoms: Flows are dropped. This can affect FTP active data channels.
bugs.conditions: "PVA Offload Initial Priority" is set to High or Low (setting to Medium works)
bugs.impact: Flows are dropped, traffic is disrupted.
bugs.fix: Fix the problem so that setting "PVA Offload Initial Priority" to High/Low does not impact traffic.

bugs.title: Add a way to look up URLs in one specified custom category
bugs.symptoms: There is no way to look up URLs in one specified custom category.
bugs.conditions: Category lookup iRule or agent using custom categories is in the policy
bugs.impact: There is no way to use iRules to look up URLs in one specified custom category. If there are multiple custom categories and the URL is only in one of them, the Category Lookup agent and iRule will look through all custom categories even if you only want to look in one.
bugs.fix: You can now use iRules to look up URLs in one specified custom category. CATEGORY::lookup <url> custom -custom_cat_match <category name>
bugs.behavior: There is now an iRule to look up URLs in one specified custom category. CATEGORY::lookup <url> custom -custom_cat_match <category name>

bugs.title: Memory leak in asm_start due to GTM score update
bugs.symptoms: Memory usage of asm_start increases steadily by approximately 450 KB per day.
bugs.conditions: GTM is provisioned (on versions with the fix for ID 864677; otherwise, the issue happens for every configuration).
bugs.impact: Memory usage of asm_start increases steadily by approximately 450 KB per day.
bugs.workaround: Restart ASM periodically.
bugs.fix: Memory usage of asm_start remains stable.

bugs.title: BotDefense JavaScript browser verification can cause low score when using Google Lighthouse tool

bugs.impact: Low performance score on Google Lighthouse tool.

bugs.title: BD crash on specific server cookie scenario
bugs.symptoms: BD crash.
bugs.conditions: Server sends many domain cookies with different domains or paths.
bugs.impact: Traffic distraction, failover.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround, except changing the server's cookies.

bugs.title: APM now displays icons of all sizes what Horizon VCS supports.

bugs.conditions: 1. Open Horizon VCS 2. Associate a custom icon to the application (size other than 32x32) and save the changes. 3. Connect to virtual server or Native client

bugs.workaround: In Horizon VCS, associate the application with an icon that is 32x32.

bugs.title: Bot Defense Profile with staged signatures prevents signature update
bugs.symptoms: When a trying to install a new bot defense signature, the installation fails with the following log message: com.f5.liveupdate.update.dosbotsignatures.file.Update.applyChanges.pl|INFO|Feb 10 13:22:12.924|7347|F5::Dos::BotSignatures::load_from_xml,,Cannot send updated objects to mcp: 01070265:3: The Bot Defense Signature (/Common/Headless Chromium, Chrome) cannot be deleted because it is in use by a Bot Defense Profile Signature Staging.
bugs.conditions: -- A Bot Defense Profile has a staged signature. -- The staged signature points to something that does not exist in the update file.
bugs.impact: The new file cannot be installed.
bugs.workaround: Enforce the staged signature.
bugs.fix: Before deleting the signature, the installation process checks to see whether the signature is staged, and if it is, the process unstages it.

bugs.title: Tmm might crash when under memory pressure
bugs.symptoms: Tmm might crash and restart when under memory pressure
bugs.conditions: SSL Orchestrator with service chaining (Security policy uses services).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: A condition where high tmm memory utilization results in memory corruption has been resolved.

bugs.title: Upgrade (or UCS load) from versions earlier than 14.1.x to 15.0.0 or greater version fails
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade (or UCS load) fails with error: When a Dedicated provision level is set, all other provision levels must be set to None. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Running v14.1.x or earlier. -- Any module provisioned as Dedicated. -- CGNAT enabled as a feature module. -- Upgrade to v15.0.0 or later, or save a v14.1.x or earlier UCS and apply it to a v15.0.0 or later installation.
bugs.impact: Configuration load fails during an upgrade (or when applying the older UCS), and the device stays in an inoperable state.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workaround: -- You must return to the previous version, reset Dedicated, and try the upgrade again. 1. Change the provisioned module's level from Dedicated to Nominal or Minimum in the older version. 2. Upgrade to v15.0.0 or newer version. -- If you cannot downgrade to the older version, do the following: 1. In v15.0.0 or later, assuming ASM is the Dedicated level provisioned module, open the file: /config/bigip_base.conf file. 2. Remove the following lines: sys feature-module cgnat { enabled } sys provision asm { (---> This could be any module, not just ASM.) level dedicated } 3. Add the following lines: sys provision asm { level nominal } sys provision cgnat { level minimum } 4. Try the upgrade again.

bugs.title: Datasync regenerating CAPTCHA table causing frequent syncs of datasync-device DG
bugs.symptoms: Frequent config syncs and spamming of logs are occurring on BIG-IP devices in a high availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.conditions: Datasync CAPTCHA table is re-generated while CAPTCHA is being consumed by users.
bugs.impact: Sync to the datasync groups cause the sync status of the devices to fluctuate.

bugs.title: Creation of new allowed HTTP URL is not possible

bugs.title: OSPF External AS LSAs not adding into RIB
bugs.symptoms: OSPF E2 Routes don't appear in "show op route ospf" although they are in OSPF database
bugs.conditions: Trigger is unknown

bugs.title: The vCMP CPU usage stats are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: The vCMP CPU usage stats are incorrect when process on a secondary blade has the same PID as that of primary blade's qemu process.
bugs.conditions: A process on a secondary blade has the same PID as that of primary blade's qemu process.
bugs.impact: The vCMP CPU usage stats are intermittently incorrect.

bugs.title: Portal Access: in some cases data is not delivered via WebSocket connection
bugs.symptoms: If a client browser opens a WebSocket connection, Portal Access may not send data to the client if the first message in the new connection comes from the server.
bugs.conditions: - Web application with WebSocket connection - First data in WebSocket connection is sent from server to client
bugs.impact: Data is not delivered to the client browser via the WebSocket connection.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing ILX::call commands
Tcpdump capture with very large packet (size close to 65535 bytes) can cause tmm to core
bugs.symptoms: When tcpdump is running to capture packets flowing through tmm, and this traffic being captured involves a very large packet (size close to 65535 bytes), tmm cores.
bugs.conditions: -- A tcpdump capture is running. -- The tcpdump trying to capture tmm packets (e.g., tcpdump -i 0.0). -- The traffic involves a very large packet, close to 65525 bytes.
bugs.impact: Tmm cores and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not run tcpdump to capture tmm traffic if packets being captured are close to 65535 bytes in size.

bugs.title: Latency reduce in case of empty parameters.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic load with many empty parameters may lead to increased latency.
bugs.conditions: Sending requests with many empty parameters
bugs.impact: Traffic load with many empty parameters may cause increased latency through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: Ignore empty parameters

bugs.title: IKEv1 IPsec daemon racoon goes into an endless restart loop
bugs.symptoms: The IKEv1 IPsec daemon racoon goes into an endless restart loop. 2020-01-02 08:36:36: ERROR: /etc/racoon/racoon.conf.BIG-IP:376: "}" duplicated sainfo: loc='ANONYMOUS', rmt='10.42.80.0/24', peer='ANY', id=0 2020-01-02 08:36:36: ERROR: fatal parse failure (1 errors) 2020-01-02 08:36:36: ERROR: failed to parse configuration file.
bugs.conditions: Duplicate wildcard traffic-selectors, one with ::/0 and one with 0.0.0.0/0, attached to different IPsec policies.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels cannot be established.
bugs.workaround: Configure duplicate traffic-selectors only when they are attached to interface mode IPsec policies.
bugs.fix: Config validation now prevents duplicate wildcard selectors attached to tunnel mode IPsec policies.

bugs.title: IKE_SA's Not mirrored of on Standby device if it reboots
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting the standby BIG-IP device, IKE SA's are not mirrored.
bugs.conditions: -- IPSEC is configured in a high availability (HA) environment -- Standby device is rebooted
bugs.impact: IKE_SA's will have to be renegotiated. The performance impact is minimal.

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS (GTM) monitoring: 'CSSLSocket:: Unable to get the session"'messages appearing in gtm log
bugs.symptoms: Err (error) level messages in /var/log/gtm log when DNS (GTM) SSL monitors such as https are used and are unable to connect to the monitored target IP address: err big3d[4658]: 01330014:3: CSSLSocket:: Unable to get the session. These messages do not indicate the IP address or port of the target that failed to connect, and this ambiguity may cause concern.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL-based DNS (GTM) monitor assigned to a target, for example https -- TCP fails to connect due to a layer 2-4 issue, for example: - No route to host. - Received a TCP RST. - TCP handshake timeout.
bugs.impact: The system reports unnecessary messages; the fact that the monitor failed is already detailed by the pool/virtual status change message, and the target changing to a red/down status. These messages can be safely ignored.
bugs.workaround: If you want to suppress these messages, you can configure a syslog filter. For more information, see K16932: Configuring the BIG-IP system to suppress sending SSL access and request messages to remote syslog servers :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K16932.
bugs.fix: Added debug messages for SSL probing with attached DB variable

bugs.title: TMM leaks memory when the 'ACCESS::session remove' iRule command is called in an event other than an ACCESS event.
bugs.symptoms: TMM leaks memory and eventually crashes when it cannot allocate any more memory.
bugs.conditions: The 'ACCESS::session remove' iRule command is called in an event other than an ACCESS event (for example, the CLIENTSSL_HANDSHAKE event). The only affected versions are 13.1.3.2 and 13.1.3.3.
bugs.impact: The leak initially causes traffic disruption, as TMM reaps flows prematurely in an effort to free up memory. Eventually, TMM crashes, as it is unable to allocate any more memory. When this happens, redundant systems fail over. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the 'ACCESS::session remove' iRule command under any event that isn't an ACCESS event. To restore TMM to a fully functional state after making all necessary configuration changes, or to temporarily work around this issue, you can restart TMM with the following command: bigstart restart tmm

bugs.title: Stats might be incorrect for iRules that get executed a large number of times
bugs.symptoms: iRules that execute a lot can make stats counters large enough to overflow in a relatively short amount of time (e.g., a couple of months).
bugs.conditions: Execute an iRule a lot (e.g., make the total number of executions greater than 32 bits) and check its stats.
bugs.impact: After the total number exceeds 32 bits, the counter stats are no longer valid.

bugs.title: Another app is currently holding the xtables lock. Perhaps you want to use the -w option?
bugs.symptoms: When running iptables-restore, you get this error: Another app is currently holding the xtables lock. Perhaps you want to use the -w option? This occurs because firewall rules are not created in iptables and therefore not enforced until after rebooting the device.
bugs.conditions: Creating firewall rules for the management interface.
bugs.impact: Firewall rules for the management interface are not reliably created or enforced.
bugs.workaround: There are four possible workarounds: ======= -- [root:Active:Disconnected] config # lsof -n 2>/dev/null | grep /run/xtables.lock iptables 14009 root 3rW REG 0,20 0 26415 /run/xtables.lock root 13945 0.5 0.3 163992 29216 ? S 19:58 0:00 | \_ /usr/bin/mgmt_acld -do -m root 14009 0.0 0.0 24900 1360 ? S 19:58 0:00 | \_ /sbin/iptables -xvL f5acl ^^^ xtables.lock held by iptables which is being run by mgmt_acld [root:Active:Disconnected] config # bigstart stop mgmt_acld [root:Active:Disconnected] config # killall iptables ^^^ stop mgmt_acld, and kill iptables [root:Active:Disconnected] config # lsof -n 2>/dev/null | grep /run/xtables.lock [root@blpv0678:Active:Disconnected] config # ^^^ verify the lock is gone perform the merge and the rules are loaded. Make sure to restart mgmt_acld afterwards. ======= -- Reboot after every management firewall rule that is created. ======= -- Manually clear the iptables lock then make your changes 1) Run: rm -rf /run/xtables.lock 2) Then make your changes ======= -- If the changes have already been made, Manually clear the iptables lock, then run load sys config. 1) Run: rm -rf /run/xtables.lock 2) Then Run: tmsh load sys config

bugs.title: ASMConfig Handler undergoes frequent restarts
bugs.symptoms: Under some settings and load the RPC handler for the tsconfd process restarts frequently.
bugs.conditions: When processing a large number of configuration updates.
bugs.impact: The RPC handler for the tsconfd process restarts frequently, causing unnecessary churn and noisy logs

bugs.title: The ASM logging Operation_id field has incorrect byte at the end
bugs.symptoms: The operation ID field has one incorrect byte at the end of the string.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if the operation ID is 255 bytes long.
bugs.impact: In the remote log, the operation ID reports the incorrect byte, which might lead to confusion.
bugs.fix: Eliminated the extra byte at the end of the operation ID.

bugs.title: Clicking 'Fix Automatically' in PCI Compliance page does not attach a PCI-compliant-profile on HTTP/2 virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: For an HTTP/2 virtual server with an insecure client SSL profile attached, clicking the 'Fix Automatically' button on the PCI Compliance page creates a PCI-compliant client SSL profile, but fails to attach to the virtual server. The compliance state shows as a red cross mark, indicating the virtual server to be noncompliant.
bugs.conditions: -- No compliant PCI profile is attached to the HTTP/2 virtual server. -- Click the 'Fix Automatically' button on the PCI Compliance page.
bugs.impact: The provision for enhanced configuring does not function as expected for HTTP/2-based virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Manually configure a PCI-compliant profile in SSL profiles, with renegotiation disabled, and attach it to the virtual server.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 virtual servers are now handled correctly in the PCI Compliance page.

bugs.title: Clicking 'Fix Automatically' on PCI Compliance page does not replace non-PCI-compliant-profile with complaint one on HTTP/2 virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Clicking the 'Fix Automatically' button in the PCI Compliance page does not replace the insecure client SSL profile attached on an HTTP/2 virtual server, with a secure one. The compliance state shows as a red cross mark, indicating the virtual server to be noncompliant.
bugs.conditions: -- Clicking the 'Fix Automatically' button on the PCI compliance page. -- A noncompliant PCI profile is attached to the HTTP/2 virtual server. -- A PCI-compliant, client SSL profile with renegotiation disabled is available in the SSL profiles.
bugs.impact: The provision for enhanced configuring does not function as expected for HTTP/2-based virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Manually configure a PCI-compliant profile in SSL profiles, with renegotiation disabled, and attach it to the virtual server.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 virtual servers are now handled correctly on the PCI Compliance page.

bugs.title: Incorrect time used with iQuery SSL certificates utilizing GenericTime instead of UTCTime
bugs.symptoms: iQuery incorrectly interprets iQuery SSL certificate times when they are using GenericTime instead of UTCTime.
bugs.conditions: An iQuery certificate using GenericTime instead of UTCTime. Note that this would only occur with a date beyond the year 2049.
bugs.impact: Internal years are interpreted to be much later than they should be.
bugs.workaround: Use SSL certificates with UTCTime instead of GenericTime.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue in iQuery SSL where GenericTime-formatted years interpreted incorrectly.

bugs.title: Untagged packet traffic does not work on vwire
bugs.symptoms: Untagged packets are going out as tagged from BIG-IP systems on platforms with specific BROADCOM chipsets.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs only on platforms containing the Broadcom Trident II switch series with Maverick/Firebolt5 ASICS.
bugs.impact: Untagged traffic is not working as expected.
bugs.workaround: Solution: Enable the bcm56xxd.hgvlan_check_disable sys db variable and restart the bcm56xxd daemon. tmsh restart /sys service bcm56xxd

bugs.title: Tagged VLAN works only if it is configured in virtual wire.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic drops occur if a VLAN is not configured on a virtual wire.
bugs.conditions: Incoming traffic with a different VLAN that is not part of virtual wire configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic drop can be observed.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Allow the traffic on all the VLANs of a virtual wire by enabling 4kvlans: 1. tmsh modify sys db bcm56xxd.vwire.4kvlans value enable 2. bigstart restart bcm56xxd -- Configure the corresponding tag on virtual wire.

bugs.title: Multi-NIC instances fail to come up when trying to use memory-mapped virtio device
bugs.symptoms: Multi-NIC instances fail to come up while using memory-mapped virtio device. Running the command 'lspci -s <pci-id> -vv' results in the 'region' field reporting 'Memory at xxxxx'.
bugs.conditions: TMM crashes as soon as the BIG-IP system tries to come up.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails to attach to the underlying virtio devices.
bugs.workaround: Switch to the sock driver by overriding tmm_init.tcl. For instructions on how to enable the sock driver, see the workaround in K74921042: BIG-IP VE may fail to process traffic after upgrading the VMware ESXi 6.7 host to Update 2 (or later), available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K74921042.

bugs.title: Mcpd validation for proxy ssl and don't-insert-empty-fragments
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP does not check that proxy ssl and don't-insert-empty-fragments do not exist together. According to the manual at https://techdocs.f5.com/kb/en-us/products/BIG-IP_ltm/manuals/product/bigip-ssl-administration-13-1-0/5.html ********* Important: For security reasons, when you enable the Proxy SSL setting, the BIG-IP® system automatically disables the Don’t insert empty fragments option. Disabling this option when Proxy SSL is enabled guards against a particular type of cryptographic attack.
bugs.conditions: SSL profile with proxy-ssl and option don't-insert-empty-fragments enabled.
bugs.impact: No impact to traffic, but BIG-IQ will reject the BIG-IP configuration since BIG-IQ has this validation.
bugs.workaround: When proxy-ssl is enabled, disable the option don't-insert-empty-fragments.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now validates proxy-ssl cannot be enabled with don't-insert-empty-fragments.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing UDP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing internally generated UDP traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes internally generated UDP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: The 'Reconnect' and 'Reconnect All' buttons do not work if reached via a particular section of the DNS GUI.
bugs.symptoms: The 'Reconnect' and 'Reconnect All' buttons (introduced in BIG-IP version 14.1.0 to restart some or all iQuery connections) do not work when clicked. The 'Reconnect' button does not become enabled when a server is selected from the list, and an error is logged in the browser console. The 'Reconnect All' button is clickable but returns the error when clicked: No response action specified by the request.
bugs.conditions: You have accessed the buttons via the following GUI path: DNS :: GSLB :: Data Centers :: [dc name] > Servers
bugs.impact: The buttons do not work, making the corresponding feature unavailable from the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Access the buttons using the following alternative GUI path: DNS :: GSLB :: Servers

bugs.title: Unanticipated restart of TMM due to heartbeat failure
bugs.symptoms: A tmm thread might stall while yielding the CPU, and trigger a failsafe restart of the tmm process. A core file might be generated without any message logged in /var/log/*.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: None known.

bugs.title: Icap server connection adjustments
bugs.symptoms: Request getting to the ICAP server takes a long time to process (several seconds), which makes the whole transaction slower than expected. When testing the connection to the ICAP server itself, you determine that it is fast.
bugs.conditions: This happens especially with large file uploads that are mixed with smaller file uploads. The smaller uploads are waiting for the bigger upload.
bugs.impact: Slow responses to specific requests.

bugs.title: Connections stall when dynamic BWC policy is changed via GUI and TMSH
bugs.symptoms: Connections stall when dynamic BWC policy is changed via GUI and TMSH.
bugs.conditions: Issue is seen when you have a dynamic bandwidth control policy configured, and you make a change to the policy via the GUI and TMSH.
bugs.impact: Connection does not transfer data.
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM. Delete the relevant configuration, create a new configuration, and apply it.

bugs.title: Flow lookup on subsequent packets fail during CMP state change.
bugs.symptoms: When there is a failover event, there is a chance that some sessions will not move over to new active blade.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) environment. -- A CMP state change occurs.
bugs.impact: For certain IP addresses that have failed to move to the new active device, a new session create request does not create/replace the current session because it is in inconsistent state.

bugs.title: Generic Message profile cannot be used in SCTP virtual
bugs.symptoms: When creating virtual server or transport config containing both SCTP and Generic Message profile, it will fail with an error: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Profile(s) found on /Common/example_virtual that are not allowed: Only (TCP Profile, SCTP Profile, DIAMETER Profile, Diameter Session Profile, Diameter Router Profile, Diameter Endpoint, SIP Profile, SIP Session Profile, SIP Router Profile, DoS Profile, profile statistics)
bugs.conditions: Create virtual server or transport config which contains both SCTP and Generic Message profile.
