bugs.title: Fqdn nodes are not getting populated after BIG-IP reboot when DNS server is accessed through a local virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: After reboot, no access to services host using fqdn nodes. -- fqdn nodes are not populated with IP addresses. -- Unable to access virtual servers served by pools using fqdn nodes.
bugs.conditions: The issue happens after the BIG-IP is rebooted. -- when DNS server is accessed through a local virtual server. -- Single arm cloud BIG-IP with virtual server listening for DNS requests to redirect.
bugs.impact: -- FQDN DNS requests bypassing the listening virtual server. -- Unable to access the pools of those configured fqdn nodes.
bugs.workaround: -- restarting dynconfd. -- Running a script to trigger off "Tmm ready" and either delete the bad flow(s) or a specific connflow entry. -- change the dummy dns server to be something in the same subnet as the single interface.

bugs.title: Unable to collect statistics from BIG-IP system after BIG-IQ restart
bugs.symptoms: AVR fails to send statistics to BIG-IQ. Lack of stats data in the BIG-IQ console.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system is connected to the Data Collection Device (DCD), BIG-IQ. -- DCD is restarted. -- DCD does not send to BIG-IQ configuration instructions via REST interface due to ID 898341.
bugs.impact: Unable to collect statistics from BIG-IP system. Lack of stats data in the BIG-IQ console.
bugs.workaround: Restart avrd: bigstart restart avrd
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with AVR failing to send statistics to BIG-IQ.

bugs.title: XML Policy cannot be imported
bugs.symptoms: XML Export does not work in configurations that have metacharacters or method overrides defined on URLs.
bugs.conditions: A policy that has metacharacter or method overrides defined on a URL is exported to XML format.
bugs.impact: Such a policy cannot be imported.
bugs.workaround: Use binary export/import or move/remove the problematic elements from the XML file: * <mandatory_body> * <operation_id>
bugs.fix: XML Policy export generates files that correctly correspond to the expected schema and can be imported.

bugs.title: Unclear message: TakesTooLong was 0.00 exceeded the lower threshold of 10000
bugs.symptoms: The system presents an unclear error message: TakesTooLong was 0.00 exceeded the lower threshold of 10000.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the AVR page load times drop below the lower acceptable threshold.
bugs.impact: The message is unclear, making resolution difficult. A more accurate message might be: The AVR page load took 0.00, which is lower than the threshold of 10000.

bugs.title: Changing the setting of apm-forwarding-fastl4 profile does not take effect
bugs.symptoms: Changing the setting of apm-forwarding-fastl4 profile does not take effect and is not getting applied to the last leg of client-initiated VPN traffic.
bugs.conditions: - APM is configured on the BIG-IP system. - BIG-IP Administrator (Admin) has configured a VPN tunnel. - Admin is trying to change the TCP characteristic of the last leg of VPN tunnel traffic by tuning the parameters of FastL4 profile apm-forwarding-fastl4.
bugs.impact: Admin cannot enforce the updated values of apm-forwarding-fastl4 profile on the last leg of client-imitated VPN tunnel traffic.

bugs.title: Traffic is not classified when adding port-list to virtual server from GUI
bugs.symptoms: Traffic is not matching to the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Using the GUI to configure traffic-matching-criteria by adding port-list to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic loss.
bugs.workaround: Creating traffic-matching-criteria from the command line root@(localhost)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# create ltm traffic-matching-criteria tmc_name_here destination-address-inline <IP ADDR>%10 route-domain <Route domain name>

bugs.title: Enable logging of IKE keys
bugs.symptoms: IPsec debug level logging does not provide encryption and authentication key information for IKEv1 IKE negotiation. This information is commonly logged by IPsec vendors in order to allow network administrators the ability to decrypt failing ISAKMP exchanges.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has an IPsec IKEv2 tunnel configured. -- debug level logging is enabled.
bugs.impact: Without the encryption and authentication key information, an ISAKMP negotiation cannot be inspected when troubleshooting tunnel negotiation.
bugs.workaround: None, although the remote peer may log this information.
bugs.fix: Added sys db variable 'ipsec.debug.logsk' to enable logging of IKE SA keys.

bugs.title: Several SCTP commands unavailable for some MRF iRule events :: 'command is not valid in current event context'
bugs.symptoms: The following SCTP iRule commands: -- SCTP::mss -- SCTP::ppi -- SCTP::collect -- SCTP::respond -- SCTP::client_port -- SCTP::server_port Are unavailable in the following MRF iRule events: -- GENERICMESSAGE_EGRESS -- GENERICMESSAGE_INGRESS -- MR_EGRESS -- MR_INGRESS Attempts to use these commands in these events result in errors similar to: 01070151:3: Rule [/Common/sctp_TC] error: /Common/sctp1: error: [command is not valid in current event context (GENERICMESSAGE_EGRESS)][SCTP::ppi 46].
bugs.conditions: -- Using MRF and SCTP. -- Using the specified set of iRule commands within the listed iRule events.
bugs.impact: Unable to use these iRule commands within these iRule events.
bugs.fix: These iRule commands are now available within these iRule events.

bugs.title: Executing a command in "mgmt tm" using iControl REST results in tmsh error
bugs.symptoms: When you try to update the frequency of live-update using iControl REST, it results in a java exception being returned instead of updating the value.
bugs.conditions: When a command for updating the frequency of live updates is executed using iControl REST in an ASM configured BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: You are unable to update the frequency of live-update via iControl REST.

bugs.title: MR::available_for_routing iRule command prevents client side connections from being counted as available for routing towards
bugs.symptoms: In systems with a large number of incoming connections from a low number of client IP addresses, the connections are not spread across all TMMs. All entries for a client IP address are stored on the same TMM. Lookup of one of the records returns all records for an IP address. This can lead to exceeding the available bits available for reference counting.
bugs.conditions: A large number of incoming connections from a low number of client IP addresses.
bugs.impact: An internal overflow can cause a fault. This might result in a crash or core.
bugs.fix: You can now identify which client side connections do not need to have messages routed towards them using a new MR::available_for_routing iRule command. Note: If reverse routing is not required, there is no need to include the client side connections.
bugs.behavior: There is a new MR::available_for_routing iRule command to flag that a connection should not have messages routed towards them.

bugs.title: SafeNet install fails with the message 'path not allowed'
bugs.symptoms: SafeNet Luna Client installation fails with the message 'path not allowed.
bugs.conditions: -- Attempting to install SafeNet Luna Client with the shell script nethsm-safenet-install.sh.
bugs.impact: Cannot install SafeNet Luna Client.
bugs.workaround: 1. Open the file "/config/ssh/scp.whitelist" in an editor 2. Add the line "/usr/safenet/lunaclient" 3. Save the changes. 4. Try the install again.

bugs.title: Order of ciphers changes after updating cipher group
bugs.symptoms: The order of cipher results may change with no modification in the cipher group.
bugs.conditions: Click 'Update' in a cipher group in the GUI without making any changes.
bugs.impact: The order of the ciphers changes. During a handshake, SSL/TLS may not be able to select ciphers in the preferred order.
bugs.workaround: Create a cipher rule with the preferred cipher order and include only a single rule in cipher group allow list.

bugs.title: IPv6 static BFD configuration is truncated or missing
bugs.symptoms: -- When an IPv6 address used in the command 'ipv6 static <addr> <gateway> fall-over bfd' exceeds 19 characters, it gets truncated. -- IPv6 static BFD configuration entries go missing during a daemon restart.
bugs.conditions: IPv6 static BFD configuration.
bugs.impact: The IPv6 static BFD configuration does not persist during reloads. -- The long IPv6 addresses get truncated. -- The configuration is removed upon daemon restart.

bugs.title: SSL handshakes fail on secondary blades for Thales keys created with fipskey.nethsm after upgrade to 14.1.x and re-import of the keys from HSM
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshakes intermittently fail for virtual servers using HSM keys. In /var/log/ltm you see errors: err pkcs11d[6575]: 01680002:3: Key table lookup failed. error.
bugs.conditions: 1. Keys were created on earlier versions of BIG-IP software with fipskey.nethsm wrapper, and the device was upgraded to 14.1.0 or later. 2. Keys were created on BIG-IP v14.1.0 or later directly, using fipskey.nethsm wrapper. 3. The platform is a multi-bladed Viprion. This can occur after applying the workaround for ID758491: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID758491.html
bugs.impact: SSL handshakes that arrive on the secondary blade(s) fail. Handshakes arriving on the primary blade work fine.
bugs.workaround: Re-install the Thales client after the upgrade.

bugs.title: Missing critical files causes FIPS-140 system to halt upon boot
bugs.symptoms: After activating a FIPS 140-2 license on a device and rebooting, the device fails to boot.
bugs.conditions: -- Device is licensed for FIPS 140 mode -- A critical system file is missing
bugs.impact: System halts during boot because of sys-eicheck.py failure.
bugs.workaround: Prior to rebooting into FIPS 140-2 mode, ensure that there are no missing critical files by running the sys-eicheck command. If the missing files are due to missing signature update files: - Manually upload the missing images in System ›› Software Management : Live Update - this will ensure that the image is associated with an installation record.

bugs.title: Multicast control-plane traffic requires handling with AFM policies
bugs.symptoms: AFM virtual-server specific rules are being matched against control-plane traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Broadcast OSPF configured. -- AFM provisioned. -- OSPF neighbor configured.
bugs.impact: OSPF neighborship is not formed.
bugs.workaround: Add an AFM route-domain policy.

bugs.title: Attack signatures are enforced on excluded headers under some conditions
bugs.symptoms: Attack signatures are marked as detected when they should be marked as excluded (i.e., a false positive).
bugs.conditions: -- A 100-continue transaction occurs in HTTP. -- The internal parameter answer_100_continue is set to a non-default value of 0.
bugs.impact: False positive enforcement for header signature.
bugs.workaround: Set the answer_100_continue to 1 (default) on versions later than 15.0.0.

bugs.title: Tmm might crash when ASM, AVR, and pool connection queuing are in use
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and generates a core file.
bugs.conditions: -- System is provisioned for at least ASM, AVR, and LTM. -- An LTM pool is configured to use connection queuing. -- The LTM pool is used on a virtual server with an analytics profile.
bugs.impact: Tmm might crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable connection queuing on the pool.

bugs.title: APM may consume excessive resources while processing VPN traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, APM may consume excessive resources while processing VPN traffic
bugs.conditions: -APM provisioned -VPN clients connected
bugs.impact: Excessive resources consumption, potentially leading to a TMM crash and failover event.
bugs.fix: APM now processes VPN traffic as expected.

bugs.title: GTP profile and GTP::parse iRules do not support information element larger than 2048 bytes
bugs.symptoms: GTP message parsing fails and log maybe observed as below: GTP:../modules/hudfilter/gtp/gtp_parser.c::242 (Failing here. ). GTP:../modules/hudfilter/gtp/gtp_parser_ver_2.c::153 (Failing here. ). GTP:../modules/hudfilter/gtp/gtp_parser.c::103 (Failing here).
bugs.conditions: - GTP profile is applied to virtual or GTP::parse command is used - GTP message contains IE (information element) which is larger than 2048 bytes
bugs.impact: - message parsing fails, traffic maybe interupted
bugs.fix: GTP profile and GTP::parse iRules now support IE larger than 2048 bytes

bugs.title: Azure Active Directory deployment fails on BIG-IP 15.1
bugs.symptoms: In restnoded.log you see an error: severe: [[azureUtils] ] Cannot get key data. Worker not available :/tm/access/certkey-file-helper/available, details: URI path /tm/access/certkey-file-helper/available not registered. Please verify URI is supported and wait for /available suffix to be responsive.
bugs.conditions: Azure Active Directory is enabled.
bugs.impact: Azure Active Directory can not be deployed on BIG-IP 15.1

bugs.title: Configuration changes made by Certificate Manager role do not trigger saving config
bugs.symptoms: Configuration changes made in the BIG-IP GUI by a user with role 'Certificate Manager' do not result in the configuration being saved. If the system is rebooted (or MCPD restarted) without saving the configuration, those changes will be lost.
bugs.conditions: -- User with role 'Certificate Manager'. -- Changes made in GUI. -- System rebooted.
bugs.impact: Loss of configuration changes.
bugs.workaround: Users with a 'Certificate Manager' role can save the configuration from tmsh: tmsh save /sys config Alternately, another user can save the configuration.

bugs.title: Existence of rewrite profile with HTTP profile response chunking mode 'sustain' always triggers client-side chunking
bugs.symptoms: When using the rewrite profile, unchunked server responses where content-type is not text/html or text/css also gets converted to chunked encoding in client-side. Also, the server response is missing a message-body (no content-type/content-length). The client device receives 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' in the message-header and receives a chunked body if the origin response has a message-body. The client receives a zero-length chunk if the origin response has no message-body. Prior to BIG-IP version 15, chunking happens only if origin server response has content-type header set to either text/html or text/css.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP profile response chunking is set to 'sustain'. - The virtual server has rewrite profile attached. - Server response has content-type set not to text/html or text/css OR no content-type header.
bugs.impact: End users may notice a change in chunking behavior after upgrading from prior release.
bugs.workaround: Use response chunking mode 'unchunk'

bugs.title: [GUI] GTM wideip-pool-manage in GUI fails when tens of thousands of pools exist
bugs.symptoms: Making changes to wide IP pools through GUI management do not take effect.
bugs.conditions: -- GTM configuration contains a sufficiently high number of pools (~ 15,000). -- Using the GUI to assign a pool to a wide IP.
bugs.impact: Changes do not take effect. Unable to use the GUI to manage which pools are associated with a wide IP.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH.

bugs.title: Custom dialup does not establish VPN
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to establish a VPN using a custom dialup does not establish the connection, and reports an error: ...finished with code, -1073740512
bugs.conditions: -- Setup simple Network Access resource. -- Download the client package onto the client system and install it. -- Use WinLogon Integration/Custom dialup to establish VPN.
bugs.impact: WinLogon Integration/Custom dialup fails to establish VPN.
bugs.workaround: Use EdgeClient or F5 Helper Applications to establish VPN.
bugs.fix: WinLogon Integration/Custom dialup establishes VPN successfully.

bugs.title: N3FIPS kernel driver crash
bugs.symptoms: The N3FIPS driver crashes and BIG-IP reboots.
bugs.conditions: Conditions are unknown. This occurs rarely.
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption due to BIG-IP system reboot

bugs.title: Listing property groups in TMSH without specifying properties lists the entire object
bugs.symptoms: When listing a property group, if you do not specify any specific properties within that group, the entire object is listed.
bugs.conditions: -- Using TMSH to list a property group of an object. -- Not specifying any properties within the property group.
bugs.impact: Unexpected output.

bugs.title: Syslog-ng 'program' filter does not work
bugs.symptoms: The 'program' filter type does not work with the BIG-IP system's version of syslog-ng.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the 'program' expression in a syslog-ng filter.
bugs.impact: Unable to filter messages as expected.

bugs.title: Alert before Brute Force Protection (BFP) hash are fully utilized
bugs.symptoms: Brute Force Protection (BFP) uses a hash table to store counters of failed logins per IP addresses and usernames. There is a separate hash table for each virtual server. When the hash table is fully utilized and new entries need to be added, the LRU entry is being removed without logging a warning.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered when Brute Force Protection is enabled and the hash table reaches its maximum capacity.
bugs.impact: No alert is sent when entries are evicted.
bugs.fix: Alert/Warning is now announced in ASM logs, describing the status of the hash table.

bugs.title: APM Brute Force Protection resources do not scale automatically
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, resources for Brute Force Protection must be manually scaled by administrators to provide full protection.
bugs.conditions: -- Many virtual server (hundreds) that have web application protection with brute force protection enabled. -- Numerous failed login requests coming to all virtual servers all the time.
bugs.impact: Administrators must manually change the hash size upon need instead of relying on the automatic configuration.
bugs.workaround: Set the internal parameter external_entity_hash_size to 0 to allow automatic recalculation of the correct value.
bugs.fix: Brute Force Protection resources are now scaled automatically based on available system resources.

bugs.title: Brute Force Protection (BFP) hash table entry cleanup
bugs.symptoms: Brute Force Protection (BFP) uses a hash table to store counters of failed logins per IPs and usernames. There is a separate hash table for each virtual server. When the hash table is fully utilized and new entries need to be added, the LRU entry is being removed. This scenario may cause mitigated entries to keep getting removed from the hash table by new entries.
bugs.conditions: There is a separate hash table for each virtual server, and its size is controlled by the external_entity_hash_size internal parameter. When it is set to 0, the size is determined automatically based on system memory. Otherwise, it is the maximum size of the hash tables together, then divided into the number of virtual servers which have traffic and BFP enabled. In case of the latter, there might be a chance that with too many virual servers the hash table may reach it's maximum capacity.
bugs.impact: Mitigated entries that keep getting removed from the hash table by new entries, may result in attacks not getting mitigated.
bugs.fix: Mitigated entries are kept in the hash table.

bugs.title: WAM image optimization can leak entity reference when demoting to unoptimized image
bugs.symptoms: WAM image optimization can leak entity reference when demoting to unoptimized image. WAM allows PNG files to be optimized to WEBP and JPG files to be optimized to JPEG XR formats, based on capabilities inferred from the client's User-Agent value. Once the optimized version is in the cache, internal check failures might cause the entity/document to be reverted to the unoptimized version. If this unoptimized version is already present in the cache, a reference to the corresponding entity is leaked, thus causing the entity to be held in memory along with attached resource/document objects and associated storage (UCI).
bugs.conditions: -- WAM-optimized PNG files (to WEBP) and JPG files (to JPEG XR) on tye system. -- A policy change occurs that causes an internal check to fail. Note: This can also occur in some cases without actual changes to the policy if the optimization step is skipped by wamd.
bugs.impact: WAM image optimization might leak entity reference.

bugs.title: TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: Rare TMM crash, failover.
bugs.conditions: Some load on specific configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing SIP data
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing SIP data
bugs.conditions: -SIP ALG profile enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes SIP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: IPsec interoperability problem with ECP PFS
bugs.symptoms: IPsec tunnels fails to remain established after initially working. On the first ESP Security Associations (SAs) establishment, an IPsec tunnel works. After the expiry of the SAs causes a re-key, the keys are calculated incorrectly by the BIG-IP system. The BIG-IP system sends ESP packets to the remote peer, but the remote peer cannot decrypt the packet. Likewise, the BIG-IP system cannot decrypt packets from the remote peer. This may also immediately present as a problem when trying to establish a second tunnel to the same peer.
bugs.conditions: - IPsec IKEv2 tunnel. - A remote peer that is not another BIG-IP system. - Elliptic curve groups (ECP) is used for Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS).
bugs.impact: Multiple IPsec tunnels to the same remote peer cannot be established concurrently, or tunnels fail after a period of time.
bugs.workaround: Do not use ECP for PFS.
bugs.fix: The ECP PFS state is now correctly maintained and will interoperate with other vendor IPsec products.

bugs.title: TCP::respond causing memory exhaustion issue when send buffer overwhelmed available TCP window
bugs.symptoms: With increasing traffic on a virtual server with an iRule configured to send TCP::respond, iRules operate fine until some threshold is reached, after which memory usage continually increases even though the traffic level remains stable. This memory growth increases until the reaper is activated and connections are removed.
bugs.conditions: A specific threshold of data is reached. The threshold varies, depending on the memory available on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Memory usage continually increases even though the traffic level remains stable. This memory growth increases until the reaper is activated and connections are removed. A tmm core is observed. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: CEC update using incorrect method of determining number of blades in VIPRION chassis
bugs.symptoms: There is an issue with the script used for the Traffic Intelligence (CEC (Classification Engine Core)) Hitless Upgrade that misses installing on some blades during install/deploy on VIPRION systems. Symptoms include: -- POST error in the GUI. -- Automatic classification updates are downloaded successfully, but downloaded packages disappear after some time if you do not proceed to install/deploy.
bugs.conditions: -- CEC hitless update. -- Using VIPRION chassis.
bugs.impact: Unable to auto-update Classification signature package on all slots, because the slot count reported for CEC is 0. These packages are installed only on the current slot.
bugs.workaround: Install the package manually on each slot. Note: When you refresh the GUI page, the downloaded package appears in the 'Available to Install' list, and you can proceed to install on each slot.

bugs.title: Safari browser might be blocked when using Bot Defense profile and related domains.
bugs.symptoms: As a fix to ID879777 (https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID879777.html), when navigating to a related domain using Safari, requests might be blocked.
bugs.conditions: - Using Bot Defense profile, with "Cross Domain Requests" mode "Validate Upon Request" - BIG-IP version containing fix of ID879777 (16.0 and higher or EngHF) - Surfing the site using Safari browser.
bugs.impact: Some requests might be blocked.
bugs.fix: Set the cookie so all requests in the target domain will contain it.

bugs.title: HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE is not raised for HTTP early response
bugs.symptoms: When server sends the response early (before the request is completed), client-side HTTP sends the response but does not raise HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP profile is configured. - Request-log profile is configured. - HTTP request is incomplete.
bugs.impact: Timeout occurs and the BIG-IP system sends shutdown.

bugs.title: AFM Debug Reroute feature not supported
bugs.symptoms: AFM Debug Reroute feature does not work.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use the AFM Debug Reroute Feature.
bugs.impact: Cannot use the AFM Debug Reroute feature.

bugs.title: Loopback traffic might get dropped when VLAN filter is enabled for a virtual server.
bugs.symptoms: Loopback traffic (local traffic) destined to a virtual server might get dropped when the incoming packet matches a terminating connection flow.
bugs.conditions: -- VLAN filter is enabled on the virtual server created for loopback traffic processing. -- An incoming packet matches a terminating connection flow (i.e., the connection flow terminates because of timeout, being dropped by iRule, etc.).
bugs.impact: Traffic that is matched against a terminating connection flow of a virtual is not processed by the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Because this filter is ignored for loopback traffic, removing the 'Enabled On VLAN' filter at the virtual server mitigates the issue.

bugs.title: TMM crash occurred while generating cookie for TCP Fast Open
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: TMM core occurred while generating a cookie for TCP Fast Open.
bugs.impact: TMM coring causes a failover event. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Error status in 'tmsh show cm failover-status', and stale data in some tmstat tables, after management IP address change.
bugs.symptoms: -- The 'tmsh show cm failover-status' command shows a status of 'Error' when the command is run on a peer of a device that underwent a management IP address change. -- Should the sod_tg_conn_stat or sod_tg_msg_stat tmstat tables be inspected using the tmctl command, the tables show stale information in the entry_key column. Note: Additionally, in certain cases, it is possible for failover functionality to be broken after the management IP address change, meaning devices remain stuck in an improper Active/Active or Standby/Standby state. This further aspect of the issue is tracked under ID999125. This ID tracks only the cosmetic defect.
bugs.conditions: -- Two or more devices in a sync-failover device-group. -- The management IP address is changed on one of the devices. The error appears under either of these conditions: -- The 'tmsh show cm failover-status' is run on a peer of the device that underwent the management IP address change. -- The sod_tg_conn_stat or sod_tg_msg_stat tmstat tables are inspected using the tmctl command.
bugs.impact: The 'tmsh show cm failover-status' command indicates an error.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by running the following command on the peers of the device which underwent a management IP address change: tmsh restart sys service sod

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator incorrectly displays unlicensed URLDB categories
bugs.symptoms: Without URLDB or SWG being provisioned, when the SSL Orchestrator guided configuration is used to deploy a topology, the security policy page will display the unlicensed Forcepoint (URLDB) categories under "Category Lookup (SNI)" conditions drop down.
bugs.conditions: URLDB or SWG are not provisioned
bugs.impact: Use of the unlicensed Forcepoint (URLDB) categories, other than custom, will lead to license failures.
bugs.workaround: Select only custom categories from the "Category Lookup (SNI)" dropdown.

bugs.title: GARPs not sent on virtual server creation
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server is created, GARPs are not sent out.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a new virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic could be impacted if other systems have the virtual server address already in their ARP caches.
bugs.workaround: After creating the virtual server, disable and re-enable the ARP setting on the corresponding virtual address.
bugs.fix: GARPs are now sent when a virtual server is created.

bugs.title: Extend logging for incomplete HTTP requests
bugs.symptoms: Logging is not triggered for incomplete HTTP requests.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP profile is configured. - Request-log profile is configured. - HTTP request is incomplete.
bugs.impact: Logging is missing for incomplete HTTP requests.
bugs.fix: Logging is now triggered at shutdown for incomplete HTTP requests.

bugs.title: Corruption detected in /var/log/btmp
bugs.symptoms: The boot_marker is written to /var/log/btmp, but /var/log/btmp is a binary file. A message similar to: warning <process>[10901]: pam_lastlog(<process>:session): corruption detected in /var/log/btmp ... may be logged to /var/log/secure.
bugs.conditions: This issue is triggered following a reboot of the BIG-IP system. Subsequently, you may observe the log message appearing in relation to various administrative activities, such as logging in through the console or restarting the tomcat service.
bugs.impact: Since this file is unknowingly corrupt after each boot, any potential investigation needing this data may be compromised.
bugs.workaround: Option 1; After bootup you can truncate the file. $ truncate --size 0 /var/log/btmp This will remove any instances of failed logins from the file. --or-- Option 2; this will stop boot_markers from logging to /var/log/btmp: CAVEATS: - If the system has FIPS enabled, do not use this workaround! Modifying this file will cause FIPS validation to fail the next time it runs, and the system will halt on next boot. - This workaround will not persist on software upgrades. - Familiarity with vi is required to perform this. Backup: cp /etc/sysconfig/sysinit/01bootlogmarker.sysinit /var/tmp/01bootlogmarker.sysinit.bak Open in vi: vi /etc/sysconfig/sysinit/01bootlogmarker.sysinit Change the following line to include "btmp": old: excludeFiles=( "lastlog" "wtmp" "tmm*tech.out" "*.json" ) new: excludeFiles=( "lastlog" "wtmp" "btmp" "tmm*tech.out" "*.json" ) Force save and quit with (required since file is RO): :wq! Truncate the "/var/log/btmp" file: truncate --size 0 /var/log/btmp Reboot

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing APM data
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing APM data.
bugs.conditions: -- An APM access policy is configured with "Modern" customization.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use Access Policies with "Standard" customization.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes APM data as expected.

bugs.title: HTML profile forces re-chunk even though HTML::disable
bugs.symptoms: HTML profile performs a re-chunk even though HTML::disable has been executed in the HTTP_RESPONSE event.
bugs.conditions: Using HTML::disable in an HTTP_RESPONSE event.
bugs.impact: The HTML profile still performs a re-chunk.

bugs.title: OSPFd SIGSEGV core when 'ospf clear' is done on remote device
bugs.symptoms: The ospfd process generates a core.
bugs.conditions: -- IA routes. -- OSPF is in FULL/DR state.
bugs.impact: An OSPF daemon generates a core, potentially losing routing information and OSPF dynamic routes for a moment while the ospfd daemon restarts.
bugs.fix: OSPF no longer cores when running 'clear ip ospf' on remote.

bugs.title: Configuration error caused by Drafts folder in a deleted custom partition
bugs.symptoms: Error during config load due to custom partition associated Draft folder exists after deleting partition. 01070734:3: Configuration error: Can't associate folder (/User/Drafts) folder does not exist Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Create draft policy under custom partition
bugs.impact: Impacts the software upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Remove the Draft folder config from bigip_base.conf or use command "tmsh delete sys folder /User/Drafts" followed by "tmsh save sys config" after removing partition.

bugs.title: ASM Policy Event Logging stops working after 'No space in shmem' error disconnection mitigation
bugs.symptoms: ASM event logging stops working.
bugs.conditions: This can occur during normal ASM operation. It occurs after ASM executes 'No space in shmem' error disconnection mitigation, and this error is logged.
bugs.impact: ASM Policy Event Logging stop working; new event is not saved.
bugs.workaround: Restart asmlogd and pabnagd: pkill asmlogd pkill pabnagd

bugs.title: Incorrect pool member concurrent connection value
bugs.symptoms: In AVR pool-traffic report, 'server-concurrent-conns' reports a larger value than 'server-max-concurrent-conns'.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when viewing the pool-traffic report.
bugs.impact: Incorrect stats reported in the pool-traffic report table
bugs.workaround: In /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tmstat_pool_traffic_measures.cfg, change the formula of server_concurrent_connections: From this: formula=round(sum(server_concurrent_conns),2) Change it to this: formula=round(sum(server_concurrent_conns)/count(distinct time_stamp),2)
bugs.fix: Changed the calculation formula of 'server-concurrent-conns' so it reports the correct statistics.

bugs.title: GUI issues for Access :: Profiles/Policies : Customization : General Customization or Advanced Customization
bugs.symptoms: Error messages when navigating to Access :: Profiles/Policies : Customization : General Customization or Advanced Customization: Button states incorrect on return from server after button push.
bugs.conditions: After creation of an Access Profile with Customization Type = modern (which is the default starting with v15.1.0).
bugs.impact: The GUI for General Customization or Advanced Customization of Access Profiles is not available.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands, in sequence, from an SSH session: cp --preserve=all /var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/eps/default_eps.xml /var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/eps/default_eps.xml.ORG sed -e 's|b\&gt\ã|b\>\ã|' /var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/eps/default_eps.xml.ORG > /var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/eps/default_eps.xml bigstart restart tomcat
bugs.fix: The GUI for General Customization or Advanced Customization of Access Profiles now renders correctly.

bugs.title: Single user mode faced sudden reboot
bugs.symptoms: Being logged into the system in single user mode (emergency shell) causes a sudden automatic reboot after some time (~5-to-10 minutes, or longer).
bugs.conditions: -- Using iSeries platforms. -- When logged into the emergency shell by appending rd.break to kernel command line.
bugs.impact: The device reboots after some time. Because of the automatic reboot, you cannot reliably use the emergency shell.

bugs.title: TMM core in bigproto_output due to NULL peer
bugs.symptoms: The following log messages: --A Enforced Device DOS attack has stopped for vector Bad UDP checksum, Attack ID 3778490180. --err tmm2[29601]: 011e0003:3: Aggressive mode sweeper: /Common/default-eviction-policy (2000000000001) (global memory) 2291 Connections killed
bugs.conditions: -- Lots of DoS attacks. -- Fast L4 protocol profile is in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: OWASP page: File Types score in Broken Access Control category is always 0.
bugs.symptoms: Under Broken Access Control category, the contribution of Disallowed File Types seems to be 0 no matter what is the number of Disallowed File Types in policy. As a result, it is not possible to reach full compliance.
bugs.conditions: Security Policy is configured. Not Applicable for parent or child policy.
bugs.impact: For any OWASP configurable policy (i.e. not parent or child policy), the policy cannot reach the maximum score for Broken Access Control category

bugs.title: Bot defense Profile list is loads too slow when there are 750 or more Virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Security :: Bot Defense : Bot Defense Profiles page loading takes a long time when there are profiles configured with hundreds of virtual servers. For example: a configuration with 750 virtual servers takes about 40 seconds to load the page. Configuration with 1300 virtual servers takes more than 70 seconds.
bugs.conditions: At least one Bot profile attached to hundreds of virtual servers. For 750 and more virtual servers attached the slow loading is significant.
bugs.impact: Bot Defense list page loading time can take more than 30 seconds.

bugs.title: TMM crash following redirect when Proactive Bot Defense is used
bugs.symptoms: TMM may rarely crash when Proactive Bot Defense is enabled.
bugs.conditions: TMM may rarely crash under specific configurations when Proactive Bot Defense is used.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.

bugs.title: VPN Tunnel establishment fails with some ipv6 address
bugs.symptoms: VPN Tunnel establishment fails with some ipv6 address
bugs.conditions: - APM is provisioned. - Network Access with IPv6 virtual server is configured.
bugs.impact: VPN Tunnel cannot be established.
bugs.workaround: 1. Disable the DB variable isession.ctrl.apm: tmsh modify sys db isession.ctrl.apm value disable 2. Perform 'Apply Access Policy' for the access policy attached to the virtual server. Important: The iSession control channel is needed if optimized apps are configured, so use this workaround only when 'No optimized apps are configured' is set (available in the GUI by navigating to Access :: Connectivity / VPN : Network Access (VPN) : Network Access Lists :: {NA resources} :: 'Optimization' tab).

bugs.title: TMM fails to sign responses from BIND when BIND has 'dnssec-enable no'
bugs.symptoms: TMM fails to sign responses from BIND.
bugs.conditions: BIND has 'dnssec-enable no' in named.conf.
bugs.impact: TMM fails to sign responses from BIND.
bugs.workaround: Remove 'dnssec-enable no' from named.conf in options section.

bugs.title: Autodosd returns small bad destination detection value when the actual traffic is high
bugs.symptoms: Bad destination detection threshold cannot accurately reflect the actual traffic pattern.
bugs.conditions: -- Enable bad destination and fully automatic mode. -- Actual traffic is high.
bugs.impact: A small bad destination detection value is returned.
bugs.fix: Fixed the threshold update algorithm.

bugs.title: AD group cache query performance
bugs.symptoms: Active Directory queries are slow.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under the following conditions: -- Active Directory (AD) authentication used. -- There are lots of AD caches in the environment, and users are in deeply nested groups.
bugs.impact: Active Directory query time can be excessive.
bugs.fix: Improved AD cache optimization.

bugs.title: The pkcs11d process cannot recover under certain error condition
bugs.symptoms: When the connection between the BIG-IP system and HSM (SafeNet) is interrupted, pkcs11d is unable to recover in some case.
bugs.conditions: Connection between the BIG-IP system and the HSM device is interrupted.
bugs.impact: SSL handshake failure.
bugs.workaround: Restart the pkcs11d process using the following command: restart /sys service pkcs11d
bugs.fix: Allow pkcs11d to re-initialize on error.

bugs.title: LTM monitor hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, LTM monitors do not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: -Authenticated administrative user -LTM monitor usage
bugs.impact: LTM monitors do not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: LTM monitors now follow current best practices.

bugs.title: Default configuration of security mechanism causes memory leak in TMM
bugs.symptoms: Over time, memory is allocated by the TMM processes for use as 'xdata' buffers, yet this memory is never de-allocated; it is leaked and becomes unusable. Eventually a disruption of service occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has been running for 8 weeks or longer without a system restart. -- The BIG-IP system's internal risk-policy subsystem (used by the security feature modules) has not been configured to communicate with an external risk-policy server. -- In a vCMP configuration, the BIG-IP 'host' instance is always susceptible, since no security features can be configured in its context.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Default configuration of security mechanism no longer causes memory leak in TMM.

bugs.title: URL properties screen does not display Advanced mode
bugs.symptoms: URL properties page is shown in Basic mode, though Advanced is selected when loading the page
bugs.conditions: -- Chrome browser used -- You navigate to another page from the URL properties with Advanced mode selected -- Press the Back button in Chrome
bugs.impact: URL properties page is shown in Basic mode, though Advanced is selected on load of page
bugs.workaround: Select Basic and then Advanced mode to see all options
bugs.fix: URL properties page is initialized correctly in Chrome browser after Back is pressed

bugs.title: Ephemeral pool members may be incorrect when modified via various actions
bugs.symptoms: Ephemeral pool members may not be in the expected state if the corresponding FQDN template pool member is modified by one of several actions. For example: A. Ephemeral pool members may be missing from a pool in a partition other than Common, after reloading the configuration of that partition. B. Ephemeral pool members may not inherit the 'session' state from the corresponding FQDN template pool member if the FQDN template pool member is disabled (session == user-disabled), the config is synced between high availability (HA) members, and BIG-IP is restarted.
bugs.conditions: Scenario A may occur when reloading the configuration of non-'Common' partition, e.g.: -- tmsh -c "cd /testpartition; load sys config current-partition" Scenario B may occur when an FQDN template pool member is disabled (session == user-disabled), the config is synced between HA members, and BIG-IP is restarted.
bugs.impact: Impacts may include: - Missing ephemeral pool members, inability to pass traffic as expected. - Ephemeral pool members becoming enabled and receiving traffic when expected to be disabled.
bugs.workaround: For scenario A, reload the entire configuration instead of just the individual partition. For scenario B, it may be possible to work around this issue by checking the status of ephemeral pool members after BIG-IP restart, and toggling the 'session' value between user-enabled and user-disabled.
bugs.fix: FQDN ephemeral pool members now better reflect expected states after the corresponding FQDN template pool member is modified by one of several actions such as config load, config sync and BIG-IP restart.

bugs.title: Unable to set ASM Main Cookie/Domain Cookie hashing to Never
bugs.symptoms: Disabling ASM Main Cookie/Domain Cookie hashing in a Policy's Learning and Blocking Setting with 'Never (wildcard only)' does not stop the ASM Main Cookie from continuing to hash server-provided cookies.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM enabled. -- Learning mode enabled for Policy. -- Learn New Cookies set to 'Never (wildcard only)' instead of default 'Selective'.
bugs.impact: A sufficient number of ASM Main Cookies and/or a sufficiently large number of cookies for each ASM Main cookie to hash can result in the HTTP header becoming prohibitively large, causing traffic to be refused by the server.
bugs.workaround: Disable Learning mode for the Policy disables Cookie hashing. Note: This affects all learning, not just Cookie hashing.
bugs.fix: Cookie hashing can now be disabled at the policy level in the Cookie subsection of an ASM Policy's Learning and Blocking Settings by setting Learn New Cookies to "Never (wildcard only)".

bugs.title: Creating a user-defined signature via iControl REST occasionally fails with a 400 response code
bugs.symptoms: Creating user-defined signature via iControl REST occasionally fails with a 400 response code.
bugs.conditions: You create a user-defined signature via iControl REST via this endpoint: POST https://<BIG-IP>/mgmt/tm/asm/signatures
bugs.impact: Signature creation fails with 400 response code: { "code": 400, "message": "remoteSender:10.10.10.10, method:POST ", "originalRequestBody": "{...}", "referer": "10.10.10.10", "restOperationId": 6716673, "kind": ":resterrorresponse" }
bugs.fix: Creating user-defined signatures via REST works correctly.

bugs.title: APMD may crash while processing certain parameters
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions APMD may crash while processing certain parameters.
bugs.conditions: -APM active. -Pre-inspection checks active.
bugs.impact: APMD crash, leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: APMD now processes parameters as expected.

bugs.title: MRF GenericMessage: Implement limit to message queues size
bugs.symptoms: The GenericMessage filter does not have a configurable limit to the number of messages that can be received.
bugs.conditions: If a message is waiting for an asynchronous iRule operation during a GENERICMESSAGE_INGRESS or GENERICMESSAGE_EGRESS iRule event, new messages are placed in either the ingress or egress queue. As the number of messages increase, more memory is required.
bugs.impact: If too many messages are queued, the system may exceed an internal count which could lead to a core.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: The existing max_pending_messages attribute of the message router profile is used to limit the size of the queues.

bugs.title: Guestagentd or devmgmtd core
bugs.symptoms: Guestagentd or devmgmtd crashes on a vCMP guest.
bugs.conditions: This can occur during normal operation in a vCMP environment.
bugs.impact: Guestagentd crashes on the vCMP guest, and the vCMP host does not have accurate guest information, such as version, provisioning, high availability (HA) status, and tmm status. Or if it is Devmgmtd that crashed on vCMP guest, the device management daemon will not establishes and maintains device trust group functionality.

bugs.title: APM vs_score for GTM-APM load balancing is not calculated correctly
bugs.symptoms: Output from the 'show ltm virtual <vs> detail' command reports an incorrect value for the APM Module-Score.
bugs.conditions: -- Using GTM/DNS and APM. -- Configure an access profile attached to a virtual server. -- Configure a non-zero number for 'Max Concurrent Users' for the access profile. -- Access the virtual server.
bugs.impact: GTM/DNS load balancing does not work as expected.
bugs.fix: APM virtual server score value is now calculated correctly, so GTM load balancing functions as expected.

bugs.title: TRUNK name in F5 ethernet trailer limited to 15 characters in tcpdump capture
bugs.symptoms: The TRUNK name in an F5 ethernet trailer is limited to 15 characters in tcpdump captures.
bugs.conditions: -- Trunk name is longer than 15 characters. -- Send traffic from client to server. -- Capture traffic on the BIG-IP system using tcpdump.
bugs.impact: TRUNK name in the F5 ethernet trailer is truncated to 15 characters in the tcpdump capture. The tcpdump utility adds internal tmm information to tcpdump captures. This is used for diagnostic purposes and is not used for communication between client and server. That said, if you have multiple trunks where the first 15 characters are the same, there is no way to distinguish between the traffic information for the various trunks in the tcpdump output. Note: The tmm process correctly handles the longer names in other circumstances (e.g., adding/removing trunks, or looking up a trunk by name).
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround for the issue of the trunk name being truncated, if you have multiple trunks in which the first 15 characters are the same, you should rename them so they are distinguishable in the case where you might need to collect tcpdump data. You can read more about the information tcpdump gathers here: K13637: Capturing internal TMM information with tcpdump :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13637.

bugs.title: TMM crash SIGSEGV - spmdb_subscriber_info_deserialize() in spm/spmdb_deser.c
bugs.symptoms: The spmdb_subscriber_info_deserialize does not handle the ERR_MEM properly and crashes the TMM.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP with PEM license, - PEM subscribers at large scale, memory issue might occur in TTM.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and service is disrupted.
bugs.fix: The ERR_MEM from TMM is handled correctly to avoid crash.

bugs.title: The csyncd process may keep trying to sync the GeoIP database to a secondary blade
bugs.symptoms: The most common symptom is when csyncd repeatedly syncs the GeoIP files and loads the GeoIP database, causing a large number of Clock advanced messages on all tmms. Repeated log messages similar to the following are reported when a secondary slot logs into the primary slot to load the sys geoip database: -- info sshd(pam_audit)[17373]: 01070417:6: AUDIT - user root - RAW: sshd(pam_audit): user=root(root) partition=[All] level=Administrator tty=ssh host=x.x.x.x attempts=1 start="Wed Apr 29 13:50:49 2020". -- notice tmsh[17401]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=17401 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=load sys geoip.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION or vCMP guests. -- Either of the following: - First installing the GeoIP database if the /shared/GeoIP/v2 directory does not exist. - When a new blade is installed into a chassis.
bugs.impact: Repeated logs of Clock advanced messages.
bugs.workaround: Run the command: clsh bigstart restart csyncd

bugs.title: Configuration overwritten when using Cloud Auto Scaling template and ASM Automatic Live Update enabled
bugs.symptoms: When a Cloud Auto Scaling deployment is set up using F5's Auto Scale Template, and ASM Live Update is configured with Automatic Download enabled, the configuration may be overwritten during a scale out event when a new host joins the sync cluster. This is caused by a config sync from the new device to the primary device, before the primary has a chance to sync the configuration to the new device, causing the configuration in the primary device to be overwritten.
bugs.conditions: -- Using F5's Auto Scaling template. -- Auto Scale script is configured with --block-sync (which is the default). -- ASM Live Update is configured with Automatic Download enabled. -- A scale out event occurs.
bugs.impact: Configuration of all devices in the Auto Scale group is overwritten.
bugs.workaround: Disable ASM Live Update Automatic Download. This can be done by disabling the liveupdate.autodownload DB variable using the onboard.js script, and adding '-d liveupdate.autodownload:disable'. For example: /usr/bin/f5-rest-node /config/cloud/aws/node_modules/@f5devcentral/f5-cloud-libs/scripts/onboard.js --log-level silly --signal ONBOARD_DONE -o /var/log/cloud/aws/onboard.log --host localhost --port 8443 -d tm.tcpudptxchecksum:software-only -d liveupdate.autodownload:disable --ping -d tm.tcpudptxchecksum:software-only -d liveupdate.autodownload:disable

bugs.title: Changes to SSL.CertRequest.* DB variables cause high availability (HA) devices go out of sync
bugs.symptoms: The GUI saves SSL certificate/CSR subject fields data into SSL.CertRequest.* DB variables to use them in pre-populating subject fields for subsequent modifications.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL certificate/CSR modification through GUI. -- Changing the content of the SSL.CertRequest.* DB variables. -- High availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.impact: HA devices go out of sync.
bugs.workaround: SSL.CertRequest.* DB variables are used only as GUI SSL certificate/CSR pre-populated suggestions. You can still review and modify them before completing SSL certificate/CSR modification operation, so it is safe to sync them onto the high availability (HA) peer.

bugs.title: Mellanox NIC speeds may be reported incorrectly on Virtual Edition
bugs.symptoms: Speeds for Mellanox NICs on BIG-IP Virtual Edition may be reported incorrectly. The behavior varies depending on what driver is in use: - Speeds are always reported as 10G when the mlxvf5 driver is used, regardless of the actual speed of the interface. - Speeds are reported as either 10G or 40G when the xnet driver is used. This is accurate unless the actual NIC speed is greater than 40G, in which is it will still be reported as 40G.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition -- Using a Mellanox NIC with the mlxvf5 or xnet driver
bugs.impact: Possibly incorrect media speed reported. (Actual speed is correct, regardless of what is displayed.)

bugs.title: Cannot clone Azure marketplace instances.
bugs.symptoms: Cannot clone Azure marketplace instances because cloned instances do not properly retrieve publisher and product code from the metadata service.
bugs.conditions: Applies to any Azure marketplace instance.
bugs.impact: Cannot clone Azure marketplace instances.
bugs.fix: Updated the version of the API used to get data from the metadata service. Cloned instances now properly retrieve the publisher and product code from the metadata service.

bugs.title: FailoverState device status and CM device status do not match shortly after triggering failover
bugs.symptoms: After triggering failover, the result returned by the API endpoint /mgmt/tm/shared/bigip-failover-state (the BIG-IP failover state worker) may not match the actual device failover state.
bugs.conditions: This may happen on an high availability (HA) setup with a sync-failover device group.
bugs.impact: Actions that require the correct output of the BIG-IP failover state worker may fail. For instance, deleting an SSL Orchestrator topology followed by immediately triggering failover may encounter this issue, causing the deletion to fail.
bugs.workaround: After waiting for a short amount of time, the BIG-IP failover state worker gets in sync with the device failover state. So in the example of deleting an SSL Orchestrator topology, the deletion should be successful if you try again after a short wait.

bugs.title: Add new macro dialogue not working for AD auth and resources and password change
bugs.symptoms: In VPE, when Add Macro button is clicked, a dialogue is opened in which when AD auth and resources and password change option are selected from the macro template dropdown and clicked on Save button, an error dialogue displays with 500 error.
bugs.conditions: - Add new Macro button to be in enabled status. - Select AD auth and resources and password change template from macro template dropdown. - Click Save.
bugs.impact: Addition of Macro template is not working when AD auth and resources and password change is selected as a template.
bugs.workaround: After performing the required actions when page is refreshed or coming back from another page, the failed macro template is appeared.
bugs.fix: The AD auth and resources and password change template is now accepted for macro addition.

bugs.title: Remotely authenticated users may experience difficulty logging in over the serial console
bugs.symptoms: -- When a remotely authenticated user attempts login over the serial console, the username and password are accepted, but the session closes immediately thereafter. -- Login over SSH is successful for the same user
bugs.conditions: -- Remote authentication (e.g., RADIUS, TACACS, LDAP) and role mapping configured on the BIG-IP system. -- Attempted login over the serial console for a remotely authenticated user who has been assigned a role.
bugs.impact: Remotely authenticated users cannot log in over the serial console.
bugs.workaround: Using either of the following workaround: -- Log in over SSH instead -- If acceptable (taking into account security considerations), enable terminal access for all remote users regardless of assigned role, using 'tmsh modify auth remote-user remote-console-access tmsh' or within the GUI.
bugs.fix: Remotely-authenticated users are now able to successfully log in to BIG-IP through the serial console.

bugs.title: VMware guest OS customization works only partially in a dual stack environment.
bugs.symptoms: The result of guest OS customization depends on the DHCP state on the management (mgmt) interface and the applied customization profile (i.e., IPv4 only, IPv4 and IPv6, or IPv6 with IPv4 prompt). By default, DHCP is enabled on the management interface. During configuration, you can customize only one IPv4 or one IPv6 address in a dual stack environment.
bugs.conditions: Applying a customization profile to VMware VM in a dual stack environment.
bugs.impact: You can only partially customize the mgmt interface IP profiles for VMware VMs in a dual stack environment.
bugs.workaround: Configure the mgmt interface addresses using the config script.
bugs.fix: VMware customization works only partially in a dual stack environment. To avoid misconfiguration, set the desired mgmt interface addresses using the config script.

bugs.title: Excessive resource consumption in zxfrd
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, zxfrd may consume excessive resources.
bugs.conditions: -- Provision GTM (Global Traffic DNS). -- Create one or more zones in the GUI via DNS::Zones::Zones::Zone List.
bugs.impact: Excessive resources consumption, potentially leading to failover event.
bugs.fix: zxfrd no longer consumes excessive resources.

bugs.title: Security hardening for APM Webtop
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the APM Webtop does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: -APM access policy is configured with webtop enabled.
bugs.impact: APM Webtop does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: The APM Webtop now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: HW offload of vector 22 (IPv6 Duplicate Extension Headers) not operational
bugs.symptoms: All mitigation for IPv6 Duplicate Extension Headers DoS vector happens at the software level. The counter in int_drops column reads 0 (zero) in dos_stat tmctl for that vector.
bugs.conditions: Double IPv6 headers in the packets (except Destination Options header).
bugs.impact: You cannot offload DDoS vector 22 to FPGA hardware. Only the software-based DDoS mitigation is supported.
bugs.workaround: Use software DDoS mitigation for this vector.

bugs.title: The sdmd daemon cores during config sync when multiple devices configured for iRules LX
bugs.symptoms: The iRules LX workspaces belong on only one device in a Device Service Cluster (DSC) (config sync device-group). If you have the same iRules LX workspace configured on multiple devices and then perform a config sync operation, the sdmd daemon cores.
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple devices configured with the same iRules LX workspace in a DSC. -- Change one of the devices such that the configuration requires a config sync. -- Perform the config sync.
bugs.impact: The sdmd daemon cores. Although having multiple devices configured with the same iRules LX workspace is an incorrect configuration, sdmd should not core.
bugs.workaround: When the iRules LX workspace is correctly configured, i.e., on only one device in a DSC, there is no need to config sync, so this issues does not occur.

bugs.title: Logging up/down transition of DNS/GTM pool resource via HSL can trigger TMM failure
bugs.symptoms: A TMM daemon logs a SIGSEGV error, halts, and then be restarted.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system configured to perform DNS/GTM Global Server Load Balancing. -- High Speed Logging (HSL) is configured. -- Multiple HSL destinations are configured. -- The enabled HSL settings include 'replication'. -- At least one HSL destination is up. -- At least one HSL destination is down. -- A pool resource changes state from up to down.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Configure HSL with only a single log destination.

bugs.title: Incorrect interaction between DataSafe credential protection and modern customization Logon Page
bugs.symptoms: -- DataSafe credential protection does not work correctly with the logon page if Access Profile customization type is set to 'modern'. -- Submitted credentials fail to get populated in the authentication form. -- You do not complete the access policy.
bugs.conditions: -- Options 'Substitute Value' and 'Obfuscate' are enabled under DataSafe Profile (Note: Default value is enabled for both attributes if APM logon page template is loaded). -- 'Modern' customization is used.
bugs.impact: Authentication is unsuccessful and the end user is unable to log in.

bugs.title: CSRF token expired message for AJAX calls is displayed incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: CSRF token expired message for AJAX calls is displayed incorrectly in alert message
bugs.conditions: This can occur if a BIG-IP administrator or user navigates to pages containing AJAX calls that modify a policy when the CSRF token is already expired. This occurs very rarely.
bugs.impact: Each letter in message is shown in new line in alert message
bugs.fix: CSRF token expired message for AJAX calls is shown correctly

bugs.title: Incorrect enforcement of policy parameters
bugs.symptoms: A parameter is not enforced correctly (i.e., it shows as a false positive or a false negative).
bugs.conditions: -- The parameter is configured as a global wildcard parameter. -- The parameter also appears as an explicit parameter on a different policy. -- Other conditions related to the name of the parameter may apply (e.g., numerical suffix).
bugs.impact: Enforcement returns false-positive or false-negative results.
bugs.workaround: Change the parameters to either explicit parameters or URL-level parameters assigned to all the URLs.

bugs.title: imish crash while checking for CLI help string in BGP mode
bugs.symptoms: imish crashes while checking the help strings of '(no) neighbor x.x.x.x fall-over bfd ?' when Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure BGP. -- Check for help strings in imish using the '?' (question mark) character in the specific command "neighbour x.x.x.x fall-over bfd ?".
bugs.impact: imish crash. Although imish crashes, BGP functionality is not impacted.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using '?' while entering the command "neighbour x.x.x.x fall-over bfd ?".

bugs.title: FastL4 UDP flows might not get offloaded to hardware
bugs.symptoms: In some cases one side - client or server - of a fastL4 UDP flow might not get offloaded to hardware.
bugs.conditions: FastL4 UDP virtual server
bugs.impact: One side of the UDP flow is not accelerated by hardware.
bugs.fix: Both sides of the fastL4 UDP flow are now offloaded correctly.

bugs.title: MTU assignment to non-existent interface
bugs.symptoms: Warning log message generated to /var/log/ltm warning mcpd[5494]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : cannot set MTU for eth1. No such device. For legacy VE driver.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when enabling or disabling VLAN-based Syn Cookies.
bugs.impact: No known functional impact. This is an incorrectly generated warning message.

bugs.title: Modification of SmartNIC MTU not supported
bugs.symptoms: During initialization, the SmartNIC driver reports a fixed MTU size. This prevents the MTU from being modified and results in the following error message in /var/log/tmm: bigip1 notice xnet[00:08.0]: Error: Command 14 failed: 5
bugs.conditions: This error message is generated each time TMM is started or restarted.
bugs.impact: Jumbo frames are not supported by SmartNIC.

bugs.title: TSIG key value logged in plaintext in log
bugs.symptoms: TSIG key is logged in /var/log/audit in clear text.
bugs.conditions: - TSIG key in the config. - Key created via tmsh ltm dns tsig-key command
bugs.impact: TSIG key is logged in audit log file in clear text.

bugs.title: Unexpected reboot when system handles large numbers of EDAC/MCE logs
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP unit is experiencing a hardware issue that results in a large number of EDAC/MCE logs (typically over a substantial number of hours or days), the unit might experience a kernel panic in the EDAC kernel code leading to a system reboot. bugs.conditions: -- The unit is producing large numbers of EDAC (error detection and correction) or MCE (machine check exception) logs, such as from a faulty DIMM. -- BIG-IP systems running CentOS 7.2 and 7.3 Linux kernels used in TMOS versions 13.1.0 through 13.1.3.2 and 14.1.0 through 14.1.2.1. (CentOS 7.5 was introduced in software versions 13.1.3.3 and 14.1.2.2 and does not contain this issue.) Note: This issue appears to be very rare. Occasional transient memory errors such as SEU (single event upsets) are not likely to trigger the kernel panic.
bugs.impact: Unit reboots. Traffic interrupted while system restarts. In high availability (HA) configurations, the system fails over.

bugs.title: Reject flood packets to prevent L2 learning problems when TCN is generated
bugs.symptoms: Mac move messages can be observed on the connected switches
bugs.conditions: Virtual wire configured in high availability (HA) mode.
bugs.impact: 1) Mac move messages can be observed on the connected switches. 2) Traffic will be impacted on failover
bugs.fix: BIG-IP will stop accepting new TCP connections if it detects a topology change during a configurable timeout (l2.virtualwire.tcn.recovery.connection.drop.timeout, default 30). This feature is not enabled by default. To enable l2.virtualwire.tcn.connection.drop this variable needs to be set.

bugs.title: MCPD crashes receiving a message from bcm56xxd
bugs.symptoms: Under rare circumstances, the Broadcom switch daemon bcm56xxd, can send more then one message at a time to MCPD. This can cause MCPD to either fail immediately or have it hang and be terminated by sod 5 minutes later. One of the messages being sent is in response to a link status change. The second message is a reply to a query, for instance a query for l2 forward statistics.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP with a Broadcom switch. - Link status change is available. - MCPD sends a query to bcm56xxd, that is, for l2 forward statistics.
bugs.impact: MCPD failure and restarts causing a failover.
bugs.fix: The Broadcom switch daemon bcm56xxd will not send more then one message to MCPD at a time.

bugs.title: iRulesLX hardening

bugs.conditions: - Authenticated administrative user
bugs.impact: iRulesLX does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: iRulesLX now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: Node, Pool Member, and Monitor Instance timestamps may be updated by config sync/load
bugs.symptoms: The text that describes the monitor state of an LTM node, pool member, or monitor instance also contains a timestamp that initially indicates when the monitor set the affected node or pool member to the indicated state. This timestamp can be affected by other actions, such as incremental or full config sync and config load. The monitor-state description and timestamp can be viewed in the CLI (CLI/TMSH) and GUI (TMUI) as follows: -- From the CLI/TMSH: tmsh show ltm monitor <monitor_type> <monitor_name> This command shows the state of ltm nodes or pool members currently monitored by the specified ltm health monitor, as in the following example: ------------------------------------- LTM::Monitor /Common/mysql_test ------------------------------------- Destination: 10.10.200.28:3296 State time: down for 1hr:58mins:42sec | Last error: No successful responses received before deadline. @2020.03.25 14:10:24 -- From the GUI: + Navigate to Local Traffic :: Nodes : Node List :: <node_name>. The 'Availability' field shows text describing the node's monitored state with a timestamp. + Navigate to Local Traffic :: Pools : Pool List :: <pool_name>, under the Members tab, click the pool member name. The 'Availability' field shows text describing the pool member's monitored state with a timestamp.
bugs.conditions: This may occur under the following conditions: -- If an incremental config sync occurs from one high availability (HA) member to another member or to the device group: + The timestamp on monitor instances for all Nodes or Pool Members (as shown by 'tmsh show ltm monitor <type> <name>') may be updated on HA members receiving the incremental config sync. + If a Node or Pool Member has been marked DOWN by a monitor, its timestamp may be updated in the GUI (Node List/Pool-Member list) on HA members receiving the incremental config sync. -- If a full/forced config sync occurs from one HA member to another member or to the device group: + The timestamp on monitor instances for all Nodes or Pool Members (as shown by 'tmsh show ltm monitor <type> <name>') may be updated on HA members receiving the incremental config sync. + The timestamp for all Nodes or Pool Members may be updated in the GUI (Node List/Pool-Member list) on HA members receiving the incremental config sync. -- If a config load occurs: + The timestamp on monitor instances for all Nodes or Pool Members (as shown by 'tmsh show ltm monitor <type> <name>') may be updated on the HA member where the config load occurred. + The timestamp for all Nodes or Pool Members may be updated in the GUI (Node List/Pool-Member list) on the HA member where the config load occurred.
bugs.impact: The timestamp indicated next to the monitored-state description for an LTM Node or Pool Member indicates when the Node or Pool Member was updated in ways other than by its configured monitor. Thus, this timestamp may not indicate the actual time of the monitor event suggested by the description text.

bugs.title: Display of LCD System Menu cannot be configured via GUI on iSeries platforms
bugs.symptoms: In the BIG-IP Graphical User Interface (TMUI), display of the System Menu on the LCD front panel of most BIG-IP platforms can be enabled or disabled under System :: Configuration :: Device :: General. However, on iSeries appliances, the 'Display LCD System Menu' option does not appear on this page.
bugs.impact: The 'Display LCD System Menu' option cannot be configured via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: You can enable display of the LCD System Menu using the Command Line (CLI) by running the following commands, in sequence: tmsh mod sys global-settings lcd-display [enabled|disabled] tmsh mod sys db lcd.showmenu value [enabled|disabled]

bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes IPSec traffic as expected.

bugs.title: CentOS Security Update for libssh2
bugs.symptoms: The vulnerability found in the libssh2 library. The libssh2 provides the library to implement the SSH2 protocol. This could have been exploited to gain the partial access to sensitive information. This can also trigger the limited Denial of service in the form of the interruptions to resource availability.
bugs.conditions: There are 2 conditions that cause this vulnerability to occur 1. Out-of-bounds reads with specially crafted SSH packets. when a specially crafted SFTP packet is received from the server. A remote attacker who compromises a SSH server may be able to cause a denial of service or read data in the client memory. 2. When SSH packets with a padding length value greater than the packet length are parsed. A remote attacker who compromises a SSH server may be able to cause a denial of service or read data in the client memory.
bugs.impact: Access to the sensitive information partially followed by limited Denial of Service.
bugs.fix: Updating the version of the libssh2 from 1.4.3 to 1.8.0.

bugs.title: MRF DIAMETER: New iRule command to skip capabilities exchange
bugs.symptoms: A new iRule command is available, DIAMETER::skip_capabilities_exchange, to skip the capabilities exchange messages.
bugs.conditions: To skip the capabilities exchange messages -- Within an internal virtual server for protocol translation. -- Analyzing a tab connection for logging/analysis. -- Internally generated DIAMETER messages (e.g., for logging, authentication, etc.).

bugs.title: BIG-IP system does not respond to ARP requests if it has a route to the source IP address
bugs.symptoms: If the BIG-IP system receives an ARP request from a source IP address for which it has a route configured, the BIG-IP system does not give an ARP reply.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system receives an ARP who-is request for one of its self ip addresses. -- The source IP address is in a different network, and the BIG-IP system has an L3 route configured for it.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP does not send an ARP reply.
bugs.fix: A db variable has been added called 'arp.verifyreturnroute' that can disable the TMM process's checking for a valid return route for ARP requests. It defaults to 'enable', which is the normal BIG-IP behavior. It can be set to 'disable' to disable the dropping of the request if a return route exists.
bugs.behavior: A db variable has been added called 'arp.verifyreturnroute' that can disable the TMM process's checking for a valid return route for ARP requests. It defaults to 'enable', which is the normal BIG-IP behavior. It can be set to 'disable' to disable the dropping of the request if a return route exists.

bugs.title: vCMP guest CPU usage may increase 4-5% after upgrade of vCMP host to v16.1.x &start;
bugs.symptoms: All vCMP guest configurations might see a 4-5% increase in CPU usage while running on VIPRION and iSeries platforms with the vCMP host upgraded to v16.1.x
bugs.conditions: -- All configurations (guest software version is not relevant) -- Running vCMP on VIPRION and iSeries platforms -- 'Host' upgraded to v16.1.x
bugs.impact: Increase of CPU usage of about 4-5% on the vCMP guest. This is not expected to cause noticeable performance impacts unless the vCMP guest CPU is already close to 100% use, when it is possible there may be up to a 15% TPS decrease. If you are running vCMP on VIPRION and iSeries platforms, first evaluate your scenarios and capacity plan if you plan to upgrade the 'host' to 16.1.x. Note: There is no CPU usage increase when v16.1.x 'guest' instances are run on an earlier 'host' version. Guidance: In determining whether to upgrade the vCMP host to v16.1.x, carefully evaluate the performance and sizing requirements of your specific configuration.

bugs.title: Limit on log framework configuration size
bugs.symptoms: While the system config is loading, numerous error messages can be seen: -- err errdefsd[26475]: 01940010:3: errdefs: failed to add splunk destination. -- err errdefsd[585]: 01940015:3: errdefs: failure publishing errdefs configuration.
bugs.conditions: This can occur during a log-config update/load that has numerous log-config objects configured.
bugs.impact: The system does not log as expected.
bugs.workaround: None. An Engineering Hotfix is available and can be requested through F5 Support.

bugs.title: Management and VLAN MAC addresses are identical
bugs.symptoms: The 'tmsh show sys mac-address' command indicates the management interface is using the same MAC address as a VLAN.
bugs.conditions: This can occur on chassis based systems and on VCMP guests. The MAC address pool does not reserve specific MAC addresses for the management interfaces and so pool entries may be reused for VLANs.
bugs.impact: The management MAC address is the same as the VLAN MAC address, resulting in issues relating to the inability to differentiate traffic to the management port or to traffic ports.
bugs.fix: The issue has been fixed for hardware platforms. That is, MAC addresses in the MAC address pool have been reserved for the management port. Due to the small MAC pool size for a few platforms (see K14513: MAC address assignment for interfaces, trunks, and VLANs :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14513#vlans), entries cannot be reserved for VCMP guest management interfaces.

bugs.title: Logrotation for /var/log/avr blocked by files with .1 suffix
bugs.symptoms: AVR logrotate reports errors in /var/log/avr: error: error creating output file /var/log/avr/avrd.log.1: File exists /var/log/avr/avrd.log will remain unchanged /var/log/avr/avrd.log.1 will remain unchanged
bugs.conditions: Files ending with .1 exist in the log directory.
bugs.impact: Logrotate does not work. This might fill the disk with logs over time.
bugs.workaround: Remove or rename all of the .1 log files.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with logrotate failing when files ending with .1 exist in the log directory.

bugs.title: Empty fields are shown in the policy version history
bugs.symptoms: Empty fields are displayed instead of N/A in the policy version history.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create and apply a new policy. 2. Open General Settings screen. 3. Open Policy Version History.
bugs.impact: Empty fields are shown (Source Policy Name and Source Host Name are empty), potentially implying an error condition, when in fact the field values are not applicable in this case.
bugs.fix: N/A text is shown in Source Policy Name and Source Host Name fields when required.

bugs.title: Trunks with names longer than 32 characters update working-mbr-count in vCMP guests incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: When a trunk is configured with a name longer than 32 characters on a vCMP host, guests update the working-mbr-count for the trunk incorrectly when another trunk on the host changes. This might result in vCMP guests failing over unexpectedly.
bugs.conditions: -- Trunk configured with a name longer than 32 characters on vCMP host. -- Trunk made available to guests for high availability (HA) Group scoring. -- At least one other trunk configured on vCMP host. -- Interface state changes in any other trunk.
bugs.impact: The vCMP guests may fail over unexpectedly.
bugs.workaround: Do not use trunk names longer than 32 characters.

bugs.title: Unable to set LACP system priority manually
bugs.symptoms: LACP system priority is calculated internally using the system MAC. This occasionally results in priority being calculated as 0, which is not accepted by third party devices, such as Cisco.
bugs.conditions: -- LACP is enabled on BIG-IP system. -- The last two octets of system MAC are zero.
bugs.impact: LACP system priority is calculated as 0 which is rejected by Cisco. Note: BIG-IP administrators have no manual control over setting the LACP system priority value.
bugs.behavior: New schema changes added for setting LACP system priority manually.

bugs.title: Request-adapt plus request-logging causes HTTP double-chunking in an ICAP request
bugs.symptoms: When an HTTP chunked request is sent to a virtual server that has both a request-adapt (e.g., for ICAP), and a request-logging profile attached, the request that is sent to the ICAP server is doubly chunked.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server is configured with both a request-adapt (ICAP) and request-logging profile. -- HTTP chunked requests are sent to this virtual server.
bugs.impact: Data corruption in the HTTP stream.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Force rechunking on the HTTP profile: request-chunking rechunk -- Remove the request-logging profile (and potentially log requests) using an iRule instead.

bugs.title: LDAP authenticating failures seen because of 'Too many open file handles at client (nslcd)'
bugs.symptoms: LDAP authentication fails with an error message: err nslcd[2867]: accept() failed: Too many open files
bugs.conditions: This problem occurs when user-template is used instead of Bind DN.
bugs.impact: You cannot logon to the system using LDAP authentication.
bugs.fix: LDAP authentication now succeeds when user-template is used.
