bugs.title: System restarts repeatedly after using the 'diskinit' utility with the '--style=volumes' option
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system boots, mcpd continually restarts.
bugs.conditions: This may occur after you issue the 'diskinit' command with the '--style=volumes' option in the MOS (Maintenance Operating System) shell, install BIG-IP into the new volume, then boot into the new installation of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system is unable to complete the boot process and become active.
bugs.workaround: In the MOS shell, do not issue the 'diskinit' command with the '--style=volumes' option. Instead, on BIG-IP v14.1.2.1 and later, you may use the 'image2disk' utility with the '-format' option to recreate the desired volume. You also can achieve the same result by following the shell guidance. To begin, type 'start<enter>'. If the system is already in the defective state, use this shell command, and then reboot: touch /.tmos.platform.init The problem should be resolved.
bugs.fix: Running 'diskinit' from MOS with the '--style=volumes' option no longer causes continuous mcpd restarts.

bugs.title: Incorrect MRHTTP proxy handling of passthrough mode in certain scenarios may lead to TMM core
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual has HTTP and httprouter profiles attached to it. - Certain scenarios where the proxy goes into passthrough mode. This was encountered during internal testing of a certain iRule configurations.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now correctly manages proxy handling of passthrough mode in specific scenarios, so the tmm crash no longer occurs.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing DNS traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash with a SIGABRT while processing DNS traffic.
bugs.conditions: Undisclosed series of DNS requests.
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes DNS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Password memory not effective even when password policy is configured
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not prevent you from specifying previously used passwords, even if Secure Password Enforcement is enabled with password memory set to a non-zero value.
bugs.conditions: -- Password memory in auth settings is not 0 (zero). -- Attempt to specify a previously specified password
bugs.impact: Password history to prevent user from using same password is not enforced.

bugs.title: SELinux policies may prevent from iqsh/iqsyncer dumping core
bugs.symptoms: SELinux policies may prevent the iqsh/iqsyncer utilities from dumping core information.
bugs.conditions: -- SELinux policies enabled. -- Run the iqsh/iqsyncer utilities to initiate a core dump.
bugs.impact: The operation does not result in dumping the core information.
bugs.workaround: Disable SELinux with 'setenforce 0'.

bugs.title: The iqsyncer utility may not write the core file for system signals
bugs.symptoms: In certain instances, the iqsyncer utility may not write the core file for system signals.
bugs.conditions: -- SELinux policies enabled. -- Run the iqsyncer utilities to initiate a core dump with system signals SIGABRT, SIGQUIT, and SIGSEGV.
bugs.impact: The iqsyncer utility does not write core file.
bugs.workaround: Disable SELinux with 'setenforce 0'. You can now generate a core with a SIGQUIT (-3), but not with SIGABRT or SIGSEGV.

bugs.title: Incorrect MRHTTP proxy handling of passthrough mode in certain scenarios may lead to tmm core
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server has HTTP and HTTP Router profiles attached. -- Certain scenarios where the proxy goes into passthrough mode. This was encountered during internal testing of a certain iRule configurations.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: A core file is generated upon avrd process restart or stop
bugs.symptoms: Sometime when avrd process is stopped or restarted, a core is generated.
bugs.conditions: Avrd process is stopped or restarted.
bugs.impact: Avrd creates a core file but there is no other negative impact to the system.

bugs.title: The mcpd process may become unresponsive
bugs.symptoms: -- The mcpd process is killed with SIGABRT by the sod watchdog due to failed heartbeat check. -- There is high memory usage by the mcpd process prior to getting killed. -- There is an mcpd core file contains a very long string. The core might contain a repeating pattern of '{ } { } { } ...'.
bugs.conditions: The mcpd process receives a malformed message from one of the control plane daemons.
bugs.impact: -- There is a temporary lack of responsiveness related to actions of inspecting and/or modifying system configuration: GUI, TMSH, etc., operations may fail or time out. -- SNMP queries might go unanswered. -- System daemons restart. -- Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed handling of malformed messages by mcpd, so the problem should no longer occur.

bugs.title: Deleting LTM data-group external object incorrectly reports 200 when object fails to delete
bugs.symptoms: When you delete an LTM external data-group object using iControl REST, it incorrectly returns '200 OK' even though the object is not deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- Deleting an external data-group object via iControl REST. -- The LTM external data-group object is referenced by another object (such as an iRule).
bugs.impact: The object still exists, even though the system returns a '200 OK' message indicating that the operation completed successfully.

bugs.title: Creating LTM data group external object fails.
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST command to create a data group fails if you do not set the externalFileName variable. The same command works in tmsh, and you are not required to specify the externalFileName.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a data group using iControl REST. -- POST payload does not contain the externalFileName variable.
bugs.impact: You are unable to create the data group.
bugs.workaround: The command works if you specify the externalFileName parameter: curl -sku $PASS https://$HOST/mgmt/tm/ltm/data-group/external -X POST -H "Content-type: application/json" -d '{"name":"fooBar", "externalFileName":"fooBar.txt"}'

bugs.title: TMM crashes when VLAN SYN cookie feature is used on iSeries i2x00 and i4x00 platforms
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when VLAN SYN cookie feature is used.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuring for VLAN SYN cookie use. -- Running on iSeries i2800/i2600 and i4800/i4600 platforms.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes and traffic processing stops. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: VLAN SYN cookie processing now functions as expected.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 full proxy always sets the :scheme pseudo-header for HTTPS requests where the server-side connection is not encrypted
bugs.symptoms: When using HTTP/2, the :scheme pseudo-header appears to always be set to HTTPS on requests, even when the server-side connection is not encrypted.
bugs.conditions: -- Using an HTTP/2 virtual server. -- The server-side connection that is unencrypted.
bugs.impact: The impact of this issue varies based on how the application reacts at the server-side.

bugs.title: HTTP CONNECT method with a delayed payload can cause a connection to be closed
bugs.symptoms: If the HTTP CONNECT method is utilized and payload arrives in a later TCP segment, the HTTP connection will be closed.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP profile. -- HTTP CONNECTION with delayed payload.
bugs.impact: The HTTP connection is incorrectly closed.
bugs.fix: Traffic containing the HTTP CONNECT method and a delayed payload no longer has its connection closed.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when AFM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources when processing forwarding flows while AFM is provisioned.
bugs.conditions: - AFM provisioned - Virtual is CMP-disabled
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now consumes resources as expected when AFM is provisioned

bugs.title: Virtual server status displays as unavailable when it is accepting connections
bugs.symptoms: After a rate limit is triggered and released, the virtual server status in the GUI remains as 'unavailable'. The virtual server resumes accepting new connections while the GUI shows the virtual server is unavailable.
bugs.conditions: -- The virtual server has a source address list configured. -- Address lists define more than one address. -- The connections are over the rate limit, and the virtual server status is marked unavailable. -- The number of connections falls below the limit.
bugs.impact: Actual virtual server status is not reflected in GUI.
bugs.workaround: If the deployment design allows, you can use either of the following workarounds: -- Remove the source address list from the virtual server. -- Have a single address in the source address list.

bugs.title: Security hardening for the TMUI Interface page
bugs.symptoms: The TMUI Interface page does not comply with current best practices.
bugs.conditions: TMUI Interface page accessed by authenticated administrative user.
bugs.impact: The TMUI Interface page does not comply with current best practices.
bugs.fix: The TMUI Interface page now complies with current best practices.

bugs.title: Changing per-request policy while tmm is under traffic load may drop heartbeats
bugs.symptoms: Cluster failover, tmm restart, and tmm killed due to missed heartbeats. tmm crash
bugs.conditions: TMM is under load due to heavy traffic while MCP attempts to configure per-request policy. This can be caused by a modification to the policy or one of its agents, or by a restart of the TMM.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: When making changes to per-request policies, use a scheduled maintenance window so that impact to traffic is minimized.

bugs.title: Partial HTTP/2 payload may freeze on the BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 allows sending the payload in both directions gradually, until a frame with an END_STREAM flag closes a direction. The BIG-IP does not properly handles an early response from a server when HTTP router is configured on a virtual and partial payload sent in each direction. In this case, communication over the stream hangs.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server is configured on the BIG-IP system with HTTP and HTTP/2 profiles on both the client and server sides. -- HTTP router profile is configured on the virtual server. -- Client sends a request and delivers a partial payload, waiting for a response from a server. -- Server responds with a partial payload.
bugs.impact: A response with a partial payload is not delivered to a client. Communication freezes on that specific stream.

bugs.title: Poor HTTP/3 throughput
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/3 throughput is poor.
bugs.conditions: Virtual Server configured with an HTTP/3 profile.
bugs.impact: Performance might be severely degraded.
bugs.workaround: There is no alternative other than not using the HTTP/3 profile.
bugs.fix: Erroneously enabled debug logs are now turned off, so performance is improved.

bugs.title: OSPF - SPF/IA calculation scheduling might get stuck infinitely
bugs.symptoms: After SPF/IA calculation gets suspended, it might enter a state where it never fires again.
bugs.conditions: SPF/IA calculation gets suspended; This occurs for various reasons; BIG-IP end users have no influence on it occurring.
bugs.impact: OSPF routes are visible in the OSPF database, but not installed in the routing table.
bugs.workaround: Restart the routing daemons: # bigstart restart tmrouted Running this command allows you to recover from this situation, but does not prevent the event from reoccurring. If due to a topology, SPF/IA calculation suspension occurs again after a restart, this workaround essentially has no effect.

bugs.title: LB::down iRule command is ineffective, and can lead to inconsistent pool member status
bugs.symptoms: Use of the LB::down command in an iRule may not have the desired effect, or may result in pool members that are down for load balancing, but indicate up/available in the GUI and CLI. Specifically, the pool member is marked down within the tmm instance executing the iRule, but the status change is not updated to mcpd, or to other tmm instances. As a result, the message 'Pool /Common/mypool member /Common/1.1.1.1:80 monitor status iRule down' does not appear in the log, and the status of the pool member is not updated when viewed in the GUI or via 'tmsh show ltm pool xxxx members'. Note: If [event info] is logged in the LB_FAILED event, it will indicate that the load balancing decision failed due to "connection limit"
bugs.conditions: Using the LB::down command in an iRule.
bugs.impact: Because mcpd believes the pool member to be up, it does not update tmm's status, so tmm continues to regard it as down indefinitely, or until a monitor state change occurs. If the LB::down command is used on all members of a pool, the affected tmms cannot load balance to that pool, even though the GUI/tmsh indicate that the pool has available members. Because pool member status is stored on per-tmm basis and incoming connections are distributed across tmms using a hash, this can lead to apparently inconsistent results, where some traffic (traffic hitting a particular tmm) is rejected with an RST cause of 'No pool member available'.
bugs.workaround: - Delete and recreate affected pool members (or) Restart tmm (or) Restart the BIG-IP. There is no direct workaround, but the use of an inband monitor instead of the LB::down command may be effective. You must tune the inband monitor's settings to values consistent with the desired behavior.

bugs.title: BD error on HTTP response after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade, some requests can cause BD errors on response: BEM|ERR |May 19 17:49:55.800|0983|response_header_accumulator.c:0200|Error: CookieMgrBuildCookie failed. ans 1 job 2957561040 IO_PLUGIN|ERR |May 19 17:49:55.800|0983|io_plugin.c:3320|TMEVT_RESPONSE: Cannot build a ts cookie.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading BIG-IP systems to v15.0.0 or later from versions earlier than v15.0.0. -- ASM policy is configured on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: For some requests, the response can arrive truncated or not arrive at all.
bugs.workaround: Add an iRule that deletes ASM cookies: when HTTP_REQUEST { set cookies [HTTP::cookie names] foreach aCookie $cookies { if {$aCookie matches_regex {^TS(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{6,8})(?:$|_[0-9]+$)}} { HTTP::cookie remove $aCookie } } } Note: Performing this workaround affects cookie-related violations (they may need to be disabled to use this workaround), session, and login protection.

bugs.title: SSL Certificate version always displays as '1' in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: In GUI an SSL certificate's version is displayed as '1', even if its version is higher than 1.
bugs.conditions: -- Viewing an SSL certificate in the GUI. -- The SSL certificate's version is higher than 1.
bugs.impact: SSL certificate's version is displayed as '1'. There is no functional impact.

bugs.title: DDoS Vector - TCP BAD ACK is not hardware-accelerated
bugs.symptoms: There is no FPGA support for vector number 105 (FPGA vector number). This is an L4 DDoS vector that rate limits the number of incorrect TCP ACK Cookies. The vector is commonly referred to as ACK_Cookie_Bad.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when a TCP BADACK DDoS vector is detected.
bugs.impact: This vector is not hardware accelerated. The DDoS mitigation can rely only on software support for this DDoS vector.

bugs.title: TMM core may be seen when reattaching a vector to a DoS profile
bugs.symptoms: TMM core resulting in potential loss of service.
bugs.conditions: Attaching and deleting the vector to a DoS profile multiple times while the traffic is ongoing.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system now validates the tracker when deleting to ensure delete of the same tracker that was created, so there is no error.

bugs.title: Tmm crash when applying config changes
bugs.symptoms: Core observed after modifying the config to change the cipher lists.
bugs.conditions: Changing the LTM configuration at runtime. The exact conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes, and the BIG-IP system generates a core file. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic
bugs.conditions: - Client HTTP profile - Server SSL profile - Server HTTP/2 profile - Undisclosed request conditions
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP traffic as expected

bugs.title: Support QUIC and HTTP draft-28
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system supports QUIC and HTTP/3 draft-25 and draft-27. IETF has released draft-28.
bugs.conditions: Browser requests draft-28.
bugs.impact: Connection downgrades to an older version, or fails if the browser cannot downgrade.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports draft-28 and draft-27, and has removed draft-25 support.

bugs.title: Continuous 'neurond restart' message on console
bugs.symptoms: Neurond continuously restarts after some configuration changes.
bugs.conditions: -- iSeries platform -- Changes are made to the underlying firmware and an automatic reboot is not triggered.
bugs.impact: -- Features that utilize Neuron are not available. -- Continuous 'neurond restart' messages are logged to the console
bugs.workaround: For some TurboFlex changes, a reboot is required. Note: If neurond is restarting after turboflex profile-config changed to turboflex-security then the following will workaround the issue: tmsh stop sys service neurond tmsh modify sys provision afm level nominal tmsh service start neurond reboot
bugs.fix: Neurond no longer continuously restarts after certain configuration changes.

bugs.title: Upgrade error 'Parsing default XML files. Failed to parse xml file'
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading BIG-IP, multiple error messages appear in /var/log/ltm: -- err mcpd[5352]: 010713cf:3: Parsing default XML files. Failed to parse xml file (/var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/secure_access_client/default_secure_access_client.xml) because Failed to stat file (/var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/secure_access_client/default_secure_access_client.xml) errno(2) strerror(No such file or directory) -- err mcpd[5352]: 010713cf:3: Parsing default XML files. Failed to parse xml file (/var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/resource_app_tunnel/default_resource_app_tunnel.xml) because Failed to stat file (/var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/modern/resource_app_tunnel/default_resource_app_tunnel.xml) errno(2) strerror(No such file or directory)
bugs.conditions: -- APM configuration following in /config/bigip.conf. apm policy customization-source /Common/modern { } apm policy customization-source /Common/standard { } -- Upgrade the BIG-IP system to v15.1.0 or newer.
bugs.impact: These are benign messages that do not indicate a functional issue. There is no impact; the system works correctly. The errors occur when the upgraded BIG-IP APM configuration attempts to load resource definitions for the modern customization schema. However, by design, the modern customization schema does not define resources. Only the standard customization schema defines resources found under '/var/sam/www/client/customization-source/Common/standard/'.

bugs.title: iRule parking in clientside/serverside command may cause tmm restart
bugs.symptoms: If an iRule utilizing the clientside or serverside command causes parking to occur while in the clientside/serverside command (table or after commands, for example), the connection is aborted while parked, and a subsequent iRule event attempts to run (CLIENT_CLOSED, for example), tmm may restart.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule using clientside or serverside command. -- Use of commands that may park while in the clientside/serverside command. -- Flow is aborted while iRule is parked. -- iRule also has CLIENT_CLOSED or SERVER_CLOSED event handler. For more information on the conditions that trigger iRule parking, see K12962: Some iRules commands temporarily suspend iRules processing, available at https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K12962.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Rework iRules to avoid use of clientside/serverside command. -- Eliminate parking within the clientside/serverside commands.
bugs.fix: iRule parking in clientside/serverside command no longer causes tmm to restart.

bugs.title: Nethsm-thales-install.sh installation fails with error 'Could not reach Thales HSM'
bugs.symptoms: Thales installation script fails with error message. ERROR: Could not reach Thales HSM "<ip>". Make sure the HSM IP address is correct and that the HSM is accessible to the BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the ICMP ping is blocked between the BIG-IP system and netHSM.
bugs.impact: Thales/nCipher NetHSM client software installation fails.
bugs.workaround: Unblock ICMP ping between the BIG-IP system and netHSM.

bugs.title: Sending ASM report via AWS SES failed duo to wrong content type
bugs.symptoms: When you attempt to send an ASM report via AWS SES, the message bounces with the following message: Could not send e-mails: SMTP Error: data not accepted.; Transaction failed: Expected MIME type, got ;; Error code: 554. This occurs because the BIG-IP system is sending out the report message with an empty Content-Type in the multipart MIME, which the AWS mail host cannot process.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered in the following scenario: 1. Set up SMTP and ASM schedule report. 2. Click Send Now, and get the error message in GUI. 3. SSH into the BIG-IP system. 4. Add this line under the following snippet: [admin@bigip:Active:Standalone] ~ # chmod 644 /var/ts/dms/script/avrexport/avrmail.php [admin@bigip:Active:Standalone] ~ # vi /var/ts/dms/script/avrexport/avrmail.php if (!$mail_subject) $mail_subject = "BIG-IP Analytics Report"; if (!$mail_body) $mail_body = "Attached to this e-mail is a BIG-IP Analytics Report issued at $mail_time＼n＼n"; if (!$mail_from) $mail_from = 'BIG-IP Reporter'; if (!$mail_content_type) $mail_content_type = 'text/html'; <<<< Add this line for add text/html into content type. [admin@bigip:Active:Standalone] ~ # chmod 444 /var/ts/dms/script/avrexport/avrmail.php 5. Click Send Now again and it works. Note: To use AWS SES, you must verify your email address first (as a Sender). You can search SES in AWS and verify your email in Email Addresses. AWS sends an email. Click the embedded link after receipt, and then you can use it as the Sender address on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Cannot receive ASM reports.

bugs.title: Unexpected tmm core
bugs.symptoms: A tmm core occurs unexpectedly and causes a failover event.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while tmm is in normal operation. An internal error occurs when deleting an old SSL session during SSL handshake.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed incorrect internal deletion of expired SSL sessions.

bugs.title: Overflow of Multicast table filling the tmm log
bugs.symptoms: Whenever a new multicast entry is added to an already full table, an error is logged to /var/log/tmm
bugs.conditions: This warning occurs when the multicast table is full
bugs.impact: When this condition occurs, this can fill the tmm log with these warning messages

bugs.title: Suspending iRule FLOW_INIT on a virtual-to-virtual flow leads to a crash
bugs.symptoms: An iRule executing on the FLOW_INIT event can suspend. If it does so while connecting to a virtual-to-virtual flow, it can cause a TCP crash, which results in a tmm restart.
bugs.conditions: An iRule executing on the FLOW_INIT event suspends while connecting to a virtual-to-virtual flow.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not include any iRules that suspend processing in FLOW_INIT.
bugs.fix: Suspending the iRule FLOW_INIT on a virtual-to-virtual flow no longer leads to a crash.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition on Hyper-V and Azure does not have SR-IOV support
bugs.symptoms: Hyper-V Standalone and Azure utilizes the sock driver and has no support for underlying VMBUS devices nor SR-IOV, which degrades system performance.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE is deployed in Hyper-V standalone or Azure environment using Mellanox Connect-X 5 NICs with accelerated networking switched on for the NICs.
bugs.impact: - There is a lack of targeted driver support for VMBUS devices which leads to lack of high performance.
bugs.fix: VE on Hyper-V Standalone and Azure makes use of xnet-DPDK driver for VMBUS devices with accelerated networking (SR-IOV) support.

bugs.title: GTP v1 APN is not decoded/encoded properly
bugs.symptoms: GTP v1 APN element was decoded/encoded as octetstring and Only GTP v2 APN element is decoded/encoded as DNS encoding.
bugs.conditions: - GTP version 1. - APN element.
bugs.impact: iRules become more complex when dealing with GTP v1 APN element, as it may need to convert between octetstring and dotted style domain name value after decoding or before encoding the data.
bugs.workaround: Use iRules to convert between octetstring and dotted style domain name values.
bugs.fix: GTP version 1 APN information element is now decoded/encoded as DNS encoding.
bugs.behavior: GTP v1 apn element is now decoded/encoded using DNS-like encoding. Previously, it was decoded/encoded as octetstring.

bugs.title: The iqsyncer utility leaks memory for large bigip_gtm.conf file when log.gtm.level is set to debug
bugs.symptoms: The iqsyncer utility leaks memory.
bugs.conditions: -- There is a large bigip_gtm.conf. -- The log.gtm.level is set to debug.
bugs.impact: The iqsyncer utility exhausts memory and is killed.
bugs.workaround: Do not set log.gtm.level equal to or higher than debug.

bugs.title: When MRF is in use, TCP::release does not immediately remove data from the TCP payload
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes because the TCP::payload is not flushed after the TCP::release command.
bugs.conditions: If a virtual server is configured for MRF, when TCP::release is used, it does not immediately remove the specified number of bytes from the TCP payload, leading to the possibility that these bytes could be retrieved multiple times by successive calls to TCP::payload.
bugs.impact: Tmm crash leads to unavailability of service. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: For example, if a GENERICMESSAGE_INGRESS event is included in the iRule, then when it gets executed the bytes are removed from the payload. Another way to do it was to explicitly call 'TCP::payload replace 0 <bytes released> ""'.

bugs.title: Unbound's backoff algorithm interacts badly with net resolver iRules
bugs.symptoms: Using RESOLVER::name_lookup in an iRule against a net resolver forward zone name server that happens to be down can result in the iRule pausing for up to a few minutes.
bugs.conditions: Nameserver configures as fwd-zone in net resolver should be down.
bugs.impact: The connection to the virtual server is paused for a significant amount of time.
bugs.workaround: Use a pool of dns-servers, and configure the pool to monitor the backend dns servers and load balance to healthy pool members.

bugs.title: PEM VE does not send CCRi when receiving multiple subscriber requests in a short interval
bugs.symptoms: PEM sessions go to a stale state and the Credit Control Request (CCRi) is not sent.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM is configured and passing normal PEM traffic. -- Using BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE)
bugs.impact: Session is not established.
bugs.fix: Enhanced application to accept new sessions under problem conditions.

bugs.title: RADIUS STOP does not delete subscribers
bugs.symptoms: RADIUS STOP does not delete subscribers when tmm.pem.session.ipv4.addr.max = 2
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when RADIUS STOP is used to delete sessions
bugs.impact: Sessions will be stale in PEM. This can lead to incorrect policies getting applied and clients could be stuck in a user session.
bugs.workaround: -- Set tmm.pem.session.ipv4.addr.max = 1 -- Enable tmm.pem.session.delete.if.max.ipaddr.per.class.exceeded -- Convert interim-updates to start such that tmm.pem.session.delete.if.max.ipaddr.per.class.exceeded deletion is triggered

bugs.title: Manual upload of LiveUpdate image file results in NULL response
bugs.symptoms: When uploading a LiveUpdate image file from the GUI, the upload fails. In /var/log/restjavad.0.log you see the following error: [SEVERE][768][25 May 2020 05:38:20 UTC][com.f5.rest.workers.liveupdate.LiveUpdateFileTransferWorker] null
bugs.conditions: LiveUpdate images are uploaded manually.
bugs.impact: LiveUpdate images fail to upload.
bugs.workaround: 1. Upload the file to LiveUpdate files directory '/var/lib/hsqldb/live-update/update-files' on the host. 2. Send a POST request with the filename for inserting the file to the LiveUpdate database: * url : https://<HOST>/mgmt/tm/live-update/<UPDATE-CONFIGURATION>/update-files * payload - json: { "filename": "<FILE_NAME>", "fileLocationReference": {"link": "<FILE_NAME>"}} 3. Get the file link reference: https://{{big_ip1}}/mgmt/tm/live-update/asm-attack-signatures/update-files?$filter=filename eq '<FILE_NAME>' 4. From the response copy the "selfLink" part : "selfLink": "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/live-update/asm-attack-signatures/update-files/<UPDATE_FILE_ID>" 5. Create a POST request with the value above for creating a new installation record: * url : https://<HOST>/mgmt/tm/live-update/<UPDATE-CONFIGURATION>/installations * payload - json: { "updateFileReference": { "link": "https://localhost/mgmt/tm/live-update/asm-attack-signatures/update-files/<UPDATE_FILE_ID>"} } 6. Now the file is available to install it from the GUI. 7. Another option is to install it via the PATCH request and the installation_id from the response received at step 5: * url: https://<HOST>/mgmt/tm/live-update/<UPDATE-CONFIGURATION>/installations/<INSTALLATION_ID> * payload: { "status" : "install" }

bugs.title: Remote event logs may truncate at 5k when maximum entry length is configured to 64k
bugs.symptoms: Remote event logs are truncated at 5k instead of the configured 64k maximum entry length
bugs.conditions: Remote logging is configured with maximum entry length set to 64k
bugs.impact: Remote event logs are truncated at 5k, resulting in incomplete log entries
bugs.workaround: As a temporary workaround, change the maximum entry length to 2k or 10k, save the configuration, then change it back to 64k. Follow the same steps if the issue occurs again.

bugs.title: Delay in Network Convergence with RSTP enabled
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not to Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP) Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) with only the proposal flag ON (i.e., without the agreement flag ON).
bugs.conditions: -- Neighbor Switch sends RSTP BPDU with only proposal flag ON. -- The agreement flag is not ON.
bugs.impact: Network convergence takes more time than expected.

bugs.title: Redundant learning suggestion to set a Maximum Length when parameter is already at that value
bugs.symptoms: Policy Builder is issuing a learning suggestion to set a specific maximum length for a parameter when that parameter already has that exact maximum length already configured.
bugs.conditions: -- Response learning is turned on -- Response parameter length is less than, but close to, the currently configured maximum length limit.
bugs.impact: Redundant learning suggestion is issued.
bugs.workaround: You can either: -- Ignore the learning suggestion (Click the Ignore button). -- Turn off Learn from response.
bugs.fix: Learning suggestion is no longer issued with already configured maximum parameter length value.

bugs.title: iControl REST endpoint response includes the request content
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, iControl REST endpoint return the request contents in the response, potentially disclosing sensitive information.
bugs.conditions: -iControl REST request processed by an authenticated administrative user. -Undisclosed environmental conditions
bugs.impact: Potential disclosure of information from REST requests.
bugs.fix: Responses are now sanitized to suppress disclosure of request data.

bugs.title: BIG-IP SSL forward proxy might drop connection to servers with revoked certificate status.
bugs.symptoms: If the server certificate status is revoked, SSL forward proxy configured with a new server SSL profile might drop the connection.
bugs.conditions: -- New SSL forward proxy server SSL profile is attached to the virtual server. -- Revoked-cert-status-response-control is set to the default value (drop). -- Certificate status service (e.g., CRL/OCSP) is configured on the server SSL profile.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP client connections are reset.
bugs.workaround: Change revoked-cert-status-response-control to ignore on the server SSL profile.
bugs.fix: If ssl-forward-proxy is enabled for new server SSL profiles, and revoked-cert-status-response-control is not specified, it will automatically be set to ignore. Client connection go through and the client will see a forged revoked certificate status.

bugs.title: TMM might crash when sending out oversize packets.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with an assert; Drop assertion similar to the following: notice panic: ../dev/ndal/ndal.c:758: Assertion "pkt length cannot be greater than MAX_PKT_LEN" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Xnet driver is used in BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- TMM tries to send oversize packets.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Stream filter chunk-size limits filter to a single match per ingress buffer
bugs.symptoms: The chunk-size profile setting of the stream filter limits memory by capping the match string allocated from an ingress buffer to <chunksize> bytes. This implicitly limits the maximum size of the match, potentially resulting in missed matches beyond chunk-size within the same ingress buffer. For more information, see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K39394712
bugs.conditions: A stream filter is configured with the chunk-size parameter set and ingress data arrives which contains matches beyond the configured chunk-size in the buffer.
bugs.impact: Potential matches beyond the configured chunk-size will be sent unmodified by the stream filter, potentially resulting in missed matches.
bugs.fix: The stream filter can now successfully find and replace matches beyond chunk-size within a single ingress buffer.

bugs.title: TMM cores on secondary blades of the Chassis system.
bugs.symptoms: When using DNS Cache on chassis systems with a forward zone pointing at a self IP for communication with local BIND, the following assert triggers: tmm_panic (... "../net/loop.c:572: %sIDX set on listener%s") at ../lib/stdio.c:1307
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis system is used. -- Secondary TMMs core dump. -- Primary works as expected.
bugs.impact: TMMs on secondary blades core dump. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: 1) Create another virtual server with a DNS profile to use configured to use the local bind server. 2) Set the forward zones to point to that virtual server instead of the self IP as name servers.

bugs.title: Some roles are missing necessary permission to perform Live Update
bugs.symptoms: Certain roles, such as Resource Administrator and Application Security Operations Administrator, do not have sufficient permission levels to perform Live Update.
bugs.conditions: -- User with Resource Administrator or Application Security Operations Administrator role assigned. -- Attempt to perform Live Update.
bugs.impact: Users with Resource Administrator and Application Security Operations Administrator role cannot perform Live Update.
bugs.fix: The following roles can now perform live-update: - Administrator - Web Application Security Administrator - Resource Administrator - Application Security Operations Administrator

bugs.title: ASM sync failure with Cgc::Channel error 'Failed to send a message, error:15638476'
bugs.symptoms: The system exhibits various symptoms related to sync and control plane, and reports errors similar to the following: /var/log/: asm: -- (asm_config_server.pl,F5::Cgc::Channel::send): Failed to send a message, error:15638476. ts_debug.log: -- |ZEROMQ|May 21 23:27:31.840|24813|25914|25914|epoll.cpp:0060|~epoll_t()|(zmq_assert) Assertion failed: load.get () == 0
bugs.conditions: -- Two devices in a sync-failover/sync-only device group. -- Other conditions required to reproduce this issue are under investigation. Note: The occurrences of the Cgc::Channel message in the /var/log/ and /var/log/ts/asm_config_server logs are the most reliable indicator of this issue.
bugs.impact: -- Config-sync does not work, resulting in a different configuration among the devices in a sync group. -- Security log profile changes are not propagated to other devices. -- Portions of the GUI hang, e.g.: Security module tab, and 'security' menu under virtual server. -- Policies with learning enabled do not generate learning suggestions.
bugs.workaround: Restart asm_config_server on the units in the device group. # pkill -f asm_config_server

bugs.title: Non-admin users cannot run show running-config or list sys
bugs.symptoms: Lower-privileged users, for instance guests or operators, are unable to list the configuration in tmsh, and get an error: Unexpected Error: Can't display all items, can't get object count from mcpd. The list /sys or list /sys telemd commands trigger the following error: 01070823:3: Read Access Denied: user (oper) type (Telemd configuration).
bugs.conditions: User account with a role of guest, operator, or any role other than admin.
bugs.impact: You are unable to show the running config, or use list or list sys commands.
bugs.workaround: Logon with an account with admin access.

bugs.title: Cannot roll back after upgrading on certain platforms
bugs.symptoms: On certain platforms, after upgrade to this release you will not be able to boot back into an earlier software version. Contact F5 Support for the reversion process if this is required.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the following platforms: + i5820-DF / i7820-DF + 5250v-F / 7200v-F + 10200v-F + 10350v-F -- Upgrade the software. -- Attempt to roll back to a previous version.
bugs.impact: Cannot boot into a previous version. Contact F5 Support for the reversion process if this is required.
bugs.fix: Contact F5 Support for the reversion process if this is required.
bugs.behavior: On certain platforms, after upgrade to particular software versions, you will not be able to boot back into an earlier software version. Contact F5 Support for the reversion process if this is required. The particular platforms are: + i5820-DF / i7820-DF + 5250v-F / 7200v-F + 10200v-F + 10350v-F The particular software versions are: + BIG-IP v12.1.6 or later in the v12.x branch of code + BIG-IP v13.1.4 or later in the v13.x branch of code + BIG-IP v14.1.4 or later in the v14.x branch of code + BIG-IP v15.1.1 or later in the v15.x branch of code + BIG-IP v16.0.0 or later

bugs.title: Persistence might not work properly on virtual servers that utilize address lists
bugs.symptoms: -- Connections to the virtual server might hang. -- Increased tmm CPU utilization. This can occur after upgrading.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server is configured with a traffic-matching-criteria that utilizes a source-address-list and/or destination-address-list. -- The virtual server utilizes certain persistence one of the following persistence types: + Source Address (but not hash-algorithm carp) + Destination Address (but not hash-algorithm carp) + Universal + Cookie (only cookie hash) + Host + SSL session + SIP + Hash (but not hash-algorithm carp)
bugs.impact: -- High tmm CPU utilization. -- Stalled connections.
bugs.workaround: Enable match-across-virtuals in the persistence profile. Note: Enabling match-across-virtuals might affect the behaviour of other virtual servers in the configuration that utilise persistence.

bugs.title: Modification of in-tmm monitors may result in crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Modify in-tmm monitors. -- Perform configuration sync.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: -- Disable in-tmm monitors. -- Avoid config syncing to the active device.
bugs.fix: This issue is now fixed.

bugs.title: Upgrade may cause an aced core file
bugs.symptoms: After loading a UCS file, aced cores.
bugs.conditions: This can occur after upgrading, while loading the UCS file. The exact conditions that trigger it are unknown.
bugs.impact: An aced core file is left on the BIG-IP system. The BIG-IP system stills functions normally.
bugs.fix: Corrected conditions that might have caused aced to crash during stop/restart. When loading UCS files, typically daemons need to stop and restart.

bugs.title: Database monitor marks pool member down if 'send' is configured but no 'receive' strings are configured
bugs.symptoms: If an LTM database monitor type (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle, or PostgreSQL database monitor type) is configured with a 'send' string but with no 'receive' string to issue a user-specified database query, pool members using this monitor are marked DOWN, even though a connection to the configured database completed successfully.
bugs.conditions: -- An LTM pool or pool members is configured to use an LTM database (MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle or PostgreSQL) monitor type. -- A 'send' string is configured for the monitor. -- A 'receive' string is not configured.
bugs.impact: The database monitor marks the pool member down, even in cases where the pool member is actually pingable.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, configure 'send' and 'recv' strings for the database monitor that will always succeed when successfully connected to the specified database (with the configured username and password, if applicable).
bugs.fix: Database monitor no longer marks pool member down if 'send' is configured but no 'receive' strings are configured.

bugs.title: Link throughput statistics are different
bugs.symptoms: Different link throughput statistics are seen on GTM/DNS systems that are connected by full-mesh iQuery.
bugs.conditions: -- The same link is used on different BIG-IP addresses as a pool member in the default gateway pool. -- A forwarding virtual server is used.
bugs.impact: Each GTM/DNS server might get different link throughput for the same link, and therefore make less-than-optimal decisions.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the same uplink for different BIG-IP devices.
bugs.fix: GTM/DNS server now calculates the link throughput based on the aggregation of the link stats for the same link on different BIG-IP systems.

bugs.title: A virtual server with multiple client SSL profiles, the profile with CN or SAN of the cert matching the SNI is not selected if cert is ECDSA-signed
bugs.symptoms: In a virtual configured with multiple client SSL profiles, the profile with ECDSA-signed cert is not selected even though its CN/SAN matching the SNI extension of ClientHello.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server with multiple client SSL profiles. -- The SNI of,,lientHello does not match the 'server name' of any profile. -- The cert in the profile is ECDSA-signed and its CN/SAN matches SNI extension of ClientHello. -- That profile in is not selected.
bugs.impact: The incorrect client SSL profile is selected.
bugs.workaround: Configure the 'Server Name' option in the client SSL profile.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with client SSL profile selection.

bugs.title: iAppsLX Security Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, iAppsLX does not follow current best security practices.
bugs.conditions: iAppsLX REST access by an authenticated administrative user
bugs.impact: iAppsLX does not follow current best security practices.
bugs.fix: iAppsLX now follows current best security practices.

bugs.title: Racoon daemon may crash once at startup
bugs.symptoms: When the IKEv1 racoon daemon starts, it may immediately exit with a core file.
bugs.conditions: One of the following events may lead to the restart: -- BIG-IP systems start or restart as a standalone device. -- BIG-IP becomes the Active member of High Availability (HA) setup.
bugs.impact: Racoon restarts. Because this restart happens when racoon is trying to start, no IPsec IKEv1 tunnels are affected because they are down anyway.

bugs.title: Avrd core when avrd process is stopped or restarted
bugs.symptoms: When the avrd process is stopped or restarted, it fails with core before the exit. A core file with the name starting with SENDER_HTTPS (for example, SENDER_HTTPS.bld0.0.9.core.gz) can be found in /shared/cores/ directory.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system is registered on BIG-IQ and has established an HTTPS connection with BIG-IQ for sending stats data.
bugs.impact: Avrd cores while exiting. There is no impact on BIG-IP system functionality.
bugs.fix: Avrd no longer cores when avrd process is stopped or restarted.
bugs.workaround: No workaround

bugs.title: Ratio Member does not work with SIP traffic with MBLB framework
bugs.symptoms: Ratio member is a connection-based load balancing algorithm. The statistics this load balancing algorithm uses will be updated when a connection is connected/disconnected. When SIP/MBLB calls flow containing BYE and the 'Terminate on BYE' option is enabled, a new connection will be created with every SIP call. That is why the ratio member seems to work in such cases. If 'Terminate on BYE' is disabled, or it is enabled but the call is not closed with a BYE, then all pool member traffic will be directed to the same server because the SIP traffic is multiplexed over the same connection.
bugs.conditions: -- Pool configured with the load balancing method set to Ratio-Member. -- Pool is assigned to a virtual server configured with SIP and MBLB. -- Multiple SIP calls are multiplexed over same connection. -- SIP Profile option 'Terminate on BYE' is disabled or 'Terminate on Bye' is enabled but the call is not closed with BYE
bugs.impact: All of the SIP traffic is directed to a single server, or the actual ratio is not maintained correctly depending on the actual calls/configuration
bugs.workaround: FIRST WORKAROUND: Create duplicate pool members using the same server. For example if you have two servers, server A and B, and you want a ratio of 2:3, configure multiple pool members to achieve the desired ratio: A:5060 A:5061 B:5060 B:5061 B:5062 Impact of workaround: You must also disable port translation for the virtual server, and you must configure round robin load balancing. Also, the ratio is not preserved if one of the pool members goes down. SECOND WORKAROUND: If you are unable to use multiple ports on the same server, you could also use multiple IP addresses. The following pool configuration also achieves a 2:3 ratio between server A and server B: ​ A1:5060 A2:5060 B1:5060 B2:5060 B3:5060 Impact of workaround: you must also configure round robin load balancing. Also, the ratio is not preserved if one of the pool members goes down. THIRD WORKAROUND: Implement a ratio algorithm in an iRule. After checking to see if the message is of type INVITE, select a pool member based on a computed algorithm in the iRule. For example you can declare an array of pool member ip:port, then loop through them. A pool member can be selected via: pool <pool name> member <ip> <port> Impact of workaround: The iRule should also check the pool member status to ensure it is up. LB::status can be used to check status of pool member

bugs.title: Ratio session based Load balancing does not work
bugs.symptoms: Ratio session based Load balancing does not work over MRF framework with Diameter, SIP protocols; all traffic is directed to a single pool member.
bugs.conditions: -- MRF virtual server configured with either a Diameter or SIP protocol profile. -- The pool's load balancing method is set to Ratio-Session.
bugs.impact: All of the SIP traffic is directed to a single server, or the actual Ratio is not maintained correctly depending on the actual calls/configuration
bugs.workaround: FIRST WORKAROUND: Create duplicate pool members using the same server. For example if you have two servers, server A and B, and you want a ratio of 2:3, configure multiple pool members to achieve the desired ratio: A:5060 A:5061 B:5060 B:5061 B:5062 Impact of workaround: You must also disable port translation for the virtual server, and you must configure round robin load balancing. Also, the ratio is not preserved if one of the pool members goes down. SECOND WORKAROUND: If you are unable to use multiple ports on the same server, you could also use multiple IP addresses. The following pool configuration also achieves a 2:3 ratio between server A and server B: ​ A1:5060 A2:5060 B1:5060 B2:5060 B3:5060 Impact of workaround: you must also configure round robin load balancing. Also, the ratio is not preserved if one of the pool members goes down. THIRD WORKAROUND: Implement a ratio algorithm in an iRule. After checking to see if the message is of type INVITE, select a pool member based on a computed algorithm in the iRule. For example you can declare an array of pool member ip:port, then loop through them. A pool member can be selected via: pool <pool name> member <ip> <port> Impact of workaround: The iRule should also check the pool member status to ensure it is up. LB::status can be used to check status of pool member

bugs.title: No learning suggestion on ASM policies enabled via LTM policy
bugs.symptoms: ASM policy has the option 'Learn only from non-bot traffic' enabled, but the Policy Builder detects that the client is a bot, and therefore does not issue learning suggestions for the traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM policy is enabled via LTM policy. -- ASM policy configured to learn only from non-bot traffic. This applies to complex policies, and in some configurations may happen also when a simple policy is enabled via LTM policy.
bugs.impact: No learning suggestions.
bugs.workaround: Disable the option 'Learn only from non-bot traffic' on the ASM policy.
bugs.fix: Policy builder now classifies non-bot traffic and applies learning suggestions.

bugs.title: Restore missing UDP statistics
bugs.symptoms: The following UDP statistics are missing: -- bufdropdgram -- maxrate_conns -- maxrate_cur_conns -- sendbuf_cur_bytes -- queue_dropped_bytes
bugs.conditions: Viewing UDP statistics.
bugs.impact: Unable to view these UDP statistics.
bugs.fix: The following UDP statistics are now restored: -- bufdropdgram -- maxrate_conns -- maxrate_cur_conns -- sendbuf_cur_bytes -- queue_dropped_bytes

bugs.title: Upgrade process does not update Tcl scripts
bugs.symptoms: The upgrade process does not update Tcl scripts (such as iRules) in the configuration.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading Tcl scripts (such as iRules).
bugs.impact: This might cause issues when iRule syntax changes between releases. After upgrading, you might need to modify iRules to reflect any changes in iRule syntax.

bugs.title: The high availability (HA) incremental sync reverts to full load after SSL Orchestrator configuration changes
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP administrator initiates a high availability (HA) sync from one high availability (HA) peer to another, pending SSL Orchestrator configuration changes yield a full configuration load instead of an incremental update.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP high availability (HA) configuration with SSL Orchestrator or similar iAppLX configurations
bugs.impact: This may impact the overall performance of the sync across the high availability (HA) peers during frequent changes of SSL Orchestrator or similar iAppLX configurations.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.
bugs.fix: Issuing the high availability (HA) sync following an SSL Orchestrator configuration change yields an incremental configuration update across the high availability (HA) configuration.

bugs.title: No connection error after failover with MRF, and no connection mirroring
bugs.symptoms: -- Unable to establish MRF connection after failover. -- Error reports 'no connection'.
bugs.conditions: - MRF configured. - Using iRule for routing. -- Failover occurs.
bugs.impact: Unable to establish new connection until existing sessions time out. No message is reported explaining the circumstances.
bugs.workaround: Any of the following: -- Enable connection mirroring on the virtual server. -- Disable session mirroring.

bugs.title: TMM generates core while deleting iFiles
bugs.symptoms: While deleting iFiles, TMM might crash and generates a core.
bugs.conditions: -- There is any ifile command in an iRule where you are giving a list object to the file name argument instead of to a string object, for example: The 2nd line returns a list object, and the 3rd line is giving it to ifile command: set ifile_name tcl.1 set ifile_name [lsearch -glob -inline [ifile listall] "*$ifile_name"] ifile get $ifile_name -- A request is processed by the iRule. -- Attempt to delete the file in which the issue occurred.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts, triggering failover in high availability (HA) configurations. Traffic disruption while TMM restarts on a standalone configuration.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that the iRule gives a string object to ifile commands. Here is a sample iRule that implements the workaround: set ifile_name tcl.1 set ifile_name [lsearch -glob -inline [ifile listall] "*$ifile_name"] ifile get [format "%s" $ifile_name]

bugs.title: Tmsh help page for GTP iRule contains incorrect and missing information
bugs.symptoms: In the tmsh help page for the GTP iRule command, it contains incorrect and missing information for GTP::header and GTP::respond command.
bugs.conditions: When running "tmsh help ltm rule command GTP::header", information regarding GTP::header and GTP::respond iRule command may be incorrect or missing.
bugs.impact: User may not be able to use related iRule command properly.
bugs.fix: Tmsh help page for GTP iRule is updated

bugs.title: GTP::header extension command may abort connection due to unreasonable TCL error
bugs.symptoms: When running "GTP::header extension" iRule command with some conditions, it may cause a TCL error and abort the connection.
bugs.conditions: Running "GTP::header extension" iRule command is used with some specific arguments and/or specific condition of GTP message
bugs.impact: TCL error log is shown and connection is aborted
bugs.fix: GTP::header extension command no longer abort connection due to unreasonable TCL error

bugs.title: 'GTP::header extension count' iRule command returns 0
bugs.symptoms: The 'GTP::header extension count' iRule command always returns 0 (zero).
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when using 'GTP::header extension count' in an iRule.
bugs.impact: The command returns false information.
bugs.fix: 'GTP::header extension count' command now returns number of header extension correctly.

bugs.title: On blade failure, some trunked egress traffic is dropped.
bugs.symptoms: When a blade fails, other blades may try to forward traffic using trunked interfaces on the down blade.
bugs.conditions: -- A multi-blade chassis. -- Interfaces are trunked. -- A blade is pulled or powered off.
bugs.impact: Some traffic is dropped until the failed blade is detected by clusterd (10 seconds by default.)

bugs.title: Tmm cores while doing Hitless Upgrade while there are active flows
bugs.symptoms: Tmm cores.
bugs.conditions: Addition of new flows to existing lib while Hitless Upgrade is in progress.
bugs.impact: Tmm core while doing app detection for new flows. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restrict addition of new flows if a Hitless Upgrade is in progress.
bugs.fix: New flows are no longer added to the classification engine to any of the library if the Hitless Upgrade process is in progress.

bugs.title: URL Categorization: wr_urldbd cores while processing urlcat-query
bugs.symptoms: The webroot daemon (wr_urldbd) cores.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while passing traffic when webroot is enabled.
bugs.impact: The wr_urldbd daemon cores. URL Categorization functionality may not work as expected.
bugs.fix: Fixed a core with wr_urldb.

bugs.title: Memory leak with WebSocket connections
bugs.symptoms: WebSocket frame memory leak might occur when connections are closed midway during transfer.
bugs.conditions: - WebSocket profile is attached to the virtual server. - HTTP and SSL profiles are attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Memory leak occurs and tmm can crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove the WebSocket profile from the virtual server.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a memory leak with WebSocket connections under these conditions.

bugs.title: Unable to complete REST API PUT request for 'tm/ltm/data-group/internal' endpoint.
bugs.symptoms: When REST API PUT request is call to modify LTM data-group internal without 'type' field in body-content, it fails intermittently with a 400 error. --{"code":400,"message":"invalid property value \"type\":\"\"","errorStack":[],"apiError":26214401} The 'type' field is not getting populated with default value and is set to null string "" instead.
bugs.conditions: -- PUT REST API request used to modify LTM data-group internal. -- Type field is not specified in the body-content.
bugs.impact: Unable to update the configuration object (LTM data-group internal) with REST API PUT.
bugs.workaround: Include 'type' field inside PUT request body content for the operation to succeed. Example Curl Command: -- curl -isku <username>:<password> -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X PUT -d '{"records":[{"name":"1.1.1.1"}, {"name":"1.1.1.2"}], "type":"ip"}' https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/data-group/internal/~Common~<Name>

bugs.title: Rebooting a blade causes MCPd to core as it rejoins the cluster
bugs.symptoms: Tmm and mcpd cores for slot2
bugs.conditions: On the standby chassis, reboot the primary blade and wait for it to rejoin the cluster. Once it does, mcpd will core.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm and mcpd mcpd restarts.

bugs.title: Support for DNSSEC Lookaside Validation (DLV) has been removed.
bugs.symptoms: Following the deprecation of DNSSEC lookaside validation (DLV) by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), support for this feature has been removed from the product.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use DLV.
bugs.impact: Cannot use DLV.
bugs.workaround: None. DLV is no longer supported.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP DNS validating resolver no longer supports DNSSEC lookaside validation (DLV). If you roll forward a configuration that contains this feature, the system removes it from the configuration and prints a log message.
bugs.behavior: The BIG-IP DNS validating resolver no longer supports DNSSEC lookaside validation (DLV).

bugs.title: Error viewing security policy settings for virtual server with FTP Protocol Security
bugs.symptoms: The system reports an error message when trying to navigate to 'Security :: Policies' under virtual server properties: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.conditions: -- An FTP or SMTP profile with protocol security enabled is attached to a virtual server. -- Attempt to navigate to 'Security :: Policies'.
bugs.impact: -- No policies appear. You cannot perform any operations on the 'Security :: Policies' screen. -- The following error message appears instead: An error has occurred while trying to process your request.
bugs.workaround: As long as an FTP or SMTP profile with protocol security enabled is defined under virtual server properties (in another words, it is attached to a virtual server), this issue recurs. There are no true workarounds, but you can avoid the issue by using any of the following: -- Use another profile, such as HTTP. -- Set the FTP/SMTP profile under the virtual server settings to None. -- Remove the profile via the GUI or the CLI (e.g., you can remove the profile from the virtual server in tmsh using this command: tmsh modify ltm virtual /Common/test-vs { profiles delete { ftp_security } }
bugs.fix: You can now attach FTP or SMTP profile with protocol security enabled and navigate to 'Security :: Policies' without error.

bugs.title: Security - Options section in navigation menu is visible for only Administrator users
bugs.symptoms: The Security - Options section in the left navigation menu is visible for only for user accounts configured with the Administrator role.
bugs.conditions: You logged in as a user configured with a role other than Administrator.
bugs.impact: No direct access to many settings that are available only for user account configured with the Administrator role.
bugs.workaround: Direct links to the pages work for those with the appropriate roles.
bugs.fix: Security - Options section is available for all user roles when at least one of the following is enabled: -- ASM -- DoS -- FPS -- AFM

bugs.title: i15000, i15800, i5000, i7000, i10000, i11000 and B4450 blades may lose efficiency when source ports form an arithmetic sequence
bugs.symptoms: Traffic imbalance between tmm threads. You might see the traffic imbalance by running the following command: tmsh show sys tmm-traffic
bugs.conditions: Source ports used to connect to i15000, i15800, i5000, i7000, i10000, i11000 and B4450 blades form an arithmetic sequence. For example, some client devices always use even source port numbers for ephemeral connections they initiate. This means the 'stride' of the ports selected is '2'. Because a sorted list of the ports yields a list like 2, 4, 6, 8... 32002, 32004. It is 'striding' over the odd ports; thus, a port stride of 2.
bugs.impact: Traffic imbalance may result in tmm threads on different CPU cores having imbalanced workloads. While this can sometimes impact on performance, an overloaded tmm thread can usually redistribute load to less loaded threads in a way that does not impact performance. However the loads on the CPU cores will appear imbalanced still.
bugs.workaround: Where possible, configure devices to draw from the largest possible pool of source ports when connecting via a BIG-IP system.
bugs.behavior: This release introduces a new variable to mitigate this issue: dagv2.pu.table.size.multiplier. You must set the variable to 2 or 3 on the host, and then restart tmm on all host blades and then all guests to mitigate the issue. dag2.pu.table.size.multiplier.

bugs.title: Syslog-ng periodically logs nothing for 20 seconds
bugs.symptoms: Once per minute, syslog-ng logs nothing for 20 seconds.
bugs.conditions: -- A remote syslog server is specified by hostname, forcing syslog-ng to resolve it. -- the DNS resolution times out (for example, if the DNS server is unreachable)
bugs.impact: When using DNS names to specify remote syslog destinations and DNS is unreachable, syslog-ng re-attempts to resolve the name every 60 seconds. This resolution has a 20 seconds timeout, and blocks the syslog process from writing logs to disk during that time. Note that the logs are buffered, not lost, and will still be written to disk (with the correct timestamps) once the DNS query times out.
bugs.fix: F5 patched syslog-ng to use a lower 1-second, 0-retries timeout back in 13.0.0, but this patch was made ineffective by the upgrade to centos 7 in 14.1.0. This fixes the patch so that it works again.

bugs.title: Unable to save UCS
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to create a backup UCS. You see a warning in /var/log/restjavad.0.log: [WARNING][8100/tm/shared/sys/backup/306b4630-aa74-4a3d-af70-0d49bdd1d89e/worker UcsBackupTaskWorker] Failure with backup process 306b4630-aa74-4a3d-af70-0d49bdd1d89e. This is followed by a list of some files in /var/named/config/namedb/.
bugs.conditions: Named has some Slave zones configured and is going through frequent zone transfer.
bugs.impact: You are unable to create a UCS file.
bugs.workaround: Stop named zone transfer while doing UCS backup.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may reject a POST request if it comes first and exceeds the initial window size
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 protocol allows a negative flow-control window on initial stage of communication while first 65,535 bytes of payload are delivered from a peer. BIG-IP may break this requirement.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP has a virtual server with http2 profile. -- A configured receive window size in the http2 profile is below 64K (default 32K). -- A peer sends POST request with payload exceeding initial receive window size over HTTP/2 connection.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP denies the POST request and sends RST_STREAM.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP allows a negative flow-control window on initial request allowing a peer to fill all 65,535 bytes of flow-control window even if it exceeds an advertised receive window size.
bugs.behavior: For an HTTP/2 client or a server BIG-IP may impose a delay up to 20 seconds if a peer sends 65,535 bytes of payload over a single stream and does not respond timely with SETTINGS/ACK frame to a SETTINGS frame sent by BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Engineering Hotfixes missing bug titles
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes may not show the summary titles for fixed bugs (as appear for the affected bugs published via Bug Tracker). -- The 'tmsh show sys version' command displays the bug numbers for fixes included in Engineering Hotfixes. -- If a given bug has been published via Bug Tracker, the summary title of the bug is expected to be displayed as well. -- Running BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes built on or after March 18, 2019.
bugs.conditions: For affected BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes, titles are not displayed for any bugs fixed in the Engineering Hotfix.
bugs.impact: Cannot see the summaries of the bugs fixed by running the 'tmsh show sys version' command.
bugs.workaround: For bugs that are published via Bug Tracker, you can query for the affected bug in Bug Tracker (https://support.f5.com/csp/bug-tracker). Note: Not all bugs fixed in BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes are published to Bug Tracker. For information on such bugs, consult F5 support, or the original Service Request submitted to F5 in which the affected Engineering Hotfix was requested.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes now include the summary titles for fixed bugs that have been published via Bug Tracker.

bugs.title: Reboot after tmsh load sys config changes sys FPGA firmware-config value
bugs.symptoms: As a part of FPGA firmware update, "tmsh load sys config" fails. Chmand reports errors: chmand[19052]: FPGA firmware mismatch - auto update, No Interruption! chmand[19052]: 012a0006:6: FPGA HSB firmware uploading now...use caution! Reloading fw_update_post configuration (via systemctl): [FAILED]
bugs.conditions: Running either of the following commands: tmsh load sys config /etc/init.d/fw_update_post reload
bugs.impact: Firmware update fails.
bugs.workaround: Use this procedure: 1. Mount /usr: mount -o rw,remount /usr 2. Add the following line to the '/usr/lib/systemd/system/fw_update_post.service' file: ExecReload=/etc/init.d/fw_update_post reload 3. Reload systemctl: systemctl daemon-reload 4. Reload the file: /etc/init.d/fw_update_post reload
bugs.fix: Added the reload option in fw_update_post service file.

bugs.title: [ASM - AWS] - Auto Scaling BIG-IP systems overwrite ASU
bugs.symptoms: When a Cloud Auto Scaling deployment is set up using F5's Auto Scale Template, and ASM Live Update is configured with Automatic Download enabled, Live Update configuration may be overwritten during a scale out event when a new host joins the sync cluster. This is caused by a config sync from the new device to the master device, before the master has a chance to sync the configuration to the new device, causing the configuration in the master device to be overwritten.
bugs.conditions: -- Using F5's Auto Scaling template. -- Auto Scale script is configured with --block-sync (which is the default). -- ASM Live Update is configured with Automatic Download enabled. -- A scale out event occurs. -- New ASU is automatically downloaded by Live Update at the new host.
bugs.impact: Live Update configuration of all devices in the Auto Scale group is overwritten.
bugs.workaround: Disable ASM Live Update Automatic Download. This can be done by disabling the liveupdate.autodownload DB variable using the onboard.js script, and adding '-d liveupdate.autodownload:disable'. For example: /usr/bin/f5-rest-node /config/cloud/aws/node_modules/@f5devcentral/f5-cloud-libs/scripts/onboard.js --log-level silly --signal ONBOARD_DONE -o /var/log/cloud/aws/onboard.log --host localhost --port 8443 -d tm.tcpudptxchecksum:software-only -d liveupdate.autodownload:disable --ping -d tm.tcpudptxchecksum:software-only -d liveupdate.autodownload:disable In order to still have automatic updates for the group, the db variable can be enabled for the master device. Then this setting will be applied on every new host after joining the group and receiving the initial sync from the master.
bugs.fix: Automatic downloads are quietly synced and do not have an impact on the device group sync status.

bugs.title: TMM SIGSEGV and crash
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crash when using iRule to reject connections when Behavioral DoS is enabled.
bugs.conditions: This can occur due to an interaction between a Behavioral DoS policy and an iRule designed to potentially drop some of the connections.
bugs.impact: With heavy traffic, the tmm process might crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use iRules to reject connections that are bound to a virtual server with a Behavioral DoS policy attached.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to iRules and Behavioral DoS policies.

bugs.title: TMM crash seen with FTP and Classification profiles
bugs.symptoms: TMM might core and restart when FTP traffic is being proxied by a BIG-IP device.
bugs.conditions: -- Both FTP and Classification profiles are applied to a virtual server. -- The FTP profile has inherit-parent-profile enabled.
bugs.impact: -- TMM crashes and restarts -- Failover, loss of service during restart. -- Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Protocol Profile (Client) for virtual server is reset to the default profile for that protocol
bugs.symptoms: The GUI page always incorrectly shows that the default protocol profile is selected in a virtual server, even though it is not the actual configured profile CLI will show the correct information for the virtual server
bugs.conditions: A virtual server is configured with a non-default protocol profile
bugs.impact: - The GUI always displays the default protocol profile (e.g., "tcp") regardless of the actual configured value - The actual tmsh configuration remains correct - If an administrator clicks "Update" while viewing the incorrect GUI values, the default profile gets pushed to the configuration, silently overwriting the intended setting, along with any other changes being made
bugs.workaround: No workarounds in the GUI to view the correctly selected profile CLI will show the correct profile selected

bugs.title: VLAN Failsafe timeout is not always respected
bugs.symptoms: VLAN Failsafe timeout is triggered later than its configured interval.
bugs.conditions: -- Rarely happen on first failover. More commonly occurs on 3rd/4th failover. -- Specific conditions that cause this issue are not known.
bugs.impact: VLAN Failsafe timeout might be triggered later than it is configured. The exact impact varies based on the configuration and traffic activity.
bugs.workaround: Use another form of automatic failover if needed (gateway failsafe, ha-groups, etc.).

bugs.title: Unable to apply LTM policies to virtual servers after running 'mount -a'
bugs.symptoms: After attempting to assign an LTM policy to a virtual server, you may get an error in the GUI: 010716d8:3: Compilation of ltm policies for virtual server /Common/VS failed; Couldn't publish shared memory segment. You may also see this logged in /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[6905]: 010716d5:3: Failed to publish LOIPC object for (loipc_VS.1589526000.777142413). Call to (shm_open) failed with errno (13) errstr (Permission denied).
bugs.conditions: -- Run the command: mount -a -- Attempt to assign an LTM policy to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Having /dev/shm mounted twice affects every process on the BIG-IP system that use that directory for shared memory. The duplicated mount can result an inability to apply LTM policies, but the impact is not limited to that issue.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command to enable assigning an LTM policy to a virtual server: umount -l /dev/shm Unmounting might not resolve every issue that is result of /dev/shm being mounted more then once. So it's best if mount -a is not run at all.

bugs.title: Support USB redirection through VVC (VMware virtual channel) with BlastX
bugs.symptoms: USB is unavailable after opening VMware View Desktop.
bugs.conditions: 1. Secure Tunnel disabled on VCS 2. Launch view virtual desktop via native view client from an APM webtop or from the View client
bugs.impact: USB is unavailable after opening VMware View Desktop
bugs.fix: USB is now available after opening VMware View Desktop

bugs.title: Value of tmm.quic.log.level can differ between TMSH and GUI
bugs.symptoms: The value of the QUIC logging level is erroneously shown as 'Error' in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Set tmm.quic.log.level to 'Info' or 'Critical' in TMSH.
bugs.impact: Misleading log level displayed in the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH to set and view values for tmm.quic.log.level.
bugs.fix: GUI values for tmm.quic.log.level are now displayed properly.

bugs.title: Crontab backup to save UCS ends with Unexpected Error: UCS saving process failed.
bugs.symptoms: Using crontab to automatically backup UCS file by scheduling cronjobs fails due to SELinux permissions. The failure produces the following error: Unexpected Error: UCS saving process failed.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when 'tmsh save sys ucs' is executed through a cronjob.
bugs.impact: UCS file is not successfully saved and backup fails.

bugs.title: AVR core files have unclear names
bugs.symptoms: If avrd fails a core file created in this case is named according to the thread name and has no indication that it belongs to avr, for example: SENDER_HTTPS.bld0.0.9.core.gz
bugs.conditions: Avrd fails with a core
bugs.impact: It is inconvenient for identifying the process that caused the core.
bugs.fix: Improved the avrd core file name.

bugs.title: Single Page Application can break the page, when hooking is done by the end server application.
bugs.symptoms: When the end server application hooks some of the XHR callback functions (onload, onreadystate, send, open..), and a Single Page Application is used, the application page may malfunction.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when a server application hooks some XHR callbacks, and one of the following: -- Bot Defense Profile with 'Single Page Application' enabled and attached to the virtual server. -- ASM Policy with 'Single Page Application' enabled and a JS feature is attached to the virtual server. -- DoS Profile with Application Security and 'Single Page Application' enabled and is attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Web page does not render properly. It might result in a blank page, missing functionality, etc.
bugs.workaround: Run the command: tmsh modify sys db dosl7.parse_html_inject_tags value "after,body"

bugs.title: Availability status of virtual server remains 'available' even after associated pool's availability becomes 'unknown'
bugs.symptoms: Availability status of virtual server can be left 'available' even if the corresponding pool's availability becomes 'unknown'.
bugs.conditions: - Pool member is configured as an FQDN node. - You set monitor to 'none' with the pool.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent availability status of pool and virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Set the FQDN node to 'force offline', and then 'enable'. This triggers virtual server's status updates and syncs to pool.

bugs.title: DoS unconditionally logs MCP messages to /var/tmp/mcpd.out
bugs.symptoms: Excessive and large DoS debug messages associated with tmsh commands and stat queries are logged to /var/tmp/mcpd.out which is not log-rotated.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM is provisioned. -- DoS queries executed via tmsh. -- Access to DoS dashboard.
bugs.impact: Disk space is consumed on the filesystem for /var/tmp, which can eventually lead to follow-on failures when the disk fills up.
bugs.workaround: Delete or purge /var/tmp/mcpd.out.

bugs.title: Do not rearm TCP Keep Alive timer under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: Increased CPU usage due to zombie TCP flows rearming TCP Keep Alive timer continuously and unnecessarily.
bugs.conditions: -- A large number of zombie flows exists. -- TCP Keep Alive timer is rearmed aggressively for zombie flows with very small idle_timeout (0) value. -- TCP Keep alive timer keeps expiring and is rearmed continuously.
bugs.impact: Continuous rearming results in consuming CPU resources unnecessarily.
bugs.fix: Rearming of TCP Keep Alive timer is improved.

bugs.title: Point-to-point tunnel flows do not refresh connection entries; traffic dropped/discarded
bugs.symptoms: Dynamic routing changes do not cause point-to-point tunnel flows to refresh their connection entries causing tunneled traffic to be dropped/discarded.
bugs.conditions: Path to a remote tunnel endpoint is provided by a dynamic routing.
bugs.impact: Tunneled traffic might be dropped/discarded by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Use static routing to provide a path to remote tunnel endpoint.

bugs.title: Accessing Dashboard page with AVR provisioned causes continuous audit logs
bugs.symptoms: Navigating to Statistics :: Dashboard in the GUI with AVR or APM provisioned causes continuous audit logging and restjavad logs.
bugs.conditions: -- AVR provisioned -- An administrator navigates to Statistics :: Dashboard.
bugs.impact: The continuous extra logs might lead to confusion and may not be helpful.

bugs.title: LTM Virtual Server Health is not affected by iRule Requests dropped
bugs.symptoms: Virtual Server Health should not take into account deliberate drop requests.
bugs.conditions: -- DoS profile is attached to Virtual Server. -- iRule that drops requests on some condition is also attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Server Health reflects it is overloading status more precisely.
bugs.workaround: Do not use iRules to drop requests when Behavioral DoS is configured.
bugs.fix: Virtual Server Health is no longer affected while dropping requests using iRules.

bugs.title: imish command hangs when ospfd is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Running the imish command hangs when ospfd is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing enabled. -- The ospfd protocol is enabled. -- Running the imish command.
bugs.impact: The imish operation hangs.
bugs.workaround: Restart the ospfd daemon.

bugs.title: New Traffic Class Page shows multiple question marks.
bugs.symptoms: When you navigate to the traffic class creation page by clicking Create button in the Traffic Class list page, Chinese characters are displayed with multiple question marks.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when creating a new Traffic Class.
bugs.impact: Multi-byte characters are displayed incorrectly.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with rendering multi-byte characters on the Traffic Class screen.

bugs.title: RADIUS Access-Reject Reply-Message should be printed on logon page if 'show extended error' is true
