bugs.symptoms: After enabling 'show-extended-error' on the RADIUS Auth agent, instead of seeing the expected message: 'The username or password is not correct. Please try again.', the system reports the message: (error: Access-Reject).
bugs.conditions: RADIUS Auth with 'show-extended-error' enabled.
bugs.impact: The content of the Reply Message is not reported. The actual reported error message is confusing and provides no assistance in resolving the condition causing the access error: username, password, passcode, or tokencode.

bugs.title: The pool statistics GUI page fails (General database error retrieving information.) when filtering on pool status.
bugs.symptoms: When using the pool statistics GUI page, the page stops displaying and the GUI shows the following error: General database error retrieving information.
bugs.conditions: You attempt to apply a Status filter (e.g., Available) to display only some pools.
bugs.impact: The Status filter is not usable. Additionally, the page continues not to display even after you navigate away from the page and later return to it.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround to prevent the issue, but if you wish to access that page again (and not use the Status filter), you can do so by clearing your browser's cache.

bugs.title: Image install fails if iRulesLX is provisioned and /usr mounted read-write
bugs.symptoms: If iRulesLX is provisioned the /usr mount points are mounted as read-write. This causes the installation of an image to fail. tmsh show software status will report the status for the target volume as one of the following: -- Could not access configuration source. -- Unable to get hosting system product info.
bugs.conditions: -- iRulesLX is provisioned. -- The /usr mount points are mounted as read-write. -- Attempt an installation or upgrade.
bugs.impact: Unable to upgrade or more generally install an image on a new or existing volume.
bugs.workaround: Re-mount /usr as read-only: mount -o remount,ro /usr

bugs.title: HTTP/2 dynamic header table may fail to identify indexed headers on the response side.
bugs.symptoms: Some HTTP/2 response headers may be added to the dynamic header table even if this header is already stored in the table. Instead of subsequent responses using the correct dynamic header table index, these headers may be continually seen as being incrementally indexed.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP/2 clientside profile. -- Concurrent HTTP/2 responses contain headers.
bugs.impact: Select HTTP/2 response headers may fail to use the dynamic header table index. These headers are incrementally indexed on subsequent responses instead of using the existing table index.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 response headers now properly use the dynamic header table index when possible.

bugs.title: Support QUIC and HTTP3 draft-29
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system supports QUIC and HTTP/3 draft-27 and draft-28. IETF has released draft-29.
bugs.conditions: Browser requests draft-29.
bugs.impact: Connection downgrades to an older version, or fails if the browser cannot downgrade.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now supports draft-29 and draft-28, and has removed draft-27 support.

bugs.title: Restart of TMM after stale interface reference
bugs.symptoms: An assert is reported in the logs: panic: ../net/ifc.c:975: Assertion "ifc ref valid" failed.
bugs.conditions: The conditions under which this occurs are unknown.
bugs.impact: Tmm crashes and restarts. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Configuration error caused by Drafts folder in a deleted custom partition while upgrading.
bugs.symptoms: A configuration error occurs during upgrade due to custom partition-associated Draft folder, which exists in configuration file after deleting a custom partition. Configuration error: Can't associate folder (/User/Drafts) folder does not exist.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in the following scenario: 1. Create Partition. 2. Create Policy under that partition. 3. Delete Policy. 4. Delete Partition. 5. Upgrade.
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails when a Drafts folder exists under the custom partition folder, if the custom partition is deleted.
bugs.workaround: Manually remove the stale folders in the configuration file, or use a script to remove them.

bugs.title: Particular Users unable to login with LDAP Authentication Provider
bugs.symptoms: With LDAP as authentication provider, some administrative users are unable to login to BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: -- LDAP remote authentication. -- Certain users, whose characteristics have not been identified.
bugs.impact: Certain client users cannot login to administer the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: BIG-IP generates duplicated ACK after SSL Handshake when SSL Session reused
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system generates two ACK packets while processing SSL.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL session reuse is enabled. -- SSL application data arrives immediately after the handshake is completed.
bugs.impact: Unnecessary packets are sent on the wire.

bugs.title: The wocplugin may get into a restart loop when AAM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: When AAM is provisioned the wocplugin resource allocation may fail, which could result in a restart loop of the plugin. This renders the AAM module nonfunctional.
bugs.conditions: Application Acceleration Manager (AAM) is provisioned
bugs.impact: AAM is not functional
bugs.fix: The wocplugin is now correctly provisioned and runs without restarts.

bugs.title: Truncated QUIC connection close reason
bugs.symptoms: The connection close reason in QUIC is limited to 5 bytes prior to the path being validated. This makes it difficult to debug early connection failures.
bugs.conditions: A connection close is sent in QUIC before the path is validated.
bugs.impact: Connection close reason is limited to 5 bytes before the path is validated.
bugs.fix: Reason string limits are now derived from the amount of credit we have remaining to send. This should allow a longer reason string in almost all cases.

bugs.title: BIG-IP SCP hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions SCP does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: - Authenticated high-privilege user - SCP file transfer
bugs.impact: BIG-IP do not follow current best practices for filesystem protection.
bugs.fix: All filesystem protections now follow best practices.

bugs.title: Tmsh install sys crypto key (SafeNet) command creates a duplicate mcp object
bugs.symptoms: Running 'tmsh install sys crypto key' command for SafeNet keys creates a new mcp object with the keyname as the label name in HSM, and with the duplicate key-id.
bugs.conditions: This happens when trying to install the key using the key-label as the argument.
bugs.impact: Even after deleting the tmsh key (tmsh delete sys crypto key), the BIG-IP system can still pass traffic because there's a duplicate key pointing to the same key in the HSM.

bugs.title: Certificate details are not added correctly to BIG-IP after license is assigned from BIG-IQ due to which IPS auto update fails on BIG IP
bugs.symptoms: After a license is assigned from BIG-IQ the f5_api_com.crt information is not added when the data is received in the license file.
bugs.conditions: The license is installed from BIG-IQ and the license text contains the f5_api_com.crt information.
bugs.impact: IPS auto update does not work

bugs.title: QUIC drops 0RTT packets if CID length changes
bugs.symptoms: QUIC sometimes rejects valid 0RTT packets.
bugs.conditions: -- QUIC enabled. -- The Connection ID length assigned by the client for the server's CID does not match what the server assigned.
bugs.impact: QUIC drops 0RTT packets. Lost 0RTT packets increase latency.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with 0RTT packets when using QUIC.

bugs.title: RESOLV::lookup returns empty string when querying against a local virtual server, and results in possible tmm core
bugs.symptoms: -- RESOLV::lookup returns an empty string. -- TMM might crash.
bugs.conditions: An iRule runs RESOLV::lookup targeting the query toward a local virtual server. For instance: RESOLV::lookup @/Common/my_dns_virtual www.example.com
bugs.impact: RESOLV::lookup does not return the expected result; tmm might crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: In the RESOLV::lookup command, replace the name of the virtual server with its IP address, or the IP address of an external DNS server. For instance, if /Common/my_dns_virtual has destination 192.0.2.53:53: instead of this: RESOLV::lookup @/Common/my_dns_virtual use this: RESOLV::lookup @192.0.2.53

bugs.title: Validation error while attaching DoS profile to GTP virtual
bugs.symptoms: Validation error is observed while attaching DoS security profile to GPRS Tunneling Protocol (GTP) virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Attach DoS security profile to GTP virtual server.
bugs.impact: Validation error. Cannot attach DoS profile to GTP virtual server.
bugs.fix: Create GTP virtual profile and attach DoS security profile to it. No validation error should be reported.

bugs.title: An authenticated user on iControlREST may gain elevated privilege level
bugs.symptoms: An authenticated iControl REST user may gain elevated privileges using unspecified means.
bugs.conditions: iControl REST users with non-admin privileges configured
bugs.impact: A lower privileged iControl REST user may be able to gain higher privilege using unspecified means
bugs.fix: Privilege levels now properly enforced in iControl REST.

bugs.title: Support of Microsoft Identity 2.0 platform
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP does not support Template for Microsoft Identity Platform 2.0.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered if you want to use Template for Microsoft Identity Platform 2.0 as an identity provider.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure Microsoft Identity Platform 2.0 on BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: OAuth provider has a custom template which provides the ability to configure and discover using new endpoints.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing FPS traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash will processing Fraud Protection Service traffic.
bugs.conditions: -BIG-IP Fraud Protection Service enabled.
bugs.impact: TMM crash, leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes FPS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: ASM processes some requests longer than usual
bugs.symptoms: ASM processes some requests longer than usual and can cause some latency when passing requests to the backend server.
bugs.conditions: Content profile parsing is enabled in ASM
bugs.impact: Latency can be noted when passing requests to the backend server
bugs.fix: ASM is processes requests as expected

bugs.title: Enabling APM debug logs can lead to leakage in file descriptors
bugs.symptoms: Cannot accept/create new connections or run access policies. Messages like the following appear in APM logs: err apmd[8655]: 01490000:3: HTTPParser.cpp func: "readFromSocket()" line: 110 Msg: epoll_create() failed [Too many open files].
bugs.conditions: Apm logs and enabled in debug mode.
bugs.impact: Apmd is unable to accept/create new connections and run access policies.
bugs.workaround: Restart apmd.

bugs.title: Tmm crash with ICAP filter
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Per-request policies configured. -- ICAP is configured. This is rare condition that occurs intermittently.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Log message with large wchan value
bugs.symptoms: A message is logged with a very large wchan (waiting channel, WCHAN :: Sleeping in Function) value that corresponds to -1 when read as signed instead of unsigned.
bugs.conditions: This happens in normal operation.
bugs.impact: The message is not accurately reporting the wchan value
bugs.workaround: Look at the /proc/PID/stack file for the correct wchan value.

bugs.title: [Win][EdgeClient] 'Enable Always Connected mode' is checked for all connectivity profiles with same Parent profile.
bugs.symptoms: The default value of 'Enable Always Connected' becomes enabled for connectivity profiles after adding 'Server List' to one of the connectivity profiles with the same Parent profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Add 'Server List' to one of the connectivity profiles with the same Parent profile. -- Enable the 'Always Connected mode' setting for one of the connectivity profiles.
bugs.impact: This change affects all of the connectivity profiles. The parent-child inheritance logic is broken.
bugs.workaround: Manually uncheck the setting in all new profiles where 'Enable Always Connected' is not needed.

bugs.title: Application Security Administrator role cannot create parent policy in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, for the Application Security Administrator role, when you create a new ASM policy, the Policy Type is greyed out and the parent policy cannot be created
bugs.conditions: -- Create user account with the Application Security Administrator user role. -- Use that account to logon to the GUI and try to create/edit the parent policy.
bugs.impact: The following actions are restricted to accounts with roles Application Security Administrator: -- Create/Edit parent policy. -- Edit Inheritance Settings for parent policy. -- Clone Policy, selecting policy type is disabled.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Have the Administrator or Resource Administrator create a parent policy instead of the Application Security Administrator. -- Create parent policy using tmsh or REST call.
bugs.fix: The Application Security Administrator role can now create the parent policy when required.

bugs.title: Access-Control-Allow-Origin header with trailing white spaces causes Portal Access CORS failure.
bugs.symptoms: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header value may contain trailing white spaces in very rare cases, for example: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://example.com \r\n In this case, Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) validation may fail if the 'Origin' header value contains the same value as that of 'Access_Control_Allow_Origin', but without trailing white spaces, for example: Origin: http://example.com\r\n If CORS validation fails, content on the browser gets blocked.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Origin' header and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header values match except for the trailing white space. -- Using Portal Access to access the resource.
bugs.impact: Web application content gets blocked on the browser when accessed through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to truncate trailing white space from 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' headers.
bugs.fix: Now, content does not get blocked if 'Origin' header and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header values match except for trailing white space.

bugs.title: Cookies set in the URI on Safari
bugs.symptoms: When Bot Defense performs a 307 Redirect, the cookie is set on the URL if Bot Defense detects the Safari browser.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is attached to virtual server. -- 'Browser Verification' set to 'Verify Before Access' or 'Verify After Access'. -- 'Cross Domain Requests' set to 'Validate Upon Request'. -- Surfing on Safari browser to a related domain.
bugs.impact: A cookie is set on the URL.
bugs.fix: A new db variable has been added, botdefense.safari_redirect_no_cookie_mode, to allow you to control whether the cookie is added to the URL.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP systems now have an option to set the cookie using a set-cookie header in the response and not save it as part of the URL. This is done by a new BigDB variable: tmsh modify botdefense.safari_redirect_no_cookie_mode value disable Default value is the original behavior (enable), which sets the cookie in the URl. NOTE: If the site is using iFrames, changing this BigDB variable might cause the cookie to be ignored and therefore for requests to be blocked.

bugs.title: The GTM/DNS HTTPS monitor may fail to mark a service up when the SSL session undergoes an unclean shutdown.
bugs.symptoms: The GTM/DNS HTTPS monitor may fail to find the configured receive string in a HTTP response, causing the monitored service to be incorrectly marked down.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are true: -- The server being monitored performs an unclean shutdown of the SSL session (the underlying TCP connection is closed without first issuing a close notify alert at the SSL level). -- The server's HTTP response does not terminate with a newline.
bugs.impact: A service is incorrectly marked down. This can cause the BIG-IP GTM/DNS to return a suboptimal answer or no answer at all to DNS queries.
bugs.workaround: This issue can be worked around by performing any one of the following actions: -- Ensure the server issues a close notify alert before it closes the underlying TCP connection. -- Ensure the server's HTTP response ends with a newline.
bugs.fix: The GTM/DNS HTTPS monitor no longer fails when the SSL peer performs an unclean shutdown.

bugs.title: GUI Network Map icons color scheme is not section 508 compliant
bugs.symptoms: Network Map color scheme is not compliant with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (section 508). There is no clear difference between a green/active node and the blue/square items. With the new system colors and flat shapes, the icons are nearly identical. Other than shape (circle vs. square), the new colors appear identical; the blue and green are nearly appearing as one color.
bugs.conditions: Accessing Network Map from GUI via Local Traffic :: Network Map.
bugs.impact: There is no clear color difference between a green/active node icon and the blue/square icon.
bugs.fix: Modified the color codes. Now the Network Map icons color scheme is section 508 compliant.

bugs.title: Slow Ramp does not take into account pool members' ratio weights
bugs.symptoms: When a pool member is within its slow-ramp period, and is a member of a pool that uses a static-ratio-based load balancing algorithm, its ratio weight is not taken into account when balancing connections to it. If it has a ratio that is higher than other pool members, this can result in a sudden influx of connections once the pool member exits the slow-ramp period.
bugs.conditions: -- Pool with a non-zero slow-ramp timeout and a static-ratio-based load balancing algorithm. -- Pool members within the pool have different ratio weights. -- At least one pool member is inside its slow-ramp period.
bugs.impact: The pool member could still be overwhelmed despite the attempt to slow-ramp connections to it.
bugs.fix: Ratio weights are now taken into account for pool members.

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator resets subsequent requests when HTTP services are being used.
bugs.symptoms: When connections are reused for subsequent requests, the subsequent requests might get aborted with reset cause 'connector service reconnected'.
bugs.conditions: SSL Orchestrator with HTTP services and multiple requests in a connection.
bugs.impact: Subsequent requests might get aborted with reset cause 'connector service reconnected'.
bugs.fix: SSL Orchestrator no longer aborts subsequent requests in the same connection.

bugs.title: BIG-IP i15600 / i15800 does not monitor all tmm processes for heartbeat failures
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP device has more than 24 tmm instances and one of the tmm processes above the 24th cpu loops (e.g., in response to an internal issue), it loops indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP i15600 / i15800 platforms. -- Another issue occurs that that causes a tmm process greater than the 24th tmm process to loop.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted on the tmm process that is looping indefinitely.
bugs.workaround: 1. Manually change /defaults/daemon.conf to include the appropriate tmm number and respective heartbeat action if the supported tmm is not listed. Note: The change does not persist across software installs. a. mount -o remount,rw /usr b. Edit /defaults/daemon.conf and put these contents at the top of the file: sys daemon-ha tmm24 { description none heartbeat enabled heartbeat-action go-offline-downlinks-restart running enabled running-timeout 2 } sys daemon-ha tmm25 { description none heartbeat enabled heartbeat-action go-offline-downlinks-restart running enabled running-timeout 2 } sys daemon-ha tmm26 { description none heartbeat enabled heartbeat-action go-offline-downlinks-restart running enabled running-timeout 2 } sys daemon-ha tmm27 { description none heartbeat enabled heartbeat-action go-offline-downlinks-restart running enabled running-timeout 2 } c. mount -o remount,ro /usr 2. After performing the edit, load the changes into the running configuration via 'tmsh load sys config partitions all'. 3. Verify that sod is now correctly monitoring tmm instances above tmm24 using a command such as: tmsh show sys ha-status all-properties | grep "daemon-heartbeat" | grep tmm

bugs.title: Under certain conditions, deleting a topology record can result in a crash.
bugs.symptoms: During a topology load balancing decision, TMM can crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Topology records are deleted. -- A load balancing decision using topology load balancing occurs.
bugs.impact: On very rare occasions, TMM can crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Topology record changes are now done in a way that prevents the possibility of TMM crashing when making load balancing decisions in which the record is used.

bugs.title: Wide IP alias validation error during sync or config load
bugs.symptoms: DB validation exception occurs during GTM config sync or config load: 01070734:3: Configuration error: DB validation exception, unique constraint violation on table (gtm_wideip_alias) object ID (1 /Common/alias.test.com www.test.com). A duplicate value was received for a non-primary key unique index field. DB exception text (Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:gtm_wideip_alias status:13) Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- A wideip alias is moved from one wideip to another -- GTM sync occurs, or a gtm config is loaded manually. This issue can occur any time a GTM config is loaded or synchronised where the new configuration has a wideip with an alias, which is already configured on a different wideip in the existing in-memory GTM configuration.
bugs.impact: You are unable to load config or full sync from peer GNS/GTM.
bugs.workaround: Follow this procedure: 1. Delete the wide IP alias on the destination device. 2. Try the sync or load config operation again.

bugs.title: Exception at rewritten Element.innerHTML=''
bugs.symptoms: If the "href" attribute of an anchor tag in a web application does not have any value, an exception will be thrown.
bugs.conditions: -- Rewrite enabled -- The href attribute of an anchor tag on a web page does not have a value, for example:
bugs.impact: Web page does not load properly.
bugs.workaround: Find the "href" attributes of anchor tag and give some empty value to it: Before: After:
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with rewrite of anchors that contain an empty href attribute.

bugs.title: PCCD restart loop when using more than 256 FQDN entries in Firewall Rules
bugs.symptoms: PCCD enters a restart loop, until the configuration is changed such that 256 or fewer FQDN entries are in use. Errors are reported to the terminal screen: pccd[23494]: 015d0000:0: pccd encountered a fatal error and will be restarted shortly...
bugs.conditions: Greater than 256 FQDN entries are in use in Firewall Rules.
bugs.impact: PCCD goes into a restart loop. PCCD is not functional until there are 256 or fewer entries.
bugs.workaround: Use 256 or fewer FQDN entries in Firewall Rules. To aid in the removal of extra rules when using tmsh, you can prevent PCCD restart messages from flooding the console: 1. Stop PCCD to halt the restart messages: bigstart stop pccd 2. Modify the configuration. 3. Bring PCCD back up: bigstart start pccd
bugs.fix: PCCD restart loop no longer occurs when using more than 256 FQDN entries in Firewall Rules.

bugs.title: NetHSM install scripts - remove references to fipskey.nethsm
bugs.symptoms: Fipskey.nethsm is deprecated However, when running the nethsm-[safenet/thales]-install script, the script logs a reference to fipskey.nethsm
bugs.conditions: Shows the following statements during the installation: Successfully set SafeNet HSM for use with 'fipskey.nethsm'. <==== > Registering SafeNet HSM in the BIG-IP config ... > Setting Thales HSM for use with 'fipskey.nethsm' ... <==== > Registering Thales HSM in BIG-IP config ...
bugs.impact: Could create a confusion since fipskey.nethsm is no longer supported.
bugs.fix: Removed the reference to fipskey.nethsm from the install scripts.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP ASM system may not properly perform signature checks on cookies
bugs.symptoms: For more information, please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K88162221
bugs.conditions: For more information, please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K88162221
bugs.impact: For more information, please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K88162221
bugs.workaround: For more information, please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K88162221
bugs.fix: For more information, please see: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K88162221

bugs.title: Live Update: Update Available notification is shown twice in rare conditions
bugs.symptoms: When entering Live Update page, sometimes Update Available notification is shown twice.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered on the first load of the Live Update page.
bugs.impact: Notification is shown twice.
bugs.fix: Notification is shown only once in all cases.

bugs.title: Guest fails to come up when vCMP guest and host both run BIG-IP v13.1.3.3, assigning FIPS partition
bugs.symptoms: The vCMP guest fails to come up.
bugs.conditions: -- Using i5820-DF, i7820-DF, or 10350v-F platforms. -- Running BIG-IP software v13.1.3.3 on the hypervisor. -- Once FIPS card is initialized on the hypervisor: 1. Create vCMP guest. 2. Assign FIPS partition (can be default PARTITION_1, or you can resize PARTITION_1 and create a different partition). 3. Change state of vCMP guest to 'deployed'.
bugs.impact: The vCMP guest fails to come up with an attached N3FIPS partition. Note: This happens only when the host is running v13.1.3.3 and the vCMP guest tries to come up with v13.1.3.3.

bugs.title: Request adapt and response adapt profile options should not be available in the GUI when ICAP is not licensed
bugs.symptoms: The Request Adapt Profile and Response Adapt Profile settings are visible when creating or editing a virtual server in the GUI on systems that do not have ICAP licensed. If these profiles are configured, traffic does not pass through the virtual server and the following error is reported in /var/log/ltm: crit tmm[3328]: 01010022:2: ICAP feature not licensed
bugs.conditions: -- ICAP is not licensed. -- At least one virtual server has been configured with a Request Adapt Profile and/or a Response Adapt Profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic does not pass through the affected virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Remove any configured Request Adapt Profiles and Response Adapt Profiles from virtual servers.

bugs.title: NETHSM installation script hardening
bugs.symptoms: The nethsm-safenet-install.sh script does not follow current best practices when installing the Safenet NETHSM.
bugs.conditions: -Installation of the Safenet NETHSM
bugs.impact: The nethsm-safenet-install.sh script does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: The nethsm-safenet-install.sh script now follows current best practices when installing the Safenet NETHSM.

bugs.title: TMM can crash while passing VPN traffic
bugs.symptoms: While passing VPN traffic, tmm crashes
bugs.conditions: -- APM configured and passing VPN traffic
bugs.impact: Under certain timing conditions, tmm can crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: GTP::ie count does not work with -message option
bugs.symptoms: The 'GTP::ie count' iRule command does not work with the -message option. The command fails with an error: wrong # args: should be "-type <ie-path>"
bugs.conditions: Issue the 'GTP::ie count' command with -message command, for example: GTP::ie count -message $m -type apn
bugs.impact: iRules fails and it could cause connection abort.
bugs.workaround: Swap order of argument by moving -message to the end, for example: GTP::ie count -type apn -message $m There is a warning message due to iRules validation, but the command works in runtime.
bugs.fix: 'GTP::ie' count is now working with -message option.

bugs.title: Appliance mode is not working on BIG-IP 14.1.x tenant deployed on VELOS.
bugs.symptoms: Appliance mode does not enable on BIG-IP 14.1.x tenants deployed on VELOS.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP 14.1.3 tenant is deployed on VELOS with Appliance Mode enabled.
bugs.impact: The appliance mode restriction is not working as expected. The root account still has bash access.
bugs.fix: Appliance mode will now function when configured on a BIG-IP tenant deployed on VELOS.

bugs.title: NSM consumes 100% CPU processing nexthops for recursive ECMP routes
bugs.symptoms: The NSM process might enter a state where it gets stuck at 100% CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: ECMP routes reachable via recursive nexthops.
bugs.impact: NSM is stuck at 100% CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using EMCP routes reachable via recursive nexthops.

bugs.title: iControl REST hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions iControl REST does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: - Authenticated administrative user - iControl REST requests
bugs.impact: iControl REST does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: iControl REST now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: Extend AFM subscriber aware policy rule feature to support multiple subscriber groups
bugs.symptoms: Currently AFM does not have support to match rules against multiple subscriber policies
bugs.conditions: -- AFM provisioned -- You wish to match rules against multiple subscriber policies
bugs.impact: AFM rules cannot be matched against multiple subscriber policies
bugs.fix: Enhancing the AFM rules matching against multiple subscriber policies

bugs.title: Disallow adding Request Adapt Profiles and Response Adapt Profiles to virtual servers in TMSH when ICAP is not licensed
bugs.symptoms: If ICAP is not licensed, the system does not prevent you from adding Request Adapt Profiles and Response Adapt Profiles to virtual servers in the CLI. If these profiles are configured, traffic does not pass through the virtual server and the following error is reported in /var/log/ltm: crit tmm[3328]: 01010022:2: ICAP feature not licensed
bugs.conditions: -- ICAP is not licensed. -- At least one virtual server has been configured with a Request Adapt Profile and/or a Response Adapt Profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic does not pass through the affected virtual servers.
bugs.workaround: Remove any configured Request Adapt Profiles and Response Adapt Profiles from virtual servers.

bugs.title: A dwbld core on configuration changes on IP Intelligence policy
bugs.symptoms: A dwbld core occurs on configuration changes on IP Intelligence policy.
bugs.conditions: Configuration changes on IP Intelligence policy with assigned feed-list.
bugs.impact: A dwbld restart. Enforcement of dynamic white/black configuration does not occur while dwbld restarts.
bugs.fix: Feed-list entries should not be present in list of entries with expiration.

bugs.title: GTM/DNS monitors based on the TCP protocol may fail to mark a service up when the server's response spans multiple packets.
bugs.symptoms: GTM/DNS monitors based on the TCP protocol may fail to find the configured receive string in the server's response, causing the monitored service to be incorrectly marked down.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the server's response spans multiple packets (for example, when the response is particularly large or includes dynamically generated content delivered in chunks).
bugs.impact: A service is incorrectly marked down. This can cause the BIG-IP GTM/DNS to return a suboptimal answer or no answer at all to DNS queries.
bugs.workaround: This issue can be worked around by ensuring your server returns a response to the BIG-IP GTM/DNS's monitor that fits in one packet.
bugs.fix: GTM/DNS monitors based on the TCP protocol no longer fail when the server's response spans multiple packets.

bugs.title: CSV files downloaded from the Dashboard have the first row with all 'NaN
bugs.symptoms: In the Dashboard .csv file, all of the values in the first row are set to 'NaN'
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when loading the downloaded Dashboard .csv files with historical data from the GUI.
bugs.impact: The first row of the downloaded .csv from Dashboard shows all the values as 'NaN'.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with 'NaN' being reported in the first line of the downloaded dashboard .csv files.

bugs.title: AVRD may crash while processing Bot Defense traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the AVRD application on BIG-IP may crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense Profile is attached to the virtual server. -- Mobile SDK is licensed and enabled.
bugs.impact: Instability in the avrd process. Statistics data can be lost.
bugs.fix: AVRD now processes Bot Defense traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Tunnel Static Forwarding Table does not show entries per page
bugs.symptoms: On the Network :: Tunnels page of the GUI, if the Tunnel Static Forwarding Table contains more than one page of data, you are unable to advance past the first page.
bugs.conditions: Tunnel Static Forwarding Table contains a large number of configured tunnels.
bugs.impact: The content displayed on screen and does not conform to the system preference for Records Per Screen.

bugs.title: A TCP connection is not closed after invoking the HTTP::respond iRule command.
bugs.symptoms: After sending a HTTP response that would normally cause the underlying TCP connection to get closed, the BIG-IP system fails to close the TCP connection.
bugs.conditions: - TCP profile is used. - HTTP profile is used. - HTTP::respond iRule command is used. - The HTTP filter sets the "Connection: close" header (for example, in response to a HTTP/1.0 request that does not request Keep-Alive behavior).
bugs.impact: The TCP connection lives longer than needed, and even allows the client to send subsequent requests over the same connection.
bugs.fix: TCP connection is now closed as necessary after invoking the HTTP::respond iRule command.

bugs.title: File permission errors during bot-signature installation
bugs.symptoms: When you install Bot-Sig IM file through LU, /var/log/ltm shows file permission errors. Cannot open lock file (/var/run/config_lock), permission denied. Cannot open command history file (/root/.tmsh-history-root), Permission denied : framework/CmdHistoryFile.cpp, line 92.
bugs.conditions: Installing bot-signature.
bugs.impact: If the BIG-IP device is rebooted, or the mcpd process is restarted, following an automatic bot-signature installation, without the config first being saved, the bot-signature installation will be reverted.
bugs.workaround: Save the BIG-IP configuration manually after the automatic bot-signature update has completed.

bugs.title: TMM does not follow TCP best practices
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, on specific platforms, TMM does not follow best practices for TCP connections.
bugs.conditions: -- Platforms without HW based syn-cookie capability. -- System DB variable connection.syncookies.algorithm value is set to "hardware."
bugs.impact: TMM does not follow best practices for TCP connections.
bugs.workaround: Set 'sys db connection.syncookies.algorithm value' to "software".
bugs.fix: TMM now follows best practices for TCP connections.

bugs.title: Live Update default factory file for Server Technologies cannot be reinstalled
bugs.symptoms: Live Update default factory file for Server Technologies cannot be reinstalled once it is no longer the currently installed update file.
bugs.conditions: This occurs: -- Once another update file for Server Technologies has been installed (most likely, a newer file). -- If the device has been upgraded from a prior release such that the currently installed Server Technologies file is from the previous release, and is not the default factory file for the current release.
bugs.impact: Live Update default factory file for Server Technologies cannot be reinstalled.

bugs.title: Brute force mitigation can stop mitigating without a notification
bugs.symptoms: A brute force attack coming from an entity (such as an IP address, etc.) may be stopped prematurely.
bugs.conditions: -- Many brute force attacks are happening at once, coming from many sources. -- Distributed attack is not detected (due to configuration).
bugs.impact: At some point, an entity might not be mitigated due to the sheer number of mitigated entities. When this occurs, there is no notification.

bugs.title: Rate shaping might suppress TCP RST
bugs.symptoms: When rate shaping is configured, the system might suppress TCP RSTs issued by itself.
bugs.conditions: Rate shaping is configured.
bugs.impact: The rate-shaping instance drops TCP RSTs; the endpoint is not informed about the ungraceful shutdown.
bugs.workaround: Do not use rate-shaping.
bugs.fix: TCP RSTs are no longer dropped by the rate-shaping instance.

bugs.title: TMM may crash if a virtual server undergoes a series of specific configuration changes involving the transparent-nexthop option.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and produces a core dump.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when: - You initially enable the transparent-nexthop setting on a virtual server. - You then disable the option. - You then disable auto-lasthop for the virtual server. - The virtual server receives traffic.
bugs.impact: Traffic is impacted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround that you can instantiate to prevent this issue. However, if you are aware that you have already performed the necessary configuration changes to cause this issue to occur, and TMM has not crashed yet, you can delete the virtual server and recreate it (with the intended/final configuration) to prevent the crash.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes after modifying a virtual server as described under Conditions.

bugs.title: WS::disconnect may result in TMM crash under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: The WebSocket profile allows use of the WS::disconnect iRule command to gracefully terminate a connection with a client or a server. Use of this command may result in crash if tmm parts the iRule before execution completes.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP has a virtual server configured with a WebSocket profile. -- An iRule the includes the WS::disconnect command is attached to the virtual server. -- BIG-IP is under heavy load and/or the iRule requires an extended time to execute, which might happen, for example, during execution on an iRule, tmm might park the iRule execution because the operation takes more CPU cycle than tmm can allocate to complete the iRule execution.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Unnecessarily high number of JavaScript Obfuscator instances when device is busy
bugs.symptoms: When the device has high CPU or I/O rate, it can cause the JavaScript Obfuscator to run multiple times simultaneously, causing even higher CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM/DoS/FPS are provisioned. -- BIG-IP device is experiencing a high CPU or I/O rate.
bugs.impact: High CPU Usage.
bugs.fix: The system now avoids creating multiple JavaScript Obfuscator processes.

bugs.title: Standby device name sent in Traffic Statistics syslog/Splunk messages
bugs.symptoms: 'Traffic Statistics' syslog/Splunk messages are sent with the hostname of the standby device.
bugs.conditions: When a virtual server is configured with a security logging profile enabled for DoS Protection logging.
bugs.impact: 'Traffic Statistics' syslog/Splunk messages show the wrong hostname. It should show the active device hostname.
bugs.fix: Corrected Traffic Statistics syslog/Splunk messages to show the hostname of the active instead of the standby device in logging messages.

bugs.title: REST GET on /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-key returns bad/wrong passphrase
bugs.symptoms: GET request on REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-key returns the incorrect value for passphrase.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when getting the ssl-key information, and the key contains a passphrase. -- Using BIG-IP v14.1.2.5 or v14.1.2.6 to deploy Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
bugs.impact: Passphrase value is incorrect. Autoscale AWS deployments fail when trying to deploy a BIG-IP v14.1.2.5 or v14.1.2.6 AMI. This is the result of a change in how ssl-key passphrases are being returned in REST calls.
bugs.fix: Can now deploy from BIG-IP v14.1.2.5 or v14.1.2.6 AMI when using passphrase from a GET request on REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/sys/file/ssl-key.

bugs.title: Rate Shaping Rate Class 'Queue Method' and 'Drop Policy' defaults are incorrect in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: When creating a Rate Shaping Rate Class in the GUI, the default values for 'Queue Method' and 'Drop Policy' are not correct.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a Rate Shaping Rate Class in the GUI. -- Leaving 'Queue Method' and 'Drop Policy' settings as their defaults.
bugs.impact: Unexpected values in the configuration: 'Queue Method' is 'sfq' and 'Drop Policy' is 'tail'.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Manually set the 'Queue Method' and 'Drop Policy' when creating a Rate Shaping Rate Class object. These settings are available in the 'Advanced' view of the 'General Properties' section. 'Queue Method' should be 'pfifo' and 'Drop Policy' should be 'fred'. -- Use TMSH to create Rate Shaping Rate Class objects.

bugs.title: Incorrect values in 'Class Attribute' in Radius-Acct STOP request
bugs.symptoms: 'Class Attribute' value in the Radius-Acct STOP request from the BIG-IP APM system does not match the 'Class Attribute' value in the Radius-Acct START request from the RADIUS server.
bugs.conditions: -- Access policy is configured with RADIUS Acct VPE item to send accounting messages to RADIUS server when users log on and off.
bugs.impact: RADIUS server does not log accounting information properly.
bugs.workaround: This workaround textually describes reconfiguring an access policy in the Visual Policy Editor (VPE). Descriptions may not be as straightforward as in regular GUI workarounds. This is a description of the visual layout of the policy: Start --+-- Logon Page --+-- RADIUS Auth --+-- RADIUS Acct --+-- Variable Assign (1) --+-- Advanced Resource Assign --+-- Variable Assign --+-- Allow 1. Decode the class attribute and save it in a temporary variable: -- Click Variable Assign (1); in the two sub-areas, enter the following: temp.radius.last.attr.class.decoded expr { [mcget -decode {session.radius.last.attr.class}] } 2. Copy the temporary variable into the class session var: -- Click Variable Assign; in the two sub-areas, enter the following: session.radius.last.attr.class, expr { [mcget {temp.radius.last.attr.class.decoded}] } In this way, when you log out, and APM sends the RADIUS Stop accounting message, it uses the decoded value that is saved in the session.radius.last.attr.class variable.

bugs.title: Changing a virtual server type in the GUI may change some options; changing back to the original type does not restore original values
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI if you change a virtual server from one type to another, there may be changes automatically applied to some of the settings. If you change the type back to its original value, those changes remain, and are saved when you click Update.
bugs.conditions: -- Modifying a virtual server from one type to another, and then changing it back to the original type. -- Clicking Update.
bugs.impact: Unexpected configuration changes, which can lead to unexpected behavior of the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: To prevent unwanted changes, when you change a virtual server's type and then change it back within the same session, click Cancel instead of Update.

bugs.title: UDP commands in iRules executed during FLOW_INIT event fail
bugs.symptoms: UDP commands in iRules executed during FLOW_INIT event fail.
bugs.conditions: An iRule that contains UDP commands is executed on the FLOW_INIT event.
bugs.impact: UDP commands in iRules executed during FLOW_INIT event fail.
bugs.fix: UDP PCB is initialized before FLOW_INIT.

bugs.title: Wide IP operations performed in quick succession result in missing resource records and out of sync journals.
bugs.symptoms: Two issues occur with Wide IP operations performed in quick succession: 1. DNS Zone syncing is missing resource records. 2. In some cases it throws named/zrd error: journal rollforward failed: journal out of sync with zone.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur when a large number of configuration changes, including Wide IP changes, are made simultaneously on multiple GTM/DNS devices in a sync group.
bugs.impact: DNS resource records can be missing from the BIND DNS database. The impact of this issue is that if GSLB Load Balancing falls back to BIND, the DNS resource records may not be present. Manually remove the .jnl files in order to restore named/zrd on all GTMs.
bugs.workaround: Restrict configuration (Wide IP) changes to one GTM/DNS device in a device group. Note: It is also possible to turn off zone syncing. GTM/DNS configuration is still synced, but you lose the ability to sync non-Wide IP changes to the BIND DB. If you do not use ZoneRunner to add additional non-Wide IP records, this is only a problem when GSLB resorts fallback to BIND. This can be mitigated with DNSX and DNS (off device) for non Wide IP Resource Records. Manually remove the .jnl files in order to restore named/zrd on all GTMs.

bugs.title: GUI banner for configuration issues frozen after repeated forced VIPRION blade failover
bugs.symptoms: Repeatedly forcing VIPRION blade failover can cause the GUI to get stuck displaying: This device is not operational because the loaded configuration contained errors or unlicensed objects. Please adjust the configuration and/or the license, and re-license the device. Examination of the configuration and license shows that there are no configuration errors or unlicensed configuration objects. Failover occurs as expected, and the device is operational.
bugs.conditions: Repeatedly forcing blade failover triggers this issue, with commands such as the following issued in rapid succession: - tmsh modify sys cluster default members { 2 { disabled } } - tmsh modify sys cluster default members { 2 { enabled } } - tmsh modify sys cluster default members { 1 { disabled } } - tmsh modify sys cluster default members { 1 { enabled } }
bugs.impact: The GUI continuously displays the banner the device-not-operational banner. However, the device is operational.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds to return the GUI to normal operation: -- Restart mcpd by running the following command: bigstart restart mcpd -- Reboot the VIPRION system.

bugs.title: Devices incorrectly report 'In Sync' after an incremental sync
bugs.symptoms: The security policies assigned to a virtual server are different among the devices in a traffic-group.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Manual Sync Active-Standby Failover Device Group with ASM sync enabled. -- An L7 ASM security policy is manually changed on a virtual server (not using the ASM wizard).
bugs.impact: After incremental sync, devices report 'In Sync' but there is a configuration discrepancy in the security policy assigned to the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Modify the underlying LTM policy to be 'legacy': # tmsh modify ltm policy <LTM Policy Name> legacy
bugs.fix: An internal config parameter is now available to work around this issue. In order to use the workaround, you must enable a db variable. To enable the workaround, run the following command from the CLI on every device in the device group: ------------------------------------ # /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add force_legacy_ltm_policy 1 Operation completed successfully. Don't forget to restart ASM to apply changes. ------------------------------------ NOTE: In this specific case, ASM restart is not required, despite the fact that a message says it is.
bugs.behavior: There is now an internal config parameter that enables a workaround for this issue. In order to use the workaround, you must enable a db variable. To enable the workaround, run the following command from the CLI on every device in the device group: ------------------------------------ # /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add force_legacy_ltm_policy 1 Operation completed successfully. Don't forget to restart ASM to apply changes. ------------------------------------ NOTE: In this specific case, ASM restart is not required, despite the fact that a message says it is.

bugs.title: After provisioning change, pfmand might keep interfaces down on particular platforms
bugs.symptoms: After a provisioning change, pfmand might keep interfaces down.
bugs.conditions: -- Provisioning change on the following platforms: + i850 + i2600 / i2800 + i4600 / i4800 + 2000- and 4000-series -- Link Down Time on Failover configured to a non-zero value (the default is '10').
bugs.impact: Interfaces remain DOWN.
bugs.workaround: Follow this procedure: 1. Set db failover.standby.linkdowntime to '0'. 2. To bring interfaces UP again, restart pfmand: bigstart restart pfmand

bugs.title: BIG-IP systems not responding to DPD requests from initiator after failover
bugs.symptoms: After failover, the active BIG-IP system fails to respond to DPD requests from some of its eNB neighbors, which results in deletion of IKE tunnel peer as well as the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP is configured with more than 300 IKE/IPsec tunnels. -- The BIG-IP system fails over.
bugs.impact: Since BIG-IP systems do not respond to DPD requests, eNB deletes the IKE tunnel after a few retries.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with the BIG-IP system not responding to DPD requests after failover.

bugs.title: Neurond cores while adding or deleting rules
bugs.symptoms: Neurond cores if it receives error while adding or deleting rules in neuron hardware.
bugs.conditions: Adding or deleting rules in neuron hardware
bugs.impact: Neurond cores

bugs.title: Tmm crash with iRule and a PEM Policy with BWC Enabled
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes while passing traffic through PEM.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM policy with bandwidth controller. -- iRule makes a traffic decision based on certain unique PEM sessions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: After applying static bandwidth controller on a virtual server, any changes to the virtual server disassociates the BWC policy
bugs.symptoms: All Bandwidth Controller (BWC) stats are 0 (zero) even though traffic is passing.
bugs.conditions: -- A BWC policy is attached to a virtual server. -- The virtual server with the attached BWC policy is modified.
bugs.impact: The system disassociates the BWC policy from the virtual server. Traffic is no longer throttled according to the policy rules.
bugs.workaround: To reattach the policy, detach the Bandwidth Controller policy from the virtual server, and then reapply it.

bugs.title: Wrong error message upon bad credential stuffing configuration
bugs.symptoms: When you try to configure credential stuffing and provide invalid parameters, you see a misleading error: HTML Tag-like Content in the Request URL/Body
bugs.conditions: Configuration of bad ApplicationID, Access Token or wrong service type, generates a validation error, but the error message is confusing.
bugs.impact: A misleading error is displayed.
bugs.fix: Wrong error message upon bad credential stuffing configuration has been corrected.

bugs.title: ASM processes some web-sockets requests longer than usual
bugs.symptoms: ASM processes some web-socket requests longer than usual and can cause some latency when passing requests to the backend server.
bugs.conditions: Content profile parsing is enabled in ASM.
bugs.impact: Latency can be noted when passing web-socket requests to the backend server.
bugs.fix: ASM is processes web-socket requests as expected

bugs.title: SSL client and SSL server profile names truncated in GUI
bugs.symptoms: Unable to see the full name of the SSL client and SSL server profiles when assigning them in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: In Local Traffic :: Virtual Server :: Properties, the fields for the 'Selected' and 'Available' lists are narrower than they were in previous versions.
bugs.impact: With longer SSL profile names, the full name is not visible. Even the default, provided profiles, such as crypto-server-default-clientssl and crypto-client-default-serverssl, are truncated. Note: The fields remain at the limited width even when the browser window is maximized.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to see the full SSL client and SSL server name.

bugs.title: IKE-SA on standby deleted due to re-transmit failure when failing over from active to standby
bugs.symptoms: IKE-SAs are deleted on standby BIG-IP systems after a failover.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) environment -- Dead-peer detection (DPD) / liveness checks are enabled -- An HA failover occurs This is a timing issue and can occur intermittently during a normal failover.
bugs.impact: Some of the IKE-SAs are missing on the standby device. When a failover happens, IPsec traffic will be dropped for those missing SAs.
bugs.workaround: Set IKE DPD interval time to ZERO (i.e., disable).
bugs.fix: When the BIG-IP system is in standby mode, the system no longer retries sending IKE/IPSEC control messages, which prevents this issue from occurring.

bugs.title: Signature verification for logs fails if the log files are modified during log rotation
bugs.symptoms: Rotated log files that are modified immediately after log rotation and before signature generation can cause signature verification failure.
bugs.conditions: -- Log integrity feature is enabled. -- A log rotation event occurs
bugs.impact: Signature verification may fail on rotated log files.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with signature verification failing on valid log files.

bugs.title: iRule support to get/set UDP's Maximum Buffer Packets
bugs.symptoms: UDP profiles have a setting to set the Maximum Buffer Packets for UDP connections. This value cannot be modified with an iRule.
bugs.conditions: -- UDP profile is used. -- You need to dynamically change the max buffer packets setting in an iRule.
bugs.impact: Unable to dynamically change the max buffer packets setting in an iRule.
bugs.fix: You can now dynamically change the max buffer packets setting in an iRule. The setting is UDP::max_buf_pkts
bugs.behavior: A new iRule command has been added, UDP::max_buf_pkts. This allows you to dynamically override the maximum number of packets setting in the UDP profile.

bugs.title: MR_INGRESS iRules that change diameter messages corrupt diam_msg
bugs.symptoms: -- 'DIAMETER::host origin' command may not be set correctly. There are errors in ltm/log: err tmm[18562]: 014c0001:3: DIAMETER: hud_diam_handle error: Not found
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server is configured with a diameter profile enabled with an ingress iRule, for example: ltm rule Diameter - iRule { when MR_INGRESS { DIAMETER:: host origin "hostname.realm.example" } } -- Traffic arrives containing CER and ULR messages.
bugs.impact: Using the iRule to change the host origin corrupts the diameter message.

bugs.title: Health monitors may fail when the HTTP RFC Compliance option is enabled in a dual BIG-IP setup.
bugs.symptoms: With the HTTP RFC enforcement profile option enabled, incoming health monitor requests without an HTTP version in the request line (HTTP/0.9) may fail to produce the correct result for dual BIG-IP configurations. This can result in incoming health monitor traffic being incorrectly blocked when traveling through a virtual server. These health monitors will be unable to provide the correct availability of the intended resource. The default HTTP and HTTPS monitors as well as any custom monitors with a missing HTTP version in their requests could see this issue.
bugs.conditions: A dual BIG-IP configuration may provisioned with the following considerations. -- One or more BIG-IP systems are in the network path for monitor traffic. -- The first BIG-IP system uses a health monitor that initiates a health check request (without an HTTP version) in the request line (HTTP/0.9) against a second BIG-IP system. -- The second (downstream) BIG-IP system has a virtual server that is the endpoint for the monitor. The virtual server is configured with an HTTP profile with the HTTP RFC Compliance profile option selected.
bugs.impact: Rather than receiving the correct health check result, the original BIG-IP system can fail to report whether the second BIG-IP is available.
bugs.workaround: You can use http_head_f5 monitor to perform health checks.

bugs.title: When certain sized payloads are gzipped, the resulting payload is chunked, incorrect, and is never delivered to the client due to missing end of chunk marker.
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP session initiated by curl hangs.
bugs.conditions: -- The problem occurs when the file to be compressed meets the following criteria: -- The following platforms with Intel QAT are affected: + B4450N (A114) + i4000 (C115) + i10000 (C116/C127) + i7000 (C118) + i5000 (C119) + i11000 (C123) + i11000 (C124) + i15000 (D116) -- File size to be compressed is less than compression.qat.dispatchsize. -- File size to be compressed is one of specific numbers from this list: 65535, 32768, 16384, 8192, 4096.
bugs.impact: Connection hangs, times out, and resets.
bugs.workaround: Use software compression.
bugs.fix: The HTTP session hang no longer occurs.

bugs.title: The gtmd process does not receive updates from local big3d.
bugs.symptoms: Oversized server.crt file causes gtmd (other devices in a same syncgroup) from receiving from local big3d.
bugs.conditions: One GTM/DNS device in the syncgroup has an oversized server.crt file (approximately 4000 or larger) and sends a client cert direct message to peer GTM/DNS devices.
bugs.impact: The gtmd process marks resources down unexpectedly and does not receive persist updates.
bugs.workaround: 1. For each GTM/DNS device, use bigip_add to add all BIG-IP servers configured in bigip_gtm.conf file. 2. Restart each GTM/DNS that is affected.

bugs.title: The certs extend function does not work for GTM/DNS sync group
bugs.symptoms: When GTM/DNS systems in the same sync group receive the error 'SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:tlsv1 alert unknown ca', these systems cannot automatically connect to BIG-IP devices with which that GTM/DNS device has not already exchanged a SSL cert. As part of normal functionality, when one GTM/DNS tries to connect to a BIG-IP server and receives 'unknown ca' SSL error, if its peer GTM/DNS has already built a connection with that BIG-IP server, then the second GTM/DNS system should also be able to connect to that BIG-IP server automatically. But it cannot because of this issue. The problem exists only when the GTM/DNS device has not exchanged a cert with the BIG-IP server object, and there are two or more certs in /config/httpd/conf/ssl.crt/server.crt on that GTM/DNS device. You might see messages similar to the following: -- iqmgmt_ssl_connect: SSL error:14094418:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:tlsv1 alert unknown ca. -- err gtmd[28112]: 011ae0fa:3: iqmgmt_ssl_connect: SSL error: error:14094418:SSL routines:SSL3_READ_BYTES:tlsv1 alert unknown ca (336151576). -- notice gtmd[28112]: 011ae03d:5: Probe to 10.10.0.3: buffer = <direct><![CDATA[<clientcert><ip>10.10.0.10</ip><target_ip>10.10.0.6</target_ip><cert>....
bugs.conditions: -- /config/httpd/conf/ssl.crt/server.crt file with two or more certs on the requesting GTM/DNS device. -- Configuration is as follows: 1. GTMDNS1 and GTMDNS2 are in a same GTM/DNS sync group. 2. GTMDNS1 has a self-authorized CA cert. 3. You add a BIG-IP server that is is reachable but with which GTMDNS1 has not exchanged SSL certs.
bugs.impact: Certain GTM/DNS systems in the sync group cannot automatically connect to BIG-IP devices as expected. You must run additional bigip_add commands on those GTM/DNS systems in the GTM/DNS sync group to add the BIG-IP server.
bugs.workaround: Run bigip_add on each GTM/DNS server to add the configured BIG-IP servers.

bugs.title: Policy Signatures: updating a filtered list causes all signatures to be updated
bugs.symptoms: After making a change to a filtered list of signatures, ASM updates all signatures instead.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when applying changes to a filtered signatures list two or more times in rapid succession.
bugs.impact: All signatures may be updated without the intention to do so.
bugs.workaround: You can use either workaround: -- Apply the filter after each action. -- Reload the page

bugs.title: Deletion of bot-related ordered items via tmsh might cause errors when adding new items via GUI.
bugs.symptoms: When deleting (via tmsh) bot-related ordered list items like bot white-lists, bot-microservices, and bot-microservices URLs, an error occurs when adding and saving new items via GUI: Bot defense profile <profile full name> error: match-order should be unique.
bugs.conditions: 1.Create three items with consecutive match-orders values via tmsh, for example: three bot allow list items, the first with match-order 1, the second with match-order 2, and the third with match-order 3. 2. Delete item with the value: match-order 2 (in tmsh), and save. 3. Switch to the GUI, add new allow list item, and save.
bugs.impact: The system reports an error, and the bot configuration cannot be saved via GUI. However, dragging between items (and then dragging back) overcomes this error.
bugs.workaround: Drag between two items, and then drag back.
bugs.fix: Deletion of bot-related ordered items via tmsh no longer causes errors when adding new items via GUI.

bugs.title: Attack signature updates fail to install with Installation Error. &start;
bugs.symptoms: Installing a new Attack Signature Update (ASU) file on ASM/AWAF device that has large number of active policies can result in a failure due to memory exceptions. The following errors can be observed: /var/log/ts/asm_config_server.log: F5::ASMConfig::Handler::handle_error,,Code: 406 , Error message = Process size (232341504) has exceeded max size (200000000) /var/log/asm crit perl[19751]: 01310027:2: ASM subsystem error (apply_asm_attack_signatures ,F5::LiveUpdate::PayloadHandler::clean_fail): Fail load update files: TSocket: timed out reading 1024 bytes from n.n.n.n:9781
bugs.conditions: 1. Adding and activating a large number of policies on a BIG-IP system configured with ASM/AWAF. It is not known exactly how many policies are required to encounter this, but it appears to be between 50 and 90 where this becomes a risk. 2. Installing a new ASU file
bugs.impact: The attack signature update fails.
bugs.workaround: Impact of workaround: Performing this workaround requires restarting ASM, so it affects traffic processing briefly; therefore, it is recommended that you perform this during a maintenance window. Increase 'max memory size' from the default ~200 MB (200000000) to 300 MB: 1. Take a backup of the original file. # cp /etc/ts/tools/asm_config_server.cfg /var/tmp/asm_config_server.original.cfg 2. Add the following to the end of file /etc/ts/tools/asm_config_server.cfg: # AsyncMaxMemorySize=314572800 3. Restart ASM. # bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: FIPS 140-2 SP800-56Arev3 compliance
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP is not compliant with a NIST revision to the SP800-56A standard for cryptographic algorithms.
bugs.conditions: Using cryptographic algorithms covered by this revision in a FIPS 140-2 deployment.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP will comply with the older standard.
bugs.workaround: Updated cryptographic key assurances and pair-wise consistency checks according to the SP800-56Arev3 standard.

bugs.title: Diameter initial negotiation is not rejected when no common application is set
bugs.symptoms: If CER received with supported-application that was not set, then capability negotiation should be rejected. In such case CEA should be returned with DIAMETER_NO_COMMON_APPLICATION (5010).
bugs.conditions: There is no common application during capability negotiation.
bugs.impact: Even if there is no common application during CER/CEA exchange, connection is established which is unexpected.
bugs.fix: During capability negotiation, if there is no common application, then CEA would be returned with DIAMETER_NO_COMMON_APPLICATION (5010) and no connection exists.

bugs.title: Use of IPFIX log destination can result in increased CPU utilization
bugs.symptoms: -- Increased baseline CPU. - The memory_usage_stats table shows a continuous increase in mds_* rows.
bugs.conditions: Configure IPFIX log destination and make regular changes to the associated configuration.
bugs.impact: Increased baseline CPU may result in exhaustion of CPU resources.
bugs.workaround: Limiting changes to associated configuration can slow the effects of this issue.

bugs.title: LTM policy with a 'contains' operator does not work as expected when using an external data group.
bugs.symptoms: If a combination of other operators and the 'contains' operator are used in LTM Policy, searches might fail if the hashing-based operators have not populated the target entries.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy with 'contains' operator. -- Use of external datagroups.
bugs.impact: LTM policy might not work as expected with external data groups.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- If applicable, change the 'contains' operator to 'starts_with' in the policy. -- Change the policy into an iRule (executing '[class get <datagroup]' )

bugs.title: Stats on a certain counter for web-acceleration profile may show excessive value
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system is configured to use the RAM Cache feature, a corresponding profile may report an excessively large value for the cache_misses_all counter under certain conditions.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has a virtual server with web-acceleration profile without an application (RAM Cache feature). -- The virtual receives uncacheable requests which are interrupted by a client or are not served by a server.
bugs.impact: A value for cache_misses_all incurs an arithmetic overflow, and shows an excessive number comparable with 1.8e19. The issue has no functional impact; the system operates as normal.

bugs.title: inaccurate number of trunk members reported by bcm56xxd/bcmLINK
bugs.symptoms: The "bcmLINK" process (sometimes referred to as "bcm56xxd") may fail with a segmentation fault and be restarted, leaving behind a core-dump file for "bcmLINK". An error message may be logged about the condition "max_mbrs > 0".
bugs.conditions: -- occurs in multi-blade VIPRION system with trunked interfaces -- precise trigger is not known
bugs.impact: Momentary disruption of traffic handling by TMM.
bugs.workaround: None known.

bugs.title: Increase iApp block configuration processor timeout
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to configure and deploy an SSL Orchestrator configuration may result in a configuration processor timeout error.
bugs.conditions: When the TMOS control plane is taking a relatively high amount of CPU processing due to intense REST framework management workflows, any attempt to configure and deploy an SSL Orchestrator configuration using the guided configuration user interface, might take longer than the default 30 seconds timeout.
bugs.impact: The operation fails, resulting in a configuration processor timeout error. The BIG-IP administrator cannot configure and deploy an SSL Orchestrator configuration.
bugs.workaround: 1. Edit the /var/config/rest/iapps/f5-iappslx-ssl-orchestrator/nodejs/gc/orchestratorConfigProcessor.js file: vi /var/config/rest/iapps/f5-iappslx-ssl-orchestrator/nodejs/gc/orchestratorConfigProcessor.js 2. Locate the var _createComponentBlock = function(...) and locate the following line inside the function body (line ~1290): requestBody.state = "BINDING"; 3. Add the following after the 'requestBody.state' line: requestBody.configProcessorTimeoutSeconds = 120; 4. Save the edited file. 5. Restart the restnoded daemon: bigstart restart restnoded

bugs.title: Avrd core when connection to BIG-IQ data collection device is not available
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP system is configured to work with BIG-IQ but cannot connect due to network problems, avrd restarts itself every 10 minutes. During such restarts, a core is sometimes generated.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system is registered on BIG-IQ, but there is no network connectivity for any number of reasons.
bugs.impact: No impact since there is no network connectivity with BIG-IQ, and the data from the BIG-IP system cannot be sent anywhere.
bugs.workaround: Attempts to connect to BIG-IQ can be disabled manually by the following command: tmsh modify analytics global-settings use-offbox disabled
bugs.fix: Avrd no longer cores when the connection to the BIG-IQ data collection device is not available.

bugs.title: Tcpdump is failing on tmm 0.x interfaces
bugs.symptoms: The tcpdump command exits immediately with an error: errbuf ERROR:TMM side closing: Aborted tcpdump: pcap_loop: TMM side closing: Aborted
bugs.conditions: Capturing the packets on tmm interfaces.
bugs.impact: Unable to capture the packets on specific tmm interfaces.
bugs.workaround: There are two possible workarounds: -- Start tcpdump on the tmm that actually owns the interface using the TCPDUMP_ADDR command; for example, using blade1 for 1/0.16, run the command: TCPDUMP_ADDR=127.1.1.16 tcpdump -w testcap.pcap -s 0 -i 1/0.16 -- Send the TCPDUMP_ADDR command to a specific tmm, which could work from any blade (127.20.<slot>.<tmmnumber+1> (e.g. 127.20.1.1 == slot1/tmm0, 127.20.2.16 == slot2/tmm15): TCPDUMP_ADDR=127.20.1.16 tcpdump -w testcap.pcap -s 0 -i 1/0.16

bugs.title: LDAP referrals not supported for 'cert-ldap system-auth' &start;
bugs.symptoms: Admin users are unable to log in.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote LDAP auth enabled. -- Administrative users are authenticated with the 'cert-ldap' source. -- The admin user tries to log in.
bugs.impact: The cert-ldap authentication does not work, so login fails.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the /etc/nslcd.conf and set the referrals to no.

bugs.title: WebSocket server messages are logged even it is not configured
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems send unexpected WebSocket server messages to the remote logging server.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- ASM policy and WebSocket profile attached to a virtual server. -- More than one remote logging profile is attached to a virtual server. -- One of the remote loggers has response-logging=all.
bugs.impact: Remote logging server overloaded with unexpected WebSocket messages.
bugs.workaround: Set response-logging=illegal in all remote logging profiles.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP sends WebSocket server messages to a remote logger only when it is enabled in the logging profile.

bugs.title: TMM does not start when using more than 11 interfaces with more than 11 vCPUs
bugs.symptoms: TMM may not start when using more than 11 network interfaces with more than 11 vCPUs configured. You see the following log entries in /var/log/tmm: -- notice ixlv(1.1)[0:5.0]: Waiting for tmm10 to reach state 1... In the TMM log for that TMM, you can see that it is waiting for tmm0, e.g.: -- notice ixlv(1.10)[0:6.0]: Waiting for tmm0 to reach state 2...
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- More than 11 interfaces configured. -- More than 11 vCPUs configured.
bugs.impact: TMM does not start.
bugs.workaround: Configure fewer network interfaces or vCPUs.
bugs.fix: Fixed a TMM startup deadloop stuck issue (when there are more than 10 interfaces and tmms/vCPUs).

bugs.title: Using the LSN::persistence_entry command in an iRule may cause crashes and/or stalled connections
bugs.symptoms: -- Stalled serverside connections visible in connection table. -- No traffic going out towards pool member. -- Sometimes tmm crashes may occur.
bugs.conditions: The LSN::persistence_entry Tcl command is used inside of an iRule triggered by a serverside event, e.g., SERVER_CONNECTED.
bugs.impact: -- Traffic not reaching pool members. -- System disruption while tmm restarts in case of crash.
bugs.workaround: Do not use the LSN::persistence_entry command in iRules triggered by serverside events.
bugs.fix: Traffic now reaches pool members, no stalled connections occur, and crashes are eliminated.

bugs.title: Excessive memory consumption with ntlmconnpool configured
bugs.symptoms: OneConnect allows load balancing of HTTP requests from the same client connection over a pool of server side connections. When NTLM authentication is used, the NTLM Conn Pool allows reuse of server-side connections for authenticated client side connections. It holds HTTP authentication headers which is no longer necessary once a client is authenticated.
bugs.conditions: -- The virtual server is configured with both OneConnect and NTLM Conn Pool profiles. -- A large number of client systems with NTLM authentication are load balanced via the virtual server with long-lived connections.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system experiences memory pressure, which may result in an out-of-memory condition and a process crash, and potentially cause failover and interruption of traffic processing.
bugs.fix: When an NTLM Conn Pool profile is attached to a virtual server, it no longer causes memory pressure on a large number connections with NTLM authentication.

bugs.title: BADOS default sensitivity of 50 creates false positive attack on some sites
bugs.symptoms: False DoS attack detected. Behavioral DoS (ASM) might block legitimate traffic.
bugs.conditions: This can occur for some requests that have high latency and low TPS.
bugs.impact: False DoS attack detected. Behavioral DoS (ASM) can block legitimate traffic.
bugs.workaround: Modify the default sensitivity value from 50 to 500: tmsh modify sys db adm.health.sensitivity value 500 For some sites with server latency issues, you might also have to increase the health.sensitivity value; 1000 is a reasonable number. The results is that the attack is declared later than for the default value, but it is declared and the site is protected.
bugs.fix: Default sensitivity value 500 now illuminates false positive DoS attacks declaration.

bugs.title: Tunnels using autolasthop might drop traffic with ICMP route unreachable
bugs.symptoms: Traffic that should be encapsulated and sent via tunnel might get dropped with an ICMP error, destination unreachable, unreachable route. This happens in a scenario where no route exists towards the remote tunnel endpoint and the BIG-IP system relies on autolasthop to send the encapsulated traffic back to the other end of the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: No route exists to the other end of the tunnel.
bugs.impact: Traffic dropped with ICMP error, destination unreachable, unreachable route.
bugs.workaround: Create a route towards the other remote end of the tunnel.

bugs.title: iRules utilize information from incorrect peer flow for connection within a clientside/serverside command.
bugs.symptoms: An iRule which utilized the clientside or serverside command might operate on the incorrect peer flow.
bugs.conditions: An iRule contains a script that parks multiple times in a clientside or serverside command. Examples of parking commands include "table" and "persist".
bugs.impact: iRules might utilize information from the wrong peer flow for connection within a clientside or serverside command. Note: The affected clientside or serverside command might not actually park. The issue could be triggered by a different iRule that does park multiple times in the clientside or serverside command.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using commands that park inside the clientside or serverside command.

bugs.title: Any iRules that park in a clientside or serverside command leave the iRule attached to the wrong flow
bugs.symptoms: iRule commands issued after a clientside or serverside command operate on the wrong peer flow.
bugs.conditions: An iRule contains a script that parks in a clientside or serverside command. Examples of parking commands include 'table' and 'persist'.
bugs.impact: The iRule commands operate on the wrong peer flow.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using commands that park inside the clientside or serverside command.

bugs.title: The admd process is terminated by watchdog on some heavy load configuration process
bugs.symptoms: The watchdog process in the BIG-IP ASM monitors terminates the admd process.
bugs.conditions: On some heavy load configuration process, such as version upgrade.
bugs.impact: Restart of admd daemon. The restarts may be continuous. No stress-based anomaly detection or behavioral statistics aggregation until admd restarts.
bugs.workaround: For the case of continuous restarts, a partial solution is to disable admd during busy periods such as upgrades. To do so, issue the following two commands, in sequence, after the upgrade is complete: bigstart stop admd bigstart start admd

bugs.title: TMM crashes with a sigsegv while passing traffic
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a sigsegv while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with a Connector profile that redirects to an internal virtual server on the same BIG-IP system. Or Service profile on the VIP causes TMM restarts.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts.

bugs.title: Live Update scheduled installation is not installing on set schedule
bugs.symptoms: A scheduled live update does not occur at the scheduled time.
bugs.conditions: A scheduled installation is set for only a single day, between 00:00-00:14.
bugs.impact: Automated installation does not initiate
bugs.workaround: There are two options: 1. Install the update manually. 2. Set two consecutive days where the second day is the day with the schedule set between 00:00-00:14

bugs.title: BIG-IP Virtual Edition does not pass traffic on ESXi 6.5
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) does not pass traffic when deployed on ESXi 6.5 hypervisors, when the VE is using VMXNET 3 network interfaces (VMXNET 3 interfaces are the default). 'tmsh show net interface' indicates that one or more interfaces are not initialized.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP VE running on VMware ESXi 6.5 hypervisor.
bugs.impact: Traffic does not pass through non-mgmt interfaces.
bugs.workaround: -- On the BIG-IP systems, you can switch to the 'sock' driver. Note: The workarounds that switch driver must be applied individually to devices, as they do not synchronize via ConfigSync. IMPORTANT: The driver must be configured the same way on all devices in a sync-failover device group. 1, At the command prompt, run the following command to enable the sock driver in tmm_init.tcl: echo "device driver vendor_dev 15ad:07b0 sock" >> tmm_init.tcl 2. Restart tmm: tmsh restart sys service tmm -- After restarting, the sock driver should be listed in the 'driver_in_use' column when running the following command. tmctl -d blade tmm/device_probed pci_bdf pseudo_name type available_drivers driver_in_use ------------ ----------- --------- --------------------- ------------- 0000:03:00.0 F5DEV_PCI xnet, vmxnet3, sock, 0000:0b:00.0 1.1 F5DEV_PCI xnet, vmxnet3, sock, sock 0000:13:00.0 1.2 F5DEV_PCI xnet, vmxnet3, sock, sock 0000:1b:00.0 1.3 F5DEV_PCI xnet, vmxnet3, sock, sock

bugs.title: Huge amount of admd processes caused oom
bugs.symptoms: The top command shows that a large number of admd processes are running.
bugs.conditions: -- Configuration with Sync-Failover device groups and BADOS. -- Some stressful (unknown) condition occurs.
