bugs.behavior: QUIC congestion window is restored to its pre-recovery value on a spurious loss recovery.

bugs.title: Bot defense profile upgrade fails from 14.x to 15.x/16.x with error match-order should be unique
bugs.symptoms: Upgrading Bot defense profile fails with match-order field 1 or 2 fails, while the error is "match-order should be unique"
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - Bot defense profile has allow list object (the GUI says whitelist object) - The object has a field match-order = 1 or 2 - Upgrade happening from 14.x to 15.x/16.x
bugs.impact: Upgrade fails
bugs.workaround: Before upgrading -- Change match-order field 1 to 3 -- Change match-order field 2 to 4
bugs.fix: Fix changes match-order field 1 to 3 and match-order field 2 to 4 programmatically

bugs.title: Zone colors in ASM swap usage graph are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: In GUI ASM memory utilization chart, 'BD swap size, Total swap size' graph show inconsistent background colors. It looks like these colors are assigned with an assumption that swap usage is shown as percentage but it is shown as absolute value.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM is provisioned. -- Viewing ASM memory utilization chart/
bugs.impact: Potential confusion viewing colors in ASM memory utilization chart.
bugs.workaround: None. This is a cosmetic issue only.

bugs.title: SSL filter does not re-initialize when an OCSP object is modified
bugs.symptoms: Create an OCSP object using DNS resolver ns1, associate the OCSP object to SSL profile and a virtual. Then, modify the OCSP object to DNS resolver ns2. After the modification, wait for cache-timeout and cache-error-timeout and then connect to virtual again. The nameserver contacted is still ns1.
bugs.conditions: An OCSP object is configured and modified.
bugs.impact: The wrong nameserver is used after modification to the OCSP object.
bugs.fix: After the fix, the correct nameserver will be contacted after the OCSP object is modified.

bugs.title: IPsec tunnel does not start after an upgrade, first configuration, or reconfiguration
bugs.symptoms: -- IPsec tunnel does not start. -- Remote IPsec networks unavailable.
bugs.conditions: -- Using IKEv1 and one of the following: + Performing an upgrade. + IPsec tunnel reconfiguration generally involving a change to, or addition of, a traffic-selector.
bugs.impact: IPsec tunnel is down permanently.
bugs.workaround: -- Reconfigure or delete and re-create the traffic selectors associated with the IPsec tunnel that does not start. Special Notes: -- This occurs rarely and does not happen spontaneously, without intentional changes (reconfiguration or upgrade). -- A BIG-IP reboot or a restart of tmipsecd does not resolve this condition. -- This symptom might also occur due to a genuine misconfiguration. -- After major version upgrades, default ciphers can change, double-check the encryption and authentication ciphers for the tunnel.

bugs.title: SIGABRT from sod watchdog when IPS has large number of hyperscan matches.
bugs.symptoms: TMM restart as SOD watchdog thinks that TMM is stuck in an infinite loop while its just busy processing of the large amount of hyperscan matches.
bugs.conditions: Certain IPS snort rules are weak (like NULL bytes) and on certain type of network traffic, it can lead to large number of hyperscan matches and hence it may lead to SIGABRT by SOD watchdog daemon.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Enable the following system compliance checks in IPS profile with action DROP/REJECT. max_inspection_count -> Change action "DROP" max_signature_engine_memory_chunk_size -> Change action "DROP" max_signature_engine_memory_size -> Change action "DROP" max_signature_hs_match_count -> Change action "DROP" This will ensure that IPS does not consume more than the allowed system resources and will prevent a crash.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to IPS

bugs.title: TMM crash is seen due to double free in SAML flow
bugs.symptoms: When this issue occurs the TMM will crash
bugs.conditions: Exact reproduction steps are not known but it occurs during SAML transactions
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Delay in using new route updates by existing connections on BIG-IP.
bugs.symptoms: If routes are updated in BIG-IP by static or dynamic methods, the existing connections will not use the new routes until ~1-8 seconds later.
bugs.conditions: Routes for existing connections on the BIG-IP are updated.
bugs.impact: Performance might be degraded when routes are updated for existing connections on BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: Added DB varible "tmm.inline_route_update". When enabled, packets are checked for new routes before sending out. Its disabled by default.
bugs.behavior: A new db variable has been added, called tmm.inline_route_update. It is disabled by default. When enabled, packets are checked for new routes before sending out.

bugs.title: Truncated or incomplete upload of a BIG-IP image causes kernel lockup and reboot
bugs.symptoms: If there is a truncated BIG-IP software image in /shared/images, a kernel lockup and reboot could occur. One way to have a truncated image in /shared/images is by using iControl/SOAP to upload the image. Using SOAP, the image is uploaded in chunks, so until the last chunk is uploaded, the image is not complete/is truncated.
bugs.conditions: -- Truncated BIG-IP image in /shared/images -- Using SOAP to upload the image.
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption caused by the reboot.
bugs.workaround: If you are using SOAP to upload BIG-IP software images, upload them to /shared first and then move them to /shared/images.

bugs.title: System should reboot (rather than restart services) when it sees a large number of HSB XLMAC errors
bugs.symptoms: The following symptoms may be seen when the HSB is experiencing a large number of XLMAC errors and is unable to recover from the errors. After attempting XLMAC recovery fails, the current behavior is to failover to the peer unit and go-offline and down links. This can be seen the TMM logs: -- notice The number of the HSB XLMAC recovery operation 11 or fcs failover count 0 reached threshold 11 on bus: 3. -- notice high availability (HA) failover action is triggered due to XLMAC/FCS errors on HSB1 on bus 3. -- notice HSBE2 1 disable XLMAC TX/RX at runtime. -- notice high availability (HA) failover action is cleared. Followed by a failover event.
bugs.conditions: It is unknown under what conditions the XLMAC errors occur.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system fails over.
bugs.workaround: Modify the default high availability (HA) action for the switchboard-failsafe to reboot instead of go offline and down links.
bugs.fix: Reboot (rather than restart services) when XLMAC errors exceed threshold.

bugs.title: A virtual server status changes to yellow because of specific sources, which causes DNS to stop responding.
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server stops DNS response and its status on GUI is yellow.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM virtual server (or Pool Member or Node) is over the limit. -- The Connection Rate Limit Mode is rate limited by source or destination.
bugs.impact: Virtual server stops all DNS response, and the virtual server state in the GUI turns yellow. Yellow is intended to signify that the virtual server is serving connections but should not receive any further traffic until it goes green. In this case, however, yellow indicates that traffic is OK, as long as it is not from a given client (or to a given destination).
bugs.fix: A new variable, Ignore LTM Rate Limit Modes, has been added to allow optionally ignoring LTM virtual server yellow state caused by connection/rate limit reached in GUI. It can be found in DNS :: Settings : GSLB : General.

bugs.title: Management route lost after reboot.
bugs.symptoms: Management route lost after reboot, leading to no access to BIG-IP systems via management address.
bugs.conditions: -- 2NIC BIG-IP Virtual Edition template deployed in GCP (see https://github.com/F5Networks/f5-google-gdm-templates/tree/v3.0.3/supported/standalone/2nic/existing-stack/byol). -- The instance is rebooted.
bugs.impact: After rebooting, the default route via the management interface no longer exists in the routing table. BIG-IP administrators are unable to connect to BIG-IP Virtual Edition via the management address.
bugs.workaround: Use either of the following workarounds: -- Delete the route completely and reinstall the route. -- Restart mcpd: bigstart restart mcpd

bugs.title: Device ID Deletions anomaly might be raised in case of browser/hardware change
bugs.symptoms: -- Valid users complain they are unable to connect, or they are required to do CAPTCHA frequently. -- On the BIG-IP device, 'Device ID Deletion' violations are being raised.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense Profile with 'Device ID' mode set to 'Generate After Access' is attached to the virtual server. -- Some change in the browser or computer hardware occurs. -- Surfing to multiple qualified pages at the same time.
bugs.impact: Valid requests might be mitigated.
bugs.workaround: Raise the threshold of 'Device ID Deletion' anomaly (recommended value according to the webserver, is approximately 4).

bugs.title: Some RESOLV::lookup queries, including PTR lookups for RFC1918 addresses, return empty strings
bugs.symptoms: RESOLV::lookup returns an empty string.
bugs.impact: RESOLV::lookup fails.
bugs.workaround: Use a DNS Resolver ('net dns') and RESOLVER::name_lookup / DNSMSG:: instead of RESOLV::lookup: 1. Configure a local 'net dns' resolver, replacing '192.88.99.1' with the IP address of your DNS resolver: tmsh create net dns-resolver resolver-for-irules answer-default-zones no forward-zones add { . { nameservers add { 192.0.2.1:53 } } } 2. Use an iRule procedure similar to this to perform PTR lookups for IPv4 addresses: proc resolv_ptr_v4 { addr_v4 } { # Convert $addr_v4 into its constituent bytes set ret [scan $addr_v4 {%d.%d.%d.%d} a b c d] if { $ret != 4 } { return } # Perform a PTR lookup on the IP address $addr_v4, and return the first answer set ret [RESOLVER::name_lookup "/Common/resolver-for-irules" "$d.$c.$b.$a.in-addr.arpa" PTR] set ret [lindex [DNSMSG::section $ret answer] 0] if { $ret eq "" } { # log local0.warn "DNS PTR lookup for $addr_v4 failed." return } # Last element in '1.1.1.10.in-addr.arpa. 600 IN PTR otters.example.com' return [lindex $ret end] } -- In an iRule, instead of: RESOLV::lookup @192.0.2.1 $ipv4_addr Use: call resolv_ptr_v4 $ipv4_addr

bugs.title: Redundant socket close when half-open monitor pings
bugs.symptoms: Sockets and log files are closed and re-opened twice instead of one time when the half-open TCP monitor pings successfully.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the half-open monitor pings successfully.
bugs.impact: Minor performance impact.

bugs.title: Some sequence of HTTP packets may cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing HTTP traffic.
bugs.conditions: A virtual with standard HTTP profile is configured.
bugs.impact: When TMM crashes it causes a failover event and may interrupt traffic processing.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: After installing a UCS file on a new BIG-IP system, some configuration items may fail to load
bugs.symptoms: The FIPS card goes offline.
bugs.conditions: After switching to new BIG-IP device, load the UCS file containing a configuration from a previously working BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: Config load errors occur: -- emerg load_config_files: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- Loading schema version: 12.1.5 Loading schema version: 12.1.5.2 01070712:3: FIPS 140 operations not available on this system Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed. -- info install_ucs.pm: ERROR: UCS installation failed. The FIPS card is offline.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the device, and the errors should resolve themselves.

bugs.title: External trunk fdb entries might end up with internal MAC addresses.
bugs.symptoms: The vCMP host might have external trunk with internal MAC addresses. This is visible via 'tmsh show net fdb'.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP is provisioned and has guests deployed on it. -- vCMP host uses trunks. -- Create VLANs using trunks and assign it to guests. -- Guests need to be in high availability (HA) configuration.
bugs.impact: Traffic processing is disrupted.

bugs.title: IPv6 hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, handling of IPv6 traffic to BIG-IP owned addressed (e.g. self-IPs) do not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: -- IPv6 strict compliance is enabled (tmsh modify sys db ipv6.strictcompliance value true) -- IPv6 traffic to BIG-IP owned addresses
bugs.impact: Handling of IPv6 traffic does not follow current best practices.
bugs.workaround: Disable IPv6 strict compliance with the command: tmsh modify sys db ipv6.strictcompliance value false
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now handles IPv6 traffic in compliance with current best practices.

bugs.title: Geolocation database does not show region_name for IP addresses of some Spain provinces
bugs.symptoms: Geolocation database does not show region_name for the IP addresses that belong to Biscay and Gipuzkoa provinces of the Pais Vasco region of Spain.
bugs.conditions: Using the geolocation database for reference of the region_name for IP addresses that belong to Biscay and Gipuzkoa provinces of the Pais Vasco region of Spain.
bugs.impact: Geolocation database does not show region_name.
bugs.fix: Geolocation database now shows the region_name for the IP addresses that belong to the Biscay and Gipuzkoa provinces of the Pais Vasco region of Spain.

bugs.title: LTM virtual address netmask does not persist after a reboot
bugs.symptoms: The virtual address netmask is missing after the system reboots.
bugs.conditions: When referencing an "ltm traffic-matching-criteria" object from the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Netmask address is set to 'any' after the system reboots.

bugs.title: NTP has predictable timestamps
bugs.symptoms: No known symptoms.
bugs.conditions: Ntpd in ntp before 4.2.8p14 and 4.3.x before 4.3.100 are vulnerable. Two main prerequisites for this to be exploited. 1. Having the BIG-IP act as an NTP server. 2. Sources for BIG-IP's time being unreliable/unauthenticated upstream NTP servers
bugs.impact: A high-performance ntpd instance that gets its time from unauthenticated IPv4 time sources may be vulnerable to an off-path attacker who can query time from the victim's ntpd instance. An attacker who can send a large number of packets with the spoofed IPv4 address of the upstream server can use this flaw to modify the victim's clock by a limited amount or cause ntpd to exit.
bugs.workaround: Redhat suggested the following mitigations: 1. Have enough trustworthy sources of time. 2. If you are serving time to a possibly hostile network, have your system get its time from other than unauthenticated IPv4 over the hostile network. 3. Use NTP packet authentication where appropriate. 4. Pay attention to error messages logged by ntpd. 5. Monitor your ntpd instances. If the pstats command of ntpq shows the value for "bogus origin" is increasing then that association is likely under attack. 6. If you must get unauthenticated time over IPv4 on a hostile network, Use restrict ... noserve to prevent this attack (note that this is a heavy-handed protection), which blocks time service to the specified network.

bugs.title: Chunked response may have DATA frame with END_STREAM prematurely
bugs.symptoms: When an HTTP/2 profile is configured on the client side, chunked responses are always sent unchunked. When a connection to a client is congested, BIG-IP systems may send the END_STREAM flag before transmitting a whole payload.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server with an HTTP/2 profile configured on the client side. -- A server responds with a chunked response.
bugs.impact: A browser may not receive the whole payload, or it may not recognize that the payload has been delivered fully (partially prior to the DATA frame with END_STREAM flag, partially after the frame).
bugs.workaround: Configure an HTTP profile on the client side with a value of 'unchunk' on the response-chunking option.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP systems no longer send a DATA frame with END_STREAM flag prematurely when a connection to a client is congested.

bugs.title: Memory leak when creating/deleting LTM node object
bugs.symptoms: A memory leak occurs when creating/deleting an LTM node object.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a node object. -- Delete the node object.
bugs.impact: This gradually causes tmm memory pressure, and eventually severe outcome is possible such as aggressive mode sweeper and tmm restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Refrain continuous creation/deletion of LTM nodes.
bugs.fix: Memory gets freed accordingly while deleting LTM node objects.

bugs.title: iControl REST framework exception handling hardening
bugs.symptoms: iControl REST framework does not follow best practices for exception handling
bugs.conditions: iControl REST framework use by an authenticated user.
bugs.impact: iControl REST framework does not follow best practices for exception handling
bugs.fix: iControl REST framework now follows best practices for exception handling

bugs.title: Payloads with large number of elements in XML take a lot of time to process
bugs.symptoms: ASM experiences high CPU and latency usage while processing a large XML request.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned -- HTTP request with a large XML payload (several MB) is sent to the backend server which triggers the XML parser.
bugs.impact: High CPU and latency occurs while bd processes the payload. This may cause a bottleneck for different requests that arrive concurrently with the large XML payload request.
bugs.fix: This fix includes performance improvements for large XML payloads.

bugs.title: AVR data might be restored from non-relevant files in /shared/avr_afm partition during upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade, AFM statistics show non-relevant data.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system upgrade -- Leftovers files remain in /shared/avr_afm partition from other versions.
bugs.impact: Non-relevant data are shown in AFM statistics.
bugs.workaround: Delete the non-relevant data manually from MariaDB/MySQL.

bugs.title: Incorrect BD Swap Size units on ASM Resources chart
bugs.symptoms: The 'BD Swap Size' reported on the 'Security :: Reporting : ASM Resources : Memory Utilization' page is much too high and incorrect.
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned.
bugs.impact: Graphically reported BD swap memory usage is incorrect.

bugs.title: Improper handling of multiple cookie headers results in security bypass
bugs.symptoms: Improper handling of multiple cookies results in security bypass when certain server technologies are used. The multiple cookie headers are handled separately in ASM, but the backend server concatenates it and can lead to potential signature attacks.
bugs.conditions: When PHP server technology is used as backend and a specially crafted request is sent with multiple cookies header.
bugs.impact: Bypass of negative security enforcement and can affect certain server technologies
bugs.fix: Templates are modified to change the default value of 'Repeated Occurrences' for HTTP header 'cookie' to 'Disallow'.

bugs.title: Local user db not synced to standby device when it is comes online after forced offline state
bugs.symptoms: Local user db is not synced to the standby device when it comes online after being forced offline.
bugs.conditions: Valid high availability (HA) configuration. - Make the standby device forced offline - create a new local db user in the online device - bring back the standby device online.
bugs.impact: The newly created user is not synced to the standby device unless localdbmgr is restarted on the standby.
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue by handling the forced offline scenario.

bugs.title: Source translation type of automap not synced properly
bugs.symptoms: After changing the FWNAT source translation type, the setting is not synced to the other devices.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) configuration -- FWNAT source translation type changed to automap
bugs.impact: Automap is not synced to the other devices and source translation is not applied at all.
bugs.fix: The source translation type now syncs correctly on the active/standby device.

bugs.title: '@' no longer valid in SNMP community strings
bugs.symptoms: The '@' character is no longer valid in SNMP community strings.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use the '@' character in SNMP community strings.
bugs.impact: Unable to use the '@' character in SNMP community strings. The system cannot process SNMP commands with community strings that contain the '@' character, and the commands fail.
bugs.workaround: Use a community string that does not contain the '@' character.

bugs.title: Tmm core is seen after multiple failover/ failback with lots of tunnels.
bugs.symptoms: When IPsec tunnel count is high (~300), a tmm core is generated after multiple failover.
bugs.conditions: Multiple failovers occur on BIG-IP systems with lots of IPsec tunnels.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to IPsec tunnels and repeated failover.

bugs.title: Loading SCF file does not restore files from tar file
bugs.symptoms: Loading an SCF configuration file does not restore file objects from the SCF's associated tar file. Restoring the SCF fails with an error similar to this if the running configuration does not already contain the file: 01070712:3: Failed: name (/Common/test-crt) Cache path (/config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/certificate_d/:Common:test-crt) does not exist and there is no copy in trash-bin to restore from. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Restore an SCF archive that references file objects, e.g.: -- SSL certificates -- SSL keys -- iFiles
bugs.impact: Restoring SCF does not restore contents of file objects.

bugs.title: Certificate update on the SSL profile server for the HTTPS monitor: BIG-IP does not use the updated certificate.
bugs.symptoms: When you overwrite the certificate that is configured on the SSL profile server and is used with the HTTPS monitor, the BIG-IP system neither uses a client certificate nor continues to use the old certificate. After you update the certificate, the stored certificate is incremented. However, the monitor log indicates that it is using the old certificate.
bugs.conditions: --Create a pool with an HTTPS pool member. --Create an HTTPS monitor with a certificate and key. --Assign the HTTPS monitor to the HTTPS pool. --Update the certificate through GUI or TMSH.
bugs.impact: The monitor tries to use the old certificate or does not present a client certificate after the update.
bugs.workaround: Use one of the following workarounds: -- Restart bigd: bigstart restart bigd -- Modify the server SSL profile certificate key. Set it to ‘none’, and switch back to the original certificate key name. The bigd utility successfully loads the new certificate file.

bugs.title: Incorrect sum(hits_count) value in aggregate tables
bugs.symptoms: If the results gathered for sum(hits_count) are very large (e.g., 15000300000), the system does not report the correct values in the AVR tables.
bugs.conditions: -- Insert a very large amount of data (approximately 4.5 milliard or more) to one of AVR tables. -- Review the value of the sum(hits_count) column.
bugs.impact: The system reports incorrect values in AVR tables when dealing with large numbers

bugs.title: Autoscale groups require multiple syncs of datasync-global-dg
bugs.symptoms: Datasync-global-dg is in 'sync pending' status and is not automatically synced as expected.
bugs.conditions: Browser Challenges update image is automatically downloaded.
bugs.impact: Peers are not synced.
bugs.workaround: Manually sync datasync-global-db group.
bugs.fix: Perform full sync for each change when having multiple live update changes in a row.

bugs.title: An HTTP request is not served when a remote logging server is down
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP systems provide an option to sanitize HTTP traffic via the http_security profile. When the profile is configured to alarm on a violation, it is possible that a connection to the violating client is reset if a remote logging server is marked down.
bugs.conditions: -- A BIG-IP system has an HTTP profile and and an http_security profile with the alarm option set. -- A remote logging server is configured via a BIG-IP pool. -- The pool has a monitor that marks all the pool members down. -- A request with an HTTP violation is processed and triggers an alarm configured in the http_security profile.
bugs.impact: -- A TCP connection to a client is reset by the BIG-IP system. -- The web page may not render, or may not render as expected. -- Data are not delivered to a server with a POST request.

bugs.title: DNS & BADOS high-speed logger messages are mixed
bugs.symptoms: Both DNS and BADOS messages use the same family ID, and the reported messages are categorized together.
bugs.conditions: BADOS & DNS are run together and application is under attack (BADOS). At this point, BIG-IP will generate BADOS messages using an ID that conflicts with DNS messages.
bugs.impact: Reporting will be confusing.

bugs.title: VPN fails to establish on Windows systems where 'Secure Boot' is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: VPN fails to connect.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Secure Boot' is enabled on Microsoft Windows systems. -- Running Windows 10. -- IP Filtering Engine is enables in the Network Access settings. -- Connecting to VPN.
bugs.impact: End user clients cannot establish a VPN connection.
bugs.workaround: There are two workarounds for this issue: -- Disable 'Secure Boot' on Windows systems. Note: Some systems running Windows 10 have a feature called 'Secure Boot' enabled by default to ensure that client computers boot using only software trusted by the computer. -- Disable IP Filtering Engine setting in the Network Access settings.

bugs.title: Delayed Gratuitous ARPs may cause traffic to go to the previous active BIG-IP device
bugs.symptoms: When the standby system in a High Availability (HA) group becomes active, it sends out gratuitous ARPs to advertise its ownership of IP addresses and direct traffic to itself. In rare conditions, when becoming active, other processes may send out traffic before Gratuitous ARPs are generated.
bugs.conditions: -- HA configured -- Protocols in use that generate frequent and fast signaling messages
bugs.impact: This has been observed as an issue for IPsec during failover, causing tunnel stability issues after failover. No other protocols are known to be affected by the issue.
bugs.fix: When the standby device in an HA pair becomes active, Gratuitous ARPs are prioritized over other traffic.

bugs.title: Delays marking Nodes or Pool Members DOWN with in-TMM monitoring
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is configured with a large number of in-TMM monitors, the Nodes or Pool Members may not be marked DOWN immediately after the configured timeout period once the target stops responding to pings.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when: -- In-TMM monitoring is enabled (via sys db bigd.tmm) -- A large number of Nodes and/or Pool Members (several hundreds or thousands) are configured and monitored.
bugs.impact: Nodes or Pool Members which are not responsive may not be marked DOWN in a timely fashion.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by disabling in-TMM monitoring, at the expense of decreased monitoring performance (higher CPU usage by the bigd daemon).

bugs.title: Delays marking Nodes or Pool Members DOWN with in-TMM monitoring
bugs.symptoms: When configured with a large number of in-TMM monitors, Nodes or Pool Members may not be marked DOWN immediately after the configured timeout period once the target stops responding to pings.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when: -- In-TMM monitoring is enabled (via sys db bigd.tmm). -- A large number of Nodes and/or Pool Members (several hundreds or thousands) are configured and monitored.
bugs.impact: Nodes or Pool Members which are not responsive may not be marked DOWN in a timely fashion.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by disabling in-TMM monitoring, at the expense of decreased monitoring performance (higher CPU usage by the bigd daemon).

bugs.title: Content profile cannot be updated after redirect from violation details in Request Log
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP issues a redirect to the content profile form that contains relevant violation details in the Request Log. If you follow this redirect and try to update profile, the action fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if you follow the redirect to the content profile page from the violation details page in the Request Log, and then try to update the profile
bugs.impact: You are unable to update the content profile.
bugs.workaround: Go to the list content profile page, and update the content profile from there.
bugs.fix: Update of content profiles works in all cases, including redirect from violation details in Request Log

bugs.title: HTTP Explicit Proxy configurations can result in connections hanging until idle timeout.
bugs.symptoms: After an HTTP return code of 400 Bad Request or 403 Forbidden, connection table entries may not be removed from the connection table until they reach the idle timeout threshold.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP Explicit Proxy Configuration. -- BIG-IP HTTP response contains a 400 Bad Request or 403 Forbidden status code.
bugs.impact: The hanging connection table entries can cause subsequent connections from the same source port to fail. Also, the subsequent connection attempts can cause the idle timer to be reset.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to prevent connections from hanging: when HTTP_REJECT { after 1 }
bugs.fix: HTTP Explicit Proxy configurations no longer results in connections hanging until idle timeout.

bugs.title: Portal Access resources are visible when they should not be
bugs.symptoms: For Access Policy created with Customization type: modern, Portal Access resource is still present on user's webtop after the checkbox "Publish on Webtop" is disabled in config
bugs.conditions: -- Access Policy created with Customization type: modern -- Disable the checkbox "Publish on Webtop" for any Portal Access resource
bugs.impact: Disabled Portal Access resource visible on the webtop when it should be hidden.
bugs.workaround: Re-create Access Policy with Customization type: standard
bugs.fix: Disabled Portal Access resource is hidden on user's webtop

bugs.title: FTP virtual server active data channels do not pass traffic
bugs.symptoms: FTP virtual server active mode data channel hangs when processing undisclosed traffic.
bugs.conditions: FTP virtual Server with active mode data channel is configured.
bugs.impact: Cannot issue commands to FTP virtual server; traffic disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Disable global syncookies
bugs.fix: Properly initialized FTP server TMM objects.

bugs.title: The process plane statistics do not accurately label some processes
bugs.symptoms: The plane process statistics can be used to track the statistics of processes even though the process ID has changed over time. The processes are characterized as belonging to the control plane, data plane, or analysis plane. Some of the processes are incorrectly labeled.
bugs.conditions: Viewing the plane process statistics when diagnosing plane usage on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The percentage of usage of each plane can be confusing or incorrect.

bugs.title: Zonerunner GUI hangs when attempting to list Resource Records
bugs.symptoms: Zonerunner GUI hangs when attempting to list Resource Records; mcpd times out.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to list Resource Records in Zonerunner GUI.
bugs.impact: Zonerunner hangs.
bugs.workaround: Zonerunner GUI is unusable until this issue is resolved. Use tmsh.

bugs.title: Tomcat upgrade via Engineering Hotfix causes live-update files removal
bugs.symptoms: After applying an Engineering Hotfix ISO that contains an updated tomcat package, live-update files are inadvertently removed and live update no longer works properly.
bugs.conditions: Occurs after installing an Engineering Hotfix that contains the tomcat package.
bugs.impact: Live-update functionality does not work properly.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, you can install an updated Engineering Hotfix that uses a fixed version of the live-install package.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with inadvertently removing live-update files while applying an Engineering Hotfix.

bugs.title: BGP multi-path candidate selection does not work properly in all cases.
bugs.symptoms: ZebOS BGP might not properly clear the multi-path candidate flag when handling a BGP route.
bugs.conditions: An inbound route-map exists that modifies a route's path selection attribute.
bugs.impact: Incorrect path selection and/or a timer on a route getting refreshed every time the Routing Information Base (RIB) is scanned.

bugs.title: Changes to support DNS Flag Day
bugs.symptoms: It is important for DNS software vendors to comply with DNS standards, and to use a default EDNS buffer size (1232 bytes) that will not cause fragmentation on typical network links.
bugs.conditions: IP fragmentation can cause transmission failures when large DNS messages are sent via UDP.
bugs.impact: Even when fragmentation does work, it may not be secure; it is theoretically possible to spoof parts of a fragmented DNS message, without easy detection at the receiving end.
bugs.fix: Create a db variable "dns.maxudp" to set a maximum UDP buffer size

bugs.title: Mandatory arguments missing in tmsh security protocol-inspection profile help
bugs.symptoms: Missing mandatory arguments for tmsh security protocol-inspection profile command list.
bugs.conditions: Profile - Configures the protocol inspection profiles Module - security protocol-inspection profile
bugs.impact: Tmsh does not specify the mandatory arguments, which makes it difficult to write any script or automate the tmsh command around this security profile.
bugs.workaround: Specify the following arguments for this profile: -- Ports

bugs.title: Security hardening in FPS GUI
bugs.symptoms: FPS GUI does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: * Provision and license Fraud Protection Service (FPS).
bugs.impact: FPS GUI does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: FPS GUI now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: Automap support in FWNAT
bugs.symptoms: Automap selects the available self IP address as the translated source IP address. FWNAT does not support automap functionality as is available in LTM.
bugs.conditions: Attempting to use automap functionality as is available in LTM
bugs.impact: In FWNAT, you cannot select automap as one of the options for source translation.
bugs.fix: FWNAT now supports automap functionality.

bugs.title: Context use and syntax changes clarification
bugs.symptoms: There are two context and syntax-related issues: -- In v14.x, the context for tmsh analytics commands related to server side connections changed. For example, 'total-server-side-conns' became a simple 'server-side-conns'. -- In v13.x and 14.x, the calculation method for 'max-tps' changed from cumulative to commutative.
bugs.conditions: This occurs in either of the following scenarios: -- Using tmsh analytics commands related to max-tps in v13.x or later. -- Using tmsh analytics commands related to server side connections in BIG-IP v14.x and later.
bugs.impact: Stats names do not reflect their actual values. The 'max-tps' value is no longer valid for client IP context. These changes might have varied impacts, depending on your configuration.
bugs.workaround: There are 2 issues: 1)tmsh display name changed from total-server-side-conns to server-side-conns etc (14.x+) 2)Change the "max-tps" attribute "commutative" from false to true and change the merge formula from SUM to MAX
bugs.fix: -- Label names for tmsh analytics commands related to server side connections changed (for example: the tmsh display name changed from 'total-server-side-conns' to 'server-side-conns', with similar changes for the other server side connection stats). -- The 'max-tps' formula changed to be commutative instead of cumulative, so it is no longer relevant in the 'client-ip' context.
bugs.behavior: -- Label names for tmsh analytics commands related to server side connections changed (for example: the tmsh display name changed from 'total-server-side-conns' to 'server-side-conns', with similar changes for the other server side connection stats). -- The 'max-tps' formula changed to be commutative instead of cumulative, so it is no longer relevant in the 'client-ip' context.

bugs.title: Too many interrupts from console serial port starve TMM for CPU time
bugs.symptoms: Kernel log file will show this message: "err kernel: serial8250: too much work for irq4" In some conditions when there are too many of these, TMM may crash.
bugs.conditions: Occurs due to performing heavy I/O over the serial console. For example, running tcpdump and dumping the output to the console while the device is under heavy load.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using the console for issuing commands that produces a lot of output.

bugs.title: Problems may occur after creating a node named '_auto_<IP address>'
bugs.symptoms: If a node is created and named '_auto_<IP address>', various problems may occur, including but not limited to: -- If the node is configured as an FQDN template node, no ephemeral nodes may be created based on the FQDN name. -- If the node is configured as an FQDN template node, when the node is deleted, an ephemeral node may be created based on the FQDN name of the deleted node. -- If the node is configured as an FQDN template node with autopopulate enabled, when the node is deleted, ephemeral nodes may be created based on the FQDN name of the deleted node, but with no FQDN template node. -- If the node is configured as an FQDN template node and then deleted, any ephemeral nodes remaining must be deleted manually.
bugs.conditions: This may occur if: -- A node is created with a name of the form '_auto_<IP address>', such as: - _auto_10.10.10.10 (IPv4 address 10.10.10.10). - _auto_fe80..f811.3eff.fe06.9ab9 (IPv6 address fe80::f811:3eff:fe06:9ab9) -- FQDN template nodes are configured (including the node described above) with FQDN names that resolve to the IP address embedded in the node name.
bugs.impact: -- Ephemeral nodes (and pool members) may not be created based on resolution of the FQDN name in the configured node. -- Ephemeral nodes may be created unexpectedly after the configured node is deleted. -- Ephemeral nodes created unexpectedly after the configured node is deleted must be deleted manually.
bugs.workaround: Do not create any node with a name beginning with '_auto_'. That is a reserved name used for creation of FQDN ephemeral nodes.

bugs.title: The turboflex-low-latency and turboflex-dns are missing.
bugs.symptoms: The turboflex-low-latency and turboflex-dns profiles are no longer available in 15.1.x and 16.0.x software releases.
bugs.conditions: The turboflex-low-latency or turboflex-dns in use.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure turboflex-low-latency or turboflex-dns profiles after an upgrade to 15.1.x or 16.0.x software release.
bugs.fix: The turboflex-low-latency and turboflex-dns profiles are restored.

bugs.title: Unable to Create/delete ltm virtual server via CLI transaction when destination is not specified on the ltm virtual object
bugs.symptoms: A CLI transaction fails with an error: transaction failed: 0107028f:3: The destination (::) address and mask (255.255.255.255) for virtual server (/Common/foo) must be be the same type (IPv4 or IPv6).
bugs.conditions: -- A CLI transaction is used to create or delete a virtual server -- When destination is not specified. -- The virtual server references a traffic matching criteria
bugs.impact: The transaction fails with error and the virtual server is not created/deleted.

bugs.title: TMM may core when using FastL4's hardware offloading feature
bugs.symptoms: TMM cores.
bugs.conditions: FastL4's hardware offloading is used. Because the error is an internal software logic implementation, there is no direct specific configuration that triggers this error condition. A quick traffic spike during a short period of time makes it more likely to occur.
bugs.impact: TMM cores and the system cannot process traffic. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable PVA/EPVA on all FastL4 profiles
bugs.fix: Fix the internal logic error.

bugs.title: APM authentication fails due to delay in sessionDB readiness
bugs.symptoms: APM Authentication fails, and apmd cores when trying to connect to sessionDB.
bugs.conditions: -- APM configured. -- SAML SP configured.
bugs.impact: It takes a long time to create the configuration snapshot. Authentication fails and apmd cores.
bugs.workaround: Restart all services by entering the following command: tmsh restart /sys service all Note: Restarting all services causes temporary traffic disruption.
bugs.fix: The sessionDB readiness has been corrected so that authentication succeeds.

bugs.title: Connection error with server with TLS1.3 single-dh-use.
bugs.symptoms: Connection failure with TLS1.3 and single-dh-use configured.
bugs.conditions: 14.1 with TLS1.3 single-dh-use.
bugs.impact: Connection failure in 14.1 versions.
bugs.workaround: Disable single-dh-use, or disable tls1.3.
bugs.fix: 14.1 now supports TLS1.3 single-dh-use and hello retry on serverside.

bugs.title: Route domain not reachable (strict mode)
bugs.symptoms: Network flows are reset and errors are found in /var/log/ltm: Route domain not reachable (strict mode).
bugs.conditions: This might happen in either of the following scenarios: Scenario 1 ========== -- LTM with iRules configured. -- The iRule directs traffic to a node that is in a route domain. Scenario 2 ========== -- LTM with an LTM policy configured. -- The policy directs traffic to a node that is in a route domain.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not sent to the node that is in a route domain. The iRule 'node' method and/or LTM policy 'node' specification require a route_domain to be specified in order for the traffic to be sent to a node that is assigned to a route domain.
bugs.workaround: Specify the node along with Route domain ID. -- For iRules, change from this: when HTTP_REQUEST { node 10.10.10.10 80 } To this (assuming route domain 1): when HTTP_REQUEST { node 10.10.10.10%1 80 } -- For LTM policies, change from this: actions { 0 { forward select node 10.2.35.20 } } To this (assuming route domain 1): actions { 0 { forward select node 10.2.35.20%1 } }

bugs.title: TMM core due to wrong assert
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a core
bugs.conditions: AFM and AVR provisioned and collecting ACL statistics.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable the server-side statistics collection for the Network Firewall Rules using the following menu path: Security :: Reporting : Settings : Reporting Settings : Network Firewall Rules.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash related to ACL statistics

bugs.title: Prevention of Audit data loss
bugs.symptoms: Audit logs can consume all available partition space.
bugs.conditions: Audit logging enabled for a sufficient period of time
bugs.impact: Audit data loss when /var/log is full.
bugs.workaround: You can recover disk space by manually removing unneeded logs in /var/log/audit.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system periodically checks for free disk space at '/var/log'. If disk usage exceeds configured threshold and when software detects a possible problem with storing audit logs, all important processes are shut down to prevent generation of audit logs. If this occurs, the admin must manually recover the system.

bugs.title: Restarting MCPD via command line may not restart the aced process
bugs.symptoms: Configurations with secure ID authentication may face issues after restarting MCPD using the command line (bigstart restart mcpd).
bugs.conditions: Executing the "bigstart restart mcpd" from command line does not always restart the aced process.
bugs.impact: Configurations with secure ID authentication may face issues after restarting MCPD and may not restart the aced process.
bugs.workaround: "bigstart restart mcpd" is not the recommended way to restart MCPD. Please restart the BIG-IP system to reflect any changes you have made.

bugs.title: Platform FIPS power-up self test failures not logged to console
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system does not log FIPS power-up self-test failures to the console.
bugs.conditions: A FIPS failure occurs during the power-up self test.
bugs.impact: Platform FIPS failures are made more difficult to identify and diagnose, because the system console fails to include anything at all that indicates a failure.

bugs.title: BIG-IP resets HTTP/2 connections when a peer exceeds a number of concurrent streams
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP/2 protocol allows informing a peer about the number of concurrent streams it is allowed to have. When this number is exceeded, the RFC stipulates that the system must serve all open streams and then terminate a connection.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP system has a virtual server with an HTTP/2 profile configured on the client side. -- A client opens more streams than a configured value for concurrent-streams-per-connection in HTTP/2 profile.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP resets a connection and a client (browser) does not receive any response for outstanding requests. It requires manually reload of the webpage to address the issue.
bugs.fix: When a peer exceeds a number of concurrent streams allowed by BIG-IP systems, it sends GOAWAY with a REFUSED_STREAM error code and allows graceful completion of all open streams, and then terminates the connection.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing IPv6 NAT traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing IPv6 NAT traffic
bugs.conditions: -IPv6 NAT configured
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes IPv6 NAT traffic as expected.
bugs.workaround: Use smaller IPV6 prefixes in NAT Pool like /120, /128, and make sure there is at least one translation address DAG back to each TMM in the system after considering the dag-ipv6-prefix-length configuration.

bugs.title: IPsec: Changing MTU or PMTU settings on interface mode tunnel cores tmm
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when the maximum transmission unit (MTU) or 'Use PMTU' setting is changed while passing IPsec traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec tunnel configured and passing traffic. -- The MTU or 'Use PMTU' setting for the IPsec tunnel (in interface mode) is changed.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not change MTU or PMTU settings for the tunnel while it is passing traffic. The settings can be changed while passing traffic, but TMM may crash very soon after the change. If the settings are changed and TMM does not crash soon after, then it will not spontaneously crash at some later point.

bugs.title: With APM and AFM provisioned, single logout ( SLO ) fails
bugs.symptoms: SAML Single log out (SLO) fails on BIG-IP platforms. The SAML module on the BIG-IP system reports following error messages: -- SAML SSO: Error (12) Inflating SAML Single Logout Request -- SAML SSO: Error (12) decoding SLO message -- SAML SSO: Error (12) extracting SAML SLO message
bugs.conditions: Failures occur with Redirect SLO.
bugs.impact: SAML single logout does not work.
bugs.workaround: Use POST binding SLO requests.

bugs.title: GTM virtual servers have the wrong status
bugs.symptoms: GTM virtual servers have the wrong status (up when they should be down, or down when they should be up).
bugs.conditions: -- The GTM virtual servers are monitored with an HTTP or HTTPS monitor that performs HTTP status matching. -- The status code (for example, 200) being searched for in the response appears elsewhere than in the first line (for example, in a following header).
bugs.impact: The system incorrectly matches the status code in a response line which is not the Status-Line. As a result, the availability status reported for a virtual server may be incorrect. This may cause the GTM system to send traffic to unsuitable resources causing application disruptions.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by not performing HTTP status matching in your HTTP/HTTPS GTM monitors.
bugs.fix: The HTTP status code is now correctly searched only in the first line of the response.

bugs.title: 'Detected Violation' Field for event logs not showing
bugs.symptoms: Violation is missing/details not populated in the event log page, when a POST request with large number of parameters are sent to the BIG IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- A large POST request with lots of parameters is sent to BIG-IP system. -- 'Learn New Parameters' is enabled.
bugs.impact: You cannot see the violation details.
bugs.workaround: Disabling parameter learning helps. Note: This happens only with a large number of parameters. Usually it works as expected.
bugs.fix: The eventlog is reserving space for violations.

bugs.title: iControl SOAP Hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain condition, iControl SOAP does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: - Undisclosed conditions.
bugs.impact: iControl SOAP doe not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: iControl SOAP now follows current best practices.
bugs.workaround: On BIG-IQ we do not recommend customers to access iControl portal through a browser. In case, you need to access the iControl portal through browser, please open another browser session and close it after the use.

bugs.title: BWC: flows might stall when using dynamic BWC policy
bugs.symptoms: When multiple flows are passing through the single instance of BWC policy, one or more flows might stall for a few seconds or more. The fairness among the flows is also affected.
bugs.conditions: -- BWC dynamic policy is enabled. -- Multiple flows are passing through a single instance of the BWC dynamic policy.
bugs.impact: Some of the flows may stall.

bugs.title: Incorrect SYN re-transmission handling with FastL4 timestamp rewrite
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 profiles configured with the TCP timestamp rewrite option enabled does not treat retransmitted SYNs in a correct manner.
bugs.conditions: FastL4 profile with TCP timestamp rewrite option is in use.
bugs.impact: Timestamp on some TCP packets sent by BIG-IP systems might be incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Do not use TCP timestamp rewrite.

bugs.title: VCMP guests or F5OS tenants may experience constant clusterd restart after host upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Sometimes, when vCMP guests or F5OS tenants are started after the host has been upgraded, the guests or tenants may enter an unhealthy state due to clusterd constantly restarting.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP guest or F5OS tenant has Mirroring IP configured. -- vCMP guest or F5OS tenant is powered on after vCMP host upgrade. -- vCMP guest or F5OS tenant is powered on and receives a new license file from the host during startup.
bugs.impact: -- This issue might prevent the guest or tenant from servicing traffic if the system fails to load the config and clusterd keeps restarting. -- During startup of the guest or tenant, the following message is logged to /var/log/ltm: err mcpd[6519]: 0107146f:3: Self-device state mirroring address cannot reference the non-existent Self IP ([IP address]); Create it in the /Common folder first. -- /var/log/ltm shows clusterd constantly restarting. -- One or more slots are in INOPERATIVE state, while the host shows slots as RUN/Healthy.
bugs.workaround: -- To avoid the issue before it occurs: 1. Prior to shutting down vCMP guests or F5OS tenants before host upgrade, ensure guests or tenants have free space in the /var partition. 2. Ensure any license updates (e.g., reactivation) are applied before shutting down the vCMP guest or F5OS tenant. 3. Issue 'tmsh save sys config' on the vCMP guest or F5OS tenant. 4. Issue 'ls /var/db/mcp*' and confirm the presence of mcpdb.bin and mcpdb.info in the /var/db directory. 5. Proceed with vCMP guest or F5OS tenant shutdown and host upgrade as per standard F5 recommended process. -- To mitigate after the issue has been experienced on a vCMP guest or F5OS tenant: 1. Set the vCMP guest or F5OS tenant to the Configured state and wait for it to complete transition to Configured. 2. Set vCMP guest or F5OS tenant to Deployed state. 3. Review startup logs and confirm 'Self-device state mirroring address cannot reference the non-existent Self IP' message is no longer present. 4. Review /var/log/ltm and confirm clusterd is no longer restarting. 5. If issue persists, delete and recreate the vCMP guest or F5OS tenant.

bugs.title: Upgrading / Rebooting BIG-IP with huge address-list configuration takes a long time
bugs.symptoms: Version upgrade takes more time than usual when the config contains address-lists with a lot of IP addresses. The same delay will be observed with 'tmsh load sys config' as well.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure address-list with 10K to 20K IP addresses or address ranges or subnets. -- Configuration loading (e.g. Post upgrade, running tmsh load sys config, modification of the configuration and subsequent full load as in full config sync)
bugs.impact: Version upgrade / 'tmsh load sys config' process takes a long time than usual.
bugs.workaround: 1) Convert continuous individual addresses in the address-lists to IP address ranges and subnets if possible. 2) Remove the huge address-lists from config before the upgrade and add back after the upgrade process is finished. 3) Upgrading to a release or EHF that contains the fix for 1209409. 1209409 does not eliminate the issue but it does reduce the time it takes to validate certain address lists.

bugs.title: With mirroring enabled on a SIP virtual server, connections on the standby are reset with MBLB internal error (Routing problem)
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server with a SIP profile has mirroring enabled, connections on the standby unit will be removed shortly after being created. If tm.rstcause.log is enabled the reset cause message appears similar to the following: -- err tmm1[18383]: 01230140:3: RST sent from 10.2.207.208:5080 to 10.2.207.201:31597, [0x2c1c820:1673] MBLB internal error (Routing problem). -- err tmm1[18383]: 01230140:3: RST sent from 10.2.207.209:51051 to 10.2.207.202:5080, [0x2c1c820:931] MBLB internal error.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) running on 2000/4000 platforms using RSS hash. -- Platforms with more than 1 tmm.
bugs.impact: Mirrored connections on the standby unit are removed.
bugs.workaround: -- On BIG-IP VE, add the following to tmm_init.tcl on both units and restart tmm: ndal ignore_hw_dag yes

bugs.title: HSB diagnostics are not provided under certain types of failures
bugs.symptoms: In rare cases where the HSB detects an error and triggers an high availability (HA) failover, HSB-specific diagnostic data is not provided. An example are XLMAC errors, which can be seen in the LTM logs: <13> Jul 25 18:49:41 notice The number of the HSB XLMAC recovery operation 11 or fcs failover count 0 reached threshold 11 on bus: 3. <13> Jul 25 18:49:41 notice high availability (HA) failover action is triggered due to XLMAC/FCS erros on HSB1 on bus 3.
bugs.conditions: The HSB detects an internal error.
bugs.impact: There is less HSB data for analysis when an internal HSB occurs.
bugs.fix: Dump HSB registers on all HSB initiated high availability (HA) failovers.

bugs.title: Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object
bugs.symptoms: Creation of a security protocol-inspection profile via the CLI fails with an unclear error: 01070710:3: Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:ips_port_service_profile status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127
bugs.conditions: Create a security protocol-inspection profile on a BIG_IP without a "port".
bugs.impact: Unclear error on the TMSH that does not provide detail on the exact root cause of the failure.

bugs.title: Rules that share the same name return invalid JSON via REST API
bugs.symptoms: When retrieving rule stats on a firewall policy, if two rules that share the same name but one of which is directly attached to the policy while the other is attached via a rule list, then a invalid JSON is returned. The JSON has identical keys for each entry associated with the rule. This is an invalid JSON structure that cannot be parsed correctly (Or data for one of the rules is lost)
bugs.conditions: A firewall policy that has one of rule directly attached to the policy while the other is attached via a rule list, and both rules share the same name.
bugs.impact: Invalid JSON structure returned for stat REST API call
bugs.workaround: Ensure that no rule shares its name with another rule.

bugs.title: GTM HTTP/HTTPS monitors cannot be modified via GUI
bugs.symptoms: GUI reports an error when modifying DNS/GTM HTTP/HTTPS monitors: 01020036:3: The requested monitor parameter (/Common/http-default 2 RECV_STATUS_CODE=) was not found.
bugs.conditions: RECV_STATUS_CODE has never been set for the DNS/GTM HTTP/HTTPS monitors.
bugs.impact: Not able to make changes to DNS/GTM HTTP/HTTPS monitors through GUI.
bugs.workaround: If 'recv-status-code' has never been set, use tmsh instead. Note: You can set 'recv-status-code' using tmsh, for example: tmsh modify gtm monitor http http-default recv-status-code 200

bugs.title: Variable session.user.agent missing for Edge Client & F5 Access clients
bugs.symptoms: When connecting with Edge Client & F5 Access clients the BIG-IP APM session variable session.user.agent is missing from APM sessions.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM Edge Client & F5 Access clients
bugs.impact: Session variable session.user.agent cannot be used for BIG-IP APM Access Policy logic flows
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be used to generate a like session variable. For example: # This event fires once per session when ACCESS_SESSION_STARTED { log local0. "Setting User-Agent based on HTTP data - [HTTP::header User-Agent]" ACCESS::session data set session.custom.client.useragent [HTTP::header User-Agent] #Use this variable in the VPE to make some decision }

bugs.title: Non-empty fipserr files loaded from a UCS archive can cause a FIPS BIG-IP platform to remain offline
bugs.symptoms: Loading a UCS file with non-empty fipserr files can cause a FIPS-based system to remain offline.
bugs.conditions: -- Using a BIG-IP with a Platform FIPS license. -- Loading a UCS file with a non-empty fipserr file.
bugs.impact: System is completely offline with spurious 'fipserr' failures, even after loading the UCS file.
bugs.workaround: Before creating a UCS archive, truncate the following files so they have zero size: /config/f5_public/fipserr /var/named/config/f5_public/fipserr /var/dnscached/config/f5_public/fipserr This can be accomplished using a command such as: truncate -c -s0 /config/f5_public/fipserr /var/named/config/f5_public/fipserr /var/dnscached/config/f5_public/fipserr

bugs.title: SNMP request times out after configuring IPv6 trap destination
bugs.symptoms: SNMP request is times out.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens with TMOS version v15.1.0.4 or beyond after a IPv6 trap destination is configured.
bugs.impact: No response is returned for SNMP request.
bugs.workaround: Restart SNMP daemon by running the following TMSH command: restart sys service snmpd

bugs.title: IPv6-based bind (named) views do not work
bugs.symptoms: Bind does not match IPv6 addresses configured for a zone view, and returns REFUSED responses, rather than the expected answers. After enabling debug logging in bind (see K14680), the apparent source address of the IPv6 DNS requests shows as being in the fe80::/96 range, rather than the IPv6 source address that sent the request. For example: debug 1: client @0x579bf188 fe80::201:23ff:fe45:6701%10#4299: no matching view in class 'IN'
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP DNS is provsioned - One or more ZoneRunner views is defined using IPv6 addresses. - A DNS query is sent from an IPv6 source address
bugs.impact: You cannot use DNS views in bind (zonerunner) based on IPv6 addresses.
bugs.workaround: If possible, use only IPv4 addresses to define views for DNS queries

bugs.title: DNS/GTM daemon big3d does not accept ECDHE or DHE ciphers
bugs.symptoms: The DNS/GTM big3d daemon does not accept ECDHE or DHE ciphers.
bugs.conditions: Connections to big3d with ECDHE or DHE ciphers.
bugs.impact: ECDHE/DHE ciphers do not work with big3d.
bugs.workaround: Configure ciphers with RSA key exchange.

bugs.title: Nitrox5 SDK driver logging messages
bugs.symptoms: The system kernel started spontaneously logging messages at an extremely high rate (~3000 per second): Warning kernel: EMU(3)_INT: 0x0000000000000020 warning kernel: sum_sbe: 0 warning kernel: sum_dbe: 0 warning kernel: sum_wd: 0 warning kernel: sum_gi: 0 warning kernel: sum_ge: 0 warning kernel: sum_uc: 1 The above set of messages seems to be logged at about 2900-3000 times a second. These messages continue after TMM fails its heartbeat and is killed. The system is rebooted by the host watchdog.
bugs.conditions: These messages are triggered by Nitrox5 driver when EMU microcode cache errors corrected by hardware.
bugs.impact: High rate of logging messages. The tmm heartbeat eventually fails, and tmm is restarted. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Scp to /var/local/ucs or /var/local/scf is not allowed when fips140 or common criteria mode is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to Export/Import a file from the BIG-IP file path(s) /var/local/ucs or /var/local/scf via SCP, you receive an error dialog: "file not allowed"
bugs.conditions: -- fips140 or common criteria mode enabled -- Export/Import file from the BIG-IP file path(s) /var/local/ucs or /var/local/scf
bugs.impact: Import/Export file using scp tool from/to the BIG-IP file path(s) /var/local/ucs or /var/local/scf not allowed when fips140 or cc mode enabled even if the file is encrypted.

bugs.title: Retransmissions of the initial SYN segment on the BIG-IP system's server-side incorrectly use a non-zero acknowledgement number when Verified Accept is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: As the BIG-IP system attempts to open a TCP connection to a server-side object (e.g., a pool member), retransmissions of the initial SYN segment incorrectly use a non-zero acknowledgement number.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are true: -- Standard TCP virtual server. -- TCP profile with Verified Accept enabled. -- Receipt of the client's ACK (as part of the client-side TCP 3-way handshake) is delayed. Due to Verified Accept being enabled, this delay causes the BIG-IP system to retransmit its SYN to the server until the client's ACK is received.
bugs.impact: Depending on the specific server implementation, or the security devices present on the BIG-IP system's server-side before the server, a SYN containing a non-zero acknowledgement number may be rejected. In turn, this may cause connections to fail to establish.
bugs.workaround: If compatible with your application and specific needs, you can work around this issue by disabling Verified Accept in the TCP profile.
bugs.fix: SYN segment retransmissions now correctly use 0 as the acknowledgement number.

bugs.title: Invalid server-side SSL profile options can be configured in tmsh

bugs.title: Tomcat restarts with error java.lang.OutOfMemoryError
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, while trying to list a large configuration, tomcat restarts with error java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space due to a large read operation.
bugs.conditions: -- From the GUI, navigate to Local Traffic :: Pools :: Pool List. -- The configuration contains approximately 10,000 objects (objects include pools, nodes, virtual servers, etc.).
bugs.impact: When the system attempts to list the large configuration, tomcat restarts, resulting in 503 error.
bugs.workaround: Use the provision.tomcat.extramb database variable to increase the maximum amount of Java virtual memory available to the tomcat process. Impact of workaround: Allocating additional memory to Apache Tomcat may impact the performance and stability of the BIG-IP system. You should perform this procedure only when directed by F5 Technical Support after considering the impact to Linux host memory resources. -- Using a utility such as free or top, determine if you have enough free memory available to use this procedure. For example, the following output from the free utility shows 686844 kilobytes available: total used free shared buffers cachedMem: 16472868 15786024 686844 807340 827748 2543836 -/+ buffers/cache: 12414440 4058428 Swap: 1023996 0 1023996 -- View the current amount of memory allocated to the tomcat process by typing one of the following commands: ps | grep " -client" | egrep -o Xmx'[0-9]{1,5}m' The command output appears similar to the following example: Xmx260m Xmx260m -- View the current value of the provision.tomcat.extramb database variable by typing the following command tmsh list /sys db provision.tomcat.extramb -- Set the provision.tomcat.extramb database variable to the desired amount of additional memory to be allocated using the following command syntax: modify /sys db provision.tomcat.extramb value <MB> -- If the device is part of a high availability (HA) configuration, the provision.tomcat.extramb database value should be synchronized to the peer devices from the command line. To run the ConfigSync process, use the following command syntax: tmsh run /cm config-sync <sync_direction> <sync_group> For example, the following command pushes the local device's configuration to remote devices in the Syncfailover device group: tmsh run /cm config-sync to-group Syncfailover -- Restart the tomcat process by typing the following command: restart /sys service tomcat

bugs.title: Connections drop in virtual server with Immediate Action On Service Down set to Drop
bugs.symptoms: In a virtual server configured with Immediate Action On Service Down set to Drop and an iRule to pick a pool different from the one attached to the virtual server, if the default pool is attached in an offline state, connections are always dropped even when the default pool becomes available later.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server configured with Immediate Action On Service Down set to Drop. - An iRule selects a different pool from the one attached to the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Connections are silently dropped.
bugs.workaround: Change the virtual server's Immediate Action On Service Down setting to None.

bugs.title: The ip-tos-to-client setting does not affect traffic to the server.
bugs.symptoms: The ip-tos-to-client setting is intended to apply to client traffic only. Server traffic IP ToS values are configured on the pool using the ip-tos-to-server property. This is a change in behavior in that previously ip-tos-to-client was loosely interpreted to apply to server traffic as well if not overwritten by the pool.
bugs.conditions: The ip-tos-to-client value is set in the L4/L7 profile.
bugs.impact: IP ToS values in traffic to the server is unmodified.
bugs.workaround: Use the ip-tos-to-server property on pools to change IP ToS values to the server. Alternatively, use an iRule to set the IP ToS to the server. For example: when SERVER_CONNECTED { IP::tos 63 }

bugs.title: Flow fwd broken with statemirror.verify enabled and source-port preserve strict
bugs.symptoms: Flow forwarding does not work with statemirror.verify enabled and source-port is preserve strict. Depending on the number of tmms and the IP addresses/ports on the network, this causes return traffic to get dropped. Traffic captures show packets leaving the BIG-IP system on one tmm and being returned on another. The return traffic that encounters the second tmm is dropped.
bugs.conditions: -- Mirroring is enabled. -- High availability (HA) peer is connected. -- The source-port setting is preserve-strict. -- The statemirror.verify option is enabled. -- There is more than one tmm.
bugs.impact: Server-side return traffic to the BIG-IP is dropped. This causes connection timeouts and resets.
bugs.workaround: -- Disable statemirror.verify, disable source-port preserve-strict, disable mirroring. -- On BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE), add the following to tmm_init.tcl on both units and restart tmm: ndal ignore_hw_dag yes

bugs.title: In-TMM Monitors time out unexpectedly
bugs.symptoms: When using the in-TMM monitoring feature, monitored targets (nodes/pool members) may be marked DOWN unexpectedly if there is a delay in responding to ping attempts. Specifically, if the ping response from the target is delayed by more than the 'interval' value configured for the monitor, but less than the 'timeout' value configured for the monitor, the target may be marked DOWN.
bugs.conditions: This may occur when either: -- In-TMM monitoring is enabled (sys db bigd.tmm = enable) and the monitor type uses in-TMM monitoring; OR -- Bigd is configured to NOT reuse the same socket across consecutive ping attempts (sys db bigd.reusesocket = disable) AND: -- The monitored target does not respond to ping attempts within the 'interval' value configured for the monitor.
bugs.impact: The monitored target may be marked DOWN if it does not respond to ping attempts within the 'interval' value configured for the monitor, instead of within the 'timeout' value configured for the monitor.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, use one of the following methods: -- Disable in-TMM monitoring and enable bigd socket reuse (sys db bigd.tmm = disable, and sys db bigd.reusesocket = enable). -- Configure the monitor with an 'interval' value longer than the expected response time for the monitored target(s).

bugs.title: Support draft-thomson-quic-bit-grease-00
bugs.symptoms: This an improvement; there is no defect or known issue
bugs.conditions: This an improvement.
bugs.impact: This should have no impact on endpoints, but it will help to preserve future extensibility of the protocol.
bugs.workaround: If you wish to disable this function, you can set the db variable quic.bit.grease to 'disable'. When disabled, BIG-IP will neither advertise the ability to accept values other than '1', nor will it send values other than '1'. It will reject packets that set it to '0'. The reasons to disable would be that (1) something in the path is dropping packets with the greased bit, or (2) future evaluation of the draft shows that this in some way introduces a security or performance impact.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now fully implements draft-thomson-quic-bit-grease-00, an optional extension that allows the second bit in each QUIC packet to be a random value instead of always '1', if the client requests it.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP now fully implements draft-thomson-quic-bit-grease-00, an optional extension that allows the second bit in each QUIC packet to be a random value instead of always '1', if the client requests it. This should have no impact on endpoints, but it will help to preserve future extensibility of the protocol. If users wish to disable this function, they can set the db variable quic.bit.grease to 'disable'. When disabled, BIG-IP will neither advertise the ability to accept values other than '1', nor will it send values other than '1'. It will reject packets that set it to '0'. The reasons to disable would be that (1) something in the path is dropping packets with the greased bit, or (2) future evaluation of the draft shows that this in some way introduces a security or preformance regression.

bugs.symptoms: Running the command 'tmsh list /sys db scheduler.minsleepduration.ltm' shows that the value is -1. The db variable 'scheduler.minsleepduration.ltm' is set to -1 on mcpd startup. This overwrites a custom value.

When the db variable reverts to the default value of unset -1, tmm may use either more or less CPU cycles when idle depending on whether the original DB variable value is bigger or less than the default value.

bugs.title: Branch parameter not parsed properly when topmost via header received with comma separated values
bugs.symptoms: MRF SIP in LoadBalancing Operation Mode inserts a VIA header to SIP request messages. This Via header is removed from the returned response message. The VIA header contains encrypted routing information to route the response message. The SIP specification states that INVITE/CANCEL messages in a dialogue should contain the same branch header. The code used to encrypt the branch field returns a different branch ID for INVITE and CANCEL messages.
bugs.conditions: -- Enabling SIP Via header insertion on the BIG-IP system. -- SIP MRF profile. -- Need to cancel an INVITE. -- INVITE Via header received with multiple comma-separated values.
bugs.impact: Some SIP clients have code to verify the branch fields in the Via header. These clients expect the branch to be same for INVITE and CANCEL in a dialogue. Because the branch received is different, these clients are unable to identify the specific INVITE transaction. CANCEL is received and client sends a 481 error: SIP/2.0 481 Call/Transaction Does Not Exist.
bugs.workaround: Use iRules to remove the topmost Via header and add new a new Via header that uses the same branch as INVITE and CANCEL while sending messages to SIP clients.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system now ensures the branch field inserted in the via header same for INVITE and CANCEL messages.

bugs.title: TMM may prematurely shut down during initialization when a lot of TMMs and interfaces are configured on a VE
bugs.symptoms: TMM may prematurely shut down (during its initialization) when several TMMs and interfaces are configured. The system logs messages in one or more TMM log files (/var/log/tmm*): MCP connection aborted, exiting.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- Happens during TMM startup. -- The issue is intermittent, but is more likely to occur on systems with a lot of TMMs (more 20 in most cases) and several interfaces (approximately 8 or more).
bugs.impact: TMM shuts down prematurely. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. Possible deadlock and MCP restart loop requiring a full reboot of the BIG-IP device.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer shuts down prematurely during initialization.

bugs.title: OAuth refresh token not found
bugs.symptoms: When an OAuth client sends a refresh token to renew the access token, BIG-IP reports an error: err tmm[13354]: 01990004:3: /Common/my_OAuth_v1:Common: Request Refresh Token from Source ID ... failed. Error Code (id_not_found) Error Description (The refresh token is not found)
bugs.conditions: -- The refresh token expiration interval is longer than authcode and accesstoken. -- The Authorization code table entry does not exist because of an internal clearing/purging operation. -- tmm restarts or failover to standby thus losing refresh-token value from primarydb
bugs.impact: OAuth APM client end user fails to renew the access token even with a valid refresh token.
bugs.workaround: Clear/reset the Authorization code column value manually: As a root user run below BIG-IP shell (tmos)# list apm oauth db-instance apm oauth db-instance oauthdb { db-name <db_name> description "Default OAuth DB." } Copy the value corresponding to <db_name>. Log into mysql from the bash prompt: # mysql -u root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) mysql> use <db_name>; mysql> update master set auth_code = NULL where refresh_token='affected_refresh_token_id'; (Substitute the affected refresh token ID with affected_refresh_token_id in the previous command.)
bugs.fix: Do not report error if the Authorization code does not exist when a valid refresh-token/access-token exists.

bugs.title: Monpd restarts every few seconds due to missing of AVR database
bugs.symptoms: Monpd reports that it is constantly restarting. A message similar to the following will appear at the console: logger[2849]: Re-starting monpd
bugs.conditions: - There is a provisioned module that requires monpd - Another module is de-provisioned which wipes the mysql database. - May occur after an upgrade.
bugs.impact: Modules that rely on monpd will not be fully functioning.
bugs.workaround: Clearing AVR database will remove all existing statistics data. 1. Stop monpd: bigstart stop monpd 2. Clean data base: touch /var/avr/init_avrdb 3. Clean the statistics file are waiting to be loaded: cd /var/avr/loader rm -rf * 4. Start monpd: bigstart start monpd

bugs.title: TMM may be killed by sod when shutting down

bugs.impact: A core file is created in /var/core/.
