bugs.title: Syslog-ng hang may lead to unexpected reboot
bugs.symptoms: A syslog-ng issue with remote logging to an invalid remote syslog server may lead to unexpected reboot. The BIG-IP may unexpectedly reboot after a host watchdog timeout when syslog-ng gets hung up. Logs via syslog-ng are no longer written, though logging not via syslog-ng continues unaffected. This happens at the time of the last 'Syslog connection broken' in /var/log/messages before reboot. That message will appear without a preceding 'Syslog connection established' just before it with same timestamp. At this time syslog-ng typically spins, using near 100% CPU (just one core equivalent, not all CPU capacity on system). Typically things appear fine on rest of system - there will usually be adequate CPU and memory. Hours or days later graphs will have a gap of usually tens of minutes to hours before an unexpected reboot. Post reboot logs (in /var/log/sel for iSeries or ltm log otherwise) show this is a host watchdog reboot. After reboot the system runs correctly, though if the syslog-ng remote server was invalid this remains the case.
bugs.conditions: Invalid syslog-ng server configuration or broken connection from BIG-IP toward configured syslog-ng remote server. A server is configured as a remote syslog destination on the BIG-IP, but it or an intervening system responds to stream of log messages by breaking connection eg by sending ICMP port unreachable to BIG-IP. Syslog-ng will note the connection attempt and that it has broken usually in the same second, and do so every 60s when it retries. There may be many of these log pairs, repeating every minute in /var/log/messages, such as: Nov 25 03:14:01 localhost.localdomain notice syslog-ng[12452]: Syslog connection established; fd='14', server='AF_INET(192.168.1.1:514)', local='AF_INET(0.0.0.0:0)' Nov 25 03:14:01 localhost.localdomain notice syslog-ng[12452]: Syslog connection broken; fd='14', server='AF_INET(192.168.1.1:514)', time_reopen='60' The final log will of a broken connection only, usually one minute after the last established/broken pair. Nov 25 03:15:01 localhost.localdomain notice syslog-ng[12452]: Syslog connection broken; fd='14', server='AF_INET(192.168.1.1:514)', time_reopen='60'
bugs.impact: Very rarely syslog-ng hangs in a non-functional state. Sometimes, this may lead to an unexpected reboot of BIG-IP. Loss of logs before restart and traffic disrupted while BIG-IP restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure syslog-ng server configuration is valid, and that the server is reachable.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with syslog-ng hang occasionally causing a system restart.

bugs.title: iCall throws error: foreign key index (name_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database
bugs.symptoms: Reconfiguring existing iapp results in an error: 01070712:3: Values (ICALL_SCRIPT_/Common/my_send_stats) specified for tcl user proc graph (ICALL_SCRIPT_/Common/my_send_stats ICALL_SCRIPT_/Common/my_send_stats:escape_json): foreign key index (name_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database.
bugs.conditions: Reconfigure existing application while iCall is in use
bugs.impact: Modification of a running iCall script results in an error

bugs.title: Certificate instances tab shows incorrect number of instances in certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: The SSL Certificate instances tab shows an incorrect number of instances when the Cert name and the Key name match. This does not occur when the cert and key are different names.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL certificate and key names match -- Viewing the SSL certificate list in the GUI
bugs.impact: All the custom profiles will be listed when only select instances for ca-bundle cert are expected
bugs.fix: The correct number of instances of certificates is now displayed.

bugs.title: icrd_child may consume excessive resources while processing REST requests
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, icrd_child may consume excessive resources while processing REST requests
bugs.conditions: - Specially-crafted REST requests
bugs.impact: Increase in ICRD resource usage over time. Eventually host memory will be exhausted potentially leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: icrd_child now processes REST requests as expected.

bugs.title: Chunked responses with congested client connection may result in server-side TCP connections hanging until timeout.
bugs.symptoms: When an HTTP/2 profile is configured on the client side, chunked responses are always sent unchunked. When a connection to a client is congested, the BIG-IP system may not properly close established server-side connections causing subsequent HTTP/2 requests to stall.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server with an HTTP/2 profile configured on the client side. -- A server responds with a chunked response.
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 requests intermittently stall due to the existing server-side TCP connection remaining open.
bugs.workaround: Configure an HTTP profile on the client side with a value of 'unchunk' on the response-chunking option.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 requests no longer stall, as the server side TCP connection is properly closed.

bugs.title: Not able to add more than 6 NICs on VE running in Azure
bugs.symptoms: Azure BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) with more than 6 NICs fails to boot.
bugs.conditions: -- Standard_DS4_v2 Azure instance type. -- Mellanox ConnectX-3 ethernet controller. -- A greater-than-2-NIC template is used, for example https://github.com/F5Networks/f5-azure-arm-templates/tree/master/supported/standalone/n-nic/existing-stack/byol with "numberOfAdditionalNics" set. -- Accelerated networking is enabled on two or more NICs.
bugs.impact: Not able to boot BIG-IP VM with 8 NICs, which should be supported for Standard_DS4_v2 instance type: 8 vCPU 28 GiB 8 Max NICs Adding more NICs to the instance makes the device fail to boot.

bugs.title: Sensitive data is not masked after "Maximum Array/Object Elements" is reached
bugs.symptoms: If "Maximum Array/Object Elements" is reached and "JSON data does not comply with format settings" is detected, then all sensitive data after last allowed element is not masked.
bugs.conditions: Define JSON profile, set "JSON data does not comply with format settings" to blocking and set "Maximum Array/Object Elements" to desired value.
bugs.impact: Data after last allowed element is not masked.
bugs.fix: Now the values are masked.

bugs.title: Support IPS package downloads via HTTP proxy.
bugs.symptoms: IPS package download via HTTP proxy does not work. 2021-08-31 16:59:59,793 WARNING Download file failed. Retrying. -- The error repeats continuously.
bugs.conditions: -- The global db key 'sys management-proxy-config' is configured -- An IPS download is triggered
bugs.impact: The IPS IM package fails to download.
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: IPS package downloads can now be successfully performed through an HTTP proxy.

bugs.title: Mobile Security 'Rooting/Jailbreak Detection' now reads 'Rooting Detection'
bugs.symptoms: MobileSafe SDK does not support iOS jailbreak detection, so the GUI should refer only to Android Rooting Detection.
bugs.conditions: -- Fraud Protection Service (FPS) provisioned. -- FPS and MobileSafe Licensed.
bugs.impact: Introduces confusion when indicating that iOS jailbreak detection is supported, which it is not.
bugs.fix: Section now reads 'Rooting Detection'.

bugs.title: Restjavad restarting with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP configuration contains a large number of configuration, restjavad is restarting with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system with no extra memory given to restjavad. -- The configuration contains a large number objects.
bugs.impact: Restjavad restarts frequently due to OutOfMemory error.
bugs.workaround: To workaround the issue you need to give restjavad extra memory. To do so please perform the following steps: 1. On GUI go to System :: Resource Provisioning. The line for Management has a drop-down box for Small, Medium, or Large. Set this to Large. 2. Connect to CLI. Run the following commands: tmsh modify sys db restjavad.useextramb value true 3. Restart restjavad processes. bigstart restart restjavad

bugs.title: Unsupported option in /etc/resolv.conf causes failure to sync DNS Zone configuration
bugs.symptoms: The 'gtm_add' script fail to sync configuration information from the peer when 'options inet6' is present in /etc/resolv.conf.
bugs.conditions: The option 'options inet6' is used in /etc/resolv.conf.
bugs.impact: The 'gtm_add' script removes the current config and attempts to copy over the config from the remote GTM. When the remote copy fails, the local device is left without any config.
bugs.workaround: Remove the 'options inet6' from /etc/resolv.conf.

bugs.title: DTLS 1.0 support for PFS ciphers
bugs.symptoms: When using DTLS 1.0 the following two PFS ciphers are no longer negotiated and they cannot be used in a DTLS handshake/connection. * ECDHE-RSA-AES128-CBC-SHA * ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-SHA
bugs.conditions: DTLS 1.0 is configured in an SSL profile.
bugs.impact: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-CBC-SHA and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-SHA are unavailable.

bugs.title: Downgrading a FIPS-enabled BIG-IP system or running big3d_install results in a system halt
bugs.symptoms: The system fails during the boot-up process, reports a libcrypto validation error, and the system halts. The console will show this error: Power-up self-test failures: OpenSSL: Integrity test failed for libcrypto.so This occurs after one of the following: -- Upgrading a FIPS-enabled BIG-IP system, booting to a volume running an earlier software version -- Running big3d_install from a BIG-IP GTM configuration to a BIG-IP LTM On a FIPS-licensed BIG-IP LTM configuration, when checking the big3d version you may see something similar to this: /shared/bin/big3d -V fips.c:204:f5_get_library_path: failed to dlopen libcrypto.so.1.0.2za ./big3d version big3d Version 17.0.0.0.0.22 for linux
bugs.conditions: -- FIPS-licensed BIG-IP system. -- Upgrade. -- Boot into a volume running an earlier version of the software. Another way to encounter the issue is: -- FIPS-licensed BIG-IP LTM. -- BIG-IP DNS (GTM) device running a higher software version than the LTM. -- Run big3d_install from a BIG-IP GTM-configuration pointing to FIPS-licensed BIG-IP LTM configuration.
bugs.impact: System boots to a halted state or big3d may continuously restart.
bugs.workaround: Before booting to the volume with the earlier version, delete /shared/bin/big3d. Note: This issue might have ramifications for DNS/GTM support. DNS/GTM is not FIPS-certified. If the target software volume has already experienced this issue (the system boots to a halted state), addition to deleting /shared/bin/big3d, follow the instructions in K25205233: BIG-IP System halted while booting. Halt at boot after FIPS Integrity Check Result FAIL :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K25205233 . For additional information, see K29290121: Rollback after upgrade or big3d_install may cause FIPS to halt system on boot :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K29290121.

bugs.title: The iRule command node is not triggered in CLIENT_ACCEPTED with HTTP/2.
bugs.symptoms: The node iRule command causes the specified server node to be used directly, thus bypassing any load-balancing. However, with HTTP/2, the node command may fail to execute within the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event. This results in no traffic being sent to configured node.
bugs.conditions: -- A node command is used under CLIENT_ACCEPTED event. -- An HTTP/2 profile applied to virtual server. -- The HTTP/2 protocol in use.
bugs.impact: With HTTP/2 configured, the iRule node command fails to execute within the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event, causing no traffic to be sent to the desired node.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you may use HTTP_REQUEST event instead of CLIENT_ACCEPTED in iRule syntax.

bugs.title: Add embedded SR-IOV support for Mellanox CX5 Ex adapter
bugs.symptoms: The Mellanox CX5 Ex adapter is not supported by the BIG-IP with a tmm embedded SR-IOV network driver.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP Virtual Edition system configured to use one or more Mellanox CX5 Ex adapters in SR-IOV mode.
bugs.impact: Systems using a CX5 Ex adapter will have to use the sock driver rather than the Mellanox driver.
bugs.fix: Added the CX5 Ex device ID to the BIG-IP's Mellanox SR-IOV driver so that it can be used with that adapter.

bugs.title: Violations are detected for incorrect parameter in case of "Maximum Array/Object Elements" is reached
bugs.symptoms: False positive violations are detected for incorrect parameter in case of "Maximum Array/Object Elements" is reached with enabled "Parse Parameter".
bugs.conditions: "JSON data does not comply with format settings" and "Illegal meta character in value" violations are enabled and content profile parsing is enabled in ASM.
bugs.impact: False positives detected, such as "Illegal meta character in value" violation and attack signature for incorrect context.
bugs.fix: No false positives detected.

bugs.title: TMM core when using Multipath TCP
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, TMM might crash when processing MPTCP traffic.
bugs.conditions: A TCP profile with 'Multipath TCP' enabled is attached to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround other than to disable MPTCP.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer produces a core.

bugs.title: Subscriber Management is not working properly with IPv6 prefix flows.
bugs.symptoms: Flows for a PEM subscriber are not deleted from the system even after the subscriber is deleted.
bugs.conditions: When IPv6 prefix flows are configured on PEM (i.e., sys db variable tmm.pem.session.ipv6.prefix.len is configured with a value other than 128).
bugs.impact: Flows for a PEM subscriber are not deleted from the system even after the subscriber is deleted. Resources are not released from the system.

bugs.title: Improvement to getcrc tool to print cookie names when cookie attributes are involved
bugs.symptoms: The name provided by getcrc tool provides incorrect ASM cookie name when cookie attributes path or/and domain is/are present in response from server
bugs.conditions: This is applicable when domain and path cookie attributes are present in response from server
bugs.impact: ASM cookie name which is displayed is incorrect
bugs.fix: More options need to be added to getcrc tool such that it caters for path/domain cookie attribute/s

bugs.title: Occasional Nitrox3 ZIP engine hang
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the Nitrox3 ZIP engine hangs. In /var/log/ltm: crit tmm[12404]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Nitrox 3, Hang Detected: compression device was reset (pci 02:00.1, discarded 1). crit tmm[12404]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Zip engine ctx eviction (comp_code=0): ctx dropped.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP appliance that uses the Nitrox 3 hardware compression chip: 5xxx, 7xxx, 12250 and B2250. You can check if your platform has the nitrox3 by running the following command: tmctl -w 200 compress -s provider provider -------- bzip2 lzo nitrox3 <-------- zlib
bugs.impact: The Nitrox3 hardware compression system becomes unavailable and the compression mode switches to software compression. This can lead to high CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: Disable http compression

bugs.title: MCP restarts when deleting an application service with a traffic-matching-criteria
bugs.symptoms: After deleting an application service that contains a virtual server and a traffic-matching-criteria, the mcpd daemon crashes.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP application service configuration containing a virtual server with traffic-matching-criteria -- Application service is deleted
bugs.impact: Traffic and control plane disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an mcpd crash related to traffic-matching-criteria.

bugs.title: Memory leak in SWG
bugs.symptoms: A memory leak was observed in TMM during internal stress testing.
bugs.conditions: SWG provisioned. Real-world conditions are unknown.
bugs.impact: System can run out of memory resource.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Release execution context when done.

bugs.title: iRules LX - nodejs processes consuming excessive memory
bugs.symptoms: iRule LX nodejs processes can leak memory. The iRule LX plugin nodejs processes memory usage climbs over time and does not return to prior levels. You can check the iRule LX plugins memory usage using the command: tmsh show ilx plugin <PLUGIN_NAME>' under 'Memory (bytes): Memory (bytes) Total Virtual Size 946.8M Resident Set Size 14.5K
bugs.conditions: -- iRulesLX in use.
bugs.impact: iRule LX nodejs processes memory usage keeps growing. The unbounded memory growth can eventually impact other Linux host daemons.
bugs.workaround: Restart the iRule LX plugin that is leaking memory: tmsh restart ilx plugin <PLUGIN_NAME>

bugs.title: Video Traffic Management - ECN detection
bugs.symptoms: When congestion is experienced in the network, all end user client traffic is affected, including video traffic. Enabling Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) and setting the flow value ECN bits to 3 in the IP header helps to manage the congestion.
bugs.conditions: -- Congestion is experienced in the network -- Video traffic is affected.
bugs.impact: Congestion in the network is unresolved.
bugs.fix: With this feature enabled and if the flow value has ECN bits set to 3, the BIG-IP system applies the actions associated with the PEM Policy. In the PEM policy you can apply rate limiting to the applicable (existing video) traffic.

bugs.title: Brute Force breaks server's Post-Redirect-Get flow
bugs.symptoms: Brute Force breaks server's Post-Redirect-Get flow
bugs.conditions: ASM policy is attached to VS Brute force protection is enabled. CSI challenge or Captcha are in use. Server implements Post-Redirect-Get flow.
bugs.impact: Brute Force breaks server's Post-Redirect-Get flow
bugs.fix: Support PRG mechanism in brute force mitigations.

bugs.title: BD sometimes encounters errors related to TS cookie building
bugs.symptoms: BD sometimes print errors related to TS cookie building when receiving ASM cookies with account_id: -- BEM|ERR |May 19 17:49:55.800|0983|response_header_accumulator.c:0200|Error: CookieMgrBuildCookie failed. ans 1 job 2957561040. -- IO_PLUGIN|ERR |May 19 17:49:55.800|0983|io_plugin.c:3320|TMEVT_RESPONSE: Cannot build a ts cookie.
bugs.conditions: -- Cookie protection is enabled. -- The BIG-IP software is upgraded from a version that was earlier than 15.1.x.
bugs.impact: The cookie is not built and an error is logged.

bugs.title: Multiple resolutions are predicted for a single video playback.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP's traffic control prediction is calculated on all individual connections of a client's video stream.
bugs.conditions: - Video streaming client downloads, audio and video data is downloaded using multiple parallel connections.
bugs.impact: - Multiple resolutions will be detected on the BIG-IP for a single video playback.

bugs.title: Video resolution mis-predictions
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP's traffic playback resolution prediction is calculated on all individual connections of a client's video stream.
bugs.conditions: - Video streaming client downloads through BIG-IP - Video is downloaded using multiple connections.
bugs.impact: - Mis-prediction in the video resolution.

bugs.title: Video resolution mis-prediction
bugs.symptoms: Certain video traffic is not getting classified with high accuracy.
bugs.conditions: - Behavioral classifier for Classification Engine is enabled
bugs.impact: - Mis-predictions can lead to higher definition videos being categorized as low-definition videos and vice versa.

bugs.title: Logging Profiles do not disassociate from virtual server when multiple changes are made
bugs.symptoms: When multiple Logging Profiles profile changes are made in a single update, the previous Logging Profiles are not disassociated from the virtual server. Additionally, when an Application Security Logging Profile change is made, newly added Protocol Security Logging Profile settings do not take effect.
bugs.conditions: Multiple Logging Profile changes are made in a single update.
bugs.impact: The previous Logging Profiles are not disassociated from the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Perform each Log Profile change individually. For example, to change an Application Security Log Profile: 1. Remove the current association and save. 2. Add the new association and save again.

bugs.title: VE performance tests in Azure causes loss of connectivity to objects in configuration
bugs.symptoms: When performance tests are run on BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) in Microsoft Azure, the BIG-IP system loses all connectivity to the pools, virtual servers, and management address. It remains unresponsive until it is rebooted from the Azure console.
bugs.conditions: Running performance tests of VE in Azure.
bugs.impact: The GUI becomes unresponsive during performance testing. VE is unusable and must be rebooted from the Azure console.
bugs.workaround: Reboot from the Azure console to restore functionality.

bugs.title: Google Analytics shows incorrect stats, when Google link is redirected.
bugs.symptoms: When server respond with a redirect, ASM challenge makes Google Analytics stats appear as if they are 'Direct' instead of 'Organic'.
bugs.conditions: -- Google link is responded to (by the server) with a redirect. -- Bot defense profile or DoS Application profile attached to a virtual server with challenge mitigation enabled.
bugs.impact: Incorrect data is displayed in the Google Analytics dashboard.

bugs.title: Upgrading system using WAM TCP profiles may prevent the configuration from loading
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP is on version 13.1.0 through 15.1.x and has profiles in use that use wam-tcp-wan-optimized and/or wam-tcp-lan-optimized as parent profiles, then when the configuration is upgraded to 16.0.0, the configuration fails to load, with an error similar to: err mcpd[10087]: 01020036:3: The requested parent profile (/Common/wam-tcp-wan-optimized) was not found. On devices that are provisioned with not just the LTM module this may lead to an out of memory condition as the config load failure prevents memory provisioning completing leaving too little 4KB page (host) memory and too much huge page memory. If suffering memory pressure then management access to device will be sluggish or not possible.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from version 13.1.0 through 15.1.x. -- Using profiles derived from wam-tcp-wan-optimized and/or wam-tcp-lan-optimized.
bugs.impact: Configuration does not load.
bugs.workaround: Remove these profiles and adjust the configuration elements that use them accordingly. If it is difficult to work on the device it may be necessary to rollback to earlier version and make changes there. Usually it would be better then to delete newer software volume and reinstall it at which point the modified config will be copied across and installed on newer volume. Here are two examples: -- Copy the definition of 'wam-tcp-wan-optimized' from /defaults/wam_base.conf into /config/bigip.conf, and then reload the configuration. -- Change the references to wam-tcp-wan-optimized to something else in your config file (e.g., tcp-wan-optimized), and then reload the configuration.

bugs.title: Support for HTTP Trailers and gRPC
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP fails to properly process trailers when HTTP or HTTP/2 is configured on the virtual. This prevents the use of protocols such as gRPC that rely on such headers.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured for use with HTTP or HTTP/2 and receives a response that includes trailing headers.
bugs.impact: The trailing headers are dropped or ignored, preventing operation of protocols such as gRPC.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP traffic profiles commonly used for gRPC deployments now support trailing headers.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP traffic profiles commonly used for gRPC deployments now support trailing headers.

bugs.title: Firewall rule hit count reset occurs
bugs.symptoms: Firewall rule hit count experiences an unexpected reset.
bugs.conditions: Changing any rule when there is policy with a scheduled blob.
bugs.impact: Stats are reset on any change in any rule
bugs.workaround: To prevent the reset from occurring, delete all scheduled policies.

bugs.title: Non-mirrored persistence records may accumulate over time
bugs.symptoms: Persistence records accumulate over time due to expiration process not reliably taking effect. The 'persist' memory type grows over time.
bugs.conditions: -- Non-cookie, non-mirrored persistence configured. -- No high availability (HA) configured or HA connection permanently down. -- Traffic that activates persistence is occurring.
bugs.impact: Memory pressure eventually impacts servicing of traffic in a variety of ways. Aggressive sweeper runs and terminates active connections. TMM may restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Persistence records are now reliably expired at the appropriate time.

bugs.title: Virtual server rejects connections even though the virtual status is 'available'
bugs.symptoms: With certain configurations, a virtual server keeps rejecting connections with reset cause 'VIP down' after 'trigger' events occur.
bugs.conditions: Required Configuration: -- On the virtual server, the service-down-immediate-action is set to 'reset' or 'drop' and 'connection-limit' to be any (not 0). -- The pool member has rate-limit enabled. Required Conditions: -- Monitor flap, or adding/removing monitor or set the connection limit to be zero or configuration change made with service-down-immediate-action. -- At that time, one of the above events occur, the pool member's rate-limit is active.
bugs.impact: Virtual server keeps rejecting connections.
bugs.workaround: Delete one of the conditions. Note: The affected virtual server may automatically recover upon the subsequent monitor flap, etc., if no rate-limit is activated at that time.

bugs.title: After 'mosreboot', MOS fails to update grub default boot location back to TMOS
bugs.symptoms: MOS fails to update the grub boot location and reports errors: [ 21.85823] setup[697]: Use of uninitialized value $l_id in concatenation (.) or string at /usr/share/perl5/tm_install/Process.pm line 2739. [ 21.87256] setup[697]: error: boot entry .4 does not exist [ 21.87629] setup[697]: info: Switching to TMOS .4 for default boot selection.
bugs.conditions: When the 'mosreboot' command is given, the following three actions occur: 1. Updates the grub default boot location to point at MOS. 2. Reboots. 3. Within MOS, updates the grub default to point back at the previous (TMOS) boot location. Step 3 does not occur in the following scenario: -- The MOS version is from v15.0.0 or later. -- BIG-IP system is from v14.1.x or earlier.
bugs.impact: The 'mosreboot' results are not temporary, and rebooting from MOS when done causes the system to boot back into MOS again.
bugs.workaround: Use grub_default, or select a different boot location from the GRUB menu during boot. switch_root:/# grub_default -l HD1.3 active no default no title BIG-IP 13.1.1.5 Build 0.0.4 <HD1.3> HD1.4 active no default no title BIG-IP 14.1.2.6 Build 0.0.2 <HD1.4> switch_root:/# grub_default -b HD1.4 info: default boot location changed to HD1.4. [ 200.103744] EXT4-fs (dm-0): mounting ext2 file system using the ext4 subsystem [ 200.112743] EXT4-fs (dm-0): mounted filesystem without journal. Opts: (null) switch_root:/#

bugs.title: TCP proxy with ramcache and OneConnect can result in out-of-order events which stalls the flow
bugs.symptoms: Due to the client resending the request, the connection is not lost but is stalled for a considerable time.
bugs.conditions: -- virtual server running 16.0.0 with compression, caching, and OneConnect enabled. -- The request has 'Accept-Encoding: gzip ...; header -- The response has 'Cache-Control: no-cache' header. -- The response payload is equal to or greater than 1024 bytes (otherwise the default compression profile does not consider it).
bugs.impact: This causes slow response times for application users.
bugs.workaround: Unconfigure any of the following profiles: -- OneConnect -- HTTP compression -- Caching

bugs.title: Declarative onboarding unable to download and install RPM
bugs.symptoms: Installation of declarative onboarding RPM fails.
bugs.conditions: Use of icontrollx_package_urls in tmos_declared block to download/install RPMs via a URL.
bugs.impact: RPMs cannot be downloaded for declarative onboarding where RPMs are referenced via URL.
bugs.workaround: RPMs must be installed manually.
bugs.fix: The installation directory was updated to fix the RPM installation issue.

bugs.title: Certificate Managers are unable to move certificates to BIG-IP via REST
bugs.symptoms: You cannot upload a cert/key via the REST API if you are using a certificate manager account
bugs.conditions: -- Using the REST API to upload a certificate and/or key -- User is logged in as a Certificate Manager
bugs.impact: Unable to upload certificates as Certificate Manager
bugs.workaround: Use admin account instead of using Certificate Manager account to upload certs and keys

bugs.title: Dataplane INOPERABLE - Only 7 HSBs found. Expected 8
bugs.symptoms: During boot of a i15xxx system you see the message: Dataplane INOPERABLE - Only 7 HSBs found. Expected 8
bugs.conditions: There are no specific conditions that cause the failure. This can occur on any i15xxx device, although some devices exhibit the failure consistently around 50% of boots and others never exhibit the issue.
bugs.impact: When this failure occurs in a system, the system is inoperable.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for systems that do not have software capable of resetting the hardware device during the HSB load process.
bugs.fix: Updating the HSB load script to support resetting the hardware device during boot completely resolves this issue. The updated HSB loader can be implemented on all versions of BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Timestamp cookies do not work with hardware accelerated flows
bugs.symptoms: Time stamp cookies and hardware accelerated flows are mutually exclusive.
bugs.conditions: Time stamp cookie enabled for TCP flows on a VLAN with hardware offload enabled as well.
bugs.impact: Reduced traffic throughput and increased CPU usage
bugs.fix: FPGA and software enhancement to allow hardware accelerate of TCP flows that have time stamp cookie enabled.

bugs.title: Website slowness
bugs.symptoms: A website that is protected by FPS loads slow.
bugs.conditions: -- FPS is enabled -- Many elements are created dynamically via document.createElement
bugs.impact: Website responses are very slow
bugs.fix: Code fix along with BLFN function (C) { C.XX.checkInDomOnly = true; } to prevent from checking elements that are not in DOM

bugs.title: Heading or tailing white spaces of variable are not trimmed in configuration utility System Variable
bugs.symptoms: Bot Defense does not accept the system variables with heading or tailing white space.
bugs.conditions: Create a system variable with heading or tailing white space in, Security ›› Options : Application Security : Advanced Configuration : System Variables
bugs.impact: The HttpOnly cookie attribute is configured, but does not appear in TSCookie.
bugs.workaround: Create the system variables even with whitspaces through CLI, it omits the blank space from system variable name.

bugs.title: Rate limit and threshold configuration checks are inconsistent when applied to Basic DoS Vectors and Bad Actors DoS vectors
bugs.symptoms: Inconsistent configuration checks may result in configuration not being applied correctly.
bugs.conditions: DoS vectors configured on the BIG-IP

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources while processing HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: When processing HTTP traffic, TMM may consume excessive resources. When BIGIP handles HTTP traffic, it provides a possibility to compress payload. Under certain conditions TMM may consume its memory inefficiently, resulting in OOM situations.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server with http and httpcompression profiles. - Undisclosed conditions at backend server.
bugs.impact: TMM exhausts its memory and may deny legitimate traffic or delay processing traffic.
bugs.workaround: Remove httpcompression profile from a virtual's configuration.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Export of big Access Policy config from GUI can fail
bugs.symptoms: Export of Access Policy times out after five minutes and fails via the GUI
bugs.conditions: Exact conditions are unknown, but it occurs while handling a large access policy.
bugs.impact: Unable to redeploy configuration
bugs.workaround: Use thge cli to export the access policy: K30575107: Overview of the ng_export, ng_import and ng_profile commands https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K30575107

bugs.title: BIG-IP system cannot accept STARTTLS command with trailing white space
bugs.symptoms: When an SMTPS profile is applied on a virtual server and the SMTP client sends a STARTTLS command containing trailing white space, the BIG-IP system replies with '501 Syntax error'. The command is then forwarded to the pool member, which can result in multiple error messages being sent to the SMTP client.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server is configured with an SMTPS profile. -- The SMTP client sends a STARTTLS command with trailing spaces.
bugs.impact: The SMTP client is unable to connect to the SMTP server.
bugs.workaround: Use an SMTP client that does not send a command containing trailing white space.
bugs.fix: The system now handles trailing white spaces in SMTP STARTTLS command.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources when processing APM traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources when processing APM traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- APM provisioned. -- VPN tunnel configured and established. -- Undisclosed network conditions.
bugs.impact: TMM consumes excessive resources leading to terminated connections and potentially to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes APM traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Keyboard locks during Windows Edge client logon when just a control button is pressed.
bugs.symptoms: Using APM Edge client version 7210.2020.827.422-5307.0, users on Microsoft Windows cannot type in the login window.
bugs.conditions: -- Edge Client for Windows. -- The CTRL key is pressed in the login dialog.
bugs.impact: The Edge Client user is unable to type anything until they press the CTRL button one more time.
bugs.workaround: The APM end user must press the CTRL button a second time.

bugs.title: Local users database can sometimes take more than 5 minutes to sync to the standby device
bugs.symptoms: Local db sync to standby devices take more than 5 minutes to sync
bugs.conditions: High availability (HA) setup - add a local db user in the active device - Wait for it to get synced to the standby device - Sometimes the sync may not happen in 5 minutes.
bugs.impact: Sync of the changes to the local user db may take several minutes to sync to the standby devices.

bugs.title: APM PRP LDAP Group Lookup agent has a syntax error in built in VPE expression
bugs.symptoms: PRP LDAP Group Lookup agent, the expression incorrectly places the 'string tolower' outside the square brackets. This causes an issue in the GUI of the LDAP Group Lookup object where the 'Simple' branch rules do not show up. You see this 'Warning': Warning, this expression was made manually and couldn't be parsed, please use advanced tab.
bugs.conditions: Configure PRP with the LDAP Group Lookup agent in the Visual Policy Editor (VPE).
bugs.impact: Tcl expression containing a syntax error prevents the LDAP Group Lookup agent from functioning properly.
bugs.workaround: Go to the LDAP Group Lookup agent advanced tab and change this: expr {[string tolower [mcget {session.ldap.last.attr.memberOf}]] contains string tolower["CN=MY_GROUP, CN=USERS, CN=MY_DOMAIN"]} To this: expr {[string tolower [mcget {session.ldap.last.attr.memberOf}]] contains [string tolower "CN=MY_GROUP, CN=USERS, CN=MY_DOMAIN"]} Click finish. Now you can click 'change', and use the 'Simple' tab and the 'Add an expression using presets' option.
bugs.fix: The syntax error in built in VPE expression of LDAP Group Lookup agent is fixed

bugs.title: Trunk interface support added for L2wire on BIG-IP Virtual Edition
bugs.symptoms: L2wire on BIG-IP Virtual Edition works with non-trunked interfaces. Trunk interfaces are not supported. Packets ingressing on a trunk are not bridged properly to the egress side.
bugs.conditions: Basic L2-wire on BIG-IP Virtual Edition with trunk interface.
bugs.impact: Trunk interfaces were not supported for L2wire deployments on BIG-IP Virtual Edition.
bugs.fix: Trunk Support in BIG-IP Virtual Edition L2WIRE added.

bugs.title: Inconsistency in node object name and node IPv6 address when IPv6 pool-member is created without providing node object name.
bugs.symptoms: When using Ansible to create a pool that contains an IPv6 pool member, you get an error: 0107003a:3: Pool member node and existing node cannot use the same IP Address.
bugs.conditions: -- Creating a new pool via Ansible. -- A new IPv6 pool member is used. -- The IPv6 pool member's name is not included.
bugs.impact: Pool creation fails.
bugs.workaround: If you are unable to specify the pool member name, you can use other available configuration tools like tmsh, the GUI, or AS3.

bugs.title: Unspecified HTTP/2 traffic may cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, HTTP/2 traffic may cause TMM to crash
bugs.conditions: - http2 profile attached to virtual server
bugs.impact: Traffic processing impacted while the TMM process restarts, possible failover event.

bugs.title: Tmm crash in cipher group delete.
bugs.symptoms: Deleting a cipher group associated with multiple profiles could cause tmm crash.
bugs.conditions: Deleting a cipher group associated with multiple profiles.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with cipher group delete.

bugs.title: Mcpd crash when bulk deleting Bot Defense profiles
bugs.symptoms: When bulk deleting a large number of Bot Defense profiles (around 450 profiles) using TMSH, mcpd could crash.
bugs.conditions: This can be encountered during bulk delete of Bot Defenese profiles via tmsh.
bugs.impact: Crash of mcpd causing failover.
bugs.workaround: Delete the Bot Defense profiles in smaller batches to avoid the possible crash.
bugs.fix: There is no longer a crash of mcpd when deleting a large number of Bot Defense in a bulk using TMSH.

bugs.title: Web-Socket request with JSON payload causing core during the payload parsing
bugs.symptoms: Any web-socket request with JSON payload may cause a core witihin the JSON parser, depending on the used machine memory distribution.
bugs.conditions: Depends on the memory distribution of the used machine. Sending web-socket request with JSON payload to the backend server.
bugs.impact: BD crash while parsing the JSON payload.
bugs.fix: No crashes during JSON payload parsing.

bugs.title: REST framework support for IPv6 ConfigSync addresses
bugs.symptoms: In an HA sync environment, the REST framework reads the ConfigSync IP address retrieved through the tm/cm/device iCRD API. For an IPv6 address, the REST framework discards the related device certificate, which leads to the REST/gossip/sync failure.
bugs.conditions: Add support for IPv6 ConfigSync IP addresses in the REST framework in an HA sync environment.
bugs.impact: For an IPv6 address, the REST framework discards the related device certificate, which leads to the REST/gossip/sync failure.
bugs.fix: Valid device trust certificates are created with their name set to uniquely generated IPv4 address from the given IPv6 address. This helps in establishing the trust between the hosts thereby eliminating the REST/Gossip-sync failures.

bugs.title: Issues in verification of Bot Defense with F5 Anti-Bot Mobile SDK
bugs.symptoms: Verification may be incomplete when using the F5 Anti-Bot Mobile SDK with the Bot Defense profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the Bot Defense profile together with the F5 Anti-Bot Mobile SDK. -- Enabling the Mobile Applications section in the profile.
bugs.impact: Mobile application verification may be incomplete.

bugs.title: LDAP monitor's test functionality has an incorrect and non-modifiable IP address field in GUI
bugs.symptoms: While trying to use the monitor test page in the GUI for an LDAP monitor, the destination address field contains the value *.*(asterisk-dot-asterisk), and it is not editable.
bugs.conditions: -- Create an LDAP monitor. -- Go to the Test page.
bugs.impact: You are unable to modify the test destination address for the LDAP monitor.
bugs.workaround: Use TMSH. -- To run the test: tmsh run /ltm monitor ldap <LDAP-Monitor-Name> destination <IP-Address> Example: tmsh run /ltm monitor ldap myldap destination 10.10.10.10:389 -- To check test results: tmsh show /ltm monitor ldap <LDAP-Monitor-Name> test-result tmsh show /ltm monitor ldap myldap test-result

bugs.title: OAuth crash
bugs.symptoms: OAuth crashes during the authorization process
bugs.conditions: This can occur while under heavy authorization load.
bugs.impact: Authorization disrupted while oauth restarts
bugs.fix: Added the null checks while sending the sql db query to fix this issue

bugs.title: Full sync failure for traffic-matching-criteria with port list under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: Performing a full configuration sync with traffic-matching-criteria (TMC) under specific conditions fails with errors similar to: err mcpd[6489]: 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:traffic_matching_criteria_port_update status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127. err mcpd[6489]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/Failover to commit id 245 6869100131892804717 /Common/tmc-sync-2-bigip1.test 0 failed with error 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:traffic_matching_criteria_port_update status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127..
bugs.conditions: This may occur on a full-load config sync (not an incremental sync) On the device receiving the ConfigSync: - a traffic-matching-criteria is attached to a virtual server - the traffic-matching-criteria is using a port-list On the device sourcing the ConfigSync: - the same traffic-matching-criteria is attached to the same virtual server - the original port-list is modified (e.g. a description is changed) - the TMC is changed to reference a _different_ port-list
bugs.impact: Unable to sync configurations.
bugs.workaround: Copy the "net port-list" and "ltm traffic-matching-criteria" objects from the source to target system, merge them with "tmsh load sys config merge", and then perform a force-full-load-push sync from source to target. If the BIG-IP systems are using device groups with auto-sync enabled, disable auto-sync temporarily while performing this workaround. 1. On the source system (the system whose configuration you want to sync to peer), save the configuration and extract the ltm traffic-matching-criteria and port-lists: tmsh save sys config (shopt -s nullglob; echo "#"; echo "# $HOSTNAME"; echo "# generated $(date +"%F %T %z")" cat /config{/partitions/*,}/bigip{_base,}.conf | awk ' BEGIN { p=0 } /^(ltm traffic-matching-criteria|net port-list) / { p=1 } /^}/ { if (p) { p=0; print } } { if (p) print; } ' ) > /var/tmp/portlists-and-tmcs.txt 2. Copy /var/tmp/portlists-and-tmcs.txt to the target system 3. On the target system, load that file: tmsh load sys config replace file /var/tmp/portlists-and-tmcs.txt 3a. If loading the config file on the target system fails with the same error message seen during a ConfigSync, follow the procedure in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K13030. tmsh save sys config clsh touch /service/mcpd/forceload clsh reboot 4. On the source system, force a full-load sync to the device-group: tmsh run cm config-sync force-full-load-push to-group <name of sync-group>

bugs.title: 'Upper Bound' and 'Lower Bound' thresholds are not displayed in Connections line chart
bugs.symptoms: On the dashboard, the line chart of 'Throughput', 'CPU Usage', and 'Memory Usage' can show the line of thresholds that indicates 'Upper Bound' and 'Lower Bound', but there is no line of thresholds on the line chart of 'Connections'.
bugs.conditions: Create a custom line chart for 'Connections' that includes 'Upper Bound' and 'Lower Bound'.
bugs.impact: Line Chart of 'Connections' does not display 'Upper Bound' and 'Lower Bound' thresholds.

bugs.title: IKEv1 IPsec in interface-mode may fail to establish after ike-peer reconfiguration
bugs.symptoms: After changing an element of the ike-peer configuration, such as the pre-shared secret, the related IPsec interface mode tunnel can no longer forward packets into the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: -- IKEv1. -- IPsec policy in interface mode. -- Configuration change or a new configuration.
bugs.impact: When the problem is exhibited on a BIG-IP Initiator, ISAKMP negotiation fails to start when interesting traffic arrives. No messages are written to /var/log/racoon.log. When the problem is exhibited on a BIG-IP Responder, the IPsec tunnel successfully establishes, but the BIG-IP fails to forward any interesting traffic into the established tunnel. No useful log messages are seen. Note: 'Interesting traffic' is packets that match a traffic-selector.
bugs.workaround: Run 'bigstart restart tmm' or reboot.

bugs.title: Allow 32-bit processes to use larger area of virtual address space
bugs.symptoms: -- The mcpd daemon terminates due to lack of memory -- The merged daemon logs 'Cannot allocate memory' error
bugs.conditions: -- May be caused by large configurations -- May be caused by heap fragmentation over time
bugs.impact: 32-bit processes may fragment/exhaust their heaps and may not have sufficient contiguous memory to function correctly. Note that the only two 32-bit processes where this has been seen on are mcpd and merged.
bugs.fix: Using a different memory layout for 32-bit processes allows them to use more of the virtual address space.

bugs.title: B4450 blade reboot
bugs.symptoms: In a rare scenario, a B4450 blade suddenly reboots.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when there is heavy traffic load on VIPRION B4450 blades. The root cause is unknown. It happens extremely rarely.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while the blade reboots.
bugs.fix: The system now monitors the pause frames and reboots when needed.

bugs.title: Neurond continuously restarting
bugs.symptoms: Neurond continuously restarts.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP iSeries hardware platform -- issuing the command "service --status-all"
bugs.impact: Neuron communications will be impacted
bugs.fix: Fix for handling neurond.init script treating unknown arg as "start": Added code for default case to handle all unknown args

bugs.title: Reopening the publisher after a failed publishing attempt
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes repeatedly on SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: This can occur after a HSL disconnect and re-connect.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: The system publishes data to HSL publisher on a second attempt successfully (after a reconnect).

bugs.title: ASM attack signature does not match
bugs.symptoms: When processing certain traffic, ASM attack signatures may not match as intended.
bugs.conditions: - ASM enabled - Undisclosed attack signature variation
bugs.impact: ASM attack signature does not match or trigger further processing.
bugs.fix: ASM now processes traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Incorrect Error message in /var/log/ltm when HTTP::respond is used in ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT iRule event
bugs.symptoms: When HTTP::respond is used in ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT in iRule event, an error message "http_process_state_prepend - Invalid action:0x10a071 clientside" is observed in /var/log/ltm log. Since HTTP::respond is not supported in ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT, a better tcl error should be shown in /var/log/ltm like "TCL error: /Common/AVScan_Content <ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT > - Illegal argument. Can't execute in the current context"
bugs.conditions: This can occur when HTTP::respond is used in ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT: when ADAPT_REQUEST_RESULT { if {[ADAPT::result] contains "respond"} { HTTP::respond 403 -version auto ... } }
bugs.impact: TCL error messages don't give adequate information to explain what triggered the TCL error.

bugs.title: Support challenge response agent to handle Access-Challenge when Logon agent is not in policy
bugs.symptoms: In case of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), the challenge response is handled by the 401 response agent, in the following scenario: -- The policy does not have logon page agent. -- AAA/Radius server action is configured to send challenge response to the client. -- The policy has a 401 response logon agent. The APM end user client sees the credentials popup for 401 response. After entering and sending credentials (challenge response code received from RSA server via email or SMS), the Access Policy action fails.
bugs.conditions: -- Challenge response via RSA server or other. -- Logon Page logon agent not implemented.
bugs.impact: Unable to use challenge response sent by RSA (or AAA RADIUS server).

bugs.title: Maximum remaining session's time on user's webtop can flip/flop
bugs.symptoms: When an Access Policy is configured with Maximum Session Timeout, the rendered value of maximum remaining session's time can flip/flop in seconds on a user's webtop
bugs.conditions: Access Policy is configured with Maximum Session Timeout >= 60000 secs
bugs.impact: End users will see the remaining time being continually reset.
bugs.fix: Rendering of value for maximum remaining session's time is fixed

bugs.title: Missing SNI information when using non-default domain https monitor running in TMM mode.
bugs.symptoms: In-TMM https monitors do not send the SNI (Server Name Indication) information for non-default route domain pool members. In-TMM monitors do not send any packet when TLS1.3 monitor is used.
bugs.conditions: -- SNI is configured in serverssl profile -- serverssl profile is assigned to in-tmm https monitors -- https monitors are monitoring pool members that are in a non-default route domain. - Another Condition : TLS1.3 Monitor is used
bugs.impact: The TLS connection might fail in case of SNI No SYN packet is sent in case of TLS1.3 monitor

bugs.title: SSL monitor stuck does not change TLS version
bugs.symptoms: The SSL monitor remains in the current TLS version and does not switch to another version when a server changes.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL monitor configured. -- Server configuration changes from TLSv1.2 to TLSv1.
bugs.impact: Pool members marked down.
bugs.workaround: Use the In-TMM monitor.

bugs.title: Session variable for Group SIDs (in Kerberos Auth agent) and Group Names (in AD Group SID Resolver agent) has a max limit
bugs.symptoms: According to Microsoft (see https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/windows-security/logging-on-user-account-fails), logging on a user account that is a member of more than 1,010 groups (or close to that range) may fail on a Windows Server-based computer. So session variable for group SIDs in Kerberos Auth agent has max limit around 256KB. Also session variable for group names in AD Group SID Resolver agent has max limit of 384KB.
bugs.conditions: 1. User account is a member of more than 1,010 groups (or close to this range) 2. Concatenated group names for the user's group membership is more than 384KB
bugs.impact: 1. User is unable to log in to windows account 2. User is denied access to the resource protected by the APM policy
bugs.workaround: 1. Reduce user's group membership 2. Shorten the DNs for the groups
bugs.fix: The user group SIDs max limit is enforced by Microsoft. The user group names max limit is enforced by BIG-IP APM to protect system resources.

bugs.title: Dynamic CRL checking for client certificate is not working when TLS1.3 is used.
bugs.symptoms: In SSL reverse proxy, dynamic CRL checking for client certificate is not working when TLS 1.3 handshake is used. The SSL handshake successfully completed even though the client certificate is revoked.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic CRL checking enabled on a client-ssl profile -- The client-side SSL handshake uses TLS1.3.
bugs.impact: The handshake should fail but complete successfully
bugs.fix: The issue was due to Dynamic CRL revocation check has not been integrated to TLS 1.3. After the Dynamic CRL checking is integrated to TLS 1.3, the TLS handshake will work as expected.

bugs.title: BD_XML logs memory usage at TS_DEBUG level
bugs.symptoms: There are two messages in BD_XML logs that the system reports at the TS_DEBUG log level, but they should be logged as TS_INFO. BD_XML|DEBUG |Sep 10 14:51:19.335|1456|xml_validation.cpp:1687|after create of profile 754. (xml memory 5111702493 bytes) BD_XML|DEBUG |Sep 10 14:51:19.335|1456|xml_validation.cpp:1586|add profile 755. name: /ws/replanifierIntervention_V1-0 is soap? 1 (xml memory before add 5111702493 bytes)
bugs.conditions: These messages can occur when XML/JSON profiles are configured.
bugs.impact: Messages that should be logged at the TS_INFO level are logged at the TS_DEBUG level. These are informational log messages.
bugs.fix: The relevant two BD_XML logs are now categorized as TS_INFO.

bugs.title: License activation through proxy server uses IP address in proxy CONNECT, not nameserver
bugs.symptoms: License activation http/https request has the license server IP address instead of license server domain name.
bugs.conditions: When the proxy server and proxy port are configured and delete default management route.
bugs.impact: This causes your proxy server to disallow the connection

bugs.title: Apache configuration file hardening
bugs.symptoms: Apache configuration file did not follow security best practice.
bugs.conditions: Normal system operation with httpd enabled.
bugs.impact: Apache configuration file did not follow security best practice.
bugs.fix: Apache configuration file has been hardened to follow security best practice.

bugs.title: HTTP2 send RST_STREAM when exceeding max streams
bugs.symptoms: If the SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS setting is exceeded, BIG-IP sends a GOAWAY frame; however, browsers expect a RST_STREAM and the GOAWAY frame results in a half-rendered web page.
bugs.conditions: The maximum streams setting is exceeded on a HTTP/2 connection.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP sends a GOAWAY frame, and the browser shows a half-rendered page.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now sends a RST_STREAM if the maximum streams setting is exceeded.

bugs.title: Admd restarting constantly. Out of memory due to loading malformed state file
bugs.symptoms: Admd consumes more than 10GB of RSS Wrong signature statistics and possible memory corruption, potentially results in high memory consumption.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from 13.x, 14.x to 15.x -- Device service clustering configuration -- App-Protect-DOS signatures configured.
bugs.impact: ADMD not working, ADMD constantly restarting, consuming all of the system memory. Out of memory. ADMD killed due to memory consumption
bugs.workaround: Make sure that all the devices within a cluster are running compatible state file version (either all with versions before 15.1.0.x or after), if not, then: 1. Stop ADMD on all of those devices: bigstart stop admd 2. Upgrade or Downgrade the BIG-IP version to match the above criteria. 3. Remove the old state files: rm -rf /var/run/adm/* 4. Start ADMD: bigstart start ADMD If there is an issue on a single blade device, then: 1. Stop ADMD on all of those machines: bigstart stop admd 2. Remove the old state files: rm -rf /var/run/adm/* 3. Start ADMD: bigstart start ADMD
bugs.fix: No more memory corruption, no OOM nor ADMD restarts.

bugs.title: Improper IP based access access restrictions via HTTPD
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions HTTPD IP based access restriction may work improperly.
bugs.conditions: When using HTTPD IP based access restriction.
bugs.impact: Improper restriction based on IP address
bugs.fix: IP Access restrictions for HTTPD now works properly
bugs.behavior: IP Access restrictions for HTTPD now works properly

bugs.title: HTTPS monitor fails due to missing ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-SHA
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade, the 'DEFAULT' cipher in the server SSL profile attached to the HTTPS monitor does not include the ECDHE-RSA-AES256-CBC-SHA cipher suite in the Client Hello.
bugs.conditions: After upgrade, HTTPS monitor cipherlist is read from server SSL profile ciphers and set to DEFAULT after upgrade.
bugs.impact: 1. Upgrade breaks the SSL pool monitoring. 2. It is also possible that the pools monitoring succeeds but with unexpected ciphers from the 'DEFAULT' list which may cause increased resource usage or unexpectedly weaker encryption. Note: The ciphers negotiated between the HTTPS backend being monitored and the server SSL profile will still belong to the 'DEFAULT' list.
bugs.workaround: BIG-IP provides ways to customize the cipher string used by the server SSL profile. Via the configuration utility: https://techdocs.f5.com/en-us/bigip-15-0-0/big-ip-ltm-configuring-custom-cipher-string-for-ssl-negotiation/configuring-a-custom-cipher-string-for-ssl-negotiation.html Via tmsh commands: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K65292843

bugs.title: BGP may advertise default route with incorrect parameters
bugs.symptoms: If a BGP neighbor is configured with 'default originate,' the nexthop advertised for the default route may be incorrect.
bugs.conditions: -- Dynamic routing enabled. -- Using BGP. -- BGP neighbor configured with 'default originate'.
bugs.impact: The default route advertised via BGP is not acceptable to peers until the BGP session is cleared.
bugs.workaround: In imish, run the command: clear ip bgp <affected neighbor address>
bugs.fix: BGP suppresses a route advertisement between BGP speakers configured in the same AS with the same router-id.
bugs.behavior: BGP now suppresses a route advertisement between BGP speakers configured in the same AS with the same router-id. Previously, the route was not acceptable to peers until the BGP session was cleared, resulting in potentially incorrect parameters.

bugs.title: BIG-IP must be able to set CA=True when creating Certificate Signing Requests from TMSH.
bugs.symptoms: A Certificate Signing Request (CSR) is generated on the BIG-IP device to be used to create a certificate. It is possible for the entity owning the just-created certificate to serve as a Certificate Authority (CA) and be able to issue certificates and private keys to other parties. However, that ability does not exist unless the certificate has the CA field set to True (by default it is set to False).
bugs.conditions: In the TMSH prompt on the Command Line Interface (CLI), an attempt is made to generate a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) to be used to eventually create a certificate and corresponding private key.
bugs.impact: Without this change, certificates and private keys generated on the BIG-IP device cannot be directly provided to certification authorities so they can be used to sign certificates they would issue to other parties.
bugs.workaround: This is a new facility, not provided before, and overcomes a limitation. Without this facility, existing users of the BIG-IP are not impacted at all. As such, there is no workaround applicable.
bugs.fix: This fix enables certificates and private keys generated on the BIG-IP device via CSR's to be directly provided to certification authorities for their use. Because the CA field is set to now True, this fix adds convenience for certification authorities.

bugs.title: Loop between keymgmtd and mcpd causes BIG-IP to be out of sync or in constant automatic config sync
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system constantly downloads the certificate bundle if the CA-bundle manager config includes a URL. Symptoms are different depending on if BIG-IP systems is in a manual or automatic sync device group. Manual sync device groups will not stay in sync. Automatic sync device groups will constantly sync.
bugs.conditions: The CA-bundle manager is configured.
bugs.impact: The keymgmtd and mcpd process gets into a loop that causes constant config changes and if the ca-bundle-manager includes a URL, the BIG-IP system constantly downloads the bundle.
bugs.workaround: The ca-bundle manager should be configured without the update-interval(i.e. update-interval value set to 0) and while updating set the update-now to YES For config sync between peers 1.If the config sync type is set to manual full/incremental Then manually sync the devices either in GUI or TMSH 2.If the config sync type is set to Automatic Then bundle manager will be synced without any manual intervention

bugs.title: [APM][tmm core detected oauth_send_response in APM Oauth Token generation
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes while passing APM traffic.
bugs.conditions: OAuth is configured and is used for Token generation.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: An incorrect LTM policy rule may be matched when a policy consists of multiple rules with TCP address matching conditions.
bugs.symptoms: An incorrect LTM policy rule is picked up e.g. a rule which should match first is omited.
bugs.conditions: Policy contains multiple rules which employ TCP address matching condition.
bugs.impact: Inocorrect LTM policy is applied.

bugs.title: Live update cannot resolve hostname if ipv6 is configured
bugs.symptoms: Live update is not working when BIG-IP DNS is configured to use IPv6
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP DNS uses IPv6
bugs.impact: -- Unable to install latest updates to signatures. -- Unable to import user-defined signatures.
bugs.workaround: If possible, use IPv4 for DNS.
bugs.fix: Replaced deprecated gethostbyname which does not work well with IPv6 with getaddrinfo

bugs.title: Remote logging conditions adjustments
bugs.symptoms: When "Null in multi-part" violation is detected, BIG-IP logs it to remote log even when the violation is not set to blocked in Learning and Blocking settings
bugs.conditions: This happens when "Null in multi-part" violation is detected
bugs.impact: Incorrect logging to remote logs
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where BIG-IP was incorrectly sending "Null in multi-part" logs to remote logs.

bugs.title: Tmm crash when multiple virtual servers are created, modified, or deleted in quick succession
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes during a configuration change.
bugs.conditions: This occurs under the following conditions: -- Create/modify/delete multiple virtual servers in quick succession. -- Perform back-to-back config loads / UCS loads containing a large number of virtual server configurations.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes during a configuration change.

bugs.title: tmm could be stuck in a restart loop when remote logging to a fqdn destination is configured
bugs.symptoms: - TMM is stuck restarting on a bigip device or VE instance - Unable to process application traffic - /var/log/tmm logfile may contain the notice "MCP connection aborted, exiting"
bugs.conditions: - Remote logging destination is configured (System-Logs-Configuration-Remote logging) and pointing to a FQDN hostname - FQDN hostname temporarily or permanently fails to resolve (e.g. DNS failure or congestion) - Reboot or upgrade of a bigip instance or other conditions leading to tmm restart
bugs.impact: - Unable to process application traffic since the required component cannot be brought up
bugs.workaround: - Perform audit of DNS server(s), make sure FQDN destination resolves successfully, OR - Use IP address as remote logging destination, OR - Disable remote logging feature

bugs.title: LTM policy applied to HTTP/2 traffic may crash TMM

bugs.title: BIG-IP might send excessive multicast/broadcast traffic.

bugs.title: SNMP user added with password less than 8 characters through tmsh is allowed but fails during snmpwalk.

bugs.workaround: Configure snmp user with password greater than or equal to 8 characters.

bugs.title: Tmm restart adds 'Revoked' tokens to 'Active' token count

Error Code (access_denied) Error Description (This user has reached configured access token limit.)

bugs.title: Unable to view iApp component due to error 'An error has occurred while trying to process your request.' &start;

Note: Although this allows you to reconfigure an iApp, it does not provide access to the iApp application details Components page.
bugs.fix: Viewing Application Service components now reports no errors in the GUI under these conditions.

bugs.title: PEM subscriber GUI hardening

bugs.title: 'System Integrity: Invalid' after Engineering Hotfix installation

bugs.impact: Incorrect presentation of system software status; the status shows INVALID when it is actually valid.

bugs.title: MRF SIP status remains unknown on GUI

bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: HTTP::close used in iRule might not close connection.
bugs.symptoms: HTTP::close used in an iRule might not close the connection. For example: when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::close HTTP::respond 200 -version 1.1 content "OK" Content-Type text/plain }
bugs.conditions: Using HTTP::close along with HTTP::respond

bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where HTTP::close might not close a connection.

bugs.symptoms: Traffic intelligence feeds to do not follow best practices

bugs.impact: Unable to delete object(s) no longer in use.

bugs.title: Irrelevant content profile diffs in Policy Diff

bugs.conditions: -- Import a policy -- Perform a policy diff
bugs.impact: Policy diff showing irrelevant diffs
bugs.fix: Removed grayed out diffs from policy diff content profile section

bugs.title: MySQL generates multiple error 24 (too many files open) for PRX.REQUEST_LOG DB tables files.
bugs.symptoms: 1) var/lib/mysql/mysqld.err is filled with log entries that contain: ------------ 200824 11:04:43 [ERROR] mysqld: Can't open file: './PRX/REQUEST_LOG.frm' (errno: 24) 200824 11:18:46 [ERROR] mysqld: Can't open file: './PRX/REQUEST_LOG.frm' (errno: 24) 200824 11:35:58 [ERROR] mysqld: Can't open file: './PRX/REQUEST_LOG.frm' (errno: 24) ------------ 2) There are a lot of PRX.REQUEST_LOG partitions, in some cases up to 1024, many of which are empty.
bugs.conditions: ASM/AVR provisioned
bugs.impact: MySQL runs out of resources when opening the file PRX.REQUEST_LOG and an error message states the file is corrupt.
bugs.workaround: 1. If the /appdata partition is filled to 100% and MySQL restarts continuously, refer to the following Knowledge Articles: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14956 https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K42497314 2. To identify the empty partitions, look into: mysql -su root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e "SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARTITIONS WHERE table_name = 'REQUEST_LOG' AND table_schema = 'PRX'\G" 3. For every partition that is empty, manually (or via shell script) execute this sql: mysql -su root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e "ALTER TABLE PRX.REQUEST_LOG DROP PARTITION <empty_partition_name>;" Note: <empty_partition_name> must be substituted with the partition name, for example p100001. 4. Increase 'open_files_limit' to '10000'. -------------------------------- In the /etc/my.cnf file: 1. Change the value of the 'open_files_limit' parameter to 10000. 2. Restart MySQL: bigstart restart mysql -------------------------------- 5. pkill asmlogd Note: This workaround does not survive upgrade. It must be reapplied after every upgrade until the upgraded version contains a fix.
bugs.fix: This release increases the default 'open_files_limit' to '10000'.

bugs.title: BD sometimes crashes when handling HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: BD sometimes crashes when handling HTTP traffic

bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.

bugs.title: Tcp proxy does not ignore HUDEVT_CHILD_CONNECTED and gives an error
bugs.symptoms: Tcp proxy does not ignore HUDEVT_CHILD_CONNECTED and gives an error message: hud_tcp_serverside_handler/3676: 10.0.0.20.21 - 10.10.10.1.51147: unexpected serverside message HUDEVT_CHILD_CONNECTE

bugs.symptoms: Pam-authenticator cores. There is a log message in /var/log/user/log: err pam-authenticator: tac_author_read: short author header, -1 of 12: Connection reset by peer

bugs.title: Upgrade from 13.1.4, 14.1.4, or 15.1.1 to 14.0.x, 15.0.x, 16.0.0 or 16.0.0.1 fails
bugs.symptoms: Loading configuration process fails after an upgrade from 13.1.4, 14.1.4, or 15.1.1 to release 14.0.0, 15.0.0, 16.0.0 or 16.0.0.1. The system posts errors similar to the following: -- info tmsh[xxxx]: cli schema (15.1.1) has been loaded from schema data files. -- crit tmsh[xxxx]: 01420001:2: Can't load keyword definition (user-account.session_limit) : framework/SchemaCmd.cpp, line 825. -- crit tmsh[xxxx]: 01420001:2: Can't load keyword definition (system-settings.ssh_max_session_limit) : framework/SchemaCmd.cpp, line 825 -- emerg load_config_files[xxxx]: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g -a load sys config partitions all base " - failed. -- Loading schema version: 15.1.1. -- err mcpd[xxxx]: 01070422:3: Base configuration load failed. -- Unexpected Error: "Can't load keyword definition (user-account.session_limit)". -- Unexpected Error: "Can't load keyword definition (system-settings.ssh_max_session_limit)" -- Syntax Error:(/config/bigip_user.conf at line: 10) "session-limit" unknown property
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from one of the following release: -- v13.1.4 or later within the v13.1.x branch -- v14.1.4 or later within the v14.1.x branch -- v15.1.1 or later within the v15.1.x branch to one of the following releases: -- v14.0 through v14.1.3.1 -- v15.0 through v15.1.0.5 -- v16.0.0 and v16.0.0.1
bugs.impact: After upgrade, config does not load. The system hangs at the base configuration load failure status.
bugs.workaround: Although there is no workaround, you can avoid this issue by upgrading to the most recent maintenance or point release in v14.1.x, v15.1.x, or v16.x. You can find a list of most current software releases in K5903: BIG-IP software support policy :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K5903

bugs.title: TMM may crash when executing L7 Protocol Lookup per-request policy agent
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash when executing the L7 Protocol Lookup per-request policy agent.
bugs.conditions: -- APM or SSL Orchestrator is licensed and provisioned. -- L7 Protocol Lookup agent is included in the per-request policy for APM/SWG use cases.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM does not crash anymore when executing the L7 Protocol Lookup agent in the per-request policy.

bugs.title: HTTP iRule commands may fail to execute within the "fallback-host" HTTP profile field.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system can redirect a request to a fallback host when the target pool is unavailable. If the configured fallback host within the HTTP profile contains HTTP iRule commands such as HTTP::host or HTTP::uri, the corresponding HTTP request can fail. A connection reset may be encountered instead.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP profile with "fallback-host" profile option configured containing an HTTP iRule command.
bugs.impact: When utilizing the HTTP profile with "fallback-host" profile option with HTTP iRule commands, incorrect connection resets can be seen by the client instead of the correct HTTP response.
bugs.workaround: Attaching an iRule containing HTTP::redirect or similar command to the virtual server can be used instead of the fallback host-profile option to redirect traffic to another virtual server.
bugs.fix: The HTTP "fallback-host" profile option with HTTP iRule commands will now properly execute and result in the correct HTTP response being delivered to the client.

bugs.title: DNS Responses egress with an incorrect source IP address.
bugs.symptoms: DNS responses over a certain size egress the BIG-IP with an incorrect source IP address set.
bugs.conditions: Large responses of ~2460 bytes from local BIND
bugs.impact: The response to the client appears to be coming from the wrong source IP address, and the request fails.
bugs.workaround: Change 'max-udp-size' in BIND to a smaller value reduces the size of response, which stops the fragmentation. Note: This workaround has limitations, as some records in 'Additional Section' are truncated.

bugs.title: Dual stack download support for IP Intelligence Database
bugs.symptoms: IP Intelligence cannot function if the BIG-IP management IP network is strict IPv6.
bugs.conditions: - IP Intelligence License installed - Management IP is configured with only IPv6 addresses.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP systems configured with IPv6 management networks cannot use IP Intelligence features even though they have installed IP Intelligence licenses.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP can now download the IP Intelligence database over IPv4 and IPv6 management networks.
bugs.behavior: BIG-IP can now download the IP Intelligence database over IPv4 and IPv6 management networks.

bugs.title: Pair of phase 2 SAs missing after reboot of standby BIG-IP device
bugs.symptoms: In the case of IPsec traffic-selector narrowing during tunnel negotiation, Security Associations (SAs) may not be mirrored to the Standby after the Standby is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP systems configured in High Availability (HA). - Mirroring is configured. - The Standby system reboots.
bugs.impact: IPsec SAs may not be mirrored to the Standby device. If a failover occurs, the newly Active device cannot handle previously established tunnels.
bugs.workaround: Configure traffic-selectors to match exactly on both IPsec peers.
bugs.fix: During reboot, the IPsec object dependency chain is maintained.

bugs.title: User-defined report scheduling fails
bugs.symptoms: A scheduled report fails to be sent. An error message with the following format may appear on /var/log/avr/monpd.log file (some parts of the error message were replaced with '.....' in here to leave only the common parts): DB|ERROR|....... Error (err-code 1054) executing SQL string : ..... ..... ..... Because : Unknown column ....... in 'order clause'
bugs.conditions: 1. Using predefined-report in scheduled-report. 2. Predefined-report has more than one measure. 3. Sort-by value is different from the first measure on predefined-report
bugs.impact: Internal error for AVR report for ASM pre-defined.
bugs.workaround: First, remount /usr to read-write: mount -o remount,rw /usr Next, open file /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/F5/AVReporter/Client.pm and change the following line: push(@measures,@{$base_request->{measures}}[0]); to this: push(@measures,@{$base_request->{sort_by}}[0]->{measure}); The above can be achieved with the following script-line (please first backup the Client.pm file and then verify it changed it correctly): sed -i 's/push(@measures,@{\$base_request->{measures}}\[0\])/push(@measures,@{$base_request->{sort_by}}[0]->{measure})/' /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/F5/AVReporter/Client.pm Lastly, remount /usr back to read-only: mount -o remount,ro /usr
bugs.fix: Using 'sort-by' measure when building PDF (instead of the first value on measure-list)

bugs.title: Count Stateful anomalies based only on Device ID
bugs.symptoms: Currently when Device ID is enabled, the BIG-IP system counts stateful anomalies on both IP and Device ID. When a client has a proxy (without XFF), and many requests arrive with the same IP, this can cause false positives
bugs.conditions: - Bot Defense profile is attached to a virtual server. - Bot Defense profile has "Browser Verification" set to "Verify After Access" or "Device ID Mode" set to "Generate After Access".
bugs.impact: False positives may occur in case of a proxy without XFF
bugs.fix: Stateful anomalies are no longer counted on IP when Device ID is enabled

bugs.title: New iRule Commands for login result and username
bugs.symptoms: The iRule commands are not available to retrieve the web-user login results or to take actions based on the result of a login request.
bugs.conditions: Configure login page and send login request.
bugs.impact: Not able to get the login_result and username details of a login request.
bugs.fix: Add iRules commands to retrieve login request result and username information.

bugs.title: Network Management Agent (Azure NMAgent) updates causes Kernel Panic
bugs.symptoms: - TMM crashes - kernel panics - BIG-IP core file created - Cloud Failover Extension unexpected behavior (where applicable)
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP Azure Virtual Edition - Azure Host performs a Network Management Agent (NMAgent) update while TMM is running - BIG-IP VE using Accelerated Networking
bugs.impact: - Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts - BIG-IP restarts - Cloud Failover Extension state data lost (where applicable)
bugs.workaround: - Disable Accelerated Networking on BIG-IP network interfaces (Reversed settings from Azure documentation) Individual VMs & VMs in an availability set First stop/deallocate the VM or, if an Availability Set, all the VMs in the Set: Azure CLI az vm deallocate \ --resource-group myResourceGroup \ --name myVM Important, please note, if your VM was created individually, without an availability set, you only need to stop/deallocate the individual VM to disable Accelerated Networking. If your VM was created with an availability set, all VMs contained in the availability set will need to be stopped/deallocated before disabling Accelerated Networking on any of the NICs. Once stopped, disable Accelerated Networking on the NIC of your VM: Azure CLI az network nic update \ --name myNic \ --resource-group myResourceGroup \ --accelerated-networking false Restart your VM or, if in an Availability Set, all the VMs in the Set and confirm that Accelerated Networking is disabled: Azure CLI az vm start --resource-group myResourceGroup \ --name myVM

bugs.title: Wr_urldbd list of valid TLDs needs to be updated

bugs.impact: The URL query with new TLDs can not be blocked with custom feed list. Custom, Webroot, and Cloud returns Unknown category.

bugs.title: File object checksum attribute is not updated when an external data-group file or external monitor file is edited from GU
bugs.symptoms: SHA1 checksum attribute/property of the file object is not persisted/published/propagated to the MCP datastore/GUI.

Below mentioned is the workflow where the issue can be seen/replicated, System ›› File Management : Data Group File List >> FILE Edit the "definition" field of the file object & click update. 1.) edit sys file data-group "filename" 2.) list sys file data-group "filename" Aforementioned commands can be used from TMOS shell to understand the correct behavior that is expected when the same is done from GUI

bugs.title: buffersize(2048) too small. Buffer truncated.
bugs.symptoms: While proc pid statistics are collected by the merged daemon it may encounter an error and log a message about buffer size being too small.: notice merged[5491]: 011b0228:5: While reading file /proc/28574/cmdline, buffersize(2048) too small. Buffer truncated.
