bugs.title: F5-pf_daemon_cond_restart uses excessive CPU
bugs.symptoms: The script /etc/init.d/f5-pf_daemon_cond_restart spawns a lot of ephemeral processes that collectively use about 10-15% of a core, regardless of the number of cores. This is contributing to higher CPU usage after upgrading from an earlier version
bugs.conditions: On upgrade to a 15.1.x version, high CPU usage is observed.
bugs.impact: Higher CPU utilization on control plane, typically the equivalent of about 10-15% (of one core) extra.

bugs.title: An undisclosed iControl REST endpoint may provide a list of usernames to unauthorized users

bugs.title: A snat-translation address responds to ARP requests but not to ICMP ECHO requests.

bugs.title: TMM panic with SCTP traffic

bugs.impact: Traffic interrupted while TMM restarts

bugs.title: False positive "Null in Request"

bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP receives a query string in the "Referrer" header
bugs.impact: False positive violation "Null in Request" is thrown
bugs.fix: Fixed a false positive violation.

bugs.title: Workaround to address Nitrox 3 compression engine hang
bugs.symptoms: Occasionally the Nitrox3 compression engine hangs. In /var/log/ltm: crit tmm[12404]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Nitrox 3, Hang Detected: compression device was reset (pci 02:00.1, discarded 1). crit tmm[12404]: 01010025:2: Device error: n3-compress0 Zip engine ctx eviction (comp_code=0): ctx dropped.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system uses Nitrox 3 hardware compression chip: 5xxx, 7xxx, 12250, and B2250. You can check if your platform has nitrox3 by running the following command: tmctl -w 200 compress -s provider provider -------- bzip2 lzo nitrox3 <-------- zlib
bugs.impact: The Nitrox3 hardware compression system becomes unavailable and the compression mode switches to software compression. This can lead to high CPU usage.
bugs.workaround: Disable HTTP compression or use software compression.

bugs.title: Error log seen on Category Lookup SNI requests for same connection
bugs.symptoms: Client connections are reset and you see an error in /var/log/apm : "(ERR_NOT_FOUND) Category Lookup failed or a Category Lookup agent is not present in the policy before Response Analytics"
bugs.conditions: -- Category Lookup agent (lookup type SNI) in the per-request policy before Request or Response Analytics agent -- Multiple requests sent in the same SSL connection.
bugs.impact: Connections are reset or they follow the fallback branch for subsequent requests in the same SSL connection
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with Category Lookup SNI requests for same connection

bugs.title: Clusterd crash and vCMP guest failover
bugs.symptoms: Clusterd crashes and a vCMP guest fails over.
bugs.conditions: The exact conditions under which this occurs are unknown. It can occur during normal operation.
bugs.impact: Memory corruption and clusterd can crash, causing failover.

bugs.title: Improve TCP's response to partial ACKs during loss recovery
bugs.symptoms: - A bursty retransmission occurs during TCP's loss recovery period.
bugs.conditions: - TCP filter is used. - TCP stack is used instead of TCP4 stack (based on profile settings). - Packet loss occurs during the data transfer and TCP's loss recovery takes place.
bugs.impact: The bursty retransmissions may lead to more data getting lost due to large amount of data being injected into the network.
bugs.workaround: In versions prior to v16.0.0, use a TCP profile which selects the TCP4 stack instead of the TCP stack. There is no workaround for version 16.0.0.
bugs.fix: Partial ACK handling during loss recovery is improved.

bugs.title: False-Positives in case of matrix path parameter enforcement
bugs.symptoms: Creating an Open-API ASM policy with the configuration "Handle Path Parameters" = "As Parameters" causes fault detection of parameter violations on valid matrix path parameters, which leads to false positives.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when an open API policy is created with the configuration "Handle Path Parameters" = "As Parameters"
bugs.impact: False-Positives on matrix path parameters
bugs.workaround: During open API policy creation, configure "Handle Path Parameters" = "As URL"
bugs.fix: No False-Positives on matrix path parameters.

bugs.title: NTLM RPC exception: Failed to verify checksum of the packet
bugs.symptoms: NTLM authentication fails with the error: RPC exception: Failed to verify checksum of the packet.
bugs.conditions: -- Start nlad process with 'encryption'. -- Configure a user, and map that user to a huge number of groups. -- Configure NTLM front-end authentication.
bugs.impact: User authentication fails.
bugs.workaround: 1. Run the 'nlad' process with '-encrypt no' in the file /etc/bigstart/startup/nlad. 2. Disable encryption for nlad: # vim /etc/bigstart/startup/nlad change: exec /usr/bin/${service} -use-log-tag 01620000 to: exec /usr/bin/${service} -use-log-tag 01620000 -encrypt no 3. Restart nlad to make the change effective, and to force the schannel to be re-established: # bigstart restart nlad

bugs.title: Eviction Policy UI Hardening
bugs.symptoms: In certain scenarios, Eviction Policy UI does not follow best security practices.
bugs.conditions: Eviction Policy in Use
bugs.fix: Best security practices are now applied in Eviction Policy UI

bugs.title: Unable to load config if AVR widgets were created under '[All]' partition &start;
bugs.symptoms: When upgrading to or loading saved configuration on BIG-IP software v13.0.0 or later, if the configuration contains AVR widgets created under a partition of '[All]', the config load fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs if one or more AVR widgets in the configuration was created under the read-only '[All]' pseudo-partition. This could have occurred if you were running a version of BIG-IP which did not include the fix for ID 721408.
bugs.impact: Upgrading to or loading an affected configuration on BIG-IP v13.x or later fails.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the /config/bigip.conf configuration file and change '[All]' to 'Common': # sed -i 's/\\\[All\]/Common/g' /config/bigip.conf # tmsh load sys config # tmsh save sys config This should be done before upgrading to BIG-IP v13.x or later, or before saving configuration to be loaded later, or before loading a saved configuration from the config files.
bugs.fix: It is possible to successfully upgrade from or load a configuration containing one or more AVR widgets created under the read-only '\[All]' pseudo-partition or under other not existing partitions. With the current fix all partitions are changed to "Common" during upgrade.

bugs.title: QUIC does not send control frames in PTO packets
bugs.symptoms: When the QUIC PTO timer fires, it may resend some in-flight data. That data will not include any in-flight control frames.
bugs.conditions: A control frame is in-flight when the PTO timer fires.
bugs.impact: Minimal. The PTO timer is a mechanism to 'get ahead' of any lost packets and if a packet containing control frames is lost, those frames will be retransmitted.
bugs.fix: Retransmittable control frames are now sent when the PTO timer fires.

bugs.title: Possible blocking on bad IP reputation
bugs.symptoms: Bad ip reputation as part of Bot Defense verification causes suspicious classification, and therefore mitigation, by itself.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense profile is attached to Virtual Server. -- Intrusive mitigation action is configured for "Suspicious Browser" class. -- Client IP appears in bad IP reputation database.
bugs.impact: Clients are mitigated when they should not be.
bugs.workaround: Suspicious Javascript free score can be increased via a BigDB variable: tmsh modify sys db botdefense.suspicious_jsfree_score value 60

bugs.title: Fix routing server initiated request dynamically when "DIAMETER::dynamic_route_lookup"
bugs.symptoms: When using "DIAMETER::dynamic_route_lookup", the functionality does not work and tmm can crash.
bugs.conditions: -- Diameter dynamic routing enabled in diameter session profile. -- Dynamic-route-lookup is disabled -- An iRule DIAMETER::dynamic_route_lookup message is enabled
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Updates and deletions to iControl REST API tokens for non-admin users (both remote and local) do not sync
bugs.symptoms: When an iControl REST API token is updated using PUT or PATCH or deleted using DELETE for a non-admin user (either remote or local users), the changes do not sync to peer devices.
bugs.conditions: - High availability (HA) configuration of BIG-IPs - iControl REST using token-based authentication - Token issued to non-admin authenticated user (Either remote or local) - token updated or deleted using iControl REST
bugs.impact: - You may reach the API token limit unexpectedly.
bugs.workaround: The workaround is to initiate a config-sync operation from Active device to Standby device after creating the token in Active device with below command tmsh run cm config-sync force-full-load-push to-group <group name> Then both Active and Standby will be in sync with respect to remote information, and the issue will be resolved.
bugs.fix: When an iControl REST API token is updated using PUT or PATCH or deleted using DELETE for a non-admin user (both for remote and local user), the changes get synced to peer devices.

bugs.title: Wr_urldbd returns unknown results for customdb on some blades
bugs.symptoms: Some blades return 'Unknown' for newly added URLs in a custom database
bugs.conditions: This might occur under when feedlist updates are done quickly in a loop
bugs.impact: BIG-IP is unable to classify using url categories defined in the custom database.
bugs.workaround: Restart wr_urldbd
bugs.fix: Customdb classification now work as expected with the provided fix

bugs.title: RDP: Username is pre-filled with f5_apm* string after clicking on webtop resource on Mobile Clients (iOS & Android)
bugs.symptoms: When user connects to the virtual server using Browser on their iPhone or Android device, webtop displays RDP resource. When they click on it, if SSO is not enabled, Remote Desktop Client App pops up with username pre-filled with string starting with f5_apm.
bugs.conditions: -- APM Webtop is configured with Single Sign-on disabled RDP resource. -- Access the RDP resource from iOS or Android using RDP client.
bugs.impact: Remote Desktop Client App pops up with username pre-filled with string starting with f5_apm.
bugs.workaround: User needs to clear the username field and enter the actual username.

bugs.title: TCP connection is not closed when necessary after HTTP::respond iRule
bugs.symptoms: HTTP does not close the TCP connection on the client if response is sent via HTTP::respond.
bugs.conditions: - TCP profile is used. - HTTP profile is used. - HTTP::respond iRule is used (via HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE). - HTTP sends "Connection: close" header.
bugs.impact: TCP connection lives longer than needed.
bugs.fix: The TCP connection is now closed after sending "Connection: close".

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing SCTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing SCTP traffic. After this crash logs will show the message: "flow not in use".
bugs.conditions: - SCTP profile enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crashing leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes SCTP traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Zonerunner can't edit TXT records containing a + symbol - "Resolver returned no such record"
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to use zonerunner to edit a TXT record that contains a plus character, BIG-IP DNS presents the error message 'Resolver returned no such record'.
bugs.conditions: A TXT record exists with RDATA (the value of the TXT record) containing one or more + symbols
bugs.impact: Unable to edit the record.
bugs.workaround: Two workarounds available: 1. Use zonerunner to delete the record and then recreate it with the desired RDATA value 2. Manually edit the bind zone file (see K7032)

bugs.title: Add configuration to ccmode for compliance with the Common Criteria STIP PPM.
bugs.symptoms: To comply with configuration requirements for the Common Criteria STIP PPM, the ccmode script must be updated.
bugs.conditions: Required compliance with Common Criteria STIP PPM configuration.
bugs.impact: Without these updates, the BIG-IP will not be compliant with the Common Criteria STIP requirements.
bugs.workaround: Follow the instructions in the Common Criteria Guidance document.
bugs.fix: This fix added configuration elements for compliance to Common Criteria STIP PPM requirements.

bugs.title: LDAP remote authentication fails when empty attribute is returned
bugs.symptoms: LDAP/AD Remote authentication fails and the authenticating service may crash. The failure might be intermittent.
bugs.conditions: LDAP/AD server SearchResEntry includes attribute with empty or NULL value. This can be seen in tcpdump of the LDAP communication in following ways 1. No Value for attribute . Example in tcpdump taken on affected user : vals: 1 item AttributeValue: 2. 1. NULL Value for attribute . Example in tcpdump taken on affected user : vals: 1 item AttributeValue: 00
bugs.impact: Logging in via the GUI will fail silently Logging in via ssh will cause the sshd service on LTM to crash and logs will be seen under /var/log/kern.log The logs will be similar to : info kernel: : [460810.000004] sshd[31600]: segfault at 0 ip 00002b3abcb2ef3e sp 00007fffef3431a0 error 4 in pam_ldap.so[2b3abcb2c000+7000] info kernel: : [460810.002036] traps: sshd[31598] general protection ip:fffffffffffffff3 sp:80000 error:0
bugs.workaround: There is no Workaround on the LTM side. For LDAP, you change/add the value from none/NULL on the affected attribute to ANY dummy value which will prevent the issue

bugs.title: On BIG-IP C124 platform, drops seen on HSB-TMM 0.x interfaces
bugs.symptoms: On the BIG-IP C124 platform, HSB-TMM 0.x interfaces drop off.
bugs.conditions: In interface_stat where the column "counters.drops_in" has a non-zero number indicating drops in High-Speed Bridge (HSB) device.
bugs.impact: Could result in packets getting dropped in HSB and service outage.

bugs.title: Tmm core on GCP
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE) is running on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with mergeable buffers enabled, tmm might core while passing traffic. Subsequently, the kernel locks up, which prevents the whole system from recovering. TMM panic with this message in a tmm log file: panic: ../dev/ndal/virtio/if_virtio.c:2038: Assertion "Valid num_buffers" failed.
bugs.conditions: -- VE running on GCP. -- Mergeable buffers (mrg_rxbuf) is enabled on the guest with direct descriptors.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Use the sock driver. For more information see K10142141: Configuring the BIG-IP VE system to use the SOCK network driver :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K10142141 -- Request an Engineering Hotfix from F5, with mrg_rxbuf and lro turned off. Note: Using either workaround has a performance impact.
bugs.fix: - Added error handling to prevent crashing when a bad packet gets received - Added a new column 'invalid_header' into tmm/virtio_rx_stats table to track incidents

bugs.title: Source address translation occurs with self IP after NAT policy removal from Virtual Server
bugs.symptoms: Address translation occurs after removal of the NAT Policy from Virtual Server
bugs.conditions: Attach the policy with virtual server and remove it and check the traffic flow
bugs.impact: Source translation happens with self IP
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm: tmsh restart sys service tmm Impact of workaround: restarting tmm disrupts network traffic.
bugs.fix: The No Translation flag is reset after policy removal if source address translation is set to None

bugs.title: Analytics data not displayed for Pool Names
bugs.symptoms: You cannot see reports (statistics->analytics->pool) when you choose to view by pool names.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered in the statistics screen.
bugs.impact: You can't see the statistics->analytics->pool report when you choose view by pool names.

bugs.title: Pool and pool members created for dynamic ECMP routes are not freed
bugs.symptoms: -- Dynamic ECMP routes. -- High usage of TMM memory may be reported. -- The ltm log may record the following errors: err merged[9436]: 011b0900:3: TMSTAT error tmstat_remerge: Cannot allocate memory.
bugs.conditions: Dynamic routing is used and routes with more then one nexthop are repeatedly added and removed by the router(s)
bugs.impact: - tmm memory leak - tmstat segments for tmm could grow very large.
bugs.workaround: Use a default gateway pool instead of dynamic routing for routes with more then one nexthop - https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K15582

bugs.title: Hardware Syncookie mode not cleared when deleting/changing virtual server config.
bugs.symptoms: Modifying a virtual server can cause BIG-IP to get stuck in hardware syncookie mode.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server is in hardware syncookie mode. -- Modifying or deleting the virtual server For a list of platforms that support hardware syncookie protection, see https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14779
bugs.impact: Device is stuck in hardware syncookie mode and generates syncookies.
bugs.workaround: tmsh restart sys service tmm Impact of workaround: restarting tmm disrupts traffic.

bugs.title: URI::basename iRule command may include the semicolon and additional characters.
bugs.symptoms: The URI::basename iRule command allows for the basename part of a given uri string to be extracted. However, the semicolon character ';' is reserved and is often used to delimit parameters and parameter values suggesting that it should not be included in the basename of the uri.
bugs.conditions: - Configured iRule command URI::basename - HTTP Request uri containing the semicolon character.
bugs.impact: The iRule command URI::basename may provide the incorrect basename of specific uris as it may include a semicolon as well as additional characters.

bugs.title: Encrypted Video traffic classification
bugs.symptoms: - Classification engine needs to classify the video playback resolution for a video session.
bugs.conditions: - Both ABR and Behavioral classifier need to be enabled by configuring sys db variables * tmm.cec.classifier.behavioral.enable to true. * tmm.cec.classifier.abr.enable to true.
bugs.impact: - Classification Engine (CEC) starts to classify the encrypted video traffic resolution prediction into one of the four resolutions 360p, 480p, 720p and 1080p. - EVC support is added for multiple video applications such as YouTube, Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+.

bugs.title: B4450N blades report page allocation failure.
bugs.symptoms: Despite having free memory, the BIG-IP system frequently logs kernel page allocation failures on B4450N blades to the /var/log/kern.log file like the following: swapper/16: page allocation failure: order:2, mode:0x104020 After that, a stack trace follows. Note that the process name in the line ('swapper/16', in this example) varies. You may see generic Linux processes or processes specific to F5 in that line.
bugs.conditions: This occurs on B4450N blades regardless of configuration.
bugs.impact: As different processes can experience this issue, the system may behave unpredictably. For example, it is possible for a TMOS installation to fail as a result of this issue. Other processes may not exhibit any side effect as a result of this issue. The exact impact depends on which process becomes affected and how this process is designed to handle such a failure to allocate memory.
bugs.workaround: You must perform the workaround on each blade installed in the system. -- If you want the workaround to survive reboots only, perform the following procedure: 1) Log on to the advanced shell (BASH) of the primary blade of the affected VIPRION system. 2) Run the following commands: # clsh "sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072" # clsh "echo -e '\n# Workaround for ID950849' >> /etc/sysctl.conf" # clsh "echo 'vm.min_free_kbytes = 131072' >> /etc/sysctl.conf" -- If you want the workaround to survive reboots, upgrades, RMAs, etc., perform the following procedure: 1) Log on to the advanced shell (BASH) of the primary blade of the affected VIPRION system. 2) Run the following commands (with the desired amount in KB): # clsh "sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072" # echo -e '\n# Workaround for ID950849' >> /config/startup # echo 'sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=131072' >> /config/startup Note that the last two commands are not wrapped inside 'clsh' because the /config/startup file is already automatically synchronized across all blades. Once the issue is fixed in a future BIG-IP version, remove the workarounds: -- To remove the first workaround: 1) Edit the /etc/sysctl.conf file on all blades and remove the added lines at the bottom. 2) Reboot the system by running 'clsh reboot'. This will restore the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter to its default value for the BIG-IP version you are running. -- To remove the second workaround: 1) Edit the /config/startup file on the primary blade only, and remove the extra lines at the bottom. 2) Reboot the system by running 'clsh reboot'. This restores the min_free_kbytes kernel parameter to its default value for the BIG-IP version you are running. To verify the workaround is in place, run the following command (this should return the desired amount in KB): # clsh "cat /proc/sys/vm/min_free_kbytes"
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer experiences kernel page allocation failures on B4450 (A114) blades.

bugs.title: Apply Policy fails due to internal signature overlap following ASU ASM-SignatureFile_20200917_175034
bugs.symptoms: Following Signature Update (-SignatureFile_20200921_124008 or later), newly added/activated policies may fail Apply Policy due to a duplicate key database error: 01310027:2: subsystem error (asm_config_server.pl,F5::SetActive::Impl::set_active): Setting policy active failed: Failed to insert to DCC.ACCOUNT_NEGSIG_SIGNATURE_PROPERTIES (DBD::mysql::db do failed: Duplicate entry '8112518117000363265' for key 'PRIMARY' at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/BatchInsert.pm line 219. )
bugs.conditions: Signature Update -SignatureFile_20200921_124008 is installed, and a newly imported or inactive policy is applied.
bugs.impact: Apply policy fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use any of the following workarounds: -- Install an older signature update -SignatureFile_20200917_175034 -- Disable staging for either signature 200101255 or signature 200101258 (or both) in the affected policies. The policy can then be successfully applied. -- Run the following SQL command to correct all affected policies on the device: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- UPDATE PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SIGNATURES policy_sigs INNER JOIN (select previous_enforced_rule_md5, policy_id, count(*) as mycount from PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SIGNATURES where previous_enforced_rule_md5 != '' group by previous_enforced_rule_md5, policy_id having mycount > 1) as multi_sigs on policy_sigs.policy_id = multi_sigs.policy_id and policy_sigs.previous_enforced_rule_md5 = multi_sigs.previous_enforced_rule_md5 SET policy_sigs.previous_enforced_rule_md5 = '', policy_sigs.previous_enforced_rule = ''; ----------------------------------------------------------------------

bugs.title: Browser Challenges update file cannot be installed after upgrade &start;
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading BIG-IP, the Browser Challenges factory default update file cannot be installed, and you see this error: Installation error: gpg: WARNING: unsafe ownership on homedir `/usr/share/live-update/share/gpg/browser_challenges_genesis_load'gpg: encrypted with 1024-bit ELG key, ID 7C3E3CE5, created 2007-03-20 "asm_sigfile_installer"gpg: Signature made Mon Aug 2
bugs.conditions: The new file that comes with the installation is ready to install
bugs.impact: New updated cannot be installed
bugs.workaround: There are 2 options: 1. download a new version of the update file (if exists) 2. 2.1 download a copy of that file from the machine to your locale machine 2.2 rename it : > cp BrowserChallenges_20200722_072935.im BrowserChallenges_<CURRENT_DATE>_<CURRENT_TIME>.im ## the date and time are for tracking and the have to be in a specific format DATE : YYYYMMDD, TIME: HHMMSS 2.3 upload the file and install it manually from the LiveUpdate screen.
bugs.fix: Modified decryption key directory to a RW file systme

bugs.title: Virtual server resets all the connections for rstcause 'VIP disabled (administrative)'
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server resets all the connections for rstcause 'VIP disabled (administrative)', after all the conditions are met. Once it happens, the virtual server starts resetting all the incoming connections for rstcause 'VIP disabled (administrative)'. This continues even after the connection limit is deactivated.
bugs.conditions: -- There is at least one pool member that is DISABLED. -- Other pool members have a connection limit configured. -- A configuration change occurs while the connection limit is activated, and the change lowers the connection limit value, for example, the value is changed from 10 to 5.
bugs.impact: A virtual server continues resetting new connections.
bugs.workaround: Use Forced offline instead of disabled to prevent this issue.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system no longer continually resets new connections when the connection limit is lowered while it is being enforced.

bugs.title: ASM logging illegal events despite adding legal logging profile
bugs.symptoms: When switching from "Log illegal requests" to "Log all requests" the security logging profile does not log legal requests.
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned.
bugs.impact: "Log all requests" security logging profile does not log legal requests.
bugs.workaround: Before switching from "Log illegal requests" to "Log all requests" (or vice versa) switch to "none": ------------------------- # tmsh modify ltm virtual <Your_VS_Name> security-log-profiles replace-all-with { "Log illegal requests" } # tmsh modify ltm virtual <Your_VS_Name> security-log-profiles none # tmsh modify ltm virtual <Your_VS_Name> security-log-profiles replace-all-with { "Log all requests" } -------------------------

bugs.title: Live Update does not work properly after upgrade &start;
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading BIG-IP version the Live Update "Check for Update" button does not respond.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading from a version that did not have Live Update to a new version which includes Live Update
bugs.impact: Live Update can't query for new updates.
bugs.workaround: Restart tomcat process: > bigstart restart tomcat

bugs.title: FTP active data channels are not established
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions FTP active data channels may not be established as expected.
bugs.conditions: -- The FTP profile has "allow-active-mode" enabled and "port" set to a non-zero value.
bugs.impact: FTP transfers with active data channels are not processed as expected.
bugs.workaround: - Disable 'active' FTP and only use passive FTP or - Use a custom FTP profile with port set to '0' on FTP virtual servers.
bugs.fix: FTP active data channels are now established as expected.

bugs.title: Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
bugs.symptoms: Web application does not work and JavaScript error is posted in the browser console: Uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned. -- Bot or DoS application profile attached to a virtual server. -- Single page application (SPA) enabled.
bugs.impact: Web application does not work as expected.
bugs.fix: SPA functionality has been corrected to avoid this issue.

bugs.title: Cross origin AJAX requests are blocked in case there is no Origin header
bugs.symptoms: When using Single Page Application, if a CORS request is sent without an Origin, the "Access-Control-Allowed-Origin" header is not set and the request is blocked.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM policy / DoS (with application) profile / Bot Defense Profile are attached to VS, with a "Single Page Application" flag enabled. -- Client is using dosl7.allowed_origin option -- CORS Request is sent without an Origin header.
bugs.impact: Request is blocked.
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to add the Origin header according to the domain in the Referrer header.
bugs.fix: Check referrer header also when modifying CORS headers.

bugs.title: Memory allocation error while creating an address list with a large range of IPv6 addresses &start;
bugs.symptoms: When trying to create a large IPv6 address-list IP range either via the GUI, tmsh, or from loading a previously saved config, MCPd will temporarily experience memory exhaustion and report an error "01070711:3: Caught runtime exception, std::bad_alloc"
bugs.conditions: When adding an IPv6 address range that contains a very large number of IPs. This does not affect IPv4.
bugs.impact: The IP address range cannot be entered. If upgrading from a non-affected version of TMOS where an IP range of this type has been saved to the config, a std::bad_alloc error will be printed when loading the config after upgrading.
bugs.workaround: Use CIDR notation or multiple, smaller IP ranges.

bugs.title: 'Current Sessions' statistics of HTTP2 pool may be incorrect
bugs.symptoms: In HTTP2 full proxy deployment, the LTM pool 'cur_sessions' statistics may show an unusually large number, such as 18446743927680663552
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP2 full proxy deployment -- A client sends multiple requests over multiple streams
bugs.impact: 'Current Sessions' statistics can be used to track number of pending requests in the queue and it can underflow.
bugs.fix: 'Current Sessions' statistics of HTTP2 pool reports correctly.

bugs.title: Azure B2C Provider OAuth URLs are updated for B2Clogin.com
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft has deprecated login.microsoftonline.com OAuth Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C) URLs. The OAuth Provider templates are updated to support the newer URLs B2Clogin.com.
bugs.conditions: Azure AD B2C Provider may be non functional if URLs are using logic.microsoftonline.com.
bugs.impact: Older AD B2C URLs using login.microsoftonline.com may not be functional.
bugs.workaround: Update existing URLs when creating OAuth B2C providers to use B2Clogin.com. For more information, see Azure Active Directory B2C is deprecating login.microsoftonline.com :: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/updates/b2c-deprecate-msol/.
bugs.fix: Azure B2C Provider OAuth URLs have been updated to use B2Clogin.com.

bugs.title: Changing access policy from multi-domain to single domain does not send domain cookies
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system sends cookies with no "domain" attribute set.
bugs.conditions: - Configure a Multidomain access profile - Change the profile to single domain
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system sends cookies with no "domain" attribute set. This causes the cookie to be not associated to a particular domain.
bugs.workaround: Manually remove the domain-groups config from the access profile by editing the bigip.conf.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when performing iterative DNS resolutions.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and produces a core file.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system configuration includes a Network DNS Resolver, which is referenced by another object (for example, a HTTP Explicit Forward Proxy profile) for DNS resolution.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You may be able to work around this issue by having the Network DNS Resolver work in forwarding/recursive mode rather than in resolving/iterative mode. To do so, you configure a Forward Zone in the Network DNS Resolver for '.' (the DNS root). This causes DNS to send all DNS requests to a different, external resolver of your choice, which will perform recursive resolution. The servers you configure for the '.' Forward Zone could be resolvers internal to your organization or public resolvers (e.g. Google DNS).
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes.

bugs.title: Hardware syncookie mode not cleared when changing dos-device-vector enforcement
bugs.symptoms: Changing DOS vector enforcement configuration can cause BIG-IP to get stuck in hardware syncookie mode.
bugs.conditions: - Changing DOS vector enforcement configuration when device is in global syncookie mode. For a list of platforms that support hardware syncookie protection, see https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14779
bugs.impact: Device is stuck in hardware syncookie mode and generates syncookies.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command: tmsh restart sys service tmm Impact of workaround: restarting tmm disrupts traffic.

bugs.title: Syncookie HW mode not cleared when modifying VLAN config.
bugs.symptoms: Changing VLAN configuration can cause BIG-IP get stuck in hardware syncookie mode.
bugs.conditions: - Changing VLAN configuration when vlan-based syncookies are active. For a list of platforms that support hardware syncookie protection, see https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14779
bugs.impact: Device is stuck in hardware syncookie mode and generates syncookies.
bugs.workaround: Run the following command: tmsh restart sys service tmm Impact of workaround: restarting tmm disrupts traffic.

bugs.title: HTTPS monitors marking pool member offline when restrictive ciphers are configured for all TLS protocol versions
bugs.symptoms: HTTPS monitor marks pool member/nodes as down and they remain down until bigd is restarted or the monitor instance is removed and created again.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured with restrictive ciphers that are only compatible with TLS 1.2 (ECDH+AESGCM) but all of the TLS protocol versions are allowed. When HTTPS monitor TLS 1.0 handshake fails, due to incompatible ciphers with the server being monitored. It does not try TLS 1.2 version and marks pool members or nodes as down.
bugs.impact: HTTPS monitor shows pool members or nodes down when they are up.
bugs.workaround: Restart bigd or remove and add monitors.
bugs.fix: In case of handshake failure, BIG-IP will try TLS 1.2 version.

bugs.title: After re-initializing the onboard FIPS HSM, BIG-IP may lose access after second MCPD restart
bugs.symptoms: When re-initializing an onboard HSM on particular platforms, BIG-IP may disconnect from the HSM after a second restart of the MCPD daemon. This can occur when using administrative commands such as: -- tmsh run util fips-util init -- fipsutil init -- tmsh run util fips-util loginreset -r -- fipsutil loginreset -r
bugs.conditions: -- Using the following platforms: + i5820-DF / i7820-DF + 5250v-F / 7200v-F + 10200v-F + 10350v-F + vCMP guest on i5820-DF / i7820-DF + vCMP guest on 10350v-F
bugs.impact: BIG-IP is unable to communicate with the onboard HSM.
bugs.workaround: The last step in using "fipsutil init" is to restart all system services ("tmsh restart sys service all") or reboot. Immediately before doing this: -- open /config/bigip.conf in a text editor (e.g. vim or nano) -- locate and delete the configuration "sys fipsuser f5cu" stanza, e.g.: sys fipsuser f5cu { password $M$Et$b3R0ZXJzCg== }
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with re-initializing the onboard FIPS HSM.

bugs.title: REST File Upload hardening
bugs.symptoms: REST file upload does not follow best security practices.
bugs.workaround: Only upload trusted files to the BIG-IP.
bugs.fix: REST file uploads now follow best security practices.

bugs.title: "switchboot -b HD1.1" fails to reboot chassis

bugs.title: Incorrect Protocol Inspection "Drop" action for UDP connection flows
bugs.symptoms: When a drop action is performed for a UDP connection flow, BIG-IP does not drop the connection correctly.
bugs.conditions: - Protocol Inspection's profile is attached at either the Virtual Server or the Firewall rule level. - UDP traffic is processed and matches an action set to "Drop" occurs.
bugs.impact: Multiple connections are created on the server side, which could lead to port exhaustion.
bugs.fix: Protocol Inspection "Drop" action drops only packet, and keeps the connection and continues to drop the subsequent traffic for a UDP connection flow.
bugs.behavior: Protocol Inspection "Drop" action on UDP connection should only drop the packet, but keep the connection in such a state that subsequent traffic gets dropped. The old behavior was to drop the packet and remove the connection.

bugs.impact: The Live-Update process does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: The Live-Update process now follows current best practices.

bugs.impact: User authorization changes for live update
bugs.fix: User authorization changes for live update

bugs.title: Excessive CPU consumption by asm_config_event_handler

bugs.title: UCS archives containing a large number of DNS zone files may fail to restore.
bugs.symptoms: This issue can manifest in the following ways: - Failure to restore a UCS archive to the currently active boot location (i.e. restoring a backup). - Failure to restore a UCS archive to a different boot location by means of using the cpcfg utility (or the the "Install Configuration" option when changing boot locations in the Web UI). - Failure to restore a UCS archive as part of a software upgrade (if rolling forward the configuration was requested, which is the default BIG-IP behavior). In all cases, error messages similar to the following example are returned to the user: /bin/sh: /bin/rm: Argument list too long Fatal: executing: /bin/sh -c rm -fr /var/named/config/namedb/* Operation aborted. /var/tmp/configsync.spec: Error installing package Config install aborted. Unexpected Error: UCS loading process failed.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when a large number of DNS zone files are already present in the /var/named/config/namedb directory of the boot location to which the UCS archive is being restored.
bugs.impact: The UCS archive fails to restore. Additionally: - If the UCS archive was being restored on the currently active boot location, the named and zrd daemons may not be running after the failure, leading to traffic outages. - If the UCS archive was being restored as part of an upgrade, the installation will fail and the destination boot location will be marked as failed (thus preventing a BIG-IP Administrator from activating it).
bugs.workaround: Depending on the failure mode, perform one of the following workarounds: - If you were restoring a UCS archive on the currently active boot location, run the following command, and then attempt the UCS archive restore operation again: find /var/named/config/namedb -mindepth 1 -delete - If you encountered the failure during an upgrade, it should mean you were installing an Engineering Hotfix (otherwise the /var/named/config/namedb directory on the destination boot location would have been empty). Installing an Engineering Hotfix will actually perform two separate installations - first the base version, and then the hotfix on top of that. Each installation restores the source location's UCS archive. The UCS installation performed during the base installation will work, and the one performed during the hotfix installation will fail (because DNS zone files are already in place now, and they will fail to be deleted). In this case, you can work around the issue by performing two distinct installations (to the same destination boot location). First the base version by itself, and then the hotfix installation by itself: Perform the first installation with the liveinstall.moveconfig and liveinstall.saveconfig db keys disabled. Perform the second installation after enabling the liveinstall.moveconfig and liveinstall.saveconfig db keys again. - If you encountered the failure while using the cpcfg utility (or equivalent WebUI functionality), take a UCS archive instead, download it off of the BIG-IP or save it in a shared directory (e.g. /var/tmp), boot the system into the destination boot location, run the below command, and then restore the UCS archive: find /var/named/config/namedb -mindepth 1 -delete
bugs.fix: The UCS restore operation succeeds, even when a large number of DNS Bind zone files are present.

bugs.title: Dynamic split tunneling for Zoom, Office 365 traffic
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP APM did not support dynamic split tunneling for Zoom and Office 365 traffic. There is no capability to automatically exclude Zoom and Microsoft Office 365 traffic in APM Network Access tunnels.
bugs.conditions: Use network access to exclude traffic for applications.
bugs.impact: The traffic was routed over the tunnel instead of being excluded and passed directly to the public internet.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP APM now provides the ability to create a dynamic address space that contains IPv4, IPv6, and DNS names for Zoom and Microsoft Office 365 applications by using their auto-discovery URL. You can also create custom address space objects by manually adding a static list of addresses for SaaS applications such as Cisco Webex. You can automatically exclude Zoom and Microsoft Office 365 traffic in APM Network Access tunnels with this capability.

bugs.title: "none" missing from the error string when snmp trap is configured with an invalid network type
bugs.symptoms: When you try to configure an SNMP trap with an invalid network type, you get a confusing error: 01070911:3: The requested enumerated (aaa) is invalid (, mgmt, other) for network in /Common/snmpd trapsess (/Common/i2_2_2_1_1)
bugs.conditions: SNMP trap is configured with an invalid network enum type.
bugs.impact: The word 'none' is not shown in the error string.

bugs.title: Cannot modify properties of a monitor that is already in use by a pool
bugs.symptoms: Modifying monitor properties gives error, if it is attached to a pool with Node/Pool member instance. 0107082c:3: Cannot modify the destination address of monitor /Common/my_monitor
bugs.conditions: -- Monitor with alias address field as default properties. -- Pool containing a node or pool member. -- Monitor is attached to the pool.
bugs.impact: Monitor properties can't be modified if they are in use by a pool.
bugs.workaround: Remove monitor, modify it, and then add it back.
bugs.fix: Monitor properties can be modified even when the monitor is attached to the node or pool, updated values reflect in the node or pool.

bugs.title: Fw_lsn_pool_pba_stat: excessively high active_port_blocks stat for IPv4
bugs.symptoms: TMM specific stats shows unrealistic values.
bugs.conditions: The respective TMMs have shortage of NAT PBAs.
bugs.impact: No functional impact. Only on stats reporting side impact.

bugs.title: Configuration may fail to load with named virtual-address for 0.0.0.0 in a non-zero route domain
bugs.symptoms: When reading the configuration from /config files, the BIG-IP system may fail to load the configuration regarding a virtual server with a named virtual-address for address 0.0.0.0 in a non-default route domain: err mcpd[21812]: 0107028b:3: The source (0.0.0.0%123) and destination (0.0.0.0) addresses for virtual server (/Common/vs1) must be in the same route domain. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- An LTM virtual-address object with a name. -- The virtual-address's address is 0.0.0.0 (or the keyword 'any'). The IPv6 address :: (or the keyword 'any6') is not affected. -- The virtual-address's address is in a route domain other than route domain 0. The route domain can be the partition's default route domain. -- An LTM virtual server that uses the affected address as its destination. Example: tmsh create net route-domain 123 tmsh create ltm virtual-address allzeros-rd123 address 0.0.0.0%123 tmsh create ltm virtual allzeros-rd123 destination 0.0.0.0%123:0 tmsh save sys config
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to load from disk when the affected objects do not yet exist in running memory or binary cache, for example, during: - Reinstalling - Upgrading - Loading manual changes to the /config/*.conf files - MCP force-reload Other operations such as rebooting, relicensing, and reloading the same configuration (such as 'tmsh load sys config' are not affected.
bugs.workaround: Replace the configuration that uses a named virtual-address with the direct address. Here is an example of the configuration in bigip.conf: ltm virtual-address allzeros-rd123 { address any%123 mask any } ltm virtual allzeros-rd123 { destination allzeros-rd123:0 mask any source 0.0.0.0%123 } This can be rewritten to remove the virtual-address object, and replace the virtual server destination with the address (0.0.0.0 or 'any'): ltm virtual allzeros-rd123 { destination any%123:0 mask any source 0.0.0.0%123 }

bugs.title: Vlan can reference a deleted partition on the primary device
bugs.symptoms: Vlan information references a deleted partition on the primary device and configuration load fails giving an error: emerg load_config_files[8487]: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g -a load sys config partitions all base " - failed. -- 01070277:3: The requested vlan, vlangroup or tunnel (/autoprov/pcs-autoprov-core-lb-link) was not found.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) environment -- A VLAN is created in a partition on one device -- The partition is deleted on the other device
bugs.impact: After config sync, the VLAN may point to the deleted partition. Configuration load will fail, and upgrade will also fail.
bugs.workaround: -- Remove the config from bigip_base.conf and load the config again (tmsh load sys config) -- Run both create and delete for VLAN on both units and then only sync it (For both auto and manual sync)

bugs.title: iRule command 'table' fails to resume when used with Diameter 'irule_scope_msg'
bugs.symptoms: 'table' command fails to resume causing processing of traffic to halt due to 'irule_scope_msg' causing iRule processing to proceed in a way that 'table' does not expect.
bugs.conditions: - iRule using 'table' command - Diameter 'irule_scope_msg' enabled
bugs.impact: Traffic processing halts (no crash)

bugs.title: System reports{{validation_errors}}
bugs.symptoms: A {{validation_errors}} at Subscriber Management :: Control Plane Listeners and Data Plane Listeners with ipv6 addresses
bugs.conditions: Specifying an IPv6 address in the expression in Subscriber Management :: Control Plane Listeners and Policy Enforcement :: Data Plane Listeners.
bugs.impact: Cannot access the BIG-IP GUI through IPv6 address from any web browser. Admin/User cannot enter input through GUI.

bugs.title: HTTP profile response-chunking "unchunk" option does not remove Content-Length from response header
bugs.symptoms: When the HTTP profile response-chunking option is set to "unchunk", chunked responses will be unchunked and the Transfer-Encoding header is removed. If the server sends a chunked response with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers, Transfer-Encoding is removed but Content-Length is not. This causes the client to receive a response with an erroneous Content-Length header.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP virtual server with response-chunking set to "unchunk" - Server response with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers present
bugs.impact: Malformed HTTP response received by client as length of response should be determined by closure of connection, not erroneous Content-Length header.
bugs.workaround: Implement iRule: at HTTP_RESPONSE time, remove the Content-Length header if the Transfer-Encoding header is also present.
bugs.fix: HTTP now removes Content-Length header when unchunking responses.

bugs.title: Websocket URLs content profiles are not created as expected during JSON Policy import
bugs.symptoms: Websocket URLs content profiles are not created as expected during JSON Policy import
bugs.conditions: Import JSON Policy with Websocket URLs configured with content profiles.
bugs.impact: Content profiles are not being added to the webscket URLs causing wrong configuration.
bugs.workaround: The content profiles can be manually associated after the import process using REST or GUI.
bugs.fix: Setting the correct profile reference during import.

bugs.title: Modifying a traffic-matching-criteria with a port-list during a full sync may result in an incorrect configuration on the sync target
bugs.symptoms: In a device service cluster, changing a traffic-matching-criteria object's port configuration and then performing a full-sync will cause the sync target's traffic-matching-criteria ports to be modified incorrectly. Once systems are in this state, further ConfigSyncs may result in these error messages: err mcpd[6489]: 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:traffic_matching_criteria_port_update status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127. err mcpd[6489]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/Failover to commit id 250 6869100131892804718 /Common/tmc-sync-2-bigip1.test 0 failed with error 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:traffic_matching_criteria_port_update status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127..
bugs.conditions: -- Two or more BIG-IPs in a DSC. -- Using traffic-matching-criteria, and making changes.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP configurations are out of sync (even though they show "In Sync"). Affected virtual servers will process more traffic than configured.
bugs.workaround: On an affected system, perform one of the two procedures to correct MCPD's in-memory configuration: 1. Remove the traffic-matching criteria from all virtual servers (or only affected virtual servers, if known), and then re-add the traffic-matching criteria. 2. Save the configuration and then follow the procedure in K13030: Forcing the mcpd process to reload the BIG-IP configuration. tmsh save sys config clsh touch /service/mcpd/forceload clsh reboot

bugs.title: MAC address might be displayed as 'none' after upgrading. &start;
bugs.symptoms: The MAC Address of a BIG-IP Virtual Edition network interface is displayed as 'none' after upgrading.
bugs.conditions: 1. The VLAN MTU is set to less than 1280 bytes on a BIG-IP network interface. 2. Upgrade BIG-IP to 14.1.0 or above from BIG-IP versions below 14.1.0.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted when the MAC address is set to 'none'.
bugs.fix: IPv6 link-local addresses are now created with MTU greater than 1280, so this issue is resolved.

bugs.title: High CPU from analytics-related REST calls - Dashboard TMUI
bugs.symptoms: When opening the GUI > Main > Statistics > Dashboard - the control plane CPU usage is around 7-15% on a completely empty system and Java consumes 3-5% CPU.
bugs.conditions: Leaving UI dashboard page left open.
bugs.impact: System performance is impacted if the dashboard page is kept open.

bugs.title: ASM sync files not cleaned up immediately after processing
bugs.symptoms: Some ASM sync files remain on disk after config sync finishes. They remain until periodic clean-up tasks activate
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned -- BIG-IP devices are in a sync group -- Relatively small "/var" partition
bugs.impact: If the files are large it may lead to "lack of disk space" problem.

bugs.title: The tmrouted daemon restarts and produces a core file
bugs.symptoms: The tmrouted daemon restarts and produces a core file.
bugs.conditions: Exact trigger is unknown, but the issue was seen on a chassis setup during a blade failover
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmrouted restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmrouted daemon should not restart during blade reset

bugs.title: Port and port-list type are both stored in a traffic-matching-criteria object
bugs.symptoms: Using "tmsh load sys config replace file ..." to change a traffic matching criteria's port type from port to port-list (or vice-versa) results in both types ending up in the traffic matching criteria object.
bugs.conditions: -- Using traffic-matching-criteria. -- Using "tmsh load sys config replace file ..." or "tmsh load sys config merge file ..." to change the port to a port-list (or vice-versa).
bugs.impact: -- System does not load the desired configuration. -- Virtual servers may match/process more traffic than expected.

bugs.title: Per-request policy execution may timeout.
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to access a resource that requires subsession validation, the client may receive an HTTP 503 "Service Unavailable" response, and the logs indicate that per-request policy execution time has expired.
bugs.conditions: Multiple connections are accessing the same subsession, triggering subsession lock contention.
bugs.impact: Some clients will fail to connect to their destination.
bugs.workaround: Add criteria to the gating criteria to enable more fine-grained subroutines to reduce subsession contention. For example, add category, or application name, to the gating criteria. In the case of API protection, consider concatenating credentials with the resource hostname (plus port). Increase the per-request policy execution timeout value, controlled by the variable tmm.access.prp_global_timeout, to a higher value.
bugs.fix: Subesssion lock contention wait time is reduced. Clients will not fail to connect due to subsession lock contention.

bugs.title: /var fills up very quickly
bugs.symptoms: Policy history files fill /var disk partition
bugs.conditions: Very large configuration with substantial history and config sync enabled
bugs.impact: ASM sync fails due to /var being full
bugs.workaround: The properties in '/etc/ts/tools/policy_history.cfg' file, for cleaning as a file-based configuration option, are a Support-oriented configuration option aimed to help in these cases.

bugs.title: HTTPS traffic may fail for Inbound topology gateway mode
bugs.symptoms: HTTPS traffic may fail for Inbound topology gateway mode.
bugs.conditions: -- SSL Orchestrator is licensed and provisioned. -- Inbound topology with gateway mode is selected and gateway iRule is attached to wildcard virtual. -- HTTPS Traffic is intercepted. -- SNI is not sent in clientHello.
bugs.impact: HTTPS traffic may fail.
bugs.workaround: Pass SNI from the client if not already sent in clientHello.
bugs.fix: HTTPS traffic does not fail anymore for inbound topology.

bugs.title: Duplicate Attack signature sets in policy containing server technologies
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new security policy, choosing a server technology for the policy causes duplicate signature sets to be created.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a new security policy using a server technology -- Create another security policy using the same server technology
bugs.impact: Duplicate signature sets are created.
bugs.workaround: You can repair the policy by navigating to “Security ›› Application Security : Policy Building : Learning and Blocking Settings”, clicking on “change”, and choosing the original created sets instead of the duplicated sets. Save, and then apply the policy. The duplicated sets can be deleted after that.

bugs.title: MRF Diameter loop-detection is enabled by default
bugs.symptoms: The default value of Message Routing Framework (MRF) Diameter loop detection is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Default diameter session profile loop detection configuration.
bugs.impact: System performance is impacted even if MRF Diameter loop detection is not used.
bugs.workaround: Disable loop detection in all message routing Diameter profiles when it is not needed.
bugs.fix: MRF Diameter loop detection is now disabled by default. Note: If you expect MRF Diameter loop detection to be enabled, you must manually change the value after upgrading.

bugs.title: When BIG-IP contains an invalid DNS Resolver, Bot Defense might wrongly classify search engines as malicious
bugs.symptoms: When the first DNS resolver is invalid, Bot Defense is unable to verify trusted bots, and is classifying them as malicious bots.
bugs.conditions: -- First DNS resolver in the list is invalid. -- Bot Defense profile is attached to a virtual server. -- Request from a search engine arrives.
bugs.impact: Bot Defense wrongly classifies valid search engines as malicious bots (and might block them if enforcement is enabled).
bugs.workaround: Fix the first DNS resolver in the list. It's possible that the first DNS resolver is the built in DNS resolver "f5-aws-dns".

bugs.title: Tab complete in 'mgmt' tree is broken
bugs.symptoms: TMSH Command: "list mgmt shared <tab>" does not display the tab complete option. You may see an error: (tmos)# list mgmt shared echo *tab* Unexpected Error: "Object contains no "method" child value"
bugs.conditions: When mgmt is used in a tmsh command and you attempt to tab complete
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure objects in mgmt. This issue also prevents users with the admin role from accessing the following REST endpoints: shared/authz/users shared/echo-js The error returned was HTTP/1.1 401 F5 Authorization Required
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with tab completion for certain commands in the 'mgmt' tree.

bugs.title: Javascript parser incompatible with ECMA6/7+
bugs.symptoms: A web application mis-functions on the client side
bugs.conditions: -- APM proxying a web application -- Web-application uses ES6/7 or higher javascript
bugs.impact: Web application mis-function
bugs.fix: The fix is implemented in two steps STEP 1: Initial implementation with ID 592353, added support for Javascript ECMA6/7+. Optional internal wrapping is added into client-side includes. With this fix, a custom iRule workaround can be applied to fix limited set of possible cases. STEP 2: With ID 957453, implementation of light rewriter on the server side is also completed. No iRule workaround is required to support ES6/7+ after the implementation of ID 957453.

bugs.title: Creating virtual server with IPv6 address or port list in destination should display source address in IPv6 format
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, while creating a virtual server with an IPv6 address or a port list in destination, the BIG-IP system should display the source address in IPv6 format rather than IPv4 format 0.0.0.0/0.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered while creating a virtual server with an IPv6 address or port list in destination.
bugs.impact: The IPv6 address list is displayed in IPv4 notation.
bugs.workaround: This is a cosmetic issue. The correct addresses are used.

bugs.title: The pfmand daemon can crash when it starts.
bugs.symptoms: The pfmand process crashes and writes out a core file during bootup (or if the process is manually restarted by an Administrator for any reason) on certain platforms. The crash may happen more than once, until the process finally settles and is able to start correctly.
bugs.impact: Network connection lost while pfmand restarts.
bugs.fix: The issue causing the pfmand daemon to occasionally crash has been resolved.

bugs.title: Possible TMM crash when using CPM, iRule, or iApp to enable/disable Bot Defense Profile
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash when using CPM, iRule, or iApp to enable/disable a Bot Defense profile.
bugs.conditions: -- Bot Defense Profile is attached to virtual server. -- Bot Defense Profile has any Javascript Browser Verification (before or after access). -- A CPM, iRule, or iApp are used to enable/disable the Bot Defense Profile.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Unable to modify gateway-ICMP monitor fields in the GUI
bugs.symptoms: While modifying a gateway-ICMP monitor you see the following error: 01070374:3: Cannot modify the address type of monitor /Common/<monitor_name>.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the GUI to modify a Gateway-ICMP monitor field. -- The monitor is attached with a pool that has one or more pool members.
bugs.impact: You cannot update the Gateway-ICMP monitor fields via the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use the tmsh command: tmsh modify ltm monitor gateway-icmp <monitor_name> [<field> <new_value>] For example, to update the description of a monitor named gw_icmp, use the following command: modify ltm monitor gateway-icmp gw_icmp description new_description
bugs.fix: You can now update the Gateway-ICMP monitor fields via the GUI.

bugs.title: SIP Requests / Responses over TCP without content_length header are not aborted by BIG-IP.
bugs.symptoms: SIP Requests that don't contain a content_length header are accepted and forwarded by the BIG-IP to the server. SIP Responses that don't contain a content_length header are accepted and forwarded to the client. The sipmsg parser does not treats the content_length header as a required header as part of the SIP Request / Response.
bugs.conditions: SIP request / response without content_length header.
bugs.impact: RFC 6731 non compliance.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now aborts the connection of any TCP SIP request / response that does not contain a content_length header. content_length header is treated as optional for UDP and SCTP.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.

bugs.title: Request is blocked by 'CSRF attack detected' violation with 'CSRF token absent'
bugs.symptoms: Request is blocked by 'CSRF attack detected' violation.
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual server - CSRF protection enabled in an ASM policy
bugs.impact: False positive request blocking occurs.
bugs.workaround: Disable 'CSRF attack detected' violation in the ASM policy.
bugs.fix: 'CSRF attack detected' now works as expected.

bugs.title: Unable to set a port list in the GUI for an IPv6 address for a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: When creating a virtual server in the GUI with an IPv6 destination address and a port list (shared object) or a source address list (shared object), the system returns an error similar to: 0107028f:3: The destination (0.0.0.0) address and mask (ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff) for virtual server (/Common/vs03-v6_dns) must be be the same type (IPv4 or IPv6).
bugs.conditions: -- Creating or updating a virtual server. -- Attempting to use an IPv6 Host address with a Port List shared object or a Source Address List shared object.
bugs.impact: Unable to create/modify virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Create an Address List shared object with the IPv6 address in it and use that instead of the Host address.

bugs.title: IM installation fails with error: Spec file not found
bugs.symptoms: IM installation fails with an error message: ERROR Error during switching: Spec file not found
bugs.conditions: This can occur when deleting an IM file that is actively installing on one volume, and the BIG-IP system is booted from another volume.
bugs.impact: Upgrading/Downgrading to another IM does not work until you install a new BIG-IP image on the same disk.
bugs.fix: During the init process, the system now installs FactoryDefaults if the active IM file is not found on disk.

bugs.title: IPv6 routes missing after BGP graceful restart
bugs.symptoms: When BGP graceful restart is configured for peers in IPv4 unicast and IPv6 unicast address families, after graceful restart for both IPv4 and Ipv6 address families, routes from IPv6 unicast address family might be missing.
bugs.conditions: - Different BGP peers configured in IPv4 unicast and IPv6 unicast address families. - BGP graceful restart happens for both IPv4 unicast and IPv6 unicast.
bugs.impact: Routes from IPv6 peers are missing. They are also not present in the RIB.

bugs.title: Hash collisions in DNS rapid-response packet processing
bugs.symptoms: DNS rapid-response (FastDNS) packet processing may cause unexpected traffic drops.
bugs.conditions: - DNS rapid-response is enabled in a DNS profile: ltm profile dns dns { enable-rapid-response yes } Note: This issue is more likely to occur on systems with a lower number of TMMs.
bugs.impact: Unexpected traffic drops

bugs.title: 'Restrict to Single Client IP' option is missing in VMware iApp.
bugs.symptoms: 'Restrict to Single Client IP' is available only in the access policy.
bugs.conditions: Configure VMware VDI using iApp.
bugs.impact: 'Restrict to Single Client IP' option cannot be configured directly in the iApp.
bugs.workaround: 'Restrict to Single Client IP' can be configured from the access policy.

bugs.title: REST API calls require “admin” user authentication.
bugs.symptoms: REST API calls will fail authentication for all users except an “admin” user.
bugs.conditions: REST API calls made by users other than “admin” user.
bugs.impact: REST API call will fail with a 401 code: “authorization failure” message.
bugs.workaround: For successful authentication, use an “admin” user for executing REST API calls.

bugs.title: Updating DNS pool monitor via transaction leaves dangling monitor_rule in MCP DB
bugs.symptoms: Dangling monitor rule after pool deletion. # tmsh delete gtm monitor tcp tcp_test 01070083:3: Monitor /Common/tcp_test is in use
bugs.conditions: Using transaction to delete pool and create pool of same name with different monitor.
bugs.impact: Unable to delete the remaining monitor.
bugs.workaround: Run: 1. # bigstart restart mcpd Or 2. Do not combine deletion and re-create pool in the same transaction.

bugs.title: Restarting the mcpd messaging service renders the PAYG VE license invalid.
bugs.symptoms: Upon mcpd service restart, the pay as you grow Virtual Edition license becomes invalid.
bugs.conditions: Restarting the mcpd messaging service.
bugs.impact: The license becomes expired. A message is displayed in the console: mcpd[5122]: 01070608:0: License is not operational (expired or digital signature does not match contents).
bugs.workaround: If you cannot avoid restarting the mcpd messaging service, then you must issue the reloadlic command, or reboot the BIG-IP (using your preferred method).
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with pay as you grow licenses following a mcpd restart.

bugs.title: in BIG-IP Virtual Edition, TMM may prematurely shut down during initialization
bugs.symptoms: TMM may prematurely shut down during its initialization when several TMMs and interfaces are configured. The system logs messages in one or more TMM log files (/var/log/tmm*): MCP connection aborted, exiting.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE). -- Happens during TMM startup. -- The issue is intermittent, but is more likely to occur on systems with a lot of TMMs (more 20 in most cases) and several interfaces (approximately 8 or more).
bugs.impact: TMM shuts down prematurely. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. Possible deadlock and MCP restart loop requiring a full reboot of the BIG-IP device.
bugs.fix: A new TCL configuration element was added: "max_poll_pre_rfw", with a default value of 4, to modulate the function of "max_poll" in TMMs which are not yet Ready-For-World. The value of "max_poll_pre_rfw" can be configured in the "tmm_base.tcl" file.

bugs.title: In the GUI, searching for virtual server addresses does not match address lists
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, if you filter the virtual server listing using an IP address, or part of an IP address, if there are any virtual servers that are using an address list that contains an address that matches that search string, those virtual servers will not show up in the search results. Similarly, if you filter the virtual server listing using an IP address, or part of an IP address, if there are any virtual servers that are using an address that matches the search string, but are using a port list, those virtual servers will not show up in the search results.
bugs.conditions: -- Using Address Lists or Port lists with a virtual server. -- Using the GUI to search for virtual servers based on address.
bugs.impact: Virtual servers that should match a search are not found.

bugs.title: [SAML SP] Assertion canonicalization fails if <AttributeValue> contains spaces.
bugs.symptoms: In /var/log/apm [apmd]modules/Authentication/Saml/SamlSPAgent.cpp: 'verifyAssertionSignature()': 5883: Verification of SAML signature #1 failed [apmd]SAML Agent: /Common/xxxxxx failed to process signed assertion, error: Digest of SignedInfo mismatch
bugs.conditions: SAML attribute values have double-byte spaces.

bugs.impact: FTP data connections are closed prematurely, causing incomplete data transfers.
bugs.workaround: This does not occur if the FTP profile for the FTP virtual server has inherit-parent-profile set to enable.

bugs.title: Fix for ID871561 might not work as expected on the VCMP host
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to deploy an engineering hot fix (EHF) for ID871561 (https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID871561.html) fails in the same manner
bugs.conditions: -- Attempting to install an EHF containing a fix for ID871561 on a vCMP guest -- The fix for ID871561 has not already been applied to the vCMP guest
bugs.impact: Unable to perform software installations on vCMP guests using installation media located on the vCMP host even if fix for ID871561 is available on VCMP guest.
bugs.workaround: Option 1: =========== Make sure that the .iso files for both base image and engineering hotfix are copied to the vCMP guest (under /shared/images) before starting the installation. If installing the software from the command line, use syntax similar to the following: tmsh install sys software hotfix <hotfix-image-name> volume <volume.name> Option 2: =========== Even if the engineering hotfix installation has failed, the base image should still have been installed properly. You can restart the vCMP guest and perform a hotfix installation on top of already installed base image, using syntax similar to the following: tmsh install sys software hotfix <hotfix-image-name> volume <volume.name> Option 3: =========== Even if the engineering hotfix installation has failed, the base image should still have been installed properly. Ensure there is copy of the engineering hotfix image locally within the vCMP Guest. Then restart the lind service on the vCMP Guest: tmsh restart sys service lind If running the vCMP Guest on multiple slots, you may need to restart lind on all slots. From the primary slot on the vCMP Guest, run: clsh tmsh restart sys service lind The hotfix installation should begin again, this time using the hotfix from within the /shared/images/ location on the vCMP Guest. Option 4: =========== Manually eject the CD from the vCMP guest's virtual CD drive, and then restart lind. On the vCMP Guest: 1. Confirm the wrong ISO image is still locked (inserted in the CD drive): isoinfo -d -i /dev/cdrom Note: Pay attention to the volume ID in the output from within the vCMP guest. 2. Unlock (eject) the image: eject -r -F /dev/cdrom && vcmphc_tool -e 3. Verify the CD drive is now empty: isoinfo -d -i /dev/cdrom The output should report an error that includes: <...> Sense Code: 0x3A Qual 0x00 (medium not present) Fru 0x0 <…> 4. Restart lind: tmsh restart sys service lind If running the vCMP Guest on multiple slots, you may need to restart lind on all vCMP Guest slots. From the primary slot on the vCMP Guest, run: clsh tmsh restart sys service lind

bugs.title: Logintegrity script for restjavad/restnoded fails
bugs.symptoms: The logintegrity script used to rotate the signature files for restnoded results in frequent cron errors similar to: find: '14232restnoded_log_pattern': No such file or directory.
bugs.conditions: When the logintegrity script runs.
bugs.impact: If the logintegrity script runs, the signature files for restnoded will not be in sync.
bugs.workaround: Modify the script file /usr/bin/rest_logintegrity: 1. mount -o remount,rw /usr 2. cp /usr/bin/rest_logintegrity /usr/bin/rest_logintegrity_original 3. vi /usr/bin/rest_logintegrity 4. Replace the following lines: restnoded_log_pattern=/var/log/restnoded/restnoded.[1-9]*.log restjavad_log_pattern=/var/log/restjavad*.[1-9]*.log With the lines: restjavad_log_pattern=/var/log/restjavad*[1-9]*.log restnoded_log_pattern=/var/log/restnoded/restnoded[1-9]*.log 5. Replace the line: wc_restnoded=$(find $$restnoded_log_pattern -cnewer $filename | wc -l) With the line: wc_restnoded=$(find $restnoded_log_pattern -cnewer $filename | wc -l) 6. mount -o remount,ro /usr
bugs.fix: When logintegrity is enabled, signature files for restnoded log files are now generated and rotated.

bugs.title: Cannot update firewall rule with ip-protocol property as 'any'

bugs.title: Asmlogd stops deleting old protobufs
bugs.symptoms: Asmlogd restarts and there are asmlogd errors: asmlogd|ERR|Oct 19 13:46:35.199|6005|,,asmlogd ended unexpectedly asmlogd|ERR|Oct 19 13:46:35.203|6005|,,Can't call method "size" on an undefined value at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/RequestLog.pm line 1902.
bugs.conditions: Disk is full -- the following warnings are being displayed: err diskmonitor[3483]: 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var/asmdata1 (slot 1) has only 0% free
bugs.impact: Old protobuf files are not cleaned up.
bugs.workaround: 0) If the /appdata partition is filled to 100% and MySQL restarts continuously, refer to the following Knowledge Articles: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14956 https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K42497314 1) To identify the empty partitions, look into: SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARTITIONS WHERE table_name = 'REQUEST_LOG' AND table_schema = 'PRX'＼G 2) For every partition that is empty, manually (or via shell script) execute this sql: ALTER TABLE PRX.REQUEST_LOG DROP PARTITION empty_partition_name where 'empty_partition_name' is the partition name as 'p100001' 4) Increase 'open_files_limit' to '10000'. -------------------------------- In the /etc/my.cnf file: 1. Change the value of the 'open_files_limit' parameter to 10000. 2. Restart MySQL: bigstart restart mysql -------------------------------- 5) pkill asmlogd Note: This workaround does not survive upgrade. It must be reapplied after every upgrade until the upgraded version contains a fix.

bugs.title: AGC 8.0 installation failure
