bugs.title: Unable to change initial admin password from GUI after root password change
bugs.symptoms: While trying to change the admin password from GUI, an error occurs: -- Authentication failed: Password expired. Update password via /mgmt/shared/authz/users.
bugs.conditions: -- Change the password for the root user the first time, before the admin password has been changed. This action sets both the root and admin password at the same time. -- Navigate to the GUI and attempt to update the admin password.
bugs.impact: GUI password change fails.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Change the password admin via the GUI before changing the root admin via ssh. -- After changing the root password, use tmsh to set the admin password using the command: modify auth user admin password.

bugs.title: Cannot specify IPv6 management IP addresses using GUI
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to set the IPv6 mgmt IP address using the GUI, even if the IPv6 address format is a not a short address. When you submit the change, the field is empty.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to set up IPv6 management address using the GUI
bugs.impact: You are unable to configure IPv6 management addresses using the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh: tmsh create sys management-ip <address>/<netmask> tmsh create sys management-route default-inet6 <address>

bugs.title: The vCMP host does not report the correct number of guest CPUs on the guest page of the GUI
bugs.symptoms: The total number of cores for a multi-slot vCMP guest is not shown correctly on the GUI page for a vCMP guest.
bugs.conditions: -- vCMP Host on VIPRION platforms with multiple blades. -- vCMP guest spanning two or more blades.
bugs.impact: Incorrect number of cores listed. -- The vCMP :: Guest List page shows all cores for all slots. -- The vCMP -> Guest List specific_guest page shows only cores for that guest's slot.
bugs.workaround: View the Guest List page to see a graphical representation of the number of cores per guest.

bugs.title: HTML meta tag URL not rewritten when received under single quotes (' ')
bugs.symptoms: The URL meta tag is not rewritten if it is encapsulated in single quotes.
bugs.conditions: HTML page with meta tag URL under single quotes('') loaded through Portal access
bugs.impact: -- Failure in redirection to URL -- Error in sending request to the URL
bugs.workaround: Use a custom iRule to find meta tag URL and remove the single ('') before it goes to rewrite. There is no standard iRule as it depends on web application accessed through Portal Access. Here is sample iRule: when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] contains "XXXXX" } { #XXXXX is accessed html file set replace_metaurl 1 set host_name [HTTP::host] } else { set replace_metaurl 0 } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if {$replace_metaurl == 1} { if { [HTTP::header exists "Content-Length"] and [HTTP::header "Content-Length"] <= 1048576 } { HTTP::collect [HTTP::header Content-Length] } else { HTTP::collect 2097152 ;# 2MB } } } when HTTP_RESPONSE_DATA { if {$replace_metaurl == 1} { # Workaround for support meta tag URL under '' # Find the meta tag URL and remove '' HTTP::release } }

bugs.title: The list of dhcp-options known to mcpd is outdated, leading to the inability to instantiate certain management-dhcp configurations.
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd daemon performs validation of the request-options and supersede-options a BIG-IP administrator specifies via the tmos.sys.management-dhcp endpoint in tmsh. As the list of dhcp-options known to mcpd is outdated, it is possible you may be returned an error when attempting to configure valid request-options or supersede-options. For example, you may be returned the following error when attempting to supersede the domain-search option: 01071627:3: Management Dhcp resource supersede-option - Invalid dhcp option: domain-search
bugs.conditions: You attempt to configure a dhcp-option unknown to mcpd as part of the request-options or supersede-options properties. Note: A common dhcp-option of which mcpd has no knowledge is domain-search. You are unlikely to experience this issue unless you are requesting or superseding this particular dhcp-option.
bugs.impact: You are unable to instantiate the desired management-dhcp configuration.
bugs.fix: The list of dhcp-options known to mcpd has been updated.

bugs.title: Virtual server may not enter hardware SYN cookie mode on BIG-IP i11000 and i15000 series appliances
bugs.symptoms: On particular platforms, virtual servers do not correctly enter hardware SYN cookie mode. Software SYN cookie mode still functions correctly.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server under SYN flood attack. -- One of the following platforms + BIG-IP i11000 series (C123) + BIG-IP i15000 series (D116)
bugs.impact: Software SYN cookies are enabled, this has a performance impact compared to the hardware mode.
bugs.fix: Virtual servers correctly enter hardware SYN cookie mode on all platforms.

bugs.title: DoS timestamp cookies are incompatible with FastL4 TCP timestamp rewrite option
bugs.symptoms: Using DoS timestamp cookies together with a FastL4 profile with the timestamp rewrite option enabled might lead to traffic failures. DoS timestamp cookies might also lead to problems with traffic generated by the Linux host.
bugs.conditions: -- DoS timestamp cookies are enabled, and either of the following: -- FastL4 profile with the timestamp rewrite option enabled. -- Traffic originating from Linux host.
bugs.impact: Traffic is dropped due to incorrect timestamps.
bugs.workaround: Disable timestamp cookies on the affected VLAN.

bugs.title: TMM core with ACCESS::policy evaluate iRule
bugs.symptoms: TMM segfaults in packtag_literal_pointer_release() during TCLRULE_CLIENT_CLOSED event attempting a session release.
bugs.conditions: -- The ACCESS::policy evaluate is still in progress when TCLRULE_CLIENT_CLOSED event is triggered. -- While the TCLRULE_CLIENT_CLOSED is in process, the ACCESS::policy evaluation completes.
bugs.impact: This triggers a race condition and causes the tmm crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes and generates a core file during the ACCESS::policy evaluate iRule under these conditions.

bugs.title: Jumbo frame issue with DPDK eNIC
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes
bugs.conditions: -- TMM is using DPDK driver with Cisco eNIC -- TMM receives jumbo sized packet
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: - Use a different driver such as sock. - Do not use or accept jumbo frames, use the following TMSH command to set the MTU to less than or equal to 1500: tmsh modify net vlan external mtu 1500
bugs.fix: Skipped initialization of structures.

bugs.title: GTM daemon leaks memory when reading GTM link objects
bugs.symptoms: The gtmd process memory consumption is higher than expected.
bugs.conditions: DNS is provisioned and a provisioned GTM link object has been loaded.
bugs.impact: Increased memory usage of the GTM daemon. This may impact other capabilities, such as starting sync operations.

bugs.title: Loading an upgraded config can result in a file object error in some cases
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade from a version prior to 13.1.0, when loading a configuration that has had an HTTPS monitor in it, if that configuration has not yet been saved, you may see errors like this in the LTM log: -- 0107134a:3: File object by name (DEFAULT) is missing. If you run 'tmsh load sys config verify' on this configuration, the system also posts the error on the screen.
bugs.conditions: -- Upgrading from a version prior to 13.1.0. -- At least one HTTPS monitor that has the kEDH cipher in its cipherlist. -- Upgrading to version 13.1.1.4 or later. -- Loading the configuration (either automatically on startup, or manually).
bugs.impact: Other than the error message, there is no impact.
bugs.workaround: After the initial reboot, save the configuration.

bugs.title: Device fails to request full sync
bugs.symptoms: Devices remain out of sync and ASM REST/GUI becomes unresponsive. asm_config_server may create many unique PIDs
bugs.conditions: -- A manual sync device group is configured and ASM sync is enabled. -- Sync pushes are typically performed in one direction, and then a sync attempt is made in the opposite direction.
bugs.impact: -- The device that is meant to receive the config sync never requests or receives it. -- The devices become unsynchronized which may cause unexpected traffic enforcement or dropped traffic. -- ASM GUI becomes unresponsive. -- Large number of asm_config_server processes increases host memory usage
bugs.workaround: Halting asm_config_server on the stuck device restores the working state and request a new sync.

bugs.title: TMM SIGSEGV core in Message Routing Framework
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while passing traffic through the message routing framework.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: TMM SIGSEGV
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: This is a rarely occurring issue associated with the iRule command 'pool XXXX member XXXX'.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use 'pool XXXX member XXXX' iRule command.
bugs.fix: This rarely occurring issue is now fixed.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when ePVA is enabled
bugs.symptoms: When ePVA is enabled on the BIG-IP system, Increased CMP redirections can cause tmm to core and report an error: tmm SIGFPE "nexthop ref valid".
bugs.conditions: -- ePVA acceleration is enabled on the BIG-IP system. -- High rate of CMP redirections.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts, and systems configured as part of a high availability (HA) group may failover.
bugs.workaround: Disable ePVA acceleration option. Note: Performing this procedure may increase CPU use because TCP connections are subsequently processed in software by the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM).
bugs.fix: TMM now operates as expected with ePVA enabled.

bugs.title: Modifying bot defense allow list via replace-all-with fails with match-order error
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs when modifying the allow list (or in case of 'load sys config verify' with similar configuration): 01b90026:3: Bot defense profile (/Common/bot-defense-device-id-generate-before-access) error: match-order should be unique.
bugs.conditions: -- Either modification via replace-all-with: tmsh modify security bot-defense profile bot-defense-device-id-generate-before-access whitelist replace-all-with { first_1 { match-order 1 source-address 10.0.0.0/8 url /foo } second_2 { match-order 2 source-address ::/32 url /bar } } -- Or delete all, add, save and load-verify: tmsh modify security bot-defense profile bot-defense-device-id-generate-before-access whitelist delete { all } tmsh modify security bot-defense profile bot-defense-device-id-generate-before-access whitelist add { first_1 { match-order 1 source-address 10.0.0.0/8 url /foo } second_2 {match-order 2 source-address ::/32 url /bar}} tmsh save sys config load sys config verify
bugs.impact: You are unable to add-replace the bot defense allow list configuration
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following workarounds: -- Change match-order of defaults in profile_base.conf to use match-order 3 and up (and load config). -- Change match-order of custom modify command (to continue with match-order 3 and up).

bugs.title: The daemon httpd_sam does not recover automatically when terminated
bugs.symptoms: APM policy redirecting users to incorrect domain, the httpd_sam daemon not running.
bugs.conditions: Daemon httpd_sam stopped with the terminate command.
bugs.impact: APM policy performing incorrect redirects.
bugs.workaround: Restart the daemons httpd_apm and httpd_sam.

bugs.conditions: -- idle timeout set to Immediate. -- iRules are configured -- performance l4, ip forwarding, l2 forwarding virtual servers are used. -- debug tmm is in use
bugs.impact: Traffic is dropped.
bugs.workaround: You can use either workaround: -- Configure a standard L4 virtual server. -- Consider removing iRules.

bugs.title: Updatecheck script hangs/Multiple updatecheck processes
bugs.symptoms: Multiple updatecheck and 'rpm -qf' processes running simultaneously. Updatecheck is not functional
bugs.conditions: Updatecheck is run periodically via a cronjob. Updatecheck runs 'rpm -qf' command.
bugs.impact: Due to that 'rpm -qf' command hangs. This causes multiple updatecheck and 'rpm -qf' processes. High CPU and memory usage. The most likely explanation is that rpmdb has gotten corrupted.
bugs.workaround: To rebuild rpmdb: 1. Halt all running updatecheck and 'rpm -qf' processes. 2. Run these commands: rm /var/lib/rpm/__db* rpm --rebuilddb

bugs.title: Inconsistency in tmsh 'object mode' for some configurations
bugs.symptoms: Tmsh does not support object mode when modifying certain configurations, such as the node configuration. This results in misleading error 'not found' even though the configuration is available.
bugs.conditions: Modify node config results in error, even though the config is present. # Node Object 'example' is created successfully (tmos)# create ltm node example address 1.2.3.4 # On modifying the node 'example', tmsh gives error (tmos)# modify ltm node example Data Input Error: node "example" not found The modify command does work when a property is specified: (tmos)# modify ltm node example description "Node 1234"
bugs.impact: Inconsistent tmsh syntax when using 'object mode' for modifying the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Use 'tmsh modify' commands, or the GUI, to make the required changes without 'entering' the object in tmsh.

bugs.title: SCP file transfer hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the SCP file transfer system does not follow current best practices.
bugs.conditions: Administrative user with SCP access.
bugs.impact: users with with SCP access but without shell access can run arbitrary commands
bugs.fix: The SCP file transfer system now follows current best practices.

bugs.title: Possible installation failure with three software volumes on a BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: When you attempt to create a third software volume (slot) on a BIG-IP device, a 'disk full' error occurs: HD1.3 BIG-IP 16.1.0 0.0.1481 no failed (Disk full (volume group). See SOL#10636) yes
bugs.conditions: -- Using iSeries platforms. -- Attempt to install certain BIG-IP software versions on a third installation volume on a BIG-IP device.
bugs.impact: Installation to the third volume fails with a disk full error.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by reducing the dat.appdata volume size. For instructions on how to do so, see K74200262: Reducing the size of the appdata volume with the lvreduce utility :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K74200262 Notes ====== -- Depending on which software versions exist, installation might succeed, or it might fail; e.g., these existing configuration succeed: - v12.1.2 + v16.0.0 + v16.1.0 - v15.1.3 + v16.0.0 + v16.1.0 -- Even though v15.1.3 and 16.0.x have a smaller footprint, if there are two 16.1.0 installation locations, the third volume installation/upgrade does not succeed. -- You can avoid the issue completely formatting the system while you install (i.e., using 'image2disk --format=volumes'). Important: Make sure to back up your configuration before formatting the system.
bugs.fix: Beginning in BIG-IP 16.1.0, the disk layout created when reformatting (i.e., using 'image2disk --format=volumes') has slightly decreased the size of the 'appdata' volume to allow for three software volumes.
bugs.behavior: Beginning in BIG-IP 16.1.0, the disk layout created when reformatting (i.e., using 'image2disk --format=volumes') has slightly decreased the size of the 'appdata' volume to allow for three software volumes.

bugs.title: Configuration is not updated during auto-discovery
bugs.symptoms: Auto-discovery fails, resulting in OAuth failure. In /var/log/apm: -- OAuth Client: failed for server '<server>' using 'authorization_code' grant type (<grant type>), error: None of the configured JWK keys match the received JWT token

bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with auto-discovery and JWKs.

bugs.title: Certain management-dhcp supersede options fail to restore correctly when the configuration is reloaded from a file.
bugs.symptoms: After reloading the configuration from a file, management-dhcp supersede options whose values contained a double quote character (") no longer contain the character. For instance, after reloading the configuration, the following section: # tmsh list sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config { supersede-options { domain-name { value { "example.com" } } domain-name-servers { value { 8.8.8.8 } } domain-search { value { "example.com" } } } } Becomes: # tmsh list sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config { supersede-options { domain-name { value { example.com } } domain-name-servers { value { 8.8.8.8 } } domain-search { value { example.com } } } } This also affects the configuration file for the dhclient/dhclient6 daemons that the system automatically generates from the aforementioned config stanza.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following statements apply: --- The values of management-dhcp supersede options contain double quote characters. --- The configuration is reloaded from file. The BIG-IP system reloads the configuration from file in the following cases: -- When you issue the 'tmsh load sys config' command. -- After an upgrade, as the mcpd binary database does not exist yet. -- When troubleshooting requires removing the mcpd binary database and reloading the config from file. -- When the system is relicensed. -- When system provisioning changes. -- When a UCS/SCF archive is restored. -- When someone merges in config from file or terminal (but this is limited to the actual contents being merged in, not the entire configuration).
bugs.impact: The in-memory mcpd configuration relating to management-dhcp supersede options is incorrect. The /etc/dhclient.conf file that is automatically generated contains incorrect syntax. As a result of this, the dhclient/dhclient6 daemons fail to parse the file and run with an incomplete configuration. Ultimately, the system does not behave as configured in regard to its management-dhcp configuration.
bugs.workaround: Reapply the desired management-dhcp supersede-options configuration using the tmsh utility. For example, to restore the intended in-memory configuration shown under Symptoms, you would run within tmsh: # modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options none # modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options add { domain-search { value add { \"example.com\" } } } # modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options add { domain-name { value add { \"example.com\" } } } # modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options add { domain-name-servers { value add { 8.8.8.8 } } } # save sys config On versions earlier than 15.0.0, you must also restart the dhclient/dhclient6 daemons by running: bigstart restart dhclient dhclient6 Note that the workaround is not permanent and will be invalidated the next time the config is loaded from file again.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system user is no longer responsible for knowing which dhcp-options require quoting and which do not. This determination is now done internally by mcpd, which uses the correct syntax for each supersede-option when writing the /etc/dhclient.conf file. This means that, as the BIG-IP system user, you are not required to quote anything when manipulating management-dhcp supersede-options in tmsh. For instance, you can enter the following command: tmsh modify sys management-dhcp sys-mgmt-dhcp-config supersede-options add { domain-search { value add { one.example.com two.example.com } } } And the system inserts the following instruction in the /etc/dhclient.conf file: supersede domain-search "one.example.com", "two.example.com" ;

bugs.title: IP fragments for the same flow are dropped if they are received on different VLANs and route domains.
bugs.symptoms: When duplicate IP fragments for the same flow (same connection tuple and flow ID) are simultaneously received on different VLANs or route domains, IP datagram reassembly fails.
bugs.conditions: -- Multicast traffic where identical fragments arrive on two different VLANs. -- IP fragments for the same flow are received on different VLANs. -- Alternatively, IP fragments for the same flow are received on different route domains.
bugs.impact: IP fragments that fail reassembly are dropped.
bugs.fix: The tm.ipfragreassemblestrict db var is disabled by default. When enabled IPv6 or IPv4 fragments arriving on different interfaces are queued separately. Note: In order to resolve this issue, a version with this fix is necessary and the tm.ipfragreassemblestrict must be set to enable.

bugs.title: DNSSEC manual key created with other algorithms ends up using RSA/SHA1 algorithm
bugs.symptoms: Generated DNSSEC keys always use RSA/SHA1 algorithm.
bugs.conditions: DNSSEC keys are generated with manual key management method.
bugs.impact: You are unable to create DNSSEC keys with other algorithms.
bugs.workaround: Choose automatic key management method.

bugs.title: After upgrade, the copied SSL vhf/vht profile prevents traffic from passing &start;
bugs.symptoms: After an RPM upgrade, SSL Orchestrator traffic does not pass
bugs.conditions: Upgrading SSL Orchestrator via RPM
bugs.impact: Traffic will not pass.
bugs.workaround: Bigstart restart tmm
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue that was preventing from passing after an RPM upgrade.

bugs.title: IPv6 truncated in /var/log/ltm when writing PPTP log information from PPTP_ALG in CGNAT
bugs.symptoms: The PPTP log entries for NAT64 traffic have a truncated IPv6 address.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered when viewing PPTP log entries.
bugs.impact: IPV6 addresses in PPTP logs are truncated.
bugs.fix: The full IPv6 address is now logged in PPTP logs.

bugs.title: PVA accelerated traffic does not update route domain stats
bugs.symptoms: PVA accelerated traffic does not update route domain stats
bugs.conditions: -- PVA accelerated traffic. -- Viewing the route domain stats.
bugs.impact: The route domain stats may be inaccurate
bugs.workaround: Use the virtual server stats or ifc_stats instead.

bugs.title: Loading UCS files may hang if ASM is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: If a UCS file from a BIG-IP system running a different software version that also has an ASM configuration is loaded onto a device that already has ASM provisioned, the load may hang indefinitely.
bugs.conditions: -- A system that has ASM provisioned. -- Loading a UCS file with an ASM configuration that comes from a different system.
bugs.impact: -- UCS load might fail. -- Config save and load operations fails while the UCS load hangs. The failure of those operations may not be obvious, leaving the BIG-IP saved configuration different from the running configuration.
bugs.workaround: If you encounter this, run 'load sys config default' and de-provision ASM. The UCS file should then load successfully.
bugs.fix: Loading UCS files no longer hangs if ASM is provisioned.

bugs.title: Bigtop command is showing inaccurate 'Conn' value for NODE ip:port
bugs.symptoms: In bigtop output, "Conn" value for "NODE ip:port" seen under "bits in prior n seconds" shows the same value as "Conn" value seen under "bits since" and "Total Connections" in show ltm node output.
bugs.conditions: There were connections established on server-side toward pool member.
bugs.impact: "Conn" value is not refreshed according to "bits in prior n seconds" interval.

bugs.title: Tmm crash SIGSEGV - rcs_getsalen() in lib/rc_net.c
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes while processing a large number of tunnels.
bugs.conditions: -- A large number of ipsec tunnels
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Memory allocation failures are handled.

bugs.title: Mixing IPv4 and IPv6 device IPs on GSLB server object results in nullGeneral database error.
bugs.symptoms: Unable to create GLSB Server object with both IPv4 and IPv6 self IPs as device IPs.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS and LTM services enabled. -- Configure two self IPs on the box for IPv4 and IPv6. -- GLSB Server object creation with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in device tab along with Virtual Server Discovery enable.
bugs.impact: GSLB Server object creation fails.
bugs.workaround: TMSH is not impacted. Use TMSH to create GSLB Server objects.
bugs.fix: GSLB Server object creation no longer fails.

bugs.title: Edge Client 'Save Password'' checkbox not visible when 'Allow Password Caching' method is 'memory'
bugs.symptoms: The 'Save Password' checkbox is not displayed.
bugs.conditions: -- 'Allow Password Caching' is selected in the connectivity profile. -- The 'Allow Password Caching' method is 'memory'. -- From the Edge Client, access the virtual server.
bugs.impact: The 'Save Password' option does not exist on the logon page.
bugs.workaround: Use the 'disk' option in 'Allow Password Caching' instead of 'memory'.

bugs.title: Username/Password JSON elements of login page detected as case sensitive when the policy is configured as case insensitive
bugs.symptoms: A JSON element of a page behaves in a case-sensitive manner even if the policy is configured as case insensitive.
bugs.conditions: - Using JSON in a page - Authentication type is json/ajax - The policy is configured case-insensitive - JSON element seen in a request has uppercase letter(s)
bugs.impact: Case-insensitive configuration fails to detect uppercase JSON elements in a page. This may cause, for example, brute force protection to not trigger.

bugs.title: In IPsec, support AES-GCM on IKE Peer phase 1
bugs.symptoms: The IKEv2 phase 1 does not support AES-GCM protocol for Authentication and Encryption algorithms.
bugs.conditions: Configuring IKE Peer.
bugs.impact: Cannot establish IKEv2 phase 1 using AES-GCM.
bugs.fix: Added AES-GCM support for IKEv2 phase 1. Configure AES-GCM at IKE Peer and establish an IKEv2 phase 1 tunnel.

bugs.title: AVR Inspection Dashboard 'Last Month' does not show all data points
bugs.symptoms: A daily-based report (report with resolution of one day in each data-point) can be provided to only request with up-to 30 days. A request with 31 days shows only 2 entries.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when generating a 'Last Month' report for a month that contains 31 days of data.
bugs.impact: AVR Inspection Dashboard displays less data than expected: 2 points instead of 31 points.
bugs.fix: Viewing a 'Last Month' graph now reports ~30 days worth of data, rather than a variable amount of data based on actual calendar periods.

bugs.title: SIP messages with unbalanced escaped quotes in headers are dropped
bugs.symptoms: Dropped SIP messages.
bugs.conditions: -- MRF SIP virtual server -- SIP Header Field has an escaped quote
bugs.impact: Certain SIP messages are not being passed via MRF.

bugs.title: The /var partition is full as cleanup of files on secondary is not executing
bugs.symptoms: The system does not boot because the /var partition is full. You see a large number of "storageXXXX.zip" files in /var/config/rest/
bugs.conditions: This may be observed on multi-blade vCMP guests and hosts, as well as on multi-blade tenants.
bugs.impact: The partition housing /var/config/ may become 100% full, impacting future disk IO operation and it may cause unexpected traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: Important: This workaround is temporary, and may need to be periodically performed either manually or from a script. Impact of Workaround: While these steps are performed, the BIG-IP REST API will be temporarily inaccessible, and higher disk IO may be seen. Run the following commands, in sequence: bigstart stop restjavad rm -rf /var/config/rest/storage*.zip rm -rf /var/config/rest/*.tmp bigstart start restjavad Manual application of these workaround steps clears the 100% utilized space condition and allows the partition to resume normal operation.
bugs.fix: N/A.

bugs.title: After UCS restore on HA pair, one of the devices is missing folder /var/config/rest/iapps/f5-iappslx-ssl-orchestrator
bugs.symptoms: After restoring via UCS file, the SSL Orchestrator page reads: Not Found The requested URL was not found on this server
bugs.conditions: -- Devices are in a high availability (HA) pair -- SSL Orchestrator deployed -- A UCS file is loaded
bugs.impact: SSL Orchestrator is not available. /var/config/rest/iapps/f5-iappslx-ssl-orchestrator is not restored correctly during UCS load.
bugs.workaround: Restore the UCS file again

bugs.title: Tomcat may crash while processing TMUI requests
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, Tomcat may crash while processing TMUI requests.
bugs.conditions: - GTM provisioned - Authenticated administrative user - TMUI request
bugs.impact: Access to the TMUI disrupted while Tomcat restarts.
bugs.fix: TMUI now processes requests as expected.

bugs.title: Zrd in restart loop with empty named.conf
bugs.symptoms: The zrd process enters a restart loop: logger[20015]: Re-starting zrd
bugs.conditions: This occurs when /var/named/config/named.conf is empty.
bugs.impact: The zrd process enters a restart loop. If the device is in a sync group, zrd enters a restart loop on all devices.
bugs.workaround: Restore content to the named.conf file.

bugs.title: ASM attack signature may not match as expected
bugs.symptoms: When processing traffic with ASM, attack signature 200000128 may not match as expected.
bugs.conditions: - Attack signature 200000128 enabled.
bugs.impact: Processed traffic may not match all expected attack signatures
bugs.fix: Attack signature 200000128 now matches as expected.

bugs.title: Password change through REST or GUI not allowed if the password is expired
bugs.symptoms: When trying to update the expired password through REST or the GUI, the system reports and error: Authentication failed: Password expired. Update password via /mgmt/shared/authz/users.
bugs.conditions: -- Password is expired. -- Password change is done through either REST or the GUI.
bugs.impact: Expired password cannot be updated through REST or the GUI.
bugs.workaround: Update password using tmsh: tmsh modify auth password <username>
bugs.fix: You can now change an expired password through REST or the GUI.

bugs.title: Improper handling of DHCP flows leading to orphaned server-side connections
bugs.symptoms: When there are multiple client-side flows tied to a single server-side DHCP flow, timeout handling on the client-side flows is incorrect and might lead to a server-side flow getting orphaned. This results in traffic from the server not making its way back to the client.
bugs.conditions: Regular DHCP virtual server in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not passed to the client.

bugs.title: iptunnel/ GRE is missing per-tmm stats
bugs.symptoms: Lack of ingress/egress stats in the iptunnel GRE layer
bugs.conditions: Tmctl -d blade tmm/iptunnel_gre
bugs.impact: iptunnel/ GRE is missing per-tmm stats

bugs.title: ASM BD process may crash while processing HTML traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the ASM BD process may crash while processing HTML traffic
bugs.conditions: - ASM profile enabled
bugs.impact: ASM traffic disrupted while BD restarts.
bugs.fix: ASM now processes HTML traffic as expected.

bugs.title: NGFIPS device lockup can cause mcpd crash
bugs.symptoms: MCPD process crashes with SIGABORT signal.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if the NGFIPS HSM device locks up.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while mcpd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Restart of the system may recover the NGFIPS HSM device lockup if the there is no hardware issue.

bugs.title: No IP address format validation while adding IP addresses in IPv6 LAN Address Space or IPv6 Exclude Address Space when configuring Network Access Resource.
bugs.symptoms: IP address format is not properly validated for IPv6 LAN Address Space and IPv6 Exclude Address Space fields which may lead to misconfiguration when IPv4 addresses are configured in this fields.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if you misconfigure the IPv6 LAN Address Space or IPv6 Exclude Address Space fields by adding IPv4 addresses while configuring Network Access Resource.
bugs.impact: This may cause the split tunnel to misfunction.
bugs.workaround: Correct the configuration by removing IPv4 Addresses in IPv6 LAN Address Space or IPv6 Exclude Address Space.

bugs.title: No IP address format validation while adding IP addresses in IPv4 LAN Address Space or IPv4 Exclude Address Space when configuring Network Access Resource.
bugs.symptoms: IP address format is not properly validated for IPv4 LAN Address Space and IPv4 Exclude Address Space fields which may lead to misconfiguration when IPv6 addresses are configured in this fields.
bugs.conditions: This can occur if you misconfigure the IPv4 LAN Address Space or IPv4 Exclude Address Space fields by adding IPv6 addresses while configuring Network Access Resource.
bugs.impact: This may cause the split tunnel to malfunction.
bugs.workaround: Correct the configuration by removing IPv6 Addresses in IPv4 LAN Address Space or IPv4 Exclude Address Space.

bugs.title: CSRF token modification may allow WAF bypass on GET requests
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions a parameter is not processed as expected.
bugs.conditions: 1. CSRF feature is configured 2. Request contains a crafted parameter
bugs.impact: Malicious request will bypass signatures and will not raise any attack signature violation
bugs.fix: The parameter is now processed as expected.

bugs.title: AFM rule not triggered
bugs.symptoms: An AFM rule is not triggered when it should be.
bugs.conditions: -- Source and destination zone configured -- A gateway pool is used in the route
bugs.impact: A firewall rule is not triggered and the default deny rule is used.
bugs.workaround: Alter the route to use an IP address and not a pool.
bugs.fix: Firewall rules are now triggered when gateway pools are used.

bugs.title: TCP connections may fail when AFM global syncookies are in operation.
bugs.symptoms: TCP connections are rejected by the BIG-IP system with reset cause "No flow found for ACK".
bugs.conditions: 1) AFM is provisioned. 2) AFM global syncookies are in operation. 3a) The traffic arrives over an APM VPN tunnel, and is handled by one of the internal default APM listeners (not a more specific listener). -or- 3b) The device is Active for multiple floating traffic-groups, said traffic-groups don't use MAC masquerading, and connection.syncookies.algorithm is set to software. -or- 3c) The traffic belongs to traffic-group-local-only, and connection.syncookies.algorithm is set to software.
bugs.impact: Application failures as TCP connections fail.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue as follows. - For the APM VPN case: define a listener (e.g. virtual server) over the tunnel to process the traffic (instead of relying on one of the default internal APM listeners). Note that the workaround may not work if the device is Active for multiple floating traffic-groups at the same time. - For the device Active for multiple floating traffic-groups case: use MAC masquerading for all floating traffic-group, or set connection.syncookies.algorithm back to its default of hardware. - For the traffic-group-local-only case: set connection.syncookies.algorithm back to its default of hardware, or disable AFM global syncookies by turning off the TCP Half-Open attack vector at the device level.
bugs.fix: TCP connections now establish successfully regardless of syncookies being in operation.

bugs.title: The management-dhcp contextual help for supersede-options is not available
bugs.symptoms: In TMSH, unable to view the contextual help for supersede-options of management-dhcp.
bugs.conditions: In TMSH, configuring DHCP settings for the management interface.
bugs.impact: The help text is not available on usage of supersede-options.
bugs.fix: Added missing contextual help for supersede-options.

bugs.title: Unable to create APM policies in a sync-only folder &start;
bugs.symptoms: Unable to configure an APM policy in a sync-only folder, or the configuration fails to load after an upgrade, with an error message similar to: -- err mcpd[mcpd_pid]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid Devicegroup Reference. The customization_group (/Common/sync-only/example_apm_customization) requires customization_source (/Common/standard) to be syncd to the same devices
bugs.conditions: -- Multiple BIG-IP devices configured in a sync-only device group, but different/non-overlapping failover device groups -- APM policy being created in a folder or partition associated with sync-only device group.
bugs.impact: -- Unable to create the access policy. -- The configuration fails to load and the device remains inoperative.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following strategies to prevent the issue: --Do not create APM policies in a sync-only folder. --Disable MCPD device-group reference validation for the sync-only folder, e.g.: tmsh modify sys folder /Common/sync-only no-ref-check true tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: iRule command "SSL:session invalidate" not working as expected
bugs.symptoms: The iRule command "SSL:session invalidate" allows session resumption to happen. Session resumption not supposed to occur when this iRule command is used in an iRule.
bugs.conditions: "SSL:session invalidate" is used in the iRule event HTTP_REQUEST
bugs.impact: Session resumption would happen where the iRule is used with "SSL:session invalidate" included which is not supposed to occur
bugs.workaround: Session resumption should be disabled in SSL profiles
bugs.fix: SSL::Session invalidate will now properly remove the current session information from the session cache.

bugs.title: Live Update via HTTPS Proxy No Longer Works
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP devices that need to use an HTTPS proxy server to communicate with callhome.f5.com, no longer receive, or check for, automatic updates.
bugs.conditions: -- The BIG-IP device is behind a network firewall. -- Outbound communication must be through an HTTPS proxy.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP cannot contact the callhome.f5.com server to check for, or receive, updates.
bugs.workaround: 1. Manually download updates from the F5 Downloads server, 2. Install the updates directly on the BIG-IP device.

bugs.title: When (DoS Detection threshold = DoS Mitigation threshold) for a vector, logging is erratic when hardware offload is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Some DoS-related log messages may be missing
bugs.conditions: -- Static DDoS vector is configured with the same mitigation threshold and detection threshold setpoint. -- The platform supports Hardware DDoS mitigation and hardware mitigation and hardware mitigation is not disabled.
bugs.impact: Applications dependent on log frequency may be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Configure the mitigation limit about 10% over the attack limit.

bugs.title: When dos.logging interval is greater than 1, the log statistics are not accumulated
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect DoS statistics may be provide via logs.
bugs.conditions: DDoS log interval is set to more than 1 second
bugs.impact: Applications dependent on log provided DoS statistics may be impacted.
bugs.workaround: Do not change the default log interval value.

bugs.title: Traffic disaggregation not working properly on i11800/i11600 platforms
bugs.symptoms: Traffic disaggregation not working properly on i11800/i11600 platforms.
bugs.conditions: -- Using i11800/i11600 platforms. -- Running a 12.1.x software release.
bugs.impact: Traffic fails with a tmm log message similar to: crit tmm10[14847]: 01010201:2: Inet port exhaustion on 1.1.1.2 to 1.1.1.1:8 (proto 1)

bugs.title: Round-robin GRE Disaggregator for hardware and software
bugs.symptoms: GRE tunnel traffic is pinned to one CPU.
bugs.conditions: GRE traffic is passed through BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: Traffic is pinned to one CPU and overall performance is degraded.

bugs.title: TMM CPU imbalance with GRE/TB and GRE/MPLS traffic
bugs.symptoms: When handling unidirectional GRE traffic, a lack of inner payload entropy can lead to CPU pinning. In some circumstances, handling this traffic should not require maintaining state across TMMs.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with GRE/TB (transparent ethernet bridging) and GRE/MPLS traffic.
bugs.impact: TMM utilization across CPUs is imbalanced, which can impact overall device performance.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP now has a 'iptunnel.ether_nodag' DB key, which defaults to 'disable'. When this DB key is enabled, the BIG-IP system always processes tunnel-encapsulated traffic on the TMM that handles the tunnel packet, rather than re-disaggregating it.

bugs.title: APM policy ending with redirection results in policy execution failure
bugs.symptoms: After successful authentication, the APM end user client connection gets reset. /var/log/apm shows errors: err tmm2[18140]: 01490514:3: (null):Common:00000000: Access encountered error: ERR_VAL. File: ../modules/hudfilter/access/access.c, Function: access_rewrite_pdp_response_to_302, Line: 19766
bugs.conditions: Access policy has a path ending with a redirect.
bugs.impact: APM end user clients cannot access the backend resources protected by the policy.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with APM policies not working when they ended with redirect.

bugs.title: Subsessionlist entries leak if there is no RADIUS accounting agent in policy
bugs.symptoms: Subsessionlist entries are not cleaned up when subsessions are deleted. For long-lived main sessions, use cases such as API protection, the number of leaked subsessionlist entries increases over time, resulting in increasing memory consumption. If high availability (HA) is configured, the standby device can experience even more memory pressure when a very large number of subsessionlist entries are sent to it for mirroring.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs if the main session is long-lived and there is no RADIUS accounting agent in the policy.
bugs.impact: TMM may run out of memory and restart. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Support for DSLITE event logging for field format and user format
bugs.symptoms: NA
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: Though Dslite tunnel src ip and route domain is supported for default mode, the tunnel destination address is not visible.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Error log: Failed to reset strict operations; disconnecting from mcpd
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting the device you are unable to access the GUI. When checking the LTM logs in the SSH/console, it repeatedly prompts an error: tmm crash. Failed to reset strict operations; disconnecting from mcpd.
bugs.conditions: -- APM provisioned. -- Previous EPSEC packages that are still residing on the system from earlier BIG-IP versions are installed upon boot.
bugs.impact: Mcpd fails to fully load and the device fails to come up fully, and it cannot pass traffic. An internal timer might cause the installation to be aborted and all daemons to be restarted through bigstart restart. Traffic is disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: You can recover by restarting the services. Traffic will be disrupted while tmm restarts: 1. Stop the overdog daemon first by issuing the command: systemctl stop overdog. 2. Restart all services by issuing the command: bigstart restart. 3. Wait for 10 to 20 mins until EPSEC packages are successfully installed and mcpd successfully starts. 4. Start the overdog daemon after the system is online systemctl start overdog. Impact of workaround: it is possible that the EPSEC rpm database is or could be corrupted. If you find that you cannot access the GUI after appying this workaround, see https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1188857.html
bugs.fix: After rebooting the device, you can now access the GUI without a 'Failed to reset' error.

bugs.title: Changing a Traffic Matching Criteria port from 'any' to another value can prevent a virtual server from processing traffic
bugs.symptoms: If a virtual server is using a traffic-matching-criteria (TMC) with a destination-inline-port of zero ('any'), and this is later changed (either to a non-zero port value, or to a port-list with non-zero port values) the virtual server stops processing traffic. If tmm is restarted (which causes an outage) the virtual server resumes accepting traffic using the new ports. In addition, changing the virtual server's port back to 'any' also causes traffic processing to resume.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server using an address list for its destination, and 'any' (zero) for its destination port. -- Changing the virtual server's destination port to a non-zero value, or to a port-list with non-zero port values.
bugs.impact: The virtual server stops processing traffic.
bugs.workaround: To recover, you can do either of the following: -- Restart tmm: bigstart restart tmm -- Change the virtual server's port back to 'any' (0).

bugs.title: BIG-IP DataSafe GUI does not save changes
bugs.symptoms: Due to a JavaScript error, the BIG-IP DataSafe GUI does not save changes.
bugs.conditions: -- Provision FPS. -- License DataSafe. -- Configure the system using the GUI.
bugs.impact: Configurations made for DataSafe using the BIG-IP Configuration Utility GUI cannot be saved.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to configure the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP DataSafe GUI is working properly and configurations are now saved.

bugs.title: Accessing pool members from configuration utility is slow with large config
bugs.symptoms: Accessing the pool members page from the BIG-IP Configuration Utility/GUI is slow compared with accessing Pool members from TMSH/CLI.
bugs.conditions: -- Accessing pool member information through the BIG-IP configuration utility. -- Thousands of pools and pool members in the configuration.
bugs.impact: In the GUI, it takes approximately 20-30 seconds, whereas the CLI returns results in less than 1 second, Managing pool members from configuration utility is very slow causing performance impact.
bugs.fix: Optimized the GUI query used for retrieving pool members data.

bugs.title: TMM crash when disabling/re-enabling a blade that triggers a primary blade transition.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes during the primary blade transition.
bugs.conditions: -- Using bidirectional forwarding detection. -- Primary blade transition occurs.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: TMM no longer crashes on primary blade transition.

bugs.title: SNI configuration is not sent via HTTPS when in-tmm monitors are disabled
bugs.symptoms: The Server Name Indication (SNI) extension is missing on the HTTPS handshake.
bugs.conditions: -- Global in-tmm monitors are disabled -- HTTPS monitor traffic
bugs.impact: The HTTPS client-server handshake occurs without a TLS SNI.

bugs.title: NTLM Authentication fails with 'RPC Fault received' error and return code: 0xc0000001 (STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL)
bugs.symptoms: NTLM Authentication fails with 'RPC Fault received' error and return code: 0xc0000001 (STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL)
bugs.conditions: 1. NTLM front-end authentication is enabled. 2. Active Directory users are subscribed to more than one hundred groups.
bugs.impact: NTLM authentication for Active Directory users which are subscribed to more than hundred groups will fail.
bugs.fix: A fix has been provided to the sequence number handling which is used to calculate the RPC checksum as part of ID 949477.

bugs.title: Hostnames that contain a period are logged incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: Sylog-ng uses the hostname (machine name) and truncates it starting at the first '.' (period). This results in hostnames that contain a period being logged incorrectly (for example, 'my.hostname' is logged as 'my' by syslog-ng). Additionally, hostnames are being truncated in bootmarker logs and the ltm, apm, apm, ipsec, saas, and fw_log that are sourced from TMM. Three sub-bugs BZ1076909, BZ1076921, BZ1080317 are created and BZ998649 is the base bug for tracking the above three issues.
bugs.conditions: Hostname contains a period '.' (For example 'my.hostname').
bugs.impact: Some logs that go directly to syslog-ng use a truncated hostname. Logs sourced from TMM uses truncated hostname.

bugs.title: Active_zombie_port_blocks counter from fw_lsn_pool_pba_stat stats may reach unrealistically large value.
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, the active_zombie_port_blocks counter from fw_lsn_pool_pba_stat statistics may reach an unrealistically large value.
bugs.conditions: -- VIPRION system with more than one blade -- ASM is provisioned -- Network address translation is in use -- Source translation type: Dynamic PAT -- PAT mode: Port Block Allocation
bugs.impact: Active_zombie_port_blocks counter indications are incorrect. Otherwise system functionality is unaffected.

bugs.title: Query for virtual address statistics is slow when there are hundreds of virtual address and address lists entries
bugs.symptoms: If there are hundreds of virtual addresses and hundreds of address entries spanning one or more address lists, mcpd might take seconds to reply to a query for virtual address statistics. One of the more commonly visible signs of this is high CPU usage by mcpd if it's processing a large number of queries for virtual address statistics. It is also likely that snmpd responses will be severely delayed to SNMP agent requests.
bugs.conditions: -- Hundreds of virtual servers. -- Hundreds of address entries spanning one or many address lists. -- Running SNMP queries for virtual address statistics.
bugs.impact: -- High CPU usage by mcpd. -- SNMP requests/polling timeouts occur because mcpd takes hundreds of milliseconds to respond. Note: If the address lists that contain the entries are not used in traffic-matching-criteria (and therefore do not increase the size of the tmstat virtual_address_stat table), mcpd response time is in the tens of milliseconds.
bugs.fix: Improved performance for query for virtual address statistics when there are hundreds of virtual address and address lists entries.

bugs.title: When large no of feed list URLs are configured, BIG-IP takes long time to sync IP list
bugs.symptoms: If large numbers of feed URLs are configured in the IPI Policy, it takes a lot of time to fetch the IP lists from the feed server. BIG-IP system performance is significantly degraded.
bugs.conditions: -- security ip-intelligence policy -- security ip-intelligence feed-list : add large number of URLs to the list
bugs.impact: It can take several minutes to multiple hours for the BIG-IP system to fetch updates from the feed server.
bugs.fix: After fix, Performance had improved significantly.

bugs.title: Load sys config is failing with OOM in MCPD processing
bugs.symptoms: While loading a large config on BIG-IP, mcpd runs at high CPU for a while, then is killed by the OOM killer when MCPD starts increasing rapidly in size.
bugs.conditions: -- Licensed and provisioned modules: LTM+APM+AFM -- large number of virtual servers configured and executing "load sys config".
bugs.impact: Config load fails with std::badalloc with OOM.

bugs.title: MCPD consumes excessive CPU while collecting statistics
bugs.symptoms: MCPD CPU utilization is 100%.
bugs.conditions: This condition can occur when the BIG-IP system has a large number of virtual servers, pools, and pool members for which statistics are being collected. The CPU impact is proportional to the number of objects configured. It appears unlikely to see a significant impact when under 1000 objects.
bugs.impact: CPU utilization by MCPD is excessive.

bugs.title: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels fail after a config sync from Standby to Active
bugs.symptoms: When racoon (the IKEv1 daemon) sees a tunnel config change, which occurs due to a config sync from the standby device, the change causes tmm and racoon to have conflicting views on the state of that tunnel. If the IKEv1 tunnel is up at the time of the config change, tmm fails to restart the tunnel.
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec IKEv1 tunnel in use. -- Changes made to IPsec IKEv1 tunnel on the Standby BIG-IP device, which are then sync'd to the Active BIG-IP device. -- And/or a full config sync from the Standby to Active BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: IPsec IKEv1 tunnels fail and do not start again.
bugs.workaround: -- Do not make changes to IPsec IKEv1 tunnels on the Standby device. -- Avoid full syncs from Standby to Active. How to recover when the problem occurs: -- Disable the affected ike-peer and re-enable it.
bugs.fix: IKEv1 tunnels are able to negotiate after Standby to Active config sync.

bugs.title: REST endpoint registration errors in restjavad logs
bugs.symptoms: Errors are logged to /var/log/restjavad.0.log at the SEVERE log level: [SEVERE]... [IcrWorker] Unable to register iControl endpoint "/xxxx/xxxx". Error: uriPath '/tm/xxxx/xxxx' already registered
bugs.conditions: The system reports these errors during startup of the restjavad service because of multiple registrations of the same endpoint.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact and these errors can be ignored.

bugs.title: SSL::profile may select profile with outdated configuration
bugs.symptoms: Under some circumstances, an iRule-selected SSL profile may a send previously configured certificate to the peer.
bugs.conditions: iRule command SSL::profile is used to select a profile that is not attached to the virtual server, and changes have been made in the profile's cert-key-chain field.
bugs.impact: The TLS client may receive an outdated certificate that does not match with the current configuration, potentially leading to handshake failures.
bugs.workaround: Avoid making changes to a profile that is actively being used by the iRule command.
bugs.fix: The system now makes sure that SSL profiles are properly reloaded after changes are made.

bugs.title: After changing management IP addresses, devices can be stuck indefinitely in improper Active/Active or Standby/Standby states.
bugs.symptoms: After a device (or multiple devices) in a sync-failover device-group undergoes a management IP change, multiple devices in the group can be stuck indefinitely in improper Active/Active or Standby/Standby failover states.
bugs.conditions: -- One or more devices belonging to a sync-failover device-group undergo a management IP change.
bugs.impact: -- The affected units are unable to pass traffic, as they are either both Standby or Active (resulting in either no service availability or IP address conflicts in the network).
bugs.workaround: If you are planning to change management IP addresses on your devices, consider doing so during a maintenance window, in order to account for the eventuality this issue might occur. Then, if this issue does occur, you can restore correct system functionality by restarting the sod daemon on all units that had their management IP address changed. To do so, run the following command: tmsh restart sys service sod Note: This is a one-time workaround, and the issue may re-occur if the devices undergo further management IP address changes in the future.
bugs.fix: Redundant devices remain in the correct failover state following a management IP address change.

bugs.title: Running Diagnostics report for Edge Client on Windows does not follow best practice
bugs.symptoms: Running Diagnostics report for Edge Client on Windows does not follow best practice
bugs.conditions: Running Diagnostics report for Edge client on Windows system
bugs.impact: Edge client does not follow best practice
bugs.workaround: No workaround.
bugs.fix: Edge Client on Windows now follows best practice

bugs.title: Some HTTPS monitors are failing after upgrade when config has different SSL option
bugs.symptoms: Some HTTPS monitors are failing after upgrade when the config has different SSL option properties for different monitors.
bugs.conditions: -- Individual SSL profiles exist for different HTTPS monitors with SSL parameters. -- A unique server SSL profile is configured for each HTTP monitor (one with cert/key, one without).
bugs.impact: Some HTTPS monitors fail. Pool is down. Virtual server is down.

bugs.title: Message 'err sha256_generic module not installed' when booting up
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system logs an error message when booting up in v14.1.3 and v14.1.3.1 on platforms with Intel Crypto. -- err /etc/sysconfig/modules/quickassist.modules[2061]: sha256_generic module not installed.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when rebooting BIG-IP devices containing Intel Crypto: -- BIG-IP i15600 / i15800 platforms -- BIG-IP i4800 platform -- VIPRION B4450N blade
bugs.impact: This message is benign and you can safely ignore it.

bugs.title: iRule 'pool'/'virtual' commands not triggered in CLIENT_ACCEPTED with HTTP/2.
bugs.symptoms: The 'pool'/'virtual' iRule commands cause the specified pool to be used directly. However, with HTTP/2, the 'pool'/'virtual' command may fail to execute within the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event. This results in no traffic being sent.
bugs.conditions: -- A 'pool'/'virtual' command is used under CLIENT_ACCEPTED event. -- An HTTP/2 profile applied to virtual server. -- The HTTP/2 protocol in use. -- HTTP/2 Message Routing is disabled.
bugs.impact: With HTTP/2 configured, the iRule 'pool'/'virtual' commands fail to execute within the CLIENT_ACCEPTED event, causing no traffic to be sent to the desired pool/virtual.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you may use HTTP_REQUEST event instead of CLIENT_ACCEPTED in iRule syntax.

bugs.title: Tcl command 'string first' not working if payload contains Unicode characters.
bugs.symptoms: Tcl command 'string first' returns an incorrect value when Unicode characters are present in the payload.
bugs.conditions: -- Tcl command 'string first' is used in iRules. -- Payload contains Unicode characters.
bugs.impact: Traffic processing with iRules that contains the 'string first' command might not work as expected.
bugs.workaround: You can use any of the following workarounds: -- Use iRuleLX. -- Do not use Unicode characters in the payload. -- Use a custom Tcl proc to iterate through the string using lindex

bugs.title: Certain LTM policies may not execute correctly after a system reboot or TMM restart.
bugs.symptoms: After a system reboot or TMM restart, LTM policies referencing an external data-group may not execute correctly, regardless of a successful matching condition. This can cause a wide range of issues, including misrouted traffic, unshaped traffic, the bypassing of ASM, or complete traffic failure (based on the policy actions). Note that if a virtual server references multiple LTM policies, and only some of those policies reference an external data-group, all LTM policies attached to the virtual server will be affected.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM policy with an external data-group configured on a virtual server. -- System reboot or TMM restart.
bugs.impact: LTM policies may be unable to execute the appropriate action on a successful matching condition, leading to a wide range of traffic-impacting consequences.
bugs.workaround: Remove and re-add the affected policy to the desired virtual-server. Alternatively, to fix a wider number of affected virtual servers in one go, reload the system configuration by executing 'tmsh load sys config'.
bugs.fix: TMM now loads LTM policies with external data-groups as expected.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing DNS traffic on certain platforms
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, hardware systems with a High-Speed Bridge (HSB) may crash while processing DNS traffic.
bugs.conditions: -DNS profile enabled -Hardware system (or vCMP guests) with a High-Speed Bridge (HSB)
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes DNS traffic as expected.

bugs.title: TMM may consume excessive resources while processing packet filters
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may consume excessive resources while processing packet filters.
bugs.conditions: - Packet filters in use
bugs.impact: Excessive resource consumption, potentially leading to memory exhaustion and reduced performance or a failover event.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes packet filters as expected.

bugs.title: Virtual server does not create the listener
bugs.symptoms: A virtual-address is in an offline state.
bugs.conditions: An address-list is used on a virtual server in a non-default route domain.
bugs.impact: The virtual IP address remains in an offline state.
bugs.workaround: Using tmsh, create the traffic-matching-criteria. Specify the route domain, and attach it to the virtual server.

bugs.title: UCS load with 'reset-trust' may not work properly if base configuration fails to load
bugs.symptoms: When loading a UCS archive using the 'reset-trust' option, if the system fails to load the base configuration from the UCS archive, the system may fail to regenerate new device trust certificates and keys. This can result in subsequent issues, including configuration load failures after an upgrade, such as: 01070712:3: Values (/Common/dtca.key) specified for trust domain (/Common/Root): foreign key index (key_fk) do not point at an item that exists in the database. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Loading a UCS file using the 'reset-trust' option. -- The system fails to load the base configuration (bigip_base.conf) in the UCS archive for any reason. -- The base configuration is corrected, and subsequently loaded (e.g., with 'tmsh load sys config').
bugs.impact: -- The system does not regenerate critical device trust keys and certificates. -- After a subsequent upgrade, the BIG-IP system goes to INOPERATIVE state, and reports this error: 01070712:3: Values (/Common/dtca.key) specified for trust domain (/Common/Root): foreign key index (key_fk) do not point at an item that exists in the database. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.workaround: Remove trust-domain from the bigip_base.conf file and reload the configuration. ★ This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Technical Support website: http://www.f5.com/support/ The MyF5 website: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/ The F5 DevCentral website: http://community.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Wed Oct 15 21:31:24 2025 PDT ©2025 F5, Inc. bugs.title: Csyncd can consume excessive CPU time
bugs.symptoms: Following a configuration change or software upgrade, the "csyncd" process becomes always busy, consuming excessive CPU.
bugs.conditions: -- can occur on any BIG-IP -- may occur with or without vCMP -- may occur after configuring F5 Telemetry Streaming, but may also occur in other circumstances -- large numbers of files are contained in one or more of the directories being monitored
bugs.impact: The overuse of CPU resources by "csyncd" may starve other control-plane processes. Handling of payload network traffic by the data plane is not directly affected.
bugs.workaround: The csyncd process monitors directories mainly to see if there are files that need to be synchronised with another blade of that instance. So generally on non multi-blade devices that use isn't required. Another reason for it to monitor directories is to be able to trigger a process when some criterion is met. For instance it monitors the directory /shared/images for new image files, and if one is seen it will run the processes that maintains the software database. This will be needed on all BIG-IP. To mitigate the processing load, identify which directory or directories contain excessive numbers of files being monitored by "csyncd". If this monitoring is not absolutely needed (see below), such a directory can be removed from the set of directories being monitored. For example: if there are too many files being generated in the "/run/pamcache" directory (same as "/var/run/pamcache"), remove this directory from the set being acted upon by "csyncd" by running the following commands to comment-out the associated lines in the configuration file. [Note it is better to follow the more complete workaround from ID 1103369, https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1103369.html ] # clsh "cp /etc/csyncd.conf /etc/csyncd.conf.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)" # clsh "sed -i '/run＼/pamcache/,+2s/^/#/' /etc/csyncd.conf" # clsh "bigstart restart csyncd" If the problem was observed soon after the installation of F5 Telemetry Streaming, the configuration can be adjusted to make csyncd ignore the related files in a subdirectory of "/var/config/rest/iapps". Run the following commands: # clsh "cp /etc/csyncd.conf /etc/csyncd.conf.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)" # clsh "sed -i '/＼/var＼/config＼/rest＼/iapps/a ＼ ＼ ＼ ＼ ＼ ＼ ＼ ＼ ignore f5-telemetry' /etc/csyncd.conf" # clsh "bigstart restart csyncd" ---- The impact of disabling replication for the pamcache folder is that in the event of a primary blade failover, the new primary blade would not be aware of the existing valid auth tokens, so the user (eg, a GUI user, or a REST script already in progress at the time of the failover) would need to authenticate again. The impact of disabling replication for a folder under the /var/config/rest/iapps is that in the event of a primary blade failover, the new primary blade would not be aware of the iApps LX package, so the user would need to install the iApps LX package on the new primary blade. ★ This issue may cause the configuration to fail to load or may significantly impact system performance after upgrade *********************** NOTICE *********************** For additional support resources and technical documentation, see: The F5 Technical Support website: http://www.f5.com/support/ The MyF5 website: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/ The F5 DevCentral website: http://community.f5.com/ ****************************************************** Generated: Fri Oct 23 04:06:22 2026 PDT ©2026 F5, Inc. bugs.symptoms: No warnings are given when the maximum prefix limit is exceeded.
bugs.conditions: BGP neighbor has a maximum-prefix warning configured
bugs.impact: If the limit is exceeded, no warnings are given. This can cause unexpected behavior.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenants on VELOS cannot install EHFs
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP tenants created on VELOS using v14.1.4 software earlier than v14.1.4.3 cannot accept engineering hotfixes (EHF).
bugs.conditions: Installing EHF updates to BIG-IP tenants on VELOS running BIG-IP v14.1.4 software earlier than v14.1.4.3.
bugs.impact: EHF installation fails.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP tenants on VELOS can now install EHFs.

bugs.title: Traffic Learning: Accept actions for multiple suggestions not localized
bugs.symptoms: When you open the accept suggestions actions list, the actions are not localized. Labels are shown instead of text, for example asm.button.Accept instead of Accept.
bugs.conditions: This occurs after selecting several suggestions and opening the Accept suggestions actions list.
bugs.impact: Actions not localized.
bugs.fix: Fixed localization for Accept suggestions actions list.

bugs.title: SSL forward proxy virtual server may set empty SSL session_id in server hello.
bugs.symptoms: End user clients are unable to establish a TLS connection. Further investigation indicates that the Session ID length field is set to 0, but there is no session ID. TLSv1.2 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Server Hello Content Type: Handshake (22) Version: TLS 1.2 (0x0303) Length: 59 Handshake Protocol: Server Hello Handshake Type: Server Hello (2) Length: 55 Version: Version: TLS 1.2 (0x0303) Random: aa957f92a5de4cedcf9750b60b3efab6b345da6c32189e93… Session ID Length: 0 <=== !!! ..... TLSv1.2 Record Layer: Change Cipher Spec Protocol: Change Cipher Spec ..... TLSv1.2 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Encrypted Handshake Message .....
bugs.conditions: -- SSL forward proxy virtual server. -- This can occur intermittently with normal HTTPS traffic. It occurs more frequently if the session cache's cache-timeout value is set to a low value.
bugs.impact: After receiving the invalid server hello message from the BIG-IP system, the client may generate unexpected_message (10) TLS alerts and the client may terminate SSL connection.

bugs.title: Performance degradation on KVM and VMware platforms.
bugs.symptoms: CPU utilization is increased.
bugs.conditions: -- KVM or VMware platforms are deployed. -- FastHTTP or L7 HTTP virtual servers are configured.
bugs.impact: A 3-13% increase in CPU utilization which may degrade throughput with higher volumes of traffic.

bugs.title: Secure iAppsLX Restricted Storage issues.
bugs.symptoms: iAppLX restricted storage needs hardening.
bugs.conditions: iAppLX applications (such as SSL Orchestrator) that contain configuration objects that use restricted parameters like password or passphrase.
bugs.impact: Stronger encryption needed for sensitive data.
bugs.fix: The iAppLX master key is now stored in mcpd's secure vault as a new secure config object name "iapp_restricted_key".

bugs.title: TMM might crash when pool routes with recursive nexthops and reselect option are used.
bugs.symptoms: When re-selecting to the non-directly-connected pool route member for which the route was withdrawn, TMM might experience a crash.
bugs.conditions: - Pool routes with non-directly-connected or recursive nexthops (pool members). - Reselect option enabled. - Pool members go down/up so that the re-select is triggered.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use non-directly-connected/recursive nexthops (pool members) in pool routes.

bugs.title: Saving UCS files can fail if /var runs out of space
bugs.symptoms: When saving a UCS, /var can fill up leading to UCS failure and the following log message: err diskmonitor[1441]: 011d0004:3: Disk partition /var has only 0% free
bugs.conditions: -- iApps LX installed. -- Multiple iApps LX applications. -- A /var partition of 1.5 GB.
bugs.impact: UCS archives can not be created.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following Workarounds: -- Manually remove the /var/config/rest/node/tmp/BUILD and /var/config/rest/node/tmp/BUILDROOT directories. -- Increase the size of /var/. For information, see K14952: Extending disk space on BIG-IP VE :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K14952

bugs.title: If there is an additional CSRT token, it triggers a No Max Parameter Protocol Compliance violation .
bugs.symptoms: No Max Parameter Protocol Compliance violation is triggered when the CSRF is enabled.
bugs.conditions: CSRF and Max Parameter Protocol Compliance violations are enabled.
bugs.impact: False-negative
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now checks to see if CSRF is enabled, and performs the necessary update on the internal data structure so that the enforcer can detect a Max Parameter Protocol Compliance violation.

bugs.title: In the violation details for Max Parameter Protocol Compliance, the incorrect number of parameters is shown.
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect number of parameter is shown in the violation details for Max Parameter Protocol Compliance.
bugs.conditions: Alarm or block flag is enabled on Max Parameter Protocol Compliance violation, and the request contains more than the maximum specified.
bugs.impact: Request event displays inaccurate number of parameters: the maximum number, plus 1 (e.g., if you specify 7, the maximum shown will be 8). This occurs because the system stops parsing parameters when the violation is triggered, which occurs when receiving a request with more than the value specified in Max Parameter Protocol. So if you enable the alarm or block flag on requests with 5 parameters, a request with more than 5 parameters will be alarmed/blocked, and the number reported will be 6. If the system receives requests with more than 6 parameters, the number of parameters is still reported as 6.

bugs.title: NIST SP800-90B compliance
bugs.symptoms: Common Criteria and FIPS 140-2 certifications require compliance with NIST SP800-90B; this completes that compliance.
bugs.conditions: This applies to systems requiring Common Criteria and/or FIPS 140-2 compliance.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP systems running without this fix on a release targeted for certification (BIG-IP 14.1.4.2 or BIG-IP 15.1.2.1) will not be running a Common Criteria and/or FIPS 140-2 certified configuration.
bugs.fix: Apply this fix to ensure that the system is compliant with NIST SP800-90B.

bugs.title: Accessing attribute using attributeNode value does not work with Portal Access

There is no generic iRule for this issue, but here is a sample iRule: XXXX is the file which usage attributeNode. when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "XXXX" } { # log "URI=([HTTP::path])" # Found the file to modify REWRITE::post_process 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { set strt [string first {<script>try} [REWRITE::payload]] if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt 0 { <script> (function (){ var old_F5_Inflate_value = F5_Inflate_value; F5_Inflate_value = function (o,sw,incr,v) { if (o && o.ownerDocument) { if (o.name == 'action') { if (o.ownerElement) { F5_Inflate_action(o.ownerElement,incr,v); } } } return old_F5_Inflate_value.apply(this,arguments) } })(); </script> } } }

bugs.title: Update angular, jquery, moment, axios, and lodash libraries in AGC

bugs.title: During config sync operation, MCPD restarts on secondary blade logging 01020012:3: A unsigned four-byte integer message item is invalid.
bugs.symptoms: While receiving a config sync operation, mcpd on a secondary blade may restart, logging: err mcpd[6383]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020012:3: A unsigned four-byte integer message item is invalid.... failed validation with error 16908306
bugs.conditions: -- A VIPRION system (or cluster-based vCMP guest) with more than one blade processes a full configuration load, i.e. as a result of running "tmsh load sys config" or receiving a full-load config sync from peer BIG-IP. -- The system generates a large number of warning messages during a configuration load, whose total length is larger than 65,535 bytes. bugs.conditions: -- Client sends a corrupted URI (for example a URI containing a space).
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system treats the URI as an HTTP/0.9 request (as per RFC) and forwards only the first request line. In previous releases, the BIG-IP system treated the URI as a HTTP/1.1 request.

bugs.fix: Added db variable tmm.http.rfc.allowinsecureverfallback to allow insecure fallback to HTTP/1.1. Default is 'disable'.

bugs.title: Requests are missing on traffic event logging
bugs.symptoms: Some traffic requests are missing in Security :: Event Logs.
bugs.conditions: -- Local logging enabled -- Two or more virtual servers passing heavy traffic
bugs.impact: High CPU load prevents the Policy Builder from analyzing and sending all traffic requests to the request log.
bugs.fix: The Policy Builder now attempts to send traffic requests to the request log, even when learning analysis is limited due to high CPU load.

bugs.title: TMM crashes when changing traffic-group on IPv6 link-local address
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes when changing the traffic-group on an IPv6 link-local address.
bugs.conditions: Changing the traffic-group on an IPv6 link-local address.
