bugs.conditions: 1) Active and Standby are on different versions during upgrade 2) Session mirroring enabled
bugs.impact: Continuous TMM crash on standby.
bugs.workaround: Disable session mirroring during the upgrade process. This can be done by disabling sys db statemirror.mirrorsessions.

bugs.title: When two policies with the same properties are configured with geo property, the geo for the second policy is ignored.
bugs.symptoms: If two policies are configured with rule lists of same type of properties (1 allow and 1 deny) with the geo property used, the geo settings of the first rule will be used in the second rule.
bugs.conditions: -- Two policies having the same type of rule lists (1 allow rule and 1 deny rule) -- The same geo is configured in a rule in each of the rule lists. -- One rule is configured to allow, one is configured to deny
bugs.impact: Connection requests for the second virtual server that uses the second policy will use the geo settings from the first policy.
bugs.fix: Connection request for second virtual server will be dropped and allowed as configured in the policy that is attached.

bugs.title: URI rewriting is incorrect for "data:" and "javascript:"
bugs.symptoms: In case of LTM rewrite, HTML content having attribute values like "javascript:", "mailto:", "data:" etc are incorrectly rewritten as URI. This can cause web applications to fail.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM rewrite profile in URI translation mode. -- HTML contents of web application contains attribute values like "javascript:abc", "data:" etc.
bugs.impact: Incorrect URI rewriting may cause web application to fail.

bugs.title: RFC Enforcement Hardening
bugs.symptoms: When the HTTP profile RFC Enforcement Flag is enabled, certain non-RFC compliant headers are still allowed.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual Server with HTTP profile. - RFC Enforcement Flag enabled. - HTTP request with non-RFC compliant headers.
bugs.impact: Non-RFC compliant headers passed to server.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP will drop non-RFC compliant HTTP requests when the RFC compliance flag is ON.

bugs.title: After certain configuration tasks are performed, TMM may run with stale Self IP parameters.
bugs.symptoms: A Self IP instantiated by performing specific configuration tasks (see Conditions) does not work (e.g. the system does not respond to ARP requests for it). On the contrary, the system continues to use (e.g. respond to ARP requests for) an old version of the Self IP specifying a different address.
bugs.conditions: This issue is known to occur when one of the following operations is performed: - Restoring a UCS or SCF archive in which a Self IP with a specific name specifies a different address. - Performing a config-sync between redundant units in which the sender changes a Self IP with a specific name to use a different address. For example: tmsh delete net self <name> tmsh create net self <name> address <new_address> ... tmsh run cm config-sync to_group ... - Performing specific tmsh CLI transactions involving Self IP modifications.
bugs.impact: The system does not utilise the configured Self IP address. Traffic will be impacted as a result (for example, in connections to the unit, in snat automap, etc.).
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM (bigstart restart tmm) on affected units.
bugs.fix: TMM now correctly handles supported Self IP address modifications.

bugs.title: Built-in Integrated Bot Defense iApp template "f5.ibd"
bugs.symptoms: There is no built-in Integrated Bot Defense iApp template on BIG-IP for configuring SED application.
bugs.conditions: Any BIG-IP version installed.
bugs.impact: You are required to download and install the Integrated Bot Defense iApp template from F5 Cloud Services and import it into the BIG-IP system.
bugs.fix: The Integrated Bot Defense iApp template is now a part of the F5 verified and certified iApp templates built-in into the BIG-IP.

bugs.title: Special JSON characters in Dom Signatures breaks configuration
bugs.symptoms: FPS modules malfunction.
bugs.conditions: Unescaped special JSON characters used in Dom Signatures.
bugs.impact: FPS client-side JS unable to load configuration JSON.
bugs.workaround: Manually escape all special JSON characters in Dom Signatures.

bugs.title: Incorrect expression in STREAM::expression might cause a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Tmm restarts and generates a core file
bugs.conditions: An iRule uses STREAM::expression that contains certain strings or is malformed. Stream expressions use a string representing a series of search/replace or search components. If there is more than one search-only component, this might cause tmm to crash. The delimiter character used is the first character of each component search/replace pair. This example uses the '@' character as the delimiter, but it is malformed. Given STREAM::expression "@dog@dot@cat@car@uvw@xyz@" This would be interpreted as three items: search for "dog" replace with "dot" search for "at@" search for "r@uvw@xyz@" This string should likely be: STREAM::expression "@dog@dot@@cat@car@@uvw@xyz@" Which would be interpreted as search for "dog" replace with "dot" search for "cat" replace with "car" search for "uvw" replace with "xyz"
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure that strings in STREAM::expression iRule statements do not have more than one search-only component and are well formed.

bugs.title: iprep.protocol with auto-detect fails when DNS takes time to resolve
bugs.symptoms: On some hardware platforms, after a reboot, DNS takes a significant amount of time to come up.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered on either a fresh installation, or upon a reboot of a BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: DNS takes time to come up (after a reboot) and till then DNS resolution fails. During this, iprepd with auto-detect fails
bugs.fix: Fixed connectivity issues in case of auto-detect protocol mode.

bugs.title: TMM may crash while processing LSN traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, TMM may crash while processing LSN traffic
bugs.conditions: - LSN listener enabled - Packet filtering enabled
bugs.impact: TMM crash leading to a failover event
bugs.fix: TMM now processes LSN traffic as expected

bugs.title: BIG-IP iRule commands FLOW::this or FLOW::peer can create zombie flows.
bugs.symptoms: Keeping a variable reference to FLOW::this or FLOW::peer in iRules can result in zombie connection flows that are never removed. TMM memory use for 'connflow' and 'tclrule_pcb' are high, and do not match the number of current connections reported by the system.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule that uses FLOW::this or FLOW::peer, and stores the result of one of those commands into a variable.
bugs.impact: Increased memory use in TMM, which can eventually result in a TMM crash or traffic disruption while connections are removed using the connection sweeper.
bugs.workaround: Do not retain the result of 'FLOW::this' or 'FLOW::peer' in a variable in an iRule. Instead, either: 1. Use the variable directly, i.e.: log local0.warning: "The flow is [FLOW::this]" 2. Unset the variable when done, i.e.: set flow [FLOW::this] log local0.warning: "The flow is $flow" unset flow If a system is already affected by this issue, the only way to free that memory is to restart TMM.

bugs.title: SSL Connection mirroring - session resumption does not occur on standby when the session ticket is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Eight-second delays occur on traffic through an SSL connection mirroring virtual server, and errors occur on the standby device: crit tmm7[11598]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec Couldn't create an OpenSSL EC group object OpenSSL error:0906D06C:PEM err tmm7[11598]: 01010282:3: Crypto codec error: sw_crypto-7 Couldn't initialize the elliptic curve parameters. crit tmm7[11598]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec No codec available to initialize request context.
bugs.conditions: All of these conditions: -- SSL connection mirroring enabled -- Session tickets are enabled -- High availability (HA) environment and one of the following: -- Running BIG-IP v14.1.4.1 or above (in the v14.1.x branch) or -- Engineering hotfix applied to v14.x/v15.x that has the ID760406 fix (see https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID760406.html)
bugs.impact: SSL traffic is significantly delayed and errors are thrown on the standby device.
bugs.workaround: Any one of the following could prevent the problem. -- client-ssl profile cache-size 0. -- client-ssl profile session-ticket disabled (default). -- disable SSL connection mirror on virtual server.

bugs.title: Invalid send strings for in-TMM HTTP monitors cause monitor probes to not be sent, and nothing is logged to indicate why
bugs.symptoms: If an in-tmm HTTP (or HTTPS) monitor has an invalid send string, the monitor probes will not be sent and nothing is logged to indicate why the probes are not sent.
bugs.conditions: -- In-TMM monitoring is being used. -- HTTP (or HTTPS) monitor with an invalid send string.
bugs.impact: Monitor probes are not sent, and nothing is logged.
bugs.workaround: Correct the monitor's send string.

bugs.title: SASP monitor does not identify specific cause of failed SASP Registration attempt
bugs.symptoms: On affected BIG-IP versions, upon startup, the SASP monitor sends a single Registration Request to the SASP GWM (Group Workload Manager) to initiate monitoring of configured LTM pool members. This Registration Request contains all configured LTM pools (SASP Groups) and members (SASP Group Members). If an error is encountered by the SASP GWM with one of the SASP Groups in the request, the registration of all groups fails. However, the GWM does not provide any indication of *which* Group or member does not match the GWM configuration, hindering troubleshooting efforts. The current BIG-IP behavior does not allow identification of the specific pool/member or monitor that is misconfigured and thus responsible for the failed SASP Registration attempt.
bugs.conditions: This behavior occurs on affected BIG-IP versions when the LTM SASP monitor is configured to monitor members of multiple LTM pools, and when BIG-IP start/restarts/reboots or the configuration is loaded.
bugs.impact: If a single Registration Request fails, the GWM terminates the connection with the Load Balancer (BIG-IP SASP monitor). This behavior is defined by the SASP protocol and SASP GWM implementation. As a result, the SASP monitor will mark all pool members DOWN that are monitored by the SASP monitor, halting traffic from flowing to all pools monitored by the SASP monitor. When an error occurs during registration of the LTM pools (SASP Groups), the GWM does not provide any indication of *which* Group or member does not match the GWM configuration. Since a single error message is returned by the SASP GWM for the entire Registration Request (for all SASP Groups), the SASP monitor cannot indicate which Group (pool/member) or monitor caused the error. This hinders efforts to troubleshoot the cause of the failure, while all traffic has stopped flowing to the SASP-monitored pools.
bugs.workaround: To diagnose this issue, first enable saspd debug logging: tmsh mod sys db saspd.loglevel value debug_msg (Optional alternative values include deep_debug and debug, but provide less detail.) With saspd debug logging enabled, a message like the following in /var/log/monitors/saspd.log confirms that an error occurred during the Registration step: SASPProcessor::processRegistrationReply: received error registering workloads with GWM ##.##.##.###:3860: 69 'InvalidGroup' If the above message is found to confirm this issue, the primary path to resolution should be for the BIG-IP administrator to very carefully compare the BIG-IP pool/member and sasp monitor configuration with the SASP GWM configuration, to identify any mismatches or inconsistencies between the configurations. On the BIG-IP system, to help isolate the misconfigured LTM pool(s)/member(s) causing the SASP Registration failure: 1. Remove the sasp monitor from configured LTM pools/members one at a time, and observe whether any pool members still monitored by the sasp monitor are marked UP. 2. Add the sasp monitor back to configured LTM pools/members one at a time, in the same order as removed, except for the last LTM pool/member from which it was removed. 3. Save and reload the configuration, and check whether the LTM pools/members monitored by the sasp monitor are still marked UP. 4. Repeat as necessary if there appear to be multiple LTM pools/members causing a SASP Registration failure. Alternately, it may be possible to choose a different monitor (using a more fault-tolerant protocol) to monitor the status of affected pool members.

bugs.title: [SSL Orchestrator] Policy fails to complete when URL branching is configured
bugs.symptoms: SessionDB returns ERR_NOT_FOUND when Allow Agent attempts to update URL info in the session entry.
bugs.conditions: SSL Orchestrator session does not have a session entry in the SessionDB corresponding to the URL info.
bugs.impact: This causes policy execution failure and connection aborts.
bugs.workaround: Setting perflow.branching.url with no value, then the Allow Agent will not update the session entry. This will avoid the ERR_NOT_FOUND error message.
bugs.fix: Ensure the session is an APM session before setting the URL info for the session entry.

bugs.title: User-defined bot sigs that are created in tmsh don't overlap staged factory bot sigs
bugs.symptoms: User-defined bot signatures that are created in tmsh are not enforced if there are similar factory bot signatures even when they are staged.
bugs.conditions: User-defined bot signature is created in tmsh and is matched also by staged factory bot signature.
bugs.impact: User-defined signature is not enforced correctly
bugs.workaround: Define user-defined bot signature using the GUI and if signature domain are needed but can't be configured by the GUI, define the domain in tmsh after the signature is created with: tmsh mod security bot-defense signature <sig_name> domains replace-all-with { domains }

bugs.title: Asmlogd suddenly deletes all request log protobuf files and records from the database.
bugs.symptoms: Asmlogd suddenly deletes all request log protobuf files and records from the database. Additionally, after the deletion happens, newly generated event logs seen in database do not show up in TMUI.
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned -- Config-sync setup, with frequent sync recovery and/or with a manual-sync device-group with ASM sync enabled.
bugs.impact: Sudden loss of request logs.
bugs.workaround: Delete all empty partitions and restart asmlogd. 1) View all the partitions: # perl -MF5::Db::Partition -MData::Dumper -MF5::DbUtils -e 'print Dumper(F5::Db::Partition::retrieve_partitions_info(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), table_name => "PRX.REQUEST_LOG"))' Take note of the 'PARTITION_NAME' and 'TABLE_ROWS' for each partition. 2) For every partition_X (in PARTITION_NAME) with '0' in TABLE_ROWS, delete it by: # perl -MF5::Db::Partition -MF5::DbUtils -e 'F5::Db::Partition::delete_partition(dbh => F5::DbUtils::get_dbh(), table_name => "PRX.REQUEST_LOG", partition_name => "partition_X")' 3) restart asmlogd if and after done all deletes: # pkill -f asmlogd NOTE: this workaround is temporary. Meaning, that the number of empty partitions will again accumulate and the same issue will happen again. The MAX number of partitions is - 100. Thus, it is advised to monitor the total number of *empty* partitions and repeat the workaround periodically. A cron script should work well. Normally, empty partitions should NOT accumulate. Thus, it is safe to run this script once an hour and remove all empty partitions. Optionally, if you are having TMUI issue with newly generated event logs, perform the additional command below to delete rows from PRX.REQUEST_LOG_PROPERTIES for which no corresponding rows exist in PRX.REQUEST_LOG. # mysql -t -u root -p$(perl -MPassCrypt -nle 'print PassCrypt::decrypt_password($_)' /var/db/mysqlpw) -e 'delete from PRX.REQUEST_LOG_PROPERTIES where request_log_id > (select id from PRX.REQUEST_LOG order by id desc limit 1)'
bugs.fix: Upgrading to a fixed software version will not delete accumulated partitions and will not clear the symptom away. The fix will prevent ASM from accumulating partitions unnecessarily in the scenarios. If your ASM system is experiencing this and partitions are accumulated, perform the workaround to clear the symptom. Using a fixed software version, you only need to perform the workaround once. You no longer have to perform it periodically.

bugs.title: APM uses wrong session key when iRule for ActiveSync is used resulting in passwords corruption
bugs.symptoms: A corrupted password is sent as part of the "Authorization" header to the backend device and as a result, http 404 is returned
bugs.conditions: -- iRule for ActiveSync is used -- The BIG-IP system has multiple tmms running
bugs.impact: User Authentication is failed by the backed server

bugs.title: Configuraton update triggers from MCP to ASM are ignored
bugs.symptoms: If a stale/incorrect but running PID is present in /var/ts/var/install/ucs_install.pid, then ASMConfig will think it is in the middle of a UCS or Sync load event and ignore updates from MCP.
bugs.conditions: A UCS load event such as an upgrade or a config sync is interrupted and ASM is not restarted until another process reuses the process id from the upgrade.
bugs.impact: Updates from MCP are ignored which can cause: * Missed sync events * Missed updates for logging or pool configuration * Missing security policies
bugs.workaround: Delete /var/ts/var/install/ucs_install.pid

bugs.title: SASP Monitor does not log significant error conditions at default logging level
bugs.symptoms: Most error conditions encountered by the SASP monitor are not logged at the default logging level ("error"). Most of the meaningful error conditions, including Exceptions, are logged at "info" or "debug" levels. Obtaining details to diagnose the SASP monitor issues requires reconfiguring sys db saspd.loglevel for a value of "info" or "debug".
bugs.conditions: -- Using the SASP monitor to monitor LTM pool members -- Leaving the saspd.loglevel system DB variable configured at the default value of "error"
bugs.impact: Errors which occur intermittently or once while monitoring LTM pool members using the SASP monitor may not be diagnosable.
bugs.workaround: Configure the saspd.loglevel system DB variable with a value of "info" (for normal operations) or "debug" (if problems are occurring repeatedly).

bugs.title: Config sync fails with error Invalid monitor rule instance identifier
bugs.symptoms: If you remove or attach a different monitor to an fqdn pool, then perform a full config-sync, an error occurs: Load failed from /Common/bigip1 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), Invalid monitor rule instance identifier: 58.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP device is configured with fqdn nodes/pools with monitors. -- Modify an fqdn pool to remove or attach a different monitor. -- Run the command: run cm config-sync to-group Failover -- Perform a full config-sync.
bugs.impact: Sync to the peer device(s) fails.
bugs.workaround: Use incremental-sync.

bugs.title: Using TMC might cause virtual server vlans-enabled configuration to be ignored
bugs.symptoms: When switching between traffic-matching-criteria (TMC) and regular virtual-server configuration, the vlans-enabled option might be ignored, causing unexpected traffic handling.
bugs.conditions: Changing virtual-server configuration when using traffic-matching-criteria.
bugs.impact: Unexpected traffic handling and disruption
bugs.workaround: Avoid using TMC (port lists and address lists). When in a 'faulty' state you can try changing vlan-enabled on and changing it back on the virtual server, you might need to clear existing connections afterwards. Follow below articles. K53851362: Displaying and deleting BIG-IP connection table entries from the command line K52091701: Handling Connections that have been matched to the wrong Virtual Server.

bugs.title: ASM Plugin Abort reset for chunked response without proper terminating 0 chunk followed by FIN
bugs.symptoms: ASM BD sends a reset back to the client when the backend server sends a response without proper terminating 0 chunk followed by FIN.
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - ASM policy attached to a virtual server - Backed server sends a bad chunked response
bugs.impact: Valid requests can be reset.
bugs.workaround: Any one of the following workarounds can be applied. -- Fix backed server behavior. -- Fix bad response using iRule, appending proper terminating 0 chunk -- Change ASM internal /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal update bypass_upon_load 1
bugs.fix: Fix ASM to properly handle bad chunked response followed by FIN

bugs.title: False positive HTTP compliance violation
bugs.symptoms: False positive HTTP compliance violation.
bugs.conditions: Authorization header with bearer token and/or some other authorization headers types.
bugs.impact: False positive traffic blocking.
bugs.workaround: Turn on an internal parameter by entering the following command from the BIG-IP CLI: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ignore_authorization_header_decode_failure 1
bugs.fix: The RFC compliance violation is no longer issued for unknown types of authorization headers.

bugs.title: WebSocket does not close cleanly when SSL enabled.
bugs.symptoms: After sending a close frame to the WebSocket server, the WebSocket client receives 1006 response.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with the following profiles: -- WebSocket -- HTTP over SSL (at least server side SSL) and connection closure is initiated by the client.
bugs.impact: Client side applications experience errors in the form of WebSocket abnormally closing connections with error code 1006.
bugs.workaround: Avoid using SSL on WebSocket server context.
bugs.fix: WebSocket connections close without any error.

bugs.title: Internal listeners (cgc, ftp data, etc) all share the same listener_key stats
bugs.symptoms: Internal stats are not accurate because they are shared across multiple listener types
bugs.conditions: This can occur when multiple virtual server types are in use and passing traffic.
bugs.impact: Internal listener stats are not accurate.

bugs.title: Payload manager lacks egress flow control when used through satellite
bugs.symptoms: Payload manager uses HUDEVT_PAUSE_EGRESS which is not supported by most filters and the TCP proxy. This causes payload manager to accept all egress offered regardless of the state of the lower part of the chain, leading to excessive xfrag buffering.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP virtual server with HTTP compression, ntlm, oneconnect - Make a request for a very large compressible document through the VIP which results in a chunked response from server. Simulating a congested client allows the lack of flow control to be much more obvious.
bugs.impact: - The xfrags usage jumps proportionally to the document size requested and slowly declines as the document is transferred. - Document transfer from server occurs without pause.

bugs.title: Restore of UCS leads to incorrect UID on authorized_keys
bugs.symptoms: After restoring a UCS from a different BIG-IP device, the admin user is unable to log in via SSH using SSH public key authentication.
bugs.conditions: -- Create a UCS on one BIG-IP system where a UCS archive has been restored in the past (including by an upgrade) -- Import the UCS to a different BIG-IP system and load it
bugs.impact: You are unable to log in as the admin user via SSH using key-based authentication. NOTE: Password authentication works without any issues.
bugs.workaround: Change the owner of /home/admin/.ssh/authorized_keys to 'root', by running the following command: chown root /home/admin/.ssh/authorized_keys This command can also be run via iControl REST using the /mgmt/tm/util/bash endpoint.

bugs.title: Wildcard server-name does not match multiple labels in FQDN
bugs.symptoms: Wildcard server-name does not match multiple labels in FQDN for example: *.domain.com matches a.domain.com or a.bc.domain.com, but it does not match domain.com but here multiple labels(a.bc.domain.com) are not matched to the wildcard (*.domain.com).
bugs.conditions: Client-ssl is configured with a wildcard server-name with the virtual server configured with multiple client-ssl profiles. The correct ssl profile (and therefore certificate) is chosen based on SNI from the client Hello.
bugs.impact: Generates default profile/certificate when trying to match with multiple labels using wildcard, when it should generate correct certificate matched to the wildcard in server name.
bugs.workaround: Add additional SAN values to the certificate with the relevant second-level domain elements, for example: When serving "site.test.example.com" using a certificate that matches just *.example.com, add a second SAN element to the certificate of *.test.example.com

bugs.title: Self IP address creation fails with 'ioctl failed: No such device'
bugs.symptoms: Creating a self IP address after a route-domain using TMSH reports an error: 01070712:3: Cannot get device index for Backend in rd2 - ioctl failed: No such device.
bugs.conditions: Using tmsh, create a Trunk, create a VLAN on the trunk, create a route-domain, then create a self IP address.
bugs.impact: Self IP address creation fails after route-domain creation. Unable to run declarative-onboarding declaration.
bugs.workaround: Add a short delay after modifying/creating the route domain before creating the self IP address. Note: Self IP address should be created after route-domain creation.

bugs.title: Firewall Manager user role is not allowed to configure/view protocol inspection profiles
bugs.symptoms: A user account with the "firewall-manager" role that is assigned permissions only to custom partitions will not be able to configure protocol inspection profiles.
bugs.conditions: -- A user account is created with the role firewall-manager. -- A custom partition is created. -- The newly created user is given access to the newly created partition.
bugs.impact: Any user account without access to "/Common" partition is not allowed to configure protocol inspection profiles.
bugs.workaround: - If the user account is provided access to "/Common" partition as well, the user should be able to configure protocol-inspection profiles in the newly created custom partitions.
bugs.fix: The permissions are granted for any non-admin user to configure protocol inspection profiles in a custom partition as long as they have access to "/Common" partition as well.

bugs.title: GUI display of DHCPv6 profile not correct for virtual server in non-default route-domain
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server created in a non-default route-domain with a DHCPv6 profile shows as using a DHCPv4 profile 'None' in the GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server using a DHCPv6 profile. -- Virtual server must be in a non-default route-domain. -- Using the GUI to view the virtual server.
bugs.impact: Incorrect view of the configuration.

bugs.title: MRF DIAMETER to select automatic removal of a persistence entry on completion of a transaction
bugs.symptoms: MRF DIAMETER is not DIAMETER-application aware. It does not have application-specific business logic. When creating a DIAMETER solution, BIG-IP operators often need to write iRule scripts that remove a session persistence entry at the end of a transaction.
bugs.conditions: Some applications require removal of the persistence entry upon successful and unsuccessful completion of a transaction. root@(bigip1)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list ltm rule log_dia_error ltm rule log_dia_error { when DIAMETER_INGRESS { set cmd_code [DIAMETER::command] if { $cmd_code == 272 } { set cc_req_type [DIAMETER::avp data get 416 integer32] if {[DIAMETER::is_response] && $cc_req_type == 3 } { log local0. "Persistence record delete-on-any" DIAMETER::persist delete-on-any } } }
bugs.impact: iRule script is required.
bugs.fix: DIAMETER::persist irule are supported to remove a persistence entry based on the result status of a answer message. below irule commands are supported. DIAMETER::persist delete-on-any DIAMETER::persist delete-on-success DIAMETER::persist delete-on-failure DIAMETER::persist delete-none

bugs.title: Loading config file with imish removes the last character
bugs.symptoms: While loading a configuration from the file with IMISH ('imish -f <f_name>'),truncating the last line. printf 'log file /var/log/zebos.log1' >/shared/tmp/new.cfg Running imish -r 0 -f /shared/tmp/new.cfg have the last character missing like below: log file /var/log/zebos.log
bugs.conditions: Loading a config with 'imish -f <f_name>' commands. Note: This command is used with the bigip_imish_config Ansible module.
bugs.impact: Configuration commands cannot be created properly.
bugs.workaround: For CLI, use extra control char at the end or \n.

bugs.title: Response code 304 from TMM Cache always closes TCP connection.
bugs.symptoms: When a virtual server is configured to accelerate HTTP traffic, it caches responses with 200 and 304 response codes. Serving a response with "304 Not Modified" code, TMM may close a connection to a client.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual server has a web-acceleration profile (without a web application for versions prior 16.0.0). -- A response with code 304, stored in TMM cache, is served to a request.
bugs.impact: A client needs to open a new TCP connection every time when a response with "304 Not Modified" code is served.
bugs.fix: TMM correctly serves a response with "304 Not Modified" code, allowing to correctly handle TCP connection status.

bugs.title: SASP monitor does not mark pool member with same IP Address but different Port from another pool member
bugs.symptoms: When the LTM SASP monitor is applied to a pool with multiple members having the same IP Address but different Ports, only one of the pool members with the duplicated IP Address will be monitored (marked UP or DOWN as appropriate). Other pool members sharing the same IP Address will remain in a 'checking' state.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when using the SASP monitor in a pool with multiple members having the same IP Address but different Ports. For example: ltm pool sasp_test_pool { members { sasp_1:80 { address 10.10.10.1 } sasp_1:8080 { address 10.10.10.1 } sasp_2:80 { address 10.10.10.2 } sasp_2:8080 { address 10.10.10.2 } } monitor sasp_test } In this case, only one pool member with a given IP Address will be correctly monitored by the sasp monitor. Any additional pool members with the same IP Address but different port will not be monitored by the SASP monitor and will remain in a 'checking' state.
bugs.impact: Not all pool members may be effectively/accurately monitored by the SASP monitor.
bugs.fix: The ltm sasp monitor correctly monitors members of a pool which share the same IP Address but different Ports.

bugs.title: Modify wideip pools with replace-all-with results pools with same order 0
bugs.symptoms: Multiple wideip pools have the order 0.
bugs.conditions: There are overlap for the pools for command replace-all-with and the pools to be replaced.
bugs.impact: iQuery flapping between GTMs.
bugs.workaround: First delete all pools from the wideip and then use replace-all-with.

bugs.title: Virtual Edition systems replicate host traffic to all TMMs when a multicast MAC address is the traffic's nexthop
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP Virtual Edition receives a host packet that has a multicast MAC address as its nexthop, it will disaggregate this by forwarding it to all TMMs. This results in all TMMs egressing the packet.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition -- A route is configured to a multicast MAC address -- Host traffic (e.g. non-TMM monitors, ping, etc.) is routed to the multicast MAC address
bugs.impact: Extraneous packets are egressed from the BIG-IP.
bugs.workaround: Partial workaround for the case of monitors: use in-TMM monitors where possible. Otherwise, there is no workaround for this.

bugs.title: Changing the sshd port breaks some BIG-IP utilities on a multi-bladed system
bugs.symptoms: After using "sys sshd port" to change the default port for sshd, some utilities may no longer work properly on the BIG-IP, such as: "tmsh reboot slot ..." or qkview or any command using clsh or ssh slot<slot number>
bugs.conditions: -- Chassis system with multiple blades. -- Default sshd port was modified.
bugs.impact: Unable to run commands on secondary blades.
bugs.workaround: -- Reconfigure SSHD to run on the default port, 22. or -- Specify an explicit port when using ssh and log in to each blade to run the desired commands, e.g. "ssh -p 40222 slot2"

bugs.title: Subsession variable values mixing between sessions
bugs.symptoms: Subsession variable lookup internally assumes that a complete session DB lookup name (Session ID + Subsession key) is used. However, when using the lookup table, only the subsession key is passed in.
bugs.conditions: Subsession variables are referenced in the Per-Request Policy outside of the Subsession without the Session ID.
bugs.impact: A Per-Request Policy execution may get the value of the subsession variable from a different APM session.
bugs.workaround: Add the session ID to the reference to the subsession variables used in Per-Request Policies.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with subsession variable lookup.

bugs.title: Improper logging of sensitive DB variables
bugs.symptoms: Certain DB variables related to configsync and management port proxying may be improperly logged.
bugs.conditions: Configuring configsync or a management port proxy.
bugs.impact: Undisclosed DB variables are logged.
bugs.workaround: Follow current guidance for transferring and accessing files from the BIG-IP device. https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K58243048
bugs.fix: The DB variables are treated as expected.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 hardening
bugs.symptoms: Under certain condition, the HTTP/2 profile does not follow current best practices
bugs.conditions: - HTTP/2 profile enabled
bugs.impact: The HTTP/2 profile does not follow current best practices.
bugs.fix: TMM now processes HTTP/2 traffic as expected

bugs.title: Network virtual-addresses fail to retain the "icmp-echo enabled" property following an upgrade or reload of the configuration from file.
bugs.symptoms: Network virtual-addresses default to "arp disabled" and "icmp-echo disabled". However, a BIG-IP Administrator can change these settings to "enabled", if required. Either following a software upgrade or a reload of the configuration from file, network virtual-addresses that had previously been set to "icmp-echo enabled" revert to the default of "icmp-echo disabled".
bugs.conditions: - One or more network virtual-addresses configured with "icmp-echo enabled". - A software upgrade or reload of the configuration from file occurs (for example, taking and restoring a UCS archive, removing the mcpd binary database and reloading the config, etc.).
bugs.impact: Traffic failures can occur as a result of the affected network virtual-addresses not being presented to the surrounding network as originally intended by the BIG-IP Administrator.
bugs.workaround: Manually configure the affected virtual-addresses to "icmp-echo enabled" again. This workaround is not permanent, and the issue will occur again in the future given the right conditions.
bugs.fix: Network virtual-addresses no longer lose the "icmp-echo enabled" property.

bugs.title: Changing syslog remote port requires syslog-ng restart to take effect
bugs.symptoms: Modified remote port in syslog configuration takes effect only after restart of the syslog-ng.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure the remote syslogs and allow some time to pass. -- Change the local IP or remote port in syslog config.
bugs.impact: Change does not occur until you reboot or restart syslog-ng.
bugs.workaround: To cause the change to occur, restart syslog-ng: bigstart restart syslog-ng

bugs.title: REST endpoint /mgmt/tm/ltm/pool does not set ratio-value to default when session value is updated to user-disabled
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP LTM on v13.1.1.5/v14.1.2.8 does not update the ratio-value to default value of 1 for LTM pool members, when the pool member's session value is updated to user-disabled by the REST endpoint /mgmt/ltm/pool.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP LTM version : v13.1.1.5/v14.1.2.8 where the LTM pool member attributes are being updated via REST API.
bugs.impact: LTM pool member attribute ratio-value is not updated to the default value of 1, when session-value set to user-disabled when updated via REST endpoint /mgmt/ltm/pool

bugs.title: Windows installer(VPN through browser components installer) as administrator user uses temporary folder to create files
bugs.symptoms: - A privileged process creates folders with user permission while installation.
bugs.conditions: - Downloading VPN components while connecting to VS for the first time from browser.
bugs.impact: - No functional impact.
bugs.workaround: - Download and install web based VPN components using BIG-IP components installer page.
bugs.fix: - Ensured that folder is created with administrator privileges.

bugs.title: In-TMM HTTPS monitor with SSL Profile set to None does not use serverssl profile.
bugs.symptoms: HTTPS monitors with SSL profile set to None (default) will not use the default ServerSSL profile of "serverssl" when In-TMM monitoring is enabled. Instead, another internal ServerSSL profile is used which has different values from "serverssl".
bugs.conditions: -- In-TMM monitoring is enabled -- HTTPS monitor(s) with SSL profile field is set to the default of "None"
bugs.impact: The TLS settings for the HTTPS monitor monitor probes will not match those of the ServerSSL "serverssl" profile and may cause unexpected behavior such as utilizing TLS 1.3 (disabled by default in the "serverssl" profile) or random session IDs.
bugs.workaround: Specify a ServerSSL profile in every HTTPS monitor when using In-TMM monitoring. Attaching the profile "serverssl" will result in the same behavior that SSL Profile "none" should provide, given that the "serverssl" profile should be the default.

bugs.title: Systemd hangs and is unresponsive
bugs.symptoms: When memory is exhausted on the system and systemd tries to fork to start or stop a service, systemd fails and enters "freeze" mode.
bugs.conditions: Following log messages can be seen in the daemon.log log file: err systemd[1]: Failed to fork: Cannot allocate memory crit systemd[1]: Assertion 'pid >= 1' failed at src/core/unit.c:1997, function unit_watch_pid(). Aborting. emerg systemd[1]: Caught <ABRT>, cannot fork for core dump: Cannot allocate memory emerg systemd[1]: Freezing execution.
bugs.impact: Systemd does not provide service anymore.
bugs.workaround: Reboot the system to restore the systemd services.

bugs.title: Active fails to resend ipsec ikev2_message_id_sync if no response received
bugs.symptoms: In high availability (HA) setup, after failover, the newly active BIG-IP device, will send ikev2_message_id_sync messages to the other device. If the BIG-IP device did not receive a response, it has to retransmit the packet. Some of the IKE tunnels are trying to retransmitting the packet, but its not going out of BIG-IP due to wrong state of relation between IKE tunnel and connection flow. After 5 retries, it marks the peer as down, and the IKE tunnel is deleted.
bugs.conditions: -- High availability (HA) environment -- IKE tunnels configured -- A failover occurs
bugs.impact: Traffic loss.
bugs.fix: Fetch latest connection flow during retransmission of IKE/IPSEC packet.

bugs.title: CMP Forwarded flows do not get syncache counter decremented when only server-side is PVA accelerated
bugs.symptoms: Virtuals with CMP forwarded flows and PVA acceleration may see a higher than expected syncache counter which can lead to permanent syncookie activation. Also, under certain conditions the internal listeners used for config-sync may have syncookies activated. Logs will show the syncookie counter increasing after every activation. bigip1 warning tmm1[18356]: 01010038:4: Syncookie counter 9830 exceeded vip threshold 2496 for virtual = 192.168.1.1:4353 bigip1 warning tmm1[18356]: 01010038:4: Syncookie counter 9834 exceeded vip threshold 2497 for virtual = 192.168.1.1:4353
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual servers with CMP forwarded flows - commonly occurring when the FTP profile is in use. -- A platform with PVA acceleration enabled. -- Only the server-side flow of a connection is offloaded to hardware.
bugs.impact: Elevated syncache_curr, epva_connstat.embryonic_hw_conns, epva_connstat, embryonic_hw_tcp_conns stas. Improper syncooke activation. Syncookie activation on the config-sync listener may cause config-sync to fail.
bugs.workaround: Remove the ftp profile or disable PVA acceleration: modify sys db pva.acceleration value none
bugs.fix: Counters are now correctly decremented.

bugs.title: Core generated for autodosd daemon when synchronization process is terminated
bugs.symptoms: Autodosd cores on SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM DoS vectors configured -- This can occur during normal operation but the specific conditions that trigger it are unknown
bugs.impact: Autodosd is restarted, but up to 15 seconds of history may be lost.
bugs.fix: Fixed an autodosd crash.

bugs.title: Unable to provision PEM on VELOS platform
bugs.symptoms: Unable to provision PEM on VELOS platform
bugs.conditions: When trying to provision PEM
bugs.impact: PEM functionality cannot be achieved
bugs.workaround: Change sys db provision.enforce value to false and load sys config
bugs.fix: Added VELOS platform to PEM provision list

bugs.title: Bdosd does not create /var/bdosd/*.json
bugs.symptoms: JSON files for historical data are not created for each virtual server in /var/bdosd. BDOS for DDoS works on current data in memory but cannot to depend on the historical data for all virtual servers
bugs.conditions: BDOS is configured for any virtual server
bugs.impact: Custom signature or BDDoS-generated signature for the virtual server does not work correctly.

bugs.title: No Error logging when BIG-IP device's IP address is not added in client list on netHSM. &start;
bugs.symptoms: "Ensure BIG-IP's IP address is added to the client list" error log is not displayed, despite the BIG-IP not being added to the client list in Thales/nShield/Entrust HSM.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is not added to the client list in Thales/nShield/Entrust HSM.
bugs.impact: Difficult to debug the error condition to due lack of error message
bugs.fix: Grep error text information on stderror stream now works.

bugs.title: Unknown subscriber in PBA deployment may cause CPU spike
bugs.symptoms: in PBA deployment, a CPU spike may be observed if the subscriber-id log is enabled and the subscriber-id is unknown.
bugs.conditions: -- PBA configuration -- Address translation persistent is enabled -- Subscriber-id log is enabled -- There is an unknown subscriber
bugs.impact: Overall system capacity reduces.
bugs.workaround: Disable subscriber-id logging.
bugs.fix: Unknown subscriber in PBA deployment no longer causes a CPU spike.

bugs.title: SCTP INIT_ACK not forwarded
bugs.symptoms: After SCTP link down/up (not physical IF link down up), SCTP session can't be established.
bugs.conditions: -- CMP forwarding enabled (source-port preserve-strict) -- The BIG-IP system is encountering heavy traffic load -- A connection is deleted from the connection table
bugs.impact: Flow state can become out of sync between TMMs
bugs.workaround: Once the problem occurs, execute "tmsh delete sys connection", and the SCTP session will be re-established.

bugs.title: Modifying mgmt-dhcp options should not be allowed on VCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: Option to modify mgmt-dhcp to dhcpv4 or dhcpv6 is available on VCMP guest.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered with the following tmsh command modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp Values: dhcpv4 dhcpv6 disabled enabled
bugs.impact: VCMP guest can be configured with options that are incompatible with VCMP operation. This might result in a loss of management IP in the guest after a reboot

bugs.title: Wrong representation of JSON/XML validation files in template based (minimal) JSON policy export
bugs.symptoms: When exporting template-based (minimal) JSON policy with profiles and associated validation files, the resulting configuration is wrong. - Configuration for the JSON validation file is missing from the exported policy - The JSON profile associated validation file has the name but no content
bugs.conditions: Export a minimal JSON policy with JSON/XML validation files associated to the JSON/XML profile.
bugs.impact: Error due to wrong configuration of the validation file during import.

bugs.title: Enabling DHCP for management should not be allowed on vCMP guest
bugs.symptoms: Options to enable DHCP for the management interface are available on vCMP guests.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP vCMP guest running on an appliance
bugs.impact: VCMP guest can be configured with options that are incompatible with VCMP operation. This might result in a loss of management IP in the guest after a reboot
bugs.workaround: Do not attempt to DHCP on the management interface of a vCMP guest.

bugs.title: Image2disk does not work on F5OS BIG-IP tenant.
bugs.symptoms: Image2disk fails to recognize the correct disk to install and installation fails.
bugs.conditions: This occurs with BIG-IP tenants that are running in F5OS partitions.
bugs.impact: Installation fails.

bugs.title: Configsync.copyonswitch variable is not functioning on reboot
bugs.symptoms: Configsync.copyonswitch variable is not functioning properly during reboot to another partition
bugs.conditions: -- db variable configsync.copyonswitch modified -- hostname is changed in global-settings -- reboot to another partition
bugs.impact: The hostname will be changed back to the default hostname after reboot

bugs.title: Some signatures are not matched under specific conditions
bugs.symptoms: Some signatures are not matched, attacking traffic may pass through.
bugs.conditions: - Undisclosed signature conditions
bugs.impact: Attacking traffic can bypass the WAF.
bugs.fix: Signatures are now matched as expected.

bugs.title: OOM errors after upgrade and BIG-IP instance unresponsive
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP is unstable or unresponsive and Out of Memory (OOM) errors after the upgrade.
bugs.conditions: - Configuration failures during upgrades - Provisioned with not just LTM
bugs.impact: BIG-IP instance may go unstable or unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: Resolve configuration error and load the configuration where provisioning will setup enough memory to host.

bugs.title: "Can't process event 16, err: ERR_NOT_FOUND" seen in tmm logs
bugs.symptoms: The following message may be logged to /var/log/tmm* Can't process event 16, err: ERR_NOT_FOUND
bugs.conditions: Applying a PEM policy to an existing session that already has that policy (eg, through an irule using 'PEM::subscriber config policy referential set xxxx'
bugs.impact: Since the PEM policy is already applied to the session, the failure message is essentially cosmetic, but it can cause the tmm logs to grow in size if this is happening frequently.

bugs.title: iControl REST 401 error caused by pam-authenticator failure
bugs.symptoms: F5 OpenStack LBaaSv2 driver code can produce many iControl REST API calls against a BIG-IP VE device. Some of those API calls get 401 responses and so, the whole configuration procedure fails.
bugs.conditions: iControl authentication code executes a pam-authenticator command to verify admin password, and the pam-authenticator command often fails, if we run several processes of it at the same time
bugs.impact: iControl API returns 401 error, even if the admin password is correct.

bugs.title: Nested address lists can increase configuration load time
bugs.symptoms: Whenever there are a number of nested address lists configured, the 'load sys config' command takes a long time to complete.
bugs.conditions: -- Several nested Address Lists are configured. -- The 'load sys config' command is run.
bugs.impact: Upgrading (load sys config) takes a lot of time of time to complete, which sometimes causes Packet Correlation Classification Daemon (pccd) to fail. If pccd fails, the system is unable to detect and compile firewall configuration changes, meaning that changes made to the firewall configuration are not enforced. Note: The firewall configuration that was running before pccd goes down continues to be enforced; only changes are not enforced.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with config load time when nested address lists are used.

bugs.title: Equinix SmartKey HSM is not working with nethsm-partition 'fortanix'
bugs.symptoms: Setting up the Equinix SmartKey HSM with nethsm-partition 'fortanix' (or anything other than 'auto') pkcs11d logs an error: err pkcs11d[21535]: 01680040:3: netHSM: Failed to find partition with label 'fortanix' on the netHSM.
bugs.conditions: Configuring a nethsm-partition other than 'auto'.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP does not connect to the HSM and SSL traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Use the nethsm-partition 'auto' tmsh create sys crypto fips nethsm-partition 'auto'

bugs.title: MCP validation should prevent defining multiple virtual servers with the same virtual address but with different subnet masks
bugs.symptoms: Multiple virtual servers with the same virtual address but with different subnet masks are allowed.
bugs.conditions: Creation of multiple virtual servers with the same virtual address but with different subnet masks.
bugs.impact: Latest virtual server instantiation implicitly and silently modifies the subnet mask of the virtual address, making the system not behave as the user thinks or intended.

bugs.title: Subnet mask property of virtual addresses not displayed in management GUI
bugs.symptoms: You cannot determine the subnet mask for a displayed virtual address using only the BIG-IP management GUI.
bugs.conditions: -- A virtual address (automatically created by any virtual server) exists in the configuration. -- Using the management GUI.
bugs.impact: Potential difficulty in troubleshooting and verifying config due to having to use other methods (accessing the CLI) to check a virtual address's netmask.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to determine the subnet mask.

bugs.title: Turboflex page in GUI reports 'profile.Features is undefined' error
bugs.symptoms: The System :: Resource Provisioning : TurboFlex page is unusable, and the BIG-IP GUI reports an error: An error occurred: profile.Features is undefined.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP iSeries appliance -- Upgrade to: --- v15.1.3 or later within v15.1.x --- v16.0.1.2 or later within v16.0.x --- v16.1.0 or later -- Accessing the System :: Resource Provisioning : TurboFlex page in the BIG-IP GUI
bugs.impact: Unable to manage TurboFlex profile via the BIG-IP GUI.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh or iControl REST to manage TurboFlex profile configuration.

bugs.title: Bot Defense does not support iOS's WKWebView framework
bugs.symptoms: When using the Bot Defense Profile, mobile apps which use iOS's WKWebView framework may get blocked from accessing the website.
bugs.conditions: -- Using the Bot Defense Profile -- Mobile apps which use iOS's WKWebView framework try to access the website
bugs.impact: Mobile apps which use iOS's WKWebView framework may get blocked from accessing the website.

bugs.title: Mcpd may run out of memory when build image is missing
bugs.symptoms: After installing a new blade, if the BIG-IP does not have the appropriate images to install all volumes onto the new blade, it can get stuck waiting to install. This may cause mcpd to eventually run out of memory. Running "tmsh show sys software" shows a message similar to this for a prolonged period of time: HD1.2 3 BIG-IP 12.1.3.5 0.0.10 no waiting for product image (BIG-IP 12.1.3)
bugs.conditions: -- Installing a new blade into a chassis-based system. -- Missing BIG-IP image(s) necessary to update all volumes on the new blade.
bugs.impact: Mcpd eventually runs out of memory and cores.
bugs.workaround: Either delete the affected volume if it is no longer necessary, or copy the appropriate BIG-IP image to /shared/images.

bugs.title: DNS msg_ObjType can cause buffer overrun due to lack of NUL terminator
bugs.symptoms: Tmm cores with umem debug enabled.
bugs.conditions: A string operation is performed against DNS resource records (RRs) from DNSMSG::section in an iRule.
bugs.impact: Tmm memory corruption. In some situations, tmm might crash. Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not use string operations against DNS RRs returned from DNSMSG::section.

bugs.title: APM daemon may crash if CRLDP agent cannot find a certificate to validate CRL
bugs.symptoms: APM daemon (apmd) crashes and a coredump is created at '/var/core/'
bugs.conditions: -- Configure On-Demand Cert Auth with any Auth Mode -- 'Request/Require' -- Configure AAA CRLDP
bugs.impact: All CRLDP based authentications fail.
bugs.fix: The system now handles this condition.

bugs.title: Missing IKEv2 listeners can send IKE packets to the IKEv1 racoon daemon
bugs.symptoms: If an IKEv2 tunnel terminates with an error condition, afterward it is possible for IKE packets to be received by the IKEv1 racoon daemon, which is listening to local host (i.e 127.0.0.1) on ports 500 and 4500.
bugs.conditions: To get the problem to occur, you may need these details: -- an IKEv2 config where traffic selector narrowing happens -- termination of an IKEv2 tunnel with an error condition -- some other BIG-IP service using the same local self IP Packets can reach the IKEv1 racoon daemon only when some BIG-IP service uses bigself as the proxy, which forwards packets to localhost (127.0.0.1) with the same port number. So even if no IKEv1 config is present for a local self IP, if some other BIG-IP service also uses bigself as a proxy, this can forward IKE packets to localhost as well.
bugs.impact: The IKEv2 tunnel does not get renegotiated, because IKE packets reach the IKEv1 daemon, which ignores them, because the proper listener to handle IKEv2 is missing. As a result, tunnel service is interrupted.
bugs.workaround: Deleting and re-adding the problematic ike-peer and traffic-selector should bring back IPsec support for that tunnel. If the initiating and responding sides of the tunnel have identical traffic-selector proposals, then narrowing should not happen, and this would also prevent the problem in the first place.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP systems now manage and handle multiple references to the same listener in a more rigorous way, so the IKEv2 listener cannot go away while it is still needed.

bugs.title: Server-side connections stall with zero window with OneConnect profile
bugs.symptoms: Serverside connections from pool member to BIG-IP hang, with the BIG-IP advertising a TCP zero window.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with OneConnect profile -- The BIG-IP applies flow-control to the serverside connection (e.g. the server's response to the BIG-IP is faster than the BIG-IP's forwarding the response to the client) -- The serverside connection is subsequently re-used
bugs.impact: Serverside connections hang in the middle of data transfer, and will eventually time out.
bugs.workaround: If possible, remove the OneConnect profile from the virtual server. Note: removing a OneConnect profile may cause problems with persistence, as described in K7964: The BIG-IP system may appear to ignore persistence information for Keep-Alive connections (https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K7964)

bugs.title: Session memory increases over time due to db_access_set_accessinfo can leak sresult key/data in error case
bugs.symptoms: Session memory is growing over time. memory_usage_stat indicates 'session' is growing.
bugs.conditions: Db_access_set_accessinfo is hitting the error case
bugs.impact: Memory will leak in tmm daemons. This affects all modules that use tmm.
bugs.workaround: Restart the tmms periodically when the memory grows

bugs.title: When HTTP CONNECT is sent, iRule event HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE is not triggered
bugs.symptoms: In an explicit proxy configuration when an HTTP request is sent to an HTTPS destination server via proxy, the HTTP CONNECT method is sent, but the iRule event HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE is not fired.
bugs.conditions: - Simple HTTP explicit proxy virtual server - An HTTP request from the client is sent to an 'https://' destination server
bugs.impact: iRule event HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE does not get triggered.
bugs.fix: When HTTP CONNECT is sent, the iRule event HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE is now triggered.

bugs.title: BIG-IP Sym-unit-key is updated on every config save operation
bugs.symptoms: Sym-unit-key in bigip.conf changes every time the config is saved.
bugs.conditions: The tmsh save sys config command is run
bugs.impact: The unit key is altered every time the config is saved

bugs.title: tmsh show analytics dos-l3 report view-by attack-id" shows "allowed-requests-per-second" instead "attack_type_name
bugs.symptoms: Output of "tmsh show analytics dos-l3 report view-by attack-id" command has changed from version 13.x to 15.x. "Attack type" was removed from the system, so it was automatically replaced by the first metric "allowed-requests-per-second". For DOS L3 "Attack type" was replaced by "Vector Name" but it currently is not shown in the report along wit "Attack ID"
bugs.conditions: AFM is provisioned
bugs.impact: This change might cause scripts to fail if they use the name of the field.
bugs.workaround: 1) edit /etc/avr/monpd/monp_dosl3_entities.cfg file. Change [dosl3_attack_id] section the following way: add 'vector_name' to measures list and add an additional parameter 'default_measure' as specified below : [dosl3_attack_id] ... measures=allowed_requests_per_sec,count,drop_per_sec,drop_count,total_per_sec,total_count,attacks_count,attack_type_name,category_name,vip_name,period,vector_name default_measure=vector_name ... 2) edit /etc/avr/monpd/monp_dosl3_measures.cfg file. Add in the end the following section: [vector_name] id=vector_crc formula=IF(count(distinct FACT.vector_crc)>1,'Aggregated',attack_vector_str) merge_formula=IF(count(distinct vector_name)>1,'Aggregated',vector_name) dim=AVR_DIM_DOS_VIS_ATTACKS_VECTOR dim_id=attack_vector_crc tmsh_display_name=vector-name display_name=Vector comulative=false priority=65 3) restart the BIG-IP system: bigstart restart After the system is up you can apply the same tmsh command: "tmsh show analytics dos-l3 report view-by attack-id" You will get a result similar to 13.x. Note that "attack_type_name" is replaced by "vector-name"
bugs.fix: Workaround applied as fix.

bugs.title: Policy versions cleanup process sometimes removes newer versions
bugs.symptoms: The policy versions cleanup process sometimes removes versions in incorrect order. Newer versions are removed while older versions are preserved.
bugs.conditions: "maxSizeOfSavedVersions" configuration parameter in "/etc/ts/tools/policy_history.cfg" has very low value.
bugs.impact: Newer versions are removed.
bugs.workaround: increase value of "maxSizeOfSavedVersions" configuration parameter in "/etc/ts/tools/policy_history.cfg"

bugs.title: Cannot deploy a four-core vCMP guest if the remaining cores are in use.
bugs.symptoms: When trying to deploy a vCMP guest on an i11800 vCMP host using four or more cores while all of the other cores are in use, the following error message may be seen: err mcpd[<pid>]: 0107131f:3: Could not allocate vCMP guest (<guest_name>) because fragmented resources -------------------------------------------------- one more similar issue has raised for 8 guests allocation failure When trying to deploy a eight core guest on an i11800 vCMP host where four 2 cores are in use, the following error message may be seen: 0107131f:3: Could not allocate vCMP guest (guest-8cores-A) because fragmented resources
bugs.conditions: -- VCMP provisioned and all or most cores are in use. -- Attempt to deploy a guest. This is more likely to occur with vCMP guests that use four or more cores.
bugs.impact: All of the available cores cannot be used.
bugs.workaround: You may be able to work around this by deploying the largest guests first, then any remaining 2-core guests. There is currently no other fix.

bugs.title: TMM crashes while passing APM traffic.
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes while passing APM traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- LTM + APM deployment. -- Allow list in use. -- iRules in use.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround:
#--- logout_irule starts when HTTP_REQUEST { if { ([string tolower [HTTP::uri]] contains "closeconnection.aspx" || [string tolower [HTTP::uri]] contains "signout.aspx") && [ACCESS::session exists -state_allow -sid [HTTP::cookie MRHSession]] } { HTTP::respond 200 content {

You are now logged out.

}＼ "Set-Cookie" "F5_ST=deleted;expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT;path=/"＼ "Set-Cookie" "MRHSHint=deleted;expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT;path=/"＼ "Set-Cookie" "F5_HT_shrinked=deleted;expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT;path=/"＼ "Set-Cookie" "F5_fullWT=deleted;expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT;path=/"＼ "Set-Cookie" "LastMRH_Session=deleted;expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT;path=/"＼ "Set-Cookie" "MRHSession=deleted;expires=Thu, 01-Jan-1970 00:00:01 GMT;path=/" ACCESS::session remove log local0. "iRule logout triggered: Removing access session for [ACCESS::session sid]" # disable HTTP_REQUEST events for all other iRules event disable } } #--- logout_irule ends
bugs.fix: Fixed a TMM crash that can occur while processing iRules.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 header frames decoding may fail with COMPRESSION_ERROR when frame delivered in multiple xfrags
bugs.symptoms: HTTP/2 request fails with COMPRESSION_ERROR.
bugs.conditions: HTTP/2 header frames are received in multiple xfrags in such a way that the first 2 bytes of 'encoded' header-field 'value-length' are the last 2 bytes of the xfrag, and the remaining bytes are in the next xfrag.
bugs.impact: The header value length is incorrectly updated, and the HTTP/2 request fails.
bugs.fix: HTTP/2 now parses the request, regardless of its xfrags distribution.

bugs.title: HTTP response may be truncated by the BIG-IP system
bugs.symptoms: Web pages are not rendered properly; HTTP responses are truncated when traversing the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with an HTTP profile -- HTTP server generates a compressed response -- BIG-IP system determines that it must decompress the payload, e.g., a rewrite profile attached to the virtual server
bugs.impact: HTTP responses are truncated when passing through the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: One of the following: -- Add an HTTP Compression profile to the virtual server, and ensure that 'Keep Accept-Encoding' is not selected. -- Use an iRule to remove the Accept-Encoding header from requests, e.g.: ltm rule workaround { when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::header remove Accept-Encoding } }

bugs.title: IPI IPV6 traffic Reputation.
bugs.symptoms: The IPI module in BIG-IP is responsible for the reputation of IP addresses. IPI only works on IPv4 traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- IP Intelligence License installed -- The environment has a mix of IPv4 and IPv6
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP Intelligence features cannot do IPV6 traffic reputation.
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP Intelligence features can now do both IPv4 and IPV6 traffic Reputation
bugs.behavior: The BIG-IP Intelligence features can do both IPv4 and IPV6 traffic Reputation

bugs.title: Config fails to load for large config on platform with Platform FIPS license enabled
bugs.symptoms: Config fails to load.
bugs.conditions: -- Platforms with Platform FIPS license enabled. -- There are several ways to encounter this. One is with a large GTM (DNS) configuration that requires extending the gtmd stats file.
bugs.impact: Config file fails to load. For the gtmd configuration, gtmd repeatedly logs error messages similar to: err gtmd[14954]: 011af002:3: TMSTAT error 'Invalid argument' creating row '/Common/vs_45_53' in table 'gtm_vs_stat' For merged daemon, reports messages similar to: err merged[9166]: 011b0900:3: TMSTAT error tmstat_row_create: Invalid argument.

bugs.title: The cmp-hash VLAN setting does not apply to trunked interfaces.
bugs.symptoms: -- CPU usage is increased. -- Throughput is reduced. -- Packet redirections occur (visible when using 'tmctl -d blade tmm/flow_redir_stats')
bugs.conditions: -- Traffic is received on trunked interfaces. -- The cmp-hash setting has a non-default value. -- The platform is BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.impact: Performance is reduced. Output from 'tmctl -d blade tmm/flow_redir_stats' shows redirections.
bugs.workaround: -- Use the default cmp-hash setting. -- Do not trunk interfaces.

bugs.title: JSON parser is not fully UTF-8 compliant
bugs.symptoms: JSON parser's character set does not include support for UTF-8 characters and that can result in 'Malformed JSON data' violation when processing requests containing those characters in JSON data.
bugs.conditions: Requests contain unsupported UTF-8 characters, such as emoji characters, in JSON payload.
bugs.impact: Requests are blocked.
bugs.workaround: The System Variable 'relax_unicode_in_json' can be utilized to ignore what JSON identifies as malformed characters when it encounters such unsupported characters. (1) Enable 'relax_unicode_in_json' through CLI: # /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add relax_unicode_in_json 1 (2) Restart ASM to ensure changes take effect: # bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: Modifying GTM pool members with replace-all-with results in pool members with order 0
bugs.symptoms: GTMpool has multiple members with order 0.
bugs.conditions: There is an overlap for the pool members for the command replace-all-with and the pool members to be replaced.
bugs.impact: Multiple pool members have the same order.
bugs.workaround: Perform this procedure: 1. Delete all pool members from the GTM pool. 2. Use replace-all-with.

bugs.title: 'http-tunnel' and 'socks-tunnel' (which are internal interfaces) should be hidden.
bugs.symptoms: The Linux command 'ifconfig' or 'ip a' shows two devices 'http-tunnel' and 'socks-tunnel' that are for TMM internal use only.
bugs.conditions: These interfaces show up regardless of the BIG-IP configuration.
bugs.impact: As long as these devices are not used there is no impact aside from possibly causing confusion. Any attempt to use those devices from a host process fails or produces unpredictable results. These devices should not be exposed on the Linux host.
bugs.fix: The devices 'http-tunnel' and 'sock-tunnel' no longer show up on the Linux host.

bugs.title: VDI desktops and apps freeze with Vmware and Citrix intermittently
bugs.symptoms: VMware VDI: Blank screen is seen while opening remote desktop when VDI is configured with VMware. Citrix: Desktop freezes immediately after opening remote desktop when VDI is configured with Citrix.
bugs.conditions: VMware VDI: -- VDI is configured with VMware -- Desktop or App is launched using native client from Webtop. wait till 2X inactivity timeout if inactivity timeout Citrix: -- VDI is configured with Citrix -- Desktop or App is launched using native client from Webtop. -- Configure Inactivity timeout to 0.
bugs.impact: VDI desktops freeze while opening or immediately after opening. The following error is seen in APM logs: "Session stats update failed: ERR_NOT_FOUND"
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Users should not experience any intermittent desktop freeze.

bugs.title: JSON Schema is not enforced if OpenAPI media-type is wild card.
bugs.symptoms: If the openAPI configuration contains a wildcard media type for an endpoint, ASM does not enforce the JSON schema for requests with a JSON payload.
bugs.conditions: Create an OpenAPI policy with media type set to wildcard.
bugs.impact: ASM doesn't enforce JSON schema validation for HTTP requests containing a JSON payload.
bugs.fix: Provided fix and verified

bugs.title: Issues when creating an LTM Policy (with a rule) through an iApp
bugs.symptoms: When trying to create LTM policy with a rule through an iApp, an error occurs: 01070712:3: Values (/Common/Drafts/test_policy) specified for policy rule (/Common/Drafts/test_policy rule1): foreign key index (policy_FK) do not point at an item that exists in the database.
bugs.conditions: Creating an LTM policy with a rule using an iApp template in the GUI.
bugs.impact: LTM policy with rule cannot be created through iApp template
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to create an LTM policy with a rule: 1. For example, run a command similar to the following: #create ltm policy /Common/Drafts/tmsh_policy controls add { forwarding } requires add { http } strategy first-match rules add { rule1 {actions add { 0 {forward select pool p_test }} conditions add { 0 { http-host values { test1.com test2.com} } } }} 2. Publish the policy: #publish ltm policy /Common/Drafts/tmsh_policy

bugs.title: Improve matching of URLs with specific characters to a policy.
bugs.symptoms: Request with a URL containing specific characters is not matched to the correct policy.
bugs.conditions: URL of request contains specific percent-encoded characters.
bugs.impact: The request will not be matched by an expected policy rule.
bugs.workaround: Add an additional rule with explicit decoded characters.

bugs.title: DDoS: ICMPv6 packets not reported properly by Virtual DDoS
bugs.symptoms: Hardware does not support ICMPv6 protocol by virtual server DOS (Dos profile attached to virtual server).
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP hardware platform -- Virtual server configured with a DoS profile -- ICMPv6 traffic reaches the virtual server
bugs.impact: ICMPv6 Packets will be mitigated as per configuration but will not be reported in stats table

bugs.title: In some cases BD enforces CSRF on all URLs, ignoring CSRF URLs
bugs.symptoms: CSRF is sometimes enforced on URLs that do not match the CSRF URLs list
bugs.conditions: ASM policy with CSRF settings
bugs.impact: URLs that do not match the CSRF URLs list can be blocked due to CSRF violation.

bugs.title: TMM may crash when processing AFM NAT64 policy
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash or become unstable after producing the error: Enabling NAT64 for virtual server (/Common/test) with security NAT policy configured is redundant/not required.
bugs.conditions: Either of the following configurations: -- NAT64 enabled and AFM NAT64 policy attached. -- security-nat-policy attached and NAT64 disabled.
bugs.impact: TMM may crash, leading to a traffic interruption and failover event.
bugs.fix: The system now handles these configurations.

bugs.title: NAT policy rules are matched regardless of route domains
bugs.symptoms: Only the first policy rule is processed, as route domain indices not respected.
bugs.conditions: -- Two custom route domains, each with a virtual server configured in them -- A policy with two rules (one per route domain ID) is assigned to both the virtual servers
bugs.impact: Unable to segregate client traffic, as route domain indices are not respected in NAT policy rules
bugs.workaround: Use a separate policy on the wildcard virtual server for each route domain.

bugs.title: Mcpd core.
bugs.symptoms: Mcpd crashes and leaves a core file.
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur if BIG-IP fails to allocate huge pages, which can occur during module provisioning.
bugs.impact: Mcpd crashes and the system goes into an inoperative state.

bugs.title: When a virtual server has an inline service profile configured, connections will be reset with cause "No server selected"
bugs.symptoms: Connections are reset with "No server selected" cause.
bugs.conditions: -- An inline service profile ("ltm profile service") attached to a normal virtual server
bugs.impact: TCP connections are reset
bugs.workaround: Delete and recreate the virtual server without the inline service profile associated with it. Simply removing the service profile from the virtual server is not sufficient.

bugs.title: TMM crash in IPIP tunnel creation with a pool route
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances, the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) process may produce a core file in the /shared/core directory while processing traffic.
bugs.conditions: 1)Virtual server attached with an ipip encapsulation enabled pool 2)Multiple paths to pool members (pool route to pool member)
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: During bootup AWS BIG-IP endpoint was not licensed when custom gateway configured over management interface
bugs.symptoms: AWS-based BIG-IP instance with a static IP assigned to the mgmt interface and a custom gateway configured, the box fails to load its license during startup.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured with static IP address and customize gateway for default route.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP fails to load license.
bugs.workaround: Once BIG-IP boots up, execute reloadlic command which installs the license.

bugs.title: DDOS: BDOS: Warning messages related to high availability (HA) watchdog seen on system bring up
bugs.symptoms: When the BDoS log message level is set to "Warning", some high availability (HA) watchdog messages are logged: info bdosd[14184]: BDoS: May 27 03:51:40|loadState|460|HA Watchdog was not found <DNS_CLASS_L>
bugs.conditions: -- DDoS is used. -- Dynamic signature is enabled on vectors -- Default BDoS log level is changed to Warning.
bugs.impact: Unwanted log messages displayed. They can be safely ignored.

bugs.title: False positive RFC compliant violation
bugs.symptoms: False positive RFC compliant violation.
bugs.conditions: Authorization header with specific types.
bugs.impact: False positive violations.
bugs.workaround: Turn on an internal parameter: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add ignore_authorization_header_decode_failure 1
bugs.fix: Added tolerance to the authorization headers parser.

bugs.title: In BIG-IP GUI using "Select All" with filters is not working appropriately for policies
bugs.symptoms: In BIG-IP GUI using "Select All" with filters is not working appropriately for policies. When you attempt to delete policies after using filtering, all policies are deleted.
bugs.conditions: In BIG-IP GUI policies page, apply filter and using select all, for an action is selecting all objects and filter not applied.
bugs.impact: All policies objects are affected for an action, and filter is not applied

bugs.title: Edge Client shows HTML encoding for non-English endpoint inspection message
bugs.symptoms: HTML encoding characters are displayed in place of non-English characters, for example: ó is displayed as ó á is displayed as á
bugs.conditions: -- Modern access profile customization with Endpoint Inspection Message. -- Using BIG-IP Edge Client on Microsoft Windows.
bugs.impact: HTML encoding displays instead of non-English characters in messages on Edge Client.

bugs.title: Ike stops with error ikev2_send_request: [WINDOW] full window
bugs.symptoms: IKE SAs will be lost.
bugs.conditions: A failover occurs while IKE is sending DPD to the peer, and the reply is received by the newly active BIG-IP. Multiple failovers can increase the likelihood that this occurs.
bugs.impact: IKE SAs may be deleted and there will be traffic loss.
bugs.workaround: Increase in DPD interval to reduce the probability of occurrence of the issue.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where IKE SAs were being lost during failover events.

bugs.title: Pendsec utility incorrectly starts on i2x00/i4x00 platform with NON WD disk
bugs.symptoms: The pendsec utility recognizes that the disk is a HDD and attempts to run a smart check against it but it does not recognize or support the disk type that is in the system and therefore you will see log messages like this in /var/log/messages when the cron job attempts to run: May 14 15:34:04 fqdn.device.com notice pendsect[11461]: skipping drive -- May 14 15:34:04 fqdn.device.com notice pendsect[11461]: No known drives detected for pending sector check. Exiting
bugs.conditions: - i2x00 or i4x00 platform with the Seagate brand HDD
bugs.impact: Cosmetic
bugs.workaround: You can mitigate the cosmetic log issue by suppressing the pendsec utility. Login to BIG-IP using SSH Navigate to /etc/cron.daily # cd /etc/cron.daily Create new directory called suppress # mkdir suppress Move the pendsect cron job to suppres # mv pendsect suppress

bugs.title: Unexpected tmm core
bugs.symptoms: A tmm core occurs unexpectedly and causes a failover event.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while tmm is in normal operation.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: IPv6 fragments are dropped when packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.symptoms: IPv6 fragments are dropped when packet filtering is enabled.
bugs.conditions: Packet filtering is enabled and the system is processing IPv6 fragments.
bugs.impact: Some or all of the fragments of an IPv6 packet are lost.
bugs.workaround: Disable packet filtering

bugs.title: Slow file descriptor leak in urldbmgrd (sockets open over time)
bugs.symptoms: Unix domain sockets are opened and never closed in urldbmgrd. This is a very slow leak over time.
bugs.conditions: SWG or URLDB is provisioned.
bugs.impact: Urldbmgrd may hit a limit of open file descriptors, and may eventually core and restart. When urldbmgrd restarts, urldb also restarts. This may result in a momentary instant where URL categorization is not available.
bugs.workaround: Restarting urldbmgrd will clear the open file descriptors. Performing a forced restart during a time of no traffic will mitigate the risk of urldbmgrd restarting at an inconvenient time if there are too many sockets open. "bigstart restart urldbmgrd" will restart the daemon.

bugs.title: Cannot modify Security "global-network" Logging Profile
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to update the settings of the Security Logging profile, the window displays a modal dialog box titled "Saving Logging Profile" and never completes the update Action
bugs.conditions: "global-network" logging profile is selected for update
bugs.impact: You are unable to update the log settings for the "global-network" profile via UI
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh

bugs.title: Profile type 'swg-transparent' should be selected on create page when 'create-new' is selected for SwgAsService in SSL Orchestrator
bugs.symptoms: When creating a new service, certain default access profiles are not automatically selected.
bugs.conditions: 1. SSL Orchestrator + APM + SWG provisioned 2. Select 'create-new' for access profile drop-down when adding a SwgAsService in SSL Orchestrator A new tab opens with the profile creation page, but the access profile type drop-down does not have any type selected.
bugs.impact: When adding a SwgAsService in SSL Orchestrator, the only supported access profile type is SWG-Transparent, hence it should be automatically selected.
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue with automatic profile selection.

bugs.title: A partition other than /Common may fail to save the configuration to disk
bugs.symptoms: A mismatch between the running-configuration (i.e. what is returned by "tmsh list ...") and the saved-configuration (i.e. what is stored in the flat configuration files) for a partition other than /Common, despite a "tmsh save config" operation was just performed (either by the user or as a result of a config-sync).
