bugs.title: Performance improvement for checking signature exclusions on header
bugs.symptoms: As part of a general performance improvement effort, we were looking into profiling data and observed that in many cases a lot of CPU is wasted, in the process to find out whether a specific signature is excluded on a specific header.
bugs.conditions: Signatures are enabled in ASM.
bugs.impact: High CPU usage when checking for signature header exclusions.
bugs.fix: Optimized the code responsible for checking signature exclusions on header.

bugs.title: Prevent zrd from rolling back named.conf file in wrong situations
bugs.symptoms: The zrd process may roll name.conf back which may cause unexpected changes. This shows up in the /var/log/gtm file or in the GUI with a message similar to the following: err zrd[27809]: 01150306:3: Error connecting to named socket 'Connection refused'. (or) err zrd[16198]: 01150306:3: Error connecting to named socket 'Connection timed out'.
bugs.conditions: As of now list include the following scenarios: -- One of the scenario is seen as part of ID1083405 - see https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1083405.html -- Named process isn’t running, updating wide IPs will cause the same symptom.
bugs.impact: Looking up or modifying zone records may fail. This will affect the other members in the gtm sync group as well.

bugs.title: Unable to retrieve SCP files using WinSCP or relative path name
bugs.symptoms: When you attempt to retrieve a file with WinSCP, you receive an error dialog and the session will be terminated: "SCP Protocol error: Invalid control record (r; elative addresses not allowed) Copying files from the remote side failed." If you attempt to transfer a file by the relative path with a command line utility the transfer will fail with the message: "relative addresses not allowed"
bugs.conditions: -- Running BIG-IP version with a fix for ID 915981 -- Using WinSCP set to use SCP protocol to retrieve files from a BIG-IP system. -- Using a relative remote path to transfer a file with the command line SCP utility.
bugs.impact: Cannot use WinSCP to retrieve files such as packet captures, log archives, or other diagnostic data from the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: Use a command line SCP tool that allows specifying an absolute path for the source and/or destination file (a path that starts with a forward slash /), when the source and/or destination locations are a BIG-IP device. You may use WinSCP in SFTP mode if the user ID is permitted to do so.

bugs.title: In Bot Defense profile, the SSE API timeout value is not considered for mobile requests
bugs.symptoms: Distributed Cloud API timeout is not considered for Mobile endpoint requests.
bugs.conditions: - Bot Defense profile configured with mobile endpoints. - Distributed Cloud API timeout value is configured. - Requests to mobile endpoint are sent from client, which triggers API request to SSE but the response is not received within the timeout configured.
bugs.impact: Distributed Cloud API timeout is not considered for Mobile endpoint requests.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 may garble responses if the client-side stream aborts while response headers are on the wire
bugs.symptoms: If the client-side stream aborts while response headers are on the wire, the subsequent requests may receive a garbled response.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP2 profile is used on both client and server side. - The client terminates the stream while the response has not yet reached the BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: The client will receive an obscure response
bugs.fix: Even if the client terminates a stream (while the response has yet not reached BIG-IP), the subsequent requests will receive a correct response.

bugs.title: FIPS Card Cannot Initialize
bugs.symptoms: Initializing the FIPS card for the first time which contains the FIPS firmware CNN35XX-NFBE-FW-1.1-02 may cause the below error and will not be able to initialize the card: Enter new Security Officer password (min. 0, max. 0 characters): ERROR: Too long input (max.: 0 characters) ERROR: Failed to read password ERROR: INITIALIZATION FAILED!
bugs.conditions: First time initialization of new device with "tmsh run util fips-util -f init" command which contains the FIPS firmware CNN35XX-NFBE-FW-1.1-02
bugs.impact: FIPS card cannot be used for the FIPS key traffic and will not be able to re-initialize.

bugs.title: Traffic classes match when they shouldn't
bugs.symptoms: Traffic classes may match when they should not.
bugs.conditions: * Fix for ID1074505 is present (without that fix this bug is hidden). * Traffic class uses none (or equivalently all 0s) for source-address.
bugs.impact: Traffic is not categorized properly.
bugs.workaround: Specify a source address, e.g. ltm traffic-class /Common/blah { source-address 1.1.1.1 source-mask none ... } Note that because the mask is none this won't have any effect (other than working around this bug).

bugs.title: Fix to avoid zombie node on the chain
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashing because of not removing complete nodes
bugs.conditions: Flush to finally remove complete nodes will avoids the TMM crash and avoids leaving zombie nodes
bugs.impact: Subsequent activities on the connection could lead to TMM to crash or misbehave in a variety of ways.

bugs.title: [APM]APM as IdP with PRP and Subroutine with Confirm Box fails
bugs.symptoms: If you configure APM as an IdP and Create a Per-Request Policy that includes a subroutine with a "Confirm Box", the POST containing the SAML Auth Request is lost and APM reports: err tmm1[27543]: 014d1080:3: /Common/IdP_ap:Common:869ab83f:SAML SSO: Authn Request has no SAMLRequest err tmm1[27543]: 014d1224:3: /Common/IdP_ap:Common:869ab83f:SAML SSO: Error (12) extracting SAML Data from Request
bugs.conditions: -- APM configured as an IdP -- PRP with Subroutine containing a Confirm Box
bugs.impact: Can't use a checkbox in a PRP subroutine
bugs.workaround: 1. Use Redirect Binding instead of POST Binding. 2. Do not use a check box in the subroutine

bugs.title: LTM/GTM config instantiated in a certain way can cause a LTM/GTM monitor to fail to delete.
bugs.symptoms: Upon attempting to delete a LTM or GTM monitor, the system returns an error similar to the following example, even though the monitor being deleted is no longer in use anywhere: 01070083:3: Monitor /Common/my-tcp is in use.
bugs.conditions: -- The configuration was loaded from file (for example, as restoring a UCS archive would do). -- A BIG-IP Administrator deletes all objects using the monitor, and then attempts to delete the monitor itself.
bugs.impact: LTM or GTM monitor no longer in use anywhere cannot be deleted from the configuration.
bugs.workaround: Run one of the following sets of commands (depending on the affected module) and then try to delete the monitor again: tmsh save sys config tmsh load sys config tmsh save sys config gtm-only tmsh load sys config gtm-only
bugs.fix: Unused monitors can now be deleted correctly.

bugs.title: API timeout observed for few requests that have telemetry data in body
bugs.symptoms: API timeout is observed in SAAS logs and bbrdump for requests that have telemetry data in the body
bugs.conditions: - Configure the BD profile and attach it to a virtual server. - Send web requests with telemetry data in the body.
bugs.impact: Observed API timeout in SAAS logs and bbrdump for requests that have telemetry data in the body.
bugs.fix: Fixed issue of API timeout timer that was started prematurely for few requests.

bugs.title: API timeout observed for few requests with telemetry data in body and such requests do not get processed successfully
bugs.symptoms: Requests with telemetry data in body may not get processed successfully. Observed API timeout in SAAS logs and bbrdump.
bugs.conditions: - Configure BD profile and attach it to virtual server - Send web requests with telemetry data in body
bugs.impact: Requests with telemetry data in body may not get processed successfully.

bugs.title: FIPS 140-2/FIPS 140-3 compliant mode is incorrect after upgrade to 16.1.2.2
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading a BIG-IP system that is licensed for FIPS 140-2 compliant mode or with the full-box FIPS license, the FIPS mode reported is FIPS 140-3 compliant mode, but FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3 mode is not properly enabled. Also, if you upgrade a BIG-IP system that is licensed for FIPS 140-2 compliant mode or with the full-box FIPS license, and upgrade to version 16.1.2.2 without first re-activating your license, after the upgrade is complete you will be prompted to reboot. After the reboot, FIPS mode will be disabled.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP system running a software version earlier than 16.1.2.2, regardless of hardware or software platform type -- The FIPS 140-2 compliant mode or full-box FIPS license is applied -- Upgrade to version 16.1.2.2
bugs.impact: After the system reboots, the BIG-IP system reports that FIPS 140-3 compliant mode is enabled, but the FIPS mode is not FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 compliant in this version. If you did not re-activate the license prior to upgrade, the BIG-IP system will prompt you to reboot, and then will start with FIPS mode disabled.
bugs.workaround: If you are upgrading a BIG-IP system that has a FIPS 140-2 compliant mode license applied, do not upgrade to version 16.1.2.2; instead, upgrade to BIG-IP version 16.1.3 or higher if your intention is to upgrade to version 16.x.

bugs.title: System CPU Usage detailed graph is not accessible on Cerebrus+
bugs.symptoms: When accessing performance reports of CPU usage detailed graph, error "Error trying to access the database." is displayed since the CPU graph name is getting truncated.
bugs.conditions: When on a single blade, if we have more than 17 TMMs this error will be seen.
bugs.impact: Detailed graph for system CPU usage will not be accessible.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: Increased the size of the detail string to support more than 32 TMMs.

bugs.title: DNS query drops on Virtual Edition platform if the packet size is above 1500 for NAPTR record.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system drops the packet if the DNS response size is larger than 2048.
bugs.conditions: When the DNS server sends a response larger than 2048 bytes.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system drops the packet and does not respond to the client.
bugs.workaround: If possible, switch from UDP to TCP to avoid dropping the packet.

bugs.title: ip_address_intelligence field is not populated with value in ArcSight remote log when source IP is IPv4
bugs.symptoms: The key used for the ip_address_intelligence field is mapped to an IPv6 Address in the latest CEF standard.
bugs.conditions: -- IP Intelligence is enabled. -- An ArcSight remote logger is configured. -- A HTTP transaction is carried out with a malicious Source IP Address
bugs.impact: The ip_address_intelligence field value is not populated in the ArcSight remote log
bugs.fix: A new key for ip_address_intelligence is implemented specific to IPv4

bugs.title: Packets are dropped when mitigation is set to infinite
bugs.symptoms: After configuring a DoS vector in full automatic mode, packets are dropped when all mitigation thresholds are set to infinite.
bugs.conditions: Configuring DoS vector in Full automatic mode with Bad Destination DoS protection enabled.
bugs.impact: -- Packets are dropped even if mitigation thresholds are set to infinite. -- Good packets may also be dropped.

bugs.title: After upgrade, Learning and Blocking Settings page is not loading because some policies are still pointing to deleted factory Negsig sets
bugs.symptoms: Learning and Blocking Settings page is not loading
bugs.conditions: Some policies are using factory sets which were deleted in later versions, and an upgrade was performed.
bugs.impact: When trying to open "Security ›› Application Security : Policy Building : Learning and Blocking Settings" page, GUI is stuck on 'loading' status
bugs.workaround: Run this mysql in the BIG-IP in order to fix the database, it will remove all unreferenced policy sets from the system: mysql -p`perl -MF5::Cfg -e 'print F5::Cfg::get_mysql_password(user => q{root})'` -e "delete from PLC. PL_POLICY_NEGSIG_SETS where set_id not in (SELECT set_id from PLC.NEGSIG_SETS);"
bugs.fix: After the fix, the 'Learning and Blocking Settings' page will be loaded with no error.

bugs.title: Self-IP allows no traffic following a modification from "Allow Custom (Include Default)" to "Allow Custom".
bugs.symptoms: Although a Self-IP address appears configured correctly (for example, when this is inspected using the WebUI or the tmsh utility), the Self-IP address does not allow through any traffic. Effectively, the Self-IP address behaves as if it was set to "Allow None".
bugs.conditions: The port-lockdown setting of the Self-IP address was recently modified from "Allow Custom (Include Default)" to "Allow Custom".
bugs.impact: The Self-IP does not allow through any traffic, whereas it should allow through the traffic in your custom list of ports and protocols.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by temporarily setting the affected Self-IP to "Allow None" and then again to "Allow Custom", specifying your desired custom list of ports and protocols.
bugs.fix: Self-IP port-lockdown modifications from "Allow Custom (Include Default)" to "Allow Custom" are now handled correctly.

bugs.title: Change ArcSight Threat Campaign key names to be camelCase
bugs.symptoms: The threat_campagin_names and staged_threat_campaign_names do not follow other key name format. Changing these key names to be camelCase (threatCampaignNames and stagedThreatCampaignNames).
bugs.conditions: ArcSight is in use with ASM remote logging.
bugs.impact: Inconsistent key name formatting.
bugs.fix: Changed name format to be camelCase (threatCampaignNames and stagedThreatCampaignNames).

bugs.title: Expired REST tokens are not getting deleted from /var/run/pamcache on standalone BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: REST tokens which are present in /var/run/pamcache on BIG-IP are not deleted after token expiration when there are a large number of tokens.
bugs.conditions: When a large number of tokens are generated.
bugs.impact: More memory will be used as /run/pamcache is an in memory filesystem
bugs.workaround: Try to remove token files from /run/pamcache manually. You can check what would be deleted by the command below by using -print in place of -delete # find /run/pamcache -regextype posix-extended -type f -regex '/run/pamcache/[A-Z0-9]{26}' -delete
bugs.fix: Expired token are removed from /run/pamcache by the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: System boots into an inoperative state after installing engineering hotfix with FIPS140-2/140-3 License
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system persistently starts up in an inoperative state after installing an engineering hotfix with a console error similar to: *** FIPS or Common Criteria power-up self-test failure. *** This system has been placed in an error state. *** To recover return to the grub menu and select another volume *** or reinstall the system. *** *** On many devices pressing the escape key followed by the ( *** key will bring up a menu which allows the system to be restarted. Power-up self-test failures: <number> Unmounting file systems System halting.
bugs.conditions: - First boot after installing an engineering hotfix. - FIPS 140-2 or FIPS140-3 license.
bugs.impact: You are unable to boot the BIG-IP system into an operational state after applying an engineering hotfix, and you are required to boot to a known good volume. For more information, see K52534643: Overview of the Platform FIPS BIG-IP system :: https://support.f5.com/csp/article/K52534643
bugs.fix: The BIG-IP system successfully boots after installing an engineering hotfix on a system with a FIPS 140-2 or FIPS140-3 license. For a complete solution for BIG-IP software v16.1.3.1 and later v16.1.x releases, you must also have the additional fix described in ID 1137037 https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1137037.html.

bugs.title: GUI unable to load Bot Profiles and tmsh is unable to list them as well.
bugs.symptoms: If there are 10s of bot defense profiles that all have hundreds of staged signatures, neither the GUI nor tmsh will be able to list the Bot Profiles.
bugs.conditions: Tens of bot defense profiles that have 100s of staged signatures.
bugs.impact: -- Unable to edit bot profiles in the GUI. -- Unable to save to config files or UCS
bugs.workaround: Remove staging for bot-signatures.

bugs.title: When OAuth profile is attached to access policy, iRule event in VPE breaks the evaluation
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to 16.1.2.1, the OAuth configuration does not work anymore. Based on the below observations, an internal redirect to /renderer/agent_irule_event_form.eui is initiated but it is not processed, so the ACCESS_POLICY_AGENT_EVENT event is never fired. Observations: Following are the results from in-house troubleshooting: Test 1: Access Policy evaluation works with a standard Access Profile, clientless mode set with iRule, and an iRule event. Test 2: Access Policy evaluation fails with a standard Access Profile but an OAuth profile attached to access policy (clientless mode to be set automatically) and an iRule event.
bugs.conditions: As soon as the iRule event is removed from VPE in Test 2, the access policy evaluation works fine.
bugs.impact: ACCESS_POLICY_AGENT_EVENT event is never fired
bugs.fix: Pass on the packet to the upper hudfilter handles.

bugs.title: SSL Certificate List GUI page takes a long time to load
bugs.symptoms: SSL Certificate List GUI page under System->Certificate Management->Traffic Certificate Management->SSL Certificate List does not load or takes a long time to load (more than 3 minutes).
bugs.conditions: -- When clicking on SSL Certificates List menu in the GUI. -- BIG-IP is loaded with heavy configuration and more number of certificates. -- BIG-IP is vCMP guest.
bugs.impact: Certificates list is not presented from GUI.
bugs.workaround: GET the certificate list through TMSH command tmsh list sys crypto cert
bugs.fix: SSL Certificate list menu is displayed with out any delay.

bugs.title: Signatures might not be detected when using truncated multipart requests
bugs.symptoms: On special cases when sending long requests that include a multipart section, signatures that should be detected in the multipart body might not be detected.
bugs.conditions: 1. WAF-policy is attached to virtual server. 2. Signatures are enabled in the WAF policy. 3. Signatures contain special characters, i.e. ;"=＼n 4. Request is longer than the value in max_raw_request_len. 5. Sending a multipart request.
bugs.impact: Signature is not detected.

bugs.title: GUI online help for IPS signatures is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Some of the fields in the GUI don't diaplay the helper definition
bugs.conditions: 1. Go to the Security -> Protocol Security : Inspection Profiles 2. Click the Add button. You are redirected redirect to a page where you need to fill in the profile name and other parameters like service etc. 3. Some of the service helper functions are not available
bugs.impact: Without helper functions, you are unable to identify the details of the parameters.

bugs.title: Headers without a space after the colon trigger an HTTP RFC violation
bugs.symptoms: An "Unparsable request content" violation is detected for valid headers without a space after the headers name ':'
bugs.conditions: Any header without a space between the ':' and the header value will trigger "Unparsable request content"
bugs.impact: Requests that suppose to pass are blocked by ASM enforcer
bugs.workaround: The client has to send headers with space after ':'
bugs.fix: No "Unparsable request content" violation for headers with space after ':'

bugs.title: Classic BIG-IP tenant running on F5OS will not correctly pin in-tenant control plane threads correctly on first deployment
bugs.symptoms: This may not impact performance in the tenant, but for tenant builds without this fix, upon initial deployment, the control plane will not be pinned correctly (should be pinned to odd-numbered cpus). Note: This pinning is inside the tenant virtual machine, not in the F5OS host. The datapath (TMM) will still be pinned correctly.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP tenant without this fix is initially deployed.
bugs.impact: The datapath (TMM) threads run at elevated priority anyway, so would be protected from the control plane threads.
bugs.workaround: If this is bothersome, redeploy the tenant, and the problem will not reoccur.
bugs.fix: Tenant platform determination no longer depends on a file that is not there on initial startup. The dmidecode utility is used instead.

bugs.title: BIG-IP 16.1.3 VE with FIPS 140-3 May Fail to start in AWS-China
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP 16.1.3 VE with FIPS 140-3 may fail to start in AWS-China
bugs.conditions: Running BIG-IP 16.1.3 VE with FIPS 140-3 with 16.1.3 in AWS China region
bugs.impact: BIG-IP 16.1.3 VE with FIPS 140-3 may fail to start in AWS-China
bugs.workaround: Upgrade to 16.1.3.1 when it is available.

bugs.title: Frequent SIGSEGV TMM crash/core in AFM FQDN | fw_iptbl_fqdn_ctx_check
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash or core
bugs.conditions: Two FQDNs associated to BIG-IP firewall rules point to same IP in the DNS server at any instance of time.
bugs.impact: 1. One of the FW rules may not work. 2. TMM crash or core.
bugs.workaround: Use IP addresses on such places of firewall rules.

bugs.title: LibUV library for latest bind 9.16
bugs.symptoms: The latest bind software requires the latest libuv for performance improvements and to support new protocol layers (for example, DNS over TLS).
bugs.conditions: The latest bind software requires the latest libuv for performance improvements and to support new protocol layers (for example, DNS over TLS).
bugs.fix: Maintain a new libuv in the BIG-IP code base.

bugs.title: Weighted static routes do not recover from BFD link failures
bugs.symptoms: If a BFD link fails and recovers, the weighted static route that should be preferred does not populate back into the routing table.
bugs.conditions: Weighted static routes with BFD configured, this is an example of the affected configuration: ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.8.8.4 100 ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.8.8.34 200 ip static 0.0.0.0/0 10.8.8.4 fall-over bfd ip static 0.0.0.0/0 10.8.8.34 fall-over bfd After BFD session to 10.8.8.4 fails and recovers the default route will still be pointing to 10.8.8.34.
bugs.impact: Incorrect route nexthop.
bugs.workaround: Re-add route config statements.

bugs.title: BIG-IP does not forward the response received after GOAWAY, to the client.
bugs.symptoms: After receiving a GOAWAY from the server followed by data on the same stream, the BIG-IP system does not forward that data to the client but rather sends RESET_STREAM.
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure an NGINX server to handle two streams per connection 2. Virtual server with http2 profile 3. Send more than two requests on the same connection
bugs.impact: The client does not get a proper response
bugs.fix: The client should receive proper response.

bugs.title: Error found when adding a new BIG-IP to the existing HA system and performing the configsync of GROUP_HA
bugs.symptoms: Log messages in /var/log/ltm indicate a validation failed for configsync of GROUP_HA. slot2 info mcpd[7759]: 0107148c:6: Received advertisement for device group /Common/GROUP_HA from remote device /Common/F5-CH4-LTM-ASM-RECO.xxxxxx.com.ar, force false, error 'Load failed from /Common/F5-LTM-ASM-RECO.xxxxxxx 01070283:3: The profile (/Common/R-SYSLOG) is currently associated with one or more virtual servers or transport configs.' commit_id 3 7102249069396191621 /Common/F5-CH4-LTM-ASM-RECO.xxxxxxx.com.ar 0, local commit id is 12 7102249979076829225 /Common/F5-LTM-ASM-RECO.xxxxxxx 0 cached remote device data 0
bugs.conditions: The issue can be reproduced by loading the user's configurations and Full ConfigSync performed.
bugs.impact: The user is unable to add a new BIG-IP to the existing HA system.
bugs.workaround: a. On F5-LTM-ASM-RECO, remove "R-SYSLOG" Request Logging Profile from all 29 virtual servers. b. Then do a CMI full sync and ensure the sync is successful. c. Next, put back the "R-SYSLOG" Request Logging Profile to all 29 virtual servers. d. Do a CMI full sync again.

bugs.title: VE on VMware with VMXNET3 fails to work with Large Receive Offload (LRO)
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP VE running on VMware may either not utilize Large Receive Offload (LRO), or may exhibit poor TCP performance for standard virtual servers using TCP profiles with Delayed ACKs enabled.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE deployed in a VMWare environment, using VMXNET3 NICs
bugs.impact: - TCP performance is not as expected when going through a standard virtual server when TMM receives LROed TCP segments. - Virtual servers are not using LRO, even when it is enabled.
bugs.workaround: Disable LRO globally: tmsh modify sys db tm.tcplargereceiveoffload value disable && tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: Route-domains should not be allowed on name server addresses via the GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Route domains are allowed on nameserver address when configuring them via the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Create a DNS resolver via the GUI and include route domain for nameserver IP address. Eg : Navigate to Network > DNS Resolvers > DNS Resolver List and can create a DNS resolver name server address with Route domain.
bugs.impact: Inconsistency between the GUI and TMSH for dns resolver namserver address.

bugs.title: Some of the valid connections may get rejected in HW SYN cookie mode
bugs.symptoms: Due to algorithm mismatch in software and hardware, valid TCP connections may get rejected with "No flow found for ACK' reset-cause while HW SYN cookie mode is active.
bugs.conditions: In vCMP environment either the host or the guest is installed with an affected version.
bugs.impact: Service degradation.
bugs.workaround: Disable HW SYN cookie globally on the guest.
bugs.fix: SYN cookie hash algorithm is correctly selected on vCMP guests.

bugs.title: Interfaces using the xnet driver are not assigned a MAC address
bugs.symptoms: Interfaces on BIG-IP Virtual Edition that are capable of 100gb are unusable when the default driver of xnet is used. The following validation error will be present in /var/log/ltm "01071ab7:3: 'not-supported' is an invalid forward-error-correction setting for Interface" The interfaces will not report a MAC address in either of: - tmsh list /net interfaces - tmsh show /sys mac
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP Virtual Edition where the interfaces report a 100gb max speed and the xnet driver is used.
bugs.impact: Interfaces are not assigned a MAC address, therefore are unusable.
bugs.workaround: Force the interface(s) to use a driver other then xnet. In order to apply the workaround you will need to get 1) the available drivers and 2) the pci id of the interfaces. The available drivers are reported using this tmctl command: # tmctl -d blade tmm/device_probed pci_bdf pseudo_name type available_drivers driver_in_use ------------ ----------- --------- -------------------- ------------- 0000:00:03.0 F5DEV_PCI mlxvf5, xnet, sock, 0000:00:05.0 1.1 F5DEV_PCI mlxvf5, xnet, sock, xnet 0000:00:06.0 1.2 F5DEV_PCI mlxvf5, xnet, sock, xnet The pci id is reported with the lspci -nnvvv command: In this example: the pci id is 15b3:101a # lspci -nnvvv | grep -i ethernet 00:03.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: Mellanox Technologies MT28800 Family [ConnectX-5 Ex Virtual Function] [15b3:101a] 00:05.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: Mellanox Technologies MT28800 Family [ConnectX-5 Ex Virtual Function] [15b3:101a] 00:06.0 Ethernet controller [0200]: Mellanox Technologies MT28800 Family [ConnectX-5 Ex Virtual Function] [15b3:101a] And to force the use of a different driver you need to modify /config/tmm_init.tcl by adding a line such as: device driver vendor_dev 15b3:101a mlxvf5 Where the last values of that line are the pci id and driver name.

bugs.title: Need larger Content-Length value supported for SIP
bugs.symptoms: SIP MRF sends error 413 when the content_length value in the SIP message is greater than 65535 (0xff).
bugs.conditions: The SIP content_length has to be greater than 65535 (0xff) on SIP MRF configuration
bugs.impact: The SIP messages with content_length greater than 65535 can't be processed by the BIG-IP successfully because of the hard coded constraint on the SIP content_length
bugs.fix: Make the allowable SIP content_length dynamic with respective to the configured max_msg_size in the SIP MRF session profile configuration.

bugs.title: Trailing slash buffer details are missing from remote logger
bugs.symptoms: Incoming requests with path parameters in the URI that cause "Trailing Slash" evasion sub-violation might be reported without buffer details in the remote logger and the GUI violation details.
bugs.conditions: In terms of configurations, "Trailing Slash" and "Trailing Dot" must be enabled in the policy builder, with the addition of "Handle Path Parameters" set to "As Parameters" in the policy. In terms of incoming requests, the URI has to contain path parameters.
bugs.impact: The buffer reported in violation details is masked with asterisks "*****" while the buffer in the remote logger is missing.
bugs.fix: For violation details and remote logger, the reported evasion sub-violation will have a buffer with value "N/A".

bugs.title: Impossible to sign out of OWA when using kerberos SSO
bugs.symptoms: Users are unable to logout from OWA.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP is configured with kerberos SSO against the exchange server. Users try to use the OWA "Sign out" button.
bugs.impact: Clicking the OWA 'Sign out' button will do nothing other than showing this message: "To finish signing out, please close all open browser windows." That means APM cookies will not be automatically deleted and session will still be active.
bugs.workaround: Any one of these will mitigate the issue: -- Send a request to "/owa/logoff.owa" will help complete the sign out process on the client and initiate the logout on APM side. -- Close the browser to clear out APM cookies on the client side (session will remain active on APM). -- Configure FBA authentication for OWA on Exchange server and client initiated form based SSO on APM

bugs.title: Tomcat fails to write log messages into /var/log/tomcat/liveupdate.log file
bugs.symptoms: You only see this message in /var/log/tomcat/liveupdate.log file. No other log messages are written, which impedes troubleshooting Live Update. liveupdate.script file is corrupted, live update repository initialized with default schema This error is emitted during tomcat startup. /var/log/tomcat/catalina.out java.io.FileNotFoundException: /usr/share/tomcat/logs/liveupdate.log (Permission denied) Tomcat memory use may grow over time which can cause it to be slower, use more CPU or fail due to being out of memory.
bugs.conditions: You are running on a version which has a bug fix for ID 907025. For more information see https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID907025.html
bugs.impact: Difficult to troubleshoot issues that occur with Live Update Tomcat memory growth can cause tomcat to run out of memory, be slow, and use higher than usual CPU due to increased garbage collection activity.
bugs.workaround: Run the following commands: chown tomcat:tomcat /var/log/tomcat/liveupdate.log bigstart restart tomcat

bugs.title: Wr_urldbd continuously crashes and restarts
bugs.symptoms: Malloc failed while wr_urldb is started
bugs.conditions: Intermittently reproduced when rebooting to a new version or after restarting wr_urldbd
bugs.impact: Wr_urldbd crashes.
bugs.workaround: - Stop the wr_urldbd to stabilize(#bigstart stop wr_urldbd) -- Update the customdb(i.e. delete or add custom urls) on the backend server -- Start wr_urldbd to download and load the new DB(#bigstart start wr_urldbd)
bugs.fix: After the fix, malloc is properly done and no crash

bugs.title: The /api, a non-existent URI returns different error response with or without correct Basic Authorization credentials
bugs.symptoms: The /api returns 401 when incorrect Basic Authorization credentials are supplied. The /api returns 404 when correct Basic Authorization credentials are supplied.
bugs.conditions: Irrespective of the DB variable "httpd.basic_auth" value set to enable or disable.
bugs.impact: There is no functional impact, but all other non-existent URIs return a 302 redirect response to the TMUI login page irrespective of correct or incorrect Basic Authorization credentials, /api should also be invariably exhibiting the same behavior.
bugs.fix: The /api like any other non-existent URI now returns a 302 redirect response to the TMUI login page irrespective of correct or incorrect Basic Authorization credentials.

bugs.title: VLAN guest tagging is not implemented for CX4 and CX5 on ESXi
bugs.symptoms: Tagged VLAN traffic is not received by the BIG-IP Virtual Edition (VE).
bugs.conditions: Mellanox CX4 or CX5 with SR-IOV on VMware ESXi.
bugs.impact: Host-side tagging is required.
bugs.workaround: If only one VLAN is required, use host-side tagging and set the VLAN to "untagged" in the BIG-IP guest. If multiple VLANs are required, use the "sock" driver instead. Edit the /config/tmm_init.tcl file and restart the Virtual Edition (VE) instance. Network traffic is disrupted while the system restarts. echo "device driver vendor_dev 15b3:1016 sock" >> /config/tmm_init.tcl CPU utilization may increase as a result of switching to the sock driver.

bugs.title: FastL4 traffic traversing the tunnels such as VXLAN, may fail on VELOS and rSeries tenants
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP tenants running on an VELOS or rSeries system may incorrectly attempt to PVA accelerate traffic that goes through a VXLAN tunnel. That is, where the pool members are reachable through a VXLAN tunnel.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP tenant running on VELOS or rSeries. - Virtual server that processes traffic over a tunnel. For example, VXLAN, GRE, or IP-IP.
bugs.impact: Connections fail. A packet capture from the F5OS layer shows packets arriving at the system, but not forwarded through the tunnel. As a result, packet retransmits are obeserved. A packet capture in the tenant shows packets arriving at the TMM, but with layer 3 and layer 4 headers rewritten to match the server-side connection information.
bugs.workaround: FastL4 acceleration is not supposed to work for traffic being load-balanced over a tunnel. To mitigate this issue, disable PVA acceleration in the FastL4 profile for virtual servers that will load-balance traffic over a tunnel.
bugs.fix: Packets are successfully forwarded through the tunnel, these flows are not accelerated.

bugs.title: Configuration load error for a non default value of 'net dag-global {dag-ipv6-prefix-len}'
bugs.symptoms: Configuration load fails after an upgrade, with the following error warning mcpd[6758]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : Configuring DAG Global IPv6 Prefix Length still might require modification of vlans previously created with the old setting. err mcpd[6758]: 01071e16:3: DAG ipv6 prefix length is not supported on this platform. err tmsh[9523]: 01420006:3: Loading configuration process failed. emerg load_config_files[9521]: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g -a load sys config partitions all base " - failed. -- Loading schema version: 15.1.5.1 err mcpd[6758]: 01070422:3: Base configuration load failed.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure a non-default value of 'net dag-global {dag-ipv6-prefix-len}'. -- Upgrade the BIG-IP software to the affected version.
bugs.impact: -- Configuration load error -- The setting of 'net dag-global {dag-ipv6-prefix-len}' is not functioning correctly
bugs.fix: Fixed configuration load error for a non default value of 'net dag-global {dag-ipv6-prefix-len}'

bugs.title: Running tmsh load sys config verify can trigger high availability (HA) failover
bugs.symptoms: When running tmsh 'tmsh load sys config verify' on a config that contains both a high availability (HA) group and a traffic group referencing that high availability (HA) group, this will trigger a high availability (HA) fault and failover.
bugs.conditions: - Running 2 BIG-IP systems in a high availability (HA) pair - Run tmsh 'load sys config verify' on a config with the following conditions: - Config to be verified contains a high availability (HA) group - Config to be verified also contains a traffic group referencing the high availability (HA) group
bugs.impact: HA fault and failover. The high availability (HA) pair will enter a degraded state.
bugs.workaround: No workaround currently known, but the failover fault can be cleared by running tmsh 'load sys config' on the system that had 'load sys config verify' run on it.

bugs.title: Removed gtmd and big3d daemon from the FIPS-compliant list
bugs.symptoms: The gtmd is not able to establish a secure connection to big3d due to failure in handshake because no common ciphers were found between big3d and gtmd in FIPS mode.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP versions 16.1.3 and above -- FIPS 140-3 license is installed on BIG-IP or its a FullBoxFIPS device. -- Connections are established between big3d and gtmd in FIPS mode.
bugs.impact: SSL handshakes fail between big3d and gtmd because no common ciphers are present.
bugs.fix: Gtmd and big3d can now communicate when FIPS mode is enabled.

bugs.title: Illegal internal request in multipart batch request
bugs.symptoms: Request parser for inner request is intolerant for a linefeed that results in a HTTP Protocol Compliance violation with the following details. HTTP Validation Bad multipart parameters parsing Details Illegal internal request in multipart batch request
bugs.conditions: - multipart/batch(ing) request - inner requests use LF for end-of-line marker, instead of canonical marker CRLF
bugs.impact: Request gets blocked

bugs.title: Unable to update the password in the CLI when password-memory is set to > 0
bugs.symptoms: A BIG-IP system with password-memory enabled will fail to update the user password in the first login using the CLI
bugs.conditions: Password-memory set to > 0 in password-policy configuration
bugs.impact: Not able to update the user password in the first login using the CLI.
bugs.workaround: Create the user using the GUI and log in from the GUI.

bugs.title: Some valid connections may get rejected in hardware SYN cookie mode
bugs.symptoms: Due to an algorithm mismatch in software and hardware, valid TCP connections may get rejected with "No flow found for ACK' reset-cause when the hardware SYN cookie mode is active.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP iSeries appliances with ePVA support and the B2250 and B44xx VIPRION blades. - Hardware SYN cookie mode is activated.
bugs.impact: Service degradation.
bugs.workaround: - Disable the hardware SYN cookie mode globally. - After a reboot, restart the TMM for an additional time.
bugs.fix: The SYN cookie hash algorithm is correctly selected on all TMMs.

bugs.title: Remove the occurrence of Shape in the BIG-IP Bot Defense configuration
bugs.symptoms: In GUI, the term Shape is available in the BD profile configuration.
bugs.conditions: - Configuring Bot Defense profile.
bugs.fix: The term "Shape" is replaced with applicable term in Bot Defense profile page.

bugs.title: Need for additional space as separator for different methods in Protected URI field
bugs.symptoms: In GUI, while configuring Bot Defense profile, need more space as separator for different methods in Protected URI field.
bugs.conditions: - Bot Defense profile configuration.
bugs.fix: Added additional space in method selection for better visibility in Protected URI field.

bugs.title: Unable to resize the /appdata: /dev/mapper/vg--db--sda-dat.appdata when in use
bugs.symptoms: On systems where ID1004833 has been fixed, the resizing instructions for /appdata from K74200262 no longer work.

Load the config. # tmsh (tmos) # load sys config from-terminal merge (tmos) # save sys config Paste the pi_diameter profile config copied in step c. CTRL-D (maybe twice) to submit the change. f) Check the config via tmsh. The action value has changed. (tmos) # list security protocol-inspection profile pi_diameter Use case 2: a) Configure protocol-inspection profiles for http, diameter, and gtp. Set all "accept" including signatures and compliances. b) tmsh save sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh save sys config file ips_test.scf no-passphrase. c) tmsh load sys config default. d) tmsh load sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh load sys config file ips_test.scf. Use case 3: Restore configuration by loading UCS/SCF after RMA. Use case 4: Perform mcpd forceload for some purpose. Use case 5: Change VM memory size or number of core on hypervisor. bugs.impact: Some of the signatures and compliance action values are changed Following commands output lists affected signatures and compliances. ## Signatures ## tmsh list sec protocol-inspection signature all-properties | egrep "protocol-inspection|^＼s*action" | awk '{ if($2 == "drop" || $2 == "reject") { print prev"＼n"$0 } } { prev = $0 }' ## Compliances ## tmsh list sec protocol-inspection compliance all-properties | egrep "protocol-inspection|^＼s*action" | awk '{ if($2 == "drop" || $2 == "reject") { print prev"＼n"$0 } } { prev = $0 }'
bugs.workaround: Workaround for use case 1: Follow the work-around mention below when you want to load the ips profile configuration from the terminal. a) Create a protocol-inspection profile. GUI: Security ›› Protocol Security: Inspection Profiles -> Click "Add" >> "New" >> ips_testing b) Check the current config via tmsh. # tmsh list security protocol-inspection profile ips_testing all-properties c) Copy the result of the command in step b. d) Delete the profile. # tmsh delete security protocol-inspection profile ips_testing e) Load the config. # tmsh (tmos) # load sys config from-terminal merge (tmos) # save sys config Paste the pi_diameter profile config copied in step c. CTRL-D (maybe twice) to submit the change. f) Check the config via tmsh using all-properties (tmos) # list security protocol-inspection profile ips_testing all-properties Workaround for use case 2: a) Configure protocol-inspection profiles for http, diameter, and gtp. Set all "accept" including signatures and compliances. b) tmsh save sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh save sys config file ips_test.scf no-passphrase c) tmsh load sys config default d) tmsh load sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh load sys config file ips_test.scf e) tmsh load sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh load sys config file ips_test.scf Workaround for use case 3: a) Load the ucs/scf config file twice. tmsh load sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh load sys config file ips_test.scf Workaround for use case 4, 5, 6: a) Before performing any of the operations of Use case 4, 5, 6, save the config. tmsh save sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh save sys config file ips_test.scf no-passphrase b) Once the operation in use cases are done then perform the load operation. tmsh load sys ucs ips_test.ucs or tmsh load sys config file ips_test.scf

bugs.title: VXLAN tunnels fail to pass traffic after TMM restarts
bugs.symptoms: After TMM restarts (or the tenant reboots), VXLAN tunnels will not pass traffic. The administrator may see messages such as the following in /var/log/tmm: notice MCP message handling failed in 0x9ce140 (16977920): May 26 14:07:19 on 1 - MCP Message: notice create { notice l2_forward_tunnel { notice l2_forward_tunnel_vlan_name "/Common/vxlan-tunnel"
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP tenant running on rSeries appliance or VELOS chassis -- VXLAN tunnels
bugs.impact: VXLAN tunnels do not function.
bugs.workaround: After TMM restarts, delete and recreate the FDB entries associated with the tunnel. To do this manually, run these commands: TMPFILE=$(mktemp -p /var/tmp) tmsh list net fdb tunnel all one-line > "$TMPFILE" tmsh delete net fdb tunnel all all-records tmsh load sys config merge file "$TMPFILE" rm -f "$TMPFILE" Or a one-line command: TMPFILE=$(mktemp -p /var/tmp) && tmsh list net fdb tunnel all one-line > "$TMPFILE" && tmsh delete net fdb tunnel all all-records && tmsh load sys config merge file "$TMPFILE" && rm -f "$TMPFILE" To configure the system to automatically apply the workaround after TMM restarts, put the following content into /config/user_alert.conf: # Delete and re-add tunnel FDBs after TMM starts up to work-around ID1122313 alert tmm_vxlan_workaround "Tmm ready - links up" { exec command="TMPFILE=$(mktemp -p /var/tmp) && tmsh list net fdb tunnel all one-line > $TMPFILE && tmsh delete net fdb tunnel all all-records && tmsh load sys config merge file $TMPFILE && rm -f $TMPFILE"; }

bugs.title: If-Modified-Since always returns 304 response if there is no last-modified header in the server response
bugs.symptoms: Requests sent with an If-Modified-Since header always return a 304 Not Modified response
bugs.conditions: The Last Modified header is not included in the origin server response headers.
bugs.impact: When the Last Modified header is not present in the response, its default value i.e., Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT, is used and 304 Not Modified is sent to the client.
bugs.workaround: Add the Last-Modified header to the response headers using iRule when HTTP_RESPONSE priority 1 { set time [clock format [clock seconds] -gmt 1 -format "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %Z"] HTTP::header insert Last-Modified $time log local0.debug "Inserting Last-Modified header as $time" }
bugs.fix: Use date header value when Last-Modified is not present in Response headers

bugs.title: A specific type of software installation may fail to carry forward the management port's default gateway.
bugs.symptoms: After performing a specific type of software installation, the unit returns on-line without the management port's default gateway.
bugs.conditions: -- A software installation that does not carry forward the entirety of the BIG-IP system's configuration is performed. For example, this is achieved by running "image2disk --format=volumes <...>", or by using the live-install subsystem after disabling the liveinstall.saveconfig and liveinstall.moveconfig db keys. This type of installation, however, does carry forward the management port's configuration (IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway). -- In addition to the default gateway, the management port is configured with additional static routes (for example, to a log server, dns server, etc.). -- When mcpd is queried for the management routes, the default gateway is not the first entry in mcpd's reply (this is something outside of your control that entirely depends on the name of the objects and how the config was loaded).
bugs.impact: On Virtual Edition systems, this issue coupled with the removal of autolasthop from the management port means you will not be able to connect to the BIG-IP system's management port from non-directly connected clients after the installation. On all systems, this issue means the BIG-IP system will not be able to initiate connections to non-directly connected systems over the management port after the installation. Note: If the system is configured for dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) this issue can affect either (or both) stack.
bugs.workaround: After the issue has occurred, you can connect to the affected BIG-IP system by means of serial console or video console and apply the default gateway again. If you are trying to prevent this issue, you can remove all management routes except the default one before performing this type of installation.
bugs.fix: The issue has been corrected; this specific type of software installation now correctly carries forward the management port's default gateway.

bugs.title: Wideip fails to display or delete in the Link Controller GUI.
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to display (i.e. click on) a WideIP in the Link Controller GUI returns an error similar to the following example: General error: Error parsing value of "null" of type "gtm_qtype_t" in statement [SELECT SINGLE *, gtm_pool.name as pool_name FROM gtm_wideip, gtm_pool WHERE (name = '/Common/example.com' AND type = '1' AND pool_name = 'null' AND pool_type = 'null')] Attempting to delete a Wideip in the Link Controller GUI returns an error similar to the following example (and the delete operation fails): 01020036:3: The requested Pool (A /Common/example.com) was not found.
bugs.conditions: -- Link Controller system. -- The Wideip in question has no associated Pool. This is likely the result of improperly creating the Wideip via the tmsh utility, or upgrading the system from an earlier version which caused your configuration to be automatically fixed up (such as creating distinct A and AAAA Wideips from an earlier unique Wideip entry).
bugs.impact: The GUI cannot be used to display or delete the Wideip.
bugs.workaround: Link Controller, unlike GTM, does not expose the concept of Pools. Link Controller only exposes WideIPs and Virtual Servers. Pools exist, but are managed automatically by the system on your behalf. If a WideIPs created using the GUI, the WideIP will be assigned a Pool of the same type and name automatically. This also happens if you initially decide to assign no Virtual Servers to the WideIP (and things work as intended in the BIG-IP GUI). However, the tmsh utility is not aligned with this Link Controller requirement, and allows you to create WideIPs with no associated Pool. If you have experienced this issue: 1) Deleted the affected WideIP using the tmsh utility. 2a) Going forward, use the GUI to define more Link Controller WideIPs. 2b) Alternatively, if you must use the tmsh utility to do so, ensure each WideIP you create is assigned an identically named Pool of the same type, even if initially you decide to place no Virtual Servers in the Pool. For example, define something like the following: gtm pool a /Common/example.com { } gtm wideip a /Common/example.com { pools { /Common/example.com { order 0 } } }

bugs.symptoms: When client authentication is enabled on the client SSL profile but the trusted-ca file includes only an intermediate certificate and no CA root cert to build the whole cert chain, although the TLS connection is made, as expected, there is an error message reported following. Jun 21 20:43:01 bigip warning tmm6[18125]: 01260006:4: Peer cert verify error: unable to get issuer certificate (depth 1; cert /CN=subca) Jun 21 20:43:01 bigip warning tmm6[18125]: 01260005:4: Unable to get certificate for peer cert issuer /CN=rootca
bugs.conditions: Trusted-ca includes only inter-cert and no root CA-cert is configured.
bugs.impact: Although the TLS handshake succeeds without any issue and the connection is processed, as expected, a confusing warning is reported.
bugs.workaround: Because the connection is made, you can safely ignore this message. Note: This issue does not occur if the root CA cert is also configured in the CA-cert bundle.

bugs.title: BD crash with a specific request
bugs.symptoms: BD crash occurs.
bugs.conditions: - TMOS versions of v14.1.x and v13.1.x that have the fix for bug ID 1061617:: https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1061617.html . - Additional undisclosed condition. Note: Versions 15.x and later are not affected, regardless of whether or not the software contains the fix for bug ID 1061617 https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1061617.html .
bugs.impact: The bd process crashes, causing the unit to fail over or go offline briefly. ASM traffic is disrupted while bd restarts.

bugs.title: DOS, Auto Thresholds, and DNS thresholds are not updating for Fully Automatic method
bugs.symptoms: Auto Thresholds are not updating correctly when the traffic is going on, as a result it will not mitigate the traffic.
bugs.conditions: - Send any DNS specific query. - Thresholds are not updating properly.
bugs.impact: Cannot mitigate the traffic.

bugs.title: Add nameserver-min-rtt (infra-cache-min-rtt) feature support for DNS validating resolver cache
bugs.symptoms: - A DNS Validating resolver returns SERVFAIL responses to clients, despite the BIG-IP system receiving a valid (albeit delayed) response from upstream servers. - When this happens, the BIG-IP system rejects the responses from the upstream servers with following ICMP error: Destination unreachable - Port unreachable. - If the db key dnscacheresolver.loglevel is set to debug5, the following error message is visible in the /var/log/ltm file when this issue occurs: debug tmm[13147]: DNScache: request example.com. has exceeded the maximum number of glue fetches 17 to a single delegation point
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: - A DNS Validating resolver is in use on the BIG-IP system. - The aforementioned object is configured with a forward-zone that uses multiple servers to perform resolutions. - The RTT of the servers fluctuates. For example, the servers are generally fast to reply for most domains, but take extra time to reply for a given domain. - 'Randomize Query Character Case' is enabled in the DNS Validating resolver. - If the requests for the domain take a long time to resolve, BIG-IP may reply with SERVFAIL.
bugs.impact: Clients of the BIG-IP DNS Validating Resolver are not returned an answer. As a result, application failures may occur.
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by changing 'Randomize Query Character Case' to 'No' in the DNS Validating resolver settings.
bugs.fix: The nameserver-min-rtt now has a setting of unbound which sets the minimum RTT with upstream servers for validating resolver cache. Increase this value if using forwarders need more time to perform recursive name resolution. The default value is 50 ms.
bugs.behavior: The nameserver-min-rtt setting is now available. This setting sets the minimum RTT with upstream servers for DNS Validating resolver objects. Increase the value if using forwarders need more time to perform recursive name resolution. The default value is 50 ms.

bugs.title: OWASP scores and configuration not synced to standby in vCMP cluster setup
bugs.symptoms: When vCMP guests are configured for high availability (HA), the changes in OWASP configuration on the active device is not synced with the standby device as expected.
bugs.conditions: 1. vCMP guests are configured for high availability (HA) 2. Make changes in OWASP configuration in Security ›› Overview : OWASP Compliance screen (In the Active machine)
bugs.impact: Configuration changes are not synced to the standby device.

bugs.title: Wrong server-side window scale used in hardware SYN cookie mode
bugs.symptoms: Client enables Window Scale in the first SYN packet with a specific factor value, however the BIG-IP system disables Window Scale in its SYN/ACK response. Instead, disabling the Window Scale TCP option in both peer BIG-IPs, TMM honors the Window Scale presented by the client in the first SYN, whereas client assumes Window Scale is disabled. This will cause BIG-IP to send data payload bytes exceeding the client's Windows Size.
bugs.conditions: Below conditions must be met in order to match this issue: - Client and server enables timestamp TCP option. - Client enables Window Scale TCP option. - SYN Cookie HW is activated in BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: This can cause performance issues because some packets could need to be retransmitted. In rare cases where client TCP stack is configured to abort connection when it receives window overflow the connection will be RST by client.
bugs.workaround: The preferred workaround is changing to Software SYN Cookie mode.
bugs.fix: Correct server-side Window Scale behavior is provided when: - Client and server enables timestamp TCP option - Client enables Window Scale TCP option - SYN Cookie HW is activated in BIG-IP

bugs.title: TCP options are disabled while hardware SYN cookie is active
bugs.symptoms: TCP options are not included in the SYN/ACK packet generated by hardware while hardware SYN cookie mode is active.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS or rSeries platform - Hardware SYN cookie is activated on a virtual server
bugs.impact: Minor performance impact on the connections of the related virtual server.
bugs.fix: The TCP options are enabled in SYN/ACK packets generated by hardware.

bugs.title: The iControl REST API does not accept an empty 'lastResortPool' property for wide IP objects.
bugs.symptoms: If you attempt a POST or PATCH iControl REST request against a wide IP, and you include an empty 'lastResortPool' property in the JSON body, the system rejects the request as invalid and returns the following validation error: { "code": 400, "message": "＼"last-resort-pool＼" requires a value", "errorStack": [], "apiError": 26214401 }
bugs.conditions: A POST or PATCH command against a wide IP object includes an empty lastResortPool property.
bugs.impact: Inability to create or modify the wide IP object.
bugs.workaround: You can use either of the following, depending on what you want to do: -- To create a new wide IP object, remove the empty 'lastResortPool' property from the JSON body. -- To remove the last-resort-pool from an already existing wide IP, define the property as follows instead: "lastResortPool":"none"

bugs.title: DNSSEC Key creation failure with internal FIPS card.
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to create dnssec keys that use the internal FIPS HSM. When this issue happens the following error messages appear in /var/log/gtm Jul 20 04:37:47 localhost failed to read password encryption key from the file /shared/fips/nfbe0/pek.key_1, error 40000229 Jul 20 04:37:47 localhost.localdomain err gtmd[28729]: 011a0312:3: Failed to initiate session with FIPS card. Jul 20 04:37:47 localhost.localdomain err gtmd[28729]: 011a0309:3: Failed to create new DNSSEC Key Generation /Common/abcd:1 due to HSM error.
bugs.conditions: -- Internal FIPS card present. -- Clean installation from an installation ISO file. -- DNSSKEY creation using internal FIPS card.
bugs.impact: DNSSEC deployments with internal FIPS HSMs are impacted.
bugs.workaround: Change the /shared/fips directory permissions. Ex: chmod 700 /shared/fips

bugs.title: BGP route advertisement might be delayed after graceful restart for peers configured with advertisement interval set to 0
bugs.symptoms: BGP routes are not immediately advertised after a graceful restart. This results in unexpected delays in route advertisement, leading to slower network convergence than anticipated
bugs.conditions: - BGP is configured with graceful restart enabled - BGP peers have the advertisement interval set to 0
bugs.impact: Route advertisement delays can affect network convergence time and potentially impact traffic routing during BGP graceful restart scenarios The issue is related to improper handling of the peer End-of-RIB (EOR) list during graceful restart when the advertisement interval is set to 0
bugs.workaround: Consider changing the advertisement interval to a number other than 0
bugs.fix: BGP now properly handles the peer EOR list during graceful restart

bugs.title: ZebOS "no log syslog" configuration is not surviving reboot
bugs.symptoms: ZebOS "log syslog" or "no log syslog" are not surviving reboot according to the user performed operations. Always revert to default setting, which is enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Under Configure no log syslog. -- Perform reboot or upgrade.
bugs.impact: If syslog logging has been disabled using 'no log syslog', and then ZebOS is restarted. For example, by rebooting or upgrading the BIG-IP, syslog logging will revert to the default setting, which is enabled.

bugs.title: TMM might crash with certain HTTP traffic
bugs.symptoms: The TMM restarts and generates a core file.

bugs.impact: The TMM restarts and generates a core file. The BIG-IP system will fail-over or traffic will be interrupted.
bugs.fix: The TMM process traffic as expected.

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator with explicit proxy mode with proxy chaining enabled fails to send the CONNECT
bugs.symptoms: SSL Orchestrator sends a TLS client hello instead of the expected HTTP CONNECT, leading to a failure in the client environment after an upgrade.

bugs.impact: The exit proxy gives an HTTP 5xx error in response to the unexpected TLS Client Hello.

bugs.title: Variables are not displayed in Debug log messages for MGMT network firewall rules

bugs.title: BD process crash
bugs.symptoms: BD process restarts with a core file.
bugs.conditions: Unknown
bugs.impact: The unit goes offline for a short period of time.
bugs.fix: A sanity check has been added in order to avoid possible crash.

bugs.symptoms: BGP daemon might core when route dampening is configured.
bugs.conditions: -- bgp configured -- route dampening is configured
bugs.impact: Unexpected process restart.
bugs.workaround: BGP dampening feature can be disabled to avoid unexpected process restarts.

bugs.title: HSB and switch pause frames impact data traffic
bugs.symptoms: There are cases where the HSB and switch report pause frames on the HSB <-> switch interfaces. This can be seen in the switch interface stats: name counters.rx_pause ---- ----------------- 9.1 11522051 10.1 11392101
bugs.conditions: The iSeries platforms with an HSB and switch.
bugs.impact: There can be an impact on networking traffic.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround for this issue. When this condition happens, the unit needs to be rebooted to clear the issue.

bugs.title: Connections over IPsec fail when hardware acceleration in fastl4 is enabled
bugs.symptoms: Connection setup fails through IPsec tunnel.
bugs.conditions: - rSeries and VELOS platform. - PVA acceleration is enabled in the fastL4 profile of the IPsec virtual on the responder BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: Connections through the IPsec tunnel do not work.
bugs.workaround: Disable PVA acceleration in the relevant fastL4 profile. PVA acceleration cannot be performed on flows going into or coming out of IPsec. This workaround returns the functionality as it was designed. F5 recommends creating Virtual Servers to specifically catch flows that go over IPsec tunnels. If a generic Virtual Server uses a fastL4 profile with acceleration disabled, then non-IPsec flows that could be accelerated will not be.

bugs.title: Performance improvement for ASM signature engine
bugs.symptoms: Bot Defense (BD) consumes high CPU power when processing signatures on headers.
bugs.conditions: Header signatures are enabled on policy.
bugs.impact: BD consumes high CPU power when processing header signatures.
bugs.fix: A header-policy-signature cache is added which improves performance. A few additional changes are implemented which enables faster lookup of signature data.

bugs.title: Provide caution banner when the system integrity check fails from daily anacron job
bugs.symptoms: When the anacron job /etc/cron.daily/integritycheck fails, the failure is logged only to /var/log/secure which might not be easily visible to the user.

bugs.impact: User might not be aware of the system integrity failure and the system will halt or brick on the next reboot.
bugs.fix: If the anacron job integrity check fails, then during the next login a caution is displayed to the user with the message "FIPS SYSTEM VALIDATION FAILED, CHECK /var/log/secure FOR DETAILS" on both Configuration utility and TMSH.

bugs.title: Increase "/shared" directory size on VELOS tenants from 15 GB

bugs.impact: Core file is corrupted.
bugs.workaround: Increase the size of the directory "/shared" from TMOS.

bugs.title: TMM CPU usage statistics may show a lower than expected value on Virtual Edition

bugs.title: Attack Signature in authorization header with base64 is not detected

bugs.conditions: If authorization header type is Bearer and base64 violations are not configured as blocking.
bugs.impact: Signature matching is skipped.
bugs.workaround: Illegal base64 value violation should be set to blocking. If base64 decoding fails, then the requests are blocked.
bugs.fix: ASM now processes signature as expected.

bugs.title: Neuron client constantly logs errors when TCAM database is full
bugs.symptoms: A database held in hardware (TCAM), shared between tenants, has a limit that is exceeded by software in tenants that adds and manages entries in the database. Symptomatic logs on tenant: in /var/log/ltm, repeating logs are recorded, following is an example: err tmm[635]: 01010331:3: Neuron client neuron_client_pva_hwl failed with rule request submit(client connection is busy (has outstanding requests)) in /var/log/tmm, cycles of following group of logs are recorded: notice neuron_client_negotiate: Neuron client connection established notice [DDOS Neuron]Neuron daemon started notice hudproxy_neuron_client_closed_cb: Neuron client connection terminated notice [DDOS Neuron]Neuron daemon stopped For F5OS host, in partition /var/F5/partitionX/log/velos.log repeating logs are recorded, following is an example: tcam-manager[41]: priority="Err" version=1.0 msgid=0x6b01000000000007 msg="ERROR" MSG="TCAM processing Error(-5) executing:TCAM_INSERT for ruleno:0x20000000937" In the log message, the msgid and ruleno can vary, but the Error(-5) is an indication of this issue.

bugs.impact: The neuron client software will restart and log repeatedly. Inefficient use of TCAM database.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: TMM core when IPsec tunnel object is reconfigured
bugs.symptoms: TMM may core when a "tunnel tunnels" object related to an IPsec interface is reconfigured. For example, a command that changes the IP address of the object may lead to a core: # tmsh modify net tunnels tunnel my-ipsec-tunnel remote-address 1.2.3.4
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec IKEv1 or IKEv2. -- Tunnel is in "interface" mode. -- Tunnel object is reconfigured while the tunnel is up.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Ensure the tunnel is down before reconfiguring it. -- Set the IKE-Peer config state to disabled. -- Delete an established IKE SA and IPsec SA related to that peer. For example: # tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer <Name> state disabled # tmsh delete net ipsec ike-sa peer-ip <IP> # tmsh delete net ipsec ipsec-sa dst-addr <IP> "Name" is the specific name given to the ike-peer config object. "IP" is the address configured to use for the remote peer. Then make the desired changes and enable the IKE-Peer. # tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer <name> state enabled
