bugs.conditions: The conditions that trigger this issue post-upgrade are unknown at this time and the occurrence is rare.
bugs.impact: Requests get blocked with an 'Illegal URL' violation despite the it being defined as an Allowed URL because the URL object's Content-Profile reference does not get inserted and is missing in the MySQL database post-upgrade.
bugs.workaround: - Delete the problematic URL within the 'Security ›› Application Security : URLs : Allowed URLs : Allowed HTTP URLs' section in Configuration Utility. - Re-create the URL again. - Save the changes with the 'Apply Policy' task.

bugs.title: Illegal file type is enabled in Rapid Deployment Template.
bugs.symptoms: The Rapid Deployment Template has a list of illegal filetypes and did not have the Illegal File Type violation enabled, by default.
bugs.conditions: A new policy is created based on the Rapid Deployment Template.
bugs.impact: Protection against Illegal File Type browsing is missing, by default.
bugs.workaround: The violation can be enabled, if required, on any existing policies.
bugs.fix: The new policies created based on the Rapid Deployment Template will have the Illegal File Type violation enabled, by default.

bugs.title: User-generated SSH identity breaks multi-bladed REST storage sync
bugs.symptoms: If the user generates their own SSH key on a multi-bladed system, the restjavad storage sync between the primary slot and secondary slots fails. This happens because the system attempts to use this private key to authenticate to the secondary slots but the secondary slots do not have the matching public key in their authorized_keys file, so authentication falls back to password auth, which ultimately fails.
bugs.conditions: The user generates their own SSH key pair with a default name of id_[rsa|dsa|ecdsa|ed25519] and stores it in /root/.ssh on a multi-bladed system.
bugs.impact: Users will not be able to generate their own SSH keys on multi-bladed systems since the restjavad storage sync between the primary slot and secondary slots will fail.

bugs.title: BD continuously restarting after upgrade to 17.1.0.1
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading a previously working BIG-IP system, ASM restarts repeatedly and the system will not process ASM traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- An upgrade was performed -- One or more virtual server names is longer than 64 characters.
bugs.impact: Repeated ASM restarts (ASM restarts in loop).
bugs.workaround: Change the virtual server name to be shorter than 64 characters.
bugs.fix: No ASM restart loop for virtual server with a name longer than 64 characters.

bugs.title: Bot Defense can crash when using SMTP security profile
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, Bot Defense can crash when SMTP security profile is being used.
bugs.conditions: - SMTP security profile is configured and applied with DNS check on. - SPF record cannot be resolved by DNS servers.
bugs.impact: BD crashes leading to disruption of traffic.
bugs.fix: BD does not crash when using SMTP security profile.

bugs.title: SMTP requests are dropped by ASM under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: When virus check is enabled on SMTP security profile, sometimes ASM drops the request even though no violation is reported.
bugs.conditions: - SMTP security profile is configured and applied with virus check on. - ICAP server is configured
bugs.impact: ASM sometimes drops valid SMTP requests even when no violation is reported.
bugs.fix: SMTP requests are now processed.

bugs.title: "fipsutil fwcheck -f" command may not correct result
bugs.symptoms: The "fipsutil fwcheck -f" command output shows as "Firmware upgrade available." even though now Firmware upgrade is not needed.
bugs.conditions: All FIPS platforms.
bugs.impact: Only a display issue with no functional impact. If we try to make a firmware upgrade, it may not work.
bugs.workaround: Use the command without the "-f" option like "fipsutil fwcheck".

bugs.title: Missing GTM probes on GTM server when an external monitor is attached to an additional pool
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect probe behavior when an external monitor is attached to an additional pool.
bugs.conditions: On a GTM sync group, try to attach an external monitor to an additional pool.
bugs.impact: Incorrect GTM server monitoring.

bugs.title: Tmsh and gui errors when checking tmm memory
bugs.symptoms: Checking statistics in the GUI (Statistics ›› Module Statistics : Memory ) may result in "As error has occurred while trying to process your request." Checking memory via tmsh may show invalid values for tmm's memory usage: # tmsh show sys memory | grep nan TMM Memory Used -nan -nan -nan
bugs.conditions: When the files in /var/tmstat/blade/ exceed 4GB. This could be to a large number of tmms or due to an extremely large config.
bugs.impact: Tmm memory stats may be zero, or may be half the size they should be.
bugs.workaround: Check tmm's memory using tmctl instead: tmctl tmm_stat -s cpu,memory_total,memory_used Or reduce the size of the config and restart tmm.

bugs.title: When END_STREAM is delayed, HTTP detects a Content-Length header and raises HUDEVT_RESPONSE_DONE before HTTP/2 raises HUDEVT_RESPONSE_DONE
bugs.symptoms: A RST_STREAM is observed from BIG-IP to server after receiving response from server.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP/2 full proxy configuration. - Server to send a DATA_FRAME with END_STREAM flag with a delay.
bugs.impact: Once the server gets around to process the RST_STREAM, it stops accepting new requests on that connection.
bugs.fix: The message HUDEVT_RESPONSE_DONE is delayed until the HTTP completes EV_BODY_COMPLETE action.

bugs.title: Icons displayed on webtop are different from Storefront server when modified
bugs.symptoms: When custom higher resolution images for Citrix resources are edited/modified to 32x32 pixels, they appear blurred on the APM webtop.
bugs.conditions: When higher resolution images are modified to 32x32 pixels
bugs.impact: Icons appear blurred on the APM webtop.
bugs.workaround: Default icon images provided by the Storefront can be used as they are displayed correctly on the APM webtop.

bugs.title: Traffic-group ID may not be updated properly on a TMM listener
bugs.symptoms: A few virtual servers may belong to incorrect traffic-group after a full sync or when mcp transaction is performed.
bugs.conditions: - The BIG-IP High Availability (HA) is configured with full load on sync. - Traffic-group is changed on a virtual-address belonging to multiple virtuals. - Sync happens, leaving the device receiving a sync in an incorrect state. OR An MCP transaction that is updating a virtual-address along with a profile change on a virtual-server is executed.
bugs.impact: Listeners may not belong to a correct traffic group and the the traffic is not forwarded.
bugs.workaround: Use an incremental sync. Do not use MCP transactions.

bugs.title: Lsn_pick_request_new_out and lsn_pick_response_new_out cmp stats incremented twice for one request
bugs.symptoms: Lsn_pick_response_new_out value becomes twice the value of lsn_pick_response_new_in lsn_pick_request_new_out value becomes twice the value of lsn_pick_request_new_in
bugs.conditions: 1. Dynamic Pat and PBA configured 2. Make remote TMM requests for LSN pick
bugs.impact: Incorrect stats.

bugs.title: The BIG-IP system's time zone database does not reflect recent changes implemented by Mexico in regard to DST
bugs.symptoms: In fall of 2023, Mexico is cancelling DST (Daylight Saving Time) and is now on standard time indefinitely. The BIG-IP time zone database need an updated to reflect this change.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IPs operated in Mexico.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP systems configured to use "America/Mexico" (or other applicable Mexican localities) will still apply DST. Hence, time will spring forward and backward on previously designated dates. This will have no impact to application traffic handled by the BIG-IP system. However, logs, alerts, reports, cron jobs, and other will use incorrect time.
bugs.workaround: As a workaround, you can set the BIG-IP time zone to that of a different country with the same UTC offset and already not observing DST.

bugs.title: Logging suspicious vector feature is not supported for tcp-flags-uncommon vector on upgrade to BIG-IP 17.1.0
bugs.symptoms: The following log is observed in the console or /var/log/ltm logs: Logging 01071d5e:3: DOS attack data (tcp-flags-uncommon): Suspicious vector feature is not supported for tcp-flags-uncommon vector. If this is after an upgrade it's likely the configuration will fail to load, which in turn will cause memory provisioning not to complete leaving the system provisioned for LTM only. This may leave insufficient 4KB page memory for the actual provisioning, for example if ASM is provisioned. The unit may show low memory symptoms such as oom killer activity, unresponsive management, cores due to daemon heartbeat timeout.
bugs.conditions: 1. The Only Count Suspicious Events option is enabled or the attribute suspicious is true on TCP Push Flood vector. 2. Upgrade to BIG-IP 17.1.0.
bugs.impact: The following log is observed in the console or /var/log/ltm logs: Logging 01071d5e:3: DOS attack data (tcp-flags-uncommon): Suspicious vector feature is not supported for tcp-flags-uncommon vector. in the console or /var/log/ltm Failure to load configuration may be shown a few lines later: emerg load_config_files[13166]: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g -a load sys config partitions all " - failed.
bugs.workaround: 1. Confirm config: grep "suspicious true" /config/bigip.conf 2. Backup bigip.conf: cp /config/bigip.conf /config/bigip.conf.bak_ID1282029 3. Change affected configuration values: sed -i 's/suspicious true/suspicious false/g' /config/bigip.conf 4. Reload MCPD per K13030. AFM comes back up with config loaded fine.

bugs.title: Assertion response attributes parsing issue after upgrade to BIG-IP 17.1.0
bugs.symptoms: During SAML Authentication while TMM parses the assertion to extract the attributes and its respective values, all the attributes values are combined into a single string with '|' as separator and are assigned to a single variable leaving remaining ones empty.
bugs.conditions: When the incoming attributes, in the assertion, are considered as multi-valued attributes, all the values of attributes are combined to form a single valued attribute in order to store in the SessionDB.
bugs.impact: All the session variables related to assertion attributes are assigned and stored incorrectly. Related IDs: ID1282105 at https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1282105.html ID1353021 at https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1353021.html ID1354673 at https://cdn.f5.com/product/bugtracker/ID1354673.html

bugs.title: High CPU or increased translation errors following upgrade or restart when DAG distribution changes
bugs.symptoms: Dagv2 tables are randomized and may change when a tmm is restarted. This can result in a change of traffic distribution, which in some cases may lead to traffic disruption. The specific condition when this option was introduced is using a CGNAT pool that is not large enough. Other ways of encountering include increased translation failed errors following an upgrade or restart or blade replacement.
bugs.conditions: - tmm is restarted (or chassis rebooted)
bugs.impact: - dag distribution changes which may cause a traffic disruption.
bugs.workaround: You can restart tmm until the distribution is good, which can be checked using tools like cmp_dest.
bugs.fix: Added a DB variable to control dagv2 behavior. A tmm restart is required after locking the new dag tables.
bugs.behavior: A new DB variable is available that allows you to lock the current dagv2 tables: tmsh modify sys db dag.dagv2.pgs value $(tmctl -d blade -q -L 1 tmm/daglib_dagv2_pgs -s table) tmsh modify sys db dag.dagv2.hsbs value $(tmctl -d blade -q -L 1 tmm/daglib_dagv2_hsbs -s table) tmsh modify sys db dag.dagv2.mirror.pgs value $(tmctl -d blade -q -L 1 tmm/daglib_dagv2_mirror_pgs -s table) tmsh modify sys db dag.dagv2.mirror.hsbs value $(tmctl -d blade -q -L 1 tmm/daglib_dagv2_mirror_hsbs -s table) It's important to store both normal and mirroring tables because of internal dag workings. The change also requires cmp state to be the same as defined in tables - this is important in case a blade is lost etc. This also works on SP DAG in LSN NAPT deployments

bugs.title: Missing NAT46/64 offload support on F5OS platforms
bugs.symptoms: Hardware offload of NAT46/64 flows are not supported on F5OS platforms.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS platform. - Mixed IP version on client- and server-side.
bugs.impact: No hardware acceleration.
bugs.fix: NAT46/64 flows are now offloaded.

bugs.title: Roll forward upgrade fails with policy that has unapplied changes and Threat Campaigns
bugs.symptoms: Roll forward upgrade fails. The following error message in /ts/log/ts_debug.log and WAF enforcement is not complete: ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Can't locate object method "id_field" via package "F5::ASMConfig::Entity::ThreatCampaign" (perhaps you forgot to load "F5::ASMConfig::Entity::ThreatCampaign"?) at /usr/local/share/perl5/F5/ImportExportPolicy/Binary.pm line 2171. ----------------------------------------------------------------------
bugs.conditions: - Roll forward upgrade when there is a policy that has unapplied changes and Threat Campaigns.
bugs.impact: Incorrect enforcement until workaround is applied.
bugs.workaround: Perform an apply policy operation on all policies.
bugs.fix: Roll forward upgrade is successful.

bugs.title: Double HTTP::disable can lead to tmm core
bugs.symptoms: Calling the HTTP::disable command more than once in an irule can result in the tmm process crashing.
bugs.conditions: ->Basic http configuration -> iRule when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { set collects 0 TCP::collect } when CLIENT_DATA { if { $collects eq 1 } { HTTP::disable HTTP::disable } TCP::release TCP::collect incr collects } when HTTP_REQUEST { log local0. "Request" } when HTTP_DISABLED { log local0. "Disabled" }
bugs.impact: BIG-IP may crash during an HTTP CONNECT request from a client.
bugs.workaround: Avoid calling HTTP::disable more than once per connflow
bugs.fix: Treat disable via iRule as a NOP when a disable is in progress

bugs.title: IS-IS protocol may discard Multi-Topology Reachable IPv6 Prefixes
bugs.symptoms: IS-IS protocol on the BIG-IP might discard some Multi-Topology Reachable IPv6 Prefixes.
bugs.conditions: This happens when the IS-IS device in the BIG-IP system is peering with RFC 7794 support for sub-TLVs.
bugs.impact: Some prefixes are incorrectly installed in a routing table.

bugs.title: Redirections on the lowest numbered blade in mirroring configuration.
bugs.symptoms: Incorrect DAG context mirroring causes redirections on the lowest numbered blade.
bugs.conditions: - B4460 platform. - Mirroring is enabled. - Failover is performed.
bugs.impact: The lowest numbered blade is redirecting packets, which can be checked by executing `tmctl -d blade tmm/flow_redir_stats`. It can cause traffic disruption/performance loss.
bugs.fix: Fixed incorrect DAG context mirroring causing redirections on the lowest numbered blade.

bugs.title: Tmsh reset-stats net interface does not work on VIPRION blade management interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Resetting the stats of the management interface on a VIPRION blade will not have any effect. Example: # tmsh reset-stats net interface -hidden # tmsh show net interface -hidden raw | grep mgmt 1/mgmt up 2480987952 481888512 2446417 156900 0 0 1000T-FD
bugs.conditions: This only applies for VIPRION blades.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic.
bugs.workaround: Users using an SNMP, SIEM, or log collector client to monitor the management interface statistics will need to adjust their settings to use delta counters.

bugs.title: Localdb user can change the password of other user
bugs.symptoms: The user was able to change the password for another user in the logon page, when local DB authentication was used.
bugs.conditions: -- At least one user in the local DB instance is forced to change the password -- the virtual server is tied in with the trusted CA certificates (that is, it would not happen if the virtual server for the SSL-VPN is associated with self-signed certificates).
bugs.impact: User authentication based on local DB will be impacted.

bugs.title: DTLS1.2 Handshakes are causing tmm crash with mTLS connection
bugs.symptoms: TMM crash will be observed during the DTLS1.2 handshake.
bugs.conditions: ServerSSL profile configured with, - key and certificate. - ssl-sign-hash value is Any A backend server configured with DTLS1.2 protocol and enabled client authentication.
bugs.impact: TMM will crash for each DTLS1.2 handshake.
bugs.workaround: In serverSSL profile, select the ssl-sign-hash to SHA-256.
bugs.fix: DTLS1.2 handshakes perform as expected.

bugs.title: TMM core when removing an entry at 'sipmsg_queue_remove'
bugs.symptoms: TMM core when removing an entry from sipmsg_queue in 'sipmsg_queue_remove' routine.
bugs.conditions: The entries in the sipmsg_queue are corrupted.
bugs.impact: TMM core
bugs.workaround: No workaround

bugs.title: Mac Edge Client Compatibility Issues with MacOS 13.3 as the support for WebView plugin is discontinued
bugs.symptoms: The WebView based End Point Inspection does not work in Mac Edge Client.
bugs.conditions: When using Edge Client on MacOS "Ventura" 13.3 Beta2 and later.
bugs.impact: Affected MacOS Edge client is unable to proceed with establishing the VPN connection.
bugs.workaround: Use the browser-based VPN. Note that there are some limitations if you are using your VPN in the AutoConnect mode and in the Blocked mode; it means the system cannot access the external network until you are disconnected. The issue is not fixed in the BIG-IP versions 14.1.5.5, 16.1.3.5, and 17.1.0.2 releases. Refer to the KB article K000134990 for recommended actions.
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed by invoking the EPI helper application instead of the inspection host plugin in Mac Edge Client running on 13.3 and newer. For more details on the deployment of the fix, refer to the K000133476 article. For more details regarding the issue, refer to the K000132932 article.

bugs.title: Vmtoolsd memory leak
bugs.symptoms: The Vmtoolsd service leaks memory on VMware BIG-IP VE guests when the Disk Type is IDE or any disk type other than SCSI.
bugs.conditions: VMware BIG-IP VE guest Disk type of IDE or another type that is not SCSI.
bugs.impact: The VE will eventually run out of memory.
bugs.workaround: 1. Create the file /etc/vmware-tools/tools.conf and add the following to the file: [guestinfo] # disable scan for disk device info diskinfo-report-device=false 2. Restart the vmtoolsd service: systemctl restart --ignore-dependencies vmtoolsd.service NB "guestinfo" must be in lower case. The workaround will not work if any letter is not lower case including the following "guestInfo" which was the reported workaround in https://github.com/vmware/open-vm-tools/issues/452

bugs.title: Systemctl start and restart fail to start the vmtoolsd service
bugs.symptoms: Because of a non-existent dependency, systemctl start and restart failed to start the vmtoolsd service. Following is the reported error: # systemctl restart vmtoolsd.service Failed to restart vmtoolsd.service: Unit not found. systetmctl stop is not affected.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP VE on VMware.
bugs.impact: Unable to start/restart the vmtoolsd service.
bugs.workaround: Systemctl restart --ignore-dependencies vmtoolsd.service or systemctl start --ignore-dependencies vmtoolsd.service

bugs.title: Cookies are truncated when number of cookies exceed the value configured in "max_enforced_cookies"
bugs.symptoms: When a request contains more cookies than configured in “max_enforced_cookies” and the “strip_asm_cookies” parameter is enabled, the cookie header is truncated and not all the cookies reach the server.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when - ASM is provisioned. - Request contains more cookies than configured in “max_enforced_cookies”. - Parameter “strip_asm_cookies” is enabled.
bugs.impact: All the cookies do not reach the server.
bugs.workaround: -- Disable the internal parameter “strip_asm_cookies”. -- Disabling the database key makes the behavior similar to the behavior in BIG-IP version 14. For more information, see K30023210. -- If you don’t want the old behavior before BIG-IP version 14, you can use the same solution as for versions before BIG-IP version 14: disable the sys db key. You can also use an iRule to remove the TS cookie from the server side. For more information, see K66438993.
bugs.fix: Skipping the removal of ASM cookies when the cookies are more than max_enforced_cookies.

bugs.title: Incorrect Enforcement After Sync
bugs.symptoms: In some scenarios, configuration updates are not sent to the enforcer which can cause unexpected enforcement. In bd and asm_config_server logs you may see the following logged repeatedly: ECARD_POLICY|NOTICE|Mar 28 12:53:26.872|18357|table_funcs.cpp:1471|handle_table_dynamic CONFIG_TYPE_INTERNAL_PARAMETERS res:[0] BD_FLUSH_TBLS|ERR |Mar 28 12:53:26.872|18357|AccountDomainsTbl.cpp:0049|attempting to add policy name crc while it already exists crc:[10127277905900865307]
bugs.conditions: A large configuration is synchronized to a device.
bugs.impact: Incorrect policy enforcement.
bugs.workaround: 1) Apply each policy individually on the affected devices/blades or 2) Restart ASM on the affected devices and blades
bugs.fix: Configuration updates are handled correctly.

bugs.title: False positive 'Illegal cross-origin request' violation
bugs.symptoms: In certain configurations, an HTTP request containing an HTTPS origin header may be blocked due to an 'Illegal cross-origin request' violation.
bugs.conditions: A request sent to a virtual server on an HTTP port (or any port other than 443) with an origin header set to HTTPS will trigger a violation under the following conditions: 1. The 'Illegal cross-origin request' violation is enabled. 2. In Security > Application Security > Security Policies > Policies List, click Create. Add a policy name (for example, Auto_Security_Policy_Services) and click Save. Then, on the Policies List page, click the created policy name and go to HTTP Message Protection > Headers > Host Names. This issue occurs when the host name is configured with the origin header value specified in this path. 3. The URL where the request is sent has 'Enforce on ASM' enabled in the 'HTML5 Cross-Domain Request' configuration area.
bugs.impact: An 'Illegal cross-origin request' violation is reported in version 17.1.x, unlike in version 16.1.x, with the same configurations and traffic.
bugs.workaround: Add the HTTPS protocol and origin name to the required URL in the 'Allowed Origins' setting, located under 'HTML5 Cross-Domain Request'.
bugs.fix: With the internal parameter enabled, an 'Illegal cross-origin request' violation will not be reported. By default, the internal parameter is disabled. However, it can be enabled using the following commands: /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add cors_match_protocol_port 1 /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add cors_default_port_80 1 tmsh restart sys service asm This enables the parameter and restarts the ASM service to apply the changes.

bugs.title: Constant traffic on DHCPv6 virtual servers may cause a TMM crash.
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash/core if there is a constant stream of DHCP traffic from the server towards the clients, not allowing a connection timeout.
bugs.conditions: Constant stream of traffic coming from DHCP server not allowing a connection timeout. Very aggressive lease settings causing constant lease refresh may be a configuration example leading to the problem.
bugs.impact: Failover/crash.

bugs.title: After upgrade to 16.1.3.2 from 16.0.1.1, BIG-IP can send CONNECT requests when no proxy select agent is used
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP uses a CONNECT to forward requests regardless of the PRP branch in use.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure BIG-IP as Explicit Forward proxy with SSL Orchestrator or SWG. -- Configure an access policy and a prp and apply to the forwarding Virtual Server. -- In the PRP, use multiple branches where one branch contains a proxy select agent, and another branch does not.
bugs.impact: Requests fail intermittently

bugs.title: AVR alert, Total Swap Memory Utilization alternates between 0% and 48% every 5 minutes
bugs.symptoms: AVR alert is observed when Swap memory is high.
bugs.conditions: - When swap memory is high.
bugs.impact: No impact of any functionality but false information gets triggered in LTM logs.
bugs.workaround: Disable swap memory alert from Alerts configuration page.

bugs.title: HTTP CONNECT request from client is not successful with the iRule 'HTTP::disable discard' command
bugs.symptoms: When you use the 'HTTP::disable discard' command in an irule to switch to HTTP transparent passthrough mode, the proxy connect / connection to server is not established. This only occurs when the 'HTTP::disable' command is used with the additional 'discard' option (which discards the existing HTTP headers before switching to passthrough mode) Refer https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/HTTP__disable.html
bugs.conditions: -> Basic HTTP VS -> iRule when HTTP_REQUEST { HTTP::disable discard node <ip port> }
bugs.impact: Client requests containing the HTTP CONNECT method hang (data is not proxied to the serverside flow)
bugs.workaround: Use 'HTTP::disable' command (without the 'discard' option)

bugs.title: F5RSS based BIG-IP system does not support `pkill -9 tmm`
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP guest configured on F5RSS platform system does not support `pkill -9 tmm` or `kill -9 <pid of tmm>`
bugs.conditions: F5RSS based BIG-IP guest
bugs.impact: BIG-IP system may encounter sudden crash and the host kernel `/var/log/messages` reports Hardware Errors.
bugs.workaround: => If you used `pkill -9 tmm` accidentally, - power cycle the system using iDRAC to recover => If did not use `pkill -9 tmm`, but wanted to kill tmm for some purpose, - Use `pkill -2 tmm` or `pkill -11 tmm` or etc.

bugs.title: TMM can crash when it exits while still processing traffic
bugs.symptoms: Unexpected TMM crash during shutdown.
bugs.conditions: This is a randomly occurring, potentially timing-related issue that might be related to other operations also occurring during shutdown.
bugs.impact: An unclean tmm exit occurs.

bugs.title: Adding ssh-rsa key for passwordless authentication
bugs.symptoms: In FIPS 140-3, SSHD does not support the ssh-rsa key for passwordless authentication.
bugs.conditions: The system must be in FIPS 140-3 mode.
bugs.impact: SSHD does not support the ssh-rsa key for passwordless authentication.
bugs.fix: SSHD should support the ssh-rsa key for passwordless authentication.

bugs.title: TLS extensions which are configured after session_ticket are not parsed from Client Hello messages
bugs.symptoms: When the client Hello message contains session_ticket extension, it was observed that the extensions which are configured after the session ticket extension were not processed and all the extensions are being ignored.
bugs.conditions: Configure SSL extensions along with session_ticket extension.
bugs.impact: A few requests are not forwarded correctly, for example, in scenario where server_name extension is configured after session_ticket but due to the current issue, [SSL::extensions exists -type 0] is returning 0 even though the server_name extension is present in Client Hello.
bugs.workaround: Configure all the required extensions before the session_ticket extension.
bugs.fix: TLS extensions which are configured after session_ticket are not parsed from Client Hello messages. Changes have been made in such a way that ext_sz variable which holds the size of all the extns configured in client Hello message is not limited to SSL_SZ_SESSIONID which is 32 bytes.

bugs.title: Improper query string handling on undisclosed pages
bugs.symptoms: On undisclosed pages, query strings are not processed as expected.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Query strings are processed as expected.

bugs.title: AFM DOS Half Open vector logs with field dos_packets_dropped having negative values
bugs.symptoms: Enable TCP Half Open DOS vector.
bugs.conditions: Enable TCP Half Open DOS vector.
bugs.impact: Dos_attack_event="Attack Sampled" logs of Half Open vector with field dos_packets_dropped values are in negative.

bugs.title: The iRule HTTP::respond with TCP:close fails at HTTP_RESPONSE
bugs.symptoms: If a server response is sent in multiple packets, HTTP::respond never serves the response to the client.
bugs.conditions: - Basic HTTP virtual server with below iRule: when HTTP_RESPONSE { HTTP::respond 200 content "CONTENT DATA in HTTP_RESPONSE＼n" noserver connection close TCP::close } -- The actual server response arrives in multiple packets.
bugs.impact: Connection towards the client is closed before HTTP::respond is served.
bugs.workaround: Use HTTP_RESPONSE_RELEASE instead of HTTP_RESPONSE.

bugs.title: JSON Schema validation failure with E notation number
bugs.symptoms: An unexpected JSON Schema validation failure is seen with E notation number.
bugs.conditions: The E notation is without a dot. For example, the following trigger this issue: - 0E-8 - 0e-8 But, the following do not trigger this issue: - 0.0E-8 - 0.0e-8 The problematic E notation number is used in object value, and the object is under an array, and the object is not the last member of the array.
bugs.impact: False positive.
bugs.workaround: Use E notation with a dot or disable schema validation violation.

bugs.title: Reducing packet loss for BIG-IP instance running on rSeries r2000 / r4000 appliances
bugs.symptoms: Packet loss occurs when DNS traffic flows through BIG-IP tenant on rSeries r2000 / r4000 appliances. This causes DNS performance to regress.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP vCMP instance running on rSeries r2000 / r4000 appliances DNS traffic (or other UDP traffic as well) flowing through BIG-IP
bugs.impact: Reduction in packet loss.
bugs.workaround: None (This change is an improvement that alleviates performance regression)
bugs.fix: The rx/tx ring buffer sizes of iavf driver are increased.

bugs.title: Improve ASM performance for BIG-IP instances running on r2k / r4k appliances
bugs.symptoms: ASM performance has regressed on BIG-IP instances running on r2k / r4k appliances (since F5OS release 1.3.0)
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP instance running on r2k / r4k ASM traffic flowing through BIG-IP
bugs.impact: Improvement in ASM performance.
bugs.workaround: None (because this change is an improvement that alleviates performance regression)
bugs.fix: The kernel scheduling parameters are modified to enable better sharing of CPU resources between TMM and ASM daemons.

bugs.title: BD crashes when the UMU OOM limit is reached and the request has an authorization bearer header
bugs.symptoms: BD crashes when the UMU OOM limit is reached and the request includes an authorization bearer header.
bugs.conditions: - UMU OOM limit is reached - The request has authorization bearer header
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.

bugs.title: BIG-IP incorrectly sets the LDAP fallback indicator for users not found in LDAP when the ignore-unknown-user option is configured.
bugs.symptoms: When LDAP remote authentication is configured with the ignore-unknown-user option, a user absent from the LDAP directory can authenticate through local fallback, but the F5FALLBACK session marker is not set.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under the following conditions: - LDAP remote authentication is configured on BIG-IP. - The ignore-unknown-user option is enabled in the LDAP authentication profile. - The LDAP server is reachable and returns a user-not-found result. - The authenticating user has a local account on the BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: A user absent from LDAP who authenticates using local credentials is not marked as a local-fallback session (F5FALLBACK is not set). As a result, any BIG-IP logic relying on F5FALLBACK to differentiate between LDAP-authenticated sessions and local-fallback sessions will not function as expected for these users.

bugs.title: In-TMM monitor may mark pool member offline despite its response matches Receive Disable String
bugs.symptoms: Despite response matching monitor's Receive Disable String, pool member may by marked offline by the in-TMM monitor while the BIGD monitor would mark it as available/disabled. It is particularly likely if the matched pattern is located in the front of the pool member's response data.
bugs.conditions: -- HTTP, HTTP2, or TCP monitor is used. -- In-TMM monitor is enabled. -- Both Receive String and Receive Disable String are provided.
bugs.impact: Pool member is marked offline while it should be marked available/disabled by the in-TMM monitor.
bugs.workaround: Use BIGD instead of in-TMM monitor.
bugs.fix: When pool member's response matches Receive Disable String it is correctly marked as Availabe/Disabled by in-TMM monitor. The same as BIGD monitor.

bugs.title: SIP response message with missing Reason-Phrase or with spaces are not accepted
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP drops SIP response messages that are missing the Reason-Phrase.
bugs.conditions: A SIP response message in this format SIP/2.0 424 ＼r＼n are dropped If the message has a reason text Status-Line = SIP-Version SP Status-Code SP Reason-Phrase CRLF Like this SIP/2.0 404 Not Found＼r＼n then it would not be dropped
bugs.impact: Connectivity issue.
bugs.fix: BIG-IP now accepts SIP response with Status-line missing a reason text.

bugs.title: Observed crash while running sweep flood tests
bugs.symptoms: While testing sweep flood tests, the TMM crashes.
bugs.conditions: The sweep flood test case was failing.
bugs.impact: TMM crash
bugs.fix: Fixed the issue where no crash is observed while testing the sweep flood tests.

bugs.title: The qkview qkvcmp (vcmp_module.xml) needs to be updated for F5OS tenancy
bugs.symptoms: F5OS tenants running TMOS is full of error messages in vcmp_module.xml.
bugs.conditions: - F5OS tenants running TMOS.
bugs.impact: Tenants will not collect some troubleshooting information while collecting troubleshooting information through qkview.

bugs.title: Missing Neuron/TCAM rules
bugs.symptoms: - Neuron/TCAM rules are missing for a virtual server that has a rule based feature activated. - /var/log/ltm has the following error : Apr 12 02:31:14 bigip1 err tmm5[23326]: 01010331:3: Neuron client neuron_app_dyn_tcam failed with rule add(request full)
bugs.conditions: - On platforms with Neuron/TCAM support. - A single virtual server requires more than 16 rules.
bugs.impact: Features that rely on the Neuron/TCAM rules are not fully offloaded to hardware and thus fall back to software.
bugs.fix: Rules are created correctly for all virtual servers.

bugs.title: Hardware mitigation is not working for a few SIP vectors
bugs.symptoms: Hardware mitigation not happening as int_drops are not incrementing bd_stats are incrementing but SPVA stat bd_hit is not incrementing
bugs.conditions: Configure SIP vectors with the threshold levels in any Hardware platform and send the related traffic
bugs.impact: Hardware mitigation will not happen for SIP Vectors
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Neuron rules had been written in the neuron chip for these vectors so that stats were counting correctly

bugs.title: Hardware SYN cookie mode may not exit
bugs.symptoms: -- Virtual server reports SYN cookie mode is "full hardware" even after a SYN flood has stopped. -- The virtual_server_stat tmstat table columns sc_mode0,sc_mode1 show "FRS" and the syncookies.hwsyncookie_inst column is greater than zero, even after a SYN flood has stopped.
bugs.conditions: -- Platform with Neuron/TCAM support. -- AFM is not provisioned.
bugs.impact: -- SYN/ACK responses that include a SYN cookie are generated by HW even after a SYN flood attacked has stopped. -- SYN pkts are not seen by the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Set the pvasyncookies.preferhwlmode BigDB variable to "true".
bugs.fix: Virtual servers properly exit HW SYN cookie mode.

bugs.title: Vxlan tunnel end point routed through the tunnel will cause a tmm crash
bugs.symptoms: Tmm generates a core file and restarts
bugs.conditions: A vxlan tunnel is configured and there is a route for the remote end point via the tunnel itself
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Do not route the tunnel endpoint through the tunnel.

bugs.title: Item filter does not work on /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/export-suggestions/
bugs.symptoms: Filter is not applied for export suggestions task.
bugs.conditions: Having a policy with suggestions. try to export in declarative format: restcurl -u admin:admin /mgmt/tm/asm/tasks/export-suggestions/ -d '{"policyReference":{"link":"https://localhost/mgmt/tm/asm/policies/uaDQEF3ndTdKkawROqwQow"},"filter":"status eq 'accept'","inline":true}'
bugs.impact: You are unable to get filtered suggestions in a declarative format.

bugs.title: Memory corruption due to use-after-free in the TCAM rule management module
bugs.symptoms: - TMM crashes. - Neuron client errors may be found in /var/log/ltm.
bugs.conditions: Platform with Neuron/TCAM support (BIG-IP iSeries).
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Released variable is cleared to avoid use-after-free.

bugs.title: PA based Hosted content does not add implicit allowed ACL
bugs.symptoms: Unable to download the hosted content from Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: ACLs with a default deny or reject rule
bugs.impact: Hosted content files are denied by ACL
bugs.workaround: Add 2 L4 ACLs similar to the rules below: apm acl /Common/allow-hostedcontent { acl-order 20 entries { { action allow dst-end-port 8080 dst-start-port 8080 dst-subnet ::1/128 log packet protocol 6 src-subnet 0.0.0.0/0 } { action allow dst-end-port 8080 dst-start-port 8080 dst-subnet 127.1.1.0/24 log packet protocol 6 src-subnet 0.0.0.0/0 } }

bugs.title: APM Modern Customization: A custom icon for the Decision Box fails to render and returns a 404 error."
bugs.symptoms: When using the Modern Customisation Framework with General Customisation, a custom image configured for the Decision Box fails to render on the access policy page, and a 404 error is returned for the image resource. The Standard Customisation Framework remains unaffected.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: - An Access Profile is configured with the profile type set to Modern. - A custom image is assigned to the Decision Box under: Access > Profiles/Policies > Customisation> General > Customisation Settings > Access Profiles > [profile] > Decision Pages > Decision Box > General > Field 1 image.
bugs.impact: End users accessing a virtual server with a Modern-type Access Profile will not see the configured custom Decision Box icon, as a 404 error is returned for the custom image resource. Standard profile types remain unaffected.
bugs.workaround: Use a Standard Access Profile type instead of Modern, as custom Decision Box icons render correctly when the Access Profile type is set to Standard.

bugs.title: TMM crash under certain traffic patterns
bugs.symptoms: Tmm may crash and restart
bugs.conditions: Vlan-groups configured. A snat listener. A listener that matches the IP address of the SNAT listener configured, but not the IP address.
bugs.impact: The TMM may crash and cause a traffic disruption
bugs.fix: The TMM handles traffic as expected.

bugs.title: Creation of wideip with alias would cause inconsistent zone data across GTM sync group
bugs.symptoms: Loss of resource record.
bugs.conditions: -- Creation of a wideip with alias and -- synchronize-zone-files is set to yes
bugs.impact: Loss of resource record.
bugs.workaround: Set synchronize-zone-files to no.

bugs.title: The Proxy Select agent fails to select the pool or upstream proxy in explicit proxy mode
bugs.symptoms: The Proxy Select agent in the per-request policy does not select the pool or upstream proxy in explicit proxy mode. This prevents SSL Orchestrator or BIG-IP from forwarding the egress data to the upstream proxy.
bugs.conditions: - Proxy Select agent is used in the per-request policy. - Proxy Select agent is set to explicit proxy mode. - Flow is set to be bypassed using per-req policy agents such as IP Based SSL Bypass Set or dynamic bypass based on SSL profiles.
bugs.impact: SSL Orchestrator or BIG-IP does not forward any egress data to the upstream proxy.

bugs.title: After upgrade to BIG-IP 14.1.4.4, data at Security › Reporting:Application:Charts did not migrate
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade to BIG-IP 14.1.4.4, the charts did not migrate as expected.
bugs.conditions: - Upgrade from BIG-IP 14.1.2.8 to BIG-IP 14.1.4.4.
bugs.impact: Loss of historical charting data.

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator SEGV TMM core
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes while passing SSL Orchestrator traffic.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when a service is added or when an existing connector node configuration is freed.
bugs.impact: TMM crash occurs. Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts. This issue occurs intermittently.

bugs.title: TCP RST internal error in tcpproxy bad transition during SSL connection closure.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP RSTs connection with Internal error in tcpproxy bad transition.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs when following condition is met: Client - DUT1 - DUT2 - Server -> Configure https virtual server on both DUT1 and DUT2 -Configure client-ssl profile with 'maximum-record-size' set to 256 and unclean-shutdown to disabled - Configure tcp profile with nagle enabled -> On DUT1 configure a default https in-tmm monitor monitoring a DUT2. -> On Server, make sure the response spans 3 to 4 times the SSL record size.
bugs.impact: Connection closes abruptly on serverside.
bugs.fix: Connection closes as expected.

bugs.title: MCPD always logs "01071323:4: Vlan (/<partition_name>/<vlan_name>:<ID>) is configured, but NOT on hypervisor allowed list" on F5OS tenant
bugs.symptoms: An F5OS Tenant at startup may print a log to indicate that a VLAN configured on the Tenant has not been assigned by the hypervisor. For example: warning mcpd[7929]: 01071323:4: Vlan (/Common/vlan-999:999) is configured, but NOT on hypervisor allowed list. This alerts the administrator to a possible problem in the hypervisor or tenant configuration. The log can appear at startup, complicating troubleshooting and leading the administrator to believe a problem exists when it does not.
bugs.conditions: This is often noticed at startup, but may also be observed when: -- Adding vlans -- Restarting chmand (bigstart restart chmand) -- Other configuration changes on the F5OS hypervisor that may affect the tenant (e.g. disabling/enabling interfaces or changing trunk configurations)
bugs.impact: This is benign but misleading.
bugs.workaround: The administrator can verify the log is false by checking the Tenant configuration (show tenants) on the F5OS hypervisor.

bugs.title: Pool member marked as offline while matching both receive string and receive disable strings
bugs.symptoms: The monitor is marked offline when the expected state is up/available.
bugs.conditions: - Monitor configured to monitor in TMM. - Monitor configured with receive string and receive disable string. - Monitor associated with a member where the response to the health monitor matches the receive string and receive disable string and the member is marked as offline.
bugs.impact: The monitor is marked offline potentially impacting traffic to the pool when the health monitor is matching both receive and receive disable strings.
bugs.workaround: Configure the monitor such that the response does not match both the receive and receive disable strings at the same time. Alternatively, adjust the receive and receive disable strings such that they will not match at the same time.

bugs.title: Tenants on r2000 and r4000 systems will not pass traffic through VLAN groups, or if ltm global-settings general share-single-mac changed from "vmw-compat"
bugs.symptoms: A tenant running on an r2000 or r4000-series appliance is not able to pass traffic through a VLAN group, regardless of the VLAN group mode. Traffic to/from the tenant does not work properly if the "ltm global-settings general share-single-mac" / "VLAN.MacAssignment" DB key is changed to "unique".
bugs.conditions: - r2000 and r4000-series appliances - tenant using VLAN groups, or with the share-single-mac setting changed from the default ("vmw-compat") to "unique".
bugs.impact: Traffic to tenant stops working and all the traffic to tenant is dropped.
bugs.workaround: Remove the vlan-group group configuration.
bugs.fix: Unicast promiscuous mode is set in the guest OS iavf driver during the initialization.

bugs.title: Tenant clustering fails when adding a lower number slot to Tenant
bugs.symptoms: If an existing Tenant is expanded to a new blade with a blade slot lower than any blade slot the Tenant is already running on, the Tenant can fail to cluster after a tenant reboot.
bugs.conditions: An existing Tenant is expanded to a new blade with a blade slot lower than any blade slot the Tenant is already running on.
bugs.impact: The Tenant can intermittently fail to cluster after a Tenant reboot.
bugs.workaround: In the partition CLI, set the tenant to provisioned, then back to deployed.

bugs.title: TMM disconnects from processes such as mcpd causing TMM to restart
bugs.symptoms: When tunnels are in use on the BIG-IP, TMM may lose its connection to MCPD and exit and restart. At the time of the restart, a log message similar to the following will be seen in /var/log/ltm: crit tmm6[19243]: 01010020:2: MCP Connection expired, exiting When this occurs, in a default configuration, no core file is generated. TMM may also disconnect unexpectedly from other services (i.e. tmrouted). TMM may also suddenly fail to match traffic for existing virtual server connections against a connection flow. This could result in traffic stalling and timing out.
bugs.conditions: -- An IPsec, GRE or IPIP tunnel is in use.
bugs.impact: -- Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts. -- Sudden poor performance
bugs.workaround: Do not use tunnels.
bugs.fix: TMM will not unexpectedly reset connections when tunnels are in use.

bugs.title: 'contentWindow' of a dynamically genereated iframe becomes null
bugs.symptoms: A web application using iframes may not work/render as expected using Portal Access.
bugs.conditions: A web application attempts to configure 'contentWindow' for an iframe while the Portal Access feature is in use.
bugs.impact: Web Application through Portal Access may fails to work/render as expected
bugs.workaround: Using a customized irule/ifile to return un-patched 'contentWindow' from cache-fm*.js file. ifile has modern cache-fm file. when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { ACCESS::restrict_irule_events disable } when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "/cache-fm-Modern.js" } { HTTP::respond 200 content [ifile get cachefmUploadIssueWorkaround] } }

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenants on F5OS r5000, r10000, and r12000 platforms don't pass traffic properly while in forced offline state
bugs.symptoms: Monitors may flap. Connections generated from the tenant will succeed and others will fail. The ConfigSync status for a tenant that is forced offline will report disconnected.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant running on r5000, r10000, and r12000-series appliances. Note: F5OS tenants on VELOS chassis will not pass traffic while the tenant is forced offline, but that behavior is not tracked by this ID. For more information, see K15122: Overview of the Force Offline option for devices and traffic groups (https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K15122)
bugs.impact: Traffic to/from the tenant does not work properly when the tenant is forced offline, although the behavior can be intermittent.

bugs.title: Cores with fail over and message routing
bugs.symptoms: Seg faults for an active unit in an high availability (HA) pair when it goes to standby.
bugs.conditions: - Generic message routing is in use. - high availability (HA) pairs - This issue is observed when generic messages are in flight when fail over happens but there is some evidence that it can happen without fail over.
bugs.impact: This is a memory corruption issue, the effects are unpredictable and may not become visible for some time, but in testing seg faults leading to a core were observed in the device going to standby within 10-25s of the device failing over. This happened roughly for about 50% of the time but the effect will be sensitive to memory layout and other environmental perturbations.
bugs.fix: The MR message store iteration is fixed, no corruption or cores observed.

bugs.title: EasySoap++-0.6.2 is not coded to add an SNI
bugs.symptoms: Microsoft Azure has a firewall that blocks any outgoing TLS ClientHello without the SNI extension. This causes our clients to be unable to orchestrate F5 VMs as they cannot successfully license the device automatically.
bugs.conditions: Clients using our devices on Azure cannot automatically license the device via f5-bigip-runtime-init using the command: /usr/bin/tmsh install /sys license registration-key ${LICENSE_KEY}
bugs.impact: Cannot successfully license the device automatically.
bugs.fix: Updated EasySoap++-0.6.2 with SNI fix

bugs.title: BIG-IP generates more multicast packets in multicast failover high availability (HA) setup
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP generates additional high availability (HA) multicast packets when the device name is changed. Running the following commands shows the duplicate multicast entries on mgmt:mgmt interface on /var/log/sodlog file # /usr/bin/cmd_sod get info
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IPs configured with Multicast failover . -- The self-device name is changed.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP multiplies the number of multicast packets when the device name is changed.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the sod would remove the duplicate multicast entries. #bigstart restart sod
bugs.fix: Cleanup the multicast entries populated on old device name when the name is updated.

bugs.title: URL categorization does not work with duplicate f5-ids
bugs.symptoms: During the configuration migration, some of the custom domain categories are attached to a duplicate F5-ID, due to this a custom domain URL remains uncategorized.
bugs.conditions: Category-ID duplication can happen when merging from another system config.
bugs.impact: URL categorization will not work for duplicate cat-ids.
bugs.workaround: 1. Find the list of Duplicate f5-id in the configuration 2. Pick the duplicate entries where categorization is not working 3. Delete the non-working URL categorization entries 4. Create again the deleted URL categorization entries 5. You should see a unique f5-ids in the config 6. At this point URL categorization should work fine for all URLs

bugs.title: IPI updates can fail if the network in unstable.
bugs.symptoms: IPI stops updating during network instability.
bugs.conditions: This issue happens only when the management network of the BIG-IP system is unstable. Issue impact on BIG-IP versions listed below which are running old SDK(vector2.brightcloud.com) version. BIG-IP v14.x BIG-IP v15.1.3 and prior versions BIG-IP v16.0.x and v16.1.2.x This won't occur on the BIG-IP versions listed below which are running new SDK(api.bcti.brightcloud.com) version. BIG-IP V15.1.4 and later versions BIG-IP v16.1.3 and later versions BIG-IP v17.x
bugs.impact: IPI database will not be updated.
bugs.workaround: Restart the iprepd deamon.

bugs.title: When using http2-to-http-gateway, tmm can crash in very rare circumstances
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes and restarts
bugs.conditions: When using http2 http gw, and chunking is present at the serverside, under very rare circumstances tmm can restart.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Tmm does not crash anymore.

bugs.title: APM WLI with SAML Authentication does not terminate APM session after Windows logoff when Azure AD is configured as the IdP
bugs.symptoms: When Access Policy Manager (APM) is configured with Windows Logon Integration (WLI), SAML authentication, and Azure AD as the Identity Provider (IdP), logging off the Windows workstation initiates a SAML Single Logout (SLO) request but does not terminate the associated APM session. The APM session remains active on the BIG-IP system until the configured idle timeout or maximum session timeout is reached
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM configured with Windows Logon Integration (WLI). SAML authentication is used within the access policy - Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) is configured as the SAML Identity Provider - A Network Access (NA) resource is assigned through the access policy - Edge Client/Dial-Up connection is configured with Enforce Access Policy in Custom Dialer enabled -The user logs off the Windows workstation while the Network Access session is active - SAML Single Logout (SLO) is initiated, but the APM session is not explicitly removed
bugs.impact: APM sessions persist after the user logs out of Windows, resulting in stale sessions remaining active until timeout

bugs.title: Neuron based HW SYN cookie broken due to ZBDDOS feature porting to 16.1.x
bugs.symptoms: In 16.1.x, Neuron based HW SYN cookie is broken.
bugs.conditions: -- Neuron-equipped hardware (BIG-IP iSeries) -- Configure TCP Half Open at profile level. -- Send Traffic. -- Check HW SYN Cookies.
bugs.impact: This breaks the HW SYN cookie functionality
bugs.fix: Updates are implemented to return the correct parameters and HW SYN Cookie is working fine

bugs.title: TMM crash while processing myvpn request
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes while processing traffic on the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: Network Access resource is configured.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: SNAT command in iRule fails to convert ICMPv6 requests to ICMPv4
bugs.symptoms: When the SNAT command is used in an iRule, ICMPv6 echo requests cannot be translated to an ICMP echo requests when nat64 is enabled on the virtual server. The snat pool in server side contains the IPV4 addresses.
bugs.conditions: -- Enable nat64 on a virtual server -- Configure a SNAT pool. -- Use "snat" command in an iRule.
bugs.impact: NAT64 translation does not occur which leads to traffic failure.
bugs.workaround: Do not use "snat" for selecting a pool member in an iRule.

bugs.title: Built-in SSL Orchestrator RPM installation timeout failure
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to install the built-in SSL Orchestrator RPM results in the following error: Installation Failed! Response timed out, try reload the page.
bugs.conditions: In the BIG-IP TMUI, the BIG-IP administrator navigates to the SSL Orchestrator Configuration page. This would automatically invoke the installation of the built-in SSL Orchestrator RPM, resulting in the failure.
bugs.impact: The built-in SSL Orchestrator RPM is not installed and SSL Orchestrator management is not possible.
bugs.workaround: Step 1. Run the following commands in the BIG-IP command line: # Get ID for f5-ssl-orchestrator-dg-data: id=$(restcurl shared/iapp/blocks/ | jq -r '.items[] | select(.name == "f5-ssl-orchestrator-dg-data") | .id') # Temporarily unlink the "f5-ssl-orchestrator-dg-data" (id). restcurl -X PATCH -d "{＼"baseReference＼": {＼"link＼": ＼"https://localhost/mgmt/shared/iapp/blocks/$id＼"}}" shared/iapp/blocks/$id # Remove all SSL Orchestrator block templates. restcurl shared/iapp/blocks | jq -r '.items[] | select(.state == "TEMPLATE") | select(.name | startswith("f5-ssl-orchestrator")) | .id' | for x in $(cat) ; do restcurl -X DELETE shared/iapp/blocks/$x; done # Remove the SSL Orchestrator RPM installation references (if any). restcurl -X DELETE shared/iapp/global-installed-packages/9beb912b-4f1c-3f95-94c3-eb1cbac4ab99 restcurl -X DELETE shared/iapp/installed-packages/9beb912b-4f1c-3f95-94c3-eb1cbac4ab99 --- Step 2. Use the BIG-IP TMUI: Log in to the TMUI and navigate to SSL Orchestrator > Configuration. This would refresh the related page and install the SSL Orchestrator RPM. Wait for the SSL Orchestrator configuration page to complete loading.

bugs.title: Enforcement of non-approved algorithms in FIPS or Common Criteria mode.
bugs.symptoms: FIPS and Common Criteria require that only FIPS-approved algorithms be used for keys.
bugs.conditions: OpenSSH used in FIPS or Common Criteria mode.
bugs.impact: OpenSSH accepts non-approved algorithms in FIPS or Common Criteria mode.
bugs.fix: The allowed cipher list is changed to allow only FIPS-Approved algorithms.

bugs.title: Uncaught ReferenceError: ReferenceError: REquest is not defined
bugs.symptoms: The Cache-fm-Modern.js file has a typo.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when using Modern JS support EHF.
bugs.impact: A Javascript error occurs: "Uncaught ReferenceError: ReferenceError: REquest is not defined".
bugs.workaround: Correct the typo and give the iRule with iFile workaround.
bugs.fix: The word "REquest" should be "Request" at all the places where there is a typo error.

bugs.title: False positive CORS violation can occur after upgrading to 17.1.x under certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: CORS violation can start appearing after upgrading to 17.1.x.
bugs.conditions: 1) CORS violation is enabled. 2) CORS configuration is done with port 80 on a particular URL. 3) Request with URL from step 2 which BIG-IP receives, is of HTTPS type.
bugs.impact: Requests with HTTPS protocol can get blocked with CORS violation.
bugs.workaround: Change configured CORS port to 443 for URLs that receive HTTPS traffic.
bugs.fix: Added a new bd internal variable "cors_default_port_80" which can be used to allow HTTPS traffic with CORS port configured as 80.

bugs.title: The date-time RegExp pattern through swagger would not cover all valid options
bugs.symptoms: Some valid hours option would not match the Regular Expression (RegExp).
bugs.conditions: Creating a policy using swagger file and uploading a swagger file which contains parameter in date time format.
bugs.impact: Valid hours options 10 and 19 would not match the RegExp.
bugs.fix: The date-time regular expression for swagger is fixed and now suppose to cover all valid options.

bugs.title: FIX protocol late binding flows that are not PVA accelerated may fail
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 connections with late binding enabled typically used for FIX protocol can stall or hang if they are evicted from PVA and not re-offloaded.
bugs.conditions: - Late binding enabled on a FastL4 flow. The flow is not accelerated, and if the flow recieves approximately 50 packets, then it will hang. Captures would show packets ingressing to the BIG-IP and not being forwarded to the peer.
bugs.impact: Connection may stall.
bugs.workaround: Disable late binding. If late binding cannot be disabled, then disable pva-flow-aging and pva-flow-evict to avoid the issue.
bugs.fix: FIX protocol flow works as expected.

bugs.title: Missing MAC filters for IPv6 multicast
bugs.symptoms: Certain drivers are missing MAC filters for multicast. This prevents TMM from receiving messages sent to All Nodes and All Routers addresses.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP VE - Using TMM's IAVF driver
bugs.impact: TMM does not receive multicast messages and traffic sent to All Nodes and All Routers, dropping potentially vital packets.

bugs.title: Page customization of Front image for standard Access profile fails for image uploaded from local disk
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to upload a custom image from your local disk to the Logon page agent customization in VPE for access profile if the Type is set to standard A popup error window occurs: 01b70117:3: local_path (/tmp/php/emc.png) starts with invalid directory. Valid directories are /var/config/rest/, /var/tmp/, /shared/tmp/, /var/system/tmp/.
bugs.conditions: -- Access profile of type "standard" -- upload new image from your local disk to Front image in Logon page agent customization from VPE
bugs.impact: You are unable to use a custom image from the local disk as the front image for the Logon page agent

bugs.title: Subviolations (e.g., IP in host header violation) are not reported to the policy builder
bugs.symptoms: Evasion Technique and HTTP Protocol Compliance subviolations (e.g., IP in host header violation) are not reported to the policy builder.
bugs.conditions: When the policy is set to only learn (alarm and block are turned off).
bugs.impact: Learning suggestions to permanently disable the subviolation is not received.
bugs.workaround: A user should also enable the alarm to receive learning and suggestions for this subviolation.

bugs.title: Credentials can be submitted to /my.policy as GET instead of POST
bugs.symptoms: A user can submit credentials in a GET request to /my.policy instead of POST. This may expose user credentials inappropriately under some circumstances.
bugs.conditions: 1. A basic logon page is configured 2. The user sends a login request to /my.policy using a GET request instead of a POST request.
bugs.impact: User credentials may be exposed.
bugs.workaround: An iRule may be used to reject such requests. A sample iRule is given below: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { ACCESS::restrict_irule_events disable } when HTTP_REQUEST { # match /my.policy with query beginning character ? if { [HTTP::uri] starts_with "/my.policy?" } { if { [HTTP::method] equals "GET" } { log local0. "HTTP method GET is not allowed for /my.policy?" reject } } }
bugs.fix: APM will no longer accept GET requests to /my.policy requests with credentials.

bugs.title: Access policies not in Partition Common are not applied in auto discovery process
bugs.symptoms: When access profiles are setup with discovery tasks in non Common partitions, the access policies are not applied.
bugs.conditions: 1. Switch to a non Common partition 2. Create an Access profile 3. Configure a DNS server, OAuth scope, OAuth Client, OAuth Provider and OAuth server 4. Go back to Provider and start the discovery process.
bugs.impact: Access Policies are not applied in Auto discovery task if they are not in partition Common.

bugs.title: The violation "Illegal cross-origin request" is raised when it is not enabled under learning-blocking settings
bugs.symptoms: Request with a cross-origin violation, raises a violation when the violation is not enabled.

bugs.title: ASM Resources Reporting graph displays over 1000% CPU usage

Run the following: $ sed -i 's|distinct time_stamp))|distinct time_stamp)*100)|g' /etc/avr/monpd/monp_asm_cpu_info_measures.cfg 3. bugs.title: TMM cored in ping access hudfilter due to ctx pointed to invalid address
bugs.symptoms: In the pingaccess, when the HUDCTL_TEARDOWN arrives and is forwarded synchronously down the chain, this causes the flow to be removed and the chain to be torn down. This also causes the CLIENT_CLOSED to be called. Coincidentally customer has iRule, and happens to need a block matching the size of the just-freed block containing ctx, thus the freed ctx is overwritten with the log message generated due to the debugging TCL variable being "1". Upon reaching lower filters, the pingaccess attempts to call pmgr_service_update_last_active where the issue occurred. This issue can be seen in the 1001041 bug.
bugs.conditions: APM provisioned. Using multiple ping access instances, the Ping access feature is mainly used for SSO.
bugs.impact: Unexpected failover occurred which impacted accessing applications.
bugs.fix: Ping_access_handler needs to avoid accessing ctx after it has been freed which means after axs2_sm_destroy has been called.

bugs.title: Pool member Forced Offline then Enabled is marked down on peer after Incremental sync
bugs.symptoms: When a Pool Member has been marked Forced Offline then later marked Enabled on one member of the Device Group, the Pool Member may be marked Down on Device Group members other than the member where the Pool Member was marked Enabled. On the BIG-IP system (Device Group member) where the Pool Member was marked Enabled, the Pool Member's status will be marked correctly according to its actual state, as determined by the Health Monitor configured for the affected Pool or Pool Member.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on BIG-IP versions where ID1095217 is fixed for the following conditions: -- Multiple BIG-IP systems are configured in a Sync-Failover Device Group -- The Device Group is configured for Incremental sync -- A pool member or the parent Node has been marked Forced Offline -- A Health Monitor is configured for the pool or pool member -- The same monitor assigned to the pool member is not set to the rule for LTM default-node-monitor -- The pool member or its parent Node is later marked as Enabled on one member of the Device Group -- This change is synced to the Device Group (either manually or automatically, through Incremental sync, not Full sync)
bugs.impact: The affected pool member that may be markded Down does not receive traffic as expected as the other Device Group members. -- If the pool member is re-enabled on the Standby member, traffic on the Active member will not be sent to the pool member. -- If the pool member is re-enabled on the Active member, traffic on the Standby member will not be sent to the pool member if the Active member fails over to the Standby member.
bugs.workaround: Perform one of the following actions as a workaround: Option 1: -- Perform a Full sync to the Device Group from the Device Group member with the correct pool member status. Option 2: -- Set the pool member as Disabled -- Sync the change with the Device Group -- Set the pool member Enabled -- Sync the change with the Device Group Option 3: -- Remove the configured Health Monitor from the affected pool or pool member. Note: If the Health Monitor is removed from the pool, all pool members may become unavailable, halting new connections to pool members. -- Sync this change to the Device Group. -- Add the previously configured Health Monitor back to the pool or pool member. -- Sync the change to the Device Group. Option 4: Do not use WebUI for Force Offline or Enable. But, use the following TMSH command with the ‘replace-all-with’ option to set Force Offline/Enable. For example: tmsh modify ltm pool http_pool { members replace-all-with { 10.xx.xx.xx:yy { session user-disabled state user-down } } } tmsh modify ltm pool http_pool { members replace-all-with { 10.xx.xx.xx:yy { session user-disabled state user-up } } } Note: If the health monitor status remain Black circle after Option 2), perform Option 1) Note: Option 4 does not resolve the issue; it prevents the issue from occurring.
bugs.fix: The pool member status is now correctly synced to other Device Group members after being Forced Offline and then Enabled on one Device Group member. This fix causes a return of ID1095217 on versions where ID1095217 had previously been Fixed.

bugs.title: Full sync failure for traffic-matching-criteria with port list update on existing object in certain conditions
bugs.symptoms: Performing a full configuration sync with traffic-matching-criteria (TMC) under specific conditions fails with errors similar to: err mcpd[5781]: 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:traffic_matching_criteria_port_update status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127. err mcpd[5781]: 01071488:3: Remote transaction for device group /Common/HA to commit id 41 failed with error 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:traffic_matching_criteria_port_update status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127..
bugs.conditions: This may occur on a full-load config sync (not an incremental sync) Both Active and Standby on sync already - a traffic-matching-criteria is attached to a virtual server - the traffic-matching-criteria is using a port-list - Update the port list (Add new port in the existing list) Ex: tmsh modify net port-list /Common/<> { ports replace-all-with { 80 { } 83 { } 84 { } } port-lists none } Assume port list already with 80,83 and adding new port 84 in the list. NOTE: No issue observed when we try to update the list with removing the port from the list.
bugs.impact: Unable to sync configurations.

bugs.title: IPsec IKEv2 tunnel may not start after it is allowed to expire
bugs.symptoms: IPsec IKEv2 tunnel was working initially, but will suddenly not respond to ISAKMP negotiation. A packet capture will show the BIG-IP refusing inbound ISAKMP. Example: 02:26:14.327847 IP 172.16.5.1.500 > 172.16.6.1.500: isakmp: parent_sa ikev2_init[I] 02:26:14.328678 IP 172.16.6.1 > 172.16.5.1: ICMP 172.16.6.1 udp port 500 unreachable
bugs.conditions: -- IPsec IKEv2 tunnel in use. -- The BIG-IP is the Responder to a tunnel negotiation. -- The tunnel expires (ages out) naturally and does not renegotiate due no interesting traffic. -- The tunnel is required again due to new traffic, but now cannot start.
bugs.impact: Remote networks are not available while the tunnel is down.
bugs.workaround: Mitigate by setting high ike-peer lifetimes so that the tunnel does not naturally go down due to lack of traffic: #tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer <name> lifetime 1440 To recover the tunnel when it is in the hard-down state:, disable the problematic ike-peer and enable it again: # tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer <name> state disabled # tmsh modify net ipsec ike-peer <name> state enabled If the above method does not work, it is likely that the encountered problem is not related to the issue described here. However, the service-impacting approach of restarting tmm would also recover this problem state, as the last option.

bugs.title: The GUI order for TCP goodput is being ordered as a string but not a number.
bugs.symptoms: Sorting on TCP goodput in GUI is not working properly.
bugs.conditions: When performing the sorting on the AVR goodput header in GUI. Statistics ›› Analytics: TCP: Goodput >> Change View By to "Remote Host IP Address" from Dropdown>> Average Connection Good through Put
bugs.impact: Unable to order/sort by the number on TCP goodput in GUI.
bugs.workaround: Login to BIG-IP and edit /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tcp_measures file and replace string("N/A") with NULL in the 'formula and merge_formula' properties of 'cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m and cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m' fields, save and restart monpd service. Procedure: Step#1: Log in to BIG-IP CLI. Step#2: Edit the /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tcp_measures.cfg file. vi /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tcp_measures.cfg Exiting Code: ... [cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m] formula=IF(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_rcv)=0,"N/A",ROUND(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_rcv)/SUM(cs_numendings),2)) merge_formula=IF(SUM(cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m)=0,"N/A",ROUND(SUM(cs_numendings_m*cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m)/SUM(cs_numendings_m),2)) ... [cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m] formula=IF(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_snt)=0,"N/A",ROUND(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_snt)/SUM(cs_numendings),2)) merge_formula=IF(SUM(cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m)=0,"N/A",ROUND(SUM(cs_numendings_m*cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m)/SUM(cs_numendings_m),2)) ... Replace "N/A" with NULL in Exiting Code: ... [cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m] formula=IF(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_rcv)=0,NULL,ROUND(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_rcv)/SUM(cs_numendings),2)) merge_formula=IF(SUM(cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m)=0,NULL,ROUND(SUM(cs_numendings_m*cs_avg_conn_goodput_rcv_m)/SUM(cs_numendings_m),2)) ... [cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m] formula=IF(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_snt)=0,NULL,ROUND(SUM(avg_conn_goodput_snt)/SUM(cs_numendings),2)) merge_formula=IF(SUM(cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m)=0,NULL,ROUND(SUM(cs_numendings_m*cs_avg_conn_goodput_snt_m)/SUM(cs_numendings_m),2)) ... Step#3: Save the file and restart the monpd service. tmsh restart /sys service monpd
