bugs.fix: ASM-SignatureFile_20230609_051926 has fixed the performance issue with those signatures. Install the updated signature that includes this improvement, and ensure that you purge the old rule.

bugs.title: Misleading error logs in SAML flow
bugs.symptoms: In a successful SAML Authentication, some unrelated and misleading errors are logged. For example, although there is no Artifact involved, you may see the below message: Failed to retrieve SAMLArtifact_b64 for SAML Agent:
bugs.conditions: Universal conditional statements written to handle different use cases of SAML authentication such as POST or ARTIFACT bindings unintentionally prints few error logs.
bugs.impact: Errors logs are misleading.
bugs.fix: All the errors logs can be converted to debug logs.

bugs.title: OSPF summary might have incorrect cost when advertised by Standby unit.
bugs.symptoms: OSPF summary might have incorrect cost when advertised by Standby unit.
bugs.conditions: - Other protocol redistribution into OSPF causing a summary route injection.
bugs.impact: Undesired traffic flow towards Standby unit.
bugs.workaround: Redistribute a summary route from static: Use: ! router ospf 1 redistribute static metric-type 1 network 10.10.10.0.32 0.0.0.255 area 0 ! ip route 192.168.0.0/16 Null Instead of: ! router ospf 1 redistribute bgp metric-type 1 network 10.10.10.0.32 0.0.0.255 area 0 summary-address 192.168.0.0/16

bugs.title: DAG transition does not complete when TMM starts in FORCED_OFFLINE mode
bugs.symptoms: When TMM restarts with force-offline enabled, it comes up waiting for a dag_transition. It never completes because CDP proxy never comes up due to no active traffic group in FORCE_OFFLINE mode.
bugs.conditions: Restarting TMM with force-offline enabled.
bugs.impact: Tenants show high CPU and idle enforcer constantly starting or exiting.
bugs.workaround: Do not perform upgrade/restart in force-offline mode.

bugs.title: Virtual address statistics being counted for different virtual address after changing the destination address of a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: After modifying the destination address of a virtual server to a new address, the virtual address statistics for subsequent traffic are still being tracked in the original virtual address.
bugs.conditions: -- Create the virtual server with a destination address -- Change the destination address of a virtual server to new address
bugs.impact: Incorrect statistics will fail to reflect actual virtual address load.

bugs.title: Sflow receiver flows are not established at TMM startup on sDAG platforms due to sDAG delay
bugs.symptoms: No sflow data is sent.
bugs.conditions: Either configure a valid sflow receiver and restart the tmm or, configure a valid sflow receiver reachable via dynamic route on non sDAG platforms and restart the tmm.
bugs.impact: Sflow data is dropped.
bugs.workaround: Modify the receiver configuration (any field, including description). This allows triggering an update which will get sflow working.
bugs.fix: Sflow receiver configurations can be configured at the TMM startup.

bugs.title: Update OEM login banner
bugs.symptoms: The login page banner (login page)in OEM builds displays outdated text.
bugs.conditions: Navigate to login page in OEM build.
bugs.impact: Changes are required to update the login banner text.
bugs.fix: Updated login banner with new text for OEM builds

bugs.title: Duplicate OID index warnings observed in /var/log/ltm
bugs.symptoms: Run snmpwalk receiving warning msg "Duplicate oid index found: bigip_l2_forward_stat.c:128" in ltm logs
bugs.conditions: Snmpwalk -v2c -Of -c public localhost .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.1.2.5.1 or snmpwalk -v2c -Of -c public localhost .1.3.6.1.4.1.3375.2.1.2.5.2
bugs.impact: Ltm logs with warning message "Duplicate oid index found:"
bugs.workaround: 1.Log in to the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) by typing the following command: tmsh 2.Add the filter by typing the following command: modify /sys syslog include "filter f_local0 { facility(local0) and not match(bigip_l2_forward_stat); };" 3.Save the changes by typing the following command: save /sys config

bugs.title: Memory leak in PEM when Policy is queried via TCL
bugs.symptoms: Memory leak of struct size ummem_alloc_112.
bugs.conditions: [PEM::session config policy get [IP::client_addr]] If above configuration is present in irule/format script and subscriber has ipv6 address.
bugs.impact: Memory leak of struct size ummem_alloc_112. TMM may go out of memory, may restart and cause service disruption.
bugs.workaround: Avoid getting policy via tcl command for IPv6 subscriber. Remove below configuration: [PEM::session config policy get [IP::client_addr]]
bugs.fix: Code fixed to avoid memory leak. cb_cookie object was not getting freed sometimes. Made sure its freed in all the required cases.

bugs.title: ASM requests to rechunk payload
bugs.symptoms: ASM requests TMM to rechunk payload in following scenarios: - Content-Length header was not found on response headers. - Response with headers only.
bugs.conditions: Content-Length header is missing from the HTTP response.
bugs.impact: Transfer-Encoding: chunked header is added to the response.
bugs.workaround: In case response connection: close header exists, user can configure internal parameter is_disable_rechunk, then ASM would not ask to rechunk response.
bugs.fix: On "Fixed" versions, create an internal ASM parameter as "is_disable_rechunk" below and restart ASM service, which would then stop tagging "Transfer Encoding: Chunked" in the Response header.

bugs.title: One defective SFP blocks all other SFP ports on I2C
bugs.symptoms: If a port has a defective SFP, then the I2C is blocking all the ports connected to it.
bugs.conditions: Have a defective SFP on the I2C bus.
bugs.impact: Traffic cannot be processed as all the ports are blocked.
bugs.workaround: Remove the problematic SFP and reboot the device.

bugs.title: Allow configuration of the number of times the CNAME chase is performed
bugs.symptoms: The client receives a SERVFAIL when the CNAME queried to the BIG-IP DNS resolver takes more than the limit configured in the DNS Cache. The limit is set as 11 for BIG-IP v17.1.0 and later. It is fixed as 8 for earlier releases.
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP DNS is configured as a resolver (as a cache or a net resolver). The domain of which CNAME resolution is asked requires chasing more times than what is pre-configured in the DNS Cache.
bugs.impact: The clients cannot resolve DNS names if the count of the CNAME chases goes beyond the limit configured in the DNS cache.
bugs.workaround: The providers whose CNAME is queried can be asked to keep chains shorter than the pre-configured limits (the limits vary between different versions of BIG-IP).
bugs.fix: A new DB variable sys db dnscache.maxqueryrestarts is introduced to allow configuration of the number of times the CNAME chase is performed.

bugs.title: AFM is not accounting Nxdomain attack for TCP query
bugs.symptoms: AFM is not accounting NXDOMAIN query with tcp. At the device level, NXDOMAIN stats are incorrect.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS cache is activated -- An NXDOMAIN DoS vector occurs
bugs.impact: NXDOMAIN flood attack is not detected.
bugs.fix: AFM is now accounting Nxdomain attack for TCP query

bugs.title: Failed to load detected bots list , when you clicked on Bot Category
bugs.symptoms: An error occurs while trying to access the bot event logs.
bugs.conditions: The bot events logs has N/A bot categories, and you clicked on one of them to see details.
bugs.impact: After clicking on the N/A bot categories, you will get an error when you click on a specific category in the event logs (for example, if you click on “Search Engine Masquerading” in Bot Categories)
bugs.workaround: "bigstart restart asm" will allow to click again and see details for a specific category. But if you click again on the 'N/A' bot category in the events log, it will reproduce again the issue.
bugs.fix: You can see the details for a specific category and for N/A with no errors.

bugs.title: In APM, persistent cookie and logout URI options are not compatible together
bugs.symptoms: After hitting the logout URI, BIG-IP is setting contradictory Set-Cookie headers, one to remove APM cookies after the logout timeout and another one to enforce the persistent cookie option.
bugs.conditions: Configure an APM with a logout URI as well as Cookies options set to persistent.
bugs.impact: Persistent cookie option will not work as intended when a logout URI is configured. Session will be removed on the BIG-IP when logout URI is hit and persistent cookie from the client will not be valid.
bugs.workaround: An iRule can be used to remove the Set-Cookie set by the persistent cookie option whenever logout URI is hit.

bugs.title: Some connections on standby not closing when using state.mirror verify
bugs.symptoms: Connections on standby are not closing after they have been closed on the server. These connections on standby will only eventually be cleaned up once the idle timeout expires.
bugs.conditions: Rare condition.
bugs.impact: Standby accumulates and hold more connections than the active leading to resource allocations depletion on standby faster than active.
bugs.workaround: Avoid the use of state.mirror verify and the issue will not occur.

bugs.title: Large numbers of URLs in url-db can cause TMM to restart
bugs.symptoms: TMM continuously restarts during startup.
bugs.conditions: This was seen when the url-db had about 64K glob URLs. Most of the globs were of the form "*foo*".
bugs.impact: TMM is unusable.
bugs.workaround: Large numbers of globs that start with the below should be OK: ".*://" ".*://.*＼＼." Note that there should be no other special glob characters, so ".*://www.example.com" would be OK but ".*://www.example.com*" might not be.

bugs.title: MCPD may crash when creating a new user.
bugs.symptoms: When existing Linux users are present along with a passwd.lock file, adding a new user via TMSH results in an MCPD crash.
bugs.conditions: /etc/passwd.lock file exists
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system will crash.
bugs.workaround: remove /etc/passwd.lock
bugs.fix: lu_user_delete() requires *error == NULL on entry. Leaving lerror set at this point can cause libuser to abort() later.

bugs.title: Duplicate SYNs to a mirrored FastL4 virtual may result in connection failures
bugs.symptoms: If a duplicate SYN arrives on a connection before the SYN/ACK is processed and the connection is pushed into PVA, then when it is later evicted from PVA it may stop passing traffic and be reset with the RST cause "Handshake Timeout".
bugs.conditions: - PVA enabled - Mirroring enabled - Duplicate SYNs on the network
bugs.impact: Connection will stop passing traffic and resets when they are evicted from PVA.
bugs.workaround: Perform one of the following as a workaround: - Disable PVA - Disable mirroring - Modify sys db tm.fastl4_ack_mirror value to Disable - Modify sys db tm.fastl4_mirroring_taciturn value to Enable.

bugs.title: Pool member monitored by both GTM and LTM monitors may be erroneously marked Down
bugs.symptoms: A GTM or LTM pool member may occasionally be marked Down in error if it is being monitored by the same type of monitor with the same name as another LTM or GTM pool member with the same address and port.
bugs.conditions: This may occur if all of the following conditions are true: -- A pool member for one module (GTM or LTM) has the same address and port as a pool member for a different module (LTM or GTM). -- Both pool members are monitored by a monitor of one of the following types: -- Microsoft SQL -- MySQL -- Oracle -- PostgreSQL -- lDAP -- Radius -- Radius-Accounting -- Scripted -- SIP -- WAP -- Both pool members are monitored by monitors of the same type (from the list above). -- Both monitors have the same name (exact match).
bugs.impact: A GTM or LTM pool member may occasionally be marked Down in error.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue, assign different names to GTM versus LTM health monitors of the same time (from the list of types above) that are used to monitor pool members for different modules with the same address and port values.

bugs.title: A certain client sequence via MRF passthrough may cause TMM to core
bugs.symptoms: If the client sends certain traffic through a SIP ALG VIP with passthrough enabled, MRF cores the TMM.
bugs.conditions: Client needs to send certain traffic pattern.
bugs.impact: TMM core
bugs.fix: MRF doesn't core TMM when certain traffic is played through a SIP ALG VIP with passthrough enabled

bugs.title: SIGSEGV core during HUDEVT_EXPIRED
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes on SIGSEGV.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while passing traffic through tmm.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a tmm crash.

bugs.title: Sync Status: Disconnected. ARP replies suspected to be dropped at the innterface
bugs.symptoms: HA Sync Status is "Disconnected" and config sync fails.
bugs.conditions: ARP replies are not received by TMM in one of the devices in an HA pair.
bugs.impact: The devices will be in Disconnected state.
bugs.workaround: Disable and enable interfaces of trunks or delete and recreate trunks or bigstart restart bcm56xxd

bugs.title: iSeries LCD displays "Host inaccessible or in diagnostic mode"
bugs.symptoms: On rare occasions, while booting up an iSeries BIG-IP system, the LCD may continuously display "Host inaccessible or in diagnostic mode" message for an extended period of time.
bugs.conditions: This can occur when booting up an iSeries BIG-IP system.
bugs.impact: LCD is unusable until the system is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: Wait for 5 minutes. If the LCD is still displaying the "Host inaccessible or in diagnostic mode" message after the specified time period, reboot the BIG-IP system.

bugs.title: Configuration option decode_value_as_base64 under parameters cannot be modified using thrift request
bugs.symptoms: The modification of decode_value_as_base64 is working fine from REST calls but it's not working from thrift calls.
bugs.conditions: A thrift call is made to modify the value of decode_value_as_base64.
bugs.impact: Cannot modify decode_value_as_base64 from thrift calls.
bugs.workaround: Use REST call to modify the value of decode_value_as_base64.
bugs.fix: Decode_value_as_base64 is now exposed via thrift so that it can be modfied.

bugs.title: Parameter does not have an option in UI to configure Base64 Decoding as disabled
bugs.symptoms: Parameter does not have an option in UI to configure Base64 Decoding as disabled although it is possible through REST
bugs.conditions: - ASM policy exists - Parameter exists
bugs.impact: Base64 Decoding option in GUI for parameter do not work as expected
bugs.fix: Base64 Decoding option in GUI for parameter works as expected

bugs.title: DecodeValueAsBase64 value not retained as disabled after import of JSON policy
bugs.symptoms: DecodeValueAsBase64 value for a parameter is not retaining the 'disabled' setting when you import a JSON policy
bugs.conditions: Export a policy with a parameter as isBase64=false from 16.1.x and import it
bugs.impact: Mismatch of values across the versions
bugs.fix: After JSON policy import Base64 decoding value is retained.

bugs.title: [vCMP] Guest on v15.1.8+, on startup chmand publishes incorrect interface_media_active for mgmt interface
bugs.symptoms: Upon system boot, chmand will publish incorrect information to mcpd regarding the mgmt interface (interface_media_active). The mgmt interface will be passing traffic normally, but if you query mcpd (e.g., 'tmsh show net interface') it will display incorrect information (mgmt interface will have 'media' showing as 'none').
bugs.conditions: Guest version - 15.1.8+ Host version - irrelevant
bugs.impact: Cosmetic only, no impact on the internal working.
bugs.workaround: Restarting the chmand service fixes the issue.

bugs.title: SSL profile "no-dtlsv1.2" option is left disabled while upgrading from v14.x or v15.x to 17.1.0
bugs.symptoms: Starting from 16.0.0, given DTLSv1.2 support, "no-dtlsv1.2" option is newly available on SSL profile. Default value is "no-dtlsv1.2" option enabled. While upgrading from older version to 16.0.0 or later, by default "no-dtlsv1.2" option is to be automatically enabled with following notification message. > bigip1 warning mcpd[XXXX]: 0107185a:4: Warning generated, for version 16.0.0 or greater : /Common/[SSL-profile-name], default option no-dtlsv1.2 set. However, when user directly upgrades from v14.x/v15.x to v17.1.0, "no-dtlsv1.2" option may not be automatically enabled on SSL profile.
bugs.conditions: - roll-forward upgrade from v14.x/v15.x to v17.1.0. upgrade from v16.x to v17.1.0 is not affected. - custom client|server-ssl profile configured on pre-upgrade version v14.x/v15.x
bugs.impact: After upgrade to 17.1.0, "no-dtlsv1.2" option may not be enabled on SSL profile.
bugs.workaround: After upgrade to 17.1.0, manually enable "no-dtlsv1.2" option.

bugs.title: Ssh to localhost not working with ssh-rsa
bugs.symptoms: The password prompt is not displayed when trying ssh to localhost.
bugs.conditions: 1. Create test_user, # tmsh create auth user test_user password abcde shell bash session-limit -1 partition-access replace-all-with { all-partitions { role admin } } # tmsh save sys config 2. Try login localhost using test_user, config # ssh test_user@localhost config # --->!!!!! no password prompt shown up
bugs.impact: SSH to localhost will not work.
bugs.workaround: Ssh-rsa key was deprecated on 17.1.0.1 and need to replace/copy ECDSA key to ssh_known_hosts. Replacing the RSA key in ssh_known_hosts with the ECDSA key. sed -ie '/^localhost/s//#&/' /config/ssh/ssh_known_hosts; echo "locahost,localhost.localdomain $(cat /config/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key.pub)" >> /config/ssh/ssh_known_hosts

bugs.title: HTTP iRule event HTTP_REQUEST_DATA is triggered even though there is no data collected via HTTP::collect command.
bugs.symptoms: When an HTTP request does not have any payload, and nothing is collected from HTTP::collect but HTTP_REQUEST_DATA event is triggered on v16.1.x onwards but in v15.1.x it's not triggered.
bugs.conditions: -- iRule configured with HTTP::collect in HTTP_REQUEST event. -- HTTP request does not contain any payload.
bugs.impact: Change in behavior due to unintended event trigger.

bugs.title: Flows that are terminated by an ILX streaming plugin may not expire immediately
bugs.symptoms: Flows that are terminated from a plugin may not shutdown/expire properly until expiry timeout which leads to bloating of the flow table
bugs.conditions: -- ILX streaming plugin configured -- Connection close initiated from the plugin (flow.client.end)
bugs.impact: Flows will stay in the table till expiry and may bloat up the flow table

bugs.title: Missing cluster hearbeart packets in clusterd process and the blades temporarily leave the cluster
bugs.symptoms: If two or more clusterd processes experience a long HAL timeout communicating with chmand, then either of those clusterd process will report a lack of cluster heartbeart packets and one or more blades will leave the cluster. Here are two example log messages that will occur when this issue is encountered. # slot 3 marking itself as failed because of a partition event where the heartbeat timeout only occurred on the mgmt_bp interface. err clusterd[21260]: 013a0004:3: Marking slot 3 SS_FAILED due to partition detected on mgmt_bp from peer 4 to local 3 # slot 2 marking slot 1 as failed due to a lack of cluster packets from slot1 on both mgmt and tmm bp interfaces. err clusterd[29069]: 013a0004:3: Local slot 2: not getting clusterd pkts from slot 1; timed out on mgmt_bp and tmm_bp after 10 seconds. Marking peer slot 1 SS_FAILED These messages are not unique to this bug. There are other bugs and conditions that can cause clusterd to stop sending/receiving heartbeat packets.
bugs.conditions: 1) Multi-blade chassis with a minimum of 5 blades. More blades increases the chances of encountering this bug. 2) A condition that causes long HAL delays between clusterd and chmand. One condition of long HAL delays that is specific to 14.1.x and prior is a full config sync. However that condition was fixed in 15.1.0 and higher with the changes for ID 721020 and ID 746122.
bugs.impact: A blade will temporarily leave the cluster but then re-join unless ID 1273161 or something similar also occurs. If the # of blades leaving the cluster causes the number of online blades to be less then the min-up-members, min-up-members-enabled is set to 'yes' and the chassis is Active a failover will occur.

bugs.title: TMM may crash after performing a full sync, when in-tmm monitors are configured and ssl-profile is changed
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash after performing a full sync
bugs.conditions: - In-tmm monitors are configured (bigd.tmm = enable) - Full sync is performed - Monitors are using a custom ssl profile - The ssl profile was changed as part of the full sync.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted on the BIG-IP that recieved the config sync while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Disable in-tmm monitors, and avoid performing a full sync after modifying in-tmm ssl monitors.

bugs.title: Drop in performance with high throughput on BIG-IP 15.1.9 Virtual Edition or tenants on r2000 or r4000 hosts.
bugs.symptoms: Up to 30% drop in performance due to non-optimal DAG algorithm.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP version 15.1.9 or 15.1.9.1 BIG-IP Virtual Edition or tenants on r2x00 or r4x00 systems.
bugs.impact: There is up to a 30% drop in the performance of the traffic. The impact will be higher on systems where packet throughput is very high and a substantial amount of the CPU use was already used for servicing packet throughput.

bugs.title: A platform error can cause DAG context to be out of sync with the tenant
bugs.symptoms: A platform error can cause the DAG context to be out of sync with the tenant.
bugs.conditions: - Writing DAG state
bugs.impact: Performance and connectivity are limited.
bugs.workaround: Restart the tenant.
bugs.fix: A platform error can no longer cause dag context to be out of sync with the tenant

bugs.title: Tmm crash with QUIC connections
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes while processing QUIC connections.
bugs.conditions: Abnormal disconnect of QUIC connection.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Hourly spike in the CPU usage causing delay in TLS connections
bugs.symptoms: 1. An hourly spike in CPU usage occurs. 2. TMM Idle enforcer gets activated. 3. Users may complain of slow connections once per hour, or timeouts may occur briefly once per hour.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the Clientssl profile is assigned to a virtual server and passing traffic. This happens during the normal operation while running an affected software version.
bugs.impact: TMM CPU Usage goes high for about one second, which may cause a delay in traffic handling, and the Idle Enforcer gets activated briefly.
bugs.workaround: When a workaround fix is applied via an EHF, a DB key is needed to be disabled for the fix to take effect. tmm.ssl.useffdhe It enables or disables the timely generation of FFDHE key pairs and the default value is set to true. When the db variable is true (enabled), BIG-IP will generate FFDHE key pairs periodically as usual. When the db variable is false (disabled), BIG-IP will disable the periodic generation of FFDHE key pairs of size >= 2048 bits. If ClientHello sends only DH groups during handshake to a virtual server, and BIG-IP is configured with tmm.ssl.useffdhe = false, then BIG-IP can still provide the FFDHE key pair for the handshake through the DH key pair available in the cache if any, or offload the request to software crypto. To enable the fix post-EHF installation, you should run $ tmsh modify sys db tmm.ssl.useffdhe value false
bugs.fix: A new db variable is introduced in the fix - tmm.ssl.useffdhe It enables or disables the timely generation of FFDHE key pairs and the default value is set to true. When the db variable is true (enabled), BIG-IP will generate FFDHE key pairs periodically as usual. When the db variable is false (disabled), BIG-IP will disable the periodic generation of FFDHE key pairs of size >= 2048 bits. If ClientHello sends only DH groups during handshake to a virtual server, and BIG-IP is configured with tmm.ssl.useffdhe = false, then BIG-IP can still provide the FFDHE key pair for the handshake through the DH key pair available in the cache if any, or offload the request to software crypto. Some default profiles are configured with cipher-groups using DH groups and are therefore incompatible with disabling this variable. This variable should not be disabled when using any profile with cipher groups from the following: f5-aes, f5-cc-stip, f5-default, f5-ecc, f5-fips, f5-hw_keys, f5-quic, and f5-secure

bugs.title: Incorrect counting of non basic latin characters for min/maxLength
bugs.symptoms: When a string field in the JSON schema has minLength/maxLength constraints, they are incorrectly interpreted as constraints on the number of bytes instead of the number of characters.
bugs.conditions: JSON profile with a schema that includes a string field with minLength and maxLength constraints.
bugs.impact: Requests incorrectly blocked, due to interpreting the constraints as byte length rather than character length.
bugs.workaround: NoneString fields in JSON schema now correctly interpret minLength/maxLength constraints based on character length rather than byte length
bugs.fix: String fields in JSON schema now correctly interpret minLength/maxLength constraints based on character length rather than byte length

bugs.title: IKEv2 allow SK_ logging to be enabled without debug2
bugs.symptoms: SK_logging requires you to enable multiple db variables and debug2 logging. When it is enabled, the message ID is the same for all the logs.
bugs.conditions: - Create tunnels, enable below sys-db variables ipsec.debug.logkeys ipsec.debug.logsk ipsec.debug.pfkey.msg - Enable debug2 logging
bugs.impact: Configuring IKEv2 key logging is cumbersome and the logs are difficult to parse through when there are many tunnels.

bugs.title: When blade replacement happens, signature config is lost in bigip.conf when IM is loading on a new blade
bugs.symptoms: The bigip.conf file differs before and after blade replacement
bugs.conditions: It happens when one of the blades is replaced
bugs.impact: The bigip.conf does not list all the signatures added in the IM which is active
bugs.workaround: 1) Try the command "tmsh save sys config" 2) If step 1 does not resolve the issue then try reloading the IM (Move to Factory Defaults IM and load the IM again). Then the bigip.conf will be updated with all the signatures supported by that IM)

bugs.title: Case APM as SAML IDP does not include all certs from bundle when metadata file is exported
bugs.symptoms: Exported IDP/SP metadata file does not include multiple certificates.
bugs.conditions: 1. BIG-IP configured as IDP/SP. 2. Certificate files containing multiple certificates are attached to the "Local SP/IDP service" configuration. 3. Perform metadata export of the "Local SP/IDP service" object.
bugs.impact: This issue may cause SAML functionality outage as 'corrupted'/'not correct' metadata from apm as saml idp is going to be shared with saml SPs.
bugs.workaround: Edit the metadata file to include other certificates also by adding them under additional XML tags <ds:X509Certificate> /ds:X509Certificate>.

bugs.title: ASM remote logging does not log to an IP address in a non-default route domain
bugs.symptoms: Starting in BIG-IP v17.1.0, ASM remote-logging to a non-default route domain does not work. The file /var/log/bd.log contains an error similar to the line below: --- BD_MISC|ERR |Jun 06 08:39:35.615|21037|LoggingAccount.cpp:4323|getaddrinfo error: unknown name or service ---
bugs.conditions: -- ASM provisioned -- ASM remote logging destination IP has a non-default route domain configured
bugs.impact: Remote logging to an IP address in a non-default route domain does not function.
bugs.workaround: Use ASM remote logging with default route domain (use an IP address that does not have a %xxx suffix)

bugs.title: BD daemon may consume excessive resource and crash
bugs.symptoms: High UMU memory utilization, this can be observed by looking at log messages in the /var/log/ts/bd.log file.
bugs.conditions: -- using v17.1.x -- certain request patterns
bugs.impact: This may cause excessive memory use by the BD daemon, leading to a BD crash and TMM failover. Memory use of tmm may increase as well in xdata component.
bugs.fix: Memory use now under control.

bugs.title: Allow SIP reply with missing FROM
bugs.symptoms: SIP Reply with a missing FROM in the header is dropped.
bugs.conditions: - SIP header not compliant with RFC requirement that a FROM must be present.
bugs.impact: SIP reply drop impacts the client not getting a response.
bugs.fix: Set allow-unknown-methods to be enabled in the SIP session profile, which relaxes the SIP parser to allow unknown SIP messages to be used.

bugs.title: AFM does not detect NXdomain attack (for DNS express)
bugs.symptoms: AFM does not account for NXDOMAIN query when DNS express is in use. At the device level, NXDOMAIN stats are incorrect.
bugs.conditions: -- DNS express is enabled -- NXDOMAIN DoS vector detection is enabled
bugs.impact: NXDOMAIN attack is not detected.
bugs.fix: Supported NXDOMAIN DOS Vector with DNSX (DNS Express)

bugs.title: IPI not working on a new device - 401 invalid device error from BrightCloud
bugs.symptoms: IPI update is failing with below error: iprepd|ERR|Jun 09 15:52:59.261|9847|getipfile failed with status code: 401: Unauthorized: Invalid or missing credentials OEM, Device, or UID iprepd|ERR|Jun 09 15:52:59.261|9847|Error code 1029: InvalidUserCredentials iprepd|ERR|Jun 09 15:52:59.261|9847|Server message: Invalid Device (f5#ipintelligence-c130 from 202.187.110.1)
bugs.conditions: Only IPI update will stop working.
bugs.impact: IPI stop working.
bugs.workaround: No workaround
bugs.fix: IPI license will work for all platforms.

bugs.title: Dot at the end of an URL is ignored
bugs.symptoms: Request with a signature ending with a dot (.) character does not raise a violation.
bugs.conditions: - Enable all signatures - A request occurs that contains a signature and ends with a dot.
bugs.impact: No signature is detected
bugs.fix: All signatures ending with a dot are raised when its signature is On.

bugs.title: Export security policy XML format fail with "too large and cannot be exported" message
bugs.symptoms: Extremely large policies may fail to export in XML format.
bugs.conditions: This is caused when an extremely large security policy is exported in XML format.
bugs.impact: The policy cannot be exported in XML format.
bugs.workaround: The policy may be exported in Binary or JSON format.

bugs.title: SMTP Server Password set through GUI gets truncated to 64 characters
bugs.symptoms: When a BIG-IP administrator tries to set password of length greater than 64 characters through GUI, then it gets truncated to only 64 characters. which in turn results in failure of Email Agent in access policy.
bugs.conditions: A limitation on maximum length of username and password to 64 characters are applied by the BIG-IP admin GUI, which directly stores a truncated string into the configuration resulting in failure of authentication of SMTP server.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP administrator will not be able to set usernames or passwords with length greater than 64 characters.
bugs.workaround: Set the password through TMSH.

bugs.title: ASM::unblock iRule is ignored for violation rating block reason
bugs.symptoms: Violation Rating is checked again on the response, where ASM::unblock irule has no effect, causing the request to be blocked (at response side).
bugs.conditions: -- WAF Policy is attached to the virtual server. -- ASM::unblock iRule is attached to the virtual server. -- Violation Rating violation is set to "block". -- A request reaches high violation rating threshold.
bugs.impact: Request is blocked (on the response side), even though ASM::unblock took place.
bugs.fix: Ignore violation rating in response if all scores were given from request.

bugs.title: Mac masquerade not working after VLAN movement on host interfaces
bugs.symptoms: Connectivity to the floating IP via the masquerade MAC fails when the VLAN is moved across interfaces.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP is configured with a floating IP on a traffic group -- MAC masquerade is enabled -- The VLAN is assigned to a different interface
bugs.impact: Connectivity to the floating IP address fails following a failover.
bugs.workaround: After the VLAN movement, delete and reconfigure the MAC masquerade.

bugs.title: Updating the masquerade address on a traffic-group fails
bugs.symptoms: Updating the masquerade address on a traffic-group does not work when the VLAN is moved between interfaces.
bugs.conditions: -- MAC masquerade is enabled on a traffic group with a floating IP. -- The VLAN is moved to a different interface on the host
bugs.impact: Following a failover, the floating IP address is unreachable.
bugs.workaround: Delete the masquerade MAC and reconfigure it.

bugs.title: Invalid response may be sent to a client when a http compression profile and http analytics profile attached to a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: The number 617 and a script is included in the beginning of an HTTP response that is sent to a client.
bugs.conditions: -- Both the http compression profile and http analytics profile are attached to a virtual server -- The server replies with a chunked response
bugs.impact: An invalid HTTP response is sent to the client.

bugs.title: DDM Receive Power value reported in ltm log is ten times too high
bugs.symptoms: The BCM56xxd process reports erroneous Receive Power value for an interface when Digital Diagnostics Monitoring (DDM) is enabled. The reporting within /var/log/ltm is erroneous by shifting a decimal point and is off by a factor of 10: 2023-06-14T17:10:35.282+00:00 bigip1 err bcm56xxd[11534]: 012c0017:3: DDM interface:2.2 receive power too high warning. Receive power:7.7933 mWatts The "show /net interface-ddm" output for this interface displays a different value: Digital Diagnostic Monitoring Interface:2.2 Laser Transmit and Receive Power Value Receive Power1 0.7904mW -1.02dBm
bugs.conditions: DDM is enabled with the "ddm.bcm56xxd.enable" db variable: sys db ddm.bcm56xxd.enable { value "enable" }
bugs.impact: Incorrect Receive Power value is recorded in warning logs.

bugs.title: DNSSEC response is not signed when failure-rcode-response is enabled and no record is returned
bugs.symptoms: DNS response is not signed for DNSSEC zone for DNSSEC request.
bugs.conditions: 1. A DNSSEC zone exists. 2. Return Code on Failure is enabled and SOA Negative Caching TTL is set to 0. 3. A query hits that wideIP and does not get a pool member selected.
bugs.impact: DNS response is not signed.
bugs.workaround: SOA Negative Caching TTL set to a number larger than 0.
bugs.fix: DNSSEC response is signed when failure-rcode-response is enabled, and relevant records are returned.
bugs.behavior: SOA records are included in the DNS response even for queries with a negative TTL (failure-rcode-response) from a WideIP that has no pools attached. Additionally: 1. NSEC3 and RRSIG records are correctly generated and signed for DNSSEC validation. 2. DNS validating clients no longer reject the response; the query completes successfully with DNSSEC validation.

bugs.title: Set-Cookie header has no value (cookie-string) in server-side, due to asm.strip_asm_cookies
bugs.symptoms: Set-Cookie header has no value (cookie-string) in server-side.
bugs.conditions: - asm.strip_asm_cookies is enabled. - Cookie header from client has TS cookie(s) that are the only cookie.
bugs.impact: Cookie header without value (cookie-string) is sent to server-side
bugs.workaround: Use an iRule to delete Cookie header in the server-side.

bugs.title: Unable to add Geo regions with spaces into blacklist, Error: invalid on shun entry adding
bugs.symptoms: Unable to add Geo regions with spaces into blacklist categories. Ex: New South Wales, West Bengal. However, we are able to add regions without spaces Ex:Delhi.
bugs.conditions: Provision AFM license and try to add any geo regions having spaces into blacklist category.
bugs.impact: Cannot mitigate traffic from the above particular Geo regions.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround
bugs.fix: After the code fix, we are able to add the above regions and mitigate traffic.

bugs.title: JWT is corrupted when the claim value is a custom variable assigned in the Variable assign agent
bugs.symptoms: OAuth bearer SSO is configured with "generate JWT", and the JWT includes claims which take "custom variable" as claim value and string as claim type. The JWT is corrupted where the custom variable is populated in Variable assign agent in the VPE, for some values of custom variable, for example, <'Some long garbage string in the Custom Variable'.>
bugs.conditions: - OAuth bearer SSO configured with Generate JWT. - Add custom variable as claim value, for example, %{session.custom.test} which is populated in Variable assign agent in the VPE.
bugs.impact: The JWT token with garbage is added, which later leads to failure of token validation causing failures in accessing applications.
bugs.workaround: As insecure custom variable is added and returned to variable assign agent. Add the custom variable as a normal string in claim value and claim type as string instead of adding to the Variable assign agent.
bugs.fix: As claim value is insecure when added through variable assign VPE agent, included validation check to not decrypt the unencrypted string.

bugs.title: UCS obtained from F5OS tenant with FPGA causes continuous TMM restarts when loaded to BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: TMM restarts continuously after loading a UCS file that was taken from an F5OS tenant with FPGA hardware.
bugs.conditions: The UCS is taken from an F5OS tenant with FPGA hardware (VELOS, r5k, r10k, r12k), and loaded to a non-F5OS tenant BIG-IP system (VE, vCMP guest, Hardware)
bugs.impact: Migrations or moving configurations across dissimilar platforms will not be successful.
bugs.workaround: Delete the file /config/tmm_velocity_init.tcl and reboot the device if necessary. Use the following example commands: # rm -fv /config/tmm_velocity_init.tcl # reboot

bugs.title: Software Update Check status shows Failure
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system is not retrieving software update information as expected; it fails to contact callhome.f5.com or display update eligibility in the Configuration utility or TMOS Shell (tmsh)
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system deployed as a tenant on rSeries
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system cannot automatically check for or receive update notifications.

bugs.title: Unchunked HTML content in response from the server gets chunked on the client-side when HTML profile is attached to a virtual server in v14.1.x
bugs.symptoms: Non-chunked HTML content responses are sent to the client as chunked data.
bugs.conditions: - HTTP profile response chunking is set to 'sustain'. - The virtual server has html/rewrite profile attached. - Server response has content-type not set to text/HTML or text/CSS or no content-type header.
bugs.impact: Unexpected and unwanted chunking behavior.
bugs.workaround: Use response chunking mode 'unchunk'.

bugs.title: APM OAuth AS returned state parameter removes URL encoding
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP APM operates as an OAuth Authorization Server, the state parameter returned to the OAuth client may have its URL encoding removed. The returned value therefore differs from the value supplied by the client The reported client sends a Base64-encoded state value and expects the Authorization Server to return the same opaque value unchanged. Instead, APM returns a redirect Location header containing the decoded form of the state parameter
bugs.conditions: OAuth clients that compare the returned state value with the originally submitted value may reject the authorization response because the values do not match. This can cause OAuth transaction failures or prevent successful completion of the authorization flow The exact end-user impact was not populated in the available bug record
bugs.impact: The issue applies when: - BIG-IP APM is configured as an OAuth Authorization Server - An OAuth client supplies a URL-encoded state parameter - The authorization flow returns the client through a redirect - The encoded representation of the state contains characters that are decoded during response generation

bugs.title: IPsec interface mode tunnel not sending icmp unreachable fragmentation needed
bugs.symptoms: When the ESP packet is not fragmentable and too large for next hop interface, ICMPv4 unreachable (type 3 code 4) or IPv6 packet too large (type 2) is not generated by IPsec interface tunnel.
bugs.conditions: - When the ESP packet is not fragmentable. - When the size of the packet is bigger than MTU.
bugs.impact: This issue causes data loss.
bugs.workaround: Https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000134901

bugs.title: Disable the f5_cspm and f5_p words from the AVR cookie disclosure.
bugs.symptoms: AVR cookie disclosure shows f5_cspm and f5_p words after changing the avr.cspmcachecookiename cookie name.
bugs.conditions: While we curl the application used behind the F5 Big IP.
bugs.impact: Changing the avr.cspmcachecookiename won't disable the f5_cspm and f5_p words from the AVR cookie disclosure.
bugs.workaround: To selectively disable the AVR f5_cspm injection follow the below document. https://clouddocs.f5.com/api/irules/AVR__disable_cspm_injection.html

bugs.title: Connection RST with reason "STREAM max match size exceeded" after upgrading to v16.1.x
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading from version 15.1.8.2 to version 16.1.3.4, connections reset with reason "STREAM max match size exceeded"
bugs.conditions: 1. Configure a virtual server with rewrite profile. 2. Configure an iRule with the stream profile.
bugs.impact: Connection resets causes traffic disturbance.

bugs.title: The graph lines do not match the source translation request value
bugs.symptoms: There is a discrepancy between the source address translation request and the graph value.
bugs.conditions: Security->Reporting: Network Address Translation:Source: Translation source address translation report details do not match the graph lines.
bugs.impact: The average source address translation requests value is not displaying properly on the page.
bugs.workaround: =========== In BIG-IP, open /etc/avr/monpd/monp_tmstat_fw_nat_measures.cfg#7 file. merge_formula=round(sum(src_translation_requests)/period,2) >>>> merge_formula=round(sum(src_translation_requests),2) restart the monpd.

bugs.title: bd instability when using many remote loggers with Arcsight format
bugs.symptoms: When using multiple arcsight remote loggers for an ASM policy, certain requests may cause bd to restart and leave a core file.
bugs.conditions: ASM policy is attached to VS. Multiple remote storage loggers, using arcsight format are attached to vs. Certain traffic patterns.
bugs.impact: bd will restart and leave a core file.
bugs.fix: bd processes traffic as expected.

bugs.title: The tmm/ehash_stat inuse field for listener name hash is incremented but not decremented
bugs.symptoms: The tmm/ehash_stat inuse field for listener name hash is incremented but not decremented.
bugs.conditions: When a virtual server is added or removed or changed.
bugs.impact: Cosmetic issue
bugs.fix: The stat is now decremented properly

bugs.title: MCPD crash on the changes of Device trust sync only group modification
bugs.symptoms: MCPD crashes on policy sync when the APM module is enabled.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs after upgrading to BIG-IP version 16.1.3.3 HF build 0.41.3.
bugs.impact: Unable to introduce a unit into the sync group, which jeopardizes production.

bugs.title: Bcdatabase file gets truncated, deleted and re-downloaded in a loop
bugs.symptoms: Bcdatabase file gets truncated, deleted and re-downloaded in a loop due to BcMd5ChecksumFile function isn't calculating the expected checksum properly and causing the bcdatabase file to re-download in a continuous loop.
bugs.conditions: The expected checksum does not match the checksum calculated by BcMd5ChecksumFile function.
bugs.impact: The bcdatabase file downloading fails.
bugs.fix: Fixing the BcMd5ChecksumFile function to calculate the expected checksum properly.

bugs.title: System Integrity Status: Invalid with some Engineering Hotfixes
bugs.symptoms: After installing an Engineering Hotfix, when to attempt to verify the TPM system integrity with either the "tpm-status" or "tmsh run sys integrity status-check" command, the following error massage may appear: System Integrity Status: Invalid Running the "tpm-status" command with a Verbosity of 1 (or greater) reveals the following detail: Verifying system integrity... ... The signature in 17 is valid Output wrong commandline parameters cmdline is *ro ima_hash=sha256 mce=ignore_ce * The pcr value in 17 is invalid. ... System Integrity Status: Invalid
bugs.conditions: This may occur if the Engineering Hotfix contains changes which cause the following packages to be included in the Engineering Hotfix ISO: -- sirr-tmos -- tboot But the Engineering Hotfix ISO does not contain the following package: -- nash-initrd The contents of the Engineering Hotfix ISO can be checked using the 'isoinfo' utility: isoinfo -Rf -i <path/to/Hotfix-*.iso> | grep -e sirr -e tboot -e nash
bugs.impact: The TPM System Integrity Status is shown as Invalid. This may incorrectly suggest that system integrity has been compromised.

bugs.title: SNMP DCA or WMI monitors cannot be edited using the GUI
bugs.symptoms: Attempting to update snmp_dca or WMI monitors fails with java.lang.NullPointerException.
bugs.conditions: -- A new snmp dca or WMI monitor has been created -- Using the GUI to make a change to the monitor
bugs.impact: You are unable to edit or modify SNMP DCA or WMI monitors via the GUI
bugs.workaround: Use the command line interface or edit the configuration in advanced shell and run tmsh load merge.

bugs.title: Significant performance drop observed for DNS cache validating resolver for responses with indeterminate and insecure validation status
bugs.symptoms: Performance drop observed when changing DNS cache resolver to validating resolver for responses with indeterminate and insecure validation status. To know more about the validation status, check RFC 4035 (section 4.3).
bugs.conditions: - Create a DNS cache validating resolver. - Ensure the responses are with Indeterminate and Insecure validation status. - Observe the performance as compared to responses with secured validation status.
bugs.impact: Performance of validating resolver will be less than expected.

bugs.title: TMM instability when DB variables avr.IncludeServerInURI or avr.CollectOnlyHostnameFromURI are enabled
bugs.symptoms: Certain http queries may lead to TMM restarts.
bugs.conditions: The DB variables avr.IncludeServerInURI or avr.CollectOnlyHostnameFromURI are enabled.
bugs.impact: The TMM may restart, resulting in traffic interruption.
bugs.fix: The DB variables can be enabled and the certain http queries will not lead to a restart anymore.

bugs.title: Restricting VwireObject and VwireNtiObject SHM and it's poll for non required platforms
bugs.symptoms: Unwanted entries are logged on VE vCMP platforms.
bugs.conditions: VE vCMP Platfoms.
bugs.impact: Too many entries are logged with unwanted SHM.
bugs.fix: Restricted VwireObject and VwireNtiObject SHM poll for non required platforms.

bugs.title: Connection on standby may stay until idle timeout when receiving ICMP error
bugs.symptoms: When a pool member server returns an ICMP error, connections will persist on standby while they have been terminated on active.
bugs.conditions: When an ICMP error such as port unreachable is returned by a pool member, the packet will be dropped by the standby while the active will process it immediately and terminate the connection.
bugs.impact: The connection will stay on the standby until the idle timeout expires.
bugs.workaround: Lower idle timeout will reduce the time before it vanishes.

bugs.title: The error "No Access" is displayed when trying to remove Bundle Manager object from list
bugs.symptoms: The error "No Access" is displayed when trying to remove a Bundle Manager object from the list using GUI.
bugs.conditions: When the checkbox next to the Bundle Manager is checked and clicks the Delete button at the bottom of the page, then "No Access" error appears.
bugs.impact: Unable to delete a Bundle Manager.
bugs.workaround: The issue has following two workarounds: - Click on the Bundle Manager and click Delete at the bottom. or - Delete the Bundle Manager from TMSH CLI.

bugs.title: TMM Crash in certain condition when processing IPSec traffic
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions the TMM may crash and leave a core when processing IPSec traffic.
bugs.conditions: The Big-IP is processing IPSec traffic.
bugs.impact: The TMM restarts
bugs.fix: IPSec traffic is handled as expected.

bugs.title: Thresholds set by auto-threshold (full-automatic) are very high
bugs.symptoms: Thresholds set by auto-threshold (fully-automatic) are in the range of 10k when the attack is in short bursts and with low PPS.
bugs.conditions: Send constant traffic at low PPS ((say 9PPS) during a whole week (no stress) mitigation_curr is infinite as expected since there is no stress. Force stress to 97%. mitigation_curr is set to 500. Hard short attacks start/stop (15s attacks - ≥1m no attack). Traffic is dropped according to mitigation_curr. mitigation_curr increases every 5 minutes while continuing to attack backend server every minute or so. While we had an average of 10PPS during more than a week, during periods of reduced attacks and fluctuating traffic above and below the set threshold, it consistently increases the thresholds. This is unexpected, as AFM should not be continuously raising the thresholds. Consequently, there comes a point where AFM permits an excessive amount of traffic, leading to adverse effects on backend servers.
bugs.impact: Due to high threshold set by auto-threshold, mitigation will not happen during attack.
bugs.workaround: No

bugs.title: 1nic VE reloads on every reboot
bugs.symptoms: When Virtual Edition (VE) is configured for 1NIC, you will see the following logs on reboot indicating that configuration has been loaded from file: notice tmsh[12232]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=12232 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=load sys config partitions all base notice tmsh[12392]: 01420002:5: AUDIT - pid=12392 user=root folder=/Common module=(tmos)# status=[Command OK] cmd_data=load sys config partitions all
bugs.conditions: - VE configured in 1NIC mode. - Unit booted either through reboot or power on.
bugs.impact: This is unlikely to have any impact if the VE is in standalone mode but could result in an unexpected config if the configuration files differ. If the VE is part of a device-group, then this will result in a commit id update and the units will show 'Changes pending'.

bugs.title: Large CRL files may only be partially uploaded
bugs.symptoms: When updating a large CRL file in BIG-IP using tmsh, the file may only be partially read due to internal memory allocation failure. Please note that the size of the CRL file causing this issue varies across hardware types, network bandwidth and usage, and system resources.
bugs.conditions: 1. Using tmsh, a large CRL file is updated to an existing CRL. 2. This large CRL file is attached to multiple profiles. 3. The system is under heavy load
bugs.impact: When a large CRL file is attached to a profile, an update may indicate success when only a partial upload has occurred. Connections to VIP with this profile may have unexpected results, such as a certificate not being blocked as expected.
bugs.workaround: A large CRL file can be divided into smaller chunks and loaded into multiple profiles.
bugs.fix: If an error occurs during CRL upload or update, the profiles containing this partial CRL file will be invalidated and further connections to the VIP will be terminated. An error will be logged to /var/log/ltm whenever a CRL file read operation fails due to memory allocation. The log received will look like: 01260028:2: Profile <profile name> - cannot load <CRL file location> CRL file error: unable to load large CRL file - try chunking it to multiple files.

bugs.title: Large CRL file update fails with memory allocation failure
bugs.symptoms: When updating a large CRL file in BIG-IP using tmsh, the file may be partially read due to internal memory allocation failure. Please note that the size of the CRL file causing this issue varies across hardware types, network bandwidth and usage, and system resources.
bugs.conditions: 1. Using tmsh, large CRL file is updated to an existing CRL. 2. This large CRL file is attached to multiple profiles. 3. The tmsh modify command is used multiple time in a short span of time that leads to the memory crunch.
bugs.impact: When large CRL file is attached to the profile which was partially read due to memory allocation failure, the profile gets successfully updated. Connections to VIP with this profile may have unexpected results. For e.g. client connecting to VIP with a revoked client certificate will succeed as the CRL was only partially read.
bugs.workaround: 1. Dynamic CRL / CRLDP on client-ssl profile can be configured to dynamically verify SSL certificate revocation status. 2. OCSP can be enabled on client-ssl profile to validate SSL certificate revocation status.

bugs.title: Upgrade from BIG-IP version 14.0.0 to 17.1.0 fails with hidden DOS
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade from BIG-IP version 14.0.0 to 17.1.0 fails. The machine stays offline.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the hidden DOS profile exists.
bugs.impact: The machine stays offline and the update fails.
bugs.workaround: Change the error response page body from default to custom.
bugs.fix: Allow DOS hidden profile captcha default to be updated.

bugs.title: When renewing SSL certificate/key pairs in an SSL profile, one pair disappears.
bugs.symptoms: When using multiple SSL certificate/key pairs of different types like RSA and EC, when trying to renew the SSL certificate/key pairs of the SSL profile, one pair of certificate/key pairs disappears.
bugs.conditions: Configure two sets of cert/key pairs of different types like RSA and EC types and try to update the client-ssl profile.
bugs.impact: Unable to renew the cert/key pair.
bugs.workaround: Periods that exist in the cert/key name will trigger this bug. Where possible, avoid using the period character in the cert/key name. If periods are required in the cert/key name, you can avoid this behavior by swapping one old/new cert/key pair at a time instead of multiple pairs.

bugs.title: Custom headers and cookies are by default configured with base64 decoding enabled
bugs.symptoms: When custom headers and cookies are created in ASM, the decode_value_as_base64 flag is enabled by default.
bugs.conditions: A custom header or cookie is created
bugs.impact: Decode_value_as_base64 flag is enabled by default.
bugs.workaround: If base64 decoding is not required, then the flag decode_value_as_base64 has to be turned off manually after creating custom header/cookie
bugs.fix: Whenever a custom header or cookie is created, the default value of decode_value_as_base64 flag will now be set to false

bugs.title: Decode_value_as_base64 flag can be modified to enabled for Authorization header
bugs.symptoms: Decode_value_as_base64 flag can be modified to enabled for Authorization header via rest call. This is not allowed as per functional spec.
bugs.conditions: A rest call is made to modify the decode_value_as_base64 flag on Authorization header
bugs.impact: User can erroneously modify decode_value_as_base64 flag on Authorization header which is not allowed
bugs.fix: Decode_value_as_base64 flag cannot be modified for Authorization header now

bugs.title: HTTP::disable not allowed after HTTP::respond
bugs.symptoms: Rule not processed and ltm logs shows this: TCL error: /Common/connect-irule <HTTP_REQUEST> - Illegal value. HTTP::disable not supported when responding or retrying (line 1) invoked from within "HTTP::disable"
bugs.conditions: When an iRule has an HTTP::respond followed by an HTTP::disable, the disable is not allowed.
bugs.impact: iRule not processed.

bugs.title: [AFM] - iRule event "ACL::action allow" skip further events
bugs.symptoms: ACL::action allow rule action works similar to an "Accept Decisively"/allow-final not considering drop actions specified in the AFM explicit FW rules.
bugs.conditions: Adding FW irules with "ACL::action allow" in conjunction with AFM FW policy rules with drop action.
bugs.impact: AFM FW policy drop rules are not honored.
bugs.workaround: The same iRule actions can be achieved with FW policy rules.

bugs.title: TMM may restart on certain DNS traffic
bugs.symptoms: The TMM may restart and leave a core while processing certain DNS traffic when AFM is licensed and enabled.
bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP is licensed and provisioned for AFM. There is a listener processing DNS traffic.
bugs.impact: The TMM crashes and leaves a core file.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: DNS traffic is handled as expected.

bugs.title: CGNAT / AFM NAT: "Clients Using Max Port Blocks" counter might be inaccurate
bugs.symptoms: When using CGNAT or AFM NAT in PBA mode (Port Block Allocation) the value of "Clients Using Max Port Blocks" might be wrong, not reflecting the actual number of total clients who have reached the max port blocks allocated to them. The value of "Clients Using Max Port Blocks" can be seen in the output of the command "tmsh show ltm lsn" along with other statistics.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP running two or more TMM threads - BIG-IP provisioned with CGNAT or AFM NAT - LSN pool using PBA (Port Block Allocation) configured
bugs.impact: The value of "Clients Using Max Port Blocks" is increased when clients reach the max port blocks allocated to them but is not decreased when the clients don't have any more port blocks allocated. As such, it keeps increasing over time.

bugs.title: illegal parameter data type' is detected on 'auto detect
bugs.symptoms: Misinterpreting Other parameter data types as URI type
bugs.conditions: -- Configure a policy that contains a parameter with Parameter Value Type = Auto detect and disable the staging. -- Set Illegal parameter data type in Learning and Blocking Settings to block
bugs.impact: The request is blocked along with other parameter data types
bugs.workaround: Modify the DEFAULT_ecard_regexp_uri through asm internal variables /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal, execute the following command /usr/share/ts/bin/add_del_internal add DEFAULT_ecard_regexp_uri '^＼＼w+:＼＼/＼＼/([^＼＼s@]+@)?([^＼＼s^＼＼/]+)(:＼＼d+)?(＼＼/[^＼＼s]*)?' Don't forget to restart ASM to apply changes: bigstart restart asm

bugs.title: Updated ccmode script
bugs.symptoms: The existing ccmode script does not invoke the required script for system integrity validation.
bugs.conditions: Trigger the ccmode script
bugs.impact: Integrity validation does not occur.
bugs.fix: Remove the integrity check invocation from the ccmode script; the integrity check will be automatically run at boot time.

bugs.title: Some OIDs using type as counter instead of expected type as gauge
bugs.symptoms: While checking via SNMP commands there are number of OIDs in the MIBs that are reporting value as counter that should be gauge/integer
bugs.conditions: Using the following OIDs: ltmDosAttackDataStatDropsRate ltmDosAttackDataStatStatsRate ltmNetworkAttackDataStatDropsRate ltmNetworkAttackDataStatStatsRate ltmVirtualServStatCsMeanConnDur
bugs.impact: Incorrect Type is seen for some OIDs.

bugs.title: Leakage point in storing assertion attributes-string in tmm
bugs.symptoms: Apmd crashes.
bugs.conditions: This can occur while passing SAML traffic.
bugs.impact: Apmd cores. Access traffic disrupted while apmd restarts.
bugs.fix: Fixed a crash in apmd.

bugs.title: Failure configuring GraphQL Schema File with Query type
bugs.symptoms: Upload GraphQL Schema File with Query type fails with the following error: "Idl failed. GraphQL schema parsing failed, 'name' "
bugs.conditions: GraphQL schema files are configured and contain a query type in the schema.
bugs.impact: Unable to configure a GraphQL profile with Query type.
bugs.fix: GraphQL schema files with Query types are now successfully processed.

bugs.title: TMM memory leak when using http+fastl4 profile with 'rtt-from-client/rtt-from-server' enabled.
bugs.symptoms: TMM might experience a memory leak when using FastL4 'rtt-from-client/rtt-from-server' options in conjunction with HTTP profile.
bugs.conditions: A single virtual server configured with: -- HTTP profile. -- Fastl4 profile with 'rtt-from-client/rtt-from-server' enabled.
bugs.impact: Memory leak in TMM process.
bugs.workaround: Disable 'rtt-from-client/rtt-from-server' on Fastl4 profile.

bugs.title: SAML Auth error "Failed to get authentication request from session variable 'session.samlcryptodata.Result'"
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP administrator fails to run a correctly configured SAML SP setup as TMM fails to sign the Authentication Request. This can be triggered on an upgrade from versions earlier than 17.0 to version 17.0 or 17.1.
bugs.conditions: -- APM is configured for clientless mode -- The SAML profile has Redirect Binding enabled -- "Sign Authentication Request" is enabled
bugs.impact: SAML SP authentication fails while signing the Authentication Request.

bugs.title: The gtm_add sync configuration is in the unintended direction with large GTM configuration
bugs.symptoms: A wrong GTM configuration can be pushed to the sync group members after using the script gtm_add.
bugs.conditions: -- Race condition with large GTM configuration while performing gtm_add. -- Following can be seen in GTM debug logs: 011a0200:7: MCP Message queued for resend. 1 backlogged messages. . . . 011a0200:7:MCP Message queued for resend. 1125 backlogged messages.
bugs.impact: GTM devices are given the wrong or unintended configuration.
bugs.workaround: Before running gtm_add make the following changes on the gtm where you intend to execute the gtm_add command: - disable synchronization - disable synchronize-zone-files - change the synchronization group name to match the remote gtm

bugs.title: Upgrading or failover of APM with lot of access policies takes long time to become "really" active
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP Administrator has lot of access policies, around 300 plus, after upgrade or failover a new unit becomes active. Users accessing one of the access policies experience error "(Your session could not be established. The session reference number: b0745df3. Access policy configuration has changed on gateway. Please login again to comply with new access policy configuration". Also, it takes lot of time, around 25 minutes for all the 347 access policies, to become really active.
bugs.conditions: After an upgrade or failover the snapshot creation process gets invoked. And while user accesses a virtual server with access policy whose snapshot is not yet created, errors occur mentioning failure in establishing the session.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP administrator having BIG-IP with a large number of access policies will have to wait for a long time, during and upgrade or failover, for the system to become really active.
bugs.workaround: -No-

bugs.symptoms: Memory leakage in a SAML SP Agent.

bugs.title: Policy with external data group may crash TMM or return nothing with search contains
bugs.symptoms: TMM may crash or return no result found when there is one when using contains external data group.
bugs.conditions: External data group sets first to "starts-with" and then switch to "contains" may crash the TMM. If on the other hand, TMM is started with search "contains" from the start, no results may be found by policy even though there might be a result. The is because, the external policy is not populated at all or entirely before the search happens. The starts-with works as it is populating on demand and is the reason and will partially populate it as needed, but when a switch to "contains" happens, it expects it to be entirely populated.
bugs.impact: TMM crashes or result not found when there should be a result.
bugs.workaround: A workaround is possible if starts-with could be used instead of "contains".
bugs.fix: Search with "contains" will make sure the policy with external data group is entirely populated, avoiding the crash and making a search result successful if there is a match.

bugs.title: Syncookies may always show as enabled if a listener address is changed while syncookies is on
bugs.symptoms: Syncookies may always show as enabled if a listener source or destination address is changed while syncookies is on. The stat epva_hwvipstat.fsu_rx_drops will be non zero when this occurs.
bugs.conditions: Syncookies on Modifications to the source or destination address
bugs.impact: Syncookies will be disabled, but the virtual server status will show syncookies enabled.

bugs.title: vCMP guest loses connectivity because of bad interface mapping
bugs.symptoms: A vCMP guest is no longer able to receive traffic when packets arrive on a trunk interface from other slots.
bugs.conditions: -- A vCMP guest has a trunk interface with one interface on the same slot as the guest and another interface on another slot. -- Another Guest on the same slot is provisioned with more cores, triggering a reboot of that slot

bugs.workaround: A reboot will resolve the issue.

bugs.title: Device DOS drop rate limits are not configured correctly on the FPGA.
bugs.symptoms: Drop limit in dos_stats tmstat table does not match with configured mitigation in device DoS.
bugs.conditions: -- VELOS or rSeries platform -- AFM is enabled -- Configuring device-level DoS mitigation.
bugs.impact: Stats might not be correct if mitigation value is high.

bugs.title: Virtual server name caused buffer overflow
bugs.symptoms: Virtual server name caused buffer overflow and TMM core occurs.
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server is renamed
bugs.impact: TMM cores, traffic disruption can occur.

bugs.title: Sock interface driver might fail to forward some packets.
bugs.symptoms: Sock interface driver might drop packets that require reassembly/re-segmentation on one side of the connection. For example, when client-side is configured with tcp-nagle and the server-side sends a stream of multiple small packets. This can increase latency on BIG-IP Virtual Edition on Azure when TSO/LRO is enabled. Drops can be monitored by running the following command: 'tmctl -d blade tmm/ndal_tx_stats -w 300' column 'drop_rej_dd'.
bugs.conditions: -- sock driver. (See K10142141) -- BIG-IP performing reassembly/re-segmentation on one side of the connection
bugs.impact: Some packets might never be forwarded by the BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: In some cases disabling Nagle Algorithm in TCP profile to avoid reassembly/re-segmentation might improve the performance.

bugs.title: BIG-IP tenant or VE fails to load the config files because the hypervisor supplied hostname is not a FQDN
bugs.symptoms: If a BIG-IP tenant (F5OS) or VE is shut down or rebooted during its initial start, it is possible the system will not become operational when it is started again.
bugs.conditions: VE or F5OS tenant. The mcpd is forced to load the config from the config files, as opposed to the binary database. The config files are missing.
bugs.impact: The tenant or VE will not become operational.

bugs.title: Error when trying to make changes in IPS Profile 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid Devicegroup Reference.
bugs.symptoms: You are unable to make changes in the IPS Profile when it is on a different partition and the device is in a sync-only device group.
bugs.conditions: 1) Create a device group with two devices. (https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K63243467) 2) Create a new partition System > Users > Partition List > Create > Add device group created in step 1 here in the partition 3) On the right corner in BIG-IP UI you can select the partition. Select the new partition created 3) Create a virtual server Local Traffic > Virtual Servers > Virtual server List > create 4) Create a IPS Profile Security > Protocol Inspection > Inspection Profiles > new > select the services you want to add to profile. 5) Add the profile to virtual server. Local Traffic > Virtual Servers > Virtual server List > click on visual server you created > Security > Policies > Protocol Inspection Profile > enabled > select profile name 6) Now go to the profile and try to make changes to action value of any of the signatures or compliances which require IPS subscription.
bugs.impact: The changes related to action value cannot be made in the IPS Profile which is in a different partition on a device which is in sync-only device group.
bugs.fix: After fixing the issue, able to make changes in the IPS Profile and also sync the config between the sync-only device group.

bugs.title: Deleting a partition may cause a sync validation error
bugs.symptoms: Deleting a partition may cause the sync to peers to fail.
bugs.conditions: 1. Have APM Provisioned 2. Create new partition and run config sync 3. Delete the partition and run config sync 4. Fails with error "01070829:5: Input error: Invalid partition ID request, partition does not exist"
bugs.impact: The sync of this change may fail on peers.
bugs.workaround: Disable auto-sync on the device group if it's enabled, delete the partition on all of the peers, and re-enable auto-sync.

bugs.title: Support AFM DOS TCP vectors behavior
bugs.symptoms: Certain AFM DOS TCP vectors are not supported.
bugs.conditions: -- AFM enabled -- New TCP vectors are configured.

bugs.fix: New TCP vectors supported.

bugs.title: Moving VLANs or interfaces between LAGs on F5OS 1.8.0 (R2600) results in loss of connectivity on tenant Self-IP
bugs.symptoms: After moving interfaces/VLANs from one LAG to another (or from interface to LAG) at the host level, there is no connectivity to the Self-IP on the tenant—even though changes appear correctly reflected on both host and tenant sides. No errors are observed in logs, nor are missing MAC addresses detected.
bugs.conditions: -- A LAG exists with assigned interfaces and VLANs. -- Interfaces/VLANs are removed from this LAG. -- A new LAG is created. -- The old LAG is removed from the tenant. -- VLANs are added to a new LAG at host level and verified present on tenant.
bugs.impact: Tenant Self-IP becomes unreachable after these changes. Network connectivity fails for affected VLANs/interfaces.
bugs.workaround: Restart MCPD within the tenant using: bigstart restart mcpd tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: BIG-IP Rewrite Profile GUI and URI Validation is inconsistent
bugs.symptoms: The rewrite profile GUI and Validation is inconsistent. New rewrite UI displays in the following navigation: Rewrite Profile (Local Traffic --> Profiles --> Services --> Rewrite), and click on Create button. bugs.title: FastL4 TCP PVA accelerated connection might not be cleared until idle timeout.
bugs.symptoms: Connection where client is re-using the source port connecting to a server in TIME_WAIT might not be cleared immediately from BIG-IP connection table after the closure.
bugs.conditions: -- FastL4 PVA acceleration at Embryonic. -- Client re-using 4-tuple, hitting server in TIME_WAIT. -- Platform has ePVA (VE, r2xxx, r4xxx have no ePVA)
bugs.impact: Connection will remain in the BIG-IP connection table until idle-timeout is reached.
bugs.workaround: Set 'tcp-pva-whento-offload establish' on a fastl4 profile.

bugs.title: Datapath is interrupted on deleting and readding Static LAG members on R2x00/R4x00 platforms.
bugs.symptoms: When you delete and re-add members of a Static LAG on R2x00/R4x00 platforms, tenants using the Static LAG will have datapath interrupted till the tenant is rebooted.
bugs.conditions: 1. Static LAG is configured on R2x00/R4x00 platform. 2. Tenants are configured with the static VLAN. 3. Once datapath starts working, delete and re-add members of the Static LAG on F5OS.
bugs.impact: Datapath using the static LAG on which members are deleted and re-added is interrupted until the next reboot of tenant.
bugs.workaround: 1. Save the config on the tenant and move the tenant to configured state and back to deployed state. 2. Reboot the tenant.

bugs.title: After config sync, FQDN node status changes to Unknown/Unchecked on peer device
bugs.symptoms: If changes are made to the FQDN node configuration, which has a node monitor configured, and the configuration is synced to a device group, ephemeral nodes generated from the FQDN node may show Availability as “unknown” and Monitor Status as “unchecked”.
bugs.conditions: This may occur on versions of BIG-IP with fixes for ID724824 and ID1006157, under the following conditions: - BIG-IP systems are configured in a device group - The device group is configured for Manual Sync (Full or Incremental) - One or more FQDN nodes are configured with a node monitor (which could be the Default Node Monitor) - A change is made to the configuration of the FQDN node - A Full configuration sync is performed (by a Manual sync with the device group configured for a Full sync, as an automatic fallback/recovery action from a failed Incremental sync, or by using the “force-full-load-push” keyword): tmsh run cm config-sync to-group example-group force-full-load-push
bugs.impact: The affected nodes will be displayed with an Availability as “unknown” and Monitor Status as “unchecked”.
bugs.workaround: To resolve this condition, remove and add the node monitor: - Remove the node monitor from the FQDN node configuration (or from default-node-monitor): tmsh mod ltm node example monitor none (tmsh mod ltm default-node-monitor rule none) - Sync this change to the device group (Incremental sync) - Add the node monitor again to the FQDN node configuration (or to default-node-monitor): tmsh mod ltm node example monitor my_node_monitor (tmsh mod ltm default-node-monitor rule my_node_monitor) - Sync this change to the device group (Incremental sync)

bugs.symptoms: Resources flap, frequent iquery reconnects occur. bugs.title: Previous Username value persists in the same browser after logout

bugs.title: Tmm crash in Google Cloud during a live migration: Assertion `empty xfrag' failed.
