bugs.title: The daemon dwbld uses 100% CPU when max port value configured in TMC port list
bugs.symptoms: When Traffic Matching Criteria (TMC) port list range is configured that includes maximum port value of 65535, counter is incremented till 65535 and wraps back to 0, as the variable used to store the counter is uint16_t.
bugs.conditions: - AFM license enabled. - Daemon dwbld enabled - Any TMC port list configured with maximum port value of 65535
bugs.impact: The daemon dwbld consumes 100% CPU impacting system performance.
bugs.workaround: Avoid configuring maximum port value of 65535 in TMC port list range.
bugs.fix: The counter is changed to uint32_t to avoid rollover when maximum port value is included in port list range.

bugs.title: In an iRule SSL::sessionid returns an empty value
bugs.symptoms: The irule SSL::sessionid command used returns an empty value after an upgrade to v15.1.9.1, when used with a TLS1.3 session. While SSL::sessionid in v15.1.8.2 returns the value specified in the ClientHello for a TLSv1.3 session, upgrading to v15.1.9.1 results in empty values returned when calling SSL::sessionid.
bugs.conditions: 1. Use SSL::sessionid in an iRule 2. Use an affected BIG-IP version 3. Client establishes a TLS1.3 connection
bugs.impact: SSL::sessionid returns an empty value, which could result in unintended behavior for applications that use that iRule command.

bugs.title: Frequent instances of provisioning-pending count spiking on various PEM devices
bugs.symptoms: PEM intermittently fails to provision subscribers and a large number of subscriber sessions go into the provisioning-pending state.
bugs.conditions: -- PEM is enabled -- BIG-IP is configured to create subscriber dynamically and receive subscriber policy from PCRF -- BIG-IP receives a large number of subscriber login/logout requests in a short period.
bugs.impact: New subscribers provisioning fails. Subscribers remain in the provision-pending state.
bugs.fix: With fix, new subscriber provisioning and old subscriber deletion is successful.

bugs.title: For certain iRules, TCP::close does not close the TCP connection
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule generates a TCP::close before a server-side connection is established, the BIG-IP system does not close the connection.
bugs.conditions: Example 1 With this iRule, if there are 2 pipelined http requests, the close will not happen after the first request Sample iRule: proc redirect {loc} { HTTP::redirect $loc TCP::close } when HTTP_REQUEST priority 1 { call redirect https://[getfield [HTTP::host] ":" 1][HTTP::uri] } Example 2: In this second example of iRule where there are no pools involved (say redirects or error message return 404 not found...) when no servers are connected to. In such case, the close will not happen. ltm rule tcp_it { when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { TCP::collect 1 } when CLIENT_DATA { table or other commands for example TCP::respond "reply" (or 404 not found...) TCP::release TCP::close } when CLIENT_CLOSED { log local0. "Client closed" } when SERVER_CONNECTED { log local0. "Server here" } } When such rule involves no servers to be connected - hence "Server here" not displayed - the close will never happen.
bugs.impact: TCP connection lingers in TMM until expiration.

bugs.title: Peer unit incorrectly shows the pool status as unknown after merging the configuration
bugs.symptoms: The peer unit incorrectly shows the state of pool members as "checking" after merging the configuration from the terminal. Note that these are the same symptoms as ID1095217.
bugs.conditions: This is encountered on BIG-IP releases or Engineering Hotfixes with the fix for ID1297257, if two or more configurations are specified for an already configured pool on the peer device when using the command "tmsh load sys config merge from-terminal". Following is an example: Existing pool: ltm pool http_pool { members { member1:http { address <IP address> monitor http } } } tmsh load sys config merge from-terminal: ltm pool http_pool { members none } ltm pool http_pool { members replace-all-with { member1:http { address <IP address> monitor http } } } This may also occur with a similar configuration using the "merge from-file" operation instead of "merge from-terminal". These symptoms, matching ID1095217, occur in the presence of the fix for ID1297257, which removes the original, incorrect fix for ID1095217.
bugs.impact: Pool members are marked with a state of "Checking".
bugs.workaround: Define all object properties at once (in a single configuration block) instead of multiple times (in multiple configuration blocks) when merging the configuration from the terminal.
bugs.fix: Specifying the configuration for an LTM pool object multiple times when issuing the "tmsh load sys config merge from-terminal" command no longer causes LTM pool members to remain marked with a state of "Checking", without resulting in the symptoms of ID1297257.

bugs.title: iApps: Importing the existing RPM package again leaves a bunch of files in /var/config/rest/tmp.XXXXX on 15.1.9.x and causing disk space issue.

This issue does not occur on 15.1.8.2, 16.x and 17.x. This behaviour is causing issues in the disk space.

bugs.impact: Increase in the disk space utilization.
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the temporary files in /var/config/rest/tmp.XXXX

bugs.title: TMM crash when running HTTP/3 and persist record

bugs.impact: The system may core.
bugs.fix: Sipmsg_parse_sdp does not crash when SIP receives the traffic pattern that caused the core previously.

bugs.title: Bypassing Tunnels in ServerIP attack: ServerIP attack, combined with DNS spoofing, that can leak traffic to an arbitrary IP address
Timestamp Cookies and ePVA acceleration are incompatible on VELOS and rSeries platforms
bugs.symptoms: VELOS and rSeries platforms don't support Timestamp Cookies when ePVA acceleration is enabled. When Timestamps Cookies and ePVA acceleration are enabled, the BIG-IP Tenant sends TCP segments to the clients with the wrong TSecr value (part of the TCP Timestamps option). Some clients drop these segments because they don't match any of the Timpestamps TSval values of the segments they previously sent to the BIG-IP Tenant.
bugs.conditions: - VELOS or rSeries platform running a BIG-IP Tenant - A Virtual Server with a fastl4 profile with PVA acceleration enabled and tcp-timestamp-mode set to 'preserve' - Timestamp Cookies enabled (this is an AFM feature): security dos device-config dos-device-config dos-device-vector { tcp-ack-ts { tscookie enabled }}
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP Tenant sends TCP segments with a wrong TCP TSecr value to the clients when Timestamp Cookies are enabled and ePVA acceleration is used. Some clients drop these packets and eventually the TCP connection times out. Some clients may issue a TCP reset.
bugs.workaround: - Disable TS cookies: "tmsh modify security dos device-config dos-device-config dos-device-vector { tcp-ack-ts { tscookie disabled }}" OR - Disable PVA acceleration in the fastl4 profile: "tmsh modify ltm profile fastl4 <profile_name> pva-acceleration none"

bugs.title: ArcSight sends a series of '000000000' values in the remote log in case of Attack Signature Detected.
bugs.symptoms: Series of 0's seen in Arcsight remote logs, in place of the Attack signature ID and Name.
bugs.conditions: Remote logging profile with ArcSight as logging format.
bugs.impact: Attack signature ID and Name is not seen in remote logs.
bugs.workaround: Use Splunk format instead.
bugs.fix: Padding with 0's will not happen.

bugs.title: Login page with URL longer than 128 bytes assigned to brute force causing ASM to restart loop
bugs.symptoms: A login page that is configured with a URL longer than 128 bytes while being assigned to a brute force profile, might cause ASM to be stuck in a restart loop.
bugs.conditions: Login page URL longer than 128 that is assigned to a brute force profile
bugs.impact: ASM might be stuck in a restart loop.
bugs.workaround: Delete the login page and the brute force profile
bugs.fix: No ASM restart looping

bugs.title: DB monitor continues to report pool member as UP after monitor credentials are changed
bugs.symptoms: When the username or password configured in a DB monitor definition (Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, or MSSQL) is changed while the BIG-IP is running, the DB monitor may continue to report the pool member as available (UP) using the previous connection credentials. The monitor does not immediately invalidate and re-establish its persistent database connection when credentials change.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: The monitor's username or password field is modified while the BIG-IP system is operational. The DBDaemon Java process is still running with an active cached connection to the database server.
bugs.impact: The pool member may be incorrectly marked as available (UP) even if the new credentials are invalid or the database account has been disabled. Health monitoring results do not accurately reflect the database server's authentication state until the persistent connection is naturally closed (by the database server, connection timeout, or BIG-IP restart). This makes troubleshooting difficult because the failure symptoms are deferred and do not occur at the time the credentials are changed.
bugs.workaround: To force immediate re-evaluation of the new credentials, restart the DBDaemon process by running the following command on the BIG-IP: bigstart restart bigd This terminates all persistent DB monitor connections, causing them to re-establish using the updated credentials on the next monitor interval.

bugs.title: Password-memory is not remembering passwords to prevent them from being used again
bugs.symptoms: Password-memory is not remembering passwords to prevent users from using the same password again.
bugs.conditions: -- Policy-enforcement is enabled. -- password-memory is configured.
bugs.impact: System should support "password memory" for each user and can't use previous password.

bugs.title: PEM AVR onbox reporting stall
bugs.symptoms: When using PEM AVR onbox reporting, the per-subscriber reporting will stop working after a set of time.
bugs.conditions: - PEM AVR reporting.
bugs.impact: No per-subscriber reporting is available.
bugs.workaround: Restart tmm to get it working again.
bugs.fix: PEM AVR reporting continues to function.

bugs.title: Error: Failed to adjust configuration: The requested Protocol Inspection Signature (2951) was not found
bugs.symptoms: The IM Upgrade fails with the error: Failed to adjust configuration: 01020036:3: The requested Protocol Inspection Signature (2951) was not found.
bugs.conditions: When trying to upgrade to IM Package pi_updates_17.1.0-20231026.1244.im
bugs.impact: IM Package upgrade fails
bugs.fix: The issue is fixed as part of the next IM pi_updates_15.1.0-20231110.0616.im

bugs.title: Remote users are unable to generate authentication tokens
bugs.symptoms: On a BIG-IP version with the fix for ID1147633, remote users are unable to generate authentication tokens. This also results in following pages in the GUI being broken for users: - Device Management >> Overview - Local Traffic >> Network Map
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP version with the fix for ID1147633 -- Remote user authentication (such as TACACS, RADIUS, Active Directory, and other)
bugs.impact: Some parts of the GUI may not load for remote users. Generating an authentication token for a remote user would result in an error message similar to the following: { "code": 400, "message": "token creation failed; target user [<id>] does not exist in the system", "referer": "https://<IP>/tmui/tmui/devmgmt/overview/app/index.html?ver=0.0.6.17.1.1", "restOperationId": <ID>, "kind": ":resterrorresponse" }
bugs.fix: The GUI pages are loading successfully for remote users.

bugs.title: Processes that are using libcrypto during their startup are causing high CPU usage
bugs.symptoms: Upon creating a new connection, the initialization of the OpenSSL library triggers self-tests, resulting in high CPU usage.
bugs.conditions: Enable FIPS mode and use SIP monitors. Initializing SIP monitors will also initialize the OpenSSL library, causing high CPU consumption.
bugs.impact: High CPU usage due to the loading of the OpenSSL library whenever a new connection is created.
bugs.workaround: Disable FIPS mode by setting the environment variable SECURITY_FIPS140_COMPLIANCE to false.

bugs.title: UDP payloads not ending with CRLF are being treated as BAD messages.
bugs.symptoms: The UDP SIP payloads that did not end with CRLF are being treated as BAD messages.
bugs.conditions: The UDP SIP payload did not end with CRLF.
bugs.impact: The UDP SIP message will be treated as a BAD message if the payload does not end with CRLF.
bugs.fix: Made SIPP parser changes to accept and process UDP SIP messages that do not end with CRLF.

bugs.title: The httpd service shows inactive/dead after "bigstart restart httpd"
bugs.symptoms: The systemd service unit for httpd shows a status of inactive (dead) after you restart httpd using bigstart restart httpd. For example: # systemctl status httpd * httpd.service - LSB: start and stop Apache HTTP Server Loaded: loaded (/etc/rc.d/init.d/httpd; enabled; vendor preset: enabled) Active: inactive (dead) since Mon 2023-11-13 09:55:06 GMT; 5s ago In versions v15.1.10.5 and above in v15.1.x, v16.1.5 and above in v16.1.x, and v17.1.1.4 and above, if a system is affected by this and then a user or process restarts httpd via systemd, the GUI will stop responding and return 403 Forbidden errors. This happens when attempting to renew or update the device certificate via the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Executing the command bigstart restart httpd. This will also happen behind-the-scenes when making HTTP configuration changes via tmsh/the GUI/iControl.
bugs.impact: httpd is running normally, but systemd is not aware of it.
bugs.workaround: To confirm httpd is running, you can use the following commands: bigstart status httpd OR ps ax | grep '[h]ttpd' If you would like to clear the stale state, restart httpd via its systemd service unit twice: systemctl restart httpd && systemctl restart httpd If the GUI is returning 403 Forbidden errors for everything, restart httpd ("systemctl restart httpd && systemctl restart httpd").

bugs.title: APM[Saml IdP] - Support for metadata containing multiple entities
bugs.symptoms: Importing a metadata file containing an <md:EntitiesDescriptor> element which in turn can contain multiple <EntityDescriptor> elements fail to import with: Configuration error: Metadata contains duplicate 'index' (0) in AssertionConsumerService elements. Service Providers must be reconfigured to provide correct metadata. Alternatively, metadata can be manually edited to have a unique 'index' in the range from 0 to 65535 for each AssertionConsumerService element.
bugs.conditions: APM acting as the SAML IDP tries to automate the metadata file controlled by a 3rd party vendor and fails to install even when trying to import manually. Because this is a multiple entities metadata file there will be multiple index values for each EntityDescriptor and they may have the same index number.
bugs.impact: Saml metadata fails to import, and fails to configure.

bugs.title: Memory leak in websense when RTU is updated
bugs.symptoms: URLDB stops responding and you may observe below logs crit tmm5[27171]: 01790602:2: [C] <IP:port> -> <IP:port>: (ERR_EXPIRED) URL category lookup failed
bugs.conditions: Websense database update.
bugs.impact: SSL Orchestrator traffic cannot be forwarded.
bugs.workaround: Restart urldb: bigstart restart urldb Impact of workaround: restarting urldb causes traffic to be disrupted while urldb is restarting.

bugs.title: Per Request Policy updates not reflected on the active device of an HA Pair
bugs.symptoms: When a per-request policy has a syntax error when configured manually using advanced expressions, subsequent updates to per-request policies are not sent in the traffic plane, causing traffic to reset.
bugs.conditions: -- Found on 15.1.8 -- SWG is provisioned and a per-request policy is created -- Policy branch rules are configured manually (advanced expressions) and has syntax error previously
bugs.impact: Any updates to per request policy won't reflect automatically on the active device, but will work on the failover device after config-sync.
bugs.workaround: Config-sync will trigger the control plane changes to be re-applied. Apply the changes on the active device, config-sync and force to standby. This will trigger changes on the peer device. Peer device is now active. Make any dummy change and config-sync again, this will make sure changes are applied on both boxes.

bugs.title: [APM][SAML IDP] BIG-IP as IDP does not include proper xml namespace declaration when thumbnailPhoto as a SAML attribute is added
bugs.symptoms: When thumbnailPhoto as a SAML attribute is added, it causes external SP to fail due to "THE SAML RESPONSE IS INVALID." "Invalid SAML Response. Not match the saml-schema-protocol-2.0.xsd - invalid_xml" The thumbNail attribute adds in a "xsi:type="xs:base64Binary" to the SAML Attribute but does not have the namespace
bugs.conditions: SAML configured with thumbnailPhoto as attributes added to BIG-IP as IDP.
bugs.impact: Malformed Assertion causes external SP to fail due to "THE SAML RESPONSE IS INVALID." which impacts in accessing resources.

bugs.title: Enabling support for SSH-RSA in Non FIPS mode
bugs.symptoms: Ssh-rsa is disabled in FIPS and non-FIPS mode, as SSH-RSA is a less secure algorithm.
bugs.conditions: Attempt to use SSH-RSA algorithm
bugs.impact: Unable to use SSH-RSA algorithm
bugs.fix: Added support for SSH-RSA in Non-FIPS mode. It is still disabled in FIPS mode.

bugs.title: Configuration error: In url-filter <filter name> allowed-category <cat name> does not exist.
bugs.symptoms: After an upgrade, the configuration fails to load with one or more errors: Configuration error: In url-filter <filter name> allowed-category <cat name> does not exist.
bugs.conditions: Upgrading SWG from a BIG-IP version that uses category names that no longer exist.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP upgrade fails.
bugs.workaround: Remove the affected category names before attempting the BIG-IP upgrade.
bugs.fix: Code exists to map older categories with new categories when upgrading in versions prior to BIG-IP 13.x. The same code will be fixed to correctly map categories when upgrading for versions BIG-IP 15.x and later.

bugs.title: TMM can not process traffic on Cisco ENIC
bugs.symptoms: - TMM cannot process traffic - Within '/var/log/tmm', there is the following log line rte_enic_pmd: Rq 0 Scatter rx mode not being used - 'tmctl -d blade tmm/xnet/dpdk/stats' stat table shows a large (several 10000) for 'mbuf_inuse' and 'frag_inuse', and 'mbuf_alloc_fail' is an extremely large count (in the scale of millions) and continuously increasing
bugs.conditions: - TMM is using Xnet-DPDK drivers - BIG-IP is connected to a Cisco ENIC card In addition to the above, one or both of the following a) Only 1 RX queue available b) MTU <= 1920 By default, TMM will set MTU to 1500 for ENIC.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted as TMM is not able to receive nor send packets.
bugs.workaround: Both of following must be done: 1) Configure ENIC to have 2 or more RX queues available 2) Create a file '/config/tmm_init.tcl' containing the following line: ndal mtu 9000 1137:0043
bugs.fix: Set TMM to default to MTU 9000 for ENIC

bugs.title: Virtual Server status change log message fails to report actual status
bugs.symptoms: -- SNMP_TRAP log message reports the virtual server status as available but does not report that it has been disabled by parent due to its default pool. -- Then, when a pool member is enabled, the virtual server status will be available again, but there is no log message indicating this change.
bugs.conditions: -- Disable all pool members in a pool and watch the virtual server status log messages
bugs.impact: Virtual server status cannot be identified and tracked via log messages.

bugs.title: External IDP Connector Certificate Settings disappears
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP administrator creates a certificate with name "SP_ADFS__saml_idp_metadata_cert.crt", the dropdown showing the list of available certificates in the External IDP Connector Settings disappeared.
bugs.conditions: The issue occurs only when the certificate is named with string "SP_ADFS__saml_idp_metadata_cert.crt"
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP administrator will not be able to select a certificate for External IDP Connector.
bugs.workaround: As the issue occurs only for chrome & Edge browsers, the BIG-IP administrator can use Safari or FireFox.

bugs.title: PEM iRule commands lead to TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: In a few circumstances PEM iRule commands lead to a TMM crash.
bugs.conditions: PEM iRule commands
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: SIP parser not parsing response when ;; in the to: or from:
bugs.symptoms: Messages are not forwarded
bugs.conditions: When a sip message contains ;; in the to or from, for example: t: <sip:+18005551212@10.10.24.2;user=phone>;;tag=70c1a1e1
bugs.impact: Message is not forwarded

bugs.title: QUIC occasionally erroneously sends connection close with QPACK decoder stream error
bugs.symptoms: QUIC connections are occasionally closed with "QPACK decoder stream error" (error code 514).
bugs.conditions: The QPACK decoder stream of a QUIC connection receives part of a request in a packet or receives an ack or cancel for a stream that has already been closed.
bugs.impact: A connection close with "QPACK decoder stream error" is sent and the QUIC connection is closed. Web browsers might also conclude that the BIG-IP's QUIC implementation is not interoperable and stop initiating HTTP/3 connections.
bugs.fix: Fixed QPACK handling when receiving part of a request in a packet or receiving an ack or cancel for a stream that has already been closed.

bugs.title: Tmm restarts due to mcpd disconnect when memory runs out with high tmm CPU and memory xdata use
bugs.symptoms: Tmm restarts with messages similar to this: alert tmm[24857]: 011a0027:1: Out of memory resources (Resource temporarily unavailable) while attempting to allocate a path table. err tmm[24857]: 011ae0f6:3: Encountered error while processing mcp message at ../gtmdb/db_gtm_path.c:151 : Unable to add path
bugs.conditions: A BIG-IP system is flooded with dns queries with load balancing methods using path metrics.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: "XML data does not comply with schema or WSDL document" violations after upgrade to 16.1.4.1
bugs.symptoms: If the "Attribute" in a schema file has an upper case letter, then schema validation fails. This does not apply to "Element", which tries to match exact case.
bugs.conditions: Create a Case insensitive ASM policy. Create an XML Schema profile which has an "Attribute" Tag with at least one upper-case letter in the Attribute name.
bugs.impact: Requests fail with Violation, even though the Schema file has a specific attribute.
bugs.workaround: Have the "Attribute" tag name with all lower case letters, then the request does not gets blocked.

bugs.title: While upgrading standby device, active device is going to standby mode for few seconds, and traffic loss is observed.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic loss due to failover.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS with BIG-IP tenants. -- Execute failovers on the active device by running "tmsh run sys failover standby". -- Proceed to upgrade F5OS on the current standby device. -- Note that during this process, the device previously in Active mode will transition to standby mode momentarily, typically lasting around 20 seconds.
bugs.impact: Traffic loss lasting up to 20 seconds approx.

bugs.title: Remote authentication improvements
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IPs with the fix for ID1147633 may experience remote authentication issues.
bugs.conditions: -- Remote user authentication (such as TACACS, RADIUS, Active Directory, and other)
bugs.fix: Remote user authentication performs as expected.

bugs.title: FrameElement Wrappers occasionaly returns 'Undefined' instead of original Window object failing to load frame/iframes
bugs.symptoms: Iframes are not loading properly
bugs.conditions: Modern Rewriting/Mode is used
bugs.impact: Application fail to load iframes
bugs.workaround: Use the below iRule: when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { ACCESS::restrict_irule_events disable } when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "cache-fm-Modern.js" } { HTTP::respond 200 content [ifile get ModernCachefm] } } iFile - Request the ifile with fix via Escalation

bugs.title: iRule event BOTDEFENSE_ACTION validation failing a subroutine call
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP system tries to save an iRule that calls a procedure from the BOTDEFENSE_ACTION event, an error occurs.
bugs.conditions: -- Configure an iRule with event BOTDEFENSE_ACTION. -- The event calls a procedure.
bugs.impact: A TCL error is thrown: Rule checker ::tclCheck::checkScript did not complete: can't read "BIGIP::ltmEventCategoryHierarchy(BOTDEFENSE)": no such element in array.

bugs.title: [REST][APM]command 'restcurl /tm/access/session/kill-sessions' output on APM is empty
bugs.symptoms: Active APM Sessions are not returned when running the kill-sessions command.
bugs.conditions: 'restcurl /tm/access/session/kill-sessions' is run.
bugs.impact: Active access sessions are not the same on BIG-IP and BIG-IQ since BIG-IQ uses this API (/tm/access/session/kill-sessions).

bugs.title: DNS Resolution for IPv6 clients is not working when dns64 is enabled with secondary in DNS Profile.
bugs.symptoms: DNS Resolution for IPv6 clients is not working when dns64 is enabled with secondary in DNS Profile. This can be encountered after an upgrade, where DNS hosts that used to reply with a AAAA record no longer provide an authoritative answer.
bugs.conditions: --- DNS64 is enabled and set to secondary in DNS Profile. --- qname-minimisation is enabled by default in code in the latest unbound. --- That Profile is configured with dns cache. --- A DNS listener is configured with the above profile. --- DNS clients requesting ipv6 resolution requests towards the listener.
bugs.impact: IPv6 resolution is failing.

bugs.title: SIP message parser should have warning logs for drops
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP SIP parser logs all messages at the notice log level.
bugs.conditions: SIP message parser logging
bugs.impact: Admin cannot easily be notified of incompatibility issues unless log messages are set to notice which can get very noisy.
bugs.fix: SIP message parser now logs messages at warning level to /var/log/ltm.

bugs.title: PVA dedicated mode does not accelerate all connections
bugs.symptoms: While in PVA dedicated mode, all flows may not be fully accelerated because neuron rules are not created for flow collisions.
bugs.conditions: A fastL4 profile with pva-acceleration set to "dedicated. sys turboflex profile-config set to "turboflex-low-latency" This type of configuration is commonly used for hardware-optimized FIX low latency electronic trading traffic.
bugs.impact: Higher latency for these connections because they are not in PVA.
bugs.fix: Dedicated mode PVA connections are now properly using the neuron and are accelerated.

bugs.title: Replace policy function fails even though local and imported (JSON format) policies have the same encoding/applicationLanguage
bugs.symptoms: Exporting and replacing a policy in JSON format fails with error "InternalError - import_policy failed: fatal: Failed action: Imported and replaced policies have different encodings."
bugs.conditions: Export a policy in JSON format and replace a policy with the exported policy.
bugs.impact: Import policy getting failed with Replace option.
bugs.workaround: Works with exporting policy as XML format.

bugs.title: Enhance HTTP2 receive-window to maximum
bugs.symptoms: While uploading a 100 MB file, the client repeatedly runs out of the window and the processing of a window update is relatively slow and builds up to quite an overhead.
bugs.conditions: Virtual server with HTTP2 profile.
bugs.impact: The transfer time of HTTP2 is increased as compared to HTTP/1.1.
bugs.fix: Increased HTTP2 receive-window maximum value to 1024.

bugs.title: Iproute2 utils do not work properly under route-domains
bugs.symptoms: When using utilities from the iproute2 family (such as ip route or ip link show) in a non-default route-domain, the commands may display incorrect interface names and routing information. Interfaces belonging to the default route-domain (for example, eth0 or lcdusb0) may be shown instead of the correct VLAN interfaces assigned to the active route-domain.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under the following conditions: - BIG-IP version 14.1.x or later. - One or more non-default route-domains configured. - VLANs assigned to those route-domains. - Execution of iproute2 utilities (ip route, ip link show, etc.) within a route-domain context. - Most commonly observed on hardware platforms with multiple interfaces.
bugs.impact: Incorrect or misleading interface and routing information is displayed by iproute2 commands.
bugs.workaround: Use netstat -rn or other BIG-IP–aware utilities to view routing and interface information in route-domains Avoid relying on iproute2 output for interface or routing validation in non-default route-domains.

bugs.title: Citrix Autodetect fails when STA is configured in Storefront
bugs.symptoms: When the user configures Citrix integration mode and configures STA servers configured on both Storefront and APM access policy, Auto-discovery of the Citrix Workspace app will fail. Users can still continue with the already installed option.
bugs.conditions: The issue is seen when Citrix Integration mode is configured and STA resolution enabled. Also, users access APM using a Browser client.
bugs.impact: The user needs to click multiple times to download the ica file and load the desktop.
bugs.fix: Citrix workspace auto discovery should work.

bugs.title: TMM crash when using internal datagroup
bugs.symptoms: When an internal data group matches a local traffic policy, tmm crashes.
bugs.conditions: Local data group involved. External data groups are fine.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use an external data group if possible
bugs.fix: Both internal and external data group works

bugs.title: GTP compliances are deprecated after BIG-IP version upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade from BIG-IP 17.1.0.1 to higher versions (like 17.1.0.2 or 17.1.0.3) below compliances are deprecated with "action" configured other than default value: gtp_allowed_apns gtp_disallowed_apns gtp_disallowed_imsi This issue is not encountered when directly installing BIG-IP 17.1.0.2.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP 17.1.0.1 is installed - Create a protocol inspection profile with GTP compliance. - Change action for gtp_allowed_apns, gtp_disallowed_apns and gtp_disallowed_imsi other than default value and commit these changes. - Upgrade to BIG-IP 17.1.0.2 or other higher versions. - Deprecated becomes "yes".
bugs.impact: These compliances are removed and cannot be used.
bugs.workaround: If the active version on BIG-IP 17.1.0.2 with an IPS Profile created, then do the following: 1) Change the Action to default "Don't Inspect" for all 3 affected compliances in profile and commit the changes. 2) Install BIG-IP 17.1.0.2. 3) Upgrade to BIG-IP v17.1.0.2. 4) Now change the action value as per the requirement (Accept/Reject/Drop) and commit the changes.

bugs.title: Nlad unstable after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: End users are unable to use Outlook when they are not inside the corporate network. If tmm debug logging is enabled, you might see the following in /var/log/tmm debug eca[13346]: 01620012:7: Retrieved 0 bytes of random number from tmm 0 debug eca[13346]: 01620012:7: Retrieved 0 bytes of random number from tmm 0 debug eca[13346]: 01620012:7: Retrieved 0 bytes of random number from tmm 1 debug eca[13346]: 01620012:7: Retrieved 0 bytes of random number from tmm 3
bugs.conditions: APM access profile with NTLM authentication enabled.
bugs.impact: Nlad unstable due to ECA random number fetch causing NTLM authentication failures.

bugs.title: TMM core dump include SIGABRT multiple times, on the Standby device.
bugs.symptoms: The tmm running on the Standby device is repeatedly killed by sod. There are number of SessionDB ERROR messages on the tmm log. /var/log/tmm1: notice session_ha_context_callback: SessionDB ERROR: received invalid or corrupt HA message; dropped message.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP configured for high availability (HA) -- Mirroring enabled -- APM enabled -- Traffic is being passed on the active device
bugs.impact: Tmm restarts on the standby device. If a failover occurs while the tmm is restarting, traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: Persisting sub-session information only in the active device, after the expiry.

bugs.title: Engineering Hotfix readme file refers to non-applicable "full_box_reboot" command
bugs.symptoms: The readme file automatically produced for BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes contains the following instructions: This hotfix may not be operational without a FULL system restart. To accomplish this, use the command: /usr/bin/full_box_reboot However, the full_box_reboot command is not part of the documented or recommended workflows for current BIG-IP versions.
bugs.conditions: These instructions are contained in the .readme file that may accompany a BIG-IP Engineering Hotfix provided by F5 to resolve critical issues, under the terms and conditions of the F5 critical issue hotfix policy as described at: https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K4918
bugs.impact: The instructions in the Engineering Hotfix readme file may be confusing due to inconsistency with documented workflows for installing BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes.
bugs.workaround: After the software installs and boots to the volume with installed software no further reboot is required.

bugs.title: MRF per-message TCL contexts and async SessionDB operations result in immortal zombie flows
bugs.symptoms: The stale connections cannot be deleted with TMSH command: #tmsh delete sys connection command Stale connection: >>> any6.any any6.any <IP> <IP> tcp 255282 (tmm: 1) none none >>> any6.any any6.any <IP> <IP> tcp 255273 (tmm: 1) none none
bugs.conditions: - When "irule-scope-message" set to Yes, in a MRF routing profile. (This is not protocol specific - it's a general MRF behaviour.) ltm message-routing generic router simple_router { app-service none defaults-from messagerouter description none ignore-client-port no irule-scope-message yes <--------- per message TCL scope And use SessionDB operations on multi-TMM configuration. when MR_INGRESS { table lookup "Freddo" log local0. "Hey, an ingress message [MR::message id]" }
bugs.impact: Attempts to delete the flow through TMSH are ineffective and the flow remains for the remainder of the TMM lifetime.
bugs.workaround: Do not use per message TCP scope. irule-scope-message no <----- not use per message TCL scope

bugs.title: A blade with a non-functional backplane may override the dag context for the whole system
bugs.symptoms: A blade with a non-functional backplane may override the dag context for the whole system.
bugs.conditions: - a blade has backplane problems, as evidenced by "shared random" not being ready in `tmctl -d blade tmm/ready_for_world_stat`.
bugs.impact: The traffic is black-holed into a non-functional blade.
bugs.workaround: Depending on the nature of the blade fault, a workaround is to either disable or just reboot the non-functional blade.
bugs.fix: A blade with a non-functional backplane cannot override the dag context for the whole system anymore.

bugs.title: Virtual Servers haviing adfs proxy configuration might have all traffic blocked
bugs.symptoms: All requests for ADFS proxy will be blocked and will not be allowed.
bugs.conditions: /var/log/apm should show a line similar to below in a normal scenario Nov 30 09:10:38 guest1.pslab.local debug adfs_proxy[9282]: 01aeffff:7: (null)::00000000: C: TMEVT_TIMER TMEVT_TIMER should occur once every minute These lines will be missing in the non-working case.
bugs.impact: Traffic to virtual servers having ADFS Proxy configuration will be disrupted.
bugs.workaround: - Restart adfs_proxy - bigstart restart adfs_proxy

bugs.title: Extending the username existence check for remote users
bugs.symptoms: The below endpoints that helps admin role users to create authentication tokens for the same or other role users, are unable to validate the username (either in the attribute or in the user link of the supplied payload) against the existence check. /mgmt/cm/system/authn/providers/tmos/token-generator /mgmt/shared/authz/tokens
bugs.conditions: When admin role user is trying to create authentication token for same or other role users on behalf of using the following endpoints, with a non-existing username supplied. /mgmt/cm/system/authn/providers/tmos/token-generator /mgmt/shared/authz/tokens
bugs.impact: Admin role user can create authentication token for any non-existing or disabled remote user, which is not expected to happen.

bugs.title: Lvm2 package upgrade from 2-2.02.166 to 2-2.02.187
bugs.symptoms: Bootup of BIG-IP tenant will fail due to logical cache/metadata corruption.
bugs.conditions: On a r10K System with Multi-Tenant BIG-IPs were deployed, sometimes this issue may come up as a timing issue.
bugs.impact: Traffic handling by the BIG-IP tenant will fail.
bugs.fix: Upgraded lvm2 package to have upgraded version which has the fix for lvm cache/metadata corruption.

bugs.title: CONNFLOW_FLAG_DOUBLE_LB flows might route traffic to a stale next hop
bugs.symptoms: Pool members configured with IP encapsulation or any type of flow using CONNFLOW_FLAG_DOUBLE_LB flag might take some time to refresh its nexthops.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP receives an ECMP route towards a server over two different BGP peers and the server is a pool member with IPIP encapsulation enabled. One of the BGP peers goes down and the route gets removed immediately, but BIG-IP is still forwarding traffic to this peer for the next few seconds, even though tmm.inline_route_update is enabled.
bugs.impact: The connection is using the old, invalid next hop for a few seconds.

bugs.title: [Standard Customization]Web VPN cannot connect with Chinese Language
bugs.symptoms: Web VPN does not work with below error in developer tools console "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token ']'"
bugs.conditions: --Standard Customization --Chinese Language (zh-cn)
bugs.impact: Unable to use web VPN (browser based VPN)
bugs.workaround: --Use other languages --Use Modern Customization

bugs.title: [NAT-LOGS] PBA Lease Duration suffers from a 32-bit rollover after 50 days
bugs.symptoms: On NAT logs, the sum of PBA start time and duration values do not match with the log-generated time.
bugs.conditions: NAT policy in action with PBA and block-life-time is 0 which implies infinite time.
bugs.impact: The duration field in the logs does not show the right value.

bugs.title: An iRule containing HTTP_REQUEST event throws the TCL error invoked from within "HTTP::path when trying to process a non-valid HTTP request.
bugs.symptoms: After upgrade from v14 to v15, an iRule containing the HTTP_REQUEST event containing HTTP::Path throws a TCL error when trying to process a non-valid HTTP request. 01220001:3: TCL error: /BPUB-DEV/bpub_route <HTTP_REQUEST> - ERR_VAL (line 2) invoked from within "HTTP::path" +++++++++++
bugs.conditions: 1) Use BIG-IP versions from v15 2) Use HTTP::Path in HTTP_REQUEST event in an iRule. 3) Send some non-valid HTTP REQUEST traffic from a client
bugs.impact: iRule execution fails with a TCL error.
bugs.workaround: 1) Add "-normalized" command option to HTTP::path command. ltm rule /Common/test-rule-normalized { when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::path -normalized] contains "test" } { HTTP::respond 200 -content "OK !!!＼n" } else { HTTP::respond 200 -content "Hit ＼"else＼" statement !!!＼n" } } } Note: Adding "-normalized" command option may change the URI, so testing and verification before applying workaround on production environment is strongly recommended. 2) Use catch command in the iRule to see the error in ltm log. Ex: when HTTP_REQUEST { if {[HTTP::has_responded]} {return} catch { if {[class match [HTTP::path ] equals /BPUB-DEV/bpub_opns]}{ return } } catch_err if { $catch_err ne ""} { # log local0. "Catch_err: $catch_err" log local0. "HTTP Request: [HTTP::request]" drop } }

bugs.title: For E810 100G SR-IOV NICs, traffic disruption is seen with ICE driver v1.11.14 and NVM 4.20 combination.
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP VE configured with E810 VFs on a host with following ICE driver and NVM versions: - ICE driver version: 1.11.14 - NVM version: 4.20
bugs.conditions: Traffic not passing.
bugs.impact: Traffic not passing.
bugs.workaround: Use the following ICE driver and NVM versions in the hypervisor when configuring BIG-IP VE with E810 SR-IOV NICs: - ICE driver version: 1.7.16 - NVM version: 3.10

bugs.title: Virtual-wire HW offload statistics are incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Flow status received from the hardware cannot be matched to flows, hence offload statistics are not updated and packet/bytes counters remain 0.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP tenant on the F5OS platform; - Virtual-wire and HW offload enabled;
bugs.impact: Incorrect offload statistics.
bugs.fix: Hardware flow status is correctly matched to software flows.

bugs.title: iRules using regexp or regsub command with large expression can lead to SIGABRT.
bugs.symptoms: When iRule is using badly crafted regexp or regsub command, sometimes large regex compilation may lead to TMM core. - Multiple clock advances will be logged in tmm logs. - A message similar to the one below will be logged in tmm logs: notice sod[9938]: 01140041:5: Killing tmm.0 pid <pid of tmm>.
bugs.conditions: - iRules using regexp or regsub command with large expression
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Update iRule to avoid using regex or regsub with large expressions. either by 1. setting an upper-limit on the permitted size for regex expression or 2. rewrite the iRule to avoid the use of 'regsub'.

bugs.title: [APM][SAML] Assertion is not occurring when the Binding is set to POST in clientless mode
bugs.symptoms: Identified during internal testing, the assertion does not occur in any use case when BIG-IP is configured as a SAML SP with POST binding. Refer to the bug ID 1318397. debug tmm5[12791]: 014d0501:7: ::6ac890bf:[saml_sp_crypto_get_header:1269] Error: ERR_FAIL err tmm5[12791]: 014d0002:3: Failed to read header 'APD_SamlCryptoAction' err 12 err tmm5[12791]: 014d0002:3: SSOv2 plugin error(-1) in sso/saml_sp.h:632
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under the following conditions: 1. Have a BIG-IP with a basic SAML POST BINDING Setup. 2. "Sign Authentication Request" is enabled. 3. Add the iRule to act as "clientless mode". iRule : when HTTP_REQUEST { # Add the "clientless mode" header to the incoming request HTTP::header insert "clientless-mode" "3" } 4. Access the SAML SP virtual server to see the error in the SAML IDP BIG-IP.
bugs.impact: The SP did not receive the assertion from the IDP, which affects the SAML authentication flow and prevents access to the resources.
bugs.fix: Proper validation has been added for SAML requests as POST in clientless mode during xbuf validation, after the earlier changes made in bug ID 1318397.

bugs.title: Enforcer crash due to the ASM parameter configuration
bugs.symptoms: An ASM policy that is configured with a parameter that has a "Parameter Value Type" value set to "Ignore value" may cause BD CPU cores to reach 90-100% of their capacity, resulting in a bd core.
bugs.conditions: The "Parameter Value Type" value is set to "Ignore value" in the ASM policy. The same parameter has to be included in the incoming request.
bugs.impact: Long request processing time that may cause the enforcer to crash. Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Set the "Parameter Value Type" value to "Auto detect" or any other value.
bugs.fix: The enforcement time is similar to other "Parameter Value Type" options.

bugs.title: VCMP guest deployment may fail on newly installed blade
bugs.symptoms: If a VCMP guest is configured to be Provisioned or Deployed to multiple blades in a VIPRION chassis, and one of those blades is replaced or has a new installation of BIG-IP installed, the VCMP guest may fail to be Provisioned or Deployed to the newly installed/reinstalled blade. A message similar to the following may be logged to the LTM log (/var/log/ltm): <date> <time> slot# err vcmpd[#####]: 01510004:3: Guest (GUEST_NAME): Install to VDisk /shared/vmdisks/GUEST_IMAGE_NAME.img FAILED: Child exited with non-zero exit code: 255 When this issue occurs, the blade where the VCMP guest image fails to be installed is found not to be running the KVM kernel module: [root@CHASSIS_NAME:/S1-green-P::Active:Standalone] ~ # clsh 'lsmod | grep kvm' === slot 2 addr 127.3.0.2 color green === kvm_intel 179624 68 kvm 603109 1 kvm_intel irqbypass 13503 1 kvm === slot 3 addr 127.3.0.3 color green === kvm_intel 179624 0 kvm 603109 1 kvm_intel irqbypass 13503 1 kvm === slot 4 addr 127.3.0.4 color green === <<<<<<< no 'kvm' module shown for affected blade === slot 5 addr 127.3.0.5 color blue === === slot 6 addr 127.3.0.6 color blue === === slot 7 addr 127.3.0.7 color blue === === slot 8 addr 127.3.0.8 color blue === === slot 1 addr 127.3.0.1 color green === kvm_intel 179624 68 kvm 603109 1 kvm_intel irqbypass 13503 1 kvm
bugs.conditions: This may occur if: -- VCMP is provisioned, and one or more VCMP guests are provisioned/deployed in a VIPRION chassis with multiple blades. -- One of the blades is replaced with a new blade (such as from an RMA replacement). -- The newly installed/reinstalled blade has a version of BIG-IP installed that does not match the BIG-IP version installed and running on the existing blades in the chassis. -- The newly installed/reinstalled blade must reboot multiple times to complete the installation of all required BIG-IP versions to match the existing blades in the chassis. -- One or more VCMP guests are configured to be Provisioned and/or Deployed to the newly installed/reinstalled blade's slot. -- The newly installed/reinstalled blade does not automatically reboot after successfully provisioning VCMP after the automated installation of the final (matching) BIG-IP version.
bugs.impact: The VCMP guest fails to be Provisioned or Deployed to the newly installed/reinstalled blade.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue when it occurs, reboot the affected blade. -- From the console of the affected blade: reboot -- From the console of another blade in the chassis: clsh --slot=# reboot (where # is the slot number of the affected blade)

bugs.title: Add action and status to monitor_instance table
bugs.symptoms: In a few instances, the status of LTM nodes and/or pool members monitored by the bigd daemon may not be correctly or completely communicated to the mcpd daemon. The mcpd daemon then communicates with the rest of the BIG-IP about the status of monitored objects. Currently, there is no clear mechanism for detecting when bigd and mcpd are out of sync for the observed status of LTM nodes and/or pool members monitored by LTM health monitors.
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur when LTM nodes and/or pool members are monitored by LTM health monitors.
bugs.impact: Without a clear indication that bigd and mcpd are out of sync for the observed status of monitored LTM nodes and/or pool members, it is not known when corrective action needs to be taken to re-synchronize the LTM node and/or pool member status between bigd and mcpd.
bugs.workaround: When it is thought that bigd and mcpd are not in sync with the status of monitored LTM nodes and/or pool members, the following actions can be taken to force a re-synchronization of the monitored object status. This causes mcpd to monitor the state of the monitored objects correctly. -- Restart the bigd using the command: "bigstart restart bigd" -- Remove the health monitor from the affected pool, pool member or node, then re-add the health monitor to the affected pool, pool member or node.
bugs.fix: The tmstat table for bigd, monitor_instance, now includes action and status which reflects the last action taken on the node and the status.

bugs.title: GUI allows to modify source '/any' in bot-defence white list
bugs.symptoms: The system goes offline as the configuration is wrong.
bugs.conditions: Bot defence white list with source as any and URL.
bugs.impact: The system goes offline as the configuration is wrong

bugs.title: BADOS signals might no sync on HA setups
bugs.symptoms: BADOS signals might no sync on HA setups.
bugs.conditions: When using High Availability setups with BADOS enabled.
bugs.impact: Standby machine is not synched in some scenarios.
bugs.workaround: Manual sync with the script that calls rsync.
bugs.fix: The state file always stays in sync.

bugs.title: [APM][NA]Read Access Denied for 'Manger role' when accessing Network Settings in Network Access config
bugs.symptoms: On GUI: 'General database error retrieving information.' In /var/log/ltm: Read Access Denied: user (es-manager) type (network acces address space include)
bugs.conditions: -- Non-admin user -- Network Access configured on APM
bugs.impact: Non-admin users cannot access Network Access settings.

bugs.title: PVA dedicated mode connections are not re-accelerated after a failover.
bugs.symptoms: After a failover, not all PVA-accelerated flows using the dedicated mode may be accelerated on the new peer.
bugs.conditions: HA mirroring on a FastL4 VIP with PVA-acceleration set to "dedicated. sys turboflex profile-config set to "turboflex-low-latency" This type of configuration is commonly used for hardware-optimized FIX low-latency electronic trading traffic.
bugs.impact: After a failover, some flows may not be accelerated. This would cause higher-than-expected latency for those flows.
bugs.workaround: Delete the affected flows and then cause them to be re-created. Disable HA mirroring.

bugs.title: The chmand fails to fully start on multi-slot F5OS tenants when the cluster members have addresses or alternate addresses
bugs.symptoms: The chassis manager daemon (chmand) is wedged and does not fully start causing MCPD and cluster to never start.
bugs.conditions: This issue is seen when IPv6 alternate addresses to the cluster members are added and rebooted to a slot.
bugs.impact: The slot does not come online and stays inoperative.
bugs.fix: Using the copy of a variable for a bad iterator has fixed the issue.

bugs.title: When interface mode ipsec-policy on custom partition and custom RD is created through CLI, tunnel-local-address and tunnel-remote-address are added to RD0 (not the correct RD)
bugs.symptoms: When interface mode ipsec-policy on custom partition and custom RD is created through CLI, tunnel-local-address and tunnel-remote-address are added to RD0 (not the correct RD). Issue is with the display, there is no impact on the protocol functionality.
bugs.conditions: Observed only when configured through CLI and these fields are not used in interface mode for tunnel establishment.
bugs.impact: No impact on the functionality

bugs.title: VLAN MCPD validation failures are not informed to user during HA setup
bugs.symptoms: VLAN MCPD validation failures are not informed to user during an HA setup in Non-VE platforms.
bugs.conditions: - Set up routed mode with an untagged interface. Network ›› Quick Configuration >> Routed Mode - Navigate to HA setup. - Try to use the same tagged/untagged interface for HA that already has a tagged/untagged VLAN attached respectively. Network ›› High Availability
bugs.impact: MCPD validation failures are not informed. DoS Hybrid Defender setup can't be established.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: MCPD throws a validation error when manual full config sync does not overwrite the peer's Security local logging profile that was applied to a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: After changing a security local logging profile on a virtual server in a HA pair, config sync fails, the devices go out of sync. On the standby device is a log message: 01071a35:3: Security log profiles '/Common/Log illegal requests' and '/Common/Log all requests' cannot be associated simultaneously with a virtual server '/Common/mysite', since they both have local logging enabled.
bugs.conditions: -- Manual full config sync enabled -- Virtual server with a security local logging profile attached -- Changing the security local logging profile setting, for example changing from 'Log illegal requests' to 'Log all requests' -- Initiating config sync
bugs.impact: Config sync fails.

bugs.title: Hardware Action:Dropped in the f5 ethernet trailer is always set
bugs.symptoms: On some platforms without Hardware DOS like the rSeries r2xxx and r4xxx, a tcpdump capture may always show the HW Action Drop field set on all ingress packets.
bugs.conditions: RSeries r2xxx r4xxx
bugs.impact: The issue is cosmetic. This platform does not have a hardware DOS mitigation engine.

bugs.title: Genesis bot signature file does not install after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Genesis bot signature file does not install after upgrade, even after removing signature overrides.
bugs.conditions: Installing the Genesis BotSignatures_xxxx_yyyy.im fails after upgrade due to a Bot Defense Signature that cannot be deleted because it is in use by a Bot Defense Profile Signature Override. Deleting the conflicting Signature Override causes subsequent installing of the Genesis BotSignatures_xxxx_yyyy.im to fail silently (install endlessly spinning in UI).
bugs.impact: Cannot install Genesis BotSignatures_xxxx_yyyy.im after upgrade.
bugs.workaround: Remove bot signature override from bot defense profile - *before upgrade*. After upgrade Genesis BotSignatures_XXX_yyy.im installs successfully.

bugs.title: Large file transfer over SFTP/SSH proxy failure
bugs.symptoms: - Large file transfer (>110MB) fails using the SFTP PUT command through a virtual server configured with AFM SSH Proxy. - Depending on the boundary byte that gets sent from BIG-IP towards the backend server, the server sends back a SSH2_MSG_UNIMPLEMENTED for a packet type corresponding to the incorrect byte being interpreted as the message type.
bugs.conditions: - SSH Proxy profile attached to BIG_IP Virtual Server. - Large file (>110MB) is uploaded using PUT command through the virtual server.
bugs.impact: File transfer fails.
bugs.workaround: Workaround options are: - Limit the file transfer rate through the SFTP client. Ex: sftp -l 1000 <VS-IP> put <filename> - Use a smaller buffer size (eg. 1400). Ex: sftp -B 1400 <VS-IP> put <filename>

bugs.title: A F5 CDP timeout for a single blade may override the DAG context for the whole system
bugs.symptoms: A timeout in the F5 Cluster Discovery Protocol for a single blade may override the DAG context for the entire system.
bugs.conditions: A timeout in the F5 Cluster Discovery Protocol for a single blade.
bugs.impact: Traffic is routed to a single blade, as seen in `tmctl -d blade tmm/sdaglib_hash_table`.
bugs.workaround: Restart any TMM.
bugs.fix: Fixed a possibility for a single blade timeout to override the DAG context for the whole system.

bugs.title: When sending traffic to an IKE peer with dynamic template and multiple traffic-selectors, the TMM crashes
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes after sending traffic to an IKE peer with dynamic template.
bugs.conditions: If more than one traffic-selector is in the dynamic template traffic-selector { /Common/ts-01 /Common/ts-02 }
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Use a single traffic-selector as multiple TS with dynamic template is not supported.

bugs.title: Keymgmtd coring or restarting in loop when we have an empty crl file inside crl_file_cache_d path.
bugs.symptoms: Keymgmtd is coring and restarting in a loop.
bugs.conditions: Create an empty file in the crl_file_cache_d path and try restarting the keymgmtd.
bugs.impact: Key management-related operations will fail.

bugs.title: DNSX returns a malformed UDP DNS response when the answer count is nonzero but there is no answer section.
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP system returns a malformed UDP DNS response.
bugs.conditions: When provided buf_size is able to fit the answer section but not able to fit authority and additional sections.
bugs.impact: Malformed UDP DNS response.
bugs.workaround: Use TCP DNS query.

bugs.title: API Protection rate limiting can cause cores with high traffic
bugs.symptoms: Tmm cores and restarts
bugs.conditions: -- APM API Protection rate limiting is enabled -- High traffic volumes
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: CMP forwarded flows can be removed by other CMP forwarded flows incorrectly
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP may fail to forward server-side traffic if flow forwarding occurs due to an overload scenario, specifically due to flow collisions on the server-side connection when using the source-port preserve-strict option with UDP virtual configuration.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured with UDP virtual configuration with source-port preserve-strict. - CMP forwarding occurs when traffic on ingress is managed by a different TMM on egress. - Overload condition occurs on TMM that leads to forwarding the flow by keeping server-side connection. - Forwarded flow causes existing connection flow to be removed and interrupts current traffic flow.
bugs.impact: Forwarding flow removes the existing flow and causes traffic to be dropped.
bugs.workaround: Clear the existing connection from the connection table. For more information, refer to the article K53851362: Displaying and deleting BIG-IP connection table entries from the command line.

bugs.title: VELOS tenant, TMM remains not ready and fails to fully come-up on secondary slots
bugs.symptoms: - TMM does not fully come up on secondary slots leaving all but one slot non-operational. Following is an example: [root@rd1:/S1-green-P::Active:Standalone] config # tmsh show sys cluster ----------------------------------------- Sys::Cluster: default ----------------------------------------- Address <IP address/subnet> Alt-Address :: Availability available State enabled Reason Cluster Enabled Primary Slot ID 1 Primary Selection Time 12/08/23 12:16:33 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | Sys::Cluster Members | ID Address Alt-Address Availability State Licensed HA Clustered Reason --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 1 :: :: available enabled true active running Run | 2 :: :: unavailable enabled false active running TMM not ready 2. The following messages will be seen on secondary slots /var/log/tmm logs file: notice SEP: Can't find SEP mapping for slot:2 port:0mac:02:01:23:45:02:00 notice SEP: Can't find SEP mapping for slot:2 port:0mac:02:01:23:45:02:00 notice SEP: Can't find SEP mapping for slot:2 port:0mac:02:01:23:45:02:00 notice SEP: Can't find SEP mapping for slot:2 port:0mac:02:01:23:45:02:00 3. On tenant run: guishell -c "select name,module_id,physport from interface" If physport for 1/0.1 is showing 0, it's another indication of the bug. Note: This issue can also occur on a single-bladed tenant, but there are no "Can't find SEP mapping" errors in tmm log, and "show sys cluster" does not show any problem on a single-bladed tenants. The guishell command is the only clear symptom that can be observed. Other symptoms of this issue include: - /var/log/ltm contains 'inet port exhaustion' logs for non-floating SelfIP addresses. - The HA channel is disconnected. - The failover channel over the HA VLAN does not work. - Health checks are down or flapping. - A BIG-IP tenant was working fine, but after a reboot, it stopped working. - A BIG-IP tenant was broken, so you restart it, and now the tenant works, but a different tenant is now broken. - You can ping some things but not other things. This issue may not be triggered immediately after the upgrade. Although it is encountered more rarely, this issue could also be triggered on rSeries devices.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenant running v17.1.1 running on VELOS.
bugs.impact: TMM does not fully start on secondary slots, leaving those slots as part of the cluster and unable to process traffic.

bugs.title: APM as oAuth AS intermittently returning HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP configured as oAuth AS on a VIPRION environment intermittently, the oAuth token request (POST /f5-oauth2/v1/token) fails with 400 Bad Request. Following is an example APM logs error: "Error Code (invalid_request) Error Description (Invalid parameter (auth_code).)"
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured as oAuth AS.
bugs.impact: Authentication failed, unable to reach back-end resources.

bugs.title: ASM introduce huge delay from time to time
bugs.symptoms: During high traffic, the response to some requests will be delayed for more than 1 second.
bugs.conditions: ASM Policy attached to the Virtual Server and during high traffic conditions.
bugs.impact: Some critical URLs like payment links, will timeout for the user.

bugs.title: NShield netHSM : Creating new nShield key does not commit this key to an external RFS with nShield 12.60
bugs.symptoms: With nShield software v12.60 when creating a new nShield key on BIG-IP which is a client of an external RFS the new key is not automatically uploaded to RFS. It works fine with nShield software v12.40 and new keys are committed to RFS without 'rfs-sync -c'. If we generate a new HSM key with fipskey.nethsm (a wrapper for /opt/nfast/bin/generatekey) the key is committed to RFS.
bugs.conditions: --> Configure BIG-IP with an external HSM. Use nShield software v12.60.x. --> Create a new nethsm key using TMSH or WebUI.
bugs.impact: Upgrading to higher versions of BIG-IP software will cause issues due to the usage of nshield v12.60 in them.
bugs.workaround: Use 'rfs-sync -c' after creating a new key.

bugs.title: Address List containing IP addresses with route domain IDs cannot be assigned as Default Allowedlist in DoS profiles
bugs.symptoms: Modifying DoS profile with default allowed list option throws error message on TMSH as well as on GUI.
bugs.conditions: Create allowlist IP address list like below, security firewall address-list test-whtlst { addresses { 8.8.8.8 { } 10.10.10.0/24 { } 192.168.0.1%2/32 { } } } assign this whitelist to dos profile.
bugs.impact: Unable to assign allowlist IP address to DoS profile.
bugs.workaround: Use same allowlist as HTTP allowlist option. Following is an example: modify security dos profile test-dos-profile http-whitelist test-whtlst

bugs.title: Modify b.root-servers.net IPv4 address to 170.247.170.2 and IPv6 address to 2801:1b8:10::b
bugs.symptoms: USC/ISI, which operates b.root-servers.net, renumbered the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses on November 27, 2023. The current IPv4 address is 170.247.170.2, and the current IPv6 address is 2801:1b8:10::b. USC/ISI continues to support the root service over the current IPv4 and IPv6 addresses until November 27, 2024,(one year). This enables a stable transition while new root hints files are distributed in software and operating system packages.
bugs.conditions: Several profiles include the b.root-servers.net
bugs.impact: As USC/ISI supports the current IPv4 and IPv6 addresses for a minimum of one year (November 27, 2024), there is minimal impact. A single timeout for pending TLD queries can occur when accessing an old IP address using round-robin. Normally, the hint's TTL which is more than a month can cause a timeout when the old IP stops responding.
bugs.fix: The IPv4 and IPv6 address for b.root-servers.net has been renumbered to 170.247.170.2 and 2801:1b8:10::b

bugs.title: VLAN name greater than or equal to 32 characters causes VLAN to lose member information
bugs.symptoms: If VLAN name is greater than or equal to 32 characters, a tenant running on an r2000 or r4000-series appliance may fail to pass traffic on that VLAN. This occurs because the tenant loses track of the interface/trunk<>VLAN association when attempting to process configuration updates from the F5OS host.
bugs.conditions: - r2000 or r4000 system - VLAN member with a name that is 32 characters or longer is assigned to a BIG-IP tenant.
bugs.impact: Traffic may not pass properly.
bugs.workaround: Use shorter VLAN names, with a maximum of 31 characters.

bugs.title: TMM might crash or leak memory with certain logging configurations
bugs.symptoms: TMM might crash or leak memory with certain logging configurations.
bugs.conditions: Virtual-to-virtual chaining is used for handling syslog messages.
bugs.impact: Memory leak or Crash.

bugs.title: BIG-IP may not remove the topmost via header from a SIP response before forwarding to server
bugs.symptoms: If extension2 contains % (percent), some clients will convert it and this causes the BIG-IP to forward it as is instead of removing it.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with a SIP profile -- A header arrives (extension2) which contains a special character. This can occur if a client converts %2a to *, for example.
bugs.impact: Extension2 ends up being forwarded by BIG-IP SIP server getting extra field (extension2) does not recognize it.

bugs.title: Modifying the destination address of a virtual server leaves behind the associated virtual address.
bugs.symptoms: Stale, orphaned virtual addresses exist without any referencing virtual servers.
bugs.conditions: Create virtual server with same destination in default and non default route domains.
bugs.impact: load sys config fails, and the license cannot be upgraded on an F5OS host when a DHCP virtual server is configured in a non-default route domain (RD).
bugs.workaround: To recover type in cli : root@(localhost)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# save sys config Saving running configuration... /config/bigip.conf /config/bigip_base.conf /config/bigip_user.conf Saving Ethernet map ...done Saving PCI map ... - verifying checksum .../var/run/f5pcimap: OK done - saving ...done And the virtual server is again in the config root@(localhost)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list ltm virtual ltm virtual dhcp { auto-lasthop enabled creation-time 2023-11-18:03:02:15 destination 255.255.255.255%30:bootps dhcp-relay ip-protocol udp last-modified-time 2023-11-18:04:43:33 mask 255.255.255.255 profiles { dhcpv4 { } } serverssl-use-sni disabled source 0.0.0.0%30/0 translate-address enabled translate-port disabled vs-index 3 }
bugs.fix: NA

bugs.title: Dag context may not match the current cluster state
bugs.symptoms: When the cluster state changes during synchronization of dag context in a HA pair, dag context may not match the current cluster state. This is a rare-occurance problem and happens only during frequent updates of the cluster state.
bugs.conditions: - HA pair is configured, the system role is the next-active - The cluster state changes during the synchronization of the dag state.
bugs.impact: - one blade is not present in the dag context
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM
bugs.fix: Fixed an error that leads to a dag context not matching the current cluster state.

bugs.title: Possible TMM core under certain client-ssl profile configurations

bugs.title: MCPD unstable/inoperative after copying SNMP configuration from another BIG-IP
bugs.symptoms: If SNMP configuration that contains Secure Vault-protected attributes ("$M$...") is copied from a BIG-IP system to another and the devices do not have the same Secure Vault master key, the target device will appear to accept the configuration, but will be unable to decrypt the attributes. If the system is subsequently rebooted, MCPD will remain inoperative or restart repeatedly during startup. The LTM log files will contain error messages similar to the following: bigip01 notice mcpd[30645]: 01071027:5: Master key OpenSSL error: 4008867572:error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt:evp_enc.c:664: bigip01 notice mcpd[30645]: 01b00001:5: Processed value is empty: class name (usmuser) field name () bigip01 err mcpd[30645]: 01071684:3: Unable to encrypt application variable (/Common/ifoobar_1_1 auth_password usmuser /Common/snmpd). Or bigip01 notice mcpd[7011]: 01b00001:5: Processed value is empty: class name (trapsess) field name () bigip01 err mcpd[7011]: 01071684:3: Unable to encrypt application variable (/Common/i192_0_2_1 auth_password trapsess /Common/snmpd). The LTM log file may contain this log message, indicating that MCPD exited and restarted while attempting to load the configuration: bigip01 emerg load_config_files[25201]: "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g -a load sys config partitions all " - failed. -- Error: failed to reset strict operations; disconnecting from mcpd. Will reconnect on next command.
bugs.conditions: - SNMP configuration that contains Secure Vault-encrypted attributes ("$M$..."), present as SNMPv3 auth-password and/or privacy-password attributes - SNMP configuration is copied from a BIG-IP system to another BIG-IP system, and the two devices do not share the same Secure Vault master key.
bugs.impact: - SNMP configuration does not function. - If the device is rebooted or MCPD is restarted, the system will remain INOPERATIVE or MCPD will be in a restart loop.
bugs.workaround: Do not copy SNMP configuration with encrypted attributes between disparate devices. If a device is currently in an inoperative state and affected by this issue: - Create a backup copy of /config/bigip_base.conf - Manually edit bigip_base.conf and remove the SNMPv3 users and traps - If the system does not recover automatically, restart MCPD or reboot the device once.

bugs.title: SAML SP fails with error 'Response/assertion is not signed' on receiving the assertion
bugs.symptoms: SP shows access denied page In SP APM logs you see the error "Response/assertion is not signed" SAML Agent: /Common/basestar_sp_policy_act_saml_auth_ag failed to parse assertion, error: $fmt

bugs.title: Oauth Discovery task is struck at "SAVE_AND_APPLY" state
bugs.symptoms: Initial symptoms could be one of the following: - Auto JWT discovery task stops or stalls and no reason is provided - OIDC discovery task stops discovering - Auto update of JWK fails - OAuth token does not renew - Oauth Discovery stuck at "SAVE_AND_APPLY" - OAuth Provider Discovery Task does not work anymore Other indications: -> Stale JWK keys will be present in the config and Authentication fails with the following error in /var/log/apm:"OAuth Scope: failed for jwt-provider-list '/Common/VPN_JWT', error: None of the configured JWK keys match the received JWT token, JWT Header: " ->restcurl -X GET tm/access/oidc/discover/ outputs the OIDC discovery task status and status will be in "SAVEANDAPPLY"
bugs.conditions: - jwk keys discovered from the openid well known url should be different from the existing JWK keys in the config - And mcp should fail while applying the config. We can identify that if the /var/log/restjavad does not show the " Applying access policies" log after the "Updating mcp jwt and jwk objects for provide" log
bugs.impact: - Config will contain stale JWK keys
bugs.workaround: - Restart restjavad so that the discovery task starts again
bugs.fix: - Moved the apply access policy operation into a child thread so that the parent thread does not block itself until it receives a response from the mcp. - Earlier the OIDC thread would be blocked until it got a successful response from the mcp for "apply access policy" and if it did receive a response, it would be blocked and would stop permanently without rescheduling itself. - Now, even if the apply access policy fails in the current discovery cycle, the OIDC discovery worker will not be blocked and will be rescheduled for the next interval and the apply access policy will be reattempted as part of the next discovery cycle.

bugs.title: ASM policy IP Address Exceptions list entry shows incorrect route_domain

bugs.title: Unable to download large files through VIP due RST Compression error.
bugs.symptoms: - Download of files exceeding maximum tmm.deflate.memory.threshold fails at client. - Client receives RSTs (Compression error)
bugs.conditions: - Virtual server with HTML profile or REWRITE profile. - Size of decompressed http response from server exceeds max tmm.deflate.memory.threshold value i.e. 4718592 bytes.
bugs.impact: - Client may lose connection to the server.
bugs.workaround: - Based on URI matches in the HTTP request, decide which responses should NOT be rewritten (e.g. big downloads) and disable REWRITE profile for the selected responses. - For example, URI starting with "/headsupp/api/data/compare/measures" : when HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::uri] starts_with "/headsupp/api/data/compare/measures" } { set no_rewrite 1 } } when HTTP_RESPONSE { if { $no_rewrite == 1 } { REWRITE::disable } }
bugs.fix: - Raised the max tmm.deflate.memory.threshold to approx. 9MB, - Changes introduced to allow disabling this threshold altogether if so desired, by changing default value for the same threshold to '0'. - NOTE: Disabling this threshold altogether can lead to exposure to zip bomb attacks.

bugs.title: tmm SIGABRT on Azure VM after VF hot plug
bugs.symptoms: There is known issue article about it - https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000138092 When a hot-plug network event occurs, it may lead to a TMM crash and TMM may not restart properly because of new interface names in the linux kernel.
bugs.conditions: When a hot-plug network event occurs in Azure cloud for a BIG-IP VE, it may cause the interface name changes at the OS level. This interface name change invalidates the mapping that TMM keeps to identify dataplane interfaces, thus causing a tmm crash with following error in the tmm.log: notice stp_state_set: err - undefined ifnet for interface 1.1
bugs.impact: User data traffic gets affected because of the tmm's restart due to SIGABRT. Even after restarting the tmm, it may not come up cleanly.
bugs.workaround: -- The MLNX_OFED (Mellanox OpenFabrics Enterprise Distribution) driver needs to be upgraded. -- Version 17.5.0 uses the upgraded version of MLNX_OFED, so 17.5.0 is not affected. -- For other release a MLNX_OFED patch (clean-up vlan rule) is applied. BIG-IP VE should be restarted to make sure the TMOS controlplane and dataplane can cleanly regenerate the dataplane interface mapping.
bugs.fix: After applying the MLNX_OFED upgrade/patch, the switching (detaching/attaching) of VF devices has become much quicker, taking less than 3 seconds. Previously, it took longer, which was causing the issue.

bugs.title: TMM fails to start up using Xnet-DPDK-virtio due to out of bounds MTU
bugs.symptoms: TMM goes into a restart loop and fails to start with an error message that the MTU is out of bounds Log message: notice virtio_mtu_set(): MTU should be between 68 and 1500
bugs.conditions: - Using Xnet-DPDK-virtio driver - NIC is configured to have an MTU less than NDAL's configured MTU. By default, this is an MTU < 9198
bugs.impact: TMM goes into a restart loop and fails to start
bugs.workaround: Create /config/tmm_init.tcl with the following entry ndal mtu <value> 1af4:1041 Replacing <value> with the corresponding value in the following log line in /var/log/tmm notice virtio_mtu_set(): MTU should be between 68 and <value>

bugs.title: DBDaemon exception logs do not include monitor/object identifiers, preventing quick diagnosis
bugs.symptoms: When DBDaemon logs Java exceptions (for example, DB connection/auth/listener failures), the log entries usually do not include enough object context (monitor, pool member, or key details) to identify which configuration object failed
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP with database monitors in use (mssql, mysql, oracle, postgresql) - Default DBDaemon logging level (debug = no) - Any runtime DB monitor failure that throws/catches exceptions in DBDaemon paths (such as DB_Pinger, MonitorWorker)
bugs.impact: Administrators and support teams cannot quickly identify errors related to the affected monitor or pool member. This results in delays for remediation and often requires debug logging to be enabled in production environments
bugs.workaround: - Enable DBDaemon debug logging (globally or per monitor where possible) to capture additional context - Correlate timestamps/thread IDs in /var/log/DBDaemon-*.log with monitor activity - Manually validate monitor credentials/connect strings on likely affected objects

bugs.title: Running tcpdump on a busy system may cause traffic drop.
bugs.symptoms: Traffic throughput can be degraded.
bugs.conditions: The tcpdump application is executed on high throughput systems.
bugs.impact: Moderate to severe throughput drop is observed.
bugs.workaround: As a general recommendation, use tcpdump filters described in K411 or K2289 while capturing the packets on moderately busy systems. However, on very busy systems, filters alone may not be enough. In this case, there is No workaround.
bugs.fix: Added a new db key 'tmm.tcpdump.pkt.ratelimit'. The default value of this db key is '0'. Also, this is the same behavior with the previous fix. When the value is set to the default value (0), the TMM doesn’t do any rate limiting on the traffic that is sent to the tcpdump application. When the value is set to any other value x, then the TMM applies rate limit of the value x and sends x packets/sec on an average to tcpdump application during capture cycle. For example, if the db variable is set to 200, then each TMM sends an average of 200 pkts/sec to tcpdump application during the life cycle of tcpdump application.
