bugs.title: Database monitor daemon process memory and CPU consumption increases over time
bugs.symptoms: When monitoring pool members using the LTM or GTM mssql (Microsoft SQL Server) monitor, memory and CPU consumption by the database monitor daemon (DBDaemon) process may increase over time. The increase in memory consumption by the DBDaemon process may be gradual and relatively steady over a long period of time, until memory consumption nears an RSS size of approximately 150MB. At that point, CPU consumption may start increasing rapidly. These increases may continue until the DBDaemon process restarts, restoring normal memory and CPU consumption until the cycle begins again.
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur when using the mssql (Microsoft SQL Server) monitor to monitor LTM or GTM pools/members. BIG-IP versions affected by this issue use the MS SQL JDBC (Java DataBase Connectivity) driver v6.4.0 to enable the DBDaemon process to connect to Microsoft SQL Server databases. This issue is not observed with other database types, which use different vendor-specific JDBC drivers, or with more current versions of the MS SQL JDBC driver. The time required for memory and CPU consumption to reach critical levels depends on the number of pool members being monitored, the probe interval for the configured mssql monitors, and whether the mssql monitors are configured to perform a database query (checking the results against a configured recv string) or to make a simple TCP connection with no query (send & recv strings) configured. In one example, a configuration with 600 monitored pool members with a mix of monitors with and without queries and an probe interval of 10 seconds was observed to reach critical memory and CPU consumption levels and restart to recover after approximately 24 hours of continuous operation. To view the memory and CPU usage for the DBDaemon process as recorded over time in tmstats tables, use the following commands. -- To obtain the Process ID (PID) of the DBDaemon process, observe the numeric first element of the output of the following command: "ps ax | grep -v grep | grep DB_monitor" -- To view memory and cpu usage for the DBDaemon process, use the PID obtained from the above command in the following command: "tmctl -D /shared/tmstat/snapshots/blade0/ -s time,cpu_usage_5mins,rss,vsize,pid proc_pid_stat pid=pid_from_above_command" The output of the above command will display statistics at one-hour intervals for the preceding 24 hours, then statistics at 24-hour intervals for prior days. The "cpu_usage_5mins" and "rss" columns display, respectively, the CPU and resident memory usage for the specified DBDaemon process. Gradual increases in "rss" to a critical upper limit near 150MB, and sharp increases in CPU usage as this critical upper memory limit is reached, are indications that this problem is occurring.
bugs.impact: As more objects remain in memory in the DBDaemon process, database monitor query operations may complete more slowly, which may cause pool members to be marked Down incorrectly. As memory and CPU consumption reach critical levels, more pool members may be marked Down. While the DBDaemon process restarts, all pool members monitored by database monitors (mssql, mysql, oracle, postgresql) may be marked Down until the restart is complete and normal operation resumes
bugs.workaround: To prevent memory and CPU consumption from reaching critical levels, you can manually restart the DBDaemon process at a time of your choosing (e.g., during a scheduled maintenance window).

bugs.title: Hybrid X25519_Kyber768 Post Quantum Cryptography Support
bugs.symptoms: Today's cryptography is entirely dependent on prime numbers factorization and discrete logarithms and there are quantum algorithms that efficiently factor the prime number and compute the discrete logarithms. But it requires Quantum computers.

bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Broadcast destination MAC may get offloaded

bugs.title: HTTP may not forward POST with large headers and parking HTTP_REQUEST_RELEASE iRule
bugs.symptoms: The request is not immediately forwarded to the server. It may be forwarded if the server closes the connection. This behavior can also be encountered after an upgrade from 15.x to 16.x or 17.x.
bugs.conditions: Under certain scenarios, the HTTP virtual server with the below iRule attached may not forward HTTP POST requests with large headers: HTTP_REQUEST_RELEASE { HTTP::header replace Authorization [string repeat x 4096] after 1 }
bugs.impact: HTTP POST request is not forwarded to the server side within 60 seconds, resulting in connection issues.
bugs.workaround: A possible workaround is to move the processing from HTTP_REQUEST_RELEASE to HTTP_REQUEST_SEND. Note: However, this workaround can be highly dependent on what actions are performed in the iRules involved.

bugs.title: BIG-IP splits the PUBLISH message when an MQTT profile is applied
bugs.symptoms: When the PUBLISH message is sent from a client, the BIG-IP system splits the message and forwards it in two packets down the chain.
bugs.conditions: Basic Virtual Server with MQTT profile applied.
bugs.impact: MQTT messages can be difficult to read due to fragmentation and poor reorganization by some applications.
bugs.fix: Reunite split messages and forward them without fragmentation.
bugs.behavior: A fix for the bug introduced behavior change, resulting in sending out an MQTT message header with payload (when it is expected) on the server side. 1) This fix works for _any_ MQTT message with a payload. 2) It would delay the egress of the message header until the first chunk of a payload is ready to egress (when a payload is expected for the message). 3) When no payload is expected, the message is immediately egressing.

bugs.title: QUIC connections from the Chrome browser does not upgrade to HTTP/3

bugs.title: Pool member from statically-configured node deleted along with ephemeral pool member using same IP address
bugs.symptoms: If an LTM pool is created containing both FQDN and statically-configured pool members using different port numbers, and the FQDN name resolves to the same IP address as the statically-configured node, if the FQDN name no longer resolves to that IP address, the statically-configured pool member may be deleted along with the ephemeral pool member with the same IP address. In this configuration, the pool in question may be found to contain: -- a statically-configured (not ephemeral) pool member referencing the statically-configured node -- an ephemeral pool member with the same node name and IP address as the statically-configured node Both pool members have the same node name and IP address, since only one node can exist for a given IP address. This prevents a separate ephemeral node from being created with the same IP address as the statically-configured node, forcing both pool members to reference the same statically-configured node with the given IP address.
bugs.conditions: -- The LTM pool contains both FQDN pool members and pool members referencing statically-configured nodes. -- The FQDN and statically-configured pool members use different port numbers. -- The FQDN name resolves to one or more IP addresses that match the statically-configured node. -- The DNS server subsequently no longer resolves the FQDN name to that IP address.
bugs.impact: Pool members may be deleted unexpectedly when DNS records/name resolution changes.
bugs.workaround: To work around this issue: -- Use the same port number for both statically-configured pool members and FQDN pool members. -- Add the statically-configured pool member(s) to the pool before adding any FQDN pool members which resolve to the same IP address(es).

bugs.impact: Datapath lockup. Requires reboot.
bugs.workaround: This has been fixed in all iSeries platforms for BIG-IP versions 15.1.x, 16.1.x, 17.1.x, 15.5.x. Fixed in these bitfiles and all bitfiles newer than these. v15.1.x: ID1757053: HSB v2.10.8.0 bitstream release for VIPRION B2250 blades ID1759517: HSB v3.8.98.0 bitstream release for VIPRION B44x0 blades ID1593933: HSB v5.6.10.0 bitstream release for i5000 / i7000 / i10000-series appliances ID1593929: HSB v5.23.10.0 bitstream release for i11000-series appliances v16.1.x: ID1554997: HSB v2.12.6.0 bitsteam release for VIPRION B2250 blades ID1564281: HSB v3.10.5.0 bitstream release for VIPRION B44x0 blades ID1572961: HSB v5.8.5.0 bitstream release for i5000 / i7000 / i10000-series appliances ID1574653: HSB v5.25.4.0 bitstream release for i11000-series appliances v17.1.x / v17.5.x: ID1587357: HSB v2.13.5.0 bitsteam release for VIPRION B2250 blades ID1582633: HSB v3.11.6.0 bitstream release for VIPRION B44x0 blades ID1587341: HSB v5.9.9.0 bitstream release to AFM for i5000 / i7000 / i10000-series appliances ID1587349: HSB v5.26.5.0 bitstream release for i11000-series appliances
bugs.fix: Bug was found and fixed in the Syn-Ack generator module in the FPGA. First bitfiles with the fix are listed in the Mitigation / Workaround section.

bugs.title: Tmm leak on request-logging or response logging on FTP virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Tmm memory leak is observed.
bugs.conditions: Either of these conditions: -- An LTM profile with request-logging enabled -- response-logging enabled on a virtual server supporting FTP
bugs.impact: A tmm memory leak occurs.
bugs.workaround: Disable request/response logging on the FTP virtual server.

bugs.title: Gtm virtual server query_all related SNMP query could get wrong result
bugs.symptoms: Gtm virtual server query_all related SNMP query could get wrong result such as gtmVsNumber with log message such as: Duplicate oid index found: bigip_gtm_vs.c:184
bugs.conditions: Similar gtm server and virtual server name combination
bugs.impact: SNMP query returns wrong results.
bugs.workaround: Use less similar virtual server names. If the virtual server name is long, ensure the string is different at the beginning of the virtual server name.

bugs.title: Excessive tmm memory during bot signature updates
bugs.symptoms: During bot signature updates, memory usage may become unusually high. In some cases, updates can fail and leave the system in an inconsistent state.
bugs.conditions: This issue may occur when multiple bot signature overrides are configured in Bot Defense profiles. Updates that involve multiple signature overrides are more likely to trigger higher memory usage.
bugs.impact: Bot signature updates may fail due to insufficient memory, which can temporarily prevent new signatures from being applied.
bugs.workaround: Increase available TMM memory by provisioning the LTM module. Reduce the number of multiple overrides (either individual signature overrides or signature category overrides) in Bot Defense profiles, as multiple overrides significantly increase memory usage during updates.
bugs.fix: The fix will optimize the bot signature update mechanism to reduce memory consumption, improve failure handling.

bugs.title: Error message for bot-signature update failure.
bugs.symptoms: Currently there is no specific error message when bot-signature installation fail due to TMM memory pressure. In the event of the failure, user needs to plan restarting TMM as it may lead further issues.
bugs.conditions: Bot-signature update performed under TMM memory pressure.
bugs.impact: No clear error for the update failure, and subsequent unexpected system state.
bugs.workaround: Look for a message "notice MCP message handling failed" in the LTM log.
bugs.fix: A clear and specific error message is introduced.

bugs.title: When F5OS tenants are part of a GTM sync group, rebooting one device may cause monitor flapping on the other
bugs.symptoms: When an F5OS tenant is part of a GTM sync group and it is rebooted, other members of the sync group may experience flapping monitors.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS Tenants -- GTM provisioned -- Prober pools configured
bugs.impact: Flapping GTM monitors when one device is rebooted.
bugs.workaround: Configure gtmd and big3d to wait until tmm is ready before starting cp /etc/bigstart/scripts/big3d /etc/bigstart/scripts/big3d.1552517 cp /etc/bigstart/scripts/gtmd /etc/bigstart/scripts/gtmd.1552517 sed -i 's/tmm running/tmm ready/' /etc/bigstart/scripts/gtmd /etc/bigstart/scripts/big3d

bugs.title: Issues are observed with APM Portal Access on Chrome browser version 122 or later
bugs.symptoms: Web application using APM Portal Access stops working after upgrading to Chrome browser version 122 or later or a similar MS Edge browser version.
bugs.conditions: -- Chrome browser version 122 or later or a similar MS Edge browser version -- APM Portal Access
bugs.impact: Applications will not work through Portal Access.
bugs.workaround: An iRule/iFile workaround is available. Refer to K000138771: APM Portal Access stops working after upgrading Chrome to version 122 (https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000138771)
bugs.fix: APM portal access will work with Chrome browser version 122 or later or a similar MS Edge browser version.

bugs.title: New subsession reads access_token from per-session policy instead of per-request policy.
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP is configured with OAuth Agents both in per-session policy and per-request policy, OAuth Flow fails to execute successfully.
bugs.conditions: When new subsessions are created TMM fails to read the access token from subsession variables. Therefore, gets the old token from the main session, i.e. per-session policy.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP Administrator will not be able to configure BIG-IP as OAuth Client & RS with both per-session policy and per-request policy.
bugs.workaround: Use OAuth Agents only in the per-request policy, configure per-session policy with just empty allow.

bugs.title: Tmm core file was observed in the AVR lookup sweeper
bugs.symptoms: Core file generated due to damaged cells in the avr lookup sweeper.
bugs.conditions: -- AVR is enabled.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: The dashboard displays a substantial increase in public IP addresses.
bugs.symptoms: The dashboard displays additional number of public IP addresses along with the requested client IP address.
bugs.conditions: When collecting statistics from AVR, the dashboard displays a additional number of client addresses in the Client IP address list.
bugs.impact: Sometimes, it provides inconsistent reports for the end user.
bugs.workaround: No Workaround.

bugs.title: For advanced/premium deployment of BD profile, incomplete single js download may lead to blocking Protected URIs.
bugs.symptoms: For Advanced/Premium deployment of a BD profile, if a request to protected URI occurs before the page is fully loaded, incomplete single js download may lead to blocking the Protected URIs.
bugs.conditions: 1. Advanced/Premium deployment of BD profile 2. Protected URI is configured with block / redirect mitigation action. 3. The backend server sends a protected URI request through some script before the entry page is fully loaded.
bugs.impact: BD may block legitimate requests towards protected URIs.

bugs.title: Parsing tcp payload using iRules can be inaccurate because of binary to string conversion
bugs.symptoms: When an iRule is used to parse tcp payload, the value returned as string can be inaccurate.
bugs.conditions: TCP payload is parsed using iRule.
bugs.impact: The iRule functionality may not work as expected, as the parsed data can be inaccurate.

bugs.title: Negative frame number might result in bd crash.
bugs.symptoms: Modifying ASM cookies like cookie prefix, suffix base and revision base might cause bd to crash.
bugs.conditions: See K54501322: Modifying ASM cookie names at https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K54501322 Change the ASM Cookie prefix name, revision base and suffix base as per the above article.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.
bugs.fix: While parsing frame numbers, need to do a check for handling negative frame numbers as well.

bugs.title: Incorrect packet statistics counting upon connection reject/closure.
bugs.symptoms: In rare circumstances, connection statistics might be inaccurate on the BIG-IP system.
bugs.conditions: Some of these conditions will make the problem more likely to happen: - Flow abruptly torn down. - iRule with drop command. - iRule with reject command.
bugs.impact: Incorrect packet statistics are reported.

bugs.title: A BD crash on a specific scenario
bugs.symptoms: A BD crash, failover.
bugs.conditions: Specific requests under specific conditions.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.

bugs.title: HTML::disable not taking effect in HTTP_REQUEST event
bugs.symptoms: A HTML::disable inside an HTTP_REQUEST event will not take effect. It does work for HTTP_RESPONSE.
bugs.conditions: When an HTML::disable is inside an HTTP_REQUEST.
bugs.impact: HTML::disable does not take effect
bugs.workaround: If possible. have the HTML::disable in the HTTP_RESPONSE.

bugs.title: APM - Websso leeway time of 60 seconds
bugs.symptoms: When JWT is cached, then the error "JWT Expired and cannot be used" is observed.
bugs.conditions: WebSSO is used with bearer option to generate JWT tokens.
bugs.impact: JWT fails in upper layer
bugs.fix: Increasing leeway time to 60 sec to accommodate jwt token to be used continuously.

bugs.title: LLDP configuration is disabled on unsupported platforms.
bugs.symptoms: TMUI displayed configuration options for LLDP (Link Layer Discovery Protocol) on platforms that do not support the feature, potentially leading to user confusion.
bugs.conditions: This issue arises when accessing the LLDP configuration page on platforms that do not support LLDP.
bugs.impact: Users may attempt to configure LLDP on unsupported platforms, leading to failed configuration attempts and a confusing user experience.

bugs.title: LLDP values can be configured on all platforms.
bugs.symptoms: LLDP options can be configured on a device, even if the device does not support LLDP.
bugs.conditions: LLDP values can be configured on a system that does not support LLDP, and the configuration will still be applied.
bugs.impact: This causes the device to display an LLDP configuration, which is invalid on systems that do not support LLDP.
bugs.workaround: Only set LLDP values on systems that support LLDP.

bugs.title: Mysql error after roll forward upgrade when uploading base version's csv over upgraded version.
bugs.symptoms: Mysql error when loading 16.1.4 ucs over 16.1.5 system can be seen in asm log.
bugs.conditions: Loading of 16.1.4 ucs on itself - does not cause to any error and loading of 16.1.5 ucs on itself - does not cause to any error. Only loading of 16.1.4 ucs over 16.1.5 system - causes to above mysql error.
bugs.impact: A Foreign key constraint fails DCC.HSL_DATA_PROFILES.
bugs.fix: No errors when loading 16.1.4 ucs over 16.1.5 system.

bugs.title: QUIC virtual server with drop in CLIENT_ACCEPTED crashes TMM
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes on connection if the drop is executed in an iRule on CLIENT_ACCEPTED event.
bugs.conditions: If an iRule contains a drop that is executed on CLIENT_ACCEPTED or CLIENT_DATA on a virtual server supporting HTTP3 (QUIC/UDP) then TMM crashes.
bugs.impact: Traffic is disrupted while restarting TMM.
bugs.workaround: In iRule use FLOW_INIT as the event instead of CLIENT_ACCEPTED to call drop.

bugs.title: TCP filter is not setting packet priority on keep-alive tx packets
bugs.symptoms: When running traffic with multi-bladed environments, some of the TCP MPI backplane packets are not marked with a packet priority.
bugs.conditions: Any multi-bladed environment.
bugs.impact: TCP keepalive packets are not prioritized in the driver
bugs.fix: When running traffic with multi bladed environments it was observed that some of the TCP MPI backplane packets were not being marked with a packet priority. The driver was not prioritizing them accordingly.

bugs.title: WCCP traffic may have its source port changed
bugs.symptoms: WCCP traffic may have its source port changed as it leaves the Linux host. This could cause WCCP sessions to not be established.
bugs.conditions: -- WCCP configured -- BIG-IP Virtual Edition platform or r2000 or r4000 tenants.
bugs.impact: WCCP messages may not be successfully processed by the peer because the source port is not 2048.
bugs.workaround: Cat >> /config/tmm_init.tcl << EOF proxy BIGSELF { listen 0.0.0.0%＼${rtdom_any} 2048 netmask 0.0.0.0 { proto ＼$ipproto(udp) srcport strict idle_timeout 30 transparent no_translate no_arp l2forward tap enable all protect } profile _bigself } EOF bigstart restart tmm

bugs.title: Tmm crash after modifying a virtual server
bugs.symptoms: Tmm crashes after making changes to a virtual server
bugs.conditions: An iRule attempting to access classification results combined with GPA (generic protocol analyser) used for classification.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Alarm and Block flags are enabled for "GraphQL disallowed pattern in response" violation in blank policy template
bugs.symptoms: A policy created with a Blank Policy template has "GraphQL disallowed pattern in response" violation enabled
bugs.conditions: - ASM policy created with Blank Policy template
bugs.impact: - Unexpected violation in Blank Policy

bugs.title: Host authority sub component not parsed properly
bugs.symptoms: URLs lacking a scheme are incorrectly parsed as paths rather than server addresses.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when the server URL is configured without the scheme.
bugs.impact: Misconfiguration of URLs leads to false positive blocks. The host authority is parsed as a path.
bugs.workaround: This behavior can be corrected by adding scheme openapi: 3.0.0 info: title: Sample API version: 1.0.0 servers: - url: https://beta.application-management-test.eset.systems/ paths: /sample_endpoint: get: summary: Create a new entry description: Endpoint to create a new entry with name, age, and date of birth. responses: '200': description: Success response '400': description: Invalid request payload

bugs.title: N3FIPS device lockup can cause TMM crash
bugs.symptoms: TMM process crashes and a core file is generated. You might see the log messages below. -- crit tmm5[21835]: 01010025:2: Device error: crypto codec fips-crypto0-5 queue is stuck. -- warning sod[6477]: 01140029:4: HA crypto_failsafe_t fips-crypto0-5 fails action is go offline and down links. -- notice sod[6477]: 010c0050:5: Sod requests links down. -- notice sod[6477]: 010c0054:5: Offline for traffic group traffic-group-1. -- notice sod[6477]: 010c003e:5: Offline
bugs.conditions: TMM crash can occur if the N3FIPS HSM device locks up.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.
bugs.workaround: Device reboot resolves the problem.

bugs.title: Pool command support functionality to be implemented in WS_REQUEST event
bugs.symptoms: We can create the following iRule in BIG-IP with the pool command. However, the iRule does not work as expected. when WS_REQUEST { log local0. "using myHttpOss2" pool myHttpOss2 }
bugs.conditions: Create an iRule with a WS_REQUEST event and include pool command in it.
bugs.impact: It limits the user functionality, and they cannot write the irules according to their need.
bugs.workaround: Whatever is supported in HTTP_REQUEST should be supportable in WS_REQUEST also. Even though we cannot use the pool command in WS_REQUEST, the purpose can be achieved using the HTTP_REQUEST event.

bugs.title: Tmsh generated config file which fails to load for VLAN specific non-default route-domain IPv6
bugs.symptoms: The configuration fails to load with an error: Syntax Error:(/config/bigip_base.conf at line: 138) "fe80::1%vlan333%1/64" invalid address
bugs.conditions: Tmsh or GUI is used to create a non-default route-domain IPv6 for a VLAN, for example: # tmsh create net self fe80:14d::1%1/64 vlan test
bugs.impact: The configuration fails to load.
bugs.workaround: Delete the affected Self IP address and reload.

bugs.title: Safenet network HSM installation shows unnecessary additional infinite installation options.
bugs.symptoms: Installation of SafeNet is incomplete, as the additional installation options are shown in the prompt. Which affects the Nethsm SafeNet installation completion.
bugs.conditions: Install Safenet UC Client 10.4. in any BIG-IP version above 15.x
bugs.impact: Incomplete installation of SafeNet, affecting the ability to create SafeNet keys and certs.
bugs.fix: Removed the code that leads to prompting additional installation options.

bugs.title: IP Reputation marking Googlebot source IPs as suspicious
bugs.symptoms: IP Reputation database is found to match some Googlebot source IPs as suspicious, which may be undesirable
bugs.conditions: When BIGIP acts as a proxy for Googlebot traffic
bugs.impact: Blocking Googlebot source IPs based on IP Reputation database match may be undesirable

bugs.title: PVA FastL4 accelerated flows might not honor configured keep-alive-interval.
bugs.symptoms: PVA FastL4 accelerated flows may not honor configured keep-alive-interval.
bugs.conditions: The keep-alive-interval option is configured on the FastL4 profile.
bugs.impact: Some connections may be prematurely terminated.

bugs.title: BIG-IP can't reach Shape server if HTTPS is missing in 'Proxy Bot Protection Endpoint URL - Web'.
bugs.symptoms: If the HTTPS scheme is not included in the 'Proxy Bot Protection Endpoint URL - Web' when the proxy is enabled, BIG-IP cannot reach the Shape server. As a result, JavaScript will not be downloaded, and inference will not be received.
bugs.conditions: Proxy is enabled, but HTTPS scheme is not included in the 'Proxy Bot Protection Endpoint URL - Web'
bugs.impact: Bot defence feature won't work. -- Without JavaScript and inference data, Security feature cannot properly analyze and block bot traffic. -- Malicious bot traffic may bypass detection, leading to potential fraud, scraping, or automated attacks. -- Applications relying on Shape's bot protection may not function as expected, potentially affecting user access or API security. -- Traffic analytics and insights from Shape may be incomplete or inaccurate.
bugs.workaround: Add HTTPS scheme along with URL in the 'Proxy Bot Protection Endpoint URL - Web' when the proxy is enabled

bugs.title: Bd crash
bugs.symptoms: Bd crash on a rare scenario.
bugs.conditions: Issue occurs during particular timings.
bugs.impact: This issue led to crashes, traffic disruptions, and failover situations.

bugs.title: Rest_logintegrity does not suppress output to stderr
bugs.symptoms: The find command in rest_logintegrity script fails and returns "No such file or directory" when no matching file is found if there are no newly rotated restnoded, restjavad log files whenever the rest_logintegrity script runs as part of the cron job.
bugs.conditions: When there are no files which matches the below patterns in the script: "/var/log/restjavad.[1-9]*.log", "/var/log/restnoded/restnoded[1-9]*.log".
bugs.impact: Overload of emails with message similar to: find: '/var/log/restnoded/restnoded[1-9]*.log': No such file or directory
bugs.workaround: Creating the files as below mitigates the error touch /var/log/restnoded/restnoded1.log touch /var/log/restjavad.1.log

bugs.title: Host is unreachable, vector is not mitigated by HW at profile level.
bugs.symptoms: HW drops are not getting incremented when traffic was sent to Host. Unreachable vector at profile level.
bugs.conditions: Configure the Host unreachable vector detection and mitigation limits at profile level.
bugs.impact: Hardware mitigation does not happen at profile level.
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: Handled, neuron support checks for host with unreachable vector as the support was not there, such that, the packets were routed directly to flow table to effect the hardware stats.

bugs.title: [GUI] error while updating the rewrite profile uri-rules name have both leading and trailing "/"
bugs.symptoms: Error when updating rewrite profile.
bugs.conditions: Uri-rules name has both leading and trailing "/".
bugs.impact: Uri-rules for rewrite profile is not able to be updated through GUI.
bugs.workaround: Remove either leading or trailing "/" from uri-rules name.

bugs.title: Initial policy sync of any address space fails
bugs.symptoms: Error: 01b7010d:3: The APM resource network-access (/Common/na2) that is associated with the APM resource address-space (/Common/any-space) does not exist."
bugs.conditions: Initial policy sync with any address-space with "Use source configuration on target" enabled.
bugs.impact: Initial Policy sync fails.

bugs.title: Page gets redirected before Captcha is displayed
bugs.symptoms: The blank frame Captcha is not displayed to the user.
bugs.conditions: -- The website is built with React -- DoSL7 profile attached -- ASM policy with blank frame Captcha is configured
bugs.impact: Blank frame Captcha is momentarily displayed and then dismissed and the user does not get a chance to solve the captcha.

bugs.title: SSL sending duplicate certificates
bugs.symptoms: Duplicate certificates sent during the SSL handshake.
bugs.conditions: The chain contains the public certificate and both are configured in the client-ssl profile.
bugs.impact: BIG-IP on clientside SSL sends duplicate certificates during handshake to the client
bugs.workaround: Remove the public server certificate from the chain.

bugs.title: Applying mutliple policies causes apmd to use a lot of CPU causes failure in sessiondb related operations
bugs.symptoms: When you apply multiple access policies, and if there are macros in VPE that expand to lot of Access policy Agents, then creation and initialization of those agents with recursive macro expansion will take more time and also cause 50% to 60% CPU usage by APMD process. Now in this case if LDAP server, especially with pool members configured may lead to 100% CPU usage for more than 2 to 5 min. This is due to clearing of LDAP cache. As LDAP servers pool members use loopback interface and also session db operations are done on same interface, this may lead to failure in session db set/get operations which ultimately leads to failures in OAuth Scope validation and other operations.
bugs.conditions: 1. Applying an access policy that is for one or more policies, with more agents (around 3000 for example). 2. LDAP servers are configured and User sends new LDAP auth and query requests to APM at same time. 3. Session db operations should fail to see any unexpected failures like oauth scope validation failure.
bugs.impact: OAuth scope validation fails due to high CPU usage by APMD and Access policy is evaluated as failure and Basic auth headers are send to backend.
bugs.fix: APMD should not use high CPU usage and Oauth Scope validation should not fail.

bugs.title: BD total_max_mem is initialized with a low (default) value resulting in many issues with long request buffers and traffic failing
bugs.symptoms: When BD starts it is assigned a very low value for total_max_mem
bugs.conditions: ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: This causes many connections to fail with ASM resetting them.
bugs.workaround: Monitor "var/log/ts/asm_start.log" for the "F5::ProcessHandler::start_bd,,bd exec line" and see the value for "total_umu_max_size". If it is "768000" or there are other visible errors - restart asm on that device.

bugs.title: Rephrase Online Help for "Base64 Decoding" option for Authorization header.
bugs.symptoms: The online help does not specify why "Base64 Decoding" value is set to disabled by default and cannot be modified.
bugs.impact: Online help does not adequately explain the Base64 Decoding setting.

bugs.title: Cannot modify the monitor type (defaults from) with "tmsh load sys config file <filename> replace" command
bugs.symptoms: When attempting to modify an existing monitor through tmsh, the "replace" verb will throw an error when attempting to modify the "defaults-from" field, while the "merge" verb will not. "01070685:3: Cannot modify the monitor type (defaults from) for monitor ..."
bugs.conditions: (1) Create a BIG-IP instance and log into the console as root. (2) In the /shared folder, create two .out files with monitor declarations in them with the following stipulations (see above for examples): (a) Both monitor declarations must have the same monitor name. (b) Each declaration must have a different parent profile and defaults-from type (ex. http for one declaration and https for the other). (c) The parent profile type for each monitor must be the same as its defaults-from value. (3) Add one of the monitors to your device by using the following command: (a) tmsh load sys config file /shared/<your-file>.out replace
bugs.impact: In tmsh using the "replace" verb throws an error when updating the default-from field, while the "merge" verb does not.

bugs.title: [APM]Access Policy Export does not write certificate authority profile correctly to ng_export.conf
bugs.symptoms: When a machine cert check agent is used in an access policy and references a certificate authority profile, policy export does not create the object properly in the ng_export.conf file. This causes the subsequent import to fail. 1. Export policy from 17.1.1 2. Attempt to import into another APM on 17.1.1 3. In the GUI it refreshes, but never imports. 4. Import command fails with this error: 21:12:06 0 error: 01020036:3: The requested profile_certificateauthority (/Common/my-ca) was not found. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.
bugs.conditions: Importing a policy from one APM system into another APM system.
bugs.impact: Can not import the access policy into a different APM.
bugs.workaround: Modify the ng_export.conf file to add @name- in the certificate-authority profile object: ltm profile certificate-authority /@partition/@name-my-ca {

bugs.title: Bd can crash using JSON schema
bugs.symptoms: Bd crashes while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: Using JSON schema
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while bd restarts.
bugs.workaround: Remove JSON schema from JSON content profile, and enforce JSON payload via "parse parameter" feature available in JSON content profile.

bugs.title: Qkview truncates log files without notification
bugs.symptoms: When generating a qkview on a BIG-IP system via the GUI or command line: -- Log files included in the qkview will be truncated if they exceed the maximum log file size. -- Log file truncation occurs even with the "-s 0" command line option or "Unlimited snaplen" GUI checkbox, if the log file exceeds 100MB in size. -- No user-visible notification is provided that log file truncation has occurred. The "Unlimited snaplen" GUI checkbox does not actually remove the maximum log file size limit of 100MB. Selecting the "Unlimited snaplen" GUI checkbox limits the maximum log file size to 100MB. Log files larger than 100MB will still be truncated, even if the "Unlimited snaplen" checkbox is selected when generating a Support Snapshot from the GUI.
bugs.conditions: Log file truncation occurs if: -- The log file exceeds 5MB in size and: -- The qkview utility is launched from the command line without the "-s" option to specify a larger maximum file size, or a Support Snapshot is request from the GUI without selecting the "Unlimited snaplen" checkbox. -- The log file exceeds 100MB in size and: -- The qkview utility is launched from the command line with the "-s 0" option to specify a 100MB maximum file size, or a Support Snapshot is request from the GUI without selecting the "Unlimited snaplen" checkbox. -- The log file exceeds the maximum file size specified by the "-s" option when running the qkview utility from the command line.
bugs.impact: Log files included in qkviews may be truncated unexpectedly without the user being aware. If additional actions are not taken to create untruncated archives of affected log files, data required to diagnose BIG-IP issues may be permanently lost due to incomplete data in the qkview, and subsequent log rotation on the affected BIG-IP system.
bugs.workaround: To check whether a qkview file contains truncated log files, use the "tar" utility at a command line to check for files with "_truncated" appended to the file name. For example: tar -tf /var/tmp/my-test-qkview.qkview | grep truncated var/log/DBDaemon-0.log_truncated If the qkview file contains truncated log files, manually create a log file archive containing untruncated versions of the affected log files.

bugs.title: Cookie SameSite attribute is removed by sesstimeout.js
bugs.symptoms: Observe samesite cookie is missing in Developer tools.
bugs.conditions: APM set SameSite attribute to F5_ST cookie, When enabled "Samesite option*". * Access Profile > SSL Orchestrator/Auth Domains > Cookie options
bugs.impact: Samesite cookie is missing

bugs.title: The SIP MRF virtual servers with mirroring enabled can lead to a connflow leak on standby
bugs.symptoms: There is a connflow memory leak on standby.
bugs.conditions: SIP MRF virtual servers with mirroring enabled
bugs.impact: TMM memory use will increase on the standby device.
bugs.fix: No memory leak in connflow observed on standby.

bugs.title: 'reject' command not working in SIP_REQUEST_SEND event
bugs.symptoms: A connection stays open even though reject was invoked in the iRule.
bugs.conditions: If the reject is within a SIP_REQUEST_SEND event, it will not take effect. It will work if it is under a SIP_REQUEST.
bugs.impact: Connection stays open until closed by idle timeout
bugs.workaround: If possible, use event SIP_REQUEST instead

bugs.title: Configuration fails to load while upgrading from BIG-IP 14.0.x to BIG-IP 15.1.10.3
bugs.symptoms: A few category names and descriptions have been updated from Forcepoint, and incorporating those changes in BIG-IP 15.1.10 triggered this upgrade failure.
bugs.conditions: Upgrade from the BIG-IP version where the latest category names were not present to the version where they exist with some additional configuration will fail the BIG-IP upgrade.
bugs.impact: After the upgrade, the configuration fails to load with one or more "In url-filter" errors. Following is an example: 01070734:3: Configuration error: In url-filter {}...
bugs.workaround: No workaround. Remove the affected category names before attempting the BIG-IP upgrade.
bugs.fix: Code exists to map older categories with new categories when upgrading in versions prior to BIG-IP 13.x. The same code will be fixed to correctly map categories when upgrading for versions BIG-IP 15.x and later.

bugs.title: Client connection gets reset after upgrade to 17.1.1
bugs.symptoms: Client connection gets reset
bugs.conditions: iRule attached to virtual server with AVR::disbale
bugs.impact: Connection reset, request does not pass.
bugs.workaround: Remove AVR::disable iRule
bugs.fix: Request gets passed without any connection reset.

bugs.title: Pool member stats are not reported for 2 of 10 pool-members in MRF diameter pool
bugs.symptoms: A problem is noticed when previous connections to the pool member exist and a new pool member is added with the same IP address and port. Due to this, the pool member (same IP and port) has no connections associated with it. If new connections are made to the new pool member, the stats will be non-zero
bugs.conditions: Pool members with long-lived connections are deleted after re-creating the pool member. Now the new pool member does not have any connections, so its stats will be zero until a new connection is made
bugs.impact: But the reason you are seeing empty stats is that the new pool member (same IP and port) has no connections associated with it. When new connections are made to the new pool member, the stats will be non-zero
bugs.workaround: If you do not want to lose the stats, it is recommended to avoid deleting pool members with outstanding connection(s) and consider disabling them instead.

bugs.title: Upgrade from version 14.X to version 15.X may encounter problems with L2 forwarding for some of the flows.
bugs.symptoms: L2 forwarding issues may be encountered for some flows. Due to this, there can be hinderances in the traffic flow towards server.
bugs.conditions: Flow 1: Client(L3 Net1)--- (vg2)--> BIG-IP --(vg1)--> Gateway --(vg1)--> BIG-IP (again) --(vg2)--> server(L3 Net2) 1. Client and server are in same vlan but not in same subnet. 2. Gateway is in another vlan, it is the gateway for both client and server. 3. connection.vlankeyed is disabled. 4. After an upgrade from 14.X to 15.X, traffic returning from gateway towards the server is dropped Flow 2: Client --(VG1)--> BIG-IP --(nonVgVlan1)--> IPS --(nonVgVlan2)--> BIG-IP (again) --(VG2)--> Server 1. Client traffic over transparent vlan-group towards Server is intercepted by a standard virtual server and sent to IPS on a non-vlan-group vlan. 2. connection.vgl2transparent is enabled 3. When traffic is sent from BIG-IP to IPS, the destination MAC will be the MAC address of a server (ARL non local) and the source MAC is still the original client MAC which is breaking the returning traffic from IPS. 4. The expectation here is traffic leaving from BIG-IP to IPS should have BIG-IP nonVgVlan1 MAC address as source MAC.
bugs.impact: Traffic drop is observed when packets are sent towards server.
bugs.workaround: For this workaround, ensure "nw_l2_transparent license enabled". 1. For Flow 1, keep connection.vgl2transparent disabled and add the following config: ltm virtual VG_transparent { destination <SERVER> ip-protocol tcp l2-forward mask 255.255.255.255 profiles { fastL4 { } } rules { t-nexthop } source 0.0.0.0/0 translate-address enabled translate-port enabled vlans { vg2 } vlans-enabled } ltm rule t-nexthop { when CLIENT_ACCEPTED { nexthop vg1 transparent } when SERVER_CONNECTED { nexthop vg2 transparent } } 2. For Flow 2, keep connection.vgl2transparent disabled.

bugs.title: Certain user roles cannot modify the Address Lists in Shared Objects in normal flow

bugs.title: MCP stats query may overflow message size and crash bcm56xxd when querying large tables
bugs.symptoms: - MCPD takes a long time to process large firewall rule stats (about 20k), and sometimes much longer - MCPD abruptly drops the LACPD connection, causing LACPD to restart - Multiple “MCPD query response exceeding” messages appear, followed by bcm core dumps (e.g., 010e0004:4: MCPD query response exceeding 60 seconds) - SNMP warnings report “MCPD query response exceeding 30 seconds” - MCP query execution times are very long and highly variable - bcm56xxd blocks in mcpmsg_send() or writev() - bcm56xxd core files are generated - MCP message body_length fields are corrupted, far exceeding the buffer size
bugs.conditions: Any of these conditions can act as a trigger: - More than 20k firewall rules are configured, and pccd.overlap.check is enabled - Large statistics tables are present - SNMP performs table walks over MCP-backed statistics - MCP message size grows beyond expected limits due to incorrect accumulation logic
bugs.impact: - MCPD fw_rule_stat queries are slow; LACPD restarts abruptly, potentially leading to bcm core - Control plane instability - SNMP monitoring disruption - bcm56xxd crash and restart
bugs.workaround: - Disable db pccd.overlap.check (if AFM is involved) - Reduce SNMP polling frequency - Avoid wide SNMP table walks over large statistics tables

bugs.title: wr_urldbd cloud lookup is not optimal using a connection
bugs.symptoms: The wr_urldbd cloud lookup is currently utilizing only one connection and that connection is not being used efficiently.
bugs.conditions: wr_urldbd does use the connection not efficiently.
bugs.impact: wr_urldbd does use the connection not efficiently.
bugs.fix: The fix introduces 2 new parameters in /etc/wr_urldb/bcsdk.cfg IpcPollMax=250 AsyncBatch=250 IpcPollMax defines the maximum messages retrieved from tmm in one poll. AsyncBatch defines the maximum outstanding messages in flight. When reached, wr_urldbd will wait to receive the responses thereof.

bugs.title: Intermittent high packet latency on R4000 and R2000 tenants
bugs.symptoms: When compared to previous platforms, BIG-IP tenants on R4000 and R2000 platforms may demonstrate higher jitter and packet latency / rtt. This affects pings, tcp, udp, and any other protocols processed by the software data plane (tmm). This is because the r4000 and r2000 appliances have a slightly different hardware architecture than other appliances. CPUs on this platform are not dedicated to the tenant and these platforms also run a different class of Intel processing, and do not utilize hyperthreading like the higher end platforms do. See: https://clouddocs.f5.com/training/community/rseries-training/html/rseries_performance_and_sizing.html#r4000-vcpu-sizing
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP tenants on R4000 and R2000 platforms
bugs.impact: Intermittent high latency and jitter.

bugs.title: In-TMM monitor marks pool/node down despite response received, reason: "missed response; remaining down"
bugs.symptoms: In-TMM Monitor marks pool/node down despite receiving a response.
bugs.conditions: in-tmm monitor mode enabled
bugs.impact: When the monitor marks a pool or node as down, traffic may not be sent to the backend pool or node if it is attached to a virtual server.

bugs.title: After merging config 'any' addresses are modified to '0.0.0.0' in fw policies
bugs.symptoms: tmsh load sys config merge file <file_path> Post merge, the configuration AFM changes 'any' to 0.0.0.0 instead of 0.0.0.0/0 destination { addresses { any { } <<<< } While merging (tmsh load sys config merge file <file_path>) AFM changes to 0.0.0.0 instead of 0.0.0.0/0 destination { addresses { 0.0.0.0 { } <<<< }

bugs.impact: When performing the change as a transaction, the transaction fails. When performing a config restore via a UCS load, config restore fails.
bugs.workaround: Before restoring, create the route-domain or modify the MTU setting ahead of time, and then load the UCS file.

bugs.title: SAML SP not sending Authnrequest and throwing an error "Failed to get authentication request from session variable 'session.samlcryptodata.CompressAuthnRQ' for SAML Agent: /Common/SP_access_policy_act_saml_auth_ag."

bugs.title: Bcm56xxd will miss sending a heartbeat if the last time it sent a heartbeat took greater than 1 second

bugs.title: Add option to QoS mark egress BFD packets
bugs.symptoms: Currently existing tm.egressdscp db variable does not provide enough flexibility in configuring Quality of Service (QoS), as it applies to all egress TMM connections (including monitor traffic and other protocols). Add an option to QoS mark egress BFD packets.
bugs.conditions: - Configuring QoS
bugs.impact: No impact
bugs.fix: Added a new db variable TM.BFDEgressDscp controlling DSCP value of egress BFD packets. Default is 0 (zero). Following is an example: root@(bigip1)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list sys db tm.bfdegressdscp sys db tm.bfdegressdscp { value "45" }

bugs.title: Add option to QoS mark egress BGP packets
bugs.symptoms: Currently existing tm.egressdscp db variable does not provide enough flexibility in configuring Quality of Service (QoS), as it applies to all egress TMM connections (including monitor traffic and other protocols). Add an option to QoS mark egress BGP packets, to apply a QoS marking to BGP packets as they leave a router.
bugs.conditions: - Configuring QoS.
bugs.impact: No impact
bugs.fix: Added a new db variable TM.BGPEgressDscp controlling DSCP value of egress BGP packets. Default is 0 (zero). A BGP session restart is required. Following is an example: root@(bigip1)(cfg-sync Standalone)(Active)(/Common)(tmos)# list sys db tm.bgpegressdscp sys db tm.bgpegressdscp { value "42" }

bugs.title: Enhanced performance for the SSL Certificate Import page in TMUI.
bugs.symptoms: The SSL Certificate Import page in TMUI may experience prolonged load times or fail to load entirely, affecting certificate management operations.
bugs.conditions: This issue may arise when accessing the SSL Certificate Import page in TMUI, especially in environments with a high volume of SSL certificates, keys, or related objects.
bugs.impact: Users may encounter delays or be unable to access the SSL Certificate Import page, hindering their ability to import or manage SSL certificates via TMUI.

bugs.title: View_proxy configuration is ignored while patching the PCoIP connection
bugs.symptoms: When the user configures view_proxy in iApp using "If external clients use a network translated address to access View, what is the public-facing IP address?" (or) In VPE using variable assign, APM VMware VDI does not consider this value in patching PCoIP connection. It only finds the Host Header value or virtual server IP address.
bugs.conditions: This issue is seen when: 1. The view_proxy is configured. 2. PCoIP is used to connect to a desktop/app.
bugs.impact: In some network deployments, the user will not be able to open a PCoIP connection to the desktop/app.
bugs.workaround: When HTTP_REQUEST { if { [HTTP::uri] contains "/broker/xml" } { set jsid [HTTP::cookie value JSESSIONID] if { $jsid != "" } { set ctype [ACCESS::session data get -sid $jsid session.client.type] if { $ctype != "" && $ctype == "apm-webtop" } { set vproxy [ACCESS::session data get -sid $jsid view.proxy_addr] set old_host [HTTP::host] if { $vproxy != "" && $old_host != "" && $vproxy != $old_host } { HTTP::header replace "Host" $vproxy log local0. "Replaced - jsid = $jsid vproxy = $vproxy host = $old_host" } } } } }
bugs.fix: APM VMware VDI should use the view_proxy address instead of the host header.

bugs.title: Expect header is not forwarded to pool when PingAccess profile is applied to VS
bugs.symptoms: When a PingAccess profile is added to a virtual HTTP, expect headers from clients are not forwarded to the HTTP server even though headers exist.
bugs.conditions: Basic PingAccess setup Attach the ping pool to the PingAccess profile PingAccess profile added to a virtual server Restart the PingAccess plugin (it will cache lookups and the Expect header is only dropped for cache misses) Bigstart restart ping_access_agent Send an HTTP request with an Expect header, e.g. curl --location --request POST https://10.10.10.88/ -H "Expect: 100-continue" -H "Foo: bar" -vk
bugs.impact: Since no HTTP 100 is received by the client, it causes connection retries and eventually times out not able to send requests further.

bugs.title: Unable to tcpdump on interface name with length = 64.
bugs.symptoms: Users cannot perform tcpdump on a TMM interface with an exact maximum interface name length of 64.
bugs.conditions: The interface name length is equal to 64.
bugs.impact: Unable to perform tcpdump.

bugs.title: Value of csrftoken is mistakenly classified as valid Base64

bugs.impact: Request is not blocked leading to a false negative

bugs.title: BIG-IP tries to resume SSL sessions when session ID only matches partially
bugs.symptoms: After receiving the SSL session ID which partially matches a session ID in the cache VIP with the client SSL profile attempts to resume the session. For example - there is an existing Session ID: session_id[32]= 28 67 9b 30 dc 8a 6e f4 d1 ef 80 f9 04 93 d6 3d fb 2e ea b5 ac c2 be f1 6b e7 42 ef 54 a3 a6 cd When a client sends Client Hello with resume [32]= 12 11 11 12 12 12 12 12 11 11 80 f9 04 93 d6 3d fb 2e ea b5 ac c2 be f1 6b e7 42 ef 54 a3 a6 cd BIG-IP resumes the session.
bugs.conditions: - Create VIP with client SSL profile. - Create a new TLS session (for example with 'openssl s_client') - Try to reuse the existing session with some of the bytes of the session ID altered.
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP sends a ServerHello with a different Session ID from the one in the ClientHello and then attempts to resume a TLS session.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: Fix for ID1168157 does not work for some non-basic latin characters.
bugs.symptoms: Malformed JSON error occurs when few non-basic latin characters are in schema block after the fix for ID1168157.
bugs.conditions: Non basic Latin characters are found in the schema entry of OpenAPI file. Fix for ID1168157 is included.
bugs.impact: The entity "JSON schema validation file" in security policy will not be created for "schema" entry that contain special ASCII characters.

bugs.title: Religion URL Categories not found on SWG database download
bugs.symptoms: Error messages in /var/log/apm "The requested URL Category (/Common/Lesser-Known_Religions) was not found." "The requested URL Category (/Common/Widely-Known_Religions) was not found."
bugs.conditions: APM provisions and SWG database downloads enabled.
bugs.impact: Religion URLs do not get get categorized properly from the SWG database

bugs.title: TMM may drop MRF messages after a failover.
bugs.symptoms: If the Standby unit of an HA pair configured for MRF mirroring drops a message, the TCP state will be out of sync between the two units and possibly cause the Standby to fail to pass traffic when it goes Active.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP configured with HA mirroring and MRF profile_diameterrouter_stat.common.tot_messages_standby_dropped has incremented on the affected profile A failover occurs
bugs.impact: After a failover, TMM will ACK incoming MRF messages and not forward them to the peer.
bugs.workaround: Delete the affected connflow. Ensure that messages are not dropped on the standby by any or all of the following: - Increase the mirrored-message-sweeper-interval: modify ltm message-routing diameter profile router <name> mirrored-message-sweeper-interval 1000 -> 5000 - Ensure that the HA connection does not have excessive latency or packet loss. The "Buffered" stat in the ha-mirror statistics table should be low. See K54622241 for details. - Ensure that the Maximum Pending Messages setting in the Diameter router profile is high enough to handle the message load.

bugs.title: APM: Disabling "Webtop Redirect on Root URI" causes TCP connection reset instead of session re-evaluation
bugs.symptoms: When the "Webtop Redirect on Root URI" option is disabled on an Access Profile, accessing the root URI (e.g., https://apm-vs/) from a browser that has an existing validated webtop session results in a TCP connection reset (RST) with the message "No server selected," instead of re-initiating the session
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following are true: - An Access Profile is configured with a webtop resource assigned (e.g., via Advanced Resource Assign) - The "Webtop Redirect on Root URI" option is disabled on the Access Profile - A client with an existing valid session accesses the root URI of the APM Virtual Server in a new tab or request
bugs.impact: Clients with active webtop sessions encounter an abrupt TCP RST (Reset) when attempting to navigate to the root URI. Since webtop sessions usually do not have a default pool configured, the request cannot be forwarded. As a result, the connection is terminated at the TCP layer instead of receiving an appropriate HTTP response. This leads to a poor user experience and unexpected session termination
bugs.workaround: Enable the "Webtop Redirect on Root URI" option in the Access Profile. When this option is enabled, clients with an active Webtop session who access the root URI will be redirected to the Webtop UI.

bugs.title: TMM instability when processing IPS pattern matches under load
bugs.symptoms: When processing many IPS patterns, the TMM may become unstable.
bugs.conditions: When an IPS profile is enabled on a virtual server.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and service disruption
bugs.fix: Instability no longer occurs.

bugs.title: TMM crash when memcached querying samlcryptodata
bugs.symptoms: Observed a TMM crash
bugs.conditions: Conditions are unknown, this was only seen once.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Jitterentropy read is restricted to FIPS mode or TMM usage only, for performance reasons
bugs.symptoms: If jitterentropy-read from CPU jitter is used in all cases, a big performance problem is seen for most cases where BIG-IP works in non-FIPS mode. This can be encountered after upgrading to version 17.x from an earlier BIG-IP version.
bugs.conditions: The issues occur when BIG-IP operates in non-FIPS or FIPS mode and use jitterentropy to generate seed.
bugs.impact: Very high CPU utilization is seen when BIG-IP handles traffic while in non-FIPS mode.
bugs.fix: Jitterentropy-read of CPU jitter is now invoked in any one of these situations, - Either BIG-IP operates in FIPS mode, - TMM is processing traffic in non-FIPS and FIPS modes. In this case, none of the other components perform the stated jitter read operations and improves performance.

bugs.title: Signatures triggered for cookies with empty values after upgrade to 17.1.1.1

bugs.title: Tmm tunnel failed to respond to ISAKMP
bugs.symptoms: While trying to negotiate the tunnel, multiple IPSEC SAs are created. This increases the tunnel count, but the tunnels are not in a working state.
bugs.conditions: -- Use wildcard ips for source/destination address in traffic selector. -- Change the destination address to a specific address.
bugs.impact: IPSEC traffic is disrupted.
bugs.workaround: Keep responder's IKE peer as passive so that it can never be an initiator.
bugs.fix: The issue occurs because next hops are not refreshed in case of traffic narrowing. (changing of destination address from wildcard to specific) Make explicit calls to refresh next hops in case of narrowing.

bugs.title: The server_connected event related logs in policy attached to a FastL4 virtual server is not logged to the LTM log

bugs.impact: The server_connected event logs not seen in LTM logs.
bugs.fix: The server_connected event logs are now logged in LTM logs.

bugs.title: MCPD thrown exception when syncing from active device to standby device.

bugs.title: Memory leak in ipsec code

bugs.title: Wr_urldbd IPC memory leak

bugs.workaround: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Existing SameSite attribute for cookie is not detected in response in case of no closing semi-colon after attribute's value
bugs.symptoms: The system does not properly recognize the presence of the SameSite=Strict attribute when the attribute value is not followed by a semi-colon, leading to the unintended addition of another SameSite attribute.
bugs.conditions: Occurs when the SameSite=Strict attribute in the response header does not have a closing semi-colon.
bugs.impact: This behavior affects the integrity of the SameSite attribute in cookies
bugs.fix: SameSite attribute is correctly identified, regardless of the presence of a trailing semi-colon

bugs.title: Unbounded GENERICMESSAGE queue growth
bugs.symptoms: TMM memory grows while passing traffic.
bugs.conditions: The GENERICMESSAGE::message iRule event is used with the no_response parameter set to 'no'. If requests messages are sent and a response message does not occur, the request messages are added to the cur_pending_requests. It keeps growing without any control.
bugs.impact: Cur_pending_requests under profile_genericmsg_stat keeps growing. "filter" memory keeps growing.
bugs.fix: Introduced new attributes in the generic message configuration such as cur_pending_request_sweeper_interval and transaction_timeout to start the timer and periodically check the queue to remove the stale entries after expiration timeout. With the fix, the expired messages are deleted from the queue once they are expired.

bugs.title: iRule 'members' command counts FQDN pool members.
bugs.symptoms: iRule 'members' command counts and lists FQDN pool members.
bugs.conditions: - create a pool with at least one FQDN member. - use the members function in an iRule.

bugs.workaround: When FQDN pool members are present, using the 'members' command in the iRule will not yield the desired result.

bugs.title: Vlan-group with ALH disabled and no self-ip configured fails to forward traffic
bugs.symptoms: Server-side returning traffic is not forwarded

bugs.title: Bcm56xxd crashes when executing qkview if the length of the trunk name exceeds 78 characters.

bugs.impact: Interfaces going down when bcm56xxd crashes.

bugs.title: F5OS tenant may not pass FastL4 accelerated traffic through VLAN group
bugs.symptoms: When a connection of a virtual server where either the client- or server-side flow is connected via a VLAN Group is offloaded, the flow-cache entry will contain VLAN ID 0 for the corresponding flow(s). VLAN ID 0 is invalid and packets hitting the flow-cache entry are dropped by the hardware.
bugs.conditions: -- F5OS platform. -- FastL4 virtual. -- Either side of the flow is connected via a VLAN Group.
bugs.impact: Service degradation of the affected virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Disable PVA offload in the fastl4 profile.
bugs.fix: Flows connecting to a VLAN Group are excluded from hardware offload.

bugs.title: SAML Single Logout should use 'SessionIndex' to disconnect SAML sessios
bugs.symptoms: APM SAML IdP locates the external SAML SP connector matching 'EntityID' from configuration and 'Issuer' from SAML SLO request. This implementation may fail if an external SAML SP configures all its SAML SP objects with the same 'EntityID' and some of them initiates the SAML SLO.

bugs.impact: SAML SLO fails

bugs.title: Input validation improvements
bugs.symptoms: A REST API endpoint may incorrectly parse certain parameters.
bugs.impact: Incorrect behavior

bugs.title: Saml traffic can rarely cause tmm cores

bugs.conditions: This was seen when there was a permissions error loading the service provider key.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Zonerunner GUI can become unresponsive when managing large number of records
bugs.symptoms: Zonerunner GUI becomes unresponsive when attempting to view a large number of resource records.
bugs.conditions: DNS zones with a large number of resource records (over 60k) or when the cumulative number of resource records of all the zones exceeds 1000k records.
bugs.impact: - Zonerunner is a DNS client just like dig and nslookup. When it displays all the resource records in a zone, it makes an AXFR request to bind. - When it is asked to display a large number of records, the process can be CPU intensive and the GUI can become unresponsive.
bugs.workaround: - Limit the number of records per zone to less than 60k. - Limit the cumulative number of records to less than 1000k

bugs.title: "Insert Secure Attribute" must be enabled and "Insert SameSite Attribute" must be set to "Lax" for pure wildcard cookie in all templates by default
bugs.symptoms: The pure wildcard cookie configuration "Insert Secure Attribute" is disabled and "Insert SameSite Attribute" is not set to "Lax".

bugs.impact: The configuration is incorrect.
bugs.workaround: Configure it manually: Enable "Insert Secure Attribute" and set "Insert SameSite Attribute" to "Lax".
bugs.fix: Fixed the templates and now BIG-IP has the correct configuration for the pure wildcard cookie.

bugs.title: TMM core in SSL operation
bugs.symptoms: During ssl operation, TMM crashes because of a use of memory element that was freed.
bugs.conditions: Rare event but the conditions are not known
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts.

bugs.title: Access Policy Export does not write OCSP profile correctly to ng_export.conf
bugs.symptoms: After exporting an Access Policy, further import shows such error: Import error: 0107134a:3: File object by name (Common/Cert_Name_Example.crt) is missing. Unexpected Error: Loading configuration process failed.)
bugs.conditions: - OCSP profile configured with "Verify Other" - OCSP Auth agent configured with such OCSP responder in an Access Policy
bugs.impact: Unable to export/import Access policy

bugs.title: "Out of bounds" TCL error in VDI iRule
bugs.symptoms: You may observe below error logs in /var/log/ltm “Out of bounds” TCL error
bugs.conditions: Citrix VDI with an Integration mode.
bugs.impact: Unable to process VDI traffic.

bugs.title: The trunk name length must not exceed 64 characters.

bugs.title: Captcha prompt not presented

bugs.title: PEM fastl4 offload with fastl4 leaks memory

bugs.title: SSL handshake failures with error message Profile <name> cannot load key/cert/chain

bugs.title: "/f5-h-$$/" string repeatedly appended to URL's path on each page refresh
bugs.symptoms: Observe multiple "/f5-h-$$/" in URLs when accessing via Protected Access.
bugs.conditions: "<base href="xxxxx">" tag in the home page.
bugs.impact: URLs become lengthy upon every refresh and may lead to webapp malfunction.
bugs.workaround: Please note that the following is an example of a customized iRule. The hex code will need to be updated for the site's specific URL. The hex below "6578616d706c652e636f6dz" represents "example.com" - Update accordingly for the affected URL. ====================== when REWRITE_REQUEST_DONE { if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "path_to_file1" } { REWRITE::post_process 1 set rewrite_new 1 } if { [HTTP::path] ends_with "path_to_file2" } { REWRITE::post_process 1 set rewrite_new1 1 } } when REWRITE_RESPONSE_DONE { if {[info exists rewrite_new]} { unset rewrite_new set rewrite_str {<base href="f5-h-$$path_in_file1">} set rewrite_str_len [string length $rewrite_str] set strt [string first $rewrite_str [REWRITE::payload]] if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt $rewrite_str_len {<base href="/f5-w-6578616d706c652e636f6d/path_in_file1">} } } if {[info exists rewrite_new1]} { unset rewrite_new1 set rewrite_str {<base href="f5-h-$$/path_in_file2">} set rewrite_str_len [string length $rewrite_str] set strt [string first $rewrite_str [REWRITE::payload]] if {$strt > 0} { REWRITE::payload replace $strt $rewrite_str_len {<base href="/f5-w-6578616d706c652e636f6d/path_in_file2">} } } } ======================

bugs.title: [F5OS Changes] vlan members fails to populate inside the tenant if vlans attached to interface before deploying the tenant if VLANs spanning multiple interfaces are configured
bugs.symptoms: You can tag the same VLAN to multiple interfaces on r2K/r4K platforms, but when you attach VLANs to interfaces before deploying the tenant, the VLAN members will not be populated in the tenant. On BIG-IP, running 'tmsh list net vlan' will not show any tagged VLANs from F5OS.

bugs.impact: The BIG-IP tenant will not show the expected VLANs.

Example: appliance-1(config)# no interfaces interface 1.0 ethernet switched-vlan config appliance-1(config)# no interfaces interface 7.0 ethernet switched-vlan config appliance-1(config)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1(config)# interfaces interface 1.0 ethernet switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 1001 3006 ] appliance-1(config-interface-1.0)# interfaces interface 7.0 ethernet switched-vlan config trunk-vlans [ 1001 3006 ] appliance-1(config-interface-8.0)# commit Commit complete. appliance-1(config-interface-8.0)#

bugs.title: Repeated toggling of the failover-method for an HA group from ha-order to ha-score may result in an unexpected failover.

bugs.title: SA Delete is not send to other end
bugs.symptoms: If an IPsec tunnel is deleted, the remote peer will not know about the deletion and invalid Security Associations (SAs) will remain valid.
bugs.conditions: - Create IPsec interface mode tunnel. - Establish tunnel. - Change the configuration so that tunnel will be recreated. - Check on remote peer. SAs is not deleted immediately.

bugs.title: Instrumentation for ID 1156149 can cause TMM to crash
bugs.symptoms: A fix for ID 1156149 causes tmm to crash due to excessive logging.
bugs.conditions: Any EHF that has CL3665282 (a fix for ID 1156149) integrated.
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.

bugs.title: When the ADMD process becomes unresponsive during the attack, TMM continues to mitigate bad traffic after the attack
bugs.symptoms: TMM continues to mitigate bad traffic after an attack.
bugs.conditions: ADMD is stuck or overloaded for a long time.
bugs.impact: Traffic mitigation continues after the attack ends.
bugs.workaround: To restart ADMD, use the following command: #bigstart restart admd
bugs.fix: Traffic mitigation stops after the attack ends.

bugs.title: Virtual address status, under certain conditions, is not changed on the Standby device
bugs.symptoms: The Standby device is not sync with the Active unit
bugs.conditions: A virtual-address has these following conditions met - 1. Route-advertisement set to 'any' 2. Has a custom name (instead of just the IP itself as a name) 3. Has at least two virtual-servers associated with it (and both virtual servers with pools) 4. All pool members are removed from both pools 5. Auto-sync is enabled (incremental)
bugs.impact: The Standby device does not mark the virtual address as RED (offline).
bugs.workaround: Workaround #1: Force full sync after an incremental sync is detected: 1. edit /config/user_alert.conf on all HA peers to add the line below: alert trigger_full_sync "Incremental sync complete" { exec command="sleep 30; tmsh run cm config-sync force-full-load-push to-group <failover-group>" } 2. restart the alert daemon using this command to activate the above change: bigstart restart alertd Workaround #2: Do not use a custom name as the virtual-address name. (will not work for AS3 as you need a custom name when using AS3).

bugs.title: Content signatures are triggered for FileUploads even though check attack signature is disabled
bugs.symptoms: Having FileUpload parameters and disabling the "Check for attack signatures" results in content and paramcontent signatures violations.
bugs.conditions: - Create parameters with a FileUpload option - Disable Check attack signature.
bugs.impact: Requests are blocked

bugs.title: The maximum value of sys db provision.extramb was reduced from 8192 to 4096 MB
bugs.symptoms: From version 16.1.0 the maximum value of sys db provision.extramb is 4096 MB, reduced from 8192 MB. It will be automatically set to 4096 during the upgrade if it has a higher setting.
bugs.conditions: Any BIG-IP device running software version 16.1.0 or higher.
bugs.impact: It is extremely rare to need values of provision.extramb above 4096 MB. If the value of sys db provision.extramb is 4096 or less prior to upgrading, then there will be no impact post-upgrade. After the upgrade, it is not possible to increase the value above 4096. If the value is greater than 4096, it will be reduced to 4096 when upgrading to version 16.1.0 or higher. This may leave devices with insufficient 4KB page memory (also known as host memory) which may lead to issues due to memory pressure, such as OOM killer killing processes, poor scheduling of processes leading to core dumps, and sluggish management access.
bugs.behavior: The maximum value of sys db provision.extramb was reduced from 8192 to 4096 MB from version 16.1.0
bugs.fix: The maximum value of sys db provision.extramb is now configurable to 8192(MB).

bugs.title: Mcpd "IP::idle_timeout 0" warning generated in /var/log/ltm
bugs.symptoms: When creating iRule with command "IP::idle_timeout 0" mcpd reports an error message similar to: May 17 07:00:53 bigip.local warning mcpd[9215]: 01071859:4: Warning generated : /Common/test.irule:13: warning: [The following errors were not caught before. Please correct the script in order to avoid future disruption. "invalid argument 0; expected syntax spec:"1077 19][IP::idle_timeout 0]

bugs.title: LTM Monitor not shown in Pool Member "Health Monitors" if Transparent attribute changes
bugs.symptoms: If an LTM monitor is created with an alias address configured and assigned to a pool or pool member(s), then the monitor's "transparent" attribute is changed (either from enabled to disabled, or from disabled to enabled), the monitor no longer appears in the Local Traffic GUI in the "Health Monitors" list for an affected pool member.
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following conditions are true: -- An LTM health monitor is configured with an Alias Address and/or Port (Destination field in TMSH) -- The monitor is assigned to an LTM pool and/or pool member(s) -- The monitor's Alias Address and/or Port are different from the address of the assigned pool member -- After the monitor is assigned to the LTM pool and/or pool member(s), its "transparent" attribute is changed (either from enabled to disabled, or from disabled to enabled) -- The list of Health Monitors assigned to a given pool member is viewed in the BIG-IP LTM GUI (Local Traffic --> Pools : Pool List --> select pool --> Members --> select member)
bugs.impact: The assignment of the monitor to the pool member is not immediately visible in the BIG-IP LTM GUI in the "Health Monitors" list for the affected pool member(s). When viewing the properties of the pool member in the Local Traffic GUI, if the "Advanced" Configuration view is selected, the Health Monitors assigned to the pool member can be viewed. If the "Inherit from Pool" option is configured, the Health Monitors assigned to the pool can be viewed under the Properties tab for the pool.
bugs.workaround: When viewing the properties of the pool member in the BIG-IP LTM GUI, if the "Advanced" Configuration view is selected, the Health Monitors assigned to the pool member can be viewed. If the "Inherit from Pool" option is configured, the Health Monitors assigned to the pool can be viewed under the Properties tab for the pool.

bugs.title: In IDP-initiated flow, Relay state sent in SAML response is not considered by the SP and SP rather uses Relay state configured in its config

bugs.title: An ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation sent to the last address on an IPv6 subnet uses the wrong Destination MAC address
bugs.symptoms: The destination MAC address of the ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation message is incorrect.
bugs.conditions: An IPv6 SelfIP address is used, and tmm attempts to resolve the address of (for example) an IPv6 pool memeber which is using the last IPv6 address in the available subnet range.
bugs.impact: Nodes on the network do not respond to ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation messages. In large environments with many affected addresses, this could potentially contribute to a broadcast storm or degrade overall network performance.
bugs.workaround: None (other than avoiding the use of the last address in the IPv6 subnet range)

bugs.title: [BGP] IPv6 routes not installed/pushed after graceful restart when IPv6 peer-groups are configured.
bugs.symptoms: Some IPv6 routes are not installed/pushed after graceful restart when IPv6 peer-groups are configured.
bugs.conditions: - BGP configured with peer-group activated under IPv6 address-family. - BGP graceful restart took place.
bugs.impact: Routes are missing on BIG-IP. Routes are not sent to IPv6 peers.
bugs.workaround: Do not use peer-groups under IPv6 address-family. Configure peers separately instead.

bugs.title: Change in behavior when setting value HTTP::payload to 0 in iRule from v16 onwards
bugs.symptoms: When HTTP_REQUEST_DATA { set empty "" HTTP::payload replace 0 $clen $empty set request_length [HTTP::header "Content-Length"] log local0. "request_length $request_length" HTTP::release } $request_lenght throws non zero value since v16.0.0
bugs.conditions: V16.x/v17.x loaded version can observe $request_length throws non zero/garbage value. (but observed $request_length as zero value in eg v15.1.10.4)
bugs.impact: $request_lenght throws non zero/garbage value.

bugs.title: DoSL7D ICC errors are observed during higher throughput with DoS profile on Active-Active setup
bugs.symptoms: Occurrence of too many Intelligent Client Cache (ICC) errors during higher throughput on Active-Active setup.
bugs.conditions: - Active-Active BIG-IP setup - DoS profile should be attached - Higher throughput condition
bugs.impact: Failure of configuration sync between Active-Active BIG-IPs, due to ICC errors.

bugs.title: High CPU utilization when enabling IPS + HTTP/2 Profile
bugs.symptoms: When running HTTP/2 requests with all IPS signatures and compliance checks enabled, 100% TMM CPU utilization peaks occur.
bugs.conditions: -- Virtual server with an IPS and HTTP2 profile -- HTTP2 traffic
bugs.impact: HTTP/2 traffic slowdown occurs, which impacts performance.
bugs.workaround: To help optimize CPU utilization, enable only the necessary IPS signatures and compliance checks based on specific requirements, rather than activating all available options. While this targeted approach reduces the system’s processing load and maintains essential protections, it may not completely eliminate CPU usage spikes under high traffic or intensive processing demands.

bugs.title: Loss of kernel routes occurs on 1NIC Virtual Edition when the DHCP lease expires.
bugs.symptoms: In the single NIC, BIG-IP Virtual Edition is assigned an IP address by a DHCP server. When the DHCP lease expires and the BIG-IP is assigned a new IP address, some of the routes are removed from the kernel routing tables.
bugs.conditions: An issue occurs in the BIG-IP system with the below condition, - Single NIC BIG-IP Virtual Edition - IP address is assigned by a DHCP server - The DHCP lease expires and the Virtual Edition is assigned a new IP address
bugs.impact: Some routes are removed from the kernel routing tables thus causing a potential loss of connectivity on the management network and on the data plane.
bugs.workaround: All the kernel routes can be reinstalled when you disable and re-enable the DHCP client using the, tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp disabled tmsh modify sys global-settings mgmt-dhcp enabled

bugs.title: APM responds with RST to 'GET /my.policy' request
bugs.symptoms: When using the Edge Client, the browser request to my.policy fails with an error "This site can't be reached" If you close the pop-up window and try again, a different error occurs: "Access policy evaluation is already in progress for your current session" If you click the link to create a new session, the original error occurs "This site can't be reached". On the BIG-IP system, there is no entry for port 10001 in "netstat -nap" command output.
bugs.conditions: -- APM HA configuration -- A failover occurs
bugs.impact: Access policies are not accessible
bugs.workaround: Restart apmd process.

bugs.title: Specific JSON enforcement is not working
bugs.symptoms: An issue was detected with the JSON schema pattern attribute
bugs.conditions: When something is defined as a pattern in the JSON schema, it's enforcement can be bypassed on a specific scenario
bugs.impact: A missed JSON schema violation

bugs.title: Event log showing the request as legal
bugs.symptoms: A blocked request is shown as passed in the logs
bugs.conditions: A specific request is sent.
bugs.impact: The Event log in the GUI shows the request as legal and the remote log shows it as illegal

bugs.title: urlcat categorization improvements

bugs.conditions: The BIG-IP system has Policy Enforcement Manager (PEM) provisioned. The URL categorization feature is licensed on the system. One or more virtual servers use URL categorization through one of the following: An iRule A Centralized Policy Matching (CPM) rule. A BIG-IP PEM policy. One or more virtual servers process malformed URL categorization input.
bugs.impact: TMM restart and service disruption
bugs.fix: URL categorization behaves as expected.

bugs.title: [APM][SAML] SP automation fails with error message 'cannot update (cert_type)'
bugs.symptoms: Whenever a certificate is updated while fetching the metadata from the metadata URL in SAML automation for creating SP connector, an error occurs: err mcpd[8894]: 01070712:3: Caught configuration exception (0), file:(/Common/sp_cert.crt) cannot update (cert_type).

(https://1.1.1.1/PS0028JP) -. Update the iFiles that returns metadata and wait till the SP-automation to update its sp-connector objects PS0028JP -> ifile that returns metadata of SP with different cert ( self signed to CA and viceversa)
