bugs.title: An LTM policy configured to only disable AVR (avr disable) cannot be applied to a virtual server unless an AVR (analytics) profile is attached.
bugs.symptoms: When attaching an LTM policy containing an avr disable action to a virtual server without an AVR (analytics) profile, the configuration is rejected, and MCP logs a validation error similar to: 01071809:3: Virtual server /<partition>/<vs_name> requires a profile of type avr for ltm policy /Common/<policy_name>. The policy applies successfully only if an AVR profile is manually attached to the virtual server.
bugs.conditions: - An LTM policy contains a rule with an avr action, and that action is set to disable (no avr enable action is present in the policy). - The policy is attached (or being attached) to a virtual server that does not have an AVR (analytics) profile. - This commonly arises when an LTM policy is used to disable AVR statistics collection for specific connections on a virtual server that has a DOS (DoSL7) profile but no AVR profile. The DOS profile causes AVR to run implicitly, and avr disable is the action used to stop AVR statistics collection for those connections.
bugs.impact: The configuration is rejected and cannot be committed. Because the AVR control requirement is keyed on the action target rather than on whether the action enables or disables AVR, MCP requires an AVR profile even when the policy only disables AVR. As a result, you cannot use an avr disable action to suppress AVR statistics collection on a virtual server unless you also attach an AVR profile that you may not otherwise need. There is no configuration-only workaround other than attaching an AVR profile to the virtual server.
bugs.workaround: Attach an AVR (analytics) profile to the affected virtual server. With an AVR profile present, the avr disable action validates successfully and takes effect.
bugs.fix: AVR disable can be done within an LTM Policy. This is meant to only be used by a Virtual server that has a DOSL7 profile, and the LTM Policy is disabling DOSL7, and the admin would prefer to also have AVR statistics disabled as well for a given set of clients, for example.

bugs.title: Flood and Sweep Attack Counters Not Incremented for Certain Suspicious Packet Types
bugs.symptoms: When the Flood attack vector is configured for the "suspicious" packet type, sending packets such as "TCP Option Overruns TCP Header," "TCP Option Present with Illegal Length," or "Unknown TCP Option Type" to the BIG-IP system should result in an increase in both the Flood attack statistics and drop counters. However, this is not occurring. The same issue also applies to the Sweep attack vector
bugs.conditions: Single Endpoint Flood/Sweep vector is configured with specific detection and mitigation thresholds, and "TCP Option Overruns TCP Header" packets are sent to the system
bugs.impact: The Flood attack vector statistics are not increasing as expected
bugs.fix: For most packet types, except for "bad packets," enforcement is typically delayed until a flow is established. Once the flow is active, enforcement is applied. However, for the three specific vector types mentioned, the flow already exists when the packet is processed, so enforcement is applied immediately within this flow rate path

bugs.title: Location entries missing in ssl.conf preventing execution of <If> exception
bugs.symptoms: TMOS version v17.5.1.5 and above are missing the Location entries around SSLVerifyClient require, this prevents Apache from executing the <if> statement.
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs on BIG-IP version greater than v17.5.1.5
bugs.impact: All commands within an <if> statement are not executed
bugs.workaround: Perform the following actions as a workaround: - locate ssl.conf (usually /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf) - edit ssl.conf - add the missing location entries around SSLVerifyClient require, should look like: <LocationMatch "^[/][^/]+[/]"> SSLVerifyClient require </LocationMatch> - save the file - restart httpd **Caution every modification to httpd required the check/modification of ssl.conf

bugs.title: Creating a TMC-based IPv6 virtual server with a port list fails if other IPv6 wildcard listeners are present.
bugs.symptoms: Attempts to create an IPv6 virtual server using Traffic Matching Criteria (TMC) with a configured port list fail if one or more IPv6 wildcard (::) virtual servers already exist on the system. The operation fails with the following error: 0107176c:3: Invalid Virtual Address, the IP address :: already exists.
bugs.conditions: One or more IPv6 wildcard (::) virtual servers already exist on the system.
bugs.impact: The system is unable to create IPv6 virtual servers that use Traffic Matching Criteria (TMC) with a port list when other IPv6 wildcard (::) listeners already exist.
bugs.workaround: Step 1: Delete the existing TMC if it was already created: tmsh delete ltm traffic-matching-criteria tmc-udp-traceroute-v6 Step 2: Create the IPv6 address list for source matching: tmsh create net address-list ipv6_any { addresses add { ::/0 } } Step 3: Recreate the TMC using destination-address-inline in place of destination-address-list: tmsh create ltm traffic-matching-criteria tmc-udp-traceroute-v6 { destination-address-inline :: destination-port-list UDP-TRACEROUTE-v6 source-address-list ipv6_any protocol udp } Step 4: Create the virtual server referencing the updated TMC: tmsh create ltm virtual vwire-udp-traceroute-bypass-v6 { ip-forward ip-protocol udp profiles add { fastL4 } traffic-matching-criteria tmc-udp-traceroute-v6 vlans-enabled vlans add { VLAN452 VLAN462 vlan-4094-10 vlan-4094-9 vlan-4096-10 vlan-4096-9 } } Step 5: Save the configuration: tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: NTP authentication method upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Currently, the authentication method between the BIG-IP and the NTP server is SHA1. That needs to be upgraded to a more secure message digest algorithm
bugs.conditions: By default, NTP is enabled and follows the SHA1 algorithm for authentication
bugs.impact: By adopting SHA512 as the default authentication method, we enhance security, making customer data and NTP authentication more resilient to security issues linked to SHA-1

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE on Azure: Traffic loss with no self-recovery after Accelerated Networking VF is rescinded by the platform
bugs.symptoms: When Azure rescinds or re-presents an SR-IOV Virtual Function (VF) on a BIG-IP VE with Accelerated Networking, the data interface associated with that VF will stop forwarding traffic and will not recover automatically without manual intervention. Other interfaces remain unaffected. The Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) does not crash, but you may see the following messages in the kernel logs: - pci_hyperv: PCI dom# 0x<N> has collision, using 0x<M> - mlx5_core <addr>: no netdev found for vf serial <N>
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP VE is deployed on Microsoft Azure - Accelerated Networking is enabled on the VM - The Azure platform may rescind and re-present the SR-IOV VF during host maintenance, platform servicing, or other internal Azure events that might not be visible to the tenant or reflected in scheduled event notifications - VF re-presentation results in a PCI domain collision in the guest kernel
bugs.impact: Traffic on the affected interface stops. Associated pool members and virtual servers become unavailable. Recovery requires restarting TMM or rebooting
bugs.workaround: Reboot the unit
bugs.fix: When an interface is affected, the BIG-IP system automatically switches to the synthetic network path, allowing traffic to continue forwarding without disruption. Accelerated Networking will not be restored on that interface until the TMM is restarted

bugs.title: After upgrading to version 17.5.1.6, APM rejects HTTP requests containing unencoded double quotes in the URI.
bugs.symptoms: - After upgrading to BIG-IP 17.5.1.6, HTTP requests containing unencoded double quotes (") in the URI query string are rejected by APM (access.c framework) - This behavior results from stricter RFC 3986 enforcement - Applications that previously functioned now fail if requests include URIs that are non-compliant with RFC 3986
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP version: 17.5.1.6 - APM enabled: Access Policy Manager is active - Request characteristics: Contains unencoded special characters (e.g., " in query strings) - Traffic flow: Processed through the APM access policy (access.c) Example Trigger: /test?option2="method"&option3="POST"
bugs.impact: - Existing applications (e.g., Oracle WebLogic) fail to function after the upgrade - Requests are rejected before reaching backend servers - This issue prevents upgrading to version 17.5.1.6 - Results in production outages or degraded functionality - Workarounds lead to performance degradation
bugs.workaround: Apply an iRule to encode unsupported characters (e.g., double quotes) before APM processing: when HTTP_REQUEST priority 100 { set my_uri [HTTP::uri] if { $my_uri contains "＼"" } { HTTP::uri [string map { "＼"" "%22" } $my_uri] } }

bugs.title: Large JWTs causes tmm core while encoding
bugs.symptoms: When JWTs with an encoded length greater than 2MB are processed by TMM for OAuth, it causes TMM to crash
bugs.conditions: JWT configured with large claims or scope - increasing the overall payload size
bugs.impact: The TMM crashes, causing the BIG-IP to become unavailable
bugs.workaround: Reduce JWT payload length by modifying the claims or scopes

bugs.title: Portal access fails with the error 'ERROR: Fetching cookie failed' when large cookies are present.
bugs.symptoms: Portal access intermittently fails when the HTTP Analytics profile is enabled. Access logs display cookie fetch errors in RewritePlugin, such as: error rewrite - RewritePlugin.cpp:3290 (0x2005bd0): ERROR: Fetching cookie failed.
bugs.conditions: Observed when large cookies are send by backends.
bugs.impact: Connections face interruptions in service availability due to the inability to fetch backend cookies.

bugs.title: IP Intelligence feedlist config with address 0.0.0.0 & no specific netmask
bugs.symptoms: IP Intelligence feedlist config with 0.0.0.0 as IP address & no netmask wrongly blocks all addresses
bugs.conditions: Configuration with 0.0.0.0 as IP address entry without netmask
bugs.impact: A wrong configuration with 0.0.0.0 as an IP address entry without a netmask can unexpectedly drop all traffic, even if such an entry was unintended. The consequences of dropping all traffic are not expected
bugs.workaround: Ensure no invalid 0.0.0.0 IP address entry. If the intention is to block a single IP, explicitly specify the netmask <ip>,32,bl, or <ip>/32,,bl, or <valid ip(non 0.0.0.0)>,,bl

bugs.title: Snat-translation object may get orphaned after running "tmsh delete ltm snat all" command.
bugs.symptoms: After running the "tmsh delete ltm snat all" command, the snat-translation object, which was automatically created while creating the snat object, may not be removed and becomes orphaned. With the orphaned snat-translation object, a couple of problems can occur - Orphaned snat-translation object cannot be deleted. An error message "01070321:3: Snat translation address /Common/x.x.x.x is still referenced by a snat pool." is returned. # tmsh delete ltm snat-translation 10.1.1.1 01070321:3: Snat translation address /Common/10.1.1.1 is still referenced by a snat pool. # - New snat-translation object cannot be created on either CLI or GUI. An error message "01070712:3: Invalid primary key on trans_addr object - path is empty." is returned. # tmsh create ltm snat-translation 10.2.2.1 { address 10.2.2.1 traffic-group traffic-group-1 } 01070712:3: Invalid primary key on trans_addr object - path is empty. # - New snat object cannot be created on either CLI or GUI. An error message "01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid primary key on trans_addr object () - not a full path 2." is returned. # tmsh create ltm snat my_snat2 origins add { 10.4.4.1 } translation 10.5.5.1 01070734:3: Configuration error: Invalid primary key on trans_addr object () - not a full path 2. #
bugs.conditions: - Executed "tmsh delete ltm snat all" command
bugs.impact: - Cannot delete orphaned snat-translation object. - Cannot create new snat object or snat-translation object
bugs.workaround: Avoid running "delete ltm snat all" TMSH command. Instead, delete snat object on GUI. Or alternatively, avoid using "all" keyword when you delete snat object on CLI (i.e., delete each snat object by "delete ltm snat [snat-object-name]" command) If you have already had orphaned snat-translation object and have difficulty in creating new snat/snat-translation object, follow K13030 and refresh mcpdb. After reboot, you can manually delete the orphaned snat-translation object without using "all" TMSH command option # touch /service/mcpd/forceload # reboot # tmsh delete ltm snat-translation 10.1.1.1 ; tmsh save sys config

bugs.title: Mdmsyncmgr truncates SAS signature when following Intune redirect to Azure Blob Storage, leading to NonCompliantDevice retrieval failure
bugs.symptoms: - mdmsyncmgr fails to retrieve NonCompliantDevice details from Intune - APM logs show authentication errors during device detail updates: “Authentication error for get all non-compliant devices request” - Azure Blob Storage responds with HTTP 403 AuthenticationFailed and message: “Signature fields not well formed” - Packet capture shows SAS signature truncated in redirected request - Issue correlates with the presence of two newly added HTTP headers in Intune redirect response
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM configured with mdmsyncmgr and Microsoft Intune integration - Intune returns an HTTP 303 redirect to Azure Blob Storage with an SAS token - Redirect response includes additional HTTP headers (recent change on Intune side) - Resulting HTTP request size exceeds internal handling limit (~1515 bytes observed) - mdmsyncmgr follows the redirect (HTTP scheme) and truncates the request payload (~15 bytes lost).
bugs.impact: - NonCompliantDevice retrieval fails completely - Device compliance data cannot be synchronized from Intune - Affects visibility and enforcement of compliance policies
bugs.fix: Fix async HTTP response header parsing for fragmented headers Accumulate fragmented header field/value callbacks in HttpSenderAsio instead of overwriting them. This prevents truncation of long Location headers, including Intune compliance retrieval redirects with long Azure Blob SAS query strings.

bugs.title: TMM may enter a crash loop when handling large configurations
bugs.symptoms: TMM panics with 'unable to extend db' error messages
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when the fix for ID2033781 is applied and very large configurations are present. Without this fix, TMM logs 'mco_db_extend failed' messages and ignores the configuration settings It can also occur with moderately sized configurations, where TMM extends the database by the product of two configuration settings. For instance, this could happen with hundreds of bot-defence profiles and thousands of bot-defence signatures
bugs.impact: TMM cannot start up

bugs.title: DNS RPZ policies are not applied when upstream server returns error responses
bugs.symptoms: DNS Response Policy Zone (RPZ) policies are not evaluated when the upstream DNS server returns error response codes such as SERVFAIL, NOTAUTH, REFUSED, NOTIMPL, or FORMERR. The error response is passed through to the client without RPZ policy enforcement.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP DNS configured with a validating cache resolver and RPZ enabled - RPZ action set to "given" or any other configured action - Upstream DNS server returns an error response code (SERVFAIL, NOTAUTH, REFUSED, NOTIMPL, or FORMERR) for a domain that has an RPZ policy record
bugs.impact: RPZ policy actions (such as NXDOMAIN, NODATA, walled garden, or local data) are not enforced for queries where the upstream server returns an error response. This creates a gap in DNS firewall coverage, allowing blocked domains to bypass RPZ when the upstream server is returning errors

bugs.title: BGP process may restart/crash due to insufficient buffer space validation when encoding MP-BGP NLRI attributes
bugs.symptoms: The BGPd process may unexpectedly terminate (either by core dump or restart) when creating UPDATE messages that include MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attributes. This issue arises because the code accesses or writes to the message buffer without first ensuring that there is enough space available. As a result, this can lead to BGP session flaps and the potential loss of routing information during the restart
bugs.conditions: This situation arises when BGP is either advertising or withdrawing routes for a multiprotocol address family, such as IPv6 or VPNv4/VPNv6. It occurs when the available space left in the outgoing UPDATE message buffer is less than what is required to encode the MP_REACH/MP_UNREACH attribute. This typically happens when the message is almost full, yet there is still additional NLRI that needs to be included
bugs.impact: Without this fix, bgpd may access buffer memory without validating available space when encoding MP_REACH_NLRI/MP_UNREACH_NLRI attributes into an outgoing UPDATE message. This can lead to memory corruption or an out-of-bounds access, causing the bgpd process to crash and restart
bugs.workaround: No direct workaround to prevent the condition; reducing the number of prefixes/attributes advertised per update cycle (e.g., lowering max prefixes per batch) may reduce the likelihood of hitting the boundary condition. If bgpd crashes, it will restart automatically and BGP sessions will re-establish, but reduce concurrent MP-BGP churn where possible until upgraded

bugs.title: Tmm core involving timing issues with TrafficShield bd
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes with a core dump (SIGSEGV) when Advanced WAF / ASM is active on a virtual server that also has iRules referencing HTTP response headers (e.g., X-Blocking-Template)
bugs.conditions: All of the following must align: - BIG-IP with Advanced WAF / ASM enabled (TrafficShield BD enforcer active) - An iRule inspects HTTP response header(s) on the server-side connection - The server returns a response (e.g., 403 Forbidden) that triggers an ASM response violation - A specific timing window occurs: BD releases the response hold before raising the ASM_RESPONSE_VIOLATION event, allowing the client-side connection to close while the server-side iRule still attempts to access the now-cleared HTTP data This is a race condition — reproducibility is extremely timing-sensitive and not consistently repeatable
bugs.impact: TMM process crashes and restarts. Active connections are dropped during restart. In standalone deployments, this causes a brief traffic outage; in HA pairs, a failover may occur
bugs.workaround: No reliable workaround due to the timing-sensitive nature of the race. Disabling ASM response violation inspection or removing iRules that read HTTP response headers on affected virtual servers may reduce exposure, but is not guaranteed to prevent the crash. A permanent fix requires a BD code change to prevent iRule event dispatch when the response hold has already been released

bugs.title: 'answer-default-zones' set to 'no' makes DNS transparent cache respond locally to _dns.resolver.arpa instead of forwarding to the pool
bugs.symptoms: Because Unbound includes new default zones, it returns default answers for resolver.arpa and service.arpa instead of forwarding to upstream servers, even when answer-default-zones is disabled.
bugs.conditions: Configure the resolver or a transparent cache in the DNS profile.
bugs.impact: The resolver returns default answers to client queries for names in the resolver.arpa and service.arpa zones instead of authoritative answers. This behavior may prevent clients from using RFC9462 mechanisms to discover higher-security DNS transports.
bugs.workaround: Setting local data with type transparent for names that receive default answers overrides the default zone and lets configured authoritative servers answer client queries. For example, add a type transparent local-data record '_dns.resolver.arpa 3600 IN TXT "workaround"'; clients can then query the same name for type SVCB, and the resolver forwards those queries to the configured pool (transparent cache).

bugs.title: TMM may ignore certain DOS L7 config objects
bugs.symptoms: This issue has been observed with bot-defense signatures, resulting in log lines that appear as follows: Notice MCP message handling failed in 0xacdf00 (16973843): Jun 24 19:34:45 on 1 - MCP Message: notice create { notice bot_defense_compiled_signatures { notice bot_defense_compiled_signatures_parent_profile "/Common/a_profile_name" notice bot_defense_compiled_signatures_name "/Common/a_signature_name" ... The 16973843 error number is a fingerprint for this.＼
bugs.conditions: This typically requires thousands of the same config objects (e.g., bot-defense signatures), but it can rarely happen with many fewer
bugs.impact: Config settings aren't honored by tmm. In the case of signatures, this can result in traffic that should be blocked but is not
bugs.workaround: The root cause is that DOS L7 config object names are hashed into a 32-bit number. This can cause collisions, which lead to the bug. So changing names can prevent the collisions, e.g., by appending a random number to the name But note that this is a probabilistic fix and is not guaranteed to work with the first random number

bugs.title: APM policy sync silently drops portal access resource items that contain HTTP headers
bugs.symptoms: When synchronizing an APM access policy between BIG-IP devices, portal access (web application) resource items that include a headers sub-block may not be transferred to the target device. Although the synchronization operation reports success and logs no errors, administrators may remain unaware that configurations have been omitted. Resource items with duplicate header names are particularly affected, but even those with unique header names can still be missing if they contain a headers block. As a result, the target device may end up with an incomplete policy
bugs.conditions: - An APM access policy that includes a portal access (web application) resource item - The resource item contains a headers sub-block (one or more header entries with duplicate header names)
bugs.impact: Portal access resource items with headers are silently missing on the target device after policy sync. The synced policy will be incomplete, which can cause portal access resources to malfunction or be unavailable on the target, with no error reported to the administrator
bugs.workaround: No configuration workaround. After a sync, manually verify on the target that portal access resource items and their header entries are present, and re-create any missing items by hand

bugs.title: GPA panics when an IM package with new category is installed on TMOS
bugs.symptoms: The GPA encounters a panic when a new IM package with a new category is installed on TMOS. During the installation of a new IM package, the URLCAT library attempts to load all the applications and categories that come with it. If any category included in the new IM package is not present in the URL database configuration, it can cause the GPA to crash due to a PANIC statement
bugs.conditions: A new category that is present in the IM Package but not present in the urldb configuration
bugs.impact: Core
bugs.workaround: Before installing the IM package that introduces a new category, please create the corresponding new category using the TMSH command. Use the following command format: ``` tmsh create sys url-db url-category <new_category_from_IM_package> description <description> ``` After executing this command, save the configuration and then proceed to install the IM package.＼

bugs.title: FIPS Key Deletion via tmsh/GUI/iControl Fails When /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d Path is Missing.
bugs.symptoms: FIPS key deletion initiated through tmsh, GUI, or iControl fails. The operation attempts to access /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d for file content manipulation during the deletion workflow, but the process errors out if the path does not exist
bugs.conditions: FIPS key deletion is performed via tmsh, GUI, or iControl /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d directory is missing or not created on the system
bugs.impact: - FIPS key deletion operation fails. - Users are unable to remove keys, potentially blocking key lifecycle management and related administrative operations.
bugs.workaround: Manually create the /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d directory prior to performing the key deletion operation
bugs.fix: With the fix applied, the /config/filestore/.trash_bin_d path is created before being accessed, ensuring the key deletion operation completes successfully

bugs.title: False-positive Illegal static parameter value violations in case-insensitive policies
bugs.symptoms: Legitimate client requests are unexpectedly blocked, triggering an Illegal static parameter value violation
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when using a case-insensitive security policy where defined static parameters contain uppercase characters
bugs.impact: Legitimate traffic is blocked (false positive), disrupting valid client requests that should otherwise be allowed by the policy

bugs.title: TLS handshake failure when intermediate CA certificates are used as Trusted CA in SSL profile
bugs.symptoms: * SSL/TLS handshake failures with "certificate unknown" alert * Certificate validation fails when an intermediate CA is used as a trusted CA * OCSP response control set to "Ignore" is not honored in server-ssl profiles * Connections fail in both forward and reverse proxy scenarios
bugs.conditions: Server-SSL Profile (Reverse Proxy): * When an intermediate CA certificate is configured as a trusted CA (ca-file) -> FAILS * When root CA is configured as trusted CA -> PASSES OCSP "Ignore" setting is not respected Client-SSL Profile (Forward Proxy): * When bundle containing root + intermediate CAs is used -> PASSES * When intermediate CA alone is configured as a trusted CA -> FAILS
bugs.impact: * SSL/TLS connections fail when intermediate CA certificates are used as trusted CAs in SSL profiles * Affects both client-ssl and server-ssl profile configurations * Prevents proper certificate validation in proxy scenarios * Admin users cannot configure intermediate CAs as trusted CAs without workarounds.
bugs.workaround: Use a certificate bundle containing both root CA and intermediate CA certificates instead of using the intermediate CA alone as the trusted CA.

bugs.title: RRSIG Records Incorrectly Added to MX and TXT Records in Delegated Zones
bugs.symptoms: RRSIG records arebeing incorrectly added to MX and TXT records in delegated zones during DNSSEC-enabled AXFR
bugs.conditions: - Configure DNS Express with DNSSEC enabled - Create a delegated zone with MX and TXT records. - Initiate a zone transfer (AXFR) for the parent zone
bugs.impact: DNSSEC validation failures

bugs.title: False positive with BruteForce in certain configuration
bugs.symptoms: False positive with BruteForce in a certain configuration
bugs.conditions: Blocking is enabled for the "Brute Force: Maximum login attempts are exceeded" policy level, but only an alarm is set at the detection object level, such as "username". For the detection object, the request should not be blocked and should alarm only; however, it is blocked
bugs.impact: - This can only happen with a release that has the fix for ID2296473 - Blocking is enabled with "Brute Force: Maximum login attempts are exceeded" - Mitigation Action" is set to "Alarm" for the detection object, such as "username - Detect Credential Stuffing" is enabled

bugs.title: TMM fails to load large number of bot defense signatures
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes during config load attempt
bugs.conditions: - 163 security bot-defense profiles - 2670 security bot-defense signatures
bugs.impact: TMM cannot load config
bugs.workaround: Remove unnecessary bot-defense profiles

bugs.title: Remote SNMPv3 fails to connect
bugs.symptoms: Trying to use SNMPv3 remotely just results in timeouts. In /var/log/snmpd, the following log message shows that v1-traps or v2-traps are configured. "The separate port argument for sinks is deprecated"
bugs.conditions: v1-traps or v2-traps have been configured.
bugs.impact: Unable to use SNMPv3 remotely when v1-traps or v2-traps are configured.
bugs.workaround: Make note of the v1-traps and v2-traps configuration, and set them to none by using tmsh: `tmsh modify sys snmp v2-traps none` Use either tmsh or the GUI to recreate the v1-traps and v2-traps, but use the generic traps with the correct version `tmsh modify sys snmp traps add`

bugs.title: Traffic-matching-criteria with no route-domain specified fails to match traffic in non-default route-domain partition
bugs.symptoms: In a partition that uses a non-default route domain, a traffic-matching criteria object created without specifying an explicit route domain (for example, through the GUI or by using the 'load sys config' command) builds its virtual address and listener in route domain 0. As a result, traffic within the partition's route domain will not match the listener. Please note that the TMSH workaround needs to be reapplied on each device after every configuration synchronization or reload
bugs.conditions: - A partition with a non-default route domain is configured - A traffic-matching-criteria object is created without an explicit route-domain (including via the GUI or config load)
bugs.impact: Traffic fails to match the virtual server. The TMSH workaround does not survive config-sync or config reload
bugs.workaround: When creating the traffic-matching-criteria object via TMSH, specify the route-domain explicitly. See K94024302 for steps
bugs.fix: The system now correctly builds the virtual address and listener in the partition's route domain when no explicit route domain is set on the traffic-matching-criteria object

bugs.title: Provisioning target build is failing intermittently due to unit test failure
bugs.symptoms: While making provisioning changes, the system relied on a database index shortcut to determine which modules were allowed on a specific platform. However, this shortcut could occasionally yield an incomplete list of results, leading to some modules being mistakenly classified as either provisionable or non-provisionable
bugs.conditions: If the platform has more than one module combo assigned to it (e.g., platform C106 has combos for asm, tam, gtm) At least one of those combos uses inverted logic It does not happen every time — only when the database engine's internal cursor happens to skip a row during lookup. The unit tests catch it because they run the same code path hundreds of times across CI builds
bugs.impact: Build creation fails; retry will work
bugs.workaround: Rebuild/retry the image build

bugs.title: Error (TypeError: "x" is not a function) in jquery-ui-1.8.17.min.js:49:4075
bugs.symptoms: Custom search not working for Security ›› Event Logs : Network : Firewall
bugs.conditions: AFM Provision - Security ›› Event Logs: Network: Firewall - Custom search = Drag and drop the required field
bugs.impact: Custom search not working for Security ›› Event Logs : Network : Firewall

bugs.title: BIG-IP terminates HTTP/2 with GOAWAY/PROTOCOL_ERROR when client sends empty initial SETTINGS frame
bugs.symptoms: The HTTP/2 protocol requires that an empty SETTINGS frame be sent as the first frame. When BIG-IP receives this empty initial SETTINGS frame, it incorrectly terminates the connection with a PROTOCOL_ERROR
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP has a virtual server with an HTTP/2 profile - Client initiates an HTTP/2 connection and sends its initial SETTINGS frame with no settings
bugs.impact: Connection is immediately terminated, preventing the client from serving any requests

bugs.title: APM Portal Access Fails to Parse "from" and "as" outside of import export cases
bugs.symptoms: Apps hosted through portal access fail if they contain "from" and "as" outside of import export cases
bugs.conditions: Have an App hosted in Portal Access that uses "from" and "as" outside of import export cases
bugs.impact: Apps hosted through Portal Access will not work as intended
bugs.fix: Applications that use "from" and "as" outside of import/export cases now work as intended in Portal Access

bugs.title: APM Portal Access Modern JavaScript rewrite engine corrupts Array.prototype prototype chain when processing document.writeln content
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP APM Portal Access proxies a web application using the Modern JavaScript rewrite engine (cache-fm-Modern.js), applications that use `document.writeln` may malfunction. The prototype chain of `Array.prototype` is set to a Proxy-wrapped `Object.prototype` instead of the actual `Object.prototype`, causing inherited properties like `hasOwnProperty` to return `undefined` and resulting in JavaScript execution failures in the proxied application
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM is configured with a Portal Access resource - The proxied application dynamically injects JavaScript using document. writeln - The Modern JavaScript rewrite engine (cache-fm-Modern.js) is active (default for modern browsers) - Affects BIG-IP APM version 21.1.0
bugs.impact: Applications proxied through APM Portal Access that rely on inherited Array.prototype properties fail to execute JavaScript correctly. The failure cascades across the application, causing it to malfunction or become completely unusable through the Portal Access proxy. Accessing the application directly without APM Portal Access is not affected

bugs.title: /etc/ntp/keys are not forwarded during software upgrade
bugs.symptoms: Device with NTP servers configured, are not forwarded during software upgrade.
bugs.conditions: - Have NTP servers configured - Upgrade to a new version
bugs.impact: Manually need to update /etc/ntp/keys file
bugs.workaround: Steps from the below articles can be followed to ensure the keys are forwarded during the upgrade: K30653031: How to set NTP Authentication and Passphrase Criteria K000139030: Changes made to the /etc/ntp/keys file are lost after an upgrade

bugs.title: Incorrect GUI HTTP Protocol Sub-Violation counts under Learning and Blocking Settings
bugs.symptoms: Under Security -> Application Security -> Policy Building -> Learning and Blocking Settings, the Enabled and Total counts for the HTTP Protocol Compliance section are each 1 higher than they should be
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP with ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: This is cosmetic only. There is no functional impact

bugs.title: ASM GUI Learning and Blocking page search result returning extra unnecessary items
bugs.symptoms: Under Security -> Application Security -> Policy Building -> Learning and Blocking Settings, if searching for "Unescaped", the HTTP Protocol Compliance section will appear despite having no matching entries
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP with ASM provisioned
bugs.impact: This is cosmetic only. There is no functional impact

bugs.title: UCS save fails for large iAppsLX packages due to rpmbuild timeout causing persistent IllegalStateException
bugs.symptoms: tmsh save sys UCS completes, but one or more iAppsLX packages are missing from RPMS.save/ inside the UCS archive The following errors appear in /var/log/ltm during UCS save: err iAppsLX_save_pre[19798]: Failed task: /shared/iapp/build-package/f9405734-9ca2-45f7-ad4c-9164c277bddb: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Invalid state in the chain of requests - RPM_BUILD_FAILED. err iAppsLX_save_pre: Failed to get getRPM build response within timeout for <package-name> err iAppsLX_save_pre[19798]: Failed to get getRPM build response within timeout for f5-service-discovery
bugs.conditions: One or more large iAppsLX packages are installed (e.g., f5-service-discovery, f5-telemetry — 100MB+) The rpmbuild for those packages exceeds the configured iapplxrpm.timeout (default: 60 seconds), and the build fails and hits an IllegalStateException immediately
bugs.impact: Large iAppsLX packages are not included in the UCS archive. The failure is silent from a UCS perspective, as the UCS is created successfully but is incomplete
bugs.workaround: Increasing the iapplxrpm timeout value allows saving the file without getting a timeout failure tmsh modify sys db iapplxrpm.timeout value 600 bigstart restart restjavad
bugs.fix: - Hard timeout set to IAPPLXRPM_TIMEOUT_SEC_MAXIMUM (600s) so large packages have sufficient time to build, and exits after build succeeds. - Stall detector added — cancels rpmbuild only if filesystem activity stops growing for 90s (distinguishes a genuinely hung build from a slow but progressing one) RPM_BUILD_FAILED case added to processStep() — calls failTask() cleanly instead of throwing IllegalStateException FAILED tasks skipped in duplicate check — next save triggers a fresh build instead of returning the stale failure

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS Wide IP status icon does not update immediately after enable or disable
bugs.symptoms: - Wide IP is disabled or enabled from the GUI - The GUI status icon continues to show the previous state - System logs show the correct enable/disable event at the time of the administrative action SNMP_TRAP: Wide IP (/Common/bac.men.gov.ma) enabled SNMP_TRAP: Wide IP (/Common/bac.men.gov.ma) disabled
bugs.conditions: - A Wide IP is enabled or disabled through the BIG-IP DNS TMUI - The admin user views the Wide IP List page
bugs.impact: - The GUI provides misleading or stale operational status - Monitoring based on the GUI icon may report an incorrect state

bugs.title: ICMP with ID 0 flows with ipother profile does not work

bugs.symptoms: Connection RST immediately after the client connects to the FTP virtual server where FTP protocol security is enabled. In pcap or rstcause, plugin abort initiated by PSM. "Internal error (PSM::FTP requested abort (plugin abort error))." In bd.log, an error below is emitted. event_open: ***ERROR: Cannot get data profile info from DB
bugs.conditions: - Protocol security - Enable/disable protocol security via GUI screen below Local Traffic ›› Profiles : Services : FTP ›› FTP_PROFILE_NAME
bugs.impact: Connection reset
bugs.workaround: Disable and reenable protocol security via GUI screen below Local Traffic ›› Virtual Servers : Virtual Server List ›› VIRTUAL_NAME ›› Security

bugs.title: BIG-IP configuration cannot be validated after f5hubblelcdadmin is synchronized to a 17.5.1.6-or-later system
bugs.symptoms: After an HA cluster upgrade, a configuration sync from a member running an earlier BIG-IP version can copy the legacy f5hubblelcdadmin user entry to the upgraded member’s /config/bigip_user.conf. Configuration validation or save then fails with: The requested user (f5hubblelcdadmin) was not found.
bugs.conditions: - An HA cluster is being upgraded - One member is upgraded to BIG-IP 17.5.1.6 or later while another member remains on an earlier version - A configuration sync is initiated from the older-version member to the upgraded member - The sync transfers the f5hubblelcdadmin entry into /config/bigip_user.conf - The upgraded member subsequently validates, saves, reloads, or reboots using the affected configuration
bugs.impact: Configuration validation and save operations fail on the upgraded member. If the invalid entry remains in the configuration, an MCPD reload or reboot may fail to load the configuration from text files, potentially leaving the BIG-IP tenant in a configuration error state. This can also affect device trust and configuration synchronization health
bugs.workaround: Do not synchronize configurations between HA members running different BIG-IP versions during an upgrade. Complete the upgrade on all cluster members according to K80173021, and verify that all members are running the same version before performing configuration synchronization If the invalid f5hubblelcdadmin entry is already present, remove the stale entry from /config/bigip_user.conf using the applicable F5 Support procedure, then revalidate the configuration

bugs.title: Intermittent traffic failures when tenant is running BIG-IP v17.5.1.6 or above and host is on version prior to F5OS-A 1.8.0 or F5OS-C 1.8.0
bugs.symptoms: Intermittent traffic failures for a tenant running BIG-IP v17.5.1.6 or above This often manifests as ICMP monitors failing
bugs.conditions: - Tenant running BIG-IP v17.5.1.6 or above - Host is one of the following platforms: - r5000, r10000, or r12000-series appliance - VELOS - Host is running a version prior to F5OS-A 1.8.0 (rSeries appliance) or F5OS-C 1.8.0 (VELOS chassis)
bugs.impact: Intermittent traffic disruption. This often manifests as ICMP monitors intermittently failing, but it will also impact virtual server traffic and other protocols (e.g., UDP and TCP)
bugs.workaround: Upgrade F5OS to version 1.8.0 or higher

bugs.title: Bigd: Failed to find EAV pinger script file for imported external monitor
bugs.symptoms: When monitoring an LTM pool using an imported external monitor, the pool members may remain in a "checking" state and never get marked UP or DOWN by the external monitor When this occurs, a message similar to the following is logged in the LTM log file (/var/log/ltm): alert bigd.#[#####]: Failed to find EAV pinger script file, /config/filestore/files_d/Common_d/external_monitor_d/:<partition_name>:<external_monitor_name>_#####_##
bugs.conditions: This may occur on affected versions of BIG-IP if: - You either upgrade to an affected version, with one or more external monitors configured, or you add an external monitor to the BIG-IP configuration while running an affected version - The external monitor was created from a script imported into the BIG-IP system as a new external monitor file, not from an external monitor included in the BIG-IP system
bugs.impact: The imported external monitor does not function. Pool members are not marked UP or DOWN by the action of the external monitor

bugs.title: Radius monitor password encryption is incorrect
bugs.symptoms: Radius monitors will send an Access-Request with a password that has been incorrectly encrypted. This will cause the pool member to return an Access-Reject packet, resulting in a monitor failure
bugs.conditions: Radius monitor configured with a password
bugs.impact: Radius monitors configured with a password will always fail and mark the pool member down

bugs.title: SOD request is updated to all BigD instances
bugs.symptoms: The heartbeat-action and heartbeat settings are not reflected in all BigD instances tmsh modify sys daemon-ha bigd { heartbeat-action restart } tmsh modify sys daemon-ha bigd { heartbeat enabled }
bugs.conditions: Configuration of daemon-ha for BigD
bugs.impact: Settings are not applied, and respective action/settings are not triggered based on SOD
bugs.workaround: Restart of BigD process "bigstart restart bigd"
bugs.fix: The BigD process are listed as bigd.0, bigd.1 etc. All process are listed to reflect the settings

bugs.title: TCL error "Invalid index 0 in class" thrown in ltm log for external data group
bugs.symptoms: TCL error "Invalid index 0 in class" thrown in /var/log/ltm for external data group
bugs.conditions: - virtual server with iRule - iRule using the class command with the element option class element -value 0 <external_dg>
bugs.impact: iRule execution will fail
bugs.fix: Added code for proper boundary check for class item

bugs.title: IPSec ESP Traffic Processing Behavior
bugs.symptoms: certain traffic conditions may cause a service interruption on the affected blade.
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts.
bugs.workaround: There is no workaround at this time.

bugs.title: Fix for external/database monitor status issue
bugs.symptoms: External monitors, and also some built-in database (MS SQL, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL) monitors may fail to correctly track pool member status (e.g., a member not returning to up after a backend outage).
bugs.conditions: When a pool uses an external or built-in 'database' type monitor
bugs.impact: Pool members monitored by external monitors or built-in database monitors may show incorrect status, potentially routing traffic to unavailable members or marking available members as down.
bugs.workaround: No workaround

bugs.title: BD may crash while handling certain JSON body
bugs.symptoms: BD might crash while processing a certain JSON body
bugs.conditions: - ASM is provisioned - JSON profile has a schema attached - Traffic includes a very large JSON body
bugs.impact: BD might crash

bugs.title: BD crashes
bugs.symptoms: bd not working as expected
bugs.conditions: ASM is provisioned
bugs.impact: bd might crash
