bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS DNSSEC AXFR response incorrectly emits OPT pseudo-record in the Answer section, causing malformed zone-transfer data
bugs.symptoms: DNS clients or packet analysers misinterpret the DNS responses
bugs.conditions: - BIGIP DNS configured with DNSX as a secondary - BIND or upstream DNS acts as a primary - DNSSEC zone configuration is active for the zone in question - AXFR request received from client for the configured zone
bugs.impact: Malformed DNS responses from the DNS server
bugs.fix: After the fix, the DNS server no longer sends malformed responses

bugs.title: False "Unable to contact BIG-IP device" message when switching partitions
bugs.symptoms: The BIG-IP Configuration utility occasionally displays "Unable to contact BIG-IP device" when switching between partitions, despite the device being reachable. The pop-up quickly indicates "Device connection has been restored" with an elapsed time of 0 seconds
bugs.conditions: - Switching between partitions in the BIG-IP Configuration utility - More likely to occur on systems with multiple partitions and provisioned modules that increase page load time
bugs.impact: No impact to traffic processing. The Configuration utility briefly shows a connectivity warning and automatically recovers; no re-authentication is required
bugs.workaround: - The message clears automatically after a few seconds - The user will need to click "Continue" to dismiss the popup

bugs.title: iControlREST API performance degradation when querying BIG-IP objects associated with iApp AppServices
bugs.symptoms: When querying BIG-IP objects (such as LTM Pools) through the iControlREST API, performance is severely degraded when those objects were created via an iApp. The issue is particularly pronounced when expanding subcollections using '?expandSubcollections=true'. In cases with many BIG-IP objects, the performance degradation can cause iControlREST to crash
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - The BIG-IP objects are associated with an AppService (e.g. when created via an iApp) - The objects are queried through iControlREST APIs - Expanding subcollections with '?expandSubcollections=true' exacerbates the issue
bugs.impact: iControlREST API performance is severely degraded when querying iApp-created BIG-IP objects. With a large number of BIG-IP objects, this can cause iControlREST to crash

bugs.title: icontrol/rest failure with response status 404
bugs.symptoms: icontrol/rest get|post fails with a 404 response ForwarderPassThroughWorker logs a 404 status for requests in the restjavad-audit log file
bugs.conditions: On a vCMP guest, requests to the /mgmt/tm/sys/service/httpd/stats endpoint may consistently return a 404
bugs.impact: This could result in failures in automated workflows and impact the ability to monitor the service
bugs.workaround: Restarting restjavad works as a temporary fix, but the problem will likely return after some time

bugs.title: MQTT traffic may cause BIG-IP crash
bugs.symptoms: A virtual MQTT profile allows to handle MQTT traffic in BIG-IP. When MQTT is not licensed, it may result in a BIG-IP crash
bugs.conditions: The virtual server is configured with the MQTT profile. MQTT protocol is not licensed
bugs.impact: BIG-IP crashes, resulting in failover and possible interruption in processing client traffic
bugs.workaround: Do not configure MQTT profile when MQTT protocol is not licensed

bugs.title: Auto Last Hop updates established flow MAC on failover GARP, causing brief traffic disruption on long-lived connections
bugs.symptoms: - With a GARP reply, the lasthop address is not changed. This is consistent with https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K2211 : "If the MAC address of the device that sends inbound traffic to the BIG-IP system changes (such as when redundant firewalls or routers failover), the BIG-IP system will continue to send return traffic to the old MAC address. " - With a GARP request, the lasthop address is changed
bugs.conditions: - Auto Last Hop is enabled on the traffic path (global and/or object level) - An upstream failover device sends GARP announcing a MAC change. - Established flows remain active during the failover window - Most visible in environments with long-lived sessions and strict failover continuity requirements
bugs.impact: - Established flows can temporarily use a new return-path MAC after failover GARP, instead of staying on the original learned MAC - This can cause a short service interruption during failover for active sessions
bugs.workaround: - Configure an explicit Last Hop Pool on affected services instead of relying on Auto Last Hop learning - This avoids GARP-driven MAC reselection behavior on established flows and provides deterministic return-path selection during failover

bugs.title: [APM] SAML Assertion memory leak
bugs.symptoms: The APM SAML assertion handling leaks memory when invoking Saml artifact resolve request. The leak occurs because the CURL header list created with curl_slist_append is not freed properly and repeated invocations can cause incremental memory consumption.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM using SAML functionality that invokes the SAML Artifact Resolve request
bugs.impact: Progressive memory consumption on the BIG-IP system may lead to high memory utilization and potentially affect system stability or service availability if resources become exhausted.

bugs.title: BIG-IP GUI does not expose supported SNMPv3 SHA-2 and extended AES protocol options
bugs.symptoms: When configuring SNMPv3 users or trap destinations through the BIG-IP Configuration utility, the authentication and privacy protocol lists do not expose all supported options. The GUI provides only MD5/SHA for authentication and AES/DES for privacy The following options are unavailable for selection in the GUI: Authentication: SHA-256 and SHA-512 Privacy: AES-192, AES-192-C, AES-256, and AES-256-C
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following apply: - BIG-IP is using a Net-SNMP version that supports the extended SNMPv3 algorithms - An administrator creates or modifies an SNMPv3 user or trap destination through the Configuration utility - The administrator needs to select SHA-256, SHA-512, AES-192, AES-192-C, AES-256, or AES-256-C - BIG-IP software using Net-SNMP 5.8 supports SHA-2 and extended AES key lengths, as documented in K82498430: SNMPv3 support for SHA2 and AES256
bugs.impact: Cannot configure SNMPv3 users or trap destinations with the required SHA-2 authentication or extended AES privacy protocols through the GUI
bugs.workaround: - Use tmsh to configure. - Specify the auth-protocol and privacy-protocol values using tmsh; the following is an example: modify /sys snmp users add { <user> { access rw security-level auth-privacy auth-protocol sha256 auth-password defaultPassword privacy-protocol aes-192 privacy-password defaultPassword username <user> } }

bugs.title: BIG-IP may crash when processing HTTP/2 traffic
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP handles HTTP/2 traffic, it performs calculations that can result in a SIGFPE (floating-point exception), crashing TMM
bugs.conditions: - Virtual has http2 - DB variable Tmm.HTTP2.EnableStreamPriority is set to True - HTTP/2 traffic is being handled by the virtual
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts, causing a temporary disruption of traffic processing and failover. Connections are reset
bugs.workaround: Disable HTTP/2 Extensible Priorities by setting Tmm.HTTP2.EnableStreamPriority to False

bugs.title: Brute Force protection tracks the wrong username under specific conditions
bugs.symptoms: Brute Force protection reports and mitigates against the username taken from a different source than the configured brute force username settings
bugs.conditions: A specific brute-force configuration
bugs.impact: Username-based Brute Force counting, mitigation, and reporting are attributed to the wrong username. Login attempts against the intended account may not be mitigated as expected, and the Brute Force event logs can be misleading during investigation

bugs.title: Proxy SSL does not forward FINISHED message from client to the server
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshakes intermittently time out. Taking a packet capture on the BIG-IP shows the FINISHED message has been received, but not forwarded
bugs.conditions: Use of the proxy SSL feature
bugs.impact: SSL handshakes intermittently time out

bugs.title: Manager role cannot modify a virtual server that uses a port list or address list
bugs.symptoms: A user account assigned the Manager role cannot save changes to a virtual server that uses a port list or address list. The system rejects the change with: Access Denied: user (<username>) does not have modify access to object (traffic_matching_criteria)
bugs.conditions: - User account assigned the built-in Manager role - Virtual server configured with a port list or address list as its source or destination
bugs.impact: The Manager-role user cannot create, modify, or delete the affected virtual server configuration. Existing virtual servers continue to process traffic normally; there is no traffic disruption
bugs.workaround: Use an account assigned the Administrator role to create or modify the virtual server

bugs.title: HMAC missing from HMAC DB for few modules in FIPS enabled device
bugs.symptoms: In a FIPS-enabled device, upgrading or installing a defective ISO image causes the BIG-IP to remain in an "INOPERATIVE" state indefinitely due to image integrity failure. This failure occurs due to missing or incorrect HMACs for several modules. In /var/log/secure: crit root[3947]: BIG-IP Integrity Check: [ FAIL ] -- THE SYSTEM WILL HALT UPON REBOOT, CONTACT F5 NETWORKS FOR TECHNICAL SUPPORT
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP FIPS-enabled device -- Upgrade to an affected version
bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system remains in "INOPERATIVE" state after upgrade
bugs.workaround: Disabling FIPS is a workaround
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue causing integrity check to fail on FIPS-enabled BIG-IP systems that are upgraded.

bugs.title: MCP Fails to Validate Dos Profile while attaching to a Virtual Server
bugs.symptoms: When a DOS profile configured with both Geolocation allowed IPs and Behavioral Detection accelerated/TLS signatures is assigned to a Virtual Server, no validation error is raised. The error only appears on a subsequent configuration reload, config sync, or when modifying the DOS profile after assignment.
bugs.conditions: 1.A DOS profile has Geolocation allowed IP entries configured 2.The same DOS profile has Behavioral Detection accelerated or TLS signatures enabled 3.The DOS profile is assigned to a Virtual Server for the first time
bugs.impact: The invalid configuration is silently accepted, potentially causing config sync failures or configuration load errors during a subsequent reload or failover event.

bugs.title: TMUI displays "Instance not found" for Virtual Servers with a colon (:) in the name
bugs.symptoms: When a Virtual Server name contains a colon character (for example, /Common/1.1.1.1:124), clicking on it in the TMUI displays "Instance not found" and the properties page fails to load, even though the object exists in the configuration and the backend returns an HTTP 200 OK response
bugs.conditions: This occurs when an LTM object (such as a virtual server) is named using the <address>:<port> convention, which includes a colon character — for example, a virtual server created via tmsh create ltm virtual /Common/1.1.1.1:124 destination 1.1.1.1:124. Navigating to that object's properties page in the TMUI (e.g., Local Traffic > Virtual Servers) triggers the issue
bugs.impact: Objects whose names contain a colon can be created and configured via tmsh, but cannot be viewed or managed through the TMUI GUI. Users attempting to access the properties, resources, or statistics pages for such objects are blocked with an "Instance not found" error, preventing GUI-based administration of these objects
bugs.workaround: Manage affected objects (those with a colon in the name) via tmsh or the REST API instead of the TMUI, until the fix is applied
bugs.fix: Fixed an issue where objects with a colon in their name, such as a virtual server named after its address and port (e.g., 1.1.1.1:124), could not be viewed or managed from the browser-based Configuration utility

bugs.title: APM VPE Unable to load Access Policies containing starts_with expressions after upgrading to 17.5.1.8
bugs.symptoms: The user is unable to open or edit Access Policies in the Visual Policy Editor (VPE). When trying to open /Common/<AP>, an error occurs indicating that "starts_with" is not a valid Tcl expression operator. Additionally, there is a warning stating that this issue may lead to TMM compile failures after a restart. Furthermore, VPE rules that do not begin with "expr {" are flagged as errors
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP with APM configured
bugs.impact: You are unable to load Access Policies containing starts_with expressions after upgrading to 17.5.1.8
bugs.fix: "starts_with" is allowed inside VPE rules and the use of "expr {" is not required to wrap all rules anymore

bugs.title: Access Profile rejects HTTP requests containing ^ in the URI
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading to BIG-IP 17.5.1.8, users experience failures with certain requests when an Access Profile is applied to the virtual server. A request containing curly braces ^ triggers the error: 'Access encountered an error (Operation not supported)
bugs.conditions: - Upgrade BIG-IP to v17.5.1.8 - Send an HTTP GET request to an APM-enabled Virtual Server with an unencoded unsafe character in the query string
bugs.impact: - The HTTP connection is immediately reset (TCP RST) by the BIG-IP, and no APM session is established - The client cannot access the requested application resource, and an APM session is not established. This can cause application search or other URI-based requests to fail
bugs.workaround: iRule: when HTTP_REQUEST priority 100 { set my_query [HTTP::query] if { ($my_query contains "{") or ($my_query contains "}") or ($my_query contains "|") or ($my_query contains "＼"") } { HTTP::query [string map {"＼＼" "%5C" "^" "%5E"} $my_query] } } This iRule checks for specific characters in the query and replaces them with their encoded equivalents

bugs.title: Auth source can be switched to RADIUS/TACACS+/LDAP/Client Cert LDAP after the corresponding system-auth object was deleted
bugs.symptoms: After deleting an inactive RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, or Client Certificate LDAP system authentication configuration object, it remained possible to change the system authentication source to that type using the command `tmsh modify auth source type <type>`. This occurred even though no corresponding authentication configuration object existed anymore. As a result, authentication relied on outdated PAM or configuration files that were left behind from before the object was deleted, instead of properly failing as expected
bugs.conditions: This occurs when all of the following are true: - A RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, or Client Cert LDAP system-auth object was previously configured (create auth <type> system-auth { ... }) - auth source is switched away from that type (so the object is no longer the active auth source) - The now-inactive system-auth object of that type is deleted (delete auth <type> system-auth) - An administrator later switches the auth source type back to that type without recreating the auth object
bugs.impact: System authentication may continue to reference outdated or deleted configurations for RADIUS, TACACS+, LDAP, or Client Certificate LDAP (PAM and confpp files) without indicating an error. As a result, administrators might experience unexpected authentication behavior from configurations they believed had been removed
bugs.workaround: Delete the config/bigip/auth/pam.d/<type>/system-auth file each time the system-auth object of that type is deleted (delete auth <type> system-auth)

bugs.title: iRule ACCESS::policy evaluate requests may experience significant delays under high concurrency with LDAP authentication
bugs.symptoms: When using iRule ACCESS::policy evaluate to invoke an access policy that performs LDAP authentication, requests may experience delays of several minutes (up to 275 seconds observed) under high traffic conditions. The iRule logs show a large gap between the request start time and when APMD begins processing the request
bugs.conditions: - Access policy invoked via iRule using ACCESS::policy evaluate (not per-request policy) - Access policy includes LDAP or other slow authentication agents - High concurrent request volume (e.g., >100 requests/second)
bugs.impact: Authentication requests queue up and experience multi-minute delays, causing timeouts and authentication failures for end users. The delay grows proportionally with traffic volume

bugs.title: BIG-IP APM incorrectly logs "session evaluated in clientless mode" for F5 Edge Android VPN client sessions after upgrade to 17.5.1.6
bugs.symptoms: - After upgrading BIG-IP APM to 17.5.1.6, the following log message appears in /var/log/apm for F5 Access Android user sessions even though the VPN tunnel establishes successfully: 01490337:5: /Common/example_ap:Common:xxxxxxxx: The session was evaluated in clientless mode - The session completes normally with Access policy result Network_Access. The log is a false positive and has no functional impact on the VPN connection - The same message might be visible for other clients (e.g., Edge Client, browser-based access, etc.) as well
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM version 17.5.1.6 or later - User is establishing a VPN tunnel with a standalone client (Edge Client, F5 Access) or browser * The issue does not occur on 17.1.3 or earlier
bugs.impact: The VPN tunnel connects successfully, and users can access network resources normally. The false log entry causes confusion for administrators who may believe VPN tunnel establishment failed

bugs.title: AFM DoS Network Events incorrectly show event=Attack None with attack ID=0 during active attacks.
bugs.symptoms: Observed Attack ID=0 and event = Attack None in the Security > Event Logs > DoS > Network > Events page
bugs.conditions: - Enable the TCP SYN Flood vector with the mitigation values configured as required. (Attached screenshot) - Generate traffic from the client using the following Scapy command: Command: send(IP(src="5.5.5.5", dst=<VS-IP>)/TCP(flags="S"), inter=0.005, loop=1) - Verify the events under: Security > Event Logs > DoS > Network > Events
bugs.impact: The spurious logs are stored in the LogDB

bugs.title: TMM core after running tmsh load sys config default
bugs.symptoms: TMM getting core
bugs.conditions: When "tmsh load sys config default"
bugs.impact: tmm is restarting
bugs.workaround: NA
bugs.fix: When the command "load sys config default" is executed, the VLAN configurations are not removed; however, the underlying trunk configurations are removed and then recreated. This operation results in a stale interface pointer (ifp) within the interface structure (ifc). Since existing VLANs are not deleted during the load system configuration process, the logic has been extended to include the associated trunks as well

bugs.title: Installing a hotfix via TMUI fails with "Hotfix test failed due to version incompatibility"
bugs.symptoms: Installing a hotfix via the BIG-IP GUI (TMUI) fails with a version-incompatibility error when installing an Engineering Hotfix (EHF) to an inactive or new boot location: Hotfix test failed due to version incompatibility Running tmsh install sys software hotfix dry-run non-persist-db Hotfix-...-ENG.iso fails with a similar error: # tmsh install sys software hotfix dry-run non-persist-db Hotfix-BIGIP-21.1.0.1.0.30.26-ENG.iso progress: analyzing install info: Active volume details: Product=BIG-IP, Version=21.1.0, Build=0.0.38 error: The hotfix is intended for version 21.1.0.1, not 21.1.0 Data Input Error: get-dry-run helper exited with status 1: {"/shared/images/Hotfix-BIGIP-21.1.0.1.0.30.26-ENG.iso":{"success":false,"error":"Hotfix test failed due to version incompatibility"}}
bugs.conditions: - The active/booted BIG-IP volume runs a different version than the EHF target version. - The administrator installs the EHF to another boot location through TMUI.
bugs.impact: TMUI blocks a valid EHF installation. This prevents GUI-based version-to-version EHF installation to an alternate boot location. Traffic processing is not affected. The problem affects the software-installation workflow.
bugs.workaround: Use tmsh to install the hotfix.

bugs.title: ICMP Echo response state is not updated after virtual server or pool availability changes
bugs.symptoms: On affected versions, BIG-IP may not properly refresh the runtime ICMP Echo response state when the availability of an associated virtual server changes. When all pool members become unavailable, the virtual server transitions to an unavailable state; however, the virtual address may continue responding to ICMP Echo requests. Conversely, after the virtual server returns to an available state, the virtual address may remain unresponsive This behavior has been observed with more than one ICMP Echo mode, including Selective and All, and is not limited to Selective mode.
bugs.conditions: - A virtual address is configured with an ICMP Echo mode that permits responses, such as Selective or All - All members of the pool associated with the virtual server become unavailable, either because they are marked down by a monitor or forced offline - The virtual server subsequently transitions from available to unavailable, or later returns to an available state
bugs.impact: The virtual address may retain a stale ICMP Echo response state after the associated virtual server changes availability: - It may continue responding to ICMP Echo requests after the virtual server becomes unavailable. - It may remain unresponsive after the virtual server returns to an available state. - ICMP-based monitoring may therefore report a virtual address state that does not reflect the current status of the virtual server. - Reapplying the ICMP Echo configuration may be required to restore the expected behavior.
bugs.workaround: Toggle and reapply the virtual address’s ICMP Echo configuration with the following two-step process: - Change the ICMP Echo setting to Disabled - Change it back to its original mode, such as Selective or All This rebuilds the ICMP response state and restores behavior consistent with the current virtual server status

bugs.title: Getting "General database error." when trying to add failover network in devices section
bugs.symptoms: While configuring the failover network from the Devices section, TMUI is showing a General Database error
bugs.conditions: When a user tries to configure Devices and Failover network settings, they get a General Database error due to the name check of the unicast failover network
bugs.impact: Not able to configure failover network
bugs.fix: While configuring the failover network, we should allow unicast_address for the network. The database rejects the standalone word "CAST" but not "unicast_address

bugs.title: SSL handshake failures between high availability peers when ConfigSync uses the management IP
bugs.symptoms: SSL handshake failures are logged between the peer address and an internal TMM address, and peer certificate verification errors referring to a self-signed certificate appear in the logs. The connection to the CMI peer is subsequently removed
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP systems in a high availability configuration where ConfigSync is configured to use the management IP address on both devices (the database variable that allows ConfigSync over the management address is enabled)
bugs.impact: Configuration synchronization between high availability peers fails, causing the peer connection to drop. As a result, configuration changes are not synchronized, and device group membership may seem disconnected until the issue is resolved

bugs.title: TMM may crash when using PQC DH group
bugs.symptoms: TMM experiences crashes on certain platforms when the PQC DH group is utilized Note that FIPS-enabled licenses use PQC in their self-tests
bugs.conditions: - Enable the DH group X25519MLKEM768 on platforms that do not support the CPU feature AVX2 - This may rarely include CPUs used on hypervisor systems, but more often will be due to virtualization software not exposing the BMI2 feature set to the guest vCPUs F5 r2xx and r4xx lack BMI2
bugs.impact: TMM cores with traffic disruption With a FIPS-enabled license, there is TMM instability and a restart loop

bugs.title: IPS IM package update may fail with version down match error
bugs.symptoms: An error message might appear when attempting to update IPS IM_package: "Error during switching: TMCTL IM does not match the active IM, falling back to FactoryDefaults"
bugs.conditions: An error may occur when updating the IPS im_package
bugs.impact: The impact is that the system reverts to the default IM package
bugs.workaround: To mitigate or fix the issue, update to an IM package released on or after August 7th 2026
bugs.fix: To mitigate or fix the issue, update to an IM package released on or after August 7th 2026

bugs.title: Error icons may appear in multiple UI sections when the DoS module is provisioned
bugs.symptoms: When the DoS module is provisioned, the BIG-IP Configuration utility may show error or blocked icons for multiple menu items, such as Network > High Availability and Silverline-related views, even when those areas are otherwise accessible
bugs.conditions: This issue can occur on BIG-IP 17.5.1.8 EHF builds when the DoS module is enabled, and the user navigates through affected TMUI sections
bugs.impact: Administrators may see misleading error or blocked indicators in the UI. This can cause confusion during configuration and status verification
bugs.workaround: No direct workaround is required for traffic handling. If encountered, use tmsh or unaffected UI paths for verification
bugs.fix: Updated TMUI app launcher routing behavior to use HTML5 mode with requireBase disabled. This prevents incorrect error or blocked icon rendering in affected UI sections when the DoS module is provisioned

bugs.title: TMSH crash when writing to the command history
bugs.symptoms: In rare instances, it is possible that TMSH will try to write to the history when the command history is NULL, which results in a crash
bugs.conditions: TMSH attempts to write to the command history when it has been destroyed and is NULL
bugs.impact: This results in a TMSH crash
bugs.fix: TMSH has been updated to check that the command history is not NULL

bugs.title: [APM][Portal Access] [PA] APM session times out despite user activity in Network Access (NA)
bugs.symptoms: An APM session may unexpectedly time out and terminate both Portal Access (PA) and the associated Network Access (NA) session, even though the user remains active and there is ongoing traffic through the Network Access tunnel The session may be redirected to the APM logout page with hangup error 12289
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM WebTop with Portal Access and Network Access resources - User has an active Network Access session with ongoing traffic/activity - A Portal Access resource is also active
bugs.impact: The entire APM session may be terminated prematurely, causing both the PA resource and active Network Access connection to be disconnected despite continued Network Access activity
bugs.workaround: Please request support for a custom irule to resolve this issue

bugs.title: BIG-IP 21.1.0: Failed gtm_vs_score checkpoint query causes mcpd SIGABRT in EdbQueryEngine::get_all()
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP 21.1.0, mcpd terminated with SIGABRT while processing a remote configuration transaction for /Common/device-group-failover Before the termination, the following messages may be logged: 01070710:3: Database error (4), Can't get index cursor, class:gtm_vs_score key:xtree, status 4 - EdbQueryEngine.cpp, line 441. 01070710:3: Database error (4), Can't get index cursor, class:gtm_vs_score key:ntree, status 4 - EdbQueryEngine.cpp, line 441.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP 21.1.0 is running as a guest tenant - The system is configured for high availability with a remote device-group transaction - A transaction is processed for /Common/device-group-failover - The configuration includes objects from the gtm_vs_score class - A configuration-database checkpoint or index-access failure occurs while accessing the gtm_vs_score xtree or ntree index - MCPD attempts to enumerate or deactivate gtm_vs_score objects during transaction processing
bugs.impact: MCPD terminates and generates a core file

bugs.title: False-positive SSRF violations due to URL parameter parsing issues
bugs.symptoms: Legitimate traffic is unexpectedly blocked, triggering a Server-side access to disallowed host violation. The system displays No DNS Record Found as the violation reason, even though the target host is properly configured on the allowed hosts list
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs under specific configurations where Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) protection is active, and incoming requests contain complex or specifically formatted URI patterns within input parameters
bugs.impact: Legitimate traffic is blocked (false positive), resulting in minor service disruptions for valid client requests

bugs.title: TMM crash when multiple access ipsec vpn tunnels are created
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and traffic stops
bugs.conditions: Access IPSec VPN is configured
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and traffic stops

bugs.title: BIG-IP may experience increased resource usage under certain traffic conditions.
bugs.symptoms: Under certain conditions, protocol interactions may lead to a minor increase in BIG-IP memory usage.
bugs.conditions: The virtual server is configured to handle the affected traffic.
bugs.impact: Over time, BIG-IP may experience resource constraints that could affect traffic processing.
bugs.workaround: No
bugs.fix: issue is fixed now

bugs.title: [PA]cache-fm-Modern.js: F5_C_IW.tryIWs() uses incorrect string "XMLHttpREquest" (uppercase E) instead of "XMLHttpRequest"
bugs.symptoms: The MODERN Portal Access JavaScript rewriter (cache-fm-Modern.js) contains a misspelled string literal "XMLHttpREquest" (uppercase E) used as the first argument to F5_C_IW.tryIWs() in three locations. The correct spelling is "XMLHttpRequest". This results in an inconsistent internal IW state key name but has no effect on application behavior or functionality
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM Portal Access configured with MODERN rewriter mode enabled. The misspelling is present in cache-fm-Modern.js at the F5_C_IW.tryIWs() calls for the onprogress, onreadystatechange, and onerror event wrappers
bugs.impact: No functional impact. XMLHttpRequest event wrapping (onprogress, onreadystatechange, onerror) works correctly. The misspelling only affects an internal IW state key name and does not cause application failures, JavaScript errors, or behavioral differences

bugs.title: An ASM Policy with IP Intelligence enabled exported in JSON format cannot be imported
bugs.symptoms: When an ASM security policy with IP Intelligence enabled is exported in JSON format, the exported policy cannot be imported successfully
bugs.conditions: When an ASM security policy with IP Intelligence enabled is exported in JSON format
bugs.impact: The import failure is associated with the description for the "Tor Proxies" category in the IP Intelligence. This appears to be a regression of Bug 1632385. After the fix for that bug, the exported description for "Tor Proxies" changed from "originator’s" to "originator’s," which is causing the import failure
bugs.workaround: Workaround is to replace originator’s with originator＼u00e2＼u0080＼u0099s and the import will be successful

bugs.title: Missing MAILTO="" statement in cron files
bugs.symptoms: /root/dead.letter gets populated with cron job outputs and errors
bugs.conditions: /etc/cron.d/ file does not have empty MAILTO="" before script execution line
bugs.impact: /root/dead.letter gets populated with unnecessary emails
bugs.workaround: /etc/cron.d/ files can be edited manually to add MAILTO="" before line executed by cron

bugs.title: Disk provisioning error does not identify available volume group capacity
bugs.symptoms: When module provisioning fails due to insufficient disk space, the system displays a message indicating that the disk limit has been exceeded. This message includes a value representing the available capacity in megabytes. It’s important to note that this value may be confused with the amount of free space available in the /shared file system
bugs.conditions: - The system or tenant does not have enough available disk space in the volume group to provision the configured modules - Configuration load or module provisioning fails and reports a disk limit exceeded message
bugs.impact: An attempt can be made to resolve the issue by increasing the size of the /shared file system. However, this action reduces the available disk space for module provisioning and does not actually fix the underlying problem; in fact, it may worsen the situation
bugs.workaround: - Increase the size of the disk allocated to the system or tenant - Do not increase the size of the /shared file system to resolve this issue
bugs.fix: The configuration load provides the right error, identifying the value as the disk capacity available for module provisioning

bugs.title: TMM crash when PEM policy tcl-filter uses PEM::session info attr on multi-blade system
bugs.symptoms: - TMM generates a SIGSEGV core file and restarts - The log contains the message: PEM: spm_tcl_filter_find_match: <policy_name> suspending iRule command not supported shortly before the crash
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP PEM provisioned on a multi-blade VELOS system - A PEM policy uses an inline tcl-filter containing an async-capable command such as PEM::session info attr [IP::client_addr] <attribute_name> - A cluster membership change occurs (blade join or leave), causing previously local PEM session lookups to become non-local (asynchronous)
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts, causing traffic disruption. Multiple TMMs may core in quick succession during cluster topology changes
bugs.workaround: Move the PEM::session info attr command out of the PEM policy inline tcl-filter and into a standard iRule where asynchronous command suspension is supported. The tcl-filter execution context does not support suspending/async commands

bugs.title: APMD rejects valid SAMLResponse POST values containing URL-encoded CRLF line folding, breaking SAML SP ACS flow
bugs.symptoms: APM as SP fails during ACS processing for otherwise valid SAML responses from the IdP /var/log/apm shows the following errors: HTTPParser.cpp func: "parsePostParam()" ... POST param 'SAMLResponse' value contains CRLF, rejecting request
bugs.conditions: - Access policy has SAML auth configured - SAMLResponse or RelayState contains CRLF characters
bugs.impact: Access policy execution fails, thereby rejecting sessions

bugs.title: [APM][VDI]VMware Horizon WebTop "Settings > here" link uses obsolete VMware client download URL and opens HTTP 404
bugs.symptoms: In VMware Horizon VDI resources presented through APM WebTop, the native client download message contains a hyperlink labeled "here". Clicking the link opens: http://www.vmware.com/go/viewclients That URL is no longer valid and returns HTTP 404
bugs.conditions: - APM WebTop configured with VMware Horizon / VMware View resources - User opens the VDI settings or native client download prompt and clicks the embedded download link
bugs.impact: When you click on "here" it goes to https://www.vmware.com/go/viewclients, which results in a 404 Page not found

bugs.title: DOS | Sweep&flood| Disabled DoS device Sweep/Flood vector's rate-tracker remains active
bugs.symptoms: On reboot, sweep, and flood rows are always observed in the rate_tracker_stats, even though the single endpoint sweep and single endpoint flood device vectors are disabled
bugs.conditions: Disable the single endpoint sweep and single endpoint flood device vectors, just reboot the big ip from the console
bugs.impact: unnecessary rows are getting created in the rate_tracker_stats
bugs.workaround: Enable and disable the vectors explictly after reboot, removes this rows from rate_tracker_stats

bugs.title: ACME client may reject valid newNonce responses with HTTP 204 from some ACME servers
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP requests an ACME nonce from the newNonce endpoint, the request may fail if the ACME server responds with an HTTP 204 No Content status, even if a valid Replay-Nonce header is included. This failure is logged as an inability to obtain a nonce, which can lead to issues with ACME account creation
bugs.conditions: ACME enrollment is configured against a server (for example, DigiCert ACME) that returns 204 No Content for newNonce. BIG-IP ACME logic accepts only HTTP 200 OK for nonce retrieval
bugs.impact: ACME account creation, certificate enrollment, or renewal can fail, preventing automated certificate management
bugs.workaround: Use an ACME endpoint/provider that returns HTTP 200 OK for newNonce responses until a software fix is available

bugs.title: Intermittent MCPD database errors for partition_object_join on BIG-IP VE HA pairs
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP intermittently logs the following MCPD error multiple times within a short period: 01070710:3: Database error (13), Cannot update_indexes/checkpoint DB object, class:partition_object_join status:13 - EdbCfgObj.cpp, line 127
bugs.conditions: - The issue was observed on a BIG-IP VE active/standby HA pair running version 17.1.2.1 - The MCPD process intermittently logged errors involving the partition_object_join database object
bugs.impact: Repeated MCPD database errors are written to the system logs

bugs.title: FDB entries may not always be deleted when a tenant is rebooted or upgraded
bugs.symptoms: In a Velocity tenant, the tenant creates FDB entries on the host that inform the host about VLAN+MAC pairings. If a tenant has multiple VLANs and different MAC addresses assigned to each VLAN, and is rebooted or upgraded, there is a chance that MAC address + VLAN mappings change. K50122514 contains details describing MAC address changes after an upgrade, which is expected behavior Example showing invalid FDB entries that do not match the current VLAN+MAC pairings on the tenant [root@localhost:Active:Standalone] config # tmsh show net vlan | grep -e Mac -e Vlan | paste - - Net::Vlan: VLAN43 Mac Address (True) 00:94:a1:6a:d5:60 Net::Vlan: VLAN44 Mac Address (True) 00:94:a1:6a:d5:61 Net::Vlan: VLAN45 Mac Address (True) 00:94:a1:6a:d5:62 R10900-R84-S35# show fdb SUB MOD NDI MAC ADDRESS VLAN TAG TYPE VLAN TAG TYPE VID ENTRY TYPE OWNER ID AGE ID SVC VTC SEP DMS DID CMDS MIRRORING INTERFACE ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 00:94:a1:6a:d5:62 43 tag_type_vid 43 tag_type_vid 43 L2-LISTENER repro-tenant-2 0 - 4095 14 - - - - 1 - - <----- WRONG 00:94:a1:6a:d5:60 43 tag_type_vid 43 tag_type_vid 43 L2-LISTENER repro-tenant-2 0 - 4095 14 - - - - 1 - - 00:94:a1:6a:d5:60 44 tag_type_vid 44 tag_type_vid 44 L2-LISTENER repro-tenant-2 0 - 4095 14 - - - - 1 - - <----- WRONG 00:94:a1:6a:d5:61 44 tag_type_vid 44 tag_type_vid 44 L2-LISTENER repro-tenant-2 0 - 4095 14 - - - - 1 - - 00:94:a1:6a:d5:61 45 tag_type_vid 45 tag_type_vid 45 L2-LISTENER repro-tenant-2 0 - 4095 14 - - - - 1 - - <----- WRONG 00:94:a1:6a:d5:62 45 tag_type_vid 45 tag_type_vid 45 L2-LISTENER repro-tenant-2 0 - 4095 14 - - - - 1 - -
bugs.conditions: A Velocity tenant deployed with a MAC block size > 1 VLAN > MAC pairings that change after an upgrade
bugs.impact: Traffic disruption. Traffic returning to the tenant on the wrong VLAN
bugs.workaround: Either delete the old invalid FDB entries manually in F5OS, reboot the F5OS Appliance or blade to clear the entries
bugs.fix: Platform-agent removes static L2 listener on shutdown

bugs.title: The workaround for Bug ID 694707 (Hardware Crypto Offload is not compatible with HTTP/3 / QUIC) may result in performance degradation for other virtual servers that use encryption.
bugs.symptoms: The workaround for Bug ID 694707 : tmsh modify sys db crypto.hwacceleration value disable may result in performance degradation for other virtual servers that use encryption
bugs.conditions: Workaround for Bug 694707 applied to a BIG-IP appliance, cluster, tenant, or vCMP guest
bugs.impact: Performance degradation for other virtual servers that use encryption

bugs.title: Removing or adding monitors to a FQDN pool on the Active device will result in a config-sync failure that does not self-heal
bugs.symptoms: The MCPD process logs a configuration exception indicating that a monitor rule cannot be found. This error causes the remote transaction for the device group to fail, impacting failover synchronization between peers.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP HA pair with Active-Standby setup, with both devices in sync. - Either a monitor is removed from an FQDN pool on the active device, or another monitor is added to the same FQDN pool on the active device. - Full config-sync runs. The active device pushes changes to the standby device.
bugs.impact: - Config-sync fails and does not self-heal - The devices remain out of sync
bugs.workaround: - Re-adding the monitor to the active device and then performing the config-sync. or - On the standby device, manually configure the same monitor as the active device. And run config-sync again from the standby device to the active device.

bugs.title: Restrict Key Types, Key Sizes, and Curve Names Using a Database Variable
bugs.symptoms: Introduce a mechanism to enforce restrictions on key types, key sizes, and cryptographic curves through a database variable when the system operates in Common Criteria mode within a tenant environment
bugs.conditions: This restriction is applicable only when Common Criteria mode is enabled
bugs.impact: There is no negative impact; this is a feature to enable key restrictions when Common Criteria mode is active
bugs.workaround: By default, this mechanism is disabled and can be enabled when operating in Common Criteria mode

bugs.title: Daemons are restarting because of an Out of Memory (OOM) issue following the provisioning of LTM, APM, ASM, GTM and AFM.
bugs.symptoms: Daemons are continuously restarting after the provisioning of LTM, APM, ASM, AFM and GTM modules
bugs.conditions: Host-level memory is low after provisioning LTM, APM, ASM, GTM, and AFM, which is resulting in services being killed due to OOM (Out of Memory)
bugs.impact: Services attempting to allocate memory during memory pressure are killed due to OOM (Out of Memory)
bugs.workaround: Update provision.extramb to 500 using the command below, then save the configuration and restart the node: tmsh modify sys db provision.extramb value 500 tmsh save sys config reboot

bugs.title: Stale iControlPortal.cgi processes accumulate after repeated httpd restarts on BIG-IP 21.1.x
bugs.symptoms: Multiple stale iControlPortal.cgi processes build up after each bigstart restart of httpd
bugs.conditions: - Occurs on BIG-IP 21.1.x only - Triggered by restarting the httpd service via bigstart restart httpd - BIG-IP 17.5.x and earlier are not affected
bugs.impact: - Stale processes consume memory over time - No impact on traffic or end users
bugs.workaround: Stale processes can be manually killed as a temporary measure, but will recur until the fix is applied. Resolved in Change 3954408. After applying the fix, exactly one iControlPortal.cgi process runs after each restart — no accumulation.
bugs.fix: Resolved in Change 3954408. After applying the fix, exactly one iControlPortal.cgi process runs after each restart — no accumulation

bugs.title: BIG-IP APM OAuth Scope selects the incoming request bearer token instead of the OAuth Client access token after PRP subroutine expiration
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP APM is set up as both an OAuth Client and an OAuth Resource Server, it utilizes an OAuth Client agent followed by an OAuth Scope agent within a per-request policy subroutine. In this configuration, SSO passthrough is also enabled. As a result, the OAuth Scope may validate a bearer token from the current request instead of the valid access token that was obtained by the OAuth Client after the subroutine's subsession has expired
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP APM is configured as both an OAuth Client and OAuth Resource Server, with an OAuth Client agent followed by an OAuth Scope agent in a per-request policy subroutine. A Bearer token is sent via the Authorization header
bugs.impact: This can result in a JWK mismatch and a blocking page when the request contains an unrelated application JWT

bugs.title: ACME: Account Status remains Updating after updating account for ACME Provider
bugs.symptoms: When updating an ACME account from the BIG-IP Configuration utility, the ACME provider may remain in an Updating or Pending state.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP 21.1.0 ACME provider Let’s Encrypt or another ACME-compatible certificate authority ACME account update initiated from the GUI
bugs.impact: After an ACME account update, the account-action value may remain set to update even though the account status is valid. This leaves the provider in an Updating or Pending state and may prevent additional account changes, certificate operations, or provider deletion.
bugs.workaround: 1. Log in to the BIG-IP command-line interface. 2. Display the ACME provider configuration: tmsh list sys crypto acme-provider <provider_name> 3. Confirm that the output contains both of the following values: account-action update account-status valid 4. Clear the pending account action: tmsh modify sys crypto acme-provider <provider_name> account-action none 5. Save the configuration: tmsh save sys config 6. Verify the provider configuration again: tmsh list sys crypto acme-provider <provider_name> The account-action update line should no longer be present. 7. Confirm that the provider is no longer displayed as Updating or Pending in the GUI, then test certificate renewal.

bugs.title: [TMM]TMM cored because accesses invalid state
bugs.symptoms: After the fires, the server-side flow has no peer due to OneConnect detachment, and the http_data pointer is no longer valid. As a result, when "ACCESS::session remove" tries to use http_data to examine the MRHSession cookie, it encounters memory that has been reused. This leads to accessing an invalid state, which causes a core error
bugs.conditions: NA
bugs.impact: TMM cored, disruption in the traffic

bugs.title: SSL Orchestrator Traffic Summary log policy-rule shows the individual policy item not the policy rule
bugs.symptoms: In the SSL Orchestrator Traffic Summary log message, the policy-rule portion prints individual policy items (like Category Lookup) instead of the policy rule the item is running under
bugs.conditions: The SSL Orchestrator traffic summary log is configured to show up (SSL Orchestrator log levels are set to info), and the flow corresponding to the log message did not complete successfully
bugs.impact: Traffic Summary log may be misinterpreted, and it seems that an unknown or unauthorized policy rule is being applied The log does not clearly distinguish between: The final matched top-level policy rule; and An internal policy node reached before the flow failed or timed out This all creates ambiguity during troubleshooting and log analysis
bugs.workaround: While there is no workaround to have the policy rule actually print the rule, you can look at the APM Per Request Policy to determine which policy rule applies to the policy item that was logged

bugs.title: Advanced WAF restarts repeatedly after changing TMM count
bugs.symptoms: After changing the TMM count, the bd process repeatedly restarts and does not fully recover. Some traffic gets through, but blocking responses and logs show short Support IDs (for example, 32, 64) that repeat across different requests
bugs.conditions: - The TMM count is manually changed from the default
bugs.impact: The WAF constantly restarts. Advanced WAF enforcement is unstable. Support IDs may repeat across different blocked requests, making it difficult to correlate and look up specific events

bugs.title: TMM may produce a core file when you update the IP geolocation database on a system processing traffic
bugs.symptoms: When you update the IP geolocation database on a BIG-IP system that is processing traffic, the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) may produce a core file and restart. If you perform the update on more than one system in turn, each system may be affected
bugs.conditions: - A legacy version 1 IP geolocation city database file is present in /shared/GeoIP. - One or more virtual servers use a TCP Analytics profile with the City or Postcode entity enabled - Client connections are open, and the client IP addresses resolve to a city or a postcode - You update the IP geolocation database while those connections are open. Updating any single geolocation database reloads all of them
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts
bugs.workaround: Disable the City and Postcode entities in the TCP Analytics profile Alternatively, update the IP geolocation database on a system that is not processing traffic: - Fail over so that the system you want to update is the standby system - Update the IP geolocation database on the standby system - Fail back, then repeat for the other system

bugs.title: BIG-IP system offline post upgrade
bugs.symptoms: The following messages/errors are displayed: Waiting for mcpd to reach phase base, current phase is platform. "/usr/bin/tmsh -n -g -a load sys config partitions all base " - failed. -- Loading schema version: 17.5.1.3 In the systemd journal or /var/log/user.log: 01070920:3: Application error for confpp: grep: /sys/block/vd?/serial: No such file or directory sh: line 1: 12768 Hangup ( /etc/init.d/syslog-ng start ) 2>&1
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP system is offline after upgrade, with a "sh: line 1: 12768 Hangup ( /etc/init.d/syslog-ng start ) 2>&1" error in /var/log/user.log
bugs.impact: Upgrade failed.
bugs.workaround: Reload the configuration: tmsh load sys config

bugs.title: SAML SP page fails to render and displays
bugs.symptoms: In the GUI, clicking on Access > Federation results in an error: "General Exception: Check logs for more information. If the problem persists, please contact support"
bugs.conditions: On the GUI select menu, Access and click on Federation, and click on SAML Service Provider
bugs.impact: Not able to view SAML Service Provider Page
bugs.workaround: Fixed with code changes
bugs.fix: Fixed in TMUI code

bugs.title: SSE blocking page can cause multiple block responses
bugs.symptoms: In some cases, MCP clients re-trigger a request when they get an error notification. In those cases, the re-triggered request will also be blocked
bugs.conditions: - MCP server responding with SSE - Response was blocked by WAF - MCP client re-triggered the errored response
bugs.impact: Client gets multiple blocking errors

bugs.title: Blocked Model Context Protocol elicitation "ACCEPT" reply might return no blocking page and times out
bugs.symptoms: When an application security policy blocks a Model Context Protocol (MCP) elicitation "accept" request and submits the requested information, the client receives a blocking (error) notification, which the MCP client might not be able to read. Therefore, the original elicitation request stays open until it times out, and the client reports the MCP error 'McpError: MCP error -32001: Request timed out'
bugs.conditions: - ASM (Application Security) provisioned with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) security policy applied to a Virtual Server - A logging profile attached to the Virtual Server with the request filter set to log illegal requests or blocked requests only - Server Responses with elicitation - Client sends an ACCEPT request and cannot handle notification as a response -- A violation is detected in a request
bugs.impact: The client cannot parse the blocking notification and shows no indication that the content was rejected. The elicitation request remains pending until it fails with a request timeout error, so the MCP interaction cannot be completed. Other traffic is not affected

bugs.title: Configurable UCS/SCF Archive Storage on /shared with BIG-IP GUI Visibility
bugs.symptoms: UCS/SCF archive files are stored under /var/local, which resides on the /var slice (approximately 4.5 GB by default). On systems with multiple modules enabled (e.g., LTM, ASM, DNS, AVR with AS3), UCS files can become very large, making it impractical to retain multiple local restore points without running out of disk space on the /var filesystem
bugs.conditions: This occurs on BIG-IP systems running multiple modules that generate large UCS archive files. The default /var slice sizing may be insufficient to store multiple UCS archives simultaneously
bugs.impact: Users cannot retain multiple UCS restore points locally, limiting the ability to perform quick rollbacks
bugs.workaround: Can delete old/unused UCS/SCF archive files to free disk space

bugs.title: HA (High Availability) peers are unable to connect when ConfigSync uses the management IP
bugs.symptoms: -- HA (High Availability) peers in a device group are shown as Disconnected. -- SSL handshake failures are logged between the peer address and a device's internal TMM address. -- Errors appear in var/log/gtm similar to: err big3d[10046]: 012b300e:3: SSL Error: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure on connection to ::ffff:127.1.1.4:58366. -- Peer certificate verification errors referring to a self-signed certificate appear in /var/log/ltm, and the connection to the CMI peer is subsequently removed. This issue has previously been reported under ID2450009 and ID2450017.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP systems in an HA (High Availability) configuration. -- ConfigSync is configured to use the management IP address on both devices: -- sys db configsync.allowmanagement value enable -- management-ip is configured as the device configsync-ip
bugs.impact: -- Configuration synchronization between HA (High Availability) peers fails. -- HA peer devices cannot connect. -- Device Group members show a Status of Disconnected. -- Configuration changes are not synchronized between devices.
bugs.workaround: Configure the device Config Sync address to use a self IP, not the device's Management IP.
bugs.fix: HA (High Availability) peers connect successfully and Config Sync succeeds when the device's Management IP is configured as the device Config Sync address.

bugs.title: For BIGIPAuthCookie/BIGIPAuthUsernameCookie change SameSite value to Lax
bugs.symptoms: BIGIPAuthCookie/BIGIPAuthUsernameCookie SameSite=Strict breaks APM WebTop redirect logins; this behaviour is seen after setting these cookie values to Strict
bugs.impact: It breaks APM WebTop redirect logins for cert/CAC auth
bugs.fix: Fix is done by changing BIGIPAuthCookie/BIGIPAuthUsernameCookie SameSite value to Lax

bugs.title: MCPD may crash during high-load control plane operations
bugs.symptoms: Under sustained high-load control plane operations (large numbers of virtual servers, pools, and policies being created and deleted in rapid succession), mcpd may crash with a SIGSEGV
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP system is under sustained high-volume control plane activity (thousands of configuration objects being created and deleted in loops) - Multiple BIG-IP modules are provisioned (LTM, ASM, APM, AFM, GTM) mcpd worker threads are enabled (default configuration) - The mcpd send buffer to a subscriber reaches the back-pressure threshold while worker threads are concurrently processing query requests
bugs.impact: MCPD crashes and restarts, causing a temporary disruption to configuration management. Dependent daemons (tmm, bigd, gtmd) may also restart. On an HA pair, failover may occur

bugs.title: TMM may restart after a geolocation database update when a FastL4 virtual server collects city or postal code analytics
bugs.symptoms: The Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) may restart after the geolocation database is updated. This occurs while connections that were established before the update are still open
bugs.conditions: - A version 1 city geolocation database is installed - A FastL4 virtual server is configured with a TCP analytics profile that has the City or Postcode entity enabled - PVA acceleration is disabled on the FastL4 profile - Client connections are open when the geolocation database is updated
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts
bugs.workaround: Disable the City and Postcode entities in the TCP analytics profile applied to the FastL4 virtual server. Alternatively, ensure no client connections are open when you update the geolocation database

bugs.title: iControl LX extension installation may fail with IP-based HTTPS URLs using cloud-init

bugs.impact: The BIG-IP system cannot download the iControl LX extension package, and the extension installation fails Existing installed iControl LX applications are not affected
bugs.workaround: Use an FQDN with a trusted certificate, or ensure the certificate is trusted and its SAN matches the hostname or IP address used in the URL

bugs.title: FQDN pool member stays offline if the FQDN template node object is forced down and then re-enabled

bugs.impact: FQDN pool member stays offline even though the parent FQDN node is re-enabled. Traffic processing for that FQDN pool containing the pool member is impacted.
bugs.workaround: Manually re-enable the affected FQDN pool member.

bugs.fix: Enhanced error handling and environment configuration for cryptographic operations. This update: Minimizes unnecessary warning output during archive creation for clearer system diagnostics. Ensures proper GPG environment initialization to maintain consistent cryptographic operation behavior across all system processes

bugs.title: BIG-IP APM PolicySync fails with a protected f5-default cipher rule error when an APM policy references the default serverssl profile
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP APM 21.1.0, APM PolicySync fails when an APM policy contains an AAA or authentication object that references the default /Common/serverssl ServerSSL profile The target peer reports: 01071b82:3: Cipher rule (/Common/f5-default): the base cipher rules may not be modified The failure occurs even though /Common/f5-default has not been manually modified. The issue was reproduced with LDAP AAA and Endpoint Management System AAA objects referencing /Common/serverssl. The same error is documented for OAuth server objects in internal KB K000162677 Changing the affected object to use /Common/serverssl-legacy allows PolicySync to complete
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM peers running version 21.1.0 - APM PolicySync configured between the peers - The access policy contains one or more AAA or authentication objects that reference /Common/serverssl - Confirmed object types: - LDAP AAA: /SSLVPN/LDAPS_DC_VOESTALPINE - Endpoint Management System AAA: EntraID-Compliance-Check - OAuth and other authentication objects referencing /Common/serverssl should also be reviewed - The issue was reproduced on a BIG-IP R5800 appliance - The reported user's build is 21.1.0.0.43.38; the exact running build should be verified on both peers
bugs.impact: APM PolicySync fails for the affected policy, preventing policy changes from synchronizing successfully to the target peer or peers The target may display a generic “Failed to create on target” message while the detailed error appears in the logs. The issue can prevent the device group from maintaining the intended synchronized APM policy state There is currently no evidence that /Common/f5-default is corrupted. The issue affects synchronization processing rather than indicating that the protected cipher rule must be modified
bugs.workaround: Review all AAA and authentication objects in the affected APM policy that reference: /Common/serverssl Change each affected object to use: /Common/serverssl-legacy Then retry APM PolicySync. In the reproduced case, changing the LDAP AAA object alone did not resolve the failure. Changing the Endpoint Management System AAA object allowed synchronization to complete. Therefore, all APM objects in the policy must be reviewed, including LDAP AAA, Endpoint Management System AAA, OAuth, and other authentication objects Do not modify, delete, or recreate the system-protected /Common/f5-default cipher rule No confirmed fixed version is currently available

bugs.title: DNS queries forwarded with duplicate EDNS0 OPT records when ECS insertion is enabled and process-rd is disabled

Only one OPT record is allowed per DNS message, so the pool member returns FORMERR and the client's query fails
bugs.conditions: A DNS virtual server with edns0-client-subnet-insert enabled and process-rd disabled receives a recursive query (RD bit set) that already contains an EDNS0 OPT record
bugs.impact: Recursive DNS queries that carry EDNS0 fail. The pool member returns FORMERR, no answer reaches the client, and name resolution fails

bugs.title: HTTP AAA form-based authentication fails with multiple hidden form fields
bugs.symptoms: HTTP AAA form-based authentication requests are rejected if the configuration of the AAA server's Hidden Form Parameters contains multiple fields. When this happens, APM logs the following error and the login attempt fails: "HttpAgent: CR/LF detected in formParams after session variable interpolation - rejecting request."
bugs.conditions: An Access Policy employs an HTTP AAA agent utilizing Form-Based authentication. The AAA server object's Hidden Form Parameters field is set up with two or more name/value pairs, each on a separate line
bugs.impact: All authentication attempts using the affected HTTP AAA form-based configuration fail, preventing user login. The failure is entirely reproducible for any request that employs a multi-field Hidden Form Parameters configuration, with no instances of partial or intermittent success
bugs.fix: The HTTP AAA agent now processes the Hidden Form Parameters configuration by breaking it down into individual name/value pairs. It first parses these pairs and then applies session-variable interpolation and CRLF-injection validation to each one separately, rather than validating the entire raw multi-line configuration as a single string. This change allows legitimate multi-field configurations to authenticate successfully while still rejecting any CR/LF characters that may be introduced through session-variable interpolation

bugs.title: TMM may crash when an in-TMM (TMA) TCP health monitor is deleted or reconfigured while a probe connection is still being established
bugs.symptoms: TMM can crash (SIGSEGV) and then restart when using in-TMM (TMA) TCP health monitors. These crashes occur because an internal monitoring object can be deallocated while a connection for a probe related to that same object is still active. As a result, any later events for that probe may reference memory that is no longer valid. The restart can happen during routine monitor probing, when a pending probe is being terminated, or when a deadman timer for a monitor expires for a probe that has already been terminated
bugs.conditions: This issue requires all of the following: - Pool members are monitored using an in-TMM (TMA) health monitor of type TCP (or a TCP-based monitor such as tcp_echo), rather than an off-box bigd monitor - The monitor or node configuration is changed (for example, monitor association added/removed, monitor modified, or node state changed) while a probe's TCP connection to a pool member is still being established (SYN outstanding, no response yet from the server) - The timing window between the configuration change and the pending probe's connection completion is short, so the two overlap Frequency increases with: Frequent monitor/pool/node configuration changes (churn). Pool members or network paths with higher connection-establishment latency, which widens the window during which the race can occur
bugs.impact: TMM crashes and restarts, causing a momentary interruption of data-plane traffic on the affected TMM/blade and a failover event on the affected device (or CMP instance). No authentication or client action is required to encounter this issue; it can occur during normal operation when in-TMM TCP monitoring is used alongside monitor/node configuration changes. Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts
bugs.workaround: Where possible, use off-box (bigd) TCP health monitoring instead of in-TMM (TMA) TCP monitoring for affected pools, as this issue only affects the in-TMM monitoring path. If in-TMM TCP monitoring must be used, avoid frequent or scripted/rapid monitor and node configuration changes (for example, repeatedly removing and re-adding a monitor on a pool) against pools with active in-TMM TCP monitors. Using longer monitor intervals/timeouts relative to expected connection-establishment time for monitored servers reduces the likelihood of the race window being hit, though it does not eliminate the underlying issue
