bugs.workaround: Manually re-apply the access policies that use the common Webtop: GUI: Access ›› Profiles / Policies : Access Profiles (Per-Session Policies) -> {check all the related Access policies} -> Apply

bugs.title: Sorting by column does not work in GUI Statistics page for virtual servers
bugs.symptoms: Clicking on columns on the statistics page of virtual servers in the GUI does not sort them by that column
bugs.conditions: - Partition is set to All [Read-only] - A column is clicked on the statistics page of the virtual servers
bugs.impact: The virtual servers are not sorted by the column that they should have been sorted by

bugs.title: Successful REST API requests are not logged in the restjavad audit log
bugs.symptoms: On affected systems, the restjavad audit log (`/var/log/restjavad-audit.*.log`) does not contain entries for successful REST API calls (HTTP status < 400), such as PUT, POST, PATCH, or GET requests. Only requests that result in an error response (status ≥ 400) are recorded. This occurs even when `audit.logging.FileHandler.level` is set to `INFO` (the default) or `FINE`
bugs.conditions: This occurs on any BIG-IP system running an affected 17.5.x version. It reproduces when sending any successful REST API request to an endpoint that does not contain `/tokens/` in its URI, for example: curl -sk -u admin:admin -X PUT https://localhost/mgmt/tm/sys/dns -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"nameServers":["8.8.8.8","1.1.1.1"],"search":["example.com"]}' curl -sk -u admin:admin -X POST https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/node -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"node1","partition":"Common","address":"10.0.3.10"}' curl -sk -u admin:admin -X PATCH https://localhost/mgmt/tm/ltm/node/~Common~node1 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"description":"web server 1 - dc1"}'
bugs.impact: Loss of audit visibility for successful configuration changes and API activity performed through the REST API
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: ConfigSync fails for a certificate with an existing OCSP cert-validator
bugs.symptoms: ConfigSync fails with error 01071bae:3, reporting that the certificate already has another OCSP cert-validator configured.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP devices have the same OCSP cert-validator associated with a certificate, and ConfigSync reapplies that association during synchronization.
bugs.impact: The sync fails, preventing the affected configuration from being applied to the peer.
bugs.workaround: On the standby device, remove the validator reference and disable OCSP for the affected certificate, then initiate ConfigSync from the active device. If OCSP does not synchronize, disable and re-enable it on the active device.

bugs.title: Error installing hotfix on iSeries appliances
bugs.symptoms: When installing the hotfix, an RPM error occurs. In liveinstall.log: info: RPM: ln: failed to create symbolic link '/config/ssh/scp.whitelist-platform': File exists
bugs.conditions: - Applying certain BIG-IP Engineering Hotfixes on iSeries platforms - Hotfix-BIGIP-17.1.3.5.0.1.14-ENG.iso is one such affected Engineering Hotfix
bugs.impact: The hotfix installation fails
bugs.workaround: Contact F5 Support for a fix

bugs.title: Error: "General database error retrieving information" seen in GUI, while accessing "System > Logs > Audit" page
bugs.symptoms: On a standalone BIG-IP VE running BIG-IP LTM 21.1.0.1, the TMUI page System > Logs > Audit fails to load and displays: "General database error retrieving information." The issue is reproducible when logged in as admin. It occurs on the Audit page despite LTM being the only provisioned module
bugs.conditions: On the GUI, from the Menu list, select "System > Logs > Audit" Option
bugs.impact: No Logs page available due to this issue

bugs.title: Missing FDB entries for mac masquerade addresses for additional traffic groups may cause packet loss
bugs.symptoms: In an F5OS tenant with multiple traffic groups, the platform_agent may fail to create the necessary FDB entries on the hypervisor for the additional traffic groups during the initial setup. However, once the tenant is rebooted or the platform_agent is restarted, the entries are successfully created
bugs.conditions: - F5OS Tenant - Multiple traffic groups - MAC masquerade configured on the additional traffic group - No floating self-ips configured on the affected VLANs - Initial traffic group creation
bugs.impact: The lack of FDB entries can cause packet loss for ingress packets destined to the mac masquerade address as DLF traffic is rate limited
bugs.workaround: Reboot the tenant or restart platform_agent

bugs.title: Serverside Client Hello's may rarely be delayed with SSL mirroring
bugs.symptoms: With SSL mirroring enabled and TLS1.3 enabled client side, Client Hellos from the BIG-IP may be delayed by 8 seconds before being sent to the pool member. On the standby BIG-IP device, logs similar to those below may be seen in /var/log/ltm Sep 11 00:07:28 <HOSTNAME> warning tmm1[10882]: 01260009:4: (null connflow): Connection error: ssl_basic_crypto_cb:703: alert(20) Decryption error Sep 11 00:07:28 <HOSTNAME> warning tmm1[10882]: 01260009:4: <IP>:<PORT> -> <IP>:<PORT>: Connection error: hud_ssl_handler:2194: alert(20) codec alert Sep 11 00:08:22 <HOSTNAME> warning tmm1[10882]: 01260013:4: SSL Handshake failed for TCP <IP>:<PORT> -> <IP>:<PORT> The associated client-ssl profile on the standby unit will also show the bad record stats counter incrementing.
bugs.conditions: - Mirroring enabled on a virtual server with client and server SSL profiles attached - TLS1.3 enabled client side
bugs.impact: SSL connections may rarely stall, before the Client Hello gets sent to the pool member.
bugs.workaround: Disable TLSv1.3 on client-ssl profile if it is not absolutely needed. Else, disable mirroring from the virtual server.

bugs.title: Vmware session isolation not working with VCS 2026
bugs.symptoms: When APM VMWare VDI is configured and accessed desktop resources or apps using native client or webtop, session isolation and Process Monitor are not working with the new VCS server version 2026
bugs.conditions: APM Vmware VDI is configured, and resources are accessed using webtop or the native client
bugs.impact: Session isolation and process monitor features of VMware do not work

bugs.title: BIG-IP TMUI may reset Client SSL Certificate Key Chain values after an entry is deleted and re-added
bugs.symptoms: When modifying a Client SSL profile through the BIG-IP Configuration utility, the values shown in the Add SSL Certificate Key Chain dialog may differ from the values applied to the profile You may observe one or both of the following: - The Chain field is saved as None, although the dialog displayed an intermediate certificate - The Certificate and Key fields are saved as default, although the dialog displayed previously configured certificate and key values - The unexpected values appear after the Certificate Key Chain entry is added - No warning indicates that the displayed and submitted values differ
bugs.conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - You manage an LTM Client SSL profile through the BIG-IP Configuration utility (TMUI) - The profile contains a Certificate Key Chain entry - You select and delete that entry - You click Add to create a replacement entry - The Add dialog displays values retained from the deleted entry - You submit the dialog without explicitly reselecting every displayed field The resulting behavior depends on which fields you modify: - If you change Certificate and Key but do not change Chain, Chain may be saved as None - If you do not change any displayed fields, Certificate and Key may be saved as default
bugs.impact: The Client SSL profile may be saved with certificate settings that differ from those displayed in the Configuration utility. Possible effects include: - The configured intermediate certificate chain may be removed - TLS clients may receive an incomplete certificate chain and fail certificate validation - The profile may use the BIG-IP default certificate and key instead of the intended certificate and key - Virtual servers using the affected profile may present an unintended certificate - TLS connections may fail or generate certificate warnings - Administrators may not notice the configuration change because the Add dialog displays the expected values before submission - The data plane is not affected until the modified profile configuration is saved and used by traffic
bugs.workaround: Before clicking Add in the Certificate Key Chain dialog, explicitly select every required value, even when the correct value is already displayed: - Select the intended Certificate - Select the intended Key - Select the intended Chain, or explicitly select None if no chain is required - Click Add - Verify the resulting Certificate Key Chain entry before saving the Client SSL profile - Alternatively, configure or verify the Certificate Key Chain using the Traffic Management Shell (tmsh) instead of the Configuration utility After making the change, verify the effective configuration: tmsh list ltm profile client-ssl <profile-name> cert-key-chain tmsh list ltm profile client-ssl repro_cssl cert-key-chain

bugs.title: TMM restarts on BIG-IP Virtual Edition in Azure or Hyper-V when a network interface link check does not complete
bugs.symptoms: TMM stops updating its heartbeat, and the system restarts TMM and writes a core file. The /var/log/ltm file shows messages similar to the following: 01140041:5: Killing tmm.0 pid <pid> 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat tmm fails action is go offline down links and restart
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP Virtual Edition runs in Microsoft Azure or Hyper-V - The data plane interfaces use the DPDK netvsc driver - A network interface link status check does not complete within approximately 10 seconds
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while tmm restarts

bugs.title: DNS Express huge-page memory exhaustion does not fail gracefully and lacks proactive warnings
bugs.symptoms: When DNS Express is configured to store zone data using huge pages (via DNSExpress.HugePages), the zxfrd process cannot store updated zone data once the allocation of huge pages is exhausted. Additionally, there is no proactive SNMP or iHealth-based warning available before reaching this limit
bugs.conditions: DNSExpress.HugePages is configured with a non-zero value, and the size of the zone data (due to upstream zone growth, frequent updates, or fragmentation) approaches or exceeds the configured huge-page allocation
bugs.impact: DNS Express service disruption occurs when huge-page memory is exhausted, as zone transfers can no longer be stored. Recovery requires manual intervention (increasing DNSExpress.HugePages and restarting TMM), and users have no advance warning before the disruption occurs
bugs.workaround: Size DNSExpress.HugePages conservatively, using the guidance in K54670218, and monitor /var/log/ltm for related messages at the info log level to detect early signs of huge-page pressure

bugs.title: Update BIG-IP time zone data (tzdata) to IANA 2026c
bugs.symptoms: BIG-IP ships tzdata 2018e, so DST rules that have changed since 2018 are wrong. America/Edmonton still shows DST transitions in 2026, even though Alberta has moved to permanent MST (ABT)
bugs.conditions: Any BIG-IP build with tzdata‑2018e‑3 using a zone whose IANA rules changed after 2018e, notably Alberta and recent BC updates
bugs.impact: Local timestamps and time‑based scheduling can be off by one hour during affected DST windows
bugs.workaround: Set timezone to UTC until fixed

bugs.title: Network Map loads very slowly on BIG-IP 17.5.x with large configurations
bugs.symptoms: - When navigating to Local Traffic >> Network Map on BIG-IP 17.5.x, the page takes several minutes to fully render when the configuration contains a large number of objects (e.g., 261 virtual servers, 272 pools, 184 nodes) - The GUI appears to hang/freeze during loading, and no other GUI operations can be performed until the Network Map finishes loading
bugs.conditions: - Running BIG-IP software version 14.1.0 or later (including 17.5.x) - Configuration contains a large number of LTM objects (virtual servers, pools, pool members, nodes) - Navigating to Local Traffic >> Network Map in the Configuration Utility (GUI)
bugs.impact: - The GUI becomes unresponsive while the Network Map is loading - Cannot perform other GUI operations during this time
bugs.workaround: - No workaround. This has been identified as a systemic iControl REST performance issue - The Network Map page issues iterative REST queries for each pool and its associated pool member stats, causing significant delays with large configurations - Increasing REST timeout db keys does not resolve the underlying slowness

bugs.title: Virtual server traffic may be reset after removing an ASM policy and performing a full configuration synchronization
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP 17.5.1.6, removing an ASM security policy from a virtual server on one member of a Sync-Failover device group and then performing a forced full-load push can leave stale compiled LTM policy data on the receiving device After synchronization: - Both devices report an in-sync and apparently correct configuration - The removed ASM policy is absent from the virtual server configuration - Client connections to the affected virtual server are reset. TMM reports: -- F5RST: policy execution error -- The compiled runtime policy data may still contain the removed policy name -- The receiving device can retain stale compiled policy data after the full synchronization. This creates a difference between the visible configuration and the policy data being used by TMM
bugs.conditions: The issue may occur when all these conditions are present: - BIG-IP 17.5.1.6 is used in a Sync-Failover device group - An ASM security policy is removed from a virtual server - The change is propagated to the traffic-active peer through a full-load configuration synchronization, including force-full-load-push - The receiving device previously had compiled policy data for that virtual server - Incremental synchronization has not reproduced the issue. Auto-sync normally uses incremental synchronization, although it can use a full load under certain recovery conditions
bugs.impact: Traffic to the affected virtual server may be interrupted immediately after the full synchronization. Existing and new connections can receive TCP resets until the runtime policy data is regenerated Other virtual servers are not expected to be affected unless they undergo the same policy-removal and full-sync sequence
bugs.workaround: Avoid forced full-load synchronization after removing an ASM policy. Use incremental synchronization where operationally possible To recover an already affected virtual server: - Reapply the ASM policy to the affected virtual server - Remove the ASM policy again using a normal configuration operation - Perform an incremental configuration synchronization - Confirm traffic passes normally - Removing and reassigning an existing virtual-server profile, such as the HTTP profile, may also regenerate the runtime policy data and restore traffic Auto-sync is the preferred temporary synchronization mode, but it is not an absolute safeguard because it may fall back to a full load when incremental synchronization is unavailable

bugs.title: FQDN ephemeral nodes and pool members may not be removed after DNS changes
bugs.symptoms: After a series of updates to the records provided by the configured DNS server, ephemeral nodes and pool members associated with fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) that are created temporarily during the transition may not be removed once the DNS change is complete and the FQDNs resolve back to the original set of IP addresses
bugs.conditions: This situation may occur under the following conditions: - LTM pools are configured using Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) nodes and pool members - Many of the configured FQDNs resolve to the same IP address(es) - The DNS server temporarily resolves the FQDNs to a different set of address records before reverting back to the original set of records. This can happen, for example, during maintenance on the DNS server or when a zone update is applied and then quickly undone - The time period during which the DNS server provides a different set of records is shorter than the "interval" value (DNS query interval) configured for the FQDN nodes. This condition also applies if the FQDN node is set with an "interval" value equal to the TTL (Time to Live), and the TTL returned by the DNS server is longer than the duration of the temporary record change
bugs.impact: Traffic may continue to be directed to IP addresses that were only provided by the DNS server for a brief period of time, after the DNS zone records revert to their original configuration
bugs.workaround: To work around this problem when it occurs, restart the Dynamic Configuration daemon (dynconfd) by issuing the following command at the BIG-IP console: bigstart restart dynconfd To prevent this issue from occurring, allow the temporary DNS server configuration change to persist longer than the query interval specified for the configured FQDN nodes, or the TTL interval configured in the DNS zone records if the FQDN nodes are configured with an interval of "ttl"

bugs.title: BIG-IP upgrades are failing when using IM packages released after pi_updates_17.5.0-20260819.1310.im.
bugs.symptoms: Upgrade fails with Invalid Signature ID '22817'
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP AFM 17.5.1.8 to 17.5.1.9 with IPS update pi_updates_17.5.0-20260916.0031 installed
bugs.impact: Target volume remains in a failed state
bugs.workaround: Install pi_updates_17.5.0-20260819.1310.im before the upgrade, then install the newer IPS update after booting 17.5.1.9

bugs.title: FastL4 with late binding enabled, if the connection is offloaded to PVA, the connection may break
bugs.symptoms: FastL4 with late binding enabled, if the connection is offloaded to PVA, the connection may break if the client-side MSS does not match the server-side MSS
bugs.conditions: - Virtual Server configuration: FastL4 Late binding enabled, with FIX profile - Hardware acceleration enabled; connection is offloaded to PVA - Client-side MSS does not match server-side MSS
bugs.impact: Connections/Transactions break
bugs.workaround: The Maximum Segment Size (MSS) Override option in the FastL4 profile can be used to override MSS value

bugs.title: TMM may crash when an L7 policy condition has a specific number of match values
bugs.symptoms: TMM crashes and restarts while evaluating an LTM policy condition
bugs.conditions: When a policy condition's compiled distinct match-value count lands on a boundary, and that condition happens to be the one with the largest such count in the LTM policy
bugs.impact: Traffic disrupted while TMM restarts
bugs.workaround: You can work around this issue by adding or removing one value from the affected condition's list so the number of distinct match values is no longer on a boundary

bugs.title: MCPD and TMM restart when SNMP polls pool member statistics on a system with a large configuration
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd process restarts and writes a core file. The /var/log/ltm file contains a message similar to the following: err mcpd[<pid>]: 01070001:3: Failed to allocate memory for size <size> at framework/MCPProcessor.cpp:1144. After mcpd restarts, tmm also restarts and logs: crit tmm[<pid>]: 01010020:2: MCP Connection aborted, exiting
bugs.conditions: - The mcpd process reaches the operating system limit for memory mappings in one process - An SNMP manager polls the pool member statistics table - The configuration contains a large number of pool members
bugs.impact: The MCPD and TMM processes restart. Traffic is disrupted while TMM restarts

bugs.title: [APM][PA]Portal Access session timeout dialog buttons (Stay Connected / Disconnect) non-functional on Chrome 150+
bugs.symptoms: Access Session Dialog box not responding to clicks
bugs.conditions: - APM Portal Access configured - Backend app has non-HttpOnly cookies
bugs.impact: Unable to extend PA session by clicking 'Stay Connected'

bugs.title: Service-down-immediate-action "reset" is not honored after a restart or reboot when the associated pool has no members
bugs.symptoms: A virtual server configured with service-down-immediate-action reset does not immediately reset (RST) new client connections when its default pool has no members. Instead, the virtual server completes the TCP handshake (SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK) and only resets the connection later, during load balancing, with the internal reason "No pool member available" instead of "VIP down". This matches the behavior of service-down-immediate-action none, meaning the configured reset action is effectively ignored
bugs.conditions: - A virtual server is configured with the "service-down-immediate-action" setting set to "reset" - The default pool associated with this virtual server has no pool members - If the BIG-IP system is restarted (using the command "bigstart restart") or rebooted while this virtual server and pool configuration exist, the following behavior is observed: Only the virtual servers that existed prior to the restart and were reloaded from the saved configuration will exhibit this behavior. Virtual servers that are created or modified after the restart or reboot are not affected
bugs.impact: Clients can briefly establish a TCP connection to a virtual server that is expected to immediately refuse it, exposing an unexpected open connection state instead of an immediate reset. This condition persists until the associated pool's configuration is otherwise changed (for example, a pool member is added or removed), which forces the virtual server's availability status to be recalculated

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS resolver cache TCP messages flood logs
bugs.symptoms: DNScache: tcp connect: errno 103 and DNScache: read (in tcp s): errno 103 messages may be logged repeatedly at error severity.
bugs.conditions: BIG-IP DNS resolver cache communicates with upstream nameservers over TCP and encounters repeated TCP connection or read failures.
bugs.impact: Excessive /var/log/ltm entries may generate unnecessary alerts, accelerate log rotation, and obscure other important messages.
bugs.workaround: NA.

bugs.title: APM OAuth Client may restart during token refresh involving ID-token validation
bugs.symptoms: apmd may terminate and restart during an OAuth token refresh. The refresh transaction may fail, and users may need to authenticate again.
bugs.conditions: Observed on BIG-IP APM 17.5.1.9 build 0.46.12 with an OAuth Client using password/ROPC grant and an openid scope. The issue requires refresh processing involving ID-token validation and an empty or invalid runtime JWT configuration.
bugs.impact: OAuth refresh processing is interrupted - apmd restarts.

bugs.title: [APM]httpd_sam logs are not rotated causing /var/log exhaustion
bugs.symptoms: The /var/log/httpd_sam directory log files access_log, agent_log, and referer_log are not rotated, grow continuously, causing /var/log exhaustion
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP APM is provisioned - APM Portal Access traffic is being processed
bugs.impact: The affected log files can consume available space in /var/log, potentially causing the filesystem to reach 100% utilization
bugs.workaround: tmsh -> save sys ucs <pre-change>.us -> load sys config merge from-terminal sys log-rotate include "/var/log/httpd_sam/access_log /var/log/httpd_sam/referer_log /var/log/httpd_sam/agent_log { compress delaycompress missingok notifempty daily rotate 14 size 100M copytruncate } " -> save sys config

bugs.title: Session Resumption can be enabled/disabled on management interface
bugs.symptoms: Session Resumption cannot be disabled on the management interface
bugs.conditions: This is applicable only when BIG-IP is in Common Criteria mode
bugs.impact: It will not comply with CSFC, which is on top of Common Criteria. This is only relevant when BIG-IP operates in Common Criteria mode; otherwise, there is no impact

bugs.title: ASM remote logging may record the X-Forwarded-For value from a previous request
bugs.symptoms: When Application Security remote logging is configured, the X-Forwarded-For header value recorded for a request can be incorrect. After a request containing this header, a subsequent request without it may be logged with the earlier value instead of N/A
bugs.conditions: - An Application Security remote logging profile is in use - The logging format includes the X-Forwarded-For header value - Requests are being logged
bugs.impact: The recorded client address information is inaccurate, which can mislead log review and anything that depends on it

bugs.title: Live Update: sync from active BIG-IP to standby fail under cirtain conditions
bugs.symptoms: Live Update system from BIG-IP active stops syncing to standby BIG-IP after upgrade or reboot
bugs.conditions: restart of the active and standby happens simultaneously, while the standby comes back ON before the active device
bugs.impact: standby BIG-IP device does not get latest Live Update data
bugs.workaround: reboot active BIG-IP first, then reboot standby BIG-IP

bugs.title: DoS vector "TCP ACK (TS)" triggered after upgrade to v17.5.1.8
bugs.symptoms: On BIG-IP AFM 17.5.1.8, the TCP ACK (TS) vector may classify legitimate timestamped ACKs as invalid and drop them when TS cookies are enabled
bugs.conditions: TCP ACK (TS) DoS vector and TS-cookie functionality enabled
bugs.impact: False-positive detection causes excessive vector matches, packet drops, and potential throughput degradation
bugs.workaround: Increase the TCP ACK (TS) detection thresholds

bugs.title: BIG-IP VE: eal-intr-thread uses 100% CPU after VF removal on some Engineering Hotfixes
bugs.symptoms: After a Mellanox virtual function (VF) is removed, eal-intr-thread uses 100% CPU, and tmm stops processing traffic. This is the issue fixed in ID 2313441. It came back in some Engineering Hotfixes
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP VE using Mellanox VFs, such as on Microsoft Azure with Accelerated Networking - An Engineering Hotfix that includes ID 2355421 but not ID 2549661 - A VF is removed while the system is running, for example, during Azure host maintenance
bugs.impact: Traffic processing stops until you restart tmm or reboot the BIG-IP system
bugs.workaround: Restart TMM by running: bigstart restart TMM
bugs.fix: eal-intr-thread no longer uses excessive CPU after a VF is removed

bugs.title: The MCPD crashed because of an issue with the sod while validating TMC overlap with a complex set of traffic matching criteria.
bugs.symptoms: The mcpd process is repeatedly killed by the sod watchdog due to daemon-heartbeat failure while validating a configuration with large traffic-matching-criteria (TMC) objects. The following log messages are observed: notice sod[7757]: 01140041:5: Killing /usr/bin/mcpd pid <PID>. warning sod[7757]: 01140029:4: HA daemon_heartbeat mcpd fails action is restart. mcpd enters a crash-restart loop, with each cycle lasting approximately 7-8 minutes. All MCP-dependent daemons (tmm, clusterd, alertd, scriptd, bigd, etc.) lose their connection to mcpd each cycle: crit tmm: 01010020:2: MCP Connection closed, exiting
bugs.conditions: - One or more virtual servers are configured with traffic-matching-criteria (TMC) that reference large address lists, resulting in a high total number of expanded address entries across all TMCs - The TMC overlap validation during config load/commit takes longer than the sod daemon heartbeat timeout (300 seconds) - More likely to occur on systems with limited CPU resources (e.g., 2vCPU VELOS tenants or small VE instances)
bugs.impact: - MCPD enters a continuous crash-restart loop and cannot complete configuration loading - All MCP-dependent daemons restart each cycle, causing repeated traffic disruption
bugs.workaround: - Before any config load/change, temporarily disable the mcpd heartbeat: tmsh modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat disabled Re-enable after the load completes: tmsh modify sys daemon-ha mcpd heartbeat enabled Note: While the heartbeat is disabled, the system will not automatically restart mcpd if it becomes genuinely unresponsive - If possible, increase the tenant vCPU allocation. Increasing `mcpd.workerthreads` may also help after additional CPUs are assigned - Optimize the TMC configuration by removing duplicate entries and consolidating overlapping or adjacent address prefixes into larger CIDRs where this does not change the intended policy. Remove unused TMC objects and unnecessary port-list entries

bugs.title: APM logs an error message similar to 'Duplicate entry found for [oauth-jwt-result]' when using an OAuth Client
bugs.symptoms: When BIG-IP APM is configured with an Access Policy that includes an OAuth Client (or OAuth Scope) item, the following error-level messages may appear repeatedly in the /var/log/apm log file, once per OAuth login attempt: err apmd[<pid>]: 01490000:3: HTTPParser.cpp func: "parsePostParam()" line: <n> Msg: Duplicate entry found for [oauth-jwt-result] old value [0] new value [0] err apmd[<pid>]: 01490000:3: HTTPParser.cpp func: "parsePostParam()" line: <n> Msg: Duplicate entry found for [crypto-match-jwk-config] old value [/Common/<jwk-config>] new value [/Common/<jwk-config>] err apmd[<pid>]: 01490000:3: HTTPParser.cpp func: "parsePostParam()" line: <n> Msg: Duplicate entry found for [alg] old value [<n>] new value [<n>] These messages appear even though the OAuth Client authentication completes successfully, and end users are not affected
bugs.conditions: This occurs on an Access Policy that uses an OAuth Client agent, where the BIG-IP system's internal cryptographic offload process verifies the ID token's JWT signature. This condition is met whenever an end user completes an OAuth login through the Access Policy (redirect to the authorization server, return with an authorization code, and token exchange)
bugs.impact: This is a cosmetic logging issue only; there is no impact on OAuth Client functionality, and end users authenticate successfully. However, because these messages are logged at ERR severity, external log monitoring, SIEM, or SOC tooling that alerts on ERR-level BIG-IP log entries may generate unnecessary false-positive alerts

bugs.title: BD may crash while handling certain XML/JSON requests
bugs.symptoms: BD may crash when handling a certain mix of XML and JSON bodies in traffic
bugs.conditions: - ASM provisioned - Content profiles for XML and JSON are configured - Traffic contains a certain mix of XML and JSON bodies in requests
bugs.impact: BD crash

bugs.title: CGNAT PBA: Negative or incorrect "Active Port Blocks" statistics displayed in fw_lsn_pool_pba_stat
bugs.symptoms: - Tmctl fw_lsn_pool_pba_stat shows an incorrect negative value for active_port_blocks (for example, -320268) - port_block_deallocations exceeds port_block_allocations, causing active_port_blocks (derived as allocations − deallocations) to go negative - Other counters (for example, active_clients_reached_limit) may appear inconsistent with actual usage - Behaviour indicates data plane/NAT functionality is unaffected; the issue is limited to statistics/visibility
bugs.conditions: On multi bladed systems like VIPRION and vCMP, NAT configuration using CGNAT Port Block Allocation (PBA) with: PAT mode: pba Mapping: address-pooling-paired Port-block parameters (example): block-size 256 client-block-limit 3 block-idle-timeout 120 block-lifetime 86400 Observed in environments with very high port block churn (hundreds of millions of allocations and deallocations).
bugs.impact: - The active_port_blocks counter does not reflect the actual number of active port blocks and may display negative values - This is a stats/visibility issue only; traffic translation and NAT functionality continue to work as expected - May cause operational confusion or misreporting in monitoring/automation systems relying on this counter

bugs.title: REST endpoint device-info returns empty slots after reboot on BIG-IP VE deployed in Azure
bugs.symptoms: After rebooting a BIG-IP VE system on Azure, the REST endpoint `/mgmt/shared/identified-devices/config/device-info` returns `"slots": []` despite the active software volume being healthy and complete. This prevents AS3 and other automation tools from identifying the active software slot. The following error is returned when attempting AS3 operations: {"code":400,"message":"patch operation failed - see logs for details. target device has no active slots"}
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP Virtual Edition deployed on Microsoft Azure - 16 vCPUs (higher vCPU counts may increase I/O contention during boot) - BIG-IP v17.5.1.8 (Engineering Hotfix 0.158.19); may also affect other 17.x versions on cloud platforms - Multiple modules provisioned at nominal: LTM + ASM + AFM (heavy boot-time I/O from module initialization) - A full system reboot is required to trigger (restjavad-only restart does not trigger the issue)
bugs.impact: - AS3 operations fail - PATCH, deploy, and declaration operations return HTTP 400 after every reboot, blocking all AS3-driven automation - Automation workflows broken - Any workflow that depends on the device-info `slots` field (AS3, F5 Terraform provider, BIG-IQ discovery, custom REST automation) fails until restjavad is manually restarted
bugs.workaround: Workaround after each reboot: bigstart restart restjavad && sleep 30 && bigstart restart restnoded Verify slots are populated: restcurl shared/identified-devices/config/device-info | python -m json.tool | grep -A5 slots

bugs.title: AVR/SSL Orchestrator URL, host name, URL category and user statistics are lost after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After upgrading, SSL Orchestrator analytics views that depend on URL category, URL, host name or user names (for example 'show analytics ssl-orchestrator report view-by url-category') return "No data available", and the matching SSL Orchestrator dashboard widgets show "No Data". Other statistics such as client IP addresses and cipher versions may still be displayed.
bugs.conditions: - SSL Orchestrator is provisioned with AVR and has collected URL category data. - The system is upgraded to a new software version. - During the first boot of the new version, monpd imports the saved upgrade data and then the AVR database is rebuilt (for example because the AVR database is recreated on the application volume).
bugs.impact: Historical AVR statistics for the affected SSL Orchestrator dimensions (URL category, URL, host name, user) are permanently lost after the upgrade. Traffic processing is not affected.

bugs.title: Continuous cores on tmm startup after upgrading to 17.5.1.9
bugs.symptoms: The tmm process may become stuck in a restart loop where it cores on startup, after upgrading to 17.5.1.9
bugs.conditions: - DNS(GTM) is provisioned - GeoIP database is present in /shared/GeoIP/ - selinux context for the geoip database files is incorrect (should be "shared_geoip_t")
bugs.impact: Tmm process unable to start, BIG-IP unable to start up.
bugs.workaround: View the current selinux context: ls -RZ /shared/GeoIP The output should show "system_u:object_r:shared_geoip_t:s0" against each file/directory If it shows a different label, such as 'default_t', then restore the expected selinux context to the geoip database files: restorecon -Rv /shared/GeoIP

bugs.title: ACL Details reports show records under Common instead of the non-Common partition where the APM Network Access ACL is configured
bugs.symptoms: ACL records generated by a Network Access configuration in a non-Common partition are not shown correctly in Access Reports when the non-Common partition is selected. The same records may appear under Common instead of the actual partition
bugs.conditions: - APM Network Access ACL logging is enabled - The access profile, network access resources, and ACLs are created in a non-Common partition, for example, TEST_PARTITION - A valid VPN / Network Access session is established in TEST_PARTITION, and traffic matches the ACLs - The matched traffic creates ACL log records in the database, including packet-filter and session data - Open the BIG-IP GUI at Access > Overview > Access Reports - Change the GUI partition between TEST_PARTITION and Common while viewing the ACL reports - Reproduce the issue when the report is opened or refreshed under TEST_PARTITION, where ACL data incorrectly appears under Common Expected result: ACL logs should be displayed only for the selected partition. They should not appear under Common unless Common is intentionally selected The issue is valid only when the session is active, ACL logs exist, and the report is checked after changing the GUI partition
bugs.impact: Users cannot view the ACL report data under the correct partition. The report visibility is misleading, and partition-scoped reporting is incorrect

bugs.title: iStats counter resets might not clear cluster-wide values on multi-blade systems
bugs.symptoms: On a multi-blade VELOS tenant, running istats remove, istats reset, or tmsh reset-stats ltm virtual <vs> from the primary blade might not clear the cluster-wide iStats counter value The commands clear the primary blade’s per-TMM values, but secondary blades can retain non-zero values. As a result, istats dump and tmsh show ltm virtual continue to report a non-zero aggregate value. Merged iStats values can also differ between blades
bugs.conditions: - A BIG-IP tenant runs across multiple VELOS blades - iStats counters contain values on multiple blades - iStats synchronization to one or more secondary blades is disrupted The issue has been observed on an eight-blade customer deployment. A similar issue was reproduced in a two-blade lab system by repeatedly restarting merged on the secondary blade while modifying iStats on the primary blade. The cause of the customer-observed synchronization failure remains under investigation Other multi-blade platforms, including VIPRION and vCMP deployments, might also be affected, but this has not been confirmed
bugs.impact: Affected iStats counters retain stale values after a reset or removal, causing cluster-wide statistics to remain non-zero and potentially differ between blades
bugs.workaround: Restart csyncd on each affected secondary blade: bigstart restart csyncd

bugs.title: Virtual server stops responding to ICMP requests
bugs.symptoms: ICMP is enabled by default on virtual server destination addresses "icmp-echo' is disabled by default on security NAT source-translation objects. "proxy-arp" is disabled by default on security NAT source-translation objects When a security NAT source-translation object shares one of its addresses with a virtual server destination address: - If the security NAT source-translation was created *before* the virtual server, enabling "proxy-arp" on the security NAT source-translation object disables ICMP on the virtual server address. Even if "proxy-arp" shouldn't have anything to do with the ICMP behaviour of the virtual address - If the security NAT source translation was created *after* the virtual server, enabling "proxy-arp" on the security NAT source translation does not have any effect on the ICMP behaviour of the virtual server address. This is the expected behaviour
bugs.conditions: - A security NAT source-translation object shares one of its addresses with a virtual server destination address - The security NAT source-translation object was created before the virtual server - The "proxy-arp" setting of the security NAT source translation object is set to "enabled"
bugs.impact: ICMP is disabled on the virtual server address
bugs.workaround: Two possible workarounds: (1) - Delete the virtual server and the security NAT source-translation object sharing the address. - Recreate the virtual server, and then recreate the security NAT source-translation object Or: (2) Set "proxy-arp" on the security NAT source-translation object to "disabled"

bugs.title: BIGIP GUI is not functioning properly after 3000 keycerts configuration
bugs.symptoms: After configuring 3000 keycerts, the BIG-IP GUI is malfunctioning. It shows "unable to contact BIGIP device" and may become inaccessible until a reboot is performed
bugs.conditions: Once, after loading 3000 keys into the BIG-IP instance using the tmsh command, it caused OutOfMemory issues
bugs.impact: Due to this issue, GC overhead and TMUI are preventing the creation of virtual servers, pools, and other functionalities. Additionally, there are times when we cannot contact the BIG-IP device, which is causing disruptions for customers in their usual operations on BIG-IP
bugs.workaround: To resolve the GC OOM issue, execute the following commands: tmsh modify sys db provision.tomcat.extramb value 512 tmsh save sys config bigstart restart tomcat

bugs.title: [SELinux] AVC denial: logrotate_t denied { getattr } on /shared/.tp_edr_mon_logs/tp_edr_mon.log (default_t)
bugs.symptoms: While executing the tpedrmon log rotation command: /usr/sbin/logrotate -s /var/lib/logrotate-tpedrmon.status /etc/logrotate.d/tpedrmon The command immediately fails with Permission denied (even as root): [root@localhost:ModuleNotLicensed::Active:Standalone] config # /usr/sbin/logrotate -s /var/lib/logrotate-tpedrmon.status /etc/logrotate.d/tpedrmon error: stat of /shared/.tp_edr_mon_logs/tp_edr_mon.log failed: Permission denied Simultaneously, an SELinux AVC denial is logged in /var/log/audit/audit.log: type=SYSCALL msg=audit(1791476642.660:6551): arch=c000003e syscall=6 success=no exit=-13 comm="logrotate" exe="/usr/sbin/logrotate" subj=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:logrotate_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 type=AVC msg=audit(1791476642.660:6551): avc: denied { getattr } for pid=24814 comm="logrotate" path="/shared/.tp_edr_mon_logs/tp_edr_mon.log" dev="dm-1" ino=524297 scontext=unconfined_u:unconfined_r:logrotate_t:s0-s0:c0.c1023 tcontext=system_u:object_r:default_t:s0 tclass=file
bugs.conditions: The denials are generated whenever the periodic tpedrmon log rotation job runs. The logrotate process (logrotate_t) is denied { getattr } access to /shared/.tp_edr_mon_logs/tp_edr_mon.log because the log file has the generic default_t:s0 SELinux context instead of a valid log context.
bugs.impact: The tpedrmon log rotation job generates SELinux AVC denials.
bugs.workaround: Modify default_t context to var_log_t in selinux config files: /shared/＼.tp_edr_mon_logs(/.*)? system_u:object_r:var_log_t:s0 Above change won't survive upgrade.

bugs.title: Applications that set tiny SO_SNDBUF values may experience a tcp connection stall from the Linux host
bugs.symptoms: If there is packet loss on the network, applications that use smaller send buffers may experience a tcp socket hang. This has been observed on ASM ICAP traffic.
bugs.conditions: -- Traffic emanating from the BIG-IP Linux host -- ASM ICAP
bugs.impact: Under certain conditions ICAP data may stop being sent to the ICAP server.
bugs.workaround: Delete the affected / stalled connections via tmsh Disable GSO (generic-segmentation-offload) on the vlan towards the ICAP servers.

bugs.title: Network packet loss to ICAP servers results in transaction pileup in BD
bugs.symptoms: If there is packet loss on the network, ICAP errors may appear in BD logs. The concurrent transaction count will also continually rise until the network issues resolve themselves. Minimal throughput from the BIG-IP is also expected as ASM holds the majority of incoming requests.
bugs.conditions: ASM is configured with an ICAP server that is actively being used for antivirus scanning during packet loss on the network.
bugs.impact: ICAP data may stop being sent to the ICAP server, resulting in transactions piling up in BD.
bugs.workaround: Delete the affected / stalled connections via tmsh Disable GSO (generic-segmentation-offload) on the vlan towards the ICAP servers. OR Disable Anti-Virus Protection

bugs.title: Higher control plane CPU usage from the ASM JavaScript obfuscator after upgrade
bugs.symptoms: After you upgrade, control plane CPU usage is higher during the period each day when the system generates obfuscated JavaScript. The Java process that runs compiler.jar uses about twice as much CPU as before, and the high CPU period lasts longer
bugs.conditions: One of these is attached to a virtual server: - A Bot Defense profile - A DoS profile with client-side defense or CAPTCHA challenge enabled
bugs.impact: Control plane CPU usage is about twice as high as expected while the system generates obfuscated JavaScript. This can last several hours each day and can trigger high CPU alerts
bugs.workaround: On each BIG-IP system, run this command: sed -i 's/ReservedCodeCacheSize=16m/ReservedCodeCacheSize=64m/' /var/datasync/datasyncd_obfuscator The change takes effect the next time the system generates obfuscated JavaScript. A restart is not needed An upgrade overwrites this file. Run the command again after you upgrade to a version that does not have the fix

bugs.title: Secondary blade config load failure loop fills /config partition with filestore trash_bin_d backups
bugs.symptoms: A secondary blade repeatedly fails to validate configuration received from the primary blade, causing MCPD to restart and retry the configuration load. Each attempt retains additional filestore backups under `/config/filestore/.trash_bin_d/.backup_*_d`. These backups accumulate and can eventually consume all available space on `/config`. config load failure on the secondary blade slot2 mcpd[31999]: 01070734:3: Configuration error: Configuration from primary failed validation: 01020036:3: The requested monitor instance (/Common/bigip 10.82.189.13 0 gtm-vs) was not found.... failed validation with error 16908342.
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP is deployed across multiple blades. - A secondary blade fails to load configuration received from the primary and repeatedly retries. - The load/reset sequence retains filestore backup generations without sufficient cleanup. - An orphaned GTM monitor instance triggers the reported reproduction.
bugs.impact: The affected secondary remains INOPERATIVE, reducing available cluster capacity and redundancy. Accumulating backups can exhaust `/config`, potentially preventing configuration writes and subsequent recovery operations. Disk exhaustion was reported in as little as 10 hours.
bugs.workaround: NA

bugs.title: BIG-IP DNS Oracle monitor intermittently reports DOWN
bugs.symptoms: An Oracle database monitor may intermittently report DOWN even when the database is available. The DBDaemon may terminate while processing a new probe, resulting in no database query being sent.
bugs.conditions: Occurs with BIG-IP DNS Oracle monitors using the Java DBDaemon when a probe arrives near the approximately 59.5-second idle timeout.
bugs.impact: The monitored resource may be incorrectly marked DOWN, causing temporary GTM availability issues or false member-down events.
bugs.workaround: Set the Oracle monitor to an interval such as 23 seconds, to avoid overlap with the DBDaemon idle timer.

bugs.title: MCPD restart loop becomes unrecoverable after prolonged cycling, requiring full system reboot
bugs.symptoms: After approximately 30 minutes of repeated configuration-load failures, MCPD may begin failing immediately during startup with the following message: 01070004:3: Can't connect to database, mco_runtime_start failed, status code: 80 - EdbDbConnection.cpp, line 473, status:0
bugs.conditions: - A full configuration load from text files encounters a large CLI shell script in `/config/bigip_script.conf` - MCPD repeatedly exits with database memory-allocation errors, including `Can't write blob data, attribute:script status:52` - The restart loop continues for approximately 30 minutes, or 90–95 restarts, before transitioning to status 80
bugs.impact: - MCPD remains in a persistent restart loop, preventing normal configuration loading and management operations - Correcting the original configuration trigger alone does not restore operation - A device reboot is required for the demonstrated recovery
bugs.workaround: - Stop MCPD to halt the restart loop: bigstart stop mcpd - Correct the original configuration issue. For example, back up the configuration and remove or reduce the oversized CLI script in `/config/bigip_script.conf`. - Reboot the device: reboot After rebooting, verify that MCPD starts successfully and the configuration loads without errors.

bugs.title: iControl REST Table of Contents app has a broken link for the services page under IControl REST Resources
bugs.symptoms: Clicking the services page under iControl REST Resources results in navigating to https://<BIG-IP IP address>/restui/default/default.html?$display=#!/ which is a broken link.
bugs.conditions: Using the services page link under iControl REST Resources.
bugs.impact: The user is redirected to a broken page instead of the correct services page
bugs.workaround: To access the services page navigate directly to https://<BIG-IP IP address>/restui/default/default.html?$display=/mgmt/tm/services#!/

bugs.title: With a small numbers of total connections, Static Bandwidth Controllers can unexpectedly restrict the available bandwidth
bugs.symptoms: When the BIG-IP handles only a few connections, the speed of a connection might be restricted further than expected depending on how the existing connections are distributed between different tmms. As a result, a connection might not be allocated the full remaining available bandwidth.
bugs.conditions: - Static Bandwidth Controller configured on a Virtual Server. - A small number of connections handled by the Virtual Server. - Connections are handled by different tmm threads.
bugs.impact: The connection speed depends on its tmm assignment relative to other existing connections.
bugs.workaround: Use a Dynamic Bandwidth Controller instead of a Static Bandwidth Controller.

bugs.title: Possible snatpool configuration mismatch in tmm.
bugs.symptoms: Connections are RST by tmm with a reset-cause of "No available SNAT addr" even though the configured snatpool has members.
bugs.conditions: -- A full config-sync was performed that removed a snatpool. -- The snatpool is recreated with the same name and includes one or more members that were in the snatpool when it was deleted. -- The snatpool is applied to a virtual server.
bugs.impact: Client connections might be RST.
bugs.workaround: Restarting tmm will clear the issue if it occurs. # tmsh restart sys service tmm Note that if the BIG-IP is active, restarting tmm will cause a traffic interruption.

bugs.title: BIG-IP iControl REST reboot request may close the HTTPS connection without returning an HTTP response or acknowledgment
bugs.symptoms: When a client sends a valid reboot request to the BIG-IP iControl REST endpoint, the system may initiate the reboot but close the HTTPS connection before returning an HTTP status code or JSON payload. The client may report response code 000. This indicates that no HTTP status line was received; it is not an HTTP status returned by BIG-IP.
bugs.conditions: -- BIG-IP iControl REST is used to initiate a system reboot. -- The request is sent to the /mgmt/tm/sys endpoint. -- The request contains the reboot command, with or without a target volume. -- The BIG-IP begins reboot processing while the HTTPS management connection is still active.
bugs.impact: -- REST API clients cannot reliably determine whether the reboot request was accepted because the BIG-IP may reboot without returning an HTTP acknowledgment. -- The issue also impacts Big-IQ-managed BIG-IP upgrades. BIG-IQ may report a false reboot or upgrade failure when the BIG-IP closes the connection during reboot, even though the BIG-IP boots to the intended volume and the upgrade may complete. The upgrade workflow may not proceed to post-installation tasks.

bugs.title: iControl REST Table of Contents app /mgmt/tm/services page does not display properly
bugs.symptoms: When navigating to the /mgmt/tm/services page (https://<BIG-IP IP address>/restui/default/default.html?$display=/mgmt/tm/services#!/) the content is not displayed as expected.
bugs.conditions: Navigating to the /mgmt/tm/services page in the iControl REST Table of Contents app.
bugs.impact: The content of the /mgmt/tm/services page is not displayed as expected.

bugs.title: XML exported ASM policy containing login pages and session awareness cannot reimport
bugs.symptoms: After exporting an ASM policy in XML format that has both a login page and session awareness configured, the following error message may appear when attempting to reimport the policy. "element delay_blocking: Schemas validity error : Element 'delay_blocking': This element is not expected. Expected is ( statuses )."
bugs.conditions: ASM policy containing both a login page and session awareness. Export of that ASM policy using an XML format. Reimport of the same policy without modification.
bugs.impact: Unable to reimport the exported ASM policy.
bugs.workaround: Manually edit the XML file to place the <login_pages> block at the very end of the <session_awareness> block, and then reimport the file.

bugs.title: Invalid REST endpoint when DoS profile name contains an iApp folder separator (/)
bugs.symptoms: A DoS Protection profile can be created successfully inside an iApp application folder, but subsequent attempts to edit the profile through the GUI fail. The issue affects profiles whose names reference an existing iApp, such as "mytestApp.app/dosprotect1", when a DoS vector family (e.g. HTTP, SIP, Network or DNS) is associated during *initial profile creation*. Found unexpected URI tmapi_mapper/security/dos/profile/~Common~
bugs.conditions: 1. Create a new empty iApp/application service with no template selected 2. Create a DOS protection profile and associated Dos vector family to it. 3. save/commit to create this DoS Protection profile. 4. Once DoS Protection profile is created, try to edit or perform some config changed (e.g. add some values into the Description field), 5. Try to save/commit this change and GUI fails.
bugs.impact: GUI fails and not able to edit or modify DOs profile on any subsequent changes.
bugs.workaround: 1. Create the DoS Protection Profile without a Vector Family selected. 2. Then select/add associate vector Family to it afterward

bugs.title: REST API TACACS+ authentication returns 401 when the primary TACACS+ server rejects the connection, instead of failing over to the next server
bugs.symptoms: REST API authentication via iControl REST ("/mgmt/shared/authn/login") fails with HTTP 401 "CreateTokenException" when the primary TACACS+ server is actively rejecting connections (TCP RST). SSH and GUI authentication continue to work correctly by failing over to the secondary TACACS+ server. The following error messages appear in "/var/log/secure": err pam-authenticator[<PID>]: pam_tacplus: connection failed srv 0: Connection refused notice pam-authenticator[<PID>]: pam_tacplus: pam_tacplus: user <username> not authenticated The REST API response contains: json { "code": 401, "message": "Authentication failed.", "kind": ":resterrorresponse" }
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP configured with two or more TACACS+ authentication servers. - The primary TACACS+ server actively rejects TCP connections on port 49 (sends TCP RST) - due to server failure, firewall policy, service crash, or misconfiguration. - Authentication is attempted via iControl REST API (token-based or basic authentication).
bugs.impact: REST API clients (automation scripts, monitoring tools, orchestration platforms) receive HTTP 401 authentication failures and cannot authenticate to BIG-IP when the primary TACACS+ server is unavailable due to active connection rejection. This blocks all iControl REST API operations including token creation, configuration management, and monitoring queries.

bugs.title: Config sync fails after AS3 tenant partition deletion - partition objects not removed from Standby device
bugs.symptoms: After deleting an AS3 tenant partition on the Active device in an HA pair, config sync fails with the following error: 0107082a:3: All objects from local device and all HA peer devices must be removed from a partition (<partition_name>) before the partition may be removed, type ID (2070), text ID (270275)
bugs.conditions: - BIG-IP version 21.1.0.x in an HA pair (sync-failover device group) - AS3 used to manage tenant partitions containing LTM objects - AS3 tenant partition is deleted (via AS3 DELETE declaration or empty tenant declaration) - Large or complex configuration with multiple partitions and high object count (e.g., 2900+ virtual servers, 40+ partitions)
bugs.impact: - Config sync between Active and Standby enters a persistent "Sync Failed" state - Configuration changes made on the Active device after the failure will not be synchronized to the Standby - The Standby device retains stale objects from the deleted partition
bugs.workaround: Manually delete the orphaned partition objects on the Standby device, then re-sync: Step 1: On the Standby device, list remaining objects in the partition: tmsh list /<partition_name>/ recursive Step 2: Delete objects in dependency order on the Standby: tmsh delete ltm virtual /<partition_name>/ recursive tmsh delete ltm pool /<partition_name>/ recursive tmsh delete ltm snatpool /<partition_name>/ recursive tmsh delete ltm snat-translation /<partition_name>/ recursive tmsh delete ltm profile client-ssl /<partition_name>/ recursive tmsh delete ltm persistence /<partition_name>/ recursive tmsh delete ltm monitor /<partition_name>/ recursive Step 3: Delete the partition on the Standby: tmsh delete auth partition <partition_name> > Note: If Step 3 fails with the same "0107082a" error, run "tmsh list /<partition_name>/ recursive" again to identify any remaining objects (e.g., nodes, SNAT translations, other profiles) and delete them individually before retrying. Step 4: Re-sync from Active: tmsh run cm config-sync to-group <device_group_name> Step 5: Verify on both devices: tmsh show cm sync-status After applying the workaround, monitor sync status following any future AS3 partition deletions until a fix is available.

bugs.title: A DNS cache containing many resource records may cause a tmm restart when the last Virtual Server referencing it is deleted
bugs.symptoms: When a DNS cache resolver has a very large number of cached resource records (in the order of millions) and the last Virtual Server referencing the cache is deleted, the tmm process might take a long time to remove the cache and free its memory, might miss its heartbeat signal and might be restarted. See https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K9231 for more details on tmm and its heartbeat timeout.
bugs.conditions: - DNS module provisioned - DNS cache resolver configured on a DNS profile and in use - The DNS cache resolver contains a large number of cached resource records (in the order of millions) - The last Virtual Server referencing the DNS profile and the DNS cache resolver is deleted
bugs.impact: The TMM process is prevented from servicing its heartbeat and can be restarted
bugs.workaround: Before deleting the last Virtual Server referencing a DNS cache, wait until most of the Resource Records present in the cache have expired. The number of resource records in the cache can be monitored with this command: "tmsh show ltm dns cache records rrset cache <CACHE_NAME> count-only" Check K42437613 for more details
